description: INVESTIGATING THE MECHANISM OF ARCTIC GROUND SQUIRREL HIBERNATION AND ADAPTATION TO EXTREME ENVIRONMENTS FOR FINDING NOVEL CHRONIC DISEASE THERAPEUTICS - PROJECT SUMMARY THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO UNDERSTAND THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING NATURAL METABOLIC RESILIENCE BY STUDYING ARCTIC GROUND SQUIRRELS, ANIMALS THAT HAVE EVOLVED EXTRAORDINARY PHYSIOLOGICAL ADAPTATIONS IN THE ARCTIC THAT ARE DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO MAJOR HUMAN HEALTH CHALLENGES. IN THIS PROPOSAL WE WANT TO ESTABLISH TOOLS THAT WILL ALLOW US TO DEVELOP ARCTIC GROUND SQUIRRELS AS A MODEL SYSTEM TO STUDY THE PHENOMENAL METABOLIC PLASTICITY. THIS APPROACH MARKS A SHIFT FROM TRADITIONAL DISEASE RESEARCH, WHICH FOCUSES ON PATHOLOGICAL STATES IN LABORATORY ANIMALS, TOWARD INVESTIGATING EVOLUTIONARY MECHANISMS THAT ALLOW ANIMALS TO SURVIVE IN THE ARCTIC. CURRENT BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH OFTEN RELIES ON INDUCING DISEASE STATES IN MODEL ORGANISMS TO STUDY DISEASES STATES. WHILE THIS APPROACH HAS YIELDED IMPORTANT INSIGHTS IN MANY HUMAN DISEASES, IT HAS NOT YIELDED DESIRED RESULTS IN MANY CHRONIC HUMAN DISEASES LIKE DIABETES, MUSCLE WASTING, AND ISCHEMIC INJURY. IN CONTRAST, MILLIONS OF YEARS OF EVOLUTION HAVE PRODUCED ANIMALS WITH NATURAL RESISTANCE TO CONDITIONS THAT CAUSE SEVERE PATHOLOGY IN HUMANS. ARCTIC GROUND SQUIRRELS REPRESENT PERHAPS THE MOST EXTREME EXAMPLE OF METABOLIC RESILIENCE IN MAMMALS, YET THESE ADAPTATIONS REMAIN LARGELY UNEXPLORED WITH MODERN MOLECULAR TOOLS. THEY EXHIBIT THREE EXTRAORDINARY CAPABILITIES WITH DIRECT THERAPEUTIC RELEVANCE. FIRST, THEY NATURALLY DEVELOP PROFOUND INSULIN RESISTANCE DURING PRE- HIBERNATION, GAINING UP TO 65% OF BODY WEIGHT—THEN COMPLETELY REVERSE THIS WITHOUT DIABETES, CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, OR OTHER COMPLICATIONS. THIS OFFERS A NATURAL MODEL OF REVERSIBLE INSULIN RESISTANCE WITH TRANSFORMATIVE POTENTIAL FOR DIABETES THERAPY. SECOND, THEY MAINTAIN MUSCLE MASS AND STRENGTH THROUGH 6–8 MONTHS OF COMPLETE INACTIVITY, ADDRESSING THE CRITICAL CHALLENGE OF MUSCLE WASTING IN AGING, DISEASE, AND THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS. THIRD, HIBERNATORS RESIST ISCHEMIA-REPERFUSION INJURY, SURVIVING GLOBAL ISCHEMIC INSULTS FATAL TO OTHER MAMMALS, OFFERING INSIGHTS INTO CARDIOVASCULAR AND NEUROLOGICAL PROTECTION. THIS PROPOSAL WILL LEVERAGE CUTTING-EDGE TOOLS TO UNLOCK THESE EVOLUTIONARY SOLUTIONS. WE ARE DEVELOPING THE FIRST IPSC LINES FROM ANY ARCTIC SPECIES, ENABLING CELLULAR MODELS FOR MECHANISTIC STUDIES PREVIOUSLY IMPOSSIBLE IN THESE DIFFICULT TO ACCESS ANIMALS. WE ARE ALSO DEVELOPING TRANSGENIC ARCTIC GROUND SQUIRRELS USING MODERN REPRODUCTION BIOLOGY TOOLS. THESE GENETIC TOOLS, COMBINED WITH CIRCUIT NEUROSCIENCE APPROACHES—INCLUDING TISSUE CLEARING, LIGHTSHEET MICROSCOPY, AND SINGLE- CELL GENOMICS—WILL ENABLE MOLECULAR DISSECTION OF PHYSIOLOGICAL ADAPTIONS IN THESE ANIMALS. THE RESEARCH INTEGRATES MY EXPERIENCE SPANNING CIRCUIT NEUROSCIENCE, BIOCHEMISTRY AND FIELD STUDIES AT TOOLIK FIELD STATION IN THE ARCTIC, CREATING A PIPELINE THAT CAPTURES NATURAL ADAPTATIONS WHILE ENABLING MECHANISTIC INVESTIGATION. BY STUDYING METABOLIC FLEXIBILITY, TISSUE PRESERVATION, AND CELLULAR PROTECTION IN ARCTIC GROUND SQUIRRELS, THIS WORK WILL IDENTIFY NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS AND STRATEGIES. THIS APPROACH REPRESENTS A PARADIGM SHIFT TOWARD STUDYING NATURAL RESILIENCE RATHER THAN ARTIFICIAL PATHOLOGY, WITH POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM TREATMENTS FOR DIABETES, MUSCLE WASTING, AND ISCHEMIC DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PHYSICS-INFORMED MACHINE LEARNING FOR MEDICAL IMAGE ANALYSIS - PROJECT SUMMARY DESPITE MAJOR ADVANCES IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI), I BELIEVE THAT THE CLINICAL UTILITY OF MACHINE LEARNING (ML) SYSTEMS FOR MEDICAL IMAGE ANALYSIS REMAINS LIMITED. WHILE FOUNDATION MODELS SUCH AS LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS (LLMS) AND VISION-LANGUAGE MODELS (VLMS) HAVE DEMONSTRATED EXCEPTIONAL PERFORMANCE IN NATURAL IMAGE AND LANGUAGE DOMAINS, THEIR REAL-WORLD PERFORMANCE IN CLINICAL IMAGING TASKS CONTINUES TO FALL SHORT, ESPECIALLY IN SETTINGS WITH LIMITED DATA, COMPLEX CLINICAL CONTEXT, OR THE NEED FOR CAUSAL REASONING. IN MY VIEW, A CENTRAL LIMITATION IS THAT THESE MODELS ARE TYPICALLY TRAINED ON LARGE, STATIC IMAGE-REPORT PAIRS WITHOUT INCORPORATING THE UNDERLYING PHYSICAL AND ANATOMICAL KNOWLEDGE THAT HUMAN EXPERTS RELY ON. IN THIS PROJECT, I PROPOSE A FUNDAMENTALLY NEW APPROACH TO MEDICAL IMAGE UNDERSTANDING BY EMBEDDING PHYSICAL AND ANATOMICAL PRIORS INTO THE TRAINING OF AI SYSTEMS. MY STRATEGY IS TWOFOLD: FIRST, I WILL BUILD A GENERATIVE SIMULATION ENVIRONMENT THAT MODELS DYNAMIC HUMAN ANATOMY AND PHYSIOLOGY AND GENERATES REALISTIC SYNTHETIC IMAGING DATA, SUCH AS RADIOGRAPHS AND CT SCANS, USING KNOWN TISSUE PROPERTIES AND FORWARD IMAGING MODELS. SECOND, I WILL DEVELOP VISION-LANGUAGE-BASED CAUSAL REASONING MODELS THAT CAN EXPLAIN IMAGING FINDINGS BASED ON UNDERLYING PHYSICAL AND PHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS. THESE TWO COMPONENTS COMPLEMENT ONE ANOTHER: THE SIMULATION ENGINE WILL PROVIDE STRUCTURED, CONTROLLABLE, AND DYNAMIC VISUAL INPUTS, WHILE THE REASONING MODELS WILL LEARN TO ASSOCIATE VISUAL CONTENT WITH CAUSAL EXPLANATIONS USING CURATED IMAGE- TEXT SOURCES. I WILL APPLY AND EVALUATE THESE APPROACHES IN TWO REPRESENTATIVE USE CASES: GENERAL RADIOGRAPH ANALYSIS AND BODY CT INTERPRETATION. I WILL LEVERAGE PUBLIC DATASETS AND ANATOMICAL ATLASES ALONGSIDE SYNTHETIC DATA GENERATED THROUGH MY SIMULATION PIPELINE. I WILL ASSESS PERFORMANCE THROUGH EXPERT RADIOLOGIST EVALUATIONS AND BENCHMARK TASKS MEASURING REALISM, GENERALIZATION, ROBUSTNESS, AND DATA EFFICIENCY. MY GOAL IS TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF MEDICAL AI SYSTEMS THAT DO NOT SIMPLY DETECT PATTERNS BUT UNDERSTAND THE PHYSICAL PRINCIPLES THAT GIVE RISE TO THEM. THIS WORK WILL OPEN NEW PATHS TO EXPLAINABILITY, MORE EFFICIENT TRAINING, AND IMPROVED CLINICAL RELEVANCE. GIVEN ITS INTERDISCIPLINARY NATURE AND ITS POTENTIAL TO SHAPE FOUNDATIONAL APPROACHES IN MEDICAL AI, I BELIEVE THIS PROJECT IS UNIQUELY SUITED FOR THE NIH NEW INNOVATOR AWARD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REIMAGINING CHELATOR DESIGN TO UNLOCK THE NEXT GENERATION OF TARGETED RADIOPHARMACEUTICALS - PROJECT SUMMARY  THIS NEW INNOVATOR PROPOSAL SUPPORTS THE LAUNCH OF AN EARLY-CAREER RESEARCH PROGRAM FOCUSED ON REIMAGINING THE DESIGN OF BIFUNCTIONAL CHELATORS TO UNLOCK THE NEXT-GENERATION OF TARGETED RADIOPHARMACEUTICALS FOR CANCER DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT. THE MOUNTING INTEREST IN TARGETED RADIOPHARMACEUTICALS, COUPLED WITH ADVANCES IN RADIOISOTOPE PRODUCTION, HAS GIVEN RISE TO AN ARSENAL OF EMERGING MEDICAL RADIONUCLIDES SPANNING THE PERIODIC TABLE. THESE RADIONUCLIDES POSSESS ATTRACTIVE NUCLEAR DECAY PROPERTIES AND HALF-LIVES THAT COULD RENDER THEM EXTREMELY VALUABLE FOR IMAGING AND TREATING A WIDER RANGE OF CANCERS. YET, MANY OF THEM REMAIN UNTAPPED—STUCK IN THE “VALLEY OF DEATH” BETWEEN PRODUCTION AND CLINICAL IMPLEMENTATION—BECAUSE OF A LACK OF BIFUNCTIONAL CHELATORS THAT CAN DELIVER THEM EFFECTIVELY TO CANCER CELLS. THE DESIGN OF BIFUNCTIONAL CHELATORS HAS REMAINED UNCHANGED OVER THE LAST TWO DECADES, WITH MOST CHELATORS ONLY ABLE TO BIND A SINGLE RADIOMETAL CATION VIA STRONG DATIVE BONDING INTERACTIONS AND ATTACH TO A SINGLE TARGETING VECTOR. THIS PARADIGM IS INCOMPATIBLE WITH THE DIVERSE CHEMICAL PROPERTIES, PURITY, AND COMPOSITION OF MANY EMERGING RADIONUCLIDES. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP STRUCTURALLY EXPANDED CHELATING FRAMEWORKS TO BUCK THE CURRENT “ONE RADIOCATION–ONE CHELATOR–ONE TARGETING VECTOR” PARADIGM THAT IS HOLDING BACK MANY RADIONUCLIDES. BECAUSE THERE IS NO ONE-SIZE-FITS-ALL APPROACH TO SATISFY EVERY EMERGING RADIONUCLIDE, WE WILL EXPLORE A THREE-PRONGED DESIGN STRATEGY TO ACHIEVE OUR GOAL. NAMELY, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT STRUCTURALLY EXPANDED CHELATING FRAMEWORKS INCORPORATING THE FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES OF ANION RECOGNITION, COOPERATIVITY, AND MULTIPLICITY CAN BE DESIGNED TO SURMOUNT THE MAJOR OBSTACLES IN MEDICAL RADIONUCLIDE ADVANCEMENT RELATED TO COMPLEX AQUEOUS SPECIATION, POOR STABILITY, AND LOW SPECIFIC ACTIVITY, RESPECTIVELY. NOTABLY, THESE CHALLENGES ARE PERVASIVE ACROSS A WIDE RANGE OF EMERGING RADIONUCLIDES WITH STRONG POTENTIAL TO ADVANCE THE FIELD OF CANCER IMAGING AND THERAPY. OUR APPROACH INTEGRATES ORGANIC SYNTHESIS, RADIOCHEMISTRY, IN VITRO EXPERIMENTS, AND COLLABORATIVE IN VIVO STUDIES TO EVALUATE THE COORDINATION CHEMISTRY OF NOVEL BIFUNCTIONAL CONSTRUCTS WITH REPRESENTATIVE EMERGING RADIONUCLIDES AND ESTABLISH THEIR ABILITY TO IMPROVE RADIONUCLIDE DELIVERY TO CANCER CELLS IN COMPARISON TO CONVENTIONAL CHELATORS. BY DIRECTLY ADDRESSING THE KEY BARRIERS LIMITING THE USE OF EMERGING RADIONUCLIDES, THIS RESEARCH WILL DELIVER BROADLY ENABLING CHELATION STRATEGIES THAT OPEN NEW FRONTIERS IN RADIOPHARMACEUTICAL SCIENCE AND PRECISION ONCOLOGY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DECODING CELL-FATE DECISIONS THROUGH MOLECULAR RECORDING - PROJECT SUMMARY DECIPHERING HOW COMBINATIONS OF INTRINSIC AND EXTRINSIC CUES DETERMINE CELL FATES IS A FUNDAMENTAL CHALLENGE IN DEVELOPMENTAL BIOLOGY, WITH BROAD IMPLICATIONS FOR REGENERATIVE MEDICINE AND CANCER. WHILE SINGLE-CELL GENOMICS TECHNOLOGIES CAN PROFILE CELL STATES IN DETAIL, CURRENT APPROACHES CANNOT RECONSTRUCT HOW PRIOR EVENTS—SUCH AS SIGNALING PATHWAY ACTIVATIONS, TRANSIENT GENE EXPRESSION CHANGES, OR CELL-CELL INTERACTIONS—SHAPE DEVELOPMENTAL OUTCOMES. HERE WE PROPOSE TO CREATE A NEW CLASS OF SINGLE-CELL GENOMIC RECORDING TECHNOLOGIES THAT INTEGRATE PAST CELLULAR HISTORIES WITH PRESENT STATES CAPTURED BY SINGLE-CELL PROFILING. WE WILL DESIGN MODULAR SYNTHETIC CIRCUITS THAT PERMANENTLY ENCODE DIVERSE BIOLOGICAL EVENTS—LINEAGE HISTORY, SIGNALING ACTIVITY, TRANSIENT TRANSCRIPT EXPRESSION, MICROENVIRONMENTAL INTERACTIONS, AND CRISPR-BASED GENETIC PERTURBATIONS—AS RETRIEVABLE DNA EDITS. THESE RECORDS WILL ENABLE THE RETROSPECTIVE RECONSTRUCTION OF DEVELOPMENTAL TRAJECTORIES AT SINGLE-CELL RESOLUTION, REVEALING HOW COMBINATIONS OF PAST CELLULAR EVENTS PROGRAM FINAL CELL TYPE. AS A PROOF OF CONCEPT, WE WILL APPLY THIS SYSTEM TO THE DIRECTED DIFFERENTIATION OF HUMAN PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS INTO PANCREATIC ISLETS, A CLINICALLY RELEVANT MODEL FOR TREATING TYPE 1 DIABETES. THIS APPROACH WILL REVEAL HOW TRANSIENT CELLULAR EVENTS AFFECT CELL-FATE DECISIONS AND ESTABLISH A BROADLY APPLICABLE PLATFORM FOR RECORDING AND RECONSTRUCTING SEQUENCES OF CELLULAR EVENTS THAT DETERMINE THE FINAL CELL FATE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BIFUNCTIONAL SMALL MOLECULES FOR BIOSENSING AND CONTINUOUS ENZYME EVOLUTION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ENZYMES ARE THE WORLD'S MOST SKILLED ORGANIC CHEMISTS. AT THEIR BEST, ENZYMES OUTPERFORM TRADITIONAL CHEMICAL REAGENTS IN EVERY CONSIDERATION FROM COST, TO SELECTIVITY AND PRODUCT PURITY, TO ENVIRONMENTAL WASTE. HOWEVER, FINDING AN ENZYME FOR A NEW REACTION REMAINS PROHIBITIVELY DIFFICULT. THERE ARE TWO PROBLEMS: FIRST, LOW-THROUGHPUT ANALYTICAL CHEMISTRY (SUCH AS LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPHY–MASS SPECTROMETRY) LIMITS CLASSICAL DIRECTED EVOLUTION TO 102 VARIANTS PER ROUND; SECOND, MANUAL OPERATIONS TO GENERATE MUTANT LIBRARIES TAKE DAYS BETWEEN ROUNDS. CONTINUOUS EVOLUTION IS THE SOLUTION. THE RAPID PHAGE LIFE CYCLE AND ULTRA-HIGH MUTATION RATES IN PHAGE-ASSISTED CONTINUOUS EVOLUTION EXPLORE VASTLY MORE SEQUENCE SPACE (~1011 VARIANTS WITH CONTINUOUS SELECTION OVER 3 DAYS) THAN CLASSICAL DIRECTED EVOLUTION. THESE NUMBERS ARE SUFFICIENT TO COVER ALL DOUBLE MUTANTS AND MOST TRIPLE MUTANTS FOR A SMALL EVOLVING PROTEIN IN A SINGLE GENERATION OF PHAGE, WITH HUNDREDS OF GENERATIONS PER DAY. HOWEVER, WE CANNOT CONDUCT SELECTIONS FOR ENZYMES THAT MAKE SMALL MOLECULES BECAUSE WE LACK THE MOLECULAR TOOLS. WE NEED BIOSENSORS TO MEASURE SMALL-MOLECULE CONCENTRATION—FOR ANY SMALL MOLECULE—AND TRANSLATE THAT SIGNAL INTO GENE EXPRESSION IN ORDER TO DISCRIMINATE BETWEEN LOW-PRODUCING AND HIGH-PRODUCING ENZYMES. MY PREVIOUS WORK REVEALED A TECHNIQUE TO DELIVER LARGE (CA. 1 KDA) SMALL MOLECULES INTO E. COLI, THE HOST ORGANISM FOR PHAGE-ASSISTED CONTINUOUS EVOLUTION. THIS DISCOVERY SETS THE STAGE TO CONTROL CELLULAR PROCESSES IN E. COLI WITH BIFUNCTIONAL SMALL MOLECULES, MOLECULES THAT ENGAGE TWO PROTEINS WITH TWO LIGANDS CONNECTED BY A LINKER. BIFUNCTIONALS HAVE REVOLUTIONIZED THE STUDY OF (MORE PERMEABLE) MAMMALIAN CELLS IN CHEMICAL BIOLOGY. ARMED WITH THESE TOOLS AND A MEANS TO DELIVER THEM, I PROPOSE: (1) A STRATEGY FOR GENERAL SMALL-MOLECULE BIOSENSING IN E. COLI; (2) A PLATFORM TO USE THESE BIOSENSORS FOR CONTINUOUS DIRECTED EVOLUTION OF ENZYMES; (3) A FULLY ENZYMATIC REPLACEMENT OF PEPTIDE SYNTHESIS REAGENTS; AND (4), A CHEMOENZYMATIC ROUTE TO PREVIOUSLY INACCESSIBLE GLYCOPEPTIDE ANTIBIOTICS. THE PROPOSAL CONSTITUTES A HIGH-RISK, HIGH-REWARD, VISION TO COMPLETELY RESHAPE CATALYSIS USING CONTINUOUS EVOLUTION, WITH BROAD IMPACTS ON NATURAL AND DESIGNED ENZYMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DISCOVERY AND ENGINEERING OF NICKEL BIOCATALYSTS FOR THE PRECISE TAILORING OF THERAPEUTICS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CATALYST DEVELOPMENT HAS TRANSFORMED BIOMEDICAL SCIENCE BY ENABLING THE SYNTHESIS OF THERAPEUTIC MOLECULES. RECENT INNOVATIONS IN NICKEL CATALYSTS HAVE ENABLED EXCITING NEW CHEMICAL TRANSFORMATIONS THAT ARISE FROM THE UNIQUE REACTIVITY OF NICKEL. HOWEVER, THE POWERFUL REACTIVITY OF NICKEL IS CHALLENGING TO PREDICT AND CONTROL, OFTEN LEADING TO THE NON-SPECIFIC MODIFICATION OF LEAD COMPOUNDS RATHER THAN THE PRECISE TAILORING OF PROMISING THERAPEUTIC CANDIDATES. THE DEVELOPMENT OF ENZYMES THAT COULD CONTROL THE OUTCOME OF NICKEL-CATALYZED REACTIONS WOULD MERGE THE REACTION VERSATILITY OF NICKEL WITH THE SELECTIVITY OF ENZYMES. HOWEVER, NICKEL BIOCATALYSIS IS SEVERELY UNDERDEVELOPED DUE TO THE LACK OF KNOWN NICKEL ENZYMES: ONLY TEN NICKEL ENZYMES HAVE BEEN REPORTED TO DATE. TO OVERCOME THIS CHALLENGE, WE WILL PIONEER SYNERGISTIC INNOVATIONS IN ENZYME DISCOVERY AND ENGINEERING TO DEVELOP A SUITE OF NICKEL ENZYMES WITH PROMISING BIOCATALYTIC PROPERTIES, INCLUDING (1) A BROAD SUBSTRATE SCOPE, (2) AN OPEN ACTIVE SITE TO ACCOMMODATE LARGE, COMPLEX MOLECULES, AND (3) ROBUST STABILITY. IN ONE APPROACH, WE WILL DEVELOP A BIOINFORMATIC PIPELINE TO DISCOVER AND CHARACTERIZE NEW NICKEL ENZYMES FROM NATURE. IN PRELIMINARY RESULTS, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED AND CHARACTERIZED A PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN NICKEL ENZYME WITH PROMISING BIOCATALYTIC PROPERTIES THAT PERFORMS CHEMISTRY ON SUGARS. IN PARALLEL, WE WILL ENGINEER ENZYMES THAT USE THE COMMON NICOTINAMIDE ADENINE DINUCLEOTIDE COFACTOR TO INSTEAD BIND AND HARNESS A NICKEL-CONTAINING COFACTOR, EXPANDING THE NUMBER OF NICKEL ENZYMES FROM TEN TO POTENTIALLY HUNDREDS. FINALLY, WE WILL APPLY THE POWER OF DIRECTED EVOLUTION TO EVOLVE A SUITE OF NICKEL CATALYSTS THAT PERFORM PRECISE, SITE-SELECTIVE CHEMISTRY ON COMPLEX BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS LIKE SUGAR DERIVATIVES AND NATURAL PRODUCTS. THIS WORK WILL EXPAND OUR KNOWLEDGE OF NICKEL BIOCHEMISTRY AND YIELD THE FIRST TOOLBOX OF NICKEL BIOCATALYSTS FOR THE SELECTIVE SYNTHESIS OF NEW THERAPEUTIC MOLECULES.

description: PREDICTIVE DESIGN OF TISSUE ARCHITECTURE USING SYNTHETIC CELL ADHESION - ENGINEERING HUMAN TISSUES TO CREATE ORGANOIDS HAS ADVANCED DISEASE MODELING AND ACCELERATED DRUG SCREENING BY DECREASING THE RELIANCE ON ANIMAL TESTING. HOWEVER, CURRENT APPROACHES CAN BE LIMITED BY PHENOTYPIC VARIABILITY, A LACK OF PRECISE CONTROL OF MULTICELLULAR INTERACTIONS, AND THE INABILITY TO DIRECT COMPLEX MULTI-TISSUE ASSEMBLIES. WE AIM TO OVERCOME THESE CHALLENGES BY APPLYING SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY TO DIRECT THE MOLECULAR INTERACTIONS THAT DETERMINE TISSUE ASSEMBLY. THIS PROPOSAL OUTLINES A SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY RESEARCH PROGRAM IN MY LAB THAT SYSTEMATICALLY MAPS THE MOLECULAR FEATURES OF CELL ADHESION MOLECULES (CAMS) TO THEIR ADHESION STRENGTH, TRAINS MACHINE LEARNING MODELS TO PREDICT MOLECULAR ORGANIZATION FROM MOLECULAR INPUTS, AND APPLIES THESE MODELS TO RATIONALLY DESIGN AND BUILD SYNTHETIC TISSUE STRUCTURES. WE HAVE DEVELOPED SYNTHETIC CAMS (SYNCAMS), A CLASS OF CHIMERIC RECEPTORS THAT ENABLE SYSTEMATIC COMPARISON OF ADHESION FUNCTION, AND WE WILL INTEGRATE THIS TECHNOLOGY WITH A NOVEL PLATFORM COMBINING POOLED CELL LIBRARIES, HIGH-THROUGHPUT SPATIAL SEQUENCING, AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING. IN INITIAL STUDIES, WE HAVE SHOWN THAT SYNCAMS CAN MEDIATE SPECIFIC CELL-CELL INTERACTIONS. OUR LAB WILL NOW ADAPT THIS PLATFORM TO RAPIDLY CHARACTERIZE THOUSANDS OF UNIQUE ADHESION-DRIVEN ARCHITECTURES TO IDENTIFY DESIGN RULES CONNECTING THE MOLECULAR FEATURES OF CAMS TO TISSUE-LEVEL PROPERTIES LIKE CELL SPREADING AND CELL SORTING. WE WILL TRAIN MACHINE LEARNING MODELS ON THIS DATA TO EXAMINE THE MODULAR FUNCTION OF CELL ADHESION MOLECULES AND APPLY THESE TOOLS TO ASSEMBLE COMPLEX MULTICELLULAR STRUCTURES THAT MODEL SKIN LAYERS. THIS WORK WILL ESTABLISH DESIGN RULES FOR MULTICELLULAR ASSEMBLY AND AN ENGINEERING-BASED APPROACH TO BUILDING COMPLEX ORGANOIDS AND CELLULAR THERAPIES.

description: CELLULAR INNOVATION VIA ORGANELLE THEFT - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE EVOLUTION OF NEW TRAITS IS A FUNDAMENTAL QUESTION IN BIOLOGY, AND UNDERSTANDING HOW IT OCCURS IS CENTRAL TO EXPLAINING THE BREADTH OF EXISTING PHYSIOLOGY, THE POTENTIAL TO ENGINEER NOVEL FUNCTIONS, AND THE CAUSES OF HUMAN PATHOPHYSIOLOGY. THE ALLARD LABORATORY ADDRESSES THIS CHALLENGE BY STUDYING UNUSUAL ORGANISMS THAT REVEAL OVERLOOKED BIOLOGY AND CONSERVED PRINCIPLES OF CELLULAR FUNCTION. THIS PROJECT FOCUSES ON ORGANELLE THEFT, A STRIKING PHENOMENON IN WHICH CERTAIN ANIMALS CAPTURE FUNCTIONAL ORGANELLES FROM OTHER SPECIES AND INTEGRATE THEM INTO THEIR OWN CELLS. THROUGH THIS LENS, THE RESEARCH EXPLORES HOW UNCONVENTIONAL BIOLOGICAL STRATEGIES CAN REVEAL CONSERVED RULES OF CELLULAR INNOVATION. THE PROJECT AIMS TO DEFINE THE MOLECULAR AND CELLULAR STRATEGIES THAT ALLOW STOLEN ORGANELLES TO BE RECOGNIZED, MAINTAINED, AND INTEGRATED INTO HOST CELLS. IT FOCUSES ON TWO EXTREME EXAMPLES OF ORGANELLE THEFT IN SEA SLUGS: ONE THAT SEQUESTERS CHLOROPLASTS FROM ALGAE TO ENABLE ANIMAL PHOTOSYNTHESIS, AND ANOTHER THAT ACQUIRES STINGING ORGANELLES FROM SEA ANEMONES FOR DEFENSE. BY IDENTIFYING BOTH COMMON AND CARGO-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS, THIS RESEARCH WILL UNCOVER GENERALIZABLE PRINCIPLES GOVERNING THE RETENTION AND USE OF FOREIGN ORGANELLES. UNDERSTANDING THE RULES BY WHICH CELLS ACQUIRE AND SUSTAIN NEW FUNCTIONAL COMPONENTS HAS BROAD BIOMEDICAL RELEVANCE, FROM DESIGNING CELLS WITH ENHANCED METABOLIC OR DEFENSIVE TRAITS TO DEVELOPING NOVEL BIOTECHNOLOGIES. BY LEVERAGING EXTREME EXAMPLES FROM NATURE, THIS WORK SEEKS TO DEFINE FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES OF CELLULAR INNOVATION WITH POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM MULTIPLE AREAS OF BIOLOGY AND MEDICINE. THE PROJECT IS WELL POSITIONED FOR SUCCESS BECAUSE IT INTEGRATES AN INNOVATIVE RESEARCH FRAMEWORK WITH INTERDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATION TO EXPLORE AND RECONSTITUTE ORGANELLE THEFT. COMBINING ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, MOLECULAR CELL BIOLOGY, EVOLUTIONARY COMPARISON, AND IN VITRO RECONSTITUTION, IT RESOLVES BOTH MECHANISTIC AND FUNCTIONAL DIMENSIONS OF FOREIGN ORGANELLE USE. THIS WORK BUILDS ON DR. ALLARD’S RESEARCH SPANNING A WIDE RANGE OF ORGANISMS AND BIOLOGICAL QUESTIONS, INCLUDING SEMINAL STUDIES OF THE CELLS AND ORGANELLES INVOLVED IN CHLOROPLAST THEFT IN ELYSIA SLUGS. ACROSS THESE DIVERSE CONTEXTS, DR. ALLARD HAS DEVELOPED AND APPLIED CHALLENGING AND INNOVATIVE MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, AND PHYSIOLOGICAL APPROACHES TO UNCOVER FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES OF ORGANISMAL AND CELLULAR BIOLOGY. THIS PROJECT REFLECTS A LONG- STANDING COMMITMENT TO CURIOSITY-DRIVEN BASIC SCIENCE, MOTIVATED BY THE CONVICTION THAT STUDYING UNCONVENTIONAL SYSTEMS CAN REVEAL NEW RULES OF BIOLOGY WITH RELEVANCE TO BOTH BASIC RESEARCH AND MEDICINE. BEYOND ITS FUNDAMENTAL BIOLOGICAL IMPACT, INSIGHTS FROM THESE STUDIES MAY INFORM NOVEL BIOTECHNOLOGIES AND THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES, GUIDING APPROACHES TO TREAT DISEASES CAUSED BY ORGANELLE DYSFUNCTION OR TO ENGINEER CELLS WITH ENHANCED METABOLIC OR DEFENSIVE CAPABILITIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE DUAL ROLE OF MEMORIZATION: COMPUTATIONAL METHODS FOR BALANCING MODEL PERFORMANCE AND PRIVACY PROTECTION IN AI - PROJECT SUMMARY RAPID ADVANCES IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) TECHNOLOGY AND INCREASING COMPUTING CAPABILITIES HAVE GIVEN RISE TO LARGE AI MODELS CAPABLE OF HARNESSING COMPLEX, MULTIMODAL PATIENT DATA. HOWEVER, RECENT STUDIES HAVE SHOWN THAT THESE MODELS MAY MEMORIZE INDIVIDUAL TRAINING SAMPLES WITH SIGNIFICANT IMPLICATIONS FOR DATA PRIVACY. PRIVACY BREACHES HAVE SEVERE CONSEQUENCES FOR DATA CONTRIBUTORS AND INSTITUTIONS, AND COULD HAMPER AI TECHNOLOGY ADOPTION AND ERODE TRUST IN RESEARCH. ALTHOUGH STATE-OF-THE-ART PRIVACY PARADIGM, NAMELY DIFFERENTIAL PRIVACY, PROVIDES RIGOROUS PRIVACY GUARANTEES, IT DOES NOT CONSIDER INDIVIDUALIZED PRIVACY RISKS AND RESULTS IN DIMINISHED UTILITY DUE TO EXCESSIVELY RESTRAINING MEMORIZATION. NEW PRIVACY-PROTECTING APPROACHES THAT TAKE A HOLISTIC VIEW OF MODEL MEMORIZATION ARE NEEDED TO MITIGATE PRIVACY RISKS AND RETAIN MODEL UTILITY. IN THIS PROJECT, WE PROPOSE AN INNOVATIVE APPROACH TO SAFEGUARDING PRIVACY IN AI. WE WILL EXAMINE THE DUAL ROLE OF MEMORIZATION, QUANTIFYING ITS ADVERSE EFFECTS ON PRIVACY LEAKAGE AND CONTRIBUTIONS TO MODEL PERFORMANCE. WE CHARACTERIZE MEMORIZATION FOR EACH TRAINING SAMPLE, ADDRESSING INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES IN PRIVACY RISKS AND UTILITY CONTRIBUTIONS. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE SAMPLE-LEVEL RISK AND INFLUENCE SCORES TO DEVELOP PRIVACY-PRESERVING TECHNIQUES THAT OPTIMIZE THE PRIVACY-UTILITY TRADE-OFF DURING TRAINING. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL INTEGRATE OUR TECHNIQUES INTO STANDARD AI DEVELOPMENT PIPELINES (E.G., MODEL SELECTION AND HYPERPARAMETER TUNING), PROVIDING DATA HOLDERS WITH NEW TOOLS FOR MAKING INFORMED DECISIONS ABOUT DEPLOYING EMERGING MODELS (E.G., LLM, MULTI-MODAL FOUNDATION MODELS) IN HEALTHCARE AND RESEARCH SETTINGS. OVERALL, THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS SIGNIFICANT AS IT TARGETS PRIVACY CONCERNS REGARDING THE BROADER UTILIZATION AND SHARING OF LARGE MULTIMODAL AI MODELS. THIS PROJECT MAKES IMPORTANT CONTRIBUTIONS TOWARDS ONE OF THE MAIN OBJECTIVES OF THE NIH, WHICH IS TO DEVELOP INNOVATIVE DATA SCIENCE AND COMPUTATIONAL METHODS TO SUPPORT AI-DRIVEN ANALYSIS WITH THE GOAL OF ADVANCING HUMAN HEALTH WHILE PRESERVING SAFEGUARDS AND ETHICAL PROTECTIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

description: IMMUNOLOGICAL REPROGRAMMING OF PAIN CIRCUITRY - PROJECT SUMMARY CHRONIC PAIN AFFECTS OVER 20% OF AMERICAN ADULTS AND IS A LEADING CAUSE OF DISABILITY, LOST PRODUCTIVITY, AND OPIOID DEPENDENCE. DESPITE ITS SOCIETAL BURDEN, THERE ARE FEW EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS THAT OFFER DURABLE RELIEF WITHOUT SYSTEMIC SIDE EFFECTS OR RISK OF ADDICTION. A KEY CHALLENGE IS THE LACK OF THERAPIES THAT CAN TARGET PAIN-DRIVING SENSORY NEURONS SELECTIVELY WITHOUT AFFECTING OTHER TISSUES OR DISRUPTING NORMAL SENSORY FUNCTIONS. THIS PROJECT PROPOSES A TRANSFORMATIVE SOLUTION BY ENGINEERING T CELLS TO ACT AS PROGRAMMABLE THERAPEUTIC DELIVERY VEHICLES THAT CAN DETECT PAIN-RELATED SIGNALS AND SECRETE NATURAL, DURABLE ANALGESIC SIGNALS DIRECTLY AT SITES OF NEURAL DYSFUNCTION. BUILDING ON OUR RECENT DISCOVERY THAT REGULATORY T CELLS CAN NATURALLY SUPPRESS PAIN THROUGH ENDOGENOUS OPIOID RELEASE, THIS CROSS-CUTTING WORK INTEGRATES IMMUNOLOGY, NEUROSCIENCE, AND SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY TO REPROGRAM T CELLS INTO SITE-SPECIFIC MODULATORS OF PAIN. USING SYNTHETIC RECEPTORS, T CELLS WILL BE DESIGNED TO HOME TO DORSAL ROOT GANGLIA, THE SENSORY RELAY HUBS OUTSIDE THE SPINAL CORD, AND SENSE MOLECULES THAT ARE SELECTIVELY UPREGULATED IN CHRONIC PAIN CONDITIONS. ONLY IN THE PRESENCE OF THESE PAIN-ASSOCIATED SIGNALS WILL THE T CELLS RELEASE ANTI-NOCICEPTIVE PEPTIDES AND CYTOKINES, SUCH AS ENKEPHALIN AND IL-10, BOTH OF WHICH ARE KNOWN TO SUPPRESS PAIN BUT ARE DIFFICULT TO DELIVER SAFELY USING CONVENTIONAL APPROACHES. THIS STRATEGY ALLOWS FOR SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL CONTROL OF ANALGESIC ACTION, REDUCING THE RISK OF SYSTEMIC SIDE EFFECTS AND TOLERANCE WHICH WILL BE DIRECTLY ASSESSED. THE MODULAR DESIGN OF THIS SYSTEM ALSO ENABLES FUTURE CUSTOMIZATION TO OTHER PAIN STATES OR DISORDERS INVOLVING NEURAL CIRCUITS. WORK FROM THIS RESEARCH WILL ESTABLISH A NEW THERAPEUTIC PLATFORM THAT TREATS PAIN NOT AS A GENERALIZED CONDITION, BUT AS A DYNAMIC CIRCUIT-LEVEL DYSFUNCTION THAT CAN BE MODULATED WITH CELL-BASED PRECISION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DISSECTING AGE-RELATED CHANGES IN STEM CELL-BASED BONE-GUT CROSSTALK - AGE-RELATED MUSCULOSKELETAL DETERIORATION, LEADING TO OSTEOPOROSIS AND OSTEOARTHRITIS, IS A MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH CHALLENGE POSED BY AN AGING SOCIETY, DRIVING MORBIDITY, MORTALITY, AND ELEVATED HEALTHCARE COSTS. THE GUT MICROBIOME (GM) HAS EMERGED AS A CRITICAL REGULATOR OF HOST PHYSIOLOGY, INCLUDING BONE HOMEOSTASIS. ALTERATIONS IN GM-DERIVED CIRCULATING METABOLITES, E.G., BILE ACIDS (BA), HAVE BEEN PROPOSED TO MEDIATE TISSUE-SPECIFIC DYSFUNCTION. WHILE STUDIES HAVE LINKED GM COMPOSITION TO BONE REMODELING, PRECISE MECHANISMS CONNECTING GM DYSBIOSIS TO THE FUNCTION OF STEM CELLS MAINTAINING SKELETAL AND HEMATOPOIETIC INTEGRITY REMAIN UNCLEAR. SPECIFICALLY, THE EFFECTS OF AGED GM ALTERATIONS ON SKELETAL STEM CELLS (SSCS) AND THEIR REGULATION OF THE BM NICHE ARE LARGELY UNKNOWN. IN FOUNDATIONAL PRELIMINARY STUDIES, I ESTABLISHED AN ANTIBIOTIC (ABX)-MEDIATED GM DEPLETION MODEL IN MICE AND FOUND THAT ERASING THE AGED (24-MONTH-OLD) GM SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVED AGED SSC FUNCTION (E.G., INJURY RESPONSE, OSTEOGENESIS IN VITRO AND IN VIVO). CONCURRENTLY, AGED ABX-TREATED MICE EXHIBITED REDUCED MYELOID-BIASED HEMATOPOIETIC PROGENITORS AND OSTEOCLAST ACTIVITY WITHIN THE BM, ALONGSIDE A MORE BALANCED LYMPHOID-TO-MYELOID RATIO IN CIRCULATION, SUGGESTING REDUCED BONE RESORPTION AND SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION. CRUCIALLY, HEMATOPOIETIC RECONSTITUTION EXPERIMENTS DEMONSTRATED THESE EFFECTS ON HSC LINEAGE OUTPUT ARE MEDIATED INDIRECTLY VIA THE BM NICHE ENVIRONMENT, RATHER THAN THROUGH INTRINSIC CHANGES TO HSCS, POINTING TO SSCS AS KEY MEDIATORS OF GM-BONE CROSSTALK. BASED ON OUR TRANSCRIPTOMIC DATA SHOWING SPECIFIC EXPRESSION OF THE BA RECEPTOR VITAMIN D RECEPTOR (VDR) ON SSCS, I HYPOTHESIZE THAT AGE-RELATED DYSBIOSIS SHIFTS THE SYSTEMIC BA POOL TOWARDS INFLAMMATORY SPECIES (I.E., ALTERED CONJUGATION) THAT IMPAIR SSC FUNCTION. I FURTHER HYPOTHESIZE THAT MODULATION OF VDR SIGNALING OR  YOUTHFUL  BAS CAN MODULATE SSC NICHE ACTIVITY. THESE HYPOTHESES WILL BE TESTED THROUGH TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 WILL MECHANISTICALLY DEFINE THE BA-VDR SIGNALING AXIS IN SSCS USING IN VITRO ASSAYS AND A NOVEL SKELETAL-SPECIFIC INDUCIBLE VDR KNOCKOUT MODEL TO CONFIRM LINEAGE- SPECIFIC CAUSALITY. AIM 2 WILL DEFINE AGE-DEPENDENT CHANGES IN THE BA POOL USING TARGETED LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPHY (LC) TANDEM MASS SPECTROMETRY (MS), KNOWN AS LC-MS/MS, AND DETERMINE THE THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY OF DIETARY BA SUPPLEMENTATION TO REINSTATE YOUTHFUL SSC NICHES AND HEMATOPOIETIC LINEAGE OUTPUT IN AGED ANIMALS. THIS STUDY COMBINES ADVANCED GENETIC MODELS, TARGETED METABOLOMICS, AND STEM CELL FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS TO ELUCIDATE A NOVEL GUT-BONE SIGNALING AXIS AND ASSESS THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF TARGETING THE GM FOR THE TREATMENT OF AGE- RELATED SKELETAL DISORDERS. FOR AN ASPIRING SURGEON-SCIENTIST, THIS PROJECT PROVIDES A UNIQUE TRAINING OPPORTUNITY, COMBINING A CLINICALLY RELEVANT PROBLEM WITH RIGOROUS, MECHANISM-CENTERED DISCOVERY RESEARCH THAT HAS THE POTENTIAL TO IMPACT FUTURE THERAPIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SUSTAINED DELIVERY OF SIRNA-LIPID NANOPARTICLES VIA POLYMER IMPLANT FOR VOCAL FOLD SCARRING - PROJECT SUMMARY VOICE DISORDERS AFFECT APPROXIMATELY 30 MILLION AMERICANS ANNUALLY—NEARLY 1 IN 8 ADULTS—AND ARE FREQUENTLY ASSOCIATED WITH VOCAL FOLD (VF) SCARRING FOLLOWING LARYNGEAL INJURY. DYSPHONIA RESULTING FROM VF FIBROSIS SIGNIFICANTLY IMPAIRS COMMUNICATION, QUALITY OF LIFE, AND WORK PRODUCTIVITY. ENDOTRACHEAL INTUBATION IS A COMMON IATROGENIC CAUSE OF VF TRAUMA, INITIATING FIBROTIC REMODELING DRIVEN BY TRANSFORMING GROWTH FACTOR-BETA (TGF) SIGNALING. CURRENT TREATMENTS, INCLUDING INTRALESIONAL STEROID INJECTIONS, PROVIDE ONLY TRANSIENT BENEFIT, REQUIRING REPEATED ADMINISTRATION AND CARRYING RISKS OF ADVERSE EFFECTS. GENE SILENCING OF SMAD3, A KEY MEDIATOR OF TGF- DRIVEN FIBROSIS, REPRESENTS A PROMISING THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY; HOWEVER, CLINICAL TRANSLATION OF SMALL INTERFERING RNA (SIRNA) THERAPIES IS LIMITED BY RAPID DEGRADATION AND POOR LOCAL RETENTION. LIPID NANOPARTICLES (LNPS) IMPROVE INTRACELLULAR DELIVERY OF SIRNA BUT DO NOT ADDRESS THE CHALLENGE OF SUSTAINED LOCAL THERAPEUTIC EXPOSURE. THIS PROJECT PROPOSES TO OVERCOME THESE LIMITATIONS BY DEVELOPING A BIODEGRADABLE POLYMER-BASED IMPLANT CAPABLE OF SUSTAINED, LOCALIZED RELEASE OF SMAD3 SIRNA-LOADED LNPS (SIRNA-LNPS). OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT SUSTAINED DELIVERY OF BIOLOGICALLY ACTIVE SIRNA-LNPS WILL MAINTAIN THERAPEUTIC LOCAL EXPOSURE OVER CLINICALLY RELEVANT TIMEFRAMES, ENABLING PROLONGED MODULATION OF FIBROTIC SIGNALING AND MEASURABLE IMPROVEMENTS IN VF FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES FOLLOWING INJURY. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL PURSUE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) DEVELOP TUNABLE SIRNA-LNP-ELUTING IMPLANTS AND VALIDATE ANTIFIBROTIC ACTIVITY OF RELEASED SIRNA-LNPS IN VITRO; AND (2) EVALUATE THE IN VIVO FEASIBILITY AND BIOLOGICAL ACTIVITY OF SUSTAINED SIRNA-LNP DELIVERY IN A RABBIT VF INJURY MODEL, BENCHMARKED AGAINST BOLUS DEXAMETHASONE INJECTION USING A MULTIMODAL ASSESSMENT OF VIBRATORY, BIOMECHANICAL, AND HISTOLOGICAL OUTCOMES. COMPLETION OF THIS WORK WILL ESTABLISH A PLATFORM FOR SUSTAINED, LOCALIZED SIRNA DELIVERY IN THE VFS AND PROVIDE FOUNDATIONAL DATA FOR FUTURE THERAPEUTIC OPTIMIZATION. THIS FELLOWSHIP WILL PROVIDE INTEGRATED TRAINING IN BIOMATERIALS-BASED DRUG DELIVERY, RNA THERAPEUTICS, VF WOUND HEALING, MULTIMODAL OUTCOME EVALUATION, AND TRANSLATIONAL OTOLARYNGOLOGY RESEARCH WITHIN AN INTERDISCIPLINARY ENVIRONMENT AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CINCINNATI WITH MENTORSHIP SPANNING BIOMEDICAL ENGINEERING, LARYNGOLOGY, AND VOCAL FOLD PHYSIOLOGY.

description: SYSTEMIC BILE ACID DYSREGULATION DRIVES ALVEOLAR BONE LOSS IN COLITIS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT COLITIS IS A CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY GUT DISORDER WITH SIGNIFICANT EXTRAINTESTINAL MANIFESTATIONS. THESE INCLUDE A HIGH PREVALENCE OF PERIODONTITIS, A DISEASE DEFINED BY SUBSTANTIAL ALVEOLAR BONE LOSS. THE MECHANISM LINKING INTESTINAL INFLAMMATION TO ORAL BONE PATHOLOGY REMAINS A CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAP. THIS F30 APPLICATION WILL INVESTIGATE A NOVEL GUT-METABOLITE-ORAL BONE AXIS. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT COLITIS-INDUCED GUT DYSBIOSIS ALTERS THE SYSTEMIC BILE ACID PROFILE, INCREASING THE RATIO OF PRIMARY TO SECONDARY BILE ACIDS, WHICH IN TURN DRIVES ALVEOLAR BONE LOSS BY INHIBITING THE PRO-OSTEOGENIC NUCLEAR FARNESOID X RECEPTOR (FXR) IN BONE CELLS. THE RESEARCH PLAN WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS THROUGH THREE SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 WILL USE A DEXTRAN SULFATE SODIUM (DSS) MOUSE MODEL OF COLITIS TO DEMONSTRATE THAT INTESTINAL INFLAMMATION INDUCES SYSTEMIC BILE ACID DYSREGULATION AND PROMOTES ALVEOLAR BONE LOSS. AIM 2 WILL DEFINE THE DIRECT EFFECTS OF A COLITIS-ASSOCIATED BILE ACID COCKTAIL ON THE FUNCTION OF PRIMARY OSTEOBLASTS AND OSTEOCLASTS IN VITRO USING FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS. AIM 3 WILL DETERMINE IF THE PATHOGENIC BILE ACID PROFILE PHENOCOPIES GENETIC FXR DELETION IN OSTEOBLAST- AND OSTEOCLAST-LINEAGE CELLS, USING IN VITRO INDUCIBLE CRE-LOX MOUSE MODELS. THE FELLOWSHIP APPLICATION WILL SUPPORT A D.M.D./PH.D. CANDIDATE WHOSE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENT ACADEMIC ORTHODONTIST-SCIENTIST. THE CANDIDATE’S TRAINING PLAN, DEVELOPED WITH SPONSORS DR. WESTWATER (HOST-MICROBE INTERACTIONS) AND DR. ENGEVIK (DIGESTIVE DISEASES), WILL STRENGTHEN THE APPLICANT’S SCIENTIFIC EXPERTISE, LEADERSHIP AND MENTORING SKILLS, AND INTERDISCIPLINARY PROFESSIONAL NETWORK. TECHNICAL TRAINING WILL INCLUDE ADVANCED CRANIOFACIAL HISTOMORPHOMETRY, IN VITRO BONE CELL FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS, LC- MS/MS METABOLOMICS, AND BIOINFORMATIC INTEGRATION OF MULTI-OMICS DATASETS. A CORE COMPONENT OF THE TRAINING PLAN IS THE INTENTIONAL INTEGRATION OF SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL COMPETENCE IN BASIC SCIENCE RESEARCH AND DENTISTRY. TRAINING WILL OCCUR WITHIN THE SUPPORTIVE ENVIRONMENT OF THE MEDICAL UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH CAROLINA, LEVERAGING THE NIDDK-FUNDED DIGESTIVE DISEASES RESEARCH CORE CENTER (DDRCC) AND THE NIDCR-FUNDED TRAINING IN CRANIOFACIAL AND ORAL HEALTH RESEARCH (T-COHR). THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE FUNDAMENTAL INSIGHTS INTO GUT-SKELETAL CROSSTALK AND PREPARE THE CANDIDATE FOR A TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH CAREER AS A DENTIST-SCIENTIST.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IDENTIFYING PATHOGENIC VARIANTS THAT CAUSE MENDELIAN CONDITIONS USING LONG-READ MULTI-OME SEQUENCING - PROJECT SUMMARY: THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS TO IMPROVE THE IDENTIFICATION OF RARE NON-CODING VARIANTS UNDERLYING MENDELIAN CONDITIONS BY DEVELOPING A COMPUTATIONAL FRAMEWORK TO ANALYZE LONG-READ MULTI-OME SEQUENCING DATA. MANY INDIVIDUALS WITH CONGENITAL ANOMALIES AND DEVELOPMENTAL CONDITIONS REMAIN UNDIAGNOSED BECAUSE CURRENT GENOMIC METHODS LACK THE RESOLUTION AND FUNCTIONAL CONTEXT NEEDED TO INTERPRET NON-CODING VARIATION. TO OVERCOME THIS CHALLENGE, THE SPONSORING LAB RECENTLY DEVELOPED LONG-READ MULTI-OME SEQUENCING AND DEMONSTRATED ITS ABILITY TO RESOLVE THE GENETIC AND MOLECULAR BASIS OF RARE HUMAN DISEASES. THIS METHOD COMBINES TWO TECHNOLOGIES PIONEERED BY THE GROUP: SINGLE-MOLECULE CHROMATIN FIBER SEQUENCING (FIBER-SEQ) AND LONG-READ FULL-LENGTH TRANSCRIPT SEQUENCING. IT PRODUCES AN INTEGRATED AND HAPLOTYPE-PHASED GENOME, CPG METHYLOME, CHROMATIN EPIGENOME, AND TRANSCRIPTOME FROM THE SAME SAMPLE. ALTHOUGH LONG-READ MULTI-OME SEQUENCING IS WELL POSITIONED TO BECOME A UNIVERSAL METHOD TO ACCURATELY DETECT AND FUNCTIONALLY EVALUATE PUTATIVE PATHOGENIC GENETIC VARIANTS, A BROAD METHODOLOGICAL GAP LIMITS THE ABILITY OF THE GENOMICS COMMUNITY TO FULLY LEVERAGE THIS PAIRED HAPLOTYPE-PHASED GENOMIC AND FUNCTIONAL INFORMATION. TO BRIDGE THIS GAP, THE APPLICANT AIMS TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A NEW COMPUTATIONAL FRAMEWORK USING LONG-READ MULTI-OME DATA ALREADY GENERATED FROM 50 UNDIAGNOSED INDIVIDUALS WITH CONGENITAL ANOMALIES AND DEVELOPMENTAL CONDITIONS. THE COMPUTATIONAL FRAMEWORK WILL GENERATE TRANSCRIPTOMIC (AIM 1) AND EPIGENOMIC (AIM 2) FUNCTIONAL ANNOTATIONS AND INTEGRATE THESE ANNOTATIONS USING MACHINE LEARNING (AIM 3) TO PRIORITIZE CANDIDATE PATHOGENIC VARIANTS. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH ALIGNS WITH THE MISSION OF THE EUNICE KENNEDY SHRIVER NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF CHILD HEALTH AND HUMAN DEVELOPMENT (NICHD) BY ADVANCING THE DIAGNOSIS AND UNDERSTANDING OF CONGENITAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL CONDITIONS. THE FELLOWSHIP INCLUDES FOCUSED TRAINING IN COMPUTATIONAL GENOMICS, VARIANT INTERPRETATION, AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH WITHIN A MULTIDISCIPLINARY ENVIRONMENT, PREPARING THE APPLICANT FOR A CAREER AS A PHYSICIAN- SCIENTIST IN RARE DISEASE RESEARCH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE STRUCTURE AND ROLE OF THE FEMALE PELVIC GANGLION IN SEXUAL FUNCTION AND REPRODUCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SEXUAL FUNCTION, FERTILITY AND REPRODUCTION ARE COMPLEX, AND THEIR DISORDERS ARE PREVALENT AND POORLY UNDERSTOOD. FEMALE SEXUAL DYSFUNCTION AFFECTS OVER 40% OF WOMEN, INFERTILITY AFFECTS ONE IN SIX REPRODUCTIVE AGE COUPLES, AND MATERNAL MORBIDITY AFFECTS NEARLY 60,000 WOMEN IN THE U.S. EVERY YEAR. AT EVERY STEP OF THE PROCESS, WOMEN SEEKING CHILDBEARING ARE CONFRONTED WITH A GRIM SPECTRUM OF HEALTH RISKS AND COMPLICATIONS, AND FEW SOLUTIONS ARE AVAILABLE FOR THEM. AN APPROACH TO ALLEVIATING THIS REPRODUCTIVE DISEASE BURDEN MAY BE TO INVESTIGATE NOVEL MECHANISMS REGULATING REPRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY, I.E., EXAMINING THE NEUROBIOLOGICAL CIRCUITS MODULATING REPRODUCTIVE PROCESSES. CLOSING THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP MAY INFORM NEW DISEASE ETIOLOGIES AND THERAPEUTIC TARGETS. REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS IN THE PELVIS ARE HIGHLY INNERVATED BY LUMBOSACRAL DORSAL ROOT GANGLIA, VAGAL GANGLIA, AND SYMPATHETIC AND PARASYMPATHETIC GANGLIA—INCLUDING THE PELVIC GANGLION. SIMILAR TO HOW VAGAL GANGLIA ARE INVOLVED IN SENSING INTERNAL CUES AND MODULATING AUTONOMIC FUNCTIONS IN THE BODY, AN ARCHETYPAL BRAIN-BODY CIRCUIT—A POSSIBLE PELVIC CIRCUIT, VIA THE PELVIC GANGLION SHOULD ALSO BE INVESTIGATED. ALTHOUGH IT IS KNOWN THAT THE PELVIC GANGLION INNERVATES FEMALE SEX ORGANS, THE GENETIC IDENTITIES OF PELVIC GANGLION NEURONS, THEIR PATTERNS, MORPHOLOGIES, AND DISTRIBUTION OF INNERVATION, AND THEIR CORRESPONDING FUNCTION AS IT RELATES TO REPRODUCTION REMAIN UNEXPLORED. THE FEMALE PELVIC GANGLION RESIDES IN THE PELVIS, AT THE INTERFACE OF THE UTERUS, CERVIX, BLADDER AND RECTUM. WHILE THIS GANGLION HAS BEEN FOUND TO BE INVOLVED IN URINARY FUNCTION, UNIQUELY, IT IS ALSO SEXUALLY DIMORPHIC. IN MALE RODENTS, THE PELVIC GANGLION MODULATES ERECTILE AND EJACULATORY FUNCTION. HOWEVER, THE CORRESPONDING ROLE THAT THE PELVIC GANGLION PLAYS IN FEMALE SEXUAL AND REPRODUCTIVE FUNCTION IS NOT KNOWN. MY PRELIMINARY WORK REVEALS IMPAIRED SEXUAL FUNCTION AND LABOR PHENOTYPES IN FEMALE MICE WITH SURGICALLY REMOVED PELVIC GANGLIA. IN MY PROPOSED RESEARCH, I WILL DETERMINE, IN AIM 1, THE SPECIFIC GENETIC SUBPOPULATIONS WITHIN THE PELVIC GANGLIA AND THEIR INNERVATION PATTERNS TO FEMALE REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS. THIS WILL BE ACHIEVED THROUGH VIRAL TRACING OF PELVIC GANGLION NEURONS PROJECTING TO FEMALE SEX ORGANS, TISSUE CLEARING OF SEX ORGANS TO VISUALIZE NEURONAL SUBTYPE DISTRIBUTION AND TERMINAL MORPHOLOGIES, AND RNA IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION OF PELVIC GANGLION NEURONS TO DETERMINE THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF GENETIC POPULATIONS WITHIN THE GANGLION, DUPLEXED WITH ORGAN-SPECIFIC IDENTITY. IN AIM 2, I WILL FUNCTIONALLY PERTURB THE GENETIC SUBPOPULATIONS WITHIN THE PELVIC GANGLION VIA GENETICALLY TARGETED CHEMOGENETIC ACTIVATION AND DIPHTHERIA TOXIN ABLATION TO DISCERN THE NUANCED ROLES PELVIC GANGLION NEURON SUBTYPES PLAY IN SEXUAL FUNCTION, FERTILITY AND REPRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REGULATED RNA DECAY IN TOTIPOTENT STATE TRANSITIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY TOTIPOTENCY IS THE EARLIEST AND MOST UNRESTRICTED DEVELOPMENTAL STATE, DEFINED BY THE CAPACITY OF A SINGLE CELL TO GENERATE ALL EMBRYONIC AND EXTRAEMBRYONIC TISSUES. A TRANSIENT STATE, TOTIPOTENCY IS LIMITED TO THE ZYGOTE (1-CELL) AND 2-CELL (2C) STAGES IN MICE AND THE 1-CELL TO 8-CELL STAGES IN HUMANS. FAILURES DURING THE TRANSITION FROM TOTIPOTENCY TO PLURIPOTENCY REPRESENT A MAJOR DEVELOPMENTAL BOTTLENECK, WITH NEARLY HALF OF HUMAN IVF EMBRYOS ARRESTING BEFORE OR DURING THIS SHIFT, UNDERSCORING THE NEED TO UNDERSTAND THE MOLECULAR PATHWAYS THAT GOVERN IT. ALTHOUGH PLURIPOTENT STEM CELL STATES HAVE BEEN WELL CHARACTERIZED, MECHANISMS CONTROLLING ENTRY INTO, MAINTENANCE OF, AND EXIT FROM TOTIPOTENCY REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. A POWERFUL MODEL FOR STUDYING THESE TRANSITIONS ARISES FROM THE DISCOVERY THAT MOUSE EMBRYONIC STEM CELL (MESC) CULTURES CONTAIN RARE, SPONTANEOUSLY CYCLING 2-CELL–LIKE CELLS (2CLCS) THAT TRANSIENTLY ACTIVATE ZSCAN4, MERVL, AND OTHER ZYGOTIC GENOME ACTIVATION (ZGA)-ASSOCIATED GENES WHILE ADOPTING CHROMATIN AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL FEATURES CHARACTERISTIC OF TOTIPOTENT EMBRYOS. PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGESTS THAT POST-TRANSCRIPTIONAL RNA REGULATORY PATHWAYS, PARTICULARLY THOSE INFLUENCING RNA TURNOVER AND STABILITY, PLAY CENTRAL ROLES IN COORDINATING THESE TRANSITIONS. SPECIFICALLY, PERTURBING THESE PATHWAYS IN VITRO INCREASES THE FRACTION OF CELLS ENTERING THE 2CLC STATE, WHILE MANIPULATION IN 1-CELL EMBRYOS PERMITS CLEAVAGE BUT RESULTS IN DEVELOPMENTAL ARREST COUPLED WITH FAILURE TO INITIATE ZGA AND TRANSITION TO PLURIPOTENCY, SUPPORTING A MODEL IN WHICH REGULATED RNA CLEARANCE AND STABILITY SHAPE THE TIMING AND FIDELITY OF EARLY TOTIPOTENT TRANSITIONS. THIS FELLOWSHIP WILL DEFINE HOW RNA STABILITY MECHANISMS GOVERN TOTIPOTENT–PLURIPOTENT TRANSITIONS USING TWO COMPLEMENTARY SYSTEMS. EXPERIMENTS IN AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE HOW SHIFTS IN RNA STABILITY CONTROL 2CLC TRANSITIONS IN MESCS. THESE ANALYSES WILL TAKE ADVANTAGE OF NEW APPROACHES THAT INTEGRATE METABOLIC LABELING AND SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING TO EXAMINE CHANGES IN RNA TRANSCRIPTION AND STABILITY TRANSCRIPTOME WIDE DURING TOTIPOTENCY ENTRY AND EXIT. EXPERIMENTS IN AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE HOW SHIFTS IN RNA STABILITY GOVERN ZGA AND TOTIPOTENCY EXIT IN EMBRYOS. TAKING ADVANTAGE OF HIGHLY SENSITIVE PULL-DOWN APPROACHES, THESE ANALYSES WILL UNCOVER HOW CHANGES IN RNA STABILITY SHAPE TRANSCRIPT CLEARANCE, ZGA ONSET, AND EARLY DEVELOPMENTAL PROGRESSION. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL REVEAL FUNDAMENTAL RNA-STABILITY NETWORKS THAT GOVERN CELL IDENTITY DURING THE FIRST HOURS OF MAMMALIAN DEVELOPMENT AND PROVIDE KEY INSIGHTS RELEVANT TO EMBRYO ARREST, INFERTILITY, CELLULAR REPROGRAMMING, AND REGENERATIVE MEDICINE. TRAINING WILL OCCUR WITHIN AN INTERDISCIPLINARY ENVIRONMENT WITH EXPERTISE IN EMBRYOGENESIS, RNA DECAY, AND RNA/ISOFORM-RESOLVED ANALYSIS, 3D CHROMATIN ARCHITECTURE. THE FELLOWSHIP PROVIDES FOCUSED TRAINING IN RNA-STABILITY, SINGLE-CELL, AND ISOFORM- RESOLVED APPROACHES, SUPPORTED BY THE GENOMICS, IMAGING, AND COMPUTING RESOURCES AT THE SANFORD CONSORTIUM. TOGETHER, THIS SETTING PROVIDES THE COMPREHENSIVE SCIENTIFIC AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT NEEDED FOR AN INDEPENDENT PHYSICIAN-SCIENTIST CAREER.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DISSECTING THE ROLE OF EPITHELIAL-FIBROBLAST CROSSTALK IN ENDOMETRIOSIS-ASSOCIATED INFERTILITY - PROJECT SUMMARY ENDOMETRIOSIS IS A CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY CONDITION AFFECTING 10-15% OF WOMEN, CAUSING SIGNIFICANT PELVIC PAIN AND INFERTILITY. WHILE THE NORMAL ENDOMETRIUM RELIES ON TIGHTLY REGULATED, SPATIAL WNT-MEDIATED CROSSTALK BETWEEN EPITHELIAL AND FIBROBLAST CELLS TO ESTABLISH A RECEPTIVE LINING, THIS PROCESS IS DISRUPTED IN ENDOMETRIOSIS. IN DISEASED TISSUE, FIBROBLASTS ARE THOUGHT TO DRIVE PATHOLOGY BY INDUCING ABERRANT WNT SIGNALING AND PREVENTING THE ENDOMETRIUM FROM PROPERLY TRANSITIONING INTO A RECEPTIVE STATE. THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO LEVERAGE A MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF THIS SPATIAL EPITHELIAL-FIBROBLAST CROSSTALK TO DEVELOP NEW THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR ENDOMETRIOSIS-ASSOCIATED INFERTILITY. MY PRELIMINARY SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMIC DATA REVEAL THAT WNT LIGANDS AND ANTAGONISTS FORM SPECIFIC EXPRESSION GRADIENTS IN FIBROBLASTS, A CELL TYPE DISRUPTED IN ENDOMETRIOSIS. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT THIS DYSREGULATED WNT- MEDIATED CROSSTALK DRIVES ABNORMAL EPITHELIAL DIFFERENTIATION, THEREBY IMPAIRING ENDOMETRIAL RECEPTIVITY. AIM 1 WILL CHARACTERIZE THE EPITHELIAL RESPONSE TO ENDOMETRIOSIS-DERIVED FIBROBLASTS USING PATIENT-DERIVED 3D CO-CULTURES AND SINGLE-CELL RNA SEQUENCING. I WILL SUBSEQUENTLY USE CRISPR-CAS9 GENE EDITING TO SYSTEMATICALLY DEMONSTRATE THE CONTRIBUTION OF SPECIFIC WNT GENES TO THE INFERTILITY PHENOTYPE. AIM 2 WILL SPATIALLY VALIDATE THESE INTERACTIONS IN HUMAN PRE-RECEPTIVE AND RECEPTIVE ENDOMETRIAL BIOPSIES USING HIGH-RESOLUTION SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS TO PROFILE CELL NEIGHBORHOODS AND SIGNALING NICHES. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS WILL ELUCIDATE THE PATHOLOGICAL NICHES UNIQUE TO ENDOMETRIOSIS-ASSOCIATED INFERTILITY AND IDENTIFY POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS. HOWEVER, THIS F30 FELLOWSHIP WILL ULTIMATELY PROVIDE ME WITH A UNIQUE RESEARCH FRAMEWORK TO ELUCIDATE MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS ACROSS MANY GYNECOLOGICAL CONDITIONS THROUGH TRANSLATABLE SKILLS IN ADVANCED IN VITRO ORGAN MODELING AND SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOMICS/SPATIAL OMICS. THEREFORE, THIS TRAINING IS IMPERATIVE FOR MY DEVELOPMENT AS A FUTURE INDEPENDENT PHYSICIAN-SCIENTIST WHO AIMS TO ADDRESS THE BENCH TO BEDSIDE GAPS IN WOMEN'S HEALTH.

description: COMPLEMENT-MEDIATED SYNAPTIC PRUNING AND DYSFUNCTION IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS FOLLOWING NEONATAL HYPOXIC-ISCHEMIC INJURY - PROJECT SUMMARY  NEONATAL HYPOXIC-ISCHEMIC ENCEPHALOPATHY (HIE) IS CAUSED BY LOSS OF BLOOD FLOW AND OXYGEN TO THE BRAIN AFTER BIRTH AND IS A LEADING CAUSE OF INFANT DEATH AND LIFELONG DISABILITY. UNFORTUNATELY, CURRENT MODELS LACK THE ABILITY TO REPLICATE NEONATAL GLOBAL CEREBRAL ISCHEMIA (NGCI) AND REPERFUSION INJURY WHICH ARE BOTH KEY FEATURES OF THE CONDITION. DURING EARLY DEVELOPMENT, BRAIN CIRCUITS ARE REFINED THROUGH COMPLEMENT–MICROGLIA INTERACTIONS, WHICH GUIDE PRUNING OF DENDRITIC SPINES. NEONATAL HYPOXIC ISCHEMIA IS KNOWN TO CAUSE STRUCTURAL CHANGES TO SPINES AND IS ASSOCIATED WITH HIPPOCAMPUS-DEPENDENT BEHAVIORAL DEFICITS, BUT THE UNDERLYING FUNCTIONAL SYNAPTIC CHANGES HAVE NOT BEEN INVESTIGATED. THIS PROPOSAL USES A NOVEL MODEL OF NEONATAL RAT CARDIAC ARREST AND CARDIOPULMONARY RESUSCITATION (CA/CPR) TO INDUCE NGCI. UNLIKE TRADITIONAL MODELS, NEONATAL CA/CPR PRODUCES FUNCTIONAL DEFICITS IN HIPPOCAMPAL- DEPENDENT MEMORY WITHOUT CELL DEATH IN THE CA1 REGION. INSTEAD, WE OBSERVE DENDRITIC SPINE LOSS AND MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION, ALONG WITH INCREASED COMPLEMENT PROTEIN EXPRESSION. THIS SUGGESTS THAT INFLAMMATION, RATHER THAN CELL DEATH, MAY DRIVE BEHAVIORAL OUTCOMES. FURTHERMORE, WE OBSERVE INCREASED PHOSPHATIDYLSERINE EXPOSURE, A WELL-KNOWN “EAT ME” SIGNAL THAT C1Q TAGS DURING DEVELOPMENTAL SYNAPTIC PRUNING. THESE DATA PROVIDE THE FRAMEWORK FOR A POSSIBLE MECHANISTIC LINK BETWEEN NEUROINFLAMMATION DUE TO INJURY AND DENDRITIC SPINE LOSS.  I HYPOTHESIZE THAT NGCI OVERACTIVATES NORMAL COMPLEMENT- AND MICROGLIA-MEDIATED PRUNING, LEADING TO REDUCED EXCITATORY SYNAPTIC FUNCTION IN THE DEVELOPING HIPPOCAMPUS. AIM 1 OF THIS PROPOSAL WILL USE WHOLE CELL PATCH CLAMP ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY TO EXAMINE HOW NGCI IMPACTS EXCITATORY SYNAPTIC FUNCTION AND SPINE MORPHOLOGY AS WELL AS A C1Q INHIBITOR TO MODULATE COMPLEMENT-MEDIATED SYNAPTIC PRUNING THAT MAY IMPACT THIS DYSFUNCTION. I PREDICT THAT DEFICITS IN CA1 SYNAPTIC FUNCTION WILL ALIGN WITH KNOWN IMPAIRMENTS IN LEARNING AND MEMORY AND THAT COMPLEMENT INHIBITION WILL RESTORE SYNAPTIC FUNCTIONAL INTEGRITY. AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE COMPLEMENT DYNAMICS AFTER NGCI AS WELL AS MICROGLIA ACTIVATION AND ROLE IN CA1 SYNAPTIC ENGULFMENT. I EXPECT COMPLEMENT TO BE UPREGULATED WITH INCREASED MICROGLIA INTERACTIONS THAT CORRESPOND TO INCREASES IN MICROGLIAL ENGULFMENT OF COMPLEMENT-TAGGED EXCITATORY SYNAPSES.  OUR NOVEL MODEL OF NGCI ENHANCES EXISTING MODELS WHILE OFFERING GREATER CLINICAL RELEVANCE FOR ADVANCING THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES TO HIE. UPON COMPLETION, THIS PROPOSAL WILL CLARIFY MECHANISMS OF COMPLEMENT-MEDIATED PRUNING AND EXCITATORY SYNAPTIC DYSFUNCTION IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS, PROVIDING KEY INSIGHTS INTO THEIR ROLE IN LONG-TERM COGNITIVE AND CIRCUIT IMPAIRMENTS AFTER HIE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NEURAL CORRELATES OF MEMORY-BASED GENERALIZATION IN HUMANS - PROJECT SUMMARY THE ABILITY TO GENERALIZE FROM PRIOR EXPERIENCE IS A CORNERSTONE OF HUMAN COGNITION. IN DAILY LIFE, PEOPLE MAKE ACCURATE PREDICTIONS IN UNFAMILIAR SITUATIONS WITHOUT NEEDING TO ENCOUNTER EVERY POSSIBLE SCENARIO. FOR EXAMPLE, WHEN VISITING A NEW SUPERMARKET, ONE CAN OFTEN ANTICIPATE WHERE ITEMS ARE LOCATED BY GENERALIZING FROM THE LAYOUT OF PREVIOUSLY VISITED STORES. HOWEVER, IMPAIRMENTS IN GENERALIZATION CAN SEVERELY DISRUPT COGNITIVE AND FUNCTIONAL ABILITIES. IN NEUROPSYCHIATRIC CONDITIONS SUCH AS PTSD, SCHIZOPHRENIA, AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, INDIVIDUALS MAY OVERGENERALIZE THREATS OR STRUGGLE TO TRANSFER LEARNED KNOWLEDGE IN NEW SITUATIONS, LEADING TO DEFICITS IN INFERENCE, REASONING, AND DECISION-MAKING. DESPITE THE IMPORTANCE OF THIS COGNITIVE PROCESS, THE NEURAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING GENERALIZATION REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THEORETICAL WORK SUGGESTS THAT GENERALIZATION RELIES ON INTERNAL MODELS THAT GUIDE PREDICTIONS IN NOVEL CONTEXTS. BOTH THEORETICAL MODELS AND SUPPORTING ANIMAL RESEARCH POINT TO THE HIPPOCAMPUS AND PREFRONTAL CORTEX AS KEY REGIONS IN THIS COGNITIVE PROCESS. BUILDING ON THIS FOUNDATION, I HYPOTHESIZE THAT GENERALIZATION IS SUPPORTED BY COORDINATED HIPPOCAMPAL-PREFRONTAL DYNAMICS, IN WHICH LEARNED STRUCTURE (I.E., SCHEMAS) REPRESENTED IN THE PREFRONTAL CORTEX GUIDE HIPPOCAMPAL PREDICTIONS TO MINIMIZE PREDICTION ERROR IN NOVEL CONTEXTS. TO TEST THIS, THE PROJECT WILL LEVERAGE RARE INTRACRANIAL RECORDINGS OF SINGLE NEURON ACTIVITY AND LOCAL FIELD POTENTIALS FROM PATIENTS WHO ARE IMPLANTED WITH DEPTH ELECTRODES FOR SEIZURE MONITORING WHILE THEY ENGAGE IN A MEMORY-BASED PREDICTION TASK. PARTICIPANTS WILL VIEW NATURALISTIC VIDEOS DEPICTING EVERYDAY ACTIVITIES AND WILL PREDICT WHAT HAPPENS NEXT AT KEY TRANSITION POINTS BETWEEN EVENTS (I.E., EVENT BOUNDARIES). THE TASK INCLUDES CONDITIONS THAT VARY IN VISUAL SIMILARITY AND EVENT STRUCTURE, ALLOWING RESEARCHERS TO PROBE HOW PEOPLE GENERALIZE LEARNED TEMPORAL PATTERNS TO NEW CONTEXTS. AIM 1 WILL TEST WHETHER CHANGES IN SPIKE RATE AND SPIKE PHASE FOR NEURONS RESPONSIVE TO EVENT BOUNDARIES PREDICT SUCCESSFUL GENERALIZATIONS. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS WHETHER THE REINSTATEMENT OF NEURAL PATTERNS ASSOCIATED WITH LEARNED EVENT SEQUENCES AND PREFRONTAL-HIPPOCAMPAL THETA-BAND SYNCHRONY SUPPORT GENERALIZATION. TOGETHER, THESE AIMS WILL PROBE THE MECHANISMS THAT SUPPORT GENERALIZATION IN NOVEL CONTEXTS. THE CANDIDATE WILL RECEIVE COMPREHENSIVE TRAINING IN SYSTEMS NEUROSCIENCE, NEURAL DATA ANALYSIS, SCIENTIFIC COMMUNICATION, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT UNDER THE MENTORSHIP OF DRS. JIE ZHENG (PRIMARY SPONSOR), JACK LIN (CO-SPONSOR), UELI RUTISHAUSER, AND JULIA SHARMA. THIS TRAINING INCLUDES STRUCTURED MENTORSHIP, HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE WITH HUMAN NEURAL RECORDINGS, NATIONAL WORKSHOPS AND CONFERENCES, AND ENGAGEMENT IN PATIENT CARE. IN ADDITION, UC DAVIS OFFERS AN EXCEPTIONAL RESEARCH AND TRAINING ENVIRONMENT TO SUPPORT THE CANDIDATE’S DEVELOPMENT AS A SURGEON-SCIENTIST DEDICATED TO ADVANCING CARE FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH COGNITIVE DISORDERS.

description: EVALUATING THE CONTRIBUTION OF CARE PATHWAYS AND CLINICAL FEATURES TO HOME HEALTH QUALITY OUTCOMES FOR PEOPLE WITH DEMENTIA - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE MEDICALLY NECESSARY, HOME-BASED SKILLED HEALTHCARE SERVICES OFFERED UNDER MEDICARE’S HOME HEALTH (HH) BENEFIT PROVIDE ESSENTIAL SUPPORT TO PEOPLE WITH DEMENTIA. HOWEVER, RECENT CHANGES IN MEDICARE REIMBURSEMENT, SPECIFICALLY THE PATIENT-DRIVEN GROUPINGS MODEL (PDGM) IN 2020, HAVE RAISED CONCERNS REGARDING REDUCED ACCESS AND QUALITY OF HH CARE FOR PEOPLE WITH DEMENTIA. PREVIOUS RESEARCH ON THESE IMPACTS PRIMARILY RELIES ON GENERALIZED BILLING DATA, WHICH, UNLIKE CLINICAL ASSESSMENT DATA, LACK THE NECESSARY PATIENT DETAILS—SUCH AS FUNCTIONAL STATUS, COGNITIVE DEFICITS, OR THE PRESENCE OF NEUROPSYCHIATRIC SYMPTOMS LIKE APATHY, DEPRESSION, AND AGGRESSION—TO ACCOUNT FOR THE KNOWN HETEROGENEITY IN THIS POPULATION. INSTEAD, THESE STUDIES GROUP PEOPLE WITH DEMENTIA INTO A SINGLE HOMOGENEOUS CATEGORY. HOWEVER, THESE CLINICAL FEATURES LIKELY DRIVE VARIATION IN CARE NEEDS AND UTILIZATION. THE FACT THAT THESE FEATURES DO NOT APPEAR IN MOST HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH (HSR) ON PEOPLE WITH DEMENTIA UNDERSCORES A CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAP. UNTIL MORE GRANULAR HSR EVIDENCE IS GENERATED, VARIATIONS IN CLINICAL PRESENTATION THAT MAY BE CLOSELY LINKED TO HH CARE UTILIZATION PATHWAYS (CARE PATHWAYS) AND QUALITY OUTCOMES WILL REMAIN UNACCOUNTED FOR; HH POLICY AND PRACTICE IMPROVEMENTS COULD SUFFER AS A RESULT. THIS STUDY ADDRESSES THAT GAP BY USING LATENT CLASS ANALYSIS (LCA) TO IDENTIFY CARE PATHWAYS OF PEOPLE WITH DEMENTIA WHO USED HH IN 2021—2022 AND THEN EVALUATING HOW CARE PATHWAYS RELATE TO QUALITY OUTCOME MEASURES (E.G., POTENTIALLY PREVENTABLE HOSPITALIZATIONS, SUCCESSFUL DISCHARGE TO THE COMMUNITY) (AIM 1) AND CLINICAL FEATURES (DEMENTIA SEVERITY, NEUROPSYCHIATRIC SYMPTOM BURDEN) (AIM 2) USING MULTIVARIABLE AND MULTINOMIAL LOGISTIC REGRESSION RESPECTIVELY. LCA WILL IDENTIFY CARE PATHWAYS BASED ON HH UTILIZATION METRICS, INCLUDING TYPES OF SERVICES RECEIVED (E.G., NURSING, PHYSICAL THERAPY, OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY, SPEECH THERAPY, MEDICAL SOCIAL WORK, AND HOME HEALTH AIDE), VISIT VOLUMES, AND CARE DURATION. FINDINGS WILL ENHANCE KNOWLEDGE OF HOW HH POLICY AND PRACTICE INTERACT TO IMPACT HH QUALITY OUTCOMES, PROVIDING EVIDENCE TO GUIDE POLICY ADJUSTMENTS AND CARE PRACTICES THAT CAN IMPROVE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR THIS GROWING POPULATION AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. THESE RESEARCH AIMS WILL ALSO SUPPORT MY FELLOWSHIP TRAINING OBJECTIVES. description: INVESTIGATING HOW CHRONIC INFLAMMATION INDUCES INNATE IMMUNE MEMORY IN HUMAN MICROGLIA - PROJECT SUMMARY CHRONIC LOW-GRADE INFLAMMATION IS A HALLMARK OF NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES, INCLUDING ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. MICROGLIA, THE LONG-LIVED RESIDENT IMMUNE CELLS OF THE BRAIN, PLAY A CENTRAL ROLE IN MAINTAINING BRAIN HOMEOSTASIS BUT ARE PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TO REPROGRAMMING BY PERIPHERAL IMMUNE CHALLENGES. REPEATED INFLAMMATORY STIMULI MAY INDUCE MALADAPTIVE STATES IN MICROGLIA THAT PERSIST BEYOND THE RESOLUTION OF ACUTE INFLAMMATION AND CONTRIBUTE TO NEURODEGENERATION. IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, DYSFUNCTIONAL MICROGLIA ARE INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED AS KEY DRIVERS OF DISEASE PROGRESSION. HOWEVER, THE MOLECULAR AND EPIGENETIC MECHANISMS THAT SUSTAIN THESE MALADAPTIVE MICROGLIAL STATES REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD, ESPECIALLY IN HUMANS, BECAUSE MOST EXISTING STUDIES RELY ON RODENT MODELS THAT FAIL TO CAPTURE THE COMPLEXITY OF HUMAN IMMUNE RESPONSES AND GENETIC RISK. TO ADDRESS THIS CRITICAL GAP, WE USE A NOVEL ORGANOID-BASED XENOTRANSPLANTATION PLATFORM THAT ENABLES IN VIVO INVESTIGATION OF HUMAN MICROGLIA WITHIN A VASCULARIZED, BRAIN-LIKE ENVIRONMENT. THE OVERARCHING GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND MANIPULATE MOLECULAR CIRCUITS THAT DRIVE MALADAPTIVE MICROGLIAL STATES INDUCED BY CHRONIC INFLAMMATION. PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT SYSTEMIC LPS ADMINISTRATION INDUCES LONG-LASTING TRANSCRIPTIONAL CHANGES IN HUMAN MICROGLIA, INCLUDING PERSISTENT ACTIVATION OF EGR1. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CHRONIC INFLAMMATION DRIVES LONG-LASTING MICROGLIAL REPROGRAMMING, COMPROMISING THEIR ABILITY TO SUPPORT BRAIN HOMEOSTASIS. WE FURTHER PROPOSE THAT THIS IS ENCODED THROUGH AN EPIGENETIC REPROGRAMMING WHICH IS PARTIALLY ORCHESTRATED BY EGR1. WE PROPOSE THAT TARGETED INTERVENTIONS OF EGR1 CAN RESTORE MICROGLIAL HOMEOSTATIC GENE EXPRESSION SIGNATURES AND SERVE AS A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC. WE WILL PURSUE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) DISSECT MOLECULAR AND EPIGENETIC CANDIDATES RESPONSIBLE FOR CHRONIC IMMUNE REPROGRAMMING AND (2) EVALUATE THE ROLE OF EGR1 IN ORCHESTRATING A CHRONIC IMMUNE REPROGRAMMING. THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO HOW IMMUNE REPROGRAMMING SHAPES HUMAN MICROGLIA STATES AND WILL INFORM THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES FOR AD AND OTHER NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES.

description: TREATMENT PATHWAYS AND ACCESS TO NOVEL AMYLOID-TARGETING ALZHEIMER'S THERAPIES: EXAMINING MULTI-LEVEL INFLUENCES - PROJECT SUMMARY ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE AFFECTS NEARLY 7 MILLION AMERICANS, A NUMBER PROJECTED TO DOUBLE BY 2060, DRIVING ANNUAL COSTS EXCEEDING $755 BILLION. AFTER TWO DECADES WITHOUT NEW TREATMENT OPTIONS, MEDICARE BEGAN COVERING AMYLOID-TARGETING THERAPIES LEQEMBI AND KISUNLA IN 2023-2024, REPRESENTING THE FIRST DISEASE-MODIFYING TREATMENTS THAT GO BEYOND SYMPTOM MANAGEMENT ALONE. THESE THERAPIES SHOW MODEST CLINICAL BENEFITS (27- 29% REDUCTION IN COGNITIVE DECLINE OVER 18 MONTHS), HAVE SIGNIFICANT SIDE EFFECTS, AND COST OVER $25,000 ANNUALLY. WITH RECENT MEDICARE COVERAGE, UPTAKE IS RAPIDLY INCREASING WITH OVER 10,000 PATIENTS ON TREATMENT. IT REMAINS UNCLEAR WHICH PATIENTS ARE ACCESSING THESE THERAPIES AND WHETHER TRADITIONAL BARRIERS TO HEALTHCARE ACCESS EXTEND TO THIS NEW TREATMENT PATHWAY. THIS RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS OF ACCESS PATTERNS AND CLINICAL ROLLOUT PATTERNS FOR THESE BREAKTHROUGH ALZHEIMER'S THERAPIES. THE STUDY USES 100% MEDICARE FEE-FOR-SERVICE CLAIMS DATA LINKED TO PATIENT DEMOGRAPHIC AND GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION TO EXAMINE THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: (AIM 1) EVALUATE WHO SEES A NEUROLOGIST WITHIN ONE YEAR OF AN ALZHEIMER'S OR MILD COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT DIAGNOSIS, (AIM 2) EVALUATE WHICH PATIENTS THEN UNDERGO BIOMARKER TESTING (REQUIRED FOR TREATMENT ELIGIBILITY) AND WHICH TESTED PATIENTS INITIATE TREATMENT, AND (AIM 3) EVALUATE WHICH PATIENTS DISCONTINUE TREATMENT USING CLAIMS DATA AND WHAT FACTORS CLINICIANS AND PATIENTS IDENTIFY AS IMPORTANT IN MAKING SUCH DECISIONS USING SEMI-STRUCTURED INTERVIEWS WITH PATIENTS AND NEUROLOGISTS TO CONTEXTUALIZE QUANTITATIVE FINDINGS. MR. JANUSZEWICZ WILL CONDUCT THIS RESEARCH UNDER THE MENTORSHIP OF DR. KAREN SCHIFFERDECKER (MIXED- METHODS EXPERTISE), CO-SPONSOR DR. EMMA DEAN (MEDICARE CLAIMS ANALYSIS), AND CONSULTANTS DRS. ELLIOTT FISHER (HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION), NICOLE FOWLER (ADRD CARE PATHWAYS), AND GUANBO WANG (CAUSAL INFERENCE METHODS). THE TRAINING PLAN INCLUDES FOUR SHORT-TERM GOALS: (1) DEVELOPING PROFICIENCY IN MEDICARE CLAIMS DATA ANALYSIS, (2) DEVELOPING QUALITATIVE INTERVIEW AND MIXED-METHODS INTEGRATION SKILLS, (3) TRAINING IN ADVANCED CAUSAL INFERENCE METHODS FOR OBSERVATIONAL HEALTHCARE DATA, AND (4) PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT IN SCIENTIFIC DISSEMINATION AND POLICY COMMUNICATION. TRAINING WILL BE CONDUCTED IN THE DARTMOUTH INSTITUTE'S NATIONALLY RECOGNIZED HEALTH POLICY RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT, WHICH PROVIDES DEDICATED COURSEWORK IN RESEARCH METHODS, REGULAR SEMINARS FEATURING LEADING RESEARCHERS, EXTENSIVE COLLABORATION OPPORTUNITIES WITH CLINICAL AND POLICY EXPERTS, AND ACCESS TO MEDICARE DATA INFRASTRUCTURE. THIS RESEARCH ADDRESSES NIA'S MISSION TO EXTEND HEALTHY YEARS OF LIFE FOR OLDER ADULTS BY GENERATING CRITICAL EVIDENCE ABOUT ACCESS TO NOVEL ALZHEIMER’S TREATMENTS, THEREBY INFORMING MEDICARE POLICY DECISIONS FOR CURRENT AND FUTURE HIGH-COST, LIMITED-BENEFIT THERAPIES. THIS WORK SUPPORTS MR. JANUSZEWICZ'S LONG-TERM GOAL OF BECOMING AN INDEPENDENT NIH-FUNDED INVESTIGATOR EXAMINING PHARMACEUTICAL ACCESS, COST, AND HEALTH IMPLICATIONS FOR AGING POPULATIONS.

description: GASDERMIN-D ASSEMBLY AT MITOCHONDRIA FACILITATES THE PROPAGATION OF STERILE NEUROINFLAMMATORY RESPONSES IN ALPHA-SYNUCLEINOPATHY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ ABSTRACT  PROGRESSIVE NEURONAL ACCUMULATION OF AGGREGATED ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN (ΑSYN) IS THE MAJOR PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL FEATURE OF NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES KNOWN AS ALPHA-SYNUCLEINOPATHIES. EXAMPLES OF THESE INCLUDE PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD) AND DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES (DLB). THESE DISORDERS ARE HALLMARKED BY MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION AND CHRONIC BRAIN INFLAMMATION. HOWEVER, THE SIGNALING MECHANISMS THAT FACILITATE THE CROSSTALK OF THESE PROCESSES REMAIN UNDER-CHARACTERIZED. PREVIOUS WORK HAS SHOWN THAT STERILE NEUROINFLAMMATION-MEDIATED MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION CAN ACTIVATE INNATE-IMMUNE SIGNALING MECHANISMS SUCH AS THE NOD-LIKE RECEPTOR PROTEIN 3 (NLRP3) INFLAMMASOME AND THE STIMULATOR OF INTERFERON GENES (STING) COMPLEX WITHIN MICROGLIA, THE RESIDENT IMMUNE CELLS IN THE BRAIN. THIS LEADS TO NEUROINFLAMMATION-MEDIATED NEUROTOXIC RESPONSES IN ΑSYN MODELS. IT REMAINS UNKNOWN HOW NLRP3/STING RESPONSES DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY CONTRIBUTE TO THE SPREAD OF STERILE NEUROINFLAMMATION AND NEURODEGENERATION.  GASDERMIN-D (GSDMD) IS A PROTEIN THAT IS ACTIVATED/CLEAVED DOWNSTREAM OF NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME ASSEMBLY AND IS BEST ASSOCIATED WITH AN INFLAMMATORY CELL DEATH MECHANISM KNOWN AS PYROPTOSIS, WHERE IT FORMS PORES IN THE CELL MEMBRANE. MY PRELIMINARY DATA USING CULTURED PRIMARY MICROGLIA, WITHIN THE ΑSYN PRE-FORMED FIBRIL (PFF) MODEL, INDICATES THAT CLEAVED GSDMD (CL-GSDMD) ACCUMULATES AT THE MITOCHONDRIA AND AMPLIFIES MITOCHONDRIAL DAMAGE WITHIN MICROGLIA. THEREFORE, THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF THIS PROPOSAL IS THAT FOLLOWING MICROGLIAL NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME ASSEMBLY, GSDMD IS CLEAVED AND ACCUMULATES WITHIN MITOCHONDRIA, SERVING TO AMPLIFY MITOCHONDRIAL DAMAGE AND NEUROINFLAMMATORY RESPONSES. TO ACCOMPLISH THIS, I WILL BE TRAINED IN ASYN-PFF MODELING, MOUSE BEHAVIORAL ASSAYS, AS WELL AS MICROGLIAL INFLAMMASOME BIOLOGY IN THE LABORATORY OF DR. NIKHIL PANICKER AT THE CLEVELAND CLINIC RESEARCH INSTITUTE.  RECENT WORK INDICATES THAT METABOLICALLY ACTIVE MITOCHONDRIA CAN BE EXPORTED FROM ONE CELL TO ANOTHER, IN A PROCESS CALLED HORIZONTAL MITOCHONDRIA TRANSFER. THIS PROCESS HAS BEEN IMPLICATED IN SEVERAL SYSTEMS, WHERE IT HAS BEEN SHOWN TO INCREASE SURVIVAL AND DAMPEN INFLAMMATION IN RECIPIENT CELLS. CURRENT RESEARCH HAS YET TO ADDRESS WHAT HAPPENS WHEN DYSFUNCTIONAL MITOCHONDRIA ARE TRANSFERRED TO A RECIPIENT CELL. MY PRELIMINARY DATA INDICATE THAT CL-GSDMD-LADEN MITOCHONDRIA CAN BE HORIZONTALLY TRANSFERRED FROM DONOR TO RECIPIENT CELLS, MEDIATING THE PROPAGATION OF NEUROINFLAMMATORY SIGNALING. THEREFORE, I SEEK TO ELUCIDATE HOW NEUROINFLAMMATORY RESPONSES CAN SPREAD WITHIN ALPHA-SYNUCLEINOPATHIES VIA GSDMD-LADEN MITOCHONDRIA. I WILL BE MENTORED BY DR. JUSTIN LATHIA TO INVESTIGATE THE METHODS OF HORIZONTAL MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSFER AND VARIOUS MITOCHONDRIAL METABOLIC ASSAYS. HORIZONTAL MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSFER HAS THUS FAR BEEN EXPLORED AS A NEUROPROTECTIVE MECHANISM IN THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. ILLUSTRATING THAT THIS PROCESS CAN BE “CORRUPTED” BY GSDMD TO SERVE AS A MECHANISM TO SPREAD NEUROINFLAMMATION REPRESENTS A PARADIGM SHIFT IN THE FIELD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN 24-HOUR ACTIVITY CYCLE PATTERNS AND COGNITION AND WHITE MATTER INTEGRITY IN AN ADULT LIFESPAN SAMPLE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT AGING IS ASSOCIATED WITH COGNITIVE DECLINE, ELEVATED RISK OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD), AND REDUCTIONS IN THE INTEGRITY OF WHITE MATTER TRACTS IN THE BRAIN CRITICAL FOR NEURAL COMMUNICATION. EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS FOR AGE- AND AD-RELATED CHANGES REMAIN LIMITED, HIGHLIGHTING THE NEED TO UNDERSTAND THE ROLE OF MODIFIABLE LIFESTYLE BEHAVIORS FOR PRESERVING COGNITION AND BRAIN HEALTH. GREATER PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, REDUCED SEDENTARY BEHAVIOR, AND SUFFICIENT SLEEP ARE EACH ASSOCIATED WITH BENEFITS TO COGNITIVE FUNCTION AND WHITE MATTER MICROSTRUCTURE. NOTABLY, PRIOR STUDIES OFTEN EXAMINE THESE BEHAVIORS INDEPENDENTLY DESPITE THEIR DEPENDENCE ON ONE ANOTHER AS COMPONENTS OF A 24-HOUR DAY. EMERGING EVIDENCE INDICATES THAT THE BALANCE OF THESE BEHAVIORS, KNOWN AS THE 24-HOUR ACTIVITY CYCLE (24HAC), IS RELATED TO EPISODIC MEMORY AND EXECUTIVE FUNCTION PERFORMANCE. HOWEVER, PREVIOUS RESEARCH IS LARGELY CROSS-SECTIONAL, LIMITED TO OLDER ADULTS, AND RARELY EXTENDED TO MARKERS OF BRAIN HEALTH SUCH AS WHITE MATTER MICROSTRUCTURE. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL ADDRESS THESE GAPS BY EXAMINING CROSS-SECTIONAL AND LONGITUDINAL ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN 24HAC PATTERNS, COGNITION, AND WHITE MATTER MICROSTRUCTURE ACROSS THE ADULT LIFESPAN, AND BY IDENTIFYING KEY MODERATORS OF THESE RELATIONSHIPS. BASELINE DATA ARE AVAILABLE FROM 303 ADULTS (18-86 YEARS; MEAN AGE = 53 YEARS), WITH 3-YEAR FOLLOW-UP DATA COLLECTION UNDERWAY (CURRENT N = 31). PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, SEDENTARY BEHAVIOR, AND SLEEP WILL BE OBJECTIVELY MEASURED USING WRIST-WORN ACCELEROMETERS AND ANALYZED USING COMPOSITIONAL DATA ANALYSIS TO ACCOUNT FOR THE INTERDEPENDENCE OF 24HAC BEHAVIORS. EPISODIC MEMORY AND EXECUTIVE FUNCTION WILL BE ASSESSED WITH STANDARDIZED NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL ASSESSMENTS. WHITE MATTER MICROSTRUCTURE WILL BE QUANTIFIED AS FRACTIONAL ANISOTROPY DERIVED FROM DIFFUSION TENSOR IMAGING OBTAINED FROM MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING. AIM 1 WILL EXAMINE THE A) CROSS-SECTIONAL AND B) LONGITUDINAL ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN 24HAC PATTERNS AND EPISODIC MEMORY AND EXECUTIVE FUNCTION AND EVALUATE WHETHER RELATIONSHIPS VARY BY AGE. AIM 2 WILL EXAMINE THE A) CROSS-SECTIONAL AND B) LONGITUDINAL ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN 24HAC PATTERNS AND FRACTIONAL ANISOTROPY AND EVALUATE WHETHER THE RELATIONSHIP VARIES BY AGE. EXPLORATORY AIM 3 WILL EXAMINE WHETHER ASSOCIATIONS OF THE 24HAC, COGNITION, AND WHITE MATTER INTEGRITY DIFFER BY GENETIC RISK FOR AD, INCLUDING APOE GENOTYPE AND POLYGENIC RISK SCORE. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW MODIFIABLE LIFESTYLE BEHAVIORS JOINTLY RELATE TO COGNITIVE AND BRAIN HEALTH AND CLARIFY THE OPTIMAL BALANCE OF 24HAC BEHAVIORS THAT EXERT THE MOST COGNITIVE AND NEUROPROTECTIVE EFFECTS TO COMBAT AGE-RELATED DECLINE. ADDITIONALLY, THIS WORK WILL HELP IDENTIFY INDIVIDUALS AT HEIGHTENED RISK FOR COGNITIVE AND BRAIN DECLINE WHO MAY RECEIVE THE GREATEST BENEFIT FROM BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS. FINDINGS WILL INFORM COMPREHENSIVE STRATEGIES TO PROMOTE HEALTHY AGING AND PROLONG THE HEALTHSPAN. THE PROPOSAL IS WELL ALIGNED WITH THE MISSION OF THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE ON AGING (NIA) TO EXTEND THE NUMBER OF INDEPENDENT, HEALTHY, ACTIVE YEARS OF LATER LIFE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SOCIAL ISOLATION CONTRIBUTES TO AD PATHOGENESIS AND RISK BY REDUCING CORTICAL BLOOD FLOW - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS A DEBILITATING NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE CHARACTERIZED BY RAPID LOSS OF COGNITIVE FUNCTION DUE TO ABERRANT ACCUMULATION OF THE NEUROTOXIC PROTEINS AMYLOID-BETA (AΒ) AND HYPERPHOSPHORYLATED TAU TANGLES. THERE IS NO CURE FOR AD, AND TREATMENTS ARE LIMITED. AS THIS DISEASE IS PRIMARILY DIAGNOSED LATER IN LIFE, RESEARCH HAS FOCUSED ON EARLY INTERVENTION, PREVENTION, AND DIAGNOSTIC PROCEDURES. INDEED, UP TO 45% OF AD CASES COULD BE PREVENTED THROUGH MODIFIABLE LIFESTYLE FACTORS. ONE SUCH FACTOR, SOCIAL ISOLATION (SI), IS RECOGNIZED BY THE NIH AS A MAJOR HEALTH HAZARD, BUT THE MECHANISMS WHEREBY SI CONTRIBUTES TO AD ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD. HERE, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED THAT REDUCED CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW (CBF), ONE OF THE EARLIEST BIOMARKERS FOR AD, IS A SHARED CHARACTERISTIC BETWEEN SI AND AD. AQUAPORIN-4 (AQP4), A WATER CHANNEL PRIMARILY EXPRESSED BY ASTROCYTES AT THEIR VASCULAR ASSOCIATED ENDFEET, HAS FOUND GROWING ATTENTION IN AD RESEARCH. INDEED, SEVERAL STUDIES HAVE IDENTIFIED MISLOCALIZATION OF AQP4 AWAY FROM ASTROCYTE ENDFEET, AND DELETION OF AQP4 RESULTS IN ABERRANT AΒ ACCUMULATION. NOTABLY, AQP4 IS MOST HIGHLY EXPRESSED AT THE PIAL SURFACE, DIRECTLY BELOW THE MAJOR ARTERIES THAT ACCOUNT FOR THE MAJORITY OF CORTICAL INFLOW. IN THE CONTEXT OF SI, WE FOUND THAT 4 MONTHS OF SI IN WILDTYPE (WT) MALE MICE RESULTED IN A MARKED REDUCTION IN PIAL AQP4 EXPRESSION. NOTABLY, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED IN OUR ANIMAL MODEL THAT THIS REGION, THE ASTROCYTE/MENINGEAL VASCULAR INTERFACE, ALSO REPRESENTS THE DENSEST ACCUMULATION OF AΒ VERSUS ANYWHERE ELSE IN THE BRAIN, PRIMARILY IN THE FORM OF VASCULAR PLAQUES OR CEREBRAL AMYLOID ANGIOPATHY (CAA). THE LEVEL OF THIS CAA CORRELATES WITH REDUCTIONS IN CBF IN OUR MODEL OF AD. ALTOGETHER, OUR FINDINGS SUGGEST AT THE SITE OF THE ASTROCYTE/MENINGEAL VASCULAR INTERFACE, 1) AQP4 FACILITATES CSF FLOW INTO THE PARENCHYMA, 2) CREATES A DIRECTIONAL FLOW RESULTING IN WASTE ACCUMULATION, I.E. AΒ, TOWARDS THE PIAL SURFACE, 3) LEADS TO HEIGHTENED AΒ ACCUMULATION AROUND BLOOD VESSELS, CHOKING CORTICAL BLOOD INFLOW. HOW SI CONTRIBUTES TO THIS PHENOMENON IS UNKNOWN. THUS, WE WILL FIRST COMPARE SI WT AND AD MICE CBF THROUGH LASER SPECKLE CONTRAST IMAGING, MENINGEAL AQP4 EXPRESSION THROUGH IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY, AND MENINGEAL AΒ ACCUMULATION THROUGH IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY AND INTRAPERITONEAL INJECTIONS OF THE BLOOD BRAIN BARRIER PERMEABLE AΒ SPECIFIC DYE METHOXY-X04. WE WILL ASSESS WHETHER PIAL AQP4 IS NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT TO DRIVE CBF AND AΒ ALTERATIONS IN AD AND SI MICE THROUGH VIRAL MANIPULATIONS OF SURFACE AQP4. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT MAY PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO HOW SI CONTRIBUTES TO AD PROGRESSION, AND PROVIDE A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC AVENUE FOR THE TREATMENT OF AD. THE APPROACHES EMPLOYED IN THIS PROPOSAL WILL PROVIDE A BREADTH OF EXPERIMENTAL TECHNIQUES INCLUDING SURGICAL TECHNIQUES AND COMPLEX IMAGE ANALYSIS. TRAINING FOR THESE PROCEDURES WILL TAKE PLACE IN THE SPONSOR’S LABORATORY. THROUGHOUT THE FELLOWSHIP, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT WILL OCCUR THROUGH SEMINARS, COURSEWORK, AND JOURNAL CLUB’S ASSOCIATED WITH VIRGINIA TECH, AND LOCAL AND NATIONAL CONFERENCES TO PREPARE THE PI FOR A CAREER AS AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCHER.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EVALUATING NEUTRALIZING IMMUNE RESPONSES TO THE ESSENTIAL INVASION PROTEIN RIPR ACROSS HUMAN PLASMODIUM SPECIES - PROJECT SUMMARY (REVISED) MALARIA IS A MOSQUITO-BORNE DISEASE THAT CONTINUES TO BE A SIGNIFICANT GLOBAL HEALTH CHALLENGE, POSING RISKS TO US TRAVELERS AND THE US MILITARY. WHILE VECTOR CONTROL MEASURES AND TREATMENT HAVE LED TO GLOBAL PROGRESS IN CONTROLLING MALARIA CASES AND DEATHS IN RECENT DECADES, THIS PROGRESS HAS STALLED SINCE 2015. CURRENT MALARIA VACCINES (RTS,S/AS01 AND R21/MATRIX-M) HAVE SHORT-LIVED PROTECTION, LIMITED EFFICACY AGAINST VARIOUS STRAINS, AND SPECIES-SPECIFICITY. AS A RESULT, DEVELOPING NEXT-GENERATION VACCINES TARGETING BLOOD-STAGE (MEROZOITE) ANTIGENS WHICH WILL REDUCE CLINICAL SYMPTOMS RESULTING FROM PLASMODIUM PARASITE REPLICATION IN RED BLOOD CELLS (RBCS) IS A PRIORITY. MY PROJECT FOCUSES ON RIPR, A PLASMODIUM PROTEIN ESSENTIAL FOR RBC INVASION THAT IS CURRENTLY BEING EVALUATED AS A BLOOD-STAGE VACCINE CANDIDATE (R78C) IN PHASE 1A CLINICAL TRIALS. MY CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT RIPR WILL SERVE AS A TARGET OF NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES ACROSS HUMAN PLASMODIUM FALCIPARUM STRAINS AND WILL SERVE AS A CROSS-SPECIES BLOOD-STAGE VACCINE CANDIDATE. THE FIRST GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO DETERMINE THE NEUTRALIZING AND SYNERGISTIC ACTIVITY OF RIPR VACCINE (R78C)-INDUCED ANTIBODIES AGAINST GENETIC VARIANTS OF P. FALCIPARUM FROM A REGION OF HIGH MALARIA TRANSMISSION. I WILL PAIR PHENOTYPIC DATA FROM FIELD-BASED EX VIVO NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS WITH GENOMIC AND PROTEIN STRUCTURE ANALYSIS OF IDENTIFIED RIPR SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE POLYMORPHISMS (SNPS) TO CHARACTERIZE THE FUNCTIONAL EFFECTS OF MUTATIONS OF INTEREST (EG: IMMUNE EVASION). FOR OTHER HUMAN PLASMODIUM SPECIES, WE LACK A CLEAR UNDERSTANDING OF THE FUNCTIONAL ROLE OF RIPR IN RBC INVASION. THEREFORE, THE SECOND GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY THE NEUTRALIZABLE EPITOPES OF RIPR IN THE FIVE NON-FALCIPARUM HUMAN PLASMODIUM SPECIES. AS P. KNOWLESI IS THE ONLY NON-FALCIPARUM PLASMODIUM SPECIES THAT CAN BE CULTURED LONG-TERM IN VITRO, I WILL USE IT AS A SYSTEM TO IDENTIFY NEUTRALIZING DOMAINS OF RIPR IN THESE SPECIES USING PHENOTYPIC ASSAYS AND PROTEIN BIOCHEMISTRY (SURFACE PLASMON RESONANCE, SPR). I WILL THEN QUANTIFY THE CROSS-SPECIES NEUTRALIZING ACTIVITY OF P. FALCIPARUM RIPR (PFRIPR)-SPECIFIC ANTIBODIES TARGETING THESE SPECIFIC DOMAINS USING TWO COMPLEMENTARY METHODS: CRISPR/CAS9-GENERATED CHIMERIC P. KNOWLESI PARASITES AND EX VIVO CLINICAL ISOLATES OF P. MALARIAE, P. OVALE CURTISI, AND P. OVALE WALLIKERI. IN SUMMARY, MY PROPOSED PROJECT WILL SHED LIGHT ON A HIGHLY CONSERVED RED BLOOD CELL INVASION PATHWAY IN HUMAN PLASMODIUM SPECIES AND EVALUATE ITS POTENTIAL AS A CROSS-SPECIES VACCINE CANDIDATE. THROUGH MY PROPOSED TRAINING ACTIVITIES AT YALE AND COLLABORATING INSTITUTIONS, I AIM TO DEVELOP TECHNICAL SKILLS IN FIELD-BASED EX VIVO ASSAYS, PROTEIN BIOCHEMISTRY, CRISPR/CAS9-BASED GENOME EDITING OF PLASMODIUM PARASITES, AND METHODS DEVELOPMENT IN RESOURCE-LIMITED SETTINGS. I ALSO AIM TO DEVELOP A STRONG CONCEPTUAL BACKGROUND IN IMMUNOLOGY, PARASITOLOGY, AND EARLY-STAGE VACCINE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPROVE MY SCIENTIFIC COMMUNICATION AND MENTORSHIP SKILLS, WITH THE GOAL OF PURSUING A CAREER AS AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR IN TRANSLATIONAL TROPICAL INFECTIOUS DISEASE RESEARCH.
