description: IN VIVO STRUCTURAL-BASED QUANTITATIVE MODELING OF AQUEOUS OUTFLOW DYNAMICS IN GLAUCOMATOUS EYES - PROJECT SUMMARY GLAUCOMA IS THE GLOBAL LEADING CAUSE OF IRREVERSIBLE BLINDNESS. IT IS AN INSIDIOUS OFTEN ASYMPTOMATIC, NEURODEGENERATIVE OCULAR DISEASE THAT, IF LEFT UNTREATED, CAN RESULT IN COMPLETE LOSS OF VISUAL PERCEPTION. THIS MAKES EARLY DETECTION OF GLAUCOMA A CRITICAL FOCUS OF RESEARCH IN OPHTHALMOLOGY. ONCE DIAGNOSED, DISEASE PROGRESSION CAN BE SLOWED USING A VARIETY OF EFFECTIVE TREATMENT STRATEGIES, ALL OF WHICH AIM TO REDUCE INTRAOCULAR PRESSURE (IOP). ELEVATED IOP IS THE LEADING RISK FACTOR RESULTING FROM A DEFECTIVE AQUEOUS HUMOR OUTFLOW (AHO) MECHANISM. CURRENT STANDARD CLINICAL TREATMENT FOR GLAUCOMA CONSISTS OF EYE DROPS, SELECTIVE LASER TRABULECTOMY (SLT), AND FILTRATION SURGERIES, ALL OF WHICH AIM TO FACILITATE EGRESS OF AQUEOUS FROM THE EYE’S ANTERIOR CHAMBER INTO THE BLOOD STREAM UNTIL A LOWER, TARGET IOP IS ACHIEVED. THESE THERAPIES CAN VARY IN SUCCESS AND LONGEVITY IN BOTH LOWERING IOP AND SLOWING DOWN DISEASE PROGRESSION. DESPITE TREATMENT MECHANISMS TARGETING AHO CELLULAR AND STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS, IN VIVO AHO MORPHOLOGY IS NOT FULLY UNDERSTOOD, IN HEALTH OR DISEASE. THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP IS AT LEAST IN PART DUE TO LIMITED VISIBILITY OF AHO AND A LACK OF QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS TOOLS. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS THESIS IS TO ESTABLISH A MORPHOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE AHO SYSTEM IN HEALTHY AND GLAUCOMATOUS EYES IN LIVE PEOPLE. THE STRATEGY IS AN INTEGRATIVE APPROACH, COMBINING IN VIVO ANTERIOR SEGMENT OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY (AS-OCT) IMAGING WITH ADVANCED IMAGE PROCESSING, DEEP LEARNING (DL) AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING BASED ON OUTFLOW FACILITY TO DESCRIBE THE AHO PATHWAY MORPHOLOGY IN HEALTHY AND GLAUCOMATOUS EYES. BY CHARACTERIZING THE THREE-DIMENSIONAL (3D) ARCHITECTURE OF KEY AHO STRUCTURES AND EVALUATING ITS CHANGES UNDER VARIOUS DISEASE STATES, THIS STUDY WILL ESTABLISH A COMPREHENSIVE IN VIVO MODEL OF THE AHO SYSTEM FOR THE FIRST TIME, PAVING THE WAY FOR IMPROVED KNOWLEDGE OF GLAUCOMA PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND POTENTIAL NOVEL TREATMENT OUTCOME MEASURES FOR IMPROVED GLAUCOMA CARE. THE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS IS THAT DETECTABLE STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES WITHIN THE AHO PATHWAY CAN BE OBSERVED IN THE AHO STRUCTURE BETWEEN HEALTHY AND GLAUCOMA USING COMPREHENSIVE IN VIVO MODELING, ENABLING PERSONALIZED OUTCOME MEASURES, PROGRESSION TRACKING, AND ADDITIONAL DISCRIMINATION BETWEEN HEALTH AND DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPACT OF PERINATAL ANTIBIOTICS ON THE GENERATION OF PROTECTIVE MAMMARY IGA - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT NEONATES ARE A PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE POPULATION DUE TO THE CHANGE IN THEIR ENVIRONMENT AT BIRTH, THE SUBSEQUENT MICROBIAL COLONIZATION THAT RESULTS, AND THE RELATIVE IMMATURITY OF THEIR IMMUNE SYSTEMS COMPARED TO ADULTS. OF IMPORTANCE IS THE FACT THAT NEONATES, ESPECIALLY THOSE OF VERY LOW BIRTH WEIGHT BORN TO PATIENTS EXPERIENCING PREMATURE BIRTH, ARE AT AN INCREASED RISK OF DEVELOPING SEPSIS RESULTING FROM A SYSTEMIC INFECTION. THOUGH PUBLISHED DATA HAS SHOWN THE BENEFIT OF MATERNAL ANTIBIOTICS WHICH REDUCE THE RISK OF EARLY-ONSET SEPSIS FROM VERTICAL BACTERIAL TRANSMISSION, THE RISK OF LATE-ONSET SEPSIS (LOS) IS INCREASED, HIGHLIGHTING THE NEED TO FURTHER UNDERSTAND HOW MATERNAL ANTIBIOTICS MIGHT IMPACT NEONATAL OUTCOMES. NEONATAL IMMUNOLOGICAL IMMATURITY AND ITS RAMIFICATIONS ARE MITIGATED THROUGH MATERNAL MEASURES INCLUDING TRANSPLACENTAL IGG TRANSFER DURING LATE PREGNANCY AND THROUGH IMMUNOGLOBULIN (IG) CONFERRED IN BREASTMILK. IN THE POST-BIRTH PERIOD BREASTMILK BECOMES THE ONLY SOURCE OF PROTECTIVE ANTIBODY WITH IGA, THE ANTIBODY FOUND MOST ABUNDANTLY AT MUCOSAL SURFACES, ACCOUNTING FOR THE HIGHEST CONCENTRATION OF IG. PRELIMINARY DATA FROM AN ONGOING COLLABORATION HAS SHOWN THAT IGA CONCENTRATIONS IN HUMAN BREASTMILK IS DECREASED FOLLOWING PERINATAL ANTIBIOTIC ADMINISTRATION IN PATIENTS. SIMILARLY, OUR LAB HAS SHOWN THAT IGA IS ALSO DECREASED IN THE BREASTMILK OF LACTATING MICE THAT WERE GIVEN ANTIBIOTICS FOR ONE WEEK PRIOR TO DELIVERY, UNDERSCORING THE POTENTIAL PERTURBATION OF PROCESSES CONTRIBUTING TO THE GENERATION OF IGA. MAMMARY IGA IS PREDOMINANTLY PRODUCED FROM PLASMA CELLS THAT TRAFFICKED TO THIS SITE AFTER GENERATION IN THE MATERNAL INTESTINE, SUGGESTING ANTIBIOTIC-MEDIATED PERTURBATION OF THE PERINATAL MATERNAL MICROBIOME DISRUPTS MAMMARY IGA. FURTHERMORE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE MATERNAL GUT MICROBIOTA DRIVES THE GENERATION OF PATHOGEN-SPECIFIC IGA IN LATE PREGNANCY THAT SERVES AS PROTECTION FROM INTESTINAL PATHOGENS IN NEONATES. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE HAVE DEVISED TWO AIMS TO FIRST, EVALUATE THE CONTRIBUTION OF THE MATERNAL MICROBIOTA IN LATE PREGNANCY IN THE GENERATION OF MAMMARY IGA AND SECOND, TO ASSESS THE ROLE OF MAMMARY IGA IN PROTECTING NEONATES FROM INTESTINAL PATHOGENS. WE WILL UTILIZE A MODEL OF PERINATAL ANTIBIOTIC ADMINISTRATION IN CONJUNCTION WITH OUR ESTABLISHED MODEL OF LOS IN BOTH WILDTYPE C57BL6 MICE AND IGA DEFICIENT MICE IN A C57BL6 BACKGROUND TO ADDRESS THESE AIMS. THIS WORK IS OF SIGNIFICANT CLINICAL IMPORTANCE DUE TO THE NEED TO BETTER UNDERSTAND MATERNAL PROTECTIONS CONFERRED TO NEONATES DURING PREGNANCY AND LACTATION. IN ADDITION, THIS WORK COULD CONTRIBUTE TO CLINICAL DECISIONS BY INFORMING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ANTIBIOTIC REGIMENS DURING PREGNANCY WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR INFORMING REGIMEN ADJUSTMENTS TO BETTER ACCOUNT FOR LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF PERINATAL MATERNAL ANTIBIOTICS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REGULATION OF THE GUT-REPRODUCTIVE AXIS IN FEMALE REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT AN EMERGING BODY OF LITERATURE SUGGESTS THE GUT MICROBIOME, OFTEN TERMED  THE FORGOTTEN ORGAN,  IS A KEY PLAYER IN REPRODUCTIVE DISORDERS SUCH AS POLYCYSTIC OVARY SYNDROME (PCOS), WHICH AFFECTS 10-15% OF THE FEMALE POPULATION WORLDWIDE. HOWEVER, THE PRECISE MECHANISMS BY WHICH THE GUT MICROBIOME MODULATES REPRODUCTIVE FUNCTION REMAIN UNCLEAR. IN THIS STUDY, I AIM TO ELUCIDATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE GUT MICROBIOME AND REPRODUCTIVE CYCLES. PREVIOUS STUDIES HAVE SHOWN THAT PCOS-LIKE MOUSE MODELS INDUCED BY LETROZOLE (LET) EXHIBIT DECREASED GUT MICROBIAL SPECIES RICHNESS CONCURRENT WITH UPREGULATED TOLL-LIKE RECEPTOR 4 (TLR4) EXPRESSION IN REPRODUCTIVE TISSUES. THESE DATA SUGGEST A LINK BETWEEN GUT MICROBIOME, TLR4 ACTIVATION, AND REPRODUCTIVE DYSFUNCTION. UNDER HEALTHY CONDITIONS, LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDES (LPS) FROM MICROBIAL CELL WALLS REMAIN CONFINED WITHIN THE GUT. HOWEVER, DISRUPTION OF THE INTESTINAL BARRIER CAN LEAD TO LPS LEAKAGE AND ACTIVATION OF TLR4. MY PRELIMINARY DATA SHOWS THAT KNOCK OUT OF TLR4 PREVENTS LET-INDUCED DYSFUNCTION RESULTING IN MAINTENANCE OF REGULAR ESTROUS CYCLES, FERTILITY, NORMALIZED HORMONE PRODUCTION AND PRESERVATION OF GUT BARRIER INTEGRITY. THEREFORE, THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF THIS PROPOSAL IS THAT GUT MICROBIOTA REGULATES THE MOUSE ESTROUS CYCLE BY ALTERING GUT PERMEABILITY AND GUT-REPRODUCTIVE AXIS COMMUNICATION THROUGH TOLL-LIKE RECEPTOR 4 (TLR4). TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, I WILL PURSUE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) DECIPHER THE DIRECTIONAL INFLUENCE BETWEEN THE ESTROUS CYCLE STAGE AND THE GUT MICROBIOME, AND 2) DETERMINE THE ROLE OF GUT PERMEABILITY AND VAGUS NERVE SIGNALING IN TLR4-DEPENDENT ESTROUS ACYCLICITY. ACROSS MY AIMS, I WILL UTILIZE WILD TYPE (C57BL/6J) AND TLR4 KNOCKOUT MICE, USING THE LET-INDUCED PCOS-LIKE MODEL. MY EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH IN AIM 1 EMPLOYS 16S RRNA SEQUENCING, METABOLOMICS, AND FECAL MICROBIOTA TRANSPLANTATION TO ANALYZE THE GUT MICROBIOME. IN AIM 2, I WILL ASSESS INTESTINAL BARRIER FUNCTION USING FLUORESCENT TRACER COMPOUNDS AND IN VIVO IMAGING, WHILE DEFINING THE ROLE OF GUT-BRAIN COMMUNICATION THROUGH SURGICAL INTERRUPTION OF VAGUS NERVE SIGNALING. COLLECTIVELY, THESE AIMS OFFER A ROBUST FRAMEWORK FOR THE CASUAL RELATIONSHIP OF MICROBIAL DYSBIOSIS ON REPRODUCTIVE CYCLES. THE FINDINGS FROM MY STUDY COULD HAVE BROAD IMPLICATIONS FOR UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE OF GUT MICROBIOTA IN OVERALL REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH, POTENTIALLY LEADING TO IMPROVED DIAGNOSTICS AND MICROBIOME-TARGETED INNOVATIVE THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES FOR CONDITIONS LIKE PCOS. 1

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNDERSTANDING PHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF SEASONAL REPRODUCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT IN HUMANS AND OTHER MAMMALS, STARVATION, EXTENSIVE EXERCISE, AND COLD EXPOSURE DEPLETE FAT RESERVES AND CAUSE WEIGHT LOSS. THE DEPLETION OF ENERGY STORES ATTENUATES THE FUNCTION OF THE REPRODUCTIVE AXIS, CAUSING HYPOGONADISM, DELAYS IN MATURATION AND INFERTILITY. THIRTEEN-LINED GROUND SQUIRRELS (ICTIDOMYS TRIDECEMLINEATUS) ARE OBLIGATORY HIBERNATORS THAT SPEND 7 MONTHS WITH NO ACCESS TO FOOD OR WATER AT LOW ENVIRONMENTAL AND BODY TEMPERATURE. FOR MOST MAMMALS THESE CONDITIONS ARE INHABITABLE AND CAN LEAD TO INFERTILITY AND ULTIMATELY DEATH. FEMALE GROUND SQUIRRELS MATE ONCE ANNUALLY, AND THEIR FERTILE WINDOW IS TIGHTLY LOCKED TO EMERGENCE FROM HIBERNATION, WITH PEAK MATING SUCCESS IN THE FIRST WEEK POST EMERGENCE. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT FEMALE GROUND SQUIRRELS UNDERGO SEXUAL MATURATION DURING HIBERNATION, AND THEIR REPRODUCTIVE AXIS IS AT LEAST PARTIALLY UNCOUPLED FROM METABOLISM AND ENERGY BALANCE. CONSISTENT WITH THIS HYPOTHESIS, OUR PRELIMINARY DATA REVEALED INCREASED LEVELS OF SEX HORMONES AND GROWTH OF REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS IN FEMALE GROUND SQUIRRELS DURING HIBERNATION. THE NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL AND MOLECULAR PATHWAYS UNDERLYING THIS REMARKABLE BIOLOGICAL CAPACITY ARE UNKNOWN. HERE WE AIM TO INVESTIGATE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS SUPPORTING SEXUAL MATURATION DURING HIBERNATION AND REVEAL HOW THE REPRODUCTIVE AXIS BECOMES UNCOUPLED FROM METABOLISM. THROUGH THE SUPPORT OF THIS FELLOWSHIP, WE AIM TO REVEAL THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE PROCESS OF FEMALE SEXUAL MATURATION VIA THE UNIQUE PERSPECTIVE OF FEMALE THIRTEEN-LINED GROUND SQUIRRELS. THIS STUDY WILL BE CONDUCTED AT YALE UNIVERSITY IN THE LABORATORY OF DR. ELENA GRACHEVA. THROUGH AIM 1, WE PROPOSE A SERIES OF LONGITUDINAL EXPERIMENTS TO REVEAL CHANGES IN ACTIVITY OF THE REPRODUCTIVE AXIS ACROSS SEASONS USING MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH INCLUDING RNA IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION, BLOOD BIOCHEMISTRY AND MORPHOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF THE REPRODUCTIVE TRACT. WITHIN AIM 2, WE WILL ASSESS THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR CHANGES ACROSS PHYSIOLOGICAL STATES IN KISSPEPTIN (REPRODUCTIVE) NEURONS IN THE ARCUATE NUCLEUS OF THE HYPOTHALAMUS USING SINGLE NUCLEUS SEQUENCING, ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY AND IN VIVO IMAGING. THIS PROPOSAL HIGHLIGHTS GENERAL PRINCIPLES OF REPRODUCTIVE NEUROPHYSIOLOGY IN MAMMALS AND WILL FURTHER OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE NEUROENDOCRINE SYSTEM DURING EXTREME DEFICITS IN ENVIRONMENTAL AND BODY CONDITIONS. OUR WORK WILL LAY FOUNDATION FOR RATIONAL DESIGN OF PHARMACOLOGICAL TOOLS TO UNDERSTAND HOW LIFE IN MAMMALS CAN PERSIST DURING PROLONGED COLD EXPOSURE AND STARVATION AND HOW THE REPRODUCTIVE AXIS FUNCTIONS UNDER EXTREME NEGATIVE ENERGY BALANCE. RESULTS FROM THIS PROPOSAL WILL GENERATE TESTABLE HYPOTHESES REGARDING THE REGULATION OF REPRODUCTION AND ALLOW US TO PREDICT WHETHER HIBERNATION CAN BE INDUCED IN OTHER MAMMALS, INCLUDING HUMANS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DETERMINING HOW NUP153 AND PRC2 ACTIVITIES ARE BALANCED TO DRIVE DEVELOPMENTAL GENE-EXPRESSION PROGRAMS - PROJECT SUMMARY GENE EXPRESSION IS TIGHTLY REGULATED DURING DEVELOPMENT TO GIVE RISE TO CELLS WITH UNIQUE MORPHOLOGIES AND FUNCTIONS. EACH CELL HAS AN IDENTICAL GENOME BUT DISTINCT GENE EXPRESSION PROFILES. A BALANCE BETWEEN GENE ACTIVATION AND REPRESSION MUST BE ESTABLISHED TO ENSURE THAT PROPER GENE-REGULATORY NETWORKS ARE EXPRESSED. CONSERVED CHROMATIN REGULATORS, SUCH AS THE POLYCOMB REPRESSIVE COMPLEX 2 (PRC2), AID IN CREATING THIS DELICATE EQUILIBRIUM REQUIRED FOR CELL-FATE SPECIFICATION. PRC2 PROMOTES GENE SILENCING BY DEPOSITING TRIMETHYLATION ON LYSINE 27 OF HISTONE 3 (H3K27ME3) AND SPREADING THIS MARK ACROSS BROAD REGIONS OF THE GENOME. PROPER REGULATION OF THE LEVELS OF H3K27ME3 IS ESSENTIAL FOR NORMAL DEVELOPMENT AND MUTATIONS THAT PREVENT PRC2 FROM SPREADING H3K27ME3 RESULT IN DIFFUSE MIDLINE GLIOMAS (DMGS), A HIGHLY AGGRESSIVE PEDIATRIC BRAIN CANCER. IN DMGS, A MISSENSE MUTATION IN HISTONE H3 (H3 K27M) DISRUPTS DIFFERENTIATION AND DRIVES TUMOR FORMATION. WE LEVERAGED THE H3 K27M MUTATION IN DROSOPHILA MELANOGASTER TO IDENTIFY THE PATHWAYS THAT FUNCTION WITH PRC2 TO MAINTAIN NORMAL DEVELOPMENTAL PROGRAMS, WHERE MANY OF THESE CHROMATIN REGULATORY PROTEINS ARE CONSERVED. BY SCREENING HUNDREDS OF GENES ENCODING CHROMATIN-REGULATORY PROTEINS FOR THOSE WHOSE LOSS OF FUNCTION SUPPRESSED THE H3 K27M MUTANT PHENOTYPES, WE IDENTIFIED A DEEPLY CONSERVED COMPONENT OF THE NUCLEAR PORE, NUP153, AS A STRONG SUPPRESSOR. PREVIOUS STUDIES IN CELL CULTURE IDENTIFIED ROLES FOR NUP153 IN GENE EXPRESSION BOTH AS AN ACTIVATOR AND REPRESSOR. NONETHELESS, THE PRECISE TISSUE-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS BY WHICH NUP153 REGULATES TRANSCRIPTION AND WHETHER THESE EFFECTS ARE DUE TO ITS INCORPORATION INTO THE NUCLEAR PORE WITHIN THE CONTEXT OF A DEVELOPING ORGANISM REMAIN UNCLEAR. GIVEN OUR STRONG GENETIC AND PHENOTYPIC DATA IMPLICATING NUP153 IN THE SUPPRESSION OF H3 K27M-INDUCED PHENOTYPES, I HYPOTHESIZE THAT PRC2 AND NUP153 WORK TOGETHER TO MAINTAIN A BALANCE BETWEEN GENE ACTIVATION AND REPRESSION THAT IS REQUIRED FOR PROPER DIFFERENTIATION AND DEVELOPMENT. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, I WILL USE A COMBINATION OF IMAGING AND GENOMICS TO DETERMINE HOW NUP153 INTERACTS WITH CHROMATIN TO REGULATE TISSUE-SPECIFIC GENE EXPRESSION DURING DEVELOPMENT (AIM 1) AND HOW IT INTERFACES WITH PRC2-MEDIATED REPRESSION TO MODULATE CHROMATIN STRUCTURE AND FACILITATES DEVELOPMENTAL DEFECTS OBSERVED UPON H3 K27M EXPRESSION (AIM 2). TOGETHER, THIS WORK WILL USE MOLECULAR BIOLOGY, IMAGING, GENETICS AND GENOMICS TO REVEAL THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT ENSURE THE REGULATORY BALANCE BETWEEN NUP153 AND PRC2 NECESSARY TO COORDINATE DEVELOPMENTAL PROGRAMS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT OF TISSUE DERIVED INTESTINAL ORGANOIDS AS A MODEL SYSTEM FOR MECHANISTIC TESTING IN CHILDREN WITH AUTISM-ASSOCIATED ENTEROCOLITIS - PROJECT SUMMARY IT IS WELL-ESTABLISHED THAT GASTROINTESTINAL (GI) SYMPTOMS OCCUR MORE FREQUENTLY IN CHILDREN WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD) THAN IN TYPICALLY DEVELOPING (TD) CHILDREN, AND RECENT PUBLICATIONS REPORT THAT THE SEVERITY OF GI DYSFUNCTION IS POSITIVELY CORRELATED WITH THE SEVERITY OF ASD-RELATED BEHAVIORS AND COGNITIVE CHALLENGE. DESPITE THESE STRONG ASSOCIATIONS, THE BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS LINKING INTESTINAL PATHOPHYSIOLOGY TO NEURODEVELOPMENTAL OUTCOMES REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. ONE COMPELLING POSSIBILITY INVOLVES SEROTONIN SIGNALING WITHIN THE GUT–BRAIN AXIS. EXCESS SEROTONIN CAN STIMULATE IMMUNE ACTIVATION, PROMOTE INTESTINAL INFLAMMATION, AND DRIVE DIARRHEA; SYMPTOMS COMMONLY OBSERVED IN CHILDREN WITH ASD. OUR DATA SUGGESTS THAT CHILDREN WITH ASD HAVE DECREASED EXPRESSION OF SERT IN THE TERMINAL ILEUM AND INCREASED EXPRESSION OF THE SEROTONIN RECEPTORS HTR3A; SUGGESTING A MECHANISM BY WHICH LOCAL SEROTONIN CLEARANCE IS IMPAIRED. IMPORTANTLY, SERT EXPRESSION IS STRONGLY MODULATED BY THE GUT MICROBIOTA. SEVERAL FLAGELLATED MICROBES SUPPRESS SERT MRNA AND PROTEIN LEVELS, WHILE BENEFICIAL COMMENSALS ENHANCE SERT EXPRESSION. CONSISTENT WITH THIS, OUR WORK IDENTIFIES DISTINCT MICROBIAL SHIFTS IN THE TERMINAL ILEUM OF CHILDREN WITH ASD, INCLUDING INCREASED ABUNDANCE OF LACHNOSPIRACEAE AND UNCLASSIFIED CLOSTRIDIUM. THESE ORGANISMS ALSO HAVE FLAGELLA AND COULD ACTIVATE TLR5 WHICH MIGHT LEAD TO DECREASED SERT AND EXCESS SEROTONIN. WE ALSO IDENTIFIED THAT HTR3A EXPRESSION WAS ELEVATED IN CHILDREN WITH ASD COMPARED TO TD CONTROL. HTR3A HAS BEEN ASSOCIATED WITH PRO-INFLAMMATORY SIGNALING, SUGGESTING THAT EXCESS SEROTONIN IN THE GUT MAY FURTHER AMPLIFY EPITHELIAL INFLAMMATION AND CONTRIBUTE TO GI DYSFUNCTION IN ASD. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CHILDREN WITH ASD HARBOR CLOSTRIDIAL AND LACHNOSPIRACEAE SPECIES WITH HIGHLY IMMUNOSTIMULATORY FLAGELLA THAT ACTIVATE TLR5 ON TERMINAL ILEUM ENTEROCYTES, LEADING TO SUPPRESSION OF EPITHELIAL SERT EXPRESSION. REDUCED SERT RESULTS IN EXCESS EXTRACELLULAR SEROTONIN, WHICH ACTIVATES THE UPREGULATED HTR3A RECEPTOR TO DRIVE MUCOSAL INFLAMMATION AND GUT DYSFUNCTION, THEREBY CONTRIBUTING TO GI AND POTENTIALLY NEUROBEHAVIORAL SYMPTOMS IN ASD. TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS, WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING TWO AIMS. AIM 1. DEFINE HOW FLAGELLATED CLOSTRIDIAL AND LACHNOSPIRACEAE SPECIES ENRICHED IN ASD ACTIVATE TLR5 AND SUPPRESS SERT EXPRESSION IN TISSUE-DERIVED HUMAN INTESTINAL ORGANOIDS. AIM 2. DEFINE HOW SEROTONIN EXCESS ACTIVATES HTR3A TO PROMOTE EPITHELIAL INFLAMMATION AND DYSFUNCTION IN HUMAN ORGANOIDS FROM ASD AND TD CHILDREN. THIS PROPOSAL DIRECTLY ADDRESSES A CRITICAL AND LONG-STANDING GAP BY IDENTIFYING SPECIFIC MICROBIAL AND EPITHELIAL PATHWAYS THAT DISRUPT SEROTONIN HOMEOSTASIS IN THE TERMINAL ILEUM, AN ANATOMIC SITE UNIQUELY AFFECTED IN ASD. BY LEVERAGING HUMAN-DERIVED ILEAL AND COLONIC ORGANOIDS AND MICROBIAL ISOLATES, THE PROPOSED RESEARCH MOVES BEYOND ASSOCIATIVE MICROBIOME STUDIES TO ESTABLISH CAUSAL MECHANISMS IN ASD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING HOW HISTONE METHYLTRANSFERASES CAUSE GENE SILENCING IN THE C. ELEGANS GERMLINE - PROJECT SUMMARY IN EUKARYOTES, THE GENOMIC INTEGRITY OF GERM CELLS IS MAINTAINED BY CHROMATIN AND SMALL RNA PATHWAYS, CONFERRING GERMLINE IMMORTALITY AND FERTILITY. IN THE CAENORHABDITIS ELEGANS (C. ELEGANS) GERMLINE, NUCLEAR RNA INTERFERENCE (RNAI) FACTORS, IN COMPLEX WITH SMALL RNAS AND NASCENT TARGET TRANSCRIPTS, RECRUIT HISTONE METHYLTRANSFERASES (HMTS) THAT DEPOSIT REPRESSIVE HISTONE MODIFICATIONS, THEREBY TRIGGERING HETEROCHROMATIN FORMATION. THIS PROCESS HAS ALSO BEEN OBSERVED IN OTHER EUKARYOTES. THE COMPLEX INTERPLAY BETWEEN SMALL RNA AND HETEROCHROMATIN PATHWAYS PRESENTS A CHALLENGE IN STUDYING HOW INDIVIDUAL HMTS CONTRIBUTE TO GENE SILENCING AND GERMLINE IMMORTALITY. THE RECENT DEVELOPMENT OF AN ASSAY IN C. ELEGANS THAT USES THE LAC OPERATOR-LAC REPRESSOR BINDING SYSTEM FROM ESCHERICHIA COLI (E. COLI) TO TETHER HMTS UPSTREAM OF A TRANSGENE (GFP) REPORTER HAS ENABLED DIRECT STUDY OF HMT EFFECTS ON GENE EXPRESSION. PRELIMINARY STUDIES USING THIS SYSTEM HAVE SHOWN THAT TETHERING AN H3K9 METHYLTRANSFERASE (MET-2 OR SET-25) TRIGGERS CIS-SILENCING OF THE DOWNSTREAM GFP REPORTER, TRANS-SILENCING OF A SECONDARY UNTETHERED GFP REPORTER INTRODUCED BY CROSSING, AND PRODUCTION OF SMALL RNAS TARGETING THE GFP REPORTER. SUBSEQUENT ANALYSIS IDENTIFIED SEVERAL NUCLEAR RNAI FACTORS REQUIRED FOR TRANS-SILENCING. THESE FINDINGS IMPLICATE TRANS-SILENCING IN THE MAINTENANCE OF GERMLINE IMMORTALITY. HOWEVER, IT REMAINS UNCLEAR WHAT THE PRECISE ROLES OF HETEROCHROMATIN AND SMALL RNAS ARE IN HMT TETHERING-INDUCED SILENCING, HOW THE GFP REPORTER TRANSCRIPTS ARE RECOGNIZED AS TARGETS FOR SMALL RNA PRODUCTION, AND WHICH OTHER GENETIC FACTORS ARE REQUIRED TO INITIATE AND/OR MAINTAIN CIS- AND TRANS-SILENCING INDUCED BY HMT TETHERING. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO UNDERSTAND HOW HMTS CAUSE GENE SILENCING AND SMALL RNA PRODUCTION IN THE C. ELEGANS GERMLINE. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE THE ROLES OF HETEROCHROMATIN AND SMALL RNAS IN HMT TETHERING-INDUCED CIS- AND TRANS-SILENCING. CHROMATIN PROFILING WILL BE USED TO IDENTIFY HISTONE MODIFICATIONS ENRICHED AT THE REPORTER LOCUS FOLLOWING TETHERING, AND CATALYTICALLY INACTIVE HMT MUTANTS WILL BE TETHERED TO DETERMINE IF METHYLTRANSFERASE ACTIVITY IS REQUIRED FOR CIS- AND TRANS-SILENCING. TO INVESTIGATE SMALL RNAS, A NUCLEAR RNAI FACTOR WILL BE IMMUNOPRECIPITATED AFTER HMT TETHERING, AND BOUND SMALL RNAS WILL BE SEQUENCED. HMTS WILL ALSO BE TETHERED IN A MUTANT STRAIN DEPLETED FOR SMALL RNAS, AND TRANS-SILENCING WILL BE MEASURED. AIM 2 WILL CHARACTERIZE REPORTER TRANSCRIPT PROCESSING AND LOCALIZATION AFTER HMT TETHERING USING LONG-READ DIRECT RNA SEQUENCING AND RNA FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION, RESPECTIVELY. AIM 3 WILL IDENTIFY GENETIC FACTORS REQUIRED TO INITIATE AND MAINTAIN CIS- AND TRANS-SILENCING. CRISPR/CAS9 GENE EDITING WILL BE USED TO GENERATE MUTATIONS IN CANDIDATE FACTORS BEFORE OR AFTER HMT-TETHERING, AND CIS- AND TRANS-SILENCING WILL BE MEASURED. THIS WORK WILL ELUCIDATE HOW HMTS AND SMALL RNAS COOPERATE TO CONTROL GENE SILENCING AND MAINTAIN GERMLINE IMMORTALITY, AND PROVIDE THE FELLOW WITH TRAINING IN WORM GENETICS, RNA BIOLOGY, CHROMATIN DYNAMICS, MICROSCOPY, AND BIOINFORMATICS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING THE PLACENTAL SELENOPROTEOME - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SELENIUM (SE) IS AN ESSENTIAL TRACE ELEMENT REQUIRED FOR A HEALTHY PREGNANCY, AND IT HAS BEEN ESTIMATED THAT 2.8 BILLION PEOPLE WORLDWIDE DO NOT CONSUME ENOUGH SE. MATERNAL SE DEFICIENCY IS ASSOCIATED WITH MISCARRIAGE, INFERTILITY, PRETERM BIRTH, FETAL GROWTH RESTRICTION (FGR), PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION, GESTATIONAL DIABETES MELLITUS, AND PREECLAMPSIA. SE IS INCORPORATED INTO SELENOPROTEINS FOR FUNCTION. SELENOPROTEINS ARE PRODUCED BY THE PLACENTA AND ARE CRITICAL FOR CELLULAR METABOLISM AND MITIGATION OF OXIDATIVE STRESS. THE PLACENTA IS A HIGHLY METABOLIC ORGAN WHOSE GROWTH AND FUNCTION ARE REQUIRED FOR PROPER FETAL DEVELOPMENT. METABOLIC DYSREGULATION CAN LEAD TO THE ACCUMULATION OF REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES AND COMPROMISE FUNCTION. DESPITE THE WELL-ESTABLISHED INVOLVEMENT OF SE AND SELENOPROTEINS IN THESE PROCESSES AND THE LINKS BETWEEN ADVERSE PREGNANCY OUTCOMES AND SE DEFICIENCY, THERE HAS BEEN NO INVESTIGATION WHICH TRULY OUTLINES THE FUNCTIONAL SIGNIFICANCE OF SELENOPROTEINS PRODUCED BY THE PLACENTA. THESE INCLUDE IODOTHYRONINE DEIODINASE 2 (DIO2), A SELENOPROTEIN RESPONSIBLE FOR THYROID HORMONE METABOLISM, WHICH IS INDISPENSABLE FOR HUMANS. MOREOVER, A RATE-LIMITING FACTOR OF SELENOPROTEIN BIOSYNTHESIS, SECIS BINDING PROTEIN 2 (SBP2), IS ALSO PRODUCED BY THE PLACENTA. SBP2 MUTATIONS MANIFEST IN ADULT INFERTILITY AND SIGNIFICANTLY IMPACTED GROWTH AND ABNORMAL THYROID HORMONE PROFILES. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS F31 PREDOCTORAL FELLOWSHIP IS TO USE OUR IN VIVO PLACENTA-SPECIFIC LENTIVIRAL-MEDIATED RNA INTERFERENCE (RNAI) TECHNIQUE TO DIRECTLY INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF THE PLACENTAL SELENOPROTEOME DURING THE FIRST HALF OF GESTATION USING THE SHEEP MODEL. AIM 1 WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT PLACENTAL DIO2 DEFICIENCY RESULTS IN PLACENTAL INSUFFICIENCY AND ABNORMAL THYROID HORMONE METABOLISM IN SHEEP AT MIDGESTATION [75 DAYS OF GESTATIONAL AGE (DGA)]. AIM 2 WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT PLACENTAL SBP2 DEFICIENCY WILL RESULT IN A DECREASED PLACENTAL SELENOPROTEOME, LEADING TO PLACENTAL METABOLIC DYSFUNCTION AND OXIDATIVE STRESS, WITH ABERRANT PLACENTAL DEVELOPMENT AND SIGNIFICANT FGR RESULTING AS CONSEQUENCE AT MIDGESTATION (75 DGA). THESE PROJECTS WILL BE THE FIRST TO DIRECTLY IDENTIFY THE ROLE OF PLACENTAL SELENOPROTEINS IN PREGNANCY. ALL WORK WILL BE COMPLETED AT THE ANIMAL REPRODUCTION AND BIOTECHNOLOGY LABORATORY AT COLORADO STATE UNIVERSITY AND OVERSEEN BY MY SUPPORTIVE SPONSOR, DR. QUINTON WINGER, AND CO-SPONSOR, DR. JANE STREMMING, WHO RESIDES AT THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO ANSCHUTZ MEDICAL CAMPUS. MY TAILORED TRAINING PLAN IS DESIGNED TO SUPPORT MY DEVELOPMENT INTO A WELL-ROUNDED, INDEPENDENT BIOMEDICAL SCIENTIST. IT WILL EMPHASIZE MY ADVANCEMENTS IN SCIENTIFIC COMMUNICATION AND GRANTSMANSHIP, SURGICAL AND LEADERSHIP SKILLS, AND OVERALL UNDERSTANDING OF PLACENTAL AND FETAL PHYSIOLOGY AS PREGNANCY PROGRESSES. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO UNDERSTAND HOW THE PLACENTAL SELENOPROTEOME CONTRIBUTES TO PREGNANCY OUTCOMES. THIS PROPOSAL DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THE NICHD’S RESEARCH GOAL 3: “SETTING THE FOUNDATION FOR HEALTHY PREGNANCIES AND LIFELONG WELLNESS” THROUGH THE USE OF INNOVATIVE BASIC AND TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE APPROACHES TO FURTHER UNDERSTAND IMPACTS ON THE PLACENTA AND ITS RESULTING FETAL IMPACTS IN GESTATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ROLE OF THE DUFFY ANTIGEN RECEPTOR FOR CHEMOKINES IN VASCULAR DYSFUNCTION AND HYPERTENSION IN THE CONTEXT OF HIV - PROJECT SUMMARY COMBINATION ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (CART) HAS TRANSFORMED HIV INTO A MANAGEABLE CHRONIC DISEASE. HOWEVER, PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV (PLWH) REMAIN AT AN INCREASED RISK FOR CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD), PARTICULARLY HYPERTENSION, EVEN WITH EFFECTIVE VIRAL SUPPRESSION. HIV VIRAL PROTEINS PERSIST IN CIRCULATION DESPITE CART AND WELL-CONTROLLED VIREMIA AND HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO CONTRIBUTE TO CVD. FURTHERMORE, CVD RISK IS DISPROPORTIONATELY HIGH AMONG INDIVIDUALS OF AFRICAN ANCESTRY, MANY OF WHOM HARBOR A MUTATION IN THE DUFFY ANTIGEN RECEPTOR FOR CHEMOKINES (DARC-NULL GENOTYPE). DARC IS AN ATYPICAL CHEMOKINE RECEPTOR EXPRESSED ON RED BLOOD CELLS (RBC) AND VENULAR ENDOTHELIAL CELLS, WHERE IT REGULATES INFLAMMATION BY SEQUESTERING CHEMOKINES. LOSS OF DARC DISRUPTS CHEMOKINE HOMEOSTASIS AND PROMOTES INFLAMMATION. TO INVESTIGATE HOW LOSS OF DARC INFLUENCES VASCULAR INJURY, WE USED THE DARC-/-, WHICH REPLICATES THE DARC NULL GENOTYPE COMMON IN THIS POPULATION, AND A NOVEL TG26DARC-/- MOUSE MODEL EXPRESSING HIV PROTEINS ON A DARC-DEFICIENT BACKGROUND TO INVESTIGATE THE COMBINED ROLES OF DARC DEFICIENCY AND HIV PROTEIN EXPOSURE. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT DARC DEFICIENCY INCREASES SYSTOLIC BLOOD PRESSURE (SBP) AND IMPAIRS VASCULAR FUNCTION, WITH NO FURTHER IMPAIRMENT IN THE TG26DARC-/- MICE, SUGGESTING THAT LOSS OF DARC AND HIV PROTEINS DRIVE HYPERTENSION THROUGH DISTINCT AND NON- SYNERGISTIC MECHANISMS. CYTOKINE PROFILING REVEALED A MECHANISTIC DIVERGENCE IN DARC–/– MICE WITH ELEVATED PLASMA IL-6, IL-1Β, TNFΑ, AND IL-17A, AND REDUCED IL-1Α AND ENDOTHELIAL NOX1 EXPRESSION, SHIFTING THE INFLAMMATORY PROFILE TOWARD AN IL-17–DOMINANT STATE. THESE FINDINGS SUGGEST THAT DARC DEFICIENCY IMPAIRS ENDOTHELIAL FUNCTION AND ELEVATES SBP THROUGH HIGH CIRCULATING CYTOKINE LEVELS BUT ALSO SHIFTS THE INFLAMMATORY MILIEU AWAY FROM IL-1Α AND POTENTIALLY TOWARD AN IL-17–DOMINANT PROFILE IN THE PRESENCE OF HIV PROTEINS. THIS PROPOSAL WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT DARC REGULATES BLOOD PRESSURE BY MODULATING CIRCULATING IL-17A AND IL- 1Α LEVELS. AIM 1 WILL TEST WHETHER DARC DEFICIENCY PROMOTES IL-17A–MEDIATED VASCULAR INFLAMMATION AND USE BONE MARROW TRANSPLANTATION TO DEFINE THE RELATIVE CONTRIBUTION OF RBC VS ENDOTHELIAL EXPRESSED DARC. AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE HOW DARC REGULATES IL-1Α PRODUCTION IN CD4⁺ T CELLS. TOGETHER, THESE PROPOSED AIMS WILL DEFINE THE MECHANISM BY WHICH A COMMON AFRICAN ANCESTRY-LINKED POLYMORPHISM DRIVES ENDOTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION AND HYPERTENSION IN THE CONTEXT OF HIV. THE PROJECT WILL BE CONDUCTED UNDER THE MENTORSHIP OF DRS. ERIC BELIN DE CHANTEMÈLE AND NEAL WEINTRAUB AT THE VASCULAR BIOLOGY CENTER, AUGUSTA UNIVERSITY, WHICH HAS A STRONG TRACK RECORD OF TRAINING SUCCESSFUL PRE- AND POST-DOCTORAL FELLOWS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS FOR 3 YEARS OF FUNDING, CULMINATING WITH A DISSERTATION DEFENSE AT THE END OF THE THIRD YEAR. FINDINGS FROM THIS WORK WILL UNCOVER A NOVEL MECHANISM LINKING DARC TO T CELL-MEDIATED VASCULAR INJURY AND OFFER MECHANISTIC INSIGHT INTO RACIAL DISPARITIES IN HIV-ASSOCIATED CVD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PRECISION PHENOGROUPING AND TREATMENT OF ATRIAL FIBRILLATION IN REAL-WORLD SETTINGS - ABSTRACT ATRIAL FIBRILLATION (AF), CHARACTERIZED BY IRREGULAR AND OFTEN RAPID BEATING OF THE ATRIA, IS THE MOST COMMON CARDIAC ARRHYTHMIA AND A MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUE, WITH INCREASING PREVALENCE AND INCIDENCE, SUBSTANTIAL MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY, AND SIGNIFICANT STROKE RISK. MANAGEMENT REMAINS CHALLENGING, OWING LARGELY TO AN INCOMPLETE UNDERSTANDING OF ITS COMPLEX PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND HETEROGENEITY. CURRENT AF CLASSIFICATIONS INTO STAGES (I.E., PAROXYSMAL, PERSISTENT, AND PERMANENT) ARE BASED PRIMARILY ON EPISODE FREQUENCY AND DURATION, CAPTURING A NARROW DIMENSION OF THE DISEASE. THIS APPROACH FAILS TO ACCOUNT FOR THE CLINICAL HETEROGENEITY SEEN IN REAL-WORLD PRACTICE, POTENTIALLY LEADING TO SUBOPTIMAL CARE. PATIENTS WITH AF VARY WIDELY IN COMORBIDITIES, CARDIAC STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION, DISEASE PROGRESSION, OUTCOME RISKS, AND TREATMENT RESPONSES, YET CURRENT GUIDELINES DO NOT INTEGRATE THESE FACTORS IN MANAGEMENT. RECENT EFFORTS HAVE SHIFTED TOWARDS THE IDENTIFICATION OF AF PHENOGROUPS, GROUPS OF PATIENTS WITH SHARED CHARACTERISTICS AND PHENOTYPES, THAT MAY HAVE DIFFERENTIAL PATTERNS OF PROGRESSION AND TREATMENT RESPONSES. ADDITIONALLY, ADVANCEMENTS IN DATA SCIENCE AND THE GROWING AVAILABILITY OF LARGE-SCALE DATA HAVE ENABLED THE APPLICATION OF MACHINE LEARNING (ML) APPROACHES TO REVEAL PREVIOUSLY UNDISCOVERED INSIGHTS. THEREFORE, THIS RESEARCH AIMS TO ADVANCE PRECISION MEDICINE IN AF TOWARD A PHENOGROUP-DRIVEN APPROACH BY INTEGRATING ML WITH REAL-WORLD DATA. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL LEVERAGE THE LARGE, LONGITUDINAL MERATIVE MARKETSCAN DATABASES OF PATIENT-LEVEL MEDICAL CLAIMS WITH >600,000 AF PATIENTS TO ADDRESS THREE SPECIFIC AIMS. IN AIM 1, TO DISCOVER AND CHARACTERIZE DISTINCT, CLINICALLY RELEVANT AF PHENOGROUPS, FOUR UNSUPERVISED ML CLUSTERING TECHNIQUES WILL BE EVALUATED. A SUPERVISED ML APPROACH WILL IDENTIFY THE MOST INFORMATIVE CLINICAL FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH PHENOGROUP MEMBERSHIP. IN AIM 2, TO ESTABLISH THE DIFFERENTIAL PROGNOSES OF THE DISCOVERED PHENOGROUPS, TIME-TO-EVENT ANALYSES WILL BE EMPLOYED. MULTI-STATE MODELS WILL MODEL TRANSITION HAZARDS FOR TWO DISTINCT PROGRESSION PATHWAYS (I.E., STRUCTURAL/THROMBOEMBOLIC AND ISCHEMIC/ATHEROSCLEROTIC). COX PROPORTIONAL HAZARDS MODELS WILL ESTIMATE DIFFERENCES IN TIME TO FIRST INCIDENT OUTCOMES, AND NEGATIVE BINOMIAL REGRESSION WILL ESTIMATE RATES OF HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION. IN AIM 3, TO EVALUATE THE COMPARATIVE EFFECTIVENESS OF ANTICOAGULANT THERAPIES ON STROKE-RELATED OUTCOMES ACROSS PHENOGROUPS, THE TARGET TRIAL FRAMEWORK WILL BE USED TO COMPARE DIRECT ORAL ANTICOAGULANTS AGAINST VITAMIN K ANTAGONISTS ON STROKE AND STROKE-RELATED OUTCOMES. CAUSAL CONTRASTS WILL BE ESTIMATED USING TARGETED MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD ESTIMATION WITH A SUPERLEARNER LIBRARY TO PROVIDE ROBUST ESTIMATES OF PERSONALIZED TREATMENT EFFECTS. IT IS HYPOTHESIZED THAT ML WILL REVEAL NOVEL AF PHENOGROUPS THAT EXHIBIT DIFFERENTIAL DISEASE PROGRESSION AND RESPONSES TO ANTICOAGULANT THERAPY. THE RESULTS WILL PROVIDE A DATA-DRIVEN APPROACH THAT CAPTURES THE HETEROGENEITY OF AF AND ESTABLISH EVIDENCE-BASED, PHENOGROUP-SPECIFIC TREATMENT RECOMMENDATIONS, ACCELERATING THE TRANSLATION OF PRECISION MEDICINE TO CARDIOVASCULAR PRACTICE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: THE TRUSTEES OF COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IN THE CITY OF NEW YORK

description: TOWARD AUTOMATED, SCALABLE KNOWLEDGE ENGINEERING FOR REAL WORLD DATA USING CLINICAL TERMINOLOGIES - PROJECT SUMMARY HIGH-QUALITY REAL-WORLD EVIDENCE DEPENDS ON TWO INTERTWINED CAPABILITIES: (1) THE EXISTENCE OF HARMONIZED CLINICAL VOCABULARIES THAT GIVE CONSISTENT MEANING TO THE CODES EMBEDDED IN ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (EHRS) AND (2) COMPUTABLE PHENOTYPES THAT TRANSLATE CONCEPT CODES, TEMPORAL RULES, AND CLINICAL CONTEXT INTO REPRODUCIBLE PATIENT COHORTS. TO DATE, NO AUTOMATED SYSTEM HAS RELIABLY HARMONIZED CLINICAL VOCABULARIES OR GENERATED HIGH-FIDELITY PHENOTYPE DEFINITIONS AT SCALE. WHILE THE ADVANCEMENT OF TRANSFORMER-BASED MODELS, SUCH AS LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS (LLMS) OFFERS SOME PROMISE, THEY MAY HALLUCINATE CODE MAPPINGS OR CONCEPT RELATIONSHIPS, AND THEY LACK EXPLICIT SEMANTIC GROUNDING REQUIRED FOR CLINICAL APPLICATIONS. THIS WORK AIMS TO ADDRESS THESE LIMITATIONS BY CREATING AN OPEN-SOURCE PIPELINE THAT FUSES SYMBOLIC ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE WITH LLMS TO AUTOMATE KNOWLEDGE ENGINEERING. THE METHODS WILL BE ANCHORED IN THE OBSERVATIONAL HEALTH DATA SCIENCES AND INFORMATICS (OHDSI) STANDARDIZED VOCABULARY, WHICH CONSISTS OF OVER 198,000 CONCEPTS AND 86 MILLION EXPERT-CURATED RELATIONSHIPS. THIS SEMANTIC ANCHORING WILL CONSTRAIN LLM OUTPUTS TO VALIDATED CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE, ALLEVIATE HALLUCINATION, AND ENABLE RIGOROUS BENCHMARKING AGAINST GOLD STANDARDS. OUR AIMS ARE AS FOLLOWS: (1) DEVELOP A VOCABULARY HARMONIZATION TOOLKIT (INCLUDING TERM SIMILARITY, SUBSUMPTION, AND GROUPING TASKS) WITH LLM AUGMENTED ALGORITHMS; AND (2) AUGMENT EXISTING KNOWLEDGE ENGINEERING PIPELINES WITH MACHINE LEARNING METHODS FOR PHENOTYPE SPECIFICATION AND REFINEMENT. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL DELIVER AN OPERATIONAL, END-TO-END PIPELINE FOR AUTOMATED CLINICAL VOCABULARY HARMONIZATION AND PHENOTYPE SPECIFICATION. BY LEVERAGING THE SCALE AND EXPERT KNOWLEDGE FROM THE OHDSI STANDARDIZED VOCABULARY AND MODERN MACHINE LEARNING CAPABILITIES, THIS HYBRID APPROACH WILL SURPASS EXISTING MANUAL AND PURELY DATA-DRIVEN METHODS IN BOTH INTERPRETABILITY AND SCALABILITY. ULTIMATELY, THIS WORK WILL REDUCE THE NEED FOR MANUAL KNOWLEDGE CURATION, AND THE TOOLS DEVELOPED WILL BE BROADLY APPLICABLE TO OTHER TASKS SUCH AS TERMINOLOGY QUALITY ASSURANCE, COHORT DEFINITION REVIEW, AND CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION SUPPORT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A COMPUTATIONAL MODEL LINKING MICROCIRCUIT PROPERTIES TO CORTEX-WIDE ACTIVITY DURING DECISION MAKING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ORGANISMS CONSTANTLY MAKE DECISIONS AS THEY MOVE THROUGH THEIR ENVIRONMENT AND GATHER EVIDENCE FOR OR AGAINST TAKING CERTAIN ACTIONS. THE PROCESSES OF ACCUMULATING INFORMATION AND COMMITTING TO A CHOICE ARE ASSOCIATED WITH DISTINCT PATTERNS OF WIDESPREAD CORTICAL ACTIVITY. BUT HOW DO THESE PATTERNS EMERGE AND HOW ARE THEY SHAPED BY CIRCUIT PROPERTIES AT MULTIPLE SPATIAL SCALES? ONE FEATURE OF CORTICAL NETWORKS CRITICAL FOR UNDERSTANDING THESE PATTERNS OF ACTIVITY IS PROPOSED BY THEORETICAL WORK: SPONTANEOUS TIMESCALE, A MEASUREMENT OF ACTIVITY PERSISTENCE WITHIN A NETWORK. DATA FROM OUR LAB SHOWS THAT, DURING SHORT-TERM MEMORY, THE PATTERN OF LARGE-SCALE CORTICAL RECRUITMENT MIRRORS ITS GRADIENT OF SPONTANEOUS ACTIVITY TIMESCALES, WHICH INCREASE ALONG THE ANATOMICAL HIERARCHY, FROM POSTERIOR TO FONTAL AREAS. THIS HIERARCHY OF TIMESCALE IS IMPLICATED IN DECISION MAKING, WHERE PRIMARY SENSORY CORTEX HAS SHORTER TIMESCALES THAT LEND IT THE CAPABILITY TO INTEGRATE SENSORY INFORMATION, AND ASSOCIATION AREAS HAVE LONGER TIMESCALES NECESSARY FOR INFORMATION MAINTENANCE. THIS HIERARCHY CO-VARIES WITH GRADIENTS IN CORTICAL CYTOARCHITECTURE AND CELLULAR PROPERTIES, SUCH AS LEVELS OF EXCITATORY RECURRENCE, PROPORTIONS OF INHIBITORY CELL TYPES, AND INTRINSIC MEMBRANE TIME CONSTANTS OF INDIVIDUAL NEURONS. HOWEVER, THE RELATIVE CONTRIBUTIONS OF THESE PROPERTIES TO SETTING NETWORK TIMESCALE AND CORTICAL RECRUITMENT PATTERNS DURING DECISION MAKING REMAIN UNKNOWN. THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP WILL BE ADDRESSED BY CREATING A COMPUTATIONAL MODEL OF SPONTANEOUS AND TASK-DRIVEN ACTIVITY ACROSS THE CORTEX, CONSTRAINED BY KNOWLEDGE OF AREA-LEVEL MICROCIRCUITRY AND BY FUNCTIONAL DATA FROM MULTIPLE CORTICAL CELL TYPES AND AREAS. SPECIFICALLY, IN AIM 1, WIDEFIELD CA2+ IMAGING DATA WILL BE USED TO MEASURE THE SPONTANEOUS ACTIVITY TIMESCALES OF DIFFERENT EXCITATORY AND INHIBITORY GENETICALLY DEFINED CELL TYPES IN THE CORTEX. IN AIM 2, MULTI-AREA RECURRENT NEURAL NETWORKS (RNNS) WILL BE CONSTRUCTED, JOINTLY CONSTRAINED BY THE NEURAL DATA AND OTHER KNOWN BIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF CORTICAL CIRCUITRY, SUCH AS LONG-RANGE CONNECTIVITY AND THE CYTOARCHITECTONIC PROPERTIES ABOVE. THESE RNNS WILL BE TRAINED TO MATCH BOTH SPONTANEOUS AND TASK-DRIVEN CORTICAL ACTIVITY. THE LATTER HAS BEEN PREVIOUSLY MEASURED IN OUR LAB DURING A NEW DECISION-MAKING TASK FOR MICE NAVIGATING IN VIRTUAL REALITY, WHICH DISSOCIATES SHORT-TERM MEMORY FROM OTHER COGNITIVE PROCESSES. PERFORMANCE OF THE TASK-SOLVING MODEL WILL BE COMPARED WHEN INITIALIZED RANDOMLY OR WITH THE SPONTANEOUS MODEL, WHERE IT IS HYPOTHESIZED THAT THE ORGANIZATION OF SPONTANEOUS TIMESCALE WILL BE LEVERAGED SO THAT THE MODEL CONVERGES MORE QUICKLY DURING TRAINING. FINALLY, IN SILICO PERTURBATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED TO RELATE NETWORK STRUCTURE TO ITS ORGANIZATION OF SPONTANEOUS TIMESCALES AND FUNCTIONAL ROLES DURING DECISION-MAKING. THIS MODEL WILL LEAD TO PROPOSED CIRCUIT MECHANISMS THAT LINK NETWORK STRUCTURE TO ITS COGNITIVE FUNCTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CEREBELLAR GABAERGIC PERTURBATION IN A NDD MOUSE MODEL - PROJECT SUMMARY AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD) IS A NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER (NDD) THAT AFFECTS MORE THAN 2% OF THE US POPULATION. DESPITE THE HIGH PREVALENCE AND KNOWN GENETIC CAUSES, LACK OF UNDERSTANDING OF CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF ASD IS A MAJOR BARRIER TOWARDS DEVELOPING EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS FOR THIS COMPLEX DISORDER. MUCH OF THE UNDERSTANDING OF THE GENETIC ETIOLOGY IN ASD COMES FROM LARGE SCALE GENOME SEQUENCING EFFORTS, WHICH HAVE REVEALED A GROWING LIST OF HIGH CONFIDENCE RISK GENES. OF THESE RARE BUT STRONGLY CAUSAL ASD RISK GENES, THE CHROMATIN REMODELING FACTOR (CRF) CHROMODOMAIN HELICASE DNA-BINDING PROTEIN 8 (CHD8) HAS AMONG THE MOST FREQUENT AND HIGHEST PENETRANCE FOR DE NOVO MUTATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH ASD DIAGNOSIS. CHD8 HAS BEEN BROADLY CHARACTERIZED AS A REGULATOR OF NEUROGENESIS AND BRAIN DEVELOPMENT THOUGH MUCH REMAINS UNKNOWN REGARDING DIRECT AND INDIRECT ROLES OF THIS PROTEIN IN SPECIFIC CELL TYPES IN THE DEVELOPING BRAIN. STUDIES OF MICE WITH GERMLINE HETEROZYGOUS LOSS-OF-FUNCTION (LOF) MUTATIONS TO CHD8 HAVE FOUND BEHAVIORAL AND COGNITIVE DEFICITS, SUBTLE SOCIAL PHENOTYPES, AND MACROCEPHALY, AS WELL AS TRANSCRIPTIONAL, CELLULAR, AND MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY RELEVANT TO ASD. MOST MOLECULAR STUDIES INTO THE FUNCTION OF THIS GENE ARE FOCUSED ON NEURODEVELOPMENT IN THE CORTEX. AND ALTHOUGH TYPICALLY STUDIED IN THE CONTEXT OF MOTOR FUNCTION, THE CEREBELLUM (CB) PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE IN HIGHER ORDER COGNITIVE FUNCTIONS AND CB DYSFUNCTION HAS BEEN SHOWN TO BE CORRELATED WITH ASD AND NDD. THERE HAVE BEEN A FEW STUDIES ON THE ROLE OF CHD8 IN THE CB, WHICH HAVE SHOWN REQUIREMENT FOR CHD8 FOR CB DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTION. HOWEVER, PREVIOUS REPORTS HAVE USED CONDITIONAL KNOCKOUT APPROACHES RATHER THAN THE ASD-RELEVANT GERMLINE HETEROZYGOUS STATE, AND LARGELY FAILED TO IDENTIFY IMPACTS IN HETEROZYGOUS MUTANT MICE IN THE CB IN PURKINJE NEURON (PN) AND GRANULE CELL PROGENITOR CKOS. PRELIMINARY DATA IN OUR LAB FOUND CELL TYPE SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND FUNCTIONAL PERTURBATION TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF CB GABAERGIC CELL TYPES, INCLUDING PNS. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE HETEROZYGOUS CHD8 MUTATION CONTRIBUTES TO ASD PATHOGENESIS THROUGH DEVELOPMENTAL DYSREGULATION OF PNS, THE ONLY PROJECTING CELL TYPE FROM THE CB CORTEX. HERE I PROPOSE WORK TO CHARACTERIZE THE EFFECT OF CHD8 HAPLOINSUFFICIENCY ON THE FUNCTION AND DEVELOPMENT OF PNS USING TRANSLATIONALLY RELEVANT CONSTITUTIVE HETEROZYGOUS CHD8 MUTANT MICE. IN AIM 1, I WILL INTEGRATE HISTOLOGY, ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, AND TRANSCRIPTOMICS TO TEST WHETHER THE COMPOSITION AND FUNCTION OF PN SUBTYPES IS ALTERED IN CHD8 HAPLOINISUFFICIENT MICE. IN AIM 2, I WILL USE SINGLE CELL TRANSCRIPTOMICS TO TEST IF GABAERGIC NEUROGENESIS IS ALTERED IN THE CB VENTRICULAR ZONE. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE MECHANISM AND EFFECTS OF DECREASED CHD8 DOSAGE ON A KEY CELL TYPE IN THE CB. IF SUCCESSFUL, THIS PROPOSAL WILL INFORM FUTURE DIRECTIONS FOR MEASURES TO TREAT UNDERLYING PATHOLOGY AND PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLE CRFS PLAY IN CB NEUROGENESIS AND ASD ETIOLOGY.

description: FUNCTIONALLY SPECIALIZED TEMPORAL AND FRONTAL LOBE REGIONS FOR IDENTITY RECOGNITION AND UPDATING - PROJECT SUMMARY A CENTRAL QUESTION IN SOCIAL BEHAVIOR RESEARCH IS HOW INDIVIDUAL IDENTITIES ARE RECOGNIZED AND UPDATED AS FEATURES CHANGE OVER TIME. DIFFICULTIES WITH IDENTITY RECOGNITION AND THEIR SOCIAL CONSEQUENCES CAN LEAD TO SOCIAL WITHDRAWAL, WHICH MAY WORSEN OTHER CONDITIONS. IDENTITY RECOGNITION IS IMPAIRED IN INDIVIDUALS WITH NEUROPSYCHIATRIC AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS LIKE ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD), CAUSING SIGNIFICANT DISRUPTIONS IN DAILY LIFE. THE DORSOLATERAL PREFRONTAL CORTEX (DLPFC) IS KNOWN TO SUPPORT HIGH-LEVEL COGNITIVE TASKS, INCLUDING PROCESSING TARGET IDENTITY, UNCERTAINTY, AND SOCIAL PREDICTION. CONVERSELY, THE SUPERIOR TEMPORAL SULCUS (STS) PROCESSES CONSPECIFIC IDENTITY AND FEATURES. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW NEURONAL ACTIVITY IN DLPFC AND STS SHIFTS TO ADAPT TO IDENTITY UPDATING AND HOW THE PROJECTION FROM STS TO DLPFC (STSDLPFC) FACILITATES THIS PROCESS. FACES AND VOICES ARE THE MOST CRUCIAL ASPECTS OF CONSPECIFIC IDENTITY, WITH HUMANS AND NONHUMAN PRIMATES EVOLVING HIGH VARIABILITY IN THESE FEATURES TO AID RECOGNITION. IN AIM 1, TO STUDY IDENTITY RECOGNITION AND UPDATING BEHAVIOR, I WILL TRAIN MARMOSET MONKEYS ON A NOVEL FACE-VOICE MATCHING TASK THAT TEACHES THEM TO RECOGNIZE SEVERAL CONSPECIFIC IDENTITIES FROM VIDEOS OF VOCALIZING INDIVIDUALS. AFTER LEARNING AN IDENTITY, WE WILL ALTER A FACIAL FEATURE'S COLOR OR SHAPE WHILE KEEPING THE VOICE UNCHANGED, ANCHORING IDENTITY THROUGH VOICE RECOGNITION AND REQUIRING SUBJECTS TO “UPDATE” THEIR FACIAL REPRESENTATION. I WILL FUNCTIONALLY LOCALIZE THE ACTIVE DLPFC AND STS DURING THE UPDATING PROCESS USING FDG-PET SCANS, AND IMPLANT MULTIELECTRODE ARRAYS INTO DLPFC AND STS TO RECORD NEURAL ACTIVITY DURING IDENTITY RECOGNITION AND UPDATING. I PREDICT THAT POPULATION ACTIVITY PATTERNS IN DLPFC WILL INITIALLY DIFFER FOR THE ALTERED FEATURES BUT WILL EVENTUALLY CONVERGE TO THE LEARNED IDENTITY AFTER UPDATING, PARALLELING BEHAVIORAL PERFORMANCE. ADDITIONALLY, I EXPECT STS ACTIVITY TO PREDICT DLPFC ACTIVITY, ESTABLISHING A CAUSAL RELATIONSHIP, ALTHOUGH ACTIVITY IN STS RELATED TO ALTERED FEATURES WILL REMAIN DISTINCT FROM THE LEARNED IDENTITY AFTER UPDATING. IN AIM 2, I WILL EXAMINE THE NECESSITY OF THE STSDLPFC PROJECTION FOR IDENTITY UPDATING. USING CHEMOGENETIC APPROACHES WITH NOVEL VIRAL VECTORS, I WILL ASSESS HOW INHIBITION OF STSDLPFC AFFECTS BEHAVIORAL UPDATING PERFORMANCE. I PREDICT THAT INACTIVATING STSDLPFC DURING UPDATING, BUT NOT RECOGNITION, WILL DECREASE PERFORMANCE ACCURACY AND INCREASE RESPONSE LATENCY. THE INSIGHTS FROM THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL PROVIDE A NEW FRAMEWORK FOR UNDERSTANDING NEURAL CIRCUITS INVOLVED IN IDENTITY PROCESSING, WHICH COULD INFORM HOW THESE CIRCUITS BREAK DOWN IN NEURODEGENERATIVE AND NEUROPSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS SUCH AS AD AND ASD. THIS WORK WILL BE CONDUCTED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH, WHERE I WILL BE SUPPORTED BY MENTORS WHO WILL TRAIN ME IN SCIENTIFIC CONCEPTS, TECHNIQUES, AND PROFESSIONALISM. MY TRAINING WILL ENCOMPASS BEHAVIORAL, NEUROIMAGING, CHEMOGENETIC, NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL, AND COMPUTATIONAL METHODS TO ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF IDENTITY PROCESSING. DEVELOPING THESE SKILLS IS ESSENTIAL FOR MY GOAL OF BECOMING AN INDEPENDENT NEUROSCIENTIST SPECIALIZING IN IDENTITY PROCESSING AND MULTISENSORY INTEGRATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IDENTIFICATION AND VALIDATION OF NOVEL AXONAL GROWTH AND PLASTICITY MODULATORS FOR CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM REPAIR. - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT STROKE, TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY, AND SPINAL CORD INJURY ARE AMONG THE LEADING CAUSES OF DISABILITY WORLDWIDE. THEY CAUSE SIGNIFICANT LONG-TERM COGNITIVE, MOTOR AND SENSORY IMPAIRMENTS DUE TO THE LIMITED REGENERATION CAPACITY OF THE ADULT CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. ALTHOUGH PARTIAL FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY HAS BEEN OBSERVED FOLLOWING ACUTE SPINAL CORD INJURY, PRIMARILY DUE TO SPROUTING FROM INTACT AXONS, THE UNDERLYING MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT FACILITATE REGENERATION OF INJURED AXONS AND PLASTICITY WITHIN PRESERVED CIRCUITS REMAIN UNKNOWN. IDENTIFICATION OF THE MECHANISMS THAT SUPPORT LONG DISTANCE GROWTH IS CRUCIAL TO DEVELOPING EFFECTIVE THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS. BASED ON MY COMPELLING PRELIMINARY DATA THAT DOWNREGULATION OF CANDIDATE GROWTH REPRESSORS IDENTIFIED BY TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROFILING IN POSTNATAL MICE CAN BE CO-OPTED TO STIMULATE AXONAL RE-GROWTH OF HUMAN NEURONS, I HYPOTHESIZE THAT MANIPULATION OF GENES THAT ENABLE DEVELOPMENTAL AXONAL EXTENSION IN MICE WILL STIMULATE ROBUST AXON GROWTH IN HUMAN NEURONS AND ADULT MICE POST-INJURY. TO THIS END, I AIM TO DEFINE THE TRANSCRIPTOMIC PROFILE OF MOUSE CORTICOSPINAL NEURONS (CSNS) DURING GROWTH-PERMISSIVE STATES, SUCH AS DURING POSTNATAL DEVELOPMENT AND WIRING (AIM 1), FOLLOWED BY VALIDATION OF NOVEL CANDIDATE GROWTH MODULATORS IN HUMAN STEM CELL-DERIVED NEURONS (AIM 2), AND ASSESSMENT OF ANATOMICAL AND FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY POST SPINAL CORD INJURY OF ADULT MICE WITH DELETION OF OUR NEWLY IDENTIFIED PUTATIVE GROWTH-REPRESSOR WASL (AIM 3). THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL BE CONDUCTED AT YALE UNIVERSITY IN THE INTERDEPARTMENTAL NEUROSCIENCE PROGRAM. THE HIGHLY COLLABORATIVE AND INCLUSIVE ENVIRONMENT OF MY TRAINING PROGRAM MADE IT POSSIBLE FOR ME TO PURSUE A NOVEL MULTI-DISCIPLINARY THESIS PROJECT UNDER THE CO-MENTORSHIP OF DR. WILLIAM CAFFERTY AND DR. KRISTEN BRENNAND. THE COMBINED EXPERTISE OF MY SPONSORS ALLOWS ME TO COMPLEMENT MY NOW ESTABLISHED EXPERTISE IN MOLECULAR NEUROSCIENCE AND STEM CELL MODELS WITH ONGOING TRAINING IN SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROFILING APPLIED TO MOUSE CNS DEVELOPMENT AND INJURY. MY TRAINING PLAN INCLUDES EXTENSIVE TRAINING IN BIOINFORMATICS (ONGOING) AND ANIMAL MODELS OF CNS INJURY (TO BE ACQUIRED), AND APPLICATION OF MY EXISTING COMPETENCY IN CRISPR-BASED SCREENING BY HIGH-CONTENT IMAGING IN HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELL NEURONS, AS WELL AS ENSURING ALL ACADEMIC, SCIENTIFIC COMMUNICATION, LEADERSHIP, AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT SKILLS ARE FOSTERED. MY SHORT-TERM GOAL IS TO DISCOVER NOVEL INSIGHTS INTO THE MECHANISMS THAT GOVERN NORMAL AND PLASTIC AXONAL GROWTH, REPRESENTING NOVEL TARGETS FOR FUTURE DEVELOPMENT OF THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS. DEVELOPMENT OF A UNIQUE MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, BEHAVIORAL, AND BIOINFORMATIC SKILL SET WILL PREPARE ME TO ACHIEVE MY LONG-TERM GOAL OF BECOMING A FUTURE LEADER IN THE FIELD OF CNS AXON INJURY AND REGENERATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ROLE OF ASTROGLIAL TNFR2 IN COGNITIVE FUNCTION IN MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS - SUMMARY  COGNITIVE DYSFUNCTION IS A MAJOR BURDEN FOR PEOPLE WITH MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS (MS), WHO SUFFER FROM A WIDE SPECTRUM OF DEFICITS (IMPAIRED INFORMATION PROCESSING SPEED, ATTENTION, MEMORY) THAT SEVERELY COMPROMISE THEIR QUALITY OF LIFE. DESPITE THE HIGH PREVALENCE AND SOCIETAL IMPACT, COGNITIVE DYSFUNCTION IN MS IS UNDERSTUDIED AND ITS MECHANISMS POORLY UNDERSTOOD. AS SUCH, NO TREATMENTS TO LIMIT COGNITIVE DECLINE AND FACILITATE COGNITIVE RECOVERY IN MS ARE AVAILABLE. THIS IS A MAJOR UNMET NEED.  MS-ASSOCIATED COGNITIVE DYSFUNCTION HAS BEEN LINKED TO IMPAIRED SYNAPTIC TRANSMISSION AND PLASTICITY, PROCESSES THAT REQUIRE THE COMMUNICATION BETWEEN NEURONS AND GLIA, PARTICULARLY ASTROCYTES. A KEY MODULATOR OF SYNAPTIC TRANSMISSION AND PLASTICITY IS TUMOR NECROSIS FACTOR (TNF), WHICH FUNCTIONS VIA BINDING TO TWO RECEPTORS, TNFR1 AND TNFR2, BOTH EXPRESSED IN ASTROCYTES. ASTROGLIAL TNFR1 IS ESSENTIAL FOR PROPER SYNAPTIC TRANSMISSION AND PLASTICITY IN PHYSIOLOGICAL CONDITIONS, BUT IN EXPERIMENTAL AUTOIMMUNE ENCEPHALOMYELITIS (EAE), THE WIDELY USED MODEL OF MS, TNFR1 ACTIVATION LEADS TO LEARNING AND MEMORY DEFICITS INDICATING THAT, IN DISEASE STATES, ASTROGLIAL TNFR1 TURNS DETRIMENTAL. REMARKABLY, WHETHER ASTROGLIAL TNFR2 ALSO PLAYS A ROLE IN SYNAPTIC FUNCTION/PLASTICITY AND COGNITION IN PATHOLOGICAL CONDITIONS WAS NEVER EXPLORED.  TO ADDRESS THIS GAP IN KNOWLEDGE, I WILL INDUCE EAE IN TRANSGENIC MICE WITH ASTROCYTE-SPECIFIC ABLATION AND OVEREXPRESSION OF TNFR2 (GFAPCREERT2:TNFRSF1BFL/FL MICE GFAPTTA:TNFRSF1BTRE MICE, RESPECTIVELY) GENERATED IN THE BRAMBILLA LAB. BASED ON PREVIOUS STUDIES AND PRELIMINARY DATA, I HYPOTHESIZE THAT TNFR2 HAS A BENEFICIAL ROLE IN PREVENTING/COUNTERACTING COGNITIVE DYSFUNCTION IN EAE BY REGULATING CELL-CELL COMMUNICATION PROCESSES AT THE BASIS OF SYNAPTIC FUNCTION AND PLASTICITY. I WILL ADDRESS MY HYPOTHESIS WITH TWO STAND-ALONE AND COMPLEMENTARY APPROACHES: 1) IN VIVO STUDIES TO ELUCIDATE THE ROLE OF ASTROGLIAL TNFR2 IN SYNAPTIC FUNCTION AND COGNITION IN EAE; 2) IN VITRO STUDIES TO DETERMINE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH ASTROGLIAL TNFR2 REGULATES NEURON-GLIA COMMUNICATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DETERMINING THE ROLE OF THE PARABRACHIAL NUCLEUS IN CHEMOSENSITIVITY AND EPILEPSY - ABSTRACT SUDDEN UNEXPECTED DEATH IN EPILEPSY (SUDEP) IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH IN PATIENTS WITH REFRACTORY EPILEPSY. SUDEP IS SECOND ONLY TO STROKE IN YEARS OF POTENTIAL LIFE LOST TO NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE, THEREFORE REPRESENTING A MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUE. VICTIMS ARE OFTEN FOUND ALONE, MAKING THE EVENTS PRIOR TO DEATH ELUSIVE AND DIFFICULT TO DEFINE. ALTHOUGH SUDEP IS A DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION, SEVERAL ETIOLOGIES HAVE BEEN PROPOSED FOR SUDEP. THE FIELD HAS INCLUDING CARDIAC AND RESPIRATORY DYSREGULATION FOLLOWING SEIZURE TERMINATION AS CRITICAL CONTRIBUTORS TO A POTENTIALLY FATAL OUTCOME. AN ADDITIONAL ETIOLOGY THAT IS POSTULATED IS POST-SEIZURE, OR POST-ICTAL, IMPAIRED AROUSAL. SEIZURES IMPAIR ONE’S ABILITY TO APPROPRIATELY RESPOND TO STIMULI. THIS IS INCLUSIVE OF STIMULUS THAT NORMALLY RESULTS IN AROUSAL. AMONG AROUSAL STIMULI, ONE THAT IS PARTICULARLY RELEVANT TO SUDEP IS CO2. CO2 RISES FOLLOWING SEIZURES AND IS PART OF THE SEIZURE CESSATION MECHANISM. SEIZURES ARE FREQUENTLY ASSOCIATED WITH ICTAL AND POST- ICTAL CENTRAL AND OBSTRUCTIVE APNEAS. AN APNEIC EPISODE FURTHER EXACERBATES THE ACCUMULATION OF CO2. IMPAIRMENT OF THE CO2-AROUSAL MECHANISM IS PROPOSED AS AN ETIOLOGICAL FACTOR IN ANOTHER SUDDEN DEATH ENTITY, SUDDEN INFANT DEATH SYNDROME, WHICH HAS MANY PARALLELS WITH SUDEP. INVESTIGATING THE MODULATION OF CHEMOSENSITIVE POPULATIONS FOR PROPER CO2-AROUSAL PROVIDES AN INITIAL COURSE OF ACTION IN UNDERSTANDING WHAT POPULATIONS ARE IMPAIRED IN THE CONTEXT OF SEIZURES AND EPILEPSY. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY HOW CO2-AROUSAL CAN BE PROMOTED AND WHAT POPULATIONS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH NEGATING SEIZURE-INDUCED DEATH. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DETERMINE THE CHEMOSENSITIVE PROPERTIES OF THE CALCITONIN GENE-RELATED PEPTIDE-EXPRESSING SUBPOPULATION IN THE EXTERNAL LATERAL REGION OF THE PARABRACHIAL NUCLEUS (PBELCGRP) BY EVALUATING CO2-AROUSAL DURING OPTOGENETIC INHIBITION. WE WILL TEST WHETHER SUPPRESSING PBELCGRP NEURONAL ACTIVITY PROLONGS AROUSAL LATENCY TO A CO2 STIMULUS. PROLONGED CO2-AROUSAL LATENCY WOULD PROVIDE ADDITIONAL EVIDENCE THAT PBELCGRP NEURONS CONTRIBUTE CRITICALLY TO THE ASCENDING AROUSAL SYSTEM THAT MEDIATES HOMEOSTATIC RESPONSES TO HYPERCAPNIA. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER OPTOGENETIC ACTIVATION OF THE PBELCGRP NEURONS REDUCES SEIZURE-INDUCED DEATH BY PROMOTING RECOVERY OF RESPIRATORY AND BEHAVIORAL FUNCTION IN A MOUSE MODEL OF SEIZURE-INDUCED DEATH. THIS MODEL, WHICH EXHIBITS A DEATH PHENOTYPE RESEMBLING SEIZURE-INDUCED RESPIRATORY ARREST, ALLOWS US TO COMPARE FINDINGS BETWEEN MICE THAT DIE AND THOSE THAT SURVIVE, MAKING THESE STUDIES HIGHLY RELEVANT TO SUDEP. SIGNIFICANT REDUCTION IN MORTALITY WOULD ESTABLISH THE PBELCGRP SUBPOPULATION AS A LOCATION FOR INTERVENTION AND FURTHER INVESTIGATION TO PROMOTE RECOVERY. COMBINED WITH PREVIOUS WORK, WE WILL HAVE A POWERFUL, RIGOROUS, AND TRANSLATABLE APPROACH TO IDENTIFY CONVERGENT AND DIVERGENT MECHANISMS ACROSS MODELS FOR HOW IMPAIRED CO2- AROUSAL CONTRIBUTES TO SUDEP RISK AND WHAT POPULATIONS CAN MITIGATE THIS RISK. THE PROPOSED WORK WILL HAVE AN IMMEDIATE POSITIVE IMPACT AS IT WILL FORM THE INITIAL FOUNDATION TO EXPAND UPON FOR FUTURE RESEARCH OF POST-ICTAL IMPAIRED AROUSAL IS A CONTRIBUTING MECHANISM OF SUDEP.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ABL2 REGULATION OF MICROTUBULE ASSEMBLY IN DENDRITES - PROJECT SUMMARY MUTATIONS IN MICROTUBULE (MT)-RELATED GENES CONTRIBUTES TO A WIDE RANGE OF BRAIN DISORDERS. THUS, IT IS CRITICAL TO UNDERSTAND THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS DRIVING MT REGULATION AND DYNAMICS IN NEURONS. LOSS OF THE ABL2 NON- RECEPTOR TYROSINE KINASE IN MICE DISRUPTS NORMAL DENDRITIC ARBOR AND SYNAPSE DEVELOPMENT AND STABILITY, SIGNIFICANTLY COMPROMISING NEURONAL MORPHOLOGY. OUR LAB RECENTLY DISCOVERED AN UNEXPECTED, KINASE- INDEPENDENT ROLE FOR ABL2: THE ABL2 C-TERMINAL HALF UNDERGOES LIQUID-LIQUID PHASE SEPARATION (LLPS), CO- CONDENSES WITH TUBULIN DIMERS, AND PROMOTES MT ASSEMBLY IN VITRO AND ASSEMBLY IN COS7 CELLS. HOWEVER, WE DO NOT UNDERSTAND AT A MOLECULAR LEVEL HOW ABL2 BINDS AND COACERVATES WITH TUBULIN OR HOW THESE PROCESSES CONTRIBUTE TO MT ASSEMBLY AND DENDRITE DEVELOPMENT. I WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT ABL2 MEDIATES MT ASSEMBLY THROUGH LLPS AND THAT THIS IS CRITICAL FOR MT ASSEMBLY IN DENDRITES VIA THREE HIGHLY COMPLEMENTARY AIMS: AIM 1: ELUCIDATE THE BIOCHEMICAL BASIS FOR ABL2 LLPS AND MT POLYMERIZATION AND REPAIR. WE DO NOT KNOW WHICH SPECIFIC RESIDUES ARE NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT TO PROMOTE LLPS OR HOW ABL2 LLPS CONTRIBUTES TO MT POLYMERIZATION. I WILL USE PURIFIED RECOMBINANT ABL2 PROTEINS AND PERFORM IN VITRO PHASE SEPARATION ASSAYS TO DETERMINE WHICH RESIDUES ARE NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT FOR PHASE SEPARATION. I WILL PERFORM COMPLEMENTARY MT ASSEMBLY AND DYNAMICS ASSAYS TO DETERMINE HOW ABL2 MUTANTS WITH DEFINED LLPS PROPERTIES IMPACT MT ASSEMBLY. FINALLY, I WILL USE MT RECOVERY ASSAYS AFTER NOCODAZOLE WASHOUT TO DETERMINE WHETHER ABL2 LLPS IS REQUIRED FOR MT ASSEMBLY IN COS7 CELLS. AIM 2: ELUCIDATE THE IMPACT OF ABL2:TUBULIN BINDING AND COACERVATION ON MT POLYMERIZATION. I WILL DETERMINE WHETHER ELECTROSTATIC INTERACTIONS BETWEEN THE BASIC PATCHES IN THE ABL2 C-TERMINAL HALF AND THE ACIDIC TUBULIN TAILS MEDIATE ABL2:TUBULIN BINDING AND COACERVATION AND MT ASSEMBLY. I WILL USE BIOLAYER INTERFEROMETRY (BLI) AND MT ASSEMBLY ASSAYS WITH POINT-MUTATED ABL2 TO DETERMINE WHETHER BASIC RESIDUES WITHIN ABL2 MEDIATE TUBULIN BINDING AND HOW THIS INTERACTION MEDIATES MT ASSEMBLY. USING BLI AND IN VITRO PHASE SEPARATION ASSAYS, I WILL DETERMINE WHETHER ABL2 CAN COACERVATE WITH AND BIND TO TAIL-LESS TUBULIN. FINALLY, I WILL TEST WHETHER THIS INTERACTION IMPACTS MT ASSEMBLY IN COS7 CELLS USING MT RECOVERY ASSAYS AFTER NOCODAZOLE WASHOUT. AIM 3: DETERMINE HOW ABL2 C-TERMINAL HALF AFFECTS DENDRITE DEVELOPMENT IN NEURONS. IT IS UNCLEAR IF ABL2 PROMOTES MT ASSEMBLY IN DENDRITES AND HOW ABL2 BINDING TO AND COACERVATION WITH TUBULIN CONTRIBUTES TO THIS PROCESS. I WILL MEASURE MT RECOVERY AFTER NOCODAZOLE WASHOUT IN CONTROL AND ABL2 KNOCKDOWN (KD) CULTURED HIPPOCAMPAL NEURONS TO DETERMINE IF ABL2 IS REQUIRED FOR MT ASSEMBLY IN DENDRITES AND AXONS. I WILL ALSO RESCUE ABL2 KD NEURONS WITH MUTANTS WITH DEFINED ABL2:TUBULIN BINDING AND COACERVATION PROPERTIES TO TEST HOW THESE PROPERTIES CONTRIBUTE TO MT ASSEMBLY AND DENDRITIC AND AXONAL DEVELOPMENT IN NEURONS.

description: ELUCIDATING NEURON-ASTROCYTE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING ULTRASOUND STIMULATION FOR ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY NEURODEGENERATIVE CONDITIONS LIKE ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IMPOSE A GROWING PUBLIC HEALTH BURDEN, AFFECTING OVER SEVEN MILLION AMERICANS AND COSTING MORE THAN $360 BILLION ANNUALLY. AD IS CHARACTERIZED BY AMYLOID-BETA (AΒ) BUILDUP, NEURONAL HYPERACTIVITY, AND COGNITIVE DECLINE, BUT GROWING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT DISRUPTED COMMUNICATION BETWEEN NEURONS AND ASTROCYTES PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN DISEASE PROGRESSION. ASTROCYTES ARE ESSENTIAL FOR MAINTAINING SYNAPTIC AND CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS THROUGH TIGHTLY REGULATED CALCIUM (CA2+)- DEPENDENT SIGNALING. HOWEVER, IN AD, ABERRANT ASTROCYTE CA2+ WAVES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH NEURAL HYPEREXCITABILITY AND IMPAIRED NETWORK FUNCTION. ELUCIDATING WHETHER MODULATING THESE ABERRANT CA2+ WAVES CAN RESTORE CIRCUIT STABILITY AND DISRUPTED NEURON-ASTROCYTE COMMUNICATION REPRESENTS A PROMISING, YET UNDEREXPLORED, THERAPEUTIC AVENUE. THIS GAP IN NEURON-ASTROCYTE COMMUNICATION PRESENTS AN URGENT NEED FOR NOVEL APPROACHES TO MITIGATE DISEASE PROGRESSION. LOW-INTENSITY PULSED ULTRASOUND (LIPUS) HAS EMERGED AS A NON-INVASIVE NEUROMODULATION APPROACH CAPABLE OF INFLUENCING CELLULAR ACTIVITY THROUGH MECHANOSENSITIVE PATHWAYS, BUT ITS UNDERLYING MECHANISMS IN AD REMAIN UNCLEAR. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT LIPUS RESTORES HEALTHY NEURON-ASTROCYTE COMMUNICATION BY ACTIVATING ASTROCYTIC CA2+ SIGNALING TO REDUCE HIPPOCAMPAL HYPERACTIVITY AND IMPROVE COGNITION. THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH THE MECHANISTIC ROLE OF ASTROCYTE CA2+ IN MEDIATING THE THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS OF LIPUS AND ASSESSING ITS POTENTIAL TO AMELIORATE CIRCUIT DYSFUNCTION AND COGNITIVE DECLINE IN AD. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER ASTROCYTE CA2+ IS NECESSARY FOR LIPUS-INDUCED MODULATION OF NEURONAL HYPERACTIVITY IN THE HIPPOCAMPAL CA1 REGION OF APP/PS1 MICE. USING VIRAL VECTORS TO REDUCE ASTROCYTIC CA2+ (CALEX) COMBINED WITH IN VIVO ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, WE WILL RECORD SPONTANEOUS AND EVOKED NEURAL ACTIVITY DURING ONE MONTH OF LIPUS OR SHAM TREATMENT TO TEST WHETHER REDUCED ASTROCYTE CA2+ DIMINISHES LIPUS EFFICACY. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS THE LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF LIPUS ON NEURONAL AND ASTROCYTIC CA2+ DYNAMICS, AMYLOID PATHOLOGY, AND COGNITION. USING DUAL-COLOR FIBER PHOTOMETRY AND BEHAVIORAL ASSAYS (NOVEL OBJECT RECOGNITION AND BARNES MAZE), WE WILL EVALUATE WHETHER LIPUS NORMALIZES NEURON-ASTROCYTE CA2+ ACTIVITY, DECREASES AΒ PLAQUE LOAD, AND IMPROVES COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE RELATIVE TO SHAM OR GAMMA-ENTRAINMENT (GENUS) CONTROLS. ACHIEVING THESE AIMS WILL ESTABLISH ASTROCYTE CA2+ AS A KEY MECHANISTIC MEDIATOR OF LIPUS EFFICACY AND REVEAL HOW ULTRASOUND NEUROMODULATION RESTORES NEURAL CIRCUIT STABILITY IN AD. THROUGH MY TRAINING PLAN, MY SPONSOR AND CO-SPONSOR WILL PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE MENTORSHIP IN ULTRASOUND TECHNOLOGIES, ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, FIBER PHOTOMETRY, AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE MODELING. COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL EQUIP ME TO BRIDGE MECHANISTIC NEUROSCIENCE AND NEUROENGINEERING – DEVELOPING NEXT-GENERATION, NON-INVASIVE TECHNOLOGIES THAT TARGET NEUROGLIAL DYSFUNCTION TO IMPROVE OUTCOMES IN AD AND RELATED NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS.

description: LINKING STIMULATION PATTERN-DRIVEN AND CELL-SPECIFIC MYELINATION TO COGNITIVE OUTCOMES IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AFFECTS MILLIONS OF AMERICANS AND IS CHARACTERIZED BY EARLY MYELIN LOSS, CIRCUIT INSTABILITY, AND COGNITIVE DECLINE. MYELIN, PRODUCED BY OLIGODENDROCYTES, IS ESSENTIAL FOR MAINTAINING NEURAL CIRCUIT STABILITY, YET CURRENT NEUROMODULATION STRATEGIES FOCUS ALMOST EXCLUSIVELY ON NEURONAL ACTIVITY, OVERLOOKING HOW OLIGODENDROCYTES RESPOND TO STIMULATION. THIS PROJECT TESTS THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT DISTINCT PATTERNS OF BRAIN STIMULATION CAN DRIVE OLIGODENDROCYTE CALCIUM ACTIVITY TO PRODUCE SPECIFIC MYELINATION OUTCOMES, AND THAT TARGETING PARTICULAR NEURONAL SUBTYPES WILL DIFFERENTIALLY INFLUENCE MYELINATION AT THE CELL- SPECIFIC AND NETWORK LEVEL, WITH IMPLICATIONS FOR COGNITIVE FUNCTION. AIM 1 WILL DEFINE HOW INTRACORTICAL MICROSTIMULATION PATTERNS EVOKE OLIGODENDROCYTE CALCIUM DYNAMICS AND DRIVE PARADIGM-SPECIFIC MYELIN REMODELING IN VIVO. AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE WHETHER STIMULATING INHIBITORY OR EXCITATORY NEURONAL SUBTYPES ALTERS MYELINATION AT THE CELL AND NETWORK LEVEL AND HOW THESE CHANGES AFFECT COGNITION IN A MOUSE MODEL OF AD. BY INTEGRATING LONGITUDINAL IMAGING, ULTRASTRUCTURAL ANALYSIS, AND BEHAVIORAL ASSESSMENT, THIS RESEARCH WILL ELUCIDATE MECHANISMS LINKING NEURONAL ACTIVITY, MYELIN REMODELING, AND CIRCUIT FUNCTION, ESTABLISHING A FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE STRATEGIES TO PRESERVE COGNITIVE FUNCTION IN AD AND RELATED NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A MOTOR CORTICAL CIRCUIT FOR ONLINE REACHING CONTROL - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SKILLED FORELIMB CONTROL IS A DEFINING FEATURE OF HUMAN BEHAVIOR, ALLOWING US TO REACH FOR, GRASP, AND MANIPULATE OBJECTS IN THE WORLD WITH PRECISION AND INTENT. THIS CONTROL DEPENDS CRITICALLY ON MOTOR CORTEX AND IS DISRUPTED IN DISORDERS OF CORTICAL FUNCTION, SUCH AS STROKE OR TRAUMATIC INJURY. THEREFORE, THERE IS AN ESSENTIAL NEED TO UNDERSTAND THE ROLE OF MOTOR CORTEX IN SKILLED FORELIMB BEHAVIORS AND HOW ITS CONSTITUTIVE CELLULAR COMPONENTS ACHIEVE ITS CIRCUIT FUNCTION. REACHING CONTROL DEPENDS ON ONGOING SOMATOSENSORY FEEDBACK, AND RECORDINGS IN PRIMATES HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT MOTOR CORTEX RESPONDS RAPIDLY TO UNEXPECTED PROPRIOCEPTIVE DISTURBANCES DURING REACHING. FURTHER STUDIES HAVE HYPOTHESIZED THAT MOTOR CORTEX PRIORITIZES ONLY CERTAIN ASPECTS OF FEEDBACK BASED ON THEIR RELEVANCE FOR ACHIEVING OVERARCHING BEHAVIORAL GOALS. ACCORDINGLY, THESE STUDIES HAVE SUGGESTED THAT DURING REACH EXECUTION, MOTOR CORTEX PROVIDES FEEDBACK CONTROL TO UPDATE COMMANDS ONLINE, CORRECTING FEEDBACK ERRORS IN TASK-RELEVANT DIMENSIONS WHILE ALLOWING NATURAL VARIABILITY IN DIMENSIONS THAT DO NOT IMPACT BEHAVIORAL SUCCESS. HOWEVER, CAUSAL EVIDENCE FOR THIS HYPOTHESIS IS LACKING, AND VIRTUALLY NOTHING IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW THE CELL TYPES THAT COMPRISE MOTOR CORTEX ACHIEVE THIS FUNCTION. WE HAVE DEPLOYED AN ANALOGOUS SKILLED REACHING BEHAVIOR IN THE MOUSE AND IDENTIFIED A MOTOR CORTICAL NODE IN SECONDARY MOTOR CORTEX, MOS-C, UPON WHICH THIS BEHAVIOR DEPENDS. THUS, WE ESTABLISHED A GENETICALLY TRACTABLE SYSTEM TO UNCOVER THE CORTICAL CIRCUIT AND CELL-TYPE MECHANISMS THAT MAY UNDERLY REACHING CONTROL. MY OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS IS THAT MOS-C ACTS AS A FEEDBACK CONTROLLER FOR REACHING THAT MONITORS THE ONGOING HAND STATE FOR ONLINE REACHING REFINEMENT AND ENDPOINT PRECISION. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, I WILL PURSUE THE FOLLOWING AIMS. AIM 1 WILL INTERROGATE THE CONTROL RULES OF SKILLED REACHING VIA MECHANICAL LIMB PERTURBATIONS, AIM 2 WILL DELINEATE THE PATTERNS IN MOS-C POPULATION ACTIVITY THAT SUPPORT ONGOING REACHING CONTROL, AND AIM 3 WILL DISCOVER CELL-TYPE SPECIFIC NEURAL DYNAMICS IN MOS- C DURING ONLINE CONTROL. MY APPROACH INCLUDES QUANTITATIVE ANALYSES OF NOVEL BEHAVIORAL VARIANTS OF REACHING WITH PERTURBATIONS, TEMPORALLY PRECISE, CLOSED-LOOP CAUSAL MANIPULATIONS OF CORTICAL ACTIVITY WITH OPTOGENETICS, AND HIGH-DENSITY IN VIVO ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY RECORDINGS OF MARKER-DEFINED PROJECTION NEURON TYPES DURING BEHAVIOR. THESE STUDIES MAY REVEAL THE CELL TYPE AND NEURAL CIRCUIT MECHANISMS IN MOTOR CORTEX THAT EXERT ONLINE CONTROL OF A SKILLED, COMPLEX, MOTOR BEHAVIOR. MY SPONSOR, DR. Z. JOSH HUANG, PH.D., IS AN EXPERT IN THE ASSEMBLY AND FUNCTION OF MAMMALIAN CEREBRAL CORTICAL CIRCUITS. CONSISTENT WITH HIS LONG-ESTABLISHED TRACK RECORD OF MENTORSHIP, THE PROPOSED STUDIES AND TRAINING PLAN WILL PROVIDE ME WITH THE CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC AND PROFESSIONAL SKILLS FOR A FUTURE CAREER AS A NEUROLOGIST-SCIENTIST FOCUSED ON CIRCUIT MECHANISMS AND DISORDERS OF MOVEMENT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GLIOBLASTOMA-DERIVED GLUTAMATE DRIVES PRO-TUMORIGENIC REACTIVE ASTROCYTES - PROJECT SUMMARY: TUMOR-ASSOCIATED ASTROCYTES (TAAS) ARE A KEY COMPONENT OF THE GLIOBLASTOMA (GBM) TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT (TME) AND EXHIBIT A REACTIVE PHENOTYPE MARKED BY INCREASED PROLIFERATION AND COMPLEMENT COMPONENT 3 (C3) AND GLIAL FIBRILLARY ACIDIC PROTEIN (GFAP) EXPRESSION. TAAS PROVIDE CANCER CELLS WITH METABOLIC SUPPORT, ENHANCE TME IMMUNOSUPPRESSION, AND PROMOTE TREATMENT RESISTANCE. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS THAT DRIVE TAA REPROGRAMMING REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. PREVIOUS STUDIES SHOWED THAT GBM CELLS SECRETE SUPRAPHYSIOLOGICAL LEVELS OF GLUTAMATE INTO THE TME VIA THE CYSTINE-GLUTAMATE ANTIPORTER, SLC7A11. FURTHERMORE, GLUTAMATE SIGNALING ENHANCES GBM CELL INVASION AND PROLIFERATION. HOWEVER, THE POTENTIAL ROLE OF GLUTAMATE IN RESHAPING THE TME REMAINS UNEXPLORED. ASTROCYTES ARE CRITICAL REGULATORS OF GLUTAMATERGIC HOMEOSTASIS IN THE BRAIN. THEY EXPRESS A RANGE OF GLUTAMATE TRANSPORTERS, RECEPTORS, AND METABOLIC ENZYMES, POSITIONING TAAS AS A NEXUS OF ABERRANT GLUTAMATE SIGNALING IN GBM. IN PRELIMINARY EXPERIMENTS, I FOUND THAT GLUTAMATE TREATMENTS, AT LEVELS FOUND IN PATIENT TUMORS, INCREASES ASTROCYTE PROLIFERATION AND UPREGULATES GFAP AND C3, WHICH HAS EMERGED AS A PRO-TUMORIGENIC SIGNAL THAT INCREASES GBM CELL STEMNESS AND IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE PROGRAMMING IN MYELOID CELLS. MOUSE AND PATIENT-DERIVED GBM CELL MODELS SECRETE VARYING LEVELS OF GLUTAMATE DEPENDING ON SLC7A11 EXPRESSION. CONDITIONED MEDIA (CM) FROM GBM CELL LINES THAT SECRETE HIGH LEVELS OF GLUTAMATE MORE ROBUSTLY INDUCE C3 AND GFAP EXPRESSION AND PROLIFERATION THAN THOSE WITH LOWER GLUTAMATE SECRETION. THIS EFFECT IS MITIGATED BY PHARMACOLOGICAL OR GENETIC SLC7A11 INHIBITION. MOREOVER, CO-IMPLANTATION OF GBM CELLS WITH ASTROCYTES ACCELERATED TUMORIGENESIS, WHILE C3 KNOCKOUT MICE EXHIBITED EXTENDED GBM SURVIVAL COMPARED TO WILD-TYPE CONTROLS. CM FROM ASTROCYTES STIMULATED WITH GLUTAMATE OR SUPERNATANTS FROM HIGH- BUT NOT LOW- GLUTAMATE -SECRETING GBM CELL LINES POTENTIATED GBM CELL PROLIFERATION. FINALLY, SLC7A11 EXPRESSION CORRELATES WITH C3 AND GFAP EXPRESSION IN GBM PATIENTS. THUS, MY CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT SLC7A11-MEDIATED GLUTAMATE SECRETION REPROGRAMS TAAS, WHICH PROMOTE GBM VIA UPREGULATION OF C3. AIM 1 WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT GLUTAMATERGIC ACTIVATION OF ASTROCYTES PROMOTES GBM VIA SECRETION OF C3. I WILL EVALUATE WHETHER GLUTAMATERGIC ACTIVATION OF ASTROCYTES PROMOTES TUMORIGENESIS VIA CO-IMPLANTATION OF WT VERSUS C3 KO ASTROCYTES WITH CANCER CELLS. I WILL ALSO INTERROGATE THE ROLE OF ASTROCYTE-DERIVED C3 IN PROMOTING CANCER CELL PROLIFERATION AND STEMNESS. AIM 2 WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT GBM CELLS DRIVE REACTIVE TAA PROGRAMMING VIA SLC7A11-DEPENDENT GLUTAMATE SECRETION. I WILL GENETICALLY MODULATE SLC7A11 IN GBM CELLS TO DETERMINE THE ROLE OF CANCER CELL-DERIVED GLUTAMATE ON REACTIVE ASTROCYTE CYTOKINE EXPRESSION, MORPHOLOGY, PROLIFERATION, AND EXPRESSION PROFILE. I WILL ALSO EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF SLC7A11 INHIBITION ON SURVIVAL AND TME REPROGRAMMING. COLLECTIVELY, THESE STUDIES WILL DEFINE THE ROLE OF SLC7A11-DEPENDENT GLUTAMATE SIGNALING IN TAA REPROGRAMMING AND IDENTIFY C3, AND SLC7A11 AS POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS TO DISRUPT GBM-TME INTERACTIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DETERMINING A MECHANISM FOR TGF-BETA-ACTIVATED KINASE 1 (TAK1) REGULATION OF NEMO-LIKE KINASE (NLK) IN SPINOCEREBELLAR ATAXIA TYPE 1 (SCA1) - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SPINOCEREBELLAR ATAXIA TYPE 1 (SCA1) IS A GENETIC NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER WITH NO THERAPEUTIC OPTIONS. IT IS CAUSED BY A CAG TRINUCLEOTIDE REPEAT EXPANSION IN THE ATXN1 GENE. THE MUTANT ATAXIN-1 PROTEIN FORMS AGGREGATES THAT RESULT IN LOSS OF NEURAL CELL HEALTH, PARTICULARLY IN CEREBELLAR PURKINJE CELLS (PCS). OUR LAB HAS IDENTIFIED NEMO-LIKE KINASE (NLK) AS AN ATAXIN-1 PHOSPHORYLATOR. AFTER CROSSING NLK+/- MICE WITH THE ATXN1154Q/2Q KNOCK-IN (SCA1-KI) MODEL, WE FOUND THAT REDUCTION OF NLK SIGNALING IMPROVES SCA1 BEHAVIORAL AND HISTOPATHOLOGICAL PHENOTYPES, NAMELY RESTORING MOTOR FUNCTION AND PC MOLECULAR LAYER INTEGRITY. FURTHERMORE, WE HAVE ALSO IDENTIFIED NLK AS A NEGATIVE REGULATOR OF LYSOSOMAL FUNCTION IN VITRO AND IN VIVO, SUCH THAT REDUCTION OF NLK PROMOTES LYSOSOMAL CLEARANCE OF PATHOGENIC AGGREGATES IN RELEVANT TISSUES IN A MOUSE MODEL OF ANOTHER NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE. THOUGH NLK APPEARS TO BE A PROMISING THERAPEUTIC TARGET IN SCA1, A LACK OF UNDERSTANDING OF NLK STRUCTURE AND INHIBITING SMALL MOLECULES IMPEDES DEVELOPMENT OF NLK- TARGETING THERAPIES. THEREFORE, IT IS CRITICAL TO DETERMINE WHETHER DRUGGABLE PROTEINS WITHIN THE NLK PATHWAY ALSO EXERT DISEASE-MODIFYING EFFECTS AND IDENTIFY A NOVEL SCA1 THERAPEUTIC TARGET FOR FURTHER DEVELOPMENT. TRANSFORMING GROWTH FACTOR-Β-ACTIVATED KINASE 1 (TAK1) IS A DRUGGABLE UPSTREAM REGULATOR OF NLK, BUT ITS ABILITY TO MODIFY SCA1 HAS NOT YET BEEN TESTED. WE PROPOSE THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT TAK1 REGULATES NLK TO MAINTAIN LYSOSOMAL HEALTH AND THAT TARGETING THIS INTERACTION CAN MODULATE SCA1 DISEASE PROGRESSION. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL CARRY OUT TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. IN SPECIFIC AIM 1, WE WILL CROSS THE SCA1-KI MODEL WITH TAK1FLOX/FLOX AND NESTIN-CRE ANIMALS, RESULTING IN SCA1-TAK1-/- MICE WITH A CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM-SPECIFIC DELETION OF TAK1. WE WILL ASSESS WHETHER THIS MODEL RECAPITULATES THE PROTECTIVE BEHAVIORAL AND CELLULAR-LEVEL EFFECTS OF DELETING A COPY OF NLK. IN SPECIFIC AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER MODULATING TAK1 SIGNALING, IN IMMORTALIZED CELLS AND NEURONS DERIVED FROM SCA1 PATIENT STEM CELLS, IMPACTS ONE OR BOTH OF NLK’S REPORTED DOWNSTREAM EFFECTS – MODULATION OF LYSOSOMAL FUNCTION OR DIRECT PHOSPHORYLATION OF ATAXIN-1. WE WILL ASSESS PROTEIN AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL MARKERS OF LYSOSOMAL FUNCTION AND ATAXIN-1 AGGREGATE SIZE AND MORPHOLOGY TO TEASE THIS APART. COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS WILL ALLOW FOR PRIORITIZATION OF A NOVEL SCA1 THERAPEUTIC TARGET FOR FURTHER DEVELOPMENT. FURTHERMORE, IT WILL ELUCIDATE PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN NLK SIGNALING MECHANISMS AND DETERMINE IF LYSOSOMAL HEALTH IS A RELEVANT PROCESS TO EXPLORE FURTHER IN SCA1. THIS PROJECT WILL BE COMPLETED IN DR. JANGHOO LIM’S LAB IN THE YALE DEPARTMENTS OF GENETICS AND NEUROSCIENCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PKA SPATIOTEMPORAL DYNAMICS DRIVE AUTOPHAGY AND MITOCHONDRIAL PHENOTYPES IN CELLULAR SENESCENCE - PROJECT SUMMARY THIS PROJECT WILL INVESTIGATE HOW COMPARTMENTALIZED PROTEIN KINASE A (PKA) SIGNALING DYNAMICS INFLUENCE THE INDUCTION AND HETEROGENEITY OF SENESCENT CELL FATES. USING LIVE-CELL BIOSENSORS, HIGH-THROUGHPUT TIME-LAPSE IMAGING, AND MACHINE LEARNING–BASED SINGLE-CELL ANALYSIS, THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL CHARACTERIZE SUBCELLULAR PKA ACTIVITY TRAJECTORIES IN RESPONSE TO SENESCENCE-INDUCING STIMULI AND IDENTIFY PREDICTIVE FEATURES OF CELLULAR AGING. INSIGHTS GAINED WILL PROVIDE A MECHANISTIC FRAMEWORK FOR UNDERSTANDING HOW DYNAMIC SIGNALING INPUTS SHAPE SENESCENT PHENOTYPES AND MAY UNCOVER TARGETS FOR SELECTIVE SENESCENCE MODULATION. THE FELLOWSHIP TRAINING PLAN EMPHASIZES DEVELOPMENT OF COMPUTATIONAL MODELING, MACHINE LEARNING, AND SINGLE- CELL BIOINFORMATICS SKILLS, ALONGSIDE CONTINUED GROWTH IN EXPERIMENTAL CELL BIOLOGY AND QUANTITATIVE IMAGING. TRAINING ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE COURSEWORK, MENTORED RESEARCH, STRUCTURED CAREER DEVELOPMENT, AND PARTICIPATION IN INTERDISCIPLINARY SEMINARS AND JOURNAL CLUBS. RESEARCH AND TRAINING WILL BE CONDUCTED IN THE LABORATORY OF DR. NAN HAO AT UC SAN DIEGO, A LEADING CENTER FOR SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND AGING RESEARCH. THE TRAINING ENVIRONMENT INCLUDES ACCESS TO STATE-OF-THE-ART IMAGING AND COMPUTATIONAL RESOURCES, CO-MENTORSHIP BY EXPERTS IN AGING AND TRANSCRIPTOMICS, AND PARTICIPATION IN COLLABORATIVE NETWORKS THROUGH THE SAN DIEGO NATHAN SHOCK CENTER AND REGIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EMOTION REGULATION AS A POTENTIAL TARGET FOR CAREGIVER HEALTH INTERVENTIONS: A LONGITUDINAL, MULTILEVEL INVESTIGATION INTO BIOBEHAVIORAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN EMOTION REGULATION AND HEALTH IN DEMENTIA - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CARING FOR A LOVED ONE WITH ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (AD/ADRD) IS OFTEN ASSOCIATED WITH RISKS OF PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS AND CHRONIC, LOW-GRADE INFLAMMATION, WHICH IS A SIGNIFICANT PREDICTOR OF PREMATURE AGING AND MORTALITY. EMOTION REGULATION, THE ABILITY TO MODIFY OUR EMOTIONAL REACTIONS AND EXPERIENCES, IS A POTENTIALLY SIGNIFICANT BUFFER AGAINST THE ADVERSE HEALTH EFFECTS OF CAREGIVING STRESS, AS IT IS ASSOCIATED WITH NUMEROUS HEALTH (E.G., INFLAMMATION, SPECIFICALLY THE INTERLEUKIN-6 PROINFLAMMATORY CYTOKINE) AND WELL-BEING (E.G., AFFECT, OR EMOTIONS) OUTCOMES. EMOTION REGULATION STRATEGIES, SUCH AS STRATEGIES THAT ENGAGE OR DISENGAGE WITH THE STRESSOR, INTERACT WITH STRESSOR CHARACTERISTICS, SUCH AS SEVERITY OR FREQUENCY, TO DETERMINE WELL-BEING OUTCOMES. HOWEVER, THERE IS LIMITED RESEARCH ON HOW EMOTION RESPONSES TO STRESS IMPACT AD/ADRD CAREGIVER HEALTH, THEREBY LIMITING THE EFFICACY OF CURRENT CAREGIVER SUPPORT PROGRAMS. THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL SEEK TO IDENTIFY POINTS OF INTERVENTION THAT REDUCE AD/ADRD CAREGIVER HEALTH RISKS IN WAYS THAT ARE EFFECTIVE AND ACCESSIBLE. TOWARD THIS END, THE PROPOSED RESEARCH PROJECT INVESTIGATES HOW SPOUSAL CAREGIVERS OF PERSONS WITH AD/ADRD ENGAGE IN EMOTION REGULATION IN RESPONSE TO REAL-WORLD SITUATIONS AND HOW THIS IS RELATED TO CAREGIVER QUALITY OF LIFE, NEGATIVE AFFECT, AND INFLAMMATION. UNDERSTANDING THE INTERACTIVE EFFECTS OF STRATEGIES AND STRESS CHARACTERISTICS IN AD/ADRD CAREGIVERS THROUGH RIGOROUS AND REPRODUCIBLE METHODOLOGIES IS AN INNOVATIVE APPROACH WHICH CAN SHED LIGHT ON THE PREDICTORS UNDERLYING CAREGIVER RISKS, THEREBY POTENTIALLY REVEALING TARGETABLE POINTS OF INTERVENTION. INCREASINGLY PERSONALIZED EMOTION REGULATION INTERVENTIONS COULD SIGNIFICANTLY ALLEVIATE THE ADVERSE EFFECTS OF EMOTION DYSREGULATION ON IMMUNOLOGICAL FUNCTIONING IN AD/ADRD CAREGIVERS. SPECIFIC AIMS: AIMS: (1) INVESTIGATE HOW THE USE OF TWO COMMONLY ASSESSED TYPES OF EMOTION REGULATION STRATEGIES (ENGAGEMENT-ORIENTED VS. DISENGAGEMENT-ORIENTED) IMPACT AD/ADRD SPOUSAL CAREGIVERS' DAILY EMOTIONAL EXPERIENCES IN RELATION TO STRESS; (2) INVESTIGATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN TRAIT-LIKE EMOTION REGULATION STRATEGY USE, INFLAMMATION, AND QUALITY OF LIFE AT T1 (BASELINE) AND T2 (6 MONTHS POST-BASELINE) AND WHETHER THESE RELATIONSHIPS DEPEND UPON STRESS DURING THE 14-DAY ECOLOGICAL MOMENTARY ASSESSMENT (EMA). HYPOTHESES ARE DETAILED IN THE RESEARCH STRATEGY DOCUMENT. STUDY DESIGN: CONCURRENT WITH A FUNDED R01 PARENT GRANT (RF1AG075946), 144 AD/ADRD SPOUSAL CAREGIVERS WILL BE ASSESSED DURING THE T1 BASELINE VISIT, WHERE I WILL MEASURE TRAIT-LIKE EMOTION REGULATION, QUALITY OF LIFE, AND INFLAMMATION VIA CIRCULATORY PROINFLAMMATORY MARKERS (I.E., INTERLEUKIN-6) FROM A BLOOD DRAW; A 13-DAY EMA MEASURING MOMENTARY AFFECT AND STRESS; AND A T2 6-MONTH FOLLOW-UP MEASURING THE SAME VARIABLES AS MEASURED AT T1.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THOUGHT AS A HEALTH MARKER: LINKING DYNAMICS OF SELF-GENERATED THOUGHTS AND NEURAL HEALTH IN AGING - PROJECT SUMMARY THE FLOW OF HUMAN THOUGHT—HOW IDEAS LINGER, SHIFT, AND EVOLVE—PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN MENTAL HEALTH AND WELL- BEING. FLEXIBLE THOUGHT TRANSITIONS SUPPORT ADAPTIVE EMOTION REGULATION AND GOAL PURSUIT, WHEREAS RIGID OR ERRATIC PATTERNS ARE LINKED TO AFFECTIVE AND COGNITIVE DYSFUNCTION. DESPITE WELL-DOCUMENTED AGE-RELATED CHANGES IN COGNITION, AFFECT, AND NEURAL FLEXIBILITY, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW THOUGHT DYNAMICS EVOLVE ACROSS THE ADULT LIFESPAN OR HOW THEY INTERACT WITH MENTAL WELL-BEING IN OLDER ADULTHOOD. THIS PROJECT INVESTIGATES AGE-RELATED DIFFERENCES IN THE DYNAMICS OF SELF-GENERATED THOUGHT THROUGH TWO COMPLEMENTARY STUDIES LEVERAGING AN EXISTING DATASET INCLUDING 162 OLDER AND 61 YOUNGER, COGNITIVELY UNIMPAIRED, ADULTS WHO VERBALIZED THEIR ONGOING THOUGHTS IN THE SCANNER USING A VALIDATED THINK-ALOUD PARADIGM. STUDY 1 CHARACTERIZES AGE-RELATED BEHAVIORAL DIFFERENCES IN THOUGHT DYNAMICS USING BOTH DISCRETE (TOPIC BOUNDARIES) AND CONTINUOUS (LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL–BASED PERPLEXITY) MEASURES. STUDY 1 WILL ALSO EXPLORE HOW THE UNFOLDING OF THOUGHTS INTERACTS WITH EMOTIONAL VALENCE, LINKING VALENCE-RELATED THOUGHT DYNAMICS WITH THE WELL-DOCUMENTED POSITIVITY BIAS IN AGING. THIS STUDY AIMS TO IDENTIFY BEHAVIORAL SIGNATURES OF ADAPTIVE VERSUS MALADAPTIVE THOUGHT PATTERNS THAT MAY PRECEDE CLINICALLY DIAGNOSED COGNITIVE DECLINE OR EMOTIONAL DYSREGULATION. STUDY 2 EXAMINES THE NEURAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THOUGHT TRANSITIONS ACROSS AGE GROUPS, TESTING WHETHER BRAIN AGING ALTERS THE NEURAL ARCHITECTURES SUPPORTING DYNAMIC THOUGHTS. TO FURTHER EXPLORE A MECHANISTIC LINK BETWEEN STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL CHANGE, A MEDIATION ANALYSIS WILL TEST WHETHER AGE-RELATED DIFFERENCES IN BRAIN CIRCUIT RECRUITMENT ARE ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY OF THE HIPPOCAMPUS. BY DELINEATING HOW AGING ALTERS THE NEURAL CIRCUITS SUPPORTING THE THOUGHT FLOW, THE RESULTS WILL PROVIDE A MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF HOW SELF-GENERATED THOUGHT REFLECTS NEURAL HEALTH IN OLDER ADULTS. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL ADVANCE THE “THOUGHT-AS-A-HEALTH-MARKER” FRAMEWORK WITH IMPLICATIONS IN PRECLINICAL DIAGNOSIS AND INTERVENTIONS. THE FELLOWSHIP PROVIDES ADVANCED TRAINING IN MRI ANALYSIS USING STATE-OF-THE-ART TOOLBOXES AND COMPUTATIONAL METHODS, AS WELL AS THEORETICAL GROUNDING IN AGING NEUROSCIENCE UNDER THE EXPERT MENTORSHIP OF THE SPONSORS. THE TRAINING WILL TAKE PLACE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA, AN INTERDISCIPLINARY ENVIRONMENT WITH RENOWNED EXPERTISE IN AGING RESEARCH, EQUIPPED WITH CUTTING-EDGE IMAGING FACILITIES AND COMPUTATIONAL INFRASTRUCTURE. THUS, THE PROPOSED RESEARCH AND TRAINING WILL PREPARE THE APPLICANT FOR AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM THAT INTEGRATES COMPUTATIONAL AND COGNITIVE NEUROSCIENCE TO STUDY SELF-GENERATED THOUGHTS WITH PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS TO PROMOTE MENTAL WELL-BEING IN OLDER ADULTHOOD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ACCESS, UTILIZATION, AND OUTCOMES OF SURGERY UNDER MEDICARE ADVANTAGE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  MEDICARE ADVANTAGE (MA) NOW INSURES MORE THAN HALF OF ALL MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES, YET ITS IMPLICATIONS FOR SURGICAL CARE DELIVERY REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. COMPARED TO TRADITIONAL MEDICARE (TM), MA PLANS IMPOSE ADDITIONAL CONSTRAINTS ON SITE-OF-CARE DECISIONS THROUGH NARROWER PROVIDER NETWORKS, PRIOR AUTHORIZATION REQUIREMENTS, AND COVERAGE DENIALS. THESE PLAN DESIGN FEATURES MAY SHAPE ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY SURGICAL CARE AND INFLUENCE POSTOPERATIVE OUTCOMES. SURGERY IN OLDER ADULTS IS ESPECIALLY HIGH STAKES GIVEN THEIR COMORBIDITY BURDEN, LIMITED PHYSIOLOGICAL RESERVE, AND FRAILTY, MAKING DECISIONS ABOUT WHERE AND HOW SURGERY IS DELIVERED PARTICULARLY CONSEQUENTIAL.  THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL INVESTIGATE HOW MA PLAN DESIGN AFFECTS SURGICAL CARE ACCESS, UTILIZATION, AND OUTCOMES FOR OLDER ADULTS THROUGH THREE AIMS: (1) ASSESS WHETHER MA BENEFICIARIES ARE LESS LIKELY THAN TM BENEFICIARIES TO UNDERGO HIGH-RISK OPERATIONS AT HIGH-VOLUME HOSPITALS AND WHETHER THIS AFFECTS OUTCOMES; (2) COMPARE MA AND TM BENEFICIARIES IN TERMS OF ACCESS TO AMBULATORY SURGICAL CENTERS, TRENDS IN OUTPATIENT UTILIZATION, AND ASSOCIATED OUTCOMES FOR ESTABLISHED OUTPATIENT-ELIGIBLE OPERATIONS; AND (3) EVALUATE DIFFERENCES IN HOW MA AND TM BENEFICIARIES RESPOND TO THE PHASED REMOVAL OF OPERATIONS FROM MEDICARE'S INPATIENT ONLY (IPO) LIST. USING NATIONWIDE TM CLAIMS AND MA ENCOUNTER DATA, AIMS 1 AND 2 WILL APPLY CAUSAL INFERENCE METHODS, INCLUDING ENTROPY BALANCING AND FIXED-EFFECTS, TO REGRESSION MODELING; AIM 3 WILL USE QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES, INCLUDING INTERRUPTED TIME SERIES AND DIFFERENCE-IN-DIFFERENCES ANALYSES, TO EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF IPO LIST CHANGES. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT MA BENEFICIARIES MAY BE STEERED TOWARD LOWER-COST SURGICAL SETTINGS BY PLAN-LEVEL INCENTIVES, WITH POTENTIAL CONSEQUENCES FOR SAFETY AND OUTCOMES. THIS WORK CLOSELY ALIGNS WITH THE MISSION OF THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE ON AGING BY ADDRESSING POLICY-RELEVANT QUESTIONS ABOUT HOW INSURANCE DESIGN AFFECTS SAFETY AND DELIVERY OF SURGICAL CARE FOR OLDER ADULTS.  THE RESEARCH WILL BE CONDUCTED AT THE HEALTHCARE QUALITY AND OUTCOMES LAB AT HARVARD T.H. CHAN SCHOOL OF PUBLIC HEALTH (HSPH) AND THE CENTER FOR SURGERY AND PUBLIC HEALTH AT BRIGHAM AND WOMEN'S HOSPITAL. DR. JULIA SONG WILL BE JOINTLY MENTORED BY DRS. THOMAS TSAI, MD, MPH, JOSE FIGUEROA, MD, MPH AND MELISSA GARRIDO, PHD, A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM OF CLINICAL INVESTIGATORS AND HEALTH ECONOMISTS WITH COMPLEMENTARY QUANTITATIVE RESEARCH EXPERTISE IN MEDICARE POLICY, AGING, AND SURGICAL OUTCOMES. THE TRAINING PLAN INCLUDES COURSEWORK IN LONGITUDINAL AND CAUSAL INFERENCE METHODS AS DR. SONG PURSUES A MASTER OF PUBLIC HEALTH IN HSPH'S QUANTITATIVE METHODS PROGRAM, MENTORED RESEARCH USING LARGE-SCALE MEDICARE DATA, AND STRUCTURED CAREER DEVELOPMENT. TOGETHER, THIS RESEARCH AND TRAINING WILL PREPARE DR. SONG FOR A CAREER AS AN INDEPENDENT SURGEON-SCIENTIST FOCUSED ON IMPROVING SURGICAL CARE DELIVERY FOR OLDER ADULTS THROUGH DATA-DRIVEN HEALTH POLICY RESEARCH.
