description: THE ROLE OF SEX IN THE GENETICS OF BRAIN GENE REGULATION AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE RISK - PROJECT SUMMARY ALZHEIMER’S (AD) AND PARKINSON’S (PD) DISEASES ARE THE TWO MOST COMMON NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES IN THE UNITED STATES, AFFECTING ~7.2 AND 1.1 MILLION AMERICANS RESPECTIVELY, WITH PREVALENCE RISING AS THE POPULATION AGES. TOGETHER, AD AND PD POSE MAJOR INDIVIDUAL, FAMILIAL, SOCIETAL, AND ECONOMIC BURDENS, EXCEEDING $400 BILLION ANNUALLY. BOTH DISEASES EXHIBIT SEX DIFFERENCES IN PREVALENCE (TWO-THIRDS OF AD CASES ARE WOMEN WHILE MEN ARE 1.5 TIMES MORE LIKELY TO DEVELOP PD), CLINICAL COURSE, AND TREATMENT RESPONSE. IDENTIFYING THE GENETIC MECHANISMS DRIVING THESE SEX DIFFERENCES MAY INFORM INDIVIDUALIZED PREVENTION AND TREATMENT. GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDIES (GWAS) DETECT GENETIC VARIANTS ASSOCIATED WITH COMPLEX DISEASES, SUCH AS AD AND PD; HOWEVER, MOST LIE IN NON-CODING REGIONS OF THE GENOME. INTEGRATING GWAS WITH EXPRESSION QUANTITATIVE TRAIT LOCI (EQTL) THAT IDENTIFY GENETIC VARIANTS ASSOCIATED WITH GENE EXPRESSION LEVELS, PROVIDE BIOLOGICAL INSIGHT TO HOW GENETIC REGULATION SHAPES SEX DIFFERENCES IN BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS. ADDITIONALLY, SOME VARIANTS EXERT SEX DIFFERENTIATED REGULATORY EFFECTS (SEX-BIASED EQTLS), WHICH CAN REVEAL GENES WHOSE EXPRESSION CONTRIBUTES DIFFERENTLY TO DISEASE IN MEN AND WOMEN. AD AND PD ARE HIGHLY HETEROGENEOUS, WITH SEX-SPECIFIC COMORBIDITIES THAT COMPLICATE DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT. IDENTIFYING SEX-SPECIFIC CO-OCCURRING CONDITIONS THAT SHAPE HOW NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES PRESENT AND PROGRESS WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO BIOLOGICAL AND CLINICAL PATHWAYS THAT DIFFER BETWEEN MEN AND WOMEN AND MAY IMPROVE INTERVENTION STRATEGIES. THE GOAL OF MY PROJECT IS TWO-FOLD: (1) DISCOVER SEX-BIASED GENE REGULATION IN BRAIN TISSUE THAT INFLUENCES SEX DIFFERENCES IN AD AND PD; (2) REVEAL SEX DIFFERENCES IN TRAIT ASSOCIATIONS WITH THE GENETIC RISK FOR AD AND PD. FIRST, I WILL COMBINE EXISTING BRAIN EQTL DATASETS IN A LARGE META-ANALYSIS TO INCREASE STATISTICAL POWER IN THREE WAYS: (1) SEX-COMBINED, (2) SEX-STRATIFIED (MALES AND FEMALES SEPARATED), AND (3) SEX-INTERACTION TO EVALUATE SEX-DIFFERENTIATED EFFECTS. I WILL INTEGRATE SEX- BIASED EQTLS WITH GWAS DATA FROM AD AND PD TO IDENTIFY GENETIC VARIANTS THAT INFLUENCE BOTH GENE EXPRESSION AND PHENOTYPE. TOGETHER, THIS WILL ALLOW ME TO DETECT GENETIC EFFECTS ON GENE REGULATION IN THE BRAIN THAT CONTRIBUTE TO AD AND PD IN A SEX-DIFFERENTIATED MANNER. SECOND, I WILL QUANTIFY ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN AD AND PD GENETIC RISK AND ALL OTHER MEASURED PHENOTYPES IN THE ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD TO ASSESS SEX DIFFERENCES IN DISEASE COMORBIDITIES. THE RESULTS WILL ALLOW ME TO DETERMINE IF AD AND PD DISEASE RISK IS LINKED TO SPECIFIC HEALTH TRAITS IN MEN AND WOMEN, REVEALING SEX-DIFFERENTIATED BIOLOGICAL DISEASE MECHANISMS. TOGETHER, THIS WORK WILL ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW SEX INFLUENCES AD AND PD GENETIC RISK AND DISEASE MANIFESTATION, INFORMING FUTURE SEX- AWARE PRECISION MEDICINE.

description: GAIT AND BALANCE IN PARKINSON’S DISEASE AND RAPID EYE MOVEMENT SLEEP BEHAVIOR DISORDER - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT RAPID EYE MOVEMENT (REM) SLEEP BEHAVIOR DISORDER (RBD) IS A SLEEP DISORDER IN WHICH INDIVIDUALS PHYSICALLY ACT OUT THEIR VIVID DREAMS DURING REM SLEEP. RBD IS RECOGNIZED AS THE STRONGEST PREDICTOR OF PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD) AND IS PRESENT IN APPROXIMATELY 50% OF INDIVIDUALS WITH PD. HOWEVER, RELATIVELY LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THE EFFECT OF RBD ON PD MOTOR SYMPTOMS. NEUROMELANIN-SENSITIVE IMAGING (NM-MRI) IS A PROMISING TOOL TO ASSESS BRAINSTEM NEURODEGENERATION IN PD. THIS IMAGING APPROACH IS NON-INVASIVE AND CAN DIRECTLY VISUALIZE BRAINSTEM STRUCTURES SUCH AS THE SUBSTANTIA NIGRA AND LOCUS COERULEUS (VIA CATECHOLAMINERGIC NEURONS). BOTH REGIONS ARE THOUGHT TO PLAY A KEY ROLE IN RBD PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND THE NEURAL MECHANISM UNDERLYING MOBILITY. THE GOALS OF THIS F32 PROPOSAL ARE TO ASSESS THE FUNCTIONAL RELEVANCE AND NEURAL MECHANISMS OF RBD-RELATED DEFICITS IN PD. SPECIFICALLY, WE PROPOSE TO 1) ASSESS THE IMPACTS OF RBD ON GAIT, QUIET STANDING SWAY (STATIC BALANCE) AND REACTIVE STEPPING (REACTIVE BALANCE), IMPROVING KNOWLEDGE OF FALL-RISK IN PEOPLE WITH RBD, AND 2) DETERMINE HOW THE BRAINSTEM STRUCTURES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH I) MOBILITY AND II) RBD SEVERITY. THERE ARE THREE INDEPENDENT AIMS WITHIN THIS PROPOSAL. AIM 1 WILL ASSESS IF THERE ARE GAIT, QUIET STANDING SWAY AND REACTIVE STEPPING DEFICITS IN PD WITH RBD (PD+RBD) COMPARED WITH PD WITHOUT RBD (PD- RBD). AIM 2 WILL ASSESS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN NM-MRI AND GAIT, REACTIVE STEPPING, AND QUIET STANDING SWAY IN PD. AIM 3 WILL ASSESS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN NM-MRI AND RBD SEVERITY IN PD. MY LONG-TERM CAREER GOAL IS TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCHER AND LEADER IN PD AND RBD RESEARCH. THE PROPOSED STUDY BUILDS ON MY PREVIOUS FORCE CONTROL, TASK-BASED FUNCTIONAL MRI AND FREE-WATER DIFFUSION IMAGING RESEARCH IN ISOLATED RBD AND EARLY-STAGE PD BY ADDING NEW SKILLS IN 1) BIOMECHANICS OF GAIT, BALANCE, AND FALLS, 2) NM-MRI, AND 3) CLINICAL EXPERIENCE IN PD WITH AND WITHOUT RBD. I PROPOSE A RIGOROUS TRAINING PROGRAM WITH ADVANCED COURSEWORK IN BIOMECHANICS, BIOSTATISTICS, AND RESPONSIBLE CONDUCT OF RESEARCH, AS WELL AS TRAINING IN NM-MRI, RESEARCH DESIGN AND EXECUTION, CLINICAL TRIALS, LEADERSHIP, AND SCIENTIFIC COMMUNICATION SKILLS. TOGETHER, THE ASSEMBLED MENTORSHIP TEAM WILL HELP ME CONDUCT MENTORED RESEARCH IN 1) BIOMECHANICS OF GAIT AND BALANCE WHICH IS IMPORTANT FOR CHARACTERIZING GAIT AND BALANCE IN THE PD+RBD PHENOTYPE, 2) ADVANCE NEUROIMAGING TECHNIQUES IMPORTANT FOR UNDERSTANDING NEURAL MECHANISMS OF MOBILITY AND RBD SYMPTOMS IN PD, AND 3) CLINICAL EXPERIENCE WITH PATIENTS WITH PD WITH AND WITHOUT RBD WHICH WILL HELP ME DEVELOP A MORE INTEGRATED UNDERSTANDING OF THESE DISEASES, ITS TREATMENTS AND DEVELOP RESEARCH QUESTIONS WITH A STRONGER CLINICAL RELEVANCE.

description: DEFINING THE LINKS BETWEEN PERTURBED MITOCHONDRIAL MASS HOMEOSTASIS AND AGING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT MITOCHONDRIA ARE BIOSYNTHETIC SIGNALING HUBS CORE TO HUMAN HEALTH, AND THEIR DYSFUNCTION HAS LONG BEEN ASSOCIATED WITH AGING AND DEVELOPMENT OF AGE-RELATED DISEASES. OFTEN OBSERVED IN AGING AND DISEASE IS DISRUPTED MITOCHONDRIAL MASS HOMEOSTASIS (I.E., AN INAPPROPRIATE ACCUMULATION OR LOSS OF MITOCHONDRIA). DESPITE THIS, THE DIRECT CONSEQUENCES OF DISRUPTED MITOCHONDRIAL MASS ON AGING AND OTHER FUNDAMENTAL CELLULAR PROCESSES REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS APPLICATION IS TO DELINEATE HOW CELLS AND ANIMALS SENSE, REACT TO, AND ABSOLVE STATES OF ABERRANT MITOCHONDRIAL MASS. THE RATIONALE IS THAT IN NORMAL AGING AND IN AGE-RELATED DISEASE, SUCH AS PARKINSON’S DISEASE AND SARCOPENIA, THE AMOUNT OF MITOCHONDRIA PRESENT WITHIN TISSUES BECOMES DYSREGULATED. THUS, IT IS PARAMOUNT TO UNDERSTAND HOW CHANGES TO MITOCHONDRIAL MASS IMPACTS CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS BOTH IN NORMAL PHYSIOLOGICAL AND AGING CONTEXTS. A MAJOR BARRIER TO OUR UNDERSTANDING IN THIS REGARD IS THE LACK OF TOOLS TO PRECISELY AND DIRECTLY MODULATE MITOCHONDRIAL MASS. THIS PROPOSAL HAS THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) DETERMINE HOW A STATE OF REDUCED MITOCHONDRIAL MASS AFFECTS CELLULAR FUNCTION AND AGE-RELATED CELL PHENOTYPES; 2) IDENTIFY GENES INVOLVED IN RESTORING MITOCHONDRIAL MASS HOMEOSTASIS AND HOW THIS PROCESS DIFFERS ACROSS TISSUES AND AGE. THIS PROPOSED APPLICATION IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE 1) IT USES A NEW STRATEGY TO PRECISELY MODULATE MITOCHONDRIAL MASS, PROVIDING A UNIQUE ANGLE TO DECIPHER THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN MITOCHONDRIAL MASS ABERRATIONS AND AGING, AND 2) IT WILL UNCOVER REGULATORS OF MITOCHONDRIAL MASS HOMEOSTASIS AND HOW THIS DIFFERS BETWEEN TISSUES IN THE MULTI-TISSUE AGING ORGANISM C ELEGANS. PREVIOUS WORK HAS USED STRESS-INDUCED MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION OR GENETIC MUTANTS OF ENDOGENOUS MITOCHONDRIAL QUALITY CONTROL PROTEINS TO GENERATE CHANGES IN MITOCHONDRIAL MASS. WHILE ENLIGHTENING, THESE METHODS ONLY ALTER MITOCHONDRIAL MASS BY INDIRECT MEANS AND THUS MAKE DECONVOLVING CONSEQUENCES OF MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION FROM CHANGES TO MITOCHONDRIAL MASS DIFFICULT. THE RESEARCH IN THIS PROPOSAL IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE BY CLARIFYING THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN MITOCHONDRIAL MASS, CELL FUNCTION, AND AGING, WE WILL FURTHER OUR UNDERSTANDING OF A FUNDAMENTAL ASPECT OF ORGANISMAL HEALTH. IN ADDITION, BY IDENTIFYING REGULATORS OF MITOCHONDRIAL MASS HOMEOSTASIS, THIS PROPOSAL WILL UNCOVER THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR CORRECTING DYSREGULATED MITOCHONDRIAL MASS THAT MANIFESTS IN HUMAN DISEASE AND AGING. ALONG WITH THE PROPOSED RESEARCH, THIS APPLICATION ALSO OFFERS A FELLOWSHIP TRAINING PLAN THAT WILL CATALYZE DR. SCHMITZ’S PERSONAL AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT. HIS GOAL IS TO BECOME AN ADEPT INDEPENDENT ACADEMIC INVESTIGATOR. TO HELP HIM ACHIEVE THIS GOAL, THIS AWARD WILL PROVIDE DR. SCHMITZ WITH THE OPPORTUNITY TO IMPROVE HIS SCIENTIFIC WRITING AND COMMUNICATIONS SKILLS, HONE HIS MENTORING ABILITY, AND BECOME AN EXPERT IN THE FIELD OF AGING. THIS WILL BE FURTHER FOSTERED BY THE EXCELLENT RESEARCH CULTURE PRESENT AT UC BERKELEY AND DR. ANDREW DILLIN’S LAB.

description: STABLE CELL STATE ENGINEERING FOR REGULATORY T CELL THERAPIES - ABSTRACT AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES SUCH AS MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS, TYPE 1 DIABETES, INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE, AND RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS AFFECT TENS OF MILLIONS OF PEOPLE AND ARE LARGELY MANAGED WITH SYSTEMIC IMMUNOSUPPRESSION THAT COMPROMISES HOST DEFENSE AND RARELY INDUCES CURE. ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC TOLERANCE—RETRAINING THE IMMUNE SYSTEM TO IGNORE SELF WHILE PRESERVING PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY—IS A MAJOR UNMET NEED DIRECTLY ALIGNED WITH THE NIH MISSION TO REDUCE THE BURDEN OF CHRONIC, IMMUNE-MEDIATED DISEASE. THIS FELLOWSHIP AIMS TO ENGINEER STABLE CELL THERAPIES FOR RESTORING ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC TOLERANCE. IT WILL FOCUS PRIMARILY ON IL-10-EXPRESSING TYPE 1 REGULATORY T (TR1) CELLS BECAUSE THEY EMERGE NATURALLY IN INFLAMED PERIPHERAL TISSUES TO RESTRAINS PATHOGENIC IMMUNE RESPONSES. THEREFORE, TO ACHIEVE THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF ENGINEERING A STABLE TR1 CELL STATE, THIS PROPOSAL WILL FIRST IDENTIFY GENETIC PERTURBATIONS THAT DRIVE TR1 DIFFERENTIATION (AIM 1) AND THEN ENGINEER SOLUTIONS THAT STABILIZE IT UNDER INFLAMMATORY PRESSURE (AIM 2). IN AIM 1, THE APPLICANT WILL SCREEN THOUSANDS OF MULTI-GENE KNOCK-INS USING STATE-OF-THE-ART EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES AND THEN REFINE CONSTRUCT DESIGNS USING ADVANCED ALGORITHMS FOR PERTURBATION MODELLING. BY ITERATIVELY SCREENING CONSTRUCTS AND REFINING DESIGNS, AIM 1 WILL CONVERGE ON SOLUTIONS FOR TR1 STATE ENGINEERING WHILE COMPARING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF TWO DIFFERENT STRATEGIES: “RATIONALLY DESIGNED” CONSTRUCTS (ENCODING PUTATIVE TR1-ASSOCIATED REGULATORS) VERSUS UNBIASED “DIVERSITY- ORIENTED” CONSTRUCTS (SYNTHETIC TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS WITH MIXED EFFECTOR AND DNA BINDING DOMAINS). IN AIM 2, THE APPLICANT WILL ENGINEER AND SCREEN CYTOKINE SWITCH RECEPTORS THAT CONVERT COMMON INFLAMMATORY CUES INTO TOLEROGENIC SIGNALS. AIM 2 WILL THEN TEST THE ABILITY OF THESE SYNTHETIC RECEPTORS TO PRESERVE TR1 IDENTITY AND SUPPRESSIVE FUNCTION UNDER TH1-, TH17-, AND TH2-LIKE CYTOKINE MILIEUS IN VITRO AND IN HUMANIZED MOUSE MODELS OF COLITIS. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL IDENTIFY A TRANSLATION-READY CELL THERAPY CANDIDATE FOR AUTOIMMUNITY WHILE ESTABLISHING DESIGN PRINCIPLES AND A BROADLY APPLICABLE FRAMEWORK FOR “STABLE CELL STATE ENGINEERING” IN ANY CONTEXT. THE INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND TRAINING PLAN WILL PROVIDE RIGOROUS MENTORING IN SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY, DYNAMICAL MODELING, CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL IMMUNOLOGY, AND STRUCTURED CAREER DEVELOPMENT IN GRANTSMANSHIP, COMMUNICATION, AND LEADERSHIP. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE RESEARCH AIMS AND TRAINING GOALS WILL DIRECTLY SUPPORT THE APPLICANT’S LONG-TERM CAREER GOAL OF LEADING AN INDEPENDENT, NIH-FUNDED RESEARCH LABORATORY FOCUSED ON CELL STATE ENGINEERING AND TRANSLATABLE THERAPIES FOR INDUCING ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC TOLERANCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING THE ROLE OF TFAM-MEDIATED MITOCHONDRIAL RESPIRATION IN OSTEOBLASTOGENESIS - PROJECT SUMMARY  BONE FRAGILITY AND OSTEOPOROTIC FRACTURES ARE MAJOR COMPLICATIONS OF AGING AND METABOLIC DISEASES. OSTEOBLAST DIFFERENTIATION, WHICH DRIVES OSTEOGENESIS, BONE MASS ACCRUAL, AND BONE REPAIR, IS AN ENERGETICALLY DEMANDING PROCESS EASILY DISRUPTED BY IMPAIRED GLUCOSE METABOLISM. WHILE GLUCOSE HAS REPEATEDLY BEEN SHOWN TO BE THE PRIMARY FUEL FOR OSTEOBLASTS, IT REMAINS CONTROVERSIAL WHETHER THESE CELLS GENERATE ATP THROUGH GLYCOLYSIS OR THROUGH MITOCHONDRIAL OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION (OXPHOS) ACROSS OSTEOBLASTOGENESIS. STUDIES OF EARLY OSTEOPROGENITORS IN THE MESENCHYMAL LIMB BUD HAVE SUGGESTED THAT OXPHOS-DERIVED ATP IS REQUIRED FOR PROPER BONE FORMATION AND GROWTH; BY CONTRAST, WE AND OTHERS HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT MATURE OSTEOBLASTS ARE LARGELY GLYCOLYTIC EX VIVO, AND THAT OXPHOS IS DISPENSABLE FOR OVERALL ATP PRODUCTION IN THESE CELLS. THESE MODELS IMPLY A DEVELOPMENTAL SHIFT IN ENERGY METABOLISM FROM OXPHOS TO GLYCOLYSIS, BUT DIRECT IN VIVO EVIDENCE DEFINING THE TIMING, NECESSITY, AND FUNCTIONAL SIGNIFICANCE OF THIS TRANSITION IS LACKING.  TO RESOLVE THESE CONFLICTING REPORTS, WE GENERATED MICE IN WHICH THE MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR, TFAM, IS CONDITIONALLY DELETED ONLY IN THE COMMITTED OSTEOBLAST LINEAGE (SP7/OSTERIX-EXPRESSING CELLS) ONWARD. TFAM IS A NUCLEAR PROTEIN REQUIRED FOR EXPRESSION OF THE ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN IN MITOCHONDRIA, AND THUS, OXPHOS, AS WELL AS FOR MITOCHONDRIAL DNA REPLICATION. THIS APPROACH BYPASSES THE EFFECTS OF TFAM DELETION IN EARLY PROGENITORS AND ISOLATES MITOCHONDRIAL REQUIREMENTS TO COMMITTED OSTEOBLASTS. PRELIMINARY DATA INDICATE THAT, UNLIKE IN EARLIER DELETION MODELS SUCH AS PRX1-CRE, TFAM LOSS IN SP7-EXPRESSING CELLS DOES NOT AFFECT BONE MASS OR ARCHITECTURE. BASED ON THESE RESULTS AND OUR PRIOR STUDIES, I THEREFORE HYPOTHESIZE THAT TFAM-DEPENDENT MITOCHONDRIAL OXPHOS IS DISPENSABLE FOR BIOENERGETICS AND FUNCTION IN PREOSTEOBLASTS AND MATURE OSTEOBLASTS. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, I WILL 1) COMPREHENSIVELY CHARACTERIZE THE EFFECTS OF SP7-MEDIATED TFAM-CKO ON BONE FORMATION AND OSTEOBLASTOGENESIS AND 2) DETERMINE THE BIOENERGETIC CONSEQUENCES OF TFAM-DELETION ON OSTEOBLAST FUNCTION, AND ISOLATE POTENTIAL NON-BIOENERGETIC ROLES FOR OSTEOBLAST MITOCHONDRIA DURING OSTEOGENESIS.  TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL DELINEATE THE ROLE OF OSTEOBLAST MITOCHONDRIA IN SKELETAL FORMATION. BY CLARIFYING WHEN AND WHY MITOCHONDRIAL RESPIRATION IS REQUIRED OR DISPENSABLE, THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A NOVEL FRAMEWORK FOR UNDERSTANDING THE ENERGY DEMANDS OF OSTEOGENESIS AND IDENTIFY POTENTIALLY NOVEL INTERVENTION STRATEGIES FOR OSTEOPOROTIC BONE LOSS AND FRACTURE ASSOCIATED WITH METABOLIC DISEASE. ACCOMPLISHING THE AIMS PROPOSED HEREIN WILL PROVIDE TRAINING IN EXPERIMENTAL METHODS TO STUDY LOCALIZED AND SYSTEMIC METABOLISM AND STRENGTHEN BOTH MY BENCHWORK AND ANALYTICAL SKILLS. ABOVE ALL, THIS FELLOWSHIP WILL PROVIDE A SOLID FOUNDATION FROM WHICH TO LAUNCH MY FUTURE CAREER AS A PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR AND FOUND MY OWN LABORATORY FOCUSED ON THE ROLE OF INTERCELLULAR BIOENERGETIC RESOURCE DISTRIBUTION IN HOMEOSTASIS AND METABOLIC DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING DIETARY MODULATION OF THE GUT MICROBIOTA DURING PREGNANCY AND ITS IMPACT ON INFANT MICROBIOTA ASSEMBLY AND HEALTH - PROJECT SUMMARY DIET IS A STRONG AND EASILY MODIFIABLE DRIVER OF THE GUT MICROBIOTA DURING PREGNANCY, WITH CONSEQUENCES FOR MATERNAL, FETAL, AND INFANT MICROBIOTA AND METABOLITES THAT MAY CONTRIBUTE TO LIFELONG WELL-BEING. HOWEVER, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW MATERNAL DIET SHAPES THE STRAIN-LEVEL DIVERSITY OR ADAPTATION OF THE MICROBIOTA OR HOW THESE CHANGES MAY INTERACT WITH DIET TO SHAPE MATERNAL AND INFANT HEALTH. THE LONG-TERM OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO BUILD PREDICTIVE MODELS THAT CONNECT DIET TO THE DEVELOPMENT AND TRANSGENERATIONAL TRANSMISSION OF HEALTHY MICROBIOTAS, ENABLING SAFE, SCALABLE, AND COST-EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS AND STRATEGIES FOR LIFELONG DISEASE PREVENTION. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT SPECIFIC DIETS DURING PREGNANCY MODULATE THE GUT MICROBIOTA’S COMMUNITY COMPOSITION, EVOLUTIONARY TRAJECTORY, AND FUNCTIONAL CAPACITY DURING PREGNANCY AND THE TRANSMISSION OF BENEFICIAL STRAINS TO OFFSPRING. THREE INTEGRATED AND INDEPENDENT AIMS TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS: AIM 1 APPLIES GENOME-RESOLVED METAGENOMICS TO LONGITUDINAL MATERNAL AND INFANT SAMPLES ACROSS THE FOUR DIET ARMS (HIGH- FIBER, HIGH-FERMENTED FOODS, HIGH-FIBER AND HIGH-FERMENTED FOODS, OR CONTROL WITH NO INTERVENTION) TO DESCRIBE COMMUNITY COMPOSITION, STRAIN STRUCTURE, ALLELE FREQUENCY SHIFTS, FUNCTIONS, AND TRANSMISSION FROM MOTHER TO INFANT. AIM 2 INTEGRATES GLOBAL AND TARGETED METABOLOMICS OF MATERNAL SERUM AND BREASTMILK WITH METAGENOMIC FEATURES TO IDENTIFY DIET- AND MICROBIALLY ASSOCIATED METABOLITES AND THEIR PUTATIVE ORIGINS. AIM 3 USES COMPLEMENTARY GNOTOBIOTIC MOUSE MODELS AND STOOL-DERIVED IN VITRO COMMUNITIES TO IDENTIFY MECHANISMS UNDERLYING OBSERVED INCREASES IN DIVERSITY FOLLOWING A HIGH-FERMENTED FOOD DIET. MY PREVIOUS EXPERIENCE IN ECOLOGY AND EVOLUTIONARY BIOLOGY, METAGENOMICS, BIOINFORMATICS, AND MOUSE HANDLING MAKE ME WELL-EQUIPPED TO ANALYZE THE DATA AND PERFORM THE PROPOSED WORK, AND THE EXPERTISE IN HOST-MICROBE INTERACTIONS, METABOLOMICS, AND IN VITRO ANALYSIS HONED BY MY MENTORING TEAM MAKE STANFORD UNIVERSITY AN IDEAL LOCATION TO LEARN THE SKILLS I WILL NEED TO PERFORM THESE EXPERIMENTS. TOGETHER, THIS WORK WILL GENERATE A DETAILED FRAMEWORK FOR UNDERSTANDING HOW NUTRITIONAL ENVIRONMENTS MODULATE MICROBIAL ADAPTATION AND TRANSMISSION, ADVANCING BOTH OUR FOUNDATIONAL UNDERSTANDING OF PROCESSES GOVERNING THE MICROBIOTA AND THEIR INTERACTION WITH MATERNAL AND EARLY-LIFE SYSTEMS BIOLOGY. AS AMERICAN GUT MICROBIOTA ARE CHARACTERISTICALLY DYSBIOTIC AND LINKED TO THE HIGH PREVALENCE METABOLIC AND IMMUNOLOGICAL DISEASES, CLARIFYING HOW DIET RESTRUCTURES THESE COMMUNITIES AND INFLUENCES HOST METABOLITES IS OF BROAD CLINICAL RELEVANCE. BY CONNECTING DIET-DRIVEN MICROBIAL SHIFTS WITH METABOLITE PROFILES TIED TO WHOLE-BODY PHYSIOLOGY, THIS PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH SPECIFIC FOODS INFLUENCE MICROBIOTA DEVELOPMENT AND METABOLIC HEALTH. THE ANTICIPATED RESULTS MAY ULTIMATELY INFORM STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR NOT ONLY PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM INDIVIDUALS AND THEIR INFANTS, BUT ALSO FOR THE BROADER POPULATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: STEREOVISION: NORMAL CIRCUITS AND IMPACT OF DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS - PROJECT SUMMARY A LARGE MISMATCH IN VISION THROUGH THE TWO EYES DURING DEVELOPMENT IS KNOWN TO CAUSE LASTING DEFICITS IN VISION EVEN AFTER NORMAL VISION HAS BEEN RESTORED, INCLUDING REDUCED VISUAL ACUITY IN ONE EYE AND IMPAIRMENTS IN STEREOVISION OR STEREOPSIS. CURRENT TREATMENTS FOR THESE VISION DEFICITS ARE LIMITED, AND VISUAL IMPAIRMENTS PERSIST INTO ADULTHOOD. FOR NORMAL STEREOPSIS, THE BRAIN MUST CALCULATE AN OBJECT’S DEPTH BASED ON THE SLIGHT DIFFERENCES IN POSITION AN IMAGE CREATES IN EACH EYE, A PROCESS KNOWN AS BINOCULAR DISPARITY. PRIMARY VISUAL CORTEX (V1) IS ONE OF THE FIRST BRAIN AREAS IN THE VISUAL PROCESSING HIERARCHY WITH NEURONS THAT RECEIVE BINOCULAR INPUT AND SHOW SELECTIVITY TO BINOCULAR DISPARITY. THE IMPACTS OF IMPAIRED VISUAL DEVELOPMENT ON DISPARITY TUNING IN V1 HAVE NOT BEEN EXPLORED FULLY AT THE LEVEL OF NEURAL CIRCUITS, AND THERE ARE LIMITED STUDIES LINKING CHANGES BETWEEN PHYSIOLOGY AND CIRCUIT STRUCTURE WITH STEREOSCOPIC BEHAVIOR. THIS RESEARCH TRAINING PROJECT AIMS TO USE A MULTI- TECHNIQUE APPROACH TO STUDY DISRUPTIONS IN BINOCULAR DISPARITY PROCESSING IN V1 AND STEREOSCOPIC BEHAVIOR CAUSED BY DISRUPTED BINOCULAR VISION DURING DEVELOPMENT, USING THE FERRET AS A MODEL. FERRETS ARE HIGHLY VISUAL CARNIVORES, THEIR VISUAL SYSTEM IS SIMILAR TO THAT OF PRIMATES, AND THEIR EARLY BIRTH MAKES THEM AN EXCELLENT MODEL FOR STUDYING VISUAL DEVELOPMENT. IN AIM 1, THIS PROJECT WILL EXAMINE DISRUPTIONS IN NEURAL ENCODING OF DISPARITY TUNING IN V1 CAUSED BY ALTERED VISUAL DEVELOPMENT, AND HOW THEY RELATE TO BEHAVIORAL DEFICITS IN STEREOSCOPIC VISUAL BEHAVIOR. AIM 2 WILL USE 2-PHOTON CALCIUM IMAGING TO EXAMINE THE ORGANIZATION OF NORMAL CIRCUIT STRUCTURE FOR BINOCULAR DISPARITY TUNING IN V1 AND TEST FOR POSSIBLE DISRUPTIONS AFTER ALTERATIONS IN VISUAL DEVELOPMENT, AGAIN RELATING RESULTS TO DEFICITS IN BEHAVIOR. IN TOTAL, THIS PROJECT WILL BRIDGE KEY GAPS IN THE STUDY OF STEREOPSIS AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS BY UTILIZING MULTIPLE TECHNIQUES IN A NOVEL MODEL. IN ADDITION TO PROVIDING THE CANDIDATE WITH TRAINING IN EXPERIMENTAL TECHNIQUES SUCH AS 2-PHOTON IMAGING AND BEHAVIORAL PSYCHOPHYSICS, THIS PROPOSAL WILL ALSO FACILITATE CAREER DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES, TRAINING IN SCIENTIFIC COMMUNICATION AND MENTORING SKILLS, AND NAVIGATING THE TRANSITION TO A FACULTY ROLE AT AN ACADEMIC RESEARCH INSTITUTION. THIS PROJECT IS SPONSORED BY THE LAB OF DR. KRISTINA NIELSEN, A RESEARCHER WITH EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN STUDYING THE DEVELOPMENT OF VISUAL STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION, IN THE MIND BRAIN INSTITUTE AND DEPARTMENT OF NEUROSCIENCE AT JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY. THIS ENVIRONMENT IS EXCELLENT FOR POSTDOCTORAL TRAINING IN NEUROSCIENCE AND WILL PROVIDE THE BEST POSSIBLE SUPPORT FOR THE RESEARCH AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT GOALS OUTLINED IN THIS PROPOSAL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF PEROXISOMAL MEMBRANE PROTEIN TRAFFICKING - PROJECT SUMMARY PEROXISOMES ARE ESSENTIAL CELLULAR ORGANELLES INVOLVED IN LIPID METABOLISM AND CELLULAR DETOXIFICATION, YET THE INTRICACIES OF THEIR FORMATION AND MAINTENANCE REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. PEROXISOME BIOGENESIS DISORDERS (PBDS), INCLUDING ZELLWEGER SPECTRUM DISORDER (ZSD) AND X-LINKED ADRENOLEUKODYSTROPHY, AFFECT 1 IN 50,000 BIRTHS AND CAUSE DEVASTATING NEUROLOGICAL AND METABOLIC DYSFUNCTION DUE TO DEFECTIVE ORGANELLE FORMATION. A CRITICAL STEP IN PEROXISOME BIOGENESIS INVOLVES SOLUBLE AND MEMBRANE PROTEIN IMPORT TO IMMATURE PEROXISOMES. THIS RESEARCH PROJECT AIMS TO UNRAVEL THE FUNDAMENTAL MECHANISMS OF PEROXISOME BIOGENESIS, WITH A FOCUS ON MEMBRANE PROTEIN TRAFFICKING TO THE PEROXISOMES. WHILE SOLUBLE PROTEIN IMPORT TO PEROXISOMES IS WELL CHARACTERIZED, PEROXISOMAL MEMBRANE PROTEIN (PMP) TRAFFICKING MECHANISMS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD, REPRESENTING A CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAP THAT IMPEDES OUR UNDERSTANDING AND TREATMENT OF PBDS. TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP, I PROPOSE TO DISSECT THE MOLECULAR DETAILS OF PMP INTERACTION WITH THE PEROXISOME IMPORT RECEPTOR AND CHAPERONE- PEX19. AIM 1 INVESTIGATES THE BIOCHEMICAL AND STRUCTURAL BASIS OF HUMAN PMP- PEX19 COMPLEX FORMATION. THIS AIM WILL DEPICT THE MOLECULAR INTERACTIONS BETWEEN PMPS AND THE IMPORT MACHINERY TO DETERMINE HOW POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATIONS AND PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS GOVERN ORGANELLE ASSEMBLY. AIM 2 EXAMINES THE DISRUPTIONS OF PEX19-DEPENDENT PMP TRAFFICKING IN THE CONTEXT OF GENETIC DISEASES, AND UPON DRUG TREATMENT. I WILL USE CRISPR-ENGINEERED, AND ZSD PATIENT-DERIVED CELL LINES TO GAIN HOLISTIC INSIGHTS INTO TRAFFICKING DISRUPTIONS IN BOTH DISEASE AND THERAPEUTIC CONTEXTS. THE PROJECT WILL EMPLOY A MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH, COMBINING CUTTING-EDGE STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY TECHNIQUES, BIOPHYSICAL ASSAYS, AND ADVANCED CELLULAR IMAGING TO INVESTIGATE KEY PROTEIN INTERACTIONS INVOLVED IN PEROXISOME FORMATION. FINDINGS FROM THIS STUDY WILL ELUCIDATE THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS OF PMP IMPORT IN PEROXISOMAL BIOGENESIS AND OPEN NEW DOORS TO DEVELOPING FUTURE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR PBDS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A BIOACTIVE MILK COMPONENT PROMOTES COGNITION THROUGH THE GUT MICROBIOME-BRAIN AXIS. - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT MILK IS AN INVALUABLE, NATURAL SOURCE OF UNIQUE MILK FAT GLOBULE MEMBRANE (MFGM) GLYCOCONJUGATES THAT PROMOTE COGNITIVE FUNCTION IN INFANTS. THESE FUNCTIONS ARE ATTRIBUTED IN PART TO SIALYLATED GLYCOCONJUGATES, WHICH CONTAIN SIALIC ACID (SIA), A CRUCIAL MOLECULE FOR NEURODEVELOPMENT. USING A NOVEL BIOACTIVE DAIRY COMPONENT (WHEY PROTEIN PHOSPHOLIPID CONCENTRATE, WPPC) ENRICHED WITH BOVINE MFGM AS A PROXY FOR BREAST MILK, THE FIRST GOAL OF THIS WORK IS TO IDENTIFY THE GENETIC ELEMENTS ENABLING SELECT BIFIDOBACTERIA WITH THE METABOLIC CAPACITY TO CONSUME WPPC AND RELEASE SIA. AIM 1 WILL INVOLVE SYSTEMATIC, HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING TO IDENTIFY BIFIDOBACTERIA SPECIES IN VITRO GROWTH ON WPPC AND MEASURING SIA RELEASE INTO THE CULTURE MEDIA. RNA SEQUENCING WILL BE PERFORMED TO DISCOVER GENETIC DIFFERENCES BETWEEN SPECIES THAT RELEASE SIA AND THOSE THAT DO NOT, AND KNOCK-OUT STRAINS AND STRAINS WITH THE NECESSARY GENETIC ELEMENTS CLONED IN WILL VALIDATE ESSENTIAL GENETIC ELEMENTS FOR SIA RELEASE. SEQUENTIAL FECAL ENRICHMENT EXPERIMENTS USING ADULT FECES AND WPPC WILL ENABLE THE IDENTIFICATION OF BIFIDOBACTERIA STRAINS THAT PERSIST IN A STABILIZED GUT MICROBIOME AND QUANTIFICATION OF SIA RELEASE. NEXT, THIS PROPOSAL WILL DETERMINE IF SIA RELEASE FROM WPPC-CONSUMING BIFIDOBACTERIA CAN PROMOTE COGNITIVE FUNCTION IN RATS. IN AIM 2, I WILL ALSO ORALLY ADMINISTER BIFIDOBACTERIA +/- WPPC TO AN INFANT MODEL OF WISTAR RATS TO DETERMINE IF WPPC PROMOTES BIFIDOBACTERIA PERSISTENCE (FECES), ENABLES THE RELEASE OF SIA FROM WPPC (FECES, BLOOD, HIPPOCAMPUS AND FRONTAL CORTEX), AND PROMOTES COGNITION THROUGH BEHAVIOR TESTS. I WILL ALSO INFUSE LABELED SIA INTO RATS TO DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF DIETARY TREATMENTS ON BRAIN MYELINATION KINETICS, WHICH IS IMPORTANT FOR COGNITION. I ANTICIPATE ENZYMATICALLY CAPABLE BIFIDOBACTERIA WILL BE ABLE TO RELEASE SIA, WHICH WILL IMPROVE COGNITIVE FUNCTION IN RATS. THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL IDENTIFY A MECHANISM FOR HOW NATURAL MILK MFGM GLYCOCONJUGATES MAY PROMOTE NEURODEVELOPMENT IN INFANTS. IN THE LONG-TERM, THESE FINDINGS COULD CONTRIBUTE TOWARDS DEVELOPING AN INTEGRATIVE FOOD-FOR-HEALTH SYNBIOTIC TO PROMOTE COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT IN EARLY LIFE. THE FELLOWSHIP TRAINING WILL BE GUIDED BY NIH FUNDED CO-SPONSORS PROFESSORS DAVID MILLS (MICROBIOLOGY) AND AMEER TAHA (NEUROBIOLOGY), AND PROFESSOR DANIELA BARILE (GLYCOCHEMISTRY) IN THE DEPARTMENT OF FOOD SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AT UC DAVIS. THE MILLS LABORATORY HAS AN ESTABLISHED, OVER 20-YEAR-OLD UC DAVIS MILK BIOACTIVES GROUP WHICH HAS FACILITATED NUMEROUS COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH PROJECTS AMONGST 100’S OF ACADEMICS RESULTING IN 100’S OF PUBLICATIONS. DR. MILLS HAS GRADUATED 24 GRADUATE STUDENTS AND MENTORED 18 POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHERS, THREE OF WHOM WERE AWARDED AN F32. TWELVE OF DR. MILLS FORMER MENTEES ARE NOW ACADEMIC FACULTY. THE MILLS LABORATORY IS PART OF THE UC DAVIS FOOD FOR HEALTH INSTITUTE, WHICH AIMS TO BRING PERSONALIZED HEALTH TO PRACTICE BY UNDERSTANDING HOW DIET CONTROLS HEALTH. AS SUCH, THE LABORATORY AND BROADER INSTITUTIONAL ENVIRONMENT AT UC DAVIS HAS THE PERSONNEL AND EXPERTISE FOR THIS RESEARCH TRAINING PLAN AND PROJECT TO BE SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETED.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UTERINE NATURAL KILLER CELL-MEDIATED CLEARANCE OF SENESCENT CELLS: A NOVEL MECHANISM IN ENDOMETRIAL DECIDUALIZATION AND IMPLICATIONS FOR ENDOMETRIOSIS-ASSOCIATED INFERTILITY - PROJECT SUMMARY ENDOMETRIOSIS AFFECTS APPROXIMATELY 10% OF REPRODUCTIVE-AGE WOMEN AND IS A MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR TO INFERTILITY, PREGNANCY LOSS, AND CHRONIC PELVIC PAIN WORLDWIDE. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ELUCIDATE THE ROLE OF UTERINE NATURAL KILLER (UNK) CELLS IN REGULATING ENDOMETRIAL CLEARANCE OF SENESCENT CELLS AND IMMUNE BALANCE, A PROCESS DISRUPTED IN ENDOMETRIOSIS-ASSOCIATED REPRODUCTIVE FAILURE5. THEREFORE, IT IS ESSENTIAL TO ESTABLISH PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT MODELS TO STUDY THE INFLUENCE OF THE IMMUNE MICROENVIRONMENT ON FERTILITY AND REGENERATION. SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL DEVELOP AND CHARACTERIZE A NOVEL 3D ENDOMETRIAL IMMUNE MICROSYSTEM INCORPORATING MENSTRUAL EFFLUENT PATIENT-DERIVED UNK, STROMAL, AND EPITHELIAL CELLS TO INVESTIGATE HOW CHRONIC INFLAMMATION ALTERS UNK FUNCTION AND SENESCENT CELL CROSSTALK EX VIVO. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL USE A GENETICALLY ENGINEERED NKP46-GFP REPORTER MOUSE TO SPATIOTEMPORALLY MAP UNK SUBSET DYNAMICS AND THEIR INTERACTIONS WITH SENESCENT CELLS DURING CONTINUOUS DECIDUAL REMODELING THROUGHOUT EARLY PREGNANCY. THIS INTEGRATIVE APPROACH COMBINING ADVANCED IMAGING, FLOW CYTOMETRY, AND TRANSCRIPTOMICS WILL PROVIDE UNPRECEDENTED INSIGHT INTO IMMUNE REGULATION OF ENDOMETRIAL HEALTH AND DISEASE. FINDINGS HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO REVEAL NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS TO IMPROVE FERTILITY OUTCOMES AND REDUCE PREGNANCY COMPLICATIONS IN WOMEN WITH ENDOMETRIOSIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: VISUAL ATTENTION DURING WALKING IN CHILDREN WITH AND WITHOUT CEREBRAL PALSY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT DURING LOCOMOTION, VISION IS USED FOR BOTH LOCOMOTOR PLANNING (LOOKING AT THE PATH TO DECIDE WHERE AND HOW TO WALK) AND VISUAL EXPLORATION OF THE ENVIRONMENT (LOOKING AT PEOPLE, PLACES, AND THINGS TO GAIN INFORMATION AND INTERACT WITH THE WORLD). HOW VISION IS ALLOCATED DURING LOCOMOTION VARIES BASED ON WALKING STABILITY—THE ABILITY TO MAINTAIN DYNAMIC BALANCE AND AVOID FALLS. MOREOVER, ACROSS DEVELOPMENT, WALKING STABILITY IMPROVES AND VISUAL GUIDANCE OF LOCOMOTION DECREASES. THE PROPOSED PROJECT TESTS THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT WALKING INSTABILITY BIASES VISUAL ATTENTION TO THE LOCOMOTOR PATH AT THE EXPENSE OF VISUALLY EXPLORING THE ENVIRONMENT. ALTHOUGH PLANNING AND MAINTAINING SAFE AND EFFICIENT LOCOMOTION IS CRITICAL, VISUAL EXPLORATION IS ALSO CRITICAL BECAUSE IT PROVIDES OPPORTUNITIES TO LEARN FROM AND ABOUT THE ENVIRONMENT. THE HYPOTHESIS WILL BE TESTED IN 4-12-YEAR-OLD CHILDREN WITH AND WITHOUT CEREBRAL PALSY (CP), A DISORDER OF POSTURE AND MOVEMENT THAT IMPACTS STABILITY. CHILDREN WITH CP FREQUENTLY USE MOBILITY AIDS, LIKE WALKERS, TO INCREASE STABILITY DURING LOCOMOTION. THEREFORE, TO GAIN MORE INSIGHT ON THE EFFECT OF MOBILITY AIDS ON VISUAL ATTENTION DURING LOCOMOTION AND THE ROLE OF STABILITY IN VISUAL ATTENTION DURING LOCOMOTION MORE BROADLY, CHILDREN WITH CP WILL BE TESTED WITH AND WITHOUT THEIR WALKER. CHILDREN WILL WEAR A MOBILE EYE TRACKER TO MEASURE WHERE THEY LOOK AS THEY WALK A GENTLY WINDING PATH SURROUNDED BY VISUALLY INTERESTING OBJECTS OF VARIOUS HEIGHTS. WALKING STABILITY WILL BE ASSESSED BY MEASURING THE PERCENTAGE OF TIME IN DOUBLE SUPPORT AND THE STANDARD DEVIATION OF TRUNK ACCELERATION USING WEARABLE SENSORS. TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE IMPACT OF MOBILITY AIDS ON STABILITY AND VISUAL ATTENTION, CHILDREN WITH CP WILL WALK WITH AND WITHOUT THEIR WALKER. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME MEASURE IS THE PROPORTION OF THE TRIAL TIME SPENT LOOKING AT THE PATH. AIM 1 COMPARES VISUAL ATTENTION OF CHILDREN WITH AND WITHOUT CP AS THEY WALK A WINDING PATH WITHOUT A MOBILITY AID. AIM 2 TESTS THE EFFECT OF MOBILITY AIDS ON VISUAL ATTENTION OF CHILDREN WITH CP AS THEY WALK A WINDING PATH. BOTH AIMS WILL TEST WHETHER MEASURES OF WALKING STABILITY EXPLAIN ADDITIONAL VARIANCE IN THE PROPORTION OF TIME LOOKING AT THE PATH, AFTER ACCOUNTING FOR AGE AND GROUP (AIM 1) AND AGE AND CONDITION (AIM 2). THROUGH THE PROPOSED PROJECT, THE FELLOWSHIP TRAINING PLAN IS DESIGNED TO: (1) INCREASE DOMAIN KNOWLEDGE IN (A) CEREBRAL PALSY AND (B) VISUAL FUNCTION; (2) DEVELOP TECHNICAL EXPERTISE IN (A) MOBILE EYE TRACKING, (B) WEARABLE SENSOR DATA, AND (C) CLINICAL GAIT ANALYSIS; AND (3) ENHANCE PROFESSIONAL AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT BY (A) DISSEMINATING RESEARCH, (B) IMPROVING GRANTSMANSHIP, AND (C) EXPANDING MENTORING SKILLS. TRAINING WILL OCCUR AT USC, ONE OF THE TOP RESEARCH UNIVERSITIES IN THE UNITED STATES, IN THE DIVISION OF BIOKINESIOLOGY AND PHYSICAL THERAPY, A NATIONAL LEADER IN REHABILITATION RESEARCH. SPONSORS PROVIDE EXPERTISE IN PEDIATRIC REHABILITATION, CEREBRAL PALSY, MOBILE EYE TRACKING IN INFANTS AND CHILDREN, WEARABLE SENSING, LOCOMOTOR CONTROL, AND GAIT ANALYSIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEFINING STRUCTURE-FUNCTION INTERPLAY IN OVIDUCT SMOOTH MUSCLE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS STUDY IS TO IDENTIFY AND CHARACTERIZE KEY DYNAMICS OF TUBAL TRANSPORT IN BOTH MOUSE AND HUMAN OVIDUCTS. TO ACCOMPLISH THIS, I WILL LEVERAGE HIGHLY INNOVATIVE, HIGH RESOLUTION VOLUMETRIC IMAGING METHODS AND DOWNSTREAM COMPUTATIONAL ANALYSES PIONEERED BY MY LAB THAT ALLOW FOR PRECISE, 4D RESOLUTION OF CROSS-SPECIES TUBAL DYNAMICS.  TUBAL FACTOR IS ESTIMATED TO BE IMPLICATED IN 30-40% OF ALL FEMALE INFERTILITY CASES; HOWEVER, DESPITE ITS PREVALENCE, OVIDUCTAL FUNCTION REMAINS A SEVERELY UNDERSTUDIED AREA OF REPRODUCTIVE BIOLOGY. MANY STUDIES RELY ON MOUSE MODELS TO ELUCIDATE HUMAN OVIDUCT FUNCTION, BUT HOW CLOSELY THE MOUSE OVIDUCT RECAPITULATES THE STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION OF THE HUMAN OVIDUCT (FALLOPIAN TUBE) IS UNKNOWN, PRESENTING A SIGNIFICANT BARRIER TO TRANSLATIONAL DISCOVERY. PRELIMINARY STUDIES IN THE MOUSE OVIDUCT REVEAL REGION-SPECIFIC LUMINAL ARCHITECTURE AND CILIA DISTRIBUTION, IN ADDITION TO A NOVEL ‘GATE-LIKE’ REGION OF FUNCTIONAL CONSTRICTION IN THE ISTHMUS-AMPULLARY JUNCTION. BY UTILIZING STATE-OF-THE-ART VOLUMETRIC IMAGING AND QUANTITATIVE ANALYSES, THIS STUDY AIMS TO COMPREHENSIVELY COMPARE THE ARCHITECTURE AND CELL TYPE DISTRIBUTION THROUGHOUT THE MOUSE AND HUMAN OVIDUCTS, PROVIDING THE FIRST COMPLETE ‘MAP’ OF THE HUMAN OVIDUCT WITH THE ADDITIONAL SPECIFIC GOAL OF FURTHER CHARACTERIZING IN MICE AND IDENTIFYING IN HUMANS THE CRITICAL ‘GATE-LIKE’ DYNAMIC STRUCTURE FOR THE FIRST TIME.  IN ADDITION TO QUANTITATIVE STRUCTURAL CHARACTERIZATIONS, THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE CROSS-SPECIES DYNAMIC FUNCTIONS OF THE OVIDUCT THAT REMAIN UNKNOWN. FOR SUCCESSFUL TUBAL TRANSPORT, THE COORDINATED, DYNAMIC ACTIONS OF MOTILE CILIA AND SMOOTH MUSCLE (SM) ARE REQUIRED TO GENERATE DIRECTIONAL MOVEMENT OF THE OOCYTES AND EMBRYOS FROM THE OVARY TO THE UTERUS. WHILE CILIARY FUNCTION IN THE OVIDUCT HAS BEEN LINKED TO CILIOPATHY- ASSOCIATED INFERTILITY AND EXTENSIVELY STUDIED BY OUR LAB, THE ROLE AND REGULATION OF SM, WHICH HAS ALSO BEEN GENETICALLY IMPLICATED IN SOME REPRODUCTIVE DISORDERS, IN THE OVIDUCT REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD. PRELIMINARY STUDIES INDICATE REGION-SPECIFIC DIFFERENCES IN SM FUNCTION TO AID IN OOCYTE/EMBRYO TRANSFER. FURTHER, RECENT CLINICAL DATA SUGGEST THAT MODULATING SM FUNCTION THROUGH THE HORMONAL REGULATOR OXYTOCIN IMPACTS IN VITRO FERTILIZATION SUCCESS, THOUGH THE FUNCTION OF OXYTOCIN IN THE OVIDUCT HAS NOT YET BEEN STUDIED. THIS PROPOSAL WILL PERFORM THE FIRST IN-DEPTH QUANTITATIVE CHARACTERIZATION OF SM DYNAMICS IN THE MOUSE AND HUMAN OVIDUCTS AND IDENTIFY SM REGULATORY PATHWAYS WITH TRANSLATIONAL IMPACT.  NEW DISCOVERIES GAINED FROM THIS PROPOSED PROJECT WILL BE EXTREMELY TRANSLATIONALLY RELEVANT, CONTRIBUTING BOTH TO OUR BASIC UNDERSTANDING OF CROSS-SPECIES OVIDUCTAL FUNCTION AND IDENTIFICATION OF REGULATORY PATHWAYS OF TUBAL TRANSPORT, A CRITICAL AND PATHOLOGICALLY RELEVANT REPRODUCTIVE PROCESS.

description: MITOCHONDRIAL ORIGINS OF PREECLAMPSIA - PROJECT SUMMARY PREECLAMPSIA (PE) IS A COMPLEX, MULTISYSTEM VASCULAR DISORDER OF PLACENTAL ORIGIN, AFFECTING 8.5 MILLION PREGNANCIES WORLDWIDE EACH YEAR. PE AND ITS FREQUENT COMPLICATION, FETAL GROWTH RESTRICTION (FGR), POSE ACUTE THREATS TO MATERNAL AND FETAL SURVIVAL AND RAISE THE LIFETIME RISK OF CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE IN AFFECTED WOMEN BY TWO TO TENFOLD. NO EFFECTIVE PREVENTION STRATEGIES EXIST, LARGELY DUE TO A LIMITED UNDERSTANDING OF THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THEIR ETIOLOGY. EVIDENCE POINTS TO PLACENTAL MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION AS A CENTRAL DRIVER. IN PE, CHRONIC PLACENTAL ISCHEMIA-REPERFUSION DRIVEN BY IMPAIRED VASODILATION OF THE UTEROPLACENTAL ARTERIES DISRUPTS MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION AND ARCHITECTURE, IMPAIRING CELLULAR ENERGY PRODUCTION AND INCREASING MITOCHONDRIAL REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES (MTROS) PRODUCTION. KNOWLEDGE GAPS REMAIN REGARDING HOW MITOCHONDRIAL NETWORK ARCHITECTURE AND OXIDATIVE CAPACITY REGULATE VASCULAR FUNCTION, AND WHETHER THESE REPRESENT THERAPEUTIC TARGETS. OUR GOAL IS TO DETERMINE HOW PLACENTAL MITOCHONDRIAL NETWORK ARCHITECTURE AND OXIDATIVE CAPACITY INTERACT TO REGULATE UTEROPLACENTAL VASCULAR FUNCTION IN PE AND ULTIMATELY FGR. IN A HIGH-ALTITUDE (HA) COHORT, WHERE PE INCIDENCE IS 3-FOLD GREATER THAN AT LOWER ALTITUDES, WE FOUND LOWER PLACENTAL MITOCHONDRIAL OXIDATIVE METABOLISM (OXPHOS) IN PE VS. CONTROLS, WITH PILOT STUDIES IMPLICATING DEFECTIVE FATTY ACID OXIDATION (FAO) AS THE PRIMARY DRIVER. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT PLACENTAL HYPOXIA BLUNTS FAO, PROMOTING MITOCHONDRIAL NETWORK FRAGMENTATION AND ELEVATED MTROS, WHICH IN TURN INCREASE UTEROPLACENTAL-FETOPLACENTAL VASCULAR RESISTANCE AND PRECIPITATE PE. AIM 1 QUANTIFIES PLACENTAL FAO-LINKED OXPHOS AND MTROS PRODUCTION USING HIGH-RESOLUTION ASSAYS. AIM 2 DEFINES MITOCHONDRIAL NETWORK DISRUPTIONS USING MACHINE-LEARNING 3D IMAGING OF MITOCHONDRIAL MORPHOLOGY AND SINGLE- NUCLEI RNA SEQUENCING. AIM 3 INTEGRATES METABOLIC AND MORPHOLOGICAL DATA WITH UTEROPLACENTAL VASCULAR FUNCTION MEASURES TO TEST WHETHER FAO DEFICITS AND MTROS SERVE AS MECHANISTIC LINKS BETWEEN PLACENTAL HYPOXIA AND IMPAIRED VASCULAR FUNCTION, AND WHETHER MITOCHONDRIAL-TARGETED ANTIOXIDANTS CAN RESTORE VASCULAR FUNCTION. THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE THE FIRST INTEGRATED MOLECULAR-TO-VASCULAR ANALYSIS OF PLACENTAL MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION IN PE. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IDENTIFYING FAO IMPAIRMENT AS A CORE METABOLIC DEFICIT, DELINEATING MITOCHONDRIAL NETWORK SIGNATURES THAT DISTINGUISH PE, AND PROOF-OF-CONCEPT FOR MITOCHONDRIAL-TARGETED THERAPIES. THIS PROJECT DIRECTLY ADVANCES MY LONG-TERM GOAL OF BUILDING A TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH PROGRAM INVESTIGATING HOW MITOCHONDRIAL PHYSIOLOGY DRIVES HYPOXIA-RELATED CARDIOVASCULAR AND PREGNANCY DISORDERS. THIS PROPOSAL WILL PROVIDE STRUCTURED TRAINING IN CLINICAL AND HUMAN RESEARCH, COMPLEMENTING MY BACKGROUND IN MITOCHONDRIAL PHYSIOLOGY AND ANIMAL MODELS. BY INTEGRATING NEW MOLECULAR AND ANALYTICAL APPROACHES, I WILL GAIN CRITICAL SKILLS TO ADDRESS MATERNAL AND FETAL VASCULAR HEALTH, PREPARING ME TO LEAD INNOVATIVE, TRANSLATIONAL INVESTIGATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENVIRONMENTAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL REGULATION OF PRIMORDIAL GERM CELL PROLIFERATION IN THE C. ELEGANS LARVAL GONAD - SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  GERM CELLS ARE ESSENTIAL TO SUSTAIN LIFE IN SEXUALLY REPRODUCING ORGANISMS. PRIMORDIAL GERM CELLS (PGCS) ARE A POPULATION OF GERMLINE STEM CELLS SPECIFIED DURING EMBRYONIC DEVELOPMENT. PGC DIVISION IS DICTATED BY SIGNALING FROM THE LOCALIZED MICROENVIRONMENT CALLED THE NICHE. UNDERSTANDING HOW THE NICHE RELAYS ENVIRONMENTAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL CUES TO INSTRUCT CELL DIVISION IS CRITICAL TO MAINTAIN HEALTHY GERM CELLS. USING C. ELEGANS, I WILL INVESTIGATE THE SIGNALS REQUIRED TO REGULATE PGC DIVISION. THE C. ELEGANS LARVAL GONAD IS COMPRISED OF TWO PGCS, TWO SOMATIC GONADAL PRECURSORS (SGPS) AND A THIN, SPECIALIZED EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX CALLED THE BASEMENT MEMBRANE (BM) SURROUNDING THE FOUR CELLS. PGCS ARE QUIESCENT, BUT UPON EMBRYO HATCHING AND FEEDING, PGCS EXIT QUIESCENCE AND DIVIDE TO FORM THE GERMLINE STEM CELLS (GSCS) IN THE FIRST LARVAL STAGE (L1). WHILE IT'S KNOWN THE NOTCH SIGNALING PATHWAY IS ESSENTIAL TO MAINTAIN THE ADULT GSCS, THE SIGNALS REQUIRED TO INITIATE PGC DIVISION ARE UNKNOWN. PGC QUIESCENCE IS REGULATED BY TWO INPUTS: THE TUMOR- SUPPRESSOR GENE PTEN/DAF-18 AND THE BM. IN DAF-18 MUTANTS, PGCS PRECOCIOUSLY DIVIDE IN THE ABSENCE OF FOOD, SUGGESTING A PRO-MITOTIC ENVIRONMENTAL SIGNAL FROM NUTRITIONAL INPUTS REGULATES PGC DIVISION. GENETIC DEPLETION OF THE GONADAL BM INDUCES NOTCH SIGNALING IN PGCS, RESULTING IN THEIR PRECOCIOUS DIVISION. IT'S UNCLEAR HOW THE BM-MEDIATED BRAKE ON PGC QUIESCENCE IS RELIEVED AS THE GONAD PROLIFERATES. PGC PROLIFERATION COULD BE INDUCED FROM COMPOSITIONAL CHANGES WITHIN THE BM OR SIGNALING CHANGES BETWEEN THE BM AND THE SGPS OR PGCS. I PROPOSE TO INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF NOTCH SIGNALING, FIRSTLY WHETHER IT'S REQUIRED FOR PGC DIVISIONS AND SECONDLY WHETHER THE PRECOCIOUS DIVISION IN DAF-18 MUTANTS IS NOTCH-DEPENDENT. I WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE HOW THE BM MEDIATES PGC PROLIFERATION, EITHER THROUGH CHANGES IN ITS COMPOSITION OR CHANGES IN BM-MEDIATED GROWTH FACTOR SIGNALING. USING A COMBINATION OF GENETIC AND QUANTITATIVE IMAGING TOOLS, I HOPE TO UNDERSTAND HOW THE NICHE USES HIGHLY CONSERVED INPUTS (NOTCH, PTEN, BM) TO REGULATE GERM CELL DIVISION AND HEALTHY GERM CELLS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MATERNAL EARLY LIFE ADVERSITY, MOTHER-INFANT PHYSIOLOGICAL COREGULATION, AND INFANT SOCIOEMOTIONAL DEVELOPMENT - PROJECT SUMMARY EARLY LIFE ADVERSITY (ELA) IS EXTREMELY PREVALENT AND HAS ENDURING CONSEQUENCES FOR INTERGENERATIONAL HEALTH. EMERGING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT MATERNAL EXPERIENCES OF ELA CAN BECOME BIOLOGICALLY EMBEDDED TO ALTER MOTHERS’ PHYSIOLOGICAL SELF-REGULATION CAPACITIES AND THE EXTENT TO WHICH THEY COREGULATE WITH THEIR INFANTS, WHICH MAY HAVE NEGATIVE DOWNSTREAM EFFECTS ON CHILDREN’S SELF-REGULATION AND SOCIOEMOTIONAL DEVELOPMENT. HOWEVER, EXISTING RESEARCH ON THIS PATHWAY IS LIMITED TO EFFECTS OF MATERNAL CUMULATIVE ELA OR GENERAL MALTREATMENT HISTORY AND DOES NOT FORMALLY LINK MOTHER-INFANT PHYSIOLOGICAL COREGULATION PROCESSES TO CHILD OUTCOMES. TO ADDRESS THESE LIMITATIONS, THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL EXAMINE HOW SPECIFIC TYPES OF MATERNAL ELA (ABUSE, NEGLECT, AND THE NOVEL ASPECT OF ENVIRONMENTAL UNPREDICTABILITY) SHAPE DYNAMIC, MOMENT-TO-MOMENT PATTERNS OF MATERNAL PHYSIOLOGICAL SELF-REGULATION AND MOTHER-INFANT PHYSIOLOGICAL COREGULATION (AIM 1), AND HOW MOTHER-INFANT PHYSIOLOGICAL COREGULATION RELATES TO INFANT SOCIOEMOTIONAL OUTCOMES ACROSS VARYING MATERNAL ELA CONTEXTS (AIM 2). THIS STUDY WILL LEVERAGE DATA FROM A HIGH-RISK SAMPLE OF 300 MOTHER-INFANT DYADS PARTICIPATING IN A LARGER LONGITUDINAL STUDY (R01HD111437). MEASURES WILL INCLUDE MATERNAL SELF-REPORTS OF THEIR ELA EXPERIENCES, MATERNAL AND INFANT PARASYMPATHETIC ACTIVITY COLLECTED DURING A SOCIAL CHALLENGE AT 6 MONTHS POSTPARTUM, AND MATERNAL REPORT OF INFANT SOCIOEMOTIONAL OUTCOMES AT 12 MONTHS POSTPARTUM. FINDINGS FROM THIS STUDY WILL ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF DISTINCT PHYSIOLOGICAL PATHWAYS THROUGH WHICH CONSEQUENCES OF ELA ARE PASSED DOWN FROM ONE GENERATION TO THE NEXT AND INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF MORE PRECISE INTERVENTION STRATEGIES THAT CAN DISRUPT THE INTERGENERATIONAL TRANSMISSION OF RISK. WHILE COMPLETING THE PROPOSED STUDY, THE APPLICANT WILL DEEPEN HER EXPERTISE IN ELA THEORY AND MEASUREMENT, GAIN NEW SKILLS IN ASSESSMENT AND ANALYSIS OF DYADIC PARASYMPATHETIC PROCESSES, AND ENHANCE HER TRAINING IN TRANSLATIONAL AND APPLIED SCIENCE. THE COMPLETION OF THIS RESEARCH PROJECT AND TRAINING ACTIVITIES UNDER THE MENTORSHIP OF DRS. BROWN (SPONSOR), DUNCAN (CO-SPONSOR), AND TALMI (CO-SPONSOR) WILL SUPPORT THE APPLICANT’S CAREER GOAL OF BECOMING AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCHER FOCUSED ON RISK AND RESILIENCE PROCESSES FOR INTERGENERATIONAL HEALTH.

description: EVALUATING TRENDS AND IMPLEMENTATION DETERMINANTS OF POST-PANDEMIC SEDATION PRACTICES IN THE INTENSIVE CARE UNIT - PROJECT SUMMARY APPROXIMATELY 800,000 CRITICALLY ILL ADULT PATIENTS WITH ACUTE RESPIRATORY FAILURE REQUIRE INVASIVE MECHANICAL VENTILATION (IMV) EVERY YEAR, ACCOUNTING FOR 20-40% OF INTENSIVE CARE UNIT (ICU) ADMISSIONS IN THE US. NEARLY ALL OF THESE PATIENTS RECEIVE SEDATIVES TO TREAT ANXIETY, REDUCE EMOTIONAL DISTRESS, PREVENT AGITATION-RELATED HARM, AND FACILITATE SYNCHRONY WITH THE VENTILATOR. HOWEVER, CERTAIN SEDATIVE MEDICATIONS AS WELL AS DIFFERENTIAL DEPTHS OF SEDATION CONFER VARIABLE RISKS OF HARM TO THE PATIENT, AND – FOR THIS REASON – CLINICAL PRACTICE GUIDELINES RECOMMEND AGAINST THE USE OF BENZODIAZEPINES AND DEEP LEVELS OF SEDATION, WHICH IS DEFINED AS A RICHMOND AGITATION-SEDATION SCALE SCORE OF -3 TO -5. WHILE SEVERAL MULTIDISCIPLINARY IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES SUCCESSFULLY IMPROVED ADHERENCE TO THESE GUIDELINES BEFORE THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC, EMERGING DATA SUGGEST POST-PANDEMIC ICU SEDATION PRACTICES ARE LESS GUIDELINE-ADHERENT. THIS F32 AWARD SEEKS TO RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN ICU SEDATION PRACTICES AND IDENTIFY CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION DETERMINANTS OF GUIDELINE-RECOMMENDED SEDATION MANAGEMENT. TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS, THE SPECIFIC AIMS OF THIS PROPOSAL ARE: (1) IDENTIFY PERCEIVED BARRIERS AND FACILITATORS OF ADHERENCE TO GUIDELINE-RECOMMENDED ICU SEDATION PRACTICES IN THE POST-COVID ERA, AND (2) EVALUATE LONGITUDINAL TRENDS IN (A) BENZODIAZEPINE USE AND (B) SEDATION DEPTH AMONG IMV PATIENTS BEFORE, DURING, AND AFTER THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. THESE AIMS UTILIZE NOVEL QUALITATIVE AND QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL EPIDEMIOLOGIC APPROACHES TO FILL SPECIFIC TRAINING AND KNOWLEDGE GAPS THAT ARE FOUNDATIONAL FOR GENERATING NOVEL IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES THAT RE-ALIGN BEDSIDE ICU SEDATION PRACTICES WITH EVIDENCE- BASED GUIDELINES. AIM 1 UTILIZES SEMI-STRUCTURED MULTIDISCIPLINARY FOCUS GROUP INTERVIEWS THAT WILL BE ANALYZED VIA DIRECTED CONTENT ANALYSIS MAPPED ONTO IMPLEMENTATION FRAMEWORKS. AIM 2 WILL EMPLOY AN INTERRUPTED TIME SERIES ANALYSIS OF BENZODIAZEPINE USE AND EARLY SEDATION DEPTH BEFORE, DURING, AND AFTER THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC WITHIN A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT OF >14,000 IMV PATIENTS ACROSS FIVE HOSPITALS AND 14 ICUS. THESE STUDIES AND THEIR ASSOCIATED SKILLSET DEVELOPMENT WILL INFORM A K-SERIES CAREER DEVELOPMENT AWARD APPLICATION FOCUSED ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES THROUGH THE INTEGRATION OF HUMAN FACTORS ENGINEERING, HUMAN-CENTERED DESIGN, AND IMPLEMENTATION MAPPING. THESE STRATEGIES WILL THEN BE TESTED IN A FUTURE R01 AWARD FOR A PRAGMATIC CLINICAL TRIAL, THEREBY POSITIONING THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENTLY FUNDED PHYSICIAN SCIENTIST WHO IMPROVES ADHERENCE TO EVIDENCE-BASED SEDATION PRACTICES AND PROMOTES IMPROVED CLINICAL OUTCOMES FOR PATIENTS WITH ACUTE RESPIRATORY FAILURE RECEIVING IMV.

description: THERAPEUTIC TARGETING OF THE 5'-UNTRANSLATED REGION IN TITIN CARDIOMYOPATHY - PROJECT SUMMARY HETEROZYGOUS TRUNCATING FRAMESHIFT AND NONSENSE MUTATIONS IN THE MYOFILAMENT PROTEIN TITIN (TTN) ARE THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF NONISCHEMIC DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY (DCM), WHICH IS A LEADING CAUSE OF CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE. TITIN IS INDISPENSABLE FOR SARCOMERE FUNCTION SINCE IT IS A MOLECULAR SCAFFOLD FOR SARCOMERE ASSEMBLY, SIGNALING, AND HOMEOSTASIS. CURRENTLY, THERE ARE NO CURRENT TTN TARGETED THERAPIES AVAILABLE. PRIOR STUDIES DEMONSTRATED INCREASING TTN PROTEIN EXPRESSION VIA CRISPR ACTIVATION OR PROTEOSOME INHIBITION RESCUED THE IMPAIRED TTN TRUNCATING VARIANT (TTNTV) CONTRACTILE PHENOTYPE. UPSTREAM OPEN READINGS FRAMES (UORFS) IN THE 5’-UNTRANSLATED REGION (5’-UTR) HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO NEGATIVELY REGULATE TITIN TRANSLATION IN A MOUSE TITIN 5’-UTR LUCIFERASE REPORTER. FURTHERMORE, MUTATION OF THE UORFS IMPROVED TITIN TRANSLATIONAL EFFICIENCY. FOR THIS PROJECT, I HYPOTHESIZE THAT DISRUPTION OF THE HUMAN UORFS INCREASES NATIVE TITIN TRANSLATION AND RESCUES THE TITIN TRUNCATING DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY PHENOTYPE. AIM 1 WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THE UORFS NEGATIVELY REGULATE TTN TRANSLATION IN HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELL-DERIVED CARDIOMYOCYTES (HIPSC-CMS). CRISPR/CAS9 GENOME EDITING WILL BE USED TO MUTATE THE UORFS ELEMENTS TO CREATE THE TITIN OVEREXPRESSION MODEL, TTN-UORF-/- HIPSC-CM. IN CONTROL AND TTN-UORF-/- HIPSC-CMS, TTN PROTEIN LEVELS WILL BE ASSESSED BY VERTICAL GEL ELECTROPHORESIS (VAGE), PULSE LABEL ASSAYS. PARALLEL RIBO-SEQ AND RNA-SEQ WILL ASSESS TRANSLATIONAL EFFICIENCY. AIM 2 WILL TEST IF MUTAGENESIS OF THE UORFS IN A TTNTV DISEASE MODEL RESCUES FUNCTION. AIM 2 WILL USE CRISPR/CAS9 GENOME EDITING TO GENERATE THE DISEASE TTNTV EXON 329 TRUNCATION MODEL (TTN-329+/- HIPSC LINE) AND DUAL TTN- UORF-/--329+/- HIPSC-CM RESCUE MODEL. TOTAL TTN PROTEIN LEVELS WILL BE ASSESSED BY WESTERN BLOTTING AND VAGE. PARALLEL RIBO-SEQ AND RNA-SEQ WILL BE USED TO ASSESS TTN TRANSLATIONAL EFFICIENCY. CARDIOMYOCYTE FUNCTION WILL BE QUANTIFIED BY SINGLE CELL CONTRACTILITY ASSAYS AND 3D ENGINEERED HEART TISSUE FORCE ASSAYS. THE FINDINGS WILL INCREASE THE BIOLOGICAL UNDERSTANDING OF THE TTN 5’-UTR AND ITS POTENTIAL ROLE AS A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGET IN TTNTV DCM. DR. CADAR’S GOAL IS TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENT PHYSICIAN-SCIENTIST FOCUSED ON INHERITED CARDIOMYOPATHIES. DR. CADAR’S TRAINING PLAN WILL INCLUDE HANDS-ON TRAINING IN RIBO-SEQ AND RNA-SEQ (INSTRUMENTATION AND ANALYSIS) IN COLLABORATION WITH DR. SEZEN MEYDAN, SCIENTIFIC WRITING, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, BIOINFORMATIC COURSEWORK, AND CLINICAL GENETIC TRAINING. VANDERBILT UNIVERSITY IS AN EXCEPTIONAL TRAINING ENVIRONMENT WITH RESOURCES TO SUPPORT DR. CADAR’S DEVELOPMENT TOWARDS INDEPENDENCE.

description: LIGHTKEEPERS: BUILDING A TRIBAL CRISIS CONTINUUM - PROJECT NAME: LIGHTKEEPERS: BUILDING A TRIBAL CRISIS CONTINUUM LIGHTKEEPERS: BUILDING A TRIBAL CRISIS CONTINUUM IS TLINGIT & HAIDA'S INTEGRATED APPROACH TO STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY-BASED SUICIDE PREVENTION, CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE 988 PARTNERSHIPS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TREATMENT, CRISIS FOLLOW-UP, AND POSTVENTION SERVICES FOR TRIBAL CITIZENS THROUGHOUT SOUTHEAST ALASKA AND WASHINGTON STATE. BUILDING UPON THE TRIBE'S SUCCESSFUL COMMUNITY & BEHAVIORAL SERVICES (CBS) HEALING CENTER AND PREVIOUS SAMHSA 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE FUNDING, THIS PROJECT WILL EXPAND TRIBAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CAPACITY, STRENGTHEN CONNECTIONS TO THE 988 SUICIDE & CRISIS LIFELINE, AND INCREASE ACCESS TO CULTURALLY GROUNDED PREVENTION, CRISIS RESPONSE, TREATMENT, RECOVERY, AND HEALING SERVICES FOR AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE TRIBAL CITIZENS AND OTHER AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE INDIVIDUALS THROUGHOUT SOUTHEAST ALASKA AND THE PUGET SOUND REGION OF WASHINGTON STATE, WHERE 8,000 TRIBAL CITIZENS LIVE. SOUTHEAST ALASKA INCLUDES MORE THAN 25 COMMUNITIES ACROSS APPROXIMATELY 35,000 SQUARE MILES, MANY ACCESSIBLE ONLY BY AIR OR FERRY AND FACING SIGNIFICANT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE SHORTAGES AND BARRIERS TO CARE. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDES ALASKA NATIVE AND AMERICAN INDIAN YOUTH AND ADULTS EXPERIENCING SUICIDE RISK, MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE CHALLENGES, HISTORICAL AND INTERGENERATIONAL TRAUMA, AND BARRIERS TO CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE CARE. THROUGH EXPANSION OF THE CBS HEALING CENTER INTO WASHINGTON STATE, THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE OUTPATIENT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, CRISIS INTERVENTION, SUICIDE RISK ASSESSMENT, CARE COORDINATION, AND FOLLOW-UP SERVICES FOR TRIBAL CITIZENS ACROSS THE LIFESPAN. CAPACITY-BUILDING STRATEGIES INCLUDE STRENGTHENING PARTNERSHIPS WITH ALASKA AND WASHINGTON 988 PROVIDERS; IMPLEMENTING STANDARDIZED REFERRAL PATHWAYS AND WARM HANDOFF PROTOCOLS; EXPANDING THE LIGHTKEEPERS SUICIDE PREVENTION INITIATIVE; INCREASING CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES THROUGH THE CBS HEALING CENTER; EXPANDING THE WHEN CEDAR TOUCHES WATER POSTVENTION MODEL; DEVELOPING A TRIBAL 988 COMMUNICATION STRATEGY; STRENGTHENING WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT; AND IMPLEMENTING CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT AND EVALUATION ACTIVITIES. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) STRENGTHEN AN INTEGRATED TRIBAL CRISIS CONTINUUM CONNECTING PREVENTION, 988, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TREATMENT, AND POSTVENTION; (2) EXPAND COMMUNITY CAPACITY FOR SUICIDE PREVENTION THROUGH THE LIGHTKEEPERS INITIATIVE; (3) INCREASE ACCESS TO CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES BY EXPANDING THE CBS HEALING CENTER INTO WASHINGTON STATE; AND (4) STRENGTHEN POSTVENTION SERVICES, EVALUATION, AND LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY. KEY MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE ESTABLISHING FORMAL PARTNERSHIPS WITH WASHINGTON 988 PROVIDERS; STRENGTHENING REFERRAL COORDINATION AND FOLLOW-UP BETWEEN TRIBAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES AND 988; EXPANDING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH STAFFING AND SERVICES; INCREASING AWARENESS AND UTILIZATION OF THE 988 SUICIDE & CRISIS LIFELINE; PARTICIPATING IN SAMHSA'S CROSS-SITE EVALUATION; AND USING PERFORMANCE DATA TO CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVE PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION AND OUTCOMES.

description: CALIFORNIA 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PROJECT - RIVERSIDE–SAN BERNARDINO COUNTY INDIAN HEALTH, INC. (RSBCIHI) LEADS THE STATEWIDE CALIFORNIA 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE TASK FORCE—A PARTNERSHIP OF 988 CRISIS CENTERS, TRIBAL AND URBAN INDIAN HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS, AND FEDERAL AND STATE AGENCIES—TO EXPAND CULTURALLY GROUNDED CRISIS CARE AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO 988 SERVICES ACROSS ALL ELEVEN 988 CALL CENTERS AND THIRTY FIVE TRIBAL AND URBAN INDIAN HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS SERVING AI/AN PEOPLE STATEWIDE.  THE CALIFORNIA 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PROJECT SPANS 58 COUNTIES ACROSS SOUTHERN, CENTRAL, AND NORTHERN CALIFORNIA—FROM RIVERSIDE AND SAN BERNARDINO TO DEL NORTE, HUMBOLDT, BUTTE, SACRAMENTO, LOS ANGELES, ORANGE, VENTURA, SAN DIEGO, ALAMEDA, AND OTHERS. THESE COUNTIES ARE HOME TO 1.4 MILLION AI/AN PEOPLE AND 109 FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBES, THE LARGEST NUMBER OF ANY STATE. THIS PROJECT WILL REACH AI/AN YOUTH AND ADULTS STATEWIDE TO STRENGTHEN CRISIS RESPONSE ACROSS DIVERSE GEOGRAPHIES, FROM REMOTE RURAL REGIONS TO DENSE URBAN CENTERS.  THE 2026 PROJECT WILL EXPAND ON WORK COMPLETED BY THE TASK FORCE—ENGAGING ALL ELEVEN 988 CALL CENTERS AND ALL THIRTY FIVE TRIBAL AND URBAN INDIAN HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS IN CALIFORNIA TO STRENGTHEN CRISIS RESPONSE, IMPROVE REFERRAL CONNECTIONS, INCREASE AWARENESS AND UTILIZATION OF 988, AND UNIFY CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE TRAINING, COMMUNICATION, AND COORDINATED CRISIS PATHWAYS NEEDED TO SUPPORT 988 SERVICES NOW AND IN THE FUTURE. SEVERAL COMPONENTS OF THIS PROJECT—INCLUDING THE CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE TRAINING PLAN, THE HSQ 7 PILOT, AND DIGITAL COMMUNICATION MATERIALS—ARE DESIGNED FOR ADAPTATION AND REPLICATION NATIONWIDE TO SUPPORT AI/AN CRISIS RESPONSE EFFORTS ACROSS THE COUNTRY.  CAPACITY BUILDING GOALS INCLUDE:  • ESTABLISH AND MAINTAIN THE PROJECT TEAM • ESTABLISH AND MAINTAIN FORMAL COLLABORATIONS  • DEVELOP A SYSTEM TO COLLECT AND REPORT ON TRIBAL MEMBERS’ 988 UTILIZATION, SERVICE OUTCOMES, REFERRAL CONNECTIONS, AND FOLLOW-UP • DELIVER CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE TRAINING FOR 988 CRISIS CENTER STAFF  • DEVELOP CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE PROGRAMS AND PROTOCOLS TO MINIMIZE SUICIDE RISK AMONG STUDENTS AND ENSURE TIMELY ACCESS TO CRISIS SERVICES • DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT, AND MAINTAIN A TRIBAL 988 COMMUNICATION STRATEGY  THE OBJECTIVES DIRECTLY ADVANCE SAMHSA’S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES BY STRENGTHENING CRISIS SYSTEM COORDINATION, EXPANDING CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE CARE, IMPROVING DATA INTEGRATION, AND BUILDING A CRISIS READY WORKFORCE. OBJECTIVES 2.1–2.2 ADVANCE COORDINATED SYSTEMS OF CARE THROUGH FORMAL STATEWIDE PARTNERSHIPS. OBJECTIVES 3.1–3.2 STRENGTHEN DATA DRIVEN DECISION MAKING THROUGH EXPANDED AI/AN SPECIFIC 988 UTILIZATION AND OUTCOME REPORTING. OBJECTIVE 4.1 SUPPORTS SAMHSA’S WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PRIORITY THROUGH STATEWIDE CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE TRAINING. OBJECTIVE 5.1 ALIGNS WITH YOUTH SUICIDE PREVENTION PRIORITIES BY DEVELOPING CULTURALLY GROUNDED STUDENT CRISIS PROTOCOLS. OBJECTIVE 6.1 INCREASES AWARENESS AND ACCESS TO CRISIS SERVICES THROUGH STATEWIDE DISSEMINATION OF TRIBAL 988 COMMUNICATION MATERIALS. TOGETHER, THESE OBJECTIVES EMBED TRAUMA INFORMED, CULTURALLY GROUNDED BEST PRACTICES ACROSS CALIFORNIA’S CRISIS CONTINUUM.

description: SPTHB 988 2.0 PROGRAM - PROJECT ABSTRACT SOUTHERN PLAINS TRIBAL HEALTH BOARD OKLAHOMA 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE FY 2026 SAMHSA SUPPORT FOR 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE COOPERATIVE AGREEMENTS (FG-26-003)  THE SOUTHERN PLAINS TRIBAL HEALTH BOARD (SPTHB) PROPOSES TO STRENGTHEN 988 CRISIS RESPONSE SERVICES FOR AMERICAN INDIAN/ALASKA NATIVE (AI/AN) INDIVIDUALS THROUGHOUT OKLAHOMA. BUILDING ON ITS FY 2023 SAMHSA TRIBAL 988 RESPONSE COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT, SPTHB WILL EXPAND STATEWIDE TRIBAL CRISIS RESPONSE CAPACITY BY STRENGTHENING PARTNERSHIPS WITH OKLAHOMA'S 988 CRISIS CENTERS, IMPROVING REFERRAL AND FOLLOW-UP SYSTEMS, EXPANDING CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE CRISIS RESPONSE PRACTICES, INCREASING 988 UTILIZATION, AND INCREASING COORDINATION AMONG TRIBAL, STATE, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS. OKLAHOMA IS HOME TO THE NATION'S THIRD-LARGEST NATIVE AMERICAN POPULATION, WITH AI/AN INDIVIDUALS REPRESENTING APPROXIMATELY 14% OF THE STATE'S POPULATION. DESPITE RECENT PROGRESS, GAPS REMAIN IN TRIBAL CALLER IDENTIFICATION, STANDARDIZED REFERRAL PATHWAYS, WARM HANDOFF PROTOCOLS, AND TIMELY ACCESS TO CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE FOLLOW-UP CARE. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN FORMAL PARTNERSHIPS WITH OKLAHOMA'S 988 CRISIS CENTERS, TRIBAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROGRAMS, TRIBAL FOCUSED NON-PROFITS, SCHOOLS, FIRST RESPONDERS, AND OTHER COMMUNITY PARTNERS; EXPAND CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE TRAINING; IMPROVE TRIBAL CALLER IDENTIFICATION AND REFERRAL PROCESSES; SUPPORT PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SPECIALISTS PROVIDING POST-CRISIS FOLLOWUP; ENHANCE DATA COLLECTION AND SPARS REPORTING; DEVELOP A TRIBAL 988 COMMUNICATION STRATEGY; STRENGTHEN THE STATEWIDE TR988 WORKGROUP; AND CREATE A TRIBAL CRISIS RESPONSE BEST PRACTICES TOOLKIT TO IMPROVE STATEWIDE COORDINATION AND CONSISTENCY. GROUNDED IN TRIBAL LEADERSHIP, EVIDENCE-INFORMED PRACTICES, AND MORE THAN 50 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE SERVING TRIBAL COMMUNITIES, SPTHB WILL LEVERAGE ESTABLISHED PARTNERSHIPS AND LESSONS LEARNED FROM ITS PREVIOUS TRIBAL 988 AWARD TO STRENGTHEN OKLAHOMA'S STATEWIDE CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEM AND IMPROVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR AI/AN INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES.

THE GEOGRAPHIC CATCHMENT AREA, THE COMANCHE TRIBAL JURISDICTION AREA, REFLECTS A POPULATION WHERE AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE INDIVIDUALS MAKE UP 11% OF RESIDENTS, MORE THAN FIVE TIMES THE NATIONAL AVERAGE, AND WHERE 988 CRISIS INFRASTRUCTURE STILL NEEDS DEEPER INTEGRATION ACROSS CALL CENTERS, SCHOOLS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND TRIBAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES. description: OSAGE NATION SI-SI A-PE-TXA TRIBAL 988 RESPONSE - OSAGE NATION SI-SI A-PE-TXA (ONSSAPT) PROPOSES THE TRIBAL 988 CONTINUUM OF CARE EXPANSION AND CRISIS RESPONSE ENHANCEMENT INITIATIVE TO STRENGTHEN AND EXPAND CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS SERVICES THROUGHOUT THE OSAGE NATION SERVICE AREA AND OSAGE COUNTY, OKLAHOMA. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS PERSISTENT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISPARITIES EXPERIENCED BY AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE POPULATIONS, INCLUDING ELEVATED RATES OF SUICIDE, SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, TRAUMA EXPOSURE, AND LIMITED ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES IN RURAL COMMUNITIES. KEY PROJECT PERSONNEL INCLUDE A FULL-TIME PROJECT DIRECTOR, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROGRAM COORDINATOR, CRISIS CARE NAVIGATOR, PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SPECIALIST, COMMUNITY OUTREACH AND EDUCATION SPECIALIST, AND A PART-TIME DATA AND EVALUATION COORDINATOR. THROUGH THIS INITIATIVE, ONSSAPT WILL STRENGTHEN THE TRIBAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS CONTINUUM, INCREASE COMMUNITY AWARENESS AND UTILIZATION OF THE 988 SUICIDE & CRISIS LIFELINE, IMPROVE ACCESS TO CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, AND ESTABLISH A SUSTAINABLE, COORDINATED SYSTEM OF CARE THAT IMPROVES BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR OSAGE NATION CITIZENS AND RESIDENTS THROUGHOUT THE SERVICE AREA.

description: TEXAS NATIVE HEALTH 988 LIFELINE PROGRAM - TEXAS NATIVE HEALTH (TNH), THE ONLY AAAHC-ACCREDITED URBAN INDIAN ORGANIZATION IN THE STATE OF TEXAS, REQUESTS $1,365,000 ANNUALLY FOR THIS 3 YEAR CYCLE TO EXPAND CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE 988 SUICIDE AND CRISIS LIFELINE ACCESS FOR AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE (AI/AN) INDIVIDUALS ACROSS THE STATE OF TEXAS. BUILDING ON A FUNDED FY 2023 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE AWARD, TNH WILL STRENGTHEN EMBEDDED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CAPACITY, DEEPEN CRISIS CENTER PARTNERSHIPS, AND INCREASE 988 AWARENESS AMONG AI/AN INDIVIDUALS WHO FACE THE HIGHEST SUICIDE MORTALITY RATE OF ANY RACIAL OR ETHNIC GROUP IN THE NATION.  TNH SERVES AI/AN INDIVIDUALS ACROSS DALLAS-FORT WORTH, HOUSTON, SAN ANTONIO, AND AUSTIN. CRITICAL CAPACITY GAPS INCLUDE LIMITED WARM HANDOFF INFRASTRUCTURE BETWEEN 988 CRISIS CONTACT CENTERS AND CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE FOLLOW-UP CARE, INSUFFICIENT AI/AN CULTURAL COMPETENCY TRAINING AMONG CRISIS CENTER STAFF, AND LOW 988 AWARENESS OUTSIDE THE DFW CORRIDOR. IN 2022, THE SUICIDE RATE AMONG NON-HISPANIC AI/AN PERSONS WAS 91% GREATER THAN THE OVERALL U.S. POPULATION RATE, AND AI/AN ADULTS IN 2024 WERE 17% LESS LIKELY THAN U.S. ADULTS OVERALL TO HAVE RECEIVED MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT IN THE PAST YEAR. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS FUNDING IS TO ENSURE AI/AN INDIVIDUALS IN URBAN TEXAS HAVE ACCESS TO A COORDINATED, CULTURALLY GROUNDED CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEM THEY TRUST.   THE POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDES AI/AN INDIVIDUALS OF ALL AGES, WITH HIGHEST NEED AMONG THOSE AGED 25 TO 44, YOUTH, VETERANS, AND INDIVIDUALS INVOLVED WITH CRIMINAL JUSTICE AND CHILD WELFARE SYSTEMS. TNH'S THREE GOALS AND NINE MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES ADVANCE SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES OF EXPANDING CRISIS INTERVENTION CARE AND PREVENTING SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS. GOAL 1 TARGETS MOU EXECUTION WITH CRISIS CONTACT CENTER PARTNERS BY MONTH 6 OF YEAR 1, A 75% WARM HANDOFF COMPLETION RATE BY YEAR 1 END, AND 80% OF INDIVIDUALS SCREENED RECEIVING A DOCUMENTED REFERRAL DISPOSITION WITHIN THE SAME CARE ENCOUNTER. GOAL 2 TARGETS A REFERRAL COMPLETION RATE OF 70% OR HIGHER BY YEAR 1 INCREASING TO 80% BY YEAR 3, MEASURABLE QIP IMPROVEMENT IN AT LEAST TWO PERFORMANCE INDICATORS PER REPORTING CYCLE, AND 100% SPARS COMPLIANCE THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT PERIOD. GOAL 3 TARGETS 80% OF CULTURAL COMPETENCY TRAINING PARTICIPANTS DEMONSTRATING 20% OR GREATER KNOWLEDGE GAIN ANNUALLY, A 25% INCREASE IN REPORTED 988 AWARENESS AMONG EVENT PARTICIPANTS BY YEAR 3, AND A 20% ANNUAL INCREASE IN COMMUNICATIONS CAMPAIGN REACH BEGINNING YEAR 1.  TNH WILL IMPLEMENT ALL SIX REQUIRED ACTIVITIES: RENEWING AND EXPANDING MOUS WITH CRISIS CONTACT CENTERS IN HOUSTON AND AUSTIN AND WITH AITSCM IN SAN ANTONIO; IMPLEMENTING A FIVE-STAGE DATA MANAGEMENT WORKFLOW; DELIVERING AI/AN CULTURAL COMPETENCY TRAINING TO A MINIMUM OF 50 PROVIDERS ANNUALLY; ENGAGING DALLAS ISD, DALLAS POLICE DEPARTMENT, AND FIRST RESPONDER AGENCIES ACROSS ALL FIVE TARGET CITIES; PARTICIPATING FULLY IN SAMHSA'S NATIONAL CROSS-SITE EVALUATION; AND EXECUTING A 988 COMMUNICATIONS STRATEGY ALIGNED WITH SAMHSA'S 988 PARTNER TOOLKIT.

description: SUPPORT FOR 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE COOPERATIVE AGREEMENTS - THE IOWA TRIBE OF OKLAHOMA WILL EXPAND TRIBAL ACCESS TO THE 988 SUICIDE AND CRISIS LIFELINE FOR AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE INDIVIDUALS IN PAYNE, LINCOLN, AND LOGAN COUNTIES, OKLAHOMA. THIS AREA IS HOME TO 170,356 RESIDENTS INCLUDING 16,306 AMERICAN INDIAN/ALASKA NATIVE (AI/AN). PROJECT GOALS: GOAL 1: ENSURE AI/AN RESIDENTS OF THE ITO CATCHMENT AREA HAVE ACCESS TO CULTURALLY COMPETENT, TRAINED 988 CRISIS CENTER SUPPORT. GOAL 2: IMPROVE COORDINATED INTEGRATION AND FOLLOW-UP CARE BETWEEN 988 CRISIS CENTERS AND ITO. GOAL 3: FACILITATE COLLABORATION WITH TRIBAL, STATE, AND COMMUNITY SYSTEM PARTNERS IN A MANNER THAT RESPECTS TRIBAL SOVEREIGNTY. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: BY YEAR 1, PLACE AND TRAIN AN EMBEDDED CULTURAL LIAISON AT AN OKLAHOMA 988 CALL CENTER AND ACHIEVE A DOCUMENTED INCREASE IN SUCCESSFUL AI/AN REFERRAL LINKAGE TO BAH-KHO-JE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES (SAMHSA STRATEGIC PRIORITY: CRISIS CARE). MAINTAIN 100% SAME/NEXT-BUSINESS-DAY APPOINTMENT ACCESS FOR AI/AN 988

description: AICA - 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PROGRAM - THE AMERICAN INDIAN CENTER OF ARKANSAS (AICA) PROPOSES TO IMPLEMENT THE 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PROGRAM, A THREE-YEAR, MULTI-STATE CAPACITY-BUILDING INITIATIVE DESIGNED TO STRENGTHEN CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEMS FOR AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE (AI/AN) COMMUNITIES IN ARKANSAS AND LOUISIANA. description: THE RED ROAD TO INTERPERSONAL POWER: BUILDING TRUST AND CAPACITY IN THE 988 CRISIS SYSTEM - THE RED ROAD TO INTERPERSONAL POWER: BUILDING TRUST AND CAPACITY IN THE 988 CRISIS SYSTEM IS A CAPACITY BUILDING INITIATIVE OF THE RHODE ISLAND INDIAN COUNCIL (RIIC) TO STRENGTHEN CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE 988 CRISIS RESPONSE FOR AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE (AI/AN) COMMUNITIES IN RHODE ISLAND, CONNECTICUT, AND MASSACHUSETTS. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES ELEVATED SUICIDE AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH RISK, HISTORIC TRAUMA, AND LOW TRUST IN CRISIS SYSTEMS BY CREATING NATIVE LED AND NATIVE-INFORMED INFRASTRUCTURE SO AI/AN INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES CAN ACCESS CULTURALLY COMPETENT, TRAINED 988 CRISIS CENTER SUPPORT AND FOLLOW UP CARE THAT IS WORTHY OF NATIVE TRUST. GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT APPROXIMATELY 33,000 NATIVE PEOPLE LIVE IN DIVERSE SETTINGS IN TRIBAL AND URBAN NATIVE COMMUNITIES IN SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND. CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS WILL START AND BUILD COORDINATION BETWEEN 988 CENTERS, TRIBAL NATIONS, URBAN INDIAN ORGANIZATIONS, INDIAN HEALTH SERVICE, AND OTHER PARTNERS; IMPROVE CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE REFERRAL PATHWAYS AND DATA SYSTEMS; AND ENHANCE WORKFORCE SKILLS TO RESPOND EFFECTIVELY TO AI/AN CALLERS. POPULATION OF FOCUS THE POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDES AI/AN ADULTS AND YOUTH EXPERIENCING DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, TRAUMA, SUICIDAL IDEATION, AND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS; ELDERS FACING ISOLATION AND UNMET BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS; NATIVE VETERANS WITH ELEVATED TRAUMA AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH RISK; YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 15–24 AT HIGH SUICIDE RISK; AND INDIVIDUALS EXPERIENCING POVERTY, HOUSING INSTABILITY, UNEMPLOYMENT, AND SYSTEMS INVOLVEMENT. THESE GROUPS EXPERIENCE SUICIDE AND SUBSTANCE USE RATES THAT EXCEED NATIONAL AVERAGES AND FACE PERSISTENT BARRIERS TO CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE SERVICES AND SAFE, TRUSTED CRISIS INTERVENTION. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS RIIC WILL CONVENE A NATIVE 988 ADVISORY COUNCIL, FORMALIZE PARTNERSHIPS WITH 988 CENTERS AND TRIBAL PARTNERS, AND BRAID INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE WITH GOLD STANDARD SCIENCE FOR IMPLEMENTATION. KEY STRATEGIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING AND DELIVERING CULTURALLY GROUNDED COUNSELOR TRAINING, HOSTING IMMERSIVE CULTURAL TEACHING AND HEALING RETREATS, IMPLEMENTING A TRIBAL 988 COMMUNICATION STRATEGY AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES, REFINING REFERRAL AND FOLLOW UP PROTOCOLS, AND BUILDING DATA SYSTEMS ALIGNED WITH SAMHSA PERFORMANCE MEASURES AND SPARS REPORTING. PROJECT GOALS AND MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES THE PROJECT GOAL IS TO BUILD A CULTURALLY COMPETENT 988 SERVICE DELIVERY STRUCTURE SO AI/AN COMMUNITIES IN THE TARGET GEOGRAPHY HAVE ACCESS TO CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE, TRAINED CRISIS SUPPORT, NAVIGATION, AND FOLLOW UP CARE THROUGH TRUSTED PARTNERSHIPS AND NATIVE LEADERSHIP. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE ESTABLISHING A NATIVE 988 ADVISORY COUNCIL WITH HIGH PARTICIPATION FORMAL AGREEMENTS; ENSURING AT LEAST 95% OF CRISIS COUNSELORS MEET CULTURAL RESPONSIVENESS COMPETENCIES; CONDUCTING AT LEAST SIX CULTURALLY GROUNDED COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES PER YEAR; INCREASING THE NUMBER OF 988 CALLERS WHO SELF IDENTIFY AS AI/AN BY 20% BY YEAR 2 AND 35% BY YEAR 3; INCREASING AI/AN CALLER SATISFACTION SCORES AS A PROXY FOR TRUST; AND ACHIEVING AT LEAST 95% COMPLETENESS AND ACCURACY IN REQUIRED SPARS DATA FIELDS, ALL OF WHICH ADVANCE SAMHSA STRATEGIC PRIORITIES FOR CRISIS INTERVENTION, CULTURAL RELEVANCE, AND EVALUATION.

description: GREAT PLAINS 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE - THE GREAT PLAINS 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN SOUTH DAKOTA’S (SD) CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEM BY INCREASING AWARENESS, ACCESSIBILITY, AND UTILIZATION OF THE 988 SUICIDE & CRISIS LIFELINE AMONG AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE (AI/AN) COMMUNITIES. THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH TRIBAL NATIONS, THE 988 LIFELINE CENTER, URBAN INDIAN ORGANIZATIONS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS, THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE CRISIS RESPONSE COORDINATION, STRENGTHEN REFERRAL PATHWAYS, EXPAND RESOURCES, AND INCREASE AWARENESS OF 988 SERVICES. THESE EFFORTS WILL HELP REDUCE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISPARITIES AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO CRISIS SUPPORT FOR AI/AN INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES STATEWIDE. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE ALL OF SD, INCLUDING THE STATE’S NINE FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBAL NATIONS AND AI/AN POPULATIONS RESIDING IN RAPID CITY AND SIOUX FALLS. SD IS HOME TO APPROXIMATELY 93,443 AI/AN RESIDENTS, REPRESENTING 10.5% OF THE STATE’S POPULATION. AI/AN COMMUNITIES EXPERIENCE SIGNIFICANT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS, INCLUDING ACCESSING CRISIS SERVICES, LIMITED AWARENESS OF 988, GEOGRAPHIC ISOLATION, TRANSPORTATION CHALLENGES, SHORTAGES OF PROVIDERS, AND INSUFFICIENT INTEGRATION OF TRIBAL RESOURCES INTO STATEWIDE CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEMS. AI/AN INDIVIDUALS ALSO EXPERIENCE DISPROPORTIONATELY HIGH RATES OF SUICIDE, SELF-HARM, SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICE UTILIZATION. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDES AI/AN CHILDREN, YOUTH, ADULTS, AND ELDERS LIVING BOTH ON AND OFF TRIBAL LANDS. PARTICULAR EMPHASIS WILL BE PLACED ON YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS, WHO ACCOUNT FOR A DISPROPORTIONATE SHARE OF AI/AN SUICIDE DEATHS IN SD. THE PROJECT WILL BENEFIT INDIVIDUALS EXPERIENCING MENTAL HEALTH CRISES, SUICIDAL IDEATION, SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, GRIEF AND LOSS, AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES. WHILE THIS IS PRIMARILY A CAPACITY-BUILDING INITIATIVE, THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE SUPPORT AND REFERRAL SERVICES FOR AI/AN INDIVIDUALS ACCESSING 988 THROUGH CALLS, TEXTS, AND CHATS. TO INCREASE CAPACITY, THE GREAT PLAINS TRIBAL LEADERS’ HEALTH BOARD WILL IMPLEMENT SEVERAL EVIDENCE-BASED AND CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE STRATEGIES. THESE INCLUDE ESTABLISHING PARTNERSHIPS WITH STATE, TRIBAL, AND LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS; SUPPORTING A DEDICATED 988 COUNSELOR POSITION WITHIN THE HELPLINE CENTER TO IMPROVE REFERRALS AND LINKAGES; UPDATING A CULTURAL CRISIS-RESPONSE HANDBOOK; DEVELOPING A TRIBAL-SPECIFIC 988 DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING SYSTEM; PROVIDING SUICIDE PREVENTION, INTERVENTION, AND POSTVENTION TRAINING; EXPANDING CULTURALLY INFORMED OUTREACH AND EDUCATION CAMPAIGNS; SUPPORTING SUICIDE PREVENTION PROGRAMMING; DISTRIBUTING HEALING KITS AND HOPE BASKETS; AND PARTICIPATING IN STATEWIDE COALITIONS AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) STRENGTHEN COLLABORATION BETWEEN TRIBAL COMMUNITIES AND 988 CRISIS CENTERS; (2) IMPROVE COORDINATION, REFERRAL SYSTEMS, DATA COLLECTION, AND FOLLOW-UP CARE; (3) ENHANCE TRAINING FOR STAFF AND PARTNERS; (4) INCREASE AWARENESS AND UTILIZATION OF 988 SERVICES ACROSS TRIBAL COMMUNITIES; (5) SUPPORT EVALUATION AND QUALITY IMPROVEMENT; AND (6) IMPLEMENT A SUSTAINABLE TRIBAL 988 COMMUNICATION STRATEGY. KEY MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE ESTABLISHING PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENTS; ENGAGING ALL SD TRIBES THROUGH TRIBAL LIAISONS; MAINTAINING A DEDICATED 988 COUNSELOR POSITION; DISTRIBUTING A REVISED CULTURAL HANDBOOK TO PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS; PROVIDING TRAININGS; IMPLEMENTING A TRIBAL 988 DATA-TRACKING SYSTEM; CONDUCTING ANNUAL OUTREACH ACROSS ALL NINE TRIBES AND TWO URBAN CENTERS; DELIVERING SUICIDE PREVENTION SESSIONS ANNUALLY; DISTRIBUTING HEALING KITS MONTHLY AND HOPE BASKETS ANNUALLY; AND IMPLEMENTING A COMPREHENSIVE TRIBAL 988 COMMUNICATIONS CAMPAIGN THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT PERIOD. BY STRENGTHENING CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE CRISIS-SERVICE CAPACITY AND INCREASING AWARENESS AND UTILIZATION OF 988, THE GREAT PLAINS 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PROJECT WILL ADVANCE SUICIDE PREVENTION, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, AND COMMUNITY-BASED CRISIS RESPONSE FOR AI/AN COMMUNITIES ACROSS SD.

description: IMPROVING WABANAKI TRIBAL 988 RESPONSE - THIS APPLICATION, IMPROVING WABANAKI TRIBAL 988 RESPONSE, WILL UTILIZE WABANAKI PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELLNESS' (WPHW) 24/7/365 CRISIS WARM LINE, THE WABANAKI CARELINE, TO ENHANCE OUR CAPACITY AND SERVICES TO BE THE TRIBAL 988 AUTHORITY IN MAINE. THIS PROJECT WILL SERVE WABANAKI PEOPLE IN MAINE WHEREVER THEY ARE, WITH PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO NORTHERN AND EASTERN RURAL COUNTIES. THE FIVE WABANAKI COMMUNITIES SERVED BY WABANAKI PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELLNESS (WPHW) EXPERIENCE SIGNIFICANT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISPARITIES THAT ARE COMPOUNDED BY RURAL GEOGRAPHY, HISTORICAL TRAUMA, LIMITED SERVICE AVAILABILITY, AND SOCIOECONOMIC BARRIERS. THESE FACTORS CREATE SUBSTANTIAL CHALLENGES IN ACCESSING TIMELY, CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE CRISIS SERVICES FOR CHILDREN, ADULTS, VETERANS, ELDERS, AND OTHER POPULATIONS AT ELEVATED RISK FOR SUICIDE, OVERDOSE, AND PSYCHIATRIC CRISES. THE STATE OF MAINE HAS MOBILE RESPONSE SERVICES OFFERED THROUGHOUT THE STATE, BUT THERE ARE SIGNIFICANT GAPS WHEN IT COMES TO CULTURALLY COMPETENT SERVICES FOR TRIBAL MEMBERS. DURING A CRISIS, HAVING RESPONSE SERVICES THAT ARE NOT CULTURALLY FOCUSED AND EDUCATED CAN LEAD TO LACK OF TRUST AND POORER OUTCOMES.  THE GOALS FOR THIS PROJECT ARE; 1) IN YEAR 1 OF THE PROJECT, WPHW WILL ENHANCE CARELINE CAPACITY THROUGH HIRING, TRAINING, OUTREACH, AND QUALITY IMPROVEMENT TO STRENGTHEN SERVICES WHERE INDICATED, AND 2) IN YEARS 1 THROUGH 3 OF THE PROJECT, WPHW WILL DEVELOP AND MAINTAIN A PARTNERSHIP NETWORK BY CREATING AND STRENGTHENING RELATIONSHIPS WITH COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS, INCLUDING OTHER GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS, TRIBAL LEADERSHIP, AND STATE ENTITIES. TO DO THIS, WPHW’S OBJECTIVES INCLUDE, INCREASE SERVICE VOLUME AND CATCHMENT AREA BY ENHANCING STAFF CAPACITY FROM 2 STAFF TO 5 STAFF BY MONTH 12, TRAIN 100% OF GRANT-FUNDED STAFF WITHIN 6 MONTHS OF HIRE AND OFFER 1 TRAINING OPPORTUNITY TO PARTNERS ANNUALLY, CONDUCT A MINIMUM OF 12 OUTREACH EVENTS ANNUALLY AND DISTRIBUTE 988/CULTURALLY-FOCUSED EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS AT EACH EVENT, IMPLEMENT A CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT (CQI) PROCESS BY MONTH 4 AND ASSESS QUARTERLY, EXECUTE MOUS THAT HIGHLIGHT REFERRAL PATHWAYS AND DATA TRACKING WITH MAINE CRISIS LINE AND OFFICE OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WITHIN 6 MONTHS, COLLABORATE WITH LEADERSHIP IN ALL 5 TRIBAL COMMUNITIES QUARTERLY TO IDENTIFY NEEDS AND SPREAD AWARENESS OF SERVICES.

description: DNHC 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE - THE EASTERN SHOSHONE TRIBE IS LOCATED ON THE WIND RIVER RESERVATION (WRR) IN CENTRAL WYOMING. WITH OVER 2.2 MILLION ACRES OF LAND, THE WRR IS HOME TO THE EASTERN SHOSHONE TRIBE. THE EASTERN SHOSHONE RECOVERY PROGRAM, NOW DOING BUSINESS AS THE DOYA NATSU HEALING CENTER (DHNC), OF THE EASTERN SHOSHONE TRIBE, DEVELOPED THIS PROPOSAL. ACCORDING TO THE EASTERN SHOSHONE ENROLLMENT OFFICE, THERE ARE 4,510 ENROLLED MEMBERS AND 3,138 DESCENDANT MEMBERS, FOR A TOTAL OF 7,648 PEOPLE. ACCESS TO MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES, SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH THERAPIES IS LIMITED ON THE WRR BECAUSE OF THE RURAL LOCATION, LIMITED TRANSPORTATION, STIGMA SURROUNDING MENTAL HEALTH, DIGITAL INEQUALITY, AND LONG WAIT TIMES FOR SERVICES. FREMONT COUNTY IS A DESIGNATED HEALTHCARE PROVIDER SHORTAGE AREA, AND LOW PAY, BURNOUT, AND COVID-19 HAVE COMPOUNDED THE CHALLENGES OF ACCESSING TRAINED MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS (WYOMING DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, 2022). DATA PROVIDED BY THE ROCKY MOUNTAIN TRIBAL EPIDEMIOLOGY CENTER SHOW THAT ANXIETY IS THE NUMBER ONE MENTAL HEALTH ISSUE BEING EXPERIENCED BY NATIVE COMMUNITIES, WITH 1,010 CASES REPORTED FROM 2016 TO 2020, AND AN AGE-ADJUSTED RATE OF 917.1 PER 10,000. DATA FROM THE INDIAN HEALTH SERVICE NATIONAL DATA WAREHOUSE SHOWS THAT FROM 2016 TO 2020, 246 INDIVIDUALS WERE TREATED AT THE DNHC CLINIC BECAUSE OF SELF-HARM, WHICH INCLUDES SELF-INJURY AND SELF-MUTILATION. DATA FROM THE CWCC INDICATE THERE WERE 6,516 CALLS TO THE 988 LIFELINE IN WYOMING IN 2024; OF THESE, 234 WERE FROM FREMONT COUNTY, AND 36 OF THOSE CALLERS WERE AIAN. ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR) DATA FROM DNHC SHOW THAT TRAUMA AND VIOLENCE ARE SHARED EXPERIENCES AMONG CLIENTS, AND 71% OF FEMALE CLIENTS REPORT LIFETIME TRAUMA (DNHC, 2025A).   THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE DNHC 988 PROJECT IS TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND USE OF THE 988 LIFELINE ON WRR AND TO TRAIN DNHC STAFF AND PARTNERING ORGANIZATIONS USING CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE AND CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE METHODS. OBJECTIVE 1: DURING THE FIRST 6 MONTHS OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, FROM SEPTEMBER 30, 2026, TO APRIL 30, 2027, THE DNHC TEAM WILL WORK WITH STATE AND LOCAL CRISIS CENTERS TO STRENGTHEN COORDINATION AND IMPROVE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF 988 RESPONSE AND LINKAGE TO TRIBAL RESOURCES THROUGH CULTURALLY TAILORED COMMUNICATIONS AND TRAINING WITH A MINIMUM OF 20 STAFF.  OBJECTIVE 2: DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD FROM SEPTEMBER 30, 2026, TO SEPTEMBER 29, 2029, THE DNHC TEAM WILL ESTABLISH AND STRENGTHEN COLLABORATIONS WITH STATES, TERRITORIES, AND LOCAL CRISIS CENTERS TO IMPROVE PARTNERSHIPS WITH CRISIS CONTACT CENTERS AND SERVICE PROVISION RESOURCES AND DEVELOP A SYSTEM TO COLLECT AND REPORT ON TRIBAL MEMBERS' 988 UTILIZATION, SERVICE OUTCOMES, REFERRAL CONNECTIONS WHEN AVAILABLE, AND FOLLOW-UP.  OBJECTIVE 3: DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD FROM SEPTEMBER 30, 2026, TO SEPTEMBER 29, 2027, THE DNHC TEAM WILL COLLABORATE WITH THE STATE OF WYOMING DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND LOCAL CRISIS CENTERS (CWCC AND WYOMING LIFELINE) ON THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE TRAINING FOR CRISIS CALL CENTER STAFF REACHING 20+ PEOPLE.  OBJECTIVE 4: DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD FROM SEPTEMBER 30, 2026, TO SEPTEMBER 29, 2029, THE DNHC TEAM WILL PARTNER WITH A MINIMUM OF TEN COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, INCLUDING SCHOOLS, SCHOOL-BASED MENTAL HEALTH PROGRAMS AT FORT WASHAKIE SCHOOLS, BOYS AND GIRLS CLUB, TRIBAL LAW ENFORCEMENT, FIRST RESPONDERS, AND OTHER MULTI-SECTORAL SYSTEM PARTNERS WITHIN THE WRR TO PROMOTE 988 RESOURCES.  OBJECTIVE 5: DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD FROM SEPTEMBER 30, 2026, TO SEPTEMBER 29, 2029, THE DNHC TEAM AND AT LEAST ONE PARTNER WILL DEVELOP A NEW CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE PROGRAM AND PROTOCOL AIMED AT MINIMIZING SUICIDE RISK AMONG STUDENTS AND ENSURING TIMELY ACCESS TO CRISIS SERVICES USING THE 988 RESOURCES AND INFORMATION DEVELOPED FROM THIS PROJECT.

description: ALBUQUERQUE AREA INDIAN HEALTH BOARD 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PROJECT - AAIHB 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PROJECT  THE 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PROJECT IS A COLLABORATION BETWEEN A TRIBAL SERVING ORGANIZATION, THE ALBUQUERQUE AREA INDIAN HEALTH BOARD, INC. (AAIHB), AND SIX ALBUQUERQUE AREA INDIAN HEALTH SERVICE (IHS) AREA TRIBES - MESCALERO APACHE TRIBE, RAMAH NAVAJO, TO'HAJIILEE NAVAJO, SOUTHERN UTE INDIAN TRIBE, ISLETA PUEBLO, AND ZUNI PUEBLO. ALL SIX COMMUNITIES ARE FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBES LOCATED IN RURAL NEW MEXICO AND SOUTHERN COLORADO. THE TOTAL POPULATION FOR THESE COMMUNITIES’ RANGES FROM 1,567 – 5,864 WITH A MEDIAN AGE OF 38.7 WITH HALF OF THE POPULATION BEING FEMALE. THE MEDIAN INCOME ACROSS ALL SIX COMMUNITIES IS $24,190 ANNUALLY. IN NEW MEXICO (NM) THE SUICIDE RATE FOR AI/AN POPULATION IS 26.2 DEATHS PER 100,000 RESIDENTS WHEREAS COLORADO’S AI/AN POPULATION SUICIDE RATE IS 17.3 PER 100,000 RESIDENTS.   MANY TRIBAL COMMUNITIES ARE IN RURAL AND GEOGRAPHICALLY ISOLATED AREAS WHERE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, CRISIS STABILIZATION SERVICES, AND MOBILE CRISIS TEAMS ARE LIMITED. WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, TRANSPORTATION CHALLENGES, AND CONCERNS REGARDING PRIVACY AND CONFIDENTIALITY FURTHER REDUCE ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES. THE AAIHB 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PROJECT IS THEREFORE SORELY NEEDED IN OUR REGION AND WILL AIM TO DISMANTLE THESE PERSISTENT BARRIERS AND FILL THE EXISTING VOID IN SERVICES BY CREATING CRITICAL LINKAGES BETWEEN TRIBES AND EXISTING 988 CRISIS CENTERS TO ENSURE AI/ANS HAVE READY ACCESS TO CULTURALLY COMPETENT SERVICES THAT HONOR TRIBAL SOVEREIGNTY. CREATING A FORMAL PARTNERSHIP WITH THE NEW MEXICO AND COLORADO 988 LIFELINE CENTERS WILL STRENGTHEN THE CONTINUUM OF CRISIS CARE FOR TRIBAL COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE TWO STATES. DEVELOPING STRONGER REFERRAL TRACKING AND COLLABORATION BETWEEN 988 LIFELINE CENTERS AND TRIBAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROGRAMS WILL HELP ENSURE THAT AI/AN INDIVIDUALS IN CRISIS ARE CONNECTED TO CULTURALLY GROUNDED SERVICES AND RECEIVE ONGOING SUPPORT BEYOND THE INITIAL CRISIS CONTACT.
