description: CN 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE - THE CHEROKEE NATION BEHAVIORAL HEALTH (CNBH) 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN CHEROKEE NATION'S (CN) CAPACITY TO RESPOND TO, MONITOR, AND GROW AWARENESS AND UTILIZATION OF THE 988 SUICIDE AND CRISIS LIFELINE ACROSS THE CHEROKEE NATION RESERVATION, A 6,950-SQUARE-MILE, 14-COUNTY JURISDICTION IN NORTHEASTERN OKLAHOMA WITH A POPULATION OF 521,336, ABOUT HALF OF WHOM LIVE IN AREAS THE CENSUS CLASSIFIES AS RURAL. CNBH CURRENTLY FIELDS 988 CONTACTS THROUGH ITS EXISTING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE, WHICH SCREENS, REFERS, AND LINKS CALLERS TO SERVICES, BUT LACKS DEDICATED PEER CAPACITY TO PROVIDE WARM TRANSITIONS AND FOLLOW-UP, A ROUTINE SYSTEM FOR TURNING CONTACT AND REFERRAL DATA INTO PLANNING INSIGHT, AND A COORDINATED COMMUNICATION STRATEGY TO REACH RURAL AND LOWER-BROADBAND COMMUNITIES BEFORE A CRISIS BECOMES URGENT. CONTINUING AND BUILDING ON CN'S WORK UNDER THE 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT SINCE 2023, THIS PROJECT ADDS A PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SPECIALIST AND A MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTANT TO CNBH'S CRISIS RESPONSE, BUILDS A FUNCTIONING DATA-TRACKING AND RECONCILIATION SYSTEM, AND LAUNCHES A COORDINATED, MULTI-TIERED COMMUNICATION STRATEGY. THE PRIMARY POPULATION OF FOCUS IS AI/AN INDIVIDUALS OF ALL AGES WHOSE 988 CONTACTS ORIGINATE IN TRIBAL COMMUNITIES OR ARE INITIATED BY AI/AN; THE SECONDARY POPULATION, TARGETED FOR 988 AWARENESS AND EDUCATION, IS ALL CITIZENS WITHIN THE ENTIRE CATCHMENT AREA. THERE ARE 144,855 CN CITIZENS RESIDING WITHIN THE RESERVATION, 27.8% OF THE CATCHMENT AREA'S TOTAL POPULATION. IN 2023, THE AGE-ADJUSTED SUICIDE RATE AMONG NON-HISPANIC AI/AN PEOPLE WAS 69% HIGHER THAN THE OVERALL U.S. RATE, AND OKLAHOMA'S OWN SUICIDE RATE HAS GROWN FASTER THAN THE NATIONAL RATE FOR CLOSE TO TWO DECADES, WITH RATES HIGHEST AMONG AI/AN AND WHITE OKLAHOMANS AND IN RURAL AREAS. CN ACCOUNTED FOR 1,545 OF THE 4,382 AI/AN-SPECIFIC 988 LIFELINE CONTACTS RECORDED ACROSS OKLAHOMA TRIBES BETWEEN APRIL 2025 AND MARCH 2026, 35% OF THE TOTAL AND MORE THAN DOUBLE THE NEXT-HIGHEST TRIBE. AT LEAST HALF OF CN’S RESIDENTS LIVE IN RURAL COMMUNITIES FACING WELL-DOCUMENTED SUICIDE RISK FACTORS- SOCIAL ISOLATION, LIMITED ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CARE, LONGER TRAVEL DISTANCES, AND HIGHER RATES OF FIREARM OWNERSHIP- AND 13.8% OF CATCHMENT-AREA HOUSEHOLDS LACK A BROADBAND SUBSCRIPTION, LIMITING AWARENESS OF 988 BEFORE A CRISIS MAKES IT URGENT. TO STRENGTHEN CN'S CAPACITY TO RESPOND TO 988 CONTACTS (GOAL 1), CNBH WILL HIRE AND ONBOARD A PROJECT DIRECTOR, MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTANT, FAMILY CARE MANAGER, AND PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SPECIALIST BY 1/31/2027, UPDATE ITS WRITTEN AGREEMENT WITH SOLARI BY 3/31/2027, AND DELIVER CRISIS-RESPONSE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT TO 75 CN EMPLOYEES IN YEAR 1 AND 200 IN EACH OF YEARS 2 AND 3, WITH AT LEAST 80% OF CITIZENS REFERRED THROUGH 988 RECEIVING A WARM HAND-OFF AND DOCUMENTED FOLLOW-UP ANNUALLY. TO BUILD CN'S CAPACITY TO MONITOR AND UTILIZE 988 DATA (GOAL 2), THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A WRITTEN LOCAL EVALUATION PLAN AND A FUNCTIONING DATA-TRACKING SYSTEM BY 9/29/2027, AND THE PROJECT EVALUATOR WILL PRODUCE QUARTERLY RECONCILIATION REPORTS COMPARING CN’S SHARE OF TRIBAL-AFFILIATED 988 CONTACTS AGAINST SERVICES ACTUALLY DELIVERED. TO GROW AWARENESS AND UTILIZATION OF 988 AMONG CN CITIZENS (GOAL 3), CN WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A MULTI-TIERED COMMUNICATION STRATEGY ALIGNED WITH SAMHSA'S 988 PARTNER TOOLKIT, CONDUCT AT LEAST SIX RURAL COMMUNITY-BASED AWARENESS EVENTS IN YEAR 1 (SCALING TO 12 IN YEARS 2 AND 3), SUSTAIN THE MENTAL HEALTH AWARENESS DAY CAMPAIGN, AND BY 9/29/2029 WILL COLLABORATIVELY DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE A TRIBAL CRISIS RESPONSE BEST PRACTICES TOOLKIT WITH THE OK TRIBAL 988 WORKGROUP. THESE GOALS ALIGN WITH SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES AND WILL BE MONITORED THROUGH A STRUCTURED CQI PROCESS, QUARTERLY SPARS REPORTING, AND ANNUAL PROGRAMMATIC PROGRESS REPORTS.

description: TOIYABE INDIAN HEALTH PROJECT 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE - PROJECT NAME: TOIYABE INDIAN HEALTH PROJECT 988 TRIBAL RESPONSE PUBLIC SUMMARY: IN INYO AND MONO COUNTIES, AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE RESIDENTS DIE BY SUICIDE AT NEARLY TWICE THE NATIONAL RATE, YET NO 988 CRISIS CENTER IN CALIFORNIA CURRENTLY PROVIDES A DEDICATED TRIBAL-SPECIFIC RESPONSE PATHWAY. TOIYABE INDIAN HEALTH PROJECT (TIHP) WILL STRENGTHEN 988 CRISIS-CENTER PARTNERSHIPS, CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE TRAINING, AND TRIBAL-SPECIFIC DATA SYSTEMS TO CLOSE THAT GAP FOR THE SEVEN FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBES OF THIS 13,277-SQUARE-MILE FRONTIER REGION. GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND CAPACITY NEED: THE PROJECT SERVES INYO AND MONO COUNTIES, A 13,277-SQUARE-MILE RURAL AND FRONTIER REGION IN EASTERN CALIFORNIA WITH NO CRISIS STABILIZATION UNIT, NO INPATIENT PSYCHIATRIC BEDS, AND SEVERE CELLULAR AND BROADBAND GAPS. 988 CALLS FROM THIS CATCHMENT ARE CURRENTLY ROUTED BY AREA CODE TO CRISIS CENTERS 275–355 MILES AWAY WITH LIMITED FAMILIARITY WITH LOCAL TRIBAL RESOURCES, RESERVATION GEOGRAPHY, OR TRIBAL SOVEREIGNTY PROTOCOLS. THE PROJECT WILL BUILD THE REGIONAL CAPACITY, FORMAL PARTNERSHIPS, TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE, AND DATA SYSTEMS, NEEDED TO CLOSE THIS GAP. POPULATION OF FOCUS: THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS THE APPROXIMATELY 3,950 ENROLLED MEMBERS AND DESCENDANTS OF THE SEVEN TRIBES SERVED THROUGH THE TIHP CONSORTIUM (BIG PINE PAIUTE, BISHOP PAIUTE, BRIDGEPORT INDIAN COLONY, FORT INDEPENDENCE, LONE PINE PAIUTE-SHOSHONE, UTU UTU GWAITU PAIUTE, AND TIMBISHA SHOSHONE), ALONG WITH OTHER AI/AN INDIVIDUALS ELIGIBLE FOR TIHP SERVICES, SPANNING ALL AGES AND INCLUDING ELDERS, ADULTS, AND YOUTH. POPULATION PLANNED TO BE SERVED: TIHP'S EXISTING CLINICAL SERVICES REACH INDIVIDUALS ACROSS THE LIFESPAN EXPERIENCING DEPRESSION, CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (ALCOHOL, OPIOID, AND METHAMPHETAMINE), AND SUICIDE RISK, USING VALIDATED INSTRUMENTS (PHQ-9/PHQ-A) AT INTAKE AND CLINICALLY INDICATED INTERVALS, WITH SERVICES RANGING FROM CRISIS INTERVENTION AND SUICIDE RISK ASSESSMENT TO COUNSELING AND RECOVERY SUPPORT. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS: TIHP WILL FORMALIZE MOUS WITH BOTH REGIONAL 988 CRISIS CENTERS; STANDARDIZE CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE CRISIS-RESPONSE TRAINING ACROSS COUNSELORS AND PARTNER STAFF; BUILD AN END-TO-END TRIBAL-SPECIFIC 988 UTILIZATION TRACKING SYSTEM WITH CRIHB/CTEC; EXPAND ITS CROSS-SECTOR TRIBAL 988 TASK FORCE TO AT LEAST 15 PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS; AND REDESIGN ITS COMMUNITY OUTREACH STRATEGY AROUND TRUST-BUILDING, INFORMED BY TIHP'S OWN 2025 COMMUNITY SURVEY. PROJECT GOALS: 1. FORMALIZE, STRENGTHEN, AND EXPAND TIHP'S 988 CRISIS-CENTER COLLABORATION AND TRAINING NETWORK; 2. BUILD AN END-TO-END 988 UTILIZATION TRACKING AND OUTCOMES SYSTEM FOR TRIBAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS; AND 3) INCREASE TRIBAL COMMUNITY TRUST, ENGAGEMENT, AND UTILIZATION OF THE 988-CRISIS SYSTEM. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: TIHP'S MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES ARE DESIGNED TO ADVANCE SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES OF ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY SERVICES, DATA-DRIVEN PRACTICE, AND PREVENTION. TIHP WILL EXECUTE OR UPDATE MOUS WITH BOTH REGIONAL 988 CRISIS CENTERS IN YEAR 1, REMOVING A KEY ACCESS BARRIER FOR TRIBAL CALLERS; CONNECT INTERNAL AND PARTNER DATA INTO THE FIRST TRIBAL-SPECIFIC 988 DATASET FOR THE CATCHMENT BY MONTH SIX OF YEAR 1; REACH AT LEAST 100 TRIBAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND 50 TRIBAL YOUTH ANNUALLY THROUGH PREVENTION-FOCUSED OUTREACH; AND INCREASE COMMUNITY TRUST IN 988 BY AT LEAST 10 PERCENTAGE POINTS ABOVE A 22% BASELINE BY THE END OF YEAR 2, FURTHER ADVANCING ACCESS FOR ELDERS AND OTHER UNDERSERVED GROUPS WITHIN THE POPULATION OF FOCUS.

description: GRAND RONDE GOOD MEDICINE INITIATIVE - THE CONFEDERATED TRIBES OF GRAND RONDE’S GOOD MEDICINE INITIATIVE AIMS TO STRENGTHEN THE WELLNESS, CONNECTEDNESS, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OF TRIBAL YOUTH AND FAMILIES BY EXPANDING CULTURALLY GROUNDED PREVENTION ACTIVITIES, INCREASING ACCESS TO SUPPORTIVE SERVICES, AND ENHANCING COMMUNITYWIDE CAPACITY TO IDENTIFY AND RESPOND TO EARLY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS. TARGETING TRIBAL YOUTH AGES 0 TO 24 AND THEIR FAMILIES, THE INITIATIVE ADDRESSES HIGH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS, EXPOSURE TO INTERGENERATIONAL TRAUMA, AND LIMITED ACCESS TO CULTURALLY SPECIFIC RESOURCES, ESPECIALLY IN RURAL AND ISOLATED REGIONS. THROUGH A STRUCTURED, EVENT-BASED REFERRAL AND EARLY-INTERVENTION SYSTEM, THE PROJECT WILL LEVERAGE TRIBAL COMMUNITY BOARD GOVERNANCE, YOUTH-FOCUSED SWOT ANALYSIS, AND THE GATHERING OF NATIVE AMERICANS PROCESS TO CREATE A CULTURALLY ROOTED, DATA-DRIVEN, AND COMMUNITY-DESIGNED SYSTEM OF CARE. THE INITIATIVE’S GOALS INCLUDE INCREASING YOUTH AND FAMILY ENGAGEMENT IN WELLNESS EVENTS, IMPROVING ACCESS AND REFERRAL PATHWAYS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND PREVENTION SERVICES, AND FORMALIZING CROSS-SYSTEM COLLABORATION WITH SOCIAL SERVICES. WITH ROBUST ORGANIZATIONAL EXPERIENCE, A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM, AND ESTABLISHED PARTNERSHIPS, THE TRIBE IS POSITIONED TO IMPLEMENT AND SUSTAIN THIS INITIATIVE, ENSURING CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT AND ALIGNMENT WITH SAMHSA’S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES FOR INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES.

description: NATIONAL RISE TSA CENTER FOR SCHOOL-BASED TRAUMA-RESPONSIVE EMOTION REGULATION (NATIONAL RISE TSA CENTER) - CMI’S NATIONAL RISE TSA CENTER FOR SCHOOL-BASED TRAUMA-RESPONSIVE EMOTION REGULATION WILL ADAPT, MANUALIZE, EVALUATE, AND NATIONALLY DISSEMINATE RECOGNIZE, IDENTIFY, SOOTHE, AND EMPOWER (RISE), A DIALECTICAL BEHAVIOR THERAPY-INFORMED, TRAUMA-RESPONSIVE EMOTION REGULATION PROTOCOL FOR SCHOOL-BASED AND SCHOOL-CONNECTED MENTAL HEALTH SETTINGS. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN PROVIDER AND SYSTEM CAPACITY TO SUPPORT CHILDREN AND YOUTH AGES 5-18 AFFECTED BY COMPLEX TRAUMA, EMOTIONAL DYSREGULATION, AND RELATED FUNCTIONAL IMPAIRMENT.   THE NATIONAL RISE TSA CENTER WILL INITIALLY FOCUS CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT IN NEW YORK CITY AND SAN MATEO COUNTY AND THE BAY AREA, CALIFORNIA, WITH NATIONAL REACH THROUGH THE NATIONAL CHILD TRAUMATIC STRESS INITIATIVE (NCTSI), CMI’S DIGITAL TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE, AND DISSEMINATION TO SCHOOL-BASED MENTAL HEALTH AND OTHER CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS. THESE URBAN, SUBURBAN, AND SEMI-RURAL COMMUNITIES NEED PRACTICAL, FIDELITY-SUPPORTED TOOLS TO IDENTIFY, REFER, ENGAGE, AND SUPPORT YOUTH AFFECTED BY TRAUMA AND CHRONIC STRESS. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THE LACK OF A MANUALIZED, SCHOOL-CONTEXTUALIZED PROTOCOL; LIMITED TRAINING, CONSULTATION, AND FIDELITY INFRASTRUCTURE; AND THE NEED FOR CAREGIVER MATERIALS, IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE, AND SCALABLE DISSEMINATION RESOURCES.   THE DIRECT POPULATION OF FOCUS IS THE WORKFORCE AND SYSTEMS THAT WILL BE TRAINED AND SUPPORTED, INCLUDING SCHOOL COUNSELORS, SOCIAL WORKERS, PSYCHOLOGISTS, MENTAL HEALTH CLINICIANS, SUPERVISORS, NCTSI CATEGORY I AND III GRANTEES, COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PARTNERS, AND OTHER K-12 CHILD-SERVING PROVIDERS. ULTIMATE BENEFICIARIES ARE CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS AGES 5-18 WITH TRAUMA HISTORIES, EMOTIONAL DYSREGULATION, INTERPERSONAL OR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONCERNS, RISK BEHAVIORS, OR IMPAIRED SCHOOL FUNCTIONING. RISE WILL ADDRESS COMPLEX AND OVERLAPPING TRAUMA, INCLUDING ABUSE, NEGLECT, DOMESTIC VIOLENCE EXPOSURE, COMMUNITY OR SCHOOL VIOLENCE, TRAUMATIC LOSS, FAMILY SEPARATION, HOMELESSNESS, HOUSING INSTABILITY, DISPLACEMENT, AND CHRONIC ADVERSITY. SAMHSA FUNDS WILL NOT SUPPORT DIRECT CLINICAL SERVICES. PILOT IMPLEMENTATION THROUGH EXISTING SCHOOL-BASED OR SCHOOL-CONNECTED SYSTEMS WILL ASSESS FEASIBILITY, FIDELITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND OUTCOMES.   CMI WILL USE A PHASED STRATEGY THAT INCLUDES A FIELD SCAN AND NEEDS ASSESSMENT; INPUT FROM NATIONAL AND FAMILY ADVISORY PANELS; PROTOCOL REFINEMENT AND MANUALIZATION; PILOT IMPLEMENTATION IN 10 SCHOOL-BASED OR SCHOOL-CONNECTED SITES; WORKFORCE TRAINING, CONSULTATION, AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE; FIDELITY MONITORING; YOUTH, FAMILY, AND PROVIDER FEEDBACK; GPRA AND PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENT; CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT; AND NATIONAL DISSEMINATION THROUGH NCTSI CHANNELS AND CMI’S LEARNING PLATFORM. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) ADAPT, MANUALIZE, PILOT, AND VALIDATE RISE FOR SCHOOL-BASED DELIVERY AND NATIONAL REPLICATION; (2) BUILD WORKFORCE CAPACITY FOR SCHOOL-BASED RISE IMPLEMENTATION; (3) DISSEMINATE SCALABLE TOOLS AND IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORTS NATIONALLY; AND (4) EVALUATE IMPLEMENTATION, FIDELITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND YOUTH OUTCOMES TO SUPPORT CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT AND EVIDENCE BUILDING. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES ARE TO CONVENE A 12-MEMBER NATIONAL ADVISORY PANEL BY MONTH 6; COMPLETE A NEEDS ASSESSMENT ACROSS 10 PILOT SCHOOLS BY MONTH 12; PRODUCE RISE PROTOCOL MATERIALS AND PUBLISH A TOOLKIT BY MONTH 18; COMPLETE PILOT IMPLEMENTATION IN 10 SITES BY MONTH 30, WITH 80% OF PARTICIPATING PROVIDERS MEETING FIDELITY BENCHMARKS; TRAIN 600 SCHOOL-BASED PROVIDERS DURING YEARS 2-5; REACH 1,500 CHILD-SERVING PROFESSIONALS THROUGH DISSEMINATION BY PROJECT END; PROVIDE ANNUAL TRAINING, CONSULTATION, OR TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO AT LEAST FIVE NCTSI CATEGORY III GRANTEE SITES; DOCUMENT TRAINING, CONSULTATION, ADOPTION, OR IMPLEMENTATION PLANNING WITH 20 NCTSI-AFFILIATED OR SCHOOL-CONNECTED SITES BY YEAR 5; AND USE VALIDATED MEASURES AND AVAILABLE SCHOOL FUNCTIONING INDICATORS TO ASSESS IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY AND YOUTH OUTCOMES.

description: CENTER FOR TRAUMA-INFORMED ADOLESCENT SUICIDE, SELF-HARM, & SUBSTANCE ABUSE TREATMENT & PREVENTION - THE ADOLESCENT SUICIDE/SELF HARM & SUBSTANCE ABUSE PREVENTION (ASAP) CENTER, WITH HUBS IN NORTH CAROLINA AND PENNSYLVANIA, WILL INCREASE ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICES AND SERVICES TO TREAT AND ADDRESS THE MENTAL HEALTH IMPACTS OF TRAUMA, INCLUDING SUICIDE/SELF-HARM AND SUBSTANCE USE, FOR ADOLESCENTS AND TRANSITION-AGE YOUTH (AGES 12-25) PRESENTING WITH SUICIDE/SELF-HARM AND SUBSTANCE ABUSE AND FOR THE PREVENTION OF THESE PROBLEMS. WE PRIORITIZE YOUTH IN PRIMARY CARE / INTEGRATED CARE, SCHOOL, AND JUVENILE JUSTICE SETTINGS - SETTINGS WHERE TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE IS OFTEN UNAVAILABLE OR INCONSISTENTLY DELIVERED.  WITHIN SERVICE SECTORS, WE WILL ALSO ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF MILITARY-INVOLVED YOUTH AND FAMILIES. RECOGNIZING THE POTENTIAL FOR SECONDARY TRAUMATIC STRESS (STS) IN WORKING WITH YOUTH WHO HAVE EXPERIENCED TRAUMA OR ARE HAVING SUICIDAL / MENTAL HEALTH CRISES, WE ALSO PRIORITIZE TRAININGS FOR THE PREVENTION OF STS. THE CENTER WILL SERVE AS A NATIONAL RESOURCE AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE HUB, WITH PARTNERS IDENTIFIED ALREADY IN NORTH CAROLINA, VIRGINIA, PENNSYLVANIA, AND CALIFORNIA.   BUILDING ON PRIOR WORK, THE ASAP CENTER WILL: (1) DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT, AND EVALUATE TRAUMA-FOCUSED TRIAGE GUIDELINES AND REFERRAL PROTOCOLS FOR MANAGING SUICIDE/SELF-HARM AND SUBSTANCE ABUSE RISK AMONG TRAUMA-EXPOSED ADOLESCENTS; (2) ADAPT, EVALUATE, AND DISSEMINATE TRAUMA-FOCUSED INTERVENTIONS (SAFETY-A AND ADAPTATIONS FOR DIFFERENT SERVICE SETTINGS) FOR EVALUATING AND ENHANCING SAFETY; (3) INTEGRATE TRAUMA-FOCUSED AND FAMILY-CENTERED BRIEF INTERVENTIONS TARGETING SUICIDE WITH TRAUMA SCREENINGS, AND A TRAUMA-FOCUSED CARE PROCESS MODEL; (4) INTEGRATE TRAUMA-FOCUSED BRIEF SUICIDE INTERVENTIONS WITH SUBSTANCE USE SCREENINGS AND TRAUMA-INFORMED SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT APPROACHES; (5) BUILD WORKFORCE CAPACITY THROUGH TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOCUSED ON PREVENTION OF STS AMONG PROVIDERS WORKING WITH SUICIDAL AND TRAUMA-EXPOSED YOUTH, INCLUDING 988 CRISIS CALL CENTERS, MOBILE CRISIS TEAMS, AND ACUTE CARE SETTINGS; (6) USE TECHNOLOGY-ENHANCED TRAINING AND DISSEMINATION TOOLS, INCLUDING A DATA-INFORMED SUPERVISION SYSTEM AND MEASUREMENT-BASED CARE, PAIRED WITH FIDELITY MONITORING AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROCESSES TO ENSURE CONSISTENT, SUSTAINABLE IMPLEMENTATION ACROSS THE NETWORK; AND (7) ENSURE MEANINGFUL STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT THROUGH A PARTNERSHIP OF NATIONAL EXPERTS, EXPERIENCED SERVICE PROVIDERS AND ADMINISTRATORS, AND YOUTHS AND PARENTS WITH LIVED EXPERIENCE, WHO WILL INFORM INTERVENTION ADAPTATION AND DISSEMINATION AND IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES.  THE CENTER'S GOALS ALIGN WITH SAMHSA PRIORITY AREAS INCLUDING (1) PREVENTING SUBSTANCE MISUSE AND ADDICTION, (2) ADDRESSING SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS (INCLUDING SUICIDAL BEHAVIORS), (3) SUPPORTING THE CRISIS AND ACUTE CARE WORKFORCE THROUGH WORKFORCE-FOCUSED STS PREVENTION, AND (4) SUPPORTING LONG-TERM RECOVERY THROUGH INTEGRATION OF TRAUMA-FOCUSED INTERVENTIONS FOR SUBSTANCE USE.  THE CENTER’S APPROACH IS DESIGNED TO BE DYNAMIC, SCALABLE, AND REPLICABLE. BASED ON THE NUMBERS OF CLIENTS SEEN AT PARTNERING SITES, WE CONSERVATIVELY ESTIMATE THAT THE CENTER WILL INTENSIVELY TRAIN AT LEAST 400 PROVIDERS PER YEAR (2000 TOTAL) TO FIDELITY BENCHMARKS OF SAFETY-A AND RELATED PROTOCOLS; DELIVER STS PREVENTION TRAINING TO AT LEAST 200 CRISIS WORKFORCE STAFF PER YEAR (1000 TOTAL); PROVIDE AT LEAST 20 BRIEF TRAININGS OR EDUCATIONAL AND AWARENESS TALKS PER YEAR (100 TOTAL); AND ESTABLISH MEASUREMENT-BASED CARE INFRASTRUCTURE ACROSS SITES. BASED ON CLIENT VOLUME AT CURRENT PARTICIPATING SITES, THE CENTER HAS THE POTENTIAL TO IMPROVE CARE FOR OVER 200,000 YOUTH ACROSS THE NATION (ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE ANNUAL CLIENT VOLUMES AT CURRENT PARTNER SITES) IN A SUSTAINABLE MANNER, WHILE INCREASING WORKFORCE CAPACITY FOR WORKING WITH TRAUMA-AFFECTED AND SUICIDAL YOUNG PEOPLE.

description: CENTER FOR PEDIATRIC TRAUMATIC STRESS - THE CENTER FOR PEDIATRIC TRAUMATIC STRESS (CPTS) IS A NATIONAL LEADER IN IDENTIFYING AND REDUCING HEALTH-RELATED TRAUMATIC STRESS IN CHILDREN AND FAMILIES. OUR MISSION IS TO MITIGATE TRAUMATIC STRESS IN YOUTH WITH MEDICAL CONDITIONS AND THEIR FAMILIES BY ADVANCING THE INTEGRATION OF TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE (TIC) INTO HEALTHCARE SETTINGS USING PRACTICAL, EVIDENCE-BASED TOOLS. WITH EXTENSIVE WEB-BASED RESOURCES, CLINICAL INTERVENTIONS, AND TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES TARGETING HEALTHCARE AND MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS AND FAMILIES, CPTS'S SCOPE IS NATIONAL. CPTS ALSO HAS 3 HOSPITAL-BASED SITES ACROSS 7 STATES TO OPTIMIZE DISSEMINATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF RESOURCES.     MILLIONS OF CHILDREN EACH YEAR INCUR INJURIES AND FACE CHRONIC MEDICAL CONDITIONS. UNEXPECTED INJURIES, NEW MEDICAL DIAGNOSES AND MEDICAL TREATMENT SERVE AS ONE OF THE MOST COMMON POTENTIALLY TRAUMATIC EXPERIENCES THAT A CHILD ENCOUNTERS IN THE UNITED STATES. MEDICAL TRAUMATIC STRESS INCLUDES CHILD AND FAMILY RESPONSES TO PAIN, INJURY, ILLNESS, AND FRIGHTENING TREATMENT EXPERIENCES. BUILDING ON GOLD STANDARD RESEARCH ON ILL AND INJURED CHILDREN AND THEIR FAMILIES, AND LEVERAGING OUR STRONG CONNECTIONS WITH KEY HEALTH PROVIDER COMMUNITIES, CPTS PROVIDES NATIONAL LEADERSHIP ON TRAUMATIC STRESS ACROSS INJURY, ILLNESS, AND OTHER MEDICAL PROBLEMS. CPTS SERVES AS A RESOURCE TO THE NATIONAL CHILD TRAUMATIC STRESS NETWORK (NCTSN) TO ADVANCE INTEGRATION OF TIC INTO HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS. TIC IN PEDIATRIC HEALTHCARE AIMS TO REDUCE DISTRESS WHILE PROMOTING RESILIENCE AND POSITIVE ADAPTATION IN THE FACE OF DIFFICULT MEDICAL EVENTS. TO ACHIEVE OUR MISSION, CPTS DEVELOPS, EVALUATES, AND SUPPORTS THE DISSEMINATION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND SUSTAINMENT OF EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS INTEGRATED WITHIN PEDIATRIC HEALTHCARE.     CPTS’S WORK IN THE 2026-2031 PROJECT PERIOD FOCUSES ON THREE GOALS / KEY CONSTITUENCIES:  GOAL 1. STRENGTHEN AWARENESS, PREVENTION OF, AND RESPONSIVENESS TO TRAUMATIC STRESS AMONG HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS AND SYSTEMS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES. ADVANCE, SCALE, AND SUSTAIN TIC ACROSS HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS AND PRACTICES IN COLLABORATION WITH HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS.  GOAL 2. DEEPEN EXPERTISE WITHIN THE MENTAL HEALTH WORKFORCE ON CARING FOR CHILDREN WITH ACUTE AND CHRONIC MEDICAL NEEDS AND THEIR FAMILIES. ENHANCE PROVIDER CAPACITY BY WORKING WITH MENTAL HEALTH TO DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED, TIC IN HEALTHCARE AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEMS. GOALS 3. DISSEMINATE TRAUMATIC STRESS PSYCHOSOCIAL RESOURCES DIRECTLY TO FAMILIES WITH CHILDREN WITH ACUTE AND CHRONIC MEDICAL NEEDS. ENSURE THAT PATIENTS AND FAMILIES HAVE ACCESS TO SCALABLE, EVIDENCE-BASED RESOURCES AND INTERVENTIONS ADDRESSING PEDIATRIC TRAUMATIC STRESS.       MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES (FOR THE GRANT CYCLE) INCLUDE ANNUAL REVIEW AND UPDATES OF WWW.HEALTHCARETOOLBOX.ORG (HCT); PROMOTING HCT VIA LIVE TRAININGS, SOCIAL MEDIA, AND PARTNERSHIPS TO REACH 30,000 HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS AND 2,500 MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS; DISSEMINATE AND SUPPORT THE SUSTAINMENT OF TIC VIA NEWLY DEVELOPED ONLINE PLATFORM THAT GUIDES ORGANIZATIONS THROUGH SETTING TIC GOALS AND ASSIGNING WEB-BASED TRAININGS AND RESOURCES (TICKET) WITH AT LEAST 15 ORGANIZATION; ADAPTING AND DISSEMINATE A PROGRAM AIMED TO DECREASE HEALTHCARE PROVIDER BURNOUT AND STRESS (TECHS) TO REACH AT LEAST 5,000 INDIVIDUALS; DISSEMINATE VALIDATED TRAUMA-BASED SCREENING TOOLS (PAT, ASC-KIDS) TO 100 HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS WHO WILL IMPLEMENT THEM WITH 7,500 FAMILIES; DISSEMINATE PROGRAM FOR FAMILIES WITH PEDIATRIC CANCER TO PROMOTE CAREGIVER COPING (SCCIP) TO AT LEAST 150 MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS OVER THE COURSE OF THE GRANT; ANNUAL REVIEW AND UPDATES OF FAMILY-FACING MATERIALS ON HCT. THIS MULTI-PRONGED APPROACH ENSURES COMPREHENSIVE IMPACT ON HEALTHCARE SYSTEM INFRASTRUCTURE TO IMPROVE ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICES FOR CHILDREN AFFECTED BY MEDICAL TRAUMA.

description: TF-CBT NATIONAL ADAPTATION AND SUPPORT CENTER - THE TF-CBT NATIONAL ADAPTATION AND SUPPORT CENTER SEEKS TO DEVELOP AND PROVIDE TRAINING ON A TRAUMA-FOCUSED COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (TF-CBT) ADAPTATION TO BUILD CAPACITY FOR EFFECTIVELY TREATING YOUTH WITH COMORBID POSTTRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER (PTSD) AND DEPRESSION. TO HELP SUSTAIN WORKFORCE CAPACITY, TF-CBT TRAIN-THE-SUPERVISOR (TTS) PROGRAMS, AND EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE COURSES AND A COURSE TRAIN-THE-TRAINER (TTT) PROGRAM WILL ALSO BE OFFERED.  LED BY ELISABETH POLLIO, PHD AND ESTHER DEBLINGER, PHD, TF-CBT CO-DEVELOPER, ALONG WITH THE OTHER TF-CBT CO-DEVELOPERS, ANTHONY MANNARINO, PHD AND JUDITH COHEN, MD, THIS PROJECT, MORE SPECIFICALLY, SEEKS TO ADDRESS THE GAP IN EFFECTIVE SERVICES FOR YOUTH WITH COMORBID PTSD AND DEPRESSION BY CONDUCTING A LEARNING COMMUNITY WITH 15 TF-CBT-TRAINED CLINICIANS AND SUPERVISORS AND SUBSEQUENTLY PROVIDING TWO LEARNING COLLABORATIVES TO 100 CLINICIANS AND SUPERVISORS FROM ACROSS THE NETWORK. THE POPULATION OF YOUTH WITH COMORBID PTSD AND DEPRESSION HAS RESPONDED LESS WELL TO EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENT, HAVE COMPLEX NEEDS, AND ARE POTENTIALLY AT HIGHER RISK FOR NEGATIVE LIFE TRAJECTORIES. THE LEARNING COMMUNITY AND COLLABORATIVES, LED BY THE TF-CBT CO-DEVELOPERS, WILL PROVIDE TRAINING, CONSULTATION, AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO TF-CBT PROVIDERS WORKING WITH YOUTH (AGES 7 TO 17 YEARS) WITH COMORBID PTSD AND DEPRESSION WHO HAVE EXPERIENCED SEXUAL ABUSE, TRAUMATIC GRIEF, AND OTHER TRAUMAS.  PARTICIPANTS' CLIENTS WILL DEMONSTRATE REDUCTIONS IN PTSD AND DEPRESSION, AS ASSESSED BY STANDARDIZED MEASURES. AN IMPLEMENTATION MANUAL AND OTHER RESOURCES (E.G., INFORMATION SHEETS, WEBINARS) FOR THIS ADAPTATION WILL BE DEVELOPED AND DISSEMINATED. TO SUPPORT ORGANIZATIONAL SUSTAINMENT OF TF-CBT IMPLEMENTATION, THREE TTS PROGRAMS WILL BE PROVIDED BY THE TF-CBT CO-DEVELOPERS TO 75 TF-CBT SUPERVISORS FROM NCTSI-III SITES WITH 80% ATTENDANCE, OFFERING SUPERVISORY STRATEGIES FOR ALL TF-CBT COMPONENTS BY THE END OF EACH PROGRAM. AS PARTICIPATION OF THE NON-OFFENDING CAREGIVER IS A CRITICAL PART OF TF-CBT, THERE WILL BE A FOCUS IN THE LEARNING COMMUNITY/COLLABORATIVES AND TTS PROGRAMS ON CAREGIVER VOICE AND CHOICE TO ENSURE THE CAREGIVER ROLE IN YOUTH RECOVERY IS VALIDATED AND SUPPORTED THROUGHOUT TREATMENT. GIVEN THE RISK OF SECONDARY TRAUMATIC STRESS, BURNOUT, AND TURNOVER AMONG TRAUMA PROFESSIONALS, FOUR EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE SELF-CARE AND RELATIONSHIP-CARE COURSES WILL BE PROVIDED TO 200 CLINICIANS, SUPERVISORS, AND SENIOR LEADERS ACROSS THE NETWORK TO HELP SUPPORT AND SUSTAIN THE CHILD TRAUMA WORKFORCE. THE PRACTICE COURSE HAS DOCUMENTED EFFECTIVENESS IN ENHANCING WELL-BEING.  COURSE PARTICIPANTS ACROSS ORGANIZATIONAL ROLES WILL DEMONSTRATE IMPROVEMENTS IN EFFECTIVE COPING SKILL USE AND BURNOUT, AND TREATMENT PROVIDERS WILL DEMONSTRATE IMPROVEMENTS IN STS AND TF-CBT FIDELITY, AS ASSESSED BY STANDARDIZED MEASURES. TO REACH A GREATER NUMBER OF CHILD TRAUMA PROFESSIONALS AND ORGANIZATIONS ACROSS THE NETWORK, 25 PRACTICE COURSE COMPLETERS WILL PARTICIPATE IN A TTT PROGRAM TO HELP PARTICIPANTS LEARN TO LEAD PRACTICE COURSES. TO HELP ENSURE CAPACITY BUILDING AND SUSTAINMENT ACROSS SETTINGS, PARTICIPANTS IN ALL PROGRAMMING (LEARNING COMMUNITY/COLLABORATIVES, TTS PROGRAMS, PRACTICE COURSES AND ASSOCIATED TTT PROGRAM) WILL BE RECRUITED FROM A VARIETY OF SETTINGS, INCLUDING COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH CENTERS, CHILD ADVOCACY CENTERS, AND SCHOOLS. ALL OF THE PROPOSED PROGRAMS AND PRODUCTS, DESIGNED TO INCREASE AND SUSTAIN WORKFORCE CAPACITY, WILL ULTIMATELY IMPROVE THE AVAILABILITY AND ACCESSIBILITY OF TRANSFORMATIVE EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENT FOR YOUTH AND THEIR CAREGIVERS NATIONWIDE.

description: EVIDENCE FOR ALL - EVIDENCE-BASED AND TRAUMA-INFORMED FAMILY STRENGTHENING - EVIDENCE FOR ALL (EFA) WILL ESTABLISH A NCTSI-II TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION CENTER TO DISSEMINATE A CLINICALLY DEEPENED VERSION OF FUNCTIONAL FAMILY THERAPY (FFT), FFT FOR TRAUMA (FFT-T), FOR YOUTH AGES 11-18 AND THEIR FAMILIES INVOLVED IN CHILD WELFARE AND JUVENILE JUSTICE NATIONWIDE. EFA WILL BUILD NCTSN'S CAPACITY TO DELIVER FFT-T WITH HIGH-FIDELITY, AT SCALE, AND SUSTAIN IT BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD.  GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT NEED. THIS PROJECT OPERATES NATIONALLY, WITH PRIORITY OUTREACH TO NCTSN SITES IN THE 34 STATES WHERE FFT IS ON APPROVED FFPSA TITLE IV-E PREVENTION PLANS. THE CAPACITY GAP IS STRUCTURAL AS FFT IS RATED  WELL-SUPPORTED  BY THE TITLE IV-E CLEARINGHOUSE AND WIDELY PUBLICLY FUNDED, YET IT IS ABSENT FROM NCTSN'S PUBLISHED GUIDANCE ON TRAUMA INTERVENTIONS. NEEDED CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT IS CLINICAL (MAKING FFT'S TRAUMA FUNCTIONS EXPLICIT AND MEASURABLE), TECHNICAL (IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE AND CONTEXTUALIZATION), AND FINANCIAL (FINANCING PATHWAYS TO SUSTAIN FFT).  POPULATION OF FOCUS. YOUTH AGES 11-18 IN CHILD WELFARE OR JUVENILE JUSTICE, INCLUDING YOUTH IN OUT-OF-HOME PLACEMENT, AT RISK OF REMOVAL, AND COURT-INVOLVED YOUTH IN FAMILY-BASED INTERVENTION, EXPERIENCING MALTREATMENT/COMPLEX TRAUMA, PLACEMENT INSTABILITY, AND/OR TRAUMA FROM JUSTICE SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT. APPROXIMATELY 80% OF JUSTICE-INVOLVED YOUTH HAVE EXPERIENCED TRAUMA, 70% MEET CRITERIA FOR A MENTAL HEALTH DISORDER, AND 30% MEET CRITERIA FOR PTSD. THE NCTSN WORKFORCE (CLINICIANS, SUPERVISORS, ADMINISTRATORS, SYSTEM LEADERS) IS THE PRIMARY CAPACITY-BUILDING AUDIENCE.  STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS. EFA WILL ADAPT FFT INTO FFT-T, DEEPENING ITS TRAUMA TREATMENT FUNCTIONS AND SUPPORTING IMPLEMENTATION OF FFT-T AND OTHER NCTSN PROGRAMS THROUGH FOUR MODULAR STRATEGIES: (1) CONTEXTUALIZATION (LISTEN, UNDERSTAND, INTEGRATE, CONTINUOUSLY LEARN) TO TAILOR FFT-T TO EACH SITE'S CONTEXT; (2) IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE, APPLYING AIRN ACTIVE IMPLEMENTATION FRAMEWORKS FOR COACHING, AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING; (3) ENGAGEMENT, INTEGRATING EFA'S CONTENT RELEVANCE AND PARTICIPANT ENGAGEMENT SURVEY (CRPES) INTO FFT PARTNERS' CARE4 PLATFORM FOR REAL-TIME FAMILY FEEDBACK; AND (4) FINANCING, BUILDING SITE-LEVEL ACCESS TO TITLE IV-E, MEDICAID, AND OTHER PUBLIC FUNDING STREAMS.  PROJECT GOALS. (1) BUILD PIPELINE AND READINESS INFRASTRUCTURE FOR 10+ NCTSN SITES TO LAUNCH HIGH-FIDELITY FFT-T. (2) DEVELOP REPLICABLE FFT-T CONTEXTUALIZATION PROTOCOLS AND A PUBLICLY AVAILABLE ROADMAP. (3) STRENGTHEN REAL-TIME PARTICIPANT ENGAGEMENT MEASUREMENT THROUGH CRPES. (4) ENSURE HIGH-FIDELITY IMPLEMENTATION THROUGH COACHING, FIDELITY MONITORING, AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING. (5) STRENGTHEN FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY THROUGH PUBLIC FUNDING PATHWAYS. (6) DISSEMINATE ALL FOUR MODULAR STRATEGIES ACROSS THE NCTSN FOR USE WITH ANY TRAUMA EBP.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES. YEAR 1: FFT-T ADAPTATION COMPLETE; ≥50 PIPELINE SITES IDENTIFIED. YEARS 1-4: ≈12 SITES OUTREACHED/YEAR; FFT-T LAUNCHED AT 10 SITES; ≥15 CLINICAL STAFF CERTIFIED/YEAR; FIDELITY REVIEWS ≥2×/YEAR/SITE. YEAR 2: FOUR MODULAR TOOLKITS PUBLICLY AVAILABLE; CRPES INTEGRATED INTO CARE4. YEAR 3: FINANCING GUIDANCE RESOURCE PUBLISHED. YEAR 4: CONTEXTUALIZATION ROADMAP FOR FIELD USE. YEARS 2-5: ≥10 NCTSN LEARNING COLLABORATIVE SESSIONS/YEAR (~300 INDIVIDUALS/YEAR); ≥4 DISSEMINATION PRODUCTS. GPRA 5-YEAR TARGETS: 439 WORKFORCE TRAINED; 2,422 EXPOSED TO MENTAL-HEALTH AWARENESS; 582 TRAINED IN TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE; 177 TRAINED IN TRAUMA INTERVENTIONS. ALIGNED WITH SAMHSA PRIORITIES: EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT ACCESS, LONG-TERM RECOVERY, PARENTAL RIGHTS AND FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, AND THE MAKE AMERICA HEALTHY AGAIN GOAL OF REDUCING CHRONIC TOXIC STRESS IN CHILDHOOD.

description: TRAUMA INFORMED TO BUILD RESILIENT, INDIGENOUS, BALANCED COMMUNITIES ENHANCED WITH STRENGTH 2 (TRIBES 2) - TRAUMA INFORMED TO BUILD RESILIENT, INDIGENOUS, BALANCED COMMUNITIES ENHANCED WITH STRENGTH (TRIBES 2), A NCTSI CATEGORY II TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION CENTER, WILL PROVIDE NATIONAL EXPERTISE ON CHILDHOOD TRAUMATIC EVENTS AND RELATED TREATMENT FOR AIAN POPULATIONS AND OTHERS IMPACTED BY TRAUMA. THROUGH NATIONAL TRAINING, CONSULTATION, AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, TRIBES 2 WILL EXPAND ACCESS TO EFFECTIVE TRAUMA TREATMENT FOR CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND FAMILIES ACROSS A BROAD RANGE OF CHILD AND FAMILY SERVING SYSTEMS. TRIBES 2 IS A NATIONAL INITIATIVE LED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF NEW MEXICO DIVISION OF COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TO EXPAND ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED, EVIDENCE-BASED AND EVIDENCE-INFORMED SERVICES FOR CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND FAMILIES IMPACTED BY ADVERSE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES (ACES), INTERGENERATIONAL TRAUMA, AND COMMUNITY STRESSORS. BUILDING ON THE PREVIOUSLY SAMHSA-FUNDED TRIBES NCTSN CATEGORY II INITIATIVE, TRIBES 2 WILL SCALE-UP AND ENSURE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE TRIBES PARENTING CURRICULUM AND OTHER TRAUMA INFORMED CARE (TIC) TRAININGS. TRIBES 2 WILL IMPLEMENT A NATIONAL TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE MODEL TO EXPAND PROVIDER CAPACITY ACROSS MENTAL HEALTH, SUBSTANCE USE, CHILD WELFARE, SCHOOL, HEALTHCARE, AND JUVENILE JUSTICE SYSTEMS, WITH A FOCUS ON AMERICAN INDIAN/ALASKA NATIVE AND OTHER TRAUMA-IMPACTED POPULATIONS.  TRIBES 2 WILL ACHIEVE THE FOLLOWING MEASURABLE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES: (1) EXPAND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE TRIBES PARENTING CURRICULUM BY TRAINING AND CERTIFYING FACILITATORS AND TRAINERS; (2) STRENGTHEN WORKFORCE CAPACITY THROUGH TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ON TRAUMA INFORMED CARE FOR PROVIDERS ACROSS CHILD- AND FAMILY-SERVING SYSTEMS; (3) ENHANCE COLLABORATION AND COORDINATION VIA A MULTIDISCIPLINARY PROJECT STEERING COMMITTEE AND NATIONAL PARTNERSHIPS; (4) DISSEMINATE ACCESSIBLE TOOLS AND RESOURCES TO SUPPORT TRAUMA-INFORMED PRACTICE; AND (5) IMPLEMENT A CQI-DRIVEN EVALUATION PLAN TO MONITOR OUTCOMES AND SUPPORT CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT. ANNUALLY, TRIBES 2 WILL REACH 400 PROVIDERS THROUGH STRUCTURED TRAINING (2,000 OVER 5 YEARS), 400 PROVIDERS THROUGH DISSEMINATION OF RESOURCES (2,000 OVER 5 YEARS), AND 84 FACILITATORS, APPRENTICES, AND TRAINERS ANNUALLY (420 OVER 5 YEARS) THROUGH INTENSIVE TRAINING AND LEARNING COLLABORATIVES.  TRIBES 2 ADDRESSES CRITICAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE AND SERVICE GAPS IN RURAL AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES BY TRAINING BOTH CLINICAL AND NON-CLINICAL PROVIDERS TO DELIVER CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE, TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICES. GROUNDED IN TRAUMA-INFORMED PRINCIPLES AND THE HISTORICAL TRAUMA AND UNRESOLVED GRIEF (H-TUG) EVIDENCE-INFORMED TREATMENT MODEL, THE PROJECT TARGETS INDIVIDUAL, FAMILY, AND COMMUNITY-LEVEL IMPACTS ON TRAUMA. EVALUATION FINDINGS WILL BE USED TO GUIDE CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT AND SHARED WITH STAKEHOLDERS TO STRENGTHEN IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINABILITY. TRIBES 2 ALIGNS WITH SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES BY INTEGRATING RECOVERY-ORIENTED, PREVENTION-BASED, AND TRAUMA-INFORMED, APPROACHES GROUNDED IN EVIDENCE-BASED AND OUTCOME-FOCUSED PRACTICES, PROGRAM INTEGRITY AND FISCAL STEWARDSHIP, PARTNERSHIP AND COORDINATION, TREATMENT FOR SERIOUS MENTAL HEALTH AND COMPLEX NEEDS, AND SUPPORTING PARENTAL RIGHTS AND FAMILY ENGAGEMENT.

description: CENTER ON CHILDHOOD TRAUMA AND SUBSTANCE USE - THE CENTER ON CHILDHOOD TRAUMA AND SUBSTANCE USE (CCTSU), LED BY INDIANA UNIVERSITY, WILL SERVE AS A NATIONAL NCTSI CATEGORY II TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION CENTER FOCUSED ON IMPROVING TRAUMA TREATMENT AND SERVICE DELIVERY FOR CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, CAREGIVERS, AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY SUBSTANCE USE-RELATED TRAUMA AND CO-OCCURRING TRAUMATIC STRESS AND SUBSTANCE USE. CCTSU WILL BUILD NATIONAL WORKFORCE CAPACITY, ADAPT AND DISSEMINATE EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT RESOURCES, AND STRENGTHEN TRAUMA-INFORMED, FAMILY-CENTERED RESPONSES ACROSS CHILD- AND FAMILY-SERVING SYSTEMS. CCTSU WILL REACH COMMUNITIES NATIONWIDE, SUCH AS RURAL AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES, AND SYSTEMS WITH LIMITED INTEGRATED TRAUMA AND SUBSTANCE USE EXPERTISE. THE CENTER IS NEEDED TO HELP TRAUMA-FOCUSED PROVIDERS UNDERSTAND SUDS, REDUCE STIGMA, SCREEN AND REFER EFFECTIVELY, AND SUPPORT FAMILIES AFFECTED BY CAREGIVER SUBSTANCE USE, OVERDOSE EXPOSURE, TRAUMATIC BEREAVEMENT, AND CO-OCCURRING TRAUMATIC STRESS AND SUBSTANCE USE. THE CENTER IS ALSO NEEDED TO HELP SUBSTANCE USE PROFESSIONALS BECOME MORE TRAUMA-INFORMED, DEVELOPMENTALLY RESPONSIVE, AND FAMILY-CENTERED. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDES CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS AFFECTED BY TRAUMATIC STRESS AND SUBSTANCE USE; YOUTH WITH CO-OCCURRING PTSD SYMPTOMS AND SUBSTANCE USE; CAREGIVERS AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY SUDS, OVERDOSE EXPOSURE, IMPAIRED CAREGIVING, FAMILY SEPARATION, AND RECOVERY NEEDS; AND THE PROFESSIONALS AND SYSTEMS THAT SERVE THEM. CHILDREN, YOUTH, CAREGIVERS, AND FAMILIES WILL BENEFIT THROUGH IMPROVED PROVIDER CAPACITY, FAMILY-FACING EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES, AND THE IMPLEMENTATION OF EVIDENCE-BASED AND EVIDENCE-INFORMED PRACTICES. CCTSU WILL IMPLEMENT A NATIONAL CAPACITY-BUILDING STRATEGY THAT INCLUDES TREATMENT ADAPTATION, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, TRAINING, CONSULTATION, TA, DISSEMINATION, STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT, FIDELITY MONITORING, AND EVALUATION. THE CENTER WILL DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE A TRAUMA AND SUBSTANCE USE PRACTICE AND IMPLEMENTATION TOOLKIT AND RESOURCE HUB WITH TF-CBT GUIDANCE, RRFT DISSEMINATION AND FIDELITY SUPPORTS, TRAUMA-INFORMED SUBSTANCE USE SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT RESOURCES, STIGMA-REDUCTION MATERIALS, FAMILY-FACING RESOURCES, AND TRAINING BUNDLES TAILORED FOR CHILD WELFARE, COURTS, JUVENILE JUSTICE, PEDIATRICS, SCHOOLS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, AND SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT SETTINGS. NATIONAL PARTNERS, PARTNERSHIP TO END ADDICTION AND OVERDOSE LIFELINE, WILL SUPPORT SUBSTANCE USE EDUCATION, PREVENTION, TREATMENT, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, AND DISSEMINATION; CCTSU WILL ALSO COLLABORATE WITH NCTSN AND SAMHSA-FUNDED CENTERS ADDRESSING OVERLAPPING POPULATIONS. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) ADAPT, REFINE, AND DISSEMINATE EVIDENCE-BASED AND EVIDENCE-INFORMED CHILDHOOD TRAUMA TREATMENT APPROACHES ADDRESSING TRAUMATIC STRESS AND SUBSTANCE USE; (2) STRENGTHEN WORKFORCE CAPACITY TO DELIVER TRAUMA-INFORMED AND TRAUMA-SPECIFIC SERVICES FOR SUBSTANCE USE-RELATED TRAUMATIC STRESS; AND (3) EXPAND IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINABILITY OF EVIDENCE-BASED CHILDHOOD TRAUMA INTERVENTIONS ACROSS CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE CONDUCTING A NATIONAL NEEDS ASSESSMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN IN Y1; DEVELOPING AND PILOTING TREATMENT ADAPTATION RESOURCES BY Y2; TRAINING AT LEAST 2,000 PROFESSIONALS ANNUALLY; PROVIDING TA AND IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT TO AT LEAST 25 ORGANIZATIONS ANNUALLY; DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING AT LEAST 20 PRACTICAL PRODUCTS OR RESOURCES; AND DEMONSTRATING IMPROVEMENTS IN PROVIDER KNOWLEDGE, CONFIDENCE, IMPLEMENTATION READINESS, AND ADOPTION OF EVIDENCE-BASED OR EVIDENCE-INFORMED PRACTICES. EVALUATION WILL USE IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE, FIDELITY MONITORING, CQI, AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING TO SUPPORT SAMHSA PRIORITIES, SUCH AS IMPROVED ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT, PREVENTION, RECOVERY, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, DATA-DRIVEN DECISION-MAKING, AND IMPROVED OUTCOMES FOR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES.

description: TF-CBT WORKBOOK COACH: SAFE AI-ASSISTED IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT FOR CHILD TRAUMA TREATMENT - THE NORTH CAROLINA YOUTH VIOLENCE PREVENTION CENTER (NC-YVPC) PROPOSES TF-CBT WORKBOOK COACH, A NATIONAL CAPACITY-BUILDING PROJECT TO EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENT FOR CHILDREN AND YOUTH THROUGH SAFE AI-ASSISTED IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP, TEST, EVALUATE, AND DISSEMINATE A SUPERVISED INTERACTIVE WORKBOOK APPLICATION THAT HELPS YOUTH COMPLETE STRUCTURED TRAUMA-FOCUSED COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (TF-CBT) PRACTICE ACTIVITIES BETWEEN HUMAN SERVICE CONTACTS. THE TOOL WILL NOT REPLACE THERAPISTS OR PROVIDE UNSUPERVISED AI THERAPY. IT WILL HELP YOUTH PRACTICE SKILLS, PREPARE FOR SESSIONS, AND ENGAGE CAREGIVERS WHILE TRAINED PROFESSIONALS RETAIN RESPONSIBILITY FOR ASSESSMENT, SAFETY, MANDATED REPORTING, TRAUMA PROCESSING, AND CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING.  CHILDREN EXPOSED TO ABUSE, NEGLECT, VIOLENCE, BULLYING, DISASTERS, OR OTHER ADVERSE EXPERIENCES NEED TIMELY TRAUMA TREATMENT, BUT RURAL AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES OFTEN LACK ENOUGH TRAINED CLINICIANS. YOUTH MAY BE IDENTIFIED THROUGH SCHOOLS, CHILD ADVOCACY CENTERS, CHILD WELFARE, JUVENILE JUSTICE, VICTIM SERVICES, OR COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH SYSTEMS, YET WAIT WEEKS OR MONTHS FOR SPECIALIZED CARE. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THAT GAP BY CREATING A SAFE, SUPERVISED TOOL THAT EXTENDS TF-CBT PRACTICE WITHOUT REDUCING THE IMPORTANCE OF THE HUMAN THERAPIST.  THE TF-CBT WORKBOOK COACH WILL FOLLOW THE ESTABLISHED TF-CBT SEQUENCE: PSYCHOEDUCATION, RELAXATION, AFFECT MODULATION, COGNITIVE COPING, TRAUMA NARRATIVE PREPARATION, CAREGIVER-SUPPORTED PRACTICE, SAFETY PLANNING, CLOSURE, AND RELAPSE PREVENTION. TRAUMA NARRATIVE MODULES WILL REQUIRE ACTIVE THERAPIST ASSIGNMENT, DOCUMENTED READINESS, AND HUMAN REVIEW. YOUTH NOT ASSIGNED TO AN ACTIVE THERAPIST MAY USE ONLY LOWER-INTENSITY ORIENTATION, COPING, CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT, AND SAFETY-PLANNING FEATURES THROUGH A SPONSORING AGENCY WITH A CLINICAL SUPERVISOR.  THE APPLICATION WILL USE CLINICALLY APPROVED CONTENT AND STRUCTURED WORKFLOWS RATHER THAN AN OPEN-ENDED PUBLIC CHATBOT. IT WILL INCLUDE ORIENTATION, CONSENT/ASSENT, SAFETY PLANNING, CRISIS CONTACTS, THERAPIST DASHBOARDS, HUMAN REVIEW OF FLAGGED CONTENT, AND ESCALATION PROCEDURES. THE AI WORKBOOK COACH WILL BE RESTRICTED FROM DIAGNOSING, GIVING MEDICATION ADVICE, MAKING LEGAL OR CUSTODY RECOMMENDATIONS, MANDATED REPORTING DECISIONS, OR REPLACING CLINICAL JUDGMENT. SAFETY FLAGS WILL INCLUDE DANGER TO SELF OR OTHERS, ABUSE OR EXPLOITATION CONCERNS, EXTREME DISTRESS, WEAPONS ACCESS, MEDICAL EMERGENCIES, AND SECRECY ABOUT DANGER. PRIVACY PROTECTIONS WILL INCLUDE DATA MINIMIZATION, ROLE-BASED ACCESS, SECURE DATA HANDLING, AUDIT LOGS, VENDOR REVIEW, AND SAFEGUARDS AGAINST USING IDENTIFIABLE YOUTH CONTENT TO TRAIN PUBLIC AI MODELS.  NC-YVPC WILL IMPLEMENT THE PROJECT THROUGH NATIONAL WORKFORCE AND IMPLEMENTATION ACTIVITIES, NOT MERELY SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT. ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE APP DEVELOPMENT; THERAPIST, SUPERVISOR, CAREGIVER, AND YOUTH MATERIALS; PROVIDER TRAINING AND CONSULTATION; COLLABORATION WITH NCTSN PARTNERS AND NCTSI CATEGORY I, II, AND III CENTERS; YOUTH, CAREGIVER, CLINICIAN, AND RURAL PROVIDER ENGAGEMENT; EVALUATION, CQI, AND DISSEMINATION. PRODUCTS WILL INCLUDE THE WORKBOOK APPLICATION, THERAPIST DASHBOARD, SAFETY PROTOCOLS, FIDELITY CHECKLISTS, READINESS TOOLS, TRAINING MODULES, CAREGIVER MATERIALS, IMPLEMENTATION BRIEFS, AND TOOLKITS.  THE PROJECT WILL BE ANCHORED IN RURAL SOUTHEASTERN NORTH CAROLINA AND DISSEMINATED NATIONALLY TO CHILD ADVOCACY CENTERS, SCHOOLS, CHILD WELFARE, JUVENILE JUSTICE, COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH, TRIBAL AND RURAL ORGANIZATIONS, VICTIM-SERVICE SYSTEMS, AND NCTSN PARTNERS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE SAFER PROVIDER USE OF SUPERVISED DIGITAL TOOLS, YOUTH COMPLETION OF TF-CBT PRACTICE ACTIVITIES, STRONGER CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT, IMPROVED THERAPIST REVIEW OF BETWEEN-SESSION WORK, AND WIDER DISSEMINATION OF TOOLS THAT HELP UNDER-RESOURCED AGENCIES DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED CHILD TRAUMA CARE WITH FIDELITY AND HUMAN CLINICAL OVERSIGHT.

description: STRYDD FORWARD FOR QUALITY CARE AND EMPOWERING PARENTS/CAREGIVERS OF YOUTH WITH IDD - THE STRYDD CENTER AT THE NORTHWELL HEALTH SYSTEM WILL BUILD ON OUR EXPERTISE SUPPORTING TRAUMA RECOVERY FOR YOUTH WITH INTELLECTUAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES (IDD). ABOUT 16% OF THE POPULATION, THESE YOUTH ARE AT INCREASED RISK OF VICTIMIZATION AND A RANGE OF OTHER TRAUMATIC EXPERIENCES (E.G. MEDICAL TRAUMA), BUT THEIR TRAUMA-RELATED NEEDS OFTEN ARE IGNORED. WE WILL CONTINUE TO BUILD AWARENESS OF THE TRAUMA-RELATED NEEDS OF THIS POPULATION WITHIN NCTSN AND THE NATION AND WORK TO INCREASE TRAUMA INFORMED CARE AND APPROPRIATE TRAUMA SCREENING AND TRAUMA TREATMENT FOR THESE YOUTH AND THEIR FAMILIES TO INCREASE CAPACITY AND ACCESS. WE WILL IMPROVE RECOGNITION OF THE MENTAL HEALTH IMPACT OF TRAUMA IN THESE VULNERABLE YOUTH THROUGH CONTINUED DISSEMINATION OF EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS IN THE COMMUNITY (SUCH AS THE ROAD TO RECOVERY TOOLKIT AND FACT SHEETS DEVELOPED WITH NCTSN COLLABORATORS) AS WELL AS TRAININGS OF PROVIDERS USING THE NCTSN CORE CURRICULUM ON CHILDHOOD TRAUMA WITH CASES WE HAVE DEVELOPED ILLUSTRATING THESE YOUTH’S NEEDS. WE WILL SERVE AS A TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE CENTER TO SUPPORT OTHERS IN THE NETWORK REGARDING USE OF THESE TOOLS. WE WILL CONTINUE TO TRAIN PROVIDERS ON TAILORING TF-CBT TREATMENT FOR YOUTH WITH IDD AND WILL EXPAND THE MATERIALS WE DEVELOPED ACROSS OTHER EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS AND SERVICE SYSTEMS. ONE PLANNED ADDITION IS INFORMATION ON BEST PRACTICES IN SCREENING FOR PRENATAL ALCOHOL EXPOSURE SINCE YOUTH WITH FETAL ALCOHOL SPECTRUM DISORDER, ONE OF THE MOST COMMON NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS, HAVE SPECIFIC TREATMENT NEEDS. WE WILL PARTNER WITH TREATMENT DEVELOPERS WITHIN NCTSN TO HELP PROVIDERS EXPAND THE RANGE OF INTERVENTIONS AVAILABLE TO YOUTH WITH IDD. WE WILL THEN GENERATE GUIDANCE ON GENERAL IDD TAILORING VERSUS TREATMENT SPECIFIC IDD ACCOMMODATIONS TO MAXIMIZE SCALABILITY. WE ALSO WILL ADDRESS THE NEED FOR EXPERT CONSULTATION ON SOME COMPLEX CASES BY PROVIDING A NETWORK-WIDE MONTHLY CASE CONSULTATION SERVICE. WHILE BROADLY DISSEMINATING OUR MATERIALS AND TRAININGS, WE WILL TARGET SOME SPECIFIC SERVICE SYSTEMS INCLUDING CHILD WELFARE AND JUVENILE JUSTICE. WE WILL PROVIDE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR CATEGORY III COMMUNITY SITES BOTH BY DIRECT TRAINING FROM US, AND BY CO-TRAINING WITH DEVELOPERS OF TREATMENTS FOR WHICH WE WILL CO-CONSTRUCT ADJUSTMENTS FOR YOUTH WITH IDD. FOR OUR POPULATION, TRAUMA-RELATED SYMPTOMS ARE OFTEN MISATTRIBUTED TO THEIR DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES (DIAGNOSTIC OVERSHADOWING) AND TREATED BY SIMPLISTIC BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS AND/OR EXCESSIVE MEDICATION. TO REDUCE THIS, WE WILL INCREASE AWARENESS OF NEED FOR TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE FOR THESE YOUTH IN A VARIETY OF SERVICE SYSTEMS. AS PART OF THIS, WE WILL CONTINUE OUR COLLABORATION WITH ABA EXPERTS TO EDUCATE ABA PROVIDERS AND DIRECT CARE STAFF ON HOW TO PROVIDE POSITIVE BEHAVIORAL SUPPORTS AND MAKE THEIR INTERVENTIONS MORE TRAUMA INFORMED WITH EMPHASIS ON DATA DRIVEN OUTCOMES INCLUDING REDUCED RELIANCE ON RESTRICTIVE PROCEDURES, EMERGENCY MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES AND/OR PHARMACOTHERAPY. TO SUPPORT NEED FOR BETTER TRAUMA SCREENING FOR YOUTH WITH IDD, A STRYDD CONTRIBUTOR WILL CONTINUE TO REFINE THE INTERACTIVE TRAUMA SCALE AND DEVELOP A SHORTENED VERSION SUITABLE FOR USE WITH PEDIATRICIANS. WE WILL CONTINUE TO DISSEMINATE OUR STRESS FIRST AID RESILIENCE BUILDING INTERVENTION FOR SCHOOL PERSONNEL AND STUDENTS AND WILL DEVELOP A VERSION FOR PARENTS. FINALLY, TO INCREASE THEIR VISIBILITY AND VOICE IN DECISION MAKING AND TO SUPPORT PARENT NEEDS AND PERSPECTIVE, WE WILL RECRUIT A PARENT ADVISORY GROUP TO BEST MEET CAREGIVER NEEDS AND FACILITATE ONGOING INPUT FROM PARENTS ON OUR FULL RANGE OF GRANT ACTIVITIES INCLUDING PSYCHOEDUCATION, TREATMENTS AND INTERVENTIONS.

description: THE CENTER FOR SAFE AND EFFECTIVE TRAUMA TREATMENT (CSETT) - THE CENTER FOR SAFE AND EFFECTIVE TRAUMA TREATMENT (CSETT) WILL SERVE AS AN NCTSN CATEGORY II TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION CENTER DEDICATED TO IMPROVING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED AND EVIDENCE-INFORMED TRAUMA TREATMENT FOR TRAUMATIZED CHILDREN WHO EXHIBIT HIGH-RISK BEHAVIORS (E.G., AGGRESSION, SELF-HARM, RUNNING AWAY, SUBSTANCE ABUSE) OR WHO ARE AT RISK OF MALTREATMENT FROM THEIR CAREGIVERS.  THESE CHILDREN AND FAMILIES POSE CONSIDERABLE CHALLENGES FOR PROVIDERS, GIVEN THE SAFETY RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH THEIR CARE, AND KNOWLEDGE TO GUIDE PROVIDERS IS LIMITED BECAUSE THEY ARE OFTEN EXCLUDED FROM CLINICAL TRIALS DUE TO THEIR RISKS. CSETT WILL SERVE AS A NATIONAL RESOURCE FOR THE SAFE AND EFFECTIVE CARE OF HIGH-RISK TRAUMATIZED CHILDREN AND FAMILIES BY ADAPTING THE TREATMENT MODEL TRAUMA SYSTEMS THERAPY (TST) AND ITS ACCOMPANYING NEVER LOOK AWAY TRAUMA TRAINING PROGRAM (NLA TTP), AND DISSEMINATING THEM ACROSS THE SERVICE SYSTEM IN FOUR U.S. REGIONS.  PROJECT NAME: THE CENTER FOR SAFE AND EFFECTIVE TRAUMA TREATMENT (CSETT) GEOGRAPHIC REACH AND CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT: CSETT WILL FOCUS ON FOUR REGIONS WITH ESTABLISHED TST INFRASTRUCTURE: THE SOUTH, NORTHEAST, MIDWEST, AND WEST. MANY HIGH-RISK CHILDREN AND FAMILIES IN THESE REGIONS HAVE INSUFFICIENT ACCESS TO SAFE AND EFFECTIVE CHILDHOOD TRAUMA TREATMENTS. CSETT WILL BUILD CAPACITY BY ESTABLISHING NEW SPECIALIZED TREATMENT TEAMS, DELIVERING SCALABLE WORKFORCE TRAINING, AND EXPANDING IMPLEMENTATION OF EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS, STARTING WITH NCTSN CATEGORY III CENTERS IN EACH REGION. POPULATION OF FOCUS: TRAUMATIZED CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS AGED 3–18 WHO EXHIBIT HIGH-RISK BEHAVIORS ENTAILING HARM TO THEMSELVES OR OTHERS OR WHO ARE AT RISK OF MALTREATMENT. WITHOUT EFFECTIVE INTERVENTION, THESE CHILDREN FACE PLACEMENT INSTABILITY, SCHOOL DISRUPTION, PSYCHIATRIC HOSPITALIZATION, AND CONTINUED MALTREATMENT IN CHILDHOOD, AND ELEVATED RISK OVER THE COURSE OF THEIR LIVES FOR CHRONIC MENTAL ILLNESS, SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, AND RELIANCE ON CRISIS AND OTHER INTENSIVE SERVICES. THIS POPULATION REPRESENTS ONE OF SAMHSA'S HIGHEST PRIORITIES FOR IMPROVING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS TO INCREASE CAPACITY: CSETT WILL LEVERAGE ESTABLISHED TST PROGRAMS IN FIVE STATES ACROSS FOUR REGIONS—ALABAMA (SOUTH), OHIO (MIDWEST), COLORADO (WEST), AND NEW YORK AND RHODE ISLAND (NORTHEAST)—PARTNERING WITH THESE PROGRAMS TO TRAIN THE WORKFORCE AND EXPAND ACCESS TO EFFECTIVE TREATMENT. WORKFORCE TRAINING WILL BE ENHANCED BY ADAPTING THE NLA TTP, A SCALABLE SIX-SESSION ANIMATED VIDEO CURRICULUM FOR PROVIDERS. ACCESS WILL BE EXPANDED WITH NEW ADAPTED TST PROGRAMS IN EACH REGION.  PROJECT GOALS: (1) ADAPT TST AND THE NLA TTP TO EXPAND ACCESS TO SAFE AND EFFECTIVE TREATMENT FOR HIGH-RISK CHILDREN AND FAMILIES. (2) BUILD WORKFORCE CAPACITY BY DELIVERING NLA TTP TO NCTSI GRANTEES AND PROVIDERS ACROSS CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS. (3) EXPAND ACCESS BY ESTABLISHING NEW TST TEAMS SERVING THE POPULATION OF FOCUS. (4) ENGAGE CHILDREN, YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND SERVICE PROVIDERS WITH CLEAR FEEDBACK LOOPS PROTECTING PARENTAL RIGHTS. (5) APPLY EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE IMPLEMENTATION, FIDELITY MONITORING, CQI, EVALUATION, AND SUSTAINABILITY FRAMEWORKS CONSISTENT WITH GOLD-STANDARD SCIENCE. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: (1) ESTABLISH 18 NEW SPECIALIZED TST TEAMS ACROSS FOUR REGIONS, EQUIPPING 180 PROVIDERS WITH SPECIALIZED SKILLS FOR THIS HIGH-RISK PO PULATION. (2) ACHIEVE ≥80% FIDELITY ADHERENCE WITH DEMONSTRATED IMPROVEMENTS IN CHILD OUTCOMES (REDUCED CRITICAL INCIDENTS, INCREASED PLACEMENT STABILITY, IMPROVED FUNCTIONING). (3) TRAIN 2,500 PROFESSIONALS (500/YEAR) VIA THE NLA TTP ACROSS MENTAL HEALTH, CHILD WELFARE, JUVENILE JUSTICE, SCHOOLS, AND SUBSTANCE USE SETTINGS.

description: ADVANCING AN INTEGRATED TRAUMA CARE CONTINUUM FOR DEAF AND HARD OF HEARING YOUTH - THE DEAF AND HARD OF HEARING CHILD RESILIENCE CENTER (DHHCRC) AT GALLAUDET UNIVERSITY WILL IMPROVE ACCESS TO TRAUMA PREVENTION, EARLY IDENTIFICATION, AND EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT FOR DEAF, HARD OF HEARING, AND DEAFBLIND YOUTH NATIONWIDE. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT AN INTEGRATED TRAUMA CARE CONTINUUM THAT EQUIPS SCHOOLS, FAMILIES, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS WITH TOOLS, TRAINING, AND INTERVENTIONS TO RECOGNIZE, RESPOND TO, AND TREAT CHILDHOOD TRAUMA. DHHCRC PROPOSES ADVANCING AN INTEGRATED TRAUMA CARE CONTINUUM FOR DEAF AND HARD OF HEARING YOUTH, A NATIONAL CHILD TRAUMATIC STRESS INITIATIVE (NCTSI) CATEGORY II TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION CENTER. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE DEAF, HARD OF HEARING, AND DEAFBLIND (DHH) CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS FROM BIRTH THROUGH AGE 21, THEIR FAMILIES, EDUCATORS, SCHOOL MENTAL HEALTH PERSONNEL, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINICIANS, AND OTHER CHILD-SERVING PROFESSIONALS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES THROUGH TRAINING, CONSULTATION, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT, AND DISSEMINATION.  THE PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT THE DEAF YOUTH TRAUMA ACCESS AND CARE CONTINUUM MODEL, A MULTI-TIERED FRAMEWORK INTEGRATING TRAUMA PREVENTION, EARLY IDENTIFICATION, REFERRAL, SCHOOL-BASED INTERVENTION, AND OUTPATIENT TREATMENT. MAJOR STRATEGIES INCLUDE: (1) DISSEMINATING TRAUMA-INFORMED PREVENTION AND RESILIENCE RESOURCES FOR FAMILIES AND SCHOOLS; (2) IMPLEMENTING ENGLISH AND ASL-ACCESSIBLE TRAUMA SCREENING AND REFERRAL PATHWAYS; (3) ADAPTING, IMPLEMENTING, AND/OR EVALUATING TRAUMA-FOCUSED COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (TF-CBT), SENSORY MOTOR AROUSAL REGULATION TREATMENT (SMART), PARENT-CHILD INTERACTION THERAPY (PCIT), AND COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTION FOR TRAUMA IN SCHOOLS (CBITS) FOR DHH YOUTH; (4) EXPANDING WORKFORCE CAPACITY THROUGH THE CORE CURRICULUM ON CHILDHOOD TRAUMA (CCCT), PSYCHOLOGICAL FIRST AID (PFA), CONSULTATION, AND IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT; AND (5) DISSEMINATING RESOURCES NATIONALLY THROUGH THE DHH RESOURCE HUB AND LEARNING COLLABORATIVE.  PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) IMPROVE PREVENTION, EARLY IDENTIFICATION, AND ACCESS TO TRAUMA SUPPORTS THROUGH SCHOOL, FAMILY, AND COMMUNITY SYSTEMS; (2) ADAPT, IMPLEMENT, AND EVALUATE EVIDENCE-INFORMED AND EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA INTERVENTIONS FOR DHH YOUTH AND FAMILIES; AND (3) STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF SCHOOLS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, AND FAMILIES TO RECOGNIZE, RESPOND TO, AND ADDRESS CHILDHOOD TRAUMA. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE PILOTING THE TRAUMA CARE CONTINUUM MODEL IN PARTNER SCHOOLS; IMPLEMENTING ENGLISH/ASL-ACCESSIBLE SCREENING AND REFERRAL PROTOCOLS; DEVELOPING AND PILOTING DHH-SPECIFIC CBITS ADAPTATIONS; EXPANDING TRAINING AND CONSULTATION IN ADAPTED TRAUMA INTERVENTIONS (E.G., TF-CBT, PCIT, SMART, CCCT, & PFA); ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL RESOURCE HUB AND IMPLEMENTATION EXCHANGE; AND EVALUATING IMPLEMENTATION, FIDELITY, FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, SERVICE ACCESS, AND SUSTAINABILITY. THE PROJECT WILL PRODUCE A SCALABLE NATIONAL MODEL THAT EXPANDS ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY TRAUMA SERVICES AND STRENGTHENS CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS FOR DHH YOUTH NATIONWIDE.

description: THE FAMILY TRAUMA ASSESSMENT OF CHILDREN AND CAREGIVERS (F-TACC) - PROJECT ABSTRACT  PROJECT NAME: THE FAMILY TRAUMA ASSESSMENT OF CHILDREN AND CAREGIVERS (F-TACC) GEOGRAPHIC AREA: THE FAMILY TRAUMA ASSESSMENT OF CHILDREN AND CAREGIVERS (F-TACC) SEEKS NCTSI-II FUNDING FOR ITS TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION CENTER, LOCATED WITHIN THE SCHOOL OF SOCIAL WORK AT WESTERN MICHIGAN UNIVERSITY.  THROUGH THIS FUNDING, F-TACC WILL OPERATE A NATIONAL CHILD TRAUMATIC STRESS INITIATIVE CATEGORY 2 TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION (TSA) CENTER TRAIN SITES TO UTILIZE OUR F-TACC COMPREHENSIVE FAMILY TRAUMA ASSESSMENT MODEL. OUR MODEL IS DESIGNED TO MEET THE NEEDS OF CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND THEIR FAMILIES TO ASSESS INTERGENERATIONAL TRAUMA AND BUILD RESILIENCY PLANS TO ADDRESS THE IMPACT TO CHILDREN AND THEIR CAREGIVERS HOLISTICALLY. IN YEAR ONE, OUR PARTNER SITES WILL BE LOCATED IN TWO STATES: MICHIGAN AND GEORGIA. BOTH STATES HAVE IDENTIFIED THE NEED FOR COMPREHENSIVE FAMILY TRAUMA ASSESSMENT FOR FAMILIES ENGAGED WITH THE PUBLIC CHILD WELFARE SYSTEM. IN YEARS 2-5 AN ADDITIONAL 24 SITES (TARGETING ENLISTMENT OF CATEGORY III SITES) WILL IMPLEMENT THE F-TACC. BOTH PRODUCTS AND VIDEO WILL BE DEVELOPED AND OFFERED TO ALL PARTICIPATING SITES AS WELL AS ALL OTHER NCTSN SITES.  SYSTEM IMPACT:  STATE CHILD WELFARE POLICY REQUIREMENTS ILLUSTRATE THE ASSESSMENT GAPS WITHIN THESE SYSTEMS. THIS PROJECT WILL LAUNCH WITH FOUR PARTNER SITES: TWO IN MICHIGAN AND TWO IN GEORGIA.  THE GEORGIA DIVISION OF FAMILY AND CHILDREN SERVICES (DFCS) CHILD WELFARE REQUIRES THAT CHILDREN IN THE CHILD WELFARE SYSTEM RECEIVE A COMPREHENSIVE CHILD AND FAMILY ASSESSMENT (CCFA) ENCOMPASSING A FAMILY ASSESSMENT, SOCIAL STUDY, TRAUMA ASSESSMENT, MEDICAL ASSESSMENT, KINSHIP ASSESSMENT, AND REASSESSMENT IF THE CCFA IS 12 MONTHS OR OLDER. THE F-TACC FAMILY ASSESSMENT MODEL IS UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO FULFILL ALL REQUIRED CCFA COMPONENTS THROUGH A SINGLE, INTEGRATED, PERSON-CENTERED PROCESS THAT NOT ONLY MEETS POLICY REQUIREMENTS BUT EXCEEDS THEM BY ADDRESSING INTERGENERATIONAL TRAUMA AND BY PROVIDING A HOLISTIC RESILIENCY PLAN FOR THE FAMILY. GEORGIA IS ONE OF SEVERAL STATES WHERE POLICY INFRASTRUCTURE ALREADY MANDATES THIS LEVEL OF ASSESSMENT BUT WHERE ACCESS TO A MODEL CAPABLE OF DELIVERING IT COMPREHENSIVELY REMAINS A SIGNIFICANT GAP. THE MICHIGAN CHILD WELFARE IMPROVEMENT TASK FORCE ANNOUNCED IN NOVEMBER 2025 THAT THEIR FOCUS WOULD BE ON  2GEN  A TWO-GENERATION OR MULTI-GENERATIONAL APPROACH TO CHILD WELFARE THAT RECOGNIZES THE INTERCONNECTION OF THE NEEDS OF CHILDREN WITH PARENTS AND OTHER CAREGIVERS. 2GEN GIVES  ATTENTION TO THE NEEDS OF BOTH THE CHILD AND THE CAREGIVER FOR THE CHILD AS A WHOLE PICTURE, A WHOLE FAMILY…PROMOTING INCREASED FAMILY WELLBEING AND PROSPERITY OF EACH FAMILY MEMBER. * THE F-TACC FAMILY ASSESSMENT APPROACH ADDRESSES THE GAPS IN GEORGIA AND IN MICHIGAN AND AIMS INCREASE FAMILY STABILIZATION AND/OR FAMILY REUNIFICATION TO ENSURE THAT EVERY CHILD HAS A SAFE, STABLE, AND LOVING HOME.               PROJECT GOALS: GOAL 1: DISSEMINATE THE F-TACC ASSESSMENT MODEL TO IMPROVE CAPACITY AND ACCESS TO IMPLEMENTING COMPREHENSIVE NEURODEVELOPMENTAL FAMILY TRAUMA ASSESSMENT NATIONWIDE. GOAL 2: UTILIZE THE KEY PRINCIPALS OF IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE THROUGH A LEARNING COLLABORATIVE. GOAL 3: BUILD CAPACITY FOR EACH COHORT SITE TO BEGIN CONDUCTING FAMILY ASSESSMENTS OF INITIAL FAMILY TRAUMA ASSESSMENT MODEL. GOAL 4: DEVELOPMENT OF PRODUCTS FOR F-TACC FAMILY TRAUMA ASSESSMENT. GOAL 5: CREATE A NETWORK OF NATIONWIDE FAMILY TRAUMA ASSESSMENT CENTERS.  GOAL 6: ESTABLISH OF AN ADVISORY BOARD FOR F-TACC. GOAL 7:  COLLABORATE WITH NCTSN LEVEL II AND LEVEL III SITES FOR INTEGRATION OF FAMILY TRAUMA ASSESSMENT.  *HTTPS://MICHIGANCWTF.ORG/MEDIA/

description: NATIONAL CENTER FOR RELATIONSHIP ORIENTED ORGANIZATIONAL TRAUMA SERVICES (THE ROOTS NATIONAL CENTER) - THE CHILDREN'S CENTER UTAH (TCCU) PROPOSES TO ESTABLISH THE NATIONAL CENTER FOR RELATIONSHIP ORIENTED ORGANIZATIONAL TRAUMA SERVICES (THE ROOTS NATIONAL CENTER) UNDER THE NATIONAL CHILD TRAUMATIC STRESS INITIATIVE (NCTSI) CATEGORY II TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION (TSA) CENTER PROGRAM. ROOTS WILL IMPROVE ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY, EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENT FOR INFANTS, YOUNG CHILDREN (BIRTH TO AGE FIVE), AND FAMILIES BY STRENGTHENING THE CAPACITY OF ORGANIZATIONS TO IMPLEMENT, ADAPT, AND SUSTAIN EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENT AND TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICES WITH FIDELITY. DESPITE THE AVAILABILITY OF EFFECTIVE EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENTS, MANY ORGANIZATIONS EXPERIENCE PERSISTENT IMPLEMENTATION BARRIERS, INCLUDING WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, STAFF TURNOVER, LIMITED LEADERSHIP ENGAGEMENT, FRAGMENTED REFERRAL PATHWAYS, GEOGRAPHIC ISOLATION, AND INADEQUATE IMPLEMENTATION INFRASTRUCTURE. THESE BARRIERS ARE ESPECIALLY PRONOUNCED IN RURAL AND FRONTIER COMMUNITIES, RESULTING IN LIMITED ACCESS TO SPECIALIZED TRAUMA TREATMENT FOR YOUNG CHILDREN. ROOTS ADDRESSES THESE CHALLENGES BY ADAPTING THE ORGANIZATIONAL IMPLEMENTATION METHODOLOGY USED TO SUPPORT EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT RATHER THAN MODIFYING THE CLINICAL COMPONENTS OF THE TREATMENT MODELS THEMSELVES.  CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY (CPP) WILL SERVE AS THE PRIMARY DEMONSTRATION MODEL BECAUSE OF ITS STRONG EVIDENCE BASE FOR CHILDREN BIRTH TO FIVE AND ITS APPLICABILITY TO CHILDREN EXPERIENCING COMPLEX TRAUMA. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO SUPPORT IMPLEMENTATION OF OTHER NCTSN-SUPPORTED EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENTS AND TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICE APPROACHES APPROPRIATE FOR PARTICIPATING ORGANIZATIONS. ROOTS WILL DEVELOP, PILOT, EVALUATE, AND DISSEMINATE A COMPREHENSIVE ORGANIZATIONAL IMPLEMENTATION MODEL CONSISTING OF THREE INTEGRATED COMPONENTS: (1) THE EARLY CHILDHOOD TRAUMA TREATMENT ORGANIZATIONAL READINESS ASSESSMENT (ECTT-ORA) TO ASSESS ORGANIZATIONAL READINESS AND IMPLEMENTATION CAPACITY; (2) THE TRAUMA TREATMENT IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP (TTIR) TO PROVIDE INDIVIDUALIZED IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING; AND (3) THE ROOTS ACADEMY, A FLEXIBLE WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT SYSTEM THAT OFFERS LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT, LEARNING COLLABORATIVES, IMPLEMENTATION COACHING, REFLECTIVE SUPERVISION, TELECONSULTATION, AND ROLE-SPECIFIC PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. ORGANIZATIONS WILL PARTICIPATE THROUGH MULTIPLE PATHWAYS, INCLUDING INTENSIVE LEARNING COLLABORATIVES, INDIVIDUALIZED CONSULTATION, AND STAND-ALONE TRAINING, ALLOWING PARTICIPATION BASED ON ORGANIZATIONAL READINESS AND CAPACITY.  DURING THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, ROOTS WILL PROVIDE ORGANIZATIONAL IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT TO AT LEAST 40 CHILD-SERVING ORGANIZATIONS, FACILITATE TWO CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY LEARNING COLLABORATIVES IN UTAH, ESTABLISH TWO NATIONAL ROOTS ACADEMY LEARNING COLLABORATIVES, DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE NATIONALLY REPLICABLE IMPLEMENTATION RESOURCES, AND STRENGTHEN THE WORKFORCE THROUGH COMPETENCY-BASED TRAINING AND SUPERVISION. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO CREATE A WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PLAN, SUPERVISION CURRICULUM, TELEHEALTH IMPLEMENTATION RESOURCES, AND IMPLEMENTATION TOOLKITS DESIGNED TO IMPROVE ORGANIZATIONAL READINESS, IMPLEMENTATION FIDELITY, WORKFORCE COMPETENCY, AND LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL BE GUIDED BY THE CONSOLIDATED FRAMEWORK FOR IMPLEMENTATION RESEARCH (CFIR) AND EVALUATED USING PROCTOR'S IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES FRAMEWORK, SPARS/GPRA PERFORMANCE MEASURES, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT METHODS. PRODUCTS AND LESSONS LEARNED WILL BE DISSEMINATED NATIONALLY THROUGH CONFERENCES, WEBINARS, PUBLICATIONS, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND COLLABORATION WITH NCTSI CATEGORY I, II, AND III CENTERS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT REQUESTS $600,000 ANNUALLY FOR FIVE YEARS TO ESTABLISH ROOTS AS A NATIONAL IMPLEMENTATION RESOURCE THAT STRENGTHENS ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY, EXPANDS ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENT AND TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICES, AND IMPROVES BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR CHILDREN AFFECTED BY TRAUMA.

description: RENEWED HOPE: CENTER FOR CHILD DISASTER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH - RENEWED HOPE: CENTER FOR CHILD DISASTER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH (RENEWED HOPE) WILL BUILD NATIONAL CAPACITY TO DELIVER TIMELY, TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE TO CHILDREN AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY DISASTERS AND MASS VIOLENCE BY CERTIFYING TRAINERS, ADAPTING INTERVENTIONS FOR PRIORITY POPULATIONS, AND DELIVERING RAPID, JUST-IN-TIME TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ACROSS THE UNITED STATES—WITH PRIORITIZED EMPHASIS ON DISASTER-PRONE STATES, INDIAN TRIBES, AND TERRITORIES IDENTIFIED WITH FEDERAL, PROJECT, AND NCTSN PARTNERS. THE PROJECT FOCUSES ON CHILDREN AND YOUTH, WITH SPECIAL ATTENTION TO DEAF AND HARD OF HEARING (DHH) YOUTH AND THOSE WHO HAVE EXPERIENCED MASS VIOLENCE. WE WILL CONDUCT COMPREHENSIVE TRAINER INSTITUTES IN PSYCHOLOGICAL FIRST AID (PFA), PSYCHOLOGICAL FIRST AID FOR SCHOOLS (PFA-S), SKILLS FOR PSYCHOLOGICAL RECOVERY (SPR), AND SAFETY-A, AND PROVIDE ONGOING IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORTS INCLUDING FIDELITY COACHING, CONSULTATION, AND COLLABORATION VIA A VIRTUAL TRAINER PLATFORM. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO (1) EXPAND THE DISASTER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE, (2) INCREASE TRAINER EXPERTISE AND FIDELITY IN EVIDENCE-BASED, TRAUMA-INFORMED PRACTICES, (3) ADAPT TRAININGS FOR PRIORITY POPULATIONS, (4) EMPOWER COMMUNITIES, CAREGIVERS, AND LOCAL SYSTEMS AFTER DISASTERS, AND (5) BUILD SUSTAINABLE SYSTEMS THROUGH STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE CERTIFYING 110 PFA TRAINERS, 40 SPR TRAINERS, AND 80 PFA-S TRAINERS, WHO WILL COLLECTIVELY TRAIN 5,000 PROVIDERS IN PFA, 1,000 IN SPR, AND 3,000 IN PFA-S; DELIVERING CONSULTATION AND TA THAT ADDRESSES BEREAVED OR INJURED CHILDREN, YOUTH WITH PRIOR TRAUMA, DISPLACED FAMILIES, AND YOUTH AT ELEVATED RISK FOR SUBSTANCE USE OR SUICIDE; DISSEMINATING MATERIALS AFTER 40 DISASTERS; AND PROVIDING COMPREHENSIVE SUPPORT TO 9 DISASTER-IMPACTED COMMUNITIES. RENEWED HOPE WILL ENGAGE 30 NEW STRATEGIC PARTNERS AND ASSIST THREE HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS TO INTEGRATE DISASTER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INTO WORKFORCE TRAINING. ALIGNED WITH SAMHSA STRATEGIC PRIORITIES, THIS PROJECT EXPANDS THE DISASTER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE AND EMBEDS EVIDENCE-BASED, OUTCOME-FOCUSED PRACTICES ACROSS SYSTEMS; EMPHASIZES EARLY INTERVENTION AND PREVENTION THROUGH PFA, PFA-S, AND SPR; STRENGTHENS SUICIDE AND SELF-HARM RISK REDUCTION VIA SAFETY-A AND TARGETED CONSULTATION; MITIGATES SUBSTANCE MISUSE RISK BY INTEGRATING SCREENING, TRIAGE, AND CLEAR REFERRAL PATHWAYS FOR INTERVENTION; ADVANCES ACCESSIBILITY THROUGH DHH SPECIFIC AND CULTURALLY-RESPONSIVE ADAPTATIONS; PROMOTES SYSTEM INTEGRATION AND SUSTAINABILITY BY PRIORITIZING COMMUNITY INTERVENTION TRAININGS WITH PROVIDERS EMBEDDED IN SCHOOLS, HEALTH SYSTEMS, CHILD WELFARE, AND HIGHER EDUCATION; AND ENSURES ACCOUNTABILITY AND CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT THROUGH EVALUATION, FIDELITY MONITORING, AND ITERATIVE QUALITY IMPROVEMENT CYCLES THAT MEASURE IMPACT AND REFINE TRAININGS AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE. BY COMBINING EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS, TARGETED ADAPTATIONS, ROBUST IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORTS, AND STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS, RENEWED HOPE WILL STRENGTHEN NATIONAL READINESS AND REDUCE THE LONG-TERM MENTAL HEALTH BURDEN OF DISASTERS ON CHILDREN, FAMILIES, AND THE SYSTEMS THAT SERVE THEM.

description: CENTER FOR ADVANCING YOUTH TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE AND SERVICES (CAYTICS) - THE CENTER FOR ADVANCING YOUTH TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE AND SERVICES (CAYTICS) AT NORTHWESTERN UNIVERSITY OFFERS NATIONAL EXPERTISE AND ADDRESSES CRITICAL SERVICE GAPS FOR OLDER YOUTH AND EMERGING ADULTS (AGES 16–25) INVOLVED IN CHILD WELFARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, AND JUVENILE JUSTICE SETTINGS WHO HAVE EXPERIENCED COMPLEX, DEVELOPMENTAL TRAUMA. CAYTICS WILL ADVANCE TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE FOR THIS POPULATION BY ESTABLISHING THE TRAUMA-INFORMED APPROACH FOR OLDER YOUTH (TIA-OY), AN EVIDENCE-INFORMED, TRAUMA TREATMENT MODEL AND SERVICE APPROACH ADAPTED FROM SAMHSA'S TRAUMA-INFORMED APPROACH. TIA-OY PROMOTES SAFETY, ENGAGEMENT, EMPOWERMENT, RESILIENCE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH RECOVERY, AND HEALTHY DEVELOPMENT THROUGH TRAUMA-INFORMED, STRENGTHS-BASED, AND PEER-SUPPORTED SERVICES. THROUGH TRAINING, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, ORGANIZATIONAL ASSESSMENT, IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT, AND RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT, CAYTICS WILL STRENGTHEN WORKFORCE CAPACITY, ORGANIZATIONAL READINESS, LEADERSHIP SUPPORTS, AND CROSS-SYSTEM COLLABORATION TO IMPROVE SERVICES AND OUTCOMES FOR OLDER YOUTH. OUR CAPACITY BUILDING EFFORTS WILL FOCUS ON PROVIDERS, SUPERVISORS, ORGANIZATIONAL LEADERS, AND YOUTH LEADERS AND WILL STRENGTHEN TRAUMA-INFORMED ORGANIZATIONAL AND SYSTEMS CAPACITY ACROSS CHILD WELFARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, JUVENILE JUSTICE, AND RELATED YOUTH-SERVING SETTINGS. INITIAL IMPLEMENTATION EFFORTS WILL FOCUS ON GEOGRAPHIC AREAS IN ILLINOIS, CALIFORNIA AND OTHER PARTNER SITES IN THE MIDWEST, SOUTHEAST, AND NORTHEAST, WHILE OUR DISSEMINATION AND CAPACITY-BUILDING ACTIVITIES WILL SUPPORT ADOPTION OF TRAUMA-INFORMED PRACTICES AND RESOURCES NATIONWIDE. THESE GEOGRAPHIC AREAS INCLUDE LARGE AND COMPLEX CHILD WELFARE, JUVENILE JUSTICE AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEMS AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS THAT PROVIDE AN OPPORTUNITY TO STRENGTHEN CAPACITY FOR TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE WITH A TARGETED FOCUS ON OLDER YOUTH AND EMERGING ADULTS. THE GOALS OF CAYTICS ARE TO: (1) ESTABLISH, IMPLEMENT, EVALUATE, AND REFINE THE TRAUMA-INFORMED APPROACH FOR OLDER YOUTH (TIA-OY); (2) INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF CHILD WELFARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, AND JUVENILE JUSTICE SETTINGS TO IMPLEMENT TRAUMA-INFORMED APPROACHES; (3) IMPROVE TRAUMA-INFORMED SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, ENGAGEMENT, REFERRAL PATHWAYS, AND SERVICE COORDINATION FOR OLDER YOUTH; AND (4) INCREASE NATIONAL AWARENESS OF THE MENTAL HEALTH, TRAUMA, AND SERVICE NEEDS OF OLDER YOUTH IMPACTED BY COMPLEX, DEVELOPMENTAL TRAUMA. TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS, CAYTICS WILL DEVELOP, ADAPT, IMPLEMENT, AND DISSEMINATE NCTSN TRAUMA-INFORMED PRACTICES AND SERVICE RESOURCES, INCLUDING THINK TRAUMA, THE CHILD WELFARE TRAUMA TRAINING TOOLKIT (CWTTT), THE TRAUMA-INFORMED ORGANIZATIONAL ASSESSMENT (TIOA), AND THE TAY/OLDER YOUTH TRAINING TOOLKIT. WE WILL ALSO DEVELOP, ADAPT AND DISSEMINATE RESOURCES ON TRAUMA-INFORMED SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT, TRAUMA-INFORMED LEADERSHIP, AND YOUTH- AND PEER-LED ENGAGEMENT RESOURCES AND WIDELY DISSEMINATE MENTAL HEALTH PUBLIC AWARENESS RESOURCES TO SUPPORT WIDESPREAD EDUCATION ON COMPLEX, DEVELOPMENTAL TRAUMA AND SPECIFIC NEEDS RELATED TO OLDER YOUTH (E.G., MENTAL HEALTH, SUBSTANCE USE, IMPROVING ACCESS TO SERVICES). BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, CAYTICS WILL IMPLEMENT AND EVALUATE TIA-OY ACROSS NUMEROUS ORGANIZATIONS, SUPPORT TRAUMA-INFORMED ORGANIZATIONAL CHANGES ACROSS CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS AND OFFER TRAINING AND IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT TO THOUSANDS OF PROVIDERS ACROSS THE COUNTRY. ADDITIONALLY, THROUGH OUR WIDESPREAD DISSEMINATION OF PUBLIC AWARENESS RESOURCES, WE EXPECT TO EXTEND OUR REACH TO OVER 10,000 PROVIDERS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS. OUR ACTIVITIES WILL ALL EMPHASIZE THE USE OF INNOVATIVE DISSEMINATION AND IMPLEMENTATION EFFORTS; PARTNERSHIP AND COLLABORATION WITH YOUTH, FAMILIES AND SERVICE PROVIDERS TO ADVANCE SYSTEMS CHANGE; USE OF A CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT FOCUS TO TRANSLATE FEEDBACK IMMEDIATELY INTO PRACTICE; AND CATALYZING ACTION THROUGH WIDESPREAD DISSEMINATION AND AWARENESS-RAISING ACTIVITIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

description: TRAUMA AND RELATED ADVERSITIES, COMORBIDITY, AND EVIDENCE-BASED CARE (TRACE) - THE TRACE (TRAUMA AND RELATED ADVERSITIES, COMORBIDITY, AND EVIDENCE-BASED CARE) INITIATIVE WILL STRENGTHEN THE NCTSN'S CAPACITY TO PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE CARE FOR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY TRAUMA AND CO-OCCURRING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES. THROUGH NATIONWIDE TRAINING, IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT, AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, TRACE ADDRESSES A NATIONAL WORKFORCE AND IMPLEMENTATION GAP BY EXPANDING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENTS (EBTS) THAT ADDRESS ANXIETY, DEPRESSION, DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOR, AND OTHER CONCERNS THAT COMMONLY CO-OCCUR WITH TRAUMATIC STRESS. TRACE WILL SERVE NCTSN CATEGORY III SITES AND AFFILIATED PROVIDERS NATIONWIDE. THE PROJECT WILL BUILD WORKFORCE CAPACITY, STRENGTHEN ORGANIZATIONAL IMPLEMENTATION, AND IMPROVE OUTCOMES ACROSS CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS FOR YOUTH AGES 2-17 EXPERIENCING TRAUMATIC STRESS AND COMORBID BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES AND THEIR CAREGIVERS.  TRACE WILL TRAIN PARTICIPATING AGENCIES IN TWO COMPLEMENTARY TRAUMA-INFORMED EBTS, THE MODULAR APPROACH TO THERAPY FOR CHILDREN (MATCH) AND PARENT CHILD INTERACTION THERAPY (PCIT). MATCH ADDRESSES ANXIETY, DEPRESSION, TRAUMATIC STRESS, AND DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOR AMONG YOUTH AGES 6-17, WHILE PCIT STRENGTHENS CAREGIVER-CHILD RELATIONSHIPS AND IMPROVES BEHAVIOR AMONG CHILDREN AGES 2-6. TOGETHER, THESE EBTS ADDRESS APPROXIMATELY 80% OF THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS THAT COMMONLY CO-OCCUR WITH TRAUMATIC STRESS. SPECIALIZED TRAINING ENHANCEMENTS WILL FOCUS ON PARENTAL SUBSTANCE MISUSE, PRENATAL SUBSTANCE EXPOSURE, YOUTH SUBSTANCE USE, AND SERVICE COORDINATION ACROSS CHILD WELFARE AND JUVENILE JUSTICE SYSTEMS. CAPACITY-BUILDING ACTIVITIES WILL TARGET CLINICIANS, SUPERVISORS, ORGANIZATIONAL LEADERS, AND PROFESSIONALS WORKING IN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, CHILD WELFARE, AND JUVENILE JUSTICE SETTINGS. THE GOALS OF TRACE ARE TO: 1) EXPAND ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE FOR YOUTH AND FAMILIES EXPERIENCING TRAUMATIC STRESS AND CO-OCCURRING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES; 2) BUILD AGENCY CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT AND SUSTAIN TRAUMA-INFORMED EBTS WITH FIDELITY, CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND DATA-DRIVEN DECISION-MAKING; 3) STRENGTHEN THE MENTAL HEALTH WORKFORCE BY IMPROVING CLINICIAN KNOWLEDGE, ATTITUDES, AND SKILLS TO DELIVER EBTS THAT TREAT TRAUMATIC STRESS AND COMORBIDITIES; AND 4) EXPAND NCTSN PARTNER CAPACITY TO ADDRESS CHALLENGES RELATED TO SUBSTANCE USE AND SYSTEMS INVOLVEMENT. PROJECT OBJECTIVES INCLUDE INCREASING CLINICIAN KNOWLEDGE OF TRAUMA-INFORMED EBTS BY 50%, ACHIEVING EBT CERTIFICATION AMONG AT LEAST 60% OF TRAINED CLINICIANS, AND ENSURING THAT 90% OF PARTICIPATING AGENCIES IMPLEMENT ONGOING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROCESSES. YOUTH ARE EXPECTED TO DEMONSTRATE SIGNIFICANT REDUCTIONS IN TRAUMA-RELATED, INTERNALIZING, AND EXTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS AND IMPROVEMENTS IN FUNCTIONING.  OVER FIVE YEARS, TRACE WILL IMPLEMENT FOUR ENHANCED LEARNING COLLABORATIVES (TWO MATCH AND TWO PCIT COHORTS) THAT COMBINE TRAINING, CONSULTATION, QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT, AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING. TRACE WILL TRAIN AN ESTIMATED 104 PROVIDERS ACROSS 24 AGENCIES IN MATCH AND PCIT AND ESTABLISH LOCAL TRAINING CAPACITY THROUGH TRAIN-THE-TRAINER STRATEGIES THAT WILL TRAIN 380 MATCH CLINICIANS AND 120 PCIT CLINICIANS BY THE END OF THE INITIATIVE. PARTICIPATING AGENCIES ARE EXPECTED TO PROVIDE TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICES TO MORE THAN 2,800 YOUTH ANNUALLY AND APPROXIMATELY 14,000 YOUTH DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD. TRAINING ENHANCEMENTS AND RESOURCES WILL BE DISSEMINATED WIDELY TO FAMILIES, CLINICIANS, AND PROVIDERS ACROSS CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS, REACHING AN ESTIMATED 1500 PROVIDERS BY THE END OF THE PROJECT. CONSISTENT WITH SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES, TRACE WILL EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, STRENGTHEN THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE, PROMOTE PERSON-CENTERED AND FAMILY-DRIVEN CARE, AND IMPROVE OUTCOMES FOR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY TRAUMA AND SUBSTANCE USE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: NEXTGEN CENTER FOR ADOLESCENT RESILIENCE AND EMPOWERMENT - THE NEXTGEN CENTER FOR ADOLESCENT RESILIENCE AND EMPOWERMENT (CARE) AT THE UNIVERSITY OF DENVER WILL SERVE AS A NATIONAL TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION CENTER FOR NEXTGEN RESILIENCE: EMPOWERED AND EQUIPPED FOR THE FUTURE, AN EVIDENCE-INFORMED MODEL THAT PROMOTES HEALING FROM CHILDHOOD TRAUMA AND BUILDS RESILIENCE AMONG ADOLESCENTS AND THEIR CAREGIVERS IN THE CONTEXT OF CONTEMPORARY RISKS. NEXTGEN CARE WILL REFINE THE MODEL, STRENGTHEN ITS EVIDENCE BASE, AND DEVELOP THE TRAINING, PRODUCTS, AND INFRASTRUCTURE TO SUPPORT HIGH-FIDELITY IMPLEMENTATION AT CHILD-SERVING SITES ACROSS THE NATION. THE CENTER IS A PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN THE UNIVERSITY OF DENVER'S BUTLER INSTITUTE FOR FAMILIES AND THE KEMPE CENTER, AN NCTSN-AFFILIATED ACADEMIC CENTER ADVANCING CLINICAL TREATMENT FOR CHILD TRAUMATIC STRESS.   ADOLESCENTS WHO EXPERIENCE TRAUMA TODAY FACE RISKS UNLIKE THOSE OF PRIOR GENERATIONS. TRAUMA-EXPOSED YOUTH ARE MORE LIKELY TO FEEL LONELY, DISCONNECTED, AND WITHOUT A SENSE OF HOPE OR PURPOSE. THESE SYMPTOMS, WHICH HEIGHTEN VULNERABILITY TO ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION, ALSO RAISE THE RISK OF POOR PHYSICAL HEALTH, SUBSTANCE AND PROCESS USE DISORDERS (ADDICTIVE BEHAVIORS), AND INCREASE SUSCEPTIBILITY TO THE NEGATIVE EFFECTS OF EXCESS SCREEN TIME, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE CHATBOTS, AND SOCIAL MEDIA. CURRENT TRAUMA TREATMENT MODELS DO NOT ADEQUATELY EQUIP YOUTH TO BUILD RESILIENCE AGAINST THESE CONTEMPORARY RISKS. NEXTGEN FILLS THIS GAP BY ADDRESSING THE UNDERLYING DRIVERS OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISORDERS: CONNECTION, HEALTHY BOUNDARIES, PHYSICAL HEALTH AND WELL-BEING (EQUIPPING YOUTH FOR THEIR FUTURE), AND A STRENGTHENED INTERNAL LOCUS OF CONTROL (EMPOWERING YOUTH TO TAKE CHARGE OF THEIR FUTURE). THESE SKILLS PROMOTE HEALING FROM TRAUMA AND PROTECT AGAINST FUTURE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISORDERS.   THE POPULATION OF FOCUS WHO ARE THE PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES OF THE CENTER'S CAPACITY-BUILDING ARE THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, EDUCATION, JUVENILE JUSTICE, CHILD WELFARE, AND SUBSTANCE USE WORKFORCE AND THE SYSTEMS THAT SUPPORT TRAUMA-EXPOSED ADOLESCENTS NATIONALLY. NEXTGEN CARE WILL REACH THESE SYSTEMS THROUGH A NATIONAL NETWORK OF NCTSN SITES AND FEDERALLY FUNDED TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PARTNERS, WHILE ALSO SERVING ADOLESCENTS AND CAREGIVERS AT A PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION SITE IN COLORADO SPRINGS, COLORADO. THE CENTER WILL ADDRESS TWO NEEDS: A GAP IN TRAUMA TREATMENT MODELS THAT BUILD RESILIENCE AGAINST CONTEMPORARY RISKS, AND LIMITED WORKFORCE CAPACITY TO DELIVER MODELS WITH FIDELITY AND EFFECTIVE IMPLEMENTATION CONTEXT. AT THE PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION SITE, WE WILL DELIVER NEXTGEN TO YOUTH AGES 12-21 WHO HAVE EXPERIENCED TRAUMATIC STRESS AND ARE AT ELEVATED RISK FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISORDERS TO REFINE THE MODEL, BUILD ITS EVIDENCE BASE, AND SUPPORT NATIONAL CAPACITY-BUILDING.   TO BUILD NATIONAL CAPACITY, THE CENTER WILL PURSUE FIVE GOALS: (1) REFINE THE NEXTGEN RESILIENCE MODEL AND BUILD ITS EVIDENCE BASE THROUGH RIGOROUS PRE-/POST- AND FOLLOW-UP EVALUATION; (2) DEVELOP NEXTGEN PRODUCTS AND INFRASTRUCTURE FOR NATIONAL DISSEMINATION, INCLUDING MANUALIZED GUIDES, PSYCHOEDUCATIONAL VIDEOS, AN IMPLEMENTATION TOOLKIT, PARTICIPANT MATERIALS, AND A WEBSITE; (3) BUILD WORKFORCE CAPACITY BY TRAINING 30 NEW NEXTGEN FACILITATORS ACROSS THE NATION AND DELIVERING THE NCTSN CORE CURRICULUM ON CHILD TRAUMA AND RELATED TRAININGS TO AT LEAST 1,000 PROVIDERS AND EDUCATORS; (4) DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE PRODUCTS AND COLLABORATE ACROSS NCTSI CATEGORY I-III AND OTHER FEDERAL PARTNERS; AND (5) ENGAGE YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND PROVIDERS IN CONTINUOUS MODEL IMPROVEMENT. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES THAT ADVANCE SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES INCLUDE IMPROVING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-INFORMED TREATMENT, PREVENTING SERIOUS BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISORDERS, USING GOLD-STANDARD SCIENCE, ENGAGING AND EMPOWERING FAMILIES, ADDRESSING EMERGING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH THREATS, AND SUPPORTING THE MAKE AMERICA HEALTHY AGAIN PRIORITIES BY ADDRESSING ROOT CAUSES AND PREVENTING LONG-TERM PHYSICAL AND MENTAL HEALTH PROBLEMS.

description: NATIONAL CENTER FOR TRAUMA-INFORMED PARENTING AND FAMILY INTERVENTIONS - THE NATIONAL CENTER FOR TRAUMA-INFORMED PARENTING AND FAMILY INTERVENTIONS WILL STRENGTHEN NATIONAL CAPACITY TO DELIVER TRAUMA-INFORMED, EVIDENCE-BASED PARENTING AND FAMILY INTERVENTIONS FOR CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS AFFECTED BY TRAUMA. LED BY THE CENTER FOR RESILIENCE AND WELL-BEING AT THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO BOULDER, THIS CATEGORY II NCTSI TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION CENTER WILL EQUIP PROVIDERS, ORGANIZATIONS, AND CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES WITH TRAINING, TOOLS, AND IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT TO IMPROVE CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT AND EXPAND ACCESS TO EFFECTIVE FAMILY-CENTERED TRAUMA INTERVENTIONS. THROUGH NATIONAL TRAINING, CONSULTATION, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, INTERVENTION ADAPTATION, WEB-BASED LEARNING, AND DISSEMINATION, THE CENTER WILL HELP CHILDREN AND FAMILIES ACCESS SUPPORT EARLIER, STAY ENGAGED IN CARE, AND BUILD THE RELATIONSHIPS AND SKILLS THAT PROMOTE RECOVERY AND RESILIENCE. THE CENTER WILL SERVE TRAUMA-EXPOSED CHILDREN AND YOUTH AGES 3-18 AND THEIR CAREGIVERS ACROSS CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS NATIONWIDE, WITH A SPECIALIZED FOCUS ON STRENGTHENING TRAUMA-INFORMED PARENTING AND IMPROVING PROVIDER CAPACITY TO ENGAGE, SUPPORT, AND PARTNER WITH PARENTS IN TRAUMA-INFORMED EVIDENCE-BASED CARE. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES TWO SIGNIFICANT NATIONAL GAPS: LIMITED ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED PARENTING AND FAMILY INTERVENTIONS FOR TRAUMA-EXPOSED CHILDREN AND FAMILIES, AND PROVIDERS LACK OF TRAINING AND STRATEGIES TO EFFECTIVELY ENGAGE CAREGIVERS IN THESE INTERVENTIONS. CAPACITY-BUILDING EFFORTS WILL TARGET COMMUNITY MENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS, CHILD WELFARE AND FAMILY PRESERVATION SERVICES, AND OTHER FAMILY SUPPORT SETTINGS. CENTER ACTIVITIES WILL DIRECTLY BENEFIT CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS NATIONWIDE BY RAISING THE STANDARD OF CARE FOR TRAUMA-INFORMED, EVIDENCE-BASED PARENTING AND TRAUMA INTERVENTIONS AND STRENGTHENING PROVIDERS' ABILITY TO ENGAGE AND SUPPORT CAREGIVERS IN TREATMENT.   THE CENTER WILL PROVIDE TRAINING, CONSULTATION, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT IN FOUR TRAUMA-INFORMED EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES: LET’S CONNECT® (LC), BREAKTHROUGH PARENTING CURRICULUM: NAVIGATING TRAUMA ACROSS GENERATIONS (BPC), TRAUMA-FOCUSED COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (TF-CBT), AND ALTERNATIVES FOR FAMILIES: A COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (AF-CBT). IT WILL ALSO DEVELOP WEB-BASED LC AND BPC TRAINING COURSES, CREATE AND PILOT A CHILD WELFARE ADAPTATION OF LC, AND DEVELOP PARENT ENGAGEMENT TOOLS TO STRENGTHEN PROVIDER CONFIDENCE AND FAMILY PARTICIPATION IN TI-EBPS. ALL PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL BE GUIDED BY A MULTIDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATIVE PLANNING TEAM, INCLUDING YOUTH AND PARENT CONSULTANTS, INTERVENTION DEVELOPERS, CHILD WELFARE LEADERS, COMMUNITY PROVIDERS, AND IMPLEMENTATION PARTNERS. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) ESTABLISH THE INFRASTRUCTURE FOR A CATEGORY II NCTSI TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION CENTER FOCUSED ON TRAUMA-INFORMED PARENTING AND FAMILY INTERVENTIONS; (2) INCREASE ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED, EVIDENCE-BASED PARENTING AND FAMILY INTERVENTIONS THROUGH PROVIDER TRAINING, CONSULTATION, AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE; AND (3) DEVELOP, PILOT, AND REFINE TOOLS AND RESOURCES TO ENGAGE, SERVE, AND SUPPORT PARENTS OF TRAUMA-IMPACTED CHILDREN. BY PROJECT END, THE CENTER WILL TRAIN 500 PROVIDERS IN LC, 150 FACILITATORS IN BPC, 1,200 PROVIDERS IN TF-CBT, AND 300 PROVIDERS IN AF-CBT; 30 TRAINERS WILL COMPLETE THE TRAIN-THE-TRAINER PROGRAMS; 600 PROVIDERS WILL COMPLETE THE WEB-BASED LC AND BPC TRAINING COURSES. IN ADDITION, THE CENTER WILL DEVELOP, PILOT, AND DISSEMINATE A CHILD WELFARE ADAPTATION OF LC AS WELL A PARENT ENGAGEMENT TOOLKIT. THE TSA CENTER WILL REACH AT LEAST 10,000 UNIQUE INDIVIDUALS AND 300 ORGANIZATIONS THROUGH NATIONAL DISSEMINATION. THESE ACTIVITIES WILL ADVANCE SAMHSA PRIORITIES BY EXPANDING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TREATMENT, STRENGTHENING PREVENTION AND EARLY INTERVENTION, SUPPORTING WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AND IMPROVING OUTCOMES FOR TRAUMA-EXPOSED CHILDREN AND FAMILIES.
