description: CHILD ADVOCACY TRAINING AND SUPPORT CENTER (CATS) - THE CHILD ADVOCACY TRAINING AND SUPPORT (CATS) CENTER, HOUSED AT BAYSTATE FAMILY ADVOCACY CENTER (BFAC) WILL OPERATE AS A SAMHSA NCTSI CATEGORY II NATIONAL TREATMENT AND SERVICE ADAPTATION (TSA) CENTER SPECIALIZING IN CHILD ABUSE AND MALTREATMENT WITHIN CHILDREN'S ADVOCACY CENTER (CAC) SYSTEMS. THE CATS CENTER TEAM, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH NATIONAL EXPERTS ON CAC SERVICE DELIVERY, EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT (EBT) TRAUMA CURRICULUM DEVELOPERS, NCTSI CAT II AND CAT III SITES, AND STAKEHOLDERS REPRESENTING EACH MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM (MDT) DISCIPLINE, WILL IMPLEMENT COMPREHENSIVE, COORDINATED CAPACITY-BUILDING EFFORTS FOCUSED ON STRENGTHENING WORKFORCE CAPACITY ACROSS THE 900 MEMBER NATIONAL CAC NETWORK THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED TRAINING, CONSULTATION, AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAMS, WHILE EXPANDING ACCESS TO GOLD-STANDARD TRAUMA TREATMENTS FOR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY ABUSE. THE PRIMARY POPULATION OF FOCUS IS CHILDREN AGES 2-18 SERVED THROUGH CAC SYSTEMS WHO HAVE EXPERIENCED SEXUAL ABUSE, PHYSICAL ABUSE, NEGLECT, COMMERCIAL SEXUAL EXPLOITATION AND TRAFFICKING (CSET), EXPOSURE TO VIOLENCE, AND DRUG ENDANGERMENT, WITH PRIORITY FOCUS ON CSET-INVOLVED YOUTH AND THOSE WITH COMPLEX TRAUMA. CAC MDT MEMBERS; MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, FORENSIC INTERVIEWERS, MEDICAL PROFESSIONALS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, CHILD WELFARE PERSONNEL, AND VICTIM ADVOCATES; ARE THE DIRECT RECIPIENTS OF CAPACITY-BUILDING SUPPORTS. THE CATS CENTER WILL BUILD SUSTAINABLE NATIONAL WORKFORCE CAPACITY ACROSS THE UNITED STATES IN THE FOLLOWING WAYS: 1) ESTABLISH AND SCALE A NATIONAL TTA INFRASTRUCTURE TO STRENGTHEN CAC SERVICE DELIVERY THROUGH BROADENED STAKEHOLDER LEADERSHIP, CONTINUOUS EVALUATION, AND STRATEGIC DISSEMINATION, ENSURING MDT MEMBERS ARE TRAUMA-INFORMED AND HAVE THE SPECIALIZED TOOLS, SKILLS, AND RESOURCES FOR EFFECTIVE SERVICE DELIVERY TO CHILDREN AND FAMILIES IMPACTED BY CHILD ABUSE. 2) REFINE AND ADAPT EVIDENCE-BASED CHILDHOOD TRAUMA TRAINING CURRICULA, INCLUDING TRAUMA-FOCUSED COGNITIVE-BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (TF-CBT), THE CORE CURRICULUM ON CHILDHOOD TRAUMA (CCCT), AND THE FOUNDATIONS FOR OUTREACH THROUGH EXPERIENTIAL CHILD ADVOCACY STUDIES TRAINING (FORECAST) SIMULATION MODEL TO MEET THE NEEDS OF CAC MDTS AND PRIORITY POPULATIONS. 3) DELIVER TRAUMA-INFORMED TREATMENT AND SERVICE RESOURCES THROUGH TARGETED DISSEMINATION OF EVIDENCE-BASED MDT TRAINING, CONSULTATION, AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO NCTSI CATEGORY II–III GRANTEES AND CAC SERVICE PROVIDERS NATIONALLY THROUGH THE INTENSIVE LEARNING COMMUNITY (ILC) MODEL. 4) BUILD LOCALIZED, SUSTAINABLE TIC TRAINING CAPACITY WITHIN CAC SYSTEMS THROUGH A TRAIN-THE-FACILITATOR (TTF) MODEL, CERTIFYING REGIONAL CAC STAFF TO INDEPENDENTLY DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED CURRICULA. 5) IMPLEMENT A RIGOROUS, DATA-DRIVEN EVALUATION PLAN TO CONTINUOUSLY ASSESS INTERVENTION EFFECTIVENESS, FIDELITY, AND CHILD HEALTH OUTCOMES, USING FINDINGS TO DRIVE CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT ACROSS ALL PROJECT ACTIVITIES. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: TRAINING A MINIMUM OF 1,000 MDT PROFESSIONALS PER YEAR AND 300 MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS IN TF-CBT ANNUALLY; INCLUDING HOSTING 2 REGIONAL ILCS PER YEAR EACH SERVING FULL CAC MDTS; ACHIEVING 90% OF ILC PARTICIPANTS REPORTING INTENT TO IMPLEMENT TRAUMA-INFORMED PRACTICE CHANGES; OFFERING FIVE DISCIPLINE-SPECIFIC VIRTUAL TRAININGS PER YEAR TO ADDRESS TRAUMA-INFORMED AND TRAUMA-SPECIFIC PRACTICES FOR EACH MDT AFFINITY GROUP (LAW ENFORCEMENT, CHILD WELFARE, MEDICAL, VICTIM ADVOCACY, MENTAL HEALTH), INCLUDING PROMOTION OF TIMELY ACCESS TO TRAUMA TREATMENT; CONDUCTING INDIVIDUAL CCCT AND FORECAST TRAINING FOR CHILD WELFARE TEAMS AND OTHER DISCIPLINES LOOKING TO DEEPEN THEIR UNDERSTANDING OF TRAUMA-INFORMED PRACTICE; CERTIFYING 4 NEW TTF FACILITATORS ANNUALLY; AND SUBMITTING THE EVALUATION PLAN WITHIN 3 MONTHS, WORKFORCE PLAN WITHIN 3 MONTHS, AND DISSEMINATION PLAN WITHIN 6 MONTHS OF AWARD, EACH UPDATED ANNUALLY.

recipient.name: THE NC YOUTH VIOLENCE PREVENTION CENTER

description: RURAL TRAUMA TREATMENT IMPLEMENTATION AND ADAPTATION CENTER - THE NORTH CAROLINA YOUTH VIOLENCE PREVENTION CENTER (NC-YVPC) WILL ESTABLISH THE RURAL TRAUMA TREATMENT IMPLEMENTATION AND ADAPTATION CENTER TO EXPAND RURAL ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED CHILD TRAUMA TREATMENT. THE CENTER WILL DISSEMINATE VIRTUAL TRAINING, CONSULTATION, FIDELITY, AND IMPLEMENTATION TOOLS FOR TF-CBT, BOUNCE BACK, TRAUMA NARRATIVE WORK, AND TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICES. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN RURAL CLINICIANS AND AGENCIES FACING GEOGRAPHIC ISOLATION, WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, LIMITED SUPERVISION, AND IMPLEMENTATION BARRIERS.  THE GRANT WILL REACH RURAL, FRONTIER, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE-SHORTAGE COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE UNITED STATES, WITH RURAL SOUTHEASTERN NORTH CAROLINA SERVING AS A FIELD LABORATORY FOR DEVELOPMENT, TESTING, FEEDBACK, AND CQI. RURAL COMMUNITIES EXPERIENCE HIGH CHILD TRAUMA, VIOLENCE EXPOSURE, POVERTY, FAMILY ADVERSITY, CHILD WELFARE INVOLVEMENT, JUVENILE JUSTICE CONTACT, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEED, WHILE MANY LACK CLINICIANS TRAINED TO DELIVER TRAUMA TREATMENT WITH FIDELITY. RURAL PROVIDERS OFTEN WORK IN SMALL AGENCIES WITH HIGH TURNOVER, LIMITED SUPERVISION, FEW CONSULTATION RESOURCES, AND LIMITED ADVANCED TRAINING IN TRAUMA NARRATIVES, CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT, AND COMPLETION.  THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS THE NATIONAL RURAL CHILD-SERVING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE: CLINICIANS, SUPERVISORS, SCHOOL MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, CAC CLINICIANS, COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH THERAPISTS, JUVENILE JUSTICE AND CHILD WELFARE PARTNERS, PEER AND FAMILY SUPPORT STAFF, AND AGENCY IMPLEMENTATION LEADERS. ULTIMATE BENEFICIARIES ARE RURAL CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND FAMILIES NEEDING TRAUMA SERVICES. WHEN SITES SUPPORT DIRECT SERVICES, THE PLANNED POPULATION WILL GENERALLY INCLUDE AGES 5-18 WITH TRAUMA EXPOSURE AND NEEDS SUCH AS POSTTRAUMATIC STRESS, ANXIETY, DEPRESSION, GRIEF, DYSREGULATION, SCHOOL IMPAIRMENT, BEHAVIOR PROBLEMS, CAREGIVER STRESS, AND SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT.  NC-YVPC WILL IMPLEMENT FIVE STRATEGIES: (1) DEVELOP A RURAL TF-CBT AND BOUNCE BACK IMPLEMENTATION TOOLKIT WITH READINESS, REFERRAL, CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT, FIDELITY, AND SUSTAINABILITY RESOURCES; (2) CREATE A TRAUMA NARRATIVE TRAINING AND FIDELITY TOOLKIT TO HELP CLINICIANS INTRODUCE, PACE, PROCESS, AND COMPLETE NARRATIVE WORK SAFELY AND WITH FIDELITY; (3) LAUNCH A VIRTUAL TRAINING ACADEMY WITH MODULES, WEBINARS, LEARNING COLLABORATIVES, OFFICE HOURS, SUPERVISOR RESOURCES, AND COACHING; (4) INTEGRATE PAINT PARTY AND SEE-IT THEATER PRODUCTS FOR OUTREACH, STIGMA REDUCTION, PSYCHOEDUCATION, SKILL REHEARSAL, CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT, AND YOUTH READINESS WITHOUT REPLACING EBP ELEMENTS; AND (5) DEVELOP SUPERVISED VIRTUAL AND AI-ASSISTED SUPPORTS, INCLUDING ROLE PLAYS, MOCK CASES, PRACTICE SCENARIOS, PROMPTS, FIDELITY DECISION TREES, AND CQI DASHBOARDS.  PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) ADAPT AND DISSEMINATE RURAL IMPLEMENTATION TOOLS FOR TF-CBT AND BOUNCE BACK; (2) STRENGTHEN RURAL WORKFORCE CAPACITY IN TRAUMA NARRATIVE READINESS, PACING, FIDELITY, CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT, AND COMPLETION; (3) EXPAND SCALABLE VIRTUAL TRAINING, CONSULTATION, AND SUPPORTS THAT REDUCE GEOGRAPHIC BARRIERS; AND (4) EVALUATE IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY, FIDELITY, REACH, ACCEPTABILITY, FEASIBILITY, AND SUSTAINABILITY THROUGH DATA-DRIVEN CQI ALIGNED WITH SAMHSA STRATEGIC PRIORITIES.  OBJECTIVES ARE TO COMPLETE A NATIONAL RURAL IMPLEMENTATION NEEDS SCAN, CONVENE ADVISORY GROUPS, LAUNCH THE ACADEMY, AND PRODUCE INITIAL TOOLKITS BY THE END OF YEAR 1; TRAIN AT LEAST 1,500 RURAL PROVIDERS OVER FIVE YEARS; PROVIDE CONSULTATION TO AT LEAST 40 RURAL ORGANIZATIONS/TEAMS; DISSEMINATE AT LEAST 12 PRODUCTS, CURRICULA, TOOLS, OR TRAINING RESOURCES; REACH AT LEAST 25,000 PROVIDERS, FAMILIES, OR COMMUNITY MEMBERS; DEMONSTRATE PRE/POST GAINS IN PROVIDER KNOWLEDGE, CONFIDENCE, READINESS, AND NARRATIVE COMPETENCE; AND USE QUARTERLY CQI REVIEWS TO REFINE TOOLS, STRENGTHEN FIDELITY, IMPROVE USABILITY, AND SUPPORT SUSTAINMENT.

description: PROJECT BRIDGE - PROJECT BRIDGE (BUILDING RECOVERY THROUGH TRAUMA-INFORMED DETECTION, GUIDANCE, AND EARLY INTERVENTION) WILL 1) IMPROVE CHILD-SERVING STAFF'S CAPACITY FOR EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF CHILDREN SUFFERING FROM TRAUMATIC STRESS AND 2) DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE A VERY BRIEF EVIDENCE-INFORMED TRAUMA INTERVENTION INTENDED FOR ANY YOUTH AGE 6-17 EXPERIENCING TRAUMATIC STRESS ACROSS A RANGE OF SETTINGS IN THE UNITED STATES WHERE TRADITIONAL, LONG-TERM EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENTS (EBTS) ARE NOT FEASIBLE OR AVAILABLE. DESPITE HIGH RATES OF TRAUMA EXPOSURE AND THE INCREASING AVAILABILITY OF TRAUMA-FOCUSED EBTS, MANY CHILDREN EXPERIENCING TRAUMATIC STRESS ARE NOT IDENTIFIED AND DO NOT RECEIVE APPROPRIATE CARE. ACROSS CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS, INCLUDING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, HEALTH CARE, EDUCATION, CHILD WELFARE, AND JUVENILE JUSTICE, ROUTINE TRAUMA SCREENING REMAINS INCONSISTENT AND PROVIDERS OFTEN LACK PRACTICAL OPTIONS TO SUPPORT YOUTH WHEN LONGER-TERM TRAUMA-FOCUSED EBTS ARE UNAVAILABLE, INACCESSIBLE, OR IMPRACTICAL. WORKFORCE LIMITATIONS, TIME CONSTRAINTS, AND BARRIERS TO TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT FURTHER CONTRIBUTE TO GAPS IN CARE. BRIDGE WILL ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES BY BUILDING CAPACITY FOR TRAUMA SCREENING AND DISSEMINATING AN EVIDENCE-INFORMED BRIEF INTERVENTION MODEL THAT CAN PROVIDE TIMELY SUPPORT AND FACILITATE CONNECTION TO LONGER-TERM TRAUMA-FOCUSED EBTS WHEN NEEDED.  BRIDGE HAS THREE MAIN GOALS. FIRST, IT WILL IMPROVE CHILD-SERVING PROFESSIONALS’ CAPACITY TO CONDUCT TRAUMA SCREENING THROUGH TRAININGS IN TRAUMA SCREENING BEST PRACTICES. THIS WILL BE DONE THROUGH UPDATES TO ONLINE COURSES ON TRAUMA SCREENING BEST PRACTICES; BY EXPANDING TRAUMA SCREENING RESOURCES TO ADDRESS POPULATIONS AND CONTEXTS IN WHICH GUIDANCE IS LIMITED, WITH AN INITIAL FOCUS ON DEVELOPING AN ONLINE COURSE FOCUSED ON CHILDREN WITH INTELLECTUAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES; AND THROUGH IN-PERSON AND VIRTUAL TRAININGS. THESE ACTIVITIES WILL RESULT IN AT LEAST 1,500 CHILD-SERVING STAFF BEING TRAINED, 5,000 CHILDREN BEING SCREENED FOR TRAUMA, AND 1,000 CHILDREN RECEIVING EBTS AS A RESULT. SECOND, BRIDGE WILL FOCUS ON DEVELOPING, DISSEMINATING, AND SUSTAINING A BRIEF INTERVENTION MODEL TO SUPPORT CHILDREN, ENTITLED BRIEF TRAUMA INTERVENTION (BTI). THIS WILL INCLUDE DEVELOPING TRAINING CURRICULA, PRACTICE MANUALS, IMPLEMENTATION RESOURCES, AND AN ONLINE COURSE. FOLLOWING THIS, BTI WILL BE DISSEMINATED THROUGH FOUR LEARNING COMMUNITIES AND A TRAIN-THE-TRAINER WITH NCTSN AND OTHER CHILD-SERVING SITES. BY THE END OF THE GRANT, AT LEAST 500 STAFF WILL BE TRAINED IN BTI AND AT LEAST 2,000 CHILDREN WILL BE SERVED ACROSS SETTINGS.  THIRD, BRIDGE WILL FOCUS ON ENSURING ALL ACTIVITIES REPRESENT AND SUPPORT CHILD, YOUTH, AND CAREGIVER PRIORITIES. YOUTH AND CAREGIVERS WILL COMPRISE AT LEAST 33% OF A MULTIDISCIPLINARY ADVISORY BOARD AND WILL PARTICIPATE IN FOCUS GROUPS AND CO-DEVELOPMENT OF TRAINING CONTENT. IN PARTNERSHIP WITH NATIONAL EXPERTS FROM THE NCTSN AND REPRESENTATIVES FROM STATE AGENCIES, OUTPATIENT SETTINGS, AND OTHER CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS, THE ADVISORY BOARD WILL PROVIDE ONGOING GUIDANCE TO SUPPORT PROJECT PLANNING, IMPLEMENTATION, QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND DISSEMINATION.

description: CENTER FOR ADJUSTMENT, RESILIENCE &RECOVERY (CARRE) - OVER FIVE YEARS, CARRE WILL: (1) DELIVER 100 TRAININGS TO 5,000 PROVIDERS; 120 TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ENGAGEMENTS; AND 20 QUARTERLY RESOURCE PRODUCTS; (2) ADAPT CFTSI AND SPARCS-ST FOR CCD-AFFECTED POPULATIONS; IMPLEMENT PILOTS AT A MINIMUM OF FOUR SITES REACHING AT LEAST 130 FAMILIES; AND EVALUATE OUTCOMES WITH RIGOROUS FIDELITY MONITORING; AND (3) CONDUCT FIVE ANNUAL NEEDS ASSESSMENTS, ENGAGE SIX LIVED-EXPERIENCE CONTENT VALIDATORS, ESTABLISH A 12-MEMBER ADVISORY COMMITTEE, AND BUILD 25+ PARTNERSHIPS ACROSS NCTSI CENTERS, CBOS, AND SAMHSA-FUNDED TA CENTERS.   NEARLY HALF OF ALL U.S. CHILDREN EXPERIENCE AT LEAST ONE TRAUMATIC EVENT, AND CHILDREN AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY CRISIS, CONFLICT, AND DISASTER (CCD) FACE COMPOUNDING EXPOSURES THAT EXISTING TREATMENT SYSTEMS ARE POORLY EQUIPPED TO ADDRESS — WITH PTSD PREVALENCE AMONG CCD-AFFECTED INDIVIDUALS ESTIMATED AS HIGH AS 47%. THREE INTERCONNECTED GAPS DEFINE THE NEED: EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENTS HAVE NOT BEEN SYSTEMATICALLY ADAPTED FOR CCD-AFFECTED POPULATIONS; EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS CANNOT SCALE WHEN DELIVERY IS LIMITED TO SCARCE, COSTLY LICENSED CLINICIANS; AND MANY AT-RISK FAMILIES NEED A PREVENTION-FOCUSED WORKFORCE TO REACH THEM BEFORE THEY CROSS CLINICAL THRESHOLDS.   CARRE’S AIM IS TO ENSURE THAT AMERICAN CITIZEN AND QUALIFIED ALIEN CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY CCD RECEIVE EVIDENCE-BASED, TRAUMA-FOCUSED TREATMENT AND SERVICES — DELIVERED ACROSS COMMUNITY, CLINICAL, AND CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS — TO PREVENT THE LONG-TERM IMPACTS OF CHILDHOOD TRAUMATIC STRESS. GROUNDED IN GOLD-STANDARD SCIENCE AND SAMHSA’S STRATEGIC PRIORITY OF IMPROVING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT, CARRE WILL ADAPT AND SCALE TWO NCTSN-RECOGNIZED EBTS THROUGH A PEER DELIVERY MODEL THAT REDUCES COST AND PROVIDER-DEGREE BARRIERS IN UNDER-RESOURCED COMMUNITIES. CARRE DIRECTLY ADVANCES SAMHSA’S PRIORITY OF IMPROVING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT BY EXPANDING NON-PHARMACOLOGICAL, ADAPTED INTERVENTIONS INTO COMMUNITY SETTINGS. ITS EARLY INTERVENTION MODEL INTERRUPTS THE DOCUMENTED PATHWAY FROM CHILDHOOD TRAUMATIC STRESS TO SUBSTANCE USE, ADDICTION, AND SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS — CONSISTENT WITH SAMHSA’S PREVENTION PRIORITIES AND MAHA’S GOALS OF REDUCING CHILDHOOD CHRONIC DISEASE.   CARRE CENTERS ON TWO COMPLEMENTARY, NON-PHARMACOLOGICAL EBTS. CFTSI (CHILD AND FAMILY TRAUMATIC STRESS INTERVENTION) CFTSI, A BRIEF EARLY INTERVENTION FOR CHILDREN AGES 3–18 AND THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND SPARCS-ST, A MODULAR GROUP TREATMENT FOR ADOLESCENTS AGES 12–21. SPARCS-ST (STRUCTURED PSYCHOTHERAPY FOR ADOLESCENTS RESPONDING TO CHRONIC STRESS – SKILLS TRAINING), A FLEXIBLE GROUP TREATMENT FOR ADOLESCENTS AGES 12–21. TOGETHER THEY FORM A CONTINUUM: CFTSI INTERVENES ACUTELY; SPARCS-ST ADDRESSES LONGER-TERM CHRONIC TRAUMATIC STRESS. CARRE WILL ADAPT BOTH EBTS FOR CCD-AFFECTED POPULATIONS AND DEVELOP PEER DELIVERY AND CO-FACILITATION MODELS FOR COMMUNITY, SCHOOL, AND CRISIS SETTINGS. ALL DIRECT SERVICES WILL BE PROVIDED TO AMERICAN CITIZENS AND QUALIFIED ALIENS IN COMPLIANCE WITH PRWORA.

description: THE TRAUMA AND GRIEF CENTER: BUILDING BEREAVEMENT-INFORMED CAPACITY ACROSS CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS - THE PROPOSED PROJECT, THE TRAUMA AND GRIEF CENTER: BUILDING BEREAVEMENT-INFORMED CAPACITY ACROSS CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS, WILL ESTABLISH THE TRAUMA AND GRIEF CENTER AS AN NCTSI CATEGORY II TSA CENTER FOCUSED ON CHILDHOOD BEREAVEMENT, TRAUMATIC AND AMBIGUOUS LOSS, AND ANTICIPATORY GRIEF. BEREAVEMENT IS ONE OF THE MOST COMMON AND DISTRESSING CHILDHOOD ADVERSITIES, WITH MORE THAN 6.6 MILLION U.S. CHILDREN GRIEVING THE DEATH OF A SIGNIFICANT PERSON. DESPITE ITS PREVALENCE, MANY SYSTEMS LACK SPECIALIZED SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, TREATMENT, AND IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORTS FOR THIS POPULATION. ANCHORED IN HOUSTON, THE TAG CENTER WILL LEVERAGE PARTNERSHIPS ACROSS TEXAS AND IN ARIZONA, CALIFORNIA, CONNECTICUT, GEORGIA, LOUISIANA, MICHIGAN, NEBRASKA, NORTH CAROLINA, AND PENNSYLVANIA TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS WHILE SERVING AS A NATIONAL RESOURCE. PROJECT STRATEGIES INCLUDE: (1) LEARNING COLLABORATIVES SUPPORTING DELIVERY OF THREE COMPLEMENTARY GRIEF-FOCUSED INTERVENTIONS: MULTIDIMENSIONAL GRIEF THERAPY (MGT), TRAUMA AND GRIEF COMPONENT THERAPY FOR ADOLESCENTS, AND PROMOTING ADAPTIVE GRIEF EXPERIENCES; (2) AN MGT CHAMPION TRAIN THE TRAINER PATHWAY; (3) ADAPTATION OF INTERVENTIONS FOR YOUTH EXPERIENCING AMBIGUOUS LOSS AND THOSE INVOLVED IN CHILD WELFARE AND JUVENILE JUSTICE; AND (4) DEVELOPMENT AND PILOT TESTING OF CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT AND TECHNOLOGY ENHANCED MGT RESOURCES. THIS PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF SCHOOLS, HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS, COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, CHILD WELFARE AGENCIES, AND JUVENILE JUSTICE SETTINGS TO SUPPORT YOUTH AFFECTED BY TRAUMA AND LOSS THROUGH ADAPTATION OF EVIDENCE-BASED AND EVIDENCE-INFORMED INTERVENTIONS, IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AND DISSEMINATION ACTIVITIES. BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, THE TAG CENTER WILL TRAIN APPROXIMATELY 1,300 CLINICIANS, ESTABLISH 10 CERTIFIED MGT TRAINERS, ACHIEVE AT LEAST 85% INCREASES IN TRAUMA  AND GRIEF INFORMED COMPETENCIES, AND STRENGTHEN ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY TO SERVE AN ESTIMATED 31,200 YOUTH.

description: THRIVE: TRAUMA-INFORMED HEALING, RECOVERY, INTERVENTION, AND VITALITY FOR EVERY YOUTH - PROJECT THRIVE (TRAUMA-INFORMED HEALING, RECOVERY, INTERVENTION, AND VITALITY FOR EVERY YOUTH), LED BY THE URBAN YOUTH TRAUMA CENTER (UYTC) AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS AT CHICAGO (UIC), WILL BUILD AND SUSTAIN TRAUMA-INFORMED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE CAPACITY BY PROVIDING SPECIALIZED TRAINING, CONSULTATION, AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO EXPAND EVIDENCE-BASED, INTEGRATED TREATMENT FOR YOUTH AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY TRAUMATIC STRESS, INTERPERSONAL VIOLENCE, AND CO-OCCURRING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES. IN CHICAGO - WHERE PERSISTENTLY HIGH RATES OF COMMUNITY VIOLENCE AND CRITICAL SHORTAGES OF TRAUMA-TRAINED PROVIDERS LEAVE THOUSANDS OF YOUTH WITHOUT ADEQUATE CARE - AND IN PARTNER CITIES NATIONWIDE, THRIVE WILL TRAIN  COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH CLINICIANS, SCHOOL-BASED COUNSELORS, JUVENILE JUSTICE STAFF, POLICE AND LAW ENFORCEMENT, SUBSTANCE USE PROVIDERS, COMMUNITY-BASED YOUTH WORKERS SERVING HIGH-NEED YOUTH AND FAMILIES.  THRIVE TARGETS YOUTH AGES 11-18 AND THEIR FAMILIES CONCENTRATED IN HIGH-VIOLENCE NEIGHBORHOODS AND IMPACTED BY INTERPERSONAL VIOLENCE, WITH THE GREATEST UNMET BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEED WHO PRESENT WITH PTSD AND TRAUMA-RELATED CONDITIONS AS WELL AS CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUD) AND DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOR DISORDERS (DBD) – INCLUDING MULTI-SYSTEM-INVOLVED YOUTH ACROSS MENTAL HEALTH, JUVENILE JUSTICE, AND SCHOOL SETTINGS, WITH PLANS TO PROMOTE TRAUMA RECOVERY AND HEALING, REDUCING SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS BURDEN, AND PREVENTING ESCALATING DELINQUENCY AND INTENSIFYING POLICE AND JUVENILE JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT. THRIVE WILL BUILD AND SUSTAIN CROSS-SYSTEM WORKFORCE CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE PROTOCOLS FOR: 1) INTEGRATED CLINICAL INTERVENTIONS (TRAUMA SYSTEMS THERAPY FOR ADOLESCENT SUBSTANCE ABUSE, STRENGTHS FOR TRAUMA RESILIENCE, OVERCOMING GROWING); 2) COMMUNITY-BASED PREVENTION PROGRAMMING (HIP-HOP H.E.A.L.S., YOUTH VIOLENCE PREVENTION ENGAGEMENT); 3) COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT CURRICULA (BEACON LIVED EXPERIENCE TRAINING); AND 4) CROSS-SYSTEM SERVICE COORDINATION AND CRISIS RESPONSE PROTOCOLS (ADVERSE CHILDHOOD CRITICAL EVENTS AND SAFETY SCREENER [ACCES]). THRIVE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES BELOW DIRECTLY ADVANCE SAMHSA'S LATEST STRATEGIC PRIORITIES - PREVENTING SUBSTANCE MISUSE, ABUSE, AND ADDICTION; ADDRESSING SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS; IMPROVING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT FOR MENTAL ILLNESS, SUBSTANCE USE, AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS; HELPING INDIVIDUALS ACHIEVE LONG-TERM RECOVERY AND SOBRIETY; AND EXPANDING CRISIS INTERVENTION CARE AND SERVICES — THROUGH: (1) SPECIALIZED TRAINING, CONSULTATION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND EVALUATION SUPPORT FOR 1,500 CLINICIANS AND 2,000 COMMUNITY PROVIDERS ON EVIDENCE-BASED, DATA-DRIVEN INTEGRATED TREATMENT THAT WILL SERVE 10,500 YOUTH AND FAMILIES WITH ≥85% SUCCESS IN OUTCOMES MONITORING; (2) COLLABORATIVELY ENGAGING 50+ ORGANIZATIONAL PARTNERS IN MULTI-SYSTEM RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (A) THROUGH UYTC'S NATIONAL ONLINE TRAINING PLATFORM, NCTSN'S COLLABORATIVE GROUP LEADERSHIP OF THE COMMUNITY VIOLENCE AND SUBSTANCE ABUSE WORKGROUPS, AND NATIONAL YOUTH VIOLENCE PREVENTION MOBILIZATION EFFORTS REACHING 10,000 INDIVIDUALS; AND (B) SUSTAINING CROSS-SYSTEM CRISIS IDENTIFICATION AND RESPONSE CAPACITY THROUGH IMPLEMENTATION OF UYTC SCREENING AND REFERRAL PROTOCOL (ACCES) DEPLOYMENT ACROSS HEALTH, MENTAL HEALTH, JUVENILE JUSTICE, SCHOOL, AND COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SETTINGS. OVER THE 5-YEAR GRANT PERIOD, THRIVE WILL SUSTAIN EVIDENCE-BASED, TRAUMA-INFORMED PRACTICES THROUGH MULTI-SECTOR STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT — SPANNING YOUTH AND FAMILIES, LIVED EXPERIENCE EXPERTS, PROVIDERS, COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, JUVENILE JUSTICE, SCHOOLS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, MENTAL HEALTH, CHILD WELFARE, HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS, AND FAITH-BASED INSTITUTIONS — TARGETING ≥85% ANNUAL INCREASE IN TRAINED WORKFORCE CAPACITY AMONG TARGETED IMPLEMENTATION PARTNERS, SERVICE SYSTEMS, AND COMMUNITY IMPLEMENTATION CHAMPIONS.

description: CONNECTWELL: BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP NETWORK - PROJECT ABSTRACT PROJECT TITLE: CONNECTWELL: BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP NETWORK  CONNECTWELL IS A FIVE-YEAR COMMUNITY CAPACITY-BUILDING INITIATIVE THAT WILL STRENGTHEN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY ACROSS MADISON AND PLATTE COUNTIES, NEBRASKA. THROUGH A COORDINATED COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP NETWORK, LEARNING COLLABORATIVE, AND CONNECTION PRESCRIPTION NETWORK, THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE PREVENTION, EARLY IDENTIFICATION, COORDINATED RESPONSE, AND RECOVERY BY EQUIPPING COMMUNITY PARTNERS WITH SHARED TOOLS, TRAINING, REFERRAL PATHWAYS, AND DATA SYSTEMS THAT ADDRESS THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS OF CRIME, VIOLENCE, TRAUMA, AND COMMUNITY DISORDER. THE WELL NE WILL IMPLEMENT CONNECTWELL IN MADISON AND PLATTE COUNTIES, NEBRASKA, TWO RURAL MENTAL HEALTH PROFESSIONAL SHORTAGE AREAS EXPERIENCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, AND LIMITED ACCESS TO CARE. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY CAPACITY RATHER THAN CREATE NEW DIRECT SERVICE PROGRAMS BY IMPROVING COLLABORATION, REFERRAL PATHWAYS, WORKFORCE TRAINING, AND SHARED COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE. THE PROJECT WILL BENEFIT YOUTH, ADULTS, AND FAMILIES IMPACTED BY CRIME, VIOLENCE, TRAUMA, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, OR SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, WITH PRIORITY FOR RURAL RESIDENTS, JUSTICE-INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS, VETERANS, VICTIMS OF INTERPERSONAL VIOLENCE, AND HISPANIC AND IMMIGRANT POPULATIONS. INDIVIDUALS RECEIVING CONNECTION PRESCRIPTIONS MAY RECEIVE BARRIER-REDUCTION ASSISTANCE TO INCREASE ENGAGEMENT WITH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, RECOVERY, AND COMMUNITY RESOURCES. KEY STRATEGIES INCLUDE ESTABLISHING A COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP NETWORK (BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY COALITION); CONDUCTING A COMMUNITY NEEDS AND RESOURCE ASSESSMENT; DEVELOPING A COMMUNITY STRATEGIC PLAN; IMPLEMENTING A LEARNING COLLABORATIVE THAT PROVIDES EVIDENCE-BASED TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE; CREATING STANDARDIZED REFERRAL PATHWAYS AND A MICROSOFT-BASED COMMUNITY RESOURCE PLATFORM; IMPLEMENTING THE CONNECTION PRESCRIPTION NETWORK; AND SUPPORTING CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO STRENGTHEN CROSS-SECTOR COLLABORATION, INCREASE COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND RESPOND TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH CRIME, VIOLENCE, AND DISORDER, IMPROVE ACCESS TO COORDINATED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND RECOVERY SUPPORTS, AND BUILD SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE. OBJECTIVES INCLUDE ESTABLISHING A COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP NETWORK WITHIN THREE MONTHS; COMPLETING A COMMUNITY NEEDS ASSESSMENT AND DEVELOPING A COMMUNITY STRATEGIC PLAN DURING YEAR 1; LAUNCHING THE CONNECTION PRESCRIPTION NETWORK, SHARED RESOURCE PLATFORM, AND STANDARDIZED REFERRAL PATHWAYS BY THE END OF YEAR 1; DELIVERING EVIDENCE-BASED TRAINING THROUGH THE LEARNING COLLABORATIVE; AND INCREASING OUTREACH, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH REFERRALS, RECOVERY SUPPORTS, AND TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE TRAINING WHILE COLLECTING ALL REQUIRED SAMHSA PERFORMANCE MEASURES.

description: SAN DIEGO COMMUNITY RESILIENCE COLLABORATIVE PROJECT - SURVIVORS OF TORTURE, INTERNATIONAL (SURVIVORS) PROPOSES THE SAN DIEGO COMMUNITY RESILIENCE COLLABORATIVE (SDCRC), A FIVE-YEAR COUNTYWIDE INITIATIVE THAT WILL STRENGTHEN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY BY BUILDING CROSS-SECTOR PARTNERSHIPS, EXPANDING ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, AND INCREASING COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND RESPOND TO THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS OF CRIME, VIOLENCE, COMMUNITY DISORDER, AND TRAUMATIC EVENTS AMONG SAN DIEGO COUNTY'S MOST VULNERABLE POPULATIONS. FOR NEARLY THREE DECADES, SURVIVORS HAS SERVED AS SAN DIEGO COUNTY'S TRUSTED LEADER IN TRAUMA-INFORMED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CARE FOR INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY TORTURE, VIOLENT CRIME, FORCED DISPLACEMENT, AND OTHER SIGNIFICANT TRAUMA. AS THE REGION'S ONLY INTERNATIONALLY ACCREDITED TORTURE TREATMENT CENTER, A CALIFORNIA-CERTIFIED TRAUMA RECOVERY CENTER, AND A COUNTY-CONTRACTED SHORT-DOYLE MEDI-CAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINIC, SURVIVORS PROVIDES AN INTEGRATED CONTINUUM OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TREATMENT, CARE COORDINATION, PREVENTION, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT.  THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL SERVE COMMUNITIES THROUGHOUT SAN DIEGO COUNTY, CALIFORNIA, WITH PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON EAST, CENTRAL, AND SOUTH SAN DIEGO COUNTY, WHERE CRIME, VIOLENCE, POVERTY, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISPARITIES ARE MOST CONCENTRATED. CAPACITY-BUILDING EFFORTS WILL ADDRESS FRAGMENTED REFERRAL SYSTEMS, LIMITED CROSS-SECTOR COORDINATION, WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH STIGMA, AND BARRIERS TO ACCESSING CULTURALLY AND LINGUISTICALLY RESPONSIVE CARE. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDES YOUTH, ADULTS, OLDER ADULTS, AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY CRIME, VIOLENCE, COMMUNITY DISORDER, TRAUMATIC EVENTS, AND FORCED DISPLACEMENT, WITH PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON REFUGEES, ASYLUM SEEKERS, ASYLEES, SPECIAL IMMIGRANT VISA HOLDERS, HUMANITARIAN PAROLEES, VICTIMS OF VIOLENT CRIME, AND OTHER HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS EXPERIENCING OR AT INCREASED RISK FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, INCLUDING DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, PTSD, PROLONGED GRIEF, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, AND OTHER TRAUMA-RELATED DISORDERS. SURVIVORS WILL SERVE AS THE LEAD ORGANIZATION FOR A COUNTYWIDE COMMUNITY RESILIENCE COALITION THAT BRINGS TOGETHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS, SCHOOLS, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, FAITH COMMUNITIES, PUBLIC AGENCIES, LAW ENFORCEMENT, UNIVERSITIES, AND INDIVIDUALS WITH LIVED EXPERIENCE. CAPACITY-BUILDING STRATEGIES INCLUDE COALITION DEVELOPMENT, A COMMUNITY NEEDS AND RESOURCES ASSESSMENT, STRATEGIC PLANNING, STANDARDIZED REFERRAL PATHWAYS, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH LITERACY, PREVENTION AND EARLY INTERVENTION PROGRAMMING, EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, HEALTHCARE NAVIGATION, COORDINATED CARE, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT.  THE PROJECT'S GOALS ARE TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND RESPOND TO THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS OF CRIME, VIOLENCE, AND COMMUNITY DISORDER; EXPAND ACCESS TO COORDINATED, CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES; IMPROVE CROSS-SECTOR COLLABORATION; AND STRENGTHEN LONG-TERM COMMUNITY RESILIENCE. KEY OBJECTIVES INCLUDE ESTABLISHING A COUNTYWIDE COALITION, COMPLETING A COMMUNITY NEEDS AND RESOURCES ASSESSMENT AND STRATEGIC PLAN, INCREASING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH REFERRALS AND SERVICE ENGAGEMENT, EXPANDING WORKFORCE TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, STRENGTHENING COORDINATED REFERRAL SYSTEMS, AND IMPROVING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES THROUGH ONGOING EVALUATION AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT. BY LEVERAGING NEARLY 30 YEARS OF TRUSTED PARTNERSHIPS, SPECIALIZED EXPERTISE, AND ESTABLISHED COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE, SURVIVORS WILL STRENGTHEN SAN DIEGO COUNTY'S BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEM WHILE ADVANCING SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES OF PREVENTION, TREATMENT, RECOVERY, AND SUSTAINABLE SYSTEMS CHANGE.

CHICAGO SUFFERS HIGH RATES OF CRIME AND COMMUNITY VIOLENCE, PARTICULARLY IN ITS SOUTH SIDE COMMUNITIES. YOUTH WHO LIVE IN THESE VIOLENCE-IMPACTED COMMUNITIES ARE AT RISK FOR SERIOUS BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISORDERS, POOR ACADEMIC ACHIEVEMENT, AND SUBSTANCE USE. DESPITE THE IMPORTANCE OF PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION STRATEGIES, YOUTH-FOCUSED RESOURCES AND PROGRAMS ARE LIMITED. WE WILL CONNECT AT-RISK YOUTH IN THESE FAR SOUTH SIDE COMMUNITIES TO A SCHOOL-BASED PREVENTION PROGRAM, TRAUMA-FOCUSED THERAPY, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SUPPORT SERVICES. WE WILL ALSO PROVIDE TRAUMA-INFORMED AND MENTAL HEALTH LITERACY TRAININGS TO KEY ADULT PARTNERS IN THE COMMUNITY, INCLUDING PARENTS, TEACHERS, AND ORGANIZATIONAL LEADERS.  THE GOALS OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDE: 1. BUILD A PROJECT TEAM DEDICATED TO UNDERSTANDING AND ENHANCING THE UNIQUE RESOURCES AND NEEDS IN CHICAGO'S FAR SOUTH SIDE COMMUNITIES, LEVERAGING EXISTING WORK AND PARTNERSHIPS. THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY COALITION WILL MEET BI-WEEKLY TO DRAFT A COMMUNITY STRATEGIC PLAN, OBTAIN COMMUNITY INPUT THROUGH COMMUNITY FORUMS AND YOUTH ADVISORY BOARD MEETINGS, AND FINALIZE THE STRATEGIC PLAN BY MONTH 9.  3. BUILD A COMPREHENSIVE REFERRAL AND RESOURCE NETWORK FOR CHICAGO’S FAR SOUTH SIDE COMMUNITIES AND EXPAND CAPACITY BOTH WITHIN AND ACROSS PREVENTION, EARLY INTERVENTION, AND TREATMENT PROGRAMS. THROUGH INCREASED STAFF AND TRAININGS STARTING IN YEAR ONE, WE WILL INCREASE CAPACITY FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SUPPORT SERVICES AND MENTORSHIP, TUTORING, CAREER EXPOSURE, AND SOCIAL EMOTIONAL LEARNING. FORMAL REFERRAL PATHWAYS WILL EXPAND YOUTH ACCESS TO SERVICES.  4. IMPLEMENT EXPANDED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INTERVENTION AND PREVENTIVE SERVICES AND CREATE CARE LINKAGES FOR YOUTH ON CHICAGO’S FAR SOUTH SIDE. STARTING MONTH 9, WE WILL DELIVER SCHOOL-BASED PREVENTION PROGRAM (MENTORSHIP, TUTORING, CAREER EXPOSURE, SOCIAL EMOTIONAL LEARNING) TO 120 YOUTH ACROSS 8 SCHOOLS ANNUALLY, INDIVIDUAL THERAPY TO 20 YOUTH ANNUALLY, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SUPPORT SERVICES TO 40 YOUTH ANNUALLY.  5. EXPAND CAPACITY OF CHICAGO’S FAR SOUTH SIDE COMMUNITIES TO RECOGNIZE AND INTERVENE ON YOUTH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS THROUGH TRAININGS AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT EVENTS. STARTING MONTH 9, WE WILL PROVIDE MENTAL HEALTH LITERACY AND TRAUMA-INFORMED TRAININGS FOR COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, SCHOOL PERSONNEL, PARENTS, CAREGIVERS, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS. WE WILL ALSO PROVIDE EMERGENCY RESPONSE TRAININGS TO YOUTH AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS. IN TOTAL, WE AIM TO REACH 200 PERSONS ANNUALLY THROUGH THESE CAPACITY BUILDING TRAININGS.

description: IMPLEMENTING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY PARTNERSHIPS - THIS IS A COMPREHENSIVE, FIVE-YEAR CAPACITY BUILDING PROJECT TO SUPPORT COMMUNITIES IN REDUCING THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS OF CRIME, VIOLENCE, AND DISORDER; TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY SAFETY; AND TO IMPROVE OUTCOMES FOR YOUTH AND FAMILIES. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE A BROAD GROUP OF YOUTH IN NEED TO OPTIMIZE ITS IMPACT. THE INDIVIDUALS TO BE SERVED INCLUDE A) YOUTH AFFECTED BY VIOLENCE, PLACING THEM AT-RISK FOR LATER ENGAGING IN VIOLENCE; B) YOUTH REFERRED TO OR ALREADY INVOLVED IN THE JUSTICE OR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEMS; C) YOUTH ENCOUNTERING LAW ENFORCEMENT THROUGH CRISIS CALLS; AND D) UNACCOMPANIED HOMELESS YOUTH. THE BH-CSC WILL BUILD BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CAPACITY USING MULTI-METHODS, INCLUDING IMPLEMENTING AND TESTING THE FEASIBILITY OF TWO EVIDENCE-BASED EARLY INTERVENTION PROGRAMS; BOLSTERING THE PEER SUPPORT WORKFORCE, CRISIS INTERVENTION, AND POST-TRAUMA RESPONSES FOR YOUTH AND COMMUNITIES; STRENGTHENING THE REFERRAL PROCESS FROM SCHOOLS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND HOSPITALS TO EVIDENCE-BASED EARLY INTERVENTION AND VIOLENCE PREVENTION SERVICES; INCREASING ACCESS TO RECOVERY AND RESILIENCY SERVICES; DEVISING SOLUTIONS TO YOUTH HOMELESSNESS; AND LEVERAGING FUNDING STREAMS TO MAINTAIN YOUTH AND FAMILY ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED PROGRAMS THAT REDUCE VIOLENCE AMONG YOUTH WITH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS.   THE PROJECT GOALS AND OBJECTIVES ADDRESS ALL SIX OF THE SAMHSA STRATEGIC PRIORITIES:  GOAL 1: TO EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, CRISIS INTERVENTION, AND RECOVERY AND RESILIENCY SERVICES FOR YOUTH AGE 12 TO 25 AND THEIR FAMILIES BY IMPLEMENTING SERVICES TO ENHANCE COMMUNITY SAFETY AND STABILITY.   OBJECTIVES INCLUDE:  A) DEVELOP A SUSTAINABLE BH-CSC COMPRISING YOUTH-SERVING STATE AGENCIES, PROVIDERS, AND INDIVIDUALS WITH LIVED EXPERIENCE;  B) IDENTIFY AND IMPLEMENT FEASIBLE EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES AND CRISIS INTERVENTION APPROACHES THAT ARE SCALABLE TO OTHER COMMUNITIES IN THE COMMONWEALTH; AND  C) CREATE A STANDARDIZED REFERRAL PROCESS FROM TO APPROPRIATE EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES.  GOAL 2: STRENGTHEN THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE CAPACITY TO INCORPORATE AND SUSTAIN EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES THAT REDUCE CRIME, VIOLENCE, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES AND THEIR IMPACT ON YOUTH AND FAMILIES.    OBJECTIVES INCLUDE:  A) DEVISE A STRATEGY FOR LEVERAGING MASSHEALTH DOLLARS TO SUSTAIN FUNDING FOR EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROGRAMS THAT REDUCE VIOLENCE;  B) PROVIDE STATEWIDE TRAINING TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS IN EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES AND VIOLENCE RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS; AND  C) STRENGTHEN THE WORKFORCE OF RETURNING CITIZENS AND PEERS WITH LIVED EXPERIENCE TO PROVIDE SUPPORTS LONGER-TERM RECOVERY AND RESILIENCY.  GOAL 3: DEVELOP A STATEWIDE PLAN FOR SERVICES TO HOMELESS YOUTH AND RESPONSES TO TRAUMA AND EMERGING THREATS TO COMMUNITY SAFETY AND SECURITY   OBJECTIVES INCLUDE:  A) DEVISE AND IMPLEMENT ACTION-ORIENTED SOLUTIONS FOR IMPROVING SERVICES TO YOUTH AND FAMILIES EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS;  B) COMPLETE AND IMPLEMENT A PLAN FOR IDENTIFYING EMERGING THREATS AND POST-TRAUMA RESPONSE.

description: PROJECT DAWN: DEVELOPING AWARENESS, WELLNESS, AND NAVIGATIONA COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP ADVANCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, RESILIENCE, AND COMMUNITY SAFETY - THE SAN ANTONIO COUNCIL ON ALCOHOL AND DRUG AWARENESS (SACADA), IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE CIRCLES OF SAN ANTONIO COMMUNITY COALITION, PROPOSES TO IMPLEMENT PROJECT DAWN (DEVELOPING AWARENESS, WELLNESS, AND NAVIGATION), A COMPREHENSIVE FIVE-YEAR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY INITIATIVE THROUGHOUT BEXAR COUNTY, TEXAS. PROJECT DAWN WILL STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO IDENTIFY, ENGAGE, AND SUPPORT YOUTH, ADULTS, AND FAMILIES EXPERIENCING OR AT RISK FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES RELATED TO CRIME, VIOLENCE, SUBSTANCE USE, TRAUMA, AND COMMUNITY DISORDER.   BEXAR COUNTY, HOME TO MORE THAN 2.1 MILLION RESIDENTS, CONTINUES TO EXPERIENCE SIGNIFICANT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISPARITIES, INCREASING RATES OF MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, SUBSTANCE USE, SUICIDE, OVERDOSE DEATHS, AND VIOLENT CRIME. PROVIDER SHORTAGES, FRAGMENTED REFERRAL SYSTEMS, TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, AND WORKFORCE LIMITATIONS CONTRIBUTE TO DELAYED ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, PARTICULARLY IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT’S POPULATION OF FOCUS WILL BE YOUTH EXPOSED TO VIOLENCE, INDIVIDUALS WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS, SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS, JUSTICE-INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS, VETERANS, INDIVIDUALS EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS, AND FAMILIES FACING MULTIPLE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND SOCIAL CHALLENGES.  PROJECT DAWN SERVICES INCLUDE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, RESOURCE NAVIGATION, CARE COORDINATION, WARM HANDOFFS, REFERRALS TO TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES, PREVENTION EDUCATION, MENTORING, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS, RESILIENCE-BUILDING ACTIVITIES, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT. BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NAVIGATORS WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO ENSURE TIMELY CONNECTIONS TO EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT, RECOVERY, AND SUPPORTIVE SERVICES WHILE IMPROVING COORDINATION ACROSS HEALTHCARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, EDUCATION, PUBLIC SAFETY, AND COMMUNITY-BASED SYSTEMS. WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES WILL STRENGTHEN THE COMMUNITY'S BEHAVIORAL HEALTH RESPONSE CAPACITY BY PROVIDING MENTAL HEALTH FIRST AID, YOUTH MENTAL HEALTH FIRST AID, QUESTION, PERSUADE, REFER (QPR), BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AWARENESS, TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE, AND REFERRAL TRAINING TO EDUCATORS, HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS, FIRST RESPONDERS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, FAITH-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND OTHER FRONTLINE PERSONNEL. THESE ACTIVITIES WILL IMPROVE THE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONCERNS AND EXPAND THE COMMUNITY'S ABILITY TO RESPOND EFFECTIVELY TO INDIVIDUALS IN NEED. BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, PROJECT DAWN ANTICIPATES SCREENING AT LEAST 500 INDIVIDUALS AND ENROLLING AT LEAST 250 HIGH-RISK YOUTH AND FAMILY MEMBERS IN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, PREVENTION, RECOVERY, OR SUPPORTIVE SERVICES; AND PROVIDING PREVENTION, COPING SKILLS, AND RESILIENCE EDUCATION TO AT LEAST 600 COMMUNITY MEMBERS THROUGH 48 PRESENTATIONS, TRAININGS AND WORKSHOPS.  PROJECT DAWN WILL BE IMPLEMENTED THROUGH A ROBUST NETWORK OF COMMUNITY PARTNERS, INCLUDING THE CENTER FOR HEALTH CARE SERVICES, UT HEALTH SAN ANTONIO BE WELL INSTITUTE, UNIVERSITY HEALTH, RISE RECOVERY, LIFETIME RECOVERY, THE SAN ANTONIO METROPOLITAN HEALTH DISTRICT, BEXAR COUNTY JUVENILE PROBATION DEPARTMENT, THE SAN ANTONIO POLICE DEPARTMENT, SOUTH TEXAS HIDTA, LOCAL SCHOOL DISTRICTS, FAMILY VIOLENCE PREVENTION SERVICES, SOUTHSIDE COLLABORATIVE, BETHEL PREVENTION COALITION, TEXAS HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES COMMISSION, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, FAITH-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND OTHER MEMBERS OF THE CIRCLES OF SAN ANTONIO COMMUNITY COALITION. TOGETHER, THESE PARTNERS WILL IMPROVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES, STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY SAFETY, EXPAND ACCESS TO CARE, AND BUILD A SUSTAINABLE, COORDINATED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEM ACROSS BEXAR COUNTY.

description: COMMUNITY ACCESS & RESOURCES EDUCATION (CARE) COALITION - BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SOLUTIONS OF SOUTH TEXAS (BHSST), IN COLLABORATION WITH THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, PROPOSES THE COMMUNITY ACCESS & RESOURCES EDUCATION (CARE) COALITION PROJECT TO ADDRESS THE SUBSTANTIAL UNMET BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS IDENTIFIED IN THE RIO GRANDE VALLEY (RGV), INCLUDING HIGH RATES OF TRAUMA EXPOSURE, SIGNIFICANT MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE NEEDS, LIMITED SERVICE COORDINATION, WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, AND INSUFFICIENT COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE TO ADDRESS THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS OF CRIME, VIOLENCE, AND DISORDER. : THE CARE COALITION WILL SERVE YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS, ADULTS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS LIVING WITHIN THE CAMERON, HIDALGO, AND WILLACY COUNTIES IN THE RGV WHO HAVE BEEN IMPACTED BY CRIME, VIOLENCE, DISORDER, TRAUMA, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, MENTAL ILLNESS, AND RELATED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS. THE SERVICE AREA INCLUDES A POPULATION EXCEEDING 1.3 MILLION RESIDENTS, WITH A HIGH PROPORTION OF YOUTH AND SIGNIFICANT RURAL DISPARITIES, PARTICULARLY IN WILLACY COUNTY. SUBSTANCE USE REMAINS A CRITICAL PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERN IN THE REGION, WITH EARLY INITIATION, INCREASING OPIOID-RELATED RISKS, AND ONGOING CHALLENGES RELATED TO ALCOHOL USE, VAPING, AND PRESCRIPTION MISUSE. THESE RISKS ARE COMPOUNDED BY ELEVATED POVERTY RATES, LIMITED ACCESS TO HEALTHCARE, AND GAPS IN PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE. THE CARE COALITION PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT A COMPREHENSIVE, DATA-DRIVEN APPROACH GUIDED BY THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK (SPF). THE PROJECT WILL ACCOMPLISH THIS THROUGH COALITION DEVELOPMENT, SYSTEMS COORDINATION, PREVENTION, EARLY INTERVENTION, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AND COMMUNITY CAPACITY-BUILDING ACTIVITIES. THE PROJECT WILL PURSUE SIX PRIMARY GOALS TO GUIDE IMPLEMENTATION AND OUTCOMES: 1) ESTABLISH AND SUSTAIN A BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY COALITION; 2) INCREASE COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO IDENTIFY AND ADDRESS BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS ASSOCIATED WITH CRIME, VIOLENCE, AND DISORDER. 3) EXPAND ACCESS TO PREVENTION, EARLY INTERVENTION, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TREATMENT, AND RECOVERY SUPPORTS; 4) STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY-BASED TRAUMA RESPONSE AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT; 5) STRENGTHEN YOUTH AND FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, RESILIENCE, AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS; AND 6) CREATE SUSTAINABLE SYSTEMS CHANGE THAT IMPROVES BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES AND COMMUNITY SAFETY. THE PROJECT WILL PRIORITIZE CAPACITY BUILDING, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES TAILORED TO LOCAL NEEDS. THE PROJECT WILL WORK TO STRENGTHEN REFERRAL PATHWAYS AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND SUPPORT SERVICES ACROSS THE REGION. OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, THE CARE COALITION WILL REACH AT LEAST 2,000 INDIVIDUALS ANNUALLY THROUGH COMMUNITY OUTREACH, PREVENTION PROGRAMMING, SCREENING, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH EDUCATION, AND REFERRAL ACTIVITIES; SCREEN AT LEAST 500 INDIVIDUALS ANNUALLY FOR TRAUMA-RELATED CONCERNS, MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, AND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, WITH AT LEAST 75 PERCENT SUCCESSFULLY LINKED TO SERVICES; PROVIDE RECOVERY-SUPPORT, FAMILY-SUPPORT, CASE-MANAGEMENT, PEER-SUPPORT, AND CARE-COORDINATION SERVICES TO A MINIMUM OF 300 INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES/YEAR; AND TRAIN AT LEAST 250 PROFESSIONALS ANNUALLY IN TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH LITERACY, PREVENTION STRATEGIES, REFERRAL PROCEDURES, AND COORDINATED RESPONSE PRACTICES.

description: SAN BERNARDINO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, COMMUNITY HEALING, AND SAFETY PARTNERSHIP INITIATIVE - EL SOL NEIGHBORHOOD EDUCATIONAL CENTER PROPOSES THE SAN BERNARDINO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, COMMUNITY HEALING, AND SAFETY PARTNERSHIP INITIATIVE, A FIVE-YEAR PROJECT TO ADDRESS THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS OF CRIME, VIOLENCE, AND TRAUMA AMONG YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND RESIDENTS OF THE CITY OF SAN BERNARDINO. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY SAFETY AND WELL-BEING BY EXPANDING COMMUNITY-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PREVENTION, EARLY INTERVENTION, RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND COORDINATED SYSTEMS OF CARE THROUGH A COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER (CHW)-LED MODEL.  THE PROJECT WILL SERVE RESIDENTS IN FIVE HIGH-NEED ZIP CODES (92410, 92411, 92404, 92405, AND 92408), WHERE EXPOSURE TO CRIME AND VIOLENCE CONTRIBUTES TO SIGNIFICANT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES. SAN BERNARDINO'S VIOLENT CRIME RATE IS APPROXIMATELY TWICE THE CALIFORNIA AVERAGE, WHILE AN ESTIMATED 15,354 COUNTY RESIDENTS WITH MENTAL HEALTH NEEDS GO WITHOUT SERVICES EACH YEAR. AMONG YOUTH, ONLY 9.1% OF THOSE NEEDING MENTAL HEALTH COUNSELING RECEIVE CARE, AND THE YOUTH SUICIDE RATE INCREASED 33% BETWEEN 2019 AND 2023. AT THE SAME TIME, THE REGION FACES SEVERE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE SHORTAGES AND FRAGMENTED SERVICE SYSTEMS THAT LIMIT TIMELY ACCESS TO CARE.   BUILDING UPON EL SOL'S EXISTING INTERDISCIPLINARY PARTNERSHIPS, THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY COALITION CONSISTING OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, SCHOOLS, PUBLIC HEALTH AGENCIES, FAITH-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, PUBLIC SAFETY PARTNERS, AND COMMUNITY RESIDENTS. THE COALITION WILL GUIDE A COMMUNITY NEEDS AND RESOURCES ASSESSMENT, DEVELOP A COMMUNITY STRATEGIC PLAN, STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF FIVE COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND IMPLEMENT COORDINATED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTREACH, SCREENING, NAVIGATION, REFERRAL, RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND COMMUNITY HEALING SERVICES. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO PROVIDE COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, MENTAL HEALTH LITERACY TRAINING, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND STANDARDIZED SCREENING, REFERRAL, AND DATA-SHARING PROTOCOLS TO IMPROVE COORDINATION ACROSS SYSTEMS.  OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, THE INITIATIVE WILL ENGAGE 12,000 RESIDENTS THROUGH COMMUNITY OUTREACH, COMPLETE 4,000 BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENINGS, PROVIDE NAVIGATION SERVICES TO 2,500 INDIVIDUALS, FACILITATE 2,000 REFERRALS, CONNECT 1,500 INDIVIDUALS TO MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES, PROVIDE RECOVERY AND RESILIENCE SUPPORTS TO 2,000 PARTICIPANTS, AND TRAIN 120 COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS AND FRONTLINE STAFF. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, REDUCED TRAUMA-RELATED SYMPTOMS, INCREASED ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, STRONGER COLLABORATION AMONG BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, COMMUNITY, AND PUBLIC SAFETY PARTNERS, EXPANDED ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY, AND A SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE THAT STRENGTHENS RECOVERY, RESILIENCE, COMMUNITY HEALING, AND COMMUNITY SAFETY BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD.

description: BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PARTNERSHIPS FOR EARLY DIVERSION OF ADULTS AND YOUTH - THE SOUTHEAST MISSOURI EARLY DIVERSION INITIATIVE WILL EXPAND MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE DIVERSION SERVICES ACROSS SEVEN RURAL COUNTIES, SERVING MORE THAN 1,300 ADULTS OVER FIVE YEARS. THIS PROJECT IDENTIFIES AND SUPPORTS INDIVIDUALS AT RISK OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED SCREENING, CRISIS RESPONSE, AND RAPID LINKAGE TO CARE. BY STRENGTHENING COORDINATION AMONG BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, EMS, CRISIS SERVICES, AND COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS, IT WILL REDUCE PREVENTABLE ARRESTS AND IMPROVE COMMUNITY SAFETY. MOBILE OUTREACH, VETERAN-FOCUSED SUPPORTS, AND VALIDATED SCREENING TOOLS WILL INCREASE ACCESS TO TREATMENT IN UNDERSERVED RURAL REGIONS. THE INITIATIVE ADVANCES SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES IN PREVENTION, CRISIS CARE, EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT, LONG-TERM RECOVERY, AND DATA-DRIVEN SYSTEM IMPROVEMENT. THE SOUTHEAST MISSOURI EARLY DIVERSION INITIATIVE WILL SERVE CAPE GIRARDEAU, BOLLINGER, MADISON, MISSISSIPPI, PERRY, SCOTT, AND STE. GENEVIEVE COUNTIES, COVERING 3,534 SQUARE MILES WITH A POPULATION OF 202,863 RESIDENTS. THE PROJECT TARGETS ADULTS AT RISK OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT WHO ARE EXPERIENCING OR SHOWING WARNING SIGNS OF MENTAL ILLNESS OR CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS. THIS INCLUDES INDIVIDUALS WITH DEPRESSION, ANXIETY DISORDERS, BIPOLAR DISORDER, SCHIZOPHRENIA, POST TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER (PTSD), TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY, AND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, AS WELL AS INDIVIDUALS WITH ELEVATED SUICIDE RISK. POPULATION DEMOGRAPHICS SHOW THAT 23% OF RESIDENTS ARE UNDER 18, 55% ARE ADULTS AGES 18-64, AND OVER 20% ARE SENIORS, WITH RURAL COUNTIES SKEWING SIGNIFICANTLY OLDER. VETERANS REPRESENT A MAJOR AT-RISK SUBGROUP, WITH 10,087 VETERANS LIVING IN THE SERVICE AREA AND EXPERIENCING DISPROPORTIONATELY HIGH RATES OF PTSD, MOOD AND ANXIETY DISORDERS, SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, AND SUICIDAL IDEATION. ACROSS THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, THE INITIATIVE WILL SERVE: YEAR 1: 150 INDIVIDUALS; YEAR 2: 225 INDIVIDUALS; YEAR 3: 255 INDIVIDUALS; YEARS 4–5: 350 INDIVIDUALS ANNUALLY-A TOTAL OF 1,330 UNDUPLICATED ADULTS SERVED. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS INCLUDE VALIDATED SCREENING TOOLS, MENTAL HEALTH FIRST AID (MHFA), QUESTION, PERSUADE, REFER (QPR) SUICIDE PREVENTION, CRISIS INTERVENTION TEAM (CIT) TRAINING, TRAUMA-INFORMED ENGAGEMENT, MOBILE OUTREACH, AND CROSS-SYSTEM COORDINATION WITH LAW ENFORCEMENT, COURTS, EMS, 988, HOSPITALS, HOUSING PROVIDERS, AND THE VA. PROJECT GOALS INCLUDE IMPROVING COMMUNITY OUTREACH AND LINKAGES, EXPANDING MOBILE TREATMENT SERVICES AND TELEHEALTH, IMPLEMENTING VALIDATED RISK ASSESSMENT AND DIVERSION TOOLS, AND IMPROVING DATA COLLECTION AND CROSS-SYSTEM COMMUNICATION. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES ALIGNED WITH SAMHSA’S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES INCLUDE INCREASING VALIDATED SCREENINGS, REDUCING PRE-BOOKING ARRESTS THROUGH EARLY LINKAGE, INCREASING REFERRALS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT BASED ON ADMISSIONS ACROSS COMMUNITY PROVIDERS, AND CONDUCTING QUARTERLY SPARS REPORTING, ANNUAL CQI CYCLES, AND YEAR-3 SEQUENTIAL INTERCEPT MAPPING UPDATES TO STRENGTHEN SYSTEM ALIGNMENT. DMH AND PARTNER AGENCIES WILL COLLABORATE WITH KEY COALITION PARTNERS, POLICE DEPARTMENTS, COURTS, AND JAILS IN THE 24TH, 32ND, AND 33RD JUDICIAL CIRCUITS TO TRACK ARREST AND BOOKING DATA OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT TIMELINE TO ASSESS OUTCOMES OF EARLY DIVERSION INTERVENTIONS.

description: CIRCLES OF CARE - INDIAN HEALTH COUNCIL, INC. (IHC) PROPOSES TO PLAN AND DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE BLUEPRINT FOR A SYSTEM OF CARE (SOC), FOCUSING ON AMERICAN INDIANS UP TO AGE 25. THIS SOC WILL COORDINATE EFFECTIVE MENTAL HEALTH AND ESSENTIAL SUPPORTIVE SERVICES.  GOALS/ACTIVITIES IN THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE CONVENING A TRIBAL COMMUNITY BOARD TO PLAN THE SOC, CONDUCTING A TRIBAL SWOT ANALYSIS, HOLDING ANNUAL GONAS, DEVELOPING CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS AND FINALIZING A SOC BLUEPRINT BY THE END OF YEAR 3.  INDIAN HEALTH COUNCIL, INC. (IHC) IS A NONPROFIT FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTER RUN BY AND SERVING NINE FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBES IN NORTHERN SAN DIEGO COUNTY. FOUNDED IN 1970, IHC PROVIDES PRIMARY CARE SERVICES FROM TWO CLINIC FACILITIES.  ALTHOUGH THERE IS A DAYTIME BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, THE TRIBAL CONSORTIUM HAS TO REFER OUT WHEN THERE IS A MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS REQUIRING HOSPITALIZATION.  THEREFORE, THERE ARE NEEDS FOR IMPROVING A TRAUMA-INFORMED RESPONSE FOR TRIBAL REFERRALS TO CRISIS STABILIZATION UNITS IN THE AREA, WHICH PRESENTLY INVOLVES  COLD HANDOFFS  AND NO ORIENTATIONS FOR WHAT TO EXPECT IN SUCH SETTINGS. IN THE AGE GROUP UNDER AGE 25, THERE WERE 878 UNDUPLICATED FEMALES AND 815 UNDUPLICATED MALES IN IHC CLINIC VISITS OVER THE PAST YEAR. IHC'S BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT HAD 734 VISITS BY FEMALES IN THAT AGE RANGE, COMPARED TO 393 BY MALES. THERE WERE 46 SUBSTANCE ABUSE DIAGNOSES IN THAT AGE RANGE, SPLIT BETWEEN 22 FEMALES AND 24 MALES. IN A RECENT REVIEW OF IHC DIAGNOSES, DEPRESSION WAS THE MOST COMMONLY EXPERIENCED MENTAL HEALTH ISSUE AND IS ASSOCIATED WITH SUICIDAL IDEATION AND ALCOHOL AND DRUG ABUSE. OF 12-24 YEAR-OLDS (N=537) SCREENED FOR DEPRESSION AT IHC IN THE PAST YEAR, 40% (N=124) HAD RESULTS CONSISTENT WITH MODERATE TO SEVERE DEPRESSION, BUT THESE ARE INDICATORS, NOT DIAGNOSES.  THE PROPOSED REQUIRED ACTIVITIES ADDRESS MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS RESPONSE CENTER REFERRAL SOC DEVELOPMENT THROUGH TRIBAL ADVISORY COUNCILS CREATING MESSAGING CAMPAIGNS, NEEDS ASSESSMENTS IN THE FIRST YEAR,  OVERDOSE RESPONSE PLAN DEVELOP-MENT AND DEPLOYMENT, AND THOROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED TRAINING IN MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING FOR IHC STAFF MEMBERS AS WELL AS A NUMBER OF COMMUNITY MEMBERS LIVING WITH AT-RISK CHILDREN/YOUNG ADULTS.  GOAL 1:  TO IDENTIFY MEMBERS AND THEN CONVENE A TRIBAL ADVISORY BOARD WHO MEET QUARTERLY TO DESIGN A CULTURALLY RELEVANT SOC THAT WILL GUIDE REFERRALS TO AND PARTNERSHIPS WITH REGIONAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS RESPONSE CENTERS.   GOAL 2: THIS TRIBAL ADVISORY BOARD AND IHC’S BOARD WILL CONDUCT A TRIBAL SWOT ANALYSIS:   IN THE FIRST QUARTER OF THE PROJECT, THE BOARDS WILL MEET TO CARRY OUT A TRIBAL STRENGTHS, WEAKNESSES OPPORTUNITIES AND THREATS ANALYSIS.  GOAL 3: HOLDING ANNUAL GONAS:  FOCUSING UPON DIFFERENT AGE GROUPS OF YOUTH (HIGH SCHOOL, ELEMENTARY SCHOOL, AND TRANSITION AGE YOUTH) IN THREE ANNUAL GONAS FACILITATED BY EXPERIENCED LOCAL INDIGENOUS LEADERS, INSIGHTS FROM PARTICIPANTS WILL BE RECORDED FOR POTENTIAL SOC INCORPORATION GOAL 4: DEVELOPING CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS: PARTICULARLY WITH LOCAL CRISIS RESPONSE CENTERS AND THE INTERTRIBAL COURT SYSTEM, THE IHC PROJECT TEAM WILL CONFER WITH THESE PARTNERS TO STANDARDIZE REFERRALS. GOAL 5: FINALIZING A SOC BLUEPRINT BY THE END OF YEAR 3, BUILDING UPON THE INFORMATION GENERATED IN THIS PROJECT, WITH THE GUIDANCE AND THE ASSISTANCE OF TRIBAL ADVISORY BOARD/TRIBAL COUNCILS. WE SHALL RECORD MEASURES OF PARTICIPATION IN ALL REQUIRED ACTIVITIES, AND THE PROJECT DIRECTOR WILL SUBMIT QUARTERLY REPORTS TO SAMHSA ON THE RELEVANT METRICS VIA SPARS, FED FROM PROJECT RECORDS.

description: CIRCLES OF CARE:  MENTAL WELLNESS PROJECT - PROJECT ABSTRACT PROJECT NAME: CIRCLES OF CARE: MENTAL WELLNESS PROJECT  PROJECT SUMMARY: THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A CULTURALLY ANCHORED SYSTEM OF CARE (SOC)A COORDINATED NETWORK OF SUPPORTS DESIGNED TO IMPROVE ACCESS, NAVIGATION, AND EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS. IT WILL DEVELOP TRAUMA-INFORMED AND CULTURAL HEALING SERVICES, BUILD CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS WHICH PROMOTES RESILIENCE, AND IMPROVES OUTCOMES FOR NATIVE CHILDREN ON THE FORT HALL INDIAN RESERVATION.  SERVICE POPULATION: NATIVE AMERICAN CHILDREN AND YOUTH (BIRTH–18) AND THEIR FAMILIES RESIDING IN THE FORT HALL INDIAN RESERVATION AND FORT HALL SERVICE AREA. THE REGION INCLUDES 1,673 NATIVE YOUTH, THE REGION EXPERIENCES SIGNIFICANT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISPARITIES DRIVEN BY HISTORICAL TRAUMA, SOCIOECONOMIC CHALLENGES, LIMITED MENTAL HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE, AND GEOGRAPHIC ISOLATION.  STRATEGIES OR INTERVENTIONS TO BE IMPLEMENTED: KEY COMPONENTS INCLUDE EXPANDING TRAUMA-INFORMED AND CULTURAL HEALING SERVICES, IMPLEMENT DARKNESS TO LIGHT’S STEWARDS OF CHILDREN® TRAINING, STRENGTHENING INTERAGENCY COORDINATION, AND IMPROVING REFERRAL AND SCREENING PROCESSES. EXTENSIVE COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT—YOUTH, FAMILIES, ELDERS, CULTURAL LEADERS WILL SHAPE PRIORITIES AND ENSURE CULTURAL RELEVANCE. SMART GOALS & OBJECTIVES:  1. ESTABLISH THE CIRCLE OF CARE COMMUNITY BOARD SPECIFIC: CREATE A DIVERSE GOVERNING BOARD TO GUIDE SYSTEM OF CARE PLANNING. MEASURABLE: • BOARD FORMED  • MONTHLY MEETINGS IN YEAR 1; QUARTERLY THEREAFTER TIME BOUND: ESTABLISH WITHIN 3 MONTHS, REGULAR MEETINGS ONGOING THROUGH YEAR 3 2. EXPAND ACCESS TO CULTURALLY GROUNDED, TRAUMA INFORMED SERVICES SPECIFIC: INCREASE AVAILABILITY OF CULTURALLY ANCHORED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SUPPORTS, TRAUMA INFORMED CARE TRAINING, AND TRADITIONAL HEALING PATHWAYS. MEASURABLE:   • PROVIDE AT LEAST 2 TRAUMA INFORMED COMMUNITY TRAININGS PER YEAR • OFFER 8 CULTURAL ENGAGEMENT WORKSHOPS ANNUALLY • TRAIN STAFF AND PROVIDERS 2 TIMES PER YEAR TIME BOUND: BEGIN WITHIN FIRST YEAR, EXPAND ANNUALLY YEARS 2–3 3. STRENGTHEN CROSS SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS SPECIFIC: FORMALIZE PARTNERSHIPS AMONG SCHOOLS, HEALTHCARE, JUSTICE SYSTEMS, HEALTHCARE MEASURABLE: • 3 LETTERS OF COMMITMENT • QUARTERLY INTERAGENCY COORDINATION MEETINGS • SERVICE MAPPING TOOL DEVELOPED BY END OF YEAR 2 TIME BOUND: MAPPING TOOLS COMPLETED BY END OF YEAR 2 4. INCREASE EARLY IDENTIFICATION AND REDUCE FRAGMENTED REFERRALS SPECIFIC: IMPLEMENT CLEAR, COORDINATED REFERRAL AND SCREENING PATHWAYS FOR NATIVE YOUTH AT RISK. MEASURABLE: • REDUCE FRAGMENTED REFERRAL CASES BY 20% BY YEAR 3 • REDUCE TIME FROM REFERRAL → SCREENING → NAVIGATION BY MEASURABLE BENCHMARKS • INCREASE REFERRALS TO COUNSELING AND SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT TIME BOUND: NEW PATHWAYS IMPLEMENTED BY END OF YEAR 2, EVALUATION YEAR 3  ESTIMATED NUMBER OF PEOPLE THE PROJECT WILL SERVE YEAR 1: 300   ENTIRE PROJECT: 450

description: PATHWAY FOR A NOBLE GENERATION PROJECT - PATHWAY FOR A NOBLE GENERATION PROJECT: AAN DATCHXANX’I YAN DEIYI AN INTERGENERATIONAL HEALING AND WELLNESS PROJECT OVERARCHING GOAL:  OVER THE THREE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, THE DOUGLAS INDIAN ASSOCIATION (DIA), IN PARTNERSHIP WITH COLLABORATING ORGANIZATIONS, WILL DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT, AND SUSTAIN THE PATHWAY FOR A NOBLE GENERATION PROJECT: AAN DATCHXANX’I YAN DEIYI, A CULTURALLY GROUNDED, COMMUNITY-BASED SYSTEM OF CARE THAT INTEGRATES INDIGENOUS LANGUAGE, CULTURE, WELLNESS, AND HEALING PATHWAYS. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A SYSTEM OF CARE THAT SERVES YOUTH AGES BIRTH TO 25 RESIDING IN THE JUNEAU AND DOUGLAS COMMUNITIES WHILE STRENGTHENING THE HEALTH AND WELL-BEING OF INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, AND THE BROADER COMMUNITY. THE PROJECT THROUGH THE NEWLY DEVELOPED SOC WILL ENGAGE A MINIMUM OF 210 YOUTH AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS ANNUALLY THROUGH COORDINATED PREVENTION, WELLNESS, AND HEALING SERVICES. GOAL 1:  BY THE END OF THE THREE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, DOUGLAS INDIAN ASSOCIATION AND ITS COLLABORATIVE PARTNERS WILL ESTABLISH AND SUSTAIN A COMPREHENSIVE, CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE SYSTEM OF CARE THAT PROVIDES COORDINATED WELLNESS AND HEALING SERVICES TO AT LEAST 210 PARTICIPANTS ANNUALLY, RESULTING IN INCREASED ACCESS TO CULTURALLY RELEVANT SUPPORTS AND STRENGTHENED COMMUNITY COLLABORATION. OBJECTIVE 1:  WITHIN THE FIRST 3 MONTHS OF THE PROJECT, DOUGLAS INDIAN ASSOCIATION WILL DESIGN AND IMPLEMENT THE PATHWAY FOR A NOBLE GENERATION SYSTEM OF CARE BY CONVENING A COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE AND ADVISORY GROUP THAT INCLUDES PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS, ELDERS, YOUTH, AND COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS. THE GROUP WILL MEET MONTHLY (12 MEETINGS ANNUALLY) TO GUIDE PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION, REVIEW PROGRESS, IDENTIFY EMERGING COMMUNITY NEEDS, AND MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT. OBJECTIVE 2:  EACH PROJECT YEAR, DOUGLAS INDIAN ASSOCIATION WILL IMPLEMENT A COORDINATED CAPACITY-BUILDING PLAN THAT PROVIDES PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE TRAINING TO AT LEAST 40 SERVICE PROVIDERS AND PARTNER STAFF ANNUALLY AND 15 ATTENDING THE TRIBAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT CONFERENCE, INCREASING PARTNER CAPACITY TO RESPOND EFFECTIVELY TO THE WELLNESS NEEDS OF YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND THE COMMUNITY. OBJECTIVE 3:  DURING EACH PROJECT YEAR, DOUGLAS INDIAN ASSOCIATION WILL PARTNER WITH THE NATIVE WELLNESS INSTITUTE TO FACILITATE ONE ANNUAL GATHERING OF NATIVE AMERICANS (GONA) SERVING AT LEAST 100 PARTICIPANTS, PROVIDING OPPORTUNITIES FOR COMMUNITY HEALING, CULTURAL CONNECTION, LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT, AND WELLNESS PLANNING. OBJECTIVE 4:  DOUGLAS INDIAN ASSOCIATION WILL IMPLEMENT AND SUSTAIN THE SYSTEM OF CARE APPROACH THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT AND CONTINUE TO COLLABORATE WITH PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS TO SUPPORT YOUTH WELLNESS INTO FUTURE YEARS WITH CONTINUING INTEGRATION OF NEW COLLABORATIVE APPROACHES AND PATHWAYS TO HEALING.  TRAINING WILL CONTINUE TO BE PROVIDED TO CARE PROVIDERS. OBJECTIVE 5:  DEVELOP A WRITTEN BLUEPRINT FOR TRIBAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEM OF CARE EXPECTED OUTCOMES:  SERVE A MINIMUM OF 210 UNDUPLICATED YOUTH, FAMILY MEMBERS, AND COMMUNITY PARTICIPANTS THROUGH CULTURALLY GROUNDED WELLNESS PROGRAMMING IN THE GEOGRAPHIC AREAS OF JUNEAU AND DOUGLAS, ALASKA; TRAIN 40 PROVIDERS AND PARTNER STAFF IN CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE SYSTEM OF CARE PRACTICES; CONVENE 12 COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE AND ADVISORY GROUP MEETINGS TO GUIDE IMPLEMENTATION AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT; HOST ONE ANNUAL GONA ENGAGING AT LEAST 100 PARTICIPANTS; STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS AND ESTABLISH A SUSTAINABLE, CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE SYSTEM OF CARE THAT CONTINUES BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD.

description: PARTNERING FOR OUTREACH, INTERVENTION, NAVIGATION, AND TRANSFORMATION: A MONTGOMERY COUNTY YOUTH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DIVERSION INITIATIVE (PROJECT POINT) - THE ADAMHS BOARD FOR MONTGOMERY COUNTY (MCADAMHS) PROPOSES THE PARTNERING FOR OUTREACH, INTERVENTION, NAVIGATION, AND TRANSFORMATION: A MONTGOMERY COUNTY YOUTH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DIVERSION INITIATIVE (PROJECT POINT) TO INCREASE PROACTIVE IDENTIFICATION OF YOUTH AT RISK OF JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT, TO ENHANCE ACCESS TO TREATMENT AND SUPPORTIVE SERVICES IN ORDER TO STABILIZE YOUTH PRIOR TO JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT, TO STREAMLINE TELECOMMUNICATION PATHWAYS FOR YOUTH NOTIFICATIONS, AND TO FACILITATE CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT AND YOUTH VOICE IN THESE EFFORTS THROUGH DEVELOPMENT OF A COMMUNITY EARLY DIVERSION PLAN AND CONVENING OF AN EARLY DIVERSION COALITION. PROJECT POINT WILL SERVE MONTGOMERY COUNTY, OHIO, (MONT.CO) A GEOGRAPHIC REGION LOCATED IN SOUTHWEST OHIO THAT COVERS APPROXIMATELY 462 SQUARE MILES. THE PROJECT WILL ENGAGE AND OUTREACH TO 700 YOUTH ANNUALLY (3,500 YOUTH OVER THE 5-YEAR GRANT PERIOD) AND WILL ENROLL TO PROVIDE TREATMENT, SUPPORTIVE SERVICES, AND EARLY DIVERSION PROGRAMMING TO 240 YOUTH ANNUALLY (1,200 YOUTH OVER THE 5-YEAR GRANT PERIOD). PROJECT POINT WILL FOCUS ON YOUTH UNDER THE AGE OF 18, WHO REPRESENT OVER 22% OF THE POPULATION, MOSTLY LIKELY IMPACTING THE ~10% OF THE POPULATION WHO ARE 12 - 18 YEARS OF AGE. IN 2025, THE MONTGOMERY COUNTY JUVENILE COURT SERVED 1,790 YOUTH THROUGH THEIR POST-ARREST INTERVENTION CENTER AND 841 YOUTH THROUGH THEIR JUVENILE DETENTION CENTER. ULTIMATELY, 900 OF THE YOUTH SERVED AT THE INTERVENTION CENTER RECEIVED A BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ASSESSMENT FOR ONGOING SERVICES. THIS POPULATION REPRESENTS A CRITICAL GAP IN SERVICES; A VITAL NEED TO INTERVENE ON BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS BEFORE ARREST OR DETENTION ARE RECOMMENDED. THIS NEED IS ESCALATED BY INCREASED HIGH RISK YOUTH POPULATIONS IN MONT. CO. DESPITE MAKING UP ONLY 4.5% OF OHIO'S POPULATION, MONT. CO. ACCOUNTS FOR 35% OF FOSTER YOUTH GROUP HOMES IN THE STATE. YOUTH IN FOSTER GROUP HOMES OFTEN HAVE EXISTING RISK FACTORS OF MENTAL HEALTH AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS THAT MAY LEAD TO BEHAVIORS THAT PUT THEM AT HIGH RISK OF JUSTICE SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT, ESPECIALLY UNDER THE CONSTANT SURVEILLANCE THAT GROUP HOMES PROVIDE. CURRENT CASE MANAGEMENT AND CARE NAVIGATION SERVICES ARE LIMITED TO MEDICAID POPULATIONS MEETING DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FOR SUPPORT WITH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS, AND MOST MEDIATION RESOURCES ARE GEOGRAPHICALLY LIMITED TO DAYTON, OHIO, LEAVING THE REMAINING COUNTY POPULATION (OF NEARLY 400,000 RESIDENTS) FURTHER UNDERSERVED. PROJECT POINT ENCOMPASSES COMPREHENSIVE STRATEGIES TO TARGET THE POPULATION OF FOCUS, INCLUDING: NON-ARREST LAW ENFORCEMENT INTERACTION FOLLOW-UP, SBIRT, PEER SUPPORT, EARLY DIVERSION PROGRAMMING, FAMILY AND HOUSING-FOCUSED MEDIATION, COMMUNITY IMPACT PANELS, COMMUNITY COALITIONS, AND SHARED STRATEGIC PLANS. THROUGH GOAL 1, PROJECT POINT WILL INCREASE ACCESS TO PEER SUPPORT, COMMUNITY-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TREATMENT, AND MEDIATION-FOCUSED EARLY DIVERSION FOR MONT. CO. YOUTH AT RISK OF ENTERING THE JUVENILE JUSTICE SYSTEM BY INCREASING EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH RISK; PROVIDING TIMELY, EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE RISK BEHAVIORS; AND IMPROVING ACCESS TO APPROPRIATE TREATMENT SERVICES FOR HIGH-RISK YOUTH BY MEASURING THE OBJECTIVES OF SBIRT SCREENINGS (300/YEAR); FOLLOW-UP CALLS TO NON-ARREST LAW ENFORCEMENT-ENGAGED YOUTH (400/YEAR); AND DEMONSTRATING FOR THOSE ENROLLED FURTHER 65% OF YOUTH AVOIDING ARREST 90 DAYS POST-INTERVENTION AND 75% REMAINING ACTIVE IN TREATMENT 90 DAYS POST-INTERVENTION. THROUGH GOAL 2, MCADAMHS WILL IMPROVE CROSS-SYSTEM COORDINATION AND REFERRAL PATHWAYS TO REDUCE RELIANCE ON THE JUVENILE JUSTICE SYSTEM TO ULTIMATELY REDUCE POST-ARREST INTERVENTION CENTER ENGAGEMENTS BY 10% AND JUVENILE DETENTION CENTER ENGAGEMENTS BY 10%. GOAL 3 WILL STRENGTHEN CONTINUITY OF CARE AND FAMILY ENGAGEMENT THROUGH YOUTH CRISIS NOTIFICATION (95% FOLLOW-UP) AND HANDLE WITH CARE TECHNOLOGIES (10 SCHOOLS).

description: DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A SUSTAINABLE CARE PROGRAM DESIGNED AS A NET TO CATCH PEOPLE BEFORE THEY FALL INTO A SEA OF DESPAIR. - THE KNIK TRIBE, A FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBE SERVING DENA'INA ATHABASCAN AND OTHER AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE (AI/AN) PEOPLE ACROSS ALASKA'S MATANUSKA-SUSITNA (MAT-SU) BOROUGH, WILL PLAN AND DESIGN A FAMILY-DRIVEN, YOUTH-GUIDED, COMMUNITY-BASED SYSTEM OF CARE (SOC) FOR AI/AN CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND YOUNG ADULTS FROM BIRTH THROUGH AGE 25 AND THEIR FAMILIES. OVER THREE YEARS, THE TRIBE WILL CONVENE A TRIBAL COMMUNITY BOARD, CONDUCT A TRIBAL SWOT ANALYSIS, HOST ANNUAL GATHERINGS OF ALASKA NATIVES, BUILD CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS, AND PRODUCE A WRITTEN BLUEPRINT FOR A COORDINATED SOC THAT KEEPS AI/AN FAMILIES TOGETHER, CONNECTED TO CULTURE, AND LINKED TO EFFECTIVE MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES. GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT NEEDED. THE PROJECT SERVES THE MAT-SU BOROUGH, A 28,682-SQUARE-MILE REGION OF 29 COMMUNITIES IN SOUTH-CENTRAL ALASKA, HOME TO 14.6% OF THE STATE'S POPULATION. KNIK TRIBE OPERATES A BROAD ARRAY OF CHILD- AND FAMILY-SERVING PROGRAMS BUT LACKS THE COORDINATED INFRASTRUCTURE OF A SYSTEM OF CARE: A GOVERNING BODY WITH AUTHORITY OVER THE SOC, SHARED SCREENING AND REFERRAL PATHWAYS, INTERAGENCY MEMORANDA OF UNDERSTANDING AND DATA-SHARING AGREEMENTS, YOUTH AND FAMILY GOVERNANCE, AND A SUSTAINABILITY AND WORKFORCE PLAN. THIS PROJECT BUILDS THAT CAPACITY. POPULATION OF FOCUS. AI/AN CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND YOUNG ADULTS (BIRTH THROUGH 25) AND THEIR FAMILIES IN THE MAT-SU BOROUGH, WITH PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO FAMILIES INVOLVED WITH, OR AT RISK OF INVOLVEMENT WITH, THE OFFICE OF CHILDREN'S SERVICES — INCLUDING CHILDREN AT RISK OF OUT-OF-HOME PLACEMENT, CHILDREN BEING REUNIFIED WITH THEIR PARENTS, TRANSITION-AGE YOUNG ADULTS (18–25), AND YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AT ELEVATED RISK FOR SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE, SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS, AND SUICIDE. THE TRIBE HAS OVER 1,500 CITIZENS AND SERVES AI/AN FAMILIES ACROSS THE BOROUGH REGARDLESS OF TRIBAL AFFILIATION. THIS IS A PLANNING AND CAPACITY-BUILDING PROJECT; GRANT FUNDS WILL NOT BE USED TO PROVIDE DIRECT CLINICAL TREATMENT SERVICES. CAPACITY-BUILDING STRATEGIES. KNIK TRIBE WILL (1) CONVENE A TRIBAL COMMUNITY BOARD OF TRIBAL OFFICIALS, ELDERS, CHILD-SERVING AGENCIES, PROVIDERS, AND YOUTH AND PARENTS WITH LIVED EXPERIENCE; (2) CONDUCT A TRIBAL SWOT ANALYSIS WITH THE BUTLER INSTITUTE FOR FAMILIES USING ITS NATIONALLY TESTED TRIBAL ORGANIZATIONAL ASSESSMENT; (3) HOST ANNUAL GATHERINGS OF ALASKA NATIVES AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND OUTREACH GROUNDED IN DENA'INA PRACTICE; (4) DEVELOP CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS AND INTERAGENCY AGREEMENTS SPANNING EDUCATION, CHILD WELFARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, LAW ENFORCEMENT AND JUVENILE JUSTICE, AND CRISIS SERVICES INCLUDING THE 988 LIFELINE; AND (5) PRODUCE A WRITTEN SOC BLUEPRINT THROUGH A FACILITATED PATHWAY TO CHANGE PROCESS, INCLUDING FISCAL MAPPING AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT STRATEGIES. PROJECT GOALS. (1) ESTABLISH AND SUSTAIN A TRIBAL COMMUNITY BOARD WITH YOUTH AND FAMILY LEADERSHIP; (2) CONDUCT A TRIBAL SWOT ANALYSIS OF THE TRIBE'S SYSTEM FOR AI/AN CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND YOUNG ADULTS; (3) STRENGTHEN BELONGING, RESILIENCE, AND INTERCONNECTEDNESS AND RAISE COMMUNITY AWARENESS OF MENTAL HEALTH AND THE SOC APPROACH; (4) DEVELOP CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS THAT LET FAMILIES NAVIGATE THE BOROUGH'S SERVICES SEAMLESSLY; AND (5) PRODUCE A WRITTEN BLUEPRINT FOR A COMPREHENSIVE, COMMUNITY-BASED, FAMILY-DRIVEN AND YOUTH-GUIDED SOC. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES. CONVENE THE BOARD (≥15 MEMBERS, ≥3 YOUTH/YOUNG ADULTS AND ≥3 CAREGIVERS IN VOTING SEATS) WITHIN 3 MONTHS; COMPLETE THE SWOT ANALYSIS (≥50 PARTICIPANTS) WITHIN 6 MONTHS; HOST ≥1 GATHERING OF ALASKA NATIVES PER YEAR (≥60 PARTICIPANTS); TRAIN ≥75% OF BOARD ORGANIZATIONS ON THE SOC FRAMEWORK BY END OF YEAR 2; EXECUTE ≥5 CROSS-SYSTEM MOUS BY END OF YEAR 2; AND COMPLETE THE FINAL WRITTEN BLUEPRINT — ADDRESSING SOC GEOGRAPHIC AREA, GOVERNANCE, CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS, OUTREACH/SCREENING/REFERRAL PROCESSES, AND THE SERVICES THE SOC WILL PROVIDE — BY THE END OF YEAR 3.

description: WASHOE COUNTY: BEHAVIORAL HEALTH EARLY DIVERSION PROJECT - WASHOE COUNTY, NEVADA WILL ESTABLISH A COUNTYWIDE PRE-ARREST BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DIVERSION  PATHWAY FOR YOUTH AND ADULTS WITH MENTAL ILLNESS OR CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS.  BUILDING ON THE COUNTY'S SEQUENTIAL INTERCEPT MODEL (SIM), PARTNER AGENCY TEAM (PAT), AND  CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEM, THE PROJECT WILL ADD SCREENING, CARE NAVIGATION, WARM HANDOFFS, TRAINING,  AND PERFORMANCE MONITORING RATHER THAN CREATE PARALLEL STRUCTURES. THE WASHOE COUNTY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH EARLY DIVERSION PROJECT WILL SERVE WASHOE COUNTY,  NEVADA (POPULATION 507,280), INCLUDING RENO-SPARKS AND RURAL COMMUNITIES. IT WILL SERVE 300  UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 1, 450 ANNUALLY IN YEARS 2-5, AND 2,100 TOTAL OVER FIVE YEARS,  CONNECTING THESE INDIVIDUALS TO THE CARE AND SERVICES NEEDED TO SUPPORT DIVERSION FROM JUSTICE  INVOLVEMENT. THE POPULATION SERVED WILL BE YOUTH (UNDER AGE 18) AND ADULTS (AGE 18 AND OLDER)  WITH MENTAL ILLNESS, SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE, OR CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE  USE DISORDERS WHO ARE AT RISK OF CRIMINAL OR JUVENILE JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT. PARTICIPANTS MAY  PRESENT WITH PSYCHIATRIC CRISES, SUICIDAL IDEATION, ALCOHOL- OR DRUG-RELATED CRISES, HOUSING  INSTABILITY, AND UNMET TREATMENT OR SOCIAL-SERVICE NEEDS. VETERANS WILL BE SERVED IN EVERY PROJECT  YEAR THROUGH VETERAN-STATUS SCREENING AND A NAMED REFERRAL PATHWAY. EXISTING DATA ILLUSTRATES STRONG NEED FOR THIS TYPE OF EARLY DIVERSION PATHWAY IN NORTHERN  NEVADA. IN 2025, RENOWN CRISIS CARE CENTER ALONE RECORDED 6,810 CRISIS ENCOUNTERS, INCLUDING  311 ENCOUNTERS (4.6%) THAT ENDED IN JAIL CUSTODY, WHILE THE WASHOE COUNTY MOBILE OUTREACH  SAFETY TEAM (MOST) AVERAGES APPROXIMATELY 2,700-2,800 ANNUAL CRISIS ENCOUNTERS.  THE PROJECT WILL BE IMPLEMENTED THROUGH AN EARLY DIVERSION COALITION BUILT ON THE EXISTING  PAT AND INCLUDING REPRESENTATIVES ACROSS THE COUNTY'S BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND JUSTICE SECTORS SUCH  AS THE WASHOE COUNTY HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY, NORTHERN NEVADA HOPES, QUEST COUNSELING,  VITALITY UNLIMITED, RENOWN CRISIS CARE CENTER, THE SECOND JUDICIAL DISTRICT COURT, THE PUBLIC  DEFENDER'S OFFICE, AND THE WASHOE COUNTY SHERIFF'S OFFICE. PARTNERS WILL CONVENE AT LEAST  QUARTERLY TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT THE EARLY DIVERSION PLAN, WITH KEY ACTIVITIES INCLUDING  EXPANDING SCREENING, CRISIS INTERVENTION, REFERRAL, AND SOCIAL-SERVICE COORDINATION; ENGAGING A RENOWN CASE MANAGER TO STRENGTHEN DISCHARGE PLANNING AND CONNECTIONS TO CARE; AND PROVIDING  TRAINING TO LAW ENFORCEMENT AND COMMUNITY PROVIDERS.  THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE EARLY IDENTIFICATION, ESTABLISH A RELIABLE PRE-ARREST PATHWAY,  STRENGTHEN CROSS-SYSTEM COORDINATION, AND BUILD WORKFORCE AND DATA CAPACITY. AT LEAST 75% OF  ENROLLED PARTICIPANTS WHO CONSENT TO REFERRAL WILL RECEIVE A DOCUMENTED REAL-TIME TRANSFER OR  CONFIRMED INTAKE APPOINTMENT WITHIN SEVEN DAYS. EACH YEAR, THE PROJECT WILL TRAIN AT LEAST 50 LAW  ENFORCEMENT OR DISPATCHER PERSONNEL AND 50 PROVIDERS, OUTREACH STAFF, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS,  WHILE REPORTING REQUIRED SPARS MEASURES AND LOCAL OUTCOMES SUCH AS REFERRAL COMPLETION, TIME  TO SERVICE, AND DIVERSION RATE. THIS DATA WILL ALSO BE USED TO ILLUSTRATE PROGRAM IMPACT, AND, AS  NEEDED, SUPPORT SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING BY SHARING THIS IMPACT WITH POTENTIAL FUTURE FUNDERS.  SUSTAINABILITY IS BUILT INTO THE PROJECT DESIGN. ALL GRANT-FUNDED POSITIONS AND PARTNER  SUBAWARDS WILL BE TERM-LIMITED AND SCALED TO THE FEDERAL AWARD, CREATING NO PERMANENT COUNTY  FTE OR GENERAL-FUND BACKFILL OBLIGATION. EXISTING BASELINE SERVICES WILL CONTINUE INDEPENDENTLY  OF THE GRANT. BY THE END OF YEAR 3, THE COALITION WILL BEGIN IMPLEMENTING A SUSTAINABILITY PLAN  THAT IDENTIFIES WHICH COMPONENTS CAN CONTINUE THROUGH MEDICAID REIMBURSEMENT, THE WASHOE  OPIOID ABATEMENT AND RECOVERY FUND, PHILANTHROPY, OR OTHER NON-FEDERAL SUPPORT AND WHICH  INCREMENTAL ACTIVITIES WILL BE REDUCED, DISCONTINUED, OR SHIFTED TO OTHER AGENCIES IF REPLACEMENT FUNDING IS NOT AVAILABLE.

description: MONTGOMERY COUNTY COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DIVERSION INITIATIVE - MONTGOMERY COUNTY, PENNSYLVANIA, PROPOSES TO IMPLEMENT THE EARLY DIVERSION PROGRAM AND CRISIS CENTER TO DIVERT ADULTS EXPERIENCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES FROM DEEPER CRIMINAL JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT PRIOR TO ARREST OR BOOKING. THROUGH COORDINATED CRISIS INTERVENTION, STABILIZATION, TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, THE PROJECT WILL CONNECT HIGH-RISK ADULTS WHO PRESENT WITH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES, INCLUDING MENTAL HEALTH (MH), SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD), SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS (SMI) AND CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE US DISORDERS (COD) TO COMMUNITY-BASED CARE. THE PROJECT STRENGTHENS PUBLIC SAFETY WHILE REDUCING REPEATED CRISIS-SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT AND IMPROVING ACCESS TO TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORTS. THIS INITIATIVE IS CENTERED ON MONTGOMERY COUNTY'S NEW EMERGENCY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CENTER (EBHC), SCHEDULED TO OPEN IN DECEMBER 2026.   MONTGOMERY COUNTY (MONTCO), WITH A POPULATION OF APPROXIMATELY 861,000, IS LOCATED IN SOUTHEASTERN PENNSYLVANIA AND INCLUDES URBAN, SUBURBAN, AND RURAL COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE ADULTS WHO COME TO THE ATTENTION OF LAW ENFORCEMENT (LE) DURING A BEHAVIORAL HEALTH (BH) CRISIS AND ARE TRANSPORTED FOR CRISIS EVALUATION, WITH A FOCUS ON INDIVIDUALS AT ELEVATED RISK OF REPEATED CRISIS-SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT AND DEEPER CRIMINAL JUSTICE (CJ) INVOLVEMENT. PARTICIPANTS ARE EXPECTED TO EXPERIENCE SMI, COD, HOUSING INSTABILITY, TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, LIMITED SOCIAL SUPPORTS, AND OTHER FACTORS THAT INTERFERE WITH SUSTAINED TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT AND RECOVERY.   THE PROJECT WILL SERVE AN ESTIMATED 200 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 1, INCREASING ANNUALLY TO 230 IN YEAR 2, 260 IN YEAR 3, 290 IN YEAR 4, AND 320 IN YEAR 5, FOR A TOTAL OF 1,300 INDIVIDUALS OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD.   THE PROJECT BUILDS UPON MONTCO’S ESTABLISHED BH, CRISIS RESPONSE, AND DIVERSION INFRASTRUCTURE, INCLUDING MOBILE CRISIS SERVICES, 988, COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CENTERS (CBHCS), RECOVERY SUPPORTS, TREATMENT COURTS, THE MONTCO MODEL, AND THE NEW EBHC. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE: COMMUNITY SYSTEM MAPPING, DEVELOPMENT AND ANNUAL UPDATING OF AN EARLY DIVERSION PLAN, EXPANSION OF DIVERSION-FOCUSED BH SERVICES, COORDINATION OF BH AND SOCIAL-SERVICE SUPPORTS, DIVERSION TRAINING FOR COMMUNITY PARTNERS, OPERATION OF A MULTIDISCIPLINARY EARLY DIVERSION COALITION, AND LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING. THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS WITH CONNECTIONS HEALTH SOLUTIONS, CBHCS, LE AGENCIES, CRISIS PROVIDERS, AND COUNTY BH LEADERSHIP, PARTICIPANTS WILL RECEIVE CRISIS ASSESSMENT, STABILIZATION, TREATMENT LINKAGE, CARE COORDINATION AND RECOVERY-SUPPORT SERVICES. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) DIVERT INDIVIDUALS EXPERIENCING BH CRISES FROM DEEPER CJ INVOLVEMENT PRIOR TO ARREST OR BOOKING; (2) REDUCE REPEAT CRISIS-SYSTEM AND CJ INVOLVEMENT THROUGH TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT, CARE COORDINATION, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT; AND (3) STRENGTHEN COORDINATION AND SUSTAINABILITY ACROSS MONTCO’S BH, CRISIS-RESPONSE, LE, AND COMMUNITY-SERVICE SYSTEMS. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE INCREASING THE ANNUAL NUMBER OF INDIVIDUALS RECEIVING EARLY DIVERSION SERVICES, INCREASING CRISIS ASSESSMENT, STABILIZATION, REFERRAL, AND LINKAGE TO COMMUNITY-BASED TREATMENT AND SUPPORTS, IMPROVING TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT AND RETENTION, AND MAINTAINING A COUNTYWIDE COALITION THAT SUPPORTS DIVERSION PLANNING, IMPLEMENTATION, QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND SUSTAINABILITY.

description: EAST TEXAS YOUTH CRISIS OUTREACH TEAM - UNDER THE PROJECT “EAST TEXAS YOUTH CRISIS OUTREACH TEAM,” ANDREWS CENTER WILL ESTABLISH A REGIONAL EARLY DIVERSION COALITION AND YOUTH CRISIS OUTREACH TEAM (YCOT) TO IDENTIFY YOUTH EXPERIENCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES, CONNECT THEM TO COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES, AND STRENGTHEN COLLABORATION AMONG BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, HEALTHCARE, EDUCATION, AND JUVENILE JUSTICE PARTNERS TO REDUCE UNNECESSARY JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT AND IMPROVE YOUTH OUTCOMES. ANDREWS CENTER, A LOCAL MENTAL HEALTH AUTHORITY (LMHA) IN EAST TEXAS, SERVES THE REGION OF HENDERSON COUNTY, TEXAS; RAINS COUNTY, TEXAS; SMITH COUNTY, TEXAS; VAN ZANDT COUNTY, TEXAS; AND WOOD COUNTY, TEXAS. BASED ON UNITED STATES CENSUS ESTIMATES (AS OF JULY 1, 2026) FOR 2025, THE POPULATIONS FOR THE FIVE-COUNTY SERVICE AREA ARE AS FOLLOWS: HENDERSON COUNTY, 88,595; RAINS COUNTY, 13,54; SMITH COUNTY, 252,549; VAN ZANDT COUNTY, 66,130; AND WOOD COUNTY, 49,688. THE TOTAL POPULATION FOR THE FIVE-COUNTY SERVICE AREA IS 470,504. ANTICIPATED NUMBER OF YOUTH TO BE SERVED FOR THE FIRST YEAR IS 458, WITH A 5% COMPOUNDING ANNUAL INCREASE OVER THE LIFETIME OF THE PROJECT. OVER THE 5-YEAR PERIOD, THE ANTICIPATED NUMBER OF YOUTH TO BE SERVED IS 2,531. IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE TEXAS HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES (HHS) ELIGIBILITY DEFINITION OF THE PROPOSED YCOT AND RELATED SERVICES, THE PLANNED AGE RANGE FOR SERVICES FROM GRANT ACTIVITIES IS YOUTH AGES THREE TO 17 YEARS OLD. [1] BASED ON CURRENT CLIENT AGE DISTRIBUTION AND COMMUNITY NEEDS, THE EXPECTED AGE DISTRIBUTION FOR THE POPULATION PLANNED TO BE SERVED IS APPROXIMATELY 1% AGES 3-5, 26% AGES 6-11, AND 73% AGES 12-17. CONSISTENT WITH HHS ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR YCOT SERVICES, THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL SERVE YOUTH EXPERIENCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES OR OTHER FACTORS THAT INCREASE THEIR RISK OF CRISIS, FAMILY DISRUPTION, OR INVOLVEMENT WITH CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS. THIS INCLUDES YOUTH EXPERIENCING FAMILY INSTABILITY, CHILD WELFARE INVOLVEMENT, SCHOOL-RELATED CHALLENGES, TRAUMA EXPOSURE, EMERGING MENTAL HEALTH CONCERNS, REPEATED PSYCHIATRIC HOSPITALIZATION, RISK OF JUVENILE JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT PRIOR TO ARREST OR BOOKING, REPEATED SCHOOL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH REFERRALS, OR ELIGIBILITY FOR THE YOUTH EMPOWERMENT SERVICES (YES) WAIVER. [1] STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS OF THE PROPOSAL INCLUDE IMPLEMENTATION OF A 24-HOUR YCOT, WITH COMPLETE SERVICES INCLUDING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ASSESSMENT, CASE MANAGEMENT, EVIDENCE-BASED PSYCHOTHERAPY, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT AND EDUCATION, CRISIS INTERVENTION, CARE COORDINATION, AND REFERRAL TO APPROPRIATE COMMUNITY-BASED MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT SERVICES. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL BUILD UPON THE SMITH COUNTY SEQUENTIAL INTERCEPT MODEL (SIM) INITIATIVE BY CONDUCTING AN EARLY DIVERSION-FOCUSED SIM REFRESH TO IDENTIFY SERVICE GAPS, STRENGTHEN REFERRAL PATHWAYS, AND ESTABLISH STRATEGIC PRIORITIES FOR IMPLEMENTING A COORDINATED REGIONAL EARLY DIVERSION SYSTEM. GUIDED BY THE EARLY DIVERSION COALITION, THESE FINDINGS WILL INFORM THE IMPLEMENTATION OF A YOUTH CRISIS OUTREACH TEAM (YCOT) TAILORED TO THE FIVE-COUNTY SERVICE AREA. THE PROJECT AIMS TO IMPROVE EARLY IDENTIFICATION, CARE COORDINATION, AND ACCESS TO COMMUNITY-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES FOR YOUTH EXPERIENCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES, REDUCING UNNECESSARY PSYCHIATRIC HOSPITALIZATION, EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT UTILIZATION, AND JUVENILE JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT THROUGH YCOT, CASE MANAGEMENT, EVIDENCE-BASED PSYCHOTHERAPY, AND FAMILY ENGAGEMENT. SUCCESS WILL BE MEASURED THROUGH THE NUMBER OF PEOPLE SERVED, DIVERSION RATES, TIMELY REFERRALS TO SERVICES, REDUCTIONS IN REPEAT CRISIS UTILIZATION, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, COALITION DEVELOPMENT, AND SATISFACTION.

description: TUNICA-BILOXI CIRCLES OF CARE - PROJECT NAME: TUNICA-BILOXI CIRCLES OF CARE GEOGRAPHIC AREA: CATCHMENT AREA - AVOYELLES AND RAPIDES PARISH PROJECT SUMMARY: THE TUNICA-BILOXI CIRCLES OF CARE PROJECT WILL CREATE A COMPREHENSIVE TRIBAL SYSTEM OF CARE FOR TRIBAL YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS, AND THEIR CHILDREN THAT SUFFER FROM BEHAVIORAL AND/OR MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO TO EDUCATE AND TRAIN TRIBAL EMPLOYEES AND PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR MENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TREATMENT IN USING CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE SERVICES WHEN TREATING NATIVE AMERICAN YOUTH THAT INVOLVE BOTH CULTURALLY-BASED PRACTICES WITH WESTERN EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES IN CREATING A COHESIVE SYSTEM OF CARE THAT IS COMMUNITY DRIVEN.   POPULATION OF FOCUS: TRIBAL YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 24 AND UNDER.  STRATEGIES: DEVELOPMENT OF A TRIBAL SYSTEM OF CARE MODEL THAT INCLUDES A SYSTEM OF CARE BOARD AND TRIBAL SYSTEM BLUEPRINT TO IMPROVE CARE COORDINATION OF BEHAVIORAL/MENTAL HEALTHCARE SERVICE WITH INTERNAL AND LOCAL PARTNERS,EXPAND PARTNERSHIP AND COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT IN SERVICE DELIVERY, AND EDUCATE TREATMENT PROVIDERS ON CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE SERVICE DELIVERY.  GOAL – 1 INCREASE THE TUNICA-BILOXI HEALTH DEPARTMENT CAPACITY TO DELIVER A COORDINATED NETWORK OF EFFECTIVE MENTAL HEALTH AND ESSENTIAL SUPPORTIVE SERVICES ORGANIZED TO ADDRESS AND MEET THE VARIED NEEDS OF CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND YOUNG ADULTS (BIRTH THROUGH AGE 25), AND THEIR FAMILIES- OBJECTIVE 1 CONDUCT 12 SYSTEM OF CARE BARD MEETINGS ANNUALLY GOAL – 2 DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT AND TRACK ORGANIZATIONAL CHANGES THAT INCLUDE COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT AND CULTURAL INCLUSION CONCERNING TREATMENT POLICIES -  OBJECTIVE 2 MAKE 12 POLICY/PROCEDURE CHANGES TO IMPROVE SYSTEM COORDINATION.  GOAL -3 INCREASE THE NUMBER OF PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS PROVIDING BEHAVIORAL AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES TO TRIBAL YOUTH AND THEIR FAMILIES BY CONDUCTING INTENSE OUTREACH, PLANNING, AND NETWORKING ACTIVITIES. OBJECTIVE 3 - ADD 12 ADDITIONAL PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS.  GOAL – 4 DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A TRAINING PROGRAM FOR BEHAVIORAL/MENTAL HEALTH PROFESSIONALS (BOTH TRIBAL AND PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS) ON PROVIDING CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE SERVICES TO TRIBAL YOUTH. OBJECTIVE 4 - TRAIN 36 BEHAVIORAL/MENTAL HEALTH PROFESSIONAL IN PROVIDING CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE SERVICES.
