description: KEETOOWAH HEALING CIRCLE: CHILDREN'S SYSTEM OF CARE INITIATIVE - THE KEETOOWAH HEALING CIRCLE CHILDREN’S SYSTEM OF CARE INITIATIVE IS A THREE-YEAR CIRCLES OF CARE PLANNING AND INFRASTRUCTURE-DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LED BY THE UNITED KEETOOWAH BAND OF CHEROKEE INDIANS IN OKLAHOMA. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE TRIBE’S CAPACITY TO ESTABLISH A SUSTAINABLE, FAMILY-DRIVEN, YOUTH-GUIDED, COMMUNITY-BASED, AND CULTURALLY GROUNDED CHILDREN’S SYSTEM OF CARE. GRANT ACTIVITIES WILL SERVE THE TRIBE’S PRIMARY NORTHEASTERN OKLAHOMA SERVICE AREA: CHEROKEE, ADAIR, DELAWARE, MAYES, AND SEQUOYAH COUNTIES. THE INITIATIVE RESPONDS TO SIGNIFICANT RURAL ACCESS BARRIERS, BEHAVIORAL-HEALTH WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, LIMITED TRANSPORTATION AND BROADBAND CONNECTIVITY, POVERTY AND FOOD INSECURITY, FRAGMENTED CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS, AND THE ABSENCE OF SHARED TRIBAL GOVERNANCE, COORDINATED SCREENING AND REFERRAL PATHWAYS, FORMAL CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS, AND A WRITTEN SYSTEM-OF-CARE BLUEPRINT. CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT WILL FOCUS ON CREATING THE GOVERNANCE, PARTNERSHIP, DATA, OUTREACH, SCREENING, REFERRAL, AND SUSTAINABILITY INFRASTRUCTURE NEEDED TO CONNECT TRIBAL CHILD-SERVING PROGRAMS, SCHOOLS, CHILD WELFARE, CHILDCARE AND EARLY-LEARNING PROVIDERS, FAMILIES, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS KEETOOWAH AND OTHER AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND YOUNG ADULTS FROM BIRTH THROUGH AGE 25, ALONG WITH THEIR FAMILIES AND CAREGIVERS, RESIDING IN THE FIVE-COUNTY SERVICE AREA. THE PROJECT WILL PRIORITIZE THE NEEDS OF INFANTS AND YOUNG CHILDREN PARTICIPATING IN TRIBAL CHILDCARE AND EARLY-LEARNING PROGRAMS; SCHOOL-AGE CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS; TRANSITION-AGE YOUTH; CHILDREN INVOLVED WITH CHILD WELFARE; AND YOUTH EXPERIENCING OR AT RISK FOR EMOTIONAL, BEHAVIORAL, SUBSTANCE-USE, TRAUMA-RELATED, OR SUICIDE-RELATED CONCERNS. ALTHOUGH THIS PLANNING GRANT DOES NOT FUND DIRECT CLINICAL TREATMENT, OUTREACH, SCREENING, REFERRAL, AND COMMUNITY-ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES WILL BE AVAILABLE TO ALL CHILDREN AND FAMILIES SERVED BY THE TRIBE, WITHOUT RACIAL PREFERENCE. THE PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT THE REQUIRED CIRCLES OF CARE ACTIVITIES BY CONVENING A TRIBAL COMMUNITY BOARD; CONDUCTING A TRIBAL SWOT ANALYSIS OF UNMET NEEDS, EXISTING RESOURCES, AND SERVICE GAPS; HOSTING A GATHERING OF NATIVE AMERICANS (GONA); FORMALIZING CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS; AND DEVELOPING A WRITTEN SYSTEM-OF-CARE BLUEPRINT. ALLOWABLE CAPACITY-BUILDING ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE CULTURALLY GROUNDED MENTAL HEALTH OUTREACH AND LITERACY EDUCATION; COMMUNITY LISTENING AND PLANNING SESSIONS; YOUTH AND CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT; CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE CREATE-TO-COPE ACTIVITIES INVOLVING ELDERS, CULTURE BEARERS, LANGUAGE, TRADITIONAL ARTS, AND INTERGENERATIONAL LEARNING; AND DEVELOPMENT OF COORDINATED SCREENING, REFERRAL, INFORMATION-SHARING, AND SUSTAINABILITY PROCEDURES. THE INITIATIVE WILL ENGAGE ECHOTA BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, UKB INDIAN CHILD WELFARE, THE HENRY LEE DOUBLEHEAD CHILD DEVELOPMENT CENTER, SCHOOLS, TRIBAL LEADERSHIP, ELDERS, CAREGIVERS WITH LIVED EXPERIENCE, YOUTH, AND OTHER COMMUNITY PARTNERS. THE PROJECT GOAL IS TO BUILD THE TRIBAL INFRASTRUCTURE, GOVERNANCE, PARTNERSHIPS, AND CULTURAL FOUNDATION NECESSARY FOR A SUSTAINABLE SYSTEM OF CARE SO THAT EVERY KEETOOWAH CHILD AND YOUTH HAS THE OPPORTUNITY TO BE SEEN, SCREENED, AND SUPPORTED. BY SEPTEMBER 29, 2029, THE TRIBE WILL PRODUCE AND ADOPT ONE WRITTEN SYSTEM-OF-CARE BLUEPRINT DEFINING THE SERVICE AREA, GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE, PARTNER ROLES, CULTURALLY GROUNDED OUTREACH APPROACH, CROSS-PROGRAM SCREENING AND REFERRAL PATHWAYS, AND SUSTAINABILITY PLAN. ADDITIONAL MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE CONVENING A TRIBAL COMMUNITY BOARD OF AT LEAST EIGHT MEMBERS THAT MEETS AT LEAST 12 TIMES ANNUALLY; COMPLETING A TRIBAL SWOT ANALYSIS WITHIN SIX MONTHS; ENGAGING AT LEAST 100 COMMUNITY MEMBERS THROUGH A GONA BY THE END OF YEAR 1; SECURING AT LEAST THREE FORMAL PARTNERSHIP OR DATA-SHARING AGREEMENTS BY THE END OF YEAR 2; AND CONDUCTING AT LEAST 12 CULTURALLY GROUNDED OUTREACH ACTIVITIES ANNUALLY.

description: SICANGU OYATE CIRCLES OF CARE INITIATIVE - THE ROSEBUD SIOUX TRIBE HEALTH ADMINISTRATION (RSTHA) PROPOSES THE SICANGU OYATE CIRCLES OF CARE INITIATIVE, A THREE-YEAR COMMUNITY-DRIVEN PLANNING PROJECT TO DEVELOP A CULTURALLY GROUNDED, COMPREHENSIVE SYSTEM OF CARE (SOC) FOR AMERICAN INDIAN CHILDREN, YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS (BIRTH THROUGH AGE 25), AND THEIR FAMILIES ACROSS THE ROSEBUD RESERVATION. GUIDED BY LAKOTA VALUES AND THE TRIBE'S VISION OF PROVIDING ACCESSIBLE, RELATIVE-CENTERED, SPIRITUALLY ADAPTIVE HEALTHCARE, THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN COORDINATION AMONG BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, PRIMARY CARE, EDUCATION, CHILD WELFARE, JUVENILE JUSTICE, PUBLIC HEALTH, FAMILY SERVICES, AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS TO IMPROVE ACCESS TO MENTAL HEALTH PROMOTION, PREVENTION, EARLY IDENTIFICATION, AND COORDINATED SYSTEMS OF SUPPORT. THE ROSEBUD SIOUX TRIBE HAS MADE SUBSTANTIAL INVESTMENTS IN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE THROUGH ITS 638 HEALTH SYSTEM, WICONI WAKAN HEALTH AND HEALING CENTER, ALCOHOL AND DRUG TREATMENT PROGRAM, SOCIAL DETOXIFICATION PROGRAM, YOUTH SHELTER, SUICIDE PREVENTION INITIATIVES, PUBLIC HEALTH EXPANSION, AND NUMEROUS FEDERALLY FUNDED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND PUBLIC HEALTH PROGRAMS. BUILDING UPON THESE EXISTING RESOURCES, THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON PLANNING AND SYSTEMS DEVELOPMENT RATHER THAN DIRECT CLINICAL SERVICES. THE INITIATIVE WILL IDENTIFY SERVICE GAPS, STRENGTHEN COLLABORATION AMONG AGENCIES, AND ESTABLISH SUSTAINABLE GOVERNANCE STRUCTURES THAT SUPPORT COORDINATED CARE FOR CHILDREN, YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS, AND FAMILIES. RSTHA WILL ESTABLISH A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TRIBAL COMMUNITY BOARD REPRESENTING TRIBAL LEADERSHIP, YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS, PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS, ELDERS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, SCHOOLS, INDIAN HEALTH SERVICE, TRIBAL PROGRAMS, JUSTICE PARTNERS, HOUSING, PUBLIC HEALTH, AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS. THE BOARD WILL GUIDE COMPLETION OF A COMPREHENSIVE TRIBAL STRENGTHS, WEAKNESSES, OPPORTUNITIES, AND THREATS (SWOT) ANALYSIS, OVERSEE A COMMUNITY-BASED GATHERING OF NATIVE AMERICANS (GONA), AND DEVELOP A STRATEGIC BLUEPRINT FOR IMPLEMENTING A SUSTAINABLE TRIBAL SYSTEM OF CARE. COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT WILL INTEGRATE LAKOTA CULTURE, LANGUAGE, TRADITIONAL TEACHINGS, AND FAMILY-CENTERED DECISION MAKING THROUGHOUT THE PLANNING PROCESS. YOUTH, FAMILIES WITH LIVED EXPERIENCE, ELDERS, AND CULTURAL LEADERS WILL PLAY MEANINGFUL LEADERSHIP ROLES IN IDENTIFYING PRIORITIES, DESIGNING REFERRAL PATHWAYS, IMPROVING OUTREACH AND ENGAGEMENT, AND ENSURING THAT THE FUTURE SYSTEM OF CARE REFLECTS COMMUNITY STRENGTHS AND CULTURAL VALUES. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS WITH ORGANIZATIONS INCLUDING MASSACHUSETTS GENERAL HOSPITAL'S RURAL MEDICINE PROGRAM, AVERA HEALTH, INDIAN HEALTH SERVICE, LOCAL SCHOOL DISTRICTS, TRIBAL COURTS, TRIBAL SOCIAL SERVICES, PUBLIC HEALTH, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, AND OTHER CHILD-SERVING AGENCIES. THESE PARTNERSHIPS WILL SUPPORT DATA-INFORMED PLANNING, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, SYSTEMS INTEGRATION, AND LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY WHILE ENHANCING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED AND CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SUPPORTS. BY THE CONCLUSION OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, THE ROSEBUD SIOUX TRIBE WILL PRODUCE A COMPREHENSIVE SYSTEM OF CARE BLUEPRINT THAT ESTABLISHES GOVERNANCE, DEFINES COORDINATED SCREENING, REFERRAL, AND CARE PATHWAYS, IDENTIFIES SUSTAINABLE FINANCING STRATEGIES, FORMALIZES CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS, AND POSITIONS THE TRIBE FOR FUTURE IMPLEMENTATION FUNDING. THIS PLANNING EFFORT WILL CREATE THE FOUNDATION FOR A COORDINATED, FAMILY-DRIVEN, YOUTH-GUIDED, CULTURALLY GROUNDED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEM THAT IMPROVES OUTCOMES FOR SICANGU CHILDREN, YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS, AND THEIR FAMILIES WHILE STRENGTHENING THE TRIBE'S CAPACITY TO ADDRESS BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS FOR GENERATIONS TO COME.

description: RESILIENT ROOTS NC: STRENGTHENING SYSTEMS, SUPPORTING FAMILIES - CHILDREN'S HOME SOCIETY OF NORTH CAROLINA (CHSNC) WILL IMPLEMENT RESILIENT ROOTS NC: STRENGTHENING SYSTEMS, SUPPORTING FAMILIES, A FIVE-YEAR INITIATIVE EXPANDING INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) SERVICES FOR CHILDREN IN OR AT RISK OF CHILD WELFARE INVOLVEMENT. CHSNC WILL TRAIN THE EARLY CHILDHOOD WORKFORCE STATEWIDE, EXPAND CHILD FIRST DYADIC TREATMENT FOR CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH FIVE IN SEVEN COUNTIES, AND ADD IECMH CONSULTATION WITH STATEWIDE ACCESS TO IMPROVE EARLY SYSTEMS OF CARE. TRAINING AND CONSULTATION ARE AVAILABLE TO THE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD WORKFORCE, INCLUDING MENTAL HEALTH CLINICIANS AND OTHER ADULTS WHO CARE FOR INFANTS AND YOUNG CHILDREN, ACROSS NORTH CAROLINA'S 100 COUNTIES AND POPULATION OF 11,197,968. DIRECT CLINICAL SERVICES COVER THE MECKLENBURG REGION (MECKLENBURG, CABARRUS, AND ROWAN COUNTIES) AND THE TRIANGLE REGION (DURHAM, WAKE, ORANGE, AND JOHNSTON COUNTIES). FOUR NEW CHILD FIRST TEAMS WILL SERVE 290 UNDUPLICATED CHILDREN WITH AWARD FUNDS.  DIRECT SERVICES REACH CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE FIVE AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. TRAINING AND CONSULTATION EXTEND THE PROJECT'S REACH TO CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE 12 THROUGH THE PROFESSIONALS, CAREGIVERS, AND CLINICIANS WHO SERVE THEM. CHILDREN SERVED EXPERIENCE OR ARE AT RISK FOR SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL AND BEHAVIORAL DIFFICULTIES RANGING FROM EARLY DYSREGULATION IDENTIFIED THROUGH SCREENING TO DIAGNOSABLE CONDITIONS, INCLUDING SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE, REQUIRING EARLY-CHILDHOOD-SPECIFIC ASSESSMENT AND TREATMENT. FAMILIES RECEIVING CHILD FIRST SERVICES DEMONSTRATE MEDICAID ELIGIBILITY AND MEET CLINICAL CRITERIA, INDICATING LOW-INCOME HOUSEHOLDS. CHSNC WILL DELIVER VIRTUAL LIVE TRAINING STATEWIDE USING COMPLEX TRAUMA TRAINING CONSORTIUM (CTTC) CURRICULA, FOR WHICH CHSNC IS NORTH CAROLINA'S SOLE REGIONAL LEAD SITE, AND WILL DEVELOP ORIGINAL IECMH CURRICULA FOR THE CHILD WELFARE-ADJACENT WORKFORCE AND FOR LICENSED CLINICIANS. CHSNC WILL EXPAND CHILD FIRST, AN EVIDENCE-BASED HOME-BASED DYADIC MODEL DELIVERED THROUGH A CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY APPROACH, FROM FOUR TO EIGHT TEAMS. A NEWLY HIRED EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH COACH WILL DELIVER IECMH CONSULTATION TO PROGRAMS, TEAMS, AND INDIVIDUAL CONSULTEES. GOAL 1 EXPANDS THE CAPACITY OF NORTH CAROLINA'S CHILD WELFARE-ADJACENT WORKFORCE AND MENTAL HEALTH CLINICIANS STATEWIDE TO IDENTIFY AND RESPOND TO IECMH NEEDS AMONG CHILDREN AGES 0-12. CHSNC WILL DELIVER A MINIMUM OF 300 VIRTUAL LIVE TRAININGS AND BUILD A PERMANENT ON-DEMAND DIGITAL TRAINING LIBRARY REACHING 25 TRAINING COURSES BY THE END OF YEAR 5. ANNUALLY, 85 PERCENT OF SURVEYED TRAINEES WILL DEMONSTRATE INCREASED KNOWLEDGE, AND 60 PERCENT WILL REPORT IMPLEMENTING TRAINING CONTENT AT THREE MONTHS. GOAL 2 EXPANDS ACCESS TO IECMH INTERVENTION STATEWIDE AND DIRECTLY THROUGH CHILD FIRST. CHSNC WILL HIRE AND TRAIN FOUR NEW TEAMS IN YEAR 1, BUILDING CASELOADS OF 12 TO 16 FAMILIES PER TEAM BY THE END OF YEAR 2. ALL EIGHT TEAMS WILL SERVE 630 UNDUPLICATED FAMILIES BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, MEETING MODEL BENCHMARKS OF 60 PERCENT OF FAMILY-IDENTIFIED NEEDS MET AND 75 PERCENT OF DISCHARGED FAMILIES DEMONSTRATING IMPROVEMENT. THE EXPANDED WORKFORCE WILL BE SUSTAINED BY MEDICAID. GOAL 3 ENHANCES THE QUALITY, REACH, AND COORDINATION OF IECMH SERVICE DELIVERY STATEWIDE THROUGH CONSULTATION, STRENGTHENING EARLY SYSTEMS OF CARE. CHSNC WILL HIRE AN EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH COACH BY MONTH 7, WITH CONSULTATION OPERATIONAL BY MONTH 9, AND BOTH THE PROJECT DIRECTOR AND THE COACH WILL COMPLETE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE IECMHC CERTIFICATE TRAINING. CONSULTATION WILL REACH AT LEAST 8 ADULTS WHO CARE FOR INFANTS AND YOUNG CHILDREN IN YEAR 1 AND AT LEAST 20 IN EACH OF YEARS 2 THROUGH 5, FOR AT LEAST 88 OVER THE PROJECT PERIOD.

description: METROCARE'S INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH PROGRAM - METROCARE SERVICES WILL IMPLEMENT THE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) PROGRAM TO ADDRESS SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL NEEDS FOR CHILDREN AGES 0-12 IN DALLAS COUNTY, TEXAS. BY INTEGRATING UNIVERSAL SCREENING, EVIDENCE-BASED DYADIC THERAPIES AND SPECIALIZED CONSULTATION, THE PROJECT WILL SERVE 750 CHILDREN AND CAREGIVERS OVER FIVE YEARS. THIS INITIATIVE EXPANDS WORKFORCE CAPACITY AND IMPROVES RELATIONAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR CHILDREN WITH SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCES (SED). POPULATION AND SERVICE AREA: THE PROGRAM TARGETS INFANTS AND CHILDREN (BIRTH TO AGE 12) IN DALLAS COUNTY WHO ARE AT RISK FOR OR DIAGNOSED WITH MENTAL ILLNESS, INCLUDING SED. METROCARE EXPECTS TO SERVE 750 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS OVER THE GRANT TERM, WITH ANNUAL TARGETS INCREASING FROM 50 IN YEAR 1 TO 250 IN YEAR 5. PARTICIPANTS ARE IDENTIFIED THROUGH CLINICAL ASSESSMENTS AS HAVING HIGH NEEDS, SPECIFICALLY LEVEL OF CARE 4 (LOC-4) OR EQUIVALENT.  STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS: METROCARE WILL EMPLOY A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM, INCLUDING A QUALIFIED MENTAL HEALTH PROFESSIONAL (QMHP) AND FAMILY PARTNER, WITH INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION PROVIDED BY THE PROJECT DIRECTOR, TO IMPLEMENT: • UNIVERSAL SCREENING: STANDARDIZED ASSESSMENT USING THE AGES AND STAGES QUESTIONNAIRE (ASQ) FOR AGES 0-3 AND THE CHILD AND ADOLESCENT NEEDS AND STRENGTHS (CANS) FOR AGES 3-12. • EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES (EBPS): DELIVERY OF CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY (CPP) AND PARENT-CHILD INTERACTION THERAPY (PCIT) TO STRENGTHEN CAREGIVER-CHILD RELATIONSHIPS. • CAPACITY BUILDING: SPECIALIZED WORKFORCE TRAINING FOR CLINICAL STAFF AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS THROUGH THE COMMUNITY RESOURCE COORDINATION GROUP (CRCG).  GOALS AND MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: • GOAL 1: TIMELY IDENTIFICATION. SCREEN 90% OF CHILDREN AT INTAKE AND REFER 80% OF THOSE WITH LOC-4 NEEDS TO THE PROGRAM WITHIN 14 DAYS. • GOAL 2: EXPANDED ACCESS. ENSURE 60% OF REFERRED FAMILIES INITIATE SERVICES WITHIN 14 DAYS AND 40% OF CHILDREN SHOW IMPROVED SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL FUNCTIONING WITHIN SIX MONTHS. • GOAL 3: RELATIONAL HEALTH. PROVIDE DYADIC OR CAREGIVER-FOCUSED INTERVENTIONS TO 85% OF ENROLLEES, AND REDUCE ACTIONABLE CAREGIVER NEEDS ON THE CANS FOR 40% OF PARTICIPANTS. • GOAL 4: WORKFORCE CAPACITY. DELIVER IECMH-FOCUSED TRAINING TO AT LEAST 40 MEMBERS OF THE EARLY CHILDHOOD WORKFORCE ANNUALLY.

description: EARLY CONNECTIONS: EXPANDING INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH IN THE LOWCOUNTRY AND BEYOND - EARLY CONNECTIONS WILL EXPAND ACCESS TO INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) SERVICES ACROSS SOUTH CAROLINA'S LOWCOUNTRY BY INCREASING SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, TREATMENT, CONSULTATION, AND WORKFORCE TRAINING. THROUGH INTEGRATED TRAINING, CLINICAL SERVICES, CONSULTATION, AND COORDINATED REFERRALS, EARLY CONNECTIONS WILL IMPROVE OUTCOMES FOR YOUNG CHILDREN AND FAMILIES WHILE ADVANCING SAMHSA PRIORITIES IN PREVENTION, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, ACCESS TO CARE, AND RESILIENCE.   OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, SCIMHA EXPECTS TO SERVE APPROXIMATELY 2,529 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS, SPECIFICALLY CHILDREN AGES 0–5 AND THEIR CAREGIVERS ACROSS BERKELEY, BEAUFORT, CHARLESTON, AND DORCHESTER COUNTIES IN SOUTH CAROLINA. IT WILL OFFER WARMLINE CONSULTATION AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES STATEWIDE. THE FOCUS IS ON CHILDREN WITH DEVELOPMENTAL, BEHAVIORAL, SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL, OR RELATIONSHIP ISSUES; FAMILIES FACING POVERTY, ADVERSE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES (ACES), INVOLVEMENT WITH CHILD WELFARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROBLEMS, OR LIMITED SERVICE ACCESS; AND FAMILIES WHO ARE MEDICAID-ENROLLED, UNDERINSURED, RURAL, OR UNDERSERVED.    OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, SCIMHA EXPECTS TO SERVE APPROXIMATELY 2,529 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS THROUGH WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT, TREATMENT, AND CONSULTATION ACTIVITIES. THIS INCLUDES APPROXIMATELY 440 PROFESSIONALS PARTICIPATING IN WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES, 1,661 CHILDREN RECEIVING SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT SERVICES, 68 CHILDREN AND FAMILIES RECEIVING DIRECT IECMH TREATMENT, AND 360 CAREGIVERS AND PROFESSIONALS RECEIVING CONSULTATION SERVICES.   THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON FOUR MAIN ACTIVITIES. FIRST, SCIMHA WILL INCREASE WORKFORCE CAPACITY BY PROVIDING TRAINING THROUGH THE IECMH FOUNDATIONS CERTIFICATE, IECMH CLINICAL CERTIFICATE, DC:0–5 TRAINING, AND CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY (CPP). SECOND, HELP ME GROW SOUTH CAROLINA (HMG) WILL BE ENHANCED AS THE PRIMARY RESOURCE FOR DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING, CARE COORDINATION, REFERRALS, AND SERVICE NAVIGATION. THIRD, SCIMHA WILL BROADEN DIRECT CLINICAL SERVICES BY ADDING AN IECMH CLINICIAN TO CONDUCT ASSESSMENTS, DYADIC TREATMENT, CAREGIVER SUPPORT, AND BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS. FINALLY, SCIMHA WILL INTRODUCE A STATEWIDE WARMLINE CONSULTATION SERVICE TO OFFER PROMPT SUPPORT TO CAREGIVERS AND PROFESSIONALS CARING FOR YOUNG CHILDREN.    PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) STRENGTHEN WORKFORCE CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT IECMH BEST PRACTICES; (2) EXPAND ACCESS TO SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, AND REFERRAL SERVICES; (3) EXPAND MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT AND CONSULTATION SERVICES; AND (4) IMPROVE CHILD AND FAMILY OUTCOMES THROUGH COORDINATED, SUSTAINABLE SUPPORTS. KEY OBJECTIVES INCLUDE TRAINING 75 GRANT-SUPPORTED PROFESSIONALS THROUGH THE IECMH FOUNDATIONS CERTIFICATE, TRAINING 100 PROFESSIONALS THROUGH THE IECMH CLINICAL CERTIFICATE, PROVIDING DC:0–5 TRAINING TO APPROXIMATELY 250 ADDITIONAL PROFESSIONALS, INCREASING DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING BY 20% ANNUALLY, EXPANDING ASSESSMENT CAPACITY TO 50 ASSESSMENTS ANNUALLY BY YEAR 4, SERVING AT LEAST 100 CHILDREN AND FAMILIES THROUGH TREATMENT SERVICES, AND PROVIDING STATEWIDE WARMLINE CONSULTATION. OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE IMPROVED CHILD SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL FUNCTIONING, DECREASED CAREGIVER STRESS, INCREASED CAREGIVER CONFIDENCE, AND STRENGTHENED ACCESS TO INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH SUPPORTS.

description: WAH-ZHA-ZHE YOUTH SYSTEM OF CARE PLANNING INITIATIVE - OSAGE NATION SI-SI A-PE-TXA RESPECTFULLY REQUESTS $350,000 ANNUALLY FOR THREE YEARS THROUGH THE SUBSTANCE ABUSE AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ADMINISTRATION (SAMHSA) CIRCLES OF CARE FOR AMERICAN INDIAN/ALASKA NATIVES (AI/AN) PROGRAM TO DEVELOP THE WAH-ZHA-ZHE YOUTH SYSTEM OF CARE PLANNING INITIATIVE. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH THE INFRASTRUCTURE, PARTNERSHIPS, GOVERNANCE, AND STRATEGIC FRAMEWORK NECESSARY TO DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE, CULTURALLY GROUNDED, FAMILY-DRIVEN, YOUTH-GUIDED SYSTEM OF CARE (SOC) THAT IMPROVES COORDINATION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES FOR AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE (AI/AN) CHILDREN, YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS (BIRTH THROUGH AGE 25), AND THEIR FAMILIES THROUGHOUT THE OSAGE NATION SERVICE AREA.  OSAGE NATION SI-SI A-PE-TXA PROVIDES INTEGRATED HEALTHCARE SERVICES, INCLUDING PRIMARY CARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, DENTAL CARE, SPECIALTY MEDICAL SERVICES, PREVENTIVE HEALTH PROGRAMS, AND COMMUNITY OUTREACH. DESPITE THESE RESOURCES, SIGNIFICANT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISPARITIES REMAIN. CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND FAMILIES CONTINUE TO EXPERIENCE FRAGMENTED SYSTEMS OF CARE, LIMITED COORDINATION AMONG CHILD-SERVING AGENCIES, TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, AND INCONSISTENT ACCESS TO CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE TRIBE'S CAPACITY TO ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES THROUGH COLLABORATIVE PLANNING, MEANINGFUL COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, AND DEVELOPMENT OF A SUSTAINABLE SYSTEM OF CARE THAT REFLECTS THE CULTURAL VALUES AND PRIORITIES OF THE OSAGE PEOPLE.  THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A TRIBAL COMMUNITY BOARD COMPOSED OF REPRESENTATIVES FROM HEALTHCARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, EDUCATION, CHILD WELFARE, JUVENILE JUSTICE, TRIBAL LEADERSHIP, YOUTH, FAMILIES, ELDERS, AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS TO GUIDE ALL PLANNING ACTIVITIES. A WAH-ZHA-ZHE YOUTH COUNCIL WILL ENSURE THAT YOUTH VOICES REMAIN CENTRAL TO PROJECT PLANNING AND DECISION-MAKING, WHILE ELDERS AND CULTURAL CONSULTANTS WILL PROVIDE TRADITIONAL KNOWLEDGE AND GUIDANCE TO ENSURE THAT ALL ACTIVITIES ARE CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE AND GROUNDED IN OSAGE TRADITIONS.  PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE COMPLETION OF A COMPREHENSIVE TRIBAL STRENGTHS, WEAKNESSES, OPPORTUNITIES, AND THREATS (SWOT) ANALYSIS, IMPLEMENTATION OF THE COMMUNITY READINESS MODEL (CRM), COMMUNITY LISTENING SESSIONS, STAKEHOLDER SURVEYS, INTERVIEWS, FOCUS GROUPS, RESOURCE MAPPING, AND A GATHERING OF NATIVE AMERICANS (GONA). THESE ACTIVITIES WILL IDENTIFY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH STRENGTHS, SERVICE GAPS, BARRIERS TO CARE, AND OPPORTUNITIES TO STRENGTHEN COORDINATION AMONG HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, SCHOOLS, JUVENILE JUSTICE, CHILD WELFARE, TRIBAL DEPARTMENTS, AND OTHER CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS.  FINDINGS FROM THESE PLANNING ACTIVITIES WILL INFORM DEVELOPMENT OF A COMPREHENSIVE SYSTEM OF CARE BLUEPRINT THAT ESTABLISHES A ROADMAP FOR FUTURE IMPLEMENTATION. THE BLUEPRINT WILL DEFINE GOVERNANCE STRUCTURES, CROSS-SYSTEM COLLABORATION STRATEGIES, REFERRAL PATHWAYS, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES, CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE PRACTICES, YOUTH AND FAMILY ENGAGEMENT STRATEGIES, FINANCING APPROACHES, AND LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY RECOMMENDATIONS DESIGNED TO IMPROVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR AI/AN CHILDREN, YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS, AND FAMILIES.

description: THE UTAH YOUTH EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS EARLY DIVERSION INITIATIVE (YEHDI) PROGRAM DIVERTS HOMELESS YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS FROM JUSTICE SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT INTO COMMUNITY-BASED PROGRAMS. - THE UTAH DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, OFFICE OF SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL HEALTH (SUMH) PROPOSES TO IMPLEMENT THE YOUTH EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS EARLY DIVERSION INITIATIVE (YEHDI). THIS PROGRAM WILL PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS TO DIVERT SALT LAKE COUNTY (SLCO) YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS EXPERIENCING, OR AT IMMINENT RISK OF, HOMELESSNESS AWAY FROM THE JUVENILE OR CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM PRIOR TO ARREST OR BOOKING AND INTO COMMUNITY-BASED RESOURCES THAT WILL ADDRESS THEIR MENTAL ILLNESS OR CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS. THE PROJECT DIRECTORS WILL ESTABLISH AND LEAD AN EARLY DIVERSION COALITION TO DEVELOP, STRENGTHEN, AND IMPLEMENT CROSS-SYSTEM STRATEGIES TO DIVERT INDIVIDUALS FROM ARREST AND BOOKING INTO COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES. SERVICES PROVIDED WILL INCLUDE: CASE MANAGEMENT, OUTREACH TO INDIVIDUALS AT RISK FOR CRIMINAL OR JUVENILE JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT, CRISIS ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION, BRIEF INTERVENTIONS TO FACILITATE CARE, AND INDIVIDUAL THERAPY. REFERRAL TO LONG-TERM SERVICES WILL INCLUDE: ASSERTIVE COMMUNITY TREATMENT, MEDICATION MANAGEMENT ACCESS, INTEGRATED MENTAL HEALTH AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDER TREATMENT, PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, PSYCHIATRIC REHABILITATION, SUPPORTED EMPLOYMENT SERVICES, ASSISTANCE WITH ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING. THE GEOGRAPHIC AREA TO BE SERVED WILL BE SLCO (POP 1,240,937); YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS (POP 148,052). THE PROGRAM INTENDS TO SERVE 175/YEAR, 875 TOTAL SERVED OVER FIVE YEARS. THE POPULATION SERVED WILL BE AGES 15 TO 22 IN SLCO WHO MEET PROGRAM CRITERIA. STATEWIDE REFERRALS TO JUVENILE COURT OCCUR AT A RATE OF 3.28 YOUTH PER 100 YOUTHS, YET IN SLCO THAT INCREASES TO 29.5 YOUTH PER 100 YOUTHS. DATA SUBMITTED TO SUMH DEMONSTRATES THAT OF CLIENTS SERVED IN THE PUBLIC MENTAL HEALTH SYSTEM IN SLCO, 55% AGES 14 TO 17, 41% AGES 18-21, AND 43% AGES 21-25 EXPERIENCE SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE OR SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS. SLCO DATA ALSO SHOWS THAT FOR THE 3,440 YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 15 TO 22 WHO RECEIVED MENTAL HEALTH OR CO-OCCURRING DISORDER SERVICES, 36% WERE HOMELESS, IN JAIL, PARTICIPATING IN DRUG COURT, OR WERE REFERRED FROM JUSTICE SERVICES. YOUNG PEOPLE EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS HAVE HIGHER RATES OF MENTAL ILLNESS AND SUBSTANCE USE, AND HIGHER RATES OF INVOLVEMENT IN THE JUVENILE AND CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEMS.   GOALS AND OBJECTIVES:  GOAL 1: IMPROVE ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES FOR 875 YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS (175/YEAR), WHO ARE SCREENED AND MEET CRITERIA FOR THE YEHDI PROGRAM. OBJECTIVES: GOALS ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH (A) BUILDING A SUSTAINABLE COALITION OF SERVICE PROVIDERS ACROSS BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, JUSTICE, HOUSING, AND EMPLOYMENT. (B) REFERRING YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS TO LONG-TERM SERVICES IN THE COMMUNITY BASED ON THEIR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS (C) FOLLOW-UP WITH YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AT 30, 60, AND 90 DAYS AFTER REFERRAL TO LONG-TERM SERVICES TO ASSESS IMPROVEMENT IN ACCESS TO CARE. GOAL 2: FACILITATE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TRAINING TO STAFF MEMBERS IN AT LEAST 125 (25/YEAR) COMMUNITY-BASED OR STAKEHOLDER ORGANIZATIONS ANNUALLY, WITH TRAININGS FOCUSED ON DIVERSION, YOUTH EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS, IDENTIFYING MENTAL ILLNESS AND CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, MENTAL HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, SUICIDE PREVENTION, AND CRISIS RESPONSE. OBJECTIVES: GOALS ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH (A) QUARTERLY EDUCATION WEBINARS (B) QUARTERLY COALITION MEETINGS (C) MONTHLY RESOURCE NEWSLETTER (D) TARGETED WEBINAR TRAINING TO SPECIFIC GROUPS AND ORGANIZATIONS IDENTIFIED IN COALITION MEETINGS (E) COLLECTED ATTENDANCE DATA FOR EACH TRAINING. GOAL 3: INCREASE THE NUMBER OF YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS WHO ARE DIVERTED FROM JUVENILE AND CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEMS. OBJECTIVES: GOAL ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH (A) FOLLOW-UP SURVEY AT 30, 60, 90 DAYS AFTER REFERRAL TO LONG-TERM SERVICES (SELF-REPORT) (B) HOMELESS MANAGEMENT INFORMATION SYSTEM REPORTS TO MEASURE ENGAGEMENT IN HOMELESS SERVICE SYSTEMS (C) INCREASED REFERRALS FROM CRISIS SYSTEMS TO DIVERSION AND LONG-TERM SERVICES.

description: OTTAWA COUNTY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DIVERSION INITIATIVE - THE OTTAWA COUNTY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DIVERSION INITIATIVE WILL EXPAND PRE ARREST BEHAVIORAL HEALTH STABILIZATION TO REDUCE JUSTICE SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT AND IMPROVE CRISIS RESPONSE. COMPRISED OF 308,459 RESIDENTS, THE INITIATIVE STRENGTHENS COUNTYWIDE DIVERSION PATHWAYS BY CONDUCTING SEQUENTIAL INTERCEPT MAPPING, DEVELOPING AN EARLY DIVERSION PLAN, AND INCREASING COORDINATED REFERRALS FROM LAW ENFORCEMENT, EMERGENCY SERVICES, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS. THE PROJECT AIMS TO DIVERT AT LEAST 75% OF ENCOUNTERS FROM ARREST, ENSURE RAPID FOLLOW UP WITHIN 72 HOURS, AND REDUCE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH RELATED EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT USE BY 20%. description: DEVELOPING RESILIENCE AND WELL-BEING (DRAW) - DEVELOPING RESILIENCE AND WELL-BEING (DRAW), A PROGRAM OF LUK CRISIS CENTER, INC. (LUK), WILL PROVIDE SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, DIAGNOSIS, MENTAL HEALTH PROMOTION AND INTERVENTION SERVICES FOR INFANTS AND YOUNG CHILDREN (IYC), AGES 0-12, AND THEIR FAMILIES. TO RAISE AWARENESS OF MENTAL HEALTH NEEDS OF IYC AND AVAILABLE SERVICES, WE WILL ALSO PROVIDE TRAINING TO THE IYC WORKFORCE INCLUDING MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, AND SUPPLEMENT TRAINING WITH INDIVIDUALIZED CONSULTATIONS.   DRAW WILL SERVE IYC AND THEIR CAREGIVERS IN WORCESTER COUNTY, MASSACHUSETTS. 113,404 CHILDREN UNDER THE AGE OF 12 RESIDE IN THE SERVICE AREA (US CENSUS, 2020-2024 AMERICAN COMMUNITY SURVEY, 5-YEAR ESTIMATES). CHILD TRENDS (2026) REPORTED THAT 32% OF CHILDREN IN MASSACHUSETTS HAVE EXPERIENCED AT LEAST ONE ACE (AN ESTIMATED 36,289 CHILDREN UNDER AGE 12 IN WORCESTER COUNTY). COMMON CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDE BEHAVIORAL DISTURBANCES (E.G., NON-COMPLIANCE, AGGRESSION), AND DYSREGULATION (E.G., TANTRUMS, CRYING/WHINING). THE MOST COMMON DIAGNOSES INCLUDE TRAUMA AND STRESSOR-RELATED, ADJUSTMENT, ANXIETY, RELATIONAL, AND REGULATORY DISORDERS.  DRAW’S GOALS ARE: (1) TO INCREASE ADULTS’ (PROFESSIONALS AND FAMILY) KNOWLEDGE OF TRAUMA SYMPTOMS IN IYC AND WHEN TO REFER FOR ADDITIONAL SERVICES, (2) TO INCREASE REFERRALS OF IYC IN NEED OF EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENT, (3) TO IMPROVE THE FUNCTIONING OF IYC IMPACTED BY TRAUMA AND THE FUNCTIONING OF THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND (4) TO IMPROVE THE SKILLS OF EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATION (ECE) PROVIDERS TO MANAGE IYC WITH TRAUMA AND OTHER STRESSORS/SYMPTOMS. DRAW WILL UTILIZE THE FOLLOWING EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENTS: ATTACHMENT, REGULATION, AND COMPETENCY (ARC); A CAREGIVER ADAPTATION OF ARC CALLED ARC GROW; AND PARENT-CHILD INTERACTION THERAPY (PCIT). CONSULTATION COMPETENCIES FROM THE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE FOR INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH WILL ALSO BE UTILIZED.  EACH YEAR, DRAW PLANS TO SCREEN 150 IYC, WITH ADDITIONAL ASSESSMENTS AND DIAGNOSES FOR 75 IYC ANNUALLY. EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT WILL BE PROVIDED TO 50 IYC AND THEIR FAMILIES ANNUALLY. OVER THE 5-YEAR PROJECT, WE WILL SCREEN 750 IYC, PROVIDE ASSESSMENT AND DIAGNOSES TO 375 IYC, AND PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT TO 250 IYC AND THEIR FAMILIES. WE ALSO PLAN TO TRAIN 150 ADULTS WHO CARE FOR IYC EACH YEAR (E.G., MEDICAL PROFESSIONALS, CHILDCARE PROVIDERS, MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS) FOR A TOTAL OF 750 TRAINED OVER THE 5-YEAR PROJECT, WITH CONSULTATION PROVIDED TO 10 EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATORS EACH YEAR, FOR A TOTAL OF 50 OVER THE 5-YEAR PROJECT.  DRAW’S PROPOSED OBJECTIVES INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING:  - BY THE END OF THE 5-YEAR PROJECT, 75% OF TRAINING PARTICIPANTS WILL REPORT INCREASED ABILITY TO IDENTIFY AND REFER THE POPULATION OF FOCUS; - BY DISCHARGE, 75% OF FAMILIES WILL BE STRENGTHENED: TO IMPROVE CHILDREN’S SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SKILLS AND FUNCTIONING, TO ENHANCE CAREGIVER-CHILD INTERACTIONS, AND TO DECREASE CHILDREN’S STRESSORS; AND - BY THE END OF 5-YEAR PROJECT, 75% OF ECE PROVIDERS ENGAGED IN CONSULTATION WILL REPORT AN IMPROVEMENT IN INDIVIDUAL SKILLS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

description: CHILDREN'S RESEARCH TRIANGLE'S STRENGTHENING INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH THROUGH TRAUMA-INFORMED INTEGRATED SERVICES - CHILDREN'S RESEARCH TRIANGLE'S (CRT) STRENGTHENING INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH THROUGH TRAUMA-INFORMED INTEGRATED SERVICES (IECMH) BUILDS SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL DEVELOPMENT, PROVIDING EVIDENCE-BASED SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, EVALUATION, TREATMENT, CRISIS CARE, AND CAREGIVER EDUCATION TO 900+ LOW-INCOME CHICAGO-AREA CHILDREN (BIRTH-12) WITH/AT RISK FOR SED, AND FAMILIES. IECMH WILL TRAIN 500 PROFESSIONALS AND CONSULT FOR 10 COMMUNITY AGENCIES. SERVICE AREA & POPULATION. IECMH PRIMARILY BENEFITS THE CHICAGO METROPOLITAN AREA, WITH 70% OF SERVICES DELIVERED AT NINE SCHOOLS AND SOCIAL SERVICE AGENCIES IN SOUTH AND WEST SIDE NEIGHBORHOODS IMPACTED BY HIGH POVERTY RATES AND WORKFORCE SHORTAGES. IECMH ALSO PROVIDES SERVICES IN ITS LOOP CLINIC AND VIA TELEHEALTH. OF THE 1,166 CLIENTS CRT SERVED IN 2025, 570 WERE AGED BIRTH–12, WITH A PROJECTED GRANT SERVICE DISTRIBUTION OF 35% INFANTS AND PRESCHOOLERS (AGES 0–5) AND 65% SCHOOL-AGED YOUTH (AGES 6–12). CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS. CRT'S POPULATION PRESENTS WITH NEGLECT; PHYSICAL, SEXUAL OR EMOTIONAL ABUSE; CAREGIVER SEPARATION; BEREAVEMENT; DOMESTIC/COMMUNITY VIOLENCE; FOOD/HOUSING INSTABILITY; PRENATAL SUBSTANCE EXPOSURE; PARENTAL INCARCERATION; DISABILITY; AND HOUSEHOLD MENTAL ILLNESS. THE MAJORITY (96%) HAVE EXPERIENCED TRAUMA AND 10% ARE IN THE CHILD WELFARE SYSTEM. DIAGNOSES INCLUDE DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, PTSD, NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DIFFERENCES, DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOR DISORDERS, AND PSYCHOSIS. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS. IECMH DELIVERS PREVENTION AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROMOTION; EVIDENCE-BASED SCREENING/ASSESSMENT AND MULTIDISCIPLINARY EVALUATION; EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT (CPP, TF-CBT, PCIT, THERAPLAY, EMDR); CRISIS INTERVENTION SERVICES; CAREGIVER EDUCATION (STEP, CIRCLE OF SECURITY PARENTING); CASE MANAGEMENT/FAMILY ENGAGEMENT; INFANT/EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION; AND WORKFORCE TRAINING. IT SUSTAINS GAINS POST-TREATMENT THROUGH ONGOING DEVELOPMENTAL GUIDANCE AND REFLECTIVE CONSULTATION. PROJECT GOALS. (1) INCREASE PROFESSIONAL AWARENESS OF DIAGNOSTIC/TREATMENT ISSUES FOR SED; (2) INCREASE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF CHILDREN AT RISK FOR SED VIA EVIDENCE-BASED SCREENING; (3) INCREASE AVAILABILITY OF COMPREHENSIVE EVALUATIONS TO IDENTIFY CLINICAL NEEDS; (4) DECREASE PARENT-CHILD RELATIONSHIP RISK FACTORS; (5) INCREASE ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT; (6) INCREASE COMPETENCY OF COMMUNITY-BASED CLINICIANS; (7) MAINTAIN A HIGH QUALITY STANDARD OF CARE; AND (8) ENGAGE AND EMPOWER PARENTS/CAREGIVERS IN DECISION-MAKING.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES. (1) TRAIN 100 PROFESSIONALS ANNUALLY (500/TERM) TO INCREASE AWARENESS OF DIAGNOSTIC AND TREATMENT ISSUES FOR CHILDREN WITH OR AT RISK FOR SED, WITH 80% ACHIEVING INCREASED KNOWLEDGE. (2) SCREEN 150 CHILDREN/CAREGIVERS ANNUALLY (750/TERM) USING EVIDENCE-BASED TOOLS TO INCREASE IDENTIFICATION OF AT-RISK YOUTH, TRACKING 100% OF REFERRAL SOURCES. (3) COMPLETE COMPREHENSIVE PSYCHOLOGICAL EVALUATIONS FOR 25 CHILDREN ANNUALLY (125/TERM), ENSURING 100% RECEIVE TREATMENT PLANS AND 70% FOLLOW THROUGH WITHIN 9 MONTHS. (4) ENROLL 15 CAREGIVERS ANNUALLY (75/TERM) IN STEP/COSP TO DECREASE PARENT-CHILD RELATIONSHIP RISK FACTORS, WITH 80% DEMONSTRATING IMPROVED PARENTING SKILLS.(5) PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT TO 70 CHILDREN/CAREGIVERS ANNUALLY (350/TERM), INCLUDING CRISIS INTERVENTION SERVICES, WITH 80% IMPROVING ON STANDARDIZED OUTCOME MEASURES. (6) PARTNER WITH TWO AGENCIES ANNUALLY (10/TERM) TO INCREASE COMMUNITY CLINICIAN COMPETENCY, WITH 80% OF STAFF IMPROVING ON THE GOAL ACHIEVEMENT SCALE. (7) MAINTAIN HIGH CARE STANDARDS BY SECURING 80% TREATMENT FIDELITY AND 100% CLINICAL SUPERVISION. (8) ENGAGE AND EMPOWER CAREGIVERS TRANSPARENTLY BY PROTECTING PARENTAL RIGHTS, CONTACTING FAMILIES WITHIN 10 DAYS OF REFERRAL, AND ENSURING 80% REPORT THAT THEIR FEEDBACK IS VALUED.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: BUTTE RESILIENCE INITIATIVE (BRI) - THE BUTTE RESILIENCE INITIATIVE (BRI) WILL TRANSFORM A DECADE OF DISASTER-DRIVEN, REACTIVE TRAUMA RESPONSES INTO A PERMANENT, SUSTAINABLE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEM EMBEDDED DIRECTLY IN BUTTE COUNTY, CALIFORNIA SCHOOLS. LED BY BUTTE COUNTY OFFICE OF EDUCATION (BCOE), IN PARTNERSHIP WITH INNOVATIVE STRATEGIES GROUP (ISG) AND FEATHER RIVER TRIBAL HEALTH (FRTH), BRI WILL SEED-FUND THE INSTALLATION OF LICENSED/ASSOCIATE CLINICIANS ON CAMPUS AT 30 SCHOOL SITES ACROSS 9 LOCAL EDUCATIONAL AGENCIES (LEAS) AND ENHANCE SCHOOL CAPACITY TO MANAGE THEIR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEMS.  USING ISG'S SCHOOL WELLNESS INTEGRATION MODEL (SWIM), CLINICAL SERVICES WILL BE INCREASINGLY BILLED TO MEDI-CAL, ELIMINATING RELIANCE ON GRANT-FUNDING FOR THESE ESSENTIAL POSITIONS AND PROGRAM INFRASTRUCTURE. THROUGH BRI, BUTTE COUNTY'S ECOSYSTEM OF CARE WILL BECOME A PORTABLE PROTOTYPE FOR OTHER DISASTER-AFFLICTED REGIONS TO IMPLEMENT.  BRI WILL SERVE SCHOOLS ACROSS BUTTE COUNTY (POPULATION 209,800), PHASING IN SERVICES OVER FOUR YEARS ACROSS THE 30 SCHOOL SITES, PRIORITIZED BY LEVEL OF NEED, EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE, AND SITE READINESS. THE SERVICE AREA SPANS MOUNTAIN (PARADISE), FOOTHILL/TOWN (OROVILLE, GRIDLEY, THERMALITO), AND RURAL/REMOTE (PALERMO, GOLDEN FEATHER, PIONEER) COMMUNITIES. THE ESTIMATED NUMBER OF K-12 STUDENTS AND STAFF SERVED WILL BE 3,688 IN YEAR 1, 5,859 IN YEAR 2, 8,821 IN YEAR 3, AND 10,698 IN YEAR 4, FOR A CUMULATIVE TOTAL OF 29,066 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS SERVED.  THE POPULATION TO BE SERVED CARRIES A DISPROPORTIONATE, CUMULATIVE TRAUMA BURDEN: HALF OF COUNTY STUDENTS REPORT CHRONIC SADNESS OR HOPELESSNESS (VS. 37% STATEWIDE), AND THE COUNTY'S SUICIDE DEATH RATE IS 60% HIGHER THAN THE STATE AVERAGE; THESE BURDENS OCCUR AGAINST A BACKDROP OF PHYSICIAN SHORTAGES AND RURAL ACCESS BARRIERS THAT LEAVE MOST OF THESE NEEDS UNIDENTIFIED AND UNTREATED. BRI ADDRESSES THIS THROUGH IMPLEMENTING SWIM, WHICH USES A MULTI-TIERED SYSTEM OF SUPPORT (MTSS) FRAMEWORK TO SUSTAIN TRAUMA-INFORMED MENTAL HEALTH CARE IN SCHOOLS: TIER 1 UNIVERSAL SCREENING AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL LEARNING (SEL) PROGRAMMING; TIER 2 CERTIFIED WELLNESS COACHES PROVIDING MENTORING, CASE MANAGEMENT, AND GROUP SUPPORT; AND TIER 3 CLINICIANS, EMBEDDED THROUGH THE FRTH PARTNERSHIP, DELIVERING EVIDENCE-BASED DIRECT TREATMENT. CAMPUS-BASED COORDINATION OF SERVICES TEAMS (COST) AND UNIVERSAL REFERRAL SYSTEMS INTEGRATE IDENTIFICATION, REFERRAL, AND SERVICE DELIVERY AT EVERY SITE, WHILE MEDI-CAL BILLING AND CALIFORNIA'S CHILDREN AND YOUTH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INITIATIVE MULTI-PAYER FEE SCHEDULE SUSTAIN SERVICES FOR ALL STUDENTS BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD.  BRI IS GUIDED BY FIVE GOALS: 1) BUILDING LEA CAPACITY FOR AN INTEGRATED, SUSTAINABLE TRAUMA-INFORMED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEM; 2) IMPLEMENTING SCHOOL-BASED TRAUMA SUPPORT AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES AT 30 SCHOOLS TO INCREASE ACCESS AND UTILIZATION; 3) ENGAGING FAMILIES, SCHOOL PERSONNEL, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO SOLICIT COMMUNITY VOICE, BUILD AWARENESS AND ENSURE RESPONSIVE SERVICE COORDINATION; 4) IMPLEMENTING A RIGOROUS EVALUATION SYSTEM TO MONITOR FIDELITY AND ASSESS OUTCOMES; AND 5) SUSTAINING THE SYSTEM OF CARE BEYOND FEDERAL FUNDING. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE EXECUTING PARTNER CONTRACTS; DEVELOPING A TRAIN-THE-TRAINER MODEL FOR CLINICIANS; PLACING AT LEAST 30 CLINICIANS ACROSS 30 SCHOOLS; IMPLEMENTING COST TEAMS AND UNIVERSAL REFERRAL SYSTEMS AT EVERY SITE; TRAINING SCHOOL PERSONNEL, FAMILIES AND PARTNERS; EXECUTING RIGOROUS EVALUATION; ESTABLISHING MEDICAL BILLING FOR SUSTAINED FUNDING; AND DEVELOPING A COMPREHENSIVE SUSTAINABILITY PLAN; OBJECTIVES THAT DIRECTLY ADVANCE SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES TO EXPAND ACCESS TO CRISIS INTERVENTION AND EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT, ADDRESS EMERGING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH THREATS, AND BUILD SYSTEMS THAT SUSTAIN OUTCOMES AFTER THE GRANT PERIOD ENDS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

description: STRONG START MENTAL HEALTH INITIATIVE - MOTIVATION, EDUCATION, AND TRAINING, INC. (MET) PROPOSES STRONG START, A COMPREHENSIVE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) INITIATIVE SERVING CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE 12, THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND EARLY CHILDHOOD PROFESSIONALS IN THE CITY OF WALLER IN NORTHEAST HARRIS COUNTY AND THE FOLLOWING ADDITIONAL COUNTIES: AUSTIN, CHAMBERS, HARDIN, JEFFERSON, LIBERTY, MONTGOMERY, POLK, WALLER, AND WALKER. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES DOCUMENTED SHORTAGES OF IECMH-TRAINED PROFESSIONALS, FRAGMENTED REFERRAL PATHWAYS, TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, AND LIMITED ACCESS TO DEVELOPMENTALLY APPROPRIATE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, CONSULTATION, AND FAMILY SUPPORT SERVICES, PARTICULARLY IN RURAL COMMUNITIES. STRONG START WILL IMPROVE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONCERNS WHILE STRENGTHENING THE REGIONAL IECMH WORKFORCE AND EXPANDING COORDINATED ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-INFORMED MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES.  STRONG STARTT WILL ESTABLISH AN IECMH LEARNING COLLABORATIVE THAT TRAINS 2,000 EARLY CHILDHOOD PROFESSIONALS THROUGH A COMPETENCY-BASED CURRICULUM THAT INTEGRATES IECMH INTO MET'S DEPARTMENT OF LABOR REGISTERED EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATION APPRENTICESHIP. STRONG START WILL ALSO ESTABLISH A REGIONAL SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, AND REFERRAL HUB TO PROVIDE DEVELOPMENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENING FOR 2,500 CHILDREN, ENSURE TIMELY REFERRAL AND FOLLOW-UP FOR CHILDREN REQUIRING ADDITIONAL SERVICES, AND DELIVER CAREGIVER EDUCATION AND EARLY INTERVENTION THROUGH THE NURTURING PARENTING PROGRAM AND WELLNESS ON WHEELS OUTREACH. LICENSED MENTAL HEALTH PROFESSIONALS WILL PROVIDE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION (IECMHC) TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF EARLY CHILDHOOD PROFESSIONALS, PROMOTE HEALTHY CAREGIVER-CHILD RELATIONSHIPS, AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO DEVELOPMENTALLY APPROPRIATE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES.  BY LEVERAGING MET'S EXISTING PROGRAMS, STRONG START WILL STRENGTHEN EXISTING SYSTEMS RATHER THAN DUPLICATE SERVICES. THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE WORKFORCE CAPACITY, INCREASE ACCESS TO EARLY IDENTIFICATION AND REFERRAL, STRENGTHEN CAREGIVER-CHILD RELATIONSHIPS, EXPAND ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, AND CREATE A SUSTAINABLE REGIONAL MODEL THAT IMPROVES BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES THROUGHOUT SOUTHEAST TEXAS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: INFANT AND CHILD NURTURE PROJECT (ICNP) - INTERBOROUGH DEVELOPMENTAL & CONSULTATION CENTER (IDCC) WILL LAUNCH THE INFANT AND CHILD NURTURE PROJECT (ICNP) WITH AN AWARD UNDER THE SAMHSA INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) SM26020 TO CLOSE A DOCUMENTED GAP IN MENTAL HEALTH IDENTIFICATION AND TREATMENT FOR THE YOUNGEST CHILDREN IN BROOKLYN'S LARGEST BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEM, WHILE FORMALIZING EXISTING BUT UNDERUTILIZED TREATMENT CAPACITY FOR SCHOOL-AGE CHILDREN. IN 2025, IDCC SERVED 1,593 CHILDREN AGES 6 TO 12 BUT ONLY 59 CHILDREN UNDER AGE 6, DESPITE THE TARGET POPULATION SPLITTING ALMOST EVENLY BY AGE. THIS INITIATIVE WILL BRING VALIDATED DEVELOPMENTAL SCREENING, EVIDENCE-BASED DYADIC TREATMENT, AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION TO FIVE IDCC CLINICS AND PARTNERED EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION SITES ACROSS KINGS COUNTY, CLOSING THAT GAP AT ITS SOURCE. SERVICES WILL BE DELIVERED THROUGHOUT KINGS COUNTY, NEW YORK, ANCHORED AT CANARSIE COUNSELING CENTER WITH FOUR SATELLITE CLINICS, FLATBUSH, CROWN HEIGHTS, CONEY ISLAND, AND WILLIAMSBURG, AND EXTENDED THROUGH 24 SCHOOL-BASED SITES AND PARTNERED EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION SETTINGS. AN ESTIMATED 436,097 CHILDREN AGES BIRTH TO 12 RESIDE IN KINGS COUNTY, SPLIT NEARLY EVENLY BETWEEN AGES BIRTH TO 5 (207,882) AND AGES 6 TO 12 (228,215). ICNP WILL SERVE 120 UNDUPLICATED CHILDREN IN YEAR 1, GROWING TO 160 ANNUALLY BY YEAR 2, FOR A FIVE-YEAR TOTAL OF 760 CHILDREN SERVED THROUGH GRANT-FUNDED SCREENING, TREATMENT, AND CONSULTATION PATHWAYS.  CHILDREN AGES 6 TO 12 ALREADY SERVED BY IDCC PRESENT MOST FREQUENTLY WITH ADHD, ANXIETY AND TRAUMA-RELATED CONDITIONS, AND DISRUPTIVE OR MOOD DYSREGULATION PRESENTATIONS. CHILDREN BIRTH TO 5 PRESENT MOST FREQUENTLY WITH SEPARATION ANXIETY, ADJUSTMENT DISORDERS, AND EARLY HYPERACTIVITY OR IMPULSIVITY INDICATORS, AN AGE GROUP SUBSTANTIALLY UNDER-IDENTIFIED DUE TO THE ABSENCE OF VALIDATED SCREENING IN IDCC'S CURRENT INTAKE PROCESS.  IDCC WILL IMPLEMENT VALIDATED DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING (ASQ-3, ASQ:SE-2, M-CHAT-R, AND DECA); CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY, AN EVIDENCE-BASED DYADIC TREATMENT MODEL FOR CHILDREN BIRTH TO 5; ATTACHMENT, REGULATION, AND COMPETENCY (ARC), A DYADIC TREATMENT FRAMEWORK ALREADY HELD BY 25 TRAINED IDCC CLINICAL STAFF, FORMALIZED UNDER THIS PROJECT INTO A STRUCTURED 10-PERSON CLINICAL TRACK FOR CHILDREN AGES 6 TO 12; AND WEEKLY PARENTING SUPPORT GROUPS THROUGH THE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION DELIVERED TO PARTNERED EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION SETTINGS. ICNP PURSUES THREE GOALS: INCREASING EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND DEVELOPMENTAL CONCERNS AMONG CHILDREN BIRTH TO 5, ACTIVATING EVIDENCE-BASED DYADIC TREATMENT CAPACITY FOR CHILDREN BIRTH TO 12 AND THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND ESTABLISHING CONSULTATION CAPACITY CONNECTING IDCC TO EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION SETTINGS ACROSS KINGS COUNTY. BY THE END OF YEAR 1, IDCC WILL SCREEN 100% OF NEWLY INTAKING CHILDREN BIRTH TO 5 AT ALL FIVE CLINICS AND DELIVER CPP TREATMENT DIRECTLY TO AT LEAST 20 CAREGIVER-CHILD DYADS. BY MONTH 6 OF YEAR 1, IDCC WILL FORMALIZE ITS 10-PERSON ARC CLINICAL CADRE, AT LEAST TWO PER CLINIC. BY MONTH 9 OF YEAR 1, IDCC WILL ESTABLISH FORMAL CONSULTATION AGREEMENTS WITH AT LEAST THREE EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION PROGRAMS. BY THE END OF YEAR 2, 80% OF CHILDREN WHO SCREEN POSITIVE WILL BE CONNECTED TO TREATMENT WITHIN 30 DAYS. THIS DESIGN REFLECTS SAMHSA'S COMMITMENT TO EVIDENCE-BASED, DATA-DRIVEN PRACTICE AND TO PARENTAL RIGHTS AND FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, WITH TREATMENT PLANS DEVELOPED JOINTLY WITH CAREGIVERS THROUGHOUT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: MONROE COUNTY, NY TISS INITIATIVE - BOCES OF THE SECONDARY SUPERVISORY DISTRICT OF MONROE AND ORLEANS COUNTIES (AKA MONROE 2-ORLEANS BOCES) PROPOSES THE MONROE COUNTY TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICES IN SCHOOLS (TISS) INITIATIVE, A FOUR-YEAR REGIONAL PARTNERSHIP DESIGNED TO INCREASE ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED SUPPORTS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, AND COORDINATED SYSTEMS OF CARE FOR ELEMENTARY-AGED STUDENTS AND FAMILIES IN MONROE COUNTY, NEW YORK. THE INITIATIVE WILL SERVE APPROXIMATELY 1,937 STUDENTS ATTENDING FOUR ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS IN THE GREECE, GATES CHILI, HILTON, AND SPENCERPORT SCHOOL DISTRICTS. MONROE 2-ORLEANS BOCES WILL COORDINATE A SYSTEM OF PREVENTION, INTERVENTION, REFERRAL, TREATMENT ACCESS, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, SUICIDE PREVENTION, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT IN PARTNERSHIP WITH SCHOOLS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS. THE INITIATIVE WILL LEVERAGE THE COMMUNITY SCHOOLS COALITION OF MONROE COUNTY, A COUNTYWIDE NETWORK OF MORE THAN 125 ORGANIZATIONS AND 303 MEMBERS DEDICATED TO IMPROVING OUTCOMES FOR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES.  PARTICIPATING SCHOOLS REPORT SIGNIFICANT LEVELS OF POVERTY, CHRONIC ABSENTEEISM, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONCERNS, HOUSING INSTABILITY, AND BARRIERS TO ACCESSING CARE. CHRONIC ABSENTEEISM RANGES FROM 17% TO 22.8%, SCHOOLS REPORT MORE THAN 1,000 OFFICE DISCIPLINE REFERRALS ANNUALLY, AND LAKESHORE ELEMENTARY DOCUMENTED APPROXIMATELY 190 THREATS OF SELF-HARM OR HARM TO OTHERS DURING THE 2025-2026 SCHOOL YEAR. PANORAMA SEL DATA REVEAL CHALLENGES IN EMOTIONAL REGULATION, SELF-AWARENESS, BELONGING, AND SOCIAL AWARENESS, WHILE DISTRICTS CITE PROVIDER SHORTAGES, TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, STIGMA, FRAGMENTED REFERRAL PATHWAYS, LANGUAGE ACCESS NEEDS, AND LONG WAITLISTS FOR SERVICES. DESPITE THESE CHALLENGES, STUDENTS REPORT STRONG RELATIONSHIPS WITH TRUSTED ADULTS, PROVIDING AN IMPORTANT PROTECTIVE FACTOR UPON WHICH THE INITIATIVE WILL BUILD.  THE INITIATIVE WILL IMPLEMENT AN INTEGRATED COMMUNITY SCHOOLS AND MULTI-TIERED SYSTEM OF SUPPORTS (MTSS) FRAMEWORK COMBINING CHARACTERSTRONG'S PURPOSEFULL PEOPLE CURRICULUM, TRAUMA-RESPONSIVE SYSTEMS DEVELOPMENT THROUGH TINRC/TIG AND TENDING THE ROOTS, RESTORATIVE PRACTICES, FAMILY NAVIGATION, SUICIDE PREVENTION ACTIVITIES, AND SCHOOL-LINKED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PARTNERSHIPS. TIER 2 INTERVENTIONS WILL BE DELIVERED BY CENTER FOR YOUTH SOCIAL LEARNING SPECIALISTS, WHILE TIER 3 SERVICES WILL BE PROVIDED THROUGH COORDINATED REFERRAL PATHWAYS WITH UNIVERSITY OF ROCHESTER MEDICAL CENTER, ROCHESTER REGIONAL HEALTH, AND CHARLIE HEALTH. FAMILY NAVIGATION AND REFERRAL FOLLOW-THROUGH WILL BE SUPPORTED THROUGH THE MYWAYFINDER PLATFORM AND COMMUNITY SCHOOLS INFRASTRUCTURE.  PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) INCREASE ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED MENTAL HEALTH SUPPORTS AND SERVICES; (2) STRENGTHEN TRAUMA-INFORMED MTSS IMPLEMENTATION; AND (3) IMPROVE STUDENT SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL WELLNESS, SCHOOL CLIMATE, ATTENDANCE, AND BEHAVIORAL OUTCOMES. EVALUATION AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT ACTIVITIES WILL BE LED BY DR. ERINN DUPREY AND CHILDREN’S INSTITUTE, UTILIZING A SHARED MEASUREMENT FRAMEWORK THAT TRACKS INDIVIDUALS TRAINED, SCREENED, REFERRED, AND LINKED TO MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES, AS WELL AS STUDENT, FAMILY, AND SCHOOL OUTCOMES. THROUGH COORDINATED IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINABLE SYSTEMS CHANGE, THE INITIATIVE WILL STRENGTHEN SCHOOL-COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PARTNERSHIPS AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO TIMELY, EFFECTIVE SUPPORTS FOR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES ACROSS MONROE COUNTY. THE YEAR 1 FEDERAL REQUEST IS $969,973 WITH A TOTAL FOUR-YEAR FEDERAL REQUEST OF $3,879,891.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: START CORPORATION'S FY26 SAMHSA INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) PROGRAM - PROJECT NAME: START CORPORATION INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH PROGRAM – LOUISIANA REGION 3  START CORPORATION (START) WILL LAUNCH LOUISIANA'S FIRST INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) PROGRAM, SERVING CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE 12 ACROSS REGION 3'S SEVEN-PARISH RIVER AND BAYOU AREA. OVER FIVE YEARS, THE PROJECT WILL SCREEN THOUSANDS OF CHILDREN, DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT, AND EXTEND CONSULTATION TO THE ADULTS WHO CARE FOR THEM, CLOSING LOUISIANA'S ONLY VALIDATED-CARE GAP FOR ITS YOUNGEST RESIDENTS.  GEOGRAPHIC AREA: THE PROJECT SERVES LOUISIANA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH REGION 3 IN ITS ENTIRETY – ASSUMPTION, LAFOURCHE, ST. CHARLES, ST. JAMES, ST. JOHN THE BAPTIST, ST. MARY, AND TERREBONNE PARISHES – ANCHORED BY START'S HOUMA AND THIBODAUX CLINICS, WITH TELEHEALTH AND IN-HOME SERVICE EXTENDING REACH REGION-WIDE.  POPULATION SIZE AND INDIVIDUALS TO BE SERVED: THE SEVEN-PARISH CATCHMENT HAS APPROXIMATELY 380,000 RESIDENTS. START PROJECTS SERVING APPROXIMATELY 680 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 1, SCALING TO APPROXIMATELY 1,040 ANNUALLY BY YEAR 5, FOR A TOTAL OF APPROXIMATELY 4,520 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD.  AGE RANGE AND POPULATION DISTRIBUTION: CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE 12 WHO ARE AT RISK FOR, SHOWING EARLY SIGNS OF, OR DIAGNOSED WITH A MENTAL ILLNESS, INCLUDING SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE (SED), TOGETHER WITH THEIR FAMILIES AND CAREGIVERS, WITH PARTICULAR CONCENTRATION IN THE BIRTH-TO-5 RANGE SERVED THROUGH START'S CLINICS AND HEALTHY START PROGRAM.  CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS: THE POPULATION PRESENTS WITH TRAUMA EXPOSURE, ADVERSE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES, SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL DELAYS, AND DIAGNOSED OR EMERGING SED, WITH EXTENSIVE DCFS SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT. REGIONAL RISK INDICATORS ARE PRONOUNCED – ELEVATED TEEN BIRTH AND LOW-BIRTHWEIGHT RATES, HIGH CAREGIVER DEPRESSION, AND A SEVERE PROVIDER SHORTAGE – AND NO ORGANIZATION IN REGION 3 CURRENTLY OFFERS IECMH-VALIDATED SCREENING OR BIRTH-5 DYADIC TREATMENT.  STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS: START WILL ADOPT DECA FOR BIRTH-5 SCREENING (COMPLEMENTING SEEK, CPSS, AND CALOCUS FOR OLDER CHILDREN), WITH DC:0–5 DIAGNOSTIC CLASSIFICATION FOR BIRTH-5 CHILDREN. CORE EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES ARE TF-CBT, CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY (CPP), AND PARENT-CHILD INTERACTION THERAPY (PCIT), WITH DBT FOR OLDER/CO-OCCURRING CASES, PLUS INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION (IECMHC) FOR ADULTS WHO CARE FOR YOUNG CHILDREN – DELIVERED THROUGH START'S CLINICS, HEALTHY START HOME VISITING, AND DCFS/MY COMMUNITY CARES REFERRAL PATHWAYS UNDER A NO WRONG DOOR MODEL, WITH WORKFORCE TRAINED THROUGH THE LSU EVIDENCE TO PRACTICE COHORT.  PROJECT GOALS: (1) INCREASE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF IECMH CONCERNS THROUGH VALIDATED SCREENING; (2) BUILD A WORKFORCE CREDENTIALED IN EVIDENCE-BASED IECMH PROMOTION, INTERVENTION, AND CONSULTATION; (3) DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED DYADIC/INDIVIDUAL TREATMENT; AND (4) EXTEND IECMHC TO CAREGIVERS OF YOUNG CHILDREN.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: SCREEN 250 CHILDREN VIA DECA WITHIN 6 MONTHS, SCALING TO ~800 ANNUALLY BY YEAR 5; TRAIN 3 CLINICIANS EACH IN CPP/PCIT AND 2 IN DBT WITHIN 4 MONTHS; SERVE 40 CHILDREN IN YEAR 1, REACHING 60-120 ANNUALLY FROM YEAR 2; AND PROVIDE IECMHC TO 80 STAFF WITHIN 9 MONTHS, EXPANDING TO DCFS AND HOME VISITORS THEREAFTER, ALIGNED WITH SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES OF GOLD-STANDARD SCIENCE/DATA AND ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY SERVICES FOR ALL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: PROJECT TEND — TRAINING, ENGAGEMENT, AND NURTURING DEVELOPMENTBUILDING AN IECMH SYSTEM OF CARE AND WORKFORCE INITIATIVE IN MA - PROJECT TEND WILL BUILD AN INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) SYSTEM OF CARE IN MA, UNITING A FRAGMENTED CONTINUUM OF SERVICES INTO ONE COORDINATED PATHWAY FOR YOUNG CHILDREN AND FAMILIES. PROJECT TEND WILL IDENTIFY AND TREAT MENTAL ILLNESS IN THE DEVELOPMENTAL WINDOW WHEN INTERVENTION WORKS BEST—PREVENTING EARLY DIFFICULTIES FROM PROGRESSING INTO SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS, SUBSTANCE USE, AND CHRONIC DISEASE IN ADULTHOOD. GEOGRAPHIC AREA. MASSACHUSETTS, CONCENTRATED IN HIGH-NEED, UNDER-RESOURCED COMMUNITIES—WORCESTER, NEW BEDFORD, LYNN, LAWRENCE, HOLYOKE, CHELSEA, LOWELL, EVERETT, HAVERHILL, AND BOSTON—AND UNDERSERVED RURAL AREAS OF WESTERN MASSACHUSETTS.  POPULATION SIZE & NUMBER SERVED. MASSACHUSETTS HAS A POPULATION OF 7,136,171, OF WHOM 4.9% (APPROXIMATELY 349,700) ARE CHILDREN UNDER AGE FIVE AND 19.2% (APPROXIMATELY 1,370,100) ARE UNDER 18 (U.S. CENSUS BUREAU, QUICKFACTS, V2024). THE PROJECT'S TARGET COMMUNITIES CARRY SUBSTANTIALLY HIGHER CONCENTRATIONS OF YOUNG CHILDREN THAN THE STATE AS A WHOLE—7.8% OF RESIDENTS ARE UNDER FIVE IN CHELSEA AND LAWRENCE. STATEWIDE, 11.1% OF CHILDREN LIVE IN POVERTY AND 8,564 WERE IN FOSTER CARE IN 2024 (U.S. CENSUS BUREAU; ACF CHILD WELFARE OUTCOMES). PROJECT TEND WILL SERVE 3,330 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS OVER FIVE YEARS, COMPRISING 1,450 CHILDREN, 1,080 PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS, AND 800 TRAINED WORKFORCE MEMBERS. AGE RANGE & DISTRIBUTION. CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE 12, WEIGHTED TOWARD BIRTH THROUGH FIVE: PERINATAL AND INFANCY (PREGNANCY–12 MONTHS), TODDLERHOOD (12–36 MONTHS), AND PRESCHOOL (3–5 YEARS); SERVICES REMAIN AVAILABLE THROUGH AGE 12 FOR CHILDREN WITH EMERGING OR IDENTIFIED SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE (SED). BOTH MALE AND FEMALE CHILDREN ARE SERVED. CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS. CHILDREN ARE AT RISK FOR, SHOW EARLY SIGNS OF, OR HAVE A DIAGNOSED MENTAL ILLNESS INCLUDING SED, WITH HIGH EXPOSURE TO ADVERSE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES AND TOXIC STRESS. NATIONALLY, 19.0% OF CHILDREN AGES 2–8 HAVE A DIAGNOSED MENTAL, BEHAVIORAL, OR DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER (CDC, 2024), YET ONLY ONE IN FOUR WITH A DIAGNOSABLE CONCERN RECEIVES TREATMENT (AAP, 2023). CAREGIVERS FREQUENTLY PRESENT WITH UNTREATED PERINATAL MOOD AND ANXIETY DISORDERS. STRATEGIES & INTERVENTIONS. (1) WORKFORCE TRAINING VIA IECMH LEARNING COLLABORATIVE, INCLUDING CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY (CPP), FAN, AND DIR/ FLOORTIME, DC:0-5, A TRAIN-THE-REFLECTIVE-SUPERVISOR PIPELINE, GROUP REFLECTIVE SUPERVISION/CONSULTATION (RS/C), AND MASSAIMH ENDORSEMENT®. (2) SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, AND DIAGNOSIS USING ASQ-3, ASQ:SE-2, SWYC, AND DECA, WITH CAREGIVER DEPRESSION SCREENING (EPDS/PHQ-9) IN THE SAME WORKFLOW AND DC:0-5 DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION AFTER POSITIVE SCREENS. (3) EVIDENCE-BASED PROMOTION, PREVENTION, AND INTERVENTION SERVICES (4) IECMH CONSULTATION (IECMHC) TO EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION PROGRAMS. (5) QUARTERLY COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE TO CREATE A COHESIVE IECMH SYSTEM OF CARE.. GOALS. (1) STRENGTHEN AND SUSTAIN THE IECMH WORKFORCE THROUGH TRAINING AND REFLECTIVE SUPERVISION/CONSULTATION. (2) CONVENE A QUARTERLY COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE TO CREATE A COHESIVE, COORDINATED IECMH SYSTEM OF CARE. (3) DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED AND EVIDENCE-INFORMED PROMOTION, PREVENTION, AND INTERVENTION SERVICES. (4) PROVIDE IECMH CONSULTATION TO EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION PROGRAMS. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES. LAUNCH THE LEARNING COLLABORATIVE WITHIN FOUR MONTHS OF AWARD; TRAIN 800 PROFESSIONALS. PROVIDE GROUP RS/C TO 150 WORKFORCE MEMBERS; PREPARE 20 REFLECTIVE SUPERVISORS AND SUPPORT 150 PRACTITIONERS TOWARD ENDORSEMENT®. IMPLEMENT STANDARDIZED SCREENING; COMPLETE DC:0–5 EVALUATION WITHIN 30 DAYS OF POSITIVE SCREEN; ACHIEVE ≥85% LINKAGE TO APPROPRIATE SERVICES. SERVE 500 CHILDREN AND CAREGIVERS IN EVIDENCE-BASED DYADIC INTERVENTION. SCREEN ≥90% OF CAREGIVERS FOR PERINATAL/PARENTAL DEPRESSION AND LINK ≥85% OF POSITIVES TO TREATMENT. DELIVER IECMHC TO 100 ECE PROGRAMS REACHING 150 PROVIDERS. PROJECT TEND WILL PRODUCE A TOOLKIT AS A BLUEPRINT FOR AN IECMH SYSTEM OF CARE.

description: CENTRAL MISSOURI INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CM-IECMH CONTINUUM - THE UNIVERSITY OF MISSOURI CENTER FOR CHILD WELL-BEING (CCWB) WILL IMPLEMENT THE CENTRAL MISSOURI INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CM-IECMH CONTINUUM TO EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ACROSS CENTRAL MISSOURI. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE REGIONAL WORKFORCE, IMPLEMENT UNIVERSAL DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING, PROVIDE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION (IECMHC), AND EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION, INTERVENTION, AND TREATMENT SERVICES THAT PROMOTE HEALTHY DEVELOPMENT, STRENGTHEN CAREGIVER-CHILD RELATIONSHIPS, AND IMPROVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR INFANTS AND YOUNG CHILDREN. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE BOONE, AUDRAIN, CALLAWAY, COLE, COOPER, HOWARD, MONITEAU, AND RANDOLPH COUNTIES, REPRESENTING APPROXIMATELY 406,000 RESIDENTS, INCLUDING AN ESTIMATED 26,000 CHILDREN FROM BIRTH THROUGH AGE FIVE. OVER THE PROJECT PERIOD, THE CM-IECMH CONTINUUM WILL SERVE 3,073 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS, INCLUDING INFANTS, YOUNG CHILDREN, CAREGIVERS, AND EARLY CHILDHOOD PROFESSIONALS. ANNUAL ENROLLMENT WILL INCREASE FROM 190 PARTICIPANTS IN YEAR 1 TO APPROXIMATELY 720 PARTICIPANTS ANNUALLY DURING YEARS 2 THROUGH 5.  THE PRIMARY POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDES CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE FIVE AND THEIR CAREGIVERS, WITH SERVICES AVAILABLE FOR CHILDREN THROUGH AGE 12 WHEN CLINICALLY APPROPRIATE. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE CHILDREN WHO ARE AT RISK FOR, DEMONSTRATE EARLY SIGNS OF, OR HAVE BEEN DIAGNOSED WITH DEVELOPMENTAL, SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL, BEHAVIORAL, TRAUMA-RELATED, OR MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, INCLUDING SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE (SED). PRIORITY POPULATIONS INCLUDE CHILDREN EXPERIENCING ADVERSE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES, DEVELOPMENTAL DELAYS, ATTACHMENT DISRUPTIONS, CAREGIVER MENTAL HEALTH CONCERNS, AND LIMITED ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES. THE CM-IECMH CONTINUUM WILL IMPLEMENT FOUR INTEGRATED STRATEGIES: (1) ESTABLISH THE CENTRAL MISSOURI EARLY CHILDHOOD PROFESSIONAL LEARNING COLLABORATIVE (ECPLC) TO STRENGTHEN THE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD WORKFORCE THROUGH INTERDISCIPLINARY TRAINING, IMPLEMENTATION COACHING, AND CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY (CPP) AND PARENT-CHILD INTERACTION THERAPY (PCIT) LEARNING COLLABORATIVES; (2) IMPLEMENT UNIVERSAL DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING USING THE SURVEY OF WELL-BEING OF YOUNG CHILDREN (SWYC) FOLLOWED BY COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT, DIAGNOSIS, AND COORDINATED REFERRALS; (3) PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED PROMOTION, PREVENTION, AND TREATMENT THROUGH SHINE, ATTACHMENT VITAMINS, CPP, AND PCIT; AND (4) DELIVER INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION (IECMHC) USING PREVENT-TEACH-REINFORCE FOR YOUNG CHILDREN (PTR-YC) TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF EARLY CHILDHOOD PROGRAMS AND IMPROVE COORDINATED SYSTEMS OF CARE.  THE PROJECT'S GOALS ARE TO STRENGTHEN THE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH WORKFORCE, INCREASE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF DEVELOPMENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONCERNS, EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED SERVICES, AND ESTABLISH A COORDINATED REGIONAL SYSTEM OF CARE. BY THE END OF YEAR 5, THE PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT UNIVERSAL DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING FOR AT LEAST 1,000 CHILDREN IN PARTICIPATING CHILDCARE PROGRAMS, COMPLETE 1,600 COMMUNITY-BASED SCREENINGS, PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED ASSESSMENT AND TREATMENT TO AT LEAST 150 INFANTS, YOUNG CHILDREN, AND CAREGIVERS, AND ESTABLISH FORMAL REFERRAL AND CARE COORDINATION PARTNERSHIPS WITH AT LEAST 26 ORGANIZATIONS ACROSS THE REGION. THROUGH WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, EARLY IDENTIFICATION, EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTION, AND COORDINATED SYSTEMS OF CARE, THE CM-IECMH CONTINUUM WILL IMPROVE ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES, STRENGTHEN CAREGIVER-CHILD RELATIONSHIPS, AND PROMOTE HEALTHY DEVELOPMENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR INFANTS, YOUNG CHILDREN, AND FAMILIES ACROSS CENTRAL MISSOURI.

description: EDMOND'S MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIP - PROJECT ABSTRACT  THE PROPOSED CITY OF EDMOND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIP (BHMCTP) PROJECT WILL SERVE THE CITY OF EDMOND, OKLAHOMA. THE CITY WILL ENHANCE MOBILE CRISIS TEAM (MCT) SERVICES AND BUILD AND STRENGTHEN PARTNERSHIPS THAT BRIDGE THE GAP BETWEEN 988 AND CRISIS STABILIZATION SERVICES, THIS WILL BENEFIT EDMOND RESIDENTS OF ALL AGES AS WELL AS RESIDENTS OF SURROUNDING AREAS WHO USE AND RELY ON CITY INFRASTRUCTURE. THE GOALS OF EDMOND'S BHMCTP PROJECT ARE TO DIVERT CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND ADULTS EXPERIENCING A MENTAL HEALTH OR SUBSTANCE USE CRISIS FROM LAW ENFORCEMENT-ONLY RESPONSES AND HOSPITAL EMERGENCY ROOMS AND TO REDUCE DEATHS FROM SUICIDE AND OVERDOSE BY STRENGTHENING PARTNERSHIPS ACROSS THE CRISIS CONTINUUM AND ENHANCING MCT SERVICES.   THE EDMOND BHMCTP GOALS AND MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES ARE: GOAL 1. THE CITY WILL EXPAND AND ENHANCE THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDER-ONLY (BHP-ONLY) MCT. OBJ.1.1. BY MONTH 1, HIRE A .5 FTE PROJECT DIRECTOR, A .25 FTE PROJECT EVALUATOR, AND CONTRACT WITH AN EVALUATION CONSULTANT. 1.2. BY MONTH 4, DEVELOP AND ADOPT A BHP-ONLY MCT IMPLEMENTATION PLAN. 1.3. BY MONTH 5, CONTRACT WITH AN MCT PROVIDER TO ADD BHP-ONLY MCT CAPACITY AND DELIVER MCT SERVICES. 1.4. BY MONTH 6, THE MCT PROVIDER WILL PROVIDE 24/7 MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE TO 50% OF THE CATCHMENT AREA WITHIN 1 HOUR, INCREASING TO 100% BY THE END OF YEAR 4. GOAL 2. ESTABLISH FORMAL COMMUNITY CRISIS RESPONSE PARTNERSHIPS WITH KEY PROVIDERS. 2.1. BY MONTH 6, IDENTIFY KEY CRISIS PROVIDERS, DOCUMENT THEIR SERVICES, AND DETERMINE IF A FORMAL WRITTEN AGREEMENT IS IN PLACE. 2.2. BY MONTH 12, FORMALIZE/REVISE PARTNERSHIPS. 2.3. BEGINNING IN YEAR 2, REVIEW FORMAL PARTNERSHIPS ANNUALLY. GOAL 3. DEVELOP AND ADOPT A CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT (CQI) PROCESS TO MONITOR AND IMPROVE MCT SERVICES. 3.1. BY MONTH 6, ESTABLISH DATA COLLECTION PROTOCOLS TO COLLECT REQUIRED SAMHSA DATA AND KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS. 3.2. BY MONTH 9, IMPLEMENT FORMAL DATA SHARING AGREEMENTS WITH THE MCT PROVIDER. 3.3. BY MONTH 9, LAUNCH A POST-CRISIS CUSTOMER SATISFACTION SURVEY. 3.4. BY MONTH 12, LAUNCH A CQI PROCESS. 3.5. BEGINNING IN YEAR 2, REVIEW QUARTERLY DATA REPORTS. 3.6. BEGINNING IN YEAR 2, REVIEW AND REVISE THE CQI PLAN ANNUALLY. GOAL 4. REGULARLY ENGAGE COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS AND CONDUCT CRISIS SYSTEM PLANNING AND MAPPING. 4.1. BY MONTH 3, CONDUCT CRISIS SYSTEM PLANNING AND ASSET MAPPING. 4.2. BEGINNING IN MONTH 6 AND BIANNUALLY THEREAFTER, CONVENE A STAKEHOLDER MEETING TO GATHER INPUT ON CRISIS SYSTEM DATA AND FINDINGS. 4.3. BY YEAR 2 AND ANNUALLY THEREAFTER, UPDATE THE CRISIS SYSTEM MAP. GOAL 5. BUILD THE CAPACITY OF EDMOND’S MCT WORKFORCE AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO ADDRESS RESIDENTS’ CRISIS NEEDS. 5.1. BY MONTH 6, DEVELOP A TRAINING PLAN. 5.2. BEGINNING IN YEAR 2, REVIEW AND REVISE THE TRAINING PLAN. 5.3. BEGINNING IN MONTH 7 AND ANNUALLY THEREAFTER, FACILITATE ACCESS TO INITIAL TRAININGS FOR THE MCT AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS. 5.4. BY MONTH 9, INCORPORATE CHILD-SPECIFIC TRAINING INTO THE MCT CURRICULUM. 5.5. BY MONTH 12, 50% OF MCT STAFF WILL HAVE COMPLETED THE CHILD-SPECIFIC TRAINING; THE OTHER 50% WILL COMPLETE THE TRAINING BY MONTH 18. GOAL 6. SUSTAIN MCT SERVICES AND ITS PARTNERSHIP INFRASTRUCTURE BEYOND THE LIFE OF THE GRANT. 6.1. BY THE END OF YEAR 1, COMPLETE A FORMAL FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN. 6.2. BEGINNING IN YEAR 2 AND ANNUALLY THEREAFTER, REVIEW AND UPDATE THE FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN WITH THE TARGET OF FULLY SUSTAINING MCT SERVICES AT THE END OF THE GRANT PERIOD.

description: TOIYABE MOBILE CRISIS TEAM (TMCT) PROJECT - TOIYABE INDIAN HEALTH PROJECT (TIHP), A CONSORTIUM-GOVERNED, TRIBALLY CONTROLLED HEALTH ORGANIZATION SERVING NINE TRIBAL COMMUNITIES ACROSS INYO AND MONO COUNTIES, CALIFORNIA, WILL ESTABLISH THE TOIYABE MOBILE CRISIS TEAM (TMCT), THE REGION'S FIRST MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE FOR AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE (AI/AN) PEOPLE, DELIVERING CLINICIAN-LED, CULTURALLY GROUNDED CRISIS CARE THAT REACHES 24/7/365 COVERAGE BY THE END OF YEAR 4 AND DIVERTS TRIBAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS FROM LAW-ENFORCEMENT-ONLY RESPONSES, EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS, AND OTHER RESTRICTIVE SETTINGS. GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND CAPACITY NEED. INYO AND MONO COUNTIES, IN CALIFORNIA'S RURAL EASTERN SIERRA, WHERE COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS COVERAGE IS LIMITED TO A SINGLE BISHOP-BASED UNIT, MONO COUNTY HAS NO TEAM, AND REMOTE COMMUNITIES SUCH AS THOSE NEAR DEATH VALLEY FACE SOME OF THE LONGEST RESPONSE DISTANCES IN THE STATE. THE PROJECT BUILDS THE CAPACITY SAMHSA'S CRISIS CONTINUUM CALLS SOMEONE TO RESPOND: A BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PRACTITIONER-ONLY MOBILE CRISIS TEAM OPERATING A FOUR-VEHICLE, TELEHEALTH-EQUIPPED FLEET STATIONED ACROSS THE REGION. POPULATION OF FOCUS. ALL AI/AN CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND ADULTS IN THE TWO-COUNTY AREA, MEMBERS OF SEVEN FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBES AND TWO ADDITIONAL TRIBAL COMMUNITIES, FOR WHOM TIHP IS THE HEALTH CARE HOME. AI/AN SUICIDE MORTALITY IS 91% HIGHER THAN THE GENERAL POPULATION, AI/AN OVERDOSE MORTALITY IS THE HIGHEST OF ANY GROUP, AND LOCAL CRISIS EPISODES ARE MOST OFTEN RESOLVED TODAY THROUGH LAW ENFORCEMENT OR EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS. ALL SEVEN REQUIRED ACTIVITIES: AN IMPLEMENTATION PLAN BY MONTH 4; SERVICE DELIVERY BEGINNING BY MONTH 6, EXPANDING IN ANNUAL PHASES TO 24/7/365; WRITTEN PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENTS ACROSS ALL THREE REQUIRED TIERS WITHIN 12 MONTHS; CQI THROUGH THE STANDING TRIBAL 988 TASK FORCE; CRISIS SYSTEM PLANNING; EVIDENCE-BASED TRAINING FOR PARTNER PERSONNEL; AND FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY ANCHORED IN CALAIM MEDI-CAL MOBILE CRISIS REIMBURSEMENT. ALLOWABLE ACTIVITIES ADD FIELD TECHNOLOGY SUITED TO A FRONTIER SERVICE AREA, A YOUTH-FOCUSED RESPONSE OPTION, COMMUNITY OUTREACH TEAM ACTIVITIES, AND CONTINUED COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT. PROJECT GOALS. (1) ESTABLISH AND OPERATE A CULTURALLY GROUNDED MOBILE CRISIS TEAM; (2) FORMALIZE CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS THROUGH WHICH CRISIS DIVERSION IS ACHIEVED; (3) DIVERT TRIBAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN CRISIS FROM RESTRICTIVE SETTINGS; (4) BUILD A DISTRIBUTED, CERTIFIED CRISIS WORKFORCE SUITED TO THE SERVICE AREA; AND (5) INSTITUTIONALIZE QUALITY IMPROVEMENT AND FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES. FACE-TO-FACE RESPONSE WITHIN TWO HOURS FOR AT LEAST 80% OF RURAL RESPONSES BY YEAR 2; AT LEAST 70% OF EPISODES RESOLVED IN THE COMMUNITY WITHOUT EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT TRANSPORT, ARREST, OR INVOLUNTARY HOLD; 100% OF INDIVIDUALS SCREENED FOR SUICIDE RISK WITH VALIDATED TOOLS AND 72-HOUR FOLLOW-UP FOR AT LEAST 90%; AT LEAST 12 PARTNER AGREEMENTS BY MONTH 12; A CERTIFIED SIX-MEMBER PER DIEM RESPONDER NETWORK IN OUTLYING COMMUNITIES BY YEAR 2; AT LEAST 100 PARTNER PERSONNEL TRAINED ANNUALLY; AND A 15% REDUCTION IN LAW-ENFORCEMENT-ONLY OR EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT DISPOSITIONS BY THE END OF YEAR 4, ADVANCING SAMHSA'S PRIORITIES FOR CRISIS INTERVENTION, SUICIDE PREVENTION, OVERDOSE PREVENTION, AND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT.

description: WESTERN ARKANSAS CRISIS RESPONSE PARTNERSHIP - SEBASTIAN COUNTY IN PARTNERSHIP WITH WESTERN ARKANSAS COUNSELING & GUIDANCE CENTER (TGC), A CERTIFIED COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINIC (CCBHC), WILL RESTORE, ENHANCE, AND SUSTAIN A BEHAVIORAL-HEALTH-LED MOBILE CRISIS TEAM (MCT) SERVING CHILDREN, YOUTH, ADULTS, AND FAMILIES EXPERIENCING MENTAL HEALTH, SUBSTANCE USE, SUICIDE-RELATED, OVERDOSE-RELATED, AND CO-OCCURRING CRISES. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE TIMELY, COMMUNITY-BASED CRISIS RESPONSE; PARTNERSHIPS WITH 988, 911/PSAP, LAW ENFORCEMENT, EMS, HOSPITALS, AND COMMUNITY PROVIDERS; AND DIVERT INDIVIDUALS FROM LAW-ENFORCEMENT, EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS (ED), AND JAIL TOWARD STABILIZATION AND CARE. GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND NEED. SEBASTIAN IS THE HUB FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, EMERGENCY RESPONSE, AND SOCIAL SERVICES FOR A BROADER SUBSTANTIALLY RURAL REGION. SEBASTIAN CARRIES DUAL HRSA DESIGNATIONS AS A MEDICALLY UNDERSERVED AREA AND A HEALTH PROFESSIONAL SHORTAGE AREA FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH. TGC PREVIOUSLY OPERATED A MCT THAT WAS REDUCED AFTER A SUDDEN LOSS OF FUNDING, LEAVING THE COUNTY WITHOUT ADEQUATE DEDICATED MOBILE CRISIS CAPACITY. BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES INCREASINGLY FLOW THROUGH LAW ENFORCEMENT AND EDS: FORT SMITH POLICE DEPARTMENT CALL VOLUME ROSE FROM 871 (2022) TO 2,814 (2024), AND THE SUICIDE (18.6 PER 100,000) AND DRUG OVERDOSE DEATH RATE (24 PER 100,000) EXCEED NATIONAL LEVELS. THIS CAPACITY-BUILDING PROJECT WILL RESTORE AND IMPROVE MCT SERVICES, BUILD FORMAL REFERRAL AND DISPATCH PATHWAYS, AND INTEGRATE TGC'S 24/7 CRISIS LINE AND CCBHC INFRASTRUCTURE INTO A COORDINATED CRISIS CONTINUUM. POPULATION OF FOCUS AND POPULATION SERVED. COMMUNITIES THAT WILL BENEFIT INCLUDE CHILDREN, YOUTH, ADULTS, FAMILIES, VETERANS, JUSTICE-INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS, RURAL RESIDENTS, AND PEOPLE WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS (SMI), SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD), OR CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS (COD). THE MCT PROVIDES SERVICES TO THE COUNTY POPULATION WITH CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS INCLUDING SUICIDE AND OVERDOSE RISK, SMI, SUD, COD, TRAUMA, AND ACUTE PSYCHIATRIC CRISIS. SERVICE NEEDS INCLUDE DE-ESCALATION, CRISIS TRIAGE AND RISK SCREENING, SAFETY PLANNING, STABILIZATION, TRANSPORTATION COORDINATION, WARM HANDOFFS, AND FOLLOW-UP. STRATEGIES TO INCREASE CAPACITY. THE PROJECT WILL (1) DEVELOP AN MCT SERVICES IMPLEMENTATION PLAN; (2) ESTABLISH/ENHANCE A BEHAVIORAL-HEALTH-LED MCT USING A TWO-PERSON MODEL WITH PEER SUPPORT AND TELEHEALTH-ENABLED CLINICAL CONSULTATION; (3) FORMALIZE PARTNERSHIPS AND STANDARDIZED DISPATCH, REFERRAL, AND DIVERSION PROTOCOLS WITH CRISIS-SYSTEM PARTNERS; (4) IMPLEMENT A CQI PROCESS TRACKING REQUIRED KPIS; (5) CONDUCT CRISIS SYSTEM PLANNING AND MAPPING; (6) DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED CRISIS TRAINING TO STAFF AND PARTNERS; AND (7) DEVELOP SUSTAINABILITY STRATEGIES. PROJECT GOALS. GOAL 1: RESTORE AND ENHANCE BEHAVIORAL-HEALTH-LED MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE CAPACITY. GOAL 2: STRENGTHEN CRISIS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS, REFERRAL PATHWAYS, AND DIVERSION FROM RESTRICTIVE SETTINGS. GOAL 3: IMPROVE CRISIS-SYSTEM PLANNING, TRAINING, QUALITY, AND ACCOUNTABILITY. GOAL 4: BUILD A SUSTAINABLE MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE MODEL FOR SEBASTIAN. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES. SUBMIT AN MCT SERVICES IMPLEMENTATION PLAN BY MONTH 4 AND ESTABLISH OPERATIONAL MCT BY MONTH 6; DOCUMENT CRISIS TRIAGE, SUICIDE SCREENING, DISPOSITION, AND FOLLOW-UP IN AT LEAST 90% OF RESPONSES BY END OF YEAR 1 (Y1); INCREASE MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE VOLUME 25% OVER Y1 BASELINE BY END OF Y2; ACHIEVE COMMUNITY STABILIZATION OR DIRECT LINKAGE TO CARE IN AT LEAST 75% OF RESPONSES BY Y4; EXECUTE WRITTEN AGREEMENTS WITH AT LEAST 4 CRISIS-SYSTEM PARTNERS AND IMPLEMENT STANDARDIZED REFERRAL/DISPATCH PROTOCOLS WITHIN 12 MONTHS; INCREASE DIVERSION OR COMMUNITY-RESOLUTION OUTCOMES 20% OVER BASELINE BY Y4; COMPLETE CRISIS-SYSTEM PLANNING AND IMPLEMENT CQI WITH QUARTERLY REVIEW IN Y1; DELIVER AT LEAST EIGHT CRISIS TRAININGS ANNUALLY, WITH AT LEAST 75% OF TRAINED PARTNERS DEMONSTRATING INCREASED KNOWLEDGE BY Y2; AND COMPLETE AND ANNUALLY UPDATE A FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN,

description: THE JONES PREP ACADEMY INTEGRATED CONTINUUM OF CARE - THE JONES PREP ACADEMY WILL ESTABLISH A REGIONAL SCHOOL-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND TRAUMA RECOVERY CENTER TO EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED, TRAUMA-INFORMED MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES FOR CHILDREN AND YOUTH ACROSS NORTHWEST ARKANSAS. THROUGH AN INTEGRATED CONTINUUM OF CARE THAT COMBINES EDUCATION, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES, STRENGTHEN SCHOOL CLIMATE, REDUCE BARRIERS TO CARE, AND BUILD SUSTAINABLE REGIONAL CAPACITY TO SERVE CHILDREN WITH COMPLEX BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS. THE PROJECT WILL CREATE A REPLICABLE MODEL THAT STRENGTHENS SCHOOL-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE AND ADVANCES SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES OF PREVENTION, TREATMENT, RECOVERY, AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT. THE PROJECT WILL BE LED BY SPRINGDALE PUBLIC SCHOOLS (SPS) AND IMPLEMENTED THROUGH THE JONES PREP ACADEMY IN COLLABORATION WITH THE 15-MEMBER NORTHWEST ARKANSAS EDUCATION SERVICE COOPERATIVE (NWAESC). THE SERVICE AREA ENCOMPASSES MORE THAN 50,000 PREK–12 STUDENTS, WITH DIRECT INTENSIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES PROVIDED TO 396 UNDUPLICATED CHILDREN AND YOUTH OVER THE FOUR-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD (70 IN YEAR 1, 90 IN YEAR 2, 110 IN YEAR 3, AND 126 IN YEAR 4). ADDITIONAL STUDENTS, FAMILIES, EDUCATORS, AND SCHOOL PERSONNEL WILL BENEFIT FROM PREVENTION ACTIVITIES, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, CONSULTATION, AND SYSTEM-WIDE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SUPPORTS. THE TARGET POPULATION INCLUDES CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS AGES 5–17, WITH AN ANTICIPATED DISTRIBUTION OF APPROXIMATELY 50% MALE AND 50% FEMALE. PRIORITY WILL BE GIVEN TO STUDENTS EXPERIENCING SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE (SED), DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, TRAUMA-RELATED DISORDERS, BIPOLAR DISORDER, PSYCHOTIC DISORDERS, SUICIDAL IDEATION OR BEHAVIOR, SELF-HARM, AND CO-OCCURRING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO PRIORITIZE STUDENTS WITH DISABILITIES REQUIRING INTENSIVE MULTIDISCIPLINARY SUPPORTS, INCLUDING AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER, INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY, DEVELOPMENTAL DELAY, AND IDEA-IDENTIFIED EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE. MANY PARTICIPATING YOUTH EXPERIENCE POVERTY, ADVERSE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES (ACES), SCHOOL DISCIPLINARY ACTIONS, CHRONIC ABSENTEEISM, FAMILY INSTABILITY, OR INVOLVEMENT WITH CHILD WELFARE, JUVENILE JUSTICE, OR OTHER COMMUNITY SERVICE SYSTEMS. PROJECT STRATEGIES INCLUDE IMPLEMENTATION OF A COMPREHENSIVE MULTI-TIERED SYSTEM OF SUPPORTS (MTSS); UNIVERSAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENING AND REFERRAL; SCHOOL-BASED MENTAL HEALTH (SBMH) SERVICES; TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE; THERAPEUTIC LEARNING COMMUNITIES; POSITIVE BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS AND SUPPORTS (PBIS); YOUTH MENTAL HEALTH FIRST AID; ARKANSAS AWARE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT; PROFESSIONAL CRISIS MANAGEMENT; UKERU TRAUMA-INFORMED CRISIS PREVENTION; COORDINATED SUICIDE PREVENTION AND 988 PROTOCOLS; FAMILY ENGAGEMENT; CASE MANAGEMENT; COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PARTNERSHIPS; AND ONGOING TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOR PARTICIPATING SCHOOL DISTRICTS. THE JONES PREP ACADEMY WILL ALSO SERVE AS A REGIONAL DEMONSTRATION, TRAINING, AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE CENTER TO STRENGTHEN THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE THROUGHOUT NORTHWEST ARKANSAS. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO (1) BUILD A SUSTAINABLE REGIONAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE; (2) IMPLEMENT AN INTEGRATED CONTINUUM OF TRAUMA-INFORMED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES; (3) EMPOWER FAMILIES AS ACTIVE MEMBERS OF THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TEAM; (4) STRENGTHEN REGIONAL WORKFORCE CAPACITY THROUGH PROFESSIONAL LEARNING; AND (5) IMPROVE OUTCOMES THROUGH CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING. IDENTIFIED PROJECT OBJECTIVES DIRECTLY SUPPORT SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES BY EXPANDING EQUITABLE ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTHCARE, STRENGTHENING THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE, PROMOTING EARLY INTERVENTION AND SUICIDE PREVENTION, IMPROVING FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, AND ADVANCING RECOVERY-ORIENTED, TRAUMA-INFORMED SYSTEMS OF CARE.

description: ALABAMA MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE COLLABORATIVE - ALABAMA MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE COLLABORATIVE (AL-MCRC) IS ESTABLISHING AND ENHANCING CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND ADULT MOBILE CRISIS TEAMS (MCT) IN BUTLER, CALHOUN, CLEBURN, COFFEE, CONVINGTON, AND CRENSHAW COUNTIES TO EXPAND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS RESPONSE CAPACITY IN ALABAMA. CURRENTLY NO MCT SERVICES ARE OFFERED IN CALHOUN AND CLEBURN COUNTIES, AND LIMITED ADULT ONLY MCT SERVICES ARE OFFERED IN BUTLER, COFFEE, COVINGTON, AND CRENSHAW COUNTIES. MCT SERVICES WILL BE PROVIDED TO MALES AND FEMALES ACROSS THE LIFESPAN. PARTICIPANTS WILL INCLUDE ANYONE EXPERIENCING A MENTAL HEALTH OR SUBSTANCE USE CRISIS. TO INCREASE CAPACITY, AL-MCRC WILL DEVELOP THE FOLLOWING STRATEGIES AND PROTOCOLS: IMPLEMENTATION PLANS, FORMAL PARTNERSHIPS WITH KEY COMMUNITY PARTNERS, TRAINING PLANS, DATA MONITORING FRAMEWORKS AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, CRISIS SYSTEM PLANNING AND MAPPING, AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANS. AL-MCRC WILL ACHIEVE THE FOLLOWING GOALS. GOAL 1: INCREASE TIMELY ACCESS TO PERSON-CENTERED MCT SERVICES THROUGH COORDINATED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS RESPONSE BY INCREASING THE NUMBER OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES DIVERTED FROM THE 911 SYSTEM TO THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS SYSTEM, INCREASING REFERRALS FROM THE 988 SUICIDE & CRISIS LIFELINE TO PARTICIPATING MOBILE CRISIS TEAMS, INCREASING THE PERCENTAGE OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES RESOLVED SAFELY IN COMMUNITY SETTINGS WITHOUT EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT UTILIZATION, INCREASING THE PERCENTAGE OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES RESOLVED SAFELY IN COMMUNITY SETTINGS WITHOUT LAW ENFORCEMENT INVOLVEMENT, ENSURING MOBILE CRISIS TEAM RESPONSES WILL MEET NATIONALLY RECOGNIZED RESPONSE TIME STANDARDS APPROPRIATE FOR URBAN AND RURAL SERVICE AREAS, AND IMPLEMENTING  A STANDARDIZED CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT (CQI) PROCESS THAT UTILIZES MOBILE CRISIS TEAM KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIS), CONSUMER SATISFACTION DATA, AND OUTCOME MEASURES TO MONITOR PERFORMANCE AND IMPLEMENT QUARTERLY QUALITY IMPROVEMENT ACTIVITIES. GOAL 2: EXPAND MOBILE CRISIS TEAM CAPACITY TO MEET DOCUMENTED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS NEEDS ACROSS THE SIX-COUNTY CATCHMENT AREA BY ESTABLISHING AND ENHANCING EVIDENCE-BASED ADULT/CHILD/YOUTH MOBILE CRISIS TEAM AT HHS, SCAMHB, INCREASING THE ANNUAL NUMBER OF MOBILE CRISIS TEAM SERVICES DELIVERED IN-PERSON, AND ENSURING INDIVIDUALS SERVED BY MOBILE CRISIS TEAMS WILL RECEIVE APPROPRIATE FOLLOW-UP AND WARM-HANDOFF TO ONGOING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TREATMENT WITHIN 72 HOURS OF CRISIS ENCOUNTER. GOAL 3: BUILD A SUSTAINABLE, HIGH-QUALITY, AND TRANSFERABLE MOBILE CRISIS TEAM INFRASTRUCTURE ACROSS ALABAMA BY DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING A STATEWIDE, DATA-INFORMED COORDINATION PLAN THAT STRENGTHENS COLLABORATION AMONG 988, 911, CRISIS CALL CENTERS, MOBILE CRISIS TEAMS, COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH CENTERS, HOSPITALS, EMS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND OTHER COMMUNITY PARTNERS, DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING STANDARDIZED MOBILE CRISIS TEAM FIDELITY MEASURES AND CONDUCTING FIDELITY ASSESSMENTS, COMPLETING A COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF ALABAMA'S EXISTING MOBILE CRISIS TEAM TRAINING CURRICULUM AND IDENTIFY STRENGTHS, GAPS, AND RECOMMENDATIONS FOR ENHANCEMENT, DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING ENHANCED MOBILE CRISIS TEAM TRAINING MODULES ADDRESSING IDENTIFIED GAPS, DEVELOPING THE ALABAMA MOBILE CRISIS TEAM IMPLEMENTATION TOOLKIT, INCLUDING GUIDANCE ON FIDELITY MONITORING, EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, DATA COLLECTION, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND COMPLETING A COMPREHENSIVE TECHNOLOGY UTILIZATION GAP ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY PRIORITY TECHNOLOGY NEEDS, AND DEVELOPING A WRITTEN IMPLEMENTATION PLAN FOR SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS.
