description: MOBILE RESPONSE AND STABILIZATION SERVICES PARTNERSHIPS - RI MOBILE RESPONSE AND STABILIZATION SERVICES PARTNERSHIPS ABSTRACT THE RHODE ISLAND DEPARTMENT OF CHILDREN, YOUTH AND FAMILIES (DCYF) SEEKS TO STRENGTHEN AND EXPAND ITS STATEWIDE MOBILE RESPONSE AND STABILIZATION SERVICES (MRSS) SYSTEM BY ENHANCING THE GEOGRAPHIC REACH, WORKFORCE CAPACITY, AND PROGRAMMATIC INFRASTRUCTURE OF RHODE ISLAND'S COLLABORATIVE NETWORK OF MRSS PROVIDERS. WITH LONGSTANDING EXPERIENCE LEADING STATEWIDE CHILD-SERVING SYSTEMS, MANAGING CROSS-AGENCY INITIATIVES, AND ADVANCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, JUVENILE JUSTICE, AND CHILD WELFARE SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS, DCYF HAS THE CAPACITY AND INFRASTRUCTURE TO EFFECTIVELY LEAD AND COORDINATE THIS EFFORT. THROUGH THE MOBILE CRISIS TRAINING PARTNERSHIPS COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT, DCYF, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH NEWPORT MENTAL HEALTH, FAMILY SERVICE OF RHODE ISLAND (FSRI), AND TIDES FAMILY SERVICES, WILL BUILD THE INFRASTRUCTURE NEEDED TO STRENGTHEN THE MRSS WORKFORCE, IMPROVE CROSS-SYSTEM COORDINATION, AND ENSURE THE LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY OF RHODE ISLAND'S CHILDREN'S BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS SYSTEM. DCYF WILL LEVERAGE ITS STATEWIDE LEADERSHIP, ESTABLISHED PARTNERSHIPS, AND SYSTEM-LEVEL EXPERTISE TO GUIDE IMPLEMENTATION IN COLLABORATION WITH THE THREE LICENSED MRSS PROVIDER PARTNERS. NEWPORT MENTAL HEALTH, FSRI, AND TIDES FAMILY SERVICES BRING EXTENSIVE CLINICAL EXPERIENCE, COMMUNITY-BASED CRISIS RESPONSE CAPACITY, AND STRONG RELATIONSHIPS WITH FAMILIES, SCHOOLS, HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS, AND COMMUNITY PROVIDERS. TOGETHER, THIS STATE-PROVIDER PARTNERSHIP IS POSITIONED TO ADVANCE A COORDINATED, SUSTAINABLE, AND HIGH-QUALITY MRSS SYSTEM FOR CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND FAMILIES ACROSS RHODE ISLAND. SPECIFICALLY, THE PROJECT WILL: (1) STRENGTHEN THE MRSS WORKFORCE BY ESTABLISHING A PERMANENT STATEWIDE TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE THAT SUPPORTS HIGH-FIDELITY, EVIDENCE-INFORMED CRISIS RESPONSE; (2) FORMALIZE CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS TO ENSURE CHILDREN AND YOUTH IN CRISIS ARE CONSISTENTLY ROUTED TO MRSS RATHER THAN LAW ENFORCEMENT-ONLY OR EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RESPONSES WHENEVER APPROPRIATE; (3) INCREASE STATEWIDE AWARENESS OF MRSS AMONG FAMILIES, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, SCHOOLS, FIRST RESPONDERS, AND OTHER REFERRAL PARTNERS TO IMPROVE TIMELY ACCESS TO SERVICES; (4) IMPLEMENT A UNIFIED STATEWIDE CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT (CQI) PROCESS ACROSS THE THREE-PROVIDER MRSS NETWORK TO PROMOTE CONSISTENT, HIGH-QUALITY SERVICE DELIVERY AND OUTCOMES; AND (5) SUSTAIN AND CONTINUOUSLY STRENGTHEN RHODE ISLAND'S CHILDREN'S CRISIS SYSTEM BY DEVELOPING THE WORKFORCE, PARTNERSHIPS, AND QUALITY INFRASTRUCTURE NEEDED TO SUPPORT MRSS BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD. TOGETHER, THESE ACTIVITIES WILL IMPROVE ACCESS TO TIMELY, FAMILY-CENTERED CRISIS CARE, REDUCE UNNECESSARY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT UTILIZATION AND SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT, AND STRENGTHEN RHODE ISLAND'S BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS CONTINUUM FOR CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND FAMILIES.

description: PROJECT CONNECT: BUILDING TRAUMA-INFORMED SCHOOLS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITY - HOMEDALE SCHOOL DISTRICT (HSD) REQUESTS SAMHSA TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICES IN SCHOOLS FUNDING TO IMPLEMENT PROJECT CONNECT: BUILDING TRAUMA-INFORMED SCHOOLS, FAMILIES,AND COMMUNITY, A FOUR-YEAR INITIATIVE TO STRENGTHEN TRAUMA-INFORMED SCHOOL MENTAL HEALTH SUPPORTS FOR STUDENTS AND FAMILIES IN RURAL OWYHEE COUNTY, IDAHO. HSD OPERATES HOMEDALE ELEMENTARY SCHOOL, HOMEDALE MIDDLE SCHOOL, AND HOMEDALE HIGH SCHOOL AND SERVES 1,256 STUDENTS. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE STUDENTS IN PRE-K THROUGH GRADE 12, ALONG WITH PARENTS/CAREGIVERS, SCHOOL STAFF, LAW ENFORCEMENT PARTNERS, EARLY CHILDHOOD PARTNERS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS WHO SUPPORT STUDENT WELL-BEING.  PROJECT CONNECT PARTNERS WILL INCLUDE INSIGHT COUNSELING, AZEVEDO CONSULTING, RESULTS LEARNING CENTER, MENTAL HEALTH COLLABORATIVE, THRIVING MINDS, DR. KIM KANE/ASTROLABE, THE CENTER FOR SAFE AND RESILIENT SCHOOLS AND WORKPLACES, A QUALIFIED CQI CONSULTANT, AND A LOCAL TRAUMA-INFORMED COMMUNITY COALITION INCLUDING HSD LEADERS, SCHOOL REPRESENTATIVES, EARLY CHILDHOOD PARTNERS, LAW ENFORCEMENT/SRO, OWYHEE COUNTY PROBATION, IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND WELFARE, COMMUNITY SCHOOL COORDINATORS, PARENTS/CAREGIVERS, AND OTHER COMMUNITY PARTNERS.  PROJECT CONNECT WILL ADDRESS STUDENT MENTAL HEALTH, SAFETY, BULLYING, SOCIAL CONNECTION, AND HELP-SEEKING NEEDS BY BUILDING ONE COORDINATED SCHOOL/COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH SYSTEM RATHER THAN A DISCONNECTED SET OF ACTIVITIES. HSD WILL FORMALIZE PARTNERSHIP WITH INSIGHT COUNSELING AS A CREDENTIALED MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT PROVIDER, ESTABLISH A TRAUMA-INFORMED COMMUNITY COALITION AND INTERAGENCY AGREEMENT, IMPLEMENT SCHOOL-BASED SCREENING, REFERRAL, TRIAGE, WARM HANDOFF, CARE COORDINATION, TREATMENT LINKAGE, AND FOLLOW-UP WORKFLOWS, AND STRENGTHEN COORDINATION WITH 988 AND LOCAL CRISIS RESPONSE RESOURCES. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO PROVIDE TRAUMA- INFORMED TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, MENTAL HEALTH LITERACY TRAINING, SUICIDE PREVENTION TRAINING, UNIVERSAL MENTAL HEALTH SCREENING IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT, PBIS/MTSS FIDELITY SUPPORT, AND SELECTED EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA INTERVENTIONS SUCH AS SSET, BOUNCE BACK, CBITS, AND/OR TF-CBT WHEN APPROPRIATE.  PROJECT CONNECT WILL USE SAMHSA’S TRAUMA-INFORMED APPROACH, PBIS/MTSS, THE INTERCONNECTED SYSTEMS FRAMEWORK, DEVELOPMENTAL RELATIONSHIPS, MENTAL HEALTH LITERACY, SUICIDE PREVENTION, AND EVIDENCE-BASED/EVIDENCE-INFORMED TRAUMA INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE EARLY IDENTIFICATION, ACCESS TO CARE, SCHOOL CLIMATE, PROTECTIVE FACTORS, AND SUSTAINABILITY. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE AN ESTIMATED 1,856 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS ACROSS THE FOUR-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD. HSD WILL USE QUARTERLY PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENT, CQI, FIDELITY MONITORING, PARTNER DATA REVIEW, AND ANNUAL SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING TO MONITOR IMPLEMENTATION, IMPROVE REFERRAL AND SERVICE WORKFLOWS, STRENGTHEN ACCOUNTABILITY, AND EMBED EFFECTIVE PRACTICES INTO DISTRICT AND COMMUNITY SYSTEMS BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD.

description: WYOMING PROJECT STRONG (SCHOOL TRAUMA RESPONSE, OUTREACH, NAVIGATION, & GROWTH) - PROJECT STRONG (SCHOOL TRAUMA RESPONSE, OUTREACH, NAVIGATION, & GROWTH) IS A MULTI-DISTRICT INITIATIVE TO STRENGTHEN & EXPAND TRAUMA-INFORMED MENTAL HEALTH SYSTEMS FOR APPROXIMATELY 12,300 PREK-12 STUDENTS ACROSS THREE WYOMING PUBLIC SCHOOL DISTRICTS. LED BY PARK COUNTY SCHOOL DISTRICT #1 IN PARTNERSHIP WITH TWO WYOMING LOCAL EDUCATION AGENCIES (LEAS), LOCAL COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, & OTHER AGENCY PARTNERS, PROJECT STRONG WILL BUILD UPON EXISTING SCHOOL MENTAL HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE TO INCREASE STUDENT ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION, EARLY INTERVENTION, REFERRAL, & TREATMENT SERVICES. THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A COORDINATED FRAMEWORK THAT INTEGRATES UNIVERSAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENING, ROBUST TIER 1 & 2 INTERVENTION SYSTEMS, EXPANDED SCHOOL-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PARTNERSHIPS, & DATA-DRIVEN CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT EFFORTS TO IMPROVE STUDENT WELL-BEING & SUPPORT POSITIVE SCHOOL CLIMATES. IN WYOMING’S FRONTIER & RURAL COMMUNITIES, SCHOOLS FREQUENTLY SERVE AS THE PRIMARY POINT OF IDENTIFICATION & REFERRAL FOR STUDENT MENTAL HEALTH CONCERNS.DUE TO PROVIDER SHORTAGES, TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, & LIMITED ACCESS TO CHILD & ADOLESCENT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES.  WHILE PARTICIPATING LEAS HAVE MADE SUBSTANTIAL PROGRESS IN IMPLEMENTING MTSS-SEB AND DEVELOPING TIER 3 REFERRAL PATHWAYS, GAPS REMAIN IN UNIVERSAL EARLY IDENTIFICATION SYSTEMS, TIER 2 CAPACITY, & ACCESS TO SCHOOL-LINKED MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT SERVICES. PROJECT STRONG WILL ADDRESS THESE  GAPS BY IMPLEMENTING UNIVERSAL MENTAL HEALTH SCREENING IN ALL PARTICIPATING SCHOOLS, WITH THE GOAL OF SCREENING AT LEAST 75% OF ENROLLED STUDENTS ANNUALLY, EXPANDING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TIER 2 SUPPORTS FOR STUDENTS DEMONSTRATING EMERGING SOCIAL, EMOTIONAL, BEHAVIORAL, OR TRAUMA-RELATED CONCERNS, & INCREASING REFERRALS & SUCCESSFUL LINKAGE TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES BY AT LEAST 30% OVER THE FOUR-YEAR GRANT PERIOD. THROUGH STRENGTHENED COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS & EXPANDED SCHOOL-BASED SERVICE DELIVERY MODELS, THE PROJECT WILL REDUCE BARRIERS TO CARE & PROMOTE EQUITABLE ACCESS TO SERVICES REGARDLESS OF GEOGRAPHIC LOCATION. KEY GOALS AND ACTIVITIES OF PROJECT STRONG INCLUDE:  GOAL 1 IS TO ESTABLISH A COMPREHENSIVE SYSTEM FOR EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF STUDENT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS THROUGH UNIVERSAL SCREENING, COORDINATED REFERRAL PROCESSES, & INTEGRATED DATA SYSTEMS.  GOAL 2 IS TO STRENGTHEN TIER 2 MTSS-SEB SUPPORTS BY IMPLEMENTING EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS & TARGETED SERVICES THAT ADDRESS EMERGING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONCERNS BEFORE THEY REQUIRE INTENSIVE TREATMENT.  GOAL 3 IS TO EXPAND ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES THROUGH ENHANCED SCHOOL-COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PARTNERSHIPS, COORDINATED CARE PATHWAYS, & IMPROVED CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEMS, INCLUDING ALIGNMENT WITH LOCAL CRISIS SERVICES & 988 RESOURCES.  GOAL 4 IS TO BUILD SUSTAINABLE DISTRICT & COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURES THROUGH PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, INTERAGENCY COLLABORATION, & CONTINUOUS EVALUATION TO ENSURE LONG-TERM IMPLEMENTATION OF EFFECTIVE SCHOOL MENTAL HEALTH PRACTICES. AN INDEPENDENT EXTERNAL EVALUATOR WILL OVERSEE PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENT, DATA QUALITY, AND OUTCOMES EVALUATION, USING FINDINGS TO DRIVE CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, INFORM SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING, & DISSEMINATE  BEST PRACTICES ACROSS PARTICIPATING DISTRICTS & COMMUNITIES. THROUGH THIS COORDINATED SYSTEMS APPROACH, PROJECT STRONG WILL CREATE A SUSTAINABLE FRAMEWORK THAT IMPROVES ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES, STRENGTHENS SCHOOL-BASED SUPPORTS, & PROMOTES RESILIENCE, WELLNESS, & ACADEMIC SUCCESS FOR WYOMING STUDENTS & FAMILIES.

description: BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIPS, EXPANSION PROJECT - THE FLATHEAD CITY-COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENT (FCCHD), THROUGH ITS BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DIVISION, PROPOSES THE FLATHEAD COUNTY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIPS (MCTP) PROJECT TO EXPAND THE MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE SERVICES IN FLATHEAD COUNTY. FLATHEAD COUNTY IS A SPRAWLING FRONTIER AND RURAL JURISDICTION WHERE MORE THAN HALF OF THE 111,814 RESIDENTS LIVE IN GEOGRAPHICALLY ISOLATED COMMUNITIES. THE REGION EXHIBITS SEVERE RISK FACTORS FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MORTALITY, HIGHLIGHTED BY A FIVE-YEAR AGGREGATE SUICIDE RATE OF 26.4 DEATHS PER 100,000 RESIDENTS, NEARLY DOUBLE THE NATIONAL AVERAGE, AND A HIGH CONCENTRATION OF SUBSTANCE USE CHALLENGES.  CURRENTLY, THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT OPERATES THE CRISIS ASSISTANCE TEAM (CAT), WHICH PROVIDES MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE SERVICES FOR FLATHEAD COUNTY. IT IS STRUCTURALLY RESTRICTED TO A 12-HOUR-PER-DAY SERVICE WINDOW. THIS LIMITATION LEAVES A CRITICAL 12-HOUR NIGHTLY BLIND SPOT THAT SHIFTS THE ENTIRE BURDEN OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES ONTO LAW ENFORCEMENT, EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES, AND THE LOCAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT. TO ELIMINATE THIS SYSTEMIC GAP, THIS PROJECT WILL EXECUTE A STRUCTURED, MULTI-YEAR WORKFORCE SCALE-UP TO TRANSITION THE CAT PROGRAM INTO A COMPREHENSIVE, 24/7/365 FACE-TO-FACE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PRACTITIONER-ONLY (BHP-ONLY) MOBILE CRISIS INFRASTRUCTURE. CONCURRENTLY, THE GRANT WILL FUND THE IMPLEMENTATION OF A NEW, DAYTIME COMMUNITY OUTREACH TEAM (COT) TO CONDUCT MOBILE CARE COORDINATION, PHYSICAL HEALTH INTEGRATION, AND REAL-TIME TELEPSYCHIATRY LINKAGE FOR HIGH-UTILIZER POPULATIONS AT UNHOUSED SHELTERS AND THE COUNTY DETENTION CENTER.  PROJECT GOALS  • GOAL 1: ESTABLISH A 24/7/365 BHP-ONLY MOBILE CRISIS INFRASTRUCTURE. EXPAND EXISTING PERSONNEL TO DELIVER UNINTERRUPTED, FACE-TO-FACE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH FIELD RESPONSES.  • GOAL 2: FORMALIZE MULTI-SYSTEM TRIAGE, DISPATCH, AND CLINICAL PARTNERSHIPS. EMBED UNIFIED FIELD WORKFLOWS WITH PUBLIC SAFETY AND HEALTHCARE ANCHORS.  • GOAL 3: OPERATIONALIZE THE DAYTIME COMMUNITY OUTREACH TEAM (COT). BREAK THE LOCAL MULTIPLE-UTILIZER CYCLE THROUGH PROACTIVE MOBILE CARE.  STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS THE PROJECT LEVERAGES AN ESTABLISHED LOCAL COLLABORATIVE FOOTPRINT TO EXPAND EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES (EBPS), INCLUDING TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE (TIC), INTENSIVE CASE MANAGEMENT, AND STANLEY-BROWN SAFETY PLANNING. ALL CRISIS SCREENINGS AND TRACKING WILL FOLLOW VALIDATED, SCIENTIFIC STRUCTURES, INCLUDING THE COLUMBIA-SUICIDE SEVERITY RATING SCALE (C-SSRS) AND THE SUICIDE ASSESSMENT FIVE-STEP EVALUATION AND TRIAGE (SAFE-T) MATRIX. LED BY A 0.50 FTE PROJECT DIRECTOR AND A 0.25 FTE PROJECT EVALUATOR, THE PROGRAM WILL UTILIZE DIRECT QUERY LINKS INTO THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT'S ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR) AND AUTOMATED LOOPS WITH 911 DISPATCH DATA TO RUN A DATA-DRIVEN CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT (CQI) PROCESS. OVER THE 4-YEAR LIFECYCLE, THE PROJECT WILL MAXIMIZE MEDICAID BILLING WORKFLOWS AND PRESENT EMPIRICAL DIVERSION METRICS TO LOCAL LEADERS TO INTEGRATE THE EXPANDED INFRASTRUCTURE INTO THE PERMANENT COUNTY BUDGET, ENSURING LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY.

description: MARTINSBURG MOBILE CRISIS INTEGRATION PARTNERSHIP - THE CITY OF MARTINSBURG, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE MARTINSBURG INITIATIVE, WILL IMPLEMENT THE MARTINSBURG MOBILE CRISIS INTEGRATION PARTNERSHIP TO STRENGTHEN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MOBILE CRISIS AND CO-RESPONSE CAPACITY IN MARTINSBURG AND CHARLES TOWN, WEST VIRGINIA. THE PROJECT WILL EXPAND THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE, IMPROVE COORDINATION AMONG 988, 911, PUBLIC SAFETY, CRISIS PROVIDERS, HOSPITALS, AND TREATMENT ORGANIZATIONS, AND PROVIDE TIMELY COMMUNITY-BASED CRISIS INTERVENTION FOR CHILDREN, YOUTH, ADULTS, AND FAMILIES. THE INITIATIVE WILL REDUCE UNNECESSARY LAW-ENFORCEMENT-ONLY RESPONSES, EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT USE, INVOLUNTARY INTERVENTIONS, AND REPEATED CRISIS-SYSTEM CONTACTS WHILE IMPROVING STABILIZATION AND CONNECTION TO CARE. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE MARTINSBURG IN BERKELEY COUNTY AND CHARLES TOWN IN JEFFERSON COUNTY, WITH LIMITED RESPONSE TO SURROUNDING MUNICIPAL AREAS WHEN REQUESTED, AUTHORIZED, AND OPERATIONALLY FEASIBLE. CAPACITY NEEDS INCLUDE LIMITED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH STAFFING WITHIN PUBLIC-SAFETY SETTINGS, INCONSISTENT AFTER-HOURS COORDINATION, FRAGMENTED REFERRAL AND DISPATCH PROCEDURES, TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, LIMITED FOLLOW-UP, AND INSUFFICIENT SHARED DATA FOR MONITORING RESPONSE TIMELINESS, SAFETY, DIVERSION, AND OUTCOMES. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDES CHILDREN, YOUTH, ADULTS, AND FAMILIES EXPERIENCING MENTAL HEALTH OR SUBSTANCE USE CRISES WHO ARE IDENTIFIED THROUGH LAW ENFORCEMENT, FIRE/EMS, 911/PUBLIC SAFETY ANSWERING POINTS, 988, HOSPITALS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, SCHOOLS, FAMILIES, OR SELF-REFERRAL. INDIVIDUALS SERVED MAY EXPERIENCE SUICIDAL IDEATION OR BEHAVIOR, SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS, SUBSTANCE USE OR OVERDOSE RISK, CO-OCCURRING CONDITIONS, BEHAVIORAL ESCALATION, TRAUMA, FAMILY INSTABILITY, HOMELESSNESS, JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT, OR REPEATED CRISIS-SYSTEM CONTACTS. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE AT LEAST 200 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 1 AND 250 ANNUALLY IN YEARS 2-4, FOR A MINIMUM OF 950 INDIVIDUALS. CAPACITY-BUILDING STRATEGIES INCLUDE SUPPORTING A FULL-TIME PROJECT DIRECTOR/CLINICAL INTEGRATION LEAD, FOUR FULL-TIME BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CO-RESPONDERS, A 0.5 FTE WEEKEND AND EXTENDED-HOUR CO-RESPONDER BEGINNING IN MONTH 7, AND A 0.25 FTE PROJECT EVALUATOR. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A MOBILE CRISIS TEAM SERVICES IMPLEMENTATION PLAN WITHIN FOUR MONTHS AND LAUNCH THE ENHANCED MODEL WITHIN SIX MONTHS. SERVICES WILL INCLUDE POLICE AND FIRE/EMS CO-RESPONSE, BEHAVIORAL-HEALTH-ONLY RESPONSE WHEN APPROPRIATE, CRISIS ASSESSMENT, DE-ESCALATION, SUICIDE AND OVERDOSE SCREENING, STANLEY-BROWN SAFETY PLANNING, EMERGENCY RESCUE COORDINATION, VOLUNTARY TRANSPORTATION, WARM HANDOFFS, AND FOLLOW-UP WITHIN 72 HOURS. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO IMPLEMENT MOBILE RESPONSE AND STABILIZATION SERVICES FOR ELIGIBLE CHILDREN AND FAMILIES, PROACTIVE OUTREACH FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH REPEATED CRISIS CONTACTS, CRISIS-SYSTEM MAPPING, PARTNER TRAINING, FORMAL OPERATING PROTOCOLS, CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) EXPAND TIMELY COMMUNITY-BASED MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE; (2) IMPROVE STABILIZATION, DIVERSION, AND CONNECTION TO TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORTS; (3) STRENGTHEN SUICIDE, OVERDOSE, YOUTH, AND FAMILY CRISIS RESPONSE; AND (4) IMPROVE CRISIS-SYSTEM COORDINATION, WORKFORCE CAPACITY, DATA QUALITY, AND LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE COMPLETING THE IMPLEMENTATION PLAN WITHIN FOUR MONTHS; LAUNCHING ENHANCED SERVICES WITHIN SIX MONTHS; FORMALIZING AT LEAST FOUR PARTNER AGREEMENTS AND IMPLEMENTING CQI WITHIN 12 MONTHS; TRAINING 50 CRISIS-SYSTEM PROFESSIONALS ANNUALLY; COMPLETING 72-HOUR FOLLOW-UP AND WARM HANDOFFS FOR AT LEAST 85% OF ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS; MEETING RESPONSE-TIME STANDARDS FOR 80% OF ACCEPTED RESPONSES BY YEAR 2; INCREASING COMMUNITY RESOLUTION FROM 60% TO 70%; AND REDUCING 90-DAY REPEAT CRISIS CONTACTS BY 15% FROM THE YEAR 1 BASELINE.

description: CHEROKEE NATION BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MOBILE CRISIS TEAM - THE CHEROKEE NATION BEHAVIORAL HEALTH (CNBH) MOBILE CRISIS TEAM (MCT) PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PRACTITIONER-ONLY (BHP-ONLY) MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE SERVICE ACROSS THE CHEROKEE NATION RESERVATION, A 6,950-SQUARE-MILE, 14-COUNTY JURISDICTION IN NORTHEASTERN OKLAHOMA WITH A POPULATION OF 521,336, ROUGHLY HALF OF WHOM LIVE IN AREAS THE CENSUS CLASSIFIES AS RURAL. CNBH CURRENTLY HAS NO TRAINED WORKFORCE TO PLACE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH RESPONDERS ON SCENE AND NO ALTERNATIVE TO LAW ENFORCEMENT FOR MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE CRISES; EXISTING CRISIS CARE IS CLINIC-BOUND, LIMITED TO BUSINESS HOURS, AND ENDS WITHOUT FOLLOW-UP WHEN A CRISIS RESOLVES ON ITS OWN. LONG DRIVING DISTANCES, SOME EXCEEDING AN HOUR TO THE NEAREST EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, COMPOUND THESE GAPS FOR THE ROUGHLY 263,000 RESIDENTS LIVING IN THE RESERVATION'S RURAL AREAS. BUILDING THE WORKFORCE, PROTOCOLS, AND PARTNERSHIPS TO LAUNCH AND SUSTAIN AN INDEPENDENT, 24/7/365 MOBILE CRISIS SERVICE IS THE FOUNDATIONAL WORK OF THIS GRANT.  THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND ADULTS EXPERIENCING A MENTAL HEALTH OR SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER CRISIS ANYWHERE IN THE CATCHMENT AREA, WITH PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO RURAL RESIDENTS, CHILDREN AND FAMILIES, VETERANS, AND INDIVIDUALS WITH LIMITED ACCESS TO TRANSPORTATION OR INSURANCE. AMONG THE AREA'S 395,219 ADULTS, AN ESTIMATED 22,800 EXPERIENCE SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS, 89,200 EXPERIENCE ANY MENTAL ILLNESS, AND 10,900 MEET CRITERIA FOR A CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER AND SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS IN A GIVEN YEAR. TWELVE OF THE FOURTEEN COUNTIES EXCEED THE STATE'S ADULT INCARCERATION RATE, HALF EXCEED THE STATE'S JUVENILE JUSTICE REFERRAL RATE, AND EIGHT EXCEED THE STATE'S CHILD MALTREATMENT RATE, REFLECTING HOW OFTEN UNADDRESSED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES RESOLVE THROUGH THE JUSTICE SYSTEM RATHER THAN CLINICAL CARE. ADOLESCENTS CARRY ACUTE RISK LOCALLY, WITH 19% OF CATCHMENT-AREA SECONDARY STUDENTS REPORTING SERIOUS THOUGHTS OF SUICIDE IN THE PAST YEAR, AND 11,126 HOUSEHOLDS, 5.6% OF THE TOTAL, HAVE NO VEHICLE TO REACH A FIXED-SITE PROVIDER DURING A CRISIS.  CNBH WILL PAIR A LICENSED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PRACTITIONER WITH A PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SPECIALIST ON EVERY CRISIS RESPONSE, LAUNCHING WITH WEEKDAY COVERAGE AND EXPANDING TO 24/7/365 RESPONSE ACROSS ALL 14 COUNTIES BY 9/29/28 (GOAL 1). TO DIVERT CRISES FROM LAW ENFORCEMENT AND EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS (GOAL 2), THE MCT WILL RESOLVE AT LEAST 75% OF CRISES IN THE COMMUNITY WITHOUT EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT ADMISSION, ARREST, OR INVOLUNTARY TRANSPORT BY 9/29/29. TO REDUCE SUICIDE DEATHS AND ATTEMPTS (GOAL 3), EVERY IN-PERSON RESPONSE WILL INCLUDE A VALIDATED SUICIDE RISK ASSESSMENT, POST-CRISIS FOLLOW-UP WILL OCCUR WITHIN 72 HOURS FOR AT LEAST 75% OF RESPONSES, AND LINKAGE TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES WILL HAPPEN WITHIN 30 DAYS FOR AT LEAST 80% OF INDIVIDUALS ASSESSED AT MODERATE OR HIGHER SUICIDE RISK. GOAL 4 WILL BUILD THE PARTNERSHIPS, WORKFORCE, AND SUSTAINABILITY NEEDED TO MAINTAIN THE MCT AS A LONG-TERM COMPONENT OF THE REGIONAL CRISIS CONTINUUM. THESE GOALS ALIGN WITH SAMHSA PRIORITIES AND WILL BE MONITORED THROUGH CQI ACTIVITIES, QUARTERLY SPARS REPORTING, AND ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS.

description: PROJECT TIKBA TOHWIKELI (SHINING FUTURE) - CNO PROPOSES PROJECT TIKBA TOHWIKELI, WHICH MEANS  SHINING FUTURE,  A TRAUMA-INFORMED NATIVE-YOUTH CENTERED INITIATIVE TO BE IMPLEMENTED AT JONES ACADEMY (JA), A BUREAU OF INDIAN EDUCATION (BIE)-FUNDED AND CHOCTAW NATION SUPPORTED RESIDENTIAL BOARDING SCHOOL LOCATED NEAR HARTSHORNE, OKLAHOMA, SERVING NATIVE YOUTH FROM ACROSS OKLAHOMA AND MULTIPLE TRIBAL NATIONS. THIS INITIATIVE WILL IMMEDIATELY SHIFT AWAY FROM FRAGMENTED CARE TOWARD A HIGHLY INTEGRATED, 24-HOUR SYSTEM OF SUPPORT, MERGING WESTERN EVIDENCE-BASED CLINICAL MODALITIES WITH CULTURAL CHOCTAW PRACTICES TO SUPPORT STUDENTS' MENTAL WELL-BEING AND CULTURAL RESILIENCE. OVER THE 48-MONTH PROJECT PERIOD, PROJECT TIKBA TOHWIKELI WILL SERVE AT MINIMUM 35 JONES ACADEMY STUDENTS ANNUALLY. JONES ACADEMY SERVES NATIVE AMERICAN STUDENTS IN GRADES 1-12 (APPROXIMATELY AGES 6-18) WHO ARE EXPERIENCING CLINICAL SYMPTOMS OF ANXIETY, DEPRESSION, AND SUICIDAL IDEATION AT RATES SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER THAN THE NATIONAL AVERAGE. PROJECT TIKBA TOHWIKELI WILL EXPAND THE ACADEMY’S BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CAPACITY BY NEARLY DOUBLING ITS BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE AND PARTNERING WITH CHOCTAW NATION HEALTH SERVICES BEHAVIORAL HEALTH (CNHSBH) TO PROVIDE SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, TREATMENT, CRISIS INTERVENTION, AND CARE COORDINATION FOR STUDENTS EXPERIENCING MENTAL HEALTH CHALLENGES. PROJECT TIKBA TOHWIKELI WILL FLOW THROUGH A MULTI-TIERED SYSTEM OF SUPPORTS (MTSS). TIER 1 (UNIVERSAL) WILL ESTABLISH AN ENVIRONMENT OF “FELT SAFETY” ACROSS ALL CLASSROOMS AND DORMITORIES FOR 100% OF STUDENTS. THIS IS ACHIEVED BY DEPLOYING THE ACADEMY’S RESIDENTIAL STUDENT SUPPORT PROGRAM (RSSP) AND THROUGH CAMPUS-WIDE TRAINING IN TRUST-BASED RELATIONAL INTERVENTION (TBRI), WHICH FOCUSES ON PROVIDING SUPPORTIVE CAREGIVING AND POSITIVE DAILY EXPERIENCES. TIER 2 (TARGETED) ADDRESSES THE NEEDS OF 20% TO 25% OF THE STUDENT BODY WHO NEED ADDITIONAL SUPPORT TO THRIVE. STAFF WILL LOOK AT THE “WHY” BEHIND THEIR ACTIONS, SUCH AS WANTING ATTENTION OR SEEKING SENSORY INPUT, BY USING THE EATS (ESCAPE, ATTENTION, TANGIBLE, SENSORY) FRAMEWORK. IN ADDITION, PROJECT TIKBA TOHWIKELI WILL ORGANIZE SMALL GROUPS USING NEUROSCIENCE-BACKED MANAGE YOUR SELF (MYS) CURRICULUM TO HELP STUDENTS BUILD ESSENTIAL LIFE SKILLS. TIER 3 (INTENSIVE) WILL PROVIDE WRAPAROUND CARE FOR 10% TO 15% OF ACUTE, HIGH-RISK STUDENTS. FOR THESE STUDENTS, PROJECT TIKBA TOHWIKELI WILL UTILIZE 90-DAY GOAL SETTING AGREEMENTS AND SPECIALIZE RESIDENTIAL SKILLS PLANS (RSPS) THAT INCLUDE TRAUMA THERAPY AND CULTURALLY-GROUNDED RESTORATIVE CIRCLES. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO INCREASE ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, IMPROVE SCHOOL CLIMATE, STRENGTHEN FAMILY AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, REDUCE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYMPTOMS, AND ESTABLISH A 24-HOUR CONTINUUM OF CARE FOR NATIVE YOUTH. DELIVERABLES WILL INCLUDE SECURELY MANAGED PATIENT DATA THAT STRENGTHENS THE EVIDENCE BASE FOR NATIVE AMERICAN YOUTH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TREATMENT. EXPECTED OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE THE REDUCTION OF BEHAVIORAL INFRACTIONS, A DECREASE IN STUDENTS’ ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION SCORES, AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN UNBROKEN 24-HOUR CONTINUUM OF TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE THAT WILL TRANSFORM OUR NATIVE AMERICAN STUDENTS’ SURVIVAL INSTINCTS INTO SUSTAINED, GENERATIONAL RESILIENCE.

description: HAMILTON COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS TEAM EXPANSION GRANT EXPANDS STAFFING, FORMALIZES PARTNERSHIPS AND BUILDS QUALITY INFRASTRUCTURE TO DIVERT CRISES FROM LAW ENFORCEMENT AND COMMUNITY CARE - PROJECT ABSTRACT THE HAMILTON COUNTY MENTAL HEALTH AND RECOVERY SERVICES BOARD (HCMHRSB) IN PARTNERSHIP WITH CENTRAL CLINIC BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND UNIVERSITY OF CINCINNATI MEDICAL CENTER (UCMC) WILL STRENGTHEN THEIR 24/7 MOBILE CRISIS TEAM (MCT) SERVING 838,418 HAMILTON COUNTY, OHIO (HC-OH) RESIDENTS. THE HAMILTON COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS TEAM ENHANCEMENT GRANT (HC-MCT-E) EXPANDS STAFFING, FORMALIZES PARTNERSHIPS, AND BUILDS QUALITY INFRASTRUCTURE TO DIVERT CRISES FROM LAW ENFORCEMENT TO COMMUNITY CARE. PROJECT NAME: HAMILTON COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS TEAM ENHANCEMENT GRANT (HC-MCT-E). GEOGRAPHIC AREA & CAPACITY NEEDED: HC-OH SPANS 405.5 SQUARE MILES AND 838,418 RESIDENTS, 63% LIVING OUTSIDE CINCINNATI. UCMC'S MCT HAS PROVIDED 24/7 COUNTYWIDE CRISIS RESPONSE SINCE 2023, BUT CAPACITY HAS NOT KEPT PACE WITH NEED: RESIDENTS OUTSIDE CINCINNATI RECEIVE ONLY 29% OF RESPONSES DESPITE COMPRISING 63% OF THE POPULATION; EVENING AND WEEKEND HOURS HAVE NO PEER COVERAGE; FORMAL PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENTS WITH 911, 988, EMERGENCY FIRST RESPONDERS, AND COMMUNITY SERVICES DO NOT EXIST; SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD) STATUS GOES UNDOCUMENTED IN 30% OF ENCOUNTERS; AND NO CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT (CQI) INFRASTRUCTURE EXISTS. POPULATION OF FOCUS: FOUR POPULATIONS WILL BENEFIT MOST: PERSONS WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS (SMI) (51% OF ENCOUNTERS), PERSONS WITH SUDS (38%), HIGH UTILIZERS WITH RECURRENT CRISIS CONTACT (65% WITH TWO OR MORE ENCOUNTERS), AND RESIDENTS OF UNDERSERVED AREAS OUTSIDE CINCINNATI. POPULATION SERVED: MCT SERVES ADULTS AND YOUTH IN HC-OH EXPERIENCING MENTAL HEALTH (MH) AND SUD CRISES; MCT RESPONDS COUNTYWIDE. 2025 ENCOUNTER DATA (N=8,022): AGES 18-54 (59%), 55+ (23%); SEX EVENLY SPLIT (48% FEMALE, 48% MALE); 2% VETERANS. PRIMARY DIAGNOSES: SCHIZOPHRENIA SPECTRUM DISORDERS (26%), BIPOLAR DISORDER (13%), DEPRESSIVE DISORDERS (12%); 38% HAVE A DOCUMENTED SUD HISTORY. STRATEGIES & INTERVENTIONS: HC-MCT-E WILL (1) HIRE CLINICAL AND PEER STAFF AT THREE SATELLITE OFFICES TO CLOSE GEOGRAPHIC AND EVENING/WEEKEND COVERAGE GAPS; (2) ESTABLISH A COMMUNITY OUTREACH TEAM (COT) FOR PEER-LED CRISIS PREVENTION AND POSTVENTION WITH HIGH UTILIZERS; (3) FORMALIZE PARTNERSHIPS VIA MEMORANDA OF UNDERSTANDING (MOUS) WITH FRONT-END (988, 911), BACK-END (COMMUNITY SERVICES), AND FIRST-RESPONDER PARTNERS, EMBEDDING A TRIAGE WORKER IN 911 DISPATCH AND DEVELOPING DISPATCH CRITERIA AND WARM-TRANSFER PROTOCOLS FOR 988- AND 911-TO-MCT REFERRALS; (4) INTEGRATE A STANDARDIZED SUD SCREENING INTO EVERY ENCOUNTER; (5) BUILD CQI INFRASTRUCTURE, INCLUDING A WRITTEN PLAN, EPIC DASHBOARD, AND PLAN-DO-STUDY-ACT (PDSA) CYCLES; AND (6) STRENGTHEN SYSTEM-LEVEL TRAINING, CRISIS PLANNING, AND FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY. PROJECT GOALS: (1) EXPAND CRISIS RESPONSE CAPACITY OUTSIDE CINCINNATI; (2) EXPAND PEER SUPPORT CAPACITY FOR CRISIS PREVENTION AND POSTVENTION; (3) ESTABLISH FORMAL PARTNERSHIPS TO IMPROVE COORDINATION AND DIVERSION; (4) STRENGTHEN SUD IDENTIFICATION AND TREATMENT LINKAGE; (5) BUILD DATA-DRIVEN CQI CAPACITY; AND (6) STRENGTHEN SYSTEM INFRASTRUCTURE TO SUSTAIN CRISIS RESPONSE. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: BY 9/30/2028, INCREASE CRISIS RUNS TO ZIP CODES OUTSIDE CINCINNATI FROM 29% TO 43% OR MORE (EXPANDING CRISIS SERVICES). BY 9/30/2028, REDUCE THE 988 CALL OVERFLOW RATE FROM 32% TO 26% OR LESS AND REDUCE ON-SITE MCT RESPONSES CO-OCCURRING WITH LAW ENFORCEMENT FROM 52% TO 41% OR LESS (EXPANDING CRISIS SERVICES). BY 9/30/2029, REDUCE 30-DAY RECIDIVISM AMONG MCT PEER-SERVICES CLIENTS FROM 22% TO 18% OR LESS (ADDRESSING SMI). BY 9/30/2028, DECREASE UNDOCUMENTED SUD STATUS FROM 30% TO 20% OR LESS, AND BY 9/30/2029, INCREASE SUD TREATMENT LINKAGE FROM 33% TO 45% OR MORE (PREVENTING SUBSTANCE MISUSE, IMPROVING TREATMENT ACCESS).

description: SENECA COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS PARTNERSHIP - SENECA COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS PROGRAM PARTNERSHIP  SAMHSA SM-26-029 BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIPS  SENECA COUNTY MENTAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT PROPOSES THE SENECA COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS PARTNERSHIP TO STRENGTHEN AN ESTABLISHED 24/7 COUNTY-OPERATED MOBILE CRISIS TEAM THROUGH WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, SPECIALIZED TRAINING, ENHANCED PEER SERVICES, IMPROVED DATA INFRASTRUCTURE, AND EXPANDED PARTNERSHIPS ACROSS THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS CONTINUUM. THE PROJECT WILL ENHANCE TIMELY, CLINICALLY LED, COMMUNITY-BASED CRISIS RESPONSE, IMPROVE COORDINATION WITH 988, EMS, HOSPITALS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND COMMUNITY PROVIDERS, AND REDUCE UNNECESSARY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT UTILIZATION AND LAW ENFORCEMENT INVOLVEMENT WHILE INCREASING ACCESS TO RECOVERY-ORIENTED SERVICES.  PROJECT NAME: SENECA COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS PARTNERSHIP  GEOGRAPHIC AREA: SENECA COUNTY, NEW YORK (RURAL COUNTY SERVING ALL MUNICIPALITIES).  CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT NEED: EXPAND ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY TO MEET INCREASING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE CRISIS NEEDS THROUGH WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, ADVANCED TRAINING, PEER SUPPORT ENHANCEMENT, INTEROPERABLE DATA SYSTEMS, QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND STRENGTHENED COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS.  POPULATION OF FOCUS AND POPULATION SERVED: CHILDREN, YOUTH, ADULTS, AND OLDER ADULTS EXPERIENCING MENTAL HEALTH AND/OR SUBSTANCE USE CRISES, INCLUDING INDIVIDUALS WITH CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS, AND THE COMMUNITY PARTNERS SUPPORTING CRISIS RESPONSE.  CAPACITY-BUILDING STRATEGIES: RECRUIT AND RETAIN STAFF; PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED CRISIS, YOUTH, OLDER ADULT, AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDER TRAINING; STRENGTHEN PEER INTEGRATION; ENHANCE DATA COLLECTION AND PERFORMANCE MONITORING; FORMALIZE CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS; IMPROVE COORDINATION WITH 988 AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE SYSTEMS.  PROJECT GOALS: INCREASE ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY, STRENGTHEN CLINICALLY LED MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE, IMPROVE COORDINATION ACROSS THE CRISIS CONTINUUM, EXPAND ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY CRISIS SERVICES, ENHANCE DATA-DRIVEN QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND IMPROVE OUTCOMES FOR INDIVIDUALS EXPERIENCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: IMPLEMENT ALL WORKFORCE AND TRAINING ACTIVITIES; STRENGTHEN PEER SUPPORT SERVICES; IMPROVE RESPONSE COORDINATION WITH KEY PARTNERS; ACHIEVE PROJECT PERFORMANCE INDICATORS FOR RESPONSE TIMELINESS, FOLLOW-UP ENGAGEMENT, STAFF COMPETENCY, PARTNERSHIP PARTICIPATION, AND QUALITY IMPROVEMENT MEASURES CONSISTENT.

description: RVA MOBILE CRISIS TEAM - THE RICHMOND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AUTHORITY (RBHA) LOCATED IN RICHMOND, VA IS REQUESTING FUNDING TO ENHANCE AND EXPAND OUR MOBILE CRISIS TEAM RESPONSE SERVICES USING A SPECIALIZED TEAM OF CLINICIANS AND PEERS WORKING IN COLLABORATION WITH THE PUBLIC SAFETY SYSTEM TO IDENTIFY AND RESPOND TO HIGH-RISK INDIVIDUALS. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE SERVICES TO INDIVIDUALS IN CRISIS SITUATIONS, OR AS FOLLOW-UP TO SERVICES IN AN EFFORT TO IMPROVED CONTINUITY OF CARE AND REFERRAL TO APPROPRIATE COMMUNITY RESOURCES FOR CONTINUED SUPPORT.                                                                                                      THE TARGET POPULATION IS INDIVIDUALS WITH MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS WITH POSSIBLE CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER. FOR THIS PROPOSED PROJECT, THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS THOSE INDIVIDUALS IN RICHMOND EXPERIENCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISORDERS AND IN NEED OF CRISIS SERVICES DEMOGRAPHICALLY, RICHMOND IS AN URBAN LOCALE; 47.4% MALE AND 52.6% FEMALE. THE MEDIAN AGE IS 35; 17.5% OF RICHMONDERS ARE UNDER 18 YEARS OLD AND 14.8% ARE OVER 65 YEARS OLD. REGARDING SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS, 18% OF INDIVIDUALS LIVING IN RICHMOND ARE BELOW THE FEDERAL POVERTY LINE; 31% OF THIS GROUP ARE UNDER 18. THE CITY HAS BEEN AFFECTED, LIKE MANY OTHER AREAS, BY THE OPIOID EPIDEMIC AS WELL AS IN NEED OF AN IMPROVED CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEM.  STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS WILL INCLUDE ENHANCED AND EXPANDED MOBILE CRISIS TEAM SERVICES, A PSAP-EMBEDDED CLINICIAN, WARM HAND-OFFS TO NEEDED SERVICES, TRAINING OF LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND CRISIS SYSTEM PLANNING EFFORTS.    MAIN GOALS ARE TO: IMPROVE CLINICAL OUTCOMES; IMPROVE CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEMS; DIVERT INDIVIDUALS FROM COSTLY AND RESTRICTIVE SERVICES; ESTABLISH INTERNAL PROTOCOLS FOR SERVICE EVALUATION AND IMPROVEMENT; AND ESTABLISH COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS AND TRAINING.

description: CITY OF MISSOULA — MISSOULA MOBILE CRISIS TEAM (MCT) EXPANSION PROJECT - CITY OF MISSOULA — MISSOULA MOBILE CRISIS TEAM (MCT) EXPANSION PROJECT  THE CITY OF MISSOULA MOBILE CRISIS TEAM (MCT) EXPANSION PROJECT WILL SUPPORT RESIDENTS OF MISSOULA COUNTY IN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS BY ADDING AN ADDITIONAL MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE UNIT TO MEET GROWING DEMAND, EXTENDING SERVICE HOURS, AND STRENGTHENING COUNTYWIDE PARTNERSHIPS IN MISSOULA COUNTY, MONTANA. SINCE 2020, MCT CLINICIANS AND EMTS HAVE SAFELY RESOLVED THOUSANDS OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES IN THE COMMUNITY, DIVERTING PEOPLE FROM EMERGENCY ROOMS, JAILS, AND UNNECESSARY LAW ENFORCEMENT INVOLVEMENT. THIS EXPANSION WILL ADD A THIRD UNIT TO THE ALREADY EXISTING TEAM AND WILL EXTEND THE MODEL INTO UNDERSERVED RURAL AREAS. THIS ADDITIONAL UNIT WILL EXPAND DAILY OPERATING HOURS FROM 10 TO AS MANY AS 18 AND BUILD A PATHWAY TOWARD 24-HOUR COVERAGE.  MISSOULA COUNTY, MONTANA'S THIRD-LARGEST COUNTY BY POPULATION (124,555 RESIDENTS ACROSS 2,600 SQUARE MILES), IS THE PROJECT'S CATCHMENT AREA. WHILE 59% OF COUNTY RESIDENTS LIVE WITHIN THE CITY OF MISSOULA, RURAL AND UNINCORPORATED COMMUNITIES — INCLUDING EAST MISSOULA, CLINTON, BONNER, EVARO, HUSON, AND CONDON — ARE GROWING FASTER THAN THE URBAN CORE. THESE OUTLYING AREAS RECEIVED ONLY 18% OF MCT'S 2025 RESPONSES DESPITE COMPRISING 41% OF THE COUNTY'S POPULATION. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS FOR THIS PROJECT ARE INDIVIDUALS OF ALL AGES IN MISSOULA COUNTY EXPERIENCING A BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS, WITH PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO GROUPS AT ELEVATED RISK: YOUTH, ADULTS WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS OR SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, VETERANS, JUSTICE-INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS, INDIVIDUALS EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS OR HOUSING INSTABILITY, AND RURAL COUNTY RESIDENTS.  THE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES OF THE PROJECT, ALIGNED WITH SAMSHA’S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES, ARE AS FOLLOWS:  GOAL 1 — EXPAND THE MISSOULA MCT RESPONSE CAPACITY • OBJECTIVE 1.1: DEVELOP AN MCT SERVICES IMPLEMENTATION PLAN BY MONTH 4 OF THE AWARD PERIOD. • OBJECTIVE 1.2: ESTABLISH AND FULLY STAFF A THIRD MCT RESPONSE UNIT IN MISSOULA COUNTY WITHIN 6 MONTHS OF AWARD. • OBJECTIVE 1.3: INCREASE MCT’S EVALUATION AND ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT CAPACITY BY THE END OF YEAR 1.  GOAL 2 — EXPAND MCT COVERAGE HOURS AND GEOGRAPHIC REACH • OBJECTIVE 2.1 – BY THE END OF YEAR 1, INCREASE MCT HOURS OF OPERATION FROM 10 TO 14 HOURS DAILY CONSISTENT WITH THE YEAR 1 STAFFING PLAN IN THE PROJECT BUDGET. • OBJECTIVE 2.2 – BY THE END OF YEAR 2, EXPAND MCT HOURS TO AN 18-HOUR DAILY SCHEDULE AND COMPLETE A PLAN FOR FULL 24-HOUR COVERAGE BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD. • OBJECTIVE 2.3 – INCREASE THE SHARE OF MCT RESPONSES OCCURRING IN OUTLYING/RURAL MISSOULA COUNTY ABOVE THE CURRENT 18% BASELINE, USING HEAT-MAPPING AND SITUATION-TABLE DATA TO TARGET EXPANSION.  GOAL 3 -STRENGTHEN THE MISSOULA MOBILE CRISIS SYSTEM THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS AND SUSTAINABLE FUNDING. • OBJECTIVE 3.1- BY THE END OF YEAR 1, FINALIZE A NEW DCO (DIRECT CARE ORGANIZATION) AGREEMENT WITH AWARE'S CERTIFIED COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINIC (CCBHC) AND UPDATED EXISTING INTERLOCAL AGREEMENTS WITH PHC AND MISSOULA COUNTY. • OBJECTIVE 3.2 – BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, COMPLETE A LONG-TERM BUSINESS PLAN AND REIMBURSEMENT STRATEGY TO SUPPORT A 24-HOUR IMPLEMENTATION MODEL WITH DIVERSIFIED FUNDING.   ALL OF OUR WORK WILL BE STRENGTHENED BY EXISTING AND EXPANDED COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP AND ENHANCED EVALUATION CAPACITY THAT WILL ALLOW US TO BETTER IDENTIFY GAPS IN THE COMMUNITY AND WORK TOGETHER TO BUILD THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS CONTINUUM OF CARE IN MISSOULA COUNTY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: YELLOWSTONE COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIP - YELLOWSTONE CITY COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENT DBA RIVERSTONE HEALTH WILL ESTABLISH THE YELLOWSTONE COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIP TO IMPLEMENT A BEHAVIORAL HEALTH-LED MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEM SERVING YELLOWSTONE COUNTY, MONTANA. YELLOWSTONE COUNTY IS THE LARGEST COUNTY IN MONTANA BY POPULATION AND SERVES AS THE REGIONAL CENTER FOR HEALTHCARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, AND PUBLIC SAFETY SERVICES. DESPITE THE PRESENCE OF 988 AND A LONGSTANDING CRISIS RECEIVING CENTER, MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE REMAINS A SIGNIFICANT GAP IN THE LOCAL CRISIS CONTINUUM. THE COUNTY CONTINUES TO EXPERIENCE ELEVATED RATES OF SUICIDE, SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, OVERDOSE DEATHS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH-RELATED EMS INCIDENTS, AND CRISIS CALLS REQUIRING LAW ENFORCEMENT OR EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT INVOLVEMENT.   THE PROJECT WILL SERVE INDIVIDUALS ACROSS THE LIFESPAN EXPERIENCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES, INCLUDING YOUTH, ADULTS, VETERANS, INDIVIDUALS WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS, INDIVIDUALS WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, INDIVIDUALS WITH CO-OCCURRING CONDITIONS, PEOPLE EXPERIENCING SUICIDAL IDEATION OR OVERDOSE RISK, JUSTICE-INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS, FREQUENT EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT USERS, AND RESIDENTS OF RURAL COMMUNITIES WITH LIMITED ACCESS TO CARE.   THROUGH A PHASED IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH, THE PROJECT WILL LAUNCH MOBILE CRISIS TEAM SERVICES IN BILLINGS WITHIN SIX MONTHS OF AWARD, EXPAND TO 24/7/365 COVERAGE BY THE END OF YEAR 2, AND EXTEND SERVICES INTO RURAL YELLOWSTONE COUNTY BY THE END OF YEAR 3. THE MCT WILL PROVIDE MOBILE CRISIS ASSESSMENT, DE-ESCALATION, SUICIDE AND OVERDOSE RISK SCREENING, STABILIZATION, SAFETY PLANNING, CARE COORDINATION, FOLLOW-UP WITHIN 72 HOURS, AND WARM HANDOFFS TO ONGOING TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES. THE PROJECT WILL BE IMPLEMENTED THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS WITH MONTANA 988 LIFELINE PROVIDERS, YELLOWSTONE COUNTY 911 COMMUNICATIONS, EMS AGENCIES, LOCAL HOSPITALS, LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES, THE COMMUNITY CRISIS CENTER, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS TO STRENGTHEN COORDINATION ACROSS THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS CONTINUUM.   OVER THE FOUR-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE DIVERSION FROM LAW-ENFORCEMENT-ONLY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS RESPONSE BY 20% BY YEAR 2, REDUCE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH-RELATED EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT UTILIZATION AMONG INDIVIDUALS SERVED BY 10% IN YEAR 1, 20% IN YEAR 2, AND 25% BY YEARS 3 AND 4, AND ACHIEVE COMMUNITY-BASED STABILIZATION FOR AT LEAST 60% OF CRISIS ENCOUNTERS BY YEAR 2 WHILE MAINTAINING OR IMPROVING THAT RATE THEREAFTER. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO INCREASE DIVERSION FROM INVOLUNTARY COMMITMENT, INCARCERATION, AND UNNECESSARY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT TRANSPORT BY 10% BY YEAR 3 WHEN CLINICALLY APPROPRIATE AND SAFE AND REDUCE LAW ENFORCEMENT TIME SPENT ON BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS INCIDENTS BY 20% BY YEAR 3.   TO IMPROVE CONTINUITY OF CARE, THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE FOLLOW-UP CONTACT WITHIN 72 HOURS FOR AT LEAST 90% OF INDIVIDUALS SERVED, ENSURE THAT AT LEAST 80% OF INDIVIDUALS RECEIVE DOCUMENTED REFERRALS OR WARM HANDOFFS TO TREATMENT AND COMMUNITY SUPPORTS, INCREASE SUCCESSFUL LINKAGE TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES BY 25% BY YEAR 2 AND 40% BY YEAR 4, AND ACHIEVE AT LEAST 85% CLIENT SATISFACTION AMONG SURVEY RESPONDENTS BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD.   BY ESTABLISHING A SUSTAINABLE, COUNTYWIDE MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEM, YCMCTP WILL IMPROVE ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CARE, REDUCE RELIANCE ON COSTLY EMERGENCY RESPONSE SYSTEMS, STRENGTHEN PUBLIC SAFETY AND HEALTHCARE PARTNERSHIPS, AND IMPROVE OUTCOMES FOR INDIVIDUALS EXPERIENCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES THROUGHOUT YELLOWSTONE COUNTY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: CLARKSVILLE POLICE DEPARTMENT CO-RESPONDS WITH MENTAL HEALTH/CRISIS PROVIDERS. - CLARKSVILLE’S BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIP WITH CENTERSTONE (C-MCTP) WILL BENEFIT CLARKSVILLE RESIDENTS, SUPPORTING CAPACITY BUILDING EFFORTS TO DELIVER ENHANCED MOBILE CRISIS CO-RESPONSE TEAM SERVICES THAT AIM TO DIVERT INDIVIDUALS IN CRISIS FROM CRIMINAL JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT AND HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS, REDUCE DEATHS FROM SUICIDE AND OVERDOSE, ETC. C-MCTP WILL SERVE 600 INDIVIDUALS (I.E., Y1-Y4: 150/YR., ANNUALLY) VIA MOBILE CRISIS CO-RESPONSE. C-MCTP WILL BENEFIT/SERVE A FOCUS POPULATION COMPRISING INDIVIDUALS (AGES 5+) APPROPRIATE FOR CRISIS CO-RESPONSE SERVICES WHO ARE EXPERIENCING A MENTAL HEALTH OR SUD CRISIS IN CLARKSVILLE, TENNESSEE. IN 2021, ONLY 5% OF AREA LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS RECEIVED CIT TRAINING. FOCUS POPULATION CHARACTERISTICS ARE EXPECTED TO MIRROR MONTGOMERY COUNTY, COMPRISING 73% ADULTS AGES 18+ AND 23% CHILDREN/YOUTH AGES 5-17; APPROXIMATELY 50% ARE MALE, AND 50%, FEMALE. ANTICIPATED CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS INCLUDE AN ESTIMATED 26.5% OF ADULTS WITH ANY MENTAL ILLNESS (AMI) AND NEARLY 15% OF AREA YOUTH AGES 12-17 HAVE HAD SERIOUS THOUGHTS OF SUICIDE. APPROXIMATELY 26.5% OF ADULTS ARE EXPECTED TO HAVE SUD; 2%, OPIOID USE DISORDER; AND 9%, CO-OCCURRING SUD/AMI. ABOUT 29% OF THOSE WITH SMI ARE EXPECTED TO HAVE POLICE INVOLVED IN THEIR PATHWAY TO CARE. CHILD WELFARE SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT IS EXPECTED TO MIMIC THE STATE RATE OF 9.2%.  C-MCTP’S STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS TO INCREASE CAPACITY INCLUDE EXPANDED STAFF POSITIONS TO INCREASE ACCESS TO MOBILE CRISIS CO-RESPONSE AND POST-CRISIS SUPPORT SERVICES; EXPANDED COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS TO STRENGTHEN THE EXISTING CRISIS CARE CONTINUUM AND COLLABORATION; AND INCREASED ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TRAINING FOR THE SAFE AND SUCCESSFUL PREVENTION, EARLY IDENTIFICATION, AND/OR INTERVENTION OF CRISIS EVENTS (E.G., CIT, MHFA, CALM). C-MCTP’S 2-PERSON CO-RESPONSE TEAMS WILL PROVIDE IN-PERSON RESPONSE INCLUDING SCREENING/ASSESSMENT; COMMUNITY STABILIZATION; SAFETY PLANNING; REFERRAL TO ENHANCED SERVICES AFTER STABILIZATION; AND POST-CRISIS FOLLOW-UP. C-MCTP WILL CONDUCT COMMUNITY CRISIS MAPPING/PLANNING TO IDENTIFY SERVICE NEEDS/GAPS, PROVIDE CRISIS INTERVENTION TRAINING, DEVELOP PROTOCOLS TO IMPROVE COORDINATION WITH FIRST RESPONDERS AND COMMUNITY PROVIDERS, COORDINATE WITH RELEVANT STATE EFFORTS, AND IMPLEMENT A QI PLAN TO TRACK OUTCOMES. C-MCTP WILL ACCOMPLISH THE FOLLOWING GOALS: 1) DEVELOP A SOUND INFRASTRUCTURE TO EXPAND MOBILE CRISIS CO-RESPONSE SERVICES FOR CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND ADULTS (AGES 5+) RESIDING IN CLARKSVILLE, TENNESSEE; 2) INCREASE COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO IDENTIFY/ADDRESS EMERGING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH THREATS; PREVENT SUBSTANCE MISUSE, ABUSE, AND ADDICTION; AND ADDRESS SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS; 3) IMPROVE CRISIS SYSTEM PERFORMANCE VIA ENHANCED MCT CO-RESPONSE PROTOCOLS THAT ALIGN WITH BEST PRACTICES; 4) IMPROVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES VIA INCREASED ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT FOR MENTAL ILLNESS, SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER, AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS; AND 5) DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A PLAN TO SUPPORT FINANCIAL AND PROGRAMMATIC SUSTAINABILITY, ENSURING MOBILE CRISIS SERVICES AVAILABILITY CAN CONTINUE BEYOND THE FUNDING PERIOD. AS A RESULT OF THESE GOALS/IMPROVEMENTS, THE PROJECT WILL ACHIEVE THE FOLLOWING MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES AMONG POPULATIONS RECEIVING CRISIS RESPONSE: SCREEN 100%, REFER 100% TO NEEDED SERVICES, ACHIEVE ACCESS TO/USE OF SERVICES AMONG 60%, REDUCE SUICIDE RISK FOR 100%, AND REDUCE ARREST/DETENTION BY 30%. THE PROJECT WILL ACHIEVE THE FOLLOWING MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES IN COMMUNITY SERVED: RESOLVE 70% OF MCRT RESPONSES IN THE COMMUNITY, DIVERT 40% FROM LAW ENFORCEMENT ARREST, AND INCREASE KNOWLEDGE OF EFFECTIVE CRISIS RESPONSE AND OTHER BEST PRACTICES AMONG 60% OF INDIVIDUALS/PROVIDERS TRAINED.

description: NC BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIPS - NC DMHDDSUS PROPOSES TO IMPLEMENT A MAGISTRATE TO 988---MCT PATHWAY IN JUDICIAL DISTRICT 7 (JD7), CONNECTING AN EXISTING, PROVEN MOBILE CRISIS TEAM (MCT) RESOURCE TO MAGISTRATE DECISION-MAKING IN BERTIE, HALIFAX, HERTFORD, AND NORTHAMPTON COUNTIES BEFORE INVOLUNTARY COMMITMENT (IVC) CUSTODY ORDERS ARE ISSUED. IN JD7, INTEGRATED FAMILY SERVICES (IFS) ALREADY RESOLVES 89.9% OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH (BH) CRISES SAFELY IN THE COMMUNITY - YET OF 307 MCT RESPONSES IN FY 2025-26, ONLY 3 ORIGINATED FROM A MAGISTRATE REFERRAL. THIS GRANT CLOSES THAT INTEGRATION GAP, OPERATIONALIZING EXECUTIVE ORDER 33 AND HB 1104 AND BUILDING ON THE PROVEN AVERY/WATAUGA MODEL THAT REDUCED IVC RATES BY 60%. SAMHSA MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIPS (MCTP) FUNDING ENABLES NC DMHDDSUS, AS THE NC STATE BH CRISIS SYSTEM AUTHORITY, TO FORMALIZE THE MAGISTRATE-988-MCT CONNECTION THAT STATE LAW AND EXECUTIVE ACTION HAVE DIRECTED. NEED: NORTH CAROLINA'S IVC SYSTEM IS  SIGNIFICANTLY OVERUSED, MISUSED, AND HARMFUL  (DISABILITY RIGHTS NC, JUNE 2025). STATEWIDE, 63% OF IVC PETITIONS (AVG. 95,191/YEAR, 2019-2024) DID NOT RESULT IN COMMITMENT, YET EACH TRIGGERED LE TRANSPORT AND ED BOARDING AVERAGING 65.4 HOURS (NC-STEP, 2024). JD7'S FOUR COUNTIES ARE AMONG NC’S HIGHEST-POVERTY, RURAL COMMUNITIES, WITH ALL FOUR EXCEEDING THE 12.5% STATEWIDE POVERTY RATE (HALIFAX 22.8%, HERTFORD 21.4%, BERTIE 19.8%, NORTHAMPTON 15.2%). NO INPATIENT PSYCHIATRIC FACILITY EXISTS IN ANY OF THE FOUR COUNTIES. STRATEGIES: (1) FORMALIZE THE MAGISTRATE TO 988---MCT PATHWAY: WHEN A MAGISTRATE RECEIVES AN IVC PETITION, THE MAGISTRATE CALLS REAL CRISIS’S 988 BACKLINE, WHICH DISPATCHES IFS TO CONDUCT A COMMUNITY-BASED FIRST EXAMINATION BEFORE ANY CUSTODY ORDER IS ISSUED; (2) ENHANCE IFS MCT CAPACITY TOWARD 24/7/365 AVAILABILITY IN ALL FOUR JD7 COUNTIES; (3) EXECUTE FORMAL MOUS WITH COURTS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, PUBLIC SERVICE ANSWERING POINTS (PSAPS), EMS, AND HOSPITALS TO ENABLE CROSS-SYSTEM DATA COLLECTION AND ACCOUNTABILITY; (4) DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED TRAINING TO MAGISTRATES, LAW ENFORCEMENT, EMS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS; AND (5) DEVELOP A SUSTAINABILITY PLAN ANCHORED IN MEDICAID BILLING, 988 TELECOM FEES, AND LME/MCO (TRILLIUM HEALTH RESOURCES) CONTRACTS.

description: MULTNOMAH COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIPS ENHANCEMENT - MULTNOMAH COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENT (MCHD) PROPOSES THE MULTNOMAH COUNTY MOBILE CRISIS TEAM (MCT) PARTNERSHIPS ENHANCEMENT PROJECT, SERVING THE GEOGRAPHIC AREA OF MULTNOMAH COUNTY, OREGON. CURRENTLY, PARTNERSHIP PROTOCOLS DO NOT ALLOW MCHD’S BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MCTS TO ACT AS FIRST RESPONDERS TO 911 CALLERS INDEPENDENT OF LAW ENFORCEMENT. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WOULD CREATE THE STAFFING CAPACITY AND DEVELOP THE PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENTS NECESSARY TO ENABLE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MCTS TO RESPOND DIRECTLY AND INDEPENDENTLY TO 911 CRISIS CALLS.   LAW ENFORCEMENT WILL ESPECIALLY BENEFIT FROM THIS CAPACITY BUILDING, AS THEY WILL NO LONGER BE OVERBURDENED BY RESPONDING TO 911 CALLS THAT COULD BE HANDLED BY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH MCTS ALONE. BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT’S SERVICES INCLUDE ALL PEOPLE EXPERIENCING A BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS IN MULTNOMAH COUNTY. SUBPOPULATIONS OF FOCUS WILL INCLUDE YOUTH, VETERANS, AND JUSTICE-INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS, AS THESE GROUPS EXPERIENCE ESPECIALLY HIGH RATES OF MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE ISSUES, INCLUDING SUICIDE AND OVERDOSE.   STRATEGIES TO ACHIEVE THIS SYSTEM ENHANCEMENT INCLUDE PLANNING ACTIVITIES WITH KEY PARTNERS; DEVELOPING NEW PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENTS AND PROTOCOLS; HIRING ADDITIONAL MCT AND 911 BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ASSESSMENT STAFFING; AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT. THE PROJECT’S GOAL IS TO INCREASE DIVERSION OF INDIVIDUALS IN CRISIS FROM CRIMINAL JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT AND REDUCE DEATHS FROM SUICIDE AND OVERDOSE BY ESTABLISHING MULTNOMAH COUNTY MCT ABILITY TO RESPOND TO 911 CALLERS IN CRISIS INDEPENDENT OF LAW ENFORCEMENT. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE 1) CONVENE KEY PARTNERS TO STRENGTHEN MULTNOMAH COUNTY’S MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE SYSTEM BY CREATING A MCT SERVICES IMPLEMENTATION PLAN BY 1/31/2027, AND UPDATING THE PLAN AT LEAST ONCE PER SUBSEQUENT YEAR IN THE PROJECT PERIOD BASED ON CROSS-SYSTEM MAPPING AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT. 2)  CREATE AN ADDITIONAL MCT AND ASSOCIATED INFRASTRUCTURE TO RESPOND TO 911 CALLS INDEPENDENT FROM LAW ENFORCEMENT, BEGINNING SERVICE DELIVERY BY MARCH 31, 2027. 3) EACH YEAR OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, DELIVER 6 EVIDENCE-BASED CRISIS TRAININGS INCORPORATING EDUCATION ON THE PROJECT’S SYSTEM ENHANCEMENTS EACH YEAR FOR MCT STAFF; FIRST RESPONDERS (FIRE, EMS, LAW ENFORCEMENT); 988 AND 911 PERSONNEL; AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROFESSIONALS (24 TRAININGS BY SEPTEMBER 29, 2030).

description: KENTUCKY RAPID RESPONSE AND STABILIZATION SERVICES-KRRSS - THE KENTUCKY DEPARTMENT FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, DEVELOPMENTAL AND INTELLECTUAL DISABILITIES (DBHDID), THE COMMONWEALTH'S STATE MENTAL HEALTH AUTHORITY, PROPOSES TO ACCELERATE STATEWIDE IMPLEMENTATION OF KENTUCKY RAPID RESPONSE AND STABILIZATION SERVICES (KRRSS) THROUGH THE MOBILE CRISIS TEAM PARTNERSHIP (MCTP) PROGRAM, WHICH HAS BEEN DESIGNED TO PROVIDE RAPID, COMMUNITY-BASED, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH-LED CRISIS RESPONSE, STABILIZATION, AND LINKAGE TO ONGOING SUPPORTS. KENTUCKY IS A PREDOMINANTLY RURAL STATE WITH SIGNIFICANT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, AND GEOGRAPHIC DISPARITIES IN ACCESS TO CRISIS SERVICES. CHILDREN, YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS, AND FAMILIES EXPERIENCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES OFTEN ENCOUNTER FRAGMENTED SERVICE SYSTEMS AND MAY RELY ON EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS, INPATIENT HOSPITALIZATION, LAW ENFORCEMENT INVOLVEMENT, RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT, OR OTHER RESTRICTIVE INTERVENTIONS WHEN TIMELY COMMUNITY-BASED ALTERNATIVES ARE UNAVAILABLE. THESE CHALLENGES ARE PARTICULARLY PRONOUNCED IN RURAL, APPALACHIAN, AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. MCTP FUNDING WILL ACCELERATE IMPLEMENTATION OF KRRSS THROUGH A PHASED EARLY ADOPTER STRATEGY INVOLVING GEOGRAPHICALLY DIVERSE COMMUNITIES REPRESENTING URBAN, SUBURBAN, RURAL, AND APPALACHIAN REGIONS OF THE COMMONWEALTH. DBHDID WILL PARTNER WITH THE KENTUCKY DEPARTMENT FOR MEDICAID SERVICES (DMS), THE INNOVATIONS INSTITUTE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CONNECTICUT (UCONN), AND SELECTED EARLY ADOPTER IMPLEMENTATION SITES TO ESTABLISH OR ENHANCE MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE TEAMS; STRENGTHEN PARTNERSHIPS AMONG 988, EMERGENCY RESPONDERS, SCHOOLS, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, CHILD WELFARE AGENCIES, JUVENILE JUSTICE AGENCIES, COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH CENTERS, AND CERTIFIED COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINICS; AND IMPROVE DIVERSION PATHWAYS TO COMMUNITY-BASED CARE. THE PROJECT IS GUIDED BY FIVE GOALS: (1) ACCELERATE IMPLEMENTATION OF KRRSS THROUGH SELECTED EARLY ADOPTER SITES; (2) STRENGTHEN CROSS-SYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS AND DIVERSION PATHWAYS; (3) BUILD WORKFORCE CAPACITY, IMPLEMENTATION FIDELITY, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT TO THE MRSS-INFORMED MODEL; (4) ESTABLISH DATA, CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND SUSTAINABILITY INFRASTRUCTURE TO SUPPORT STATEWIDE SCALE-UP; AND (5) ENSURE MEANINGFUL YOUTH, FAMILY, AND LIVED EXPERIENCE LEADERSHIP THROUGHOUT IMPLEMENTATION. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE IMPLEMENTATION PLANNING, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, MOBILE CRISIS TEAM ENHANCEMENT, IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE COACHING, CRISIS SYSTEM PLANNING, CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, EVALUATION, AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING. THROUGH THESE EFFORTS, KENTUCKY WILL IMPROVE ACCESS TO TIMELY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS INTERVENTION AND STABILIZATION SERVICES, IMPROVE TIMELY ACCESS TO COMMUNITY-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISIS SERVICES, STRENGTHEN COORDINATION ACROSS KENTUCKY’S CRISIS CONTINUUM, REDUCE RELIANCE ON EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND OTHER RESTRICTIVE INTERVENTIONS, AND ESTABLISH A SUSTAINABLE, SCALABLE FRAMEWORK FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH-LED MOBILE CRISIS RESPONSE ACROSS THE LIFESPAN.

description: EAST PROVIDENCE STOP ACT INITIATIVE: REDUCING YOUTH ALCOHOL USE THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES, POLICY, EDUCATION, AND ENGAGEMENT TO PROMOTE HEALTHY LIFESTYLES. - THE EAST PROVIDENCE PREVENTION COALITION (EPPC) WILL IMPLEMENT THE SOBER TRUTH ON PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING (STOP ACT) PROJECT TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY CAPACITY AND REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12–20 IN EAST PROVIDENCE, RHODE ISLAND. USING THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK (SPF) AND CADCA'S SEVEN STRATEGIES FOR COMMUNITY CHANGE, EPPC WILL IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES, ENVIRONMENTAL APPROACHES, POLICY INITIATIVES, AND COMMUNITY COLLABORATION TO REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL AND STRENGTHEN PROTECTIVE FACTORS. STOP ACT FUNDING WILL STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF SCHOOLS, PARENTS, CAREGIVERS, YOUTH-SERVING ORGANIZATIONS, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, ALCOHOL RETAILERS, MUNICIPAL AGENCIES, AND OTHER COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO IMPLEMENT AND SUSTAIN COORDINATED PREVENTION EFFORTS. EAST PROVIDENCE IS RHODE ISLAND'S FIFTH-LARGEST MUNICIPALITY, WITH APPROXIMATELY 48,249 RESIDENTS, INCLUDING 7,928 YOUTH UNDER AGE 18. THE COMMUNITY EXPERIENCES SEVERAL FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE, INCLUDING FAVORABLE COMMUNITY ALCOHOL NORMS, HIGH ALCOHOL RETAILER DENSITY (93 LICENSED ESTABLISHMENTS), CHRONIC HIGH SCHOOL ABSENTEEISM (31%), AND EASY ACCESS TO ALCOHOL THROUGH BOTH COMMERCIAL AND SOCIAL SOURCES. MORE THAN HALF OF PUBLIC-SCHOOL STUDENTS ARE CLASSIFIED AS LOW INCOME, AND OVER 4,400 CHILDREN RECEIVE MEDICAL ASSISTANCE. LOCAL ASSESSMENT DATA INDICATE THAT ALCOHOL REMAINS ONE OF THE MOST COMMONLY USED SUBSTANCES AMONG YOUTH, DEMONSTRATING THE CONTINUED NEED TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY PREVENTION CAPACITY. EPPC WILL STRENGTHEN PREVENTION CAPACITY BY IMPLEMENTING EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION PROGRAMS, INCLUDING LIFESKILLS TRAINING, PREVENTION PLUS WELLNESS SPORT, INSHAPE, AND THE LIFESKILLS PARENT PROGRAM, ALONG WITH RESPONSIBLE BEVERAGE SERVICE TRAINING, ALCOHOL COMPLIANCE CHECKS, ENVIRONMENTAL SCANS, YOUTH LEADERSHIP THROUGH THE EAST PROVIDENCE YOUTH COUNCIL (EPYC), COMMUNITY EDUCATION CAMPAIGNS, STICKER SHOCK, LOCALLY ADAPTED TALK. THEY HEAR YOU. MATERIALS, COALITION MEETINGS, COMMUNITY FORUMS, AND POLICY INITIATIVES THAT SUPPORT LONG-TERM ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE. THE PROJECT WILL REDUCE PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH FROM 6% (2024) TO 4% BY 2030, DECREASE PERCEIVED EASE OF YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL FROM 38% TO 25%, INCREASE PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL OF UNDERAGE DRINKING FROM 78% TO 90%, AND INCREASE YOUTH PERCEPTION OF HARM AND PEER DISAPPROVAL, AS MEASURED THROUGH THE RHODE ISLAND STUDENT SURVEY (RISS) AND EPPC PARENT AND COMMUNITY SURVEYS. EPPC HAS DEMONSTRATED SUCCESS IMPLEMENTING COMMUNITY-BASED PREVENTION INITIATIVES AND HAS BEEN RECOGNIZED NATIONALLY AS A CADCA BLUE RIBBON COALITION AND 2023 CADCA COALITION OF THE YEAR. BY STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, INCREASING PREVENTION CAPACITY, AND IMPLEMENTING COORDINATED ENVIRONMENTAL STRATEGIES, THE PROPOSED STOP ACT PROJECT WILL REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AND CREATE HEALTHIER, SAFER ENVIRONMENTS FOR EAST PROVIDENCE YOUTH.

description: STOP ACT-GARVIN COUNTY - WICHITA MOUNTAINS PREVENTION NETWORK, A 501(C)(3) NONPROFIT ORGANIZATION LOCATED IN SOUTHERN OKLAHOMA, IS APPLYING TO BE THE SPONSORING AGENCY FOR THE PASS COALITION AS A SOBER TRUTH ON PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING ACT GRANTEE TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS IN GARVIN COUNTY RESIDENTS 12 TO 20 YEARS OF AGE. WMPN HAS A HOME OFFICE IN LAWTON AND A SATELLITE OFFICE IN ARDMORE THAT SERVES GARVIN COUNTY. GARVIN COUNTY IS A RURAL COUNTY LOCATED IN SOUTH-CENTRAL OKLAHOMA WITH A POPULATION OF 25,860. PASS IS A COMMUNITY COALITION THAT WAS ESTABLISHED IN 2017 BY A GROUP OF PARENTS CONCERNED ABOUT SUBSTANCE USE ISSUES IN LINDSAY PUBLIC SCHOOLS WHO DECIDED TO TAKE ACTION. IN 2021, PASS AND WMPN PARTNERED TO FACILITATE COMMUNITY-BASED PREVENTION SERVICES GRANTS THROUGHOUT THE WHOLE COUNTY. WHEN THE COALITION TRANSITIONED FROM LINDSAY TO SERVING THE WHOLE COUNTY, PASS'S CAPACITY CHANGED AND IS STILL IN NEED OF SUPPORT. PASS HAS A GOOD FOUNDATION OF KEY STAKEHOLDERS, BUT THE COALITION IS IN NEED OF CAPACITY BUILDING IN AREAS SUCH AS ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE REBUILDING, COALITION MEMBER RECRUITMENT, WORKING WITH AND OR ESTABLISHING A YOUTH ADVISORY GROUP, KNOWLEDGE OF EVIDENCED-BASED PRACTICES AND EFFECTIVE IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES, AS WELL AS IDENTIFYING AND ADDRESSING OVERLAPPING RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS AT A COMMUNITY LEVEL. THE STOP ACT GRANT WOULD PROVIDE THE TOOLS AND FUNDING FOR PASS TO INCREASE THE COALITION’S CAPACITY TO EFFECT POSITIVE CHANGE IN A RURAL LANDSCAPE WHERE EXISTING RESOURCES COULD BE MAXIMIZED TO ADDRESS CURRENT AND FUTURE CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE. PASS HAS AN EXISTING PARTNERSHIP WITH THE GARVIN COUNTY SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT WHO OVERSEES THE MAJORITY OF THE COUNTY’S STUDENT RESOURCE OFFICERS (SRO’S), AND HAS BEEN VITAL TO PREVENTION EFFORTS. THE SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT, PASS, AND SRO’S FROM ACROSS THE COUNTY HAVE ESTABLISHED REGULAR COLLABORATIVE MEETINGS TO DISCUSS ISSUES EACH SCHOOL IS FACING AND IDENTIFY SPECIFIC NEEDS TO ASSIST THE SCHOOLS, STUDENTS, AND THE OFFICERS. THESE MEETINGS HAVE HELPED IDENTIFY THAT UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE IS A MAJOR CONCERN. THERE IS A NEED FOR LAW ENFORCEMENT TRAINING ON ALCOHOL COMPLIANCE CHECKS OKLAHOMA’S SOCIAL HOST LAW, A LAW THAT HOLDS PEOPLE ACCOUNTABLE FOR ALLOWING UNDERAGE DRINKING ON THEIR PROPERTY. PASS HAS HAD YOUTH PARTICIPATE IN DEVELOPING MEDIA, VOLUNTEERING AT EVENTS, AND PARTICIPATING IN YOUTH FOCUS GROUPS. THE STOP ACT GRANT WOULD BE AN INCREDIBLE OPPORTUNITY TO EXPAND OUR YOUTH INVOLVEMENT INTO A MORE FORMALIZED ADVISORY GROUP THAT CAN CONTRIBUTE TO PREVENTION DECISIONS AND CO-HOST EVENTS SUCH AS PARTY DISPERSAL EXERCISES AND SAFE AFTER-PROM ACTIVITIES. THROUGH THIS OPPORTUNITY, PASS MEMBERS WILL UTILIZE THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK TO ASSESS THE NEEDS OF THE COMMUNITY, INCREASE COALITION CAPACITY TO ADDRESS IDENTIFIED NEEDS, DEVELOP A PLAN TO ADDRESS INDICATED NEEDS, IMPLEMENT APPROPRIATE PREVENTION STRATEGIES, AND EVALUATE THE PROGRESS AND OUTCOME OF OUR EFFORTS. THE GOAL OF THIS GRANT IS TO STRENGTHEN COLLABORATION AND INCREASE PASS’S CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AND RELATED PROBLEMS AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12-20, BY INCREASING ITS CAPACITY TO PREVENT SUBSTANCE USE AND RELATED MENTAL AND PHYSICAL HEALTH OUTCOMES. AS THE SPONSORING AGENCY, WMPN HAS THE EXPERIENCE TO MANAGE FEDERAL AND STATE GRANTS. WMPN CURRENTLY SERVES 5 COUNTIES IN SOUTHERN OKLAHOMA THROUGH GRANTS FUNDED BY THE OKLAHOMA DEPARTMENT OF MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE ABUSE SERVICES, THE SUBSTANCE ABUSE AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ADMINISTRATION, AND THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL. THESE OPPORTUNITIES HAVE ALLOWED WMPN TO ADDRESS SCOPES OF ALCOHOL, CANNABIS, OPIOIDS, STIMULANTS, AND TOBACCO. WMPN AND THE MEMBERS OF PASS ARE SEEKING STOP ACT GRANT FUNDING DUE TO THE NEED FOR ADDITIONAL RESOURCES TO ADDRESS SUBSTANCE USE AND PREVENT FURTHER DAMAGE TO THE WELL-BEING OF GARVIN COUNTY YOUTH AND FUTURE GENERATIONS.

description: THE PREVENTION OF UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AND IMPAIRED BOATING - UPLIFT IRONDEQUOIT (D-FI DRUG-FREE IRONDEQUOIT TOGETHER) PROPOSES TO IMPLEMENT THE FY2026 SOBER TRUTH ON PREVENTING (STOP) UNDERAGE DRINKING ACT PROJECT. OUR PROJECT IS ENTITLED,  THE PREVENTION OF UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AND ALCOHOL-IMPAIRED BOATING . FOR THIS PROJECT, OUR FOCUS POPULATION WILL BE YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 16-20 RESIDING IN THE TOWN OF IRONDEQUOIT AND ITS SHARED ZIP CODES WITH THE CITY OF ROCHESTER (14609, 14617, 14621, 14622).  THE PROPOSED PROJECT AIMS TO ADDRESS A SIGNIFICANT PREVENTION NEED IN OUR COMMUNITY. OUR COMMUNITY IS CHARACTERIZED BY ITS UNIQUE WATERFRONT ACCESS, INCLUDING THE IRONDEQUOIT BAY, LAKE ONTARIO, AND THE GENESEE RIVER. GIVEN THIS, WATERFRONT RECREATION IS POPULAR WITHIN OUR COMMUNITY DURING THE SPRING AND SUMMER MONTHS. OUR COMMUNITY HOUSES NUMEROUS BOAT LAUNCHES, MARINAS, AND WATERFRONT RESTAURANTS AND BARS, MAKING POPULAR GATHERING SPACES FOR YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS IN OUR COMMUNITY. THESE CHARACTERIZATIONS PROVIDE INCREASED OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AND IMPAIRED BOATING AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS. CURRENT DATA REVEALS ONGOING CONCERNS RELATED TO YOUTH ALCOHOL USE. HOWEVER, THERE IS A SIGNIFICANT ASSESSMENT GAP, AS EXISTING SYSTEMS OF DATA COLLECTION DO NOT ADEQUATELY CAPTURE INDIVIDUALS AGES 18-20, AS WELL AS BOATING-RELATED ALCOHOL BEHAVIORS. THROUGH THIS PROJECT, THE COALITION WILL CONDUCT ADDITIONAL ASSESSMENT ACTIVITIES TO ADDRESS THIS SERVICE GAP AND TO BETTER UNDERSTAND LOCAL CONDITIONS THAT WILL GUIDE EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION EFFORTS.  THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT, UPLIFT WILL STRENGTHEN COALITION CAPACITY BY ENGAGING IN NEW COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, ENGAGING INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES, AND EXPANDING A YOUTH ADVISORY COMMITTEE THAT IS REFLECTIVE OF THE FOCUS POPULATION. WE WILL CONDUCT A COMMUNITY READINESS ASSESSMENT, CONDUCT LISTENING SESSIONS, AND DEVELOP AND ADMINISTER A NEW COALITION SURVEY TO GATHER INPUT AND TO ESTABLISH BASELINE DATA ON UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE, PERCEPTION OF HARM, PEER AND PARENTAL PERCEPTIONS, BOATING BEHAVIORS, AND IMPAIRED BOATING, AMONG YOUTH AGES 16-20 IN OUR CATCHMENT AREA. THESE FINDINGS WILL ASSIST THE COALITION IN IDENTIFYING EVIDENCE-BASED, EVIDENCE-INFORMED, AND COMMUNITY-DEFINED ENVIRONMENTAL PREVENTION STRATEGIES THAT EFFECTIVELY ADDRESS THE ASSESSED NEEDS OF THE COMMUNITY.  THE COALITION WILL ENGAGE IN PROJECT ACTIVITIES, INCLUDING COALITION CAPACITY BUILDING, THE EXPANSION OF THE YOUTH ADVISORY COMMITTEE, EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION TRAINING, EDUCATIONAL MEDIA CAMPAIGNS, COMMUNITY OUTREACH, INTERGOVERNMENTAL COLLABORATION, AND ENVIRONMENTAL PREVENTION INITIATIVES. THESE ACTIVITIES WILL BE SELECTED AND IMPLEMENTED BASED ON THE ASSESSED NEEDS OF THE COMMUNITY AND WILL AIM TO REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AND IMPAIRED BOATING. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL EXPAND PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS, SUCH AS SCHOOLS, COLLEGES, MARINAS, WATERFRONT BUSINESSES AND ORGANIZATIONS, MARINE LAW ENFORCEMENT, PREVENTION ORGANIZATIONS, AND OTHER COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS.  AS A RESULT OF THIS PROJECT, THE COALITION EXPECTS TO HAVE INCREASED CAPACITY, EXPANDED COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, IMPROVED LOCAL ASSESSMENT DATA FOR YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 16-20, INCREASED AWARENESS OF IMPAIRED BOATING, IMPROVED PERCEPTION OF HARM, REDUCED SOCIAL ACCESS TO ALCOHOL, AND IMPLEMENTED SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY STRATEGIES TO ADDRESS UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AND IMPAIRED BOATING.

description: OSWEGO COUNTY YOUTH ALCOHOL PREVENTION AND ENFORCEMENT (YAPE) INITIATIVE - THE OSWEGO COUNTY PREVENTION COALITION (OCPC), UNDER THE PREVENTION SERVICES DEPARTMENT OF FARNHAM FAMILY SERVICES, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS WILL IMPLEMENT THE YOUTH ALCOHOL PREVENTION AND ENFORCEMENT (YAPE) INITIATIVE IN THE RURAL CATCHMENT AREA OF OSWEGO COUNTY, NEW YORK, WITH A SPECIFIC FOCUS ON THE PULASKI AND ALTMAR-PARISH-WILLIAMSTOWN (APW) SCHOOL DISTRICTS. THE CAPACITY-BUILDING EFFORTS WILL IMPACT MIDDLE AND HIGH SCHOOL YOUTH (AGES 12-18), ALONG WITH THEIR PARENTS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS, TO ADDRESS UNDERAGE DRINKING IN A REGION MARKED BY GEOGRAPHIC ISOLATION, ELEVATED POVERTY, AND LIMITED ACCESS TO PREVENTION SERVICES. SOBER TRUTH ON PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING ACT (STOP-ACT) FUNDING WILL ALLOW OCPC TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 12-20 IN THE MOST RURAL PARTS OF OSWEGO COUNTY THROUGH DIRECT COLLABORATION WITH SCHOOL, LAW ENFORCEMENT, HEALTHCARE, AND GOVERNMENT SECTOR PARTNERS. THE PROJECT CONSISTS OF A 4-YEAR ACTION PLAN (SEPTEMBER 30, 2026 - SEPTEMBER 29, 2030) BUILT AROUND THREE GOALS: GOAL 1, ENHANCE COMMUNITY-DRIVEN PREVENTION OF UNDERAGE DRINKING THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES AND MEANINGFUL YOUTH ADVISORY GROUP ENGAGEMENT; GOAL 2, PROMOTE INTERGOVERNMENTAL AND COMMUNITY COLLABORATION TO REDUCE YOUTH ALCOHOL USE THROUGH COORDINATED ACTIONS; AND GOAL 3, IMPLEMENT A STRATEGIC PLANNING FRAMEWORK TO SUPPORT AND ENHANCE COMMUNITY-DRIVEN PREVENTION EFFORTS. THESE GOALS ARE GROUNDED IN THE 2026 ISA DATA YOUTH DEVELOPMENT SURVEY (FORMERLY PRIDE SURVEYS), WHICH FOUND PAST-30-DAY YOUTH ALCOHOL USE HOLDING STEADY AT 14.6% DESPITE RISING PROTECTIVE FACTORS, INCLUDING INCREASED PERCEPTION OF RISK (66% TO 71.7%) AND PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL (85.1% TO 86.4%) - INDICATING THAT CURRENT COALITION-LED PREVENTION EFFORTS ARE SHIFTING NORMS BUT HAVE NOT YET REDUCED ACTUAL USE. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE DECREASING PAST-30-DAY ALCOHOL USE TO 12.0%, INCREASING PERCEPTION OF RISK TO 76.0%, DECREASING PERCEPTION OF ALCOHOL AVAILABILITY TO 22.0%, AND INCREASING PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL TO 90.0%, ALL BY SEPTEMBER 29, 2030. THE PROJECT WILL COLLABORATE WITH THE COALITION'S SCHOOL SECTOR ACROSS THE PULASKI AND APW DISTRICTS, ENGAGING 100 STUDENTS PER SEMESTER IN EVIDENCE-BASED EDUCATION THROUGH THE ALCOHOL LITERACY CHALLENGE (ALC), A SINGLE-SESSION INTERVENTION RECOGNIZED BY SAMHSA, DELIVERED BY FARNHAM'S STUDENT ASSISTANCE COUNSELORS IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE NEW YORK UPSTATE POISON CONTROL CENTER. THE COALITION WILL CONDUCT FOUR ALC CLASSROOM PRESENTATIONS PER SEMESTER AND DEVELOP 25 ORIGINAL MEDIA MATERIALS ANNUALLY, PROJECTING A COMBINED REACH OF 2,500 ADULTS AND YOUTH. YOUTH LEADERS IN ACTION (YLA), OCPC'S EXISTING YOUTH ADVISORY BODY, WILL BE ENGAGED FROM IDEATION THROUGH IMPLEMENTATION ON ALL ASPECTS OF THE INITIATIVE. ENFORCEMENT EFFORTS WILL FOCUS ON COMPLIANCE CHECKS, EXPANDED LAW ENFORCEMENT PATROLS IN IDENTIFIED UNDERAGE DRINKING HOTSPOTS, AND COMMUNITY EDUCATION. LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT WILL CONDUCT COMPLIANCE CHECKS ON TWO BARS/RESTAURANTS AND TWO LIQUOR STORES BIENNIALLY TO MAINTAIN ACCOUNTABILITY WITHOUT OVERBURDENING THE SMALL NUMBER OF RETAILERS IN THIS RURAL CATCHMENT AREA. IN COLLABORATION WITH OSWEGO COUNTY STOP-DWI, THE PROJECT WILL EXPAND MOCK DWI DEMONSTRATIONS TO INCLUDE ATVS AND SNOWMOBILES, REFLECTING THE RECREATIONAL CULTURE AND UNIQUE RISK FACTORS OF RURAL COMMUNITIES WHERE SOME ESTABLISHMENTS ARE ACCESSIBLE ONLY BY THESE VEHICLES. THE COALITION WILL ALSO CONVENE TWO TOWN HALL MEETINGS ANNUALLY TO GATHER PUBLIC FEEDBACK AND PRESENT SURVEY FINDINGS TO UNDERSERVED AND GEOGRAPHICALLY ISOLATED COMMUNITIES. THIS PROJECT BUILDS ON OCPC'S DECADE-PLUS HISTORY AS AN ACTIVE COALITION WITH REPRESENTATION ACROSS COMMUNITY SECTORS, AND FORMALLY EXTENDS EXISTING PARTNERSHIPS WITH FARNHAM INC., OSWEGO COUNTY STOP-DWI, AND SCHOOL AND LAW ENFORCEMENT SECTOR PARTNERS, CONSISTENT WITH SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES AND THE ADMINISTRATION'S MAKE AMERICA HEALTHY AGAIN (MAHA) INITATIVE.

description: MERIDEN HEALTHY YOUTH COALITION SOBER TRUTH ON PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING - RUSHFORD CENTER, INC., FISCAL AGENT FOR THE MERIDEN HEALTHY YOUTH COALITION (MHYC), REQUESTS STOP ACT GRANT FUNDING TO BUILD MHYC'S CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 12 TO 20 IN MERIDEN, CONNECTICUT. MERIDEN YOUTH REPORT DECLINING BUT STILL CONCERNING RATES OF ALCOHOL USE, AND NATIONAL DATA SHOW THAT STAGNANT RISK PERCEPTION COMBINED WITH GROWING EXPOSURE TO DIGITAL ALCOHOL MARKETING THREATENS TO ERODE LOCAL PREVENTION GAINS. THIS PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN COALITION INFRASTRUCTURE, FORMALIZE YOUTH LEADERSHIP, AND UPDATE PREVENTION MESSAGING TO ADDRESS THESE EMERGING RISKS OVER A 48-MONTH PROJECT PERIOD. MHYC WILL BUILD CAPACITY TO SERVE THE CITY OF MERIDEN, A 24-SQUARE-MILE URBAN COMMUNITY BISECTED BY INTERSTATES 91 AND 691. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS YOUTH AGES 12 TO 20, WITH PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO STUDENTS IN GRADES 6 THROUGH 12 ATTENDING MERIDEN PUBLIC SCHOOLS.  MERIDEN'S POPULATION IS APPROXIMATELY 60,830 RESIDENTS. THE COMMUNITY CARRIES DUAL FEDERAL DESIGNATIONS AS A HEALTH PROFESSIONAL SHORTAGE AREA FOR MENTAL HEALTH AND A MEDICALLY UNDERSERVED AREA. LOCAL DATA SHOW THAT WHILE LIFETIME AND PAST-MONTH ALCOHOL USE AMONG MERIDEN YOUTH REMAIN LOW, MHYC'S MOST RECENT ALCOHOL-SPECIFIC FUNDING CYCLE ENDED SEVERAL YEARS AGO, AND CURRENT PREVENTION EFFORTS HAVE CONCENTRATED ON OTHER SUBSTANCES, LEAVING A CAPACITY GAP IN DEDICATED ALCOHOL-FOCUSED COORDINATION, STAFF TRAINING, AND YOUTH-LED MESSAGING SUITED TO TODAY'S SOCIAL MEDIA ENVIRONMENT.  UNDER THIS GRANT, MHYC WILL IDENTIFY AND IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION STRATEGIES DRAWN FROM THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK AND CADCA'S SEVEN STRATEGIES FOR COMMUNITY LEVEL CHANGE. WITHIN 120 DAYS, THE COALITION WILL FORMALIZE ITS YOUTH ADVISORY GROUP, DEVELOP A LOGIC MODEL AND 12-MONTH ACTION PLAN, AND CONVENE COMMUNITY FORUMS TO GATHER PUBLIC INPUT. PLANNED STRATEGIES INCLUDE ADAPTING SAMHSA'S  TALK. THEY HEAR YOU.®  CAMPAIGN FOR MERIDEN AUDIENCES, DISTRIBUTING PREVENTION MESSAGING THROUGH SCHOOL, BUSINESS, AND MEDIA SECTOR PARTNERS, CONDUCTING ALCOHOL RETAILER COMPLIANCE CHECKS AND TIPS TRAINING, PROMOTING CONNECTICUT'S SOCIAL HOST LAW, AND DEVELOPING YOUTH-LED DIGITAL CAMPAIGNS TO COUNTER ALGORITHM-DRIVEN ALCOHOL MARKETING.  MHYC'S GOALS ARE TO STRENGTHEN COALITION CAPACITY, REDUCE AND PREVENT YOUTH ALCOHOL USE, AND INCREASE COMMUNITY AND PUBLIC CONSEQUENCES FOR UNDERAGE DRINKING. BY SEPTEMBER 2029, MHYC AIMS TO INCREASE COALITION MEMBERSHIP BY 30 PERCENT (FROM 12 TO 16 MEMBERS), INCREASE THE PERCENTAGE OF MERIDEN YOUTH IN GRADES 6 THROUGH 12 WHO BELIEVE UNDERAGE DRINKING IS WRONG, AND INCREASE THE PERCENTAGE OF YOUTH WHO PERCEIVE ALCOHOL AS DIFFICULT TO ACCESS, ALL AS MEASURED BY THE YOUTH VOICES COUNT SURVEY. THESE OBJECTIVES DIRECTLY RESPOND TO THE LOCAL NEED FOR RENEWED, ALCOHOL-SPECIFIC PREVENTION CAPACITY DOCUMENTED IN THE STATEMENT OF NEED.

description: SOUTH COUNTY YOUTH ALCOHOL INITIATIVE - THE 3-D COMMUNICATIONS, INC. WILL IMPLEMENT THE SAMHSA SOBER TRUTH ON PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING ACT GRANTS (STOP ACT) TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG HIGH SCHOOL YOUTH AGES 14 TO 18 IN SOUTH COUNTY OF PRINCE GEORGE'S COUNTY, MARYLAND. THE GOALS ARE TO: (1) IMPLEMENT ACTIVITIES THAT SUPPORT CAPACITY BUILDING, SUCH AS IMPLEMENTING EVIDENCE-BASED COMMUNITY APPROACHES AND (2) ENHANCE COLLABORATION, COOPERATION, AND COORDINATION AMONG COMMUNITIES, FEDERAL, STATE, TERRITORIAL, AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS MALE AND FEMALE HIGH SCHOOL YOUTH AGES 12 TO 17 RESIDING IN SOUTHERN PRINCE GEORGE'S COUNTY, THE RURAL PART OF THE COUNTY. ACCORDING TO THE 2024 CENSUS DATA, YOUTH AGES 10-19 TOTAL 11,949 (9.9% OF THE COUNTY POPULATION), 50.8% MALE AND 49.2% FEMALE.   THE CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT NEEDED IS TO BUILD A COORDINATED COMMUNITY PREVENTION SYSTEM BY EXPANDING THE PREVENTION WORKFORCE, STRENGTHENING COLLABORATION AMONG PREVENTION PROVIDERS, ENGAGING YOUTH AND PARENTS AS PREVENTION PARTNERS, AND IMPLEMENTING EVIDENCE-BASED/INFORMED AND COMMUNITY DEFINED STRATEGIES THAT REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING AND PROMOTE ALCOHOL-FREE NORMS.   THE OBJECTIVES ARE: OBJECTIVE 1: CONDUCT A NEEDS ASSESSMENT TO IDENTIFY THE COMMUNITY NORMS REGARDING ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 14 TO 18.  OBJECTIVE 2: IDENTIFY, ESTABLISH, AND IMPLEMENT ONE EVIDENCE-BASED, EVIDENCE-INFORMED, OR COMMUNITY-DEFINED PREVENTION STRATEGY TO EXPAND AND INCREASE YPCI’S DFC CAPACITY.  OBJECTIVE 3: CONDUCT COMMUNITY TAILORED ALCOHOL PREVENTION EDUCATION AND INFORMATION DISSEMINATION THROUGH A SOCIAL NORMS CAMPAIGN AND SOCIAL MEDIA CAMPAIGN.  OBJECTIVE 4: ESTABLISH A YOUTH UNDERAGE DRINKING ADVISORY TASKFORCE AS A PART OF THE DFC’S YOUTH ADVISORY COUNCIL TO PROVIDE STOP PROGRAM INPUT FROM IDEATION TO IMPLEMENTATION.  OBJECTIVE 5: ESTABLISH A COMMUNITY-WIDE UNDERAGE DRINKING TASKFORCE TO INCREASE CITIZEN PARTICIPATION TO FACILITATE PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING.  OBJECTIVE 6: REVIEW THE STATE PERFORMANCE AND BEST PRACTICES FOR THE PREVENTION AND REDUCTION OF UNDERAGE DRINKING REPORT AND IDENTIFY WHICH POLICIES, PROGRAMS, AND PRACTICES NEED TO BE ADDED OR MODIFIED TO MAXIMIZE THE STOP PROGRAM’S IMPACT TO PREVENT AND REDUCE OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERAGE DRINKING.   OBJECTIVE 7: CREATE A PREVENTION CORPS TO REDUCE THE NEGATIVE CONSEQUENCES ASSOCIATED WITH UNDERAGE DRINKING.  OBJECTIVE 8: SUPPORT FOUR (4) PREVENTION CORPS MEMBERS TO BECOME CERTIFIED PREVENTION SPECIALISTS.

description: STOP UNDERAGE DRINKING PISCATAQUIS COUNTY - MRH CORP D/B/A/ NORTHERN LIGHT MAYO HOSPITAL’S PISCATAQUIS YOUTH SUBSTANCE USE PREVENTION COALITION (PYSUP) PROJECT, STOP UNDERAGE DRINKING PISCATAQUIS COUNTY, AIMS TO BOLSTER ALCOHOL PREVENTION EFFORTS IN RURAL MAINE. DATA INDICATES AREA YOUTH ARE ENGAGING IN HIGH-RISK DRINKING PATTERNS AND AT EARLIER AGES.  EXPANDING EFFORTS AND INCREASING CAPACITY IS ESSENTIAL TO HAVING A GREATER AND LASTING IMPACT ON THE REDUCTION OF YOUTH ALCOHOL USE IN THE REGION.   ALL LOCATIONS WHERE THE POPULATION OF FOCUS (POF), APPROXIMATELY 1,800 YOUNG PEOPLE BETWEEN THE AGES OF 12-20, RESIDE IN PISCATAQUIS COUNTY AND DEXTER, MAINE, ARE DESIGNATED RURAL. SUBSTANCE USE PREVENTION AND TREATMENT RESOURCES ARE LIMITED, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS RELY ON STRONG COLLABORATION WITH MULTI-SECTOR ORGANIZATIONS TO REACH REMOTE TOWNS AND RESIDENTS. EXPANDED PARTNERSHIPS WILL ENHANCE ACCESS, REDUCE BARRIERS, AND IMPROVE CONNECTIONS BETWEEN SYSTEMS AND SERVICES THAT SEEK TO PREVENT YOUTH ALCOHOL USE. MAYO HOSPITAL STAFF WILL WORK IN CLOSE PARTNERSHIP WITH LOCAL AND STATE PREVENTION ORGANIZATIONS TO COMPLEMENTARILY PROVIDE THE MOST CURRENT INFORMATION, BEST PRACTICE APPROACHES, AND EVIDENCE-BASED PROGRAMMING TO THE POF AND WITHIN THEIR COMMUNITIES TO EFFECTIVELY ADDRESS CONCERNING YOUTH ALCOHOL USE IN THE REGION.   AREA YOUTH INDICATE A LOW PERCEPTION OF RISK RELATED TO UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE, AND LOW PERCEPTION OF RISK FROM THE CONSUMPTION OF FIVE OR MORE DRINKS IN ONE SETTING (BINGE DRINKING). CORRESPONDINGLY, THE POF INDICATES HIGHER THAN STATE AVERAGES FOR PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE. THE POF ALSO REFLECTS A CONCERNING INCREASE IN THE NUMBER WHOSE PERCEPTION OF PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL OF YOUTH ALCOHOL USE IS ‘LITTLE’ OR ‘NOT WRONG AT ALL’. SOCIAL NORMS AROUND UNDERAGE DRINKING WITH THIS POPULATION INCLUDE A HIGH PERCENTAGE OF STUDENTS REPORTING THAT THEIR PARENTS ACCEPT ALCOHOL USE (1-2 DRINKS PER DAY). FURTHER, THERE HAS BEEN AN INCREASE IN RECENT YEARS IN THE NUMBER OF MIDDLES SCHOOL STUDENTS WHO ARE USING ALCOHOL.  THE PYSUP COALITION WILL UTILIZE THE STOP ACT GRANT TO ACHIEVE ITS GOAL OF FURTHER REDUCING YOUTH ALCOHOL USE, ALTERING YOUTH PERCEPTIONS, INCREASE PROTECTIVE FACTORS, AND DECREASE RISK FACTORS CONTRIBUTING TO UNDERAGE USE. THE PYSUP COALITION HAS DEVELOPED A FOUR-YEAR TIMELINE OF STRATEGIC APPROACHES AND WILL DEVELOP AN ACTION PLAN EACH YEAR OF PROGRAMMING THAT IS RESPONSIVE TO NEWLY RELEASED MAINE INTEGRATED YOUTH HEALTH SURVEY DATA AND COMMUNITY CONDITIONS. AT THE ONSET, COMPLIANCE CHECKS WILL BE CONDUCTED TO PROTECT AGAINST YOUTH OBTAINING ALCOHOL FROM RETAIL SOURCES. RESPONSIBLE BEVERAGE SERVICE TRAINING WILL BE PROVIDED TO BOTH ON- AND OFF-PREMISE LIQUOR LICENSEES.  ANOTHER OBJECTIVE IS TO INCREASE YOUTHS’ PERCEPTIONS OF THE LIKELIHOOD THAT UNDERAGE DRINKERS WILL BE CAUGHT BY LAW ENFORCEMENT. THIS WILL BE ACHIEVED VIA PARTY PATROLS PROVIDED BY LAW ENFORCEMENT PARTNERS, SOCIAL MEDIA CAMPAIGNS, AND EDUCATION FROM LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICIALS. PYSUP WILL ALSO CONTINUE TO NURTURE AND SUPPORT YOUTH POSITIVE ACTION TEAMS IN AREA SCHOOLS TO EMPOWER YOUTH VOICE AND PEER INFLUENCE.

description: STRENGTHENING RURAL CAPACITY TO PREVENT UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE THROUGH COMMUNITY COLLABORATION AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT - PROJECT ABSTRACT: STRENGTHENING RURAL CAPACITY TO PREVENT UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE THROUGH COMMUNITY COLLABORATION AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT  PROSSER THRIVE COALITION WILL IMPLEMENT THE STOP ACT PROJECT, STRENGTHENING RURAL CAPACITY TO PREVENT UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE THROUGH COMMUNITY COLLABORATION AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT, TO INCREASE COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 12–20 IN PROSSER, WASHINGTON. THROUGH STRENGTHENED COALITION INFRASTRUCTURE, YOUTH ENGAGEMENT, FAMILY EDUCATION, AND COORDINATED PREVENTION STRATEGIES, THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT HEALTHIER ENVIRONMENTS WHERE YOUTH CAN THRIVE AND MAKE HEALTHY CHOICES.  THE PROJECT WILL SERVE THE CITY OF PROSSER, A RURAL AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITY LOCATED IN BENTON COUNTY, WASHINGTON, WITH APPROXIMATELY 6,366 RESIDENTS AND APPROXIMATELY 2,450 STUDENTS SERVED BY PROSSER SCHOOL DISTRICT. THE POPULATION BENEFITING FROM CAPACITY BUILDING INCLUDES PROSSER THRIVE COALITION, ITS COMMUNITY PREVENTION PARTNERS, AND THE SYSTEMS THAT INFLUENCE YOUTH ENVIRONMENTS, INCLUDING SCHOOLS, FAMILIES, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, LOCAL GOVERNMENT, BUSINESSES, AND YOUTH-SERVING ORGANIZATIONS. CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT NEEDS INCLUDE STRENGTHENING COORDINATED PREVENTION PLANNING, EXPANDING YOUTH AND FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, IMPROVING COMMUNITY COLLABORATION, AND INCREASING THE SUSTAINABILITY OF ENVIRONMENTAL PREVENTION STRATEGIES ADDRESSING UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE.  THE POPULATION SERVED THROUGH EXPANDED PREVENTION ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE YOUTH AGES 12–20, PRIMARILY MIDDLE AND HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, ALONG WITH PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS. YOUTH PARTICIPANTS WILL BENEFIT FROM INCREASED ACCESS TO ALCOHOL-FREE ENVIRONMENTS, POSITIVE PEER ACTIVITIES, LEADERSHIP OPPORTUNITIES, TRUSTED ADULTS, AND PREVENTION EDUCATION. FAMILY AND COMMUNITY PARTICIPANTS WILL BENEFIT FROM PREVENTION RESOURCES AND ENGAGEMENT OPPORTUNITIES DESIGNED TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNICATION AND REINFORCE COMMUNITY NORMS THAT DISCOURAGE UNDERAGE DRINKING.  USING THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK (SPF) AND CADCA’S SEVEN STRATEGIES FOR COMMUNITY CHANGE, THRIVE WILL IMPLEMENT CAPACITY-BUILDING STRATEGIES INCLUDING COMMUNITY ASSESSMENT, LOGIC MODEL AND ACTION PLAN DEVELOPMENT, YOUTH ADVISORY ENGAGEMENT, CROSS-SECTOR PARTNERSHIP COORDINATION, EVIDENCE-INFORMED PREVENTION CAMPAIGNS, CAREGIVER EDUCATION, AND EXPANSION OF THE THRIVE YOUTH CAFÉ AS AN ENVIRONMENTAL PREVENTION STRATEGY.  PROJECT GOALS ARE TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE, INCREASE PROTECTIVE FACTORS, EXPAND ALCOHOL-FREE YOUTH OPPORTUNITIES, STRENGTHEN FAMILY AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, AND SUSTAIN COORDINATED PREVENTION EFFORTS. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: (1) COMPLETING A COMMUNITY ASSESSMENT, LOGIC MODEL, AND 12-MONTH ACTION PLAN WITHIN THE FIRST SIX MONTHS; (2) ENGAGING YOUTH THROUGH MUSTANG THRIVE YOUTH COALITIONS TO PROVIDE MEANINGFUL INPUT INTO PREVENTION STRATEGIES; (3) EXPANDING YOUTH CAFÉ PREVENTION PROGRAMMING TO ENGAGE AT LEAST 75 YOUTH ANNUALLY; (4) IMPLEMENTING PARENT AND COMMUNITY PREVENTION ACTIVITIES ANNUALLY; AND (5) MONITORING CHANGES IN YOUTH ENGAGEMENT, PROTECTIVE FACTORS, COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, AND PREVENTION CAPACITY THROUGH ONGOING EVALUATION.  THROUGH STOP ACT FUNDING, PROSSER THRIVE COALITION WILL STRENGTHEN THE COMMUNITY SYSTEMS, RELATIONSHIPS, AND PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE NEEDED TO MAINTAIN LONG-TERM REDUCTIONS IN UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AND SUPPORT POSITIVE OUTCOMES FOR YOUTH AND FAMILIES.
