description: YOUTH SOBRIETY MOVEMENT - FIGHTING BACK SANTA MARIA VALLEY'S (FBSMV)  YOUTH SOBRIETY MOVEMENT  PROJECT IS A YOUTH-LED INITIATIVE TO PREVENT AND REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12-20 IN THE SANTA MARIA VALLEY. THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE LOCAL CAPACITY TO PREVENT SUBSTANCE MISUSE, ABUSE, AND ADDICTION BY USING DATA-DRIVEN, EVIDENCE-INFORMED, AND COMMUNITY-DEFINED STRATEGIES TO REDUCE EARLY ALCOHOL USE, STRENGTHEN PROTECTIVE FACTORS, AND PREVENT LONG-TERM BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY CONSEQUENCES.  STOP ACT FUNDING WILL BUILD COALITION CAPACITY BY FORMALIZING THE FBSMV YOUTH ACTION COALITION AS THE YOUTH ADVISORY BODY FOR THE PROJECT. THE YOUTH ACTION COALITION WILL WORK WITH THE FBSMV COMMUNITY COALITION TO ENGAGE COMMUNITY SECTORS, IDENTIFY GAPS, STRENGTHEN RELATIONSHIPS, AND DEVELOP A LOGIC MODEL AND 12-MONTH ACTION PLAN TO GUIDE UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION STRATEGIES.  THE PROJECT WILL SERVE NORTHERN SANTA BARBARA COUNTY, INCLUDING THE CITY OF SANTA MARIA, THE CITY OF GUADALUPE, AND THE UNINCORPORATED COMMUNITY OF ORCUTT, WITH A COMBINED POPULATION OF MORE THAN 154,000 RESIDENTS. THE CATCHMENT AREA INCLUDES COMMUNITIES EXPERIENCING SIGNIFICANT ECONOMIC AND PREVENTION ACCESS DISPARITIES. ACCORDING TO 2023 CENSUS DATA, PER CAPITA INCOME VARIES FROM $21,100 IN GUADALUPE, WITH 27.7% POVERTY, TO $27,440 IN SANTA MARIA, WITH 17.3% POVERTY, AND $49,979 IN ORCUTT, WITH 8.0% POVERTY. LOCAL SCHOOLS SERVING THE TARGET POPULATION INCLUDE HIGH PERCENTAGES OF HISPANIC/LATINO STUDENTS, ENGLISH LEARNERS, AND FAMILIES EXPERIENCING POVERTY. RECENT 2024-2025 CHKS DATA SHOW EARLY ALCOHOL INITIATION WITH GUADALUPE STUDENTS REPORTING INCREASES FROM 7TH TO 8TH GRADE IN LIFETIME ALCOHOL USE, PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE, AND BINGE DRINKING. AMONG SANTA MARIA JOINT UNION HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE WAS REPORTED BY 5% OF 9TH GRADERS, 5% OF 10TH GRADERS, AND 8% OF 11TH GRADERS, WITH BINGE DRINKING REPORTED BY 2%, 2%, AND 3%, RESPECTIVELY. THESE DATA POINTS, COMBINED WITH LOW PERCEIVED HARM AND YOUTH-REPORTED EASE OF ACCESS TO ALCOHOL, DEMONSTRATE THE NEED FOR PREVENTION STRATEGIES THAT BEGIN BEFORE HIGH SCHOOL AND CONTINUE THROUGH HIGH SCHOOL..  THE YOUTH SOBRIETY MOVEMENT WILL USE THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK AND CADCA'S SEVEN STRATEGIES FOR COMMUNITY LEVEL CHANGE TO ASSESS LOCAL CONDITIONS, GATHER PUBLIC FEEDBACK, STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, AND IMPLEMENT STRATEGIES THAT ADDRESS THE FIVE STOP ACT PROGRAM AIMS. STRATEGIES WILL INCLUDE ADAPTING AND DISSEMINATING SAMHSA'S TALK THEY HEAR YOU CAMPAIGN, HOSTING ALCOHOL- AND DRUG-FREE YOUTH EVENTS, PROVIDING YOUTH LEADERSHIP AND ADVOCACY DEVELOPMENT, AND COORDINATING ENVIRONMENTAL PREVENTION STRATEGIES WITH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FROM PREVENTION PARTNERS.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE REACHING APPROXIMATELY 21,150 YOUTH, PARENTS, AND ADULTS ANNUALLY THROUGH CAMPAIGN AND EVENT ACTIVITIES, FOR AN ESTIMATED 84,600 INDIVIDUALS OVER FOUR YEARS. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO GENERATE AN ESTIMATED ANNUAL MEDIA REACH OF 720,000 THROUGH PREVENTION MESSAGING AND OUTREACH, FOR A FOUR-YEAR MEDIA REACH OF 2,880,000. FBSMV WILL MONITOR PROGRESS USING LOCAL DATA AND PERFORMANCE MEASURES.

description: CRANSTON YOUTH ALCOHOL PREVENTION AND COMMUNITY AWARENESS INITIATIVE - COMPREHENSIVE COMMUNITY ACTION PROGRAM (CCAP), THROUGH THE CRANSTON SUBSTANCE PREVENTION COALITION (CSPC), PROPOSES A COMPREHENSIVE FOUR-YEAR UNDERAGE ALCOHOL PREVENTION INITIATIVE SERVING YOUTH AGES 12–20 IN CRANSTON, RHODE ISLAND. THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON STUDENTS ENROLLED AT HUGH B. BAIN MIDDLE SCHOOL AND CRANSTON EAST HIGH SCHOOL WHILE ALSO ENGAGING PARENTS, CAREGIVERS, AND THE BROADER COMMUNITY IN COORDINATED PREVENTION EFFORTS. THE GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE BY INCREASING KNOWLEDGE OF ALCOHOL-RELATED RISKS, STRENGTHENING PROTECTIVE FACTORS AMONG YOUTH AND FAMILIES, REDUCING YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL, AND SHIFTING COMMUNITY NORMS REGARDING UNDERAGE DRINKING.  CSPC WILL IMPLEMENT A MULTI-LEVEL PREVENTION STRATEGY GROUNDED IN THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK AND EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES. KEY ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DELIVERING THE PREVENTION PLUS WELLNESS (PPW) CURRICULUM TO STUDENTS IN ALL MIDDLE AND HIGH SCHOOLS; CONDUCTING UNDERAGE ALCOHOL COMPLIANCE CHECKS IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE CRANSTON POLICE DEPARTMENT; IMPLEMENTING LOCALIZED PUBLIC AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS AND PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENTS; CONVENING MONTHLY COMMUNITY MEETINGS; AND PROVIDING BILINGUAL ALCOHOL PREVENTION EDUCATION AND RESOURCES TO PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS.  THROUGH THESE ACTIVITIES, THE PROJECT WILL ACHIEVE THE FOLLOWING OBJECTIVES:  - BY THE END OF THE FOUR-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, REDUCE SELF-REPORTED 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE AMONG CRANSTON MIDDLE AND HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS BY AT LEAST 10 PERCENT FROM BASELINE, AS MEASURED BY THE RHODE ISLAND STUDENT SURVEY.  - BEGINNING IN YEAR 1 AND CONTINUING ANNUALLY, CONDUCT A MINIMUM OF SIX UNDERAGE ALCOHOL COMPLIANCE CHECKS AT CRANSTON RESTAURANTS AND BARS EACH YEAR.  - DURING EACH PROJECT YEAR, INCREASE STUDENT KNOWLEDGE OF ALCOHOL-RELATED RISKS AND PERCEIVED HARM BY AT LEAST 10 PERCENT FROM PRE-TEST TO POST-TEST AMONG STUDENTS PARTICIPATING IN PREVENTION PLUS WELLNESS PROGRAMMING. - CONDUCT AT LEAST 12 ALCOHOL PREVENTION SOCIAL MEDIA CAMPAIGNS ANNUALLY AND MONITOR ENGAGEMENT THROUGH IMPRESSIONS, SHARES, LIKES, AND OVERALL ENGAGEMENT RATES.  - DISTRIBUTE A MINIMUM OF SIX PARENT/CAREGIVER PREVENTION NEWSLETTERS ANNUALLY AND DEMONSTRATE ANNUAL INCREASES IN CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT THROUGH QR-CODE ACCESS DATA AND PARTICIPANT FEEDBACK.  - REACH AT LEAST 90% OF BAIN MIDDLE AND CRANSTON EAST HIGH SCHOOL WITH EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION EDUCATION BY YEAR 3.  - CONVENE PUBLIC COMMUNITY MEETINGS AT LEAST 10 MONTHS ANNUALLY THROUGHOUT THE GRANT PERIOD TO GATHER FEEDBACK AND STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT IN UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION EFFORTS.   BY COMBINING EVIDENCE-BASED YOUTH EDUCATION, CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT, ENVIRONMENTAL PREVENTION STRATEGIES, PUBLIC AWARENESS EFFORTS, AND STRONG COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, THE PROJECT WILL CREATE A SUSTAINABLE FRAMEWORK FOR REDUCING UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AND IMPROVING THE HEALTH AND SAFETY OF CRANSTON YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND THE BROADER COMMUNITY.

description: GUARD: GUIDING UNDERAGE ALCOHOL RISK REDUCTION - TRY COALITION'S STOP ACT INITIATIVE - GUARD: GUIDING UNDERAGE ALCOHOL RISK REDUCTION IS A FOUR-YEAR SAMHSA STOP ACT PROJECT LED BY TRY COALITION TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 12 TO 20 IN DURHAM CITY AND COUNTY, NORTH CAROLINA. BUILDING ON 25 YEARS OF COALITION EXPERIENCE, GUARD BUILDS TRY'S FIRST ALCOHOL-SPECIFIC PREVENTION CAPACITY ACROSS SCHOOLS, RETAILERS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND FAMILIES. GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT NEEDED: THE PROJECT WILL BE IMPLEMENTED ACROSS DURHAM CITY AND COUNTY ZIP CODES 27701, 27703, 27704, 27707, 27709, AND 27713, AN AREA OF APPROXIMATELY 181,700 RESIDENTS. TRY'S DEDICATED ALCOHOL-SPECIFIC PREVENTION CAPACITY LAPSED WHEN ITS DRUG-FREE COMMUNITIES AWARD CONCLUDED IN 2022. GUARD WILL REBUILD THIS CAPACITY THROUGH A FORMAL YOUTH ADVISORY STRUCTURE, A NEW ALCOHOL-SPECIFIC LOCAL SURVEY INSTRUMENT, AND EXPANDED GOOD NEIGHBOR BUSINESS NETWORK RETAILER TRAINING WITHIN TRY'S EXISTING 650-PLUS-MEMBER RETAIL NETWORK. POPULATION OF FOCUS: YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12 TO 20 RESIDING IN THE CATCHMENT AREA, WITH DOCUMENTED EARLY ONSET OF USE (16% OF DURHAM MIDDLE SCHOOL STUDENTS REPORT HAVING HAD A DRINK BEYOND A FEW SIPS; 13.8% OF HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS REPORT A FIRST DRINK BY AGE 13) AND ELEVATED RISK WITHIN THE 18-20 COLLEGE-AGE COHORT. POPULATION TO BE SERVED: IN ADDITION TO CAPACITY BUILDING, GUARD DIRECTLY SERVES YOUTH THROUGH PEER-LED EDUCATION (AT LEAST 100 YOUTH BY DAY 120, GROWING TO AT LEAST 25 LIFT MEMBERS SERVING AS TRAINED HEALTH AMBASSADORS BY YEAR 2) AND IMPAIRED-DRIVING PREVENTION PROGRAMMING (500 YOUTH AGES 16-20 BY YEAR 2). THIS IS A UNIVERSAL PREVENTION POPULATION; NO CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS, REFERRAL, OR ELIGIBILITY SCREENING IS REQUIRED FOR PARTICIPATION. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS: YOUTH ADVISORY CO-CREATION THROUGH LIFT (AGES 12-17) AND COLLEGE TRY (AGES 18-20); A LOCALLY ADAPTED TALK. THEY HEAR YOU. CAMPAIGN; GOOD NEIGHBOR BUSINESS NETWORK RASP RESPONSIBLE BEVERAGE SERVICE TRAINING; THE TALK IT UP. LOCK IT UP. HOME-ACCESS INITIATIVE AND SAFE HOMES PLEDGE; JOINT LAW ENFORCEMENT AND ABC ENFORCEMENT PLANNING; GOOD SAMARITAN LAW (G.S. 90-96.2) EDUCATION; TRAUMA-INFORMED TRAINING FOR YOUTH-SERVING ADULTS; AND ALCOHOL-FREE YOUTH EVENTS. PROJECT GOALS: (1) ADDRESS NORMS REGARDING UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE; (2) REDUCE OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERAGE DRINKING; (3) CREATE CHANGES IN UNDERAGE DRINKING ENFORCEMENT EFFORTS; (4) ADDRESS PENALTIES FOR UNDERAGE USE; (5) REDUCE NEGATIVE CONSEQUENCES ASSOCIATED WITH UNDERAGE DRINKING, INCLUDING ALCOHOL-INVOLVED MOTOR VEHICLE CRASHES. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: REACH 1,000 YOUTH AND 500 PARENTS/CAREGIVERS WITH ALCOHOL PREVENTION MESSAGING BY SEPTEMBER 2027; TRAIN 50 GOOD NEIGHBOR BUSINESS NETWORK RETAILERS IN RASP BY SEPTEMBER 2027; DECREASE BY 10% THE PROPORTION OF SURVEYED HIGH SCHOOLERS WHO REPORT OBTAINING ALCOHOL FROM ANOTHER PERSON BY SEPTEMBER 2028; CONVENE 2 JOINT LAW ENFORCEMENT/ABC PLANNING MEETINGS BY SEPTEMBER 2027; AND REACH 500 YOUTH AGES 16-20 WITH IMPAIRED-DRIVING PREVENTION PROGRAMMING BY SEPTEMBER 2028.

description: THE MARTINSBURG INITIATIVE’S SOBER TRUTH ON PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING (STOP) ACT GRANT, JEFFERSON COUNTY EXPANSION - THE MARTINSBURG INITIATIVE (TMI), A POLICE-SCHOOL-COMMUNITY HEALTH-EDUCATION COALITION, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE JEFFERSON-BERKELEY ALLIANCE ON SUBSTANCE USE PREVENTION (JBA), WILL EXPAND ITS PROVEN, COALITION-DRIVEN UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION MODEL INTO JEFFERSON COUNTY, WEST VIRGINIA, TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12–20 THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED ENVIRONMENTAL STRATEGIES, YOUTH-LED PREVENTION, AND COORDINATED COMMUNITY ACTION ACROSS THE COUNTY'S FIVE MUNICIPALITIES AND PUBLIC SCHOOLS.      JEFFERSON COUNTY (POPULATION 61,264, WITH 20.5% UNDER AGE 18) IS THE EASTERNMOST COUNTY IN WEST VIRGINIA'S EASTERN PANHANDLE AND SITS DIRECTLY ADJACENT TO TMI'S CURRENT BERKELEY COUNTY SERVICE AREA, MAKING THIS APPLICATION A NEW GEOGRAPHIC CATCHMENT AREA ENTIRELY DISTINCT FROM TMI'S EXISTING WORK. ALTHOUGH THE COUNTY BENEFITS FROM STRONG SCHOOLS, LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES, AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, IT LACKS AN INTEGRATED, YOUTH-FOCUSED PREVENTION SYSTEM TO CONNECT THEM. THE NEED IS WELL DOCUMENTED AND KEENLY FELT BY RESIDENTS THEMSELVES. THE NEED IS WELL DOCUMENTED: NEARLY ONE IN FOUR WEST VIRGINIA HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS CURRENTLY DRINKS ALCOHOL AND ONE IN EIGHT BINGE DRINKS, BOTH ABOVE NATIONAL RATES (CDC YRBS, 2021). THIS PROJECT WILL SERVE THE COUNTY'S YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12–20, A POPULATION THAT INCLUDES THE 8,389 STUDENTS ENROLLED IN JEFFERSON COUNTY SCHOOLS AS WELL AS YOUNG ADULTS ATTENDING SHEPHERD UNIVERSITY IN SHEPHERDSTOWN.      TMI AND JBA WILL LAUNCH A JEFFERSON COUNTY YOUTH ADVISORY GROUP BUILT ON TMI'S DRUG-FREE WV YOUTH COALITION MODEL AND ITS UNDER 21 ALCOHOL CONSUMPTION TASK FORCE, ENSURING THAT YOUNG PEOPLE CO-CREATE THE PROGRAM FROM THE START. WORKING ALONGSIDE THESE YOUTH LEADERS, THE PROJECT WILL ADAPT AND DISSEMINATE SAMHSA'S NATIONAL  TALK. THEY HEAR YOU.  CAMPAIGN FOR JEFFERSON COUNTY AUDIENCES, DELIVER TIPS (TRAINING FOR INTERVENTION PROCEDURES) RESPONSIBLE BEVERAGE SERVER TRAINING TO THE COUNTY'S RETAIL AND HOSPITALITY ESTABLISHMENTS, AND CONDUCT YOUTH-LED STICKER SHOCK CAMPAIGNS AND MERCHANT COMPLIANCE CHECKS IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE JEFFERSON COUNTY SHERIFF'S OFFICE AND MUNICIPAL POLICE DEPARTMENTS. TMI WILL ALSO REPLICATE ITS SOCIAL HOSTING PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT CAMPAIGN, MODELED ON ITS MARTINSBURG DMV PSAS, AT JEFFERSON COUNTY PUBLIC VENUES, AND IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION CURRICULA IN PARTNERSHIP WITH JEFFERSON COUNTY SCHOOLS.      THROUGH THESE STRATEGIES, THE PROJECT PURSUES THREE GOALS: REDUCING UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH, STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY NORMS AGAINST UNDERAGE DRINKING AND YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL, AND BUILDING SUSTAINABLE, YOUTH-DRIVEN PREVENTION CAPACITY. BY THE END OF YEAR 4, THE PROJECT WILL REDUCE PAST 30-DAY AND ANNUAL YOUTH ALCOHOL USE BY 5% FROM BASELINE, AS MEASURED BY LOCAL SCHOOL SURVEYS ADMINISTERED IN AT LEAST THREE GRADE LEVELS, AND WILL INCREASE YOUTH-REPORTED PERCEPTION OF RISK OR HARM, PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL, AND PEER DISAPPROVAL OF ALCOHOL USE BY 5% EACH ON THE SAME INSTRUMENT. ON THE ACCESS SIDE, THE PROJECT WILL ACHIEVE A MERCHANT COMPLIANCE RATE OF 90% OR GREATER ON UNANNOUNCED COMPLIANCE CHECKS AND WILL TIPS-TRAIN STAFF AT A MINIMUM OF 20 JEFFERSON COUNTY ESTABLISHMENTS THAT SELL OR SERVE ALCOHOL. THESE OBJECTIVES DIRECTLY ADVANCE SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITY OF PREVENTING SUBSTANCE MISUSE, ABUSE, AND ADDICTION, PARTICULARLY AMONG YOUTH.

description: FACES 4 CHANGE: YOUTH RAISING THE MIC FOR ALCOHOL PREVENTION INITIATIVE - THE FACES 4 CHANGE: YOUTH RAISING THE MIC FOR ALCOHOL PREVENTION INITIATIVE WILL IMPLEMENT THE SAMHSA SOBER TRUTH ON PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING ACT GRANTS TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS IN THE CITY OF HARRISONBURG AND ROCKINGHAM COUNTY, VIRGINA. THE GOALS ARE FOR THE YOUTH POPULAR CULTURE INSTITUTE, INC. (YPCI) AND ITS DRUG-FREE COMMUNITY COALITION (DFC) TO (1) IMPLEMENT ACTIVITIES THAT SUPPORT CAPACITY BUILDING, SUCH AS IMPLEMENTING EVIDENCE-BASED COMMUNITY APPROACHES AND (2) ENHANCE COLLABORATION, COOPERATION, AND COORDINATION AMONG COMMUNITIES, FEDERAL, STATE, TERRITORIAL, AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. THE COMBINED POPULATION OF THE CITY AND COUNTY IS APPROXIMATELY 171,000 RESIDENTS, INCLUDING AN ESTIMATED 9,500 YOUTH. THE PROJECT'S PRIMARY POPULATION THAT WILL BENEFIT FROM THE CAPACITY BUILDING IS YOUTH AGES 14-18 (5.2% OF THE TOTAL POPULATION), WITH THE CATCHMENT AREA'S PUBLIC HIGH SCHOOL (HS) STUDENTS SERVING AS THE PRINCIPAL POPULATION REACHED THROUGH PROJECT ACTIVITIES. THE PUBLIC HSS ENROLL 5,674 STUDENTS, INCLUDING 2,017 STUDENTS IN HARRISONBURG AND 3,657 STUDENTS IN THE COUNTY WHERE UNDERAGE DRINKING IS EVIDENT. THE CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT NEEDED IS TO BUILD A COORDINATED COMMUNITY PREVENTION SYSTEM BY EXPANDING THE PREVENTION WORKFORCE, STRENGTHENING COLLABORATION AMONG PREVENTION PROVIDERS, ENGAGING YOUTH AND PARENTS AS PREVENTION PARTNERS, AND IMPLEMENTING EVIDENCE-BASED/INFORMED AND COMMUNITY DEFINED STRATEGIES THAT REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING AND PROMOTE ALCOHOL-FREE NORMS.   THE OBJECTIVES ARE: OBJECTIVE 1: CONDUCT A NEEDS ASSESSMENT TO IDENTIFY THE COMMUNITY NORMS REGARDING ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 14 TO 18.  OBJECTIVE 2: IDENTIFY, ESTABLISH, AND IMPLEMENT ONE EVIDENCE-BASED, EVIDENCE-INFORMED, OR COMMUNITY-DEFINED PREVENTION STRATEGY TO EXPAND AND INCREASE YPCI’S DFC CAPACITY.  OBJECTIVE 3: CONDUCT COMMUNITY TAILORED ALCOHOL PREVENTION EDUCATION AND INFORMATION DISSEMINATION THROUGH A SOCIAL NORMS CAMPAIGN AND SOCIAL MEDIA CAMPAIGN.  OBJECTIVE 4: ESTABLISH A YOUTH UNDERAGE DRINKING ADVISORY TASKFORCE AS A PART OF THE DFC’S YOUTH ADVISORY COUNCIL TO PROVIDE STOP PROGRAM INPUT FROM IDEATION TO IMPLEMENTATION.  OBJECTIVE 5: ESTABLISH A COMMUNITY-WIDE UNDERAGE DRINKING TASKFORCE TO INCREASE CITIZEN PARTICIPATION TO FACILITATE PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING (SAMHSA’S STRATEGIC PRIORITY).  OBJECTIVE 6: REVIEW THE STATE PERFORMANCE AND BEST PRACTICES FOR THE PREVENTION AND REDUCTION OF UNDERAGE DRINKING REPORT AND IDENTIFY WHICH POLICIES, PROGRAMS, AND PRACTICES NEED TO BE ADDED OR MODIFIED TO MAXIMIZE THE STOP PROGRAM’S IMPACT TO PREVENT AND REDUCE OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERAGE DRINKING.   OBJECTIVE 7: CREATE A PREVENTION CORPS TO REDUCE THE NEGATIVE CONSEQUENCES ASSOCIATED WITH UNDERAGE DRINKING.  OBJECTIVE 8: SUPPORT FOUR (4) PREVENTION CORPS MEMBERS TO BECOME CERTIFIED PREVENTION SPECIALISTS.

description: PARENT AND CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT (PACE) PROJECT 2 - PACE (PARENT AND CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT), A PROJECT PROPOSED BY THE STRATEGIC PLANNING INITIATIVE FOR FAMILIES AND YOUTH (SPIFFY) COALITION, AIMS TO PREVENT ALCOHOL USE AND RELATED HARMS AMONG 12-20 YEAR OLD YOUTH BY ENGAGING AND EDUCATING PARENTS/CAREGIVERS ACROSS OUR LARGELY (80%) RURAL GEOGRAPHIC CATCHMENT AREA, HAMPSHIRE COUNTY, MA.   THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS HAMPSHIRE COUNTY, MA YOUTH AGES 12-20; 79% ARE WHITE, 4% ASIAN, 7% BLACK, 11% LATINO, 2% AMERICAN INDIAN/ALASKA NATIVE, AND 1% NATIVE HAWAIIAN/PACIFIC ISLANDER (PERCENTAGES ADD TO MORE THAN 100% BECAUSE YOUTH COULD SELECT MORE THAN ONE OPTION). ROUGHLY 45% ARE BOYS, 47% ARE GIRLS, AND 71% ARE STRAIGHT. THE MAJORITY OF THE COUNTY (80%) IS RURAL (MA STATE OFFICE OF RURAL HEALTH, 2025), MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME IS $79,969, AND 12% OF HOUSEHOLDS LIVE BELOW THE POVERTY LINE (US CENSUS BUREAU, 2023). 37% OF HAMPSHIRE COUNTY RESIDENTS EXPERIENCE FOOD INSECURITY (GREATER BOSTON FOOD BANK, 2024) AND 18,104 RESIDENTS RECEIVE SNAP BENEFITS (FEDERAL RESERVE ECONOMIC DATA, 2022).   SINCE 1995, SPIFFY HAS ENGAGED WITH COUNTLESS STAKEHOLDERS TO CREATE LOCAL PARTNERSHIPS TO PREVENT YOUTH SUBSTANCE USE. HOWEVER, PARENT/CAREGIVER ENGAGEMENT REMAINS A PERSISTENT CHALLENGE FOR OUR COALITION, AND HAS BEEN AMPLIFIED POST-PANDEMIC. GIVEN THE CRITICAL ROLE PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS PLAY IN SHAPING YOUTH ALCOHOL USE, COUPLED WITH CONCERNING RATES OF BOTH ADULT AND YOUTH USE IN OUR REGION, THIS AREA FOR GROWTH IN OUR COALITION WORK MUST BE ADDRESSED IMMEDIATELY. PACE WILL DO JUST THAT.  PACE WILL HELP SPIFFY ACCOMPLISH THE PROPOSED PROJECT GOALS BY CONVENING A PARENT/CAREGIVER SUBCOMMITTEE WITH A GOAL OF PARTNERING WITH 15-20 PARENTS/CAREGIVERS TO ENGAGE IN DATA-DRIVEN, EVIDENCE-BASED DISCUSSIONS RELATED TO PARENT ENGAGEMENT AND EDUCATION THAT WILL DRIVE DOWN YOUTH ALCOHOL USE RATES LOCALLY. BASED ON THESE, THE SUBCOMMITTEE WILL SELECT STRATEGIES TO INCREASE LASTING PARENT/CAREGIVER PARTNERSHIPS AND CREATE A COMPREHENSIVE EDUCATION CAMPAIGN TO INCREASE PARENT KNOWLEDGE, PERCEPTIONS OF HARM AND DISAPPROVAL, EFFICACY FOR HAVING CONVERSATIONS WITH YOUTH, AND AWARENESS OF THE BENEFITS OF MODELING HEALTHY USE; AND DECREASE PERMISSIVE ATTITUDES AND BEHAVIORS.  THROUGHOUT IMPLEMENTATION, WE WILL CONTINUOUSLY EVALUATE PROGRESS AND MAKE ADJUSTMENTS. OUR PRIMARY EVALUATION TOOLS WILL BE AN ANNUAL PARENT/CAREGIVER SURVEY AND BIANNUAL YOUTH SURVEILLANCE SURVEY, BUT WE WILL ALSO PLAN TO CONDUCT QUALITATIVE RESEARCH, SUCH AS FOCUS GROUPS. WE ANTICIPATE SERVING 2,000 PARENTS/CAREGIVERS (AND LIKEWISE, 12-20 YEAR OLD YOUTH) ANNUALLY, OR 8,000 THROUGHOUT THE DURATION OF PACE BASED ON OUR RECENT PARENT WORK.  BY ENGAGING AND EDUCATING PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS - AND USING FACT-BASED INFORMATION TO DISPEL MYTHS AND CHANGE HEARTS AND MINDS – OUR ENDGAME IS TO DECREASE 12-20 YEAR OLDS' ACCESS TO ALCOHOL VIA PARENTS AND FAMILY BY 10%; DECREASE THE PERCENTAGE OF YOUTH WHO REPORT USING WITH PARENT PERMISSION BY10%; INCREASE THEIR RISK PERCEPTIONS RELATED TO ALCOHOL BY 5%, DECREASE PAST 30 DAY USE RATES BY 5%, AND DECREASE RATES OF DRIVING UNDER THE INFLUENCE BY 5%.

description: BNYP: BISBEE-NACO YOUTH PROJECT - AMISTADES, INC. PROPOSES TO IMPLEMENT BNYP: BISBEE-NACO YOUTH PROJECT, A YOUTH ALCOHOL PREVENTION AND LEADERSHIP INITIATIVE THAT WILL EXPAND THE CAPACITY OF THE COCHISE COUNTY COALITION TO PREVENT AND REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING IN BISBEE AND NACO, ARIZONA. THROUGH COALITION EXPANSION, YOUTH LEADERSHIP, COMMUNITY ASSESSMENT, PARENT AND ADULT EDUCATION, ALCOHOL-FREE PROSOCIAL YOUTH ENGAGEMENT, AND ENVIRONMENTAL PREVENTION STRATEGIES, THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN RURAL BORDER COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL AND INCREASE YOUTH VOICE IN PREVENTION.  AMISTADES IS A SEASONED PREVENTION PROVIDER AND DRUG-FREE COMMUNITIES RECIPIENT WITH AN ESTABLISHED PREVENTION COALITION IN DOUGLAS, ARIZONA. THROUGH STOP FUNDING, AMISTADES WILL WORK WITH COCHISE COUNTY COALITION MEMBERS REPRESENTING ALL 12 COMMUNITY SECTORS TO EXPAND EVIDENCE-BASED, EVIDENCE-INFORMED, AND POLICY-FOCUSED UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION STRATEGIES INTO THE NEIGHBORING BORDERLAND COMMUNITIES OF BISBEE AND NACO, ARIZONA, WHICH HAVE A COMBINED POPULATION OF APPROXIMATELY 6,000 RESIDENTS. THESE COMMUNITIES FACE CULTURAL NORMS FAVORABLE TO YOUTH ALCOHOL USE, RURAL GEOGRAPHIC ISOLATION, SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC DISPARITIES, LIMITED PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE, AND SIGNIFICANT GAPS IN LOCAL DATA. TOGETHER, THESE CONDITIONS PLACE YOUTH AT INCREASED RISK FOR UNDERAGE DRINKING AND RELATED CONSEQUENCES. GIVEN THE SMALL POPULATION SIZE OF BISBEE AND NACO, THIS INITIATIVE HAS THE POTENTIAL TO REACH YOUTH AGES 10 TO 20 ACROSS BOTH COMMUNITIES, ALONG WITH THEIR PARENTS, CAREGIVERS, SCHOOLS, AND OTHER TRUSTED ADULTS.  ALCOHOL REMAINS THE MOST COMMONLY USED SUBSTANCE AMONG YOUTH IN THESE COMMUNITIES. ACCORDING TO THE 2024 ARIZONA YOUTH SURVEY, 19.3% OF YOUTH REPORTED PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE AND 13.3% REPORTED PROBLEM DRINKING, DEFINED AS CONSUMING FIVE OR MORE DRINKS ON ONE OCCASION IN THE PAST TWO WEEKS. THE DATA ALSO SHOWED AN INCREASE IN ALCOHOL USE AMONG 8TH AND 10TH GRADERS FROM 9.5% TO 13.8%, ALONG WITH A 3.3% DECREASE IN PERCEPTION OF PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL. THESE TRENDS POINT TO THE NEED FOR A COORDINATED, COMMUNITY-WIDE PREVENTION APPROACH THAT STRENGTHENS YOUTH, FAMILY, SCHOOL, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND COMMUNITY PARTNER ENGAGEMENT. THE PROJECT’S TWO GOALS ARE TO REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL AND INCREASE YOUTH LEADERSHIP IN ALCOHOL USE PREVENTION. CAPACITY-BUILDING ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE: 1) INCREASING COALITION MEMBERSHIP TO INCLUDE NEW ADULT MEMBERS REPRESENTING BISBEE AND NACO; 2) COMPLETING A NEEDS ASSESSMENT AND PLANNING PROCESS WITH TARGET COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND CAUSAL FACTORS AND DEFINE PREVENTION PRIORITIES; 3) GROWING THE COALITION’S YOUTH LEADERSHIP COUNCIL BY USING A NEAR-PEER MODEL TO ENGAGE EIGHT YOUTH FROM THE TARGET COMMUNITIES AND ADDING TWO OF THEM AS YOUTH REPRESENTATIVES ON THE COALITION; 4) BROADENING COALITION-HOSTED ALCOHOL-FREE PROSOCIAL ACTIVITIES TO ENGAGE YOUTH AND FAMILIES FROM BISBEE AND NACO; 5) TRAINING NEW YOUTH IN PREVENTION SCIENCE, PUBLIC SPEAKING, PRESENTATION SKILLS, ADVOCACY, DATA COLLECTION, AND REPORTING; AND 6) DEVELOPING AN ENVIRONMENTAL NORMS CAMPAIGN AIMED AT REDUCING YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL THROUGH PARENT AND ADULT EDUCATION, WITH ACCOMPANYING SOCIAL HOST ORDINANCE DEVELOPMENT  AMISTADES WILL PARTNER WITH FOUR AGENCIES IN THE TARGET COMMUNITIES: BOYS & GIRLS CLUB OF BISBEE, BISBEE POLICE DEPARTMENT, NACO ELEMENTARY SCHOOL DISTRICT, AND BISBEE UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT.

description: FAIRFIELD HERITAGE PREVENTION COALITION STOP ACT GRANT APPLICATION - THE FAIRFIELD HERITAGE PREVENTION COALITION (FHPC) SEEKS FUNDING THROUGH THE STOP ACT TO REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 12–20 IN FAIRFIELD, OHIO, WHILE STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY COLLABORATION TO PREVENT ALCOHOL MISUSE BEFORE IT BEGINS. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE YOUTH, FAMILIES, SCHOOLS, AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS THROUGHOUT FAIRFIELD, WITH PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO NEIGHBORHOODS EXPERIENCING HIGHER LEVELS OF SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC VULNERABILITY.  UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE CONTINUES TO BE A SIGNIFICANT PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERN IN BUTLER COUNTY. LOCAL AND STATE DATA INDICATE THAT MANY MIDDLE AND HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS REPORT ALCOHOL USE, WITH SOME BEGINNING AS EARLY AS SIXTH GRADE. EARLY ALCOHOL USE INCREASES THE RISK OF SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, POOR ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE, INJURIES, MENTAL HEALTH CHALLENGES, AND OTHER LONG-TERM HEALTH CONSEQUENCES. EXISTING PREVENTION EFFORTS ARE LIMITED BY INSUFFICIENT COORDINATION, RESOURCE CONSTRAINTS, AND A LACK OF CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE PROGRAMMING FOR UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS.  USING SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK (SPF), FHPC WILL IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED, COMMUNITY-LEVEL PREVENTION STRATEGIES THAT ADDRESS THE FACTORS CONTRIBUTING TO UNDERAGE DRINKING. THE COALITION WILL STRENGTHEN PARTNERSHIPS AMONG SCHOOLS, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, YOUTH-SERVING ORGANIZATIONS, BUSINESSES, FAITH-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, PARENTS, AND COMMUNITY LEADERS TO CREATE A COORDINATED PREVENTION SYSTEM.  KEY PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE EXPANDING COALITION MEMBERSHIP AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT; DELIVERING EDUCATIONAL PRESENTATIONS AND AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS; PROVIDING YOUTH LEADERSHIP AND PEER-TO-PEER PREVENTION OPPORTUNITIES; CONDUCTING RETAILER EDUCATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL PREVENTION STRATEGIES TO REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL; PROMOTING RESPONSIBLE COMMUNITY POLICIES; IMPLEMENTING SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY PREVENTION PROGRAMS; AND COLLECTING DATA TO MONITOR PROGRESS AND IMPROVE OUTCOMES.  THE PROJECT AIMS TO INCREASE COMMUNITY AWARENESS OF THE HARMS OF UNDERAGE DRINKING, EXPAND PARTICIPATION IN PREVENTION INITIATIVES, STRENGTHEN PARTNERSHIPS, INCREASE YOUTH PERCEPTION OF THE RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH ALCOHOL USE, REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL, AND DECREASE PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH. PROGRESS WILL BE MEASURED USING VALIDATED SURVEYS, COALITION PERFORMANCE MEASURES, TRAINING PARTICIPATION RECORDS, PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENTS, COMMUNITY OUTREACH DATA, AND OTHER ESTABLISHED EVALUATION TOOLS CONSISTENT WITH FEDERAL PERFORMANCE REPORTING REQUIREMENTS.  FHPC HAS DEMONSTRATED EXPERIENCE MANAGING FEDERALLY FUNDED PREVENTION INITIATIVES AND MAINTAINS STRONG PARTNERSHIPS THROUGHOUT FAIRFIELD. THE COALITION CURRENTLY COLLABORATES WITH SCHOOLS, COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, YOUTH-SERVING AGENCIES, AND OTHER LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS TO IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION STRATEGIES. THROUGH THIS PROJECT, FHPC WILL BUILD A SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE THAT REDUCES UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE, PROMOTES HEALTHY YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, AND IMPROVES THE LONG-TERM HEALTH AND WELL-BEING OF FAIRFIELD'S YOUNG PEOPLE AND FAMILIES.

description: SAN CLEMENTE UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION INITIATIVE: BUILDING CITYWIDE CAPACITY - THE WELLNESS & PREVENTION FOUNDATION, FISCAL AGENT FOR THE WELLNESS & PREVENTION COALITION (WPC), REQUESTS STOP ACT FUNDING TO EXPAND THE COALITION'S CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12 TO 20 WITH A PRIMARY FOCUS ON AGES 12 TO 18 IN SAN CLEMENTE, CALIFORNIA. BUILDING ON NINE YEARS OF DRUG-FREE COMMUNITIES AND FOUR YEARS OF STOP ACT-FUNDED PREVENTION WORK, THE WPC WILL CONTINUE TO DEEPEN COMMUNITY-WIDE COLLABORATION, DELIVER TWO EVIDENCE-BASED CURRICULA, AND STRENGTHEN DATA-DRIVEN DECISION-MAKING TO REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING AND ITS ASSOCIATED HARMS ACROSS SAN CLEMENTE.     SAN CLEMENTE HAS APPROXIMATELY 62,626 RESIDENTS, AND IS BORDERED BY THE PACIFIC OCEAN, CAMP PENDLETON, AND THE CITIES OF DANA POINT AND SAN JUAN CAPISTRANO. WHILE THE WPC'S DFC-FUNDED WORK HAS HELPED REDUCE PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE (ONE OR MORE DRINKS OF ALCOHOL) AMONG 11TH GRADERS, DOWN FROM 35% IN 2017 TO 16% IN 2024, UNDERAGE DRINKING REMAINS A COMMUNITY CONCERN: WITH 50% OF 7TH GRADERS, 46% OF 9TH GRADERS, AND 50% OF 11TH GRADERS PERCEIVING SLIGHT TO NO RISK FROM OCCASIONAL ALCOHOL USE (CHKS, 2024), AND 21.6% OF SAN CLEMENTE ADULTS REPORTING REGULAR BINGE DRINKING (U.S. CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION (CDC), PLACES: LOCAL DATA FOR BETTER HEALTH, 2022), REINFORCING PERMISSIVE COMMUNITY NORMS. STOP ACT FUNDING WILL BUILD THE COALITION'S CAPACITY TO CLOSE THIS GAP BY REACHING A BROADER CROSS-SECTION OF SAN CLEMENTE'S YOUTH AND FAMILIES THAN CURRENT DFC CAPACITY ALLOWS.     CAPACITY-BUILDING ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE EXPANDING COALITION MEMBERSHIP AND ESTABLISHING A FORMALIZED YOUTH ADVISORY GROUP; DEVELOPING A LOGIC MODEL AND 12-MONTH ACTION PLAN; INCREASING INTERGOVERNMENTAL COORDINATION WITH CITY GOVERNMENT, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND COUNTY PARTNERS HOLDING PUBLIC COALITION MEETINGS, AND COMMUNITY MEETINGS FOR PUBLIC FEEDBACK ACCESSIBLE TO ALL SAN CLEMENTE HOUSEHOLDS.     AS ITS PRIMARY EVIDENCE-BASED CURRICULA, THE WPC WILL DELIVER ACTIVE PARENTING, A SAMHSA-RECOGNIZED PARENT EDUCATION PROGRAM, TO STRENGTHEN FAMILY COMMUNICATION AND PROTECTIVE ATTITUDES TOWARD ALCOHOL USE, AND SPORT PREVENTION PLUS WELLNESS, A SINGLE SESSION ADOLESCENT MOTIVATIONAL INTERVENTION INTEGRATING SUBSTANCE USE PREVENTION WITH HEALTH PROMOTION.     PROJECT GOALS/OBJECTIVES ARE TO: (1) BUILD COALITION CAPACITY THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED PROGRAMMING AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT INFRASTRUCTURE, INCLUDING MEASURABLE DELIVERY TARGETS FOR BOTH ACTIVE PARENTING AND SPORT PPW; (2) INCREASE FAMILY PROTECTIVE FACTORS AMONG SAN CLEMENTE PARENTS/GUARDIANS WHO COMPLETE ACTIVE PARENTING, AS MEASURED BY PRE/POST ASSESSMENT; AND (3) REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE (PAST 30-DAY USE, PERCEIVED RISK, PARENTAL/PEER DISAPPROVAL) AMONG SAN CLEMENTE YOUTH WHO COMPLETE SPORT PPW, AS MEASURED THROUGH A LOCAL SURVEY.    THESE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES DIRECTLY ADVANCE SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITY OF PREVENTING SUBSTANCE MISUSE AND ADDICTION AMONG YOUTH THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED, OUTCOME-FOCUSED, DATA-DRIVEN PRACTICE.

description: SOBER TRUTH ON PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING ACT GRANTS (STOP ACT GRANT) - THE PATERSON 5TH WARD COALITION FOR PREVENTION AND EMPOWERMENT (C.O.P.E.), LED BY  MONTCLAIR STATE UNIVERSITY, WILL IMPLEMENT AN INITIATIVE UNDER SAMHSA'S SOBER TRUTH ON  PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING ACT (STOP ACT) PROGRAM TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG  YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12–20 IN PATERSON'S 5TH WARD. THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON PATERSON'S  5TH WARD, A DEFINED URBAN CATCHMENT THAT IS DISTINCT FROM THE ORGANIZATION'S CURRENT STOP ACT  SERVICE AREA. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDES YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12–20 WHO RESIDE IN,  ATTEND SCHOOL IN, OR RECEIVE SERVICES WITHIN THE 5TH WARD.  LOCAL DATA SHOW ALCOHOL USE ABOVE NATIONAL BENCHMARKS, LIMITED ACCESS TO ADOLESCENT  BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, FRAGMENTED COORDINATION AMONG SCHOOLS AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS, AND A NEED FOR CLEARER REFERRAL PATHWAYS AND STRONGER PARENT AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT. PREVENTION AND REFERRAL ACTIVITIES WILL BE DELIVERED THROUGH SCHOOLS, YOUTH-SERVING ORGANIZATIONS, PARENT/CAREGIVER OUTREACH, COMMUNITY PARTNERS, AND NEIGHBORHOOD SETTINGS, REACHING AN ESTIMATED 250 YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS ANNUALLY AND APPROXIMATELY 1,000 OVER THE FOUR-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD.  TO BUILD CAPACITY TO MEET THESE NEEDS, C.O.P.E. WILL EXPAND ITS YOUTH LEADERSHIP COUNCIL  (YLC), STRENGTHEN COALITION PARTNERSHIPS, AND IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED AND EVIDENCE-INFORMED  PREVENTION PROGRAMMING GROUNDED IN THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK (SPF) AND COMMUNITY DEFINED APPROACHES. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE PHOTOVOICE, STICKER SHOCK, ENVIRONMENTAL SCANS, AND  GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM (GIS) MAPPING PROJECTS, CULMINATING IN A SHARED 5TH WARD YOUTH  PREVENTION RESOURCE MAP AND STANDARDIZED REFERRAL PROTOCOL.  PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: 1) STRENGTHEN C.O.P.E.'S CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT AND SUSTAIN UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION FOR YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12–20 IN PATERSON'S 5TH WARD; 2) REDUCE  UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE BY STRENGTHENING PROTECTIVE FACTORS AND HEALTHY DECISION-MAKING; AND 3)  STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY SYSTEMS AND PARTNERSHIPS TO REDUCE YOUTH ALCOHOL ACCESS AND IMPROVE  CONNECTIONS TO PREVENTION, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, TREATMENT, RECOVERY, AND CRISIS RESOURCES. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE INCREASING ACTIVE YLC MEMBERSHIP TO AT LEAST 15 YOUTH BY DAY 120; ENGAGING  AT LEAST FIVE NEW ORGANIZATIONAL OR SECTOR PARTNERS BY THE END OF YEAR 1; REDUCING PAST-30-DAY ALCOHOL USE BY 20% FROM THE YEAR 1 BASELINE BY YEAR 4; INCREASING PERCEIVED RISK OF ALCOHOL USE, PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL, AND PEER DISAPPROVAL BY 20% FROM BASELINE BY YEAR 4; SERVING 250 YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS ANNUALLY, WITH 75% OF MATCHED RESPONDENTS SHOWING IMPROVED ALCOHOL-RISK KNOWLEDGE OR PREVENTION SKILLS; REACHING 100 PARENTS/CAREGIVERS ANNUALLY, WITH 75% OF MATCHED STRUCTURED-SESSION PARTICIPANTS SHOWING INCREASED PREVENTION KNOWLEDGE; PUBLISHING A 5TH WARD YOUTH PREVENTION RESOURCE MAP AND STANDARDIZED REFERRAL PROTOCOL BY SEPTEMBER 29, 2027; AND IMPLEMENTING AT LEAST ONE COMMUNITY-LEVEL STRATEGY BY YEAR 2 BASED ON LOCAL ASSESSMENT FINDINGS.  THE PROJECT WILL USE LOCAL SURVEY DATA FROM AT LEAST THREE GRADE LEVELS, MATCHED PRE- AND  POST-ASSESSMENTS, ANNUAL PERFORMANCE REPORTING, QUARTERLY UPDATES TO SAMHSA'S PERFORMANCE  ACCOUNTABILITY AND REPORTING SYSTEM (SPARS), AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT TO MONITOR  IMPLEMENTATION, MEASURE PROGRESS, AND GUIDE TIMELY REFINEMENTS THROUGHOUT THE FOUR-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD.

description: LEAD PHILLIPSBURG: LEARN, EDUCATE, ADVOCATE, DEVELOP DRUG FREE COMMUNITIES COALITION-STOP! BE SAFE & SOBER! - LEAD PHILLIPSBURG: LEARN, EDUCATE, ADVOCATE, DEVELOP DRUG FREE COMMUNITIES COALITION (LEAD-DFC) HAS ESTABLISHED STRONG PARTNERSHIPS WITH KEY COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS AND DEMONSTRATED SUCCESS IN PREVENTION INITIATIVES THAT REDUCE YOUTH SUBSTANCE MISUSE IN THE TOWN OF PHILLIPSBURG. THE PROPOSED STOP! BE SAFE & SOBER! PROJECT WILL EXPAND LEAD-DFC’S CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT AND SUSTAIN COMPREHENSIVE, EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES THAT PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG AGES 12-20 RESIDING IN PHILLIPSBURG (ZIP: 08865).  PHILLIPSBURG IS THE LARGEST, MOST DENSELY POPULATED, AND MOST SOCIOECONOMICALLY CHALLENGED MUNICIPALITY IN WARREN COUNTY, WITH A POPULATION OF 15,291 RESIDENTS. THE COMMUNITY IS ALSO THE COUNTY’S MOST DIVERSE, WITH 66.7% IDENTIFYING AS CAUCASIAN, 14.4% AS HISPANIC/LATINO, AND 12% AS AFRICAN AMERICAN. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES IDENTIFIED CAPACITY GAPS BY EXPANDING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION PROGRAMMING, INCREASING STAKEHOLDER TRAINING, ENHANCING YOUTH ENGAGEMENT OPPORTUNITIES, AND STRENGTHENING DATA COLLECTION AND EVALUATION.   THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS APPROXIMATELY 3,300 YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12-20 RESIDING IN IN PHILLIPSBURG WITH A BALANCED DISTRIBUTION OF MALES AND FEMALES. ALTHOUGH THE POPULATION IS NOT DEFINED BY CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS, MANY YOUTH EXPERIENCE ANXIETY, DEPRESSION, TRAUMA EXPOSURE, AND EARLY EXPERIMENTATION WITH SUBSTANCES. LOCAL DATA INDICATES CONTINUED ALCOHOL USE CONCERNS AND ELEVATED RISK AMONG YOUTH. STOP! BE SAFE & SOBER! WILL IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION STRATEGIES THAT STRENGTHEN PROTECTIVE FACTORS, REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL, AND INCREASE ENGAGEMENT IN POSITIVE, PRO-SOCIAL OPPORTUNITIES.  CAPACITY-BUILDING ACTIVITIES INCLUDE MONTHLY LEAD-DFC COALITION MEETINGS, PRESENTATIONS TO TOWN COUNCIL AND OTHER COMMUNITY GROUPS, TOWN HALLS AND TEENS TALK FORUMS, EXPANDED COLLABORATION WITH COMMUNITY PARTNERS, AND STRENGTHENED PARTNERSHIPS ACROSS SECTORS TO ENHANCE PREVENTION SERVICES AND ENGAGEMENT.   STOP! BE SAFE & SOBER! INCLUDES TWO GOALS TO ENHANCE AND EXPAND COALITION EFFORTS DURING THE FOUR-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD. THE FIRST IS TO INCREASE KNOWLEDGE, AWARENESS, AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS TO REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 12-20, AS MEASURED BY 30-DAY PAST USE SURVEY DATA. TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL, THREE MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES ARE NECESSARY: 1. BY SEPTEMBER 29, 2030, PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION CURRICULA, AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS, AND ALTERNATE ACTIVITIES THAT REACH AT LEAST 150 YOUTH ANNUALLY WITHIN THE CATCHMENT AREA. 2. BY SEPTEMBER 29, 2030, CONDUCT FOUR EVIDENCE-BASED TRAININGS FOR PARENTS, GUARDIANS, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO INCREASE AWARENESS OF THE RISKS OF UNDERAGE DRINKING.  3. BY SEPTEMBER 29, 2030, INCREASE YOUTH ENGAGEMENT IN PREVENTION EFFORTS BY 10% THROUGH PARTICIPATION IN THE ILEAD YOUTH COALITION.  THE SECOND GOAL IS TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY COLLABORATION TO CREATE SUSTAINABLE STRATEGIES THAT PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 12-20. TWO OBJECTIVES ARE NECESSARY TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL: 1. BY SEPTEMBER 29, 2030, ENHANCE COORDINATION AMONG KEY STAKEHOLDERS TO COMPLETE A BIANNUAL REVIEW OF POLICIES RELATED TO UNDERAGE DRINKING IN THE TARGETED MUNICIPALITY. 2. BY SEPTEMBER 29, 2030, INCREASE COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION IN PREVENTION EFFORTS BY 10% THROUGH THE EXPANSION OF LEAD-DFC COALITION MEMBERSHIP AND ENGAGEMENT OF REPRESENTATIVES FROM ALL SECTORS.

description: RIVER VALLEY RISING STOP ACT TO REDUCE AND PREVENT UNDERAGE DRINKING - THE RIVER VALLEY RISING STOP ACT PROJECT WILL REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AND BINGE DRINKING AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12-20 ACROSS NINE TOWNS IN THE RIVER VALLEY REGION OF WESTERN MAINE THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED COMMUNITY PREVENTION STRATEGIES. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF LOCAL COALITIONS, SCHOOLS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, BUSINESSES, PARENTS, AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS TO PREVENT UNDERAGE DRINKING BY CHANGING COMMUNITY NORMS, REDUCING YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL, AND INCREASING COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT. THESE COORDINATED EFFORTS WILL STRENGTHEN PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE, FOSTER SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY-LEVEL CHANGE, AND REDUCE THE HEALTH AND SOCIAL CONSEQUENCES ASSOCIATED WITH UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AND BINGE DRINKING, INCREASE COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION STRATEGIES, STRENGTHEN CROSS-SECTOR COLLABORATION, AND PROMOTE HEALTHY COMMUNITY NORMS THAT DISCOURAGE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE.  THE PROJECT ADDRESSES AN IDENTIFIED NEED FOR INCREASED COMMUNITY PREVENTION CAPACITY IN THIS PREDOMINANTLY RURAL REGION, WHERE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE REMAINS A SIGNIFICANT PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERN. CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS WILL STRENGTHEN LOCAL PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE BY ENHANCING COLLABORATION AMONG COMMUNITY PARTNERS, EXPANDING EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION PROGRAMMING, IMPROVING COMMUNITY READINESS, AND INCREASING THE ABILITY OF LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS TO IMPLEMENT, EVALUATE, AND SUSTAIN EFFECTIVE ALCOHOL PREVENTION INITIATIVES. THE PRIMARY POPULATION BENEFITING FROM THESE CAPACITY-BUILDING EFFORTS IS YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12-20 LIVING WITHIN THE NINE-TOWN SERVICE AREA. FAMILIES, SCHOOLS, AND THE BROADER COMMUNITY WILL ALSO BENEFIT THROUGH STRONGER PREVENTION SYSTEMS AND HEALTHIER ENVIRONMENTS THAT DISCOURAGE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE.  THE RIVER VALLEY RISING STOP ACT PROJECT IS A PRIMARY PREVENTION INITIATIVE AND DOES NOT PROVIDE CLINICAL TREATMENT SERVICES. PREVENTION STRATEGIES WILL INCLUDE STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS; CONDUCTING PUBLIC EDUCATION AND AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS; PROMOTING RESPONSIBLE BEVERAGE SERVICE, RETAILER COMPLIANCE, AND SOCIAL HOST EDUCATION; SUPPORTING ENFORCEMENT OF UNDERAGE DRINKING LAWS; REDUCING YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL THROUGH ENVIRONMENTAL PREVENTION STRATEGIES; ENGAGING YOUTH IN PREVENTION LEADERSHIP ACTIVITIES; AND USING LOCAL DATA TO GUIDE PLANNING, IMPLEMENTATION, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT. THE COALITION WILL STRENGTHEN THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS OF COMMUNITY PARTNERS THROUGH TRAINING, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND COORDINATED PLANNING TO ENSURE THE LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY OF PREVENTION EFFORTS.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: (1) INCREASING COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION IN PREVENTION INITIATIVES AND COALITION ACTIVITIES BY AT LEAST 20 PERCENT OVER THE PROJECT PERIOD; (2) INCREASING THE NUMBER OF COMMUNITY SECTORS ACTIVELY IMPLEMENTING EVIDENCE-BASED ALCOHOL PREVENTION STRATEGIES; (3) INCREASING AWARENESS AMONG YOUTH, PARENTS, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS OF THE RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AND BINGE DRINKING THROUGH ANNUAL EDUCATION CAMPAIGNS AND SURVEYS; (4) INCREASING RETAILER COMPLIANCE AND COMMUNITY SUPPORT FOR POLICIES AND PRACTICES THAT REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL; AND (5) REDUCING PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE AND BINGE DRINKING AMONG YOUTH AGES 12-20, AS MEASURED THROUGH LOCAL AND STATE SURVEY DATA. THESE OBJECTIVES ALIGN WITH SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES BY ADVANCING PREVENTION, STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY RESILIENCE, PROMOTING HEALTH EQUITY IN RURAL COMMUNITIES, AND IMPROVING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES THROUGH SUSTAINABLE, COMMUNITY-BASED PREVENTION EFFORTS.

description: OWN YOUR VIBE: HAMBLEN COUNTY UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION INITIATIVE - THE HAMBLEN COUNTY SUBSTANCE ABUSE COALITION (HCSAC) PROPOSES OWN YOUR VIBE: HAMBLEN COUNTY UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION INITIATIVE TO PREVENT AND REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING ACROSS HAMBLEN COUNTY, TENNESSEE. THIS INITIATIVE WILL STRENGTHEN LOCAL PREVENTION CAPACITY THROUGH COORDINATED EDUCATION, YOUTH AND PARENT ENGAGEMENT, RESPONSIBLE RETAIL PRACTICES, COMMUNITY AWARENESS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL STRATEGIES THAT REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL WHILE PROMOTING HEALTHIER YOUTH DEVELOPMENT.  THE OWN YOUR VIBE PROJECT WILL SERVE HAMBLEN COUNTY, A PREDOMINANTLY RURAL COMMUNITY OF APPROXIMATELY 68,000 RESIDENTS. IT RESPONDS TO THE NEED FOR STRONGER PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE, INCLUDING IMPROVED COORDINATION AMONG COMMUNITY PARTNERS, EXPANDED ACCESS TO SHARED DATA, INCREASED YOUTH LEADERSHIP OPPORTUNITIES, ENHANCED PARENT EDUCATION, STRONGER RETAILER ENGAGEMENT, AND MORE EFFECTIVE POLICY AND ENFORCEMENT STRATEGIES THAT LIMIT YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS YOUTH AGES 12-20 WHO ARE AT RISK FOR ALCOHOL INITIATION, CONTINUED USE, AND ALCOHOL-RELATED CONSEQUENCES. DIRECT SERVICES WILL INCLUDE SCHOOL-BASED PREVENTION EDUCATION, YOUTH LEADERSHIP AND PEER ACTIVITIES, PARENT OUTREACH AND EDUCATION, AND ALCOHOL-FREE COMMUNITY EVENTS THAT PROVIDE SAFE, STRUCTURED ALTERNATIVES TO UNDERAGE DRINKING.  HCSAC WILL IMPLEMENT FIVE COORDINATED, EVIDENCE-INFORMED STRATEGIES DESIGNED TO CREATE LASTING COMMUNITY IMPACT. THESE INCLUDE YOUTH ALCOHOL PREVENTION EDUCATION, THE PARENT POWER INITIATIVE, ALCOHOL-FREE COMMUNITY EVENTS, A RESPONSIBLE RETAILER PROGRAM, AND COUNTYWIDE AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS, SUPPORTED BY COMMUNITY MOBILIZATION THROUGH DATA REVIEW AND POLICY DEVELOPMENT. COLLECTIVELY, THESE STRATEGIES WILL ENGAGE SCHOOLS, PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS, YOUTH, RETAILERS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, FAITH LEADERS, LOCAL GOVERNMENT, AND OTHER COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS IN A UNIFIED PREVENTION EFFORT.  THE GOALS OF THE PROJECT ARE TO REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING, INCREASE YOUTH PERCEPTION OF RISK RELATED TO ALCOHOL USE, STRENGTHEN FAMILY PROTECTIVE FACTORS, REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL, INCREASE YOUTH PARTICIPATION IN HEALTHY, ALCOHOL-FREE ACTIVITIES, AND BUILD LONG-TERM COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO SUSTAIN PREVENTION EFFORTS THROUGH COLLABORATION AND SYSTEMS-LEVEL CHANGE.  THE PROJECT INCLUDES CLEAR AND MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES. EACH YEAR, HCSAC WILL PROVIDE ALCOHOL PREVENTION EDUCATION TO AT LEAST 3,000 YOUTH AND ENGAGE AT LEAST 250 PARENTS THROUGH OUTREACH AND EDUCATION ACTIVITIES. THE INITIATIVE WILL ALSO CONDUCT SIX ALCOHOL-FREE YOUTH EVENTS ANNUALLY, REACHING AT LEAST 1,500 PARTICIPANTS, AND ENGAGE 100 PERCENT OF LOCAL ALCOHOL RETAILERS IN RESPONSIBLE RETAIL EDUCATION AND AWARENESS ACTIVITIES. IN ADDITION, THE PROJECT WILL GENERATE AT LEAST 100,000 PREVENTION MESSAGE IMPRESSIONS THROUGH COUNTYWIDE AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS AND CONVENE TWO ANNUAL COMMUNITY TOWN HALL MEETINGS TO REVIEW LOCAL DATA, IDENTIFY EMERGING CONCERNS, AND GUIDE PREVENTION ACTION PLANNING.  THESE OBJECTIVES DIRECTLY SUPPORT SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES, INCLUDING PREVENTION, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, HEALTH PROMOTION, AND REDUCING SUBSTANCE MISUSE AMONG YOUTH.

description: PROTECTING HARDEE COUNTY YOUTH: DRUG FREE HARDEE A  COMMUNITY COALITION APPROACH TO PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING. - PROJECT ABSTRACT  PROJECT NAME: PROTECTING HARDEE COUNTY YOUTH: DRUG FREE HARDEE - A COMMUNITY COALITION APPROACH TO PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING, DRUG FREE HARDEE, INC., A DRUG-FREE COMMUNITIES (DFC)-PAST FUNDED PREVENTION COALITION, WILL USE STOP ACT GRANT FUNDING TO EXPAND ITS CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12 TO 20 IN HARDEE COUNTY, FLORIDA A RURAL, GEOGRAPHICALLY ISOLATED COMMUNITY WHERE 29.2% OF HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS REPORT ALCOHOL USE, BINGE DRINKING RATES EXCEED THE STATE AVERAGE BY NEARLY 85%, AND NO DEDICATED UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE CURRENTLY EXISTS OUTSIDE OF THE DFC COALITION.  GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND CAPACITY NEED: HARDEE COUNTY IS A 637-SQUARE-MILE AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITY IN SOUTH-CENTRAL FLORIDA WITH 26,068 RESIDENTS, NO PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION, NO HOSPITAL-BASED PREVENTION PROGRAMMING, AND NO COUNTY-FUNDED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTREACH FOR YOUTH. DRUG FREE HARDEE HAS THE ESTABLISHED COALITION INFRASTRUCTURE AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS TO ADDRESS UNDERAGE DRINKING BUT LACKS THE DEDICATED CAPACITY TO SUSTAIN A FOCUSED EFFORT ACROSS THE FULL 12-20 AGE RANGE. STOP ACT FUNDING WILL DIRECTLY CLOSE THIS GAP. POPULATION OF FOCUS: YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12 TO 20, REPRESENTING APPROXIMATELY 24.7% OF THE COUNTY'S POPULATION. THE GROUP IS 55.2% HISPANIC OR LATINO, WITH 18.9% WHITE NON-HISPANIC AND 5.2% BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN. NEARLY 31% OF HOUSEHOLDS SPEAK A LANGUAGE OTHER THAN ENGLISH AT HOME. THE POPULATION CARRIES COMPOUNDING RISK: 18.9% POVERTY RATE, 34% REPORT HOUSEHOLD SUBSTANCE ABUSE, AND 34.5% REPORT AN INCARCERATED HOUSEHOLD MEMBER ALL EXCEEDING FLORIDA STATE AVERAGES (2024 FYSA). STRATEGIES TO INCREASE CAPACITY • SPF-ALIGNED ENVIRONMENTAL STRATEGIES INCLUDING RETAIL ALCOHOL COMPLIANCE MONITORING WITH LAW ENFORCEMENT PARTNERS • EXPANSION OF YOUTH ADVISORY GROUPS UTHMPACT HARDEE (HIGH SCHOOL) AND STAND (MIDDLE SCHOOL) TO CO-CREATE PREVENTION PROGRAMMING • EVIDENCE-BASED SOCIAL NORMS CAMPAIGNS TARGETING MISPERCEPTIONS OF PEER ALCOHOL USE • CROSS-SECTOR COALITION COORDINATION WITH SCHOOLS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, AND YOUTH-SERVING ORGANIZATIONS. GOALS • GOAL 1: STRENGTHEN DRUG FREE HARDEE'S ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT AND SUSTAIN EVIDENCE-BASED UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION COUNTYWIDE. • GOAL 2: REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AND ALCOHOL-RELATED HARM AMONG HARDEE COUNTY YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12 TO 20. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES TIED TO SAMHSA STRATEGIC PRIORITIES • BY 9/29/2030, REDUCE HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS REPORTING PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE BY 5% FROM THE 2024 FYSA BASELINE OF 29.2%. • BY 9/29/2030, REDUCE STUDENTS REPORTING RIDING WITH AN IMPAIRED DRIVER FROM 16.4% TO NO MORE THAN 5% (2024 FYSA BASELINE). • BY 9/29/2028, INCREASE YOUTH AGES 12-17 PERCEIVING GREAT RISK FROM BINGE DRINKING FROM 58.1% TO 65% (2024 FYSA BASELINE). • BY 9/29/2027, ACHIEVE 90% RETAIL COMPLIANCE THROUGH ANNUAL UNDERAGE SALES COMPLIANCE CHECKS. • BY 9/29/2027, ENGAGE A MINIMUM OF 20 ACTIVE YOUTH MEMBERS IN COALITION PREVENTION PROGRAMMING.

description: WAKULLA COUNTY COALITION FOR YOUTH STOP ACT 2026 - PROJECT ABSTRACT WAKULLA COUNTY COALITION FOR YOUTH STOP ACT PROJECT OPPORTUNITY NUMBER SP-26-001  THE WAKULLA COUNTY COALITION FOR YOUTH (WCCY), WITH FISCAL AGENT FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY- FLORIDA CENTER FOR PREVENTION RESEARCH, REQUESTS A 4-YEAR STOP ACT GRANT TO EXPAND OUR CURRENT DRUG-FREE COMMUNITIES (DFC) SUPPORT PROGRAM TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 12 TO 20 IN RURAL WAKULLA COUNTY, FLORIDA.  GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND CAPACITY NEED  WAKULLA COUNTY SPANS 736 SQUARE MILES IN THE FLORIDA PANHANDLE, WITH AN ESTIMATED POPULATION OF 38,089 AS OF JULY 1, 2025, QUALIFYING AS RURAL UNDER SECTION 288.0656, FLORIDA STATUTES. THE CAPACITY NEED IS SUBSTANTIAL: COUNTY-LEVEL 2022 FLORIDA YOUTH SUBSTANCE ABUSE SURVEY (FYSAS) DATA SHOW WAKULLA STUDENTS EXCEED STATE AVERAGES ON EVERY ALCOHOL INDICATOR, INCLUDING 30-DAY USE (WAKULLA 11.5% VS. STATE 6.7%, MIDDLE SCHOOL; 28.7% VS. 15.5%, HIGH SCHOOL), WHILE WCCY'S CURRENT PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE REACHES ONLY ABOUT 200 STUDENTS ANNUALLY.  POPULATION OF FOCUS AND POPULATION SERVED THE POPULATION OF FOCUS FOR CAPACITY BUILDING IS WCCY AND ITS COALITION MEMBERSHIP. DIRECT PREVENTION SERVICES WILL ALSO REACH MIDDLE AND HIGH SCHOOL-AGED YOUTH (GRADES 6–12, AGES 11–18) IN THE WAKULLA COUNTY SCHOOL DISTRICT, WHERE MIDDLE AND HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS EXCEED STATE AVERAGES ON EVERY MEASURED ALCOHOL INDICATOR.  THIS WILL INCLUDE APPROXIMATELY 2,531 OF 5,134 TOTAL STUDENTS; THIS IS UNIVERSAL PREVENTION, NOT TREATMENT FOR A CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS.  SECONDARY POPULATIONS INCLUDE PARENTS, CAREGIVERS, AND EDUCATORS.  STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS THE PROGRAM BUILDS ON WCCY'S DRUG-FREE COMMUNITIES GRANT AND APPLIES THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK AND CADCA'S SEVEN STRATEGIES FOR COMMUNITY LEVEL CHANGE: EXPANDING TOO GOOD FOR DRUGS THROUGH A TRAIN-THE-TRAINER MODEL; ENGAGING THE FUTURE LEADERS OF WAKULLA YOUTH ADVISORY GROUP IN CO-CREATING PROGRAM ACTIVITIES; CONDUCTING A CAPACITY ASSESSMENT AND LOGIC MODEL; STRENGTHENING COORDINATION WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND LAW ENFORCEMENT ON ALCOHOL POLICY; CONVENING ANNUAL TOWN HALLS; AND RUNNING A LOCAL COMMUNICATIONS CAMPAIGN ALIGNED WITH SAMHSA'S TALK. THEY HEAR YOU RESOURCES.  GOALS AND MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES GOAL 1 IS TO BUILD WCCY'S CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT AND SUSTAIN EVIDENCE-BASED ALCOHOL PREVENTION SERVICES, ADVANCING SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITY OF PARTNERSHIP AND COORDINATION.  GOAL 2 IS TO PREVENT AND REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED PROGRAMS, ADVANCING SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITY OF PREVENTING SUBSTANCE USE AMONG YOUTH. OBJECTIVES INCLUDE TRAINING SCHOOL PERSONNEL TO DELIVER TOO GOOD FOR DRUGS TO MORE THAN 1,200 STUDENTS BY YEAR 4, RECRUITING MORE THAN 4 NEW COALITION MEMBERS ANNUALLY, AND CONVENING 1 TOWN HALL YEARLY. BY YEAR 4, MEASURED VIA AN ANNUAL WCCY YOUTH SURVEY OR FYSAS (IF AVAILABLE), WCCY TARGETS A 10% DECREASE IN PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE AMONG 6 TO 12TH GRADE STUDENTS, AND A 10% INCREASE IN PERCEIVED RISK OF HARM, PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL, AND PEER DISAPPROVAL, RELATIVE TO THE YEAR 1 BASELINE.

description: CREEK COUNTY PREVENTION PARTNERSHIP (C2P2) - THE CREEK COUNTY PREVENTION PARTNERSHIP (C2P2) IS A DRUG-FREE COMMUNITIES (DFC) COALITION DEDICATED TO REDUCING YOUTH SUBSTANCE USE THROUGH COMMUNITY COLLABORATION AND EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION STRATEGIES. USING THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK (SPF), C2P2 WORKS WITH SCHOOLS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, BUSINESSES, YOUTH-SERVING ORGANIZATIONS, PARENTS, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO ADDRESS CONDITIONS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO UNDERAGE DRINKING AND OTHER SUBSTANCE USE BEHAVIORS.  THE C2P2 STOP ACT PROJECT WILL ENHANCE EXISTING PREVENTION EFFORTS TO REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 12-20 IN CREEK COUNTY, OKLAHOMA. THE PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED ENVIRONMENTAL STRATEGIES DESIGNED TO REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL, STRENGTHEN PROTECTIVE FACTORS, AND PROMOTE HEALTHY COMMUNITY NORMS. KEY OBJECTIVES INCLUDE DECREASING PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE AMONG TWELFTH-GRADE STUDENTS; INCREASING COMMUNITY EDUCATION ACTIVITIES FOCUSED ON UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION; IMPLEMENTING A RESPONSIBLE BEVERAGE SERVICE AND SALES (RBSS) REFRESHER TRAINING INITIATIVE; INCREASING ADOPTION OF ALCOHOL-RELATED POLICIES AND BEST PRACTICES AMONG ALCOHOL RETAILERS AND SERVERS; EXPANDING RBSS PARTICIPATION; STRENGTHENING PARTNERSHIPS WITH LAW ENFORCEMENT TO CONDUCT ALCOHOL COMPLIANCE CHECKS (ACCS); AND REDUCING LOCAL ACC VIOLATION RATES.  THE COALITION WILL UTILIZE PUBLIC AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS, STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT, COMMUNITY MOBILIZATION, DATA-DRIVEN PLANNING, AND POLICY ENHANCEMENT EFFORTS TO ADDRESS LOCAL CONDITIONS ASSOCIATED WITH UNDERAGE DRINKING. THESE STRATEGIES WILL SUPPORT LONG-TERM REDUCTIONS IN YOUTH ALCOHOL USE WHILE INCREASING AWARENESS OF THE RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH UNDERAGE DRINKING AMONG YOUTH, PARENTS, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS.  THE STOP ACT PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON THE RURAL COMMUNITIES OF BRISTOW, DRUMRIGHT, MANNFORD, AND OILTON IN CREEK COUNTY, OKLAHOMA. THESE COMMUNITIES FACE UNIQUE PREVENTION CHALLENGES DUE TO GEOGRAPHIC ISOLATION AND LIMITED ACCESS TO RESOURCES. ACCORDING TO RECENT U.S. CENSUS BUREAU ESTIMATES, APPROXIMATELY 9,700 YOUTH AGES 10–19 RESIDE IN CREEK COUNTY. THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON YOUTH AGES 12–20 AND THE COMMUNITY SECTORS THAT INFLUENCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL AND PERCEPTIONS OF UNDERAGE DRINKING.  PROGRAM OUTCOMES WILL BE MEASURED USING THE FOUR STOP ACT CORE MEASURES AND DATA COLLECTED THROUGH THE OKLAHOMA PREVENTION NEEDS ASSESSMENT (OPNA), WHICH IS ADMINISTERED BIENNIALLY IN PARTICIPATING SCHOOLS. DATA FROM SIXTH, EIGHTH, TENTH, AND TWELFTH-GRADE STUDENTS WILL BE USED TO ASSESS CHANGES IN ALCOHOL USE, PERCEPTIONS OF RISK, PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL, AND PEER DISAPPROVAL. THESE MEASURES WILL GUIDE CONTINUOUS PROGRAM IMPROVEMENT AND HELP EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF COALITION-LED PREVENTION EFFORTS.

description: PROJECT STOP WILL WORK TO PREVENT UNDERAGE DRINKING AMONG YOUTH AGES 12-20, IN CENTRAL, SE AND SW SEATTLE AND THE CITIES OF AUBURN AND BURIEN IN SOUTH KING COUNTY, WA. - NEIGHBORHOOD HOUSE AND THE KING COUNTY DREAM COALITION (DFC COALITION) WILL IMPLEMENT PROJECT STOP TO PREVENT UNDERAGE DRINKING AMONG YOUTH AGES 12-20, IN CENTRAL, SE AND SW SEATTLE AND THE CITIES OF BURIEN AND AUBURN IN SOUTH KING COUNTY, WA WITH A TOTAL POPULATION OF 373,218 PEOPLE, 21% OF WHOM ARE BETWEEN THE AGES OF 9-25 YEARS OLD.   DATA INDICATE THAT THESE AREAS HAVE HIGH RISK FACTORS FOR ALCOHOL MISUSE AND THE HIGHEST RATES OF IMPAIRED DRIVING FATALITIES IN THE COUNTY. KING COUNTY IS EXPERIENCING A DRAMATIC RISE IN YOUTH TRAFFIC FATALITIES, THE MAJORITY OF WHICH INVOLVE ALCOHOL.  KING COUNTY HAS SEEN A TRIPLING OF TRAFFIC FATALITIES AMONG YOUTH UNDER AGE 25, FROM 16 FATALITIES IN 2019, TO 45 IN 2023, AND 31 IN 2024, THE TWO HIGHEST NUMBERS OF FATALITIES IN A DECADE. OUR PROJECT STOP PROPOSAL SEEKS TO REVERSE THIS TREND.    THROUGH A COMMUNITY NEEDS AND GAPS ASSESSMENT WE IDENTIFIED THE FOLLOWING CAPACITY NEEDS IN OUR COMMUNITY THAT OUR PROPOSAL SEEKS TO ADDRESS.   #1: INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF THE KING COUNTY DREAM COALITION TO CREATE A DATA-DRIVEN AND EVIDENCE-BASED NEEDS ASSESSMENT, LOGIC MODEL, 12 MONTH ACTION PLAN AND COALITION TRAININGS TO REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING AND ASSOCIATED HARMS.  #2: INCREASE COLLABORATION WITH COALITION MEMBERS AND 12 SECTORS TO IMPLEMENT DIRECT SERVICES THAT BUILD SKILLS FOR STRONG FAMILY MANAGEMENT, KNOWLEDGE OF PREVENTION ISSUES, YOUTH REFUSAL SKILLS, AND PROVIDE SUPPORT TO YOUTH AND REDUCE OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERAGE DRINKING THROUGH ALCOHOL FREE ACTIVITIES.    #3: INCREASE ENVIRONMENTAL STRATEGIES FOR COMMUNITY-LEVEL CHANGE THAT ENHANCE ACCESS/REDUCE BARRIERS, CHANGE CONSEQUENCES WITH INCENTIVES/DISINCENTIVES, CHANGE PHYSICAL DESIGN, AND MODIFY/CHANGE POLICIES AND SOCIAL NORMS INCLUDING MEDIA CAMPAIGNS SUCH AS  WWW.MOSTSTEERCLEAR.ORG, WWW.HELLOMYFUTURE.ORG & SAMHSA’S TALK THEY HEAR YOU.  USING THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK AND THE 7 STRATEGIES FOR COMMUNITY-LEVEL CHANGE WE WILL ACCOMPLISH OUR GOALS TO: 1) INCREASE CAPACITY IN OUR COMMUNITY TO FOSTER A LONG-TERM COMMITMENT TO REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING; AND 2) ENHANCE COLLABORATION AMONG 12 SECTORS TO CHANGE YOUTH, PEER AND PARENTAL PERCEPTION OF SOCIAL NORMS AND INCREASE PERCEIVED RISKS OF HARM OF UNDERAGE DRINKING THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES INCLUDING: YOUTH AND PARENT WORKSHOPS, COMMUNITY EDUCATION EVENTS, TOWN HALLS, POSITIVE NORMS MEDIA CAMPAIGNS & ALCOHOL-FREE EVENTS.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES FOR THE ENTIRE PROJECT PERIOD INCLUDE 10% INCREASE IN YOUTH PERCEPTION OF RISK/HARM OF DRINKING; 10% REDUCTION IN 30 DAY ALCOHOL USE; 10% INCREASE IN PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL; 10% INCREASE IN PEER DISAPPROVAL OF UNDERAGE DRINKING; AND 10% REDUCTION IN DRIVING UNDER THE INFLUENCE, OVER 4 YEARS BASED ON WA STATE HEALTHY YOUTH SURVEY). EACH YEAR WE WILL INVOLVE 50 YOUTH AND ADULTS IN A NEEDS ASSESSMENT; ENGAGE 200 COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN EVALUATION ACTIVITIES; TRAIN 40 FACILITATORS TO IMPLEMENT SPORT PREVENTION PLUS WELLNESS, GUIDING GOOD CHOICES AND OTHER ALCOHOL PREVENTION PROGRAMS; IMPLEMENT 32 ALCOHOL FREE YOUTH AND FAMILY ACTIVITIES TO 400 PEOPLE; PROVIDE ASSESSMENT/REFERRAL FOR ALCOHOL USE TO 80 YOUTH/PARENTS; AND REACH A TOTAL OF 40,000 PEOPLE IN OUR CATCHMENT AREA THROUGH BILLBOARDS, TRANSIT ADS, MOVIE THEATER TRAILERS, RADIO AND OTHER MEDIA/SOCIAL MEDIA.

description: GROWING STRONG, STAYING FOCUSED: WORKING TO PREVENT UNDERAGE DRINKING IN NORTH RIVER - NORTH RIVER PREVENTION PARTNERS (NRPP) HAS WORKED TO REDUCE SUBSTANCE USE AND MISUSE IN THE NORTH RIVER COMMUNITIES OF MANATEE COUNTY, FLORIDA SINCE 2015. THROUGH GROWING STRONG, STAYING FOCUSED, NRPP WILL BUILD ON PROVEN COALITION CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND REDUCE UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12 TO 20. AS A 2019 DRUG-FREE COMMUNITIES GRANTEE AND PRIOR STOP ACT RECIPIENT, NRPP WILL LEVERAGE STRONG PARTNERSHIPS TO POSITIVELY IMPACT COMMUNITY NORMS, INCREASE AWARENESS AND ENFORCEMENT OF EXISTING LAWS, REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS AND AVAILABILITY, AND STRENGTHEN PROTECTIVE FACTORS THAT SUPPORT HEALTHY YOUTH DEVELOPMENT.  DURING THE PANDEMIC, NRPP USED THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK TO IDENTIFY UNDERAGE DRINKING AS A SIGNIFICANT CONCERN IN NORTHERN MANATEE COUNTY AND BUILD PREVENTION CAPACITY THROUGH PARTNERSHIP DEVELOPMENT, STRATEGIC PLANNING, COMMUNITY EDUCATION, YOUTH LEADERSHIP, AND EVALUATION. THIS APPROACH WAS STRENGTHENED THROUGH NRPP'S 2022 STOP ACT AWARD. DURING THE FOUR-YEAR PROJECT CYCLE, NRPP DOCUMENTED A 24.3% REDUCTION IN 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND A 49.25% REDUCTION IN BINGE DRINKING. PEER PERCEPTION OF HARM AND SELF-PERCEPTION OF HARM INCREASED BY 3.13% AND 5.33%, RESPECTIVELY, WHILE PARENTAL PERCEPTION OF HARM DECREASED BY 0.3%, DEMONSTRATING THE CONTINUED NEED FOR PARENT-FOCUSED EDUCATION AND ENGAGEMENT.  PROPOSED ACTIVITIES INCLUDE EXPANDING ALTERNATIVE-TO-ATOD ACTIVITIES AND KNOW THE LAW, INCREASING THE NUMBER AND SCOPE OF LET’S TALK TOWN HALL EVENTS, EXPANDING PARENTS WHO HOST, LOSE THE MOST AND SAMHSA’S TALK. THEY HEAR YOU.® MEDIA CAMPAIGNS, AND ENHANCING THE NORTH RIVER YOUTH COALITION THROUGH YOUTH-LED PREVENTION MESSAGING ON SOCIAL MEDIA AND STREAMING PLATFORMS. NRPP WILL ALSO CONVENE COMMUNITY FEEDBACK MEETINGS, STRENGTHEN INTERGOVERNMENTAL AND CROSS-SECTOR COORDINATION, WORK WITH LOCAL PREVENTION PROGRAMS TO IDENTIFY GAPS AND AVOID DUPLICATION, DEVELOP A PROJECT LOGIC MODEL, AND IMPLEMENT A 12-MONTH ACTION PLAN WITHIN THE REQUIRED PROJECT PERIOD.  NRPP SERVES MORE THAN 52,000 RESIDENTS, PRIMARILY IN ZIP CODES 34219, 34220, 34221, AND 34222, INCLUDING PALMETTO, PARRISH, ELLENTON, RUBONIA, AND SURROUNDING NORTH RIVER COMMUNITIES. THE RAPIDLY GROWING CATCHMENT AREA INCLUDES PUBLIC SCHOOLS, CHARTER SCHOOLS, YOUTH-SERVING ORGANIZATIONS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITY SYSTEMS THAT NEED SUSTAINED PREVENTION CAPACITY, EXPANDED PARENT ENGAGEMENT, YOUTH-LED PREVENTION MESSAGING, AND COORDINATED STRATEGIES TO REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO REDUCE 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AGES 12 TO 20, INCREASE PERCEIVED PEER AND PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL, STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY COLLABORATION, AND EXPAND THE REACH OF EVIDENCE-BASED, EVIDENCE-INFORMED, AND COMMUNITY-DEFINED PREVENTION STRATEGIES. NRPP WILL TRACK REQUIRED STOP ACT MEASURES, INCLUDING PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE, PERCEPTION OF RISK OR HARM, PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL, AND PEER DISAPPROVAL FOR AT LEAST THREE GRADE LEVELS, ALONG WITH SPARS PERFORMANCE MEASURES, COALITION RECORDS, TRAINING PARTICIPATION, MEDIA REACH, SOCIAL MEDIA ANALYTICS, EVENT PARTICIPATION, AND PARTNER FEEDBACK. BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, NRPP WILL REDUCE 30-DAY YOUTH ALCOHOL USE BY 5%, INCREASE PERCEIVED PEER DISAPPROVAL BY 3%, AND INCREASE PERCEIVED PARENTAL DISAPPROVAL BY 3% FROM 2024 FYSAS MANATEE COUNTY BASELINES.  GROWING STRONG, STAYING FOCUSED ALIGNS WITH SAMHSA’S STRATEGIC PRIORITY OF PREVENTING SUBSTANCE USE AND MISUSE BY USING EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED PREVENTION STRATEGIES TO BUILD SOCIAL CONNECTEDNESS, STRENGTHEN FAMILIES, INCREASE COMMUNITY COHESION, AND SUPPORT HEALTHIER OUTCOMES FOR YOUTH AND FAMILIES IN NORTH RIVER.

description: UNITE FOR YOUTH: BUILDING HOPE IN LINCOLN COUNTY - PROJECT ABSTRACT - STOP ACT NOFO SP-26-01 LINCOLN COUNTY UNITE FOR YOUTH: BUILDING HOPE IN LINCOLN COUNTY LINCOLN COUNTY UNITE FOR YOUTH (UFY) WILL STRENGTHEN ITS CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12-20 IN LINCOLN COUNTY, MONTANA BY ADVANCING HOPE, RESILIENCE, AND WELLBEING. ALTHOUGH YOUTH ALCOHOL USE HAS DECLINED OVER THE PAST 16 YEARS, LOCAL DATA SHOW A CONCERNING DECREASE IN YOUTH CONNECTIONS TO TRUSTED ADULTS - A KEY PROTECTIVE FACTOR AGAINST SUBSTANCE USE. IN RESPONSE, UFY WILL ESTABLISH A YOUTH ADVISORY COMMITTEE AND IMPLEMENT POSITIVE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES (PCES), DEVELOPMENTAL RELATIONSHIPS, AND HEALTHY OUTCOMES FROM POSITIVE EXPERIENCES (HOPE) FRAMEWORKS TO STRENGTHEN YOUTH-ADULT CONNECTIONS, INCREASE PROTECTIVE FACTORS, AND SUPPORT SUSTAINED REDUCTIONS IN UNDERAGE DRINKING. LINCOLN COUNTY IS A FRONTIER COUNTY OF 3,612 SQUARE MILES, POPULATION 21,525, WITH NEARLY 1 IN 6 RESIDENTS BELOW THE POVERTY LEVEL. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12 TO 20; WHILE 2022 PNA DATA SHOW LONG-TERM DECLINES IN EARLY SUBSTANCE USE AND BINGE DRINKING, FEWER THAN ONE IN THREE LOCAL YOUTH REPORT A TRUSTED NEIGHBORHOOD ADULT, AND YOUTH-REPORTED DEPRESSION, SUICIDAL IDEATION, AND BULLYING EXCEED MONTANA STATE AVERAGES, IDENTIFYING A POPULATION NEEDING STRENGTHENED DEVELOPMENTAL RELATIONSHIPS ALONGSIDE CONTINUED ENVIRONMENTAL PREVENTION WORK. UFY WILL IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES INCLUDING SAMHSA'S SOURCES OF STRENGTH PROGRAM AND MONTANA INSTITUTE’S POSITIVE COMMUNITY NORMS (PCN) TRAINING. CONSISTENT COMMUNITY OUTREACH WILL ADAPT SAMHSA'S TALK. THEY HEAR YOU CAMPAIGN AND UTILIZE THE COMMUNITIES TALK PLATFORM. YOUTH AND TRUSTED ADULTS REPRESENTING AREA SCHOOLS, THE LINCOLN COUNTY SHERIFF'S OFFICE/NORTHWEST MONTANA DRUG TASK FORCE, AND LINCOLN COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENT, WILL WORK COLLABORATIVELY TO STRENGTHEN RELATIONSHIPS, PROMOTE HEALTHY LIFESTYLES, AND ELEVATE WELLBEING DURING NATIONAL DRUG AND ALCOHOL FACTS WEEK, ALCOHOL AWARENESS MONTH, AND SAMSHA’S PREVENTION WEEK.  A YOUTH ADVISORY COMMITTEE WILL CO-CREATE PROGRAMMING FROM DESIGN THROUGH IMPLEMENTATION. UFY ANTICIPATES SERVING APPROXIMATELY 800 TO 1,200 YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS ANNUALLY THROUGH DIRECT PROGRAMMING, AND REACHING THE FULL POPULATION OF FOCUS, APPROXIMATELY 3,600 TO 4,000 YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12 TO 20 COUNTYWIDE, ANNUALLY THROUGH INDIRECT, POPULATION-BASED PREVENTION EFFORTS OVER THE LIFE OF THE PROJECT. PROJECT GOALS: INCREASE UFY'S ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY TO DESIGN, IMPLEMENT, AND SUSTAIN RELATIONSHIP-CENTERED PREVENTION STRATEGIES THAT ELEVATE HOPE, RESILIENCE, AND WELLBEING AND PREVENT/REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12 TO 20 IN LINCOLN COUNTY. STRENGTHEN COOPERATION, COORDINATION, AND CITIZEN PARTICIPATION AMONG LOCAL, STATE, TRIBAL, AND FEDERAL PREVENTION PARTNERS THROUGH A DOCUMENTED LOGIC MODEL AND ACTION PLAN GROUNDED IN POSITIVE YOUTH DEVELOPMENT. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: WITHIN 120 DAYS, ESTABLISH A YOUTH ADVISORY COMMITTEE (10+ MEMBERS, AGES 12-20) TO CO-CREATE THE STOP PROJECT. BY PROJECT END, INCREASE BY AT LEAST 10 PERCENTAGE POINTS THE PROPORTION OF LINCOLN COUNTY YOUTH IN GRADES 8-12 REPORTING A TRUSTED ADULT RELATIONSHIP OUTSIDE THE FAMILY, VS. THE 2022 PNA BASELINE. ANNUALLY, REACH AT LEAST 3,600 INDIVIDUALS THROUGH INDIRECT/POPULATION-BASED PREVENTION EFFORTS AND SERVE AT LEAST 800 INDIVIDUALS THROUGH DIRECT/INDIVIDUAL-BASED PREVENTION EFFORTS.

description: EXPANDING YOUTH, PARENT, AND COMMUNITY AWARENESS OF AND ENGAGEMENT WITH ALCOHOL MISUSE PREVENTION IN MARTIN COUNTY - SUMMARY: MARTIN COUNTY SUBSTANCE ABUSE PREVENTION COALITION WORKS WITH STUDENTS MAINLY IN GRADES 7-12 IN MARTIN COUNTY, MINN., A RURAL COUNTY IN SOUTH CENTRAL MINNESOTA. ALCOHOL FELL OUT OF FAVOR WITH HIGH SCHOOLERS A FEW YEARS AGO, BUT NOW THE ALCOHOL CONSUMPTION NUMBERS ARE INCREASING AGAIN. THIS GRANT WILL HELP US REFOCUS ON UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION THROUGH ADVOCACY, EDUCATION, AND COMMUNITY COLLABORATION.  ABSTRACT: MARTIN COUNTY SUBSTANCE ABUSE PREVENTION COALITION HAS A GEOGRAPHIC FOCUS ON MARTIN COUNTY, MINN., A RURAL, AGRICULTURAL COUNTY IN SOUTH CENTRAL MINNESOTA KNOWN FOR ITS DRINKING CULTURE. ANECDOTALLY ALCOHOL CONSUMPTION IS UP BY OUR YOUTH, SO WE NEED TO STEER OUR ATTENTION THAT DIRECTION TO REDUCE RISK FACTORS AND BUILD UP PROTECTIVE FACTORS. OUR COUNTY HAS A POPULATION OF 19,657. NEARLY ONE-QUARTER IS MADE UP OF THOSE AGED 17 AND UNDER (24.8%, CENSUS.GOV). ABOUT 50% OF THOSE IN THE COUNTY ARE ON FREE/REDUCED MEALS. WE WILL BE WORKING PRIMARILY WITH STUDENTS IN GRADES 3-12 IN ALL PUBLIC SCHOOLS AND MANY OF THE PRIVATE SCHOOLS WITH SECONDARY INFLUENCE ON FAMILY UNITS, BUSINESSES, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS. WE WILL CREATE EVENTS AND IMPLEMENT STRATEGIES THAT ALIGN WITH THE 40 DEVELOPMENTAL ASSETS FROM SEARCH INSTITUTE STUDENTS NEED TO BECOME INDEPENDENT, MAKE GOOD CHOICES, AND THRIVE. THESE INCLUDE EXTERNAL ASSETS LIKE SUPPORT, EMPOWERMENT, BOUNDARIES, CONSTRUCTIVE USE OF TIME AND INTERNAL ASSETS LIKE COMMITMENT TO LEARNING, POSITIVE VALUES, SOCIAL COMPETENCIES, AND POSITIVE IDENTITY. WE WILL BE USING CADCA’S SEVEN STRATEGIES (CADCA IS AN ASSOCIATION FOR PREVENTION COALITIONS) AND SAMHSA’S STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK IN ADDITION TO A LOGIC MODEL. THESE WILL HELP US CRAFT OUR 12-MONTH ACTION PLAN. OUR GOALS FOR THE NEXT FOUR YEARS INCLUDE INCREASING YOUTH KNOWLEDGE OF AND ENGAGEMENT IN ADVOCACY IN ALCOHOL PREVENTION EFFORTS (90 STUDENTS); PROMOTE AND EXPAND AVAILABILITY OF SAFE, ALCOHOL-FREE COMMUNITY AND YOUTH CELEBRATIONS AND EVENTS (BY 25%) WITH INCREASED ATTENDANCE (BY 20%); INCREASE COMMUNITY AND PARENTAL INVOLVEMENT AND EDUCATION ON UNDERAGE DRINKING AND PREVENTION; AND EXPAND COMMUNITY AWARENESS OF AND ENFORCEMENT OF UNDERAGE DRINKING LAWS. WE WILL WORK TO INCREASE THE NUMBER OF STUDENTS INVOLVED WITH OUR COALITION WORK (BY 25%), TRAIN THEM IN ADVOCACY AND HAVE THEM PRESENT TO SCHOOL, CITY, AND COUNTY ELECTED OFFICIALS, AND SUPPORT THE EXPANSION OF THE ALATEEN SUPPORT GROUPS AND TEEN INTERVENE EVIDENCED-BASED CURRICULUM TO ALL PUBLIC HIGH SCHOOLS. WE ALSO WILL REACH OUT TO ALL EVENT VENUES TO ASSIST IN CRAFTING WRITTEN BEST PRACTICES FOR ALCOHOL SERVICE. WE WILL WORK TO INCREASE OUR SUPPORT OF AND STUDENT PARTICIPATION IN ALCOHOL-FREE COMMUNITY EVENTS LIKE POST-PROM, WORK TO HAVE 100% SUCCESSFUL COMPLIANCE CHECKS IN THE COUNTY, AND RECOGNIZE THOSE BUSINESSES THAT PASS COMPLIANCE CHECKS AND HAVE SERVERS ATTEND RESPONSIBLE BEVERAGE SERVER TRAINING. AS WE EDUCATE PARENTS, WE WILL WORK WITH LAW ENFORCEMENT TO ASSESS, PLAN, AND IMPLEMENT INCREASED ENFORCEMENT OF THE SOCIAL HOST ORDINANCE; SHARE KEY EDUCATIONAL MATERIAL LIKE THE OPERATION PARENT HANDBOOK WITH AT LEAST 1,000 PARENTS; RAISE AWARENESS OF ALCOHOL-RELATED HARMS TO YOUTH, AND FOCUS ON ALCOHOL REDUCTION BY 15% (AS GAUGED BY THE MINNESOTA STUDENT SURVEY) TO PROMOTE HEALTH AND WELLNESS. WE ESTIMATE OUR WORK WILL DIRECTLY IMPACT 2,000 STUDENTS, 1200 FAMILIES, AND 3,500 ADDITIONAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS ANNUALLY. OVER THE LIFE OF THE PROJECT, WE ESTIMATE 2,300 STUDENTS, 1,350 FAMILIES, AND 5,000 ADDITIONAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL BE SERVED. INDIRECTLY, MEDIA CAMPAIGNS WILL HAVE ANOTHER 750,000 IMPRESSIONS (NOT UNIQUE).

description: REDUCING UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE IN THE SOMERSET HILLS - THE COMMUNITY IN CRISIS (CIC) REDUCING UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE IN THE SOMERSET HILLS INITIATIVE IS A COMPREHENSIVE COMMUNITY-BASED PREVENTION EFFORT SERVING YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12-20 IN BEDMINSTER, BERNARDS TOWNSHIP, BERNARDSVILLE, FAR HILLS, AND PEAPACK-GLADSTONE, NEW JERSEY. THE PROJECT WILL REACH APPROXIMATELY 5,902 YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS, INCLUDING 4,565 AGES 12–17 AND 1,337 AGES 18–20. BUILDING ON SUCCESSFUL PREVENTION EFFORTS THAT CONTRIBUTED TO A DECLINE IN LOCAL HIGH SCHOOL ALCOHOL USE RATES, THE INITIATIVE BRINGS TOGETHER SCHOOLS, PARENTS, YOUTH LEADERS, COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, RETAILERS, AND HEALTHCARE PARTNERS TO REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING AND CREATE HEALTHIER ENVIRONMENTS FOR YOUNG PEOPLE. THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED EDUCATION, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, AND ENVIRONMENTAL PREVENTION STRATEGIES, THE PROJECT SEEKS TO STRENGTHEN PROTECTIVE FACTORS, PROMOTE HEALTHY DECISION-MAKING, AND REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL. THE PURPOSE OF THE PROJECT IS TO PREVENT AND REDUCE ALCOHOL USE AMONG YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 12–20 IN THE SOMERSET HILLS. THE INITIATIVE IS GUIDED BY SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK AND FOCUSES ON TWO PRIMARY GOALS: (1) CHANGING SOCIAL NORMS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO UNDERAGE DRINKING AND INCREASING AWARENESS OF THE RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH ALCOHOL USE, AND (2) REDUCING YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL WHILE INCREASING PARENTAL MONITORING AND ENGAGEMENT. TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS, CIC WILL IMPLEMENT A COMPREHENSIVE SET OF PREVENTION STRATEGIES, INCLUDING INTERACTIVE ENGAGEMENT STATIONS IN SCHOOLS, CLASSROOM AND SMALL-GROUP EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS, SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL LEARNING WORKSHOPS, YOUTH-LED SOCIAL NORMS AND MEDIA CAMPAIGNS, TARGETED OUTREACH TO STUDENT ATHLETES, PARENT UNIVERSITY EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS, RETAILER EDUCATION, STICKER SHOCK CAMPAIGNS, SOCIAL HOSTING AWARENESS INITIATIVES, LOCK YOUR STOCK CAMPAIGNS, AND PARENT COMMUNICATION CAMPAIGNS BASED ON SAMHSA’S TALK. THEY HEAR YOU RESOURCES. BY SEPTEMBER 2030, THE PROJECT WILL ACHIEVE MEASURABLE OUTCOMES INCLUDING REDUCTIONS IN PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE AMONG 8TH AND 12TH GRADE STUDENTS; INCREASES IN YOUTH DISAPPROVAL OF ALCOHOL USE AND PERCEPTION OF PEER DISAPPROVAL; REDUCTIONS IN ADULT APPROVAL OF UNDERAGE DRINKING; DECREASES IN PERCEIVED EASE OF OBTAINING ALCOHOL; INCREASES IN PARENT-CHILD COMMUNICATION ABOUT SUBSTANCE USE; REDUCTIONS IN COMMUNITY ACCEPTANCE OF SOCIAL HOSTING. PROGRESS WILL BE MEASURED THROUGH THE PRIDE STUDENT SURVEY, CIC COMMUNITY ASSESSMENT, PROGRAM PARTICIPATION RECORDS, AND COALITION PERFORMANCE MONITORING SYSTEMS. THROUGH SUSTAINED COLLABORATION AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, THIS INITIATIVE WILL HELP ENSURE THAT SOMERSET HILLS YOUTH HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, SUPPORT, AND OPPORTUNITIES NEEDED TO MAKE HEALTHY CHOICES AND AVOID THE RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH UNDERAGE ALCOHOL USE.

description: PROJECT LAZARUS WILKES YOUTH COALITION: STOP ACT - PROJECT LAZARUS WILKES YOUTH COALITION (PLWYC) WILL IMPLEMENT A FOUR-YEAR, COMMUNITY-DRIVEN PREVENTION INITIATIVE TO REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING AMONG YOUTH AGES 12–20 IN RURAL WILKES COUNTY, NORTH CAROLINA. THROUGH THE STRATEGIC PREVENTION FRAMEWORK (SPF), PLWYC WILL STRENGTHEN PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE CAPACITY, EXPAND EVIDENCE-BASED PROGRAMMING, ENGAGE YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND YOUTH SERVING PROFESSIONALS, AND BUILD SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS THAT REDUCE ALCOHOL-RELATED HARMS AND PROMOTE HEALTHY YOUTH DEVELOPMENT. THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE COMMUNITY CAPACITY, SHIFT SOCIAL NORMS SURROUNDING ALCOHOL USE, AND CREATE LONG-TERM SYSTEMS CHANGE THAT SUPPORTS YOUTH AND FAMILIES THROUGHOUT WILKES COUNTY.  PLWYC WILL SERVE WILKES COUNTY, NORTH CAROLINA, A LARGE RURAL COUNTY OF APPROXIMATELY 66,000 RESIDENTS THAT FACES SIGNIFICANT SOCIOECONOMIC AND HEALTH DISPARITIES. CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT IS NEEDED DUE TO LIMITED TRANSPORTATION, SHORTAGES OF YOUTH-SERVING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, INCREASING YOUTH MENTAL HEALTH CONCERNS, AND ALCOHOL-RELATED MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY RATES THAT CONSISTENTLY EXCEED STATE AVERAGES. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE COUNTY’S PREVENTION INFRASTRUCTURE BY EXPANDING CROSS-SECTOR PARTNERSHIPS, INCREASING YOUTH ENGAGEMENT, FORMALIZING PREVENTION SYSTEMS, AND IMPROVING COORDINATION AMONG SCHOOLS, HEALTHCARE ORGANIZATIONS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS. CAPACITY-BUILDING ACTIVITIES WILL ALSO BENEFIT PARENTS, CAREGIVERS, EDUCATORS, YOUTH-SERVING PROFESSIONALS, ALCOHOL MERCHANTS, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS WHO INFLUENCE YOUTH HEALTH BEHAVIORS. DIRECT PREVENTION EDUCATION WILL BE PROVIDED TO YOUTH AGES 12–20 THROUGH SCHOOL- AND COMMUNITY-BASED EVIDENCE-BASED PROGRAMS.   CAPACITY-BUILDING INTERVENTIONS WILL INCLUDE ESTABLISHING A YOUTH ADVISORY GROUP, FORMALIZING COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, CONDUCTING COALITION MEETINGS, IMPLEMENTING PARENT AND ALCOHOL MERCHANT TRAININGS, AND STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS. PREVENTION ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE DELIVERING SAMHSA-RECOGNIZED CURRICULA, TOO GOOD FOR DRUGS AND PROJECT TOWARD NO DRUG ABUSE, DISSEMINATING THE TALK. THEY HEAR YOU. CAMPAIGN, HOSTING ALCOHOL-FREE YOUTH EVENTS, TRAINING YOUTH-SERVING PROFESSIONALS, AND UTILIZING CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT TO REFINE INTERVENTIONS OVER TIME. THE PROJECT HAS THREE PRIMARY GOALS: (1) STRENGTHEN ORGANIZATIONAL AND COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING AMONG YOUTH AGES 12–20; (2) REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING AND SHIFT YOUTH, FAMILY, AND COMMUNITY NORMS RELATED TO ALCOHOL USE; AND (3) EXPAND THE REACH, COORDINATION, AND SUSTAINABILITY OF EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION STRATEGIES THROUGHOUT WILKES COUNTY.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: ESTABLISHING A YOUTH ADVISORY GROUP OF 10–15 YOUTH WITHIN 120 DAYS OF AWARD; FORMALIZING PARTNERSHIPS WITH AT LEAST THREE KEY COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS BY THE END OF YEAR 1; CONVENING AT LEAST FOUR COALITION MEETINGS AND FACILITATING SEVEN COMMUNITY TRAININGS ANNUALLY; ADMINISTERING LOCAL YOUTH SURVEYS TO MONITOR SAMHSA CORE MEASURES WITHIN 120 DAYS AND AGAIN IN YEAR 3; ACHIEVING A 3% REDUCTION IN PAST 30-DAY ALCOHOL USE AMONG SURVEYED YOUTH BY THE END OF YEAR 3; TRAINING 100 YOUTH-SERVING PROFESSIONALS BY SEPTEMBER 2030; AND PROVIDING EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION SERVICES TO AT LEAST 500 YOUTH ANNUALLY. THIS PROJECT DIRECTLY SUPPORTS SAMHSA’S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES OF PREVENTING SUBSTANCE MISUSE AND PROMOTING COMMUNITY-BASED PREVENTION SYSTEMS BY STRENGTHENING LOCAL CAPACITY, INCREASING PROTECTIVE FACTORS, AND CREATING SUSTAINABLE, DATA-DRIVEN APPROACHES THAT REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING AND IMPROVE LONG-TERM HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR YOUTH AND FAMILIES IN RURAL NORTH CAROLINA.

description: BUILDING COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO PREVENT UNDERAGE DRINKING IN ORANGE COUNTY - OP'S STOP PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION STRATEGIES TO BUILD CAPACITY FOR UNDERAGE DRINKING PREVENTION IN ORANGE COUNTY, NC, FOCUSING ON YOUTH IN GRADES 6-12. THE PROJECT WILL ADDRESS GROWING CONCERNS SURROUNDING ALCOHOL AND EXPAND THE COALITION’S EFFORTS THROUGH INCREASING COLLABORATION AMONG COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS AND ORGANIZATIONS AND REDUCING YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL.    ORANGE PARTNERSHIP (OP) IS A COMMUNITY COALITION WHOSE MISSION IS TO EMPOWER YOUTH TO IDENTIFY THESE RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS CONTRIBUTING TO YOUTH SUBSTANCE USE, PROPOSE STRATEGIES AND SOLUTIONS, AND FOSTER A SAFER AND HEALTHIER COMMUNITY WHERE ALL YOUTH CAN THRIVE. THE COALITION HAS OVER 60 ACTIVE MEMBERS FROM LOCAL YOUTH, SUBSTANCE USE PREVENTION ORGANIZATIONS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, HEALTHCARE AGENCIES, COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS, AND REPRESENTATIVES FROM TWO SCHOOL DISTRICTS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL SERVE YOUTH IN ORANGE COUNTY, NORTH CAROLINA, AN AREA KNOWN FOR ITS URBAN-RURAL SPLIT WITH TWO DISTINCT HALVES: CHAPEL HILL-CARRBORO, IN THE SOUTHERN HALF OF THE COUNTY AND HOME TO THE UNIVERSITY OF NORTH CAROLINA AT CHAPEL HILL, AND HILLSBOROUGH, THE COUNTY SEAT SURROUNDED BY FARMLAND. YOUTH UNDER 18 MAKE UP 18% OF THE COUNTY POPULATION, WHILE 29.6% ARE UNDER 21. ACCORDING TO THE YOUTH RISK BEHAVIOR SURVEY, ALCOHOL REMAINS THE MOST USED SUBSTANCE IN ORANGE COUNTY BY ADOLESCENTS (2025 OC YRBS). GIVEN THE PROXIMITY TO UNC-CHAPEL HILL, A SCHOOL WITH IN-STADIUM ALCOHOL SALES, TAILGATING, ROBUST GREEK LIFE, AND LARGE AMOUNTS OF UNDERAGE AND BINGE DRINKING, UNDERAGE DRINKING IS NORMALIZED IN THE COUNTY AMONG ADOLESCENTS AND EMERGING ADULTS. STUDENTS HAVE ALSO IDENTIFIED HOW EASY ALCOHOL IS TO ACCESS WHILE UNDERAGE BECAUSE MANY RETAILERS AND EVENT VENDORS DO NOT FOLLOW BEST PRACTICES FOR ALCOHOL SALES. WHILE EFFORTS HAVE BEEN MADE BY THE COALITION TO LIMIT EASY ACCESS TO ALCOHOL, IT REMAINS A LARGE PROBLEM IN THE COUNTY.    OVER THE COURSE OF FOUR YEARS, OP WILL INCREASE ADAPT YOUTH ENGAGEMENT THROUGH THE FOLLOWING GOALS: (1) INCREASE COLLABORATION AMONG COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS AND ORGANIZATIONS TO ADDRESS YOUTH SUBSTANCE USE AND (2) REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL. OBJECTIVES FOR GOAL 1 ARE INCREASING COALITION PREVENTION ACTIVITIES BY 20% AND INCREASING COMMUNITY PARTNER ENGAGEMENT IN ALCOHOL PREVENTION ACTIVITIES BY 10%, AS MEASURED BY COALITION MEETING ATTENDANCE AND ALCOHOL PREVENTION INITIATIVES. TO ADDRESS EASE OF ACCESS, OP WILL DECREASE YOUTH RETAIL ACCESS OF ALCOHOL BY 10% (MEASURED BY PURCHASE SURVEYS AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCANS), INCREASE NUMBER OF EVENT ORGANIZERS AND/OR SPONSORS THAT FORMALLY ADOPT BEST PRACTICES REGARDING ALCOHOL SALES FOR AT LEAST 3 COMMUNITY EVENTS (MEASURED BY EVENT PLANNER AGREEMENTS), AND INCREASE THE NUMBER OF FARM EVENT SPACES UTILIZING SAFE ALCOHOL USE POLICIES BY TWO (MEASURED BY SIGNED FARMER/LANDOWNER AGREEMENTS). STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS USED IN THE PROJECT INCLUDE RECRUITING AND ENGAGING YOUTH COALITION MEMBERS THROUGH SCHOOL-BASED ACTIVITIES, IDENTIFYING CONCERNS SURROUNDING UNDERAGE DRINKING IN COALITION MEETINGS AND CREATING A LOGIC MODEL AND 12-MONTH ACTION PLAN, CONDUCTING THE YOUTH RISK BEHAVIOR SURVEY (YRBS) BIENNIALLY TO COLLECT DATA, HOLDING TOWN HALL MEETINGS TO IDENTIFY ALCOHOL PREVENTION PRIORITIES, ASSESSING 20 ALCOHOL RETAILERS VIA PURCHASE SURVEYS OR ENVIRONMENTAL SCANS, AND CREATING MATERIALS OUTLINING BEST PRACTICES FOR ALCOHOL SALES/USE AT COMMUNITY AND BONA FIDE FARM EVENTS, AND IN CASE OF SOCIAL DISTRICT POLICY.

description: LAWRENCE COUNTY STOP PROJECT: PREVENTING UNDERAGE DRINKING THROUGH COMMUNITY AND YOUTH ENGAGEMENT - LAWRENCE COUNTY COALITION (LCC) WILL IMPLEMENT THE STOP PROJECT TO PREVENT AND REDUCE UNDERAGE DRINKING AMONG YOUTH IN GRADES 6-12 ACROSS LAWRENCE COUNTY, SOUTH DAKOTA. BUILDING ON LCC'S HISTORY OF COMMUNITY-BASED PREVENTION WORK, THE PROJECT WILL ENGAGE YOUTH, PARENTS, SCHOOLS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT TO STRENGTHEN ALCOHOL-SPECIFIC PREVENTION CAPACITY COUNTYWIDE. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE YOUTH-LED PREVENTION PLANNING, RETAILER ALCOHOL MANAGEMENT TRAINING, PARENT EDUCATION, AND DATA-DRIVEN COORDINATION WITH LOCAL YOUTH-SERVING SYSTEMS. THE PROJECT AIMS TO REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL AND INCREASE RECOGNITION OF THE RISKS OF BINGE DRINKING AMONG LAWRENCE COUNTY YOUTH.  THE PROJECT WILL BE IMPLEMENTED ACROSS THE ENTIRETY OF LAWRENCE COUNTY, AN 800-SQUARE-MILE RURAL COUNTY IN THE BLACK HILLS REGION OF WESTERN SOUTH DAKOTA COMPRISING SPEARFISH, LEAD, DEADWOOD, CENTRAL CITY, AND WHITEWOOD, WITH A RESIDENT POPULATION OF 28,809. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS IS ALL LAWRENCE COUNTY YOUTH IN GRADES 6-12, WITHIN SAMHSA'S TARGET AGE RANGE OF 12 TO 20. THIS IS A CAPACITY-BUILDING PROJECT; NO DIRECT CLINICAL OR TREATMENT SERVICES ARE PROPOSED. PREVENTION ACTIVITIES, INCLUDING TRAINING, EDUCATION, AND COMMUNITY PLANNING, ARE DELIVERED TO THE POPULATION OF FOCUS AND TO THE COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS, INCLUDING PARENTS, RETAILERS, AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT, WHO INFLUENCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL. LCC'S TWO PROJECT GOALS ARE TO INCREASE ORGANIZATIONAL AND COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO PREVENT UNDERAGE DRINKING IN LAWRENCE COUNTY, AND TO REDUCE YOUTH ACCESS TO ALCOHOL AND INCREASE PERCEIVED RISK OF BINGE DRINKING AMONG LAWRENCE COUNTY YOUTH IN GRADES 6-12. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE INCREASING THE PERCENTAGE OF STUDENTS WHO PERCEIVE GREAT RISK IN BINGE DRINKING FROM 41.4% TO AT LEAST 46.4%, DECREASING PERCEIVED EASE OF ALCOHOL ACCESS AMONG 12TH GRADERS FROM 30.9% TO 25.9%, AND INCREASING COMBINED YET MEMBERSHIP FROM 13 TO AT LEAST 18 YOUTH BY PROJECT END, CONSISTENT WITH SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES OF DATA-DRIVEN PREVENTION SCIENCE AND EXPANDED ACCESS TO PREVENTION SERVICES.
