description: CPNJ'S YOUTH AND FAMILY TREE: TREATMENT RECOVERY ENGAGEMENT AND EXPANSION - CARE PLUS NJ, INC. (CPNJ) WILL LAUNCH THE YOUTH AND FAMILY TREATMENT RECOVERY ENGAGEMENT AND EXPANSION (YF-TREE) PROJECT THROUGH SAMHSA’S TI-26-011 FUNDING OPPORTUNITY. THIS COMPREHENSIVE PROGRAM IS DESIGNED TO DELIVER CRITICAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CARE AND SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT TO CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUNG ADULTS AGES 0-25 EXPERIENCING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD) AND/OR CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS (COD), ALONG WITH THEIR FAMILIES AND PRIMARY CAREGIVERS.  THIS INITIATIVE WILL TARGET BERGEN AND PASSAIC COUNTIES IN NORTHERN NEW JERSEY, A HIGH-NEEDS REGION CHARACTERIZED BY ELEVATED RATES OF SUD AND COD, SOCIOECONOMIC HARDSHIP, AND LIMITED ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CARE FOR YOUTH, WITH A DENSE POPULATION OF APPROXIMATELY 1.5 MILLION INDIVIDUALS. OVER FIVE YEARS, THE YF-TREE PROJECT WILL SERVE A TOTAL OF 345 CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUNG ADULTS, REACHING 25 PARTICIPANTS IN YEAR 1 (ALLOWING FOR STARTUP AND RAMP-UP) AND 80 PARTICIPANTS ANNUALLY IN YEARS 2 THROUGH 5. THIS POPULATION MAKES UP A SIGNIFICANT PORTION OF THE GEOGRAPHIC AREA, INCLUDING 35% OF BERGEN COUNTY’S POPULATION AND 39% OF PASSAIC COUNTY. THE SERVICE POPULATION CONSISTS OF YOUTH AND EMERGING ADULTS AT HIGHER LIKELIHOOD FOR SUD/COD DUE TO TRAUMA EXPOSURE, SOCIOECONOMIC CHALLENGES, TRANSPORTATION ISSUES, AND A LACK OF EARLY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INTERVENTIONS.  CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS ARE DEFINED BY MOOD AND ANXIETY DISORDERS, TRAUMA- AND STRESSOR-RELATED CONDITIONS, SUD, AND SEVERE PREVALENCE OF COD, AS WELL AS HIGH RATES OF SUICIDAL IDEATION, SELF-HARMING BEHAVIORS, AND SECONDARY HEALTH RISKS SUCH AS OBESITY, BINGE DRINKING, AND SMOKING/VAPING.  YF-TREE WILL INCORPORATE TRAUMA-INFORMED, DEVELOPMENTALLY APPROPRIATE, AND COST-EFFECTIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE RECOVERY SERVICES. CPNJ’S COMPREHENSIVE CONTINUUM OF CARE INCLUDES SCREENING, EARLY INTERVENTION, OUTPATIENT TREATMENT, OVERDOSE PREVENTION, AND CARE COORDINATION. CPNJ WILL DELIVER THESE SERVICES VIA TELEHEALTH, AT ITS FAIR LAWN FACILITY, OR DIRECTLY IN THE COMMUNITY. BY LEVERAGING ESTABLISHED PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL SCHOOL DISTRICTS, SOCIAL SERVICE AGENCIES, AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, CPNJ WILL ENSURE RAPID REFERRALS AND SEAMLESS CONTINUITY OF CARE. THE PROGRAM WILL IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES, INCLUDING SEEKING SAFETY, COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (CBT), MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING (MI), AND TOBACCO CESSATION. MEDICATION-ASSISTED TREATMENT (MAT) WILL BE AVAILABLE AND COORDINATED THROUGH CPNJ’S OUTPATIENT SYSTEM. ALL SERVICES ARE EXPECTED TO COMMENCE WITHIN FOUR MONTHS OF THE AWARD.  GOALS INCLUDE: 1) EXPANDING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED SUD/COD TREATMENT FOR CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUNG ADULTS; 2) IMPROVING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, SUBSTANCE USE, RECOVERY AND FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES FOR CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, YOUNG ADULTS, THEIR FAMILIES, AND PREGNANT/PARENTING WOMEN; 3) STRENGTHENING FAMILY ENGAGEMENT; AND 4) STRENGTHENING CROSS-SYSTEM COORDINATION. ANTICIPATE OUTCOMES ARE SCREENING, ENROLLING, AND DEVELOPING INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT PLANS FOR 90% OF ELIGIBLE REFERRALS; ENSURING 75% OF ENROLLED CLIENTS PARTICIPATE IN 3 BRIEF INTERVENTION ACTIVITIES WITHIN THE FIRST 90 DAYS; IMPROVING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES, REDUCING SUBSTANCE USE, AND STRENGTHENING SERVICE RETENTION RATES; CONDUCTING 15 EDUCATIONAL WORKSHOPS ON OVERDOSE PREVENTION; AND FORMALIZING PARTNERSHIPS WITH A TOTAL OF 20 COMMUNITY AND YOUTH-SERVING ORGANIZATIONS.  THE PROJECT SUPPORTS SAMHSA’S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES BY ADDRESSING SUD/COD NEEDS AMONG YOUTH, REDUCING OVERDOSE RISK, AND STRENGTHENING REGIONAL CARE SYSTEMS. YF-TREE AIMS TO REMOVE OBSTACLES TO CARE AND CREATE SUSTAINABLE RECOVERY PATHWAYS FOR DISCONNECTED YOUTH IN NORTHERN NEW JERSEY.

OBJECTIVES INCLUDE INCREASING ENROLLMENT, ENSURING TIMELY SCREENING AND TREATMENT INITIATION, EXPANDING COMMUNITY EDUCATION AND REFERRALS, IMPROVING RETENTION, INCREASING ENGAGEMENT AMONG JUSTICE-INVOLVED YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS, AND ENSURING INTEGRATED ASSESSMENTS AND INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT PLANS FOR ALL ENROLLED PARTICIPANTS. GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND POPULATION. description: TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES FOR YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS, AND FAMILIES - THE PROPOSED PROJECT TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES FOR YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS, AND FAMILIES (TI-26-011) IS DESIGNED TO DELIVER COMPREHENSIVE TREATMENT, EARLY INTERVENTION, TREATMENT, RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES TO YOUTH (12-17) AND YOUNG ADULTS (18-25) YEARS OLD DIAGNOSED WITH A SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD) AND/OR CO-OCCURRING (COD) SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL HEALTH DISORDER. EARLY INTERVENTION AND EDUCATION SERVICES WILL BE DELIVERED TO CHILDREN UNDER 11 YEARS OF AGE AND THEIR FAMILIES.  THE PROJECT, WITHIN CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL LOS ANGELES, WILL FOCUS ON DELIVERING SERVICES AT TWO URBAN HIGH SCHOOLS, THREE COMMUNITY PARTNER AGENCIES, AND A LARGE URBAN PEDIATRIC EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT IN LOS ANGELES COUNTY. THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE EVIDENCE-BASED SUD AND COD TREATMENT SERVICES FOR YOUTH IN INDIVIDUAL AND GROUP SESSIONS, INTEGRATED CASE MANAGEMENT, FAMILY SUPPORT SERVICES, AND YOUTH RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES. FURTHERMORE, A YOUTH ADVISORY BOARD WILL BE DEVELOPED BY YOUTH IN TREATMENT AND RECOVERY TO ADVANCE THE PROJECT'S GOALS UTILIZING CRUCIAL ADVISEMENT FROM YOUTH.   THE PROJECT GOALS ARE: 1) TO EXPAND ACCESS TO COMPREHENSIVE EVIDENCE-BASED SUD/COD TREATMENT SERVICES FOR ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS; 2) TO ENHANCE ACCESS TO FAMILY CENTERED TREATMENT, SUPPORT, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES FOR ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS AND THEIR FAMILIES; 3) TO IMPROVE PARENT/CAREGIVER AWARENESS OF EARLY INTERVENTION STRATEGIES AND RESOURCES FOR SUD/COD TO SUPPORT HEALTHY AND DRUG FREE LIFESTYLES FOR THEIR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES THROUGH THE DELIVERY OF EDUCATIONAL PRESENTATIONS AT SCHOOLS, PARTNER AGENCIES, AND/OR AT COMMUNITY EVENTS; AND 4) TO RESPOND TO POTENTIAL THREATS AND SUBSTANCE USE TRENDS AMONG YOUTH THAT IMPACT SERVICE DELIVERY BY ENGAGING BY ESTABLISHING A YOUTH ADVISORY BOARD (YAB) THAT WILL PROVIDE REAL TIME AND CANDID RECOMMENDATIONS TO HELP PEERS.   IF FUNDED, CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL LOS ANGELES WILL ENROLL A MINIMUM OF 25 YOUTH IN THE FIRST YEAR AND 80 YOUTH ANNUALLY IN EACH SUBSEQUENT YEAR OF THE PROJECT'S TERM, YEARS 2-5. CHLA WILL ALSO REACH 500 PARENTS/CAREGIVERS THROUGH EDUCATIONAL AND INTERACTIVE PRESENTATIONS THAT INCLUDES LIFESAVING INFORMATION ON OVERDOSE PREVENTION AND HOW TO USE NALOXONE. THIS PROJECT WILL DEMONSTRATE THE POSITIVE IMPACT AND EFFECTIVENESS OF YOUTH, FAMILY, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS IN THE TREATMENT AND RECOVERY OF SUD AND COD AMONG OUR YOUTH.

description: 17TH CIRCUIT COURT TASC EXPANSION.  ENHANCE ITS CAPACITY TO SERVE ADULTS RESIDING IN KENT COUNTY MI WITH SIGNIFICANT SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, MENTAL HEALTH NEEDS, AND HIGH CRIMINOGENIC RISK. - THE KENT COUNTY TREATMENT AND SUPPORT COURT (TASC) REQUESTS FUNDING TO ENHANCE ITS CAPACITY TO SERVE ADULTS RESIDING IN KENT COUNTY MI WITH SIGNIFICANT SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, MENTAL HEALTH NEEDS, AND HIGH CRIMINOGENIC RISK. CURRENT STAFFING SHORTAGES AND LIMITED TREATMENT ACCESS HAVE RESULTED IN LIMITING THE NUMBER OF PEOPLE SERVED, DELAYS IN SCREENING/ASSESSMENT, INCONSISTENT ENGAGEMENT, AND GAPS IN RECOVERY SUPPORT. TASC AIMS TO INCREASE THE NUMBER OF PEOPLE SERVED, REDUCE DELAYS IN PROGRAM ENTRY, IMPROVE TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT, INCREASE RECOVERY CAPITAL, AND REDUCE RECIDIVISM. TASC WILL IMPLEMENT FIVE KEY STRATEGIES: (1) EXPAND RAPID SCREENING AND ELIGIBILITY DETERMINATION THROUGH A CONTRACTED CLINICIAN; (2) INCREASE RECOVERY CAPITAL VIA PEER COACHING, PROSOCIAL COMMUNITY CONNECTION, AND SUPPORTIVE HOUSING; (3) STRENGTHEN ACCESS TO MEDICATIONS FOR OPIOID USE DISORDER AND EVIDENCE BASED TREATMENT; AND (4) EXPAND PROGRAM CAPACITY; AND 5.) IMPROVE GRADUATION READINESS BY STABILIZING PARTICIPANTS IN HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, AND EDUCATION. THE PROJECT ALIGNS WITH SAMHA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES BY PREVENTING SUBSTANCE MISUSE, ABUSE, AND ADDICTION, IMPROVING ACCESS TO CO-OCCURRING TREATMENT COURT AND EVIDENCE BASED CO-OCCURRING TREATMENTS, HELPING INDIVIDUALS TO ACHIEVE LONG-TERM RECOVERY AND SOBRIETY, ADDRESSING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS AND CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS AND USING INTEGRATED EVIDENCE BASED APPROACHES. THE COURT WILL USE MONTHLY DATA MONITORING AND SEMI-ANNUAL PERFORMANCE REPORTING TO ENSURE ADHERENCE TO BEST PRACTICES, SUPPORT CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND DEMONSTRATE MEASURABLE GAINS IN PARTICIPANT SOBRIETY AND PUBLIC SAFETY.

description: SACRAMENTO COUNTY FAMILY TREATMENT COURT - PROJECT ABSTRACT-SACRAMENTO COUNTY FAMILY TREATMENT COURT- NOFO TI-26-015 SACRAMENTO COUNTY FAMILY TREATMENT COURT EXPANSION WILL DELIVER COORDINATED, TRAUMA-INFORMED SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORTS TO PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS INVOLVED WITH SACRAMENTO COUNTY CHILD PROTECTIVE SERVICES (CPS), ADDRESSING CHILD SAFETY CONCERNS AND PROMOTING FAMILY REUNIFICATION. THE PROJECT SERVES SACRAMENTO COUNTY, CALIFORNIA, COVERING 994 SQUARE MILES AND A POPULATION OF APPROXIMATELY 1.61 MILLION. ANNUALLY, AT LEAST 40 UNDUPLICATED PARENTS WILL BE ENROLLED, WITH A MINIMUM OF 200 SERVED OVER THE FIVE-YEAR GRANT PERIOD. THE INITIATIVE TARGETS ADULTS AGED 18 AND OLDER, INCLUDING MOTHERS, FATHERS, NON-BIRTHING PARENTS, KINSHIP CAREGIVERS, AND LEGAL GUARDIANS, WITHOUT PREFERENCE OR EXCLUSION. GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND POPULATION- SERVICE AREA: SACRAMENTO COUNTY, CALIFORNIA (994 SQ. MILES; ~1.61 MILLION RESIDENTS). ANNUAL REACH: AT LEAST 40 UNDUPLICATED PARENTS/CAREGIVERS PER YEAR; MINIMUM 200 OVER FIVE YEARS. AGE RANGE: ADULTS 18+; CHILDREN AGES 0-17 YEARS. DISTRIBUTION: PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS INVOLVED WITH CPS DUE TO SUBSTANCE USE-RELATED CHILD SAFETY CONCERNS CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS-DIAGNOSES: MODERATE TO SEVERE SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (METHAMPHETAMINE, OPIOIDS, INCLUDING FENTANYL, ALCOHOL, CANNABIS, POLYSUBSTANCE USE). SERVICE NEEDS: CO-OCCURRING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS (DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, PTSD, TRAUMA-RELATED DISORDERS, DOMESTIC VIOLENCE HISTORIES), HOUSING INSTABILITY, POVERTY, UNEMPLOYMENT, LIMITED TRANSPORTATION, INADEQUATE CHILDCARE, AND PUBLIC ASSISTANCE RELIANCE. ELIGIBILITY: BASED ON CHILD WELFARE INVOLVEMENT, FAMILY TREATMENT COURT PARTICIPATION, AND CLINICAL NEED; RACE/ETHNICITY NOT USED AS A CRITERION. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS: COMPREHENSIVE SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT, OVERDOSE PREVENTION EDUCATION AND NALOXONE DISTRIBUTION, EVIDENCE-BASED SUD TREATMENT (OUTPATIENT, INTENSIVE OUTPATIENT, RESIDENTIAL REFERRALS, MOUD/MAUD, COUNSELING, RELAPSE PREVENTION), TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICES AND RECOVERY SUPPORTS (HOUSING, PEER SUPPORT, TRANSPORTATION, CHILDCARE, EMPLOYMENT/EDUCATION REFERRALS), FAMILY ENGAGEMENT (THERAPY, PARENTING CLASSES, FATHERHOOD PROGRAMMING), INFECTIOUS DISEASE SCREENING AND LINKAGE TO CARE, EVIDENCE-BASED DRUG TESTING PROTOCOLS, ONGOING TRAINING FOR STAFF AND JUDICIAL OFFICERS. PROJECT GOALS: EXPAND ACCESS TO COORDINATED, EVIDENCE-BASED, TRAUMA-INFORMED SUD TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORTS FOR FAMILIES IN FAMILY TREATMENT COURT. STRENGTHEN FAMILY PRESERVATION AND SUPPORT TIMELY, SAFE REUNIFICATION FOR FAMILIES AFFECTED BY SUBSTANCE USE. REDUCE RELAPSE RISK AND PROMOTE LONG-TERM RECOVERY STABILITY THROUGH EXPANDED FAMILY-CENTERED RECOVERY HOUSING AND SUPPORT. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: ENROLL AT LEAST 40 PARENTS ANNUALLY; SERVE 200 OVER FIVE YEARS, ENSURE 75% OF ENROLLED PARENTS REMAIN ENGAGED IN TREATMENT/RECOVERY FOR 90+ DAYS EACH YEAR, ACHIEVE 75% REUNIFICATION OR PROGRESS FOR ELIGIBLE CHILDREN ANNUALLY, MAINTAIN AT-HOME PLACEMENT FOR 90% OF CHILDREN RESIDING WITH ENROLLED PARENTS, LINK 85% OF CHILDREN NEEDING SERVICES TO APPROPRIATE CARE, PROVIDE RECOVERY HOUSING/SUPPORTS TO 75% OF HOMELESS/HOUSING-UNSTABLE PARENTS, DEMONSTRATE REDUCED SUBSTANCE USE OR MAINTAINED ABSTINENCE FOR 60% OF PARENTS RECEIVING RECOVERY HOUSING, ACHIEVE PERMANENT HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, EDUCATION, OR SELF-SUFFICIENCY FOR 50% OF PARENTS AT DISCHARGE.

description: VAN BUREN COUNTY MENTAL HEALTH COURT EXPANSION & ENHANCEMENT - THE VAN BUREN COUNTY MENTAL HEALTH COURT (MHC) EXPANSION & ENHANCEMENT PROJECT SEEKS TO EXPAND PARTICIPANTS' ACCESS TO TREATMENT & RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES. FURTHERMORE, THE PROGRAM SEEKS TO INCREASE THE MHC TEAM'S CAPACITY TO MEET PARTICIPANTS NEEDS AS WELL AS MONITOR THE DEGREE TO WHICH THE PROGRAM OPERATES WITH FIDELITY TO THE MODEL AND IS ACHIEVING THE STATED GOALS/OBJECTIVES. THE GEOGRAPHIC SERVICE AREA IS VAN BUREN COUNTY, WHICH IS A RURAL COUNTY IN SOUTHWEST LOWER MICHIGAN WITH A POPULATION OF ~77,000 RESIDENTS. A TOTAL OF 225 INDIVIDUALS WILL BE SERVED DURING THE 5-YEAR FUNDING PERIOD (45 INDIVIDUALS PER YEAR). THE MHC SERVES NON-VIOLENT, HIGH-RISK/HIGH-NEED INDIVIDUALS 18 YEARS OR OLDER UNDER THE JURISDICTION OF VAN BUREN COUNTY'S CIRCUIT COURT (MISDEMEANOR & FELONY LEVEL) WHOSE CRIMINAL CONDUCT IS ROOTED IN AN UNDERLYING CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL HEALTH DISORDER. AMONG MHC PARTICIPANTS SERVED TO DATE, THE AGE RANGE WAS 18-69 YEARS. 98.1% HAD A CO-OCCURRING DISORDER & THE MOST OFTEN REPORTED SUBSTANCES OF USE WERE MARIJUANA (31.2%), METHAMPHETAMINE (27.9%), ALCOHOL (22.7%), HEROIN/OPIOIDS (7.7%). IN TERMS OF MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS, 30.8% HAD PTSD, 23.9% HAD BIPOLAR WITHOUT PSYCHOSIS, 22.0% HAD MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER, 12.6% HAD GENERAL ANXIETY DISORDER, & 9.4% HAD PERSISTENT DEPRESSIVE DISORDER (PDD). AT THE TIME OF PROGRAM ENROLLMENT, 68.5% HAD UNSTABLE HOUSING & 59.5% WERE UNEMPLOYED. THERE ARE 4 GOALS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS PROJECT ALL OF WHICH ALIGN WITH SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES. GOAL 1 - EXPAND PARTICIPANTS' ACCESS TO TREATMENT SERVICES. OBJECTIVE 1A) SCREEN & ASSESS INDIVIDUALS FOR SUD & COD, PRIMARY & BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, TRAUMA, & CRIMINOGENIC RISK/NEED. OBJECTIVE 1B) SCREEN INDIVIDUALS FOR INFECTIOUS DISEASES FOR WHICH THOSE WITH SUDS ARE AT HIGH RISK. PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH COORDINATED CASE MANAGEMENT SERVICES (OBJECTIVE 1C) & INTEGRATED EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT SERVICES (OBJECTIVE 1D) INFORMED BY SCREENING & ASSESSMENT RESULTS. OBJECTIVE 1E) PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH ACCESS TO FAMILY COUNSELING. OBJECTIVE 1F) PROVIDE MALE PARTICIPANTS WITH CRIMINAL THINKING PROGRAMMING THROUGH THE FACILITATION OF MORAL RECONATION THERAPY (MRT) & FEMALE PARTICIPANTS WITH MOVING ON. OBJECTIVE 1G) PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH PARENTING CLASSES THROUGH FACILITATION OF THE PARENTING INSIDE OUT - COMMUNITY (PIOC) CURRICULUM. OBJECTIVE 1H) FACILITATE TRAUMA SERVICES THROUGH THE DELIVERY OF SEEKING SAFETY (FOR WOMEN) & HELPING MEN RECOVER (FOR MEN) CURRICULA. OBJECTIVE 1) PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH ACCESS TO FDA-APPROVED MEDICATIONS (AS NEEDED). GOAL 2 - EXPAND PARTICIPANTS' ACCESS TO RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES. OBJECTIVE 2A) PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES INFORMED BY SCREENING & ASSESSMENT RESULTS. OBJECTIVE 2B) PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES THROUGH MEETINGS WITH A DEDICATED PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SPECIALIST (PRSS). OBJECTIVE 2C) PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH TRANSPORTATION ASSISTANCE TO/FROM PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS. OBJECTIVE 2D) PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH OVERDOSE REVERSAL EDUCATION & NALOXONE ADMINISTRATION TRAINING. PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS IN NEED WITH RECOVERY HOUSING (OBJECTIVE 2E) & HYGIENE PRODUCTS (OBJECTIVE 2F). GOAL 3 - INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF THE PROGRAM TO MEET THE NEEDS OF PARTICIPANTS. OBJECTIVE 3A) PROVIDE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR TEAM MEMBERS (E.G., ALL RISE ANNUAL MEETING & PEER-TO-PEER LEARNING SITE VISITS). ENSURE THE TEAM IS ABLE TO RESPOND APPROPRIATELY TO PARTICIPANTS' NEEDS THROUGH THE ADMINISTRATION OF DRUG/ALCOHOL TESTING (OBJECTIVE 3B) & CONDUCTING HOME VISITS WITH LAW ENFORCEMENT (OBJECTIVE 3C). GOAL 4 - ENSURE THE PROGRAM IS OPERATING WITH FIDELITY TO THE MODEL & ACHIEVING STATED GOALS/OBJECTIVES. CONDUCT SPARS INTAKE & FOLLOW-UP INTERVIEWS (OBJECTIVE 4A), ANALYZE DATA & DISSEMINATE REPORTS TO STAKEHOLDERS FOR CONTINUOUS PROGRAM IMPROVEMENT (OBJECTIVE 4B), & SUBMIT REQUIRED SEMI-ANNUAL SAMHSA REPORTS (OBJECTIVE 4C).

description: PROJECT RISE BIG SKY - PROJECT ABSTRACT - RISE BIG SKY THE 13TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT, YELLOWSTONE COUNTY, MONTANA, IS REQUESTING FUNDING THROUGH SAMHSA'S FUNDING OPPORTUNITY NO. TI-26-015: GRANTS TO EXPAND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT CAPACITY IN ADULT TREATMENT DRUG COURTS. THIS JOINT PROJECT SEEKS TO ENHANCE YELLOWSTONE COUNTY’S DUI COURT, STEER (SOBRIETY, TREATMENT, EDUCATION, EXCELLENCE, AND RECOVERY), AND ITS VETERANS TREATMENT COURT, CAMO (COURTS ASSISTING MILITARY OFFENDERS). BOTH ARE POST-ADJUDICATION COURTS THAT SERVE JUSTICE-INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUD) AND/OR CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS (COD). STEER AND CAMO JOINTLY REQUEST AVAILABLE FUNDING OF $400,000 PER YEAR FOR FIVE YEARS. FUNDS WILL BE UTILIZED TO IMPLEMENT PROJECT RISE BIG SKY, ALLOWING STEER AND CAMO TO EXPAND COURT CAPACITY AND ADDRESS BURGEONING WAIT LISTS.  RISE BIG SKY WILL OFFER IN-HOUSE COMPREHENSIVE TRAUMA-SPECIFIC ASSESSMENT AND INITIALIZE SUD/COD TREATMENT TO ALLEVIATE A SIGNIFICANT TREATMENT GAP WHEREIN PARTICIPANTS CURRENTLY RELY ON LIMITED RESOURCES. IN ADDITION, STEER AND CAMO WILL UTILIZE FUNDS TO EXPAND THEIR EVIDENCE-BASED CONTINUUM OF CARE, ENHANCE CASE MANAGEMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, AND FUND A TELESERVICES TRACK TO SERVE THE TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT NEEDS OF JUSTICE-INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS LIVING IN MONTANA’S VAST REMOTE AND RURAL AREAS. PROPOSED ENHANCEMENTS FOCUS ON AN EXISTING TREATMENT GAP WHEREIN CAMO AND STEER PARTICIPANTS EXPERIENCE DELAYS IN THE PROVISION OF SUD AND/OR COD TREATMENT. THIS PROJECT WILL ENABLE STEER AND CAMO TO HIRE DEDICATED STAFF (1.5 FTE) TO PROVIDE IMMEDIATE AND ONGOING COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT, LEVEL 1.0 SUD/COD TREATMENT AND RECOVERY CAPITAL-BASED PEER SUPPORT FOR PARTICIPANTS AND THEIR FAMILIES. THIS CONTINUUM OF CARE WILL BE AUGMENTED BY EXPERIENCED AND LICENSED PARTNERING SERVICE PROVIDERS.  YELLOWSTONE COUNTY CONTAINS APPROXIMATELY 169,000 RESIDENTS, WHICH REPRESENTS APPROXIMATELY 17% OF MONTANA'S TOTAL POPULATION, YET IT IS RESPONSIBLE FOR ROUGHLY 26% OF CRIMINAL FILINGS IN MONTANA. YELLOWSTONE COUNTY IS ADJACENT TO TWO OF MONTANA'S SEVEN NATIVE AMERICAN RESERVATIONS AND SITS ALONG INTERSTATE 90, A HIGH INTENSITY DRUG TRAFFICKING AREA. THE TARGET POPULATION FOR STEER INCLUDES HIGH-RISK/HIGH-NEED ADULTS CHARGED WITH A FELONY DUI, WHILE CAMO SERVES JUSTICE-INVOLVED VETERANS CHARGED WITH A QUALIFYING OFFENSE PER STATUTORY REQUIREMENTS. THE AGE RANGE OF STEER AND CAMO PARTICIPANTS IS DIVERSE, WITH THE YOUNGEST PARTICIPANT AGED 18 AND THE OLDEST AGED 92. OVER THE FIVE YEARS OF GRANT FUNDING, THE COURTS PLAN TO SERVE 300 UNDUPLICATED CLIENTS WITH A CENSUS OF 50 TO 70 CLIENTS ANNUALLY. MULTI-TRACK PARTICIPATION TIME RANGES FROM 15-24 MONTHS. THE COURTS ARE COMMITTED TO THE ALL RISE BEST PRACTICE STANDARDS AND ARE EVALUATED BI-ANNUALLY BY AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH FIRM TO DETERMINE THE EFFICACY OF POLICIES, PROCESSES, AND PROCEDURES. REQUESTED FUNDS WILL ALLOW STEER AND CAMO TO MORE EFFICIENTLY AND EFFECTIVELY SCREEN AND ASSESS PARTICIPANTS FOR SUD/COD, AND PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION, TREATMENT, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES TAILORED TO THE POPULATION’S SPECIFIC NEEDS. THE COURTS ARE ALSO COMMITTED TO ADVANCING SAMHSA’S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES BY PROVIDING EVIDENCE-BASED AND OUTCOME-FOCUSED TREATMENT; ADVANCING PROGRAM INTEGRITY AND FISCAL STEWARDSHIP; ENGAGING IN PARTNERSHIP AND COORDINATION BETWEEN LAW ENFORCEMENT, THE JUDICIARY, TREATMENT PROVIDERS, AND COMMUNITY RESOURCES; PROMOTING RECOVERY, SOBRIETY, AND SELF-SUFFICIENCY; AND RESPONDING TO EMERGING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH THREATS IN THE COMMUNITY.

description: PTW TREATMENT PROGRAM - THE PUEBLO OF POJOAQUE IS SEEKING FEDERAL FUNDING TO EXPAND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD) TREATMENT CAPACITY IN THE PATH TO WELLNESS (PTW) INTERTRIBAL HEALING TO WELLNESS ADULT DRUG COURT PROGRAM. THE GEOGRAPHIC CATCHMENT AREA INCLUDES THE PUEBLO OF POJOAQUE, A RURAL TRIBAL COMMUNITY WITH A LAND BASE OF 13,800 ACRES, AND THE RURAL TRIBAL AND HISPANIC COMMUNITIES OF THE POJOAQUE VALLEY, INCLUDING SAN ILDEFONSO, NAMBE, SANTA CLARA, TESUQUE AND OHKAY OWINGEH. POJOAQUE IS SITUATED JUST SOUTH OF RIO ARRIBA COUNTY, A COMMUNITY THAT HAS BEEN SEVERELY IMPACTED BY OPIOID USE DISORDER (OUD) AND SUD FOR DECADES, AND JUST NORTH 30 MINUTES NORTH OF THE CAPITAL CITY OF SANTA FE, NM, ALONG THE ONLY MAJOR HIGHWAY NORTH TOWARDS COLORADO OUTSIDE OF INTERSTATE 25. DUE TO THE GEOGRAPHICAL PROXIMITY TO THE STATE CAPITOL, LOS ALAMOS NATIONAL LABS, AND ALL ROUTES NORTH TO COLORADO, APPROXIMATELY 25,000 VEHICLES TRAVEL THROUGH THE PUEBLO OF POJOAQUE DAILY MAKING POJOAQUE PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TO THE SALE AND DISTRIBUTION OF SUBSTANCES.  DUE TO GEOGRAPHIC ISOLATION, LIMITED TREATMENT AVAILABILITY, AND MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDER SHORTAGES, THERE IS LIMITED ACCESS TO APPROPRIATE EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT (EBT) AND STEP-DOWN OPTIONS FOR INDIVIDUALS TRANSITIONING FROM TREATMENT (NM HCA, 2026). POJOAQUE VALLEY IS DESIGNATED AS A MENTAL HEALTH PROFESSIONAL SHORTAGE AREA WITH A SCORE OF 16, INDICATING A MODERATE-TO-HIGH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE SHORTAGE (HRSA DATA, 2026).  THE POJOAQUE PTW TREATMENT PROGRAM WILL ADDRESS THE UNMET TREATMENT NEEDS OF COURT-INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS EXPERIENCING SUD AND CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS. THIS PROJECT HAS ONE OVERALL GOAL, TWO PRIMARY GOALS AND FIVE OBJECTIVES. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE POJOAQUE PTW TREATMENT PROGRAM IS TO IMPROVE HEALTH AND RECOVERY OUTCOMES FOR JUSTICE-INVOLVED ADULTS WITH SUD.  THE PROGRAM WILL ACHIEVE THIS THROUGH COORDINATION, EBT, TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE, COMPREHENSIVE CASE MANAGEMENT, AND CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE RECOVERY SUPPORTS.  GOAL 1: EXPAND ACCESS TO COMPREHENSIVE SUD TREATMENT AND CASE MANAGEMENT FOR JUSTICE-INVOLVED ADULTS. ● OBJECTIVE 1.1. BY SEPTEMBER 30, 2031, ENGAGE 125 ELIGIBLE JUSTICE-INVOLVED ADULTS IN EBT FOR SUD AND CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS, WITH 90% RETAINED IN TREATMENT FOR AT LEAST SIX MONTHS AND 80% SUCCESSFULLY GRADUATING FROM THE PTW PROGRAM. ● OBJECTIVE 1.2. DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD, STRENGTHEN COORDINATED CARE AND REFERRAL PATHWAYS AMONG PTW PARTNERS, INCLUDING THE COURTS, PROBATION DEPARTMENT, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, TREATMENT PROVIDERS, OVERDOSE PREVENTION PROGRAM (ROAD), MEDICATION-ASSISTED TREATMENT (MAT) PROVIDERS, COMMUNITY HEALTH REPRESENTATIVES (CHRS), WITH 100% OF PARTICIPANTS RECEIVING LINKAGE TO APPROPRIATE SERVICES.  ● OBJECTIVE 1.3. DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD, PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE CASE MANAGEMENT SERVICES TO IMPROVE HEALTH AND RECOVERY OUTCOMES AMONG PTW PARTICIPANTS, RESULTING IN A 60% REDUCTION IN CRIMINAL JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT OR RECIDIVISM, A 60% INCREASE IN EMPLOYMENT, EDUCATION, OR VOCATIONAL PARTICIPATION, A 55% REDUCTION IN SELF-REPORTED SUBSTANCE USE, AND 80% SUSTAINED ENGAGEMENT IN TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES WITHIN SIX MONTHS OF ENROLLMENT. GOAL 2: STRENGTHEN FAMILY ENGAGEMENT AND LONG-TERM RECOVERY.  ● OBJECTIVE 2.1. BY SEPTEMBER 30, 2031, 85% OF PARTICIPANTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN AT LEAST ONE FAMILY CENTERED RECOVERY SERVICE OR FAMILY ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITY.  ● OBJECTIVE 2.2. BY SEPTEMBER 30, 2031, AT LEAST 50 PTW GRADUATES WILL ENGAGE IN AN ALUMNI RECOVERY PROGRAM TO STRENGTHEN SOCIAL CONNECTIONS, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND LONG-TERM RECOVERY.  WITH THESE CORE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES, POJOAQUE PTW TREATMENT PROGRAM WILL STRENGTHEN ITS CAPACITY TO DELIVER EFFECTIVE SUD TREATMENT, ADDRESS THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDER SHORTAGES FOR A REGION THAT LACKS ADEQUATE ACCESS TO PROVIDERS, EBT, AND TIMELY DIVERSION PROGRAMS, RESPOND TO THE ESCALATING DRUG-RELATED INCIDENTS WITHIN THE REGION, AND PREVENT OVERDOSE WITH RESPONSIVE, COORDINATED CAR

description: THE LHC/KINGMAN/BULLHEAD TRI-CITIES REGIONAL VETERANS TREATMENT COURT (TRI-CITIES RVTC) - THE LHC/KINGMAN/BULLHEAD TRI-CITIES REGIONAL VETERANS TREATMENT COURT (TRI-CITIES RVTC) BUILDS UPON A DECADE OF SUCCESSFUL COLLABORATION AND SERVICE DELIVERY TO JUSTICE-INVOLVED VETERANS IN MOHAVE COUNTY. FOLLOWING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE LAKE HAVASU CITY VETERANS TREATMENT COURT AND THE CITY OF KINGMAN VETERANS TREATMENT COURT, THE TWO JURISDICTIONS COMBINED RESOURCES IN 2016 TO FORM THE LAKE HAVASU CITY/KINGMAN REGIONAL VETERANS TREATMENT COURT. THE PROGRAM HAS DEMONSTRATED SUCCESS IN REDUCING RECIDIVISM AND IMPROVING PARTICIPANT OUTCOMES THROUGH THE USE OF EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES, INCLUDING JUDICIAL SUPERVISION, INTENSIVE CASE MANAGEMENT, SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT, AND VETERAN PEER MENTORSHIP.  THE PROPOSED TRI-CITIES RVTC WILL EXPAND THESE PROVEN SERVICES TO BULLHEAD CITY, ADDRESSING CRITICAL GAPS IN TREATMENT AND SUPPORT FOR JUSTICE-INVOLVED VETERANS THROUGHOUT MOHAVE COUNTY. WHILE THE CURRENT REGIONAL MODEL HAS IMPROVED ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, MANY VETERANS WHO ARE NON-COMBAT OR OTHERWISE INELIGIBLE FOR VETERANS ADMINISTRATION SERVICES CONTINUE TO FACE SIGNIFICANT BARRIERS TO TREATMENT. ADDITIONALLY, BULLHEAD CITY CURRENTLY LACKS A STRUCTURED VETERANS TREATMENT COURT PROGRAM.   THE PRACTICAL AND GAINFUL EXPERIENCE THE LAKE HAVASU PROGRAM HAS CULTIVATED AS IT HAS GROWN AND EXPANDED IS INVALUABLE AS COURTS IN OTHER COMMUNITIES SEEK TO DEVELOP THEIR OWN PROGRAMS AND BEST PRACTICES,  CONGRESSMAN PAUL A. GOSAR, D.D.S., NINTH DISTRICT, ARIZONA.   BY EXPANDING INTO BULLHEAD CITY, THE TRI-CITIES RVTC WILL INCREASE ACCESS TO COMPREHENSIVE TREATMENT, STRENGTHEN REGIONAL COORDINATION OF SERVICES, ENHANCE ACCOUNTABILITY, SUPPORT LONG-TERM RECOVERY, AND IMPROVE COMMUNITY REINTEGRATION OUTCOMES FOR VETERANS INVOLVED IN THE JUSTICE SYSTEM ACROSS MOHAVE COUNTY. BY THE 29TH OF SEPTEMBER 2031, THE TRI-CITIES RVTC IS PROJECTED TO SERVE A TOTAL OF 200 VETERANS; AT LEAST 50 VETERANS ANNUALLY RANGING IN AGE FROM 19 TO 90 YEARS OLD. AS THE NUMBER OF VETERANS TO BE SERVED BY THE TRI-CITIES RVTC CONTINUES TO GROW, SO DOES THE GAP IN SERVICE FOR SUBSTANCE ABUSE TREATMENT FOR THE PARTICIPANTS IN THIS PROGRAM WHO ARE INELIGIBLE TO RECEIVE LOCAL VA TREATMENT SERVICES, AS WELL AS THE NEED TO PROVIDE MORE PEER SUPPORT SERVICES TO ALL PARTICIPANTS.  THE TRI-CITIES RVTC IS REQUESTING $1,429,145 OVER A FIVE-YEAR PERIOD TO SUPPORT THIS EXPANSION AND ENHANCE ACCESS TO COMMUNITY-BASED SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT AND PEER SUPPORT SERVICES. THESE FUNDS WILL DIRECTLY SUPPORT PROGRAM CAPACITY TO SERVE VETERANS INELIGIBLE FOR VA SERVICES, WHO WOULD OTHERWISE REMAIN UNDERSERVED IN MOHAVE COUNTY. THIS INITIATIVE WILL STRENGTHEN THE PROGRAM'S ABILITY TO DELIVER A COORDINATED, EVIDENCE-BASED RESPONSE TO ALL JUSTICE-INVOLVED VETERANS, ADVANCING PRIORITIES OF THE SUBSTANCE ABUSE AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ADMINISTRATION (SAMHSA) BY REDUCING SUBSTANCE USE, IMPROVING QUALITY OF LIFE, AND INCREASE PARTICIPANT RETENTION AND GRADUATION RATES, WHILE ALSO LOWERING RECIDIVISM BY EXPANDING ACCESS TO SERVICES FOR JUSTICE-INVOLVED VETERANS WHO ARE INELIGIBLE FOR VA SERVICES, AS WELL AS BY PROVIDING STATE-MANDATED TREATMENTS-SUCH AS DOMESTIC VIOLENCE COUNSELING AND DRIVING UNDER THE INFLUENCE (DUI) PROGRAMS—TO VA ELIGIBLE VETERANS WHO LACK LOCAL ACCESS TO THESE SERVICES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: RECOVERY SUPPORTS ENHANCEMENT PROJECT - THE OTTAWA COUNTY RECOVERY COURT (OCRC) IS A PROGRAM OF THE 20TH JUDICIAL CIRCUIT COURT IN OTTAWA COUNTY, MICHIGAN.  FUNDS WILL SUPPORT OUR  RECOVERY SUPPORTS ENHANCEMENT PROJECT .  THIS PROJECT WILL SERVE A MINIMUM OF 45 NEW PARTICIPANTS PER YEAR AND IN DOING SO WILL: (1) EXPAND PROGRAM CAPACITY TO ADMIT ADDITIONAL ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS; (2) STRENGTHEN THE IDENTIFICATION AND ENROLLMENT OF HIGH-RISK/HIGH-NEED INDIVIDUALS WITH OPIOID AND METHAMPHETAMINE USE DISORDERS; AND (3) ENHANCE EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT, INTENSIVE CASE MANAGEMENT, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES FOR PARTICIPANTS WITH OPIOID AND METHAMPHETAMINE USE DISORDERS TO IMPROVE PROGRAM GRADUATION RATES AND REDUCE RECIDIVISM.  THE OCRC TARGETS ADULT, NON-VIOLENT FELONY OFFENDERS WITH SUBSTANCE USE (DRUGS AND/OR ALCOHOL) AND/OR CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS.  ALL PERSONS MUST HAVE A MODERATE TO SEVERE SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER ACCORDING TO THE DSM-5-TR, QUALIFY FOR INTENSIVE OUTPATIENT TREATMENT OR HIGHER ACCORDING TO THE AMERICAN SOCIETY OF ADDICTION MEDICINE (ASAM) CRITERIA, AND QUALIFY AS HIGH-RISK USING THE CORRECTIONAL OFFENDER MANAGEMENT AND PROFILING FOR ALTERNATIVE SANCTIONS (COMPAS) ASSESSMENT.  THIS PROJECT WILL SERVE RESIDENTS OF OTTAWA COUNTY, MICHIGAN.  ALL RECOVERY COURT PARTICIPANTS ARE OTTAWA COUNTY RESIDENTS, ALL DIRECT SERVICES PROVIDERS ARE IN OTTAWA COUNTY, AND ALL SERVICES WILL BE DELIVERED IN OTTAWA COUNTY.  OTTAWA COUNTY COVERS 565 SQUARE MILES, HAS AN ESTIMATED POPULATION OF 308,459, WITH 60% OF THE POPULATION FALLING BETWEEN AGES 18-65, WHICH HAS BEEN THE AGE RANGE FOR OVER 98% OF OUR PARTICIPANTS.  THE GOALS, OBJECTIVES, AND IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH FOR THIS PROJECT DIRECTLY ALIGN WITH SAMHSA'S SIX STRATEGIC PRIORITIES AND ARE GUIDED BY THE CROSS-CUTTING PRINCIPLES THAT SERVICES ARE DATA-DRIVEN, INNOVATIVE, AND GROUNDED IN GOLD-STANDARD SCIENCE.  OUR PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) INCREASE CAPACITY OF THE OCRC; (2) PROVIDE ENHANCED RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES; (3) PROVIDE ENHANCED TREATMENT SERVICES; (4) IMPROVE PARTICIPANTS' RECOVERY CAPITAL / SOCIAL FUNCTIONING; AND (5) REDUCE RECIDIVISM.  TO MEET THESE GOALS, WE WILL BE IMPLEMENTING EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES THAT INCLUDE THE USE OF CASE MANAGEMENT, PEER RECOVERY COACHING, MEDICATION ASSISTED TREATMENT, AND TRAUMA THERAPY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: PREVENTED TREATMENT COURTS APPLICATION - PREVENTED PROPOSES TO EXPAND EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES FOR ADULTS PARTICIPATING IN THE FRANKLIN COUNTY AND LINCOLN COUNTY TREATMENT COURTS IN RURAL EASTERN MISSOURI. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE A MINIMUM OF 45 UNDUPLICATED ADULTS ANNUALLY (225 OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD) WHO HAVE SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUD) AND, WHEN PRESENT, CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS (COD). THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE EXISTING TREATMENT COURTS BY EMBEDDING CERTIFIED PEER SPECIALISTS (CPS) AS PEER LIAISONS WITHIN EACH MULTIDISCIPLINARY TREATMENT COURT TEAM TO IMPROVE PARTICIPANT ENGAGEMENT, STRENGTHEN RECOVERY CAPITAL, REDUCE BARRIERS TO TREATMENT, AND INCREASE SUCCESSFUL TREATMENT COURT COMPLETION. WORKING IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE FRANKLIN COUNTY AND LINCOLN COUNTY TREATMENT COURTS, ARCA (ASSISTED RECOVERY CENTERS OF AMERICA) AND OTHER COMMUNITY RECOVERY ORGANIZATIONS, PREVENTED WILL COORDINATE COMPREHENSIVE SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT, EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT, MEDICATIONS FOR OPIOID AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDERS (MOUD/MAUD), OVERDOSE PREVENTION AND OPIOID OVERDOSE REVERSAL MEDICATION (OORM) EDUCATION, TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE, RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, EVIDENCE-BASED DRUG TESTING COORDINATION, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, INFECTIOUS DISEASE SCREENING AND REFERRAL, AND ONGOING EDUCATION FOR TREATMENT COURT PROFESSIONALS. CERTIFIED PEER SPECIALISTS WILL PROVIDE INDIVIDUALIZED RECOVERY COACHING, SYSTEMS NAVIGATION, TRANSPORTATION COORDINATION, RESOURCE LINKAGE, RECOVERY PLANNING, EMPLOYMENT AND EDUCATIONAL REFERRALS, FAMILY SUPPORT, AND TRANSITION PLANNING TO HELP PARTICIPANTS SUCCESSFULLY ENGAGE IN TREATMENT AND SUSTAIN LONG-TERM RECOVERY. THE PROJECT BUILDS UPON PREVENTED'S EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE DELIVERING RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, COORDINATING MULTIDISCIPLINARY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PARTNERSHIPS, AND ADMINISTERING FEDERALLY FUNDED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INITIATIVES THROUGHOUT EASTERN MISSOURI. PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION WILL EMPHASIZE COLLABORATION AMONG JUDICIAL, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, HEALTHCARE, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO IMPROVE CONTINUITY OF CARE AND REDUCE SERVICE FRAGMENTATION FOR JUSTICE-INVOLVED ADULTS. PROJECT OUTCOMES INCLUDE INCREASED TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT AND RETENTION, EXPANDED ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, INCREASED UTILIZATION OF MOUD/MAUD WHEN CLINICALLY INDICATED, IMPROVED RECOVERY CAPITAL, GREATER TREATMENT COURT RETENTION AND SUCCESSFUL PROGRAM COMPLETION, REDUCED OVERDOSE RISK, AND STRENGTHENED LONG-TERM RECOVERY. PERFORMANCE WILL BE MONITORED THROUGH SAMHSA'S PERFORMANCE ACCOUNTABILITY AND REPORTING SYSTEM (SPARS), PARTICIPANT OUTCOME MEASURES, FIDELITY MONITORING, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT ACTIVITIES TO ENSURE ACCOUNTABILITY AND ONGOING ENHANCEMENT OF PROGRAM EFFECTIVENESS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: JASPER COUNTY CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS COURT SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT EXPANSION PROJECT - THE COUNTY OF JASPER REQUESTS FEDERAL SUPPORT UNDER SAMHSA'S TREATMENT DRUG COURTS PROGRAM TO EXPAND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD) TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES WITHIN THE EXISTING JASPER COUNTY CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS COURT (CODC). CODC IS AN OPERATIONAL ADULT TREATMENT DRUG COURT SERVING JUSTICE-INVOLVED ADULTS AGE 18 AND OLDER WHOSE PRIMARY CLINICAL CONDITION IS SUD, INCLUDING INDIVIDUALS WITH CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL SERVE 50 UNDUPLICATED PARTICIPANTS ANNUALLY, FOR A TOTAL OF 250 ANNUAL PARTICIPANT SERVICE SLOTS OVER THE 5-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD. THIS ANNUAL TARGET REFLECTS UNDUPLICATED PARTICIPANTS EXPECTED TO RECEIVE GRANT-SUPPORTED SERVICES DURING EACH BUDGET YEAR, INCLUDING BOTH NEWLY ADMITTED PARTICIPANTS AND CONTINUING PARTICIPANTS IN A TREATMENT COURT MODEL THAT COMMONLY EXTENDS BEYOND 12 MONTHS.  THE PROPOSED SERVICE AREA IS JASPER COUNTY, MISSOURI. COUNTY AND LOCAL JUSTICE SYSTEM INDICATORS DEMONSTRATE A SUBSTANTIAL NEED. MISSOURI DEPARTMENT OF MENTAL HEALTH DATA IDENTIFY DRUG- AND ALCOHOL-RELATED MORTALITY, POVERTY, DRUG ARRESTS, AND TREATMENT-COURT DEMAND IN JASPER COUNTY, WHILE THE 2024 SEQUENTIAL INTERCEPT MODEL MAPPING REPORT IDENTIFIED TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, HOUSING INSTABILITY, SERVICE WAIT TIMES, HOSPITAL DISCHARGE COORDINATION PROBLEMS, AND CONTINUITY-OF-CARE GAPS BETWEEN THE JAIL, COURTS, AND COMMUNITY PROVIDERS. THE 29TH JUDICIAL CIRCUIT, IN ITS 2025 ANNUAL REPORT, FURTHER CONFIRMS LOCAL READINESS BY DOCUMENTING ACTIVE TREATMENT-COURT, PRETRIAL-SERVICES, AND JAIL-BASED CASE-MANAGEMENT INFRASTRUCTURE THAT CAN SUPPORT IMMEDIATE IMPLEMENTATION. GRANT FUNDS WILL EXPAND SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT FOLLOW-UP, CLINICAL TREATMENT ACCESS, COORDINATED CASE MANAGEMENT, PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT, RECOVERY HOUSING AND TRANSPORTATION LINKAGE, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, OVERDOSE PREVENTION EDUCATION, AND ACCESS TO MEDICATIONS FOR OPIOID AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDERS WHEN CLINICALLY INDICATED. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE IDENTIFIED THROUGH COURT, JAIL, PROSECUTION, DEFENSE, PROBATION AND PAROLE, AND OTHER JUSTICE-SYSTEM REFERRAL POINTS. JAIL-LINKED CASE MANAGEMENT WILL HELP REDUCE THE TIME BETWEEN IDENTIFICATION, ASSESSMENT, TREATMENT INITIATION, AND CONTINUITY OF CARE DURING DETENTION-TO-COMMUNITY TRANSITIONS. SERVICES WILL BEGIN WITHIN FOUR MONTHS OF THE AWARD. SAMHSA FUNDS WILL SUPPLEMENT, NOT SUPPLANT, EXISTING CODC COURT OPERATIONS, JUDICIAL SUPERVISION, PROBATION FUNCTIONS, OR BASELINE SERVICES.  THE PROJECT'S MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE STANDARDIZED SCREENING AND CLINICAL ASSESSMENT FOR ALL ADMITTED PARTICIPANTS; TREATMENT INITIATION WITHIN 14 DAYS FOR AT LEAST 90 PERCENT OF ADMITTED PARTICIPANTS; OVERDOSE PREVENTION EDUCATION FOR ALL PARTICIPANTS; DOCUMENTED ACCESS TO OPIOID OVERDOSE REVERSAL MEDICATION FOR AT LEAST 90 PERCENT OF PARTICIPANTS IDENTIFIED AS BEING AT RISK FOR OPIOID OVERDOSE; DOCUMENTED EVALUATION, LINKAGE TO, OR CONTINUATION OF MOUD OR MAUD FOR AT LEAST 90 PERCENT OF PARTICIPANTS FOR WHOM SUCH TREATMENT IS CLINICALLY INDICATED; AND DOCUMENTED LINKAGE TO KEY RECOVERY SUPPORTS FOR AT LEAST 85 PERCENT OF PARTICIPANTS WITH IDENTIFIED NEEDS.  THE PROJECT WILL COORDINATE WITH THE MISSOURI DEPARTMENT OF MENTAL HEALTH, DIVISION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, AS MISSOURI'S SINGLE STATE AGENCY FOR SUBSTANCE USE SERVICES DURING PLANNING, IMPLEMENTATION, PERFORMANCE MONITORING, EVALUATION, AND SUSTAINABILITY. THE PROJECT WILL USE SPARS AND ADMINISTRATIVE DATA TO SUPPORT REQUIRED PERFORMANCE REPORTING, IMPLEMENTATION MONITORING, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT. AN INDEPENDENT EVALUATION TEAM WILL PROVIDE FOCUSED IMPLEMENTATION AND OUTCOME REVIEW CONSISTENT WITH SAMHSA EXPECTATIONS. THE 29TH JUDICIAL CIRCUIT OF MISSOURI HAS NOT PREVIOUSLY RECEIVED SAMHSA TREATMENT DRUG COURTS FUNDING UNDER ANY PRIOR NOFOS.

description: SEMINOLE COUNTY ADULT TREATMENT COURT - PROJECT NAME: SEMINOLE COUNTY ADULT TREATMENT COURT - EXPANDING SUD TREATMENT CAPACITY APPLICANT: SEMINOLE COUNTY, FLORIDA | NOFO: TI-26-015 THE SEMINOLE COUNTY ADULT TREATMENT COURT (ATC) REQUESTS FIVE YEARS OF SAMHSA FUNDING TO EXPAND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD) TREATMENT CAPACITY BY EMBEDDING A LICENSED TREATMENT COURT CLINICAL COORDINATOR AND A PROGRAM INTAKE SPECIALIST WITHIN ITS  EXISTING MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM AND STRENGTHENING RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES FOR 50 UNDUPLICATED PARTICIPANTS ANNUALLY (250 OVER FIVE YEARS). OPERATING SINCE 2001 WITHIN THE 18TH JUDICIAL CIRCUIT NORTHEAST OF ORLANDO, THE ATC HAS ADMITTED 1,082 PARTICIPANTS, GRADUATED 617, AND MAINTAINS A 6.6 PERCENT CUMULATIVE RECIDIVISM RATE. GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND POPULATION. SEMINOLE COUNTY SPANS 344 SQUARE MILES WITH APPROXIMATELY 455,479 RESIDENTS. THE ATC SERVES ADULTS AGE 18 AND OLDER CHARGED WITH NON-VIOLENT FELONY OFFENSES WITH A PRIMARY SUD DIAGNOSIS, RANGING PRIMARILY FROM AGES 26 TO 45 (38 PERCENT FEMALE, 62 PERCENT MALE). ALCOHOL (41 PERCENT) AND OPIOIDS (28 PERCENT) ACCOUNT FOR NEARLY 70 PERCENT OF THE ACTIVE CASELOAD. CO-OCCURRING TRAUMA IS PREVALENT, AND PARTICIPANTS ARE HIGH-RISK FELONY-LEVEL OFFENDERS WHO WOULD OTHERWISE CYCLE THROUGH INCARCERATION WITHOUT INTERVENTION. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS. THE PROJECT IMPLEMENTS ALL TEN NOFO-REQUIRED ACTIVITIES: COMPREHENSIVE SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT; NALOXONE DISTRIBUTION AND OVERDOSE TRAINING; EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT (CBT, MET, SEEKING SAFETY, EMDR); MOUD/MAUD; TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE; PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT; EVIDENCE-BASED DRUG TESTING; FAMILY ENGAGEMENT; INFECTIOUS DISEASE SCREENING; AND ONGOING WORKFORCE TRAINING. GOALS AND OBJECTIVES. REDUCE REFERRAL-TO-TREATMENT TIME BY 25 PERCENT FROM THE FY2025 BASELINE OF 78.1 DAYS (YEAR 1); ACHIEVE 70 PERCENT 90-DAY RETENTION (YEAR 1); REACH A 60 PERCENT GRADUATION RATE (YEAR 3); ENSURE 100 PERCENT OF OPIOID-INVOLVED PARTICIPANTS RECEIVE NALOXONE AT ENROLLMENT (YEAR 1); AND SECURE NON-FEDERAL FUNDING FOR THE CLINICAL COORDINATOR POSITION BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD (YEAR 5).

subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: NJCRI TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES FOR YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS, AND FAMILIES PROGRAM - SUMMARY. NJCRI IS PROPOSING A PROJECT TO ENHANCE AND EXPAND COMPREHENSIVE TREATMENT, EARLY INTERVENTION, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES FOR TRANSITIONAL AGED YOUTH (AGES 18 TO 25) WITH SUD AND/OR COD, AND THEIR FAMILIES/PRIMARY CAREGIVERS IN THE GREATER NEWARK, NJ AREA. NJCRI WILL SERVE 125INDIVIDUALS A YEAR, TO SERVE A TOTAL OF 575 INDIVIDUALS THROUGHOUT THE PROGRAM PERIOD.  PROJECT NAME. TREATMENT ACCESS FOR YOUTH POPULATIONS TO BE SERVED. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS (POF) WILL BE TRANSITIONAL AGED YOUTH (AGES 18 TO 25) WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUD) AND/OR CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL DISORDERS (COD), AND THEIR FAMILIES/PRIMARY CAREGIVERS. FAMILIES/CAREGIVERS WILL INCLUDE LGBTQ MAKESHIFT FAMILIES AS WELL: MANY LGBTQ YOUTH, PARTICULARLY RUNAWAYS AND HOMELESS YOUTH, CREATE THEIR OWN SUPPORTIVE FAMILIES FROM FRIENDS AND MENTORS. THE POF IS MOSTLY AFRICAN AMERICAN/BLACK AND HISPANIC/ LATINO AND INCUDES LGBTQ PERSONS.  NJCRI’S CATCHMENT AREA WHERE SERVICES WILL BE DELIVERED WILL BE THE UNDERSERVED AND HIGH-NEED COMMUNITIES IN THE GREATER NEWARK, NJ AREA, AND WILL INCLUDE IRVINGTON, ELIZABETH, AND EAST ORANGE. STRATEGIES/INTERVENTIONS. PROGRAM ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE: 1) ENROLL AT LEAST 25 UNDUPLICATED CLIENTS IN YEAR 1 AND AT LEAST 80 IN EACH SUBSEQUENT YEAR. 2) SCREEN AND PROVIDE EARLY IDENTIFICATION FOR CLIENTS WHO ARE AT RISK FOR SUD. 3) DEVELOP PERSONALIZED TREATMENT PLANS. 4) PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED COMMUNITY-TAILORED SUD AND/OR COD SERVICES. 5) PROVIDE A CONTINUUM OF INTEGRATED TREATMENT SERVICES. 6) PROVIDE TREATMENT THAT RESPONDS TO THE UNIQUE NEEDS OF MALE AND FEMALE TREATMENT RECIPIENTS. 7) PROVIDE SUBSTANCE MISUSE INTERVENTION AND TREATMENT TO ELIMINATE ALCOHOL USE. 8) PROVIDE BRIEF BEHAVIORAL COUNSELING INTERVENTIONS AND TREATMENT TO REDUCE ALCOHOL MISUSE. 9) PROVIDE BRIEF INTERVENTION TO PROMOTE A TOBACCO-FREE LIFESTYLE. 10) PROVIDE EDUCATION ON MOUD, MAUD, OVERDOSE PREVENTION, NALOXONE, AND OVERDOSE REVERSAL MEDICATIONS. 11) PROVIDE EDUCATION ON MAKING HEALTHY CHOICES THAT INCLUDE NO USE OF ANY SUBSTANCES. 12) COORDINATE SERVICES WITH OTHER SOCIAL SERVICE AGENCIES. 13) COLLABORATE WITH COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS SPECIALIZING IN SERVING THE POF. 14) LINK PREGNANT AND PARENTING WOMEN TO COMMUNITY RESOURCES AND SUD/COD TREATMENT. 15) PROVIDE AFTERCARE SERVICES. 16) ENSURE THAT ALL SERVICES ARE DELIVERED IN AN EVIDENCE-BASED AND COST-EFFECTIVE MANNER. PROJECT GOALS AND MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES. THE GOAL IS TO ENHANCE AND EXPAND COMPREHENSIVE TREATMENT, EARLY INTERVENTION, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES FOR TRANSITIONAL AGED YOUTH (AGES 18 TO 25) WITH SUD AND/OR COD, AND THEIR FAMILIES/PRIMARY CAREGIVERS. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: 1) PROVIDE INTEGRATED OUTPATIENT SERVICES THROUGH ITS STATE-LICENSED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CARE PROGRAM TO 75 CLIENTS IN YEAR 1 AND 125 PARTICIPANTS PER YEAR IN THE FOLLOWING YEARS; 2: SCREEN CLIENTS (75 IN YEAR 1, 125 IN SUBSEQUENT YEARS) AND THEIR FAMILY MEMBERS FOR ALCOHOL MISUSE AND ILLICIT DRUG USE; 3: PROVIDE PERSONS ENGAGED IN RISKY OR HAZARDOUS DRINKING WITH BRIEF BEHAVIORAL COUNSELING INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE ALCOHOL MISUSE; 4: SCREEN ALL CLIENTS (75 IN YEAR 1 AND 125 IN SUBSEQUENT YEARS) AND THEIR FAMILY MEMBERS/PRIMARY CAREGIVERS FOR TOBACCO USE AND PROVIDE TOBACCO USE COUNSELING AND INTERVENTIONS AS PART OF A STANDARD OF PRACTICE, AS APPROPRIATE; 5: PROVIDE TOBACCO CESSATION COUNSELING TO 95% OF PARTICIPANTS IN NEED PER YEAR; 6: PROVIDE BI-WEEKLY EDUCATION AND MESSAGING ON MAKING HEALTHY CHOICES THAT INCLUDES NO USE OF ANY SUBSTANCES THROUGH SOCIAL MEDIA AND MARKETING, REACHING 5,000 PERSONS FROM THE POF PER YEAR; 7: PROVIDE MEDICATION FOR THE TREATMENT OF SUD TO 95% OF PARTICIPANTS IN NEED PER YEAR; 8: PROVIDE PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES TO 95% OF PARTICIPANTS IN NEED PER YEAR; 9: PROVIDE REFERRALS TO NJCRI’S COUNSELING, TESTING AND REFERRAL PROGRAM FOR HIV AND HCV TESTING AND HEPATITIS A AND B VACCINATIONS FOR 95% OF PARTICIPANTS IN NEED PER YEAR.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES FOR YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS, AND FAMILIES - LA MAESTRA FAMILY CLINIC, INC. (LA MAESTRA) REQUESTS $545,000 ANNUALLY FOR FIVE YEARS THROUGH THE SUBSTANCE ABUSE AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ADMINISTRATION (SAMHSA) YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULT TREATMENT (YTREE) PROGRAM TO EXPAND EVIDENCE-BASED SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD) AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDER (COD) TREATMENT SERVICES FOR CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUNG ADULTS (AGES 12–25) RESIDING IN SAN DIEGO COUNTY. AS A FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTER (FQHC), LA MAESTRA PROVIDES INTEGRATED PRIMARY CARE, MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES, PSYCHIATRIC CARE, OUTPATIENT SUD TREATMENT, RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, AND CARE COORDINATION THROUGH THE LA MAESTRA CIRCLE OF CARE® MODEL.  THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL IMPROVE TIMELY ACCESS TO COMPREHENSIVE, FAMILY-CENTERED CARE BY INTEGRATING SCREENING, BRIEF INTERVENTION, AND REFERRAL TO TREATMENT (SBIRT), MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING (MI), COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (CBT), PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, CARE COORDINATION, TELEHEALTH, AND MEDICATIONS FOR OPIOID, ALCOHOL, AND TOBACCO USE DISORDERS WHEN CLINICALLY INDICATED. PARTICIPANTS WILL RECEIVE COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENTS, INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT AND RECOVERY PLANS, RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, AND REFERRALS TO PRIMARY CARE, MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES, SPECIALTY TREATMENT, EDUCATION, HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, CHILD WELFARE, DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITY SERVICES, AND OTHER COMMUNITY RESOURCES BASED ON INDIVIDUAL NEEDS.  DURING THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, LA MAESTRA WILL ENROLL 50 UNDUPLICATED CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUNG ADULTS DURING PROJECT YEAR 1 AND 100 UNDUPLICATED PARTICIPANTS ANNUALLY DURING PROJECT YEARS 2–5, SERVING A TOTAL OF 450 UNDUPLICATED PARTICIPANTS. THE PROJECT WILL ENSURE THAT 100% OF PARTICIPANTS RECEIVE A COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT, AN INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT AND RECOVERY PLAN, AND APPROPRIATE EVIDENCE-BASED SERVICES WITHIN 30 DAYS OF ENROLLMENT; 100% OF PARTICIPANTS WILL RECEIVE RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, CARE COORDINATION, TRANSITION PLANNING, AND REFERRALS, AS APPROPRIATE; AND 80% OF PARTICIPANTS WILL HAVE AT LEAST ONE FAMILY MEMBER OR CAREGIVER PARTICIPATE IN TREATMENT PLANNING, FAMILY EDUCATION, FAMILY THERAPY, OR ANOTHER FAMILY SUPPORT ACTIVITY WHEN CLINICALLY APPROPRIATE.  LA MAESTRA WILL COLLABORATE WITH CHILDREN OF THE RAINBOW, TURN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, MCALISTER INSTITUTE, RADY CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL, THE SAN DIEGO COUNTY OFFICE OF EDUCATION'S JUVENILE COURT AND COMMUNITY SCHOOLS (JCCS), OPTUM, AND THE SAN DIEGO REGIONAL CENTER TO STRENGTHEN CARE COORDINATION AND ENSURE PARTICIPANTS HAVE ACCESS TO THE FULL CONTINUUM OF SERVICES. PROGRAM PERFORMANCE AND OUTCOMES WILL BE MONITORED THROUGH NEXTGEN, I2ITRACKS, GPRA, AND THE SAMHSA PERFORMANCE ACCOUNTABILITY AND REPORTING SYSTEM (SPARS). AN INDEPENDENT EVALUATOR FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA, SAN DIEGO HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH CENTER WILL CONDUCT ONGOING PROGRAM EVALUATION TO ASSESS PROGRESS TOWARD PROJECT GOALS, SUPPORT CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND PROMOTE LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY OF EVIDENCE-BASED SERVICES.  BY EXPANDING ACCESS TO INTEGRATED, EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES, STRENGTHEN FAMILIES, AND PROMOTE LONG-TERM RECOVERY FOR CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUNG ADULTS WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS THROUGHOUT SAN DIEGO COUNTY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
description: LOTUS HOUSE: EXPANDING A FAMILY-CENTERED CONTINUUM OF CARE FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN IN SOUTHERN INDIANA - LOTUS HOUSE: EXPANDING A FAMILY-CENTERED CONTINUUM OF CARE FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN IN SOUTHERN INDIANA. FAMILY ARK'S LOTUS HOUSE WILL EXPAND ACCESS TO COMPREHENSIVE, FAMILY-CENTERED SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD) TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT, POSTPARTUM, AND PARENTING WOMEN AND THEIR DEPENDENT CHILDREN IN SOUTHERN INDIANA. BUILDING UPON AN ESTABLISHED PROGRAM, THE PROJECT WILL ADD ASAM LEVEL 3.5 CLINICALLY MANAGED HIGH-INTENSITY RESIDENTIAL SERVICES TO AN EXISTING CONTINUUM THAT INCLUDES OUTPATIENT TREATMENT, INTENSIVE OUTPATIENT TREATMENT, RECOVERY HOUSING, PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND COORDINATED FAMILY SERVICES. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES A CRITICAL REGIONAL GAP BY ENABLING MOTHERS TO RECEIVE TREATMENT WHILE REMAINING WITH THEIR CHILDREN, EXPANDING ACCESS TO FAMILY-CENTERED RESIDENTIAL CARE IN RURAL COMMUNITIES WHERE THESE SERVICES ARE UNAVAILABLE, AND SERVING PREGNANT AND PARENTING WOMEN WHOSE RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT IS NOT OTHERWISE REIMBURSED THROUGH THE INDIANA DEPARTMENT OF CHILD SERVICES (DCS). FAMILY ARK SERVES CLARK, FLOYD, HARRISON, SCOTT, AND WASHINGTON COUNTIES, INCLUDING THREE HRSA-DESIGNATED RURAL COUNTIES. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE APPROXIMATELY 30-35 UNDUPLICATED WOMEN ANNUALLY (155 OVER FIVE YEARS), ALONG WITH THEIR DEPENDENT CHILDREN.  THE PROJECT WILL: (1) IMPLEMENT ASAM LEVEL 3.5 RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT INTEGRATED WITH EXISTING OUTPATIENT, INTENSIVE OUTPATIENT, RECOVERY HOUSING, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES; (2) INCREASE TIMELY ACCESS THROUGH TARGETED RURAL OUTREACH AND COORDINATED REFERRAL PARTNERSHIPS WITH HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, CHILD WELFARE AGENCIES, CRIMINAL JUSTICE PARTNERS, AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS; (3) ENSURE 100 PERCENT OF ENROLLED WOMEN AND THEIR CHILDREN RECEIVE COMPREHENSIVE SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT, INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT PLANNING, CARE COORDINATION, AND ACCESS TO NEEDED MEDICAL, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, DEVELOPMENTAL, AND SOCIAL SERVICES; (4) PROVIDE INDIVIDUALIZED RECOVERY SUPPORT AND TRANSITION PLANNING FOR 100 PERCENT OF PARTICIPANTS TO PROMOTE SUCCESSFUL COMMUNITY REINTEGRATION; AND (5) STRENGTHEN MULTIDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATION AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT THROUGH INDEPENDENT EVALUATION TO IMPROVE TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT, RECOVERY OUTCOMES, FAMILY PRESERVATION, AND LONG-TERM RECOVERY.

description: TRIBAL OPIOID RESPONSE: THE PURPOSE IS ADDRESS THE OUDS AND AODS IN TRIBAL COMMUNITIES BYPROVIDING MEDICATION ASSISTED TREATMENT, AS WELL AS COUNSELING, PREVENTION AND RECOVERY SUPPORT. - TRIBAL OPIOID RESPONSE GRANT: THE FALLON PAIUTE SHOSHONE TRIBE (FPST) WILL PRIMARILY SERVE AMERICAN INDIANS/ALASKAN NATIVES IN THE GEOGRAPHIC AREAS OF CHURCHILL COUNTY AND PERSHING COUNTRY WHERE THE FPST AND THE LOVELOCK PAIUTE TRIBE (LPT) ARE LOCATED. HOWEVER, IT IS COMMON FOR THE NORTHERN NEVADA AIAN POPULATION TO SEEK SERVICES THROUGH THE FPST BECAUSE IT HAS A HEALTH CENTER PARTIALLY FUNDED BY INDIAN HEALTH SERVICES AND ANY AIAN INDIVIDUAL CAN RECEIVE SERVICES THERE. THE AIAN POPULATION IN CHURCHILL COUNTY HAS APPROXIMATELY 1,523 PEOPLE AND PERSHING COUNTY HAS A POPULATION OF APPROXIMATELY 353 FOR A TOTAL OF ABOUT 1,876. THE NUMBER OF PEOPLE TO BE SERVED THROUGH THIS GRANT INCREASES EACH YEAR STARTING WITH 4 INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 1, 6 INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 2, 8 INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 3, 10 INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 4, AND 12 INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 5 FOR A TOTAL OF 40 INDIVIDUALS RECEIVING MAT THROUGHOUT THE LIFETIME OF THE PROJECT. THERE IS A DEARTH OF MAT PROVIDERS IN RURAL NORTHERN NEVADA SO WE BELIEVE THAT AS THE MAT PROGRAM DEVELOPS IT WILL ATTRACT MORE INDIVIDUALS SEEKING SERVICES. DATA FROM THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROGRAM FROM PRIOR YEARS SHOWS THAT THE MAJORITY OF INDIVIDUALS WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS OR CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS WERE GROUPED INTO THE 30-49 AGE GROUP WITH A RATIO OF MALE TO FEMALE BEING APPROXIMATELY 3:2.   INDIVIDUALS WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER OFTENTIMES STRUGGLE IN OTHER PARTS OF THEIR LIVES. THEY MAY BE INVOLVED IN THE CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM, LACK FORMAL EDUCATION, THEY MAY BE LIVING IN POVERTY AND UNABLE TO FIND EMPLOYMENT, THEY MAY HAVE CHILDREN IN OUT-OF-HOME CARE, AND THEY MAY HAVE UNTREATED HEALTH CARE ISSUES. IN ADDITION TO THEIR SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER, THEY MAY HAVE A MENTAL HEALTH DISORDER. DATA FROM THE FPST ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD SHOWS THAT THE MOST FREQUENT DIAGNOSIS FOR CLIENTS SERVED IN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WERE ANXIETY DISORDER AND POST-TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER. DEPRESSION IS ALSO ASSOCIATED WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS. SERVING INDIVIDUALS WITH THESE DISORDERS AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC STRUGGLES, THE TREATMENT APPROACH MUST BE WHOLISTIC AND COMPREHENSIVE. THROUGH THIS GRANT, THE FPST WILL PROVIDE MAT SERVICES TO INDIVIDUALS WITH AN OPIOID DISORDER OR OTHER SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER THAT CAN BE SERVED THROUGH MAT. INDIVIDUALS IN MAT TREATMENT WILL RECEIVE SUBSTANCE ABUSE COUNSELING TO ADDRESS BEHAVIORS AND MALADAPTIVE COPING ASSOCIATED WITH ADDICTION AS WELL AS MENTAL HEALTH THERAPY AS NEEDED. RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES WILL ASSIST THE INDIVIDUAL WITH COORDINATING CARE AND REFERRAL TO AND ASSISTANCE WITH OTHER NEEDS SUCH AS HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, SOCIAL SERVICES, COURT SERVICES, HEALTH CARE, AND MORE. THE FPST HAS ITS OWN VOCATIONAL REHABILITATION PROGRAM, COURT SERVICES, HOUSING DEPARTMENT, HEALTH CENTER, YOUTH AND FAMILY SERVICES, AND FOOD BANK THAT CAN PROVIDE SUPPORT TO INDIVIDUALS INVOLVED IN THE MAT PROGRAM.  PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: DECREASE OPIOID RELATED ADDICTION THROUGH MAT, THROUGH PROVIDING EVIDENCE-BASE PRACTICE TO INDIVIDUALS, THROUGH PROVIDING RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, AND THROUGH OVERDOSE EDUCATION AND NALOXONE DISTRIBUTION (OEND). OTHER GOALS INCLUDE DISSEMINATING WORKFORCE TRAINING AND EDUCATION TO ADDRESS OPIOID USE DISORDERS AND TO EXPAND PREVENTION EFFORTS AND INCREASE COMMUNITY OUTREACH. OBJECTIVE ARE TO: SERVE A TOTAL OF 40 INDIVIDUALS OVER THE 5-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, IMPLEMENT OEND (NARCAN KITS), TRAIN STAFF AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS IN OEND TOTALING 375 OVER 5-YEARS OF THE GRANT PERIOD AND CONDUCT PREVENTION ACTIVITIES INCLUDING CULTURAL PRACTICES THAT REACHES AT LEAST 700 PEOPLE OVER THE 5-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD. THE FPST WILL ADDRESS FOUR OF THE SAMHSA STRATEGIC PRIORITIES IN ITS OBJECTIVES.

description: MEETING KIDS WHERE THEY ARE: BUILDING AGE-APPROPRIATE SUBSTANCE USE CAREAND PREVENTION IN NORTH TEXAS - THE NORTH TEXAS BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AUTHORITY (NTBHA) REQUESTS FUNDING TO EXPAND CAPACITY TO A FULL CONTINUUM OF SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDER TREATMENT AND PREVENTION SERVICES FOR CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUNG ADULTS ACROSS ITS SIX-COUNTY NORTH TEXAS REGION, EXTENDING ITS EXISTING CERTIFIED COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINIC'S CARE TO A DEVELOPMENTALLY APPROPRIATE STANDARD FOR YOUNGER POPULATIONS. HOMEWARD BOUND, INC., NTBHA'S DESIGNATED SUD TREATMENT PROVIDER, WILL DELIVER THIS PROJECT'S SERVICES ALONGSIDE STRUCTURAL PARTNERS CHILD AND FAMILY GUIDANCE CENTER (CFGC) AND SOUTHERN AREA BEHAVIORAL HEALTHCARE SERVICES (SABH). NTBHA SERVES A SIX-COUNTY CATCHMENT AREA OF DALLAS, ELLIS, HUNT, KAUFMAN, NAVARRO, AND ROCKWALL COUNTIES, TEXAS, WITH A POPULATION OF APPROXIMATELY 3.3 MILLION RESIDENTS. THIS PROJECT WILL SERVE NO FEWER THAN 30 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 1 AND NO FEWER THAN 80 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS IN EACH SUBSEQUENT PROJECT YEAR, TOTALING NO FEWER THAN 350 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS ACROSS THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, SPLIT EVENLY BETWEEN ADOLESCENT OUTPATIENT SUD/COD TREATMENT (AGES 12-17) AND CHILDREN'S PREVENTION EDUCATION (AGES 11 AND UNDER), WITH YOUNG ADULTS (AGES 18-25) SERVED THROUGH THE ADOLESCENT OUTPATIENT TREATMENT TRACK. THE POPULATION PLANNED TO BE SERVED PRESENTS WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS AND/OR CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL DISORDERS (COD), INCLUDING OPIOID USE DISORDER, AMID RISING FENTANYL-DRIVEN ADOLESCENT OVERDOSE MORTALITY IN NTBHA'S CATCHMENT AREA. THIS PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT CRAFFT 2.1+N SCREENING, EXTENDED BUPRENORPHINE-NALOXONE MEDICATION FOR OPIOID AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDER (MOUD/MAUD), A DEVELOPMENTALLY ADAPTED OUTPATIENT SUD/COD TREATMENT MODEL, RAINBOW DAYS' EVIDENCE-INFORMED CURRICULUM-BASED SUPPORT GROUP PREVENTION PROGRAM, CASE MANAGEMENT, AND PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT, DELIVERED THROUGH HOMEWARD BOUND'S EXISTING CCBHC INFRASTRUCTURE UNDER A NO WRONG DOOR MODEL WITH CFGC AND SABH. TREATMENT AND PREVENTION SERVICES ARE PATIENT-CENTERED AND GENDER-RESPONSIVE, AND ARE PAIRED WITH BRIEF COUNSELING TO REDUCE RISKY DRINKING AMONG YOUNG ADULTS AND FAMILIES AND WITH OVERDOSE PREVENTION EDUCATION AND NALOXONE ACCESS COORDINATED THROUGH NTBHA'S EXISTING OUTREACH AND COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER PROGRAMS. THIS PROJECT'S GOAL IS TO BUILD A FULL CONTINUUM OF SUD/COD CARE FOR CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUNG ADULTS ON HOMEWARD BOUND'S EXISTING CCBHC CLINICAL INFRASTRUCTURE, EXTENDING PROTOCOLS THAT CURRENTLY SERVE ADULTS TO A DEVELOPMENTALLY APPROPRIATE STANDARD OF CARE FOR YOUNGER POPULATIONS. THIS PROJECT HAS THREE MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: (1) ENROLL NO FEWER THAN 30 UNDUPLICATED CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUNG ADULTS IN YEAR 1, AND NO FEWER THAN 80 UNDUPLICATED CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUNG ADULTS IN EACH SUBSEQUENT PROJECT YEAR; (2) ESTABLISH ADOLESCENT-SPECIFIC MOUD/MAUD PRESCRIBING, CONSENT, AND CONFIDENTIALITY PROTOCOLS WITHIN THE FOUR-MONTH SERVICE-START WINDOW REQUIRED BY THIS NOFO; AND (3) FORMALIZE PROJECT-SPECIFIC REFERRAL AND COORDINATION AGREEMENTS WITH PARTNER AGENCIES WITHIN FOUR MONTHS OF AWARD.

description: COMPREHENSIVE FAMILY-CENTERED SUBSTANCE USE AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDER TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES FOR ADOLESCENTS AND FAMILIES IN SOUTH CAROLINA'S CHARLESTON TRI-COUNTY REGION - THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROPOSAL, COMPREHENSIVE FAMILY-CENTERED SUBSTANCE USE AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDER TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES FOR ADOLESCENTS AND FAMILIES IN SOUTH CAROLINA'S CHARLESTON TRI-COUNTY REGION, IS TO EXPAND AND STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF THE FAMILY TREE PROGRAM AT MUSC, TO PROVIDE A COMPREHENSIVE, FAMILY-CENTERED, TRAUMA-INFORMED, EVIDENCE-BASED, COORDINATED, AND COST-EFFECTIVE OUTPATIENT SYSTEM OF CARE FOR ADOLESCENTS 12–17 WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUD), WITH AND WITHOUT CO-OCCURRING TRAUMA-RELATED MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS (COD), AND THEIR FAMILIES, THROUGHOUT CHARLESTON, BERKELEY, AND DORCHESTER COUNTIES (POPULATION APPROXIMATELY 830,000). THROUGH AN INTEGRATED NETWORK OF CLINICAL PROGRAMS, MULTI-DISCIPLINARY TREATMENT PROVIDERS, AND LONGSTANDING COMMUNITY COLLABORATIONS, THE PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT A COORDINATED CONTINUUM OF SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT, WRAPAROUND SERVICES, INDIVIDUALLY-TAILORED RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND COMPREHENSIVE SUBSTANCE USE EDUCATION PROGRAMMING DESIGNED TO REDUCE ADOLESCENT SUBSTANCE USE, IMPROVE TRAUMA-RELATED MENTAL HEALTH OUTCOMES, STRENGTHEN FAMILY FUNCTIONING, AND PROMOTE LONG-TERM RECOVERY. FAMILY TREE WILL ENROLL 48 UNDUPLICATED ADOLESCENTS AGES 12-17 IN YEAR 1 AND 80 UNDUPLICATED ADOLESCENTS ANNUALLY IN YEARS 2–5, SERVING 368 UNDUPLICATED ADOLESCENTS OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, WHILE ENGAGING THEIR FAMILIES/CAREGIVERS THROUGHOUT TREATMENT AND RECOVERY. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE MALE AND FEMALE ADOLESCENTS AGES 12–17 WITH SUD, WITH AND WITHOUT TRAUMA-RELATED COD (E.G., PTSD, DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, EMOTION DYSREGULATION, BEHAVIORAL PROBLEMS, SCHOOL IMPAIRMENT, FAMILY CONFLICT), INCLUDING YOUTH INVOLVED WITH THE CHILD WELFARE, JUVENILE JUSTICE, AND OTHER SOCIAL SERVICE SYSTEMS. THE PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT SBIRT; COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT; INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT PLANNING; EVIDENCE-BASED OUTPATIENT TREATMENT USING RISK REDUCTION THROUGH FAMILY THERAPY (RRFT) AND FAMILY-ENHANCED MOTIVATIONAL ENHANCEMENT THERAPY PLUS COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (MET/CBT); FAMILY-CENTERED WRAPAROUND CARE, CASE MANAGEMENT, AND AFTERCARE GUIDED BY A COLLABORATIVELY DEVELOPED INDIVIDUAL RECOVERY PLAN (IRP); EDUCATION REGARDING MAUD, MOUD, OVERDOSE PREVENTION, NALOXONE, TOBACCO CESSATION, AND NICOTINE REPLACEMENT THERAPY (NRT) REFERRAL WHEN CLINICALLY INDICATED; COORDINATED REFERRAL FOR PREGNANT AND PARENTING ADOLESCENTS AND FAMILY MEMBERS; SCHOOL- AND COMMUNITY-BASED PREVENTION AND EARLY IDENTIFICATION; AND COORDINATION WITH SCHOOLS, JUVENILE JUSTICE, CHILD WELFARE, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, FAITH-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND COMMUNITY AGENCIES.. THE OVERARCHING GOAL IS TO REDUCE ADOLESCENT SUD AND TRAUMA-RELATED COD BY EXPANDING ACCESS TO INTEGRATED, EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: SCREENING ≥90% OF ADOLESCENTS AND FAMILY MEMBERS USING SBIRT, ENSURING 100% OF THOSE SCREENING POSITIVE RECEIVE BRIEF INTERVENTION AND REFERRAL AS INDICATED; COMPLETING COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENTS AND INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT/RECOVERY PLANS FOR 100% OF ENROLLED ADOLESCENTS; PROVIDING RRFT OR FAMILY-ENHANCED MET/CBT TO 48 ADOLESCENTS IN YEAR 1 AND 80 ANNUALLY THEREAFTER; PROVIDING FAMILY-CENTERED WRAPAROUND SERVICES, RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND AFTERCARE TO 100% OF ENROLLED ADOLESCENTS AND FAMILIES; ENSURING 100% OF INDICATED PARTICIPANTS RECEIVE EDUCATION AND LINKAGE REGARDING MAUD/MOUD, NALOXONE, OVERDOSE PREVENTION, AND NRT; DELIVERING CATCH MY BREATH AND OTHER SUBSTANCE USE EDUCATION TO AT LEAST 330 ADOLESCENTS; AND COORDINATING REFERRALS WITH COMMUNITY PARTNERS FOR 100% OF ENROLLED ADOLESCENTS. BY ADDRESSING THE CRITICAL GAP IN INTEGRATED, FAMILY-CENTERED TREATMENT FOR ADOLESCENTS WITH SUD AND TRAUMA-RELATED COD, THE PROJECT DIRECTLY ADVANCES SAMHSA STRATEGIC PRIORITIES BY PREVENTING SUBSTANCE MISUSE, EXPANDING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT, ADDRESSING SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS THROUGH INTEGRATED CARE, AND SUPPORTING LONG-TERM RECOVERY.

description: LAZARUS FAMILIES IN RECOVERY SUPPORT TOGETHER (LAZARUS FIRST) - PROJECT LAZARUS WILL IMPLEMENT LAZARUS FIRST (LAZARUS FAMILIES IN RECOVERY SUPPORT TOGETHER), A FAMILY-CENTERED TREATMENT AND RECOVERY PROGRAM SERVING CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, YOUNG ADULTS, AND THEIR FAMILIES/PRIMARY CAREGIVERS AFFECTED BY SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER IN WILKES AND YADKIN COUNTIES, NORTH CAROLINA. OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, LAZARUS FIRST WILL ENROLL 490 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS, PAIRING FAMILY-CENTERED PEER RECOVERY COACHING, TRAUMA-INFORMED YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULT MENTORING, AND EVIDENCE-BASED PARENT EDUCATION TO STRENGTHEN FAMILIES, EXPAND ACCESS TO TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, AND REDUCE THE SUBSTANCE USE BURDEN DRIVING THE REGION’S ELEVATED OVERDOSE RATES AND CHILD-WELFARE SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS SPANS CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS (AGES 0–17), YOUNG ADULTS (AGES 18–25), AND THEIR FAMILIES, REFLECTING THE LOCAL AGE DISTRIBUTION IN WHICH RESIDENTS UNDER 18 MAKE UP ROUGHLY 20 PERCENT OF BOTH COUNTIES.  LAZARUS FIRST WILL SERVE RESIDENTS OF WILKES AND YADKIN COUNTIES, TWO NEIGHBORING, ENTIRELY RURAL COUNTIES IN NORTHWESTERN NORTH CAROLINA WITH A COMBINED POPULATION OF APPROXIMATELY 104,000. THE PROGRAM WILL ENROLL 50 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 1 (30 CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND/OR YOUNG ADULTS 0–25, AND 20 PARENTS/PRIMARY CAREGIVERS) AND 110 INDIVIDUALS ANNUALLY IN YEARS 2 THROUGH 5 (80 CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUNG ADULTS, AND 30 PARENTS/CAREGIVERS), FOR A PROJECT LIFETIME TOTAL OF 490 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS. CLINICALLY, THE POPULATION OF FOCUS PRESENTS PRIMARILY WITH OPIOID AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDERS, FREQUENTLY WITH UNTREATED CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH NEEDS, CONSISTENT WITH THE COUNTIES’ PERSISTENTLY ELEVATED OVERDOSE MORTALITY AND ALCOHOL-ATTRIBUTABLE MORTALITY. SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT IS SUBSTANTIAL: PARENTAL SUBSTANCE USE ACCOUNTS FOR 62 PERCENT OF FOSTER CARE ENTRIES IN WILKES COUNTY AND 50 PERCENT IN YADKIN COUNTY, AND PROJECT LAZARUS’ JAIL-BASED REENTRY PROGRAM HAS SERVED 155 INCARCERATED PARENTS RESPONSIBLE FOR 331 MINOR CHILDREN.  LAZARUS FIRST WILL ADDRESS THESE NEEDS THROUGH FAMILY-CENTERED PEER RECOVERY COACHING, YOUTH SERVICES ADVOCATE MENTORING USING MENTORING CENTRAL’S RESEARCH-BASED CURRICULA, THE BOTVIN LIFESKILLS PARENT PROGRAM, AND WRAPAROUND CASE MANAGEMENT. ENROLLED INDIVIDUALS ARE SCREENED USING THE TAPS AND S2BI TOOLS, REFERRED FOR A FULL SUD/COD DIAGNOSTIC ASSESSMENT, AND CONNECTED TO TREATMENT PROVIDERS OFFERING FDA-APPROVED MEDICATIONS FOR OPIOID AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDER (MOUD/MAUD), ALONG WITH NALOXONE EDUCATION AND DISTRIBUTION. THE PROJECT’S GOALS ARE TO: (1) ESTABLISH PROGRAM INFRASTRUCTURE AND BEGIN SERVICES WITHIN FOUR MONTHS OF AWARD (2) ENROLL AND RETAIN UNDUPLICATED CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, YOUNG ADULTS, AND FAMILIES IN COMPREHENSIVE TREATMENT, RECOVERY, AND WRAPAROUND SERVICES; (3) ENSURE EVERY ENROLLED INDIVIDUAL HAS AN INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT/RECOVERY PLAN AS INDICATED, INCLUDING MOUD/MAUD REFERRAL WHEN CLINICALLY INDICATED, AND NALOXONE EDUCATION; (4) AND EXPAND THE SERVICE-PARTNER NETWORK BY AT LEAST FOUR ORGANIZATIONS BY SEPTEMBER 29, 2028.   MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES ADVANCE SAMHSA’S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES BY PREVENTING SUBSTANCE MISUSE THROUGH BOTVIN-BASED FAMILY AND YOUTH EDUCATION (PREVENTION OF SUBSTANCE USE AND ADDICTION); INCREASING LINKAGE TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT THROUGH TAPS/S2BI SCREENING AND MOUD/MAUD REFERRAL (TREATMENT FOR MENTAL ILLNESS AND COMPLEX NEEDS); SUSTAINING PEER-SUPPORTED AFTERCARE TO HELP FAMILIES ACHIEVE LONG-TERM RECOVERY AND SELF-SUFFICIENCY (RECOVERY, SOBRIETY, AND SELF-SUFFICIENCY); AND CENTERING PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS IN EVERY CARE DECISION (PARENTAL RIGHTS AND FAMILY ENGAGEMENT). PROGRESS WILL BE TRACKED MONTHLY USING SMART, PROJECT LAZARUS’ HIPAA-COMPLIANT ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORD, COMPARING ENROLLMENT, SERVICE DELIVERY, AND COMPLETION RATES AGAINST THESE OBJECTIVES.

description: INDIANA ADOLESCENT AND FAMILY RECOVERY AND INTERVENTION SERVICES EXPANSION (RISE) 2.0 - INDIANA YOUTH AND FAMILY RECOVERY SERVICES EXPANSION (RISE 2.0) WILL SUSTAIN AND EXPAND COMPREHENSIVE TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES FOR INDIANA ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUD), INCLUDING THOSE WITH CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS (SUD/COD). RISE 2.0 WILL PROVIDE INTEGRATED, FAMILY-CENTERED, TRAUMA-INFORMED, EVIDENCE-BASED, AND COST-EFFECTIVE CARE THAT INCLUDES MEDICATION MANAGEMENT, CARE COORDINATION, RECOVERY SUPPORTS, AFTERCARE, CAREGIVER SERVICES, STATEWIDE TELECONSULTATION, AND WORKFORCE TRAINING.  RISE 2.0 WILL SERVE THE STATE OF INDIANA, WHICH HAS 6.97 MILLION RESIDENTS. THE PROJECT WILL ENROLL AT LEAST 25 UNDUPLICATED ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS IN YEAR 1 AND AT LEAST 80 ANNUALLY IN YEARS 2 THROUGH 5, FOR A MINIMUM OF 345 OVER 5 YEARS. THE EXPECTED DISTRIBUTION AND AGE RANGES ARE AS FOLLOWS: 65%-75% ADOLESCENTS (AGES 12-17) AND 25%–35% YOUNG ADULTS (18–25). CAREGIVERS AND FAMILY MEMBERS WILL PARTICIPATE THROUGH FAMILY-BASED TREATMENT, CRAFT GROUPS, NAVIGATION, REFERRAL SUPPORT, RECOVERY PLANNING, AND AFTERCARE.  RISE 2.0 WILL SERVE THOSE WITH CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS INCLUDING CANNABIS, ALCOHOL, NICOTINE/TOBACCO, OPIOID, AND STIMULANT USE DISORDERS; EXPOSURE TO FENTANYL-CONTAMINATED SUBSTANCES; PRESCRIPTION MEDICATION MISUSE; OVERDOSE EXPOSURE; WITHDRAWAL CONCERNS; IMPAIRED SCHOOL OR WORK FUNCTIONING; FAMILY CONFLICT; TRAUMA EXPOSURE; AND PSYCHIATRIC NEEDS, INCLUDING DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, ADHD, DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOR, AND SUICIDAL IDEATION. SERVICE NEEDS WILL INCLUDE DEVELOPMENTALLY APPROPRIATE ASSESSMENT; MOTIVATIONAL ENHANCEMENT; COGNITIVE-BEHAVIORAL AND FAMILY-BASED TREATMENT; MEDICATION EVALUATION FOR ALCOHOL, OPIOID, NICOTINE/TOBACCO, AND PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS; CARE COORDINATION; RECOVERY SUPPORT AND AFTERCARE.  RISE 2.0 WILL IMPLEMENT A COORDINATED CONTINUUM OF STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS: OUTPATIENT ENCOMPASS FOR ADOLESCENTS WITH SUD/COD AND FAMILIES; TEEN INTERVENE FOR MILDER SUBSTANCE USE CONCERNS; CRAFT GROUPS FOR CAREGIVERS; MET/CBT FOR YOUNG ADULTS; REFERRAL PATHWAYS TO ADULT ADDICTION/COD SERVICES FOR CAREGIVERS; ACCESS TO MULTIDISCIPLINARY CARE INCLUDING THERAPY, MEDICATION MANAGEMENT, AND CARE COORDINATION; RECOVERY SUPPORT AND AFTERCARE; A STATEWIDE ADOLESCENT ADDICTION TELECONSULTATION LINE; AND A MONTHLY PROJECT ECHO TRAINING SERIES ON ADOLESCENT SUD CLINICAL MANAGEMENT.  PROGRAM GOALS ARE AS FOLLOWS: 1) PROVIDE EFFECTIVE, COMPREHENSIVE TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES FOR ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS WITH SUD/COD IN INDIANA; 2) PROVIDE SERVICES TARGETING FAMILIES AND CAREGIVERS, INCLUDING CAREGIVER GROUPS, CARE COORDINATION, RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND AFTERCARE SERVICES; AND 3) INCREASE STATEWIDE CAPACITY TO IDENTIFY, TREAT, AND REFER ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS WITH SUD/COD.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES ARE TO ENROLL AT LEAST 25 INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 1 AND AT LEAST 80 ANNUALLY THEREAFTER; SCREEN 100% FOR SUBSTANCE USE, MENTAL HEALTH, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT NEEDS; PROVIDE 100% WITH INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT/RECOVERY PLANS, INCLUDING MEDICATION REVIEW; ENSURE AT LEAST 70% OF TREATMENT PARTICIPANTS COMPLETE BRIEF INTERVENTION OR AT LEAST 3 TREATMENT SESSIONS; PROVIDE AT LEAST 90% WITH AN AFTERCARE PLAN; SUPPORT ADOLESCENT IOP RECOVERY SUPPORT AND AFTERCARE; OFFER AT LEAST 4 CRAFT CAREGIVER GROUPS PER YEAR BEGINNING IN YEAR 1, SERVING AT LEAST 40 CAREGIVERS ANNUALLY; PROVIDE CARE COORDINATION/PATIENT NAVIGATION TO AT LEAST 80% OF ENROLLED FAMILIES; LAUNCH YOUNG ADULT GROUP SERVICES BY YEAR 2; OPERATE THE TELECONSULTATION LINE THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT, COMPLETING AT LEAST 75 ENCOUNTERS PER YEAR; DELIVER MONTHLY PROJECT ECHO SESSIONS, REACHING AT LEAST 250 PROFESSIONALS ANNUALLY; PROVIDE SUPERVISED TRAINING FOR AT LEAST 1 FTE CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY POSTDOC ANNUALLY, PROVIDE CLINICIAN TRAINING AND EDUCATION VIA OVERDOSE LIFELINE IN YEARS 1-3, AND USE SAMHSA-REQUIRED PERFORMANCE DATA AND LOCAL EVALUATION FINDINGS FOR CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT.

description: NORTHWEST PORTLAND AREA INDIAN HEALTH BOARD TRIBAL OPIOID RESPONSE CONSORTIUM PHASE 7 (TOR7) - ESTABLISHED IN 1972, NORTHWEST PORTLAND AREA INDIAN HEALTH BOARD (NPAIHB) IS A TRIBALLY-DESIGNATED ORGANIZATION SERVING THE 43 FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBES OF IDAHO (ID), OREGON (OR), AND WASHINGTON (WA). THE MISSION OF THE NPAIHB IS TO ASSIST NW TRIBES IN IMPROVING THE HEALTH STATUS AND QUALITY OF LIFE OF MEMBER TRIBES AND AMERICAN INDIAN/ALASKA NATIVE (AI/AN) PEOPLE IN THEIR DELIVERY OF CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE AND HOLISTIC HEALTH CARE. THE NPAIHB'S TOR7 WILL WORK WITH THREE NW TRIBES: THE CONFEDERATED TRIBES OF SILETZ INDIANS, THE PUYALLUP TRIBE OF INDIANS, AND THE SKOKOMISH INDIAN TRIBE, TO INCREASE ACCESS FOR THEIR TRIBAL MEMBERS TO CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE TREATMENT AND RECOVERY ACTIVITIES WITH THE INTENT OF REDUCING UNMET TREATMENT NEEDS AND SUBSTANCE USE-RELATED DEATHS, WITH A FOCUS ON USING CULTURAL AND COMMUNITY STRENGTHS FOR PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION.    THIS FUNDING WILL STRENGTHEN NPAIHB’S ABILITY TO PROVIDE LEADERSHIP, COORDINATION, DATA MANAGEMENT AND ANALYTIC SUPPORT, TRAINING, AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO PARTICIPATING TRIBES. OUR PROPOSED ACTIVITIES WILL STRENGTHEN OUR PARTNERSHIPS WITH NW TRIBES, THE SUBSTANCE ABUSE AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ADMINISTRATION (SAMHSA), THE INDIAN HEALTH SERVICE (IHS), AND THE STATES OF OR AND WA. THROUGH OUR PROPOSED PROJECT ACTIVITIES, WE PLAN TO REACH AT LEAST 5,105 TRIBAL MEMBERS ANNUALLY THROUGH OUTREACH, EDUCATION, SOCIAL MARKETING, AND MEDIA MESSAGES, AND PROVIDE SAMHSA UNIFIED PERFORMANCE REPORTING TOOL (SUPRT) TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SERVICES TO 12 TRIBAL MEMBERS. description: TREATMENT DRUG COURT PROGRAM: HOOPA VALLEY TRIBE ADULT AND FAMILY HEALING TO WELLNESS COURT - THE HOOPA VALLEY TRIBE WILL EXPAND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT AND RECOVERY CAPACITY IN ITS OPERATIONAL ADULT TRIBAL HEALING TO WELLNESS COURT AND JOINT-JURISDICTION FAMILY WELLNESS COURT — ONE OF ONLY A SMALL NUMBER OF TRIBAL COURTS IN THE NATION THAT SHARE JURISDICTION WITH A COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT — DELIVERING SEVEN-DAY ASSESSMENT, MEDICATION ACCESS, PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT, TRAUMA CARE, FAMILY SERVICES, AND CULTURALLY GROUNDED HEALING TO A REMOTE NORTHERN CALIFORNIA TRIBAL COMMUNITY WHOSE OPIOID-OVERDOSE DEATH RATE HAS RUN MANY TIMES THE STATE AVERAGE. PROJECT NAME: NA:TINI-X' WE' HEALING TO WELLNESS COURT EXPANSION. GEOGRAPHIC AREA: THE HOOPA VALLEY RESERVATION (THE LARGEST IN CALIFORNIA, ~141 SQ. MI.) AND THE KLAMATH-TRINITY REGION OF HUMBOLDT AND DEL NORTE COUNTIES, WHERE 100% OF RESIDENTS LIVE IN A FEDERALLY DESIGNATED HEALTH PROFESSIONAL SHORTAGE AREA. POPULATION: 3,649 ENROLLED HOOPA VALLEY TRIBE MEMBERS; COUNTY AI/AN POPULATION 11,576. NUMBER SERVED: NO FEWER THAN 45 UNDUPLICATED DIRECT CLIENTS PER YEAR — 225 OVER FIVE YEARS — ACROSS AN ADULT DOCKET (JUSTICE-INVOLVED ADULTS 18+) AND A FAMILY DOCKET (PARENTS OF CHILDREN AGE FIVE AND YOUNGER IN OR AT RISK OF DEPENDENCY, SERVED TWO-GENERATIONALLY), WITH ADDITIONAL FAMILY AND HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS REACHED THROUGH ENGAGEMENT, NALOXONE TRAINING, AND RECOVERY SUPPORTS. AGE RANGE: ADULTS 18 AND OLDER, WITH FAMILY-DOCKET CHILDREN REACHED THROUGH THEIR PARENTS. CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS: OPIOID, METHAMPHETAMINE, AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDERS; HIGH RATES OF CO-OCCURRING DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, AND PTSD; AND HISTORICAL AND INTERGENERATIONAL TRAUMA. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS: MEDICATION FOR OPIOID AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDER THROUGH K'IMA:W MEDICAL CENTER; MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING, THE MATRIX MODEL AND COGNITIVE-BEHAVIORAL RELAPSE PREVENTION, CONTINGENCY MANAGEMENT, SEEKING SAFETY, AND TRAUMA-FOCUSED CBT; CONTRACTED CULTURAL RECOVERY-SUPPORT AND RECONNECTION WORKSHOPS; TWO-GENERATION FAMILY WELLNESS AND YOUTH RECONNECTION SERVICES; TELEHEALTH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT; AND RECOVERY/TRANSITION SUPPORT RESOURCES — ORGANIZED WITHIN THE TRIBAL HEALING TO WELLNESS COURT TEN KEY COMPONENTS AND THE ALL RISE ADULT TREATMENT COURT BEST PRACTICE STANDARDS, AND GROUNDED IN THE EVIDENCE THAT CULTURAL CONNECTEDNESS IS A SOCIAL DETERMINANT OF HEALTH. GOALS: (1) EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED SUD TREATMENT; (2) PREVENT OVERDOSE AND OVERDOSE DEATH; (3) REDUCE RECIDIVISM AND PROMOTE RECOVERY, SOBRIETY, AND SELF-SUFFICIENCY; AND (4) STRENGTHEN FAMILIES AND ACHIEVE SAFE, TIMELY REUNIFICATION. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: ASAM-BASED ASSESSMENT WITHIN 7 BUSINESS DAYS FOR 90% OF CLIENTS; MEDICATION OFFERED AND REFERRED WITHIN 72 HOURS FOR 85% OF CLINICALLY INDICATED CLIENTS; NALOXONE AND OVERDOSE-PREVENTION TRAINING OFFERED TO 100% OF CLIENTS AND HOUSEHOLDS; SIX-MONTH RETENTION OF AT LEAST 75%; NO NEW ARREST DURING ENROLLMENT FOR THE MAJORITY OF CLIENTS, VERIFIED BY COURT AND PROBATION RECORDS; GAINS IN EMPLOYMENT, EDUCATION, OR TRAINING FROM INTAKE TO DISCHARGE; AND REUNIFICATION OR ANOTHER SAFE, PERMANENT PLACEMENT FOR THE MAJORITY OF FAMILY-DOCKET CASES WITHIN 12 MONTHS. THE TRIBE REQUESTS UP TO $400,000 PER YEAR FOR FIVE YEARS (UP TO $2,000,000 TOTAL).

description: HATTIESBURG MUNICIPAL COURT - HATTIESBURG BEHAVIORAL HEALTH COURT TREATMENT EXPANSION - HATTIESBURG BEHAVIORAL HEALTH COURT WILL CONTRACT WITH PINE BELT MENTAL HEALTHCARE RESOURCES TO ASSESS POTENTIAL ELIGIBLE MISDEMEANOR OFFENDERS. AN INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT PLAN WILL BE DEVELOPED BASED ON THE RESULTS OF CLINICAL AND RISK ASSESSMENTS. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE TESTED FOR SUBSTANCE USE REGULARLY AT COURT APPEARANCES AND RANDOMLY THROUGHOUT THE PROGRAM. THEY WILL BE REFERRED TO IN PATIENT TREATMENT AS NEEDED, WITH AN ULTIMATE GOAL OF DECREASING SUBSTANCE USE IN THE GREATER HATTIESBURG AREA.  THE TARGET POPULATION WILL BE MISDEMEANANTS WHO HAVE A MENTAL HEALTH DIAGNOSIS AND/OR A SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (CODS). BASED ON HISTORICAL DATA, OUR POPULATION WILL BE A MIXTURE OF GENDERS (60% MALE, 40% FEMALE); AGES (AVERAGE AGE RANGE OF 22-45); PRIMARILY AFRICAN AMERICAN (60%); LOW SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS (75% UNEMPLOYED; 50% HOMELESS); AND 80% OF WHOM DID NOT COMPLETE HIGH SCHOOL. THE CITY OF HATTIESBURG HAS AN OVERALL POPULATION OF APPROXIMATELY 48,800.  THE TREATMENT TEAM WILL INCLUDE THE JUDGE, PROJECT DIRECTOR, PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SPECIALIST (PRSS), CLINICIAN, RECOVERY SUPPORT SPECIALIST (RSS), PSYCHIATRIST, AND EVALUATOR. AT TIMES, THE CITY OF HATTIESBURG’S HOMELESS COORDINATOR AND A REPRESENTATIVE OF HATTIESBURG CODE ENFORCEMENT WILL BE ADDED TO THE TEAM. THE PROPOSED EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT PRACTICES INCLUDE INTEGRATED DUAL DISORDER TREATMENT (IDDT), COGNITIVE- BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (CBT), DIALECTICAL BEHAVIOR THERAPY (DBT), SEEKING SAFETY, MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING (MI), AND MEDICATION-ASSISTED TREATMENT (MAT). GROUP AND INDIVIDUAL SESSIONS WITHIN EACH TREATMENT MODALITY WILL ADDRESS FIVE CATEGORIES OF STRATEGIES: (I.E. ASSESSMENT, INSIGHT, COPING SKILLS, COGNITIVE STRATEGIES, AND LIFESTYLE MODIFICATION) USING A VARIETY OF TECHNIQUES, INCLUDING TALK THERAPY, STRUCTURED WRITING, GUIDED IMAGERY, ROLE PLAY, SKILLS BUILDING, PROBLEM SOLVING, RELAPSE REHEARSAL, AND SAFETY PLANNING. INDIVIDUALIZED RECOVERY SUPPORT PLANS WILL BE DEVELOPED COLLABORATIVELY TO ADDRESS PARTICIPANTS’ BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL NEEDS. EXAMPLES OF SUPPORTS INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO, 12-STEP SELF-HELP GROUPS, HOUSING ASSISTANCE, SUPPORTED EMPLOYMENT, HEALTH CARE, ENTITLEMENT BENEFITS, AND TRANSPORTATION. THE TREATMENT TEAM WILL HOLD MEETINGS TO REVIEW PROGRESS, AND TREATMENT PLANS WILL BE REVISED AS NEEDED. THE PROJECT GOAL IS TO DECREASE SUBSTANCE USE OF A MINIMUM OF 200 HBHC PARTICIPANTS WITH CODS. THE OBJECTIVES ARE: 1) A MINIMUM OF 40 INDIVIDUALS PER YEAR WILL BE SCREENED AND ASSESSED TO HAVE A COD; 2) BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, A MINIMUM OF 5 COURT PARTICIPANTS WITH AN OPIATE AND/OR ALCOHOL USE DISORDER WILL HAVE BEEN ENROLLED IN MAT; 3) BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, A MINIMUM OF 20 COURT PARTICIPANTS WITH COD WILL HAVE PARTICIPATED IN INTEGRATED RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT; 4) BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, A MINIMUM OF 200 COURT PARTICIPANTS WILL HAVE ACCESSED INTEGRATED TREATMENT FOR THEIR CODS; AND 5) 100% OF COURT PARTICIPANTS’ RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES WILL BE GUIDED BY AN INDIVIDUALIZED SERVICE PLAN (ISP) THAT IDENTIFIES WRAPAROUND SUPPORTS.
