description: SOUTHEAST ALASKA TRIBAL PREVENTION & COMMUNITY RESILIENCE INITIATIVEEDUCATING COMMUNITIES. EMPOWERING FIRST RESPONDERS. SAVING LIVES. - THE CENTRAL COUNCIL OF TLINGIT & HAIDA INDIAN TRIBES OF ALASKA (TLINGIT AND HAIDA), THE FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBAL GOVERNMENT REPRESENTING MORE THAN 38,000 CITIZENS ACROSS 19 SOUTHEAST ALASKA COMMUNITY COUNCIL CHAPTERS, REQUESTS $3,750,000 OVER A FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD (SEPTEMBER 30, 2026 – SEPTEMBER 29, 2031) UNDER SAMHSA'S TRIBAL OPIOID RESPONSE (TOR) PROGRAM. THE PROJECT WILL EXPAND NALOXONE ACCESS, OVERDOSE-RECOGNITION TRAINING, AND CULTURALLY GROUNDED PREVENTION EDUCATION ACROSS NINE SOUTHEAST ALASKA HUB COMMUNITIES — JUNEAU, ANGOON, KAKE, KLUKWAN, SAXMAN, THORNE BAY, HYDABURG, KLAWOCK, AND KASAAN — TO REDUCE OPIOID- AND STIMULANT-RELATED OVERDOSE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY AMONG TRIBAL CITIZENS AND COMMUNITY RESIDENTS.   SERVICES WILL REACH INDIVIDUALS AT RISK FOR OPIOID OR STIMULANT MISUSE AND OVERDOSE, THEIR FAMILIES, YOUTH (AGES 10–24), PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS, ELDERS, SCHOOL PERSONNEL, AND TRIBAL CITIZENS ACROSS THE NINE-COMMUNITY CATCHMENT AREA, ACCESSIBLE ONLY BY AIR OR SEA ACROSS THE ALEXANDER ARCHIPELAGO. THE POPULATION SPANS BOTH SEXES AND THE FULL ADULT AND YOUTH AGE RANGE AND REFLECTS THE SOCIOECONOMIC CONDITIONS COMMON TO RURAL SOUTHEAST ALASKA, INCLUDING SEASONAL-ECONOMY EMPLOYMENT, HIGH COST OF LIVING, AND GEOGRAPHIC ISOLATION. CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS OF CONCERN INCLUDE OPIOID AND STIMULANT MISUSE, CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, AND HISTORICAL AND INTERGENERATIONAL TRAUMA; SOME INDIVIDUALS SERVED HAVE SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT THROUGH CRIMINAL JUSTICE, SOCIAL SERVICES, OR CHILD WELFARE SYSTEMS. OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE PREVENTION SERVICES TO AN ESTIMATED 5,000 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS AND OPIOID OVERDOSE/INFECTIOUS DISEASE PREVENTION SERVICES TO AN ESTIMATED 6,000 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS; IT DOES NOT DELIVER DIRECT TREATMENT OR CLINICAL RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES, AND INDIVIDUALS NEEDING THOSE SERVICES ARE CONNECTED THROUGH REFERRAL AND WARM HAND-OFF AGREEMENTS WITH REGIONAL PARTNERS.   TO REDUCE OVERDOSE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY AND STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY PROTECTIVE FACTORS, TLINGIT AND HAIDA WILL IMPLEMENT THREE INTEGRATED COMPONENTS: COMMUNITY EDUCATION, DELIVERING SEMI-ANNUAL COMMUNITY FORUMS, ANNUAL HEALTH FAIRS, MONTHLY VILLAGE OUTREACH THROUGH LOCAL COMMUNITY NAVIGATORS, AND A CULTURALLY TAILORED PSA/SOCIAL-MEDIA CAMPAIGN PRODUCED IN TLINGIT, HAIDA, AND ENGLISH; OVERDOSE PREVENTION, DELIVERING SEMI-ANNUAL, IN-PERSON OVERDOSE-RECOGNITION TRAINING FOR COMMUNITY MEMBERS AND TRIBAL CITIZENS, WITH FENTANYL AND STIMULANT CO-USE AWARENESS EMBEDDED THROUGHOUT; AND NALOXONE ACCESS, DISTRIBUTING NALOXONE KITS AND ESTABLISHING FIXED DISTRIBUTION SITES AND VENDING MACHINES/EMERGENCY CABINETS IN ALL NINE COMMUNITIES BY YEAR 3. PROGRAMMING DRAWS ON FOUR EVIDENCE-BASED/EVIDENCE-INFORMED PRACTICES — GONA/GOAN, BOTVIN LIFESKILLS, OVERDOSE EDUCATION AND NALOXONE DISTRIBUTION (OEND), AND THE TRIBAL PRACTICES FOR WELLNESS IN INDIAN COUNTRY (TPWIC) CULTURAL FRAMEWORK — DELIVERED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH EIGHT REGIONAL ORGANIZATIONS, INCLUDING THE SOUTHEAST ALASKA REGIONAL HEALTH CONSORTIUM, BARTLETT REGIONAL HOSPITAL, JAMHI HEALTH & WELLNESS, AND THE JUNEAU SCHOOL DISTRICT.   BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, TLINGIT AND HAIDA WILL HAVE ESTABLISHED NALOXONE DISTRIBUTION CAPACITY IN ALL NINE COMMUNITIES (BY YEAR 5), DISTRIBUTED 5,000 NALOXONE KITS, TRAINED 250 TRIBAL CITIZENS, COMMUNITY MEMBERS, AND SCHOOL/HUMAN-SERVICE PERSONNEL IN OVERDOSE RECOGNITION AND NALOXONE ADMINISTRATION, DELIVERED AT LEAST 160 PREVENTION/TRAINING EVENTS (32 PER YEAR), AND DOCUMENTED A MEASURABLE INCREASE IN REPORTED OVERDOSE REVERSALS BY YEAR 3. PROGRESS WILL BE TRACKED THROUGH SAMHSA'S PERFORMANCE ACCOUNTABILITY AND REPORTING SYSTEM (SPARS) VIA THE QUARTERLY SOR/TOR PROGRAM INSTRUMENT.

description: MENTAL HEALTH SERVICE AND FAMILY SUPPORT EXPANSION PROJECT IN BENTON COUNTY ARKANSAS - THE BENTON COUNTY MENTAL HEALTH COURT (BCMHC) WILL IMPLEMENT THE MENTAL HEALTH SERVICE AND FAMILY SUPPORT EXPANSION PROJECT IN BENTON COUNTY, AR, COLLABORATING WITH EIGHT PROVIDERS STATEWIDE TO INCREASE ACCESS TO ACUTE CARE SERVICES FOR THE CO-OCCURRING CLIENTS MOST IN NEED OF INTENSIVE SUPPORT. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE THE ENTIRE GEOGRAPHIC AREA OF BENTON COUNTY, WHICH HAS A POPULATION OF 343,107. OVER THE FIVE-YEAR FUNDING PERIOD, BCMHC ANTICIPATES SERVING 45 CLIENTS PER YEAR FOR A TOTAL OF 225 UNDUPLICATED CLIENTS. OF THESE, THE PROGRAM EXPECTS TO PROVIDE RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT TO 60 CLIENTS, INTENSIVE OUTPATIENT SERVICES TO 20 CLIENTS, AND EXPANDED PSYCHOLOGICAL TESTING TO 25 CLIENTS. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS FOR BCMHC IS MALE AND FEMALE ADULTS AGED 18 AND OLDER WHO HAVE CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS (COD), ARE INVOLVED IN THE CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM, AND HAVE A SIGNIFICANT NEED FOR ENHANCED SERVICES; THOSE WITH HIGH RISK/HIGH NEED, WHO, WITHOUT INTERVENTION, ARE MOST AT RISK FOR RELAPSE AND RE-OFFENSE. PARTICIPANTS WILL PRESENT WITH CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT DISTURBANCES IN COGNITION, EMOTIONAL REGULATION, OR BEHAVIOR, ALONG WITH A SEVERE AND PERSISTENT MENTAL HEALTH DIAGNOSIS. MOST WILL BE LOW-INCOME AND EITHER UNINSURED OR MEDICAID-ELIGIBLE, UNEMPLOYED OR UNDEREMPLOYED, AND FACING BARRIERS SUCH AS HOUSING INSTABILITY AND LIMITED TRANSPORTATION. THE PROGRAM WILL PRIORITIZE THOSE IN THE HIGH RISK/HIGH NEED CATEGORY-THE PARTICIPANTS LEAST LIKELY TO SUCCEED WITH TRADITIONAL TREATMENT APPROACHES BECAUSE OF THEIR GREATER PERSONAL VULNERABILITIES; PROBLEM SEVERITY, COMPLEXITY, AND CHRONICITY; AND FEWEST NATURAL SUPPORTS. GIVEN THE CHARACTERISTICS OF THE CO-OCCURRING POPULATION BEING TARGETED, THIS GROUP IS EXPECTED TO INCLUDE INDIVIDUALS WITH TRAUMA HISTORIES, REPEAT OFFENDERS (LEGAL COMPLICATIONS), AND THOSE WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS (HIGH PROBLEM COMPLEXITY). THIS SERVICE ENHANCEMENT PROJECT IS DESIGNED PRIMARILY TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY, QUANTITY, AND INTENSITY OF TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES AVAILABLE TO BCMHC CLIENTS WITH THE MOST COMPLEX NEEDS. BY ENABLING THE PROGRAM TO DELIVER SERVICES AT THE LEVEL REQUIRED, THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE OUTCOMES FOR THOSE WITH THE MOST SEVERE AND COMPLEX CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS. THIS WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH ADDED RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT, EXPANDED INTENSIVE OUTPATIENT SERVICES, TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE, INCREASED MENTAL HEALTH ASSESSMENT AND SERVICES, PEER SUPPORT SERVICES, STI EDUCATION AND TESTING, OVERDOSE PREVENTION, AND FAMILY SUPPORT AND EDUCATION. CLINICAL AND RECOVERY SERVICES WILL DRAW ON MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING, MRT, SEEKING SAFETY, LIVING IN BALANCE, HAZELDEN LIVING SKILLS, WELLNESS SELF-MANAGEMENT, MAT, AND TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE. PROJECT GOALS INCLUDE: 1) INCREASE ACCESS TO EVIDENCE BASED TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH CO OCCURRING DISORDERS, OBJECTIVES: 50% INCREASE IN ADMISSIONS, REGULAR DRUG TESTING, EXPAND TREATMENT ACCESS, PROVIDE OORM TRAINING, IMPLEMENT TRAUMA INFORMED CARE. 2) REDUCE RECIDIVISM AND IMPROVE MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT COURT COMPLETION RATES, OBJECTIVES INCREASE COMPLETION RATES AND REDUCE RECIDIVISM, 3) IMPLEMENT INFECTIOUS DISEASE SCREENING, PROVIDE MONTHLY TESTING AND EDUCATION, 4) INTEGRATE PARENTING EDUCATION, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, AND FAMILY-CENTERED CARE, OBJECTIVE: DELIVER PARENTING PSYCHOEDUCATION, TRAIN STAFF; 5) ENSURE COMPREHENSIVE ACCESS TO BCMHC SERVICES FOR ALL ELIGIBLE INDIVIDUALS, IMPROVE SCREENING, COLLECT DATA FOR ADMISSIONS AND REJECTIONS; 6) STRENGTHEN EVALUATION AND DATA CAPACITY TO SUPPORT CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT AND LONG TERM SUSTAINABILITY, OBJECTIVES: IMPLEMENT DATA COLLECTION, CONDUCT SELF-ASSESSMENT, CONDUCT RECIDIVISM STUDY; 7) TRAINING FOR MENTAL HEALTH COURT TEAM, OBJECTIVES: ATTEND STATE AND NATIONAL TRAINING.  THE PROJECT WILL BE CLOSELY INTEGRATED WITH BROADER STATE-LEVEL SYSTEMS OF CARE TO ENSURE SUSTAINABILITY FOR THE SYSTEM. PLANS FOR QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, REPLICATION AND SUSTAINABILITY WI

description: HEALING PATHWAYS FOR STRONG COMMUNITIES - HEALING PATHWAYS FOR STRONG COMMUNITIES (HPSC) IS A STATEWIDE PREVENTION INITIATIVE LED BY THE ALASKA NATIVE TRIBAL HEALTH CONSORTIUM (ANTHC) TO REDUCE OPIOID MISUSE AND STRENGTHEN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH THROUGH CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE, COMMUNITY-DRIVEN STRATEGIES. THIS PROJECT EXPANDS ACCESS TO PREVENTION EDUCATION, WORKFORCE TRAINING, AND FAMILY-CENTERED SUPPORTS, WITH A FOCUS ON ALASKA NATIVE COMMUNITIES ACROSS URBAN, RURAL, AND REMOTE REGIONS.   HPSC SERVES COMMUNITIES ACROSS ALASKA, REACHING 670 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS ANNUALLY AND 3,350 INDIVIDUALS OVER FIVE YEARS UNDER THE PREVENTION SERVICES CATEGORY. THIS PROGRAM SUPPORTS INDIVIDUALS ACROSS THE LIFESPAN, INCLUDING YOUTH, ADULTS, ELDERS, AND FAMILIES, WITH AN EMPHASIS ON YOUTH AND FAMILY SYSTEMS.   PARTICIPANTS INCLUDE INDIVIDUALS AT RISK FOR OR EXPERIENCING SUBSTANCE MISUSE, OPIOID USE DISORDER (OUD), TRAUMA, ADVERSE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES (ACES), AND CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, AS WELL AS FAMILIES AND CAREGIVERS SEEKING PREVENTION AND SUPPORT RESOURCES.   KEY STRATEGIES INCLUDE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE TRAINING, CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE EDUCATIONAL MATERIAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNITY OUTREACH, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT PROGRAMMING, AS WELL AS LAND-BASED AND CULTURAL ACTIVITIES. THIS PROGRAM ALSO EXPANDS NALOXONE ACCESS, REDUCES STIGMA, AND SUPPORTS THE DEVELOPMENT OF A STATEWIDE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH RESOURCE DIRECTORY. ALL HPSC ACTIVITIES INTEGRATE ALASKA NATIVE KNOWLEDGE AND VALUES THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH ELDERS AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS.   PROJECT GOALS ARE TO INCREASE WORKFORCE CAPACITY, IMPROVE ACCESS TO PREVENTION AND RECOVERY SUPPORTS, STRENGTHEN FAMILY SYSTEMS, EXPAND CULTURAL ENGAGEMENT, AND REDUCE OPIOID MISUSE AND RELATED HARMS.   MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE DELIVERING 30 TRAINING COURSES ANNUALLY, REACHING 500 WORKFORCE PARTICIPANTS, AND ENGAGING 170 INDIVIDUALS ANNUALLY THROUGH OUTREACH, EDUCATION, AND PARTICIPATION IN FAMILY AND CULTURAL PROGRAMMING.   HEALING PATHWAYS FOR STRONG COMMUNITIES (HPSC) ALIGNS WITH SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES BY ADVANCING PREVENTION, IMPROVING ACCESS TO CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE CARE, STRENGTHENING PROTECTIVE FACTORS, AND ADDRESSING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISPARITIES IN ALASKA NATIVE COMMUNITIES.

description: GASTON COUNTY VETERAN AND ADULT TREATMENT COURTS EXPANSION GRANT - GASTON TREATMENT COURT SYSTEM (GTCS) WILL SUPPORT TWO ESTABLISHED TREATMENT COURTS WITH A SINGLE APPLICATION IN THE SAME JUDICIAL DISTRICT, THE GASTON ADULT TREATMENT COURT (ATC) AND THE GASTON VETERANS TREATMENT COURT (VTC, NORTH CAROLINA, BY SERVING 270 INDIVIDUALS WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUD) AND CO-OCCURRING CONDITIONS (COC), AN AVERAGE OF 54 PER YEAR. ABOUT 25% OF THE ATC CLIENTS AND 30% VTC ARE FELONY INVOLVED/HIGH RISK. TWO POPULATIONS OF FOCUS ARE THOSE WITH MH/SUD WITHOUT MILITARY EXPERIENCE (ATC) AND WITH MILITARY EXPERIENCE (VTC). VETERANS WILL REQUIRE ADDITIONAL SUPPORT FOR TRAUMA AS COUNTY DATA FINDS THAT LESS THAN 12% OF CJ/SUD/COC CLIENTS WITH A DOCUMENTED TRAUMA HISTORY RECEIVE TRAUMA FOCUSED TREATMENT. BOTH COURTS HAVE BEEN UNDERUTILIZED AND HAVE INCLUDED LIMITED OR NO FIDELITY/EVALUATION COMPONENT THAT WILL ELEVATE IMPACT AND PROVIDE DATA FOR SUSTAINABILITY POST GRANT. WE WILL INCREASE EFFICIENCY, PROVIDE ADDITIONAL CASE MANAGEMENT (CM) AND PEER SUPPORT SPECIALIST (PSS) STAFF, AND HIRE A MENTOR COORDINATOR (MC). WE FOCUS ON DIRECT SERVICES TO CLIENTS WHILE ALSO (1) ENSURING FIDELITY TO THE ADULT TREATMENT COURT BEST PRACTICE STANDARDS (BPS), (2) REDUCING RECIDIVISM OF PERSONS WITH CJ/SUD/COC BY ASSESSING FOR MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS AND TRAUMA HISTORY DURING A COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT AND PROVIDING APPROPRIATE EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES/TREATMENTS (EBP), (3) ENSURE THAT ALL CLIENTS HAVE ACCESS TO COMMUNITY RECOVERY-BASED SERVICES; AND, (5) ADDRESS THE STIGMA PREVALENT IN THE COMMUNITY THAT RESTRICTS RECOVERY OPTIONS FOR CLIENTS THAT INTERFERES WITH TREATMENT, RECOVERY AND RECIDIVISM SUCCESS. OTHER EBPS SPECIFIC TO TREATMENT GAPS THAT THE TEAM WILL IMPLEMENT INCLUDE MENTORING SUPPORT, WELLNESS RECOVERY AND ACTION PLANNING (WRAP), MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING, COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY FOR SUD AND FOR TRAUMA, MEDICATION ASSISTED TREATMENT, INTENSIVE OUTPATIENT TREATMENT, 12-STEP FACILITATION, LIVING IN BALANCE, AND EYE MOVEMENT DESENSITIZATION AND REPROCESSING. WITH THIS APPROACH WE WILL TARGET FIVE GOALS WITH 23 LINKED OBJECTIVES. EACH GOAL WAS DEVELOPED TO ADDRESS THE FIVE OVERARCHING NEEDS THAT EMERGED DURING PREPARATION FOR SUBMISSION. GOAL 1: INCREASE THE NUMBER OF ELIGIBLE INDIVIDUALS SERVED BY THE ATC AND VTC AND ESTABLISH A UNIFIED EVALUATION AND FIDELITY-MONITORING INFRASTRUCTURE ACROSS THE NEWLY INTEGRATED GTCS. GOAL 2: IMPLEMENT INTEGRATED, TRAUMA-INFORMED ASSESSMENT PRACTICES ACROSS THE GTCS THAT EXPAND FAMILY INVOLVEMENT AND ADDRESS THE HIGH RATE OF TRAUMA, PTSD, AND DOMESTIC-VIOLENCE-RELATED NEEDS AMONG PARTICIPANTS. GOAL 3: STRENGTHEN THE OPERATIONAL INFRASTRUCTURE OF THE GTCS BY EXPANDING FIDELITY MONITORING, INCREASING DRUG-TESTING CAPACITY, ESTABLISHING A DEDICATED MENTORING COORDINATOR (MC) FOR THE VTC, AND FORMALIZING INTEGRATION WITH THE LOCAL VA SYSTEM. GOAL 4: EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED, TRAUMA-SPECIFIC AND MAT SERVICES, INCLUDING MOUD/MAUD AND FAMILY/PARENTING-FOCUSED INTERVENTIONS, TAILORED TO THE NEEDS OF ATC AND VTC PARTICIPANTS. GOAL 5: EXPAND LONG-TERM RECOVERY SUPPORT INFRASTRUCTURE FOR GTCS PARTICIPANTS, INCLUDING ADDITIONAL CASE MANAGEMENT CAPACITY, CERTIFIED PEER SUPPORT SERVICES, AND ACCESS TO RECOVERY/SOBER LIVING HOUSING. FIDELITY IS CRITICAL FOR THE PROPOSED IMPLEMENTATION AND THE TREATMENT MODEL OFFERED BY PROVIDERS COMMITTING TO THE PROJECT. description: THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ACCESS AND RECOVERY OF KANSAS INITIATIVE - PROJECT TITLE: BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ACCESS AND RECOVERY FOR KANSAS (BHARK) THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ACCESS AND RECOVERY FOR KANSAS (BHARK) INITIATIVE WILL TEST A COURT-FACILITATED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ACCESS MODEL DESIGNED TO REDUCE DELAYS BETWEEN JUDICIAL REFERRAL AND PARTICIPANT ENGAGEMENT IN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES. THROUGH SECURE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ACCESS POINTS (BHAPS) LOCATED IN COURTHOUSES AND OTHER APPROVED COURT-CONNECTED SITES, ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS WILL BE IMMEDIATELY CONNECTED WITH CLINICIANS FROM REGIONAL CERTIFIED COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINICS (CCBHCS) FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, CRISIS INTERVENTION, AND CONNECTION TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT. RATHER THAN RELYING ON PARTICIPANTS TO INDEPENDENTLY NAVIGATE THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEM AFTER A COURT ORDER, BHARK ENABLES THE COURT TO ACTIVELY FACILITATE TIMELY ENTRY INTO CARE. BY REPLACING PASSIVE REFERRALS WITH ACTIVE COURT FACILITATION, BHARK SEEKS TO IMPROVE TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT, STRENGTHEN RECOVERY OUTCOMES, AND ESTABLISH A PRACTICAL MODEL FOR EXPANDING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ACCESS IN RURAL KANSAS. THE KANSAS JUDICIAL BRANCH, OFFICE OF JUDICIAL ADMINISTRATION, WILL ADMINISTER THIS FIVE-YEAR PROOF-OF-CONCEPT DEMONSTRATION IN PARTNERSHIP WITH PARTICIPATING TREATMENT COURTS AND REGIONAL CCBHCS. THE PROJECT WILL TARGET SIX RURAL JUDICIAL DISTRICTS SELECTED TO REPRESENT DIVERSE GEOGRAPHIC REGIONS, TREATMENT COURT STRUCTURES, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICE ENVIRONMENTS. PREFERRED IMPLEMENTATION JURISDICTIONS INCLUDE THE 8TH, 9TH, 19TH, 21ST, 23RD, AND 30TH JUDICIAL DISTRICTS, SERVING DICKINSON, GEARY, HARVEY, MCPHERSON, COWLEY, RILEY, ELLIS, AND SUMNER COUNTIES. THE PROPOSED SERVICE AREA INCLUDES APPROXIMATELY 276,000 RESIDENTS. BHARK WILL SERVE AN AVERAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 200 UNDUPLICATED PARTICIPANTS ANNUALLY AND AN ESTIMATED 1,000 UNDUPLICATED PARTICIPANTS OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD. THE TARGET POPULATION INCLUDES ADULTS AGE 18 AND OLDER PARTICIPATING IN ADULT DRUG TREATMENT COURTS AND FAMILY TREATMENT COURTS WHO HAVE DIAGNOSED SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, MANY WITH CO-OCCURRING MENTAL ILLNESS AND OTHER COMPLEX BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS. PARTICIPANTS FREQUENTLY EXPERIENCE DELAYS AFTER JUDICIAL REFERRAL BECAUSE OF TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, PROVIDER SHORTAGES, AND DIFFICULTY NAVIGATING THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEM. BHARK ADDRESSES THESE BARRIERS BY PROVIDING IMMEDIATE SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, CRISIS RESPONSE, CARE NAVIGATION, AND FACILITATED CONNECTION TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT THROUGH REGIONAL CCBHCS. WHEN CLINICALLY APPROPRIATE, BHAPS MAY ALSO SUPPORT INDIVIDUAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES DELIVERED THROUGH TELEHEALTH, INCLUDING INTAKE, MEDICATION MANAGEMENT, PSYCHIATRIC CONSULTATION, COUNSELING, PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND FOLLOW-UP CARE. THESE SERVICES WILL HELP PARTICIPANTS MAINTAIN ENGAGEMENT WHILE TRANSITIONING TO OR CONTINUING TREATMENT THROUGH THEIR REGIONAL CCBHC. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) REDUCE THE TIME BETWEEN JUDICIAL REFERRAL, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ASSESSMENT, AND TREATMENT INITIATION; (2) INCREASE COMPLETION OF COURT-ORDERED EVALUATIONS AND PARTICIPANT ENGAGEMENT IN EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORTS; AND (3) ESTABLISH PROOF OF CONCEPT FOR A COURT-FACILITATED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ACCESS MODEL THAT IS OPERATIONALLY FEASIBLE, CLINICALLY EFFECTIVE, AND FINANCIALLY SUSTAINABLE. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE REDUCING REFERRAL-TO-SCREENING, REFERRAL-TO-TREATMENT, AND REFERRAL-TO-ASSESSMENT INTERVALS; INCREASING EVALUATION COMPLETION, TREATMENT INITIATION, AND TREATMENT RETENTION; IMPROVING ACCESS TO CLINICALLY APPROPRIATE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES; AND EVALUATING IMPLEMENTATION AND PARTICIPANT OUTCOMES TO INFORM FUTURE KANSAS JUDICIAL BRANCH INVESTMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY.

description: RHODE ISLAND MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT COURT SUBSTANCE USE EXPANSION - THE RHODE ISLAND MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT COURT (RI MHTC) PROPOSES TO EXPAND EVIDENCE-BASED SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD) TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES FOR JUSTICE-INVOLVED ADULTS WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS (SMI) AND CO-OCCURRING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS. THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS AMONG THE STATE OF RHODE ISLAND JUDICIARY, CERTIFIED COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINICS (CCBHCS), PEER RECOVERY ORGANIZATIONS, AND COMMUNITY PROVIDERS, THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE ACCESS TO INTEGRATED BEHAVIORAL HEALTHCARE, REDUCE SUBSTANCE USE, OVERDOSE RISK, AND RECIDIVISM, AND PROMOTE LONG-TERM RECOVERY, COMMUNITY STABILITY, AND PUBLIC SAFETY. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL SERVE 12 PARTICIPANTS IN YEAR 1, INCREASING TO 20 ANNUALLY BY YEARS 4 AND 5, FOR AN ESTIMATED 81 UNDUPLICATED PARTICIPANTS OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD. GRANT-FUNDED SERVICES WILL PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT FOR SUDS, CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, TRAUMA, INFECTIOUS DISEASE RISK, OVERDOSE RISK, AND SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH; INTEGRATED TREATMENT COORDINATION BY A DEDICATED CLINICIAN; PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT; EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS INCLUDING MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING, COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY, SEEKING SAFETY, AND INTERACTIVE JOURNALING; OVERDOSE PREVENTION EDUCATION AND NALOXONE TRAINING; ACCESS TO FDA-APPROVED MEDICATIONS FOR OPIOID AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDERS (MOUD/MAUD) WHEN CLINICALLY APPROPRIATE; TRANSPORTATION ASSISTANCE; FAMILY ENGAGEMENT; AND COORDINATED REFERRALS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES. THE PROJECT ADVANCES SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES BY EXPANDING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED CARE, PROMOTING LONG-TERM RECOVERY, AND IMPROVING OUTCOMES THROUGH DATA-DRIVEN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES.

description: WASHINGTON COUNTY SPECIALTY COURT DRUG COURT ENHANCEMENT: FAMILY-CENTERED CARE INTEGRATION - PROJECT ABSTRACT WASHINGTON/MADISON COUNTY ADULT TREATMENT DRUG COURT: FAMILY-CENTERED ENHANCEMENT THE WASHINGTON/MADISON COUNTY ADULT TREATMENT DRUG COURT (WMCATDC) FAMILY-CENTERED ENHANCEMENT EXPANDS SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT, MEDICATION ACCESS, OVERDOSE PREVENTION, AND RECOVERY SUPPORT FOR JUSTICE-INVOLVED ADULTS WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUDS) ACROSS WASHINGTON AND MADISON COUNTIES IN NORTHWEST ARKANSAS, AND EMBEDS STRUCTURED FAMILY-CENTERED SERVICES FOR THE MAJORITY OF PARTICIPANTS WHO ARE PARENTS. OPERATED BY THE WASHINGTON COUNTY DRUG COURT (CONTINUOUSLY OPERATIONAL SINCE 1999) WITH INDEPENDENT EVALUATION BY THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS FOR MEDICAL SCIENCES (UAMS), THE PROJECT WILL SERVE A MINIMUM OF 100 UNDUPLICATED PARTICIPANTS PER YEAR (500 OVER FIVE YEARS), WITH SERVICE DELIVERY BEGINNING WITHIN FOUR MONTHS OF AWARD. GEOGRAPHIC AREA AND POPULATION. THE CATCHMENT IS WASHINGTON AND MADISON COUNTIES TWO ADJOINING COUNTIES ANCHORED BY FAYETTEVILLE AND EXTENDING EAST INTO THE RURAL OZARKS, WHERE MADISON COUNTY IS A FEDERALLY DESIGNATED MENTAL-HEALTH PROFESSIONAL SHORTAGE AREA WITH SPARSE BEHAVIORAL-HEALTH AND SUD CAPACITY. PARTICIPANTS ARE JUSTICE-INVOLVED ADULTS, GENERALLY AGES 18-55, WHO ARE MEDIUM-TO-HIGH RISK AND HIGH NEED. THEIR PRIMARY CONDITION IS A DIAGNOSED SUD (OPIOIDS, METHAMPHETAMINE, AND ALCOHOL PREDOMINATING), WITH HIGH RATES OF CO-OCCURRING DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, AND PTSD; MORE THAN 75% REPORT SIGNIFICANT LIFETIME TRAUMA, AND A MAJORITY ARE PARENTS OR CAREGIVERS, INCLUDING MANY FATHERS. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS. THE PROJECT DELIVERS THE EVIDENCE-BASED ADULT DRUG-COURT MODEL THROUGH A SINGLE, RECOVERY-ORIENTED SYSTEM OF CARE: VALIDATED SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT (RANT, GAIN-SS, TCU); MORAL RECONATION THERAPY AND MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING; FULL ACCESS TO FDA-APPROVED MEDICATIONS FOR OPIOID USE DISORDER (BUPRENORPHINE, NALTREXONE; METHADONE BY REFERRAL) AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDER WITH COMPREHENSIVE MEDICATION MANAGEMENT; TRAUMA-SPECIFIC TREATMENT (SEEKING SAFETY, DBT, AND REFERRAL TO PROLONGED EXPOSURE, TF-CBT, AND EMDR); UNIVERSAL TAKE-HOME NALOXONE WITH OVERDOSE-RECOGNITION TRAINING; ON-SITE INFECTIOUS-DISEASE TESTING AND LINKAGE; AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES INCLUDING RECOVERY HOUSING, PEER SUPPORT, CHILDCARE, AND TRANSPORTATION. THE FAMILY-CENTERED ENHANCEMENT PAIRS THE REACHING PARENTS AND MYTE TRAUMA-PSYCHOEDUCATION CURRICULA WITHIN THE STRENGTHENING FAMILIES PROTECTIVE FACTORS FRAMEWORK, SUPPORTED BY FAITH- AND COMMUNITY-BASED PARTNERS, A FAMILY-CENTERED PEER SPECIALIST, AND A FAMILY SOCIAL WORKER. PROJECT GOALS. (1) EXPAND TREATMENT CAPACITY ACROSS WASHINGTON AND RURAL MADISON COUNTIES; (2) DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED, TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE WITH FULL MOUD/MAUD ACCESS; (3) PREVENT OVERDOSE AND INFECTIOUS DISEASE; (4) EMBED FAMILY-CENTERED SERVICES TO STRENGTHEN PROTECTIVE FACTORS AND INTERRUPT INTERGENERATIONAL TRAUMA; AND (5) SUSTAIN QUALITY THROUGH GOLD-STANDARD DATA. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES. ≥100 UNDUPLICATED PARTICIPANTS ENROLLED ANNUALLY; 100% SCREENED WITH INDIVIDUALIZED, LEVEL-OF-CARE-MATCHED PLANS; MOUD/MAUD AVAILABLE ACROSS OUTPATIENT AND RESIDENTIAL SETTINGS FROM QUARTER 1; 100% OF PARTICIPANTS OFFERED NALOXONE AND OVERDOSE TRAINING; ≥4 RECOVERY-ORIENTED FAMILY ENGAGEMENT EVENTS PER YEAR; ≥90% OF STAFF TRAINED IN THE STRENGTHENING FAMILIES FRAMEWORK BY QUARTER 1; AND SUPRT-ADMINISTRATIVE AND SUPRT-CLIENT/CAREGIVER MEASURES REPORTED THROUGH SPARS AT EVERY REQUIRED POINT (INTAKE, 6-MONTH, 12-MONTH/ANNUAL, CLOSEOUT) WITH ≥90% REASSESSMENT AND 100% OF CLOSEOUTS ENTERED WITHIN 30 DAYS. description: HAYMARKET'S RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN (PPW-RH) - HAYMARKETS RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN (PPW-RH). HAYMARKET CENTER, CHICAGO’S LARGEST AND MOST COMPREHENSIVE SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (SUD) TREATMENT PROVIDER, PROPOSES HAYMARKET RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN (PPW-RH) TO PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE, INTEGRATED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND PRIMARY CARE SERVICES FOR 119 PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM (PPW) WOMEN AND 48 CHILDREN, WHO WILL RESIDE WITH THEIR MOTHERS IN RESIDENTIAL SUD TREATMENT, TO PROMOTE LONG-TERM RECOVERY AND SOBRIETY. THE GEOGRAPHIC CATCHMENT AREA IS COOK COUNTY, IL WITH A POPULATION OF 5,194,625 WITH A FOCUS ON COMMUNITIES WITH HIGHER PREVALENCE OF SUD. YEAR 1 YEAR 2 YEAR 3 YEAR 4 YEAR 5 TOTAL PPW 19 25 25 25 25 119 CHILDREN 8 10 10 10 10 48. TARGETS INCLUDE SERVING 19 UNDUPLICATED WOMEN IN YEAR 1, FOLLOWED BY 25 WOMEN EACH IN YEARS 2-5, WITH A CUMULATIVE TOTAL OF 119. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROJECT AIMS TO SERVE 8 CHILDREN IN YEAR 1, AND 10 CHILDREN IN EACH SUBSEQUENT YEAR, FOR A CUMULATIVE TOTAL OF 48 CHILDREN. THE ADULT PPW POPULATION OF FOCUS WILL BE 100% ADULT FEMALES WITH A MEDIAN AGE OF 35. CHILDREN WILL BE 50% MALE AND 50% FEMALE, RANGING FROM NEWBORNS TO 6 YEARS OLD. ALL ADULT INDIVIDUALS RECEIVING PPW-RH SERVICES WILL HAVE A SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER AND WILL LIKELY BE EXPERIENCING CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS OR SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESSES. 89% OF PARTICIPANTS WILL BE UNSTABLY HOUSED AT THE TIME OF ADMISSION WITH 94% UNEMPLOYED. 30% WILL HAVE CRIMINAL JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT. GOALS INCLUDE IDENTIFYING AND ENGAGING 119 WOMEN WITH SUD/COD AND THEIR CHILDREN, IMPROVING ACCESS TO EBP TO REDUCE SU/MH SYMPTOMS, PROMOTING LONG-TERM RECOVERY, AND STRENGTHENING SUSTAINED RECOVERY POST-TREATMENT. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE PROVIDING FDA-APPROVED MEDICATION TO 95% OF WOMEN WHO CHOOSE TO RECEIVE THIS TREATMENT, CONNECTING 95% OF WOMEN TO RECOVERY HOUSING AND OTHER WRAPAROUND SERVICES, PROVIDING FAMILY PRESERVATION SERVICES TO 75% OF CLIENTS, PROVIDING SUD COUNSELING AND SUPPORTS TO 75% OF ELIGIBLE FAMILY MEMBERS, CASE MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR ALL WOMEN, AND SUPPORTING SAFE FAMILY REUNIFICATION FOR 75% OF ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS.

description: EXPANDING FAMILY-CENTERED RESIDENTIAL SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN IN RURAL WESTERN MONTANA. - EXPANDING FAMILY-CENTERED RESIDENTIAL SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN IN RURAL WESTERN MONTANA.. AWARE, INC. IS ESTABLISHING A RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT PROGRAM FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER WHO MAY LIVE WITH THEIR MINOR CHILDREN AT 3335 LT MOSS RD, FORT MISSOULA, MT. THE FACILITY WILL SERVE AS THE REGIONAL HUB FOR RURAL WESTERN MONTANA AND THE FLATHEAD RESERVATION, WHERE A LACK OF RESIDENTIAL OPTIONS THAT KEEP MOTHERS AND CHILDREN TOGETHER, COMBINED WITH HALF OF MONTANA'S COUNTIES BEING MATERNITY CARE DESERTS, ALREADY DRIVES WOMEN TO MISSOULA FOR CARE; AWARE IS PLACING THE PROGRAM ALONG THIS EXISTING REFERRAL ROUTE. A 50-YEAR-OLD, CARF-ACCREDITED, MEDICAID-ENROLLED PROVIDER, AWARE OPERATES THE RECOVERY CENTER OF MISSOULA, A LICENSED ASAM 3.1 RESIDENTIAL SUD PROGRAM OFFERING MEDICATION-ASSISTED AND CO-OCCURRING CARE, ALONGSIDE STATEWIDE EARLY-CHILDHOOD AND FAMILY SERVICES. POPULATION AND NUMBERS SERVED: PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN (AGED 18-44) WITH SUD AND CO-OCCURRING DISORDERS, AND THEIR MINOR CHILDREN (BIRTH–5). AWARE WILL SERVE 8 WOMEN IN THE RESIDENTIAL PROGRAM IN YEAR 1, INCREASING TO 10 PER YEAR (48 TOTAL), AND 30 WOMEN THE FIRST YEAR, INCREASING TO 80 WOMEN IN YEARS 4 AND 5 ACROSS THE COMMUNITY-BASED CONTINUUM, APPROXIMATELY 333 UNDUPLICATED WOMEN OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT, PLUS THEIR CHILDREN. CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS: OPIOID, ALCOHOL, METHAMPHETAMINE, AND POLYSUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS WITH HIGH RATES OF CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS AND TRAUMA.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: SERVE THE UNDUPLICATED NUMBERS ABOVE EACH YEAR; ENSURE AT LEAST 60% OF WOMEN SERVED ARE DRAWN FROM RURAL/FRONTIER COUNTIES OR FLATHEAD RESERVATION COMMUNITIES; ACHIEVE REDUCED OR ABSTINENT SUBSTANCE USE FOR 60% OF ACTIVE WOMEN AT SIX-MONTH REASSESSMENT; ENGAGE 90% OF PREGNANT ENROLLEES IN PRENATAL CARE WITHIN 30 DAYS; LINK 75% OF POSTPARTUM ENROLLEES TO POSTPARTUM CARE; AND SUPPORT CUSTODY RETENTION OR REUNIFICATION FOR 90% OF MOTHERS. THIS EXPERIENCE GIVES AWARE A PROVEN, FAMILY-CENTERED RESIDENTIAL MODEL FOR IMPLEMENTING THE NEW PROGRAM EFFICIENTLY, INCLUDING MOUD/MAUD, TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE, CHILDREN'S SERVICES, RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND CASE MANAGEMENT, ALL AIMED AT INCREASING ABSTINENCE, REDUCING INFANT AND MATERNAL MORTALITY, AND PRESERVING FAMILY UNITS.

description: NORTHERN OHIO RECOVERY ASSOCIATION SERVICES PROGRAM FOR RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN (NORA-PPW-R) - NORTHERN OHIO RECOVERY ASSOCIATION SERVICES PROGRAM FOR RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN (NORA-PPW-R). WITH GRANT FUNDS, NORA WILL SERVE 60 WOMEN PER YEAR FOR A TOTAL OF 300 WOMEN OVER THE GRANT’S LIFETIME. NORA’S PROJECT WILL ALSO SERVE MINOR CHILDREN, PARTNERS, AND FAMILY MEMBERS, FOSTERING FAMILY-CENTERED RECOVERY. ABOUT 50 PERCENT OF THE WOMEN TO BE SERVED WILL HAVE LESS THAN A HIGH SCHOOL EDUCATION, MORE THAN 60 PERCENT ARE EXPECTED TO HAVE CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS, AND 70% WILL BE HOUSING AND FOOD INSECURE. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS INCLUDE LEVERING MOBILE CRISIS UNIT, MOBILE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH UNIT, AND 2-PERSON OUTREACH TEAM TO MEET WOMEN WHERE THEY ARE AND PRIORITIZE PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN WITH SUDS. EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES INCLUDE ISCREENING, BRIEF INTERVENTION AND REFERRAL TO TREATMENT (SBIRT) MODEL, MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING, MAT/MOUD, AND TREM TO ENGAGE AND RETAIN WOMEN IN TREATMENT. PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES WILL BE USED TO PROVIDE ONGOING SUPPORT, IN-HOME VISITS, AND FOLLOW-UPS FOR AT LEAST 90 DAYS POST-INITIAL ASSESSMENT. PROJECT GOALS INCLUDE: (1) IMPROVE ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT. (2) IMPROVE ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT. (3) HELPING INDIVIDUALS ACHIEVE LONG-TERM SOBRIETY. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: (1) CLIENT ENGAGEMENT: SCREEN AND ASSESS 300 UNIQUE INDIVIDUALS. (2) SUBSTANCE USE REDUCTION: 70% OF WOMEN (210) ENROLLED AT NORA WILL COMPLETE THEIR TREATMENT PROGRAM, AND 80% OF THOSE (168) WILL REPORT A SIGNIFICANT SUBSTANCE USE REDUCTION. (3) IMPROVED MENTAL HEALTH: 50% OF PROGRAM COMPLETERS (105) WILL REPORT A DECREASE IN MENTAL HEALTH SYMPTOMS. (4) IMPROVED ACCESS TO CARE: 70% OF PARTICIPANTS WILL REPORT IMPROVED ACCESS TO CARE .

description: BI-BETT RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT AT ORCHID AND WOLLAM - BI-BETT RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT AT ORCHID AND WOLLAM. SUMMARY BI-BETT REQUESTS SAMHSA FUNDING TO EXPAND RESIDENTIAL SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN AND THEIR YOUNG CHILDREN AT ORCHID WOMEN'S RECOVERY CENTER (OAKLAND) AND EAST COUNTY WOMEN'S RECOVERY CENTER/EAST COUNTY WOLLAM (PITTSBURG). GRANT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT A COMMUNITY OUTREACH COORDINATOR, A WOMEN AND CHILDREN'S COORDINATOR, A PROGRAM VEHICLE, AND STAFF TRAINING TO CONNECT ELIGIBLE WOMEN IN ALAMEDA AND CONTRA COSTA COUNTIES TO EXISTING, UNDERUSED FAMILY-CENTERED TREATMENT BEDS — ADDRESSING THE STIGMA, FEAR OF CHILD WELFARE INVOLVEMENT, AND TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS THAT KEEP WOMEN FROM ENTERING CARE.  POPULATION SIZE AND NUMBER SERVED: 160 UNDUPLICATED WOMEN IN YEAR 1 (ORCHID: 60; WOLLAM: 100), RISING TO 176 ANNUALLY IN YEARS 2–5 (ORCHID: 66; WOLLAM: 110) AS OUTREACH EXPANDS ENROLLMENT. OVER FIVE YEARS, THE PROJECT WILL SERVE 864 UNDUPLICATED PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN, STRENGTHENING RECOVERY AND FAMILY STABILITY ACROSS THE REGION.  AGE RANGE AND DISTRIBUTION: ADULT WOMEN 18 AND OLDER, PREDOMINANTLY 18–40, WHO MAY RESIDE IN TREATMENT WITH DEPENDENT CHILDREN AGES 0–5 (UP TO 4 AT ORCHID; UP TO 6 AT WOLLAM). CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS: OPIOID, STIMULANT, AND POLYSUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, FREQUENTLY WITH CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS; NAS RISK IS A PRIMARY CONCERN FOR PREGNANT CLIENTS. PROJECT GOALS: INCREASE THE NUMBER OF PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN WITH SUD IDENTIFIED, ENROLLED, AND RETAINED IN TREATMENT. REDUCE THE BARRIERS — FEAR OF CHILD WELFARE INVOLVEMENT, STIGMA, TRANSPORTATION, AND LACK OF AWARENESS — THAT PREVENT ENTRY AND RETENTION. IMPROVE TREATMENT AND FAMILY OUTCOMES FOR MOTHERS AND CHILDREN. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES (ALIGNED WITH SAMHSA'S PRIORITIES OF EXPANDING TREATMENT ACCESS AND RECOVERY SUPPORT): REACH 3,000+ INDIVIDUALS ANNUALLY THROUGH OUTREACH AND BUILD REFERRAL RELATIONSHIPS WITH AT LEAST 20 HOSPITALS, CLINICS, AND COURTS BY END OF YEAR 1. INCREASE WOMEN SERVED FROM 160 IN YEAR 1 TO 176 BY YEAR 2, SUSTAINED THROUGH YEAR 5. CONNECT AT LEAST 80% OF ENROLLED WOMEN TO BENEFITS, HOUSING, AND FAMILY REUNIFICATION SUPPORT. ACHIEVE ABSTINENCE FROM ILLICIT SUBSTANCE USE AMONG AT LEAST 70% OF CLIENTS WHO COMPLETE TREATMENT. PROJECT NAME: BI-BETT CARE FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN GEOGRAPHIC AREA SERVED: ALAMEDA AND CONTRA COSTA COUNTIES IN CALIFORNIA'S SAN FRANCISCO BAY AREA — A COMBINED CATCHMENT POPULATION OF APPROXIMATELY 2.8 MILLION. ORCHID DRAWS PRIMARILY FROM ALAMEDA COUNTY; WOLLAM ALSO DRAWS FROM MARIN, NAPA, AND SOLANO COUNTIES.

description: VOLUNTEERS OF AMERICA MID-STATES, INC.'S MANCHESTER FREEDOM HOUSE - VOLUNTEERS OF AMERICA MID-STATES, INC.S MANCHESTER FREEDOM HOUSE. description: VOLUNTEERS OF AMERICA SOUTHEAST LOUISIANA'S CANAL POINTE: FAMILY-FIRST RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN - VOLUNTEERS OF AMERICA SOUTHEAST LOUISIANA (VOASELA) WILL EXPAND COMPREHENSIVE, FAMILY-CENTERED RESIDENTIAL SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN AND THEIR CHILDREN THROUGH ITS PROGRAM AT CANAL POINTE. SERVING NEW ORLEANS AND A 16-PARISH REGION, THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT THAT ALLOWS MOTHERS AND CHILDREN TO REMAIN TOGETHER WHILE ADDRESSING SUBSTANCE USE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, MATERNAL HEALTH, PARENTING, AND LONG-TERM RECOVERY. THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE ACCESS TO LIFE-SAVING TREATMENT, STRENGTHEN FAMILIES, AND ADVANCE RECOVERY THROUGH COORDINATED CLINICAL CARE, RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND PARTNERSHIPS. VOASELA WILL SERVE PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN AGE 18 AND OLDER, WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, ALONG WITH THEIR CHILDREN AGES 0–12. THE SERVICE AREA ENCOMPASSES APPROXIMATELY 2.0 MILLION RESIDENTS ACROSS ORLEANS, JEFFERSON, PLAQUEMINES, ST. BERNARD, ST. CHARLES, ST. JOHN THE BAPTIST, ST. JAMES, ST. TAMMANY, WASHINGTON, TANGIPAHOA, LIVINGSTON, ASCENSION, ASSUMPTION, LAFOURCHE, TERREBONNE, AND ST. MARY PARISHES. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE SERVICES TO 33 UNDUPLICATED WOMEN DURING YEAR 1, 80 WOMEN ANNUALLY DURING YEARS 2–5, AND 353 UNDUPLICATED WOMEN OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, AND THEIR ELIGIBLE CHILDREN. PARTICIPANTS PRESENT WITH COMPLEX CLINICAL NEEDS, INCLUDING HIGH-ACUITY POLYSUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS INVOLVING OPIOIDS, COCAINE, ALCOHOL, AND OTHER SUBSTANCES. APPROXIMATELY 75 PERCENT ARE EXPECTED TO RECEIVE MEDICATION-ASSISTED TREATMENT (MOUD/MAUD), AND APPROXIMATELY 75 PERCENT ARE ANTICIPATED TO HAVE CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS. MANY PARTICIPANTS ALSO FACE SIGNIFICANT SOCIAL CHALLENGES, INCLUDING INVOLVEMENT WITH CHILD WELFARE OR THE JUSTICE SYSTEM, HOUSING INSTABILITY, LIMITED FINANCIAL RESOURCES, AND BARRIERS TO ACCESSING PRENATAL CARE AND LONG-TERM RECOVERY SERVICES. GRANT-FUNDED SERVICES WILL PROVIDE A COMPREHENSIVE CONTINUUM OF EVIDENCE-BASED CARE BEGINNING WITHIN FOUR MONTHS OF AWARD. WOMEN WILL RECEIVE RESIDENTIAL SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT, MEDICATION-ASSISTED TREATMENT THROUGH DEPAUL COMMUNITY HEALTH CENTERS, INDIVIDUAL, GROUP, AND FAMILY COUNSELING, TRAUMA-INFORMED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, RECOVERY SUPPORT, PEER MENTORING, COMPREHENSIVE CASE MANAGEMENT, PARENTING EDUCATION, AND COORDINATED PRENATAL AND POSTPARTUM HEALTHCARE THROUGH CRESCENTCARE. ELIGIBLE CHILDREN WILL RECEIVE DEVELOPMENTALLY APPROPRIATE TRAUMA-INFORMED SERVICES WHILE RESIDING WITH THEIR MOTHERS. EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS INCLUDE MEDICATIONS FOR OPIOID AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDERS (MOUD/MAUD), CONTINGENCY MANAGEMENT, SEEKING SAFETY, TRAUMA-FOCUSED COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY, MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING, AND THE NURTURING PARENTING PROGRAM. IMPLEMENTATION FIDELITY WILL BE SUPPORTED THROUGH VOASELA'S NIATX CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT FRAMEWORK. THE PROJECT SEEKS TO INCREASE TIMELY ACCESS TO RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT, IMPROVE TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT AND RETENTION, PROMOTE SUSTAINED RECOVERY, STRENGTHEN PARENTING CAPACITY, IMPROVE MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH OUTCOMES, AND SUPPORT SUCCESSFUL FAMILY REUNIFICATION WHEN APPROPRIATE. KEY OBJECTIVES INCLUDE INITIATING ALL REQUIRED SERVICES WITHIN FOUR MONTHS OF AWARD, ENSURING COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT AND INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT PLANNING FOR ALL PARTICIPANTS REMAINING IN TREATMENT LONGER THAN 72 HOURS, EXPANDING ACCESS TO PRENATAL AND POSTPARTUM HEALTHCARE, IMPLEMENTING EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES WITH FIDELITY, AND REPORTING 100 PERCENT OF REQUIRED PERFORMANCE MEASURES THROUGH SAMHSA'S PERFORMANCE ACCOUNTABILITY AND REPORTING SYSTEM (SPARS). THROUGH INTEGRATED CLINICAL CARE, COORDINATED COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, VOASELA WILL ADVANCE SAMHSA'S PRIORITIES OF RECOVERY, EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE, FAMILY-CENTERED CARE, AND DATA-DRIVEN ACCOUNTABILITY WHILE IMPROVING OUTCOMES FOR WOMEN, CHILDREN, AND FAMILIES ACROSS SOUTHEAST LOUISIANA.

description: FAMILY WORKS RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT & POSTPARTUM WOMEN - FAMILY WORKS RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT & POSTPARTUM WOMEN. description: ADVANCING NURTURING CARE, HOUSING, OUTCOMES, AND RECOVERY THROUGH AN ESTABLISHED COMMUNITY-ACADEMIC PARTNERSHIP (ANCHOR) - ADVANCING NURTURING CARE, HOUSING, OUTCOMES, AND RECOVERY THROUGH AN ESTABLISHED COMMUNITY-ACADEMIC PARTNERSHIP (ANCHOR). ANCHOR WILL DELIVER COMPREHENSIVE SUD TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT TO PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUDS) AND THE MINOR CHILDREN WHO WILL LIVE ALONGSIDE THEM. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE URBAN MARYLAND AND ALSO RURAL MARYLAND, WHERE RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT BUILT FOR THIS POPULATION IS LARGELY ABSENT. THE ANCHOR INITIATIVE PAIRS HELPING UP MISSION’S (HUM) RESIDENTIAL RECOVERY INFRASTRUCTURE AND JOHNS HOPKINS’ COMPREHENSIVE ADDICTION AND PREGNANCY (CAP) PERINATAL SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT EXPERTISE TO PROVIDE FAMILY-CENTERED RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT, RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND CARE COORDINATION FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN WITH SUDS AND THEIR MINOR CHILDREN. ANCHOR WILL SERVE WOMEN DURING PREGNANCY AND THE FIRST POSTPARTUM YEAR. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE 40 WOMEN AND 32 CHILDREN IN YEAR 1, AND 60 WOMEN AND 40 CHILDREN IN EACH OF YEARS 2 THROUGH 5, A TOTAL OF 472 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD.  ANCHOR WILL PURSUE THREE GOALS: TO ENGAGE AND RETAIN WOMEN IN INTEGRATED TREATMENT THROUGH DELIVERY AND THE FOURTH TRIMESTER; TO DELIVER EACH MOTHER AND CHILD COORDINATED MEDICAL, BEHAVIORAL, AND DEVELOPMENTAL CARE WITHOUT THE HANDOFFS THAT FRAGMENT IT; AND TO IDENTIFY KEY MARKERS OF TREATMENT, THAT, WHEN IDENTIFIED EARLY, WILL STRENGTHEN RECOVERY, FAMILY STABILITY, AND SELF-SUFFICIENCY IN ORDER TO INTERRUPT THE INTERGENERATIONAL TRANSMISSION OF ADDICTION. ABOUT THREE QUARTERS OF THE CURRENT CAP POPULATIONS CARRY AN OPIOID USE DISORDER, MANY WITH A CO-OCCURRING PSYCHIATRIC CONDITION, AND UNSTABLE HOUSING. THEIR CHILDREN CARRY THE DEVELOPMENTAL RISKS OF PRENATAL SUBSTANCE EXPOSURE AND EARLY ADVERSITY.

description: SAC AND FOX NATION HEALING PATHWAYS INITIATIVE - THE SAC AND FOX NATION PROPOSES THE HEALING PATHWAYS INITIATIVE, A COMPREHENSIVE, CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROGRAM DESIGNED TO EXPAND PREVENTION, TREATMENT, AND RECOVERY SERVICES FOR TRIBAL CITIZENS AFFECTED BY OPIOID AND OTHER SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS. SERVING A PREDOMINANTLY RURAL POPULATION, THE NATION CONTINUES TO EXPERIENCE SIGNIFICANT BARRIERS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTHCARE, INCLUDING LIMITED ACCESS TO SPECIALTY PROVIDERS, TRANSPORTATION CHALLENGES, WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, AND INCREASING RATES OF OPIOID AND POLYSUBSTANCE USE. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE NATION'S EXISTING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE BY INCREASING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED SERVICES WHILE ADDRESSING SOCIAL AND GEOGRAPHIC BARRIERS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO DELAYED TREATMENT AND POOR HEALTH OUTCOMES. THE HEALING PATHWAYS INITIATIVE WILL ESTABLISH AN INTEGRATED CONTINUUM OF CARE THAT INCLUDES BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT, MEDICATION FOR OPIOID USE DISORDER (MOUD) WHEN CLINICALLY APPROPRIATE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH COUNSELING, PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT, CARE NAVIGATION, OVERDOSE RECOGNITION AND RESPONSE EDUCATION, COMMUNITY PREVENTION ACTIVITIES, AND COORDINATED REFERRALS TO HEALTHCARE AND COMMUNITY RESOURCES. THIS INVESTMENT WILL IMPROVE TREATMENT ACCESS, REDUCE MISSED APPOINTMENTS, INCREASE PARTICIPANT ENGAGEMENT, AND STRENGTHEN CONTINUITY OF CARE THROUGHOUT THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD. THESE INTERVENTIONS WILL BE DELIVERED WITHIN A CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE FRAMEWORK THAT HONORS TRIBAL VALUES, PROMOTES FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, AND RECOGNIZES THE IMPORTANCE OF COMMUNITY IN SUPPORTING RECOVERY.

description: INVESTIGATING CD200 SIGNALING AS A REGULATOR OF IMMUNOSUPPRESSION AND OSTEOCLASTOGENESIS IN BONE METASTATIC NICHE - PROJECT SUMMARY IMMUNE CHECKPOINT INHIBITORS (ICIS) ENABLE ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNITY BY BLOCKING IMMUNOREGULATORY RECEPTOR-LIGAND INTERACTIONS (E.G., PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH PROTEIN 1 [PD-1] AND ITS LIGAND [PD-L1]). DESPITE THEIR WIDESPREAD SUCCESS AS AN ANTI-CANCER THERAPY, ICIS FUNCTION POORLY IN PATIENTS WITH BONE METASTASES, AND PATIENTS RECEIVING THERAPY ARE AT RISK OF DEVELOPING BONE LOSS AND FRACTURES. I HAVE PREVIOUSLY OBSERVED BONE LOSS, IMMUNE SUPPRESSION, AND NO REDUCTION IN BONE METASTATIC TUMOR BURDEN IN MICE INOCULATED WITH MURINE BREAST CANCER CELLS AND TREATED WITH A PD-1 INHIBITOR. GIVEN THAT MANY BREAST CANCER SURVIVORS WILL SUCCUMB TO THE DISEASE DUE TO RESIDUAL TUMOR CELLS THAT EVADE THERAPY, UNDERSTANDING THE MECHANISMS OF IMMUNE SUPPRESSION IN THE BONE METASTATIC NICHE IS CRITICAL. CD200 HAS BEEN INDICATED AS AN IMMUNOREGULATORY GENE ENRICHED IN DORMANT TUMOR POPULATIONS COMMONLY ASSOCIATED WITH THE BONE MARROW NICHE AND ITS RECEPTOR, CD200R, IS PRIMARILY EXPRESSED ON MYELOID LINEAGE CELLS INCLUDING OSTEOCLAST PRECURSORS. THUS, INCREASED SIGNALING THROUGH THE CD200/CD200R AXIS MAY PROMOTE T CELL DYSFUNCTION DIRECTLY, PROMOTE OSTEOCLASTOGENESIS, AND AMPLIFY THE “VICIOUS CYCLE” OF BONE METASTASIS IN WHICH TUMOR-INDUCED BONE RESORPTION FUELS TUMOR GROWTH AND IMMUNOSUPPRESSION. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT CD200 SIGNALING REPROGRAMS BM MYELOID LINEAGE CELLS TO SUPPRESS T CELL ACTIVITY AND PROMOTE OSTEOCLASTOGENESIS, THEREBY CONTRIBUTING TO BONE METASTATIC RESISTANCE TO ICI THERAPY. THE USE OF IMMUNOCOMPETENT MOUSE MODELS IS ESSENTIAL FOR THE PROPOSED STUDIES; THE BONE METASTATIC MICROENVIRONMENT IS COMPOSED OF DYNAMIC INTERACTIONS BETWEEN TUMOR CELLS, IMMUNE CELLS, AND BONE TISSUE THAT CANNOT BE ADEQUATELY MODELED IN VITRO. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, I PROPOSE TO (1) DEFINE HOW CD200/CD200R SHAPES IMMUNE COMPOSITION AND T CELL FUNCTION IN THE BONE METASTATIC MICROENVIRONMENT, (2) DETERMINE WHETHER CD200 SIGNALING IN BONE METASTASES PROMOTES OSTEOCLASTOGENESIS, AND (3) DETERMINE WHETHER TARGETING CD200 ENHANCES RESPONSE TO ICI THERAPY IN A BONE METASTATIC SETTING. IN AIM 1, I WILL COMBINE IN VITRO PROFILING COMBINED WITH IN VIVO FUNCTIONAL  STUDIES TO DEFINE HOW CD200 SIGNALING SHAPES MYELOID-MEDIATED IMMUNOMODULATORY MECHANISMS AND T CELL FUNCTION IN THE BONE METASTATIC NICHE. IN AIM 2, I WILL TREAT XENOANTIGEN-TOLERANT “NOGLOW” MICE WITH CD200LO OR CD200HI BREAST CANCER CELLS AND/OR A CD200 INHIBITOR TO DISSECT THE RELATIVE CONTRIBUTIONS OF TUMOR- VS HOST-DERIVED CD200 SIGNALING IN DRIVING PATHOGENIC OSTEOCLASTOGENESIS DURING BONE METASTASIS. IN AIM 3, I WILL USE IN VIVO APPROACHES TO EVALUATE THERAPEUTIC TARGETS TO INCREASE LONG-TERM ICI EFFICACY IN PATIENTS WITH BONE METASTASES. GIVEN THE HIGH INCIDENCE OF BONE METASTASES FOR MULTIPLE TUMOR TYPES AND THE POOR SURVIVAL OF BONE METASTATIC PATIENTS IN RESPONSE TO ICI THERAPY, THIS PROPOSAL WILL HELP IDENTIFY MOLECULAR MECHANISMS DRIVING IMMUNE RESISTANCE IN THE BONE NICHE AND REVEAL NEW THERAPEUTIC OPPORTUNITIES FOR IMPROVING OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS WITH BONE METASTATIC DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: METABOLITE- MACROMOLECULE INTERACTIONS MODULATING INTRATUMORAL T-CELL FATE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ ABSTRACT A DOMINANT FEATURE OF THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT IS THE PROGRESSIVE DYSFUNCTION OF CYTOTOXIC CD8+ T-CELLS, A PROCESS KNOWN AS EXHAUSTION. EXTENSIVE EFFORT TO MECHANISTICALLY INTERROGATE T-CELL EXHAUSTION HAVE IDENTIFIED KEY TRANSCRIPTOMIC AND EPIGENETIC DRIVERS, HOWEVER, COMBINING IMMUNOTHERAPIES WITH INHIBITOR OF THESE PATHWAYS HAS ONLY MODESTLY IMPROVED CLINICAL OUTCOME, IMPLYING ADDITIONAL DETERMINANTS MIGHT BE INVOLVED. NOTABLY, TUMORS WITH HIGH METABOLIC ACTIVITY, TEND TO BE RESISTANT TO IMMUNOTHERAPY, SUGGESTING ALTERATIONS IN METABOLIC MICROENVIRONMENT AS A DRIVER OF PERSISTENT INTRATUMORAL T-CELL DYSFUNCTION. HOWEVER, THE UNDERLYING MECHANISM BY WHICH METABOLITES DIRECTLY MODULATE IMMUNE CELL FATE IS LESS UNDERSTOOD. EMERGING EVIDENCE SUPPORTS THE NOTION THAT METABOLITES CAN ALLOSTERICALLY BIND TO PROTEINS OR MRNAS TO REGULATE THEIR FUNCTION AND STABILITY. HOWEVER, WHETHER AND HOW SUCH INTERACTIONS FINE-TUNE T-CELL RECEPTOR (TCR) SIGNALING TRANSDUCTION AND DOWNSTREAM EFFECTOR PROGRAMS IN CYTOTOXIC CD8+ T-CELLS WITHIN THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT REMAINS UNCLEAR.  THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO ELUCIDATE THE REGULATORY MECHANISMS BY WHICH METABOLIC SIGNALING, SPECIFICALLY METABOLITE-MACROMOLECULE INTERACTIONS, MODULATE T-CELL FATE WITHIN THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT. SPECIFIC AIM 1 AIMS TO INVESTIGATE HOW METABOLITES BINDING TO THE UNTRANSLATED REGIONS (UTRS) OF EXHAUSTION-SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTS REPROGRAM DOWNSTREAM EXHAUSTION PROGRAM. IN AIM 1.1, I WILL VALIDATE INDIVIDUAL INTERACTION BETWEEN METABOLITES AND EXHAUSTION-SPECIFIC MRNA THROUGH THE ESTABLISHED MASS SPECTROMETRY INTEGRATED WITH EQUILIBRIUM DIALYSIS FOR THE DISCOVERY OF ALLOSTERY SYSTEMATICALLY (MIDAS) PLATFORM, AND PINPOINT WHICH SPECIFIC METABOLITES MEDIATE THESE INTERACTIONS. IN AIM 1.2, I WILL MAP THE CIS ELEMENTS ON THE UTRS THAT ARE RESPONSIBLE OF METABOLITE BINDING AND ASSESS WHETHER THEY ALTER MRNA STABILITY OR TRANSLATIONAL EFFICIENCY. IN AIM 1.3, I WILL DETERMINE WHETHER THESE INTERACTIONS PROMOTE EXHAUSTION IN TUMOR-INFILTRATING T-CELLS IN VIVO. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE WHETHER INTERACTIONS BETWEEN TUMOR-ASSOCIATED METABOLITES AND PROXIMAL TCR SIGNALING COMPONENTS REGULATE AND ALTER TCR SIGNALING TRANSDUCTION. IN AIM 2.1, I WILL LEVERAGE THE MIDAS PLATFORM AND PROFILE THE METABOLITES THAT BIND TO PROXIMAL TCR SIGNALING COMPONENTS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO LCK, ZAP-70, AND LAT. I WILL THEN IDENTIFY THE BINDING SITE OF THESE METABOLITE-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS VIA HIGH-RESOLUTION CRYSTALLOGRAPHY. IN AIM 2.2, I WILL PERFORM SITE-DIRECTED MUTAGENESIS ON THESE PROTEINS IN T-CELL AND DETERMINE WHETHER DISRUPTED METABOLITE-PROTEIN INTERACTION WOULD ALTER TCR SIGNALING THRESHOLD OR STRENGTH UPON STIMULATION. FINALLY, I WILL DETERMINE WHETHER THESE INTERACTIONS MODULATE T-CELL EXHAUSTION DYNAMICS AND RESTRICTS ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNITY. TOGETHER, THE PROPOSED WORK WILL HIGHLIGHT THE REGULATORY MECHANISM BY WHICH DIRECT METABOLITE INTERACTIONS MODULATE UPSTREAM TCR SIGNALING AND DRIVES DOWNSTREAM EXHAUSTION PROGRAM. THIS WILL ALSO PROVIDE THE RATIONALE FOR TREATMENT STRATEGIES THAT ALTER THESE METABOLITE INTERACTIONS TO RESTORE T-CELL FUNCTION WITHIN THE TUMOR.

description: EXAMINATION OF GUT-MICROBIOME-BRAIN INTERACTIONS IN A NOVEL GENE X ENVIRONMENT MODEL OF NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE NERVOUS SYSTEM IS A COMPLEX, DYNAMIC PROCESS THAT IS DYSREGULATED IN NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS (NDDS). ALTHOUGH PROGRESS HAS BEEN MADE TO IDENTIFY GENETIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL NDD-RISK FACTORS, WE LAG BEHIND WITH RIGOROUS INVESTIGATION OF HOW ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS MAY ACT ON CERTAIN GENETIC VULNERABILITIES TO ALTER NEURODEVELOPMENT. MY DISSERTATION PROJECT BUILDS ON MY CO-SPONSOR, DR. BLASER’S, RECENT HUMAN EPIDEMIOLOGICAL STUDY THAT IDENTIFIED INFANT CEPHALOSPORIN ANTIBIOTIC EXPOSURE AS AN ENVIRONMENTAL FACTOR ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED NDD RISK. IT IS WELL ESTABLISHED THAT ANTIBIOTICS DECREASE THE DIVERSITY AND ABUNDANCE OF BENEFICIAL MICROBIAL TAXA IN THE GUT, WHICH CAN CONSEQUENTLY ALTER BRAIN STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISM(S) BY WHICH AN ANTIBIOTIC-INDUCED PERTURBED MICROBIOME AFFECTS EARLY NEURODEVELOPMENTAL PROCESSES IMPLICATED IN NDD PATHOGENESIS REMAINS LARGELY UNEXPLORED. MY CURRENT WORK ADDRESSES THIS RESEARCH GAP BY INVESTIGATING GUT-MICROBIOME-BRAIN INTERACTIONS IN A NOVEL GENE BY ENVIRONMENT (GXE) MOUSE MODEL OF NDDS UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF DRS. EMANUEL DICICCO-BLOOM (SPONSOR, NEUROSCIENCE) AND MARTIN BLASER (CO-SPONSOR, MICROBIOLOGY). THE PRIMARY GOAL OF AIM 1 IS TO RECEIVE RIGOROUS TRAINING IN MICROBIOLOGY AND DEVELOPMENTAL NEUROBIOLOGY DURING THE F99 PHASE TO EXAMINE HOW EARLY LIFE CEPHALOSPORIN EXPOSURE ALTERS THE GUT MICROBIOME AND CONSEQUENTIALLY DYSREGULATES NEURODEVELOPMENT. THE PROPOSED EXPERIMENTS WILL UTILIZE BOTH WILDTYPE AND 16P11.2 MICRODELETION COPY NUMBER VARIATION (+/16PDEL CNV) MICE, WHICH ARE A ROBUST GENETIC RISK MODEL FOR INVESTIGATING NDD PATHOGENESIS DUE TO THEIR HIGHLY CONSERVED 28 GENE DELETION REGION ALSO OBSERVED IN HUMAN +/16PDEL HETEROZYGOTES. MY PRELIMINARY FINDINGS INDICATE SEX- AND GENOTYPE-DEPENDENT EFFECTS OF CEPHALOSPORIN EXPOSURE ON ALTERED NEURODEVELOPMENT. FOR THE REMAINING F99 PHASE, I WILL FINISH CHARACTERIZING HOW EARLY LIFE CEPHALOSPORIN EXPOSURE ALTERS NEURODEVELOPMENT AND THE GUT- MICROBIOME AND THEN INCORPORATE A MECHANISTIC APPROACH TO DETERMINE IF MICROBIOME RESTORATION CAN RESCUE ALTERED NEURODEVELOPMENT. THIS TRAINING WILL PROVIDE ME WITH A STRONG TECHNICAL AND INTELLECTUAL SKILLSET TO CONTINUE INVESTIGATING GUT-MICROBIOME-BRAIN RESEARCH AS A POSTDOCTORAL SCHOLAR. HOWEVER, A GAP IN MY SKILLSET THAT AIM 2 WILL EXPAND ON IS THE ABILITY TO ANALYZE AND INTERPRET THE METABOLOME AND EPIGENOME, TWO INTERMEDIATE SYSTEMS THAT MEDIATE GUT-MICROBIOME-BRAIN GXE INTERACTIONS. TO ENSURE I ADDRESS THIS GAP, I WILL IDENTIFY A POSTDOCTORAL LABORATORY THAT CAN TRAIN ME IN ROUTINE AND CUTTING-EDGE TECHNIQUES TO STUDY AND MANIPULATE THE METABOLOME AND EPIGENOME DURING THE K00 PHASE. THESE STUDIES WILL COLLECTIVELY ESTABLISH AND BUILD ON A MECHANISTIC FRAMEWORK TO INVESTIGATE GUT-MICROBIOME-BRAIN GXE INTERACTIONS WHILE SIMULTANEOUSLY FACILITATING MY PATH TOWARDS INDEPENDENCE AS A NEUROSCIENCE INVESTIGATOR.

description: CIRCUIT MECHANISMS GOVERNING ANXIOUS ANTICIPATION DURING MOTIVATIONAL CONFLICT - ANXIETY DISORDERS ARE CHARACTERIZED BY MALADAPTIVE AVOIDANCE: ANTICIPATED THREAT SUPPRESSES REWARD-SEEKING EVEN WHEN DANGER IS DISTANT, UNCERTAIN, OR ABSENT. THIS BEHAVIOR REFLECTS A FAILURE TO APPROPRIATELY ARBITRATE BETWEEN COMPETING MOTIVATIONAL SYSTEMS AS A FUNCTION OF VALUE AND TIME. WHILE SUBSTANTIAL PROGRESS HAS BEEN MADE IN IDENTIFYING THE NEURAL SUBSTRATES OF THREAT AND REWARD, THE CIRCUIT-LEVEL MECHANISMS THAT DETERMINE WHEN BEHAVIOR TRANSITIONS FROM APPROACH TO AVOIDANCE REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. CLINICAL EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THIS TRANSITION IS BIASED TOWARD PREMATURE SWITCHING IN ANXIETY, YET THE COMPUTATIONAL AND CIRCUIT MECHANISMS GOVERNING THIS BIAS REMAIN UNRESOLVED. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PRODUCE A CIRCUIT-LEVEL, COMPUTATIONALLY SPECIFIED ACCOUNT OF HOW ANXIOUS ANTICIPATION ALTERS THE TIMING OF APPROACH-TO-AVOIDANCE TRANSITIONS DURING MOTIVATIONAL CONFLICT. A NOVEL APPROACH–AVOIDANCE CONFLICT PARADIGM PROVIDES AN ACTIVE, TEMPORALLY PRECISE READOUT OF THE MOMENT REWARD PURSUIT IS ABANDONED. EXPERIMENTAL MANIPULATION OF REWARD MAGNITUDE, THREAT MAGNITUDE, AND TEMPORAL CONTINGENCIES ENABLE DISSOCIATION OF TEMPORAL PROXIMITY COMPUTATIONS FROM VALUATION AND ACTION THRESHOLDS. NATURAL INTER-INDIVIDUAL VARIABILITY IN C57BL/6 MICE WILL BE LEVERAGED TO IDENTIFY MECHANISMS THAT VARY ALONG A CONTINUOUS AXIS OF ANXIETY. IN AIM 1, THIS WORK WILL DISSOCIATE THE COMPUTATIONAL BASIS OF PREMATURE AVOIDANCE BY DETERMINING WHETHER EARLIER SWITCHING IN HIGH ANXIETY SUBJECTS ARISES FROM ALTERED VALUATION OR DISTORTED TEMPORAL REPRESENTATIONS OF THREAT. IN AIM 2, IT WILL IDENTIFY THE CIRCUIT MECHANISMS THAT IMPLEMENT THIS BIAS BY CHARACTERIZING HOW LIMBIC–CORTICOSTRIATAL INTERACTIONS RESHAPE MEDIAL PREFRONTAL AND DORSAL STRIATAL POPULATION DYNAMICS, AND BY TESTING WHETHER PREMATURE AVOIDANCE REFLECTS PERSISTENT INCREASE IN CORTICOLIMBIC ACTIVITY OR STRONG, TRANSIENT LIMBIC DRIVE IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO TRANSITIONS. IN AIM 3, IT WILL ESTABLISH CAUSAL SUFFICIENCY BY IMPOSING THE IDENTIFIED CIRCUIT MOTIFS IN LOW ANXIETY ANIMALS TO DETERMINE WHETHER THESE DYNAMICS ARE SUFFICIENT TO RECAPITULATE PREMATURE AVOIDANCE BEHAVIOR. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL ESTABLISH A COMPUTATIONAL AND CIRCUIT-LEVEL FRAMEWORK FOR APPROACH–AVOIDANCE ARBITRATION, DEFINE CANDIDATE INTERVENTION TARGETS, AND IDENTIFY QUANTITATIVE BIOMARKERS TRANSLATABLE TO HUMAN NEUROIMAGING MEASURES OF MALADAPTIVE AVOIDANCE.

description: AGE-SPECIFIC ANTIDEPRESSANT-GUT MICROBIOME INTERPLAY IN ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNITY. - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT RESEARCH: EARLY ONSET COLORECTAL CANCER (CRC) INCIDENCE RATES HAVE SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, BUT THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD. ANTIDEPRESSANTS, LIKE SELECTIVE SEROTONIN REUPTAKE INHIBITORS (SSRIS), ARE AMONG THE LARGEST INCREASES IN PRESCRIPTION MEDICATIONS DURING PREGNANCY OVER THE PAST DECADES. RECENT WORK BY OUR LAB AND OTHERS HAVE ELUCIDATED THE GUT AS A MAJOR SOURCE OF THE NEUROTRANSMITTER SEROTONIN (5-HYDROXYTRYPTAMINE, 5-HT). HOWEVER, IT REMAINS UNKNOWN HOW MATERNAL ANTIDEPRESSANT USE AFFECTS NEONATAL GUT 5-HT, IMMUNE REGULATION, AND CRC SUSCEPTIBILITY IN ADULTHOOD. I HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT NEONATAL GUT BACTERIA INCREASE PRODUCTION OF 5-HT WHILE INHIBITING BREAKDOWN 5-HT, LEADING TO SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER LEVELS OF 5-HT IN THE NEONATAL GUT WHICH IN TURN SHAPES T CELL RESPONSE TO PROMOTE IMMUNE TOLERANCE IN EARLY LIFE. I HAVE ESTABLISHED A MATERNAL SSRI MOUSE MODEL; MY PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT POSTNATAL EXPOSURE TO MATERNAL SSRI SIGNIFICANTLY ELEVATES GUT 5-HT LEVELS AND CHANGES THE GUT MICROBIOME COMPOSITION IN NEONATAL MICE. USING A MOUSE CRC MODEL, I FOUND THAT CONTINUOUS SSRI EXPOSURE STARTING FROM NURSING REDUCED TUMOR SIZE IN MALE MICE, BUT NOT IN FEMALE MICE; THIS WAS ASSOCIATED WITH AN INCREASE OF TUMOR INFILTRATING T CELLS PRODUCING INTERFERON-GAMMA AND PERFORIN AND A DECREASE OF TUMOR INFILTRATING B CELLS IN SSRI-EXPOSED MALE MICE. THEREFORE, I HYPOTHESIZE THAT EXPOSURE TO ANTIDEPRESSANTS (SSRIS) SHAPES IMMUNE CELL DEVELOPMENT AND ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNITY IN AN AGE AND SEX-DEPENDENT MANNER. TO TEST MY HYPOTHESIS, I WILL: 1) USE AOM/DSS AND MC38 MOUSE MODELS OF CRC TO CHARACTERIZE AGE/SEX-SPECIFIC EFFECTS OF SSRIS ON ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNITY AND 2) USE HTR3AFLOXCD4CRE OR HTR2AFLOXMBLCRE MICE AND 13C-LABELED 5-HT TO INVESTIGATE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH EARLY LIFE SSRI EXPOSURE ALTERS ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNITY. CAREER GOALS: MY LONG-TERM CAREER GOAL IS TO LEAD AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH LABORATORY INVESTIGATING HOW DIET AND THE GUT MICROBIOME SHAPE DEVELOPMENT OF IMMUNITY AND GUT DISEASE IN INFANTS, WITH THE GOAL TO UNCOVER SIGNIFICANT EARLY LIFE FACTORS THAT COULD BE LEVERAGED TO LOWER CANCER. CAREER DEVELOPMENT: I WILL MEET WEEKLY WITH MY MENTOR DR. MELODY ZENG AND BI-WEEKLY WITH MY CO-MENTORS (DRS. TAHA MERGHOUB, GREGORY SONNENBERG, AND CHUN-JUN GUO) TO DISCUSS MY RESEARCH PROGRESS AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT. ADDITIONALLY, I WILL PARTICIPATE IN AT LEAST 2 SCIENTIFIC CONFERENCES AND ATTEND WORKSHOPS TO POLISH MY PRESENTATION, GRANT WRITING, MENTORING, AND JOB SEARCH AND INTERVIEWING SKILLS. ENVIRONMENT: I WILL PRIMARILY WORK IN THE LABORATORY OF DR. ZENG, A RESEARCH SPACE ADEQUATELY EQUIPPED TO CONDUCT MY PROPOSED EXPERIMENTS WITH ADDITIONAL TECHNICAL SUPPORT FROM MY CO-MENTORS. MOREOVER, THE TRI-INSTITUTIONAL CONSORTIUM (WCM, MSKCC, AND ROCKEFELLER) IS HOME TO AN OUTSTANDING IMMUNOLOGY AND MICROBIOLOGY COMMUNITY, PROVIDING ME WITH A DIVERSE GROUP OF COLLEAGUES AND COLLABORATORS; THIS UNIQUE ENVIRONMENT HAS RESOURCES FOR RESEARCH AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT, INCLUDING IMMUNOLOGY AND CANCER CORE FACILITIES.

description: CANNABIS USE AND ASSAULT INJURY RISK IN YOUTH: A SPATIOTEMPORAL AND ECOLOGICAL MOMENTARY ASSESSMENT APPROACH - THE PROPOSED K01 MENTORED RESEARCH SCIENTIST DEVELOPMENT AWARD WILL PROVIDE DR. DANIEL LEE WITH TRAINING TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCHER SPECIALIZING IN YOUTH SUBSTANCE USE, PARTICULARLY CANNABIS USE, AND IN UNDERSTANDING ITS HEALTH RISKS, INCLUDING VIOLENCE (I.E., VICTIMIZATION, AGGRESSION). CANNABIS USE AMONG EMERGING ADULTS (EAS; AGES 18–25) IS A SIGNIFICANT PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERN, WITH EAS REPORTING THE HIGHEST PREVALENCE RATE. THE HEALTH RISKS OF CANNABIS USE HAVE BEEN WELL DOCUMENTED AMONG EAS, INCLUDING VIOLENCE. IT IS IMPORTANT TO INVESTIGATE CANNABIS USE, INCLUDING ITS RELATION TO VIOLENCE, DUE TO THE WIDESPREAD LEGALIZATION (24 STATES RECREATIONAL; 48 STATES MEDICAL) OF CANNABIS AND THE PROLIFERATION OF HIGHER-POTENCY PRODUCTS AND ALTERNATIVE ROUTES OF ADMINISTRATION (E.G., VAPING, EDIBLES), WHICH SPEED PROGRESSION TO EARLY CANNABIS USE DISORDER (CUD) SYMPTOMS. YET, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT NEAR-TERM RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS THAT FOCUS ON CANNABIS USE AND WHY IT’S ASSOCIATED WITH VIOLENCE FOR SOME YOUTH. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, I WILL COLLECT PILOT DATA FROM EAS WITH OR WITHOUT AN ASSAULT INJURY (N=80; 40 PER GROUP) IN THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT (ED) WHO USED CANNABIS IN THE PAST MONTH. THE PILOT STUDY WILL: (1) IDENTIFY NEAR-TERM RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS FOR CANNABIS USE AND VIOLENCE AMONG EAS USING RETROSPECTIVE, GEOREFERENCED ACTIVITY-SPACE INTERVIEWS; (2) CONDUCT A 30-DAY PROSPECTIVE PILOT USING DAILY ECOLOGICAL MOMENTARY ASSESSMENT (EMA) AND PASSIVE GPS TO COMPARE EAS (WITH/WITHOUT ASSAULT INJURY) ON CANNABIS USE (AND OTHER SUBSTANCE USE) AND EXPOSURE TO HIGH-RISK ACTIVITY SPACES; AND (3) EVALUATE MULTILEVEL MECHANISMS LINKING ACTIVITY SPACES TO RISK AND PROTECTIVE MECHANISMS AS THEY CONTRIBUTE TO CANNABIS USE AND VIOLENCE. THIS PROJECT DIRECTLY ADVANCES THE NIDA STRATEGIC OBJECTIVE TO UNDERSTAND THE CONTEXTUAL LANDSCAPE OF DRUG USE AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS THAT INFLUENCE DRUG-RELATED OUTCOMES (PRIORITY SCIENTIFIC AREA #1). THIS PROPOSAL INCLUDES A COMPREHENSIVE MENTORSHIP AND DIDACTIC PLAN THAT WILL SUPPORT NEW DIRECTIONS IN MY RESEARCH FOCUSED ON CANNABIS AND OTHER DRUG USE, AND EXPAND MY EXPERTISE IN METHODS RELATED TO VIOLENCE BY: (1) GAINING KNOWLEDGE IN SUBSTANCE USE EPIDEMIOLOGY, ETIOLOGY, AND ASSESSMENT, FOCUSED ON CANNABIS USE, TO ADVANCE RESEARCH ON YOUTH CANNABIS USE AND VIOLENCE (AGGRESSION, VICTIMIZATION); (2) ACQUIRING SKILLS IN COLLECTING, PROCESSING, AND ANALYZING GEOREFERENCED SPATIOTEMPORAL DATA ON DAILY ACTIVITIES FOR CANNABIS USE AND VIOLENCE; (3) TRAINING IN DESIGNING, COLLECTING, AND ANALYZING EMA DATA WITH PASSIVE GPS TRACKING TO TRACK CANNABIS USE, VIOLENCE, AND RELEVANT RISK/PROTECTIVE FACTORS; AND (4) ASSESSING MEDIATION USING INTENSIVE LONGITUDINAL DATA FROM EMAS AND PASSIVE GPS TRACKING USING DYNAMIC STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELING. TRAINING WILL ENTAIL A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM OF MENTORS: DR. MAUREEN WALTON (PRIMARY MENTOR) AND DRS. PATRICK CARTER, DOUGLAS WIEBE, AND CYNTHIA EWELL FOSTER (COLLABORATORS). THIS K01 AWARD WILL ALLOW ME TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR WHO CAN ELUCIDATE THE SOCIOECOLOGICAL AND SITUATIONAL RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS RELATED TO CANNABIS USE AND ITS RELATION TO VIOLENCE.

description: UNRAVELING THE ROLE OF FIBROBLAST-DERIVED LYSYL OXIDASE IN AVF MATURATION FAILURE - ABSTRACT END-STAGE KIDNEY DISEASE AFFECTS OVER 800,000 AMERICANS, WITH ~60% UNDERGOING HEMODIALYSIS (HD). FOR THESE PATIENTS ON HD, VASCULAR ACCESS IS CRITICAL, WITH THREE MAIN TYPES AVAILABLE: CENTRAL VENOUS CATHETER, ARTERIOVENOUS GRAFT, AND ARTERIOVENOUS FISTULA (AVF). AMONG THESE, THE AVF IS THE PREFERRED CHOICE DUE TO ITS SUPERIOR LONGEVITY AND LOWER RISK OF INFECTION. HOWEVER, AVFS FACE SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGES, AS UP TO 40% REQUIRE ENDOVASCULAR OR SURGICAL INTERVENTION TO ADDRESS STENOSIS, WHICH IMPAIRS THEIR ABILITY TO FUNCTION FOR DIALYSIS. THESE FREQUENT INTERVENTIONS INCREASE THE RISK OF COMPLICATIONS AND HOSPITALIZATIONS, CONTRIBUTING TO THE HIGH ANNUAL COST OF MAINTAINING VASCULAR ACCESS, WHICH EXCEEDS $2 BILLION. THUS, THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR NOVEL ANTI-STENOTIC TREATMENTS TO ENHANCE AVF MATURATION AND REDUCE FAILURE RATES. IN FACT, THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS STUDY WILL ALLOW ME TO UNCOVER THE ROLE OF FIBROBLAST-SPECIFIC LOX IN THE MATURATION AND FAILURE OF ARTERIOVENOUS FISTULAS (AVF). SPECIFICALLY, I AIM TO ELUCIDATE THE MOLECULAR AND CELLULAR MECHANISMS BY WHICH LOX UPREGULATION INCREASES THE RISK OF AVF FAILURE. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA PROVIDES A ROBUST FOUNDATION TO EXPLORE LOX'S ROLE IN MODULATING FIBROBLAST PHENOTYPES FOLLOWING AVF CREATION. I AM CONFIDENT THAT THE OUTCOMES OF THIS K01 GRANT WILL HELP IDENTIFY NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS TO PREVENT OR REDUCE AVF FAILURE IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE (CKD), POTENTIALLY ACCELERATING THE DEVELOPMENT OF INNOVATIVE TREATMENTS. THIS AWARD WILL ALSO BE INSTRUMENTAL IN ADVANCING MY CAREER GOAL OF BECOMING AN INDEPENDENT, WELL-FUNDED SCIENTIST AND SECURING A TENURE-TRACK FACULTY POSITION WITHIN THE VASCULAR DIVISION OF THE DEPARTMENT OF SURGERY AT THE MILLER SCHOOL OF MEDICINE, UNIVERSITY OF MIAMI. MY LONG-TERM RESEARCH VISION FOCUSES ON ARTERIAL AND VENOUS DISEASES, WITH A SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON VENOUS REMODELING FOLLOWING SURGICAL INTERVENTIONS SUCH AS AVF. ULTIMATELY, MY GOAL IS TO DEVELOP PHARMACOLOGICAL AND NON-PHARMACOLOGICAL THERAPIES, INCLUDING EXERCISE TRAINING, TO TREAT ARTERIAL AND VENOUS DISORDERS AND TRANSLATE THESE DISCOVERIES INTO CLINICAL PRACTICE TO IMPROVE PATIENT OUTCOMES. BY ACCOMPLISHING THE PROPOSED AIMS AND PARTICIPATING IN THE COMPREHENSIVE TRAINING PLAN, I WILL STRENGTHEN MY EXPERTISE IN ADVANCED IMAGING TECHNIQUES, BIOSTATISTICS, GRANT WRITING, TRANSGENIC MOUSE MODEL MANAGEMENT, AND GENOMICS. THESE SKILLS WILL BE CRITICAL IN MY PATH TO SCIENTIFIC INDEPENDENCE AND WILL ENABLE ME TO MAKE SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE FIELD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: FEMALE PROTECTION FROM MASLD VIA BILE ACID REGULATION OF CHOLESTEROL LEVELS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT:  I AM AN ASSISTANT PROJECT SCIENTIST WITH INTEREST IN HOW HORMONE REGULATION OF METABOLIC PROCESSES CONTRIBUTES TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF LIVER DISEASES. MY LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO BECOME AN EXPERT IN SEX DIFFERENCES IN LIPID METABOLISM AND BECOME AN ACADEMIC LEADER IN CHOLESTEROL REGULATION, BILE ACID METABOLISM, DEVELOPING NOVEL RESOURCES AND RESEARCH TOOLS, AND MENTORING TOMORROW’S SCIENTISTS. I AIM TO EXPAND CURRENT UNDERSTANDING OF BILE ACID METABOLISM AND CHOLESTEROL HOMEOSTASIS IN LIVER LIPID REGULATION BY INTEGRATING THEM WITH MY INTEREST IN SEX DIFFERENCES. I WILL BE SUPPORTED BY MY PRIMARY MENTOR, DR. THOMAS VALLIM, A LEADER IN BILE ACID AND LIPID METABOLISM, ALONG WITH CO-MENTORS DR. KAREN REUE AND DR. ANDREA HEVENER, LEADERS IN SEX DIFFERENCES AND HORMONAL REGULATION OF METABOLISM. THEIR MENTORSHIP AND THE COMPLETION OF MY PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL ESTABLISH MY INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM AND PUT ME ON PACE TO BECOME A LEADER AT THE INTERSECTION OF OUR FIELDS. THROUGH UCLA’S CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE INSTITUTE, I WILL ACCESS TRAINING IN GRANT WRITING, MANUSCRIPT PREPARATION, AND ETHICAL RESEARCH. I WILL ALSO REFRESH MY ETHICS TRAINING AND TAKE DIDACTIC TRAINING IN BIOSTATISTICS AND SEX DIFFERENCES IN METABOLISM. WITH THE SUPPORT OF THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA LOS ANGELES, A RENOWNED RESEARCH CENTER, I AM WELL POSITIONED TO ADVANCE MY CAREER TO INDEPENDENCE.  MY FIVE-YEAR RESEARCH AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN WILL EXPAND MY EXPERTISE WHILE PROVIDING THE TRAINING NECESSARY TO GAIN INDEPENDENCE. MY PROJECT INVESTIGATES HOW HORMONAL REGULATION OF BILE ACID METABOLISM INFLUENCES CHOLESTEROL HOMEOSTASIS AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF METABOLIC-ASSOCIATED STEATOTIC LIVER DISEASE (MASLD), A PROGRESSIVE DISEASE DRIVEN BY HEPATIC LIPID ACCUMULATION. MASLD HAS INCREASED PREVALENCE IN MEN, BUT INCIDENCE DRASTICALLY INCREASES IN WOMEN AFTER MENOPAUSE. CHOLESTEROL, A KEY DRIVER OF CARDIOMETABOLIC DISEASE, IS NOW EMERGING AS A KEY CONTRIBUTOR TO MASLD. THE PRIMARY ROUTE OF CATABOLISM OF CHOLESTEROL IN THE LIVER IS THE SYNTHESIS OF BILE ACIDS, WHICH ALSO SERVE TO FACILITATE CHOLESTEROL ABSORPTION. USING AAV-CRISPR TOOLS I DEVELOPED, I DISRUPTED THE RATE LIMITING STEP OF BILE ACID SYNTHESIS, CYP7A1, IN MICE. WHILE MALES WERE PROTECTED FROM MASLD, FEMALES EXHIBITED SEVERE HEPATIC CHOLESTEROL ACCUMULATION WITH MASLD-LIKE FEATURES. FURTHER ANALYSIS REVEALED THAT FEMALES WERE STILL PRODUCING SUFFICIENT BILE ACIDS TO ABSORB CHOLESTEROL, WHICH THEN OVERWHELMS THE LIVER. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT FEMALE-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS REGULATING BA SYNTHESIS ARE REQUIRED TO MAINTAIN CHOLESTEROL HOMEOSTASIS AND PREVENT THE LIPID ACCUMULATION THAT LEADS TO MASLD. TO TEST THIS, I HAVE DESIGNED TWO AIMS. I WILL (1) INVESTIGATE FEMALE BILE ACID PRODUCTION FOLLOWING LOSS OF CYP7A1, AND (2) EXAMINE THE ROLE OF ESTROGEN IN MASLD PREVENTION VIA CYP7A1-MEDIATED CATABOLISM OF CHOLESTEROL. THESE STUDIES WILL REFINE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HORMONE-DRIVEN REGULATION OF BILE ACID AND CHOLESTEROL METABOLISM IN MASLD DEVELOPMENT, FIRMLY ESTABLISH MY NICHE IN SEX DIFFERENCES RESEARCH, AND ACCELERATE MY TRANSITION TO AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR.

description: DESIGN, SYNTHESIS AND VALIDATION OF ADVANCED CARBON TRACERS TO IMAGE GLUCONEOGENESIS - ABSTRACT THIS PROPOSAL OUTLINES A COMPREHENSIVE TRAINING AND RESEARCH PLAN FOR DR. MAI THUAN HUYNH TO FURTHER HER ACADEMIC DEVELOPMENT UNDER THE MENTORSHIP OF DRS. CRAIG MALLOY, ZOLTAN KOVACS, AND XIANKAI SUN, WITH ADDITIONAL GUIDANCE FROM DRS. DEAN SHERRY, PHILIPP SCHERER, AND SPENCER BOWEN. THE GOAL IS TO FACILITATE HER TRANSITION TO AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR SPECIALIZING IN METABOLISM AND MOLECULAR IMAGING. TYPE 2 DIABETES IS A GROWING GLOBAL HEALTH CONCERN, CHARACTERIZED BY FASTING HYPERGLYCEMIA DRIVEN BY EXCESSIVE GLUCONEOGENESIS. GLUCOGENIC SUBSTRATES LIKE LACTATE AND AMINO ACIDS MUST FIRST BE CONVERTED TO OXALOACETATE VIA PYRUVATE OR THE TCA CYCLE. THE RATE OF GLUCONEOGENESIS HAS BEEN ESTIMATED USING VARIOUS TRACERS, INCLUDING 14C AND 13C-LABELED MOLECULES. A COMMON FLAW IN THESE STUDIES IS THE ASSUMPTION THAT ALL GLUCOSE IS SYNTHESIZED IN THE LIVER, NEGLECTING THE ROLE OF OTHER ORGANS, PARTICULARLY THE KIDNEYS. THE KEY QUESTION SHE SEEKS TO ADDRESS IN THIS K01 APPLICATION IS: WHERE IS GLUCOSE PRODUCED IN TYPE 2 DIABETES? SHE HYPOTHESIZES THAT RENAL GLUCONEOGENESIS INCREASES DURING DIABETES PROGRESSION, POTENTIALLY RIVALING OR SURPASSING HEPATIC GLUCOSE PRODUCTION. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, METABOLIC FLUXES WILL BE VISUALIZED USING ADVANCED MOLECULAR IMAGING TECHNIQUES IN THESE ORGANS. METABOLIC TRACERS (OXALOACETATE AND LACTATE) WILL BE LABELED WITH CARBON ISOTOPES, 13C OR 11C, ENSURING THAT THEY ARE METABOLIZED IDENTICALLY TO THEIR NATURAL COUNTERPARTS. SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL FOCUS ON THE DEVELOPMENT AND HYPERPOLARIZATION OF CELL-PERMEABLE [1,4-13C2]OXALOACETATE DERIVATIVES TO MEASURE GLUCONEOGENESIS AND TCA CYCLE FLUXES IN DIABETIC MOUSE LIVER AND KIDNEYS USING HYPERPOLARIZED 13C MRI. AIM 2 WILL USE [1-11C]LACTATE POSITRON EMISSION TOMOGRAPHY (PET) TO EVALUATE FLUX THROUGH THE PYRUVATE CARBOXYLASE–PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE (PC–PDH) BRANCH POINT BASED ON TRACER RETENTION KINETICS. AIM 3 WILL ASSESS HOW METFORMIN, THE FIRST-LINE MEDICATION FOR TYPE 2 DIABETES, AFFECTS HEPATIC AND RENAL GLUCONEOGENESIS AND TCA CYCLE ACTIVITY IN DIABETES. NONINVASIVE EVALUATION OF KEY ENZYMES USING 13C MRS, COMBINED WITH WHOLE-BODY GLUCOSE PRODUCTION IMAGING WITH PET AS PROPOSED IN THIS APPLICATION, WILL BE EXTREMELY USEFUL IN DESIGNING PATIENT-TAILORED MEDICATIONS AND MONITORING DISEASE PROGRESSION AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE. HER LONG-TERM CAREER GOAL IS TO DEVELOP TOOLS TO QUANTIFY FLUX IN VIVO THROUGH SPECIFIC ENZYME-CATALYZED REACTIONS, ALLOWING HER TO LEAD TRANSLATIONAL AND CLINICAL RESEARCH PROJECTS IN A MEDICAL ENVIRONMENT. THE ADVANCED METABOLIC IMAGING TOOLS SHE PROPOSES WILL BE APPLICABLE TO SEVERAL OTHER HIGH-IMPACT DISEASES SUCH AS CANCER, HEART FAILURE AND OBESITY, WHICH ARE ASSOCIATED WITH OR CAUSED BY ABNORMAL INTERMEDIARY METABOLISM. AT UT SOUTHWESTERN, SHE WILL BE MENTORED BY INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNIZED LEADERS IN METABOLISM, PET, AND MRI. THIS GUIDANCE, COMBINED WITH HER PREVIOUS EXPERIENCE IN MOLECULAR IMAGING WILL GREATLY FACILITATE MY TRANSITION TO AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR POSITION.

description: A PLACE-BASED FRAMEWORK TO QUANTIFY DRINKING WATER PFAS MIXTURES AND REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH RISKS - PER- AND POLYFLUOROALKYL SUBSTANCES (PFAS) ARE A FAMILY NEARLY 15,000 SYNTHETIC ENVIRONMENTAL CHEMICALS FOUND IN THE BLOOD OF NEARLY ALL AMERICANS AND IN THE DRINKING WATER OF 200+ MILLION AMERICANS. AT THE SAME TIME, INFERTILITY AFFECTS NEARLY 1 IN 7 U.S. COUPLES. TOXICOLOGICAL EVIDENCE INDICATES THAT PFAS MIXTURES CAN IMPAIR ENDOCRINE, IMMUNE, AND METABOLIC FUNCTION, ALL CRITICAL TO FERTILITY. MOST EPIDEMIOLOGIC STUDIES FOCUS ON A SMALL NUMBER OF SERUM-MEASURED “LEGACY PFAS,” LIMITING THEIR ABILITY TO ASSESS “REPLACEMENT PFAS”. DESPITE WIDESPREAD EXPOSURE, THE REPRODUCTIVE CONSEQUENCES OF DRINKING WATER PFAS MIXTURES REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THIS PROPOSAL ADDRESSES A CRITICAL GAP: NO NATIONAL FRAMEWORK CURRENTLY EXISTS TO ESTIMATE DRINKING WATER PFAS MIXTURE AND EVALUATE ITS IMPACT ON REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH AT SCALE. BUILDING ON DR. HU'S NIEHS- FUNDED WORK (P42-ES030990) IN PRIVATE WELL CONTAMINATION MODELING, AIM 1 DEVELOPS A GEOSPATIAL EXPOSURE SURFACE BY INTEGRATING FEDERAL MONITORING (UCMR3/5) AND A 28-STATE DATASET FOR PUBLIC WATER SUPPLIES, AND MACHINE LEARNING PREDICTIVE MODELING FOR PRIVATE WELLS. AIM 2 VALIDATES PREDICTIONS USING CONTEMPORARY CITIZEN SCIENCE TAP WATER DATA FROM SIMPLELAB (2018–2025) AND ASSESSES TEMPORAL TRENDS BY COMPARING TO ARCHIVED SAMPLES FROM THE NURSES' HEALTH STUDY (1989–1990). AIM 3 LINKS ESTIMATED PRECONCEPTION EXPOSURE TO DRINKING WATER PFAS MIXTURES TO FECUNDABILITY IN PREGNANCY STUDY ONLINE (PRESTO, R01-HD086742), A LARGE NORTH AMERICAN PRECONCEPTION COHORT (>23,000 PARTICIPANTS TO DATE). THIS COHORT HAS REMARKABLE GEOGRAPHIC DIVERSITY (SPANNING ALL 50 U.S. STATES) AND RESIDENTIAL STABILITY (<2% OF PARTICIPANTS MOVED DURING PRECONCEPTION PERIOD). ALL CODE, METADATA, AND EXPOSURE SURFACES WILL BE PUBLICLY RELEASED ON THE CAFE COLLECTION OF THE HARVARD DATAVERSE, WITH CLEAR DOCUMENTATION AND UPDATE PLANS. THIS WILL CREATE THE FIRST OPEN, VALIDATED NATIONAL DATASET OF PFAS MIXTURES IN U.S. DRINKING WATER, ENABLING HARMONIZED RESEARCH ACROSS ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH, REPRODUCTIVE EPIDEMIOLOGY, AND CLINICAL RESEARCH. THIS K01 WILL LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM AT THE INTERSECTION OF DRINKING WATER QUALITY, ENVIRONMENTAL DATA SCIENCE, AND REPRODUCTIVE EPIDEMIOLOGY. THE RESEARCH WILL BE USED TO DEVELOP A NATIONAL FRAMEWORK TO ESTIMATE PFAS MIXTURE EXPOSURES FROM DRINKING WATER AND EVALUATE THEIR IMPACT ON FECUNDABILITY (THE PROBABILITY OF CONCEIVING DURING A MENSTRUAL CYCLE). GUIDED BY AN INTERDISCIPLINARY MENTORING TEAM WITH EXPERTISE IN EPIDEMIOLOGY AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH (WELLENIUS, LADEN), REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH (WISE), AND GEOSPATIAL SCIENCE (ANENBERG), DR. HU WILL RECEIVE TRAINING THAT INCLUDES ADVANCED COURSEWORK, MENTORED RESEARCH, DISSEMINATION AT CONFERENCES/SEMINARS, AND GRANT- WRITING. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH ALIGNS WITH NIH PRIORITIES IN WOMEN'S HEALTH AND EXPOSOMICS. BY AWARD END, THE PROJECT WILL DELIVER A VALIDATED NATIONAL PFAS EXPOSURE SURFACE, MULTIPLE PUBLICATIONS, AND A COMPETITIVE R01 APPLICATION TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE PFAS EXPOSURE DURING SENSITIVE WINDOWS FOR HEALTHIER CONCEPTION AND PREGNANCY.
