description: FOOD GENOMICS AND MULTI-OMICS INTEGRATION TO OBJECTIVELY CHARACTERIZE HEALTHY DIETARY PATTERNS AND THEIR ASSOCIATIONS WITH CARDIOMETABOLIC HEALTH - PROJECT SUMMARY  DR. CURTIS TILVES, PHD, IS A RESEARCH ASSOCIATE AT THE LIFECOURSE EPIDEMIOLOGY OF ADIPOSITY AND DIABETES (LEAD) CENTER IN THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO ANSCHUTZ MEDICAL CAMPUS. HE SEEKS A K01 AWARD TO OBTAIN THE SKILL SET, KNOWLEDGE, AND MENTORED RESEARCH EXPERIENCE CRITICAL FOR HIS TRANSITION TO AN INDEPENDENT SCIENTIST WITH A RESEARCH PROGRAM FOCUSED ON USING ‘OMICS TO IDENTIFY: 1) OBJECTIVE BIOMARKERS OF LIFESTYLE FACTORS THAT CAN BE TARGETED FOR IMPROVING CARDIOMETABOLIC HEALTH, 2) MECHANISMS OF CARDIOMETABOLIC DISEASE, AND 3) FACTORS THAT EXPLAIN HETEROGENEITY OF INTERVENTION EFFECTS. ESSENTIAL COMPONENTS OF HIS TRANSITION INCLUDE TRAINING IN (1) THE ABILITY TO CONDUCT AND ANALYZE CLINICAL TRIALS; (2) THE EXPERTISE TO GENERATE, PROCESS, AND ANALYZE DIFFERENT TYPES OF ‘OMICS DATA; AND (3) THE MACHINE LEARNING SKILLS TO INTEGRATE MULTIPLE ‘OMICS MEASUREMENTS.  THE RESEARCH IN THIS K01 AIMS TO LEVERAGE MULTIOMICS, INCLUDING PLANT FOOD GENOMICS, TO QUANTIFY PLANT FOOD DIVERSITY AND ADHERENCE TO THE CARDIOPROTECTIVE DIETARY APPROACHES TO STOP HYPERTENSION (DASH) DIET AND TO USE THESE OBJECTIVE ‘OMICS-ESTIMATED DIET MEASURES TO UNDERSTAND HOW DASH CAN IMPACT CARDIOVASCULAR (CVD) HEALTH. MOST EPIDEMIOLOGIC EVIDENCE INFORMING HEALTHY DIETARY PATTERNS COME FROM SELF-REPORTED DIETARY INTAKE, WHICH HAS SUBSTANTIAL MEASUREMENT ERROR AND SYSTEMATIC BIAS. OBJECTIVE DIETARY BIOMARKERS CAN OVERCOME THESE LIMITATIONS, AND THEIR IDENTIFICATION REMAINS A NATIONAL HIGH PRIORITY FOR NUTRITIONAL RESEARCH. HIGH-DIMENSIONAL ‘OM- ICS DATASETS (E.G., MICROBIOME, METABOLOME) LACK THE SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY FOR CHARACTERIZING DIET. RESIDUAL PLANT FOOD GENOMICS IN FECES MAY PROVIDE MORE SPECIFIC BIOMARKERS FOR CHARACTERIZING DIET, BUT THIS HAS NOT BEEN TESTED IN A RIGOROUS RANDOMIZED FEEDING TRIAL WHERE FOOD IS PROVIDED AND WEIGHT IS ISOCALORICALLY MAINTAINED. THIS K01 WILL LEVERAGE A RANDOMIZED FEEDING TRIAL OF A DASH VS. TYPICAL U.S. DIET (DASH FOR DIABETES, DASH4D) AND A LARGE OBSERVATIONAL COHORT (BALTIMORE LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF AGING, BLSA) TO (1) DISCOVER AND VALIDATE INDIVIDUAL AND INTEGRATED ‘OMICS SIGNATURES (FOOD GENOMIC, MICROBIOME, AND METABOLOME) OF PLANT FOOD DIVERSITY AND DASH DIET, (2) EXAMINE THESE SIGNATURES VS SELF-REPORTED DIET WITH CVD RISK FACTORS, AND (3) TEST IF MULTIOMICS CAN PREDICT AND EXPLAIN INDIVIDUAL CVD RESPONSES TO A DASH DIET.  DR. TILVES WILL CARRY OUT THIS RESEARCH IN THE RICH TRAINING ENVIRONMENT OF THE LEAD CENTER AND THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO. HE WILL BE MENTORED BY DR. NOEL MUELLER, PHD, MPH (LEAD FACULTY AND FORMER K01 AWARDEE), CO- MENTOR DR. DANA DABELEA, MD, PHD (DISTINGUISHED UNIVERSITY PROFESSOR AND DIRECTOR OF THE LEAD CENTER), AND A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM OF SCIENTIFIC ADVISORS. DR. TILVES WILL ALSO ATTEND COURSES, WORKSHOPS, SEMINARS, SCIENTIFIC MEETINGS, AND PARTICIPATE IN STUDY MEETINGS TO FURTHER ENHANCE HIS RESEARCH AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT SKILLS. THIS MENTORED K01 WILL ALLOW DR. TILVES TO ACHIEVE HIS CAREER TRAINING AND RESEARCH AIMS, AND TO GROW INTO AN INDE- PENDENT RESEARCHER WHO LEVERAGES MULTI-OMICS TO IMPROVE CARDIOMETABOLIC HEALTH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A DIGITAL SLEEP INTERVENTION FOR PRESCHOOLERS IN FOSTER CARE - PROJECT SUMMARY CHILDREN IN FOSTER CARE (FC) ARE AT RISK FOR CHRONIC HEALTH CONDITIONS, IN PART DUE TO EXPOSURE TO EARLY LIFE ADVERSITY. EARLY INTERVENTION MAY HELP REDUCE LONG-TERM HEALTH ISSUES AND THE ECONOMIC BURDEN ASSOCIATED WITH EARLY LIFE ADVERSITY, WITH THE PRESCHOOL PERIOD YIELDING A SUBSTANTIALLY LARGER RETURN ON INVESTMENT COMPARED TO INTERVENTIONS ADMINISTERED LATER IN DEVELOPMENT. A MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR TO THE DEVELOPMENT AND EXACERBATION OF CHRONIC HEALTH CONDITIONS ARE SLEEP DISTURBANCES, WHICH ARE COMMON AMONG CHILDREN IN FC, YET WIDELY ACCESSIBLE SLEEP INTERVENTIONS FOR THIS POPULATION ARE NONEXISTENT. THIS K01 PROPOSAL AIMS TO ADDRESS THIS CRITICAL GAP IN CARE THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A TRAUMA-INFORMED DIGITAL PUBLIC-HEALTH-LEVEL SLEEP INTERVENTION, NURTURING SLEEP, WHICH WILL BE ADMINISTERED TO FOSTER CAREGIVERS OF YOUNG CHILDREN AGES 36-71 MONTHS. OUR INNOVATIVE APPROACH INVOLVES COLLABORATION WITH FC WORKERS AND PARENTS, AND EXPERTS IN SLEEP, TRAUMA, HEALTH, AND INTERVENTIONS IN THE CONTEXT OF FC. THE GOAL OF AIM 1 IS TO COLLABORATIVELY DEVELOP AND DIGITIZE INITIAL NURTURING SLEEP INTERVENTION CONTENT, INFORMED BY THE LITERATURE ON TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE, EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES TO SUPPORT HEALTHY SLEEP, FC LICENSING REGULATIONS, AND FOSTER PARENT NEEDS AND EXPERIENCES. IN AIM 2, NURTURING SLEEP WILL BE PRETESTED BY FOSTER CAREGIVERS WHO WILL PROVIDE QUALITATIVE FEEDBACK ON THE INTERVENTION, WHICH WILL BE USED TO MAKE FINAL INTERVENTION MODIFICATIONS. AIM 3 WILL EVALUATE WHETHER NURTURING SLEEP IS ASSOCIATED WITH IMPROVEMENTS IN FOSTER CAREGIVER BEHAVIORS AROUND SLEEP, AND IN CHILD SLEEP FROM PRE TO POST INTERVENTION, AND AT A 3-MONTH FOLLOW-UP. THIS WILL BE THE FIRST LARGE SCALE SLEEP INTERVENTION DEVELOPED AND TESTED IN THIS POPULATION. LOCAL AND NATIONAL STAKEHOLDERS HAVE EXPRESSED ENTHUSIASM AND HAVE COMMITTED TO INVOLVEMENT IN THE DEVELOPMENT, IMPLEMENTATION, AND EVALUATION OF NURTURING SLEEP. TO ACHIEVE THE RESEARCH PLAN, THE PI WILL EXECUTE A STRUCTURED COMPREHENSIVE TRAINING PLAN TO GAIN SPECIALIZED SKILLS IN (1) SLEEP, MENTAL HEALTH, AND ADVERSITY IN EARLY CHILDHOOD IN THE CONTEXT OF FC, (2) DEVELOPING PARTNERSHIPS WITH THE CHILD WELFARE COMMUNITY, (3) INTERVENTION DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE, (4) IMPLEMENTATION AND DISSEMINATION OF DIGITAL INTERVENTIONS, AND (5) DESIGNING, CONDUCTING, AND ANALYZING CLINICAL TRIALS. TRAINING WILL BE OVERSEEN BY AN OUTSTANDING MENTORSHIP TEAM WITH CROSS-CUTTING EXPERTISE IN THESE AREAS AND A TRACK RECORD OF SUCCESSFUL MENTORSHIP EXPERIENCES AND COLLABORATIONS. IMPLEMENTATION OF THE RESEARCH AND TRAINING PLANS WILL ALSO BE BOLSTERED BY SUPPORT FROM THE INSTITUTIONAL ENVIRONMENT, NAMELY BRADLEY HOSPITAL, BROWN MEDICAL SCHOOL, AND TWO MAJOR CENTER GRANTS FOCUSED ON PROMOTING THE CAREER DEVELOPMENT OF EARLY-STAGE INVESTIGATORS IN 1) CHILDHOOD STRESS, TRAUMA, AND RESILIENCE, AND 2) SLEEP AND CIRCADIAN RHYTHMS IN CHILD AND ADOLESCENT MENTAL HEALTH. THIS AWARD WILL CATAPULT PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR DR. DARLYNN ROJO-WISSAR’S TRANSITION TO AN INDEPENDENT TRANSLATIONAL SCIENTIST WITH A CAREER HIGH IN SCIENTIFIC AND PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT IN EARLY LIFE ADVERSITY, SLEEP, AND HEALTH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GENETIC, METABOLIC, AND SOCIODEMOGRAPHIC FACTORS UNDERPINNING PEDIATRIC CARDIAC ARREST: DEVELOPING MECHANISTIC DRIVERS AND INTEGRATIVE FRAMEWORKS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT AFFECTING >20,000 CHILDREN ANNUALLY IN THE UNITED STATES, PEDIATRIC OUT-OF-HOSPITAL CARDIAC ARREST IS FATAL IN >90% OF CASES, OFTEN OCCURRING IN CHILDREN WHO OTHERWISE HEALTHY. WHILE EXISTING RESEARCH FOCUSES ON SINGLE GENE CAUSES, LINKING CARDIAC ARREST TO CARDIAC CHANNELOPATHIES, NEURO-EPILEPTIC, DEVELOPMENTAL, AND METABOLIC ABNORMALITIES, ITS DIAGNOSTIC YIELD REMAINS LOW, SUGGESTING SOME CAUSES MAY BE OLIGOGENIC. ADDITIONALLY, SOCIODEMOGRAPHIC, ENVIRONMENTAL, AND CLINICAL (NON-GENETIC) FACTORS MAY CONTRIBUTE TO RISK, YET IT REMAINS UNCLEAR: HOW 1) HOW GENETICS INTERACT WITH ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL FACTORS TO INCREASE CARDIAC ARREST RISK, 2) WHETHER ABNORMAL METABOLISM UNDERLIES RACE- OR COMMUNITY-BASED DIFFERENCES IN INCIDENCE, AND 3) THE RELATIVE CONTRIBUTIONS OF GENETIC, METABOLIC, AND SOCIODEMOGRAPHIC FACTORS TO OVERALL CARDIAC ARREST RISK. EXPANDING ON OUR PRIOR POPULATION-BASED RESEARCH EVALUATING >900 CHILDREN WITH CARDIAC ARREST, WE WILL FIRST EVALUATE OLIGOGENIC PATTERNS OBSERVED IN A LARGE COHORT OF CHILDREN WITH CARDIAC ARREST, EXAMINING VARIANTS IN GENES ASSOCIATED WITH METABOLIC, CARDIAC, AND NEURODEVELOPMENTAL FUNCTION (AIM 1). TO ADDITIONALLY INVESTIGATE BIOMARKERS DETECTABLE IN EARLY LIFE, WE WILL THEN ASSESS THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN NEWBORN METABOLIC SCREENING RESULTS AND CARDIAC ARREST RISK IN EARLY LIFE (AIM 2). FINALLY, WE WILL GENERATE A COMPREHENSIVE RISK MODEL OF PEDIATRIC CARDIAC ARREST, SIMULTANEOUSLY INTEGRATING GENETIC, METABOLIC, AND COMMUNITY-BASED DATA (AIM 3). USING ONE OF THE MOST COMPREHENSIVE DATA REPOSITORIES AVAILABLE, THIS RESEARCH AIMS TO CLARIFY THE MULTIFACTORIAL DRIVERS OF PEDIATRIC OUT-OF-HOSPITAL CARDIAC ARREST AND INFORM TARGETED PUBLIC HEALTH INTERVENTIONS TO GENERATE MORE ROBUST PRE-ARREST SCREENING MECHANISMS AND IMPROVE POST- ARREST OUTCOMES. WITH THIS RESEARCH, MY OBJECTIVE IS TO CHARACTERIZE THE MULTIFACTORIAL ETIOLOGY OF PEDIATRIC CARDIAC ARREST TO BETTER IDENTIFY EFFECTIVE SCREENING AND PUBLIC HEALTH INTERVENTIONS AIMED AT REDUCING ITS INCIDENCE AND MORTALITY IN AT-RISK CHILDREN. USING STRUCTURED MENTORSHIP, FORMAL TRAINING IN BIOINFORMATICS AND GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY, AND ONGOING COLLABORATIONS WITH THE PROPOSED MULTIDISCIPLINARY PANEL OF EXPERTS, THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL ALLOW ME TO FURTHER CULTIVATE MY EXPERTISE AS A PEDIATRIC EPIDEMIOLOGIST, POSITIONING ME TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR WITH MY OWN UNIQUE EXPERTISE IN PEDIATRIC PUBLIC HEALTH, CARDIAC ARREST, AND GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY.

description: DEFINING CELLULAR CORRELATES OF PROTECTION ACROSS ATTENUATED WHOLE-SPOROZOITE VACCINE PLATFORMS - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT  MALARIA REMAINS A MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH THREAT. HIGHLY EFFICACIOUS MALARIA VACCINES HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY. TWO MALARIA SUBUNIT VACCINES ARE LICENSED, BUT THESE VACCINES HAVE LIMITED EFFICACY AND A SHORT DURATION OF PROTECTION. VACCINES MADE BY ATTENUATING WHOLE MALARIA SPOROZOITES HAVE SHOWN PROMISING EFFICACY AND DURABILITY. HOWEVER, THE IMMUNOLOGIC MECHANISMS OF VACCINE INDUCED PROTECTION HAVE NOT BEEN ESTABLISHED. PREVIOUS STUDIES HAVE SUGGESTED THAT HUMORAL IMMUNE RESPONSES DO NOT CORRELATE WITH PROTECTION; IN CONTRAST, CELLULAR IMMUNE RESPONSES SEEM TO BE VITAL, BUT HAVE YET TO BE ROBUSTLY DEFINED AND REPRODUCED. HIGH-DIMENSIONAL LONGITUDINAL PROFILING OF SPECIMENS FROM CONTROLLED HUMAN MALARIA INFECTION (CHMI) TRIALS PROVIDES A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO DIRECTLY ASSOCIATE CELLULAR IMMUNE RESPONSES WITH PROTECTION.  IN THIS PROJECT, THE CANDIDATE PROPOSES TO COMPARE CELLULAR IMMUNE RESPONSES TO THREE DIFFERENT ATTENUATED WHOLE SPOROZOITE VACCINES IN MALARIA NAÏVE INDIVIDUALS AND CORRELATE THESE RESPONSES WITH PROTECTION AFTER CHMI. SHE WILL ALSO COMPARE CELLULAR IMMUNOGENICITY OF THE LEADING ATTENUATED SPOROZOITE VACCINE (A GENETICALLY ATTENUATED LATE LIVER ARRESTING SPOROZOITE VACCINE) CANDIDATE IN MALARIA NAÏVE AND EXPERIENCED INDIVIDUALS. BY ANALYZING CELLULAR IMMUNE RESPONSES TO THREE DIFFERENT VACCINES IN PERIPHERAL BLOOD COLLECTED DURING FOUR CLINICAL TRIALS, THE CANDIDATE WILL ADDRESS TWO MAIN RESEARCH AIMS: (1) IDENTIFY SHARED AND DISTINCT CELLULAR CORRELATES OF IMMUNOGENICITY AND PROTECTION FOLLOWING VACCINATION WITH THREE DIFFERENT ATTENUATED WHOLE SPOROZOITE VACCINES AND (2) DEFINE THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL PHENOTYPE AND CLONOTYPES OF T CELLS ASSOCIATED WITH PROTECTION. THE PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS OF THIS WORK INCLUDE ELUCIDATING THE CELLULAR IMMUNE MECHANISMS RESPONSIBLE FOR CREATING PROTECTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES FOLLOWING VACCINATION WITH ATTENUATED SPOROZOITES WHICH HAS THE POTENTIAL TO ACCELERATE VACCINE DEVELOPMENT.  THE CANDIDATE IS FIRMLY COMMITTED TO A CAREER IN TRANSLATIONAL VACCINOLOGY AND IS STRONGLY SUPPORTED IN HER CAREER AND RESEARCH GOALS BY HER MENTORS AND HER DIVISION AT THE FRED HUTCH CANCER CENTER. THE CURRENT PROPOSAL INCLUDES A COMPREHENSIVE MENTORSHIP AND DIDACTIC PLAN TO ADVANCE THE CANDIDATE’S SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE IN HIGH-DIMENSIONAL CYTOMETRY, SINGLE-CELL MULTI-OMICS, AND TCR REPERTOIRE ANALYSIS. UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF HER PRIMARY MENTOR, DR. JAMES KUBLIN, AND HER CO-MENTORS, DR. JAMES HEATH AND DR. EVAN NEWELL, SHE WILL ADVANCE HER COMPUTATIONAL AND EXPERIMENTAL IMMUNOLOGY SKILLS. SHE WILL LEVERAGE THE OUTSTANDING ENVIRONMENT AT FRED HUTCH/UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON—SPANNING IMMUNOLOGY CORES, SINGLE-CELL SEQUENCING FACILITIES, AND VACCINE TRIAL NETWORKS—TO ENSURE FEASIBILITY, REPRODUCIBILITY, AND IMPACT. COMPLETION OF THIS COMPREHENSIVE TRAINING PLAN WILL PROVIDE THE CANDIDATE WITH THE SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE NECESSARY TO BECOME A SUCCESSFUL INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR AT THE INTERSECTION OF HUMAN IMMUNOLOGY, VACCINE CLINICAL TRIALS, AND CELLULAR CORRELATES OF IMMUNITY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNDERSTANDING THE LINK BETWEEN INFECTION AND REJECTION IN KIDNEY TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS: DEFINING MECHANISMS OF BK POLYOMAVIRUS REACTIVATION AND HETEROLOGOUS IMMUNITY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT BK POLYOMAVIRUS (BKPYV) REACTIVATION IS A LEADING CAUSE OF ALLOGRAFT INJURY AND LOSS IN KIDNEY TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS. CURRENT APPROACHES RELY ON REACTIVE MONITORING AND REDUCTION OF IMMUNOSUPPRESSION AFTER BKPYV IS DETECTED, YET THESE STRATEGIES CAN PRECIPITATE ALLOSENSITIZATION AND REJECTION. THERE IS AN URGENT NEED TO UNDERSTAND THE MECHANISMS OF BKPYV-SPECIFIC CELLULAR IMMUNITY IN ORDER TO IDENTIFY PATIENTS AT HIGHEST RISK FOR BKPYV REACTIVATION BEFORE TRANSPLANTATION, THUS ENABLING INDIVIDUALIZED IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE STRATEGIES AND TARGETED MONITORING. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO CHARACTERIZE FEATURES OF THE PRE-TRANSPLANT T CELL REPERTOIRE THAT PREDICT BKPYV REACTIVATION AND SUBSEQUENT ALLOGRAFT REJECTION. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE ELEMENTS OF THE T CELL REPERTOIRE—INDEPENDENT OF IMMUNOSUPPRESSION INTENSITY— DIFFERENTIATE RECIPIENTS WHO EXPERIENCE BKPYV REACTIVATION AND ALLOSENSITIZATION FROM THOSE WHO DO NOT. THE RATIONALE FOR THIS PROJECT IS THAT DEFINITION OF HOST CELLULAR IMMUNE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING BKPYV REACTIVATION AND ALLOSENSITIZATION CAN BE LEVERAGED TO RISK-STRATIFY KIDNEY TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS WILL BE TESTED BY PURSUING TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) DEFINE PHENOTYPIC AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL FEATURES OF BKPYV-SPECIFIC T CELLS TO IDENTIFY IMMUNE CORRELATES AND CELLULAR MECHANISMS OF VIRAL REACTIVATION AND 2) ASSESS HETEROLOGOUS IMMUNITY BETWEEN BKPYV-SPECIFIC MEMORY AND ALLOREACTIVE T CELLS. THESE AIMS WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED BY MEANS OF STRUCTURED MENTORSHIP WHEREIN THE APPLICANT WILL ESTABLISH EXPERTISE IN IMMUNOLOGIC LABORATORY METHODS UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF ESTABLISHED INVESTIGATORS AND OBTAIN A SKILLSET IN ADVANCED TRANSPLANT AND COMPUTATIONAL IMMUNOLOGY THROUGH STRUCTURED COURSEWORK. THE RESEARCH PROPOSED IN THIS APPLICATION IS INNOVATIVE IN THAT NOVEL METHODS SUCH AS SINGLE CELL TRANSCRIPTOMICS AND T CELL RECEPTOR SEQUENCING WILL BE APPLIED TO INVESTIGATE MECHANISMS OF BKPYV REACTIVATION AND CROSS-REACTIVITY WITH HUMAN LEUKOCYTE ANTIGENS (HLA). THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT IS EXPECTED TO YIELD A MECHANISTIC FRAMEWORK FOR BKPYV IMMUNE RISK CLASSIFICATION THAT INCORPORATES T CELL SUBSET COMPOSITION, TRANSCRIPTIONAL SIGNATURES, AND HLA PRESENTATION CAPACITY. THIS WORK WILL LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR THE APPLICANT TO LEAD AN R01 PROPOSAL STUDYING HOW A BIOMARKER- GUIDED APPROACH TO IMMUNOSUPPRESSION CAN REDUCE INFECTIOUS COMPLICATIONS AND MITIGATE ALLOIMMUNE INJURY. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION WILL EQUIP THE APPLICANT WITH THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLSET TO DEVELOP A NICHE AS A KIDNEY TRANSPLANT CLINICIAN-SCIENTIST PREPARED TO TRANSITION TO AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: USE OF ANTENATAL DISEASE MODIFYING ANTIRHEUMATIC DRUGS AND MATERNAL-CHILD HEALTH AMONG WOMEN WITH CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY ARTHRITIS - ABSTRACT RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS, AXIAL SPONDYLOARTHRITIS, AND PSORIATIC ARTHRITIS- COLLECTIVELY KNOWN AS CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY ARTHRITIS (CIA), AFFECT 4% OF THE U.S POPULATION. PREGNANCY IS A UNIQUE SITUATION FOR WOMEN WITH CIA, PUTTING THEM AT ALMOST TRIPLE THE RISK OF ADVERSE PREGNANCY OUTCOMES, COMPARED TO THE GENERAL POPULATION. DESPITE GUIDELINES RECOMMENDING CONTINUED USE OF PREGNANCY-COMPATIBLE DISEASE MODIFYING ANTIRHEUMATIC DRUGS (DMARDS) TO CONTROL INFLAMMATION, ALMOST TWO-THIRDS OF PREGNANT WOMEN WITH RHEUMATIC DISEASES DISCONTINUE THERAPY DUE TO CONCERNS ABOUT FETAL SAFETY. WE DO NOT KNOW HOW THIS MAY IMPACT THEIR CHILDREN’S LONG-TERM HEALTH. THIS K08 PROPOSAL WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL EVIDENCE ON WHETHER ADHERING TO DMARDS DURING DIFFERENT STAGES OF PREGNANCY YIELDS BETTER OUTCOMES FOR MOTHERS WITH CIA AND THEIR CHILDREN THAN NONADHERENCE. I AM A BOARD-CERTIFIED RHEUMATOLOGIST AND HOLD A MASTER OF PUBLIC HEALTH DEGREE. MY LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO LEAD AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM THAT HARNESSES REAL-WORLD EVIDENCE AND INNOVATIVE EPIDEMIOLOGIC TECHNIQUES TO GENERATE ACTIONABLE EVIDENCE TO IMPROVE MATERNAL-CHILD HEALTH OUTCOMES AMONG INDIVIDUALS WITH RHEUMATIC DISEASES. ALTHOUGH I HAVE A STRONG CLINICAL BACKGROUND AND TRAINING IN EPIDEMIOLOGY, I REQUIRE ADDITIONAL SKILLS IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS TO ACHIEVE MY LONG-TERM GOALS: (1) PROFICIENCY IN PERINATAL AND PHARMACOEPIDEMIOLOGIC METHODS TO ANALYZE AND INTERPRET DATA FROM LONGITUDINAL MATERNAL-CHILD COHORTS; (2) EXPERTISE IN COHORT STUDY DESIGN, PATIENT RECRUITMENT, AND DATA COLLECTION; AND (3) COMPETENCIES IN TEAM LEADERSHIP AND COLLABORATION. I HAVE CREATED A MULTIDISCIPLINARY MENTORSHIP TEAM AND CURATED A RIGOROUS CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN. MY PROPOSED K08 PROJECT WILL MEET THE TRAINING AIMS IN THE FOLLOWING WAYS: IN THE FIRST AND SECOND AIMS, WE WILL EXAMINE WHETHER DMARD ADHERENCE AT DIFFERENT TRIMESTERS OF PREGNANCY AFFECTS MATERNAL-CHILD HEALTH OUTCOMES AMONG PREGNANT WOMEN WITH CIA. I WILL HARNESS THE STRENGTHS OF US HEALTHCARE ADMINISTRATIVE CLAIMS DATA (MEDICAID) AND DANISH CLINICAL REGISTRIES TO ACHIEVE THE GOAL (TOTAL SAMPLE SIZE OF ~40,000 PREGNANCIES OF WOMEN WITH CIA). THESE DATABASES HAVE COMPLEMENTARY STRENGTHS. MEDICAID FINANCES ABOUT HALF OF ALL PREGNANCIES IN THE US, MAKING IT ONE OF THE LARGEST DATABASES TO STUDY PREGNANCY OUTCOMES ACROSS DIVERSE POPULATIONS. THE DANISH CLINICAL REGISTRIES PROVIDE LONGITUDINAL, PROSPECTIVE CLINICAL DATA ON WOMEN WITH CIA AND THEIR OFFSPRING, ALONG WITH DISEASE ACTIVITY MEASURES DURING PREGNANCY. IN THE THIRD AIM, I WILL DEVELOP A PROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY OF WOMEN WITH CIA BY RECRUITING THEM DURING EARLY PREGNANCY AND CONDUCTING LONGITUDINAL FOLLOW-UPS OF THEIR PREGNANCIES AND OFFSPRING. OVERALL, OUR FINDINGS WILL DIRECTLY INFORM ANTENATAL MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES BY IDENTIFYING THE CRITICAL WINDOW DURING PREGNANCY WHEN DMARD ADHERENCE MOST BENEFITS MATERNAL-CHILD HEALTH AMONG WOMEN WITH CIA. THE RESEARCH EXPERIENCE AND TRAINING FROM THE K08 AWARD WILL EQUIP ME WITH THE SKILLSET TO DEVELOP A MULTIDISCIPLINARY, COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH PROGRAM THAT LEVERAGES REAL-WORLD EVIDENCE TO EVALUATE AND IMPROVE MATERNAL-CHILD HEALTH AMONG INDIVIDUALS WITH RHEUMATIC DISEASES.

description: MAPPING REAL-WORLD CAR T-CELL IMPLEMENTATION TO SUPPORT FUTURE SCALE OUT - DR. DUFFY’S CAREER GOAL IS TO BE AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR IN CLINICAL AND IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE RESEARCH WITH THE SKILLS TO IMPROVE ACCESS AND EFFECTIVELY TRANSLATE NOVEL, EVIDENCE-BASED THERAPIES FOR CHILDREN WITH CANCER GLOBALLY. CHIMERIC ANTIGEN RECEPTOR (CAR) T CELLS WERE FDA-APPROVED FOR PEDIATRIC ALL IN 2017, YET SUBSTANTIAL MULTILEVEL BARRIERS LIMIT ACCESS TO CAR-T IN RESOURCE-CONSTRAINED SETTINGS. THIS AWARD WILL PROVIDE DR. DUFFY WITH THE TRAINING AND RESEARCH EXPERIENCE TO IDENTIFY GENERALIZABLE LESSONS FOR IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES AND DEVELOP TOOLS TO FACILITATE CAR-T PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS A VARIETY OF HEALTHCARE ENVIRONMENTS. USING THE EXPLORATION, PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND SUSTAINMENT (EPIS) FRAMEWORK, AIM 1 WILL ENGAGE FIVE PEDIATRIC ONCOLOGY CENTERS ADMINISTERING CAR-T THERAPY TO IDENTIFY MULTILEVEL DETERMINANTS, STAKEHOLDER NETWORKS, AND IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES ASSOCIATED WITH SUCCESSFUL PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT. EACH OF THESE FIVE CENTERS (TWO IN BRAZIL, ONE IN INDIA, ONE IN SINGAPORE, AND ONE IN VIETNAM) HAS RECENTLY ESTABLISHED UNIQUE APPROACHES TO CAR-T PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT AND PROVIDES EXPERTISE IN PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION ACROSS A VARIETY OF REGULATORY, FINANCING, MANUFACTURING, AND HEALTHCARE DELIVERY ENVIRONMENTS. AIM 2 WILL USE THESE FINDINGS TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE AN IMPLEMENTATION PLANNING TOOLKIT TO FACILITATE FUTURE CAR-T PROGRAM SCALE-OUT. RESEARCH ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE STAKEHOLDER INTERVIEWS AND FOCUS GROUPS, COLLECTION OF PROGRAM-LEVEL IMPLEMENTATION DATA, AND SOCIAL NETWORK ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY THE INFRASTRUCTURE, WORKFORCE, PARTNERSHIPS, AND IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES REQUIRED TO DELIVER CAR-T ACROSS HETEROGENEOUS SETTINGS. ENGAGEMENT WITH THESE SUCCESSFUL “EARLY ADOPTER” CENTERS IS NECESSARY TO IDENTIFY NOVEL STRATEGIES, INFRASTRUCTURE MODELS, AND MANUFACTURING APPROACHES THAT DO NOT CURRENTLY EXIST IN THE UNITED STATES (U.S.) AND MAY INFORM MORE EFFICIENT, SCALABLE, AND ACCESSIBLE CAR-T DELIVERY DOMESTICALLY. THIS RESEARCH DIRECTLY SUPPORTS THE MISSION OF THE NIH AND NCI BY GENERATING EVIDENCE TO ACCELERATE THE ADOPTION OF LESS TOXIC, MORE EFFECTIVE CANCER IMMUNOTHERAPIES AND TO ENSURE REAL-WORLD IMPLEMENTATION KEEPS PACE WITH SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY. FURTHERMORE, IT WILL ALSO PROVIDE IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES TO EXPAND CAR-T ACCESS IN UNDERSERVED AND RESOURCE-CONSTRAINED U.S. HEALTHCARE SETTINGS, IMPROVING SURVIVAL AND REDUCING THE BURDEN OF THE MOST COMMON PEDIATRIC CANCER. THE RESULTS FROM THIS K08 WILL INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF A FUTURE R01 TO EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF THIS CAR-T IMPLEMENTATION TOOLKIT ON CAR-T PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT. THROUGH THE PROPOSED ACTIVITIES, DR. DUFFY WILL ACQUIRE TRAINING IN 1) METHODOLOGIES TO FACILITATE TRANSLATION OF COMPLEX INTERVENTIONS (SOCIAL NETWORK ANALYSIS, QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS, DELPHI METHODOLOGY); 2) GLOBAL POLICY; 3) CLINICAL IMMUNOLOGY; 4) AND LEADERSHIP AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT AT THE INTERSECTION OF PEDIATRIC GLOBAL ONCOLOGY AND IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE. THESE SKILLS WILL GENERATE RIGOROUS, MULTILEVEL EVIDENCE AND STRATEGIES TO SUPPORT THE REAL-WORLD TRANSLATION OF CAR T-CELLS AND FOSTER DR. DUFFY’S TRANSITION TO INDEPENDENCE.

description: DEFINING AND TARGETING EPIGENOMIC DRIVERS OF CONSENSUS TRANSCRIPTOMIC PROGRAMS IN CLEAR CELL RENAL CANCER - PROJECT SUMMARY THIS IS A PROPOSAL FOR A 5-YEAR DEVELOPMENT PLAN TO STUDY EPIGENETIC AND TRANSCRIPTOMICALLY DEFINED BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES AS THERAPEUTIC TARGETS IN CLEAR CELL RENAL CELL CARCINOMA. THE CANDIDATE IS CURRENTLY AN ASSISTANT PROFESSOR OF ONCOLOGY AT THE JOHNS HOPKINS SCHOOL OF MEDICINE. THE PROPOSAL INTEGRATES A MULTI-DISCIPLINARY TEAM OF MENTORS AND COLLABORATORS BRINGING EXPERTISE IN ADVANCED MACHINE LEARNING, KIDNEY CANCER BIOLOGY, EPIGENETICS, AND CANCER DRUG DEVELOPMENT. METASTATIC CCRCC IS A HIGHLY LETHAL DISEASE, WITH FEWER THAN 30% OF AFFLICTED INDIVIDUALS SURVIVING FIVE YEARS AFTER DIAGNOSIS. THE ONCOGENESIS OF CCRCC IS CANONICALLY DRIVEN THROUGH BI-ALLELIC LOSS OF VHL, FOLLOWED BY MUTATIONS IN EPIGENETIC REGULATORS SUCH AS PBRM1 (A COMPONENT OF THE SWI/SNF COMPLEX) AND BAP1 (A HISTONE DEUBIQUITINASE). THOUGH BAP1 MUTATIONS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH POOR OUTCOMES AND AGGRESSIVE DISEASE BIOLOGY, THE ROLE OF PBRM1 MUTATIONS IS CONFLICTING, AND LIKELY REFLECTS A HETEROGENOUS GROUP. OUR LONGTERM GOAL IS TO LEVERAGE THERAPEUTIC VULNERABILITIES GAINED BY SPECIFIC CHROMATIN STATES IN CCRCC. TOWARDS THIS END, WE APPLIED A NOVEL, UNSUPERVISED, COMPUTATIONAL APPROACH TO IDENTIFY CONSENSUS TRANSCRIPTOMIC PROGRAMS (CTPS). MAPPING THESE CTPS ONTO SINGLE-CELL RNA-SEQ DATA REVEALED THAT CERTAIN PROGRAMS ARE HIGHLY ENRICHED IN MALIGNANT EPITHELIAL CELLS AND REFLECT CCRCC-SPECIFIC PROCESSES. NOTABLY, WE IDENTIFIED THREE PBRM1 MUTATION-ENRICHED SUBGROUPS (CTP3, CTP4, AND CTP5) WITH DISTINCT CO-MUTATIONS, GENE EXPRESSION PROFILES, AND SURVIVAL OUTCOMES. ADDITIONALLY, MANY TUMORS WITHOUT DETECTABLE PBRM1 MUTATIONS WERE ENRICHED FOR THESE PBRM1-MUTATION ENRICHED CTPS, SUGGESTING THE PRESENCE OF ALTERNATIVE GENOMIC OR EPIGENOMIC ALTERATIONS WHICH CONVERGE ON A TRANSCRIPTOMIC STATE. FURTHERMORE, CCRCC CELL LINES ENRICHED FOR CTP3—OFTEN HARBORING PBRM1/PTEN CO-MUTATIONS—EXHIBITED UNIQUE SENSITIVITY TO EGLN1 INHIBITORS, WHICH STABILIZE HIF-1Á. THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROPOSAL ARE TO (AIM 1) DETERMINE THE EPIGENETIC AND GENETIC DRIVERS OF PBRM1-MUTATION ASSOCIATED CTPS, AND (AIM 2) DETERMINE THE SENSITIVITY OF CTP3-ENRICHED CCRCC CELL LINES AND PATIENTDERIVED XENOGRAFT MODELS TO HIF-AXIS MODULATION WITH DUAL EGLN1 AND HIF-2Á INHIBITION. AT STUDY COMPLETION, WE EXPECT TO DEFINE THE GENOMIC AND EPIGENOMIC ALTERATIONS CONVERGING ON SPECIFIC CTPS, PARTICULARLY IN PBRM1-MUTANT AND PBRM1-SIMILAR CCRCC, AND TO DETERMINE THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF HIF-AXIS MODULATION. THESE FINDINGS WILL DEEPEN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF PBRM1 MUTANT RCC BIOLOGY, POTENTIALLY EXPLAIN CLINICAL HETEROGENEITY, AND NOMINATE A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY FOR AN AGGRESSIVE SUBSET OF CCRCC. VERTEBRATE ANIMALS (PATIENT-DERIVED XENOGRAFT MOUSE MODELS) ARE REQUIRED BECAUSE THE ANTITUMOR EFFICACY AND PHARMACODYNAMIC EFFECTS OF DUAL HIF-AXIS MODULATION CANNOT BE RECAPITULATED IN CELL-CULTURE SYSTEMS, WHICH LACK AN INTACT TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT, VASCULAR PHYSIOLOGY, AND SYSTEMIC DRUG EXPOSURE. IN VIVO PDX STUDIES ARE THEREFORE ESSENTIAL TO EVALUATE TUMOR REGRESSION AND ON-TARGET HIF PATHWAY ENGAGEMENT IN CTP3-ENRICHED CCRCC.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TRANSFORMING THE PERIPARTUM PERIOD FROM A BREAST CANCER SCREENING “BLIND SPOT” INTO A WINDOW FOR ENHANCED CANCER DETECTION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT BREAST CANCERS DIAGNOSED DURING THE POSTPARTUM PERIOD CONSTITUTE A PARTICULARLY AGGRESSIVE CANCER SUBTYPE WITH POOR PROGNOSIS; PATIENTS ARE TYPICALLY DIAGNOSED AT A MORE ADVANCED STAGE AND HAVE A 60 PERCENT HIGHER RISK OF DEATH COMPARED TO NULLIPAROUS CONTROLS. ALTHOUGH PREGNANCY AND CHILDBIRTH CONFER LONG-TERM PROTECTIVE EFFECTS AGAINST BREAST CANCER, THEY ARE ASSOCIATED WITH AN INCREASED SHORT-TERM RISK OF THE DISEASE. THIS PROBLEM IS COMPOUNDED BY THE LIMITED EFFECTIVENESS OF STANDARD BREAST CANCER SCREENING TESTS (I.E. MAMMOGRAM, ULTRASOUND, MRI) DURING THE PERIPARTUM PERIOD. IN EFFECT, EVERY TIME A WOMAN HAS A BABY, SHE MUST ENDURE A SCREENING BLACKOUT PERIOD/QUASI-BLACKOUT PERIOD OF UP TO TWO YEARS. THERE IS AN URGENT CLINICAL NEED TO DEVELOP BETTER SCREENING TESTS TO SERVE WOMEN DURING THE PERIPARTUM PERIOD. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS WORK IS TO DEVELOP SPECIALIZED BREAST MRI TECHNOLOGY THAT TRANSFORMS THE PERIPARTUM PERIOD FROM A “DIAGNOSTIC BLIND SPOT” INTO A TIME OF ENHANCED DETECTION CAPABILITY. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT PHYSIOLOGICAL CHANGES DURING PREGNANCY AND LACTATION, INCLUDING LOBULAR PROLIFERATION AND LUMINAL DISTENSION WITH SECRETORY MATERIAL, CREATE ENDOGENOUS CONTRAST MECHANISMS THAT CAN BE EXPLOITED BY MRI FOR CANCER DETECTION. TUMOR GROWTH EFFACES THE SURROUNDING MILK-FILLED DUCTS AND LOBULES, A CHANGE IN MICROSTRUCTURE THAT THIS WORK PROPOSES TO CAPTURE WITH A SPECIALIZED MRI ACQUISITION AND BIOPHYSICAL MODELING. IN THIS WORK, PERIPARTUM MRI (PPMRI), A NOVEL NON- CONTRAST MRI TECHNIQUE WILL BE DEVELOPED THAT WILL SAMPLE A RANGE OF ECHO TIMES, DIFFUSION TIMES AND B-VALUES AND THEN SOLVE FOR A DIFFUSION-RELAXATION MODEL TO DISENTANGLE THE UNDERLYING TUMOR AND LUMINAL COMPARTMENTS. THIS WILL ENABLE LUMINAL WATER FRACTION AND LUMINAL DIAMETER MAPPING, IDENTIFYING REGIONS WHERE THE DUCTAL ARCHITECTURE IS EFFACED BY TUMOR, THEREBY ENHANCING CANCER DETECTION. THIS CONSTITUTES A NEW WAY TO VISUALIZE BREAST CANCER ON MRI, TAILORED TO THE UNIQUE PHYSIOLOGY OF THE PERIPARTUM BREAST. AIM 1: CONDUCT NUMERICAL MRI SIMULATIONS TO DEMONSTRATE FEASIBILITY OF MRI-BASED MULTICOMPARTMENT MODELING FOR BREAST CANCER DETECTION DURING LACTATION. A RANGE OF MRI ACQUISITION AND MODELING PARAMETERS WILL BE TESTED TO GENERATE AN OPTIMIZED PROTOCOL. AIM 2: DEVELOP A NOVEL PERIPARTUM MRI (PPMRI) TECHNIQUE USING DIFFUSION-BASED MICROSTRUCTURE IMAGING, SPECIFICALLY TAILORED FOR CANCER DETECTION IN THE PERIPARTUM BREAST. BY APPLYING BIOPHYSICAL MODELING OF MAMMARY GLAND MICROSTRUCTURE, PPMRI WILL ENABLE QUANTITATIVE MAPPING OF LUMINAL DUCT DIAMETER, AN ENDOGENOUS SOURCE OF CONTRAST TO VISUALIZE TUMOR THAT IS EFFACING FLUID-FILLED DUCTS. LACTATING BREAST PHANTOMS WILL BE CONSTRUCTED AND SCANNED FOR QUANTITATIVE VALIDATION OF THE PPMRI TECHNIQUE. AIM 3: ASSESS VISUALIZATION OF SUSPICIOUS LESIONS IN THE LACTATING BREAST USING PPMRI. COMPARE LESION VISIBILITY WITH PPMRI VERSUS STANDARD DCE-MRI, DWI-MRI, MAMMOGRAPHY, AND ULTRASOUND IN A STUDY OF 36 LACTATING PATIENTS WITH RECENTLY DIAGNOSED BREAST CANCER AND/OR SUSPICIOUS LESIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADAPTATION OF AN EVIDENCE-BASED GOALS OF CARE COMMUNICATION INTERVENTION FOR ADOLESCENT AND YOUNG ADULT CANCER PATIENTS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  ADOLESCENT AND YOUNG ADULT CANCER PATIENTS (AYAC) BETWEEN 15-39 EXPERIENCE POOR CARE OUTCOMES AT END OF LIFE (EOL). MORE THAN 50% RECEIVE AT LEAST ONE FUTILE, AGGRESSIVE CARE INTERVENTION (E.G., INTUBATION) IN THE LAST 30 DAYS OF LIFE, UP TO 65% DIE IN ACUTE CARE SETTINGS, AND FEWER THAN 30% ENROLL IN HOSPICE. THE CLINICAL PRACTICE OF GOALS-OF-CARE CONVERSATIONS (GOCC) BETWEEN CANCER PATIENTS AND ONCOLOGISTS IS KNOWN TO PROMOTE HIGH QUALITY EOL CARE. HOWEVER, LESS THAN 20% OF AYAC HAVE GOCC IN THE LAST 2 MONTHS OF LIFE. THIS DEFICIT IS DRIVEN BY INSUFFICIENT GUIDANCE FOR PROVIDERS ABOUT HOW TO TAILOR GOCC FOR DEVELOPMENTAL FACTORS UNIQUE TO AYAC, INCLUDING IDENTITY FORMATION, PURSUIT OF NEW EDUCATIONAL AND VOCATIONAL ENDEAVORS, AND CHANGING INTERPERSONAL RELATIONSHIPS. FOR EXAMPLE, CLINICIANS ARE OFTEN UNSURE HOW TO BALANCE THE PERSPECTIVES OF FAMILY MEMBERS AND AYAC IN GOCC AND FEAR CAUSING AYAC TO LOSE HOPE ABOUT THEIR FUTURE ADULTHOOD. IN PREVIOUS RESEARCH, AYAC DESCRIBE PREFERENCES FOR COMMUNICATION THAT ADDRESSES FACTORS UNIQUE TO THEIR DEVELOPMENTAL STAGE, INCLUDING EFFECTIVE INTEGRATION OF THEIR VOICE WITH FAMILY MEMBERS (E.G., PARENTS), DIRECT AND HONEST DISCUSSIONS ABOUT EOL, AND EMPATHIC, “NORMALIZING” COMMUNICATION. HOWEVER, THESE PREFERENCES ARE NOT CONSISTENTLY INCORPORATED INTO BEST COMMUNICATION PRACTICES FOR AYAC. GIVEN THIS INFORMATION, THERE IS AN URGENT NEED TO TAILOR A GOCC INTERVENTION TO SUPPORT HIGH QUALITY GOCC FOR AYAC. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ADAPT AN GOCC INTERVENTION FOR AYAC. THIS K08 APPLICATION WILL BE THE FIRST TO LEVERAGE ADAPTATION OF A LOW COST, LOW RISK, EVIDENCE-BASED COMMUNICATION INTERVENTION TO IMPROVE CARE QUALITY FOR A SPECIFIC PATIENT POPULATION WITH POOR EOL CARE OUTCOMES USING A MULTI-PHASE PROCESS MODEL FOR ADAPTING INTERVENTIONS. THE FINDINGS FROM THIS PROJECT, ALONG WITH THE PROPOSED MENTORED TRAINING GOALS OF (1) ADAPTATION OF COMMUNICATION INTERVENTIONS IN CANCER CONTROL RESEARCH, (2) EOL CARE NEEDS SPECIFIC TO AYA CANCER PATIENTS, (3) CONDUCTING RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS IN CANCER CONTROL RESEARCH, AND (4) PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, WILL PREPARE ME TO FULLY LAUNCH MY INDEPENDENT PROGRAM OF RESEARCH IN MY FORTHCOMING FACULTY ROLE. THE PROPOSED TRAINING PLAN BUILDS ON AND EXTENDS MY PREVIOUS EXPERIENCE TO SUPPORT EFFECTIVE END-OF-LIFE COMMUNICATION BETWEEN ADULTS ACROSS THE LIFESPAN WITH SPECIFIC COMMUNICATION NEEDS AND THEIR CLINICIANS. THE FINDINGS FROM THIS PILOT TRIAL, ALONG WITH THE PROPOSED CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN AND SUPPORT FROM MY MENTORS (DRS. PATRICIA PARKER AND KELLY MCCONNELL) AND SCIENTIFIC ADVISORS (DRS. ROSARIO COSTAS MUNIZ, ANDREW EPSTEIN, ERIN KROSS, AND ABBY ROSENBERG) WILL PREPARE ME TO SUBMIT AN R01 APPLICATION AT THE END OF YEAR 4 OF THE AWARD PERIOD TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFICACY OF AN ADAPTED GOCC INTERVENTION FOR AYAC IN A FULLY-POWERED RANDOMIZED TRIAL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE ROLE OF HUMAN MILK MIRNA AT THE INTERSECTION BETWEEN MATERNAL HEALTH AND CHILD GROWTH AND IMMUNE DEVELOPMENT - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT MICRORNA (MIRNA) ARE SHORT, NON-CODING RNA THAT ACT AS POST-TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATORS OF GENE EXPRESSION AND HAVE BEEN IMPLICATED IN MANY PATHWAYS IN INFANT DEVELOPMENT. MILK IS ONE OF THE RICHEST SOURCES OF MIRNA IN THE HUMAN BODY, YET WE KNOW VERY LITTLE ABOUT HOW THE MATERNAL ENVIRONMENT IMPACTS MIRNA PROFILES, AND HOW THIS INFLUENCES INFANT DEVELOPMENT. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO A) CHARACTERIZE VARIATIONS IN THE HUMAN MILK MIRNA PROFILE OF MOTHERS WHO ARE UNDERWEIGHT OR HARBOR A HELMINTH INFECTION, AND B) EXAMINE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN MIRNA PROFILE AND BOTH INFANT WEIGHT GAIN AND IMMUNE SYSTEM MATURATION. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL LEVERAGE A WELL-CHARACTERIZED LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF 400 PREGNANT WOMEN AND THEIR INFANTS RESIDING IN THE PHILIPPINES. HENCE, THIS PROPOSAL REQUIRES NO ADDITIONAL SUBJECT RECRUITMENT OR SAMPLE COLLECTION. IN AIM 1 WE WILL DETERMINE THE HUMAN MILK MIRNA PROFILE IN STATES OF MATERNAL DISEASE INCLUDING A) UNDERWEIGHT MOTHERS, WITH THE HYPOTHESIS THAT MOTHERS WHO ARE UNDERWEIGHT WILL HAVE DECREASES IN MIRNA RELATED TO GROWTH, AND B) MOTHERS INFECTED WITH THE HELMINTH SCHISTOSOMA JAPONICUM, WITH THE HYPOTHESIS THAT IMMUNOMODULATORY MIRNA WILL BE DOWN REGULATED. IN AIM 2 WE WILL THEN EXAMINE THE IMPACT OF HUMAN MILK MIRNA ON INFANTS, INCLUDING A) IMPAIRED WEIGHT GAIN, WITH THE HYPOTHESIS THAT MOTHER’S MILK WITH LOW LEVELS OF GROWTH-RELATED MIRNA WILL BE ASSOCIATED WITH INFANT WASTING, AND B) IMMUNE SYSTEM MATURITY, WITH THE HYPOTHESIS THAT INFANTS RECEIVING MILK WITH HIGHER LEVELS OF IMMUNOREGULATORY MIRNA WILL HAVE A MORE MATURE IMMUNE SYSTEM. THE CANDIDATE IS FIRMLY COMMITTED TO A CAREER IN INVESTIGATING THE IMPACT OF HUMAN MILK COMPOSITION ON INFANT GROWTH AND IMMUNE DEVELOPMENT AND IS STRONGLY SUPPORTED IN HER CAREER AND RESEARCH GOALS BY HER MENTORS AND HER DIVISION AT THE WARREN ALPERT MEDICAL SCHOOL OF BROWN UNIVERSITY, WHERE SHE IS AN ASSISTANT PROFESSOR OF EMERGENCY MEDICINE. THE CURRENT PROPOSAL INCLUDES A COMPREHENSIVE CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN INCLUDING HANDS-ON TRAINING, COURSEWORK, AND STRUCTURED MENTORSHIP, TO 1) ACQUIRE THE CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORKS AND SPECIFIC KNOWLEDGE TO UNDERSTAND HUMAN MILK SCIENCE IN RELATION TO MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH, 2) STRENGTHEN SKILLS IN CLINICAL EPIDEMIOLOGY AND BIOSTATISTICS, WITH A FOCUS ON ANALYSIS OF GENOMIC DATA IN RELATION TO HEALTH OUTCOMES, 3) DEVELOP EXPERTISE IN THE CONDUCT OF MIRNA SCIENCE, AND 4) FURTHER CAREER DEVELOPMENT AS AN INDEPENDENT PHYSICIAN SCIENTIST IN GLOBAL MATERNAL CHILD HEALTH RESEARCH. THE CANDIDATE’S PRIMARY MENTOR, DR. JEFFREY BAILEY, AND HER CO-MENTORS, DR. JENNIFER FRIEDMAN, DR. ANN MOORMANN, DR. SARBATTAMA SEN, AND DR. ZHIJIN WU ALL ARE NIH-FUNDED CAREER SCIENTISTS WITH EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN MENTORSHIP OF EARLY STAGE INVESTIGATORS TO RESEARCH INDEPENDENCE. COMPLETION OF THIS COMPREHENSIVE TRAINING PLAN WILL PROVIDE THE CANDIDATE WITH THE SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE NECESSARY TO BECOME A SUCCESSFUL INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR SPECIALIZING IN THE IMPACT OF HUMAN MILK PROFILES IN INFANT GROWTH AND IMMUNE DEVELOPMENT.

description: THERAPEUTIC GENE EDITING NANOPARTICLES FOR SICKLE CELL DISEASE - ABSTRACT THE CURE OF BLOOD DISEASES, SUCH AS SICKLE CELL DISEASE (SCD), REQUIRES USING HEALTHY DONOR (ALLOGENEIC) HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS (HSC) OR GENETICALLY MODIFIED SELF-HSC. TOXIC CHEMOTHERAPY OR RADIATION (I.E., CONDITIONING) IS REQUIRED TO DEPLETE EXISTING STEM CELLS AND MAKE SPACE FOR NEW CELLS. IF THE DONOR IMMUNE SYSTEM (GRAFT) IS NOT MATCHED TO THE RECIPIENT (HOST), POTENTIALLY FATAL GRAFT-VERSUS-HOST DISEASE (GVHD) WILL DEVELOP. THERE IS APPROXIMATELY A 10% MORTALITY RATE FROM CONDITIONING AND GVHD IN THE FIRST 100 DAYS AFTER HSC TRANSPLANTATION (HSCT). THIS MEANS THAT THOSE WHO CAN ACCESS ALLOGENEIC HSCT ARE LIMITED TO HEALTH-CARE INTENSIVE COUNTRIES AND TRADITIONALLY MUST HAVE A MATCHED DONOR, WHICH IS ONLY ~30% FOR CERTAIN U.S. GROUPS. GENE THERAPY, I.E., THE PERSONALIZED CORRECTION OF ONE’S OWN CELLS, CURRENTLY UTILIZES EX VIVO VIRAL TRANSDUCTION OR ELECTROPORATION OF HSC. THIS THEN REQUIRES CONDITIONING TO REMOVE THE DISEASED HSCS THAT REMAIN IN THE BODY BEFORE GENE CORRECTED CELLS CAN BE RETURNED. CURRENT GENE THERAPY UTILIZES SUBOPTIMAL METHODS, VIRAL VECTORS OR ELECTROPORATION, THAT CAUSE CELL TOXICITY AND DELAYED ENGRAFTMENT. >10% OF PATIENTS CANNOT PROVIDE ENOUGH HSC FOR THE CURRENT CLUSTERED REGULARLY INTERSPACED SHORT PALINDROMIC REPEATS (CRISPR)-CAS9-BASED GENE THERAPY FOR SCD. THE LONG-TERM OBJECTIVE OF DEVELOPING NON-VIRAL PLATFORMS FOR LESS TOXIC DELIVERY TO HSC IS THUS CRITICAL FOR CREATING A NEW CLASS OF GENETIC MEDICINES FOR BLOOD DISORDERS. TO DO THIS, NANOPARTICLE (NP)-MEDIATED DELIVERY OF CRISPR-CAS9 WILL BE EXPLORED. IN PRELIMINARY STUDIES, DR. TRIEBWASSER HAS SHOWN THAT POLY(BETA-AMINO ESTER) (PBAE) POLYMERIC NP CARRYING CAS9 CAN EFFICIENTLY EDIT PRIMARY HUMAN HEMATOPOIETIC STEM AND PROGENITOR CELLS (HSPC, CD34+ CELLS) WITH REDUCED TOXICITY COMPARED TO ELECTROPORATION AND WITHOUT AFFECTING ERYTHROPOIESIS. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT PBAE CAS9 NP GENE EDITING OF HSC HAS REDUCED TOXICITY COMPARED TO EXISTING METHODS (I.E., ELECTROPORATION). IN THIS GRANT, DR. TRIEBWASSER WILL DEEPLY CHARACTERIZE THE PHENOTYPE AND NUMBER OF STEM AND PROGENITOR CELL SUBSETS THAT ARE EDITED BY PBAE NP USING FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SINGLE CELL RNA-SEQ. THE FUNCTION OF GENE-EDITED STEM CELLS WILL BE ASSESSED WITH COLONY FORMING ASSAYS AND XENOTRANSPLANTATION (SA1). THE ABILITY OF THIS NP PLATFORM TO GENE EDIT CD34+ CELLS FROM PATIENTS WITH SCD AT THE CLINICALLY VALIDATED BCL11A +58 ERYTHROID ENHANCER FOR GAMMA-GLOBIN REACTIVATION WILL BE ASSESSED IN VITRO AND IN VIVO (SA2). FINALLY, CHEMICAL VARIANTS OF THIS EFFECTIVE POLYMERIC NANOPARTICLE WILL BE STUDIED FOR IMPROVED EFFICACY AND STABILITY (SA3), WITH IN VIVO STUDIES IN THE FUTURE. BY COMPLETING THIS EXPERIMENTAL WORK UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF HIS MENTORS AND ADVISORY TEAM AND PURSUING RELEVANT COURSEWORK, DR. TRIEBWASSER WILL GAIN THE SKILLS NEEDED (PHENOTYPIC AND FUNCTIONAL CHARACTERIZATION OF GENE EDITED HSC, ASSESSMENT OF ERYTHROPOIESIS AND GLOBIN SWITCHING, NP SYNTHESIS AND CHARACTERIZATION, TRAINING IN FUNDING ACQUISITION, AND LABORATORY MANAGEMENT) TO SUCCEED AS AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR. AFTER THIS K08 PERIOD, DR. TRIEBWASSER WILL BE WELL-POSITIONED TO LEAD THE APPLICATION OF NANOMEDICINE-BASED GENE THERAPY TO HEMATOPOIETIC DISEASES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO SCD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HUMAN APOE ISOFORMS DRIVE DIFFERENTIAL REGULATION OF EFFEROCYTOSIS IN HFPEF - HEART FAILURE WITH PRESERVED EJECTION FRACTION (HFPEF) ACCOUNTS FOR HALF OF THE PATIENTS WITH HF AND IS ASSOCIATED WITH SIGNIFICANT MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY; UNFORTUNATELY, FEW EFFECTIVE THERAPIES EXIST. THERE IS INCREASING EVIDENCE THAT HFPEF IS ASSOCIATED WITH A SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATORY STATE. TO UNDERSTAND THE ROLE THAT SPECIFIC IMMUNE CELLS AND SIGNALING PATHWAYS PLAY IN HFPEF, OUR GROUP USED THE SINGLE CELL SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGY IN THE DOCA (DEOXYCORTICOSTERONE ACETATE)-SALT MOUSE MODEL OF HFPEF. WE FOUND PROFOUND ALTERATIONS IN MACROPHAGE TRANSCRIPTIONAL SIGNATURES AND IDENTIFIED APOLIPOPROTEIN E (APOE) AS AN INTERESTING TARGET. APOE HAS PLEIOTROPIC EFFECTS ON BOTH ADAPTIVE AND INNATE IMMUNITY IN MANY DISEASE CONTEXTS, HOWEVER ITS IMPACT ON HFPEF HAS NOT BEEN DEFINED. HUMANS HAVE THREE COMMON GENETIC VARIANTS OF APOE – APOE2, APOE3, AND APOE4. OF THESE, APOE3 IS THE MOST COMMON (65-70%) AND CONSIDERED THE NEUTRAL VARIANT. APOE4 OCCURS IN 15-20% AND APOE2 OCCURS IN 5-10% OF THE POPULATION. WE FOUND THAT PATIENTS WITH THE APOE4 ALLELE ARE LESS LIKELY TO DEVELOP HFPEF IN BIOVU (VANDERBILT’S DNA BIOBANK) AND APOE2/E2 PATIENTS HAVE AN INCREASED RISK FOR HFPEF IN ALL OF US (NIH’S BIOBANK). USING MICE WITH TARGETED REPLACEMENT OF THE ENDOGENOUS MURINE APOE BY HUMANIZED APOE (APOE-TR), WE RECAPITULATE SOME OF THESE FINDINGS. IN ADDITION, WE SHOW THAT THE APOE ISOFORMS ALTERS THE EFFEROCYTIC CAPACITY OF MACROPHAGES. EFFEROCYTOSIS, THE CLEARANCE OF APOPTOTIC CELLS BY MACROPHAGES, IS AN ESSENTIAL PROCESS IN MANY DISEASE PATHOLOGIES, BUT ITS ROLE IN HFPEF IS UNKNOWN. THESE NOVEL PRECLINICAL AND CLINICAL PRELIMINARY DATA LED US TO HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE HUMAN GENETIC VARIANTS OF APOE CONFERS DIFFERENTIAL RISK FOR HFPEF DEVELOPMENT AND PROGRESSION THROUGH ITS IMMUNOMODULATORY FUNCTIONS. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS THROUGH THREE AIMS. IN THE FIRST, WE WILL ASSESS THE HFPEF PHENOTYPE OF APOE -TR MICE IN THE DOCA-SALT MODEL AND PROFILE THE CARDIAC IMMUNE CELLS. WE WILL THEN TEST THE RELATIVE CONTRIBUTION OF HEMATOPOIETIC PRODUCED APOE TO THE HFPEF PHENOTYPE BY TRANSPLANTING APOE-TR BONE MARROW INTO IRRADIATED WILD TYPE MICE. IN THE SECOND, WE WILL ESTABLISH THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH APOE ISOFORMS REGULATE MACROPHAGE EFFEROCYTOSIS AND ITS FUNCTIONAL CONSEQUENCES IN APOE-TR MACROPHAGES. WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE THE DIFFERENCES IN EFFEROCYTOSIS ACROSS APOE- TR MICE AFTER DOCA-SALT. IN THE THIRD, WE WILL EXAMINE HOW APOE GENETIC VARIANTS MODULATE RISK FOR HFPEF IN HUMANS BY EXPANDING PRELIMINARY FINDINGS TO MORE HETEROGENOUS COHORTS AND EVALUATE EFFECTS ON HFPEF PROGRESSION BY EXAMINING HF OUTCOMES. WE WILL ALSO EXPLORE THE ASSOCIATION OF THE GENETIC VARIANTS WITH CARDIAC STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION IN PRE-HF POPULATIONS. RESULTS FROM THE PROPOSED RESEARCH PLAN WILL FURTHER OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF HFPEF AND POTENTIALLY IDENTIFY APOE AS A NOVEL MEDIATOR. FURTHERMORE, SKILLS THE PI WILL DEVELOP THROUGH MENTORED EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND FORMAL DIDACTICS WILL ALLOW HER TO ACHIEVE HER CAREER GOAL OF BECOMING AN INDEPENDENT PHYSICIAN-SCIENTIST INVESTIGATING THE IMMUNE MECHANISMS OF HFPEF WITH THE EXPERTISE OF TRANSLATING FINDINGS FROM ANIMAL MODELS TO HUMAN PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DECIPHERING THE GENETIC ARCHITECTURE OF HEART FAILURE WITH PRESERVED EJECTION FRACTION - PROJECT SUMMARY OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, ADVANCES IN SEQUENCING, STATISTICAL METHODS, AND MACHINE LEARNING HAVE TRANSFORMED OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE GENETIC BASIS OF DISEASE. YET, PROGRESS ACROSS DISEASES HAS NOT BEEN EVEN: MORE THAN 300 LOCI HAVE BEEN DISCOVERED FOR CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE, BUT ONLY TWO FOR HEART FAILURE WITH PRESERVED EJECTION FRACTION (HFPEF). GIVEN THAT THERE ARE NO TRULY DISEASE-MODIFYING TREATMENTS AND GENOMIC INSIGHTS TRIPLE DRUG DISCOVERY SUCCESS, THERE ARE URGENT CALLS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HFPEF GENETICS. THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DECIPHER THE GENETIC ARCHITECTURE OF HFPEF AND IDENTIFY NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS. CURRENT LIMITATIONS FOR HFPEF GENOMIC DISCOVERY INCLUDE IMPRECISE PHENOTYPING, LACK OF ECHOCARDIOGRAMS IN BIOBANKS, AND PARSIMONIOUS USE OF BIOLOGICAL DATA TO DEFINE HFPEF. DR. O’SULLIVAN’S PRELIMINARY DATA BEGINS TO ADDRESS THESE LIMITATIONS. HE DEVELOPED A MODEL TRAINED TO PREDICT HFPEF FROM 40 BIOMARKERS AND DEPLOYED THIS MODEL TO THE UK BIOBANK, ASSIGNING A PREDICTED HFPEF PROBABILITY TO THE ~500K PARTICIPANTS. USING THESE PROBABILITIES AS INPUT FOR A GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDY (GWAS), HE IDENTIFIED OVER 50 HFPEF LOCI. THIS WORK DEMONSTRATES THE FEASIBILITY OF HIS MACHINE LEARNING APPROACH AND PROVIDES DATA FOR PRIORITIZING CAUSAL LOCI. HOWEVER, HIS CURRENT MODEL LACKS CRITICAL CARDIAC DATA: ECGS AND IMAGING, AND IT REMAINS UNCLEAR WHICH OF THE IDENTIFIED LOCI REPRESENT NOVEL THERAPEUTIC PATHWAYS. TO ADDRESS THESE UNMET NEEDS, AIM 1 WILL ENHANCE HIS MACHINE LEARNING MODEL BY INCORPORATING CARDIAC MRIS AND ECGS. THESE CARDIAC-SPECIFIC DATA WILL IMPROVE MODEL SPECIFICITY, FACILITATING ENHANCED GENOMIC DISCOVERY. AIM 2 WILL REDEFINE DIASTOLIC FUNCTION ASSESSMENT USING VISION ENCODERS. THESE MODELS WILL EXTRACT BIOLOGICAL FEATURES FROM FULL DIASTOLIC ECHOCARDIOGRAM IMAGES TO GENERATE NOVEL DIASTOLIC SCORES FOR EACH PATIENT, WHICH WILL THEN BE USED AS INPUT FOR GWAS USING LINKED GENETIC DATA. THIS WILL BE THE FIRST EFFORT TO DEFINE THE GENOMICS OF DIASTOLIC DYSFUNCTION, A HALLMARK OF HFPEF. AIM 3 WILL IDENTIFY CAUSAL GENE-PROTEIN PATHWAYS DYSREGULATED IN HFPEF THROUGH PROTEOMICS AND MENDELIAN RANDOMIZATION. THE PROPOSED DIDACTIC AND APPLIED PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT EXPERIENCES, INCLUDING TRAINING IN ADVANCED MACHINE LEARNING AND GENOMICS, WILL FACILITATE DR. O’SULLIVAN’S TRANSITION TO SCIENTIFIC INDEPENDENCE. HIS MENTORSHIP TEAM, LED BY DR. EUAN ASHLEY, INCLUDES EXPERTS IN HEART FAILURE (LEWIS, ADVISOR), MACHINE LEARNING (CHAUDHARI AND PIRRUCCELLO, ADVISORS), COMPUTER SCIENCE (RIVAS, MENTOR AND CHAUDHARI, ADVISOR), AND STATISTICAL GENOMICS (ASSIMES AND RIVAS, ADVISORS). THE RESEARCH AND TRAINING PLAN PROPOSED IN THIS K08 APPLICATION WILL DEVELOP DR. O’SULLIVAN INTO A UNIQUE AND HIGHLY SKILLED PHYSICIAN-SCIENTIST, READY TO COMPETE FOR R-LEVEL FUNDING AND LAUNCH HIS INDEPENDENT CAREER IN COMPUTATIONAL GENOMICS RESEARCH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A PILOT RCT OF A DIGITALLY-ENHANCED COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER-LED INTERVENTION FOR EARLY STEPPED PALLIATIVE CARE IN HEPATOBILIARY CANCERS - HEPATOPANCREATOBILIARY (HPB) CANCERS WILL BECOME THE PRIMARY CAUSE OF CANCER MORTALITY BY 2030. THESE PATIENTS HAVE SUBSTANTIAL MORBIDITY, INCLUDING HIGH SYMPTOM BURDEN AND POOR QUALITY OF LIFE. WHILE EARLY PALLIATIVE CARE (PC) CAN IMPROVE SYMPTOMS AND QUALITY OF LIFE, THERE ARE LOW RATES OF PC UTILIZATION IN HPB CANCERS, WITH PC PRIMARILY BEING USED AT THE END OF LIFE, LIMITING THE BREADTH OF ASSISTANCE PC CAN OFFER. THUS, INNOVATIVE, EQUITABLE, AND SCALABLE, COMMUNITY-BASED PC INTERVENTIONS ARE NEEDED TO FACILITATE EARLY PC IN PATIENTS WITH HPB MALIGNANCIES. COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS (CHWS) ARE FRONTLINE PUBLIC HEALTH WORKERS TRUSTED BY THE COMMUNITIES THEY SERVE. IN PRELIMINARY STUDIES, WE DEVELOPED A DIGITALLY ENHANCED CHW-LED INTERVENTION THAT DELIVERS EARLY-STAGE PC CARE, NAVIGATION, AND CLINICAL TRIAL ENGAGEMENT, AND PROVIDES RESOURCES TO HELP ALLEVIATE THE FINANCIAL BURDEN OF CANCER TREATMENT (PAL-CHW-PDAC INTERVENTION). THIS INTERVENTION WAS FEASIBLE AND ACCEPTABLE AND REDUCED SYMPTOM BURDEN IN A PILOT STUDY. HOWEVER, HEPATOBILIARY (HB) CANCERS HAVE DISTINCT DIFFERENCES FROM PDAC, INCLUDING UNDERLYING LIVER DYSFUNCTION CONTRIBUTING TO SYMPTOMS AND LIMITING PALLIATIVE PROCEDURES AND MEDICATIONS, AND IMPROVED PROGNOSIS IN EARLY-STAGE AND INTERMEDIATE-STAGE PATIENTS REQUIRING A TAILORED INTERVENTION. THE CURRENT PROPOSAL WILL ADAPT THE PRIOR PAL-CHW-PDAC INTERVENTION TO PATIENTS/CAREGIVERS WITH HB CANCERS. WE WILL FIRST USE KEY INFORMANT INTERVIEWS TO CAPTURE PATIENT, CAREGIVER, AND CHW PERSPECTIVES TOWARD THE DISEASE COURSE, TREATMENTS, AND ROLE OF PC IN HB CANCERS. WE WILL THEN UTILIZE THESE PERSPECTIVES, ALONG WITH INPUT FROM HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS, TO ADAPT THE PAL-CHW-PDAC INTERVENTION FOR HEPATOBILIARY CANCERS. WE WILL SUBSEQUENTLY CONDUCT A PILOT FEASIBILITY STUDY WITH 24 PATIENTS TO ASSESS ITS FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY, FOLLOWED BY A PILOT RCT ENROLLING 70 PATIENTS/CAREGIVERS TO GET A PRELIMINARY ESTIMATE OF EFFICACY. THE CANDIDATE'S OVERALL CAREER GOALS ARE TO DESIGN AND LEAD CLINICAL TRIALS, COMPARATIVE EFFECTIVENESS, AND IMPLEMENTATION STUDIES FOR PC INTERVENTIONS. THE CAREER DEVELOPMENT GOALS INCLUDE DEVELOPING EXPERTISE IN IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE, INCLUDING ADVANCED QUALITATIVE METHODOLOGY, CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN, AND USING FRAMEWORKS TO DESIGN AND ADAPT INTERVENTIONS. THIS TRAINING PLAN INCLUDES STRONG MENTORSHIP, FORMAL COURSEWORK, INCLUDING COMPLETING A CERTIFICATE IN IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE, SEMINARS, AND LABORATORY MEETINGS TO EXECUTE THIS CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN. THIS PROPOSAL INVESTIGATES A POTENTIALLY TRANSFORMATIVE INTERVENTION THAT ADDRESSES THE CRITICAL GAP IN EARLY PC UTILIZATION IN HPB MALIGNANCIES FOR EARLY DETECTION AND INTERVENTION FOR SYMPTOMS. THIS REPRESENTS THE BLUEPRINT FOR DEVELOPING THE APPLICANT INTO AN INDEPENDENT CLINICAL INVESTIGATOR.

description: IMPROVING GUIDANCE FOR CARE TRANSITIONS FOR CLIENTS OF ASSERTIVE COMMUNITY TREATMENT (ACT) AND FLEXIBLE ACT - PROJECT SUMMARY  ASSERTIVE COMMUNITY TREATMENT (ACT) IS A TIME-UNLIMITED INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM MODEL OF INTENSIVE OUTPATIENT CARE WITH DEMONSTRATED EFFECTIVENESS FOR TREATING PEOPLE WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS AND COMPLEX NEEDS SUCH AS HOMELESSNESS, FORENSIC INVOLVEMENT, OR SUBSTANCE USE. HOWEVER, MANY MATURE ACT PROGRAMS NOW HAVE LOW TURNOVER AND LONG WAITING LISTS, LIMITING PROGRAM REACH. UNCERTAINTY ABOUT A CLIENT'S FUTURE STABILITY IS A LIMITATION TO DISCHARGING CLIENTS FROM ACT, DUE TO THE DIFFICULTY OF REESTABLISHING CARE FOLLOWING DISCHARGE. IN ADDITION, THERE HAS BEEN INCREASING INTEREST IN ADOPTION OF PROCEDURES SUCH AS TIERED STEPDOWN THAT ALLOW ACT TEAMS TO DECREASE SERVICE INTENSITY WITHOUT NECESSITATING DISCHARGE FROM THE PROGRAM. THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL INFORM EFFORTS TO REDUCE UNCERTAINTY AROUND DISCHARGE PRACTICES IN ACT BY ASSESSING PREDICTORS OF PSYCHIATRIC HOSPITALIZATION FOLLOWING ACT DISCHARGE AND BY SURVEYING ACT TEAMS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND VARIATION IN THEIR DISCHARGE PRACTICES.  THE SPECIFIC AIMS OF THE STUDY ARE (1) TO IDENTIFY CLIENT CHARACTERISTICS THAT PREDICT RISK OF PSYCHIATRIC HOSPITALIZATION DURING THE 12 MONTHS FOLLOWING ACT DISCHARGE, (2) TO ESTIMATE THE EFFECT OF CARE STEPDOWN WITHIN ACT ON 12-MONTH POST-DISCHARGE PSYCHIATRIC HOSPITALIZATION RISK, (3) TO CONDUCT A SURVEY TO UNDERSTAND VARIATION IN DISCHARGE RESOURCES AND PRACTICES BETWEEN ACT TEAMS AND CORRELATE THESE DIFFERENCES WITH POST- DISCHARGE OUTCOMES.  WE WILL ADDRESS THESE AIMS BY LINKING DATA FOR THE OVER 22,000 CURRENT AND PREVIOUS ACT PARTICIPANTS ACROSS NEW YORK STATE MEDICAID AND THE CHILD AND ADULT INTEGRATED REPORTING SYSTEM (CAIRS), AN ADMINISTRATIVE DATABASE COLLECTED EVERY 6-MONTHS BY ACT TEAMS. description: MULTIOMIC AND SPATIAL REGULATION OF HIPPOCAMPAL RADIAL GLIA AND SUBFIELD SPECIFICATION - PROJECT SUMMARY MANY NEUROPSYCHIATRIC ORDERS HAVE NEURODEVELOPMENTAL ORIGINS THAT FEATURE CORTICAL DYSFUNCTION. ALTHOUGH THE HIPPOCAMPUS IS A CORTICAL TISSUE THAT PLAYS KEY ROLES IN THESE DISORDERS, ITS DEVELOPMENTAL ROLE IN NEUROPSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS REMAINS LARGELY UNEXPLORED. THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP EXISTS IN PART BECAUSE THE HIPPOCAMPAL DEVELOPMENT IN HEALTHY INDIVIDUALS IS POORLY UNDERSTOOD AS WELL. THE MECHANISMS THAT DRIVE DIVERGENCE OF THE HIPPOCAMPUS AND NEOCORTEX IN THE DORSAL TELENCEPHALON AND THE MOLECULAR MACHINERY THAT SPECIFIES CORTICAL PROGENITORS ALONG A HIPPOCAMPAL SUBFIELD LINEAGE REMAIN LARGELY A MYSTERY. TO IDENTIFY THESE REGULATORS, WE PROPOSE A PAIRED APPROACH THAT DEPLOYS MULTI-OMICS PROFILING INCLUDING SNRNA-SEQ, SNATAC- SEQ, AND SPATIAL SEQUENCING ON IN VIVO FETAL TISSUE FROM HUMAN HIPPOCAMPUS AND NEOCORTEX (GESTATIONAL WEEKS 16 TO 24) AND HIPSC-DERIVED 3D IN VITRO HIPPOCAMPAL AND NEOCORTICAL ORGANOIDS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL USE IN VITRO HIPPOCAMPAL ORGANOIDS TO STUDY THE ROLE OF WNT AND BMP SIGNALING IN COMMITTING CORTICAL RADIAL GLIA TO THE HIPPOCAMPAL LINEAGE. IN AIM 2, WE WILL UTILIZE SPATIAL SEQUENCING ON DEVELOPING FETAL HIPPOCAMPUS TO IDENTIFY NOVEL MARKERS THAT DEFINE THE SUBFIELDS, IDENTIFY THE CELL TYPES THAT ARE PRESENT AND ABSENT IN THE HIPPOCAMPAL ORGANOID, THEN VALIDATE NEWLY IDENTIFIED AND CANDIDATE PATHWAYS IN THE HIPPOCAMPAL ORGANOID TO CONTROL SUBFIELD FATE SPECIFICATION WITHIN THE ORGANOID. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS STUDY WILL MOLECULARLY DEFINE HIPPOCAMPAL RADIAL GLIA AS A UNIQUE CELL FATE, IDENTIFY REGULATORS OF THE SUBFIELDS, AND PRODUCE A COMPREHENSIVE IN VIVO AND IN VITRO MULTI-OMICS ATLAS OF THE DEVELOPING HIPPOCAMPUS THAT ESTABLISHES THE HIPPOCAMPAL ORGANOID AS A POWERFUL TOOL FOR MODELING DEVELOPMENT AND DISEASE.

description: DETECTING MALIGNANCY AND TREATMENT RESPONSE IN NF1-PERIPHERAL NERVE SHEATH TUMORS THROUGH CFDNA FRAGMENTOMICS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT MALIGNANT PERIPHERAL NERVE SHEATH TUMORS (MPNSTS) ARE AGGRESSIVE MALIGNANCIES AND THE LEADING CAUSE OF MORTALITY AMONG INDIVIDUALS WITH NEUROFIBROMATOSIS TYPE 1 (NF1), A COMMON GENETIC DISORDER AFFECTING APPROXIMATELY 1 IN 2,500 PEOPLE. MPNSTS OFTEN ARISE FROM PRE-EXISTING PLEXIFORM NEUROFIBROMAS (PNS), YET CLINICALLY IDENTIFYING THIS MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION REMAINS DIFFICULT. AS A RESULT, TUMORS ARE LARGE AT PRESENTATION, TREATMENT OPTIONS ARE LIMITED, AND SURVIVAL OUTCOMES ARE POOR. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO DEVELOP NONINVASIVE CELL-FREE DNA (CFDNA) BIOMARKERS FOR EARLY DETECTION AND TREATMENT MONITORING OF NF1-ASSOCIATED MPNSTS. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT INTEGRATED CFDNA EPIGENOMIC FEATURES CAN DETECT MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION AND TRACK TREATMENT RESPONSE EARLIER AND MORE SPECIFICALLY THAN CURRENT CLINICAL TOOLS. THIS WORK WILL LEVERAGE CFDNA METHYLATION PATTERNS AND INFERRED NUCLEOSOME POSITIONING, WHICH REFLECT THE TUMOR’S EPIGENETIC STATE AND GENE EXPRESSION. A CFDNA MALIGNANCY RISK SCORE WILL QUANTIFY MALIGNANT POTENTIAL ACROSS THE FULL SPECTRUM OF PERIPHERAL NERVE SHEATH TUMORS (PNSTS) FROM BENIGN PN TO MPNST. IN PARALLEL, PATIENT-DERIVED XENOGRAFT (PDX) MODELS WILL BE USED TO RELATE CFDNA TRAJECTORIES FROM SERIAL NONTERMINAL SAMPLES TO TUMOR GROWTH AND PATHWAY ACTIVITY DURING TARGETED THERAPY, PROVIDING A FRAMEWORK FOR MONITORING TREATMENT RESPONSE AND RESISTANCE IN REAL TIME. THE CANDIDATE’S CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN IS DESIGNED TO ESTABLISH HIM AS AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR LEADING A CFDNA RESEARCH PROGRAM FOR NF1 AND RELATED HEREDITARY CANCER SYNDROMES. UNDER THE MENTORSHIP OF DR. AADEL CHAUDHURI, AN EXPERT IN CFDNA ANALYSIS, AND OTHER LEADERS IN PRECLINICAL MODELING AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH, HE WILL RECEIVE TARGETED TRAINING IN CFDNA FRAGMENTOMICS AND EPIGENOMICS, PDX MODELING, ADVANCED BIOINFORMATICS, AND CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN. THE MAYO CLINIC ENVIRONMENT, WITH STRONG INFRASTRUCTURE FOR GENOMIC ANALYSIS AND CLINICAL ASSAY DEVELOPMENT, WILL SUPPORT BOTH HIS SCIENTIFIC GROWTH AND THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE PROPOSED STUDIES. BY ADVANCING NONINVASIVE CFDNA DIAGNOSTICS AND TREATMENT MONITORING FOR NF1-ASSOCIATED MPNSTS, THIS WORK ADDRESSES A CRITICAL UNMET NEED: TIMELY DETECTION AND EFFECTIVE MONITORING OF MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION AND TREATMENT RESPONSE IN A HIGH-RISK POPULATION. IMPROVED EARLY DETECTION AND PRECISE MONITORING HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO SIGNIFICANTLY ENHANCE OUTCOMES AND SURVIVAL FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH NF1, IN ALIGNMENT WITH THE MISSION TO REDUCE THE BURDEN OF NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE.

description: INVESTIGATING MUCOSAL AND PERIPHERAL IMMUNE CORRELATES OF PROTECTION AGAINST PEDIATRIC INFLUENZA VIRUS - ABSTRACT INƲUENZA VIRUS INFECTIONS ARE TYPICALLY MILD BUT CAN CAUSE SEVERE RESPIRATORY ILLNESS IN INFANTS AND THE ELDERLY. RECENT EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT THIS POLARIZATION IN INƲUENZA SEVERITY MAY BE DRIVEN BY AGE-DEPENDENT VARIATIONS IN MAGNITUDE, FUNCTION, AND COMPOSITION OF PROTECTIVE IMMUNE FACTORS, TERMED CORRELATES OF PROTECTION (COP), ACROSS CIRCULATING AND MUCOSAL IMMUNE SITES. FOR DECADES, MEASURES OF PERIPHERAL ANTIBODY TITERS AGAINST INƲUENZA VIRUS HAVE DEFLNED COP AND ARE THE STANDARD METRICS TO COMPARE VACCINE QUALITY. HOWEVER, CELLULAR COP, WHETHER WORKING INDEPENDENTLY OR IN SYNC WITH SEROLOGY, HAD NOT BEEN FLRMLY ESTABLISHED. AS A POSTDOC, I LED NIAID F32-FUNDED STUDIES INVESTIGATING CELLULAR AND SEROLOGIC RESPONSES TO INƲUENZA VIRUS INFECTION AND VACCINATION. IN A RECENT NATURE IMMUNOLOGY ARTICLE, WE USED STATISTICAL AND PREDICTIVE MODELING TO DEFLNE PROTECTION- AND SUSCEPTIBILITY-ASSOCIATED CELL PROFLLES FROM ADULT PERIPHERAL BLOOD AND FOUND THAT INNATE AND T CELL POPULATIONS OUTPERFORMED TRADITIONAL SEROLOGY IN PREDICTING SYMPTOMATIC INƲUENZA RISK. INDEED, MUCH OF WHAT WE KNOW ABOUT INƲUENZA COP COMES FROM ADULT STUDIES AND IT IS UNKNOWN IF SIMILAR CIRCULATING OR MUCOSAL RESPONSES WILL CORRELATE WITH FAVORABLE OUTCOMES IN CHILDREN. GIVEN THAT INƲUENZA TARGETS THE RESPIRATORY TRACT, EXAMINING BOTH SYSTEMIC AND MUCOSAL IMMUNITY IS CRITICAL FOR UNDERSTANDING PROTECTIVE MECHANISMS. THIS K22 PROPOSAL WILL LEVERAGE A SUITE OF IMMUNOMIC, FUNCTIONAL, AND COMPUTATIONAL APPROACHES DEVELOPED DURING MY POSTDOC TO DEFLNE IMMUNOLOGICAL PREDICTORS OF DIVERSE INƲUENZA OUTCOMES IN PEDIATRIC POPULATIONS. SPECIFLCALLY, WE ARE INTERESTED IN ANSWERING TWO OUTSTANDING QUESTIONS REGARDING PEDIATRIC IMMUNITY TO INƲUENZA: WHAT ARE THE CIRCULATING- AND MUCOSAL-ASSOCIATED IMMUNE RESPONSES THAT PREDICT INƲUENZA OUTCOMES IN CHILDREN? CAN MEASURES OF CIRCULATING IMMUNITY BE USED TO EVALUATE MUCOSAL IMMUNE RESPONSES DURING ACUTE INƲUENZA? ENABLING THESE PROPOSED EFFORTS ARE COLLABORATIONS WITH THREE ESTABLISHED HUMAN COHORT STUDIES, WHICH HAVE AGREED TO PROVIDE HUNDREDS OF BANKED PERIPHERAL AND RESPIRATORY SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM CHILDREN PRIOR TO AND FOLLOWING INƲUENZA EXPOSURES. BUILDING ON MY PREVIOUS WORK ON CORRELATES OF PROTECTION IN ADULTS, AIM 1 WILL USE SIMILAR FUNCTIONAL, COMPUTATIONAL, AND PREDICTIVE MODELING METHODS TO DEFLNE BASELINE COPS AND IMMUNE PREDICTORS OF INƲUENZA SEVERITY IN CHILDREN FROM (I) PERIPHERAL AND (II) RESPIRATORY SAMPLES. AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN SYSTEMIC AND MUCOSAL IMMUNE RESPONSES, BY DETERMINING WHETHER SYSTEMIC IMMUNE MEASURES CAN ACT AS TRANSLATORS OF MUCOSAL RESPONSES. USING PAIRED NASAL WASH AND BLOOD SAMPLES WE WILL (I) IDENTIFY CIRCULATING IMMUNE SIGNATURES THAT PREDICT A DEFLNED MUCOSAL RESPONSE SCORE IN CHILDREN WITH SEVERE ACUTE INƲUENZA, AND (II) DETERMINE HOW THESE TRANSLATOR PROFLLES CHANGE WITH SEVERITY IN A COMPLEMENTARY MURINE MODEL. I EXPECT THE RESULTS FROM THESE INDEPENDENT AIMS WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF PEDIATRIC INƲUENZA IMMUNITY AND PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR AGE- OR SITE-SPECIFLC VACCINE PLATFORMS. LASTLY, THE K22 AWARD WILL ALLOW ME TO ESTABLISH AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM FOCUSED ON PEDIATRIC VIRAL IMMUNITY AT MY HIRING INSTITUTION, WHERE OUR GROUP WILL BE COMMITTED TO IMPROVING DIAGNOSIS, TREATMENT, AND PREVENTION OF PEDIATRIC VIRAL DISEASES.

description: ELUCIDATING THE MECHANISMS OF MRE11-MEDIATED CGAS ACTIVATION IN DNA SENSING: MECHANISMS OF CGAS ACTIVATION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  THE CGAS-STING PATHWAY PLAYS A CRUCIAL ROLE IN INITIATING THE INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE BY RECOGNIZING CYTOSOLIC DOUBLE-STRANDED DNA (DSDNA) RESULTING FROM ONCOGENE-INDUCED DNA DAMAGE, LEADING TO THE ELIMINATION OF DAMAGED OR CANCEROUS CELLS. MRE11, A DNA REPAIR PROTEIN, FACILITATES THE RELEASE OF CGAS FROM CHROMATIN, ENABLING IT TO DETECT CYTOSOLIC DSDNA OR MICRONUCLEAR (MN) DNA AND ACTIVATE THE STING PATHWAY. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH MRE11 MEDIATES CGAS RELEASE AND HOW CGAS RECOGNIZES AND RESPONDS TO DSDNA AND MN REMAIN UNCLEAR. RECENT STUDIES SUGGEST THAT NUCLEAR ENVELOPE RUPTURE ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT FOR CGAS RECRUITMENT TO MN, AND HISTONE MODIFICATIONS SUCH AS H3K79ME2 PLAY A CRUCIAL ROLE IN CGAS ACTIVATION WITHIN MN. THE GOAL OF THIS STUDY IS TO DETERMINE HOW CGAS IS RELEASED AND ACTIVATED BY MRE11 AND TO IDENTIFY OTHER INTERACTING PROTEINS THAT CLARIFY THE MECHANISMS OF MRE11-MEDIATED CGAS ACTIVATION. AIM 1 FOCUSES ON HOW SPECIFIC HISTONE MODIFICATIONS, SUCH AS H3K79ME2 AND H3K27AC, INFLUENCE CGAS RELEASE FROM CHROMATIN THROUGH INTERACTIONS WITH MRE11, FACILITATING ITS RELOCATION TO CYTOSOLIC DSDNA AND MN. WE WILL UTILIZE HISTONE METHYLATION INHIBITORS, SIRNA, AND CRISPR/CAS9-BASED GENE KNOCKDOWN OR CHROMATIN IMMUNOPRECIPITATION (CHIP) ASSAYS TO INVESTIGATE THIS, ALONGSIDE IN VITRO EXPERIMENTS WITH MODIFIED NUCLEOSOMES TO ASSESS THE BINDING AFFINITY BETWEEN MRE11 AND CGAS. AIM 2 INVESTIGATES WHETHER ADDITIONAL REGULATORY STEPS ARE REQUIRED FOR FULL CGAS ACTIVATION, BUILDING ON PREVIOUS DATA THAT SUGGEST CYTOPLASMIC TRANSLOCATION AND DSDNA SENSING ALONE ARE INSUFFICIENT. WE WILL USE R255A MUTANTS AND CGAS VARIANTS WITH NUCLEAR LOCALIZATION SIGNALS (NLS) OR NUCLEAR EXPORT SIGNALS (NES) TO EXPLORE MECHANISMS REQUIRED FOR STING PATHWAY ACTIVATION. AIM 3 INVOLVES CREATING STABLE CELL LINES EXPRESSING BIOID2-TAGGED CGAS AND MRE11 TO MAP THEIR INTERACTION NETWORKS AND IDENTIFY PROTEINS INVOLVED IN CGAS-MRE11 INTERACTIONS THROUGH PROTEOMICS. IDENTIFIED PROTEINS WILL BE ASSESSED FOR THEIR ROLES IN MODULATING CGAS ACTIVATION AND DOWNSTREAM SIGNALING, REVEALING POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS. THIS STUDY AIMS TO ELUCIDATE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF CGAS-STING PATHWAY-MEDIATED TUMOR SUPPRESSION, POTENTIALLY OFFERING NEW THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TO ENHANCE IMMUNE RESPONSES IN CANCER.

description: BOOSTING AUD TREATMENT BY TARGETING HIGH-RISK DRINKING DAYS WITH AI-GENERATED CBT CONTENT - ABSTRACT ALCOHOL USE DISORDER (AUD) IS A MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH PROBLEM IN THE U.S., CONTRIBUTING TO OVER 100,000 DEATHS AND BILLIONS OF DOLLARS IN ECONOMIC LOSSES EACH YEAR. FEWER THAN 10% OF PEOPLE WITH AUD RECEIVE TREATMENT ANNUALLY DUE TO COST, STIGMA, AND LOGISTICAL CHALLENGES; LINGUISTIC AND CULTURAL DIFFERENCES FURTHER LIMIT ACCESS FOR U.S. COMMUNITIES THAT PRIMARILY SPEAK A LANGUAGE OTHER THAN ENGLISH (E.G., SPANISH). MANY OF THESE CHALLENGES CAN BE ADDRESSED BY EVIDENCE-BASED DIGITAL INTERVENTIONS, SINCE >90% OF THE U.S. POPULATION OWNS A SMARTPHONE. YET MANY DIGITAL INTERVENTIONS FAIL TO SUSTAIN PATIENTS’ ENGAGEMENT OVER TIME. THIS PROJECT WILL APPLY INNOVATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) AGENTS TO AUTONOMOUSLY GENERATE HIGHLY ENGAGING, MULTIMEDIA COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (CBT) CONTENT TAILORED FOR ENGLISH SPEAKERS AND SPANISH SPEAKERS. THE GOAL OF THE NEW DIGITAL CONTENT WILL BE TO PROVIDE CONDENSED CBT SKILLS TRAINING VIA PATIENTS’ PHONES TO SPECIFICALLY TARGET PERIODS OF HIGH RISK FOR DRINKING (E.G., WEEKENDS). UNLIKE CONVENTIONAL APPROACHES TO DEVELOPING DIGITAL CONTENT, AI AGENTS CAN RAPIDLY CREATE NEW CONTENT TO MATCH PATIENTS’ NEEDS AND CONTEXT (E.G., LANGUAGE PREFERENCE; ENVIRONMENT), OFFERING A SCALABLE SOLUTION TO IMPROVE ENGAGEMENT WITH DIGITAL INTERVENTIONS FOR AUD. AI AGENTS CAN ALSO EFFICIENTLY GENERATE NEW CONTENT BY LEARNING FROM EXISTING DIGITAL PROGRAMS FOR AUD, SUCH AS COMPUTER BASED TRAINING FOR COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (CBT4CBT-A), WHICH HAS DEMONSTRATED EFFICACY IN 3 RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIALS, INCLUDING A TRIAL WITH ONLY SPANISH-SPEAKING PATIENTS. BUT CBT4CBT-A IS NOT DESIGNED FOR EASY AND RAPID MOBILE USE DURING PERIODS OF HIGH RISK FOR DRINKING, AS EACH PROGRAM MODULE TAKES ~35 MINUTES TO COMPLETE AND IS STRUCTURED FOR PERSONAL COMPUTERS. TO DEVELOP AI AGENTS THAT GENERATE ENGAGING CONTENT TO ENHANCE PATIENTS’ PRACTICE OF CBT SKILLS ON DAYS OF HIGH RISK FOR DRINKING, THE FOLLOWING RESEARCH AIMS WILL BE PURSUED: 1) DEVELOP AI AGENTS THAT GENERATE MULTIMEDIA CBT CONTENT TO SUPPLEMENT AUD TREATMENT; 2) EVALUATE THE FEASIBILITY OF INTERACTING WITH AI-GENERATED CBT CONTENT ON THE WEEKENDS; 3) ESTIMATE THE EFFECT OF AI- GENERATED CBT CONTENT ON ALCOHOL USE AND PSYCHIATRIC SYMPTOMS. TO ACHIEVE THESE AIMS, MY CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN INCLUDES MENTORED TRAINING IN THE FOLLOWING DOMAINS: DEVELOPING AI AGENTS TO GENERATE AUD TREATMENT CONTENT; DIRECTING A CLINICAL TRIAL OF A TREATMENT FOR AUD; USING INNOVATIVE STATISTICAL METHODS TO ANALYZE CLINICAL TRIAL ENDPOINTS; FOSTERING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT THROUGH GRANT WRITING, PUBLISHING, LEADERSHIP, AND NETWORKING. TRAINING ACTIVITIES INCLUDE ACADEMIC COURSEWORK, AN NIH- SPONSORED TRAINING PROGRAM, APPLIED WORKSHOPS, AND ANNUAL SYMPOSIUMS/CONFERENCES. THESE ACTIVITIES BUILD ON MY PRIOR TRAINING IN ADDICTION TREATMENT, CLINICAL RESEARCH, QUALITATIVE METHODS, CULTURALLY-ADAPTED INTERVENTIONS, MOBILE TECHNOLOGY, AND ADVANCED STATISTICS. THIS AWARD WILL POSITION ME TO LEAD A NEW GENERATION OF AI-DRIVEN DIGITAL INTERVENTIONS THAT CAN IMPROVE TREATMENTS AND EXPAND ACCESS FOR ALL PEOPLE IN THE U.S. WITH AUD.

description: KETAMINE THERAPY FOR ALCOHOL USE DISORDER: REAL-WORLD INSIGHTS AND HOSPITAL-BASED CLINICAL TRIAL - PROJECT SUMMARY  1 CANDIDATE: DALE TERASAKI, MD, MPH, IS A HOSPITAL-BASED ADDICTION MEDICINE SPECIALIST WHO IS COMMITTED TO  2 REDUCING THE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY OF PATIENTS WITH ALCOHOL AND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (AUD/SUD). HIS  3 CAREER GOAL IS TO BECOME A LEADING EXPERT IN KETAMINE/PSYCHEDELICS AND INDEPENDENT CLINICAL RESEARCHER  4 DEVELOPING INNOVATIVE PHARMACOTHERAPIES FOR AUD/SUD IN MEDICAL SETTINGS.  5 CAREER DEVELOPMENT: TO ACHIEVE THIS CAREER GOAL, DR. TERASAKI WILL PURSUE COURSEWORK, TRAININGS,  6 AND INDIVIDUALIZED INSTRUCTION IN THREE SPECIFIC AREAS: (1) PHARMACOEPIDEMIOLOGIC ASSESSMENT OF RISKS &  7 BENEFITS OF NOVEL TREATMENTS TO INFORM RESEARCH & PRACTICE, (2) CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN & MANAGEMENT IN MEDICAL  8 SETTINGS, AND (3) ALCOHOL OUTCOME VALIDATION BY BIOMARKER AND OTHER MEASURES. CURRENT OPTIONS ARE LARGELY 12 INSUFFICIENT FOR THE HIGHEST-RISK PATIENTS WHO ARE FREQUENTLY ADMITTED TO THE HOSPITAL. THE NMDA ANTAGONIST, 13 KETAMINE, MAY BE WELL SUITED FOR THESE PATIENTS, AND DR. description: QUANTITATIVE CHEST IMAGING AND SERUM PROTEOMICS IN PATIENTS WITH SYSTEMIC AUTOIMMUNE RHEUMATIC DISEASE-ASSOCIATED INTERSTITIAL LUNG DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SYSTEMIC AUTOIMMUNE RHEUMATIC DISEASE-ASSOCIATED INTERSTITIAL LUNG DISEASE (SARD-ILD, ALSO KNOWN AS CONNECTIVE TISSUE DISEASE-ASSOCIATED ILD) IS A MAJOR DRIVER OF MORBIDITY, MORTALITY, AND HEALTHCARE COSTS IN PATIENTS WITH AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE AND ACCOUNTS FOR 30% OF ALL PATIENTS WITH ILD. RECENT ADVANCES IN IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE AND ANTIFIBROTIC TREATMENT OPTIONS HAVE EMPHASIZED THE IMPORTANCE OF EARLY DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT OF SARD-ILD. MACHINE LEARNING-DERIVED QUANTITATIVE COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (QCT) ANALYSIS OF CHEST IMAGING AND SERUM PROTEOMICS OFFER SIGNIFICANT PROMISE FOR IDENTIFYING SARD-ILD PATIENTS AT HIGH RISK OF DISEASE PROGRESSION AND POOR OUTCOMES, BUT HAVE NOT BEEN EXTENSIVELY EVALUATED IN SARD-ILD. THIS 5-YEAR K23 PATIENT-ORIENTED RESEARCH CAREER DEVELOPMENT AWARD ADDRESSES THIS RESEARCH GAP BY: 1) EXAMINING ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN QCT FEATURES PRESENT AT DIAGNOSIS AND MORTALITY IN PATIENTS WITH RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS- ASSOCIATED ILD (RA-ILD), 2) IDENTIFYING SERUM PROTEOMIC PROFILES OF PATIENTS WITH FIBROTIC RA-ILD AT HIGH RISK OF PROGRESSION, AND 3) EXPANDING THE SERUM PROTEOMIC FINDINGS TO PATIENTS WITH OTHER FORMS OF FIBROTIC AND NONFIBROTIC SARD-ILD. THIS INNOVATIVE PROJECT WILL GENERATE IMPORTANT CLINICAL INSIGHTS ABOUT THE USE OF QCT AND SERUM PROTEOMICS TO IDENTIFY SARD-ILD PATIENTS AT HIGH RISK OF DISEASE PROGRESSION. FURTHERMORE, THE CORRESPONDING TRAINING PLAN WILL SUPPORT DR. GREGORY MCDERMOTT, INSTRUCTOR IN MEDICINE AND ATTENDING RHEUMATOLOGIST AT BRIGHAM AND WOMEN'S HOSPITAL (BWH), IN BECOMING AN INDEPENDENT CLINICAL INVESTIGATOR STUDYING APPROACHES TO IMPROVE EARLY DETECTION, TREATMENT, AND OUTCOMES FOR PATIENTS WITH SARD-ILD. TRAINING IN THREE AREAS WILL SUPPORT DR. MCDERMOTT'S TRANSITION TO RESEARCH INDEPENDENCE: 1) GENERATION AND INVESTIGATION OF MACHINE LEARNING QCT IMAGING DATA, 2) DERIVATION AND ANALYSIS OF SERUM PROTEOMICS DATA, AND, 3) PROSPECTIVE PATIENT RECRUITMENT TECHNIQUES. A MULTIDISCIPLINARY MENTORSHIP TEAM CONSISTING OF RHEUMATOLOGISTS, PULMONOLOGISTS, AND BIOSTATISTICIANS WILL OVERSEE DR. MCDERMOTT'S TRAINING: DR. JEFFREY SPARKS (PRIMARY MENTOR); DRS. GEORGE WASHKO, KATHERINE LIAO, AND MICHAEL CHO (CO-MENTORS); AND DRS. PUI LEE, SUZANNE BYRNE, AND MISTI PAUDEL (SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTORS). DR. MCDERMOTT HAS A COMMITMENT FROM HIS DIVISION FOR AT LEAST 75% PROTECTED TIME FOR RESEARCH AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES DURING THE K23 AWARD PERIOD AND WILL COMPLETE FOCUSED COURSEWORK IN `OMICS RESEARCH, SURVIVAL ANALYSIS METHODS, AND MACHINE LEARNING TO FACILITATE HIS PATH TO INDEPENDENCE. THE BWH DIVISION OF RHEUMATOLOGY AND SECTION OF CLINICAL SCIENCES WILL PROVIDE RESOURCES AND EXPERTISE FOR THE PROPOSED STUDIES. SUPPORT FROM THE DIVISION AND HIS PRIMARY MENTOR'S RESEARCH FUNDS WILL SUPPLEMENT HIS SALARY AND PROJECT-RELATED EXPENSES. THE PROPOSED PROJECT AND TRAINING WILL INFORM PREPARATION OF A FUTURE R01 APPLICATION TO APPLY QCT AND SERUM PROTEOMICS TECHNIQUES TO ENABLE EARLY IDENTIFICATION AND INITIATION OF DISEASE MODIFYING TREATMENTS IN SARD-ILD PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A COMMUNITY-BASED PRODUCE PRESCRIPTION INTERVENTION TO IMPROVE NUTRITION SECURITY IN POPULATIONS WITH NUTRITION INSECURITY AND OBESITY. - PROJECT ABSTRACT: HEALTH DISPARITIES INCLUDING SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS, HEALTH INSURANCE STATUS, AND ACCESS TO HEALTH CARE, TO NAME A FEW, HAVE A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT ON HEALTH AND DISEASE. NUTRITION INSECURITY IS A MAJOR FACTOR FOR OBESITY WHICH IS DEFINED AS INDIVIDUALS NOT HAVING CONSISTENT ACCESS TO AFFORDABLE, HEALTHY, AND SAFE FOODS WHICH ARE ESSENTIAL FOR HEALTH. THIS IS OF PARTICULAR RELEVANCE FOR PATIENTS IN URBAN SETTINGS.  BASED ON A NEEDS ASSESSMENT OF OVER 1000 PATIENTS FROM FIVE SAFETY NET URBAN CLINICS IN PROVIDENCE, RHODE ISLAND, INCLUDING THE STUDY SITE FOR THIS PROPOSED RESEARCH, ALMOST HALF OF THE PATIENTS (47%) REPORTED REGULARLY REDUCING MEALS OR PORTION SIZES DUE TO A LACK OF FOOD.  NOVEL NUTRITION INTERVENTION EFFORTS ARE NEEDED TO ADDRESS THESE IMPORTANT HEALTH DISPARITIES TO INCREASE ACCESS AND AFFORDABILITY OF FRUITS AND VEGETABLES IN ORDER TO COMBAT OBESITY AND IMPROVE NUTRITION SECURITY, WHICH IS THE KEY PREMISE BEHIND THIS PROPOSED RESEARCH. TO ADDRESS THIS, THE SPECIFIC AIMS OF THIS PROPOSAL ARE TO 1) CONDUCT FOCUS GROUPS TO EXPLORE THE ACCEPTABILITY AND FEASIBILITY OF A PRODUCE PRESCRIPTION PROGRAM (PPR) WITH PATIENT AND HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS IN AN URBAN CLINIC; 2) PERFORM AN OPEN PILOT OF A PPR INTERVENTION FOCUSED ON PROGRAM UTILIZATION IN 10-15 PATIENTS WITH OBESITY AND NUTRITION INSECURITY; AND 3) CONDUCT A PILOT RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL (RCT) TO EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF A PPR INTERVENTION ON PRODUCE CONSUMPTION AND CLINICALLY RELEVANT HEALTH OUTCOMES. THE FINDINGS FROM THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL AND MUCH NEEDED APPROACHES TO IMPROVE PRODUCE CONSUMPTION IN POPULATIONS IMPACTED BY OBESITY AND NUTRITION INSECURITY. THE PROPOSAL WILL SUPPORT THE MENTORING AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE PI TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENTLY FUNDED PHYSICIAN SCIENTIST WHO SPECIALIZES IN IMPLEMENTATION OF COMMUNITY-BASED INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE HEALTHY EATING AND REDUCE THE IMPACT OF NONCOMMUNICABLE DIETARY RELATED DISEASES IN POPULATIONS MOST IMPACTED BY OBESITY AND NUTRITION INSECURITY.  THE PROPOSED RESEARCH BUILDS UPON THE EXPECTATIONAL RESOURCES AND MENTORSHIP PROVIDED AT THE WARREN ALPERT MEDICAL SCHOOL OF BROWN UNIVERSITY AND RHODE ISLAND HOSPITAL, ALONG WITH OTHER INSTITUTIONS TO PROVIDE THE PI WITH TRAINING IN KEY NEW AREAS OF RESEARCH, ENHANCE APPLICATIONS FOR COMPETITIVE GRANT FUNDING, PROVIDE UNIQUE COLLABORATION OPPORTUNITIES, AND BUILD THE NECESSARY FOUNDATION TO ATTAIN RESEARCH INDEPENDENCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BRIDGING THE GUT-BRAIN CONNECTION: A NOVEL INTEGRATED APPROACH TO ESOPHAGEAL SYMPTOM PERCEPTION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE (GERD) IS A HIGHLY PREVALENT ESOPHAGEAL CONDITION, AFFECTING 20–30% OF U.S. ADULTS, AND CAUSES SYMPTOMS SUCH AS HEARTBURN, REGURGITATION, AND CHEST PAIN. ALTHOUGH FIRST-LINE ACID SUPPRESSING THERAPIES EFFECTIVELY REDUCE STOMACH ACID, UP TO 40% OF PATIENTS CONTINUE TO EXPERIENCE PERSISTENT, REFRACTORY SYMPTOMS. RESEARCH INDICATES THAT MOST SYMPTOMS ARE NOT DIRECTLY LINKED TO ACID REFLUX EVENTS. INSTEAD, ESOPHAGEAL SYMPTOM PERCEPTION IS INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED AS MULTIFACTORIAL, ARISING FROM DYNAMIC INTERACTIONS BETWEEN PERIPHERAL (GUT) AND CENTRAL (BRAIN) PROCESSES ALONG THE BIDIRECTIONAL GUT-BRAIN AXIS. THUS, ADDRESSING ACID REFLUX ALONE IS OFTEN INSUFFICIENT WHEN CENTRAL FACTORS, SUCH AS PSYCHOLOGICAL PROCESSES, ALSO CONTRIBUTE. PSYCHOLOGICAL PROCESSES, SUCH AS ESOPHAGEAL HYPERVIGILANCE AND SYMPTOM-SPECIFIC ANXIETY HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO SIGNIFICANTLY AND INDEPENDENTLY INFLUENCE GERD SYMPTOM SEVERITY. HOWEVER, RESEARCH HAS RELIED ALMOST EXCLUSIVELY ON RETROSPECTIVE QUESTIONNAIRES AND CROSS-SECTIONAL DESIGNS, LIMITING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW PSYCHOLOGICAL PROCESSES DRIVE SYMPTOMS BOTH ON THEIR OWN AND THROUGH THEIR INTERACTION WITH PHYSIOLOGY. THIS K23 PROPOSAL ADDRESSES THIS CRITICAL GAP BY DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING A NOVEL APPROACH TO ASSESS REAL-TIME PSYCHOLOGICAL AND PHYSIOLOGICAL PROCESSES AS MECHANISTIC DRIVERS OF REFRACTORY GERD SYMPTOMS. THE PROJECT WILL INTEGRATE ECOLOGICAL MOMENTARY ASSESSMENT (EMA), A METHOD OF CAPTURING REAL-TIME PSYCHOLOGICAL STATES, WITH 96-HOUR WIRELESS PH MONITORING, A CLINICAL TEST THAT CONTINUOUSLY RECORDS ACID REFLUX EVENTS AND SYMPTOM REPORTS. THIS COMBINED APPROACH ENABLES SIMULTANEOUS, REAL-WORLD MEASUREMENT OF PSYCHOLOGICAL AND PHYSIOLOGICAL PROCESSES AND THEIR DYNAMIC INTERPLAY IN SHAPING ESOPHAGEAL SYMPTOM PERCEPTION. AIM 1 WILL DEVELOP A PATIENT-CENTERED EMA TOOL TO CAPTURE RELEVANT PSYCHOLOGICAL PROCESSES IN GERD. AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE THE FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, RELIABILITY, AND VALIDITY OF THE EMA TOOL AND ITS INTEGRATION WITH 96-HOUR WIRELESS PH MONITORING. AIM 3 WILL DETERMINE HOW PSYCHOLOGICAL PROCESSES AND REFLUX EVENTS INTERACT OVER TIME TO SHAPE SYMPTOM REPORTING, IDENTIFYING MECHANISTIC DRIVERS OF SYMPTOMS AND TARGETS FOR PRECISION BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS. THIS PROPOSAL ALIGNS WITH A CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN DESIGNED TO SUPPORT DR. GUADAGNOLI IN BECOMING AN INDEPENDENT TRANSLATIONAL INVESTIGATOR. TRAINING GOALS INCLUDE BUILDING EXPERTISE IN ESOPHAGEAL PHYSIOLOGY AND PATHOGENESIS, GAINING COMPETENCY IN EMA METHODOLOGY AND IMPLEMENTATION, TRANSLATING MECHANISTIC FINDINGS INTO CLINICAL TARGETS FOR PRECISION-BASED INTERVENTIONS, AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT. MENTORSHIP WILL BE PROVIDED BY DR. JOHN PANDOLFINO (PRIMARY), DR. DOERTE JUNGHAENEL (CO-MENTOR), AND DR. LAUREN HEATHCOTE (CO-MENTOR), WITH GUIDANCE FROM AN INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM OF CONSULTANTS, INCLUDING DRS. JACOB SCHAUER, SALVA BALBALE, AND KATHRYN TOMASINO. FINDINGS FROM THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO REFRACTORY GERD, INFORM FUTURE CLINICAL TRIALS, AND ADVANCE PRECISION-BASED TREATMENT STRATEGIES TARGETING BOTH CENTRAL AND PERIPHERAL DRIVERS OF ESOPHAGEAL SYMPTOMS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DRIVERS AND CONSEQUENCES OF MOVEMENT ANXIETY AFTER STROKE - PROJECT SUMMARY AFTER STROKE, MANY INDIVIDUALS UNDERUSE THEIR PARETIC UPPER EXTREMITY (UE) DESPITE SUFFICIENT MOTOR CAPACITY, LIMITING FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY. ONE POTENTIAL CAUSE OF UE UNDERUSE IS MOVEMENT ANXIETY—THE FEAR THAT MOVEMENT MAY WORSEN PAIN, CAUSE INJURY, OR TRIGGER RECURRENCE OF A MEDICAL EVENT. PREVIOUS STUDIES HAVE FOUND THAT 48– 83% OF STROKE PATIENTS EXPERIENCE MOVEMENT ANXIETY, BUT HAVE MAINLY FOCUSED ON WALKING AND BALANCE. MOVEMENT ANXIETY RELATING TO UE USE IS LESS WELL UNDERSTOOD, AND NO REHABILITATION INTERVENTIONS CURRENTLY TARGET THIS ISSUE. THIS GAP IN KNOWLEDGE LEAVES A POTENTIALLY MODIFIABLE BARRIER TO RECOVERY UNADDRESSED. IN THIS STUDY, WE WILL CLOSE THIS GAP BY PROSPECTIVELY TRACKING UE MOVEMENT ANXIETY IN SUBACUTE STROKE PATIENTS DURING INPATIENT REHABILITATION. WE WILL MEASURE MOVEMENT ANXIETY USING THE TAMPA SCALE OF KINESIOPHOBIA AND WILL CHARACTERIZE PATIENT AND REHABILITATION FACTORS USING CLINICAL SCALES AND THE ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD. WE WILL ALSO USE WRIST-WORN ACCELEROMETERS TO MEASURE A 24-HOUR EPOCH OF SPONTANEOUS UE USE. IN AIM 1, WE WILL IDENTIFY PATIENT FACTORS THAT PREDICT HIGHER LEVELS OF MOVEMENT ANXIETY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT UE PAIN WILL BE THE PRIMARY CONTRIBUTOR TO MOVEMENT ANXIETY, WITH PAIN CATASTROPHIZING A SECONDARY CONTRIBUTOR. IN AIM 2, WE WILL IDENTIFY PATIENT AND REHABILITATION FACTORS THAT INFLUENCE CHANGE IN MOVEMENT ANXIETY DURING THE INPATIENT REHABILITATION COURSE. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT REDUCTIONS IN UE PAIN AND PAIN CATASTROPHIZING WILL RELATE TO REDUCTIONS IN MOVEMENT ANXIETY. IN AIM 3, WE WILL DETERMINE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN MOVEMENT ANXIETY AND UE USE. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT HIGHER MOVEMENT ANXIETY PREDICTS LOWER UE USE AND VICE VERSA. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT WOULD IDENTIFY AT-RISK PATIENTS, GUIDE THE DEVELOPMENT OF TARGETED INTERVENTIONS, AND JUSTIFY THE NEED TO ADDRESS MOVEMENT ANXIETY IN REHABILITATION. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT EXAMINES A SURPRISINGLY UNDERSTUDIED PSYCHOLOGICAL CHALLENGE USING GOLD-STANDARD AND QUANTITATIVE METHODS. BY IDENTIFYING MOVEMENT ANXIETY AS A MODIFIABLE CONTRIBUTOR TO UE UNDERUSE, THIS STUDY LAYS THE GROUNDWORK FOR EARLY SCREENING AND TARGETED INTERVENTIONS TO ENHANCE REHABILITATION ENGAGEMENT AND RECOVERY. TO ACCOMPLISH THE PROPOSED WORK, DR. SHI HAS ASSEMBLED A MENTORING AND ADVISORY TEAM OF SEASONED INVESTIGATORS AND CLINICIANS WHO WILL OVERSEE HER CONCEPTUAL, TECHNICAL, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. IN ADDITION TO HER HANDS- ON RESEARCH EXPERIENCE, DR. SHI WILL UNDERTAKE TUTORIALS, COURSEWORK, AND SHADOWING TO BUILD HER KNOWLEDGE IN CLINICAL RESEARCH EXECUTION, TRANSLATING PSYCHOLOGICAL INSIGHTS INTO REHABILITATION, MOTION DATA CAPTURE AND PROCESSING, AND ADVANCED STATISTICAL ANALYSES. THIS ENHANCED SKILLSET WILL ENABLE DR. SHI TO INTEGRATE PSYCHOLOGICAL INSIGHTS INTO STROKE REHABILITATION, OPENING NEW THERAPEUTIC AVENUES TO ADVANCE THE FIELD OF NEUROREHABILITATION.

description: THE INFLUENCE OF EXPOSURE TO COMMUNITY-LEVEL HOUSING COST BURDEN ON PERINATAL HEALTH - TRAINING: THE PURPOSE OF THIS K23 PROPOSAL IS TO EQUIP DR. DARIA MUROSKO FOR A CAREER AS AN INDEPENDENT PHYSICIAN-SCIENTIST. HER LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO CONDUCT HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH THAT ADDRESSES THE COMMUNITY DRIVERS OF HEALTH, SUCH AS HOUSING, THAT CONTRIBUTE TO MATERNAL AND INFANT HEALTH. HER IMMEDIATE GOAL IS TO PERFORM RIGOROUS RETROSPECTIVE STUDIES WITH ADVANCED SPATIAL ANALYSES TO ELUCIDATE HOW MEASURES OF HOUSING AFFORDABILITY INFLUENCE PERINATAL OUTCOMES AND ASSOCIATED DIFFERENCES BY SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS, WHICH MAY GUIDE HOW PHYSICIANS ALTER TREATMENT PLANS TO OPTIMIZE OUTCOMES. DR. MUROSKO AND HER MENTORSHIP TEAM HAVE CREATED A CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN INCORPORATING: 1) COMPREHENSIVE AND COLLABORATIVE MENTORSHIP BY SUCCESSFUL INVESTIGATORS WITH A BROAD RANGE OF EXPERTISE IN PERINATAL CARE AND BIOSTATISTICS, IN AN EXCEPTIONAL RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT FOR HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; 2) ADVANCED TRAINING IN SPATIAL STATISTICS AND CAUSAL INFERENCE MODELING; AND 3) INNOVATIVE RESEARCH EXAMINING THE EFFECT OF HOUSING COST BURDEN ON PERINATAL OUTCOMES.  RESEARCH: IN THE UNITED STATES, 10.4% OF INFANTS ARE BORN PRETERM, CONTRIBUTING TO INFANT MORTALITY AND CHRONIC HEALTH COMPLICATIONS. THERE IS SIGNIFICANT VARIATION IN PRETERM BIRTH AND INFANT MORTALITY ACROSS COMMUNITIES, DRIVEN PARTIALLY BY THE UNEVEN DISTRIBUTION OF COMMUNITY AND INDIVIDUAL FACTORS THAT INFLUENCE HEALTH. STABLE, AFFORDABLE HOUSING IS ONE SIGNIFICANT DRIVER OF HEALTH, RECENTLY THREATENED BY RISING HOUSING COSTS. OVER 42 MILLION AMERICANS EXPERIENCE HIGH HOUSING COST BURDENS, A MEASURE OF UNAFFORDABILITY, PUTTING THEM AT RISK FOR HOUSING INSTABILITY. EXTREME HOUSING INSTABILITY, INCLUDING EVICTIONS AND HOMELESSNESS, IS A RISK FACTOR FOR POOR HEALTH. HOWEVER, THE ASSOCIATION OF HOUSING COST BURDEN WITH PERINATAL HEALTH REMAINS UNKNOWN. DR. MUROSKO’S RESEARCH WILL ADDRESS THIS GAP. BY CREATING AN ENHANCED BIRTH COHORT, SHE WILL: 1) EXAMINE HOW HOUSING COST BURDEN INFLUENCES PERINATAL HEALTH; 2) QUANTIFY THE EXTENT TO WHICH HOUSING COST BURDEN CONTRIBUTES TO VARIATION IN PERINATAL OUTCOMES; AND 3) DETERMINE HOW THIS RISK FACTOR IS MODIFIED BY EXISTING RISK FACTORS, POTENTIALLY INFORMING TARGETED SCREENING AND DELIVERY OF PHYSICIAN-LED INTERVENTIONS TO HIGH RISK PATIENTS. THIS RESEARCH DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THE TOP NICHD RESEARCH PRIORITY OF “SETTING THE FOUNDATION FOR HEALTHY PREGNANCIES AND LIFELONG WELLNESS” BY EXAMINING THE IMPACT OF SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES ON PREGNANCY OUTCOMES AND NEONATAL MORTALITY.
