description: CHARACTERIZING ABSORPTION KINETICS OF ORAL ANTIBIOTICS IN YOUNG INFANTS TO ENHANCE PRECISION DOSING - PROPOSAL SUMMARY (ABSTRACT): THIS K23 CAREER DEVELOPMENT AWARD APPLICATION ADDRESSES THE UNMET NEED FOR SAFE AND EFFECTIVE ORAL (PO) ANTIBIOTIC DOSING IN NEONATES AND YOUNG INFANTS. TRANSITIONING FROM INTRAVENOUS (IV) TO PO ANTIBIOTICS IS STANDARD PRACTICE FOR SERIOUS PEDIATRIC INFECTIONS, OFFERING SIMILAR CLINICAL OUTCOMES WITH SHORTER HOSPITAL STAYS, FEWER SIDE EFFECTS, AND REDUCED COSTS. HOWEVER, NEONATES AND YOUNG INFANTS ARE OFTEN EXCLUDED DUE TO THEIR VULNERABILITY TO SERIOUS INFECTIONS, A LACK OF PHARMACOKINETIC (PK) AND PHARMACODYNAMIC (PD) DATA, AND HIGH INTER-INDIVIDUAL VARIABILITY (IIV) IN DRUG ABSORPTION, ALL OF WHICH COMPLICATE OPTIMAL DOSING. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES BY LEVERAGING PK/PD APPROACHES TO OPTIMIZE PO DOSING OF AMOXICILLIN AND LINEZOLID, TWO ANTIBIOTICS THAT ARE WELL ABSORBED AND EFFECTIVE AGAINST COMMON NEONATAL PATHOGENS BUT REMAIN UNDERUTILIZED DUE TO LIMITED DATA CHARACTERIZING THEIR ABSORPTION AND DISPOSITION IN THIS POPULATION. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT COVARIATE-BASED DOSING, CONSIDERING PATIENT-SPECIFIC FACTORS SUCH AS POST-NATAL AGE AND GESTATIONAL AGE, WILL IMPROVE PD TARGET ATTAINMENT COMPARED TO STANDARD WEIGHT-BASED DOSING. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH INTEGRATES POPULATION PK (POPPK) MODELING, PHYSIOLOGICALLY-BASED PK (PBPK) MODELING, AND IN VITRO METABOLISM STUDIES TO OPTIMIZE PO ANTIBIOTIC DOSING STRATEGIES. AIM 1 WILL USE EXISTING DATA TO DEVELOP POPPK AND PBPK MODELS FOR AMOXICILLIN, IDENTIFYING COVARIATES TO SUPPORT COVARIATE-INFORMED DOSING STRATEGIES, AND WILL EXTEND THIS WORK BY DEVELOPING A MODEL-INFORMED PRECISION DOSING (MIPD) FRAMEWORK IN MWPHARM++, PROVIDING A FOUNDATION FOR A FUTURE R01 APPLICATION FOCUSED ON IMPLEMENTATION. AIM 2 WILL DEVELOP A PRELIMINARY PBPK MODEL TO PREDICT PO LINEZOLID PK IN YOUNG INFANTS BY COMBINING PUBLISHED PK DATA WITH IN VITRO MICROSOMAL STABILITY ASSAYS THAT WILL DEFINE NEONATAL LINEZOLID METABOLISM. AIM 3 WILL VALIDATE THE PBPK MODEL THROUGH A PROSPECTIVE, OPTIMALLY-DESIGNED CLINICAL STUDY IN YOUNG INFANTS, REFINE COVARIATE-BASED DOSING STRATEGIES, AND IDENTIFY PATIENT-SPECIFIC FACTORS DRIVING ABSORPTION VARIABILITY. COMPLETING THESE AIMS IS FEASIBLE AND WILL ADDRESS THE CRITICAL NEED FOR PERSONALIZED PO DOSING REGIMENS IN THIS VULNERABLE POPULATION. THIS RESEARCH REFLECTS DR. HAYNES’S COMMITMENT TO IMPROVING OUTCOMES FOR INFANTS WITH BACTERIAL INFECTIONS AND ALIGNS WITH HIS CAREER GOAL OF BECOMING AN INDEPENDENT CLINICIAN-SCIENTIST SPECIALIZING IN PHARMACOMETRICS AND PEDIATRIC CLINICAL TRIALS. TO SUPPORT THIS GOAL, THIS PROPOSAL OUTLINES A FOUR-YEAR MENTORED CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN ENCOMPASSING DIDACTIC AND EXPERIENTIAL TRAINING IN ADVANCED PK MODELING, SIMULATION, MIPD, CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN, AND LABORATORY TECHNIQUES, WHICH IS A NATURAL EXTENSION FROM HIS K12 CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY CAREER DEVELOPMENT AWARD. DR. HAYNES HAS ASSEMBLED A MULTIDISCIPLINARY MENTORSHIP TEAM LED BY PETER ANDERSON, PHARMD, AND KEVIN MESSACAR, MD, PHD, WITH ADDITIONAL SUPPORT FROM A DIVERSE AND ACCOMPLISHED GROUP OF CO- MENTORS AND ADVISORS, ENSURING THE RESOURCES AND GUIDANCE NEEDED TO ADVANCE HIS LONG-TERM OBJECTIVE OF IMPROVING PERSONALIZED PO ANTIBIOTIC DOSING STRATEGIES ACROSS PEDIATRICS.

description: IDENTIFYING THERAPEUTIC MECHANISMS FOR INCRETIN-BASED TREATMENT IN OBESITY-RELATED HFPEF - THE PROPOSED K23 CAREER DEVELOPMENT AWARD WILL ENABLE DR. ELISSA DRIGGIN TO ESTABLISH AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH CAREER WITH EXPERTISE IN HEART FAILURE WITH PRESERVED EJECTION FRACTION (HFPEF) AND CARDIOMETABOLIC DISEASE. DR. DRIGGIN IS A BOARD-CERTIFIED CARDIOLOGIST AND ASSISTANT PROFESSOR OF MEDICINE WORKING IN ADVANCED HEART FAILURE AND TRANSPLANT CARDIOLOGY WHOSE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO UNDERSTAND THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF CARDIOMETABOLIC HFPEF TO IMPROVE FUNCTIONAL AND CARDIAC OUTCOMES FOR PATIENTS WITH THESE DISEASES, BUT FURTHER TRAINING IS REQUIRED TO ACCOMPLISH THIS GOAL. SHE HAS ASSEMBLED A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM OF MENTORS TO PROVIDE TRAINING IN: (1) CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN AND QUANTITATIVE METHODS; (2) CONTENT EXPERTISE IN OBESITY MEDICINE AND BODY COMPOSITION ANALYSIS; (3) CLINICAL RESEARCH PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT; AND (4) RESEARCH DISSEMINATION, GRANT WRITING, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. THE CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN INCLUDES MENTORED MEETINGS, COURSEWORK AT THE MAILMAN SCHOOL OF PUBLIC HEALTH AT COLUMBIA, AND OTHER APPLIED ACTIVITIES THROUGH THE VAST RESOURCES AVAILABLE AT COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY. FOR HER RESEARCH PROJECT, DR. DRIGGIN WILL CONDUCT A PILOT CLINICAL TRIAL AMONG AMBULATORY PATIENTS WITH OBESITY AND HFPEF. PREVIOUS RESEARCH HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT INCRETIN-BASED THERAPIES, SUCH AS THE GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE 1 (GLP1) RECEPTOR/GLUCOSE-DEPENDENT INSULINOTROPIC POLYPEPTIDE (GIP) RECEPTOR CO-AGONIST, TIRZEPATIDE, IMPROVES CLINICAL OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS WITH OBESITY AND HFPEF. THE MECHANISMS OF BENEFIT ARE INCOMPLETELY CHARACTERIZED. PRELIMINARY DATA FROM SECONDARY ANALYSES OF PRIOR CLINICAL TRIALS SUGGESTS THAT PLASMA VOLUME (PV) REDUCTION, MEDIATED BY LOSS OF FAT MASS AND SERUM LEPTIN, MAY PLAY A KEY ROLE. MOREOVER, NO PRIOR STUDY HAS ADEQUATELY QUANTIFIED CHANGES IN BODY COMPOSITION THAT MAY LEAD TO CHANGES IN PV. THIS PROPOSAL ENTAILS A PILOT CLINICAL TRIAL OF 50 PARTICIPANTS WITH OBESITY AND HFPEF PRESCRIBED TIRZEPATIDE THERAPY. THE FIRST AIM IS TO MEASURE CHANGES IN PV OVER TIME WITH TIRZEPATIDE TREATMENT USING 131IODINE-LABELED ALBUMIN. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT TREATMENT WILL SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCE PV OVER TIME. THE SECOND AIM IS TO PERFORM BODY COMPOSITION ANALYSIS WITH A STATE-OF-THE-ART METHODOLOGY, QUANTITATIVE MAGNETIC RESONANCE (QMR), TO DETERMINE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN FAT MASS REDUCTION AND PVR. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT FAT MASS REDUCTION WILL LEAD TO REDUCTION IN PV. WE WILL ALSO QUANTIFY CHANGES SERUM LEPTIN WITH TREATMENT, WHICH WE BELIEVE WILL SIGNIFICANTLY PREDICT PV REDUCTION. THE THIRD AIM IS TO UTILIZE QMR TO ASSESS CHANGES IN LEAN MASS OVER TIME WITH TREATMENT. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT REDUCTIONS IN LEAN MASS WILL OCCUR WITH TIRZEPATIDE TREATMENT, WHICH IS IMPORTANT TO ESTABLISH AS A POTENTIAL ADVERSE EFFECT. WE WILL PERFORM TRANSTHORACIC ECHOCARDIOGRAMS TO DETERMINE CHANGE IN CARDIAC STRUCTURE OVER TIME THAT MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH PV REDUCTION. WE WILL PERFORM QUALITY OF LIFE ASSESSMENTS WITH THE KANSAS CITY CARDIOMYOPATHY QUESTIONNAIRE (KCCQ) TO DETERMINE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN PV REDUCTION WITH QUALITY OF LIFE IMPROVEMENT. THESE DATA WILL ALSO INFORM HER LARGER PROGRAM OF RESEARCH ON HFPEF AND CARDIOMETABOLIC DISEASE.

description: ROLE OF B-CELLS IN SYSTEMIC SCLEROSIS-RELATED PULMONARY HYPERTENSION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT PULMONARY HYPERTENSION (PH) IS A MAJOR DRIVER OF MORTALITY IN THE PATIENTS DIAGNOSED WITH SYSTEMIC SCLEROSIS (SSC). DESPITE BEING CONVENTIONALLY CLASSIFIED AS GROUP 1 PULMONARY ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION (PAH) BY THE WORLD SYMPOSIUM ON PH, THE BIOLOGY OF SSC-PH IS NOT THE SAME AS IDIOPATHIC PAH DESPITE TYPICALLY EXHIBITING PATTERNS OF PRE-CAPILLARY PH BY CARDIOPULMONARY HEMODYNAMICS. THERAPIES IN SSC-PH ARE LIMITED, MANY OF WHICH TARGET VASODILATION. TO UNCOVER NOVEL THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES, IT WILL BE NECESSARY TO GAIN A MORE DETAILED UNDERSTANDING INTO THE MECHANISMS AND MOLECULAR PATHWAYS OF SSC-PH. THE SCOPE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DETERMINE THE ROLE OF B-CELLS IN THE PATHOGENESIS SSC-PH. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT B-CELLS PROVIDE FURTHER ENDOTYPING NEEDED TO RISK STRATIFY PATIENTS WITH SSC-PH THROUGH THE FOLLOWING AIMS: 1) TEST WHETHER SSC PATIENTS WITH PRE-CAPILLARY PH HAVE INCREASED EFFECTOR B-CELL SUBSETS AND DIFFERENCES IN PATTERNS OF CYTOKINES AND AUTOANTIBODIES COMPARED TO THOSE WITHOUT; 2) DETERMINE THE DIFFERENTIAL B-CELL MRNA GENE EXPRESSION BETWEEN SSC PATIENTS WITH AND WITHOUT PRE-CAPILLARY PH; AND 3) DELINEATE A PATTERN OF B-CELL SUBSETS, CYTOKINES, AUTOANTIBODIES, AND MRNA GENE EXPRESSION PROFILE IN SSC PATIENTS WITH PRE- CAPILLARY PH WHO PROGRESS TO RIGHT VENTRICULAR DYSFUNCTION. THE OVERALL SIGNIFICANCE OF THIS WORK IS TO EVENTUALLY HELP GUIDE TREATMENT BY IDENTIFYING PATIENTS WHO MAY POTENTIALLY BENEFIT FROM B-CELL TARGETED APPROACHES TO THERAPY. THIS K23 AWARD, WITH THE COMBINED DIDACTICS, MENTORSHIP, AND RESEARCH EXPERIENCE IT AFFORDS WILL ME ADVANCE TOWARD MY CAREER GOAL OF BECOMING AN INDEPENDENT PHYSICIAN SCIENTIST. UPON COMPLETION OF THIS 5-YEAR CAREER DEVELOPMENT AWARD, I WILL HAVE CREATED THE FOUNDATION FOR A SUBSEQUENT R01 BY 1) EXPLORING THE B-CELL-SPECIFIC MECHANISTIC PATHWAYS IMPLICATED IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND PROGRESSION OF SSC-PH; AND 2) CREATING A DEEP ENDOTYPING OF THESE PATIENTS. OVER THE COURSE OF THIS PROPOSAL, I WILL BROADEN MY SKILLSET IN A) GENOMIC DATA MINING; B) DATA SCIENCE; C) BIOBANKING AND BIOREPOSITORY SCIENCE; D) IMMUNOPHENOTYPING; AND E) PROFICIENCY IN GRANT WRITING FOR INDEPENDENT RESEARCH FUNDING. OUR FINDINGS WILL PROVIDE THE RATIONALE FOR A MULTICENTER PROSPECTIVE STUDY TO CONFIRM B-CELL ENDOTYPES CHARACTERIZED IN PATIENTS WITH SSC-PH. THIS PROPOSED WORK ALIGNS WITH THE FOLLOWING GOALS OF THE NATIONAL HEART, LUNG, AND BLOOD INSTITUTE IN: 1) INVESTIGATING NEWLY DISCOVERED PATHOBIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS IMPORTANT TO THE ONSET AND PROGRESSION OF HEART, LUNG, BLOOD, AND SLEEP DISEASES; 2) IDENTIFYING FACTORS THAT ACCOUNT FOR INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES IN PATHOBIOLOGY AND TREATMENT RESPONSES; AND 3) LEVERAGING EMERGING OPPORTUNITIES IN DATA SCIENCE TO OPEN NEW FRONTIERS IN OF HEART, LUNG, BLOOD, AND SLEEP RESEARCH.

description: ADVANCING SUSTAINABLE OBESITY CARE: INTEGRATING FOOD IS MEDICINE WITH GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS - PROJECT SUMMARY OBESITY IS ONE OF THE MOST PRESSING PUBLIC HEALTH CHALLENGES IN THE UNITED STATES, WITH WIDESPREAD CONSEQUENCES FOR CHRONIC DISEASE, INCLUDING CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, AND ESCALATING HEALTHCARE COSTS. GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS (GLP-1 RAS) HAVE EMERGED AS A PROMISING PHARMACOLOGIC TREATMENT, OFFERING SIGNIFICANT WEIGHT LOSS AND CARDIOMETABOLIC BENEFITS. HOWEVER, THEIR LONG-TERM USE IS LIMITED BY CONCERNS ABOUT SAFETY, COST-EFFECTIVENESS, AND FEASIBILITY FOR BROAD, POPULATION-WIDE ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND MAINTENANCE. MOREOVER, GLP-1 RAS MAY NOT DIRECTLY IMPROVE OVERALL DIETARY BEHAVIOR, WHICH IS ESSENTIAL FOR ACHIEVING LONG-TERM OBESITY MANAGEMENT. DR. YOO’S K23 CAREER DEVELOPMENT PROPOSAL AIMS TO EVALUATE THE INTEGRATION OF A FOOD IS MEDICINE (FIM) IMPLEMENTATION BUNDLE FOR PATIENTS INITIATING GLP-1 RA FOR WEIGHT MANAGEMENT THROUGH A TYPE 1 HYBRID RANDOMIZED TRIAL EMBEDDED IN WASHU MEDICINE/BJC HEALTHCARE, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH SEASON HEALTH, A NATIONAL FIM PROVIDER. THE STUDY INCLUDE: (1) FORMATIVE MIXED-METHODS RESEARCH TO GUIDE ADAPTATION OF THE FIM BUNDLE, INFORMED BY STAKEHOLDER INTERVIEWS AND SECONDARY ANALYSIS OF PRIOR FIM TRIALS; (2) AN EVALUATION OF THE EFFICACY OF THE ADAPTED FIM IMPLEMENTATION BUNDLE IN IMPROVING FRUIT AND VEGETABLE INTAKE AT 6 MONTHS AMONG 240 PATIENTS; AND (3) AN ASSESSMENT OF IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES USING THE RE-AIM/PRISM FRAMEWORK. THIS PROPOSAL ALIGNS WITH RESEARCH PRIORITIES IDENTIFIED BY NHLBI AND NATIONAL STRATEGIES TO INTEGRATE NUTRITION INTO CLINICAL CARE, AND IT WILL LEVERAGE IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE TO GUIDE ADAPTATION AND OPTIMIZE SUCCESS. THE K23 AWARD WILL ALSO PROVIDE ESSENTIAL METHODOLOGICAL TRAINING TO SUPPORT DR. YOO’S TRANSITION TO RESEARCH INDEPENDENCE. DR. YOO PROPOSES FOCUSED TRAINING IN: (1) QUALITATIVE AND MIXED-METHODS RESEARCH; (2) FOOD IS MEDICINE SCIENCE; (3) DISSEMINATION AND IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE; (4) PRAGMATIC CLINICAL TRIALS; AND (5) EXPERIENTIAL HEALTH SYSTEM-LEVEL SCIENCE. DR. YOO’S EXPERIENCED AND HIGHLY SUPPORTIVE MENTORING TEAM IS LED BY DR. MARK HUFFMAN (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY IN ST. LOUIS), WITH CO-MENTORSHIP FROM DRS. JASON WU (THE GEORGE INSTITUTE FOR GLOBAL HEALTH) AND THOMAS KANNAMPALLIL (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY IN ST. LOUIS). THIS TEAM IS FURTHER SUPPORTED BY KEY COLLABORATORS AND ADVISORS, DRS. MADDOX, GOSS, TABAK, AND LI, WHO WILL ENSURE SCIENTIFIC SUCCESS AND OVERSEE DR. YOO’S ADVANCED TRAINING. INSIGHTS FROM THIS STUDY WILL LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR A FUTURE MULTI-SITE R01 TRIAL TO ASSESS FOOD IS MEDICINE IMPLEMENTATION IN OBESITY CARE. THIS K23 AWARD WILL PREPARE DR. YOO FOR A SUCCESSFUL INDEPENDENT RESEARCH CAREER AND POSITION HIM AS A LEADER IN FOOD IS MEDICINE TO ADVANCE CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH.

description: EVALUATING AN EVIDENCE-BASED, SUICIDE SPECIFIC TREATMENT WITH YOUTH INVOLVED IN THE JUVENILE JUSTICE SYSTEM - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE PERCENTAGE OF LEGALLY INVOLVED YOUTH (LIY) WHO ATTEMPT SUICIDE IS NEARLY DOUBLE THAT OF THEIR NON-LEGALLY INVOLVED COUNTERPARTS, AND LIY ARE UP TO FIVE TIMES MORE LIKELY TO DIE BY SUICIDE. LIY HAVE UNIQUE NEEDS, AS THEY TYPICALLY REPORT COMPOUNDING RISK FACTORS FOR SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS (STB) THAT REQUIRE ADDITIONAL CONSIDERATION (E.G., JUDICIAL PROCESSING, SUBSTANCE USE, TRAUMA EXPOSURE). UNFORTUNATELY, OPTIONS FOR EFFECTIVE STB TREATMENT ARE LIMITED. THE PROPOSED PILOT RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL (RCT) AIMS TO ASSESS THE PLAUSIBLE EFFECTS OF THE COLLABORATIVE ASSESSMENT AND MANAGEMENT OF SUICIDALITY ADAPTED FOR USE WITH ADOLESCENTS (CAMS-4TEENS) ON STB AMONG LIY WHILE CONSIDERING COPING SKILL USE AS A CANDIDATE MECHANISM OF ACTION USING ECOLOGICAL MOMENTARY ASSESSMENT (EMA). THE FIRST AIM (AIM 1) WILL BE TO CONDUCT A PILOT RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL OF CAMS-4TEENS COMPARED TO ENHANCED TREATMENT AS USUAL CONDITION (E-TAU). THIS AIM WILL INCLUDE ESTABLISHING THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF THE TRIAL PROTOCOL AND ASSESSING CHANGES IN THE FREQUENCY, DURATION, AND SEVERITY OF STB AMONG LIY. IF FOUND ACCEPTABLE AND FEASIBLE, THIS AIM CAN SET THE STAGE FOR FUTURE CLINIC TRIALS TO TEST THE EFFECTIVENESS OF CAMS-4TEENS AMONG LIY IN THE COMMUNITY- BASED SETTINGS WHERE THEY TYPICALLY RECEIVE CARE. THE SECOND AIM (AIM 2) WILL EVALUATE COPING SKILLS USE AS A CANDIDATE MECHANISM OF ACTION CONTRIBUTING TO REDUCTIONS IN STB. COPING SKILLS ASSESSED DURING THE TRIAL WILL INCLUDE A GENERAL LIST AND THOSE SPECIFICALLY DELINEATED ON A SAFETY PLAN. THIS PILOT RCT WILL RECRUIT LIY THROUGH AN EXISTING NIMH-FUNDED GRANT PROJECT THAT SCREENS AND REFERS LIY TO COMMUNITY-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES AND CONNECTIONS WITH JUVENILE LEGAL AGENCIES THROUGHOUT THE STATE. AS A PART OF THIS PROCESS, YOUTH WHO ARE SCREENED AS AT-RISK FOR SUICIDE WILL BE ELIGIBLE TO PARTICIPATE. YOUTH WILL RECEIVE 60-MINUTE, WEEKLY CAMS- 4TEENS SESSIONS UNTIL THEY MEET PREDETERMINED DISCHARGE CRITERIA. YOUTH IN E-TAU WILL RECEIVE SINGLE-SESSION SAFETY PLANNING WITH A FOLLOW-UP APPOINTMENT AND CASE MANAGEMENT. DURING THE FIRST 28 DAYS OF TREATMENT, YOUTH WILL PARTICIPATE IN DAILY EMA ASSESSMENTS TO ASSESS STB AND ASSOCIATED MECHANISMS OF ACTION. CAREGIVERS AND YOUTH WILL EACH COMPLETE SURVEYS AT BASELINE, 4 WEEKS (TO ALIGN WITH EMA DATA COLLECTION), AND 3 MONTHS POST- BASELINE. CLINICIANS WILL PARTICIPATE IN FIDELITY MONITORING AND SUPERVISION WITH RESEARCH STAFF. THE PRIMARY MENTOR, DR. AALSMA, AND CO-MENTORS, DRS. ELKINGTON, JOBES, ADRIAN, AND TURNER, ARE EXTREMELY WELL-QUALIFIED TO ASSIST ME IN REACHING MY TRAINING GOALS AND EXECUTING THE PROPOSED RESEARCH. THEIR COMBINED EXPERTISE SPANS SUICIDOLOGY, WORKING WITH LIY, CONDUCTING CLINICAL TRIALS, RESEARCH ETHICS WITH VULNERABLE POPULATIONS, AND EMA METHODOLOGY AND ANALYSES. TRAINING GOALS UNDER THIS AWARD INCLUDE DEVELOPING EXPERTISE IN DESIGN AND METHODS FOR CLINICAL TRIALS OF PSYCHOSOCIAL INTERVENTIONS, ETHICAL DECISION MAKING AND SAFETY MONITORING IN RESEARCH WITH VULNERABLE POPULATIONS, DESIGN AND ANALYSIS OF INTENSIVE LONGITUDINAL DATA (E.G., EMA), AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. THIS AWARD WILL ALLOW ME TO FURTHER DEVELOP MY SKILLS AS AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCHER AND PREPARE ME FOR A SUCCESSFUL, INDEPENDENT RESEARCH CAREER FOCUSED ON PROMOTING EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENTS FOR REDUCING STB IN YOUTH.

description: IRRITABILITY AS A SIGNAL OF PERINATAL DEPRESSION: IDENTIFYING NOVEL CLINICAL, ENDOCRINE, AND NEUROBEHAVIORAL SIGNATURES OF RISK IN PREGNANCY. - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT PERINATAL DEPRESSION (PND) IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF MATERNAL MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY AND IMPACTS OVER 500 MILLION PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN IN THE UNITED STATES EACH YEAR. DESPITE THE PROFOUND URGENCY OF THE MATERNAL MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS, ONLY 6-8% OF CASES RECEIVE ADEQUATE TREATMENT. WHEN LEFT UNTREATED IN PREGNANCY, PND CAN HAVE WIDE-RANGING DELETERIOUS IMPACTS: PROLONGING SUFFERING IN THE MOTHER AND CONFERRING RISK FOR POOR MENTAL AND PHYSICAL HEALTH OUTCOMES ONTO THE DEVELOPING FETUS. DETECTING EARLY, PRENATAL SIGNALS OF PND IS THEREFORE ESSENTIAL TO FACILITATE PREVENTION. RECENT EXPERIMENTAL WORK IN NON-PREGNANT WOMEN SUGGESTS THAT IRRITABILITY, A PERVASIVE YET UNDERRECOGNIZED AFFECTIVE SYMPTOM, IS A PLAUSIBLE EARLY INDICATOR OF PND THAT CAN BE TRIGGERED BY THE HORMONAL CHANGES OF PREGNANCY. HOWEVER, THE RELATION BETWEEN ENDOGENOUS HORMONE FLUCTUATIONS AND MOOD, INCLUDING IRRITABILITY, HAS BEEN UNDERSTUDIED IN PREGNANCY. THE PROPOSED K23 PROJECT WILL THUS EMPLOY A PROSPECTIVE, LONGITUDINAL STUDY DESIGN TO IDENTIFY EARLY EMERGING CLINICAL AND NEUROBEHAVIORAL SIGNATURES OF PND DURING PREGNANCY. WE WILL TEST STUDY AIMS IN A SAMPLE OF 78 PREGNANT, EUTHYMIC INDIVIDUALS. RISK FOR PND WILL BE STRATIFIED. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE RECRUITED EARLY IN PREGNANCY AND FOLLOWED TO 6 WEEKS POSTPARTUM. URINARY METABOLITES OF ESTRADIOL (E1G) AND MOOD SYMPTOMS WILL BE ASSESSED FOR 30 CONSECUTIVE DAYS DURING THE 2ND TRIMESTER. NEURAL AND BEHAVIORAL RESPONSE TO THREAT AND FRUSTRATIVE NON-REWARD, TWO KEY DIMENSIONS OF IRRITABILITY, WILL BE ASSESSED DURING A SERIES OF EEG TASKS, ADMINISTERED AT THE END OF THE HORMONE COLLECTION PERIOD. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT FLUCTUATIONS IN ESTRADIOL DURING PREGNANCY TRIGGER IRRITABILITY FOR SOME BUT NOT ALL WOMEN, AND THAT IRRITABILITY IS AN EARLY SIGNAL OF PND. TO ACCOMPLISH THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS APPLICATION, WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) TO TEST THE EXTENT TO WHICH E1G-IRRITABILITY SENSITIVITY STRENGTH (I.E., THE DEGREE TO WHICH DAY-TO-DAY E1G FLUCTUATIONS RELATE TO CHANGES IN IRRITABLE MOOD) IN THE 2ND TRIMESTER PREDICTS PND OUTCOMES; 2) TO DETERMINE THE EXTENT TO WHICH DYSFUNCTIONAL THREAT PROCESSING CHARACTERIZES PRENATAL E1G-IRRITABILITY SENSITIVITY STRENGTH AND PREDICTS PND OUTCOMES; AND 3) TO DETERMINE THE EXTENT TO WHICH DYSFUNCTIONAL REWARD PROCESSING CHARACTERIZES PRENATAL E1G-IRRITABILITY SENSITIVITY STRENGTH AND PREDICTS PND OUTCOMES. CAREER GOAL: MY LONG- TERM CAREER GOAL IS TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENTLY FUNDED CLINICAL RESEARCHER, CARRYING OUT A PROGRAM OF RESEARCH THAT BRIDGES THE GAP BETWEEN MECHANISTIC SCIENCE AND CLINICAL INTERVENTIONS FOR PERINATAL MENTAL HEALTH. CAREER DEVELOPMENT: THIS APPLICATION WILL PROVIDE ME WITH THE NECESSARY TRAINING AND MENTORSHIP TO ACHIEVE THIS CAREER OBJECTIVE. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH COMPLEMENTS MY PREVIOUS RESEARCH EXPERIENCE AND KNOWLEDGE WITH NEW TECHNICAL, PROFESSIONAL, AND SCIENTIFIC SKILLS IN REPRODUCTIVE ENDOCRINOLOGY, LONGITUDINAL STATISTICAL ANALYSES, AND EEG RESEARCH METHODS, TO DEVELOP A UNIQUE AND COMPETITIVE RESEARCH NICHE.

description: SPACED TRANSCRANIAL DIRECT CURRENT STIMULATION FOR TREATMENT-RESISTANT DEPRESSION: A HOME-BASED RANDOMIZED SHAM-CONTROLLED TRIAL AND BIOMARKERS OF RESPONSE - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT UP TO 55% OF PATIENTS WITH MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER (MDD) FAIL TO RESPOND TO STANDARD TREATMENTS AND PROGRESS TO TREATMENT-RESISTANT DEPRESSION (TRD). THE NEUROPLASTICITY DEFICIT HYPOTHESIS OF DEPRESSION—CENTERED ON DISRUPTED EXCITATORY AND INHIBITORY SIGNALING AND IMPAIRED SYNAPTIC REMODELING—OFFERS A COMPELLING FRAMEWORK FOR DEVELOPING NOVEL INTERVENTIONS. CURRENT INTERVENTIONAL PSYCHIATRY APPROACHES SUCH AS ELECTROCONVULSIVE THERAPY, KETAMINE, AND REPETITIVE TRANSCRANIAL MAGNETIC STIMULATION TARGET NEUROPLASTICITY BUT LACK SCALABILITY. TRANSCRANIAL DIRECT CURRENT STIMULATION (TDCS) HAS EMERGED AS A PROMISING ALTERNATIVE THAT IS SAFE, COST-EFFECTIVE, AND SUITABLE FOR REMOTE, HOME-BASED DELIVERY. HOWEVER, CLINICAL TRIALS USING CONVENTIONAL ONCE-DAILY TDCS PROTOCOLS IN TRD HAVE YIELDED MIXED RESULTS, LIKELY DUE TO SUBTHERAPEUTIC DOSING. OUR GROUP DEVELOPED A NOVEL “SPACED” TDCS PROTOCOL, INVOLVING MULTIPLE DAILY SESSIONS SEPARATED BY SHORT INTERVALS TO BETTER ENGAGE LATE- PHASE NEUROPLASTICITY, WHICH SHOWED PROMISING PRELIMINARY THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS. IN ADDITION TO IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS AND SCALABILITY OF TDCS, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED TO ELUCIDATE ITS NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS. TRANSCRANIAL MAGNETIC STIMULATION COMBINED WITH ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAPHY (TMS-EEG) ENABLES CAUSAL, REAL-TIME ASSESSMENT OF CORTICAL EXCITABILITY AND INHIBITION THROUGH TMS-EVOKED POTENTIALS. RESTING-STATE EEG (RSEEG) PROVIDES A COMPLEMENTARY, SCALABLE TOOL FOR ASSESSING LARGE-SCALE BRAIN NETWORK DYNAMICS AND HAS SHOWN PROMISE IN PREDICTING TREATMENT RESPONSE. WE PROPOSE A RANDOMIZED, DOUBLE-BLIND SUPERIORITY TRIAL COMPARING ACTIVE VERSUS SHAM HOME-BASED SPACED TDCS IN 74 ADULTS WITH TRD. WE WILL USE TMS-EEG TO ASSESS CHANGES IN NEUROPLASTICITY, AS INDEXED BY CORTICAL EVOKED ACTIVITY (CEA), OVER THE DORSOLATERAL PREFRONTAL CORTEX (AIM 1). RSEEG METRICS, INCLUDING SPECTRAL POWER AND INTER-SITE PHASE CLUSTERING, WILL BE EXAMINED AS COMPLEMENTARY MARKERS OF LARGE-SCALE NETWORK PLASTICITY AND AS PREDICTORS OF TREATMENT RESPONSE (AIM 2). THE PRIMARY CLINICAL OUTCOME WILL BE CHANGE IN DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS MEASURED BY THE MONTGOMERY-ÅSBERG DEPRESSION RATING SCALE, TESTING THE HYPOTHESIS THAT ACTIVE SPACED TDCS IS SUPERIOR TO SHAM IN REDUCING DEPRESSION SEVERITY (AIM 3). THE APPLICANT’S CAREER DEVELOPMENT OBJECTIVES INCLUDE GAINING EXPERTISE IN NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL BIOMARKER ACQUISITION AND ANALYSIS (TMS-EEG, RSEEG), ADVANCED TRAINING IN CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN AND STATISTICAL METHODS, AND LAUNCHING AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM FOCUSED ON BIOMARKER-INFORMED NEUROMODULATION STRATEGIES FOR TRD. THE APPLICANT WILL BE MENTORED BY DR. ZAFIRIS DASKALAKIS (CHAIR, UCSD PSYCHIATRY AND TMS-EEG EXPERT), WITH CO-MENTORSHIP FROM DR. ANDRÉ BRUNONI (TDCS TRIALIST) AND DR. LAWRENCE APPELBAUM (RSEEG EXPERT). CONSULTANT DR. XIN TU WILL PROVIDE GUIDANCE IN BIOSTATISTICS AND DATA MODELING. THE APPLICANT WILL DEVELOP THE SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE NECESSARY TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENT INTERVENTIONAL PSYCHIATRY PHYSICIAN-SCIENTIST, AND HIS WORK WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE MECHANISMS AND CLINICAL UTILITY OF SPACED HOME-BASED TDCS FOR TRD.

description: UTILIZING MRI AND SENSORIMOTOR MEASURES TO PHENOTYPE ADRENOMYELONEUROPATHY PROGRESSION. - PROJECT SUMMARY ADRENOMYELONEUROPATHY (AMN), THE MOST COMMON FORM OF X-LINKED ADRENOLEUKODYSTROPHY, IS AN UNTREATABLE DISORDER WITH A HETEROGENEOUS SYMPTOM PROFILE AND PROGRESSION RATE. ADULT MALES AND FEMALES EXPERIENCE SIGNIFICANT DISABILITY DUE TO LONG-TRACT DISTAL AXONOPATHY IN THE SPINAL CORD. NOVEL THERAPIES ARE BEING DEVELOPED, BUT THE LACK OF SENSITIVE OUTCOME MEASURES AND BIOMARKERS OF PROGRESSION HAS LIMITED THE SUCCESS OF CLINICAL TRIALS. IT WAS RECENTLY SHOWN THAT QUANTITATIVE SENSORIMOTOR MEASURES CAN REFLECT PROGRESSION IN AMN. DESPITE THIS, CHALLENGES WITH SYNTHESIZING AND INTERPRETING MEANING ACROSS HUNDREDS OF DATA POINTS FOR THESE MEASURES HAS LED TO TRIAL FAILURE AND LACK OF CLARITY ON HOW TO ACCURATELY DEFINE CHANGE ACROSS THIS RARE DISEASE COHORT WITH VARIABLE DISEASE COURSE. THE OVERALL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT PHENOTYPIC SUBTYPES AND TRAJECTORIES OF DISEASE CAN BE IDENTIFIED IN AMN AND LOCALIZED TO MRI INDICES OF DAMAGE IN SPINAL CORD WHITE MATTER TRACTS. THIS HYPOTHESIS WILL BE INVESTIGATED THROUGH THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1. OBTAIN CROSS-SECTIONAL SENSORIMOTOR OUTCOME MEASURES TO DETERMINE AMN PHENOTYPIC SUBTYPES, AND CORRELATE THEM WITH SPINAL CORD DTI, QMT AND MFFE INDICES TO DEFINE THEIR NEUROANATOMIC SUBSTRATES. QUANTITATIVE SENSORIMOTOR MEASURES WILL BE OBTAINED IN A TOTAL OF 80 INDIVIDUALS WITH AMN TO DETERMINE THE PRESENCE OF DISTINCT PHENOTYPIC SUBTYPES THROUGH MACHINE LEARNING CLUSTER ANALYSIS. THE RELATIONSHIP OF PHENOTYPIC SUBTYPE CLUSTERS TO MRI ABNORMALITIES IN THE DORSAL COLUMNS AND LATERAL CORTICOSPINAL TRACTS WILL THEN BE EVALUATED. AIM 2A. DETERMINE IF LONGITUDINAL SENSORIMOTOR OUTCOME MEASURES AND LONGITUDINAL SPINAL CORD DTI, QMT, AND MFFE INDICES CHANGE OVER 2 YEARS. PUBLISHED DATA SHOWS THE FEASIBILITY OF MEASURING AMN PROGRESSION USING QUANTITATIVE SENSORIMOTOR ASSESSMENTS. AIM 2A WILL VALIDATE THIS WORK IN A PROSPECTIVE STUDY AND CONCURRENTLY EVALUATE IF ADVANCED MRI INDICES CHANGE WITHIN 2 YEARS, USING AI-BASED TOOLS AND HIGH-RESOLUTION MFFE SEQUENCES TO QUANTIFY SPINAL CORD WHITE MATTER MICROSTRUCTURAL CHANGES. AIM 2B. USE LONGITUDINAL SENSORIMOTOR OUTCOME MEASURES TO DETERMINE DISEASE TRAJECTORY CLUSTERS OVER 2 YEARS AND DETERMINE THE RELATIONSHIP OF THESE TRAJECTORIES WITH CHANGES IN SPINAL CORD DTI, QMT AND MFFE INDICES. THIS AIM WILL EVALUATE IF 2-YEAR TRAJECTORY CLUSTERING OF QUANTITATIVE SENSORIMOTOR ASSESSMENTS CAN IDENTIFY FAST VS. SLOW PROGRESSOR CLUSTERS, AS INDICATED IN THE PRELIMINARY DATA, THEN DETERMINE IF THE CLUSTERS ARE RELATED TO MRI INDICES OF SPINAL CORD PATHOLOGY. THE CANDIDATE REQUIRES ADDITIONAL TRAINING IN MRI ACQUISITION AND ANALYSIS, ADVANCED MACHINE LEARNING, AND BIOSTATISTICS TO COMPLETE THESE AIMS. THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE CRITICALLY NEEDED INFORMATION ON PHENOTYPES AND PATHOLOGICAL STRUCTURE-FUNCTION RELATIONSHIPS IN AMN. THE KNOWLEDGE GAPS ADDRESSED MAY INFORM DISEASE PROGNOSTICATION AND CONDUCT OF TRIALS. THIS APPROACH CAN ALSO BE USEFUL ACROSS OTHER LEUKODYSTROPHIES WITH MODEST SAMPLE SIZE AND HIGH-DIMENSIONAL DATA ACQUISITION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BEYOND NEUROFILAMENT: ALS PROGNOSTICATION - PROJECT ABSTRACT THE SCIENTIFIC GOAL OF THIS K23 IS TO APPLY CUTTING-EDGE PROTEOMIC, GENOMIC, AND MACHINE-LEARNING ALGORITHMS TO DEFINE ALS BIOMARKERS THAT RESOLVE CLINICAL DIFFERENCES BETWEEN AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (ALS) PATIENTS. WHILE IT HAS BEEN COMMONLY ACCEPTED THAT ALS IS A SINGLE DISEASE ENTITY, THERE IS NOW CONSIDERATION THAT IT IS, IN FACT, MULTIPLE DISEASES WITH DIFFERENT UNDERLYING MOLECULAR CAUSES. IF GENETIC AND PROTEOMIC DRIVERS OF CLINICAL VARIABILITY ARE IDENTIFIED, IT WILL BE POSSIBLE TO DEVELOP IMPROVED ALS BIOMARKER PANELS THAT CAN BE USED IN EVERYDAY CLINICAL PRACTICE AND TO IMPROVE ALS CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN. THIS K23 APPLICATION PROPOSES A 5-YEAR TRAINING PROGRAM TO PROPEL DR. ELEANOR THOMAS TOWARDS HER CAREER AS A LEADER IN ALS BIOMARKER DISCOVERY AND CLINICAL APPLICATION. DR. THOMAS WILL ACCOMPLISH THIS GOAL WITH ADDITIONAL TRAINING IN (1) PROTEOMIC NETWORK ANALYSIS AND BIOINFORMATICS (2) ANALYSIS OF WHOLE GENOME SEQUENCING DATA AND (3) DATA SCIENCE, INCLUDING MACHINE LEARNING METHODS FOR PREDICTIVE MODELING. DR. THOMAS HAS OUTLINED AN INTEGRATIVE PROGRAM OF FORMAL COURSEWORK, HANDS-ON RESEARCH TRAINING, SEMINARS, CONFERENCES, AND CONSISTENT MENTORING FROM LEADING EXPERTS IN THE FIELDS OF ALS TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH (DR. JONATHAN GLASS), NEURODEGENERATION BIOMARKER DISCOVERY (DR. NICHOLAS SEYFRIED), ALS GENOMIC ANALYSIS (DR. JOHN LANDERS), AND BIOSTATISTICS AND DATA SCIENCE (DR. VICKI HERTZBERG). LEVERAGING THE UNIQUE CLINICAL RESOURCES HELD IN THE EMORY ALS CENTER DATABASE AND BIOBANK, DR. THOMAS WILL DEFINE ALS MOLECULAR SUBGROUPS THROUGH UNSUPERVISED CLUSTERING OF PLASMA PROTEOMIC DATA AND MAP THESE TO CLINICAL FEATURES, SUCH AS AGE OF ONSET, SITE OF ONSET AND PROGRESSION RATE (AIM 1). IN AIM 2 SHE WILL INTEGRATE WHOLE-GENOME SEQUENCING WITH PROTEOMIC DATA USING PROTEIN QUANTITATIVE TRAIT LOCI (PQTL) AND PROTEOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDIES (PWAS) TO IDENTIFY GENETIC VARIANTS THAT REGULATE CIRCULATING PROTEIN ABUNDANCE AND INFLUENCE DISEASE TRAJECTORY. AIM 3 WILL DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A NEXT- GENERATION ALS SURVIVAL PREDICTION MODEL THAT COMBINES CLINICAL, PROTEOMIC, AND GENOMIC FEATURES TO ACHIEVE IMPROVED PROGNOSTIC ACCURACY. THIS WORK REPRESENTS THE LARGEST SINGLE-CENTER ALS PLASMA PROTEOMIC STUDY TO DATE AND THE LARGEST ALS PLASMA PQTL ANALYSIS. THE INTEGRATION OF PROTEOGENOMIC BIOMARKERS INTO ALS PROGNOSTIC MODELING WILL ENABLE PRECISE, INDIVIDUALIZED PREDICTION OF DISEASE PROGRESSION AND INFORM THE DESIGN OF FUTURE SUBTYPE-SPECIFIC CLINICAL TRIALS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TOWARDS CIRCUIT-BASED DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION REPROGRAMMING FOR COGNITION IN PARKINSON'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT PATIENTS WITH PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD) MAY EXPERIENCE COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT FOLLOWING DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION (DBS), A COMMON AND EFFECTIVE TREATMENT FOR MOTOR SYMPTOMS. WHEN DETECTED, THE IMPAIRMENT MAY BE REVERSED BY DBS REPROGRAMMING. PREDICTING WHICH PATIENTS WILL HAVE DBS-INDUCED COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND OFFERING TREATMENT WILL HAVE A PERSONAL BENEFIT TO A VAST NUMBER OF PATIENTS AND FAMILIES, AS WELL AS IMPORTANT PUBLIC HEALTH IMPLICATIONS FOR A SOCIETY THAT WILL BEAR THE COST OF SUPPORTING PD PATIENTS. PAST STUDIES SHOWED 1) DBS CONTACTS MORE CONNECTED TO A COGNITIVE CIRCUIT COMPRISING THE ANTERIOR CINGULATE, CAUDATE NUCLEUS, HIPPOCAMPUS, AND COGNITIVE REGIONS OF THE CEREBELLUM ARE ASSOCIATED WITH DIMINISHED GLOBAL COGNITIVE STATUS 1 YEAR AFTER DBS SURGERY; 2) HIGHER CONNECTIVITY BETWEEN THE DBS CONTACTS AND COGNITIVE CIRCUIT IS ASSOCIATED WITH IMPAIRMENT IN WORKING MEMORY; AND 3) IMPAIRMENT CAN BE REVERSED BY CHANGING THE DBS CONTACTS CONFIGURATION TO REDUCE THE COGNITIVE CIRCUIT CONNECTIVITY (REPROGRAMMING) WHILE MAINTAINING MOTOR BENEFIT. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO BUILD ON THESE STUDIES AND ADDRESS THEIR LIMITATIONS. THE PI HAS LOCALIZED DBS ELECTRODES IN PD PATIENTS FOLLOWED FOR DBS PROGRAMMING AT BRIGHAM AND WOMEN’S HOSPITAL (BWH, N=120, 0.5-10 YEARS POST-SURGERY), AND USED AN ALGORITHM TO DETERMINE THE COGNITIVELY OPTIMAL DBS CONFIGURATION (I.E., THE CONTACTS LEAST CONNECTED TO THE COGNITIVE CIRCUIT) FOR EACH INDIVIDUAL. AIM 1 OF THIS STUDY WILL EVALUATE WHETHER CONNECTIVITY BETWEEN THE COGNITIVE CIRCUIT AND THE NEUROLOGIST-DETERMINED/MOTORICALLY OPTIMAL DBS CONFIGURATION CORRELATES WITH GLOBAL AND DOMAIN-SPECIFIC COGNITIVE STATUS AS MEASURED BY DEMENTIA RATING SCALE-2 AND A NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL TEST BATTERY. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS WHETHER CONNECTIVITY-BASED DBS REPROGRAMMING IMPROVES COGNITIVE TASK PERFORMANCE WHILE MAINTAINING MOTOR BENEFITS, IN A 2-DAY, DOUBLE-BLINDED, CROSSOVER REPROGRAMMING CLINICAL TRIAL COMPARING PATIENTS’ MOTORICALLY OPTIMAL DBS CONFIGURATION WITH THE COGNITIVELY OPTIMAL CONFIGURATION. COGNITION WILL BE MEASURED USING A 2-BACK WORKING MEMORY TASK AND A SUBSET OF THE AIM 1 COGNITIVE BATTERY; MOTORIC STATUS WILL BE ASSESSED WITH THE MOVEMENT DISORDER SOCIETY-UNIFIED PD RATING SCALE, PART III. THIS PROJECT ALIGNS WITH NINDS PRIORITIES TO IDENTIFY BIOMARKERS FOR NON-MOTOR SYMPTOMS OF PD AND PROVIDE PROOF OF CONCEPT FOR FUTURE TRIALS. THE RESEARCH AND TRAINING PLAN WILL EQUIP THE PI TO LEAD AN R01- FUNDED TRIAL AND ADVANCE PERSONALIZED CIRCUIT-BASED NEUROMODULATION THERAPY, AND HER MENTORS, ADVISORS, AND THE TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT AT BWH WILL ENSURE HER SUCCESS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DIFFERENTIATING THE EFFECTS OF DIRECT ELECTRICAL STIMULATION ON EPILEPTIFORM ACTIVITY IN THE HUMAN BRAIN - ABSTRACT DIRECT ELECTRICAL STIMULATION HAS BECOME A STANDARD OF MEDICATION-REFRACTORY EPILEPSY CARE FOR BOTH DIAGNOSTIC INVESTIGATION, VIA STIMULATION-INDUCED SEIZURE MAPPING IN PATIENTS UNDERGOING AN INTRACRANIAL EEG (IEEG) EPILEPSY MONITORING UNIT HOSPITAL STAY, AND THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES, VIA CHRONICALLY IMPLANTED NEUROSTIMULATION DEVICES. HOWEVER, THERAPEUTIC NEUROSTIMULATION DEVICES, WHICH WORK BY REDUCING EPILEPTIFORM ACTIVITY, OFTEN FAIL TO ACHIEVE SUSTAINED SEIZURE CONTROL IN A TIMELY AND CONTROLLED FASHION. THIS PROPOSAL INVESTIGATES HOW INDIVIDUAL, STRUCTURAL HUMAN BRAIN NETWORKS ENABLE NEUROSTIMULATION TO INDUCE, INHIBIT, AND TERMINATE EPILEPTIFORM ACTIVITY. A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF NEUROSTIMULATION’S VARIED EFFECTS ON THE HUMAN BRAIN COULD HERALD NOVEL APPROACHES TO EPILEPSY NEUROSTIMULATION WITH RAPID, PREDICTABLE, AND CONSISTENT SEIZURE CONTROL. THIS K23 MENTORED PATIENT-ORIENTED RESEARCH CAREER DEVELOPMENT AWARD PROPOSAL OUTLINES A 5-YEAR TRAINING PROGRAM FOR THE MENTORED RESEARCHER TO GET TRAINING AND MENTORSHIP IN IEEG AND NEUROSTIMULATION. THE CANDIDATE’S 3-PART PROPOSAL SEEKS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW NEUROSTIMULATION CAN INDUCE, INHIBIT, AND TERMINATE EPILEPTIFORM ACTIVITY. FIRST, THE CANDIDATE WILL ANALYZE THE SEIZURE CHARACTERISTICS OF PATIENTS WITH EPILEPSY IN THE IEEG EPILEPSY MONITORING UNIT WITH DIRECT ELECTRICAL STIMULATION TO INDUCE SEIZURES (AS PART OF STANDARD CLINICAL CARE) TO DETERMINE IF STRONGER BRAIN CONNECTIVITY, VIA WHITE MATTER CONNECTIONS SEEN ON DIFFUSION IMAGING, IS ASSOCIATED WITH GREATER INDUCTION OF TYPICAL SEIZURE TYPES. SECOND, THE CANDIDATE WILL PROSPECTIVELY STIMULATE THE THALAMUS OF PATIENTS WITH EPILEPSY IN THE IEEG EPILEPSY MONITORING UNIT, AT DIFFERENT FREQUENCIES AND DURATIONS, TO EXAMINE IF STRONGER BRAIN CONNECTIVITY WITH INHIBITORY STIMULATION IS ASSOCIATED WITH DECREASED EPILEPTIFORM ACTIVITY. THIRD, THE CANDIDATE WILL RETROSPECTIVELY EVALUATE IF PATIENTS WITH EPILEPSY AND CHRONICALLY, THALAMIC-IMPLANTED RESPONSIVE NEUROSTIMULATION DEVICES CAN UNDERGO WEAKER NEUROSTIMULATION TO TERMINATE SEIZURES AND IMPROVE SEIZURE CONTROL (SHORTER SEIZURE DURATION) WHEN THEY HAVE STRONGER BRAIN CONNECTIVITY. DURING THE K23, THE CANDIDATE WILL INVESTIGATE UNDERLYING STRUCTURAL BRAIN NETWORKS THAT DICTATE THE ABILITY OF NEUROSTIMULATION TO INDUCE, INHIBIT, AND TERMINATE EPILEPTIFORM ACTIVITY. THE CANDIDATE IS A BOARD-CERTIFIED NEUROLOGIST AND BOARD-CERTIFIED EPILEPTOLOGIST WITH A PRIOR MASTER’S DEGREE AND NIH-FUNDED TRAINING PRIMARILY IN NEUROIMAGING WITH SIGNIFICANT EXPERIENCE IN IEEG. THIS K23 WILL SERVE AS A STEPPINGSTONE TO DEVELOP THE CANDIDATE’S EXPERTISE IN IEEG AND NEUROSTIMULATION IN ANTICIPATION OF A FUTURE R01. AS THE YOUNG INVESTIGATOR TRANSITIONS FROM A MENTORED TO INDEPENDENT RESEARCH CAREER, THE CANDIDATE WILL COMPLETE COURSEWORK AND TRAINING IN NEURAL SIGNAL ANALYSIS TECHNIQUES, IMAGING ANALYSES, STATISTICS, MEDICAL DEVICES, AND CLINICAL TRIALS. THE CANDIDATE’S TRAINING WILL BE LED BY AN EXPERT MENTOR, WHO IS A LEADER IN THE FIELDS OF IEEG ANALYSIS, NEUROSTIMULATION, AND NEUROIMAGING, AND OVERSEEN BY A WORLD-CLASS TRAINING ADVISORY COMMITTEE WITH BACKGROUNDS IN EPILEPSY, MACHINE LEARNING, NEUROIMAGING, COMPUTATIONAL NEUROSCIENCE, AND NEUROSTIMULATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MENTORSHIP IN PATIENT-ORIENTED RESEARCH TO IMPROVE HEALTH OF OLDER ADULTS WITH DIABETES - ABSTRACT MORE THAN 16.5 MILLION OLDER ADULTS, OR 29.2% OF U.S. ADULTS ≥65 YEARS, ARE LIVING WITH DIABETES. OLDER ADULTS WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES (T2D) ARE A HIGHLY HETEROGENEOUS POPULATION, WITH WIDE VARIATION IN CLINICAL COMPLEXITY, FUNCTIONAL STATUS, AND AVAILABLE PERSONAL, COMMUNITY, AND CLINICAL SUPPORTS, WHICH COLLECTIVELY IMPACT THEIR CAPACITY FOR SELF- MANAGEMENT, ACCESS TO HEALTHCARE, AND HEALTH. REDUCING THE DISABILITY, MORBIDITY, AND MORTALITY CAUSED BY T2D IN OLDER ADULTS THEREFORE REQUIRES OPTIMIZED SELECTION OF T2D PHARMACOTHERAPY, ACCESSIBLE DELIVERY OF HIGH QUALITY T2D CARE, AND MITIGATION OF ADVERSE SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH (SDOH). THE GROWING POPULATION OF OLDER ADULTS WITH T2D AND THE STAGNANT AND UNACCEPTABLY HIGH RATES OF POTENTIALLY PREVENTABLE DIABETES-RELATED DISABILITY, MORBIDITY, AND MORTALITY DESPITE MAJOR ADVANCES IN AVAILABLE T2D PHARMACOTHERAPIES SIGNAL THE NEED FOR RIGOROUS PATIENT-ORIENTED RESEARCH FOCUSED ON T2D IN OLDER ADULTS. THE DUAL OBJECTIVES OF THIS MIDCAREER INVESTIGATOR AWARD IN PATIENT-ORIENTED RESEARCH (K24) ARE: 1) TO PROVIDE DR. MCCOY WITH THE TIME AND RESOURCES NECESSARY TO MENTOR AND SUPPORT PROMISING CLINICAL INVESTIGATORS POISED FOR CAREERS IN PATIENT-ORIENTED RESEARCH AND COMMITTED TO IMPROVING THE HEALTH OF OLDER ADULTS WITH T2D; AND 2) TO GENERATE ESSENTIAL EVIDENCE ON THE OPTIMAL TREATMENT OF T2D IN OLDER ADULTS (AIMS 1-2) AND ON THE DISTRIBUTION AND HEALTH IMPACTS OF MULTI-LEVEL, MULTI-DIMENSIONAL DRIVERS OF HEALTH IN THIS HIGHLY HETEROGENEOUS POPULATION (AIM 3), WITH OPPORTUNITIES FOR MENTEES TO CONDUCT IMPACTFUL, DISTINCT RESEARCH INVESTIGATIONS USING A WIDE RANGE OF RESEARCH METHODS, LEVERAGING DR. MCCOY’S ROBUST RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE, AND AS PART OF A THRIVING INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH TEAM. THE PROPOSAL’S RESEARCH AND MENTORING ACTIVITIES WILL BE CONDUCTED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND SCHOOL OF MEDICINE, WHICH HAS A STRONG HISTORY OF TRAINING PHYSICIAN SCIENTISTS AND CLINICAL INVESTIGATORS IN PATIENT-ORIENTED RESEARCH, A WELL-DEVELOPED INFRASTRUCTURE FOR EDUCATION AND RESEARCH, AND A LARGE POOL OF TALENTED TRAINEES AND JUNIOR FACULTY FROM DIFFERENT DISCIPLINES AND BACKGROUNDS. DR. MCCOY’S INTERDISCIPLINARY NIH- AND PCORI-FUNDED RESEARCH PROGRAM IS IDEALLY SUITED TO SUPPORT MENTEES ACROSS THE UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND SYSTEM BY PROVIDING ACCESS TO RICH REAL-WORLD DATA; STRONG PARTNERSHIPS ACROSS THE CLINICAL PRACTICE TO FACILITATE PRIMARY DATA COLLECTION; SUPPORT OF AN EXCEPTIONAL TEAM OF COLLABORATORS AND METHODOLOGISTS WITH COMPLEMENTARY EXPERTISE IN ADVANCED CAUSAL INFERENCE METHODS, GEOSPATIAL ANALYSES, IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE, AND PRAGMATIC TRIALS; EXTENSIVE CAREER DEVELOPMENT AND TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES; AND A STRONG TRACK RECORD OF DEDICATED AND SUPPORTIVE MENTORSHIP. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO STRENGTHEN DR. MCCOY’S MENTORSHIP CAPABILITIES AND GENERATE NOVEL AVENUES FOR HER MENTEES TO SUCCEED IN BOLSTERING THEIR INDEPENDENT RESEARCH CAREERS, WHILE SIMULTANEOUSLY FURTHERING DR. MCCOY’S CONTINUED CAREER DEVELOPMENT AS A PHYSICIAN SCIENTIST, MENTOR, AND LEADER IN PATIENT-ORIENTED RESEARCH IN T2D IN OLDER ADULTS.

description: PRECISION ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY USING MULTIMODALITY IMAGING - PROJECT SUMMARY  CARDIAC ARRHYTHMIAS SUCH AS ATRIAL TACHYCARDIA, ATRIAL FLUTTER, PREMATURE VENTRICULAR COMPLEXES AND VENTRICULAR TACHYCARDIA ARE A MAJOR CAUSE OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY. CURRENTLY THE STANDARD OF CARE TO AID ELECTROPHYSIOLOGISTS IN LOCALIZING ARRHYTHMIAS IS UTILIZING THE NONINVASIVE DIAGNOSTIC TOOL OF THE 12-LEAD ELECTROCARDIOGRAM (ECG). OUR VISION IS THAT PRECISION IMAGING USING COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (CT) AND ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY WILL ENABLE 3-DIMENSIONAL (3D) VISUALIZATION AND ENABLE UNDERSTANDING OF ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS AND LOCALIZATION OF AREAS OF ARRHYTHMOGENESIS. ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY DATA ARE USUALLY RECORDED USING ELECTROANATOMICAL MAPPING AND THIS DATA CAN PROVIDE UNIQUE DATA AS TO CARDIAC ANATOMY, TISSUE MOTION, TISSUE STRUCTURE, AND ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL FUNCTION. ELECTROANATOMICAL MAPPING DATA WILL BE USED TO QUANTIFY CERTAIN PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL FEATURES INCLUDE LEFT ATRIAL TISSUE THICKNESS, CHAMBER SURFACE AREA, CHAMBER VOLUME, SPHERICITY, SHAPE, NUMBER/CONFIGURATION OF PULMONARY VEINS, TOTAL ACTIVATION TIME, REGIONAL AND GLOBAL CONDUCTION VELOCITY, MEAN VOLTAGE, PERCENTAGE LOW VOLTAGE, LOW VOLTAGE AREA, ELECTROGRAM DURATION AND FRACTIONATION. OVER TEN YEARS, THE COLLABORATIVE TEAM EFFORT BETWEEN CARDIAC ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY AND BIOMEDICAL ENGINEERING AT COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IRVING MEDICAL CENTER, HAS DEVELOPED NOVEL ULTRASOUND, COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY IMAGING TECHNIQUES AND MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS, TO NON-INVASIVELY LOCALIZE ARRHYTHMIAS. WE PROPOSE THREE AIMS TO VALIDATE PREDICTIONS WITH COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY TO WITH HIGH DENSITY ACTIVATION MAPS (HDAM) ACQUIRED DURING INVASIVE ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY STUDY. WE PROPOSE THAT CT AND ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY IMAGING AREAS INITIATING ARRHYTHMOGENESIS CAN (1) PROVIDE TARGET LOCALIZATION AND IMPROVE PROCEDURAL PLANNING, (2) TO DETERMINE HOW STRUCTURAL ALTERATIONS SUCH AS SCAR, FIBROSIS, FAT, CHAMBER DILATATION AFFECTS ELECTROMECHANICAL COUPLING IN CARDIAC ARRHYTHMIAS (3) DETERMINE HOW PREPROCEDURAL IMAGING PRIOR TO EPS AND ABLATION CAN IDENTIFY TRIGGERS FOR ATRIAL FIBRILLATION. THIS PROJECT PRESENTS A STRONG TEAM WITH MULTI-MODALITY IMAGING EXPERTISE IN ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY AND CARDIAC COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY AND MACHINE LEARNING TO PREDICT AREAS OF TARGET ABLATION BASED ON LOCATION ON ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY AND CT. THIS PROJECT IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT TESTS THE SUCCESS OF NOVEL IMAGING TECHNIQUES AGAINST CURRENT STANDARD OF CARE, AND BECAUSE IT USES NOVEL IMAGING STRATEGIES TO TEST THE FUNDAMENTAL MECHANISMS THAT CAUSE CARDIAC ARRHYTHMOGENESIS. USING A COLLABORATIVE CROSS DISCIPLINARY INTEGRATED EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH WE WILL ENABLE A WIDE BREADTH OF MENTORSHIP INCLUDING IMAGING SPECIALISTS, BIOMEDICAL ENGINEERS AND MACHINE LEARNING SPECIALISTS TO IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF ARRHYTHMIC MECHANISMS WHILE ENABLING PHYSICIAN SCIENTISTS TO IMPROVE THEIR UNDERSTANDING OF ADVANCES IN IMAGING TECHNIQUES, CELLULAR ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY, ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY AND BIOSTATISTICS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PRIME STUDY - PREECLAMPSIA RISK IDENTIFICATION, MITIGATION, AND PREVENTION IN TYPE 2 DIABETES THROUGH RESEARCH AND MENTORSHIP - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT UP TO ONE-THIRD OF PREGNANT PATIENTS WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES (T2D) DEVELOP PREECLAMPSIA, A MAJOR CAUSE OF MATERNAL MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY AND A RISK FACTOR FOR FUTURE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD). OFFSPRING ALSO FACE INCREASED LIFELONG RISKS FOR OBESITY, DIABETES, AND CVD. THUS, PREVENTING THE DEVELOPMENT OF PREECLAMPSIA OFFERS THE POTENTIAL TO IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES ACROSS GENERATIONS. CURRENT CHALLENGES INCLUDE INADEQUATE EARLY RISK IDENTIFICATION, LIMITED UNDERSTANDING OF MODIFIABLE FACTORS SUCH AS BLOOD PRESSURE (BP) AND GLYCEMIC CONTROL DURING PREGNANCY, AND INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE FOR EFFECTIVE PREVENTION STRATEGIES, PARTICULARLY IN T2D. THE ONGOING R01-FUNDED CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITORING FOR MANAGEMENT OF T2D IN PREGNANCY (CGM2) TRIAL OFFERS A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP, ENROLLING 564 DIVERSE PREGNANT PATIENTS WITH T2D AND COLLECTING COMPREHENSIVE LONGITUDINAL DATA ON SOCIAL DRIVERS, BP AND GLYCEMIC CONTROL, HEALTH BEHAVIORS, MEDICATION USE, AND BIOSPECIMENS. LEVERAGING THIS COHORT, THE PROPOSED PREECLAMPSIA RISK IDENTIFICATION, MITIGATION, AND PREVENTION IN T2D THROUGH RESEARCH AND MENTORSHIP (PRIME) STUDY WILL INTEGRATE INNOVATIVE INVESTIGATION WITH A FORMAL, STRUCTURED MENTORING PLATFORM TO TRAIN EARLY-STAGE CLINICIAN SCIENTISTS ASPIRING TO PATIENT-ORIENTED RESEARCH (POR) CAREERS IN WOMEN’S HEALTH. OUR SCIENTIFIC AIMS INCLUDE: 1) TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A RISK PREDICTION MODEL FOR PREECLAMPSIA IN PATIENTS WITH T2D BY INTEGRATING CLINICAL AND SOCIAL FACTORS AND CVD BIOMARKERS FROM EARLY PREGNANCY, 2) TO QUANTIFY THE EFFECT OF BP AND GLYCEMIC CONTROL DURING PREGNANCY ON PREECLAMPSIA, AND 3) TO EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF ASPIRIN REGIMEN (DOSE AND TIMING) ON PREECLAMPSIA PREVENTION IN PREGNANT PATIENTS WITH T2D. FURTHERMORE, IMMERSION OF MENTEES IN THE CGM2 AND PRIME TRIALS WILL PROMOTE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE FOLLOWING MENTORING AIMS: 1) PROVIDE MENTEES HANDS-ON TRAINING IN POR INCLUDING PARTICIPANT RECRUITMENT, INTERVENTION IMPLEMENTATION, DATA COLLECTION AND MANAGEMENT, BIOSPECIMEN PROCESSING, AND MULTIVARIABLE MODELING, BUILDING FOUNDATIONAL SKILLS FOR INDEPENDENT RESEARCH IN WOMEN’S HEALTH, 2) ADVANCE MENTEES UNDERSTANDING AND SKILLS IN HUMAN SUBJECTS PROTECTION, SCIENTIFIC WRITING, PEER-REVIEW, AND PRESENTING AND DISSEMINATING RESULTS, AND 3) TEACH MENTEES HOW TO FORMULATE NOVEL RESEARCH QUESTIONS AND BUILD A ROBUST NETWORK OF INTERDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATORS THAT ADVANCE THEIR CAREER DEVELOPMENT AND EMPOWER THEM TO INDEPENDENTLY DESIGN RIGOROUS POR STUDIES. IT WILL ALSO FACILITATE FURTHER CAREER DEVELOPMENT OF THE PD/PI BY 1) EXPANDING METHODOLOGIC EXPERTISE IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MACHINE LEARNING, 2) BUILDING ADVANCED DISSEMINATION AND IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE CAPACITY 3) ENHANCING RESEARCH MENTORSHIP AND LEADERSHIP SKILLS. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL INSPIRE THE NEXT GENERATION OF CLINICIAN-SCIENTISTS IN ADVANCING WOMEN’S HEALTH RESEARCH AND INFORM FUTURE STUDIES OF TARGETED SURVEILLANCE AND INTERVENTIONS TO PREVENT PREECLAMPSIA AND CVD LATER IN LIFE, THUS IMPROVING THE LIVES OF PREGNANT PATIENTS WITH T2D AND THEIR CHILDREN.

description: UNDERSTANDING THE IMPACT OF SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS AND VAGINAL MICROBIOME IMBALANCE ON CERVICAL CANCER DEVELOPMENT IN MALI: IMPLICATIONS FOR NEW PREVENTION STRATEGIES - HUMAN PAPILLOMAVIRUS (HPV) IS INDEED THE MOST COMMON SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTION (STIS) IN THE UNITED STATES (U.S.), WITH THE VAST MAJORITY OF SEXUALLY ACTIVE PEOPLE CONTRACTING AT LEAST ONE TYPE OF HPV IN THEIR LIFETIME. IN SUB- SAHARAN AFRICA (SSA), NEARLY ALL WOMEN LIVING WITH HIV WHO DEVELOP CERVICAL CANCER (CC) ARE CO-INFECTED WITH HPV (~99%) AND CC REMAINS ONE OF THE LEADING CAUSES OF CANCER-RELATED DEATHS AMONG WOMEN, WHERE THE BURDEN IS DISPROPORTIONATELY HIGH (~60% OF ALL CC CASES OCCUR IN THIS REGION), YET FEW OF THE ELIGIBLE WOMEN ARE SCREENED DESPITE FREE SERVICES. THIS MAKES MALI (A COUNTRY IN SSA) A VALUABLE SETTING FOR CONDUCTING SUCH RESEARCH AND FOR APPLYING LESSONS LEARNED TO BENEFIT U.S. AND GLOBAL HEALTH. WHILE MOST HPV INFECTIONS (80%-90%) ARE NATURALLY CLEARED BY THE HOST IMMUNE SYSTEM, PERSISTENT INFECTION WITH HIGH-RISK HPV (HRHPV) TYPES MARKEDLY INCREASES THE RISK OF ONCOGENIC PROGRESSION, ULTIMATELY LEADING TO INVASIVE CC. THIS PROGRESSION UNFOLDS OVER SEVERAL YEARS, PROVIDING A LONG WINDOW FOR PREVENTIVE MEASURES. CURRENTLY, THERE ARE NO APPROVED TREATMENTS TO DIRECTLY ELIMINATE HPV INFECTION, UNDERSCORING THE IMPORTANCE OF ADDRESSING AND MITIGATING THE FACTORS (E.G., CO-INFECTION WITH OTHER STIS) THAT PROMOTE HPV PERSISTENCE AS A KEY STRATEGY FOR CC PREVENTION AND CONTROL. RECENT STUDIES HIGHLY SUGGEST THAT CO-INFECTION WITH OTHER STIS (CO-STIS) MAY FACILITATE HPV PERSISTENCE AND ACCELERATE THE PROGRESSION TO CC. THESE FINDINGS HIGHLIGHT A CRUCIAL OPPORTUNITY TO DESIGN, TEST, AND IMPLEMENT INTEGRATED DUAL-SCREENING APPROACHES THAT DETECT AND ADDRESS BOTH HPV AND CO-STIS WITH APPROPRIATE TREATMENTS, AS A STRATEGY TO PREVENT PERSISTENCE OF HPV AND ULTIMATELY, CC. A BALANCED MICROBIOME, USUALLY DOMINATED BY LACTOBACILLUS SPECIES, HELPS SUSTAIN A PROTECTIVE ACIDIC ENVIRONMENT THAT INHIBITS THE GROWTH OF PATHOGENIC MICROORGANISMS AND REDUCES THE RISK OF STIS. ITS IMBALANCE HAS BEEN ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED SUSCEPTIBILITY TO STIS AND A GREATER LIKELIHOOD OF PERSISTENT HPV INFECTIONS. FOR THIS K43, WE SEEK TO CONDUCT A LONGITUDINAL COHORT STUDY, WHICH WILL INCLUDE BOTH HIV AND NON-HIV WOMEN, USING CLINICAL DATA, SELF-SAMPLED MICROBIOLOGY DIAGNOSTICS, AND METAGENOMIC ANALYSIS TO DETERMINE THE ROLE OF CO-STIS AND VAGINAL MICROBIOME IN HPV PERSISTENCE AND CERVICAL CARCINOGENESIS. WE WILL ALSO DEVELOP A PREDICTIVE FRAMEWORK TO GUIDE DUAL-SCREENING STRATEGIES, PREDICTIVE TOOLS, AND TARGETED PREVENTIVE INTERVENTIONS TAILORED TO CC CONTROL. THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM OVERALL ADDRESSES AN IMPORTANT EPIDEMIOLOGICAL GAP BY ADVANCING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW CO-OCCURRING STIS AND VAGINAL MICROBIOME IMBALANCE CONTRIBUTE TO HRHPV PERSISTENCE AND CERVICAL CARCINOGENESIS, WHICH WILL BENEFIT WOMEN IN LOW-RESOURCE SETTINGS IN MALI, U.S., AND WORLDWIDE.

description: A UNIVERSAL TOOLKIT FOR SINGLE-CELL SOMATIC MUTATION DETECTION AND ITS APPLICATION TO AGING-RELATED PROCESSES - PROJECT SUMMARY UNLIKE THE FIXED NATURE OF INHERITED GENETIC VARIANTS AND MUTATIONS THAT OCCUR BEFORE FORMATION OF THE ZYGOTE, POST-ZYGOTIC SOMATIC MUTATIONS (SMS) ACCUMULATE THROUGHOUT LIFE. ALTHOUGH THE MOST WELL-STUDIED ADVERSE EFFECT OF SMS IS CANCER, IN WHICH ONCOGENIC SMS CAUSE CLONAL OUTGROWTHS THAT DEVELOP INTO TUMORS, IT HAS BEEN APPRECIATED FOR DECADES THAT SMS CAN LEAD TO OTHER FORMS OF DISEASE. SMS MAY ALSO PLAY A ROLE IN “HEALTHY” AGING BY GRADUAL LOSS OF FUNCTION—INDEED, ORGANISM LIFESPANS INVERSELY CORRELATE WITH ORGANISM-SPECIFIC RATES OF SM ACCUMULATION—BUT THE EXTENT OF THIS CONTRIBUTION IS UNKNOWN. THIS IS LARGELY DUE TO THE DIFFICULTY IN DETECTING AGING-ASSOCIATED SMS BECAUSE, BY VIRTUE OF BEING ACQUIRED LATE IN LIFE, THEY ARE MOSTLY PRESENT IN A TINY FRACTION OF THE ORGANISM’S CELLS, UNLESS A CLONAL OUTGROWTH OCCURS AS IS THE CASE IN CANCER. THESE RARE SMS ARE DIFFICULT TO DIFFERENTIATE FROM ERRORS GENERATED BY STANDARD SEQUENCING TECHNIQUES. OVER THE PAST TEN YEARS, SINGLE CELL WHOLE GENOME SEQUENCING (SCWGS) AND ACCURATE SINGLE DNA MOLECULE SAMPLING-IN-BULK TECHNIQUES (“DUPLEX SEQUENCING”) HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED TO ADDRESS THIS LIMITATION AND ENABLE THE STUDY OF SMS IN HEALTHY AGING TISSUE. SCWGS POTENTIALLY YIELDS ACCESS TO ALL SMS PRESENT IN THE CELL, BUT THE WHOLE GENOME AMPLIFICATION PROCESS GENERATES SUBSTANTIAL ARTIFACTS THAT CONFOUND STANDARD MUTATION DETECTION METHODS. DUPLEX SEQUENCING IDENTIFIES ARTIFACTS USING MOLECULAR BARCODES, BUT ONLY COVERS A SMALL FRACTION OF THE GENOME AND CANNOT GIVE INFORMATION ON WHICH SMS ARE PRESENT IN THE SAME CELL. ALTHOUGH SMS HAVE BEEN DETECTED IN OTHER SINGLE CELL DATA (E.G., RNA- AND ATAC-SEQ), THESE METHODS CAN ONLY RECOVER SMS SHARED BY MANY CELLS, MISSING MANY AGE-RELATED SMS. I SPENT MY GRADUATE AND POSTGRADUATE STUDIES DEVELOPING METHODS TO ACCURATELY ANALYZE SCWGS DATA, ALLOWING US TO INFER THE RATES AND PATTERNS OF SMS THAT ACCUMULATE WITH AGE IN HUMAN NEURONS AND OLIGODENDROCYTES AND TO TRACE THE LINEAGE OF BRAIN CELLS TO THEIR PRECURSORS. THE GOAL OF THIS K99/R00 APPLICATION IS TO STUDY THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF AGING THROUGH SINGLE-CELL AND SINGLE-MOLECULE TECHNOLOGIES. IN AIM 1, I PROPOSE TO BUILD A UNIVERSAL (I.E., DESIGNED FOR SCWGS AND DUPLEX SEQUENCING) TOOLKIT THAT WILL BRING SINGLE CELL SM DETECTION TO A BROAD AUDIENCE BY REDUCING THE EXPERTISE REQUIRED FOR SUCCESSFUL ANALYSIS OF SINGLE CELL DATA AND PROVIDING ACCESS TO STATE-OF-THE-ART METHODS IN A SINGLE PACKAGE. THE TOOLKIT WILL ALSO PROVIDE NEW CAPABILITIES TO EXPLORE THE FUNCTIONAL EFFECTS OF SMS BY INTEGRATING SINGLE CELL RNA- AND ATAC-SEQ DATA. IN AIM 2, I WILL DEVELOP ALGORITHMS TO DETECT CLONES OF CELLS, EVIDENCED BY SHARED SMS, WHICH HAVE BEEN RECENTLY SHOWN TO COLONIZE ALL TISSUES WITH AGE AND CAN LEAD TO LOSS OF FUNCTION. I WILL THEN MEASURE THE RATES AT WHICH CLONES DEVELOP IN THE HUMAN BRAIN (NEURONS AND OLIGODENDROCYTES) WITH AGE. IN AIM 3, I WILL APPLY THE TOOLKIT TO A MASSIVE DATASET OF DUPLEX AND SINGLE CELL DNA-, RNA- AND ATAC-SEQ FROM >10 TISSUES FROM >100 INDIVIDUALS OF VARIOUS AGES GENERATED BY THE SMAHT NETWORK TO EXPLORE PATTERNS AND EFFECTS OF SMS IN AGING ACROSS TISSUES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MOLECULAR INSIGHTS INTO MEMBRANE PATHWAYS OF ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY  ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS A PROGRESSIVE NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER AND THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEMENTIA; IT AFFECTS MILLIONS GLOBALLY. DESPITE RECENT FDA APPROVALS OF THERAPIES LIKE LECANEMAB AND DONANEMAB INTENDED TO TARGET AMYLOID-Β (AΒ) PEPTIDE AGGREGATES, THEIR RELATIVELY LIMITED EFFICACY HIGHLIGHTS THE NEED FOR MORE EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS. THIS PROJECT FOCUSES ON TWO CRITICAL PROTEASES INVOLVED IN AD PATHOLOGY: Γ-SECRETASE AND SIGNAL PEPTIDE PEPTIDASE–LIKE 2B (SPPL2B). Γ-SECRETASE PLAYS A KEY ROLE IN AD BY CLEAVING AMYLOID PRECURSOR PROTEIN (APP); THIS LEADS TO PRODUCTION OF AΒ PEPTIDE, THE ACCUMULATION AND AGGREGATION OF WHICH ARE HALLMARKS OF THE DISEASE. INTERFERON-INDUCED TRANSMEMBRANE PROTEIN 3 (IFITM3) REGULATES Γ-SECRETASE ACTIVITY, MAKING THE IFITM3-Γ-SECRETASE INTERACTION A PROMISING THERAPEUTIC TARGET. ANOTHER PROTEASE, SPPL2B, WHICH IS RELATED TO THE CATALYTIC SUBUNIT OF Γ-SECRETASE (PRESENILIN), CONTRIBUTES TO AD BY CLEAVING SUBSTRATES THAT LINK AMYLOID METABOLISM (I.E., APP TRAFFICKING AND AΒ GENERATION) AND NEUROINFLAMMATION. MOREOVER, SPPL2B IS UPREGULATED DURING THE EARLY STAGES OF AD. TOGETHER, THESE OBSERVATIONS SUGGEST THAT INHIBITING SPPL2B CLEAVAGE MIGHT REPRESENT A STRATEGY TO REDUCE AΒ PATHOLOGY IN AD. TO EXPLOIT THESE POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS, HOWEVER, WE NEED A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF THESE CRITICAL PROTEASES.  THIS PROJECT AIMS TO INVESTIGATE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF Γ-SECRETASE REGULATION BY IFITM3 AND SPPL2B SUBSTRATE PROCESSING. IN AIM 1 (K99 PHASE), I AIM TO DETERMINE HOW IFITM3 INTERACTS WITH AND REGULATES Γ- SECRETASE BY USING STRUCTURAL, FUNCTIONAL, AND BIOPHYSICAL APPROACHES; IN AIM 2 (R00 PHASE), I AIM TO DETERMINE HOW SPPL2B ENGAGES AND PROCESSES ITS SUBSTRATES USING INTEGRATED STRUCTURAL, BIOPHYSICAL, AND FUNCTIONAL METHODS. THE PROPOSED STUDIES INTEGRATE PROTEIN STRUCTURE, FUNCTION, AND DYNAMICS TO DELIVER INSIGHTS INTO AMYLOID METABOLISM AND NEUROINFLAMMATION, WHICH MAY FACILITATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR AD. BUILDING UPON MY EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY AND BIOCHEMISTRY––EVIDENCED BY A STRONG PUBLICATION RECORD––I HAVE DESIGNED A COMPREHENSIVE CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN THAT WILL DEEPEN MY EXPERTISE IN AD RESEARCH AND BIOPHYSICAL TECHNOLOGIES. WITH THE GUIDANCE OF A HIGHLY EXPERIENCED TEAM OF MENTORS WHO ARE EXPERTS IN AD RESEARCH, STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY, AND BIOPHYSICS, THESE STUDIES WILL POSITION ME FOR A SUCCESSFUL TRANSITION TO INDEPENDENT RESEARCH. THIS PROPOSAL WILL PROVIDE A STRONG FOUNDATION TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR. COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO THE REGULATION OF INTRAMEMBRANE PROTEASES IN AD, WITH THE POTENTIAL TO LEAD TO NEW THERAPIES AIMED AT MITIGATING AΒ PATHOLOGY. THIS RESEARCH WILL MAKE A SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTION TO THE UNDERSTANDING AND FUTURE TREATMENT OF AD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: COMPUTATIONAL METHOD DEVELOPMENT FOR 3D SPATIAL-OMICS TO UNCOVER CELLULAR DYNAMICS IN HUMAN INTESTINAL AGING - PROJECT SUMMARY BY 2030, ONE IN SIX INDIVIDUALS WORLDWIDE WILL BE OVER THE AGE OF 60, PLACING A GROWING BURDEN ON HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS. GASTROINTESTINAL (GI) DISORDERS ARE AMONG THE MOST COMMON AGE-ASSOCIATED CONDITIONS, WITH OVER 50% OF OLDER ADULTS EXPERIENCING SYMPTOMS LINKED TO IMMUNE DYSREGULATION, SUCH AS DIVERTICULITIS AND IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME. THESE DISORDERS VARY BY ANATOMICAL LOCATION AND AGE, SUGGESTING SPATIALLY LOCALIZED IMMUNE DYSFUNCTION ACROSS THE INTESTINAL TRACT. AGING IS ASSOCIATED WITH WELL-DOCUMENTED CHANGES IN SYSTEMIC AND MUCOSAL IMMUNITY; HOWEVER, HOW THESE IMMUNE ALTERATIONS MANIFEST SPATIALLY ALONG THE GUT REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD. GUT-ASSOCIATED LYMPHOID TISSUES (GALTS), WHICH ARE ESSENTIAL FOR INITIATING ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES, UNDERGO STRUCTURAL REMODELING WITH AGE, YET THE COMPARTMENT-SPECIFIC IMPACT OF AGING ON GALTS IS UNKNOWN. UNDERSTANDING HOW AGING RESHAPES IMMUNE ARCHITECTURE ACROSS INTESTINAL REGIONS IS CRITICAL FOR IDENTIFYING THE SPATIAL ORIGINS OF DYSFUNCTION AND DEVELOPING TARGETED INTERVENTIONS FOR AGE-ASSOCIATED GI DISEASE. CAPTURING THE COMPLEX CHANGES IN GALT STRUCTURES DURING AGING REQUIRES A 3D, MULTIPLEXED APPROACH—3D TO DETECT SPARSE STRUCTURES, AND MULTIPLEXING TO REVEAL CELLULAR INTERACTIONS. HOWEVER, THE LACK OF COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS AND MACHINE LEARNING MODELS TO ANALYZE SUCH DATA HINDERS MEANINGFUL DISCOVERY. THEREFORE, I PROPOSE TO ADDRESS THIS GAP BY 1) DEVELOPING 3D COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS LEVERAGING MY EXPERTISE IN MACHINE LEARNING, AND 2) APPLYING THEM TO STUDY SPATIAL EPIGENETIC, TRANSCRIPTOMIC, PROTEOMIC, AND STRUCTURAL CHANGES IN GALTS ACROSS THE DUODENUM AND ILEUM DURING AGING. TO THIS END, I HAVE PILOTED THE FIRST HUMAN 3D MULTIPLEXED IMAGING ATLAS OF THE INTESTINE FROM EIGHT DONORS (AGES 23-62), COVERING THE DUODENUM TO THE ILEUM. USING THIS PILOT DATA, I WILL DEVELOP COMPUTATIONAL METHODS FOR ANALYZING 3D MULTIPLEXED IMAGING (AIM 1: K99), INTEGRATE MULTIPLE SPATIAL- OMICS (AIM 2: K99), AND INVESTIGATE IMMUNE STRUCTURE REMODELING THROUGH VIRTUAL STAINING (AIM 3: R00). THIS WORK WILL REVEAL THE PROTEOMIC, TRANSCRIPTOMIC, EPIGENETIC, AND STRUCTURAL MECHANISMS OF INTESTINAL AGING WHILE PROVIDING COMPUTATIONAL MODELS AND EXPERIMENTAL RESOURCES TO THE BROADER RESEARCH COMMUNITY. MY EXPERTISE IN MACHINE LEARNING AND SPATIAL BIOLOGY UNIQUELY POSITIONS ME TO LEAD THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH. I WILL COMPLETE AIM 1 IN MY CURRENT POSTDOCTORAL LAB; AIM 2 WILL INCORPORATE NEW TRAINING IN DEEP LEARNING AND EPIGENETIC DATA ANALYSIS, PREPARING ME FOR AIM 3 IN MY INDEPENDENT LAB, WHICH FOCUSES ON VOLUMETRIC IMAGING DATA. THE METHODOLOGIES DEVELOPED THROUGH THIS WORK WILL BE BROADLY APPLICABLE TO STUDYING OTHER TISSUES AND DISEASE CONTEXTS. SUPPORTED BY OUTSTANDING MENTORS AND STANFORD’S TRAINING ENVIRONMENT, I AM WELL-PREPARED FOR ACCOMPLISHING MY GOALS. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES A CRITICAL PUBLIC HEALTH NEED BY UNCOVERING IMMUNE DYSREGULATION IN AGING AND CREATING INNOVATIVE TOOLS FOR HIGH-RESOLUTION SPATIAL ANALYSIS, LAUNCHING A NEW RESEARCH DIRECTION AND SUPPORTING MY TRANSITION TO INDEPENDENCE.

description: LIFESPAN CELLULAR AND SPATIAL MECHANISMS LINKING BRAIN AGING AND ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE IN THE HUMAN PREFRONTAL CORTEX - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT THE PREFRONTAL CORTEX (PFC) SUPPORTS EXECUTIVE FUNCTION AND COGNITION BUT UNDERGOES PROFOUND CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR REMODELING FROM PRENATAL DEVELOPMENT THROUGH AGING, CHANGES THAT MAY INFLUENCE VULNERABILITY TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD). HOW AGE-ALIGNED CELLULAR TRANSITIONS, INTERCELLULAR COMMUNICATION, AND SPATIAL ORGANIZATION COLLECTIVELY SHAPE COGNITIVE RESILIENCE OR DISEASE SUSCEPTIBILITY REMAINS UNKNOWN. THIS PROPOSAL WILL INTEGRATE SINGLE-NUCLEUS AND SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS WITH MACHINE-LEARNING MODELS FOR SPATIOTEMPORAL INFERENCE TO ESTABLISH A COMPREHENSIVE LIFESPAN REFERENCE OF THE HEALTHY HUMAN PFC AND IDENTIFY AD-SPECIFIC DEVIATIONS. THIS INTEGRATIVE FRAMEWORK WILL UNCOVER CELLULAR AND SPATIAL MECHANISMS LINKING NORMAL AGING TO AD PATHOLOGY, ADVANCING MOLECULAR UNDERSTANDING OF COGNITIVE RESILIENCE AND NEURODEGENERATION. UNDER THE MENTORSHIP OF DRS. PANOS ROUSSOS, GUO-CHENG YUAN AND ALISON GOATE, I WILL RECEIVE INTERDISCIPLINARY TRAINING IN AGING NEUROSCIENCE, ADVANCED COMPUTATIONAL APPROACHES AND NEURODEGENERATION. MY INDEPENDENT LABORATORY WILL INTEGRATE MULTI-MODAL TRANSCRIPTOMIC APPROACHES TO UNCOVER THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING COGNITIVE DECLINE AND AD VULNERABILITY, IDENTIFYING POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS. IN SUM, THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR UNDERSTANDING THE MOLECULAR AND CELLULAR BASIS OF COGNITIVE AGING AND NEURODEGENERATION. MORE BROADLY, THE ADDITIONAL TRAINING AFFORDED BY THIS AWARD WILL IDEALLY PREPARE ME TO LAUNCH AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM DEDICATED TO UNCOVERING STAGE- SPECIFIC MECHANISMS OF BRAIN AGING AND DEVELOPING TARGETED STRATEGIES TO PRESERVE COGNITIVE FUNCTION AND PREVENT NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES.

description: INVESTIGATING THE EPIGENETIC REGULATION OF AGE-RELATED MEMORY DECLINE - PROJECT SUMMARY. UNDERSTANDING THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF COGNITIVE DECLINE IS CRITICALLY IMPORTANT GIVEN THE INCREASING INCIDENCE OF DEMENTIA AND MEMORY DECLINE IN ELDERLY POPULATIONS. EPIGENETIC ALTERATIONS ARE A SIGNATURE OF AGING IN DIVERSE TISSUES, INCLUDING THE NERVOUS SYSTEM. HOW THE AGING NEURONAL EPIGENOME IMPACTS NEURONAL FUNCTIONS, SPECIFICALLY, AGE-RELATED DEFICITS IN LEARNING AND MEMORY, IS LARGELY NOT UNDERSTOOD. THE PRELIMINARY WORK IN THIS PROPOSAL DISCOVERED AN EXCITING ROLE FOR AN EPIGENETIC REGULATOR, THE CONSERVED COMPASS HISTONE METHYLTRANSFERASE COMPLEX, IN THE MAINTENANCE OF AN APPETITIVE ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY IN ADULT AND AGED C. ELEGANS. USING NEURON-SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTOMICS AND CHROMATIN PROFILING, IMAGING, AND BEHAVIOR ASSAYS IN C. ELEGANS, AND CROSS-SPECIES COMPARISONS WITH VERTEBRATE AGING DATASETS, THIS PROPOSAL WILL UNCOVER THE MECHANISMS OF REGULATION OF AGE-RELATED ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY DECLINE BY THE COMPASS COMPLEX. THE PROPOSED WORK WILL EXAMINE THE TEMPORAL DYNAMICS OF COMPASS COMPLEX FUNCTION IN THE REGULATION OF MEMORY (AIM 1), IDENTIFY CONSERVED DOWNSTREAM TARGETS OF THE COMPASS COMPLEX (AIM 2), AND DETERMINE THE AGE-ASSOCIATED UPSTREAM REGULATORS (AIM 3) OF THIS COMPLEX IN THE REGULATION OF MEMORY. OVERALL, THIS PROPOSAL WILL ESTABLISH THE MECHANISMS OF REGULATION OF AN ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY BY A CONSERVED EPIGENETIC MODIFIER AND PROVIDE POTENTIAL TARGETS WITH CONSERVED ROLES IN AGE-RELATED MEMORY DECLINE. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROPOSED WORK WILL PROVIDE VALUABLE RESEARCH AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT TRAINING FOR THE SUBMITTING CANDIDATE, WHO WILL RECEIVE THE REQUIRED TRAINING FROM THE PRIMARY MENTOR, DR. COLEEN MURPHY, CO- MENTORS DR. ANNE BRUNET AND DR. MARCELO WOOD, AND COLLABORATORS DR. OLGA TROYANSKAYA, DR. ANDREW LEIFER, DR. RACHEL KALETSKY, AND DR. WEI WANG. THE MURPHY LAB AND THE CANDIDATE’S ADVISORY COMMITTEE HAVE SIGNIFICANT EXPERTISE IN NEURON-SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTOMICS, CHROMATIN PROFILING, CROSS-SPECIES MULTI-OMIC ANALYSIS, AUTOMATED NEURON IDENTIFICATION METHODS, AND VERTEBRATE NEUROSCIENCE, WHICH WILL BENEFIT THE CANDIDATE’S LONG-TERM GOAL OF ESTABLISHING A RESEARCH PROGRAM EXAMINING THE EPIGENETIC REGULATION OF AGE-RELATED BEHAVIORAL DECLINE. THIS AWARD WILL ALSO SUPPORT THE CANDIDATE’S CAREER GOALS BY PROVIDING TRAINING IN TEACHING AND MENTORING, AND ACCESS TO GUIDANCE AND ADVICE IN NAVIGATING THE FACULTY JOB MARKET. WITH THE PROPOSED TRAINING PLAN, THE CANDIDATE WILL BE ABLE TO SUCCESSFULLY ACCOMPLISH THE PROPOSED RESEARCH AND CAREER GOALS, AND TRANSITION TO AN INDEPENDENT FACULTY POSITION.

description: DEFINING CD4+ T CELLS DRIVING PROTECTION AND SUSCEPTIBILITY IN HELMINTH REINFECTION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ ABSTRACT PARASITIC HELMINTHS CAUSE LONG-LASTING INFECTIONS BY ALTERING IMMUNE RESPONSES THAT WOULD OTHERWISE PROMOTE PARASITE CLEARANCE. HOOKWORM AND RELATED SOIL-TRANSMITTED HELMINTHS HAVE A WELL-DOCUMENTED HISTORY IN THE UNITED STATES, MAY PERSIST IN FOCAL AREAS OF THE AMERICAN SOUTH AND APPALACHIA, AND CONTINUE TO BE DIAGNOSED IN U.S. PATIENTS FOLLOWING DOMESTIC OR INTERNATIONAL EXPOSURE. THESE INFECTIONS CAN CAUSE ANEMIA, NUTRITIONAL IMPAIRMENT, GASTROINTESTINAL DISEASE, AND SEVERE COMPLICATIONS IN PATIENTS RECEIVING IMMUNE-SUPPRESSING TREATMENT. DEFINING THE IMMUNE MECHANISMS THAT PREVENT PARASITE CLEARANCE WILL BENEFIT U.S. HEALTH BY IMPROVING THE SCIENTIFIC BASIS FOR PREVENTION, DIAGNOSIS, AND TREATMENT OF CHRONIC PARASITIC INFECTIONS. THIS K99/R00 PROJECT WILL DEFINE THE CD4+ T-CELL POPULATIONS THAT PROMOTE PROTECTION AGAINST HOOKWORM AND DETERMINE HOW CHRONIC INFECTION ALTERS THEIR COMPOSITION AND FUNCTION. MECHANISTIC STUDIES IN A RODENT HOOKWORM MODEL WILL USE IMMUNE-CELL DEPLETION, ADOPTIVE TRANSFER, VACCINATION, AND TISSUE ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY CELLULAR PATHWAYS NECESSARY FOR ACQUIRED PROTECTION. COMPLEMENTARY STUDIES WILL EXAMINE DEIDENTIFIED, CRYOPRESERVED BLOOD CELLS COLLECTED FROM ADULTS WITH HOOKWORM INFECTION BEFORE AND AFTER TREATMENT. SPECTRAL FLOW CYTOMETRY, ACTIVATION-INDUCED MARKER ASSAYS, PAIRED SINGLE-CELL RNA AND T-CELL RECEPTOR SEQUENCING, AND FUNCTIONAL STUDIES WILL DETERMINE WHETHER INFECTION-ASSOCIATED IMMUNE CHANGES REVERSE AFTER PARASITE CLEARANCE. HELMINTHS REGULATE MANY OF THE SAME IMMUNE PATHWAYS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO ASTHMA, ALLERGY, AND OTHER INFLAMMATORY DISEASES THAT AFFECT PATIENTS THROUGHOUT THE UNITED STATES. DEFINING HOW THESE PARASITES SUPPRESS, REDIRECT, OR RESTORE CD4+ T-CELL ACTIVITY MAY REVEAL NEW MOLECULAR AND CELLULAR TARGETS FOR REDUCING HARMFUL INFLAMMATION, WHILE ALSO ADVANCING TREATMENTS FOR PARASITIC DISEASE. THE PROJECT THEREFORE HAS DUAL RELEVANCE TO U.S. HEALTH: IT ADDRESSES PARASITIC INFECTIONS ENCOUNTERED IN U.S. CLINICAL PRACTICE AND MAY IDENTIFY IMMUNE-REGULATORY PATHWAYS APPLICABLE TO COMMON INFLAMMATORY DISORDERS. THE CANDIDATE WILL RECEIVE ADVANCED TRAINING IN SINGLE-CELL ANALYSIS, COMPUTATIONAL IMMUNOLOGY, SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP, AND LABORATORY MANAGEMENT AT UT SOUTHWESTERN, WITH CONTINUED MENTORSHIP AND SCIENTIFIC COLLABORATION FROM YALE UNIVERSITY AND OTHER PARTNER INSTITUTIONS. THIS TRAINING WILL ESTABLISH AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM FOCUSED ON TRANSLATING HOST-PARASITE BIOLOGY INTO NEW APPROACHES FOR INFECTIOUS AND INFLAMMATORY DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENGINEERED B CELLS TO PREVENT AND CONTROL VIRAL INFECTIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY B CELLS SECRETE ANTIBODIES THAT NEUTRALIZE VIRUSES AND HELP CLEAR INFECTED CELLS. EACH B CELL EXPRESSES A UNIQUE B-CELL RECEPTOR (BCR), A MEMBRANE-ASSOCIATED FORM OF AN ANTIBODY, WHICH IS DIVERSIFIED THROUGH SOMATIC HYPERMUTATION (SHM). HIGHER AFFINITY BCR VARIANTS ARE THEN SELECTED BY COMPETITION FOR ACCESS TO ANTIGENS. THIS PROCESS OF AFFINITY MATURATION IS CENTRAL TO OUR ADAPTIVE HUMORAL RESPONSE TO VACCINES AND PATHOGENS. B CELLS AND ANTIBODIES WORK CLOSELY WITH OTHER IMMUNE SYSTEM CELLS, INCLUDING PHAGOCYTES, T CELLS, AND NATURAL KILLER CELLS TO COORDINATE A RESPONSE TO PATHOGENS. THE IMPORTANCE OF B CELLS TO OUR IMMUNE RESPONSES TO PATHOGENS HAS MOTIVATED EFFORTS TO ENGINEER B CELLS TO EXPRESS NEW BCRS. THESE ENGINEERED B CELLS ALLOW NEW STUDIES OF IMMUNE SYSTEM FUNCTION AND MIGHT BE USED IN CELL-BASED THERAPIES. I HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED A NEW METHOD TO ENGINEER THE BCR OF MOUSE AND MACAQUE B CELLS SO THEY EXPRESS HIV-1 BROADLY NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES (BNABS). UNLIKE EARLIER APPROACHES, OUR METHOD IS SCARLESS AND PRESERVES KEY B-CELL ACTIVITIES IN VIVO, INCLUDING IMPORTANTLY THEIR ABILITY TO AFFINITY MATURE. AFFINITY MATURATION IS CRITICAL BECAUSE IT REFLECTS THE OVERALL VIABILITY AND FUNCTIONALITY OF ENGINEERED B CELLS, AND IT ENABLES SEVERAL IMPORTANT APPLICATIONS. FOR EXAMPLE, IT FACILITATES ADAPTIVE CONTROL OF A MUTATING PATHOGEN AND THE STUDY OF BCR EVOLUTION AS IT RESPONDS TO A DEFINED ANTIGEN EPITOPE. MY GOAL IS TO DEVELOP ENGINEERED B CELLS TO PREVENT AND TREAT INFECTIOUS DISEASES, STARTING WITH HIV-1. THUS, IN AIM 1, I WILL EMPLOY B CELLS THAT EXPRESS HUMAN BNABS TO PROTECT FROM A CHALLENGE WITH AN HIV-LIKE VIRUS. I WILL THEN USE THESE CELLS TO ADAPTIVELY CONTROL AN ESTABLISHED INFECTION. THESE STUDIES WILL ALSO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT ENGINEERED B CELLS CAN ACCELERATE THE DECAY OF THE VIRAL RESERVOIR COMPARED TO STANDARD ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY. IN AIM 2, I WILL FURTHER ENHANCE THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL OF THESE ENGINEERED B CELLS BY APPLYING NEW DEVELOPMENTS IN THE GENOME-EDITING FIELDS TO DIRECTLY EDIT B CELLS IN VIVO. THESE STUDIES WILL ALSO EXPLORE EDITING STRATEGIES THAT CAN LIMIT OFF-TARGET EFFECTS AND THE GENOTOXICITY ASSOCIATED WITH DOUBLE-STRANDED BREAKS IN THE CHROMOSOME. AIM 3 ADDRESSES A MAJOR LIMITATION OF CURRENT HIV-1 VACCINE RESEARCH. SPECIFICALLY, CURRENT ANIMAL MODELS DO NOT EXPRESS KEY VARIABLE (V) AND DIVERSITY (D) SEGMENTS THAT DEFINE PRECURSORS TO BNABS. I WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT MICE EXPRESSING MULTIPLE BNAB PRECURSORS CAN USEFULLY ANTICIPATE HUMAN B CELL RESPONSES. THIS MODEL WILL ALSO BE USED TO ADDRESS KEY OPEN QUESTIONS IN B-CELL BIOLOGY IMPORTANT TO DEVELOPMENT OF MORE EFFECTIVE VACCINES. THESE STUDIES WILL ADVANCE HIV-1 VACCINE RESEARCH, ADDRESS KEY QUESTIONS IN VACCINOLOGY AND B-CELL BIOLOGY, ESTABLISH THE FOUNDATIONS FOR NEW CELL-BASED THERAPIES, AND MAKE THESE THERAPIES SAFER AND MORE ACCESSIBLE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MODELLING IMMUNE AND MICROBIOTA DEVELOPMENT TO PREDICT HEALTH OUTCOMES IN CHILDREN - SUMMARY ABSTRACT IMMUNE HEALTH IS A KEY DETERMINANT OF DISEASE IN MANY PATHOLOGIES IN BOTH ADULTS AND CHILDREN. ENVIRONMENTAL VARIABLES SUCH AS INFECTIONS, DIET, AND MICROBIOTA ALTERATIONS ARE INCREASINGLY UNDERSTOOD AS KEY DETERMINANTS AND TARGETABLE FACTORS. A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW A CHILD'S MICROBIOTA SHAPES HEALTH OUTCOMES VIA THE IMMUNE STATE IS CRITICAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE CHILD HEALTH. WE PROPOSE INTEGRATING LONGITUDINAL IMMUNE AND MICROBIOTA MONITORING TO PREDICT BENEFICIAL IMMUNE STATES, THOSE ASSOCIATED WITH STRONG AND DURABLE RESPONSES TO ROUTINE IMMUNIZATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT EARLY-LIFE EXPOSURES LIKE INFECTION AND ENTERIC DYSFUNCTION CONTRIBUTE TO MALADAPTIVE IMMUNE STATES THAT PREDISPOSE TO POOR HEALTH OUTCOMES AND SEROLOGICAL RESPONSES. WE PROPOSE POTENTIATING THE IMPACT OF TWO INDEPENDENT CLINICAL TRIALS TAKING PLACE IN EAST AFRICA: MICDROP AND PROSYNK. BOTH STUDIES ENROLLED BIRTH COHORTS AND PROVIDED INTERVENTIONS TARGETING MALARIA (MICDROP) OR SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION THROUGH PREVENTION OF ENTERIC DYSFUNCTION (PROSYNK). BOTH STUDIES ACCUMULATED EXTENSIVE CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION THROUGH THOUSANDS OF CLINIC VISITS FOR ROUTINE MEDICAL CARE, IMMUNIZATIONS, AS WELL AS IN- AND OUTPATIENT TREATMENT FOR ACUTE ILLNESSES. IN ADDITION, PLASMA PROTEOMICS AND STOOL METAGENOMICS DATA HAVE ALREADY BEEN GENERATED FROM BOTH COHORTS. WE WILL COMBINE THOSE EXISTING DATASETS ACROSS STUDIES AND GENERATE HIGHLY MULTIPLEXED SEROLOGICAL DATA, MEASURING RESPONSES TO CHILDHOOD VACCINATION. MACHINE LEARNING METHODS WILL INTEGRATE GUT MICROBIOTA AND PLASMA PROTEOMIC DATA TO PREDICT KEY HEALTH OUTCOMES: GROWTH, NEUROCOGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT AND VACCINE RESPONSIVENESS. LEVERAGING PUBLICLY AVAILABLE DATA AND A PARTNERSHIP WITH KAISER PERMANENTE WE WILL TEST OUR PREVIOUSLY DEFINED MOLECULAR SIGNATURES PREDICTIVE OF IMMUNE HEALTH IN INDEPENDENT COHORTS OF U.S. CHILDREN. DR. BACH’S CAREER GOALS ARE TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENTLY FUNDED SYSTEMS IMMUNOLOGIST WITH A RESEARCH PROGRAM FOCUSED ON HOW ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES SHAPE CHILD HEALTH OUTCOMES VIA THE IMMUNE SYSTEM. THE TRAINING PLAN IS FOCUSED ON BUILDING SKILLS IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: (1) ADVANCED INFANT IMMUNOLOGY AND CHILD HEALTH TRAINING, (2) MACHINE LEARNING FOR DATA INTEGRATION, VARIANCE DECOMPOSITION AND PREDICTION (3) ANALYSIS OF MICROBIOME METAGENOMICS. (4) PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. STANFORD UNIVERSITY STRONGLY SUPPORTS COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH EFFORTS AND PROVIDES NUMEROUS VENUES FOR SCIENTIFIC AND SOCIAL INTERACTION INCLUDING SEMINAR SERIES AND RESEARCH SYMPOSIA. OF PARTICULAR RELEVANCE FOR DR. BACH’S WORK ARE THE STANFORD MATERNAL & CHILD HEALTH RESEARCH INSTITUTE, THE STANFORD CENTER FOR HUMAN SYSTEMS IMMUNOLOGY AND THEIR SCIENTIFIC PROGRAMMING. IN ADDITION, THE SCHOOL OF MEDICINE FACILITATES FREQUENT INTERFACING WITH CLINICIANS AND PHYSICIAN SCIENTISTS WHO PROVIDE SIGNIFICANT CLINICAL TRANSLATION OPPORTUNITIES, RELEVANT FOR DR. BACH’S PROPOSAL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MOLECULAR AND PHYSIOLOGICAL REGULATION OF MRNA TRAFFICKING AND TRANSLATION IN OSTEOCYTE DENDRITES - PROJECT SUMMARY OSTEOCYTE DENDRITIC PROJECTIONS EXTEND GREAT DISTANCES THROUGH BONE TO CONNECT OSTEOCYTES TO OTHER CELLS. PROPER FORMATION OF DENDRITES AND THEIR CONNECTIONS ENABLES OSTEOCYTES TO FULFILL CRITICAL FUNCTIONS IN MECHANOSENSATION, BONE REMODELING, AND MAINTENANCE OF SKELETAL AND SYSTEMIC HOMEOSTASIS. HOWEVER, THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT CONTROL OSTEOCYTE MORPHOGENESIS ARE NOT FULLY UNDERSTOOD. PREVIOUS WORK BY DR. MAZUR DEMONSTRATED THAT OCY454 OSTEOCYTE DENDRITES CONTAIN A DISTINCT ENRICHED MRNA TRANSCRIPTOME AND THAT LOCALIZATION OF A SUBSET OF THE TRANSCRIPTS IS REGULATED BY SHORT ‘ZIP CODE’ LOCALIZATION SEQUENCES WITHIN THEIR 3’ UNTRANSLATED REGIONS. LOCAL PROTEIN TRANSLATION OF DENDRITE-ENRICHED MRNAS WAS ALSO DEMONSTRATED WITHIN DENDRITES. FURTHERMORE, DELETION OF CERTAIN ENDOGENOUS MRNA ‘ZIP CODE’ SEQUENCES CAUSES STARK MORPHOLOGIC DEFICITS IN OSTEOCYTES. THESE FINDINGS ILLUMINATE A NOVEL MECHANISM BY WHICH OSTEOCYTES CAN REGULATE THEIR GENE AND PROTEIN EXPRESSION WITH SPATIOTEMPORAL PRECISION, WITH IMPLICATIONS FOR DENDRITE MORPHOLOGY AND OSTEOCYTE FUNCTION. THEREFORE, THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO INVESTIGATE MOLECULAR AND PHYSIOLOGICAL CONTROL OF MRNA TRAFFICKING AND LOCAL TRANSLATION IN OSTEOCYTES AND THE FUNCTIONAL IMPACT OF THESE PROCESSES ON OSTEOCYTES. SPECIFICALLY, THIS PROJECT WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESES THAT (1) TRAFFICKING AND TRANSLATION OF MRNAS IN OSTEOCYTE DENDRITES IS REGULATED AT THE MOLECULAR LEVEL BY THE ACTIVITY OF SPECIFIC ZIP CODE-TARGETING RBPS AND (2) AT THE PHYSIOLOGICAL LEVEL BY MECHANICAL LOADING. HAVING IDENTIFIED ‘ZIP CODE’ SEQUENCES THAT CONTROL MRNA LOCALIZATION, AIM 1 WILL INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF THESE ‘ZIP CODE’ SEQUENCES ON TRANSLATION, PROTEIN LOCALIZATION, AND CHARACTERISTIC OSTEOCYTE GENE EXPRESSION IN STATIC AND MECHANICALLY STIMULATED CONDITIONS. AIM 2 WILL FOCUS ON THE REGULATION OF ONE DENDRITE-ENRICHED MRNA BY IDENTIFYING ITS RNA BINDING PROTEIN (RBP) AND MEASURING THE DIFFERENTIAL EFFECTS OF GENE DELETION OR RBP ABLATION ON THE OSTEOCYTE DENDRITE TRANSCRIPTOME AND MORPHOLOGY. AIM 3 WILL VISUALIZE DENDRITE MRNA AND LOCAL TRANSLATION IN SITU IN MOUSE AND HUMAN BONE, AND MEASURE THE RESPONSE OF MRNA LOCALIZATION AND LOCAL TRANSLATION IN OSTEOCYTE DENDRITES TO MECHANICAL STIMULATION THROUGH IN VITRO AND IN VIVO LOADING PROTOCOLS. TOGETHER, THIS WORK WILL REVEAL MOLECULAR-LEVEL REGULATION OF OSTEOCYTE BIOLOGY THAT COULD BE TARGETED TO TREAT DISEASES OF BONE FRAGILITY. IN THE K99 PHASE OF THIS PROPOSAL, DR. MAZUR WILL BE GUIDED BY A SCIENTIFIC ADVISORY COMMITTEE (DRS. WEIN, BOUXSEIN, TALIAFERRO, AND VAN DER MEULEN) TO DEVELOP CRITICAL SKILLS IN RESEARCH, SCIENTIFIC COMMUNICATION, AND LEADERSHIP. SHE WILL ALSO TAKE ON ADDITIONAL TRAINING FROM COLLABORATORS IN QUANTITATIVE IMAGING & ANALYSIS (DR. BROWN), IN VITRO LOADING MODELS (DR. DIVIETI PAJEVIC), AND ADAPTATION OF CUTTING EDGE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION METHODS FOR MOUSE AND HUMAN BONE (DRS. WANG AND DELGADO-CALLE). TOGETHER THIS TRAINING PERIOD WILL PROVIDE A STRONG STARTING POINT FOR ESTABLISHING AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM FOCUSED ON NOVEL MOLECULAR PATHWAYS THAT CONTROL OSTEOCYTE FUNCTION AND BONE BIOLOGY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DAILY STEP COUNT, PATIENT- REPORTED OUTCOMES, AND RECURRENCE-FREE SURVIVAL IN EARLY BREAST CANCER SURVIVORS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT BREAST CANCER IS THE MOST COMMON NONCUTANEOUS CANCER AND THE SECOND LEADING CAUSE OF CANCER DEATH AMONG US WOMEN, WITH AN ESTIMATED 316,950 NEW CASES AND 42,170 DEATHS IN 2025. OBESITY AND PHYSICAL INACTIVITY ARE POOR PROGNOSTIC FACTORS IN EARLY BREAST CANCER. ADOPTING A PHYSICALLY ACTIVE LIFESTYLE SHOWS PROMISE IN IMPROVING DISEASE AND PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES DUE TO ITS FAVORABLE EFFECTS ON BODY COMPOSITION, AS WELL AS METABOLIC, INFLAMMATORY, AND IMMUNE PATHWAYS. HOWEVER, EVIDENCE LINKING PHYSICAL ACTIVITY WITH HEALTH OUTCOMES IN EARLY BREAST CANCER HAS PRIMARILY BEEN GENERATED FROM STUDIES USING SELF-REPORTED MEASURES OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AT A SINGLE TIME POINT OR FROM SMALL-SCALE CLINICAL TRIALS IN HIGHLY CONTROLLED SETTINGS, WHICH MAY NOT DEMONSTRATE REAL-WORLD EFFECTIVENESS. ADVANCEMENTS IN WEARABLE DEVICES HAVE FACILITATED THE CONTINUOUS MONITORING OF ACTIVITY TRAJECTORIES IN LARGE-SCALE STUDIES TO COLLECT MORE DETAILED AND PRECISE LONGITUDINAL DATA. WEARABLE DEVICES MEASURE MOVEMENTS OR ACCELERATIONS OF THE HUMAN BODY IN REAL TIME, WHICH CAN BE TRANSLATED INTO UNDERSTANDABLE, BEHAVIOR-ORIENTED METRICS. STEP COUNT IS ONE OF THE MOST ACCESSIBLE AND WIDELY USED METRICS FOR MONITORING PHYSICAL ACTIVITY LEVELS, SERVING BOTH AS A TOOL FOR GOAL SETTING FROM THE PATIENT'S PERSPECTIVE AND AS A METHOD OF MONITORING FROM THE CLINICIAN'S PERSPECTIVE. YET, NO STUDY HAS INVESTIGATED THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DAILY STEP COUNT TRAJECTORIES AFTER A CANCER DIAGNOSIS AND PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES OR SURVIVAL AMONG EARLY BREAST CANCER SURVIVORS. THE BREAST CANCER WEIGHT LOSS (BWEL) TRIAL IS AN NCI-FUNDED PHASE III RANDOMIZED TRIAL IN THE US TESTING THE IMPACT OF A SUPERVISED WEIGHT LOSS INTERVENTION (WLI) ON INVASIVE DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL (IDFS) IN 3180 WOMEN WITH STAGE II-III BREAST CANCER AND A BMI ≥27 KG/M2. WRIST-WORN ACTIGRAPH DEVICES WERE USED TO MEASURE OBJECTIVE PHYSICAL ACTIVITY IN A SUBSET OF 540 WLI AND CONTROL PARTICIPANTS AT BASELINE AND AT 6, 24 AND 36 MONTHS. ALL WLI PARTICIPANTS RECEIVED A FITBIT TRACKER AS A MOTIVATIONAL DEVICE. AFTER BEGINNING MY POSTDOC TRAINING, I WAS ABLE TO DERIVE STEP COUNT DATA FROM THE FITBIT AND ACTIGRAPH, ENABLING ME TO TRACK ACTIVITY METRICS OVER TIME IN BWEL PARTICIPANTS. THE GOAL OF THIS K99/R00 PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP, VALIDATE AND APPLY DAILY STEP COUNT METRICS FROM FITBIT AND ACTIGRAPH (AIM 1) AND EVALUATE THE LONGITUDINAL RELATIONSHIP OF DAILY STEP COUNT METRICS WITH PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES (AIM 2) AND RECURRENCE-FREE SURVIVAL IN EARLY BREAST CANCER SURVIVORS (AIM 3). THROUGH COURSEWORK AND MENTORSHIP, I WILL DEVELOP EXPERTISE IN CANCER SURVIVORSHIP, DIGITAL HEALTH, EPIDEMIOLOGIC AND BIOSTATISTICS METHODS, AND PRIMARY DATA COLLECTION IN ONCOLOGY SETTINGS. BUILDING ON MY TRAINING IN ONCOLOGY POPULATION SCIENCES, I AIM TO ESTABLISH AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM IN DIGITAL HEALTHY LIVING FOR CANCER CONTROL, FOCUSING ON REAL-WORLD EVIDENCE AND LEVERAGING WEARABLE DEVICES TO DELIVER TARGETED BEHAVORIAL INTERVENTIONS FOR DIVERSE CANCER SURVIVORS.
