description: MECHANISM AND THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF MACROPHAGE-STEM CELL SYMBIOTIC INTERACTION IN GLIOBLASTOMA - GLIOBLASTOMA (GBM) IS THE MOST COMMON AND LETHAL PRIMARY BRAIN TUMOR, WITH A MEDIAN SURVIVAL OF 15-20 MONTHS AFTER INITIAL DIAGNOSIS. BOTH CONVENTIONAL STANDARD-OF-CARE TREATMENT (SURGERY, RADIOTHERAPY, AND CHEMOTHERAPY) AND NOVEL IMMUNOTHERAPIES HAVE FAILED TO IMPROVE GBM PATIENT SURVIVAL, WHICH IS LARGELY ATTRIBUTED TO THE IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT (TME). AMONG THE TME COMPONENTS, TUMOR-ASSOCIATED MACROPHAGES (TAMS) ARE THE LARGEST POPULATION OF IMMUNE CELL POPULATIONS REPRESENTING UP TO 50% OF TOTAL CELLS IN THE WHOLE GBM TUMOR MASS. MOREOVER, GBM STEM CELLS (GSCS) ARE A SUBPOPULATION OF TUMOR CELLS THAT ARE CHARACTERIZED BY STEM CELL-LIKE CAPABILITIES, AND THEIR INTERACTIONS WITH TAMS WITHIN GBM TME CONTRIBUTES TO THE TUMORIGENICITY, THERAPEUTIC RESISTANCE, AND RECURRENCE OF THIS DEADLY DISEASE. EMERGING EVIDENCE DEMONSTRATES THAT THE CROSSTALK BETWEEN GSCS AND TAMS IS IMPORTANT FOR PROMOTING IMMUNE ESCAPE OF GBM TUMORS. MY RECENT STUDY (LIU ET AL., JCI INSIGHT, 2025) IDENTIFIED GLYCOPROTEIN-NMB (GPNMB) AS A KEY FACTOR MEDIATING THE BI-DIRECTIONAL INTERACTION BETWEEN GSCS AND TAMS IN GBM. SPECIFICALLY, GSCS CAN EDUCATE MACROPHAGES TO PREFERENTIALLY EXPRESS GPNMB IN THE GBM TME AND THIS TAM-DERIVED GPNMB RECIPROCALLY PROMOTES GSC SELFRENEWAL VIA ACTIVATING CD44-PYK2-RSK1/2 SIGNALING AXIS. HOWEVER, THE ROLE AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF GPNMB IN SHAPING THE IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE TME REMAIN POORLY DEFINED. ADDRESSING THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP IS VITAL FOR DESIGNING THERAPEUTICS THAT TARGET GPNMB-MEDIATED TAM-GSC INTERPLAY. MY PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATED THAT GPNMB WAS POSITIVELY RELATED TO IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE TAMS AND NEGATIVELY ASSOCIATED WITH IMMUNE RESPONSE IN GBM PATIENT TUMORS. TARGETING TAM-DERIVED GPNMB PROVIDED SURVIVAL BENEFIT IN IMMUNOCOMPETENT GBM MICE MODELS. BASED ON THESE OBSERVATIONS, I HYPOTHESIZE THAT GPNMB SERVES AS A KEY MEDIATOR IN GBM IMMUNOSUPPRESSION VIA AN AUTOCRINE MECHANISM, AND THAT TARGETING TAM-GSC INTERACTION CAN IMPROVE THE ANTI-TUMOR EFFICACY OF IMMUNE CHECKPOINT INHIBITORS (E.G., ANTI-PD1). SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT TAM-DERIVED GPNMB CAN DRIVE MACROPHAGE IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE POLARIZATION IN AN AUTOCRINE MANNER AND REVEAL THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE WHETHER GPNMB ORCHESTRATES A MACROPHAGE-DEPENDENT PROGRAM TO REGULATE T CELL ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNE RESPONSES. SPECIFIC AIM 3 WILL DEVELOP COMBINATION THERAPIES DUAL TARGETING TAMS AND GSCS AND INVESTIGATE WHETHER THESE INHIBITIONS OF GPNMBMEDIATED TAM-GSC INTERPLAY CAN ENHANCE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF IMMUNE CHECKPOINT INHIBITORS (E.G., ANTI-PD1) IN GBM. TOGETHER, THIS PROJECT WILL UNCOVER NOVEL MECHANISMS OF GBM PROGRESSION AND OFFER NEW THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR GBM BY UNDERSTANDING IMMUNE CELL-TUMOR CELL INTERACTIONS, ADDRESSING VARIATIONS IN ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNITY, AND DEFINING TARGETABLE PATHWAYS. ANIMAL MODELS ARE ESSENTIAL FOR EVALUATING GBM PROGRESSION AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSES WITHIN AN INTACT IMMUNE SYSTEM. ORTHOTOPIC MOUSE MODELS ALLOW INVESTIGATION OF TAMS, T-CELL IMMUNITY, AND TUMOR-IMMUNE CELL INTERACTIONS THAT CANNOT BE ADEQUATELY MODELED IN VITRO.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATION INTO THE REGULATION OF MITOCHONDRIAL DYNAMICS, INTRA-ORGANELLE COMMUNICATION, AND METABOLIC REPROGRAMMING BY THE PKA-FUSION ONCOPROTEIN - PROJECT SUMMARY FIBROLAMELLAR CARCINOMA (FLC) IS A RARE AND AGGRESSIVE LIVER CANCER PREDOMINANTLY AFFECTING ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS, WITH LIMITED EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS FOR ADVANCED STAGES. NEARLY ALL FLC TUMORS HARBOR THE UNIQUE DNAJB1-PRKACA FUSION GENE (PKAFUS) AND SHOW ABNORMAL MITOCHONDRIAL ACCUMULATION. MAJOR CHALLENGES INCLUDE UNDERSTANDING HOW PKAFUS PROMOTES TUMOR GROWTH AND IDENTIFYING TARGETABLE THERAPEUTIC VULNERABILITIES, COMPLICATED BY A LACK OF RELEVANT MODELS. TO FILL THIS GAP, I HAVE DEVELOPED NOVEL PATIENT-DERIVED FLC MODELS, INCLUDING THE FIRST AND ONLY FLC PERMANENT PATIENT-DERIVED FLC CELL LINE, AND ENGINEERED SYSTEMS EXPRESSING PKAFUS. MY RECENT FINDINGS REVEAL THAT PKAFUS-DRIVEN GROWTH INVOLVES PHOSPHORYLATION AND INACTIVATION OF SALT- INDUCIBLE KINASES (SIKS), TRIGGERING TRANSCRIPTIONAL CHANGES VIA CRTC2 ACTIVATION AND P300-MEDIATED ACETYLATION, THUS FACILITATING MALIGNANT CELL PROLIFERATION. THIS DATA HIGHLIGHTS A CRUCIAL ONCOGENIC MECHANISM OF PKAFUS AND SUGGESTS POTENTIAL TARGETING OF CRTC2/P300 IN TREATING FLC, WHILE PROMPTING FURTHER QUESTIONS FOR UNDERSTANDING FLC BIOLOGY AND ENHANCING THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES. I PLAN TO EXPLORE THE CELLULAR PROCESSES REGULATED BY THE PKAFUS-SIK AXIS. MY PRIMARY SCIENTIFIC GOAL, AS PART OF THIS NIH PATHWAY TO INDEPENDENCE, IS TO EXPLORE HOW THE PKA-SIK-CRTC2 AXIS INFLUENCES MITOCHONDRIAL AND ORGANELLES REMODELING AND METABOLIC REWIRING NEEDED BY CANCER CELLS. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT PKAFUS PROMOTES TUMORIGENESIS BY ALTERING MITOCHONDRIAL AND LYSOSOMAL FUNCTIONS, DISRUPTING CELLULAR BALANCE TO FACILITATE MALIGNANT GROWTH. I PROPOSE AN INTEGRATIVE APPROACH USING ADVANCED METABOLOMICS, SPATIAL IMAGING, AND IN VIVO STUDIES. MY RESEARCH FOCUSES ON THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) UNDERSTANDING HOW PKAFUS DISRUPTS MITOCHONDRIAL DYNAMICS; (2) EXAMINING THE IMPACT OF MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION ON LYSOSOMAL FUNCTION AND STRESS RESPONSES IN FLC; (3) IDENTIFYING METABOLIC VULNERABILITIES FROM THESE DISRUPTIONS AND ASSESSING THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES. THE BARDEESY AND MOSTOSLAVSKY LABORATORIES AT MASSACHUSETTS GENERAL HOSPITAL CANCER CENTER OFFER AN IDEAL SETTING FOR MY RESEARCH, FOCUSING ON CANCER METABOLISM AND SIGNALING PATHWAYS. DURING THE K99 PHASE, I WILL RECEIVE CRUCIAL TRAINING IN ORGANELLE IMAGING, METABOLISM, AND IN VIVO METABOLIC FLUX STUDIES ESSENTIAL FOR MY INDEPENDENT RESEARCH CAREER. THE K99/R00 PATHWAY TO INDEPENDENCE AWARD WILL HELP ME ESTABLISH A MULTIDISCIPLINARY PROGRAM ON ORGANELLE DYSFUNCTION AND METABOLIC REWIRING IN CANCER, ADVANCING TARGETED THERAPIES FOR FLC AND TUMORS LINKED TO MITOCHONDRIAL AND LYSOSOMAL CHANGES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE EPITRANSCRIPTOMIC-MICROTUBULE AXIS AS A NOVEL MECHANISM OF PONATINIB INDUCED CARDIOTOXICITY - PROJECT SUMMARY THIS 5-YEAR CAREER DEVELOPMENT PROJECT OUTLINES THE DETAILED PLAN FOR DR. ZHENBO HAN TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR. THE PLAN AIMS TO ENHANCE DR. HAN'S EXPERTISE IN CARDIO-ONCOLOGY AND EPITRANSCRIPTOMICS THROUGH SPECIALIZED TRAINING IN MICROTUBULE BIOLOGY AND ONCOLOGY. THE K99 PHASE WILL INCLUDE GUIDANCE FROM THE ADVISORY COMMITTEE, RELEVANT COURSEWORK, A CHALLENGING RESEARCH PROJECT, AND A STRUCTURED CAREER TRANSITION PROGRAM. WHILE THE DISCOVERY OF TYROSINE KINASE INHIBITORS (TKIS) HAS REVOLUTIONIZED CANCER TREATMENT, THEIR USE IS FREQUENTLY ACCOMPANIED BY ADVERSE CARDIOVASCULAR EFFECTS. PONATINIB, A TKI, IS THE PREFERRED AND ONE OF ONLY TWO EFFECTIVE TREATMENT OPTIONS FOR CHRONIC MYELOID LEUKEMIA PATIENTS HARBORING THE T315I MUTATION. IT ALSO SERVES AS A LAST-LINE THERAPY FOLLOWING OTHER TKIS FAILURE TO HALT DISEASE PROGRESSION. DESPITE THE SIGNIFICANT CLINICAL VALUE OF PONATINIB, ITS USE IS CONSTRAINED BY SEVERE CARDIOTOXICITY, THE MECHANISMS OF WHICH REMAINS UNCLEAR. N6- METHYLADENOSINE (M6A), THE MOST ABUNDANT POST-TRANSCRIPTIONAL MRNA MODIFICATION, PLAYS REGULATORY ROLES IN TUMORIGENESIS AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES, BUT ITS INVOLVEMENT IN CANCER DRUG-INDUCED CARDIOTOXICITY REMAINS UNCLEAR. DR. HAN EMPLOYS HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELL-DERIVED CARDIOMYOCYTE (HIPSC-CM) AND A NEW MOUSE MODEL OF PONATINIB-INDUCED CARDIOTOXICITY, AND DISCOVERED THAT PONATINIB INHIBITED FTO, AN M6A DEMETHYLASE, THEREBY INDUCE M6A HYPERMETHYLATION. THE DATA FURTHER DEMONSTRATED THAT FTO OVEREXPRESSION ALLEVIATED PONATINIB-INDUCED CARDIOTOXICITY. ALTHOUGH THE TARGETS OF FTO IN PONATINIB-INDUCED CARDIOTOXICITY REMAIN INCOMPLETELY CHARACTERIZED, DR. HAN’S PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGESTS MICROTUBULE-RELATED PROCESSES AS POTENTIAL MEDIATORS. THIS IS EVIDENCED BY M6A MERIP-SEQ OF CARDIOMYOCYTES REVEALED THAT PONATINIB SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED M6A LEVELS ON MICROTUBULE ASSOCIATE GENES, WITH CLIP1 PROTEIN EXPRESSION BEING POSITIVELY REGULATED BY FTO. MOREOVER, THE M⁶A INHIBITOR STM2457 NOT ONLY CONFERS CARDIOPROTECTION AGAINST PONATINIB IN VITRO BUT ALSO EXHIBITS CYTOTOXIC ACTIVITY AGAINST CANCER CELLS. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT FTO REPRESSION LEADS TO HYPERMETHYLATION OF CLIP1, INDUCING CARDIOMYOCYTE MICROTUBULE DYSFUNCTION AND THEREBY PROMOTING PONATINIB- INDUCED CARDIOTOXICITY. DR. HAN WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS WITH THE FOLLOWING AIMS: AIM 1 WILL EMPLOY A KINOME‐ SCREENING APPROACH TO DISSECT THE SPECIFIC MECHANISM AND USE TRANSGENIC MICE TO ASSESS THE ROLE OF M6A IN PONATINIB-INDUCED CARDIOTOXICITY. AIM 2 WILL EMPLOY RNA IMMUNOPRECIPITATION AND M6A MOTIF MUTAGENESIS TO DEFINE THE MECHANISM BY WHICH M6A MODIFICATION REGULATES CLIP1 AND DETERMINE HOW CLIP1 LOSS INDUCE MICROTUBULE DYSFUNCTION AND AUTOPHAGY INHIBITION, LEADING TO CARDIOTOXICITY. FINALLY, AIM 3 WILL USE A XENOGRAFT MOUSE MODEL TO SEPARATELY EVALUATE HOW STM2457 OR AAV9-MEDIATED CARDIAC-SPECIFIC CLIP1 OVEREXPRESSION AFFECT PONATINIB-INDUCED CARDIAC DYSFUNCTION AND ANTITUMOR EFFICACY. COLLECTIVELY, THIS PROJECT MAY ELUCIDATE NOVEL LINKS BETWEEN RNA MODIFICATION, MICROTUBULE DYNAMICS, AND PONATINIB-INDUCED CARDIOTOXICITY. MOREOVER, SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROPOSAL WILL ESTABLISH THE FOUNDATION FOR DR. HAN’S INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: RIBOSOME BIOGENESIS REGULATION OF NEURAL CREST CELL DIFFERENTIATION IN DEVELOPMENT AND DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY ONE THIRD OF ALL CONGENITAL ANOMALIES AFFECT STRUCTURES IN THE HEAD AND FACE, AND TO DATE, MORE THAN 700 DISTINCT CRANIOFACIAL SYNDROMES HAVE BEEN DESCRIBED. THE MAJORITY OF THE CARTILAGE, BONE AND CONNECTIVE TISSUE IN THE HEAD AND FACE, AS WELL AS SENSORY GANGLIA, DENTAL PULP AND PIGMENT CELLS ARE DERIVED FROM NEURAL CREST CELLS (NCC), A STEM AND PROGENITOR CELL POPULATION FORMED DURING EARLY EMBRYOGENESIS. MOST CRANIOFACIAL DISORDERS ARE ATTRIBUTED TO DEFECTS IN NCC DEVELOPMENT, HENCE, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED TO UNDERSTAND THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT DICTATE NCC DEVELOPMENT DURING CRANIOFACIAL MORPHOGENESIS AND IDENTIFY ETIOLOGICAL FACTORS DRIVING PATHOGENICITY. RECENT WORK FROM THE TRAINOR LAB DEMONSTRATED THAT RNA POLYMERASE I (POL I)- MEDIATED RIBOSOMAL RNA (RRNA) TRANSCRIPTION, WHICH IS THE RATE LIMITING STEP IN RIBOSOME BIOGENESIS, IS ELEVATED IN NCCS COMPARED TO OTHER CELL TYPES. IN SUPPORT OF THIS IDEA, NCC-SPECIFIC DISRUPTION OF POL I FUNCTION IN EARLY STAGES OF NCC DEVELOPMENT LEADS TO INCREASED NCC DEATH AND CRANIOFACIAL ANOMALIES CHARACTERISTIC OF CONGENITAL CRANIOFACIAL DISORDERS LIKE TREACHER COLLINS SYNDROME. ADDITIONALLY, EVIDENCE FROM OTHER STUDIES SUPPORTS ELEVATED REQUIREMENTS FOR RIBOSOMES AND TRANSLATIONAL CAPACITY IN ORDER FOR STEM CELLS TO ACQUIRE NEW FATES, SUGGESTING THAT RIBOSOME BIOGENESIS ALSO PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE DURING THE DIFFERENTIATION STAGE OF NCC DEVELOPMENT. FROM THIS COLLECTIVE EVIDENCE, I HYPOTHESIZE THAT INCREASED RRNA TRANSCRIPTION AND RIBOSOME BIOGENESIS ARE ESSENTIAL FOR NCC FATE ACQUISITION AND DIFFERENTIATION DURING CRANIOFACIAL DEVELOPMENT. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, I WILL GLOBALLY DELETE POLR1A, WHICH FORMS THE CATALYTIC CORE OF POL I, IN A TEMPORAL FASHION IN MICE AND EXAMINE EFFECTS ON CARTILAGE, BONE AND SENSORY NEURON PROGENITORS. IN PARALLEL, I WILL INVESTIGATE THE CONSEQUENCES OF POL I LOSS-OF-FUNCTION ON PLURIPOTENT IPSCS AND MULTIPOTENT NCCS DURING THEIR DIFFERENTIATION. THESE IN VIVO AND IN VITRO MODELS WILL BE EXAMINED FURTHER USING MULTIOMIC APPROACHES TO IDENTIFY THE MOLECULAR MECHANISM DRIVING PATHOGENICITY UPON POL I AND RIBOSOME BIOGENESIS DISRUPTION. FOR THE R00 PORTION OF THIS PROJECT, I WILL DEFINE THE REQUIREMENT FOR DISTINCT POL I PROTEINS DURING CRANIOFACIAL DEVELOPMENT BY GENERATING ZEBRAFISH MUTANTS FOR ALL POL I-SPECIFIC SUBUNITS THAT LACK ANIMAL MODELS. THE EXPECTED OVERALL IMPACT OF THIS INNOVATIVE PROPOSAL IS THAT IT WILL ADVANCE OUR MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF HOW DISRUPTIONS IN RIBOSOME BIOGENESIS DURING CRANIOFACIAL DEVELOPMENT CAN AFFECT SPECIFIC CELL TYPES, WHICH HAS BROAD IMPLICATIONS FOR RIBOSOMOPATHIES IN GENERAL, AND HUMAN HEALTH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTERROGATING SELECTION OF AUTOREACTIVE T CELLS USING ISOGENIC HUMAN THYMIC ORGANOIDS - PROJECT SUMMARY TYPE 1 DIABETES (T1D) IS AN AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE THAT RESULTS IN THE DESTRUCTION OF INSULIN-PRODUCING PANCREATIC Β-CELLS, RENDERING THE T1D PATIENT DEPENDENT ON A CONTINUOUS SUPPLY OF EXOGENOUS INSULIN. INSULIN THERAPY IS A COMMON TREATMENT BUT DOES NOT PROVIDE A CURE. INDEED, INSULIN INJECTIONS AND INSULIN PUMPS CAN SUCCESSFULLY EXTEND LIFE EXPECTANCY, BUT PERSISTENT FLUCTUATIONS IN GLUCOSE LEVELS CAN RESULT IN LIFE-THREATENING COMPLICATIONS INCLUDING EPISODES OF HYPOGLYCEMIA, CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, NEUROPATHY, AND RENAL FAILURE. MANY ATTEMPTS TO CIRCUMVENT THE AUTOIMMUNE RESPONSE UNDERLYING T1D HAVE UTILIZED BROAD, NON-SPECIFIC IMMUNE SUPPRESSION, WHICH CAN TEMPORARILY SLOW THE PROGRESSION OF DISEASE IN NEWLY DIAGNOSED INDIVIDUALS, BUT NONE HAVE DEMONSTRATED CLINICAL REMISSION OR EVEN ANY OVERT EFFECT ON DISEASE COURSE LONG TERM. THE ESTABLISHMENT OF IMMUNE SELF-TOLERANCE REQUIRES THE SYNERGY OF TWO DIFFERENT SYSTEMS, CENTRAL TOLERANCE IN THE THYMUS AND PERIPHERAL TOLERANCE IN THE TISSUES, THAT WORK IN CONCERT TO PREVENT AUTOIMMUNITY. DEFICIENCIES IN PERIPHERAL TOLERANCE ARE MORE WIDELY STUDIED AND HAVE BEEN CORRELATED WITH HUMAN AUTOIMMUNE DISORDERS INCLUDING T1D. YET, ATTEMPTS TO RENEW SELF-TOLERANCE MECHANISMS IN THE PERIPHERY HAVE DISPLAYED ONLY MODEST, IF ANY, IMPACT ON DISEASE PROGRESSION. THESE DATA SUGGEST THAT OVERCOMING THE INITIAL BREAKDOWN IN CENTRAL TOLERANCE IS KEY TO PREVENTING AUTOIMMUNITY. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS GOVERNING CENTRAL TOLERANCE THAT CONTRIBUTE TO OR INFLUENCE T1D ONSET ARE STILL LARGELY UNKNOWN, FOREMOST DUE TO THE ABSENCE OF HUMAN SYSTEMS THAT CAN BE USED TO INTERROGATE SELECTION PROCESSES IN A MATCHED MANNER. THE DEVELOPMENT OF PROTOCOLS IN OUR LAB AS WELL AS OTHERS TO INDUCE THE IN VITRO DIFFERENTIATION OF HUMAN PLURIPOTENT STEM CELL (HPSC)-DERIVED THYMIC CELLS (STC) FOLLOWED BY IN VITRO CULTURE OF HUMAN THYMIC ORGANOIDS OR TRANSPLANTATION OF STC INTO THYMUS-DEFICIENT MICE HAVE OPENED THE DOOR FOR INNOVATIVE APPROACHES TO ANSWERING THESE PRESSING QUESTIONS. IN THIS PROPOSAL, I HYPOTHESIZE LOW AFFINITY TCR AUTOREACTIVE T CELLS WILL ESCAPE THE SELECTION PROCESS, ULTIMATELY ALLOWING FOR Β-CELL-REACTIVE T CELLS TO PERSIST, WHILE HIGH AFFINITY TCRS WILL BE REMOVED OR DIVERTED TO THE TREG FATE. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, THE FOLLOWING INDEPENDENT BUT INTERRELATED AIMS USING HUMAN ISOGENIC SYSTEMS WILL BE PERFORMED: (1) DETERMINE HOW AUTOREACTIVE TCR AFFINITY INFLUENCES HUMAN THYMIC T CELL SELECTION, AND (2) EVALUATE THE FUNCTIONAL CONSEQUENCES OF AUTOREACTIVE TCR AFFINITY ON Β-CELL REACTIVITY. COLLECTIVELY, GENETIC ENGINEERING OF STEM CELL-DERIVED THYMIC CELLS AND T CELL PROGENITORS TO DEVELOP ISOGENIC THYMIC ORGANOIDS OR NOVEL IN VIVO HUMANIZED SYSTEMS WILL PROVIDE KEY INSIGHTS INTO CELLULAR TOLERANCE MECHANISMS IN HUMAN T1D, ADDRESSING A CRITICAL NEED IN THE T1D FIELD. COMPLETION OF THESE STUDIES MAY ALSO ILLUMINATE NOVEL TARGETS FOR T1D INTERVENTION OR TREATMENT, ALLOWING US TO UNDERSTAND AND GENERATE PATIENT-DERIVED POLYCLONAL THYMUS EDUCATED REGULATORY T CELL POOLS OR DIVERSE T CELL REPERTOIRES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPRINTED GRB10 IN DOPAMINE NEURONS AND TRANSGENERATIONAL TRANSMISSION OF HEDONIC FEEDING - PROJECT SUMMARY HEDONIC FEEDING IS CHARACTERIZED BY THE EXCESSIVE CONSUMPTION OF PALATABLE OR REWARDING FOODS AND IS CONSIDERED A MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR TO THE RAPIDLY INCREASING RATES OF OBESITY. MATERNAL OVERNUTRITION HAS BEEN SHOWN TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE TRANSGENERATIONAL TRANSMISSION OF HEDONIC FEEDING, OBESITY RISK, AND METABOLIC DISORDERS TO FUTURE GENERATIONS. HOWEVER, THE NEUROBIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. GROWTH FACTOR RECEPTOR-BOUND PROTEIN 10 (GRB10) IS AN IMPRINTED GENE THAT CAN BE REGULATED BY THE MATERNAL ENVIRONMENT, INCLUDING DIET. IN THE BRAIN, PATERNALLY BUT NOT MATERNALLY INHERITED GRB10 IS EXPRESSED IN DOPAMINE (DA) NEURONS. IN MY PILOT STUDIES, I DEMONSTRATED THAT DELETION OF PATERNAL AND MATERNAL GRB10 ALLELES IN DA NEURONS REDUCES HEDONIC FEEDING BUT DOES NOT AFFECT MOOD-LIKE BEHAVIORS IN MICE. I FURTHER SHOWED THAT MATERNAL HIGH-FAT DIET (HFD) INTAKE REACTIVATES THE MATERNAL GRB10 ALLELE EXPRESSION AFTER DELETING THE PATERNAL ALLELE IN VENTRAL TEGMENTAL AREA (VTA) DA NEURONS. TOGETHER, I DEVELOPED A HYPOTHESIS THAT MATERNAL OVERNUTRITION ALTERS THE IMPRINTING PATTERN OF GRB10 IN DA NEURONS TO CAUSE TRANSGENERATIONAL TRANSMISSION OF HEDONIC FEEDING. THE AIM 1 WILL FOCUS ON UNRAVELLING THE PHYSIOLOGICAL ROLE OF DIFFERENT GRB10 ALLELES IN DA NEURONS IN HEDONIC FEEDING AND LONG-TERM ENERGY BALANCE. I WILL USE INTERSECTIONAL GENETICS TO GENERATE FOUR MOUSE MODELS: 1) DELETION OF BOTH GRB10 ALLELES IN DA NEURONS, 2) DELETION OF THE PATERNAL GRB10 ALLELE IN DA NEURONS, 3) DELETION OF THE MATERNAL GRB10 ALLELE IN DA NEURONS, AND 4) OVEREXPRESSION OF GRB10 IN DA NEURONS TO DETERMINE THE SPECIFIC ROLE OF GRB10 IN DA NEURONS. IN ADDITION, I WILL EMPLOY FIBER PHOTOMETRY TO MONITOR THE DA NEURON'S RESPONSE DURING THE HEDONIC FEEDING ASSESSMENT IN THESE MODELS. IN AIM 2, I WILL ACQUIRE ESSENTIAL SINGLE- NUCLEUS RNA SEQUENCING (SNRNA-SEQ) SKILLS TO PRECISELY QUANTIFY THE MATERNAL GRB10 ALLELE EXPRESSION IN OFFSPRING’S DA NEURONS AT NORMAL AND MATERNAL OVERNUTRITION CONDITIONS UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF DR. HONGJIE LI. I WILL THEN COMBINE THE CRE-LOXP, TRANSGENERATIONAL TRANSMISSION PARADIGM, AND PROBLEM-SOLVING SKILLS THAT I LEARNED IN THE MENTORED PHASE TO DETERMINE WHETHER MATERNAL OVERNUTRITION INDUCES HEDONIC FEEDING AND LONG- TERM METABOLIC DYSREGULATION IN THE OFFSPRING THROUGH ACTIVATION OF THE MATERNAL GRB10 ALLELE EXPRESSION IN DA NEURONS. I WILL ALSO PERFORM THE FIBER PHOTOMETRY TO MONITOR THE OFFSPRING’S DA NEURON ACTIVITY DURING THE HEDONIC FEEDING TO DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF MATERNAL OVERNUTRITION. THE COMPLETION OF THIS EXCITING PROPOSAL WILL UNCOVER A NOVEL NEUROBIOLOGICAL MECHANISM INVOLVING THE REGULATION OF IMPRINTED GRB10 IN THE BRAIN THAT UNDERLIES THE TRANSGENERATIONAL TRANSMISSION OF HEDONIC FEEDING AND OBESITY. DURING THE MENTORED PHASE, I WILL ACQUIRE ESSENTIAL TECHNICAL, KNOWLEDGE, AND PROBLEM-SOLVING SKILLS THAT WILL STRENGTHEN MY TRAINING AND FACILITATE MY TRANSITION INTO AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH CAREER FOCUSED ON THE NEURAL MECHANISMS DRIVING THE TRANSGENERATIONAL TRANSMISSION OF HEDONIC FEEDING AND OBESITY.

description: ENHANCING DIABETES EDUCATION THROUGH TAILORED INTERVENTION FOR BLACK AFRICANS - MODIFIED PROJECT ABSTRACT: DIABETES IS A LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH AND DISABILITY, CONTRIBUTING SIGNIFICANTLY TO BOTH ECONOMIC AND HEALTH BURDENS. WHILE DIABETES EDUCATION IS THE CORNERSTONE OF EFFECTIVE MANAGEMENT, TAILORED PROGRAMS FOR AFRICAN IMMIGRANTS ARE SCARCE. HOWEVER, ACCESS TO AND UTILIZATION OF DIABETES EDUCATION REMAIN LOW, PARTICULARLY AMONG INCREASING POPULATION OF AFRICAN IMMIGRANTS WHO FACE UNIQUE BARRIERS SUCH AS CULTURAL, LINGUISTIC, AND SOCIAL CHALLENGES. EVIDENCE SHOWS HIGHER DIABETES PREVALENCE, RISK FACTORS, AND OUTCOMES AMONG AFRICAN IMMIGRANTS COMPARED TO OTHER POPULATIONS. ADDITIONALLY, THEIR HEALTHCARE NEEDS ARE OFTEN GROUPED WITH OTHER POPULATIONS, LIMITING CULTURALLY TAILORED CARE. ADDRESSING THESE DISPARITIES REQUIRES DIABETES EDUCATION TAILORED TO AFRICAN IMMIGRANTS TO IMPROVE ACCESS, ENGAGEMENT, AND HEALTH OUTCOMES. THIS APPLICATION HAS THE FOLLOWING RESEARCH AIMS: AIM 1 WILL ADAPT AN EVIDENCE-BASED DIABETES EDUCATION TO MEET THE CULTURAL NEEDS OF AFRICAN IMMIGRANTS WITH T2D BY CONDUCTING INTERVIEWS AND ADMINISTERING SURVEYS AS WELL AS ENGAGING IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE FRAMEWORK FOR THE ADAPTATION. AIM 2 WILL EXAMINE THE PRELIMINARY EFFICACY OF THE TAILORED DIABETES EDUCATION ON DIABETES-RELATED OUTCOMES THROUGH A PILOT STUDY AMONG AFRICAN IMMIGRANTS WITH T2D. AIM 3 WILL IDENTIFY THE IMPLEMENTATION DETERMINANTS AND STRATEGIES FOR THE TAILORED DIABETES EDUCATION USING THE ITERATIVE PRACTICAL, ROBUST IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINABILITY MODEL (IPRISM). AIM 4 WILL EVALUATE THE FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND PRAGMATIC IMPLEMENTABILITY OF THE TAILORED DIABETES EDUCATION FOR AFRICAN IMMIGRANTS WITH T2D. THIS RESEARCH WILL LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR A R01 GRANT FOCUSED ON A CULTURALLY TAILORED DIABETES EDUCATION INTERVENTION FOR AFRICAN IMMIGRANTS LIVING WITH T2D. DR. LESHI HAS ASSEMBLED A TRANSDISCIPLINARY MENTORSHIP TEAM OF NIH-FUNDED SCHOLARS IN HEALTH DISPARITIES AND IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE, ALONG WITH A COMPREHENSIVE TRAINING PLAN. THE K99/R00 TRAINING OBJECTIVES WILL ALLOW DR LESHI TO DO THE FOLLOWING: (1) GAIN ADVANCED SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE IN COMMUNITY-ENGAGED RESEARCH, RECRUITING AND RETAINING UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS IN RESEARCH, (2) DEVELOP SKILLS AND EXPERTISE IN IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INTERVENTION STUDIES, AND (3) ENGAGE IN PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES, BUILD PROFESSIONAL NETWORK WITH ACADEMICS WORKING WITH AFRICAN IMMIGRANTS, AND STRENGTHEN GRANTSMANSHIP TO ESTABLISH AN INDEPENDENT LINE OF RESEARCH. DR. LESHI’S LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING COMMUNITY-ENGAGED RESEARCH TO IMPROVE CARDIOMETABOLIC HEALTH OUTCOMES OF UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS AND PROMOTE APPROACHES THAT IMPROVE OVERALL QUALITY OF LIFE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A CORTEX-MIDBRAIN CIRCUIT REGULATES ENERGY BALANCE - PROJECT SUMMARY OBESITY PREVALENCE IS A GROWING PROBLEM AROUND THE WORLD. WHILE TREATMENTS ARE IMPROVING, THEY ARE NOT KEEPING UP WITH THE GROWING RATE OF OBESITY. ONE OF THE REASONS THIS IS THE CASE IS DUE TO THE LACK OF UNDERSTANDING IN HOW APPETITE, FOOD CONSUMPTION, AND ENERGY EXPENDITURE ARE REGULATED BY THE BRAIN. ONE OF THE MAJOR CONTRIBUTORS OF APPETITE REGULATION INCLUDES BRAIN-DERIVED SEROTONIN (5-HT), WHICH IS SYNTHESIZED PRIMARILY IN THE DORSAL RAPHE NUCLEUS (DRN). 5-HTDRN NEURONS HAVE BEEN WELL ESTABLISHED TO REGULATE APPETITE, FOOD CONSUMPTION AND ENERGY EXPENDITURE. HOWEVER, A GAP IN THE RESEARCH WHICH FOCUSES ON UPSTREAM INPUTS TO 5-HTDRN NEURONS REMAINS. ONE UNDERSTUDIED UPSTREAM NUCLEUS WHICH PROJECTS TO 5-HTDRN NEURONS IS THE AGRANULAR INSULAR CORTEX (AIC). THE AIC IS A MAJOR INTEROCEPTIVE HUB OF THE BRAIN THAT PROCESS FOOD CUES AND HAS BEEN IMPLICATED TO RESPOND TO BOTH WEIGHT GAIN AND WEIGHT LOSS IN HUMANS. CONSISTENTLY, EVIDENCE FROM A FEW ANIMAL STUDIES INDICATE THAT THE AIC CONTRIBUTES TO FOOD CUE PROCESSING. NO ANIMAL STUDIES HAVE FOCUSED ON 5-HTDRN-PROJECTING AIC NEURONAL REGULATION OF APPETITE, FOOD CONSUMPTION, ENERGY HOMEOSTASIS, AND BEHAVIOR. TOGETHER, THESE FINDINGS LED TO A CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT AIC PROJECTIONS TO 5-HTDRN NEURONS PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN ENERGY HOMEOSTASIS. THE FOCUS OF THIS PROPOSAL WILL REVEAL THAT ACTIVATION OF AIC→DRN CIRCUIT PROVIDES A “PHYSIOLOGICAL SIGNAL” TO COORDINATE ENERGY BALANCE WITH INTERNAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL CUES AND WILL REVEAL THE IDENTITY OF AIC NEURONS WHICH PROJECT TO THE DRN. FURTHER, I WILL DETERMINE THE ROLE OF 5-HTDRN NEURONS IN MEDIATING THE EFFECTS OF THE AIC ON ENERGY BALANCE. THESE OBJECTIVES WILL BE ACHIEVED BY VIRALLY ACTIVATING OR INHIBITING THE AIC→DRN CIRCUIT TO STUDY THE IMPACT ON BODY WEIGHT, FEEDING, BODY COMPOSITION, METABOLISM, AND BROWN ADIPOSE TISSUE (BAT) THERMOGENESIS, AT VARIED ENVIRONMENTAL TEMPERATURES, IN ANXIOGENIC ENVIRONMENTS, AND IN DIFFERENT HUNGER STATES. FURTHERMORE, I WILL LEARN FIBER PHOTOMETRY TO DETERMINE THE AIC→DRN NEURONAL ACTIVITY AND CORRESPONDING BAT ACTIVITY DURING THE DIFFERENT STAGES OF FEEDING IN DIFFERENT HUNGER STATES, DURING STRESS, AND WITH COLD EXPOSURE. I WILL ALSO CONDUCT SINGLE NUCLEI RNASEQ IN LEFT AND RIGHT AIC→DRN NEURONS TO DETERMINE THEIR IDENTITY. FINALLY, I WILL USE A NOVEL COMBINATION OF VIRAL AND GENETIC TECHNIQUES TO ISOLATE THE ROLE OF AIC→5-HTDRN NEURONS SPECIFICALLY USING ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY AND FIBER PHOTOMETRY. WITH SUPPORT FROM THIS OPPORTUNITY, I WILL UTILIZE THE MENTORED PHASE TO EXPAND MY EXPERTISE SO THAT I CAN ADVANCE AND LEARN MORE NOVEL AND COMPREHENSIVE METHODS TO STUDY THE AIC→5-HTDRN CIRCUIT AND ENERGY HOMEOSTASIS. THIS OPPORTUNITY WILL PROVIDE ME WITH THE NECESSARY TOOLS TO ENHANCE MY TRAINING AND TRANSITION INTO MY CAREER AS AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH SCIENTIST AT AN ACADEMIC INSTITUTION.

description: INVESTIGATING THE IMPLICATIONS OF VASCULAR PATTERNING AND MATURATION FOR KIDNEY INJURY AND REPAIR - PROJECT SUMMARY KIDNEY DISEASE AFFECTS MORE THAN 37 MILLION AMERICANS AND IS A MAJOR CAUSE OF PREMATURE MORTALITY. IT IS THEREFORE CRITICAL TO UNDERSTAND THE INTRICATE MECHANISMS WHICH COORDINATE NORMAL KIDNEY FUNCTION AND HOW DYSREGULATION RESULTS IN PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL CONSEQUENCES TO PROMOTE EARLIER DETECTION AND IMPROVED TREATMENTS. EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT THE KIDNEY VASCULATURE PLAYS AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN BOTH THE DEVELOPMENT AND PROGRESSION OF KIDNEY DISEASES. DESPITE THIS, OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE PROGRAMS WHICH REGULATE BOTH VESSEL MATURATION AND POST-INJURY REPAIR REMAINS INCOMPLETE. THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO INVESTIGATE HOW RENAL VASCULARIZATION AND PATTERNING REGULATE KIDNEY DEVELOPMENT, PHYSIOLOGY AND RESPONSE TO INJURY TO IDENTIFY NOVEL MOLECULAR TARGETS THAT ENHANCE VASCULAR REGENERATION IN THE KIDNEY. THIS PROPOSAL WILL TEST THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT RENAL VASCULARIZATION PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN KIDNEY MATURATION AND THAT MECHANISMS OF VASCULAR INTEGRITY DIRECTLY REGULATE KIDNEY REGENERATION. AS SUCH, AIM 1 (K99) WILL IDENTIFY PROGRAMS MODULATING POST-NATAL KIDNEY MATURATION. WE WILL UTILIZE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS TO IDENTIFY REGIONAL DIFFERENCES IN VESSEL MATURATION AND CROSSTALK. KIDNEY-SPECIFIC KNOCKOUT MICE WILL BE USED TO INTERROGATE THE ROLE OF ARTERIAL PATTERNING AND VASCULAR MURAL CELLS. AIM 2 (K99) WILL DETERMINE THE ROLE OF RENAL VASCULAR PATTERNING ON KIDNEY FUNCTION AND INJURY THROUGH THE ANALYSIS OF BASELINE AND POST-ISCHEMIC MORPHOLOGY AND FUNCTION USING GOLD-STANDARD PHYSIOLOGICAL ASSAYS AND HIGH-RESOLUTION IMAGING IN MICE. THIS AIM WILL IDENTIFY WHETHER CORRECT, GUIDED VASCULAR PATTERNING IS CRUCIAL FOR KIDNEY FUNCTION, INJURY, AND REPAIR. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGESTS THAT VASCULAR MATURATION IS DELAYED, AND PATTERNING OF THE KIDNEY ARTERIAL TREE IS DISRUPTED FOLLOWING THE LOSS OF ANGIOGENIC GUIDANCE CUE, NETRIN-1 (NTN1). DESPITE THESE CHANGES DURING KIDNEY DEVELOPMENT, NTN1 MUTANT MICE HAVE NORMAL BASELINE KIDNEY FUNCTION. FURTHER, FOLLOWING A MODEL OF ISCHEMIC KIDNEY INJURY, NTN1 MUTANT MICE WITH ABNORMAL VASCULAR PATTERNING HAD REDUCED TUBULAR INJURY AND IMPROVED RENAL FUNCTION COMPARED WITH CONTROLS. WHILE SURPRISING, THESE DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT ORGANIZED AND GUIDED VASCULAR PATTERNING MAY NOT BE REQUIRED AND THAT OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE KIDNEY VASCULATURE NEEDS TO BE EXPANDED. THUS, IDENTIFYING THE MOLECULAR MEDIATORS OF THIS RESPONSE HAS IMPORTANT IMPLICATIONS FOR IMPROVING VASCULAR RECOVERY FOLLOWING INJURY AND TO GREATLY ENHANCE KIDNEY TISSUE ENGINEERING STRATEGIES. AS SUCH, AIM 3 (R00 PHASE) WILL ELUCIDATE NOVEL MOLECULAR MEDIATORS OF VASCULAR INTEGRITY WHICH REGULATE KIDNEY FUNCTION. THIS AIM WILL TEST WHETHER ARTERIAL PATTERNING AND/OR MOLECULAR ALTERATIONS TO MURAL CELLS CONTRIBUTE TO FUNCTION AND RESPONSE TO INJURY BY SINGLE CELL RNASEQ. TO FURTHER ASSESS ENHANCED VASCULARIZATION STRATEGIES, IPSC-DERIVED KIDNEY ORGANOIDS WILL BE USED. DATA GENERATED FROM THIS PROPOSAL WILL HAVE BROAD IMPLICATIONS FOR UNDERSTANDING VASCULAR MATURATION, CROSSTALK AND REPAIR IN THE KIDNEY. THE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES IN THIS PROPOSAL HAVE EXPANSIVE TRANSLATIONAL VALUE FOR A WIDE VARIETY OF RESEARCH QUESTIONS AND WILL FACILITATE SUCCESSFUL TRANSITION TO A COMPETITIVE AND INDEPENDENT TENURE-TRACK RESEARCH POSITION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BITE-SIZED BIOMARKERS: PROMOTING HEALTH BEHAVIOR CHANGE THROUGH OBJECTIVE DIETARY MONITORING - PROJECT SUMMARY DIET-RELATED CHRONIC DISEASES, SUCH AS OBESITY, DIABETES, AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, ARE THE LEADING CAUSE OF MORTALITY AND MORBIDITY IN THE UNITED STATES. THE EXPERIENCE OF FOOD INSECURITY MAY EXACERBATE THE SEVERITY OF DIET-RELATED CHRONIC CONDITIONS DUE TO A LACK OF ACCESS TO HEALTH-PROMOTING FOODS, WARRANTING THE NEED FOR EFFECTIVE NUTRITIONAL INTERVENTIONS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT AIMS TO RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE DIETARY CHANGES ASSOCIATED WITH A PRIMARY CARE-BASED FOOD IS MEDICINE (FIM) INTERVENTION AND DETERMINE THE ROLE OF NUTRITIONAL MONITORING ON INITIATING AND SUSTAINING PATIENT HEALTH BEHAVIOR CHANGE (K99), WITH THE GOAL OF IDENTIFYING FACILITATORS AND BARRIERS OF INTEGRATING NON-INVASIVE NUTRITIONAL BIOMARKERS INTO EXISTING HEALTHCARE INFRASTRUCTURE (R00). RECIPE4HEALTH IS AN ON-GOING QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL FIM TRIAL THAT INCLUDES WEEKLY PRODUCE DELIVERIES AND A BEHAVIORAL LIFESTYLE INTERVENTION FOR 12 WEEKS THAT WILL SERVE AS THE PARENT STUDY. THE EXISTING EVALUATION INCLUDES 24-HOUR DIETARY RECALLS, PHYSICAL AND MENTAL HEALTH SURVEYS, CLINICAL LAB VALUES, AND ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR) DATA ON PARTICIPANTS AND PROPENSITY SCORE-MATCHED CONTROLS. AS A CRITICAL EXTENSION OF THIS WORK, WE WILL EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF RECIPE4HEALTH ON CHANGES IN DIETARY INTAKE (N=75 INTERVENTION AND N=75 CONTROLS) USING THE VEGGIE METER®, A NON-INVASIVE AND OBJECTIVE QUANTIFICATION OF CAROTENOIDS IN THE SKIN, AT BASELINE AND 6-MONTH (SA1). INTERVENTION AND CONTROL PARTICIPANTS (N=150) WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO RECEIVE SKIN CAROTENOID SCORES AND CLINICAL LAB VALUES (HBA1C, LIPIDS, BP, ANTHROPOMETRICS) OR TO ONLY RECEIVE CLINICAL LAB VALUES TO DETERMINE WHETHER RECEIVING DIETARY INTAKE INFORMATION AT BASELINE IS EFFECTIVE FOR INCREASING DIET QUALITY AT 6 MONTHS COMPARED TO STANDARD OF CARE (SA2). A CONVERGENT MIXED METHOD APPROACH USING EHR DATA, QUANTITATIVE MEASURES OF CHRONIC DISEASE RISK, AND QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS WITH PATIENTS, PRIMARY CARE PROVIDERS, AND HEALTHCARE LEADERSHIP WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO INCORPORATING NUTRITIONAL BIOMARKERS, SUCH AS THE VEGGIE METER®, IN THE EXISTING PRIMARY CARE INFRASTRUCTURE (SA3). WITH THE SUPPORT OF THE K99/R00 AWARD, I WILL LEVERAGE THE EXPERTISE OF MY INTERDISCIPLINARY MENTORING TEAM TO GAIN ADDITIONAL TRAINING IN 1) DEVELOPING, IMPLEMENTING, AND EVALUATING BEHAVIORAL NUTRITION INTERVENTIONS TO ADDRESS DIET-RELATED CHRONIC DISEASE, 2) CAUSAL INFERENCE METHODS FOR FIM RESEARCH, AND 3) TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH AND IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE IN PRIMARY CARE, TO EMERGE AS A LEADER IN BEHAVIORAL NUTRITION INTERVENTIONS IN PRIMARY CARE. COMPLETION OF MY RESEARCH AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES WILL RESULT IN SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS AND PRESENTATIONS, A FACULTY POSITION AT A RESEARCH-INTENSIVE INSTITUTION, AND THE ACQUISITION OF PRELIMINARY DATA FOR MY FUTURE R01. RESULTS FROM THIS PROPOSAL WILL FILL A CRITICAL RESEARCH GAP BY RIGOROUSLY EVALUATING DIETARY CHANGES RESULTING FROM FIM INTERVENTIONS AND PROVIDE ROBUST EVIDENCE OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF IMPROVING NUTRITIONAL MONITORING IN PRIMARY CARE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PALMITOYLATION-DEPENDENT INTERFERON SIGNALING IN TYPE 1 DIABETES - PROJECT SUMMARY: MOLECULAR INITIATION OF T1D OCCURS YEARS BEFORE CLINICAL SYMPTOMS MANIFEST, WITH PANCREATIC Β CELLS PLAYING A CRUCIAL ROLE IN TRIGGERING AUTOIMMUNITY. PRO-INFLAMMATORY MACROPHAGES ARE THE EARLIEST IMMUNE INFILTRATORS, INITIATING LOCAL INFLAMMATION THAT BRIDGES Β CELL STRESS AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE ACTIVATION. ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSORS, SUCH AS EARLY-LIFE VIRAL INFECTIONS AND CYTOKINE STRESS, ARE BELIEVED TO INDUCE Β CELL DYSFUNCTION THROUGH THE ACTIVATION OF INTERFERON SIGNALING, LEADING TO THE PHOSPHORYLATION OF STAT PROTEINS, SUCH AS STAT1, WHICH ACTIVATE THE INTERFERON-STIMULATED GENE SIGNATURE (ISG). S-PALMITOYLATION, A REVERSIBLE LIPID MODIFICATION REGULATED BY PALMITOYLTRANSFERASES (DHHC ENZYMES) AND DEPALMITOYLASES (APT1/2, PPT1), REGULATE STAT1 MEMBRANE LOCALIZATION AND ITS SUBSEQUENT PHOSPHORYLATION. CONCURRENTLY, THE STRESSORS THAT STIMULATE INTERFERON SIGNALING ALSO ACTIVATE THE INTEGRATED STRESS RESPONSE (ISR), WHICH INHIBITS GLOBAL MRNA TRANSLATION INITIATION BY PHOSPHORYLATING EUKARYOTIC TRANSLATION INITIATION FACTOR 2 ALPHA. ALTHOUGH THE ISR IS A PROTECTIVE MECHANISM, ITS CHRONIC ACTIVATION CAN PUSH CELLS TOWARD APOPTOSIS. MY RECENT FINDINGS INDICATE THAT INHIBITING PERK, AN ISR KINASE, SIGNIFICANTLY DELAYS THE ONSET OF HYPERGLYCEMIA IN NON-OBESE DIABETIC (NOD) MICE AND DOWNREGULATES PALMITOYLATION-RELATED GENES IN BOTH Β AND MYELOID CELLS. DESPITE EMERGING EVIDENCE THAT LINKS INTERFERON SIGNALING TO T1D, ITS REGULATION IN DIABETES REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT STAT1 PALMITOYL CYCLING AUGMENTS IFN SIGNALING IN Β CELLS AND MACROPHAGES VIA DISTINCT BUT COORDINATED MECHANISMS THAT PROMOTE Β-CELL AUTOIMMUNITY, AND THAT THE ISR STRENGTHENS THIS RESPONSE POST-TRANSCRIPTIONALLY IN A CELL-TYPE-SPECIFIC FASHION. IN SPECIFIC AIM 1, I WILL CHARACTERIZE THE EFFECT OF ISR ON INTERFERON SIGNALING AND PALMITOYLATION IN Β CELLS AND MACROPHAGES USING OMICS-BASED APPROACHES SUCH AS RIBO-SEQ TO ASSESS MRNA TRANSLATION DYNAMICS, IMMUNOLOGY, AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY. THE EXPERIMENTS IN AIM 1 (COMPLETED IN THE K99 PHASE) WILL GIVE ME THE BIOINFORMATICS TRAINING ESSENTIAL FOR INDEPENDENCE. IN AIM 2 (K99 AND R00 PHASES), I WILL IDENTIFY THE ROLE OF S-PALMITOYLATION AND SPECIFIC PALMITOYLTRANSFERASES IN REDEFINING THE STAT1 LANDSCAPE IN Β CELLS AND MACROPHAGES. I WILL TRAIN IN PALMITOYL-PROTEOMICS AND DATA ANALYSIS TO TRANSITION TO INDEPENDENCE. IN AIM 3 (K99 AND R00 PHASES), I WILL DETERMINE HOW S-PALMITOYLATION INFLUENCES INTERFERON SIGNALING IN VIVO. I WILL TEST BROAD PALMITOYLTRANSFERASE AND DEPALMITOYLASE INHIBITORS AND THEN VALIDATE THE IN VIVO EFFECTS OF PROMISING CANDIDATES IDENTIFIED IN AIM 2. I WILL LEVERAGE IN VIVO STABILIZED SIRNA AND CRISPR-CAS9 BASED KNOCKDOWN/KNOCKOUT STRATEGIES TO INVESTIGATE THE IN VIVO ROLE OF PALMITOYL CYCLING IN T1D. THESE STUDIES WILL ELUCIDATE THE ROLE OF S-PALMITOYLATION IN T1D, ULTIMATELY FORMING THE BASIS FOR FUTURE R01 SUBMISSIONS AND THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEFINING REGULATORS OF POLYCYSTIN-2 CILIARY TRAFFICKING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT POLYCYSTIN-2 (PC2) IS ONE OF THE KEY PROTEINS, WHOSE MUTATION IS RESPONSIBLE FOR MANY CASES OF AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT POLYCYSTIC KIDNEY DISEASE (ADPKD). ALTHOUGH PC2 HAS LONG BEEN OBSERVED IN PRIMARY CILIA—AND IT IS WIDELY ACCEPTED THAT CILIARY LOCALIZATION IS ESSENTIAL FOR PC2 FUNCTION—THE MOLECULAR MECHANISM THAT GOVERNS PC2 ENTRY INTO, AND RETENTION WITHIN CILIA REMAINS POORLY DEFINED. PROGRESS HAS BEEN GREATLY LIMITED BY THE LACK OF ROBUST TOOLS FOR IN VIVO, LIVE-CELL IMAGING OF ENDOGENOUS PC2 WITHOUT OVEREXPRESSION ARTIFACTS. IN THE FIRST PART OF MY POSTDOCTORAL TRAINING, I DEVELOPED A PKD2-HALOTAG KNOCK-IN MOUSE MODELS, THAT ALLOWED ME TO INVESTIGATE ENDOGENOUS PC2 LOCALIZATION, DYNAMICS, COMPLEX FORMATION, AND TURNOVER DURING HOMEOSTASIS AND DISEASE STATUS IN LIVE AND FIXED MATERIALS. USING THIS MODEL, I GENERATED WIDE-TYPE PKD2-HALOTAG CELL LINE WITH NORMAL CILIARY PC2 LOCALIZATION, AND MULTIPLE MUTANT CELL LINES THAT REPRODUCIBLY LOSE PC2 CILIARY TRAFFICKING VIA CRISPR/CAS9 TECHNIQUES. WITH THESE RESOURCES, THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY NOVEL REGULATOR PROTEINS THAT GOVERN THE TRAFFICKING AND RETENTION OF PC2 IN THE PRIMARY CILIA. AIM 1 WILL DISCOVER NOVEL REGULATORS OF PC2 CILIARY TRAFFICKING BY COMPARING NATIVE PC2 COMPLEXES FROM CELLS LINES THAT ARE EITHER COMPETENT OR DEFECTIVE FOR PC2 CILIARY LOCALIZATION, USING QUANTITATIVE AND SUBTRACTIVE INTERACTOMICS. BONA FIDE REGULATORS WILL BE PRIORITIZED AND VALIDATED USING A STANDARDIZED FRAMEWORK EXEMPLIFIED BY CEP290, WHICH IS TRANSITION-ZONE SCAFFOLD PROTEIN EMERGING FROM PILOT MASS SPECTROMETRY DATASETS AND FROM EVIDENCE GENERATED FROM CEP290 MUTANT PATIENT FIBROBLASTS. AIM 2 WILL EXAMINE THE FUNCTIONAL CONSEQUENCES OF DISRUPTED PC2 TRAFFICKING OR CILIARY RETENTION ON CYSTOGENESIS IN A HUMAN-RELEVANCE 3D KIDNEY ORGANOID MODEL DERIVED FROM IPSC CARRYING THE ENDOGENOUS PKD2-HALOTAG ALLELE. I WILL TEST TWO CAUSAL QUESTIONS: (1) WHETHER DELETION OF A GIVEN REGULATOR IMPAIRS PC2 CILIARY TRAFFICKING IN ORGANOIDS, AND (II) WHETHER SUCH TRAFFICKING FAILURE IS SUFFICIENT TO INITIATE OR ACCELERATE CYST FORMATION. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL DELINEATE THE TRAFFICKING STEPS THAT DELIVER AND ANCHOR PC2 IN CILIA AND DETERMINE HOW THEIR FAILURE INITIATES CYSTOGENESIS. CAREER DEVELOPMENT: THE K99 PHASE, CONDUCTED IN THE LABORATORY OF DR. BRADLEY K. YODER WITH CO-MENTORSHIP FROM DR. CHENG “JACK” SONG AT UAB, WILL PROVIDE RIGOROUS TRAINING IN ADVANCED BIOCHEMISTRY, QUANTITATIVE INTERACTOMICS, HIGH-RESOLUTION IMAGING, AND HUMAN KIDNEY ORGANOID BIOLOGY. THE DETAILED TRAINING PLAN INTEGRATES FORMAL COURSEWORK, MENTORED PRACTICE IN EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN AND DATA ANALYSIS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT IN RESEARCH RIGOR, GRANT WRITING, AND LAB LEADERSHIP, WITH ADDITIONAL SUPPORTS FROM THE ADVISORY COMMITTEE. THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL POSITION ME TO LAUNCH AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM FOCUSED ON THE MECHANISMS OF PC2 CILIARY TRAFFICKING AND ON TARGETING PC2 TRAFFICKING FOR DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPY IN ADPKD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CHARACTERIZING LEARNING-INDUCED REMODELING OF CORTICAL CIRCUITRY AND COMPUTATION DURING THE CRITICAL PERIOD - PROJECT SUMMARY NEURONAL PLASTICITY IS A FUNDAMENTAL ABILITY FOR SURVIVAL, AND IMPAIRED PLASTICITY UNDERLIES NUMEROUS NEURO- DEVELOPMENTAL AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS, INCLUDING AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER AND ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE. WHILE BRAIN PLASTICITY PERSISTS THROUGH LIFE, BRAINS ARE PARTICULARLY MALLEABLE AND SENSITIVE TO EXTERNAL STIMULI DURING DEVELOPMENTAL CRITICAL PERIODS. CRITICAL PERIOD PLASTICITY HAS BEEN EXTENSIVELY STUDIED USING SENSORY DEPRIVATION, WHICH INDUCES DRAMATIC AND PERSISTENT ALTERATIONS IN CIRCUITRY AND FUNCTION, INCLUDING IN HUMANS; HOWEVER, THE IMPACT OF SENSORY ENHANCEMENT, FOR INSTANCE BY LEARNING, REMAINS UNDEREXPLORED. DURING HER POSTDOCTORAL WORK, DR. BISSEN SHOWED THAT PREY CAPTURE LEARNING, A COMPLEX AND ETHOLOGICALLY RELEVANT VISION-DEPENDENT PARADIGM, ENHANCES VISUAL FUNCTION AND PROFOUNDLY REWIRES L5 CIRCUITRY IN THE VISUAL CORTEX OF CRITICAL PERIOD MICE – BUT NOT IN ADULT HUNTERS, SUGGESTING THAT THESE CHANGES ARE MEDIATED BY CRITICAL PERIOD-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL RECONTEXTUALIZE LEARNING-INDUCED REWIRING WITHIN ITS NETWORK DURING THE CRITICAL PERIOD OF THE VISUAL SYSTEM AND INVESTIGATE THE ROLES OF GENETICALLY DEFINED L5 SUBTYPES AND THEIR ASSOCIATED CIRCUITRY DURING LEARNING. DEPENDING ON THEIR AFFERENTS AND PROJECTIONS, SUBTYPES OF L5 PYRAMIDAL NEURONS, A MAIN OUTPUT LAYER OF THE CORTEX, ARE PROPOSED TO MEDIATE DIFFERENT PHASES (I.E. MOVEMENT PREPARATION OR EXECUTION) DURING ADULT BEHAVIOR AND LEARNING. IN AIM 1, DR. BISSEN WILL ASSESS WHETHER THESE SUBTYPES PLAY SIMILARLY DISTINCT ROLES DURING THE CRITICAL PERIOD AND WILL CHARACTERIZE THEIR BEHAVIORAL CONTRIBUTIONS TO VISION-DEPENDENT LEARNING AND THEIR UNDERLYING STRUCTURAL PLASTICITY. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF VISION-DEPENDENT LEARNING ON NEURONAL COMPUTATION IN THESE NEURONS, I.E. HOW THEY PROCESS AND INTEGRATE THEIR MYRIADS OF SENSORY AND NON-SENSORY (E.G. CONTEXTUAL OR MOTIVATIONAL) INPUTS INTO A SINGLE FIRING STREAM. FINALLY, AIM 3 WILL IDENTIFY THE DRIVING FORCES BEHIND LEARNING-INDUCED CHANGES IN L5 NEURONS BY ASSESSING THE BEHAVIORAL AND STRUCTURAL CONTRIBUTIONS OF MAJOR L5 AFFERENTS TO VISION-DEPENDENT LEARNING. TOGETHER, THESE AIMS WILL CHARACTERIZE THE LEARNING-INDUCED, AFFERENT- SPECIFIC REMODELING OF CORTICAL CIRCUITRY AND COMPUTATION DURING THE CRITICAL PERIOD AND LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR A COMPREHENSIVE MODEL OF THE MECHANISMS MEDIATING ENHANCED PLASTICITY DURING THIS WINDOW. TO COMPLETE THESE AIMS, THE SCIENTIFIC TRAINING PLAN WILL CAPITALIZE ON DR. BISSEN’S EXPERTISE IN STRUCTURAL PLASTICITY AND DEVELOP CRUCIAL SKILLS IN NOVEL METHODS FOR FINE BEHAVIORAL ANALYSIS AND CUTTING-EDGE DENDRITIC AND AXONAL CALCIUM IMAGING AND COMPUTATION, THANKS TO TECHNICAL AND CONCEPTUAL ADVICE FROM HER ADVISORY COMMITTEE, DRS. MARK ANDERMANN, CHRISTINE GRIENBERGER AND MARK HARNETT. DR. BISSEN WILL ALSO BENEFIT FROM THE GUIDANCE OF HER MENTOR, DR. GINA TURRIGIANO, AS WELL AS FROM THE HIGHLY INNOVATIVE, COLLABORATIVE, AND SUPPORTIVE NEUROSCIENCE COMMUNITY AT BRANDEIS. FINALLY, AN EXTENSIVE AND PERSONALIZED CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN WILL FOCUS ON HONING HER COMMUNICATION, MENTORING, LEADERSHIP AND LAB MANAGEMENT SKILLS, TO FULLY PREPARE DR. BISSEN TO LEAD AN INDEPENDENT LAB ADDRESSING INNOVATIVE AND IMPACTFUL RESEARCH QUESTIONS IN THE FIELD OF NEURONAL PLASTICITY.

description: SPATIOTEMPORAL NEUROPEPTIDOMICS WITH ISOMER-RESOLVED MASS SPECTROMETRY - PROJECT SUMMARY: NEUROPEPTIDES PLAY CRITICAL ROLES IN MEMORY, BEHAVIOR AND DISEASE, YET THEIR CHEMICAL COMPLEXITY AND LONG-DISTANCE TRANSPORT MAKE THEM ONE OF THE LEAST UNDERSTOOD CLASSES OF MOLECULES IN THE BRAIN. THIS PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL CREATE NEW MASS SPECTROMETRY-BASED INSTRUMENTATION AND COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS TO MAP NEUROPEPTIDE DISTRIBUTION AND RELEASE WITH HIGH- RESOLUTION IN TIME AND SPACE AND WITH INCREASED THROUGHPUT. THE OUTCOMES WILL UNCOVER NEW MOLECULAR SIGNATURES OF NEUROPEPTIDE SIGNALING, AND PROVIDE BROADLY APPLICABLE STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE THEIR DETECTION, MONITORING, AND THERAPEUTIC TARGETING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISMS OF NUCLEASE-BASED BACTERIAL IMMUNITY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT BACTERIA AND BACTERIOPHAGES HAVE BEEN LOCKED IN A MOLECULAR ARMS RACE FOR BILLIONS OF YEARS, DRIVING THE EVOLUTION OF DIVERSE ANTI-PHAGE DEFENSE SYSTEMS. NUCLEASE DOMAINS ARE THE MOST ABUNDANT DOMAIN TYPE IN THESE SYSTEMS, UNDERSCORING THE IMMUNOLOGICAL UTILITY OF NUCLEIC ACID CLEAVAGE. SOME ANTI-PHAGE NUCLEASES CAN DIRECTLY DISTINGUISH PHAGE FROM HOST DNA, SELECTIVELY DEGRADING PHAGE GENOMES WHILE SPARING HOST CHROMOSOMES. OTHERS ARE ACTIVATED DURING PHAGE INFECTION AND INDISCRIMINATELY CLEAVE BOTH VIRAL AND HOST DNA, SACRIFICING THE INFECTED CELL TO PREVENT VIRAL PROPAGATION. RECENT GENETIC AND COMPUTATIONAL SCREENS HAVE DRAMATICALLY EXPANDED THE CATALOG OF KNOWN ANTI-PHAGE NUCLEASES AND UNCOVERED A WIDE RANGE OF UNUSUAL NUCLEASE-ASSOCIATED DOMAINS. THESE FINDINGS SUGGEST THAT ANTI-PHAGE NUCLEASES EMPLOY NOVEL MECHANISMS OF ACTIVATION AND DNA-TARGETING SPECIFICITY, AND THAT DEFINING THESE PRINCIPLES WILL ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF BACTERIAL IMMUNITY WHILE LAYING THE FOUNDATION FOR AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM. THE PROPOSED K99 PHASE WILL COMBINE GENETIC AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY APPROACHES WITH NEW TRAINING IN BIOCHEMISTRY, STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY, AND COMPUTATIONAL METHODS TO DISSECT THE MECHANISMS OF SELECT ANTI-PHAGE NUCLEASES. AIM 1 WILL INVESTIGATE A MEMBRANE-BOUND NUCLEASE THAT CLEAVES PHAGE DNA DURING GENOME INJECTION, INCLUDING CONSTRUCTION OF CHIMERAS BETWEEN HOMOLOGS THAT TARGET DIFFERENT PHAGES. AIM 2 WILL EXAMINE A NOVEL NUCLEASE WITH AN AUXILIARY DOMAIN RESEMBLING A PHAGE VIRION COMPONENT, WITH THE HYPOTHESIS THAT IT BECOMES ACTIVATED THROUGH CO-ASSEMBLY WITH PHAGE PARTICLES INSIDE THE CELL. AIM 3, PURSUED PRIMARILY DURING THE R00 PHASE, WILL CLASSIFY A DIVERSE PANEL OF NUCLEASES BASED ON TIMING OF CLEAVAGE, TARGETING SPECIFICITY, AND DOMAIN ARCHITECTURE, ESTABLISHING GENERAL PRINCIPLES THAT EXTEND BEYOND INDIVIDUAL SYSTEMS. THE K99 PHASE WILL ALSO PROVIDE CAREER DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES BEYOND EXPERIMENTAL TRAINING. THIS PERIOD WILL INCLUDE EXPERIENCE MENTORING STUDENTS, STRENGTHENING SKILLS IN LABORATORY LEADERSHIP, AND DEVELOPING STRATEGIES TO FOSTER A WELCOMING AND COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT. PARTICIPATION IN NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCES, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT WORKSHOPS, AND INTERACTIONS WITH LEADERS IN MICROBIOLOGY, STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY, AND PHAGE BIOLOGY WILL BROADEN PROFESSIONAL NETWORKS. TRAINING IN GRANT WRITING, MANUSCRIPT PREPARATION, AND FACULTY APPLICATION PROCESSES WILL FURTHER FACILITATE A SMOOTH TRANSITION TO INDEPENDENCE. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH PROGRAM IS DISTINCT FROM THAT OF THE SPONSORING LABORATORY AND WILL BE CARRIED FORWARD INTO A FUTURE INDEPENDENT GROUP, WHERE THE LONG-TERM RESEARCH TRAJECTORY WILL FOCUS ON UNCOVERING THE MECHANISTIC LOGIC OF BACTERIAL DEFENSE AND EXPLORING THE UNTAPPED DIVERSITY OF ANTI-PHAGE NUCLEASES.

description: THE IMPACT OF STATE-LEVEL FACTORS ON INFANT HEALTH - ABSTRACT MODIFIED PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SECTION  THE RECENT INCREASING TRENDS IN INFANT MORTALITY, PRETERM BIRTH, AND LOW BIRTHWEIGHT ARE MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH PROBLEMS IN THE US. STATE-LEVEL FACTORS ARE INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED AS IMPORTANT DRIVERS OF THESE OUTCOMES. FOR EXAMPLE, SOME CURRENT APPROACHES TO SUBSTANCE USE DURING PREGNANCY OR REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH CARE HAVE BEEN LINKED TO MATERNAL AND INFANT HEALTH OUTCOMES, SUCH AS DELAYED PRENATAL CARE UTILIZATION AND INFANT MORTALITY. HOWEVER, THERE IS A PAUCITY OF RESEARCH THAT EXAMINES THE CLINICAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH EFFECTS OF STRATEGIES THAT INTEND TO PROMOTE FETAL HEALTH BY REGULATING PREGNANCY, KNOWN AS FETAL PROTECTION LAWS (FPLS). THIS PROJECT WILL LEVERAGE NATIONAL CENTER FOR HEALTH STATISTICS NATALITY DATA AND SYNTHETIC CONTROLLED INTERRUPTED TIME SERIES MODELS TO INVESTIGATE THE OVERALL (AIM 1A) AND HETEROGENOUS (AIM 1B) EFFECTS OF FPLS ON PRENATAL CARE, LOW BIRTHWEIGHT, AND PRETERM BIRTH. WE WILL ALSO CONDUCT IN-DEPTH QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS WITH PHYSICIANS TO ILLUMINATE HOW FPLS ARE INTERPRETED AND IMPLEMENTED IN PRENATAL, LABOR, AND DELIVERY SETTINGS AND HOW THEY INFLUENCE PATIENT CARE AND OUTCOMES (AIM 2). THIS TIMELY AND INNOVATIVE RESEARCH WILL PRODUCE CRITICAL INFORMATION FOR CLINICIANS, HEALTH CARE SYSTEMS, AND MEDICAL INTERVENTIONS AIMED AT IMPROVING INFANT HEALTH. THIS PROPOSAL ALIGNS WITH NICHD’S RESEARCH PRIORITIES ON PREGNANCY, INFANT HEALTH, AND MATERNAL HEALTH. THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR, DR. RILEY, IS UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO CONDUCT THIS RESEARCH BY BUILDING ON HER PRIOR EXPERTISE IN SOCIAL AND REPRODUCTIVE EPIDEMIOLOGY AND EXPANDING HER SKILLSET IN MATERNAL AND INFANT HEALTH RESEARCH. DURING THE K99 MENTORED PHASE, THE CANDIDATE WILL RECEIVE STRUCTURED MENTORSHIP FROM HER THOUGHTFULLY ASSEMBLED MENTORSHIP TEAM AND COMPLETE COURSEWORK, WORKSHOPS, AND DIRECTED STUDIES IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: 1) LEGAL EPIDEMIOLOGY; 2) ADVANCED QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES; 3) QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWING AND ANALYSIS; AND 4) INDEPENDENT RESEARCH LEADERSHIP SKILLS, SUCH AS GRANT WRITING, PROJECT MANAGEMENT, AND RESEARCH COMMUNICATION. THE EXCEPTIONAL MENTORSHIP TEAM WITH RELEVANT RESEARCH EXPERTISE AND SUBSTANTIAL MENTORING EXPERIENCE WILL SUPPORT COMPLETION OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH, TRAINING PLAN, AND A SUCCESSFUL TRANSITION TO INDEPENDENCE. THE STRATEGICALLY INTEGRATED MENTORSHIP, TRAINING, AND RESEARCH PLANS WILL PROVIDE THE CANDIDATE WITH A DISTINCT SET OF EXPERTISE AND SKILLS TO CONDUCT LONG-TERM, IMPACTFUL RESEARCH ON REPRODUCTIVE, MATERNAL, AND INFANT HEALTH IN FUTURE R-SERIES PROPOSALS. THIS PATHWAY TO INDEPENDENCE AWARD WILL ENABLE THE CANDIDATE TO DEVELOP INTO AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR LEADING RESEARCH THAT GENERATES RIGOROUS EPIDEMIOLOGICAL EVIDENCE TO IMPROVE REPRODUCTIVE, MATERNAL, AND INFANT HEALTH OUTCOMES IN THE US.

description: LEVERAGING BIOBANK-SCALE DATA TO ELUCIDATE THE ROLE OF THE X CHROMOSOME IN HUMAN COMPLEX DISEASES - THE X CHROMOSOME COMPRISES 5% OF THE GENOME AND CONTAINS OVER 800 PROTEIN CODING GENES. LARGE GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDIES HAVE MADE ADVANCES IN THE PAST ~20 YEARS IN CONNECTING GENES AND VARIANTS TO DISEASES; HOWEVER, THEY HAVE REGULARLY NEGLECTED TO INCLUDE THE X CHROMOSOME. RECENT STUDIES, THOUGH, HAVE SHOWN SIGNIFICANT ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN A NUMBER OF TRAITS INCLUDING ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, LIPID LEVELS, AND KIDNEY DISORDERS AND THE X CHROMOSOME POINTING TO ITS IMPORTANT ROLE IN DISEASE GENETICS. I PROPOSE TO USE BIOBANK SCALE DATA TO GENERATE A COMPREHENSIVE PICTURE OF THE ROLE OF THE X CHROMOSOME IN COMPLEX TRAIT GENETICS AND HOW SELECTION HAS IMPACTED ITS GENETIC ARCHITECTURE. FIRST, I WILL USE A NEW METHODOLOGY DEVELOPED BY THE REICH GROUP THAT EXAMINES IMPUTED GENOTYPES FROM ANCIENT DNA TIME SERIES DATA TO DETECT SIGNALS OF DIRECTIONAL SELECTION IN THE HUMAN PAST. THIS TECHNIQUE WILL ALLOW FOR INSIGHT INTO HOW VARIATION ON THE X CHROMOSOME HAS BEEN SHAPED BY ADAPTATION AND THE GENES AND PHENOTYPES AFFECTED. NEXT, I WILL USE LARGE, DEEPLY-PHENOTYPED BIOBANKS SUCH AS UK BIOBANK AND ALL OF US TO CONDUCT ASSOCIATION TESTING ON THE X CHROMOSOME WITH AN EXTENSIVE SET OF TRAITS AND DISEASES AND FINE-MAP THE IMPLICATED LOCI. FROM THIS, I WILL BE ABLE TO EXPLORE HOW TRAIT HERITABILITY IS DISTRIBUTED ON THE X CHROMOSOME AND EXAMINE SOME OF THE COMMON VARIANTS ASSOCIATED WITH DISEASE. FINALLY, USING THESE SAME LARGE DATASETS, I WILL PERFORM RARE VARIANT AND GENE-BASED ASSOCIATION TESTING. THESE TWO ANALYSES WILL LEVERAGE RARE VARIATION AVAILABLE FROM SEQUENCING DATA AND WILL COMPLEMENT THE COMMON VARIANT ASSOCIATIONS TO PRODUCE A COMPLETE PORTRAIT OF THE PART THE X CHROMOSOME PLAYS IN COMPLEX DISEASES. ELUCIDATING THIS RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE FORCES OF NATURAL SELECTION AND THE GENETIC ARCHITECTURE OF DISEASES ON THE X CHROMOSOME WILL EXPAND OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLE OF THE X CHROMOSOME IN SHAPING HUMAN HEALTH. THIS PROJECT WILL TAKE PLACE AT DR. DAVID REICH’S GROUP AND UNDER HIS MENTORSHIP AT HARVARD UNIVERSITY. DR. REICH IS AN EXPERT ON ANCIENT DNA, SELECTION SCANS, AND THE ROLE OF ADMIXTURE AND POPULATION STRUCTURE IN GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION TESTS. MY ADVISORY TEAM INCLUDES ADDITIONAL EXPERTISE IN FINE-MAPPING, THE HERITABILITY OF COMPLEX TRAITS, RARE VARIANTS, AND FUNCTIONAL INTERPRETATION OF VARIANTS. DURING THE K99 PHASE OF THE AWARD, I WOULD TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THEIR EXPERTISE TO BEGIN STUDYING SELECTION, VARIANT IDENTIFICATION AND INTERPRETATION, AND THE POPULATION STRUCTURE OBSERVED ON THE X CHROMOSOME. THIS, ALONG WITH THE TRAINING I WILL RECEIVE FROM DR. REICH IN WRITING PAPERS, LAB MANAGEMENT, AND OTHER PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT TOPICS, WILL PREPARE ME WITH THE SKILLS NEEDED TO TRANSITION MY INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROJECT EXAMINING THE IMPACT OF COMMON AND RARE VARIANTS ON THE X CHROMOSOME ON DISEASES TO A FACULTY POSITION. IN MY LONG-TERM RESEARCH CAREER, I PLAN TO COMBINE MY EXPERIENCE IN POPULATION GENETICS AND RARE VARIANT STUDIES TO UNDERSTAND HOW COMMON AND RARE GENETIC VARIANTS HAVE BEEN SHAPED BY SELECTION AND THEIR INTERTWINED EFFECTS ON THE ARCHITECTURE OF COMPLEX DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MODELING CELL FATE AND PERTURBATION DYNAMICS WITH GENERATIVE AI USING SINGLE-CELL AND SPATIAL OMICS DATA - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT BIOLOGICAL SYSTEMS ARE INHERENTLY DYNAMIC, SPATIALLY STRUCTURED, AND GOVERNED BY COMPLEX NONLINEAR GENE REGULATORY PROGRAMS. TRADITIONAL COMPUTATIONAL MODELS OFTEN STRUGGLE TO CAPTURE THE FULL EXTENT OF THIS COMPLEXITY, PARTICULARLY THE CONTEXT-DEPENDENT WAYS IN WHICH CELLS INTERACT, DIFFERENTIATE, AND RESPOND TO PERTURBATIONS OVER TIME AND SPACE. EXPLORING DISEASE MECHANISMS AND OPTIMIZING THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS TYPICALLY REQUIRES LABOR- INTENSIVE, LARGE-SCALE EXPERIMENTAL SCREENS. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT CONDITIONAL GENERATIVE AI MODELS, SPECIFICALLY DIFFUSION-BASED ARCHITECTURES THAT INCORPORATE MOLECULAR, SPATIAL, AND TEMPORAL INFORMATION FROM HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING TECHNOLOGIES, CAN LEARN BIOLOGICALLY GROUNDED LATENT REPRESENTATIONS OF GENE REGULATORY DYNAMICS TO ACCURATELY FORECAST CELL STATE TRANSITIONS OVER TIME AND ACROSS PERTURBATIVE CONTEXTS. THESE MODELS WILL ENABLE THE DISCOVERY OF CAUSAL MOLECULAR DRIVERS OF FATE DECISIONS AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSES, GENERATING TESTABLE PREDICTIONS FOR DEVELOPMENT, DISEASE, AND REGENERATIVE PROCESSES. BUILDING ON MY PHD WORK IN THE LABS OF DR. ELHAM AZIZI AND DR. KAM LEONG AT COLUMBIA AND MY POSTDOCTORAL WORK WITH DR. JAMES ZOU AND DR. STEPHEN QUAKE AT STANFORD, I LEVERAGE INTERDISCIPLINARY EXPERTISE IN DISEASE MODELING, COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY, AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE. I HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED A CONDITIONAL DIFFUSION-BASED GENERATIVE AI MODEL FOR PREDICTING CELLULAR TRANSCRIPTOMICS. IN MY K99 MENTORED PHASE, I WILL EXTEND THIS WORK TO BUILD A GENERATIVE TIME-SERIES VIRTUAL CELL FOUNDATION MODEL (AIM 1) THAT GENERATES TRANSCRIPTOMIC TRAJECTORIES AND PREDICTS CELL FATE TRANSITIONS ACROSS SPECIES AND DEVELOPMENTAL SYSTEMS, IN COLLABORATION WITH DR. ZHI HUANG (UNIVERSITY OF PENNSYLVANIA) AND DR. XIAO YANG (JOHNS HOPKINS). IN THE R00 INDEPENDENT PHASE, I WILL EXTEND THIS PLATFORM TO INCORPORATE SPATIAL AND MULTIMODAL DATA, INCLUDING SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS AND HISTOLOGY, TO SIMULATE VIRTUAL CELL BEHAVIOR WITHIN TISSUE CONTEXTS (AIM 2). APPLICATIONS WILL INCLUDE MODELING SPATIOTEMPORAL BRAIN AGING AND GENERATING SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOME CONDITIONED ON HISTOPATHOLOGY FEATURES IN CANCER MICROENVIRONMENTS, IN COLLABORATION WITH DR. FAN RONG (YALE), DR. ALEXANDER Y. RUDENSKY AND DR. GEORGE PLITAS (MSK), AND FACULTY AT MY FUTURE INSTITUTION. TO GROUND THE MODELS IN BIOLOGICAL REALISM AND TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE, I WILL APPLY THIS COMPREHENSIVE PLATFORM TO PREDICT GENETIC RESPONSE TO THERAPEUTIC PERTURBATIONS, IDENTIFYING KEY MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING DRUG SENSITIVITY AND RESISTANCE (AIM 3), IN COLLABORATION WITH DR. DHAVAL SHAH (BUFFALO) AND CLINICAL PARTNERS, USING PRECLINICAL AND PATIENT-DERIVED DATASETS FOR MODEL VALIDATION. description: FIBRIL-TARGETING NANOBODIES FOR RESTORING MITOCHONDRIAL STRESS AND CARDIAC FUNCTION IN ATTR-CM - PROJECT SUMMARY TRANSTHYRETIN AMYLOIDOSIS CARDIOMYOPATHY (ATTR-CM) IS A PROGRESSIVE, LIFE-THREATENING DISEASE CAUSED BY EXTRACELLULAR DEPOSITION OF MISFOLDED TRANSTHYRETIN (TTR) FIBRILS IN THE MYOCARDIUM. THESE AGGREGATES IMPAIR MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION, CALCIUM SIGNALING, AND CARDIOMYOCYTE CONTRACTILITY, LEADING TO HEART FAILURE. WHILE STABILIZERS AND RNAI THERAPIES LIMIT TTR PRODUCTION/STABILITY LOSS, THEY DO NOT REMOVE DEPOSITED FIBRILS, WHICH IS THE ONGOING SOURCE OF CARDIAC DYSFUNCTION. THIS PROJECT WILL DEFINE HOW FIBRILS DRIVE MITOCHONDRIAL AND CA²⁺ FAILURE, IDENTIFY HOST-DIRECTED DRIVERS TO NOMINATE A CO-THERAPY TARGET, AND DEVELOP NANOBODY THERAPEUTICS TO CLEAR FIBRILS AND RESTORE CARDIAC FUNCTION. USING PATIENT-ANCHORED RESOURCES, ATTR-CM CARDIAC TISSUE, PATIENT IPSC LINES, AND VASCULARIZED CARDIAC ORGANOIDS (VCOS) BENCHMARKED TO ADULT HUMAN HEART, WITH ESTABLISHED FIBRIL-DEPOSITION PROTOCOLS, DR. ZEHRA YILDIRIM WILL MODEL DISEASE PHENOTYPES IN A HUMAN-RELEVANT SYSTEM. AIM 1 WILL DEFINE HOW FIBRIL DEPOSITION DRIVES MITOCHONDRIAL AND CA²⁺ DYSFUNCTION USING SEAHORSE METABOLIC ANALYSIS, CRYO-FIB/SEM, OPTICAL MAPPING, AND MEA ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, AND WILL INTEGRATE MULTI-OMICS AND QUANTITATIVE PROTEOMICS TO MAP TIME-DEPENDENT, TTR-LINKED NICHE MATURATION (APOLIPOPROTEIN COAT, COMPLEMENT/ECM, LYSOSOME) AND ASSOCIATED RESPIRATORY-CHAIN ATTRITION AND OXIDATIVE/IRON STRESS CONSISTENT WITH FUNCTIONAL READOUTS. AIM 2 WILL LEVERAGE AI-GUIDED PROTEIN ENGINEERING COMBINED WITH A PRE-EXISTING NANOBODY REPERTOIRE AND YEAST-DISPLAY SELECTION TO GENERATE HIGH-SPECIFICITY ANTI-FIBRIL NANOBODIES WITH MULTIPLE HIGH-PRIORITY BINDERS READILY IDENTIFIED AND ARE ADVANCING THROUGH EXPRESSION AND DEVELOPABILITY TESTING, DE-RISKING TRANSLATION. AIM 3 WILL EVALUATE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF THE TOP CANDIDATE IN PRECLINICAL ORGANOID AND MOUSE MODELS. DR. YILDIRIM’S CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN INTEGRATES TRAINING IN COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY, AI-DRIVEN DRUG DISCOVERY, AND STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY TO COMPLEMENT HER EXPERTISE IN CARDIOVASCULAR MOLECULAR BIOLOGY AND BIOENGINEERING. POSSU HUANG (AI-DRIVEN PROTEIN ENGINEERING), SHE WILL GAIN EXPERTISE IN PROTEIN ENGINEERING, STRUCTURAL PROTEOMICS, AND THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT. COLLABORATION WITH DR. WAH CHIU AT SLAC WILL PROVIDE HANDS-ON CRYO-FIB/SEM TRAINING. EXTERNSHIPS IN DR. HUANG’S LAB (AI NANOBODY DESIGN) AND DR. CHIU’S LAB (MITOCHONDRIAL STRUCTURAL ANALYSIS), TOGETHER WITH COURSEWORK IN BIOINFORMATICS, STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY, AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH, WILL POSITION HER TO LAUNCH AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION WILL CLARIFY ATTR-CM PATHOGENESIS, DELIVER A TRANSLATABLE NANOBODY PLATFORM FOR AMYLOIDOSIS, AND ACCELERATE CLINICAL TRANSLATION OF AI-DESIGNED THERAPEUTICS, IMPROVING PATIENT OUTCOMES AND ADVANCING PRECISION CARDIOVASCULAR MEDICINE. THIS INTEGRATED, HUMAN-ANCHORED PLATFORM AND VALIDATED BINDER PIPELINE DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THE UNMET NEED FOR FIBRIL CLEARANCE IN ATTR-CM AND DE-RISKS THE K99 TO R00 TRANSITION WITH CLEAR, MEASURABLE MILESTONES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING THE GENETIC MODULATION OF PHENOTYPIC AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC CONVERGENCE IN BIPOLAR DISORDER AND SCHIZOPHRENIA - ABSTRACT SCHIZOPHRENIA (SCZ) AND BIPOLAR DISORDER (BD) ARE SEVERE PSYCHIATRIC CONDITIONS THAT AFFECT OVER 2% OF THE GLOBAL POPULATION, LEADING TO SIGNIFICANT DISABILITY, REDUCED LIFE EXPECTANCY, AND A HEAVY SOCIOECONOMIC BURDEN. GENETIC STUDIES HAVE ADVANCED OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE FACTORS CONTRIBUTING TO THESE DISORDERS, BUT MOST RESEARCH HAS BEEN CONDUCTED ON POPULATIONS OF FEW ANCESTRIES, LEAVING MAJOR GAPS IN HOW SCZ AND BD MANIFEST IN COMPREHENSIVE POPULATIONS. UNDERSTANDING THE GENETIC ARCHITECTURE OF THESE DISORDERS ACROSS MINIMALLY CHARACTERIZED GROUPS IS CRUCIAL FOR DEVELOPING MORE BROADLY APPLICABLE PRECISION MEDICINE APPROACHES. IN THIS RESEARCH PROPOSAL, I AIM TO INVESTIGATE THE GENETIC AND BIOLOGICAL CONVERGENCE OF SCZ AND BD BY LEVERAGING LARGE-SCALE DATASETS THAT INCLUDE MULTI-OMICS DATA—GENOMICS, TRANSCRIPTOMICS, AND CLINICAL DATA FROM COMPREHENSIVE AND UNIQUE POPULATIONS. SPECIFICALLY, I WILL (1) EVALUATE THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL CONVERGENCE OF SCZ AND BD GENES USING SINGLE-CELL RNA SEQUENCING (SCRNA-SEQ) DATA FROM NEURONS; (2) EXPLORE HOW RARE GENETIC VARIANTS IN SCZ AND BD IMPACT PHENOTYPIC COMORBIDITIES AND CONVERGENCE BY EXAMINING CLINICAL TRAJECTORIES AND COMORBIDITIES IN INDIVIDUALS USING LONGITUDINAL ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (EHRS); AND (3) EXTEND MY PRIOR WORK DEVELOPING THE GISMO EVOLUTIONARY CONSTRAINT METRIC TO NONCODING REGIONS THROUGH GISMO-REG, ENABLING SYSTEMATIC PRIORITIZATION OF REGULATORY ELEMENTS INTOLERANT TO DISRUPTION, AND PERFORMING RARE VARIANT BURDEN ANALYSES WITHIN THESE ELEMENTS TO IDENTIFY CONVERGENT NONCODING RISK FACTORS. TOGETHER, THESE AIMS WILL REVEAL KEY MOLECULAR, REGULATORY, AND CLINICAL PATHWAYS SHARED BETWEEN SCZ AND BD WHILE CLARIFYING DISORDER-SPECIFIC DIFFERENCES, PROVIDING A FOUNDATION FOR MORE PRECISE PSYCHIATRIC DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT. THIS PROJECT WILL BE LED BY DR. CALWING (CAL) LIAO, A STATISTICAL GENETICIST WITH EXPERTISE IN PSYCHIATRIC GENETICS, MULTI-OMIC DATA INTEGRATION, AND THE ANALYSIS OF RARE VARIANTS. DR. LIAO HAS DEVELOPED A COMPREHENSIVE RESEARCH PLAN TO COMPLETE THESE AIMS WHILE ADVANCING HIS CAREER DEVELOPMENT THROUGH TRAINING IN ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD ANALYSIS, SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOMICS, AND PSYCHIATRIC GENOMICS IN COMPREHENSIVE POPULATIONS. THIS WILL SUPPORT HIS LONG-TERM GOAL OF BECOMING AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR WHO INTEGRATES MULTI-OMIC AND GENETIC DATA TO UNCOVER THE MOLECULAR UNDERPINNINGS OF COMPLEX PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS SUCH AS SCZ AND BD. DR. LIAO’S EXCEPTIONAL ADVISORY TEAM WILL DIRECTLY SUPPORT HIS CAREER DEVELOPMENT. HIS PRIMARY MENTOR, DR. BEN NEALE, IS A LEADER IN PSYCHIATRIC GENETICS AND LARGE-SCALE GENETIC ANALYSIS. ADDITIONAL ADVISORY TEAM MEMBERS INCLUDE EXPERTS IN BIOSTATISTICS, FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS, AND PSYCHIATRIC PHENOTYPING, PROVIDING CRITICAL GUIDANCE ACROSS THE RESEARCH AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT OBJECTIVES. DR. LIAO’S ADVISORY TEAM, COMBINED WITH THE COLLABORATIVE AND RESOURCE-RICH ENVIRONMENT AT THE BROAD INSTITUTE OF MIT AND HARVARD, WILL ENSURE HIS SUCCESSFUL TRANSITION TO AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH CAREER IN PSYCHIATRIC GENETICS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMAGING AND PERTURBING CORTICAL NETWORK DYSREGULATION DURING SOCIAL BEHAVIOR IN AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER - PROJECT SUMMARY AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD) AFFECTS APPROXIMATELY 1.6% OF AMERICANS, WITH SEVERE CASES CHARACTERIZED BY PERVASIVE SOCIAL DEFICITS AND ALTERED SENSORY PROCESSING, YET EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS FOR THESE CORE SYMPTOMS REMAIN ELUSIVE. EMERGING EVIDENCE INDICATES THAT ASD ARISES FROM DISTRIBUTED CORTICAL NETWORK DYSREGULATION DRIVEN BY IMBALANCES IN EXCITATORY–INHIBITORY (E/I) ACTIVITY AND ALTERED NEUROMODULATORY SIGNALING. REMARKABLY, OPTOGENETIC AND PHARMACOLOGICAL INTERVENTIONS CAN RESCUE SOCIAL BEHAVIOR IN ASD MOUSE MODELS, OFFERING A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO UNCOVER THE NETWORK PRINCIPLES UNDERLYING BEHAVIORAL RESTORATION. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH LOCAL MANIPULATIONS IN KEY HUBS, SUCH AS OPTOGENETIC INHIBITION OF THE MEDIAL PREFRONTAL CORTEX (MPFC), PROPAGATE TO NORMALIZE CORTEX-WIDE ACTIVITY REMAIN UNKNOWN. DISSECTING THESE MECHANISMS IS KEY FOR DEVELOPING NEW THERAPEUTICS, BUT REQUIRES TOOLS CAPABLE OF CAPTURING AND CONTROLLING DISTRIBUTED CORTICAL NETWORKS DURING BEHAVIOR—CAPABILITIES THAT CURRENT METHODS LACK. TO BRIDGE THIS GAP, I WILL DEVELOP AND APPLY NEXT-GENERATION IMAGING AND PERTURBATION TECHNOLOGIES TO MAP AND MANIPULATE CORTEX-WIDE NETWORKS DURING BOTH HEAD-FIXED AND FREELY MOVING SOCIAL BEHAVIOR. IN THE K99 MENTORED PHASE, I WILL USE THE ULTRASENSITIVE, DUAL-COLOR HEAD-FIXED MACROSCOPE THAT I DEVELOPED TO SIMULTANEOUSLY MEASURE EXCITATORY, INHIBITORY, AND SUBTHRESHOLD VOLTAGE ACTIVITY ACROSS THE DORSAL CORTEX, COMBINED WITH OPTOGENETIC AND PHARMACOLOGICAL INTERVENTIONS, TO DETERMINE HOW LOCAL RESTORATION OF E/I BALANCE RESHAPES LARGE-SCALE NETWORK DYNAMICS. IN PARALLEL, I WILL DEPLOY A MINIATURIZED MACROSCOPE FOR CORTEX-WIDE IMAGING AND TARGETED OPTOGENETIC STIMULATION IN FREELY MOVING MICE TO INVESTIGATE NETWORK DYSFUNCTION DURING NATURALISTIC SOCIAL INTERACTIONS. THIS WILL ESTABLISH A UNIQUE EXPERIMENTAL PLATFORM FOR CAUSAL INSIGHT INTO THE RESTORATION OF E/I BALANCE AND SOCIAL BEHAVIOR. BUILDING ON THIS FOUNDATION, THE R00 INDEPENDENT PHASE WILL INTEGRATE GENETICALLY ENCODED SENSORS FOR ACETYLCHOLINE, SEROTONIN, DOPAMINE, AND NOREPINEPHRINE TO MAP NEUROMODULATORY DYNAMICS ALONGSIDE NEURAL ACTIVITY DURING SOCIAL BEHAVIOR. THESE STUDIES WILL GENERATE A COMPREHENSIVE ATLAS LINKING NEURAL AND NEUROMODULATORY NETWORK DYSREGULATION TO BEHAVIOR AND TO PHARMACOLOGICAL OR OPTOGENETIC RESCUE. COLLECTIVELY, THIS RESEARCH WILL REVEAL THE CORTEX-WIDE CIRCUIT MECHANISMS UNDERLYING ASD, PROVIDE MECHANISTIC INSIGHT INTO HOW PRO-SOCIAL INTERVENTIONS ACT AT THE NETWORK LEVEL, AND ESTABLISH A SCALABLE FRAMEWORK FOR STUDYING BRAIN-WIDE CIRCUIT DYSFUNCTION. I WILL BE MENTORED TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS BY LEADERS IN SYSTEMS NEUROSCIENCE, OPTOGENETICS, AND THEORETICAL MODELING, WITH GUIDANCE FROM AN ADVISORY TEAM AT THE FOREFRONT OF BRAIN NETWORK AND AUTISM RESEARCH. STANFORD’S EXCEPTIONAL RESOURCES, TRAINING, AND COLLABORATIVE ENVIRONMENT WILL PROVIDE THE TECHNICAL AND PROFESSIONAL FOUNDATION TO LAUNCH AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM THAT BRIDGES TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT AND SYSTEMS NEUROSCIENCE TO UNCOVER FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES OF CORTICAL NETWORK FUNCTION AND DYSFUNCTION.

description: MAPPING NEUROENDOCRINE RISK FOR DEPRESSION ACROSS ADOLESCENCE - PROJECT ABSTRACT  NEUROENDOCRINE TRANSITIONS, SUCH AS PUBERTY, PREGNANCY, AND MENOPAUSE, ARE INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED AS VULNERABLE WINDOWS FOR DEPRESSION RISK. MENARCHE (THE ONSET OF MENSTRUATION) IS A UNIVERSAL MILESTONE DURING THE FIRST POSTNATAL NEUROENDOCRINE TRANSITION, PUBERTY. MENARCHE MARKS THE ACTIVATION OF THE HYPOTHALAMIC- PITUITARY-OVARIAN AXIS AND A SHIFT TOWARD CYCLICAL OVARIAN HORMONE SURGES WHICH CAN SHAPE THE DEVELOPMENT OF BRAIN NETWORKS. OF PARTICULAR RELEVANCE IS THE SALIENCE NETWORK, WHICH IS ENRICHED FOR OVARIAN HORMONE RECEPTORS AND IMPLICATED IN DEPRESSION. FOLLOWING MENARCHE, THE SUBSEQUENT MENSTRUAL CYCLE STABILIZATION PERIOD CAN LAST SEVERAL YEARS, CREATING A PROLONGED WINDOW DURING WHICH IRREGULAR HORMONE PATTERNS MAY INFLUENCE NEURAL DEVELOPMENT AND AFFECTIVE RISK. THIS PROPOSAL INVESTIGATES MENARCHE AND MENSTRUAL CYCLE STABILIZATION AS TWO COMPONENTS OF A NEUROENDOCRINE TRANSITION UNDERLYING ADOLESCENT VULNERABILITY TO DEPRESSION. THE OVERARCHING GOAL IS TO UNDERSTAND HOW THE PRONOUNCED CHANGES IN HORMONAL FLUCTUATIONS THAT ACCOMPANY THIS TRANSITION SHAPE SALIENCE NETWORK DEVELOPMENT AND MENTAL HEALTH RISK. AIM 1 WILL CHARACTERIZE HOW MENARCHE FUNCTIONS AS A DEVELOPMENTAL INFLECTION POINT FOR DEPRESSION RISK AND SALIENCE NETWORK ORGANIZATION. USING CURRENTLY AVAILABLE DATA FROM THE ABCD STUDY (V6.0, AGES 9–16; N=5,676 FEMALES), WE WILL QUANTIFY HOW MENARCHE ONSET INFLUENCES CHANGES IN DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS AND SALIENCE NETWORK TOPOGRAPHY. WE WILL EXTEND THESE ANALYSES TO THE COMPLETE ABCD DATASET (V10.0, AGES 9–20) TO EXAMINE HOW AGE AT MENARCHE MODERATES CUMULATIVE RISK AND SALIENCE NETWORK TOPOGRAPHY. AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE MENSTRUAL CYCLE STABILIZATION AS A SECOND WINDOW OF VULNERABILITY IN ADOLESCENCE USING A MULTI-COHORT APPROACH. WE WILL LEVERAGE A RETROSPECTIVE ULTRA-HIGH-FIELD 7T DATASET (N=45, AGES 16–20, ~3–11 YEARS POST-MENARCHE) ALONGSIDE A NEWLY COLLECTED DENSE PROSPECTIVE DATASET (N=45, AGES 13–15, ~2 YEARS POST-MENARCHE). THIS DESIGN ALLOWS US TO EXAMINE BOTH SHORT-TERM NEUROENDOCRINE DYNAMICS IN THE EARLY POST-MENARCHEAL YEARS AND LONGER-TERM PATTERNS OF SALIENCE NETWORK ORGANIZATION AND DEPRESSION RISK. TOGETHER, THESE AIMS WILL IDENTIFY HOW EARLY NEUROENDOCRINE TRANSITIONS AND THE PROCESS OF MENSTRUAL CYCLE STABILIZATION RELATE TO DEPRESSION RISK, HIGHLIGHTING THE ROLE OF DEVELOPMENTAL CHANGES IN SALIENCE NETWORK ORGANIZATION THAT ARE INFLUENCED BY OVARIAN HORMONE DYNAMICS. THE SUPPORT OF THIS K99/R00 PATHWAY TO INDEPENDENCE AWARD WILL PROVIDE THE APPLICANT WITH THE TRAINING NECESSARY TO ACHIEVE THESE AIMS, INCLUDING TRAINING IN DEVELOPMENTAL NEUROSCIENCE, NEUROENDOCRINOLOGY, AND PSYCHIATRY, BIG DATA NEUROINFORMATICS, NETWORK NEUROSCIENCE, AND PRECISION FUNCTIONAL MAPPING. THESE TRAINING OBJECTIVES WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED WITH THE SUPPORT OF AN OUTSTANDING MENTORSHIP TEAM, DRS. LARSEN, JACOBS, BELTZ, CULLEN, FAIR, AND NELSON, AND THE WORLD CLASS TECHNICAL AND INTELLECTUAL RESOURCES OF THE UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA. TOGETHER, THE PROPOSED SCIENTIFIC AIMS AND TRAINING OBJECTIVES WILL ESTABLISH THE FOUNDATION FOR AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM AIMED AT ELUCIDATING THE NEURODEVELOPMENTAL PATHWAYS LINKING NEUROENDOCRINE TRANSITIONS TO ADOLESCENT DEPRESSION.

description: LINKING ADOLESCENT ENVIRONMENTAL ENRICHMENT TO ASSOCIATION CORTEX PLASTICITY AND PSYCHIATRIC RESILIENCY - PROJECT ABSTRACT THE MAJORITY OF LIFETIME PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS ONSET IN ADOLESCENCE, THUS THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR ACTIONABLE, NEUROSCIENCE-INFORMED APPROACHES TO PROMOTING ADOLESCENT WELL-BEING. RISK FOR PSYCHOPATHOLOGY IN ADOLESCENCE IS STRONGLY SHAPED BY INTERACTIONS BETWEEN ENVIRONMENTAL INPUTS AND PLASTICITY IN THE BRAIN’S HIGHER- ORDER ASSOCIATION CORTICES. RESEARCH IN HUMANS HAS FOUND THAT ENVIRONMENTAL ADVERSITY EXPERIENCED IN ADOLESCENCE LIMITS ASSOCIATION CORTEX PLASTICITY, LEADING TO POORER COGNITIVE HEALTH AND GREATER PSYCHOPATHOLOGY. IN CONTRAST, RESEARCH IN RODENTS HAS SHOWN THAT ENVIRONMENTAL ENRICHMENT—ENCOMPASSING PHYSICAL, COGNITIVE, AND SOCIAL STIMULATION—ENHANCES CORTICAL PLASTICITY, IMPROVES COGNITION, AND MITIGATES PHENOTYPES OF PSYCHIATRIC DISEASE. DESPITE THE TRANSFORMATIVE POTENTIAL OF ENRICHMENT, STUDIES IN HUMANS HAVE PRIMARILY EXAMINED THE DETRIMENTAL IMPACT OF NEGATIVE ENVIRONMENTS ON THE YOUTH BRAIN. IT IS THEREFORE NOT KNOWN HOW AND WHEN THE ENVIRONMENT CAN BE OPTIMALLY ENRICHED TO FOSTER HEALTHY DEVELOPMENTAL TRAJECTORIES. THIS PROPOSAL WILL TEST THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT THERE IS A MID-ADOLESCENT CRITICAL PERIOD OF HEIGHTENED ASSOCIATION CORTEX PLASTICITY DURING WHICH ENRICHMENT MAXIMALLY PROMOTES HEALTHY COGNITION AND RESILIENCE TO PSYCHOPATHOLOGY. IT WILL TAKE THE FORM OF A NATIONWIDE, NATURAL EXPERIMENT OF ENRICHMENT IN THE ADOLESCENT BRAIN COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT STUDY (ABCD; N = 11,878). MRI, COGNITIVE, CLINICAL, AND ENVIRONMENTAL DATA COLLECTED FROM YOUTH LONGITUDINALLY AT AGES 9-10, 11-12, 13-14, 15-16, AND 17-18 WILL BE USED. AIM 1 WILL EMPLOY DEEP PHENOTYPING OF POSITIVE ASPECTS OF YOUTHS’ PHYSICAL, COGNITIVE, AND SOCIAL ENVIRONMENTS TO DERIVE AN INDIVIDUALIZED INDEX OF ENRICHMENT AND IDENTIFY WHEN ENRICHMENT HAS THE LARGEST IMPACT ON COMPLEX COGNITION. AIM 2 WILL CHARACTERIZE WHEN NEUROBIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF PLASTICITY HYPOTHESIZED TO CONFER SENSITIVITY TO ENRICHMENT DEVELOP ACROSS THE SENSORIMOTOR- ASSOCIATION CORTICAL HIERARCHY. PRECLINICAL RESEARCH ON CRITICAL PERIODS HAS ESTABLISHED THAT ENVIRONMENT-DRIVEN INCREASES IN THALAMOCORTICAL STRUCTURAL CONNECTIVITY PROMOTE CORTICAL PLASTICITY, WHEREAS INCREASES IN CORTICAL MYELIN CONSOLIDATE PLASTICITY FOLLOWING ENVIRONMENTAL ADAPTATION. BY TRANSLATING THESE NEUROBIOLOGICAL HALLMARKS OF PLASTICITY TO IN VIVO MRI, THIS AIM WILL TEMPORALLY DEMARCATE THE OPENING AND CLOSING OF AN ADOLESCENT CRITICAL PERIOD OF ASSOCIATION CORTEX PLASTICITY. AIM 3 WILL EXAMINE WHEN—BETWEEN THE AGES OF 9 AND 18—ENRICHMENT MOST IMPACTS THALAMIC CONNECTIVITY AND MYELIN IN THE ASSOCIATION CORTEX TO CONFER RESILIENCY TO TRANSDIAGNOSTIC PSYCHIATRIC VULNERABILITY. THE PI, DR. SYDNOR, WILL RECEIVE TRAINING IN DEVELOPMENTAL PSYCHOPATHOLOGY, ENVIRONMENTAL ENRICHMENT, POPULATION NEUROIMAGING INFORMATICS, AND LONGITUDINAL AND CAUSAL MODELING. TRAINING WILL OCCUR WITHIN THE UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH’S WORLD-CLASS RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT WITH THE SUPPORT OF OUTSTANDING MENTORS DRS. LUNA, FORBES, SHERIDAN, FAIR, THOMPSON, AND BARCH. THIS K99/R00 PATHWAY TO INDEPENDENCE AWARD WILL ALLOW THE PI TO ESTABLISH AN INNOVATIVE AND INDEPENDENT RESEARCH LAB STUDYING HOW MENTAL ILLNESS CAN BE PREVENTED BY LEVERAGING THE DEVELOPING BRAIN’S CAPACITY FOR ADAPTIVE, ENVIRONMENT-DRIVEN PLASTICITY.

description: CLINICAL PREDICTION, GENETIC ARCHITECTURE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATION IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, LATE, AND MIXED PATHOLOGY - PROJECT SUMMARY RECENT STUDIES HIGHLIGHT THE FACT THAT THE LARGE PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT OF LIMBIC-PREDOMINANT AGE-RELATED TDP-43 ENCEPHALOPATHY (LATE), WHICH AFFECTS APPROXIMATE ONE-THIRD OF ADULTS OVER AGE 85. LATE IS FREQUENTLY UNDER- RECOGNIZED OR MISCLASSIFIED AS ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD). CURRENTLY, AUTOPSY-CONFIRMED AD AND LATE NEUROPATHOLOGIC CHANGES (ADNC AND LATE-NC) REMAIN THE GOLD STANDARD FOR DIAGNOSIS. ADNC AND LATE-NC OFTEN CO-OCCUR (MIXED-NC) IN ADVANCED AGE. TO ENABLE EARLY PREDICTION, IT IS URGENT TO: (1) ACCURATELY PREDICT UNDERLYING NEUROPATHOLOGIC (NP) PHENOTYPES USING ANTE-MORTEM PROGNOSTIC APPROACHES; (2) IDENTIFY DISEASE- SPECIFIC GENETIC CONTRIBUTORS; AND (3) CHARACTERIZE TIME-VARYING ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS MODIFYING GENETIC RISK. PREVIOUS PREDICTIVE MODELS FOCUSED ON ADNC, OVERLOOKING LATE-NC AND MIXED-NC. MOST EXISTING GENETIC ANALYSES RELIED ON CATEGORICAL NP OUTCOMES AND UTILIZED BIALLELIC VARIANTS EXCLUDING MULTIALLELIC VARIATION. PRIOR GENE–ENVIRONMENT (G×E) INTERACTION ANALYSES TYPICALLY EXAMINED ONE-BY-ONE AND SINGLE-TIME-POINT MODELS. TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS, WE WILL INTEGRATE MULTIMODALITIES TO DEVELOP PREDICTIVE MODELS FOR ADNC, LATE- NC, AND MIXED-NC BY CONSTRUCTING LATENT SCORES WITHIN A UNIFIED FRAMEWORK. WE WILL EMPLOY TWO COMPLEMENTARY APPROACHES: SUPERVISED STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELING (SEM) TO YIELD “LATENT BRAIN FUNCTION SCORES (LBFSS)” CAPTURING THE AGE-DEPENDENT AND MULTIDIMENSIONAL BRAIN FUNCTIONS, AND PSEUDOTIME ANALYSIS TO DERIVE “LATENT DISEASE PROGRESSION SCORES (LDPSS)” TRACING AGE-ANCHORED TRAJECTORIES OF DISEASE PROGRESSION. WE WILL INCLUDE MULTIALLELIC VARIANTS IN GENETIC ANALYSES AND CONSTRUCT MIDLIFE AND LATER-LIFE ENVIRONMENTAL RISK SCORES (ERSS) TO TEST COMPREHENSIVE G×E INTERACTIONS. BY LEVERAGING LBFSS AND LDPSS AS CONTINUOUS NP PROXIES IN PARTICIPANTS WITH AND WITHOUT NP DATA, WE WILL INCREASE SAMPLE SIZES AND STATISTICAL POWER AND ENHANCE THE DISCOVERY OF NOVEL GENETIC RISKS AND INSIGHTFUL ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFIERS. SPECIFIC AIM 1: DEVELOP AND EVALUATE PREDICTIVE MODELS FOR ADNC, LATE-NC, AND MIXED-NC. USING DATA FROM THE NATIONAL ALZHEIMER’S COORDINATING CENTER, THE ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE NEUROIMAGING INITIATIVE, THE RELIGIOUS ORDERS STUDY, THE MEMORY AND AGING PROJECT, AND THE ADULT CHANGES IN THOUGHT STUDY, WE WILL PERFORM SEM AND PSEUDOTIME ANALYSIS TO CONSTRUCT LBFSS AND LDPSS AND DEVELOP PREDICTIVE MODELS. SPECIFIC AIM 2: UNCOVER NOVEL GENETIC CONTRIBUTORS TO ADNC, LATE-NC, AND MIXED-NC. THE ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE SEQUENCING PROJECT WHOLE-GENOME SEQUENCING DATA WILL BE USED TO IDENTIFY SUSCEPTIBILITY LOCI INCLUDING BIALLELIC AND MULTIALLELIC VARIANTS. DERIVED LBFSS AND LDPSS WILL SERVE AS CONTINUOUS NP PROXIES. SPECIFIC AIM 3: EXAMINE ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS MODIFYING ADNC, LATE-NC, AND MIXED-NC GENETIC RISK. NACC, ROS, AND MAP DATA, INCLUDING SOCIAL, PHYSICAL, BEHAVIROAL, AND LIFESTYLE FACTORS, WILL BE USED TO CREATE MIDLIFE AND LATER-LIFE ERSS, BY APPLYING THE ITEM RESPONSE THEORY-BASED MULTIDIMENSIONAL GENERALIZED PARTIAL CREDIT MODEL, AND ASSESS HOW THESE ERSS MODIFY GENETIC RISK ON LBFSS AND LDPSS.

description: DEFINING NETWORK FUNCTION ACROSS SLEEP AND WAKE IN NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE MAMMALIAN BRAIN IS FUNDAMENTALLY INTERCONNECTED. INDIVIDUAL NEURONS CONTACT HUNDREDS TO THOUSANDS OF LOCAL- AND LONG‑RANGE PARTNERS. WITHIN THIS ARCHITECTURE, ADAPTIVE BEHAVIOR RELIES ON THE COORDINATED ACTIVATION OF DISTRIBUTED NETWORKS. ATYPICAL NETWORK ACTIVATION IS COMMON IN MONOGENIC NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS (MNDDS) – INCLUDING ANGELMAN (AS), DUPLICATION 15Q (DUP15Q), PITT HOPKINS (PTHS), AND RETT (RTT) SYNDROMES – YET THE TRANSLATIONAL IMPACT OF THIS KNOWLEDGE IS LIMITED BY OPEN QUESTIONS:  1) DO SPECIFIC FEATURES OF NETWORK DYSFUNCTION DRIVE CORE MNDD-RELATED BEHAVIOR IMPAIRMENTS?  2) DOES DISRUPTED SLEEP – A KEY REGULATOR OF NETWORK PLASTICITY – CONTRIBUTE TO NETWORK DYSFUNCTION?  3) DO SHARED BEHAVIOR IMPAIRMENTS ACROSS DIVERSE CONDITIONS ARISE FROM COMMON NETWORK DYSFUNCTION? ANSWERING THESE QUESTIONS CAN LEAD TO UNTAPPED THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES, INCLUDING NETWORK-LEVEL, SLEEP-TARGETED, AND CROSS-CONDITION APPROACHES – A CRITICAL NEED AS DISEASE-MODIFYING TREATMENTS REMAIN RARE. IMPAIRED MOTOR CONTROL IS ONE OF THE EARLIEST, MOST CONSERVED, AND MOST IMPACTFUL PHENOTYPES ACROSS THESE MNDDS. IN THIS PROJECT, I STUDY VALIDATED MOUSE MODELS THAT RECAPITULATE GENETIC DISRUPTIONS IN AS, DUP15Q, PTHS, AND RTT, AND ALLOW PRECISE MONITORING AND MANIPULATION OF NETWORK FUNCTION ALONGSIDE THE HIGH-RESOLUTION QUANTIFICATION OF MOTOR CONTROL. I WILL STUDY THE REACH-TO-GRASP ACTION, AN ETHOLOGICALLY-RELEVANT, EVOLUTIONARILY- CONSERVED ACTION THAT HAS BEEN EXTENSIVELY STUDIED IN BOTH HUMANS AND RODENTS, PROVIDING A RARE CROSS-SPECIES FRAMEWORK TO STUDY MOTOR CONTROL IN THE MAMMALIAN BRAIN. DURING THE MENTORED PHASE OF THIS AWARD (AIM 1), I WILL TEST HOW UBE3A MISREGULATION ALTERS NETWORK FUNCTION TO CAUSE MOTOR DEFICITS IN AS AND DUP15Q. THIS PHASE WILL LEVERAGE MY MENTORSHIP TEAM’S PRECLINICAL AND CLINICAL EXPERTISE WITH THESE CONDITIONS, PROVIDING THE MULTIDISCIPLINARY TRAINING REQUIRED TO LAUNCH AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM IN TWO UNDEREXPLORED AREAS. FIRST (AIM 2), I WILL DETERMINE HOW SLEEP DISRUPTIONS IMPACT NETWORK FUNCTION IN AS AND DUP15Q. SLEEP IS A POWERFUL REGULATOR OF NETWORK PLASTICITY AND IS DISRUPTED IN MANY MNDDS, INCLUDING AS AND DUP15Q. I WILL TEST WHETHER SLEEP DISRUPTION DRIVES NETWORK DYSFUNCTION, RATHER THAN MERELY REFLECTING IT. SECOND (AIM 3), I WILL TEST CROSS-CONDITION CONVERGENCE AND DIVERGENCE OF NETWORK DYSFUNCTION IN THREE GENETICALLY DISTINCT MNDDS WITH OVERLAPPING CLINICAL FEATURES – AS, PTHS, AND RTT. THESE CONDITIONS ARE FREQUENTLY MISDIAGNOSED DUE TO THEIR SIMILAR PRESENTATIONS, SUGGESTING SHARED NEURAL FEATURES, YET CROSS-CONDITION STUDIES ARE RARE. UNDERSTANDING WHETHER BEHAVIOR IMPAIRMENTS ARISE FROM DISTINCT OR COMMON NEURAL DYSFUNCTION WOULD INFORM INDIVIDUALLY TAILORED OR CROSS-CONDITION THERAPIES. THIS K99/R00 WILL PROVIDE THE NECESSARY TRAINING AND SUPPORT TO LAUNCH AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM AND ADVANCE TOWARD MY LONG-TERM MISSION OF DEVELOPING BETTER METHODS TO REWIRE THE BRAIN TO IMPROVE THE WELL-BEING OF INDIVIDUALS WITH NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNDERSTANDING THE CONTRIBUTION OF EYE MOVEMENTS TO SUCCESSFUL SPATIAL NAVIGATION IN RODENTS - PROJECT SUMMARY NAVIGATION IS FUNDAMENTAL FOR SURVIVAL, ENABLING ANIMALS TO MAINTAIN SPATIAL AWARENESS AND ORIENT TOWARD GOALS. A STABLE SENSE OF DIRECTIONAL HEADING DEPENDS ON INTEGRATING VESTIBULAR, PROPRIOCEPTIVE, AND VISUAL CUES, COMPUTATIONS CARRIED OUT BY THE HEAD DIRECTION (HD) NETWORK. IN RODENTS, THIS NETWORK RELIES HEAVILY ON VESTIBULAR SIGNALS—PARTICULARLY ANGULAR HEAD VELOCITY INPUTS FROM THE VESTIBULAR NUCLEI—TO UPDATE HD CELL ACTIVITY. HOWEVER, DESPITE EXTENSIVE WORK ON VESTIBULAR CONTRIBUTIONS, THE INFLUENCE OF EYE MOVEMENTS ON DIRECTIONAL ENCODING HAS BEEN LARGELY OVERLOOKED. HISTORICALLY, MOUSE EYE MOVEMENTS WERE THOUGHT TO BE PURELY REFLEXIVE, A VIEW THAT HAS CONSTRAINED INTERPRETATIONS OF HOW GAZE (THE COMBINED MOTION OF THE EYES AND HEAD) CONTRIBUTES TO NAVIGATION. MY RECENT FINDINGS CHALLENGE THIS VIEW BY SHOWING THAT MICE ACTIVELY GENERATE RAPID, SACCADE-LIKE EYE MOVEMENTS THAT ARE TIGHTLY COUPLED TO HEAD MOTION. THIS DISCOVERY REFRAMES GAZE AS AN ACTIVE COMPONENT OF SPATIAL ORIENTATION AND RAISES A FUNDAMENTAL QUESTION: HOW DO EYE MOVEMENT SIGNALS INTERACT WITH VESTIBULAR INPUTS TO MAINTAIN STABLE DIRECTIONAL REPRESENTATIONS, AND DOES DISRUPTION OF THIS INTERACTION LEAD TO SPATIAL DISORIENTATION IN DISEASE? IN THE MENTORED K99 PHASE, I WILL COMBINE NATURALISTIC BEHAVIORAL PARADIGMS WITH HIGH-DENSITY NEUROPIXELS 3.0 RECORDINGS TO IDENTIFY WHERE IN THE ASCENDING HD PATHWAY EYE MOVEMENT SIGNALS CONVERGE WITH VESTIBULAR INPUTS AND EXPLORE THE ROLE OF SACCADES IN UPDATING HEADING. THESE STUDIES WILL ESTABLISH THE FIRST CIRCUIT-LEVEL FRAMEWORK FOR HOW GAZE CONTRIBUTES TO DIRECTIONAL CODING IN RODENTS. IN THE INDEPENDENT R00 PHASE, I WILL EXTEND THIS FRAMEWORK TO A TRANSGENIC ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) MODEL. SPATIAL DISORIENTATION AND GAZE INSTABILITY ARE AMONG THE EARLIEST SYMPTOMS IN AD, YET THE UNDERLYING CIRCUIT MECHANISMS REMAIN UNKNOWN. BY LINKING BREAKDOWNS IN GAZE STABILIZATION TO DYSFUNCTION WITHIN SUBCORTICAL SENSORY-MOTOR CIRCUITS, THIS WORK WILL GENERATE QUANTITATIVE NEURAL AND BEHAVIORAL MEASURES THAT CAN SERVE AS CANDIDATE BIOMARKERS OF EARLY VISUO-VESTIBULAR DECLINE. THIS PROJECT IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT FILLS A LONG-STANDING GAP IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF RODENT EYE MOVEMENTS AND THEIR ROLE IN NAVIGATION. IT IS INNOVATIVE IN RECONCEPTUALIZING EYE MOVEMENTS AS ACTIVE CONTRIBUTORS TO HEADING COMPUTATION AND IN APPLYING NEXT-GENERATION RECORDING TECHNOLOGY DURING NATURAL BEHAVIOR. IT IS IMPACTFUL IN BRIDGING FUNDAMENTAL SYSTEMS NEUROSCIENCE WITH TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE, OFFERING NEW MECHANISTIC INSIGHT INTO HOW GAZE CONTROL AND SPATIAL NAVIGATION ARE DISRUPTED IN A NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE CONTEXT.
