description: HOST-PATHOGEN INTERACTIONS IN MELIOIDOSIS - PROJECT SUMMARY - OVERALL BURKHOLDERIA PSEUDOMALLEI (BPM), THE CAUSATIVE AGENT OF MELIOIDOSIS, IS AN ENVIRONMENTAL PATHOGEN WITH GROWING IMPORTANCE TO GLOBAL AND U.S. PUBLIC HEALTH. ENDEMIC IN SOUTHEAST ASIA AND NORTHERN AUSTRALIA, BPM HAS ALSO BEEN IDENTIFIED IN THE CONTINENTAL UNITED STATES, THE CARIBBEAN, AND CENTRAL AND SOUTH AMERICA, INCREASING THE RISK OF DOMESTIC EXPOSURE THROUGH ENVIRONMENTAL EMERGENCE, INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL, AND GLOBAL COMMERCE. AN ESTIMATED 165,000 PEOPLE DEVELOP MELIOIDOSIS ANNUALLY, RESULTING IN APPROXIMATELY 89,000 DEATHS WORLDWIDE. BPM CAUSES DIVERSE CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS, EXHIBITS INTRINSIC RESISTANCE TO MULTIPLE ANTIBIOTICS, AND IS ASSOCIATED WITH RECURRENT INFECTION. INHALATION IS THE MOST EFFICIENT ROUTE OF INFECTION, WITH PULMONARY DISEASE FREQUENTLY PROGRESSING TO SEPTICEMIA AND DEATH, PARTICULARLY FOLLOWING INFECTION WITH HIGHLY VIRULENT STRAINS. THIS PROJECT WILL DEFINE THE MECHANISMS RESPONSIBLE FOR PULMONARY MELIOIDOSIS BY IDENTIFYING BACTERIAL VIRULENCE DETERMINANTS REQUIRED FOR LUNG INFECTION, DISSEMINATION, AND IMMUNE MODULATION, WHILE CHARACTERIZING HOST IMMUNE PATHWAYS ASSOCIATED WITH DISEASE SEVERITY AND OUTCOMES. STUDIES CONDUCTED IN ENDEMIC REGIONS PROVIDE ESSENTIAL ACCESS TO CLINICALLY RELEVANT ISOLATES, WELL-CHARACTERIZED PATIENT COHORTS, AND PATHOGEN DIVERSITY UNAVAILABLE ELSEWHERE, ENABLING RIGOROUS INVESTIGATION OF NATURALLY OCCURRING DISEASE. HAVING ACCESS TO THE GENOMIC ANALYSIS OF OVER 1,300 BPM ISOLATES WILL HIGHLIGHT THE ROLE OF LINEAGE-SPECIFIC GENES IN DISEASE PROGRESSION AND MORTALITY. INTEGRATING BACTERIAL PATHOGENESIS, IMMUNOLOGY, GENOMICS, AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH WILL IDENTIFY THERAPEUTIC TARGETS, INFORM DIAGNOSTICS AND VACCINES, AND STRENGTHEN U.S. PREPAREDNESS AGAINST THIS HIGH-CONSEQUENCE PATHOGEN BY ADVANCING EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES TO PREVENT SEVERE DISEASE AND REDUCE MORTALITY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MULTIMODAL MICROBE-MEDIATED THERAPIES FOR SYNERGISTIC TREATMENT OF TRIPLE NEGATIVE BREAST CANCER - SUMMARY – OVERALL THE GOAL OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO DEVELOP MICROBIAL THERAPIES THAT GENERATE DURABLE ANTITUMOR RESPONSES. MOST BREAST CANCER SUBTYPES, PARTICULARLY TRIPLE NEGATIVE BREAST CANCER (TNBC), RESPOND POORLY TO IMMUNE CHECKPOINT INHIBITORS (ICI), WHICH MAKES DEVELOPING TREATMENTS FOR ICI-RESISTANT TUMORS A CRITICAL UNMET MEDICAL NEED. OUR PROGRAM WILL ENGINEER MICROBIAL THERAPIES THAT RELEASE THERAPEUTICS INTO CANCER CELLS, DELIVER ONCOLYTIC VIRUSES, AND TARGET RADIATION PRECISELY TO TUMORS. UNDERSTANDING THE BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS THAT CONTROL HOW THESE THERAPIES INTERACT WITH TUMOR TISSUE AND THE IMMUNE SYSTEM IS ESSENTIAL FOR THEIR CLINICAL TRANSLATION. THE PROGRAM WAS DESIGNED TO INTEGRATE COMPLEMENTARY EXPERTISE IN TUMOR BIOLOGY, DRUG DELIVERY, IMMUNE ONCOLOGY, SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY, AND RADIOLOGY ACROSS UMASS AMHERST AND WEILL CORNELL MEDICINE. IT HAS THREE MAIN AIMS: (AIM 1) DEVELOP MICROBIAL THERAPIES TO TREAT ICI-RESISTANT TNBC; (AIM 2) DETERMINE THE BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF MICROBIAL IMMUNE INDUCTION; AND (AIM 3) DEVELOP A SUITE OF CLINICALLY RELEVANT MULTIMODAL BACTERIAL THERAPIES. THROUGH THESE AIMS, THE PROPOSED PROGRAM PROJECT WILL CREATE VERSATILE TREATMENTS TO OVERCOME ICI RESISTANCE IN TNBC AND ADDRESS KEY BARRIERS TO THE CLINICAL ADOPTION OF MICROBIAL THERAPIES. THE PROGRAM HAS THREE PROJECTS, EACH DESIGNED TO ADDRESS DISTINCT MECHANISMS OF IMMUNE RESISTANCE IN BREAST CANCER: PROJECT 1 AIMS TO OVERCOME IMMUNE SUPPRESSION BY INTRACELLULAR DELIVERY OF THE SARS-COV-2 SPIKE ANTIGEN AND CRISPR-CONTROLLED SALMONELLA EFFECTORS; PROJECT 2 TARGETS TUMOR HETEROGENEITY BY DELIVERING ONCOLYTIC VIRUSES; AND PROJECT 3 FOCUSES ON DEVELOPING A THERANOSTIC APPROACH FOR TNBC USING BACTERIA-TARGETED RADIOHAPTENS. THESE PROJECTS ARE SUPPORTED BY TWO SHARED RESOURCE CORES: CORE 1 WILL DEVELOP SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY TOOLS FOR VECTOR CONSTRUCTION AND STRAIN OPTIMIZATION; AND CORE 2 WILL PROVIDE IMMUNOLOGICAL ANALYSIS TOOLS AND CLINICALLY RELEVANT ANIMAL MODELS. ANIMAL MODELS ARE NECESSARY BECAUSE THE COMPLEX INTERACTIONS AMONG LIVE BACTERIAL VECTORS, TUMOR TISSUE, AND THE IMMUNE SYSTEM CANNOT BE RECAPITULATED IN VITRO. IMMUNOCOMPETENT TNBC MOUSE MODELS PROVIDE THE PHYSIOLOGICAL COMPLEXITY NEEDED TO EVALUATE SAFETY AND ANTITUMOR EFFICACY PRIOR TO CLINICAL TRANSLATION. THE PROJECTS EACH GENERATE A DISTINCT THERAPEUTIC MODALITY AND ARE SYNERGISTICALLY INTEGRATED TO CREATE MULTIMODAL BACTERIAL THERAPIES THAT TARGET MULTIPLE IMMUNE RESISTANCE PATHWAYS. THE FOUNDATIONS OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH ARE WELL ESTABLISHED. IN PRELIMINARY STUDIES, WE HAVE (1) DEVELOPED A STRAIN OF SALMONELLA CAPABLE OF DELIVERING PROTEINS INTO CANCER CELLS; (2) ENGINEERED SALMONELLA TO DELIVER ONCOLYTIC VIRUSES INTO CANCER CELLS AND BIND RADIOTHERAPEUTIC AGENTS; (3) DEMONSTRATED THAT INTRACELLULAR DELIVERY OF EXOGENOUS ANTIGENS CAN CLEAR IMMUNOLOGICALLY COLD TUMORS AND ESTABLISH DURABLE ANTICANCER IMMUNITY. MICROBIAL THERAPY COULD BENEFIT A BROAD RANGE OF BREAST CANCER PATIENTS, PARTICULARLY THOSE WITH TNBC AND IN RURAL COMMUNITIES WITH ICI-RESISTANT, IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE CANCER TYPES. IF SUCCESSFUL, THIS RESEARCH WILL YIELD POTENT, SAFE, AND ‘OFF-THE-SHELF’ MICROBIAL THERAPIES THAT REQUIRE NO PATIENT-SPECIFIC CUSTOMIZATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: WILDFIRE EXPOSURE: CARDIOVASCULAR AND AIRWAY INFLAMMATION RESEARCH (WE-CAIR) - OVERALL SUMMARY WILDFIRE SMOKE EXPOSURE IS NOW RECOGNIZED AS A MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR TO CARDIOVASCULAR AND COPD EXACERBATIONS. HOWEVER, THE LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCES, CELLULAR-MOLECULAR MECHANISMS, RISK FACTORS, AND BIOMARKERS OF DISEASE SEVERITY REMAIN UNKNOWN. THROUGH THE “WILDFIRE EXPOSURE – CARDIOVASCULAR AND AIRWAY INFLAMMATION RESEARCH (WE-CAIR)” PROGRAM OUR INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM WITH LONG-STANDING COLLABORATIVE RELATIONSHIPS AIMS TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES IN HEALTHY VOLUNTEERS AND COPD PATIENTS AS WELL AS IN MOUSE MODELS SUGGEST A ROLE FOR GROUP 2 INNATE LYMPHOID CELLS (ILC2) IN WILDFIRE SMOKE-INDUCED INFLAMMATION. INVESTIGATIONS INTO THE ARYL HYDROCARBON RECEPTOR (AHR) AND THE EPIGENETIC REGULATORY ENZYME TEN-ELEVEN TRANSLOCATION METHYLCYTOSINE DIOXYGENASE 1 (TET1) REVEALED POTENTIAL EPIGENETIC AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL MODIFICATIONS OF AIRWAY INFLAMMATION. PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS SIGNIFICANTLY CONTRIBUTES TO GLUCOCORTICOID RESISTANCE AND WORSENING OF CARDIOVASCULAR AND AIRWAY DISEASE POTENTIALLY THROUGH CONVERGENT EPIGENETIC PATHWAYS. WE POSTULATE THAT WILDFIRE SMOKE EXPOSURE COUPLED WITH PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS INDUCES NON-CANONICAL IL-17 EXPRESSION IN ILC2 BY ALTERING THE AHR/TET1/2 AXIS THROUGH EPIGENETIC AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATION THAT ACCELERATES LUNG FUNCTION DECLINE IN COPD AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. GOAL I: TO UNDERSTAND HOW NON- CANONICAL IL-17 PRODUCTION IN ILC2 VIA THE IMPAIRED AHR/TET1 AXIS MEDIATES THE EFFECTS OF WILDFIRE SMOKE AND PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS ON INFLAMMATORY CARDIOVASCULAR AND AIRWAY DISEASE. WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF ILC2 (PROJECT 1), AHR (PROJECT 2), TET1 (PROJECT 3), AND STRESS (PROJECT 4) IN MOUSE MODELS OF SIMULATED WILDFIRE SMOKE EXPOSURE (CORE C) AND HUMAN COPD AND HEALTHY SUBJECTS WITH A HISTORY OF HIGH OR LOW LEVELS OF WILDFIRE SMOKE EXPOSURE (CORE D). GOAL II: ELUCIDATE THE ROLE AND EXTENT OF EPIGENETIC REGULATION OF THE WILDFIRE SMOKE EFFECTS. EPIGENETIC MEMORY AND AHR/TET1/2 CROSS-REGULATION OF THE IL17A PROMOTER PLASTICITY AND OTHER NOVEL CANDIDATE MECHANISMS MEDIATING WILDFIRE SMOKE EXPOSURE AND STRESS EFFECTS WILL BE STUDIED IN HUMAN PERIPHERAL BLOOD, NASAL EPITHELIUM AND SPUTUM AND BLOOD, NASAL CELLS AND LUNG TISSUE FROM MOUSE MODELS (CORE B, PROJECT 3). GOAL III: DETERMINE THE POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC AND PREDICTIVE SIGNIFICANCE OF IL-17+ILC2 AND OTHER CANDIDATE (EPIGENETIC, MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, AND BEHAVIORAL) SIGNATURES IN WILDFIRE-SMOKE INDUCED SEVERITY, AND LONG-TERM EFFECTS ON COPD. INNOVATIVE SYSTEMS LEVEL INTEGRATION AND MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES (CORE A, CORE B) WILL ANALYZE THE CLINICAL, BEHAVIORAL, EXPOSURE, AND BIOSPECIMEN-DERIVED EPIGENETIC, CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR DATA DERIVED FROM CORES C, D AND PROJECTS 1-4. THE WE-CAIR PROGRAM'S STRENGTH LIES IN ITS NOVEL HYPOTHESIS, INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACH, CENTRALIZED EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN AND DATA PROCESSING ACROSS ALL PROJECTS SUPPORTED BY CUTTING EDGE EPIGENETICS, ENGINEERING AND BIOINFORMATICS TECHNOLOGY. BY FOSTERING COLLABORATION AMONG INTERDISCIPLINARY COLLEAGUES AND SUPPORTING EMERGING SCIENTIFIC LEADERS, THE PROGRAM WILL DRIVE INNOVATION AND ADVANCE RESEARCH IN THE FIELDS OF PULMONARY, CARDIOVASCULAR, AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TARGETING HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS BY LIPID NANOPARTICLES TO TREAT HEMATOLOGICAL DISORDERS - PROJECT ABSTRACT – OVERALL THIS PROGRAM PROJECT GRANT (PPG) AIMS TO DEVELOP SAFE, EFFECTIVE, AND SCALABLE CURATIVE THERAPIES FOR HEMOGLOBINOPATHIES (INCLUDING SICKLE CELL DISEASE (SCD), A-THALASSEMIA (AT), AND B-THALASSEMIA (BT)) AND FANCONI ANEMIA (FA) BY TARGETING HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS (HSC) IN VIVO. WHILE HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANTATION (HSCT) CAN BE CURATIVE, THE TOXICITIES ASSOCIATED WITH CURRENT CONDITIONING REGIMENS LIMIT ELIGIBILITY AND THREATEN FERTILITY AND LONG-TERM HEALTH. THE HEAVY STRAIN PLACED ON PATIENTS, FAMILIES, AND HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS, SPANNING INPATIENT CARE, EMERGENCY SERVICES, TRANSFUSIONS, AND LONG-TERM COMPLICATION MANAGEMENT, HIGHLIGHTS THE PRESSING NEED FOR INNOVATIVE, SAFER, AND MORE WIDELY ACCESSIBLE CURATIVE TREATMENTS. OUR COMPREHENSIVE AND INTEGRATED RESEARCH STRATEGY BRINGS TOGETHER CUTTING-EDGE TECHNOLOGIES AND INNOVATIVE METHODOLOGIES TO ADDRESS HSC DISORDERS. SPECIFICALLY, WE EMPLOY ANTIBODY-DIRECTED, HSC-TARGETED LIPID NANOPARTICLES (LNP) DESIGNED TO DELIVER MRNA-ENCODED PRO-APOPTOTIC (PA) PAYLOADS OR GENE EDITORS DIRECTLY TO DISEASED STEM CELLS. THIS PRECISE DELIVERY SYSTEM IS COUPLED WITH ADVANCED DISEASE MODELING PLATFORMS, INCLUDING HUMANIZED MOUSE MODELS AND PRECLINICAL LARGE ANIMAL SYSTEMS SUCH AS SHEEP AND NON-HUMAN PRIMATES, TO RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE BOTH SAFETY AND EFFICACY. THE ULTIMATE GOAL IS TO ACHIEVE EITHER THE SELECTIVE DEPLETION OF DISEASED POPULATIONS OR DURABLE GENETIC CORRECTION OF FAULTY HSC, PAVING THE WAY FOR TRANSFORMATIVE THERAPIES. SUPPORTING THIS APPROACH ARE THREE INTERCONNECTED RESEARCH PROJECTS, WHICH ARE REINFORCED BY TWO SPECIALIZED SCIENTIFIC CORES AND A CENTRAL ADMINISTRATIVE CORE. TOGETHER, THESE COMPONENTS ENSURE SCIENTIFIC RIGOR, FOSTER COLLABORATION AND SYNERGY ACROSS TEAMS, AND ENABLE RAPID ITERATIVE CYCLES OF DISCOVERY, REFINEMENT, AND TRANSLATION TOWARD CLINICAL APPLICATION. PROJECT 1 IMPROVES FERTILITY-PRESERVING CONDITIONING THROUGH TARGETED HSC DEPLETION AND DEVELOPS IN VIVO GENE EDITING FOR HEMOGLOBINOPATHIES. PROJECT 2 EXPLORES INTERHOMOLOG RECOMBINATION FOR ALLELE REPAIR AND NON-TOXIC IN VIVO SELECTION IN FA. PROJECT 3 FOCUSES ON PRENATAL LNP-MEDIATED BASE EDITING OF FETAL HSC TO INTERVENE BEFORE DISEASE BEGINS. CORE B (OPTIMIZED NUCLEIC ACID AND CELL-SPECIFIC DELIVERY) DESIGNS AND PRODUCES HSC-TARGETED LNP AND CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVES FORMULATIONS BASED ON PROJECT FEEDBACK. CORE C (GENE EDITING, IPSC, AND HSC) SUPPLIES EDITING PLATFORMS, IPSC-DERIVED HSPCS, AND HUMANIZED XENOGRAFT MODELS; CORE A (ADMINISTRATIVE) MANAGES GOVERNANCE, COMPLIANCE, DATA SHARING, AND EVALUATION. INNOVATION INVOLVES IN SITU HSC EDITING AND CONDITIONING USING ANTIBODY-FUNCTIONALIZED LNP, PRENATAL DELIVERY TO THE FETAL LIVER HSC NICHE, AND CAREFUL MEASUREMENT OF ON- AND OFF-TARGET EFFECTS ACROSS SPECIES. ANTICIPATED OUTCOMES INCLUDE FERTILITY-PRESERVING TRANSPLANT CONDITIONING, EFFECTIVE IN VIVO CORRECTION OF DISEASE ALLELES, AND ROBUST PRECLINICAL EVIDENCE TO MITIGATE RISKS IN TRANSLATION. BY REDUCING TOXICITY, SIMPLIFYING PROCEDURES, AND ENABLING EARLIER INTERVENTION, THIS PROGRAM AIMS TO EXPAND ACCESS TO CURATIVE THERAPIES AND LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR FIRST-IN-HUMAN STUDIES.

description: KANSAS SUCCESSFUL AGING AND RESILIENCE COBRE (K-SARC) - MODIFIED PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SECTION - KANSAS SUCCESSFUL AGING AND RESILIENCE COBRE (K-SARC) OVERALL  THIS PROPOSAL WILL ESTABLISH THE KANSAS SUCCESSFUL AGING AND RESILIENCE COBRE (K-SARC) TO UNIFY INVESTIGATORS FROM MULTIPLE DEPARTMENTS AND RESEARCH CENTERS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF KANSAS MEDICAL CENTER (KUMC), AND TO ENHANCE GEROSCIENCE RESEARCH OF SUCCESSFUL AGING AND RESILIENCE.  GEROSCIENCE IS AT THE INTERSECTION OF THE BIOLOGIC MECHANISMS OF AGING, CHRONIC DISEASE, FRAILTY, AND RESILIENCE.  RESILIENCE IS THE CAPACITY TO RECOVER FROM STRESS-INDUCED CHALLENGE AT THE MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, ORGAN, AND ORGANISMAL LEVELS.  REDUCED RESILIENCE OFTEN PRECEDES FRAILTY, WHICH INCREASES THE RISK OF ADVERSE OUTCOMES INCLUDING FALLS, HOSPITALIZATION, AND EXCESS MORTALITY AND IS LIKELY THE CRITICAL DETERMINANT OF FUNCTIONAL CAPACITY, HEALTHSPAN, AND QUALITY OF LIFE DURING AGING.  IN THE UNITED STATES, FRAILTY AFFECTS 20% OF ADULTS 70 – 79 YEARS OLD AND 50% OF ADULTS 85 YEARS AND OLDER.  IT IS UNKNOWN WHY SOME OLDER ADULTS HAVE HIGH RESILIENCE TO AND “BOUNCE BACK” FROM SUBSTANTIAL CHALLENGES, WHILE OTHERS DO NOT.  THE K SARC WILL: (1) FUND AND MENTOR EARLY-STAGE GEROSCIENCE INVESTIGATORS WHO STUDY SUCCESSFUL AGING AND RESILIENCE TO ESTABLISH THEIR INDEPENDENT RESEARCH CAREERS, (2) ESTABLISH SCIENTIFIC CORES TO FACILITATE TRANSLATIONAL RESILIENCE RESEARCH BY EARLY STAGE AND ESTABLISHED INVESTIGATORS, (3) CREATE A SHARED INTELLECTUAL HOME FOR GEROSCIENCE RESEARCHERS THROUGH AN EDUCATIONAL AND SEMINAR PROGRAM, AND (4) PARTNER WITH DEPARTMENTS TO JOINTLY RECRUIT NEW INVESTIGATORS TO KUMC WHO ARE FOCUSED ON K SARC THEMES.  THIS WILL ALLOW KUMC TO LEAD AND COORDINATE RESEARCH ON SUCCESSFUL AGING AND RESILIENCE, INCENTIVIZE FUTURE RESOURCES AND RECRUITMENT, AND FORM INTERDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATIONS IN GEROSCIENCE. THESE EFFORTS CAN ONLY BE SUCCESSFUL WITH COBRE FUNDING.  THE K SARC WILL BE LED BY DR. BRUCE TROEN, AN ACCOMPLISHED ACADEMIC GERIATRICIAN-GEROSCIENTIST, AND DR. RUSSELL SWERDLOW, AN INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNIZED NEUROLOGIST-INVESTIGATOR.  THEY HAVE MULTI-DISCIPLINARY AND COMPLEMENTARY EXPERTISE IN BASIC, CLINICAL, AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH.  THE K SARC WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF FOUR RESEARCH PROJECT LEADERS (RPLS) TO CONDUCT ANIMAL AND HUMAN STUDIES ON RESILIENCE IN AGING, CHRONIC PAIN, EXERCISE, AND CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE.  IT WILL ADMINISTER A PILOT PROJECT PROGRAM TO DEVELOP FUTURE K SARC RESEARCHERS.  THE K SARC WILL ESTABLISH TWO NEW SCIENTIFIC CORES THAT PROVIDE A FOUNDATION FOR TRANSLATIONAL RESILIENCE RESEARCH CAPABILITIES (K-PARC: PHENOTYPIC AGING RESILIENCE CORE AND K MARC: MOLECULAR AGING RESILIENCE CORE).  THE CORES WILL SUPPORT INFRASTRUCTURE AND METHODOLOGIES FOR THE RPLS, THE PILOT PROJECT RECIPIENTS, AND AN INCREASING CADRE OF GEROSCIENCE RESEARCHERS ON CAMPUS.  A CRITICAL GOAL OF THE K SARC WILL BE TO HELP RPLS DEVELOP INDEPENDENT R01-FUNDED RESEARCH PROGRAMS.  OVERALL, THE K-SARC WILL DEVELOP A TRANSLATIONAL AND INTER-DISCIPLINARY GEROSCIENCE RESEARCH PROGRAM THAT WILL HAVE A SIGNIFICANT FUTURE IMPACT BY PROMOTING SUCCESSFUL AGING AND RESILIENCE DURING AGING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: POLYSUBSTANCE ADDICTION RESEARCH CENTER - ABSTRACT OVERALL SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUDS) REMAIN A MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH CRISIS, DRIVEN INCREASINGLY BY POLYSUBSTANCE USE. DESPITE DECADES OF RESEARCH, WE STILL LACK AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK THAT EXPLAINS HOW GENETIC, CELLULAR, AND PHYSIOLOGICAL VULNERABILITIES CONVERGE TO PROMOTE COMPULSIVE DRUG USE, ABSTINENCE, AND RELAPSE. MOST STUDIES ISOLATE SINGLE DRUGS, NARROW BEHAVIORAL PHENOTYPES, OR INDIVIDUAL BIOLOGICAL LEVELS, PRODUCING FRAGMENTED RESULTS THAT LIMIT PREDICTIVE POWER AND THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT. THE POLYSUBSTANCE ADDICTION RESEARCH CENTER (PARC) DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THIS GAP BY UNITING BEHAVIORAL, MOLECULAR, CIRCUIT, AND IMMUNOMETABOLIC DATA WITHIN THE SAME GENETICALLY DIVERSE HETEROGENEOUS STOCK (HS) RATS AND ALIGNING THESE FINDINGS WITH HUMAN OMICS AND IMAGING DATASETS WITH THREE RESEARCH POJECTS: BRAIN CONNECTOMIC, BRAIN TRANSCRIPTOMIC, AND GUT-VAGUS MULTIOMIC. THIS DESIGN ENABLES SYSTEMATIC COMPARISONS ACROSS DRUGS (COCAINE, OXYCODONE, ALCOHOL, AND THEIR CO-USE), ACROSS SPECIES (HS RATS VERSUS HUMAN SUD/AUD COHORTS AND HEALTHY CONTROLS), AND ACROSS THE SEVERITY SPECTRUM OF ADDICTION-LIKE BEHAVIORS. ALL DATA CONVERGE IN THE ONE-INDIVIDUAL MULTISCALE ATLAS, A CENTER-WIDE MANDATE THAT HARMONIZES MULTIMODAL DATASETS INTO A REUSABLE TRANSLATIONAL RESOURCE. SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL IDENTIFY MULTILEVEL BIOMARKERS OF ADDICTION-LIKE BEHAVIORS BY QUANTIFYING BEHAVIORAL, NEURAL, MOLECULAR, AND IMMUNOMETABOLIC SIGNATURES ACROSS SEX, DRUGS, AND SEVERITY OF ADDICTION-LIKE BEHAVIORS. ADVANCED AI/ML APPROACHES WILL INTEGRATE THESE DATA INTO INTERPRETABLE PROFILES OF VULNERABILITY AND RESILIENCE, SPANNING GENES TO BEHAVIOR. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL REVEAL AND VALIDATE DRUGGABLE TARGETS. CANDIDATE TARGETS, INCLUDING OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION STRESS PATHWAYS, CHOLINERGIC AND IMMUNE SIGNALING PATHWAYS, WILL BE TESTED USING PHARMACOLOGICAL AND VIRAL APPROACHES AND TRANSLATIONALLY-RELEVANT MODELS OF RELAPSE. SPECIFIC AIM 3 WILL ACCELERATE DISCOVERY BY DEPLOYING AN INTEGRATED CENTER PLATFORM. THIS INCLUDES EXPANDING THE ADDICTION BIOBANK, CREATING CLOUD-BASED PIPELINES FOR DATA SHARING AND ANALYSIS, PROVIDING PILOT FUNDING FOR INNOVATIVE PROJECTS, AND TRAINING THE NEXT GENERATION OF SCIENTISTS IN MULTISCALE ADDICTION RESEARCH. ALL PROJECTS SHARE HARMONIZED LONGITUDINAL COHORTS, EXPERIMENTAL DESIGNS, AND TIME POINTS, ENSURING CROSS-VALIDATION AND IMMEDIATE BIDIRECTIONAL FEEDBACK. INTEGRATION IS FURTHER SUPPORTED BY FOUR CORES: BEHAVIORAL PHENOTYPING, BIOBANK, COMPUTATIONAL & ANALYTICAL, AND PILOT PROJECTS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE A VALIDATED BIOMARKER PANEL FOR DIAGNOSIS AND STRATIFICATION, EXPERIMENTALLY CONFIRMED THERAPEUTIC TARGETS, PUBLICLY AVAILABLE DATASETS AND BIOSPECIMENS, AND A TRAINED WORKFORCE FLUENT IN INTEGRATIVE ADDICTION SCIENCE. TOGETHER, PARC WILL TRANSFORM ADDICTION RESEARCH FROM SILOED OBSERVATIONS INTO A PREDICTIVE, MECHANISTIC, AND TRANSLATIONAL ENTERPRISE.

description: GREAT PLAINS IDEA-CTR - PROJECT SUMMARY – OVERALL THE GREAT PLAINS IDEA CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH NETWORK (GP IDEA-CTR-N) ADVANCES THE PAR- 23-241–ALIGNED INFRASTRUCTURE UNITING RURAL AND URBAN PARTNERS TO ACCELERATE DISCOVERY AND IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES ACROSS A REGION WHERE GEOGRAPHIC AND ACCESS BARRIERS LIMIT CARE. ESTABLISHED IN 2016 AND LED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF NEBRASKA MEDICAL CENTER (UNMC) WITH PARTNERS ACROSS NEBRASKA AND NEIGHBORING IDEA STATES, THE NETWORK HAS BUILT ENDURING CAPACITY IN GOVERNANCE, INFRASTRUCTURE, WORKFORCE, AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT. OVER THE PAST CYCLE, GP IDEA-CTR-N BECAME A REGIONAL HUB FOR TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH, LAUNCHING 200+ PILOT PROJECTS, MENTORING 70+ EARLY-CAREER INVESTIGATORS, AND SECURING MAJOR NIH AND FEDERAL AWARDS. COLLABORATIONS WITH NATIONAL CTRS, CTSAS, AND NIH ADVANCED BEST PRACTICES, TEAM SCIENCE, AND COMPETITIVENESS. THIS RENEWAL TRANSITIONS THE PROGRAM FROM A U54 TO A P50 FUNDING MECHANISM, REFLECTING MATURITY, SUSTAIN- ABILITY, AND NATIONAL LEADERSHIP READINESS. SPECIFIC AIMS ARE: 1) EXPAND A COHESIVE, MULTIDISCIPLINARY NETWORK OF ACADEMIC, CLINICAL, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS; 2) STRENGTHEN THE CTR WORKFORCE; 3) SUPPORT COMMUNITY-DRIVEN RESEARCH ON REGIONAL HEALTH PRIORITIES; AND 4) BUILD AN INTEROPERABLE DATA INFRASTRUCTURE TO ACCELERATE DISCOVERY. THESE AIMS ARE GUIDED BY NIGMS, PARTNER INSTITUTIONS, ADVISORY BODIES, AND A COMMUNITY ADVISORY BOARD. THE P50 TRANSITION STRENGTHENS IMPACT BY CONSOLIDATING BERD AND BIBCE INTO THE RESEARCH DESIGN, COMPLIANCE, AND DATA MANAGEMENT (RDCD) CORE; INTEGRATING TRACKING AND EVALUATION INTO THE ADMINISTRATIVE CORE; AND FORMING THE HEALTH RESEARCH (HR) CORE FROM THE PILOT PROJECTS PROGRAM. OVERSIGHT BY STEERING, EXECUTIVE, AND EXTERNAL ADVISORY COMMITTEES ENSURES PROGRESS AND ACCOUNTABILITY. THE GP IDEA-CTR-N UNITES PARTNERS FROM THE NEBRASKA UNIVERSITY SYSTEM (UNMC, UNO, UNL, UNK), BOYS TOWN NATIONAL RESEARCH HOSPITAL, CREIGHTON UNIVERSITY, CHILDREN’S NEBRASKA, VA NEBRASKA-WESTERN IOWA, AND NEBRASKA MEDICINE, FOSTERING ROBUST UNIVERSITY, HOSPITAL, AND COMMUNITY COLLABORATION. IT ENGAGES IDEA COLLABORATORS ACROSS STATES TO EXTEND ITS REACH AND ENABLE MULTI-INSTITUTIONAL RESEARCH. THE NETWORK POWERS KEY INNOVATIONS, INCLUDING NIH ODSS DATA COUNTS; THE TRIAD INITIATIVE FOR DATA SCIENCE AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE; AND THE TEAM SCIENCE MENTORING COMMITTEE, WHICH DEVELOPS LEADERSHIP PATHWAYS ACROSS THE CTR WORKFORCE. WITH A 104-SITE PBRN, FHIR-HL7 INTEGRATION, AND SECURE, REUSABLE DATA, THE NETWORK DELIVERS THE REGION’S FIRST COMPREHENSIVE LEARNING HEALTH SYSTEM. THE INTEROPERABLE INFRASTRUCTURE OFFERS SECURE DATA SHARING, RAPID COHORT DISCOVERY, DECENTRALIZED TRIALS, AND EFFICIENT RESEARCH TRANSLATION. THE NETWORK EXPANDS WORKFORCE CAPACITY THROUGH TIERED TRAINING, CAREER DEVELOPMENT, AND DIGITAL HEALTH CURRICULA, WHILE STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS THROUGH CO-DESIGN. STRENGTHENED BY IDEA, CTR-D, AND CTSA COLLABORATIONS, THE GP IDEA-CTR-N ACCELERATES DISCOVERY, IMPROVES CARE, AND SERVES AS A NATIONAL MODEL FOR HEALTH INNOVATION.

description: ADVANCE CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH (ADVANCE-CTR) - ABSTRACT – OVERALL THIS SECOND COMPETITIVE RENEWAL AIMS TO ADVANCE THE RHODE ISLAND (RI) CENTER FOR CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH (ADVANCE RI-CTR) TO THE NEXT LEVEL OF IMPACT AS A NETWORKED CTR (CTR-N). THE OVERALL GOAL OF ADVANCE RI-CTR IS TO ACCELERATE INNOVATIVE RESEARCH TO IMPROVE HEALTH IN RI AND BEYOND. RI IS AN IDEAL “TEST SITE” FOR INNOVATIONS IN BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH BECAUSE IT IS A SMALL STATE IN AREA WITH A SMALL STABLE POPULATION, BUT WITH SIGNIFICANT HEALTH PROBLEMS, INCLUDING CHRONIC DISEASE, BEHAVIORAL/MENTAL HEALTH, AND MATERNAL & CHILD HEALTH AS WELL AS CROSS-CUTTING ISSUES OF SUBSTANCE USE, HEALTHY AGING, AND ACCESSIBILITY AND COST OF HEALTHCARE. UNDER THE LEADERSHIP OF BROWN UNIVERSITY AND ITS INSTITUTIONAL PARTNERS, THE PROPOSED ADVANCEMENT TO A CTR-N STRUCTURE DURING PHASE III WILL ENABLE ADVANCE RI-CTR TO BETTER ADDRESS THESE PERSISTENT HEALTH PRIORITIES. THE VISION FOR PHASE III IS “A FUTURE WHERE INNOVATIVE RESEARCH LEADS TO IMPROVED HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR ALL OF RI’S COMMUNITIES.” TO THIS END, OUR MISSION IS “TO ENHANCE AN ECOSYSTEM OF CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH, SYNERGISTIC COLLABORATION, AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT THAT SUPPORTS THE DEVELOPMENT AND EDUCATION OF THE CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH WORKFORCE, ACCELERATES HEALTH DISCOVERIES, AND TRANSLATES THEM INTO SOLUTIONS THAT ARE RESPONSIVE TO THE HEALTH NEEDS OF ALL RI'S COMMUNITIES.” AS A CTR- N, ADVANCE RI-CTR WILL EXPAND COLLABORATIVE MULTIDISCIPLINARY AND TEAM SCIENCE BY PROVIDING ADDITIONAL INNOVATIVE AWARD INCENTIVES, INCREASE PARTICIPATION IN MULTI-CENTER TRIALS, EXPAND COMMUNITY-BASED RESEARCH INVOLVING OUR ESTABLISHED PRACTICE-BASED RESEARCH NETWORK (PBRN) AND COMMUNITY ADVISORY AND ACTION BOARD (CAAB), AND EXPAND RESEARCH USING “REAL WORLD” DATA FROM ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS AND OTHER SOURCES. ADVANCE RI-CTR WILL PROVIDE CONSULTATIONS AND TRAINING IN ESTABLISHED AND INNOVATIVE RESEARCH METHODOLOGIES, EXPAND AND DEVELOP A RESEARCHER WORKFORCE RANGING FROM CLINICAL FELLOWS TO ESTABLISHED FACULTY, EXPAND THE POOL OF QUALIFIED RESEARCH COORDINATORS, AND PROMOTE DATA SHARING AMONG RESEARCHERS AFFILIATED WITH OUR PARTNER INSTITUTIONS. OUR CONTINUOUS EVALUATION APPROACH WILL KEEP US ABREAST OF THE EXTENT TO WHICH THE RESEARCH WE SUPPORT ALIGNS WITH THE STATE’S HEALTH PRIORITY AREAS AND PROMOTES INNOVATION IN THE CLINIC AND HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS, IMPROVES POPULATION HEALTH, AND BENEFITS RI’S ECONOMY. OUR THEME – “COLLABORATE TO INNOVATE” – WILL BE PROMOTED BY THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: BUILD CAPACITY FOR CTR BY SUPPORTING CONSULTATIONS, TRAINING, AND INFRASTRUCTURE (AIM 1), ENHANCE NETWORKING FOR CTR BY EXPANDING BEYOND OUR CURRENT STATE-WIDE INSTITUTIONAL PARTNERS (AIM 2); AND DEVELOP THE WORKFORCE FOR CTR BY PROMOTING THE CAREER DEVELOPMENT OF RESEARCH FACULTY, CLINICIANS, AND STAFF (AIM 3). BUILDING ON THE IMPACTFUL ACHIEVEMENTS OF PHASES I AND II, THE EXPECTED OUTCOME OF PHASE III IS A SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED CAPACITY FOR CTR THAT IS COLLABORATIVE AND INNOVATIVE, ENHANCING HEALTH WITHIN RI AND BEYOND.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IDENTIFYING THE MECHANISTIC ROLE OF AND REVERSING ABERRANT NEURAL ACTIVITY IN ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS A DEVASTATING DISEASE WITH ENORMOUS UNMET MEDICAL NEED. IT IS LIKELY NECESSARY TO UNDERSTAND, DETECT, AND TREAT ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE EARLIER IN DISEASE DEVELOPMENT. PATIENTS OFTEN EXHIBIT ABERRANT NEURAL ACTIVITY EVEN BEFORE PATHOLOGY OR COGNITIVE DECLINE. AMYLOID-BETA (AB) AND TAU CAN PERTURB NEURAL ACTIVITY, AND ACTIVITY CAN AFFECT THEIR LEVELS, THUS ABERRANT NEURAL ACTIVITY MAY BE BOTH A SYMPTOM AND CAUSE OF AB AND TAU, FORMING A VICIOUS CYCLE. THIS PROJECT WILL INVESTIGATE THE HYPOTHESIS THAT ABERRANT NEURAL ACTIVITY IS A PRIMARY DRIVER OF AND TRACTABLE THERAPEUTIC TARGET FOR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, AND THAT TARGETING IT CAN RESCUE COGNITIVE DEFICITS. THERE IS A LACK OF DIRECT EVIDENCE ON THE CAUSATIVE ROLE OF ABERRANT NEURAL ACTIVITY IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, LET ALONE THE MECHANISMS, A SIGNIFICANT GAP IN OUR UNDERSTANDING. HUMAN IMAGING METHODS HAVE LOW RESOLUTION, AND HUMAN STUDIES CANNOT USE PRECISE PERTURBATIONS TO TEST DIRECT CAUSE AND EFFECT. YET, STIMULATION THERAPIES ARE USED ON PATIENTS, USING LIMITED DATA TO INFORM PROTOCOLS, RESULTING IN PROMISING BUT INCONCLUSIVE RESULTS. THIS PROJECT WILL USE CUTTING-EDGE SYSTEMS NEUROSCIENCE TECHNIQUES TO CONDUCT SINGLE-CELL RESOLUTION EXAMINATION AND PERTURBATION OF THE BRAIN TO DETERMINE THE MECHANISTIC ROLE OF ABERRANT NEURAL ACTIVITY IN COGNITIVE DECLINE IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE MICE, AND TO REVERSE IT. TO IDENTIFY ABERRANT SINGLE-NEURON AND NETWORK DYNAMICS, 2-PHOTON CA2+ IMAGING WILL BE USED IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE MICE DURING COGNITIVE TASKS OVER DISEASE PROGRESSION. THIS WILL BE THE FIRST LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF SINGLE-NEURON ACTIVITY IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE MICE DURING COGNITIVE TASKS, AND THE FIRST LIFELONG STUDY OF NEURAL ACTIVITY. TO DISCOVER ACTIVITY-BASED ANATOMICAL CONNECTIVITY CHANGES, ACTIVITY- DEPENDENT NEURON PROJECTION LABELING WILL BE USED TO LABEL NEURONS ACTIVATED DURING LEARNING AND RECALL. TISSUE- CLEARING WILL ENABLE IMAGING OF PROJECTIONS ACROSS THE ENTIRE BRAIN IN 3D, ALONG WITH AB AND TAU, OVER DISEASE PROGRESSION. THIS WILL DISCOVER SPECIFIC BRAIN REGIONS, CIRCUITS, AND CELLS THAT CHANGE IN PARALLEL TO AB AND TAU AND CORRELATE WITH COGNITION. THESE WILL BE THE FIRST BRAIN-WIDE, ACTIVITY-DEPENDENT PROJECTION TRACING EXPERIMENTS, AND THE FIRST LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF ANATOMICAL CONNECTIVITY CHANGES IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. TO TEST THE FUNCTIONAL ROLE OF ABERRANT ACTIVITY AND TO RESTORE COGNITION, SINGLE-CELL OPTOGENETICS WILL BE USED TO RECAPITULATE OR REVERSE THE ACTIVITY PATTERNS CHANGED IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, AND CIRCUITS WILL BE MODULATED TO CORRECT CONNECTIVITY. OPTOGENETICS WILL BE USED IN AD MICE TO DETERMINE IF AD THERAPIES IMPROVE COGNITION THROUGH EFFECTS ON NEURAL ACTIVITY. THE INVESTIGATOR WILL RECEIVE TECHNICAL, CONCEPTUAL, AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT TRAINING FROM A MENTORING TEAM OF LEADING EXPERTS IN WORLD-CLASS LABS AT STANFORD UNIVERSITY IN PREPARATION FOR TRANSITION TO A FACULTY POSITION. THIS WORK WILL DISCOVER FUNDAMENTAL MECHANISMS OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. IT WILL RESULT IN UNPRECEDENTED, HIGH- RESOLUTION, COMPREHENSIVE DATA ON CHANGES IN NEURAL ACTIVITY AND CONNECTIVITY DURING ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE THAT WILL IDENTIFY THE SPECIFIC CIRCUITS, CELLS, AND ACTIVITY DYNAMICS THAT DRIVE COGNITIVE DECLINE, WHICH WILL HELP INFORM INTELLIGENT DESIGN OF NEW, PRECISE, AND EARLIER BIOMARKERS, DIAGNOSTIC STRATEGIES, AND THERAPEUTIC TREATMENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADAPTATION OF PATH-PAIN FOR DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS LIVING WITH PERSISTENT PAIN AND NEGATIVE EMOTIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS FREQUENTLY EXPERIENCE PERSISTENT MUSCULOSKELETAL PAIN. PAIN IS OFTEN MADE WORSE BY PERFORMING CAREGIVING TASKS, IMPAIRING DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS’ ABILITY TO PROVIDE CARE. DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS’ WHO HAVE PAIN OFTEN HAVE CO-EXISTING EMOTIONAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL HEALTH CHALLENGES, SUCH AS HIGH NEGATIVE EMOTIONS AND/OR COMORBID DEPRESSION, WHICH MAKES MANAGING THEIR PAIN AND THEIR CAREGIVING TASKS MORE DIFFICULT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS K99/R00 PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP DR. SHELBIE TURNER’S CAPACITY TO CONDUCT TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH TO SUPPORT DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS’ HEALTH AND WELL-BEING THROUGH IMPROVED MANAGEMENT OF THEIR OWN PERSISTENT PAIN. DR. TURNER WILL WORK TOWARDS FIVE TRAINING OBJECTIVES IN THE K99 PHASE OF THE PROJECT. DOING SO WILL ALLOW HER TO DEVELOP AND TRANSITION TO AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR WHO DESIGNS, ADAPTS, EVALUATES, AND DISSEMINATES INNOVATIVE, EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS TO PREVENT OR MITIGATE DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS’ NEGATIVE HEALTH OUTCOMES, WITH A FOCUS ON THE PROBLEM OF PERSISTENT PAIN AND ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS (E.G., NEGATIVE EMOTIONS) AND COMORBIDITIES (E.G., DEPRESSION). FIRST, SHE WILL ADD TO AND EXTEND HER KNOWLEDGE IN CORE SUBSTANTIVE AREAS TO INCLUDE PAIN, NEGATIVE EMOTIONS, DEMENTIA CAREGIVING, AND HEALTH BEHAVIOR CHANGE. SECOND, SHE WILL IMPROVE HER ABILITY TO DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT, AND DISSEMINATE BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS WITH AN EMPHASIS ON BOTH PAIN MANAGEMENT INTERVENTIONS AND CAREGIVER INTERVENTIONS. THIRD, SHE WILL GAIN EXPERIENCE NEEDED TO DESIGN AND CONDUCT CLINICAL TRIALS, INCLUDING CONVENTIONAL, PRAGMATIC, AND ADAPTIVE CLINICAL TRIALS WITH DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS. FINALLY, SHE WILL PURSUE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN GRANT WRITING (FOURTH TRAINING OBJECTIVE) AND LEADERSHIP AND COLLABORATION (FIFTH TRAINING OBJECTIVE). THE THREE RESEARCH AIMS OF THIS APPLICATION WILL PROGRESS AS FOLLOWS. AIM 1 ADAPTS AN EVIDENCE- BASED PAIN SELF-MANAGEMENT INTERVENTION, PROBLEM ADAPTATION THERAPY FOR PAIN IN PRIMARY CARE (PATH-PAIN), FOR USE BY DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS WITH PERSISTENT PAIN. AIM 2 TESTS THE USABILITY OF THE ADAPTED INTERVENTION WITH DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS, AND AIM 3 EXAMINES THE FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND PRELIMINARY EFFICACY OF THE INTERVENTION THROUGH A PILOT RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL. THE ADAPTED INTERVENTION WILL BE THE FIRST EVIDENCE- BASED PAIN SELF-MANAGEMENT PROGRAM CUSTOMIZED SPECIFICALLY FOR DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS CONSISTENT WITH NIA’S MISSION TO CONDUCT BEHAVIORAL RESEARCH ON AGING AND FOSTER THE DEVELOPMENT OF RESEARCH SCIENTISTS IN AGING. IT IS ALIGNED WITH NIA’S SPECIAL INTERESTS IN DEMENTIA CAREGIVER INTERVENTION RESEARCH AND PAIN MANAGEMENT RESEARCH. DR. TURNER PROPOSES TO PURSUE HER DEVELOPMENTAL GOALS AND BEGIN THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WITH THE SUPPORT OF THE DIVISION OF GERIATRICS AND PALLIATIVE MEDICINE AT WEILL CORNELL MEDICAL COLLEGE OF CORNELL UNIVERSITY, WHICH PROVIDES AN IDEAL ENVIRONMENT OF RESEARCH SUPPORT AND RESOURCES TO HELP HER ACHIEVE HER TRAINING AND RESEARCH GOALS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TARGETING DEFECTIVE DIFFERENTIATION IN THE TREATMENT OF PEDIATRIC RHABDOMYOSARCOMA INVASION AND METASTASIS - PROJECT SUMMARY RHABDOMYOSARCOMA (RMS) IS A CANCER OF THE SKELETAL MUSCLE THAT AFFECTS AROUND 350 CHILDREN EACH YEAR. DESPITE ADVANCES IN THE TREATMENT OF LOCALIZED DISEASE, THE OUTCOMES FOR PATIENTS WITH ADVANCED OR METASTATIC DISEASE HAVE NOT IMPROVED IN MORE THAN FORTY YEARS. THIS IS PARTLY DUE TO A LACK OF UNDERSTANDING OF THE PROCESSES DRIVING RMS INVASION AND METASTASIS. RMS IS CHARACTERIZED IN PART BY A BLOCK IN DIFFERENTIATION OF SKELETAL MUSCLE (MYOGENIC) PRECURSOR CELLS. MY MENTOR, DR. YOHE DISCOVERED THAT DIFFERENTIATION CAN BE INDUCED WITH MEK1/2 INHIBITORS IN PAX/FOXO1 FUSION NEGATIVE RMS (FN-RMS) TUMORS WITH ONCOGENIC RAS MUTATIONS SLOWING FN-RMS TUMOR GROWTH AND EXTENDING SURVIVAL IN PRECLINICAL MODELS. HOWEVER, BECAUSE DYNAMIC MODULATION OF DIFFERENTIATION IS A MECHANISM BY WHICH MANY CANCERS PROMOTE METASTASIS AND ESCAPE THERAPY, A DEEPER UNDERSTANDING OF THE EFFECT OF DIFFERENTIATION ON RMS INVASION AND METASTASIS IS NEEDED FOR THE EFFECTIVE TRANSLATION OF DIFFERENTIATION THERAPY. THIS PATHWAY TO INDEPENDENCE (K99/R00) PROPOSAL OUTLINES EXPERIMENTS TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT YAP/TAZ-MEDIATED PERTURBATIONS OF FN-RMS DIFFERENTIATION PROGRAMS DRIVE LOCAL INVASION AND METASTASIS. THIS HYPOTHESIS WILL BE TESTED IN THREE AIMS. AIM 1 IDENTIFY MECHANISMS BY WHICH LATE MYOGENIC DIFFERENTIATION IS DYSREGULATED IN FN-RMS IN A MECHANISTIC STUDY OF NF-KB ACTIVITY COMPLIMENTED BY SINGLE CELL TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS, INNOVATIVE DIFFERENTIATION REPORTER CELL LINES, AND A DRUG SCREEN TO IDENTIFY TARGETABLE PERTURBATIONS OF MYOGENIC DIFFERENTIATION IN FN-RMS. AIM 2 INVESTIGATES TUMOR-STROMAL INTERACTIONS TO DETERMINE THE MECHANISMS DRIVING INVASION IN DIFFERENTIATION THERAPY-RESISTANT CELLS USING BOTH IN VITRO SPHEROID INVASION ASSAYS AND IN VIVO ZEBRAFISH TUMOR INVASION STUDIES. AIM 3 UTILIZES A NOVEL ORTHOTOPIC XENOGRAFT MOUSE MODEL OF SPONTANEOUS FN-RMS METASTASIS AND SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS TO STUDY DYNAMIC REGULATION OF DIFFERENTIATION ON FN-RMS METASTASIS. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL 1) DEVELOP NOVEL TOOLS THAT WILL BENEFIT THE LARGER COMMUNITY IN THE INVESTIGATION OF RMS INVASION AND METASTASIS, 2) ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE MECHANISMS DRIVING FN-RMS INVASION AND METASTASIS, 3) IDENTIFY NEW THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR THE TREATMENT OF PATIENTS WITH ADVANCED FN-RMS. MY ROBUST PUBLICATION AND FUNDING RECORD DEMONSTRATES MY POTENTIAL AS AN INDEPENDENT SCIENTIST. THE EXCEPTIONAL RESEARCH, TRAINING, AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES AT THE NIH INTRAMURAL RESEARCH PROGRAM WILL BE COMPLEMENTED BY THE MENTORSHIP OF DR. MARIELLE YOHE, DR. KANDICE TANNER, AND DR. CORINNE LINARDIC. WITH THE HELP OF MY ADVISORY COMMITTEE (DR. JACK SHERN, DR. JOHN BROGNARD, AND DR. TROY MCEACHRON) DURING THE K99 PHASE, I WILL DEVELOP A STRONG SKILL SET IN TRANSCRIPTOMIC DATA ANALYSIS, ANIMAL MODELING, ADVANCED IMAGING, AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH. THIS TECHNICAL SKILL SET WILL BE COMPLEMENTED BY TRAINING IN LEADERSHIP, COMMUNICATION, PERSONNEL MANAGEMENT, AND MENTORING. UPON TRANSITION TO THE R00 PHASE, I WILL LAUNCH A CAREER AS AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR LEADING A TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH PROGRAM STUDYING INVASION AND METASTASIS IN ADVANCED SARCOMAS.

description: DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING PROGNOSTIC MODELS FOR BLACK WOMEN WITH ENDOMETRIAL CANCER FOLLOWING HYSTERECTOMY - ENDOMETRIAL CANCER (EC) INCIDENCE AND MORTALITY ARE RISING RAPIDLY IN THE U.S. BLACK WOMEN ARE EXPERIENCING THE SHARPEST INCREASE, WITH INCIDENCE AND MORTALITY RISING 46% AND 29%, RESPECTIVELY, FROM 1999–2015. WHILE THE 5-YEAR SURVIVAL FOR EC OVERALL IS 80%, FOR BLACK PATIENTS IT IS ONLY 63%. THIS IS DUE, IN PART, TO THE MORE FREQUENT DIAGNOSIS OF AGGRESSIVE NON-ENDOMETRIOID TUMOR SUBTYPES IN BLACK WOMEN (~35% VS ~17% NON-BLACK). PRIMARY STAGING AND TREATMENT FOR EC IS SURGICAL HYSTERECTOMY WITH BILATERAL SALPINGO-OOPHORECTOMY; SEVERAL ADJUVANT THERAPIES ALLOW FOR THE TAILORING OF POST-SURGICAL TREATMENT, REQUIRING CAREFUL BALANCING OF PROGNOSIS/RECURRENCE RISKS WITH ADVERSE EFFECTS OF THERAPY TO IMPROVE OUTCOMES AND AVOID MISTREATMENT. BLACK WOMEN ARE MORE COMMONLY DIAGNOSED WITH THESE AGGRESSIVE HISTOLOGIC SUBTYPES NOT AMENABLE TO SURGICAL RESECTION ALONE. THERE ARE NO PROGNOSTIC TOOLS TO INFORM DISCUSSION OF ADJUVANT THERAPIES FOR BLACK WOMEN DIAGNOSED WITH EC. THIS EARLY K99/R00 APPLICATION LEVERAGES YEARS OF NIH FUNDING AND COLLABORATION TO DEVELOP AND EXTERNALLY VALIDATE PROGNOSTIC TOOLS FOR BLACK WOMEN WITH EC POST-HYSTERECTOMY. THIS RESEARCH WILL INFORM DISCUSSION OF TAILORED ADJUVANT THERAPIES IN CLINICAL SETTINGS. IT IS FOUNDATIONAL FOR DR. PEERI TO ACHIEVE RESEARCH INDEPENDENCE FOCUSED ON CREATING CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING TOOLS FOR ALL POPULATIONS. OUR SPECIFIC AIMS ARE TO: 1A) BUILD A ROBUST PROGNOSTIC TOOL TAILORED FOR BLACK EC PATIENTS USING READILY AVAILABLE CLINICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGIC FACTORS TO PREDICT SURVIVAL 3- AND 5-YEARS POST-HYSTERECTOMY, AND TO EXTERNALLY VALIDATE THIS TOOL IN THE MSK COHORT; 1B) COMPARE MODEL PERFORMANCE FOR BLACK PATIENTS WITH AN ESTABLISHED MODEL DEVELOPED PRIMARILY IN WHITE WOMEN; 1C) DEVELOP AN EASY-TO-USE SURVIVAL NOMOGRAM WEB-BASED TOOL FOR CLINICIAN AND PATIENT USE; 2A) ASSESS THE UTILITY OF ADDING EXISTING TCGA MOLECULAR SUBTYPES TO OUR PROGNOSTIC TOOL FOR BLACK WOMEN AND EXTERNALLY VALIDATE IN THE MSK COHORT; AND 2B) USE ESTABLISHED CLINICAL TOOLS IN OUR POPULATION AS A POINT OF REFERENCE FOR EVALUATING THE PERFORMANCE OF OUR MODEL; 3) BUILD BIOMARKER-BASED PROGNOSTIC TOOLS TO PREDICT OVERALL SURVIVAL AT 3- AND 5-YEARS POST-HYSTERECTOMY IN 3A) BLACK WOMEN, EXPANDING UPON THE PROGNOSTIC TOOLS DEVELOPED IN AIM 1, AND 3B) WHITE WOMEN, EXPANDING ON AN ESTABLISHED TOOL. THE TRAINING GOALS ARE TO: 1) RECEIVE TRAINING IN RIGOROUS PROGNOSTIC MODEL DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION METHODS; 2) RECEIVE TRAINING IN CANCER GENOMICS INCLUDING ADVANCED METHODS FOR WHOLE-EXOME SEQUENCE DATA; 3) EXPAND KNOWLEDGE OF BIOMARKERS OF CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE AND MACHINE-LEARNING METHODS FOR MODEL DEVELOPMENT; AND 4) LAY A FOUNDATION TO SUPPORT AN INDEPENDENT RESEARCH CAREER IN CANCER HEALTH DISPARITIES. ULTIMATELY, THIS PROPOSAL WILL ADVANCE THE CAREER OF A YOUNG INVESTIGATOR WITH A STRONG RESEARCH BACKGROUND FROM POSTDOCTORAL FELLOW TO INDEPENDENCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DOWNFIELD MR SPECTROSCOPIC IMAGING OF THE HUMAN BRAIN - PROJECT SUMMARY: IN PROTON MAGNETIC RESONANCE SPECTROSCOPY (MRS) OF THE HUMAN BRAIN, SIGNALS ARISE BOTH UPFIELD (UF) AND DOWNFIELD (DF) FROM THE WATER RESONANCE. WHILE UF MRS AND MR SPECTROSCOPIC IMAGING (MRSI) HAVE BEEN EXTENSIVELY STUDIED IN HUMANS OVER THE LAST 30 YEARS, THERE HAVE BEEN VERY FEW DOWNFIELD STUDIES, AND ALL OF THEM USED SINGLE VOXEL SPATIAL LOCALIZATION. CURRENTLY, THERE ARE TWO SIGNIFICANT TECHNICAL CHALLENGES FOR DF-MRSI, NAMELY (A) THE LACK OF PULSE SEQUENCES TO ACQUIRE 3D DF-MRSI WITH OPTIMUM SENSITIVITY IN THE SHORTEST POSSIBLE SCAN TIME, AND (B) SPECIFIC SOFTWARE FOR THE ACCURATE QUANTIFICATION AND VISUALIZATION OF THE BROAD AND SIGNIFICANTLY OVERLAPPING DF SIGNALS. IN ADDITION, THE CLINICAL AND NEUROSCIENCE APPLICATIONS OF DF-MRSI HAVE YET TO BE EXPLORED. THE INITIAL GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP OPTIMIZED 3D DF-MRSI PULSE SEQUENCES FOR BOTH 3T AND 7T, AND AN OPEN- SOURCE SOFTWARE PACKAGE FOR IMPROVED QUANTIFICATION, ANALYSIS, AND VISUALIZATION OF DF RESONANCES. DF SPECTRA CONTAIN SIGNALS FROM BOTH EXCHANGEABLE AND NON-EXCHANGEABLE PROTONS, AND THE INFORMATION CONTENT OF DF- MRSI MAY THEREFORE BE COMPLEMENTARY TO CHEMICAL EXCHANGE SATURATION TRANSFER (GEST) MRI. IN PARTICULAR, AMIDE-PROTON TRANSFER (APT) GEST HAS PROVEN QUITE SUCCESSFUL FOR THE EVALUATION OF HUMAN BRAIN TUMORS; IN THE R00 PHASE OF THIS PROPOSAL, AFTER ESTABLISHING NORMATIVE VALUES AND REPRODUCIBILITY, A COMPARISON OF THE VALUE OF 3D DF-MRSI VS. APT-GEST IN PATIENTS WITH GLIOMA WILL BE PERFORMED. IN PARTICULAR, THE FOCUS WILL BE ON THE ABILITY TO DISTINGUISH RECURRENT TUMOR FROM RADIATION NECROSIS IN PATIENTS TREATED FOR HIGH GRADE GLIOMA; THIS IS AN IMPORTANT DIAGNOSTIC QUESTION THAT DIRECTLY EFFECTS CHOICE OF TREATMENT, AND WHICH IS OFTEN DIFFICULT TO ANSWER USING CONVENTIONAL MRI. THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP NEW TOOLS TO INVESTIGATE METABOLIC PROCESSES IN BOTH NORMAL AND DISEASED NEUROLOGICAL CONDITIONS AND LEVERAGE THESE INSIGHTS TO ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF BRAIN TUMORS, POTENTIALLY REVEALING NEW AVENUES FOR IMPROVED DIAGNOSIS AND MORE EFFECTIVE THERAPIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: FAST HIGH-RESOLUTION MICROSTRUCTURE DIFFUSION MRI EXPLOITING DATA REDUNDANCY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT DIFFUSION MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (DMRI) IS INDISPENSABLE IN EVERYDAY CLINICAL NEUROIMAGING DUE TO ITS CAPACITY FOR NONINVASIVE WHOLE-BRAIN IMAGING. IT HAS A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT ON DIAGNOSING CONDITIONS AFFECTING MILLIONS OF AMERICANS. FURTHERMORE, ADVANCED DMRI HOLDS PROMISE FOR MAPPING MICROSTRUCTURAL TISSUE FEATURES, REVEALING HIDDEN DAMAGE IN WHITE MATTER, GUIDING NEUROSURGERY, AND STUDYING COMPLEX BRAIN STRUCTURES. HOWEVER, LENGTHY ACQUISITION TIMES PREVENT ADVANCED DIFFUSION ENCODINGS AND HIGH-RESOLUTION IMAGING (1MM^3) FROM REACHING CLINICAL APPLICATIONS. TO BRIDGE THIS GAP, I PROPOSE A NOVEL APPROACH TO ACCELERATE ADVANCED DMRI WHILE MAINTAINING IMAGE QUALITY AND MICROSTRUCTURE SENSITIVITY. THIS INNOVATIVE METHOD AIMS TO ACHIEVE UP TO FIVE-FOLD SPEED IMPROVEMENT BY EFFICIENTLY EXPLOITING DATA REDUNDANCY. WHILE CONVENTIONAL MRI ACCELERATION HAS FOCUSED EXCLUSIVELY ON SPATIAL UNDERSAMPLING, DMRI DATASETS ARE INTRINSICALLY HIGHER-DIMENSIONAL DUE TO THE MULTIPLE DIFFUSION ENCODING VOLUMES ACQUIRED, OPENING ADDITIONAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR ACCELERATION. MY GOAL IS TO PIONEER A NOVEL IMAGING APPROACH CALLED ZERO-SHELL IMAGING (ZSI) THAT USES TISSUE BIOPHYSICS TO SPEED UP DMRI DATA ACQUISITION AND IMPROVE IMAGE RESOLUTION. THIS TECHNIQUE ENCOMPASSES JOINT UNDERSAMPLING IN BOTH SPATIAL (K-SPACE) AND DIFFUSION WEIGHTING (Q-SPACE) DOMAINS, FACILITATING DIRECT RECONSTRUCTION OF DIFFUSION CONTRASTS WITH FEWER SPATIAL SAMPLES PER DIFFUSION ENCODING. ACCOUNTING FOR PATIENT MOTION BETWEEN SAMPLES AND MERGING SEQUENTIAL IMAGES, I AIM TO OPTIMIZE THE ALLOCATION OF SCAN TIME, TO ENABLE HIGHER RESOLUTION AND TO INCREASE THE NUMBER OF DIFFUSION ENCODINGS WITHOUT LENGTHENING THE OVERALL SCAN TIME. DURING THE K99 PHASE OF THIS AWARD, I LAID THE TECHNICAL FOUNDATIONS FOR ZSI. I HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT ZSI CAN SUCCESSFULLY UNDERSAMPLE THE DIFFUSION ACQUISITION SPACE, SEPARATING DIFFUSION WEIGHTINGS AND DIRECTIONS. I HAVE SHOWN THAT IT IS POSSIBLE TO RECONSTRUCT DMRI SIGNAL'S ROTATIONAL INVARIANTS, ORIENTATION-INDEPENDENT MICROSTRUCTURE FEATURES, FROM UNDERSAMPLED Q-SPACE DATASETS. ADDITIONALLY, JOINT K-Q-SPACE UNDERSAMPLING HAS BEEN SHOWN FEASIBLE FOR SPEEDING UP DATA ACQUISITION. IN THE R00 PHASE, I WILL PERFORM A MORE COMPREHENSIVE VALIDATION OF MY K-Q JOINT IMAGE RECONSTRUCTION TOGETHER WITH AN EVALUATION OF THE CLINICAL UTILITY FOR TRACKING DISEASE PROGRESSION IN MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS (MS) PATIENTS AND FOR DETECTING MS BRAINSTEM LESIONS. OVERALL, THIS RESEARCH WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP AN INNOVATIVE IMAGING METHOD THAT HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM MRI DIAGNOSIS. THIS PROJECT COMBINES, FOR THE FIRST TIME, THE LOW-RANK NATURE OF MRI IMAGES (K-SPACE) TOGETHER WITH MICROSTRUCTURE MODELING CONSTRAINTS THAT EFFECTIVELY FACTORIZE AND REDUCE THE DIMENSIONALITY OF THE DIFFUSION WEIGHTING SPACE (Q-SPACE). THIS WORK IS MOTIVATED BY OBSERVATIONS THAT THE COMBINED K-Q-SPACE SAMPLES ARE SPARSE AND PERMIT MASSIVE UNDERSAMPLING. IN THE LONG TERM, THE INCREASED SPEED ENABLED BY THIS PROJECT MAY FINALLY ENABLE THE TRANSLATION OF MICROSTRUCTURE IMAGING TO CLINIC.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DELINEATING THE NEURAL COMPUTATIONAL NETWORK FOR OBJECT RECOGNITION - PROJECT SUMMARY (SEE INSTRUCTIONS): A CORE FUNCTION OF THE HUMAN BRAIN IS VISUAL OBJECT RECOGNITION, WHICH UNDERLIES MANY HIGHER-ORDER FUNCTIONS SUCH AS MEMORY AND EMOTION. DEFICITS IN RECOGNIZING OBJECTS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH VARIOUS NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS, INCLUDING VISUAL AGNOSIA, PROSOPAGNOSIA, AND ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE. HOWEVER, THE NEURAL MECHANISMS FOR OBJECT RECOGNITION REMAIN ELUSIVE. SPECIFICALLY, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW THE BRAIN TRANSFORMS VISUAL INPUTS INTO MEANINGFUL SEMANTIC REPRESENTATIONS. PREVIOUS STUDIES HAVE PROPOSED A HIERARCHICAL NEURAL NETWORK FOR OBJECT PROCESSING, INCLUDING THE VENTRAL TEMPORAL CORTEX (VTC) AND THE DOWNSTREAM MEDIAL TEMPORAL LOBE (MTL). WHILE RECENT SINGLE-NEURON STUDIES IN NON-HUMAN PRIMATES HAVE DEMONSTRATED AXIS-BASED VISUAL FEATURE ENCODING IN THE VTC, HUMAN MTL NEURONS HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO SELECTIVELY ENCODE INDIVIDUAL EXEMPLARS (EXEMPLAR-BASED CODING) BASED ON SEMANTIC CONCEPTS. YET, THE PROCESS BY WHICH VISUAL FEATURE REPRESENTATIONS IN THE VTC ARE TRANSFORMED INTO SEMANTIC REPRESENTATIONS OF ABSTRACT LABELS IN THE MTL REMAINS UNKNOWN. THIS CURRENT PROJECT AIMS TO ADDRESS THIS QUESTION BY EXAMINING THE NEURAL COMPUTATIONS AND NETWORK DYNAMICS DURING OBJECT RECOGNITION IN THE VENTRAL VISUAL PATHWAY. I WILL CONDUCT INTRACRANIAL RECORDINGS FROM BOTH INDIVIDUAL NEURONS AND LOCAL NEURAL POPULATIONS, COUPLED WITH SOPHISTICATED COMPUTATIONAL ALGORITHMS. DURING THE K99 PHASE, I HAVE SURVEYED THREE DISTINCT NEURAL MODELS ACROSS SUBREGIONS IN THE VTC AND MTL, INCLUDING THE AXIS-BASED FEATURE MODEL, THE EXEMPLAR-BASED MODEL, AND THE REGION-BASED FEATURE MODEL (PROPOSED IN MY RECENT WORK). I DEMONSTRATED THAT THESE CODING MECHANISMS ARE DISTRIBUTED ACROSS DIFFERENT REGIONS, CORRESPONDING TO DIFFERENT STAGES OF OBJECT PROCESSING. I HAVE ALSO IDENTIFIED VTC-MTL INTERACTIONS THAT ARE CRITICAL TO OBJECT RECOGNITION. DURING THE INDEPENDENT R00 PHASE, I WIL L LEVERAGE THE RESULTS AND ANALYTIC PIPELINE ESTABLISHED IN THE K99 PHASE TO INVESTIGATE HOW VTC-MTL INTERACTIONS ARE MODULATED BY BEHAVIORAL PERFORMANCE AND HOW DIFFERENT NEURAL CODING SCHEMES TRANSITION FROM ONE TO ANOTHER ALONG THE VTC-MTL PATHWAY TO ACHIEVE THE TRANSFORMATION OF OBJECT REPRESENTATIONS. SPECIFICALLY, I WILL TEST HOW VTC-MTL INTERACTIONS VARY WITH BEHAVIORAL PERFORMANCE AND HOW THESE INTERACTIONS DYNAMICALLY SUPPORT TRANSITIONS AMONG DISTINCT CODING SCHEMES. MY CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT REGION-BASED CODING SERVES AS AN INTERMEDIATE MECHANISM BRIDGING AXIS-BASED CODING IN THE VTC AND EXEMPLAR-BASED CODING IN THE MTL, THEREBY ENABLING THE TRANSFORMATION FROM DETAILED VISUAL REPRESENTATIONS TO ABSTRACT, MNEMONIC REPRESENTATIONS. WHILE THIS PROJECT AIMS TO PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO OBJECT RECOGNITION IN HUMANS, THE ANTICIPATED OUTCOMES HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO INSPIRE NEW THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS FOR DISORDERS INVOLVING IMPAIRED OBJECT RECOGNITION. MY LONG-TERM GOAL AS A PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR IS TO ELUCIDATE HOW VISUAL PERCEPTION SUPPORTS HUMAN NAVIGATION OF THE COMPLEX SOCIAL WORLD IN BOTH HEALTHY AND CLINICAL POPULATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING NOVEL METHODS TO COMBAT URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS - URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (UTIS) AFFECT MORE THAN 150 MILLION PEOPLE ANNUALLY AND ARE BECOMING INCREASINGLY DIFFICULT TO TREAT BECAUSE OF RISING ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE. BACTERIAL ADHESION TO HOST TISSUES AND MEDICAL DEVICES IS THE CRITICAL FIRST STEP IN INFECTION AND IS MEDIATED BY SPECIALIZED SURFACE PROTEINS KNOWN AS ADHESINS. BECAUSE ADHESION IS REQUIRED FOR INFECTION TO BE ESTABLISHED, ADHESINS REPRESENT ATTRACTIVE THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR PREVENTING INFECTION. THE ADHESIN FIMH FROM UROPATHOGENIC ESCHERICHIA COLI HAS VALIDATED ANTI-ADHESION STRATEGIES AS A THERAPEUTIC APPROACH. A KEY OUTSTANDING QUESTION IS WHETHER THIS APPROACH CAN BE GENERALIZED TO OTHER ADHESINS, MANY OF WHICH REMAIN STRUCTURALLY AND MECHANISTICALLY UNCHARACTERIZED. THIS PROJECT FOCUSES ON TWO CLINICALLY IMPORTANT ADHESINS: FMLH FROM UROPATHOGENIC ESCHERICHIA COLI, WHICH PROMOTES PERSISTENT COLONIZATION OF THE URINARY TRACT, AND MRKD FROM MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT KLEBSIELLA PNEUMONIAE, WHICH MEDIATES BIOFILM FORMATION AND IS IMPLICATED IN CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (CAUTIS). BUILDING ON DISCOVERIES FROM THE K99 PHASE, WHICH ESTABLISHED THE STRUCTURAL AND MECHANISTIC BASIS OF A NOVEL ADHESIN INHIBITORY MECHANISM TERMED PARASTERIC INHIBITION USING THE PROTOTYPICAL ADHESIN FIMH, THIS WORK WILL TEST WHETHER THE CONFORMATIONAL DYNAMICS AND ALLOSTERIC REGULATORY MECHANISMS GOVERNING FIMH FUNCTION ARE CONSERVED IN FMLH AND MRKD, AND WHETHER THEY CAN BE EXPLOITED TO INHIBIT BACTERIAL ADHESION. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL DEFINE THE CONFORMATIONAL LANDSCAPES OF FMLH AND MRKD USING MUTAGENESIS AND NMR SPECTROSCOPY, CHARACTERIZE THE CONFORMATIONAL DYNAMICS THAT REGULATE LIGAND BINDING AND ADHESION USING NMR AND BIOPHYSICAL TOOLS, AND DEVELOP PEPTIDE INHIBITORS THAT TARGET THESE ADHESINS TO BLOCK BACTERIAL ATTACHMENT. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES GOVERNING ADHESIN STRUCTURE, DYNAMICS, AND FUNCTION WHILE PROVIDING A GENERALIZABLE FRAMEWORK FOR DEVELOPING ANTI-ADHESION THERAPEUTICS AGAINST MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT UROPATHOGENS. THESE STUDIES HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO ADVANCE A NEW CLASS OF NON-ANTIBIOTIC INTERVENTIONS FOR THE PREVENTION AND TREATMENT OF URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CONTRIBUTION OF DNA REPLICATION TO EPIGENETIC INHERITANCE IN A MODEL MULTI-CELLULAR ORGANISM - PROJECT SUMMARY (SEE INSTRUCTIONS):  ASYMMETRIC CELL DIVISION (ACD) CONTRIBUTES TO CELLULAR DIVERSITY DURING DEVELOPMENT AND ADULT TISSUE  HOMEOSTASIS. ACD GENERATES TWO GENETICALLY IDENTICAL DAUGHTER CELLS WITH DISTINCT CELL FATES INFLUENCED BY THE  INFORMATION THEY INHERIT. FAILURE TO PROPERLY REGULATE ACD LEADS TO DISEASES SUCH AS TISSUE DEGENERATION AND CANCER.  UNDERSTANDING THE MECHANISMS THAT UNDERLIE ACD IS THEREFORE CRITICAL TO UNCOVERING HOW STEM CELL BEHAVIORS ARE  REGULATED IN BOTH NORMAL DEVELOPMENT AND DISEASE.    ONE KEY DETERMINANT OF CELL FATE IS CHROMATIN, WHICH IS ESTABLISHED AND MAINTAINED THROUGH THE PACKAGING OF  DNA AND HISTONES INTO NUCLEOSOMES. DURING DNA REPLICATION, HISTONE CHAPERONES ORCHESTRATE NUCLEOSOME  DISASSEMBLY AND REASSEMBLY, ALLOWING FAITHFUL TRANSMISSION OF EPIGENETIC INFORMATION. ABERRANT CHROMATIN DYNAMICS  CAN DISRUPT CRITICAL CELL FUNCTIONS AND ARE IMPLICATED IN MANY DISEASES. ALTHOUGH REPLICATION-COUPLED CHROMATIN  ASSEMBLY IS WELL STUDIED IN VITRO AND IN UNICELLULAR ORGANISMS, HOW THIS PROCESS CONTRIBUTES TO CELL FATE SPECIFICATION  WITHIN A MULTICELLULAR ORGANISM REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD.   MY RESEARCH ADDRESSES THIS GAP BY INVESTIGATING HOW DNA REPLICATION INFLUENCES CELL-TYPE SPECIFICATION IN THE  DROSOPHILA MALE GERMLINE. THIS SYSTEM OFFERS POWERFUL ADVANTAGES: WELL-DEFINED STEM CELL LINEAGES, ROBUST MODELS FOR  ACD, SPATIALLY ORGANIZED CELL DIFFERENTIATION, AND THE CAPACITY FOR IN VIVO CELL REPROGRAMMING. IN THIS CONTEXT, A  GERMLINE STEM CELL (GSC) DIVIDES ASYMMETRICALLY TO GENERATE A SELF-RENEWING STEM CELL AND A DIFFERENTIATING  GONIALBLAST. MEANWHILE, ASSOCIATED CYST STEM CELLS (CYSCS) ALSO DIVIDE ASYMMETRICALLY, AND THEIR PROGENY PROVIDE  SUPPORT TO THE DEVELOPING GERMLINE. USING THE MALE DROSOPHILA GERMLINE, THIS PROPOSAL ASKS, “HOW DOES DNA  REPLICATION-COUPLED CHROMATIN ASSEMBLY INFLUENCE CELL FATE DECISIONS?”  GENOMIC STUDIES OF GSCS WERE LIMITED BY THEIR SCARCITY IN WILDTYPE TISSUE, BUT A GSC-LIKE TUMOR ENABLED US TO  OVERCOME THIS CHALLENGE AND GENERATE COMPREHENSIVE TRANSCRIPTIONAL, CHROMATIN, AND REPLICATION TIMING MAPS OF GSC LIKE AND CYSC-LIKE CELLS. THESE DATA REVEALED DIFFERENCES IN REGULATORY FACTORS, CHROMATIN STATES, AND REPLICATION  PROGRAMS, INCLUDING ELEVATED EXPRESSION OF HISTONE CHAPERONES AND DNA REPLICATION FACTORS IN GSCS. BUILDING ON THIS  FOUNDATION, WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW DNA REPLICATION-COUPLED HISTONE ASSEMBLY CONTRIBUTES TO GERMLINE CELL FATE  TRANSITIONS AND SOMATIC EPIGENETIC INHERITANCE. WE WILL ALSO DEVELOP A NOVEL GERMLINE DIFFERENTIATION PROCEDURE TO  DISSECT HOW CHROMATIN AND GENE EXPRESSION ARE REMODELED DURING CELL IDENTITY CHANGES. TOGETHER, THESE EXPERIMENTS  WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH DNA REPLICATION CONTRIBUTES TO CELL DATE DECISIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EMOTIONAL AND BIOBEHAVIORAL MECHANISMS OF PARENT-INFANT EMOTIONAL SYNCHRONY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT MY CAREER GOAL IS TO LEAD A TRANSDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH TEAM THAT INVESTIGATES MULTI-LEVEL MECHANISMS LEADING TO OPTIMAL CHILD SOCIOEMOTIONAL DEVELOPMENT FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF EARLY-LIFE DYADIC EMOTIONAL SYNCHRONY. THE OVERARCHING GOAL WILL BE TO IMPLEMENT TRANSLATIONAL, MECHANISTIC AND CLINICAL RESEARCH TO UNCOVER THE EMOTIONAL AND BIOBEHAVIORAL ORIGINS OF PARENT-INFANT EMOTIONAL SYNCHRONY AND THE PATHWAYS THROUGH WHICH EARLY DYADIC INTERACTIONS LEAD TO SOCIOEMOTIONAL FUNCTIONING ACROSS THE LIFE COURSE. ULTIMATELY THIS WORK WILL LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF APPROPRIATELY TARGETED INTERVENTIONS TO PROMOTE EARLY RELATIONAL HEALTH AND OPTIMAL CHILD SOCIOEMOTIONAL FUNCTIONING. TO EFFECTIVELY ESTABLISH AND LEAD THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM, I REQUIRE ADDITIONAL TRAINING IN MOTHER-INFANT ECG/EEG, QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS OF SUBJECTIVE EXPERIENCES, MULTIMODAL DATA INTEGRATION (QUALITATIVE-QUANTITATIVE, NEURO-BIO-BEHAVIOR, LONGITUDINAL), BIOSTATISTICS, PSYCHOLOGY AND NEUROSCIENCE. MY TRAINING TO DATE HAS PROVIDED ME WITH A STRONG FOUNDATION OF SKILLS IN INTERVENTION RESEARCH, EXPERIMENTAL DESIGNS AND EARLY RELATIONAL HEALTH FROM THE LENS OF PARENTAL SENSITIVITY. MY CAREER DEVELOPMENT PLAN EXPANDS ON THIS SKILL SET TO PROVIDE ESSENTIAL FURTHER TRAINING IN HUMAN DYADIC FACE-TO-FACE INTERACTIONS, ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAPHY (EEG), ELECTROCARDIOGRAM (ECG), ANALYSES OF BIOBEHAVIORAL SYNCHRONY, QUALITATIVE METHODS AND BIOSTATISTICS. BY ENGAGING IN THIS PROTECTED TRAINING TIME, I WILL ENTER MY INDEPENDENT STAGE OF RESEARCH WELL PREPARED TO LEAD A RESEARCH TEAM PURPOSEFULLY ESTABLISHED TO STUDY THE ORIGINS OF SOCIAL COGNITION FROM THE LENS OF PARENT-INFANT DYADIC EMOTIONAL SYNCHRONY. STUDIES HAVE FOUND THAT PARENT-INFANT DYADS SYNCHRONIZE THEIR HEART RHYTHMS AND BRAIN ACTIVITY DURING EPISODES OF FACE-TO-FACE MATCHED BEHAVIORS (BEHAVIORAL SYNCHRONY). BIOBEHAVIORAL SYNCHRONY, I.E., COORDINATION OF BRAIN, HEART AND BEHAVIORAL SIGNALS BETWEEN PARENTS AND INFANTS WHEN ENGAGING IN FACE-TO-FACE INTERACTION, PROVIDES A BASIS FOR STUDYING PARENT-INFANT DYADIC INTERACTIONS IN THE FIRST 12 MONTHS AS A MECHANISM LEADING TO IMPROVED SOCIO-EMOTIONAL FUNCTIONING IN LATER YEARS. THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING BIOBEHAVIORAL SYNCHRONY ARE STILL RELATIVELY UNKNOWN. HERE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT EMOTIONAL SYNCHRONY MAY BE A VEHICLE STRENGTHENING BIOBEHAVIORAL SYNCHRONY. THE K99 STUDY AIMS TO IDENTIFY THE BIOBEHAVIORAL (AIM 1) AND EMOTIONAL (AIM 2) CORRELATES OF MOTHER-INFANT EMOTIONAL SYNCHRONY. THE R00 STUDY (AIM 3) WILL EXPAND THE K99 AIMS TO MOTHER-INFANT AND FATHER-INFANT DYADS, AND LINK EMOTIONAL AND BIOBEHAVIORAL SYNCHRONY TO LATER CHILD SOCIOEMOTIONAL FUNCTIONING.

description: MULTI-TRAIT ANALYSIS IN LARGE-SCALE BIOBANK DATASETS LINKED TO ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS. - LARGE-SCALE BIOBANKS LINKED TO ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (EHR) INTEGRATE DIAGNOSES, QUANTITATIVE BIOMARKERS, AND FAMILY HISTORY, ENABLING GENETIC ANALYSES THAT CAPTURE COMPLEMENTARY SIGNALS OF DISEASE RISK. LIABILITY THRESHOLD MODELS CAN LEVERAGE THESE MULTI-SOURCE PHENOTYPES TO INCREASE STATISTICAL POWER AND BETTER APPROXIMATE LATENT DISEASE LIABILITY FOR CLINICALLY RELEVANT GENETIC RISK PREDICTION. HOWEVER, THESE MULTI-TRAIT MODELS FACE TWO KEY CHALLENGES: GWAS USING LIABILITY ESTIMATES MAY YIELD EFFECT ESTIMATES THAT DIFFER FROM CONVENTIONAL CASE-CONTROL ANALYSES, AND MODEL TRANSFERABILITY ACROSS BIOBANKS MAY BE LIMITED. CURRENT EHR-BASED LIABILITY MODELS GENERALLY ASSUME THAT GENETIC RELATIONSHIPS AMONG TRAITS ARE CONSISTENT ACROSS THE GENOME, WHICH MAY OVERLOOK IMPORTANT LOCUS-SPECIFIC DIFFERENCES. THIS LIMITATION MAY INTRODUCE NON-TARGET GENETIC SIGNALS, CONTRIBUTING TO INCONSISTENT ASSOCIATION ESTIMATES AND REDUCED CROSS-BIOBANK TRANSFERABILITY. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP LOCUS-AWARE METHODS FOR EHR-BASED DISEASE LIABILITY ESTIMATION THAT INCORPORATE LINKAGE DISEQUILIBRIUM-INFORMED LOCAL GENETIC CORRELATION AND HERITABILITY INTO MULTI-TRAIT MODELS. AIM 1 WILL DEVELOP AND EVALUATE LOCUS-LEVEL LIABILITY MODELING APPROACHES FOR DOWNSTREAM GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDIES. AIM 2 WILL VALIDATE THE FRAMEWORK ACROSS LARGE-SCALE BIOBANKS BY ASSESSING REPRODUCIBILITY, GENETIC DISCOVERY, AND POLYGENIC RISK PREDICTION. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES A CRITICAL BARRIER TO EHR-BASED GENETIC STUDIES AND MAY IMPROVE RISK PREDICTION FOR COMPLEX DISEASES WHILE ENHANCING THE RELIABILITY OF GENETIC DISCOVERY ACROSS BIOBANKS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTEGRATING GENETICS AND SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS TO PREDICT DISEASE PROGRESSION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  COMMON, COMPLEX DISEASES EVOLVE OVER TIME THROUGH INTERACTIONS BETWEEN GENETIC LIABILITY AND SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES, SHAPING DISEASE ONSET AND PROGRESSION. WHILE POLYGENIC RISK SCORES (PRS) DERIVED FROM GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDIES (GWAS) HAVE SHOWN PROMISE FOR POPULATION RISK STRATIFICATION, MOST EXISTING MODELS ARE BASED ON STATIC CASE-CONTROL OUTCOMES AND DO NOT EXPLICITLY MODEL THE TIMING OF DISEASE ONSET OR PROGRESSION. THIS LIMITS THEIR UTILITY FOR UNDERSTANDING DISEASE TRAJECTORIES AND INFORMING CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING. ADVANCING PRECISION MEDICINE REQUIRES MOVING BEYOND STATIC RISK PREDICTION TOWARD LONGITUDINAL MODELS THAT CAPTURE HOW GENETIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS JOINTLY INFLUENCE DISEASE PROGRESSION.   DURING THE K99 PHASE, I DEVELOPED GENOME-WIDE SURVIVAL STUDY (GWSS) FRAMEWORKS TO MODEL TIME-TO-EVENT (TTE) PHENOTYPES AND CONSTRUCTED PHENOME-WIDE TTE OUTCOMES IN LARGE-SCALE, MULTI-ANCESTRY BIOBANKS. I ESTABLISHED ANALYTICAL PIPELINES FOR CONSTRUCTING AND EVALUATING PRS FOR LONGITUDINAL OUTCOMES AND DEMONSTRATED THEIR REPRODUCIBILITY ACROSS MULTIPLE COHORTS. I ALSO DEVELOPED AND APPLIED GENE-BASED RARE VARIANT ASSOCIATION METHODS FOR TTE PHENOTYPES, DEMONSTRATING THE FEASIBILITY OF IDENTIFYING GENE-LEVEL CONTRIBUTIONS TO DISEASE ONSET, AND INITIATED HARMONIZATION OF SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL DATA ACROSS BIOBANKS THROUGH COLLABORATIVE EFFORTS. THE R00 PHASE WILL BUILD ON THIS FOUNDATION TO DEVELOP INTEGRATED MODELS OF DISEASE PROGRESSION THAT JOINTLY INCORPORATE COMMON AND RARE GENETIC VARIATION WITH SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS. SPECIFICALLY, THIS PROJECT WILL: (1) EXTEND GWSS-DERIVED PRS TO MODEL DISEASE ONSET AND PROGRESSION ACROSS MULTIPLE GENETIC ANCESTRY GROUPS; (2) INCORPORATE GENE-LEVEL RARE VARIANT SIGNALS INTO POLYGENIC PREDICTION MODELS TO CAPTURE GENETIC EFFECTS ACROSS THE ALLELE-FREQUENCY SPECTRUM; AND (3) INTEGRATE SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS WITH GENETIC PREDICTORS USING SCALABLE REPRESENTATIONS OF EXPOSURE DATA TO MODEL CONTEXT-DEPENDENT DISEASE RISK. THESE APPROACHES WILL BE EVALUATED ACROSS MULTIPLE LARGE BIOBANKS TO ASSESS PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE, GENERALIZABILITY, AND CLINICAL RELEVANCE.  THIS WORK WILL ADVANCE PRECISION MEDICINE BY ENABLING MORE ACCURATE, INTERPRETABLE, AND GENERALIZABLE PREDICTION OF DISEASE PROGRESSION. BY INTEGRATING GENETIC AND SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH WITHIN A UNIFIED FRAMEWORK, THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO HOW DISEASE TRAJECTORIES ARE SHAPED ACROSS POPULATIONS AND SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF MORE TARGETED PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION STRATEGIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF ALCOHOL-ASSOCIATED LIVER DISEASE IN PRIMARY CARE USING A BRIEF ALCOHOL SCREENING QUESTIONNAIRE - SUMMARY MORTALITY DUE TO LIVER DISEASE IS INCREASING IN THE US. ALCOHOL-ASSOCIATED LIVER DISEASE (ALD) ACCOUNTS FOR MOST LIVER-RELATED DEATHS, AND THE AMOUNT OF ALCOHOL USE IS THE STRONGEST PREDICTOR OF MAJOR ADVERSE LIVER OUTCOMES (MALOS): LIVER CIRRHOSIS, DECOMPENSATED CIRRHOSIS, LIVER CANCER, TRANSPLANT, OR DEATH. ALCOHOL USE ALSO INTERACTS WITH METABOLIC FACTORS, SUCH AS DIABETES AND OBESITY, TO INCREASE MALOS. REDUCING DRINKING IMPROVES LIVER DISEASE OUTCOMES, AND EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE DRINKING CAN BE DELIVERED IN PRIMARY CARE. HOWEVER, 89% OF ALD IS DIAGNOSED AFTER COMPLICATIONS DEVELOP WHEN PROGNOSIS IS POOR. REDUCING ALD MORTALITY WILL REQUIRE EARLY IDENTIFICATION. TRANSIENT ELASTOGRAPHY, AN IMAGING TEST, PROVIDES A PRESUMPTIVE DIAGNOSIS OF CIRRHOSIS. DUE TO COST, TRANSIENT ELASTOGRAPHY IS TYPICALLY OFFERED TO SELECTED PATIENTS AT INCREASED RISK. U.S. GUIDELINES RECOMMEND FIBROSIS-4 INDEX (FIB-4), CALCULATED FROM BLOOD TESTS, TO IDENTIFY PATIENTS AT INCREASED RISK, BUT FIB-4 MISSES ABOUT HALF OF PRIMARY CARE PATIENTS WHO GO ON TO DEVELOP MALOS. CURRENT GUIDELINES FOR SCREENING FOR LIVER DISEASE DO NOT INCLUDE ALCOHOL USE. THE AUDIT-C ALCOHOL SCREENING QUESTIONNAIRE IS A WIDELY USED, VALIDATED, SCALED MEASURE OF ALCOHOL USE WITH SCORES 0-12. WIDESPREAD SCREENING WITH THE AUDIT-C IN PRIMARY CARE PRACTICES COULD BE READILY INCORPORATED INTO SCREENING FOR LIVER DISEASE, BUT TO DATE, NO RESEARCH HAS EVALUATED THIS APPROACH. OBJECTIVE. THE PROPOSED STUDY SEEKS TO DETERMINE HOW ROUTINE PRIMARY CARE AUDIT-C ALCOHOL SCREENING CAN BE USED TO EFFICIENTLY IDENTIFY PATIENTS AT-RISK FOR ALD. AIM 1 RECRUITS A SAMPLE OF 1,300 PATIENTS TO DETERMINE THE PREVALENCE OF CURRENT LIVER DISEASE BASED ON TRANSIENT ELASTOGRAPHY ACROSS ALL AUDIT-C SCORES. AIM 2 USES EXISTING DATA TO DETERMINE THE INCIDENCE OF MALOS OVER 11 YEARS FOLLOW-UP ACROSS AUDIT-C SCORES IN OVER 700,000 PRIMARY CARE PATIENTS. AIMS 1-2 WILL PROVIDE DATA TO ASSESS RISKS OVERALL AND HETEROGENEITY ACROSS IMPORTANT PATIENT SUB-GROUPS (E.G., AGE, SEX, DIABETES, OBESITY), TO ALLOW CLINICIANS TO EASILY IDENTIFY HIGH RISK PATIENTS BY AUDIT-C ALONE. THEY CAN THEN OFFER TRANSIENT ELASTOGRAPHY AND PROVIDE TREATMENTS TO DECREASE DRINKING AND OTHER RISK FACTORS. AIM 3 USES MACHINE LEARNING TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE TWO CLINICAL TOOLS THAT COMBINE THE AUDIT-C WITH OTHER CLINICAL FACTORS FOR MORE REFINED RISK STRATIFICATION. WE WILL DEVELOP A SIMPLE CALCULATOR FOR USE BY FRONTLINE CLINICIANS THAT COMBINES THE AUDIT-C WITH FIB-4 (AIM 3A), AND A MORE PRECISE AUTOMATED ALGORITHM COMBINING ALL AUDIT-C SCORES AND OTHER RISK FACTORS FROM ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD DATA (AIM 3B). BOTH TOOLS DEVELOPED IN AIM 3 CAN BE RAPIDLY INTEGRATED INTO PRIMARY CARE BY CLINICIANS AND HEALTH SYSTEMS. PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT. THE PROPOSED STUDY PROVIDES CRITICALLY NEEDED INFORMATION AND TWO PRACTICAL TOOLS EASILY INTEGRATED INTO CARE TO IDENTIFY EARLY LIVER DISEASE SO CLINICIANS CAN SUPPORT PATIENTS IN DECREASING DRINKING AND MODIFYING OTHER RISK FACTORS TO IMPROVE OUTCOMES. IF EVEN 10% OF PATIENTS WITH LIVER DISEASE WERE IDENTIFIED AND RISK FACTORS MODIFIED, 5,000 UNNECESSARY LIVER-RELATED DEATHS COULD BE AVOIDED EACH YEAR IN THE U.S. ALONE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NEUROCOMPUTATIONAL AND ECOLOGICAL ASSESSMENTS OF THE MUTUAL INFLUENCE BETWEEN ALCOHOL CRAVING AND DECISION-MAKING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT BINGE AND HEAVING DRINKING CONTRIBUTE TO A MULTITUDE OF PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUES, INCLUDING LIVER AND HEART DISEASES, CANCER, ALCOHOL USE DISORDER, AND OTHER SUBSTANCE USE AND PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS. CRAVING AND MALADAPTIVE DECISION-MAKING ARE TWO CENTRAL INTERACTING ELEMENTS OF HEAVY/BINGE DRINKING. ABERRANT DECISION-MAKING, WHICH IS DIRECTLY ASSOCIATED WITH BEHAVIORS SUCH AS CONTINUING TO DRINK DESPITE OF NEGATIVE CONSEQUENCES, IS TYPICALLY OPERATIONALIZED VIA REWARD-BASED DECISION-MAKING PARADIGMS AND TIED TO NEURAL ACTIVITIES IN THE MESOLIMBIC CIRCUIT. ALCOHOL CRAVING, ON THE OTHER HAND, REPRESENTS THE SUBJECTIVE URGE TO CONSUME ALCOHOL, CAN PERSIST EVEN AFTER LONG PERIODS OF ABSTINENCE, AND IS MUCH HARDER TO TREAT COMPARED TO DRINKING PER SE. IN LABORATORY STUDIES, CRAVING IS OFTEN EXAMINED WITH CUE REACTIVITY PARADIGMS AND MAY INVOLVE BOTH MESOLIMBIC (STRIATAL-PREFRONTAL) AND INSULA-CINGULATE CIRCUITS; YET IT IS STILL DEBATABLE HOW CUE REACTIVITY PARADIGMS RELATE TO REAL-LIFE CRAVINGS. THESE TWO LITERATURES HAVE LARGELY REMAINED IN SILO, LEAVING THE MECHANISMS SUBSERVING THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN ALCOHOL CRAVING AND DECISION-MAKING ELUSIVE. FURTHERMORE, ALCOHOL CRAVING AND REWARD BEHAVIORS (AND THEIR INTERACTIONS) ARE HIGHLY DYNAMIC IN THE REAL-WORLD, YET THE FIELD CURRENTLY LACKS COMPUTATIONAL MODELS THAT CAN ACCOUNT FOR SUCH COMPLEX NON-LINEAR DYNAMICS. THE CURRENT PROPOSAL AIMS TO ADDRESS THESE KNOWLEDGE GAPS BY EXAMINING THE NEURO-COMPUTATIONAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE BIDIRECTIONAL INTERACTIONS BETWEEN ALCOHOL CRAVING AND DECISION-MAKING AND THEIR UTILITY IN PREDICTING REAL-LIFE ALCOHOL CRAVING AND CONSUMPTION IN HEAVY/BINGE DRINKERS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL IDENTIFY THE COMPUTATIONAL ALGORITHMS UNDERLYING THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN ALCOHOL CRAVING AND ADDICTIVE DECISION-MAKING IN BINGE/HEAVY DRINKERS. WE WILL DEPLOY A NOVEL COMPUTATIONAL TASK AND MODEL TO QUANTIFY THE BIDIRECTIONAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN ALCOHOL CRAVING AND DECISION- MAKING (N=260 TOTAL; N=130 FOR EACH BINGE/HEAVY (BH) DRINKING AND NON-BINGE CONTROL (NC) GROUP). IN AIM 2, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE NEURAL CIRCUITRY MECHANISMS SUBSERVING ALCOHOL CRAVING-CHOICE INTERACTION BY MODELING TASK- BASED FUNCTIONAL MRI DATA IN AN IN-PERSON SAMPLE OF BH AND NC PARTICIPANTS (N=130 TOTAL) USING BOTH GRAPH- THEORETIC NETWORK ANALYSIS AND BIOPHYSICAL MODELING. IN AIM 3, WE WILL EXAMINE INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES IN REAL- WORLD ALCOHOL CRAVING AND DRINKING FOR 12 WEEKS AND TIE THESE ECOLOGICAL MEASURES WITH NEUROCOMPUTATIONAL METRICS OF CRAVING-CHOICE RELATIONSHIPS. COLLECTIVELY, FINDINGS FROM THIS PROJECT COULD PROVIDE A FORMAL, NEURO- COMPUTATIONAL ACCOUNT FOR THE “SPIRAL OF ADDICTION”, THE RESULT OF A MUTUALLY REINFORCING RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN ALCOHOL CRAVING AND DECISION-MAKING THAT CAN BE GENERALIZED TO A WIDE RANGE OF RISKY SUBSTANCE USE BEHAVIORS. FURTHERMORE, THIS STUDY COULD ALSO INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF SCALABLE DIGITAL HEALTH TOOLS FOR OBJECTIVELY TRACKING AND PREDICTING REAL-LIFE ALCOHOL CRAVING AND DRINKING PATTERNS. AS SUCH, THE PROPOSED STUDY COULD POTENTIALLY BREAK NEW GROUND FOR BOTH BASIC AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH ON ALCOHOL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF A HOMELESSNESS PREVENTION AND RAPID REHOUSING INITIATIVE FOR HOUSING UNSTABLE VETERANS ON ALCOHOL-RELATED HARMS: ANALYSIS OF LINKED HOUSING PROGRAM AND HEALTH CARE DATA - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT PERSONS WHO LACK STABLE HOUSING EXPERIENCE A DISPROPORTIONATE BURDEN OF ALCOHOL USE DISORDER (AUD). THREE IN FIVE (60%) HOMELESS ADULTS HAVE A HISTORY OF AUD, LEADING TO ELEVATED RATES OF ALCOHOL-RELATED HARMS (E.G., POISONING AND WITHDRAWAL, ALCOHOL-RELATED INJURY, CHRONIC DISEASE, AND PREMATURE MORTALITY). THE LACK OF STABLE HOUSING NEGATIVELY IMPACTS ALCOHOL-RELATED OUTCOMES PRIMARILY BY CAUSING HIGHER STRESS, RUPTURING CONNECTIONS TO HEALTH-PROMOTING SOCIAL SUPPORTS, INCREASING EXPOSURE TO RISKY ENVIRONMENTS, AND CREATING BARRIERS TO ACCESSING BOTH PREVENTATIVE CARE AND AUD TREATMENT. LITTLE IS KNOWN REGARDING WHETHER HOUSING INTERVENTIONS COULD IMPROVE ALCOHOL USE AND RELATED OUTCOMES. THE SUPPORTIVE SERVICES FOR VETERAN FAMILIES (SSVF) PROGRAM IS THE LARGEST PROGRAM TO PREVENT AND END HOMELESSNESS AMONG VETERANS IN THE US. SSVF IS A PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN THE DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS (VA) AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS (REFERRED TO AS GRANTEES). IN THIS PARTNERSHIP, GRANTEES PROVIDE TEMPORARY FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE AND OTHER SUPPORT SERVICES TO VETERANS WHO ARE EITHER CURRENTLY HOMELESS OR FACING IMMINENT RISK OF HOMELESSNESS. IN FY 2023, VA PROVIDED $712 MILLION IN FUNDING TO 249 GRANTEES COVERING EVERY STATE IN THE US WHO DELIVERED SERVICES TO ROUGHLY 80,000 VETERANS NATIONWIDE. OUR PREVIOUS EFFORTS HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT SSVF HAS A POSITIVE IMPACT ON VETERAN HOUSING, HEALTHCARE COSTS, AND ALL- CAUSE MORTALITY OUTCOMES. HOWEVER, THE IMPACTS OF SSVF ON ALCOHOL USE AND ALCOHOL-RELATED TREATMENT AND OUTCOMES HAVE NOT BEEN ESTABLISHED. IN THIS STUDY, OUR TEAM WILL USE A UNIQUE, LONGITUDINAL, PERSON-LEVEL DATASET THAT LINKS BOTH DATA ON PARTICIPATION IN SSVF AND VETERAN ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD DATA FOR MORE THAN A DECADE ALONG WITH INNOVATIVE METHODOLOGICAL APPROACHES INCLUDING TARGET TRIAL EMULATION AND NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF THE SSVF PROGRAM ON UNHEALTHY ALCOHOL CONSUMPTION AMONG VETERANS WITH AND WITHOUT A HISTORY OF UNHEALTHY ALCOHOL USE. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ASSESS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN SSVF AND ALCOHOL-RELATED ADVERSE OUTCOMES—INCLUDING TRAUMATIC INJURY, ALCOHOL POISONING, CIRRHOSIS, SUICIDAL IDEATION, AND MORTALITY—AMONG VETERANS WITH A DIAGNOSIS OF ALCOHOL USE DISORDER. IN AIM 3, WE WILL EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF SSVF ON INITIATION OF MEDICATIONS FOR ALCOHOL USE DISORDER (MAUD) AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INTERVENTIONS, AS WELL AS RETENTION ON MAUD. OUR FINDINGS WILL PROVIDE ACTIONABLE INFORMATION TO TAILOR HOMELESSNESS PREVENTION AND RAPID REHOUSING INTERVENTIONS—BOTH WITHIN THE VA AND IN THE COMMUNITY-BASED HOMELESS ASSISTANCE SYSTEM—TO MITIGATE ALCOHOL-RELATED HARMS AMONG PERSONS WITH UNSTABLE HOUSING.

description: THE HONORING AND EXAMINING ALCOHOL RECOVERY (HEAR) STUDY: A LONGITUDINAL EXAMINATION OF RECOVERY CAPITAL AND ITS ASSOCIATION WITH RECOVERY OUTCOMES - PROJECT SUMMARY THE HONORING AND EXAMINING ALCOHOL RECOVERY (HEAR) STUDY WILL ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF RECOVERY CAPITAL (RC) AND ITS RELATIONSHIP TO NIAAA-DEFINED RECOVERY, USING LONGITUDINAL METHODS. RELEASED IN 2022, NIAAA’S OPERATIONAL DEFINITION OF RECOVERY IS BASED ON REMISSION OF DSM-5 ALCOHOL USE DISORDER SYMPTOMS AND CESSATION OF HEAVY DRINKING. ALTHOUGH RC—THE SOCIAL, PHYSICAL, HUMAN, AND CULTURAL RESOURCES THAT FACILITATE SUBSTANCE USE PROBLEM RESOLUTION—IS CONCEPTUALLY ALIGNED WITH THIS DEFINITION, IT IS NOT KNOWN IF RC PREDICTS NIAAA-DEFINED RECOVERY, AND IF AND HOW THIS RELATIONSHIP MIGHT VARY FOR PARTICIPANTS WITH DIFFERENT INCOME LEVELS. THE HEAR STUDY WILL ADDRESS THIS BY USING THE MULTIDIMENSIONAL INVENTORY OF RECOVERY CAPITAL (MIRC) TOOL THAT OUR TEAM DEVELOPED IN A PREVIOUS PROJECT TO MEASURE RC AND ITS ASSOCIATION WITH NIAAA-DEFINED RECOVERY OVER TIME. WORKING WITH KNOWLEDGEPANEL, A PROBABILITY-BASED ONLINE PANEL, WE WILL RECRUIT A SAMPLE OF U.S. ADULTS WHO REPORT RESOLVING AN ALCOHOL PROBLEM 3-11 MONTHS AGO (N=300; 50% LOWER-INCOME). PARTICIPANTS WILL COMPLETE ONLINE SURVEYS AT BASELINE AND WHEN THEY REACH 12, 18, AND 24 MONTHS SINCE RESOLVING THEIR ALCOHOL PROBLEM. IN AIM 1, WE WILL TEST 3 HYPOTHESES TO UNDERSTAND BETWEEN-PERSON DIFFERENCES AND WITHIN-PERSON CHANGE IN RC IN EARLY RECOVERY: H1.1. TOTAL RC WILL VARY BETWEEN-PERSONS AND WITHIN- PERSONS OVER TIME. ON AVERAGE, TOTAL RC WILL INCREASE OVER THE FIRST 3-24 MONTHS OF RECOVERY WITHIN INDIVIDUALS, WITH SIGNIFICANT BETWEEN-PERSON DIFFERENCES; H1.2. SOCIAL AND PHYSICAL RC WILL EXHIBIT GREATER WITHIN-PERSON GROWTH OVER THE FIRST 3-24 MONTHS OF RECOVERY THAN HUMAN AND CULTURAL RC ON AVERAGE, WITH SIGNIFICANT BETWEEN-PERSON VARIABILITY; AND H1.3. INCOME WILL BE LINKED TO RC SUCH THAT LOWER-INCOME INDIVIDUALS WILL EXHIBIT LOWER OVERALL RC BETWEEN-PERSONS AND ATTENUATED RC GROWTH WITHIN-PERSONS OVER TIME. IN AIM 2, WE WILL TEST 3 HYPOTHESES EXAMINING THE BETWEEN- AND WITHIN-PERSON ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN RC AND NIAAA-DEFINED RECOVERY OVER TIME: H2.1. AT THE BETWEEN-PERSON LEVEL, INDIVIDUALS WITH HIGHER LEVELS OF TOTAL RC ON AVERAGE WILL HAVE A GREATER LIKELIHOOD OF ACHIEVING NIAAA-DEFINED RECOVERY AT EACH TIMEPOINT. THE STRENGTH OF THESE ASSOCIATIONS WILL BE SIMILAR ACROSS RC SUBSCALES; H2.2. AT THE WITHIN-PERSON LEVEL, INDIVIDUALS WILL HAVE GREATER LIKELIHOOD OF ACHIEVING NIAAA-DEFINED RECOVERY AT TIME POINTS WHEN THEIR RC SCORES ARE GREATER THAN THEIR PERSONAL AVERAGE. WE EXPECT THIS POSITIVE WITHIN-PERSON ASSOCIATION TO BECOME STRONGER OVER TIME. THE STRENGTH OF THESE ASSOCIATIONS WILL BE SIMILAR ACROSS RC SUBSCALES; AND H2.3. BETWEEN-PERSON DIFFERENCES IN INCOME WILL MODERATE THE WITHIN-PERSON ASSOCIATION BETWEEN RC AND NIAAA RECOVERY, SUCH THAT HIGHER RC WILL BE LESS STRONGLY LINKED TO ACHIEVING NIAAA-DEFINED RECOVERY AMONG LOWER-INCOME INDIVIDUALS RELATIVE TO MIDDLE/HIGH-INCOME INDIVIDUALS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL ESTABLISH MIRC BENCHMARK SCORES THAT PREDICT THE LIKELIHOOD OF ACHIEVING NIAAA RECOVERY. THESE FINDINGS WILL ADDRESS CRITICAL RESEARCH GAPS ON RC AND WILL INFORM PRACTICE BY PROVIDING BENCHMARK MIRC SCORES THAT PRACTITIONERS CAN USE TO TARGET RESOURCES AND INTERVENTIONS.

description: BIOMARKERS TO TRACK EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS THAT DELAY DEMENTIA ONSET IN PARTICIPANTS OF THE "RISK REDUCTION FOR ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (RRAD)" TRIAL - PROJECT SUMMARY IT IS OFTEN HARD TO DISTINGUISH BETWEEN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND AD-RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRDS), INCLUDING VASCULAR CONTRIBUTIONS TO COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA (VCID), DUE TO A SIMILAR CLINICAL PRESENTATION OF MEMORY LOSS AND THE PRESENCE OF CARDIOVASCULAR (CV) RISK FACTORS (E.G. HYPERTENSION, DYSLIPIDEMIA). WHILE CV RISK FACTORS HAVE AVAILABLE DRUG THERAPIES, INCREASED  PHYSICAL ACTIVITY ALSO SIGNIFICANTLY LOWERS THESE CO-MORBIDITIES. UNFORTUNATELY, EVIDENCE LINKING CV AND EXERCISE INTERVENTIONS TO THE PREVENTION OF COGNITIVE DECLINE IS INCONCLUSIVE, NOR ARE  BIOMARKERS AVAILABLE TO DETERMINE THE EFFICACY OF PRE-DEMENTIA LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS. THIS ANCILLARY R01 WILL USE PLASMA-BASED BIOMARKERS AND NEUROIMAGING FROM SUBJECTS ENROLLED IN OUR  NIH-FUNDED TRIAL “RISK REDUCTION FOR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (RRAD; NCT02913664).” THIS PHASE II RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL WILL DETERMINE THE INDEPENDENT AND COMBINED EFFECTS OF INTENSIVE PHARMACOLOGICAL REDUCTION OF VASCULAR RISK FACTORS (IRVR; I.E. BLOOD PRESSURE, LIPIDS) AND AEROBIC EXERCISE (EX) ON COGNITIVE FUNCTION. PARTICIPANTS WERE RANDOMIZED INTO 2-YEAR INTERVENTIONS (IRVR, EX, IRVR+EX, AND A CONTROL ARM OF STANDARD CARE (SC)) WITH PLASMA AND NEUROIMAGING COLLECTED AT BASELINE AND YEARLY. OF THE 513  INITIAL RRAD SUBJECTS (63% FEMALES; 34% AGED 71-85; 13% AFRICAN-AMERICAN; 4% LATINO), 89% (458 SUBJECTS) HAVE LONGITUDINAL SERUM AND NEUROIMAGING BIOMARKERS AVAILABLE FOR LINEAR MIXED-MODELS ANALYSES. BANKED LONGITUDINAL RRAD PLASMA SAMPLES WILL BE USED TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT 1) BENCHMARK AD, 2) BENCHMARK VCID, AND/OR 3) NOVEL CIRCULATING BRAIN-DERIVED BIOMARKERS CAN BE MODULATED BY POSITIVE LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS. AIM 1 WILL TEST IF THE BENCHMARK AD BIOMARKERS AΒ42/AΒ40 RATIO WILL INCREASE, WHILE PTAU181 AND PTAU 231 WILL DECREASE, THE GREATEST WITH IRVR+EX. HIGHER RATIOS AND LOWER TAU WILL BE ASSOCIATED WITH OUR SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES OF PRESERVED HIPPOCAMPAL VOLUME (T1-WEIGHTED MRI). AIM 2 WILL TEST IF PRIMARY BENCHMARK VCID BIOMARKERS WILL REVEAL EFFECTS OF VASCULAR AND EXERCISE INTERVENTIONS ON CEREBROVASCULAR HEALTH. WE WILL TEST IF LOWER PATHOLOGIC PRO-ANGIOGENIC PROTEINS (I.E. VEGF-D, PLGF, BFGF) MEASURED LONGITUDINALLY DECREASE WITH INTERVENTION. LOWER EXPRESSION WILL COINCIDE WITH SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES OF INCREASED REGIONAL CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW (I.E. ARTERIAL SPIN LABELING, MRI) AND FEWER WHITE MATTER HYPERINTENSITIES (I.E. T2 FLAIR, MRI). AIM 3 WILL TEST IF VASCULAR AND EXERCISE INTERVENTIONS ALTER THE NEUROTROPHIC CARGO OF CIRCULATING NEURONAL-ENRICHED EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES (EVS). WE WILL TEST IRVR+EX LOWERS PRO- (I.E. UNCLEAVED) BRAIN-DERIVED NEUROTROPHIC FACTOR (BDNF) AND INCREASES MATURE BDNF IN NEURONAL-ENRICHED EVS. HIGHER BDNF WILL COINCIDE WITH THE SECONDARY OUTCOME OF PRESERVED DEFAULT-MODE NETWORK (DMN) CONNECTIVITY MEASURED BY RESTING-STATE FUNCTIONAL (RS-F)MRI. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT AD, VCID, AND EV BIOMARKERS NOT ONLY IDENTIFY INDIVIDUALS WITH HIGH RISK FOR AD/ADRDS BUT CAN ALSO TRACK EFFICACY OF INDEPENDENT AND COMBINED LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS THAT IMPROVE CEREBROVASCULAR HEALTH AND DELAY DEMENTIA ONSET IN SEDENTARY ADULTS.
