description: THE DEAR STUDY: DYAD ENGAGEMENT IN ALZHEIMER'S RESEARCH - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT THIS PROJECT WILL EVALUATE NOVEL, DIGITAL METHODS FOR RECRUITMENT, ENGAGEMENT, AND ASSESSMENT OF OLDER ADULTS AND THEIR STUDY PARTNERS (DYADS) IN THE BRAIN HEALTH REGISTRY (BHR), AN INTERNET-BASED COHORT TO FACILITATE ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE RELATED DEMENTIAS (AD/ADRD) RESEARCH AND TRIALS. AD/ADRD ARE AN IMMENSE AND GROWING PUBLIC HEALTH THREAT CAUSING DISABILITY AND DEATH IN MILLIONS OF OLDER ADULTS. THE BURDEN AND EXPENSE OF RECRUITMENT, SCREENING, AND LONGITUDINAL MONITORING OF COGNITION AND EVERYDAY FUNCTIONING IN TRIALS AND OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES SLOW PROGRESS. STUDY PARTNERS (SOMEONE WHO KNOWS THE PARTICIPANT WELL, E.G., A SPOUSE OR ADULT CHILD) ARE REQUIRED FOR AD STUDIES. THEY ARE AN EFFICIENT AND RELIABLE SOURCE OF INFORMATION ABOUT PARTICIPANTS’ DECLINE IN COGNITION AND EVERYDAY FUNCTIONING. THIS 5-YEAR, LONGITUDINAL, STUDY WILL EVALUATE STUDY PARTNER-FOCUSED RECRUITMENT, ENGAGEMENT, AND ASSESSMENT OF DYAD-REPORT OF SUBJECTIVE COGNITIVE DECLINE (SCD) IN THE BHR, AN INTERNETBASED DIGITAL COHORT. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE AND COHORT OF THE BHR STUDY PARTNER PORTAL, A SCALABLE TOOL FOR REMOTE, LONGITUDINAL COLLECTION OF DIGITAL DYAD-REPORT SCD. WE WILL WORK IN PARTNERSHIP WITH COMMUNITY SCIENCE PARTNERSHIP BOARDS TO ENSURE COMMUNITY ALIGNMENT AT ALL STUDY STAGES. WE WILL DEVELOP, DEPLOY, AND EVALUATE ENGAGEMENT STRATEGIES TAILORED TOWARDS REACHING THE STUDY PARTNERS OF OLDER ADULTS. WE WILL COLLECT DEMOGRAPHICS, DYAD-REPORT SCD, AND EXPOSOMIC FACTOR DATA (SOCIAL EXPOSURES AND ADVERSITY AT THE INDIVIDUAL AND SOCIETAL LEVEL). IN AIM 1, WE WILL RECRUIT 930 DYADS, INCLUDING DEMOGRAPHIC GROUPS WHO FACE AD/ADRD HEALTH DISPARITIES. WE WILL EVALUATE THE COMPARATIVE EFFECTIVENESS OF RECRUITMENT EFFORTS, INCLUDING MESSAGING TAILORED TOWARDS STUDY PARTNERS AND THOSE WITH MCI. WE WILL IDENTIFY PARTICIPANT CHARACTERISTICS (DEMOGRAPHIC, EXPOSOMIC, COGNITIVE) ASSOCIATED WITH RECRUITMENT AND ENGAGEMENT EFFECTIVENESS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL USE THE LONGITUDINAL DATA COLLECTED TO CHARACTERIZE DYAD-REPORT SCD. WE WILL ESTIMATE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN DYAD-REPORT SCD AND OBJECTIVE COGNITION AND DECLINE, AND EVALUATE THE ACCURACY OF DYAD-REPORT SCD TO IDENTIFY THOSE WITH MCI. IN AIM 3, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE CONTRIBUTIONS OF DEMOGRAPHICS, EXPOSOMIC FACTORS, DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, AND DYAD RELATIONSHIP TO DYAD-REPORT SCD. THROUGHOUT THE STUDY, BHR PARTICIPANTS AND STUDY PARTNERS WILL BE REFERRED TO COLLABORATOR STUDIES, PROVIDING A RESOURCE TO BROADLY FACILITATE RECRUITMENT INTO AD STUDIES. THE OVERALL IMPACT: THIS STUDY ADDRESSES THE NIA PRIORITY AREAS OF IMPROVED AD/ADRD RESEARCH RECRUITMENT AND DEVELOPMENT OF EARLY COGNITIVE ASSESSMENT TOOLS. RECRUITMENT AND ENGAGEMENT METHODS FOCUSED ON DYADS AND MCI CAN BE ADAPTED TO BROADLY IMPROVE RECRUITMENT FOR AD RESEARCH AND TRIALS. CHARACTERIZATION OF DYAD-REPORT SCD, INCLUDING CONTRIBUTIONS OF EXPOSOMIC AND OTHER KEY FACTORS, CAN INFORM USE OF SCD FOR SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, AND LONGITUDINAL MONITORING OF OLDER ADULTS FOR AD RISK IN FUTURE STUDIES AND TRIALS, AND IN CLINICAL CARE SETTINGS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPROVING POST-ACUTE CARE DELIVERY AND OUTCOMES FOR MEDICARE ADVANTAGE BENEFICIARIES - PROJECT SUMMARY MEDICARE ADVANTAGE (MA), THE PRIVATE INSURANCE PLAN ALTERNATIVE TO TRADITIONAL MEDICARE (TM), HAS BECOME THE DOMINANT FORM OF MEDICARE COVERAGE, ENROLLING 32.8 MILLION IN 2024 (54% OF TOTAL ENROLLMENT). MA PLANS ARE PAID USING A CAPITATED FIXED-PAYMENTS MODEL THAT CREATES STRONG INCENTIVES FOR MA PLANS TO REDUCE HEALTHCARE SPENDING. POST-ACUTE CARE (PAC) IS A MAJOR HEALTH SERVICE WHERE MA PLANS SPEND LESS ON COMPARED WITH TM. SOME STUDIES HAVE FOUND LOWER PAC UTILIZATION AMONG MA ENROLLEES WITHOUT CORRESPONDING DIFFERENCES IN HEALTH OUTCOMES. HOWEVER, THE RAPID GROWTH IN MA ENROLLMENT IN RECENT YEARS HAS RESULTED IN LARGE CHANGES IN THE MA POPULATION CASE-MIX AND IN GREATER MA MARKET PENETRATION THAT INCREASED THE LEVERAGE OF MA PLANS OVER PROVIDERS THAT QUESTION THE RELEVANCE OF PRIOR STUDIES BASED ON A DECADE OLD DATA TO INFORM MEDICAL CARE PROVIDERS AND PATIENTS. FURTHERMORE, PRIOR STUDIES DID NOT CORRECT FOR SIGNIFICANT SELECTION BIAS DUE TO SELECTIVE ENROLLMENT, AND HAVE ALSO VIEWED MA AS A UNIFORM PROGRAM, HOWEVER, THERE ARE IMPORTANT DIFFERENCES IN PLAN CHARACTERISTICS THAT CAN GREATLY INFLUENCE PAC REFERRALS AND OUTCOMES THAT NEED TO BE UNDERSTOOD. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO INFORM WAYS TO IMPROVE CARE DELIVER MODELS FOR AMERICANS IN NEED OF POST-ACUTE CARE. TO THAT EFFECT, WE WILL FOCUS ON MA AND TM BENEFICIARIES IN MARKETS WITH DIFFERENT LEVELS OF MA PENETRATION GROWTH DISCHARGED FROM HOSPITALS IN RECENT YEARS (2011-2027), WE PROPOSE A NOVEL APPROACH THAT LEVERAGES THE LARGE GROWTH OF MA IN THE LAST DECADE AS A QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL ENCOURAGEMENT DESIGN THAT ALLOWS FOR A MORE RIGOROUS ESTIMATION OF THE CAUSAL IMPACT OF MA VS. TM ON PAC USE AND PATIENT OUTCOMES. WE WILL EXAMINE THE IMPACT OF MA ON PAC BY PURSUING THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1: COMPARE HOW ENROLLMENT IN DIFFERENT MA VS TM MODELS OF CARE LEAD TO DIFFERENT PAC UTILIZATION OUTCOMES AFTER A HOSPITALIZATION; AIM 2: COMPARE THE PAC HEALTH OUTCOMES OF SIMILAR MA AND TM PATIENTS WITH VARIOUS CONDITIONS (STROKE, CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE, HIP FRACTURE, AND OTHERS); AND AIM 3: EXAMINE WHETHER PAC UTILIZATION AND OUTCOMES DIFFER SIGNIFICANTLY BY MA PLAN CHARACTERISTICS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOME OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO PROVIDE UPDATED CAUSAL INFERENCE ABOUT WHETHER MA IMPROVED PAC PATIENT OUTCOMES, AND TO UNDERSTAND WHAT PLAN CHARACTERISTICS HAD A STRONGER EFFECT, OVERALL AND FOR HIGH-NEED POPULATIONS. THIS RESEARCH WILL HELP TO INFORM HOW TO BEST IMPROVE POST-ACUTE CARE OUTCOMES FOR AMERICAN MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES AS CARE DELIVERY MODELS CONTINUE TO CHANGE WITH THE GROWTH OF MA.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES OF IPSC-DERIVED BRAIN ORGANOIDS AS THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE ACCUMULATION, AGGREGATION, AND DEPOSITION OF AMYLOID-Β (AΒ) AND TAU IN THE BRAIN ACCOMPANIED WITH NEURODEGENERATION ARE CENTRAL EVENTS IN THE PATHOGENESIS OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD). AD IS A PROGRESSIVE NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE, WHICH IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEMENTIA IN THE ELDERLY. WHEREAS THE SPATIAL PROGRESSION PATTERN OF AΒ AND TAU PATHOLOGIES DIFFERS IN THE BRAINS, AΒ AND TAU LEAD TO NEURODEGENERATION IN A SYNERGIC MANNER DURING THE PROGRESSION OF AD. THEREFORE, TO DETERMINE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE COMPLEX AD PATHOGENESIS AND IDENTIFY POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS, THE GREATER UNDERSTANDING OF CROSS-TALK BETWEEN AΒ AND TAU IN THE DISEASE DEVELOPMENT AND PROGRESSION MIGHT BE CRITICAL. IN PARTICULAR, EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES (EVS) PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN MAINTAINING TISSUE HOMEOSTASIS, BY MODULATING IMMUNE SYSTEM, SENESCENCE, PROLIFERATION AND DIFFERENTIATION IN VARIOUS BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT TAU, AΒ, AND EVS INTERACTIVELY TRIGGER THE PATHOGENIC CASCADES FOR NEURODEGENERATION IN AD. FURTHERMORE, SUSCEPTIBLE LOCI FOR LATE-ONSET AD INCLUDING APOE PREDOMINANTLY EXPRESS IN MICROGLIA, WHICH CAUSATIVELY OR CONSEQUENTLY PARTICIPATE IN THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS IN THE DISEASE. THUS, IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE WILL COMPREHENSIVELY ADDRESS TAU- AND AΒ-RELATED PHENOTYPES USING INNOVATIVE INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELL (IPSC)-DERIVED 3-D MODELS COMPOSED OF DORSAL/VENTRAL BRAIN ORGANOIDS AND MICROGLIA AS WELL AS MOUSE MODELS, AND EVALUATE THE CONTRIBUTIONS AND THE THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS OF EVS TO THE PATHOGENIC PHENOTYPES THROUGH PROTEOMICS AND MIRNA PROFILING. THE COMBINATION OF HUMAN IPSC ORGANOID TECHNOLOGY, EV ENGINEERING, AND ANIMAL MODELS WITH TARGETED AND NON-TARGETED APPROACHES SHOULD ALLOW US TO BOTH TEST HYPOTHESES AND GENERATE POTENTIAL THERAPEUTICS IN OUR COLLECTIVE EFFORTS TO ADDRESS THE SYNERGIC ROLES OF TAU AND AΒ IN NEURODEGENERATION, AND INVOLVEMENTS OF MICROGLIA AND EVS IN THE PATHOGENIC PATHWAYS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL EXAMINE TAU- AND AΒ-RELATED PHENOTYPES IN IPSC-DERIVED BRAIN ORGANOIDS. WE WILL DEFINE HOW GENETIC BACKGROUNDS IN MICROGLIA IMPACT TAU- AND AΒ-RELATED PHENOTYPES IN THE 3-D ORGANOID AD MODELS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL EXAMINE THE CONTRIBUTIONS OF EVS TO THE PATHOGENIC PHENOTYPES IN THE 3-D ORGANOID MODELS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL ENGINEER EVS FROM THE IPSC-DERIVED ORGANOIDS AND REVEAL THE THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS OF EVS IN MOUSE AD MODELS. COLLECTIVELY, THESE STUDIES ENABLE US REFINING HOW AΒ AND TAU LEAD TO NEURODEGENERATION, WHICH IS HIGHLY SIGNIFICANT IN DEVELOPING NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR AD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: RESCUE OF SYNAPTIC LOSS AND PATHOLOGY IN ALZHEIMER'S MOUSE MODEL BY ENHANCING MET RECEPTOR TYROSINE KINASE SIGNALING - PROJECT SUMMARY ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS AN AGE-ASSOCIATED NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY Β-AMYLOID PLAQUES, TAU NEUROFIBRILLARY TANGLES, AND PROGRESSIVE COGNITIVE DECLINE. AMONG THE EARLIEST AND MOST PREDICTIVE FEATURES OF AD IS SYNAPSE LOSS, WHICH CORRELATES MORE STRONGLY WITH COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT THAN AMYLOID OR TAU PATHOLOGY ALONE. RECENT CLINICAL STUDIES HAVE REPORTED SIGNIFICANT REDUCTIONS OF MET RECEPTOR TYROSINE KINASE IN THE AD BRAIN. MET IS HIGHLY EXPRESSED IN EXCITATORY NEURONS DURING DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTIONS IN THE ADULT BRAIN AS A SYNAPTIC SIGNALING MOLECULE. ACTIVATION OF MET BY ITS SOLE LIGAND, HEPATOCYTE GROWTH FACTOR (HGF), TRIGGERS A PLEIOTROPIC SIGNALING CASCADE WITH NEUROTROPHIC AND NEUROPROTECTIVE EFFECTS ACROSS VARIOUS NEURODEGENERATIVE MODELS. THIS PROPOSAL TESTS THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT SYNAPTIC DEGENERATION AND CIRCUIT DYSFUNCTION IN AD CAN BE MITIGATED BY REACTIVATING MET SIGNALING IN THE ADULT BRAIN. OUR RECENT WORK HAS SHOWN THAT MET PROMOTES SYNAPTOGENESIS, REFINES CORTICAL CONNECTIVITY, AND REGULATES THE MATURATION OF EXCITATORY SYNAPSES. PRELIMINARY DATA USING A NOVEL HUMANIZED MET CONDITIONAL KNOCK-IN (HMETCKI) MOUSE LINE DEMONSTRATE THAT MET ACTIVATION IN ADULT CORTICAL CIRCUITS INDUCES NEW FUNCTIONAL SYNAPSES, ENHANCES HIPPOCAMPAL SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY, AND IMPROVES LEARNING AND MEMORY. SINGLE-NUCLEUS RNA SEQUENCING IN PRE- SYMPTOMATIC 5XFAD MICE REVEALED CELL-TYPE-SPECIFIC EXPRESSION OF MET IN EXCITATORY NEURONS AND HGF IN ASTROCYTES, HIGHLIGHTING A POTENTIAL GLIA-NEURON SIGNALING AXIS DISRUPTED IN EARLY AD PATHOLOGY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT RESTORING MET SIGNALING IN AD MOUSE MODELS WILL REVERSE MOLECULAR AND PATHOLOGICAL SYNAPSE LOSS, RESTORE CORTICAL CIRCUIT CONNECTIVITY, AND IMPROVE COGNITIVE FUNCTION. TO TEST THIS, WE PROPOSE THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER ENHANCING MET SIGNALING MITIGATES MOLECULAR, TRANSCRIPTOMIC, AND PATHOLOGICAL CHANGES IN 5XFAD AND PS19 MICE AT BOTH PRE- AND POST-SYMPTOMATIC STAGES. AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE WHETHER HMET ACTIVATION RESTORES SYNAPTIC FUNCTION AND CORTICAL CIRCUIT CONNECTIVITY IN AFFECTED BRAIN REGIONS. AIM 3 WILL ASSESS WHETHER MET SIGNALING IMPROVES SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY AND RESCUES DEFICITS IN LEARNING, MEMORY, AND COGNITIVE FUNCTION IN AD MODELS. IMPACT: COMPLETION OF THESE STUDIES WILL REVEAL WHETHER ENHANCING AN ENDOGENOUS NEUROTROPHIC SIGNALING PATHWAY CAN REGENERATE SYNAPSES AND CIRCUITS IN THE DISEASED BRAIN. THIS WORK MAY UNCOVER NOVEL, DISEASE-MODIFYING MECHANISMS AND THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR TREATING AD AND RELATED NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS.

description: BURDEN OF CHRONIC LATENT INFECTIONS AND ADRD RISK IN TWO IMMUNOLOGICAL WORLDS - HOW EXPOSURE TO PATHOGENS MIGHT RESHAPE THE IMMUNE SYSTEM AND THEREBY INFLUENCE RISK FOR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DISEASES (ADRD) IS NOT YET UNDERSTOOD BUT IS INCREASINGLY THOUGHT TO BE CRUCIAL IN ADRD ETIOLOGY AND THEREFORE A MAJOR ACTIONABLE TARGET FOR PREVENTION AND TREATMENT. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT PATHOGEN EXPOSURE HISTORY, PARTICULARLY BURDEN OF CHRONIC LATENT INFECTIONS, SHAPES RISK FOR ADRD. HOWEVER, DIFFERENT TYPES OF PATHOGENS MAY INTERACT WITH EACH OTHER, AND WE FURTHER HYPOTHESIZE, ALONG THE LINES OF THE HYGIENE HYPOTHESIS, THAT CERTAIN HELMINTH INFECTIONS ATTENUATE THE RISKS OF OTHER CHRONIC LATENT INFECTIONS FOR ADRD.  IN ORDER TO TEST THESE HYPOTHESES, WE HAVE CHOSEN TWO HUMAN POPULATIONS FROM ENVIRONMENTS AS DIFFERENT AS POSSIBLE. THE TSIMANE HEALTH AND LIFE HISTORY PROJECT (THLHP) STUDIES THE TSIMANE, AN INDIGENOUS, SUBSISTENCE POPULATION IN THE BOLIVIAN AMAZON WITH HIGH PATHOGEN EXPOSURE, INCLUDING HIGH HELMINTH PREVALENCE. THE BERLIN AGING STUDY-II (BASE-II) STUDIES MOSTLY OLDER ADULTS IN AND AROUND BERLIN. BOTH HAVE DETAILED LONGITUDINAL DATA ON MULTIPLE DOMAINS OF COGNITIVE FUNCTION AS WELL AS BRAIN IMAGING ALLOWING US TO CALCULATE CHANGES IN BRAIN VOLUME OVER TIME. WE WILL SUPPLEMENT THESE EXISTING DATA WITH (A) STATE-OF-THE-ART BLOOD BIOMARKERS OF ADRD AND (B) EMERGING PATHOGENOMICS TECHNOLOGY (VIRSCAN) TO SIMULTANEOUSLY QUANTIFY ANTIBODIES TO TENS OF THOUSANDS OF VIRAL PROTEINS FROM THOUSANDS OF VIRAL STRAINS AS WELL AS FROM NON-VIRAL PATHOGENS. THIS WILL ALLOW US, FOR THE FIRST TIME, TO ASSESS HOW INFECTION HISTORY INFLUENCES ADRD RISK AND COGNITIVE TRAJECTORIES.  SPECIFICALLY, IN AIM 1, WE WILL COMPARE BASE-II AND THLHP FOR OVERALL INFECTION BURDEN, CHRONIC INFECTION BURDEN, AND PREVALENCE OF SPECIFIC PATHOGEN INFECTIONS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ASSESS WHETHER THESE INFECTION HISTORIES PREDICT CURRENT LEVELS OF ADRD BIOMARKERS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL ASSESS WHETHER THE INFECTION HISTORIES PREDICT SUBSEQUENT TRAJECTORIES OF COGNITIVE FUNCTION OR BRAIN VOLUME, AND WHETHER ANY ASSOCIATIONS ARE MEDIATED BY ADRD BIOMARKERS. THROUGHOUT, WE WILL TEST FOR EFFECT MODIFICATION BY HELMINTH BURDEN IN THLHP, AND FOR INDICES OF OVERALL INFECTION BURDEN TO HELMINTH BURDEN.  TOGETHER, THESE RESULTS WILL GENERATE THE FIRST BROAD TEST OF THE INFECTIOUS ORIGINS OF ADRD, IDENTIFYING INFECTIONS OR CLASSES OF INFECTIONS THAT INCREASE ADRD RISK OR PROVIDING KEY EVIDENCE AGAINST THE HYPOTHESIS. THE INABILITY TO QUANTIFY INFECTION HISTORY BROADLY WAS PREVIOUSLY A BARRIER TO THIS KIND OF EPIDEMIOLOGICAL ANALYSIS, OVERCOME HERE BY USING VIRSCAN TECHNOLOGY. THESE RESULTS WILL POINT THE WAY TOWARD INTERVENTIONS TO PREVENT OR TREAT ADRD, POTENTIALLY INCLUDING VACCINES, ANTIVIRAL MEDICATIONS, AND IMMUNOMODULATION. SIMILAR FINDINGS BETWEEN THESE TWO POPULATIONS WILL SUGGEST FINDINGS THAT ARE LIKELY TO BE UNIVERSAL IN HUMANS; DIFFERENCES WILL INDICATE WHERE FUTURE RESEARCH IS NEEDED.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AN AI-DRIVEN METABOLIC CLOCK FOR HEALTHY AGING AND AD/ADRD - AGE IS THE GREATEST RISK FACTOR FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND AD-RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRDS). AD PROGRESSION IS CURRENTLY UNDERSTOOD AS PATHOPHYSIOLOGIC PROCESSES THAT BEGIN YEARS, IF NOT UP TO A DECADE AHEAD OF ANY NEUROLOGICAL SYMPTOMS. HOWEVER, THESE PATHOLOGICAL CHANGES ALONE ARE NOT SUFFICIENT FOR THE CLINICAL EXPRESSION OF AD DEMENTIA SYMPTOMS. IN THE BACKGROUND OF AD RISK, AGING IS ASSOCIATED WITH SYSTEMIC CHANGES IN METABOLISM WHICH MAY PROVIDE BIOLOGICAL SIGNALS THAT CAN DISTINGUISH THE SHIFT FROM HEALTHY AGING TO AD INITIATION AND PROGRESSIVE COGNITIVE DECLINE, WHICH IS CRUCIAL FOR DEVELOPING TREATMENT OR PREVENTION STRATEGIES. SYSTEMIC METABOLISM IS MOST COMPREHENSIVELY ASSAYED THROUGH UNTARGETED METABOLOMICS PERFORMED ON A BIOFLUID SAMPLE. TO DATE, THE METABOLIC DRIVERS OF COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT IN AD REMAIN UNKNOWN OUTSIDE OF A FEW PUTATIVE CONNECTIONS BETWEEN INSULIN RESISTANCE AND DEMENTIA RISK. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP IN KNOWLEDGE, THIS PROJECT WILL USE LARGE-SCALE UNTARGETED METABOLOMICS TO REVEAL A MORE COMPLETE CONNECTION BETWEEN METABOLIC STATE, AGING, AND AD/ADRD. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT THE SHIFT FROM HEALTHY AGING TO LATENT (ALSO KNOWN AS PRECLINICAL OR ASYMPTOMATIC) AD AND ULTIMATELY TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE DEMENTIA (ADD) CAN BE UNDERSTOOD THROUGH METABOLIC DEVIATIONS FROM A HEALTHY AGING TRAJECTORY. OUR MAIN RESEARCH DESIGN IS PERFORMING UNTARGETED METABOLOMICS IN TWO MAJOR COHORTS (THE NCRAD COHORT REPRESENTING AD PATIENTS AND HEALTHY CONTROLS (HCS) FROM MULTIPLE SITES, AND THE STANFORD ADRC COHORT THAT REPRESENTS AD PATIENTS AND HC MATCHES WHEREIN THE COMPLETE ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR) IS AVAILABLE FOR STUDY). IN SPECIFIC AIM 1, TO DEVELOP A METABOLIC “CLOCK” OF HUMAN AGING AND STUDY DEVIATIONS THAT ARE ASSOCIATED WITH AD/ADRD, WE WILL TEST THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS BY FIRST CREATING A DEEP LEARNING-BASED METABOLOMIC SIGNATURE OF CALENDAR AGE AS BASELINE MULTIVARIATE COMPOSITE BIOMARKER (SUB-AIM 1.1). BY STUDYING DEVIATIONS FROM METABOLIC AGE AND ASSOCIATED COMORBIDITIES (SUB-AIM 1.2) AND CHARACTERIZING THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN INSULIN RESISTANCE, THE METABOLOMIC CLOCK, AND AD/ADRD DIAGNOSIS (SUB-AIM 1.3), WE WILL DETERMINE HOW METABOLIC AGE CAN DELINEATE VARIOUS RISK GROUPS IN THE GENERAL ELDERLY POPULATION. SPECIFIC AIM 2 IS TO DEVELOP A METABOLOMICS MODEL TO PROVIDE IN-DEPTH INSIGHTS INTO AD/ADRD. HERE, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT METABOLOMICS CONTAINS A SPECIFIC SIGNATURE OF AD/ADRD PROGRESSION OVER TIME BY DEVELOPING LONGITUDINAL TRANSFORMER MODELS (SUB-AIM 2.1) AND END-TO-END RAW METABOLOMICS MODELS THAT PROVIDE INTERPRETABLE READ-OUTS OF METABOLITE AND METABOLIC PATHWAY IMPORTANCE (SUB-AIM 2.2) TO POWER BIOLOGICAL DISCOVERY. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL EXPLORE THE POTENTIAL OF INTEGRATING THE EHR (SUB-AIM 2.3) TO CREATE MORE POWERFUL MODELS OF AD/ADRD RISK. THE LONG-TERM OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP AD/ADRD RISK GROUPS BASED ON AN UNTARGETED METABOLOMICS WHICH TAKE INTO CONTEXT AGING, COGNITIVE STATUS, QUALITY OF LIFE, AND THE PRESENCE OF COMORBIDITIES. ACHIEVING A METABOLIC RISK DIFFERENTIATION STRATEGY AND AD/ADRD-FOCUSED RISK MANAGEMENT WILL HELP ELDERLY PATIENTS LIVE LONGER, MORE ACTIVE LIVES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HEALTH CARE CONTACT DAYS: ASSESSING KEY PERSPECTIVES, THE ROLE OF HEALTH SYSTEMS, AND IMPACT ON PATIENT OUTCOMES - PROJECT SUMMARY FOR OLDER ADULTS, DAYS SPENT OBTAINING HEALTH CARE OUTSIDE THE HOME (“HEALTH CARE CONTACT DAYS”) REPRESENT NOT ONLY ACCESS TO NEEDED CARE, BUT ALSO SUBSTANTIAL TIME, EFFORT, FINANCIAL, AND OTHER OPPORTUNITY COSTS FOR THEMSELVES AND THEIR CARE PARTNERS. CONTACT DAYS REPRESENT A CLAIMS- BASED, PERSON-CENTERED MEASURE THAT INCLUDES DAYS SPENT RECEIVING INSTITUTIONAL CARE (HOSPITAL, EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, SKILLED NURSING FACILITY, OR INPATIENT HOSPICE) AND AMBULATORY CARE (OFFICE VISITS, PROCEDURES, TREATMENTS, IMAGING, OR TESTS). GIVEN THE TRADEOFFS, AND EARLY EVIDENCE THAT CONTACT DAYS ARE INFLUENCED BY FACTORS BEYOND PATIENTS’ HEALTH NEEDS, THERE IS BOTH NEED AND AMPLE OPPORTUNITY TO UNDERSTAND AND OPTIMIZE CONTACT DAYS. SOME OF THIS EFFORT SHOULD LIKELY COME FROM HEALTH SYSTEMS – WHICH SERVE A LARGE AND GROWING SHARE OF OLDER ADULTS AND HAVE MAJOR INFLUENCE ON THEIR CARE, E.G., THROUGH PAYMENT MODELS AND TECHNOLOGY. YET THERE IS SCANT RESEARCH ON CONTACT DAYS; SPECIFICALLY, THERE ARE NO QUALITATIVE STUDIES OF CONTACT DAYS AND NO QUANTITATIVE EVIDENCE ON THE ROLE OF HEALTH SYSTEMS OR HOW CONTACT DAYS IMPACT PATIENT OUTCOMES THAT MIGHT JUSTIFY, OR BE NEGATIVELY AFFECTED BY, HAVING MORE OF THESE DAYS. THIS PROPOSAL WILL ADDRESS THESE CRITICAL GAPS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL USE SEMI-STRUCTURED INTERVIEWS AND FOCUS GROUPS TO ELICIT AND ANALYZE PATIENT, CARE PARTNER, CLINICIAN, CARE MANAGER, AND OPERATIONAL LEADER PERSPECTIVES ON HEALTH CARE CONTACT DAYS IN TWO LARGE HEALTH SYSTEMS SERVING A RANGE OF POPULATIONS ACROSS 5 STATES. IN AIM 2, WE WILL USE SURVEY AND MEDICARE BILLING DATA TO DETERMINE HOW CONTACT DAYS VARY ACROSS HEALTH SYSTEMS AND TO QUANTIFY THE ASSOCIATION OF MODIFIABLE HEALTH SYSTEM ATTRIBUTES (E.G., LOW-VALUE SERVICE USE, TELEMEDICINE ADOPTION) WITH PATIENT SEVERITY-ADJUSTED CONTACT DAYS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL USE A RIGOROUS NATURAL EXPERIMENT (A “MOVER” ANALYSIS) AND 100% MEDICARE CLAIMS DATA TO DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF QUASI-RANDOMIZING PATIENTS TO HIGHER CONTACT DAY ENVIRONMENTS ON PATIENTS’ OWN CONTACT DAYS AND OTHER OUTCOMES SUCH AS CHRONIC CONDITION CARE QUALITY AND RECEIPT OF POTENTIALLY INAPPROPRIATE MEDICATIONS. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THE NIA GOAL TO IDENTIFY INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISMS THAT AFFECT THE HEALTH OF OLDER ADULTS TO INFORM ORGANIZATIONAL INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE THEIR HEALTH. RESULTS WILL ALLOW RESEARCHERS, SYSTEM LEADERS, AND POLICYMAKERS TO CONTEXTUALIZE CONTACT DAYS THROUGH KEY STAKEHOLDER PERSPECTIVES, REPLICATE THE MEASURE ACROSS POPULATIONS AND SETTINGS, AND ULTIMATELY, TAKE PRACTICAL STEPS TO IMPROVE ON CONTACT DAYS, E.G., THROUGH REDUCING UNNEEDED CARE, COORDINATING CARE, AND SHIFTING CARE TO THE HOME.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPACT OF HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE AND TELEMEDICINE USE ON DEMENTIA CARE AMONG MEDICARE ENROLLEES WITH ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS - PROJECT SUMMARY HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE (HBMC) -  HOUSE CALLS  BY PHYSICIANS AND ADVANCED CARE PROVIDERS - IS ESSENTIAL FOR THE GROWING POPULATION OF COMMUNITY-LIVING PERSONS LIVING WITH ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD). PERSONS WITH ADRD LIVE WITH MULTIPLE CHRONIC CONDITIONS (MCCS), WHICH NECESSITATE COMPLEX CARE REGIMENS, BUT AS FUNCTIONAL IMPAIRMENT WORSENS, THEY MAY STRUGGLE TO ACCESS OFFICE-BASED MEDICAL CARE. HBMC HELPS ALLEVIATE THIS STRUGGLE BY ENABLING CONTINUITY OF PATIENT CARE, TAILORING MEDICAL MANAGEMENT TO EVOLVING PATIENT NEEDS, AND MITIGATING THE CAREGIVING BURDEN FOR PERSONS LIVING WITH ADRD (PLWD). HOWEVER, HBMC IS LIMITED, LARGELY DUE TO LIMITED AVAILABILITY. THE RAPID EXPANSION OF TELEMEDICINE USE SINCE 2020 PROVIDES ANOTHER ALTERNATIVE TO OFFICE-BASED MEDICAL CARE. OUR STUDY AIMS TO EXAMINE HBMC AND TELEMEDICINE USE AMONG PLWD IN TRADITIONAL MEDICARE (TM) AND MEDICARE ADVANTAGE (MA) AND THEIR IMPACT ON PATIENT OUTCOMES. AMONG PLWD, WHILE THE CONCEPTUAL RATIONALE FOR IMPROVED MANAGEMENT AND OUTCOMES FROM HBMC RELATIVE TO OFFICE-BASED MEDICAL CARE IS COMPELLING, THE EVIDENCE IS SCANT. MOST STUDIES OF THE IMPACT OF HBMC ON OLDER ADULTS FOCUS ON THOSE WITH MCCS AND PRESENT A MIXED PICTURE, WITH SOME STUDIES FINDING A SIGNIFICANT REDUCTION IN ACUTE COMPLICATIONS. THE RAPID EXPANSION OF TELEMEDICINE SINCE EARLY 2020 HAS NOT ONLY INTRODUCED ANOTHER ALTERNATIVE TO OFFICE-BASED MEDICAL CARE BUT MAY HAVE INDIRECTLY AFFECTED HBMC USE. PRIOR STUDIES WERE LARGELY LIMITED TO TM ENROLLEES. OVER THE RECENT DECADE, THE PROPORTION OF MEDICARE ENROLLEES IN MA HAS GROWN RAPIDLY, FROM 25% IN 2010 TO 54% IN 2024. EVIDENCE OF HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION IN MA IS NASCENT, WITH VIRTUALLY NO PRIOR WORK ON HBMC OR TELEMEDICINE USE AMONG PLWD. FURTHER, WE WILL EXAMINE USE AND IMPACT OF THESE SERVICES AMONG SUBPOPULATIONS BY SEX, CO-EXISTING SERIOUS ILLNESS, AND HIGH-NEED, AS THEIR NEED FOR THESE SERVICES MAY DIFFER SYSTEMATICALLY. TO FILL THE SIGNIFICANT EVIDENCE GAPS, WE PROPOSE TO USE MEDICARE ADMINISTRATIVE DATA (2017-2026) FOR TM AND MA ENROLLEES WITH ADRD. WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE NATIONAL TRENDS IN HBMC AND TELEMEDICINE - ALONGSIDE OFFICE-BASED CARE - AND RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE THEIR POTENTIAL IMPACT ON THE PATIENT OUTCOMES FOR COMMUNITY LIVING PLWD. OUR MAIN OUTCOMES WILL BE DAYS SPENT AT HOME, POTENTIALLY PREVENTABLE ACUTE COMPLICATIONS (E.G., FALLS AND TRAUMA), MEDICATION DEPRESCRIBING, TIME TO TRANSITION TO LONG-TERM CARE, AND MEDICARE SPENDING. AS SECONDARY OUTCOMES, WE WILL EXAMINE OVERALL HEALTHCARE CONTACT DAYS, CONTINUITY OF CARE, TREATMENT FOR ADRD, AND DEATH. USING QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL CAUSAL INFERENCE MODELS, WE WILL ESTIMATE THE POTENTIAL IMPACT OF HBMC AND TELEMEDICINE ON OUTCOMES FOR TM AND MA ENROLLEES SEPARATELY. WE WILL ESTIMATE THE IMPACT ACROSS SUBGROUPS BY SEX, CO-EXISTING SERIOUS ILLNESS, AND HIGH NEED. OUR FINDINGS AIM TO DEVELOP RIGOROUS AND GENERALIZABLE EVIDENCE ON THE POTENTIAL BENEFITS OF HBMC AND TELEMEDICINE USE FOR DEMENTIA OUTCOMES, PARTICULARLY THOSE WITH SERIOUS ILLNESS AND HIGH-NEED.

description: AN MHEALTH INTERVENTION TO PROMOTE PHYSICAL ACTIVITY IN MIDDLE-AGED AND OLDER ADULTS TO REDUCE THE RISK OF ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS: THE MOVE2JOY RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL - ABSTRACT DEMENTIA IS A TOP PUBLIC-HEALTH CONCERN AS PEOPLE AGE. OVER 6.5 MILLION PEOPLE HAVE DEMENTIA AND THIS NUMBER IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE TO 12.7 MILLION BY 2050. DESPITE EFFORTS TO IDENTIFY MEDICAL TREATMENTS FOR DEMENTIA, SO FAR NONE HAVE SHOWN TO BE CURATIVE. AS A RESULT, THE BEST CURRENT STRATEGY FOR REDUCING THE BURDEN OF DEMENTIA IS NON-PHARMACOLOGIC PREVENTION THAT REDUCES RISK FACTORS FOR DEMENTIA. PHYSICAL ACTIVITY (PA) IS A KEY PREVENTIVE STRATEGY FOR DEMENTIA. THERE IS STRONG EVIDENCE THAT PA PROTECTS AGAINST COGNITIVE DECLINE AND DEMENTIA ONSET IN MID-LIFE AND OLDER ADULTHOOD. IN ADDITION, PA IMPROVES A NUMBER OF OTHER RISK FACTORS FOR DEMENTIA, INCLUDING HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE, POOR GLYCEMIC CONTROL, DEPRESSION, SLEEP, AND SOCIAL ISOLATION. THEREFORE, TO SUPPORT DEMENTIA PREVENTION, THERE IS A GREAT NEED FOR SCALABLE AND EFFECTIVE PA INTERVENTIONS. MOBILE HEALTH (MHEALTH) TOOLS, SUCH AS MOBILE APPS AND WEARABLES, HOLD PROMISE AS A PLATFORM FOR DELIVERING SUCH INTERVENTIONS. HOWEVER, THE EFFECTIVENESS OF MHEALTH PA INTERVENTIONS TO-DATE TYPICALLY DECLINES BY 6 TO 12 MONTHS, LEAVING SUPPORT FOR LONG-TERM PA MAINTENANCE—WHICH IS NECESSARY FOR EFFECTIVE DEMENTIA PREVENTION—AS AN UNMET CHALLENGE. IN THIS PROJECT, WE ADDRESS THIS CHALLENGE THROUGH A NOVEL MHEALTH INTERVENTION CALLED MOVE2JOY THAT INCLUDES TWO KEY INNOVATIONS: 1) LEVERAGING REINFORCEMENT LEARNING ALGORITHMS TO PERSONALIZE INTERVENTION PROVISION IN ORDER TO PROMOTE LONG-TERM EFFECTIVENESS AND MHEALTH ENGAGEMENT; AND, 2) DIRECTLY ADDRESSING A KEY BARRIER TO SUSTAINED PA AS PEOPLE AGE: THE NEGATIVE EMOTIONS, FEELINGS, AND JUDGEMENTS ABOUT PA (CALLED AFFECTIVE ASSOCIATIONS) THAT MANY AGING PEOPLE DEVELOP DUE TO CHRONIC CONDITIONS AND OTHER HEALTH CHALLENGES THAT MAKE PA UNCOMFORTABLE AND UNAPPEALING. IN THE PROPOSED WORK, WE WILL EVALUATE THE MOVE2JOY INTERVENTION FOR ITS ABILITY TO SUPPORT LONG-TERM PA IN A 12-MONTH RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL WITH 150 INACTIVE ADULTS WITH HYPERTENSION AGED 55+. PARTICIPANTS IN THE ACTIVE ARM OF THE TRIAL WILL USE MOVE2JOY AND A FITBIT ACTIVITY TRACKER TO HELP THEM STAY ACTIVE, WHILE CONTROL-ARM PARTICIPANTS WILL RECEIVE THE FITBIT TRACKER AND QUARTERLY EMAIL NEWSLETTER ON DEMENTIA PREVENTION, BUT WILL NOT HAVE ACCESS TO THE MOVE2JOY INTERVENTION. THE STUDY WILL ASSESS WHETHER MOVE2JOY IMPROVES AVERAGE DAILY MINUTES OF MODERATE-TO-VIGOROUS ACTIVITY (MVPA; PRIMARY OUTCOME), ACHIEVEMENT OF PA GUIDELINES OF 150 MINUTES/WEEK OF MVPA, STEPS/DAY, AND BLOOD PRESSURE (SECONDARY OUTCOMES), AND COGNITIVE FUNCTION (EXPLORATORY OUTCOME) AT 12 MONTHS MORE THAN THE FITBIT-ONLY CONTROL. THE STUDY WILL ALSO EXAMINE IF THESE IMPACTS ARE MEDIATED BY IMPROVEMENTS IN THE AFFECTIVE MECHANISMS THAT MOVE2JOY IS TARGETING. IF SUCCESSFUL, THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE A SCALABLE, OPEN-SOURCE MHEALTH INTERVENTION FOR SUPPORTING LONG-TERM PA AS A MEANS OF DEMENTIA PREVENTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: COGNITION AFTER ARMED CONFLICT: CREATION OF A HARMONIZED COGNITIVE ASSESSMENT PROTOCOL (HCAP) AND EXAMINATION OF ADRD RISKS RELATED TO OLDER ADULT ADRD RISKS RELATED TO EARLY LIFE WAR EXPOSURE - PROJECT SUMMARY: CURRENT COHORTS OF OLDER ADULTS, ESPECIALLY MILITARY VETERANS IN THE U.S. AND WORLDWIDE, WERE WIDELY AND DIFFERENTIALLY EXPOSED TO THE VIOLENCE, TRAUMA, AND SUBSEQUENT MENTAL HEALTH PROBLEMS OF TWENTIETH-CENTURY WARS. THESE OLDER ADULTS, EXPOSED TO NUMEROUS, OFTEN SEVERE, WAR-RELATED STRESSORS AT VARIOUS SENSITIVE STAGES IN EARLY LIFE, MAY EXPERIENCE HEIGHTENED RISK OF LATER LIFE COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA. SUCH RAMIFICATIONS NOT ONLY IMPACT DIRECTLY-EXPOSED INDIVIDUALS BUT ALSO PLACE SIGNIFICANT BURDENS UPON FAMILY CAREGIVERS AND HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS. SIGNIFICANT STRIDES IN UNDERSTANDING THE IMPACT OF ADRD HAVE BEEN MADE THROUGH THE HARMONIZED COGNITIVE ASSESSMENT PROTOCOL (HCAP) NETWORK, WHICH HAS GENERATED FLEXIBLE BUT COMPARABLE INSTRUMENTS FOR ASSESSING OLDER ADULTS’ COGNITIVE FUNCTION, ILLUMINATING COMMON AND DIVERGENT ADRD RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS AROUND THE WORLD. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF ADRD RISK AND RESILIENCE RELATED TO EARLY LIFE WAR EXPOSURES BY DESIGNING AND IMPLEMENTING A NEW HCAP IN A COHORT OF OLDER ADULTS AND THEIR MIDDLE-AGED CHILDREN WITHIN AN ONGOING STUDY THAT HAS COLLECTED RARE AND HIGHLY DETAILED DATA ON EARLY LIFE WAR EXPOSURE - THE VIETNAM HEALTH AND AGING STUDY (VHAS). AIM 1 IMPLEMENTS A THIRD ROUND OF DATA COLLECTION WITH ORIGINAL VHAS PARTICIPANTS (N≈1500) AND BASELINE DATA COLLECTION WITH PARTICIPANTS’ SPOUSES (N≈1100) AND TWO RANDOMLY CHOSEN CHILDREN NOW IN MIDLIFE (N≈2500) TO SUPPORT LONGITUDINAL AND LIFE COURSE INVESTIGATION OF WAR-RELATED ADVERSITIES AND ADRD RISK. THIS AIM INCLUDES IN-DEPTH INTERVIEWS ON HEALTH, SOCIAL RELATIONAL, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL CHARACTERISTICS; THE MAP OF LIFE COURSE EVENTS TO ASSESS EARLY-LIFE WAR EXPOSURE TIMING; AND BIOMARKERS OF CARDIOMETABOLIC DISORDER (CMD). AIM 2 DEVELOPS AND IMPLEMENTS A PROTOCOL TO IDENTIFY MILD COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT (MCI) AND DEMENTIA, SPECIFICALLY BY: DESIGNING, PILOTING, AND ADMINISTERING AN HCAP IN THE VHAS SAMPLE; IMPLEMENTING CLINICAL DEMENTIA RATING (CDR) INTERVIEWS AND CONSENSUS DIAGNOSES OF MCI/DEMENTIA IN A RANDOMLY-SELECTED GROUP OF PARTICIPANTS WITH LOW HCAP SCORES (N≈200) AND RANDOMLY-SELECTED CONTROLS (N≈100) FOR HCAP VALIDATION AND DIAGNOSTIC ALGORITHMS; AND ASSAYING PLASMA-BASED BIOMARKERS WITH HIGH DISCRIMINATIVE ACCURACY FOR DETECTING AD PATHOLOGY (AΒ42/40, P-TAU217, GFAP, & NFL) IN A SUBSET OF PARTICIPANTS (N=500) STRATIFIED BY DEGREES OF WAR-RELATED ADVERSITY. AIM 3 ESTIMATES ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN EARLY-LIFE WAR STRESSORS, MEDIATING ADRD RISK FACTORS (E.G., CMD, PTSD), AND HCAP-BASED MEASURES OF MCI/DEMENTIA IN MID-LATE ADULTHOOD. THE PARENT-OFFSPRING AND SIBLING RELATIONAL DATA GENERATED WILL SUPPORT FUTURE ANALYSES OF GENETIC, EPIGENETIC, AND FAMILY ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS INFLUENCING ADRD. IN ADDITION TO ENRICHING THE NIH-SUPPORTED HCAP NETWORK, THIS STUDY FURTHER INFORMS U.S. HEALTH BY EXPANDING KNOWLEDGE ON THE SOCIAL AND BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH EARLY LIFE WARRELATED STRESSORS CONTRIBUTE TO ADRD RISK AND RESILIENCE. SUCH FINDINGS WILL SHED LIGHT ON APPROACHES TO ADRD PREVENTION WITHIN WAR-AFFECTED POPULATIONS, IN PARTICULAR MILITARY VETERANS AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY WAR.

description: IDENTIFICATION OF AGE AND SEX DEPENDENT CONTRIBUTIONS TO SUPRASPINAL MECHANISMS INVOLVED IN UNDERACTIVE BLADDER - THE LOWER URINARY TRACT (LUT) FUNCTIONS BY SWITCHING BETWEEN STORAGE AND VOIDING PHASES AND IS INTRICATELY REGULATED BY SPINAL AND SUPRASPINAL (BRAIN, CEREBELLUM, BRAINSTEM) NEURAL CONTROL. IN DYSFUNCTIONAL STATES ACROSS THE LUT STORAGE-VOIDING CYCLE, PATIENTS EXPERIENCE LUT SYMPTOMS (LUTS), WHICH NEGATIVELY IMPACT THEIR QUALITY OF LIFE. LUTS SYNDROMES SUCH AS OVERACTIVE BLADDER (OAB) AND BLADDER PAIN ARE WELL CHARACTERIZED AND HAVE MULTIPLE EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS. IN CONTRAST, THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING UNDERACTIVE BLADDER (UAB) REMAIN POORLY IS CHARACTERIZED BY SYMPTOMS SUCH AS SLOW URINARY STREAM, HESITANCY, AND STRAINING TO VOID, WITH OR WITHOUT A FEELING OF INCOMPLETE BLADDER EMPTYING AND, IN SOME CASES, ACCOMPANIED BY STORAGE SYMPTOMS. IF UNTREATED, INCOMPLETE BLADDER EMPTYING INCREASES THE RISKS OF RECURRENT URINARY TRACT INFECTION, RENAL FAILURE, AND BLADDER STONES. UNDERSTOOD, AND EFFECTIVE THERAPIES ARE LACKING. UAB  UAB IS MOST PREVALENT IN OLDER ADULTS AND IMPOSES SUBSTANTIAL QUALITY OF LIFE AND FINANCIAL BURDENS. CURRENTLY, AVAILABLE THERAPIES HAVE LIMITED EFFICACY. CATHETERIZATION, THE MOST COMMONLY USED TREATMENT, IS OFTEN UNCOMFORTABLE, LEADING TO POOR COMPLIANCE. ALTERED SUPRASPINAL NETWORK ACTIVITY DURING BLADDER FILLING, AS SEEN IN FUNCTIONAL MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (FMRI), IS A HALLMARK OF AGING-ASSOCIATED LUTS SUCH AS OAB. REGION OF INTEREST (ROIS) WITH ABNORMAL ACTIVITY SERVE AS TARGETS FOR SUPRASPINAL NEUROMODULATION IN BOTH NON-UROLOGIC DISORDERS AND IN LUT SYNDROMES, INCLUDING OAB, VOIDING DYSFUNCTION, AND BLADDER PAIN. HOWEVER, THE SUPRASPINAL ROIS INVOLVED IN UAB REMAIN UNKNOWN AND DETRUSOR MUSCLE WEAKENING. T LIES IN THE ESSENTIAL ROLE OF SUPRASPINAL ACTIVITY IN REGULATING THE LUT STORAGE/VOIDING CYCLE. UNDERSTANDING SUPRASPINAL CONTROL OF THE LUT IN UAB AND HEALTHY AGING ADULTS IS CRITICAL TO ADVANCING TREATMENT OPTIONS. MAY BE INFLUENCED BY AGING-RELATED STRUCTURAL AND PHYSIOLOGIC CHANGES IN THE LUT, SUCH AS HE SIGNIFICANCE OF THIS STUDY THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS STUDY IS TO CHARACTERIZE NEURAL ACTIVITY AND STRUCTURE IN ADULTS WITH UAB USING A HIGH-RESOLUTION FMRI PLATFORM. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT AGING-RELATED DEGENERATION OF STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION ASSOCIATED WITH UAB CONTRIBUTES TO SUPRASPINAL ACTIVITY DURING THE LUT STORAGE/VOIDING CYCLE AND WM MICROSTRUCTURAL ORGANIZATION WHICH DEVIATES FROM SIMILARLY AGED HCS. WE WILL TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS WITH THESE SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1: IDENTIFY AND CHARACTERIZE SUPRASPINAL ACTIVITY AND FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY (FC) IN ADULTS WITH UAB IN REGIONS INVOLVED IN THE LUT STORAGE/VOIDING CYCLE. AIM 2: ELUCIDATE CHANGES IN SUPRASPINAL ACTIVITY, FC AND WHITE MATTER (WM) MICROSTRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES IN UAB VERSUS SIMILAR AGED HEALTHY CONTROLS. AIM 3: CHARACTERIZE CONTRIBUTIONS OF AGING AND SEX TO SUPRASPINAL ACTIVITY, FC, AND WM MICROSTRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES. THIS WILL BE THE FIRST STUDY TO DEFINE SUPRASPINAL NETWORKS IN UAB WHILE ALSO ADDRESSING THE PHYSIOLOGICAL CHANGES OF AGING AND SEX DIFFERENCES. THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH FOSTERS FUNDAMENTAL DISCOVERY OF THE SUPRASPINAL MECHANISM FOR UAB AND CONTRIBUTIONS OF AGE AND SEX USING AN INNOVATIVE STRATEGY WHICH ALIGNS WITH THE PARENT R01 GRANT MECHANISM.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MENOPAUSE TRANSITION AND CORONARY MICROVASCULAR DISEASE - PROGRAM SUMMARY/ABSTRACT HORMONAL IMBALANCE DURING THE MENOPAUSE TRANSITION SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASES THE RISK OF CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, INCLUDING CARDIAC ISCHEMIA AND STROKE. RECENT STUDIES HIGHLIGHT THE IMPORTANCE OF CORONARY MICROVASCULAR DISEASE (CMD, ONE TYPE OF NON-OBSTRUCTIVE CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE) IN WOMEN WITH MENOPAUSE. OBSTRUCTIVE CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE (CAD) AND CMD BOTH REDUCE CORONARY BLOOD FLOW AND MAKE THE HEART PRONE TO CARDIAC ISCHEMIA; THE MECHANISMS ARE, HOWEVER, DIFFERENT. OBSTRUCTIVE CAD IS PRIMARILY CAUSED BY LIPID PLAQUE FORMATION IN CORONARY ARTERIES (CAS), WHEREAS THE MECHANISMS RESPONSIBLE FOR CMD ARE ATTENUATED VASODILATATION AND VASCULAR REMODELING IN SMALL CAS AND MICROVASCULAR RAREFACTION. UP TO NOW, THERE HAS BEEN NO TREATMENT SPECIFIC TO CMD, AND PATIENTS WITH CMD ARE COMMONLY TREATED WITH MEDICATIONS FOR OBSTRUCTIVE CAD, RESULTING IN UNSATISFACTORY EFFECTIVENESS. THE GOAL OF THIS STUDY IS TO ELUCIDATE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF MENOPAUSE- INDUCED CMD AND ULTIMATELY DEVELOP NOVEL THERAPIES FOR CMD IN WOMEN WITH MENOPAUSE. TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFECT OF MENOPAUSE TRANSITION ON CORONARY MICROVASCULAR FUNCTION, WE UTILIZE THE INDUCIBLE MENOPAUSE MOUSE MODEL GENERATED BY VCD INJECTION, TOGETHER WITH OVARIECTOMIZED MICE. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT I) CORONARY MICROVASCULAR FUNCTION (ASSESSED BY CORONARY FLOW VELOCITY RESERVE [CFVR]) IS SIGNIFICANTLY DECREASED IN PERIMENOPAUSAL AND POSTMENOPAUSAL MICE COMPARED TO THE CONTROL, II) OUR RNA SEQUENCING DATA REVEALED THAT MANY GENES RELATED TO ENDOTHELIUM-DEPENDENT RELAXATION (EDR) ARE DOWNREGULATED, INCLUDING TRPV4 AND SOD2, IN CARDIAC ENDOTHELIAL CELLS (CECS) FROM PERIMENOPAUSAL MICE, III) EDR AND ENDOTHELIUM-DEPENDENT HYPERPOLARIZATION (EDH)-MEDIATED RELAXATION IN CAS ARE SIGNIFICANTLY ATTENUATED IN PERIMENOPAUSAL MICE, IV) CHRONIC ADMINISTRATION OF TRPV4 AGONIST IMPROVES CFVR IN PERIMENOPAUSAL MICE, AND V) FOLLICLE-STIMULATING HORMONE (FSH) ATTENUATES EDR AND TRPV4 AGONIST-MEDIATED RELAXATION IN CAS. DURING THE MENOPAUSE TRANSITION, ESTRADIOL AND PROGESTERONE LEVELS BEGIN TO DECLINE, WHILE FSH AND LUTEINIZING HORMONE LEVELS INCREASE. IN THIS PROJECT, WE INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF FSH IN REGULATING ENDOTHELIAL AND CORONARY MICROVASCULAR FUNCTION DURING MENOPAUSE TRANSITION. TRPV4 IS A NON-SELECTIVE CATION CHANNEL THAT REGULATES VASCULAR TONE VIA EDH-MEDIATED RELAXATION, AND DOWNREGULATION OF ENDOTHELIAL TRPV4 IS IMPLICATED IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SEVERAL TYPES OF HYPERTENSION. INCREASED MITOCHONDRIAL ROS DUE TO REDUCED SOD2 ACTIVITY IS A HALLMARK OF MANY CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES. BASED ON OUR PRELIMINARY DATA, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT MENOPAUSE LEADS TO CMD VIA FSH-MEDIATED DOWNREGULATION OF TRPV4/SOD2 SIGNALING IN CECS, AND THAT THE FSH/TRPV4/SOD2 AXIS IS A VALID TARGET FOR PREVENTING CMD IN WOMEN UNDERGOING THE MENOPAUSE TRANSITION. THREE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE PROPOSED IN THIS STUDY TO TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS: 1) TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFECT OF MENOPAUSE TRANSITION ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF CMD, 2) TO DEFINE THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF CORONARY ENDOTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION DURING THE MENOPAUSE TRANSITION, AND 3) TO EXAMINE WHETHER AND HOW FSH CONTRIBUTES TO THE DEVELOPMENT AND/OR PROGRESSION OF CMD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HEALTH OUTCOMES OF CAPABLE IN PERMANENT SUPPORTIVE HOUSING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  A MODEL OF CARE KNOWN AS COMMUNITY AGING IN PLACE, ADVANCING BETTER LIVING FOR ELDERS, OR CAPABLE, IS AN EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTION DESIGNED TO IMPROVE PHYSICAL FUNCTION AMONG INDEPENDENT LIVING, LOW-INCOME OLDER ADULTS. IT CONSISTS OF A 10-SESSION HOME-BASED PROGRAM DELIVERED OVER 5 MONTHS BY AN OCCUPATIONAL THERAPIST, REGISTERED NURSE, AND MAINTENANCE WORKER TO ADDRESS AN OLDER ADULT’S CAPABILITIES AND HOME ENVIRONMENT. PREVIOUS RESEARCH HAS SHOWN THAT CAPABLE IMPROVES BASIC AND INSTRUMENTAL ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING (ADLS, IADLS) AS WELL AS OVERALL COST SAVINGS ACROSS MULTIPLE CLINICAL TRIALS WITH OLDER ADULT POPULATIONS. OUR TEAM CONDUCTED A PILOT RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL OF CAPABLE IN PERMANENT SUPPORTIVE HOUSING (PSH), WHICH IS AN EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTION TO ADDRESS HOMELESSNESS. A SIGNIFICANT PORTION OF THE POPULATION THAT NOW RESIDES IN PSH IS ALSO AT HIGH RISK OF PREMATURE ONSET OF GERIATRIC CONDITIONS THAT CAN JEOPARDIZE ONE’S ABILITY TO LIVE INDEPENDENTLY. INDEED, THE TARGET POPULATION FOR PSH INCLUDES PEOPLE CONSIDERED TO BE CHRONICALLY HOMELESS WHO HAVE AN AVERAGE AGE JUST UNDER 60 YEARS OLD BUT EXPERIENCE SIGNIFICANT ACCELERATED AGING. INITIAL FINDINGS ESTABLISHED THAT CAPABLE CAN IMPROVE OUTCOMES IN PSH WHERE TENANTS ARE ON AVERAGE YOUNGER BUT HAVE HIGHER RATES OF CHRONIC MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS THAN THE TYPICAL TARGET POPULATION FOR CAPABLE. THE PILOT STUDY ALSO IDENTIFIED THAT CAPABLE CLINICIANS NEED TRAINING ON AND/OR REFERRALS TO PSYCHIATRIC REHABILITATION WHEN WORKING IN PSH.  THE PROPOSED 5-YEAR STUDY IS TO CONDUCT A LARGE-SCALE RANDOMIZED CONTROL TRIAL OF CAPABLE VERSUS USUAL CARE IN PSH, WHICH CONSISTS OF INTENSIVE CASE MANAGEMENT SERVICES (ICMS). THIS STUDY WILL BE CONDUCTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH SERVICES THAT PROVIDES SERVICES TO OVER 20,000 PSH TENANTS. A TOTAL OF 634 PSH TENANTS WHO HAVE ADL OR IADL LIMITATIONS WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO EITHER RECEIVE CAPABLE OR USUAL CARE. STUDY PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SURVEYED AT 5 TIME POINTS (0-, 3-, 6-, 9- AND 12-MONTHS) SO THAT THOSE WHO RECEIVE CAPABLE CAN BE FOLLOWED FOR 6 MONTHS AFTER THE INTERVENTION, WHICH CAN TAKE BETWEEN 5 TO 6 MONTHS TO COMPLETE. QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS WITH CAPABLE CLINICIANS, RECIPIENTS, AND THEIR ICMS WORKERS WILL ALSO BE CONDUCTED. THE GOALS OF THE STUDY ARE TO: EXAMINE THE IMPACT OF CAPABLE ON PSH TENANTS’ ADLS AND IADLS; COMPARE THE COST-EFFECTIVENESS OF CAPAPBLE VERSUS USUAL CARE; AND CONSIDER ANY BARRIERS OR FACILITATORS TO IMPLEMENTING CAPABLE IN PSH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: RESISTANCE EXERCISE TRAINING FOR OLDER ADULTS WITH OBESITY USING GLP- RECEPTOR AGONISTS - PROJECT ABSTRACT THE RAPID ADOPTION AND DIFFUSION OF GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 (GLP-1) RECEPTOR AGONISTS IS TRANSFORMING OBESITY TREATMENT IN THE UNITED STATES. MEDICATIONS IN THIS DRUG CLASS, INITIALLY APPROVED FOR THE TREATMENT OF TYPE 2 DIABETES, HAVE PROVEN TO BE HIGHLY EFFECTIVE AT PROMOTING SUBSTANTIAL WEIGHT LOSS (>15% INITIAL BODY WEIGHT) AMONG ADULTS WITH OBESITY. DESPITE THESE BENEFITS, GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS MAY POSE UNIQUE RISKS FOR OLDER ADULTS DUE TO THE LOSS OF MUSCLE MASS THAT OCCURS WITH SUBSTANTIAL AND RAPID WEIGHT REDUCTION. TO DATE, THERE IS LIMITED INFORMATION ON THE EFFECTS OF THESE MEDICATIONS IN OLDER ADULTS WITH OBESITY AND INTERVENTIONS TO THWART THEIR IMPACT ON MUSCLE. HOWEVER, PRESERVING MUSCLE MASS IN OLDER ADULTS IS CRITICAL BECAUSE LOSS OF MUSCLE IN THIS POPULATION INCREASES THE RISK OF CLINICAL DECOMPENSATION, STRENGTH AND POWER LOSS, DISABILITY, MOBILITY IMPAIRMENT, AND INJURIOUS FALLS—ALL OF WHICH LOWER PHYSICAL FUNCTION AND QUALITY OF LIFE. MUSCLE-SPARING BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS, SUCH AS A PROGRESSIVE INTENSITY RESISTANCE EXERCISE, HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO MITIGATE SKELETAL MUSCLE LOSS AMONG OLDER ADULTS USING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS. WE POSIT THAT PROGRESSIVE, MODERATE TO HIGH-INTENSITY RESISTANCE TRAINING WILL MITIGATE MUSCLE LOSS AND STRENGTH IN OLDER ADULTS WITH OBESITY INITIATING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONIST THERAPY. AS A RESULT, WE ALSO POSIT THAT A MODERATE TO HIGH-INTENSITY RESISTANCE TRAINING PROGRAM WILL IMPROVE MEASURES OF PHYSICAL FUNCTION AND QUALITY OF LIFE TO A GREATER EXTENT THAN CONVENTIONAL CARE ALONE, WHICH WE DEFINE AS HEALTH EDUCATION WORKSHOPS. IN ADDITION, A MODERATE TO HIGH-INTENSITY RESISTANCE TRAINING PROGRAM MAY REDUCE REBOUND WEIGHT GAIN COMMONLY EXPERIENCED AFTER DISCONTINUATION OF GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS, A CLINICAL EVENT THAT AFFECTS MANY PATIENTS AND CONTRIBUTES TO POOR COST-EFFECTIVENESS. TO ASSESS THESE HYPOTHESES, WE PROPOSE TO ENROLL 198 SOCIOECONOMICALLY DIVERSE OLDER ADULTS (≥60 YEARS-OLD) WITH OBESITY WHO ARE INITIATING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONIST THERAPY FOR WEIGHT LOSS. WITHIN 3 WEEKS OF THEIR THERAPY, WE WILL RANDOMLY ASSIGN OLDER ADULTS TO EITHER A SUPERVISED, CENTER-BASED MODERATE-TO-HIGH INTENSITY RESISTANCE TRAINING PROGRAM (RT, 3 DAYS PER WEEK) OR TO AN ENHANCED USUAL CARE GROUP WHO, IN ADDITION TO FOLLOWING PHYSICIAN RECOMMENDATIONS, WILL PARTICIPATE IN WEEKLY HEALTH EDUCATION AS AN “ACTIVE CONTROL” GROUP. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE CHANGE IN MUSCLE MASS, MEASURED USING DEUTERATED CREATINE (D3CR) DILUTION. OUR AIMS/HYPOTHESES ARE AIM/HYPOTHESIS 1: COMPARED TO EUC, RT WILL ATTENUATE THE LOSS IN MUSCLE MASS AMONG OLDER ADULTS WITH OBESITY USING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS; AIM/HYPOTHESIS 2: COMPARED TO EUC, RT WILL IMPROVE OBJECTIVE MEASURES OF PHYSICAL FUNCTION AND STRENGTH AMONG OLDER ADULTS WITH OBESITY USING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS; AIM/HYPOTHESIS 3: COMPARED TO EUC, RT WILL IMPROVE SELF-ASSESSED QUALITY OF LIFE AND PHYSICAL FUNCTION AMONG OLDER ADULTS USING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PERSONALIZED MEDICINE UNDER THE CO-EVOLUTION OF CONNECTOMES AND PATHOLOGICAL PROTEINS - ABSTRACT WITH THIS PROPOSAL, WE WILL DEVELOP COMPUTATIONAL METHODS THAT ENABLE PATIENT-CENTERED PROGNOSTIC PROFILING FOR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD) THAT INCORPORATES THEIR UNIQUE COGNITIVE RESILIENCE CAPABILI- TIES IN THE FACE OF LONGITUDINAL NEUROPATHOLOGICAL CHANGES REFLECTED IN THEIR MEDICAL IMAGING (PET AND MRI) DATA ACROSS MULTIPLE TIME POINTS. THE APPROVAL OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODY MEDICATIONS HIGHLIGHTS THE URGENCY IN ADDRESS- ING AN AGE-OLD QUESTION IN THE AD FIELD: THE EXTENT TO WHICH THE PRESENCE OF NEUROPATHOLOGICAL HALLMARKS (A AND TAU) DESTINES ACCELERATED DECLINE OF A PATIENT’S COGNITION. CONSIDERING THAT PATIENTS ARE PRIMARILY CONCERNED WITH MAINTAINING THEIR DAILY FUNCTIONING CAPABILITIES, THIS REPRESENTS A CRITICAL CHALLENGE FOR THE FIELD. OUR PROPOSAL IS UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO ADDRESS THIS GAP BY (1) MODELING EACH INDIVIDUAL’S DISTINCT CONNECTOME ARCHITECTURE AND COGNITIVE PROFILE IN ADRD PROGRESSION, BUILDING ON OUR POWERFUL LATENTSNA FRAMEWORK (NATURE METHODS, 2025); (2) IDENTIFYING NOVEL MOLECULAR SIGNATURES THAT INFLUENCE CELLULAR PATHWAYS (E.G., MICROGLIA, ASTROCYTES) AND MEDI- ATE DIFFUSION PROCESSES CONTRIBUTING TO HETEROGENEOUS AD PROGRESSION; AND (3) PERFORMING EXTENSIVE VALIDATION OF MODEL-DERIVED ADRD PROGRESSION SUBTYPES TO DETERMINE WHETHER MEDICATION EFFECTS CAN BE MORE PRECISELY ESTIMATED WITHIN STRATIFIED COHORTS—EFFECTS THAT MAY OTHERWISE REMAIN OBSCURED IN UNSTRATIFIED ANALYSES. INNOVA- TIVE SOFTWARES WILL BE DEVELOPED, TESTED, AND IMPLEMENTED TO MODEL LONGITUDINAL NETWORK DIFFUSION, SELECTION, AND CO-EVOLUTION MECHANISMS OCCURRING BETWEEN LARGE PROTEIN MOLECULES AND NEUROIMAGING-DERIVED CONNECTIONS IN THE BRAIN. THE RESULTING SOFTWARE WILL BE OPEN SOURCE AND FREELY AVAILABLE TO ALL PERTINENT RESEARCH COMMUNITIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NEUROCHEMICAL AND COMPUTATIONAL SUBSTRATES OF AGE-RELATED DECISION MAKING - PROJECT SUMMARY CURRENTLY, THERE ARE MORE AMERICANS THAT ARE 65 YEARS OR OLDER THAN ANY OTHER TIME IN HISTORY. IT IS WELL DOCUMENTED THAT THERE ARE CHANGES IN DECISION MAKING ACROSS THE LIFESPAN, EVEN IN THE ABSENCE OF DISEASE. SUCH CHANGES IN DECISION MAKING CAN MODIFY HOW PEOPLE INTERACT WITH HEALTHCARE SERVICES AND LEAVE THEM VULNERABLE TO EXPLOITATION BY OTHERS. DECISION MAKING THEREFORE REPRESENTS A CRITICAL HEALTH BEHAVIOR IN THE AGING POPULATION. AGE-RELATED CHANGES IN DECISION MAKING ARE LIKELY DUE, IN PART, TO CHANGES IN THE REGULATION OF DOPAMINE, SEROTONIN AND NOREPINEPHRINE RELEASE WITHIN THE BRAIN CIRCUITS THAT MEDIATE THESE FUNCTIONS. HOWEVER, DUE TO A LACK OF ENABLING TECHNOLOGIES, TO DATE FEW STUDIES HAVE DIRECTLY MONITORED MONOAMINE RELEASE DYNAMICS IN HUMANS ENGAGED IN DECISION MAKING, CREATING A FUNDAMENTAL GAP IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW THESE COGNITIVE CHANGES EMERGE AS A FUNCTION OF AGE. TO THAT END, HERE WE PROPOSE TO UTILIZE A NOVEL TECHNOLOGY OUR GROUP HAS DEVELOPED CAPABLE OF CAPTURING SUB SECOND AND SIMULTANEOUS CHANGES IN DOPAMINE, SEROTONIN, AND NOREPINEPHRINE RELEASE. WE HAVE VALIDATED OUR ABILITY TO USE THIS APPROACH IN PATIENTS UNDERGOING DBS SURGERY, AS WELL AS IN PATIENTS IMPLANTED WITH CLINICAL DEPTH ELECTRODES IN THE EPILEPSY MONITORING UNIT. THESE ADVANCES HAVE PROVIDED US WITH THE UNPRECEDENTED OPPORTUNITY TO MEASURE MONOAMINE RELEASE DYNAMICS ACROSS SEVERAL BRAIN AREAS KEY FOR DECISION MAKING (ANTERIOR CINGULATE CORTEX, THALAMUS, HIPPOCAMPUS, AND AMYGDALA), IN HUMANS, AND ACROSS A LARGE RANGE OF AGES. HERE, WE PROPOSE TO BUILD UPON THESE ADVANCES TO RECORD MONOAMINE RELEASE DYNAMICS IN CONSCIOUS HUMANS AS THEY PERFORM BOTH SOCIAL AND NON-SOCIAL DECISION MAKING TASKS. WE WILL ALSO UTILIZE COMPUTATIONAL MODELS TO DESCRIBE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN MONOAMINE SIGNALING AND AGE-RELATED CHANGES IN DECISION MAKING BEHAVIOR. TOGETHER, COMPLETION OF THE AIMS IN THIS PROPOSAL WILL PROVIDE A FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND DATASET THAT WILL INCREASE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE MONOAMINE RELEASE DYNAMICS THAT MEDIATE DECISION MAKING, AND HOW THESE SYSTEMS CHANGE AS A FUNCTION OF AGING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: STUDY OF DEMENTIA CARE STAFF: ADAPTATION OF INSTRUMENTS FOR MULTINATIONAL RESEARCH (SUSTAIN) - PROJECT ABSTRACT MAINTAINING A STABLE DEMENTIA CARE WORKFORCE IS AN INTERNATIONAL CHALLENGE. PEOPLE LIVING WITH DEMENTIA HAVE BETTER CARE OUTCOMES WHEN THEY RECEIVE CARE FROM CONSISTENT AND SPECIALLY TRAINED DEMENTIA CARE WORKERS. UNFORTUNATELY, LONG-TERM CARE FACILITIES (LTCFS), WHERE MANY PEOPLE WITH DEMENTIA RECEIVE CARE, CONTINUE TO EXPERIENCE A STAFFING CRISIS. THE STUDY OF DEMENTIA CARE STAFF: ADAPTATION OF INSTRUMENTS FOR MULTINATIONAL RESEARCH (SUSTAIN) STUDY WILL ADAPT A U.S. BASED SURVEY AND TEST INTERNATIONAL MEASURES FOR DEMENTIA CARE WORKERS (DCWS) IN THREE DIFFERENT CULTURAL CONTEXTS SPANNING SOCIOECONOMIC LEVELS FROM HIGH- TO LOWER-MIDDLEINCOME AND GEOGRAPHICALLY SPANNING THREE CONTINENTS. THIS CROSS-NATIONAL (UNITED STATES, BRAZIL, SWITZERLAND AND GHANA) STUDY WILL BUILD THE CAPACITY OF RESEARCHERS TO INVESTIGATE THE DEMENTIA CARE WORKFORCE USING INTERNATIONALLY VALIDATED COMMON DATA ELEMENTS TO MEASURE HIGH PRIORITY DCWS CONCEPTS, INCLUDING EXAMINING FACTORS THAT LEAD TO DEMENTIA CARE WORKERS EXPRESSING AN INTENT TO STAY, CONTINUING TO CARE FOR PERSONS WITH DEMENTIA. IN AIM 1, THE SUSTAIN STUDY WILL ADAPT THE U.S. NATIONAL DEMENTIA WORKFORCE STUDY (NDWS) SURVEYS FOR LTCF ADMINISTRATORS AND STAFF FOR MULTINATIONAL ADMINISTRATION THROUGH A STEPWISE SYSTEMATIC PROCESS FOR TRANSLATION AND CULTURAL ADAPTATION. THE ADAPTED SURVEY WILL BE FIELDED (AIM 2) WITH 600 DCWS (200 WORKERS PER COUNTRY) AND 60 ADMINISTRATORS (20 PER COUNTRY) RECRUITED FROM LTCFS. IN AIM 3, SURVEY DATA WILL BE USED FOR VALIDATION TESTING AND ANALYZED TO DESCRIBE LTCF STAFF AND ADMINISTRATOR RESPONSES IN GHANA, BRAZIL AND SWITZERLAND, TO COMPARE STAFF AND ADMINISTRATOR RESPONSES BETWEEN COUNTRIES AND WITH THE U.S., AND TO IDENTIFY FACTORS RELATED TO LTCF WORKERS’ DEMENTIA CARE KNOWLEDGE, ATTITUDES, AND PRACTICES, AND INTENT TO STAY IN THEIR JOBS, WITHIN AND ACROSS COUNTRIES, AND TO DETERMINE HOW THESE RELATIONSHIPS DIFFER BETWEEN THE THREE STUDY COUNTRIES AND THE U.S. THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHT AND A DATASET TO ADVANCE MEASUREMENT OF DEMENTIA CARE WORKFORCE STABILITY AND THE CONDITIONS THAT ENABLE THESE WORKERS TO CONTINUE TO CARE FOR PERSONS WITH DEMENTIA IN LTCFS. SUSTAIN WILL STRENGTHEN COLLABORATIVE INTERNATIONAL RESEARCH IN LONG-TERM CARE. RESULTS WILL INFORM WORKFORCE INTERVENTIONS, WORKPLACE PRACTICES, AND PROGRAMS IN LTCFS WORLDWIDE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISMS OF SKELETAL MUSCLE MAINTENANCE RELEVANT TO AD/ADRD - PROJECT SUMMARY A DECLINE OF MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION IS ASSOCIATED WITH AGING AND AGE-RELATED DISORDERS, FROM AGE-RELATED MUSCLE DISEASES SUCH AS SARCOPENIA AND INCLUSION BODY MYOSITIS (IBM) TO ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (AD) AND AD RELATED DEMENTIA (ADRD). MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION FEATURES PROMINENTLY AMONG THE FUNDAMENTAL HALLMARKS OF AGING, BUT THE PRIMARY MITOCHONDRIAL PROCESSES CONTRIBUTING TO AGING AND AGE-RELATED DISEASES REMAIN POORLY DE?NED. MITOCHONDRIA ARE INTIMATELY INVOLVED IN NAD+/NADH METABOLISM. THE CENTRAL ROLES OF NAD+ AND NADH IN THE TRICARBOXYLIC ACID (TCA) CYCLE AND ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN (ETC) UNDERSCORE THE IMPORTANCE OF BALANCED NAD+/NADH METABOLISM TO CELLULAR HEALTH. NAD+ LEVEL IS KNOWN TO DECLINE WITH AGE AND BOOSTING THE NAD(H) POOL WITH PRECURSORS PROVES TO BE BENE?CIAL IN AGING AND AGE-RELATED DISEASE SETTINGS. HOWEVER, THE CAUSES OF NAD+ DEPLETION DURING AGING ARE NOT WELL DE?NED AND THE LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCE OF BOOSTING THE NAD(H) POOL ON HUMAN HEALTH REMAINS UNCERTAIN. WE HAVE FOUND THAT REVERSE ELECTRON TRANSPORT (RET) ALONG MITOCHONDRIAL COMPLEX I IS A MAJOR MECHANISM OF NAD+ DECLINE ASSOCIATED WITH AGING. DURING NORMAL OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION, NADH IS OXIDIZED TO NAD+ AT COMPLEX I AND ELECTRONS ARE TRANSFERRED FROM NADH TO UBIQUINONE. UNDER CERTAIN THERMODYNAMIC CONDITIONS, FOR EXAMPLE WHEN FORWARD ELECTRON TRANSPORT (FET) IS BLOCKED WHILE MEMBRANE POTENTIAL IS STILL HIGH, OR WHEN COQH2 LEVEL IS HIGH, RET WILL PREVAIL. RET MOVES ELECTRONS FROM COQH2 BACK TO THE NAD+/NADH BINDING SITE OF COMPLEX I, CONVERTING NAD+ TO NADH AND THUS LOWERING THE NAD+/NADH RATIO WITHOUT CHANGING THE TOTAL NAD(H) POOL, AND GENERATING EXCESS ROS (RET-ROS) IN THE PROCESS. RET HAS BEEN WIDELY CONSIDERED A MAJOR SOURCE OF ROS, AND OUR STUDIES INDICATE THAT IT IS ALSO A MAIN DETERMINANT OF CELLULAR NAD+/NADH RATIO. IN RECENT STUDIES, WE SHOWED THAT RET IS ACTIVATED DURING MUSCLE AND ORGANISMAL AGING IN ANIMAL MODELS. INHIBITION OF RET INCREASES NAD+/NADH RATIO AND IT EXTENDS THE LIFESPAN AND PROMOTES HEALTHSPAN OF NORMAL ANIMALS THROUGH NAD+ REGULATED SIGNALING PATHWAYS. SUPPORTING ITS CLINICAL RELEVANCE, RET WAS FOUND ELEVATED IN NORMALLY AGED SKELETAL MUSCLE AND DISEASED MUSCLE IN HUMANS, AND OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES SUGGEST THAT IT ALSO CONTRIBUTES TO AGING-ASSOCIATED SARCOPENIC PROGRAM. HOW RET IS DEREGULATED IN MUSCLE AGING IS A MAJOR UNANSWERED QUESTION. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES HAVE IDENTI?ED A NEW PROTEIN THAT REGULATES MUSCLE HEALTH AND ORGANISMAL AGING, IS REQUIRED FOR THE BENE?CIAL EFFECT OF RET INHIBITION, AND IS DOWNREGULATED DURING MUSCLE AGING AND IN AGE-RELATED MUSCLE DISEASES IN ANIMAL MODELS AND HUMANS. THIS UNCOVERS FOR THE ?RST TIME A NON-ETC PROTEIN THAT MEDIATES THE EFFECT OF RET ON MUSCLE HEALTH AND LIFESPAN. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THIS NEWLY IDENTI?ED PROTEIN ACTS IN AN UNCONVENTIONAL MANNER TO DIRECTLY INTERACT WITH THE RET MACHINERY INSIDE MITOCHONDRIA, AND THAT RET DEREGULATION IS A CONSERVED MECHANISM AND ACTIONABLE TARGET IN AGE-RELATED MUSCLE DISEASES. UNDERSTANDING THE REGULATION AND FUNCTION OF RET IN MUSCLE AGING AND DISEASE WILL HAVE SIGNI?CANT IMPACT ON OTHER AGE-RELATED DISEASES SUCH AS AD/ADRD, AS KEY AD/ADRD ASSOCIATED GENES WILL BE STUDIED IN THIS CONTEXT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LEVERAGING DATA LINKAGES TO EVALUATE THE EFFECTS OF A GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT ONCOLOGY CARE MODEL IN OLDER ADULTS WITH ADVANCED CANCER - PROJECT SUMMARY: A GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT (GA) ONCOLOGY CARE MODEL IMPROVES OUTCOMES FOR OLDER ADULTS WITH CANCER BY OPTIMIZING TREATMENT DECISIONS. THE GA ONCOLOGY CARE MODEL USES VALIDATED TOOLS TO IDENTIFY AGING-RELATED HEALTH IMPAIRMENTS (E.G., COMORBIDITIES, COGNITIVE DECLINE) THAT INCREASE THE RISK OF CANCER TREATMENT SIDE EFFECTS (I.E., TOXICITY). THE GA ONCOLOGY CARE MODEL FACILITATES EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF AGING-RELATED TOXICITY RISK FACTORS TO ALLOW ONCOLOGY TEAMS TO PROACTIVELY IMPLEMENT TARGETED INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE TOXICITY RISK. THIS RESULTS IN LOWER CANCER TREATMENT TOXICITY AND POSSIBLY LOWER REACTIVE HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION, SUCH AS UNPLANNED HOSPITALIZATIONS AND EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT VISITS, TO CARE FOR TREATMENT TOXICITY. THIS PROACTIVE APPROACH MAY ALSO INCREASE THE TIME OLDER PATIENTS WITH CANCER CAN SPEND AT HOME (I.E., “HOME TIME”), WHICH OLDER ADULTS VALUE FOR INDEPENDENCE, SOCIAL ACTIVITY, AND IMPROVED MOOD. OUR TEAM DEVELOPED AND TESTED A SCALABLE GA ONCOLOGY CARE MODEL WHERE PATIENTS COMPLETE MOST OF THE GA, WITH THRESHOLDS GUIDING EVIDENCE-BASED RECOMMENDATIONS TO REDUCE AGING-RELATED TOXICITY RISK. THE GA ONCOLOGY CARE MODEL HAS BEEN SHOWN TO REDUCE TREATMENT TOXICITY AND IMPROVE PATIENT-CLINICIAN COMMUNICATION, OFTEN LEADING TO LESS INTENSIVE TREATMENTS WITHOUT COMPROMISING SURVIVAL. IT MAY ALSO REDUCE CANCER CARE COSTS BY MINIMIZING REACTIVE UTILIZATION, SUCH AS HOSPITALIZATIONS FOR TREATMENT TOXICITY. HOWEVER, THE IMPACT OF GA ON HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION AND ECONOMIC OUTCOMES IN THE U.S. REMAINS UNCLEAR. SUPPORTED BY THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE ON AGING LINKAGES PROGRAM, WE CAN LINK DATA FROM OUR TWO MAJOR TRIALS EVALUATING GA ONCOLOGY CARE WITH CENTERS FOR MEDICARE AND MEDICAID SERVICES UTILIZATION AND COST DATA. OUR TRIALS (NCT02107443, NCT02054741) ENROLLED OLDER ADULTS WITH ADVANCED CANCER NATIONWIDE, RANDOMIZING PRACTICES TO GA ONCOLOGY CARE OR USUAL CARE. WHILE CLINICAL OUTCOMES WERE ASSESSED, DETAILED UTILIZATION AND COST DATA WERE NOT COLLECTED. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO INVESTIGATE THE IMPACTS OF A GA ONCOLOGY CARE MODEL VERSUS USUAL CARE FOR OLDER ADULTS WITH ADVANCED CANCER ON HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION, HOME TIME, COSTS, AND COST-EFFECTIVENESS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THE GA ONCOLOGY CARE MODEL WILL HAVE HIGHER PROACTIVE HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION AND COSTS YET LOWER REACTIVE TOXICITY- RELATED UTILIZATION AND COSTS, RESULTING IN INCREASED HOME TIME, LOWER TOTAL COST, AND FAVORABLE COST- EFFECTIVENESS VERSUS USUAL CARE. USING THE NOVEL DATA LINKAGE, WE AIM TO EVALUATE PATTERNS OF HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION UNDER THE GA ONCOLOGY CARE MODEL VS USUAL CARE, INCLUDING CHARACTERIZING PROACTIVE HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION (AIM 1A), REACTIVE HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION (AIM 1B), AND ESTIMATING THE EFFECT OF THE GA ONCOLOGY CARE MODEL VERSUS USUAL CARE ON HOME TIME. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL ASSESS THE COST AND COST-EFFECTIVENESS OF THE GA ONCOLOGY CARE MODEL VERSUS USUAL CARE (AIMS 2A AND 2B). OUR FINDINGS WILL INFORM HEALTHCARE ORGANIZATION AND PAYER POLICIES TO IMPLEMENT GA ONCOLOGY CARE FOR >1 MILLION OLDER AMERICANS DIAGNOSED WITH CANCER ANNUALLY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CAUSES AND EFFECTS OF SOMATIC MUTATION IN PARKINSON’S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY  THIS PROJECT AIMS TO STUDY SOMATIC MUTATIONS IN THE HUMAN BRAIN IN PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD), A COMMON AGE-ASSOCIATED NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER IN THE UNITED STATES. A MAJOR GAP IN THE FIELD OF PD RESEARCH IS THE INCOMPLETE UNDERSTANDING OF THE MECHANISMS OF NEURON LOSS IN THIS DISEASE. SOMATIC MUTATIONS ARISE IN CELLS OF MULTICELLULAR ORGANISMS, EITHER DURING DEVELOPMENT OR POSTNATALLY. DNA REPAIR PATHWAYS HAVE EVOLVED TO PROTECT THE GENOME BY PREVENTING SOMATIC MUTATIONS BECAUSE VIRTUALLY ALL CELLS RELY ON AN INTACT GENOME. PD DISPLAYS INCREASED OXIDATIVE STRESS, DNA DAMAGE, AND NEURON CELL DEATH, BUT WHETHER SOMATIC MUTATIONS PLAY A ROLE IN PD PATHOLOGY, THE MECHANISMS THAT MIGHT CAUSE SUCH MUTATIONS, AND THEIR EXACT FUNCTIONAL CONSEQUENCES, ARE UNKNOWN.  WE PIONEERED NEW MOLECULAR AND BIOINFORMATIC METHODS TO STUDY THE SINGLE NEURONAL GENOMES TO STUDY SOMATIC MUTATION IN THE POSTMORTEM HUMAN BRAIN AT UNPRECEDENTED RESOLUTION. USING THESE NOVEL TECHNOLOGIES, WE SHOWED THAT EACH HUMAN NEURON CONTAINS AT LEAST DOZENS OF SOMATIC SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE VARIANTS (SNVS) AND SHORT INSERTIONS AND DELETIONS (INDELS) AT BIRTH. SNVS AND INDELS INCREASE LINEARLY IN POSTMITOTIC NEURONS AFTER BIRTH, REACHING LEVELS IN THE THOUSANDS IN ELDERLY DONORS. NEURON MUTATIONAL SIGNATURE ANALYSIS REVEALED SEVERAL NEURONAL MUTATIONAL SIGNATURES ARISING FROM DISTINCT SOURCES, ANALOGOUS TO SIMILAR STUDIES IN CANCER, WHERE SOMATIC MUTATION SIGNATURES MARK TUMORS EXPOSED TO CERTAIN MUTAGENS OR THOSE WITH DEFICIENCIES IN SPECIFIC DNA REPAIR PATHWAYS. SOME NEURON MUTATION SIGNATURES RELATED TO AGING GENERALLY, WHILE OTHERS WERE LINKED TO OXIDATIVE DAMAGE IN AGING BUT ESPECIALLY IN CERTAIN NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES. NEURON SOMATIC MUTATIONS ARE ENRICHED IN TRANSCRIBED REGIONS AND ACTIVE ENHANCER ELEMENTS, SUGGESTING THAT SOMATIC MUTATIONS DIRECTLY IMPACT GENE EXPRESSION. THESE PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGEST AN APPROACH TO EXPLORING MECHANISMS OF NEURONAL DYSFUNCTION IN PD THAT MAY BE DOWNSTREAM OF KNOWN RISK FACTORS SUCH AS PROTEIN MISFOLDING.  THE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS OF THIS PROPOSAL IS THAT SOMATIC MUTATIONS INCREASE IN PD BY DISCRETE MECHANISMS AND PLAY A ROLE IN DISEASE BY DYSREGULATING NEURONAL GENE EXPRESSION PROGRAMS. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS IN THREE AIMS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL MEASURE RATES OF SOMATIC MUTATION IN PD AND NEUROTYPICAL NEURONS USING SINGLE-CELL AND DUPLEX SEQUENCING. IN AIM 2, WE WILL USE MUTATION SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND HUMAN IPSC- DERIVED NEURON MODELING IN VITRO TO IDENTIFY AND VALIDATE MECHANISMS CAUSING SOMATIC MUTATION IN PD. IN AIM 3, WE WILL STUDY THE EFFECTS OF SOMATIC MUTATION IN THE PD AND NEUROTYPICAL BRAIN USING MULTIOMIC APPROACHES, SINGLE-NUCLEUS, AND SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS. THIS PROJECT WILL SHED LIGHT ON THE MOLECULAR BIOLOGY OF BRAIN SOMATIC MUTATION IN HEALTH AND DISEASE, IDENTIFY GENOME-MAINTENANCE-RELEVANT PATHWAYS THAT BECOME DYSREGULATED IN PD, AND TEST THE FUNCTIONAL RELEVANCE OF SOMATIC MUTATION IN NEUROTYPICAL AND PD NEURONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: FUZZY COAT DYNAMICS OF POST-TRANSLATIONALLY MODIFIED TAU - PROJECT SUMMARY: FUZZY COAT DYNAMICS OF POST-TRANSLATIONALLY MODIFIED TAU  AGGREGATION OF THE MICROTUBULE-ASSOCIATED PROTEIN TAU IS THE HALLMARK OF ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (AD) AND TWENTY OTHER NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES. THESE TAU AGGREGATES SPREAD IN THE BRAIN IN A PRION-LIKE MANNER DURING THE PROGRESSION OF AD. DEFINING THE STRUCTURAL PROPERTIES OF TAU THAT CAUSE THIS PATHOLOGICAL AGGREGATION AND SPREADING IS IMPERATIVE FOR TREATING AD. STRUCTURES OF EX VIVO TAU FIBRILS INDICATE THAT EACH TAUOPATHY HAS A SPECIFIC FIBRIL CORE STRUCTURE WHEREAS DIFFERENT DISEASES HAVE DIFFERENT STRUCTURES, SUGGESTING THAT TAU'S RIGID CORE STRUCTURE DEFINES THE DISEASE ITSELF. HOWEVER, EMERGING DATA THAT WILD-TYPE TAU SEEDED BY AD PAIRED HELICAL FILAMENT (PHF) TAU LACKS THE ABILITY TO TEMPLATE NEW MONOMERS EVEN THOUGH IT ADOPTS THE AD TAU STRUCTURE CHALLENGES THIS NOTION. INSTEAD, THESE DATA SUGGEST THAT TAU'S MOBILE DOMAINS, THE FUZZY COAT, PLAY A CRUCIAL ROLE IN THE PRION-LIKE PROPAGATION OF TAU AGGREGATES. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATION (PTMS) OF TAU CAUSE DISEASE-SPECIFIC DYNAMICS AND RESIDUAL STRUCTURES OF THE FUZZY COAT THAT CONTROL WHICH PART OF THE AMINO ACID SEQUENCE FORMS THE RIGID CORE, WHICH STRUCTURE IS ADOPTED BY THE CORE, AND WHETHER THE RIGID CORE CAN PROPAGATE. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS BY STUDYING TAU WITH TWO COMMON PTMS: PHOSPHORYLATION AT SERINE AND THREONINE RESIDUES AND ACETYLATION AT LYSINE RESIDUES. BOTH MODIFICATIONS REDUCE TAU'S POSITIVE CHARGES AND PROMOTE AGGREGATION. IN AIM 1, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE DYNAMICS AND RESIDUAL STRUCTURES OF PHOSPHO-MIMETIC TAU AND AD PHF-SEEDED TAU. WE WILL CONDUCT SOLUTION NMR EXPERIMENTS ON MONOMERS AND J-COUPLING BASED MAGIC-ANGLE-SPINNING SOLID-STATE NMR (SSNMR) EXPERIMENTS ON FIBRILS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE FUZZY COAT OF PHOSPHO-MIMETIC TAU DIFFERS FROM THE FUZZY COAT OF WILD-TYPE TAU, AND THE FUZZY COAT OF AD PHF-SEEDED TAU HAS DISTINCT PROPERTIES. WE WILL IDENTIFY THE PHOSPHO- MIMETIC MUTATIONS THAT PROPAGATE THE AD PHF STRUCTURE IN MULTIPLE GENERATIONS, THUS DEFINING THE FUZZY COAT PROPERTIES REQUIRED FOR PRION-LIKE PROPAGATION. IN AIM 2, WE WILL INVESTIGATE ACETYLATION-MIMETIC TAU BY MUTATING KEY LYSINE RESIDUES TO GLUTAMINE IN THE MICROTUBULE-BINDING REPEATS. THESE EXPERIMENTS TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT ACETYLATION REGULATES AND REFINES THE STRUCTURE OF TAU'S RIGID CORE. WE WILL CONDUCT SSNMR AND CRYOEM EXPERIMENTS TO DETERMINE THE RIGID-CORE STRUCTURES OF THE ACETYLATION MUTANTS AND SOLUTION AND SSNMR EXPERIMENTS TO CHARACTERIZE THE MOBILE DOMAINS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW PHOSPHO-MIMETIC TAU EVOLVES FROM MONOMERS TO FIBRILS BY STUDYING AGGREGATION INTERMEDIATES USING TIME-RESOLVED 19F SSNMR. TOGETHER, THESE AIMS WILL PROVIDE FUNDAMENTAL NEW INSIGHTS INTO HOW CHEMICAL MODIFICATION AND THE DYNAMICS OF CRYOEM-INVISIBLE FUZZY COAT CRITICALLY IMPACT THE STRUCTURE AND PROPAGATION OF PATHOLOGICAL TAU FIBRILS. THIS KNOWLEDGE WILL STIMULATE NEW AD THERAPIES THAT TARGET THE TAU FUZZY COAT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE CHEMICAL LANGUAGE OF HUMAN GUT BACTERIA IN HEALTHY AGING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT WITH AGE, THE GUT MICROBIOME CHANGES IN COMPOSITION AND BECOMES LESS DIVERSE. RECENT STUDIES IN FISH AND MOUSE MODELS HAVE SHOWN THAT TRANSPLANTING FECAL BACTERIA FROM YOUNG DONORS IMPROVES THE LIFESPAN AND HEALTHSPAN OF OLDER RECIPIENTS. MOREOVER, DIETARY SUPPLEMENTATION WITH HUMAN INFANT-ASSOCIATED BIFIDOBACTERIA EXTENDS THE LIFESPAN OF C. ELEGANS AND MICE AND IMPROVES COGNITIVE FUNCTIONS IN MOUSE MODELS OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD). THEREFORE, THE GUT MICROBIOME REPRESENTS AN ATTRACTIVE THERAPEUTIC TARGET TO PROMOTE HEALTHY AGING. HOWEVER, WE DO NOT FULLY UNDERSTAND THE UNDERLYING MOLECULAR MECHANISMS BY WHICH IMPLICATED MICROBES SUCH AS BIFIDOBACTERIA MODULATE AGING PHYSIOLOGY. ONE KEY WAY THAT HUMAN GUT BACTERIA IMPACT HOST BIOLOGY IS THROUGH METABOLITE PRODUCTION. THESE MICROBIOME-DERIVED METABOLITES (MDMS) HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO INTERACT WITH THE INTESTINAL TISSUES AND INFLUENCE SYSTEMIC AGING AFTER ENTERING THE HOST CIRCULATION. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT BIFIDOBACTERIA PRODUCE A COLLECTION OF BENEFICIAL MDMS, WHICH IN TURN FUNCTIONALLY CONTRIBUTE TO AGING PHYSIOLOGY BY INTERACTING WITH CONSERVED HOST PATHWAYS. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO USE A NOVEL EXPERIMENTAL STRATEGY TO IDENTIFY BIOACTIVE MDMS FROM BENEFICIAL GUT BACTERIA AND TO DETERMINE THEIR MECHANISMS OF ACTION ON HOST AGING. PURSUING THE BIOLOGY OF DIVERSE MDMS HAS BEEN A SCIENTIFIC CHALLENGE. THIS IS LARGELY DUE TO DIFFICULTIES IN IDENTIFYING THEIR BIOCHEMICAL STRUCTURES AND BACTERIAL BIOSYNTHETIC PATHWAYS, AS WELL AS THEIR FUNCTIONS AND MECHANISMS IN THE HOST. TO ADDRESS THESE KNOWLEDGE GAPS, WE HAVE DEVELOPED A HIGH-THROUGHPUT, MASS SPECTROMETRY-BASED PIPELINE TO CONSTRUCT STRAIN-SPECIFIC METABOLIC PROFILES OF HUMAN ANAEROBIC GUT BACTERIA. THIS HAS ENABLED THE PRELIMINARY IDENTIFICATION OF A PANEL OF PROMISING MDMS THAT ARE BOTH HIGHLY PRODUCED BY PRO-LONGEVITY BIFIDOBACTERIA GROWN IN BACTERIAL CULTURE AND DETECTED IN HUMAN BIOFLUIDS. TO TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS ON THEIR FUNCTIONAL ROLES IN AGING, WE WILL EXPLOIT A HUMAN GUT BACTERIA-C. ELEGANS AGING PLATFORM THAT WE HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED AND TRANSLATE THESE FINDINGS TO RELEVANT MAMMALIAN MODELS. AIM 1 WILL DEFINE THE ROLES OF BIFIDOBACTERIA MDMS IN LIFESPAN AND STRESS RESISTANCE IN GENETICALLY TRACTABLE IN VIVO MODELS. AIM 2 WILL IDENTIFY THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH BIFIDOBACTERIA MDMS CONFER NEUROPROTECTION IN C. ELEGANS AND HUMAN CELL MODELS OF NEUROPATHOGENESIS. THIS PROPOSED WORK IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT UNIQUELY LEVERAGES 1) A GUT MICROBE-FOCUSED, HIGH-RESOLUTION MASS SPECTROMETRY TO IDENTIFY LONGEVITY-ASSOCIATED MDMS IN VITRO AND IN VIVO, AND 2) TRACTABLE BACTERIAL AND HOST MODELS (C. ELEGANS, MICE, HUMAN CELLS) TO DISSECT CONSERVED INTRA-ORGANISMAL PATHWAYS UNDERLYING LIFESPAN, STRESS RESISTANCE, AND NEUROPROTECTION. IT IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT MOVES BEYOND ASSOCIATION TO MECHANISM, ADDRESSING A KEY KNOWLEDGE GAP IN HOW BENEFICIAL HUMAN GUT MICROBES CONTRIBUTE TO HOST AGING BIOLOGY AND IDENTIFYING NEW MOLECULAR TARGETS TO DELAY AGE-RELATED DECLINE.

description: I-DECIDE (INCREASING DOCUMENTATION, ENGAGEMENT, AND COMPLETION IN STROKE ADVANCED CARE PLANNING) TRIAL - ADVANCE CARE PLANNING (ACP) IS A PROCESS OF PREPARING PATIENTS AND SURROGATES FOR COMMUNICATION AND MEDICAL DECISION-MAKING. DESPITE FACING A HIGH RISK OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY, INCLUDING A SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED RISK OF ALZHEIMER DISEASE AND ALZHEIMER DISEASE-RELATED DEMENTIA (ADRD) AND RECURRENT STROKE, MORE THAN HALF OF STROKE SURVIVORS HAVE NOT PREPARED THEMSELVES OR THEIR SURROGATES FOR THEIR FUTURE MEDICAL DECISION-MAKING. IMPORTANTLY, NO EVIDENCE-BASED ACP PROGRAMS EXIST FOR STROKE SURVIVORS. PREPAREFORYOURCARE/PREPAREFORTHEIRCARE (PREPARE) IS AN EVIDENCE-BASED ACP INTERVENTION THAT IS EASY TO USE AND SELF-DIRECTED. HOWEVER, IT HAS NOT BEEN TESTED AMONG SURVIVORS OF RECENT STROKE AND THEIR ACP PARTNERS, AND HAS ONLY BEEN TESTED WITHIN A SUPERVISED RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT. BECAUSE STROKE SURVIVORS DIFFER FROM THE GENERAL POPULATION IN MANY WAYS, INCLUDING THEIR AGE, COGNITIVE AND PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENTS, AND THE PRESENCE OF ADDITIONAL PRIORITIES (E.G., STROKE RECOVERY AND PREVENTION), ACP INTERVENTIONS SHOULD BE TESTED AMONG STROKE SURVIVORS SEPARATELY. THEREFORE, WE PROPOSE TESTING THE EFFICACY OF PREPARE DELIVERED AT HOME AND FACILITATED BY A ROBUST ENGAGEMENT PROGRAM (TOGETHER: THE “I-DECIDE” INTERVENTION) AMONG SURVIVORS OF RECENT STROKE AND THEIR ACP PARTNERS. THE ENGAGEMENT PROGRAM WAS DEVISED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH OUR LONGSTANDING STROKE ADVISORY BOARD. IT INCLUDES (1) AN INTRODUCTORY VIDEO WITH TESTIMONIALS FROM STROKE SURVIVORS AND THEIR ACP PARTNERS ABOUT ACP, AND (2) A MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING-BASED AI-DRIVEN TEXT MESSAGING TOOL. EFFICACY OF THE I-DECIDE INTERVENTION WILL BE TESTED WITHIN A MULTICENTER, PROSPECTIVE, RANDOMIZED OPEN-, BLINDED-ENDPOINT (PROBE) ATTENTION-CONTROLLED TRIAL WITH OUTCOMES ASSESSED AT 6 MONTHS. OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE SELF-REPORTED COMPLETION OF 4 SPECIFIC CRITICAL ELEMENTS OF ACP (SIGNING OFFICIAL PAPERS NAMING A MEDICAL DECISION MAKER; SPEAKING TO THE DECISION MAKER ABOUT DESIRED CARE; SPEAKING TO A MEDICAL PROVIDER ABOUT DESIRED CARE; AND COMPLETION OF AN ADVANCE DIRECTIVE), AS WELL AS ACP DOCUMENTATION AND AN ACP OUTCOME AMONG ACP PARTNERS. ACP IS ONE OF THE FEW INTERVENTIONS THAT IMPROVE PATIENT, FAMILY, AND PROVIDER OUTCOMES. IF EFFICACIOUS, THE I-DECIDE INTERVENTION HAS THE POTENTIAL TO IMPROVE SATISFACTION WITH MEDICAL CARE, DECISION-MAKING, AND COMMUNICATION FOR STROKE SURVIVORS AND THEIR FAMILIES, WHILE REDUCING THE BURDEN OF SURROGATE DECISION MAKERS. HAVING AN EVIDENCE-BASED ACP INTERVENTION WOULD RESULT IN A NEW STANDARD OF CARE FOR STROKE SURVIVORS AND WOULD BE GUIDELINE-CHANGING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NEUROBIOLOGICAL SUBSTRATES OF FALLS IN COGNITIVELY UNIMPAIRED OLDER ADULTS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT FALLS ARE A LEADING CAUSE OF MORBIDITY, MORTALITY, AND HEALTH CARE ECONOMIC BURDEN AMONG OLDER AMERICANS (OVER AGE 65). THE IMPACT OF FALLS HAS GROWN AS THE SIZE OF THE OLDER POPULATION EXPANDS. WHILE FALLS ARE MULTIFACTORIAL, GAIT AND BALANCE DECLINE RESULTING FROM CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM PATHOLOGIES IS AN IMPORTANT CONTRIBUTOR. ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE NEUROPATHOLOGIC CHANGE (ADNPC) AND CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE (CEVD) ARE TWO OF THE MOST COMMON NEUROPATHOLOGIES THAT ACCUMULATE IN THE AGING BRAIN. SUBCLINICAL GAIT DECLINE OCCURS IN THESE CONDITIONS EARLY IN THE DISEASE COURSE, OFTEN PRECEDING CLINICAL COGNITIVE SYNDROMES. DUAL-TASK PARADIGMS THAT SIMULTANEOUSLY ENGAGE MOTOR AND COGNITIVE BRAIN SYSTEMS CAN UNCOVER SUBCLINICAL GAIT DEFICITS. WE USE DUAL-TASK PARADIGMS TO INTERROGATE DISTINCT NEURAL SYSTEMS AND ESTABLISH BRAIN-BEHAVIOR RELATIONSHIPS THAT CHARACTERIZE SUBCLINICAL GAIT IMPAIRMENT PATTERNS AMONG COGNITIVELY UNIMPAIRED FALLERS (AIM 1). WE FOCUS ON COGNITIVELY UNIMPAIRED INDIVIDUALS TO ELUCIDATE EARLY DEFICITS. SUBSEQUENTLY, WE WILL ASSESS HOW THESE PATTERNS OF GAIT IMPAIRMENT RELATE TO THE TWO MOST COMMON NEUROPATHOLOGIES ADNPC AND CEVD AS MEASURED BY ACCURATE AND NOVEL BIOMARKERS IN PLASMA AND NEUROIMAGING (AIM 2). PLASMA BIOMARKERS WILL INCLUDE AMYLOID AND TAU (MARKERS OF ADNPC), NEUROFILAMENT LIGHT NFL (AXONAL DEGENERATION) AND GLIAL FIBRILLARY ACIDIC PROTEIN GFAP (ASTROGLIAL ACTIVATION, A MARKER OF INFLAMMATION). IMAGING MARKERS WILL INCLUDE MEASURES OF CEVD (PEAK SKELETONIZED MEAN DIFFUSIVITY- PSMD, ARTERIOLOSCLEROSIS- ARTS- SCORE, WHITE MATTER HYPERINTENSITY), VOLUME LOSS OR ATROPHY OF CORTICAL AND SUBCORTICAL BRAIN REGIONS THAT PLAY A ROLE IN GAIT CONTROL, AS WELL AS NEURITE ORIENTATION DISPERSION AND DENSITY IMAGING (NODDI), TO ASSESS MICROSTRUCTURAL INTEGRITY OF WHITE MATTER TRACTS THAT CONNECT THESE REGIONS. FINALLY, WE WILL FOLLOW INDIVIDUALS PROSPECTIVELY TO ASSESS HOW BASELINE GAIT PHENOTYPES RELATE TO RISK OF INCIDENT AND RECURRENT FALLS (AIM 3). WE WILL RECRUIT COMMUNITY DWELLING, COGNITIVELY UNIMPAIRED OLDER ADULTS FROM THE EXISTING LONGITUDINAL POPULATION-BASED MAYO CLINIC STUDY OF AGING IN MINNESOTA AND MISSISSIPPI COVERING THE MIDWEST AND SOUTHERN STROKE BELT WHICH WILL LEAD TO ROBUST AND MORE WIDELY GENERALIZABLE DATA, INCREASING THE IMPACT. WE WILL LEVERAGE EXISTING RESOURCES, INFRASTRUCTURE AND BIOMARKER DATA AS WELL AS A MULTI-DISCIPLINARY TEAM OF EXPERTS IN THE FIELD OF GERIATRICS, NEUROIMAGING, AGING, ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DISORDERS. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF OUR PROPOSAL WILL ADVANCE KNOWLEDGE OF EARLY SUBCLINICAL GAIT IMPAIRMENT PATTERNS RELATED TO FALLS AND THEIR NEUROBIOLOGICAL SUBSTRATES (ADNPC AND CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE) AMONG COGNITIVELY UNIMPAIRED OLDER AMERICANS. THE IMPACT WILL INCLUDE EARLY RECOGNITION OF FALL RISK AMONG FALL-NAÏVE HEALTHY OLDER ADULTS AND ITS UNDERLYING NEURAL MECHANISM, PROVIDING OPPORTUNITY FOR EARLY RECOGNITION, IMPLEMENTATION PERSONALIZED INTERVENTIONS TARGETING NEUROPATHOLOGICAL SUBSTRATES AND FALL PREVENTION AND OVERALL BETTER HEALTH AND LONGEVITY OUTCOMES FOR OLDER AMERICANS.
