description: FUNCTIONAL APPROACHES TO THE GENETICS OF HEALTHSPAN IN HUMANS - PROJECT SUMMARY AGING IS THE SINGLE GREATEST RISK FACTOR FOR CHRONIC DISEASES, MULTIMORBIDITY, AND FUNCTIONAL DECLINE. TARGETING AGING ITSELF, RATHER THAN INDIVIDUAL DISEASES, PRESENTS A TRANSFORMATIVE OPPORTUNITY. WHILE GENETIC MODULATION OF THE FUNDAMENTAL BIOLOGY OF AGING CAN SIGNIFICANTLY EXTEND HEALTHSPAN AND LIFESPAN IN MODEL ORGANISMS, PROVIDING THE FOUNDATION FOR THE GEROSCIENCE HYPOTHESIS, THE BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING HUMAN AGING AND HEALTHSPAN REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. HUMAN GENETICS OFFERS A POWERFUL FRAMEWORK FOR TESTING THE GEROSCIENCE HYPOTHESIS BY UNCOVERING SHARED GENETIC MECHANISMS UNDERLYING MULTIPLE AGE-RELATED DISEASES (ARDS) AND HEALTHSPAN, PROVIDING CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO THE FUNDAMENTAL PATHWAYS DRIVING HUMAN AGING. WITHIN THE GEROSCIENCE FRAMEWORK, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT GENETIC FACTORS INFLUENCING FUNDAMENTAL MECHANISMS OF HUMAN AGING CONTRIBUTE TO MULTIPLE ARDS AND, ULTIMATELY, HEALTHSPAN AND LIFESPAN. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL EMPLOY TWO COMPLEMENTARY GENETIC DEFINITIONS OF HEALTHSPAN: 1) THE DISEASE-FREE PERIOD BEFORE THE ONSET OF MAJOR ARDS OR DEATH, AND 2) A SHARED GENETIC ARCHITECTURE SHAPING MULTIPLE ARDS. TO BRIDGE THE CRITICAL GAPS IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS AND GENETIC BASIS OF HUMAN HEALTHSPAN, WE PROPOSE AN INTEGRATIVE, MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH COMBINING HUMAN GENETIC ANALYSES, FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS, AND HUMAN CELL MODELING. OUR OBJECTIVES ARE: 1) TO IDENTIFY THE SHARED GENETIC ARCHITECTURE UNDERLYING ARDS AND AGING- RELATED TRAITS (AIM 1), PROVIDING NOVEL GENETIC EVIDENCE FOR THE GEROSCIENCE HYPOTHESIS; 2) TO EXPERIMENTALLY VALIDATE THE REGULATORY ROLES OF HEALTHSPAN-ASSOCIATED NON-CODING VARIANTS AND ESTABLISH THEIR TARGET GENES (AIM 2); AND 3) TO ELUCIDATE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS BY WHICH FUNCTIONAL HEALTHSPAN-ASSOCIATED VARIANTS INFLUENCE GENE EXPRESSION AND CELLULAR AGING PROCESSES (AIM 3). BY ADDRESSING THESE FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS, THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEFINE KEY REGULATORY DRIVERS OF HUMAN AGING AND IDENTIFY POTENTIAL GEROTHERAPEUTIC TARGETS TO IMPROVE HEALTHSPAN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ABETA BETA-HAIRPIN PEPTIDES AND OLIGOMERS AS TREATMENTS FOR ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT. ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS CHARACTERIZED BY PROGRESSIVE SYNAPTIC AND NEURONAL LOSS DRIVEN IN PART BY THE AGGREGATION OF Β-AMYLOID (AΒ) INTO SOLUBLE OLIGOMERS AND FIBRILS. PASSIVE ADMINISTRATION OF ANTIBODIES TARGETING AΒ HAS EMERGED AS A LEADING DISEASE-MODIFYING APPROACH AIMED AT REDUCING PATHOGENIC AΒ ASSEMBLIES AND SLOWING COGNITIVE DECLINE. CLINICAL SUCCESS WITH ANTIBODIES SUCH AS LECANEMAB AND DONANEMAB DEMONSTRATES THAT AMYLOID REDUCTION CAN ALTER DISEASE TRAJECTORY BUT ALSO EXPOSES KEY CHALLENGES, INCLUDING MODEST COGNITIVE BENEFIT AND AMYLOID-RELATED IMAGING ABNORMALITIES (ARIA) ASSOCIATED WITH VASCULAR AΒ CLEARANCE. ACTIVE AΒ VACCINATION, WHICH ELICITS ENDOGENOUS ANTIBODY RESPONSES, OFFERS A COMPLEMENTARY AND PREVENTIVE APPROACH BUT HAS SHOWN INCONSISTENT EFFICACY IN HUMANS DESPITE PROMISING PRECLINICAL AND EARLY CLINICAL RESULTS. BOTH ACTIVE AND PASSIVE STRATEGIES HAVE PREDOMINANTLY TARGETED PROTOFIBRILLAR AND FIBRILLAR AΒ SPECIES, LEAVING EARLY, SOLUBLE ASSEMBLIES—THE CONFORMATIONS MOST STRONGLY ASSOCIATED WITH SYNAPTIC DYSFUNCTION AND NEUROINFLAMMATION—INSUFFICIENTLY EXPLORED.  THIS PROJECT DEVELOPS AND EVALUATES STRUCTURE-GUIDED ACTIVE AND PASSIVE AΒ IMMUNOTHERAPIES THAT TARGET CONFORMATIONAL EPITOPES WITHIN EARLY, NON-FIBRILLAR AΒ ASSEMBLIES. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT VACCINES AND MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS) DIRECTED AGAINST STRUCTURALLY DEFINED Β-HAIRPIN AND OLIGOMER-MIMETIC ANTIGENS CAN SAFELY ENGAGE EARLY AΒ CONFORMATIONS TO PREVENT OR REVERSE AD-LIKE PATHOLOGY WHILE MINIMIZING VASCULAR COMPLICATIONS SUCH AS ARIA. PRELIMINARY STUDIES SHOW THAT THE Β-HAIRPIN PEPTIDE 2AM-L AND THE COVALENTLY STABILIZED OLIGOMER MIMETIC 2AT-L REPRODUCE STRUCTURAL FEATURES OF EARLY AΒ ASSEMBLIES AND ELICIT ANTIBODIES THAT SELECTIVELY BIND DISEASE-RELEVANT AΒ PATHOLOGY. CORRESPONDING MABS, F20-5 AND F20-12, RECOGNIZE CONFORMATIONAL EPITOPES ON THESE ANTIGENS AND LABEL DISTINCT PATTERNS OF AΒ PATHOLOGY IN HUMAN AD BRAIN TISSUE.  AIM 1 EVALUATES THE THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF 2AM-L AND 2AT-L PEPTIDE VACCINES IN MAD2 KNOCK- IN MICE, A MODEL EXPRESSING HUMAN APP, TAU, AND APOE Ε4. VACCINES DISPLAYING THESE ANTIGENS ON LUMAZINE SYNTHASE VIRUS-LIKE PARTICLES WILL BE TESTED UNDER PREVENTIVE AND DISEASE-MODIFYING REGIMENS AND BENCHMARKED AGAINST THE CLINICAL VACCINE CAD106. AIM 2 ASSESSES THE CORRESPONDING MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES F20-5 AND F20- 12 IN THE SAME MODEL AND USING IDENTICAL ENDPOINTS, BENCHMARKED AGAINST MAB158, THE MURINE PRECURSOR OF LECANEMAB. OUTCOMES FOR BOTH AIMS INCLUDE AΒ DEPOSITION, COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE, TAU PATHOLOGY, NEUROINFLAMMATION, SYNAPTIC INTEGRITY, AND ARIA-LIKE MICROHEMORRHAGE.  COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL DETERMINE WHETHER STRUCTURE-GUIDED AΒ IMMUNOTHERAPIES BASED ON 2AM-L, 2AT-L, F20-5, AND F20-12 CAN SAFELY AND EFFECTIVELY MODIFY AD PATHOLOGY. BY INTEGRATING STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY, IMMUNOLOGY, AND PRECLINICAL MODELING, THE RESEARCH ESTABLISHES A MECHANISTIC FRAMEWORK FOR DESIGNING NEXT- GENERATION AΒ IMMUNOTHERAPIES INTENDED TO TARGET EARLY, PATHOGENIC AΒ CONFORMATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE MOLECULAR INTERSECTION OF TAU, PHOSPHATASES AND ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - ABSTRACT AGING IS TYPICALLY ACCOMPANIED BY A DETERIORATION OF PHYSIOLOGICAL FUNCTIONS, INCLUDING, FOR SOME, COGNITIVE DE- CLINE. TAU IS A NEURONAL MICROTUBULE (MT) ASSOCIATED PROTEIN THAT IS ESSENTIAL FOR STABILIZING MTS. TAU HYPER- PHOSPHORYLATION IS FREQUENTLY OBSERVED IN OLDER HUMANS AND IN AN ACCELERATED FASHION IN PATIENTS WITH NEURO- DEGENERATIVE DISEASES. AS HUMANS AGE, REGULATORY MECHANISMS THAT CONTROL PROTEIN PHOSPHORYLATION BECOME LESS EFFECTIVE, LEADING TO ABNORMAL TAU PHOSPHORYLATION AND THE SUBSEQUENT FORMATION OF ALZHEIMER DISEASE (AD)-ASSOCIATED TAU FILAMENTS. DIFFERENT SER/THR KINASES (GSK3Β, ERK2, CDK5, PKA, MARKS AND CAMKII) HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO CATALYZE TAU PHOSPHORYLATION, WITH GSK3Β ACTIVITY LEADING TO THE MOST RAPID TAU FIBRIL FOR- MATION. HOWEVER, WHY SER/THR PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES (PPPS), ENZYMES THAT TYPICALLY COUNTERACT THE ACTION OF SER/THR KINASES, FAIL TO COUNTERACT TAU HYPERPHOSPHORYLATION IS CURRENTLY ENTIRELY UNKNOWN. THE PPP FAMILY OF ENZYMES INCLUDES 7 MEMBERS. HERE WE WILL IDENTIFY HOW PPPS BIND TAU AND DETERMINE PPP-SPECIFIC TAU PHOS- PHOSITES TO DEFINE HOW PPPS REGULATE TAU PHOSPHORYLATION STATUS IN HEALTH AND DISEASE. TO ACHIEVE THIS, WE WILL LEVERAGE THE POWER OF NMR SPECTROSCOPY, THE ONLY TECHNIQUE CAPABLE OF DEFINING MOLECULAR INTERACTIONS OF INTRINSICALLY DISORDERED PROTEINS LIKE TAU AND WITH WHICH WE ARE LEADING EXPERTS, CRYO-EM AND SOPHISTICATED PHOSPHORYLATION AND DEPHOSPHORYLATION EXPERIMENTS (WE ARE ALSO EXPERTS IN THE STUDY OF PHOSPHATASES AND KINASES, ESPECIALLY THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THEY USE FOR SUBSTRATE RECRUITMENT). WE WILL: (1) DEFINE WHICH, WHERE AND HOW EACH PPP BINDS TAU, (2) DEFINE HOW TAU MUTATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH FAMILIAL TAUOPATHIES IMPACT PPP RECRUITMENT, (3) USE KINASE-SPECIFIC TAU PHOSPHORYLATION ASSAYS TO DEFINE WHICH TAU PHOSPHOSITES ARE SPECIFIC DEPHOSPHORYLATED BY WHICH PPP, (4) IDENTIFY IF THERE ARE PHOSPHOSITE DEPENDENCIES ON THE ORDER AND TIMING OF TAU DEPHOSPHORYLATION, (5) ELUCIDATE HOW TAU PHOSPHORYLATION IMPACTS PPP RECRUITMENT AND ACTIVITY, AND (6) QUANTIFY HOW THE DISTINCT STRUCTURAL STATES OF TAU (SOLUBLE/FIBRILS) ALTER PPP RECRUITMENT AND ACTIVITY. TO- GETHER, THESE DATA WILL CREATE THE FIRST PHOSPHORYLATION/DEPHOSPHORYLATION ATLAS OF TAU AND ESTABLISH A SYSTEMS BIOLOGY OF TAU PHOSPHORYLATION AND DEPHOSPHORYLATION IN AD. FINALLY, DEFINING HOW, AT A MOLECULAR LEVEL, PPPS RECRUIT AND DEPHOSPHORYLATE TAU, AND HOW THESE INTERACTIONS ARE ALTERED IN HYPERPHOSPHORYLATED TAU AND TAU FIBRILS, WILL LEAD TO CRITICALLY NEEDED NOVEL ROUTES OF THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION FOR AD FOCUSED ON PPPS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: RNAI-MEDIATED COMBINATORIAL MODULATION OF APOE, INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE, AND TAU PATHOLOGY FOR A DISEASE-MODIFYING TREATMENT OF ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (AD) - PROJECT ABSTRACT ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD), A NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER AFFECTING OVER 50 MILLION INDIVIDUALS WORLDWIDE, IS CHARACTERIZED BY EXTRACELLULAR AMYLOID-Β (AΒ) DEPOSITION AND INTRACELLULAR TAU AGGREGATION. RECENT EVIDENCE HIGHLIGHTS THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN APOLIPOPROTEIN E (APOE), TAU PATHOLOGY, AND INTERFERON-GAMMA-DRIVEN INFLAMMATION AS KEY CONTRIBUTORS TO DISEASE PROGRESSION, LEADING TO BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER DISRUPTION AND T-CELL INFILTRATION THAT DRIVES NEURODEGENERATION. WHILE THESE FACTORS ARE WELL ESTABLISHED, THEIR RELATIVE CONTRIBUTIONS TO AD PROGRESSION AND THE EFFECTS OF MODULATING EACH INDIVIDUALLY OR IN COMBINATION HAVE YET TO BE CLEARLY DEFINED. ADVANCES IN RNA INTERFERENCE (RNAI) TECHNOLOGY HAVE ENABLED POTENT, LONG-LASTING (>90%, MULTI-MONTH) GENE SILENCING IN THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS). THE KHVOROVA LAB HAS DEVELOPED AND OPTIMIZED CNS-ACTIVE MULTIVALENT SMALL INTERFERING RNA (SIRNA) SCAFFOLDS THAT CAN SIMULTANEOUSLY TARGET UP TO FOUR GENES, MAKING THEM WELL-SUITED FOR MODULATING ONE OR MULTIPLE AD PATHWAYS. WITH CURRENT CHEMICAL OPTIMIZATION, A SINGLE DOSE OF MULTI-VALENT SIRNA CAN SILENCE GENES FOR UP TO SIX MONTHS IN THE CNS OF RODENTS AND SIX TO TWELVE MONTHS IN THE CNS OF HUMANS WHILE ACHIEVING MINIMAL SYSTEMIC EXPOSURE—A CRITICAL REQUIREMENT FOR APOE MODULATION. THIS CLASS OF DRUGS, ANTICIPATED TO ENTER CLINICAL TRIALS IN 2025, HOLDS PROMISE FOR AD-MODIFYING TREATMENTS. TO EXPLORE THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN KEY AD-DRIVING PATHWAYS, A PANEL OF FULLY CHEMICALLY MODIFIED SIRNAS TARGETING APOE, TAU, AND JAK1, A MASTER REGULATOR OF INTERFERON-GAMMA SIGNALING, WAS DEVELOPED ALONG WITH ADDITIONAL SECONDARY SIRNAS TARGETING IMMUNE AND AMYLOID PATHWAY GENES. IN AN AMYLOID-DRIVEN AD MOUSE MODEL, SIRNA-MEDIATED SILENCING OF CNS APOE SIGNIFICANTLY ENHANCED AMYLOID CLEARANCE BUT ALSO TRIGGERED AN INCREASE IN MICROGLIA-DRIVEN IMMUNE ACTIVATION. CO-SILENCING JAK1 ALONGSIDE APOE MITIGATED INFLAMMATION WHILE PRESERVING AMYLOID CLEARANCE. IN A TAUOPATHY-DRIVEN AD MODEL, LATE SHORT-TERM RNAI-BASED MODULATION OF TAU SUBSTANTIALLY REDUCED PHOSPHORYLATED TAU, IMPROVED BEHAVIORAL PHENOTYPES, AND PREVENTED THALAMIC VOLUME LOSS BUT FAILED TO EXTEND LIFESPAN, SUGGESTING TAU MODULATION ALONE MAY BE INSUFFICIENT TO MODIFY AD. THESE PRELIMINARY FINDINGS LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR AN IN-DEPTH INVESTIGATION INTO THE LONG-TERM (9 TO 12 MONTHS) EFFECTS OF CO-MODULATING APOE, INFLAMMATION, AND TAU PATHWAYS IN AD. AIM 1 WILL DESIGN, OPTIMIZE, AND SYNTHESIZE A PANEL OF ADVANCED MULTIVALENT SIRNA TARGETING APOE, JAK1, TAU, AND THEIR COMBINATIONS, AND RIGOROUSLY CHARACTERIZE THEIR LONG-TERM SAFETY, EFFICACY, AND DURABILITY IN THE CNS OF WILD-TYPE MICE. AIM 2 AND AIM 3 WILL EVALUATE THE EFFECTS OF INDIVIDUAL AND COMBINATORIAL LONG-TERM MODULATION OF APOE, TAU, AND JAK1 IN AN AMYLOID-DRIVEN AD MODEL AND TAU-DRIVEN AD MODEL, RESPECTIVELY. THE EFFECTS OF GENE MODULATION ON AD WILL BE ASSESSED USING BIOCHEMICAL, TRANSCRIPTOMIC, HISTOLOGICAL, IMMUNE, MRI, BEHAVIORAL, AND SURVIVAL ANALYSES. COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL DEFINE THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN CRITICAL PATHWAYS IN AD PATHOLOGY AND GENERATE RNAI-BASED COMPOUNDS READY FOR FURTHER EXPLORATION AS NEXT-GENERATION AD THERAPIES.

description: STATISTICAL METHODS FOR SPATIAL PROTEOGENOMICS DATA IN ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY  ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS A LEADING CAUSE OF DISABILITY AND MORTALITY AMONG OLDER ADULTS, YET ITS UNDERLY- ING MECHANISMS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. SPATIAL PROTEOGENOMICS (SPG) INTEGRATES SPATIALLY RESOLVED PROTEIN AND TRANSCRIPT INFORMATION TO PROVIDE UNPRECEDENTED INSIGHTS INTO CELLULAR ORGANIZATION AND INTERACTIONS. RECENT ADVANCEMENTS IN SPATIAL PROTEOMICS, NAMED METHOD OF THE YEAR 2024 BY NATURE METHODS, HIGHLIGHT THE NEED FOR ROBUST DATASETS, INNOVATIVE COMPUTATIONAL METHODS, AND ADVANCED SPATIAL ANALYSES TO FULLY LEVERAGE SPG’S POTENTIAL IN AD RESEARCH. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ADVANCE SPG DATA ANALYSIS BY ADDRESSING KEY GAPS IN IMAGE ANNOTATION, STATISTICAL METHODOLOGY, AND BIOLOGICAL INFERENCE. IN AIM 1, WE WILL FIRST GENERATE LARGE-SCALE, MANUALLY ANNOTATED BRAIN CELL IMAGES TO BENCHMARK SEGMENTATION METHODS. THESE HIGH-QUALITY ANNOTATIONS WILL PROVIDE ESSENTIAL TRAINING DATA FOR COMPUTATIONAL MODELS AND RIGOROUS VALIDATION OF SEGMENTATION METHODS. THEN WE WILL DEVELOP STATISTICAL METHODS FOR BRAIN CELL SEGMENTATION, INCLUDING A DEEP-LEARNING-BASED ALGORITHM ADAPTED FOR IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE IMAGES AND A STATISTICAL FRAMEWORK FOR DELINEATING CELL BOUNDARIES IN MULTIPLEXED SPATIAL PRO- TEOMICS DATA WITH CORRESPONDING SPOT-LEVEL SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS. THESE APPROACHES WILL IMPROVE SEGMENTATION AND CLASSIFICATION ACCURACY ACROSS DIVERSE CELL MORPHOLOGIES. AIM 2 WILL DEVELOP SPATIAL INFERENCE METHODS TO INVESTIGATE CELL-CELL CO-LOCALIZATION USING SPATIAL PROTEOMICS OR IMAGE-BASED SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS. AIM 3 WILL INFER SPATIAL GENE CO-EXPRESSION NETWORKS IN AD AND CONTROLS USING IMAGE-BASED SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS. BY AD- DRESSING CRITICAL GAPS IN SPG ANALYSIS, THIS RESEARCH WILL ADVANCE THE UNDERSTANDING OF AD AND UNCOVER POTENTIAL NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS. THE RESULTS, INCLUDING ANNOTATED DATASETS AND OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE, WILL BE SHARED PUBLICLY, FOSTERING COLLABORATION AND ACCELERATING PROGRESS IN THE FIELD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: POST-KIDNEY TRANSPLANT DEMENTIA AND ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE PREDICTION LEVERAGING THE PRE-TRANSPLANT EVALUATION DATA - ABSTRACT OF THE >225,000 OLDER KIDNEY TRANSPLANT (KT) RECIPIENTS IN THE US, 19% EXPERIENCE POST-KT COGNITIVE DECLINE, WHICH ELEVATES THEIR DEMENTIA AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) RISK. COMPARED TO A 10-YEAR RISK FOR COMMUNITY- DWELLING OLDER ADULTS OF <1%, THE RISK OF POST-KT DEMENTIA/AD DIAGNOSIS IS 7.2-17.0%, AND THIS EVEN UNDERESTIMATES THE PROBLEM, AS ONLY HALF OF THOSE WHO MEET DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA RECEIVE A DIAGNOSIS. TRANSPLANT EVALUATION IS THE IDEAL SETTING FOR POST-KT DEMENTIA/AD RISK PREDICTION BECAUSE THERE IS AMPLE TIME TO INTERVENE WITH COGNITIVE PREHABILITATION/REHABILITATION, ROUTINE MONITORING FOR COGNITIVE CHANGES, CAREGIVER MEDICATION TRAINING, IMMUNOSUPPRESSION TAILORING, AND/OR ENHANCED NURSING INTERVENTIONS. FOR EXAMPLE, COGNITIVE PREHABILITATION IMPROVES PRE-KT COGNITION IN JUST 3 MONTHS. YET, PREDICTING POST-KT DEMENTIA/AD RISK WITH PRE- KT DATA IS NOT PART OF KT EVALUATION. EXISTING MODELS FROM THE GENERAL GERIATRICS POPULATION HAVE POOR PREDICTIVE ABILITY IN KT AND ARE NO BETTER THAN THOSE WITH ONLY AGE AT KT. THEY FAIL TO GENERALIZE TO THIS UNIQUE POPULATION BECAUSE KT IS A MAJOR SURGERY THAT CAN LEAD TO DELIRIUM AND COGNITIVE DECLINE, BOTH ARE EXACERBATED BY IMMUNOSUPPRESSION. IT IS LIKELY THAT IN KT, THE UPPER BOUND OF PREDICTION (BEST GENERAL POPULATION MODELS) IS 0.86, BUT WILL REQUIRE BURDENSOME TESTING THAT IS NOT PART OF KT EVALUATION. PRE-KT GERIATRIC-SPECIFIC RISK FACTORS AS WELL AS TABULAR AND MULTIMODAL DATA WILL LIKELY BE REQUIRED FOR FURTHER PREDICTION IMPROVEMENT. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT POST-KT DEMENTIA/AD RISK CAN BE PREDICTED USING TABULAR/MULTIMODAL DATA DURING PRE-KT EVALUATION AND UPDATED WITH NEW DATA AT THE TIME OF KT. WE WILL USE COSMOS DATA ON >170,000 OLDER (≥50) KT CANDIDATES TO PREDICT POST-KT DEMENTIA/AD RISK DURING KT EVALUATION. THEN WE WILL USE OUR EXISTING NIA-FUNDED COHORT OF 3,900 OLDER CANDIDATES (FAIR) TO ESTABLISH A NEW STUDY (FAIR-COG) WITH UP TO 14 YEARS OF FOLLOW-UP FOR INTERNAL VALIDATION, RECRUITING AN ADDITIONAL 500 OLDER CANDIDATES FOR EXTERNAL VALIDATION. WE SEEK TO: 1) DESIGN AN ASSESSMENT TO PREDICT POST-KT DEMENTIA/AD RISK DURING KT EVALUATION USING TABULAR DATA; 2) EVALUATE WHETHER MULTIMODAL DATA FROM FAIR-COG IMPROVES DEMENTIA/AD RISK PREDICTION; AND 3) STUDY VALIDITY, IMPLEMENTATION, AND GENERALIZABILITY OF THE BEST ASSESSMENT FROM AIMS 1 AND 2. WE WILL IMPROVE POST-KT DEMENTIA/AD RISK PREDICTION FOR THE 21,000 OLDER CANDIDATES EVALUATED EACH YEAR. THIS WILL ALLOW FOR THE IDENTIFICATION OF PATIENTS WHO WOULD BENEFIT FROM PRE- AND POST-KT INTERVENTIONS, LIKE COGNITIVE PREHABILITATION/REHABILITATION AND IMMUNOSUPPRESSION TAILORING. ULTIMATELY, THESE METHODS FOR DEVELOPING A VALID AND IMPLEMENTABLE RISK PREDICTION WILL BE GENERALIZED TO OTHER SURGICAL SETTINGS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MULTI-OMIC CHARACTERIZATION OF MOLECULAR PATHWAYS DRIVING VULNERABILITY AND RESILIENCE TO ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE IN THE OLDEST-OLD - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (AD) IS A SIGNIFICANT PUBLIC HEALTH CRISIS. THIS PROJECT INVESTIGATES THE UNIQUE COGNITIVE RESILIENCE AND VULNERABILITY TO AD IN THE UNDERSTUDIED OLDEST-OLD (90+ YEARS) TO IDENTIFY NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS BY ELUCIDATING UNDERLYING MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, AND GENETIC MECHANISMS. USING AN INTEGRATIVE MULTI-OMIC APPROACH (SINGLE-NUCLEUS RNA AND ATAC SEQUENCING, SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS, WHOLE-GENOME SEQUENCING) ON THE 90+ STUDY COHORT, WE WILL DEFINE CELL-TYPE SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND SPATIAL SIGNATURES, DETERMINE EPIGENOMIC LANDSCAPES AND REGULATORY NETWORKS, AND IDENTIFY HOW GENETIC VARIANTS INFLUENCE THIS MOLECULAR ARCHITECTURE IN RELATION TO DIVERSE COGNITIVE OUTCOMES. THIS RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO AD PATHOGENESIS IN EXTREME AGING, REVEALING NEW TARGETS FOR PRESERVING BRAIN HEALTH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADVANCE CARE PLANNING FOR OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME EXPERIENCING EARLY ONSET AND ACCELERATED DEMENTIA: A MECHANISTIC EVALUATION - PROJECT SUMMARY OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME ARE DISPROPORTIONALLY AFFECTED BY DEMENTIA. DOWN SYNDROME IS THE MOST COMMON GENETIC ETIOLOGY OF INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY AFFECTING >400,000 INDIVIDUALS NATIONALLY, AND ITS PREVALENCE IS HISTORICALLY INCREASING, WITH ~5,300 BABIES BORN ANNUALLY IN THE U.S. IN THE LAST 25 YEARS, THE AVERAGE LIFE EXPECTANCY FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME HAS MORE THAN DOUBLED FROM 25 TO 60 YEARS. THOUGH INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME ARE BORN WITH SERIOUS, LIFE-LIMITING ILLNESSES, THEY FACE THE ADDITIONAL HARDSHIP OF EARLY-ONSET AND ACCELERATED DEMENTIA, RESULTING IN THE #1 CONTRIBUTOR OF DEATH IN THIS POPULATION. DESPITE THE PRESSING NEED, NO STANDARDIZED METHODS EXIST TO PREPARE OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME AND THEIR CAREGIVERS FOR END-OF- LIFE CARE ANTICIPATED TO BE COMPLICATED BY EARLY-ONSET AND ACCELERATED DEMENTIA. CONVERSATIONS BETWEEN PATIENTS WITH SERIOUS ILLNESS AND THEIR CLINICIANS ABOUT VALUES, GOALS, AND PROGNOSIS (I.E., SERIOUS ILLNESS CONVERSATIONS, SICS) CAN LEAD TO WELL-INFORMED SHARED DECISION-MAKING AND IMPROVED QUALITY OF LIFE. THE SERIOUS ILLNESS CARE PROGRAM (SICP, A MULTI-MODAL INTERVENTION THAT INCLUDES A STRUCTURED CONVERSATION GUIDE AND CLINICIAN TRAINING, DESIGNED TO SUPPORT CLINICIANS TO HAVE EARLIER, PERSON-CENTERED SICS), HAS DEMONSTRATED SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENTS IN ACCESS TO AND TIMING OF SICS, POSITIVE PATIENT AND CLINICIAN EXPERIENCES, AND LOWER RATES OF ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION FOR PATIENTS IN VARIOUS SETTINGS. SICP IS DISSEMINATED WIDELY IN 87 COUNTRIES WITH >28,000 CLINICIANS REACHING >378,000 PATIENTS. HOWEVER, SICP IS NOT TAILORED TO OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME EXPERIENCING DEMENTIA. THIS VULNERABLE POPULATION FACES INTELLECTUAL, COMMUNICATION, BEHAVIORAL, AND COGNITIVE CHALLENGES THAT OFTEN RESULT IN MISTREATMENT DURING CLINICAL ENCOUNTERS, WHICH LEADS TO LOWER RATES OF TRUST, RESPECT, AND FAIRNESS BY CLINICIANS. AT THE SAME TIME, CLINICIANS EXPRESS CHALLENGES IN NOT KNOWING HOW TO ENGAGE WITH THESE PATIENTS AND FOCUS ON CAREGIVERS FOR CONVERSATIONS, RESULTING IN SUBOPTIMAL CARE. THUS, OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO TAILOR SICP FOR OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME AND THEIR CAREGIVERS AND DETERMINE THE MECHANISM OF THE REFINED SICP (I.E., SICPDOWN) TO LEAD TO PATIENT-CENTERED CARE IN A SINGLE CENTER, MECHANISTIC RANDOMIZED TRIAL OF 100 OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT SICPDOWN WILL LEAD TO SIMILAR IMPROVEMENT IN PATIENT-CENTERED OUTCOMES. WE WILL REFINE SICP TO MEET THE NEEDS OF OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME (AIM 1) AND CLINICIANS IN VARIOUS CARE SETTINGS (AIM 2), THEN DETERMINE THE MECHANISM OF SICP ON PATIENT-CENTERED ADVANCE CARE PLANNING (AIM 3). THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE MECHANISTIC: ANXIETY, PROGNOSTIC UNDERSTANDING, AND FEELING HEARD AND UNDERSTOOD ABOUT VALUES AND GOALS. OUR STUDY RESULTS WILL DEEPEN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW SICS, TAILORED TO OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME, LEAD TO PATIENT- CENTERED CARE AND SERVE AS A RICH RESOURCE TO DEVELOP EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES TO TAILOR SICS FOR OTHER 2.3 MILLION AGING ADULTS WITH INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY, MEETING PRIORITIES OF THE NIH INCLUDE PROJECT AND ITS NIA GOALS, AND THE NATIONAL ALZHEIMER’S PROJECT ACT (PUBLIC LAW 111-375).

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE POINTER NEUROVASCULAR EXTENSION STUDY - PROJECT SUMMARY AS A CRITICAL ANCILLARY STUDY TO THE U.S. STUDY TO PROTECT BRAIN HEALTH THROUGH LIFESTYLE INTERVENTION TO REDUCE RISK (U.S. POINTER), POINTER NEUROVASCULAR (POINTER-NV) WAS DESIGNED TO INVESTIGATE NEUROVASCULAR MECHANISMS THAT MAY UNDERLIE IMPROVEMENTS IN COGNITIVE FUNCTION IN RESPONSE TO A 2-YEAR MULTIDOMAIN LIFESTYLE INTERVENTION. BETWEEN APRIL 2021 AND OCTOBER 2023, WE SUCCESSFULLY ENROLLED 491 U.S. POINTER PARTICIPANTS INTO THE POINTER-NV ANCILLARY STUDY TO CONDUCT A COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF AUTONOMIC FUNCTION AND VASCULAR STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION AT BASELINE, MONTH 12, AND MONTH 24. U.S. POINTER ESTABLISHED THAT THE ADDITIONAL SUPPORT, STRUCTURE, AND ACCOUNTABILITY OF THE STRUCTURED (STR) LIFESTYLE INTERVENTION RESULTED IN CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT COGNITIVE BENEFITS COMPARED TO THE SELF-GUIDED (SG) INTERVENTION, AND AMONG THOSE ENROLLED IN POINTER-NV, WE OBSERVED SIGNIFICANTLY GREATER IMPROVEMENTS IN AUTONOMIC FUNCTION AND VASCULAR HEMODYNAMICS IN THE STR GROUP IN PARALLEL WITH IMPROVED COGNITIVE FUNCTION. TO DETERMINE WHETHER SHORT-TERM NEUROVASCULAR BENEFITS ARE MAINTAINED POST-INTERVENTION, WHETHER SUCH CHANGES PROMOTE LONG-TERM PRESERVATION OF COGNITIVE HEALTH, AND WHICH INTERVENTION-RELATED ACTIVITIES / LIFESTYLE BEHAVIORS ARE MOST IMPACTFUL, WE PROPOSE TO EXTEND THE POINTER-NV STUDY INTO A 4-YEAR FOLLOW-UP PERIOD ALONG WITH THE PARENT STUDY. IN THE PROPOSED POINTER-NV EXTENSION STUDY, VAGAL AND SYMPATHETIC ACTIVITY (VIA CONTINUOUS HEART RATE AND BLOOD PRESSURE MONITORING) AND AORTIC AND CAROTID STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION (VIA APPLANATION TONOMETRY AND ULTRASOUND) WILL BE MEASURED USING GOLD STANDARD METHODS. WE WILL ALSO TAKE ADVANTAGE OF STORED BLOOD SAMPLES TO MEASURE PLASMA LEVELS OF INFLAMMATORY BIOMARKERS AND NEUROTRANSMITTERS. THE AIMS OF THIS STUDY ARE TO DETERMINE WHETHER SHORT-TERM IMPROVEMENTS IN AUTONOMIC AND VASCULAR FUNCTION ARE SUSTAINED LONG-TERM (AIM 1); ASSESS THE LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF THE POINTER LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS ON INFLAMMATION (AIM 2); AND ASSESS LONGITUDINAL ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN AUTONOMIC/VASCULAR FUNCTION AND INFLAMMATION AND DETERMINE THEIR LONG-TERM IMPACT ON COGNITIVE TRAJECTORIES (AIM 3). DATA COLLECTED AT THE BASELINE AND MONTH 24 VISITS DURING THE INTERVENTION PHASE AND AT THE YEAR 2 AND YEAR 4 VISITS DURING THE EXTENSION PHASE WILL BE USED TO PROVIDE RELEVANT INFORMATION ACROSS SIX YEARS OF FOLLOW-UP. IN EXPLORATORY ANALYSES, WE WILL EXAMINE THE CONSISTENCY OF THE ASSOCIATIONS BY AGE, SEX, AND BASELINE AUTONOMIC FUNCTION. WE WILL ALSO UTILIZE AVAILABLE BRAIN MRI SCANS TO ASSESS THE IMPACT OF NEUROPATHOLOGY IN THE CENTRAL AUTONOMIC NETWORK ON LONG-TERM NEUROVASCULAR AND COGNITIVE OUTCOMES. THIS INNOVATIVE AND COST-EFFECTIVE PROPOSAL PRESENTS A VALUABLE TIME-LIMITED OPPORTUNITY TO ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW AUTONOMIC FUNCTION IMPACTS BRAIN HEALTH (I.E., THROUGH THE REGULATION OF BOTH BLOOD FLOW AND INFLAMMATION), HOW CHANGES IN THESE OUTCOMES TRACK OVER TIME, AND WHETHER THESE PATHWAYS CAN BE FAVORABLY ALTERED BY LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS AND SUSTAINED BEHAVIOR CHANGE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNDERSTANDING PATHWAYS TO IMPROVED NURSING HOME QUALITY: A MIXED-METHODS STUDY OF THE SPECIAL FOCUS FACILITIES - PROJECT SUMMARY: OVER A MILLION OLDER ADULTS RESIDE IN NURSING HOMES ACROSS THE U.S., WHERE THEY RECEIVE POST ACUTE AND LONG-TERM CARE SERVICES. ENSURING HIGH-QUALITY CARE IN THESE SETTINGS IS CRITICAL TO IMPROVING THE HEALTH, SAFETY, AND WELL-BEING OF OLDER AMERICANS. THE SPECIAL FOCUS FACILITY (SFF) PROGRAM IDENTIFIES NURSING HOMES WITH PERSISTENT QUALITY CHALLENGES AND PROVIDES ENHANCED OVERSIGHT INTENDED TO SUPPORT IMPROVEMENTS IN CARE QUALITY. SINCE ITS INCEPTION IN 1998, OVER 1000 NURSING HOMES HAVE PARTICIPATED IN THE PROGRAM. ALTHOUGH MANY FACILITIES HAVE DEMONSTRATED IMPROVEMENT, THERE IS LIMITED EVIDENCE REGARDING WHETHER THESE IMPROVEMENTS ARE SUSTAINED OVER TIME AND HOW THEY RELATE TO RESIDENT OUTCOMES AND FACILITY OPERATIONS. THIS STUDY WILL EXAMINE PATHWAYS TO SUSTAINED QUALITY IMPROVEMENTS AMONG NURSING HOMES THAT HAVE PARTICIPATED IN THE SFF PROGRAM. SPECIFICALLY, THE RESEARCH WILL ASSESS WHETHER SFF PARTICIPATION IS ASSOCIATED WITH SUSTAINED IMPROVEMENTS IN HEALTH DEFICIENCIES, RESIDENT OUTCOMES, FACILITY FINANCES AND STAFFING. THE STUDY WILL ALSO EXPLORE WHY SOME NURSING HOMES MAINTAIN IMPROVEMENTS AFTER COMPLETING THE PROGRAM WHILE OTHERS EXPERIENCE DECLINES. USING RESIDENT LEVEL DATA FROM 2011-2023, THE STUDY WILL EMPLOY RIGOROUS QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL METHODS TO EXAMINE CHANGES IN NURSING HOME QUALITY, RESIDENT OUTCOMES, STAFFING, AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE. IN ADDITION, QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS WITH STATE AGENCIES AND NURSING HOME STAFF WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO ORGANIZATIONAL PRACTICES, IMPLEMENTATION APPROACHES, AND FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH SUSTAINED IMPROVEMENTS. THE STUDY HAS THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) TO EXAMINE CHANGES IN HEALTH DEFICIENCY CITATIONS FOLLOWING PARTICIPATION IN THE SFF PROGRAM AND IDENTIFY FACILITIES WITH SUSTAINED IMPROVEMENT VERSUS REGRESSION; (2) TO ASSESS ASSOCIATION BETWEEN SFF PARTICIPATION AND RESIDENT OUTCOMES, INCLUDING PRESSURE ULCERS, FALLS, AND HOSPITAL ADMISSIONS, AS WELL AS NURSING HOME STAFFING, OCCUPANCY, AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE; AND (3) TO CHARACTERIZE THE VARIATIONS IN PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION ACROSS STATES AND IDENTIFY ORGANIZATIONAL FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH SUSTAINED QUALITY IMPROVEMENT AMONG PARTICIPATING NURSING HOMES. BY IDENTIFYING FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH DURABLE IMPROVEMENTS IN NURSING HOME QUALITY, THIS RESEARCH WILL GENERATE EVIDENCE TO SUPPORT HIGH-QUALITY CARE FOR OLDER ADULTS, IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF ORGANIZATIONAL STRATEGIES ASSOCIATED WITH BETTER RESIDENT OUTCOMES, AND INFORM HEALTH SYSTEMS AND CARE PROVIDERS SEEKING TO STRENGTHEN QUALITY IMPROVEMENTS IN NURSING HOMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ALZHEIMER'S RISK INTERVENTION TRIAL WITH ESTRADIOL (ARITE) - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (AD/ADRD) AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD) ARE AGE-RELATED PROCESSES THAT DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECT POSTMENOPAUSAL WOMEN. HOWEVER, THERE ARE NO FDA-APPROVED PHARMACOLOGICAL INTERVENTIONS AVAILABLE FOR AD/ADRD THAT SLOW THE PROGRESSIVE DAMAGE AND DESTRUCTION OF NEURONS FOR THIS DEVASTATINGLY FATAL DISEASE. FURTHER, DATA SHOW LIMITED USEFULNESS OF STANDARD PRIMARY PREVENTION THERAPIES FOR CVD EVENTS WITH NO EFFECT ON ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY IN WOMEN. UNLESS EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS TO PREVENT OR DELAY AD/ADRD AND CVD ARE IDENTIFIED, MORTALITY AND MORBIDITY AS WELL AS PERSONAL AND ECONOMIC COST WILL CONTINUE TO INCREASE. WE HAVE SHOWN THAT A ‘CRITICAL WINDOW’ (WITHIN 6 YEARS OF MENOPAUSE) EXISTS FOR MENOPAUSAL HORMONE THERAPY (MHT) INITIATION FOR CVD PREVENTION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT LIKEWISE, MHT WILL PREVENT OR DELAY ONSET OF AD/ADRD IN AGING WOMEN WHEN ADMINISTERED DURING THAT ‘CRITICAL WINDOW.’ DETERMINING THE EFFECTS OF MHT ON INCIDENT AD WHEN STARTED IN PROXIMITY TO MENOPAUSE WOULD REQUIRE DECADES OF FOLLOW-UP, BUT BRAIN IMAGING CAN ASSESS SHORTER-TERM MHT EFFECTS ON BRAIN HEALTH. EXPANDING ON OUR PRIOR MHT TRIAL SUCCESS IN REDUCING VASCULAR RISK (IMAGING SUBCLINICAL ATHEROSCLEROSIS), WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE UNDERSTUDIED MHT EFFECTS ON AD RISK. IN THIS FIRST LARGE, LONG-DURATION, RANDOMIZED, DOUBLE-BLINDED, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED TRIAL DESIGNED A PRIORI TO RIGOROUSLY INVESTIGATE THE LONGITUDINAL EFFECTS OF MHT ON CHANGE IN NEUROIMAGING MARKERS OF AD/ADRD RISK, 360 POSTMENOPAUSAL WOMEN <60 YEARS OF AGE WITHIN 6 YEARS OF MENOPAUSE AND WITHOUT COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND CVD WILL BE RECRUITED. HALF WILL BE APOLIPOPROTEIN E Ε4 ALLELE (APOE4) CARRIERS. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO DAILY ORAL NATIVE 17Β-ESTRADIOL 1 MG/NATIVE PROGESTERONE 100 MG THERAPY (E2/P4) OR TO PLACEBO FOR 3-YEARS. E2/P4 EFFECTS ON LONGITUDINAL CHANGE IN AD RISK WILL BE DETERMINED WITH A MULTI-MODAL NEUROIMAGING APPROACH THAT INCLUDES STATE-OF-THE-ART MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING TO INVESTIGATE LONGITUDINAL CHANGE IN CEREBROVASCULAR HEALTH AS WELL AS WELL-KNOWN AD-RISK NEUROIMAGING ENDPOINTS INCLUDING MEASURES OF THE AMYLOID-TAU-NEURODEGENERATION (ATN) AD RESEARCH FRAMEWORK. WE WILL EVALUATE WHETHER HIGH-RESOLUTION B-MODE CAROTID ARTERY MEASURES OF SUBCLINICAL ATHEROSCLEROSIS MEDIATE AN ASSOCIATION BETWEEN MHT AND THE NEUROIMAGING MEASURES OF CEREBROVASCULAR HEALTH, BRAIN STRUCTURE, MICROSTRUCTURE, FUNCTION, AND CONNECTIVITY. FURTHER, WE WILL EVALUATE WHETHER NEUROIMAGING AND SUBCLINICAL ATHEROSCLEROSIS MEASURES MEDIATE AN ASSOCIATION BETWEEN MHT AND COGNITION AND WHETHER APOE4 MODIFIES THE EFFECTS OF E2/P4 THERAPY ON THE TRIAL OUTCOMES. OUR TRIAL ADDRESSES AN IMPORTANT GAP IN KNOWLEDGE SINCE NO RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL HAS ADEQUATELY EVALUATED MHT EFFECTS ON AD/ADRD RISK WHEN INITIATED IN PROXIMITY TO MENOPAUSE. FURTHER, THIS INNOVATIVE AREA OF RESEARCH HAS THE POTENTIAL OF PROVIDING EFFECTIVE THERAPY FOR WOMEN, PARTICULARLY AS THEY REACH MENOPAUSE, WHICH COULD HAVE BROADER IMPLICATIONS FOR PREVENTING OR DELAYING AD AS WELL AS OPENING NEW AVENUES OF DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPIES FOR AD/ADRD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: POWER-MED: POWER OUTAGES, SEVERE WEATHER EVENTS, AND RISK OF MORTALITY AMONG ELECTRICITY-DEPENDENT DURABLE MEDICAL EQUIPMENT USERS IN MEDICARE - PROJECT ABSTRACT OVER 3 MILLION MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES RELY ON ELECTRICITY-DEPENDENT DURABLE MEDICAL AND ASSISTIVE EQUIPMENT (EDME) THAT HELPS MAINTAIN THEIR INDEPENDENCE AND AGE IN THEIR OWN HOMES. COMMON TYPES OF AT-HOME EDME INCLUDE OXYGEN DELIVERY SYSTEMS, INFUSION PUMPS, VENTILATORS, DIALYSIS MACHINES, AND WHEELCHAIRS. DURING POWER OUTAGES, EDME-RELIANT BENEFICIARIES HAVE UNIQUE HEALTHCARE NEEDS, REQUIRING RAPID ASSISTANCE TO IDENTIFY AN ALTERNATIVE POWER SOURCE, AS THE BACKUP BATTERIES OFTEN ONLY LAST FOR 4-12 HOURS. A SUBSTANTIAL PORTION OF OUTAGES ARE DRIVEN BY SEVERE WEATHER EVENTS (E.G., WILDFIRES, TROPICAL STORMS, FLOODS, EARTHQUAKES, HEAT WAVES), HEIGHTENING HEALTH RISKS. EDME-RELIANT BENEFICIARIES MAY ALSO FACE PROBLEMS SAFELY EVACUATING THEIR HOMES WITHOUT ASSISTANCE, STRANDING THEM FOR THE DURATION OF THE POWER OUTAGE AND ANY CO-OCCURRING SEVERE WEATHER EVENT. OUR PRELIMINARY ESTIMATES INDICATE THAT 1.7 MILLION EDME-RELIANT MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES (57%) LIVED IN A COUNTY WITH PROLONGED POWER OUTAGE (8+ HOURS) IN 2024. DESPITE THE CLEAR HAZARD, LIMITED RESEARCH EXAMINES THE EXTENT TO WHICH EDME-RELIANT BENEFICIARIES ARE CONSIDERED IN EMERGENCY PLANNING (E.G., EVACUATION PLANS) OR BENEFIT FROM INTERVENTIONS (E.G., SUPPORT FOR BACKUP GENERATOR PURCHASES). THIS PROPOSAL LAUNCHES A NATIONAL-SCALE EVALUATION OF POWER OUTAGES, CO-OCCURRING SEVERE WEATHER EVENTS, AND RISK OF MORTALITY AMONG COMMUNITY-DWELLING EDMERELIANT MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES AGED ≥65 FROM 2016 TO 2026. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT POWER OUTAGES INCREASE THE RISK OF MORTALITY AMONG EDME-RELIANT BENEFICIARIES DUE TO THE LOSS OF ELECTRICITY FOR LIFE-SUPPORTING AND OTHER DEVICES. WE WILL DEVELOP VALIDATED SPATIAL (E.G., NEIGHBORHOOD, COUNTY) AND TEMPORAL (E.G., HOURLY, DAILY) MEASURES OF POWER OUTAGES AND CHARACTERIZE CO-OCCURRING SEVERE WEATHER EVENTS THAT MAY AMPLIFY HEALTH RISKS. IN PARALLEL, WE WILL CHARACTERIZE STATE-LEVEL EMERGENCY PLANS AND OTHER EXISTING PROGRAMS THAT MAY SUPPORT THE UNIQUE NEEDS OF EDME USERS AND EVALUATE EXISTING STATE-LEVEL PROGRAMS THAT SUPPORT INTERVENTIONS WITH HEALTHPROTECTIVE POTENTIAL. FOR INSTANCE, SOME STATES PROVIDE FUNDS TO PURCHASE BACKUP GENERATORS FOR EDME BENEFICIARIES AMONG DUAL ENROLLEES (I.E., LOW-INCOME OLDER ADULTS [AGED ≥65] WHO ARE SUPPORTED BY MEDICARE AND MEDICAID, ~17% OF EDME-RELIANT BENEFICIARIES). DATA WILL BE LINKED TO THE RESIDENTIAL LOCATIONS OF EDME-RELIANT MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES TO ACHIEVE THE FOLLOWING AIMS: 1) QUANTIFY THE ACUTE IMPACT OF POWER OUTAGES ON MORTALITY (E.G., ALL-CAUSE, CARDIOVASCULAR, RESPIRATORY, INJURIES) AMONG EDME-RELIANT BENEFICIARIES IN A CASE-CROSSOVER STUDY DESIGN, 2) ASSESS STATE-LEVEL EMERGENCY PLANS AND OTHER EXISTING PROGRAMS TO CHARACTERIZE HEALTH-PROTECTIVE STRATEGIES THAT HAVE BEEN INCORPORATED TO ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF EDME-RELIANT BENEFICIARIES DURING POWER OUTAGES, AND 3) EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF SPECIFIC STATE-LEVEL PROGRAMS (E.G., SUPPORT FOR GENERATOR PURCHASES) WITH GOALS TO SUPPORT EDME-RELIANT DUAL ENROLLEES ON THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN POWER OUTAGES AND MORTALITY IN A DIFFERENCE-INDIFFERENCES STUDY DESIGN. THESE FINDINGS WILL PROVIDE TIMELY, DATA-DRIVEN INSIGHTS TO INFORM HOW PATIENTS, CLINICIANS, AND HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS CAN BETTER IDENTIFY AND RESPOND TO MORTALITY RISK IN THIS VULNERABLE POPULATION.

description: THE TECHRESERVE COHORT STUDY: TECHNOLOGICAL ENGAGEMENT FOR COGNITIVE HEALTH AND RESERVE - ABSTRACT ACTIVE ENGAGEMENT WITH DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES, SUCH AS THE INTERNET AND SMARTPHONES, MAY LOWER RISK FOR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND ITS CLINICAL SYMPTOMS. FOR EXAMPLE, OUR RECENT META-ANALYSIS AGGREGATED DATA FROM 411,430 OLDER ADULTS, SHOWING THAT ENGAGEMENT WITH DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES HALVED THE ODDS OF DEVELOPING COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT OR DEMENTIA (OR=.42, 95%CI=.35-.52).1 SIMILAR FINDINGS THAT SUGGEST CAUSAL EFFECTS HAVE EMERGED FROM POPULATION-BASED LONGITUDINAL STUDIES, CONTROLLING FOR DEMOGRAPHIC, SOCIOECONOMIC, AND COHORT FACTORS. THEORY SURROUNDING THE PROTECTIVE EFFECTS OF TECHNOLOGY USE HAS BEEN FORMALIZED IN THE TECHNOLOGICAL RESERVE HYPOTHESIS, WHICH ASSERTS THAT DIGITAL ENGAGEMENT INCREASES RESISTANCE TO COGNITIVE AND FUNCTIONAL DECLINE BY STIMULATING COGNITIVE COMPLEXITY, PROMOTING SOCIAL CONNECTION, AND FACILITATING COMPENSATORY STRATEGY USE. WHILE THE TECHNOLOGICAL RESERVE HYPOTHESIS HOLDS GREAT PROMISE, THREE CRITICAL RESEARCH QUESTIONS NEED TO BE ANSWERED. FIRST, IT IS UNCLEAR WHETHER TO MEASURE TECHNOLOGICAL RESERVE AS A UNITARY VERSUS MULTIDOMAIN CONSTRUCT, NECESSITATING STUDY OF ITS FACTOR STRUCTURE. A SECOND IMPORTANT QUESTION IS WHETHER TECHNOLOGICAL RESERVE HAS INDEPENDENT PREDICTIVE UTILITY FROM OTHER ESTABLISHED CONSTRUCTS, LIKE COGNITIVE RESERVE, REQUIRING RIGOROUS LONGITUDINAL RESEARCH. THIRD, THE NEUROBIOLOGICAL PROCESSES THAT UNDERLIE TECHNOLOGICAL RESERVE HAVE NOT BEEN IDENTIFIED AND COMPARED TO THOSE FOR COGNITIVE RESERVE, WHICH COULD BE ACCOMPLISHED USING FUNCTIONAL IMAGING TECHNIQUES. TO ADDRESS THESE THREE GAPS, WE WILL DEVELOP THE TECHNOLOGICAL ENGAGEMENT FOR COGNITIVE HEALTH AND RESERVE (TECHRESERVE) COHORT. THE TECHRESERVE COHORT WILL BE THE FIRST LARGE (N=300) LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF OLDER ADULTS AT RISK FOR AD THAT INCLUDES SUFFICIENT DATA ON TECHNOLOGICAL RESERVE, COGNITIVE RESERVE, AD BIOMARKERS, AND NEUROCOGNITIVE FUNCTION (OBJECTIVE BEHAVIORAL AND FUNCTIONAL MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING [FMRI] ASSESSMENTS). THE CURRENT R01 WILL SUPPORT BASELINE AND 1-YEAR FOLLOW UP ASSESSMENTS IN THIS COHORT TO EXAMINE COMPETING MEASUREMENT STRUCTURES FOR TECHNOLOGICAL RESERVE (AIM 1), TEST FOR LONGITUDINAL EVIDENCE OF A TECHNOLOGICAL RESERVE EFFECT (AIM 2), AND DETERMINE WHETHER THE EFFECTS OF TECHNOLOGICAL RESERVE ARE EVIDENT IN BRAIN ACTIVATION PATTERNS (AIM 3). WE ANTICIPATE THAT INDIVIDUALS HIGH IN TECHNOLOGICAL RESERVE WILL DEMONSTRATE LESS COGNITIVE DECLINE IN THE PRESENCE OF AD PATHOLOGY COMPARED TO THOSE LOW IN TECHNOLOGICAL RESERVE. RESULTS OF THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO THE ROLE THAT ENGAGEMENT WITH DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES PLAYS IN PROTECTING AGAINST AD CLINICAL SYMPTOMS. IN FUTURE R01 RESEARCH, WE WILL EXPAND THE TECHRESERVE COHORT AND EXTEND FOLLOW UP TO ASSESS CHANGE AND MAINTENANCE OF TECHNOLOGY USE IN RELATION TO AD BIOMARKER ACCUMULATION, FUNCTIONAL AND STRUCTURAL BRAIN CHANGE, AND INCIDENT COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT. ULTIMATELY, THIS WORK WILL INFORM TECHNOLOGY-BASED PREVENTION STRATEGIES TO REDUCE AD RISK AND IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR OLDER ADULTS LIVING WITH NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PROTEOMIC INTERROGATION OF N-TERMINAL ACETYLATION ON MISFOLDED PROTEINS IN EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES - PROJECT SUMMARY NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES, SUCH AS ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD), CLOSELY RELATE TO THE AGGREGATION OF INTRINSICALLY DISORDERED PROTEINS (IDPS), PATHOGENIC POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATIONS (PTMS), AND IMPAIRED CLEARANCE MECHANISMS. HERE IN THIS R01 APPLICATION, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP INNOVATIVE MASS SPECTROMETRY- BASED STRATEGIES TO EXAMINE PTMS RELATED TO IDP AGGREGATION AND EXTRACELLULAR VESICLE (EV)-MEDIATED PROPAGATION. OUR HYPOTHESIS POSITS THAT SPECIFIC COVALENT MODIFICATIONS AND CELLULAR STRESS CONDITIONS FACILITATE IDP MISFOLDING AND ABNORMAL PTMS, CONTRIBUTING TO THEIR AGGREGATION AND PROPAGATION IN DISEASE STATES. WE WILL FOCUS ON N-TERMINAL ACETYLATION (NT-ACETYLATION), ONE OF THE MOST ABUNDANT, WHILE UNDERSTUDIED AND UNDERAPPRECIATED, PROTEIN MODIFICATIONS IN EUKARYOTES, WHICH INFLUENCE PROTEIN STABILITY, LOCALIZATION, AND INTERACTIONS. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES INDICATE THAT QUANTIFYING BOTH CANONICAL NT-ACETYLATION AND NEO NT- ACETYLATION STOICHIOMETRY MAY SERVE AS INDICATORS FOR DISEASE ONSET AND PROGRESSION, PARTICULARLY IN AD PATIENTS EXPERIENCING INCREASED PROTEIN MISFOLDING AND AGGREGATION. TO CORRELATE ALTERATIONS IN THE EV PROTEOME WITH AD PROGRESSION, WE WILL PROFILE BOTH CANONICAL AND NEO NT-ACETYLATION IN NEURON CELLS AND CIRCULATING EVS, REVEALING SIGNIFICANT LINKS TO AD. WE PROPOSE ESTABLISHING A NOVEL PROTEOMICS PLATFORM TO PROFILE THE NT- ACETYLATION LANDSCAPE IN PRIMARY NEURON CELLS, IPSCS, BRAIN TISSUES FROM AD PATIENTS, AND THEIR SECRETED EVS. ACCORDINGLY, OUR INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM WILL PURSUE THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) MEASUREMENT OF CANONICAL AND NEO TERMINAL ACETYLATION STOICHIOMETRY OF MISFOLDED PROTEINS IN CELLS AND EVS; 2) INVESTIGATE HOW IMPAIRED AUTOPHAGY-LYSOSOMAL PATHWAY AFFECTS PROTEIN NT-ACETYLATION IN PRIMARY NEURON-SECRETED EVS; AND 3) CORRELATE NT-ACETYLATION STOICHIOMETRY OF MISFOLDED PROTEINS IN EVS WITH THE STAGES OF AD PROGRESSION. BY THE COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT, WE WILL ESTABLISH CORRELATIONS BETWEEN PROTEIN MISFOLDING, COVALENT MODIFICATIONS, AND EV- MEDIATED CLEARANCE, PROVIDING A NOVEL BIOMARKER PLATFORM FOR EARLY DETECTION, DISEASE MONITORING, AND POTENTIALLY GUIDING THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS IN NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DIMENSIONAL COMPLEXITY AS A BIOMARKER FOR RESILIENCE IN AGING AND DEMENTIA (DC-RAD) - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THERAPIES TO PREVENT ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS CRITICALLY LIMITED BY A LACK OF SENSITIVE BIOMARKERS THAT CAN RELIABLY PREDICT COGNITIVE RESILIENCE. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, WE HAVE DEVELOPED DIMENSIONAL COMPLEXITY (DC), A NOVEL RESTING-STATE FMRI BIOMARKER THAT QUANTIFIES THE DYNAMIC ORGANIZATION OF BRAIN ACTIVITY. HAVING COMPLETED THE INITIAL ANALYTICAL VALIDATION AND SUPPORTED BY STRONG PRELIMINARY DATA, THIS PROJECT WILL NOW PERFORM THE CLINICAL AND BIOLOGICAL VALIDATION OF DC BY LEVERAGING TWO POWERFUL COHORTS: THE ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE NEUROIMAGING INITIATIVE (ADNI), THE FIELD’S BENCHMARK DATASET, AND THE RECENTLY COMPLETED RISK REDUCTION FOR ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (RRAD) CLINICAL TRIAL. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT HIGHER FUNCTIONAL COMPLEXITY IS A FUNDAMENTAL FEATURE OF A RESILIENT BRAIN THAT CAN PROSPECTIVELY IDENTIFY INDIVIDUALS LIKELY TO REMAIN COGNITIVELY STABLE, AND THAT ITS INTEGRITY IS ASSOCIATED WITH A HEALTHIER BIOLOGICAL PROFILE AND A GREATER CAPACITY FOR RESPONSE TO INTERVENTION. WE WILL TEST THIS THROUGH THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 WILL DEVELOP A DC-BASED PROGNOSTIC MODEL IN ADNI AND RIGOROUSLY VALIDATE IT IN THE INDEPENDENT RRAD COHORT. AIM 2 WILL ESTABLISH DC AS A PREDICTIVE BIOMARKER BY TESTING WHETHER IT IDENTIFIES RRAD PARTICIPANTS MOST LIKELY TO BENEFIT FROM INTENSIVE VASCULAR RISK REDUCTION AND EXERCISE INTERVENTIONS. AIM 3 WILL DETERMINE THE BIOLOGICAL UNDERPINNINGS OF DC BY IDENTIFYING ITS CONSISTENT PHYSIOLOGICAL MODULATORS, INCLUDING PLASMA BIOMARKERS AND STRUCTURAL BRAIN INTEGRITY, IN A COMBINED ANALYSIS ACROSS BOTH COHORTS. IN PARALLEL, WE WILL DEVELOP AND RELEASE A CONTAINERIZED DC TOOLBOX TO ENSURE REPRODUCIBLE AND HARMONIZED DC COMPUTATION. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL DELIVER A VALIDATED, ACCESSIBLE, AND REPRODUCIBLE BIOMARKER OF COGNITIVE RESILIENCE. BY ESTABLISHING DC AS A PRECISION-HEALTH TOOL TO ENRICH CLINICAL TRIALS, THIS WORK WILL ACCELERATE THE DISCOVERY OF EFFECTIVE PREVENTION STRATEGIES FOR AD AND ITS RELATED DEMENTIAS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: C9ORF72 AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS/FRONTOTEMPORAL DEMENTIA PREVENT - ABSTRACT A REPEAT EXPANSION IN THE C9ORF72 GENE IS THE MOST COMMON GENETIC CAUSE OF AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (ALS) AND FRONTOTEMPORAL DEMENTIA (FTD). DESPITE THE LIFELONG RISK CONFERRED BY THIS GENETIC VARIATION, CARRIERS DO NOT USUALLY DEVELOP CLINICALLY MANIFEST ALS OR FTD UNTIL LATER IN LIFE, TYPICALLY IN THEIR 50S AND 60S. KNOWLEDGE OF THIS GENETIC RISK YIELDS AN OPPORTUNITY FOR EARLY THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION, WHILE EXPANSION CARRIERS ARE STILL PRE- SYMPTOMATIC, TO PREVENT THE EMERGENCE OF CLINICALLY MANIFEST ALS AND FTD. A MAJOR CHALLENGE TO THE DESIGN AND PRACTICAL IMPLEMENTATION OF C9ORF72 PREVENTION TRIALS, HOWEVER, IS THAT WE ARE CURRENTLY UNABLE TO PREDICT, AT THE INDIVIDUAL LEVEL, THE AGE OF FUTURE PHENOCONVERSION OR WHETHER ALS OR FTD WILL EMERGE FIRST. UNLIKE FAMILIAL ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, WHERE AGE OF ONSET MAY BE PREDICTED UPON THAT OF FAMILY MEMBERS, AND UNLIKE HUNTINGTON’S DISEASE, WHERE THE SIZE OF THE REPEAT EXPANSION IN THE HUNTINGTIN GENE PREDICTS AGE OF ONSET, NO RELIABLE PREDICTORS OF ONSET AGE HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED AMONG C9ORF72 REPEAT EXPANSION CARRIERS. AS SUCH, TIME TO PHENOCONVERSION CANNOT MEANINGFULLY BE ESTIMATED FOR AN INDIVIDUAL. THE C9 ALS/FTD PREVENT STUDY OUTLINED IN THIS PROPOSAL FOCUSES ON C9ORF72 PREVENTION TRIAL READINESS. SPECIFICALLY, WE AIM TO EVALUATE LEADING CLINICAL MARKERS AND BIOMARKERS (PRESENCE OF A PRODROMAL SYNDROME, THALAMIC VOLUME, PLASMA NFL CONCENTRATION, C9ORF72 REPEAT LENGTH, AND PERSONALIZED PENETRANCE ESTIMATES) FOR THEIR UTILITY IN PREDICTING TIME TO PHENOCONVERSION TO CLINICALLY MANIFEST ALS OR FTD, A LIKELY PRIMARY ENDPOINT IN FUTURE PREVENTION TRIALS. HYPOTHESIZING THAT THE PREDICTIVE UTILITY OF THESE MARKERS WILL BE GREATER WHEN CONSIDERED TOGETHER, WE WILL THEN COMBINE THESE MARKERS TO DEVELOP AND INTERNALLY VALIDATE A COMPOSITE RISK SCORE THAT IDENTIFIES THE SUBSET OF C9ORF72 EXPANSION CARRIERS AT THE GREATEST SHORT-TERM RISK FOR ALS OR FTD PHENOCONVERSION. IN SO DOING, WE WILL DEVELOP CRITERIA THAT COULD BE USED TO ENRICH C9ORF72 PREVENTION TRIAL POPULATIONS WITH THOSE MOST LIKELY TO PHENOCONVERT DURING THE COURSE OF THE TRIAL. WE WILL ALSO DETERMINE THE SUITABILITY OF THIS RISK SCORE AS A POTENTIAL OUTCOME MEASURE FOR FUTURE PREVENTION TRIALS BY CHARACTERIZING ITS TEMPORAL COURSE AND ASSESSING ITS RELIABILITY AND SENSITIVITY TO CHANGE AS PRE-SYMPTOMATIC DISEASE EVOLVES. WHILE THIS C9 ALS/FTD PREVENT STUDY IS AGNOSTIC TO THE SPECIFICS OF ANY THERAPEUTIC CANDIDATE THAT MIGHT EMERGE, THE FOUNDATIONS LAID THROUGH THE STUDY OUTLINED IN THIS PROPOSAL ARE ESSENTIAL FOR ALL PREVENTION TRIALS. MOREOVER, THIS STUDY IS UNIQUE IN THE TRULY EQUAL CREDENCE IT GIVES TO CONSIDERATIONS AROUND THE MOTOR NEURON AND COGNITION/BEHAVIOR PHENOTYPES, WHICH IS ESSENTIAL TO PREPARING FOR TRIALS THAT AIM TO PREVENT BOTH ALS AND FTD IN PRE-SYMPTOMATIC C9ORF72 CARRIERS.

description: THE BRAIN GIFTING COUNSELING PROGRAM: A NOVEL PEER-PROFESSIONAL INTERVENTION TO ENHANCE BRAIN DONATION AMONG OLDER ADULTS AT RISK FOR ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS - PROJECT SUMMARY ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD) ARE AMONG THE MOST COMMON NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES, AFFECTING 7.1 MILLION AMERICANS. ADRD ACCOUNTS FOR $384 BILLION IN HEALTHCARE COSTS AND $413.5 BILLION IN UNPAID WAGES FOR INFORMAL CAREGIVERS ANNUALLY, CONSTITUTING BOTH A PUBLIC HEALTH AND FINANCIAL CRISIS. WHILE RESEARCH HAS DRIVEN SIGNIFICANT PROGRESS IN UNDERSTANDING AND TREATING THE DISEASE, COMPLEX AD PATHOGENESIS IS STILL POORLY UNDERSTOOD, AND TREATMENT EFFECTIVENESS REMAINS LOW. POST-MORTEM AUTOPSY OF THE BRAIN ENABLES CORRELATION OF CLINICAL DATA WITH UNDERLYING ETIOLOGY, ANALYSIS OF MIXED PATHOLOGIES AND COMORBIDITIES, DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF IN VIVO BIOMARKERS, AND IDENTIFICATION OF NOVEL TREATMENT TARGETS; AS SUCH, BRAIN DONATION REPRESENTS AN UNPARALLELED AND ESSENTIAL TOOL FOR PROGRESS IN THE FIELD OF ADRD. DESPITE THE URGENT NEED, BRAIN DONATION HAS DECLINED STEADILY SINCE THE 1950S DUE TO POOR AWARENESS OF BRAIN DONATION NEED AND PROCEDURES, SUPERFICIAL FAMILY INTEGRATION, POOR RETENTION OF CONSENTED PARTICIPANTS, AND MEDICAL/RESEARCH MISTRUST. THIS PROJECT LEVERAGES INTERDISCIPLINARY EXPERTISE AND RESOURCES ACROSS THE MICHIGAN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE RESEARCH CENTER (MADRC) AND THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN BRAIN BANK TO TARGET THESE POINTS OF FAILURE IN THE BRAIN DONATION PROCESS. GROUNDED IN THE TRANSTHEORETICAL MODEL OF HEALTH BEHAVIOR CHANGE AND INCORPORATING TENETS OF COMMUNITY ENGAGED RESEARCH, WE TEST TWO PRAGMATIC INTERVENTIONS: A BRAIN GIFTING EDUCATION TOOLKIT AND A PEER-PROFESSIONAL FACILITATED BRAIN GIFTING COUNSELING PROGRAM. FOCUSING ON PARTICIPANTS IN THE RESEARCH REGISTRY AND LONGITUDINAL COHORT OF THE MADRC AND THEIR FAMILIES, WE EMPLOY RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL DESIGN TO SYSTEMATICALLY TEST ACUTE AND LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF THESE PROGRAMS ON FAMILIARITY WITH BRAIN DONATION (AIM 1), CONSENT FOR BRAIN DONATION AND CONFIDENCE IN THIS DECISION (AIM 2), AND RETENTION IN THE BRAIN DONATION PROGRAM (AIM 3). IF EFFECTIVE, THESE PRACTICAL INTERVENTIONS WILL DRIVE ENGAGEMENT IN BRAIN DONATION NOT ONLY LOCALLY, BUT THROUGHOUT ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE CENTER NETWORK AND BEYOND. IN TURN, ENHANCED BRAIN DONATION RATES WILL PROVIDE THE LINKAGE TO EXISTING LONGITUDINAL PRE-MORTEM DATABASES NECESSARY TO REALIZE THE POTENTIAL OF THE MASSIVE FINANCIAL AND SCIENTIFIC INVESTMENT FEDERAL TAXPAYERS AND RESEARCHERS HAVE MADE IN ADRD RESEARCH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A METABOLIC SENSOR–DRIVEN METABOLITE REPAIR SYSTEM MAINTAINS MUSCLE STEM CELL HOMEOSTASIS - PROJECT SUMMARY LOSS OF SKELETAL MUSCLE STEM CELL (SATELLITE CELL, SC) FUNCTION IS A CENTRAL DRIVER OF IMPAIRED REGENERATION, PROGRESSIVE MUSCLE WASTING, AND FRAILTY IN AGING, MUSCULAR DYSTROPHIES, AND METABOLIC DISEASES. THESE CONDITIONS REPRESENT A RAPIDLY GROWING PUBLIC HEALTH BURDEN, CONTRIBUTING TO LOSS OF MOBILITY AND INDEPENDENCE, DIMINISHED QUALITY OF LIFE AND INCREASED HEALTHCARE COSTS WORLDWIDE, YET NO EFFECTIVE THERAPIES EXIST TO PRESERVE SC FUNCTION OR RESILIENCE. SCS ARE NORMALLY POISED TO REMAIN QUIESCENT UNTIL ACTIVATED BY INJURY OR STRESS, AT WHICH POINT THEY EXPAND, DIFFERENTIATE TO REPAIR DAMAGED FIBERS, OR SELF-RENEW TO REPLENISH THE STEM CELL POOL. WITH AGE AND DISEASE, THIS BALANCE OF FATE DECISIONS IS DISRUPTED, LEADING TO STEM CELL DEPLETION AND IMPAIRED REGENERATIVE CAPACITY. ALTHOUGH METABOLISM IS RECOGNIZED AS A CRITICAL REGULATOR OF SC FATE TRANSITIONS, THE MECHANISMS THAT PRESERVE MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION AND METABOLIC FIDELITY ACROSS THE LIFESPAN REMAIN POORLY DEFINED. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES IDENTIFY THE CREB-REGULATED TRANSCRIPTIONAL COACTIVATORS (CRTCS) AS ESSENTIAL, PREVIOUSLY UNEXPLORED METABOLIC SENSORS IN SCS. WE DISCOVERED THAT CRTCS PRESERVE MITOCHONDRIAL RESPIRATION NOT BY REGULATING CANONICAL PGC1Α–DRIVEN BIOGENESIS, BUT THROUGH CONTROLLING THE MITOCHONDRIAL METABOLITE REPAIR ENZYME FAHD2A. FAHD2A PREVENTS BUILDUP OF TOXIC ENOL-OXALOACETATE, A BY-PRODUCT THAT INHIBITS SUCCINATE DEHYDROGENASE, THEREBY SAFEGUARDING OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION AND SC PROLIFERATION. IMPORTANTLY, FAHD2A LEVELS DECLINE WITH AGE IN BOTH MOUSE AND HUMAN SCS, LINKING DISRUPTION OF THIS PATHWAY TO SC ATTRITION AND REGENERATIVE FAILURE. THESE FINDINGS UNCOVER A CRTC–DRIVEN METABOLITE REPAIR SYSTEM AS A CRITICAL SAFEGUARD OF SC METABOLISM AND FUNCTION. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO ESTABLISH THE CRTC- FAHD2A AXIS AS A NOVEL METABOLIC SENSOR–DRIVEN METABOLITE REPAIR PATHWAY THAT PROTECTS MITOCHONDRIAL METABOLISM, PRESERVES STEM CELL COMPETENCE, AND SUSTAINS REGENERATION DURING INJURY AND AGING. AIM 1 WILL DEFINE THE FUNCTION OF CRTCS IN SC MITOCHONDRIAL HOMEOSTASIS USING SC-SPECIFIC CRTC MUTANT MICE, HIGH- RESOLUTION IMAGING, AND MITOCHONDRIAL DIAGNOSTICS TO TEST HOW CRTCS PRESERVE RESPIRATION EFFICIENCY INDEPENDENT OF BIOGENESIS. AIM 2 WILL DISSECT THE MECHANISM BY WHICH CRTCS REGULATE FAHD2A, AND TEST WHETHER FAHD2A RESTORATION RESCUES MITOCHONDRIAL AND REGENERATIVE DEFECTS IN CRTC-DEFICIENT SCS. AIM 3 WILL ESTABLISH THE ROLE OF THE CRTC-FAHD2A AXIS IN AGING, ASSESSING HOW THIS PATHWAY IS ALTERED IN AGED MOUSE AND HUMAN SCS, WHETHER ITS LOSS EXACERBATES MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION AND REGENERATIVE FAILURE, AND WHETHER REACTIVATION REJUVENATES AGED SCS IN VIVO AND IN PRIMARY HUMAN MYOBLASTS ACROSS THE AGING SPECTRUM. COMPLETION OF THESE STUDIES WILL ESTABLISH A NEW PARADIGM IN STEM CELL BIOLOGY BY IDENTIFYING METABOLITE REPAIR AS A FUNDAMENTAL SAFEGUARD OF MITOCHONDRIAL INTEGRITY AND REGENERATIVE CAPACITY. THIS WORK REFRAMES STEM CELL DECLINE DURING AGING AS A BREAKDOWN OF METABOLITE QUALITY CONTROL AND POSITIONING CRTCS AND FAHD2A AS THERAPEUTIC TARGETS TO PRESERVE MUSCLE HEALTH AND COMBAT MUSCLE-WASTING DISEASES.

description: DYING ALONE: UNDERSTANDING AND ADDRESSING END-OF-LIFE ISOLATION AMONG OLDER ADULTS - PROJECT ABSTRACT DYING ALONE IS A FEARED OUTCOME AMONG OLDER ADULTS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES, AND AN INCREASINGLY COMMON OCCURRENCE AFFECTING NEARLY 1 IN 5 DEATHS. THE CONSEQUENCES OF DYING ALONE OR SOCIAL ISOLATION AT THE END OF LIFE ARE PROFOUND. ISOLATED OLDER ADULTS REPORT UP TO TWICE THE SYMPTOM BURDEN, INCLUDING DEPRESSION, LONELINESS, AND PAIN; OFTEN MUST NAVIGATE OVERWHELMING MEDICAL LOGISTICS ALONE; AND ARE LESS LIKELY TO ENROLL IN HOSPICE AND MORE LIKELY TO USE ACUTE CARE LIKE THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT. DURING HEALTH CRISES COMMON TO THE END OF LIFE (I.E. NEW CANCER DIAGNOSES, HOSPITALIZATIONS, SUDDEN DEBILITATING SYMPTOMS), THEY MAY HAVE FEW CONFIDANTES OR HEALTH CARE AGENTS TO GUIDE DECISION MAKING, AND HAVE DIFFICULTY RETURNING HOME AFTER HOSPITALIZATIONS DUE TO A LACK OF CAREGIVERS, LEADING TO LOSS OF INDEPENDENCE IN THE COMMUNITY. DESPITE THE MAGNITUDE OF THE CLINICAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH NEED, KEY KNOWLEDGE GAPS IMPEDE SOLUTIONS. PRIOR QUANTITATIVE WORK HAS BEEN LARGELY FOCUSED ON THE MONTHS AND WEEKS BEFORE DEATH. IN REALITY, END-OF-LIFE ISOLATION DEVELOPS OVER MANY YEARS OR DECADES THROUGH BEHAVIORAL CHOICES, SHIFTS IN SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS, AND KEY HEALTH EVENTS. UNDERSTANDING LONGITUDINAL TRAJECTORIES LEADING TO END-OF-LIFE ISOLATION CAN INFORM CLINICAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH INTERVENTIONS. IN ADDITION, THE LIVED EXPERIENCE OF SOCIALLY ISOLATED, SERIOUSLY ILL OLDER ADULTS IS POORLY UNDERSTOOD. PRIOR STUDIES ARE LIMITED TO SMALL, COMMUNITY-BASED SAMPLES AND HAVE FOCUSED UNIQUE SCENARIOS (E.G. ISOLATED OLDER ADULTS LACKING DECI- SIONAL CAPACITY, SOCIAL RESTRICTIONS DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC). MISSING FROM PUBLISHED LITERATURE ARE HOW OLDER ADULTS MANAGE COMPLEX CARE NEEDS OF SERIOUS ILLNESS ON THEIR OWN, AND THE PERSPECTIVES OF CLINICIANS FROM DIFFERENT CARE SETTINGS (COMMUNITY, HOSPITAL, NURSING HOME, HOSPICE) WHO STRUGGLE TO CARE FOR THIS POPULA- TION. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS THEREFORE TO DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF THE EXPE- RIENCE OF “DYING ALONE” AND TO USE THIS KNOWLEDGE TO IDENTIFY CLINICAL RECOMMENDATIONS AND INTERVENTION STRATE- GIES. WE WILL USE A CONVERGENT, PARALLEL MIXED-METHODS DESIGN THAT LEVERAGES THE NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE HEALTH AND RETIREMENT STUDY (HRS) LINKED TO MEDICARE CLAIMS DATA AND RIGOROUS QUALITATIVE METHODS. WE HAVE THE FOLLOWING AIMS: 1) IDENTIFY DISTINCT TRAJECTORIES LEADING TO END-OF-LIFE SOCIAL ISOLATION AND THEIR RELATIONSHIP TO HEALTH OUTCOMES; 2) UNDERSTAND HOW SOCIALLY ISOLATED OLDER ADULTS EXPERIENCE SERIOUS ILLNESS AT THE END OF LIFE AND MULTI-LEVEL BARRIERS AND FACILITATORS TO CARE; AND 3) DEVELOP CONSENSUS CLINICAL RECOMMENDATIONS AND IDEN- TIFY PRIORITY COMPONENTS FOR FUTURE INTERVENTIONS FOR ISOLATED OLDER ADULTS AT THE END OF LIFE THROUGH A SYNTHESIS OF FINDINGS AND A MODIFIED DELPHI PANEL. THIS RESEARCH IS CRITICAL TO MEETING THE NEEDS OF OLDER ADULTS WHO ARE DY- ING ALONE, A LARGE AND HIGHLY MARGINALIZED POPULATION. BECAUSE THESE TOPICS ARE VASTLY UNDERSTUDIED, WE ANTICI- PATE THAT THIS WORK WILL OPEN A NEW LINE OF RESEARCH ON ISOLATION AT THE END OF LIFE, INCLUDING PROPOSALS TO TEST NEW INTERVENTIONS FOR HIGH-RISK GROUPS, EVALUATE POLICY LEVERS, AND DESIGN PRAGMATIC TRIALS THAT INTEGRATE SOCIAL AND CLINICAL CARE IN SERIOUS ILLNESS AND PALLIATIVE SETTINGS.

description: PATHWAY-SPECIFIC VULNERABILITY OF DOPAMINE-GLUTAMATE NEURONS IN AGING AND MEMORY - PROJECT SUMMARY DOPAMINE (DA) NEURONS IN THE VENTRAL TEGMENTAL AREA (VTA) PLAY A CRUCIAL ROLE IN MEMORY AND OTIVATION, AND THEIR FUNCTION DECLINES WITH AGE. IMAGING STUDIES HAVE CONSISTENTLY SHOWN THAT AGE-RELATED DA DEFICITS ARE NOT UNIFORM, POSSIBLY TARGETING DIFFERENT SUBPOPULATIONS. YET, TO THIS DAY, WE DO NOT KNOW WHICH DA NEURON SUBPOPULATIONS ARE MOST VULNERABLE TO AGING AND THEIR CONTRIBUTION TO COGNITIVE DEFICITS. THIS CIRCUIT-SPECIFIC DYSFUNCTION MAY EXPLAIN WHY BRAIN-WIDE DA INTERVENTIONS YIELD MIXED COGNITIVE RESULTS. TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP, WE USED INTERSECTIONAL VIRAL STRATEGIES TO LABEL DIFFERENT DA SUBPOPULATIONS. WE FOUND THAT DA NEURONS CO- RELEASING GLUTAMATE (DA-GLU NEURONS) ARE PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TO AGING. VTA DA-GLU NEURONS PROJECT DENSELY TO THE LATERAL ENTORHINAL CORTEX (LEC) AND NUCLEUS ACCUMBENS (NAC) SHELL, REGIONS CRUCIAL FOR MEMORY AND MOTIVATION, RESPECTIVELY. THE DETERIORATION OF DA-GLU NEURONS WITH AGING IS OBSERVED IN LEC DA TERMINALS AS EARLY AS 14 MONTHS BUT ONLY PROGRESSES TO THE NAC SHELL BY 24 MONTHS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE PROGRESSIVE DETERIORATION OF DA-GLU NEURON FUNCTION WITH AGING RESULTS IN PATHWAY-SPECIFIC AND AGE-SPECIFIC BEHAVIORAL DEFICITS, WHICH INITIALLY IMPAIR MEMORY AND LATER EXTEND THEIR EFFECTS TO MEMORY AND MOTIVATION. WE WILL ADDRESS THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IN 3 AIMS. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF AGE-RELATED DA- GLU NEURON DETERIORATION ON DA AND GLU RELEASE ACROSS BY COMBINING DATA FROM FIBER PHOTOMETRY, PATCH-CLAMP TECHNIQUES AND MATRIX ASSISTED LASER DESORPTION/IONIZATION (MALDI) IMAGING. THIS RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE A COMPREHENSIVE ANATOMICAL ROADMAP OF PATHWAY-SPECIFIC DA DYSFUNCTIONS IN AGING. SINCE MOLECULAR MARKERS NECESSARY FOR THE CO-RELEASE OF DA AND GLU FROM VTA DA NEURONS DECREASE WITH AGE (I.E., TYROSINE HYDROXYLASE, TH, AND VESICULAR GLU TRANSPORTER 2, VGLUT2), AIM 2 WILL PARSE THE SELECTIVE CONTRIBUTION OF TH (AIM 2.1) AND VGLUT2 (AIM 2.2) FROM DA-GLU NEURONS TO AGE-RELATED DEFICITS IN NOVELTY DISCRIMINATION (LEC- DEPENDENT BEHAVIOR) AND BEHAVIORAL SWITCHING (NAC-DEPENDENT BEHAVIOR). FINALLY, AIM 3 WILL DETERMINE HOW AGING AFFECTS NOVELTY-INDUCED DOPAMINE RELEASE IN THE LEC AND NAC SHELL USING FIBER PHOTOMETRY AND DA SENSORS. THIS AIM WILL INVESTIGATE HOW CHANGES DA DYNAMICS CORRELATE WITH BEHAVIORAL PERFORMANCE IN NOVELTY DISCRIMINATION AND BEHAVIORAL SWITCHING TASKS (AIM 3.1). WE WILL THEN USE CLOSED-LOOP OPTOSTIMULATION TO ACTIVATE DA TERMINALS IN THE LEC AND NAC SHELL OF OLD MICE AND ESTABLISH STRATEGIES TO REVERSE THE AGE-ASSOCIATED BEHAVIORAL DEFECTS. UNDERSTANDING CIRCUITS AND MECHANISMS IMPACTED BY THE DECLINE OF DA SYSTEM IN AGING WILL UNCOVER NEW STRATEGIES THAT MITIGATE AGE-RELATED COGNITIVE DEFICITS.
