description: STRENGTHENING U.S. PHARMACEUTICAL SUPPLY CHAINS: UNDERSTANDING, PREDICTING, AND PREVENTING DRUG SHORTAGES (SUPPLY-US) - MOST PRESCRIPTIONS FILLED IN THE U.S. ARE DISPENSED TO OLDER ADULTS. MEDICATIONS ARE A CORNERSTONE OF MANAGING CHRONIC CONDITIONS, WHICH ARE PREVALENT IN OLDER ADULTS. THE UNAVAILABILITY OF MEDICATIONS DURING DRUG SHORTAGES CAN LEAD TO SIGNIFICANT ADVERSE OUTCOMES, ESPECIALLY IN A HIGH-RISK POPULATION. HOWEVER, OUR MEDICATION ACCESS IS DEPENDENT ON A COMPLEX GLOBAL SUPPLY CHAIN; MOST MEDICATIONS TAKEN BY OLDER ADULTS IN THE U.S. ARE MANUFACTURED OVERSEAS. ONE METHOD TO MITIGATE THE IMPACT OF DRUG SHORTAGES RECOMMENDED BY OTHER COUNTRIES IS AN AT-RISK MEDICINE LIST. AT-RISK MEDICINE LISTS CONSIDER CLINICAL IMPORTANCE AND SUPPLY CHAIN VULNERABILITIES. MEANWHILE, PRIOR WORK ON DRUG SHORTAGES HAS BEEN LIMITED TO DRUG SHORTAGE INCIDENCE (PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF A SHORTAGE) AND HAS IGNORED THE LARGE VARIABILITY IN SHORTAGE DURATION AND AMOUNT OF SUPPLY DECREASE. THEREFORE, CONSIDERING SHORTAGE INTENSITY IS CRITICAL TO DESIGNING INTERVENTIONS THAT MITIGATE SEVERE OR PROLONGED DISRUPTIONS AND ENSURE OLDER ADULTS MAINTAIN MEDICATION ACCESS. OUR OVERALL OBJECTIVE IS TO ASSESS DRUG SHORTAGE INTENSITY, FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH HIGHER INTENSITY SHORTAGES, AND BUILD UPON OUR PAST INNOVATIVE COMBINATION OF DATASETS TO DEVELOP AN AT-RISK MEDICINE LIST TO HELP PRIORITIZE DRUGS CRITICAL TO THE CARE OF OLDER ADULTS. GUIDED BY PRELIMINARY DATA, WE WILL BE PURSUING 3 SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) MEASURE AND COMPARE SHORTAGE INTENSITY AND FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH SHORTAGE INTENSITY IN THE U.S. AND CANADA, 2) DEVELOP A U.S.-SPECIFIC AT-RISK MEDICINE LIST CONSIDERING CLINICAL IMPORTANCE AND SUPPLY CHAIN DISRUPTIONS, AND 3) DETERMINE THE VALIDITY, ACCURACY AND USABILITY OF OPERATIONALIZING AN AT-RISK MEDICINE LIST. THE PROPOSED STUDY IS ALIGNED WITH THE RESEARCH PRIORITY AREAS OF THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE ON AGING (HEALTH-SYSTEM DECISIONS; IMPROVING MEDICATION MANAGEMENT AND AVOIDING ADVERSE OUTCOMES IN OLDER ADULTS). WE PROPOSE TO CONDUCT A POPULATION-BASED STUDY TO ASSESS DRUG SHORTAGE INTENSITY AND IDENTIFY DRUG- AND SUPPLY CHAIN-CHARACTERISTICS ASSOCIATED WITH HIGHER INTENSITY SHORTAGES. WE WILL ALSO COMPARE SHORTAGES IN THE U.S. TO CANADA, COUNTRIES WITH DIFFERENT SHORTAGE MITIGATION STRATEGIES. WE WILL USE THESE DATA AND LEVERAGE PRIOR WORK TO CREATE AN AT-RISK MEDICINE LIST THAT FOCUSES ON DRUGS WITH SUPPLY CHAIN VULNERABILITIES WHICH ARE CLINICALLY IMPORTANT TO OLDER ADULTS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF THIS STUDY INCLUDE TIMELY EVIDENCE ON THE IMPACT OF HIGHER INTENSITY SHORTAGES AND AN AT-RISK MEDICINE LIST TESTED FOR USABILITY AND ACCURACY. BY COMPARING SHORTAGES IN THE U.S. AND CANADA, WE WILL PROVIDE VALUABLE INSIGHTS ON HOW SHORTAGE MITIGATION STRATEGIES IMPROVE RESILIENCY OF THE GLOBAL SUPPLY CHAIN. AN EXPERT PANEL OF KEY STAKEHOLDERS WILL AID IN OPERATIONALIZATION, DISSEMINATION AND IDENTIFY RECOMMENDATIONS FOR EFFECTIVE SHORTAGE MITIGATION STRATEGIES BASED ON OUR RESULTS. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO PLAN FOR FUTURE DRUG SHORTAGES, PROVIDE STRATEGIES TO MITIGATE THE IMPACT OF SHORTAGES, AND INFORM INITIATIVES TO DECREASE THE IMPACT OF DRUG SHORTAGES ON PATIENT OUTCOMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NONPARAMETRIC METHODS TO ADDRESS SCIENTIFIC QUESTIONS IN AGING INTEGRATING REAL-WORLD AND RESEARCH DATABASES - PROJECT SUMMARY ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (EHR) DATA COLLECTED DURING ROUTINE CLINICAL CARE ARE A COST-EFFECTIVE DATA RESOURCE TO INFORM STUDIES OF DISEASE PATHOLOGY AND PROGNOSIS. IN AGING RESEARCH FOCUSING ON EYE-BRAIN CONNECTIONS, THERE IS GREAT INTEREST IN USING EHR DATA TO DEVELOP PROGNOSTIC TOOLS FOR EYE DISEASES (E.G., AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION [AMD]), AND TO UNDERSTAND THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN OPHTHALMIC BIOMARKERS AND RISK OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD). HOWEVER, IN LARGE COHORTS SUCH AS THE EYE ADULT CHANGES IN THOUGHT (EYE ACT) STUDY, TARGET VARIABLES ARE OFTEN EXTRACTED FROM THE EHR, PARTICULARLY UNSTRUCTURED TEXT IN CLINICAL NOTES, USING ERROR-PRONE TEXT-MINING ALGORITHMS. AS IN MANY OTHER SETTINGS, VALIDATED DATA BY CHART ABSTRACTION IN EYE ACT ARE ONLY AVAILABLE ON A SUBSET OF THE COHORT. MACHINE LEARNING METHODS THAT LEVERAGE DETAILED DATA OF VARYING QUALITY CAN IMPROVE ACCURACY AND ROBUSTNESS OF ANALYSES TO PROVIDE RELIABLE SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL EVIDENCE. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL ADDRESS THREE KEY METHODOLOGICAL ISSUES THAT REMAIN IN USING MACHINE LEARNING TO INCORPORATE ERROR-PRONE AND VALIDATED EHR DATA INTO ANALYSES TO ANSWER SCIENTIFIC QUESTIONS: 1) IMPROVING ACCURACY AND PRECISION OF MACHINE-LEARNED INVERSE-PROBABILITY WEIGHTED (IPW) ANALYSES; AND IMPROVING DESIGN OF VALIDATION STUDIES FOR 2) CAUSAL INFERENCE AND 3) PREDICTION MODEL EVALUATION. MANY ANALYSES THAT COMBINE ERROR-PRONE AND VALIDATED DATA INVOLVE IPW ANALYSES OF THE VALIDATED SUBSET. WEIGHTS DERIVED USING MACHINE LEARNING METHODS, WHILE USEFUL FOR PREDICTION, CAN RESULT IN OVERLY VARIABLE WEIGHTS, LEADING TO REDUCED ACCURACY OR PRECISION OF AN ESTIMATOR. THIS PROBLEM CAN BE EXACERBATED IN SMALL SAMPLES. WE WILL DEVELOP METHODS THAT PROPERLY INCORPORATE MACHINE LEARNING-BASED WEIGHTS, COMBINING ADVANCES IN GENERALIZED RAKING WITH TARGETED LEARNING (E.G., TARGETED MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD ESTIMATION) FOR ROBUST AND STABLE WEIGHTS. WHEN DESIGNING DATA- VALIDATION STUDIES, SIMPLE RANDOM SAMPLING IS OFTEN INEFFICIENT; STRATIFIED SAMPLES CAN INCREASE EFFICIENCY BY VALIDATING KEY SUBGROUPS AND BY UTILIZING EXISTING OPTIMAL DESIGN METHODS THAT MINIMIZE THE VARIANCE OF REGRESSION PARAMETER ESTIMATES. WE WILL GENERALIZE THESE OPTIMAL DESIGN APPROACHES TO ESTIMATE AVERAGE TREATMENT EFFECTS AND OTHER TARGETS OF CAUSAL INFERENCE, ADDRESSING AN IMPORTANT VOID IN THE CURRENT OPTIMAL STRATIFIED-DESIGN LITERATURE. WE WILL FURTHER EXTEND THESE METHODS TO DEVELOP THE OPTIMAL DESIGN FOR EVALUATING A PREDICTION MODEL AND FOR SIMULTANEOUSLY EVALUATING A MODEL AND PERFORMING CAUSAL INFERENCE. BY COMBINING ADVANCES IN MACHINE LEARNING, TARGETED LEARNING, AND SURVEY STATISTICS, WE WILL PROVIDE MORE ROBUST AND PRECISE STATISTICAL TOOLS TO STUDY THE EYE-BRAIN CONNECTION IN AGING AND TO GENERATE RELIABLE EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE ON ACTIONABLE FACTORS. OUR WORK USING EYE ACT HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM PREVENTIVE CARE FOR IMPORTANT AGING OUTCOMES LIKE AMD AND ADRD, WHILE ALSO SERVING AS A STATISTICAL FRAMEWORK FOR IMPROVED INFERENCE AND STUDY DESIGN MORE BROADLY IN BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH THAT LEVERAGES OBSERVATIONAL DATA WITH MISSING OR ERROR-PRONE DATA.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A PRAGMATIC CLINICAL TRIAL TO IMPROVE SCREENING FOR COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT IN OLDER ADULTS WITH DIABETES - PROJECT ABSTRACT IN THE UNITED STATES, MORE THAN 17 MILLION ADULTS AGED 65 YEARS AND OLDER LIVE WITH DIABETES MELLITUS, A CHRONIC CONDITION THAT SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASES THE RISK OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD). IN OLDER ADULTS WITH DIABETES, COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND ADRD IS A MAJOR RISK FACTOR FOR COMPLICATIONS, INCLUDING SEVERE HYPOGLYCEMIA, FALLS, FRACTURES, FRAILTY, AND MORTALITY. ALTHOUGH COGNITIVE SCREENING IS RECOMMENDED TO REDUCE OVERTREATMENT AND COMPLICATIONS, THE RATES OF SCREENING IN OLDER ADULTS WITH DIABETES ARE UNKNOWN. MOREOVER, SIMPLE APPROACHES THAT CAN BE SCALED TO IMPROVE POPULATION-WIDE SCREENING ARE LACKING. IN THIS PROJECT, WE PROPOSE TO LEVERAGE ADVANCED NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING (NLP) AND LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS (LLMS) TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE NOVEL TOOLS FOR IDENTIFYING COGNITIVE AND ADRD SCREENING IN ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD DATA. WE WILL THEN CONDUCT A PRAGMATIC TRIAL OF A CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT (CDS) INTERVENTION TO IMPROVE GERIATRIC COGNITIVE SCREENING, DIAGNOSIS, AND MANAGEMENT IN OLDER ADULTS WITH COMORBID DIABETES. AS THE U.S. POPULATION CONTINUES TO AGE, THE DUAL BURDEN OF AGE-RELATED COGNITIVE DECLINE/ADRD AND DIABETES WILL GROW RAPIDLY. OUR STUDY WILL SUPPORT SCALABLE, SYSTEM-LEVEL INTERVENTIONS TO SUPPORT GERIATRIC SCREENING PRACTICES, AND ULTIMATELY PROMOTE HEALTHY AGING, PREVENT INJURY, AND IMPROVE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR OLDER ADULTS WITH COMORBID DIABETES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MEASURING MEANINGFUL OUTCOMES FOR ADULTS WITH COCHLEAR IMPLANTS ACROSS THE LIFESPAN - PROJECT SUMMARY HEARING LOSS (HL) IS THE MOST COMMON SENSORY DISORDER IN THE U.S., AFFECTING OVER HALF OF ADULTS OVER AGE 65. NEARLY A QUARTER OF THOSE HAVE HL SEVERE ENOUGH TO BENEFIT FROM A SURGICALLY PLACED COCHLEAR IMPLANT (CI). HEARING LOSS CONTRIBUTES TO POORER COMMUNICATION ABILITIES AND IS ASSOCIATED WITH COGNITIVE DECLINE, SOCIAL WITHDRAWAL, AND REDUCED QUALITY OF LIFE (QOL). WHILE TREATMENT WITH A CI MAY HELP MITIGATE THESE NEGATIVE IMPACTS, SPEECH COMMUNICATION OUTCOMES REMAIN HIGHLY VARIABLE. ADDITIONALLY, UP TO 42% OF CI RECIPIENTS REPORT DECISIONAL REGRET IN PURSUING IMPLANTATION, WITH OLDER ADULTS DEMONSTRATING POORER OUTCOMES AND REPORTING HIGHER DECISION REGRET. NONETHELESS, THE EFFECTS OF AGING ON CI OUTCOMES REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. ADDITIONALLY, CURRENT CLINICAL MEASURES OF SPEECH PERCEPTION USED TO EVALUATE CI OUTCOMES FAIL TO CAPTURE THE REAL-WORLD LIVED EXPERIENCES OF CI RECIPIENTS. AS A RESULT, WE LACK MEANINGFUL ASSESSMENT TOOLS TO IDENTIFY AND REHABILITATE INDIVIDUALS WHO STRUGGLE TO COMMUNICATE IN THE REAL WORLD. THUS, A SIGNIFICANT GAP IN KNOWLEDGE REMAINS REGARDING THE IMPACTS OF CIS ON MEANINGFUL OUTCOMES ACROSS THE ADULT LIFESPAN, HOW NEEDS DIFFER ACROSS AGES, AND THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING AGE-RELATED DIFFERENCES. THIS PROJECT WILL CHARACTERIZE AGE-SPECIFIC COMMUNICATION AND PSYCHOSOCIAL OUTCOMES THROUGH CARRYING OUT THREE SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 WILL CHARACTERIZE AGE-RELATED DIFFERENCES USING A NEW CORE CI OUTCOME SET AND A BATTERY OF AUDITORY AND COGNITIVE TESTS WITH QUANTITATIVE METHODS. AIM 2 WILL IDENTIFY THE SHARED AND UNIQUE COMMUNICATIVE AND PSYCHOSOCIAL NEEDS ACROSS AGE GROUPS USING QUALITATIVE APPROACHES. AIM 3 WILL INTEGRATE QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE FINDINGS TO IDENTIFY AGE- SPECIFIC OUTCOME PRIORITIES. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT CI USERS WILL DEMONSTRATE AGE-SPECIFIC DIFFERENCES IN COMMUNICATION AND PSYCHOSOCIAL FUNCTIONS AS WELL AS DISTINCT NEEDS. FINDINGS WILL LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR DEVELOPMENT OF AN ECOLOGICALLY MEANINGFUL TOOLBOX OF CI OUTCOME MEASURES RELEVANT FOR DEVELOPING INDIVIDUAL PROFILES OF NEEDS AND ABILITIES OF ADULTS WITH HEARING LOSS ACROSS THE LIFESPAN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ABERRANT NUCLEAR MATERIAL PROPERTIES IN AGING CELLS - THE NUCLEUS UNDERGOES DRAMATIC ORGANIZATIONAL CHANGES DURING SENESCENCE, INCLUDING CHROMATIN REDISTRIBUTION AND ALTERED LAMIN NETWORKS, BUT WHETHER THESE STRUCTURAL ALTERATIONS AFFECT THE PHYSICAL PROPERTIES OF THE NUCLEAR INTERIOR REMAINS UNKNOWN. THIS REPRESENTS A CRITICAL GAP BECAUSE TRANSCRIPTION AND SPLICING DEPEND ON LARGE MACROMOLECULAR COMPLEXES OPERATING AT THE MESOSCALE (10-200 NM), WHERE PHYSICAL PROPERTIES LIKE MOLECULAR CROWDING AND VISCOELASTICITY PROFOUNDLY INFLUENCE BIOCHEMICAL REACTIONS. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF THIS PROPOSAL IS THAT AGE-RELATED ALTERATIONS IN NUCLEAR PHYSICAL PROPERTIES DIRECTLY CONTRIBUTE TO TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND SPLICING DYSREGULATION CHARACTERISTIC OF CELLULAR AGING. UNTIL NOW, IT WAS EXTREMELY LABOR INTENSIVE TO CHARACTERIZE NUCLEAR PHYSICAL PROPERTIES. WE HAVE OVERCOME THIS BARRIER BY INNOVATION OF MULTIPLE TOOLS INCLUDING NUCLEAR GENETICALLY ENCODED MULTIMERIC NANOPARTICLES (GEMS), A TRANSFORMATIVE TECHNOLOGY ENABLING HIGH-THROUGHPUT CHARACTERIZATION OF NUCLEAR BIOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES FOR THE FIRST TIME. USING GEMS, WE DISCOVERED THAT NUCLEAR FLUIDITY INCREASES DRAMATICALLY DURING BOTH CDK4/6 INHIBITION AND REPLICATIVE SENESCENCE—CONTRARY TO PRIOR EXPECTATIONS OF CHROMATIN RIGIDIFICATION. REMARKABLY, INHIBITING H3K27 TRIMETHYLATION NOT ONLY SUPPRESSES THESE PHYSICAL CHANGES BUT INCREASES REPLICATIVE LIFESPAN AFTER CDK4/6 INHIBITOR TREATMENT, SUGGESTING THAT PHYSICAL CHANGES MAY BE THERAPEUTICALLY TARGETABLE. AIM 1 WILL COMPREHENSIVELY MEASURE NUCLEAR MATERIAL PROPERTIES ACROSS BIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT LENGTHSCALES USING OUR COMPLETE TOOLKIT: NUCGEMS (40-50 NM), NEWLY DEVELOPED LARGER GEMS (140 NM), SYNTHETIC PROTEIN CRYSTALS (200-500 NM), AND SYNDROP CONDENSATES (50 NM-3 ΜM). WE WILL PERFORM MICRORHEOLOGY TO QUANTIFY NUCLEAR FLUIDITY, VISCOSITY, AND DYNAMICS IN YOUNG VERSUS AGED CELLS ACROSS MULTIPLE SENESCENCE MODELS. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE MECHANISMS DRIVING BIOPHYSICAL CHANGES BY SYSTEMATICALLY PERTURBING HISTONE MODIFICATIONS, REMODELING FACTORS, NUCLEAR PERIPHERY COMPONENTS (LAMINS, LINC COMPLEX, NUCLEAR PORES), AND PROTEINS THAT HAVE BEEN REPORTED TO SUBSCALE OR SUPERSCALE WITH CELL SIZE PERTURBATIONS. WE WILL IDENTIFY PERTURBATIONS THAT EITHER RECAPITULATE SENESCENCE-ASSOCIATED NUCLEAR FLUIDITY IN YOUNG CELLS OR RESCUE NORMAL PHYSICAL PROPERTIES IN SENESCENT CELLS. AIM 3 WILL ESTABLISH CAUSAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN NUCLEAR PHYSICAL PROPERTIES AND GENE EXPRESSION BY INTEGRATING RNA-SEQ, SINGLE-MOLECULE TRACKING OF TRANSCRIPTIONAL MACHINERY, AND CHROMATIN CONFORMATION ANALYSIS. WE WILL EXPERIMENTALLY MANIPULATE NUCLEAR PHYSICAL PROPERTIES THROUGH OSMOTIC PERTURBATIONS, SYNTHETIC CONDENSATE EXPRESSION, AND TARGETED GENETIC INTERVENTIONS TO DETERMINE WHETHER PHYSICAL MANIPULATIONS CAN RESCUE SENESCENCE-RELATED TRANSCRIPTIONAL SIGNATURES. THIS WORK WILL ESTABLISH NUCLEAR BIOPHYSICS AS A FUNDAMENTAL AGING MECHANISM, PROVIDE A NEW CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR MAINTAINING NUCLEAR FUNCTION DURING AGING, AND IDENTIFY NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS TO REVERSE CELLULAR SENESCENCE PHENOTYPES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNDERSTANDING AND ENHANCING INTEROCEPTION TOWARD REDUCING EXPLOITATION RISK IN AGING AND ADRD: MECHANISMS AND TRAINABILITY - PROJECT SUMMARY OLDER ADULTS ARE NOTABLY VULNERABLE TO FINANCIAL EXPLOITATION AND SHOW REDUCED DECEPTION DETECTION, WITH INCREASED VULNERABILITY AMONG THOSE WITH AGE-ASSOCIATED NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE (ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS; ADRD). AGING AND ADRD ARE TYPICALLY ASSOCIATED WITH STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL BRAIN CHANGES THAT RESULT IN DAMPENED PHYSIOLOGICAL AND NEURAL RESPONDING TO DECEPTIVE CUES, PRESENTING A LIKELY MECHANISM FOR HIGHER EXPLOITATION RISK IN AGING WITH DEVASTATING CONSEQUENCES. AT PRESENT, AGE-RELATED CHANGES TO THE NEUROBIOLOGICAL PROCESSES THAT SUPPORT PERCEPTION AND INTEGRATION OF ONE'S PHYSIOLOGICAL STATES (INTEROCEPTION), AND THEIR ROLE IN DETERMINING EXPLOITATION RISK IN AGING, REMAIN UNEXPLORED. TO ADDRESS THIS PRESSING PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERN, THIS PROJECT TESTS THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT INTEROCEPTION CONSTITUTES A NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISM OF DECEPTION DETECTION IN AGING AND ADRD. GROUNDED IN OUR CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK, CHANGES IN INTEGRATION FOR SOCIAL DECISIONS IN AGING (CISDA) AND LEVERAGING A PROMISING INTERVENTION TO ENHANCE INTEROCEPTION IN AGING, THIS PROJECT WILL BE THE FIRST TO (I) DELINEATE THE PHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING DECEPTION DETECTION; (II) CHARACTERIZE THE ROLE INTEROCEPTION PLAYS IN DECEPTION DETECTION IN ‘EARLY’ PRECLINICAL AD; (III) DETERMINE THE NEURAL CORRELATES OF INTEROCEPTION IN DECEPTION DETECTION; AND (IV) IDENTIFY PATHWAYS TO IMPROVED INTEROCEPTION AND DECEPTION DETECTION AMONG OLDER ADULTS WITH AND WITHOUT COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS. ACROSS TWO STUDIES AND FOUR AIMS, WE WILL RECRUIT A REPRESENTATIVE SAMPLE OF OLDER ADULTS WITH AND WITHOUT MILD COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT (MCI). IN STUDY 1 (AIMS 1 & 2), 206 PARTICIPANTS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CENTRAL FLORIDA WILL COMPLETE A HEARTBEAT COUNTING TASK (TO MEASURE INTEROCEPTIVE ACCURACY) AND A DECEPTION DETECTION TASK (TO ASSESS DISCERNMENT OF DECEPTION AND TRUTH-TELLING) DURING RECORDING OF PHYSIOLOGICAL RESPONSES. IN STUDY 2, A SEPARATE SAMPLE OF 212 PARTICIPANTS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA WILL PERFORM THESE TASKS WITH MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (AIM 3). THE SAME STUDY 2 PARTICIPANTS WILL RETURN FOR RANDOMIZATION INTO AN INTEROCEPTION TRAINING (DIRECTLY LINKING SENSATIONS DURING EMOTION-INDUCING VIDEOS WITH SENSATIONS TO TRUE-CRIME GENUINE VS. DECEPTIVE PLEADERS) OR A CONTROL CONDITION TO ASSESS TRAINING BENEFITS AND TRANSFER (AIM 4). STUDY 2 PARTICIPANTS WILL ALSO COMPLETE A 6-MONTH FOLLOW-UP TO ASSESS LONGER-TERM (REAL-LIFE) TRAINING EFFECTS. THIS PROJECT WILL EXAMINE INTEROCEPTION AND PHYSIOLOGICAL RESPONSE TO DECEPTION IN AGING/ADRD WITH A DIRECT LINK OF THESE MEASURES TO MULTIMODAL BRAIN DATA FOR IDENTIFICATION OF THE UNDERLYING NEUROBIOLOGICAL SUBSTRATES. THE PROJECT WILL LEVERAGE AN INTEROCEPTION TRAINING WITH DEMONSTRATED EFFECTIVENESS FOR DECEPTION DETECTION IN YOUNGER POPULATIONS, TESTING IT FOR THE FIRST TIME IN AGING/ADRD. COLLECTIVELY, THIS PROJECT’S INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACH WILL TRANSLATE NOVEL BASIC SCIENCE RESEARCH INTO CLINICAL INTERVENTION IMPACT BY DELINEATING THE NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS THAT FACILITATE DECEPTION DETECTION AND IDENTIFYING PATHWAYS TO MITIGATE EXPLOITATION RISK IN COGNITIVELY HEALTHY AGING AND ADRD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE ENERGETIC COST OF WALKING AND MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION IN COGNITIVE AGING AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT EXTENSIVE LITERATURE HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT HIGHER PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND FITNESS LEVELS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH REDUCED RISK OF COGNITIVE DECLINE AND DEMENTIA IN OLDER ADULTS. MOREOVER, INTERVENTION STUDIES INDICATE THAT INCREASING PHYSICAL ACTIVITY CAN YIELD MEASURABLE COGNITIVE IMPROVEMENTS, BUT MODEST EFFECT SIZES HIGHLIGHT THE CRITICAL NEED TO IDENTIFY AND TARGET THE MOST IMPACTFUL PHYSIOLOGICAL FACTORS TO PRODUCE MORE ROBUST AND SUSTAINED COGNITIVE BENEFITS. RECENT K01─FUNDED RESEARCH BY THE PI INDICATES THAT THE ENERGETIC COST OF WALKING (ECOW) ─THE OXYGEN NEEDED FOR CUSTOMARY PACED WALKING─ MAY OPTIMALLY CAPTURE THE BENEFICIAL EFFECTS OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND FITNESS ASSOCIATED WITH COGNITIVE DECLINE. THESE STUDIES DEMONSTRATE THAT A LOWER ECOW (MORE EFFICIENT) IS ASSOCIATED WITH DECREASED ODDS OF AMYLOID POSITIVITY, SLOWER RATES OF HIPPOCAMPAL AND BRAIN ATROPHY, AND LOWER RISK OF COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT. IMPORTANTLY, THE ASSOCIATIONS OF ECOW WITH AMYLOID, BRAIN ATROPHY, AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT ARE STRONGER THAN STANDARD MEASURES OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND FITNESS. ALTHOUGH PRIOR STUDIES SUGGEST THE ECOW MAY BE A NOVEL PHYSICAL FITNESS-RELATED MEASURE, CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAPS PERSIST, PARTICULARLY THE LACK OF LONGITUDINAL INVESTIGATIONS ON AD-SPECIFIC BIOMARKERS AND LIMITED RESEARCH ON POTENTIAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE ECOW-BRAIN ASSOCIATIONS. IN RESPONSE TO NOFO PAR-25-332, THIS APPLICATION WILL DIRECTLY ADDRESS THESE GAPS THROUGH DETERMINING: (1) THE IMPACT OF BASELINE AND LONGITUDINAL ECOW LEVELS ON PROSPECTIVE AD BIOMARKER CHANGES, (2) WHETHER ECOW MODIFIES THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN AD BIOMARKER LEVELS AND CHANGES IN COGNITIVE FUNCTIONING, AND (3) IF SKELETAL MUSCLE MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION IS A POTENTIAL MECHANISM UNDERLYING MEASUREMENTS OF ECOW AND AD BIOMARKERS. THE PROPOSED 5-YEAR LONGITUDINAL STUDY WILL INVESTIGATE THE TEMPORALITY OF, AND EXTENT TO WHICH, CHANGES IN ECOW TRACK WITH CHANGES IN AD BIOMARKERS AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE AND DETERMINE THE INVOLVEMENT OF SKELETAL MUSCLE MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION AS A CANDIDATE UNDERLYING BIOLOGICAL MECHANISM. TARGETING LIFESTYLE BEHAVIORS REMAIN THE LEADING EDGE OF AD AND DEMENTIA PREVENTION RESEARCH. THE PROPOSED AIMS WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING INTO THE PHYSIOLOGICAL AND BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS LINKING PHYSICAL FITNESS AND WALKING PERFORMANCE TO RISK OF COGNITIVE DECLINE, RESULTING IN NEW ACTIONABLE TARGETS FOR SCALABLE CLINICAL AND BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE RISK OF COGNITIVE DECLINE AND DEMENTIA IN OLDER ADULTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HEALTH OUTCOMES AND CARE DELIVERY FOR PEOPLE LIVING WITH DEMENTIA DURING HOME HEALTH AGENCY OWNERSHIP TRANSITIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT EACH YEAR, SIX MILLION MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES RELY ON HOME HEALTH AGENCIES (HHAS) FOR CARE THAT IS CRITICAL YET SUSCEPTIBLE TO ORGANIZATIONAL DISRUPTION. AFTER DISCHARGE FROM A HOSPITALIZATION, THE MAJORITY OF PEOPLE LIVING WITH ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD, PLWD) RECEIVE HOME HEALTH CARE. ADRD MAY REDUCE THEIR CAPACITY TO MONITOR OR RESPOND TO LOW-QUALITY CARE THUS PLACING THEM AT INCREASED HEALTH RISKS FROM OWNERSHIP RELATED DISRUPTIONS. PLWD COMPRISE NEARLY ONE-FIFTH OF ALL HOME HEALTH PATIENTS, AND ANOTHER ONE IN TEN HOME HEALTH PATIENTS RECEIVE AN INCIDENT ADRD DIAGNOSIS WITHIN A YEAR AFTER RECEIVING HHA CARE. EVIDENCE OF SUBSTANTIAL ADRD UNDERDIAGNOSIS SUGGESTS THESE NUMBERS STILL UNDERSTATE THE TRUE SIGNIFICANCE OF ADRD IN HOME HEALTH, UNDERSCORING HOW ESSENTIAL THIS SETTING IS FOR DEMENTIA CARE. FREQUENT OWNERSHIP CHANGES HAVE ALTERED THE HHA LANDSCAPE OVER THE LAST DECADE, WITH UNKNOWN CONSEQUENCES FOR CARE OUTCOMES AND MARKET-WIDE SPILLOVERS. EXISTING RESEARCH FINDS THAT PE OWNERSHIP OF NURSING HOMES AND HOSPITALS REDUCED STAFFING AND INCREASED MORTALITY. RESEARCH ON THE IMPACT OF HHA OWNERSHIP SHIFTS AND CONSOLIDATION ON PATIENT CARE IS SCARCE. GIVEN THE GROWING IMPORTANCE OF HOME-BASED CARE, THIS IS A RESEARCH GAP. THE KEY BARRIER IS A LACK OF DATA INFRASTRUCTURE. CMS ONLY BEGAN RELEASING DETAILED HHA OWNERSHIP INFORMATION IN 2023; SIMILAR NURSING HOME FILES REVEAL MAJOR GAPS, AND NO SYSTEMATIC INVESTIGATION EXISTS FOR HHAS. MOREOVER, NO NATIONAL RESOURCE COMPREHENSIVELY TRACKS HHA OWNERSHIP OR MARKET STRUCTURES OF THE LAST DECADE. WE WILL CREATE THE FIRST LONGITUDINAL PLATFORM ON HHA OWNERSHIP, LINKING TO HEALTH OUTCOMES TO GENERATE NEW SCIENTIFIC INSIGHT ON OWNERSHIP AND CONSOLIDATION IMPACTS IN ADRD CARE. THE RESULTING EVIDENCE WILL DEEPEN KNOWLEDGE OF HOW SUCH PROFOUND CHANGES AFFECT HOME HEALTH DELIVERY AND OUTCOMES FOR THE PATIENTS AND FAMILIES WHO DEPEND ON HOME HEALTH CARE. AIM 1 WILL CHARACTERIZE OWNERSHIP DYNAMICS, QUANTIFY EXPOSURE OF PLWD AND OTHER BENEFICIARIES, AND DISTINGUISH “OWNERSHIP CHURN” FROM CONSOLIDATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT AGENCY ATTRIBUTES (E.G., HIGH ADRD SHARE, STAFFING INTENSITY) AND STATE ACTIONS (E.G., MLTSS ADOPTION, ABSENCE OF CON LAWS) INCREASE ACQUISITION RISK, DISPROPORTIONATELY EXPOSING PLWD. AIM 2 WILL TEST WHETHER OWNERSHIP CHANGE, ESPECIALLY PE ACQUISITIONS, ALTERS CARE DELIVERY (VISIT INTENSITY, STAFFING MIX, CONTINUITY, CODING) AND OUTCOMES (REHOSPITALIZATION, FUNCTIONAL DECLINE, PRESCRIBING, NURSING HOME PLACEMENT, MORTALITY). USING DIFFERENCE-IN-DIFFERENCES, EVENT STUDIES, AND VALIDATED QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL DESIGNS, WE WILL ASSESS WHETHER ADVERSE EFFECTS ARE AMPLIFIED AMONG PLWD AND WHETHER THEY VARY ACROSS STATE AND MARKET SETTINGS. AIM 3 WILL ASSESS MARKET SPILLOVERS, EVALUATING WHETHER PE PENETRATION, CONSOLIDATION, AND OWNERSHIP CHURN AFFECT PATIENTS EVEN AT AGENCIES NOT UNDERGOING OWNERSHIP CHANGE. OUR BROWN AND INDIANA TEAM BRINGS COMPLEMENTARY EXPERTISE IN HEALTH ECONOMICS, ADRD CARE, CAUSAL METHODS, AND DATA INFRASTRUCTURE. BY INTEGRATING NOVEL DATA INFRASTRUCTURE, RIGOROUS CAUSAL METHODS, AND MARKET-LEVEL ANALYSES, THIS PROJECT WILL GENERATE THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE EVIDENCE ON HOW OWNERSHIP CHANGES AND CONSOLIDATION AFFECT HOME HEALTH DELIVERY AND OUTCOMES, EQUIPPING PATIENTS, DOCTORS, AND HEALTH SYSTEMS TO IMPROVE CARE.

description: THE VALUE OF MEDICAID FOR ADULTS AGES 50-64 - PROJECT SUMMARY FOR ADULTS AGES 50-64, HEALTH, FUNCTIONAL STATUS, AND FINANCIAL STATUS ARE IRREVOCABLY INTERTWINED; EACH AFFECTS THE OTHER, AND ALL THREE ARE NEEDED TO ENSURE A TRAJECTORY OF HEALTHY AGING IN THE FUTURE. FOR LOW-INCOME ADULTS AGES 50-64, MEDICAID EXPANSIONS UNDER THE AFFORDABLE CARE ACT (ACA) ENABLED MILLIONS OF PEOPLE TO OBTAIN HEALTH INSURANCE COVERAGE, REDUCED MORTALITY, IMPROVED ACCESS TO CARE AND REDUCED MEDICAL DEBT, AND IMPROVED FUNCTIONAL STATUS, ABILITY TO WORK, AND EMPLOYMENT. HOWEVER, IN JULY 2025, CONGRESS APPROVED CHANGES TO MEDICAID FUNDING AND ELIGIBILITY THAT WILL LIKELY RESULT IN 2 MILLION LOW-INCOME ADULTS AGES 50-64 LOSING MEDICAID COVERAGE. LOSS OF COVERAGE DISRUPTS PREVENTIVE CARE AND TREATMENT FOR CHRONIC CONDITIONS, LEADING TO POORER HEALTH, DECREASED FUNCTIONAL STATUS, AND FINANCIAL INSTABILITY THAT WILL COMPOUND AS THESE ADULTS CONTINUE TO AGE. AS A RESULT, THE UPCOMING MEDICAID DISENROLLMENTS COULD HAVE LONG-TERM EFFECTS ON THE HEALTH, FUNCTIONAL STATUS, AND FINANCIAL STABILITY OF LOW-INCOME OLDER ADULTS FOR DECADES TO COME. OUR RESEARCH TEAM HAS SPENT THE PAST DECADE PARTNERING WITH THE STATE OF MICHIGAN TO EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF MICHIGAN’S MEDICAID EXPANSION FROM 2014-2024. AS PART OF THAT WORK, WE HAVE DEVELOPED STRONG COLLABORATIONS WITH STATE PARTNERS, SURVEY ADMINISTRATION INFRASTRUCTURE, AND DATA MANAGEMENT PROCESSES TO ACCESS STATE ENROLLEE DATA TO LINK AND ANALYZE LARGE ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL DATASETS. WE ARE THEREFORE UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO ACHIEVE THE FOLLOWING AIMS: AIM 1: INVESTIGATE IMPACTS OF MEDICAID DISENROLLMENT ON HEALTH AND ABILITY TO MANAGE CHRONIC CONDITIONS FOR ADULTS AGES 50-64. USING A LONGITUDINAL TWO-WAVE SURVEY OF MICHIGAN MEDICAID ENROLLEES AGES 50-64, WE WILL EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF DISENROLLMENTS ON CHANGES IN INSURANCE COVERAGE, SELF-REPORTED HEALTH, FUNCTIONAL STATUS, ABILITY TO MANAGE HEALTH CONDITIONS, AND FINANCIAL BARRIERS TO CARE. AIM 2: ESTIMATE THE IMPACT OF MEDICAID DISENROLLMENT ON FUNCTIONAL STATUS FOR ADULTS AGES 50-64. USING DIFFERENCE-IN-DIFFERENCES (DID) ANALYSES AND A NOVEL DATA LINKAGE OF MICHIGAN MEDICAID ENROLLEES TO THEIR INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL RESPONSES IN THE U.S. CENSUS AMERICAN COMMUNITY SURVEY, WE WILL ESTIMATE THE IMPACT OF DISENROLLMENTS ON FUNCTIONAL STATUS AND ABILITY TO WORK. AIM 3: ASSESS THE IMPACT OF MEDICAID DISENROLLMENT ON FINANCIAL OUTCOMES FOR ADULTS AGES 50-64. USING DID ANALYSES AND A DATA LINKAGE OF MICHIGAN MEDICAID ENROLLEES TO THEIR LONGITUDINAL CONSUMER CREDIT DATA, WE WILL ESTIMATE THE IMPACT OF DISENROLLMENTS ON MEDICAL/NON-MEDICAL DEBT SENT TO COLLECTIONS AND CREDIT SCORE. THIS EVIDENCE WILL BE CRITICAL TO UNDERSTANDING HOW UPCOMING CHANGES TO MEDICAID ELIGIBILITY WILL IMPACT THE HEALTH OF LOW-INCOME ADULTS AS THEY AGE AND WILL HELP US TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL CLINICAL INTERVENTIONS TO HELP ADULTS AGES 50-64 MAINTAIN THEIR HEALTH AND FINANCIAL WELL-BEING INTO OLDER ADULTHOOD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SCH: SMARTGAIT: SMARTPHONE VIDEO-BASED AI FOR PERSONALIZED FALL RISK ASSESSMENT - PROJECT SUMMARY (SEE INSTRUCTIONS):   FALLS CONTRIBUTE TO OVER 3 MILLION EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT (ED) VISITS, 800,000 HOSPITALIZATIONS, AND 30,000  DEATHS ANNUALLY IN THE U.S. YET, FALL PREVENTION REMAINS LARGELY REACTIVE AND INEFFECTIVE, AS BROAD, ONE-SIZE FITS-ALL STRATEGIES TARGETING ALL OLDER ADULTS HAVE SHOWN LIMITED SUCCESS. WHAT IS URGENTLY NEEDED ARE SCALABLE  FALL-RISK ASSESSMENT TOOLS THAT ENABLE CLINICIANS TO IDENTIFY HIGH-RISK INDIVIDUALS AND INTERVENE AT THE RIGHT TIME.  ONE COMMONLY USED FALL-RISK ASSESSMENT IS THE TIMED UP AND GO (TUG), A QUICK, STRUCTURED, AND REPEATABLE  TEST THAT CAPTURES KEY GAIT AND BALANCE PHASES (SIT-TO-STAND, WALKING, TURNING, AND SITTING). HOWEVER, ITS  CURRENT CLINICAL USE, BASED SOLELY ON STOPWATCH-MEASURED TOTAL TIME AND FIXED POPULATION-WIDE THRESHOLDS  (E.G., >13.5 SECONDS), FAILS TO DETECT SUBTLE FALL-RELATED GAIT AND BALANCE IMPAIRMENTS AND ESTIMATE WHEN FALL RELATED EVENTS MIGHT OCCUR, LEAVING CLINICIANS WITHOUT ACTIONABLE INSIGHTS FOR TARGETED, TIMELY INTERVENTIONS.  THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THESE GAPS BY DEVELOPING NOVEL AI MODELS THAT TRANSFORM THE UBIQUITOUS SMARTPHONE  INTO A FAST, EASY-TO-USE, COST-EFFECTIVE PLATFORM FOR ANALYZING TUG TESTS AND GENERATING PERSONALIZED, TIME SPECIFIC FALL-RISK PREDICTIONS. OUR APPROACH STANDS APART FROM EXISTING GAIT METHODS BY ADVANCING AI MODELS  THAT ELIMINATE THE NEED FOR COSTLY, LAB-BASED TOOLS (E.G., VICON, DEPTH CAMERAS, PRESSURE MATS) AND ENABLE  PERSONALIZED TIME-TO-EVENT FALL-RISK PREDICTIONS. AIM 1 WILL DEVELOP NOVEL 3D POSE ESTIMATION MODELS THAT  INTEGRATE BIOMECHANICAL CONSTRAINTS, TRANSFORMER-BASED TEMPORAL FUSION, AND DEPTH-AWARE LOSS FUNCTIONS TO  EXTRACT HIGH-FIDELITY GAIT AND BALANCE MARKERS, VALIDATED AGAINST ZENO WALKWAY AND DUAL-CAMERA GROUND-TRUTH  DATA FROM 100 OLDER ADULTS. AIM 2 WILL DEVELOP INTERPRETABLE, TRANSFORMER-BASED DEEP SURVIVAL MODELS TO  PREDICT MONTHLY PROBABILITIES OF FALLS, FALL-RELATED ED VISITS, AND INJURIES OVER SIX MONTHS, TRAINED AND VALIDATED  ON 500 ED PATIENTS, WITH SHAP-BASED EXPLANATIONS FOR EACH PREDICTION. AIM 3 WILL INTEGRATE THESE MODELS  INTO A FULLY AUTOMATED, HIPAA-COMPLIANT PLATFORM AND EVALUATE ITS PREDICTIVE ACCURACY, USABILITY, AND CLINICAL  WORKFLOW FIT IN AN INDEPENDENT COHORT OF 150 ED PATIENTS. THE PROPOSED WORK IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT IS THE  FIRST SMARTPHONE-ONLY SYSTEM TO DELIVER PERSONALIZED, TIME-TO-EVENT FALL-RISK PREDICTION WITHOUT WEARABLE  SENSORS OR COSTLY LABORATORY EQUIPMENT. THE EXPECTED OUTCOME IS A RIGOROUSLY VALIDATED TOOL WITH THE POTENTIAL  TO TRANSFORM FALL PREVENTION FROM REACTIVE, ONE-SIZE-FITS-ALL CARE TO PROACTIVE, TARGETED INTERVENTIONS. THE USE  OF UBIQUITOUS SMARTPHONES WILL MAKE FALL-RISK ASSESSMENT SCALABLE, EXPANDING ACCESS IN EDS, CLINICS, AND  RURAL COMMUNITIES WHILE EXTENDING THE HEALTHY, ACTIVE, AND INDEPENDENT YEARS OF LIFE FOR OLDER ADULTS.

description: THE NATIONAL NEIGHBORHOOD DATA ARCHIVE: A RESOURCE TO UNDERSTAND HEALTH RISK & RESILIENCE FOR AGING IN THE UNITED STATES - ABSTRACT: NATIONAL, REPRODUCIBLE, PUBLICLY AVAILABLE DATA ARE CRITICAL FOR ADVANCING THE UNDERSTANDING OF ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS FOR OLDER ADULT HEALTH. THE PROPOSED PROJECT SEEKS TO EXPAND AND ENHANCE THE NATIONAL NEIGHBORHOOD DATA ARCHIVE (NANDA), A NATIONAL REPOSITORY OF CONTEXTUAL MEASURES THAT ARE DESIGNED FOR SEAMLESS INTEGRATION INTO RESEARCH WORKFLOWS AND LINKAGES WITH LONGITUDINAL AGING STUDIES ACROSS TIME AND GEOGRAPHIC LEVELS. RECOGNIZING THAT THE NEIGHBORHOODS WHERE PEOPLE LIVE ARE A CRITICAL DETERMINANT OF HEALTH, THIS PROPOSAL WILL DEVELOP CUTTING-EDGE DATA AND RESEARCH FINDINGS ON MACROSOCIAL FACTORS SHAPING OLDER ADULT HEALTH AND WELL-BEING. WE WILL DO SO THROUGH THE SEAMLESS INTEGRATION OF SIX SPECIFIC AIMS. THREE AIMS WILL SUPPORT AND AUGMENT NANDA’S DATA INFRASTRUCTURE: AIM 1: ADMINISTRATIVE ACTIVITIES, AIM 2: DATA CREATION AND DISSEMINATION ACTIVITIES, AND AIM 3: METHODOLOGICAL INNOVATION WITH SPATIALLY AND TEMPORALLY LINKED DATA. THIS INFRASTRUCTURE WILL THEN SUPPORT 3 NOVEL AND SUBSTANTIVE RESEARCH AIMS EXAMINING HOW NEIGHBORHOOD-LEVEL SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS CONTRIBUTE TO RESPIRATORY ILLNESS AMONG OLDER ADULTS: AIM 4 WILL IDENTIFY AND CHARACTERIZE HIGH- AND LOW-BURDEN RESPIRATORY ILLNESS NEIGHBORHOODS ACROSS THE U.S.; AIM 5 WILL DETERMINE THE OPTIMAL SPATIAL SCALE THAT BEST CAPTURES HETEROGENEITY IN ILLNESS BURDEN AND HOW IT VARIES BY RURAL/URBAN CONTEXT, TRANSMISSION PATHWAY, AND SEASON; AND AIM 6 WILL ASSESS WHETHER RESIDENCE IN HIGH-BURDEN NEIGHBORHOODS INCREASES THE RISK OF OLDER ADULT HOSPITALIZATION OR MORTALITY, WITH A FOCUS ON THE MODIFYING ROLE OF IMMUNE AGING USING LINKED DATA FROM THE HEALTH AND RETIREMENT STUDY. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO ADVANCE AGING RESEARCH BY GENERATING CUTTING-EDGE DATA ON MACROSOCIAL FACTORS THAT SHAPE OLDER ADULT HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, DEVELOPING INNOVATIVE STATISTICAL METHODS FOR RIGOROUS NEIGHBORHOOD CONTEXT ANALYSIS, AND CURATING AND DISSEMINATING THESE RESOURCES FOR PUBLIC USE. BY ADDRESSING CRITICAL ISSUES SUCH AS PLACE-BASED RISK FOR RESPIRATORY ILLNESS, THIS PROPOSAL WILL ENHANCE THE NATION’S DATA INFRASTRUCTURE ON AGING AND EMPOWER RESEARCHERS TO TACKLE THE MOST PRESSING ISSUES OF AN AGING SOCIETY. THIS PROPOSAL IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT INTEGRATES ADVANCED METHODS IN SPATIAL ANALYSIS AND NEIGHBORHOOD-LEVEL EPIDEMIOLOGY TO DEVELOP CUTTING-EDGE DATA AND METHODOLOGICAL TOOLS FOR ADVANCING AGING RESEARCH. THE PROPOSAL IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT WILL ENHANCE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW NEIGHBORHOOD ENVIRONMENTS SHAPE AGING-RELATED HEALTH RISKS AND RESILIENCE BY PUBLICLY SHARING ACTIONABLE DATA PRODUCTS TO IMPROVE AGING-RELATED SCIENCE AND INFORM CLINICAL PRACTICE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEFINING MRSA NICHES IN THE KIDNEY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT BLOODSTREAM INFECTIONS CAUSED BY METHICILLIN-RESISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (MRSA) REMAIN A MAJOR CLINICAL PROBLEM. EARLY DETECTION AND COMPLETE ERADICATION OF THESE LIFE-THREATENING INFECTIONS ARE HINDERED BY MRSA’S DIVERSE IMMUNE EVASION MECHANISMS. THE KIDNEY IS FREQUENTLY COMPROMISED DURING MRSA BACTEREMIA, THROUGH BOTH SYSTEMIC EFFECTS OF SEPSIS AND DIRECT MICROBIAL INVASION OF RENAL TISSUE. THE LATTER MECHANISM IS OFTEN OVERLOOKED IN CLINICAL SETTINGS DUE TO THE LACK OF SENSITIVE DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS, YET IT PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN MRSA NICHE EXPANSION AND CONTRIBUTES TO HIGH MORTALITY. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA INDICATE THAT THE INNER MEDULLA, WHERE URINE IS CONCENTRATED, IS THE INITIAL SITE OF MRSA RENAL INVASION, FACILITATING ITS SUBSEQUENT SPREAD THROUGHOUT THE KIDNEY. NOTABLY, THE INNER MEDULLA EXHIBITS MINIMAL NEUTROPHIL RESPONSES EARLY ON, CREATING A PROTECTED NICHE FOR MRSA. THE INNER MEDULLA IS A PHYSIOLOGICALLY EXTREME ENVIRONMENT, CHARACTERIZED BY EXCEPTIONALLY HIGH OSMOLALITY, ELEVATED UREA AND SALT LEVELS, AND ACIDOSIS. WHY AND HOW MRSA ESTABLISHES INFECTION UNDER THESE CONDITIONS IS UNKNOWN. OUR ONGOING WORK SUGGESTS THAT HIGH LEVELS OF BASAL TISSUE POLYAMINES, WHICH ARE FURTHER UPREGULATED AFTER KIDNEY INFECTION, ENHANCE MRSA’S ABILITY TO WITHSTAND RENAL OSMOTIC STRESS. SPECIFIC AIM 1 OF THIS PROPOSAL WILL CHARACTERIZE THE SPATIOTEMPORAL DYNAMICS OF MRSA INVASION AND HOST IMMUNE RESPONSES USING DUAL-SPECIES RNA SEQUENCING, SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS, AND MULTIPLEXED IMAGING, AND WILL TEST THE EFFECTS OF MODULATING MEDULLARY OSMOLALITY. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE HOW TISSUE POLYAMINES INFLUENCE MRSA TOLERANCE TO RENAL OSMOTIC STRESS THROUGH IN VIVO INTERVENTIONS AND IN VITRO ASSAYS THAT CONTROL HOST AND BACTERIAL FACTORS. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL DEFINE THE MOLECULAR AND CELLULAR BASIS OF MRSA PERSISTENCE IN THE KIDNEY AND IDENTIFY THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TO DISRUPT THIS RESERVOIR AND IMPROVE PATIENT OUTCOMES.

description: THE FLAGELLUM ORGANIZES CAMP SIGNALING, ATTACHMENT, AND DIFFERENTIATION IN KINETOPLASTID PARASITES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT KINETOPLASTID PARASITES ARE WIDESPREAD AGENTS OF HUMAN AND ANIMAL DISEASE. DESPITE THEIR GLOBAL IMPACT, MANY FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS REMAIN THAT COULD INFORM INNOVATIVE NEW STRATEGIES FOR CONTROL. DURING THEIR LIFE CYCLE, PARASITES UNDERGO DRAMATIC MORPHOLOGICAL AND FUNCTIONAL CHANGES AS THEY ADAPT TO DIFFERENT HOST NICHES AND PREPARE FOR TRANSMISSION TO NEW HOSTS. THE CELL’S SINGLE FLAGELLUM SERVES TO SPATIALLY REGULATE SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION CASCADES WHICH MAY DRIVE DIFFERENTIATION EVENTS IN RESPONSE TO EXTERNAL CUES. PATHOGENIC KINETOPLASTIDS ARE TRANSMITTED BY INSECT VECTORS, IN WHICH THEY UNDERGO COMPLEX CELL FATE TRANSFORMATIONS THAT ARE DIFFICULT OR IMPOSSIBLE TO REPLICATE IN VITRO. A RELATIVELY UNEXPLORED PHENOMENON IS PARASITE ATTACHMENT VIA A HEMIDESMOSOME-LIKE STRUCTURE THAT FORMS BETWEEN THE FLAGELLUM AND A SURFACE IN THE INSECT. ALL KINETOPLASTIDS FORM THIS ATTACHMENT, WHICH APPEARS CRUCIAL BOTH FOR INSECT COLONIZATION AND DIFFERENTIATION TO INFECTIOUS FORMS. HOWEVER, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THE SIGNALS THAT CONTROL ATTACHMENT OR HOW THIS CONNECTS TO DIFFERENTIATION. THE FLAGELLUM MAY SERVE AS A PLATFORM TO INTEGRATE THESE PROCESSES, BUT ADDRESSING THIS QUESTION IN PATHOGENIC KINETOPLASTIDS IS TECHNICALLY CHALLENGING. WE HAVE DEVELOPED THE MOSQUITO PARASITE CRITHIDIA FASCICULATA AS A ROBUST MODEL TO ADDRESS THESE QUESTIONS. SWIMMING C. FASCICULATA CELLS ARE EASY TO CULTURE AND READILY ADHERE IN VITRO TO ARTIFICIAL SUBSTRATES, FORMING ATTACHMENTS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THOSE OBSERVED IN VIVO. SURFACE CONTACT TRIGGERS MORPHOLOGICAL CHANGES INCLUDING DRAMATIC SHORTENING OF THE FLAGELLUM, CELL ROUNDING, AND SHIFTS IN GENE EXPRESSION CONSISTENT WITH A CHANGE IN CELL FATE. WE HAVE DEVELOPED AND STANDARDIZED ASSAY CONDITIONS TO PERMIT TIME-LAPSE STUDIES AND QUANTITATION. USING THIS ASSAY, WE HAVE FOUND THAT GENETIC AND PHARMACOLOGICAL MANIPULATIONS THAT INCREASE CYCLIC AMP (CAMP) PREVENT CELLS FROM TRANSITIONING TO THE ATTACHED CELL FATE. SINCE MANY CAMP SIGNALING PROTEINS ARE FOUND IN THE FLAGELLUM, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT HIGH FLAGELLAR CAMP IS A BARRIER TO DIFFERENTIATION FROM SWIMMING TO ATTACHED. TO TEST THIS MODEL, WE WILL LOCALIZE CAMP SIGNALING PROTEINS DURING THE PROCESS OF ATTACHMENT. BASED ON OUR PRELIMINARY DATA, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED CANDIDATES FOR CREATION AND DESTRUCTION OF CAMP AND CONFIRMED THEIR FLAGELLAR LOCALIZATION. WE HAVE ESTABLISHED A STRAIGHTFORWARD KNOCKDOWN SYSTEM TO IDENTIFY GENES REQUIRED FOR ATTACHMENT. AS C. FASCICULATA IS GENETICALLY AND BIOCHEMICALLY TRACTABLE, WE CAN EXAMINE THE DYNAMIC LOCALIZATION AND FUNCTION OF THESE CANDIDATES DURING THE ATTACHMENT PROCESS USING OUR IN VITRO ASSAY, LIVE CELL IMAGING, METABOLOMICS, AND PROTEIN STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ANALYSIS. WE WILL ALSO TEST MUTANTS IN VIVO IN THE MOSQUITO HOST USING A NEWLY DEVELOPED REPORTER STRAIN THAT ALLOWS SENSITIVE QUANTITATION IN INDIVIDUAL MOSQUITOES. THIS WILL FACILITATE EVALUATION OF PHYSIOLOGICAL RELEVANCE AND PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO THE ROLE OF CAMP SIGNALING AND ATTACHMENT IN DEVELOPMENTAL PROGRESSION IN THE INSECT.

description: CD1-DEPENDENCE AND LIPID ANTIGEN SPECIFICITY OF THE HUMAN CD4-/CD8- DOUBLE-NEGATIVE T CELL REPERTOIRE - PROJECT SUMMARY DOUBLE-NEGATIVE ΑΒ T CELLS (DN T CELLS), WHICH LACK CD4 AND CD8 CO-RECEPTOR EXPRESSION, ARE A SMALL POPULATION OF T CELLS IN PERIPHERAL BLOOD, CONSTITUTING APPROXIMATELY 1% OF ALL T CELLS. THE FREQUENCY OF DN T CELLS, HOWEVER, IS MUCH HIGHER AMONG RESIDENT T CELLS IN CERTAIN TISSUES, SUCH AS KIDNEYS, INTESTINE, AND FEMALE GENITAL TRACT. CLINICAL INTEREST IN DN ΑΒ T CELLS HAS BEEN IN THE FIELD OF AUTOIMMUNITY, SINCE THEY ARE EXPANDED IN MULTIPLE AUTOIMMUNE CONDITIONS, IN PARTICULAR SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS (SLE). HOWEVER, BEYOND AUTOIMMUNE CONDITIONS, DN T CELLS ARE EXPANDED IN GRAFT VERSUS HOST DISEASE (GVHD), ARE DETECTED AMONG TUMOR INFILTRATING LYMPHOCYTES (TIL), AND ARE BEING HARNESSED AS VEHICLES FOR OFF-THE-SHELF CAR T CELLS, PRIMARILY BASED ON THEIR LACK OF ALLOREACTIVITY AND ANTI-TUMOR PROPERTIES. THEIR REPORTED PROINFLAMMATORY AND IMMUNOREGULATORY FUNCTIONS SUGGEST THAT DN T CELLS ARE NOT A HOMOGENEOUS SUBSET, BUT RATHER A HETEROGENEOUS COLLECTION OF POPULATIONS WITH DISTINCT ANTIGEN SPECIFICITIES AND FUNCTIONS. FURTHERMORE, THE LACK OF CD4 AND CD8 CO-RECEPTORS, WHICH ARE ESSENTIAL FOR INTERACTION WITH MHC-PEPTIDE COMPLEXES, SUGGESTS THAT DN T CELLS LIKELY INTERACT WITH ANTIGEN PRESENTING MOLECULES OTHER THAN MHC. INDEED, WE HAVE RECENT, UNPUBLISHED EVIDENCE THAT THE HUMAN DN ΑΒ T CELL REPERTOIRE IS ENRICHED FOR T CELL POPULATIONS THAT ARE RESTRICTED BY CD1 PROTEINS, WHICH ARE NON-POLYMORPHIC ANTIGEN PRESENTING MOLECULES THAT PRESENT LIPID ANTIGENS TO T CELLS. WE DETECTED DISTINCT CD1A, CD1B, CD1C AND CD1D-RESTRICTED DN T CELL POPULATIONS THAT DISPLAYED CD1-AUTOREACTIVITY, MEANING THEY RESPOND TO CD1 HARBORING ENDOGENOUS SELF-LIPID ANTIGENS. IN THE CURRENT PROPOSAL WE AIM TO UNDERSTAND THE HETEROGENEOUS FUNCTIONS AND SPECIFICITIES OF THE HUMAN DN T CELL REPERTOIRE AND DETERMINE HOW CD1 AND SELF-LIPID ANTIGENS CONTRIBUTE TO DN T CELL ACTIVATION. RESULTS FROM THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO CONDITIONS IN WHICH DN T CELLS ARE EXPANDED, AND ENABLE THE IDENTIFICATION OF SPECIFIC TARGETS FOR IMMUNOMODULATION OF DN T CELLS IN DISEASE. COMBINING A PANEL OF CD1 TETRAMERS FOR CD1A, CD1B, CD1C, AND CD1D WITH SINGLE CELL RNA-SEQUENCING AND TCR-SEQUENCING, WE WILL LINK PROINFLAMMATORY AND IMMUNOREGULATORY SUBPOPULATIONS OF DN T CELLS TO CONSERVED CD1-RESTRICTED TCRS. FURTHER, WE WILL USE COMPARATIVE LIPIDOMICS TO IDENTIFY SELF-LIPIDS THAT FUNCTION AS ANTIGENS FOR CD1- AUTOREACTIVE DN T CELLS. LAST, IN OUR PRELIMINARY ANALYSIS OF DN T CELLS, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED TWO PREVIOUSLY UNREPORTED T CELL SUBPOPULATIONS WITH UNUSUAL GENE EXPRESSION PROFILES AND WILL EXPLORE THE ORIGINS AND FUNCTIONS OF THESE NEWLY IDENTIFIED DN T CELLS. COLLECTIVELY, THIS WORK WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE TCR SPECIFICITY, FUNCTIONS, AND REGULATION OF HUMAN DOUBLE-NEGATIVE T CELLS, ESTABLISHING A FOUNDATION FOR THEIR TARGETED IMMUNOMODULATION AND THERAPEUTIC APPLICATION IN DISEASE.

description: ENFORCED HIV-1 SILENCING AT THE TIME OF ART INITIATION TO CONTROL VIREMIA, RESERVOIR PERSISTENCE, AND VIRAL REBOUND - PROJECT SUMMARY ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART) SUPPRESSES HIV-1 REPLICATION TO UNDETECTABLE LEVELS. HOWEVER, INTERRUPTION OF ART ALMOST INEVITABLY RESULTS IN RESURGENCE OF VIRAL REPLICATION. THAT IS BECAUSE ART DOES NOT PREVENT THE ESTABLISH- MENT OF LONG-LIVED VIRAL RESERVOIRS THAT REKINDLE VIRAL REPLICATION AFTER TREATMENT INTERRUPTION. FURTHER, ART DOES NOT PREVENT SPONTANEOUS REVERSAL OF LATENCY AND RESIDUAL VIRAL EXPRESSION, WHICH CONTRIBUTE TO PERSISTENT INFLAM- MATION. THESE LIMITATIONS MAY BE COMPENSATED BY NEW INTERVENTIONS TARGETING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND MAINTE- NANCE OF LATENCY. THEIR IMPLEMENTATION AROUND THE TIME OF ART INITIATION/RESTART MAY ACCELERATE THE DECAY OF VIREMIA BEFORE ART, REDUCE VIRAL EXPRESSION DURING ART, AND BLOCK, DELAY, OR MITIGATE VIRAL REBOUND AFTER ART. THE AIM OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP A NEW INTERVENTION DELIVERED BEFORE INITIATION/RESTART OF ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART) THAT (1) SILENCES HIV-1 AND ACCELERATES DECAY OF VIREMIA; (2) REDUCES RESIDUAL HIV-1 EXPRESSION DURING ART; AND (3) BLOCKS OR DELAYS VIRAL REBOUND IMPROVING POST-TREATMENT CONTROL. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT THESE GOALS CAN BE ACHIEVED VIA ECTOPIC EXPRESSION OF AN HIV-1-ENCODED ANTISENSE TRANSCRIPT (AST), WHICH WE HAVE SHOWN TO SILENCE HIV-1 EXPRESSION VIA HETEROCHROMATIZATION OF THE HIV-1 5’ LONG TERMINAL REPEAT (LTR), PROMOTING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF VIRAL LATENCY. THE APPLICATION IS CENTERED AROUND THREE SPECIFIC AIMS. IN SPECIFIC AIM 1, WE PROPOSE TO INVESTIGATE THE MOLEC- ULAR MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH AST SILENCES HIV-1 TRANSCRIPTION. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT AST PROMOTES THE FORMATION OF BIOMOLECULAR CONDENSATES AT THE 5’ LTR. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL UTILIZE A CD4-SPECIFIC ENGINEERED LENTIVIRAL (ELV) AST DELIVERY PLATFORM TO TEST ITS EFFICACY USING IN-VITRO AND EX-VIVO CULTURE SYSTEMS, INCLUDING A NOVEL LYMPH NODE ON-A-CHIP ORGANOID MODEL. FINALLY, SPECIFIC AIM 3 WILL TEST THE EFFICACY OF THE NEW AST-BASED INTERVENTION IN A PRECLINICAL HUMANIZED MOUSE MODEL. WE WILL INVESTIGATE WHETHER ECTOPIC EXPRESSION OF AST ACCELERATES THE DECLINE OF VIREMIA AT ART INITIATION, REDUCE VIRAL EXPRESSION DURING ART, AND INCREASE CONTROL OF VIRAL REPLICATION AFTER INTERRUPTION OF ART. THE INNOVATIVE ASPECTS OF THE PROPOSAL INCLUDE: (1) A NEW STRATEGY TO BLOCK RESIDUAL VIRAL EXPRESSION DURING ART AND TO ACHIEVE POST-TREATMENT CONTROL; (2) AN HIV-SPECIFIC BIOLOGICAL MOLECULE TO INDUCE VIRAL SILENCING VIA BIO- MOLECULAR CONSENSATES; (3) A CD4-SPECIFIC LENTIVIRAL DELIVERY PLATFORM; (4) A NOVEL LYMPH NODE ORGANOID SYSTEM; AND (5) THE TRIPLE KNOCKOUT HUMANIZED MOUSE MODEL THAT EXHIBITS SIGNIFICANTLY DELAYED GRAFT VERSUS HOST DISEASE. THESE STUDIES WILL BE LED BY A TEAM OF INVESTIGATORS WITH COMPLEMENTARY SETS OF EXPERTISE THAT WILL ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THIS APPLICATION. DR. ROMERIO’S WORK HAS FOCUSED ON HIV-1 REGULATION BY AST; DR. CAI SPECIALIZES ON THE ROLE OF BIOMOLECULAR CONDENSATES IN CHROMATIN ORGANIZATION; DR. FERRARI HAS PIONEERED THE DEVELOPMENT OF ORGANOID MODELS; DR. SIMONETTI FOCUSES ON MONITORING VIRAL DYNAMICS AND RESERVOIR PERSISTENCE; AND DR. HEREDIA IS AN EXPERT OF HUMANIZED MOUSE MODELS.

description: INVESTIGATING THE ROLE OF REASSORTMENT, SEASONALITY, AND AVIAN MOVEMENT IN H5N1 TRANSMISSION AND SPILLOVER RISK - PROJECT SUMMARY SINCE 2021, HIGHLY PATHOGENIC H5N1 VIRUSES HAVE SPREAD THROUGHOUT THE AMERICAS, SPARKING A PANZOOTIC THAT HAS DEVASTATED WILDLIFE AND AGRICULTURE AND CAUSED 70 HUMAN INFECTIONS. SHIFTING H5N1 ECOLOGY HAS RENDERED PAST METHODS FOR OUTBREAK CONTROL INSUFFICIENT FOR PREVENTING SPILLOVERS INTO HUMANS AND AGRICULTURE, NECESSITATING NEW APPROACHES FOR UNDERSTANDING TRANSMISSION AND SPILLOVER RISK. WE RECENTLY SHOWED THAT THE 2022 PANZOOTIC HAS FUNDAMENTALLY DISTINCT FROM PAST OUTBREAKS BECAUSE TRANSMISSION WAS SUSTAINED BY WILD, MIGRATING BIRDS, WHICH NOW CARRY THESE VIRUSES ENDEMICALLY. HOWEVER, THE ECOLOGICAL AND EVOLUTIONARY FACTORS THAT GOVERN TRANSMISSION IN WILD BIRDS ARE CURRENTLY POORLY UNDERSTOOD, INHIBITING EFFECTIVE SURVEILLANCE, OUTBREAK RESPONSE, AND RISK MODELING. WE PROPOSE THAT H5N1 SPILLOVER RISK IS JOINTLY DETERMINED BY THREE PHENOMENA THAT ARE CURRENTLY POORLY UNDERSTOOD: THE FORMATION OF FIT VIRUSES IN THE WILD BIRD RESERVOIR, EXPOSURE TO THESE VIRUSES DURING SEASONAL TRANSMISSION UPTICKS, AND GEOGRAPHIC DISSEMINATION VIA MIGRATORY MOVEMENT. IN AIM 1, WE WILL PERFORM THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF H5N1 REASSORTMENT IN NORTH AMERICA TO INTERROGATE HOW NOVEL REASSORTANT VIRUSES ARE GENERATED, SELECTED, AND SPILL OVER INTO MAMMALS. WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT REASSORTMENT IS A KEY DETERMINANT OF VIRAL FITNESS, AND THAT PARTICULAR GENETIC COMBINATIONS ARE PARTICULARLY PRONE TO MAMMAL INFECTION. IN AIM 2, WE WILL MEASURE HOW TRANSMISSION INTENSITY VARIES ACROSS HOST GROUPS AND SEASONS, AND HOW THIS VARIATION RELATES TO SPILLOVER. WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT SEASONALLY-VARYING TRANSMISSION INTENSITY IN WILD BIRDS RESULTS IN H5N1 RISK THAT VARIES ACROSS TIME, AND CAN PREDICT SPILLOVERS INTO MAMMALS AND AGRICULTURE. IN AIM 3 WE WILL QUANTIFY THE IMPACT OF ANIMAL MOVEMENT ON VIRAL DISSEMINATION. WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THE MOVEMENT OF WILD ANSERIFORMES (DUCKS, GEESE, SWANS) RESULTS IN H5N1 RISK THAT VARIES ACROSS TIME AND SPACE, AND COULD PROVIDE A SURVEILLANCE-FREE APPROACH FOR ASSESSING TIME-VARYING SPILLOVER RISK. WE WILL LEVERAGE PRELIMINARY DATA SHOWING THAT WE CAN ACCURATELY QUANTIFY AVIAN INFLUENZA REASSORTMENT AND TRANSMISSION, AND RELATE THESE MEASUREMENTS TO KEY ECOLOGICAL CORRELATES OF SPREAD. BY EXTENDING THESE METHODOLOGIES TO SURVEILLANCE AND WILD BIRD MOVEMENT DATA, WE WILL DEVELOP A TIME AND GEOGRAPHY-VARYING “RISK MAP” THAT COULD BE USED TO DEVELOP TARGETED BIOSECURITY UPDATES, MORE EFFECTIVE SURVEILLANCE STRATEGIES, AND MORE INFORMED VACCINE STRAIN SELECTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REGULATION OF CYTOSKELETAL REORGANIZATION BY CHLAMYDIA - ABSTRACT.  CHLAMYDIA TRACHOMATIS IS AN INTRACELLULAR BACTERIUM THAT CAUSES SIGNIFICANT HUMAN MORBIDITY. IT IS THE MOST COMMON ETIOLOGICAL AGENT OF BACTERIAL SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASES AND INFECTIOUS BLINDNESS. WITHOUT A PREVENTIVE VACCINE, IT IS CRUCIAL TO IDENTIFY CHLAMYDIA’S INTRACELLULAR SURVIVAL STRATEGIES AND HOW THEY INFLUENCE DISEASE PROGRESSION. TO SURVIVE WITHIN ITS HOST, CHLAMYDIA MUST ESTABLISH AND MAINTAIN ITS INTRACELLULAR NICHE, KNOWN AS THE INCLUSION. CHLAMYDIA ACCOMPLISHES THIS BY CO-OPTING THE HOST CELL AND HIJACKING CRITICAL CELLULAR PATHWAYS. OF PARTICULAR INTEREST IS THE REORGANIZATION OF THE HOST CYTOSKELETON AROUND THE INCLUSION TRIGGERED BY CHLAMYDIA. BY BUILDING ACTIN AND MICROTUBULE SCAFFOLDS AROUND THE INCLUSION, CHLAMYDIA EXTENSIVELY REDIRECTS HOST ORGANELLES AND NUTRIENTS TO THE INCLUSION, WHILE ALSO CREATING A PHYSICAL BARRIER TO PROTECT THE EXPANDING INCLUSION MEMBRANE, WHICH IS CRUCIAL FOR CHLAMYDIA DEVELOPMENT.  OUR LABORATORY HAS A LONG-STANDING INTEREST IN STUDYING THESE EVENTS AS WE SEEK TO IDENTIFY THE MOLECULAR PLATFORM INVOLVED IN FORMING AND MAINTAINING THESE CYTOSKELETAL SCAFFOLDS, AS WELL AS THEIR ROLE IN VIVO. OUR PREVIOUS WORK HAS ESTABLISHED THAT THE INCLUSION MEMBRANE PROTEIN CALLED INAC PLAYS A SIGNIFICANT ROLE IN STABILIZING THESE SCAFFOLDS. YET, FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS REMAIN: (1) HOW DOES CHLAMYDIA INITIALLY FORM CYTOSKELETAL SCAFFOLDS, (2) WHAT IS THE ROLE OF INDIVIDUAL SCAFFOLDS IN CHLAMYDIA DEVELOPMENT, AND (3) TO WHAT EXTENT DO THESE SCAFFOLDS CONTRIBUTE TO CHLAMYDIA PATHOGENESIS IN VIVO? THESE REMAIN SIGNIFICANT KNOWLEDGE GAPS IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF CHLAMYDIA’S INTRACELLULAR SURVIVAL STRATEGIES. THIS PROJECT PROPOSES TO ANSWER THESE OUTSTANDING QUESTIONS USING MULTIDISCIPLINARY IN VIVO AND IN VITRO APPROACHES. BASED ON OUR PRELIMINARY RESULTS, WHICH IDENTIFY TWO NEW INCLUSION PROTEINS INVOLVED IN CYTOSKELETAL REORGANIZATION, WE PROPOSE TESTING THE HYPOTHESIS THAT CHLAMYDIA SEQUENTIALLY USES DISTINCT PROTEIN COMPLEXES TO REMODEL THE HOST CYTOSKELETON AND CONTROL CHLAMYDIA PATHOGENESIS.  OVERALL, THE RESULTS OBTAINED FROM THIS WORK WILL IDENTIFY THE FUNCTION OF TWO NEW CHLAMYDIAL PROTEINS AND THEIR ASSOCIATED HOST-BINDING PARTNERS, REVEAL NEW ELEMENTS IN THE MOLECULAR PLATFORM USED BY CHLAMYDIA TO COORDINATE CYTOSKELETAL REORGANIZATION, ELUCIDATE THE CONTRIBUTION OF NEW CHLAMYDIAL PROTEINS AND CYTOSKELETAL SCAFFOLDS TO CHLAMYDIA PATHOGENESIS IN VIVO, AND, IMPORTANTLY, IDENTIFY NEW VIRULENCE FACTORS. THE UNIVERSAL ROLE OF THE CYTOSKELETON IN REGULATING PROCESSES FROM CELL SHAPE AND STABILITY TO CANCER METASTASIS, IMMUNITY, AND WOUND REPAIR UNDERSCORES THE BROAD IMPACT OF THIS STUDY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTEGRATED ROLE OF NASAL AIRWAY & GUT MICROBIOME DYNAMICS IN ALLERGIC RHINITIS - PROJECT ABSTRACT THE MAJOR CHALLENGES FOR DEVELOPING PRIMARY PREVENTION STRATEGIES FOR ALLERGIC RHINITIS (AR) ARE THE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF MODIFIABLE RISK FACTORS (E.G., AIRWAY AND GUT MICROBIOME) AND THE HETEROGENEITY OF AR. OUR GROUP HAS APPLIED INTEGRATED OMICS (E.G., AIRWAY METAGENOME, HOST GENOME AND TRANSCRIPTOME) APPROACHES TO INFANCY DATA, AND IDENTIFIED ENDOTYPES AT HIGH RISK FOR AR AND ASTHMA. TO DATE, NO STUDY HAS EXAMINED THE DYNAMIC ROLE OF AIRWAY-GUT MICROBIOME IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF AR AND ITS PHENO/ENDOTYPES. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT AN INTERRELATION BETWEEN LONGITUDINAL CHANGES IN THE DUAL NASAL AIRWAY-GUT MICROBIOME (BOTH COMPOSITION AND FUNCTIONAL POTENTIAL) AND HOST AR GENETIC RISK CONTRIBUTES TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF AR. WE WILL LEVERAGE LONGITUDINAL SAMPLES AND COMPREHENSIVE CLINICAL AND OMICS DATA FROM OUR ONGOING NIH-FUNDED COHORTS. THE 43RD MULTICENTER AIRWAY RESEARCH COLLABORATION (MARC-43) STUDY (UH3 OD023253) IS AN ONGOING MULTICENTER COHORT STUDY OF 599 HEALTHY INFANTS. THE PROPOSED R01 PROJECT WOULD EXTEND THIS WELL-CHARACTERIZED COHORT BY LONGITUDINALLY SEQUENCING BOTH NASAL AIRWAY AND GUT METAGENOME, AND THEN EXAMINING THEIR RELATIONS TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF AR AND ITS PHENOTYPES BY AGE 7 YEARS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL IDENTIFY INTEGRATED LONGITUDINAL NASAL AIRWAY METAGENOME (AGES 0, 1, AND 2 YEARS) AND HOST GENOME SIGNATURES OF DEVELOPING AR (AND ITS PHENOTYPES). IN AIM 2, WE WILL IDENTIFY INTEGRATED LONGITUDINAL GUT METAGENOME (AGES 0, 1, AND 2 YEARS) AND HOST GENOME SIGNATURES OF DEVELOPING AR (AND ITS PHENOTYPES). IN AIM 3, WE WILL USE NOVEL MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES TO INTEGRATE THE DUAL NASAL-GUT METAGENOME DATA WITH AVAILABLE MULTI-OMICS DATA TO DETERMINE LONGITUDINAL ENDOTYPES RELATED TO AR RISK. WE WILL VALIDATE OUR FINDINGS IN CHILDREN FROM TWO ALREADY-HARMONIZED COHORTS UNDERGOING SIMILAR PROCEDURES AND TESTING AT SIMILAR AGES. THE LONGITUDINAL DUAL AIRWAY-GUT METAGENOME DATA GENERATED BY THIS R01 PROJECT—ALONG WITH PARALLEL, ALREADY AVAILABLE MULTI-LEVEL OMICS (E.G., GENOME, TRANSCRIPTOME) AND IMMUNOLOGICAL DATA—OFFER AN UNPRECEDENTED OPPORTUNITY TO DEVELOP DATA-DRIVEN MECHANISTIC MODELS FOR AR. RESULTS WILL INCLUDE THE FIRST DATA ON THE LONGITUDINAL AIRWAY-GUT METAGENOME IN AR DEVELOPMENT. THIS R01 PROJECT PROVIDES A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO ELUCIDATE THE MECHANISMS OF AR AND TO HIGHLIGHT MOLECULAR TARGETS FOR THE PREVENTION OF AR.

description: HIV-1 RESERVOIR CHARACTERIZATION AND IMMUNE PROFILING OF INDIVIDUALS WITH ANTIRETROVIRAL EXPOSURE AT THE TIME OF HIV ACQUISITION - PROJECT SUMMARY SUSTAINED ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART)-FREE REMISSION REMAINS A MAJOR GOAL IN HIV-1 RESEARCH. SOME INDIVIDUALS WHO BEGIN TREATMENT IN EARLY INFECTION HAVE SMALLER RESERVOIR SIZES, AND A SUBSET OF THEM HAVE MAINTAINED ART- FREE VIROLOGICAL CONTROL. THESE CASES HAVE GENERATED OPTIMISM THAT A COMBINATION OF VERY EARLY TREATMENT AND SPECIFICALLY-TARGETED IMMUNE RESPONSES COULD ACHIEVE SUSTAINED ART-FREE REMISSION. PEOPLE WHO ACQUIRE HIV- 1 WHILE ON PRE-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS (PREP) EXHIBIT ALTERED INFECTION DYNAMICS, INCLUDING NEARLY SUPPRESSED LEVELS OF VIRAL REPLICATION AND LONG INTERVALS BEFORE DETECTABILITY OF INFECTION. WE PROPOSE TO DEEPLY CHARACTERIZE HIV-1 RESERVOIR AND IMMUNE MARKERS FROM A UNIQUE POPULATION OF INDIVIDUALS WHO ACQUIRE HIV-1 WHILE ON PREP (SUCH AS INDIVIDUALS USING LONG-ACTING CABOTEGRAVIR PRIOR TO INFECTION) (GROUP A, N=20) AS COMPARED TO INDIVIDUALS WHO START ART IN ACUTE INFECTION (GROUP B, N=40). IN AIM 1 WE CHARACTERIZE LEVELS, SEQUENCE INTACTNESS AND DECAY DYNAMICS OF HIV-1 PROVIRAL DNA, WITH THE HYPOTHESIS THAT INDIVIDUALS WHO ACQUIRE HIV-1 ON PREP WILL HAVE LOWER LEVELS OF TOTAL AND INFERRED SEQUENCE INTACT PROVIRAL DNA WITH A FASTER RATE OF DECAY. IN AIM 2, WE INVESTIGATE SPONTANEOUS AND INDUCIBLE EXPRESSION OF HIV-1 BY EXAMINING LEVELS AND INFERRED SEQUENCE INTACTNESS OF VIRAL RNA IN PLASMA, AND SPONTANEOUS AND INDUCIBLE VIRUS RELEASE IN EX VIVO CELL CULTURE EXPERIMENTS WITH THE HYPOTHESIS THAT INDIVIDUALS WHO ACQUIRE HIV-1 ON PREP WILL HAVE LOWER LEVELS OF BOTH SPONTANEOUS AND INDUCIBLE INFECTIOUS VIRUS THAN INDIVIDUALS WHO STARTED ART IN ACUTE INFECTION. IN AIM 3, WE CHARACTERIZE HIV-SPECIFIC T CELL AND ANTIBODY RESPONSES, T CELL ACTIVATION AND EXHAUSTION AND SOLUBLE MARKERS OF INFLAMMATION AND IMMUNE ACTIVATION THAT CONTRIBUTE TO HIV-ASSOCIATED DISEASE. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT INDIVIDUALS WHO ACQUIRE HIV-1 WHILE ON PREP WILL HAVE ALTERED HIV-SPECIFIC IMMUNE RESPONSES AND LOWER LEVELS OF IMMUNE ACTIVATION AND INFLAMMATION THAN THOSE WHO START ART IN ACUTE INFECTION. WE WILL APPLY A NOVEL AND INTERPRETABLE MACHINE LEARNING METHOD THAT WILL INTEGRATE ALL RESERVOIR AND IMMUNE ASSAY DATA TO UNCOVER UNDERLYING PATTERNS AND MECHANISTIC RELATIONSHIPS THAT MAY DISTINGUISH THESE TWO CLINICAL POPULATIONS. CHARACTERIZING HIV-1 RESERVOIRS AND IMMUNE FUNCTION IN THIS POPULATION COULD IDENTIFY IMPORTANT VIROLOGIC OR IMMUNOLOGIC FACTORS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO SUSTAINED ART-FREE REMISSION. THESE AIMS, WHICH REPRESENT A NEW AREA OF CROSS-CUTTING RESEARCH AT THE INTERSECTION OF HIV-1 PROPHYLAXIS, TREATMENT AND REMISSION, WILL SET THE STAGE FOR FURTHER INVESTIGATIONS FOR PWH TO ACHIEVE AN ART-FREE LIFE, WITH OR WITHOUT ADDITIONAL THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NANOSCALE IMAGING OF CELL SURFACE HIV ENV IMMUNE COMPLEXES TO OPTIMIZE NK CELL ADCC ANTIBODY THERAPEUTICS - SUMMARY NATURAL KILLER (NK) CELL-MEDIATED ANTIBODY-DEPENDENT CELLULAR CYTOTOXICITY (ADCC) IS A POWERFUL MECHANISM BY WHICH THE IMMUNE SYSTEM CAN CLEAR HIV-1-INFECTED CELLS AND DRIVE THE LONG-TERM SUPPRESSION OF VIRAL RESERVOIRS, LIKELY SUPPORTED BY THE EARLY ANTIBODY-BASED IMMUNE RESPONSE. DESPITE PROMISING ADVANCES IN ANTIBODY-BASED THERAPIES, NK CELL ACTIVATION AND CLEARANCE OF HIV INFECTED CELLS REMAINS LIMITED BY VIRAL EVASION STRATEGIES. THE SPATIAL ORGANIZATION AND CONFORMATIONAL STATE OF ENVELOPE (ENV) IMMUNE COMPLEXES (ICS), ALONG WITH NK CELL RECEPTOR COORDINATION, ARE CRITICAL DETERMINANTS OF ADCC EFFICACY, YET REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD AT THE MOLECULAR LEVEL. WE HAVE SHOWN THAT ANTIBODY STOICHIOMETRY SUBSTANTIALLY INFLUENCES NK CELL ADCC. FURTHER, WE PROVIDE PRELIMINARY DATA THAT DEMONSTRATES THAT IC GEOMETRY CAN SIGNIFICANTLY ALTER NK CELL ADCC ACTIVITY. HOWEVER, OUR LIMITED UNDERSTANDING OF THE BASIS OF NK CELL ADCC ABROGATES OUR ABILITY TO PREDICTABLY ENGINEER POTENT IN VIVO ADCC ACTIVITY INTO ANTIBODY THERAPEUTICS, INCLUDING BROADLY NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES (BNABS) CURRENTLY IN CLINICAL TRIALS. WE HAVE PREVIOUSLY DEMONSTRATED THAT INTEGRATING MACHINE LEARNING (ML) WITH IN SILICO PROTEIN MODELING CAN ENABLE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL PROTEIN DESIGNS, INCLUDING NANOBODIES. RAPID DEVELOPMENT IN THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) FIELD HAS SHOWN THAT SUCH DESIGNS COULD BE USED TO BUILD FULL ANTIBODIES DE NOVO. BY TRAINING NEW ALGORITHMS ON STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL DATA, WE CAN ACCELERATE THE PRODUCTION OF NEW ANTIBODIES THAT GO BEYOND TRADITIONAL METHODS, SUCH AS MONOCLONAL ANTIBODY ISOLATION OR LIBRARY SCREENING USING BIOLOGICAL ASSAYS. THIS PROPOSAL WILL ADDRESS KEY GAPS IN OUR KNOWLEDGE OF NK CELL ADCC USING INTEGRATED MULTIDISCIPLINARY EXPERTISE, BUILDING ON PROMISING PRELIMINARY DATA TOWARD DESIGNING DE NOVO ANTIBODIES WITH ENHANCED ADCC ACTIVITY. IN AIM 1, WE WILL EVALUATE THE NK CELL ADCC ACTIVITY OF A PANEL OF BOTH BNABS AND NON-NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES THAT ARE KNOWN TO ENHANCE ADCC. WE WILL ALSO USE MINFLUX NANOSCOPY TO RESOLVE THE NANOSCALE STRUCTURE OF HIV ENV AND ENV ICS ON THE SURFACE OF HIV ENV PRESENTING CELLS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL BUILD UPON OUR PREVIOUS WORK DEFINING THE SPATIAL ORGANIZATION OF THE IGG RECEPTOR CD16 WITHIN THE NK CELL SYNAPSE TO DETERMINE HOW ENV ICS INFLUENCES THE SPATIAL ORGANIZATION OF CD16 AS WELL AS ADDITIONAL ACTIVATING RECEPTORS WITHIN THE IMMUNE SYNAPSE. IN AIM 3, WE WILL CREATE AND VALIDATE A ML ALGORITHM CAPABLE OF ACCURATELY PREDICTING THE STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL PROPERTIES OF HIV-TARGETING NANOBODIES. USING THIS MODEL, WE WILL DESIGN NEW NANOBODY CANDIDATES IN SILICO THAT TARGET ENV EPITOPES PREDICTED TO ELICIT ENHANCED ADCC AND VALIDATE PROMISING CANDIDATES. THIS PROPOSAL WILL DEFINE THE MOLECULAR ARCHITECTURE OF THE ADCC SYNAPSE AGAINST ENV PRESENTING TARGET CELLS AND USE THIS TO CREATE A ML FRAMEWORK LINKING ENV MOLECULAR FEATURES TO NK CELL ADCC. DUAL INNOVATION IN OUR APPROACH (APPLYING MINFLUX NANOSCOPY TO ENV IMMUNOBIOLOGY AND UTILIZING CUTTING-EDGE ML AND PROTEIN DESIGN TO DEVELOP NOVEL THERAPEUTICS) DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THE GOALS OF PAR-25-300 TO ADVANCE IMMUNE-BASED HIV CURE STRATEGIES. THE RESULTING INSIGHTS FROM OUR STUDIES WILL GUIDE SUBSEQUENT THERAPEUTIC ANTIBODY DESIGNS TO TARGET HIV RESERVOIRS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GENOME-SCALE IDENTIFICATION OF ESSENTIAL PLASMODIUM FALCIPARUM DETERMINANTS OF ERYTHROCYTE INVASION - PLASMODIUM PARASITES ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR HUNDREDS OF MILLIONS OF MALARIA CASES ANNUALLY. THE DEADLIEST OF THE HUMAN MALARIA PARASITES, PLASMODIUM FALCIPARUM, PROLIFERATES WITHIN RED BLOOD CELLS (RBCS), AND CAN REACH ENORMOUS PARASITE BIOMASS, CAUSING SEVERE DISEASE AND DEATH. INVASION OF RBCS BY MEROZOITE FORMS OF P. FALCIPARUM IS A COMPLEX PROCESS THAT REQUIRES NUMEROUS MOLECULAR INTERACTIONS BETWEEN THE PARASITE AND HOST. THE P. FALCIPARUM GENOME IS PREDICTED TO ENCODE SEVERAL HUNDRED ANTIGENS AND SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION PROTEINS, SEVERAL OF WHICH ARE PROMISING VACCINE CANDIDATES OR THERAPEUTIC TARGETS. THE DEPLOYMENT OF INVASION LIGANDS IS ORCHESTRATED BY A CASCADE OF SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION ENZYMES THAT COORDINATE THE EVENTS OF EGRESS AND INVASION. FUNCTIONAL GENOMIC APPROACHES PROMISE TO COMPREHENSIVELY REVEAL THE CRITICAL MOLECULES AND PATHWAYS UNDERLYING HOST-PATHOGEN INTERACTIONS. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL LEVERAGE A NOVEL TRANSPOSON-BASED STRATEGY TO IDENTIFY DETERMINANTS OF RBC INVASION IN MULTIPLE P. FALCIPARUM STRAINS WITH DISTINCT PHENOTYPES IN RBC INVASION, ANTIMALARIAL DRUG-RESISTANCE, CONTINENTAL ORIGIN, AND TRANSMISSION. OUR MAJOR HYPOTHESIS IS THAT MULTIPLE GENES INTERACT TO FORM CRITICAL HUBS REQUIRED FOR THE INVASION PROCESS IN P. FALCIPARUM, SPANNING BOTH LIGAND-RECEPTOR INTERACTIONS AND SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO PRODUCE A HIGH CONFIDENCE MAP OF THE ESSENTIAL GENOME OF P. FALCIPARUM THAT WE WILL INTEGRATE WITH AVAILABLE OMIC DATA TO CREATE AN INVALUABLE RESOURCE FOR THE RESEARCH COMMUNITY.

description: TARGETING A35 TO UNLOCK BROAD-SPECTRUM HUMAN IMMUNITY AGAINST ORTHOPOXVIRUSES - SUMMARY THE 2022 GLOBAL OUTBREAK OF MPOX (MONKEYPOX DISEASE), CAUSED BY MONKEYPOX VIRUS (MPXV), UNDERSCORED THE URGENT NEED FOR MORE EFFECTIVE TOOLS TO COMBAT THIS RE-EMERGING PATHOGEN. CURRENT COUNTERMEASURES—NAMELY, THE JYNNEOS VACCINE AND THE ANTIVIRAL TECOVIRIMAT—ARE INADEQUATE: THE VACCINE ELICITS ONLY MODEST AND SHORT-LIVED PROTECTION, AND TECOVIRIMAT HAS FAILED TO DEMONSTRATE EFFICACY IN HUMAN CLINICAL TRIALS. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA REVEAL THAT NATURAL MPXV INFECTION, BUT NOT VACCINATION, INDUCES A ROBUST ANTIBODY RESPONSE TO THE VIRAL PROTEIN A35, AND WE HAVE ISOLATED THREE HIGHLY PROTECTIVE A35-SPECIFIC MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS) FROM AN INFECTED INDIVIDUAL. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO DEFINE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH THESE MABS CONFER PROTECTION AND TO ELUCIDATE THE QUALITATIVE DIFFERENCES IN A35-TARGETED ANTIBODY RESPONSES ELICITED BY INFECTION VERSUS VACCINATION. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DISSECT THE ROLE OF FC-MEDIATED EFFECTOR FUNCTIONS IN THE PROPHYLACTIC AND THERAPEUTIC ACTIVITY OF THESE ANTIBODIES, INCLUDING IN A MUCOSAL CHALLENGE MODEL THAT MIMICS HUMAN MPXV TRANSMISSION. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ISOLATE AND CHARACTERIZE NEW A35- SPECIFIC MABS FROM INFECTED AND VACCINATED INDIVIDUALS TO DEFINE STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF PROTECTION AND ANALYZE B CELL RESPONSES AT SINGLE-CELL RESOLUTION. THESE STUDIES WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO ANTIBODY-MEDIATED IMMUNITY TO MPXV AND LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR RATIONAL DESIGN OF IMPROVED ANTIBODY-BASED THERAPEUTICS AND NEXT-GENERATION VACCINES TO PREVENT FUTURE MPOX OUTBREAKS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMMUNE PROTECTION AGAINST H5N1 INFLUENZA VIRUS INFECTION AND TRANSMISSION - PROJECT SUMMARY A GLOBAL PANDEMIC WITH A RESPIRATORY VIRUS CAN BE DEVASTATING, AS EVIDENCED BY THE SARS-COV-2 PANDEMIC FIVE YEARS AGO. HIGHLY PATHOGENIC AVIAN INFLUENZA VIRUSES, INCLUDING CLADE 2.3.4.4, HAVE REMAINED A MAJOR THREAT FOR CAUSING THE NEXT PANDEMIC. THE RISK OF AN H5 INFLUENZA PANDEMIC HAS INCREASED CONSIDERABLY BECAUSE OF THE CLADE 2.3.4.4B H5N1 OUTBREAK IN THE UNITED STATES IN POULTRY, DAIRY COWS, AND MANY OTHER WILDLIFE SPECIES. THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE VACCINES THAT PROTECT AGAINST H5N1 INFECTION AND REDUCE SPREAD OF THE VIRUS ARE URGENTLY NEEDED IN THE EVENT OF FURTHER VIRUS ADAPTATION AND HUMAN TRANSMISSION. MUCOSAL VACCINES HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO INDUCE LOCAL IMMUNITY AT THE PORTAL OF VIRUS ENTRY AND PROVIDE SUPERIOR PROTECTION AGAINST INFLUENZA AND OTHER RESPIRATORY VIRUSES. THE PRIMARY GOAL OF THIS APPLICATION IS TO DEVELOP A MUCOSAL H5 INFLUENZA VIRUS VACCINE THAT CONFERS ROBUST PROTECTION AGAINST A HIGH-DOSE H5N1 CHALLENGE AND TRANSMISSION IN TWO DIFFERENT PRE-CLINICAL ANIMAL MODELS. UNIVARIATE REGRESSION ANALYSIS WILL IDENTIFY THE DOMINANT CORRELATES OF IMMUNE PROTECTION MEDIATED BY OUR MUCOSAL VACCINE. A SECOND GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY STRATEGIES AND MECHANISMS TO OVERCOME IMMUNE IMPRINTING AND GENERATE DE NOVO ANTIBODY RESPONSES AGAINST EPITOPES ON THE HA PROTEIN OF INFLUENZA VIRUS THAT ELICIT POTENTLY NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES. OUR INTERACTIVE TEAM HAS AN ESTABLISHED TRACK RECORD IN DESIGNING VIRAL IMMUNOGENS, DEVELOPING MUCOSAL VACCINES USING THE CHIMPANZEE ADENOVIRUS VECTORED PLATFORM, PERFORMING PRE-CLINICAL STUDIES, AND EVALUATING IMPRINTED ANTIBODY RESPONSES IN HUMANS AND ANIMAL MODELS AFTER VACCINATION. COLLECTIVELY, THE STUDIES DESCRIBED IN THIS APPLICATION HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO PRODUCE A SINGLE-DOSE H5 VACCINE THAT PROTECTS AGAINST H5N1 VIRUS IN THE SETTING OF PRIOR IMMUNITY TO SEASONAL INFLUENZA VIRUSES.
