description: HIGH AVIDITY MULTIEPITOPE TARGETING OF RNA-INDUCED CELL SURFACE HIV ENV - PROJECT SUMMARY DESPITE THE SUCCESS OF ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART), HIV-1 PERSISTS IN LONG-LIVED CELLULAR RESERVOIRS THAT EVADE IMMUNE CLEARANCE. THESE LATENT PROVIRUSES REMAIN THE MAJOR BARRIER TO CURE, AS THEY RE- EMERGE WHEN ART IS WITHDRAWN. THE HIV-1 ENVELOPE GLYCOPROTEIN (ENV), EXPRESSED ON THE SURFACE OF INFECTED CELLS, PROVIDES A LOGICAL TARGET FOR IMMUNE CLEARANCE BUT IS IMMUNOLOGICALLY ELUSIVE. LATENT CELLS EXPRESS LITTLE TO NO ENV, AND ACTIVELY INFECTED CELLS DISPLAY ENV AT LOW DENSITY AND IN HETEROGENEOUS CONFORMATIONS, REDUCING SENSITIVITY TO ANTIBODY-MEDIATED RESPONSES. THIS PROPOSAL INTEGRATES TWO TRANSFORMATIVE TECHNOLOGIES—RNA-BASED LATENCY REVERSAL AND ENGINEERED HIGH-AVIDITY ANTIBODIES—TO OVERCOME THESE BARRIERS AND ADVANCE A RATIONAL “INDUCE-AND-CLEAR” THERAPEUTIC FRAMEWORK. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES SHOW THAT LIPID NANOPARTICLE (LNP) DELIVERY OF TAT MRNA AND CRISPRA MRNA CAN POTENTLY AND SYNERGISTICALLY REACTIVATE LATENT PROVIRUSES, IN SOME CASES EXCEEDING THE ACTIVITY OF STRONG MITOGEN STIMULATION WHILE AVOIDING BROAD T CELL ACTIVATION. FURTHER ENHANCEMENT IS ACHIEVED WITH DNA METHYLATION INHIBITORS SUCH AS 5-AZACYTIDINE OR WITH CAS9-TETHERED TET1, PROVIDING SITE- SPECIFIC EPIGENETIC REPROGRAMMING TO AWAKEN REFRACTORY PROVIRUSES. AT THE SAME TIME, OUR WORK DEMONSTRATES THAT ENV DISPLAYED ON INFECTED CELLS IS STRUCTURALLY DISTINCT FROM VIRION-ASSOCIATED ENV, OFTEN UNCLEAVED AND DYNAMICALLY SAMPLING CONFORMATIONS POORLY RECOGNIZED BY MANY BROADLY NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES (BNABS). THIS HETEROGENEITY UNDERLIES INCOMPLETE NEUTRALIZATION OF CELL-TO-CELL TRANSMISSION, EMPHASIZING THE NEED FOR NEW ANTIBODY DESIGNS. WE PROPOSE TO TEST A STRATEGY THAT MAXIMIZES ENV EXPRESSION AND OPTIMIZES ITS RECOGNITION BY ENGINEERED ANTIBODIES. IN AIM 1, WE WILL ENHANCE RESERVOIR CLEARANCE BY COMBINING TAT, CRISPRA, AND CAS9-TETHERED TET1 MRNAS IN TARGETED LNPS, DEFINING CONDITIONS THAT YIELD ROBUST ENV INDUCTION IN VITRO AND IN HUMANIZED MICE. IN AIM 2, WE WILL IDENTIFY MAXIMALLY SYNERGISTIC BNAB COMBINATIONS THAT ACHIEVE HIGH CELL-SURFACE BINDING AND POTENT FCΓRIIIA CROSSLINKING, ENGINEERING BISPECIFIC ANTIBODIES THAT RECRUIT NK CELLS FOR ANTIBODY-DEPENDENT CELLULAR CYTOTOXICITY (ADCC). IN AIM 3, WE WILL ADAPT THE ADAPTIVE MULTI-EPITOPE TARGETING WITH ENHANCED AVIDITY (AMETA) PLATFORM PIONEERED BY MPI YI SHI TO HIV ENV, CREATING MULTIVALENT IGM-SCAFFOLDED ANTIBODIES WITH ULTRAHIGH AVIDITY AND ENGINEERED FC DOMAINS THAT DRIVE NK CELL RECRUITMENT AND CLEARANCE OF ENV-EXPRESSING CELLS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ANTIMICROBIAL AGENTS DERIVED FROM AAPEPTIDE BIOMATERIALS - THE WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION (WHO) HAS RECENTLY IDENTIFIED ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE AS ONE OF THE THREE GREAT- EST THREATS IN THE 21ST CENTURY, HIGHLIGHTING THE URGENT NEED TO DEVELOP NEW ANTIBACTERIAL BIOMATERIALS WITH NOVEL MECHANISMS TO COMBAT INFECTIONS CAUSED BY THESE VIRTUALLY UNTREATABLE PATHOGENS. HOST-DEFENSE PEPTIDES (HDPS) ARE CATIONIC PEPTIDES FOUND IN VIRTUALLY ALL LIVING ORGANISMS AND HAVE BROAD-SPECTRUM ACTIVITY AGAINST BOTH GRAM-POSITIVE AND GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA, AS THEY KILL BACTERIA MAINLY BY DISRUPTING THEIR MEMBRANES, REDUCING THE LIKELIHOOD OF BACTERIA DEVELOPING DRUG RESISTANCE OBSERVED WITH CURRENT ANTIBIOTIC TREATMENTS. DESPITE SIGNIF- ICANT ENTHUSIASM, THERE ARE INTRINSIC DRAWBACKS ASSOCIATED WITH PEPTIDE ANTIBIOTICS, INCLUDING THEIR COMMON SUS- CEPTIBILITY TO ENZYMATIC DEGRADATION, LOW-TO-MODERATE ACTIVITY, INCONVENIENT OPTIMIZATION AND HIGH COST.  IN THE PAST FEW YEARS, WE HAVE DESIGNED AAPEPTIDE-DERIVED BIOMATERIALS, INCLUDING A CLASS OF NOVEL HYDANTOIN DERIVATIVES LICENSED TO A PHARMACEUTICAL COMPANY FOR FURTHER DEVELOPMENT. THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL INSPIRES US TO DEVELOP NOVEL CLASS OF HDP-MIMICKING SMALL MOLECULES AS ANTIMICROBIAL AGENTS TO COMBAT ANTIBIOTIC RE- SISTANCE. IN THIS STRATEGY, WE PROPOSED A MODULAR APPROACH TO DEVELOP SMALL SCORPION-LIKE AMPHIPATHIC PEP- TIDOMIMETIC BIOMATERIALS BEARING CATIONIC CHARGES AND HYDROPHOBIC GROUPS, LEADING TO IDENTIFICATION OF NEW CLASS OF MOLECULES EXHIBITING POTENT AND BROAD-SPECTRUM ANTIMICROBIAL ACTIVITY AGAINST A PANEL OF MULTIDRUG RESISTANT BACTERIAL STRAINS. AS SUCH, OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO DEVELOP A NEW CLASS OF ANTIBIOTIC AGENTS WITH NOVEL MECHA- NISMS FOR THE TREATMENT OF DRUG-RESISTANT BACTERIAL INFECTIONS. THE OBJECTIVE HERE, IS TO FURTHER DEVELOP SCORPION- LIKE MOLECULE DERIVATIVES WITH GREATER POTENCY THROUGH OPTIMIZATION OF CURRENT LEAD COMPOUNDS. OUR CENTRAL HY- POTHESIS IS THAT THESE SMALL MOLECULES BASED ON THE SCORPION-LIKE SCAFFOLD, WITH PROPER DESIGN AND MODIFICATION, COULD BE FURTHER IMPROVED IN BACTERIAL KILLING THROUGH NOVEL MECHANISMS. TO TEST OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS AND, WE WILL FIRST DESIGN AND SYNTHESIZE ANALOGS OF PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED LEAD MOLECULES, AND IDENTIFY MORE POTENT MOLE- CULES AGAINST BOTH GRAM-POSITIVE METHICILLIN-RESISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (MRSA) (MIC ≤ 1 ΜG/ML) AND GRAM-NEGATIVE PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA (MIC ≤ 2 ΜG/ML). NEXT, WE WILL STUDY IF THEIR BACTERICIDAL MECHANISM INVOLVES MEMBRANE ACTION, AND ASSESS THEIR PROBABILITY OF ELICITING ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL EVALUATE THE IN VIVO ACTIVITY OF LEAD COMPOUNDS IN A THIGH-INFECTION MOUSE MODEL TO DEMONSTRATE THEIR POTENTIAL AS A NEW GENERATION OF ANTIBIOTICS WITH NOVEL MECHANISMS.  THE WORK PROPOSED IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE THESE COMPOUNDS ARE A NEW CLASS OF SCORPION-LIKE SMALL MOLECULES THAT KILL BOTH GRAM-POSITIVE AND GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA WITH NOVEL MECHANISMS. THEY ARE HIGHLY AMENABLE TO DERIVATIZATION AND OPTIMIZATION AND POSSESS LOW PROPENSITY TO INDUCE ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE. THE PROPOSED WORK IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE CURRENTLY THERE ARE NO EFFECTIVE METHODS TO COMBAT EMERGING DRUG RESISTANCE. OUR RE- SEARCH STRATEGY WILL LEAD TO A PROMISING THERAPEUTIC APPROACH TO TREATING ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANT PATHOGENS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CONTRIBUTIONS OF NEONATAL-ORIGIN CD4 T CELLS TO IMMUNITY AND TISSUE FUNCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY NEONATAL T CELLS HAVE DISTINCT PROPERTIES THAT REPRESENT AN ADAPTION TO THE RAPIDLY CHANGING TISSUE ENVIRONMENT DURING EARLY LIFE. THOSE FEATURES INCLUDE A T CELL RECEPTOR (TCR) REPERTOIRE SKEWED TOWARDS SELF-REACTIVITY, ENHANCED EFFECTOR FUNCTION, RAPID PROLIFERATION, AND EFFICIENT TISSUE SEEDING. IMPORTANTLY, T CELLS OF NEONATAL ORIGIN PERSIST INTO ADULTHOOD AND REPRESENT A FUNCTIONAL LAYER OF THE ADULT IMMUNE SYSTEM. MOST OF THE WORK HAS CENTERED ON NEONATAL-DERIVED CD8 T CELLS AND THEIR CONTRIBUTIONS TO EARLY PATHOGEN CLEARANCE. WE HAVE DEVELOPED A NOVEL TIMESTAMPING SYSTEM THAT ALLOWS US TO TRACK T CELLS OF NEONATAL ORIGIN AND THEIR PERSISTENCE AND FUNCTIONAL CONTRIBUTIONS TO ADULT IMMUNITY. WE WILL LEVERAGE THIS SYSTEM TO UNCOVER FUNDAMENTAL FEATURES OF THE NEONATAL LAYER OF CD4 T CELLS AND THEIR CONTRIBUTION TO IMMUNITY THROUGHOUT THE LIFESPAN OF AN ANIMAL. OUR INITIAL CHARACTERIZATION CONFIRMED THAT NEONATAL-ORIGIN CD4 T CELLS PERSIST INTO ADULTHOOD AND LIKELY CONTRIBUTE TO FUNCTIONAL IMMUNITY BY OCCUPYING A SPECIALIZED NICHE. INTRIGUINGLY, NEONATAL-ORIGIN CD4 T CELLS WERE ENRICHED FOR MEMORY-PHENOTYPE CELLS, A CELL STATE USUALLY ASSOCIATED WITH RAPID EFFECTOR CAPACITY AND INNATE (TCR-INDEPENDENT) RESPONSE CAPACITY BUT INCOMPLETELY UNDERSTOOD. DO NEONATAL-ORIGIN CD4 T CELLS CONTRIBUTE TO EARLY INNATE-LIKE RESPONSES DURING ACUTE INFECTIONS? WHAT ARE THE UNDERLYING REGULATORY NETWORKS THAT FACILITATE MEMORY-PHENOTYPE RESPONSES? WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT NEONATAL-ORIGIN CD4 T CELLS REPRESENT AN IMPORTANT FUNCTIONAL LAYER OF THE ADULT IMMUNE SYSTEM AS RAPID RESPONDERS TO ACUTE INFECTION THROUGH THEIR PERSISTENCE AS MEMORY-PHENOTYPE CELLS. USING OUR TIMESTAMPING MODELS, WE WILL LEVERAGE ACCESS TO THE NEONATAL CD4 T CELL LAYER IN ADULT MICE TO DEFINE THEIR FUNCTIONAL CONTRIBUTIONS TO ADDRESS THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS: 1) WHAT IS THE BREADTH OF INNATE RESPONSIVENESS OF THESE NEONATAL-ORIGIN MEMORY-PHENOTYPE CELLS, AND CAN WE DEFINE THE UNDERLYING TRANSCRIPTIONAL NETWORK? 2) DO MEMORY-PHENOTYPE CELLS HELP PROTECT THE HOST DURING EARLY INFECTION? 3) CAN NEONATAL-ORIGIN T CELLS RETAIN THEIR EFFECTOR PROPERTIES IN SETTINGS OF CHRONIC ANTIGEN EXPOSURE? ARE THEY BETTER ANTI-TUMOR EFFECTORS? 4) CAN WE LEVERAGE THE ENRICHMENT OF NEONATAL-ORIGIN TREG CELLS IN ADIPOSE AND SKIN TO UNCOVER THE ORGANIZING PRINCIPLES OF HOW THEY PROMOTE TISSUE HOMEOSTASIS? OUR WORK WILL PROVIDE FOUNDATIONAL INSIGHTS INTO THE CONTRIBUTIONS OF THE NEONATAL CD4 T CELL LAYER TO THE ROBUSTNESS OF THE ADULT IMMUNE SYSTEM THROUGH THEIR RAPID ELABORATION OF EFFECTOR PROGRAMS LINKED TO THEIR MEMORY-PHENOTYPE FEATURES. ELUCIDATION OF THE PROGRAMS GOVERNING RAPID EFFECTOR RESPONSES FOR NEONATAL-ORIGIN CD4 T CELLS AND NEONATAL-ORIGIN TREG-MEDIATED TISSUE HOMEOSTASIS WILL PAVE THE WAY TOWARDS THERAPEUTIC TARGETING OR MANIPULATION TO ENHANCE EFFECTOR RESPONSES AND PROMOTE TISSUE ROBUSTNESS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INDUCTION OF ACQUIRED FETAL TOLERANCE THROUGH AN EPO-DEPENDENT PATHWAY - PROJECT SUMMARY  ACQUIRED TOLERANCE PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE ACROSS A BROAD SPECTRUM OF HUMAN BIOLOGY SPANNING ORGAN TRANSPLANTATION AND PREGNANCY. THE WORK PROPOSED HERE DRAWS INSPIRATION FROM OUR WORK EXAMINING EPOR SIGNALING IN CONVENTIONAL TYPE 1 DENDRITIC CELLS (CDC1S) IN SOLID ORGAN TRANSPLANTATION TO UNDERSTAND HOW T-CELL MEDIATED TOLERANCE IS INITIATED AND MAINTAINED IN HUMAN PREGNANCY. TISSUE HYPOXIA AT THE MATERNAL-FETAL INTERFACE IS A KEY REGULATOR OF PLACENTAL INVASION, SPIRAL ARTERY REMODELING, AND EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX REMODELING THAT TRIGGERS EPO PRODUCTION BY THE PLACENTA. ADDITIONALLY, PLACENTAL TROPHOBLASTS UNDERGO EXTENSIVE APOPTOSIS THROUGHOUT GESTATION. OUR HYPOTHESIS IS THAT THE CONVERGENCE OF PLACENTAL EPO AND TROPHOBLAST APOPTOSIS DRIVE FETAL AG-SPECIFIC TREG INDUCTION AND CD8 T-CELL EXHAUSTION THROUGH A CDC1-DEPENDENT MECHANISM. TO TEST THIS, WE WILL USE A STRATEGY THAT LEVERAGES PRIMARY HUMAN TISSUE, ANIMAL MODELS, AND NEXT-GENERATION ASSAYS IN SPATIAL BIOLOGY TO UNDERSTAND THIS PROCESS. WE WILL USE TRANSGENIC MOUSE MODELS TO ELUCIDATE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH EPOR SIGNALING IN CDC1S PROMOTES FETAL TOLERANCE DURING SUCCESSIVE PREGNANCIES. USING NEXT GENERATION TOOLS FOR SPATIAL BIOLOGY, WE WILL ANALYZE CDC1S IN HUMAN TISSUE TO DETERMINE IF THE COMPOSITION AND STRUCTURE OF DECIDUA AND UTERINE DRAINING LYMPH NODES ALIGN WITH OUR PROPOSED MODEL AND THE RESULTS OF OUR TRANSGENIC MOUSE EXPERIMENTS. THESE RESULTS WILL BE COMPARED WITH SAMPLES FROM WOMEN WITH A HISTORY OF RECURRENT PREGNANCY LOSS TO IDENTIFY DIFFERENCES IN DECIDUAL DCS, TREGS, AND CD8 T-CELLS THAT COULD EXPLAIN THIS DISORDER. LASTLY, WE WILL CULTURE HUMAN CDC1S AND DECIDUAL EXPLANTS WITH TROPHOBLASTS OR TROPHOBLAST CONDITIONED MEDIA (CM) TO DETERMINE IF THE PLACENTAL SECRETOME IS SUFFICIENT FOR INDUCING CDC1 TOLEROGENIC PHENOTYPES. TOGETHER, THIS COMBINATION OF MURINE FUNCTIONAL MODELS, DEEP SPATIAL ANALYSIS OF HUMAN TISSUES, AND IN VITRO STUDIES OF HUMAN DECIDUA, PLACENTA, AND IMMUNE CELLS WILL ALLOW US TO TEST OUR MODEL, TO ASSESS ITS RELEVANCE IN HUMANS, AND TO PROVIDE NEW DIRECTIONS FOR TREATING PREGNANCY DISORDERS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING AND CHARACTERIZATION OF SMALL-MOLECULE INHIBITORS OF N-TERMINAL AUTOPROTEOLYSIS OF CORONAVIRUS MAIN PROTEASE PRECURSORS - HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING AND CHARACTERIZATION OF SMALL-MOLECULE INHIBITORS TARGETING N-TERMINAL  AUTOPROTEOLYSIS OF CORONAVIRUS MAIN PROTEASE PRECURSORS PROJECT SUMMARY MANY VIRUSES—INCLUDING RETROVIRUSES AND SEVERAL PATHOGENS OF PANDEMIC POTENTIAL (PPPS) SUCH AS CORONAVIRUSES, FLAVIVIRUSES, AND PICORNAVIRUSES—SHARE A CONSERVED REPLICATION STRATEGY INVOLVING POLYPROTEIN PRECURSORS THAT CONTAIN A VIRUS-ENCODED PROTEASE. THESE PROTEASE-CONTAINING PRECURSORS UNDERGO REGULATED AUTOPROCESSING TO RELEASE MATURE ENZYMES ESSENTIAL FOR VIRAL REPLICATION. WHILE MATURE VIRAL PROTEASES ARE PROVEN ANTIVIRAL DRUG TARGETS, THEIR PRECURSOR FORMS REMAIN LARGELY UNEXPLORED. OUR TEAM HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT THE HIV- 1 PROTEASE PRECURSOR IS ENZYMATICALLY DISTINCT FROM ITS MATURE COUNTERPART AND DEVELOPED A CELL-BASED HIGH- THROUGHPUT SCREENING (HTS) PLATFORM TO IDENTIFY COMPOUNDS THAT SELECTIVELY INTERFERE WITH PRECURSOR-MEDIATED AUTOPROTEOLYSIS. USING THIS APPROACH, WE RECENTLY IDENTIFIED SEVERAL SMALL-MOLECULE HITS THAT SUPPRESS BOTH WILD- TYPE AND MULTIPLE DRUG-RESISTANT HIV VARIANTS WITH COMPARABLE POTENCY, VALIDATING THE PRECURSOR AUTOPROTEOLYSIS AS A PROMISING PAN-HIV ANTIVIRAL TARGET. TO EXTEND THIS STRATEGY, WE DEVELOPED AN ANALOGOUS CELL-BASED ASSAY FOR N-TERMINAL AUTOPROTEOLYSIS OF THE CORONAVIRUS MAIN PROTEASE (MPRO). NOTABLY, AS WITH HIV-1 PROTEASE, PRECURSOR FORMS OF SARS-COV-2 AND MERS-COV MPRO EXHIBIT MARKEDLY REDUCED SENSITIVITY (≥20-FOLD) TO INHIBITORS DESIGNED FOR THE MATURE ENZYME. THIS PLATFORM ALSO ENABLES PARALLEL SCREENING FOR INHIBITORS TARGETING EITHER PRECURSOR OR MATURE MPRO FORMS. PILOT SCREENS OF 130 KNOWN PROTEASE INHIBITORS AND 1,120 NATURAL PRODUCT EXTRACTS (NPES: ~22,000 INDIVIDUAL COMPOUNDS) CONFIRMED THE ASSAY'S ROBUSTNESS AND IDENTIFIED ~10 NPES WITH REPRODUCIBLE, ALBEIT MODEST, ACTIVITIES. BUILDING ON THIS FOUNDATION, THE PROPOSED PROJECT AIMS TO IDENTIFY SMALL-MOLECULE THERAPEUTIC CANDIDATES WITH PAN-CORONAVIRUS ACTIVITY THAT SELECTIVELY INTERFERE WITH THE CONSERVED N-TERMINAL AUTOPROTEOLYSIS OF MPRO PRECURSORS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL: SCREEN THE SBP SMALL-MOLECULE LIBRARY (~100,000 ENAMINE REAL COMPOUNDS) USING OUR CELL-BASED FUNCTIONAL ASSAY TO IDENTIFY HIT COMPOUNDS THAT CAN INHIBIT PRECURSOR AUTOPROTEOLYSIS (AIM 1); DEFINE ACTIVE COMPONENTS FROM THE POSITIVE NPES THROUGH SYSTEMATIC SUBFRACTIONATION AND CHARACTERIZATION (AIM 2); ESTABLISH AND VALIDATE ADDITIONAL PROCESSING ASSAYS FOR OTHER CORONAVIRUSES, INCLUDING SARS-COV, MERS-COV, NL63, OC43, ETC., TO ENABLE COMPREHENSIVE HIT CHARACTERIZATION (AIM 3); EVALUATE CONFIRMED HITS IN ORTHOGONAL BIOCHEMICAL, CELLULAR, AND VIROLOGICAL ASSAYS TO DEFINE MECHANISMS OF ACTION (MOAS) AND DISTINGUISH BROAD-SPECTRUM HITS FROM SUBTYPE-SPECIFIC INHIBITORS (AIM 4). IN SUMMARY, THIS PROJECT ADVANCES A NOVEL ANTIVIRAL STRATEGY THAT TARGETS PROTEASE PRECURSOR AUTOPROTEOLYSIS— A CONSERVED PROCESS ACROSS MULTIPLE VIRAL FAMILIES—WITH THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF IDENTIFYING NEW THERAPEUTIC CANDIDATES FOR COMBINATION THERAPY AND ENHANCING PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF BROAD- SPECTRUM ANTIVIRALS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ELUCIDATING THE VIRAL FACTORS AND MECHANISMS DRIVING ORTHOBUNYAVIRUS NEUROPATHOGENESIS - PROJECT SUMMARY: THE ORTHOBUNYAVIRUSES ARE ARBOVIRUSES THAT CAN CAUSE SIGNIFICANT DISEASE IN HUMANS, INCLUDING ENCEPHALITIS AND SEVERE NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE. SOME ORTHOBUNYAVIRUSES CAUSE A HIGH NUMBER OF CASES OF NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE, WHILE OTHERS CAUSE VERY LITTLE OR NONE. VIRAL INFECTIONS IN THE BRAIN ARE MEDIATED BY COMPLEX INTERACTIONS BETWEEN VIRAL AND HOST FACTORS. ENCEPHALITIC VIRUSES MUST BE ABLE TO BOTH CROSS THE BLOOD BRAIN BARRIER TO GAIN ACCESS TO THE BRAIN (NEUROINVASION) AND REPLICATE AND CAUSE DAMAGE ONCE IN THE BRAIN (NEUROVIRULENCE). THE ORTHOBUNYAVIRUS PROTEINS INVOLVED IN NEUROPATHOGENESIS ARE CURRENTLY POORLY UNDERSTOOD, AND THE FACTORS THAT MAKE ONE ORTHOBUNYAVIRUS MORE VIRULENT THAN ANOTHER ARE UNKNOWN. TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP, DIFFERENCES IN NEUROPATHOGENIC PHENOTYPES BETWEEN MEMBERS OF THE CALIFORNIA SEROGROUP (CSG) ORTHOBUNYAVIRUSES WILL BE LEVERAGED TO IDENTIFY THE SPECIFIC VIRAL PROTEINS THAT MEDIATE NEUROINVASION AND NEUROVIRULENCE. LA CROSSE VIRUS (LACV) IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF PEDIATRIC ARBOVIRAL ENCEPHALITIS IN THE UNITED STATES, JAMESTOWN CANYON VIRUS (JCV) IS AN EMERGING VIRUS IN NORTH AMERICA, AND INKOO VIRUS (INKV) HAS CAUSED A SMALL NUMBER OF NEUROINVASIVE CASES IN SCANDINAVIA. IN PREVIOUS STUDIES, IT WAS SHOWN THAT THESE THREE VIRUSES HAVE KEY DIFFERENCES IN NEUROPATHOGENIC PHENOTYPES IN MICE. LACV IS BOTH NEUROINVASIVE AND HAS HIGH NEUROVIRULENCE, JCV IS NOT NEUROINVASIVE BUT HAS HIGH NEUROVIRULENCE, AND INKV IS NEUROINVASIVE BUT HAS LOW NEUROVIRULENCE. CHIMERIC VIRUSES WILL BE GENERATED IN A NEWLY DEVELOPED REVERSE GENETICS SYSTEM THAT ALLOWS FOR FULL GENE SWAPS BETWEEN LACV, JCV AND/OR INKV. THIS WILL ALLOW FOR THE IDENTIFICATION AND CHARACTERIZATION OF VIRAL PROTEINS THAT DRIVE NEUROPATHOGENESIS. IN AIM 1, CHIMERIC VIRUSES WILL BE GENERATED BETWEEN LACV (HIGH NEUROVIRULENCE) AND INKV (LOW NEUROVIRULENCE) TO DETERMINE THE VIRAL PROTEINS THAT MEDIATE LACV’S HIGH NEUROVIRULENCE. THE ROLE OF VIRAL PROTEINS IN NEURONAL REPLICATION, NEURONAL CELL DEATH, AND IMMUNE EVASION IN VITRO AND IN VIVO WILL BE INVESTIGATED. IN AIM 2, CHIMERIC VIRUSES WILL BE GENERATED BETWEEN LACV (NEUROINVASIVE) AND JCV (NOT NEUROINVASIVE) TO DETERMINE THE VIRAL PROTEINS THAT MEDIATE NEUROINVASION. CHIMERIC VIRUSES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR THEIR ABILITY TO FACILITATE NEUROINVASION IN MICE IN VIVO, THEIR ABILITY TO DISRUPT ENDOTHELIAL CELLS OF THE BLOOD BRAIN BARRIER IN MICE IN VIVO AND HUMAN BRAIN ENDOTHELIAL CELLS IN VITRO, AND THE ASSOCIATED HOST RESPONSES THAT LEAD TO VIRAL NEUROINVASION. TOGETHER, THE RESULTS FROM THIS PROPOSAL WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO THE VIRAL PROTEINS AND MECHANISMS THAT MEDIATE ORTHOBUNYAVIRUS NEUROPATHOGENESIS. THESE NOVEL INSIGHTS CAN FURTHER BE EXPANDED TO OTHER ORTHOBUNYAVIRUSES IN THE FUTURE. ULTIMATELY, RESULTS FROM THIS PROPOSAL WILL SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCE FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE OF THE VIRAL AND HOST FACTORS THAT DRIVE ORTHOBUNYAVIRUS NEUROPATHOGENESIS AND WILL IDENTIFY TARGETS FOR TREATMENTS.

description: COMPLEMENT-BOUND EXOSOMES IN HUMAN KIDNEY TRANSPLANT IMMUNITY - SUMMARY KIDNEY TRANSPLANTATION IS THE BEST TREATMENT FOR PATIENTS WITH END-STAGE KIDNEY DISEASE, BUT GRAFT SURVIVAL REMAINS SUBOPTIMAL. A MAJOR BARRIER IS ISCHEMIA–REPERFUSION INJURY (IRI), WHICH INCREASES THE RISK OF DELAYED GRAFT FUNCTION, REJECTION, AND EARLY GRAFT FAILURE, ESPECIALLY IN ORGANS FROM HIGH-RISK DONORS. ALTHOUGH COMPLEMENT ACTIVATION HAS EMERGED AS A CENTRAL DRIVER OF IRI IN EXPERIMENTAL MODELS, TRANSLATION INTO EFFECTIVE HUMAN THERAPIES HAS FAILED, REFLECTING CRITICAL GAPS IN MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING. THIS PROPOSAL WILL ADDRESS THESE GAPS USING EX VIVO NORMOTHERMIC MACHINE PERFUSION (NMP) OF DISCARDED HUMAN KIDNEYS, A UNIQUE PLATFORM TO STUDY IRI DIRECTLY IN HUMAN TISSUE. WE WILL DEFINE HOW KIDNEY-DERIVED COMPLEMENT ACTIVATION REMODELS THE RENAL TRANSCRIPTOME AND EXOSOME CARGO, AND HOW THESE EXOSOMES SHAPE ANTIGEN- PRESENTING CELL AND T CELL RESPONSES. BY TESTING THE EFFECTS OF PATHWAY-SPECIFIC COMPLEMENT INHIBITION DURING NMP, WE WILL DETERMINE MECHANISTIC LINKS BETWEEN IRI AND ALLOIMMUNITY AND IDENTIFY STRATEGIES FOR EX VIVO IMMUNOMODULATION. THIS INNOVATIVE PROPOSAL COMBINES PROLONGED HUMAN KIDNEY PERFUSION WITH STATE-OF-THE-ART TRANSCRIPTOMIC, PROTEOMIC, AND FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS TO REVEAL PATHWAYS THAT CANNOT BE CAPTURED IN ANIMAL MODELS OR CLINICAL RECIPIENTS. THE RESULTS WILL ESTABLISH A NEW EXPERIMENTAL PLATFORM FOR MECHANISTIC DISCOVERY, YIELD BIOMARKERS OF KIDNEY INJURY AND IMMUNOGENICITY, AND PROVIDE A FRAMEWORK FOR RATIONAL COMPLEMENT-TARGETED INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE ORGAN UTILIZATION AND LONG-TERM KIDNEY TRANSPLANT OUTCOMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NANOTRAP THERAPEUTIC VACCINES FOR HIV VIRION CAPTURE AND INFECTED CELL TARGETING - PROJECT SUMMARY: THERAPEUTIC VACCINATION FOR HIV REMAINS AN UNSOLVED CHALLENGE DUE TO HIV’S EXTREME GENETIC DIVERSITY, GLYCAN MASKING OF ENV, AND EARLY ESTABLISHMENT OF VIRAL RESERVOIRS. MOST THERAPEUTIC VACCINES FAIL BECAUSE THEIR ANTIGENS DO NOT MATCH THE PATIENT’S AUTOLOGOUS VIRUS, RESULTING IN WEAK OR NON-PROTECTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES. TO OVERCOME THIS LIMITATION, WE DEVELOPED NANOTRAP THERAPEUTIC VACCINES (NTVS)—ENGINEERED LIPOSOMAL NANOPARTICLES THAT DISPLAY MULTIVALENT CD4 MIMETIC (CD4M) LIGANDS TO CAPTURE CIRCULATING HIV AND ENCAPSULATE INNATE IMMUNE AGONISTS THAT ARE DELIVERED SPECIFICALLY TO ANTIGEN-PRESENTING CELLS (APCS) DURING VIRION UPTAKE. NTVS TRANSFORM THE PATIENT’S OWN VIRUS INTO AN AUTOLOGOUS IMMUNOGEN, ELIMINATING THE NEED FOR VIRAL SEQUENCE PREDICTION. PRELIMINARY STUDIES DEMONSTRATED THAT NTVS EFFICIENTLY BIND HIV VIRIONS, PROMOTE APC UPTAKE, AND INDUCE STRONG ANTIVIRAL CD8 T-CELL RESPONSES IN VIVO. WE ALSO OBSERVED THAT NTVS BIND GP120 EXPRESSED ON INFECTED CELLS, SUGGESTING A SYNERGISTIC MECHANISM IN WHICH NTVS ACTIVATE AND EXPOSE INFECTED CELLS FOR IMMUNE CLEARANCE WHILE SIMULTANEOUSLY AMPLIFYING VIRION RELEASE FOR FURTHER CAPTURE. THIS R01 WILL DEFINE THE MOLECULAR AND IMMUNOLOGICAL DESIGN RULES GOVERNING NTV ACTIVITY. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE HOW NTV–VIRION COMPLEX SIZE AND BIOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES INFLUENCE APC UPTAKE AND DOWNSTREAM IMMUNITY. AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE HOW NTV-DELIVERED INNATE AGONISTS REGULATE APC ACTIVATION STATES AND THERAPEUTIC CD8 T-CELL PRIMING. AIM 3 WILL CHARACTERIZE NTV INTERACTIONS WITH INFECTED CELLS AND IDENTIFY MECHANISMS BY WHICH NTVS ENHANCE VIRAL ANTIGEN VISIBILITY AND PROMOTE IMMUNE-MEDIATED CLEARANCE. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A MECHANISTICALLY GROUNDED THERAPEUTIC VACCINE PLATFORM AND IDENTIFY A PRECLINICAL NTV CANDIDATE SUITABLE FOR ADVANCEMENT INTO NON-HUMAN PRIMATE TESTING. THESE STUDIES ADDRESS KEY OBSTACLES IN THERAPEUTIC HIV VACCINE DEVELOPMENT AND MAY ULTIMATELY REDUCE THE NEED FOR LIFELONG ART.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADVANCING PREP ACCESS FOR WOMEN IN GEORGIA - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE HIV INCIDENCE RATE IN GEORGIA IS 26.0 PER 100,000, BUT DESPITE THIS HIGH RATE, PRE-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS (PREP) UPTAKE IS STILL LOW, ESPECIALLY AMONG WOMEN. RESEARCH INDICATES THAT MOST WOMEN PERCEIVE PREP AS INAPPROPRIATE FOR THEM BECAUSE OF UBIQUITOUS PREP MESSAGING FEATURING MEN. HOWEVER, ONCE WOMEN ARE EDUCATED ABOUT PREP, THEY ARE OPEN TO TAKING ORAL AND INJECTABLE PREP, PREFER TO RECEIVE IT FROM THEIR USUAL CARE PROVIDERS, AND VALUE THEIR PROVIDERS’ PREP RECOMMENDATION. INCREASING PREP AWARENESS AMONG WOMEN MAY NOT BE SUFFICIENT FOR PREP UPTAKE BECAUSE OF BARRIERS TO ACCESS, INCLUDING LACK OF PROVIDER KNOWLEDGE OR CONFIDENCE TO PRESCRIBE PREP. INDEED, MOST PROVIDERS IN THE SOUTH DO NOT PRESCRIBE PREP. THEREFORE, IT IS IMPORTANT TO ADDRESS BOTH WOMEN’S PERCEPTION AND KNOWLEDGE RELATED TO PREP AND PROVIDERS’ ABILITY TO PROVIDE PREP. THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL EVALUATE A MULTILEVEL APPROACH TO ADDRESS PREP BARRIERS. TWO STRATEGIES TO SUPPORT WOMEN AND PROVIDERS IN PREP DECISION-MAKING AND TO INCREASE ACCESS AND UPTAKE HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED AND PILOTED WITH WOMEN AND THE PROVIDERS WHO SERVE THEM. THE PREP TRAINING IS DESIGNED TO HELP PROVIDERS PRESENT PREP AS AN HIV PREVENTION OPTION TO WOMEN AND PROVIDE WOMEN- CENTERED PREP CARE. THE SAVVYHER MOBILE APPLICATION IS DESIGNED TO HELP WOMEN MAKE DECISIONS ABOUT USING PREP. RTI INTERNATIONAL, EMORY UNIVERSITY, MOREHOUSE SCHOOL OF MEDICINE, SISTERLOVE, INC., AND OUR COMMUNITY COLLABORATIVE BOARD (CCB) HAVE DESIGNED THE PROPOSED STUDY AND SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1: COMPARE THE COMBINED EFFICACY THE PREP TRAINING AND THE SAVVYHER APP ON PROVIDER PREP ADOPTION (I.E., THE WEEKLY NUMBER OF PREP-ELIGIBLE WOMEN WHO ARE OFFERED PREP) BY THE 3- AND 6-MONTH FOLLOW-UPS AND MAINTENANCE BY THE 9-MONTH FOLLOW-UP RELATIVE TO THE EFFECTS OF THE TRAINING-ONLY AND APP-ONLY ARMS. AIM 2: ASSESS THE COMBINED EFFICACY OF THESE STRATEGIES ON PATIENTS’ PERCEIVED APPROPRIATENESS OF PREP AND PREP REACH (I.E., PROPORTION OF PARTICIPANTS WHO INITIATE PREP) BY THE 3- AND 6-MONTH FOLLOW-UPS AND PERSISTENCE (I.E., REFILLS/INJECTIONS) BY THE 9-MONTH FOLLOW-UP COMPARED WITH THE TRAINING-ONLY AND APP-ONLY ARMS. AIM 3: EXPLORE THE FACILITATORS AND BARRIERS TO PREP PROVISION, UPTAKE, AND USE OF THE STRATEGIES AMONG PROVIDERS AND PATIENTS VIA JOURNEY MAPPING INTERVIEWS. IF EFFICACIOUS, THESE INTERVENTIONS CAN BE SCALED UP TO HAVE AN IMMENSE PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT, HELPING TO REDUCE HIV AMONG WOMEN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: VIRUS-DRIVEN HUMAN GENE MISREGULATION IN DISEASE - THOUSANDS OF GENETIC VARIANTS HAVE BEEN ESTABLISHED FOR HUNDREDS OF HUMAN DISEASES. LIKEWISE, ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, INCLUDING VIRUS INFECTION, PLAY ESTABLISHED, POTENT ROLES IN DISEASE. YET, THE VAST MAJORITY OF HUMAN DISEASES REMAIN IDIOPATHIC. FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS-BASED APPROACHES FROM OUR GROUP AND OTHERS ARE REVEALING THAT CHANGES IN HUMAN CHROMATIN STATE AND GENE EXPRESSION ARE IMPORTANT MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH GENETIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS INFLUENCE HUMAN DISEASE RISK. IN PARTICULAR, PIONEERING STUDIES OF THE EPSTEIN-BARR VIRUS (EBV), WHICH PLAYS AN ESTABLISHED CAUSATIVE ROLE IN MONONUCLEOSIS, BURKITT'S LYMPHOMA, HODGKIN LYMPHOMA, AND MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS, HAVE LED TO VALUABLE INSIGHTS INTO HOW VIRUS-ENCODED TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATORS (VTRS) INTERACT WITH THE HUMAN GENOME TO MODIFY HUMAN GENE EXPRESSION. MORE RECENTLY, FUNCTIONAL GENOMIC CHARACTERIZATION OF THE IMPACT OF DIVERSE VIRUSES ON HUMAN GENE REGULATION BY OUR GROUP AND OTHERS HAS REVEALED MANY ADDITIONAL IMPACTED HOST MECHANISMS, MANY WITH DISEASE-RELEVANT CONSEQUENCES. MOUNTING EVIDENCE SUPPORTS THE HYPOTHESIS THAT RISK ALLELE-DEPENDENT BINDING OF VIRAL TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATORS CONTRIBUTES SUBSTANTIALLY TO VIRUS-INDUCED CHRONIC DISEASES. HOWEVER, THE DATA REQUIRED TO SYSTEMATICALLY DISCOVER THESE MECHANISMS ARE CURRENTLY FAR FROM COMPLETE. IN THIS RENEWAL, WE PROPOSE A SERIES OF GENOME-SCALE EXPERIMENTS AND COMPUTATIONAL METHODOLOGIES AIMED AT THE COMPREHENSIVE DISCOVERY OF VIRUS- INDUCED HUMAN GENE REGULATORY MECHANISMS THAT LEAD TO DISEASE. IN OUR PREVIOUS ROUND OF FUNDING, WE BUILT A STRONG FOUNDATION REVEALING THE FUNCTIONAL IMPACT OF INTRODUCING EACH INDIVIDUAL VTR INTO HUMAN CELLS ON A WHOLE GENOME SCALE, FOR EACH OF THE SEVEN MAJOR HERPESVIRUS AND FOUR DISEASE-RELEVANT STRAINS OF HUMAN PAPILLOMA VIRUS. HERE, WE BUILD UPON THIS FOUNDATION BY EXAMINING THESE MECHANISMS IN THE CONTEXT OF FULL VIRUS INFECTION. USING THESE DATA, WE WILL DISCOVER NEW ALLELE- AND VIRUS-DEPENDENT MECHANISMS AND BUILD AN UNPRECEDENTED, FREELY AVAILABLE RESOURCE FOR STUDYING THE IMPACT OF VIRAL INFECTION ON HUMAN GENE REGULATION AND HUMAN DISEASES. THESE AMBITIOUS GOALS WILL BE ACHIEVED THROUGH THE FOLLOWING AIMS: AIM 1. CREATE GENOME-WIDE MAPS OF THE VIRUS-ALTERED PRIMARY HUMAN CELL EPIGENETIC LANDSCAPE. AIM 2. GLOBALLY DISCOVER VTR GENE TARGETS AND IMPACTED CELLULAR PHENOTYPES IN PRIMARY HUMAN CELLS. AIM 3. CREATE A UNIQUE WEB RESOURCE ENABLING THE DISCOVERY OF VTR IMPACTS ON HUMAN DISEASES. WE ANTICIPATE THAT THIS WORK WILL LEAD TO THE DISCOVERY OF MULTIPLE CAUSAL HUMAN DISEASE VARIANTS WHOSE MECHANISMS ACT IN A VTR AND ALLELE-DEPENDENT MANNER, LEADING TO UNDERSTANDING OF DISEASE MECHANISMS AND NEW THERAPEUTIC OPPORTUNITIES. OUR APPROACH PROVIDES A GENERALIZABLE BLUEPRINT FOR THE GLOBAL CHARACTERIZATION OF PATHOGENIC EFFECTS ON HOST GENE REGULATION IN VIRTUALLY ANY CONTEXT, PAVING THE WAY FOR FUTURE EFFORTS AIMED AT UNDERSTANDING GENE X ENVIRONMENT INTERACTIONS IN THE CONTEXT OF HUMAN DISEASES.

description: THE ROLE OF DYNAMIC JOINT STABILITY IN GENERALIZED JOINT HYPERMOBILITY: ACOMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS OF BIOMECHANICAL CONTRIBUTIONS TO CHRONIC PAIN - PROJECT SUMMARY HYPERMOBILE EHLERS-DANLOS SYNDROME (HEDS) AND HYPERMOBILITY SPECTRUM DISORDER (HSD) ARE UNDERRECOGNIZED CONNECTIVE TISSUE DISORDERS CHARACTERIZED BY GENERALIZED JOINT HYPERMOBILITY (GJH) AND CHRONIC MUSCULOSKELETAL PAIN. CLINICAL MANAGEMENT REMAINS CHALLENGING DUE TO A LACK OF MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING AND EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT STRATEGIES. ALTHOUGH GJH AFFECTS UP TO 35% OF WOMEN UNDER AGE 40, ONLY A SUBSET DEVELOPS CHRONIC PAIN, SUGGESTING THAT HYPERMOBILITY ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT TO EXPLAIN SYMPTOM ONSET. INCREASING EVIDENCE IMPLICATES BIOMECHANICAL JOINT INSTABILITY AS A KEY CONTRIBUTOR TO PAIN AND DISABILITY IN HEDS/HSD, YET CERVICAL SPINE INSTABILITY HAS NEVER BEEN DIRECTLY MEASURED IN THIS POPULATION. DYNAMIC JOINT STABILITY IS MAINTAINED BY THE COORDINATED FUNCTION OF THREE INTERDEPENDENT SUBSYSTEMS: PASSIVE (LIGAMENTOUS STRUCTURES), ACTIVE (MUSCULATURE), AND NEURAL (PROPRIOCEPTION AND MOTOR CONTROL). WE PROPOSE THAT JOINT INSTABILITY IN HEDS/HSD ARISES FROM SUBSYSTEM-SPECIFIC IMPAIRMENTS, AND THAT ASYMPTOMATIC INDIVIDUALS WITH GJH MAY MITIGATE SYMPTOMS BY COMPENSATING FOR PASSIVE LAXITY WITH STRONGER ACTIVE AND/OR NEURAL CONTROL. THIS FRAMEWORK IS QUANTIFIED USING A NOVEL METRIC—THE DYNAMIC JOINT STABILITY INDEX (DJSI)—THAT INTEGRATES MEASURES FROM ALL THREE SUBSYSTEMS. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUPPORT THIS HYPOTHESIS, REVEALING ABERRANT CERVICAL SPINE MOTION IN SYMPTOMATIC INDIVIDUALS AND ELEVATED STRENGTH IN ASYMPTOMATIC GJH PARTICIPANTS. THIS STUDY WILL ENROLL 120 BIOLOGICAL FEMALES (AGES 18–39), STRATIFIED INTO SYMPTOMATIC GJH (S-GJH; HEDS/HSD WITH CHRONIC NECK PAIN), ASYMPTOMATIC GJH (A-GJH), AND NON-GJH CONTROLS. PARTICIPANTS WILL COMPLETE STANDARDIZED ASSESSMENTS AT BASELINE AND TWO-YEAR FOLLOW-UP. AIM 1 WILL CHARACTERIZE GROUP DIFFERENCES AND LONGITUDINAL CHANGES IN DJSI SUBSYSTEM PERFORMANCE AND CLINICAL OUTCOMES. AIM 2 WILL DIRECTLY ASSESS CERVICAL SEGMENTAL INSTABILITY USING BIPLANE VIDEORADIOGRAPHY AND EVALUATE ITS RELATIONSHIP WITH DJSI AND TISSUE HEALTH VIA QUANTITATIVE MRI. AIM 3 WILL USE MULTIVARIABLE MODELING TO IDENTIFY PREDICTORS OF INSTABILITY, PAIN, AND DISABILITY, INTEGRATING BIOMECHANICAL, IMAGING, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL DATA. FINDINGS WILL DEFINE BIOMECHANICAL PHENOTYPES ACROSS THE GJH SPECTRUM AND IDENTIFY MECHANISM-INFORMED TARGETS FOR FUTURE INTERVENTIONS. THIS WORK ADDRESSES A CRITICAL GAP IN THE CARE OF INDIVIDUALS WITH HEDS/HSD AND HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF HYPERMOBILITY-RELATED NECK PAIN.

description: INVESTIGATING A BASOPHIL-FIBROBLAST PRO-INFLAMMATORY AXIS IN ATOPIC DERMATITIS - PROJECT SUMMARY ATOPIC DERMATITIS (AD) IS A HIGHLY PREVALENT INFLAMMATORY SKIN DISEASE THAT CAUSES RELAPSING ITCHY SKIN RASHES AND SUBSTANTIAL MORBIDITY. OUR INCOMPLETE UNDERSTANDING OF THE PATHOGENESIS OF AD, INCLUDING HOW CELL-CELL INTERACTIONS CONTRIBUTE TO ONGOING INFLAMMATION, HINDERS THERAPEUTIC SUCCESS. THROUGH SINGLE-CELL AND SPATIAL PROFILING, WE HAVE UNCOVERED A FEED-FORWARD BASOPHIL-FIBROBLAST CROSSTALK AXIS THAT CONTRIBUTES TO WORSENING INFLAMMATION IN COMMON MOUSE MODELS OF INDUCIBLE AD-LIKE INFLAMMATION, MC903 AND OXAZOLONE. MOREOVER, THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROFILES OF PRO-INFLAMMATORY FIBROBLASTS FROM THESE MODELS RESEMBLE THOSE OF HUMAN FIBROBLASTS ISOLATED FROM HUMAN AD TISSUES. OUR DATA PREDICT THAT BASOPHIL-DERIVED OSM, IL-4, AND IL-13 CAN ACTIVATE FIBROBLASTS INTO UPREGULATING CHEMOKINES PREDICTED TO DRIVE IMMUNE RECRUITMENT. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE WILL EXAMINE (1) WHETHER BASOPHILS AND BASOPHIL-DERIVED IL-4/13 AND OSM ARE REQUIRED FOR FIBROBLAST ACTIVATION DURING AD-LIKE INFLAMMATION, AND (2) HOW FIBROBLASTS CONTRIBUTE TO IMMUNE CELL RECRUITMENT AND WORSENING INFLAMMATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT A BASOPHIL-FIBROBLAST CROSSTALK AXIS AUGMENTS INFLAMMATION IN AD. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS THROUGH TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 WILL USE GENETIC APPROACHES TO DEPLETE BASOPHILS AND DISRUPT BASOPHIL-DERIVED IL-4/13 DURING AD-LIKE INFLAMMATION IN MICE AND DETERMINE WHETHER OVERALL INFLAMMATION IS REDUCED AND WHETHER FIBROBLASTS EXHIBIT DECREASED PRO-INFLAMMATORY FEATURES IN THESE SETTINGS. WE WILL TEST WHETHER BLOCKING OSM CAN FURTHER DISRUPT INFLAMMATION AND FIBROBLAST ACTIVATION. WE WILL THEN PROFILE HUMAN AD TISSUE TO ASSESS FOR BASOPHIL-FIBROBLAST CO-LOCALIZATION AND INFERRED CROSSTALK USING BOTH CLASSIC IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE APPROACHES AND CUTTING-EDGE SINGLE-CELL RESOLUTION SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMIC PROFILING. AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF PRO-INFLAMMATORY FIBROBLASTS IN IMMUNE CELL RECRUITMENT USING BOTH IN VITRO AND IN VIVO APPROACHES. WE WILL FIRST CHARACTERIZE A MOUSE MODEL IN WHICH WE HAVE DELETED IL4-R, THE RECEPTOR FOR IL-4 AND IL-13 CYTOKINES, SPECIFICALLY IN FIBROBLASTS, WHERE WE OBSERVED DECREASED INFLAMMATION, INCLUDING REDUCTION OF BASOPHILS, DURING INDUCTION OF AD-LIKE INFLAMMATION. USING THIS MODEL, WE WILL ASSESS WHICH CHEMOKINES ARE DOWNSTREAM OF IL-4/13 AND OSM FIBROBLAST SIGNALING AND WHICH IMMUNE CELLS ARE RECRUITED BY FIBROBLASTS. WE WILL THEN CONDUCT IN VITRO STIMULATION OF BOTH MOUSE AND HUMAN FIBROBLASTS WITH IL-4 AND IL-13 TO (1) PERFORM IN VIVO INTRADERMAL INJECTION OF STIMULATED MOUSE FIBROBLASTS AND ASSESS WHETHER THEY ARE SUFFICIENT TO INDUCE IMMUNE RECRUITMENT IN VIVO, AND (2) GENERATE CONDITIONED MEDIA FROM HUMAN FIBROBLASTS TO TEST WHETHER THEY CAN INDUCE HUMAN IMMUNE CELL MIGRATION IN VITRO. WE WILL THEN TEST WHETHER BLOCKING THE SPECIFIC CHEMOKINES CXCL1 AND CXCL12, ALONE OR IN COMBINATION, CAN BLOCK MIGRATORY EFFECTS OF HUMAN FIBROBLAST CONDITIONED MEDIA TO TEST THEIR FUNCTIONAL ROLES IN HUMAN IMMUNE CELL MIGRATION. THIS NEW KNOWLEDGE OF MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF AN IMMUNE-STROMAL CROSSTALK AXIS WILL ESTABLISH AID DESIGN OF NOVEL STROMA-TARGETING THERAPIES FOR AD.

description: NUTRIENT SENSING AND CELL FATE DETERMINATION THROUGH STRUCTURAL ALLOSTERY IN PASK - PROJECT SUMMARY NUTRIENT SENSING IS FUNDAMENTAL TO LINKING ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS WITH CELLULAR ENERGY BALANCE AND FATE DECISIONS—PROCESSES THAT ARE CENTRAL TO HUMAN HEALTH AND, WHEN DEREGULATED, CONTRIBUTE TO DISEASES SUCH AS CANCER, DIABETES, TISSUE DEGENERATION, AND AGING. NUTRIENT-SENSITIVE KINASES SUCH AS MTOR, GCN2, AMPK, AND PASK PLAY PIVOTAL ROLES IN MAINTAINING CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS BY DYNAMICALLY RESPONDING TO ENVIRONMENTAL CUES. AMONG THESE, THE PER-ARNT-SIM (PAS) DOMAIN KINASE (PASK) IS PARTICULARLY NOTABLE DUE TO ITS UNIQUE MONOMERIC ARCHITECTURE. IT COMBINES METABOLITE-SENSING PAS DOMAINS WITH A SERINE/THREONINE KINASE DOMAIN, ENABLING IT TO DIRECTLY INTERPRET METABOLIC AND NUTRIENT SIGNALS. THIS STREAMLINED DESIGN ALLOWS PASK TO TRANSLATE ENVIRONMENTAL INPUTS INTO PRECISE CELLULAR RESPONSES THAT REGULATE METABOLISM, GROWTH, AND DIFFERENTIATION. DESPITE ITS CRITICAL ROLE, THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH PAS DOMAINS DETECT ENVIRONMENTAL CUES AND TRANSMIT THIS INFORMATION TO THE KINASE DOMAIN REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THROUGH STRUCTURAL PHYLOGENETIC ANALYSIS, WE RECENTLY REVISED THE DOMAIN ARCHITECTURE OF PASK. IN ADDITION TO THE PREVIOUSLY KNOWN PAS-A DOMAIN, WE IDENTIFIED TWO ADDITIONAL PAS DOMAINS—PAS-B AND PAS-C—WITHIN ITS PRIMARY SEQUENCE. NOTABLY, THE PAS-C DOMAIN COMPRISES TWO SUBDOMAINS: THE PAS-FOLD AND THE PAC-MOTIF, SEPARATED BY A LONG, UNSTRUCTURED REGULATORY LOOP—AN ARCHITECTURE THAT IS CONSERVED ACROSS METAZOANS. THIS LOOP SERVES AS A TARGET FOR NUTRIENT SIGNALS, DRIVING THE DYNAMIC ASSEMBLY OF THE PAS-C DOMAIN. THIS ASSEMBLY, IN TURN, ORGANIZES PASK’S QUATERNARY STRUCTURE AND ACTIVATES ITS CATALYTIC FUNCTION, REVEALING A NOVEL MECHANISM OF ENVIRONMENTAL SENSING THROUGH STRUCTURAL ALLOSTERY. BUILDING ON THIS DISCOVERY, WE AIM TO EXPLORE HOW THE PAS DOMAINS COORDINATE WITH THE KINASE DOMAIN TO REGULATE PASK’S ACTIVITY, STABILITY, AND SUBSTRATE SPECIFICITY. IN AIM 1, WE WILL MAP INTER- AND INTRA-DOMAIN AMINO ACID CONTACT SITES ACROSS THE PASK QUATERNARY STRUCTURE AND EXAMINE HOW THESE ARE REMODELED IN RESPONSE TO SIGNALING CUES AND ARE EXPLOITED BY DISEASE-CAUSING VARIANTS TO LOCK PASK IN A CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVE OR INACTIVE STATE. IN AIM 2, WE WILL INVESTIGATE A METABOLICALLY REGULATED ACETYLATION-UBIQUITYLATION SWITCH THAT TARGETS THE PAS DOMAIN AND CONTROLS PASK STABILITY DURING THE STEM CELL CYCLE, INFLUENCING THE BALANCE BETWEEN SELF-RENEWAL AND DIFFERENTIATION. IN AIM 3, WE WILL CHARACTERIZE HOW NUTRIENT SIGNALS FLOW THROUGH THE PAS DOMAINS TO PHOSPHORYLATE NEWLY IDENTIFIED PASK-INTERACTING PARTNERS AND SUBSTRATES IN MAMMALIAN STEM CELLS. BY INTEGRATING STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY, BIOCHEMISTRY, AND STEM CELL BIOLOGY, THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEFINE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS BY WHICH PASK REGULATES CELL BEHAVIOR AND METABOLIC PROCESSES. THESE INSIGHTS WILL ILLUMINATE THE PATHOGENESIS OF METABOLIC SYNDROME AND TISSUE DYSFUNCTION OBSERVED IN PASK-DEFICIENT MODELS, POTENTIALLY OPENING NEW AVENUES FOR THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISTIC-BASED THERAPEUTIC TO AMELIORATE CELLULAR SENESCENCE AND REVERSE QUADRICEPS MUSCLE ATROPHY IN HUMANS FOLLOWING ACL INJURY - PROJECT SUMMARY ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT (ACL) INJURY AND SUBSEQUENT RECONSTRUCTION RESULT IN LOCALIZED INFLAMMATION AND ALTERATIONS WITHIN THE EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX WHICH HAVE BEEN LINKED TO PROTRACTED QUADRICEPS WEAKNESS AND ATROPHY. THERE IS A SIGNIFICANT GAP IN KNOWLEDGE CONCERNING THE SIGNALING CASCADES AND INTERCELLULAR COMMUNICATION AMONG IMMUNE CELLS (E.G., MACROPHAGES), FIBRO-ADIPOGENIC PROGENITORS (FAPS), AND SATELLITE CELLS THAT DIRECTLY REGULATE EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX REMODELING WITHIN THE QUADRICEPS, LIMITING PROGRESS IN THE FIELD TO ADDRESS THE INCEPTIVE EVENTS UNDERLYING POOR FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY. COMPELLING PRELIMINARY DATA IDENTIFY A SUBSET OF IMMUNE CELLS AND FAPS THAT UNDERGO CELLULAR SENESCENCE THAT MAY UNDERLIE A FIBROTIC AND INFLAMMATORY MUSCLE PHENOTYPE THROUGH THE INDUCTION OF SENESCENCE ASSOCIATED SECRETORY PHENOTYPE (SASP) SIGNALING WITHIN THE ACL-INJURY QUADRICEPS. METFORMIN HAS BEEN IMPLICATED TO HAVE POSITIVE EFFECTS ON MUSCLE SIZE AND FUNCTION IN AGED INDIVIDUALS FOLLOWING A PERIOD OF DISUSE BY ENHANCING MACROPHAGE FUNCTION AND AN ATTENUATED CELLULAR SENESCENT BURDEN BY TARGETING SASP IN A VARIETY OF MUSCLE INTERSTITIAL CELL TYPES. WHETHER METFORMIN IS CAPABLE OF MODULATING EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX REMODELING AND IMMUNE CELL PROFILE FOLLOWING ACUTE LIGAMENT INJURY AND RECONSTRUCTION IS UNKNOWN. THE OVERARCHING OBJECTIVE OF THE CURRENT PROPOSAL IS TO DEFINE CELLULAR SENESCENCE AS A MODIFIABLE TARGET TO IMPROVE QUADRICEPS HEALTH AND FUNCTION IN PATIENTS FOLLOWING ACL RECONSTRUCTION. IN THIS RANDOMIZED, DOUBLE BLIND, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED CLINICAL TRIAL, THE HYPOTHESIS IS THAT TREATMENT WITH METFORMIN (VS PLACEBO) WILL MITIGATE QUADRICEPS CELLULAR SENESCENCE AND THIS WILL ENHANCE ECM REMODELING, MUSCLE STRENGTH AND SIZE FOLLOWING ACL RECONSTRUCTION. TWO INTERCONNECTED BUT INDEPENDENT AIMS WILL ADDRESS THE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS AND PROVIDE CRITICAL MECHANISTIC INSIGHT INTO THE ETIOLOGY OF MUSCLE CELLULAR SENESCENCE FOLLOWING INJURY. SPECIFICALLY, INNOVATIVE IMAGING AND SINGE CELL ANALYSES WILL REVEAL THE IMPACT OF METFORMIN TREATMENT ON MACROPHAGE AND FAP CELLULAR SENESCENCE AND SASP, COLLAGEN ORGANIZATION, AND MUSCLE RECOVERY FOLLOWING ACL RECONSTRUCTION. RESULTS FROM THIS WORK WILL DIRECTLY SUPPORT THE REPURPOSING OF METFORMIN TO ACCELERATE FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY IN PATIENTS WHO HAVE SUSTAINED ACL INJURIES.

description: THIN-FILAMENT LENGTH REGULATION IN MUSCLE SARCOMERES: MECHANISMS AND DISEASE - SUMMARY ACTIN AND MYOSIN POLYMERS FORM THE THIN AND THICK FILAMENTS OF MUSCLE SARCOMERES, WHICH INTERACT AND SLIDE PAST ONE ANOTHER DURING MUSCLE CONTRACTION. THE THIN-FILAMENT LENGTH (TFL) DETERMINES THE OVERLAP WITH THE THICK FILAMENT, WHICH IN TURN DEFINES THE NUMBER OF INTERACTING MYOSIN HEADS AND THE FORCE OUTPUT. DYSREGULATION OF TFL CONTRIBUTES TO SKELETAL AND CARDIAC MUSCLE DISEASES, INCLUDING NEMALINE MYOPATHY (NM) AND DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY (DCM). THIS GRANT AIMS TO ELUCIDATE THE STRUCTURAL-FUNCTIONAL MECHANISMS THAT REGULATE TFL AND ITS DYSREGULATION IN MUSCLE DISEASES. TFL IS REGULATED BY PROTEINS CONTROLLING SUBUNIT ADDITION AND DISSOCIATION AT THE POINTED AND BARBED ENDS OF THIN FILAMENTS (TFS). KEY REGULATORY PROTEINS INCLUDE: (A) NEBULIN, WHICH SPANS THE LENGTH OF TFS AND ACTS AS A GENERAL RULER OF TFL; (B) CAPZ, A BARBED-END CAPPER; (C) TROPOMODULIN (TMOD), A POINTED-END CAPPER; (D) LEIOMODIN (LMOD), A POINTED-END ELONGATOR; (E) TROPOMYOSIN (TPM), WHICH INTERACTS WITH BOTH TMOD AND LMOD TO MODULATE THEIR ACTIVITIES; AND (F) SH3BGR, A NOVEL REGULATOR THAT WE HAVE IDENTIFIED BASED ON BIOCHEMICAL AND STRUCTURAL EVIDENCE. GIVEN THE IMPORTANCE OF THE ENDS IN TFL REGULATION, WE AIM TO DETERMINE HIGH-RESOLUTION CRYO-EM STRUCTURES OF THE POINTED AND BARBED ENDS UNDER VARIOUS CONDITIONS AND USING TWO PARALLEL STRATEGIES: RECONSTITUTING THE ENDS FROM RECOMBINANT PROTEINS AND STUDYING NATIVE TFS PURIFIED FROM DIFFERENT MUSCLE TYPES (FAST AND SLOW). ALL THE SPECIMENS AND SOME PRELIMINARY STRUCTURES AND BIOCHEMICAL DATA HAVE BEEN OBTAINED. OUR LAB IS ALSO IDEALLY POSITIONED FOR THIS WORK, HAVING RECENTLY SOLVED THE FIRST CRYO-EM STRUCTURES OF ACTIN FILAMENT ENDS. THE STRUCTURAL WORK WILL BE SUPPORTED AND COMPLEMENTED BY BIOCHEMICAL AND CELLULAR ANALYSES, AND THE STUDY OF DISEASE-CAUSING MUTATIONS IN THESE PROTEINS. OUR AIMS ARE: (1) DETERMINE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH TMOD, LMOD, AND TPM CONTROL TFL AT THE POINTED END BY STUDYING TMOD, LMOD, AND THEIR INTERACTIONS WITH TPM, ALONG WITH A POTENTIAL INTERACTION OF TMOD WITH NEBULIN; (2) TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT SH3BGR IS A NOVEL TFL REGULATOR AT THE POINTED END USING BIOCHEMICAL, STRUCTURAL, LOCALIZATION, AND FUNCTIONAL STUDIES IN MUSCLE; (3) DETERMINE THE MECHANISMS THAT CONTROL TFL AT THE BARBED END BY ELUCIDATING HOW CAPZ AND NEBULIN INTERACT. WE EXTEND THESE STUDIES TO THE CARDIAC-SPECIFIC HOMOLOG OF NEBULIN, I.E., NEBULETTE. OUR PUBLISHED WORK AND EXTENSIVE PRELIMINARY DATA DESCRIBED IN THE APPLICATION SUPPORT THE LIKELY SUCCESS OF THE AIMS. 1

description: MECHANISMS OF SYSTEMIC BONE LOSS FOLLOWING FRACTURE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT OSTEOPOROSIS AND LOW BONE MASS AFFECT OVER 50 MILLION AMERICANS, AND OSTEOPOROSIS-RELATED FRACTURES ACCOUNT FOR OVER THREE MILLION BROKEN BONES AND $25 BILLION IN RELATED COSTS ANNUALLY IN THE US. IDENTIFYING THE UNDERLYING CAUSES OF BONE LOSS IS THEREFORE OF UTMOST IMPORTANCE FOR IMPROVING THE SKELETAL HEALTH OF A RAPIDLY AGING POPULATION. ONE UNDERAPPRECIATED MECHANISM OF BONE LOSS IS THAT FRACTURE INITIATES POST-TRAUMATIC BONE LOSS THROUGHOUT THE SKELETON, WHICH INCREASES FUTURE FRACTURE RISK AT ALL SKELETAL SITES. INJURY-INDUCED INFLAMMATION FOLLOWING FRACTURE IS A LIKELY CONTRIBUTOR TO POST-TRAUMATIC SYSTEMIC BONE LOSS. HOWEVER, MULTIPLE OTHER UNIDENTIFIED BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES MAY ALSO CONTRIBUTE TO SYSTEMIC BONE LOSS FOLLOWING FRACTURE. THEREFORE, IT IS NECESSARY TO DEVELOP A MORE HOLISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF PHYSIOLOGICAL PROCESSES INITIATED BY INJURY AND THEIR EFFECTS ON THE SKELETAL SYSTEM. THE PARENT R01 IS AN ONGOING LONGITUDINAL STUDY THAT USES CLINICAL AND CUTTING-EDGE HIGH- RESOLUTION IMAGING TO CHARACTERIZE THE TIME COURSE AND MAGNITUDE OF SYSTEMIC BONE LOSS AND RECOVERY FOLLOWING HUMERUS FRACTURE. FOR THIS ANCILLARY STUDY, WE PROPOSE TO COLLECT ADDITIONAL BLOOD FROM FRACTURE PATIENTS AT MULTIPLE TIME POINTS POST-INJURY TO PERFORM AN EXTENSIVE UNBIASED MULTIMODAL ANALYSIS OF CIRCULATING CELLS AND FACTORS UTILIZING GENOMIC, PROTEOMIC, AND METABOLOMIC PROFILING TECHNIQUES. WE WILL FIRST PERFORM: 1) SINGLE-CELL RNASEQ OF CIRCULATING LEUKOCYTES AND OSTEOCLAST PRECURSORS TO DETERMINE GENE EXPRESSION AT THE LEVEL OF INDIVIDUAL CELLS, 2) PROTEOMIC ANALYSIS OF SERUM SAMPLES TO DETERMINE WHOLE-TISSUE PROTEIN EXPRESSION, AND 3) METABOLOMIC ANALYSIS OF SERUM SAMPLES TO DETERMINE SMALL MOLECULES (METABOLITES) PRESENT IN BLOOD AT VARIOUS TIME POINTS FOLLOWING FRACTURE. NEXT, WE WILL USE MULTIMODAL PREDICTIVE MODELING TO IDENTIFY KEY BIOMARKERS AND MECHANISMS DRIVING POST-FRACTURE SYSTEMIC BONE LOSS, WHICH WILL ALLOW US TO IDENTIFY NOVEL PROCESSES AND DEVELOP A HOLISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE INJURY RESPONSE AND INDIVIDUAL EFFECTS ON POST-FRACTURE SYSTEMIC BONE LOSS. THESE NOVEL STUDIES WILL BE HIGHLY IMPACTFUL AS THEY WILL: 1) REVEAL THE INFLAMMATORY LANDSCAPE INITIATED BY FRACTURE AND CORRELATE THIS RESPONSE TO THE MAGNITUDE OF POST-TRAUMATIC SYSTEMIC BONE LOSS AND RECOVERY, 2) IDENTIFY NOVEL PATHWAYS INITIATED BY FRACTURE THAT MAY CONTRIBUTE TO THE SYSTEMIC BONE LOSS RESPONSE, AND 3) GENERATE NEW BIOMARKERS AND POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR PRESERVING SKELETAL HEALTH IN OLDER PATIENTS FOLLOWING A BONE FRACTURE. THIS MULTIMODAL UNBIASED ANALYSIS OF CIRCULATING CELLS AND FACTORS WILL ADD AN UNPARALLELED LEVEL OF INVESTIGATIVE POWER TO THE PARENT R01 AND WILL ALLOW US TO EXPAND THESE STUDIES TOWARD DEEPER MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING AND GREATER TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REGULATORS OF THE SKIN INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT BACKGROUND: IN THE SKIN, EPIDERMAL KERATINOCYTES WHICH COMPRISE THE VAST MAJORITY OF THE CELLS IN THE EPIDERMIS PROVIDE THE INITIAL RESPONSE TO ENVIRONMENTAL INSULTS SUCH AS TISSUE DAMAGE, BACTERIAL, OR VIRAL INFECTION. THE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE OF KERATINOCYTES MUST BE TIGHTLY REGULATED. EXCESSIVE AND PROLONGED CUTANEOUS INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES CAN CONTRIBUTE TO SKIN DISEASES SUCH AS PSORIASIS. IT IS STILL UNCLEAR THE REGULATORS THAT MEDIATE THE INFLAMMATORY PROCESS OF EPIDERMAL KERATINOCYTES. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE HAVE SHOWN THAT ZNF750 AND ITS ASSOCIATED PROTEINS DAMPEN THE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE IN DIFFERENTIATED KERATINOCYTES AND THAT LOSS OF THESE PROTEINS LEAD TO EXCESSIVE AND PROLONGED INFLAMMATION. OBJECTIVE/HYPOTHESIS: THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS TO UNDERSTAND THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT CONTROL EPIDERMAL KERATINOCYTES’ RESPONSE TO INFLAMMATORY STIMULI. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGESTS THAT ZNF750 AND ITS ASSOCIATED PROTEINS FORM A SILENCING COMPLEX THAT SHUTS DOWN THE UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM MEDIATORS OF THE INFLAMMATORY GENE EXPRESSION PROGRAM TO DAMPEN THE INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE OF DIFFERENTIATED KERATINOCYTES. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO CHARACTERIZE THE ROLE OF THESE FACTORS IN MEDIATING A RESPONSE TO A VARIETY OF INFLAMMATORY STIMULI. WE ALSO PLAN TO DEFINE THE INFLAMMATORY GENES THAT THE ZNF750 COMPLEX DIRECTLY REGULATES AS WELL UNDERSTAND HOW THOSE GENES ARE SILENCED. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT LOSS OF ZNF750 OR ITS ASSOCIATED PROTEINS WILL LEAD TO EXCESSIVE AND PROLONGED INFLAMMATION IN THE SKIN. SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) TO DETERMINE THE ROLE OF ZNF750 AND ITS ASSOCIATED PROTEINS (KDM1A/LSD1, SETDB1, TRIM28/KAP1, AND HNRNPU) IN MEDIATING SKIN INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES AND (2) TO DETERMINE THE GENES BOUND AND SILENCED BY ZNF750 AND ITS COMPLEX THAT ARE NECESSARY FOR MEDIATING SKIN INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES. STUDY DESIGN: TO STUDY HOW ZNF750 AND ITS ASSOCIATED PROTEINS IMPACT THE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE OF THE SKIN, WE PLAN TO USE PRIMARY HUMAN KERATINOCYTES AS WELL AS MICE WITH EPIDERMAL SPECIFIC DELETION OF EACH GENE. THE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE OF THESE CELLS/MICE TO TISSUE DAMAGE, IMIQUIMOD, OR BACTERIAL INFECTION WILL BE DETERMINED. WE WILL USE CHIP-SEQ TO DETERMINE THE GENES BOUND AND REGULATED BY ZNF750, KDM1A/LSD1, SETDB1, TRIM28/KAP1, AND HNRNPU IN RESPONSE TO INFLAMMATORY STIMULI.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISMS OF INTRA-EPITHELIAL MIGRATION IN THE DEVELOPING EPIDERMIS - SUMMARY THE APPROPRIATE DISTRIBUTION OF SPECIALIZED CELL TYPES IS CRITICAL FOR TISSUE HEALTH AND FUNCTION. THE EPIDERMIS IS A STRATIFIED EPITHELIUM CONTAINING SEVERAL SPECIALIZED CELL TYPES—INCLUDING IMMUNE, SENSORY, AND PIGMENT CELLS—THAT MIGRATE BETWEEN EPITHELIAL CELLS TO DISPERSE WIDELY THROUGH THE SKIN. EPIDERMAL BASAL KERATINOCYTES, CHARACTERIZED BY THEIR EXPRESSION OF THE TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR P63, ARE STEM CELLS THAT GIVE RISE TO ALL KERATINOCYTES IN THE STRATIFIED EPITHELIUM, AS WELL AS DISPERSED, SPECIALIZED CELL TYPES. IN MUCOSAL TISSUES, INCLUDING THE CORNEA, LINING OF THE MOUTH, AND MANY INTERNAL ORGANS (INCLUDING GUT, LUNG, KIDNEY, INNER EAR, PROSTATE, AND BLADDER), SIMILAR P63-EXPRESSING BASAL EPITHELIAL CELLS GIVE RISE TO SPECIALIZED MUCUS-SECRETING CELLS (MCS) AND ION-TRANSPORTING CELLS (IONOCYTES, ICS), WHICH DISTRIBUTE WIDELY THROUGH THESE EPITHELIA. TOGETHER, THESE TWO CELL TYPES ARE CRITICAL FOR TISSUE HEALTH AND FUNCTION. DESPITE THEIR IMPORTANCE IN TISSUE HOMEOSTASIS AND DISEASE, HOW SPECIALIZED CELL TYPES ARISING FROM BASAL EPITHELIAL CELLS TRANSIT FROM ONE EPITHELIAL LAYER TO ANOTHER AND ACHIEVE THEIR BROAD DISTRIBUTION IS NOT KNOWN IN ANY ORGAN. THIS STUDY PROPOSES TO USE THE ZEBRAFISH EPIDERMIS TO CHARACTERIZE HOW BASAL CELL-DERIVED SPECIALIZED CELL TYPES DISPERSE THROUGH THE EPIDERMIS. LIVE IMAGING OF DEVELOPING ZEBRAFISH REVEALED THAT MC/IC PRECURSORS ARISE FROM BASAL EPIDERMAL CELLS IN THE VENTRAL PART OF THE EMBRYO, MIGRATE AWAY FROM THEIR ORIGIN WITHIN THE INTRA-EPITHELIAL SPACE, INTEGRATE INTO THE SUPERFICIAL EPITHELIUM, AND DIFFERENTIATE INTO MCS OR ICS. THE MIGRATION OF THESE PRECURSORS HAS NOT PREVIOUSLY BEEN REPORTED, BUT IS LIKELY TO SERVE AS A MECHANISM FOR DISPERSAL. MUCH IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW CELLS MIGRATE THROUGH ECM-RICH ENVIRONMENTS USING FOCAL ADHESIONS, BUT RELATIVELY LESS IS UNDERSTOOD ABOUT HOW THEY MOVE THROUGH ECM-POOR EPITHELIA, SUCH AS THE EPIDERMIS. OUR UNDERSTANDING OF MIGRATORY MECHANISMS HAS BEEN FURTHER ENRICHED IN RECENT YEARS BY THE DISCOVERY THAT MECHANICAL FEATURES OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND SELF-ORGANIZING CELL INTERACTIONS INFLUENCE CELL MIGRATION. THIS PROPOSAL INVESTIGATES THE INTRINSIC MOTILITY MECHANISMS AND EXTRINSIC MOLECULAR AND MECHANICAL CUES THAT THESE CELLS USE TO DISPERSE THROUGH THE EPIDERMIS. AIM 1 CHARACTERIZES HOW THESE CELLS MOVE BY EXAMINING KNOWN MOTILITY MECHANISMS AND IDENTIFYING NEW GENES REQUIRED FOR THEIR MOTILITY USING TRANSCRIPTOMICS AND A FOCUSED GENETIC SCREEN; AIM 2 TESTS THE HYPOTHESIS THAT FEATURES OF SURROUNDING EPITHELIAL CELLS—NUCLEAR STIFFNESS AND ADHESION—INFLUENCE MIGRATORY PATHS; AND AIM 3 TESTS IF CONTACT WITH SENSORY AXONS GROWING IN THE SAME INTER-EPITHELIAL SPACE REPOLARIZES MIGRATORY MC/IC PRECURSORS TO PROMOTE THEIR DISPERSAL. GIVEN THEIR SHARED MOLECULAR PROPERTIES, ORIGINS, AND DISTRIBUTION PATTERNS, THESE STUDIES ARE LIKELY TO EXPLAIN HOW SPECIALIZED CELL TYPES ARE DISTRIBUTED NOT ONLY IN THE SKIN BUT ALSO IN MANY OTHER EPITHELIAL ORGANS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SCH: DIGITAL TWIN SYSTEMS FOR PERSONALIZED PREDICTION OF OSTEOPOROTIC SPINE - PROJECT SUMMARY (SEE INSTRUCTIONS): OSTEOPOROSIS WEAKENS VERTEBRAL BONE BY REDUCING BONE MASS, DETERIORATING TRABECULAR MICROSTRUCTURE, AND ALTERING SPATIAL STIFFNESS DISTRIBUTIONS, INCREASING THE RISK OF VERTEBRAL FRACTURES THAT CAUSE PAIN, DEFORMITY, DISABILITY, LOSS OF INDEPENDENCE, AND MORTALITY IN OLDER ADULTS. CURRENT CLINICAL TOOLS ESTIMATE POPULATION-LEVEL FRACTURE PROBABILITY, BUT THEY DO NOT PREDICT HOW PATIENT-SPECIFIC VERTEBRAL GEOMETRY, TRABECULAR DETERIORATION, HETEROGENEOUS STIFFNESS, AND DAILY ACTIVITY LOADING COMBINE TO CREATE LOCALIZED STRAINS THAT PRECEDE FRACTURE. THE LONG-TERM OBJECTIVE IS TO ADVANCE PREDICTIVE AND MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF OSTEOPOROTIC VERTEBRAL FRACTURE AND TRANSLATE THIS KNOWLEDGE INTO A PATIENT-SPECIFIC, PHYSICS-INFORMED DIGITAL TWIN FRAMEWORK FOR FRACTURE PREDICTION, PREVENTION, AND SPINE TREATMENT PLANNING. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT CT-DERIVED BONE MICROSTRUCTURE AND PATIENT COVARIATES, CONSTRAINED BY ELASTICITY AND FRACTURE PHYSICS AND GROUNDED IN CADAVERIC DEFORMATION DATA, CAN SUPPORT RELIABLE ESTIMATION OF HETEROGENEOUS VERTEBRAL STIFFNESS AND ACCURATE PREDICTION OF LOCALIZED, ACTIVITY-DEPENDENT FRACTURE RISK WITH QUANTIFIED UNCERTAINTY. THE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE TO (1) INFER THREE-DIMENSIONAL, SPATIALLY VARYING VERTEBRAL ELASTICITY AND FRACTURE-RELATED DESCRIPTORS FROM CADAVERIC CT IMAGES AND DIGITAL VOLUME CORRELATION DISPLACEMENT FIELDS; (2) DEVELOP PERSONALIZED BAYESIAN INFERENCE METHODS THAT LINK CT-DERIVED BONE MICROARCHITECTURE AND CLINICAL COVARIATES TO PATIENT-SPECIFIC VERTEBRAL MATERIAL PROPERTIES WITH UNCERTAINTY; (3) BUILD A SCALABLE VERTEBRAL DIGITAL TWIN THAT PREDICTS LOCALIZED STRAIN AND FRACTURE-RISK PATTERNS FROM PATIENT-SPECIFIC BONE-PROPERTY MAPS; AND (4) EXTEND THE FRAMEWORK TO WHOLE-SPINE, ACTIVITY-SPECIFIC PREDICTION BY LINKING MOTION-DERIVED VERTEBRAL LOADING DURING DAILY ACTIVITIES TO VERTEBRA-LEVEL STRAIN AND FRACTURE PROBABILITY. THE RESEARCH DESIGN INTEGRATES CADAVERIC VERTEBRAL TESTING, CT IMAGING, DIGITAL VOLUME CORRELATION, FINITE ELEMENT MODELING, MUSCULOSKELETAL LOAD ESTIMATION, BAYESIAN PHYSICS-INFORMED MACHINE LEARNING, AND BLINDED CLINICAL REVIEW. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE VALIDATED METHODS FOR ESTIMATING PATIENT-SPECIFIC VERTEBRAL MATERIAL PROPERTIES, UNCERTAINTY-AWARE FRACTURE-RISK MAPS, AND ACTIVITY-SPECIFIC RISK PREDICTIONS. BY USING THESE PREDICTIONS TO IDENTIFY WHY, WHERE, AND UNDER WHAT LOADING CONDITIONS OSTEOPOROTIC VERTEBRAE BECOME MECHANICALLY VULNERABLE , THIS PROJECT WILL GENERATE NEW BIOMECHANICAL KNOWLEDGE OF VERTEBRAL FRAGILITY AND DIRECTLY ADVANCE THE NIAMS MISSION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EFFECTS OF A MOBILE APP-BASED MINDFULNESS INTERVENTION IN PERSONS WITH SPINAL CORD INJURY AND CHRONIC PAIN: A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL - PROJECT SUMMARY: THE PREVALENCE OF DEBILITATING CHRONIC PAIN IN PEOPLE WITH SPINAL CORD INJURY (PWSCI) RANGES FROM 65-85%. CHRONIC PAIN AFTER SCI CONTRIBUTES TO DEPRESSION AND ANXIETY, LIMITS PARTICIPATION IN ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING, AND DIMINISHES HEALTH-RELATED QUALITY OF LIFE (QOL). PHARMACOLOGICAL AGENTS, SUCH AS OPIOIDS, ARE THE PRIMARY THERAPEUTIC OPTIONS TO MANAGE CHRONIC PAIN AFTER SCI, BUT THEY ARE INEFFECTIVE IN RELIEVING PAIN AND ARE ASSOCIATED WITH SIGNIFICANT SIDE EFFECTS.1-5 MINDFULNESS MEDITATION (MM) TRAINING HAS BEEN SHOWN TO IMPROVE MENTAL AND PHYSICAL SYMPTOMS, INCLUDING PAIN, IN MANY STUDIES OF PEOPLE WITHOUT SCI WHO HAVE CHRONIC PAIN. HOWEVER, THESE INTERVENTIONS ARE TYPICALLY LENGTHY, EXPENSIVE, AND REQUIRE IN-PERSON VISITS WITH A THERAPIST, MAKING THEM INACCESSIBLE TO MANY PWSCI. MOUNTING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT MOBILE APPS MAY PROVIDE AN EFFECTIVE AND LOW-COST WAY TO PROVIDE MM INTERVENTIONS. ONLY ONE FEASIBILITY STUDY HAS EXPLORED AN APP-BASED MM INTERVENTION IN PWSCI, AND IT WAS CONDUCTED BY THIS RESEARCH TEAM. THE RESULTS OF THIS STUDY SUGGEST THAT THE MOBILE APP-BASED MM INTERVENTION IS FEASIBLE AND ACCEPTABLE TO PWSCI AND SHOWS PROMISE IN IMPROVING PAIN AND MENTAL HEALTH. HOWEVER, RESEARCH POWERED TO EXAMINE THE EFFICACY OF AN EASILY ACCESSIBLE MOBILE APP-BASED MINDFULNESS INTERVENTION AMONG PWSCI WITH CHRONIC PAIN (PWSCI-CP) HAS NOT YET BEEN CONDUCTED. DETERMINING THE EFFICACY OF AN EXISTING, FREE, PUBLICLY AVAILABLE MM MOBILE APP TO MANAGE CHRONIC PAIN IS THE NEXT ESSENTIAL STEP IN IDENTIFYING AND DISSEMINATING TOOLS TO IMPROVE QOL AMONG PWSCI-CP, A POPULATION FACING PROFOUND BARRIERS TO ACCESSING HEALTHCARE SERVICES. THE PRESENT STUDY WILL BUILD ON THE PROMISING RESULTS OF AN NIH/NCCIH R34-FUNDED FEASIBILITY/ACCEPTABILITY PILOT RCT OF MOBILE APP-BASED MM INTERVENTION IN PWSCI-CP THAT OUR MULTIDISCIPLINARY, INTERINSTITUTIONAL TEAM RECENTLY COMPLETED. SPECIFICALLY, THE PRESENT STUDY WILL TEST THE EFFICACY OF A MOBILE APP-GUIDED MM INTERVENTION (MINDFULNESS COACH APP ≥ 10 MINUTES DAILY FOR 6 WEEKS) COMPARED TO A HEALTH EDUCATION ACTIVE CONTROL CONDITION (TED TALK APP ≥ 10 MINUTES DAILY FOR 6 WEEKS) ON PAIN INTENSITY IN PWSCI-CP. THE SECONDARY AIM IS TO EVALUATE THE INTERVENTION’S EFFICACY ON PAIN INTERFERENCE, DEPRESSION, AND ANXIETY, AND THE TERTIARY AIM IS TO EXPLORE THE MAINTENANCE OF INTERVENTION EFFECTS OVER A 6-MONTH FOLLOW-UP PERIOD. THIS STUDY WILL FACILITATE THE TEAM’S LONG-TERM GOAL TO IMPROVE PAIN MANAGEMENT AND QOL OF PWSCI-CP BY IDENTIFYING AFFORDABLE AND ACCESSIBLE INTERVENTIONS WHICH CAN BE USED AS AN ADJUVANT TOOL IN CONJUNCTION WITH OTHER TREATMENTS. WITH THE EMERGING USE OF DIGITAL HEALTH TECHNOLOGIES, THIS STUDY IS BOTH TIMELY AND INNOVATIVE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MULTICENTER FEASIBILITY OF INTEGRATIVE HEALTH COACHING FOR BACK PAIN AFTER AN EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT DISCHARGE - ABSTRACT THIS FEASIBILITY CLINICAL TRIAL IS BEING PROPOSED TO CONTRIBUTE TO OUR RESEARCH TEAM’S LONGER-TERM GOAL OF ESTABLISHING EFFECTIVE BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL INTERVENTIONS FOR PAIN THAT CAN BE INTEGRATED WITHIN THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT (ED) SETTING. CHRONIC LOW BACK PAIN (LBP) IS A CHALLENGING CONDITION FOR ED PROVIDERS TO MANAGE AND OFTEN CO-EXISTS WITH MEDICAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL CONDITIONS, WHICH COMPLICATES RECOVERY. DESPITE GROWING SUPPORT FOR A BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL ASSESSMENT AND MANAGEMENT APPROACH AS FIRST-LINE CHRONIC PAIN TREATMENT, UP TO 60% OF ED PATIENTS WITH ACUTE EXACERBATION OF CHRONIC LBP ARE PRESCRIBED OPIOID MEDICATIONS. LESS THAN 5% OF THESE PATIENTS RECEIVE AN EVIDENCE-BASED BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL INTERVENTION TO PROMOTE SELF-MANAGEMENT AFTER DISCHARGE AND REDUCE PROLONGED OPIOID USE AND RETURN ED VISITS. INTEGRATIVE HEALTH COACHING IS A SELF- MANAGEMENT INTERVENTION THAT IS TAILORED TO THE INDIVIDUAL PATIENT AND HAS SHOWN PROMISE FOR IMPROVING CHRONIC LBP AND DISABILITY. EVIDENCE IS LACKING ON THE BENEFITS OF HEALTH COACHING AS AN ED OPTION. INTEGRATIVE HEALTH COACHING SUPPORTS PATIENTS IN ACTIVELY MANAGING LBP AND ASSOCIATED COMORBIDITIES WITH EVIDENCE-BASED COMPLEMENTARY AND CONVENTIONAL STRATEGIES, BUT REMOTE INTERVENTIONS APPLYING INTEGRATIVE HEALTH COACHING AS A POST-DISCHARGE ED TREATMENT APPROACH HAVE BEEN INSUFFICIENTLY STUDIED. IT IS CRITICAL THAT ED PROVIDERS HAVE AN EVIDENCE-BASED NONPHARMACOLOGICAL STRATEGY THAT CAN BE OFFERED AFTER ED DISCHARGE TO IMPROVE MEANINGFUL PAIN-RELATED OUTCOMES. GIVEN OUR RESEARCH TEAM’S EXPERTISE IN OPTIMIZING BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL PAIN INTERVENTIONS AND IN TESTING HEALTH COACHING FOR CHRONIC CONDITIONS, OUR EXISTING ED RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE, AND OUR PRELIMINARY EXPERIENCE WITH A SINGLE-SITE TRIAL, WE ARE UNIQUELY PREPARED TO CONDUCT THIS MULTICENTER 2-ARMED RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL. THE OVERALL PURPOSE OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS TO ASSESS THE MULTICENTER FEASIBILITY OF OUR INTEGRATIVE HEALTH COACHING PROGRAM PROVIDED IN COMBINATION WITH USUAL ED CARE (COACH-ED) VS USUAL CARE ALONE FOR ADULT PATIENTS PRESENTING TO THE ED WITH ACUTE EXACERBATION OF CHRONIC LBP. OUR MAIN AIMS ARE TO ASSESS 1) THE FEASIBILITY OF OUR MULTICENTER TRIAL METHODOLOGY, 2) THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF OUR COACH-ED INTERVENTION, AND 3) PATIENT AND PROVIDER PERCEPTIONS OF INTERVENTION IMPLEMENTATION, DELIVERY, AND BENEFITS. THE FINDINGS FROM THIS FEASIBILITY CLINICAL TRIAL WILL FILL IMPORTANT GAPS IN THE EXISTING SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE AND ARE CRUCIAL FOR PLANNING AND CONDUCTING THE SUBSEQUENT EFFICACY TRIAL. OUR STUDY WILL BE A PIVOTAL STEP IN ADVANCING UNDERSTANDING OF A BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL MODEL OF CARE THAT COULD REDUCE RELIANCE ON OPIOIDS AMONG ED PATIENTS AND IN FINALIZING THE METHODS AND INFRASTRUCTURE FOR OUR FUTURE RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED EFFICACY TRIAL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING A MULTI-OMIC, PSYCHOSOCIAL, AND ENVIRONMENTAL MODEL OF INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES IN PAIN AND PLACEBO RESPONSES - THIS PROJECT INVESTIGATES CHRONIC PAIN CONDITIONS, PARTICULARLY TEMPOROMANDIBULAR DISORDER (TMD), FOCUSING ON THE VARIABILITY IN PAIN SENSITIVITY, TREATMENT RESPONSES, AND COMORBIDITIES SUCH AS DEPRESSION AND ANXIETY. A KEY MECHANISM INFLUENCING PAIN EXPERIENCE IS ENDOGENOUS PAIN MODULATION (EPM), WHICH INVOLVES NEURAL PATHWAYS THAT INHIBIT NOCICEPTIVE SIGNALING. PLACEBO HYPOALGESIA, A FORM OF EPM, IS KNOWN TO DEPEND ON PSYCHOLOGICAL, GENETIC, AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS. ALTHOUGH MUCH IS KNOWN ABOUT THE FACTORS CONTRIBUTING TO PLACEBO RESPONSES, THE REASONS FOR INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES IN PLACEBO EFFICACY REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. IT IS ALSO UNCLEAR HOW EPM INFLUENCES PAIN SEVERITY AND CHRONIC PAIN SEVERITY. CURRENT KNOWLEDGE INCLUDES THE FINDING THAT PAIN CATASTROPHIZING DIMENSIONS (RUMINATION, MAGNIFICATION, HELPLESSNESS) MEDIATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PSYCHOLOGICAL FACTORS AND CHRONIC PAIN SEVERITY. ADDITIONALLY, JAW FUNCTION, PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS, CHRONIC OVERLAPPING PAIN CONDITIONS (COPC), INSOMNIA, AND SOCIOECONOMIC POSITION (SEP) HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED AS INFLUENCING TMD SEVERITY AND PLACEBO RESPONSES. DESPITE THIS, MUCH REMAINS UNKNOWN ABOUT THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN OMIC VARIABILITY, SEP, AND PLACEBO RESPONSES, AND HOW THESE FACTORS TOGETHER SHAPE INDIVIDUAL PAIN OUTCOMES. TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS, THE PROJECT USES MACHINE LEARNING (ML) APPROACHES TO UNCOVER NOVEL INSIGHTS AND DEVELOP PERSONALIZED PREDICTIVE MODELS FOR PAIN MANAGEMENT. THE PROPOSED ML STRATEGIES INCLUDE: 1. SUPERVISED ML (RANDOM FORESTS, XGBOOST): THESE MODELS WILL BE USED TO IDENTIFY AND PREDICT PAIN PHENOTYPES AND PLACEBO RESPONSE VARIABILITY BASED ON CLINICAL DATA (E.G., DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, PAIN SENSITIVITY) FROM 402 INDIVIDUALS WITH CHRONIC TMD PAIN AND 400 HEALTHY CONTROLS. 2. UNSUPERVISED ML (GAUSSIAN MIXTURE MODELS, HIERARCHICAL CLUSTERING): THIS APPROACH WILL EXPLORE HOW GENETIC FACTORS, SUCH AS OPRM1 POLYMORPHISMS, INTERACT WITH SEP (E.G., INCOME, EDUCATION) TO INFLUENCE PAIN SEVERITY AND PLACEBO RESPONSES. IT AIMS TO UNCOVER HIDDEN PATTERNS OF GENETIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL INTERACTIONS THAT AFFECT PAIN EXPERIENCES. 3. GRAPH-BASED ML AND DEEP LEARNING: THESE ADVANCED MODELS WILL BE USED TO IDENTIFY BIOLOGICAL PATHWAYS RELATED TO PLACEBO RESPONSES AND PAIN SENSITIVITY BY ANALYZING TRANSCRIPTOMIC AND PROTEOMIC DATA, INTEGRATING MOLECULAR, IMMUNE-RELATED, AND GENETIC FACTORS. BY EMPLOYING THESE INNOVATIVE COMPUTATIONAL METHODS, THE PROJECT SEEKS TO MOVE BEYOND POPULATION-LEVEL ASSOCIATIONS AND DEVELOP PERSONALIZED MODELS THAT CAN PREDICT PLACEBO RESPONSIVENESS AND PAIN SENSITIVITY. ULTIMATELY, THE GOAL IS TO IMPROVE PAIN MANAGEMENT BY IDENTIFYING INDIVIDUALS MOST LIKELY TO BENEFIT FROM PLACEBO-DRIVEN ANALGESIC MECHANISMS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BIDIRECTIONAL BRAIN-COMPUTER INTERFACE WITH CLOSED-LOOP MIND-BODY INTERACTIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY BRAIN-COMPUTER INTERFACES (BCIS) ENABLE DIRECT COMMUNICATION BETWEEN THE BRAIN AND THE EXTERNAL WORLD. WE PROPOSE TO ESTABLISH AND INVESTIGATE THE MECHANISMS OF A NOVEL, NONINVASIVE BIDIRECTIONAL BCI (BI-BCI) PLATFORM. THIS SYSTEM COMBINES ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAPHY (EEG)-BASED NEURAL DECODING (“READING” BRAIN ACTIVITY) WITH CLOSED-LOOP, LOW-INTENSITY TRANSCRANIAL FOCUSED ULTRASOUND (TFUS) NEUROMODULATION (“WRITING” TO THE BRAIN). THIS DUAL APPROACH ENABLES REAL-TIME MEASUREMENT OF BEHAVIOR VIA BCI DECODING AND ADAPTIVE MODULATION OF NEURAL CIRCUITS. BY INTEGRATING NONINVASIVE NEURAL DECODING WITH PRECISION NEUROMODULATION, THE PROPOSED BI-BCI OFFERS A TRANSFORMATIVE PLATFORM FOR MECHANISTIC STUDIES OF MIND–BODY INTERVENTIONS—REVEALING HOW SPECIFIC BRAIN ACTIVITY PATTERNS RELATE TO BEHAVIOR AND HOW TARGETED MODULATION CAN SHIFT THESE PATTERNS TO ACHIEVE DESIRED OUTCOMES. TO REALIZE THIS VISION, WE PROPOSE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS UNIFIED UNDER A CENTRAL THEME: TO DEVELOP AND INVESTIGATE A BI-BCI FRAMEWORK THAT ENGAGES BOTH THE “MIND” (INTENTION AND COGNITION) AND “BODY” (PHYSIOLOGICAL PROCESSES) FOR TWO KEY APPLICATIONS—COMMUNICATION PROSTHESES (AIM 1) AND MOTOR PROSTHESES (AIM 2). THIS FOUNDATIONAL WORK WILL CATALYZE A NEW CLASS OF MIND–BODY INTERVENTIONS. AIM 1: ESTABLISH A TFUS-INTEGRATED MOTION-ONSET VISUAL EVOKED POTENTIAL BCI SPELLER FOR COMMUNICATION AND INVESTIGATE NEURAL MECHANISMS OF COGNITIVE ATTENTION DURING MIND–BODY INTERACTIONS. WE WILL ENHANCE FEATURE-BASED ATTENTION MECHANISMS BY COMBINING MOTION-ONSET VISUAL STIMULATION WITH TARGETED NEUROMODULATION OF VISUAL AREA V5. THIS APPROACH WILL YIELD A NOVEL BI-BCI WITH SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVED ACCURACY AND INFORMATION THROUGHPUT. AIM 2: ESTABLISH AND INVESTIGATE A TFUS-MODULATED SENSORIMOTOR RHYTHM (SMR) BI-BCI USING MOTOR IMAGERY FOR MOTOR CONTROL. WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT TFUS MODULATES THE DYNAMICS OF EVENT-RELATED DESYNCHRONIZATION/SYNCHRONIZATION (ERD/ERS), THEREBY ENHANCING MOTOR IMAGERY-BASED BCI CONTROL OF AN EXTERNAL OBJECT. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS RESEARCH WILL SIGNIFICANTLY ENHANCE BCI PERFORMANCE AND YIELD CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO THE NEURAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING MIND–BODY INTERVENTIONS MADE POSSIBLE BY NEUROMODULATION-ENHANCED, CLOSED-LOOP BI-BCIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NEUROBIOLOGY OF PAIN CATASTROPHIZING IN BURN SURVIVORS: IDENTIFICATION AND TARGETING OF A CRITICAL TREATMENT MECHANISM - ABSTRACT  EACH YEAR, APPROXIMATELY ½ MILLION PEOPLE IN THE U.S. SUSTAIN AND RECEIVE MEDICAL TREATMENT FOR BURN INJURIES. PAIN IS PARTICULARLY PREVALENT (>50% OF BURN SURVIVORS) AND DISABLING FOLLOWING BURNS, AND BOTH BURN- RELATED TISSUE INJURY AS WELL AS THE PROCEDURES REQUIRED FOR WOUND CARE CAN INITIATE SEVERE AND LONG-LASTING CHRONIC PAIN. AS PAIN IS KNOWN TO BE STRONGLY MODULATED BY NEGATIVE AFFECT, AND CATASTROPHIZING IN PARTICULAR, THE PAIN-REDUCING EFFECTS OF MANY NON-PHARMACOLOGIC TREATMENTS APPEAR TO BE DUE PARTIALLY TO THEIR EFFECTS ON COGNITIVE-EMOTIONAL PROCESSES SUCH AS CATASTROPHIZING. FOR EXAMPLE, STUDIES OF COGNITIVE-BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (CBT) FREQUENTLY IDENTIFY CATASTROPHIZING AS A CRITICAL MECHANISTIC VARIABLE, REDUCTIONS IN WHICH ARE LINKED TO IMPROVEMENTS IN PAIN, AND CBT HAS BEEN SHOWN TO IMPROVE PAIN IN SEVERAL STUDIES WITH BURN-INJURY SURVIVORS. IMPORTANTLY, THE NEUROBIOLOGY SUPPORTING CATASTROPHIZING IN BURN SURVIVORS IS UNKNOWN AND OBJECTIVE CATASTROPHIZING-LINKED BIOMARKERS MAY SERVE AS IMPORTANT THERAPEUTIC TARGETS AND/OR PREDICT LONG-TERM OUTCOMES IN THESE PATIENTS. THUS, OUR OVERALL GOAL IS TO ESTABLISH THE ROLE OF CATASTROPHIZING IN CHRONIC BURN- INJURY MORBIDITY BY IDENTIFYING HOW THE NEURAL CIRCUITRY UNDERLYING CATASTROPHIZING CAN BE MODULATED BY CBT, AND CAN PREDICT PAIN OUTCOMES - THUS FOSTERING FUTURE PERSONALIZATION FOR THERAPY. OUR AIMS WILL INVESTIGATE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN BRAIN PROCESSING OF CATASTROPHIZING AND INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES IN PAIN INTENSITY AND INTERFERENCE AMONG BURN-INJURY SURVIVORS. WE WILL ALSO EVALUATE WHETHER CBT (COMPARED TO A CONTROL INTERVENTION) RESULTS IN GREATER IMPROVEMENT IN PAIN AND CATASTROPHIZING, AND REDUCED BRAIN RESPONSE TO CATASTROPHIZING CUES. FINALLY, OUR PROPOSAL WILL DETERMINE WHETHER BASELINE BRAIN FMRI RESPONSE TO CATASTROPHIZING CUES (AFTER CONTROLLING FOR PATIENT-REPORTED CATASTROPHIZING SCORES) PREDICTS IMPROVEMENT IN PAIN OUTCOMES FOLLOWING CBT, AND WHETHER CHANGES IN BRAIN CATASTROPHIZING RESPONSE MEDIATE CHANGES IN PAIN ENDPOINTS. THIS STUDY WILL SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCE OUR MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF IMPROVEMENTS IN PAIN INTERFERENCE FOLLOWING CBT IN BURN INJURY SURVIVORS, AND HELP PREDICT WHICH PATIENTS WILL BEST RESPOND TO CBT THERAPY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MULTI-SITE FEASIBILITY TRIAL OF SMARTPHONE-BASED MINDFULNESS TREATMENT FOR PROMOTING ADDICTION RECOVERY - ABSTRACT/PROJECT SUMMARY  SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUDS) ARE PREVALENT AND LINKED WITH DEVASTATING NEGATIVE COSTS1. RELAPSE (I.E., RETURN TO FREQUENT SUBSTANCE USE2-5) AFTER INTENSIVE TREATMENT (E.G., IOP) IS A MAJOR PROBLEM: 50% RELAPSE AFTER INTENSIVE TREATMENT6-13. AFTERCARE TREATMENTS EXIST, SUCH AS COGNITIVE-BEHAVIORAL THERAPY (CBT) AND TWELVE- STEP FACILITATION (TSF), AND THEY HELP SOME INDIVIDUALS14,15, BUT MANY DO NOT RESPOND TO THEM15-18. THUS, THERE IS A NEED FOR ADDITIONAL AFTERCARE TREATMENT OPTIONS, WHICH MAY BENEFIT NON-RESPONDERS. MINDFULNESS-BASED TREATMENT (MBT) IS A PROMISING AFTERCARE TREATMENT FOR SUDS THAT INVOLVES TRAINING IN MINDFULNESS MEDITATION TO IMPROVE AWARENESS AND ACCEPTANCE OF MOMENTARY EXPERIENCES (E.G., NEGATIVE AFFECT AND CRAVING), AS WELL AS SAVORING PLEASANT EXPERIENCES 19,20. AFTERCARE MBT FOR SUDS IS EFFECTIVE IN REDUCING RELAPSE BASED ON META- ANALYSES21-25 , AND HAS SIMILAR EFFECTS TO OTHER EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENTS (E.G. CBT). HOWEVER, ACCESSIBILITY OF AFTERCARE MBT IS POOR, DUE TO A LACK OF TRAINED PROVIDERS26. A DIGITAL MBT FOR SUDS ELIMINATES THE NEED TO TRAIN PROVIDERS AND CAN INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY, THEREBY INCREASING THE PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT OF MBT FOR SUDS.  A DIGITAL AFTERCARE MBT FOR SUDS IS ALSO IMPORTANT TO DEVELOP BECAUSE: (1) THERE IS A SMALL NUMBER OF AVAILABLE DIGITAL AFTERCARE TREATMENTS27,28 THEY DO NOT BENEFIT ALL INDIVIDUALS28-33, AND (2) EXISTING MINDFULNESS APPS (E.G. CALM) ARE NOT SUITABLE AS AFTERCARE INTERVENTIONS FOR SUDS BECAUSE THEY ARE GENERIC AND NOT TAILORED FOR SUDS, WHICH IS IMPORTANT BECAUSE DISORDER-SPECIFIC APPS ARE MORE EFFECTIVE THAN GENERIC APPS34, AND ALSO APPS SHOULD BE DEVELOPED WITH INPUT/FEEDBACK FROM PEOPLE WITH SUDS35,36 (I.E., USER-CENTERED DESIGN, UCD36). ALTOGETHER, A DIGITAL MBT FOR SUDS HAS GREAT POTENTIAL TO BE AN ACCESSIBLE AND EFFECTIVE AFTERCARE TREATMENT.  ACCORDINGLY, VIA UCD36, WE DEVELOPED MINDFUL JOURNEY, AN APP-BASED AFTERCARE MBT FOR SUDS THAT TARGETS AWARENESS, ACCEPTANCE, AND SAVORING VIA 15 LESSONS (~30-45 MIN EACH) WITH AUDIO-GUIDED PRACTICES, ANIMATED VIDEOS, AND QUESTIONS. IN OUR BETA-TESTING37 (N=10) AND IN OUR SINGLE-SITE FEASIBILITY TRIAL38(N=36) WE FOUND HIGH FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY. WE NOW PROPOSE A MULTI-SITE FEASIBILITY TRIAL IN WHICH 90 INDIVIDUALS WITH SUDS INITIATING OUTPATIENT AFTERCARE TREATMENT ARE RANDOMIZED TO 8 WEEKS OF STANDARD AFTERCARE TREATMENT (SAT) + MINDFUL JOURNEY OR SAT + DOSE-MATCHED SMARTPHONE-BASED STRESS MANAGEMENT (SSM; ACTIVE CONTROL CONDITION). SSM ALSO INCLUDES 15 LESSONS AND COVERS TOPICS SUCH AS GUIDED IMAGERY, BUT WITH NO MINDFULNESS. AIMS INCLUDE EVALUATING: (1) FEASIBILITY OF RECRUITMENT, RANDOMIZATION, AND RETENTION; AND (2) FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF MINDFUL JOURNEY AND SSM. EXPLORATORY AIMS INCLUDE QUALITATIVE ASSESSMENT OF FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY, AND TESTING SENSITIVITY TO CHANGE OVER TIME (WITHIN EACH CONDITION) FOR SUBSTANCE USE AND OTHER OUTCOMES. WE WILL RECRUIT FROM THREE SUD TREATMENT CLINICS: LOCATED NEAR YALE, ARIZONA STATE UNIVERSITY, AND UC BERKELEY. THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE ESSENTIAL DATA TO PREPARE FOR A FULL-POWERED MULTI-SITE EFFICACY TRIAL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CRCNS: LINKING RESPIRATION AND VISUAL PERCEPTION THROUGH BRAIN-BODY INTEGRATION - PROJECT SUMMARY (SEE INSTRUCTIONS): WHILE PEOPLE ENGAGE WITH THE WORLD, INTERNAL BODILY PROCESSES SUCH AS RESPIRATION, HEART RATE, AND BLOOD OXYGENATION CONTINUOUSLY FLUCTUATE AND INTERACT WITH NEURAL SYSTEMS. EMERGING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT THESE RHYTHMS SHAPE PERCEPTION AND DECISION MAKING, YET THE UNDERLYING BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. TO ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF THESE MIND-BODY INTERACTIONS, THIS PROJECT INVESTIGATES HOW BREATHING INFLUENCES BRAIN ACTIVITY, PERCEPTION, AND DECISION MAKING. THIS PROJECT COLLECTS A UNIQUE MULTI-MODAL DATASET COMBINING DETAILED PHYSIOLOGICAL MONITORING WITH ADVANCED HUMAN BRAIN RECORDINGS. PATIENTS UNDERGOING MONITORING FOR CLINICAL PURPOSES WITH INTRACRANIAL EEG AND HEALTHY PARTICIPANTS MEASURED WITH SCALP EEG AND FUNCTIONAL NEAR-INFRARED SPECTROSCOPY WILL PERFORM THE SAME VISUAL PERCEPTION TASKS. SIMULTANEOUSLY, MEASUREMENTS OF RESPIRATION, CARDIOVASCULAR ACTIVITY, BLOOD OXYGENATION, AND PUPIL DIAMETER WILL BE OBTAINED. THESE PHYSIOLOGICAL MEASUREMENTS WILL BE LINKED TO NEURAL DYNAMICS AND BEHAVIORAL OUTCOMES TO QUANTIFY BRAIN-BODY INTERACTIONS. FIRST, THESE UNIQUE DATA WILL BE USED TO QUANTIFY HOW BREATHING IS COUPLED TO NEURAL SIGNALS, CEREBRAL HEMODYNAMICS, AND PERCEPTUAL TASK PERFORMANCE. THE PROJECT WILL EXTRACT FINE-GRAINED FEATURES OF PHYSIOLOGY AND RESPIRATION THAT ALIGN WITH NEUROVASCULAR PROCESSES. THE LINK BETWEEN THESE FEATURES AND PERCEPTUAL TASK PERFORMANCE WILL THEN BE QUANTIFIED TO UNDERSTAND THE MECHANISMS THAT COUPLE INTEROCEPTIVE RHYTHMS TO BEHAVIOR. SECOND, THE MULTIMODAL MEASUREMENTS WILL BE USED TO EXTEND VISUAL ENCODING MODELS BY INCORPORATING INTERPRETABLE PARAMETERS THAT CAPTURE PHYSIOLOGY DRIVEN VARIABILITY IN BRAIN RESPONSES. THIS MODELING APPROACH WILL TEST HOW PHYSIOLOGICAL FACTORS LIKE RESPIRATION INFLUENCE TRIAL-TO-TRIAL FLUCTUATIONS IN VISUAL RESPONSES. BY TREATING TRIAL-TO-TRIAL VARIABILITY AS A MEANINGFUL BIOLOGICAL SIGNAL RATHER THAN NOISE, THE PROJECT MAKES QUANTITATIVE ASSESSMENTS OF BRAIN-BODY INTERACTIONS. BY INTEGRATING AND MODELING MULTIPLE INTERACTING PHYSIOLOGICAL SYSTEMS, INCLUDING RESPIRATORY, CARDIOVASCULAR, NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL, AND NEUROVASCULAR PROCESSES, THIS STUDY ADVANCES INSIGHT INTO COMPLEX, MULTISYSTEM MIND-BRAIN INTERACTIONS THAT UNDERLIE WHOLE PERSON HEALTH, ALIGNING WITH THE NCCIH STRATEGIC PLAN. THE FINDINGS MAY HAVE FUTURE CLINICAL RELEVANCE BY INFORMING STRATEGIES TO OPTIMIZE THERAPIES-SUCH AS NEUROSTIMULATION OR BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS-BASED ON PHYSIOLOGICAL STATE, THEREBY IMPROVING TREATMENT PRECISION AND EFFECTIVENESS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENHANCING CAR-T CELL THERAPY FOR DLBCL - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IMPROVE ANTI-CD19 CHIMERIC ANTIGEN RECEPTOR T CELL (CART19) THERAPY FOR PATIENTS WITH RELAPSED OR REFRACTORY LARGE B CELL LYMPHOMA (R/R LBCL). UNFORTUNATELY, 50%-60% OF PATIENTS WITH R/R LBCL RECEIVING FDA-APPROVED AUTOLOGOUS CART19 THERAPY (TISA-, AXI- OR LISO-CEL) WILL RELAPSE, OFTEN DUE TO POOR IN VIVO EXPANSION AND PERSISTENCE OF THE CART19. IL-7, IL-15, AND IL-21 ARE CRITICAL HOMEOSTATIC REGULATORS OF T CELLS AND PROMOTE STEM CELL MEMORY PHENOTYPES. NT-I7 IS A LONG-ACTING VERSION OF HUMAN IL-7, WHILE HCW11-006 IS A LONG-ACTING MULTIMERIC PROTEIN CONTAINING IL-7, IL-15, AND IL-21. WHILE OUR RECENT PHASE 1B TRIAL (NCT05075603) CONFIRMED THAT NT-I7 IS SAFE 21 DAYS POST-CART19, THIS TIMING COINCIDED WITH THE CART19 CONTRACTION PHASE, RESULTING IN MINIMAL EXPANSION. IN AIM 1A, WE WILL CONDUCT A NEW PHASE 1B TRIAL EVALUATING EARLY (DAY 10) AND REPEATED (DAY 31) DOSING OF NT-I7 FOLLOWING AXI- OR LISO-CELL INFUSION IN R/R LBCL PATIENTS. AIM 1B WILL INVOLVE EXTENSIVE CORRELATIVE STUDIES TO ANALYZE THE IMPACT OF NT-I7 ON (1) SERUM CYTOKINES, (2) CART19 AND ENDOGENOUS T CELLS, (3) OTHER NON-T CELL SUBSETS, AND (4) THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT (TME) USING FLOW CYTOMETRY, SINGLE CELL RNA-SEQUENCING, AND MULTIPLEXED TME PROFILING. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT INITIATING A REPEATED NT-I7 DOSING SCHEDULE DURING CART19 EXPANSION (DAY 10) IS SAFE, PROMOTES SUPERIOR IN VIVO CART19 PERSISTENCE/EXPANSION AND IMPROVES CLINICAL OUTCOMES FOR R/R LBCL PATIENTS. HOWEVER, BECAUSE NT-I7 MAY NOT PROVIDE DURABLE REMISSIONS, WE WILL PERFORM AN UNBIASED CRISPR SCREEN TO IDENTIFY GENES ENHANCING NT-I7-TREATED CART19 FUNCTION (AIM 1C). IN AIM 2, WE WILL EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF NT-I7 OR HCW11-006 (IL-7/IL-15/IL-21) ON CART19-MEDIATED TOXICITIES (CRS/ICANS) AND EFFICACY USING AUTOLOGOUS (AIM 2A) AND ALLOGENEIC (AIM 2B) PRECLINICAL MOUSE MODELS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT EARLY, REPEATED CYTOKINE ADMINISTRATION SUSTAINS CART19 PROLIFERATION, PERSISTENCE, AND TUMOR KILLING WITHOUT EXACERBATING TOXICITY. USING IMMUNOCOMPETENT AND “HUMANIZED” NSGS MICE, WE WILL COMPARE AN EARLY REGIMEN (DAYS 1 AND 21) AGAINST THE CLINICAL SCHEDULE (DAYS 10 AND 31). SINCE NEW APPROACHES ARE NEEDED TO OVERCOME HOST-MEDIATED ALLOGENEIC CART REJECTION BY CD2-EXPRESSING T CELLS AND NK, WE WILL TEST IF CD2 EPITOPE EDITING OF ALLOGENEIC CART19 CONFERS RESISTANCE TO CD2 ANTIBODY-MEDIATED LYMPHODEPLETION AND ENHANCES THEIR PERSISTENCE AND EFFICACY IN MURINE ALLOGENEIC OR XENOGENEIC HOSTS WITH LBCL. PRECLINICAL MOUSE MODELS ARE ESSENTIAL TO CAPTURE THE COMPLEX DYNAMICS OF AUTOLOGOUS AND ALLOGENEIC CART19, INCLUDING TRAFFICKING, TME REMODELING, AND CRS/ICANS, WHICH IN SILICO AND IN VITRO METHODS CANNOT REPLICATE. BY PRESERVING AN INTACT VASCULAR SYSTEM AND HOST IMMUNITY, THESE MODELS PROVIDE A ROBUST FOUNDATION FOR CLINICAL TRIALS DESIGNED TO IMPROVE LBCL SURVIVAL WHILE MINIMIZING TOXICITIES.
