description: SRIN009, A CANNABIDIOL FORMULATION TO TREAT CHEMOTHERAPY-INDUCED NEUROPATHIC PAIN - CHEMOTHERAPY-INDUCED PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY (CIPN) IS A DEBILITATING ADVERSE EFFECT EXPERIENCED BY UP TO 75% OF PATIENTS RECEIVING CERTAIN CHEMOTHERAPY REGIMENS. COMMON SENSORY SYMPTOMS INCLUDE PAIN, PARESTHESIA, DYSESTHESIA, AND HYPERSENSITIVITY TO TOUCH AND TEMPERATURE. CIPN IS A MAJOR CAUSE OF DOSE REDUCTION OR EARLY CESSATION OF CANCER TREATMENT, WHICH MAY INCREASE RECURRENCE RISK AND REDUCE SURVIVAL. CHEMOTHERAPEUTIC AGENTS DISRUPT CYTOSKELETAL AND MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION, DNA SYNTHESIS, AND PROMOTE INFLAMMATORY CELL DEATH; INFLAMMATION IS A PROMINENT CONTRIBUTOR TO CIPN. THERE ARE CURRENTLY NO FDA-APPROVED THERAPIES FOR PREVENTION OR TREATMENT OF CIPN. ALTHOUGH OPIOIDS HAVE BEEN USED FOR PAIN FOR DECADES, THEIR UTILITY IN CIPN IS LIMITED BY QUESTIONABLE EFFICACY AND WELL-KNOWN ADVERSE EFFECTS. CANNABIDIOL (CBD), A NON-PSYCHOACTIVE AND NON-ADDICTIVE PHYTOCANNABINOID, HAS ANTI-INFLAMMATORY AND NEUROPROTECTIVE ACTIVITY IN PRECLINICAL CELL-BASED AND RODENT STUDIES AND IS WIDELY USED BY PATIENTS BECAUSE OF ITS PERCEIVED THERAPEUTIC BENEFIT. OUR LABORATORY WAS THE FIRST TO DESCRIBE PROTECTIVE EFFECTS OF CBD IN RODENT MODELS OF CIPN AND HAS SUBSEQUENTLY DEMONSTRATED ANTI-NEUROPATHIC EFFECTS OF CBD ACROSS MULTIPLE ANIMAL MODELS. HOWEVER, THREE BARRIERS MUST BE ADDRESSED BEFORE CBD CAN BE ADVANCED AS A PHARMACOTHERAPY FOR CIPN: POOR WATER SOLUBILITY AND BIOAVAILABILITY; AN INCOMPLETE UNDERSTANDING OF DISEASE- AND SYMPTOM-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS; AND THE CRITICAL NEED TO ESTABLISH THAT PROPHYLACTIC CBD DOES NOT DIMINISH THE ANTI-NEOPLASTIC EFFICACY OF CHEMOTHERAPY. TO ADDRESS THESE BARRIERS, WE DEVELOPED TWO NANOEMULSION FORMULATIONS OF CBD, SRIN-009, WITH AND WITHOUT TERPENES. IN WELL-DEFINED PRECLINICAL BRAFV600E MELANOMA AND NON-SMALL-CELL LUNG CANCER MODELS, SRIN-009 DID NOT DIMINISH THE IN VIVO ANTI-TUMOR EFFICACY OF DACARBAZINE OR CARBOPLATIN. CBD ALSO DID NOT REDUCE THE ANTI-NEOPLASTIC EFFECTS OF PACLITAXEL IN TWO BREAST-CANCER CELL LINES IN VITRO. TUMOR-BEARING RODENT MODELS ARE ESSENTIAL BECAUSE THEY ALLOW SIMULTANEOUS ASSESSMENT OF CHEMOTHERAPY-INDUCED SENSORY NEUROPATHY, SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATORY AND NEUROIMMUNE RESPONSES, DRUG EXPOSURE, AND ANTI-TUMOR EFFICACY WITHIN AN INTACT ORGANISM. THESE INTEGRATED OUTCOMES CANNOT BE ADEQUATELY MODELED USING CELL CULTURE OR OTHER NON-ANIMAL APPROACHES ALONE. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SRIN-009 WILL PREVENT CIPN BY MINIMIZING CHEMOTHERAPY-ASSOCIATED NEUROTOXICITY AND INFLAMMATION WITHOUT COMPROMISING ANTI-CANCER TREATMENT EFFICACY, THEREBY IMPROVING PATIENTS’ ABILITY TO COMPLETE PRESCRIBED CHEMOTHERAPY. THE AIMS OF THIS R01 PROPOSAL ARE TO: (1) DETERMINE THE SRIN-009 FORMULATION THAT PROVIDES OPTIMAL THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY AGAINST CIPN; (2) DEFINE ANTI-INFLAMMATORY MECHANISMS UNDERLYING SRIN-009-MEDIATED PREVENTION OF CIPN; AND (3) EVALUATE COMPATIBILITY OF SRIN-009 WITH TARGETED-PATHWAY AND IMMUNE-CHECKPOINT INHIBITORS TO ESTABLISH ITS SAFETY FOR USE IN CANCER PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HYPOXIA INDUCES A STATE OF IMMUNOGENIC DORMANCY IN CANCER CELLS - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT DEFICIENCIES IN TUMOR IMMUNOGENICITY PREVENT RESPONSE TO IMMUNOTHERAPIES AND REPRESENT A PERVASIVE MEANS OF TUMOR IMMUNE ESCAPE ACROSS MANY CANCERS. EFFORTS TO ADDRESS LOW TUMOR IMMUNOGENICITY HOLD GREAT PROMISE AS ADJUVANTS TO EXISTING IMMUNOTHERAPIES, OR AS NOVEL THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION STRATEGIES, BUT THE BIOLOGIC PROCESSES OF HOW TUMORS LOSE IMMUNOGENICITY IS NOT WELL DEFINED. ADAPTIVE RESPONSE TO TUMORS REQUIRES TUMOR ANTIGENS (TA) TO BE PROCESSED AND PRESENTED BY THE MHC CLASS I PRESENTATION PATHWAY. REDUCED EXPRESSION OR DEFICIENCIES IN THIS PATHWAY ARE ASSOCIATED WITH TUMOR IMMUNE ESCAPE AND WORSE DISEASE OUTCOMES. REDUCED TUMOR IMMUNOGENICITY IS ALSO CORRELATED WITH TUMOR HYPOXIA, AN INTRINSIC FEATURE PERVASIVE ACROSS NEARLY ALL SOLID TUMORS. WHILE HYPOXIA HAS WELL-DEFINED DETRIMENTAL EFFECTS ON IMMUNE CELL FUNCTION, MUCH LESS IS KNOWN REGARDING THE EFFECTS OF REDUCED OXYGEN ON THE CLASS I PRESENTATION PATHWAY. HERE, WE PRESENT EVIDENCE THAT PATHOPHYSIOLOGIC LEVELS OF OXYGEN BLOCK THE INDUCTION OF CRITICAL COMPONENTS OF THE CLASS I PROCESSING PATHWAY NORMALLY INDUCED BY INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES LIKE INTERFERON GAMMA (IFN-Ã). THIS BLOCKADE INCLUDES THE THREE INDUCIBLE CATALYTIC SUBUNITS OF THE IMMUNOPROTEASOME (IP), CRITICAL ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM (ER) PEPTIDE TRANSPORTERS, AND ER-ASSOCIATED CHAPERONES AND PEPTIDE-LOADING COMPLEX (PLC) PROTEINS, RESULTING IN REDUCED NUMBERS AND DIVERSITIES OF MHC CLASS I-PRESENTED ANTIGENS. FURTHERMORE, WE DEMONSTRATE THIS OCCURS AT THE LEVEL OF PROTEIN TRANSLATION AND IS SENSITIVE TO MRNA M5C METHYLATION. OUR OVERALL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT TUMOR HYPOXIA INDUCES A STATE OF IMMUNOGENIC DORMANCY BY BLOCKING THE TRANSLATION OF ANTIGEN PROCESSING MACHINERY PROTEINS THROUGH EPITRANSCRIPTOMIC MODIFICATIONS, LEADING TO UNDER-PRESENTED MHC CLASS I TA PEPTIDES AND DIMINISHED TC ACTIVATION. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS USING THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1: TO VALIDATE AND QUANTIFY THE DETRIMENTAL EFFECT HYPOXIA HAS ON THE LANDSCAPE OF MHC CLASS I-PRESENTED NEOANTIGEN PEPTIDES IN CANCER CELLS. AIM 2: TO DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF HYPOXIA-INDUCED IMMUNOGENIC DORMANCY ON TC ANTI-TUMOR RESPONSE. AIM 3: TO MAP M5C MODIFICATIONS UNDER HYPOXIA AND IDENTIFY WHICH METHYLTRANSFERASES AND DEMETHYLASES GOVERN IMMUNOGENIC DORMANCY. WHY ANIMAL MODELS ARE REQUIRED: THIS PROJECT STUDIES HOW LOW OXYGEN INSIDE TUMORS PREVENTS THE IMMUNE SYSTEM FROM RECOGNIZING AND ATTACKING CANCER CELLS. THIS REQUIRES AN INTACT, FUNCTIONING IMMUNE SYSTEM INTERACTING WITH A LIVING TUMOR OVER TIME, WHICH CANNOT BE REPRODUCED IN CELLS GROWN IN A DISH OR BY COMPUTER MODELING, AND CANNOT BE TESTED IN PATIENTS BECAUSE IT REQUIRES DIRECTLY CONTROLLING OXYGEN LEVELS INSIDE THE TUMOR. MOUSE TUMOR MODELS ARE THE SIMPLEST AVAILABLE SYSTEM IN WHICH THESE QUESTIONS CAN BE ANSWERED, AND NO SUITABLE ALTERNATIVES WERE IDENTIFIED. COMPLETION OF THIS WORK WILL DEMONSTRATE THE DIRECT IMPACT TUMOR HYPOXIA HAS ON TA PROCESSING AND PRESENTATION, IDENTIFY TA-DERIVED IMMUNOPEPTIDES MOST AFFECTED BY THIS BLOCKADE, AND ELUCIDATE THE MECHANISM LEADING TO HYPOXIA-INDUCED IMMUNOGENIC DORMANCY. THESE OUTCOMES WILL REVEAL AN UNDERAPPRECIATED DIRECT LINK BETWEEN INTRINSIC BIOPHYSICAL ATTRIBUTES OF THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT AND SUPPRESSED IMMUNOGENICITY AND LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR IDENTIFYING NOVEL TARGETS CAPABLE OF INCREASING TUMOR CELL IMMUNOGENICITY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CRITICAL ROLE FOR HSF2 AND HSP110 AXIS IN REGULATION OF PRE-MRNA SPLICING AND RADIATION RESPONSE - ABSTRACT PANCREATIC DUCTAL ADENOCARCINOMA (PDAC) HAS A POOR 5-YEAR SURVIVAL OUTCOME WITH A LIMITED THERAPEUTIC OPPORTUNITY. A MAJOR BARRIER TO THE DURABLE CLINICAL RESPONSES IS THE TUMOR’S ABILITY TO ADAPT TO THERAPEUTIC PRESSURES (SUCH AS CYTOTOXIC CHEMOTHERAPY, RADIOTHERAPY, TARGETED AGENTS, AND IMMUNOTHERAPY) THROUGH TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND POST-TRANSCRIPTIONAL MECHANISMS THAT PROMOTE CELL SURVIVAL, ENHANCE DNA REPAIR, AND SUPPRESS IMMUNE SURVEILLANCE. DISRUPTING TRANSCRIPTIONAL FIDELITY CAN SIMULTANEOUSLY IMPAIR DNA REPAIR, ONCOGENIC SIGNALING, AND ENHANCE ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNE RESPONSES, OFFERING BROAD THERAPEUTIC LEVERAGE. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO ADDRESS THESE CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL UNMET NEEDS. OUR PRELIMINARY RESULTS SHOW THAT HEAT SHOCK TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR 2 (HSF2) AND ITS DOWNSTREAM TRANSCRIPTIONAL TARGET HSP110 ARE UPREGULATED IN CELLS IN RESPONSE TO X-IRRADIATION (IR) EXPOSURE. LOSS OF HSF2 OR HSP110 INCREASES TRANSCRIPTION-ASSOCIATED DNA DAMAGE IN CELLS, AND THEIR LOSS LEADS TO SUPPRESSION OF RNA POLYMERASE II (RNAPII) C-TERMINAL DOMAIN (CTD) PHOSPHORYLATION AT SERINE 7 (RNAPIICTD PS7). RNAPIICTD PS7 REGULATES TRANSCRIPTION OF SMALL NUCLEAR RNAS (SNRNAS), WHICH ARE ESSENTIAL COMPONENTS OF PRE-MRNA SPLICING AND SPLICEOSOMES. CONSEQUENTLY, REDUCTION IN PS7 IN HSF2- OR HSP110-DEFICIENT CELLS REDUCES SNRNA LEVELS, RESULTING IN ALTERED ALTERNATIVE SPLICING AND POTENTIALLY GENERATING NOVEL TRANSCRIPTS. FURTHERMORE, LOSS OF HSF2 OR HSP110 IMPAIRS RNAPII PROCESSIVITY, RESULTING IN ALTERED RNAPII OCCUPANCY DYNAMICS, REDUCED TRANSCRIPTIONAL FIDELITY, AND TRANSCRIPTION-ASSOCIATED GENOME INSTABILITY. UNDER GENOTOXIC STRESS INDUCED BY IR, LOSS OF HSF2 OR HSP110 REDUCES THE EXPRESSION OF DNA REPAIR GENES, LEADING TO CELLULAR SENSITIVITY TO IR EXPOSURE, WHICH IS CONSISTENT WITH A SIGNIFICANT INCREASE IN DNA DAMAGE, CELL DEATH, AND INFILTRATION OF CD8+ T CELLS, THEREBY SIGNIFICANTLY INHIBITING PDAC TUMOR GROWTH IN MICE. BASED ON THESE OBSERVATIONS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT: DISRUPTION OF THE HSF2-HSP110 AXIS IMPAIRS ADAPTIVE TRANSCRIPTIONAL RESPONSES, SENSITIZES TUMOR CELLS TO GENOTOXIC THERAPIES, AND ENHANCES ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNITY, REVEALING A NOVEL AND ACTIONABLE VULNERABILITY IN CANCER TREATMENT. TO DETERMINE THE THERAPEUTIC VULNERABILITY OF TUMORS FOLLOWING HSF2 OR HSP110 LOSS, WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING AIMS: (1). DETERMINE THE ROLE OF HSF2 OR HSP110 IN REGULATING RNAPII PROCESSIVITY THAT CULMINATES IN DNA DAMAGE AND X-IRRADIATION SENSITIVITY AND ALTERED SPLICING PROVIDING MULTIPLE AVENUES OF PDAC-SPECIFIC CELL KILLING. (2). DETERMINE THE THERAPEUTIC SIGNIFICANCE OF THE HSF2–HSP110 AXIS IN GENOTOXIC STRESS RESPONSE AND IDENTIFY HSF2/HSP110 INHIBITORS AS CANDIDATE THERAPEUTICS. WE PREDICT THAT THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS STUDY WILL ESTABLISH NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR TREATING PDAC THROUGH SIMULTANEOUS INDUCTION OF TRANSCRIPTION STALLING, SPLICING IMPAIRMENT, IMMUNOMODULATION, AND TUMOR CELL-SPECIFIC RADIATION SENSITIVITY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EVOLUTION OF INFLUENCER-DRIVEN E-CIGARETTE MARKETING ON SOCIAL MEDIA AND ITS EFFECT ON E-CIGARETTE PERCEPTIONS AND USE PATTERNS AMONG ADOLESCENTS - ABSTRACT/PROJECT SUMMARY E-CIGARETTE USE AMONG ADOLESCENTS REMAINS A CONCERN IN THE UNITED STATES WITH OVER 1.6 MILLION (6%) OF MIDDLE- AND HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS REPORTING PAST 30-DAY USE IN 2024. SOCIAL MEDIA ADVERTISING EXPOSURE IS ASSOCIATED WITH E-CIGARETTE USE AMONG YOUTH. CONTENT HOSTED BY MICRO-INFLUENCERS - E.G., MODELS, BLOGGERS, BRAND AMBASSADORS WHO TYPICALLY HAVE 1,000-100,000 FOLLOWERS AND POST ON BEHALF OF E-CIGARETTE BRANDS – IS PREVALENT, ESPECIALLY ON SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS POPULAR AMONG ADOLESCENTS: INSTAGRAM AND TIKTOK. MICROINFLUENCERS HAVE BEEN INCREASINGLY USING COVERT MARKETING TACTICS SUCH AS AUDIO-VISUAL EFFECTS, INCLUDING STYLIZING THEMSELVES TO APPEAR YOUNGER, USING AUTONOMOUS SENSORY MERIDIAN RESPONSE (ASMR) SOUNDS (E.G., TAPPING ON AN E-CIGARETTE) THAT CAN TRIGGER PLEASANT SENSATIONS, AND DEPICTING E-CIGARETTES IN ATTRACTIVE LIFESTYLE CONTEXTS (E.G., HEALTHY LIFESTYLE, GAMING, COMPUTER-GENERATED AVATAR). MICRO-INFLUENCERS’ POSTS ALSO OFTEN LACK OR HAVE NON-COMPLIANT WITH REQUIREMENTS IMPLEMENTED BY THE U.S. FEDERAL FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION (FDA) AND THE FEDERAL TRADE COMMISSION (FTC) E-CIGARETTE BRAND SPONSORSHIP DISCLOSURES OR NICOTINE WARNING LABELS. THESE TACTICS COULD DIMINISH ADOLESCENTS’ HARM PERCEPTIONS OF E-CIGARETTES, CONTRIBUTE TO NORMALIZATION OF E-CIGARETTE USE, AND EXPOSE E-CIGARETTE NEVER-USERS TO E-CIGARETTE CONTENT. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO INFORM THE FIELD ABOUT E-CIGARETTE-RELATED INFLUENCER MARKETING ON SOCIAL MEDIA AND ITS EFFECTS ON YOUTH. TO UNDERSTAND THE IMPACT OF THESE MARKETING TACTICS, THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL 1) CONDUCT TWO RANDOMIZED BETWEEN-SUBJECT EXPERIMENTS AMONG 6,000 ADOLESCENTS (PER EACH EXPERIMENT) RECRUITED NATIONWIDE AND AN EYE-TRACKING WITHIN-SUBJECT EXPERIMENT AMONG 300 CALIFORNIA ADOLESCENTS TO TEST THE EFFECTS OF AUDIO-VISUAL FEATURES OF E-CIGARETTE INFLUENCER MARKETING ON PERCEPTIONS OF INFLUENCER CREDIBILITY, E-CIGARETTE HARM PERCEPTIONS, APPEAL, AND SUSCEPTIBILITY TO E-CIGARETTE USE (AIM 1), AND 2) DETECT AND MONITOR INFLUENCERS’ USE OF AUDIO-VISUAL MARKETING FEATURES ON SOCIAL MEDIA OVER TIME (2019-2029), USING MULTIMODAL DEEP LEARNING (AIM 2). FINDINGS FROM THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE INFORMATION ABOUT ADOLESCENTS’ RISKS OF EXPOSURE TO E-CIGARETTE-RELATED CONTENT PROMOTED BY INFLUENCERS ON SOCIAL MEDIA. THIS INFORMATION CAN INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE TOBACCO PREVENTION AND CESSATION INTERVENTIONS FOR ADOLESCENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EPIGENETIC REGULATION OF PREMALIGNANT STATES IN THE SKIN - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CUTANEOUS SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (CSCC) IS THE SECOND MOST COMMON CANCER AFFECTING PATIENTS IN THE UNITED STATES AND IS A MAJOR CAUSE OF CANCER-RELATED DEATH. DESPITE THIS, THERE ARE FEW CLINICALLY RELEVANT ANIMAL MODELS OR TRANSLATIONAL EFFORTS TO STUDY CSCC PATHOGENESIS. WE ESTABLISHED THAT THE HISTONE DEMETHYLASE KDM6A IS A CSCC TUMOR SUPPRESSOR IN MICE WITH COMBINED KERATINOCYTE SPECIFIC KDM6A AND TRP53 DEFICIENCY, WHICH INVARIABLY DEVELOP SPONTANEOUS CSCC COMPARED TO 10% AND 0% OF MICE WITH RESPECTIVE TRP53 OR KDM6A SINGLE DEFICIENCY. WE ALSO FOUND THAT KDM6A IS PREDOMINANTLY EXPRESSED AT HIGH LEVELS IN KERATINOCYTE NUCLEI IN NORMAL HUMAN SKIN, BUT ITS ABUNDANCE AND LOCALIZATION ARE ALTERED IN OVER HALF OF CSCC TUMORS AS WELL AS EARLY IN SITU TUMORS. TAKEN TOGETHER, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT KDM6A FUNCTIONAL ALTERATION OCCURS EARLY IN CSCC PATHOGENESIS, AND ITS CYTOPLASMIC LOCALIZATION IMPAIRS ITS TUMOR SUPPRESSIVE FUNCTION. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DEFINE THE CAUSES AND CONSEQUENCES OF KDM6A MISLOCALIZATION BY DEFINING GENOMIC CORRELATES OF KDM6A MISLOCALIZATION USING EXOME SEQUENCING FROM BANKED HUMAN TUMORS. WE WILL TEST THE EFFECTS OF CANCER-ASSOCIATED KDM6A MUTATIONS ON ITS LOCALIZATION AND DETERMINE WHETHER KDM6A MUTATIONS ALTER ITS TUMOR SUPPRESSOR FUNCTION IN VITRO. WE WILL THEN DETERMINE WHETHER KDM6A PROXIMITY NETWORKS ARE DISRUPTED BY CANCER-ASSOCIATED MUTATIONS BY PROXIMITY LIGATION ANALYSIS, WHICH WILL GIVE US CLUES TO THE MECHANISM BY WHICH KDM6A MISLOCALIZES AND HOW IT MIGHT LOSE ITS TUMOR SUPPRESSOR ACTIVITY. IN AIM 2, WE DEFINE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH KDM6A DEFICIENCY ESTABLISHES A TUMOR PRONE STATE BY CHARACTERIZING THE EXPRESSION AND EPIGENOMIC LANDSCAPE OF PREMALIGNANT SKIN AND HOW IT EVOLVES WITH TRANSFORMATION. WE WILL THEN DETERMINE HOW PTEN, WHICH WAS DEFINED BY EXOME SEQUENCING AS A RECURRENTLY MUTATED GENE IN DKO, FUNCTIONALLY RESTRAINS TUMORIGENESIS IN MICE BY ANALYZING KDM6A, TRP53, AND PTEN TRIPLY DEFICIENT MOUSE. THIS PROJECT REQUIRES THE USE OF VERTEBRATE MODELS TO ACCURATELY RECAPITULATE THE NATURAL HISTORY OF CSCC DEVELOPMENT IN THE CONTEXT OF A MAMMALIAN ORGANISM WITH INTACT TUMOR AND IMMUNE MICROENVIRONMENTS. TOGETHER, HUMAN TUMOR STUDIES AND THE VERTEBRATE MODELS WILL MAXIMIZE OUR ABILITY TO DEFINE MECHANISMS OF CSCC TUMORIGENESIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE CELLULAR PROPERTIES AND PATHOGENESIS OF DOUBLE-NULL PROSTATE CANCER - UNLIKE OTHER HUMAN MALIGNANCIES, ACTIVATING ANDROGEN RECEPTOR (AR) MEDIATED SIGNALING PATHWAYS THROUGH THE BINDING OF ANDROGENS IS ESSENTIAL FOR PROSTATE TUMORIGENESIS. ALMOST ALL PRIMARY PROSTATE CANCER CELLS EXPRESS THE AR AND RELY ON ANDROGENS FOR THEIR ONCOGENIC SURVIVAL, GROWTH, AND PROGRESSION. THEREFORE, ANDROGEN DEPRIVATION THERAPY (ADT) THAT DIRECTLY TARGETS ANDROGEN/AR-MEDIATED SIGNALING PATHWAYS IS THE FIRST-LINE TREATMENT FOR ADVANCED PROSTATE CANCER. HOWEVER, ADT EVENTUALLY FAILS IN MOST PATIENTS WHO CONSEQUENTLY DEVELOP CASTRATION-RESISTANT PROSTATE CANCER (CRPC). IN RECENT YEARS, MORE POTENT AR ANTAGONISTS AND INHIBITORS FOR BLOCKING ANDROGEN SYNTHESIS HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED TO INHIBIT THE RE-ACTIVATION OF AR-PROMOTED TUMOR GROWTH VIA RESIDUAL ANDROGENS AND ALTERED AR ACTIVATION. WHILE THESE SECOND-GENERATION ANTAGONISTS AND INHIBITORS SHOWED SOME CLINICAL RESPONSES, RECENT CLINICAL DATA ALSO SUGGESTED THAT THEY CAN INDUCE MORE DIVERSE CRPC PHENOTYPES. SPECIFICALLY, A NEW TYPE OF CRPC, NAMED DOUBLE-NULL PROSTATE CANCER (DNPC), HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED IN PATIENTS TREATED WITH ABIRATERONE (ABI) AND ENZALUTAMIDE (ENZ), FEATURING AR- AND NEUROENDOCRINE (NE)-NULL PROSTATE CANCER CELLS, WHICH DIRECTLY CONTRIBUTES TO THE MORTALITY OF PROSTATE CANCER. THEREFORE, INVESTIGATING THE PATHOGENESIS OF DNPC IS URGENTLY NEEDED FOR DESIGNING EFFECTIVE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES BUILT ON NEW PARADIGMS FOR SAVING LIVES. BY ANALYZING HUMAN CRPC DATA, WE UNCOVERED CURRENT ADT INDUCES ABERRANT ACTIVATION OF HGF AND MET-MEDIATED SIGNALING PATHWAYS, WHICH FURTHER ELEVATES WNT/Â-CATENIN SIGNALING ACTIVATION SPECIFICALLY IN CLINICAL DNPC SAMPLES. USING THE NEW AND CLINICALLY RELEVANT GENETICALLY ENGINEERED MOUSE MODELS (GEMMS), WE DEMONSTRATED FOR THE FIRST TIME THAT ABERRANT CO-ACTIVATION OF HGF/MET AND WNT/Â-CATENIN SIGNALING PATHWAYS INDUCES PROSTATE TUMOR GROWTH AND DNPC DEVELOPMENT. PATHOLOGICAL ANALYSES FURTHER IDENTIFIED DNPC-LIKE CELLS IN THE MOUSE PROSTATE TUMORS. SINGLE-CELL RNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS ALSO SHOWED INCREASED NUCLEAR EXPORTING AND RIBOSOMAL SYNTHESIS SIGNALING PATHWAYS IN MOUSE TUMOR CELLS. IN THIS STUDY, WE PROPOSED THREE SPECIFIC AIMS TO TEST THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT INHIBITING ANDROGEN SIGNALING BY CURRENT ADT (WITH ABI AND ENZ) CAN ACTIVATE HGF/MET AND WNT/Â-CATENIN SIGNALING PATHWAYS TO PROMOTE PROSTATE CANCER CELL GROWTH AND DNPC DEVELOPMENT THROUGH ELEVATING NUCLEAR EXPORTING AND RIBOSOMAL BIOSYNTHESIS AXES USING HUMAN SAMPLES AND OTHER ADVANCED IN VITRO AND IN VIVO APPROACHES AND ANALYSES. DUE TO THE HETEROGENEOUS NATURE OF HUMAN PROSTATE CANCERS AND THE DIFFICULTIES OF OBTAINING PAIRED PATIENT SAMPLES THROUGH ADT DURING DISEASE PROGRESSION, IN THIS STUDY, WE ALSO PLANNED SEVERAL ESSENTIAL AND NECESSARY EXPERIMENTS USING OUR NOVEL AND BIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT GEMMS. THESE EXPERIMENTS ARE FULLY SUPPORTED BY A LARGE BODY OF SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE IN THE FIELD, CANNOT BE DUPLICATED IN VITRO SYSTEMS, AND ALSO CANNOT BE PERFORMED IN PATIENTS. HOWEVER, THEY ARE CLINICALLY RELEVANT AND SCIENTIFICALLY SIGNIFICANT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: USING SURVIVORLINK TO RE-ENGAGE ADULTS IN CANCER CARE AFTER TRANSITION (SURVIVORLINK RE-ACCT) - SURVIVORLINK RE-ACCT- PROJECT SUMMARY FACILITATING THE SUCCESSFUL HEALTHCARE TRANSITION (HCT) OF SURVIVORS FROM THE PEDIATRIC TO ADULT SETTING IS CRITICAL TO THE LONG-TERM HEALTH OF THE GROWING CHILDHOOD CANCER SURVIVOR POPULATION. THE NATIONAL ACADEMY OF MEDICINE AND CHILDREN'S ONCOLOGY GROUP (COG) RECOMMEND LIFELONG RISK-BASED SURVEILLANCE FOR SURVIVORS BECAUSE MANY LATE EFFECTS DO NOT EMERGE UNTIL YEARS AFTER TREATMENT. HOWEVER, MOST YOUNG ADULT SURVIVORS OF CHILDHOOD CANCER (YASCC) NO LONGER ENGAGE IN SURVIVOR CARE AFTER LEAVING THE PEDIATRIC SETTING, DISCONTINUING RISK-BASED SURVEILLANCE AS THEY BECOME INCREASINGLY VULNERABLE TO LATE EFFECTS. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO FACILITATE RE- ENGAGEMENT IN SURVIVOR CARE AMONG YASCC USING THE CANCER SURVIVORLINKTM PLATFORM AS A CRITICAL FOUNDATION FOR A NOVEL MOBILE APPLICATION (APP) TO ADDRESS THE COMPLEX SYSTEM- AND PATIENT-LEVEL BARRIERS EXPERIENCED BY YASCC AFTER HCT. WE PROPOSE TO CO-DESIGN A MOBILE APP WITH YASCC AND CLINICIANS (AIM 1), FOLLOWED BY A RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL (RCT) WITH N=170 YASCC (AIM 2) AND ORGANIZATIONAL READINESS ASSESSMENTS AMONG 20 PEDIATRIC CANCER CENTERS (AIM 3). IN AIM 1, WE WILL ENGAGE IN ITERATIVE CO-DESIGN AND USABILITY TESTING WITH YASCC (N=30) AND CLINICIANS (N=20) TO INFORM ADAPTATIONS TO THE EXISTING SURVIVORLINK APP—FOCUSED ON INFORMATION SHARING—INTO THE NOVEL SURVIVORLINK RE-ACCT MOBILE APP, WHICH WILL ALSO SUPPORT SELF- MANAGEMENT AND DELIVER EDUCATIONAL CONTENT TO AID HCT. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ASSESS THE EFFICACY AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SURVIVORLINK RE-ACCT MOBILE APP THROUGH AN RCT WITH N=170 YASCC (≤29.99 YEARS OLD) WHO ARE TRANSFERRING FROM PEDIATRIC TO ADULT SURVIVOR CARE (E.G., NEXT VISIT TO BE IN ADULT SETTING). EFFICACY OUTCOMES INCLUDE: 1) RE-ENGAGEMENT IN SURVIVOR CARE (I.E., ATTENDANCE AT ≥1 RISK-BASED SURVEILLANCE APPOINTMENT) WITHIN 18 MONTHS POST-DISCHARGE FROM PEDIATRICS, AND 2) PATIENT-REPORTED HEALTH BELIEFS, CANCER COMMUNICATION, SELF-EFFICACY, AND TRANSITION READINESS. IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES INCLUDE: 1) REACH AND 2) PATIENT-LEVEL ADOPTION FROM SURVIVORLINK USAGE DATA OVER 18 MONTHS, AND 3) IMPLEMENTATION ASSESSED BY SURVEYS AND INTERVIEWS TO DETERMINE THE ACCEPTABILITY, FEASIBILITY, AND APPROPRIATENESS OF THE RE-ACCT MOBILE APP. IN AIM 3, WE WILL ASSESS THE READINESS FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SURVIVORLINK HCT MOBILE APP AND IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES FOR DELIVERY THROUGH A MIXED-METHODS STUDY AMONG 20 COG INSTITUTIONS SERVING YASCC. WE WILL ASSESS READINESS FOR IMPLEMENTATION AND DELIVERY CAPACITY IN TERMS OF RESOURCES, OPTIMAL WORKFLOW, AND RECOMMENDED IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES AMONG PEDIATRIC INSTITUTIONS THAT TRANSFER YASCC TO ADULT SURVIVOR CARE. THESE DATA WILL INFORM THE IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES FOR INTERVENTION SITES FOR A FUTURE SCALABILITY TRIAL. OUR APPROACH TO LEVERAGE MOBILE HEALTH TECHNOLOGY TO SUPPORT COMMUNICATION AND CARE NAVIGATION FOLLOWING HCT IN PEDIATRIC ONCOLOGY IS NOVEL, MEETS AN IDENTIFIED NEED, AND CAN BE READILY SCALED FOR USE AT PEDIATRIC CANCER CLINICS NATIONWIDE.

description: THE ROLE OF ERNA M6A MODIFICATION IN LIGAND-INDEPENDENT ER ACTIVATION AND BREAST CANCER PROGRESSION - SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE ROLE OF ERNA M6A MODIFICATION IN LIGAND-INDEPENDENT ER ACTIVATION AND BREAST CANCER PROGRESSION ESTROGENS (E2) AND ESTROGEN RECEPTOR (ERΑ) ARE ESSENTIAL FOR THE NORMAL FUNCTION OF THE MAMMARY GLAND. ABERRANT REGULATION OF ERΑ SIGNALING IS CLOSELY LINKED TO BREAST CANCER PROGRESSION, MAKING ENDOCRINE THERAPIES USING AROMATASE INHIBITORS, TAMOXIFEN, AND FULVESTRANT CRUCIAL FOR TREATING ER+ BREAST CANCER. HOWEVER, DESPITE INITIAL EFFICACY, MANY TUMORS DEVELOP RESISTANCE AND ADVANCE TO A LETHAL METASTATIC STATE. RECENT FINDINGS HIGHLIGHT MUTATIONS IN THE LIGAND-BINDING DOMAIN (LBD) OF THE ERΑ GENE AS SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTORS TO ENDOCRINE RESISTANCE AND METASTATIC PROGRESSION. UNDERSTANDING THE IMPACT OF THESE ERΑ LBD MUTATIONS IS VITAL FOR DEVELOPING NEW THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES FOR AGGRESSIVE BREAST CANCER. N6- METHYLADENOSINE (M6A) MODIFICATION, A COMMON RNA MODIFICATION, PLAYS SIGNIFICANT ROLES IN NORMAL BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES AND CANCER. ALTHOUGH METTL3-CATALYZED M6A MODIFICATION IS KNOWN TO HAVE ONCOGENIC ROLES IN BREAST CANCER, ITS IMPACT ON ERΑ SIGNALING, PARTICULARLY IN ENDOCRINE-RESISTANT BREAST CANCER, REMAINS UNCLEAR. OUR DATA REVEAL THAT PHASE-SEPARATED CONDENSATION OF HORMONE RECEPTORS IS CRITICAL FOR ASSEMBLING ENHANCER TRANSCRIPTIONAL MACHINERY, WITH ERΑ CONDENSATE FORMATION FACILITATED BY M6A MODIFICATION ON ENHANCER RNAS (ERNAS) AND THE NUCLEAR M6A READER YTHDC1. INHIBITING M6A MODIFICATION OR DISRUPTING M6A BINDING TO YTHDC1 LEADS TO THE DISSOLUTION OF ERΑ CONDENSATES, DECREASED CHROMATIN BINDING OF ERΑ AND ITS COFACTORS, AND REDUCED TRANSCRIPTIONAL ACTIVITY. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES ON ENDOCRINE-RESISTANT ERΑ MUTANTS (Y537S AND D538G) SHOW THAT THESE MUTATIONS ENABLE CHROMATIN BINDING AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL ACTIVATION INDEPENDENT OF E2. UNLIKE WILD-TYPE ERΑ, WHICH ONLY FORMS CONDENSATES UPON E2 STIMULATION, THESE CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVE ERΑ MUTANTS FORM CONDENSATES WITHOUT E2. OUR FINDINGS FURTHER DEMONSTRATE THAT INHIBITING M6A MODIFICATION AND DISRUPTING CONDENSATION COULD SUPPRESS THE LIGAND-INDEPENDENT ACTIVATION OF ERΑ MUTANTS, SUGGESTING THAT M6A-MEDIATED ERΑ CONDENSATION DRIVES THE CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVE SIGNALING OBSERVED IN ADVANCED BREAST CANCER. THUS, THESE FINDINGS LEAD US TO PROPOSE AN ERΑ SIGNALING ACTIVATION MODEL LINKING M6A MODIFICATION OF ERNA, ERΑ CONDENSATION, ENHANCER ASSEMBLY, AND TRANSACTIVATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT TARGETING M6A MODIFICATION COULD INHIBIT THE CONSTITUTIVE ACTIVATION OF THESE ERΑ MUTANTS AND OVERCOME BREAST CANCER PROGRESSION. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE PROPOSE THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: 1). DETERMINE THE ROLE OF M6A-ERNAS IN E2-INDEPENDENT ACTIVATION OF ENDOCRINE-RESISTANT ERΑ MUTANTS. 2). ELUCIDATE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH M6A- ERNAS PROMOTE E2-INDPENDENT ENHANCER ACTIVATION. 3). EVALUATE THE POTENTIAL OF TARGETING M6A MODIFICATION AS A THERAPEUTIC APPROACH TO COMBAT CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVE ERΑ SIGNALING AND TUMOR PROGRESSION. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THESE STUDIES WILL HAVE A BROAD IMPACT BY ELUCIDATING THE ROLE OF ERNA M6A MODIFICATION IN ERΑ SIGNALING ACTIVATION AND OFFERING A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY TO TREAT AGGRESSIVE BREAST CANCER BY TARGETING M6A MODIFICATION AND MUTANT ER ENHANCER CONDENSATES TO INHIBIT CONSTITUTIVE ACTIVATION OF MUTANT ERΑ.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNDERSTANDING THE CONTRIBUTION OF TOLL-LIKE RECEPTOR 4 ACTIVITY IN MESENCHYMAL STROMAL CELLS TO CANCER TREATMENT INDUCED SKELETAL MUSCLE DECLINE AND FIBROSIS - SUMMARY ONE OF THE GREAT ACHIEVEMENTS IN MEDICAL SCIENCES IS THE IMPROVED SURVIVAL RATE AMONG CHILDREN DIAGNOSED WITH CANCER. ALTHOUGH ESTIMATES INDICATE THE 5-YEAR SURVIVAL RATE OF CHILDREN DIAGNOSED WITH A MALIGNANCY IS NEAR 80%, MOST OF THESE INDIVIDUALS PRIOR TO THE AGE OF 40 DEMONSTRATE INDICES OF PHYSICAL LIMITATION NORMALLY ASSOCIATED WITH THE ELDERLY POPULATION. AMONG THE INDUCTION REMISSION TREATMENTS RECEIVED BY PEDIATRIC CANCER PATIENTS IS FRACTIONATED X-RAY IRRADIATION, WHICH INDUCES GENOTOXIC STRESS THAT ELIMINATES PROLIFERATIVE CANCER CELLS. HOWEVER, MULTIFARIOUS DIRECT AND INDIRECT EFFECTS OF RADIATION CAN NEGATIVELY IMPACT NORMAL TISSUE GROWTH AND MAINTENANCE ESPECIALLY IN ACTIVELY GROWING POPULATIONS. PHENOTYPES OBSERVED EARLIER IN PEDIATRIC CANCER SURVIVORS IS THE ACCELERATED ONSET OF FRAILTY INDICES SUCH AS MUSCULAR DECLINE. IN A MURINE MODEL, WE FIND WEEKS AFTER IMAGE GUIDED PEDIATRIC FRACTIONATED X-RAY IRRADIATION OF HINDLIMBS DECREASES IN MUSCLE FORCE PRODUCTION, MYOFIBER SIZE, MYONUCLEAR CONTENT AND SKELETAL MUSCLE STEM CELL (SATELLITE CELL) NUMBER. WE ALSO FIND OTHER PHENOTYPES CONSISTENT WITH SKELETAL MUSCLE DECLINE SUCH AS INTRAMUSCULAR FIBROSIS AND AN ELEVATION OF C-C CHEMOKINE RECEPTOR 2 (CCR2) EXPRESSING MONOCYTE/MACROPHAGE CONTENT. THROUGH SCRNASEQ ANALYSIS WE OBSERVE WEEKS AFTER PEDIATRIC FRACTIONATED RADIATION AN INCREASE IN THE EXPRESSION OF THE TOLL-LIKE RECEPTOR 4 (TLR4) LIGAND TENASCIN C (TNC), AND THE TLR4 EFFECTOR MYELOID DIFFERENTIATION PRIMARY RESPONSE 88 (MYD88) IN MESENCHYMAL STROMAL CELLS (MSCS). THIS IS ACCOMPANIED BY ELEVATIONS IN THE EXPRESSION OF TLR4 TARGET GENES MONOCYTE CHEMOATTRACTANT PROTEIN-1/C-C MOTIF CHEMOKINE LIGAND 2 (MCP-1/CCL2) AND THROMBOSPONDIN 1 (THBS1), WHICH RESPECTIVELY CONTRIBUTE TO MONOCYTE/MACROPHAGE RECRUITMENT AND TRANSFORMING GROWTH FACTOR BETA (TGFΒ) SIGNALING AN INHIBITOR OF SATELLITE CELL ACTIVITY, REGULATOR OF VASCULAR ADAPTATION AND EXPRESSION OF ECM FACTORS FROM MSCS. FINALLY, WE FIND OUR MURINE MODEL OF PEDIATRIC RADIATION EFFECTIVELY INDUCES TUMOR REMISSION, HOWEVER, IN THE CONTEXT OF TUMOR TREATMENT EXACERBATES SKELETAL MUSCLE PHENOTYPES. THEREFORE, OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO RIGOROUSLY CHARACTERIZE THE MECHANISMS WHEREBY TREATMENT RELATED EXPRESSION OF THE TLR4 TARGET CCL2, AND TLR4 ACTIVITY IN MSCS CONTRIBUTE TO PEDIATRIC RADIATION RELATED INHIBITION OF SKELETAL MUSCLE GROWTH, FIBROSIS AND INFLAMMATION. IDEALLY, SUCH INSIGHT WOULD BE USED TO UNCOVER INTERVENTIONS TO ATTENUATE PEDIATRIC RADIATION RELATED MUSCULAR DECLINE THAT INCREASES MORBIDITY AND BURDENS SURVIVORS. TO ACCOMPLISH OUR OBJECTIVES, WE WILL UTILIZE, ASSESSMENT OF SKELETAL MUSCLE INTEGRITY, MUSCULAR FUNCTION, IMAGING ANALYSIS, MOUSE GENETICS, SCRNASEQ ANALYSIS, FLOW CYTOMETRY, PROTEIN ANALYSIS, AND PHARMACOLOGICAL TREATMENTS. THE SPECIFIC AIMS OF THIS PROPOSAL ARE 1) DETERMINE IF CELL-SPECIFIC LOSS OF CCL2 OR CCR2, AND 2) EXAMINE WHETHER TLR4 ACTIVITY IN MSCS IMPACTS PEDIATRIC RADIATION AND CANCER TREATMENT RELATED SKELETAL MUSCLE ALTERATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPING MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTIC METHODS FOR CERVICAL CANCER - PROJECT SUMMARY CERVICAL CANCER IS THE FOURTH MOST COMMON CANCER IN WOMEN WORLDWIDE, LEADING TO OVER 300,000 DEATHS EACH YEAR. THE DEATH RATE OF CERVICAL CANCER DECREASED SUBSTANTIALLY IN THE US IN THE TWENTIETH CENTURY, MAINLY DUE TO SUCCESSFUL IMPLEMENTATION OF CERVICAL CANCER SCREENING PROGRAMS BASED ON CERVICAL CYTOLOGY (PAP TEST). HOWEVER, POPULATION SCREENING WITH THE PAP TEST REQUIRES EXTENSIVE CLINICAL EXPERTISE AND INFRASTRUCTURAL SETUP, WHICH ARE LACKING IN LOW-RESOURCE REGIONS. ADDITIONALLY, PAP TESTING MAY NOT BE ACCESSIBLE TO WOMEN WHO ARE UNWILLING OR UNABLE TO PRESENT TO A PROVIDER AND UNDERGO GYNECOLOGIC EXAMINATION FOR TISSUE SAMPLING. OVER 95% OF CERVICAL CANCERS ARE CAUSED BY HUMAN PAPILLOMAVIRUS (HPV) INFECTION. RECENT STUDIES DEMONSTRATE THAT DETECTION OF HIGH-RISK HPV CERVICAL INFECTION IS A MORE EFFECTIVE STRATEGY THAN PAP TESTING FOR EARLY SCREENING OF CERVICAL CANCER. HOWEVER, MOST CLINICALLY APPROVED METHODS FOR HPV DIAGNOSIS ARE BASED ON REAL-TIME PCR PERFORMED AT CENTRAL DIAGNOSTIC LABS, WHICH MAY NOT BE WIDELY ACCESSIBLE TO THE PATIENT POPULATION. TO ADDRESS THIS ISSUE, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A ROBUST LAMP-BASED METHOD FOR HPV SCREENING. LOOP-MEDIATED ISOTHERMAL AMPLIFICATION (LAMP) IS A FAST AND CONVENIENT METHOD TO AMPLIFY AND IDENTIFY THE NUCLEIC ACIDS OF A TARGET PATHOGEN. LAMP WITH COLORIMETRIC READOUT IS PARTICULARLY ATTRACTIVE FOR POINT-OF-CARE DIAGNOSIS OF INFECTIOUS PATHOGENS INCLUDING HPV. THE MAIN OBJECTIVE OF THIS APPLICATION IS TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE LAMP-BASED HPV ASSAY WITH A LARGE PATIENT COHORT. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL PERFORM COMPREHENSIVE RNA-SEQ PROFILING STUDIES TO CHARACTERIZE GENE EXPRESSION CHANGES THAT ARE ASSOCIATED WITH PRECANCEROUS CERVICAL LESIONS. IN THIS WAY, WE EXPECT TO IDENTIFY NOT ONLY MOLECULAR BIOMARKERS THAT COULD BE APPLIED TO THE TRIAGE OF HPV-POSITIVE CASES, BUT ALSO GENE TARGETS THAT ARE KEY TO EARLY DEVELOPMENT OF CERVICAL CANCER FOR POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EFFECTS, METABOLIC MECHANISMS AND PREDICTORS OF RESPONSE TO ACUPUNCTURE IN TREATING PSYCHONEUROLOGICAL SYMPTOMS AMONG BREAST CANCER SURVIVORS - ABSTRACT UP TO 68% OF BREAST CANCER SURVIVORS REPORT A CLUSTER OF CO-OCCURRING PSYCHONEUROLOGICAL SYMPTOMS (PNS), INCLUDING JOINT PAIN, FATIGUE, AND SLEEP DISTURBANCE, DURING AND AFTER LIFE-SAVING TREATMENT WITH ENDOCRINE THERAPY. THESE SYMPTOMS REDUCE QUALITY OF LIFE AND ADVERSELY IMPACT ADHERENCE TO ENDOCRINE THERAPY. ACUPUNCTURE IS A SAFE, HOLISTIC THERAPY KNOWN TO RELIEVE MULTIPLE PNS SYMPTOMS, YET TREATMENT RESPONSES VARY WIDELY. EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT PRIOR TREATMENTS, BASELINE EXPECTANCY FOR ACUPUNCTURE, AND BASELINE PHYSICAL FUNCTION INFLUENCE INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES IN RESPONSE TO TREATMENT. FURTHER, THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH ACUPUNCTURE AFFECTS PNS, EITHER INDIVIDUALLY OR AS A CLUSTER, REMAIN UNCLEAR. IN OUR PILOT STUDY OF 42 BREAST CANCER SURVIVORS WITH PNS, WE CONDUCTED BOTH TARGETED AND UNTARGETED METABOLOMICS OF SERUM SAMPLES DRAWN BEFORE AND AFTER 10 ACUPUNCTURE SESSIONS. THE ANALYSIS REVEALED A SIGNIFICANT DECREASE IN DIMETHYL SULFONE (ALSO KNOWN AS METHYLSULFONYLMETHANE, MSM) AND OXIDIZED GLUTATHIONE (GSSG), ALONG WITH AN INCREASE IN THE GLUTATHIONE (GSH)/GSSG RATIO. CHANGES IN MSM WERE SIGNIFICANTLY CORRELATED WITH IMPROVEMENTS IN THE PNS CLUSTER, PARTICULARLY FOR PAIN AND FATIGUE. FINDINGS SUGGEST THAT MSM IS A POTENTIAL MEDIATOR OF ACUPUNCTURE’S THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS, WITH CRITICAL LINKS BETWEEN OXIDATIVE STRESS AND REDOX BALANCE. THE PROPOSED 3-ARM PHASE III RCT WILL COMPARE THE EFFECTS OF 10 SESSIONS OF ACUPUNCTURE DELIVERED IN 6 WEEKS WITH SHAM ACUPUNCTURE AND USUAL CARE AMONG 252 BREAST CANCER SURVIVORS UNDERGOING ENDOCRINE THERAPY. BLOOD SAMPLES AND SYMPTOM DATA WILL BE COLLECTED THROUGH WEEK 24, THEREBY REFLECTING BOTH THE INITIAL AND LONG-TERM HEALING EFFECTS OF ACUPUNCTURE. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL (1) EVALUATE ACUPUNCTURE’S EFFECT ON THE PNS CLUSTER (PRIMARY OUTCOME) AND ON INDIVIDUAL PNS (SECONDARY OUTCOMES: PAIN, FATIGUE, AND SLEEP DISTURBANCE); (2) EXAMINE THE ROLE OF MSM AS A MEDIATOR OF ACUPUNCTURE’S EFFECTS; AND (3) DETERMINE MULTILEVEL PREDICTORS OF TREATMENT RESPONSE IN THE ACUPUNCTURE GROUP, INCLUDING A) BIOLOGICAL (METABOLOMIC SIGNATURE, AGE); B) CLINICAL (PREVIOUS TREATMENT, SYMPTOMS AT BASELINE) AND C) PSYCHOSOCIAL (TREATMENT EXPECTANCY) CHARACTERISTICS. THIS RESEARCH WILL ULTIMATELY REFINE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE MECHANISM OF ACUPUNCTURE IN TREATING THE PNS CLUSTER AND OFFER A FOUNDATION FOR METABOLOMICS-DRIVEN PRECISION TREATMENTS. RESULTS OF THIS STUDY WILL HELP TO REDUCE SYMPTOM BURDEN, ENHANCE SURVIVORSHIP CARE, AND PROMOTE PRECISION ACUPUNCTURE TREATMENT FOR ALL BREAST CANCER SURVIVORS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPROVING CANCER AND TOBACCO CESSATION CARE FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS - SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS (SMI) INCLUDING SCHIZOPHRENIA, BIPOLAR DISORDER, AND SEVERE MAJOR DEPRESSION AFFECTS MORE THAN 15 MILLION U.S. ADULTS WHO DIE 15-25 YEARS EARLIER THAN THE GENERAL POPULATION. MORE THAN 50% OF ADULTS WITH SMI SMOKE4; SMOKING-RELATED ILLNESSES ACCOUNT FOR >70% OF THAT MORTALITY GAP. ADULTS WITH SMI ARE LESS LIKELY TO RECEIVE TOBACCO CESSATION TREATMENT AND GUIDELINE-CONCORDANT CANCER CARE AND 2-4 TIMES MORE LIKELY TO DIE FROM MANY COMMON CANCERS. DIAGNOSTIC DELAYS AND DIFFERENCES IN CANCER TREATMENT CONTRIBUTE TO POOR CANCER SURVIVAL. PATIENT, CLINICIAN, AND SYSTEMS FACTORS IMPACT CANCER OUTCOMES: HIGH SMOKING RATES CAN INCREASE CANCER RECURRENCE; UNTREATED PSYCHIATRIC ILLNESS CAN IMPAIR PROGNOSTIC UNDERSTANDING, AND INADEQUATE ACCESS TO CARE. CLINICIANS LACK CROSS-DISCIPLINARY TRAINING, PSYCHO-ONCOLOGY SERVICES REMAIN INADEQUATE, AND CLINICAL TRIALS EXCLUDE PATIENTS WITH SMI. THE TIME OF CANCER DIAGNOSIS IS A CRITICAL OPPORTUNITY TO IMPROVE CANCER CARE DELIVERY AND OUTCOMES FOR ALL PATIENTS WITH SMI. EARLY, INTEGRATED MENTAL HEALTH CARE PROTECTS AGAINST CANCER CARE DISRUPTIONS FOR PEOPLE WITH SMI, HOWEVER, MANY PATIENTS WITH SMI LACK MENTAL HEALTH CARE. COLLABORATIVE CARE IMPROVES DEPRESSION COST-EFFECTIVELY FOR PATIENTS WITH CANCER BUT HAS EXCLUDED PATIENTS WITH SMI. WE DEVELOPED AND PILOTED BRIDGE, PERSON-CENTERED COLLABORATIVE CARE FOR SMI AND CANCER. WE COMPLETED THE FIRST RANDOMIZED TRIAL (N=120) FOR SMI AND A NEW CANCER. BRIDGE WAS FEASIBLE (85% CONSENTED) AND DELIVERED REMOTELY DURING THE PANDEMIC. COMPARED TO ENHANCED USUAL CARE (EUC), PATIENTS ON BRIDGE HAD FEWER CANCER CARE DISRUPTIONS (TREATMENT DELAYS, DEVIATIONS FROM GUIDELINE-CONCORDANT CANCER CARE, TREATMENT INTERRUPTIONS; 17% VS. 35%, P<.035) AND DECREASED PSYCHIATRIC ILLNESS SEVERITY. WE CONDUCTED A 2-SITE RCT THAT FOUND THAT ADULTS WITH SMI CAN BENEFIT FROM VIRTUAL TOBACCO CESSATION COUNSELING BEGINNING AT CANCER DIAGNOSIS. ONE CRITICAL NEXT STEP IS INCREASING REACH TO COMMUNITY SETTINGS. GUIDED BY A STAKEHOLDER COALITION, WE NOW PROPOSE A HYBRID TYPE I EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION TRIAL OF BRIDGE-FREE WHICH INTEGRATES TOBACCO CESSATION INTO PERSON-CENTERED COLLABORATIVE CARE ACROSS THE MGH AND DANA-FARBER NETWORKS (N=248). WE WILL DETERMINE THE IMPACT ON CANCER CARE DISRUPTIONS, TOBACCO CESSATION, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL OUTCOMES AND IDENTIFY BARRIERS TO IMPLEMENTATION. THE OVERARCHING GOAL IS TO INFORM SCALABLE APPROACHES THAT ADDRESS MODIFIABLE CAUSES OF PREMATURE CANCER MORTALITY.

description: MUTATIONAL EPIDEMIOLOGY OF CHILDHOOD ACUTE LYMPHOBLASTIC LEUKEMIA IN CALIFORNIA - ABSTRACT ACUTE LYMPHOBLASTIC LEUKEMIA (ALL) IS THE MOST COMMON CHILDHOOD MALIGNANCY AND, DESPITE HIGH CURE RATES IN DEVELOPED COUNTRIES, IT REMAINS A LEADING CAUSE OF CHILDHOOD MORTALITY. MOREOVER, SURVIVORS OF CHILDHOOD ALL FACE LONG-TERM TREATMENT-RELATED MORBIDITIES. THUS, PREVENTION OF ALL REMAINS AN IMPORTANT GOAL; HOWEVER, THERE ARE FEW KNOWN MODIFIABLE RISK FACTORS. THE RISING INCIDENCE OF CHILDHOOD ALL, PARTICULARLY AMONG HISPANIC/LATINO CHILDREN, SUGGESTS A ROLE FOR COMMON ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES. CASE-CONTROL STUDIES HAVE IDENTIFIED SEVERAL ENVIRONMENTAL RISK FACTORS FOR CHILDHOOD ALL, BUT THESE HAVE LARGELY RELIED ON QUESTIONNAIRE DATA AND, THUS, MAY BE PRONE TO RECALL BIAS. RECENT POPULATION-BASED GEOSPATIAL STUDIES REPORTED SIGNIFICANT ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES TO AIR POLLUTION, PESTICIDES, AND ULTRAVIOLET (UV) RADIATION AND RISK OF ALL, ALTHOUGH THEY PROVIDE NO INSIGHTS INTO BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS. WE PROPOSE TO ADDRESS THESE SHORTCOMINGS THROUGH “MUTATIONAL EPIDEMIOLOGY”, A PROMISING APPROACH THAT COMBINES STUDYING PATTERNS OF TUMOR MUTATIONS WITH EPIDEMIOLOGICAL ANALYSES TO ELUCIDATE THE CAUSES OF CANCER. WHILE MUTATIONAL EPIDEMIOLOGY STUDIES OF ADULT CANCERS HAVE LED TO NOVEL DISCOVERIES, THIS APPROACH HAS YET TO BE APPLIED TO CHILDHOOD LEUKEMIA. TWO MAJOR PATTERNS OF SOMATIC MUTATIONS ARE DETECTABLE IN CHILDHOOD ALL: I) SINGLE-BASE SUBSTITUTION (SBS) MUTATIONAL SIGNATURES RELATED TO APOBEC MUTAGENESIS, REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES (ROS), AND UV RADIATION; AND II) DELETIONS MEDIATED BY “OFF- TARGET” RECOMBINATION-ACTIVATING GENE (RAG) RECOMBINATION; YET THE ETIOLOGIES OF THESE PATTERNS ARE LARGELY UNKNOWN. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE CALIFORNIA CHILDHOOD LEUKEMIA STUDY (CCLS), IN WHICH WE HAVE ACCESS TO AVAILABLE DIAGNOSTIC LEUKEMIA (TUMOR) AND GERMLINE SAMPLES AS WELL AS RICH EPIDEMIOLOGICAL DATA, INCLUDING RESIDENTIAL HISTORY, QUESTIONNAIRE DATA, AND OMICS DATA, FROM 630 CHILDHOOD ALL PATIENTS OF WHICH ~50% ARE HISPANIC/LATINO. THROUGH OUR INNOVATIVE AND COLLABORATIVE APPROACH, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT WE WILL IDENTIFY RISK FACTORS FOR THE SOMATIC MUTATIONAL PATTERNS IN CHILDHOOD ALL. IN OUR FIRST AIM, WE WILL INVESTIGATE RISK FACTORS FOR OFF-TARGET RAG RECOMBINATION THROUGH TUMOR-NORMAL WHOLE-GENOME SEQUENCING (WGS) OF 630 CHILDHOOD ALL PATIENTS. WE WILL EXPAND UPON OUR PRIOR DISCOVERY OF AN ASSOCIATION BETWEEN EARLY-LIFE TOBACCO SMOKE EXPOSURE AND RAG-MEDIATED DELETIONS IN ALL TO A LARGER SET OF PATIENTS AND EXAMINE THE POTENTIAL ROLE OF AIR POLLUTION (FROM GEOSPATIAL MODELS) AND EARLY-LIFE INFECTIONS. IN OUR SECOND AIM, WE WILL ANALYZE TUMOR MUTATIONAL SIGNATURES IN THE 630 PATIENTS, FOCUSING ON THE APOBEC, ROS, AND UV SBS SIGNATURES, AND INVESTIGATE ASSOCIATIONS WITH SPECIFIC EXPOSURES OF INTEREST, INCLUDING EARLY-LIFE INFECTIONS, AIR POLLUTION, PESTICIDES OF INTEREST, AND UV RADIATION. FINALLY, IN OUR THIRD AIM, WE WILL INVESTIGATE WHETHER GENETIC VARIATION IS ASSOCIATED WITH RAG-MEDIATED DELETIONS AND MUTATIONAL SIGNATURES AND IF GENETIC VARIANTS MODERATE THE EFFECTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES ON SOMATIC MUTATIONAL PATTERNS. OUR INNOVATIVE MUTATIONAL EPIDEMIOLOGY STUDY OF CHILDHOOD ALL WILL FURTHER OUR UNDERSTANDING OF ITS CAUSES, HIGHLIGHT NOVEL AVENUES OF PREVENTION, AND INFORM FUTURE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL STUDIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMAGING-COMPUTATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR GUIDING TREATMENT OF HGG: AN OHSV CLINICAL TRIAL - PROJECT SUMMARY  THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO INTEGRATE MOLECULAR AND FUNCTIONAL IMAGING WITH COMPUTATIONAL MODELING TO GUIDE TREATMENT PLANNING TO OPTIMIZE TUMOR RESPONSE FOR PATIENTS WITH HIGH GRADE GLIOMAS (HGGS) TREATED WITH INTRATUMORALLY DELIVERED NOVEL ONCOLYTIC HERPES SIMPLEX VIRUS (OHSV) IMMUNOTHERAPY. HGGS, INCLUDING GLIOBLASTOMAS (GBMS), ARE HIGHLY HETEROGENOUS, AND PATIENTS HAVE DIRE OUTCOMES WITH LOW RATES OF SURVIVAL. THIS IS PARTIALLY DUE TO TUMOR HETEROGENEITY AND RESISTANCE TO CURRENTLY AVAILABLE TREATMENT STRATEGIES. LEVERAGING AN ONGOING FDA-APPROVED NOVEL CLINICAL TRIAL, NCT03657576, WE CAN APPLY ADVANCED, CLINICALLY RELEVANT IMAGING TO GUIDE AND PREDICT EARLY RESPONSE TO AN INTRATUMORALLY INJECTED NOVEL OHSV IN COMBINATION WITH STANDARD-OF-CARE THERAPIES. PET AND MRI SIMULTANEOUSLY CAN PROVIDE BIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT INFORMATION ON HYPOXIA, AMINO ACID UTILIZATION, CELLULARITY, AND PERFUSION THAT CAN GUIDE PLACEMENT OF INTRATUMORAL CATHETERS, IDENTIFY FACTORS INTRATUMOR HETEROGENEITY, AND INFORM MATHEMATICAL MODELS THAT CAN COMPUTATIONALLY PREDICT FORWARD THE GROWTH OF THE TUMOR. WE POSIT THAT PET/MRI CAN DEFINE THE REGIONAL TUMOR BIOLOGY TO DIRECT THE SITES OF OHSV ADMINISTRATION AND PROVIDE AN EARLIER ASSESSMENT OF RESPONSE THAN CONVENTIONAL IMAGING. OUR INITIAL CLINICALLY TRIAL WITH THIS OHSV SIGNIFICANTLY EXTENDED THE SURVIVAL IN PATIENTS WITH RECURRENT HGG COMPARED TO STANDARD-OF-CARE. FURTHER, WITH MULTIPARAMETRIC MRI, WE IDENTIFIED THAT TUMORS WITH LOWER PERFUSION IN AREAS OF HIGH CELLULARITY HAD DECREASED SURVIVAL. THESE COMPLIMENTARY PIECES OF DATA PROVIDE RATIONALE TO EXPAND THE OHSV CLINICAL TRIAL TO INCLUDE PET/MRI WHICH WILL USE FET-PET TO IDENTIFY BIOLOGICAL TUMOR VOLUME (BTV) DURING THE COURSE OF THERAPY IN ADDITION TO FMISO-PET TO EVALUATE REGIONS OF HYPOXIA FOR CATHETER PLACEMENT. FURTHERMORE, WE PROPOSE PAIRING THE PET/MRI DATA WITH AN IMAGE-BASED COMPUTATIONAL MODEL TO OPTIMIZE, ON A PATIENT-SPECIFIC BASIS, CATHETER SELECTION FOR ENHANCED DELIVERY STRATEGY AND PREDICTING THE TUMOR RECURRENCE. OUR STUDY WILL BE THE FIRST TO ASSESS THE ABILITY OF QUANTITATIVE FET/FMISO- PET/MRI TO GUIDE AN INTERVENTIONAL STRATEGY, AND PAIRED WITH COMPUTATIONAL MODELING, TO MONITOR AND PREDICT CHANGES IN HGGS. WE WILL TEST THIS THROUGH THE FOLLOWING AIMS: AIM 1) UTILIZE PRE-TREATMENT IMAGING FEATURES TO GUIDE LOCATION OF CATHETER PLACEMENT FOR INTRA-CRANIAL INJECTION OF OHSV AND BIOLOGICALLY VALIDATE DISTINCT TUMOR HABITATS; AIM 2) QUANTIFY LONGITUDINAL PET/MRI METRICS THAT HAVE FAVORABLE RESPONSE TO OHSV.; AIM 3) USE AN IMAGE-BASED COMPUTATIONAL MODEL TO PREDICT THE SPATIO-TEMPORAL RESPONSE AND GUIDE WHICH CATHETERS SHOULD BE UTILIZED FOR SUBSEQUENT INJECTIONS OHSV-IOT. NEW METHODS FOR PREDICTING AND OPTIMIZING RESPONSES FOR HGG ARE DESPERATELY NEEDED. OUR PROJECT WILL DEVELOP RIGOROUS—BUT PRACTICAL— APPROACHES TO OPTIMIZE A NOVEL OHSV INTERVENTION FOR HGG. THIS PARADIGM IS ADAPTABLE TO MULTICENTER TRIALS AND OTHER IMMUNE- AND SPATIALLY-DIRECTED THERAPIES FOR BRAIN TUMORS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: THE MEDICAL UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH CAROLINA

description: NEURAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL MECHANISMS OF CISPLATIN OTOTOXICITY - PROJECT SUMMARY CISPLATIN IS A WIDELY USED AND POTENTIALLY LIFE-SAVING CHEMOTHERAPY, HOWEVER, CISPLATIN ACCUMULATES IN THE COCHLEA WITH CONTINUED TREATMENT LEADING TO IRREVERSIBLE HEARING LOSS. CISPLATIN-INDUCED HEARING LOSS IMPOSES SIGNIFICANT MEDICAL, PSYCHOLOGICAL, FINANCIAL, AND LIFESTYLE BURDENS ON MANY CANCER SURVIVORS. ALTHOUGH SODIUM THIOSULFATE OTOPROTECTIVE THERAPY PROVIDES PARTIAL PROTECTION IN ELIGIBLE YOUNG PATIENTS, COMPROMISED CHEMOTHERAPEUTIC ACTIVITY REMAINS A MAJOR LIMITATION. TARGETED OTOPROTECTIVE THERAPIES THAT DO NOT INTERFERE WITH CISPLATIN ANTICANCER ACTIVITY ARE NEEDED. TO REALIZE THIS GOAL, WE SEEK TO BETTER DEFINE THE MOST CRITICAL CELLULAR TARGETS OF CISPLATIN IN THE COCHLEA, WHICH IS COMPLICATED DUE TO ITS BROAD GENOTOXIC EFFECTS. RECENT FINDINGS, INCLUDING OUR PRELIMINARY DATA, DEMONSTRATE THAT CISPLATIN OTOTOXICITY EXTENDS BEYOND THE WELL-CHARACTERIZED LOSS OF OUTER HAIR CELLS (OHC), AND MAY RELATE TO DAMAGE IN NEURAL AND OTHER CELL TYPES. NOTABLY, WE FIND SIGNIFICANT CHANGES IN LOW-FREQUENCY AUDITORY BRAINSTEM RESPONSES (ABR) THAT ARE NOT EXPLAINED BY OHC LOSS IN CORRESPONDING COCHLEAR REGIONS. COMPLEMENTARY FUNCTIONAL, TRANSCRIPTIONAL, AND PATHOLOGICAL FINDINGS INDICATE NEURAL INJURY PROCESSES IN THESE REGIONS AND WE THEREFORE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CISPLATIN DISRUPTS CHROMATIN ACCESSIBILITY AND GENE EXPRESSION IN COCHLEAR CELLS, LEADING TO DISRUPTED AUDITORY NEURAL FUNCTION INDEPENDENT OF SENSORY LOSS ALONE. TO TEST THIS, WE WILL EVALUATE CISPLATIN’S EFFECTS ON NEW ASPECTS OF AUDITORY NERVE FUNCTION ALONGSIDE HISTOPATHOLOGY AND EPIGENETIC AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC STUDIES. MOUSE MODELS PROVIDE ACCESS TO INNER EAR TISSUES, A FUNCTIONAL HEARING SYSTEM, AND CAREFULLY CONTROLLED CONDITIONS FOR RIGOROUS MECHANISTIC STUDIES, CAPABILITIES NOT AVAILABLE IN HUMAN AND ALTERNATIVE MODELS. AIM 1 WILL CHARACTERIZE CELL-SPECIFIC CISPLATIN INSULTS AT THE GENOMIC LEVEL BY SINGLE-NUCLEUS MULTIOMIC PROFILING. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS AUDITORY FUNCTION DURING THE COURSE OF CISPLATIN TREATMENT AND STUDY THE PROGRESSION OF PATHOLOGICAL CHANGES. THESE STUDIES WILL IDENTIFY CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR TARGETS OF CISPLATIN IN THE COCHLEA, WITH A FOCUS ON NEURAL INJURY. FINDINGS WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF TARGETED OTOPROTECTIVE THERAPIES TO FURTHER PREVENT HEARING LOSS WITHOUT INTERFERING WITH CHEMOTHERAPEUTIC ACTIVITY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: RUTGERS THE STATE UNIVERSITY OF NEW JERSEY

description: CHARACTERIZING THE ROLE OF AIR POLLUTION IN BREAST CANCER PROGNOSIS AND SURVIVORSHIP - PROJECT SUMMARY BLACK WOMEN DIAGNOSED WITH BREAST CANCER (BC) EXPERIENCE HIGHER MORTALITY RATES, GREATER CARDIOMETABOLIC BURDEN, AND WORSE SURVIVORSHIP OUTCOMES COMPARED TO WHITE WOMEN. THEY ARE ALSO MORE LIKELY TO LIVE IN AREAS WITH HIGHER EXPOSURE TO OUTDOOR AIR POLLUTION, WHICH HAS BEEN CLASSIFIED AS CARCINOGENIC IN HUMANS BY THE INTERNATIONAL AGENCY FOR RESEARCH ON CANCER AND IS LINKED TO INFLAMMATION, CARDIOTOXICITY, IMPAIRED QUALITY OF LIFE, CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, AND MORTALITY. BECAUSE EXPOSURE TO AIR POLLUTION IS UBIQUITOUS, UNAVOIDABLE, AND MORE PREVALENT IN SOCIOECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES, IT REPRESENTS AN IMPORTANT YET UNDERSTUDIED CONTRIBUTOR TO DIFFERENCES IN BC OUTCOMES. DESPITE BIOLOGICAL PLAUSIBILITY AND EMERGING EVIDENCE, THE LONG-TERM ASSOCIATIONS OF AIR POLLUTION WITH SURVIVAL, PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES (PROS), AND BIOMARKERS OF SYSTEMIC HEALTH IN BLACK BC SURVIVORS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS, WE WILL LEVERAGE THE WOMEN’S CIRCLE OF HEALTH FOLLOW-UP STUDY (WCHFS), A WELL-CHARACTERIZED, POPULATION-BASED COHORT OF 1,900 BLACK BC SURVIVORS IN NEW JERSEY WITH DETAILED DATA ON CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS, LIFESTYLE, AREA-BASED FACTORS, STRUCTURAL FACTORS,, AND BIOSPECIMENS. THIS PROJECT WILL EVALUATE WHETHER LONG-TERM RESIDENTIAL OUTDOOR AIR POLLUTION EXPOSURE ADVERSELY IMPACTS SURVIVAL, PROS, AND BIOMARKERS OF INFLAMMATION AND CARDIAC INJURY IN THIS DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTED POPULATION. THIS STUDY IS DESIGNED TO PURSUE THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) ASSESS ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN CUMULATIVE RESIDENTIAL AIR POLLUTION EXPOSURE AND BC-SPECIFIC AND ALL-CAUSE SURVIVAL; (2) EVALUATE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN AIR POLLUTION AND PROS, INCLUDING HEALTH-RELATED QUALITY OF LIFE (HRQOL), FATIGUE, AND SLEEP DISTURBANCE, MEASURED APPROXIMATELY TWO YEARS POST-DIAGNOSIS; AND (3) EXAMINE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN AIR POLLUTION AND BIOMARKERS OF SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION (HSCRP, IL-6, IL-1Β, TNF-Α) AND CARDIAC INJURY (HS-CTNT, NT-PROBNP) MEASURED TWO TO THREE YEARS POST-DIAGNOSIS. OUTDOOR AIR POLLUTION WILL BE ESTIMATED FROM SPATIOTEMPORAL MODELS YIELDING PREDICTIONS IN 1KM GRIDS (PARTICULATE MATTER WITHIN 2.5 MICRONS IN DIAMETER (PM2.5), NITROGEN DIOXIDE (NO2), PARTICULATE MATTER TRACE ELEMENTS, AND PARTICULATE MATTER COMPONENTS). THESE GRIDDED ESTIMATES WILL BE LINKED TO RESIDENTIAL ADDRESS HISTORIES OF STUDY PARTICIPANTS TO EXAMINE TIME-VARYING EXPOSURE WINDOWS. WE WILL APPLY ADVANCED MIXTURES-BASED STATISTICAL APPROACHES TO EVALUATE THE JOINT IMPACTS OF MULTIPLE POLLUTANTS AND WILL EVALUATE EFFECT MODIFICATION OF PRIMARY ANALYSES BY INDIVIDUAL AND NEIGHBORHOOD- LEVEL STRUCTURAL AND AREA-BASED FACTORS. BY INTEGRATING AIR POLLUTION EXPOSURES WITH CLINICAL, EPIDEMIOLOGIC, PRO, AND BIOMARKER INFORMATION IN A LARGE, WELL-CHARACTERIZED COHORT OF BLACK BC SURVIVORS, THIS PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY MODIFIABLE ENVIRONMENTAL CONTRIBUTORS TO DIFFERENCES IN CANCER OUTCOMES. FINDINGS WILL PROVIDE AN EVIDENCE BASE TO INFORM SURVIVORSHIP CARE, CLINICAL GUIDELINES, AND PUBLIC HEALTH STRATEGIES, WITH THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF IMPROVING OUTCOMES FOR CANCER SURVIVORS.

description: UNDERSTANDING THE ONCOGENIC FUNCTIONS OF ENL AND AF9 FOR BETTER LEUKEMIA THERAPIES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ACUTE MYELOID AND LYMPHOID LEUKEMIAS (AML AND ALL) ARISE BECAUSE OF A BLOCK IN HEMATOPOIETIC DIFFERENTIATION OFTEN DUE TO MUTATIONS IN EPIGENETIC REGULATORS. EPIGENETIC PROTEINS DEPOSIT, REMOVE AND READ CHEMICAL MODIFICATIONS ON GENOMIC REGULATORY ELEMENTS THAT IMPACT GENE EXPRESSION AND ARE COMMONLY MISREGULATED IN CANCER, INCLUDING 70% OF AML PATIENTS. MLL (KMT2A) IS AN EPIGENETIC WRITER THAT IS COMMONLY TRANSLOCATED IN AML PATIENTS AND ASSOCIATED WITH A DISMAL PROGNOSIS (~29% 5-YEAR EFS) NECESSITATING BETTER THERAPIES. MLL TRANSLOCATIONS FUSE THE N-TERMINUS OF MLL WITH THE C-TERMINUS OF A PARTNER PROTEIN. TWO OF THE MOST COMMON TRANSLOCATION PARTNERS ARE THE HIGHLY HOMOLOGOUS PROTEINS ENL AND AF9. BOTH PROTEINS BIND CHROMATIN THROUGH A YEATS DOMAIN AND ASSOCIATE WITH THE SUPER ELONGATION COMPLEX (SEC) OR THE EPIGENETIC DOT1L COMPLEX THROUGH AN ANC1 HOMOLOGY DOMAIN (AHD). HOWEVER, ENL IS CRITICALLY REQUIRED IN LEUKEMIC CELLS WHILE AF9 IS DISPENSABLE. WE CHARACTERIZED UNIQUE TRANSLOCATION EVENTS IN MLL::ENL AND MLL::AF9 PATIENTS SUCH THAT DIFFERENT DOMAINS ARE RETAINED OR LOST IN RESULTANT MLL::ENL AND MLL::AF9 FUSION PROTEINS. IMPORTANTLY, WE FOUND THAT WHILE THE AHD WAS INVARIABLY RETAINED IN ALL MLL::ENL AND MLL::AF9 PATIENTS, THE AHD OF ENL AND AF9 POSSESS DIFFERENT ONCOGENICITY. OUR BIOCHEMICAL ANALYSIS FOUND THAT THE AHD OF AF9 BINDS MORE TIGHTLY TO DOT1L THAN ENL. AMONG THE 12 AMINO ACIDS THAT DIFFERENTIATE THE ENL AND AF9 AHD, WE FOUND A SINGLE AMINO ACID ON AF9 THAT DIFFERENTIATES AF9 AND ENL BINDING TO DOT1L. FURTHER, WE HAVE DEVELOPED NOVEL COMPOUNDS THAT BIND TO THE ENL/AF9 AHD LEADING TO IMPAIRED CELL GROWTH. IMPORTANTLY, THE IMPLICATIONS OF THE BIOCHEMICAL DIFFERENCES BETWEEN ENL AND AF9 AND WHETHER THEY INFLUENCE PATIENT THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE IS NOT UNDERSTOOD. WE DISCOVERED THAT FUSION OF ONLY THE AHD IS SUFFICIENT FOR MLL::AF9 LEUKEMIA, BUT INSUFFICIENT FOR MLL::ENL LEUKEMIA. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO UNDERSTAND HOW BIOCHEMICAL DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THE AHD OF ENL AND AF9 IMPACT MLL FUSION LEUKEMOGENESIS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT DIFFERENTIAL AHD AFFINITY FOR THE SEC AND DOT1L COMPLEXES BETWEEN AF9 AND ENL AFFECTS MLL::FUSION MEDIATED ACTIVATION OF LEUKEMIA GENE PROGRAMS AND LEUKEMOGENESIS AND IS AN IDEAL THERAPEUTIC TARGET FOR AML. WE WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING AIMS. (1) DETERMINE HOW THE AHD OF ENL AND AF9 AFFECT MLL::ENL AND MLL::AF9 MEDIATED EPIGENETIC AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL OUTPUT. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE FUSION OF THE AHD OF ENL OR AF9 TO MLL WILL INDUCE UNIQUE EPIGENETIC LANDSCAPES AND TRANSCRIPTION. WE WILL TEST GENOME WIDE CHROMATIN CONDENSATION, EPIGENETIC REPROGRAMMING AND EPIGENETIC COMPLEX LOCALIZATION. (2) EXAMINE HOW AHD STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES IMPACT PROTEIN INTERACTIONS WITH ENL AND AF9. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT NON-CONSERVED RESIDUAL DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THE ENL AND AF9 AHD DICTATE BINDING TO PARTNER PROTEINS. WE WILL USE MUTAGENESIS TO IDENTIFY CRITICAL AMINO ACID DIFFERENCES IMPACTING BINDING AFFINITY AND LEUKEMIC POTENTIAL. (3) ASSESS THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF TARGETING AHD IN MLL REARRANGED LEUKEMIA. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT TARGETING THE AHD WITH DEGRADER MOLECULES WILL DISPLAY ANTITUMOR ACTIVITY FOR MLL-FUSION LEUKEMIAS AND AML IN GENERAL. WE USE MOUSE MODELS THAT PROVIDE AN IN VIVO SYSTEM THAT ACCURATELY REFLECTS MLL::FUSION PATIENT SURVIVAL. IN VIVO STUDIES UTILIZE MOUSE MODELS DRIVEN SOLELY BY MLL::FUSION PROTEINS, WHICH ARE IDEAL FOR MECHANISTIC STUDIES. WE ALSO USE MOUSE SYNGENEIC MODELS AND HUMAN LEUKEMIA CELL XENOGRAFTS TO EVALUATE THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CFDNA FRAGMENTOMES FOR NON-INVASIVE EARLY DETECTION OF HCC - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA (HCC) IS A LEADING CAUSE OF CANCER MORTALITY, WITH OVER 60% OF PATIENTS DIAGNOSED AT ADVANCED STAGES, RESULTING IN A 5-YEAR SURVIVAL RATE BELOW 20%. EARLY DETECTION SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVES SURVIVAL RATES, BUT CURRENT SURVEILLANCE TOOLS LIKE ALPHA-FETOPROTEIN (AFP) AND ULTRASOUND ARE INADEQUATE, ESPECIALLY FOR AFP-NEGATIVE TUMORS. THIS STUDY AIMS TO DEVELOP A MULTIMODAL BLOOD-BASED CLASSIFIER FOR EARLY HCC DETECTION BY INTEGRATING GENOME-WIDE METHODS WE HAVE CREATED, INCLUDING FRAGMENTOMICS (DELFI), REPEAT LANDSCAPES (ARTEMIS), METHYLOMICS, MUTATIONAL SIGNATURES (GEMINI), AND PLASMA PROTEOMICS INTO A SINGLE MACHINE LEARNING CLASSIFIER. THE PROPOSED APPROACH WILL BE TESTED USING PLASMA SAMPLES FROM TWO COHORTS: THE DTECT LIVER STUDY FROM VIETNAM INCLUDES HCC PATIENTS AND AT-RISK CONTROLS, WHILE THE STOP-HCC STUDY FROM VIETNAM AND SAUDI ARABIA INVOLVES HIGH-RISK PATIENTS UNDER SEMI-ANNUAL SURVEILLANCE. VIETNAM AND SAUDI ARABIA HAVE LARGE POPULATIONS WITH CHRONIC LIVER DISEASE, ALLOWING TIMELY ACCRUAL OF EARLY-STAGE AND AFP-NEGATIVE HCC CASES THAT WOULD BE IMPRACTICAL AND MORE COSTLY TO ACHIEVE IN THE US, WHILE REPRESENTING DISEASE ETIOLOGIES RELEVANT TO US PATIENTS. IMPORTANTLY, THESE COLLABORATIONS DIRECTLY BENEFIT THE US BY ENABLING DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A MORE GENERALIZABLE HCC SURVEILLANCE TEST FOR US POPULATIONS, INCLUDING THOSE AFFECTED BY HBV, HCV, AND NAFLD-ASSOCIATED LIVER DISEASE. SPECIFIC AIMS INCLUDE EXAMINING GENOME-WIDE CHANGES IN CFDNA AND TISSUE, DEVELOPING A MULTIMODAL PLASMA CLASSIFIER, AND VALIDATING ITS PERFORMANCE IN AN INDEPENDENT COHORT. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT GENOME-WIDE CFDNA FRAGMENTATION PROFILES (DELFI) AND REPEAT LANDSCAPES (ARTEMIS) CAN DISTINGUISH HCC PATIENTS FROM CONTROLS WITH HIGH SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY. THE INTEGRATION OF THESE FEATURES WITH METHYLOMICS AND PROTEOMICS IS EXPECTED TO ENHANCE EARLY DETECTION, PARTICULARLY FOR AFP NEGATIVE TUMORS. THE STUDY ALSO EXPLORES THE POTENTIAL OF GENOME-WIDE MUTATIONAL SIGNATURES (GEMINI) AND CFDNA FRAGMENT END POSITIONS AS SURROGATE MEASURES OF DNA METHYLATION. THIS APPROACH HAS BROAD CLINICAL APPLICATIONS IN CANCER SCREENING, EARLY DIAGNOSIS, AND DISEASE MONITORING, POTENTIALLY REDUCING CANCER MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY, ESPECIALLY IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. BY LEVERAGING ESTABLISHED INTERNATIONAL SURVEILLANCE COHORTS WHILE PERFORMING ADVANCED ASSAY DEVELOPMENT AND COMPUTATIONAL ANALYSES IN THE US, THIS PROJECT WILL ACCELERATE A US-LED, SCALABLE APPROACH TO HCC SURVEILLANCE. THE SUCCESS OF THIS APPROACH COULD TRANSFORM HCC SURVEILLANCE, MAKING IT MORE SENSITIVE, ACCESSIBLE, AND SCALABLE ACROSS POPULATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEFINING AND TARGETING MECHANISMS OF THE NEUROLYSIN-KIF11-WNT3A AXIS DRIVING THERAPY RESISTANCE IN PROSTATE CANCER - DESPITE ADVANCES IN TARGETED THERAPIES, RAPID RESISTANCE REMAINS A MAJOR CAUSE OF POOR OUTCOMES IN ADVANCED PROSTATE CANCER (PCA), PARTICULARLY FOLLOWING TREATMENTS TARGETING THE ANDROGEN RECEPTOR (AR) SIGNALING AXIS. THIS HIGHLIGHTS THE URGENT NEED TO DEFINE HOW PCA CELLS ADAPT TO AR-TARGETED THERAPEUTIC STRESS AND IDENTIFY ACTIONABLE VULNERABILITIES. A KEY UNRESOLVED QUESTION IS WHETHER PCA CELLS CAN AUTONOMOUSLY REMODEL THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT (TME) TO UNDERMINE THERAPEUTIC ACTIVITY. WE DEMONSTRATED THAT PCA CELLS EXPLOIT NEUROLYSIN, A REGULATOR OF NEURONAL SIGNALING, TO COUNTER AR-TARGETED THERAPIES. NEUROLYSIN DEFICIENCY, OBSERVED IN 30% OF PCA CASES, INDUCES ECTOPIC WNT3A EXPRESSION AND RELEASES THE MOTOR PROTEIN KIF11, WHICH ACCELERATES WNT3A TRANSPORT AND SECRETION INTO THE TME. ELEVATED WNT3A ACTIVATES WNT SIGNALING IN NEIGHBORING PCA CELLS AND ESTABLISHES A POSITIVE FEEDBACK LOOP THAT AMPLIFIES WNT SIGNALING AND DRIVES THERAPEUTIC RESISTANCE. GENETIC AND PHARMACOLOGICAL INHIBITION OF THIS PATHWAY SUPPRESSES RESISTANCE, SUGGESTING THAT NEUROLYSIN-DEFICIENT TUMORS ACQUIRE A TARGETABLE DEPENDENCE ON THE NEUROLYSIN-KIF11-WNT3A AXIS. OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS STUDY IS TO COMPREHENSIVELY DEFINE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS BY WHICH PCA AUTONOMOUSLY TRANSFORMS THE TME AND PROMOTES RESISTANCE THROUGH MODIFICATIONS IN THE NEUROLYSIN-KIF11-WNT3A AXIS, WITH THE GOAL OF ADVANCING MECHANISM-BASED THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES TO OVERCOME RESISTANCE AND IMPROVE PATIENT OUTCOMES. WE PROPOSE THREE AIMS TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT NEUROLYSIN DEFICIENCY ENABLES PCA TO AUTONOMOUSLY INDUCE WNT3A EXPRESSION AND MODULATE KIF11- DEPENDENT WNT3A SECRETION INTO THE TME, THEREBY ACQUIRING RESISTANCE TO AR-TARGETED THERAPY. IN AIM 1, WE WILL COMPREHENSIVELY DEFINE THE ROLE OF NEUROLYSIN AND ECTOPIC WNT SIGNALING IN PCA TUMORIGENESIS AND RESISTANCE TO AR-TARGETED THERAPY. SINGLE-CELL RNA-SEQ AND SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS WILL BE EMPLOYED TO DISSECT BOTH CELL-AUTONOMOUS AND TME-MEDIATED EFFECTS RESULTING FROM NEUROLYSIN DEFICIENCY AT SINGLE-CELL RESOLUTION. MOUSE MODELS ARE REQUIRED ONLY FOR EXPERIMENTS THAT MUST EVALUATE DYNAMIC TUMOR-TME INTERACTIONS, INCLUDING IMMUNE AND STROMAL COMPONENTS, UNDER CONTROLLED GENETIC PERTURBATION AND AR-TARGETED THERAPY, WHILE PATIENTDERIVED ORGANOIDS WILL BE USED WHEREVER FEASIBLE TO REDUCE ANIMAL USE. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DELINEATE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS BY WHICH NEUROLYSIN DEFICIENCY DRIVES KIF11-DEPENDENT TRANSPORT AND SECRETION OF ECTOPIC WNT3A INTO THE TME, PROMOTING ESCAPE FROM AR-TARGETED THERAPY. IN AIM 3, WE WILL TEST THE EFFICACY OF TARGETING PROTEINS WITHIN THE NEUROLYSIN-KIF11-WNT3A AXIS IN MULTIPLE NLN-DEFICIENT MODELS AND ASSESS ITS PREDICTIVE VALUE AS A BIOMARKER FOR RESPONSES TO AR ANTAGONISTS AND NOVEL THERAPEUTIC COMBINATIONS. THE COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL NOT ONLY REFINE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE MECHANISMS DRIVING AR-TARGETED THERAPY RESISTANCE BUT ALSO LEAD TO A NEW PREDICTIVE BIOMARKER AND INNOVATIVE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TO COMBAT RESISTANCE AND IMPROVE CLINICAL OUTCOMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DRIVERS OF LINEAGE REPROGRAMMING IN MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION OF DIFFUSE GASTRIC CANCER - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT IDENTIFYING EARLY DRIVERS OF MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION IS ESSENTIAL TO IMPROVING OUTCOMES IN DIFFUSE GASTRIC CANCER (DGC), AN AGGRESSIVE MALIGNANCY WITH A HIGH 5-YEAR MORTALITY DUE TO LATE DIAGNOSIS AND POOR RESPONSE TO STANDARD THERAPIES. HEREDITARY DGC (HDGC), A MODEL OF DGC INITIATION, IS A SYNDROME CAUSED BY MUTATIONS IN CDH1 AND CTNNA1 AND CONVEYS A 33-70% LIFETIME RISK OF INVASIVE CANCER. THE STOMACHS OF MOST PATIENTS WITH HDGC CONTAIN SMALL CLUSTERS OF SIGNET-RING CELL (SRC) CARCINOMA FROM AN EARLY AGE, WHICH MAY REMAIN DORMANT YET UNPREDICTABLY AND RAPIDLY PROGRESS TO METASTATIC DISEASE. PRIOR ANALYSES HAVE FAILED TO IDENTIFY GENES ASSOCIATED WITH EARLY MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION OF SRCS. MOREOVER, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT CONVERGENT AND DIVERGENT PATHWAYS OF NEOPLASTIC TRANSFORMATION IN HDGC COMPARED TO SPORADIC DGC (SDGC), WHERE INDIVIDUALS LACK A HEREDITARY PREDISPOSITION BUT ACCUMULATE SOMATIC MUTATIONS IN GENES LIKE CDH1, LEADING TO MALIGNANCY. WE HAVE SUCCESSFULLY DEVELOPED AN INTEGRATED, MULTIDISCIPLINARY WORKFLOW TO OVERCOME LONGSTANDING CHALLENGES OF STUDYING ENIGMATIC, RARE SRCS IN HUMAN TISSUES. OUR PRELIMINARY SPATIAL AND SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOMIC STUDIES OF HDGC UNVEIL REMARKABLE DETAILS ON THE BIOLOGY OF SRCS. WE HAVE FOUND PREVIOUSLY UNCHARACTERIZED GENE EXPRESSION PROGRAMS THAT IDENTIFY SRCS AND DELINEATE 3 DISTINCT, SPATIALLY SEGREGATED SRC STATES: ENTEROCYTE-LIKE SRCS FOUND IN SUPERFICIAL LESIONS, EXPRESSING SLC26A3; GOBLET-LIKE SRCS FOUND IN DEEPER MUCOSAL LESIONS, EXPRESSING TFF3; AND STEM-LIKE SRCS FOUND IN SUBMUCOSAL ADVANCED TUMORS, CHARACTERIZED BY OLFM4. SRC LESIONS DEMONSTRATE EARLY FIBROBLAST INFILTRATION, WHILE ADVANCED MULTI-FOCAL LESIONS REVEAL SHARED CLONAL ORIGIN WITH COPY NUMBER ALTERATIONS. BASED ON THESE DATA, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION IN DGC PROCEEDS THROUGH CELL STATE REPROGRAMMING OF SRCS, REINFORCED BY INTERACTIONS WITH INFILTRATIVE FIBROBLASTS THAT DETERMINE INVASIVE POTENTIAL. WE WILL LEVERAGE OUR UNIQUE PATIENT BIOBANK ALONG WITH SPATIALLY-RESOLVED SINGLE-CELL AND GENOMIC PLATFORMS TO ESTABLISH ASSOCIATIONS AMONG SRC STATES, STROMAL REMODELING AND INVASION. BECAUSE CROSS-SECTIONAL HUMAN DATA CANNOT DIRECTLY ESTABLISH TEMPORAL CAUSALITY, WE WILL USE VALIDATED CDH1-KNOCKOUT MOUSE MODELS TO DETERMINE WHETHER INFLAMMATION DRIVES SRC REPROGRAMMING AND MALIGNANT EXPANSION. IN AIM 1, WE WILL CHARACTERIZE SRC TRANSCRIPTIONAL REPROGRAMMING FROM INDOLENT ENTEROCYTE-LIKE STATES TO INVASIVE STEM-LIKE STATES IN CDH1- AND CTNNA1-ASSOCIATED HDGC. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ELUCIDATE HOW MOLECULAR INTERPLAY BETWEEN SRCS AND FIBROBLASTS DRIVES SRC REPROGRAMMING AND IMPACTS MALIGNANT EXPANSION IN HIGH-RISK PATIENT LESIONS AND TRACK INFLAMMATION-DRIVEN SRC TRANSFORMATION IN THE MOUSE MODEL. IN AIM 3, WE WILL ESTABLISH THE IMPACT OF SOMATIC CDH1 INACTIVATION OF SRC TRANSCRIPTIONAL REPROGRAMMING IN SDGC. ELUCIDATING THE DRIVERS OF SRC TRANSFORMATION IN HDGC AND SDGC WILL RESHAPE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THEIR COMMON AND DIVERGENT PATHWAYS, IDENTIFYING MARKERS OF EARLY NEOPLASTIC TRANSFORMATION AND LEADING TO CLINICALLY ACTIONABLE INTERVENTIONS.
