description: TARGETING ERBB3-POSITIVE DIFFERENTIATED POPULATIONS TO ELIMINATE THERAPY RESISTANT RHABDOMYOSARCOMAS. - ABSTRACT: RHABDOMYOSARCOMA (RMS) IS THE MOST COMMON SOFT TISSUE SARCOMA IN CHILDREN, AFFECTING APPROXIMATELY 350 CHILDREN ANNUALLY IN THE U.S. FUSION-POSITIVE (FP) RMS DRIVEN BY PAX3/PAX7-FOXO1 FUSIONS IS THE MOST AGGRESSIVE SUBTYPE WITH SURVIVAL RATES BELOW 50% AND POST-RELAPSE SURVIVAL UNDER 20%. DESPITE THREE DECADES OF CLINICAL RESEARCH, NO NEW THERAPEUTIC REGIMENS HAVE BEEN APPROVED. THE FIELD HAS UNSUCCESSFULLY ATTEMPTED TO ELIMINATE RMS BY FORCING TERMINAL DIFFERENTIATION, BASED ON THE DOGMA THAT DIFFERENTIATED CELLS ARE BENIGN. HOWEVER, FP-RMS TUMORS RESIST TERMINAL DIFFERENTIATION YET RESEMBLE DIFFERENTIATED MUSCLE CELLS, AND RECENT STUDIES SHOW DIFFERENTIATED TUMOR CELLS SURVIVE VINCRISTINE TREATMENT. WE CHALLENGE THIS PARADIGM BY PROVIDING COMPELLING EVIDENCE THAT ERBB3-EXPRESSING DIFFERENTIATED CELLS ACTIVELY PROMOTE TUMORIGENESIS, SELF-RENEWAL, AND THERAPY RESISTANCE IN FP-RMS. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT: (I) ERBB3 EXPRESSION IS RESTRICTED TO DIFFERENTIATED RMS SUBPOPULATIONS; (II) HIGH ERBB3 CORRELATES WITH POOR OUTCOMES (P=0.031); (III) ERBB3 IS ELEVATED IN VAC-RESISTANT MODELS; (IV) ERBB3 IS ESSENTIAL FOR TUMOR GROWTH AND SELF-RENEWAL; (V) ERBB3-HIGH FP-RMS SHOW COMPLETE TUMOR ELIMINATION IN 3/3 PATIENT-DERIVED XENOGRAFTS (PDXS) TREATED WITH PATRITUMAB DERUXTECAN, AN ERBB3-TARGETING ANTIBODY-DRUG CONJUGATE IN CLINICAL TRIALS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT ERBB3 DRIVES SELF-RENEWAL, CELL STATE PLASTICITY, GROWTH, AND THERAPY RESISTANCE IN FP-RMS THROUGH A STAT3-DEPENDENT MECHANISM, AND THAT TARGETING ERBB3-POSITIVE POPULATIONS WILL PREVENT RELAPSE. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DEMONSTRATE THAT AN ERBB3-STAT3 AXIS DRIVES TUMOR INITIATION AND THERAPY RESISTANCE BY COREGULATING PAX3- -INITIATING CAPACITY UPON ERBB3 OR STAT3 DISRUPTION. IN AIM 2, WE WILL UNCOVER THE REGULATORY CIRCUITRY CONTROLLING ERBB3 EXPRESSION, TESTING WHETHER HDAC INHIBITORS DISRUPT SNAI2-MEDIATED REPRESSION (SNAI2 REPRESSES ERBB3 IN PROGENITORS WHILE FOXO3 ACTIVATES ERBB3 IN DIFFERENTIATED CELLS) TO EXPAND ERBB3-POSITIVE POPULATIONS TO >90%, MAXIMIZING PATRITUMAB DERUXTECAN EFFICACY. IN AIM 3, WE WILL TEST WHETHER PATRITUMAB DERUXTECAN ELIMINATES ERBB3- DEPENDENT FP- - NEGATIVE RMS, WE WILL DETERMINE IF COMBINING PATRITUMAB DERUXTECAN WITH RAS-MEK INHIBITION ABLATES ERBB3- POSITIVE PERSISTER CELLS THAT EMERGE POST-RAS PATHWAY BLOCKADE, PREVENTING RELAPSE. OUR TEAM'S 30+ RMS PDX MODELS AND ERBB3 SIGNALING EXPERTISE POSITION US TO ACCOMPLISH THESE AIMS. THIS PROPOSAL FUNDAMENTALLY REFRAMES RMS THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES BY DEMONSTRATING THAT ELIMINATING DIFFERENTIATED ERBB3-POSITIVE POPULATIONS, RATHER THAN PROMOTING DIFFERENTIATION, IS SUFFICIENT TO ABROGATE TUMOR GROWTH AND PREVENT RELAPSE, PROVIDING IMMEDIATE CLINICAL TRANSLATION AS PATRITUMAB DERUXTECAN IS IN CLINICAL TRIALS. OUR FINDINGS ESTABLISH THERAPEUTIC LEVERAGE OVER TUMOR HETEROGENEITY WITH BROAD RELEVANCE TO ERBB3-DRIVEN THERAPY RESISTANCE IN OTHER SOLID TUMORS. TO ENSURE SAFE AND EFFECTIVE TRANSLATION OF OUR PROPOSED DRUG COMBINATIONS IN THERAPY RESISTANT RHABDOMYOSARCOMA, IN VIVO STUDIES IN MICE ARE ESSENTIAL TO DETERMINE EFFICACY, AND TO ASSESS FOR TOXICITIES THAT MAY ARISE IN PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTERCEPTING OVARIAN CANCER AT ITS EARLIEST STAGE: VALIDATION OF TU-STROMA AS A BLOOD-BASED DIAGNOSTIC BIOMARKER - PROJECT SUMMARY OVARIAN CANCER IS THE MOST LETHAL GYNECOLOGIC MALIGNANCY, WITH HIGH-GRADE SEROUS OVARIAN CARCINOMA (HGSC) ACCOUNTING FOR THE MAJORITY OF DEATHS AND MORE THAN 450,000 WOMEN DYING GLOBALLY EACH YEAR. THE DISMAL SURVIVAL RATE STEMS FROM LATE DIAGNOSIS, AS MOST WOMEN PRESENT ONLY AFTER PERITONEAL SPREAD. CURRENT BLOOD TESTS SUCH AS CA-125, HE4, AND ROMA ARE INADEQUATE: THEY FAIL TO DETECT PRE-INVASIVE DISEASE, PERFORM POORLY IN PREMENOPAUSAL WOMEN, AND HAVE NOT REDUCED MORTALITY IN CLINICAL TRIALS. THERE IS THEREFORE AN URGENT PUBLIC HEALTH NEED FOR A BLOOD TEST THAT CAN DETECT HGSC AT ITS INCEPTION, WHEN SURGICAL INTERVENTION IS MOST EFFECTIVE. OUR WORK AND THAT OF OTHERS HAS ESTABLISHED SEROUS TUBAL INTRAEPITHELIAL CARCINOMA (STIC) AS THE OBLIGATE PRECURSOR OF HGSC, YET NO EXISTING BIOMARKER CAPTURES THIS EARLIEST WINDOW. WE RECENTLY DISCOVERED TU-STROMA, A LONG NON-CODING RNA SECRETED IN EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES THAT REPROGRAMS THE SURROUNDING STROMA. THIS RNA APPEARS IN CIRCULATION AT THE STIC STAGE, WELL BEFORE INVASIVE CANCER DEVELOPS, AND IS MECHANISTICALLY LINKED TO TUMOR–STROMAL INTERACTIONS. PILOT STUDIES DEMONSTRATE THAT TU-STROMA DETECTS STIC AND EARLY-STAGE HGSC WITH AUC VALUES APPROACHING 0.99 AND PERFORMS EQUALLY WELL IN PREMENOPAUSAL WOMEN, A GROUP WHERE CA-125 AND HE4 ARE UNRELIABLE. THIS R01 WILL RIGOROUSLY VALIDATE TU-STROMA ACROSS BLINDED, GLOBALLY SOURCED COHORTS USING A QRT-PCR ASSAY ON SERUM EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES WITH LOCKED THRESHOLDS TO ENSURE REPRODUCIBILITY. INTER- LABORATORY REPRODUCIBILITY WILL BE TESTED THROUGH DISTRIBUTED SAMPLE ANALYSIS AND HARMONIZED PIPELINES. OUR TEAM INTEGRATES EXPERTISE IN OVARIAN CANCER BIOLOGY, MOLECULAR PROFILING, EPIGENETICS, AND STATISTICAL MODELING, AND HAS ASSEMBLED A 600-SAMPLE TRAINING AND VALIDATION SET SPANNING STIC, EARLY-STAGE HGSC, AND CONTROLS, WITH ADDITIONAL COHORTS FOR EXTERNAL REPLICATION. THE INNOVATION IS THREE-FOLD: FIRST, TU-STROMA IS THE ONLY BLOOD-BASED BIOMARKER CAPABLE OF DETECTING STIC; SECOND, IT PROVIDES RELIABLE DETECTION IN PREMENOPAUSAL WOMEN, ADDRESSING A MAJOR UNMET CLINICAL NEED; AND THIRD, IT IS MECHANISTICALLY ANCHORED, REFLECTING TUMOR-STROMAL FITNESS REPROGRAMMING RATHER THAN NONSPECIFIC TUMOR BURDEN. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION WILL DELIVER A CLINICALLY READY, INEXPENSIVE, AND SCALABLE TEST THAT CAN BE DEPLOYED FOR HIGH-RISK BRCA OR LYNCH CARRIERS, SYMPTOMATIC TRIAGE, AND EVENTUALLY POPULATION-LEVEL SCREENING TRIALS. THE IMPACT IS TRANSFORMATIVE: SHIFTING HGSC DIAGNOSIS FROM LATE- STAGE TO PRE-INVASIVE DISEASE, ENABLING RISK-REDUCING SURGERY AT THE RIGHT TIME, AND PREVENTING THOUSANDS OF DEATHS EACH YEAR. BY BRIDGING FUNDAMENTAL BIOLOGY WITH RIGOROUS CLINICAL VALIDATION, THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A NEW PARADIGM FOR OVARIAN CANCER EARLY DETECTION AND CANCER INTERCEPTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTEGRATING TOBACCO AND ALCOHOL COUNSELING AND TREATMENT INTO HIV CARE IN KISUMU COUNTY, KENYA- INTACT STUDY - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT ADVANCES IN HIV TREATMENT HAVE SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED LIFE EXPECTANCY AMONG PEOPLE WITH HIV (PWH), BUT HAVE ALSO HIGHLIGHTED A GROWING BURDEN OF NON-COMMUNICABLE DISEASES (NCDS). HIGHER RATES OF TOBACCO AND ALCOHOL USE AMONG PWH INCREASE THE RISK OF CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, CANCER, AND OTHER CHRONIC CONDITIONS. THIS STUDY WILL EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS, IMPLEMENTATION, AND COSTEFFECTIVENESS OF INTEGRATING PHARMACOLOGIC AND BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS FOR TOBACCO AND ALCOHOL USE INTO ROUTINE HIV PRIMARY CARE. IN THE UNITED STATES, HIV CARE REMAINS FRAGMENTED, WITH LIMITED INTEGRATION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT, ALCOHOL USE DISORDER SERVICES, AND OTHER NCD CARE. THIS FRAGMENTATION CREATES BARRIERS TO PROVIDER ADOPTION, PARTICIPANT RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION, AND EVALUATION OF INTEGRATED INTERVENTIONS IN REAL-WORLD SETTINGS. KENYA PROVIDES A STRONG IMPLEMENTATION SETTING BECAUSE INTEGRATED HIV AND NCD SERVICES ARE ALREADY EMBEDDED WITHIN PRIMARY HEALTHCARE, OFFERING ESTABLISHED INFRASTRUCTURE FOR INTEGRATING TOBACCO AND ALCOHOL DEPENDENCE TREATMENT. LEVERAGING THIS PLATFORM WILL ENABLE EFFICIENT RECRUITMENT AND RIGOROUS EVALUATION OF INTERVENTION EFFECTIVENESS, COST-EFFECTIVENESS, FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND SCALABILITY, WHILE GENERATING IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE THAT WOULD BE MORE DIFFICULT AND COSTLY TO OBTAIN IN THE FRAGMENTED U.S. HEALTHCARE SYSTEM. BUPROPION AND NALTREXONE ARE FDA-APPROVED TREATMENTS FOR TOBACCO DEPENDENCE AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDER, RESPECTIVELY, BUT EVIDENCE SUPPORTING THEIR COMBINED USE AMONG PWH WITH CONCURRENT TOBACCO AND HEAVY ALCOHOL USE REMAINS LIMITED. FINDINGS FROM THIS STUDY COULD INFORM INTEGRATED TREATMENT APPROACHES IN U.S. HIV CARE SETTINGS, INCLUDING FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS AND RYAN WHITE HIV/AIDS PROGRAM CLINICS. WE WILL CONDUCT A 2×2 FACTORIAL CLUSTER-RANDOMIZED TRIAL IN 12 PRIMARY CARE CLINICS IN KISUMU, KENYA, ENROLLING 600 PWH WHO USE TOBACCO AND ALCOHOL. AIM 1: CONDUCT FORMATIVE RESEARCH TO DEVELOP AND ADAPT INTERVENTIONS AND ONLINE PROVIDER TRAINING FOR INTEGRATING MEDICATION MANAGEMENT AND MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING-BASED COUNSELING INTO HIV PRIMARY CARE. AIM 2: EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF BUPROPION PLUS NALTREXONE AND/OR INTENSIVE COUNSELING ON BIOCHEMICALLY VERIFIED TOBACCO CESSATION AND ALCOHOL REDUCTION AT 6 MONTHS. AIM 3: ESTIMATE THE INCREMENTAL COST-EFFECTIVENESS OF THE INTERVENTION STRATEGIES. AIM 4: ASSESS IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES AND CONTEXTUAL DETERMINANTS USING THE PRISM FRAMEWORK.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DESTIGMA: DETECTING STIGMA USING GENERATIVE AI AMONG MULTISITE PATIENTS WITH SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS - PROJECT SUMMARY THE UNITED STATES (US) HAS EXPERIENCED A GROWING SUBSTANCE OVERDOSE CRISIS OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, RESULTING IN OVER 105,000 DRUG OVERDOSE DEATHS IN 2023. DESPITE 48.7 MILLION AMERICANS OVER AGE 12 HAVING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUD) IN THE PAST YEAR, ONLY 1 IN 4 RECEIVED TREATMENT. STIGMA IS A SIGNIFICANT BARRIER TO TREATMENT AND IS MORE SEVERE FOR SUDS THAN OTHER MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS. IN HEALTHCARE SETTINGS, STIGMA, CHARACTERIZED BY IMPLICIT BIAS AND NEGATIVE ATTITUDES FROM PROVIDERS, CRITICALLY IMPEDES TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT. SUD-RELATED PROVIDER STIGMA MAY LEAD TO A RANGE OF NEGATIVE HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR PEOPLE WITH SUD, INCLUDING RELUCTANCE TO SEEK CARE, NOT DISCLOSING DRUG USE, DELAYING CARE, OPTING FOR SELF-DIRECTED DISCHARGE, AND DISCONTINUING TREATMENT. WHILE SOME RESEARCH HAS EXAMINED INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL IMPACTS OF EXPOSURE TO PROVIDER STIGMA, THE VARIATIONS IN EXPERIENCING DIFFERENT TYPES OF PROVIDER STIGMA DUE TO CONTEXTUAL-LEVEL NON-CLINICAL HEALTH DETERMINANTS, SUCH AS GEOLOCATION (E.G., RURAL VS. URBAN), INCOME, EDUCATION, OR ACCESS TO HEALTHCARE, AND THEIR COMPOUNDING IMPACT, REMAIN LARGELY UNKNOWN. PROVIDER STIGMA/IMPLICIT BIAS IS MALLEABLE AND CAN BE RECTIFIED VIA INTERVENTIONS, WHICH IN TURN CAN BE CRUCIAL TO IMPROVING TREATMENT OUTCOMES FOR SUD PATIENTS. INVESTIGATIONS OF LINGUISTIC BIAS AND STIGMA IN PATIENT NOTES HAVE IDENTIFIED SALIENT FEATURES, SUCH AS THE EXPRESSION OF DOUBT IN PATIENT TESTIMONY VIA QUOTATIONS OR EVIDENTIAL USE, AND USE OF STIGMATIZING AND NEGATIVE DESCRIPTORS. RECENT STUDIES EMPLOYING NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING (NLP) TO DETECT STIGMATIZING EXPRESSIONS VIA LEXICAL MATCHING HAVE LIMITATIONS IN CAPTURING THE FULL SPECTRUM OF STIGMATIZING LANGUAGE AND ITS CONTEXTUAL VARIATIONS. ADVANCES IN NLP, INCLUDING THE EMERGENCE OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS (LLMS), PRESENT AN OPPORTUNITY TO ADDRESS THIS GAP BY COMPREHENSIVELY DETECTING STIGMATIZING LANGUAGE, ENABLING LARGE-SCALE ANALYSES OF ITS IMPACT, AND MITIGATING STIGMATIZING LANGUAGE. OUR OVERARCHING OBJECTIVE IS TO EMPLOY NLP, MACHINE LEARNING, AND LLMS, IN A MULTI-AGENT AI ARCHITECTURE TO SYSTEMATICALLY DETECT AND DE-STIGMATIZE PROVIDER LANGUAGE IN CLINICAL NOTES OF SUD PATIENTS, EXAMINING ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN STIGMATIZING LANGUAGE AND PATIENT OUTCOMES ACROSS DATA FROM FOUR SITES (EMORY, CORNELL, UPENN, AND MT. SINAI). WE PROPOSE THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: (AIM 1) TO EXTEND OUR PILOT SUPERVISED MACHINE LEARNING APPROACH FOR DETECTING STIGMATIZING LANGUAGE TO ACHIEVE HUMAN-LEVEL AGREEMENT; (AIM 2) TO EXAMINE THE PREVALENCE OF STIGMATIZING LANGUAGE ACROSS PATIENT GROUPS, AND THEIR ASSOCIATIONS WITH PATIENT OUTCOMES; AND (AIM 3) TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A REAL- TIME CO-PILOT SYSTEM, POWERED BY AN OPEN-SOURCE, INSTRUCTION-TUNED GENERATIVE LLM, TO ASSIST PROVIDERS IN USING NON-STIGMATIZING LANGUAGE IN SUD PATIENT NOTES. SUCCESSFUL EXECUTION OF THIS PROJECT WILL CREATE THE FIRST EHR INTEGRATION-READY CO-PILOT SYSTEM TO SUBSTANTIALLY REDUCE STIGMATIZING LANGUAGE IN SUD PATIENT NOTES, WITH APPLICABILITY BEYOND SUD TREATMENT. IT WILL ALSO PROVIDE UNPRECEDENTED INSIGHTS INTO THE IMPACT OF STIGMATIZING LANGUAGE ON TREATMENT OUTCOMES ACROSS PATIENT POPULATIONS, INFORMING TARGETED FUTURE INTERVENTIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CHRONIC CANNABINOID VAPOR EXPOSURE: LONG-TERM EFFECTS ON MYELIN, FUNCTIONAL NEURAL NETWORKS, AND BEHAVIOR - ABSTRACT INHALATION IS THE MOST COMMON ROUTE OF ADMINISTRATION OF CANNABIS PRODUCTS, AND VAPING OF DELTA-9- TETRAHYDROCANNABINOL (THC) RESULTS IN MORE RAPID DELIVERY OF DRUG TO THE BRAIN, HIGHER CONCENTRATIONS IN BRAIN AND BLOOD, GREATER SUBJECTIVE EFFECTS, AND GREATER IMPAIRMENT COMPARED TO OTHER ROUTES OF ADMINISTRATION. THE POTENTIAL HARMS ASSOCIATED WITH CHRONIC VAPING OF THC ARE LARGELY UNKNOWN; HOWEVER, CHRONIC USE OF THC AND CANNABIS HAS BEEN LINKED WITH INCREASED RISKS OF ANXIETY AND OTHER MOOD DISORDERS, PSYCHOSIS, AND CANNABIS USE DISORDER. RETROSPECTIVE STUDIES IN ADULTS WHO REGULARLY USE CANNABIS USE HAVE OBSERVED STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL BRAIN ABNORMALITIES, COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS AND MOOD DISORDERS, THOUGH THE EXTENT TO WHICH THIS IS CAUSED BY THC IS UNKNOWN. GIVEN THE RAPIDLY INCREASING USE OF THC-CONTAINING CANNABIS VAPE PRODUCTS IN THE UNITED STATES IT IS VITAL TO INCREASE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE IMPACT OF CHRONIC VAPORIZED THC ON THE BRAIN. THIS MULTIDISCIPLINARY PROJECT AIMS TO DETERMINE WHETHER CHRONIC VAPORIZED DELTA-9-TETRAHYDROCANNABINOL (THC) EXPOSURE CAUSES LASTING BEHAVIORAL AND BRAIN ALTERATIONS, INCLUDING DISRUPTED CONNECTIVITY, WHITE MATTER DAMAGE, AND NEUROINFLAMMATION IN ADULT MALE AND FEMALE RATS. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT REPEATED EXPOSURE TO THC VAPOR INCREASES NEUROINFLAMMATION, WHICH TRIGGERS INFLAMMATORY DRIVEN CHANGES TO WHITE MATTER INCLUDING DEGRADATION AND DAMAGE, AND RESULTS IN PERSISTENT DISRUPTIONS IN NEURAL CONNECTIVITY AND ASSOCIATED BEHAVIORAL DEFICITS. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS BY ASSESSING THE LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF CHRONIC THC VAPOR EXPOSURE ON EXECUTIVE FUNCTION, ANXIETY-LIKE BEHAVIOR, AND FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY (AIM 1); WHITE MATTER INTEGRITY AND MYELIN PLASTICITY (AIM 2); AND CHANGES TO THE NEURO-IMMUNE LANDSCAPE BY ASSESSING INFLAMMATORY BIOMARKERS, IMMUNE CELL POPULATION SIGNATURES, AND MICROGLIAL AND ASTROCYTIC MOLECULAR DYNAMICS. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL TEST WHETHER REDUCING INFLAMMATION PREVENTS THC-INDUCED WHITE MATTER DAMAGE AND BEHAVIORAL DEFICITS (AIM 3). TO ACHIEVE THESE OBJECTIVES, WE WILL USE INNOVATIVE CANNABINOID VAPORIZATION TECHNOLOGY AND VALIDATED THC VAPOR DOSING PROTOCOLS ALONG WITH TRANSLATIONAL BEHAVIORAL ASSESSMENTS OF EXECUTIVE FUNCTION AND ANXIETY- LIKE BEHAVIOR, PRECLINICAL FUNCTIONAL MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (FMRI) AND DIFFUSION TENSOR IMAGING (DTI), ELECTRON MICROSCOPY AND IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY FOR RIGOROUS EVALUATION OF MYELIN PLASTICITY, VALIDATED BIOASSAYS OF IMMUNE MARKERS, GLIAL MORPHOLOGY, AS WELL AS FLOW CYTOMETRY. THIS RESEARCH WILL ELUCIDATE KEY MECHANISMS UNDERLYING LONG-TERM STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL BRAIN CHANGES CAUSED BY CHRONIC THC VAPOR EXPOSURE, ULTIMATELY, INFORMING PUBLIC HEALTH GUIDELINES ON USE OF THC-CONTAINING VAPE PRODUCTS AND GUIDING FUTURE LINES OF RESEARCH INTO MECHANISMS OF NEUROREPAIR.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IDENTIFYING MECHANISMS OF COGNITIVE COMPUTATIONS FROM HETEROGENEOUS NEURAL RESPONSES AND BEHAVIOR - PROJECT SUMMARY ADVANCES IN NEUROTECHNOLOGY HAVE ENABLED LARGE-SCALE RECORDINGS OF NEURAL ACTIVITY ACROSS THE ENTIRE BRAIN AT SINGLE-CELL RESOLUTION, AS WELL AS PRECISE STIMULATION OF TARGETED NEURAL ENSEMBLES IN BEHAVING ANIMALS. THESE LARGE-SCALE DATASETS REVEAL THAT NEURAL RESPONSES ARE HIGHLY HETEROGENEOUS, WITH SINGLE NEURONS ENCODING COMPLEX COMBINATIONS OF BEHAVIORAL AND TASK VARIABLES, WITHOUT CLEAR ORGANIZING PRINCIPLES UNDERLYING THIS MIXED SELECTIVITY. DESPITE THIS APPARENT COMPLEXITY, NEURAL ACTIVITY DURING COGNITIVE TASKS OFTEN FORMS LOW-DIMENSIONAL MANIFOLDS WITHIN THE POPULATION STATE SPACE. HOWEVER, CIRCUIT MECHANISMS THAT GENERATE THESE LOW-DIMENSIONAL POPULATION DYNAMICS REMAIN LARGELY UNKNOWN, LIMITING OUR ABILITY TO PRODUCE TESTABLE PREDICTIONS FOR CAUSAL PERTURBATION EXPERIMENTS. THIS PROPOSAL WILL ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES BY DEVELOPING NEW THEORETICAL FRAMEWORKS AND COMPUTATIONAL METHODS TO BETTER LEVERAGE RECURRENT NEURAL NETWORK (RNN) MODELS IN IDENTIFYING MECHANISMS OF COGNITIVE COMPUTATIONS FROM EXPERIMENTAL DATA. WHILE RNNS ARE INCREASINGLY USED TO MODEL NEURAL DYNAMICS, THE COMPLEXITY OF THEIR HIGH-DIMENSIONAL CONNECTIVITY HINDERS UNDERSTANDING OF THE UNDERLYING CIRCUIT MECHANISMS. FURTHERMORE, HIGH-DIMENSIONAL RNNS ARE INSUFFICIENTLY CONSTRAINED BY LOW-DIMENSIONAL NEURAL RESPONSES OBSERVED DURING COGNITIVE TASKS, WHICH MAY COMPROMISE THEIR PREDICTIVE POWER FOR PERTURBATION EXPERIMENTS TARGETING SPECIFIC NEURAL ENSEMBLES. TO OVERCOME THESE LIMITATIONS, WE PROPOSE THREE AIMS: (AIM 1) FORMULATE A MATHEMATICAL THEORY RELATING THE DIMENSIONALITY OF NEURAL POPULATION DYNAMICS TO THE STRUCTURE OF SINGLE-CELL SELECTIVITY, AND TEST THIS THEORY USING BRAIN-WIDE NEURAL RECORDINGS. (AIM 2) DEVELOP A CONVEX FRAMEWORK FOR EFFICIENTLY FITTING RNNS TO DATA WITH FLEXIBLE RANK CONTROL. (AIM 3) DEVELOP METHODS FOR DESIGNING EFFECTIVE STIMULATION PATTERNS TO GUIDE TARGETED OPTOGENETIC PERTURBATION EXPERIMENTS USING RANK-CONTROLLED RNNS WITH CONNECTIVITY UNIQUELY CONSTRAINED BY DATA. WE WILL VALIDATE THESE THEORIES AND COMPUTATIONAL METHODS USING RNN MODELS OF COGNITIVE TASKS AND DATA FROM BRAIN-WIDE NEURAL RECORDINGS AND PATTERNED PHOTOSTIMULATION OPTOGENETICS EXPERIMENTS. OUR THEORY WILL HELP RECONCILE CONFLICTING EXPERIMENTAL FINDINGS ON NEURAL REPRESENTATIONS AND SELECTIVITY. THE RESULTING MODELS AND METHODS WILL AFFORD MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO NEURAL CIRCUITS UNDERLYING COGNITIVE FUNCTIONS AND ENABLE MORE EFFECTIVE DESIGN OF OPTOGENETIC PERTURBATION EXPERIMENTS, BRIDGING THE GAP BETWEEN NEURAL ACTIVITY DATA AND CAUSAL MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: COARSE-GRAINING APPROACHES TO NETWORKS, LEARNING AND BEHAVIOR - PROJECT SUMMARY THE THEORY MODELS AND METHODS (TMM) HUB PUT FORWARD IN THIS RENEWAL PROPOSAL WILL WORK TO TRANSLATE SUCCESSFUL AND POWERFUL APPROACHES TO DESCRIBING EMERGENT COLLECTIVE BEHAVIOR IN NEURAL SYSTEMS AND BEHAVIOR INTO USABLE CODE FOR THE BROAD NEUROSCIENCE COMMUNITY. WORKING CLOSELY TOGETHER, THE THREE THEORISTS WILL DEVELOP METHODS FOR FINDING AND INTERPRETING THE RELEVANT MODES OF POPULATION ACTIVITY IN THE BRAIN, BOTH IN INSTANTANEOUS SNAPSHOTS OF ACTIVITY AND ACTIVITY AS IT EVOLVES IN TIME. METHODS WILL BE TESTED IN A WIDE RANGE OF NEURAL SYSTEMS AT DIFFERENT PROCESSING STAGES AND SCALES: FROM SALAMANDERS TO RODENTS TO HUMANS, FROM THE RETINA TO THE CORTEX, FROM TENS TO THOUSANDS OF CELLS. THE APPROACH WILL BE VALIDATED BY CHECKING THAT THE NEURAL CODE CAN BE READ OUT WITH HIGH FIDELITY EVEN AFTER BEING COMPRESSED INTO A MUCH SMALLER SUBSPACE. THE PROJECT WILL PRODUCE DATA ANALYSIS CODE THAT WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE FOR NEUROSCIENCE RESEARCHERS TO USE ON THEIR OWN DATA, IN ADDITION TO THE RESULTS OF THE ANALYSES OF THE PARTICULAR SYSTEMS STUDIED. THE NEURAL CODE IS INHERENTLY COLLECTIVE; WHILE SINGLE NEURONS EXECUTE SOPHISTICATED COMPUTATIONS, HUNDREDS TO THOUSANDS OF NEURONS ARE UTILIZED TO SENSE THE ENVIRONMENT AND DRIVE BEHAVIOR IN EVEN THE SIMPLEST ORGANISMS. ALTHOUGH THE PAST HUNDRED YEARS HAVE YIELDED SUBSTANTIAL PROGRESS IN NEUROSCIENCE, ONLY RECENTLY HAVE RESEARCHERS HAD THE CAPACITY TO RECORD FROM COMPLETE NEURAL POPULATIONS - THAT IS, TO VIEW THE COLLECTIVE BEHAVIOR OF A FUNCTIONING NEURAL NETWORK. WITH THESE RAPID EXPERIMENTAL ADVANCES, THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR COMPLEMENTARY THEORETICAL AND COMPUTATIONAL APPROACHES TO GUIDE THE EXPLORATION OF EMERGENT BEHAVIOR IN LARGE GROUPS OF NEURONS, ALLOWING ONE TO TURN `BIG DATA' INTO `BIG IDEAS'. THIS PROPOSAL OUTLINES A PATH FROM PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED TOOLS FOR COARSE-GRAINING NEURAL DATA TO NEW TECHNIQUES FOR INTERPRETING THESE COLLECTIVE CODES, MAKING NEW BESPOKE COARSE-GRAININGS THAT ARE TAILORED TO SPECIFIC COMPUTATIONAL GOALS, AND DISSEMINATING THESE METHODS IN SHAREABLE CODE REPOSITORIES. THE PROJECT DRAWS HEAVILY ON THE SUCCESS OF SO- CALLED RENORMALIZATION GROUP APPROACHES IN THEORETICAL PHYSICS THAT REVOLUTIONIZED THE UNDERSTANDING OF COLLECTIVE PHENOMENA IN PHYSICAL SYSTEMS, AND SCULPTED MUCH OF THE PROGRESS IN STATISTICAL PHYSICS IN THE SECOND HALF OF THE TWENTIETH CENTURY. THE METHODS EXPLORED IN THIS PROPOSAL GENERALIZE SUCH TECHNIQUES SO THEY CAN BE APPLIED TO A MUCH WIDER RANGE OF PROBLEMS. THE METHODS DEVELOPED BY THIS TMM HUB WILL BE APPLICABLE TO A WIDE RANGE OF NEURAL DATA SINCE THEY ARE EXPLICITLY DESIGNED TO GENERALIZE TECHNIQUES FROM THEORETICAL PHYSICS TO A MUCH BROADER SETTING. INDEED, A LARGER GOAL OF THE APPROACH IS TO SEARCH FOR UNIVERSALITY IN COLLECTIVE BEHAVIOR IN THE NEURAL CODE. THE TECHNIQUES PROPOSED ARE RELATIVELY STRAIGHTFORWARD TO EXECUTE AND WILL PROVIDE A FUNDAMENTAL METHODOLOGY FOR INTERROGATING HIGH-DIMENSIONAL DATA IN FIELDS AS DIVERSE AS BEHAVIORAL NEUROSCIENCE AND BIOPHYSICS. THE NEW TECHNIQUES WILL ALSO BE TAUGHT AS PART OF THE THREE THEORISTS' ONGOING EFFORTS TO EXPOSE INCOMING GRADUATE STUDENTS IN BIOLOGICAL SCIENCES TO QUANTITATIVE METHODS IN BIOLOGY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AVAILABILITY OF TELEHEALTH-DELIVERED BUPRENORPHINE TREATMENT FOR PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN WITH OPIOID USE DISORDER: A MIXED METHODS STUDY - ABSTRACT THE OPIOID CRISIS CONTINUES TO BE AN URGENT AND PRESSING NATIONAL PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY, AND PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM WOMEN (PPW) ARE ESPECIALLY VULNERABLE. BETWEEN 2010 AND 2017, THE NUMBER OF WOMEN WITH OPIOID-RELATED DIAGNOSES AT DELIVERY INCREASED BY 131%, AND OPIOID OVERDOSE IS NOW A LEADING AND PREVENTABLE CAUSE OF MATERNAL MORTALITY. UPTAKE OF TREATMENT FOR PERINATAL OUD CAN INCREASE THE LIKELIHOOD OF A HEALTHY PREGNANCY AND POSTPARTUM PERIOD FOR THE MOTHER-INFANT DYAD. DESPITE THE SAFETY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF MEDICATIONS FOR OUD (MOUD) – SPECIFICALLY BUPRENORPHINE AND METHADONE – DURING THE PERINATAL PERIOD, ONLY HALF OF PREGNANT WOMEN WITH OUD RECEIVE MOUD. BECAUSE BUPRENORPHINE IS AVAILABLE IN OUTPATIENT SETTINGS AND REQUIRES FEWER IN-PERSON VISITS, IT IS OFTEN A MORE ACCESSIBLE TREATMENT OPTION THAN METHADONE, BUT MANY PPW WITH OUD FACE SUBSTANTIAL BARRIERS TO RECEIVING THIS LIFESAVING TREATMENT, INCLUDING A LACK OF PROVIDERS, STIGMA, LONG WAIT TIMES FOR APPOINTMENTS, INSURANCE AND PAYMENT BARRIERS, AND TRANSPORTATION AND CHILDCARE CHALLENGES. TELEHEALTH DELIVERY OF BUPRENORPHINE TREATMENT (TELEBUP) HAS SIGNIFICANT POTENTIAL TO MITIGATE MANY OF THESE BARRIERS TO IN-PERSON OUD CARE AND IMPROVE TREATMENT RETENTION AND HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR PPW WITH OUD. POLICIES REGULATING THE USE OF TELEBUP HAVE EVOLVED CONSIDERABLY SINCE 2020, AND DESPITE PRELIMINARY EVIDENCE SHOWING TREATMENT SUCCESS FOR PPW WHO ARE ABLE TO ACCESS CARE VIA A DEDICATED TELEHEALTH OUD PROGRAM, THE EXTENT TO WHICH THIS TRANSFORMATIVE CHANGE IN TREATMENT DELIVERY HAS IMPACTED THE ACCESSIBILITY, DELIVERY, AND QUALITY OF CARE THAT PPW WITH OUD CAN AND DO RECEIVE IS UNKNOWN. FURTHER, THE IMPACT OF TELEHEALTH POLICY CHANGES ON ACCESS TO TELEBUP AMONG PPW – AND THE EXTENT TO WHICH THESE IMPACTS VARY BY PROVIDER AND COMMUNITY CHARACTERISTICS – REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD. AS THE OPIOID CRISIS CONTINUES AND MANY TELEHEALTH FLEXIBILITIES ARE MADE PERMANENT, IT IS CRITICAL THAT PUBLIC HEALTH OFFICIALS, POLICYMAKERS, AND PRACTITIONERS BETTER UNDERSTAND THE REAL EXPERIENCES OF PPW WITH OUD SEEKING TREATMENT, WHICH WILL ALLOW DECISIONMAKERS TO STRATEGICALLY INVEST IN AND STRENGTHEN LOCAL OUD TREATMENT INFRASTRUCTURE. IN THE PROPOSED MIXED-METHODS STUDY, WE WILL (1) CONDUCT A LONGITUDINAL SECRET SHOPPER SURVEY OF A NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE SAMPLE OF SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT FACILITIES, MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT FACILITIES, AND OFFICE-BASED PROVIDERS TO DETERMINE THE AVAILABILITY OF TELEBUP FOR OUD, OVERALL AND BY INSURANCE STATUS (PRIVATE, MEDICAID, NO INSURANCE); (2) ESTIMATE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN STATE-LEVEL POLICIES AROUND PERINATAL OUD TREATMENT, INCLUDING TELEHEALTH AND PERINATAL SUBSTANCE USE POLICIES, ON TELEBUP AVAILABILITY TO PPW WITH OUD, OVERALL AND BY PROVIDER AND COUNTY CHARACTERISTICS AND OVER TIME; AND (3) CONDUCT KEY INFORMANT INTERVIEWS WITH PROVIDERS OF TELEBUP AND PATIENTS WITH LIVED EXPERIENCE OF PERINATAL OUD TO QUALITATIVELY EXAMINE FACILITATORS OF AND BARRIERS TO TELEBUP ACCESS AND IDENTIFY ACTIONABLE STRATEGIES TO EXPAND ACCESS TO TELEBUP CARE AND IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES OF PPW WITH OUD.

description: OPIOID USE DISORDER COUNTY AREA PREVALENCE THROUGH USE OF RECAPTURE ESTIMATES (OUD CAPTURE) - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT OPIOID USE DISORDER (OUD) REMAINS A CRITICAL PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERN IN THE UNITED STATES WITH AN ESTIMATED 2.08% PREVALENCE AMONG INDIVIDUALS AGED 12 AND OLDER. THIS ESTIMATE IS WIDELY RECOGNIZED AS AN UNDERESTIMATE ARISING FROM INHERENT LIMITATIONS OF DIRECT MEASURES SUCH AS SURVEYS FROM THE NATIONAL SURVEY ON DRUG USE AND HEALTH. COMPOUNDING THESE LIMITATIONS IS THE LACK OF COUNTY-LEVEL PREVALENCE ESTIMATES, WHICH ARE ESSENTIAL FOR TARGETED TREATMENT, RESOURCE ALLOCATION, AND POLICY DEVELOPMENT. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO CHANGE THIS STATUS QUO BY USING CAPTURE-RECAPTURE (CRC) ANALYSIS AND TWO STATE-OF-THE-ART BAYESIAN MODELING TECHNIQUES TO ESTIMATE OUD PREVALENCE FOR THE LARGEST NUMBER OF COUNTIES EVER ATTEMPTED WITH PROJECTIONS TO ALL U.S. COUNTIES ONCE RECRUITMENT AIMS ARE ACHIEVED. IN AIM 1, WE GENERATE ESTIMATES OF OUD PREVALENCE USING CRC, THE BEST AVAILABLE METHOD FOR ESTIMATING THE UNKNOWN COMPONENT OF THE POPULATION WITH OUD, BY COUNTY AND YEAR (MOST RECENT AVAILABLE) WITH LINKED DATA FROM MULTIPLE PARTICIPATING STATES AND COMPARE RESULTS TO BAYESIAN BENCHMARK MULTIPLIER (BBM) AND BAYESIAN INTEGRATED ABUNDANCE (BIA) MODELS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL CONDUCT BAYESIAN SPATIAL REGRESSION ANALYSES TO ASSOCIATE OUD PREVALENCE ESTIMATES FROM CRC WITH PUBLICLY AVAILABLE COVARIATES AT THE COUNTY-LEVEL TO EVENTUALLY USE THOSE COEFFICIENTS FOR ITERATIVELY PROJECTING OUD PREVALENCE TO MISSING COUNTIES. IN AIM 3, WE FOCUS ON RECRUITMENT OF ADDITIONAL STATES PRIMARILY PARTICIPATING IN THE U.S. CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION'S OVERDOSE TO ACTION PROJECT. THE FINDINGS FROM THIS PROJECT, CALLED OPIOID USE DISORDER COUNTY AREA PREVALENCE THROUGH USE OF RECAPTURE ESTIMATES (OUD CAPTURE), WILL INFORM TARGETED PUBLIC HEALTH RESPONSES, PROVIDE A TRANSFERABLE AND ADAPTABLE FRAMEWORK FOR ESTIMATING “HIDDEN” AND VULNERABLE POPULATIONS UNDER VARIOUS STATE RESOURCE ENVIRONMENTS, AND OPTIMIZE THE NATION'S CONSIDERABLE STATE AND FEDERAL INVESTMENTS IN LINKING ADMINISTRATIVE DATASETS.

description: DIFFERENTIATING HARMS FROM COMBUSTION VS. ADDICTION: EFFECTS OF LOW NICOTINE CIGARETTE EDUCATION ON BELIEFS AND BEHAVIORS - PROJECT ABSTRACT  SMOKING TOBACCO IS RESPONSIBLE FOR 490,000 DEATHS IN THE U.S. EACH YEAR AND THESE DEATHS RESULT FROM EXPOSURE TO CARCINOGENS AND OTHER TOXICANTS IN TOBACCO OR PRODUCED BY TOBACCO COMBUSTION. NICOTINE IS THE ADDICTIVE SUBSTANCE IN TOBACCO PRODUCTS, BUT NOT THE CAUSE OF SMOKING-ATTRIBUTABLE DISEASE AND DEATH. FOR DECADES, U.S. ADULTS HAVE EQUATED THE HARMS OF TOBACCO USE WITH THE NICOTINE IN TOBACCO PRODUCTS, FAILING TO DIFFERENTIATE THE HEALTH HARMS OF COMBUSTION VERSUS ADDICTION. LOW NICOTINE CIGARETTES ARE A UNIQUE PRODUCT AT THE NEXUS OF THESE MISPERCEPTIONS. MARKETED AS HAVING “95% LESS NICOTINE” AND PROPOSED AS A POLICY STRATEGY TO REDUCE TOBACCO-RELATED HARMS LARGELY THROUGH SMOKING CESSATION, PERVASIVE MISPERCEPTIONS ABOUT LOW NICOTINE CIGARETTES HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO HARM HEALTH, PARTICULARLY AMONG PEOPLE WHO SMOKE CIGARETTES. PEOPLE WHO PERCEIVE THAT “LOWER NICOTINE MEANS LESS HARM” MAY CONTINUE SMOKING CIGARETTES RATHER THAN QUIT, AVOID EVIDENCE- BASED NICOTINE REPLACEMENT THERAPY, OR WORSE, SWITCH FROM NON-COMBUSTED TOBACCO TO LOW NICOTINE CIGARETTES TO REDUCE THEIR NICOTINE EXPOSURE. A CIGARETTE PERCEIVED AS “LESS HARMFUL” OR “LESS ADDICTIVE” MAY ALSO FACILITATE SMOKING UPTAKE IN NON-USERS OR NON-COMBUSTED TOBACCO USERS. ADDRESSING THE DISCONNECT BETWEEN PERCEPTIONS OF ADDICTION AND HARM WILL BE ESSENTIAL TO REDUCING SMOKING-RELATED MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY IN THE CONTEXT OF LOW NICOTINE CIGARETTES. THIS STUDY BUILDS ON OUR EXPERTISE USING RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS WITH COMPLEMENTARY MEASURES TO UNDERSTAND THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN TAILORED EDUCATION ABOUT LOW NICOTINE CIGARETTES (LNC) AND ASSOCIATED BELIEFS AND BEHAVIORS IN THE REAL WORLD. AIM 1 ESTIMATES THE PROSPECTIVE POPULATION-LEVEL IMPACT OF TAILORED LNC EDUCATION IN A NATIONAL SAMPLE OF ADULTS WHO SMOKE CIGARETTES, WHILE CAPTURING POSSIBLE UNINTENDED EFFECTS IN ADULT NON-USERS AND NON-COMBUSTED TOBACCO USERS. AIM 2 ESTIMATES THE INDEPENDENT AND JOINT EFFECTS OF TAILORED LNC EDUCATION AND EXPOSURE TO “LOW NICOTINE” MARKETING ON SMOKING BELIEFS AND BEHAVIORS IN ADULTS WHO SMOKE AND RECEIVE LOW NICOTINE CIGARETTES FOR THE DURATION OF THE STUDY. PRIMARY OUTCOMES FOR BOTH TRIALS ARE LNC BELIEFS AND INTENTION/USE OF LNC CIGARETTES; SECONDARY OUTCOMES ARE BELIEFS ABOUT NICOTINE, COMBUSTION, AND ADDICTION, AND INTENTIONS/USE OF COMBUSTED AND NON-COMBUSTED TOBACCO. GUIDED BY THE THEORY OF PLANNED BEHAVIOR, FINDINGS FROM THIS PROJECT WILL INFORM COMMUNICATION STRATEGIES TO EDUCATE CONSUMERS AND THE PUBLIC ABOUT LOW NICOTINE CIGARETTES ALONGSIDE CHANGES IN THE MARKET. THIS STUDY MAY ALSO PROVIDE A MODEL FOR EDUCATING CONSUMERS ABOUT SUBSTANCES WITH VARYING RISKS AND BENEFITS, LIKE CANNABIS, WHERE RAPID EVOLUTION IN POLICIES AND MARKETING MAY IMPACT MISPERCEPTIONS OF ADDICTIVENESS AND HARM.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NEUROBIOLOGICAL CORRELATES OF SUSCEPTIBILITY, RESILIENCE, AND RECOVERY TO SUBSTANCE ABUSE IN PARTICIPANTS WITH CHILDHOOD MALTREATMENT - PROJECT SUMMARY CHILDHOOD ADVERSITY IS A CRITICAL RISK FACTOR FOR SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUDS), YET SUBSTANTIAL NUMBERS OF EXPOSED INDIVIDUALS REMAIN RESILIENT. UNDERSTANDING NEUROBIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING RESILIENCE MAY PROVIDE INSIGHTS FOR PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION. USING DIFFUSION TENSOR IMAGING AND STRUCTURAL CONNECTOME ANALYSIS, WE IDENTIFIED NINE BRAIN NETWORK NODES WHERE REDUCED NODAL EFFICIENCY DISTINGUISHED RESILIENT FROM SUSCEPTIBLE YOUNG ADULTS WITH COMPARABLE CHILDHOOD MALTREATMENT, ACHIEVING ~80% CROSS-VALIDATED CLASSIFICATION ACCURACY. THESE FINDINGS SUGGEST RESILIENT INDIVIDUALS ARE NOT UNAFFECTED BUT EFFECTIVELY COMPENSATED THROUGH SPECIFIC NETWORK ADAPTATIONS. THIS PROPOSAL VALIDATES AND EXTENDS THESE FINDINGS IN THE ADOLESCENT BRAIN COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT (ABCD) STUDY, THE LARGEST LONGITUDINAL NEUROIMAGING STUDY OF ADOLESCENT DEVELOPMENT (N~11,000). WE EMPLOY AN EXPOSOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDY (EXWAS) APPROACH TO IDENTIFY HIGH-RISK YOUTH BASED ON COMPREHENSIVE MULTI-DOMAIN ADVERSITY BURDEN. GROWTH MIXTURE MODELING WILL IDENTIFY SUBSTANCE USE TRAJECTORIES, CLASSIFYING PARTICIPANTS AS RESILIENT (HIGH ADVERSITY, LOW SUBSTANCE USE), SUSCEPTIBLE (HIGH ADVERSITY, ESCALATING USE), OR LOW-RISK CONTROLS. THREE AIMS WILL: (1) VALIDATE OUR RESILIENCE NETWORK MODEL USING MODERN TRACTOGRAPHY AND HIGHER-RESOLUTION PARCELLATIONS, TESTING WHETHER NETWORK FEATURES DISTINGUISH RESILIENT FROM SUSCEPTIBLE ADOLESCENTS DESPITE EQUIVALENT EXPOSOME BURDEN AND EXAMINING DISORDER-SPECIFIC VERSUS TRANSDIAGNOSTIC MECHANISMS; (2) DISTINGUISH CONSTITUTIONAL RESILIENCE (PROTECTIVE FEATURES PRESENT AT BASELINE, AGES 9-10) FROM ACQUIRED RESILIENCE (PROGRESSIVE NODE RECRUITMENT ACROSS ADOLESCENCE), REVEALING WHETHER RESILIENCE IS FIXED OR MODIFIABLE; (3) IDENTIFY MODIFIABLE PROTECTIVE FACTORS (FAMILY SUPPORT, SCHOOL ENGAGEMENT, PEER RELATIONSHIPS, ACTIVITIES) ASSOCIATING WITH RESILIENT ARCHITECTURE AND PRECEDING NODE RECRUITMENT, USING MACHINE LEARNING TO DETERMINE WHICH FACTORS AT WHICH AGES MOST STRONGLY PROMOTE RESILIENCE. EXPLORATORY ANALYSES TEST WHETHER SLEEP DISRUPTION MEDIATES NETWORK EFFECTS ON SUBSTANCE USE, BUILDING ON OUR FINDING THAT SLEEP EFFICIENCY MEDIATED 39-46% OF MALTREATMENT EFFECTS ON BRAIN STRUCTURE. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SLEEP DEGRADATION EMERGES 12-18 MONTHS BEFORE SUBSTANCE USE ESCALATION, PROVIDING AN INTERVENTION WINDOW. THIS RESEARCH ESTABLISHES WHETHER NETWORK ARCHITECTURE REPRESENTS A ROBUST BIOMARKER OF SUD RESILIENCE; REVEALS MODIFIABLE ENVIRONMENTAL TARGETS AND CRITICAL DEVELOPMENTAL WINDOWS; AND DISTINGUISHES CONSTITUTIONAL FROM ACQUIRED RESILIENCE TO INFORM PRECISION PREVENTION. IDENTIFYING NATURALLY-OCCURRING PROTECTIVE BRAIN ADAPTATIONS AND FOSTERING EXPERIENCES TRANSFORMS RESILIENCE FROM ABSTRACT CONSTRUCT INTO ACTIONABLE PREVENTION TARGETS FOR HIGH-RISK YOUTH.

description: NATIONAL LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF VIOLENCE AND SUBSTANCE USE IN THE UNITED STATES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT VIOLENCE REMAINS A SIGNIFICANT AND PREVENTABLE CAUSE OF INJURY, MORTALITY, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUDS), AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH BURDEN IN THE UNITED STATES. DESPITE THIS, MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH DATA SYSTEMS FREQUENTLY HAVE OMITTED VARIABLES, CONTRIBUTING TO SURVEILLANCE GAPS IN HOW VIOLENCE IS TRACKED AND UNDERSTOOD. THESE OMISSIONS LIMIT OUR ABILITY TO ASSESS SAFETY RISKS, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, SUDS, AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS THAT INFLUENCE THE ONSET AND PROGRESSION OF HARM. EXISTING LIMITATIONS IN NATIONAL DATA COLLECTION AND COHORT DESIGN MAKE IT DIFFICULT TO ACCURATELY ESTIMATE PREVALENCE, UNDERSTAND RISK TRAJECTORIES, OR IDENTIFY PROTECTIVE FACTORS ACROSS AFFECTED POPULATIONS. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A NATIONWIDE PROSPECTIVE DIGITAL COHORT OF 1,200 ADULTS AT INCREASED RISK OF EXPOSURE TO VIOLENCE. PARTICIPANTS WILL COMPLETE STRUCTURED SURVEYS EVERY SIX MONTHS OVER A 24-MONTH PERIOD, AND A SUBSET WILL PARTICIPATE IN LONGITUDINAL QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS TO PROVIDE CONTEXTUAL DEPTH ON EXPERIENCES OF VIOLENCE, PERCEIVED SAFETY, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, SUDS, AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES. THE STUDY’S OBJECTIVES ARE TO: (1) ESTIMATE THE PREVALENCE AND PATTERNS OF VIOLENCE AND CO- OCCURRING SUBSTANCE MISUSE AND SUDS; (2) EXAMINE INDIVIDUAL, RELATIONAL, COMMUNITY, AND SOCIETAL FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH RISK AND PROTECTION; AND (3) ASSESS ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN VIOLENCE EXPOSURE, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, SUDS, AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS. BY LEVERAGING A FLEXIBLE DIGITAL COHORT MODEL, THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE TIMELY, ACTIONABLE DATA TO ENHANCE PUBLIC HEALTH SURVEILLANCE, INFORM PREVENTION STRATEGIES, AND GUIDE RESOURCE ALLOCATION FOR INDIVIDUALS AFFECTED BY VIOLENCE, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, SUDS, AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT OF THE PAIN (PAIN AI INTERVENTION) PLATFORM FOR PATIENTS AT HOME - PROJECT SUMMARY PAIN MEASUREMENT RELIES ON PATIENT-REPORTED SCALES, PRONE TO FOUR CRUCIAL OBSTACLES: HIGH SUBJECTIVITY, THE NEED FOR CONSCIOUSNESS, THE EVALUATION AT ONLY ONE POINT, AND THE INABILITY TO DESCRIBE PAIN’S COMPLEXITY. THE CORE INNOVATION WITHIN THIS PROJECT CENTERS ON DEPLOYING OUR PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED AND VALIDATED DEEP LEARNING ALGORITHMS LEVERAGING CONTINUOUS PHYSIOLOGIC DATA CAPTURED USING A WEARABLE SENSOR. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE RECOGNITION OF PHYSIOLOGIC PATTERNS DRIVEN BY PAIN RESPONSES (I.E., PHYSIOLOGICAL DATA SUCH AS HEART RATE, RESPIRATORY RATE, AND HEART RATE VARIABILITY (HRV)) WILL ALLOW FOR ACCURATE AND SAFE THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION IN A CLOSED-LOOP INDIVIDUALIZED SENSOR-BASED ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)-ENABLED SYSTEM. THIS PROJECT WILL ALLOW THE CREATION OF A REAL-TIME, AT-HOME CONTINUOUS PHYSIOLOGIC MONITORING DATABASE FROM WHICH A PAIN BIOMARKER WILL BE CREATED USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE. THE OVERARCHING GOAL IS TO PERSONALIZE PAIN MEDICATION REGIMENS LEVERAGING SENSOR-DRIVEN, DIGITAL ECOSYSTEMS THAT CAN RECOGNIZE SUBTLE MARKERS OF PAIN AND OVER-MEDICATION. MULTIPLE SENSORS IN A SINGLE DEVICE (ECG, PPG, EDA, BODY MOVEMENT, TEMPERATURE, BAROMETRIC PRESSURE, AND OXYGEN SATURATION) WILL BE USED, SUPPLEMENTED WITH A BLOOD PRESSURE CUFF AND FINGER PULSE OXIMETER, THEREBY BUILDING A COMPOSITE AND OBJECTIVE PROFILE TO DETERMINE PAIN NEEDS AND SAFETY INDICATORS. TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS, WE PLAN ON 1) CHARACTERIZING MULTIMODAL PHYSIOLOGIC AND PSYCHOSOCIAL SIGNATURES OF POSTOPERATIVE PAIN, 2) VALIDATING MACHINE LEARNING/ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (ML/AI) MODELS TO ESTIMATE PAIN INTENSITY AND OPIOID RESPONSE, AND 3) EVALUATING THE ACCEPTABILITY, APPROPRIATENESS, FEASIBILITY, AND INTEGRATION POTENTIAL OF THE OMNI-AI ECOSYSTEM IN OUTPATIENT CARE. A TOTAL OF 500 PATIENTS WILL BE RECRUITED AT THEIR INITIAL PREOPERATIVE CONSULTATION AND GENERAL ANXIETY LEVELS AND PAIN CATASTROPHIZING ATTITUDES WILL BE MEASURED USING THE STATE-TRAIT ANXIETY INVENTORY (STAI) AND PAIN CATASTROPHIZING SCALE (PCS). THE PATIENTS WILL EVALUATE THEIR PAIN INTENSITY USING THE NUMERICAL RATING SCORE (NRS) CONCOMITANTLY. AFTER THE SURGERY, THE WEARABLE OMNI DEVICES WILL CONTINUOUSLY RECORD PHYSIOLOGIC SIGNALS, WHICH WILL BE STORED ON-DEVICE DURING THE 5-DAY HOME MONITORING PERIOD AND SECURELY TRANSFERRED TO MAYO CLINIC SERVERS AFTER DEVICE RETURN. DURING DAYTIME HOURS (8 AM, 12 PM, 4 PM, AND 8 PM), PATIENTS WILL BE PROMPTED BY A MAYO CLINIC-DEVELOPED MOBILE APP TO SUBMIT AN NRS PAIN EVALUATION AND RECORD MEDICATION CONSUMPTION, WITH THE OPTION TO ENTER ADDITIONAL REPORTS AT ANY TIME WHEN THEY EXPERIENCE PAIN. WE WILL CREATE A DATA BANK WITH SUBJECT-SPECIFIC TIME SERIES, INCLUDING PHYSIOLOGICAL VARIABLES AND SELF-REPORTED PAIN SCORES. TO MEASURE THE ACCEPTABILITY, APPROPRIATENESS, AND FEASIBILITY OF OUR PROPOSED INTERVENTION, WE WILL USE THE VALIDATED ACCEPTABILITY OF INTERVENTION MEASURE (AIM), INTERVENTION APPROPRIATENESS MEASURE (IAM), AND THE FEASIBILITY OF INTERVENTION MEASURE (FIM) SURVEYS. THIS WILL BE ACHIEVED BY PERFORMING A PHONE INTERVIEW FIVE DAYS AFTER THE STUDY DISCHARGE. THE CONSOLIDATED FRAMEWORK FOR IMPLEMENTATION RESEARCH (CFIR) WILL ALSO BE DEPLOYED TO ASSESS INTEGRATION POTENTIAL.

description: PSILOCYBIN-ASSISTED ACT FOR CO-OCCURRING COCAINE USE DISORDER AND MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER - PROJECT SUMMARY  COCAINE USE DISORDER (CUD) IS NOTORIOUSLY DIFFICULT TO TREAT AND IS FREQUENTLY COMPLICATED BY MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER (MDD), A CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT COMORBIDITY AFFECTING AS MANY AS 40% OF INDIVIDUALS WITH CUD. THIS CO-OCCURRENCE IS ASSOCIATED WITH GREATER ILLNESS SEVERITY, IMPAIRED PSYCHOSOCIAL FUNCTIONING, AND POORER TREATMENT OUTCOMES. DESPITE ITS HIGH PREVALENCE AND CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE, CUD-MDD HAS RECEIVED FAR LESS RESEARCH ATTENTION THAN EITHER CONDITION ALONE, AND TRADITIONAL PHARMACOLOGICAL APPROACHES HAVE SHOWN LIMITED EFFICACY. ALTHOUGH THERE IS BROAD CONSENSUS ON THE NEED FOR INTERVENTIONS THAT TARGET SHARED MECHANISMS UNDERLYING BOTH CUD AND MDD, NO INTEGRATED INTERVENTIONS HAVE YET BEEN DEVELOPED OR EMPIRICALLY VALIDATED. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS INITIAL RESEARCH IS TO ADDRESS THIS CRITICAL GAP BY EVALUATING AN INTEGRATED TREATMENT FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH CO-OCCURRING CUD-MDD.  WE PRESENT A STRONG SCIENTIFIC PREMISE FOR DEVELOPING AND PRELIMINARILY TESTING PSILOCYBIN-ASSISTED ACCEPTANCE AND COMMITMENT THERAPY (ACT) FOR CUD-MDD. PSILOCYBIN HAS SHOWN ROBUST, CONSISTENT EFFICACY FOR MDD, EARNING “BREAKTHROUGH THERAPY” DESIGNATION FROM THE US FDA, WITH EMERGING EVIDENCE SUPPORTING ITS POTENTIAL UTILITY IN TREATING SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS. CONTEXTUAL BEHAVIORAL THERAPIES SUCH AS ACT HAVE SHOWN EFFICACY IN TREATING CUD IN OUR PRIOR WORK AND HAVE ALSO BEEN FOUND TO ENHANCE OUTCOMES IN PSILOCYBIN- ASSISTED THERAPY FOR MDD. AT THE PROCESS LEVEL, BOTH PSILOCYBIN AND ACT PROMOTE PSYCHOLOGICAL FLEXIBILITY (PF) BY DISRUPTING MALADAPTIVE REPETITIVE OR RUMINATIVE THOUGHT PATTERNS AND ALLOWING FOR INCREASED FOCUS ON VALUES-BASED ACTION. NEUROIMAGING STUDIES FURTHER INDICATE THAT BOTH INTERVENTIONS REDUCE ACTIVITY WITHIN THE DEFAULT MODE NETWORK (DMN) – A BRAIN NETWORK ASSOCIATED WITH SELF-REFERENTIAL PROCESSING AND RUMINATION, WHICH ARE CENTRALLY IMPLICATED IN PF. THESE SHARED PSYCHOLOGICAL AND NEURAL PROCESSES REPRESENT KEY TRANSDIAGNOSTIC MECHANISMS THAT CAN BE EFFECTIVELY TARGETED THROUGH PSILOCYBIN-ASSISTED ACT.  WE WILL CONDUCT A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL TO EVALUATE PSILOCYBIN-ASSISTED ACT FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH CUD-MDD. IN A 6-WEEK PRIMARY TREATMENT PHASE (PHASE 1), PARTICIPANTS (N=50) WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO A SINGLE, BLINDED DOSE OF PSILOCYBIN (25 MG) OR AN ACTIVE PLACEBO (DIPHENHYDRAMINE, 50 MG), BOTH DELIVERED WITHIN A MANUALIZED ACT PLATFORM. AIM 1 WILL ASSESS EFFECTS ON COCAINE ABSTINENCE AND DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS; AIM 2 WILL EXAMINE MECHANISTIC OUTCOMES, INCLUDING PF AND DMN CHANGES USING NOVEL MULTIMODAL IMAGING. IN A SUBSEQUENT 6-WEEK BLINDED EXTENSION PHASE (PHASE 2), ALL PARTICIPANTS WILL RECEIVE 25 MG PSILOCYBIN TO EXAMINE WITHIN- AND BETWEEN-GROUP EFFECTS OF ONE VERSUS TWO DOSES (EXPLORATORY AIM 3), WHILE MITIGATING POTENTIAL UNBLINDING AND NOCEBO EFFECTS. BAYESIAN POSTERIOR PROBABILITIES INDICATING STRONG EVIDENCE FOR PSILOCYBIN-ASSISTED ACT WILL INFORM PROGRESSION TO A LARGER EFFICACY-EFFECTIVENESS TRIAL, LAYING THE FOUNDATION FOR AN INTEGRATED, BEHAVIORAL-PHARMACOLOGICAL INTERVENTION FOR THIS UNDERSERVED POPULATION.

description: CRCNS: EFFICIENT CONTROL OF BEHAVIORAL AND NEURAL VARIABILITY DURING PERCEPTUAL DECISION-MAKING - PERCEPTUAL DECISIONS UNDER UNCERTAINTY FEATURE BEHAVIORAL VARIABILITY. A MAJOR SOURCE OF THIS VARIABILITY ARE COMPUTATIONAL LIMITS IN COGNITIVE CONTROL AND INFERENCE UNDERLYING THESE DECISIONS. FOR HIGHER-LEVEL COGNITIVE TASKS, HUMANS CAN INCREASE THE ACCURACY OF MENTAL OPERATIONS THROUGH MOTIVATED (EFFORTFUL) CONTROL. WE ASK IF THEY CAN ALSO DO SO FOR PERCEPTUAL DECISIONS UNDER UNCERTAINTY, BY CONTROLLING THE PRECISION OF SENSORY EVIDENCE ACCUMULATION. WE WILL ADDRESS THIS QUESTION THROUGH A MULTI-FACETED APPROACH. COMBINING IDEAS FROM NOISY PERCEPTUAL DECISION-MAKING WITH THOSE FROM CONTROL OF MENTAL EFFORT, WE WILL DERIVE NORMATIVE PRINCIPLES FOR THE CONTROL OF COMPUTATIONAL NOISE IN PERCEPTUAL DECISION-MAKING. THESE PRINCIPLES TRADE OFF THE EXPECTED INCREASE IN DECISION-MAKING PERFORMANCE DUE TO LOWER NOISE WITH THE INTRINSIC EFFORT COST OF CONTROL. WE WILL USE THE RESULTING MODELS TO MAKE PREDICTIONS ALONG TWO AXES: THE IMPACT OF (I) MOTIVATION/REWARD AND (II) PRIOR BELIEFS/EXPECTANCIES ON THE EXPECTED CONTROL OF COMPUTATIONAL NOISE. WE WILL TEST THESE PREDICTIONS IN HUMAN BEHAVIORAL DECISION-MAKING EXPERIMENTS TO ASSESS THEIR IMPACT ON DECISION-MAKING PERFORMANCE. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL PERFORM SIMILAR EXPERIMENTS WHILE RECORDING TIME- RESOLVED BRAIN ACTIVITY IN MAGNETOENCEPHALOGRAPHY (MEG) TO CHARACTERIZE THE TIME COURSE OF THE NEURAL PATTERNS AND ASSOCIATED COMPUTATIONS LEADING TO THESE DECISIONS. WE WILL COMPARE THE GEOMETRY OF THESE PATTERNS TO PREDICTIONS FROM HIGH-DIMENSIONAL ARTIFICIAL RECURRENT NEURAL NETWORKS WITH INTRINSIC NOISE THAT CAN CONTROL THEIR OWN NOISE AT A COST, AND THAT ARE TRAINED ON THE SAME TASKS AS HUMAN PARTICIPANTS. LASTLY, WE WILL PERFORM A LONGITUDINAL ONLINE STUDY TO LINK INTERINDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES IN THE ABILITY OF DECISION-MAKING NOISE CONTROL TO COGNITIVE TRAITS AND SUBCLINICAL PSYCHIATRIC SYMPTOMS, INCLUDING TRANSDIAGNOSTIC DIMENSIONS ASSOCIATED WITH SUBSTANCE ABUSE. OVERALL, OUR STUDY WILL PROVIDE A THOROUGH INVESTIGATION OF THE CONTROL OF THE PRECISION OF NOISY COMPUTATION UNDERLYING HUMAN PERCEPTUAL DECISIONS, USING A MULTI-FACETED APPROACH THAT COMBINES NORMATIVE AND MECHANISTIC MODELS WITH HUMAN BEHAVIORAL AND MEG EXPERIMENTS, AND WITH POTENTIAL RELEVANCE TO MECHANISMS OF DECISION DYSFUNCTION IN ADDICTION. RELEVANCE (SEE INSTRUCTIONS): THE PROPOSED WORK TARGETS MECHANISMS OF DECISION VARIABILITY AND COGNITIVE CONTROL UNDER UNCERTAINTY. IT CHARACTERIZES PROCESSES CENTRAL TO JUDGMENT AND SELF-REGULATION THAT ARE DISRUPTED IN SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, SHAPING RISKY CHOICE AND DIFFICULTY ABSTAINING FROM DRUGS. THE LONGITUDINAL COMPONENT LINKS DECISION PHENOTYPES TO SYMPTOMS AND TRANSDIAGNOSTIC DIMENSIONS ASSOCIATED WITH ADDICTIVE BEHAVIORS, HELPING IDENTIFY MARKERS AND TARGETS FOR FUTURE INTERVENTIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE ROLE OF SALIVARY PROTEINS IN MODULATING TASTE PERCEPTION IN HUMANS - PROJECT SUMMARY WE PROPOSE TO COMBINE PSYCHOPHYSICAL ASSESSMENTS OF TASTE PERCEPTION WITH SALIVARY PROTEOMIC ANALYSIS IN INDIVIDUALS WITH VARYING DEGREES OF DIETARY RESTRICTION TO DETERMINE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DIET, THE SALIVARY PROTEOME, AND TASTE PERCEPTION. THIS RESEARCH AIMS TO FILL A CRITICAL VOID OF LONGITUDINAL STUDIES ASSOCIATING CHANGES IN THE SALIVARY PROTEOME WITH CHANGES IN TASTE DETECTION, LIKING, AND ACCEPTANCE IN HUMANS AS A FUNCTION OF DIET. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL USE ESTABLISHED PROTOCOLS TO ACQUIRE SALIVA AND MEASURE TASTE PERCEPTION AND FOOD INTAKE IN INDIVIDUALS WITH A RIGIDLY RESTRICTED LOW-CALORIE DIET (I.E., ANOREXIA NERVOSA; AN), VEGETARIAN DIET, KETOGENIC DIET, AND UNRESTRICTED DIET AT TWO TIMEPOINTS. IN THE AN GROUP, MEASURES WILL BE COLLECTED PRIOR TO AND FOLLOWING ~ 5 WEEKS (AVERAGE LENGTH OF INPATIENT STAY) OF REPEATED CONSUMMATORY EXPOSURES OF A WIDE VARIETY DIET AS PART OF A STRUCTURED, BEHAVIORAL TREATMENT PROTOCOL. MEASURES WILL BE COLLECTED ~5 WEEKS APART IN THE OTHER DIET GROUPS. THIS STUDY DESIGN WILL PERMIT US TO TEST THE FOLLOWING HYPOTHESES: 1) HABITUATION TO A RESTRICTED DIET IS ACCOMPANIED BY CHANGES IN THE SALIVARY PROTEOME AND ALTERED TASTE PREFERENCE AND ACCEPTANCE FOR AND SENSITIVITY TO THIS RESTRICTED DIET; 2) SALIVARY PROTEINS ARE UPREGULATED AND DOWNREGULATED IN RESPONSE TO CHANGES IN CONSUMPTION FROM A RIGID LOW CALORIE ANORECTIC DIET TO A WIDE VARIETY DIET; 3) CHANGES IN THE SALIVARY PROTEOME WILL CORRELATE WITH CHANGES IN TASTE PERCEPTION AND FOOD CHOICE. WE ANTICIPATE THAT THIS STUDY WILL ALSO FILL A CRITICAL NEXT STEP TOWARD THE DEVELOPMENT OF ESSENTIAL OBJECTIVE RESEARCH AND CLINICAL TOOLS FOR MONITORING DIETARY INTAKE.

description: INTERACTIONS BETWEEN RESIDENT MICROBIOTA AND INVADING MIDDLE EAR PATHOGENS - SUMMARY ACUTE INFECTIONS OF THE MIDDLE EARS (ACUTE OTITIS MEDIA, AOM) ARE A WIDESPREAD PROBLEM AND A LEADING CAUSE OF ANTIBIOTIC (OVER) USE AND AMBULATORY SURGERIES IN CHILDREN GLOBALLY, INCLUDING IN THE UNITED STATES. THE REASON(S) WHY LARGE NUMBERS OF INFANTS ARE PRONE TO RECURRENT BACTERIAL EAR INFECTIONS IS NOT FULLY UNDERSTOOD, BUT THERE IS GROWING EVIDENCE OF A CENTRAL ROLE OF THE RESIDENT MICROBIOTA OF THE NASOPHARYNX IN MEDIATING SUSCEPTIBILITY/RESISTANCE TO AOM. HUMAN AND ANIMAL STUDIES SHOW THAT THE RESPIRATORY MICROBIOTA OF HEALTHY ADULTS IS RELATIVELY STABLE AND CAN CONFERS PROTECTION AGAINST COLONIZATION AND INVASION BY PATHOGENS OF THE MIDDLE EAR (ME). HOWEVER, IN NEONATES/INFANTS/CHILDREN THE MICROBIOTA CAN BE MUCH MORE DYNAMIC AND CHANGING, AND CAN MORE EASILY BE DISRUPTED BY ANTIBIOTICS (DYSBIOSIS). THUS THE MOST COMMON TREATMENT FOR AOM, ANTIBIOTICS, COULD POTENTIALLY DESTABILIZE THE CHILD'S MICROBIOTA, DISRUPTING THE RESISTANCE IT CAN CONFER AND MAKING THE CHILD MORE SUSCEPTIBLE TO SUBSEQUENT, POTENTIALLY REPEATED AOM. ALTHOUGH THIS STRING OF ARGUMENTS IS FAIRLY WELL ACCEPTED, THERE IS A SUBSTANTIAL KNOWLEDGE GAP IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW RESIDENT MICROBES PROTECT AGAINST RESPIRATORY AND OTOPATHOGENS, AND HOW ANTIBIOTIC- INDUCED DISRUPTION OF THE RESPIRATORY MICROBIOTA MIGHT CAUSE SUSCEPTIBILITY TO COLONIZATION AND PATHOGENESIS, INCREASING AOM. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT INFANTS ARE MORE SENSITIVE TO RESPIRATORY AND OTOPATHOGENS BECAUSE THEY LACK A STABLE MICROBIOTA THAT CAN CONFER RESISTANCE. WE WILL TEST THIS IN TWO COMPLEMENTARY WAYS. WE WILL USE TOPICAL ANTIBIOTICS TO LOCALLY DISRUPT THE RESIDENT MICROBIOTA, INDUCING A STATE OF DYSBIOSIS WITHIN THE RESPIRATORY TRACT. OUR NEW PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT SUCH TREATMENT CAN SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASE SUSCEPTIBILITY TO RESPIRATORY AND MIDDLE EAR (ME) PATHOGENS. HERE WE WILL DEFINE THIS EFFECT AND MEASURE HOW IT DIFFERS IN NEONATES, ADOLESCENTS AND ADULTS, WHICH DIFFER SUBSTANTIALLY IN THE MAKEUP AND STABILITY OF MICROBIOTA. WE WILL FOLLOW A HIGHLY COMPLEMENTARY APPROACH THAT TAKES ADVANTAGE OF OUR RECENT WORK ESTABLISHING A NASOPHARYNGEAL CONSORTIUM OF COMMENSALS (NPCC) COMPOSED OF MICROORGANISMS THAT CORRELATE WITH HEALTH (LACK OF AOM) IN A LARGE COHORT OF CHILDREN. OUR EXCITING PRELIMINARY DATA IN EXPERIMENTAL INFECTIONS IN MICE NOW DEMONSTRATE THAT THIS NPCC CAN SUCCESSFULLY COLONIZE/PERSIST AND CONFER SUBSTANTIAL RESISTANCE TO RESPIRATORY AND OTOPATHOGENS IN MICE. WE WILL NOW DEFINE THE RESISTANCE CONFERRED IN NEONATES, ADOLESCENT AND ADULT MICE. THESE IN VIVO EXPERIMENTS WILL IDENTIFY SPECIFIC INTERBACTERIAL INTERACTIONS THAT CONFER RESISTANCE TO AOM, AND CAN GUIDE THE USE OF IN VITRO EXPERIMENTS IN AIR-LIQUID INTERFACE (ALI) CONDITIONS THAT CLOSELY MIMIC THE MAMMALIAN RESPIRATORY TRACT, THAT WILL DEFINE THE MECHANISMS INVOLVED. THIS WORK WILL SUBSTANTIALLY GUIDE MORE ENLIGHTENED APPROACHES TO REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF AOM AND THE ANTIBIOTIC-INDUCED DYSBIOSIS THAT HAS THE POTENTIAL TO CONTRIBUTE TO LONG TERM HEALTH PROBLEMS FOR MANY CHILDREN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DENDRITIC INTEGRATION AND SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY IN THE MSO - PROJECT SUMMARY HUMANS AND OTHER MAMMALS USE THE TEMPORAL FINE STRUCTURE IN SOUNDS TO IDENTIFY AND HELP LOCALIZE AUDITORY OBJECTS IN THREE-DIMENSIONAL SPACE. THE BROAD GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH IS BOTH TO UNDERSTAND HOW SOUND LOCALIZATION CUES ARE PROCESSED IN THE BRAIN AS WELL AS TO UNDERSTAND HOW NEURONS IN THE UNDERLYING CIRCUITRY ACQUIRE THE APPROPRIATE SYNAPTIC WEIGHTS AND FIRING PROPERTIES DURING DEVELOPMENT. THIS PROPOSAL FOCUSES ON THE MEDIAL SUPERIOR OLIVE (MSO), THE FIRST AND CRITICAL STAGE FOR PROCESSING INTERAURAL TIME DIFFERENCES (ITDS) FROM THE TWO EARS, CUES THAT ARE USED FOR HORIZONTAL SOUND LOCALIZATION AS WELL AS FOR UNDERSTANDING SPEECH PATTERNS IN CHALLENGING LISTENING ENVIRONMENTS. MSO NEURONS ARE RELATIVELY UNSPECIALIZED AT HEARING ONSET AND MUST PROGRESSIVELY DEVELOP THE ABILITY TO PROCESS ITDS DURING EARLY AUDITORY EXPERIENCE. TO DO SO, MSO NEURONS MUST COORDINATE ALTERATIONS IN INTRINSIC CELL EXCITABILITY WITH CHANGES IN DENDRITIC MORPHOLOGY AND SYNAPTIC STRENGTH. HEARING LOSS DURING EARLY DEVELOPMENT, EVEN IF ONLY TEMPORARY, IS KNOWN TO PRODUCE LONG-TERM DEFICITS IN BOTH SOUND LOCALIZATION AND SPEECH PERCEPTION IN HUMANS. HOWEVER, WE HAVE A GAP IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW BINAURAL PROCESSING IN THE MSO IS IMPACTED BY AUDITORY EXPERIENCE BECAUSE MOST MECHANISTIC STUDIES ARE PERFORMED IN MICE, WHICH UNLIKE HUMANS DO NOT USE ITDS AND HAVE A DIMINISHED MSO. IN THIS PROPOSAL WE ADDRESS FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS IN ITD CIRCUIT PROCESSING AND DEVELOPMENT IN THE MONGOLIAN GERBIL, A RODENT SPECIES WITH LOW FREQUENCY HEARING COMPARABLE TO HUMANS AND PROMINENT MSO CIRCUITRY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT MORPHOLOGICAL, SYNAPTIC AND INTRINSIC PLASTICITY ARE TIGHTLY COORDINATED TO ADJUST CELL EXCITABILITY AND ITD COMPUTATIONS BOTH IN NORMAL DEVELOPMENT AND FOLLOWING HEARING LOSS. WE WILL ADDRESS THIS HYPOTHESIS BY COMBINING PLASTICITY INDUCTION PARADIGMS WITH NOVEL ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL AND IMAGING APPROACHES IN BRAIN SLICES, TOGETHER WITH IN VIVO MANIPULATIONS OF EARLY AUDITORY EXPERIENCE. AIM 1 WILL EXPLORE THE CONCEPT OF DENDRITIC ASYMMETRY AS A MAJOR DETERMINANT OF SPATIAL RECEPTIVE FIELDS IN MSO NEURONS, AND WE WILL TEST THIS CONCEPT THROUGH CHRONIC IN VIVO MANIPULATIONS OF ITDS. AIM 2 WILL EXAMINE HOW THE SUBTYPES AND SPATIAL DISTRIBUTIONS OF ION CHANNELS UNDERLYING THE ACTION POTENTIAL CHANGE UPON HEARING ONSET AND EXPLORE THE FUNCTIONAL SIGNIFICANCE OF THESE CHANGES. AIM 3 WILL EXPLORE IN BRAIN SLICES HOW THE DYNAMIC DEVELOPMENTAL CHANGES IN SYNAPSES, INTRINSIC MEMBRANE AND ACTION POTENTIAL PROPERTIES INTERACT TO ADJUST SYNAPTIC WEIGHTS. THE INFORMATION FROM THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL REVEAL FUNDAMENTAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE DEVELOPMENT AND ENCODING OF SOUND LOCALIZATION CUES. AS BINAURAL HEARING IS CRITICAL FOR SPEECH PERCEPTION AND LANGUAGE ACQUISITION IN CHILDREN, A MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF BINAURAL CIRCUIT DEVELOPMENT MAY ULTIMATELY INFORM CLINICAL STRATEGIES FOR ADDRESSING HEARING IMPAIRMENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PIPKIGAMMAI5 IN THE IMMUNE RESPONSE TO HEAD AND NECK SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA - PROJECT SUMMARY INTERFERON-Γ (IFN-Γ) SIGNALING PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN ANTITUMOR IMMUNITY AGAINST HEAD AND NECK SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (HNSCC). LOSS OF IFN-Γ RESPONSIVENESS DIMINISHES TUMOR IMMUNOGENICITY AND UNDERLIES RESISTANCE TO IMMUNE CHECKPOINT BLOCKADE (ICB). HOWEVER, THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS CONTROLLING IFN-Γ SENSITIVITY REMAIN POORLY DEFINED, AND STRATEGIES TO ENHANCE TUMOR RESPONSE TO IFN-Γ ARE LIMITED. OUR RECENT WORK IDENTIFIES TYPE IΓ PHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOL PHOSPHATE KINASE I5 (PIPKIΓI5), AN ENDOSOME-LOCALIZED LIPID KINASE THAT GENERATES PHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOL-4,5-BISPHOSPHATE (PIP2), AS A PREVIOUSLY UNRECOGNIZED REGULATOR OF CELLULAR IFN-Γ RESPONSIVENESS. GENETIC DEPLETION OR PHARMACOLOGIC INHIBITION OF PIPKIΓI5 AMPLIFIES IFN-Γ SIGNALING IN BOTH HNSCC CELLS AND HOST DENDRITIC CELLS (DCS). WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT TARGETING PIPKIΓI5 WILL ENHANCE TUMOR IMMUNOGENICITY, IMPROVE ANTITUMOR IMMUNE ACTIVATION, AND SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASE THERAPEUTIC RESPONSES TO ICB. AIM 1 WILL DEFINE THE TUMOR-INTRINSIC ROLE OF PIPKIΓI5 IN REGULATING HNSCC IMMUNOGENICITY AND SENSITIVITY TO ANTI- PD-1 THERAPY, INCLUDING MECHANISTIC STUDIES ON ITS INTERACTION WITH STAT1 AND KINASE-DEPENDENT PIP2 GENERATION. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE HOW PIPKIΓI5 MODULATES DC ACTIVATION AND T-CELL PRIMING CAPACITY. AIM 3 WILL EVALUATE THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF PIPKIΓI5-TARGETING STRATEGIES TO STRENGTHEN ANTITUMOR IMMUNITY IN VIVO. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THESE STUDIES WILL UNCOVER A NOVEL SIGNALING PATHWAY GOVERNING IFN-Γ RESPONSE IN HNSCC AND PROVIDE A TRANSFORMATIVE FOUNDATION FOR DEVELOPING NEXT-GENERATION IMMUNOTHERAPY-AUGMENTING TREATMENTS FOR THIS LETHAL DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEFINING MLL3 AS AN EARLY DRIVER OF ORAL NEOPLASTIC EVOLUTION AND ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNE REGULATOR USING HUMAN ORGANOIDS AND MURINE MODELS - PROJECT SUMMARY  HEAD AND NECK SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (HNSCC) IS AN AGGRESSIVE MALIGNANCY DERIVED FROM STRATIFIED SQUAMOUS EPITHELIUM OF THE ORAL CAVITY. LEUKOPLAKIA IS A PREMALIGNANT CONDITION AND IS RECOGNIZED AS THE PRECURSOR LESION OF HNSCC. DURING LEUKOPLAKIA-ASSOCIATED NEOPLASTIC EVOLUTION, BENIGN SQUAMOUS EPITHELIUM FIRST BECOMES DYSPLASIA, THEN CARCINOMA IN SITU, AND FINALLY PROGRESSES TO INVASIVE SCC. THEREFORE, LEUKOPLAKIA SERVES AS AN IDEAL PRE-MALIGNANT MODEL FOR THE INVESTIGATION OF THE STEP-WISE NEOPLASTIC EVOLUTION OF ORAL SQUAMOUS EPITHELIAL CELLS. HOWEVER, OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS PROMOTING LEUKOPLAKIA- ASSOCIATED NEOPLASIA REMAINS QUITE LIMITED. THIS SHORTCOMING IS DUE TO DIFFICULTIES IN PERFORMING MOLECULAR RESEARCH INTO THE STEPWISE NEOPLASTIC EVOLUTION OF HNSCC, LARGELY BECAUSE VIABLE AND VALID HUMAN MODELS REPRESENTING THIS UNIQUE PATHOLOGICAL TRANSITION HAVE BEEN LACKING. TO ADDRESS THIS KEY CHALLENGE, IN THIS PROPOSAL WE HAVE DEVELOPED 3D ORGANOID MODELS DIRECTLY FROM: 1) NORMAL HUMAN ORAL TISSUES, 2) PATIENT-DERIVED LEUKOPLAKIA SAMPLES, 3) HNSCC PATIENT TUMORS, SPANNING THE STEPWISE NEOPLASTIC EVOLUTION OF HNSCC.  NEOPLASTIC EVOLUTION IS DRIVEN STRONGLY BY EPIGENOMIC CHANGES, WHICH ARE CONTROLLED BY CHROMATIN REGULATORS. ONE OF THE CENTRAL CHROMATIN REGULATORS, MLL3 (ALSO KNOWN AS KMT2C, A HISTONE METHYLTRANSFERASE), IS AMONG THE MOST FREQUENTLY MUTATED GENES IN HNSCC. IMPORTANTLY, IN OUR ANALYSIS OF CANCER CLONAL EVOLUTION, MLL3 MUTATIONS ARE TRUNCAL (I.E., FOUNDATIONAL), EARLY EVENTS DURING TUMORIGENESIS. MOREOVER, MLL3 LOSS IS ASSOCIATED WITH POOR SURVIVAL OF HNSCC PATIENTS. NOTABLY, IN OUR ORGANOID MODELS OF EARLY PREMALIGNANT STAGES, LOSS OF MLL3 STRONGLY PROMOTES ORAL SQUAMOUS NEOPLASTIC EVOLUTION. WE THUS HYPOTHESIZE THAT LOSS OF MLL3 IS A FUNCTIONAL EARLY DRIVER OF HNSCC NEOPLASTIC EVOLUTION AND CAN DIRECTLY PROMOTE MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION OF ORAL SQUAMOUS CELLS. THIS HYPOTHESIS WILL BE TESTED USING A SPECTRUM OF HUMAN CRISPR-EDITED ORGANOIDS AND MLL3- CONDITIONAL KNOCKOUT HNSCC MOUSE MODEL.  OUR PRELIMINARY DATA FURTHER REVEAL AN UNEXPECTED, PROMINENT ROLE OF MLL3 IN ENHANCING ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNE RESPONSE IN HNSCC, WHICH IS EVIDENT IN UNBIASED BIOINFORMATIC ANALYSES OF BOTH PERTURBATION ASSAYS AND PATIENT- DERIVED SINGLE-CELL GENOMIC DATA. IMPORTANTLY, OUR SYNGENEIC MOUSE MODEL DEMONSTRATES THAT LOSS OF MLL3 IMPAIRS THE RECRUITMENT OF T CELLS TO HNSCC TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT. WE THUS HYPOTHESIZE THAT MLL3 FUNCTIONALLY PROMOTES ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNITY IN HNSCC, AND MLL3 MUTATIONS CAN SERVE AS BIOMARKERS PREDICTING IMMUNOTHERAPEUTIC RESPONSE IN HNSCC PATIENTS. WE WILL EXPLORE THESE BY STUDYING THE MECHANISTIC BASIS AND BIOLOGICAL SIGNIFICANCE OF THE MLL3-REGULATED ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNITY USING ANIMAL MODELS. THESE INVESTIGATIONS PROMISE TO ESTABLISH PRIMARY DRIVING FORCES OF EARLY ORAL SQUAMOUS TRANSFORMATION, WHICH WILL FUNDAMENTALLY TRANSFORM OUR INSIGHTS INTO THE BIOLOGY OF LEUKOPLAKIA AND HNSCC. MORE IMPORTANTLY, SUCCESSFUL EXECUTION OF THIS PROPOSAL MAY IDENTIFY NOVEL TARGETS FOR EARLY PREVENTION AND IMMUNOTHERAPY AGAINST HNSCC.

description: THE ROLE OF TREM2 IN THE REGULATION OF PERIODONTAL INFLAMMATION - PROJECT SUMMARY MACROPHAGES ARE HIGHLY PLASTIC AND DEMONSTRATE DIVERSE PHENOTYPES THAT REGULATE THE PROMOTION AND RESOLUTION OF PERIODONTAL INFLAMMATION. IMPROVED CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF PD IS NEEDED AND TARGETING MACROPHAGE POLARIZATION IS AN EXCITING STRATEGY GIVEN ITS CENTRAL ROLE IN DISEASE PATHOGENESIS. HOWEVER, THERE IS A CRITICAL GAP IN OUR KNOWLEDGE OF THE MECHANISMS THAT REGULATE MACROPHAGE POLARIZATION. TOWARDS UNDERSTANDING MECHANISMS OF MACROPHAGE REGULATION IN PD, WE HAVE BEEN INVESTIGATING THE ROLE OF TRIGGERING RECEPTOR EXPRESSED ON MYELOID CELLS 2 (TREM2). TREM2 IS A POTENT IMMUNOREGULATOR EXPRESSED ON MACROPHAGES THAT DOWNREGULATES INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINE EXPRESSION, IN PART, THROUGH INTRACELLULAR INHIBITION OF TLR4 SIGNALING. THE IMMUNOREGULATORY FUNCTION OF TREM2 IS ATTENUATED VIA CLEAVAGE OF ITS EXTRACELLULAR DOMAIN BY PROTEASES ADAM10 AND ADAM17 (ADAM10/17), AND CLEAVAGE RESULTS IN A SOLUBLE FORM OF THE RECEPTOR (STREM2). DYSREGULATION OF TREM2 IN HUMANS HAS BEEN IMPLICATED IN MULTIPLE CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY CONDITIONS. HOWEVER, THE ROLE OF TREM2 IN PD IS UNDERSTUDIED. HERE, WE PROPOSE TO INVESTIGATE TREM2-DRIVEN MECHANISMS OF MACROPHAGE REGULATION IN PERIODONTAL INFLAMMATION. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATES THAT TREM2IS EXPRESSED IN MACROPHAGES FROM THE PERIODONTIUM OF HUMAN SUBJECTS. IN OUR MOUSE MODELS OF PD, WE DEMONSTRATED THE DIFFERENTIAL REGULATION OF TREM2, WITH DOWNREGULATED SURFACE EXPRESSION OF TREM2 ON MACROPHAGES DURING PD AND UPREGULATED DURING RESOLUTION OF PD. FURTHERMORE, TREM2 DEPLETION RESULTED IN INADEQUATE PD RESOLUTION WITH INCREASED EXPRESSION OF IL1Β AND TNF IN THE ORAL MUCOSA. WE HAVE ALSO SHOWN THAT ADAM10/17EXPRESSION WAS INCREASED IN VIVO DURING PD AND IN VITRO WITH P. GINGIVALIS-DERIVED LPS. THE INCREASED ADAM10/17 EXPRESSION WAS ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED STREM2 PRODUCTION AND DECREASED TREM2 SURFACE EXPRESSION ON MACROPHAGES. FROM THE PRELIMINARY DATA, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT TREM2 PROMOTES AN IMMUNOREGULATORY MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPE, AND THAT PD STIMULATES ADAM10/17 ACTIVITY RESULTING IN INCREASED CLEAVAGE OF SURFACE TREM2 EXPRESSION AND A RESULTING PRO-INFLAMMATORY MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPE. WE WILL TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS IN THE FOLLOWING AIMS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DEMONSTRATE THE EXTENT TO WHICH DIFFERENTIAL TREM2 EXPRESSION DRIVES MACROPHAGE POLARIZATION IN THE REGULATION OF PERIODONTAL INFLAMMATION. WE WILL USE MOUSE MODELS OF PD AND DETERMINE THE DIFFERENTIAL REGULATION OF THE TREM2-TLR4 REGULATORY AXIS IN MACROPHAGES. WE WILL ENHANCE AND DIMINISH THE SIGNALING THROUGH THE COMPETING SIGNALING PATHWAYS AND EVALUATE THE EFFECT ON MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPE AND PD SEVERITY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE POST-TRANSLATIONAL REGULATORY MECHANISMS OF TREM2 SURFACE EXPRESSION DURING PD. WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE ADAM10/17 ACTIVITY DURING PD AND EVALUATE THE EXTENT TO WHICH INHIBITING ADAM10/17 ACTIVITY INFLUENCES PERIODONTAL INFLAMMATION. IN AIM 3, WE WILL EXPLORE ENDOGENOUS AND EXOGENOUS TREM2 LIGANDS THAT DIRECT MACROPHAGE ACTIVITY LOCALLY WITHIN THE ORAL MUCOSA.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: FUNCTIONAL CHARACTERIZATIONS OF PHOSPHOLIPASE A2 IN PORPHYROMONAS GINGIVALIS - PROJECT SUMMARY PHOSPHOLIPASES (PLAS) ARE ENZYMES THAT HYDROLYZE PHOSPHOLIPIDS TO PRODUCE FATTY ACIDS AND LIPOPHILIC SUBSTANCES. THESE UBIQUITOUS AND DIVERSE ENZYMES PLAY CRITICAL ROLES IN MAINTAINING CELL MEMBRANE INTEGRITY, LIPID SIGNALING, AND ENERGY HOMEOSTASIS REGULATION. THE METABOLITES OF PLAS, SUCH AS PROSTAGLANDIN E2 (PGE2) AND LEUKOTRIENE B4 (LTB4), ARE POTENT INFLAMMATORY MEDIATORS AND IMPLICATED IN NUMEROUS HUMAN DISEASES, INCLUDING ATHEROSCLEROSIS, ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE, AND CANCER. PERIODONTITIS IS A PREVALENT INFLAMMATORY DISEASE THAT AFFECTS NEARLY HALF OF AMERICAN ADULTS. ACCUMULATING EVIDENCE DEMONSTRATES A POSITIVE CORRELATION BETWEEN PLA ACTIVITY AND PERIODONTITIS SEVERITY: THE LEVELS OF PLA AND ITS METABOLITES (E.G., PGE2 AND LTB4) ARE SIGNIFICANTLY ELEVATED IN GINGIVAL CREVICULAR FLUID (GCF) FROM PERIODONTITIS PATIENTS AND RETURN TO NORMAL LEVELS FOLLOWING TREATMENT. HOWEVER, THE UNDERLYING PATHOGENIC MECHANISMS DRIVING THIS ASSOCIATION REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. EMERGING EVIDENCE POINTS TO A POTENTIAL BACTERIAL CONTRIBUTION TO THIS PHENOMENON. PORPHYROMONAS GINGIVALIS (PG), A KEYSTONE PERIODONTAL PATHOGEN, STIMULATES HOST PLA2 (A SUPERFAMILY OF PLAS) PRODUCTION IN ORAL EPITHELIAL CELLS. BUILDING ON THIS OBSERVATION, WE INTERROGATED PG GENOMES AND IDENTIFIED TWO PLA2 HOMOLOGS IN ALL SEQUENCED PG ISOLATES (E.G., PG0898 AND PG1879 IN STRAIN W83). SEQUENCE ANALYSES REVEAL THAT THESE HOMOLOGS CONTAIN A CONSERVED PATATIN-LIKE PHOSPHOLIPASE A2 DOMAIN PRESENT IN SEVERAL BACTERIAL VIRULENCE FACTORS SUCH AS EXOU, A KEY VIRULENCE DETERMINANT OF PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA. INTRIGUINGLY, SIMILAR PLA2 HOMOLOGS ARE PRESENT IN OTHER MAJOR ORAL PATHOBIONTS (TREPONEMA DENTICOLA AND TANNERELLA FORSYTHIA) BUT ABSENT IN ORAL COMMENSALS, SUGGESTING THAT BACTERIAL PLA2S MAY BE A CONSERVED VIRULENCE DETERMINANT AMONG PERIODONTAL PATHOGENS. HOWEVER, THESE PLA2 HOMOLOGS HAVE NOT BEEN FUNCTIONALLY CHARACTERIZED IN ORAL PATHOGENS AND THEIR ROLES IN PERIODONTITIS PATHOGENESIS REMAIN UNEXPLORED. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO ADDRESS THIS CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAP USING PG AS A MODEL ORGANISM, FOCUSED ON THREE INTEGRATED SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) ELUCIDATE THE BIOCHEMICAL AND STRUCTURAL FEATURES OF PG0898 AND PG1879 AND THEIR CATALYTIC MECHANISM AS PLA2 ENZYMES; (2) INVESTIGATE HOW THESE TWO PLA2 ENZYMES INFLUENCE PG PHYSIOLOGY; AND (3) DECIPHER THEIR ROLES IN PG VIRULENCE USING INTEGRATED IN VITRO AND IN VIVO APPROACHES. THIS PROJECT IS SIGNIFICANT AND INNOVATIVE AS IT REPRESENTS THE FIRST STUDY TO INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF BACTERIAL PLA2S IN PERIODONTITIS PATHOGENESIS. COMPLETION OF THIS WORK WILL ELUCIDATE THE BIOCHEMICAL AND STRUCTURAL FEATURES OF PG0898 AND PG1879 AND THEIR ROLES IN PG PATHOPHYSIOLOGY, ESTABLISH A FOUNDATION FOR INVESTIGATING PLA2 ENZYMES IN OTHER ORAL PATHOGENS AND THEIR IMPLICATIONS IN PERIODONTITIS PATHOGENESIS, AND POTENTIALLY LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL THERAPEUTIC MODALITIES (E.G., PLA2 INHIBITORS) FOR TREATING AND PREVENTING PERIODONTITIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNRAVELING THE GUT-SALIVARY GLAND AXIS: MICROBIAL AND MICROBIAL METABOLITE-BASED STRATEGIES FOR SJÖGREN'S SYNDROME THERAPY - PROJECT SUMMARY SALIVARY GLAND FUNCTION IS CHRONICALLY IMPAIRED IN SJӦGREN’S DISEASE (SJD), WHICH IS A CHRONIC AUTOIMMUNE EXOCRINE GLAND DISORDER WITH NO CURE OR EFFECTIVE TREATMENT AVAILABLE. DYSREGULATED INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES, INCLUDING HEIGHTENED INTERFERON RESPONSES, DRIVE THE ONSET AND CHRONIC PERSISTENCE OF SALIVARY GLAND INFLAMMATION, DAMAGE AND FUNCTIONAL IMPAIRMENT. THERE IS A PRESSING NEED FOR NOVEL, EFFECTIVE THERAPIES THAT PROTECT/IMPROVE SALIVARY GLAND FUNCTION AND MITIGATE SJD. GUT MICROBIOME DYSBIOSIS IS CLOSELY LINKED TO VARIOUS AUTOIMMUNE AND INFLAMMATORY DISEASES, INCLUDING SJӦGREN’S DISEASE, WHILE HEALTHY FECAL MICROBIOTA TRANSPLANT (FMT) SHOWS PROMISE IN MITIGATING INFLAMMATORY PATHOLOGY AND PRESERVING/RESTORING TISSUE FUNCTION. IN MURINE MODELS OF SJD, TRANSPLANTING CERTAIN GUT BACTERIAL SPECIES OR THEIR METABOLITES, SUCH AS SHORT-CHAIN FATTY ACIDS (SCFAS) ALLEVIATES SALIVARY GLAND PATHOLOGY. HOWEVER, MANY CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAPS REMAIN, PARTICULARLY REGARDING THE TISSUE PROTECTIVE MECHANISMS OF THE GUT-SALIVARY GLAND AXIS. THE MAIN OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEFINE THE GUT–SALIVARY GLAND AXIS IN SJD, FOCUSING ON THE SALIVARY GLAND–BENEFICIAL EFFECTS OF HEALTHY FMT AND SPECIFIC GUT BACTERIA, AND UNRAVELING TWO MECHANISTIC LAYERS UNDERLYING THESE ACTIONS: (I) MICROBIAL METABOLITES AS KEY MEDIATORS LINKING THE GUT AND SALIVARY GLANDS, AND (II) CELLULAR TARGETS AND MOLECULAR CHANGES IN SALIVARY TISSUES. WE WILL TEST THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT HEALTHY GUT MICROBIOTA HARBOR BACTERIAL SPECIES THAT PROTECT/IMPROVE SALIVARY GLAND INTEGRITY AND FUNCTION, AND TRANSPLANTATION OF THESE HEALTHY GUT MICROBIOTA OR BENEFICIAL BACTERIAL SPECIES CAN EXERT PROTECTIVE AND THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS IN SJD-ASSOCIATED SALIVARY GLAND PATHOLOGY BY PRODUCING SCFAS AND OTHER METABOLITES, WHICH MEDIATE GUT–SALIVARY GLAND COMMUNICATION AND MITIGATE INTERFERON-INDUCED DETRIMENTAL RESPONSES IN SALIVARY EPITHELIAL CELLS. IN AIM 1 OF THE PROJECT, WE WILL ELUCIDATE KEY SALIVARY TISSUE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE PROTECTIVE EFFECTS OF HEALTHY FMT IN A MURINE MODEL OF SJD OBSERVED IN OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES. WE WILL ALSO EVALUATE THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF HEALTHY FMT ON ESTABLISHED SJD IN THIS MOUSE MODEL. IN AIM 2, WE WILL EXAMINE THE PROTECTIVE AND THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS OF TWO SPECIFIC GUT BACTERIAL SPECIES, IDENTIFIED IN OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES, ON SALIVARY GLAND FUNCTION IN THE MURINE MODEL OF SJD. IN AIM 3, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE PREVIOUSLY UNEXPLORED EFFECTS OF SCFAS ON HUMAN SALIVARY GLAND CELLS AND PERIPHERAL AND IMMUNE CELLS FROM SJD PATIENTS, AND IDENTIFY KEY BENEFICIAL MICROBIAL METABOLITES LINKING GUT MICROBIOME TO SALIVARY GLANDS IN FMT AND SJD IN BOTH MICE AND HUMANS. THIS PROJECT WILL EMPLOY ADVANCED IMMUNOLOGICAL, MICROBIOLOGICAL AND SYSTEMS BIOLOGICAL APPROACHES, INCLUDING 16S RRNA GENE SEQUENCING FOR MICROBIOME PROFILING, TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS OF SALIVARY GLAND EPITHELIAL POPULATIONS, AND METABOLOMIC PROFILING. THE NOVEL AND HIGHLY TRANSLATABLE FINDINGS FROM THIS PROJECT WILL SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCE THE DEVELOPMENT OF INNOVATIVE MICROBIAL-BASED THERAPIES FOR SJD AND OTHER INFLAMMATORY SALIVARY GLAND DISORDERS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SABERGEL, A MULTIMODAL DELIVERY SYSTEM FOR THE TREATMENT OF ORAL CANCER - PROJECT SUMMARY.  SURGICAL RESECTION IS THE PRIMARY TREATMENT FOR ORAL CAVITY SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (OCSCC), OFTEN FOLLOWED BY CHEMORADIOTHERAPY FOR ADVANCED CASES. HOWEVER RECURRENCE IS COMMON, AND THE 5-YEAR SURVIVAL RATE REMAINS AROUND 50%. IMMUNOTHERAPY SHOWS PROMISE FOR RECURRENT OR METASTATIC OCSCC, BUT ONLY 15-20% OF PATIENTS RESPOND DURABLY. CURRENT IMMUNOTHERAPY IS LIMITED BY THE TOXICITY OF SYSTEMICALLY-DELIVERED IMMUNOMODULATORS, WHICH REQUIRE HIGH DOSES AND FREQUENT RE-DOSING, LEADING TO SEVERE IMMUNE-RELATED ADVERSE EVENTS. THEREFORE, MORE EFFECTIVE AND LESS TOXIC ADJUVANT STRATEGIES ARE NEEDED TO HELP PREVENT RECURRENCE. TWO STRATEGIES ARE CRITICAL TO SUCCESSFUL IMMUNOTHERAPY: 1) RECRUITMENT AND ACTIVATION OF EFFECTOR CELLS TO KILL THE TUMOR; AND 2) DEPLETION OF IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE CELLS WHICH ANTAGONIZE THE ANTI-TUMOR EFFICACY OF EFFECTOR CELLS. THIS PROPOSAL ADDRESSES BOTH STRATEGIES BY USING A NOVEL BIOMATERIALS PLATFORM WHICH OPTIMIZES DRUG RELEASE DIRECTLY INTO THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT.  WE WILL DEVELOP A NANOFIBROUS, PEPTIDE-BASED HYDROGEL WHICH CAN DELIVER FOUR AGENTS WITH DIFFERENTIAL SPATIOTEMPORAL CONTROL. TWO ARE SMALL MOLECULES WHOSE INHIBITORY ACTION IS KNOWN TO HELP DEPLETE IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE CELLS. TWO ARE CYTOKINES WHICH RECRUIT AND THEN ACTIVATE EFFECTOR CELLS TO MORE EFFECTIVE KILL THE TUMORS. DELIVERY OF THESE FOUR CARGOS WILL BE CONTROLLED BY SELF-ASSEMBLING BORONATE ESTER RELEASE (SABER) PEPTIDES WHICH ASSEMBLE TO FORM GELS THAT CAN RELEASE THE MULTIPLE IMMUNOTHERAPEUTICS LOCALLY OVER VARYING AND EXTENDED PERIODS. THIS “SABERGEL” IS SHEAR THINNING AND SELF-HEALING WHICH ALLOWS IT TO BE EASILY DELIVERED IN VIVO TO THE TIME BY SYRINGE NEEDLE ENABLING ENHANCING TARGETED EFFECTS WHILE MINIMIZING OFF-TISSUE TOXICITY. OVERALL, OUR GOAL IS TO STUDY THE POTENTIAL SYNERGY OF SABERGEL WITH RADIOTHERAPY AND CHEMORADIOTHERAPY TO STIMULATE ROBUST ANTI-TUMOR EFFECTOR FUNCTION AND SYSTEMIC IMMUNE MEMORY.  AIM 1 WILL SYNTHESIZE A SERIES OF SABERGELS DESIGNED TO OPTIMIZE PAYLOAD DELIVERY AND RELEASE PROFILES, FOR RAPID EARLY RELEASE (DAYS) OF SOME CARGO WHILE MAINTAINING MUCH LONGER RELEASE (WEEKS) OF OTHERS BASED ON THEIR INTENDED SEQUENCING AND BIOLOGICAL EFFECT.  AIM 2 WILL FUNCTIONALLY CHARACTERIZE ANTI-TUMOR MECHANISMS INDUCED BY SABERGEL LOCALIZED IMMUNOTHERAPY IN TREATMENT-RESISTANT, IMMUNE-SILENT TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENTS.  AIM 3 WILL COMBINE SABERGEL WITH ADJUVANT CHEMORADIOTHERAPY TO ENHANCE EFFICACY AND DURABILITY OF THE IMMUNE RESPONSE IN THE IMMUNE-DEPLETED ORAL CANCER TUMOR IMMUNE MICROENVIRONMENT.  BY SUCCESSFULLY ACCOMPLISHING THESE AIMS, WE WILL CLARIFY THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH THIS NOVEL BIOMATERIAL CAN PREVENT CANCER RECURRENCE AND ENHANCE ADJUVANT CHEMORADIOTHERAPY IN HIGH RISK CASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ROLE OF P75NTR IN TMJ CARTILAGE HOMEOSTASIS AND DEGENERATIVE DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY TMJ OSTEOARTHRITIS (TMJ-OA) IS A PROGRESSIVE DEGENERATIVE DISORDER CARRYING DISPROPORTIONALLY HIGH MORBIDITY, LEADING TO CHRONIC PAIN, IMPAIRED JAW FUNCTION, AND SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCED QUALITY OF LIFE. UNLIKE OTHER JOINTS, THE TMJ IS BILATERALLY LINKED AND COVERED WITH FIBROCARTILAGE, WHICH ALLOWS FOR ADAPTIVE REMODELING, BUT ALSO MAKES IT UNIQUELY VULNERABLE TO DEGENERATION. DESPITE THE HIGH PREVALENCE AND DEBILITATING NATURE OF TMJ-OA, EFFECTIVE DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPIES ARE LIMITED. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO DEFINE THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT REGULATE TMJ CARTILAGE HOMEOSTASIS AND DEGENERATION AND TO DEVELOP NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR DEGENERATIVE TMJ DISORDERS. EMERGING EVIDENCE, INCLUDING OUR PRELIMINARY DATA, SUGGESTS THAT NEUROTROPHINS AND THEIR RECEPTORS PLAY A PREVIOUSLY UNRECOGNIZED ROLE IN TMJ PATHOLOGY. SPECIFICALLY, P75 NEUROTROPHIN RECEPTOR (P75NTR), A KEY REGULATOR OF CRANIOFACIAL PROGENITOR CELLS, IS HIGHLY EXPRESSED IN TMJ CARTILAGE—15-FOLD HIGHER THAN IN LONG BONE CARTILAGE. OUR DATA FURTHER SHOW THAT P75NTR EXPRESSION IS SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCED IN TMJ CARTILAGE FROM TMJ-OA PATIENTS, SUGGESTING A CRITICAL ROLE IN TMJ HOMEOSTASIS AND DEGENERATION. USING GLOBAL AND CONDITIONAL DELETION MODELS IN MICE, OUR GROUP HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT P75NTR SIGNALING DISRUPTION RESULTS IN SIGNIFICANT TMJ PATHOLOGY, INCLUDING COMPROMISED CARTILAGE AND DISC INTEGRITY, INCREASED INFLAMMATION, AND CHONDROCYTE APOPTOSIS. THESE FINDINGS HIGHLIGHT P75NTR AS A CENTRAL REGULATOR OF TMJ CARTILAGE HEALTH AND SUGGEST THAT RESTORING ITS SIGNALING MAY BE A VIABLE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY. THIS STUDY WILL DEFINE THE EFFECTS OF LINEAGE-SPECIFIC P75NTR DELETION ON TMJ DEVELOPMENT AND REMODELING, INVESTIGATE HOW P75NTR SIGNALING DISRUPTION AFFECTS TMJ PATHOLOGY IN A CLINICALLY RELEVANT DEGENERATION MODEL, AND EVALUATE THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF AN ENGINEERED P75NTR AGONIST TO MITIGATE TMJ-OA PROGRESSION THROUGH INTRA-ARTICULAR DELIVERY. THE COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE FUNDAMENTAL INSIGHTS INTO TMJ BIOLOGY BY IDENTIFYING KEY CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT GOVERN TMJ CARTILAGE HOMEOSTASIS AND DEGENERATION. FURTHERMORE, THIS STUDY WILL INTRODUCE A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC APPROACH TARGETING P75NTR, POTENTIALLY OFFERING DISEASE-MODIFYING TREATMENT FOR TMJ-OA. BY BRIDGING BASIC SCIENCE WITH TRANSLATIONAL APPLICATIONS, THIS WORK HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM THE TREATMENT LANDSCAPE FOR TMJ-OA, ALLEVIATING PAIN AND IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR MILLIONS OF PATIENTS.

description: UNRAVELING THE MOLECULAR BASIS OF TOOTH AGENESIS - PROJECT SUMMARY THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DISCOVER PUTATIVELY CAUSAL GENETIC VARIANTS FOR HUMAN TOOTH AGENESIS (TA), A COMMON CRANIOFACIAL BIRTH DEFECT THAT AFFECTS ~200 MILLION HUMANS WORLDWIDE AND IMPOSES SIGNIFICANT AESTHETIC, FUNCTIONAL, PSYCHOSOCIAL, AND FINANCIAL BURDENS FOR AFFECTED INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES. DESPITE RESEARCH PROGRESS, MUTATIONS IN KNOWN GENES ACCOUNT FOR LESS THAN 50% OF ALL TA CASES, SUGGESTING THAT ADDITIONAL ETIOLOGIC GENES REMAIN TO BE FOUND. GENOME-WIDE STUDIES OF TA ARE SCARCE, AND THE INTERPRETATION OF IDENTIFIED VARIANTS HAS BEEN CHALLENGING DUE TO THE PAUCITY OF STUDIES COMBINING UNBIASED GENE DISCOVERY WITH FUNCTIONAL GENOMIC CHARACTERIZATION APPROACHES. THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP HAS HAMPERED OUR UNDERSTANDING OF TA GENOTYPE-PHENOTYPE CORRELATIONS AND LIMITS OUR ABILITY TO IMPROVE DIAGNOSTIC AND REGENERATIVE THERAPIES. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE COMBINE LARGE-SCALE NEXT- GENERATION SEQUENCING GENE DISCOVERY WITH FUNCTIONAL GENOMIC CHARACTERIZATION APPROACHES AS AN INNOVATIVE AND POWERFUL STRATEGY TO UNCOVER THE GENETIC ETIOLOGY AND IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING TA. WE WILL CONDUCT WHOLE-EXOME AND/OR WHOLE-GENOME SEQUENCING IN ~450 INDIVIDUALS FROM OUR WELL-CHARACTERIZED TA DATASET TO SYSTEMATICALLY EVALUATE THE CONTRIBUTIONS OF RARE VARIANTS TO TA, DETECT SEGREGATION OF PUTATIVE CAUSAL VARIANTS WITHIN AND ACROSS FAMILIES, AND TEST COMPLEX INHERITANCE MODELS THAT ARE CRITICAL FOR UNRAVELING THE ETIOLOGY OF TA. WE WILL VALIDATE THESE FINDINGS AND PERFORM ADDITIONAL VARIANT DISCOVERY USING WGS DATA FROM MORE THAN 1 MILLION INDIVIDUALS FROM THREE LARGE BIOBANKS LINKED TO ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (BIOVU, UK BIOBANK, ALL OF US). IN VITRO FUNCTIONAL CHARACTERIZATION APPROACHES WILL DETERMINE WHETHER A VARIANT HAS FUNCTIONAL CONSEQUENCES ON GENE/PROTEIN FUNCTION BASED ON PREDICTED IMPACT. THE CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE OF TA-ASSOCIATED LOCI WILL BE FURTHER EXPLORED BY ASSESSING THE INTRINSIC GENETIC EFFECTS OF REGULATION OF TA GENES WITH ADDITIONAL HEALTH OUTCOMES, PHENOME-WIDE, IN THREE LARGE BIOBANKS LINKED TO ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (BIOVU, UK BIOBANK, ALL OF US). OUR RESULTS WILL GENERATE A VALUABLE RESOURCE OF HUMAN EXOME/GENOME SEQUENCE DATA AND FUNCTIONALLY-CONFIRMED PATHOGENIC VARIANTS THAT CAN BE TRANSLATED INTO IMPROVED CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF TA BY REFINING OUR ABILITY TO PROPOSE NEW GENOTYPE-PHENOTYPE CORRELATIONS AND SET THE STAGE FOR MULTIPLE TRANSLATIONAL EFFORTS TOWARDS FUTURE PREVENTIVE/REGENERATIVE THERAPIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: OBSERVATIONAL RESEARCH TO ASSESS THE PROLONGED EFFECTS OF MEDICATION FOR OPIOID USE DISORDER (ORAL-MOUD) ON ORAL HEALTH: A MIXED METHODS STUDY - ABSTRACT INCREASED TREATMENT ACCESS, UPTAKE, AND RETENTION ARE ESSENTIAL FOR ADDRESSING THE OVERDOSE EPIDEMIC THAT HAS CLAIMED OVER 1 MILLION AMERICAN LIVES OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES. AMONG THE FEW FDA-APPROVED MEDICATIONS FOR OPIOID USE DISORDER (MOUD), DISSOLVABLE FORMULATIONS OF BUPRENORPHINE (D-BUP) AND ORALLY ADMINISTERED METHADONE ARE THE MOST UTILIZED. PAST RESEARCH HAS DEMONSTRATED AN ASSOCIATION BETWEEN THESE MEDICATIONS AND ORAL DISEASES THAT CAN NEGATIVELY IMPACT PATIENTS’ OVERALL HEALTH AND QUALITY OF LIFE. HOWEVER, THESE CLAIMS ARE LIMITED TO EVIDENCE FROM RETROSPECTIVE AND CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDIES WITH NO OR LIMITED COMPARISON GROUPS. MOREOVER, NON-ORAL MOUD ALTERNATIVES ARE OFTEN LESS APPEALING AND ACCESSIBLE TO PEOPLE WITH OUD. COMPETING ORAL HEALTH AND ADDICTION MEDICINE PRIORITIES AND LIMITATIONS OF PRIOR STUDIES IN THIS AREA HIGHLIGHT THE NEED FOR RESEARCH TO DETERMINE (A) IF CAUSAL LINKS EXIST BETWEEN ONE OR BOTH OF THESE MEDICATIONS (E.G., D-BUP AND METHADONE) AND ORAL HEALTH PROBLEMS, (B) WHETHER ONE MEDICATION MIGHT BE MORE DETRIMENTAL TO ORAL HEALTH, AND (C) HOW POTENTIAL ORAL DISEASE MIGHT BE MITIGATED DURING MOUD TREATMENT. THIS PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY THE POTENTIAL FACTORS UNDERLYING THE ONSET AND PROGRESSION OF ORAL DISEASE ASSOCIATED WITH D-BUP AND METHADONE. WE ALSO SEEK TO UNDERSTAND THE CONTRIBUTION OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL FACTORS TO ORAL DISEASE AMONG PATIENTS RECEIVING MOUD AS WELL AS PATIENTS’ RELATIONSHIPS WITH DENTAL CARE ACCESS AND OUD TREATMENT AND RECOVERY. THE STUDY FOLLOWS A SEQUENTIAL EXPLANATORY MIXED METHOD STUDY GUIDED BY AN ORAL HEALTH DISPARITIES FRAMEWORK ADAPTED TO INCLUDE OUD TREATMENT AND RECOVERY CONSTRUCTS (E.G., TREATMENT ADHERENCE, RECOVERY CAPITAL, STIGMA). OUR STUDY HAS A UNIQUE SETTING: A FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTER WITH INTEGRATED MOUD, DENTAL, AND PRIMARY CARE THAT OFFERS BOTH D-BUP AND METHADONE. THIS STUDY HAS THE FOLLOWING AIMS: (AIM 1) EXAMINE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN MOUD AND DENTAL CARIES (TOOTH DECAY) THROUGH A CROSS-SECTIONAL COMPARISON OF PREVALENCE AND SEVERITY AMONG A SAMPLE (N=381) OF PEOPLE WITH OUD WHO ARE MOUD-NAÏVE AND MOUD PATIENTS; (AIM 2) DOCUMENT AND COMPARE DIFFERENCES IN DENTAL CARIES INCREMENT AMONG A COHORT OF D-BUP AND METHADONE PATIENTS (N=376) OVER 12 MONTHS; (AIM 3) IDENTIFY ACTIONABLE ORAL HEATH INTERVENTION POINTS: (A) QUALITATIVELY UNDERSTANDING HOW MODERATING AND MEDIATING FACTORS INFLUENCE ORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES AMONG PATIENTS (N=30-80) RECEIVING MOUD AND (B) COLLABORATING WITH AN EXPERT ADVISORY BOARD TO IDENTIFY POINTS OF INTERVENTION TO INFORM CLINICAL RECOMMENDATIONS FOR PATIENTS RECEIVING MOUD.
