description: ADVANCING FTIR-BASED MULTIMODAL IMAGING WITH AI FOR RISK STRATIFICATION OF ORAL PRECANCER - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SUCCESSFUL TREATMENT AND MANAGEMENT OF ORAL MUCOSAL LESIONS DEPEND ON DEFINITIVE, ACCURATE, AND TIMELY DIAGNOSIS. ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (OSCC) IS HIGHLY AGGRESSIVE AND OFTEN DIAGNOSED AT LATE STAGES, LEADING TO POOR PROGNOSIS. A SIGNIFICANT PORTION OF OSCC IS PRECEDED BY ORAL POTENTIALLY MALIGNANT DISORDER (OPMD), A HETEROGENEOUS GROUP OF PRECANCEROUS ORAL LESIONS ASSOCIATED WITH AN INCREASED RISK OF MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION (MT). HOWEVER, GOLD-STANDARD HISTOPATHOLOGICAL DIAGNOSIS IS SUBJECTIVE AND LACKS PREDICTIVE POWER FOR ASSESSING MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION RISK IN INDIVIDUAL OPMD PATIENTS, CREATING A CRITICAL BARRIER IN ORAL PRECANCER MANAGEMENT. TO ADDRESS THIS UNMET MEDICAL NEED, WE PROPOSE AN INNOVATIVE MULTIMODAL IMAGING SYSTEM THAT INTEGRATES FTIR IMAGING AND HISTOLOGICAL IMAGING TO CAPTURE BOTH BIOCHEMICAL AND MORPHOLOGICAL FEATURES OF TISSUE. LEVERAGING ADVANCED MACHINE LEARNING (ML) AND DEEP LEARNING (DL) METHODS, WE WILL DEVELOP PREDICTIVE MODELS BASED ON THE TWO COMPLEMENTARY IMAGING TECHNIQUES FOR OPMD RISK STRATIFICATION. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT AI-DRIVEN INTEGRATION OF BIOCHEMICAL FINGERPRINTS FROM FTIR IMAGING WITH MORPHOLOGICAL FEATURES FROM HISTOLOGICAL IMAGING WILL YIELD A MORE PRECISE MODEL FOR PREDICTING MT IN OPMDS, OUTPERFORMING TRADITIONAL HISTOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT OR EITHER MODALITY ALONE. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) DEVELOP FTIR IMAGING-BASED ML AND DL MODELS FOR OPMD RISK STRATIFICATION; 2) DEVELOP HISTOLOGICAL IMAGING- BASED DL MODELS FOR OPMD TISSUE SEGMENTATION AND RISK STRATIFICATION; AND 3) DEVELOP AND VALIDATE MULTIMODAL IMAGING SYSTEMS FOR OPMD RISK STRATIFICATION. THE PROPOSED SYSTEM CAN BE EASILY INCORPORATED INTO EXISTING CLINICAL WORKFLOWS TO ENHANCE OPMD DIAGNOSIS AND MANAGEMENT, FACILITATE EARLY ORAL CANCER DETECTION, AND ULTIMATELY REDUCE THE GLOBAL BURDEN OF THE DISEASE.

description: DIABETES DYSREGULATED DENDRITIC - T CELL ACTIVITY IN PERIODONTITIS - PROJECT SUMMARY POORLY CONTROLLED DIABETES SIGNIFICANTLY WORSENS PERIODONTITIS, A CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE THAT AFFECTS NEARLY HALF OF U.S. ADULTS AND IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF TOOTH LOSS, WHICH NEGATIVELY IMPACTS QUALITY OF LIFE. PERIODONTITIS ALSO CONTRIBUTES TO SYSTEMIC CONDITIONS SUCH AS RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS, CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, DEMENTIA, AND IMPAIRED GLYCEMIC CONTROL. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT DIABETES PROFOUNDLY ALTERS DENDRITIC CELL (DC) GENE EXPRESSION AND DISRUPTS COMMUNICATION WITH T CELLS, PROMOTING A DESTRUCTIVE PRO-INFLAMMATORY SHIFT. THIS FINDING IS CONCEPTUALLY IMPORTANT BECAUSE DCS ARE CENTRAL REGULATORS OF ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY, AND THEIR DYSREGULATION PROVIDES A NOVEL MECHANISM THROUGH WHICH DIABETES SIGNIFICANTLY EXACERBATES PERIODONTAL DISEASE. PREL DATA SHOW THAT HYPERGLYCEMIA AFFECTS BOTH MURINE AND HUMAN GINGIVAL SPECIMENS BY SELECTIVELY EXPANDING IL-17A⁺ T CELLS AND REDUCING TREGS. MECHANISTICALLY, HYPERGLYCEMIA UPREGULATES CD137L IN DCS AND CD137 IN IL- 17A⁺ T CELLS. KEY PREL DATA SHOW THAT THIS IS DUE TO DYSREGULATION OF A ΓΔ TCELL COMMUNICATION AXIS. EPIGENETIC REGULATORS ARE ALSO ALTERED IN DCS AND T CELLS CONSISTENT WITH THIS DYSREGULATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT HYPERGLYCEMIA REPROGRAMS DCS AND T CELLS THROUGH SPECIFIC EPIGENETIC MECHANISMS, ACTIVATING A CD137L/CD137 COSTIMULATORY CIRCUIT THAT PROMOTES EXPANSION OF IL-17A⁺ EFFECTOR T CELLS WHILE SUPPRESSING FOXP3⁺ TREGS. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE HOW HYPERGLYCEMIA INDUCES EPIGENETIC REPROGRAMMING TO DYSREGULATE DC–T CELL COMMUNICATION. TO ADDRESS THIS, WE WILL ISOLATE GINGIVAL DCS, TH17/ΓΔ17 T CELLS, AND TREGS FROM DIABETIC AND NORMOGLYCEMIC MICE AS WELL AS FROM HUMAN SUBJECTS, AND ASSESS EPIGENETIC MARKS INVOLVING HISTONE-3 MODIFICATION AND DNA METHYLATION/DEMETHYLATION. CO-CULTURE STUDIES WILL TEST WHETHER THESE EPIGENETIC CHANGES DRIVE CD137L/CD137 UPREGULATION OR SUPPRESS PATHWAYS THAT SUPPORT TREG FUNCTION. AIM 2 PROPOSES TRANSLATIONAL STUDIES TO TEST WHETHER EPIGENETIC INHIBITORS CAN RESTORE IMMUNE BALANCE AND REDUCE PERIODONTITIS IN A DIABETIC MODEL. WE WILL TARGET EPIGENETIC MODULATORS SUCH AS HISTONE DEACETYLASE (HDAC), DNA METHYLTRANSFERASE (DNMT), AND HISTONE METHYLTRANSFERASE BY USE OF SPECIFIC INHIBITORS SUCH AS ROMIDEPSIN, MM- 102, AND BOBCAT339. MICROCT AND SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS ANALYSIS WILL MEASURE BONE LOSS AND WHETHER THE HYPERGLYCEMIA-INDUCED IMMUNE CELL DYSREGULATION IS RESCUED BY EPIGENETIC INHIBITORS. THESE STUDIES WILL DEFINE CAUSAL EPIGENETIC SIGNATURES AND EVALUATE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TO BLOCK THEM. THE AMERICAN ACADEMY OF PERIODONTOLOGY RECOGNIZES THE IMPORTANCE OF DIABETES AS A MODIFYING FACTOR IN PERIODONTITIS BY INCORPORATING IT IN ITS CLASSIFICATION OF PERIODONTAL DISEASE. THUS, WE PROPOSE TO ADDRESS A FUNDAMENTAL GAP IN UNDERSTANDING HOW DIABETES ACCELERATES PERIODONTITIS AND ITS DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCES. BY DEFINING THE EPIGENETIC MECHANISMS THAT DYSREGULATE DENDRITIC CELL–T CELL INTERACTIONS, THE PROPOSED WORK HAS THE POTENTIAL TO SUBSTANTIALLY ADVANCE OUR KNOWLEDGE AND IDENTIFY PATHWAYS AMENABLE TO THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION. BECAUSE SIMILAR IMMUNE DYSREGULATION UNDERLIES MULTIPLE DIABETES-RELATED COMPLICATIONS, THE INSIGHTS GAINED ARE LIKELY TO HAVE BROAD TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE BEYOND ORAL HEALTH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HOST GENETIC AND MICROBIAL DETERMINANTS OF ORAL HEALTH: INTEGRATIVE ANALYSES ACROSS POPULATION-SCALE DATASETS - SUMMARY ORAL DISEASES SUCH AS XEROSTOMIA, SALIVARY GLAND DYSFUNCTION, DENTAL CARIES, AND PERIODONTITIS ARE AMONG THE MOST COMMON CHRONIC CONDITIONS WORLDWIDE. THEY IMPAIR NUTRITION AND QUALITY OF LIFE AND ARE LINKED TO SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION AND INCREASED RISK OF CANCER, CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, AND OTHER CHRONIC DISORDERS. DESPITE THEIR HIGH PREVALENCE, THE BIOLOGICAL DETERMINANTS OF ORAL HEALTH AND DISEASE REMAIN POORLY DEFINED. DYSBIOSIS OF THE ORAL MICROBIOME IS CONSISTENTLY IMPLICATED IN DISEASE ETIOLOGY, YET THE FACTORS SHAPING MICROBIAL VARIATION, PARTICULARLY THE CONTRIBUTION OF HOST GENETICS ARE NOT WELL UNDERSTOOD AT THE POPULATION SCALE. LARGE BIOBANK RESOURCES NOW PROVIDE AN UNPRECEDENTED OPPORTUNITY TO ADDRESS THIS GAP BY INTEGRATING HOST GENOMIC DATA, ORAL MICROBIOME PROFILES, AND ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR)-DERIVED PHENOTYPES. THIS PROJECT LEVERAGES THE ALL OF US RESEARCH PROGRAM, VANDERBILT BIOVU, THE ALLIANCE FOR GENOMIC DISCOVERY (AGD), AND UK BIOBANK TO CREATE THE FIRST MULTI-BIOBANK FRAMEWORK FOR INTEGRATIVE ANALYSIS OF HOST GENETICS AND THE ORAL MICROBIOME, ENCOMPASSING APPROXIMATELY 1.5 MILLION PARTICIPANTS. AMONG ALL OF US PARTICIPANTS, 49,000 SALIVA SAMPLES HAVE UNDERGONE WHOLE-GENOME SEQUENCING (WGS), PROVIDING PAIRED HOST GENOMIC AND MICROBIAL SEQUENCE DATA. OUR PRELIMINARY ANALYSES DEMONSTRATE FEASIBILITY, AS SALIVA WGS CAPTURES DEEP MICROBIAL COVERAGE AND REVEALS DISEASE-ASSOCIATED TAXA IN XEROSTOMIA. WE ALSO PERFORMED AN INITIAL PHENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDY (PHEWAS) IN ALL OF US, INCLUDING CANDIDIASIS OF THE MOUTH, TESTING ASSOCIATIONS ACROSS THE COMPLETE PHECODE MAP TO EXPLORE BROADER ORAL SYSTEMIC RELATIONSHIPS. THE PROJECT HAS THREE AIMS: (1) CHARACTERIZE ORAL MICROBIOME DIVERSITY AND FUNCTIONAL POTENTIAL AT THE POPULATION SCALE, INCLUDING ASSOCIATIONS WITH DEMOGRAPHICS, LIFESTYLE, AND ORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES; (2) DEFINE HOST GENETIC CONTRIBUTIONS TO ORAL HEALTH AND ORAL MICROBIOME VARIATION THROUGH GENOME-WIDE AND PHEWAS ACROSS MULTIPLE BIOBANKS; AND (3) DEVELOP AND VALIDATE INTEGRATED HOST–MICROBIOME MODELS OF ORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES USING STATISTICAL FRAMEWORKS TO IMPROVE RISK PREDICTION AND MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING. THIS WORK IS INNOVATIVE IN LEVERAGING POPULATION-SCALE GENOMIC DATA TO JOINTLY CHARACTERIZE HOST GENETIC VARIATION AND ORAL MICROBIAL DIVERSITY, WHILE INTEGRATING MULTIPLE BIOBANK COHORTS FOR REPLICATION AND GENERALIZABILITY. BY COMBINING TAXONOMIC AND FUNCTIONAL MICROBIOME PROFILING WITH HOST GENETICS AND EHR PHENOTYPES, THIS PROJECT WILL GENERATE THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE MAP OF HOST-MICROBIOME DETERMINANTS OF ORAL HEALTH. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE THE DISCOVERY OF GENETIC VARIANTS AND MICROBIAL FEATURES ASSOCIATED WITH ORAL DISEASES, IDENTIFICATION OF FUNCTIONAL PATHWAYS UNDERLYING SUSCEPTIBILITY, AND PREDICTIVE MODELS THAT INTEGRATE HOST AND MICROBIAL PROFILES. THE IMPACT OF THIS WORK LIES IN ADVANCING MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF ORAL HEALTH AND IDENTIFY CANDIDATE BIOMARKERS FOR DISEASE RISK PREDICTION AND INFORM STRATEGIES FOR PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TARGETED GENE DELIVERY TO TRIGEMINAL NOCICEPTORS - PROJECT SUMMARY: TRIGEMINAL NEURALGIA ARISES FROM NERVE COMPRESSION OR INJURY THAT PRODUCES PERSISTENT HYPEREXCITABILITY AND SENSITIZATION OF TRIGEMINAL NOCICEPTORS, LEADING TO SEVERE MORBIDITY AND ELEVATED SUICIDE RISK. UNFORTUNATELY, EXISTING TREATMENTS ARE LIMITED BY UNDESIRABLE AND POTENTIALLY DANGEROUS SIDE EFFECTS THAT STEM FROM THEIR OFF- TARGET ACTIONS. THIS PROPOSAL HAS TWO MAIN GOALS: 1) TO IDENTIFY THE TRIGEMINAL NOCICEPTOR SUBTYPES THAT DRIVE CHRONIC FACIAL PAIN IN TRIGEMINAL NEURALGIA, USING NOCICEPTOR-SPECIFIC CRE RECOMBINASE MOUSE LINES IN A VALIDATED TRIGEMINAL NEURALGIA MODEL; AND 2) TO DEVELOP A NOVEL GENE THERAPY THAT SELECTIVELY SILENCES THESE TRIGEMINAL NOCICEPTORS WITHOUT AFFECTING OTHER PERIPHERAL OR CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM CELL TYPES. BECAUSE CURRENT VIRAL VECTORS CANNOT DISCRIMINATE AMONG SENSORY NEURON SUBTYPES – AN IMPORTANT LIMITATION IN THE FACE, WHERE MECHANOSENSATION IS CRITICAL, WE WILL LEVERAGE SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOMICS AND EPIGENOMICS TO IDENTIFY CIS- REGULATORY ELEMENTS (E.G. GENE ENHANCERS) THAT DRIVE GENE EXPRESSION SELECTIVELY IN TRIGEMINAL NOCICEPTORS. TO ACCOMPLISH THIS GOAL, WE WILL GENERATE SINGLE-CELL EPIGENOMIC PROFILES OF MOUSE, MACAQUE AND HUMAN TRIGEMINAL GANGLIA TO NOMINATE EVOLUTIONARILY CONSERVED ENHANCERS ACTIVE IN NOCICEPTORS. WE WILL THEN CONSTRUCT ADENO- ASSOCIATED VIRUSES (AAVS) IN WHICH EACH CANDIDATE ENHANCER DRIVES THE EXPRESSION OF A REPORTER AND A UNIQUE MOLECULAR BARCODE. WE WILL ASSESS THE CELL-TYPE SPECIFICITY OF EACH AAV VIVO BY SINGLE-CELL RNA SEQUENCING AND ADVANCE THE TOP CANDIDATES FOR VALIDATION. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROPOSAL WILL YIELD BOTH NOVEL INSIGHT INTO THE NOCICEPTOR SUBTYPE(S) THAT CONTRIBUTE TO TRIGEMINAL NEURALGIA AS WELL AS TRIGEMINAL NOCICEPTOR-SPECIFIC AAVS FOR IMMEDIATE USE IN PAIN RESEARCH. WE ARE ALSO OPTIMISTIC THAT THE USE OF EVOLUTIONARILY CONSERVED ENHANCERS WILL RESULT IN A SIMILAR DEGREE OF CELL-TYPE SPECIFICITY ACROSS SPECIES, INCLUDING HUMAN. WE ENVISION THAT THESE TRIGEMINAL NOCICEPTOR-SPECIFIC VECTORS CAN BE ENGINEERED TO DRIVE THE EXPRESSION OF INHIBITORY PAYLOADS (E.G. CHEMOGENETIC OR OPTOGENETIC ACTUATORS) TO PROVIDE RESEARCHERS – AND ULTIMATELY PATIENTS – WITH OPIOID-FREE, ON- DEMAND, ANALGESIA FOR REFRACTORY TRIGEMINAL NEURALGIA.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISMS OF RENAL DISEASE PROGRESSION IN OFFSPRING FROM OBESE PARENTS - OBESITY IS A MAJOR RISK FACTOR FOR HYPERTENSION AND CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE (CKD), AND ACCUMULATING EVIDENCE INDICATES THAT PARENTAL OBESITY INCREASES THE SUSCEPTIBILITY OF OFFSPRING TO CARDIORENAL DISEASE. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES DEMONSTRATE THAT OFFSPRING FROM OBESE PARENTS EXHIBIT EARLY RENAL DYSFUNCTION, HEIGHTENED KIDNEY INFLAMMATION, INCREASED EXPRESSION OF THE PURINERGIC RECEPTOR P2X7 (P2X7R), AND ALTERED MACROPHAGE IMMUNOMETABOLISM, EVEN WHEN MAINTAINED ON A NORMAL DIET. WE ALSO FOUND THAT GENETIC DELETION OF P2X7R, INCLUDING IN MACROPHAGES, ATTENUATES RENAL INFLAMMATION AND INJURY FOLLOWING ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY (AKI), SUGGESTING THAT EXCESSIVE P2X7R ACTIVATION CONTRIBUTES TO MALADAPTIVE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES IN OFFSPRING FROM OBESE PARENTS. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DETERMINE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH PARENTAL OBESITY PROGRAMS MACROPHAGE IMMUNOMETABOLISM TO INCREASE SUSCEPTIBILITY TO ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY (AKI) AND AGING-RELATED CKD. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT EXCESSIVE P2X7R ACTIVATION AND ALTERED MACROPHAGE METABOLISM PROMOTE A PRO-INFLAMMATORY MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPE THAT IMPAIRS KIDNEY REPAIR FOLLOWING AKI AND ACCELERATES PROGRESSION TO CKD. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL (1) DETERMINE HOW PARENTAL OBESITY ALTERS MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPE AND METABOLISM DURING AKI AND AGING-RELATED KIDNEY DYSFUNCTION; (2) DETERMINE THE CONTRIBUTION OF MACROPHAGE P2X7R ACTIVATION TO RENAL INFLAMMATION AND INJURY; AND (3) DETERMINE WHETHER TARGETING MACROPHAGE METABOLISM BY REDUCING GLYCOLYSIS AND PROMOTING OXIDATIVE METABOLISM IMPROVES KIDNEY REPAIR AND LIMITS CKD PROGRESSION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: WEARABLE FOCAL VIBRATION ON MOBILITY AND PAIN IN PATIENTS WITH DIABETIC PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT DIABETIC PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY (DPN) IS THE MOST COMMON COMPLICATION OF DIABETES, AFFECTING MORE THAN 50% OF THE 34 MILLION ADULTS IN THE U.S. (~1 IN 10) WITH DIABETES. PEOPLE WITH DPN DISPLAY MARKED REDUCTIONS IN FUNCTIONAL MOBILITY AND QUALITY OF LIFE (QOL). PREVENTING AND TREATING DPN SYMPTOMS REMAINS A DAUNTING CHALLENGE FOR CLINICIANS AND DIABETES RESEARCHERS. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGEST THAT FOUR WEEKS OF WEARABLE FOCAL VIBRATION (FV) THERAPY IMPROVES FUNCTIONAL MOBILITY AND REDUCES SEVERE PAIN. FV THERAPY MAY BE EFFECTIVE DUE TO ITS WIDESPREAD EFFECTS ON THE SHARED NEURAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING MOBILITY AND PAIN IN DPN. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY EFFECTIVE PREVENTIVE AND THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE THE SYMPTOMS IN PATIENTS WITH PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY (PN), A HIGHLY PREVALENT CHRONIC DISEASE AND A LEADING CAUSE OF ADULT DISABILITY IN THE U.S. THIS APPLICATION USES AN EIGHT-WEEK RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL OF 120 PARTICIPANTS TO COMPARE THE TREATMENT EFFECTS OF FOUR WEEKS OF WEARABLE FV THERAPY AND THE PERSISTENCE OF THE THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS AT EIGHT WEEKS VERSUS CONTROL WITH SHAM VIBRATION FOR MOBILITY AND PAIN IN DPN. THIS RESEARCH PROPOSAL AIMS TO (1) DETERMINE IF THE WEARABLE FV WILL IMPROVE MOBILITY AT TREATMENT COMPLETION AND FOUR WEEKS AFTER; (2) DETERMINE IF THE WEARABLE FV WILL REDUCE PAIN AT TREATMENT COMPLETION AND FOUR WEEKS AFTER; AND (3) TO EXPLORE PAIN PHENOTYPES, MODERATORS AND MEDIATORS OF FV TREATMENT RESPONSES FOR DPN. PARTICIPANTS WITH DPN WILL BE RANDOMLY ASSIGNED TO ARM 1: STANDARD CARE AND EDUCATION PLUS WEARABLE FV, OR ARM 2: STANDARD CARE PLUS EDUCATION PLUS SHAM FV (CONTROL). THE ESTABLISHED WEARABLE FOCAL VIBRATION TECHNOLOGY (MYOVOLT), DEVELOPED BY DR. WANG (PI) AND THE INDUSTRIAL PARTNER, INVOLVES FACE-TO-FACE INSTRUCTION AND A PRESCRIPTION FOR AN AT-HOME VIBRATION THERAPY DELIVERED TO THREE TARGET MUSCLES. BOTH ARMS INVOLVE EQUAL TIME AND ATTENTION TO DPN EDUCATION BASED ON THE AMERICAN DIABETES ASSOCIATION'S RECOMMENDATION. OUTCOMES INCLUDE PATIENT-REPORTED DPN SYMPTOMS, CLINICAL PAIN AND SENSATION ASSESSMENTS, MOBILITY, BALANCE, GAIT, TOE AND ANKLE AND KNEE STRENGTH, PAIN QUESTIONNAIRE, QUANTITATIVE SENSORY TESTING PRE-INTERVENTION, POST-INTERVENTION, AND FOUR WEEKS POST-INTERVENTION, AND DAILY PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, SLEEP, AND STRESS MONITORED USING A FITBIT DEVICE. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE VALUABLE INSIGHT INTO THE EFFECT OF FV ON DPN, PROVIDE VARIANCE OF RESPONSE FOR SEVERAL OUTCOME MEASURES TO CONDUCT POWER ANALYSIS, ENDORSE SUBGROUPING TO INDIVIDUALIZE THE EVALUATION AND TREATMENT AND BE USED TO OPTIMIZE FV PARAMETERS FOR A LARGER DEFINITIVE CLINICAL TRIAL. THIS WORK IS PARTICULARLY IMPORTANT BECAUSE DPN HAS NO EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS AND IS UNDERMANAGED.

description: ROLE OF AHR IN SIV-ASSOCIATED INTESTINAL DYSFUNCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY  DESPITE EFFECTIVE VIRAL CONTROL WITH ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART), PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV EXPERIENCE A HIGH PREVALENCE OF NONINFECTIOUS COMORBIDITIES INCLUDING METABOLIC, CARDIOVASCULAR, KIDNEY, & LIVER DISEASES, DRIVEN BY INCOMPLETE IMMUNE RESTORATION AND CHRONIC INFLAMMATION. INTESTINAL EPITHELIAL BARRIER DISRUPTION (IEBD) AND MICROBIAL TRANSLOCATION (MT) ARE CENTRAL TO THIS INFLAMMATORY STATE, YET THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS LINKING CHRONIC VIRAL INFECTION, GUT BARRIER DYSFUNCTION, AND SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD. RECENT FINDINGS FROM OUR RHESUS MACAQUE MODEL OF ART-SUPPRESSED SIMIAN IMMUNODEFICIENCY VIRUS (SIV) INFECTION DEMONSTRATE THAT LOSS OF IL-17/IL-22 (TYPE-3) CYTOKINE FUNCTION IN GUT ΓΔ T CELLS CORRELATES WITH INCREASED IEBD, SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION, AND DISRUPTION OF THE GUT MICROBIOME. THESE DEFECTS ARE LINKED TO DYSREGULATION OF THE ARYL HYDROCARBON RECEPTOR (AHR)–RORΓT SIGNALING PATHWAY, CRITICAL REGULATORS OF MUCOSAL IMMUNE HOMEOSTASIS AND EPITHELIAL INTEGRITY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SIV-INDUCED AHR DYSREGULATION IMPAIRS TYPE-3 CYTOKINE RESPONSES, DISRUPTS GUT EPITHELIAL TIGHT JUNCTIONS, AND PROMOTES CHRONIC INFLAMMATION. WE FURTHER POSIT THAT THERAPEUTIC ACTIVATION OF AHR SIGNALING, COMBINED WITH IN VIVO ΓΔ T CELL MODULATION, CAN RESTORE EPITHELIAL INTEGRITY AND REDUCE INFLAMMATION.  THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEFINE THE ROLE OF AHR SIGNALING IN REGULATING INTESTINAL BARRIER INTEGRITY AND INFLAMMATION DURING ART-SUPPRESSED INFECTION. THE SPECIFIC AIMS OF THIS STUDY ARE: (1) TO DEFINE HOW GUT AHR SIGNALING PRESERVES EPITHELIAL BARRIER INTEGRITY AND RESTRAINS SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION DURING CHRONIC SIV+ART INFECTION; AND (2) TO DETERMINE WHETHER THERAPEUTIC ACTIVATION OF AHR SIGNALING—VIA EXOGENOUS AHR LIGANDS AND IN VIVO ΓΔ T CELL STIMULATION—CAN RESTORE GUT BARRIER FUNCTION BY ENHANCING THE AHR–IL-22 IMMUNE AXIS. TO ACHIEVE THESE AIMS, WE WILL INTEGRATE MULTIOMICS PROFILING (TRANSCRIPTOMICS, METABOLOMICS, MICROBIOMICS) WITH MECHANISTIC STUDIES IN A PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT MODEL OF CHRONIC SIV+ART INFECTION, INCLUDING MACAQUES ON A HIGH-FAT, HIGH-CALORIE WESTERN DIET. OUR STUDIES WILL DISSECT THE INTERRELATIONSHIP BETWEEN AHR SIGNALING, TYPE-3 IMMUNITY, AND THE GUT MICROBIOME, AND PROVIDE MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO HOW GUT DYSFUNCTION SUSTAINS CHRONIC INFLAMMATION DESPITE ART.  SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TARGETING AHR PATHWAYS TO RESTORE INTESTINAL BARRIER FUNCTION, LIMIT SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION, AND REDUCE THE LONG-TERM BURDEN OF COMORBIDITIES IN PLWH.

description: DETERMINING THE ROLE OF E-CADHERIN AND PAR-3 IN EPITHELIAL SYMMETRY BREAKING AND REPAIR - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT EPITHELIAL TISSUES ENCASE METAZOANS, PROTECTING THEM FROM AND ALLOWING REGULATED INTERACTION WITH THE ENVIRONMENT. ESSENTIAL TO THESE FUNCTIONS IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN APICAL-BASOLATERAL POLARITY AXIS WITHIN CELLS AND COORDINATION OF THESE AXES ACROSS TISSUES, WHERE APICAL SURFACES FACE THE ENVIRONMENT, BASOLATERAL SURFACES CONTACT NEIGHBORING CELLS OR SUBSTRATES, AND TRANSMEMBRANE JUNCTIONS SEPARATE THESE DOMAINS AND MAINTAIN INTERCELLULAR ADHESION. THE EMERGENCE OF A COORDINATED POLARITY AXIS IN EPITHELIAL TISSUES IS CENTRAL TO HUMAN HEALTH AS FAILURE IN THESE PROCESSES CAN LEAD TO TISSUE MALFUNCTIONS, DIGESTIVE DISEASES, EMBRYONIC LETHALITY, OR SEVERE BIRTH DEFECTS. ALTHOUGH SOME PRIMORDIA THAT GIVE RISE TO EPITHELIA LEVERAGE STRUCTURAL ASYMMETRIES SUCH AS A BASEMENT MEMBRANE OR NATURALLY CONTACT-FREE SURFACE TO DIRECT APICO-BASOLATERAL POLARIZATION, MANY EPITHELIAL TISSUES DERIVE FROM UNPOLARIZED PRIMORDIA AND MUST GENERATE POLARITY DE NOVO. THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THIS EPITHELIAL SYMMETRY BREAKING ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD, ESPECIALLY IN VIVO, AND HAVE MOSTLY BEEN STUDIED IN CELL CULTURE MODELS WHICH DO NOT REPLICATE THE DEVELOPMENTAL CONTEXTS IN WHICH SYMMETRY BREAKING NORMALLY OCCURS. ALL EPITHELIA TEND TO POLARIZE THE SAME MOLECULAR COMPONENTS, INCLUDING THE INTRACELLULAR SCAFFOLDING PROTEIN PAR-3 WHICH DESIGNATES THE APICAL SURFACE AND THE TRANSMEMBRANE ADHESION PROTEIN E-CADHERIN WHICH COMPRISES ADHERENS JUNCTIONS. THESE PROTEINS COMMONLY FORM CLUSTERS BEFORE LOCALIZING IN THIS TERMINAL CONFIGURATION AND, CONSISTENTLY, WE FOUND THAT PAR-3 AND E- CADHERIN CO-CLUSTER INTO STEREOTYPED ‘LOCAL POLARITY COMPLEXES’ (LPCS) AT CELL CONTACTS TO BREAK SYMMETRY WITHIN DEVELOPING C. ELEGANS INTESTINAL EPITHELIAL CELLS. THESE LPCS THEN DELIVER POLARITY COMPONENTS TO THE FUTURE APICAL SURFACE TO DEFINE TISSUE-WIDE POLARITY. THUS, LPC FORMATION AND MOVEMENT GENERATE ASYMMETRY AT THE CELL AND TISSUE-LEVEL IN THE C. ELEGANS INTESTINE AND WE WILL USE STATE OF THE ART GENETIC, PROTEOMIC, AND IMAGING TOOLS DEVELOPED IN MY LAB TO DETERMINE HOW PAR-3 AND E-CADHERIN ENABLE THIS SYMMETRY BREAKING. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE THE STRUCTURE AND COMPOSITION OF LPCS. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE THE MOLECULAR FUNCTION OF PAR-3 AND E- CADHERIN, TESTING THE HYPOTHESIS THAT PAR-3 MODULATES E-CADHERIN BASED ADHESION AND THAT THIS MODULATION WITHIN LPCS IS REQUIRED FOR POLARITY ESTABLISHMENT. AIM 3 WILL LEVERAGE A NEW MODEL FOR THE REPAIR OF CONGENITAL EPITHELIAL DEFECTS, CAPITALIZING ON THE DISCOVERY THAT PAR-3 CAN PROMOTE THE REPAIR OF C. ELEGANS CYSTIC LARVAL INTESTINES WHILE E-CADHERIN ANTAGONIZES THIS PROCESS. THIS SYSTEM WILL SERVE AS A COMPANION SYSTEM TO EMBRYONIC INTESTINAL POLARIZATION TO DETERMINE THE MOLECULAR INTERPLAY BETWEEN PAR-3 AND E-CADHERIN, ADDING AN EXPERIMENTAL FRAMEWORK TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT PAR-3 CAN MODULATE E-CADHERIN-BASED ADHESION. THESE STUDIES WILL REVEAL THE MECHANISMS OF EPITHELIAL SYMMETRY BREAKING AND THUS ARE CRITICAL FOR OUR BASIC UNDERSTANDING OF DEVELOPMENT AND EPITHELIAL DISEASES SUCH AS POLYCYSTIC KIDNEY AND MICROVILLUS INCLUSION DISEASE AND MAY ALSO GUIDE THE REPAIR CONGENITAL ORGAN DEFECTS.

description: KIDNEY TUBULE DYSFUNCTION IN APOL1 - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE (CKD) IS COMMON, COSTLY, AND STRONGLY ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED MORTALITY. CURRENTLY, CLINICIANS ARE LIMITED IN THEIR ASSESSMENT OF CKD SINCE THE ONLY MARKERS TO MEASURE AND MONITOR KIDNEY HEALTH ARE SERUM CREATININE AND ALBUMINURIA. THESE TRADITIONAL MARKERS, HOWEVER, DO NOT CAPTURE FUNCTIONS CRITICAL TO LIFE DONE BY THE KIDNEY TUBULES, SUCH AS NUTRIENT REABSORPTION AND TOXIN SECRETION. DURING MY CAREER DEVELOPMENT AWARD, I MADE IMPORTANT DISCOVERIES IDENTIFYING THE ROLE THAT TUBULAR MARKERS PLAY IN THE PROGRESSION OF CKD, RISK OF ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY (AKI), AND MORTALITY AND HOW TO COMBINE BIOMARKERS IN SUMMARY SCORES THAT COULD INCREASE THEIR UTILITY. IN THIS GRANT, I SEEK TO ADVANCE THE CURRENT KNOWLEDGE OF APOL1 BY EXPLORING A NOVEL AXIS OF TUBULAR BIOMARKERS IN THIS DISEASE TO UNDERSTAND THE VARIABILITY IN PROGRESSION BETTER. AFRICAN AMERICANS HAVE A 2-TO-4-FOLD HIGHER INCIDENCE OF KIDNEY FAILURE REQUIRING DIALYSIS COMPARED TO THEIR WHITE COUNTERPARTS. THIS DISPARITY IS PARTLY DUE TO APOL1, A GENE FOUND AMONG AFRICAN ANCESTRY INDIVIDUALS STRONGLY ASSOCIATED WITH KIDNEY FAILURE. EVEN THOUGH APOL1 INCREASES THE CKD), AND IS PRESENT IN THE KIDNEY TUBULES, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THE ROLE THAT THE TUBULES PLAY IN THE PROGRESSION OF KIDNEY DISEASE. THE KDIGO CONTROVERSIES CONFERENCE ON APOL1 KIDNEY DISEASE, HELD THIS YEAR, HIGHLIGHTED THE IMPORTANCE OF EVALUATING WHICH BIOMARKERS PREDICT THE DEVELOPMENT AND PROGRESSION OF APOL1 KIDNEY DISEASE. IN PRELIMINARY STUDIES, I HAVE FOUND THAT INDIVIDUALS WITH APOL1 RISK VARIANTS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH A HIGHER RISK OF FASTER KIDNEY FUNCTION DECLINE. IT IS ESSENTIAL TO UNDERSTAND THE ROLE OF TUBULES IN THE PROGRESSION OF CKD. TO THAT END, I WILL FIRST EXPAND THE PANEL OF MARKERS TO MORE FULLY CAPTURE THE MYRIAD BIOLOGICAL FUNCTIONS OF KIDNEY TUBULES. THEN, SINCE USING MANY BIOMARKERS IS NOT PRACTICAL IN THE CLINICAL SETTING AND THERE IS LIKELY OVERLAP IN THE UNDERLYING PATHOLOGY REFLECTED BY THESE BIOMARKERS, I WILL USE EXPLORATORY FACTOR ANALYSIS TO COMBINE BIOMARKERS OF KIDNEY TUBULE HEALTH IN URINE AND PLASMA AND STUDY THEIR ROLE IN LONGITUDINAL ESTIMATED GLOMERULAR FILTRATION RATE CHANGE. SINCE AKI) IS AN IMPORTANT DRIVER OF CKD, AND SOME STUDIES SUGGEST THAT PEOPLE WITH APOL1 ARE MORE VULNERABLE TO AKI, I WILL EVALUATE THIS SYNDROME IN A WELL-CHARACTERIZED COHORT. I WILL UTILIZE THE SPRINT AND REGARDS COHORTS FOR THESE FIRST TWO AIMS, WHICH INCLUDE NUMEROUS PARTICIPANTS WITH APOL1 RISK VARIANTS. FINALLY, FOR THE FIRST TIME, I WILL EVALUATE THE ROLE OF TUBULAR BIOMARKERS IN INTERSTITIAL FIBROSIS AND TUBULAR ATROPHY, THE FINAL COMMON PATHWAY OF CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE, USING THE NEPHROTIC SYNDROME STUDY NETWORK AND CURE GLOMERULOPATHY, TWO RELATED LONGITUDINAL COHORTS WITH EXTREMELY DETAILED CLINICAL PHENOTYPES, INCLUDING BIOPSY DATA AS WELL AS URINE AND BLOOD SAMPLES. OUR RESULTS IN THIS PROPOSAL WILL IDENTIFY A NOVEL PARADIGM OF KIDNEY DISEASE PROGRESSION IN APOL1 AND SET THE STAGE FOR A CLINICAL TRIAL TO EVALUATE INNOVATIVE THERAPIES TO MITIGATE OR PREVENT CKD PROGRESSION AMONG PATIENTS WITH APOL1 RISK VARIANTS.

description: NON-INVASIVE RISK STRATIFICATION OF NEUROGENIC LOWER URINARY TRACT DYSFUNCTION WITH MAGNETIC RESONANCE FINGERPRINTING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  NEUROGENIC LOWER URINARY TRACT DYSFUNCTION (NLUTD) AFFECTS >80% OF THE 300,000 AMERICANS WITH SPINAL CORD INJURY (SCI), SIGNIFICANTLY IMPAIRING QUALITY OF LIFE AND POTENTIALLY LEADING TO RENAL FAILURE AND DEATH. CURRENT AMERICAN UROLOGICAL ASSOCIATION (AUA) GUIDELINES RECOMMEND STRATIFYING PATIENTS BY THEIR RISK OF DAMAGE TO THE UPPER URINARY TRACT. ALTHOUGH RISK STRATIFICATION CURRENTLY RELIES ON URODYNAMIC STUDIES (UDS) TO EVALUATE BLADDER FUNCTION, THESE TESTS ARE INVASIVE (INVOLVING URETHRAL AND RECTAL CATHETERIZATION), SUFFER FROM POOR REPRODUCIBILITY, ASSESS THE BLADDER UNDER NON-PHYSIOLOGIC CONDITIONS, AND CAN PROVOKE SEVERE REACTIONS (E.G., AUTONOMIC DYSREFLEXIA) IN SOME SCI PATIENTS. MOREOVER, NEITHER UDS NOR CONVENTIONAL DIAGNOSTIC IMAGING (ULTRASOUND OR CT) PROVIDE INFORMATION ABOUT UNDERLYING TISSUE-LEVEL BLADDER WALL REMODELING THAT DRIVES DISEASE PROGRESSION. WE PROPOSE A QUANTITATIVE MAGNETIC RESONANCE FINGERPRINTING (MRF) SOLUTION TO NON-INVASIVELY ASSESS BLADDER WALL TISSUE CHARACTERISTICS. THIS TECHNOLOGY WILL IMPROVE BIOLOGICAL UNDERSTANDING OF PATHOLOGICAL BLADDER WALL REMODELING IN NLUTD, ENABLE EARLIER INTERVENTION AND IMPROVED RISK STRATIFICATION, AND SUPPORT PERSONALIZED MANAGEMENT GUIDED BY DISCRETE PHENOTYPES (DEFINED BY QUANTITATIVE IMAGING BIOMARKERS). MRF IS AN INNOVATIVE MRI FRAMEWORK THAT PRODUCES CO-REGISTERED, QUANTITATIVE MAPS OF MULTIPLE TISSUE PROPERTIES FROM A SINGLE RAPID SCAN. ALTHOUGH MRF HAS BEEN DEMONSTRATED IN OTHER ORGANS, QUANTITATIVE MRI OF THE BLADDER REMAINS NASCENT DUE TO CHALLENGES OF IMAGING THE THIN BLADDER WALL. WE WILL OPTIMIZE MRF FOR SIMULTANEOUS, HIGH-RESOLUTION, 3D ISOTROPIC WHOLE-BLADDER MAPPING OF TISSUE PROPERTIES RELEVANT TO NLUTD, INCLUDING T1 (TO ASSESS CHRONIC INFLAMMATION AND FIBROSIS), T2 (TO EVALUATE ACUTE INFLAMMATION AND EDEMA), AND EXTRACELLULAR VOLUME FRACTION (ECV, A MARKER OF INTERSTITIAL EXPANSION AND FIBROSIS). IN AIM 1, WE WILL OPTIMIZE MRF FOR HIGH-RESOLUTION TISSUE CHARACTERIZATION WITH 3D WHOLE-BLADDER COVERAGE AND ESTABLISH NORMATIVE RANGES FOR BLADDER T1, T2, AND ECV VALUES IN HEALTHY ADULTS ACROSS THE AGE SPAN. IN AIM 2, WE WILL SCAN PATIENTS WITH SCI-RELATED NLUTD UNDERGOING CLINICAL UDS TO DEVELOP A PREDICTIVE MODEL THAT INCORPORATES QUANTITATIVE MRF BIOMARKERS AND LIMITED CLINICAL VARIABLES TO NON-INVASIVELY IDENTIFY PATIENTS WITH HIGH-RISK URODYNAMIC PROFILES, YIELDING A COMPOSITE RISK SCORE TERMED THE MRF VESICAL SCI (MIVESCI) SCORE. IN AIM 3, WE WILL PROSPECTIVELY EVALUATE THE MIVESCI SCORE IN A BLINDED STUDY, COMPARING DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY AGAINST STANDARD AUA RISK STRATIFICATION BASED ON UDS. IN ADDITION, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE PROGNOSTIC UTILITY OF THE MIVESCI SCORE TO PREDICT CLINICAL PROGRESSION OF NLUTD OVER ONE YEAR. THIS RESEARCH HAS THE POTENTIAL TO USHER A SEISMIC SHIFT IN NLUTD MANAGEMENT. THE OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE A RAPID (≤30-MIN), NON-INVASIVE, PUSH-BUTTON MRF EXAM YIELDING QUANTITATIVE BLADDER WALL BIOMARKERS FOR NLUTD RISK STRATIFICATION AND PROGNOSTICATION. THIS WORK ALIGNS WITH CURRENT PRIORITIES IN NEUROUROLOGY, SEEKING TO SHIFT NLUTD CARE TOWARD OBJECTIVE, TISSUE-BASED PHENOTYPING TO PRESERVE LONG-TERM HEALTH OF THE URINARY TRACT.

description: DISSECTING FUNCTIONAL DECOMPENSATION OF END-STAGE LIVER DISEASE AND THE MECHANISM AND IMPACT OF TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS ON LONG-TERM FUNCTIONAL REPROGRAMMING - PROJECT SUMMARY  END-STAGE LIVER DISEASE (ESLD) IS RESPONSIBLE FOR ROUGHLY 300,000 DEATHS ANNUALLY IN THE US AND IMPOSES A SIGNIFICANT ECONOMIC BURDEN ON SOCIETY. DESPITE ITS PREVALENCE, THERE ARE CURRENTLY NO EFFECTIVE PHARMACOLOGICAL THERAPIES. THE ONLY TREATMENT FOR ESLD IS ORTHOTOPIC LIVER TRANSPLANT, BUT THE DEMAND FOR ORGANS FAR OUTWEIGHS WHAT IS AVAILABLE. TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSES OF ESLD LIVERS HAVE REVEALED SIGNIFICANT CHANGES IN THE EXPRESSION OF TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS THAT ARE ASSOCIATED WITH ESLD. TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS ARE SEQUENCE-SPECIFIC DNA BINDING PROTEINS RESPONSIBLE FOR CONTROLLING CELL IDENTITY, DEVELOPMENT, AND OTHER CELLULAR PROCESSES. APPROXIMATELY 1,600 TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS IN THE HUMAN GENOME COORDINATE CELL TYPE– SPECIFIC EXPRESSION OF MORE THAN 25,000 PROTEIN-CODING GENES, EMPHASIZING THEIR CENTRAL ROLE IN CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS AND DISEASE. THE WIDESPREAD REGULATORY IMPACT THESE FACTORS HAVE ON CELLULAR PROCESSES HIGHLIGHTS THEM AS POTENTIAL DRIVERS OF DISEASE PROGRESSION, AS WELL AS TARGETS FOR THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION. OUR PREVIOUS STUDIES IDENTIFIED HNF4Α, A TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR REQUIRED FOR APPROPRIATE HEPATOCYTE FUNCTION, AS DIFFERENTIALLY EXPRESSED IN DECOMPENSATED CIRRHOSIS AND ESLD. HNF4Α CONTROLS KEY METABOLIC, DETOXIFICATION, AND SYNTHETIC PATHWAYS CRITICAL FOR LIVER FUNCTION. MORE RECENTLY, WE FOUND THAT RE-EXPRESSION OF HNF4Α MRNA ALLEVIATES TRANSCRIPTOMIC CHANGES ASSOCIATED WITH HEPATIC FAILURE AND IMPROVES LIVER FUNCTION AND SURVIVAL IN VIVO. ALTHOUGH PREVIOUS STUDIES HAVE DETERMINED THE EFFICACY OF HNF4Α-MRNA LIPID NANOPARTICLES (LNPS) IN TREATING LIVER DISEASE, THESE EFFORTS HAVE BEEN LIMITED TO EARLY, REVERSIBLE STAGES. AS THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH ESLD PROGRESSES AND HNF4Α REPROGRAMMING SUCCESSFULLY ALLEVIATES DECOMPENSATED CIRRHOSIS AND HEPATIC FAILURE ARE UNKNOWN, THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS TO ADDRESS THIS GAP IN KNOWLEDGE. AIM 1 WILL INVESTIGATE THE EFFICACY AND STABILITY OF HNF4Α-MRNA-LNP TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND METABOLIC REPROGRAMMING IN PRIMARY HUMAN DECOMPENSATED CIRRHOTIC HEPATOCYTES AND A RODENT MODEL OF ESLD. AIM 2 WILL ENHANCE THE STABILITY AND EFFICACY OF HEPATOCYTE FITNESS REPROGRAMMING. USING PREVIOUS TRANSCRIPTOMIC FINDINGS, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED CANDIDATE GENES WHOSE CO-EXPRESSION MAY HEIGHTEN HEPATOCYTE REPROGRAMMING. WE WILL TEST WHETHER CANDIDATE FACTORS, ALONE OR IN COMBINATION WITH HNF4Α, AUGMENT REPROGRAMMING EFFICACY AND HEPATOCYTE FITNESS BOTH IN VITRO AND IN VIVO. AIM 3 WILL DETERMINE THE UPSTREAM MECHANISMS CAUSING HNF4Α MISEXPRESSION DRIVEN BY THE HYPOTHESIS THAT ENHANCER DECOMMISSIONING, EITHER THROUGH CELL COMPOSITION CHANGES OR REDUCED P300-BASED ENHANCER ACTIVITY, DRIVES DOWNREGULATION OF HNF4Α EXPRESSION IN ESLD. COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL DEFINE THE MOLECULAR BASIS OF HNF4Α DYSREGULATION IN ESLD AND ESTABLISH MRNA-LNP–BASED TRANSCRIPTIONAL REPROGRAMMING AS A TRANSFORMATIVE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY FOR TERMINAL LIVER FAILURE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: METABOLOMICS-DRIVEN INSIGHTS INTO ULTRA-PROCESSED FOODS: IDENTIFYING HIGH-RISK UPF SUBTYPES FOR T2D PREVENTION - TYPE 2 DIABETES (T2D) IS A SIGNIFICANT PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERN, AFFECTING OVER 38 MILLION ADULTS IN THE U.S. AND COSTING THE ECONOMY NEARLY $413 BILLION ANNUALLY. DESPITE THE ESTABLISHED ROLE OF DIET IN T2D RISK, THE SPECIFIC CONTRIBUTIONS OF ULTRA-PROCESSED FOODS (UPFS) REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. UPFS, CHARACTERIZED BY INDUSTRIAL PROCESSING AND THE USE OF COSMETIC ADDITIVES FOR ENHANCED PALATABILITY AND EXTENDED SHELF-LIFE, ACCOUNT FOR APPROXIMATELY 58% OF CALORIC INTAKE IN THE U.S. POPULATION. ALTHOUGH SOME UPF SUBTYPES HAVE BEEN IMPLICATED IN INCREASING T2D RISK, OTHERS MAY BE RELATIVELY INERT OR EVEN BENEFICIAL, UNDERSCORING THE NEED FOR DISCERNING THEIR DISTINCT HEALTH EFFECTS. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO CLARIFY THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN UPF CONSUMPTION AND T2D BY INTEGRATING A NOVEL CONTROLLED FEEDING TRIAL WITH LARGE-SCALE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL ANALYSES. IN A CROSSOVER FEEDING TRIAL DESIGN, 40 HEALTHY ADULTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN FOUR ISOCALORIC DIET PHASES: ONE CONTROL DIET AND THREE DIETS FOCUSED ON DIFFERENT UPF SUBTYPES-STARCHY AND REFINED GRAINS, MEATS AND FISH, AND DAIRY-BASED PRODUCTS. FOODS AND BEVERAGES WILL BE PROVIDED DURING THE STUDY, AND PARTICIPANTS WILL ATTEND WEEKLY CLINIC VISITS FOR IN-PERSON ASSESSMENTS AND BIOSPECIMEN COLLECTIONS. WE WILL OBTAIN METABOLOMIC PROFILING OF THE FASTING PLASMA SAMPLES AND CONDUCT DATA ANALYSES TO ISOLATE BIOMARKERS OF THE SPECIFIC UPF SUBTYPES, INDUSTRIAL ADDITIVES, OR PROCESSES. THESE BIOMARKERS WILL BE VALIDATED AGAINST DIETARY DATA IN WELL-CHARACTERIZED, CONTEMPORARY U.S.-BASED COHORTS. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN THESE MARKERS AND T2D RISK IN LONGITUDINAL OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES TO COST-EFFECTIVELY LEVERAGE EXISTING DATA FOR PLASMA METABOLOMIC PROFILES COLLECTED AT THE COHORTS' BASELINES, WITH FOLLOW-UP FOR INCIDENT T2D CASES, TO EVALUATE UPF-DERIVED METABOLITES WITH T2D RISK, CONTROLLING FOR OTHER DIETARY AND LIFESTYLE FACTORS. LEADING THIS RIGOROUS AND FEASIBLE EFFORT IS A TEAM OF MULTIPLE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS (MPLS) WHO BRING TOGETHER COMPLEMENTARY EXPERTISE. THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM COMBINES PROFICIENCY IN NUTRITION SCIENCE, METABOLOMICS, EPIDEMIOLOGY, AND NUTRI-KINETIC FEEDING STUDIES, ENSURING A ROBUST APPROACH CRUCIAL FOR ACHIEVING THE PROJECT GOALS. BY IDENTIFYING METABOLOMICS ASSOCIATED WITH HIGH-RISK UPF SUBTYPES THIS RESEARCH WILL ENHANCE UNDERSTANDING OF THE BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS LINKING DIET TO T2D. THE FINDINGS ARE EXPECTED TO INFORM TARGETED DIETARY RECOMMENDATIONS AND POLICY INTERVENTIONS, FACILITATING HEALTHIER FOOD CHOICES AND PROMOTING EFFECTIVE REFORMULATIONS IN THE FOOD INDUSTRY. THROUGH THIS METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK, OUR STUDY STRIVES TO ADDRESS CRITICAL GAPS IN THE EVIDENCE-BASE, ULTIMATELY REDUCING THE BURDEN OF T2D AND IMPROVED PUBLIC HEALTH OUTCOMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TESTING STRATEGIES TO INCREASE THE IMPACT OF AN OBESITY PREVENTION INTERVENTION IN A COMMUNITY SETTING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT AMONG YOUNG ADULT WOMEN 40% AND 12% HAD OBESITY AND SEVERE OBESITY IN 2017-2020, RESPECTIVELY, ELEVATING THEIR RISK OF CHRONIC DISEASE SUCH AS DIABETES AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. YET YOUNG ADULT WOMEN FACE BARRIERS TO PARTICIPATING IN INTERVENTIONS THAT PROMOTE HEALTHY WEIGHT AND PREVENT CHRONIC DISEASES SUCH AS DIABETES. TO ADDRESS THIS, OUR TEAM DEVELOPED AND TESTED THE EVIDENCE-BASED HEALTHY EATING AND ACTIVE LIVING TAUGHT AT HOME (HEALTH) INTERVENTION, DEMONSTRATING HEALTH’S EFFECTIVENESS TO REDUCE WEIGHT GAIN AMONG MOTHERS OF YOUNG CHILDREN AND TO PROMOTE HEALTHY GESTATIONAL WEIGHT GAIN AND POSTPARTUM WEIGHT LOSS, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH PARENTS AS TEACHERS (PAT). PAT IS A NATIONAL, EVIDENCE-BASED HOME VISITING ORGANIZATION WITH EXPERTISE IN ENGAGING AND SUPPORTING FAMILIES, ESPECIALLY THOSE NOT WELL REACHED BY THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM. PAT REACHES 73,283 FAMILIES NATIONWIDE THROUGH A NETWORK OF 4,300 PARENT EDUCATORS ACROSS 920 AFFILIATES. PAT HAS DECIDED TO DELIVER HEALTH AT SCALE, WHICH PRESENTS A UNIQUE AND TIMELY OPPORTUNITY TO DEVELOP AND TEST STRATEGIES TO SUPPORT SYSTEM-WIDE HEALTH IMPLEMENTATION. OUR PREVIOUS STUDIES DEMONSTRATED POSITIVE PERCEPTIONS OF HEALTH AMONG PARENT EDUCATORS AND MOTHERS AND IDENTIFIED POTENTIAL IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES TO SUPPORT ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND REACH. THE CURRENT STUDY WILL USE IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE, PARTICIPATORY SYSTEMS SCIENCE MODELING, PAT NATIONAL CENTER EXPERTISE AND ADMINISTRATIVE DATA, AND ADAPTIVE STRATEGY METHODS TO: 1) REFINE IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY BUNDLES TO PROMOTE HEALTH ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND REACH; 2) EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE STRATEGY BUNDLES REFINED IN AIM 1 ON HEALTH ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND REACH AT 12- MONTHS USING A SEQUENTIAL MULTIPLE ASSIGNMENT RANDOMIZED TRIAL (SMART) DESIGN WITH 627 PAT AFFILIATES; AND 3) CHARACTERIZE THE MECHANISMS BEHIND IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY BUNDLES. THIS STUDY IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT AIMS TO EXPAND ACCESS TO AN EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTION TO PREVENT WEIGHT GAIN AND CHRONIC DISEASE SUCH AS DIABETES FOR MOTHERS THROUGH A NATIONAL HOME VISITING ORGANIZATION'S EXISTING NATIONAL SYSTEM AND INFRASTRUCTURE. IT BUILDS ON OUR TEAM’S EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN APPLYING IMPLEMENTATION AND SYSTEM SCIENCE TO LEVERAGE THE STRENGTHS OF COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS TO REACH AND ENGAGE COMMUNITIES OFTEN NOT REACHED BY THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM. THIS INNOVATIVE RESEARCH 1) OPTIMIZES AND TESTS STRATEGY BUNDLES USING A SMART DESIGN IN REAL-WORLD SITES AND 2) EXPLORES MECHANISMS FOR BUNDLE EFFECTIVENESS. OUR RESULTS WILL IMPACT PUBLIC HEALTH BY REACHING MOTHERS NATIONWIDE WITH HEALTH AND EXPANDING IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY AND MECHANISM EVIDENCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IDENTIFYING NEURAL AND COMPUTATIONAL UNDERPINNINGS OF SELF-CONTROL COSTS IN OBESITY AND LOSS-OF-CONTROL EATING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT OVER A THIRD OF US ADULTS HAVE BODY MASS INDICES (BMIS) IN THE “OBESITY” RANGE, WHICH ARE ASSOCIATED WITH SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED RISKS FOR MEDICAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL COMORBIDITIES. THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED TO IDENTIFY THE DECISION-MAKING MECHANISMS UNDERLYING EATING BEHAVIORS THAT PROMOTE AND EXACERBATE OBESITY. ONE SUCH EATING BEHAVIOR IS LOSS-OF-CONTROL (LOC) EATING, WHICH IS DEFINED BY A SENSE OF BEING UNABLE TO STOP EATING OR CONTROL WHAT OR HOW MUCH ONE IS EATING. LOC EATING PREDICTS WEIGHT GAIN AND INDEPENDENTLY INCREASES THE RISK FOR A RANGE OF MEDICAL ISSUES AND PSYCHOSOCIAL IMPAIRMENTS, SUGGESTING THAT IT REPRESENTS A BEHAVIORAL PHENOTYPE OF OBESITY WITH A PARTICULARLY HIGH BURDEN OF DISEASE. TO DATE, MOST STUDIES HAVE ASSUMED THAT DYSREGULATED FOOD INTAKE, AND THEREFORE, HIGHER WEIGHT, IS PERPETUATED BY DEFICITS IN THE ABILITY TO DEPLOY SELF- CONTROL. HOWEVER, RECENT THEORETICAL AND EMPIRICAL WORK STEMMING FROM THE COGNITIVE AND DECISION NEUROSCIENCE LITERATURE SUGGESTS THAT FAILURES TO SUCCESSFULLY DEPLOY SELF-CONTROL DEPEND MORE CENTRALLY ON PEOPLES’ ESTIMATES OF HOW COGNITIVELY COSTLY (I.E., DIFFICULT OR EFFORTFUL) THE ATTEMPTED USE OF CONTROL WILL BE. THIS NEW FRAMEWORK VIEWS CONTROL DEPLOYMENT AS THE RESULT OF A DECISION THAT EMERGES FROM INDIVIDUALS WEIGHING THE PERCEIVED BENEFITS VS. COGNITIVE COSTS OF EXERCISING CONTROL. HERE, WE APPLY THIS NOVEL FRAMEWORK TO CHARACTERIZE HOW ESTIMATED SELF- CONTROL COSTS MAY PROMOTE LOC EATING AND OBESITY. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL COMBINE NEUROIMAGING AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING WITH A SELF-CONTROL DECISION-MAKING TASK TO TEST THE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS THAT MORE DYSREGULATED EATING AND HIGHER BMIS ARE MAINTAINED BY INCREASES IN THE PERCEIVED COGNITIVE COST ASSOCIATED WITH DEPLOYING CONTROL. DURING FUNCTIONAL MRI, SAMPLES OF ADULTS WITH BMIS IN THE OBESE RANGE WHO ENDORSE LOC EATING, ADULTS WITH OBESITY BUT WITHOUT COMORBID LOC EATING, AND CONTROLS WITHOUT OBESE BMIS OR LOC EATING WILL COMPLETE OUR VALIDATED TASK THAT MEASURES SELF-CONTROL COSTS: HOW MUCH INDIVIDUALS ARE WILLING TO PAY TO RESTRICT THEIR ACCESS TO TEMPTING FOOD REWARDS SO THEY CAN AVOID HAVING TO USE SELF-CONTROL. WE WILL COMPARE GROUPS ON THESE SELF-CONTROL COSTS AND ON COMPUTATIONAL PARAMETERS DESCRIBING HOW THESE COSTS CHANGE WITH INCREASING TEMPTATION INTENSITY (AIM 1). WE WILL ALSO COMPARE GROUPS ON THESE COSTS’ UNDERLYING NEURAL SUBSTRATES (AIM 2). FINALLY, WE WILL TEST HOW INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES IN SELF-CONTROL COSTS AND NEURAL ACTIVATION CORRELATE WITH AND PREDICT CHANGES IN EATING AND WEIGHT OVER TIME (AIM 3). THE RESEARCH TEAM INCLUDES EXPERTS IN THE COGNITIVE NEUROSCIENCE OF DYSREGULATED EATING, SELF-CONTROL AND VALUE-BASED DECISION-MAKING, COMPUTATIONAL MODELING, AND NEUROIMAGING. THE STUDY IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT MEASURES A DECISION-MAKING PROCESS THAT OCCURS BEFORE THE ULTIMATE SUCCESSFUL OR FAILED DEPLOYMENT OF CONTROL OVER EATING. BY ASSESSING HOW THIS PROCESS AND ITS NEURAL UNDERPINNINGS VARY BY WEIGHT STATUS AND WITH THE PRESENCE OF LOC EATING, AND BY TESTING SELF-CONTROL COST ESTIMATION AS A POTENTIAL PROGNOSTIC BIOMARKER FOR FUTURE EATING AND WEIGHT CHANGE OVER TIME, THIS PROJECT WILL REVEAL POTENTIAL TARGETS FOR NEW NEUROMODULATORY AND COGNITIVE-BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: 3D INTESTINAL ORGANOID MODELS TO DISSECT THE BIDIRECTIONAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN GUT BARRIER AND HIV TRANSCRIPTION - PROJECT ABSTRACT THE GUT IS A PRIMARY SITE OF HIV REPLICATION DURING ACUTE INFECTION, LEADING TO PROFOUND IMMUNE DEPLETION AND BARRIER DISRUPTION THAT IS ONLY PARTIALLY RESTORED BY ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART). DESPITE DECADES OF RESEARCH SHOWING THAT HIV INFECTION CAUSES PERSISTENT GUT DAMAGE LEADING TO CHRONIC INFLAMMATION AND COMORBIDITIES IN PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV (PLWH), THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THIS RELATIONSHIP REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD, PRIMARILY DUE TO DIFFICULTIES REPLICATING THE GUT MICROENVIRONMENT IN VITRO AND CHALLENGES IN OBTAINING IN VIVO SAMPLES. WE PROPOSE TO INVESTIGATE THE CRITICAL BIDIRECTIONAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN HIV TRANSCRIPTION AND INTESTINAL BARRIER FUNCTION USING COMPLEMENTARY THREE-DIMENSIONAL ORGANOID MODELS: PATIENT-DERIVED ORGANOIDS (PDOS) ISOLATED FROM INTESTINAL BIOPSIES THAT PRESERVE DONOR-SPECIFIC CHARACTERISTICS AND DISEASE PHENOTYPES, AND INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELL-DERIVED INTESTINAL ORGANOIDS (HIOS) THAT OFFER HIGH-THROUGHPUT GENETIC MANIPULATION CAPABILITIES AND INCLUDE A MESENCHYMAL LAYER CRITICAL FOR GUT-IMMUNE INTERACTIONS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL EXAMINE HOW HIV TRANSCRIPTION INFLUENCES INTESTINAL INFLAMMATION AND BARRIER INTEGRITY BY CO-CULTURING ORGANOIDS WITH HIV- INFECTED CD4+ T CELLS FROM BOTH PLWH AND PLWOH. IN AIM 2, WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW THE INTESTINAL MICROENVIRONMENT INFLUENCES HIV TRANSCRIPTION, EXPLORING THE MECHANISMS THAT REGULATE VIRAL ACTIVITY IN THE GUT THROUGH COMPREHENSIVE TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND METABOLIC ANALYSES. THIS INNOVATIVE STUDY WILL ESTABLISH ROBUST EXPERIMENTAL PLATFORMS FOR BOTH MECHANISTIC DISSECTION OF HIV-GUT INTERACTIONS AND TRANSLATIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS. UNDERSTANDING THIS BIDIRECTIONAL RELATIONSHIP IS CRITICAL FOR HIV CURE STRATEGIES, AS INTESTINAL BARRIER DYSFUNCTION DRIVES SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION CONTRIBUTING TO HIV PERSISTENCE AND COMORBIDITIES. OUR FINDINGS WILL INFORM NOVEL APPROACHES TO RESTORE INTESTINAL HOMEOSTASIS, MITIGATE CHRONIC INFLAMMATION, AND ULTIMATELY IMPROVE LONG-TERM HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE EFFECT OF VERAPAMIL ON BETA CELL FUNCTION IN ADOLESCENTS AND ADULTS WITH CYSTIC FIBROSIS-RELATED DYSGLYCEMIA - ABSTRACT CYSTIC FIBROSIS-RELATED DIABETES (CFRD) IS INCREASINGLY PREVALENT COMORBIDITY IN PEOPLE WITH CYSTIC FIBROSIS (PWCF). CFRD AND ITS PRECURSOR STATE, ABNORMAL GLUCOSE TOLERANCE (AGT), ARE ASSOCIATED WITH PROGRESSIVE PULMONARY DECLINE AND NUTRITIONAL DETERIORATION. INSULIN IS THE MAINSTAY OF TREATMENT FOR CFRD AND IS KNOWN TO IMPROVE LONG-TERM CLINICAL OUTCOMES. HOWEVER NO THERAPIES, INCLUDING INSULIN, CURRENTLY EXIST TO IMPROVE CLINICAL OUTCOMES IN AGT, LIMIT BETA CELL DYSFUNCTION, OR HALT PROGRESSION FROM AGT TO CFRD. OXIDATIVE STRESS IS KNOWN TO CONTRIBUTE TO BOTH TYPE 1 (T1D) AND TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS (T2D). THIOREDOXIN- INTERACTING PROTEIN (TXNIP), A KEY REGULATOR OF OXIDATIVE STRESS, IS UPREGULATED IN HYPERGLYCEMIC STATES AND CONTRIBUTES TO BETA CELL APOPTOSIS AND IMPAIRED INSULIN SECRETION. VERAPAMIL, A WIDELY USED CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKER, DOWNREGULATES TXNIP AND HAS SHOWN PROMISE IN PRESERVING BETA CELL FUNCTION IN T1D AND T2D. EMERGING DATA IMPLICATES OXIDATIVE STRESS AS A CENTRAL COMPONENT OF CYSTIC FIBROSIS PATHOLOGY, INCLUDING WITHIN THE CF PANCREATIC ISLETS. OXIDATIVE STRESS IN PWCF IS LIKELY EXACERBATED BY CHRONIC INFLAMMATION, IMPAIRED ANTIOXIDANT DEFENSES, AND CFTR-RELATED CELLULAR DYSFUNCTION. THE EFFECTS OF VERAPAMIL ON BETA CELL FUNCTION AND DYSGLYCEMIA IN PEOPLE WITH CF-RELATED DYSGLYCEMIA ARE CURRENTLY UNKNOWN. WE PROPOSE A PILOT PRE/POST INTERVENTIONAL CLINICAL TRIAL TO ASSESS THE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF VERAPAMIL IN 30 ADOLESCENTS (>14 YEARS) AND ADULTS WITH CF AND AGT OR EARLY CFRD (NOT YET ON INSULIN). AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER VERAPAMIL (A) IMPROVES BETA CELL FUNCTION, MEASURED BY MIXED MEAL TOLERANCE TEST (MMTT)-STIMULATED C-PEPTIDE AREA UNDER THE CURVE (AUC), AND (B) REDUCES DYSGLYCEMIA, ASSESSED VIA CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITORING (CGM), OVER A 6-MONTH TREATMENT PERIOD. AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE THE SAFETY, TOLERABILITY, AND ADHERENCE TO VERAPAMIL IN THIS POPULATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT VERAPAMIL WILL IMPROVE BETA CELL FUNCTION AND GLYCEMIC CONTROL, WHILE DEMONSTRATING A FAVORABLE SAFETY PROFILE. THIS STUDY WILL ADDRESS A PRESSING UNMET NEED IN THE MANAGEMENT OF AGT AND EARLY CFRD AND PROVIDE FURTHER INSIGHT INTO THE MECHANISM OF CF-RELATED DYSGLYCEMIA. THIS PROPOSAL HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM THE MANAGEMENT OF AGT AND CFRD THROUGH A TARGETED, LOW RISK, LOW-COST INTERVENTION AIMED AT PRESERVING BETA CELL FUNCTION AND IMPROVING DYSGLYCEMIA, PROVIDING KEY PRELIMINARY DATA TO INFORM A LARGER PHASE 3 TRIAL IN THIS PATIENT POPULATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENHANCING KIDNEY CARE IN COMMUNITY HEALTH CENTERS (ENRICH) - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE AFFECTS OVER 35 MILLION PEOPLE IN THE UNITED STATES, COST MEDICARE OVER $130 BILLION ANNUALLY, AND CONTRIBUTES TO PREMATURE DEATH AND DISABILITY. NOTABLY, THE RISK OF KIDNEY FAILURE – MOST OFTEN FROM TREATABLE CONDITIONS SUCH AS DIABETES AND HYPERTENSION – IS CONCENTRATED AMONG INDIVIDUALS WHO ARE LOW- INCOME, UNDERINSURED, OR FROM RURAL OR UNDER-RESOURCED COMMUNITIES. DESPITE DECADES OF ELEVATED KIDNEY FAILURE RISK IN THESE POPULATIONS AND THE AVAILABILITY OF INTERVENTIONS TO PREVENT KIDNEY DISEASE PROGRESSION, HIGH RATES OF DISEASE PROGRESSION AND UNPLANNED DIALYSIS AND LOW RATES OF PRE-EMPTIVE KIDNEY TRANSPLANT PERSIST. PRIOR STUDIES OF NON-DIALYSIS DEPENDENT KIDNEY DISEASE HAVE LARGELY EXCLUDED POPULATIONS AT HIGHEST RISK FOR KIDNEY FAILURE BECAUSE THEY DO NOT ROUTINELY RECEIVE CARE AT URBAN, SPECIALIZED CENTERS. INSTEAD MANY OF THESE PATIENTS RELY ON COMMUNITY HEALTH CENTERS − A PATCHWORK OF FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS, RURAL HEALTH CLINICS, AND OTHER PROGRAMS THAT COLLECTIVELY CARE FOR OVER 30 MILLION PATIENTS ANNUALLY. TO DATE, THE ABSENCE OF LARGE-SCALE DATA FROM COMMUNITY HEALTH CENTERS HAS LEFT MANY HIGH-RISK, HIGH-NEEDS PATIENTS WITH KIDNEY DISEASE INVISIBLE TO HEALTH SYSTEMS, RESEARCHERS, AND POLICYMAKERS UNLESS THEY SURVIVE TO KIDNEY FAILURE, WHEN MOST WILL QUALIFY FOR MEDICARE’S $45 BILLION END-STAGE RENAL DISEASE PROGRAM. THIS PROPOSAL WILL LEVERAGE INNOVATIVE MIXED METHODS AND THE NATION’S LARGEST NETWORK OF COMMUNITY HEALTH CENTERS (OCHIN INC., 8+ MILLION PATIENTS, 2400+ CLINICS IN 43 STATES) TO IDENTIFY OPPORTUNITIES TO IMPROVE THE DELIVERY AND EFFICIENCY OF CARE TO PATIENTS WITH KIDNEY DISEASE. WE AIM TO: (1) DETERMINE THE HEALTH CENTER FACTORS AND SERVICES ASSOCIATED WITH THE HIGHEST IMPLEMENTATION OF GUIDELINE-BASED PRACTICE AND LOWEST RISK OF ADVERSE KIDNEY OUTCOMES IN NON-DIALYSIS DEPENDENT CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE; AND (2) IDENTIFY THE PATIENT, PROVIDER AND HEALTH CENTER PATHWAYS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO OUTCOMES OF NON-DIALYSIS DEPENDENT KIDNEY DISEASE IN COMMUNITY HEALTH SETTINGS. OUR WORK ALIGNS WITH THE HHS ADVANCING AMERICAN KIDNEY HEALTH INITIATIVE – TO REDUCE THE COSTLY BURDEN OF KIDNEY DISEASE. TOGETHER, THIS WORK WILL DELIVER IMMEDIATELY ACTIONABLE DATA TO ADVANCE KIDNEY CARE IN AMERICA’S COMMUNITY HEALTH CENTERS. OCHIN’S NATIONAL SCOPE AND INTEGRATED ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS NETWORK CAN FACILITATE RAPID CHANGES TO CLINICAL PRACTICE AND TEST STRATEGIES FOR ENHANCING KIDNEY CARE DELIVERY TO PATIENTS IN COMMUNITY HEALTH SETTINGS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH - OF THE COMMONWEALTH SYSTEM OF HIGHER EDUCATION

description: ECONSULTS TO OPTIMIZE CARE FOR CHILDREN WITH OBESITY - ABSTRACT OBESITY AFFECTS 1 IN 5 US CHILDREN, MANY OF WHOM HAVE COMORBIDITIES SUCH AS TYPE 2 DIABETES, STEATOTIC LIVER DISEASE, DYSLIPIDEMIA, HYPERTENSION, AND OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEA. CHILDREN WITH THESE COMORBIDITIES MAY REQUIRE SPECIALIZED CARE BY ENDOCRINOLOGISTS, GASTROENTEROLOGISTS, CARDIOLOGISTS, NEPHROLOGISTS, AND SLEEP MEDICINE SPECIALISTS. HOWEVER, THE DEMAND FOR PEDIATRIC SUBSPECIALISTS EXCEEDS SUPPLY, RESULTING IN SUBSTANTIAL DELAYS AND TRAVEL BARRIERS. DELAYED AND INCOMPLETE REFERRALS, EXPERIENCED DISPROPORTIONATELY BY CHILDREN INSURED BY MEDICAID, RESULT IN MISSED OPPORTUNITIES FOR SECONDARY PREVENTION AND DISEASE MANAGEMENT, NEGATIVELY IMPACTING LONG-TERM HEALTH. THIS INADEQUATE SUPPLY OF SUBSPECIALISTS IS PROJECTED TO WORSEN WITH FEWER PHYSICIANS ENTERING PEDIATRIC SUBSPECIALTY FELLOWSHIPS AND MORE DEMAND FOR SUBSPECIALTY CONSULTATION IN THE CONTEXT OF FDA-APPROVAL OF WEIGHT MANAGEMENT MEDICATIONS FOR CHILDREN WITH OBESITY. ONE EMERGING STRATEGY TO ENHANCE SUBSPECIALTY CARE RECEIPT IS THE ELECTRONIC CONSULTATION, OR ECONSULT, AN ASYNCHRONOUS CARE MODEL IN WHICH A REFERRING CLINICIAN DIRECTS A PATIENT-SPECIFIC CLINICAL QUESTION TO A SUBSPECIALIST WHO THEN PROVIDES WRITTEN RECOMMENDATIONS BACK TO THE REFERRING CLINICIAN. THE FEDERAL MEDICAID PROGRAM AUTHORIZED ECONSULT COVERAGE IN JANUARY 2023, AND 22 STATES AUTHORIZED ECONSULTS IN THE SUBSEQUENT 24 MONTHS. GIVEN CURRENT STATE-LEVEL VARIATION IN AUTHORIZATION AND USE, WE HAVE AN OPPORTUNITY TO ANSWER URGENT QUESTIONS ABOUT BEST PRACTICES IN ECONSULT USE FOR YOUTH WITH OBESITY. WITHOUT SUCH GUIDANCE, ECONSULTS HAVE THE POTENTIAL FOR INADEQUATE USE (BLUNTING IMPACT ON HEALTH) AND FOR SUPPLY-INDUCED OVERUSE (INCREASING UTILIZATION BUT NOT HEALTH). PAYERS, HEALTH SYSTEMS, AND CLINICIANS NEED EVIDENCE FOCUSED ON PEDIATRIC MEDICAID BENEFICIARIES DUE TO THE DISTINCT HEALTH CARE NEEDS OF CHILDREN, LIMITED ACCESS TO PEDIATRIC SUBSPECIALISTS, AND OUTSIZED ROLE OF MEDICAID IN FINANCING PEDIATRIC HEALTHCARE. THUS, THIS STUDY WILL ASSESS THE IMPACT OF MEDICAID AUTHORIZATION AND USE OF ECONSULTS ON CHILDREN WITH OBESITY. FIRST, WE WILL USE NATIONAL MEDICAID CLAIMS TO EXAMINE ECONSULTS USE AFTER STATE MEDICAID AUTHORIZATION AND ANY ASSOCIATED CHANGE IN USE OF SUBSPECIALTY CONSULTATIVE VISITS AMONG PEDIATRIC MEDICAID BENEFICIARIES WITH OBESITY (AIM 1). NEXT, WE WILL EXAMINE THE ASSOCIATION OF COUNTY-LEVEL VOLUME OF ECONSULTS ON HEALTHCARE USE AND OUTCOMES AMONG CHILDREN WITH OBESITY USING NATIONAL MEDICAID CLAIMS, IDENTIFYING DOWNSTREAM IMPACT OF ECONSULTS ON SCREENING, DIAGNOSIS, MANAGEMENT, HEALTH CARE UTILIZATION, AND DAYS OF HEALTH CARE CONTACT (AIM 2). FINALLY, WE WILL ASSESS CLINICIAN PERSPECTIVES ON THE USABILITY AND USEFULNESS OF ECONSULTS FOR THE CARE OF CHILDREN WITH OBESITY, GENERATING EVIDENCE TO MAXIMIZE BENEFIT AND MINIMIZE HARMS OF THIS NEW CARE MODALITY (AIM 3). OUR STUDY IS FEASIBLE AND RIGOROUS DUE TO OUR ROBUST ANALYTIC METHODS FOR CAUSAL INFERENCE AND QUALITATIVE INQUIRY. OUR STUDY IS IMPORTANT DUE TO THE NEED TO UNDERSTAND AN EMERGING CARE MODALITY AND THE OPPORTUNITY TO IMPROVE MANAGEMENT OF OBESITY AND OBESITY-RELATED COMORBIDITIES IN US CHILDREN TO PROMOTE LIFELONG HEALTH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ALTERATIONS TO ADIPOSE TISSUE REGULATION AND FUNCTION BY CART IN SIV-INFECTED RHESUS MACAQUES - ABSTRACT LONG-TERM COMBINATION ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (CART) HAS SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVED THE MANAGEMENT OF HIV, BUT IT COMES WITH COMPLICATIONS. OVER 75% OF CHRONIC HIV PATIENTS ON CART EXPERIENCE CLINICAL ISSUES, WITH A NOTABLE ONE BEING LIPODYSTROPHY, WHICH IS CHARACTERIZED BY ABNORMAL FAT REDISTRIBUTION AND METABOLISM. ADIPOSE TISSUE, COMPOSED OF FAT CELLS (ADIPOCYTES) AND THEIR PRECURSORS (ADIPOSE STEM CELLS OR ASCS), PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE IN THESE COMPLICATIONS. HIV AND CART CAN COMPROMISE THESE CELLS, LEADING TO ALTERED FAT DISTRIBUTION, INFLAMMATION, AND ACCELERATED AGING, OR “INFLAMMAGING”. THE VIRUS AND ITS PROTEINS INITIALLY EXPOSE THE ADIPOSE CELLS TO THE EFFECTS OF THE INFECTION. LATER, CART DRUGS ARE ALSO INTRODUCED, FURTHER AFFECTING THE CELLULAR PROCESSES. TOGETHER, THESE DECREASE THE MATURATION OF ASCS INTO FUNCTIONAL ADIPOCYTES, WHICH IN TURN DISRUPTS FAT METABOLISM. TO INVESTIGATE THIS, WE PROPOSE USING A RHESUS MACAQUE/SIV-INFECTION MODEL. THIS MODEL WILL ALLOW US TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT BOTH THE VIRUS AND ANTIRETROVIRAL DRUGS CONTRIBUTE TO ACCELERATED AGING AND ADIPOSE TISSUE DYSFUNCTION. WE WILL ASSESS THE EFFECTS OF INFECTION ALONE, CART ALONE, AND THEIR COMBINATION ON ADIPOCYTES AND ASCS. THIS STUDY IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE WE WILL LONGITUDINALLY ASSESS ASCS AND ADIPOCYTES FROM THE SAME ANIMALS BEFORE AND AFTER SIV INFECTION AND CART TREATMENT. WE WILL ALSO PERFORM REAL-TIME MEASUREMENTS OF ADIPOCYTE FUNCTION. WE WILL TRACK CHANGES IN FAT DISTRIBUTION USING CT IMAGING, ADVANCED DIGITAL IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY, AND FLOW CYTOMETRY OF BIOPSIES. THE MECHANISMS BEHIND THESE ALTERATIONS WILL BE DETERMINED BEFORE AND AFTER NECROPSY. OUR TEAM IS HIGHLY QUALIFIED TO PERFORM THIS RESEARCH, WITH EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN STUDYING ASCS AND ADIPOCYTES IN NON-HUMAN PRIMATES AND EXPERTISE IN LONGITUDINAL SAMPLING IN SIV-INFECTED MONKEYS. THE FINDINGS WILL PROVIDE CRUCIAL MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO ADIPOGENESIS, ADIPOCYTE FUNCTION, AND OBESITY IN THE CONTEXT OF LONG-TERM CART.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE ROLE OF MACROPHAGES IN STEATOTIC LIVER DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT MACROPHAGES PLAY CRITICAL ROLES IN THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF STEATOTIC LIVER DISEASE (SLD), CONTRIBUTING TO TISSUE DAMAGE THROUGH INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES THAT PROMOTE HEPATOTOXICITY, RECRUIT ADDITIONAL PRO-INFLAMMATORY IMMUNE CELLS, AND DRIVE PROGRESSION TO FIBROSIS. PARADOXICALLY, MACROPHAGES CAN ALSO PROMOTE DISEASE RESOLUTION THROUGH THEIR IMMUNOREGULATORY FUNCTIONS, SUCH AS CLEARANCE OF DEAD OR DYING CELLS, PRODUCTION OF ANTI-INFLAMMATORY MEDIATORS, AND DEGRADATION OF EXCESS EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX. UNDERSTANDING HOW MACROPHAGES BALANCE THESE OPPOSING BEHAVIORS IS ESSENTIAL FOR DEVELOPING TARGETED THERAPIES FOR SLD. A KEY FACTOR IS THE EXPANSION OF LIVER MACROPHAGE HETEROGENEITY—BOTH IN POPULATION AND PHENOTYPE—DRIVEN IN PART BY RECRUITMENT AND DIFFERENTIATION OF PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONOCYTES. THIS EXPANDING HETEROGENEITY CORRELATES WITH SLD PROGRESSION AND CLINICAL SEVERITY. WHILE BLOCKING MACROPHAGE EXPANSION HAS SHOWN BENEFIT IN SOME EXPERIMENTAL MODELS, IT HAS PROVEN DETRIMENTAL IN OTHERS AND FAILED TO MEET EFFICACY ENDPOINTS IN A RECENT PHASE III TRIAL. THESE FINDINGS SUGGEST THAT THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES MUST SELECTIVELY INHIBIT INFLAMMATORY MACROPHAGES WHILE HARNESSING IMMUNOREGULATORY SUBSETS. HOWEVER, WE LACK A FUNDAMENTAL UNDERSTANDING OF HOW SPECIFIC MACROPHAGE POPULATIONS CONTRIBUTE TO SLD PROGRESSION. THIS PROPOSAL WILL USE EXPERIMENTAL MODELS TO DEFINE POPULATION-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS FOR THE TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR ATF3 IN REPRESSING SLD PROGRESSION. GIVEN THE LARGE-SCALE TRANSCRIPTIONAL DIFFERENCES AMONG LIVER MACROPHAGE SUBSETS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT ATF3 REGULATES DISTINCT FUNCTIONS IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS. THIS HYPOTHESIS IS RELEVANT TO HUMAN HEALTH BECAUSE ATF3 EXPRESSION IN HUMAN LIVER BIOPSIES CORRELATES STRONGLY WITH SLD PROGRESSION TO STEATOHEPATITIS, AND ATF3 ACTIVITY IN GLOBAL MACROPHAGE POPULATIONS SUPPRESSES INFLAMMATION, ATHEROSCLEROSIS, AND SLD IN MURINE MODELS. HOWEVER, THE SUBSET-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS FOR TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS LIKE ATF3 REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THIS KNOWLEDGE IS CRITICAL, AS TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATORY MECHANISMS DIFFER ACROSS LIVER MACROPHAGE POPULATIONS AND DICTATE THEIR CONTRIBUTIONS TO SLD. SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL INVESTIGATE THE ROLES OF ATF3 IN KUPFFER CELLS VERSUS OTHER LIVER MACROPHAGE SUBSETS IN PROTECTING AGAINST EXPERIMENTAL SLD AND STEATOHEPATITIS. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL DEFINE CONTRASTING REQUIREMENTS FOR ATF3 IN KUPFFER CELLS AND/OR OTHER LIVER MACROPHAGE SUBSETS IN ASSEMBLING A MULTI-LAYERED TRANSCRIPTIONAL PLATFORM THAT GOVERNS IMMUNOREGULATORY AND INFLAMMATORY GENE EXPRESSION. THESE GOALS WILL BE AIDED BY COMBINATIONS OF ESTABLISHED CRE DRIVERS, AS WELL AS A NOVEL INDUCIBLE CRE STRAIN PERMITTING TARGETED GENE ACTIVATION WITH IMPROVED SUBSET SPECIFICITY. FILLING THESE KNOWLEDGE GAPS WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HUMAN HEALTH BY IDENTIFYING TRANSCRIPTIONAL PATHWAYS SPECIFIC TO SLD-RELEVANT MACROPHAGE POPULATIONS THAT MAY BE TARGETED TO PROMOTE BENEFICIAL BEHAVIORS AND LIMIT DETRIMENTAL ONES.

description: BIOFILM-HOST DEFENSE MECHANISM UNDERLYING DIABETIC WOUND CHRONICITY - ABSTRACT BIOFILM INFECTIONS, STRUCTURED COMMUNITIES OF BACTERIA THAT ADHERE TO SURFACES AND ARE ENCASED IN A SELF-PRODUCED EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX EMBEDDED IN HOST TISSUE, ARE AN EMERGING AND INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED THREAT TO HUMAN HEALTH. THEY ARE COMMONLY ASSOCIATED WITH MEDICAL DEVICES SUCH AS CATHETERS AND IMPLANTS, AND DISEASES LIKE CYSTIC FIBROSIS AND CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE (COPD). UNDERSTANDING THE COMPLEX BIOLOGY OF BIOFILMS, THEIR FORMATION, AND THEIR ROLE IN PERSISTENT INFECTIONS IS CRUCIAL FOR ADVANCING MEDICAL PRACTICES AND IMPROVING PATIENT OUTCOMES. NON-HEALING DIABETIC ULCERS ARE COMPLICATED BY BIOFILM INFECTION. THE IMBALANCE BETWEEN THE THREAT OF BFI AND HOST DEFENSES IN FAVOR OF THE FORMER MAY DETERMINE WOUND CHRONICITY. BFI DIRECTLY CONTRIBUTES TO CHRONIC INFLAMMATION IN A WIDE RANGE OF DISORDERS SUCH AS CYSTIC FIBROSIS, IMPLANTS ETC. IN DIABETIC WOUNDS, BFI AND CHRONIC INFLAMMATION CO-EXIST. HOWEVER, UNDERLYING MECHANISMS REMAIN UNCLEAR. MACROPHAGES (MPH) ARE CENTRAL PLAYERS IN WOUND HOST DEFENSE AND SUBSEQUENT HEALING. THIS PROPOSAL RESTS ON OUR NOVEL OBSERVATION USING SCRNASEQ AND SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS THAT MPH, EXPOSED TO BFI, ACQUIRE A UNIQUE PHENOTYPE AND ARE FUNCTIONALLY COMPROMISED IN A WAY THAT LIMIT THE HEALING PROCESS. PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT THIS UNIQUE BIOFILM RESPONSIVE MPH AKA MPH-BFR (MARCOHI/PLIN2HI) IS ABUNDANT IN HUMAN CHRONIC WOUNDS WITH BFI. WE PROPOSE TO TEST THE OVERALL HYPOTHESIS THAT IN DFU, BFI LEADS TO EMERGENCE OF A UNIQUE BIOFILM RESPONSIVE MPH-BFR THAT IS DYSFUNCTIONAL LEADING TO PERSISTENT INFECTION, INFLAMMATION AND POOR DFU HEALING OUTCOMES. THE FOLLOWING AIMS ARE PROPOSED: AIM 1: DETERMINE MECHANISMS OF STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (SA) BIOFILM INFECTION (BFI) IMPAIRMENT OF WOUND MACROPHAGE (MPH) EFFEROCYTOSIS THAT CAUSES CHRONIC INFLAMMATION AND IMPAIRED HEALING IN DIABETIC WOUNDS. AIM 2: TEST THE SIGNIFICANCE OF SA BIOFILM-INDUCED IMPAIRMENT OF LYSOSOMAL MATURATION, COMPROMISING MACROPHAGE BACTERIAL CLEARANCE, THUS ENABLING PERSISTENCE OF INTRACELLULAR BACTERIA WITH BIOFILM PHENOTYPE. AIM 3: STUDY IN DFU PATIENTS WHETHER THE PROPORTIONATE ABUNDANCE OF BIOFILM- RESPONSIVE: TOTAL MACROPHAGE (MPH-BFR: TOTAL MPH) IS HIGHER IN: (A) RESPONSE TO BIOFILM SEVERITY, AND (B) NON- HEALING OUTCOMES. UNDERSTANDING THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING BIOFILM-MEDIATED HOST DYSFUNCTIONS IN DFU IS CRUCIAL FOR EFFECTIVE MANAGEMENT AND TREATMENT STRATEGIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NOVEL MECHANISMS PROMOTING ENERGY INTAKE COMPENSATION IN RESPONSE TO AEROBIC AND RESISTANCE EXERCISE - PROJECT SUMMARY NOVEL MECHANISMS PROMOTING ENERGY INTAKE COMPENSATION IN RESPONSE TO AEROBIC AND RESISTANCE EXERCISE  OVER 70% OF AMERICANS ARE EITHER OVERWEIGHT OR OBESE, PUTTING THEM AT RISK FOR MANY CHRONIC DISEASES. DESPITE EXERCISE BEING A PREVALENT WEIGHT LOSS STRATEGY, WEIGHT LOSS FROM EXERCISING IS OFTEN SUBOPTIMAL. INDIVIDUALS COMPENSATE FOR A LARGE PORTION OF THE ENERGY EXPENDED DURING EXERCISE, THEREBY RESISTING MAINTENANCE OF THE NEGATIVE ENERGY BALANCE NEEDED FOR WEIGHT LOSS. INCREASES IN ENERGY INTAKE ARE OBSERVED WHEN EXERCISING FOR WEIGHT LOSS, ALTHOUGH THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS PROMOTING THESE RESPONSES HAVE YET TO BE FULLY ELUCIDATED. WITH OBESITY PREVALENCE CONTINUALLY RISING, AND THE LIMITED ACCESS TO PHARMACOLOGICAL TREATMENT MANY INDIVIDUALS FACE, INNOVATIVE RESEARCH IS NEEDED TO DEVELOP LIFESTYLE OBESITY TREATMENT STRATEGIES. RESEARCH HAS PRIMARILY FOCUSED ON AEROBIC EXERCISE, ALTHOUGH MORE RESEARCH IS RECENTLY DEMONSTRATING RESISTANCE EXERCISE CAN CONFER ADDITIONAL BENEFITS. FOR THIS REASON, CURRENT PHYSICAL ACTIVITY GUIDELINES RECOMMEND ENGAGING IN BOTH AEROBIC AND RESISTANCE EXERCISE TRAINING. PRIOR TRIALS COMPARING AEROBIC EXERCISE ALONE TO AEROBIC PLUS RESISTANCE EXERCISE TRAINING HAVE BEEN PROMISING, ALTHOUGH NO PRIOR TRIAL HAS MATCHED EXERCISE GROUPS ON EXERCISE ENERGY EXPENDITURE, THUS IT IS UNCERTAIN IF ADDITIONAL WEIGHT LOSS / FAT MASS LOSS BENEFITS FROM ADDING RESISTANCE EXERCISE TO AN AEROBIC EXERCISE INTERVENTION IS SOLELY FROM THE ADDED ENERGY EXPENDITURE OF THE AEROBIC PLUS RESISTANCE GROUP. THE IMMEDIATE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DETERMINE WEIGHT LOSS AND BODY COMPOSITION OUTCOMES IN AN AEROBIC VS. AEROBIC PLUS RESISTANCE EXERCISE TRAINING INTERVENTION WHERE GROUPS ARE MATCHED ON EXERCISE ENERGY EXPENDITURE. WE ARE ALSO INTERESTED IN ELUCIDATING MECHANISMS DRIVING EXERCISE-INDUCED INCREASE IN ENERGY INTAKE BETWEEN THESE TWO GROUPS. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO UNDERSTAND HOW LIFESTYLE OBESITY TREATMENT METHODS (SUCH AS EXERCISE) CAN BE BETTER USED TO REDUCE INCIDENCE OF OBESITY AND IMPROVE CHRONIC DISEASE OUTCOMES.  THE CURRENT PROPOSAL WILL RANDOMIZE PHYSICALLY INACTIVE ADULTS (BMI: 30-40 KG/M2) TO EITHER A 24-WEEK AEROBIC EXERCISE INTERVENTION OR AEROBIC PLUS RESISTANCE EXERCISE INTERVENTION WITH BOTH GROUPS PROGRESSING TO A WEEKLY EXERCISE ENERGY EXPENDITURE OF 1600 KCAL (4 DAYS PER WEEK). BODY COMPOSITION WILL BE ASSESSED VIA DXA WHILE ENERGY EXPENDITURE AND ENERGY INTAKE WILL BE ASSESSED VIA THE DOUBLY LABELED WATER METHOD. ASSESSMENTS OF UNDERLYING PHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS CONTRIBUTING TO ENERGY INTAKE (HORMONAL MEDIATORS OF APPETITE) IN ADDITION TO NOVEL BEHAVIORAL MECHANISMS (ATTENTIONAL BIAS TOWARDS FOOD CUES, FOOD REINFORCEMENT) WILL BE PERFORMED. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS FOR THE PRESENT TRIAL IS THAT ADDING RESISTANCE EXERCISE TO AN AEROBIC EXERCISE INTERVENTION WILL ATTENUATE INCREASES IN FOOD REINFORCEMENT, CAUSING LESS ENERGY INTAKE COMPENSATION TO PROMOTE DECREASES IN FAT MASS AND IMPROVE CARDIOMETABOLIC HEALTH. THIS CONTRIBUTION IS SIGNIFICANT, AS A GREATER UNDERSTANDING OF THE PHYSIOLOGY DRIVING COMPENSATORY RESPONSES TO EXERCISE IS THE FIRST STEP TOWARDS IMPROVING THE EFFICACY OF EXERCISE FOR WEIGHT CONTROL AND CHRONIC DISEASE MANAGEMENT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ROLE OF ALPHA-BETA CELL COMMUNICATION IN THE FUNCTIONAL HETEROGENEITY OF BETA CELLS IN HEALTH AND T2D - VIRA KRAVETS, PHD R01 ABSTRACT  TYPE 2 DIABETES (T2D) IS MARKED BY PROGRESSIVE BETA CELL DYSFUNCTION, BUT EMERGING EVIDENCE INDICATES THIS FAILURE IS NOT UNIFORM. OUR GROUP AND OTHERS HAVE IDENTIFIED FUNCTIONALLY DISTINCT BETA CELL SUBPOPULATIONS—“FIRST RESPONDERS” AND “LEADERS”—THAT INITIATE AND COORDINATE THE ISLET’S BIPHASIC INSULIN RESPONSE. THESE CELLS CONTRIBUTE DISPROPORTIONATELY TO INSULIN SECRETION AND PLAY ESSENTIAL ROLES IN ISLET COORDINATION. YET, THE MECHANISMS GOVERNING THEIR EMERGENCE REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD.  THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THREE MAJOR KNOWLEDGE GAPS: - THE ROLE OF ALPHA-CELL–MEDIATED GLP-1 RECEPTOR (GLP-1R) SIGNALING IN SHAPING BETA CELL HETEROGENEITY, - THE EFFECT OF BETA CELL PROXIMITY TO ALPHA CELLS ON LOCAL GENE EXPRESSION, AND - THE SELECTIVE VULNERABILITY OF THESE SUBPOPULATIONS TO T2D.  WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT ALPHA-TO-BETA PARACRINE SIGNALING—PRIMARILY VIA GLP-1 AND GLUCAGON— CREATES SPATIAL MICROENVIRONMENTS THAT REPROGRAM NEIGHBORING BETA CELLS BOTH METABOLICALLY AND TRANSCRIPTIONALLY, PREDISPOSING THEM TO DYSFUNCTION IN T2D.  AIM 1 WILL QUANTIFY HOW GLP-1R AND DOWNSTREAM PKA SIGNALING CONTRIBUTE TO BETA CELL HETEROGENEITY. WE WILL USE OPTICAL CA²⁺ IMAGING, PHASOR-FLIM NAD(P)H READOUTS, AND PKA SENSORS IN LIVE HUMAN AND MOUSE PANCREATIC SLICES TO EVALUATE HOW ALPHA-CELL SECRETIONS DRIVE DIFFERENTIAL BETA CELL ACTIVATION. PHARMACOLOGICAL BLOCKADE AND TRANSGENIC MODELS WILL TEST THE ROLES OF GLP-1R AND GLUCAGON RECEPTOR SIGNALING. IN-SILICO MODELING WILL COMPLEMENT EXPERIMENTAL DATA.  AIM 2 WILL DEFINE THE ROLE OF ALPHA CELLS IN SHAPING BETA CELL SUBPOPULATIONS THAT ARE PREFERENTIALLY VULNERABLE IN T2D. WE WILL COMBINE FUNCTIONAL IMAGING WITH SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS IN PANCREATIC SLICES FROM NON-DIABETIC (ND) AND T2D DONORS. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW ENHANCED OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION, INSULIN/IAPP EXPRESSION, AND GLUCOSE RESPONSIVENESS IN ALPHA-PROXIMAL BETA CELLS. WE ALSO FOUND GREATER DYSFUNCTION IN T2D DONOR TISSUE AND IN ISLETS WITH HIGHER ALPHA-CELL CONTENT.  OUR INTEGRATED APPROACH—MERGING LIVE FUNCTIONAL IMAGING, SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS, AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING—WILL CLARIFY HOW PARACRINE SIGNALING AND SPATIAL ISLET ARCHITECTURE SHAPE BETA CELL HETEROGENEITY. BY IDENTIFYING SUBPOPULATION-SPECIFIC FAILURE PATTERNS IN T2D, THIS WORK WILL MOVE THE FIELD BEYOND THE CURRENT VIEW OF BETA CELL FAILURE AS UNIFORM OR STOCHASTIC. IMPACT: THIS RESEARCH MAY REVEAL EARLY BIOMARKERS OF ISLET DYSFUNCTION, OPTIMIZE GLP-1R–BASED THERAPIES, AND INFORM THE DESIGN OF STEM-CELL–DERIVED ISLETS WITH IMPROVED RESILIENCE FOR TRANSPLANTATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GLIAL NEURONAL CROSSTALK IN NEUROPATHIC PAIN AND DIABETES - NEUROPATHIC PAIN IS A CHRONIC, DEBILITATING CONDITION THAT AFFECTS MILLIONS OF AMERICANS AND REMAINS CHALLENGING TO TREAT DUE TO LIMITED THERAPEUTIC OPTIONS. EMERGING RESEARCH IMPLICATES GLIAL CELLS INCLUDING MICROGLIA, ASTROCYTES, AND SATELLITE GLIAL CELLS (SGCS) AS CRITICAL PLAYERS IN NEUROPATHIC PAIN PATHOGENESIS AND RESOLUTION. SGCS, WHICH TIGHTLY SURROUND SENSORY NEURONS IN THE DORSAL ROOT GANGLIA (DRG), BECOME REACTIVE UNDER NEUROPATHIC PAIN CONDITIONS SUCH AS NERVE INJURY, CHEMOTHERAPY-INDUCED PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY (CIPN), AND DIABETIC NEUROPATHY (DPN). THESE GLIAL-NEURONAL INTERACTIONS INFLUENCE BOTH PAIN SENSITIVITY AND NEURONAL RECOVERY. MITOCHONDRIA ARE THE POWERHOUSE OF THE CELL DUE TO THEIR CRUCIAL ROLE IN ENERGY PRODUCTION. MITOCHONDRIAL DYSREGULATION AND LIPID OXIDATIVE STRESS HAVE BEEN IMPLICATED IN NEURODEGENERATION, CELL DEATH (E.G., FERROPTOSIS), AND NEUROPATHIC PAIN. THE LONG AXONS OF PRIMARY SENSORY NEURONS FACE EXCEPTIONAL CHALLENGES IN MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSPORT AND DELIVERY. HOW SENSORY NEURONS SUSTAIN MITOCHONDRIAL HOMEOSTASIS IS UNCLEAR. ACCUMULATING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT MITOCHONDRIA CAN BE TRANSFERRED BETWEEN CELLS. THE GOAL OF THIS STUDY IS TO INVESTIGATE HOW MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSFER FROM SATELLITE GLIAL CELLS TO SENSORY NEURONS PROTECTS AGAINST NEUROPATHIC PAIN AND HOW DYSFUNCTION OF THIS PROCESS CONTRIBUTES TO DIABETIC PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY IN MOUSE AND HUMAN DISEASE MODELS. OUR GOAL WILL BE ACHIEVED BY ACCOMPLISHING THE FOLLOWING TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 WILL EXAMINE THE ROLE OF SGC-NEURON MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSFER IN HEALTH AND NEUROPATHIC PAIN AFTER NERVE INJURY AND DIABETES IN MICE. AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSFER FROM SATELLITE GLIAL CELLS TO SENSORY NEURONS IN HUMAN DRG IN HEALTH AND DIABETES. WE WILL EMPLOY HIGH-RESOLUTION SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS TO DELINEATE GENE REGULATORY NETWORKS IN HUMAN DRG NEURONS AND GLIAL CELLS AND TO IDENTIFY DYSREGULATED PATHWAYS ASSOCIATED WITH DIABETIC NEUROPATHY. WE PROPOSE A MULTI-DISCIPLINARY APPROACH THAT COMBINES SCANNING AND TRANSMISSION ELECTRON MICROSCOPY, CALCIUM IMAGING, ADOPTIVE TRANSFER OF GLIAL CELLS AND MITOCHONDRIA, AND MEASUREMENTS OF EVOKED AND SPONTANEOUS PAIN. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL YIELD NOVEL MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO NEUROGLIAL INTERACTIONS IN NEUROPATHIC PAIN AND IDENTIFY POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR NEUROPATHIC PAIN AND DIABETIC NEUROPATHY.

description: UNEVEN GEOGRAPHIC DISTRIBUTION OF DIALYSIS FACILITY EXPANSION AND ITS DIFFERENTIAL IMPACT ON HEALTH OUTCOMES AMONG PATIENTS WITH END-STAGE KIDNEY DISEASE - DIALYSIS IS ONE OF THE MOST FREQUENTLY USED OUTPATIENT SERVICES IN MEDICINE. BECAUSE TREATMENT GENERALLY INVOLVES MULTIPLE WEEKLY SESSIONS, THE PROXIMITY OF DIALYSIS FACILITIES TO THE PATIENTS WHO RELY ON THEM IS CRITICALLY IMPORTANT. THE TOTAL NUMBER OF DIALYSIS CENTERS HAS INCREASED BY 70% OVER THE LAST 20 YEARS. IN ADDITION, THERE HAVE BEEN RECENT IMPROVEMENTS IN DIALYSIS TECHNOLOGY AND CARE PROTOCOLS THAT CAN SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE CLINICAL OUTCOMES, THOUGH NOT ALL FACILITIES OFFER THESE SERVICES. HOWEVER, IT IS UNKNOWN WHETHER THE BENEFITS OF DIALYSIS CENTER MARKET EXPANSION AND/OR TECHNOLOGICAL ADVANCEMENTS HAVE BEEN EVENLY DISTRIBUTED ACROSS ALL COMMUNITIES. INDEED, MAJOR DIFFERENCES PERSIST IN WHERE AND HOW DIALYSIS IS DELIVERED, PARTICULARLY FOR BLACK, HISPANIC, MEDICAID-ELIGIBLE, AND RURAL POPULATIONS. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH CHANGES IN DIALYSIS INFRASTRUCTURE INFLUENCE DISPARITIES IN ESKD TREATMENT AND OUTCOMES. TOWARDS THIS END, THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DETERMINE HOW THE BENEFITS OF DIALYSIS MARKET EXPANSION ARE EXPERIENCED ACROSS AND WITHIN COMMUNITIES.  USING DIALYSIS FACILITY EXPANSION AS AN IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY AND 10 YEARS OF NATIONAL MEDICARE CLAIMS LINKED WITH FACILITY- AND COMMUNITY-LEVEL DATA, THIS STUDY WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT RECENT GROWTH IN OUTPATIENT DIALYSIS FACILITIES HAS: (AIM 1) UNEVENLY INCREASED DIALYSIS CAPACITY ACROSS COMMUNITIES DEFINED BY SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS AND RURALITY; (AIM 2) PRODUCED UNEVEN BENEFITS ACROSS COMMUNITIES, WHEREBY PATIENTS IN HIGHER-RESOURCED AREAS EXPERIENCE GREATER IMPROVEMENTS IN ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY FACILITIES AND HEALTH OUTCOMES; AND (AIM 3) WIDENED DIFFERENCES WITHIN COMMUNITIES, AS FACILITY OPENINGS MAY BENEFIT SOME PATIENTS MORE THAN OTHERS EVEN WHEN LIVING IN THE SAME ZIP CODE. OUR LONGITUDINAL, POPULATION-BASED APPROACH IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT WILL CAPTURE HOW CHANGES IN DIALYSIS INFRASTRUCTURE INFLUENCE ACCESS AND OUTCOMES OVER TIME, WILL INCLUDE BOTH TRADITIONAL MEDICARE AND MEDICARE ADVANTAGE BENEFICIARIES, AND WILL EVALUATE ACCESS BASED ON REAL-WORLD, CARE-SEEKING BEHAVIOR RATHER THAN STATIC FACILITY CATCHMENT AREAS.   THIS RESEARCH WILL GENERATE A FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND, NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE, LONGITUDINAL DATABASE OF DIALYSIS FACILITY OPENINGS AND CLOSURES, QUALITY SHIFTS, AND ESKD PATIENT CLINICAL OUTCOMES. BY LINKING THESE DATA TO DEMOGRAPHIC AND GEOGRAPHIC COMMUNITY CHARACTERISTICS, WE OFFER A NOVEL FRAMEWORK FOR IDENTIFYING ACTIONABLE DISPARITIES IN ESKD CARE. THESE FINDINGS WILL IDENTIFY SPECIFIC COMMUNITIES IN WHICH ADDITIONAL INTERVENTIONS (E.G., SUBSIDIZED TRANSPORT TO HIGH-QUALITY FACILITIES, REGULATORY INCENTIVES TO ENCOURAGE FACILITY OPENINGS IN HIGH-ADI AREAS) COULD YIELD THE GREATEST BENEFITS FOR ALL PATIENTS, THUS ADVANCING NIDDK’S MISSION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EFFECT OF STATE-WIDE CENTRALIZED PATIENT COACHING ABOUT LIVE DONOR KIDNEY TRANSPLANTATION - LIVE DONOR KIDNEY TRANSPLANTATION (LDKT) DOUBLES EXPECTED GRAFT SURVIVAL FOR RECIPIENTS COMPARED WITH DECEASED DONOR TRANSPLANTATION. LIVE DONOR CHAMPION (LDC) IS A PROGRAM WE DESIGNED TO EDUCATE END-STAGE KIDNEY DISEASE (ESKD) PATIENTS, THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND THEIR SOCIAL NETWORKS ABOUT THE BENEFITS OF KIDNEY TRANSPLANTATION (KT) AND LIVING DONATION. WE CREATED LDC TO INCREASE ACCESS TO LDKT. POST-LDC VERSUS PRE-LDC, PARTICIPANTS INCREASED KNOWLEDGE (83% VS 63% ON 12-QUESTION QUIZ; P < 0.001) AND COMFORT (1.8 VS 1 ON 4-POINT LIKERT SCALE; P < 0.001). KT CANDIDATES WHO PARTICIPATED IN THE LDC PROGRAM WERE ALMOST 5.8 TIMES AS LIKELY AS MATCHED CONTROLS TO HAVE A DONOR REFERRAL.  IN OUR HRSA-FUNDED IMPLEMENTATION STUDY OF LDC, TWO MAIN THEMES EMERGED: (1) LIMITED STAFF CAPACITY AND TIME, AND (2) TRANSPORTATION AND SCHEDULING BARRIERS TO PARTICIPATION. CENTERS NOTED THAT SESSIONS WERE TIME-INTENSIVE, OFTEN REQUIRED WORK OUTSIDE REGULAR HOURS, AND DEMANDED ADDITIONAL OR DEDICATED STAFF. THEY ALSO REPORTED THAT TRANSPORTATION CHALLENGES, SESSION LENGTH, NUMBER OF MEETINGS, AND WEEKEND DELIVERY DISCOURAGED SOME CANDIDATES AND THEIR CHAMPIONS FROM PARTICIPATING. THE LDC INTERVENTION HAS NOW BEEN SUCCESSFULLY ADAPTED TO A VIRTUAL FORMAT AND TRANSFORMED INTO A PATIENT COACHING PROGRAM DELIVERED BY NON-TRANSPLANT PROFESSIONALS IN COMMUNITY HEALTH SETTINGS (R01DK125509).   NEW YORK STATE PROVIDES AN IDEAL SETTING TO EXAMINE STRATEGIES FOR ENSURING THAT EVERY TRANSPLANT CENTER HAS ACCESS—WHETHER SERVING RURAL OR URBAN POPULATIONS. THE NEW YORK CENTER FOR KIDNEY TRANSPLANTATION (NYKIDNEY) PARTNERS WITH 12 TRANSPLANT PROGRAMS TO SUPPORT EDUCATION INITIATIVES THAT ADVANCE TRANSPLANT ACCESS AND OUTCOMES BY MAKING EDUCATION ACCESSIBLE TO ALL.   THIS STUDY AIMS TO ADAPT THE LDC PROGRAM FOR VIRTUAL DELIVERY BY NYKIDNEY, EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF LDC PROGRAM DELIVERED BY NYKIDNEY, AND CONDUCT A MIXED-METHODS ASSESSMENT OF IMPLEMENTATION OF THE ADAPTED LDC PROGRAM DELIVERED BY NYKIDNEY. FOR TRANSPLANT CENTERS AND TRANSPLANT ORGANIZATIONS, THIS EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION TRIAL WILL GUIDE EXPANSION AND SUSTAINABILITY DECISIONS AND SUPPORT GREATER ACCESS TO LDKT.
