description: MECHANICAL MEMORY OF CONFINED MIGRATION - ABSTRACT: WHILE METABOLISM HAS BEEN RECENTLY THERAPEUTICALLY TARGETED AS A MECHANISM TO CONTROL PROLIFERATION, WE NOW KNOW THAT METABOLISM ALSO PLAYS AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN CELL MIGRATION. OUR RECENT WORK HAS SHOWN THAT THE ENERGETIC STATE OF A CELL MEDIATES ITS ABILITY TO MIGRATE, ITS VELOCITY, THE PATH IT WILL TAKE, AND THE MODE OF MIGRATION IT WILL EMPLOY. INTERESTINGLY, OUR RECENT WORK IDENTIFIED FOR THE FIRST TIME THAT MIGRATION THROUGH CONFINED SPACES PRIMES CELLS TO MIGRATE FASTER AND INCREASE CELLULAR ATP LEVELS, BEHAVIORS THAT ARE MAINTAINED EVEN AFTER CELLS HAVE LEFT CONFINEMENT. TO OUR KNOWLEDGE, THIS IS THE FIRST EVIDENCE OF CELLULAR MEMORY IN RESPONSE TO CONFINEMENT. HERE, WE PROPOSE TO STUDY THE CONNECTION BETWEEN CONFINEMENT, MIGRATION, AND CELLULAR ENERGETICS WITH A FOCUS ON THE EFFECTS OF CONFINEMENT ON THE MECHANICAL MEMORY OF A CELL. USING A MICROFABRICATED PLATFORM TO CONTROL CELL MIGRATION PATH AND CONFINEMENT, SINGLE CELL BIOSENSORS OF METABOLIC ACTIVITY, MOLECULAR CONSTRUCTS TO TUNE CELL-MATRIX ADHESION, AND ORGANOID MODELS OF WOUND HEALING, WE WILL EXAMINE HOW CELLS DEVELOP METABOLIC AND MIGRATION MEMORY IN CONFINEMENT AND WE WILL DESCRIBE THE GOVERNING PARAMETERS OF BIOMATERIAL ARCHITECTURE WHICH HARNESS THIS RELATIONSHIP TO DRIVE MIGRATION. IN AIM 1, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE MECHANISM BY WHICH CONFINEMENT CONFERS MIGRATION AND METABOLIC MEMORY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DEFINE THE BIOMATERIAL PARAMETER SPACE THAT PRIMES CELLS FOR MIGRATION, AND WE ASSAY CELL MIGRATION POST-PRIMING IN VITRO, EX VIVO, AND IN VIVO INCLUDING IN A HUMAN SKIN WOUND HEALING MODEL. IN AIM 3, WE WILL TAKE AN ORTHOGONAL APPROACH TO STUDYING THE CONNECTION BETWEEN METABOLISM AND MIGRATION BY SORTING FOR THE MOST ENERGETIC CELLS, DISRUPTING METABOLISM USING PHARMACOLOGICAL AGENTS, AND TESTING FOR MIGRATION ABILITY. TUNING MIGRATION AND TESTING FOR ENERGY WHILE SEPARATELY TUNING ENERGY AND TESTING FOR MIGRATION WILL ENABLE US TO DETERMINE COMMON DRIVERS OF EACH AND DETERMINANTS OF CELL PRIMING FOR MIGRATION. THE OUTCOME OF THIS WORK IS THE IDENTIFICATION OF A NOVEL MECHANISM, THAT WE HAVE CALLED MECHANOMETABOLIC MEMORY, BY WHICH BIOMATERIAL ARCHITECTURE PRIMES CELLS FOR MIGRATION.

description: APICAL JUNCTION FLUIDITY CONTROL DURING EPITHELIAL MORPHOGENESIS - ABSTRACT TISSUE FLUIDITY IS THE ABILITY OF EPITHELIA TO DEFORM IN RESPONSE TO CUES IN THE ENVIRONMENT. THE EPITHELIUM IS INITIALLY FLAT. RESPONDING TO CUES SUCH AS MECHANICAL FORCE, EPITHELIAL CELLS CHANGE SHAPES AND EXCHANGE NEIGHBORS, FOLDING THE EPITHELIA INTO 3D STRUCTURES, SUCH AS A TUBE. DYNAMIC REMODELING OF APICAL CELL‒CELL JUNCTIONS IS ESSENTIAL FOR TISSUE DEFORMATION. IMPORTANTLY, TISSUE FLUIDITY VARIES AMONG EPITHELIA. FOR EXAMPLE, ANTEROPOSTERIOR (AP) ELONGATION OF EMBRYOS GENERATES AN AP-ORIENTED TENSILE FORCE, PULLING THE NEUROECTODERM AND THE ADJACENT FUTURE EPIDERMIS ALONG THE AP AXIS. IN THE NEUROECTODERM, JUNCTIONS REMODEL FLEXIBLY, ELONGATING AND FOLDING THE NEUROECTODERM INTO THE NEURAL TUBE, WHEREAS THE ADJACENT ECTODERM IS MORE SOLID-LIKE AND REMAINS FLAT. TO REMODEL JUNCTIONS IN RESPONSE TO MECHANICAL CUES, CELLS FIRST SENSE THE FORCE, TRANSDUCING THE FORCE SIGNAL TO THE MACHINERY OF JUNCTION REMODELING AND ACTOMYOSIN REORGANIZATION. THUS, CELLS IN FLUID-LIKE EPITHELIA MAY REQUIRE ACTIVATING THE MACHINERY OF JUNCTION REMODELING AND ACTOMYOSIN MORE EFFICIENTLY THAN CELLS IN SOLID-LIKE EPITHELIA. THE MECHANISMS OF JUNCTION REMODELING HAVE BEEN STUDIED. MECHANOSENSITIVE JUNCTION REMODELING HAS BEEN REPORTED. HOWEVER, WHAT CONTROLS THE SENSITIVITY OF EPITHELIA TO MECHANICAL CUES TO FLEXIBLY REMODEL JUNCTIONS REMAINS UNDERSTUDIED. MOREOVER, MANY EPITHELIAL DEFORMATIONS ARE DIRECTIONAL, WHICH REQUIRES ANISOTROPIC FORCE GENERATION AND JUNCTION REMODELING. HOWEVER, THE UNDERLYING MECHANISM IS NOT WELL UNDERSTOOD. THIS STUDY INVESTIGATES THE ROLE OF PRICKLE 2 (PK2), A CORE COMPONENT OF THE PLANAR CELL POLARITY (PCP) PATHWAY, IN CONTROLLING THE FLEXIBILITY AND DIRECTIONALITY OF JUNCTIONAL REMODELING. WE RECENTLY REPORTED THAT PK2 IS REQUIRED FOR FLEXIBLE JUNCTION REMODELING IN THE NEUROECTODERM DURING NEURAL TUBE CLOSURE IN XENOPUS EMBRYOS. CONVERSELY, PK2 OVEREXPRESSION INCREASED TISSUE FLUIDITY BY ACCELERATING JUNCTION ELONGATION AND SHRINKAGE IN THE GASTRULA ECTODERM. THE TISSUE FLUIDIZING ACTIVITY OF PK2 REQUIRED VANGL2 BINDING, THE EVOLUTIONALLY CONSERVED SER-THR RICH REGION, AND RAC1 ACTIVATION. NOTABLY, PK2-MEDIATED JUNCTION REMODELING WAS DIRECTIONAL, AND THE DIRECTIONALITY WAS ALIGNED WITH THE ORIENTATION OF THE PULLING FORCE IN THE NEUROECTODERM. OUR HYPOTHESIS IS THAT PK2 INCREASES THE SENSITIVITY OF JUNCTIONS TO MECHANICAL FORCE, SO THAT JUNCTIONS WITH PK2 FLEXIBLY REMODEL IN RESPONSE TO FORCE, INCREASING TISSUE FLUIDITY FOR DEFORMATION. IN AIM 1, WE WILL EXPLORE THE DOWNSTREAM EFFECTORS OF PK2-RAC1 TO PROMOTE JUNCTION REMODELING. IN AIM 2, WE WILL EXPLORE THE UPSTREAM REGULATORS OF PK2 TO PROMOTE DIRECTIONAL JUNCTION REMODELING, INCLUDING THE ROLE OF MECHANICAL FORCE IN CONTROLLING PK2 ACTIVITY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMMUNOMODULATORY NANOFIBROUS MODULAR AEROGELS FOR CHRONIC WOUND HEALING - PROJECT SUMMARY CHRONIC WOUNDS (CWS) AFFECT ~6.5 MILLION AMERICANS AND COST THE U.S. HEALTHCARE SYSTEM OVER ~$25 BILLION ANNUALLY. UNLIKE ACUTE WOUNDS, CWS SUCH AS DIABETIC, VENOUS, AND PRESSURE ULCERS, ARE CHARACTERIZED BY A PROLONGED INFLAMMATORY PHASE DUE TO AN OVERABUNDANCE OF M1 MACROPHAGE ACTIVATION AND ELEVATED PRO- INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES, LEADING TO POOR HEALING OUTCOMES. THERE IS A PRESSING NEED FOR EFFECTIVE PROGRAMMING OF MACROPHAGES FROM THE M1 (PRO-INFLAMMATORY) TO M2 (PRO-HEALING) PHENOTYPE TO SHORTEN THE INFLAMMATION PHASE AND ACCELERATE HEALING IN CWS. OUR TEAM’S RECENT STUDIES HAVE SHOWN THAT THE PROTEOGLYCAN-4 (PRG-4) PROTEIN CAN MODULATE MACROPHAGE POLARIZATION; HOWEVER, ITS LARGE MOLECULAR WEIGHT (~460 KDA) LIMITS ITS WOUND PENETRATION, STABILITY, AND THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT PRG-4-DERIVED PEPTIDES (C-TERMINAL PRG4 MOTIFS) POSSESS IMPROVED STABILITY AND BIOACTIVITY FOR IMMUNOMODULATION FROM M1 TO M2 OVER PRG-4 PROTEIN. IN ADDITION, A LACK OF OXYGEN CAN CAUSE PROLONGED HYPOXIA, AFFECTING CWS AND STALLING THE MACROPHAGE POLARIZATION FROM M1 TO M2. GENERALLY, HYPERBARIC OXYGEN THERAPY (HBOT) HAS BEEN USED TO TREAT CWS TO AVOID HYPOXIA, SYSTEMIC OXYGEN TOXICITY, AND POOR CONTROL OVER OXYGEN RELEASE, WHICH REMAIN SIGNIFICANT LIMITATIONS OF HBOT TREATMENTS. TO ADDRESS THIS, WE HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED A NEXT-GENERATION OXYGEN- GENERATING SYSTEM (OGS) COMPOSED OF ZEIN/CALCIUM PEROXIDE(CAO₂)/CERIUM OXIDE (CEO₂) THAT ENABLES CONTROLLED, SUSTAINED OXYGEN RELEASE FOR OVER ONE MONTH. FURTHERMORE, CURRENT WOUND DRESSINGS OFTEN LACK THE NECESSARY POROSITY FOR EFFECTIVE GRANULATION AND CELL MIGRATION, WHICH CAN ACCELERATE HEALING. OUR NEWLY ENGINEERED POROUS NANOFIBROUS MICROSPHERES (NMS) HAVE SHOWN >80% GRANULATION TISSUE FORMATION IN A MURINE MODEL WITHIN 14 DAYS. INSPIRED BY THIS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT A MULTIMODAL APPROACH COMBINING EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX-MIMICKING POROUS NMS, SUSTAINED OXYGENATION OVER ONE MONTH, AND A PRG-4 PEPTIDE-DRIVEN IMMUNOMODULATION STRATEGY CAN SYNERGISTICALLY ENHANCE MACROPHAGE PROGRAMMING FROM M1 TO M2, THEREBY SHORTENING INFLAMMATION, CELL MIGRATION, VASCULARIZATION, AND RE-EPITHELIZATION IN CWS WITHIN ONE MONTH. THE PROPOSED WORK WILL BE EXECUTED WITH THE FOLLOWING AIMS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL ENGINEER NMS-LADEN MODULAR AEROGELS (NLMA) USING POROUS NMS EMBEDDED IN PHOTO-CROSSLINKED GELMA THROUGH SIMPLE FREEZE CASTING, RESULTING IN TUNABLE POROSITY AND DEGRADATION PROFILES. IN AIM 2, WE WILL INCORPORATE OGS AND PRG-4 PEPTIDE INTO NLMA AND EVALUATE THE CAPABILITY OF MACROPHAGE POLARIZATION (M1 TO M2) AND CELL COMPATIBILITY UNDER VARYING OXYGEN AND PRG-4 PEPTIDE CONCENTRATIONS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL ASSESS THE IN VIVO EFFICACY OF IMMUNOMODULATORY NLMA IN A MURINE CW MODEL BY ANALYZING INFLAMMATION, GRANULATION, ANGIOGENESIS, AND REEPITHELIALIZATION. THIS STUDY AIMS TO ESTABLISH A NEXT-GENERATION, IMMUNOMODULATORY WOUND DRESSING PLATFORM THAT OVERCOME CRITICAL CHALLENGES IN CW HEALING BY RESOLVING INFLAMMATION, SUSTAINING OXYGENATION, PROMOTING ANGIOGENESIS, AND FACILITATING CELL MIGRATION TO ACCELERATE TISSUE REGENERATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: COMPREHENSIVE CHARACTERIZATION OF CRISPR-CAS BINDING FOR OPTIMAL EPIGENOME EDITING - ABSTRACT CRISPR-BASED EPIGENOME EDITING, WHICH USES CATALYTICALLY INACTIVE CAS (DCAS) PROTEINS TO TARGET GENE REGULATORY REGIONS AND MODULATE GENE EXPRESSION, HOLDS GREAT PROMISE FOR BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH AND NEW THERAPEUTICS. HOWEVER, CRISPR EPIGENOME EDITING HAS MAJOR CHALLENGES WITH VARIABILITY OF TARGET SITE ACTIVITY AND OFF-TARGET BINDING, WHICH DIFFERS SUBSTANTIALLY FROM GENOME EDITING. WE AND OTHERS HAVE DEVELOPED HIGH-THROUGHPUT CRISPR EPIGENOME EDITING FOR SILENCING (CRISPRI) OR ACTIVATING (CRISPRA) 1000S OF DISTAL GENE REGULATORY ELEMENTS. WHILE SUCCESSFUL, IT IS WELL KNOWN THAT ONLY 10-20% OF GRNAS THAT TARGET DISTAL REGULATORY ELEMENTS FUNCTION TO IMPACT TARGET GENE EXPRESSION. THIS IS PROBLEMATIC GIVEN THE DISCOVERY OF OVER 2 MILLION PUTATIVE DISTAL REGULATORY ELEMENTS ACROSS THE GENOME BY ENCODE AND OTHERS. IMPROVING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF DCAS-DNA BINDING SPECIFICITY AND OFF-TARGET EFFECTS IS CRUCIAL FOR ENHANCING THE PRECISION AND EFFECTIVENESS OF EPIGENOME EDITING, WHICH WILL BE CRITICAL FOR COST-EFFECTIVE HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENS AND FOR MORE EFFECTIVE THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS. TO ADDRESS THIS UNMET NEED IN EPIGENOME EDITING, WE WILL DEVELOP PURGE, A SUITE OF TOOLS FOR PRIORITIZING GRNAS FOR CRISPR EPIGENOME EDITING APPLICATIONS. COMPARED TO EXISTING METHODS, PURGE WILL BE UNIQUE IN THAT IT WILL BE BASED PRIMARILY OF DCAS9-DNA BINDING DATA, AS APPOSED TO CURRENT TOOLS THAT ARE BASED ON NUCLEASE-ACTIVE CAS9 CUTTING DATA (DESPITE THE FACT THAT EPIGENOME EDITING ASSAYS USE NUCLEASEDEAD CAS PROTEINS). AIM 1 WILL FOCUS ON DERIVING ON-TARGET DCAS9 BINDING AND ACTIVITY SCORES FOR CRISPRI, BASED ON A NOVEL USE OF HIGH-DENSITY DNA-BINDING ARRAYS. AIM 2 WILL FOCUS ON DERIVING DCAS9 OFF-TARGET BINDING AND ACTIVITY SCORES FOR CRISPRI, BASED ON EXTENSIVE ORTHOGONAL IN VITRO AND CELL-BASED CRISPRI EXPERIMENTS. AIM 3A WILL TEST THE ON-TARGET AND OFF-TARGET PURGE SCORES FOR CRISPRA. EXTENSIVE VALIDATION AND BENCHMARKING AGAINST STATE-OF-THE-ART TOOLS WILL BE PERFORMED. TOGETHER, THE EXPERIMENTAL STRATEGIES AND COMPUTATIONAL METHODS DEVELOPED IN THIS STUDY WILL GUIDE THE SELECTION OF OPTIMAL CRISPRI/A GRNAS THAT ENHANCE TARGET SITE ACTIVITY WHILE REDUCING UNINTENDED OFF-TARGET INTERACTIONS. IMPORTANTLY, OUR PURGE TOOLS WILL PROVIDE ORTHOGONAL INFORMATION THAT WILL BE INTEGRATED INTO EXISTING GRNA DESIGN METHODS TO ENSURE AN IMMEDIATE IMPACT ON CRISPR-BASED EPIGENOMIC SCREENS FOR STUDYING GENE REGULATION, AS WELL AS THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS OF EPIGENOME EDITING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF NUCLEOSOME REMODELING BY THE BAF CHROMATIN REMODELING COMPLEXES - ABSTRACT  GENES ENCODING SUBUNITS OF MAMMALIAN SWI/SNF (MSWI/SNF OR BAF) CHROMATIN REMODELING COMPLEXES ARE MUTATED IN OVER 20% OF HUMAN CANCERS. MUTATIONS IMPACTING BAF SUBUNITS ALSO CAUSE NEURODEVELOPMENT DISORDERS, SUCH AS COFFIN-SIRIS SYNDROME. MAMMALIAN BAF COMPLEXES EXIST AS THREE MAJOR COMPLEXES -- CBAF, PBAF, AND NCBAF, WHICH DIFFER BASED ON THEIR DISTINCT SUBUNIT COMPOSITIONS. AMONG THESE SUBUNITS, ARID1A, A CBAF-SPECIFIC SUBUNIT, IS THE MOST FREQUENTLY MUTATED GENE (~9 % OF ALL TYPES OF CANCER). THE MAJORITY OF ARID1A MUTATIONS ARE FRAMESHIFT OR NONSENSE MUTATIONS, CAUSING LOSS OF FUNCTION. PREVIOUS STUDIES HAVE SUGGESTED THAT ARID1A FACILITATES THE FORMATION OF OPEN CHROMATIN DOMAINS, BUT A BIOCHEMICAL ROLE FOR ARID1A IN BAF REMODELING ACTIVITY HAS NOT BEEN IDENTIFIED. WE HAVE RECENTLY ESTABLISHED THE IN VITRO RECONSTITUTION SYSTEM OF CBAF, PBAF, AND NCBAF, AND WE COMPARED THEIR BIOCHEMICAL ACTIVITIES. IN ADDITION, WE RECONSTITUTED A VARIETY OF CBAF SUBCOMPLEXES, DEFINING ROLES FOR SEVERAL SUBUNITS IN HIGH AFFINITY NUCLEOSOME BINDING AND NUCLEOSOME SLIDING ACTIVITY. REMARKABLY, WE FOUND THAT THE ARID1A SUBUNIT OF CBAF IS LARGELY DISPENSABLE FOR NUCLEOSOME BINDING, NUCLEOSOME SLIDING, AND ATPASE ACTIVITY, BUT ARID1A IS REQUIRED FOR CBAF TO TRANSFER HISTONE OCTAMERS BETWEEN DNA TEMPLATES. OUR STUDY REVEALED THE NOVEL BIOCHEMICAL FUNCTION OF ARID1A IN CBAF-MEDIATED CHROMATIN REMODELING AND SUGGESTS THAT DYSREGULATION OF HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY OF BAF COMPLEXES MAY BE RELEVANT TO CANCER FORMATION (MORO ET AL., NUCLEIC ACIDS RESEARCH, IN PRESS). BASED ON THESE RECENT FINDINGS BY OUR GROUP, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY IS A KEY BIOCHEMICAL ACTIVITY OF BAF COMPLEXES FOR CHROMATIN REGULATION AND CANCER FORMATION. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO ELUCIDATE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY OF BAF COMPLEXES AND HOW HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY OF BAF COMPLEXES REGULATES CHROMATIN ORGANIZATION AND GENE EXPRESSION, BY EXPLOITING A POWERFUL COMBINATION OF BIOCHEMICAL AND BIOPHYSICAL TECHNIQUES INCLUDING CRYO-ELECTRON MICROSCOPY (EM), AND GENOMICS APPROACHES IN EMBRYONIC STEM CELLS (ESCS). THIS PROPOSAL HAS TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM1 WILL DISSECT THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY OF BAF COMPLEXES. WE HAVE DISCOVERED THAT ARID1A IS REQUIRED FOR THE HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY OF CBAF, BUT THE MOLECULAR MECHANISM BY WHICH AIRD1A MEDIATES HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY IS UNCLEAR. TO OBTAIN MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO THIS, WE WILL PERFORM CRYO-EM ANALYSIS OF CBAF COMPLEX THAT LACKS ARID1A (∆ARID1 COMPLEX). FURTHERMORE, WE FOUND THAT THE NOT ONLY CBAF, BUT ALSO PBAF AND NCBAF, EXHIBIT HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY, SUGGESTING THAT HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY MAY BE ALSO A KEY BIOCHEMICAL ACTIVITY OF PBAF AND NCBAF. WE WILL ELUCIDATE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF THE HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY OF PBAF AND NCBAF. WE SHOWED THAT BAF SUBCOMPLEX RECONSTITUTED WITH 8 CORE SUBUNITS SHARED AMONG ALL BAF COMPLEXES LACKS HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY, DEMONSTRATING THAT PBAF- AND NCBAF-SPECIFIC SUBUNIT(S) IS REQUIRED FOR THE HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY OF EACH COMPLEX. TO IDENTIFY SUBUNIT(S) REQUIRED FOR THE HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY OF PBAF AND NCBAF, WE WILL ELIMINATE EACH OF PBAF- AND NCBAF-SPECIFIC SUBUNITS FROM EACH COMPLEX USING OUR RECONSTITUTION SYSTEM AND INVESTIGATE THE BIOCHEMICAL ACTIVITIES OF THE PURIFIED SUBCOMPLEXES. SINCE PBAF AND NCBAF-SPECIFIC SUBUNITS (ARID2, PBRM1, BRD7, GLTSCR1, AND BRD9) ARE FREQUENTLY MUTATED IN VARIOUS CANCERS, THIS STUDY WILL CERTAINLY UNCOVER NOVEL MOLECULAR FUNCTIONS OF THESE SUBUNITS. WE WILL ALSO DEFINE THE ROLES FOR THE HISTONE OCTAMER TRANSFER ACTIVITY OF BAF COMPLEXES IN CHROMATIN ACCESSIBILITY IN ESCS USING VARIOUS GENOMICS ANALYSES, SUCH AS ATAC-SEQ AND CUT&RUN. description: THE ROLE OF SWI/SNF CHROMATIN REMODELING COMPLEXES IN GERM LINE TRANSCRIPTION AND NUCLEAR ORGANIZATION - SUMMARY ERRORS IN HOMOLOGOUS CHROMOSOME SEGREGATION DURING MEIOSIS ARE THE LEADING CAUSE OF BIRTH DEFECTS, SPONTANEOUS PREGNANCY LOSS, AND CONTRIBUTE TO INFERTILITY. PROPER CHROMOSOME SEGREGATION, WHICH REQUIRES PAIRWISE ASSOCIATIONS OF THE HOMOLOGOUS CHROMOSOMES ARE GOVERNED BY GENES WHICH EXPRESSION PATTERN ARE EXQUISITELY REGULATED IN DEVELOPING GAMETES. CHROMATIN REMODELING COMPLEXES PLAY A CRUCIAL ROLE IN FACILITATING GENE TRANSCRIPTION DURING MEIOTIC CELL DIVISION BY REGULATING ACCESS TO CHROMATIN. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH THESE COMPLEXES CONTROL THE RECRUITMENT AND ACTIVITY OF THE TRANSCRIPTION MACHINERY AT GENE PROMOTERS REMAIN UNCLEAR. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS POSITS THAT PBAF/BAF/NCBAF (SWI/SNF) COMPLEXES AT PROMOTERS ARE ESSENTIAL FOR RECRUITING AND ACTIVATING THE TRANSCRIPTION MACHINERY. ADDITIONALLY, WE PROPOSE THAT SWI/SNF COMPLEXES REGULATE THE EXPRESSION AND ACTIVITY OF OTHER CRITICAL CHROMATIN FEATURES, SUCH AS NON-CODING RNAS AND TRANSPOSONS. TO TEST OUR MODEL, WE HAVE OUTLINED THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: FIRSTLY, WE WILL EXPLORE THE ROLES OF SPECIFIC SUBUNITS OF PBAF (PBRM1 AND ARID2), BAF (ARID1A), AND NCBAF (BRD9), ALONG WITH THE COMMON CATALYTIC SUBUNIT BRG1, IN MEIOTIC DNA DOUBLE-STRAND BREAK REPAIR, CROSSOVER FORMATION, AND THE ASSOCIATION AND DISJUNCTION OF HOMOLOGOUS CHROMOSOMES. USING IMAGING TECHNIQUES AND GENETICALLY MODIFIED MICE, WE AIM TO DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN THE UNIQUE AND SHARED FUNCTIONS OF PBAF, BAF, AND NCBAF AS REGULATORS OF MEIOSIS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PBAF/BAF/NCBAF COMPLEXES AND PROMOTERS IN DEVELOPING GAMETES, AS WELL AS OTHER GENOMIC ELEMENTS, BY GENERATING GENOME-WIDE BINDING PROFILES FOR THESE COMPLEXES AND TRANSCRIPTION MACHINERY COMPONENTS IN MOUSE SPERMATOCYTES. SUBSEQUENTLY, WE WILL STUDY THE IMPACT OF DELETING SPECIFIC SUBUNITS ON THE DISTRIBUTION AND COMPOSITION OF PBAF, BAF, AND NCBAF AT PROMOTERS, AS WELL AS ON GENE TRANSCRIPTION (RNA-SEQ). IN THE THIRD AIM, WE WILL UTILIZE HIGH-THROUGHPUT FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH) ON WHOLE-MOUNTED SEMINIFEROUS TUBULES TO EXAMINE HOW 3D NUCLEAR ORGANIZATION CHANGES AS MEIOSIS PROGRESSES AND THE CONSISTENCY OF THESE CHANGES BETWEEN CELLS. TO EVALUATE THE ROLE OF SWI/SNF COMPLEXES IN NUCLEAR ORGANIZATION, WE WILL EMPLOY A PANEL OF FISH PROBES STRATEGICALLY PLACED ACROSS THE GENOME, INCLUDING AT PROMOTERS, ENHANCERS, AND MEIOTIC SUPER-ENHANCERS, IN BOTH WILD-TYPE AND KNOCKOUT CELLS LACKING PBRM 1, ARID2, ARID1A, BRD9, OR BRG1. OUR FINDINGS WILL PROVIDE VALUABLE INSIGHTS INTO THE ROLE OF SWI/SNF COMPLEXES CONTROLLING GLOBAL NUCLEAR CHANGES VERSUS SPECIFIC ALTERATIONS MEDIATED BY BAF/PBAF/NCBAF SUBTYPES IN THE EXPRESSION OF MEIOTIC GENES, DNA REPAIR, AND HOMOLOGOUS CHROMOSOME PAIRING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DISTRIBUTIONAL BALANCING FOR COMPLEX CAUSAL INFERENCE IN CRITICAL CARE - PROJECT SUMMARY (SEE INSTRUCTIONS): DISTRIBUTIONAL BALANCING IS A DESIGN-BASED STRATEGY FOR CAUSAL INFERENCE THAT ALIGNS COVARIATE DISTRIBUTIONS ACROSS EXPOSURE GROUPS AND A TARGET POPULATION, REDUCING RELIANCE ON CORRECTLY SPECIFIED PROPENSITY MODELS OR SELECTED COVARIATE MOMENTS. EXISTING METHODS OFTEN ASSUME IDEAL CONDITIONS, INCLUDING NO UNMEASURED CONFOUNDING AND SINGLE-TIME EXPOSURES. THESE ASSUMPTIONS RARELY HOLD IN BIOMEDICAL STUDIES, ESPECIALLY IN CRITICAL CARE, WHERE CLINICAL ACUITY IS IMPERFECTLY MEASURED, TREATMENT DECISIONS ARE SEQUENTIAL, AND DOSING IS OFTEN CONTINUOUS. THE LONG-TERM OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP ROBUST, SCALABLE, AND INTERPRETABLE CAUSAL INFERENCE METHODS FOR RELIABLE EVIDENCE GENERATION FROM COMPLEX BIOMEDICAL DATA. THE PROPOSED WORK ADVANCES DISTRIBUTIONAL BALANCING IN THREE SETTINGS CENTRAL TO CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING. AIM 1 WILL DEVELOP PROXIMAL CAUSAL LEARNING METHODS FOR UNMEASURED CONFOUNDING USING TREATMENT- AND OUTCOME-CONFOUNDING PROXIES. AIM 2 WILL DEVELOP SEQUENTIAL DISTRIBUTIONAL BALANCING METHODS FOR LONGITUDINAL TREATMENT DECISIONS. AIM 3 WILL DEVELOP CONTINUOUS-TREATMENT DOSE-RESPONSE METHODS INTEGRATING DISTRIBUTIONAL WEIGHTING WITH SPLINE-EXPANDED NEURAL NETWORKS. THE METHODS WILL DELIVER IDENTIFICATION RESULTS, ESTIMATORS, THEORY, DIAGNOSTICS, AND SOFTWARE FOR CAUSAL INFERENCE WITH PROXIES, SEQUENTIAL DECISIONS, AND CONTINUOUS DOSES. IN AIM 1, BALANCING WEIGHTS WILL BE CONSTRUCTED FROM PROXY VARIABLES USING FLEXIBLE DISTANCE-BASED CRITERIA, WITH SENSITIVITY ANALYSES FOR PROXIMAL ASSUMPTIONS. IN AIM 2, UNSTABLE INVERSE-PROBABILITY PRODUCTS WILL BE REPLACED WITH HISTORY-AWARE BALANCING WEIGHTS AND DIAGNOSTICS FOR BALANCE, OVERLAP, AND LIMITED SUPPORT. IN AIM 3, DISTANCE COVARIATE OPTIMAL WEIGHTS WILL BE INTEGRATED WITH NEURAL OUTCOME MODELS THROUGH A WEIGHTED SPLINE-EXPANDED NETWORK AND TARGETED REGULARIZATION. THE METHODS WILL BE EVALUATED THROUGH SIMULATIONS AND CRITICAL CARE APPLICATIONS, INCLUDING EARLY ANTIBIOTICS AND VASOPRESSORS IN SEPSIS AND OXYGEN TITRATION IN MECHANICALLY VENTILATED PATIENTS. OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE AND REPRODUCIBLE TOOLS WILL SUPPORT BROAD ADOPTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTEGRATING LANGUAGE MODELS AND TOPOLOGY FOR MULTI-SCALE R-LOOP PREDICTION - PROJECT SUMMARY (SEE INSTRUCTIONS): R-LOOPS ARE THREE-STRANDED STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF AN RNA:DNA HYBRID AND A DISPLACED SINGLE DNA STRAND THAT TYPICALLY FORM DURING TRANSCRIPTION AND CONSTITUTE 3-5% OF THE GENOME ACROSS TAXA. WHILE R-LOOPS ARE FUNDAMENTAL TO GENOME REGULATION, ABERRANT R-LOOP FORMATION, OFTEN DRIVEN BY TOPOLOGICAL STRESS, PROMOTES REPLICATION STRESS AND DOUBLE-STRAND BREAKS THAT DRIVE CHROMOSOMAL REARRANGEMENTS. THE PHYSICAL AND TOPOLOGICAL FACTORS THAT DRIVE R-LOOP FORMATION, STABILITY, AND COMPLEX 3D ARCHITECTURE REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THIS RESEARCH ESTABLISHES A PREDICTIVE, MULTI-SCALE, QUANTITATIVE FRAMEWORK TO ANALYZE THESE FACTORS BY INTEGRATING EXPERIMENTAL TECHNIQUES WITH NEW MATHEMATICAL AND MACHINE LEARNING MODELS. SPECIFIC AIM 1 INTEGRATES SINGLE-MOLECULE DATA WITH PROBABILISTIC GRAMMARS AND LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS (LLMS) TO CREATE A NEW CLASS OF PREDICTIVE MODELS OF R-LOOP FORMATION ON NATURAL GENOMIC SEQUENCES. SPECIFIC AIM 2 DETERMINES HOW DNA TOPOLOGY REGULATES THE FORMATION AND 3D STRUCTURE OF R-LOOPS BY COUPLING BIOCHEMICAL EXPERIMENTS AND MATHEMATICAL APPROACHES BASED ON TOPOLOGY AND DISCRETE MATHEMATICS. THE PROJECT USES SINGLE-MOLECULE FOOTPRINTING, DNA TOPOLOGY EXPERIMENTS, AND ATOMIC FORCE MICROSCOPY TO QUANTIFY THE EFFECT OF TOPOLOGY AND ADDRESS FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS ABOUT R-LOOP ENTANGLEMENT. THE RESEARCH INTRODUCES A PROBABILISTIC GRAMMAR FRAMEWORK, A STRUCTURE BASED ON TILE SYSTEMS, AND TOPOLOGICAL MODELS ROOTED IN LATTICE WALKS AND POLYGONS TO FORMALIZE ENTANGLEMENT IN MULTI-STRANDED NUCLEIC ACIDS. THESE MODELS PREDICT HOW AND WHERE R-LOOPS INITIATE, AND HOW TOPOLOGY AND OTHER FACTORS SHAPE 3D STRUCTURE. THE INTEGRATION OF MACHINE LEARNING WITH FORMAL GRAMMARS WILL ENABLE PREDICTIVE MODELS THAT CAPTURE BOTH SEQUENCE-LEVEL SIGNALS AND HIGHER-ORDER TOPOLOGICAL ENTANGLEMENT, PROVIDING A UNIFIED APPROACH TO DESCRIBE, CLASSIFY, AND PREDICT R-LOOP STRUCTURES. BY IDENTIFYING HOTSPOTS FOR R-LOOPS ALONG HUMAN GENOMIC SEQUENCES, THIS RESEARCH PROVIDES THE BIOPHYSICAL FRAMEWORK NECESSARY TO DEFINE THE MECHANISTIC LINK BETWEEN R-LOOP FORMATION, GENOME INSTABILITY, AND DISEASE.

description: THE TEEN PERIOD (T-DOT) COHORT: A LONGITUDINAL STUDY TO UNDERSTAND PATTERNS OF MENSTRUATION AND RISK FACTORS FOR IRON DEFICIENCY IN THE EARLY POST-MENARCHAL YEARS - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT THE MENSTRUAL CYCLE IS RECOGNIZED AS A VITAL SIGN REFLECTIVE OF OVERALL HEALTH IN PEDIATRICS. THE ABILITY TO DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN NORMAL AND ABNORMAL MENSTRUATION IS ESSENTIAL BECAUSE MANY HEALTH ISSUES CAN MANIFEST AS IRREGULARITIES IN MENSTRUAL FLOW, DURATION, OR TIMING. EARLY RECOGNITION OF HEAVY MENSTRUAL BLEEDING IS CRUCIAL BECAUSE IT OFTEN LEADS TO IRON DEFICIENCY (ID), WHICH IS LINKED TO FATIGUE, REDUCED EXERCISE CAPACITY, AND COGNITIVE ISSUES. WHILE AGE-SPECIFIC PARAMETERS FOR BLOOD PRESSURE AND OTHER VITAL SIGNS ARE READILY AVAILABLE, DATA ON MENSTRUATION, ESPECIALLY IN EARLY ADOLESCENCE, ARE LIMITED AND OUTDATED. FURTHERMORE, WHILE NON-MEDICAL FACTORS INFLUENCING HEALTH MAY AFFECT MENSTRUATION AND RISK OF ID, POPULATION DATA FROM NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE COHORTS ARE EVEN MORE LIMITED. SMARTPHONES AND TABLETS ENABLE GREATER ACCESS TO ADOLESCENTS AND DECREASE BARRIERS TO RESEARCH ON MENSTRUATION. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS R01 APPLICATION IS TO PROSPECTIVELY STUDY NEWLY MENARCHAL ADOLESCENTS USING THE T-DOT (TEEN PERIOD) MOBILE APP TO ESTABLISH A NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE POPULATION-LEVEL DATABANK THAT INFORMS THE EXPECTED PARAMETERS OF THE MENSTRUAL CYCLE VITAL SIGN, PATTERNS, AND RISK FACTORS FOR ID. T-DOT IS A TEEN-FRIENDLY, HIPAA-COMPLIANT MENSTRUAL TRACKING APP THAT SECURELY TRANSFERS DATA DIRECTLY TO OUR RESEARCH TEAM. THE RESULTS FROM OUR NICHD R21 AWARD DEMONSTRATED FEASIBILITY AND SUSTAINED PARTICIPANT ENGAGEMENT WITH T-DOT. WE ARE NOW WELL-POSITIONED TO ACHIEVE OUR OBJECTIVES THROUGH THE FOLLOWING AIMS: 1) ESTABLISH POPULATION MENSTRUAL PATTERNS (FREQUENCY, DURATION, AND FLOW) USING THE T-DOT MENSTRUAL TRACKING APP, AND 2) IDENTIFY THE FREQUENCY, TIMING, AND RISK FACTORS FOR ID IN THE EARLY POST-MENARCHAL YEARS. OUR STUDY POPULATION WILL INCLUDE 500 ADOLESCENTS WITHIN SIX MONTHS OF THEIR FIRST MENSTRUAL CYCLE WHO ARE NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE WITH RESPECT TO RACE, ETHNICITY, AND BODY WEIGHT. PARTICIPANTS WILL TRACK THEIR MENSTRUAL PATTERNS USING THE T-DOT APP OVER TWO YEARS AND COMPLETE VIRTUAL STUDY VISITS EVERY EIGHT MONTHS, WHICH WILL INCLUDE AT- HOME ID SCREENING. OUR RATIONALE FOR THIS RESEARCH IS THAT USING SMARTPHONES TO IDENTIFY POPULATION PATTERNS AMONG YOUNG ADOLESCENTS OFFERS AN OPPORTUNITY TO DETECT ABNORMAL MENSTRUATION EARLIER AND TO PROMPT INTERVENTIONS TO ENHANCE REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH AND QUALITY OF LIFE. OUR WORK IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE WE WILL RECRUIT A NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE SAMPLE FROM ACROSS THE UNITED STATES, FOCUS ON THE EARLY GYNECOLOGICAL YEARS PROSPECTIVELY, AND UTILIZE A DECENTRALIZED APPROACH TO INCREASE FEASIBILITY AND REDUCE PARTICIPANT BURDEN. COMPLETION OF THIS WORK WILL YIELD THE FOLLOWING EXPECTED OUTCOMES: 1) A CONTEMPORARY NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE POPULATION-LEVEL DATABANK TO INFORM THE EXPECTED PARAMETERS OF THE MENSTRUAL CYCLE VITAL SIGN IN EARLY POST- MENARCHAL ADOLESCENTS, AND 2) IDENTIFICATION OF THE FREQUENCY OF AND RISK FACTORS FOR ID IN ADOLESCENT FEMALES TO IDENTIFY PATIENTS WHO WOULD BENEFIT FROM EARLY LABORATORY SCREENING. OUR WORK IS RESPONSIVE TO THE 2024-2028 NIH-WIDE STRATEGIC PLAN FOR RESEARCH ON WOMEN'S HEALTH, WHICH HIGHLIGHTS THE NEED FOR FOCUSED INVESTIGATION OF FEMALE REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH, INCLUDING MENSTRUATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ANDROGEN-ESTROGEN BALANCE AND FGF PATHWAYS: MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE CONTRIBUTION OF EFFERENT DUCTS TO HUMAN SPERM MATURATION - SUMMARY THE EFFERENT DUCTS (EDS) OF THE EPIDIDYMIS ARE PIVOTAL IN SPERM MATURATION. REGULATORY MECHANISMS DEPENDENT UPON THE ANDROGEN RECEPTOR (AR) AND ESTROGEN RECEPTOR (ER/ESR) ARE CRUCIAL FOR NORMAL FUNCTIONS OF THE HUMAN EPIDIDYMIS. THIS PROJECT EXPLORES THE ROLES OF AR, ESR1, AND FIBROBLAST GROWTH FACTOR (FGF) SIGNALING IN DIFFERENTIATION AND FUNCTION OF THE HUMAN EDS USING AN INNOVATIVE 3D ORGANOID CULTURE MODEL. IN PRELIMINARY DATA WE SHOW THAT BOTH ANDROGENS (DIHYDROTESTOSTERONE [DHT] AND TESTOSTERONE [T]) AND ESTROGEN (17-Β-ESTRADIOL [E2]) FACILITATE ED ORGANOID GROWTH AT PHYSIOLOGICAL CONCENTRATIONS. ADDITIONALLY, FGF2, FGF7, AND FGF10 ENHANCE ORGANOID GROWTH OR BRANCHING. BUILDING UPON THESE DATA, WE PROPOSE THE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS THAT THE BALANCE BETWEEN ANDROGENS AND ESTROGEN IS ESSENTIAL FOR THE NORMAL FORMATION AND FUNCTION OF EDS. OUR FOCUS WILL BE ON ELUCIDATING THE REGULATORY MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH THE ANDROGEN:ESTROGEN BALANCE IMPACTS GENE EXPRESSION AND CELLULAR FUNCTIONS IN EDS. BEYOND THIS BALANCE, FGF SIGNALING PATHWAYS FURTHER REGULATE EPIDIDYMIS CELL FUNCTION BY INFLUENCING ORGANOGENESIS AND MORPHOGENESIS OF THE EPIDIDYMIS EPITHELIUM. DISRUPTION OF THESE TWO CRITICAL MECHANISMS CAN IMPAIR EPIDIDYMIS FUNCTION. WE WILL ALSO UTILIZE OUR ED ORGANOID CULTURE SYSTEM TO INVESTIGATE HOW HIGH ESTROGEN LEVELS AND ENDOCRINE DISRUPTORS CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EPIDIDYMIS EPITHELIUM. FIRST (SA1), WE WILL ANALYZE HOW PHYSIOLOGICAL LEVELS OF DHT/T AND E2 CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF ED ORGANOIDS, USING RNA SEQUENCING AND CHROMATIN IMMUNOPRECIPITATION SEQUENCING TECHNIQUES. THESE EXPERIMENTS AIM TO PINPOINT THE DIRECT TARGETS OF AR AND ESR1 AND THE RELATED NETWORK OF ANDROGEN- AND ESTROGEN-MEDIATED GENE EXPRESSION. SECOND (SA2), WE WILL EXAMINE THE ROLE OF FGF SIGNALING AND STROMAL CELL-SECRETED FACTORS IN THE GROWTH AND MORPHOGENESIS OF ED ORGANOIDS. BY MANIPULATING FGF LEVELS OR APPLYING SELECTIVE FGF RECEPTOR (FGFR) INHIBITORS IN 3D CULTURE MODELS, WE AIM TO UNDERSTAND THEIR IMPACT ON ORGANOID FORMATION AS REGULATED BY FGF SIGNALING. THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL IDENTIFY HOW FGFS AND STROMAL CELL-SECRETED FACTORS MAINTAIN NORMAL EPIDIDYMIS FUNCTION. THIRD (SA3), WE WILL USE ORGANOID MODELS TO EXPLORE THE MECHANISMS BEHIND ED EPITHELIAL DAMAGE CAUSED BY ESTROGEN THERAPY AND ENDOCRINE DISRUPTORS. USING SINGLE-CELL RNA SEQUENCING AND IN VITRO SYSTEMS, THE EXPERIMENTS OF THIS AIM WILL EXPLORE HOW AN ANDROGEN/ESTROGEN IMBALANCE, HIGH E2 CONDITIONS, AND ENDOCRINE DISRUPTORS CONTRIBUTE TO EPITHELIAL DAMAGE IN EDS. THE OUTCOMES OF THIS RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE INSIGHTS THAT ENHANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE CRITICAL FACTORS FOR NORMAL EPIDIDYMAL FUNCTION, HIGHLIGHTING THE REGULATORY MECHANISMS ESSENTIAL FOR SPERM MATURATION. THIS RESEARCH EMPHASIZES THE ROLE OF AR, ESR1, AND FGF SIGNALING IN MAINTAINING NORMAL EPIDIDYMAL FUNCTION. BY UNCOVERING THESE MECHANISMS, OUR FINDINGS MAY IDENTIFY FACTORS AFFECTING SPERM QUALITY AND AID IN CREATING THERAPIES FOR MALE INFERTILITY. ADDITIONALLY, THE RESULTS MAY CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE AND REVERSIBLE MALE CONTRACEPTIVES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING SYNAPTIC DEFICIENCY IN DOWN SYNDROME - ABSTRACT  HUMAN BRAIN DEVELOPMENT REQUIRES THE PRECISE COORDINATION OF SEVERAL BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES, SUCH AS NEUROGENESIS, NEURONAL MIGRATION, AND SYNAPTOGENESIS TO ESTABLISH THE FUNCTIONAL NEURAL CIRCUITS THAT UNDERLIE COGNITION AND BEHAVIOR. SYNAPTOGENESIS, WHICH IN HUMANS BEGINS DURING MID-FETAL DEVELOPMENT AND PEAKS IN EARLY POSTNATAL LIFE, FORMS THE FOUNDATION OF CORTICAL CONNECTIVITY. DEFECTS IN THIS PROCESS USUALLY LEAD TO INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY AND ARE A HALLMARK OF SEVERAL NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS, INCLUDING DOWN SYNDROME. IN FACT, PREVIOUS RESEARCH INDICATES THAT DOWN SYNDROME CORTICAL NEURONS HAVE REDUCED SYNAPSES AND SYNAPTIC COMMUNICATION. THE APPEARANCE OF THESE DEFICITS IN INFANCY SUGGESTS THAT ALTERATIONS EMERGE DURING THE EARLIEST STAGES OF BRAIN DEVELOPMENT IN DOWN SYNDROME. HOWEVER, THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT UNDERLIE THESE SYNAPTIC DEFICITS REMAIN UNKNOWN.  AMONG THE PROTEINS INVOLVED IN HUMAN SYNAPSE FORMATION AND FUNCTION, CBLN2 IS OF PARTICULAR RELEVANCE. CBLN2 IS A SYNAPTIC ORGANIZER WITH A HUMAN-SPECIFIC EXPRESSION PATTERN DURING MIDFETAL AND LATE-FETAL DEVELOPMENT, A PERIOD THAT CORRESPONDS TO THE START OF NEUROGENESIS. IMPORTANTLY, OUR PRELIMINARY DATA HAS SHOWN THAT CBLN2 IS SIGNIFICANTLY DOWNREGULATED DURING PRENATAL DEVELOPMENT IN DOWN SYNDROME CORTICAL EXCITATORY NEURONS. WE THEREFORE HYPOTHESIZE THAT REDUCED CBLN2 CAUSES REDUCED SYNAPTOGENESIS AND DEFICIENT SYNAPTIC FUNCTION IN DOWN SYNDROME.  IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE AIM TO GAIN INSIGHT INTO THE DECREASED SYNAPSE FORMATION AND IMPAIRED SYNAPTIC COMMUNICATION IN DOWN SYNDROME. USING NOVEL ISOGENIC TRISOMY 21 DISORDER-SPECIFIC HUMAN IPSCS, WE WILL DISSECT HOW DIFFERENCES IN CBLN2 EXPRESSION AFFECT SYNAPSE FORMATION AND SPINE MORPHOLOGY, AND WILL DETERMINE HOW THESE DIFFERENCES AFFECT SUBTHRESHOLD AND SYNAPTIC PROPERTIES OF EXCITATORY NEURONS. WE WILL ALSO RIGOROUSLY QUANTIFY DIFFERENCES IN MORPHOLOGY, SYNAPTIC DENSITY, SPINE MORPHOLOGY, AND ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES BETWEEN TRISOMY 21 NEURONS AND ISOGENIC CONTROLS AT DIFFERENT DEVELOPMENTAL PERIODS. FINALLY, WE WILL TEST WHETHER RESTORING CBLN2 EXPRESSION CAN REESTABLISH NORMAL SYNAPTOGENESIS IN TRISOMY 21 NEURONS. THIS STUDY WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING ON THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT MAY UNDERLIE INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY IN DOWN SYNDROME.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EVALUATING THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS FOR PRE-PREGNANCY WEIGHT MANAGEMENT AND IMPROVED PREGNANCY OUTCOMES - SUMMARY WOMEN WHO ARE OBESE AT PREGNANCY ONSET HAVE A HIGH LIKELIHOOD FOR ADVERSE OUTCOMES DURING PREGNANCY, INCLUDING SPONTANEOUS ABORTION, GESTATIONAL DIABETES (GDM), HYPERTENSIVE DISORDERS, CESAREAN DELIVERY, AND PRETERM BIRTH, AS WELL AS CARDIOVASCULAR AND METABOLIC CONDITIONS POST-PREGNANCY. OFFSPRING OF MOTHERS WHO ARE OBESE ARE ALSO AT INCREASED RISK OF OUTCOMES SUCH AS LARGE FOR GESTATIONAL AGE (LGA), MALFORMATIONS, METABOLIC DISORDERS. HEALTHY WEIGHT LOSS BEFORE PREGNANCY IS RECOMMENDED TO REDUCE RISKS RELATED TO OBESITY. ADDITIONALLY, WEIGHT LOSS ATTEMPTS ARE COMMON AMONG WOMEN WITH OBESITY WHO ARE PLANNING TO BECOME PREGNANT. OF PREVAILING WEIGHT LOSS TREATMENTS, LONG-ACTING GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS (GLP- 1RA) (SEMAGLUTIDE, LIRAGLUTIDE) AND RELATED THERAPIES (TIRZEPATIDE) HAVE RECENTLY EMERGED AS POPULAR AND EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS FOR BOTH DIABETES AND OBESITY. HOWEVER, DESPITE WIDESPREAD USE, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT GLP-1RA USE PRIOR TO OR DURING PREGNANCY. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE NATIONAL PATIENT CENTERED CLINICAL RESEARCH NETWORK (PCORNET) TO IDENTIFY A RETROSPECTIVE ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR)-BASED COHORT OF WOMEN WITH PREGNANCIES AND THEIR INFANTS TO ADDRESS IMPORTANT KNOWLEDGE GAPS RELATED TO GLP-1RA USE AND PREGNANCY OUTCOMES. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT GLP-1RA USE PRIOR TO PREGNANCY, BY VIRTUE OF REDUCING PRE-PREGNANCY OBESITY, WILL REDUCE RISKS OF OBESITY-RELATED PREGNANCY OUTCOMES, INCLUDING (BUT NOT LIMITED TO) GESTATIONAL DIABETES AND HYPERTENSIVE DISORDERS OF PREGNANCY. HOWEVER, UNDER THE PREMISE THAT DISCONTINUATION OF GLP-1RAS HAS BEEN SHOWN TO PROMPTLY INITIATE REBOUND WEIGHT GAIN IN CLINICAL TRIALS, WE ALSO HYPOTHESIZE THAT PRE-PREGNANCY GLP- 1RA USE (AND DISCONTINUATION PRIOR TO OR EARLY IN PREGNANCY) WILL RESULT IN HIGHER GWG THAN OTHER LESS EFFECTIVE ANTI-OBESITY MEDICATIONS. FINALLY, AS ANIMAL MODELS SUGGEST POTENTIAL RISKS TO THE DEVELOPING FETUS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT GLP-1RA USE IN EARLY PREGNANCY WILL BE ASSOCIATED WITH FETAL/NEONATAL OUTCOMES SUCH AS STILLBIRTH, MALFORMATIONS AND NICU ADMISSION. THE USE OF PCORNET WILL FACILITATE THE IDENTIFICATION AND LONGITUDINAL FOLLOW-UP OF A MULTI-CENTER COHORT OF WOMEN AND THEIR INFANTS, INCLUDING WEIGHT/BMI, MEDICATION PRESCRIBING, ENCOUNTERS (INCLUDING DIAGNOSES AND PROCEDURES), AND LABORATORY RESULTS, THEREBY PROVIDING CONCRETE AND NOVEL ADVANTAGES OVER EXISTING STUDIES OF GLP-1RAS AND PREGNANCY TO DATE. BY ASKING INNOVATIVE QUESTIONS AROUND GLP-1RAS AND PREGNANCY, WE WILL HELP INFORM NEW CLINICAL GUIDELINES FOR GLP- 1RA USE AMONG WOMEN WHO ARE PREGNANT OR PLANNING TO BECOME PREGNANT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CAREGIVER REPORTED DYSTONIA IMPACT IN CEREBRAL PALSY: CARDI-CP - PROJECT SUMMARY DYSTONIA IN CEREBRAL PALSY (CP) COMMONLY CAUSES MOTOR FUNCTIONAL LIMITATIONS IN CHILDHOOD AND AFFECTS 1 OUT OF EVERY 500 PEOPLE IN THE US. DYSTONIA CAN BE DEBILITATING BUT HARD TO EVALUATE IN CP AS IT OFTEN CO-OCCURS WITH SPASTICITY. YET, MISSING FUNCTIONALLY IMPACTFUL DYSTONIA CAN PREVENT TARGETED DYSTONIA TREATMENT OR LEAD TO UNNECESSARY SURGERIES MEANT ONLY TO TREAT SPASTICITY. UNFORTUNATELY, DYSTONIA IS DRAMATICALLY UNDERDIAGNOSED IN CLINIC EVEN BY EXPERT CLINICIANS. FURTHERMORE, EXISTING CLINICIAN-ADMINISTERED DYSTONIA SEVERITY SCALES ARE TIME- CONSUMING, MISS FUNCTIONALLY IMPACTFUL DYSTONIA, AND HAVE LITTLE RESPONSIVENESS DATA IN CP. THE LACK OF FUNCTIONALLY MEANINGFUL DYSTONIA MEASURES IS A CRITICAL GAP FOR CLINICAL TRIALS SEEKING TO IMPROVE DYSTONIA TREATMENT. AS A NOVEL WAY TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, CAREGIVERS CAN BE PARTNERS IN DYSTONIA ASSESSMENT. HOWEVER, OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT ONLY 40% OF CAREGIVERS OF CHILDREN DIAGNOSED WITH DYSTONIA ARE AWARE OF THIS DIAGNOSIS, LET ALONE KNOW HOW TO DIFFERENTIATE THE RELATIVE IMPACTS OF DYSTONIA VERSUS SPASTICITY. SINCE EVEN EXPERT CLINICIANS UNDERDIAGNOSE DYSTONIA IN CLINIC, INCREASED CAREGIVER EDUCATION ON DYSTONIA CANNOT FULLY ADDRESS THE NEED FOR IMPROVED DYSTONIA ASSESSMENT. INSTEAD, WE PROPOSE CREATING A CAREGIVER-REPORTED DYSTONIA IMPACT SCALE THAT IS NOT DEPENDENT ON CAREGIVERS’ PRIOR KNOWLEDGE OF DYSTONIA. WE HAVE SHOWN THAT CAREGIVERS’ YES/NO RESPONSES TO TWO QUESTIONS ABOUT TRIGGERED INVOLUNTARY MOVEMENTS CAN IDENTIFY DYSTONIA WITH 75% SENSITIVITY AND 81% SPECIFICITY. HAVING CLINICIANS ASK CAREGIVERS ABOUT THEIR CHILD’S VARIABLE MOVEMENTS IN CLINIC CAN IMPROVE DYSTONIA DIAGNOSTIC RATES FROM 57% TO 74% OF CHILDREN WITH CP, MATCHING RESEARCH-BASED ESTIMATES. FINALLY, OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT CAREGIVERS DESCRIBE A GREATER VARIETY OF TRIGGERED INVOLUNTARY MOVEMENTS IN CHILDREN WITH GREATER DYSTONIA SEVERITY, REGARDLESS OF WHETHER CAREGIVERS KNEW THEIR CHILDREN HAD DYSTONIA. THEREFORE, OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT CAREGIVERS’ DESCRIPTIONS OF TRIGGERED INVOLUNTARY MOVEMENTS WILL COVARY WITH CLINICIAN-ASSESSED DYSTONIA IMPACT INDEPENDENT OF PRIOR CAREGIVER DYSTONIA KNOWLEDGE. WE CONCURRENTLY PROPOSE USING CAREGIVERS’ DESCRIPTIONS OF TRIGGERED INVOLUNTARY MOVEMENTS TO CONSTRUCT, VALIDATE, AND TEST THE RESPONSIVENESS OF A LIKERT-SCALE ASSESSMENT CALLED CAREGIVER-REPORTED DYSTONIA IMPACT IN CP (CARDI-CP). IN AIM 1, WE DETERMINE HOW CAREGIVERS AND CLINICIANS DESCRIBE THE SAME MOVEMENTS IN VIDEOS OF CHILDREN WITH CP TO BUILD A SHARED LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE FUNCTIONALLY IMPACTFUL DYSTONIA AND FACILITATE CLINICAL COMMUNICATION. IN AIM 2, WE USE RIGOROUS PSYCHOMETRIC ANALYSIS AND ITEM RESPONSE THEORY MODELING TO CONSTRUCT AND VALIDATE CARDI-CP AS COMPARED TO CLINICIAN-ASSESSED DYSTONIA IMPACT. IN AIM 3, WE DETERMINE WHETHER CARDI-CP IS RESPONSIVE TO CHANGES IN DYSTONIA AFTER DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION BUT NOT TO CHANGES IN SPASTICITY AFTER SELECTIVE DORSAL RHIZOTOMY. BY THUS DEVELOPING CARDI-CP AS A FAMILY-CENTERED, FUNCTIONALLY MEANINGFUL, AND RESPONSIVE DYSTONIA IMPACT ASSESSMENT, THIS PROPOSAL IS FOUNDATIONAL FOR OPTIMIZING CP CARE AND IMPROVING DYSTONIA TREATMENT TRIAL OUTCOME MEASURES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CLINICAL IMPLEMENTATION AND VALIDATION OF AN AI-ENHANCED TOOL FOR REAL-TIME PREDICTION OF POSTPARTUM HEMORRHAGE RISK - ABSTRACT POSTPARTUM HEMORRHAGE (PPH) REMAINS THE LEADING CAUSE OF MATERNAL MORTALITY WORLDWIDE, CONTRIBUTING SIGNIFICANTLY TO MATERNAL MORBIDITY. IN THE UNITED STATES, PPH ACCOUNTS FOR APPROXIMATELY 21% OF MATERNAL DEATHS, WITH A STEADILY RISING INCIDENCE. CURRENT PREDICTIVE TOOLS RELY HEAVILY ON MANUAL DATA ENTRY AND STATIC RISK FACTORS, LEADING TO MISCLASSIFICATION OF AT-RISK INDIVIDUALS AND INEFFICIENT USE OF HEALTHCARE RESOURCES. BUILDING UPON ROBUST PRELIMINARY DATA FROM OUR K08-FUNDED WORK DEMONSTRATING THAT OUR MACHINE LEARNING MODEL IDENTIFIES APPROXIMATELY 20% MORE PATIENTS AT RISK OF PPH THAN EXISTING TOOLS, WE PROPOSE TO VALIDATE AND IMPLEMENT AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)-ENHANCED TOOL FOR AUTOMATED, REAL-TIME PPH RISK PREDICTION INTEGRATED DIRECTLY INTO THE ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR). IN AIM 1, WE WILL REFINE OUR AI MODEL THROUGH ITERATIVE, STAKEHOLDER-INFORMED USABILITY TESTING WITHIN A SIMULATED EHR ENVIRONMENT, ACHIEVING PREDEFINED BENCHMARKS FOR USABILITY AND WORKFLOW INTEGRATION GUIDED BY THE CONSOLIDATED FRAMEWORK FOR IMPLEMENTATION RESEARCH (CFIR). IN AIM 2, WE WILL RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE REFINED AI TOOL THROUGH AN INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL CONDUCTED AT A HIGH-VOLUME TERTIARY CARE HOSPITAL. FOLLOWING AN INITIAL 6-MONTH SILENT VALIDATION TO CONFIRM REAL-TIME MODEL PERFORMANCE, THE TOOL’S IMPACT WILL BE TESTED OVER TWO YEARS. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME IS IMPROVED TIMELINESS OF CLINICAL INTERVENTIONS FOR PPH; SECONDARY OUTCOMES INCLUDE SEVERE PPH INCIDENCE, QUANTITATIVE BLOOD LOSS, TRANSFUSION RATES, MATERNAL MORBIDITY, AND HEALTHCARE RESOURCE UTILIZATION. ADVANCED STATISTICAL METHODS, INCLUDING COX PROPORTIONAL HAZARDS MODELS FOR THE PRIMARY OUTCOME AND MIXED-EFFECTS REGRESSION ANALYSES FOR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, WILL BE EMPLOYED. THIS PROJECT ESTABLISHES A SCALABLE AND GENERALIZABLE FRAMEWORK FOR IMPLEMENTING PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS IN OBSTETRIC CARE, WITH POTENTIAL TO SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE MATERNAL SAFETY, REDUCE PREVENTABLE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY, AND OPTIMIZE RESOURCE UTILIZATION NATIONALLY.

description: PERTURBATIONS OF FGF-DEPENDENT CROSS TALK BETWEEN MESENCHYME AND MESOTHELIUM AS CAUSES OF CONGENITAL ASPLENIA - ABSTRACT THE MAMMALIAN SPLEEN IS A LYMPHOID ORGAN THAT CONTRIBUTES TO IMMUNE RESPONSES AND ACTS AS A FILTER OF BLOOD PATHOGENS. IT HAS HEMATOPOIETIC FUNCTIONS IN DEVELOPMENT AND ALSO POSTNATALLY IN CASES OF BONE MARROW FAILURE AND INFECTIONS. ISOLATED CONGENITAL ASPLENIA (ICA) IS THE ONLY KNOWN BIRTH DEFECT INVOLVING SOLELY THE SPLEEN, WHICH DOES NOT FORM, WITHOUT OTHER ABNORMALITIES. ICA IS A RARE, BUT UNDERDIAGNOSED, CONGENITAL DISEASE. IN THE ABSENCE OF INFECTIONS, IT IS SILENT. HOWEVER, INFECTIONS OFTEN LEAD TO SUDDEN DEATH OF NEWBORNS AND CHILDREN WITH ICA. DESPITE THE DEVASTATING CONSEQUENCES OF ASPLENIA, THE MECHANISMS THAT UNDERLIE SPLENIC ANLAGE DEVELOP- MENT ARE STILL POORLY UNDERSTOOD AND UNDERSTUDIED. SPLEEN DEVELOPMENT RELIES ON CELL INTERACTIONS BETWEEN THE MESENCHYME THAT WILL GIVE RISE TO THE STROMA AND THE MESOTHELIUM THAT WILL FORM THE CAPSULE. USING MOUSE MODELS, WE REPORTED TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR-DIRECTED REGULATORY NETWORKS ESSENTIAL FOR SPLEEN DEVELOPMENT. A RE- CENT STUDY FURTHER SHOWED THAT MOUSE EMBRYOS WITH CONSTITUTIVE LOSS-OF-FUNCTION (LOF) OF THE SIGNALING MOLE- CULE FGF9 EXHIBIT PANCREATIC DEFECTS AND ASPLENIA, WHICH WAS NOT CHARACTERIZED. TO UNCOVER THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING FGF-DEPENDENT SPLEEN PHENOTYPES, WE HAVE INCORPORATED NEW EXPLORATIONS OF FGF SIGNALING IN SPLENIC DEVELOPMENT. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA REVEAL THAT: 1) CONSTITUTIVE OR CONDITIONAL LOF OF FGF GENES CAUSES MURINE SPLEEN DEFECTS, WITH LOSS OR DOWNREGULATION OF TLX1 AND NKX2-5, ESSENTIAL SPLEEN REGULATORS; 2) FGF SIGNALING CONTROLS THE CROSSTALK BETWEEN THE SPLENIC FGF9+ MESOTHELIAL CELL CLUSTER AND THE NKX2-5+ MESENCHY- MAL CELL CLUSTER (ENRICHED FOR FGFR1 TRANSCRIPTS), IDENTIFIED BY SINGLE CELL RNASEQ OF THE ANLAGE; 3) SPLENIC FGF EFFECTOR GENES HAVE FUNCTIONAL ROLES IN ATTRACTING ENDOTHELIAL AND HEMATOPOIETIC CELLS; 4) EXPRESSION OF FGF PATHWAY GENES IS CONSERVED IN HUMAN EMBRYONIC SPLEENS; AND 5) THE NR2F2 GENE, AN FGF EFFECTOR REQUIRED FOR MURINE SPLEEN FORMATION, CARRIES A PREDICTED PATHOGENIC MUTATION IN A PATIENT FROM A COHORT OF ICA CASES. BASED ON THESE RESULTS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT PERTURBATIONS OF FGF-DEPENDENT CROSSTALK BETWEEN MAMMALIAN SPLENIC MESOTHELIUM AND MESENCHYME CAUSE DEFECTS IN SPLEEN DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTION. WE FURTHER POSIT THAT LESIONS OF FGF PATHWAY EFFECTOR GENES CAN RESULT IN SPLEEN DEFECTS IN MICE AND HUMANS. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS VIA THESE AIMS: AIM 1: DETERMINE THE REQUIREMENTS OF THE FGF PATHWAY IN SPLEEN SPECIFICATION AND MORPHOGENESIS USING NEW CONDITIONAL LOF MOUSE MODELS. AIM 2: ESTABLISH HOW FGF SIGNALING IN SPLENIC MESENCHYME MEDIATES ENDOTHELIAL AND HEMATOPOIETIC CELL COLONIZATION CRITICAL FOR SPLEEN FUNCTION. AIM 3: IDEN- TIFY NEW MUTATIONS OF FGF PATHWAY GENES IN HUMAN ICA AND VALIDATE THEM IN THE MOUSE. THIS MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH, BASED ON THE STUDY OF NEW MOUSE LINES AND OF THE ONLY COHORT OF INTERNATIONAL ICA CASES, WILL UN- COVER MECHANISMS UNDERLYING ROLES OF FGF SIGNALING IN SPLEEN DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTION. THIS RESEARCH WILL FURTHER ELUCIDATE FGF9 TEMPORAL REQUIREMENTS AND SPECIFIC ROLES OF THE FGF9 LIGAND VERSUS ITS RECEPTORS, WHILE ALSO IDENTIFYING NEW MARKERS FOR SCREENING AND MOLECULAR DIAGNOSIS OF ICA, A SILENT AND LETHAL BIRTH DEFECT.

description: MAKING HEALTHY BABIES: HOLISTIC EVALUATION AND OPTIMIZATION OF TARGETED NANOMEDICINES TO TREAT PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION IN COMMON PREGNANCY COMPLICATIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION IS THE MAJOR UNDERLYING CAUSE OF THE SERIOUS PREGNANCY COMPLICATIONS PREECLAMPSIA (PE), INTRAUTERINE GROWTH RESTRICTION (IUGR) AND STILLBIRTH, WHICH AFFECT UP TO 15% OF PREGNANCIES IN THE US. NO TREATMENTS ARE AVAILABLE, LEAVING CLINICIANS RELIANT ON PRENATAL MONITORING AND EARLY DELIVERY, WHICH CAN FURTHER EXACERBATE ADVERSE MATERNAL AND INFANT OUTCOMES. DEVELOPING NEW THERAPEUTICS FOR USE IN PREGNANCY IS HAMPERED BY THE POTENTIAL RISK OF HARMFUL SIDE EFFECTS AND TERATOGENESIS, SEVERELY LIMITING INVESTMENT AND PROGRESS IN THIS AREA. TO ADDRESS THIS ROADBLOCK, WE HAVE CREATED TARGETED NANOPARTICLES DECORATED WITH PLACENTAL HOMING PEPTIDES, WHICH CAN SELECTIVELY DELIVER A WIDE RANGE OF DRUGS DIRECTLY TO THE PLACENTA, BUT DO NOT CROSS TO THE BABY. THE OVERARCHING AIM OF THIS PROJECT IS TO CONDUCT ROBUST PHARMACOKINETIC/ PHARMACODYNAMIC (PK/PD), SAFETY AND EFFICACY STUDIES TO QUANTIFY, OPTIMIZE AND MODEL THE TRUE BENEFITS OF THIS PLACENTAL-SPECIFIC DRUG DELIVERY APPROACH. USING WELL-CHARACTERIZED MOUSE MODELS OF HEALTHY PREGNANCY AND DIET-INDUCED PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION, HUMAN PLACENTAL EXPLANT CULTURES AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING, WE WILL COMPREHENSIVELY ASSESS THE BIODISTRIBUTION AND ACTIONS OF THREE DRUGS WITH PROVEN EFFICACY TO TREAT PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION: ASPIRIN, MELATONIN AND SE175. WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT ADMINISTRATION OF THESE DRUGS IN TARGETED LIPOSOMES DECORATED WITH THE WELL-CHARACTERIZED PLACENTAL HOMING PEPTIDE IRGD WILL INCREASE THEIR SAFETY, EFFICACY AND UTEROPLACENTAL-SPECIFIC DELIVERY, COMPARED TO ADMINISTRATION OF THE FREE DRUG. WE WILL PERFORM BIODISTRIBUTION STUDIES IN MICE TO QUANTIFY AND MODEL CHANGES IN THE DRUG CONCENTRATIONS IN MATERNAL, PLACENTAL AND PUP TISSUES OVER TIME. WE WILL ALSO PERFORM A TREATMENT STUDY TO COMPARE THE EFFECTS OF SYSTEMIC VERSUS TARGETED DELIVERY OF DRUGS ON (I) PLACENTAL STRUCTURE, GENE AND PROTEIN EXPRESSION, AND LEVELS OF PLACENTAL INFLAMMATION AND OXIDATIVE STRESS, (II) PUP OUTCOMES AND ANTHROPOMETRIC MEASUREMENTS, AND (III) INFLAMMATORY BIOMARKERS IN MATERNAL AND PUP PLASMA, TO ASSESS THE EXTENT OF RESCUE OF PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION. USING DATA FROM OUR IN VIVO STUDIES, WE WILL BUILD COMPUTATIONAL MODELS OF DRUG/LIPOSOME TISSUE DISTRIBUTION AND CLEARANCE OVER TIME, THEN INCORPORATE UPTAKE DATA FROM HUMAN PLACENTAL EXPLANT CULTURES TO CREATE PHYSIOLOGICAL-BASED PHARMACOKINETIC (PBPK) MODELS, WHICH WILL PREDICT THE LIPOSOME CONCENTRATIONS AND DOSING STRATEGIES REQUIRED TO ACHIEVE OPTIMAL THERAPEUTIC RESPONSES IN RODENTS, NON-HUMAN PRIMATES AND HUMANS. THIS RESEARCH SUPPORTS THE MISSION OF NICHD TO DEVELOP SAFE AND EFFECTIVE PLACENTAL-SPECIFIC THERAPEUTICS FOR THE TREATMENT OF PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION. ACCURATE QUANTITATION OF MATERNAL, PLACENTAL AND PUP DRUG DISTRIBUTION AND CLEARANCE, AS WELL AS THE GLOBAL AND PLACENTAL-SPECIFIC DRUG EFFECTS OBSERVED, IS IMPERATIVE TO FACILITATE DATA-DRIVEN APPROACHES TO BETTER INFORM THE DESIGN AND SUCCESS OF FUTURE PRE-CLINICAL AND CLINICAL PREGNANCY STUDIES, A KEY HURDLE THAT CURRENTLY IMPEDES CLINICAL TRANSLATION OF OBSTETRIC THERAPEUTICS.
