description: CHILDHOOD MALTREATMENT, ACCELERATED BIOLOGICAL AGING AND COGNITIVE FUNCTION AT MIDLIFE: A BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL STUDY ACROSS THE LIFESPAN - PROJECT SUMMARY EMERGING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT CHILDHOOD ABUSE AND TRAUMA INCREASE THE RISK OF ACCELERATED BIOLOGICAL AGING AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT IN ADULTHOOD. YET, THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THESE ASSOCIATIONS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD, PARTICULARLY IN MIDLIFE, A CRITICAL PERIOD WHEN AGING PROCESSES AND CUMULATIVE LIFE EXPOSURES MAY CONVERGE TO SHAPE LONG-TERM HEALTH, INCLUDING ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD). THIS PROJECT USES A DEVELOPMENTAL LIFESPAN PERSPECTIVE TO EXAMINE PATHWAYS THROUGH WHICH CHILDHOOD MALTREATMENT (CM) MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH ACCELERATED BIOLOGICAL AGING AND COGNITIVE OUTCOMES, INCLUDING PSYCHOSOCIAL AND INFLAMMATORY PATHWAYS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CM ALTERS THE EARLY ENVIRONMENT IN WAYS THAT DISRUPT HEALTHY DEVELOPMENT ACROSS THE LIFESPAN, INITIATING A CASCADE OF RISK THAT MAY INCREASE THE LIKELIHOOD OF ACCELERATED BIOLOGICAL AGING AND COGNITIVE DECLINE. WE FURTHER HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE MANIFESTATION OF THESE DISRUPTIONS DIFFERS BY SEX, DUE TO WELL-ESTABLISHED DIFFERENCES IN STRESS-RESPONSE BIOLOGY. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW ADVERSE PSYCHOSOCIAL FACTORS IN EMERGING ADULTHOOD, INCLUDING ELEVATED STRESS, DEPRESSION, AND POOR RELATIONSHIP QUALITY WITH PARENTS, FREQUENTLY OBSERVED AMONG CM SURVIVORS—CONTRIBUTE TO INCREASED INFLAMMATION DURING EARLY ADULTHOOD, THEREBY HEIGHTENING THE RISK FOR ACCELERATED BIOLOGICAL AGING AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT IN MIDLIFE. LEVERAGING DATA FROM THE NATIONAL LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF ADOLESCENT TO ADULT HEALTH (ADD HEALTH), A NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE COHORT FOLLOWED FROM ADOLESCENCE (AGES 12-19) INTO MIDLIFE (AGES 39-51), WE WILL USE STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELING TO TEST THESE PATHWAYS AND EVALUATE SEX-SPECIFIC PATTERNS. THIS RESEARCH SUPPORTS THE GROWING FOCUS ON MIDLIFE AS A CRITICAL OPPORTUNITY TO IDENTIFY MODIFIABLE FACTORS AND INTERVENTION TARGETS BEFORE THE ONSET OF AGE-RELATED DISEASE, INCLUDING ADRD. FINDINGS WILL DEEPEN UNDERSTANDING OF HOW EARLY ADVERSITY SHAPES AGING AND UNCOVER POTENTIAL SEX-SPECIFIC PATHWAY DIFFERENCES, WHILE INFORMING FUTURE RESEARCH, CLINICAL PRACTICE, AND PUBLIC POLICY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PRECISE CHARACTERIZATION OF SELECTIVE MOTOR CONTROL IN CEREBRAL PALSY - CEREBRAL PALSY (CP) IS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF PHYSICAL DISABILITY IN CHILDREN AND VARIABILITY IN TREATMENT RESPONSE IS UNACCEPTABLY HIGH. MUCH OF THIS VARIABILITY MAY BE EXPLAINED BY THE FAILURE OF CURRENT PRACTICE TO MATCH TREATMENTS TO INDIVIDUAL PATTERNS OF MOTOR CONTROL IMPAIRMENT. DESPITE BEING THE UNIVERSAL DEFICIT IN CP, IMPAIRMENT IN SELECTIVE MOTOR CONTROL (SMC) IS NOT ROUTINELY MEASURED AND EVEN WHEN MEASURED, EXISTING SCALES LACK PRECISION TO CHARACTERIZE INDIVIDUAL VARIABILITY AND GUIDE TREATMENT. PERSONALIZED TREATMENT APPROACHES FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH CP WILL REMAIN UNATTAINABLE WITHOUT THE ABILITY TO PRECISELY CHARACTERIZE THE TYPES AND DEGREES OF IMPAIRMENTS IN SMC. IMPAIRED NEUROMOTOR CONTROL IN CP CAUSES EXCESS ACTIVATION OF MUSCLES NOT NEEDED FOR THE TASK, OFTEN CALLED OVERFLOW, WHICH DISRUPTS THE COORDINATION OF MOVEMENT AND IMPAIRS PHYSICAL FUNCTION. SOME OF THIS EXCESS MUSCLE ACTIVATION CAN BE FURTHER DESCRIBED (DEPENDING ON ITS LOCATION AND LATERALITY) AS CO-ACTIVATION, MIRRORING, OR SYNERGISTIC MOVEMENT – AND THESE DISTINCTIONS MAY BE CRITICAL TO GUIDE TREATMENT PRESCRIPTIONS. THIS WORK IS PARTICULARLY IMPORTANT FOR YOUNG CHILDREN WITH CP WHOSE IMPAIRMENTS IN MOTOR CONTROL MAY BE MORE AMENABLE TO TREATMENT THAN IN OLDER CHILDREN. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO DEVELOP PERSONALIZED MEASURES THAT PREDICT TREATMENT RESPONSE AND GUIDE PERSONALIZED TREATMENT DECISIONS FOR CHILDREN WITH CP. WE HAVE ESTABLISHED THE FEASIBILITY OF A NEW METHODOLOGICAL APPROACH THAT QUANTIFIES MUSCLE ACTIVATION PATTERNS USING ELECTROMYOGRAPHY PAIRED WITH BIOFEEDBACK DURING SINGLE-JOINT MOVEMENT. THE APPROACH RESULTS IN FOUR INDEX VALUES OF SMC (COACTIVATION, MIRRORING, SYNERGY AND TOTAL OVERFLOW) FOR EACH OF SIX LOWER LIMB JOINT ACTIONS (HIP EXTENSION, HIP ABDUCTION, KNEE EXTENSION, KNEE FLEXION, ANKLE DORSIFLEXION AND ANKLE PLANTARFLEXION). THE BIOFEEDBACK GAME MAINTAINS THE CHILD'S ENGAGEMENT WHILE PROVIDING RIGOROUS STANDARDIZATION OF SUB-MAXIMAL EFFORT ON EACH OF THE SIX TASKS. OUR PRELIMINARY OBSERVATIONS SUGGEST LARGE DIFFERENCES BETWEEN CHILDREN WITH CP AND THEIR TYPICALLY DEVELOPING PEERS AND STRONG RELATIONS TO MOTOR FUNCTION FOR SEVERAL SMC INDICES, BUT AS EXPECTED, WITH WIDE VARIATION BETWEEN INDIVIDUAL CHILDREN WITH CP. THE NEXT PHASE OF THE WORK IS TO IDENTIFY WHICH MEASURES ARE MOST REPEATABLE AND INFORMATIVE, AND THUS MOST LIKELY TO PREDICT TREATMENT RESPONSE. THE OBJECTIVE OF THE PROPOSED WORK IS TO PRECISELY CHARACTERIZE SMC IN YOUNG CHILDREN WITH AND WITHOUT CP AGED 2-7 YEARS AND EVALUATE THE METRICS FOR REPEATABILITY, INTERNAL CONSISTENCY (AIM 1) AND DISCRIMINATIVE VALIDITY (AIM 2). WE WILL ALSO IDENTIFY PATTERNS OF MOTOR PERFORMANCE BASED ON TYPE, LOCATION, AND DEGREE OF SMC IMPAIRMENT WITHIN THE CP COHORT USING A MACHINE LEARNING CLUSTERING APPROACH AND INTERPRETED IN RELATION TO THE NORMATIVE DATASET AND TO EXISTING CLINICAL MEASURES (AIM 3). CHARACTERIZING THE TYPE, LOCATION AND DEGREE OF INDIVIDUAL SMC IMPAIRMENT IN CHILDREN WITH CP, ACCOMPANIED BY A NORMATIVE DATABASE FROM AGE-MATCHED PEERS, WILL ESTABLISH A FOUNDATION FOR PERSONALIZED MEASUREMENT TO GUIDE INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT PLANNING FOR CP AND SUPPORTS THE NICHD MISSION TO OPTIMIZE ABILITIES FOR ALL PEOPLE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NON-INVASIVE SPINAL STIMULATION TO REDUCE SPASTICITY AND IMPROVE MOBILITY FOR CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL PALSY - PROJECT SUMMARY CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL PALSY EXPERIENCE SPASTICITY AND OTHER NEUROMUSCULAR IMPAIRMENTS WHICH NEGATIVELY AFFECT MOBILITY AND ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING. CURRENT SPASTICITY MANAGEMENT APPROACHES REQUIRE INVASIVE SURGERIES LIKE SELECTIVE DORSAL RHIZOTOMY THAT PERMANENTLY SEVERS SENSORY PATHWAYS, OR MEDICATIONS LIKE BACLOFEN THAT CAN HAVE SUBSTANTIAL SIDE-EFFECTS. THESE INTERVENTIONS DISRUPT SENSORY FEEDBACK AND WEAKEN MUSCLES, SOMETIMES REQUIRING MONTHS OF REHABILITATION TO REGAIN PRE-INTERVENTION LEVELS OF FUNCTION. THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR NON-INVASIVE INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE SPASTICITY FOR CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL PALSY. HERE WE PROPOSE TO CONDUCT A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL TO EVALUATE THE INDIVIDUAL AND COMBINED EFFECTS OF SPINAL CORD STIMULATION AND INTENSIVE TREADMILL TRAINING SPECIFICALLY DESIGNED FOR CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL PALSY. OUR NEUROMODULATION APPROACH IS DELIVERED THROUGH THE SKIN OVER THE LUMBAR SPINAL CORD TO TARGET PRIMARY SENSORY AFFERENTS, WHICH OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES HAVE FOUND RESULTS IN SUBSTANTIAL AND LASTING REDUCTIONS IN SPASTICITY. IN THE PROPOSED RESEARCH, WE WILL RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF COMBINING SPINAL CORD STIMULATION WITH SHORT- BURST LOCOMOTOR TREADMILL TRAINING ON SPASTICITY THROUGH A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL FOR CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL PALSY. WE WILL QUANTIFY CHANGES IN SPASTICITY AND GAIT FOR CHILDREN THAT UNDERGO 24-SESSIONS (3X/WEEK FOR 8 WEEKS) OF EITHER WITH OR WITHOUT SPINAL STIMULATION. WE WILL ALSO EVALUATE SUSTAINED EFFECTS FOR 6-MONTHS OF FOLLOW-UP. WE WILL MEASURE CHANGES IN MOBILITY THROUGH BOTH QUANTITATIVE GAIT ANALYSIS AND WEARABLE SENSORS TO MONITOR COMMUNITY WALKING. FINALLY, WE WILL EXAMINE THE LIVED EXPERIENCES OF CHILDREN AND CAREGIVERS THROUGH SEMI-STRUCTURED INTERVIEWS TO UNDERSTAND HOW NEUROMODULATION AND TREADMILL TRAINING MAY SUPPORT THEIR GOALS FOR MOBILITY AND PARTICIPATION. TOGETHER, THIS RESEARCH WILL TEST NOVEL INTERVENTIONS FOR REDUCING SPASTICITY, WITH THE GOAL OF TRANSLATING NON-INVASIVE TREATMENT STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH CEREBRAL PALSY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REDUCING HARM FOR HOSPITALIZED CHILDREN THROUGH A HEALTH IT INTERVENTION TO ENHANCE FAMILY-CENTERED ROUNDING: A MULTISITE HYBRID TRIAL OF Q-ROUNDS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT HARMFUL MEDICAL ERRORS AFFECT MORE THAN 70,000 HOSPITALIZED CHILDREN EACH YEAR, UP TO 60% PREVENTABLE. FAMILY-CENTERED ROUNDS (FCRS) ARE BEDSIDE, DAILY DISCUSSIONS WHERE FAMILIES, NURSES, AND CLINICIANS JOINTLY REVIEW THE CARE PLAN AND MAKE DECISIONS TOGETHER. ENDORSED BY THE AMERICAN ACADEMY OF PEDIATRICS AS STANDARD PRACTICE SINCE 2012, FCRS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH FEWER HARMFUL ERRORS AND BETTER FAMILY AND NURSE EXPERIENCE; YET MORE THAN HALF OF ROUNDS STILL LACK EITHER A FAMILY MEMBER OR A NURSE. IN OUR MULTICENTER WORK, ROUNDING ENCOUNTERS WITH AT LEAST ONE FAMILY MEMBER AND A NURSE PRESENT WERE ASSOCIATED WITH ~40% FEWER HARMFUL ERRORS, WITH EVEN GREATER BENEFITS FOR CHILDREN WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS. UNFORTUNATELY, PARTICIPATION REMAINS INCONSISTENT DUE TO UNPREDICTABLE TIMING, DISTANCE AND FINANCIAL CONSTRAINTS, AND LIMITED LANGUAGE ACCESS. TO ADDRESS THESE BARRIERS, WE DEVELOPED Q-ROUNDS, AN EHR-INTEGRATED TOOL THAT SENDS REAL-TIME ROUNDING NOTIFICATIONS SO FAMILIES, NURSES, AND INTERPRETERS CAN JOIN IN PERSON OR REMOTELY. IN A SINGLE-CENTER NICU, Q-ROUNDS WAS ASSOCIATED WITH A 210% INCREASE IN NURSE PRESENCE AND A 115% INCREASE IN FAMILY PRESENCE, WITH >12,500 ROUNDING ENCOUNTERS CONDUCTED WITH Q-ROUNDS OVER THE LAST TWO YEARS. WHILE Q-ROUNDS HAS SHOWN PROMISE IN A SINGLE-CENTER NICU, ITS IMPACT ON PATIENT SAFETY AND USE IN GENERAL PEDIATRIC INPATIENT SETTINGS HAS NOT BEEN EVALUATED. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO ASSESS THE IMPACT OF Q- ROUNDS ON HARMFUL MEDICAL ERRORS (PRIMARY OUTCOME) AND ON FAMILY/NURSE PRESENCE, FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, AND HOSPITAL EXPERIENCE, AND TO ASSESS IMPLEMENTATION ON GENERAL PEDIATRIC SERVICES AT TWO DEMOGRAPHICALLY DIVERSE CHILDREN’S HOSPITALS (UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN AMERICAN FAMILY CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL AND UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA DAVIS CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL). WE WILL CONDUCT A HYBRID TYPE 1 EFFECTIVENESS– IMPLEMENTATION STUDY USING A PRAGMATIC INTERRUPTED TIME-SERIES DESIGN WITH A MULTIPLE-BASELINE, STAGGERED, RANDOMIZED ROLLOUT ACROSS FOUR SERVICES (TWO PER SITE). MULTI-SOURCE SAFETY SURVEILLANCE (CHART REVIEW, FAMILY SAFETY INTERVIEW, PROVIDER/INCIDENT REPORTS) WITH BLINDED ADJUDICATION WILL QUANTIFY HARMFUL ERRORS PRE- AND POST-IMPLEMENTATION. OUR AIMS INCLUDE: (1) TEST WHETHER Q-ROUNDS IS ASSOCIATED WITH A ≥20% REDUCTION IN HARMFUL ERRORS AND WITH INCREASED FAMILY/NURSE PRESENCE (OBSERVATIONS) AND IMPROVED FAMILY ACTIVATION AND HOSPITAL EXPERIENCE (DISCHARGE SURVEYS); (2) DETERMINE WHETHER EFFECTS VARY BY LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY, SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS, AND RURALITY; AND (3) EVALUATE IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES (E.G., ACCEPTABILITY, FEASIBILITY, FIDELITY, SUSTAINMENT) TO GUIDE SCALE-UP. THIS MULTISITE STUDY WILL PRODUCE REAL-WORLD EVIDENCE ON A SCALABLE DIGITAL STRATEGY TO REDUCE PREVENTABLE HARM AND STRENGTHEN FAMILY-CENTERED CARE FOR HOSPITALIZED CHILDREN. AS THE FIRST MULTISITE STUDY OF A HEALTH IT SOLUTION DESIGNED TO OPTIMIZE ROUNDING PARTICIPATION, IT WILL YIELD ACTIONABLE STRATEGIES FOR INTEGRATING Q-ROUNDS INTO HOSPITAL WORKFLOWS AND ADVANCE NICHD PRIORITIES IN PEDIATRIC PATIENT SAFETY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPACT OF SEMAGLUTIDE ON MATERNAL-FETAL HEALTH OUTCOMES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT OBESITY PREVALENCE HAS BEEN STEADILY RISING IN THE U.S., INCLUDING AMONG PREGNANT WOMEN. ACCUMULATING EVIDENCE LINKS MATERNAL OBESITY TO INCREASED RISK FOR ADVERSE PREGNANCY OUTCOMES AND, IN THEIR OFFSPRING, FOR OBESITY AND OTHER CHRONIC DISEASES. MOREOVER, INTERVENTION STRATEGIES TARGETING PERINATAL WEIGHT MANAGEMENT HAVE YIELDED DISAPPOINTING RESULTS, SHIFTING FOCUS TO THE PRECONCEPTION PERIOD. INTENSIVE LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS FOR WEIGHT LOSS ARE MODEST IN EFFECT, RESULTING IN AN INITIAL AVERAGE 8% WEIGHT LOSS THAT BACK-TRACKS TO APPROXIMATELY 4% LONG-TERM. METABOLIC-BARIATRIC SURGERY ACHIEVES WEIGHT LOSSES AVERAGING BETWEEN 20% AND 30% OF TOTAL BODY WEIGHT AND IMPROVEMENTS IN MATERNAL-FETAL OUTCOMES BUT WILL HAVE LIMITED APPLICATION TO WOMEN WITH THE MOST SEVERE OBESITY. ON THE OTHER HAND, HIGHLY EFFECTIVE OBESITY MEDICATIONS OF THE GLUCAGON- LIKE PEPTIDE 1 RECEPTOR AGONIST (GLP-1RA) CLASS ACHIEVE AVERAGE TOTAL WEIGHT LOSSES OF 15% OR GREATER. WITH INDICATIONS FOR BOTH DIABETES AND OBESITY IN WOMEN STARTING AT A BMI OF 27 KG/M2, THE GLP-1RA SEMAGLUTIDE HAS THE POTENTIAL FOR MILLIONS OF WOMEN TO IMPROVE PRECONCEPTION DIABETES MANAGEMENT AND ACHIEVE WEIGHT LOSS APPROACHING WHAT CAN BE ACHIEVE WITH BARIATRIC SURGERY. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO DETERMINE IF PRECONCEPTION WEIGHT LOSS IN A MODEL OF MATERNAL OBESITY USING SEMAGLUTIDE, WHICH IS THEN CONTINUED THROUGH PREGNANCY AND WEANING TO AVOID POTENTIAL WEIGHT REGAIN IS SAFE AND EFFECTIVE FOR MOTHERS AND CAN REDUCE THEIR OFFSPRING'S LONG-TERM RISK OF OBESITY AND OBESITY- RELATED COMPLICATIONS. THIS WILL BE COMPARED TO CESSATION OF SEMAGLUTIDE THE INSTANCE PREGNANCY IS CONFIRMED, POTENTIALLY LEADING TO RECURRENCE OF OBESITY OR EXCESSIVE GESTATIONAL WEIGHT GAIN. WE WILL UTILIZE A WELL CHARACTERIZED NON-HUMAN PRIMATE MODEL OF MATERNAL OBESITY TO ADDRESS THE FOLLOWING RESEARCH QUESTIONS: COMPARED TO STOPPING IT AT THE TIME OF CONCEPTION, DOES PRECONCEPTION WEIGHT LOSS WITH SEMAGLUTIDE AND CONTINUATION DURING PREGNANCY 1) PROTECT AGAINST EXCESSIVE GESTATIONAL WEIGHT GAIN AND STILL ALLOW NORMAL PLACENTAL FUNCTION AND FETAL DEVELOPMENT; AND 2) IMPROVE OFFSPRING WEIGHT, BODY COMPOSITION, AND METABOLIC HEALTH. OUR UNIQUE ANIMAL RESOURCE WILL PROVIDE VITAL INFORMATION ON SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF PRECONCEPTION WEIGHT LOSS USING SEMAGLUTIDE ON MATERNAL HEALTH AND LONGER-TERM CHILD HEALTH OUTCOMES. FINDINGS FROM OUR STUDY WILL HAVE APPLICATION TO MILLIONS OF WOMEN ELIGIBLE FOR THIS MEDICATION FOR OBESITY, DIABETES, POLYCYSTIC OVARIAN SYNDROME, AND OBESITY-RELATED INFERTILITY AS WE ENTER THE ERA OF HIGHLY-EFFECTIVE ANTI-OBESITY MEDICATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISTIC INVESTIGATION OF TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENOME DYSREGULATION IN LEIOMYOMAS/UTERINE FIBROIDS - ABSTRACT UTERINE LEIOMYOMATA (UTERINE FIBROIDS OR LEIOMYOMAS) IS A MAJOR GYNECOLOGIC DISEASE AFFECTING UP TO 70% OF WOMEN, CAUSING SIGNIFICANT MORBIDITY SUCH AS BLEEDING, UTERINE STIFFNESS, PELVIC PAIN, AND INFERTILITY. THIS CONDITION IMPOSES SUBSTANTIAL CLINICAL, SOCIAL, EMOTIONAL, AND FINANCIAL BURDENS ON WOMEN AND THEIR FAMILIES. LEIOMYOMAS ARE BENIGN TUMORS CHARACTERIZED BY EXCESSIVE EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX (ECM) DEPOSITION. DESPITE THEIR PREVALENCE AND ASSOCIATED HEALTHCARE COSTS, THIS DISEASE REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD AND UNDERFUNDED. CURRENT NON-SURGICAL TREATMENTS HAVE SIGNIFICANT SIDE EFFECTS THAT LIMIT THEIR USE. WHILE GENETIC EVENTS DRIVE MANY DISEASES INCLUDING LEIOMYOMAS, THE EPIGENOME HAS RECENTLY EMERGED AS A CRUCIAL REGULATOR OF DISEASE MANIFESTATION. OUR PREVIOUS RESEARCH SHOWED THAT LEIOMYOMA SAMPLES WHEN COMPARED TO MYOMETRIAL TISSUES HAVE SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER HISTONE H3 LYSINE 27 ACETYLATION (H3K27AC EPIGENOMIC MARK) ON GENE PROMOTERS AND ENHANCERS, POTENTIALLY LEADING TO ALTERED EXPRESSION OF ECM GENES AND TUMORIGENESIS. TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE ROLE OF H3K27AC WHICH IS MEDIATED BY THE EP300/CBP COACTIVATORS, WE HAVE ESTABLISHED A REPRODUCIBLE LEIOMYOMA PATIENT-DERIVED PRECISION-CUT EX VIVO TISSUE EXPLANT CULTURE SYSTEM THAT CLOSELY MIMICS IN VIVO HUMAN CONDITIONS AND REPRESENTS A NON-ANIMAL ASSAY MODEL SYSTEM. PRELIMINARY EXPERIMENTS USING A SPECIFIC EPIGENOMIC INHIBITOR TARGETING EP300/CBP SHOWED PROFOUND EFFECTS ON LEIOMYOMA-ASSOCIATED GENES AND SIGNALING PATHWAYS. WE WILL INTEGRATE ADVANCED MOLECULAR AND GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES WITH BIOINFORMATICS AND THIS NOVEL EX VIVO TISSUE PLATFORM AND RECENTLY ENGINEERED HUMAN CELL- BASED STUDIES TO FURTHER EXPLORE EPIGENOME DYSREGULATION IN LEIOMYOMAS. THESE STUDIES ARE HIGHLY SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE THEY WILL IDENTIFY THE EPIGENOME AS A KEY DRIVER OF UTERINE TUMORIGENESIS AND FIBROSIS, WILL ADVANCE KNOWLEDGE, AND HELP ESTABLISH A FRAMEWORK TO ASSESS EPIGENOME- TARGETING DRUGS AND DEVELOP FUTURE THERAPEUTICS FOR LEIOMYOMAS. CONDUCTING THIS RESEARCH IN AN EXCEPTIONAL ENVIRONMENT WITH SCIENTIFIC LEADERS IN GYNECOLOGIC DISEASES WILL FURTHER ENHANCE THE IMPACT OF OUR WORK.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THIAMINE FOR RECOVERY IN VULNERABLE EARLY-LIFE INFECTIONS (THRIVE) - ABSTRACT INFANT INFECTIONS ARE A COMMON CAUSE OF DEATH GLOBALLY AND SURVIVORS FREQUENTLY EXPERIENCE PERMANENT SERIOUS SEQUELAE. FOR EXAMPLE, MENINGITIS IS THE MOST COMMON ETIOLOGY OF INFANT HYDROCEPHALUS GLOBALLY. HEARING LOSS, CEREBRAL PALSY AND NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT ARE ALSO COMMON. THESE NEUROLOGIC SEQUELAE ARE OFTEN DUE TO DIRECT IMPACTS OF THE BACTERIAL INFECTION ON THE BRAIN TISSUE BUT CAN ALSO BE CAUSED BY ALTERATIONS IN BLOOD FLOW, CYTOTOXICITY FROM THE IMMUNE RESPONSE AND FROM ALTERATIONS IN THE MICRONUTRIENT ENVIRONMENT RESULTING IN INJURY TO NEURONAL CELLS. SOME BACTERIA, SUCH AS PAENIBACILLUS THIAMINOLYTICUS, PRODUCE A THIAMINASE AND CAUSE SEVERE DESTRUCTION OF THE BRAIN TISSUE. THIAMINE SUPPLEMENTATION MAY IMPROVE NEUROLOGIC OUTCOMES FOLLOWING SEVERE EARLY-LIFE INFECTION AND THE IMPACT MAY VARY BY BASELINE THIAMINE STATUS OR WHETHER THE PATHOGEN PRODUCES A THIAMINASE. WE PROPOSE TO ADDRESS THESE IMPORTANT KNOWLEDGE GAPS THROUGH 3 INTEGRATED AIMS: FIRST, WE WILL DETERMINE BASELINE WHOLE BLOOD AND CEREBROSPINAL FLUID THIAMINE CONCENTRATIONS FOR HOSPITALIZED INFANTS WITH AND WITHOUT INVASIVE BACTERIAL INFECTIONS. FOR INFECTED INFANTS, WE WILL ALSO COMPARE THE BASELINE THIAMINE CONCENTRATIONS BEFORE AND AFTER TREATMENT (AIM 1). INFANTS WITH BACTEREMIA OR MENINGITIS WILL BE RANDOMIZED 1:1 TO RECEIVE STANDARD-OF-CARE ANTIBIOTIC THERAPY OR STANDARD-OF-CARE ANTIBIOTIC THERAPY PLUS THIAMINE SUPPLEMENTATION. WE WILL COMPARE NEURODEVELOPMENT AT 18 MONTHS OLD AS THE PRIMARY OUTCOMES ALONG WITH ADDITIONAL SECONDARY OUTCOMES AT HOSPITAL DISCHARGE AND AT 18 MONTHS (AIM 2). FINALLY, WE WILL COMPARE OUTCOMES FOR INFANTS WHO HAD INFECTIONS DUE TO A THIAMINASE-PRODUCING ORGANISM VS. THOSE WHOSE PATHOGEN DID NOT PRODUCE A THIAMINASE (AIM 3). THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IMPROVE OUTCOMES FOR INFANTS WITH INVASIVE BACTERIAL INFECTIONS BY PREVENTING DEATH AND NEURODEVELOPMENTAL IMPAIRMENT THROUGH AN IMPROVED UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLE OF THIAMINE IN THE TREATMENT OF SERIOUS PEDIATRIC INFECTIONS. THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS TO BRING IMPROVED HEALTH TO INDIVIDUAL PATIENTS WHILE ADDING TO OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE EPIDEMIOLOGY AND PATHOGENICITY OF SERIOUS BACTERIAL INFECTIONS IN INFANTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AUTISM-RELATED AUTOANTIBODIES AND IMMUNE DYSREGULATION: OUTCOMES IN BRAIN AND BEHAVIOR - THE HETEROGENEITY OF AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD) REMAINS THE CORE CHALLENGE IN DEVELOPING MODELS FOR UNDERSTANDING AND TREATING AUTISM. IDENTIFYING BIOLOGICALLY MEANINGFUL SUBGROUPS WITHIN THE AUTISM SPECTRUM IS NOW SEEN AS ESSENTIAL TO PROGRESS. THIS PRINCIPLE UNDERLIES THE FOUNDING MISSION OF THE AUTISM PHENOME PROJECT (APP), A LONGITUDINAL NATURAL HISTORY NEUROIMAGING STUDY THAT HAS PIONEERED IDENTIFICATION OF AUTISM NEUROPHENOTYPES. OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, MATERNAL AUTOANTIBODY-RELATED AUTISM (MAR) HAS EMERGED AS ONE OF THE MOST COMPELLING BIOLOGICALLY GROUNDED SUBTYPES. MAR IS DEFINED BY MATERNAL IGG ANTIBODIES THAT REACT WITH FETAL BRAIN PROTEINS DURING GESTATION (E.G., CRMP1, CRMP2, STIP1, GDA, NSE, YBOX). PRENATAL EXPOSURE TO MAR AUTOANTIBODIES OCCURS IN UP TO 20% OF AUTISTIC CHILDREN AND IS ENTIRELY ABSENT IN NON-AUTISTIC CHILDREN. THIS STRIKING SPECIFICITY OFFERS A HIGH-VALUE DIRECTION TO EXPLAIN AND ACCOUNT FOR A SIGNIFICANT PORTION OF AUTISM'S CAUSAL AND PHENOTYPIC HETEROGENEITY. PRELIMINARY HUMAN NEUROIMAGING INDICATES A DISTINCT MAR NEUROPHENOTYPE THAT CONSISTS OF EXTREME EARLY BRAIN OVERGROWTH AND SELECTIVE FRONTAL LOBE ENLARGEMENT. CONVERGENT ANIMAL MODELS DEMONSTRATE THAT MAR ANTIBODIES CROSS THE PLACENTA, BIND TO FETAL BRAIN, AND PRODUCE SEX-SPECIFIC ALTERATIONS IN BRAIN GROWTH, WHITE MATTER, AND NETWORK COORDINATION. WHILE PRECLINICAL MODELS HAVE PROVIDED GREAT INSIGHTS INTO MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF MAR ANTIBODIES, THERE HAVE BEEN NO COMPREHENSIVE HUMAN IMAGING STUDIES OF MAR CHILDREN. THE APP—A LONGITUDINAL COHORT OF AUTISTIC (N=395; 285 MALE, 128 FEMALE) AND TYPICALLY DEVELOPING (N=166; 92 MALE, 74 FEMALE) CHILDREN WITH MULTIMODAL NEUROIMAGING SPANNING 2-18 YEARS OF AGE, DEEP PHENOTYPING, AND BANKED MATERNAL/CHILD PLASMA—PROVIDES AN UNPARALLELED PLATFORM TO CLOSE THE TRANSLATIONAL GAP. OUR OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS IS THAT GESTATIONAL MAR EXPOSURE PERTURBS BRAIN DEVELOPMENT IN OFFSPRING, YIELDING A BIOLOGICALLY-GROUNDED SUBGROUP OF AUTISM WITH IDENTIFIABLE AND SEX-SPECIFIC PROFILES IN BRAIN, BEHAVIOR, AND IMMUNE FUNCTION. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DEFINE THE LONGITUDINAL STRUCTURAL NEUROPHENOTYPE OF MAR ACROSS DEVELOPMENT AND SEX, FOCUSING ON TOTAL BRAIN VOLUME AND FRONTAL, CORTICO-STRIATAL, AND CEREBELLAR REGIONS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER MAR EXPOSURE DISRUPTS COORDINATION OF BRAIN DEVELOPMENT USING MULTI-MODAL MRI TO ASSESS STRUCTURAL COVARIANCE, WHITE-MATTER CONNECTIVITY, AND FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY. IN AIM 3, WE WILL DEFINE THE BEHAVIORAL AND CLINICAL PHENOTYPE OF MAR BY EXAMINING TRAJECTORIES OF AUTISM SYMPTOM SEVERITY, COGNITIVE AND LANGUAGE DEVELOPMENT, ADAPTIVE FUNCTIONING, AND RESTRICTED/REPETITIVE BEHAVIORS. IN AIM 4, WE WILL EXAMINE WHETHER MAR EXPOSURE PREDICTS ALTERED PERIPHERAL CYTOKINE/CHEMOKINE PROFILES ACROSS DEVELOPMENT. THIS WILL BE THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE STUDY TO ESTABLISH THE NEUROBIOLOGY, BEHAVIORAL PHENOTYPE, AND IMMUNE PROFILE OF MAR+ AUTISTIC OFFSPRING, SETTING THE STAGE FOR TRANSLATING PRECLINICAL FINDINGS INTO FUTURE CLINICAL TREATMENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF MEDICATION RISK-BENEFIT IN AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE FOR HEALTHY PREGNANCIES (CARE-HP) - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ADVANCED TREATMENTS (ADVTX) SUCH AS BIOLOGICS AND JANUS KINASE INHIBITORS FOR PATIENTS WITH AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE (AID) HAVE GROWN RAPIDLY, BUT THERE IS LIMITED EVIDENCE ON THEIR OUTCOMES IN PREGNANCY. DECISIONS TO CONTINUE, STOP OR START ADVTX DURING PREGNANCY RELY ON A SMALL NUMBER OF OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES, MOSTLY CONDUCTED AMONG PATIENTS WITH INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE, THAT DO NOT CAPTURE THE FULL BREADTH OF OUTCOMES AND CLINICAL SCENARIOS TO DEFINE ADVTX BENEFIT-RISK. GIVEN THE COMPLEX INTERPLAY OF AUTOIMMUNITY AND REPRODUCTION, WITH SOME AIDS WORSENING AND OTHERS IMPROVING DURING PREGNANCY, THERE IS A NEED FOR CONDITION- SPECIFIC EVALUATIONS THAT COMPARE THE FULL BREADTH OF OUTCOMES AFFECTING MOTHER AND CHILD. SUCH BREADTH REQUIRES MASSIVE DATA REPOSITORIES AND SCALABLE APPROACHES PAIRED WITH SOPHISTICATED DESIGNS TO CAPTURE HETEROGENEOUS TREATMENT EFFECTS AND ACCELERATE THE AVAILABILITY OF CLINICALLY RELEVANT EVIDENCE. BUILDING ON OUR PRIOR WORK, WE PROPOSE A COMPREHENSIVE INVESTIGATION OF ADVTX CONSIDERING PREGNANCY, MATERNAL AND INFANT OUTCOMES. WE WILL USE THE METHODOLOGY DEVELOPED FOR DRUG EVALUATIONS IN PREGNANCY IN OUR ONGOING PROJECT BIG DATA APPROACHES FOR SAFE THERAPEUTICS IN HEALTHY PREGNANCIES (BOOST-HP), WHICH OPTIMIZES SAFETY ASSESSMENTS IN TWO STEPS: DATA-MINING, WHICH FACILITATES SIMULTANEOUS EXAMINATION OF THOUSANDS OF OUTCOMES, FOLLOWED BY CONFIRMATORY STUDIES; AND LEVERAGE OUR RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE, INCLUDING BILLING RECORDS FROM PRIVATE AND PUBLIC INSURANCE FOR >13M PREGNANCIES AND >92,000 AMONG WOMEN WITH AIDS. COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF MEDICATION RISK-BENEFIT IN AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE FOR HEALTHY PREGNANCIES (CARE-HP) AIMS TO CUT THROUGH SILOS OF SPECIALTY CARE BY INCLUDING KEY AIDS THAT RELY ON SIMILAR THERAPIES, ALLOWING FOR DISEASE-SPECIFIC AND DRUG CLASS-SPECIFIC ASSESSMENTS ACROSS A BROAD RANGE OF OUTCOMES. WE CONSIDER TWO CLINICALLY RELEVANT SCENARIOS: (A) HEAD-TO-HEAD COMPARISONS WITHIN ADVTX CLASSES OR SINGLE AGENTS OR VS. CONVENTIONAL DISEASE MODIFYING THERAPY, AND (B) ADVTX CONTINUATION VS. DISCONTINUATION. USING SOPHISTICATED METHODS FOR CONFOUNDING CONTROL AND ASSESSMENT OF TREATMENT EFFECT HETEROGENEITY ACROSS AIDS, THE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE TO: (1) EVALUATE THE RISK OF PREGNANCY LOSS FOLLOWING ADVTX USE; (2) SCAN FOR ADVTX ASSOCIATIONS WITH A BROAD RANGE OF MATERNAL PREGNANCY COMPLICATIONS, USING DATA-MINING METHODOLOGY, FOLLOWED BY FORMAL PHARMACOEPIDEMIOLOGIC STUDIES OF THE TOP TWO PRIORITIZED SIGNALS FROM DATA-MINING, AND FIVE PRE-SPECIFIED OUTCOMES (PRETERM BIRTHS, AID FLARES, HOSPITALIZATION, SERIOUS INFECTION, AND PREECLAMPSIA); (3) SCAN FOR ADVTX ASSOCIATIONS WITH CONGENITAL MALFORMATIONS AMONG AID-SPECIFIC MOTHER-INFANT LINKED COHORTS, FOLLOWED BY FORMAL PHARMACOEPIDEMIOLOGIC STUDIES OF THE TOP TWO PRIORITIZED SIGNALS GLEANED FROM DATA-MINING, AND FOUR PRE-SPECIFIED OUTCOMES (SMALL FOR GESTATIONAL AGE, SERIOUS INFECTIONS, AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER AND ATTENTION DEFICIT/HYPERACTIVITY DISORDER). OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO DEVELOP COMPREHENSIVE EVIDENCE ON ADVTX BENEFIT-RISK THAT CAN SUPPORT PERSONALIZED TREATMENT PLANS FOR PREGNANT PATIENTS WITH VARIOUS AIDS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LOWER LIMB HETERONYMOUS SPINAL REFLEXES AND MOTOR IMPAIRMENT AFTER STROKE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT AFTER A STROKE, IMPAIRED COORDINATION AND WEAKNESS OF LOWER LIMB MUSCLES ARE KEY BARRIERS TO RECOVERY OF WALKING AND BALANCE. CURRENT THERAPIES STRUGGLE TO IMPROVE THESE IMPAIRMENTS BECAUSE WE LACK A CLEAR NEURAL MECHANISM TO TARGET. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, WE WILL INVESTIGATE ALTERED CORTICAL CONTROL OF HETERONYMOUS REFLEX PATHWAYS AS A PLAUSIBLE, YET UNDERSTUDIED, MECHANISM CAPABLE OF CAUSING ABNORMAL COORDINATION AND FUNCTIONAL WEAKNESS AFTER STROKE. HETERONYMOUS SPINAL REFLEXES HAVE A UNIQUE ABILITY TO PROMOTE, OR IMPAIR, MOTOR COORDINATION ACROSS JOINTS AS EXCITATORY LENGTH AND INHIBITORY FORCE-RELATED FEEDBACK FROM A MUSCLE CAN ENHANCE (EXCITE) AND SUPPRESS (INHIBIT) MOTOR OUTPUT OF OTHER MUSCLES. NORMALLY, THE MOTOR CORTEX ADJUSTS THE MAGNITUDES OF THESE REFLEXES TO ENSURE TASK-APPROPRIATE COORDINATION. THUS, WE HYPOTHESIZE, SUPPORTED BY STRONG PRELIMINARY DATA, THAT AFTER CORTICAL DAMAGE, MODULATORY CONTROL IS IMPAIRED, CAUSING REFLEXES TO BECOME EXCESSIVE AND POORLY REGULATED. WE FOCUS ON REFLEXES FROM QUADRICEPS (Q) ONTO SOLEUS (SOL) BECAUSE, IN NEUROTYPICAL ADULTS, THESE REFLEXES ARE CORTICALLY MODULATED TO ENSURE THE MUSCLES ARE COORDINATED DURING STANDING AND WALKING. AFTER STROKE, HOWEVER, Q AND SOL ARE OFTEN COACTIVE AT THE WRONG TIME, AND SOL IS POORLY RECRUITED DURING BALANCE REACTIONS AND PROPULSION, DIRECTLY LIMITING BALANCE AND WALKING ABILITY. PI LYLE AND CO-IS KESAR AND TING WILL LEVERAGE THEIR EXPERTISE SPANNING SPINAL CIRCUITS AND NEUROMECHANICS TO TEST WHETHER THESE PERSISTENT IMPAIRMENTS POST-STROKE ARE DUE TO POORLY REGULATED HETERONYMOUS REFLEXES. WE WILL RIGOROUSLY EXAMINE Q TO SOL REFLEX MODULATION ACROSS STRATEGICALLY CHOSEN FUNCTIONAL CONTEXTS TO ESTABLISH MECHANISTIC LINKS TO CLINICALLY RELEVANT BEHAVIOR. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE HOW LIMB LOADING AND POSTURAL ORIENTATION INFLUENCE REFLEX MAGNITUDES TO CLARIFY MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE COMMON CLINICAL OBSERVATION OF INCREASED MOTOR IMPAIRMENT WHEN STANDING. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS IF STROKE DISRUPTS THE BRAIN’S CAPACITY TO MODULATE REFLEXES BASED ON TASK CONTEXT, ESSENTIAL FOR FUNCTIONING IN REAL-WORLD ENVIRONMENTS. AIM 3 WILL PROVIDE NOVEL MECHANISTIC INSIGHT INTO TWO DIFFICULT-TO-TREAT GAIT DEFICITS BY DETERMINING WHETHER ABNORMAL Q–SOL COACTIVATION IN EARLY STANCE POST-STROKE REFLECTS EXCESSIVE EXCITATION, AND WHETHER REDUCED PROPULSION AND GAIT SPEED REFLECT EXCESSIVE INHIBITION OF SOL IN LATE STANCE. ACROSS AIMS, WE WILL CORRELATE REFLEX MAGNITUDES WITH CLINICAL MEASURES OF DYNAMIC BALANCE AND WALKING SPEED TO ASSESS THEIR FUNCTIONAL RELEVANCE. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA PROVIDES STRONG SUPPORT FOR ALTERED REFLEX MODULATION IN STROKE SURVIVORS AS A NEURAL MECHANISM UNDERLYING POORER DYNAMIC BALANCE AND SLOWER GAIT. WE ANTICIPATE THIS WORK WILL GENERATE NEW OPPORTUNITIES FOR PERSONALIZED TREATMENT OF A NEURAL MECHANISM LINKED TO IMPAIRMENT (TOO MUCH EXCITATION/INHIBITION) VIA TARGETED NEUROMODULATION APPROACHES TO RESTORE FUNCTION AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR STROKE SURVIVORS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: VASCULAR MACHINE LEARNING OPTIMIZED PROGNOSTIC AND TREATMENT PATHWAYS IN HUMAN FETAL GROWTH RESTRICTION - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT ABNORMAL MATERNAL-FETAL BLOOD FLOW IS A SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTOR TO ADVERSE PERINATAL OUTCOMES, LIKE HYPERTENSIVE PREGNANCY DISORDERS AND FETAL GROWTH RESTRICTION (FGR). FGR AFFECTS APPROXIMATELY 30 MILLION FETUSES GLOBALLY, WITH A PREVALENCE OF 23.8%. FGR IS ASSOCIATED WITH MANY SHORT- AND LONG-TERM COMPLICATIONS SUCH AS PREMATURITY- RELATED ISSUES (NECROTIZING ENTEROCOLITIS, CHRONIC LUNG DISEASE, HYPOXIC BRAIN INJURY), PERINATAL MORTALITY, METABOLIC DISEASES LIKE DIABETES, AND CARDIOVASCULAR CONDITIONS SUCH AS CHRONIC HYPERTENSION. THE SOCIETY FOR MATERNAL FETAL MEDICINE RECOMMENDS MANAGING FGR BASED ON THE SYSTOLIC-TO-DIASTOLIC (S/D) VELOCITY RATIO OF UMBILICAL ARTERY DOPPLER FLOW (UADF). A HIGH S/D RATIO AND LOSS OF DIASTOLIC FLOW INDICATE RESISTANCE AND POOR FETAL PERFUSION. OBSTETRIC PROVIDERS FACE CHALLENGES IN APPROPRIATELY TIMING DELIVERY AND IMPROVING INTACT SURVIVAL AMID LIMITED MITIGATION OPTIONS. DETERMINING THE OPTIMAL GESTATIONAL AGE FOR DELIVERY TO MAXIMIZE SURVIVAL. HOWEVER, THE TIMING OF DELIVERY BASED ON CURRENT UADF FINDINGS VARIES DUE TO NUANCES MISSED IN THE S/D RATIO. MACHINE LEARNING (ML) CAN DETECT SUBTLE CHANGES IN BLOOD FLOW THAT MORE ACCURATELY PREDICT OUTCOMES. OUR PUBLISHED ML UADF ANALYSES SHOW THAT ML PREDICTS FGR DEVELOPMENT MORE ACCURATELY THAN CLINICAL DATA AND THE S/D RATIO ALONE. ALSO, MANAGING FGR IS COMPLICATED BY THE LIMITED MITIGATION OPTIONS DUE TO ITS MULTIPLE ETIOLOGIES. FGR’S ETIOLOGY PARTLY INVOLVES VASCULAR DYSFUNCTION AS EVIDENCED BY ABNORMAL UADF, THOUGH A CENTRAL MECHANISM IS NOT YET CLEAR. SPARSE DATA EXIST ON UMBILICAL ARTERY (UA) MECHANISMS AND HOW THESE MECHANISMS INFLUENCE UADF. YET, MODELS OF FGR IN WHICH UA FUNCTION IS EXPERIMENTALLY IMPROVED DEMONSTRATE IMPROVEMENTS IN FETAL GROWTH AND OUTCOMES. ONE POTENTIAL MECHANISM INVOLVES ARGININE VASOPRESSIN (AVP). IN OUR AVP INFUSION MOUSE MODEL OF VASCULARLY MEDIATED FGR WE HAVE DEMONSTRATED ABNORMAL PLACENTAL FUNCTION AND BLOOD FLOW. FGR IS ALSO ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED LARGE ARTERY STIFFNESS AND CONSTRICTED PLACENTAL ARTERIES, AFFECTING UADF PULSATILITY. DATA FROM THE AVP MODEL SUGGEST INCREASED VASCULAR STIFFNESS, LINKING VASCULAR DYSFUNCTION AND UADF. THIS RESEARCH AIMS TO IDENTIFY ML-DETECTED UADF FEATURES THAT ENHANCE PREDICTION AND RISK STRATIFICATION OF POOR HUMAN FGR OUTCOMES COMPARED TO CLINICAL DATA AND THE S/D RATIO ALONE. USING PREGNANCY DATA AND UADF DOPPLER IMAGES FROM LARGE PERINATAL COHORTS (IOWA, NCH/OSU), WE WILL REFINE, TEST, AND VALIDATE A ML ALGORITHM TO PREDICT THE TIMING OF DELIVERY FOR POOR FGR-RELATED OUTCOMES. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROJECT AIMS TO ELUCIDATE NOVEL FGR-RELATED DYSFUNCTIONAL HUMAN UMBILICAL ARTERY VASCULAR MECHANISMS. IN HUMAN UMBILICAL ARTERIES FROM CONTROL AND FGR-AFFECTED PREGNANCIES, THE STUDY WILL EXAMINE MOLECULAR VASCULAR FUNCTION, REMODELING, AND BIOMECHANICS THROUGH MYOGRAPHY. WE WILL USE A DISCOVERY APPROACH BY USING A SINGLE CELL RNASEQ WORKFLOW TO LINK GENETIC SIGNATURES IN PRIMARY HUMAN UA TO INVESTIGATE MANY PATHWAYS AND A CANDIDATE PATHWAY (AVP) IN THE DEVELOPMENT FGR RELATED UA VASCULAR DYSFUNCTION. THIS RESEARCH AIMS TO ENHANCE UNDERSTANDING AND MANAGEMENT OF FGR, POTENTIALLY IMPROVING TREATMENT FOR AFFECTED PREGNANCIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HIGH-THROUGHPUT AND ACCESSIBLE SINGLE-CELL MULTIOMIC TECHNOLOGIES FOR DNAMETHYLATION ANALYSIS - PROJECT SUMMARY  DNA METHYLATION FORMS ONE OF THE KEY LAYERS THE EPIGENOME – SHAPING THE GENE REGULATORY LANDSCAPE TO PRODUCE A SPECIFIED CELL PHENOTYPE. AS A COVALENT MODIFICATION TO THE DNA ITSELF, DNA METHYLATION IS ONE OF THE MORE STABLE MODIFICATIONS, CONVEYING LONG-TERM REPRESSION OF GENOMIC LOCI, OFTEN IN THE FORM OF “CPG ISLANDS” SPANNING PROMOTER REGIONS OF GENES AS WELL AS ITS ABILITY TO IMPEDE TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR BINDING AT ENHANCER LOCI. DESPITE THE RELATIVE STABILITY, DNA METHYLATION IS HIGHLY DYNAMIC DURING DEVELOPMENT TO ESTABLISH AND ENFORCE CELL LINEAGE SPECIFICATION. FURTHERMORE, DNA METHYLATION IS OFTEN DYSREGULATED IN A NUMBER OF DISEASES, INCLUDING THOSE ASSOCIATED WITH GENOMIC IMPRINTING, CANCER, AUTOIMMUNE DISORDERS, AS WELL AS NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES AMONG MANY OTHERS. DUE TO ITS DYNAMIC NATURE, DNA METHYLATION, LIKE OTHER CELL-TYPE AND STATE SPECIFIC PROPERTIES, NECESSITATES THE USE OF SINGLE-CELL TECHNOLOGIES FOR WHICH WE HAVE DEVELOPED THE FIRST HIGH-THROUGHPUT AND COST-EFFECTIVE PLATFORM.  HERE, WE WILL DEVELOP NEW STRATEGIES TO PROBE DNA METHYLATION ALONGSIDE OTHER PROPERTIES EFFICIENTLY AT HIGH -THROUGHPUT. WE WILL FIRST LEVERAGE A CUTTING-EDGE CELL ENCAPSULATION TECHNOLOGY TO ENABLE HIGH CELL CAPTURE EFFICIENCY, A PROPERTY CURRENTLY LACKING FOR PLATFORMS THAT RELY ON MULTI-TIER CELL BARCODING. WE WILL ALSO LEVERAGE NEW TECHNIQUES FOR CAPTURE AND RETENTION OF MRNA-DERIVED CDNA THROUGH OUR HIGH-THROUGHPUT METHYLATION ASSAY, ENABLING THE CAPTURE OF RNA TRANSCRIPTION ALONGSIDE METHYLATION WITH THE ABILITY TO PRODUCE A NEARLY TWO ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE THROUGHPUT IMPROVEMENT OVER EXISTING WORKFLOWS. FINALLY, WE WILL LEVERAGE OUR EXTENSIVE EXPERTISE IN EFFICIENT TRANSPOSASE-BASED LIBRARY CONSTRUCTION AND CELL INDEXING TO PRODUCE SINGLE-CELL LIBRARIES COMPATIBLE WITH NANOPORE SEQUENCING FOR THE DIRECT DETECTION OF STANDARD DNA METHYLATION USING LONG READS THAT DO NOT UNDERGO CONVERSION. THIS TECHNOLOGY WILL ENABLE THE ASSESSMENT OF PREVIOUSLY ELUSIVE REGIONS OF THE GENOME, INCLUDING REPETITIVE REGIONS WHERE DNA METHYLATIONS SERVES AS A PRIMARY REGULATORY CONTROL MECHANISM, AS WELL AS ASSESS ALLELE-SPECIFIC METHYLATION PATTERNS WITHIN CELL TYPES.  WE WILL DEMONSTRATE THESE TECHNOLOGIES ON A DIVERSE SET OF INDEX SAMPLES THAT EXHIBIT DISTINCT OR DYNAMIC CELL TYPE AND STATE METHYLATION PATTERNS INCLUDING HUMAN PBMCS, CEREBRAL CORTEX AND INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS (IPSCS) IN ADDITION TO HUMAN AND MOUSE CONTROL CELL LINES. THESE INDEX SAMPLES WILL DEMONSTRATE SAMPLE TYPE VERSATILITY, ENSURING BROAD UTILITY OF THE DEVELOPED TECHNOLOGIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A SINGLE-CELL MULTIOMICS PLATFORM FOR STUDYING GENOME STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY THE THREE-DIMENSIONAL (3D) GENOME ORGANIZATION IN THE NUCLEUS IS PIVOTAL TO VARIOUS GENOME FUNCTIONS SUCH AS TRANSCRIPTION AND DNA REPLICATION. 3D GENOME ORGANIZATION WORKS IN CONCERT WITH CHROMATIN ACCESSIBILITY, TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR (TF) BINDING AND OTHER EPIGENETIC FEATURES OF THE CHROMATIN TO ENSURE SPATIOTEMPORAL GENE EXPRESSION DURING TISSUE DEVELOPMENT. HOWEVER, DUE TO THE INTERDEPENDENCY BETWEEN THEM, IT REMAINS CHALLENGING TO DISSECT THE INTRICATE INTERPLAYS BETWEEN THESE DIFFERENT REGULATORY LAYERS OF GENE EXPRESSION. WE RECENTLY DEVELOPED GAGE-SEQ, A SCALABLE SINGLE-CELL MULTIOMIC METHOD TO SIMULTANEOUSLY PROFILE 3D GENOME AND TRANSCRIPTOME IN INDIVIDUAL CELLS (ZHOU ET AL. NATURE GENETICS, 2024). GAGE-SEQ HELPS DIRECTLY CONNECT MULTISCALE 3D FEATURES WITH GENE EXPRESSION IN SINGLE CELLS, REFINE CELL SUBTYPES IN COMPLEX TISSUES, UNVEIL GENE REGULATORY NETWORKS, AND ANALYZE 3D GENOME DYNAMICS DURING DIFFERENTIATION. DESPITE ITS POTENTIAL, GAGE-SEQ AND OTHER METHODS LACK THE SENSITIVITY AND THROUGHPUT NEEDED TO DELINEATE FINE-SCALE CHROMATIN FEATURES, CHROMATIN ACCESSIBILITY, TF BINDING, AND TRANSCRIPTION REGULATION AT THE SINGLE-CELL LEVEL. TO ADDRESS THIS, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A SINGLE-CELL MULTI-OMICS TOOLKIT BASED ON GAGE-SEQ TO ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF GENOME STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION. WITH THE EXPANDED CAPACITY TO DETECT MORE MOLECULAR MODALITIES WITHIN A SINGLE CELL, OUR NEW GENOMIC TOOLS WILL ENABLE US TO CO-MEASURE NOT ONLY MULTISCALE 3D ARCHITECTURAL FEATURES AND TRANSCRIPTOME BUT ALSO A DIVERSITY OF OTHER MOLECULAR MODALITIES INCLUDING CHROMATIN ACCESSIBILITY, TF BINDING FOOTPRINTS, AND SPLICING ISOFORMS WITHIN THE SAME CELL. IN PARALLEL, WE WILL IMPLEMENT DATA PROCESSING PIPELINES AND DEVELOP NEW COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS FOR INTEGRATIVE ANALYSIS OF THE MULTIMODAL DATA. TO DEMONSTRATE THE UTILITY OF THESE NEW TOOLS, WE WILL THEN APPLY THEM TO INVESTIGATING THE EPIGENETIC MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE COMPLEX HEMATOPOIETIC MALIGNANCIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ELUCIDATING THE ROLE OF IRS2 IN CARDIAC CA2+ HOMEOSTASIS AND ARRHYTHMOGENESIS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SUDDEN CARDIAC DEATH (SCD) FROM VENTRICULAR ARRHYTHMIAS IS A LEADING CAUSE OF MORTALITY WORLDWIDE, PARTICULARLY FOLLOWING MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION (MI). A PRIMARY DRIVER OF POST-MI ARRHYTHMOGENESIS IS CHRONIC SYMPATHETIC OVERACTIVATION, WHICH CAUSES SUSTAINED STIMULATION OF MYOCARDIAL Β-ADRENERGIC RECEPTORS (ΒARS). THIS SIGNALING CASCADE HYPERACTIVATES DOWNSTREAM KINASES THAT DISRUPT CARDIOMYOCYTE CALCIUM (CA²⁺) HOMEOSTASIS, LEADING TO PATHOLOGICAL SARCOPLASMIC RETICULUM CA²⁺ LEAK AND TRIGGERED ACTIVITIES. WHILE Β-BLOCKERS ARE STANDARD THERAPY, THEIR NON-SPECIFIC ANTAGONISM SUPPRESSES NOT ONLY PATHOLOGICAL SIGNALING BUT ALSO ESSENTIAL PHYSIOLOGICAL FUNCTIONS, LEADING TO SIGNIFICANT LIMITATIONS AND LEAVING A SUBSTANTIAL PATIENT POPULATION UNPROTECTED. THIS HIGHLIGHTS A CRITICAL UNMET NEED FOR THERAPIES THAT SELECTIVELY TARGET THE ARRHYTHMOGENIC COMPONENTS OF ΒAR SIGNALING. OUR RECENT WORK HAS IDENTIFIED A PREVIOUSLY UNRECOGNIZED, NON-METABOLIC ROLE FOR INSULIN RECEPTOR SUBSTRATE 2 (IRS2) IN SAFEGUARDING CARDIOMYOCYTE CA²⁺ HOMEOSTASIS DURING SYMPATHETIC STRESS. OUR NEW PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT IRS2 IS INDUCED IN POST-MI HEARTS OF BOTH HUMANS AND MICE – A CONSERVED STRESS-ADAPTIVE RESPONSE – AND THAT ITS GENETIC OVEREXPRESSION SUPPRESSES CATECHOLAMINE-INDUCED ARRHYTHMIAS. FURTHERMORE, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED A SPECIFIC PHOSPHORYLATION SITE ON IRS2 THAT ACTS AS A SYMPATHETIC STRESS- ACTIVATED PHOSPHO-SWITCH TO DRIVE ΒAR INTERNALIZATION. OUR NOVEL PHOSPHO-DEFICIENT IRS2 KNOCK-IN MOUSE MODEL RECAPITULATES THE ARRHYTHMIC PHENOTYPE OF CARDIAC IRS2 DEFICIENCY. BASED ON THESE FINDINGS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT IRS2 ORCHESTRATES A DISTINCT CARDIOPROTECTIVE MECHANISM THAT PRESERVES CA²⁺ HOMEOSTASIS DURING SYMPATHETIC STRESS AND PROTECTS AGAINST VENTRICULAR ARRHYTHMIAS AND ADVERSE REMODELING IN THE ISCHEMIC HEART. THIS PROJECT WILL COMBINE MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, AND PHYSIOLOGICAL TECHNIQUES, ALONG WITH INNOVATIVE MOUSE MODELS, TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS THROUGH TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE THE THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY OF CARDIOMYOCYTE-SPECIFIC IRS2 OVEREXPRESSION IN SUPPRESSING VENTRICULAR ARRHYTHMIAS AND ADVERSE REMODELING AFTER MI. AIM 2 WILL DELINEATE THE MECHANISTIC BASIS OF IRS2-MEDIATED CARDIOPROTECTION, FOCUSING ON HOW ITS PHOSPHORYLATION ORCHESTRATES ΒAR INTERNALIZATION TO RESTRAIN PRO-ARRHYTHMIC SIGNALING. THE OUTCOMES OF THIS RESEARCH WILL ESTABLISH IRS2 AS A STRESS-ACTIVATED REGULATOR OF CARDIAC CA2+ HOMEOSTASIS IN THE HEART, PROVIDING NOVEL INSIGHTS INTO MECHANISMS THAT PREVENT SCD AFTER MI. ULTIMATELY, THESE FINDINGS MAY GUIDE THE DEVELOPMENT OF TARGETED THERAPIES THAT RESTORE CARDIAC HOMEOSTASIS, PROTECT HIGH-RISK PATIENTS WITH ISCHEMIC HEART DISEASE, AND IMPROVE LONG-TERM SURVIVAL.

description: ULTRAFAST ULTRASOUND IN PEDIATRIC PULMONARY HYPERTENSION - PROJECT SUMMARY PEDIATRIC PULMONARY ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION (PAH) IS A PROGRESSIVE DISEASE ASSOCIATED WITH HIGH MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY, LEADING TO EVENTUAL RIGHT VENTRICULAR (RV) FAILURE. THE HYPERTROPHIC RESPONSE OF THE RV LEADS TO RV DIASTOLIC DYSFUNCTION (DD) CHARACTERIZED BY A VARIABLE COMBINATION OF IMPAIRED RELAXATION AND INCREASED MYOCARDIAL STIFFNESS. RV DD HAS BEEN ASSOCIATED WITH OUTCOME PREDICTION IN PEDIATRIC PAH AND A POTENTIAL TO GUIDE THERAPEUTIC MANAGEMENT. THE GOLD STANDARD OF DIASTOLIC ASSESSMENT IS FILLING PRESSURE BY INVASIVE CARDIAC CATHETERIZATION, WHICH HAS INTRINSIC LIMITATIONS. THUS, A CLINICAL NEED FOR DEVELOPMENT OF NONINVASIVE TECHNOLOGY SUCH AS ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY AND CARDIAC MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (MRI) IS NECESSARY TO DETECT, AND RISK STRATIFY DD IN CHILDREN WITH PAH. IN THE PRESENT PROSPECTIVE TWO-CENTER OBSERVATIONAL COHORT STUDY, NOVEL ULTRASOUND TECHNIQUES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR THE DIFFERENT PHASES OF DIASTOLE RELATED TO PAH. THIS INCLUDES EARLY RELAXATION, EARLY FILLING DETERMINED BY DIASTOLIC SUCTION, AND LATE FILLING DURING ATRIAL CONTRACTION. WE WILL USE BOTH CONVENTIONAL AND ULTRAFAST ULTRASOUND (UFUS) WHICH IS A NOVEL ULTRASOUND TECHNIQUE CAPABLE OF RECORDING SHORT-LIVED AND FAST OCCURRING CARDIAC EVENTS. WHILE CONVENTIONAL ULTRASOUND TECHNIQUES CAPTURE IMAGES BETWEEN 25-100 FRAMES/SEC, UFUS IS CAPABLE OF IMAGING THE HEART AT 5000-10000 FRAMES/SEC. THREE DIFFERENT PHASES OF DIASTOLE WILL BE STUDIED USING NOVEL ULTRASOUND TECHNIQUES TO UNDERSTAND AND CHARACTERIZE RV DD. NON-INVASIVE ULTRASOUND MEASUREMENTS WILL BE VALIDATE WITH INVASIVE DIASTOLIC PRESSURE MEASUREMENTS. MYOCARDIAL TISSUE PROPERTIES (FIBROSIS) AND BLOOD FLOW WILL BE STUDIED BY MRI T1 MAPPING AND RV 4D FLOW. A NONINVASIVE RISK SCORE COMBINING UFUS AND MRI MEASUREMENTS WILL HELP PREDICT OUTCOMES IN THIS PATIENT POPULATION. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT BY COMBINING DIFFERENT METHODS OF STUDYING RV DD, THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF RV DD AND ITS RELATIONSHIP TO DISEASE PROGRESSION AND OUTCOMES WILL BE ELUCIDATED.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: THE TRUSTEES OF COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IN THE CITY OF NEW YORK

description: E-CIGARETTE USE AND EMPHYSEMA DEVELOPMENT: THE VAPESCAN STUDY - PROJECT SUMMARY E-CIGARETTE (E-CIG) USE IS COMMON, PARTICULARLY IN ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS. WHILE THE RESPIRATORY RISKS OF E-CIG USE REMAIN CONTROVERSIAL, CELLULAR AND ANIMAL STUDIES HAVE SUGGESTED POTENTIAL LUNG TOXICITY, AND EPIDEMIOLOGIC STUDIES HAVE ASSOCIATED E-CIGS WITH GREATER ODDS OF RESPIRATORY SYMPTOMS AND SELF-REPORTED ASTHMA AND, IN OLDER ADULTS, COPD. THIS APPLICATION WILL COMPARE EARLY LUNG TOXICITY ASSOCIATED WITH E-CIG VS CIGARETTE (CIG) USE TO INFORM ONGOING DEBATES ON WHETHER E-CIGS ARE A “SAFER” ALTERNATIVE TO CIGS. PRELIMINARY RESULTS FROM THE VAPESCAN STUDY (R01HL155576, OELSNER; R01ES029967, NAVAS ACIEN), A HIGHLY CHARACTERIZED PROSPECTIVE COHORT OF 372 E-CIG USERS AND NON-USERS AGED 18-50 (MEAN, 28) YEARS, SUGGEST THAT E-CIG USE IS ASSOCIATED WITH LOWER DIFFUSING CAPACITY OF THE LUNG FOR CARBON MONOXIDE (DLCO) AND GREATER LOW ATTENUATION AREAS ON LUNG COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY—FINDINGS SUGGESTING PULMONARY EMPHYSEMA. YET, THE LACK OF AN EXCLUSIVE CIG USER GROUP IN THE ORIGINAL COHORT LIMITS INFERENCES FROM DUAL E-CIG/CIG USERS, AND ADDITIONAL STRUCTURAL, FUNCTIONAL, AND MECHANISTIC INVESTIGATION IS WARRANTED. THIS APPLICATION AIMS TO ADD INNOVATIVE DEEP PHENOTYPING TO OUR UNIQUE COHORT OF YOUNG ADULT E-CIG USERS, PLUS A NEW CIG-ONLY COMPARISON GROUP, TO ELUCIDATE THE ROLE OF E-CIG VS CIG USE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF EMPHYSEMA IN YOUNG ADULTS, AND TO EXAMINE POTENTIAL MECHANISMS. THIS STUDY WILL RE-EXAMINE 200 YOUNG ADULTS (50 E-CIG USERS, 50 CIG USERS, 50 DUAL E-CIG/CIG USERS, AND 50 DUAL NON-USERS [CONTROLS]) AND PERFORM 129XE MRI AND GENE EXPRESSION PROFILING OF WHOLE BLOOD, HAIR, AND NASAL SAMPLES, WHILE PERFORMING METALS ASSESSMENT IN BLOOD, URINE, AND PERSONAL E-CIG AEROSOLS, SPIROMETRY, DLCO, URINARY COTININE AND TETRAHYDROCANNABINOL (THC), AND QUESTIONNAIRES ON USE OF E-CIGS, CIGARETTES, AND OTHER POTENTIALLY RELEVANT (E.G., OCCUPATIONAL, ENVIRONMENTAL) EXPOSURES. AIM 1 IS TO DETERMINE THE ASSOCIATION OF E-CIG USE AND E-CIG RELATED METAL EXPOSURES WITH EARLY EMPHYSEMATOUS CHANGES ON 129XENON MRI. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT COMPARED TO CIG USERS AND CONTROLS, E-CIG USERS DEMONSTRATE DILATED AIRSPACES AND IMPAIRED REGIONAL GAS EXCHANGE, PARTICULARLY FOR MEMBRANE GAS TRANSFER, AND THAT METAL EXPOSURES, PARTICULARLY TO COPPER, CADMIUM, LEAD, AND ZINC, WILL ASSOCIATE WITH THE SAME CHANGES. AIM 2 IS TO IDENTIFY GENE EXPRESSION PROFILES ASSOCIATED WITH E-CIG USE AND E-CIG RELATED METAL EXPOSURES. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT E-CIG USERS AND THOSE WITH HIGHER METAL EXPOSURES SHOW DIFFERENTIAL GENE EXPRESSION FOR PATHWAYS LINKED TO PROTEASE ACTIVITY, EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX PRODUCTION, AND ENDOTHELIAL INTEGRITY. THROUGHOUT, WE WILL LEVERAGE DATA IN DUAL USERS TO EXPLORE SYNERGISTIC EFFECTS OF CIG AND E-CIG USE AND WE WILL EXPLORE ASSOCIATIONS WITH INTENSITY/DURATION OF E-CIG OR CIG USE AS WELL AS NICOTINE AND THC EXPOSURES. ACCOMPLISHMENT OF THE AIMS WOULD INFORM E-CIG REGULATION AND ADDRESS KNOWLEDGE GAPS ON THE MECHANISMS OF EMPHYSEMA DEVELOPMENT IN YOUNG ADULTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENHANCING LAMELLAR BODY FUNCTION VIA LRRK2 INHIBITION TO REDUCE RESPIRATORY DISTRESS SYNDROME (RDS) SEVERITY - PROJECT SUMMARY  RESPIRATORY DISTRESS SYNDROME (RDS) IS A SIGNIFICANT CAUSE OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY IN PRETERM NEWBORNS DUE TO INSUFFICIENT SURFACTANT PRODUCTION AND LUNG IMMATURITY. LAMELLAR BODIES (LBS), WHICH STORE AND SECRETE SURFACTANT, ARE OFTEN UNDERDEVELOPED IN PRETERM LUNGS. CURRENT THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES FOR RDS INCLUDE EXOGENOUS SURFACTANT THERAPY, MECHANICAL VENTILATION, AND STEROIDS, WHICH ARE ASSOCIATED WITH LUNG INJURY, BRONCHOPULMONARY DYSPLASIA (BPD) AND POOR NEURODEVELOPMENTAL OUTCOMES. THEREFORE, THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR NOVEL THERAPEUTICS THAT CAN ENHANCE ENDOGENOUS SURFACTANT PRODUCTION AND REDUCE RELIANCE ON INVASIVE INTERVENTIONS. LEUCINE-RICH REPEAT KINASE 2 (LRRK2) IS A PROTEIN INVOLVED IN THE REGULATION OF AUTOPHAGY AND VESICLE TRAFFICKING WITHIN LUNG CELLS. ITS ROLE IN LB DEVELOPMENT HAS NOT BEEN FULLY ELUCIDATED, BUT RESEARCH ON ADULT ANIMAL MODELS WITH THE LRRK2 KINASE KNOCKED OUT (KO) DEMONSTRATED ENLARGED LBS WITH NORMAL BASAL SECRETION UNDER UNSTRESSED CONDITIONS. PHARMACOLOGICAL INHIBITION OF THE LRRK2 KINASE WITH GNE-7915 RESULTED IN REVERSIBLE LB ENLARGEMENT WITHOUT LUNG INJURY. HOWEVER, NO STUDIES HAVE TESTED WHETHER LRRK2 INHIBITION ENHANCES SURFACTANT PRODUCTION DURING PERINATAL DEVELOPMENT OR UNDER STRESS CONDITIONS RELEVANT TO RDS. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA IN IPSC-DERIVED LUNG ORGANOIDS SHOW THAT LRRK2 KINASE KNOCKOUT ENHANCES AUTOPHAGY (INCREASED LC3B-II), ENLARGES LBS (TEM), UPREGULATES SURFACTANT GENES (RNA-SEQ), AND INCREASES SURFACTANT SECRETION BY 20% (ELISA). WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT ACUTE LRRK2 INHIBITION DURING AT2 MATURATION ENHANCES AUTOPHAGY-DRIVEN LB BIOGENESIS, PROVIDING SURFACTANT RESERVE CAPACITY THAT BECOMES CRITICAL DURING HIGH-DEMAND STRESS OF PRETERM BIRTH. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT TIMED LRRK2 INHIBITION DURING THE CRITICAL POSTNATAL WINDOW ENHANCES SURFACTANT PRODUCTION AND PROVIDES INCREASED RESERVE CAPACITY THAT IMPROVES RESPIRATORY FUNCTION UNDER STRESS CONDITIONS. THE OUTCOMES OF THIS RESEARCH COULD LEAD TO SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENTS IN THE TREATMENT OF RDS, OFFERING A NOVEL STRATEGY TO MITIGATE THE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONDITION IN PRETERM INFANTS. AIM 1 WILL DEFINE THE AUTOPHAGY-ABCA3 MECHANISM REGULATING LB BIOGENESIS USING IPSC ORGANOIDS, MEASURING AUTOPHAGY FLUX, TESTING CAUSALITY VIA AUTOPHAGY INHIBITION, ASSESSING ABCA3 LIPID TRANSPORT, AND DISTINGUISHING BASAL VERSUS STIMULATED SECRETION CAPACITY. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER LRRK2 INHIBITION IMPROVES RESPIRATORY FUNCTION IN PRETERM LAMBS UNDER STRESS CONDITIONS. LAMBS (127-130D GESTATION, EQUIVALENT TO 26-28WK HUMAN) WILL RECEIVE VEHICLE OR GNE-7915; WE WILL ASSESS GAS EXCHANGE, LUNG MECHANICS, SURFACTANT BIOCHEMISTRY, LB ULTRASTRUCTURE, AND AT2 TRANSCRIPTOMICS. AIM 3 WILL ASSESS MULTI-ORGAN SAFETY IN DEVELOPING NEONATES (KIDNEY, BRAIN, PHARMACOKINETICS, REVERSIBILITY), ADDRESSING THE CRITICAL DATA GAP AS NO NEONATAL SAFETY STUDIES EXIST. THIS RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE THE COMPLETE PRECLINICAL FOUNDATION FOR FIRST-IN-HUMAN TRIALS. GIVEN THAT LRRK2 INHIBITORS ARE DEVELOPED FOR PARKINSON'S DISEASE, REPURPOSING FOR RDS OFFERS RAPID TRANSLATION, POTENTIALLY PROVIDING A SAFER ALTERNATIVE TO STEROIDS AND TRANSFORMING OUTCOMES FOR PRETERM INFANTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISMS UNDERLYING SLEEP DISTURBANCES IN CEREBELLAR DYSFUNCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY SLEEP DYSFUNCTION IS FOUND IN MANY CEREBELLAR DISORDERS (I.E. SPINOCEREBELLAR ATAXIAS, FRIEDREICH’S ATAXIA, ATAXIA TELANGIECTASIA). IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THE CEREBELLUM’S VAST ARRAY OF MOTOR AND NONMOTOR FUNCTIONS ALSO EXTEND TO SLEEP. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA INDICATES THAT CEREBELLAR PURKINJE CELLS INNERVATE BRAINSTEM TERRITORIES THAT CONTROL RAPID-EYE-MOVEMENT (REM) SLEEP. WE FIND THAT DRIVING ACTIVITY IN SPECIFIC TERRITORIES IN THE CEREBELLAR CORTEX SHIFTS SLEEP TOWARDS REM. THE ACTIVITY OF PURKINJE CELLS CORRELATES WITH REM PERIODS, AND THEY ARE EQUALLY CAPABLE OF ENCODING EYE MOVEMENTS IN WAKEFULNESS AND SLEEP. THIS SUGGESTS THAT THE CEREBELLUM MAY HAVE A CAUSAL ROLE IN REM. WE WILL EXPAND THESE PRELIMINARY INVESTIGATIONS AND TEST WHETHER CEREBELLAR ACTIVITY IS SUFFICIENT TO MODULATE REM. NEXT, WE WILL ANATOMICALLY AND ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICALLY CHARACTERIZE THE PURKINJE CELL TO BRAINSTEM PATHWAY THAT ENABLES THE CEREBELLUM TO MODULATE REM. TO FURTHER TEST WHETHER CEREBELLAR DYSFUNCTION MIGHT LEAD TO SLEEP DYSFUNCTION, WE WILL EXAMINE TWO CLASSIC CEREBELLAR MODELS: THE TOTTERING MICE (EPISODIC ATAXIA TYPE 2) AND THE PURKINJE-CELL SPECIFIC TSC1 KO MICE (AUTISM). WE WILL SUPPLEMENT THESE CLINICALLY RELEVANT MODELS WITH TARGETED INHIBITION OF SPECIFIC LOBULES OF THE CEREBELLUM. WE WILL MONITOR THESE MOUSE MODELS USING AN INNOVATIVE SYSTEM TO LONGITUDINALLY (24/7, UP TO LIFELONG) MONITOR SLEEP-STATE AND ACTIGRAPHY. THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL MECHANISTICALLY LINK THE CEREBELLUM WITH REM AND UNCOVER WHY CEREBELLAR DYSFUNCTION IS COMORBID WITH SLEEP DYSFUNCTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DECODING REGULATORY VARIANTS IN CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD) IS THE MOST PREVALENT CAUSE OF DEATH IN THE DEVELOPED WORLD. MANY BEHAVIORAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL CVD RISK FACTORS HAVE BEEN ESTABLISHED, BUT GENETIC CONTRIBUTIONS REMAIN DIFFICULT TO QUANTIFY. IN RECENT YEARS, SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE POLYMORPHISMS (SNPS) ASSOCIATED WITH CVD HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED BY GENOME WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDIES (GWAS). MOST GWAS SNPS CONTRIBUTE MODESTLY TO OVERALL DISEASE RISK, LAND IN THE NON-CODING GENOME, AND FUNCTION BY UNKNOWN MECHANISMS. THUS, THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR SYSTEMATIC AND COMPREHENSIVE FUNCTIONAL ANNOTATION OF NON-CODING VARIANTS (NCVS) ASSOCIATED WITH CVD. COLLECTIVELY, THIS KNOWLEDGE IS EXPECTED TO GREATLY INFORM OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE GENETIC UNDERPINNINGS OF CVD. TO ADDRESS THE CHALLENGE OF CHARACTERIZING NCVS AT SCALE, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED FOR HIGH-THROUGHPUT EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES TO CHARACTERIZE THE FUNCTION AND MECHANISM OF NCVS AFFECTING GENE EXPRESSION IN HEART CELLS. WE WILL LEVERAGE OUR COLLECTIVE EXPERTISE TO ACCOMPLISH THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS RESEARCH PROPOSAL: TO IDENTIFY AND CHARACTERIZE NON-CODING, REGULATORY VARIANTS ASSOCIATED WITH CVD THAT ALTER GENE EXPRESSION AND THE BINDING OF GENE-REGULATORY COMPLEXES COMPOSED OF TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS (TFS) AND RECRUITED EPIGENETIC COFACTORS (COFS). TO ACCOMPLISH OUR RESEARCH OBJECTIVES, WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING AIMS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE BIOPHYSICAL MECHANISM OF DISEASE-ASSOCIATED NCVS. WE WILL USE A HUMAN EMBRYONIC STEM CELL (HESC)-TO-CARDIOMYOCYTE (CM) CELL SYSTEM AND THE IN VITRO CASCADE APPROACH TO CHARACTERIZE HOW ~9,000 DISEASE-ASSOCIATED NCVS ALTER THE BINDING OF TFS AND TF-COF COMPLEXES. WE WILL TEST THE IMPACT OF SMALL MOLECULE INHIBITORS AGAINST TARGET EPIGENETIC COFS TO MODULATE THE IMPACT OF NCVS ON CHROMATIN AND GENE EXPRESSION. RESULTS WILL BE FURTHER CHARACTERIZED USING GENOMIC (E.G., CHIP-SEQ) AND CRISPR-BASED GENE PERTURBATION APPROACHES. IN AIM 2, WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE IMPACT OF HEART DISEASE-ASSOCIATED NCVS ON GENE EXPRESSION. WE WILL USE MASSIVELY PARALLEL REPORTER ASSAYS (MPRAS) AND THE HESC-TO-CM SYSTEMS TO PROFILE OUR PANEL OF ~9,000 NCVS TO IDENTIFY CAUSAL VARIANTS THAT IMPACT GENE EXPRESSION. IN AIM 3, WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE BIOLOGICAL EFFECT OF HEART DISEASE-ASSOCIATED REGULATORY ELEMENTS AND NCVS. WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE IMPACT OF ~10 INDIVIDUAL ELEMENTS AND NCVS DEFINED BY OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES AND LARGE ANALYSES (AIMS 1 AND 2). WE WILL CARRY FORWARD HESC LINES THAT ENABLE CONTROLLABLE EPIGENETIC SILENCING OF INDIVIDUAL GWAS-ASSOCIATED ENHANCER ELEMENTS USING CRISPR INTERFERENCE. IN ADDITION, WE PLAN TO DELETE SPECIFIC ELEMENTS AND GENERATE NCV KNOCKIN LINES FOR A SUBSET OF HIGH-VALUE TARGETS. WE ENVISION THAT COMPREHENSIVE ANNOTATION OF NCVS ASSOCIATED WITH CVD WILL PROVIDE DETAILED INSIGHT INTO THE GENETICS OF CVD THAT MAY LEAD TO THERAPEUTIC OPPORTUNITIES TO TREAT DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TISSUE-ENGINEERED ARTERIOVENOUS GRAFTS FROM HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS - PROJECT SUMMARY GLOBAL PREVALENCE OF END-STAGE RENAL DISEASE (ESRD) IS PROJECTED TO DRASTICALLY RISE WITHIN THE NEXT DECADE. THE MAJORITY OF ESRD PATIENTS RECEIVE TREATMENT THROUGH HEMODIALYSIS, WHICH REQUIRES A CHRONIC FORM OF FUNCTIONAL VASCULAR ACCESS. THE GOLD STANDARD OF ACCESS IS THE SURGICAL ESTABLISHMENT OF AN AUTOLOGOUS ARTERIOVENOUS FISTULA (AVF), BUT A LARGE POPULATION OF ESRD PATIENTS EITHER FAIL TO MATURE AN AVF OR ARE INELIGIBLE FOR THIS ACCESS TYPE. THUS, CLINICIANS TURN TOWARDS THE IMPLANTATION OF AN ARTERIOVENOUS GRAFT (AVG), WHICH ARE COMMONLY FABRICATED FROM EXPANDED POLYTETRAFLUOROETHYLENE (EPTFE). EPTVE AVGS OFTEN SUFFER MAJOR COMPLICATIONS, SUCH AS THROMBOSIS, NEOINTIMAL HYPERPLASIA, INFECTION FROM REPEATED CANNULATION, AND ANEURYSM, DUE TO BOTH ABNORMAL LOADING FROM ALTERED HEMODYNAMICS IN ADDITION TO INCOMPATIBILITY AT THE BLOOD/SYNTHETIC BIOMATERIAL INTERFACE. RESOLUTION OF THESE COMPLICATIONS REQUIRES OFTEN REPETITIVE CLINICAL RESOURCES LEADING TO A HIGH TREATMENT COST. RECENTLY, ACELLULAR TISSUE-ENGINEERED VASCULAR GRAFTS (TEVGS), FABRICATED FROM HUMAN VASCULAR SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS (VSMCS) SEEDED ON BIODEGRADABLE SCAFFOLDS WITHIN BIOREACTORS FOLLOWED BY DECELLULARIZATION, HAVE SHOWN PROMISE AS ROBUST VASCULAR GRAFTS IN RECENT CLINICAL TRIALS FOR HEMODIALYSIS. HOWEVER, WITHIN ONE YEAR OF IMPLANTATION, ONLY 28% RETAIN PRIMARY PATENCY PRINCIPALLY DUE TO THROMBOSIS. THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL AVGS IS OF HIGH CLINICAL NEED IN ORDER TO IMPROVE ESRD PATIENT TREATMENT AND REDUCE GROWING REINTERVENTION COSTS. THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ENDOTHELIUM ON THE LUMINAL SURFACE OF TEVGS COULD PROVIDE PROTECTION AGAINST CAUSES OF CLINICAL AVG FAILURE. WE HAVE PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED A HYPOIMMUNOGENIC, UNIVERSAL HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELL (HIPSC) LINE BY MODULATION OF CLASS I AND II HUMAN LEUKOCYTE ANTIGEN (HLA) EXPRESSION, MITIGATING ALLOGENEIC AND HOST IMMUNE RESPONSES TO THE CELLS. WE PROPOSE TO UTILIZE THESE UNIVERSAL HIPSCS TO DERIVE BOTH VASCULAR SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS AND ENDOTHELIAL CELLS (ECS) AND DEVELOP A TEVG WITH LUMINAL EC COATING. HIPSC- VSMCS WILL BE DYNAMICALLY CULTURED WITHIN A BIOREACTOR, AND, SUBSEQUENTLY, THE SCAFFOLDS WILL BE DECELLULARIZED. THEN, UNIVERSAL HIPSC-ECS WILL BE SEEDED ON THE LUMINAL SURFACE AND PRECONDITIONED WITH PULSATILE, SUPRAPHYSIOLOGICAL FLUID SHEAR STRESS. EC-COATED TEVGS WILL THEN BE IMPLANTED IN VIVO WITHIN A HUMANIZED RODENT MODEL TO EVALUATE THE THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY OF THE DEVICES. THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL, UNIVERSAL ENDOTHELIALIZED AVGS IS VITAL TO IMPROVING LONG-TERM HEMODIALYSIS ACCESS FOR ESRD PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISMS OF SEX-SPECIFIC RESPONSES TO OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEA THERAPIES (MOST) - PROJECT SUMMARY OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEA (OSA) — A CHRONIC DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY INTERMITTENT HYPOXEMIA AND RECURRENT AROUSAL — DELETERIOUSLY AFFECTS HEALTH VIA OXIDATIVE STRESS, WHICH IN TURN TRIGGERS INFLAMMATION AND DECREASES NITRIC OXIDE BIOAVAILABILITY. ACCORDINGLY, OXIDATIVE STRESS IS A KEY INTERMEDIARY THROUGH WHICH OSA ERODES VASCULAR FUNCTION. ACROSS YOUNG- TO LATE-ADULTHOOD, MEN EXPERIENCE A STEADY, LINEAR INCREASE IN CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD). IN CONTRAST, THE RELATIVELY ABRUPT LOSS OF ESTROGEN—A POWERFUL ANTIOXIDANT DEFENSE SYSTEM—WITH MENOPAUSE APPEARS TO HEIGHTEN WOMEN’S MODIFIABLE CVD RISK FACTORS, CVD PREVALENCE, AND CARDIOVASCULAR- ASSOCIATED DEATHS, ALL OF WHICH ARE HIGHER COMPARED WITH SAME-AGE MEN. NOTABLY, OSA PREVALENCE ALSO RISES SHARPLY AFTER MENOPAUSE, APPROACHING THAT OF MEN. CONCURRENTLY, IN POSTMENOPAUSAL WOMEN THE VASCULATURE BECOMES VULNERABLE TO SHARP RISES IN ACUTE OXIDATIVE STRESS, POSSIBLY EXPLAINING THEIR INCREASED OSA-BASED SEQUELAE. IN PARTICULAR, THE CRITICAL, ENDOGENOUS GLUTATHIONE (GSH)-BASED ANTIOXIDANT DEFENSE SYSTEM IS DIMINISHED IN BOTH OSA AND IN WOMEN AGES 50–55, CORRESPONDING WITH MENOPAUSE ONSET. GIVEN THAT OSA IS A MODIFIABLE CVD RISK FACTOR BUT ADHERENCE TO FIRST-LINE OSA THERAPY (I.E., POSITIVE AIRWAY PRESSURE [PAP] THERAPY), IS KNOWN TO BE DIFFICULT AND INADEQUATE, IDENTIFYING SAFE ALTERNATIVE THERAPIES FOR OSA IS CRITICAL. N-ACETYLCYSTEINE (NAC) IS A READILY AVAILABLE, SAFE, PRECURSOR ANTIOXIDANT THAT BOOSTS THE INTRACELLULAR GSH POOL. NAC IS A PRIME CANDIDATE FOR MITIGATING MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OSA-ASSOCIATED OXIDATIVE STRESS AND RESULTANT CVD GIVEN THE PROFILE OF OXIDATIVE STRESS, OSA, AND ASSOCIATED MORBIDITIES. HOWEVER, AND IMPORTANTLY, WOMEN AND MEN MAY RESPOND DIFFERENTLY TO THIS POTENTIAL THERAPY. THUS, IN MIDDLE- AND OLDER-AGED WOMEN AND MEN (AGED 52–70 YEARS WHO HAVE BEEN DIAGNOSED WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OSA), THIS RANDOMIZED, CROSSOVER CLINICAL TRIAL, WILL ADDRESS BOTH THE UNIQUE IMPACTS OF OSA ON VASCULAR FUNCTION, AND THE CRITICAL NEED FOR SEX-SPECIFIC PREVENTATIVE THERAPIES. THE STUDY IS EXPECTED TO REVEAL THAT: 1) WOMEN AND MEN EXPERIENCE DISTINCT PROFILES OF ADVERSE, INTERMEDIARY CARDIOVASCULAR CONSEQUENCES WITH OSA — REVEALED BY OXIDATIVE STRESS, INFLAMMATION, AND ENDOTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION; 2) PAP THERAPY DIFFERENTIALLY IMPACTS OVERNIGHT OXIDATIVE STRESS, INFLAMMATION, AND ENDOTHELIAL FUNCTION IN WOMEN AND MEN; AND 3) NAC DECREASES OXIDATIVE STRESS IN OSA BUT MAY DO SO UNEQUALLY IN MEN VERSUS WOMEN, WITH WOMEN EXPERIENCING GREATER IMPROVEMENTS IN OXIDATIVE STRESS WITH NAC THERAPY COMPARED TO AGE-MATCHED MEN. ACCOMPLISHING THE STUDY AIMS WILL LEAD TO PIONEERING, TRANSLATABLE INSIGHTS ABOUT OSA- INDUCED CHANGES AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE TO INTRACELLULAR ANTIOXIDANT CAPACITY. THIS WILL ALSO FACILITATE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF TARGETED, SEX-BASED INTERVENTIONS. GIVEN THE STAGGERING PUBLIC HEALTH BURDEN OF CVD IN BOTH MEN AND WOMEN, TARGETING OSA AS A TREATABLE RISK FACTOR—AND USING THE OPTIMAL TREATMENT APPROACHES FOR BOTH WOMEN AND MEN—IS ESSENTIAL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENT OF CARDIOMETABOLIC OUTCOMES IN WOMEN LIVING WITH HIV ON DOLUTEGRAVIR-BASED ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY ACROSS THE LIFESPAN - PROJECT ABSTRACT/SUMMARY WITH EFFECTIVE ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART), HIV HAS BECOME A CHRONIC DISEASE, REQUIRING COMPREHENSIVE STRATEGIES TO OPTIMIZE LONG-TERM HEALTH OUTCOMES. AMONG THE AVAILABLE ART REGIMENS, DOLUTEGRAVIR (DTG)-BASED THERAPIES HAVE EMERGED AS A CORNERSTONE IN HIV MANAGEMENT DUE TO THEIR UNPARALLELED EFFICACY, ROBUST SAFETY PROFILE, AND SUPERIOR ABILITY TO ACHIEVE SUSTAINED VIRAL SUPPRESSION. HOWEVER, CURRENT EVIDENCE DEMONSTRATES INCREASED RISK OF CARDIOMETABOLIC COMPLICATIONS, INCLUDING HYPERTENSIVE DISEASES, DYSLIPIDEMIA, INSULIN RESISTANCE, AND OBESITY WITH DTG-BASED ART. THESE RISKS ARE PARTICULARLY PRONOUNCED AMONG WOMEN WITH HIV (WHIV), A POPULATION THAT FACES UNIQUE METABOLIC CHALLENGES DUE TO HORMONAL FLUCTUATIONS ACROSS CRITICAL REPRODUCTIVE LIFE STAGES - PRE-MENOPAUSE, POST-MENOPAUSE, AND PREGNANCY. THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN DTG-BASED ART AND THESE PHYSIOLOGICAL TRANSITIONS MAY EXACERBATE CARDIOMETABOLIC VULNERABILITY. THIS STUDY SEEKS TO UNRAVEL THE LONGITUDINAL CARDIOMETABOLIC IMPACT OF DTG-BASED (COMPARED TO ATAZANAVIR/RITONAVIR (ATV/R)-BASED ART) IN WHIV ACROSS THE REPRODUCTIVE LIFESPAN THROUGH A METICULOUSLY DESIGNED FIVE-YEAR PROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY CONDUCTED AT TWO HIGH-VOLUME STUDY SITES IN NIGERIA. BY LEVERAGING CUTTING-EDGE CLINICAL ASSESSMENTS, INCLUDING LIPID PANELS, GLUCOSE AND INSULIN ASSAYS, FLOW-MEDIATED DILATION, AND MYOCARDIAL PERFORMANCE INDICES, WE WILL SYSTEMATICALLY EVALUATE THE CARDIOMETABOLIC COMPLICATIONS OF DTG- VS ATV/R-BASED ART IN NON-PREGNANT WHIV. AS THE COHORT EVOLVES, WE WILL MONITOR PARTICIPANTS WHO BECOME PREGNANT DURING THE STUDY, PROVIDING AN UNPARALLELED OPPORTUNITY TO CAPTURE DYNAMIC CHANGES IN CARDIOMETABOLIC PROFILES DURING PREGNANCY AND POSTPARTUM - A PERIOD OF HEIGHTENED METABOLIC AND CARDIOVASCULAR STRESS. BUILDING ON THESE ASSESSMENTS, WE WILL EMPLOY ADVANCED TRANSCRIPTOMIC PROFILING TECHNIQUES TO ANALYZE RNA EXPRESSION PATTERNS AMONG WHIV WITH DIAGNOSED CARDIOMETABOLIC COMPLICATIONS COMPARED TO THOSE WHO DO NOT DEVELOP THESE COMPLICATIONS. SPECIFICALLY, WE AIM TO IDENTIFY TRANSCRIPTOMIC SIGNATURES, INCLUDING RNA CLUSTERS AND PATHWAYS, ASSOCIATED WITH ADVERSE CARDIOMETABOLIC OUTCOMES ACROSS REPRODUCTIVE STAGES AND DURING PREGNANCY. THIS NUANCED APPROACH WILL ENABLE US TO ELUCIDATE WHETHER UNIQUE TRANSCRIPTOMIC PROFILES UNDERPIN THE DEVELOPMENT OF CARDIOMETABOLIC COMPLICATIONS, AND IF SPECIFIC RNA CLUSTERS PREDICT ADVERSE MATERNAL OUTCOMES. BY STRATIFYING FINDINGS BY REPRODUCTIVE STAGE AND PREGNANCY STATUS, THE STUDY WILL OFFER UNPRECEDENTED INSIGHTS INTO STAGE-SPECIFIC CARDIOMETABOLIC RISKS AND THEIR MOLECULAR CORRELATES, THUS BRIDGING CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAPS. THE ANTICIPATED FINDINGS HAVE IMPORTANT IMPLICATIONS. FIRST, THEY WILL INFORM DEVELOPMENT OF PERSONALIZED, STAGE-SPECIFIC RISK MITIGATION STRATEGIES FOR WHIV ON DTG-BASED ART. SECOND, THEY WILL PROVIDE A FOUNDATION FOR TARGETED INTERVENTIONS AIMED AT REDUCING THE CARDIOMETABOLIC DISEASE BURDEN. FINALLY, BY OFFERING A COMPREHENSIVE LIFE- COURSE PERSPECTIVE, THE STUDY WILL GUIDE THE OPTIMIZATION OF DTG-ART REGIMENS TO BALANCE VIRAL SUPPRESSION WITH THE MINIMIZATION OF LONG-TERM CARDIOMETABOLIC RISKS, ULTIMATELY ENHANCING HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR WHIV GLOBALLY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPROVING ENDOTHELIAL REPAIR IN PEDIATRIC ARDS - PROJECT SUMMARY. ACUTE RESPIRATORY DISTRESS SYNDROME (ARDS) IS A LIFE-THREATENING COMPLICATION OF SEPSIS AND ACUTE LUNG INJURY (ALI). COMPARED TO ADULT ARDS, LUNG REPAIR AFTER PEDIATRIC ARDS (PARDS) IS DEPENDENT UPON RE-ESTABLISHMENT OF POSTNATAL ANGIOGENESIS WHICH IS REQUIRED TO CONTINUE NORMAL ALVEOLARIZATION IN CHILDHOOD. DISRUPTION OF NORMAL ALVEOLARIZATION AND ANGIOGENESIS AFTER PARDS REPRESENTS A RISK FACTOR FOR SEVERE CHRONIC LUNG DISEASES, SUCH AS BRONCHOPULMONARY DYSPLASIA IN CHILDREN AND CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE IN ADULTS. GIVEN THE LACK OF MAJOR IMPROVEMENTS IN PARDS CLINICAL MANAGEMENT, THERE IS A COMPELLING NEED FOR INNOVATIVE MOLECULAR APPROACHES TO COMPLEMENT EXISTING THERAPIES. ONE APPROACH IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF NANOPARTICLE (NP) CARRIERS THAT CAN DELIVER EITHER DRUGS OR NUCLEIC ACIDS (ENCODING THERAPEUTIC TARGETS) TO LUNG ENDOTHELIAL CELLS (ECS) WITH HIGH EFFICIENCY AND PRECISION. WHILE SEVERAL EC-SPECIFIC NP DELIVERY SYSTEMS HAVE BEEN RECENTLY DEVELOPED, NONE OF THESE NANOCARRIERS ARE SPECIFIC TO LUNG ECS WITHOUT TARGETING ECS OF OTHER ORGANS. FURTHERMORE, MANY TYPES OF NPS BECOME TOXIC IN DISEASE SETTINGS, ESPECIALLY DURING INFLAMMATORY CONDITIONS LIKE ALI/ARDS, HIGHLIGHTING THE NEED FOR INNOVATIVE AND NON-TOXIC NP SYSTEMS FOR FUTURE THERAPIES. FOXF1 IS A TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR CRITICAL FOR LUNG DEVELOPMENT AND LUNG REPAIR AFTER INJURY. MY LAB PREVIOUSLY FOUND THAT FOXF1 IS DECREASED IN LUNGS OF PATIENTS WITH ARDS AND THAT EC-SPECIFIC INACTIVATION OF THE FOXF1 GENE IN MICE EXACERBATES ALI AND CAUSES ARDS. WHILE THESE STUDIES INDICATE AN IMPORTANT ROLE FOR FOXF1 IN LUNG REPAIR, IT IS UNCLEAR WHETHER FOXF1 IS A “DRUGGABLE” TARGET IN PARDS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL TEST THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF LUNG EC-SPECIFIC P22-F1 PBAE/PEI/PEG NANOPARTICLES COMPLEXED WITH FOXF1 MRNA TO INHIBIT EC APOPTOSIS AND STIMULATE VASCULAR REPAIR IN 2 MODELS OF PEDIATRIC SEPSIS-INDUCED ARDS (I.P. ADMINISTRATION OF LPS AND THE CECAL LIGATION AND PUNCTURE). WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER FOXF1 PROTECTS ACAP CAPILLARY ECS FROM APOPTOSIS THROUGH TRANSCRIPTIONAL ACTIVATION OF THE BCL2 GENE. MOLECULAR MECHANISMS AND FOXF1 TARGET GENES FOUND IN ANIMAL MODELS WILL BE ALSO TESTED USING HUMAN LUNG TISSUES AND PRECISION-CUT LUNG SLICES (PCLS) FROM DONORS AND PARDS PATIENTS. RECENTLY, WE IDENTIFIED THE TANFE SMALL MOLECULE COMPOUND, WHICH DISRUPTS THE INTERACTION OF THE FOXF1 PROTEIN WITH HECTD1 E3 UBIQUITIN LIGASE, PROTECTING THE FOXF1 PROTEIN FROM DEGRADATION. IN OUR PRELIMINARY DATA FOR AIM 2, WE CHEMICALLY MODIFIED THIS COMPOUND TO PRODUCE A NON-TOXIC DERIVATIVE, TANFE[F], WHICH CAN BE DELIVERED USING PBAE-1.4DA-PEG4X NANOPARTICLES TO LUNG ECS IN A MOUSE PARDS MODEL. WE ALSO FOUND THAT NP DELIVERY OF A KNOWN HECTD1 INHIBITOR, I3C, A PLANT-DERIVED SMALL MOLECULE COMPOUND WHICH IS CURRENTLY IN CLINICAL TRIALS FOR CANCER PATIENTS, INCREASES FOXF1 PROTEIN LEVELS IN INJURED NEONATAL MOUSE LUNGS AND IN HUMAN PCLS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER NP DELIVERY OF FOXF1-STABILIZING COMPOUNDS PRECISELY TO LUNG ECS WILL INCREASE VASCULAR REPAIR IN PARDS MODELS. ALTOGETHER, WE AIM TO DEVELOP NEW THERAPIES FOR PEDIATRIC ARDS THAT ARE BASED ON SPECIFIC ACTIVATION OF FOXF1 SIGNALING IN PULMONARY ECS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TRANSCRIPTIONAL MUTAGENESIS AND OXIDATIVE DNA REPAIR: NOVEL MECHANISM AND THERAPEUTIC TARGET IN HEART FAILURE - HEART FAILURE (HF), CHARACTERIZED BY PROGRESSIVE MYOCARDIAL DYSFUNCTION AND REMODELING DRIVEN BY OXIDATIVE STRESS IS A LEADING CAUSE OF MORTALITY. OXIDATIVE STRESS PROMOTES FORMATION OF 8-OXO-DEOXYGUANOSINE (8-OXO- DG) IN DNA WHICH IS PARTICULARLY HARMFUL BECAUSE IT DISRUPTS GENOMIC INTEGRITY AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL FIDELITY. WHEN RNA POLYMERASE ENCOUNTERS 8-OXO-DG, IT FREQUENTLY MISINCORPORATES ADENINE, PRODUCING TRANSCRIPTIONAL MUTAGENESIS (TM)—MUTANT RNA TRANSCRIPTS THAT CAN GENERATE DYSFUNCTIONAL PROTEINS LEADING TO CELLULAR DYSFUNCTION. ALTHOUGH TM HAS BEEN IMPLICATED IN CANCER AND NEURODEGENERATION, ITS ROLE IN HF REMAINS COMPLETELY UNEXPLORED. AS TERMINALLY DIFFERENTIATED CELLS, CARDIOMYOCYTES DEPEND ON STRINGENT TRANSCRIPTION FOR EFFICIENT FUNCTION, WHICH FURTHER MAKES THEM HIGHLY VULNERABLE TO OXIDATIVE DNA LESION-DRIVEN RNA ERRORS. THIS PROPOSED PROJECT STUDIES TM AS A NOVEL MOLECULAR MECHANISM CAUSING HF. IN AIM 1, WE WILL INTEGRATE LONG- READ SINGLE-NUCLEUS RNA SEQUENCING FROM HUMAN HF HEARTS WITH MATCHED BLOOD-DNA WHOLE-GENOME SEQUENCING TO IDENTIFY TM EVENTS IN FAILING HUMAN HEARTS. NEXT, WE WILL DEVELOP A QUANTITATIVE TRANSCRIPTIONAL MUTAGENESIS BURDEN SCORE (TMBS) WILL PRIORITIZE TM CANDIDATES BY FREQUENCY, LESION PROXIMITY, AND TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE. FUNCTIONAL EFFECTS OF THESE SELECTED TM-DERIVED TRANSCRIPTS WILL BE ASSESSED IN IPSC-DERIVED CARDIOMYOCYTES BY EVALUATING CONTRACTILITY, CALCIUM HANDLING, AND MITOCHONDRIAL ENERGETICS, WITH IN VIVO VALIDATION OF THE TOP TARGET IN MOUSE HEARTS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DEVELOP TARGETED OGG1-BASED REPAIR STRATEGIES TO MITIGATE THE UPSTREAM OXIDATIVE DNA LESIONS BY TWO COMPLEMENTARY SYSTEMS: (1) A CARDIOMYOCYTE-SPECIFIC, ROS- RESPONSIVE OGG1 CONSTRUCT TO ACTIVATE REPAIR SELECTIVELY UNDER OXIDATIVE STRESS, AND (2) A PRECISION DCAS9– OGG1 PLATFORM TO REMOVE 8-OXO-DG LESIONS AT GENOMIC HOTSPOTS CRITICAL FOR CARDIAC FUNCTION. THESE APPROACHES MINIMIZE OFF-TARGET OGG1 EFFECTS BY PROVIDING BOTH GLOBAL AND LOCUS-SPECIFIC REPAIR. BY COMBINING ADVANCED SEQUENCING WITH INNOVATIVE DNA-REPAIR TECHNOLOGIES, THIS HIGH-RISK, HIGH-REWARD PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH TM AS A NEW PARADIGM IN HF PATHOGENESIS AND ESTABLISH OXIDATIVE LESION-SPECIFIC DNA REPAIR AS A THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY TO RESTORE TRANSCRIPTIONAL FIDELITY IN THE DISEASED HEART.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DISCOVERY OF MODIFIER GENES AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS IN ARRHYTHMOGENIC CARDIOMYOPATHY - ARRHYTHMOGENIC CARDIOMYOPATHIES (ACMS) ARE INHERITED HEART MUSCLE DISEASES CHARACTERIZED LIFE-THREATENING ARRHYTHMIAS, SUDDEN CARDIAC DEATH (SCD), FIBRO-FATTY INFILTRATIONS IN THE MYOCARDIUM AND HEART FAILURE (HF). WHILE LIFESTYLE, SEX, AGE, DIET, AND/OR ENVIRONMENT FACTORS ARE SHOWN TO INFLUENCE CLINICAL HETEROGENEITY OF ACMS, IT IS STILL DIFFICULT TO FULLY EXPLAIN AND PREDICT DISEASE ONSET, PHENOTYPES, AND SEVERITY AND ESTABLISH A PERSONALIZED PREVENTION AND TREATMENT FOR PATIENTS. THE LIKELY REASON FOR THIS IS THAT COMPARED TO OTHER FAMILIAL CMS LIKE HYPERTROPHIC CARDIOMYOPATHY (HCM) WITH SCD, ACMS EXHIBIT MUCH LOWER PENETRANCE OF CAUSAL GENES, WHILE MODIFIER GENES AND EPISTATIC (GENE-GENE) INTERACTIONS HAVE ADDITIONAL RISKS FOR CAUSING SCD. OUR PILOT STUDIES HAVE IDENTIFIED THE GENES INVOLVED IN ENERGY AND LIPID METABOLISM (PPARGC1A, LEP) AS SHARED COMMON GENETIC REGULATORS OF TOP COMMON CAUSAL GENES IN PATIENTS WITH ACM AND ARRHYTHMOGENIC DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY (ADCM) WITH COMMON ARRHYTHMOGENIC FEATURES. BASED ON THESE DATA, WE HYPOTHESIZED THAT THE GENES MODIFYING THE METABOLIC HOMEOSTASIS (AKA MODIFIER GENES) PARTLY CONTROL THE VARIANCE IN VULNERABILITY OR RESILIENCE TO ARRHYTHMIAS. HOWEVER, IDENTIFICATION OF THOSE MODIFIER GENES IMPACTING THE SEVERITY AND OUTCOMES OF ACM AND ADCM REMAINS CHALLENGING IN HUMANS. SIMULATING GENETIC HETEROGENEITY OF HUMAN POPULATIONS, WE UTILIZED A MURINE GENETIC REFERENCE POPULATION (GRP) OF BXD MICE MAINTAINED IN CONTROLLED LABORATORY ENVIRONMENT FOR SYSTEMS GENETICS ANALYSIS. THIS APPROACH IDENTIFIED A TRANSMEMBRANE PROTEIN 43 (TMEM43), A TARGET OF PPARΓ, AS A CRITICAL PARTICIPANT THAT PLAYS KEY ROLES FOR BOTH CARDIAC- AND METABOLIC- RELATED PATHWAYS VIA ENHANCING EXPRESSION OF GENES INVOLVED IN FATTY ACID AND CHOLESTEROL UPTAKE IN THE SMALL INTESTINE. FURTHER, WE HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT A FULLY PENETRANT ACM-CAUSAL TMEM43 P.S358L MUTATION INDUCES BOTH ARRHYTHMOGENIC AND METABOLIC ABNORMALITIES IN KNOCK-IN (KI) MICE BRED IN THE SAME ENVIRONMENT AS THE BXDS, CONFIRMING SHARED S358L-INDUCED MECHANISMS THAT UNDERLIE ARRHYTHMIAS AND DISTURBED ENERGY AND LIPID METABOLISM IN VIVO. THE GOALS OF THIS STUDY WILL FOCUS ON THE IDENTIFICATION OF SUCH MODIFIER GENES AND MOLECULAR PATHWAYS THAT STRONGLY INFLUENCE THE SUSCEPTIBILITY (OR RESILIENCE) AND SEVERITY IN ACMS AND ADCM. IN THIS STUDY, WE WILL INTRODUCE THE TMEM43 S358L MUTATION IN MURINE GRP OF BXD MICE AND IDENTIFY SHARED GENES AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING ARRHYTHMOGENIC AND METABOLIC PHENOTYPES IN MICE UNDER THE S358L MUTATION USING THE POWER OF SYSTEMS GENETICS METHODS (AIM 1). IN AIM 2, THE MOUSE RESULTS WILL THEN BE ASSESSED AND VALIDATED IN OUR REGISTRIES BY CORRELATING CARDIAC- AND METABOLIC-RELATED PHENOTYPES AND GENOTYPES IN ACM AND ADCM PATIENTS. THE MAJOR ACHIEVEMENTS OF TRANSLATING PRECLINICAL AND CROSS-SPECIES AND CROSS-TISSUE FINDINGS INTO A CLINICAL SETTING WILL BE A FULLER UNDERSTANDING OF ARRHYTHMOGENIC DISEASE SPECTRUM, INCLUDING FIBRO-FATTY INFILTRATIONS IN THE MYOCARDIUM, IDENTIFYING NOVEL REALISTIC STRATEGIES FOR RISK STRATIFICATION, DIAGNOSTICS AND, POTENTIALLY, IMPROVING SCD PREVENTION AND PERSONALIZED CARE OF PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GLYCORNA BASED CONTROL OF ANGIOGENESIS THROUGH HEPARAN SULFATE BINDING GROWTH FACTORS - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT VASCULATURE IS A HALLMARK OF VERTEBRATE LIFE AND NECESSARY FOR THE COMPLEX ORGANIZATION OF 3D TISSUES AND THEIR COMMUNICATION OF INFORMATION AND NUTRIENTS ACROSS VAST SCALES – CELLULAR TO ORGANISMAL. A REGULATORY PARADIGM THAT HAS BEEN LONG INVESTIGATED MECHANISTICALLY AND CLINICALLY HAS BEEN THE ACTION OF MORPHOGENIC FACTORS LIKE VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR (VEGF) ON TARGET ENDOTHELIUM TO ORCHESTRATE VASCULAR AND CARDIAC DEVELOPMENT. MECHANISTICALLY, THE PRO-ANGIOGENIC FORM (VEGF-A) CAUSES SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION TO OCCUR FROM THE OUTSIDE OF CELLS, IN, THROUGH ITS MEMBRANE-EMBEDDED RECEPTOR (CLASSICALLY VEGFR). AT THE MOLECULAR LEVEL, ENDOTHELIAL CELLS (ECS) FACILITATE THE RECRUITMENT OF VEGF-A BY SELECTIVE EXPRESSION OF HEPARAN SULFATE PROTEOGLYCANS (HSPGS), WHICH ARE RECOGNIZED AS CRITICAL REGULATORS OF MANY CENTRAL BIOLOGICAL PATHWAYS, SUCH AS CELL-CELL COMMUNICATION, VIRAL BINDING AND ENTRY, AND GROWTH FACTOR SIGNALING. THE CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK ON WHICH ALL MODELS FOR THE ACTION OF HS-BINDING GROWTH FACTORS HAS, TO DATE, INCLUDED REGULATION ONLY BY GLYCANS, PROTEINS, AND LIPIDS, BUT NOT RNA. OUR RECENT DISCOVERIES OF BOTH GLYCOSYLATED RNAS (GLYCORNA) AND CLUSTERED DOMAINS OF RNA BINDING PROTEINS ON THE CELL SURFACE (CSRBPS), RAISE THE POSSIBILITY THAT THESE NEWLY UNCOVERED COMPONENTS CONTRIBUTE TO EXTERNAL INTERACTIONS, SUCH AS VEGF-A’S ABILITY TO BIND AND SIGNAL TO ECS. BUILDING ON THE INITIAL GLYCORNA AND CSRBP DISCOVERIES; WE HAVE NOW UNCOVERED THE GENETICS, MOLECULAR DETAILS, AND INITIAL FUNCTIONAL CONSEQUENCES OF THESE CLUSTERED GLYCORNAS AND CSRBPS ON SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION ACROSS THE PLASMA MEMBRANE. SPECIFICALLY, WE FOUND THAT: (1) HEPARAN SULFATE (HS) CHAINS CONTAINING 6-O-SULFATE GROUPS ARE CRITICAL FOR THE FORMATION OF GLYCORNA-CSRBP CLUSTERS, (2) CLUSTERS ARE DYNAMICALLY ORGANIZED, (3) HS-BINDING GROWTH FACTORS, LIKE THE VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR ISOFORM VEGF-A165, BIND CELLS AT THE CLUSTERS IN AN RNA- DEPENDENT MANNER, AND (4) INTRACELLULAR SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION ACTIVITIES OF VEGF-A165 ARE MODULATED BY GLYCORNA BINDING. OUR NEW RESULTS SUGGEST THAT GLYCORNA IS AN IMPORTANT, YET POORLY UNDERSTOOD, REGULATORY MOLECULE ON THE CELL SURFACE IN THE CONTEXT OF ANGIOGENIC FACTORS ON ECS. THROUGH COMPLETION OF OUR AIMS, WE WILL DEFINE THE MOLECULAR LOGIC AND FUNCTIONAL INTERACTIONS INTERACTION BETWEEN VEGF-A PROTEOFORMS AND GLYCORNAS ON TISSUE- SPECIFIC ECS (AIM 1), ESTABLISH THE TEMPORAL AND DOSE-DEPENDENCIES OF GLYCORNA-BASED REGULATION OF EC VESSEL FORMATION IN 3D AND IN THE CONTEXT OF SOLUBLE OR CELL-SOURCE GROWTH FACTORS (AIM 2), INTERROGATION OF THE GLYCORNA- MEDIATED EFFECTS OF VEGFA, IN VIVO DURING VESSEL AND CARDIAC DEVELOPMENT OF ZEBRAFISH (AIM 3). SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES OF ACTION FOR MORPHOGENS (LIKE VEGF-A), PROVIDING A NEW MECHANISTIC FRAMEWORK UPON WHICH HS-BINDING FACTORS CAN BE FINE- TUNED IN THEIR ACTIVITY TO ALLOW FOR PRECISE AND COMPLEX TISSUES TO BE FORMED.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: STATISTICAL METHODS FOR QUANTIFYING THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN HIGH-DIMENSIONAL MULTI-CHANNEL HEMODYNAMICS DATA AND CARDIAC SURGERY OUTCOMES - ABSTRACT. CARDIAC SURGERY ADDRESSES LIFE THREATENING AND LIFE LIMITING CARDIAC DISEASES THAT ARE NOT AMENABLE TO MEDICAL THERAPY. IN THE UNITED STATES ALONE, APPROXIMATELY 400,000 PATIENTS PER YEAR UNDERGO CORONARY ARTERY BYPASS GRAFTING (CABG). A REPORT FROM 2016 [21] ESTIMATED THE DIRECT AV- ERAGE COST OF CABG SURGERIES IN THE US AT $151,271 OR $60 BILLION DOLLARS PER YEAR. THIS DOES NOT ACCOUNT FOR INFLATION, CHANGES IN PRICING BETWEEN 2016 AND 2025, OTHER CARDIAC SURGERY PROCEDURES, OR THE LARGE INDIRECT COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH POST-SURGICAL COMPLICATIONS [16, 50]. THUS, THERE IS AN UR- GENT NEED FOR NEW STUDIES THAT CAN IDENTIFY MODIFIABLE EXPOSURES DURING SURGERY THAT COULD IMPROVE PATIENT OUTCOMES AND REDUCE HEALTHCARE COST. TO ADDRESS THESE PROBLEMS, OUR TEAM HAS STANDARDIZED AND INTEGRATED DATA FROM MULTIPLE SOURCES, INCLUDING CONTINUOUS HEMODYNAMICS DATA DURING SURGERY, POST-SURGERY ADVERSE OUTCOMES, AND COMBINED IT WITH COMPLETE ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORDS (EMR). THIS LED TO A UNIQUE, CURATED, AND QUALITY CONTROLLED DATA SET THAT CONTAINS MORE THAN 2,000 CARDIAC SURGERIES, INCLUDING 1,199 CORONARY ARTERY BYPASS GRAFT (CABG) SURGERIES (DATA SET 1). WE ALSO HAVE ACCESS TO AN ADDITIONAL 3,600 CARDIAC SURGERIES INCLUDING 2,100 CABG SURGERIES (DATA SET 2). THE MULTICENTER PERIOPERATIVE OUTCOMES GROUP (MPOG) HAS ALSO GRANTED US ACCESS TO ANOTHER 220,000 CARDIAC SURGERIES, INCLUDING 54,996 CABG SURGERIES FROM MORE THAN 50 HOSPITALS (DATA SET 3). THIS PROPOSAL IS FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING NEW BIOSTATISTICS METHODS THAT CAN ADDRESS THE COMPLEXITY OF DATA SETS 1, 2, AND 3 AND PROVIDE A TRANSLATABLE SET OF ANALYTIC TOOLS TO INFORM CLINICAL DECISION MAKING AND IMPROVE CARDIAC SURGERY OUTCOMES. ORGANIZING DATA SETS 2 AND 3 TO THE SAME STANDARDS AS DATA SET 1 IS A PART OF THIS PROPOSAL AND COULD NOT BE DONE WITHOUT THE CURRENT GRANT APPLICATION.
