description: DECIPHERING TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATION OF DISTAL LUNG PROGENITORS IN INJURY AND REGENERATION ACROSS SPECIES - DECIPHERING TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATION OF DISTAL LUNG PROGENITORS IN INJURY AND REGENERATION ACROSS SPECIES PROJECT SUMMARY THIS PROJECT WILL STUDY THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATION OF DISTAL LUNG EPITHELIAL PROGENITOR POPULATIONS AND COMPARE THESE RESPONSES ACROSS THREE SPECIES. THE GOAL IS TO DEFINE THE ROLE OF THE TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR SOX4 IN LUNG DISEASE, REPAIR, AND REGENERATION IN HUMANS, FERRETS, AND MICE. WHILE SOX4 HAS BEEN SHOWN TO BE A KEY REGULATOR OF PROGENITOR POPULATIONS IN OTHER ORGAN SYSTEMS, ITS ROLE IN LUNG BIOLOGY REMAINS RELATIVELY UNEXPLORED. USING A CROSS-SPECIES ANALYTICAL APPROACH WITH HUMAN, MURINE, AND FERRET MODELS, OUR GROUP WILL INVESTIGATE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS BY WHICH SOX4 INFLUENCES LUNG PROGENITOR BIOLOGY AND EXAMINE HOW THE MOLECULAR PATHWAYS INVOLVED ARE SIMILAR OR DIFFERENT ACROSS THESE THREE SPECIES. IN THE HUMAN LUNG, WE WILL WORK TO UNDERSTAND HOW SOX4 CONTROLS THE PROGENITOR FUNCTION OF HUMAN RESPIRATORY AIRWAY SECRETORY (RAS) CELLS. RAS CELLS ARE A RECENTLY DISCOVERED PROGENITOR IN THE DISTAL AIRWAY IN THE HUMAN LUNG THAT CAN GIVE RISE TO AT2 CELLS. WE WILL DETERMINE HOW SOX4 REGULATES THE FATE AND PROGENITOR FUNCTION OF RAS CELLS USING EX VIVO MODEL SYSTEMS AND PRIMARY CELL ORGANOIDS. WE WILL EMPLOY PERTURBATIVE SYSTEMS COUPLED WITH TRANSCRIPTOMICS, EPIGENOMICS, AND ADVANCED BIOINFORMATIC APPROACHES TO STUDY THIS PROCESS. WE WILL THEN MOVE TO THE MURINE MODEL, WHERE WE WILL INTERROGATE THE ROLE OF SOX4 IN THE PROCESS OF AIRWAY- DRIVEN ALVEOLAR REPAIR AND IDENTIFY WHETHER IT REGULATES DYSPLASTIC OR ABERRANT REPAIR (THE FORMATION OF SCAR-LIKE TISSUE) VERSUS EUPLASTIC OR NORMAL REGENERATION (THE GENERATION OF HEALTHY TISSUE WITH RETURN OF NORMAL LUNG FUNCTION). WE WILL ALSO CHARACTERIZE HOW SOX4 IMPACTS THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROGRAM OF AIRWAY CELLS DURING INJURY AND REGENERATION. THIRD, WE WILL TURN TO THE FERRET MODEL, GIVEN THE SHARED ANATOMICAL FEATURES WITH THE HUMAN LUNG. HERE, WE WILL INTERROGATE THE GENE REGULATION IN FERRET INJURY AND REPAIR WITH A FOCUS ON SOX4 IN THE FERRET INJURY RESPONSES AND USE THAT IN TURN TO ‘MAP BACK’ THE REGULATION OF PROGENITOR CELLS TO MOUSE AND HUMAN. THIS APPROACH WILL AID IN UNDERSTANDING HOW SOX4 AFFECTS THE BEHAVIOR OF PROGENITOR CELLS IN ALL THREE SPECIES, WITH A FOCUS ON THE ROLE IN HUMAN DISEASE. THESE INSIGHTS WILL IMPROVE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF OUR MOST OFTEN-USED MODELS OF LUNG BIOLOGY. ULTIMATELY, THIS WORK WILL YIELD NOVEL INSIGHTS INTO TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATION OF DISTAL AIRWAY CELL BIOLOGY AND WILL DEFINE THE ROLE OF SOX4 IN THESE RESPONSES. ADDITIONALLY, OUR INVESTIGATIONS WILL FACILITATE A COMPREHENSIVE APPROACH TO UNDERSTANDING TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATION AND PROGENITOR BIOLOGY ACROSS HUMANS, FERRETS, AND MICE. THIS EFFORT WILL ENHANCE OUR ABILITY TO COMPARE THESE CRITICAL BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES ACROSS SPECIES AND DRIVE SIGNIFICANT NEW DISCOVERIES IN LUNG REGENERATIVE BIOLOGY.

description: MECHANISMS OF PERINATAL NICOTINE VAPING-INDUCED PULMONARY ILC2 DYSREGULATION AND ALLERGIC ASTHMA DEVELOPMENT - PROJECT SUMMARY ASTHMA IS A MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUE, WITH 28 MILLION INDIVIDUALS AFFECTED IN THE U.S., INCLUDING A SIGNIFICANT PEDIATRIC BURDEN. EXPOSURE TO PERINATAL NICOTINE, THROUGH CIGARETTE SMOKE OR VAPING, IS A CRITICAL CONTRIBUTOR TO ASTHMA PATHOGENESIS AND OTHER ALLERGIC DISEASES, WITH EVIDENCE OF LIFELONG AND TRANSGENERATIONAL IMPACTS. PULMONARY GROUP 2 INNATE LYMPHOID CELLS (ILC2S) ARE PIVOTAL IN ALLERGIC AIRWAY HYPER-RESPONSIVENESS (AHR) IN ADULTS, YET THEIR ROLE IN PERINATAL NICOTINE SMOKING/VAPING EXPOSURE-INDUCED ASTHMA REMAINS UNEXPLORED. THIS PROPOSAL INVESTIGATES HOW EXPOSURE TO PERINATAL NICOTINE VAPING MODULATES ILC2S AND THEIR INTERACTIONS WITH THE MATERNAL AND OFFSPRING METABOLIC MILIEU, FOCUSING ON TH2 POLARIZATION AND ALLERGIC AHR. USING A WELL-ESTABLISHED ELECTRONIC NICOTINE DELIVERY SYSTEM (ENDS) AND INNOVATIVE TOOLS, INCLUDING THE NMUR1CRERORAFLX AND NICOTINIC ACETYLCHOLINE RECEPTOR Α7 (NACHRΑ7) KO MOUSE MODELS, SINGLE-CELL RNA SEQUENCING, ATAC SEQUENCING, AND T-DISTRIBUTED STOCHASTIC NEIGHBOR EMBEDDING (T-SNE) CYTOMETRIC ANALYSES, WE AIM TO ELUCIDATE MECHANISMS DRIVING NICOTINE-INDUCED ILC2 ACTIVATION. AIM 1 EXAMINES WHETHER PERINATAL NICOTINE VAPING RESULTS IN ALLERGIC AHR AND THE CENTRALITY OF ILC2 IN THIS RESPONSE, ASSESSING HOW NICOTINE EXPOSURE IMPACTS ILC2S IN THE LUNG. AIM 2 FOCUSES ON DETERMINING THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS, PARTICULARLY THE ROLE OF NACHRΑ7 ON ILC2S SUBPOPULATIONS, TRANSCRIPTOMIC AND EPIGENOMIC CHANGES, AND EFFECTOR FUNCTIONS. AIM 3 EVALUATES WHETHER SHORT CHAIN FATTY ACID (SCFA) BUTYRATE SUPPLEMENTATION, A CLINICALLY TRANSLATABLE THERAPEUTIC, MITIGATES PERINATAL NICOTINE VAPING EXPOSURE-INDUCED ILC2 DYSFUNCTION, METABOLIC CONSEQUENCES OF GUT DYSBIOSIS, AND OFFSPRING AHR. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT PERINATAL NICOTINE EXPOSURE VIA BOTH PARENTERAL AND INHALED ROUTES INCREASES LUNG ILC2 NUMBERS AND ENHANCES TH2 CYTOKINE SECRETION IN RESPONSE TO IL-33 AND HOUSE DUST MITE STIMULATIONS. MATERNAL NICOTINE EXPOSURE ALSO ALTERS GUT MICROBIOTA AND REDUCES SCFAS, KEY MODULATORS OF ILC2 ACTIVITY. NOTABLY, BUTYRATE SUPPLEMENTATION SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCES TH2 CYTOKINE PRODUCTION AND CYTOKINES MEDIATING AHR IN MOUSE MODELS, HIGHLIGHTING ITS THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL. THIS STUDY BRIDGES CRITICAL GAPS IN UNDERSTANDING PERINATAL NICOTINE-INDUCED ILC2 DYSREGULATION, LINKING MATERNAL METABOLIC ALTERATIONS TO OFFSPRING ASTHMA. BY IDENTIFYING NOVEL CLINICALLY EASILY TRANSLATABLE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES, OUR FINDINGS WILL INFORM INTERVENTIONS TO MITIGATE PERINATAL NICOTINE EXPOSURE-RELATED ASTHMA AND ADDRESS THIS GROWING PUBLIC HEALTH CRISIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DIFFUSION TENSOR IMAGING OF THE RIGHT VENTRICLE - ABSTRACT: THE RIGHT VENTRICLE (RV) PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE IN CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. IN SEVERAL CONDITIONS MECHANICAL FAILURE OF THE RV CAN RESULT IN SEVERE MORBIDITY OR MORTALITY, AND IT CAN ALSO BE A SOURCE OF LETHAL VENTRICULAR ARRHYTHMIAS. CHANGES IN THE ARRANGEMENT OF CARDIOMYOCYTES IN THE RV COULD PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN THESE PROCESSES BUT CANNOT BE CHARACTERIZED AT PRESENT IN THE HUMAN HEART. THE MICROSTRUCTURE OF THE RV HAS BEEN EXAMINED HISTOLOGICALLY IN ANIMAL MODELS, BUT THIS HAS SEVERAL MAJOR LIMITATIONS. THE RV IS A THIN AND HIGHLY COMPLIANT CHAMBER, AND ITS MICROSTRUCTURE COULD BE INFLUENCED BY ITS SHAPE AND LOADING CONDITIONS. A COMPELLING NEED, THEREFORE, EXISTS TO DEVELOP AN APPROACH TO IMAGE THE MICROSTRUCTURE OF THE HUMAN RV IN VIVO. DIFFUSION TENSOR MRI (DTI) HAS BEEN USED WITH SIGNIFICANT SUCCESS TO IMAGE THE MICROSTRUCTURE OF THE LEFT VENTRICLE (LV). WE AND OTHERS HAVE USED A SPIN ECHO SEQUENCE WITH DIFFUSION-ENCODING GRADIENTS COMPENSATED FOR THE FIRST AND SECOND MOMENTS OF MOTION (M2SE) TO IMAGE THE LV. IMAGING WITH THIS APPROACH IS TYPICALLY PERFORMED WITH AN IN-PLANE SPATIAL RESOLUTION OF 2.5X2.5MM, WHICH SEVERELY UNDER-RESOLVES THE THIN RV WALL. WE HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED AN APPROACH TO PERFORM FREE-BREATHING M2SE OF THE HEART WITH SUB-MILLIMETER IN-PLANE RESOLUTION. THIS HAS IMPROVED THE VISUALIZATION OF THE RV, BUT ITS MICROSTRUCTURE HAS REMAINED DIFFICULT TO FULLY RESOLVE. WE HYPOTHESIZE HERE THAT DTI OF THE RV WITH M2SE IS LIMITED BY THE COMPLEX MOTION PATTERNS OF THE RV, AND THAT THE DIFFUSION-ENCODED IMAGES REMAIN CORRUPTED BY MOTION. THE KEY GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS, THEREFORE, TO DEVELOP A DIFFUSION-ENCODED SEQUENCE COMPENSATED FOR THE FIRST 3 MOMENTS OF MOTION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THIS M3SE SEQUENCE WILL RESULT IN A SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENT IN THE VISUALIZATION OF RV MICROSTRUCTURE. THE PRINCIPAL CHALLENGE OF M3SE LIES IN THE POTENTIAL OF THE MORE COMPLEX GRADIENT WAVEFORMS TO SIGNIFICANTLY LENGTHEN THE ECHO TIME (TE) OF THE SEQUENCE, WHICH IS NOT WELL TOLERATED IN THE HEART. TO ADDRESS THIS, WE WILL USE CONVEX OPTIMIZATION TO DESIGN A M3-NULLED GRADIENT WAVEFORM WITH THE SHORTEST POSSIBLE TE AS WELL AS COMMERCIAL MRI SCANNERS WITH 200MT/M WHOLE BODY GRADIENTS. IN AIM 1 OF THE PROPOSAL, WE WILL FOCUS ON THE OPTIMIZATION OF THE M3SE SEQUENCE. IN AIM 2 WE WILL USE THE SEQUENCE TO CHARACTERIZE RV MICROSTRUCTURE IN HEATHY SUBJECTS. PARTICULAR ATTENTION WILL BE PAID TO THE IMPACT OF ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL LOADING CONDITIONS ON READOUTS OF RV MICROSTRUCTURE. IN AIM 3, WE WILL USE OUR APPROACH TO CHARACTERIZE RV MICROSTRUCTURE IN PATIENTS WITH ARRHYTHMOGENIC RIGHT VENTRICULAR CARDIOMYOPATHY (ARVC). CHANGES IN RV MICROSTRUCTURE WILL BE CORRELATED WITH MECHANICAL AND ELECTRICAL MANIFESTATIONS OF THE DISEASE. EXECUTION OF THE STUDY WILL NOT ONLY ADVANCE THE TECHNICAL SOPHISTICATION OF DIFFUSION TENSOR IMAGING, BUT ALSO PROVIDE IMPORTANT INSIGHTS INTO THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF THE RV AND ITS ROLE IN A BROAD RANGE A CARDIOVASCULAR CONDITIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ROLE OF SECRETED PHOSPHOLIPASE A2 GROUP X IN AIRWAY PHYSIOLOGY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ASTHMA IS A COMMON CHRONIC DISEASE OF THE AIRWAYS CHARACTERIZED BY AIRWAY INFLAMMATION AND AIRWAY DYSFUNCTION IN THE FORM OF AIRWAY HYPERRESPONSIVENESS (AHR) THAT OCCURS IN RESPONSE TO A VARIETY OF ALLERGIC AND NON-ALLERGIC STIMULI. WE IDENTIFIED A SPECIFIC PHOSPHOLIPASE A2 (PLA2) THAT IS SECRETED INTO THE AIRWAYS AND IS INCREASED IN ASTHMA IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE SEVERITY OF AHR. THE PLA2S ARE A GROUP OF ENZYMES THAT CATALYZE THE RATE-LIMITING STEP IN THE FORMATION OF EICOSANOIDS SUCH AS LEUKOTRIENES (LTS) AND PROSTAGLANDINS (PGS), AND NOVEL MEMBERS OF THIS ENZYME FAMILY ARE SECRETED (SPLA2S). ALTHOUGH 12 MEMBERS OF THIS SPLA2 FAMILY HAVE BEEN DESCRIBED IN MAMMALS, OUR PRIOR WORK DEMONSTRATES THAT THE MAJORITY OF THE RELEVANT SPLA2 ACTIVITY IN THE AIRWAYS IS ATTRIBUTABLE TO A SPECIFIC ENZYME SPLA2 GROUP 10 (SPLA2-X) AND THAT THE LEVELS OF THIS ENZYME IN THE AIRWAYS ARE ABOUT 2-3 TIMES HIGHER IN ASTHMA AND CORRELATE WITH THE DEGREE OF AHR. IN HUMANS WE HAVE LOCALIZED THE EXPRESSION OF THIS ENZYME PRIMARILY TO CILIATED AIRWAY EPITHELIAL CELLS AND MACROPHAGES AND TO A LESSER EXTENT IN EOSINOPHILS AND MAST CELLS. FOLLOWING ALLERGEN CHALLENGE, THE LEVEL OF THE ENZYME INCREASES IN INDIVIDUALS WITH ASTHMA, AND IN EPITHELIAL CELL CULTURE, THE ENZYME IS SECRETED IN RESPONSE TO OSMOTIC STRESS, A KEY NON-ALLERGIC STIMULUS CAUSING BRONCHOCONSTRICTION. WE HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT GLOBAL DELETION OF THE SPLA2-X GENE PLA2G10 IN MICE RESULTS IN MARKED PROTECTION FROM THE DEVELOPMENT OF AIRWAY INFLAMMATION AND DYSFUNCTION. OUR WORK SHOWS THAT SPLA2-X IS CRITICAL FOR ALLERGEN-SENSITIZATION BOTH IN THE AIRWAYS AND IN THE PERIPHERY AND FURTHER IMPLICATES ALLERGEN-INDEPENDENT INNATE PATHWAYS IN THE AIRWAYS AND DURING THE EFFECTOR PHASE OF ASTHMA. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT CILIATED EPITHELIAL CELL-DERIVED SPLA2-X IS NECESSARY FOR AIRWAY DYSFUNCTION IN MICE AND THAT SENSITIZATION OCCURS THROUGH GENERATION OF SPLA2- X IN THE AIRWAYS OR PERIPHERY IN A MANNER DEPENDENT UPON 5-LIPOXYGENASE (5-LO) DERIVED LIPID MEDIATORS. WE ANTICIPATE THAT TARGETING THIS PATHWAY AT THE CORRECT TIME WILL REVERSE HDM-MEDIATED CHRONIC INFLAMMATION AND AIRWAYS DYSFUNCTION. IN SPECIFIC AIM 1, WE DEFINE THE FUNCTION OF CILIATED CELL- DERIVED SPLA2-X AS A MEDIATOR OF AIRWAY DYSFUNCTION INNATE TO THE AIRWAYS AND FOLLOWING SENSITIZATION IN THE AIRWAYS WHERE THE ENZYME PLAYS A KEY ROLE. IN SPECIFIC AIM 2, WE FURTHER EXAMINE THE ROLE OF PLA2G10 IN THE SKIN AND DERMIS AS A MEDIATOR OF PERIPHERAL SENSITIZATION, FURTHER TEASING OUT THE FUNCTION DURING INNATE AND ADAPTIVE RESPONSES THAT ARE CRITICAL TO ASTHMA. IN SPECIFIC AIM 3, WE USE A TRANSGENIC MOUSE EXPRESSING THE HUMAN PLA2G10 GENE IN THE MURINE PLA2G10 LOCUS TO EXAMINE APPROACHES TO THERAPEUTICALLY TARGET THIS PATHWAY WITH A SMALL MOLECULE INHIBITOR AND WITH A BLOCKING ANTIBODY THAT HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED. THESE STUDIES ARE BASED ON SOLID HUMAN DATA IMPLICATING THIS ENZYME AS A MEDIATOR OF AIRWAY DYSFUNCTION IN ASTHMA AND THE STUDIES PROPOSED WILL PROVIDE IMPORTANT INSIGHTS INTO INNATE AND ADAPTIVE MECHANISMS LEADING TO AIRWAY DYSFUNCTION, PROVIDING A STRONG BASIS FOR THE FURTHER DEVELOPMENT OF THIS THERAPEUTIC TARGET IN ASTHMA.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LEVERAGING EXISTING AND ACCESSIBLE DATA TO REDUCE SODIUM INTAKE AND PREVENT CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES IN U.S. COUNTIES THROUGH COMMUNITY-ENGAGED POLICY IMPLEMENTATION (LEAD-US) - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT AMERICANS CONSUME ABOUT 3,400 MG OF SODIUM (NA+) EACH DAY, NEARLY 50% HIGHER THAN THE LIMIT RECOMMENDED BY THE DIETARY GUIDELINES FOR AMERICANS. EXCESS NA+ IS THE LEADING DIETARY RISK FACTOR FOR CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD), WHICH CAUSES ROUGHLY 950,000 DEATHS IN THE U.S. EACH YEAR AND ACCOUNTS FOR 39.5% OF ALL DEATHS. REDUCING NA+ INTAKE AT THE POPULATION LEVEL IS AN EFFECTIVE AND SCALABLE STRATEGY FOR HYPERTENSION CONTROL AND CVD PREVENTION. RECENT EVIDENCE SHOWS THAT MUCH OF THE SYSTOLIC BLOOD PRESSURE (SBP) LOWERING EFFECT COMES FROM INCREASED DIETARY POTASSIUM (K+) RATHER THAN DECREASED NA+. THIS HIGHLIGHTS THE IMPORTANCE OF THE DIETARY SODIUM-TO-POTASSIUM (NA/K) RATIO AS A MORE PREDICTIVE MARKER OF CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH THAN NA+ ALONE. BECAUSE MANY CONSUMERS PREFER SALTY TASTE, POLICIES THAT RAISE K+ INTAKE THROUGH FRUITS AND VEGETABLES (F&V) AS WELL AS POTASSIUM-ENRICHED SALT SUBSTITUTES (SS) MAY BE MORE ACCEPTABLE AND SUSTAINABLE THAN NA+ RESTRICTION ALONE. THE DIETARY APPROACHES TO STOP HYPERTENSION (DASH) DIET, WHICH IS RICH IN K+ BUT NOT EXTREMELY LOW IN NA+, CONTINUES TO BE RECOGNIZED AS THE “BEST HEART-HEALTHY DIET.” THE PROPOSED PROJECT, LEVERAGING EXISTING ACCESSIBLE DATA FOR U.S. SODIUM REDUCTION (LEAD-US), WILL RIGOROUSLY ASSESS HEALTHY FOOD POLICIES THAT INFLUENCE THE DIETARY NA/K RATIO. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO ASSESS THE REACH, EFFECTIVENESS, ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND MAINTENANCE (RE-AIM) OF PRAGMATIC LOCAL POLICIES THAT PROMOTE HEALTHIER FOODS. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO REDUCE CVD BURDEN BY ENGAGING POLICYMAKERS, INSTITUTIONAL PURCHASERS, AND CONSUMERS IN IMPLEMENTING FEASIBLE HEALTHY FOOD POLICIES. MOST PREVIOUS U.S. SODIUM MODELING STUDIES ASSUME IDEAL SODIUM TARGETS WITHOUT TESTING REAL-WORLD FEASIBILITY OR POLICY ACCEPTABILITY. LEAD-US ADDRESSES THIS GAP BY ANALYZING WHAT POLICIES HAVE BEEN ADOPTED, MODELING WHAT COULD BE ACHIEVED, AND EXAMINING WHAT CAN BE IMPLEMENTED. AIM 1 WILL ANALYZE COUNTY-LEVEL HEALTHY FOOD POLICY ADOPTION AND REACH (2010–2030) USING LINKED POLICY AND AMERICAN COMMUNITY SURVEY DATA. AIM 2 WILL PROJECT POTENTIAL HEALTH GAINS (2031– 2051) FROM HEALTHY FOOD POLICY ADOPTION USING INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL MICROSIMULATION IN THE VIVARIUM FRAMEWORK TO ESTIMATE CVD DEATHS AND DISABILITY-ADJUSTED LIFE YEARS (DALYS) AVERTED. AIM 3 WILL IDENTIFY IMPLEMENTATION BARRIERS AND FACILITATORS THROUGH INTERVIEWS WITH POLICYMAKERS AND INSTITUTIONAL PURCHASERS IN KING COUNTY, WASHINGTON. LEAD-US IS INNOVATIVE IN INTEGRATING IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE, MICROSIMULATION, AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT. IT WILL PRODUCE A STATE-BASED, INTERACTIVE VISUALIZATION TOOL THAT COMMUNICATES FINDINGS IN CLEAR, NONTECHNICAL LANGUAGE. THE INTENDED IMPACT OF OUR STUDY IS TO APPLY POLICY IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE TO CVD PREVENTION TO ACCELERATE THE TRANSLATION OF CARDIOVASCULAR SCIENCE INTO REAL-WORLD HEALTH IMPROVEMENTS WITH A FOCUS ON OPTIMIZING DIETARY NA/K RATIO.

description: DECODING NEUTROPHIL MEMBRANES IN ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID SYNDROME - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID SYNDROME (APS) IS AN INCURABLE AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE AND A LEADING ACQUIRED CAUSE OF THROMBOSIS. THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF APS IS PROPELLED BY CIRCULATING ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID ANTIBODIES THAT ENGAGE PHOSPHOLIPID-BINDING PROTEINS AT CELL SURFACES TO ACTIVATE NEUTROPHILS, PLATELETS, AND ENDOTHELIAL CELLS—THEREBY TIPPING CIRCULATING BLOOD TOWARD THROMBOSIS. ALTHOUGH MEMBRANE PHOSPHOLIPIDS HAVE A CENTRAL ROLE IN APS PATHOPHYSIOLOGY, FEW MODERN STUDIES HAVE ASSESSED POTENTIALLY CORRECTABLE DISTORTIONS IN MEMBRANE PERMEABILITY OR THE CHARACTERISTICS OF THE PHOSPHOLIPIDS THEMSELVES. WE PROPOSE A REINVIGORATED FOCUS ON APS MEMBRANES, WHICH WE ANTICIPATE WILL OPEN NEW AVENUES TO APS DIAGNOSIS, SUBPHENOTYPING, AND TREATMENT. GASDERMIN D (GSDMD)—A SUBSTRATE OF INFLAMMATORY CASPASES THAT FORMS MEMBRANE PORES UPON CLEAVAGE AND OLIGOMERIZATION—WAS RECENTLY SHOWN TO HAVE A KEY ROLE IN THE MEMBRANE RUPTURE REQUIRED FOR NEUTROPHIL EXTRACELLULAR TRAP RELEASE (I.E., NETOSIS). OUR PRELIMINARY DATA NOW DEMONSTRATE: (I) GSDMD CLEAVAGE AND LIKELY PALMITOYLATION IN THE CONTEXT OF APS IGG-MEDIATED NETOSIS, (II) REDUCED NETOSIS AND THROMBOSIS IN GSDMD-KNOCKOUT MICE, (III) UPREGULATION OF GSDMD-REGULATING GENES LIKE CASP1 AND CASP4 IN APS PATIENT NEUTROPHILS, AND (IV) ACCUMULATION OF CLEAVED GSDMD ON THE CIRCULATING NEUTROPHILS OF MANY APS PATIENTS. INSPIRED BY THE RECENTLY RECOGNIZED ROLE OF MYELOPEROXIDASE (MPO)-DEPENDENT LIPID PEROXIDATION IN NETOSIS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT LIPID PEROXIDATION OF NEUTROPHIL MEMBRANES IS ALSO A KEY DRIVER OF APS PATHOPHYSIOLOGY. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA NOW DEMONSTRATE: (I) THE REQUIREMENT OF MPO'S ENZYMATIC ACTIVITY FOR NETOSIS TRIGGERED BY APS IGG, (II) INHIBITION OF THIS NETOSIS BY LIPID PEROXIDATION-QUENCHING VITAMIN E ANALOGS, (III) SMOLDERING LIPID PEROXIDATION IN THE CIRCULATING NEUTROPHILS OF MANY PATIENTS WITH APS, AND (IV) ACCUMULATION OF Β2GPI (POSSIBLY AS AN ALDEHYDE-DERIVED COVALENT ADDUCT) ON THE SURFACES OF PATIENT NEUTROPHILS. HOW TO COMBAT THE INFLAMMATORY, ANTICOAGULANT-RESISTANT MANIFESTATIONS OF APS IS UNKNOWN. THIS PROJECT'S AIMS WILL DEEPEN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF APS NEUTROPHIL MEMBRANES BY SYNERGISTICALLY LEVERAGING WELL-DEFINED AUTOANTIBODIES, UNIQUE MOUSE MODELS, AND A ROBUST, HIGHLY MOTIVATED PATIENT COHORT. AIM 1 WILL CHARACTERIZE THE MOLECULAR PATHWAYS IN ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID ANTIBODY-ACTIVATED NEUTROPHILS THAT TRIGGER GSDMD CLEAVAGE AND DOWNSTREAM THROMBO-INFLAMMATORY EFFECTOR FUNCTIONS. AIM 2 WILL ELUCIDATE THE ROLE OF PHOSPHOLIPID OXIDATION IN ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID ANTIBODY-MEDIATED NEUTROPHIL ACTIVATION AND THROMBO-INFLAMMATORY NETOSIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENDOTHELIAL MECHANOSENSING OF CIRCULATORY FLOW IN HEALTH AND DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THIS PROJECT AIMS TO UNDERSTAND HOW ENDOTHELIAL CELLS (ECS) LINING BLOOD AND LYMPHATIC VESSELS RESPOND TO FLUID FLOW FORCES. THESE MECHANICAL STIMULI ARE CRUCIAL FOR CARDIOVASCULAR DEVELOPMENT AND HEALTH. THEY ALSO PLAY A SIGNIFICANT ROLE IN DISEASES THAT OFTEN AFFECT OTHER ORGANS AND CAN LEAD TO DISABILITY, MENTAL IMPAIRMENT, AND EVEN DEATH. WE WILL FOCUS ON BETTER UNDERSTANDING THE ROLES THAT PLXND1 (A TRANSMEMBRANE SEMAPHORIN (SEMA) RECEPTOR ON THE SURFACE OF ECS) AND KLF2 (A TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR) PLAY IN ENDOTHELIAL RESPONSES TO FLUID SHEAR STRESS DURING VASCULAR DEVELOPMENT. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL USE A CRISPR SCREEN TO IDENTIFY NEW FACTORS INVOLVED IN ENDOTHELIAL MECHANOBIOLOGY AND CONDUCT INNOVATIVE STUDIES TO CHARACTERIZE THESE EMERGING PLAYERS. IT HAS LONG BEEN KNOWN THAT PLXND1 GUIDES THE GROWTH OF BLOOD AND LYMPHATIC VESSELS. HOWEVER, IT WAS ONLY RECENTLY DISCOVERED THAT PLXND1 FUNCTIONS AS A MECHANOSENSOR DETECTING FLUID SHEAR STRESS, A TYPE OF CIRCULATORY FORCE. WE HAVE UNCOVERED THE DEVELOPMENTAL ROLE OF THIS NOVEL RECEPTOR ACTIVITY BY DEMONSTRATING THAT PLXND1 MECHANOSENSING IS ESSENTIAL FOR THE ENDOTHELIUM OF THE AORTA TO PROMOTE THE EXPRESSION OF KLF2, WHICH INCREASES EC SIZE TO EXPAND THIS ARTERY IN RESPONSE TO CIRCULATORY DYNAMICS. KLF2 AND FLUID FORCES ALSO INFLUENCE LYMPHATIC DEVELOPMENT. INSPIRED BY THESE FINDINGS AND LEVERAGING THE TRANSPARENT ZEBRAFISH EMBRYO AND HUMAN-CULTURED ECS AS POWERFUL MODELS FOR CARDIOVASCULAR MECHANOBIOLOGY RESEARCH, WE AIM TO ANSWER THREE KEY QUESTIONS: (1) WHICH PARTS OF PLXND1 ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR SENSING FLUID FORCES AND DIRECTING BLOOD VESSEL GROWTH, AND HOW DO DISEASE-ASSOCIATED VARIANTS DISRUPT THESE FUNCTIONS TO AFFECT CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH? (2) WHAT OTHER FACTORS INTERACT WITH KLF2 TO REGULATE EC SIZE? (3) HOW DOES PLXND1'S MECHANOSENSING ABILITY SUPPORT LYMPHATIC SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT, AND WHICH OTHER MOLECULES ARE INVOLVED, ESPECIALLY AS MECHANOEFFECTORS? ADDRESSING THESE QUESTIONS WILL SIGNIFICANTLY ENHANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF PLXND1, KLF2, AND OTHER NOVEL PLAYERS IN CARDIOVASCULAR BIOLOGY. THESE INSIGHTS COULD LEAD TO IMPROVED PREVENTION, DIAGNOSIS, AND TREATMENT OF CONDITIONS SUCH AS HEART MUSCLE THICKENING, HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE, STENOTIC VESSELS, ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUE BUILDUP IN ARTERIES, AND EDEMA.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPROVED TREATMENT OF INTRAMURAL VENTRICULAR ARRHYTHMIA USING ROBOT-ASSISTED MRI-GUIDED INTRAMYOCARDIAL NEEDLE ABLATION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT:  THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP A DEXTEROUS INTRAMYOCARDIAL NEEDLE ABLATION (D-INA) CATHETER AND ROBOTIC CONTROL METHOD WITH MRI-BASED NAVIGATION FOR EFFECTIVE VENTRICULAR TACHYCARDIA (VT) TREATMENT. VT IS A MAJOR CAUSE OF SUDDEN CARDIAC DEATH (SCD), WHICH KILLS 325,000 PEOPLE IN THE U.S. PER YEAR. VT RESULTS FROM ABERRANT ELECTRIC CONDUCTION IN THE HEART, TYPICALLY OCCURRING AROUND SCAR TISSUE. THE MOST EFFECTIVE THERAPY TO PREVENT VT IS CATHETER-BASED ELECTROANATOMIC MAPPING (EAM) FOLLOWED BY RADIO-FREQUENCY ABLATION (RFA) TO THERMALLY INDUCE TISSUE NECROSIS. HOWEVER, CONVENTIONAL CATHETER ABLATION IS ONLY ~60% SUCCESSFUL IN ONE YEAR DESPITE LENGTHY PROCEDURES. IMPORTANT REASONS FOR POOR SUCCESS ARE 1) THE LIMITED ABILITY OF RFA APPLIED FROM THE ENDOCARDIAL SURFACE TO ELIMINATE TARGETS DEEPER WITHIN THE LEFT VENTRICLE (LV) WALL, WHICH IS ESTIMATED TO BE REQUIRED IN 38% OF VT ABLATIONS, 2) DIFFICULTY IN DEXTEROUSLY AND SYSTEMATICALLY NAVIGATING THE CATHETER ALONG THE LV ENDOCARDIAL SURFACE FOR COMPLETE TREATMENT, ESPECIALLY AROUND LV SUMMIT AND PAPILLARY MUSCLES, AND 3) LACK OF METHODS TO IDENTIFY SITES OF INCOMPLETE ABLATION INTRAOPERATIVELY. INCOMPLETE ABLATION CAN APPEAR EFFECTIVE ACUTELY BUT RECOVER OVER DAYS TO WEEKS, LEADING TO VT RECURRENCE. ISSUE 1) WAS MOSTLY RESOLVED BY THE INA CATHETER, WHICH USES AN INSTRUMENTED NEEDLE THAT PENETRATES THE VENTRICULAR WALL AND DELIVERS ABLATION FROM DEEPER WITHIN THE MYOCARDIUM. HOWEVER, THE EXISTING INA STILL SUFFERS FROM ISSUES 2) AND 3), NECESSITATING A NEW TOOL WITH FAR GREATER DEXTERITY, IMPROVED CATHETER CONTROL, AND ADVANCED INTRAOPERATIVE MONITORING TO ACHIEVE EFFECTIVE TREATMENT. TO ADDRESS THESE LIMITATIONS, WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1: DEVELOP NOVEL D-INA WITH ENHANCED SENSING. WE WILL DEVELOP A NOVEL DEXTEROUS INA TOOLSET WITH ENHANCED SENSING OF SHAPE, FORCE, AND TEMPERATURE TO ENABLE EFFECTIVE INTRAMYOCARDIAL NEEDLE ABLATION. AIM 2: SYSTEMATIC D-INA MANIPULATION VIA ROBOTIC CONTROL AND MRI GUIDANCE. WE WILL DEVELOP THE ROBOTIC CONTROL AND MR-BASED NAVIGATION FRAMEWORK TO MANIPULATE THE D-INA UNDER MRI GUIDANCE FOR EFFECTIVE AND SYSTEMATIC ABLATION IN THE VENTRICLE. AIM 3: ACCURATE MRI-GUIDED VT ABLATION IN A PORCINE MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION (MI) MODEL. WE WILL FIRST DEVELOP THE WORKFLOW FOR ACCURATE MRI-GUIDED LV ABLATION AND THEN VALIDATE THE PERFORMANCE OF THE PROPOSED D- INA AND ROBOTIC CONTROL TO PERFORM MRI-GUIDED ABLATION FOR VT TREATMENT. IMPACT: IF SUCCESSFUL, THIS PROPOSAL WILL PERMIT MORE ACCURATE AND EFFICIENT ABLATION OF DEEP-SEATED VT CIRCUITS IN THE VENTRICULAR WALL, ADDRESSING IMPORTANT SHORTCOMINGS IN CURRENT VT THERAPY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MUTATION-SPECIFIC RESPONSES TO MYOSIN INHIBITORS IN HUMAN IPSC MODELS OF HCM - PROJECT SUMMARY MYOSIN ATPASE INHIBITORS SUCH AS MAVACAMTEN (CAMZYOS®) ARE THE FIRST PHARMACEUTICALS DESIGNED TO SPECIFICALLY TARGET AN UNDERLYING DISEASE-CAUSING MECHANISM IN HYPERTROPHIC CARDIOMYOPATHY (HCM). MAVACAMTEN REDUCES LEFT VENTRICULAR HYPERTROPHY AND OUTFLOW TRACT OBSTRUCTION, INCREASES EXERCISE CAPACITY, AND IMPROVES HEART FAILURE IN MANY PATIENTS WITH OBSTRUCTIVE HCM, BUT DID NOT IMPROVE OVERALL HEART FAILURE SYMPTOMS IN 30% OF THIS GROUP AND HAD NO SYMPTOMATIC BENEFIT IN NON-OBSTRUCTIVE HCM. WHILE MAVACAMTEN SERVES A PREVIOUSLY UNMET THERAPEUTIC NEED FOR A SUBSET OF HCM PATIENTS, IT IS NOT KNOWN WHAT DIFFERENTIATES MAVACAMTEN RESPONDERS FROM NON-RESPONDERS. HCM IS CAUSED BY MUTATIONS IN GENES ENCODING CARDIAC SARCOMERIC PROTEINS THAT GENERATE OR REGULATE FORCE WITH MOST MUTATIONS OCCURRING IN THE CARDIAC MYOSIN BINDING PROTEIN-C (CMYBP-C) AND BETA MYOSIN HEAVY CHAIN GENES. MANY (BUT NOT ALL) MUTATIONS IN THESE GENES RESULT IN A BIOPHYSICAL DEFECT THAT RESULTS IN AN INCREASE IN THE POOL OF MYOSIN CROSS-BRIDGES AVAILABLE TO PARTICIPATE IN FORCE-PRODUCTION, A CONDITION REFERRED TO AS THE DISORDERED RELAXED (DRX) STATE. MAVACAMTEN, AN ALLOSTERIC MYOSIN INHIBITOR, STABILIZES THE OPPOSING SRX (SUPER RELAXED) STATE OF MYOSIN THAT CANNOT FORM FORCE- PRODUCING INTERACTIONS. GIVEN THE GROWING EVIDENCE THAT INDIVIDUAL MUTATIONS HAVE SPECIFIC EFFECTS ON CONTRACTION, AND THAT SOME DO NOT ACT BY INCREASING THE DRX:SRX RATIO, WE POSTULATE THAT THIS FUNCTIONAL DIFFERENCE MAY DIFFERENTIATE MAVACAMTEN RESPONDERS FROM NON-RESPONDERS. WE WILL APPLY OUR VALIDATED HUMAN STEM CELL DERIVED ENGINEERED HEART TISSUE (HIPSC-EHT) PLATFORM TO EVALUATE THE EFFECTS OF CHRONIC MYOSIN INHIBITION USING SIX ISOGENIC IPSC LINES, EACH EXPRESSING A KNOWN HCM-CAUSING MUTATION, WITH VALIDATION STUDIES IN A SECOND UNRELATED LINE. BASED ON FUNCTIONAL ANALYSES, WE WILL GROUP THE RESPONDER AND NON- RESPONDER MUTATIONS FOLLOWED BY A SYSTEMATIC ASSESSMENT OF THE TRANSCRIPTOME AND PROTEOFORMS TO UNCOVER DIFFERENTIAL MOLECULAR PROFILES AT BASELINE AND AFTER EXPOSURE TO MYOSIN INHIBITORS. OUR EHT DATA WILL BE VALIDATED IN VIVO USING OUR EXISTING HCM MOUSE MODELS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT RESPONDERS AND NON-RESPONDERS TO ALLOSTERIC MYOSIN INHIBITORS SEGREGATE BASED ON A MUTATION-SPECIFIC BIOPHYSICAL DEFECT AND THIS RESPONSE IS REFLECTED IN THEIR DIFFERENTIAL MOLECULAR PROFILES. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS IN THE FOLLOWING AIMS: AIM 1: ASSESS THE CONTRACTILE RESPONSE TO SUSTAINED MYOSIN INHIBITION IN HIPSC-EHT WITH HCM MUTATIONS; AIM 2: ASSESS THE IN VIVO EFFICACY OF MYOSIN INHIBITION THERAPY IN MURINE MODELS THAT CARRY RESPONDER AND NON-RESPONDER HCM MUTATIONS, AND AIM3: ELUCIDATE THE TRANSCRIPTOME AND PROTEOME LANDSCAPES TO IDENTIFY DIFFERENTIATING MOLECULAR PROFILES IN EHTS KNOWN TO EITHER RESPOND OR NOT RESPOND TO MYOSIN INHIBITOR TREATMENT. THIS PROJECT LEVERAGES INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGIES AND A PROJECT TEAM THAT BRINGS UNIQUE EXPERTISE AND RECORD OF SUCCESS TO COMPLETE THE AIMS AND ADDRESS GAP IN KNOWLEDGE, PROMOTE APPROPRIATE USE OF EXISTING THERAPIES, AND ADVANCE NOVEL DRUG DISCOVERY TO TREAT A SIGNIFICANT HUMAN DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DECIDE-AF: IMPLEMENTING AN INTEROPERABLE SHARED DECISION-MAKING TOOL IN THE ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD TO PREVENT STROKE IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION - ATRIAL FIBRILLATION (AF) ACCOUNTS FOR 100,000 STROKES, 62,000 DISABILITY CASES, AND 20,000 DEATHS PER YEAR IN THE US. ANTICOAGULATION (AC) DECREASES THE RISK OF STROKE BY TWO-THIRDS, BUT DESPITE ESTABLISHED GUIDELINES, ONLY 65% OF PATIENTS USE IT. ADHERENCE WITH THIS PROPHYLAXIS GUIDELINE SUFFERS FROM SUBOPTIMAL INITIATION AND PERSISTENCE, PARTICULARLY IN SOME DEMOGRAPHIC GROUPS WHOSE USE LOWER BUT STROKE RISK HIGHER. COUNTERING AC BENEFITS IS THE RISK OF BLEEDING, ESPECIALLY FOR VULNERABLE OLDER ADULTS AND THOSE WITH COMORBIDITIES. FOR SOME PATIENTS, THE OPTIMAL DECISION MAY BE NOT TO USE AC AND/OR PURSUE LAAO I.E., PREVENTING EMBOLIZATION OF CLOTS WHERE THEY OCCUR MOST FREQUENTLY. DESPITE AVAILABLE OPTIONS, PROVIDERS DO NOT ALWAYS INDICATE TO PATIENTS THAT THERE IS A DECISION TO BE MADE OR PROVIDE PATIENTS WITH SUFFICIENT INFORMATION TO DECIDE. SHARED DECISION-MAKING (SDM) IS A GUIDELINE-RECOMMENDED, EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE TO ARRIVE AT THE OPTIMAL DECISION FOR A PATIENT. THE MAYO CLINIC’S ANTICOAGULATION CHOICE DECISION AID (AC DA) SUCCESSFULLY IMPROVED DECISION QUALITY, BUT LARGER- SCALE IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRES ADDITIONAL CONSIDERATION OF PATIENT AND PROVIDER ACCEPTABILITY AND WORKFLOWS. PATIENT PORTAL AND E-CHECK-IN USE ARE EXPANDING ACROSS DEMOGRAPHICS, MAKING PORTAL-BASED INTERVENTIONS FEASIBLE. THEREFORE, TO OVERCOME THE PRIOR IMPLEMENTATION GAPS, WE HAVE DEVELOPED A PROTOTYPE OF A PATIENT PORTAL-BASED AC DA TOOL ENHANCED WITH AN LAAO OPTION AND PROVIDER INTERFACE TO ALLOW THE PROVIDER TO REVIEW TOOL-SUPPLIED INFORMATION IN THE EHR. ACROSS 3 DIVERSE SITES WITH DIFFERENT EHRS - UMASS (EPIC), UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN- UMICH (EPIC), AND BAYSTATE (ORACLE HEALTH), WE WILL CONDUCT A HYBRID TYPE II EFFECTIVENESS- IMPLEMENTATION TRIAL WITH PROVIDER RANDOMIZATION. PATIENTS OF PROVIDERS ALLOCATED TO THE INTERVENTION WILL RECEIVE A REQUEST TO ACCESS OUR TOOL AS PART OF ROUTINE PRE-VISIT PORTAL INFORMATION GATHERING. TO UNDERSTAND THE IMPACT OF THE INTERVENTION, WE WILL PURSUE THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS. SPECIFIC AIMS INCLUDE: AIM 1: EFFECTIVENESS. IN 3,000 PATIENTS WITH AF HAVING VISITS WITH ~600 PROVIDERS OVER ONE YEAR, COMPARE THE FOLLOWING EFFECTIVENESS OUTCOMES OVERALL AND THEN AGAIN IN A PATIENT OF COLOR SUBSET (N=1084): QUALITY OF SDM - MEASURED THROUGH AN AFTER-VISIT SURVEY WITH SDM-Q-9 + DECISIONAL CONFLICT SCALE TO CAPTURE THE EXTENT TO WHICH PATIENTS FELT THEIR PROVIDER AIDED THEM BOTH IN DECIDING ABOUT INITIATING PROPHYLAXIS AND IN DECREASING DECISIONAL CONFLICT AROUND THE CHOICE; STROKE PROPHYLAXIS (PRIMARY)- AC INITIATION/LAAO AT 30 DAYS + AC PERSISTENCE OVER 1 YEAR; NET CLINICAL BENEFIT (EXPLORATORY) - OCCURRENCE OF AT LEAST ONE STROKE OR BLEEDING EVENT OVER 1 YEAR. AIM 2: IMPLEMENTATION. FOLLOWING THE PRACTICAL, ROBUST, IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINABILITY MODEL (PRISM), MEASURE REACH, ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION, MAINTENANCE (RE-AIM) AS WELL AS ORGANIZATIONAL FACTORS IN THE OVERALL POPULATION AND PATIENT OF COLOR SUBSET. OUR TEAM COMPOSED OF FACULTY FROM RECRUITMENT SITES UMASS, UMICH, BAYSTATE AND SEPARATELY, VICTORI MONTORI AT MAYO, HAS THE EXPERIENCE TO EXECUTE THE PROPOSED AIMS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GLYCEMIC OBSERVATION AND METABOLIC PROFILING OF MOTHERS IN PREGNANCY TO PREDICT CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH (GO MOMS PREDICT) - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH AMONG WOMEN IN THE UNITED STATES (US). PREGNANCY, EXPERIENCED BY >80% OF US WOMEN, UNMASKS CARDIOMETABOLIC DYSFUNCTION, PROVIDING A WINDOW INTO FUTURE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE RISK. DURING PREGNANCY CARE, UNIVERSAL BLOOD PRESSURE, BLOOD GLUCOSE AND OTHER LABORATORY SCREENINGS PROVIDE A VALUABLE OPPORTUNITY TO PREDICT AND PREVENT FUTURE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. YET, CURRENT PRACTICE RESULTS IN INADEQUATE IDENTIFICATION OF THOSE WHO COULD BENEFIT FROM EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION. OUR PRIOR WORK SUGGESTS THAT METABOLIC PROFILING DURING PREGNANCY COULD BE HARNESSED TO DEVELOP A NEW APPROACH FOR EARLY RECOGNITION OF FUTURE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE RISK DURING OBSTETRIC CARE. WE PROPOSE TO RE- ENVISION RISK ASSESSMENT FOR FUTURE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE IN PREGNANCY BY LEVERAGING OUR MULTICENTER OBSERVATIONAL COHORT STUDY (GO MOMS, N=2178), WHICH ENROLLED PARTICIPANTS DURING THE FIRST TRIMESTER AND COLLECTED GLYCEMIC, LIPID, AND OTHER CARDIOMETABOLIC DATA ACROSS GESTATION. THE PROPOSED STUDY (GO MOMS PREDICT, N=1565) WILL DEVELOP AND TEST NEW PREGNANCY CVD RISK ASSESSMENT MODELS FOR PREDICTION OF CARDIOVASCULAR RISK OUTCOMES 5 YEARS AFTER DELIVERY. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME IS A COMPOSITE OF ESTABLISHED, CLINICALLY ACTIONABLE CONDITIONS THAT ARE CAUSAL CVD RISK FACTORS: HYPERTENSION, PREDIABETES/DIABETES, AND HYPERCHOLESTEROLEMIA. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CARDIOMETABOLIC MEASURES IN PREGNANCY IMPROVE PREDICTION OF A COMPOSITE CVD RISK OUTCOME AT 5 YEARS POSTPARTUM OVER A BASE MODEL THAT INCLUDES PRE-PREGNANCY FACTORS (AGE, BMI, SMOKING, FAMILY HISTORY) AND PREGNANCY DIAGNOSES (GESTATIONAL DIABETES, HYPERTENSIVE DISORDERS OF PREGNANCY). GO MOMS PREDICT WILL CREATE A NEW PARADIGM FOR CVD RISK ASSESSMENT IN OBSTETRICS USING 3 COMPLEMENTARY APPROACHES: CONVENTIONAL CLINICAL TESTING (AIM 1), CUTTING-EDGE CGM PROFILING (AIM 2), AND METABOLIC SUBTYPING VIA MACHINE LEARNING (AIM 3). THIS PROPOSAL OPPORTUNISTICALLY LEVERAGES A UNIQUE OBSTETRIC COHORT TO ENABLE EARLY DETECTION OF CVD RISK THAT IS MODIFIABLE THROUGH LIFESTYLE AND PHARMACOLOGIC INTERVENTION, SETTING THE STAGE FOR A FUTURE CLINICAL TRIAL OF CVD RISK FACTOR PREVENTION IN AT RISK POSTPARTUM INDIVIDUALS. THE RESULTS OF GO MOMS PREDICT COULD TRANSFORM CVD RISK PROGNOSTICATION IN PREGNANCY, AFFORDING AN OPPORTUNITY TO PREVENT CVD ON A MASSIVE SCALE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ROLE OF THE ENDOCANNABINOID SYSTEM, METABOLIC DISEASE PROGRESSION, AND ASSOCIATED CARDIOVASCULAR RISK - PROJECT SUMMARY INDIVIDUALS WHO PROGRESS FROM HAVING OBESITY TO DEVELOPING OVERT DIABETES WILL EXPERIENCE, IN PARALLEL, A STEADY TWO- TO THREE-FOLD RISE IN THEIR RISK FOR CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. THE DYNAMIC AND COMPLEX DRIVERS OF BOTH ADVANCING METABOLIC DISEASE AND ITS ASSOCIATED CARDIOVASCULAR RISK REMAIN UNCLEAR. THE ENDOCANNABINOID SYSTEM IS AN ENDOGENOUS NETWORK OF SMALL LIPID SIGNALING MOLECULES INCLUDING CIRCULATING ENDOCANNABINOID SPECIES, SUCH AS ANANDAMIDE AND 2-ARACHIDONOYLGLYCEROL, WHICH NORMALLY INTERACT WITH CANNABINOID RECEPTORS TO REGULATE ENERGY BALANCE, APPETITE, AND LIPID METABOLISM. OVERACTIVATION OF THE ENDOCANNABINOID SYSTEM IS KNOWN TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE PROGRESSION OF METABOLIC DISEASES WHILE CONCURRENTLY INTERFACING WITH PRO-ATHEROGENIC VASCULAR MECHANISMS. PHARMACOLOGICAL INTERVENTIONS DESIGNED TO TARGET THE ENDOGENOUS ENDOCANNABINOID SYSTEM HAVE DEMONSTRATED THE POTENTIAL TO MITIGATE THESE METABOLIC DISTURBANCES IN CLINICAL STUDIES. DESPITE THESE ADVANCES, HOWEVER, PROGRESS HAS BEEN STYMIED BY A STILL LIMITED UNDERSTANDING OF THE COMPLEX INTERRELATIONS AMONG CIRCULATING ENDOCANNABINOIDS AND THEIR ROLE IN CONTRIBUTING TO HUMAN METABOLIC PHYSIOLOGICAL AND PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL PROCESSES. IN PRELIMINARY WORK, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED A NUMBER OF DISTINCT ENDOCANNABINOIDS AND RELATED SPECIES THAT APPEAR CONCORDANTLY RELATED TO RISK FOR BOTH INCIDENT DIABETES AND INCIDENT CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. OUR MOST RECENT FINDINGS NOW INDICATE THAT A SUBSET OF THESE BIOACTIVE LIPIDS IS ASSOCIATED WITH METABOLIC RELATED CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE IN A CONTEXT DEPENDENT MANNER – OFFERING A POTENTIAL EXPLANATION FOR THE MIXED RESULTS SEEN IN PRIOR CLINICAL TRIALS OF CANNABINOID RECEPTOR INHIBITORS OR INVERSE AGONISTS. TO INFORM ONGOING EFFORTS TO DEVELOP NEW AND TAILOR EXISTING METABOLIC THERAPIES, WE NOW PROPOSE A COMPREHENSIVE PROSPECTIVE INVESTIGATION DESIGNED TO MORE PRECISELY IDENTIFY THE KEY ENDOCANNABINOID PATHWAYS THAT UNDERLIE PROGRESSIVE METABOLIC DISEASE AND ITS ASSOCIATED CARDIOVASCULAR RISK. WE ANTICIPATE THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE THE CRITICAL INSIGHTS NEEDED TO EFFECTIVELY DEVELOP AND TAILOR INTERVENTIONS, INCLUDING EXISTING AND NOVEL THERAPIES, AIMED AT MITIGATING EXCESS CARDIOVASCULAR RISKS FOR ALL PERSONS WITH METABOLIC DISEASE INCLUDING THOSE WITH OBESITY AND/OR DIABETES.

description: IMPROVING EXTERNAL VALIDITY OF THE RECHARGE TRIAL THROUGH A PARTIALLY RANDOMIZED PATIENT PREFERENCE FRAMEWORK - PROJECT SUMMARY CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE (CAD) REMAINS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH FOR AMERICANS OF ALL SEXES, RACES, AND ETHNICITIES, YET RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS (RCTS) INFORMING PRACTICE GUIDELINES HAVE PREDOMINANTLY ENROLLED WHITE MEN. OBSERVATIONAL DATA SUGGEST THAT OUTCOMES AFTER CORONARY ARTERY BYPASS GRAFTING (CABG) AND PERCUTANEOUS CORONARY INTERVENTION (PCI) VARY BY SEX AND RACE. TO ADDRESS THIS, THE RECHARGE (REVASCULARIZATION CHOICES AMONG UNDER-REPRESENTED GROUPS EVALUATION) PROGRAM WAS DEVELOPED. IT INCLUDES TWO INTEGRATED, MULTICENTER, OPEN-LABEL, 1:1 RANDOMIZED SUPERIORITY TRIALS—RECHARGE:WOMEN (NCT06399692) AND RECHARGE:MINORITIES (NCT06399705)—FUNDED BY THE US PATIENT-CENTERED OUTCOMES RESEARCH INSTITUTE (PCORI). THE TRIALS WILL ENROLL 1,200 PATIENTS IN UP TO 100 SITES TO COMPARE PCI VS. CABG IN WOMEN AND BLACK OR HISPANIC PATIENTS WITH MULTIVESSEL CAD REFERRED FOR REVASCULARIZATION. THE PRIMARY ENDPOINT IS A HIERARCHICAL COMPOSITE OF DEATH AND TIME-AVERAGED CHANGE IN GENERIC QUALITY OF LIFE. RECHARGE HAS BROAD INCLUSION CRITERIA TO MAXIMIZE EXTERNAL VALIDITY, BUT STRONG PATIENT PREFERENCES FOR CABG OR PCI MAY LEAD TO RANDOMIZATION REFUSAL, LIMITING GENERALIZABILITY. IN RECHARGE'S FEASIBILITY PHASE, 80% OF ELIGIBLE PATIENTS DECLINE PARTICIPATION DUE TO TREATMENT PREFERENCES. BY ENROLLING THESE PATIENTS IN A PARALLEL  PREFERENCE COHORT  WITHIN A UNIFIED PARTIALLY RANDOMIZED PATIENT PREFERENCE (PRPP) ANALYTIC FRAMEWORK, WE CAN ENHANCE EXTERNAL VALIDITY. PRPP TRIALS HAVE NEVER BEEN USED IN CORONARY REVASCULARIZATION, WHERE PATIENT PREFERENCES STRONGLY INFLUENCE DECISION-MAKING. WITH RECHARGE ENTERING ITS FULL PHASE IN NOVEMBER 2025, WE HAVE A TIME-SENSITIVE OPPORTUNITY TO INTEGRATE A PRPP FRAMEWORK TO (I) IMPROVE GENERALIZABILITY AND (II) EVALUATE THE FEASIBILITY OF INCORPORATING PREFERENCE COHORTS IN CARDIOVASCULAR RCTS. WE WILL ENROLL 1,000 WOMEN AND 1,000 BLACK OR HISPANIC PATIENTS WHO DECLINE RANDOMIZATION IN RECHARGE INTO A PARALLEL OBSERVATIONAL COHORT. WE WILL COLLECT DETAILED BASELINE CHARACTERISTICS, DOCUMENT REASONS FOR DECLINING RANDOMIZATION, AND TRACK OUTCOMES IN PARALLEL WITH THE RANDOMIZED COHORT. IN AIM I, WE WILL DETERMINE SOCIAL, BIOLOGICAL, AND INSTITUTIONAL PREDICTORS OF UNWILLINGNESS TO BE RANDOMIZED TO CABG VS. PCI, TO UNDERSTAND WHICH WOMEN AND BLACK AND HISPANIC PATIENTS THE RCT FINDINGS ARE DIRECTLY APPLICABLE TO. IN AIM II WE WILL FIRST POOL PATIENTS FROM THE RCTS AND OBSERVATIONAL COHORTS TO DEVELOP PREDICTION MODELS FOR THE STRENGTH OF PREFERENCE FOR CABG VERSUS PCI, AND THEN USE THESE MODELS TO EXTRAPOLATE THE TREATMENT EFFECTS OBSERVED IN THE RANDOMIZED COHORT TO THE FULL COHORT OF ELIGIBLE PATIENTS. IN AIM III WE WILL ANALYZE OUTCOMES DATA FOR RECHARGE:PRPP COHORT TO IMPROVE PRECISION IN THE ESTIMATED AVERAGE TREATMENT EFFECT FROM THE RCT AND EXPLORE TREATMENT EFFECT HETEROGENEITY ACROSS PATIENT CHARACTERISTICS. BY INTEGRATING THE PATIENTS WHO DECLINED RANDOMIZATION IN THE RCTS IN A PRPP FRAMEWORK ALONGSIDE THE RCT COHORTS, RECHARGE:PRPP WILL PROVIDE A MORE REPRESENTATIVE EVALUATION OF CABG VS. PCI, SETTING A PRECEDENT FOR FUTURE CARDIOVASCULAR RCTS.

description: PHYSICAL FUNCTION AND ACTIVITY POST CARDIAC EVENT IN FEMALES: EFFECTS OF MOVEMENT-RELATED ANXIETY - PROJECT SUMMARY WOMEN EXPERIENCING A MAJOR ACUTE CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT (MACE) TYPICALLY DISPLAY PROLONGED PHYSICAL INACTIVITY AND MORE SEVERE FUNCTIONAL DECLINE DURING HOSPITALIZATION THAN MEN. TO REGAIN INDEPENDENCE, RESUMPTION OF FREE-LIVING PHYSICAL ACTIVITY (PA) AND RECOVERY OF PHYSICAL FUNCTION (I.E., BALANCE, MOBILITY, STRENGTH) ARE CRUCIAL, YET WOMEN ALSO DEMONSTRATE A RECOVERY GAP POST-MACE RELATIVE TO MEN. ONE POSSIBLE EXPLANATION FOR THIS RECOVERY GAP IS AVOIDANCE OF PA DUE TO HEIGHTENED ATTENTION TO BODILY SENSATIONS AND AN OVERABUNDANT PERCEPTION OF RISK FOR RECURRENT CARDIAC EVENTS, INJURY, OR FALLING. BY REDUCING EXERCISE AS WELL AS EVERYDAY MOVEMENTS SUCH AS THOSE ASSOCIATED WITH ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING (E.G., CARRYING LAUNDRY UP THE STAIRS), INDIVIDUALS PARADOXICALLY INCREASE THEIR RISK OF FALLING, REINFARCTION, INJURY, DECONDITIONING, AND ULTIMATELY LOSS OF INDEPENDENCE. GIVEN THAT ANXIETY IS UP TO TWICE AS PREVALENT IN WOMEN AS IN MEN, AND THAT WOMEN ARE AT ESPECIALLY ELEVATED RISK OF FALLS AND INJURY RELATIVE TO MEN DUE TO ESTROGEN-RELATED DECLINES IN MUSCLE MASS, STRENGTH, AND BALANCE, ANXIETY-DRIVEN ACTIVITY AVOIDANCE MAY DISPROPORTIONATELY UNDERMINE WOMEN’S PHYSICAL RECOVERY. WE WILL RECRUIT 489 WOMEN AGED 18 OR OLDER HOSPITALIZED FOR MACE AND TREATED WITH PERCUTANEOUS CORONARY INTERVENTION (PCI) PRIOR TO DISCHARGE FROM HOSPITALS AFFILIATED WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS MEDICAL BRANCH, RUTGERS UNIVERSITY, AND BROWN UNIVERSITY HEALTH. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE PROSPECTIVELY EVALUATED AT THEIR INDEX HOSPITALIZATION AND AGAIN AT 1 WEEK AND 1, 3-, 6-, 9-, AND 12-MONTHS POST-DISCHARGE. OUR MULTI-PRONGED APPROACH WILL INCLUDE ACCELEROMETRY USING NOVEL ALGORITHMS THAT BETTER CAPTURE STEPS IN THIS UNIQUE POPULATION, AS WELL AS ASSESSMENTS OF FUNCTIONAL PHYSICAL PERFORMANCE, PSYCHOSOCIAL FACTORS, SYMPTOMS, AND COGNITION. FIRST, WE WILL EXAMINE BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL PREDICTORS OF ANXIETY AND LOW PHYSICAL FUNCTION DURING HOSPITALIZATION, HYPOTHESIZING THAT BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL CHARACTERISTICS WILL DISTINCTLY CLUSTER WITH ANXIETY AND LOWER PHYSICAL FUNCTION. SECOND, WE WILL DETERMINE AGE-BASED TRAJECTORIES OF ANXIETY, PHYSICAL FUNCTION, AND PA POST- DISCHARGE, HYPOTHESIZING THAT THESE TRAJECTORIES WILL DIFFER BY AGE. WE WILL USE PARALLEL PROCESS LONGITUDINAL LATENT CLASS ANALYSIS TO INVESTIGATE ASSOCIATIONS OVER TIME BETWEEN MOVEMENT-RELATED ANXIETY AND PHYSICAL FUNCTION ACROSS DIFFERENT CLASSES. FINALLY, WE WILL EXAMINE TIME-INVARIANT BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCE FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH CLASS MEMBERSHIP, HYPOTHESIZING THAT SOME WOMEN WILL DEMONSTRATE PERSISTENTLY HIGH ANXIETY AND LOW PHYSICAL FUNCTION IN THE RECOVERY YEAR. THIS EMPIRICALLY GUIDED APPROACH WILL ALLOW US TO DEFINE AND CHARACTERIZE WOMEN AT HIGH RISK FOR BOTH ANXIETY AND POOR FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY WHO WOULD BE BEST TARGETED BY A FUTURE AUGMENTATIVE TREATMENT. OUR ULTIMATE GOALS ARE TO INFORM THEORIES OF MACE RECOVERY IN WOMEN AND IMPROVE PSYCHOLOGICAL AND PHYSICAL FUNCTION IN WOMEN TO PRESERVE HEALTH, INDEPENDENCE, AND FUNCTIONING ACROSS THE ADULT LIFESPAN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TESTING THE IMPLEMENTATION AND EFFECTIVENESS OF ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD-BASED INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE HYPERTENSION CONTROL - HYPERTENSION AFFECTS ONE IN THREE U.S. ADULTS AND IS A LEADING MODIFIABLE RISK FACTOR FOR CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. DESPITE WIDELY AVAILABLE, LOW-COST MEDICATIONS AND CLEAR CLINICAL GUIDELINES, FEWER THAN HALF OF PATIENTS WITH HYPERTENSION ACHIEVE ADEQUATE BLOOD PRESSURE CONTROL. KEY CONTRIBUTORS INCLUDE LACK OF TREATMENT INTENSIFICATION, SUBOPTIMAL ADHERENCE, AND INSUFFICIENT FOLLOW-UP, PARTICULARLY PRONOUNCED IN PRIMARY CARE.  ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR) INTERVENTIONS OFFER SCALABLE OPPORTUNITIES TO IMPROVE HYPERTENSION MANAGEMENT, YET FEW MULTI-COMPONENT EHR-BASED INTERVENTIONS HAVE BEEN RIGOROUSLY EVALUATED IN REAL-WORLD U.S. PRIMARY CARE SETTINGS, ESPECIALLY THOSE SERVING DIVERSE POPULATIONS. IN OUR PRIOR NIH-FUNDED TRIAL OF 49,210 PATIENTS AND 560 PRIMARY CARE PROVIDERS (PCPS), WE DEVELOPED AND TESTED THE REDUCE-BP INTERVENTION, A MULTI-COMPONENT EHR-BASED STRATEGY THAT INCLUDES POINT-OF-CARE TOOLS FOR PRIMARY CARE PROVIDERS, AN EHR- EMBEDDED DASHBOARD TO MONITOR HYPERTENSION CONTROL, AND SOCIAL NEEDS SCREENING AND REFERRAL TOOLS. ALTHOUGH THE INTERVENTION SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVED SYSTOLIC BLOOD PRESSURE AT THE POPULATION LEVEL (0.6 MMHG REDUCTION VS. USUAL CARE), ITS IMPACT WAS MARKEDLY HIGHER, UP TO 10 MMHG SBP REDUCTIONS, WHEN THE TOOLS WERE ACTIVELY USED. THESE FINDINGS INDICATE THAT LIMITED UPTAKE WAS THE PRINCIPAL BARRIER TO EFFECTIVENESS.  TO ADDRESS THIS, OUR STUDY TEAM CONDUCTED A POST-TRIAL IMPLEMENTATION EVALUATION GUIDED BY THE CONSOLIDATED FRAMEWORK FOR IMPLEMENTATION RESEARCH (CFIR). THROUGH SURVEYS AND INTERVIEWS, WE IDENTIFIED AND PRIORITIZED KEY BARRIERS TO REDUCE-BP INTERVENTION IMPLEMENTATION. USING CFIR AND THE EXPERT RECOMMENDATIONS FOR IMPLEMENTING CHANGE (ERIC), WE MAPPED THESE BARRIERS TO CANDIDATE IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES AND PRIORITIZED SIX COMBINATIONS. THIS PROJECT WILL BE CONDUCTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH ADVOCATE HEALTH CARE, A LARGE HEALTH SYSTEM WHERE WE HAVE BUILT A STRONG COLLABORATIVE INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE PAST 5 YEARS.  THE AIMS ARE TO: (1) TO PRIORITIZE AND PILOT TEST IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES FOR THE EVIDENCE-BASED REDUCE- BP INTERVENTION, AND (2) CONDUCT A 3-ARM PRAGMATIC EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION HYBRID TYPE 2 TRIAL TO TEST TWO IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES FOR THE REDUCE-BP INTERVENTION COMPARED TO USUAL CARE. IN AIM 1, WE WILL REFINE SIX PRE-IDENTIFIED IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY ARMS, ALL DRAWING FROM PEER CHAMPIONS, AUDIT AND FEEDBACK, AND TRAINING AND EDUCATION, AND PILOT THEM IN LOW-FIDELITY CONDITIONS ACROSS THREE PRIMARY CARE CLINICS. WE WILL THEN SELECT AND REFINE THE TWO MOST PROMISING FOR FURTHER TESTING. IN AIM 2, WE WILL CLUSTER-RANDOMIZE 24 PRIMARY CARE PRACTICES TO THE TWO MOST PROMISING IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES OR USUAL CARE. OUTCOMES WILL BE EVALUATED ACROSS AT LEAST 40,000 ADULT PATIENTS WITH ELEVATED BLOOD PRESSURE OVER A 12-MONTH FOLLOW-UP.  THIS STUDY OFFERS A SCALABLE, HEALTH SYSTEM–EMBEDDED SOLUTION TO IMPROVE HYPERTENSION OUTCOMES BY OPTIMIZING IMPLEMENTATION OF AN EXISTING, EVIDENCE-BASED EHR INTERVENTION. FINDINGS WILL YIELD GENERALIZABLE INSIGHTS FOR EMPLOYING IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES IN PRIMARY CARE SETTINGS FOR MULTI-COMPONENT EHR TOOLS.

description: MECHANISMS MEDIATING THE EXAGGERATED EXERCISE PRESSOR REFLEX IN A MURINE MODEL OF HINDLIMB ISCHEMIA - PERIPHERAL ARTERY DISEASE (PAD) IS A PREVALENT DISEASE RESULTING IN LOWER LIMB ISCHEMIA AND IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF AMPUTATIONS. PAD IS ASSOCIATED WITH HIGH CARDIOVASCULAR MORTALITY AND IS ESTIMATED TO OCCUR IN 20-25% OF THE OCTOGENARIAN POPULATION. WHILE A MULTIFACETED APPROACH, INCLUDING LIPID LOWERING AGENTS, ANTIPLATELET AND ANTICOAGULATION THERAPIES, IS USED FOR THE TREATMENT OF THIS DISEASE, ONE MAJOR THERAPEUTIC FOCUS IS EXERCISE. EXERCISE IS BELIEVED TO BE BENEFICIAL IN IMPROVING FUNCTIONAL CAPACITY IN PATIENTS WITH PAD YET EXERCISE HAS ALSO BEEN DEMONSTRATED TO EVOKE AN ABNORMAL AND EXAGGERATED CARDIOVASCULAR RESPONSE IN PATIENTS WITH PAD. THESE ABNORMALITIES ARE HIGHLY CORRELATED WITH MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY, HOWEVER, THE MECHANISM(S) THAT MEDIATES THESE ABNORMALITIES IS UNCLEAR. THE EXERCISE PRESSOR REFLEX (EPR) IS EVOKED BY MUSCLE CONTRACTION AND PROPAGATED VIA GROUP III (PREDOMINATELY MECHANICALLY-SENSITIVE) AND GROUP IV (PREDOMINATELY METABOLICALLY- SENSITIVE) AFFERENT FIBERS RESULTING IN A RISE IN MEAN ARTERIAL PRESSURE (MAP) AND HEART RATE (HR). THESE REFLEXIVE CARDIOVASCULAR FUNCTIONS SERVE TO MAINTAIN ADEQUATE BLOOD FLOW TO EXERCISING MUSCLE AND ABNORMALITIES IN THE EPR ARE CORRELATED WITH SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED CARDIOVASCULAR RISK. WE HAVE DEVELOPED A NOVEL MURINE MOUSE MODEL FOR THE STUDY OF THE EPR. WITH OUR MOUSE MODEL, WE HAVE MADE MECHANISTIC DISCOVERIES DEMONSTRATING THAT THE EPR IS EXAGGERATED IN MICE WITH HINDLIMB ISCHEMIA AND, FURTHER, THAT THESE MICE DISPLAY REDUCED TOLERANCE FOR EXERCISE. WE HAVE DETERMINED THAT THE EXAGGERATED EPR IS MEDIATED BY MECHANOSENSITIVE AFFERENT NEURONS AND THAT THESE RESPONSES ARE MEDIATED, IN PART, BY ACTIVATION OF THE PIEZO2 ION CHANNEL. IN THE PROPOSED STUDIES, WE WILL USE PIEZO2 REPORTER MICE AS WELL AS MICE IN WHICH WE HAVE CONDITIONALLY DELETED PIEZO2 FROM DORSAL ROOT GANGLIA (DRG) TO FULLY CHARACTERIZE THE MECHANISMS THAT MEDIATE THE EXAGGERATED EPR IN HINDLIMB ISCHEMIA. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE WILL USE MORPHOLOGICAL, HISTOLOGICAL, PHYSIOLOGICAL, MOLECULAR, AND WHOLE CELL PATCH CLAMP TECHNOLOGIES TO DEFINE THE PATHOLOGICAL MECHANISM(S) THAT DRIVE THE EXAGGERATED EPR AS WELL AS REDUCED EXERCISE TOLERANCE IN HINDLIMB ISCHEMIA. OUR HYPOTHESIS IS THAT PIEZO2 EXPRESSING MECHANOSENSITIVE AFFERENT NEURONS MEDIATE THE EXAGGERATED EPR IN MICE WITH HINDLIMB ISCHEMIA. WE WILL RIGOROUSLY TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS AND INTERROGATE THE DOWNSTREAM PATHWAYS OF PIEZO2 TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL THERAPIES IN NORMALIZING THE EPR IN ISCHEMIA TO ALLOW FOR THE SAFE PRESCRIPTION OF EXERCISE IN PAD PATIENTS.

description: A MULTISCALE MODELING APPROACH TO UNCOVER MECHANISMS BY WHICH PROCOAGULANT AGENTS RESTORE HEMOSTASIS IN PLATELET INTEGRIN DISORDERS - PROJECT SUMMARY GLANZMANN'S THROMBASTHENIA (GT) IS A RARE CONGENITAL BLEEDING DISORDER CAUSED BY DEFICIENCY OR DYSFUNCTION OF THE PLATELET INTEGRIN ΩIIBΕ3, WHICH MEDIATES PLATELET-PLATELET COHESION ESSENTIAL FOR STABLE CLOT FORMATION. THE STANDARD OF CARE FOR SEVERE BLEEDING IN GT AND OTHER PLATELET INTEGRIN DISORDERS (PIDS) IS PLATELET TRANSFUSION. WHEN PLATELETS ARE NOT AVAILABLE, PROCOAGULANT AGENTS SUCH AS RECOMBINANT ACTIVATED FACTOR VII (RFVIIA) ARE USED. HOWEVER, TREATMENT REMAINS LARGELY EMPIRICAL BECAUSE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH RFVIIA AND TRANSFUSED PLATELETS RESTORE HEMOSTASIS IN THE PRESENCE OF DYSFUNCTIONAL ENDOGENOUS PLATELETS ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD. IT IS UNCLEAR WHETHER GT PLATELETS CAN ADOPT A PROCOAGULANT PHENOTYPE, WHETHER PROCOAGULANT PLATELETS ARE REQUIRED FOR RFVIIA EFFICACY, AND HOW ΩIIBΕ3-DEFICIENT PLATELETS INTERACT WITH FIBRIN. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES ALONE CANNOT RESOLVE THESE QUESTIONS DUE TO THE COMPLEXITY OF PLATELET FUNCTIONS, THE INABILITY TO SELECTIVELY BLOCK SPECIFIC INTERACTIONS IN VIVO, AND THE LOW THROUGHPUT OF ANIMAL MODELS. THIS GAP IN MECHANISTIC UNDER- STANDING LIMITS THE DEVELOPMENT OF TARGETED, DURABLE THERAPIES FOR GT AND RELATED DISORDERS. COMPUTATIONAL APPROACHES, USED ALONGSIDE EXPERIMENTAL ONES, OFFER MECHANISTIC HYPOTHESIS GENERATION, OPTIMIZATION IN SE- LECTING TARGETED EXPERIMENTS, AND VISUALIZATION THAT EXPERIMENTS ALONE CANNOT ACHIEVE. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO DEVELOP A COMPUTATIONAL MODELING FRAMEWORK THAT INTEGRATES THE BIOCHEMISTRY, BIOPHYSICS, AND BIOME- CHANICS OF CLOTTING WITH EXPERIMENTAL DATA TO PROVIDE ACCURATE MECHANISTIC PREDICTIONS FOR BLEEDING AND CLOTTING DISORDERS. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS APPLICATION IS TO DEVELOP SPARKS-DCM, AN EXPERIMENTALLY VALIDATED MULTISCALE COMPUTATIONAL MODELING FRAMEWORK THAT INCLUDES SINGLE-PLATELET RESOLUTION AND ON-PLATELET BIOCHEM- ISTRY TO ENABLE MECHANISTIC STUDIES OF PIDS. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT GPVI ENABLES ΩIIBΕ3-INDEPENDENT HEMOSTASIS BY (1) ENHANCING PLATELET PROCOAGULANT ACTIVITY UPON ACTIVATION BY COLLAGEN OR FIBRIN AND (2) ANCHOR- ING ΩIIBΕ3-DEFICIENT PLATELETS TO THE FIBRIN NETWORK. THE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE TO 1) DEVELOP A MICROSCALE MODEL OF PLATELET BONDING AND SURFACE-DEPENDENT COAGULATION REACTIONS (SPARKS-D), 2) DEVELOP THE MESOSCALE MODEL AND CREATE SPARKS-DCM THROUGH TWO-WAY COUPLING OF FLUID DYNAMICS AND PLATELET REACTIONS, AND 3) DETER- MINE THE ROLE OF GPVI IN THE PROHEMOSTATIC EFFECTS OF RFVIIA AND PLATELET TRANSFUSION IN PIDS. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE, BY INTEGRATING COMPUTATIONAL MODELS AND EXPERIMENTS, IT WILL REVEAL THE MECH- ANISMS THAT RESTORE HEMOSTASIS IN PIDS AND OFFER A FREELY-AVAILABLE COMPUTATIONAL TOOL TO STUDY AND TEST NOVEL PROHEMOSTATICS IN PIDS. THESE OUTCOMES ARE EXPECTED TO POSITIVELY IMPACT TREATMENT STRATEGIES FOR PIDS AND BLEEDING DISORDERS MORE BROADLY BY PROVIDING EVIDENCE-BASED SELECTION OF PROHEMOSTATIC AGENTS WITH PLATELET TRANSFUSION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENHANCING OXPHOS EFFICIENCY TO PROMOTE MUSCLE FUNCTION AND REGENERATION IN PERIPHERAL ARTERY DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT PERIPHERAL ARTERIAL DISEASE (PAD), CAUSED BY ATHEROSCLEROTIC NARROWING OR OCCLUSION IN THE LOWER EXTREMITIES, IS A LEADING CAUSE OF CARDIOVASCULAR MORTALITY. CURRENT MEDICAL MANAGEMENT GUIDELINES FOR PAD CENTER ON REDUCING CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT RISK, HOWEVER, THE DECREASE BLOOD FLOW TO THE LEGS OF PATIENTS WITH PAD IMPAIRS LEG FUNCTION, LIMITS WALKING ABILITY, AND COMPROMISES QUALITY OF LIFE. UNFORTUNATELY, THERE IS ONLY ONE MEDICATION (CILOSTAZOL) THAT IMPROVES WALKING PERFORMANCE IN PATIENTS WITH INTERMITTENT CLAUDICATION (A SYMPTOM OF MILD PAD), BUT ITS USE IS LIMITED DUE TO SIDE EFFECTS OR RISK OF ADVERSE EVENTS DUE TO CO-MORBID CONDITIONS (I.E., HEART FAILURE). THIS PROPOSAL FOCUSES ON DEVELOPING STRATEGIES TO OPTIMIZE LEG MUSCLE OXIDATIVE METABOLISM WITH THE GOAL OF IMPROVING THE ABILITY TO USE THE LIMITED OXYGEN AND NUTRIENTS THAT ARE DELIVERED TO THE PAD LIMB. HEREIN WE PROPOSE THAT FAM210A, A RECENTLY DISCOVERED MITOCHONDRIAL PROTEIN LOCATED WITHIN THE INNER MEMBRANE, IS A KEY REGULATOR OF MITOCHONDRIAL EFFICIENCY IN THE ISCHEMIC LIMB MUSCLE. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL EMPLOY POWERFUL GAIN- AND LOSS-OF-FUNCTION MOUSE MODELS TEST IF THE ABUNDANCE OF FAM210A IN THE MUSCLE DETERMINES ISCHEMIC MITOCHONDRIAL ENERGETIC EFFICIENCY AND THE LEG WORK OUTPUT. USING MECHANISTIC BIOCHEMICAL AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY ANALYSES, WE WILL ALSO DETERMINE HOW FAM210A REGULATES MITOCHONDRIAL ELECTRON TRANSPORT SYSTEM FUNCTION AND IDENTIFY ITS PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS WITHIN THE INNER MITOCHONDRIAL MEMBRANE USING HUMAN PATIENT MUSCLE BIOPSIES. BEYOND THE MUSCLE FIBER, WE WILL ALSO DETERMINE IF FAM210A REGULATES THE MUSCLE SATELLITE CELL FUNCTION, A KEY ASPECT OF ISCHEMIC MUSCLE REGENERATION AND SOURCE OF MITOCHONDRIA TO THE ISCHEMIC MUSCLE FIBERS. BY INTEGRATING PRECLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL EXPERIMENTS, THIS PROPOSAL IS POSITIONED TO IDENTIFY NOVEL MECHANISMS TO IMPROVE THE ENERGETIC EFFICIENCY IN THE ISCHEMIC LIMB FACILITATING OPTIMAL UTILIZATION OF OXYGEN AND NUTRIENTS AVAILABLE TO THE DISEASE LIMB TO PROMOTE IMPROVE LEG FUNCTION. THIS EXPERIMENTAL FRAMEWORK OFFERS A PLATFORM FOR DEVELOPING THERAPIES TO IMPROVE WALKING PERFORMANCE AND QUALITY OF LIFE IN PAD THROUGH OPTIMIZATION OF OXIDATIVE METABOLIC FUNCTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A PREVENTION-FOCUSED BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTION FOR PRESCHOOLERS VIA THEIR PARENTS - INSUFFICIENT SLEEP AFFECTS ONE IN THREE PRESCHOOL-AGED CHILDREN, INCREASING THEIR RISK FOR CHRONIC DISEASES, ALL- CAUSE MORTALITY, AND MENTAL HEALTH DIFFICULTIES. DESPITE THESE RISKS, FEW PREVENTION-FOCUSED SLEEP INTERVENTIONS ARE DEVELOPMENTALLY TAILORED FOR PRESCHOOL-AGED CHILDREN, A CRITICAL DEVELOPMENTAL PERIOD WHEN FOUNDATIONAL HEALTH HABITS ARE FORMED. ADDRESSING INSUFFICIENT SLEEP DURING THE PRESCHOOL YEARS IS NEEDED TO PREVENT SLEEP PROBLEMS FROM WORSENING, THUS IMPROVING POPULATION HEALTH AND REDUCING LONG-TERM HEALTHCARE COSTS. DOING SO WARRANTS IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENTAL CONSIDERATIONS AND DISTINCT INTERVENTION STRATEGIES TO STRENGTHEN EMOTION AND BEHAVIOR REGULATION SKILLS. FURTHERMORE, CHILD SLEEP PROBLEMS CAN DISRUPT PARENTS’ OWN SLEEP AND WELLBEING, YET FEW INTERVENTIONS HAVE EVALUATED THE POTENTIAL DUAL BENEFITS FOR BOTH PARENT AND CHILD. THIS STUDY WILL ADDRESS THESE GAPS BY EVALUATING THE EFFICACY OF A PREVENTION-FOCUSED, BEHAVIORAL SLEEP INTERVENTION DELIVERED TO PARENTS OF PRESCHOOL-AGED CHILDREN. THIS STUDY AIMS TO IMPROVE CHILD SLEEP AND EXPLORE THE POTENTIAL BROADER BENEFITS FOR CHILD SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL FUNCTIONING, PARENT SLEEP, AND PARENT WELLBEING. A TWO-ARM RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL WILL BE CONDUCTED. PARENTS WITH A CHILD 2-4 YEARS OF AGE (N=198 DYADS) WILL BE ELIGIBLE. CHILDREN MUST HAVE INSUFFICIENT SLEEP AT BASELINE AND NO REPORTED SLEEP DISORDER, GIVEN THE FOCUS ON INDICATED PREVENTION. PARENTS WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO RECEIVE 1) THE SLEEP TIGHT INTERVENTION OR 2) A STANDARD-OF-CARE WAIT-LIST CONTROL. RECRUITMENT WILL OCCUR ON A ROLLING BASIS. THE SLEEP TIGHT INTERVENTION WILL BE DELIVERED IN TWO PHASES. FIRST, PARENTS WILL ATTEND WEEKLY VIRTUAL, ONE-ON-ONE SESSIONS WITH AN INTERVENTIONIST FOR 6 WEEKS. SECOND, 12 WEEKS OF BOOSTER MESSAGING WILL BE DELIVERED VIA TEXT MESSAGES AND BRIEF PHONE CALLS DURING A MAINTENANCE PERIOD. ASSESSMENTS WILL OCCUR AT BASELINE, POST-INTERVENTION (6 WEEKS), AND FOLLOW-UP TIMEPOINTS (18 WEEKS). THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE CHANGES IN CHILD NIGHTTIME SLEEP DURATION MEASURED VIA ACTIGRAPHY FROM BASELINE TO 18 WEEKS. SECONDARY OUTCOMES INCLUDE OTHER CHILD SLEEP PARAMETERS (EFFICIENCY, TIMING, DAYTIME AND 24-HOUR SLEEP), CHILD SOCIAL- EMOTIONAL WELLBEING (E.G., PROBLEM BEHAVIORS), AND PARENT OUTCOMES (SLEEP, STRESS, PERSONAL FUNCTIONING) ACROSS TIMEPOINTS. A MIXED-METHODS PROCESS EVALUATION, INCLUDING PARENT INTERVIEWS, WILL BE USED TO ASSESS BARRIERS AND FACILITATORS TO IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINABILITY, TO INFORM FUTURE DISSEMINATION. IF EFFECTIVE, THIS STUDY WILL YIELD CRUCIAL KNOWLEDGE ON A PREVENTION-FOCUSED BEHAVIORAL SLEEP INTERVENTION DELIVERED TO PARENTS OF PRESCHOOL-AGED CHILDREN WHILE EVALUATING THE POTENTIAL BROADER BENEFITS FOR CHILD AND PARENT WELLBEING. ULTIMATELY, THIS WORK SEEKS TO IMPROVE CHILD SLEEP AS A PATHWAY FOR PROMOTING PHYSICAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL HEALTH AND PARENT WELLBEING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LIMITING RNA PSEUDOURIDYLATION TO TREAT ADVERSE CARDIAC REMODELING AND HEART FAILURE - 1 PROJECT SUMMARY  2 HEART FAILURE AFFECTS OVER 6 MILLION AMERICANS WITH 5-YEAR MORTALITY RATES APPROACHING 50%, REPRESENTING AN 3 URGENT UNMET THERAPEUTIC NEED. CURRENT FDA-APPROVED THERAPIES FAIL TO DIRECTLY TARGET ADVERSE CARDIAC 4 REMODELING, THE FUNDAMENTAL PATHOLOGICAL PROCESS DRIVING DISEASE PROGRESSION. THIS PROPOSAL DEVELOPS  5 PSEUDOURIDINE SYNTHASE 7 (PUS7) AS A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGET FOR PREVENTING CARDIAC REMODELING AND TREATING  6 HEART FAILURE. PSEUDOURIDINE REPRESENTS THE MOST ABUNDANT RNA MODIFICATION ACROSS ALL LIFE FORMS, YET ITS ROLE IN  7 CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE REMAINS UNEXPLORED. OUR RECENT STUDY DEMONSTRATED THAT PUS7 INHIBITION ACTIVATES RNA  8 AUTOPHAGY, PROVIDING ORGAN PROTECTION THROUGH SELECTIVE DEGRADATION OF DEFICIENT TRANSCRIPTS. BUILDING ON THIS 9 BREAKTHROUGH, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THERAPEUTIC TARGETING OF PUS7 INDUCES PSEUDOURIDINE DEFICIENCY IN 10 PATHOLOGICAL FIBROTIC AND HYPERTROPHIC MRNAS, PROMOTING THEIR AUTOPHAGIC DEGRADATION AND PREVENTING ADVERSE 11 CARDIAC REMODELING. OUR COMPELLING PRECLINICAL DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT PUS7 INHIBITION PROVIDES REMARKABLE 12 CARDIOPROTECTION: PUS7+/- MICE SHOW SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVED CARDIAC FUNCTION AND REDUCED PATHOLOGICAL 13 REMODELING IN BOTH MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION AND PRESSURE OVERLOAD MODELS. MECHANISTICAL STUDY CONFIRMED THAT 14 PUS7 INHIBITION ACTIVATES RNA AUTOPHAGY IN CARDIAC CELLS/TISSUES. WE HAVE DEVELOPED TWO COMPLEMENTARY 15 THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES: ANTISENSE OLIGONUCLEOTIDES (ASOS) TARGETING PUS7 MRNA AND A SMALL MOLECULE PUS7 16 INHIBITOR (C17), BOTH SHOWING SIGNIFICANT CARDIOPROTECTIVE EFFECTS IN CELL CULTURE MODELS. WE PROPOSE THREE SPECIFIC 17 AIMS TO ADVANCE THIS THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM. FIRST, WE WILL ESTABLISH THE MECHANISTIC BASIS FOR PUS7- 18 TARGETED THERAPY BY CHARACTERIZING THE PSEUDOURIDYLATION DYNAMICS AND FATES OF PUS7-TARGETED FIBROTIC AND 19 HYPERTROPHIC MRNAS DURING CARDIAC REMODELING USING OPTIMIZED PSEUDO-SEQ AND RNA FLUORESCENCE IN SITU 20 HYBRIDIZATION IN CARDIAC CELL CULTURE MODELS. SECOND, WE WILL DEFINE CELL-TYPE-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS UNDERLYING 21 PUS7-SILENCING-INDUCED CARDIOPROTECTION IN CARDIAC REMODELING USING CONDITIONAL PUS7 KNOCKOUT MICE COMBINED 22 WITH SINGLE-NUCLEUS RNA SEQUENCING, WITH A FOCUS ON PRESSURE OVERLOAD-INDUCED CARDIOMYOPATHY MODEL. THIRD, 23 WE WILL ADVANCE BOTH ASO AND SMALL MOLECULE CANDIDATES THROUGH RIGOROUS PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT, INCLUDING 24 PHARMACOKINETIC/PHARMACODYNAMIC CHARACTERIZATION, DOSE OPTIMIZATION, AND EFFICACY EVALUATION IN THE MURINE 25 PRESSURE OVERLOAD MODEL. THIS STUDY REPRESENTS A PIONEERING INVESTIGATION DEFINING FUNCTIONAL ROLES OF RNA 26 PSEUDOURIDYLATION IN CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION WILL ESTABLISH PUS7 AS A DRUGGABLE TARGET 27 WITH TWO VALIDATED THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES, POTENTIALLY LEADING TO PROMISING THERAPIES SPECIFICALLY TARGETING 28 ADVERSE CARDIAC REMODELING AND HEART FAILURE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PET IMAGING TO DEFINE MECHANISMS AND STRATIFY RISK IN ARRHYTHMOGENIC CARDIOMYOPATHY - PROJECT SUMMARY ARRHYTHMOGENIC CARDIOMYOPATHY (ACM) IS A HERITABLE HEART DISEASE CHARACTERIZED BY LETHAL ARRHYTHMIAS, PROGRESSIVE HEART FAILURE, AND SUDDEN CARDIAC DEATH IN OTHERWISE YOUNG, HEALTHY INDIVIDUALS. ALTHOUGH CAUSATIVE MUTATIONS IN DESMOSOMAL PROTEINS HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED, THERE REMAINS NO RELIABLE WAY TO PREDICT WHICH MUTATION CARRIERS WILL DEVELOP DISEASE. THIS LACK OF PROGNOSTIC TOOLS LEAVES PATIENTS AND FAMILIES WITHOUT EFFECTIVE RISK-STRATIFICATION STRATEGIES.  POSITRON EMISSION TOMOGRAPHY (PET) USING [18F]FLUORODEOXYGLUCOSE (FDG) DETECTS MYOCARDIAL INFLAMMATION AND HYPERMETABOLISM. BOTH OUR PRELIMINARY WORK AND PUBLISHED STUDIES DEMONSTRATE INCREASED FDG UPTAKE IN ACM, BUT THE CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE AND UNDERLYING CELLULAR SOURCES OF THIS SIGNAL REMAIN UNCLEAR. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT PET IMAGING CAN SERVE AS A NON-INVASIVE PREDICTIVE IMAGING TOOL TO DETECT AND PREDICT ACM DISEASE DEVELOPMENT AND PROGRESSION. WE PROPOSE THAT FDG UPTAKE REFLECTS IMMUNE CELL INFILTRATION WITHIN THE MYOCARDIUM, AND THAT CCR2⁺ MONOCYTE-DERIVED MACROPHAGES REPRESENT A CRITICAL POPULATION DRIVING ARRHYTHMIAS, VENTRICULAR REMODELING, AND ADVERSE OUTCOMES.  TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL INTEGRATE MOLECULAR IMAGING, IMMUNE PROFILING, AND CARDIAC PHYSIOLOGY IN MECHANISTICALLY RELEVANT MOUSE MODELS OF ACM. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DEFINE THE IMMUNE AND CARDIAC CELL POPULATIONS RESPONSIBLE FOR FDG UPTAKE, TESTING WHETHER GLOBAL MACROPHAGE PROLIFERATION ACCOUNTS FOR THE PET SIGNAL WHILE CCR2⁺ SUBSETS DETERMINE DISEASE PROGRESSION. IN AIM 2, WE WILL UTILIZE TARGETED CCR2 IMMUNE PET WITH A RADIOTRACER SPECIFIC TO CCR2-POSITIVE CELLS TO DIRECTLY IMAGE PATHOGENIC MACROPHAGES IN VIVO, AND WE WILL LINK THESE IMAGING FINDINGS TO ARRHYTHMIA BURDEN, VENTRICULAR REMODELING, AND SURVIVAL. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL ESTABLISH IMMUNE PET AS A POWERFUL TOOL TO NONINVASIVELY MONITOR DISEASE ACTIVITY AND PROGRESSION IN A PRECLINICAL MODE OF ACM. BY BRIDGING MECHANISTIC BIOLOGY WITH TRANSLATIONAL IMAGING, THIS PROJECT WILL CLARIFY THE CELLULAR BASIS OF FDG UPTAKE, VALIDATE CCR2-PET AS A NOVEL DIAGNOSTIC APPROACH, AND PROVIDE THE FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE STRATEGIES TO STRATIFY RISK AND TARGET INFLAMMATION IN ACM.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TRANSPARENT ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FROM CLINICAL TEXT, ECGS, AND IMAGING FOR PEDIATRIC CARDIOLOGY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI), PAIRED WITH INCREASINGLY RICH PATIENT HEALTH DATA, HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM THE CLINICAL INTERPRETATION OF CARDIAC MEASUREMENTS SUCH AS ELECTROCARDIOGRAMS (ECGS), ECHOCARDIOGRAMS (ECHOS), CHEST X-RAYS, AND CARDIAC MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (CMR). A MAJOR BARRIER TO DEPLOYING AI FOR MANY PEDIATRIC CARDIOVASCULAR PATHOLOGIES IS THE LIMITED SIZE OF PATIENT COHORTS, WHICH CONSTRAINS MODEL TRAINING AND GENERALIZATION. FOUNDATION MODELS OFFER A SOLUTION BY PRE-TRAINING ON LARGE VOLUMES OF UNLABELED DATA TO LEARN THE PHYSIOLOGIC AND ANATOMIC STRUCTURE OF SIGNALS, THEN FINE-TUNING ON SMALLER, LABELED COHORTS TO ENABLE ACCURATE AND GENERALIZABLE MODELS EVEN FOR RARE DISEASES. THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP AND EVALUATE PEDIATRIC CARDIAC FOUNDATION MODELS USING EXTENSIVE ECG, ECHO, CHEST X-RAYS, AND CLINICAL TEXT DATA FROM BOSTON CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL, TEXAS CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL, AND PUBLIC REPOSITORIES. THE INVESTIGATIVE TEAM IS UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO LEAD THIS WORK THROUGH ACCESS TO ONE OF THE WORLD’S LARGEST PEDIATRIC CARDIAC DATASETS, STRONG INSTITUTIONAL COLLABORATIONS, AND EXTENSIVE PRIOR EXPERIENCE IN DEVELOPING AND DEPLOYING AI-ECG AND AI-ECHO MODELS. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO ESTABLISH A ROBUST, INTERPRETABLE AI PLATFORM FOR PEDIATRIC CARDIOVASCULAR CARE THAT ACCELERATES DISCOVERY, IMPROVES DIAGNOSIS, AND FACILITATES TREATMENT. THE RESEARCH WILL PROCEED IN THREE COORDINATED DIRECTIONS. FIRST, MODALITY-SPECIFIC FOUNDATION MODELS WILL BE TRAINED FOR ECGS, ECHOS, CHEST X-RAYS, AND CLINICAL TEXT, LEVERAGING MILLIONS OF UNLABELED RECORDS AND FINE-TUNING ON SITE-SPECIFIC DATA TO PREDICT VENTRICULAR DYSFUNCTION, PERFORM DIAGNOSTIC PHENOTYPING, AND ESTIMATE SURVIVAL. SECOND, MULTIMODAL INTEGRATION STRATEGIES WILL BE DEVELOPED TO MERGE MODALITY-SPECIFIC MODELS THROUGH BRIDGE NETWORKS INTO A SHARED REPRESENTATION SPACE THAT ALLOWS RICHER CLINICAL REASONING AND MORE ACCURATE PREDICTION OF COMPLEX OUTCOMES. THIRD, INTERPRETABLE AI METHODS TAILORED TO MULTIMODAL CARDIAC DATA WILL BE DESIGNED TO REVEAL PHYSIOLOGIC, ANATOMIC, AND CONTEXTUAL DRIVERS OF PREDICTIONS, THEREBY ENHANCING TRUST AND ENABLING NEW AVENUES OF SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY. OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE PUBLICLY SHAREABLE PEDIATRIC CARDIAC FOUNDATION MODELS, NOVEL MULTIMODAL BRIDGE MODELS THAT IMPROVE RISK PREDICTION AND PHENOTYPING IN PEDIATRIC CARDIOLOGY, AND INTERPRETABLE AI TOOLS DESIGNED FOR CLINICIAN USE. BY OVERCOMING DATA SCARCITY AND ENABLING TRANSPARENT MULTIMODAL REASONING, THIS WORK WILL ESTABLISH THE FIRST PEDIATRIC-FOCUSED MULTIMODAL CARDIAC FOUNDATION MODELS. THE RESULTING TOOLS WILL ACCELERATE SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY, IMPROVE DIAGNOSIS AND MANAGEMENT OF CONGENITAL AND ACQUIRED HEART DISEASE, CONTRIBUTE TO NHLBI STRATEGIC GOALS, AND ULTIMATELY ADVANCE THE USE OF AI TO IMPROVE CARDIOVASCULAR OUTCOMES FOR CHILDREN AND YOUNG ADULTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: RISK PREDICTION FOR AORTIC STENOSIS AND THE IMPACT OF STATIN THERAPY AMONG ADULTS >75 YEARS OLD IN THE PREVENTABLE TRIAL - THE PREVALENCE OF CALCIFIC AORTIC VALVE DISEASE (CAVD) IS HIGHEST AMONG ADULTS ≥75 YEARS OLD AND AORTIC VALVE CALCIUM (AVC) IS THE PRIMARY UNDERLYING CAUSE LEADING TO AORTIC STENOSIS (AS). AS THE US LIFE EXPECTANCY CONTINUES TO INCREASE, THE NUMBER OF ADULTS WITH SEVERE AS IS EXPECTED TO DOUBLE BETWEEN 2025 AND 2050 TO 1.4 MILLION. HOWEVER, THE TRUE BURDEN OF AVC EXTENDS BEYOND AS, AS AVC IS ALSO ASSOCIATED WITH AN INCREASED RISK FOR DEMENTIA AND STROKE. UNFORTUNATELY, MOST RESEARCH IN THIS AREA HAS EXCLUDED ADULTS ≥75 YEARS OLD AND AS A RESULT, THERE IS NO ESTABLISHED ALGORITHM TO IDENTIFY HIGH-RISK PERSONS. FURTHERMORE, THERE IS NO TREATMENT TO SLOW OR PREVENT AS, MAKING IT BOTH UNDERSTUDIED AND ONE OF THE VERY FEW CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES WITHOUT A PROVEN PREVENTIVE THERAPY.  ELEVATED LEVELS OF LDL-C AND LIPOPROTEIN(A) [LP(A)] LEAD TO INFILTRATION OF THE AORTIC VALVE LEAFLETS, WHICH IS WORSENED BY HIGHER LEVELS OF INFLAMMATION (E.G. HSCRP). HOWEVER, PRIOR TRIALS INVESTIGATING LIPID LOWERING THERAPIES TO REDUCE THE RISK OF SEVERE AS HAD CRITICAL LIMITATIONS INCLUDING SMALL SAMPLE SIZE AND ENROLLMENT OF ADULTS WITH PREDOMINANTLY BORDERLINE SEVERE AS, AT WHICH TIME IT IS LIKELY TOO LATE TO INTERVENE WITH MEDICAL THERAPY. RECENT PROVOCATIVE SUBGROUP ANALYSES FROM THE SIMVASTATIN AND EZETIMIBE IN AORTIC STENOSIS (SEAS) TRIAL AND FOURIER TRIAL TESTING THE PCSK9 INHIBITOR EVOLOCUMAB SHOWED A 35-60% LOWER RATE OF SEVERE AS WITH MEDIAN FOLLOW-UP TIMES OF ONLY 2.2 TO 4.3 YEARS AND SEPARATION OF THE CURVES AT 1.3-1.6 YEARS. THESE RESULTS SUGGEST THAT IT MAY BE POSSIBLE TO PREVENT SEVERE AS IN APPROPRIATELY SELECTED PATIENTS WITH SUFFICIENTLY LONG FOLLOW-UP USING A TREATMENT STRATEGY WITH A SOLID MECHANISTIC BASIS FOR POTENTIAL BENEFIT.  HOWEVER, COMPLICATING THE POTENTIAL TRANSLATION OF PREVENTIVE THERAPIES, THERE IS NO RISK-SCORE/ALGORITHM TO IDENTIFY OLDER ADULTS AT HIGHEST RISK FOR SEVERE AS. OUR PIONEERING WORK HAS DEMONSTRATED AN EXTREMELY STRONG ASSOCIATION BETWEEN AVC MEASURED USING NON-CONTRAST CARDIAC CT AND SEVERE AS ALONG WITH A SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER RISK FOR DEMENTIA AND STROKE. WE HAVE ALSO DEMONSTRATED THAT AMONG INDIVIDUALS WITH AVC >0, THOSE WITH AN ELEVATED LP(A), HSCRP, AND PROBNP PROGRESS TO CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT AS TWICE AS QUICKLY.  THE PREVENTABLE TRIAL, TESTING 1:1 RANDOMIZATION TO ATORVASTATIN 40 MG VERSUS PLACEBO AMONG 14,000 ADULTS ≥75 YEARS OLD, IS THE IDEAL TRIAL TO EFFICIENTLY EMBED THE CLINICAL ENDPOINT OF ADJUDICATED SEVERE AS. MEASUREMENT OF AVC FROM THE ALREADY PERFORMED CARDIAC CT SCANS IN THE CAC PREVENTABLE SUBSTUDY AND LP(A), HSCRP, AND PROBNP FROM THE ALREADY PERFORMED RESEARCH LAB DRAWS IS A PRAGMATIC, HIGHLY EFFICIENT, AND COST EFFECTIVE APPROACH TO IDENTIFY OLDER PERSONS AT THE HIGHEST RISK FOR SEVERE AS WHO MAY HAVE THE GREATEST BENEFIT FROM LIPID LOWERING THERAPIES. OUR APPROACH MAXIMIZES THE ENORMOUS INVESTMENT ALREADY MADE BY THE NIA/NHLBI (BOTH TIME AND MONETARY) IN THE PREVENTABLE TRIAL AND WOULD CREATE THE LARGEST EVER TRIAL INVESTIGATING THE UTILITY OF LIPID LOWERING THERAPIES TO REDUCE THE RISK OF SEVERE AS IN OLDER ADULTS.
