description: ROLE OF ENDOTROPHIN IN THE PATHOGENESIS OF HEART FAILURE WITH PRESERVED EJECTION FRACTION - PROJECT SUMMARY HEART FAILURE WITH PRESERVED EJECTION FRACTION (HFPEF) IS NOW THE MOST COMMON FORM OF HEART FAILURE AND A MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH BURDEN, YET NO THERAPIES HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO RELIABLY MODIFY DISEASE PROGRESSION. HFPEF ARISES FROM A COMPLEX INTERPLAY OF METABOLIC STRESS, INFLAMMATION, MICROVASCULAR DYSFUNCTION, AND INTERSTITIAL FIBROSIS, BUT THE UPSTREAM MOLECULAR DRIVERS THAT COORDINATE THESE PROCESSES REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. ENDOTROPHIN (ETP), A BIOACTIVE CLEAVAGE PRODUCT OF THE COLLAGEN VI Α3 CHAIN (COL6A3), HAS RECENTLY EMERGED AS A PROMISING BIOMARKER OF FIBROINFLAMMATORY DISEASE. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES IDENTIFY ETP AS A STRONG PREDICTOR OF INCIDENT HFPEF IN HUMANS AND DEMONSTRATE THAT ETP IS BOTH SUFFICIENT TO INDUCE HFPEF-LIKE CARDIAC DYSFUNCTION AND NECESSARY FOR FULL DISEASE EXPRESSION IN ESTABLISHED MOUSE MODELS. WE FURTHER SHOW THAT RECOMBINANT ETP ACTIVATES SMAD SIGNALING IN CARDIAC FIBROBLASTS WITH DISTINCT KINETICS FROM TGF-Β AND DRIVES A TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROGRAM ENRICHED FOR INFLAMMATORY MEDIATORS. FINALLY, NEUTRALIZATION OF ENDOGENOUS ETP WITH A HUMANIZED ANTIBODY IMPROVES DIASTOLIC FUNCTION AND REDUCES CARDIAC FIBROSIS IN MICE WITH FULLY ESTABLISHED HFPEF, HIGHLIGHTING THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF TARGETING THIS PATHWAY. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEFINE THE ROLE OF ETP AS A CAUSAL DRIVER OF HFPEF AND TO ESTABLISH WHETHER ETP INHIBITION REPRESENTS A VIABLE DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPY. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT ETP IS AN UPSTREAM MEDIATOR THAT LINKS METABOLIC AND INFLAMMATORY COMORBIDITIES TO CARDIAC FIBROSIS AND DIASTOLIC DYSFUNCTION, AND THAT THERAPEUTIC INHIBITION OF ETP CAN REVERSE KEY COMPONENTS OF THE HFPEF PHENOTYPE. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE HOW ETP EXPRESSION ALTERS CARDIAC STRUCTURE, FUNCTION, METABOLISM, AND SUSCEPTIBILITY TO HFPEF USING GAIN- AND LOSS-OF-FUNCTION MOUSE MODELS. AIM 2 WILL IDENTIFY THE RECEPTOR PATHWAYS AND SIGNALING NETWORKS THROUGH WHICH ETP ACTIVATES FIBROINFLAMMATORY REMODELING, INTEGRATING IN VITRO MECHANISTIC STUDIES WITH SINGLE-CELL RNA SEQUENCING IN ETP-OVEREXPRESSING HEARTS. AIM 3 WILL TEST WHETHER NEUTRALIZATION OF ENDOGENOUS ETP REVERSES ESTABLISHED HFPEF AND WILL DEFINE THE CARDIAC, INFLAMMATORY, AND SYSTEMIC EFFECTS OF CHRONIC ETP INHIBITION. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH ETP AS A MECHANISTIC DRIVER OF HFPEF, UNCOVER ITS SIGNALING ARCHITECTURE IN THE HEART, AND PROVIDE RIGOROUS PRECLINICAL EVIDENCE SUPPORTING ETP-DIRECTED THERAPY. THIS WORK HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM HFPEF TREATMENT BY INTRODUCING A NEW BIOLOGICALLY GROUNDED THERAPEUTIC TARGET FOR A DISEASE WITH PROFOUND UNMET CLINICAL NEED.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REMAP-BP: REMOTE BLOOD PRESSURE MONITORING AND PHARMACIST-LED TELEHEALTH PROGRAM IN AN EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT TRANSITIONAL CARE CLINIC (ED-TCC) - SUMMARY/ABSTRACT HYPERTENSION (HTN), DEFINED AS BLOOD PRESSURE (BP) ≥130/80 MMHG OR USE OF ANTIHYPERTENSIVE MEDICATIONS, AFFECTS NEARLY HALF OF U.S. ADULTS AND REMAINS THE LEADING MODIFIABLE RISK FACTOR FOR CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD). DESPITE EXTENSIVE PUBLIC HEALTH AND CLINICAL EFFORTS, BP CONTROL IS SUBOPTIMAL, WITH ONLY 51% OF ADULTS WITH HTN CONTROLLED IN 2021-2023, DOWN FROM 54% IN 2013-2014. PREVALENCE AND POOR CONTROL ARE DISPROPORTIONATELY HIGHER AMONG UNINSURED ADULTS AND THOSE WITHOUT REGULAR INTERACTIONS WITH PRIMARY CARE. THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT (ED) IS OFTEN THE PRIMARY HEALTHCARE CONTACT FOR THESE GROUPS, AND UP TO 45% OF ED PATIENTS PRESENT WITH ELEVATED BP. YET MOST ARE DISCHARGED WITHOUT A DEFINITIVE FOLLOW-UP STRATEGY, LEAVING A CRITICAL GAP IN CONTINUITY OF HTN CARE. REMOTE BP MONITORING (RBPM), PHARMACIST-LED MEDICATION MANAGEMENT VIA TELEHEALTH, AND AUTOMATED TEXT REMINDERS ARE EACH EVIDENCE-BASED APPROACHES THAT IMPROVE HTN OUTCOMES, BUT THEY HAVE RARELY BEEN INTEGRATED INTO A BUNDLED STRATEGY FOR PATIENTS DISCHARGED FROM THE ED. IN 2022, THE UNIVERSITY OF ALABAMA AT BIRMINGHAM (UAB) ESTABLISHED AN ED-TRANSITION CARE CLINIC (ED-TCC) TO PROVIDE STRUCTURED FOLLOW-UP WITHIN 3 TO 7 DAYS OF ED DISCHARGE. FROM JULY 2024 TO APRIL 2025, WE CONDUCTED A PILOT RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL (RCT) OF THIS BUNDLED STRATEGY AT THE UAB ED-TCC WITH 24 PATIENTS. THE INTERVENTION DEMONSTRATED HIGH FEASIBILITY (92% ENROLLMENT, 80% VISIT COMPLETION), STRONG ADHERENCE TO BP MONITORING (85% MEASURED BP ≥2 TIMES/DAY), AND PRELIMINARY BENEFIT (78% ACHIEVING BP <130/80 MMHG VS 50% IN USUAL CARE). BUILDING ON THESE DATA, WE PROPOSE A FULLY POWERED, HYBRID TYPE 1 IMPLEMENTATION- EFFECTIVENESS RCT ACROSS TWO SOUTHERN U.S. HEALTH SYSTEMS: THE UAB ED-TCC AND THE TAMPA GENERAL HOSPITAL ED-TCC. WE WILL RANDOMIZE 400 PATIENTS WITH ELEVATED BP TO INTERVENTION OR USUAL CARE. THE BUNDLED INTERVENTION INCLUDES RBPM, PHARMACIST-LED TELEHEALTH VISITS WITH GUIDELINE-BASED MEDICATION TITRATION AND AUTOMATED TEXT REMINDERS. EFFECTIVENESS WILL BE ASSESSED THROUGH BP CONTROL AND PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES AT 12 AND 24 WEEKS. IMPLEMENTATION WILL BE EVALUATED THROUGH FIDELITY AND ACCEPTABILITY METRICS USING VALIDATED MEASURES, SUPPLEMENTED WITH QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS. SUSTAINABILITY WILL BE ASSESSED THROUGH SEMI-STRUCTURED INTERVIEWS WITH PROVIDERS, PAYERS, AND HEALTH SYSTEM LEADERS GUIDED BY THE EXPLORATION, PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND SUSTAINMENT FRAMEWORK. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE BUNDLED INTERVENTION WILL IMPROVE BP CONTROL BY ≥10% COMPARED WITH USUAL CARE, ENHANCE PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES, BE DELIVERED WITH HIGH FIDELITY AND ACCEPTABILITY, AND YIELD POTENTIAL STRATEGIES FOR LONG-TERM SUSTAINMENT. THIS PRAGMATIC TRIAL TARGETS A POPULATION WITH A HIGH BURDEN OF UNCONTROLLED HTN IN AN UNDERSTUDIED TRANSITIONAL CARE SETTING AND A POPULATION WITH LIMITED ACCESS TO ROUTINE CARE. FINDINGS WILL GENERATE ESSENTIAL EVIDENCE ON THE EFFECTIVENESS, IMPLEMENTATION, AND SCALABILITY OF AN ED-TCC BASED HTN MANAGEMENT MODEL, DIRECTLY INFORMING STRATEGIES TO STRENGTHEN POST-ED TRANSITIONAL CARE AND ADVANCING NHLBI'S MISSION TO PREVENT AND TREAT CVD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR COORDINATION OF ALVEOLAR REGENERATION - PROJECT SUMMARY THE LUNG IS EXPOSED TO NUMEROUS INJURIOUS STIMULI THROUGHOUT LIFE, INCLUDING INFECTIONS, ENVIRONMENTAL PARTICULATES, TOXINS, AND CLINICAL INTERVENTIONS SUCH AS HYPEROXIA OR BAROTRAUMA. WHILE THE LUNG HAS REMARKABLE REPAIR CAPACITY, REPEATED INJURIES OR INSULTS DURING CRITICAL DEVELOPMENTAL PERIODS CAN RESULT IN FAILED REPAIR PROCESSES, PERMANENT RESPIRATORY DEFICITS, AND CHRONIC LUNG DISEASES. ALVEOLAR REPAIR REQUIRES COORDINATED SPATIAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN EPITHELIAL, ENDOTHELIAL, AND MESENCHYMAL CELLS TO RESTORE GAS-EXCHANGE STRUCTURES. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS THAT ORCHESTRATE THESE PROXIMITY-DEPENDENT INTERACTIONS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD, LIMITING THE DEVELOPMENT OF THERAPIES TO PROMOTE ALVEOLAR REGENERATION. INJURY TO THE ALVEOLI DISRUPTS ALVEOLAR TYPE 1 EPITHELIAL CELLS (AT1) AND ALVEOLAR CAPILLARY ENDOTHELIAL CELLS (ACAPS), REQUIRING PROGENITOR CELLS TO MIGRATE, MATURE, AND REESTABLISH FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIONS AT THE BASEMENT MEMBRANE TO RESTORE GAS-EXCHANGE CAPACITY. WHILE SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOMICS HAS ADVANCED OUR UNDERSTANDING OF CELL STATES DURING INJURY AND REPAIR, CRITICAL GAPS REMAIN IN UNDERSTANDING HOW CELLULAR PROXIMITY IS REESTABLISHED TO ENABLE STRUCTURAL REPAIR. OUR NOVEL PARADIGM INCORPORATES REVERSIBLE INJURY MODELS, REVEALING PATHWAYS THAT PROMOTE REGENERATION. PRELIMINARY SPATIAL AND SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOMIC DATA FROM HUMAN INFANT AND ADULT LUNGS WITH EVOLVING LUNG DISEASE HIGHLIGHT SEMAPHORIN SIGNALING AS A KEY DRIVER OF REPAIR. SEMAPHORINS ARE CONSERVED GUIDANCE MOLECULES THAT DIRECT CELLULAR MOVEMENTS AND POSITIONAL RELATIONSHIPS, FACILITATING SIGNALING PATHWAYS SUCH AS BMP, WNT, AND NOTCH. OUR DATA SHOW SEMAPHORIN SIGNALING IS DISRUPTED IN BRONCHOPULMONARY DYSPLASIA (BPD), WHERE AT1 SEMAPHORIN LIGAND EXPRESSION AND ACAP NEUROPILIN-1 (NRP1) RECEPTOR EXPRESSION ARE DOWNREGULATED, IMPAIRING BMP SIGNALING AND DIFFERENTIATION. CONVERSELY, REGENERATIVE MOUSE MODELS SHOW PRESERVED SEMAPHORIN SIGNALING, WHILE NRP1 DELETION IN ACAPS PREVENTS ALVEOLAR REPAIR. THESE FINDINGS SUPPORT OUR HYPOTHESIS THAT SEMAPHORIN SIGNALING RESTORES AT1-ACAP PROXIMITY, ENABLING ALVEOLAR REGENERATION. WE WILL INVESTIGATE THIS IN TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) CHARACTERIZE SPATIOTEMPORAL SEMAPHORIN SIGNALING DYNAMICS IN RESOLVING VERSUS PERSISTENT LUNG INJURY USING HUMAN TISSUE, MOUSE MODELS, AND SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS. 2) DETERMINE HOW SEMAPHORIN SIGNALING RESTORES ALVEOLAR STRUCTURE USING GENETIC, MOLECULAR, AND LIVE IMAGING APPROACHES IN CHRONIC INJURY MODELS. THIS WORK WILL DEFINE SEMAPHORIN SIGNALING IN ALVEOLAR REGENERATION, GUIDING STAGE-SPECIFIC THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR CHRONIC LUNG DISEASES ACROSS THE LIFESPAN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DIFFUSE OPTICAL TOMOGRAPHY FOR BEDSIDE NEUROIMAGING OF EXTRACORPOREAL MEMBRANE OXYGENATION IMPACT ON BRAIN HEALTH - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THESE STUDIES IS TO ADVANCE HIGH-DENSITY DIFFUSE OPTICAL TOMOGRAPHY (HD-DOT) METHODS FOR EVALUATING BRAIN HEALTH VIA BEDSIDE NEUROIMAGING OF FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY (FC) AND CEREBRAL OXYGENATION IN CHILDREN ON EXTRACORPOREAL MEMBRANE OXYGENATION (ECMO). WE ARE SUBMITTING THIS APPLICATION IN RESPONSE TO NIH PA-25-301. ECMO IS AN ADVANCED, HIGH-RISK, RESOURCE-INTENSIVE LIFE SUPPORT TECHNIQUE TO SUPPORT PATIENTS WITH CARDIAC AND OR PULMONARY FAILURE WHEREIN VENOUS BLOOD IS DRAINED FROM THE BODY INTO THE EXTRACORPOREAL CIRCUIT AND PUMPED THROUGH AN OXYGENATOR FOR GAS EXCHANGE. ECMO USE HAS EXPANDED OVER THE LAST 15 YEARS TO BECOME AN INVALUABLE TOOL IN SUPPORTING CHILDREN WITH SEVERE CARDIAC AND PULMONARY FAILURE REFRACTORY TO CONVENTIONAL MANAGEMENT. HOWEVER, PATIENTS SUPPORTED ON ECMO CONTINUE TO BE AT SIGNIFICANT RISK FOR NEUROLOGICAL INJURY, INCLUDING HYPOXIC-ISCHEMIC INJURY IN THE PERI-CANNULATION PERIOD, SEIZURES, THROMBOEMBOLIC AND HEMORRHAGIC STROKE WHILE ON ECMO SUPPORT. THUS, A CLEAR NEED EXISTS FOR A NEW TECHNIQUE THAT CAN PROVIDE SAFE, ROUTINE, PROACTIVE, SENSITIVE, ROBUST, AND DETAILED NEUROLOGIC ASSESSMENT CONSISTENTLY THROUGHOUT A CHILD’S ECMO COURSE TO BETTER UNDERSTAND WHEN OR HOW INJURY OCCURS. HD-DOT PROVIDES AN EMERGING AND COMPELLING TECHNOLOGY THAT OVERCOMES THE SIGNIFICANT LIMITATIONS OF FUNCTIONAL MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (MRI) TO SAFELY AND SILENTLY IMAGE BRAIN FUNCTION WITH A PORTABLE CONSOLE IDEAL FOR BEDSIDE NEUROIMAGING. THE PROPOSED PROGRAM OF RESEARCH IS HIGHLY INNOVATIVE, TRANSFORMATIVE, AND HAS THE POTENTIAL TO SIGNIFICANTLY ENHANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF MECHANISMS, TIMING, AND OTHER FACTORS CONTRIBUTING TO NEUROLOGICAL INJURIES, THUS ENABLING PREVENTION STRATEGIES TO BE DEVELOPED THAT WILL IMPROVE SHORT- AND LONG-TERM NEUROLOGICAL OUTCOMES. AS SUCH, THIS RESEARCH IS HARMONIOUS WITH THE MISSION OF NHLBI: TO ENHANCE THE HEALTH OF ALL INDIVIDUALS BY STIMULATING BASIC DISCOVERIES, TRANSLATING RESEARCH INTO CLINICAL PRACTICE, FOSTERING A STRONG WORKFORCE, AND COMMUNICATING RESEARCH FINDINGS TO THE PUBLIC TO LEAD TO LONGER, MORE FULFILLING LIVES. IN AIM 1, WE WILL OPTIMIZE METHODS FOR EFFICIENT AND ACCURATE MRI- FREE PHOTOMETRIC CAPTURE OF THE SUPINE PATIENT HEAD SURFACE AND HD-DOT ARRAY LOCALIZATION, WITH VALIDATION AGAINST PARTICIPANT-MATCHED FMRI IN HEALTHY YOUNG CHILDREN. IN AIM 2, IN CHILDREN SUPPORTED ON ECMO WE WILL ESTABLISH RELATIONSHIPS AMONG BEDSIDE-HD-DOT-ASSESSED BRAIN FC VARIABILITY WITH CONCURRENTLY MONITORED PHYSIOLOGICAL VARIABLES. IN AIM 3, TO INVESTIGATE HOW VARIABILITY AND CHANGES IN FC DURING ECMO RELATE TO CURRENT NEUROIMAGING METHODS, WE WILL TEST THE ASSOCIATION OF FC-DOT METRICS WITH CLINICALLY OBTAINED IMAGING, INCLUDING POST-ECMO BRAIN STRUCTURE MRI, AS WELL AS POST-ECMO FC-DOT AND FC-MRI. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL RELATE HD- DOT-DERIVED METRICS WITH FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES AT HOSPITAL DISCHARGE AND 6-MONTH FOLLOW-UP. THE PROJECT’S SUCCESS WILL ESTABLISH HD-DOT AS A NOVEL TOOL FOR BEDSIDE NEUROIMAGING ON ECMO, ESTABLISH RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN HD-DOT DERIVED METRICS TO LONGER-TERM OUTCOMES, AND PROVIDE ESSENTIAL DATA FOR FOLLOW-UP MULTI-SITE AND INTERVENTIONAL STUDIES TO OPTIMIZE ECMO OUTCOMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INCORPORATING THE MISSING TIME DIMENSION INTO IDENTITY-BY-DESCENT-BASED MALARIA GENOMIC SURVEILLANCE - PROJECT SUMMARY INTENSIVE MALARIA CONTROL AND ELIMINATION EFFORTS HAVE LED TO SUBSTANTIAL REDUCTIONS IN THE MALARIA BURDEN GLOBALLY OVER THE LAST TWO DECADES; HOWEVER, PROGRESS TOWARD MALARIA ELIMINATION HAS STALLED IN RECENT YEARS. THE CAPACITY TO SEQUENCE MALARIA PARASITE GENOMES AT EPIDEMIOLOGICAL SCALES HAS HEIGHTENED INTEREST IN UTILIZING GENOMIC SURVEILLANCE TO COMPLEMENT TRADITIONAL SURVEILLANCE METHODS. ANALYZING PARASITE GENOMIC DATA USING RECOMBINATION-BASED METRICS, SUCH AS IDENTITY-BY-DESCENT (IBD), PROVIDES KEY INFORMATION ABOUT THE DEMOGRAPHIC HISTORY OF PARASITES ON A FINER SCALE AND IN MORE RECENT EVOLUTIONARY TIMEFRAMES. IBD-BASED METHODS ARE EMPLOYED TO UNDERSTAND REDUCED TRANSMISSION INTENSITY FOLLOWING INTERVENTIONS, IDENTIFY DRUG RESISTANCE MARKERS, DETECT DISTINCT PARASITE GENETIC SUBPOPULATIONS AND PARASITE MIGRATION, AND DESCRIBE TRANSMISSION NETWORKS TO DIFFERENTIATE LOCAL TRANSMISSION FROM IMPORTED INFECTIONS. HOWEVER, EXISTING METHODS OFTEN TREAT PARASITE POPULATIONS AS TIME-HOMOGENEOUS AND DO NOT DIRECTLY MODEL SAMPLING TIME, ASSUMING THAT IBD SEGMENTS OF THE GENOME ARE SHARED BETWEEN PARASITES AT THE PRESENT TIME. INDEED, PARASITES SAMPLED OVER ONLY A DECADE MAY ENCOMPASS GENOMES FROM UP TO 70 DIFFERENT GENERATIONS, POTENTIALLY CONFOUNDING DATA INTERPRETATION RELATED TO TIME AND LIKELY REDUCING STATISTICAL POWER TO IDENTIFY MORE TRANSIENT AND EPIDEMIOLOGICALLY ACTIONABLE MALARIA TRANSMISSION PATTERNS. INCORPORATING SAMPLE TIME INFORMATION HAS THE POTENTIAL TO IMPROVE THE ACCURACY AND PRECISION OF DEMOGRAPHY ESTIMATES, AS “ANCIENT DNA” STUDIES HAVE INFORMED ESTIMATES OF HUMAN POPULATION DEMOGRAPHY. IN ADDITION, EXISTING APPROACHES TO ESTIMATE PARASITE MIGRATION PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO MALARIA TRANSMISSION PATTERNS RETROSPECTIVELY. SUCH ANALYSES REFLECT SOURCE/SINK DYNAMICS FROM THE RECENT PAST BUT MAY BE LESS INFORMATIVE ABOUT FUTURE PATTERNS IN PARASITE POPULATIONS THAT EVOLVE QUICKLY. THEREFORE, MODELS THAT CAN PREDICT FUTURE PATTERNS FROM EXISTING DATA ARE CRITICAL FOR PLANNING ELIMINATION STRATEGIES, ESPECIALLY FOR PARASITE POPULATIONS UNDER SUBSTANTIAL EVOLUTIONARY PRESSURE DUE TO MALARIA INTERVENTIONS. IN THE PROPOSED STUDY, WE WILL DEVELOP A NEW IBD-BASED ESTIMATOR OF RECENT EFFECTIVE POPULATION SIZE (𝑁𝑁𝑒𝑒), UTILIZING IBD SEGMENTS FROM PARASITE GENOMES WITH HETEROGENEOUS SAMPLING TIMES. WE WILL BENCHMARK THE NEW TOOL AGAINST EXISTING ALTERNATIVE 𝑁𝑁𝑒𝑒 ESTIMATORS TO ASSESS HOW INCORPORATING SAMPLING TIME INFORMATION IMPROVES THE ACCURACY OF DEMOGRAPHY ESTIMATES (AIM 1). WE WILL ALSO PERFORM NETWORK ANALYSIS AND LINK PREDICTION USING DEEP LEARNING MODELS TO FORECAST FUTURE PARASITE POPULATION MIGRATION AND THE SPREAD OF DRUG RESISTANCE, USING TIME-SERIES DATA (AIM 2). BY INCORPORATING SAMPLING TIME INTO OUR ANALYTICAL FRAMEWORK, WE WILL BE ABLE TO MORE PRECISELY QUANTIFY THE IMPACT OF MALARIA INTERVENTIONS ON PARASITE POPULATION DEMOGRAPHY AND IDENTIFY TRANSMISSION SOURCES AND SINKS TO INFORM TARGETED MALARIA CONTROL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PUBLIC HEALTH INSURANCE AND MORTALITY AMONG PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES - PEOPLE LIVING WITH DISABILITIES EXPERIENCE WORSE HEALTH OUTCOMES, GREATER UNMET HEALTHCARE NEEDS, AND HIGHER MORTALITY, YET EVIDENCE ON THE CAUSES OF DEATH AND HOW MORTALITY VARIES ACROSS GROUPS REMAINS LIMITED. IT IS UNCLEAR WHETHER HEALTH INSURANCE COVERAGE IS SUFFICIENT TO IMPROVE HEALTHCARE ACCESS, UTILIZATION, AND HEALTH FOR THIS POPULATION. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL ADDRESS THESE GAPS BY LEVERAGING TWO SOURCES OF VARIATION IN MEDICAID COVERAGE: MEDICAID EXPANSIONS AND STATE TRANSITIONS FROM 209(B) TO 1634 STATUS, WHICH AUTOMATICALLY ENROLL ELIGIBLE SUPPLEMENTAL SECURITY INCOME RECIPIENTS IN MEDICAID.  FIRST, WE WILL CHARACTERIZE ALL-CAUSE AND CAUSE-SPECIFIC MORTALITY AMONG PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES AND EXAMINE VARIATION BY SELF-REPORTED DISABILITY, SSA-DEFINED PRIMARY IMPAIRMENT, RACE AND ETHNICITY, SEX, EDUCATION, AND RURALITY. SECOND, WE WILL USE QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL METHODS TO ESTIMATE HOW MEDICAID EXPANSION AND AUTOMATIC ENROLLMENT AFFECT INSURANCE COVERAGE AND MORTALITY, WHILE EXPLORATORY ANALYSES WILL EXAMINE REALIZED ACCESS TO CARE, HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION, AND SELF-REPORTED HEALTH. THIRD, WE WILL USE STRATIFIED AND MACHINE-LEARNING METHODS TO IDENTIFY POPULATIONS THAT EXPERIENCE LARGER, SMALLER, OR NO CHANGES IN COVERAGE, CARE, AND MORTALITY. BY LINKING CHANGES IN COVERAGE TO DOWNSTREAM CHANGES IN CARE AND HEALTH, THE PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY WHERE INSURANCE ALONE IS SUFFICIENT AND WHERE ADDITIONAL SUPPORTS MAY BE NEEDED. FOR EXAMPLE, COVERAGE GAINS WITHOUT INCREASED HEALTHCARE USE MAY POINT TO A NEED FOR OUTREACH, NAVIGATION, OR CARE COORDINATION, WHILE INCREASED UTILIZATION WITHOUT HEALTH IMPROVEMENT MAY INDICATE A NEED TO STRENGTHEN THE QUALITY OR CONTINUITY OF CARE. CAUSE-SPECIFIC MORTALITY FINDINGS WILL ALSO IDENTIFY THE POPULATIONS AND CONDITIONS FOR WHICH EVIDENCE-BASED SCREENING, PREVENTION, TREATMENT, AND DISEASE-MANAGEMENT SERVICES SHOULD BE PRIORITIZED. THESE FINDINGS WILL HELP CLINICIANS, HEALTH SYSTEMS, AND DISABILITY-SERVING ORGANIZATIONS DIRECT RESOURCES TOWARD IMPROVING HEALTH AND REDUCING PREVENTABLE MORTALITY AMONG PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: STRESS MANAGEMENT AND RESPONSE TRAINING FOR PRENATAL EVALUATION AND PARENTING (SMART-PREP) - PROJECT SUMMARY A CRITICAL GAP REMAINS IN UNDERSTANDING HOW STRUCTURED PRENATAL EDUCATION CAN IMPROVE PERINATAL AND CHILD OUTCOMES IN REGIONS WITH LIMITED HEALTHCARE ACCESS. CURRENT CLINICAL PRACTICES OFTEN LACK INTEGRATION OF PHYSIOLOGICAL RISK ASSESSMENT AND BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT, PARTICULARLY IN SETTINGS FACING INFRASTRUCTURE INSTABILITY OR OVERLAPPING PUBLIC HEALTH CHALLENGES. THERE IS A CLEAR UNMET NEED FOR SCALABLE MODELS THAT CONNECT PERINATAL HEALTH WITH INFANT DEVELOPMENTAL OUTCOMES. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL IS TO EVALUATE THE LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF A VIRTUALLY DELIVERED PRENATAL EDUCATION PROGRAM FOCUSED ON SELF-REGULATION– MINDFULNESS-BASED CHILDBIRTH AND PARENTING (MBCP)–COMPARED TO A STANDARD LAMAZE-BASED PROGRAM AND USUAL CARE. THE STUDY WILL ENROLL 300 PREGNANT INDIVIDUALS RECEIVING PRENATAL CARE IN PUERTO RICO, WHERE HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS FREQUENTLY FACE SERVICE INTERRUPTIONS. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY REPLICABLE STRATEGIES THAT CAN BE IMPLEMENTED ACROSS HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS EXPERIENCING LOGISTICAL CHALLENGES. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT STRUCTURED PRENATAL EDUCATION IMPROVES OUTCOMES FOR BOTH CAREGIVERS AND INFANTS BY REDUCING PHYSIOLOGICAL DISTRESS AND PROMOTING ADAPTABILITY. THIS HYPOTHESIS IS INFORMED BY PRELIMINARY DATA AND PRIOR RESEARCH LINKING STRESS-RELATED IMMUNE DISRUPTION AND PHYSIOLOGICAL STRAIN TO NEGATIVE PERINATAL AND INFANT HEALTH OUTCOMES. TWO SPECIFIC AIMS WILL GUIDE THIS WORK: 1) EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF MINDFULNESS-BASED CHILDBIRTH AND PARENTING (MBCP) ON FAMILY ADAPTABILITY AND PERINATAL HEALTH OUTCOMES; 2) ASSESS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN CAREGIVER PRENATAL HEALTH INDICATORS AND EARLY INFANT HEALTH OUTCOMES, INCLUDING GESTATIONAL AGE, BIRTH WEIGHT, AND EARLY MEASURES OF INFANT FUNCTIONING. THE STUDY WILL USE VALIDATED SELF-REPORT INSTRUMENTS, AN ALLOSTATIC LOAD INDEX, CLINICAL RECORDS, AND NIH DEVELOPMENTAL ASSESSMENT TOOLS TO MEASURE PHYSIOLOGICAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL OUTCOMES. THE RESEARCH TEAM BRINGS EXPERTISE IN PSYCHOLOGY, PHYSIOLOGY, PEDIATRICS, OBSTETRICS, PRENATAL EDUCATION, CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN, STATISTICS, EPIDEMIOLOGY, AND APPLIED RESEARCH. ANTICIPATED OUTCOMES INCLUDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO HOW PRENATAL STRESS MANAGEMENT INFLUENCES PERINATAL AND EARLY CHILDHOOD HEALTH. KEY CONTRIBUTIONS WILL INCLUDE EVIDENCE SUPPORTING VIRTUAL DELIVERY OF STRUCTURED EDUCATION, BIOLOGICAL MEDIATION MODELS, AND CONTEXT-SENSITIVE STRATEGIES TO SUPPORT CAREGIVER-INFANT HEALTH. INNOVATIONS INCLUDE THE INTEGRATION OF BIOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL METRICS, VIRTUAL ADAPTATION OF MBCP FOR LOW- RESOURCE ENVIRONMENTS, AND ASSESSMENT OF FAMILY INVOLVEMENT AND INFANT DEVELOPMENT USING STANDARDIZED NIH TOOLS. POSITIVE FINDINGS FROM THIS TRIAL WILL INFORM FUTURE PRENATAL CARE APPROACHES AND SUPPORT SCALABLE INTERVENTIONS AIMED AT IMPROVING HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR CAREGIVERS AND INFANTS ACROSS VARIED HEALTHCARE ENVIRONMENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MOBILIZING STUDENTS TO IMPROVE SCHOOL MEALS, BOOST PARTICIPATION, AND PREVENT OBESITY - ONE IN FIVE CHILDREN AND TEENS IN THE US HAS OBESITY, PARTICULARLY IMPACTING LOW-INCOME YOUTH. SCHOOL MEAL PROGRAMS SERVE ~30 MILLION US CHILDREN DAILY, PLAYING AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN IMPROVING NUTRITION AND HEALTH. THESE MEALS MUST ADHERE TO STANDARDS, OFFERING HEALTHIER OPTIONS THAN MANY MEALS FROM HOME OR ELSEWHERE. THIS IS ESPECIALLY CRITICAL FOR STUDENTS FROM LOWER-INCOME BACKGROUNDS WHO HAVE POORER DIETARY QUALITY AND HIGHER OBESITY RATES AND BLOOD PRESSURE. SOME STATES, LIKE CALIFORNIA PROVIDE FREE MEALS TO ALL PUBLIC-SCHOOL STUDENTS, BUT~ 20 MILLION STUDENTS STILL DON’T PARTICIPATE. WHILE SOME PROGRAMS HAVE SUCCESSFULLY INCREASED MEAL PARTICIPATION, HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS ARE USUALLY NOT INVOLVED IN CREATING SOLUTIONS, DESPITE THEIR LOWER PARTICIPATION RATES. THE SAN JOAQUIN VALLEY (SJV) CHILD NUTRITION ALLIANCE IS A COMMUNITY-ACADEMIC PARTNERSHIP COLLABORATING TO IMPROVE HEALTHY FOOD ACCESS IN THE LARGELY RURAL AND LOW-INCOME SJV REGION WITH HIGH RATES OF DIET-RELATED DISEASES. THE ALLIANCE’S RESEARCH FOUND CHALLENGES TO MEAL PARTICIPATION INCLUDING LACK OF AWARENESS ABOUT THE PROGRAM’S BENEFITS, CONCERNS ABOUT THE QUALITY OF FOOD SERVED (E.G., HIGH ADDED SUGAR, PROCESSED ITEMS, LACK OF FRESH PRODUCE), LIMITED KNOWLEDGE OF SCHOOLS’ CHALLENGES IN PROVIDING HEALTHY MEALS (E.G., LIMITED KITCHEN SPACE, STAFFING, BUDGETS,) AND A NEED FOR BETTER COLLABORATION WITH SCHOOLS. SCHOOL MEAL ACTION WILL BE IMPLEMENTED IN HIGH SCHOOLS SERVING LOW-INCOME STUDENTS, WHO HAVE POORER DIET QUALITY, TO ADDRESS THESE ISSUES. THE YOUTH-LED PROGRAM WILL TRAIN STUDENTS ON: 1) THE HISTORY, REQUIREMENTS, AND LOGISTICS OF SCHOOL NUTRITION PROGRAMS, 2) PHOTOVOICE METHOD THAT USES PHOTOGRAPHY AND DISCUSSIONS TO HIGHLIGHT CHALLENGES AND SOLUTIONS RELATED TO SCHOOL NUTRITION, AND 3) WAYS TO WORK WITH THEIR LOCAL SCHOOL AND SCHOOL DISTRICT TO ADVANCE SOLUTIONS IDENTIFIED FROM PHOTOVOICE. THIS STUDY WILL EVALUATE SCHOOL MEAL ACTION IN 24 SJV HIGH SCHOOLS SERVING LOW-INCOME STUDENTS. HALF WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO RECEIVE THE INTERVENTION IMMEDIATELY; THE OTHER HALF WILL FOLLOW A FINANCIAL LITERACY CURRICULUM. AFTER THE STUDY, CONTROL SCHOOLS WILL BE ENCOURAGED TO INDEPENDENTLY IMPLEMENT SCHOOL MEAL ACTION WITH MATERIALS FROM THE STUDY TEAM. ALL SCHOOLS WILL RECEIVE EVALUATION AT STUDY START AND AGAIN AT 1- AND 12-MONTHS POST-INTERVENTION. A MAJOR GOAL IS TO ASSESS THE PROGRAM’S IMPACT ON STUDENTS’ BMI Z-SCORES (WEIGHT/HEIGHT MEASUREMENTS) AND DIETARY QUALITY (VALIDATED 24- HOUR DIET RECALLS). THE STUDY WILL ALSO EXAMINE CHANGES IN STUDENTS’ KNOWLEDGE, ATTITUDES, SKILLS, AND SELFCONFIDENCE (SURVEYS) AND BLOOD PRESSURE (MEASUREMENTS). AT THE SCHOOL-LEVEL, RESEARCHERS WILL ASSESS CHANGES IN MEAL PARTICIPATION AND NUTRITION GUIDELINES AND PRACTICES (HIGH SCHOOL PHYSICAL ACTIVITY & NUTRITION TOOL). THIS HYBRID TRIAL WILL UTILIZE IMPLEMENTATION FRAMEWORKS TO EXAMINE THE PROGRAM’S REACH, EFFECTIVENESS, AND SUSTAINABILITY USING THE DATA DESCRIBED, ALONG WITH SCHOOL OBSERVATIONS, AND INTERVIEWS/FOCUS GROUPS WITH STUDENT PARTICIPANTS AND PROGRAM IMPLEMENTERS. IF SUCCESSFUL, SCHOOL MEAL ACTION COULD OFFER A SCALABLE SOLUTION TO ENHANCE NUTRITION AND PROMOTE HEALTH FOR MILLIONS OF US STUDENTS.

description: USING A PRE-VISIT ASTHMA QUESTION PROMPT LIST/VIDEO INTERVENTION TO INCREASE HISPANIC YOUTH INVOLVEMENT DURING VISITS AND IMPROVE PATIENT OUTCOMES - HISPANIC YOUTH ARE MORE LIKELY TO HAVE ASTHMA-RELATED EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT VISITS AND HOSPITALIZATIONS AND WORSE HEALTH OUTCOMES THAN NON-HISPANIC YOUTH. HISPANICS ARE ALSO 40% MORE LIKELY TO DIE OF ASTHMA THAN THEIR NON-HISPANIC COUNTERPARTS. SIMPLE INTERVENTIONS ARE NEEDED TO ENGAGE ENGLISH- AND SPANISH-SPEAKING HISPANIC YOUTH MORE DURING ASTHMA VISITS. OUR TEAM FOUND THAT A PRE-VISIT ASTHMA VIDEO AND QUESTION PROMPT LIST INTERVENTION SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED YOUTH QUESTION-ASKING AND PROVIDER EDUCATION ABOUT ASTHMA IN A SAMPLE PRIMARILY COMPRISED OF NON-HISPANIC ENGLISH SPEAKERS SEEN IN PEDIATRIC CLINICS. YOUTH WHO RECEIVED THE INTERVENTION AND ASKED THEIR PROVIDERS QUESTIONS WERE SIGNIFICANTLY MORE LIKELY TO HAVE IMPROVED QUALITY-OF-LIFE AND ASTHMA CONTROL AT 12 MONTHS. WHEN FOCUSING ON THE 18 HISPANIC YOUTH WITH UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA AT BASELINE IN OUR PRIOR WORK, YOUTH IN THE INTERVENTION GROUP HAD A CLOSE TO CLINICALLY MEANINGFUL CHANGE IN ASTHMA CONTROL AND A SIGNIFICANT CLINICALLY MEANINGFUL CHANGE IN QUALITY-OF-LIFE AT 12 MONTHS COMPARED TO THOSE IN USUAL CARE; THESE PROMISING RESULTS WITH A SMALL SAMPLE OF HISPANIC ADOLESCENTS JUSTIFY CONDUCTING AN ADEQUATELY POWERED TRIAL TO DETECT DIFFERENCES IN OUTCOMES. THEREFORE, OUR TEAM PROPOSES TO EXPAND THIS PRIOR WORK TO EXAMINE IF THE INTERVENTION CAN IMPROVE THE OUTCOMES OF ENGLISH OR SPANISH-SPEAKING HISPANIC YOUTH WITH UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA WHO SEEK CARE IN CARE SETTINGS SUCH AS FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS, COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENTS, OR PEDIATRIC CLINICS. USING SOCIAL COGNITIVE THEORY AS A GUIDE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT AN ASTHMA VIDEO/QUESTION PROMPT LIST INTERVENTION THAT IS AVAILABLE IN SPANISH AND ENGLISH WILL INCREASE HISPANIC YOUTH QUESTION-ASKING WHICH, IN TURN, WILL INCREASE PROVIDER EDUCATION DURING THE MEDICAL VISIT, WHICH ULTIMATELY WILL IMPROVE YOUTH SELF-EFFICACY, ASTHMA CONTROL, AND QUALITY-OF-LIFE. OUR TEAM WILL ENROLL 276 ENGLISH AND SPANISH SPEAKING HISPANIC YOUTH AGES 11-17 WITH UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA FROM 5 CLINICS IN GEORGIA AND NORTH CAROLINA. PATIENTS WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO THE INTERVENTION OR CONTROL GROUP. DURING PRE-VISIT WAIT TIME, HISPANIC YOUTH IN THE INTERVENTION GROUP WILL WATCH A SHORT VIDEO ON THE IMPORTANCE OF BEING ACTIVELY INVOLVED DURING VISITS AND THEY WILL RECEIVE THE ONE-PAGE QUESTION PROMPT LIST IN ENGLISH OR SPANISH TO MARK WHICH QUESTIONS THEY WANT TO ASK THE PROVIDER. THE CONTROL GROUP WILL RECEIVE A 1-PAGE AMERICAN ACADEMY OF PEDIATRICS GENERAL HEALTH PROMOTION EDUCATIONAL SHEET. OUR AIMS ARE: (1) TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE ASTHMA QUESTION PROMPT LIST/VIDEO INTERVENTION BY EXAMINING WHETHER YOUTH IN THE INTERVENTION GROUP HAVE BETTER ASTHMA CONTROL AND QUALITY-OF-LIFE AT 12 MONTHS COMPARED TO THOSE IN THE CONTROL GROUP AND (2) TO EXAMINE WHETHER THE INTERVENTION SIGNIFICANTLY IMPACTS THE PROPOSED MECHANISMS BY INVESTIGATING WHETHER MORE YOUTH IN THE INTERVENTION GROUP: (A) ASK AT LEAST ONE QUESTION ABOUT ASTHMA AND RECEIVE MORE PROVIDER EDUCATION ABOUT ASTHMA DURING THEIR BASELINE AND 6 MONTH VISITS AND (B) HAVE HIGHER SELF-EFFICACY IN ASTHMA MANAGEMENT AT 6 AND 12 MONTHS THAN YOUTH IN THE CONTROL GROUP.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PRIMARY CARE AFTER PREGNANCY: A NEW CARE MODEL - HIGH RATES OF MATERNAL MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY IN THE UNITED STATES (US) ARE RELATED IN PART TO TREATABLE CHRONIC DISEASES (E.G., DIABETES, HYPERTENSION, DEPRESSION) THAT PRIMARY CARE PROVIDERS (PCPS) ARE WELL POSITIONED TO ADDRESS. INTERCONCEPTION CARE, DEFINED AS HEALTHCARE SERVICES PROVIDED AFTER THE END OF A PREGNANCY TO SUPPORT OPTIMAL OUTCOMES IN A FUTURE PREGNANCY, IS UNDERUTILIZED IN THE US. AMONG WOMEN WITH A PRIOR BIRTH, <30% RECEIVE ANY COUNSELING TO OPTIMIZE THEIR HEALTH BEFORE A FUTURE PREGNANCY. MOST REPRODUCTIVE AGE WOMEN IN THE US HAVE AT LEAST ONE PHYSICIAN VISIT PER YEAR, MOST WITH A PCP. WOMEN WHO ARE POOR, LIVE IN RURAL AREAS, AND HAVE LOWER EDUCATION LEVELS ARE DISPROPORTIONATELY MORE LIKELY TO RECEIVE PRIMARY REPRODUCTIVE CARE FROM PCPS RATHER THAN FROM WOMEN’S HEALTH SPECIALISTS. PRIOR WORK BY THIS STUDY TEAM ENGAGED PCPS (PHYSICIANS AND ADVANCE PRACTICE PROVIDERS IN FAMILY MEDICINE AND GENERAL INTERNAL MEDICINE), CLINIC STAFF, AND WOMEN ELIGIBLE FOR INTERCONCEPTION CARE TO EXPLORE THE CHALLENGES AND FACILITATORS TO INTERCONCEPTION CARE. WE FOUND THAT MANY POST-PREGNANCY WOMEN HAVE HEALTHCARE NEEDS WITHIN THE SCOPE OF PCP PRACTICE YET REPORT BEING UNCERTAIN FROM WHOM TO SEEK CARE (E.G., PCP, OBSTETRICIAN, SPECIALIST). DESPITE THE AVAILABILITY OF PUBLISHED PRECONCEPTION AND INTERCONCEPTION CARE TOOLS, PCPS REPORT AN INABILITY TO PROACTIVELY IDENTIFY PATIENTS WHO ARE ELIGIBLE FOR INTERCONCEPTION CARE; POOR COORDINATION OF CARE BETWEEN OBSTETRICS AND PRIMARY CARE; PCP LACK OF UNDERSTANDING OF INTERCONCEPTION CARE NEEDS; AND LIMITED TIME DURING PRIMARY CARE VISITS. WE USED THESE FINDINGS TO CONCEPTUALIZE AND CONDUCT ADDITIONAL RESEARCH IN WHICH WE DEVELOPED A MULTI-COMPONENT, INTERCONCEPTION CARE INTERVENTION, “PRIMARY CARE AFTER PREGNANCY” (PCAP). PCAP INCLUDES (1) ESTABLISHING A STANDARD OF CARE FOR POSTPARTUM PATIENTS TO RECEIVE AT LEAST ONE PRIMARY CARE, INTERCONCEPTION CARE VISIT WITHIN 6 MONTHS AFTER A DELIVERY; (2) LEVERAGING THE ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD TO IDENTIFY PATIENTS ELIGIBLE FOR INTERCONCEPTION CARE, THEREBY; (3) CREATING A PROCESS FOR THE TRANSFER OF CLINICAL INFORMATION BETWEEN OBSTETRICS AND PRIMARY CARE; (4) CREATING A WAY TO PROACTIVELY ENGAGE ELIGIBLE PATIENTS FOR INTERCONCEPTION CARE; (5) USING A PRE-VISIT NEEDS ASSESSMENT TO IDENTIFY AND TAILOR ELIGIBLE PATIENT INTERCONCEPTION HEALTHCARE CONCERNS AND NEEDS; AND (6) INTEGRATING INTERCONCEPTION CARE TOOLS AND RESOURCES INTO PRIMARY CARE. THIS STUDY WILL (A) USE PARTICIPATORY DESIGN TO ADVANCE AND REFINE THE PCAP INTERVENTION; (B) APPLY THE EXPLORATION, PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION, SUSTAINMENT (EPIS) FRAMEWORK FOR IMPLEMENTATION IN PRIMARY CARE CLINICS AND FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS AFFILIATED WITH TWO LARGE ACADEMIC HEALTH SYSTEMS, THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO AND THE UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS AT CHICAGO; AND (C) APPLY THE REACH, EFFECTIVENESS, ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION, MAINTENANCE (RE-AIM) FRAMEWORK TO DUALLY EVALUATE THE IMPLEMENTATION AND EFFECTIVENESS OF THE INTERVENTION.

description: LEVERAGING DIGITAL TOOLS AND ADAPTIVE PRECISION FACILITATION TO ENHANCE TEACHER IMPLEMENTATION FIDELITY AND PROMOTE STUDENT HEALTH IN RURAL APPALACHIAN SCHOOLS: A HYBRID TYPE 3 TRIAL - MODIFIED PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SECTION.  RELATIVE TO THEIR URBAN COUNTERPARTS, YOUTH RESIDING IN RURAL REGIONS HAVE POORER DIETS, INCLUDING EXCESSIVE SUGAR-SWEETENED BEVERAGE (SSB) CONSUMPTION, AND DISPROPORTIONATELY SUFFER FROM OBESITY AND RELATED CHRONIC CONDITIONS. KIDS SIPSMARTER (KSS) IS MULTI-LEVEL, SCHOOL-BASED, BEHAVIORAL AND HEALTH LITERACY INTERVENTION THAT HAS YIELDED STATISTICALLY AND CLINICALLY MEANINGFUL IMPROVEMENTS IN SSB BEHAVIORS AMONG MIDDLE SCHOOL STUDENTS AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. OUR R01 APPLICATION BUILDS FROM OUR SUCCESS IN APPALACHIA MIDDLE SCHOOLS, ADDRESSES PROMINENT GAPS IN IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE LITERATURE, AND IS GUIDED BY THE INTEGRATED PROMOTING ACTION ON RESEARCH IMPLEMENTATION IN HEALTH SERVICES (I-PARIHS) FRAMEWORK. PHASE 1 USES A HUMAN-CENTERED DESIGN PROCESS TO UNDERSTAND TEACHERS’ NEEDS AND EXPERIENCES TO GUIDE DEVELOPMENT OF THE AUTOMATED BUNDLED IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES FOR KSS. PHASE 2 IS A HYBRID TYPE 3 EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION TRIAL AND CLUSTER, ADAPTIVE RANDOMIZED TRIAL DESIGNED TO EVALUATE KSS’S IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES AND OUTCOMES IN 60 RURAL APPALACHIA MIDDLE SCHOOLS. ALL SCHOOLS WILL RECEIVE THE AUTOMATED BUNDLE THAT INCLUDES AN INTERVENTION ACTION PLAN TO PROACTIVELY PLAN FIDELITY-CONSISTENT KSS MODIFICATIONS AND SET TEACHER-SPECIFIC FIDELITY BENCHMARKS AS WELL AS A WEB-BASED APPLICATION FOR TEACHER TRAINING, FIDELITY MONITORING WITH FEEDBACK, AND REMINDERS. SOME SCHOOLS WILL ACHIEVE FIDELITY BENCHMARKS (I.E., >80% OF FIDELITY BENCHMARKS) WITH THE AUTOMATED BUNDLED, BUT OTHERS WILL NEED ADAPTIVE PRECISION HUMAN-SUPPORTED FACILITATION STRATEGIES - WHICH WILL BE TESTED IN OUR CLUSTER, ADAPTIVE RANDOMIZED TRIAL. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL IMPLEMENT STRATEGIES INTENDED TO PROMOTE FIDELITY-CONSISTENT INTERVENTION ADAPTATIONS THROUGHOUT ALL IMPLEMENTATION PHASES AND USE A MIXED-METHODS EVALUATION APPROACH GUIDED BY THE FRAMEWORK FOR REPORTING ADAPTATIONS AND MODIFICATIONS (AIM 1). WE WILL ALSO EVALUATE IMPACTS OF THE AUTOMATED BUNDLED IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES VS. THE AUTOMATED BUNDLED IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES + ADAPTIVE PRECISION HUMAN-SUPPORTED VIRTUAL FACILITATION ON INTERVENTION FIDELITY (PRIMARY OUTCOME, AIM 2) AND COST OF IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES AND INCREMENTAL COST EFFECTIVENESS OF THE ADAPTIVE STRATEGY (AIM 2A). KSS’S INTERVENTION EFFECTIVENESS ON STUDENT SSB BEHAVIORS AND BMI WILL ALSO BE EVALUATED (SECONDARY AIM). FINALLY, WE WILL EXPLORE PRELIMINARY MECHANISMS OF ACTION AND THEIR IMPACT ON IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES USING A MIXED-METHODS APPROACH (EXPLORATORY AIM). IN SUM, THIS STUDY WILL DEVELOP AND EVALUATE AN AUTOMATED BUNDLE OF IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES TO SUPPORT FIDELITY IN SCHOOL SETTINGS. BY ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF ADAPTIVE, PRECISION-BASED VIRTUAL FACILITATION ON IMPLEMENTATION FIDELITY AND COST, WE AIM TO ADVANCE THE SUSTAINABLE DELIVERY OF EVIDENCE-BASED DIETARY INTERVENTIONS IN REAL-WORLD SCHOOLS. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO DEVELOP COST-EFFECTIVE IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES THAT FIT SCHOOL CONTEXTS, IMPROVE DIETARY BEHAVIORS—PARTICULARLY BY REDUCING SSB INTAKE—AND HELP PREVENT DIET-RELATED CHRONIC CONDITIONS, INCLUDING OBESITY AND METABOLIC DISORDERS, AMONG RURAL APPALACHIAN YOUTH AND BEYOND.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: KAKUA HOOLAUPAI: MEASURING IMPACT OF A NATIVE HAWAIIAN BIRTHING MOVEMENT - PROJECT SUMMARY  HAWAIʻI RANKS LAST FOR ADEQUATE PRENATAL CARE, WITH ONLY 60% OF PREGNANT WOMEN RECEIVING PRENATAL CARE IN THE FIRST 4 MONTHS OF PREGNANCY. NATIVE HAWAIIAN (NH) AND PACIFIC ISLANDER WOMEN ACCOUNT FOR 22% OF WOMEN OF REPRODUCTIVE AGE IN HAWAIʻI, BUT ACCOUNT FOR 44% OF MATERNAL DEATHS. NH AND PACIFIC ISLANDER WOMEN HAVE THE HIGHEST MATERNAL MORTALITY RATIO OF ANY RACE AND ETHNIC GROUP, WITH 63 DEATHS PER 100,000 BIRTHS. HAWAIʻI’S MATERNAL MORTALITY REVIEW COMMITTEE REPORTED THAT OVER HALF OF MATERNAL DEATHS OCCURRED ON OʻAHU AND THAT MENTAL HEALTH CONTRIBUTED TO 32% OF ALL MATERNAL DEATHS. TO SUPPORT MATERNAL HEALTH EQUITY, REDUCE RISK FACTORS FOR MATERNAL MORBIDITY AND MATERNAL MORTALITY (MMM), AND SUSTAIN CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE PRACTICES, WE WILL PARTNER WITH KŌKUA KALIHI VALLEY (KKV), A FEDERALLY-QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTER ON OʻAHU TO CONDUCT A QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL COHORT STUDY OF AN ESTABLISHED COMMUNITY-BASED BIRTH PREPARATION PROGRAM, KA LĀHUI O KA PŌ (KLP), WHICH IS GROUNDED IN NH CULTURE, FOCUSES ON THE FAMILY, AND PROMOTES PREGNANCY EMPOWERMENT. FIRST, WE WILL ANALYZE 5+ YEARS OF EVALUATION DATA TO LEARN ABOUT THE EXPERIENCES OF PREGNANT WOMEN AND THEIR PARTNERS IN KLP AND TO IDENTIFY ITS UNIQUE FEATURES AND RESOURCES THAT SUPPORT MATERNAL HEALTH, FOCUSING ESPECIALLY ON THE FIRST (INTRODUCTORY) SESSION AND THE PARTICIPANT BIRTH STORY TO DEVELOP PATIENT-CENTERED VIGNETTES. SECOND, USING A COMMUNITY-BASED PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH APPROACH, WE WILL CONDUCT A PROSPECTIVE, OBSERVATIONAL COHORT STUDY OF OUTCOMES AMONG WOMEN COMPLETING KLP AND THEIR COUNTERPARTS WHO RECEIVED STANDARD PRENATAL CARE FROM OBSTETRIC CLINICS AT 2 LARGE HEALTHCARE FACILITIES IN HAWAIʻI. ACROSS THE 3 SETTINGS, WE WILL SURVEY 320 PREGNANT WOMEN AND ASCERTAIN OUR PRIMARY OUTCOMES OF ENGAGEMENT IN PRENATAL CARE, PERINATAL DEPRESSION, COMPLETION OF THE POSTPARTUM VISIT, AND PREGNANCY EMPOWERMENT. FINALLY, WE WILL CONDUCT 40 KEY INFORMANT INTERVIEWS WITH MATERNITY CARE PROVIDERS USING VIGNETTES TO IDENTIFY IMPLEMENTATION DETERMINANTS AND FEASIBLE AND ACCEPTABLE STRATEGIES TO INTEGRATE COMPONENTS OF THE KLP PROGRAM INTO OTHER HEALTHCARE SETTINGS. OUR SPECIFIC AIMS ARE TO: 1) ANALYZE KKV’S EVALUATION DATA ON KLP, FOCUSING SPECIFICALLY ON FIRST SESSION AND BIRTH STORY, TO IDENTIFY THE NATURE, EXTENT, AND SALIENCE OF PRENATAL SUPPORT FOR NH WOMEN AND DEVELOP PATIENT-CENTERED VIGNETTES FOR INTERVIEWS WITH HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS IN AIM 3; 2) ESTIMATE THE EFFECT OF KLP ON PERINATAL CARE ENGAGEMENT, PRESENCE OF PERINATAL DEPRESSION, AND PREGNANCY EMPOWERMENT, AMONG 320 BIRTHING NH WOMEN; 3) INTERVIEW HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS WHO SERVE PREGNANT AND POSTPARTUM NH WOMEN AND USE VIGNETTES TO IDENTIFY DETERMINANTS AND STRATEGIES TO IMPLEMENT CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE BIRTH PREPARATION PROGRAMS AT OTHER CLINICS SERVING NH WOMEN. BY ANALYZING THE RICH DATA AVAILABLE FROM KLP AND RIGOROUSLY COMPARING MATERNAL HEALTH OUTCOMES AMONG ITS PARTICIPANTS TO SIMILAR WOMEN RECEIVING STANDARD PERINATAL CARE, WE WILL LAY THE SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION FOR AN INNOVATIVE AND TRUSTED PROGRAM TO PROMOTE MATERNAL HEALTH AMONG NH WOMEN. FINDINGS WILL ILLUSTRATE HOW INTEGRATING NH CULTURE INTO PERINATAL CARE CAN HELP ADDRESS RISK FACTORS FOR MMM IN NH WOMEN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TAILORED MOBILE HEALTH TECHNOLOGY TO ADDRESS NATIVE AMERICAN CHRONIC PAIN - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CHRONIC PAIN IS A PERVASIVE AND DEBILITATING CONDITION THAT AFFECTS MILLIONS OF AMERICANS AND NATIVE AMERICAN (NA) COMMUNITIES EXPERIENCE A SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER PAIN BURDEN THAN OTHER SEGMENTS OF THE U.S. POPULATION. FOR EXAMPLE, OUR LONGITUDINAL RESEARCH SHOWS THAT 28% OF PAIN-FREE NAS DEVELOP CHRONIC PAIN WITHIN 5 YEARS OF FOLLOW-UP, COMPARED TO 12% OF NON-HISPANIC WHITES. OUR PRIOR RESEARCH HAS IDENTIFIED KEY PREDICTORS OF CHRONIC PAIN IN NAS, INCLUDING SENSITIZED PAIN PATHWAYS LINKED TO SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH (EG, UNFAIR TREATMENT, TRAUMA), STRESS, STRESS PHYSIOLOGY (ALLOSTATIC LOAD), SLEEP DISTURBANCE, AND COGNITIVE-EMOTIONAL AMPLIFIERS OF PAIN (CATASTROPHIZING, PAIN-RELATED ANXIETY). PSYCHOLOGICAL TREATMENTS FOR PAIN ARE EFFICACIOUS, AND TAILORED TREATMENTS ARE EVEN MORE EFFICACIOUS. BUT THESE TREATMENTS ARE OFTEN INACCESSIBLE TO NAS DUE TO GEOGRAPHIC, FINANCIAL, AND SOCIAL BARRIERS. MOBILE HEALTH (MHEALTH) INTERVENTIONS CAN PROVIDE EFFECTIVE PAIN SELF-MANAGEMENT, OVERCOME ACCESS BARRIERS, AND EASILY SCALE UP GIVEN WIDESPREAD USE OF SMARTPHONES AMONG NAS. YET, FEW VALIDATED MHEALTH PAIN INTERVENTIONS EXIST, AND NONE ARE TAILORED FOR NAS. THIS PROPOSAL WILL DEVELOP AND TEST THE FEASIBILITY OF THE FIRST MHEALTH CHRONIC PAIN INTERVENTION SPECIFICALLY DESIGNED FOR NAS THAT INTEGRATES THE PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCE OF PAIN WITH INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE. OUR TEAM BRINGS DEEP EXPERTISE IN NA PAIN/HEALTH (RHUDY, SHADLOW), PSYCHOLOGICAL TREATMENTS FOR PAIN (LUMLEY), AND MHEALTH APP INNOVATION (BUSINELLE). GUIDED BY A COMMUNITY- ENGAGED FRAMEWORK, WE WILL CO-DEVELOP AND TEST THE INTERVENTION WITH INPUT FROM NA TEAM MEMBERS, NAS LIVING WITH CHRONIC PAIN, NA COMMUNITY ADVISORY BOARD, NA COMMUNITY PARTNERS, AND TRIBAL IRBS TO ENSURE CULTURAL RELEVANCE AND SCIENTIFIC INTEGRITY. IN AIM 1, 2 TALKING CIRCLES (6 NAS EXPERIENCING CHRONIC PAIN PER CIRCLE) LED BY NA TEAM MEMBERS WILL CO-CREATE TREATMENT CONTENT THAT IS GROUNDED IN VALIDATED PSYCHOLOGICAL APPROACHES TO PAIN MANAGEMENT, WITH TREATMENT TARGETS INFORMED BY OUR 15 YEARS OF MECHANISTIC PAIN RESEARCH. A NOVEL TREATMENT COMPONENT WILL BE DEVELOPED TO ENHANCE CULTURAL CONNECTEDNESS (CC), A NA PROTECTIVE FACTOR ASSOCIATED WITH RESILIENCE TO STRESS AND PAIN. IN AIM 2, TREATMENT CONTENT AND APP DESIGN WILL BE OPTIMIZED THROUGH 3 ITERATIVE USABILITY STUDIES (N=6 NAS LIVING WITH CHRONIC PAIN PER STUDY) TO ENSURE ENGAGEMENT AND CULTURAL FIT, AS WELL AS TO REDUCE BARRIERS TO UPTAKE AND RETENTION. IN AIM 3 WE WILL ESTABLISH TREATMENT FEASIBILITY THROUGH A SINGLE-ARM TRIAL (N=125 NAS LIVING WITH CHRONIC PAIN) WITH FOLLOW-UP TO 3 MONTHS POST-TREATMENT. THIS WILL EVALUATE RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, ENGAGEMENT, ACCEPTABILITY, USABILITY, QUALITY, AND PRELIMINARY SIGNALS OF EFFICACY (IE, VALIDATED PAIN AND FUNCTIONAL MEASURES). THIS INNOVATIVE, PRECISION-MEDICINE INTERVENTION WILL BE COST-EFFECTIVE AND CULTURALLY-GROUNDED AND DIRECTLY RESPONDS TO PAR-25-379 BY DEVELOPING AND TESTING THE FEASIBILITY OF A NOVEL MHEALTH INTERVENTION FOR NA CHRONIC PAIN THAT INTEGRATES INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE WITH PSYCHOLOGICAL PAIN SCIENCE. BY TARGETING SHARED MECHANISMS ACROSS CHRONIC CONDITIONS, SUCH AS STRESS AND SLEEP DISTURBANCE, THIS INTERVENTION MAY ALSO YIELD HEALTH BENEFITS BEYOND PAIN.

description: LEVERAGING TELEMEDICINE TO IMPROVE GUIDELINE-DIRECTED MEDICAL THERAPY USE AND OUTCOMES AMONG RURAL PATIENTS WITH HEART FAILURE- THE RURAL-HF TRIAL - MODIFIED PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SECTION  PATIENTS WITH HEART FAILURE (HF) IN RURAL COMMUNITIES FACE APPROXIMATELY 20% HIGHER MORTALITY RISK COMPARED TO URBAN COUNTERPARTS, DRIVEN LARGELY BY POOR ACCESS TO CARDIOLOGY SPECIALTY CARE AND UNDERUTILIZATION OF GUIDELINE-DIRECTED MEDICAL THERAPY (GDMT). WHILE EVIDENCE-BASED HF THERAPIES CAN REDUCE MORTALITY BY MORE THAN 50%, ONLY 4-6% OF PATIENTS ACHIEVE OPTIMAL GDMT DOSING WITHIN SIX MONTHS OF DIAGNOSIS. UNDERUTILIZATION OF GDMT ACCOUNTS FOR AN ESTIMATED 16% OF THE EXCESS MORTALITY RISK EXPERIENCED BY RURAL VERSUS URBAN HF PATIENTS. TELEHEALTH AND REMOTE PATIENT MONITORING REPRESENT PROMISING STRATEGIES TO OVERCOME GEOGRAPHIC CHALLENGES AND IMPROVE GDMT UTILIZATION. HOWEVER, WHILE SMALL PILOT STUDIES HAVE DEMONSTRATED FEASIBILITY, NO ADEQUATELY POWERED RANDOMIZED TRIAL HAS EVALUATED TELEHEALTH-ENABLED GDMT OPTIMIZATION SPECIFICALLY DESIGNED FOR PATIENTS WITH HF IN RURAL AREAS. TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP, WE PROPOSE A TYPE 1 HYBRID EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION, MULTI-CENTER, RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL ENROLLING 600 PATIENTS HOSPITALIZED WITH ACUTE HF AT RURAL HOSPITALS ACROSS TWO HEALTH SYSTEMS. THE INTERVENTION LEVERAGES PROVIDER-TO-PROVIDER TELEHEALTH COLLABORATION, WHERE CARDIOVASCULAR SPECIALISTS FROM THE STUDY TEAM PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED, PROTOCOL-DRIVEN GDMT INITIATION AND UPTITRATION RECOMMENDATIONS TO PARTICIPANTS' OUTPATIENT CARE TEAMS (PRIMARY CARE PROVIDERS OR CARDIOLOGISTS). THIS APPROACH IS SUPPORTED BY CONTINUOUS REMOTE MONITORING OF PATIENT VITAL SIGNS THROUGH CELLULAR-ENABLED DEVICES (BLOOD PRESSURE, HEART RATE, WEIGHT) THAT TRANSMIT DATA WITHOUT REQUIRING HOME INTERNET ACCESS. THE STUDY TEAM WILL REVIEW PHYSIOLOGIC DATA WEEKLY AND PROVIDE SPECIFIC MEDICATION RECOMMENDATIONS AT WEEKLY INTERVALS DURING THE FIRST SIX WEEKS POST-DISCHARGE. THE INTERVENTION TARGETS ACHIEVEMENT OF MAXIMALLY TOLERATED GDMT WITHIN 90 DAYS, WITH CONTINUED SAFETY MONITORING THROUGH THIS PERIOD. THE PRIMARY, WIN-RATIO BASED COMPOSITE HIERARCHICAL OUTCOME INCLUDES ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY, HEART TRANSPLANT OR VENTRICULAR ASSIST DEVICE, HF HOSPITALIZATION (FIRST AND RECURRENT), AND CHANGE IN QUALITY OF LIFE ASSESSED BY THE KANSAS CITY CARDIOMYOPATHY QUESTIONNAIRE OVER SIX MONTHS OF FOLLOW-UP. IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES WILL BE EVALUATED USING THE RE-AIM FRAMEWORK TO ASSESS REACH, EFFECTIVENESS, ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION FIDELITY, AND MAINTENANCE. A MIXED-METHODS APPROACH COMBINING QUANTITATIVE METRICS WITH QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS OF CLINICIANS AND PATIENTS WILL EXAMINE ACCEPTABILITY, IMPLEMENTATION COSTS, AND CHALLENGES AND FACILITATORS ACROSS VARIOUS RURAL SETTINGS TO INFORM FUTURE SCALABILITY. THIS TRIAL ADDRESSES THE CRITICAL NEED FOR SCALABLE, EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES TO REDUCE CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH DISPARITIES IN RURAL AMERICA. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION WILL PROVIDE THE FIRST RIGOROUS EVIDENCE FOR TELEHEALTH-ENABLED GDMT OPTIMIZATION FOR PATIENTS WITH HF IN RURAL AREAS AND GENERATE ESSENTIAL IMPLEMENTATION DATA TO GUIDE BROADER DISSEMINATION OF THIS APPROACH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GENETIC DETERMINANTS OF CARDIOVASCULAR-KIDNEY-METABOLIC SYNDROME - ABSTRACT CARDIAC, KIDNEY, AND METABOLIC CONDITIONS, INCLUDING CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE, AND TYPE 2 DIABETES, ARE LEADING CAUSES OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY IN THE UNITED STATES AND AFFECT INDIVIDUALS FROM ALL BACKGROUNDS. THESE INTERCONNECTED CONDITIONS, RECENTLY RECOGNIZED AS CARDIOVASCULAR-KIDNEY-METABOLIC (CKM) SYNDROME, SHARE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND RISK FACTORS, INCLUDING DYSFUNCTIONAL ADIPOSITY, DYSGLYCEMIA, DYSLIPIDEMIA, ECTOPIC LIPID DEPOSITION, AND HYPERTENSION. NATIVE HAWAIIANS AND PACIFIC ISLANDERS (NHPI), WHO HAVE AMONG THE WORLD'S HIGHEST BURDEN OF METABOLIC DISEASE, ARE AT DISPROPORTIONALLY HIGHER RISK FOR OTHER ASSOCIATED COMORBIDITIES, INCLUDING CKD AND CVD, AND ALSO HAVE AMONG THE WORLD'S HIGHEST BURDEN OF CKM SYNDROME. THE UTAH PACIFIC ISLANDER STUDY (UPIS) WAS IMPLEMENTED TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE BASIS OF CKM SYNDROME IN NHPI. WITH COMMUNITY SUPPORT, MORE THAN 800 PARTICIPANTS WITH EXTENSIVE PHENOTYPIC INFORMATION WERE ENROLLED INTO THE UPIS WITHIN A 20-MONTH PERIOD. ONGOING GENETIC AND MULTI-OMICS ANALYSES HAVE ALREADY IDENTIFIED A POPULATION-SPECIFIC VARIANT IN THE ASAH2 GENE THAT IS ASSOCIATED WITH DIABETES AND KIDNEY DISEASE RISK IN NHPI. IN ADDITION, WE HAVE OBSERVED A RECENTLY IDENTIFIED NHPI POPULATION-SPECIFIC VARIANT IN ACADVL THAT IS ASSOCIATED WITH CKM RISK FACTORS. LEVERAGING LONG-READ WHOLE-GENOME SEQUENCES (WGS) FROM UPIS PARTICIPANTS FROM 8 ISLANDS ACROSS THE PACIFIC, WE CREATED THE FIRST NHPI PANGENOME REFERENCE TO VASTLY IMPROVE GENETIC ANALYSES IN THIS POPULATION, INCLUDING THE IDENTIFICATION OF NOVEL STRUCTURAL VARIATION. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO LEVERAGE THESE EXPERIENCES AND RESOURCES TO FURTHER ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF THE GENETIC BASIS OF CKM SYNDROME. SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL EXPAND THE ALREADY EXISTING BIOREPOSITORY OF DEEPLY PHENOTYPED NHPI INDIVIDUALS ACROSS THE CKM SYNDROME SPECTRUM TO >1,800 NHPI INDIVIDUALS, ARCHIVE BIOSPECIMENS (PLASMA, SERUM, URINE, DNA, RNA, AND PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMCS)) FROM PARTICIPANTS OF THE UPIS AND PERFORM WGS IN 1,000 NEWLY RECRUITED UPIS PARTICIPANTS. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL ASSESS THE CONTRIBUTION OF GENETIC FACTORS TO CKM SYNDROME RISK BY CONDUCTING GENOTYPE-BASED DISCOVERY AND REPLICATION ANALYSES USING STATE-OF-THE-ART METHODOLOGIES, INCLUDING PANGENOME-BASED VARIANT DISCOVERY USING OUR PACIFIC ANCESTRY PANGENOME REFERENCE AND AN NHPI IMPUTATION REFERENCE PANEL, AND COHORTS TOTALING >20,000 NHPI. SPECIFIC AIM 3 WILL ADVANCE THE FUNCTIONAL AND MECHANISTIC ASSESSMENT OF GENETIC VARIANTS IN NHPI WITH CKM SYNDROME USING VARIANT GENE EDITING IN DIFFERENTIATED HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS DERIVED FROM PBMCS FROM ASAH2 AND ACADVL VARIANT CARRIERS AND FUNCTIONALLY CHARACTERIZE THE CONSEQUENCE OF THE OBSERVED ALLELES. THIS PROJECT WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE BASIS OF CKM SYNDROME. THIS RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE A SOLID FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE EFFORTS AIMED AT ELUCIDATING THE MECHANISMS BEHIND THE DISPARITY OF CKM SYNDROME IN NHPI, FACILITATE TRANSLATION OF THESE FINDINGS TO IMPROVED DIAGNOSTICS AND THERAPEUTICS, AND FACILITATE ADDITIONAL STUDIES ON RISK FACTORS, BOTH GENETIC AND NON-GENETIC, THAT CONTRIBUTE TO THE BURDEN OF CKM SYNDROME FOR ALL AT RISK INDIVIDUALS IN THE US.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LIFESTYLE STRATEGIES TO PRESERVE MUSCLE AND REDUCE CARDIOVASCULAR RISK IN ADULTS WITH OBESITY USING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS - PROJECT SUMMARY  GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS ARE NOW AMONG THE MOST WIDELY PRESCRIBED WEIGHT LOSS MEDICATIONS IN THE UNITED STATES. WHILE EFFECTIVE FOR WEIGHT REDUCTION, UP TO 25–40% OF WEIGHT LOST IS LEAN MASS, RAISING CONCERNS ABOUT MOBILITY, METABOLIC HEALTH, AND LONG-TERM WEIGHT MAINTENANCE. PROFESSIONAL SOCIETIES, INCLUDING THE AMERICAN COLLEGE OF LIFESTYLE MEDICINE, THE AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR NUTRITION, THE OBESITY MEDICINE ASSOCIATION, AND THE OBESITY SOCIETY, RECOMMEND INTEGRATING NUTRITIONAL MANAGEMENT AND RESISTANCE TRAINING FOR PATIENTS STARTING GLP-1 THERAPY. YET RIGOROUS EVIDENCE SUPPORTING THESE RECOMMENDATIONS IN REAL-WORLD PRACTICE IS LACKING.  TO ADDRESS THIS EVIDENCE GAP, WE PROPOSE A RANDOMIZED TRIAL ENROLLING 670 ADULTS WITH OBESITY (BMI ≥30 OR ≥27 WITH COMORBIDITY) FROM DIFFERENT SOCIOECONOMIC GROUPS WHO INITIATE GLP-1 THERAPY. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE RANDOMIZED WITHIN THREE WEEKS OF THEIR FIRST DOSE TO (1) A GLP-1 LIFESTYLE MANAGEMENT PROGRAM BASED ON YMCA OF FLORIDA’S FIRST COAST’S EVIDENCE-BASED  PHYSICAL ACTIVITY/RESISTANCE TRAINING PROGRAMS OR (2) ENHANCED USUAL CARE CONSISTING OF MONTHLY HEALTH EDUCATION WORKSHOPS PLUS STANDARD PHYSICIAN GUIDANCE. THE FIRST COAST YMCA GLP-1 LIFESTYLE MANAGEMENT PROGRAM WILL INTEGRATE NUTRITIONAL AND EXERCISE COMPONENTS TAILORED TO PATIENTS USING GLP-1S. AN ENHANCED USUAL CARE GROUP WILL SERVE AS AN ATTENTION-MATCHED CONTROL WITHOUT SPECIFIC DIET OR EXERCISE PRESCRIPTIONS. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME IS 6-MONTH CHANGE IN LEAN MASS, AS MEASURED BY APPENDICULAR LEAN TISSUE MASS BY DXA. SECONDARY OUTCOMES INCLUDE CHANGES IN ATHEROSCLEROTIC CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (ASCVD) RISK, TOTAL LEAN MASS, WEIGHT LOSS, DIET QUALITY, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND SELF-REPORTED QUALITY OF LIFE. WE HYPOTHESIZE THE FIRST COAST YMCA GLP-1 PROGRAM WILL (AIM 1) PRESERVE LEAN MASS, (AIM 2) REDUCE ASCVD RISK BY IMPROVING METABOLIC MARKERS, AND (AIM 3) ENHANCE QUALITY OF LIFE COMPARED TO ENHANCED USUAL CARE. THIS STUDY IS INNOVATIVE BY (1) TARGETING A RAPIDLY GROWING PATIENT POPULATION AT RISK FOR LEAN MASS LOSS, INCLUDING AN EMPHASIS ON LOWER-INCOME POPULATIONS THAT ARE DISPROPORTIONALLY IMPACTED BY OBESITY; (2) LEVERAGING A NONPROFIT SCALABLE PLATFORM FOR DIET, EXERCISE, AND BEHAVIOR CHANGE; AND (3) RIGOROUSLY EVALUATING ASCVD RISK REDUCTION, AN OUTCOME RARELY MEASURED IN THIS POPULATION. OUR MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM HAS EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE WITH LARGE CLINICAL TRIALS, WEIGHT LOSS AND EXERCISE INTERVENTIONS, BIOSTATISTICS, AND RECRUITMENT OF LOW-INCOME POPULATIONS. PARTNERSHIPS WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA AND THE FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH PROVIDE ACCESS TO A LARGE COHORT OF NEW GLP-1 USERS.  BY PRODUCING HIGH-QUALITY EVIDENCE ON HOW TO INTEGRATE LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS WITH GLP-1 THERAPY, THIS PROJECT WILL ADDRESS A CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION GAP BETWEEN PROFESSIONAL SOCIETY RECOMMENDATIONS AND CLINICAL PRACTICE, AS WELL AS IMPROVE LONG-TERM OUTCOMES FOR ADULTS WITH OBESITY.

description: SHARED DECISION MAKING FOR DEPRESSION CARE IN PRIMARY CARE: THE ENGAGE-D TRIAL - DEPRESSION AFFECTS MILLIONS OF AMERICAN ADULTS, CREATING SUBSTANTIAL HEALTHCARE AND ECONOMIC EFFECTS. MOST AMERICANS WITH DEPRESSION RECEIVE CARE IN PRIMARY CARE SETTINGS, WHERE PRIMARY CARE PROVIDERS (PCPS) DELIVER MUCH OF THE DEPRESSION CARE, PARTICULARLY IN SAFETY-NET SETTINGS. DESPITE EXISTING GUIDELINES, PCPS OFTEN HAVE LIMITED TIME AND STRUCTURED TOOLS TO DISCUSS DEPRESSION TREATMENT OPTIONS WITH PATIENTS DURING ROUTINE VISITS. THESE COMMUNICATION CHALLENGES CAN CONTRIBUTE TO PROBLEMS WITH TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT: PCPS SOMETIMES PRESCRIBE ANTIDEPRESSANTS WITHOUT FULLY DISCUSSING THE RATIONALE, ASSESSING PATIENT PREFERENCES, OR PRESENTING ALTERNATIVES. CONSEQUENTLY, PATIENTS MAY NOT FULLY UNDERSTAND THEIR DEPRESSION DIAGNOSIS, AVAILABLE TREATMENT OPTIONS, OR REASONS FOR PRESCRIBED TREATMENTS. SHARED DECISION MAKING (SDM) IS A BRIEF, LOW-COST HEALTH COMMUNICATION STRATEGY THAT IMPROVES TREATMENT DECISION-MAKING. IN SDM, PATIENTS AND PROVIDERS COLLABORATE TO MAKE HEALTHCARE DECISIONS TOGETHER, WITH PROVIDERS HELPING PATIENTS GAIN NEEDED KNOWLEDGE, IMPROVE DECISION-MAKING SELF-EFFICACY, AND ENHANCE PROVIDER TRUST AS TREATMENT RECOMMENDATIONS BECOME BETTER ALIGNED WITH PATIENTS' NEEDS, PREFERENCES, AND VALUES. PATIENT-PERCEIVED SDM CONSISTENTLY CORRELATES WITH BETTER TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT AND IMPROVED HEALTH OUTCOMES. HOWEVER, RIGOROUS AND EFFECTIVE SDM INTERVENTIONS SPECIFICALLY DESIGNED FOR DEPRESSION CARE IN SAFETY-NET PRIMARY CARE SETTINGS ARE CURRENTLY LACKING. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, THIS TWO-ARM, PCP-LEVEL CLUSTER RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL EVALUATES THE RIGOR AND EFFECTS OF AN SDM INTERVENTION FOR DEPRESSION TREATMENT IN 300 SAFETY-NET PRIMARY CARE PATIENTS WITH DEPRESSION, CLUSTERED BY 16 PCPS (8 PER ARM: INTERVENTION VS. TREATMENT AS USUAL). THE INTERVENTION INCLUDES PCP TRAINING, ENCOUNTER DECISION AID, AND STRUCTURED SDM DISCUSSION TO ENABLE PCPS TO FACILITATE SDM DURING ROUTINE APPOINTMENTS, AND TO IMPROVE COMMUNICATION ABOUT TREATMENT OPTIONS AND ALTERNATIVES. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO EXAMINE INTERVENTION EFFECTS ON FOUR OUTCOMES ACROSS TWO DOMAINS: AIM 1 EXAMINES IMPROVED DEPRESSION CARE OVER SIX MONTHS (DEPRESSION SYMPTOM SEVERITY AND TREATMENT ENGAGEMENT); AIM 2 EVALUATES IMPROVED PATIENT-PERCEIVED SDM POST-INTERVENTION (ENHANCED PATIENT-PROVIDER COMMUNICATION QUALITY AND REDUCED DECISIONAL CONFLICT); AIM 3 INVESTIGATES MECHANISMS OF ACTION, FOCUSING ON HOW PATIENT KNOWLEDGE OF DEPRESSION AND TREATMENT, DECISION-MAKING SELF-EFFICACY, AND TRUST ARE AFFECTED BY THE INTERVENTION AND MEDIATE IMPROVEMENTS IN THE FOUR OUTCOMES. BY DETERMINING THE EFFECTS OF SDM ON BOTH THE PATIENT-PROVIDER RELATIONSHIP AND DEPRESSION CARE OUTCOMES, IDENTIFYING THE MECHANISMS DRIVING SDM EFFECTIVENESS, AND MEASURING TREATMENT UTILIZATION AND IMPLEMENTATION-RELEVANT FEASIBILITY INDICATORS, THIS PROJECT HAS THE POTENTIAL TO ESTABLISH A SCALABLE MODEL OF DEPRESSION CARE WITH BROAD APPLICABILITY ACROSS PRIMARY CARE SETTINGS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EVALUATING THE HEALTH AND DEVELOPMENTAL IMPACTS OF WILDFIRE EXPOSURE ON CHILDREN - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE MAUI WILDFIRE EXPOSURE STUDY – CHILDREN’S COHORT (MAUIWES-CHILDREN) INVESTIGATES THE LONG-TERM HEALTH, DEVELOPMENTAL, AND EDUCATIONAL IMPACTS OF THE AUGUST 8, 2023, MAUI WILDFIRES, THE DEADLIEST U.S. WILDFIRE IN OVER A CENTURY. THE FIRES DISPLACED OVER 12,000 RESIDENTS, DESTROYED 2,200 BUILDINGS, AND DEEPENED EXISTING INEQUITIES ACROSS NATIVE HAWAIIAN, PACIFIC ISLANDER, AND IMMIGRANT FAMILIES. PRELIMINARY MAUIWES FINDINGS FROM 200 CHILDREN REVEAL HIGH RATES OF DEPRESSION (50.5%), ANXIETY (29.5%), PROBABLE PTSD (15%), AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION (43.2%), AND ACADEMIC SETBACKS, UNDERSCORING AN URGENT NEED FOR LONG-TERM INVESTIGATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT WILDFIRE-EXPOSED CHILDREN WILL EXPERIENCE POORER PHYSICAL, MENTAL, AND ACADEMIC OUTCOMES THAN UNEXPOSED PEERS, DRIVEN BY TOXICANT EXPOSURE, CHRONIC STRESS, AND DISRUPTED SOCIAL ENVIRONMENTS, AND THAT DISPARITIES WILL WIDEN WITHOUT EARLY INTERVENTION. WE WILL EXPAND MAUIWES BY ENROLLING 400 WILDFIRE-EXPOSED AND 400 MATCHED UNEXPOSED CHILDREN AND FOLLOW THEM OVER FOUR YEARS. INTEGRATING ENVIRONMENTAL, CLINICAL, BEHAVIORAL, AND EDUCATIONAL DATA, WE WILL MODEL TRAJECTORIES OF LUNG FUNCTION, MENTAL HEALTH, COGNITION, AND ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE TO IDENTIFY RISK AND RESILIENCE PATHWAYS. THIS FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND LONGITUDINAL STUDY UNITES ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE, PEDIATRICS, AND SOCIAL DETERMINANTS RESEARCH TO DEFINE THE BIOLOGICAL, PSYCHOLOGICAL, AND SOCIAL SEQUELAE OF WILDFIRE EXPOSURE. FINDINGS WILL INFORM PEDIATRIC MENTAL HEALTH AND RESPIRATORY SCREENING, SCHOOL-BASED RECOVERY PROGRAMS, AND DISASTER-RESPONSE POLICIES, ESTABLISHING MAUIWES AS A NATIONAL MODEL FOR PROTECTING CHILD HEALTH AND RESILIENCE FOLLOWING ENVIRONMENTAL CRISES.

description: A NETWORK SCIENCE APPROACH TO EMERGENCY SURGICAL CARE FOR OLDER ADULTS: EVALUATING THE IMPACT OF HEALTH SYSTEM STRUCTURE ON OUTCOMES AND ACCESS TO CARE - MODIFIED PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SECTION  EACH YEAR, OVER 3 MILLION PATIENTS IN THE UNITED STATES ARE ADMITTED WITH EMERGENCY GENERAL SURGERY (EGS) CONDITIONS, WHICH ARE A GROUP OF ACUTE NON-TRAUMATIC THORACIC, ABDOMINAL AND SOFT TISSUE CONDITIONS THAT REQUIRE URGENT SURGICAL EVALUATION AND MANAGEMENT. OLDER ADULTS REPRESENT APPROXIMATELY HALF OF ALL EGS PATIENTS, WHO EXPERIENCE VARIABLE RATES OF POOR OUTCOMES, WITH 1-YEAR MORTALITY THAT APPROACHES 30% AND OVER HALF READMITTED TO HOSPITAL WITHIN 30-DAYS. A CENTRAL CHALLENGE IN EGS CARE DELIVERY IS THAT HOSPITALS WITH EMERGENCY SURGICAL CAPABILITIES ARE DISTRIBUTED DIFFERENTLY ACROSS THE UNITED STATES, LEADING TO WIDE VARIANCE IN AVAILABILITY OF CARE THAT INCREASES MORTALITY AND AFFECTS RURAL PATIENTS AND COMMUNITIES THAT EXPERIENCE PERSISTENT DIFFERENCES IN HEALTH STATUS. TO DEVELOP EFFECTIVE HEALTH SYSTEMS FOR EGS, IT IS CRITICAL TO UNDERSTAND GEOGRAPHIC PATTERNS OF HOSPITAL UTILIZATION AND HOW HEALTH SYSTEM STRUCTURE IMPACTS PATIENT OUTCOMES. THIS PROPOSAL ADDRESSES THESE KNOWLEDGE GAPS BY APPLYING NETWORK-BASED COMMUNITY DETECTION METHODS TO IDENTIFY AND CHARACTERIZE NATURALLY OCCURRING GEOGRAPHIC REGIONS OF EGS CARE AND EXAMINE HOW HOSPITAL NETWORKS WITHIN THESE REGIONS CONTRIBUTE TO DIFFERENCES IN AVAILABILITY OF CARE AND OUTCOMES FOR OLDER ADULTS. OUR OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS IS THAT THE STRUCTURE AND ORGANIZATION OF REGIONAL NETWORKS INFLUENCES AVAILABILITY OF CARE AND CONTRIBUTES TO OUTCOMES AND CLINICALLY MEANINGFUL DIFFERENCES FOR SPECIFIC SUBPOPULATIONS. THE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE: 1) USING NATIONAL MEDICARE CLAIMS DATA AND NETWORK SCIENCE METHODS, WE WILL IDENTIFY AND CHARACTERIZE EMPIRIC GEOGRAPHIC HEALTH REFERRAL REGIONS ACROSS THE US FOR OLDER ADULTS RECEIVING EGS CARE. WE WILL QUANTIFY VARIATION IN NETWORK STRUCTURE AND ORGANIZATION, AS WELL AS AVAILABILITY AND RECEIPT OF CARE THROUGH ED PRESENTATION AND INTERHOSPITAL TRANSFER. 2) TEST THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN NETWORK CHARACTERISTICS AND CLINICAL OUTCOMES FOR OLDER EGS PATIENTS. WE WILL USE MULTI-LEVEL GEOGRAPHICALLY WEIGHTED REGRESSION MODELING TO EXAMINE THE CONTRIBUTION OF NETWORK ORGANIZATION TO ACUTE IN-HOSPITAL OUTCOMES AND POST-DISCHARGE CARE UTILIZATION. 3) ASSESS NETWORK CONTRIBUTIONS TO DIFFERENCES IN AVAILABILITY, RECEIPT OF CARE AND OUTCOMES AMONG POPULATIONS THAT EXPERIENCE ELEVATED RISK OF POOR OUTCOMES. IMPACT: USING INNOVATIVE NETWORK SCIENCE METHODS, THIS WORK WILL ADVANCE ONGOING EFFORTS TO DEVELOP EFFECTIVE EGS SYSTEMS FOR OLDER ADULTS BY INCREASING OUR KNOWLEDGE OF HOW HEALTH SYSTEM STRUCTURE CONTRIBUTES TO PATIENT OUTCOMES. IT WILL HAVE AN IMMEDIATE IMPACT BY DEFINING NATIONAL REFERRAL REGIONS FOR SURGICAL CARE, INFORMING THE ONGOING DEVELOPMENT OF REGIONALIZED EGS PROGRAMS, AND OFFERS NOVEL METHODS TO MONITOR CHANGES IN AVAILABILITY OF EMERGENCY SURGICAL CARE.

description: STATE MODULATION OF HIPPOCAMPAL MEDIATED MEMORY FORMATION IN THE HUMAN BRAIN - PROJECT SUMMARY EVERY MOMENT OF OUR DAILY EXPERIENCE SETS THE STARTING POINT FOR A NEW MEMORY TO POTENTIALLY FORM. HOWEVER, A HOST OF NEURAL EVENTS MUST CONSPIRE TOGETHER FOR ANY GIVEN EXPERIENCE TO FIND A PERSISTENT PLACE IN OUR MEMORIES. HOW AND WHEN ARE MEMORIES STRENGTHENED OVER TIME TO SUPPORT THEIR LONG-TERM CONSOLIDATION? ONE MECHANISM FOR STRENGTHENING PUTATIVE MEMORY TRACES IS THOUGHT TO BE THE REPEATED “REPLAY” OR “REACTIVATION” OF NEURAL ACTIVITY PATTERNS FROM THE PAST, WHICH OCCURS IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS DURING SHARP WAVE RIPPLE EVENTS. A PREVAILING VIEW IS THAT “OFFLINE” PERIODS OF REST, PARTICULARLY SLEEP, ARE CRUCIAL FOR PROMOTING THESE HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLE EVENTS IN THE SERVICE OF PROGRESSIVELY STRENGTHENING AND CONSOLIDATING LONG-TERM MEMORIES. HOWEVER, A NUMBER OF RECENT FINDINGS FROM THE HUMAN HAVE SUGGESTED HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLE EVENTS OCCUR READILY DURING AWAKE “ONLINE” MEMORY PROCESSING STAGES, SUCH AS ENCODING AND RETRIEVAL. IF FURTHER SUPPORTED, THESE DATA ARGUE FOR A POTENTIAL RECONSIDERATION OF WHAT STATES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLE GENESIS, PROMOTING A BROADER FUNCTIONAL ROLE, BUT SUCH FINDINGS ARE HIGHLY VARIABLE ACROSS HUMAN STUDIES AND SHOW DIVERGENCE FROM THE RODENT. THEREFORE, A CENTRAL QUESTION THAT REMAINS TO BE RESOLVED IN THE FIELD IS: WHEN DO AWAKE HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLES OCCUR IN HUMANS? IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE SEEK TO TEST A PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL STATE MODEL TO ANSWER THIS QUESTION, WHICH WE ARGUE BETTER ACCOUNTS FOR RECENT FINDINGS IN THE HUMAN AND IS CLOSELY BASED ON THE MECHANISMS OF RIPPLE GENESIS DERIVED FROM ANIMAL MODELS. SPECIFICALLY, WE ARGUE IN SUPPORT OF HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLES BEING ASSOCIATED WITH OFFLINE STATES, BUT THAT SUCH STATES OCCUR TRANSIENTLY AND DYNAMICALLY WITH NATURAL FLUCTUATIONS IN AWAKE AROUSAL. MECHANISTICALLY, THIS STATE MODEL LINKS THE CAUSAL ROLE OF ACETYLCHOLINE IN MODULATING BOTH AROUSAL STATES AS WELL AS HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLE GENESIS. TO TRACK THIS INFLUENCE, WE WILL USE PUPILLOMETRY, TOGETHER WITH INVASIVE RECORDINGS FROM THE HUMAN HIPPOCAMPUS. ACROSS TWO AIMS WE WILL CORRELATE AND CAUSALLY TEST I) THE INFLUENCE OF AROUSAL STATE ON HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLE GENESIS (AIM 1); II) THE INFLUENCE OF AROUSAL STATE MODULATION OF RIPPLE EVENTS ON LONG-TERM MEMORY BEHAVIOR (AIM 2). THROUGH THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS, WE WILL PROVIDE IMPORTANT EVIDENCE TOWARDS UNDERSTANDING HOW AND WHEN MEMORIES ARE FORMED AND CONSOLIDATED OVER TIME AND THE ROLE PLAYED BY AROUSAL IN THIS PROCESS, WHICH HAS BROAD LINKS TO THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF AROUSAL DYSREGULATION COMMON TO MANY PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS. FURTHERMORE, THE PROPOSED PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL MODEL MAY PROVIDE IMPORTANT TEMPORAL INFORMATION FOR TARGETING NEUROMODULATORY INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE MEMORY AND RELATED DYSFUNCTIONS IN DISEASE.

description: PROGRESSION OF NEUROMETABOLIC DYSFUNCTION AND MECHANISMS OF COGNITIVE TRAINING IN MID- TO LATE-LIFE SCHIZOPHRENIA - PROJECT SUMMARY COGNITIVE AND VISUAL IMPAIRMENTS AMONG PEOPLE WITH SCHIZOPHRENIA (SZ) REPRESENT A SIGNIFICANT MENTAL HEALTH AND HEALTHCARE COST BURDEN. COGNITIVE AND VISUAL FUNCTIONS RELY ON BRAIN ENERGY SUPPLY AND EXCITATORY:INHIBITORY BALANCE, WHICH ARE ALTERED IN SZ AND HEALTHY AGING. EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THE EFFECTS OF AGING ON BRAIN FUNCTION MAY BE PREMATURELY ADVANCED IN SCHIZOPHRENIA, BUT WHETHER COGNITION AND PERCEPTION DECLINE MORE RAPIDLY WITH AGE IN SZ, AND THE NEUROCHEMICAL MECHANISMS OF THOSE CHANGES, REMAINS UNCLEAR. ENCOURAGINGLY, BOTH SZ AND HEALTHY OLDER ADULTS SHOW IMPROVEMENTS IN FUNCTIONING AFTER COGNITIVE TRAINING THAT TARGETS COGNITION AND PERCEPTION. THIS PROPOSAL WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT GLUCOSE METABOLISM AND EXCITATORY GLUTAMATERGIC FUNCTIONING ARE DYSREGULATED IN SCHIZOPHRENIA DURING MID-TO-LATE LIFE, WHICH CONTRIBUTE TO COGNITIVE AND VISUAL IMPAIRMENTS, AND MAY NORMALIZE IN RESPONSE TO COGNITIVE TRAINING. WE WILL USE 7 T MRS TO QUANTIFY BRAIN CHEMISTRY IN PREFRONTAL AND OCCIPITAL CORTEX IN 81 SZ AND 81 HEALTHY CONTROLS (AGED 35-79) IN AN ACCELERATED LONGITUDINAL EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN ACROSS 3 SCANNING SESSIONS PER PERSON (0, 18, 30 MONTHS), PLUS A FOURTH SESSION AFTER COGNITIVE TRAINING (32 MONTHS). PARTICIPANTS WILL BE DIVIDED INTO 3 AGE COHORTS (DEMOGRAPHICALLY BALANCED; N = 27 PER COHORT PER GROUP). WE RECENTLY COLLECTED A LARGE 7 T MRS DATA SET AS PART OF THE PSYCHOSIS HUMAN CONNECTOME PROJECT, WHICH SUPPORTS THE FEASIBILITY OF OUR APPROACH. WE WILL RE-RECRUIT PARTICIPANTS FROM THE PREVIOUS STUDY, WHICH WILL GIVE US ADDITIONAL LONGITUDINAL DATA. ASSESSING HOW BRAIN CHEMISTRY CHANGES LONGITUDINALLY IN MID-TO-LATE LIFE SCHIZOPHRENIA WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHT INTO THE NEURAL BASIS OF COGNITIVE AND VISUAL IMPAIRMENTS. USING COGNITIVE TRAINING WILL ALLOW US TO PROBE THE MECHANISMS OF PLASTICITY THAT SUPPORT IMPROVED COGNITIVE AND VISUAL PERFORMANCE IN SZ AND OLDER ADULTS. OUR WORK WILL HELP TO IDENTIFY NOVEL BIOMARKERS FOR PREDICTING INDIVIDUAL TRAJECTORIES OF BRAIN HEALTH IN MID-TO-LATE LIFE SCHIZOPHRENIA, AS WELL AS BRAIN MECHANISMS FOR FUTURE INTERVENTIONAL WORK USING COGNITIVE TRAINING. THESE ARE IMPORTANT STEPS TO REDUCE SUFFERING AND HEALTHCARE COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH SZ.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE IMPORTANCE OF SLEEP FOR PREDICTION OF DEPRESSION IN ADOLESCENCE - ABSTRACT DEPRESSION INCREASES DRAMATICALLY DURING ADOLESCENCE, WITH A PREVALENCE RATE INCREASING TO OVER 25% AT AGE 17 YEARS FOR MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER (MDD), AND A 3-FOLD GREATER RISK FOR FEMALES. DEPRESSION IN LATER ADOLESCENCE REPRESENTS THE GREATEST GLOBAL BURDEN OF DISEASE, IS ASSOCIATED WITH SUBSTANCE USE AND IMPAIRMENT ACROSS MULTIPLE DOMAINS, AND IS A MAJOR RISK FOR SUICIDE. ALTHOUGH A HIGH-RISK PERIOD, THE NEURAL PLASTICITY DURING THIS PHASE OF LIFE PROVIDES A WINDOW OF OPPORTUNITY FOR EARLY INTERVENTION EFFORTS TARGETING MODIFIABLE BEHAVIORS, SUCH AS SLEEP. COMPLICATING INTERVENTION IS THE HETEROGENEITY OF DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, POTENTIALLY WITH DIFFERENT UNDERLYING BIOLOGICAL PATHWAYS, THE BROADER SOCIAL/ENVIRONMENTAL CONTEXT THAT FORMS THE BACKDROP FOR DEPRESSION RISK, AND THE INTERACTIVE NATURE OF KEY RISK FACTORS. TO ACCOUNT FOR THESE CHALLENGES AND TO ADVANCE DISCOVERY, WE CONDUCT INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL ANALYSES WITH A LARGE NUMBER OF ADOLESCENTS TRACKED OVER TIME, CONSIDERING NEUROBIOLOGICAL PATHWAYS, CONTEXTUAL FACTORS, AND DIVERGENCE BY SEX. WE FOCUS ON MODIFIABLE SLEEP BEHAVIOR, WHICH SHOWS PROMISE AS A PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION TARGET. APPLYING OUR NOVEL DEEP-LEARNING FRAMEWORK USING TWO PUBLIC LONGITUDINAL DATASETS OF ADOLESCENTS (NATIONAL CONSORTIUM ON ALCOHOL AND NEURODEVELOPMENT IN ADOLESCENCE [NCANDA; N=624] AND THE ADOLESCENT BRAIN COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT COHORT [ABCD; N=11800]), OUR OVERALL OBJECTIVE IS TO CLARIFY NEUROMECHANISTIC AND BEHAVIORAL RISK FOR DEPRESSION BY IDENTIFYING CONSTELLATIONS OF MEASURES AND THEIR INTERACTIONS ACROSS SOCIODEMOGRAPHIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, MODIFIABLE BEHAVIORS (E.G. SLEEP), COGNITIVE FUNCTION, PERSONALITY, AND NEURAL CIRCUITY THAT FORECAST DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS AND HERALD MDD IN INDIVIDUAL ADOLESCENTS. DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS ARE GROUPED ACCORDING TO CONSTRUCTS OF THE NIMH RDOC DOMAINS NEGATIVE AND POSITIVE VALENCE. AIM 1 USES A DATA-DRIVEN SEARCH ACROSS SLEEP HEALTH AND BRAIN CIRCUITRY MEASURES TO CHARACTERIZE DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS ACROSS RDOC CONSTRUCTS AND MDD DIAGNOSIS, ALSO CONSIDERING INTERACTIONS WITH SOCIODEMOGRAPHIC FACTORS, IN INDIVIDUALS IN NCANDA (AGES 12-17 YRS) AND SEEKS TO REPLICATE FINDINGS IN THE LARGE, DIVERSE ABCD COHORT (AGES: 9-17YRS). AIM 2 FOCUSES ON THE ABCD COHORT, TO FORECAST RDOC CONSTRUCTS AND MDD IN OLDER ADOLESCENTS (16-17 YRS) BASED ON THE CLOSEST PRIOR VISIT, EXPLICITLY EXAMINING DIFFERENCES BY SEX. ANALYSES ARE ENHANCED WITH PERSONALITY MEASURES AND OBJECTIVE MEASURES OF SLEEP, COGNITIVE ASSESSMENTS, AND TASK-FMRI OF EMOTION AND REWARD. AIM 3 USES ALL AVAILABLE LONGITUDINAL ABCD DATA TO FORECAST THE MAGNITUDE OF RDOC CONSTRUCTS AND MDD IN FUTURE YEARS TO IDENTIFY TRAJECTORIES OF INTERACTIONS ACROSS RISK FACTORS. OUR INNOVATIVE, INDIVIDUAL-FOCUSED ANALYSES TO IDENTIFY RISK FACTORS FOR DEPRESSION IN DEVELOPING ADOLESCENTS ENSURE RIGOR AND REPRODUCIBILITY, POTENTIALLY IMPROVING DEPRESSION RISK ASSESSMENT IN PREVENTION PROGRAMS. THE OUTCOME IS POISED TO HAVE HIGH PUBLIC HEALTH SIGNIFICANCE FOR ADVANCING EFFORTS FOR EARLY INTERCESSION, MITIGATION, AND PREVENTION OF THIS DEBILITATING, LIFE-THREATENING DISORDER.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A MULTI-LEVEL INTERVENTION TO UPSCALE HIV TESTING AND PREP UPTAKE FOR MEN WITH HIGH HIV EXPOSURE VIA COMMUNITY PHARMACIES IN RESOURCE-LIMITED SETTINGS - COMMUNITY PHARMACIES (CPS) ARE A PROMISING BUT UNDERUSED HIV PREVENTION PLATFORM. PHARMACISTS ARE OFTEN THE FIRST POINT OF CONTACT FOR HEALTHCARE IN COMMUNITIES WHERE FORMAL HEALTH FACILITIES MAY BE LESS ACCESSIBLE. WE HAVE A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO EFFICIENTLY STUDY THE POTENTIAL BENEFITS OF PHARMACIES FOR HIV PREVENTION IN GHANA. MEN WITH INCREASED HIV EXPOSURE IN GHANA EXPERIENCE A DISPROPORTIONATE HIV BURDEN, WITH RECENT DATA SHOWING HIV PREVALENCE OF 26.1% IN 2024, UP FROM 18% IN 2017, COMPARED WITH APPROXIMATELY 2% IN THE GENERAL POPULATION. ITS ESPECIALLY HIGH IN URBAN INFORMAL CENTERS, WHERE BEHAVIORAL EXPOSURE, LIMITED HIV KNOWLEDGE, CONFIDENTIALITY CONCERNS, AND CONSTRAINED ACCESS TO PREVENTION SERVICES REDUCE HIV TESTING AND PREP UPTAKE. GHANA, , HAS ADOPTED NATIONAL GUIDELINES FOR HIV SELF-TESTING (HIVST) AND PREP AND PRIORITIZED COMMUNITY-BASED PREVENTION ACCESS. HOWEVER, IMPLEMENTATION REMAINS LIMITED, AND EXISTING APPROACHES OFTEN EMPHASIZE ENROLLMENT AND DISTRIBUTION TARGETS RATHER THAN THE BEHAVIORAL, SOCIAL, AND SERVICE-ACCESS DETERMINANTS THAT SHAPE HIVST, PREP INITIATION, AND PREP ADHERENCE. OUR PILOTS SHOW THAT MEN ARE WILLING TO RECEIVE HIVST AND ORAL OR LONG-ACTING INJECTABLE (LAI) PREP THROUGH CPS AND THAT PHARMACISTS IN CPS ARE WILLING TO PROVIDE THESE SERVICES. YET CP-BASED IMPLEMENTATION HAS NOT BEEN SYSTEMATICALLY TESTED. TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS, WE DEVELOPED LAFIYA PHARMACY, A MULTILEVEL INTERVENTION THAT COMBINES AN EVIDENCE-BASED U.S. PHARMACY PREP DELIVERY MODEL WITH BEHAVIORAL COMPONENTS FROM LAFIYA, AN INTERVENTION DEVELOPED FOR URBAN INFORMAL SETTLEMENT CONTEXTS. LAFIYA PHARMACY IS DESIGNED TO ADDRESS PREVENTION KNOWLEDGE, SERVICE NAVIGATION, LINKAGE TO CARE, IMPLEMENTATION CAPACITY, AND ORAL OR LAI PREP ADHERENCE WHILE EXPANDING CONFIDENTIAL ACCESS TO HIV PREVENTION THROUGH CPS. THIS WORK TESTS WHETHER AN ENHANCED U.S. CP-BASED MODEL CAN FUNCTION UNDER CONDITIONS WHERE SOCIAL DETERRENTS, INFORMAL SETTLEMENT CONDITIONS, AND LIMITED FACILITY ENGAGEMENT SHAPE PREVENTION DECISIONS. GUIDED BY IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE FRAMEWORKS, THIS STUDY WILL FINALIZE AND EVALUATE LAFIYA PHARMACY TO INCREASE HIVST AND ORAL OR LAI PREP UPTAKE AMONG MEN WITH INCREASED HIV EXPOSURE. AIM 1 WILL FINALIZE THE INTERVENTION PROTOCOL THROUGH FOCUS GROUP DISCUSSIONS WITH MEN, COMMUNITY PHARMACISTS, AND HIV/PHARMACY POLICY STAKEHOLDERS, FOLLOWED BY EXPERT AND COMMUNITY ADVISORY BOARD REVIEW AND PILOT TESTING. AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE EFFECTIVENESS USING A STEPPED-WEDGE DESIGN WITH 12 RETAIL PHARMACIES, 60 PHARMACISTS, AND 240 MEN ACROSS SIX COMMUNITY CLUSTERS, WITH PRIMARY OUTCOMES OF HIVST UPTAKE AND ORAL OR LAI PREP UPTAKE. AIM 3 WILL CONDUCT FOLLOW-UP QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS TO EXPLAIN TRIAL FINDINGS AND INFORM SCALABILITY, SUSTAINABILITY, AND INTEGRATION INTO NATIONAL HIV PREVENTION SYSTEMS. THIS STUDY WILL GENERATE IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE ON WHETHER CPS CAN DELIVER CONFIDENTIAL, DECENTRALIZED HIV TESTING AND PREP SERVICES WHERE FACILITY-BASED ACCESS IS CONSTRAINED. GIVEN THE HEAVY BURDEN OF HIV IN THESE POPULATIONS IN GHANA, CONDUCT OF THE STUDY THERE WILL PROVIDE TIME- AND COST-EFFICIENIES RELATIVE TO US-BASED CONDUCT. FINDINGS WILL INFORM PHARMACY-BASED HIV PREVENTION IN GHANA AND PROVIDE TRANSFERABLE EVIDENCE FOR U.S. COMMUNITIES WHERE SIMILAR DETERMINANTS LIMIT HIV TESTING, PREP INITIATION, AND PREP PERSISTENCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE ASSEMBLY OF AXO-AXONIC SYNAPSES IN THE CEREBRAL CORTEX - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE PROPER FUNCTIONING OF CORTICAL CIRCUITS DEPENDS ON THE PRECISE FORMATION OF SYNAPTIC CONNECTIONS BETWEEN EXCITATORY PYRAMIDAL NEURONS (PYNS) AND A DIVERSE ARRAY OF INHIBITORY GABAERGIC INTERNEURONS (INS), EACH WITH DISTINCT AXONAL ARBORS THAT TARGET SPECIFIC SUBCELLULAR COMPARTMENTS OF PYNS AND SHAPE THEIR OUTPUT PROPERTIES. AMONG THESE INS, CHANDELIER CELLS (CHCS), ALSO KNOWN AS AXO-AXONIC CELLS, ARE ARGUABLY THE MOST DISTINCTIVE DUE TO THEIR EXQUISITE AXONAL MORPHOLOGY AND UNIQUE SUBCELLULAR INNERVATION. THESE CELLS POSSESS A HIGHLY BRANCHED AXON WITH MULTIPLE TERMINAL ARRAYS OF PRESYNAPTIC BOUTONS, REFERRED TO AS CARTRIDGES, ALLOWING ONE CHC TO CONNECT WITH A LARGE POPULATION OF PYNS. MOREOVER, CHCS ARE THE ONLY IN TYPE THAT FORMS SYNAPSES EXCLUSIVELY AT THE AXON INITIAL SEGMENT (AIS) OF PYNS, THE SITE OF ACTION POTENTIAL INITIATION. THESE FEATURES ENABLE CHCS TO EXERT DECISIVE YET PRECISE CONTROL OVER PYN FIRING AND POPULATION OUTPUT. CONSISTENT WITH THEIR FUNCTIONAL SIGNIFICANCE, DEFECTS IN CHC SYNAPTIC CONNECTIVITY HAVE BEEN IMPLICATED IN NEURAL DISORDERS, SUCH AS SCHIZOPHRENIA, AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER, AND EPILEPSY. DESPITE THEIR IMPORTANCE, THE MOLECULAR PROCESSES UNDERLYING THE SUBCELLULAR FORMATION OF CHC SYNAPSES ON PYN AISS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD, REPRESENTING A SIGNIFICANT KNOWLEDGE GAP. SYNAPSE FORMATION IS A COMPLEX, MULTISTEP PROCESS THAT INCLUDES SYNAPTIC TARGET RECOGNITION, THE FORMATION OF PRE- AND POST-SYNAPTIC CONTACTS, AND THE DIFFERENTIATION AND STABILIZATION OF SYNAPSES. BEYOND NEURON-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS, MICROGLIA, THE BRAIN'S IMMUNE CELLS, HAVE ALSO EMERGED AS KEY CONTRIBUTORS TO SYNAPSE DEVELOPMENT. WHILE WE AND OTHERS HAVE IDENTIFIED CHC-EXPRESSED SIGNALING AND CYTOSKELETAL REMODELING PROTEINS INVOLVED IN THE LATER STAGES OF SYNAPSE FORMATION, THE MOLECULAR COMPONENTS DRIVING THE SUBCELLULAR INNERVATION OF PYN AISS BY CHCS, AS WELL AS MICROGLIA'S ROLE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE AXO-AXONIC SYNAPSES, REMAIN LARGELY ELUSIVE. IN RECENT STUDIES SCREENING FOR PYN-EXPRESSED CELL ADHESION MOLECULES (CAMS) ENRICHED AT THE AIS, WE IDENTIFIED L1CAM AND CNTN1 AS KEY MOLECULES REQUIRED FOR PROPER CHC/PYN AIS INNERVATION. ADDITIONALLY, WE FOUND THAT MICROGLIA PROMOTE CHC CARTRIDGE/BOUTON DEVELOPMENT AND AIS SYNAPTOGENESIS, UNCOVERING FOR THE FIRST TIME A SYNAPTOGENIC ROLE FOR THESE CELLS IN REGULATING INHIBITORY SYNAPSES. BUILDING ON THESE DISCOVERIES, WE PROPOSE HERE TO IDENTIFY THE PRESYNAPTIC BINDING PARTNERS OF L1CAM AND CNTN1 ON CHCS, CRUCIAL FOR UNDERSTANDING CHC TARGETING OF PYN AISS AT THE SUBCELLULAR LEVEL. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL DEFINE HOW MICROGLIA ARE RECRUITED TO CHC-INNERVATED PYN AISS AND HOW THEY PROMOTE SYNAPTOGENESIS AND MODULATE CHC/PYN SYNAPTIC FUNCTION, REVEALING THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THEIR PREVIOUSLY UNRECOGNIZED ROLE IN INHIBITORY SYNAPSE FORMATION. TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS, WE WILL USE A MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH THAT COMBINES CUTTING-EDGE TECHNIQUES SUCH AS TARGETED IN UTERO ELECTROPORATION, TWO-PHOTON LIVE IMAGING IN AWAKE MICE, AND ADVANCED GENETIC, MOLECULAR, AND ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL METHODS. TOGETHER, OUR STUDIES WILL PROVIDE PIONEERING INSIGHTS INTO THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF CHC/PYN AIS SYNAPTIC CONNECTIVITY, WITH IMPLICATIONS FOR HEALTH AND DISEASE.
