description: DECIPHERING CORTICAL CIRCUIT ABNORMALITIES UNDERLYING DEFICITS IN VISUAL AND PREFRONTAL GAMMA OSCILLATIONS IN SCHIZOPHRENIA - ABSTRACT THE MOST PERSISTENT, DEBILITATING, AND UNDERTREATED FEATURES OF SCHIZOPHRENIA (SZ) INCLUDE DEFICITS IN WORKING MEMORY (WM). WM DEPENDS ON BOTH THE ACCURATE ENCODING OF A STIMULUS AND THE MAINTENANCE OF THIS INFORMATION IN THE ABSENCE OF A STIMULUS. THESE PROCESSES RELY ON GAMMA (Γ) OSCILLATIONS WITH DISTINCT DYNAMICS: TRANSIENT Γ-OSCILLATIONS IN SENSORY CORTICES SUCH AS THE PRIMARY VISUAL CORTEX (V1) SUPPORT STIMULUS ENCODING, WHILE SUSTAINED Γ-OSCILLATIONS IN THE PREFRONTAL CORTEX (PFC) SUPPORT MEMORY MAINTENANCE. IN SZ, THE POWER OF Γ- OSCILLATIONS IS LOWER IN BOTH V1 AND PFC, CONSISTENT WITH DEFICITS IN BOTH SENSORY ENCODING AND WM RETENTION IN THE ILLNESS. CORTICAL Γ-OSCILLATIONS ARE GENERATED BY A CANONICAL MICROCIRCUIT OF PYRAMIDAL NEURONS (PNS) AND PARVALBUMIN-EXPRESSING INTERNEURONS (PVIS). IN THIS CIRCUIT, EXCITATORY INPUTS FROM PNS TO PVIS (E→I) VIA AMPA RECEPTORS (AMPAR) AND INHIBITION FROM PVIS TO PNS (I→E) VIA GABAA RECEPTORS (GABAAR) ARE THOUGHT TO BE KEY DETERMINANTS OF Γ-POWER. SYNAPTIC STRENGTHS AT THESE SITES ARE SHAPED BY THE ORGANIZATION OF POSTSYNAPTIC RECEPTORS, WHICH ARE TRAFFICKED TO POSTSYNAPTIC DENSITY AND ARRANGED INTO NANOSCALE CLUSTERS THAT TRANS- SYNAPTICALLY ALIGN WITH PRESYNAPTIC ACTIVE ZONES. PRIOR STUDIES SUGGEST THAT THE STRENGTHS OF E→I AND I→E ARE LOWER IN SZ, WITH MORE SEVERE DEFICITS IN V1 THAN IN PFC. IN PARALLEL, OUR PILOT COMPUTATIONAL MODELING INDICATES THAT SUSTAINED Γ-OSCILLATIONS MAY BE MORE VULNERABLE TO SYNAPTIC DISRUPTION THAN TRANSIENT Γ-OSCILLATIONS. TOGETHER, THESE FINDINGS MOTIVATE A NOVEL DISEASE MODEL OF SZ IN WHICH SHARED SYNAPTIC DEFICITS WITH REGION-SPECIFIC SEVERITY DISRUPT Γ-OSCILLATIONS WITH DISTINCT TEMPORAL DYNAMICS. TO TEST THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS OF THIS MODEL, WE PROPOSE TO COMBINE HIGH-RESOLUTION EXPANSION MICROSCOPY (EXM) WITH MULTISCALE MODELING TO EVALUATE TWO COMPLEMENTARY HYPOTHESES: (H1) RECEPTOR ORGANIZATION AT E→I AND I→E SYNAPSES IS DISRUPTED IN SZ, WITH GREATER SEVERITY IN V1 THAN IN PFC; AND (H2) THIS REGIONAL DIFFERENCE IS REQUIRED TO IMPAIR TRANSIENT Γ-POWER IN V1 AND SUSTAINED Γ-POWER IN PFC DUE TO THEIR DIFFERENTIAL VULNERABILITY. TO TEST H1, WE WILL USE EXM TO QUANTIFY KEY ORGANIZATIONAL PARAMETERS OF RECEPTOR TRAFFICKING, CLUSTERING AND ALIGNMENT FOR AMPARS AT E→I SYNAPSES (AIM 1.1) AND OF GABAAR AT I→E SYNAPSES (AIM 1.2) IN V1 AND PFC OF 40 MATCHED PAIRS OF SZ AND UNAFFECTED SUBJECTS. TO TEST H2, THE PARAMETERS OF RECEPTOR ORGANIZATION FOR EACH INDIVIDUAL SYNAPSE OBTAINED IN AIM1 WILL BE INCORPORATED INTO A SPATIALLY EXPLICIT SYNAPSE MODEL TO SIMULATE POSTSYNAPTIC CONDUCTANCE PROFILES AT THESE SYNAPSES (AIM 2.1). THE CONDUCTANCE PROFILES FROM AIM 2.1 WILL THEN SERVE AS INPUTS TO A SUBJECT-SPECIFIC SPIKING NETWORK MODEL THAT GENERATES EITHER TRANSIENT OR SUSTAINED Γ-OSCILLATIONS (AIM 2.2) TO ASSESS HOW CHANGES IN SYNAPTIC CONDUCTANCE DRIVEN BY RECEPTOR ORGANIZATION DIFFERENTIALLY AFFECT TRANSIENT Γ-POWER IN V1 AND SUSTAINED Γ-POWER IN PFC. THE INSIGHTS GAINED FROM THIS STUDY WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE CIRCUIT MECHANISMS UNDERLYING DEFICITS IN Γ-OSCILLATIONS WITH DISTINCT DYNAMICS AT THE LEVEL OF POSTSYNAPTIC RECEPTORS, WHICH WILL PAVE THE WAY FOR DEVELOPING NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TARGETING THESE RECEPTORS TO ADDRESS WM IMPAIRMENTS IN SZ.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SPECTRALLY COMPATIBLE SENSORS AND ACTUATORS OF IN VIVO PKA ACTIVITY - ABSTRACT  PROTEIN KINASE A (PKA) IS A PIVOTAL KINASE IN BIOLOGY, REGULATING A WIDE ARRAY OF PROCESSES ACROSS NEARLY ALL ORGANS. PKA ACTIVITY IS GOVERNED BY PRECISE SPATIAL, TEMPORAL, AND AMPLITUDE CONTROLS, AND DISRUPTIONS IN THESE FEATURES CAN LEAD TO SERIOUS CONDITIONS SUCH AS BRAIN DISORDERS AND CANCER. DESPITE THE IMPORTANT ROLES OF PKA IN PLASTICITY AND LEARNING, CANCER METASTASIS, METABOLISM, AND HORMONE SECRETION, AND DESPITE THE RICH DYNAMICS OF PKA REVEALED BY OPTICAL REPORTERS, KEY GAPS IN KNOWLEDGE REMAIN: (1) WHAT FUNCTIONS DO THESE SPATIOTEMPORAL DYNAMICS SERVE IN VIVO? (2) HOW CAN WE PERTURB SUCH SPATIOTEMPORAL DYNAMICS AND CONCURRENTLY EVALUATE THE EFFICACY AND PHYSIOLOGICAL OUTCOMES OF PKA PERTURBATION IN VIVO? (3) HOW DO MULTIPLE INTRACELLULAR SIGNALS COORDINATE TO INFLUENCE CELL BIOLOGY AND ANIMAL BEHAVIOR? ADDRESSING THESE QUESTIONS REQUIRES MOLECULAR TOOLS CAPABLE OF PERTURBING AND RECORDING PKA ACTIVITY WITH HIGH SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL PRECISION IN VIVO. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO CREATE A SUITE OF SPECTRALLY COMPATIBLE OPTICAL SENSORS AND ACTUATORS THAT CAN RECORD AND PERTURB THE ACTIVITY OF KEY KINASES IN REAL TIME, BRIDGING THE GAP BETWEEN CELL BIOLOGY AND SYSTEMS BIOLOGY. THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP HIGH-PERFORMING TOOLS SPECIFICALLY FOR IN VIVO REAL-TIME RECORDING AND PERTURBATION OF PKA ACTIVITY. WE ARE UNIQUELY EQUIPPED TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL GIVEN THE UNIQUE EXPERTISE OF OUR TEAM IN PKA SENSOR AND ACTUATOR DEVELOPMENT AND PKA BIOLOGY, AS WELL AS PROMISING PRELIMINARY DATA THAT DEMONSTRATES THE FEASIBILITY OF OUR APPROACHES. WE WILL DEVELOP A SET OF FUNCTIONAL PHOTOACTIVATABLE PKA INHIBITORS (PA-PKI) (AIM 1). WE WILL ALSO DEVELOP RED AND FAR-RED PKA ACTIVITY SENSORS AND TEST THEM FOR MULTIPLEXED IMAGING WITH OTHER GREEN BIOSENSORS (AIM 2). TO ENABLE CONCURRENT IN VIVO PERTURBATION AND EVALUATION OF THE PERTURBATION EFFICACY, WE WILL TEST SIMULTANEOUS INHIBITION AND OPTICAL RECORDING OF PKA ACTIVITY WITH OUR BLUE LIGHT-STIMULATED PA-PKIS AND RED/FAR-RED PKA ACTIVITY SENSORS (AIM 3). WE WILL VALIDATE THESE TOOLS WITH PROOF-OF-PRINCIPLE EXPERIMENTS IN CELLS, BRAIN SLICES, AND IN TWO WELL-ESTABLISHED SYSTEMS IN VIVO ACROSS TWO ORGANISMS (AIM 3). WE WILL FURTHER DEMONSTRATE THE EXCITING POTENTIAL OF OUR TOOLS WITH A QUESTION WHERE THESE TOOLS CAN BRING NEW BIOLOGICAL INSIGHTS (AIM 3). TOGETHER, OUR WORK WILL CREATE TOOLS THAT CAN ILLUMINATE THE NATURE AND FUNCTION OF SPECIFIC PKA ACTIVITY DYNAMICS ACROSS CELLS, ORGANS, AND ORGANISMS IN VIVO. THIS WILL IN THE LONG TERM REVEAL HOW SPECIFIC FEATURES OF PKA DYNAMICS IMPACT DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AN EXAMINATION OF SOCIAL CONNECTION IN SUICIDE RISK DURING THE COLLEGE TRANSITION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  SUICIDE IS THE SECOND LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH AMONG INDIVIDUALS AGED 15–24, UNDERSCORING THE URGENT NEED TO ELUCIDATE THE CONTEXTS AND MECHANISMS THAT SHAPE SUICIDE RISK DURING THIS DEVELOPMENTAL PERIOD. THE TRANSITION TO COLLEGE REPRESENTS A PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE WINDOW, MARKED BY MAJOR SOCIAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL ADJUSTMENTS THAT HEIGHTEN DISTRESS AND RISK FOR SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS. SOCIAL CONNECTION, WHICH ENCOMPASSES BOTH PERCEIVED BELONGING AND OBJECTIVE SOCIAL ENGAGEMENT, IS A CENTRAL DETERMINANT OF THIS RISK. HOWEVER, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW DIFFERENT DIMENSIONS OF CONNECTION, ESPECIALLY THOSE OCCURRING IN DIGITAL SPACES, INFLUENCE SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS DURING THIS CRITICAL TRANSITION.  WE WILL LEVERAGE MULTIMODAL, HIGH-RESOLUTION ASSESSMENTS TO ELUCIDATE HOW SOCIAL CONNECTION ACROSS DIGITAL AND PHYSICAL CONTEXTS CONTRIBUTES TO SUICIDE RISK DURING THE TRANSITION TO COLLEGE. WE WILL COLLECT NEAR-CONTINUOUS SMARTPHONE SCREENSHOTS (SCREENOMICS) AND GEOLOCATION DATA ALONGSIDE DAILY DIARIES OF SUBJECTIVE CONNECTEDNESS AND SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS ACROSS FOUR MONTHS DURING PARTICIPANTS’ FIRST COLLEGE SEMESTER. THESE DATA WILL PROVIDE AN INTEGRATED, TEMPORALLY RICH CHARACTERIZATION OF BOTH ONLINE AND OFFLINE CONNECTION, ALLOWING US TO EXAMINE CONVERGENCE AND DIVERGENCE BETWEEN OBJECTIVE AND SUBJECTIVE INDICATORS OF CONNECTEDNESS (AIM 1), EVALUATE HOW DIGITAL SOCIAL BEHAVIORS PROSPECTIVELY PREDICT DAILY AND LONGITUDINAL STB PATTERNS (AIM 2), AND TEST SEX DIFFERENCES IN THESE DYNAMIC PROCESSES (AIM 3). CONTEXTUALIZED GEOLOCATION WILL FURTHER CLARIFY THE PHYSICAL ENVIRONMENTS IN WHICH CONNECTION AND RISK UNFOLD (EXPLORATORY AIM). TOGETHER, THIS APPROACH WILL YIELD THE FIRST FINE-GRAINED, REAL-TIME MAPPING OF SOCIAL CONNECTION AS IT UNFOLDS IN DAILY LIFE, PROVIDING THE FOUNDATION FOR PERSONALIZED, SCALABLE SUICIDE-PREVENTION STRATEGIES.  THE RESEARCH TEAM, LED BY PI AMMERMAN AND SUPPORTED BY CO-IS JACOBUCCI, TUCKER, SINGH, WALSH, AND CURTIN IS FURTHER ENRICHED BY THE EXPERTISE OF CONSULTANT RAM. TOGETHER, THEY BRING WORLD-CLASS PROFICIENCY TO THIS PROJECT. THEY HAVE EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN CONDUCTING INTENSIVE LONGITUDINAL RESEARCH WITH HIGH-RISK POPULATIONS ON COLLEGE CAMPUSES, APPLYING MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES TO PREDICT SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS, AND COLLECTING, AS WELL AS MODELING, CONTINUOUS DATA STREAMS, INCLUDING SCREENSHOT DATA. THEIR COMBINED KNOWLEDGE ALSO EXTENDS TO UNDERSTANDING AND ADDRESSING THE ETHICAL AND PRIVACY CONCERNS UNIQUE TO TECHNOLOGICAL INNOVATIONS. TO BEST UNDERSTAND THE ROLE OF SOCIAL CONNECTION IN SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS AMONG YOUNG ADULTS, A MORE NUANCED AND INTENSIVE APPROACH IS REQUIRED. THESE FINDINGS WILL INFORM OUR THEORETICAL UNDERSTANDING OF THE SOCIAL CONNECTION – SUICIDALITY RELATIONSHIP AND LAY THE GROUNDWORK NECESSARY FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF INTERVENTION EFFORTS FOR SUICIDE RISK REDUCTION DURING THE TRANSITION TO COLLEGE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CIRCUIT MECHANISMS LINKING INFLAMMATORY CHALLENGES TO BEHAVIOR - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE RISK OF PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS IS ELEVATED IN INDIVIDUALS WITH INFLAMMATORY DISEASES, SUGGESTING A SHARED UNDER- LYING BIOLOGY. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS DRIVING THIS ASSOCIATION REMAIN UNCLEAR. WHILE RESEARCH HAS PRIMARILY FO- CUSED ON SUBCORTICAL AND BRAINSTEM REGIONS, THE CORTEX IS ALSO CONSISTENTLY ACTIVATED BY PERIPHERAL INFLAMMATION. IN PARTICULAR, THE INSULAR CORTEX (IC) RESPONDS TO INFLAMMATION AND IS DYSFUNCTIONAL IN PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS. PRE- LIMINARY DATA IN MICE SHOW THAT TYPE 2 AND TYPE 3 INFLAMMATION ACTIVATE VARIOUS SUBTYPES OF IC NEURONS. PERIPHERAL INFLAMMATION ALSO INDUCES BEHAVIORAL RESPONSES THAT ARE THE OUTPUT OF THE AMYGDALA AND PREFRONTAL CORTEX—DIRECT TARGETS OF IC NEURONS. DESPITE THE STRONG POTENTIAL ROLE OF THE IC IN LINKING IMMUNE CHALLENGES TO PSYCHIATRIC SYMP- TOMS, CRITICAL GAPS REMAIN IN UNDERSTANDING THE IDENTITY, PROPERTIES, AND FUNCTION OF IC IMMUNE-RESPONSIVE NEURONS. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY THE CIRCUIT MECHANISMS BY WHICH IC IMMUNE-RESPONSIVE NEURONS ALTER BE- HAVIOR DURING PERIPHERAL INFLAMMATION. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT HETEROGENEOUS AND MORE EXCITABLE IC NEU- RONS RESPOND TO MULTIPLE IMMUNE STIMULI AND DIRECTLY ACTIVATE BRAIN REGIONS INVOLVED IN EMOTIONAL REGULATION. TO TEST THIS, MOUSE MODELS OF TYPE 2 AND TYPE 3 INFLAMMATION WILL BE USED. IDENTIFYING THE IC NEURONS INVOLVED, DEFINING THEIR PROPERTIES, AND UNDERSTANDING HOW THEY ARE RECRUITED IS KEY FOR PREVENTING BEHAVIORAL RESPONSES TO INFLAM- MATION. USING SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOMICS, ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, AND CHEMOGENETICS, THE PROJECT WILL DETERMINE WHETHER IC IMMUNE-RESPONSIVE NEURONS ARE HETEROGENEOUS AND MORE EXCITABLE RATHER THAN A DEFINED SUBPOPU- LATION. THE STIMULUS SPECIFICITY OF IC IMMUNE-RESPONSIVE NEURONS WILL BE EXAMINED USING TWO COMPLEMENTARY APPROACHES: ACTIVITY-TAGGING TRAP2 MICE AND LONGITUDINAL IN VIVO CALCIUM IMAGING. ADDITIONALLY, THE STUDY WILL INVESTIGATE WHETHER THE ACTIVATION OF IC NEURONS BY INFLAMMATION DRIVES BEHAVIORAL RESPONSES THROUGH DIRECT ACTIVATION OF THE AMYGDALA AND PREFRONTAL CORTEX. VIRAL TRACING WILL BE USED TO CONFIRM PROJECTIONS FROM IC IMMUNE- RESPONSIVE NEURONS TO THESE REGIONS. CHEMOGENETICS WILL THEN BE APPLIED TO REACTIVATE OR SILENCE IC IMMUNE- RESPONSIVE NEURONS TO ASSESS THEIR CAUSAL IMPACT ON THE BEHAVIORAL RESPONSES INDUCED BY INFLAMMATION. WITH EXPERTISE IN MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, AND CIRCUIT NEUROSCIENCE, INFLAMMATION, AND IMAGING, THE TEAM IS UNIQUELY POSI- TIONED TO CARRY OUT THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY PROJECT. THE PROJECT’S INNOVATION LIES IN ITS PREMISE THAT PERIPHERAL INFLAM- MATION IS “RECORDED” WITHIN IMMUNE-RESPONSIVE IC NEURONS TO COORDINATE IMMUNOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL RE- SPONSES. METHODOLOGICALLY, THIS WORK IS INNOVATIVE IN USING PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT MODELS OF PERIPHERAL INFLAM- MATION AND CONDUCTING ANALYSES ACROSS MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, CIRCUIT, AND BEHAVIORAL LEVELS. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT ADDRESSES CRITICAL GAPS IN UNDERSTANDING HOW THE ACTIVATION OF IC NEURONS BY PERIPHERAL INFLAMMATION DRIVES BEHAVIORAL RESPONSES. DEFINING THE IDENTITY, PROPERTIES, AND FUNCTIONS OF IC IMMUNE-RESPON- SIVE NEURONS WILL PROVIDE A FOUNDATION FOR UNDERSTANDING THE CAUSAL NEUROBIOLOGICAL LINKS BETWEEN INFLAMMATION AND PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS AND COULD INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF PHARMACOLOGICAL OR IMMUNOMODULATORY THERAPIES.

description: SPATIALLY-ORGANIZED PREFRONTAL CIRCUITS REGULATING FEAR EXPRESSION AND DISCRIMINATION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT FEAR RESPONSES ARE ESSENTIAL FOR AVOIDING HARM BUT WHEN TRIGGERED EXCESSIVELY ARE MALADAPTIVE. WHILE INDIVIDUALS WITH ANXIETY AND TRAUMA-RELATED DISORDERS EXHIBITED RESPONSES TO LEARNED THREATS, THEY EXHIBIT OVERGENERALIZED RESPONSES TO NON-THREATS. THUS, UNDERSTANDING THE PATHOGENESIS OF THESE DISORDERS REQUIRES DIFFERENTIATING THE CIRCUITS THAT SUPPRESS FEAR TO NON-THREATS FROM THOSE THAT PROMOTE FEAR TO THREATS, YET BOTH OF THESE FUNCTIONS HAVE BEEN ASCRIBED TO THE DORSOMEDIAL PREFRONTAL CORTEX. HERE, WE PROVIDE NOVEL PRELIMINARY EVIDENCE THAT THE MOUSE PRELIMBIC CORTEX (PL) AND ITS OUTPUTS TO SUBCORTICAL REGIONS, INCLUDING THE BASOLATERAL AMYGDALA (BLA) AND PERIAQUEDUCTAL GRAY (PAG), ARE ORGANIZED ROSTROCAUDALLY, AND WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT ROSTRAL PL SUPPRESSES FEAR DURING NON-THREATS TO PROMOTE DISCRIMINATION WHILE CAUDAL PL PROMOTES FEAR. AIM 1 WILL SPATIALLY MAP PL NEURAL RESPONSES DURING FEAR DISCRIMINATION USING IN VIVO TWO-PHOTON CALCIUM IMAGING THROUGH A MICROPRISM. PRELIMINARY FINDINGS SUGGEST THAT ROSTRAL PL RESPONSES PREFERENTIALLY TO LEARNED NON-THREAT CUES, WHILE CAUDAL PL RESPONSES TO THREAT CUES. WE WILL LABEL PL-BLA AND PL-PAG PROJECTING NEURONS TO DETERMINE TO WHAT EXTENT THEY SHARE THIS ROSTROCAUDAL ORGANIZATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SUPERFICIAL NEURONS IN PL ENCODE CONDITIONED STIMULI, WHILE DEEPER NEURONS IN PL ENCODE FEAR RESPONSES. AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE THE FUNCTIONAL ROLES OF ROSTRAL AND CAUDAL PL IN REGULATING FEAR DISCRIMINATION. USING OPTOGENETICS DURING FEAR RECALL, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT ROSTRAL PL AND ITS PROJECTORS TO BLA AND PAG CONSTRAIN OVERGENERALIZED RESPONSES, WHILE CAUDAL PL AND ITS PROJECTORS ENHANCE FEAR RESPONSES. AIM 3 WILL MAP DIFFERENCES IN CONNECTIVITY AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC EXPRESSION ALONG THE ROSTROCAUDAL AXIS OF PL. WE WILL USE ANTEROGRADE AND RETROGRADE VIRUSES TO COMPARE THE CONNECTIVITY OF ROSTRAL AND CAUDAL PL. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUPPORTS ENRICHED BLA OUTPUTS ROSTRALLY, MOST PREDOMINANTLY IN FEMALE MICE, WHILE PAG OUTPUTS ARE PREFERENTIALLY FROM ROSTRAL PL TO VENTROLATERAL PAG AND CAUDAL PL TO DORSOLATERAL PAG, MOST PREDOMINANTLY IN MALE MICE. TO EVALUATE ROSTRAOCAUDAL PATTERNS OF TRANSCRIPTOMIC EXPRESSION, WE WILL APPLY MACHINE LEARNING MODELS TO SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMIC DATA. OUR PRELIMINARY ANALYSIS SUGGESTS THAT TRANSCRIPTOMIC EXPRESSION VARIES ALONG THE ROSTROCAUDAL AXIS OF PL, WITH SOME SEX SPECIFIC DIFFERENCES IN THESE PATTERNS. THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE KEY INSIGHTS FOR DIFFERENTIATING THE PREFRONTAL CIRCUITS THAT PROMOTE FEAR FROM THOSE THAT SUPPRESS FEAR TO SUPPORT FEAR DISCRIMINATION. THESE RESULTS WILL BE TRANSLATIONALLY RELEVANT GIVEN THAT DEFICITS IN FEAR DISCRIMINATION ARE OBSERVED ACROSS ANXIETY AND TRAUMA-RELATED DISORDERS, FEAR OVERGENERALIZATION IS PREDICTIVE OF RISK FOR DEVELOPING POSTTRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER, AND IMPROVING FEAR DISCRIMINATION REDUCES TRAUMA-RELATED SYMPTOMS. THUS, WE ANTICIPATE THAT OUR FINDINGS WILL BE IMPORTANT FOR IDENTIFYING TARGETS FOR THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SYNAPTIC MECHANISMS OF INTERMITTENT THETA BURST STIMULATION FOR MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER IS ASSOCIATED WITH DEFICITS IN NEUROPLASTICITY. RESCUE OF THIS PLASTICITY IS THE PUTATIVE MECHANISM OF ACTION OF AN FDA-CLEARED TREATMENT FOR DEPRESSION CALLED INTERMITTENT THETA BURST STIMULATION (ITBS), A PATTERNED FORM OF TRANSCRANIAL MAGNETIC STIMULATION (TMS). WE HAVE PREVIOUSLY FOUND THAT AGONISM OF THE N-METHYL-D-ASPARTATE RECEPTOR (NMDAR), WHICH ACTS AS A GATEKEEPER FOR SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY, IS SUFFICIENT TO ENHANCE THE FACILITATION PRODUCED BY TMS TO THE MOTOR CORTEX OF HEALTHY SUBJECTS. THIS SUGGESTING THAT LONG- TERM POTENTIATION (LTP) IS THE UNDERLYING CAUSE OF TMS-INDUCED FACILITATION. WE FURTHER FOUND A PARTIAL RESCUE OF MDD PLASTICITY DEFICITS IN THE MOTOR CORTEX, AND IN A CLINICAL TRIAL FOR DEPRESSION, HAVE OBSERVED AN UNPRECE- DENTED IMPROVEMENT IN CLINICAL SYMPTOMS WITH NMDAR AGONIST, D-CYCLOSERINE (DCS) COMBINED WITH ITBS. IT IS ESSENTIAL NOW THAT THIS PROMISING NEW TREATMENT APPROACH WHICH IS BASED ON THE PREMISE OF PROMOTING SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY BE DIRECTLY TESTED TO VALIDATE THE THEORETICAL UNDERPINNINGS ENABLING OPTIMIZATION AND GUIDANCE OF PO- TENT PLASTICITY INDUCERS FOR THE TREATMENT OF DEPRESSION AND OTHER DISORDERS. WE PROPOSE TO DETERMINE WHETHER ITBS, AS DELIVERED CLINICALLY, WORKS THROUGH ENHANCING SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY, AND TO VALIDATE OUR THEORY THAT DCS PHARMACOLOGIC AUGMENTATION OF ITBS INDEED WORKS THROUGH THIS MECHANISM OF ACTION. WE PROPOSE TO EXAMINE SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY INDUCED BY ITBS USING CONCURRENT PHARMACOLOGY TO BLOCK (AIM 1) AND ACTIVATE (AIM 2) THE NMDAR DURING ITBS IN 40 DEPRESSED PATIENTS COMPARED TO 40 HEALTHY CONTROLS. FOR THE FIRST TIME, THIS PHARMACOLOGIC AUGMENTATION STRATEGY WILL BE USED TO ASSESS LTP-ASSOCIATED CHANGES IN THE DORSOLATERAL PREFRONTAL CORTEX (DLPFC), WHERE CLINICAL ITBS TREATMENTS ARE DELIVERED, USING ELECTROENCEPHALOG- RAPHY (EEG)-BASED TMS-EVOKED POTENTIALS (TEPS). IN A DOUBLE-BLIND, RANDOMIZED, CROSSOVER DESIGN, EACH SUBJECT WILL RECEIVE A SINGLE SESSION OF 1) ITBS + NMDAR ANTAGONIST, DEXTROMETHORPHAN, 2) ITBS + NMDAR AGONIST, DCS, 3) ITBS + PLACEBO, 4) SHAM ITBS + PLACEBO. IN AN EXPLORATORY AND INDEPENDENT AIM 3, WE WILL TEST EACH DRUG, INCLUDING PLACEBO, OVER 30 DAILY (ACTIVE) ITBS SESSIONS IN A PARALLEL DESIGN WITH ONLY MDD SUB- JECTS. TOGETHER, THESE AIMS WILL TEST THE LTP-LIKE MECHANISMS OF A SESSION OF ITBS AS WELL AS A COURSE OF ITBS, WHICH CAN, AND LIKELY DOES, INVOLVE HOMEOSTATIC CHANGES WHEREBY NEURONS GLOBALLY SCALE RECEPTOR LEVELS TO MAINTAIN THE ABILITY TO RECEIVE ADDITIONAL INPUTS. WE WILL THEN UNDERSTAND HOW PLASTICITY CHANGES OVER THE COURSE OF ITBS, AS WELL AS PHARMACOLOGICALLY AUGMENTED ITBS. WITHIN EACH SESSION, TEP ASSESSMENTS WILL BE GIVEN AT BASELINE, AFTER DRUG, AND THEN AFTER ITBS + DRUG. THIS DESIGN WILL CONTROL FOR THE EFFECTS OF ITBS AND DRUG, AND WILL DEMONSTRATE THE NECESSITY AND SUFFICIENCY OF NMDAR ACTIVITY FOR ITBS-INDUCED PLASTICITY, BOTH ESSENTIAL EVIDENCES FOR LTP, AND WILL DIRECTLY TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT OUR PROMISING CLINICAL TRIAL RESULTS WERE DUE TO EN- HANCED PLASTICITY, VALIDATING AND PAVING THE WAY TO TRANSFORMATIVE TREATMENT APPROACHES IN THE BRAIN THAT MAY TRIPLE CURRENT EFFICACY RATES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HARNESSING ROUTINE CLINICAL SUICIDE RISK ASSESSMENT FOR MACHINE LEARNING-GUIDEDPREDICTION AND PRECISION TREATMENT IN OUTPATIENT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CARE - ABSTRACT SUICIDE IS CURRENTLY THE 11TH LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH, AND OVER THE PAST 25 YEARS, THE SUICIDE RATE HAS INCREASED BY NEARLY ONE-THIRD. HEALTHCARE SETTINGS OFFER A KEY OPPORTUNITY TO IDENTIFY INDIVIDUALS AT HIGHEST RISK, AS OVER 75% OF THOSE WHO DIE BY SUICIDE SAW A CLINICIAN IN THE YEAR BEFORE THEIR DEATH. IN OUTPATIENT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, IT REMAINS CHALLENGING FOR CLINICIANS TO IDENTIFY THE SMALL SUBSET OF PATIENTS AT HIGHEST RISK FOR SUICIDE AND WHO MAY REQUIRE ADDITIONAL SUICIDE PREVENTION INTERVENTIONS, WHICH ARE OFTEN COSTLY OR DIFFICULT TO ACCESS. RECENT MACHINE LEARNING MODELS THAT LEVERAGE ROUTINELY COLLECTED ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR) DATA (E.G., DIAGNOSTIC CODES, LABORATORY RESULTS, MEDICATIONS, ETC.) TO PROSPECTIVELY PREDICT PATIENTS’ RISK OF SUICIDAL BEHAVIOR ARE HIGHLY PROMISING, GENERALLY OUTPERFORMING TRADITIONAL METHODS. HOWEVER, EVEN THOUGH CLINICAL SUICIDE RISK ASSESSMENT (SRA) IS CONSIDERED STANDARD OF CARE IN MOST OUTPATIENT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SETTINGS AND ROUTINELY DOCUMENTED IN THE EHR, THE FIELD HAS NOT YET SYSTEMATICALLY INTEGRATED CLINICIAN-CONDUCTED SRAS INTO STATISTICAL MODELS FOR SUICIDE RISK PREDICTION. OUR TEAM RECENTLY USED MACHINE LEARNING TO ANALYZE THE DATA (ON CLINICIANS’ OVERALL JUDGMENTS OF RISK AND PATIENTS’ RECENT SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS AND DOCUMENTED RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS) FROM > 600,000 SRAS COMPLETED AT THE POINT OF CARE IN OUTPATIENT SETTINGS, AND ACHIEVED HIGH ACCURACY (AUC=0.88 [0.86-0.91]) WHEN PREDICTING SUICIDE ATTEMPT WITHIN 6 MONTHS. THE NEXT FRONTIER IS TO INTEGRATE CLINICIAN SRA FEATURES INTO VALIDATED EHR-BASED STATISTICAL MODELS, WHICH WE EXPECT TO MARKEDLY ENHANCE PREDICTION AND PRECISION INTERVENTION. IN THIS STUDY, OUR OVERALL AIM IS TO STRENGTHEN THE ACCURACY AND CLINICAL UTILITY OF SUICIDE RISK IDENTIFICATION IN OUTPATIENT BEHAVIORAL HEALTHCARE THROUGH BOTH STATE-OF-THE-ART STATISTICAL MODELS THAT INTEGRATE CLINICIAN SRA WITH TRADITIONAL EHR DATA AND LEADING IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE FRAMEWORKS TO MAXIMIZE POTENTIAL FOR SUCCESSFUL CLINICIAN IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINABILITY. AIM 1 WILL INVOLVE DEVELOPING AND EVALUATING MACHINE LEARNING MODELS THAT COMBINE CLINICIAN SRA FEATURES WITH VALIDATED EHR-BASED MODELS IN OUTPATIENT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TO PREDICT FUTURE SUICIDE ATTEMPT AND DEATH. WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER COMBINING CLINICIAN SRA WITH PREVIOUSLY VALIDATED EHR-BASED MODELS IMPROVES CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING COMPARED TO MODELS WITHOUT CLINICIAN SRA. AIM 2 FOCUSES ON DEVELOPING AND EVALUATING A NOVEL PRECISION TREATMENT RULE (PTR) THAT INCORPORATES CLINICIAN SRA DATA TO GUIDE TARGETED INTERVENTION DECISIONS FOR OUTPATIENTS IDENTIFIED AS AT ELEVATED SUICIDE RISK. WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER THE PTR DEMONSTRATES SIGNIFICANT TREATMENT EFFECT HETEROGENEITY, PROVIDING CLINICIANS WITH ACTIONABLE GUIDANCE ON KEY CARE DECISIONS FOR HIGH-RISK OUTPATIENTS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL CONDUCT IN-DEPTH QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS TO IDENTIFY IMPLEMENTATION DETERMINANTS (I.E., BARRIERS AND FACILITATORS) OF INTEGRATING CLINICIAN SRA AND EHR-BASED SUICIDE RISK MODELS AND THE PTR INTO OUTPATIENT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINICIANS’ WORKFLOWS. OVERALL, THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH THE UTILITY AND FEASIBILITY OF COMBINING CLINICIAN ASSESSMENT AND EHR-BASED SUICIDE RISK PREDICTION MODELS, CONTRIBUTING TO SCALABLE AND CLINICALLY IMPACTFUL STRATEGIES FOR SUICIDE PREVENTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SOCIAL PERCEPTION AND COGNITION IN A MARMOSET MODEL OF PHELAN MCDERMID SYNDROME - PROJECT SUMMARY AND ABSTRACT PHELAN-MCDERMID SYNDROME (PMS) IN HUMANS IS CAUSED BY MUTATIONS IN THE SHANK3 GENE, LEADING TO SEVERE INTELLECTUAL IMPAIRMENT AND SOCIAL AND EMOTIONAL DIFFICULTIES THAT ARE OFTEN FOUND IN AUTISM. TO IDENTIFY POSSIBLE NEURAL IMPAIRMENTS IN SOCIAL PERCEPTION AND COGNITION IN A MARMOSET MODEL OF PMS, AND HOW THEY MIGHT BE CORRECTED WITH GENE THERAPY, WE PROPOSE TO STUDY MARMOSETS WITH IMPLANTED ELECTROCORTICOGRAPHY ARRAYS OVER THE VISUAL CORTEX, INFERIOR TEMPORAL CORTEX, AUDITORY CORTEX, AND PREFRONTAL CORTEX, WITH NEURAL RECORDINGS TAKEN BEFORE AND AFTER GENE THERAPY. OUR HYPOTHESES ARE GUIDED BY EXTENSIVE PRELIMINARY DATA. IN AIM 1, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THE CORTICAL SYSTEMS FOR SOCIAL INFORMATION PROCESSING ARE IMPAIRED IN MARMOSETS WITH SHANK3 MUTATIONS COMPARED TO WILD-TYPE ANIMALS, PRIOR TO GENE THERAPY. RECORDINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED BOTH UNDER HIGHLY CONTROLLED EXPERIMENTAL CONDITIONS WHILE ANIMALS VIEW STATIC IMAGES AND VIDEO CLIPS, AND IN THE HOME CAGE WITH THE CAGE-MATE, WITH MORE NATURALISTIC BEHAVIOR THAT IS ANALYZED WITH AUTOMATED VIDEO METHODS. PRELIMINARY RESULTS SUGGEST THAT WHILE LOW-LEVEL VISUAL INFORMATION IS PROCESSED NORMALLY IN SHANK3 MUTANTS, SOCIAL INFORMATION REPRESENTED IN RELEVANT NEURAL CIRCUITS IS DEGRADED, ESPECIALLY IN THE PREFRONTAL CORTEX. THIS IMPAIRMENT IN NEURAL PROCESSING IS FOUND EVEN WHEN THEIR GAZE AND OTHER BEHAVIOR ARE RELATIVELY NORMAL. IN THE RECORDINGS OF AIM 2, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THESE SAME CIRCUITS ARE IMPAIRED WHEN THE ANIMALS ARE TESTED IN DIFFICULT COGNITIVE TASKS. PRELIMINARY RESULTS FROM REVERSAL LEARNING AND WORKING MEMORY SUGGEST THAT WHILE REVERSAL LEARNING IS NORMAL, WORKING MEMORY PERFORMANCE IS IMPAIRED IN SHANK3 MUTANT ANIMALS, AND THIS IMPAIRMENT SEEMS TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH ABNORMAL ACTIVITY IN PREFRONTAL CORTEX. THUS, PREFRONTAL CORTEX IS EMERGING IN THE PRELIMINARY DATA AS A KEY REGION WHERE NEURAL CIRCUITS MAY BE AFFECTED IN BOTH SOCIAL PERCEPTION AND GENERAL COGNITION IN PMS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL REPEAT ALL OF THESE MEASUREMENTS AFTER THE ANIMALS HAVE RECEIVED A TYPE OF GENE THERAPY, CONSISTING OF GENE REPLACEMENT WITH A SHANK3 MINI-GENE. THE BEFORE-AND-AFTER MEASUREMENTS IN THE SAME ANIMALS WILL HELP NARROW DOWN THE CIRCUIT ABNORMALITIES IN PMS AND HELP IDENTIFY WHICH ABNORMALITIES MIGHT BE AMELIORATED BY GENE THERAPY. BECAUSE PMS SHARES MANY FEATURES WITH SEVERE FORMS OF AUTISM, THE RESULTS MAY HAVE GENERAL IMPLICATIONS FOR UNDERSTANDING SOME OF THE CIRCUIT ABNORMALITIES UNDERLYING THE SOCIAL AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS FOUND IN MORE COMMON FORMS OF AUTISM.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CIRCUIT OPERATION UNDERLYING FEAR MEMORY PROCESSES IN THE AMYGDALA - PROJECT SUMMARY OUR SURVIVAL RELIES ON THE EXECUTION OF APPROPRIATE DEFENSIVE BEHAVIORS IN RESPONSE TO THREATS AND THE FORMATION OF FEAR MEMORIES ASSOCIATED WITH SUCH EVENTS. THE AMYGDALA IS A CENTRAL BRAIN REGION REGULATING BOTH PROCESSES. ACCORDING TO THE PREVAILING MODEL, THE LATERAL AMYGDALA (LA) SERVES AS THE PRIMARY INPUT SITE WHERE SENSORY INFORMATION ENTERS THE AMYGDALA DURING FEAR LEARNING, AND IT IS CONSIDERED THE PRINCIPAL SITE OF SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY UNDERLYING THIS LEARNING. HOWEVER, RECENT FINDINGS - INCLUDING OUR OWN PRELIMINARY DATA - CHALLENGE THIS VIEW. IN LABORATORY SETTINGS, PAVLOVIAN FEAR CONDITIONING IS A WIDELY USED PARADIGM FOR INVESTIGATING THE NEURAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING FEAR LEARNING. BASED ON THE CURRENT MODEL, THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN A CONDITIONED STIMULUS (CS), SUCH AS A TONE, AND AN UNCONDITIONED STIMULUS (US), SUCH AS A FOOT-SHOCK, IS FORMED WITHIN LA CIRCUITS. HOWEVER, THE NEURAL RESPONSES TO US PRESENTATIONS WITHIN THE AMYGDALA HAVE RARELY BEEN EXAMINED IN DETAIL AT HIGH TEMPORAL RESOLUTION, DESPITE BEING CRITICAL FOR UNDERSTANDING THE MECHANISMS THAT SUPPORT FEAR LEARNING. BY OPTIMIZING IN VIVO RECORDING CONDITIONS, WE FOUND THAT LA NEURONS THAT WERE INITIALLY RESPONSIVE TO THE CS EXHIBITED HABITUATION ACROSS REPEATED CS PRESENTATIONS SHOWED RENEWED CS-EVOKED SPIKING WHEN THE US WAS INTRODUCED. IN CONTRAST, THEIR US-DRIVEN RESPONSES CONCURRENTLY DECREASED. THIS INVERSE RELATIONSHIP, WHERE CS-EVOKED RESPONSES ARE RE-GAINED WHILE US-TRIGGERED ACTIVITY IS SUPPRESSED, REFLECTS THE CELLULAR MECHANISM BY WHICH A NEUTRAL STIMULUS ACQUIRES SIGNIFICANCE. FURTHER, AMYGDALA NEURONS IN DISTINCT NUCLEI RESPONDED TO THE US WITH COMPARABLY SHORT LATENCIES, IMPLYING THAT THESE NUCLEI RECEIVE US-RELATED INPUT IN PARALLEL, RATHER THAN SEQUENTIALLY. FINALLY, USING PROJECTION-SPECIFIC SILENCING OF NEURAL FUNCTION IN AN AMYGDALA SUBNUCLEUS WHERE THE AXON COLLATERALS OF LA NEURONS ARE RARE, WE OBSERVED AN IMPAIRMENT IN CONTEXTUAL FEAR MEMORY. BY DETERMINING THE SPIKE DYNAMICS IN AMYGDALA NEURONS DURING CS AND US PRESENTATIONS IN AWAKE MICE USING MULTICHANNEL ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL RECORDINGS COMBINED WITH OPTOGENETICS, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE CELLULAR AND CIRCUIT-LEVEL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING FEAR LEARNING. IN ADDITION, WE WILL DISSECT THE FUNCTIONAL ROLES OF DISTINCT AMYGDALA SUBNUCLEI AND PROJECTION-DEFINED NEURONAL POPULATIONS USING CELL TYPE-SPECIFIC CIRCUIT MANIPULATIONS. THIS PROJECT HAS THE POTENTIAL TO OVERTURN THE PREVAILING MODEL OF AMYGDALA FUNCTION. WE PROPOSE THAT AMYGDALA NUCLEI PROCESS US INFORMATION IN PARALLEL. FURTHERMORE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT A SUBPOPULATION OF AMYGDALA NEURONS PLAYS A DIRECT AND ESSENTIAL ROLE IN THE FORMATION OF CONTEXTUAL FEAR MEMORIES. THESE NOVEL INSIGHTS WILL SUBSTANTIALLY REFINE AND BROADEN THE CURRENT OPERATIONAL FRAMEWORK OF AMYGDALA CIRCUITRY IN FEAR LEARNING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NOVEL APPROACHES TO SUPPORTING STUDENTS WITH ADHD IN MULTI-TIERED SYSTEMS OF SUPPORT (MTSS) - ABSTRACT  CHILDREN WITH ADHD ARE LIKELY TO EXHIBIT BEHAVIORAL DIFFICULTIES IN THE CLASSROOM THAT INHIBIT LEARNING (DALEY & BIRCHWOOD, 2010; DUPAUL & STONER, 2003; FABIANO ET AL., 2006; FRIEDMAN & PFIFFNER, 2020; LOE & FELDMAN, 2007; RAGGI & CHRONIS, 2006; RAPPORT, CHUNG, SHORE, & ISAACS, 2001). THESE ISSUES MAKE ADDRESSING ADHD AN AREA IN NEED OF CONTINUOUS AND CONTEMPORARY SUPPORT, PARTICULARLY DURING EARLY ELEMENTARY SCHOOL (BITSKO ET AL., 2022), IN ORDER TO PREVENT THE WORSENING, LIFE-LONG ISSUES THAT INDIVIDUALS WITH ADHD MAY CONFRONT THROUGHOUT THE LIFESPAN. THE PRESENT APPLICATION FOCUSES ON SUPPORTS AND INTERVENTIONS FOR STUDENTS IN ELEMENTARY SCHOOL, AS THAT IS WHERE INITIAL IDENTIFICATION AND INTERVENTION TYPICALLY OCCURS (VISSER ET AL., 2014). WITH THE ADVENT OF MULTI-TIERED SYSTEMS OF SUPPORT (MTSS) WITHIN SCHOOL SETTINGS, A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TO THE DELIVERY OF UNIVERSAL, TARGETED, AND INDICATED SCHOOL MENTAL HEALTH AND EDUCATIONAL SUPPORTS MAY BE ENHANCED. THE MOST INTENSIVE TIER OF THE MTSS (I.E., TIER 3) IS CURRENTLY THE MOST UNDER-DEVELOPED. THE CREATION OF A POSITIVE BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT CLASSROOM THROUGH TIER 3 OF THE MTSS WILL ASSIST TEACHERS IN IMPROVING THE POSITIVE BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PROVIDED TO THE STUDENT WITH ADHD. THUS, THE PRESENT INVESTIGATION WILL BE SITUATED WITHIN EVERYDAY SCHOOL PROCEDURES FOR SUPPORTING A STUDENT WITH BEHAVIORS CONSISTENT WITH ADHD. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE 288 ELEMENTARY SCHOOL CHILDREN RECRUITED FROM PARTICIPATING SCHOOL DISTRICTS WITHIN THE EXISTING SCHOOL-BASED PROBLEM SOLVING TEAMS. WE WILL WORK WITH GRADES FIRST TO FOURTH. REFERRED CHILDREN WILL THEN ALL RECEIVE A LEAD-IN, TIER 2 INTERVENTION TO INCLUDE A DAILY REPORT CARD (DRC) INTERVENTION. THOSE WHO CONTINUE TO NEED ADDITIONAL BEHAVIOR SUPPORTS IN THE SPRING -- TIER 3 INTERVENTION -- WILL BE ALLOCATED THROUGH RANDOM ASSIGNMENT TO SCHOOL AS USUAL OR ACADEMIC/BEHAVIOR COMPETENCY (ACE) CLASSROOM IN A HYBRID TYPE 1 DESIGN. THE ACE CLASSROOM IS AN APPROACH BASED ON DECADES OF RESEARCH IN SUMMER TREATMENT PROGRAM CLASSROOMS (FABIANO ET AL., 2007; PELHAM ET AL., 2025). AIM 1 EVALUATES THE OUTCOMES OF THE APPROACH RELATIVE TO SCHOOL AS USUAL. AIM 2 EVALUATES THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE APPROACH AND EXPLORES COMPONENTS OF USER IMPLEMENTATION THAT PROMOTE FIDELITY. AIM 3 EXPLORES MODERATORS OF THE INTERVENTION OUTCOMES (E.G., COMORBID OPPOSITIONAL/AGGRESSIVE BEHAVIOR OR LEARNING DISABILITIES).

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MENTAL HEALTH EMERGENCY RESPONSE: UTILIZATION, OUTCOMES AND IMPLEMENTATION OF MOBILE CRISIS SERVICES IN MEDICAID - PROJECT ABSTRACT ADULTS AND ADOLESCENTS IN MENTAL-HEALTH CRISIS OFTEN FACE A DISJOINTED RESPONSE: MOST 911 CALLS END AT AN EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT OR WITH POLICE, SETTINGS THAT LACK THE TIME, STAFF, AND FOLLOW-UP LINKS NEEDED FOR SAFE STABILIZATION. MOBILE CRISIS SERVICES (MCS) ARE TEAMS OF CLINICIANS AND PEERS WHO TRAVEL TO THE PERSON, DE- ESCALATE, AND CONNECT TO OUTPATIENT CARE. MCS PROGRAMS HAVE GROWN RAPIDLY; MORE THAN 1,800 PROGRAMS NOW COVER 40 PERCENT OF U.S. COUNTIES AND MEDICAID SPENDING ON THE MODEL HAS DOUBLED IN TWO YEARS. YET NO NATIONAL WORK SHOWS WHO ACTUALLY RECEIVES MCS RATHER THAN ED BASED CARE, WHETHER MCS REDUCES ADMISSIONS OR REPEAT CRISES, OR WHICH STATE ACTIONS HELP PROGRAMS EXPAND AND LAST. THIS PROJECT WILL FILL THOSE GAPS BY MERGING 2021-2025 MEDICAID CLAIMS WITH LOCAL WORKFORCE, SOCIOECONOMIC, AND POLICY FILES FOR NINE STATES AND THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA AND PAIRING THOSE DATA WITH 45 STAKEHOLDER INTERVIEWS. WE WILL PURSUE THREE AIMS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL MEASURE HOW INDIVIDUAL FACTORS (AGE, SEX), COMMUNITY CONTEXT (RURALITY, PROVIDER SUPPLY), AND THE CLARITY OF STATE MEDICAID GUIDANCE PREDICT RECEIPT OF MCS VERSUS AN EMERGENCY-DEPARTMENT VISIT DURING A BEHAVIORAL-HEALTH CRISIS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ESTIMATE THE EFFECT OF RECEIVING MCS CARE ON (A) PSYCHIATRIC HOSPITALIZATION DURING THE INDEX EPISODE, (B) OUTPATIENT MENTAL-HEALTH FOLLOW-UP WITHIN 7 AND 30 DAYS, AND (C) ANY REPEAT CRISIS WITHIN 90 DAYS. A STAGGERED, POLICY-BASED FUZZY DIFFERENCE-IN-DIFFERENCES DESIGN WILL USE FOUR EXTERNAL POLICY SHOCKS (ARPA MOBILE-CRISIS FUNDS, SAMHSA PLANNING GRANTS, NEW STATE APPROPRIATIONS, AND 988 DISPATCH STATUTES) TO ISOLATE VARIATION IN MCS AVAILABILITY. IN AIM 3, WE WILL IDENTIFY WORKFORCE, FINANCE, AND COORDINATION FACTORS THAT EXPLAIN THE QUANTITATIVE FINDINGS AND SHAPE PROGRAM SCALE-UP THROUGH SEMI-STRUCTURED INTERVIEWS WITH NATIONAL EXPERTS, STATE OFFICIALS, AND FRONTLINE PROVIDERS. BY SHOWING WHERE MCS TEAMS WORK, HOW LARGE THEIR EFFECTS ARE, AND WHICH POLICY LEVERS MATTER, THE STUDY WILL PROVIDE ACTIONABLE EVIDENCE FOR CLINICIANS, PATIENTS, AND POLICYMAKERS TO SET FAIR PAYMENT, BUILD STAFFING PLANS, AND CHOOSE WHEN A MOBILE RESPONSE IS THE RIGHT OPTION, DIRECTLY ADVANCING NIMH STRATEGIC PLAN OBJECTIVE 4.2 AND THE FEDERAL GOAL OF STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY CRISIS CARE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DECIPHERING THE ROLE OF DELAY PERIOD ACTIVITY IN HUMAN WORKING MEMORY - PROJECT SUMMARY WORKING MEMORY IS ESSENTIAL FOR HUMAN COGNITION, ALLOWING US TO THINK, PLAN, IMAGINE, AND FLEXIBLY ADJUST TO TASK DEMANDS. DESPITE THE IMPORTANCE OF WORKING MEMORY FOR HUMAN COGNITION, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS AND THEIR DISRUPTION BY DISEASE OR INJURY. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH IS A CIRCUIT-LEVEL UNDERSTANDING OF WORKING MEMORY TO ENABLE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW TREATMENTS FOR THE DEVASTATING EFFECTS OF PSYCHIATRIC AND NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS IN WHICH WORKING MEMORY IS IMPAIRED. OUR EXPERIMENTS UTILIZE THE RARE OPPORTUNITY TO RECORD IN-VIVO FROM HUMAN SINGLE NEURONS SIMULTANEOUSLY IN MULTIPLE BRAIN AREAS IN PATIENTS UNDERGOING TREATMENT FOR DRUG-RESISTANT EPILEPSY. WE INVESTIGATE THE CONTRIBUTION OF DELAY-PERIOD ACTIVITY, WHICH IS THOUGHT TO BE ONE OF THE PRINCIPAL MECHANISMS FOR MAINTAINING WORKING MEMORY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CELLS WITH DELAY-PERIOD ACTIVITY IN DIFFERENT BRAIN AREAS SPECIFICALLY SUPPORT THE MAINTENANCE OF VISUAL, SEMANTIC, AND CONTROL SIGNALS, RESPECTIVELY. USING A NOVEL COMPUTATIONAL FRAMEWORK AND SIMULTANEOUS RECORDINGS, WE EXAMINE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN MEMORANDA AND NEURAL ACTIVITY AND THE ROLE OF INTER-AREAL INTERACTIONS IN CONTROL, TEST CAUSALITY, AND EXAMINE HUMAN-SPECIFIC ASPECTS OF WORKING MEMORY INCLUDING LANGUAGE-BASED REPRESENTATIONS. WE WILL INVESTIGATE THREE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESES. FIRST, WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE NEURAL CODE OF DELAY-PERIOD ACTIVITY DURING WORKING MEMORY MAINTENANCE (AIM 1). SECOND, WE WILL IDENTIFY HOW INTERFERENCE BETWEEN WORKING MEMORY AND PERCEPTUAL DISTRACTORS IS AVOIDED (AIM 2). THIRD, WE WILL EXAMINE THE CAUSAL ROLE OF DELAY-PERIOD ACTIVITY WITH ELECTRICAL STIMULATION (AIM 3). THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF THIS WORK INCLUDE (I) A NOVEL COMPUTATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR DETERMINING WHAT ASPECTS OF MEMORANDA HELD IN WORKING MEMORY ARE ENCODED BY A GIVEN NEURON, (II) DETERMINING WHICH CELLS AND BRAIN AREAS SUPPORT VISUAL, SEMANTIC, AND CONTROL ASPECTS THROUGH DELAY-PERIOD ACTIVITY, (III) CIRCUIT-LEVEL KNOWLEDGE OF HOW FRONTAL CORTEX EXERTS TOP-DOWN CONTROL TO AVOID INTERFERENCE, AND (IV) A CAUSAL UNDERSTANDING OF HOW DELAY-PERIOD ACTIVITY CONTRIBUTES TO WORKING MEMORY IN DIFFERENT AREAS. THE PROPOSED WORK IS UNUSUALLY INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT COMBINES SINGLE-NEURON RECORDINGS IN BEHAVING HUMANS WITH NEW TOOLS TO EXAMINE DELAY-PERIOD ACTIVITY QUANTITATIVELY WITH AN AXIS TUNING FRAMEWORK IN FEATURE SPACES DEFINED BY DEEP NEURAL VISION AND LANGUAGE NETWORKS, TEST A MAJOR THEORY OF HOW THE HUMAN BRAIN SUPPORTS WORKING MEMORY, AND USE NEW METHODS TO EXAMINE THE CAUSAL ROLE OF DELAY-PERIOD ACTIVITY. THIS INTEGRATED MULTI- DISCIPLINARY COMBINATION OF PHYSIOLOGY, BEHAVIOR, AND MODELING WILL CONTRIBUTE SIGNIFICANTLY TO OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE CIRCUITS AND PATTERNS OF NEURAL ACTIVITY THAT GIVE RISE TO WORKING MEMORY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BIDIRECTIONAL INFLUENCES BETWEEN SOCIAL MEDIA USE AND ADOLESCENT DEPRESSION: TESTING THE ROLE OF FRONTOPARIETAL CONNECTIVITY - ABSTRACT SOCIAL MEDIA IS NOW A MAJOR SOURCE OF ENVIRONMENTAL INPUT FOR ADOLESCENTS. OVER 90% OF U.S. ADOLESCENTS ARE REGULARLY USING SOCIAL MEDIA, WITH 45% REPORTING THAT THEY ARE ONLINE “NEARLY CONSTANTLY”. WHILE 80% OF ADOLESCENTS REPORT THAT SOCIAL MEDIA USE (SMU) MAKES THEM FEEL “MORE CONNECTED” WITH THEIR PEERS, THERE ARE NONETHELESS GROWING CONCERNS THAT PATHOLOGICALLY HEAVY USE IS IMPACTING ATTENTIONAL FOCUS, EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONING, AND SOCIAL COGNITION, AND DRIVING INCREASES IN DEPRESSION AMONG YOUTH, PARTICULARLY AMONG GIRLS. MANY OF THE BRAIN REGIONS CONSTITUTING FRONTOPARIETAL NETWORKS (FPNS) THAT SUPPORT ATTENTIONAL FOCUS, EXECUTIVE FUNCTION, AND SOCIAL COGNITION HAVE ALSO BEEN IMPLICATED IN DEPRESSION. HOWEVER, THERE IS LIMITED DATA LINKING SMU WITH ALTERATIONS IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF FPNS IN THE CONTEXT OF PSYCHOPATHOLOGY RISK. WE HAVE PREVIOUSLY DEMONSTRATED THAT GREATER USE OF NEGATIVE EMOTIONAL WORDS ON SOCIAL MEDIA APPS IS ASSOCIATED WITH GREATER WITHIN-NETWORK FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY OF BOTH MEDIAL AND DORSAL FPNS; A DIAGNOSIS OF DEPRESSION HAS ALSO BEEN ASSOCIATED WITH GREATER FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY OF THE MEDIAL FPN BUT LOWER FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY OF THE DORSAL FPN WITH MIDCINGULO-INSULAR NETWORKS. HOWEVER, NO STUDIES TO DATE HAVE EXAMINED WHETHER PATHOLOGICAL SMU POTENTIATES DEPRESSION RISK (OR VICE-VERSA), AND THE EXTENT TO WHICH FPN DEVELOPMENT IS IMPACTED BY SMU. TOWARD THIS END, WE PROPOSE TO LEVERAGE FIVE WAVES OF LONGITUDINAL DATA FROM THE ADOLESCENT BRAIN COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT (ABCD) STUDY (N>10,000, AGES 13–18) TO TEST ASSOCIATIONS AMONG PROBLEMATIC (V. NORMATIVE) SMU, RISK FOR ADOLESCENT DEPRESSION, AND FPN DEVELOPMENT. UNLIKE PREVIOUS STUDIES IN THIS AREA WHICH FOCUS ON SELF-REPORTED SMU, WE WILL LEVERAGE SMARTPHONE-BASED PASSIVE SENSING TECHNOLOGY TO ASCERTAIN OBJECTIVE MEASURES OF TOTAL EXPOSURE (I.E., AMOUNT OF TIME SPENT) AND NATURE OF ENGAGEMENT (E.G., APPLYING SENTIMENT ANALYSES TO DETERMINE FREQUENCY OF NEGATIVE EMOTIONAL CONTENT) WITH SOCIAL MEDIA APPS. THESE METRICS OF SOCIAL MEDIA EXPOSURE AND ENGAGEMENT WILL BE COMBINED WITH CLINICAL AND SELF-REPORTED ASSESSMENTS OF DEPRESSION AND MULTIMODAL (RESTING-STATE FMRI, DIFFUSION MRI) MEASURES OF DORSAL, LATERAL, AND MEDIAL FPN CONNECTIVITY TO TEST THREE INDEPENDENT AIMS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL TEST WHETHER AND HOW SMU SHAPES ADOLESCENT DEVELOPMENT OF FPN CONNECTIVITY (AIM 1), WHETHER TRAJECTORIES OF FPN CONNECTIVITY MEDIATE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN SMU AND DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS AND VICE-VERSA (AIM 2), AND ADOPT A DATA-DRIVEN MACHINE LEARNING STRATEGY TO TEST WHETHER SMU AND FPN CONNECTIVITY OUTPERFORM OTHER FACTORS IN PREDICTING ADOLESCENT-ONSET DEPRESSION (AIM 3). THE RESULTS OF THIS INNOVATIVE AND SCIENTIFICALLY RIGOROUS STUDY WILL ANSWER CRITICAL QUESTIONS ON WHAT CONSTITUTES POTENTIALLY PATHOLOGICAL SMU, WHO MAY BE DISPROPORTIONATELY IMPACTED BY SMU IN THE CONTEXT OF DEPRESSION RISK, AND IDENTIFY MODIFIABLE NEURODEVELOPMENTAL MECHANISMS BY WHICH SMU MAY LEAD TO DEPRESSION. ALL RESEARCH FINDINGS WILL BE DISSEMINATED RESPONSIBLY TO INFORM GUIDANCE FOR YOUTH AND THEIR FAMILIES, CLINICIANS, EDUCATORS, TECHNOLOGY-BASED STAKEHOLDERS, AND POLICYMAKERS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE IMPACT OF EVICTION ON PREVENTIVE AND PRIMARY CARE: A LARGE-SCALE ADMINISTRATIVE LINKAGE STUDY - IMPROVING PREVENTIVE CARE IS CRUCIAL FOR PUBLIC HEALTH: TODAY, ONLY 8% OF ADULTS RECEIVE ALL RECOMMENDED, HIGH-PRIORITY PREVENTIVE SERVICES. DISRUPTED PRIMARY CARE CONTINUITY COMPOUNDS THIS CHALLENGE, LOWERING CARE QUALITY AND INHIBITING PREVENTIVE CARE UPTAKE. THE CONSEQUENCES ARE DIRE: POOR PRIMARY AND PREVENTIVE CARE COST TENS OF THOUSANDS OF LIVES AND >$700 BILLION EACH YEAR WHILE BURDENING ACUTE CARE SYSTEMS WITH AVOIDABLE UTILIZATION. STILL, KEY GAPS REMAIN IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW PRIMARY OR PREVENTIVE CARE MIGHT BE IMPROVED. ONE POORLY UNDERSTOOD CHALLENGE IS HOUSING INSECURITY. US HOUSING PRICES HAVE RISEN FASTER THAN WAGES FOR DECADES, CAUSING A NATIONWIDE CRISIS. MORE THAN HALF OF RENTERS ARE NOW “RENT-BURDENED,” AND 4 MILLION AMERICANS ARE EVICTED ANNUALLY. EMERGING EVIDENCE SHOWS EVICTIONS CAUSE NUMEROUS HEALTH PROBLEMS AND INCREASE MORTALITY RISK BY 40%. OUR PRELIMINARY RESEARCH SUGGESTS EVICTIONS ALSO MAKE IT HARDER FOR TENANTS TO RETAIN MEDICAID COVERAGE, ACQUIRE AMBULATORY CARE, OR FILL PRESCRIPTIONS. YET WE KNOW ASTONISHINGLY LITTLE ABOUT EVICTIONS’ HEALTHCARE IMPACTS, INCLUDING ON KEY PREVENTIVE SERVICES; PRIMARY CARE CONTINUITY, ESPECIALLY FOR CHRONIC DISEASES; OR AVOIDABLE ACUTE CARE UTILIZATION. A BETTER GRASP ON HOW EVICTIONS SHAPE THESE OUTCOMES IS IMPORTANT FOR INFORMING HEALTHCARE AND HOUSING PROGRAMS. UNFORTUNATELY, CLARIFYING EVICTIONS’ HEALTHCARE IMPACTS (AND THEIR IMPLICATIONS FOR LATER CHRONIC DISEASE) HAS PROVEN DIFFICULT, AS ALMOST NO STUDIES HAVE LINKED EVICTION RECORDS WITH HEALTHCARE DATA AT SCALE.  TO OVERCOME THAT ROADBLOCK AND ADVANCE TOWARDS OUR LONG-TERM GOAL OF REDUCING PREVENTABLE MORBIDITY WHILE LOWERING HEALTHCARE COSTS, WE WILL MERGE 14 YEARS OF UNIQUELY PUBLICLY-AVAILABLE EVICTION DATA IN NEW YORK CITY TO MEDICAID CLAIMS—AN APPROACH WE PIONEERED IN PRELIMINARY STUDIES. THIS WILL CREATE THE LARGEST, AND ONE OF THE ONLY, DATABASES IN THE US LINKING INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL EVICTIONS TO DETAILED HEALTHCARE INFORMATION. OUR DATA WILL ALLOW US TO ANSWER CRITICAL QUESTIONS ABOUT HOW EVICTIONS AFFECT HEALTHCARE, ESPECIALLY IN WAYS THAT COULD CREATE LONG-TERM ISSUES FOR POPULATION HEALTH AND HEALTHCARE FINANCING.   WE APPROACH THIS QUESTION COMPREHENSIVELY, EXAMINING HEALTHCARE OUTCOMES ACROSS THE PREVENTIVE CARE SPECTRUM AND APPLYING STATE-OF-THE-SCIENCE CAUSAL INFERENCE METHODS, INCLUDING (A) COARSENED EXACT MATCHING AND (B) A NATURAL EXPERIMENT / INSTRUMENTAL VARIABLES ANALYSIS. AIM 1 QUANTIFIES EVICTIONS’ IMPACT ON PREVENTIVE CARE SERVICES WHOSE INTERRUPTION CAN WORSEN CHRONIC DISEASE PROGNOSES. AIM 2 THEN EXAMINES EVICTIONS’ RELATIONSHIP TO PRIMARY CARE CONTINUITY, FOCUSING ON PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS. FINALLY, AIM 3 ASSESSES THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN EVICTION AND POTENTIALLY AVOIDABLE ACUTE CARE AND RELATED HEALTHCARE COSTS. RESULTS WOULD OFFER FRESH INSIGHTS FOR CLINICIANS AND HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS LOOKING TO PROTECT EVICTED PATIENTS’ HEALTH, AND ALLOW HEALTHCARE PAYERS TO WEIGH THE FULL HEALTHCARE EXTERNALITIES OF INVESTING IN EVICTION PREVENTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNKNOWABLE UNCERTAINTY: TOWARDS COMMUNICATING THE LIMITS OF EVIDENCE IN THE CARE OF MULTIMORBIDITY - ABSTRACT EFFECTIVELY COMMUNICATING THE UNCERTAINTY AROUND ESTIMATES OF TREATMENT RISKS AND BENEFITS (I.E., AMBIGUITY AND COMPLEXITY) IS A CRITICAL AND UNIQUE COMPONENT OF SHARED DECISION MAKING (SDM) FOR CHILDREN WITH MEDICAL COMPLEXITY. FOR CHILDREN WITH MEDICAL COMPLEXITY, MUCH IMPRECISION REMAINS AROUND ESTIMATES OF TREATMENT RISKS AND BENEFITS DUE TO DIFFICULTIES PERFORMING RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS IN A MEDICALLY FRAGILE AND HETEROGENOUS POPULATION. WHEN FACED WITH UNCERTAIN OUTCOMES, FAMILIES OFTEN CHOOSE HIGH-INTENSITY INTERVENTIONS AT THE COST OF QUALITY OF LIFE WHEN LOWER INTENSITY OPTIONS ARE ALSO REASONABLE. INSTEAD, IN THESE SITUATIONS OF CLINICAL EQUIPOISE, SDM SHOULD BE USED TO HELP FAMILIES AND PROVIDERS EFFECTIVELY TALK ABOUT DECISION-RELATED UNCERTAINTY. HOW TO DO SO REMAINS LARGELY UNKNOWN. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO TRANSFORM CLINICAL COMMUNICATION OF AMBIGUITY AND COMPLEXITY TO ENABLE HIGHER QUALITY SDM IN ENGLISH- AND SPANISH-SPEAKING POPULATIONS, THE TWO MOST COMMON LANGUAGES IN THE UNITED STATES. TO DO SO THIS PROPOSAL INNOVATES ON METHODS TO COMMUNICATE AMBIGUITY AND COMPLEXITY AND TESTS THE EFFICACY OF THOSE METHODS IN THE CARE OF CHILDREN WITH MEDICAL COMPLEXITY. IN AIM 1, WE WILL EXAMINE WHETHER VISUAL DISPLAYS WHEN COMBINED WITH TEXT- BASED DESCRIPTIONS OF UNCERTAINTY REDUCE KNOWLEDGE GAPS IN UNDERSTANDING AMBIGUITY AND COMPLEXITY TYPES OF UNCERTAINTY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL REFINE AN EXISTING UNCERTAINTY COMMUNICATION TOOLKIT USING HUMAN-CENTERED DESIGN TO BE CONTEXTUALLY ALIGNED WITH NEEDS AND EXPERIENCES BY LANGUAGE PREFERENCE. IN AIM 3, WE WILL ASSESS THE EFFICACY OF THE UNCERTAINTY COMMUNICATION TOOLKIT COMPARED TO USUAL CARE IN IMPROVING SDM IN A TEST CASE OF CHILDREN WITH NEUROMUSCULAR SCOLIOSIS. THIS PROPOSAL BRIDGES A GAP IN UNCERTAINTY COMMUNICATION THAT CRITICALLY HINDERS SDM BY DEVELOPING AND OPTIMIZING STRATEGIES TO EFFECTIVELY CONVEY AMBIGUITY AND COMPLEXITY OF TREATMENT RISKS. THIS RESEARCH CAN TRANSFORM CLINICAL COMMUNICATION PRACTICES TO IMPROVE SDM AND OUTCOMES FOR CHILDREN WITH MEDICAL COMPLEXITY. BY ADDRESSING THE CORE ISSUES OF AMBIGUITY AND COMPLEXITY IN UNCERTAINTY COMMUNICATION, THE PROPOSAL WILL PROVIDE A ROBUST FRAMEWORK TO IMPROVE SDM FOR GROWING POPULATIONS OF ADULTS AND CHILDREN WITH MULTIPLE COMORBIDITIES FACING SIMILAR GAPS IN EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE THAT RESULT IN IMMENSE UNCERTAINTIES DURING HIGH- STAKES DECISION-MAKING. THIS WORK WILL SERVE AS A FOUNDATION FOR HOW TO IMPROVE PATIENT-CAREGIVER-PROVIDER COMMUNICATION ABOUT DECISION-RELATED UNCERTAINTIES TO FACILITATE ETHICAL, INFORMED DECISION MAKING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PARTNERING WITH ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS WITH SICKLE CELL DISEASE IN TREATMENT DECISIONS - SICKLE CELL DISEASE (SCD) IS A LIFE-THREATENING CONDITION MARKED BY DEBILITATING COMPLICATIONS, POOR QUALITY OF LIFE, AND EARLY MORTALITY. HISTORICALLY, SCD HAS RECEIVED FAR LESS FUNDING AND PUBLIC POLICY EFFORTS THAN OTHER CHRONIC DISEASES, RESULTING IN DECADES OF STAGNATION IN MEDICAL ADVANCES. HOWEVER, TREATMENT OPTIONS FOR SCD ARE NOW EXPANDING WITH RECENT FEDERAL AND INDUSTRY INVESTMENTS. FOR THE FIRST TIME, PATIENTS LIVING WITH SCD ARE MAKING DECISIONS ABOUT MULTIPLE DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPIES, EACH WITH UNIQUE CLINICAL INDICATIONS AND TRADEOFFS IMPACTING QUALITY OF LIFE. UNFORTUNATELY, MOST DO NOT REAP THE BENEFITS OF THESE ADVANCES. HYDROXYUREA IS THE MAINSTAY TREATMENT, YET ONLY ABOUT 25% RECEIVE IT; UPTAKE OF OTHER THERAPIES IS ESTIMATED AT LESS THAN 5% OF THE POPULATION. USE OF THERAPIES IS ESPECIALLY SUBOPTIMAL AMONG ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS (AYAS) DUE TO PATIENT (LACK OF INVOLVEMENT IN DECISIONS, INADEQUATE KNOWLEDGE), PROVIDER (NOT OFFERING HU DUE TO CONCERNS ABOUT AYAS’ ADHERENCE), AND HEALTHCARE ACCESS CHALLENGES (LIMITED TRANSPORTATION, INADEQUATE INSURANCE). IN TURN, SUBOPTIMAL USE OF THERAPIES CONTRIBUTES TO HIGH MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY AMONG AYAS WITH SCD. HEALTH PROMOTION INTERVENTIONS THAT CAN EFFECTIVELY OVERCOME THESE BARRIERS ARE URGENTLY NEEDED TO OPTIMIZE UPTAKE AND ADHERENCE TO SCD THERAPIES AMONG AYAS AND THEREBY REDUCE PREVENTABLE DISEASE COMPLICATIONS. SHARED DECISION-MAKING (SDM) ENHANCES PATIENT KNOWLEDGE, ENGAGEMENT AND SATISFACTION WITH CARE, ADHERENCE TO TREATMENTS, AND HEALTH OUTCOMES. HOWEVER, SDM IS DIFFICULT TO ACHIEVE IN ROUTINE CARE, AND THERE ARE NO INTERVENTIONS THAT SUPPORT SDM FOR AYAS WITH SCD. TO ADDRESS THIS UNMET NEED, WE DEVELOPED THE SCD SHARED DECISION-MAKING TOOLKIT FOR AYAS (SDMT-AYA). SDMT-AYA TARGETS MULTI-LEVEL BARRIERS TO USE OF DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPIES BY PROVIDING TOOLS FOR: 1) MULTIDISCIPLINARY CLINICIANS (SKILLS-BASED TRAINING, COMMUNICATION SUPPORT TOOLS USED AT POINT-OF-CARE); 2) AYAS AND CAREGIVERS (DECISION AIDS THAT LEVERAGE ADVANCED LEARNING TECHNOLOGIES); AND 3) IMPLEMENTATION (PROCESS MAPPING, AUDIT AND FEEDBACK). PRELIMINARY FINDINGS SUGGEST HIGH USABILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND FEASIBILITY OF THE TOOLKIT. THIS STEPPED-WEDGE CLUSTER RANDOMIZED TRIAL WILL EVALUATE EFFECTIVENESS OF SDMT-AYA ON PATIENT EXPERIENCES OF SDM, PATIENT KNOWLEDGE OF SCD AND TREATMENT OPTIONS, AND CLINICAL OUTCOMES (USE OF THERAPIES, ACUTE CARE UTILIZATION), TEST MECHANISMS OF ACTION, AND EXAMINE BARRIERS AND FACILITATORS TO IMPLEMENTING AND SUSTAINING SDMT-AYA. FOUR SITES WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO CROSS OVER FROM USUAL CARE (USE OF A POCKET GUIDE FOR DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPY DISCUSSIONS) TO THE INTERVENTION CONDITION (USE OF SDMT-AYA TO DISCUSS DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPIES) AT DISTINCT TIME POINTS. WE WILL INTERVIEW KEY INFORMANTS AT EACH SITE TO EXPLORE BARRIERS AND FACILITATORS AFFECTING IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINMENT OF THE TOOLKIT. THIS RESEARCH HAS THE POTENTIAL TO REINVENT HOW HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS EDUCATE, ENGAGE, AND PARTNER WITH AYAS IN MAKING CARE DECISIONS. IF SUCCESSFUL, THIS PROJECT CAN SERVE AS A MODEL FOR FACILITATING SDM TO IMPROVE CARE AND OUTCOMES FOR AYAS WITH OTHER CHRONIC CONDITIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ELUCIDATING GBA-LINKED PARKINSON'S DISEASE AND DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES - PROJECT SUMMARY GBA IS A MAJOR RISK GENE FOR PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD) AND DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES (DLB), TWO NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES, WITH Α-SYNUCLEIN-CONTAINING LEWY BODY PATHOLOGY AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT. SIGNIFICANTLY, PD PATIENTS WITH GBA MUTATIONS, ESPECIALLY L444P, EXHIBIT GREATER COGNITIVE DEFICITS AND MORE RAPID DECLINE THAN IDIOPATHIC PD. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH GBA PREDISPOSES TO DEMENTIA ARE NOT WELL UNDERSTOOD. TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP, WE CONDUCTED A LONGITUDINAL BEHAVIORAL STUDY OF WILDTYPE (WT), GBA L444P/KO MICE, SNCA PD TRANSGENICS (TG) THAT OVEREXPRESS MUTANT HUMAN Α-SYNUCLEIN, AND THEIR CROSSBREEDS, I.E. GBA-SNCA MICE, A MODEL FOR DLB. WE FOUND THAT COGNITIVE AND MOTOR DEFICITS ARE DISSOCIABLE BY GENOTYPE, WITH GBA L444P/KO MUTANTS EXHIBITING COGNITIVE DEFICITS ONLY, SNCA TG MOTOR DIFFICULTIES ONLY, AND GBA-SNCA EARLY COGNITIVE DEFICITS THAT PERSIST AND LATER WORSE MOTOR DIFFICULTIES. HISTOPATHOLOGICAL ANALYSIS REVEALED THAT GBA L444P/KO MUTANT MICE LACK Α-SYNUCLEIN PATHOLOGY, BUT GBA-SNCA MICE SHOW EXACERBATED CORTICAL AND HIPPOCAMPAL Α-SYNUCLEIN PATHOLOGY COMPARED TO SNCA TG. THESE UNEXPECTED FINDINGS SUGGEST THAT COGNITIVE DEFICITS IN GBA L444P MUTANTS MAY EMERGE INDEPENDENTLY OF Α-SYNUCLEIN PATHOLOGY, WHILE MOTOR DEFICITS IN SNCA TG AND GBA-SNCA MICE ARE CLOSELY RELATED TO Α-SYNUCLEIN PATHOLOGY BURDEN. TO UNDERSTAND THE BASES OF THESE PHENOTYPES, WE PERFORMED SINGLE-NUCLEUS RNA SEQUENCING AND QUANTITATIVE PROTEOMICS WHICH REVEALED A CLEAR ROLE FOR GBA MUTANTS IN SYNAPTIC DYSFUNCTION, PARTICULARLY IN PRESYNAPTIC VESICLE CYCLING. BASED ON THESE COMPELLING RESULTS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT GBA L444P MUTATIONS LEAD TO COGNITIVE DEFICITS THROUGH SYNAPTIC DYSFUNCTION INDEPENDENT OF Α-SYNUCLEIN PATHOLOGY. WE PROPOSE THAT GBA MUTATIONS LEAD TO EARLY SYNAPTIC DEFICITS BY ALTERING THE SYNAPTIC LIPIDOME. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS BY ELUCIDATING HOW GBA L444P/WT AND L444P/KO MUTATIONS IMPACT SYNAPTIC VESICLE CYCLING AND ULTRASTRUCTURE OF CORTICAL AND HIPPOCAMPAL SYNAPSES (AIM 1). IDENTIFY MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH GBA MUTATIONS INFLUENCES LYSOSOME-SYNAPSE CROSS TALK, WITH A FOCUS ON LIPIDS (AIM 2). TEST IF OVEREXPRESSION OF GBA TO INCREASE GLUCOCEREBROSIDASE ACTIVITY IN AGED WILDTYPE MICE WILL AMELIORATE AGE-DEPENDENT COGNITIVE DECLINE (AIM 3). UNDERSTANDING HOW GBA CONTRIBUTES TO SYNAPTIC DYSFUNCTION AND COGNITIVE DECLINE WILL PROVIDE A MECHANISTIC FRAMEWORK TO GUIDE THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT FOR BOTH PD AND DLB.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BIOPHYSICAL MECHANISMS OF CORTICAL MICROSTIMULATION - DIRECT LOCAL ELECTRICAL STIMULATION (DLES) IS AN INCREASINGLY IMPORTANT THERAPEUTIC TOOL FOR TREATING BRAIN DISORDERS SUCH AS PARKINSON’S, EPILEPSY, AND OCD. THERE IS CONSIDERABLE DISAGREEMENT, HOWEVER, AS TO HOW NEURAL STIMULATION, ESPECIALLY AT THE SCALE OF NEURONS, AFFECTS HUMAN BRAIN FUNCTION. THIS LACK OF UNDERSTANDING HAMPERS THE DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF MORE EFFECTIVE STIMULATION APPROACHES, PARTICULARLY IN THE CORTEX. TO DELIVER ON THE PRECISE, INCLUSIVE, AND EFFECTIVE THERAPEUTIC PROMISE OF DLES, A MORE MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE BIOPHYSICS OF CORTICAL STIMULATION IS REQUIRED. THIS PROJECT COMBINES SINGLE-CELL ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY IN BOTH HUMAN AND MOUSE CORTEX, BOTH EX-VIVO AND IN VIVO WITH PHARMACOLOGY, OPTICAL PHYSIOLOGY, AND SOPHISTICATED COMPUTATIONAL MODELING TO IDENTIFY THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING ELECTRICAL STIMULATION. IN A TRULY TRANSLATIONAL APPROACH, THESE MULTIPLE RESEARCH ANGLES WILL ALLOW US TO TEST IN-DEPTH MECHANISTIC HYPOTHESES IN THE MOUSE AND WHETHER THESE RESULTS HOLD TRUE IN THE HUMAN. WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT DLES INDUCES A DYNAMIC SEQUENCE OF EXCITATORY (E) NEURON OUTPUT COUNTERED BY SUBSEQUENT INHIBITORY (I) NEURON. WE WILL EVALUATE STIMULATION INTENSITY, FREQUENCY, PHASE, DISTANCE, AND SPECIES AS KEY PARAMETERS IN MODULATING THE TIMING AND STRENGTH OF THIS E-I DYNAMIC SEQUENCE. THESE DATA ON NEURONAL DYNAMICS WILL BE LEVERAGED INTO ACTIONABLE KNOWLEDGE THROUGH AN INTEGRATE-AND-FIRE BASED RECURRENT NEURONAL NETWORK MODEL WHICH WE WILL USE TO PREDICT CORTICAL RESPONSES TO NOVEL STIMULI AND DEVELOP SPECIFIC STIMULATION PATTERNS TO EVOKE DESIRED NEURAL OUTPUTS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL IDENTIFY THE BIOPHYSICAL MECHANISMS BY WHICH DLES RECRUITS DIFFERENT NEURONAL POPULATIONS IN ACUTE BRAIN SLICES OF HUMAN AND MOUSE CORTEX USING WHOLE-CELL ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY AND PHARMACOLOGY (AIM 1). WE WILL THEN CHARACTERIZE NEURON AND POPULATION RESPONSES TO DLES IN VIVO, USING NEUROPIXELS PROBES IN AWAKE HUMAN AND MOUSE CORTEX, COMPLEMENTED BY OPTICAL RECORDINGS IN THE AWAKE MOUSE (AIM 2). THIS EXTENSIVE AND DETAILED DATA SET WILL BE USED TO REFINE AND VALIDATE A TRAINABLE NEURAL NETWORK MODEL WE HAVE DEVELOPED TO ASSESS STIMULATION EFFECTS ON E AND I CELL TYPES (AIM 3). THE MODEL WILL BE THE TESTING GROUND TO DEVELOP SPECIFIC PATTERNS OF STIMULATION BASED ON DESIRED OUTPUTS SUCH AS TARGETING EITHER E OR I CELLS. THE MODEL WILL ALSO BE USED TO TEST NOVEL INPUT STIMULI INCLUDING AMPLITUDE AND FREQUENCY RAMPS, CHIRPS, AND STEP FUNCTIONS TO PREDICT NEURAL RESPONSES. TESTING THESE MODEL-PREDICTED OUTPUTS, OR RESPONSES, WILL THEN BE CARRIED OUT THROUGH FURTHER EX- AND IN-VIVO PHYSIOLOGY. NOT ONLY WILL WE CONNECT DYNAMICS OF A PRIMARY MODEL SYSTEM TO ACTIVITY IN THE HUMAN BRAIN, BUT THIS WORK WILL ALSO PROVIDE A UNIQUE ROUTE TOWARD PREDICTABLE MODULATION OF ACTIVITY IN INDIVIDUAL NEURONS AND LOCAL CIRCUITS TO DESIGN TAILORED NEUROMODULATION THERAPIES. OUR MULTI-SCALE ANALYSES OF THE NEURAL MECHANISMS OF ELECTRICAL STIMULATION WILL CATALYZE NOVEL, TARGETED, AND MECHANISTICALLY DRIVEN THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES THAT COULD REVOLUTIONIZE STIMULATION-BASED TREATMENT FOR MEMORY DISORDERS, DEPRESSION, STROKE RECOVERY, AND A HOST OF OTHER NEUROPSYCHIATRIC AILMENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CORTICAL CIRCUIT DYNAMICS UNDERLYING MULTISENSORY DECISION MAKING - PROJECT SUMMARY TO NAVIGATE AND GUIDE LOCOMOTION IN A COMPLEX 3D ENVIRONMENT, HUMANS AND ANIMALS MUST MAKE COUNTLESS JUDGMENTS OF THEIR DIRECTION OF SELF-MOTION, OR HEADING. EACH OF THESE IS A MULTISENSORY PERCEPTUAL DECISION, ABLE TO ACHIEVE GREATER ACCURACY AND PRECISION BY COMBINING SIGNALS FROM THE VISUAL, VESTIBULAR, AND KINESTHETIC SENSES. AT THE SAME TIME, THE BRAIN MUST DECIDE WHEN TO COMMIT TO A COURSE OF ACTION (E.G., TO QUICKLY CHANGE DIRECTION TO AVOID AN OBSTACLE), AND MAKE PREDICTIONS OF THE LIKELIHOOD OF SUCCESS IN THAT ACTION. THESE FEATURES OF A DECISION—CHOICE ACCURACY, RESPONSE TIME (RT), AND CONFIDENCE—HAVE BEEN STUDIED BY PSYCHOLOGISTS FOR OVER A CENTURY, BUT PRIMARILY FOR ONLY A SINGLE MODALITY, INSTEAD OF THE MORE NATURAL CASE OF INTEGRATING MULTIPLE SOURCES OF SENSORY EVIDENCE. MOREOVER, THE NEURAL BASIS OF MULTISENSORY INTEGRATION IS LARGELY STUDIED AT THE LEVEL OF INDIVIDUAL CELLS OR BRAIN REGIONS, WHEREAS NEARLY ALL PERCEPTUAL AND COGNITIVE FUNCTIONS DEPEND ON POPULATION-LEVEL COMPUTATIONS AND COMMUNICATION BETWEEN AREAS. TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS, WE TRAINED MONKEYS TO PERFORM A VISUAL-VESTIBULAR HEADING DISCRIMINATION TASK WHICH MEASURES CHOICE, RT, AND CONFIDENCE VIA A POST-DECISION WAGER (PDW). DURING PERFORMANCE OF THE TASK, WE WILL RECORD ENSEMBLE ACTIVITY SIMULTANEOUSLY FROM TWO KEY NODES IN THE SENSORY CORTICAL NETWORK REPRESENTING VISUAL AND VESTIBULAR SELF-MOTION CUES (MST AND PIVC, RESPECTIVELY), AS WELL AS ONE NODE (LATERAL INTRAPARIETAL AREA, LIP) IN THE DOWNSTREAM DECISION NETWORK THAT CONVERTS SENSORY EVIDENCE INTO A MOTOR PLAN. THESE REGIONS HAVE INDIVIDUALLY BEEN LINKED TO HEADING PERCEPTION, BUT LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW THEIR COORDINATED ACTIVITY PATTERNS, OBSERVABLE ONLY THOUGH POPULATION RECORDINGS, SUPPORT MULTISENSORY DECISION MAKING. IN AIM 1 OF THE PROPOSAL, WE WILL QUANTIFY THE COORDINATED ACTIVITY ACROSS SENSORY NEURAL POPULATIONS AND TEST WHETHER THE PERCEPTUAL IMPROVEMENT FROM MULTISENSORY INTEGRATION DEPEND ON THE STRENGTH OF COUPLING BETWEEN THEM, BEYOND WHAT CAN BE EXPLAINED BY THEIR ACTIVITY CONSIDERED INDEPENDENTLY. WHEN VISUAL AND VESTIBULAR CUES ARE ARTIFICIALLY PLACED IN CONFLICT, WE WILL ASK WHETHER AND HOW THE RELATIVE PRECISION OF HEADING ESTIMATES DECODED FROM THESE SENSORY POPULATIONS PREDICTS CHOICE AND CONFIDENCE, GUIDED BY PREDICTIONS OF A MULTISENSORY EVIDENCE ACCUMULATION MODEL. IN AIM 2, WE WILL EXTEND OUR INVESTIGATION OF INTER-AREAL INTERACTIONS TO THE DECISION STAGE, QUANTIFYING THE STRENGTH AND TIMING OF FUNCTIONAL COUPLING BETWEEN LIP AND EACH OF THE TWO SENSORY AREAS. THE RELATIVE TIMING OF THIS COORDINATED ACTIVITY CAN INDICATE FEEDFORWARD VERSUS FEEDBACK PROCESSES, REVEALING HOW PERCEPTUAL DECISIONS EVOLVE VIA RECURRENT LOOPS BETWEEN SENSATION AND DEGREE OF BELIEF IN A PROPOSITION (OR COMMITMENT TO A PLAN OF ACTION). THE RESULTS WILL YIELD NEW INSIGHTS INTO THE REPRESENTATION AND READOUT OF SENSORY EVIDENCE AND ITS ASSOCIATED DEGREE OF (UN)CERTAINTY, AND WILL ADVANCE A POPULATION- AND CIRCUIT-LEVEL UNDERSTANDING OF DECISION COMPUTATIONS IN A MULTISENSORY TASK.
