description: COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA, VASCULAR BRAIN INJURY, AND ATRIAL MYOPATHY: IMPLICATIONS FOR PREVENTION OF ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE-RELATED DEMENTIAS - ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND AD-RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD) ARE PROJECTED TO AFFECT 115 MILLION PEOPLE WORLDWIDE BY 2050. VASCULAR CONTRIBUTIONS TO COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA (VCID)—A PRIMARY TYPE OF ADRD—IS A MAJOR RESEARCH FOCUS FOR THE NIH, WHICH HAS CALLED FOR THE NEED TO DISCOVER NOVEL NON-INVASIVE, NON-CNS ORGAN-RELATED (E.G., HEART) MARKERS TO DETECT PRESENCE AND PROGRESSION OF VCID (ADRD SUMMIT 2022). THE OLDEST-OLD (>85 YEARS) ARE THE FASTEST GROWING SEGMENT OF THE POPULATION IN MOST OF THE WORLD AND HAVE THE HIGHEST RATES OF DEMENTIA. YET, THE RISK FACTORS FOR AD/ADRD IN THE OLDEST-OLD ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD AND ARE DIFFERENT FROM THE YOUNG-OLD (65-74 YEARS) AND MIDDLE-OLD (75-84 YEARS). FOR EXAMPLE, IN THE OLDEST- OLD, HYPERTENSION IS PROTECTIVE AND ABOUT HALF OF ALL DEMENTIA CASES IS RELATED TO NON-AD PATHOLOGIES SUCH AS MICROBLEEDS AND SMALL VESSEL ISCHEMIC DISEASE. ATRIAL MYOPATHY (DEFINED BY ALTERED LEFT ATRIAL [LA] FUNCTION OR STRUCTURE) IS AN UNDERRECOGNIZED BUT IMPORTANT CONTRIBUTOR TO VCID, AND IS ASSOCIATED WITH LOWER COGNITIVE FUNCTION, GREATER VASCULAR BRAIN INJURY, AND INCIDENT DEMENTIA. ATRIAL MYOPATHY IS ALSO ASSOCIATED WITH GREATER GLOBAL CORTICAL Β-AMYLOID (AD PATHOLOGY). HOWEVER, THE EXTENT TO WHICH ATRIAL MYOPATHY IS ASSOCIATED WITH DEMENTIA RISK IN THE OLDEST-OLD IS UNKNOWN. FURTHERMORE, PRIOR RESEARCH HAS EVALUATED ATRIAL MYOPATHY AS A STATIC ENTITY AND THE ETIOLOGY AND PROGNOSTIC RELEVANCE OF ATRIAL MYOPATHY PROGRESSION ARE NOT KNOWN. THESE ARE CRUCIAL BARRIERS TO TARGETING THIS POTENTIALLY MODIFIABLE RISK FACTOR FOR AD/ADRD PREVENTION. THUS, THE OVERARCHING OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO DETERMINE THE PROGNOSTIC IMPORTANCE OF ATRIAL MYOPATHY FOR INCIDENT DEMENTIA IN THE OLDEST-OLD; RELATE ATRIAL MYOPATHY PROGRESSION OR TRAJECTORIES OF ATRIAL MYOPATHY IN THE YOUNG-OLD AND MIDDLE-OLD TO INCIDENT DEMENTIA AND CHANGE IN NEUROIMAGING AND PLASMA BIOMARKERS OF AD/ADRD; AND DEFINE THE CLINICAL/LIFESTYLE RISK FACTORS AND PROTEOMIC AND METABOLOMIC SIGNATURES OF ADVERSE ATRIAL MYOPATHY TRAJECTORIES. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE EXTENSIVELY WELL-CHARACTERIZED ATHEROSCLEROSIS RISK IN COMMUNITIES (ARIC) COHORT (INCLUDING THE LONGEST FOLLOWED COHORT OF BLACK ADULTS) WITH EXISTING MCI/DEMENTIA ASCERTAINMENT AND NEUROIMAGING DATA, AND WILL PERFORM SERIAL MEASUREMENT OF LA FUNCTION, MEASURE CIRCULATING AD/ADRD BIOMARKERS, AND CONDUCT AMBULATORY HEART RHYTHM MONITORING TO RIGOROUSLY DETECT ATRIAL FIBRILLATION (AF) SO THAT WE CAN ACCOUNT FOR THE CONTRIBUTION OF AF TO ASSOCIATIONS. TO ENSURE RIGOR AND REPRODUCIBILITY, WE WILL REPLICATE FINDINGS IN 2 INDEPENDENT COMMUNITY-BASED COHORTS: MULTIETHNIC STUDY OF ATHEROSCLEROSIS AND THE JACKSON HEART STUDY. THIS PROJECT WILL HAVE SIGNIFICANT IMPACT. OUR FINDINGS WILL (A) BROADEN VCID TO ENCOMPASS ATRIAL MYOPATHY AS AN INSULT TO THE NEUROVASCULAR UNIT, THUS IDENTIFYING A NEW AVENUE FOR AD/ADRD TREATMENT OR PREVENTION; (B) CLARIFY THE PATHOLOGY UNDERLYING THE NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPACT OF ATRIAL MYOPATHY, HENCE FACILITATING RESEARCH TO DISCOVER NOVEL AD/ADRD PREVENTION STRATEGIES; (C) IDENTIFY SPECIFIC LIFESTYLE OR MOLECULAR TARGETS FOR ATRIAL MYOPATHY PROGRESSION, THUS INFORMING FUTURE CLINICAL TRIALS AIMED AT PREVENTING AD/ADRD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE YOUNG GUT MICROBIOME: A FOUNTAIN OF YOUTH FOR BRAIN INJURY IN THE AGED? - TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY (TBI) IS A LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH AND DISABILITY WORLDWIDE. PATIENTS AGED 65 YEARS AND OLDER ACCOUNT FOR AN INCREASING PROPORTION OF PATIENTS WITH TBI AND LESS THAN HALF OF AGED TBI PATIENTS BECOME FUNCTIONALLY INDEPENDENT AFTER INJURY. IN FACT, TBI IS ONE OF THE GREATEST NON-GENETIC RISK FACTORS FOR THE SUBSEQUENT DEVELOPMENT OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE-RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD). CHRONIC NEUROINFLAMMATION RESULTING FROM THE CONSTITUTIVE ACTIVATION OF MICROGLIA IS COMPLICIT IN AD, ADRD AND RELATED DISEASE PROCESSES, AND REPRESENTS A COMPLEX INTERPLAY BETWEEN AGED MICROGLIA AND THE STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION OF THE AGED GUT MICROBIOME. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISM(S) UNDERLYING GUT MICROBIOTA-MICROGLIA INTERACTION IN AD, ADRD, AND AGING HAVE YET TO BE ELUCIDATED. PUBLISHED DATA FROM OUR LABORATORY SHOWS THAT AGED MICROGLIA ADOPT A CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVATED STATE. THESE “PRIMED” MICROGLIA ARE THEN CAPABLE PRODUCING AN EXAGGERATED INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE AND MAY REPRESENT ONE OF THE MECHANISMS LEADING TO THE INCREASED INCIDENCE OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE-RELATED DEMENTIA IN AGED PATIENTS AFTER TBI. PUBLISHED AND PRELIMINARY DATA FROM OUR LABORATORY FURTHER DEMONSTRATES THAT POST-INJURY GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY STRUCTURE IS A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR IN THE DEGREE OF NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT INCLUDING IN AD AND ADRD DIAGNOSES AFTER TBI. OUR DATA SHOWS THAT RESTORATION OF A PREINJURY GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY MARKEDLY IMPROVED NEUROCOGNITIVE INCLUDING AD/ADRD-RELATED OUTCOMES AND ATTENUATED THE CONSTITUTIVE ACTIVATION OF MICROGLIA AFTER TBI IN MICE. WE PUBLISHED SIMILAR FINDINGS WITHIN THE GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY ASSOCIATED WITH NORMAL AGING WITH AN INCREASE IN THE RELATIVE ABUNDANCE OF SEVERAL MICROBIAL TAXA STRONGLY ASSOCIATED WITH AD AND ADRD. NONETHELESS, MECHANISM(S) LINKING ALTERATIONS IN THE AGED GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUBSEQUENT AD AND ADRD HAVE YET TO BE FULLY ELUCIDATED. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT RESTORATION OF A YOUTHFUL GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY BEFORE OR AFTER TBI WILL ATTENUATE THE CONSTITUTIVE ACTIVATION OF MICROGLIA AND IMPROVE NEUROCOGNITIVE AND AD/ADRD-RELATED OUTCOMES IN AGED TBI MICE. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER RESTORING A YOUTHFUL GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY STRUCTURE VIA FECAL MICROBIOTA TRANSPLANT WITH STOOL FROM YOUNG MICE WILL ATTENUATE THE ACTIVATION OF MICROGLIA IN AGED MICE. WE WILL UTILIZE BOTH A PRE-INJURY “PREBIOTIC” MODEL AS WELL AS A POST-INJURY TREATMENT PARADIGM. WE WILL USE BULK POPULATION CELL SORTING (FACSORTING) OF MICROGLIA FOLLOWED BY SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING (SCRNASEQ). WE WILL COMPARE CANDIDATE GENES TO MICROBIAL ACTIVITY VIA FECAL 16S RRNA GENE AMPLICON SEQUENCING AND FECAL METABOLITE ANALYSIS. HARMONIZED WITH THE TRANSCRIPTOMIC AND GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY PROFILING, WE WILL UTILIZE LONGITUDINAL PET/CT IMAGING OF THE 18-KDA TRANSLOCATOR PROTEIN (TSPO) WITH A NOVEL FLUORINE-BASED RADIOTRACER DEVELOPED BY OUR GROUP TO TRACK AND COMPARE THE ONSET, PROGRESSION, AND DEGREE OF MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION BEFORE, DURING, AND AFTER GUT MICROBIAL INTERVENTION AFTER TBI. COLLECTIVELY, THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL IDENTIFY THE KEY ROLE OF AN AGED GUT MICROBIOME IN THE ONSET AND PROGRESSION OF CONSTITUTIVE MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION OVER THE COURSE OF TBI, THUS RAISING THE POTENTIAL FOR NOVEL THERAPEUTIC AND BIOMARKER DEVELOPMENT IN AGED TBI, AD, AND ADRD PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES SECRETED BY HUMAN STEM CELL-DERIVED M2 MICROGLIA-LIKE CELLS FOR STROKE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO ENGINEER AND BIO-MANUFACTURE EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES (EVS) SECRETED BY M2 MICROGLIA-LIKE CELLS DERIVED FROM HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS (HIPSCS) IN ORDER TO PROMOTE NEURAL REGENERATION IN ISCHEMIC STROKE. MICROGLIA, THE RESIDENT MACROPHAGE-LIKE CELLS IN THE HUMAN BRAIN, ACCOUNT FOR 5 TO 20 PERCENT OF TOTAL NEURAL CELLS IN THE PARENCHYMA AND ARE LIMITED IN ACCESSIBILITY. PUBLISHED IN 2023 NATURE, THE SIGNALING PROVIDED BY MICROGLIA IS FOUND TO BE CRITICAL FOR BRAIN ORGANOID MATURATION AND TISSUE DEVELOPMENT. EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES, THE MEMBRANE-BOUND NANOVESICLES (30-1000 NM), SECRETED BY MICROGLIA CONTAIN PROTEIN, LIPID, AND MICRORNA CARGO THAT REFLECT OR ENRICH THERAPEUTIC FUNCTION OF THE PARENT CELLS BY REGULATING CELL-CELL COMMUNICATIONS. IN PARTICULAR, EXOSOMES ARE THE THERAPEUTIC SMALL SUBPOPULATION (30-200 NM) OF THE EVS. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESES OF THIS RESEARCH INCLUDE: (1) EVS OF M2 MICROGLIA-LIKE CELLS IN BRAIN-REGION-SPECIFIC ORGANOIDS PROMOTE NEUROGENESIS AND SYNAPTOGENESIS, ENHANCING THE BRAIN-LIKE MICROENVIRONMENT OF THE SPECIFIC BRAIN REGION; AND (2) BY INTEGRATION THE ISOLATED EVS WITH ORGANOIDS OF DIFFERENT BRAIN REGIONS, THE EVS UPREGULATE NEURAL PROTECTIVE FUNCTION AND SUPPRESSES PRO-INFLAMMATORY SIGNALING, MAINTAINING HOMEOSTATIC STATE. SPECIFICALLY, FOUR AIMS ARE PROPOSED: (1) TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT METABOLIC MONITORING PROMOTES BIO-MANUFACTURING OF EVS SECRETED BY M2 MICROGLIA-LIKE CELLS DERIVED FROM HIPSCS IN A VERTICAL-WHEEL BIOREACTOR; (2) TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT EVS SECRETED BY M2 MICROGLIA-LIKE CELLS POSSESS THERAPEUTIC CARGO AND IMMUNOMODULATION PROPERTIES; AND (3) AND (4) TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT EVS SECRETED BY M2 MICROGLIA-LIKE CELLS PROMOTE NEURAL REGENERATION AND SYNAPTIC ACTIVITIES (3) IN VITRO USING BRAIN ORGANOID MODELS AND (4) IN VIVO. THE NOVELTY OF THE PROPOSED STUDY IN CONTRAST TO PREVIOUS STUDY IS THAT THE M2 PRIMED MICROGLIA-LIKE CELLS SECRETE THE EVS THAT ARE INTEGRATED BY CELLS OF BRAIN REGION-SPECIFIC ORGANOIDS (E.G., FOREBRAIN, CEREBELLAR, SPINAL CORD, ETC.), BETTER PROMOTING PHENOTYPE AND FUNCTION OF HUMAN BRAIN-LIKE TISSUE. THE FUNCTION OF EVS OF MICROGLIA-LIKE CELLS WILL BE CHARACTERIZED UNDER PRO-INFLAMMATORY (M1 PHENOTYPE) OR ANTI-INFLAMMATORY (M2 PHENOTYPE) STIMULATIONS. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL USE MULTI-OMICS TOOL (TRANSCRIPTOME ANALYSIS OF EVS AND CELLS, MICRORNA-SEQUENCING TO ANALYZE EV MICRORNA CARGO, QUANTITATIVE LIPIDOMICS TO ANALYZE EV LIPID COMPOSITION, AND PROTEOMICS TO ANALYZE EV PROTEIN CARGO) TO CORRELATE WITH IN VITRO AND IN VIVO FUNCTIONAL STUDIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DORSOMEDIAL STRIATAL DOPAMINE AND DEMENTIA IN PARKINSON'S DISEASE - ABSTRACT PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD) IS A MOVEMENT DISORDER THAT ALSO IMPAIRS COGNITION, AFFECTING EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS SUCH AS WORKING MEMORY, ATTENTION, AND TIMING. THESE SYMPTOMS CONTRIBUTE TO MORBIDITY, EMPLOYMENT LOSS, NURSING HOME PLACEMENT, MORTALITY, AND CAN DEVELOP INTO DEMENTIA IN PD (PDD). THESE OUTCOMES DEVASTATE THE LIVES OF PATIENTS, THEIR FAMILIES, AND THEIR COMMUNITIES. BECAUSE THE INCIDENCE OF PD IS GROWING, THE BURDEN OF THIS DISEASE WILL SURGE IN COMING DECADES. CURRENT TREATMENTS FOR MOTOR SYMPTOMS OF PD DO NOT IMPROVE AND CAN WORSEN EXECUTIVE FUNCTION. THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED TO BETTER UNDERSTAND EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS AND DYSFUNCTION IN PD TO DEVELOP NEW NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL MARKERS AND TARGETED TREATMENTS. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO MAP CIRCUITS UNDERLYING EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS IN PD. PD IS A COMPLEX DISEASE INVOLVING DOPAMINE THAT ORIGINATES FROM THE SUBSTANTIA NIGRA PARS COMPACTA (SNC) AND MODULATES STRIATAL FUNCTION. STRIATAL CIRCUITS ARE DEFINED BY MEDIUM-SPINY NEURONS (MSNS) THAT EXPRESS EITHER D1 OR D2 DOPAMINE RECEPTORS (D1-MSNS AND D2-MSNS, RESPECTIVELY). OUR RECENT WORK HAS SHOWN THAT D1- AND D2-MSNS ARE CRITICAL FOR AN ELEMENTARY EXECUTIVE PROCESS: INTERVAL TIMING. INTERVAL TIMING REQUIRES PARTICIPANTS TO ESTIMATE AN INTERVAL OF SEVERAL SECONDS WITH A MOTOR RESPONSE AND DEPENDS ON WORKING MEMORY FOR TEMPORAL RULES AND ATTENTION TO THE PASSAGE OF TIME. INTERVAL TIMING IS IMPAIRED IN PATIENTS WITH PDD. OUR RECENT WORK SHOWS THAT D1- AND D2-MSNS ENCODE TIME BY LINEAR “RAMPING” CHANGES IN FIRING ACROSS TEMPORAL INTERVALS AND INTEGRATE TEMPORAL EVIDENCE. WE WILL TEST THE OVERALL HYPOTHESIS THAT DOPAMINE ENGAGES MSN RAMPING ACTIVITY. WE WILL FOCUS ON THE MOUSE DORSOMEDIAL STRIATUM AND COMBINE DOPAMINE FIBER PHOTOMETRY, OPTOGENETICS, NEURONAL RECORDING, AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING. DATA FROM THIS PROPOSAL ARE HIGHLY SIGNIFICANT IN EXPLORING FUNDAMENTAL CIRCUIT MECHANISMS OF STRIATAL DOPAMINE AND WILL ELUCIDATE HOW DORSOMEDIAL STRIATAL CIRCUITS ENCODE INTERVAL TIMING. THIS PROPOSAL ADVANCES OUR LONG-TERM GOAL OF DETERMINING WHERE AND HOW TO DELIVER BRAIN STIMULATION TO TREAT EXECUTIVE DYSFUNCTION IN PD, PDD, AND OTHER ALZHEIMER’S-DISEASE-RELATED DEMENTIAS SUCH AS DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SEX-SPECIFIC ROLE OF GABA SIGNALING IN GLIOBLASTOMA IMMUNE RESPONSE - PROJECT SUMMARY: GLIOBLASTOMA (GBM) IS THE MOST COMMON PRIMARY MALIGNANT BRAIN TUMOR, WITH A MEDIAN SURVIVAL OF ~20 MONTHS. THE STANDARD OF CARE HAS NOT CHANGED IN TWO DECADES, AND IMMUNOTHERAPIES HAVE HAD LIMITED SUCCESS IN IMPROVING OUTCOMES. ACCUMULATION OF MYELOID CELLS IN THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT (TME), INCLUDING MYELOID-DERIVED SUPPRESSOR CELLS (MDSCS), IS A MAJOR FACTOR UNDERLYING THE TREATMENT RESISTANCE. THUS, IDENTIFYING MDSC REGULATORY MECHANISMS IS CRITICAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS FOR GBM. WE AND OTHERS HAVE SHOWN THAT SEX DIFFERENCES IN IMMUNE RESPONSES, CANCER CELL SIGNALING, AND TME INTERACTIONS INFORM GBM OUTCOMES. IN EARLIER STUDIES, WE REPORTED THAT GRANULOCYTIC/POLYMORPHONUCLEAR MDSCS (GMDSCS) DRIVE GBM IN FEMALES. HOWEVER, A LIMITED UNDERSTANDING OF THE HOST FACTORS THAT UNDERLY SEX-SPECIFIC PRO- TUMORIGENIC ROLES OF MDSC SUBSETS DAMPENS OUR ABILITY TO EFFECTIVELY TARGET THESE CELLS. IN PRELIMINARY EXPERIMENTS, WE OBSERVED THAT GMDSCS EXPRESS GAMMA-AMINOBUTYRIC ACID (GABA) RECEPTORS UNLIKE MONOCYTIC MDSCS. GABA METABOLICALLY REPROGRAMED FEMALE, BUT NOT MALE GMDSCS, BY ENHANCING L-ARGININE (L-ARG) UPTAKE VIA CATIONIC AMINO ACID TRANSPORTER 2B (CAT2B). SIGNALING THROUGH GABA RECEPTOR B (GABBR) ALSO INCREASED THE T CELL SUPPRESSIVE CAPACITY OF FEMALE GMDSCS THROUGH NITRIC OXIDE SYNTHASE 2 (NOS2)-MEDIATED PEROXYNITRITE FORMATION. FEMALE GBM PATIENTS HAD HIGHER INTRATUMORAL GABA CONCENTRATIONS AND MYELOID CELL GABBR EXPRESSION COMPARED TO MALE PATIENTS. FURTHERMORE, FEMALE MICE ADMINISTERED WITH A GABBR AGONIST SUCCUMBED TO GBM EARLIER, WHICH WAS MITIGATED BY THE DEPLETION OF GMDSCS OR TARGETING THE ARGININE-NOS2 SIGNALING AXIS. CONVERSELY, THE ANTAGONISM OF GABBR EXTENDED SURVIVAL OF FEMALE MICE, PROVIDING A TREATMENT OPPORTUNITY. BASED ON THESE OBSERVATIONS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SEX DIFFERENCES IN GABA RESPONSE INFORM GMDSC-MEDIATED GBM IMMUNOSUPPRESSION BY REWIRING ARGININE METABOLISM. SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT INHERENT SEX DIFFERENCES IN IMMUNOBIOLOGY INFORMS GBM INTERACTIONS AND GABA RESPONSE. SUB AIM 1A WILL SEEK TO DETERMINE THE HORMONAL VERSUS CHROMOSOMAL BASIS OF SEX-SPECIFIC GABA EFFECT ON GBM GROWTH AND IMMUNE RESPONSE USING A TRANSGENIC MOUSE MODEL. SUB-AIM 1B WILL DELINEATE THE CONTRIBUTION OF SEX CHROMOSOMES AND HORMONES ON GABA-MEDIATED METABOLIC, AND FUNCTIONAL REPROGRAMMING OF MDSCS. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT GABA DRIVES GBM IN FEMALES VIA THE L-ARG-PEROXYNITRITE AXIS. SUB- AIM 2A WILL EXAMINE THE ROLE GMDSC GABBR EXPRESSION AND L-ARG ACCUMULATION IN MODULATING THE GBM TME, SIGNALING, AND ANTI-TUMOR IMMUNE RESPONSE. SUB-AIM 2B WILL INTERROGATE PEROXYNITRITE FORMATION AS A DOWNSTREAM EFFECTOR OF GABBR-DRIVEN GBM AND MODULATOR OF TUMOR-PROMOTING GMDSC FUNCTION. THESE STUDIES WILL HIGHLIGHT THE ROLE OF GABA SIGNALING AS A HOST MECHANISM THAT INFORMS MYELOID CELL BIOLOGY AND TUMOR-IMMUNE INTERACTIONS IN A SEX-SPECIFIC MANNER. SUCH FINDINGS WILL LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR USING GABA INHIBITORS AND PEROXYNITRITE SCAVENGERS FOR IMMUNOTHERAPY OF GBM BY ACCOUNTING FOR SEX AS A BIOLOGICAL VARIABLE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE IMPACT OF PHOTOPHOBIA ON DAILY LIGHT EXPOSURE IN ADOLESCENTS WITH MIGRAINE: A REAL-WORLD STUDY. - PROJECT SUMMARY PHOTOPHOBIA (I.E., LIGHT SENSITIVITY) IS ONE OF THE MOST COMMON AND DISABLING SYMPTOMS ASSOCIATED WITH MIGRAINE THAT IS PRESENT EVEN IN THE ABSENCE OF HEADACHE. THOSE WITH MIGRAINE REPORT AVOIDING HIGH-INTENSITY VISUAL ENVIRONMENTS, WHICH IS FURTHER ENCOURAGED BY HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS TO REDUCE SYMPTOMS. HOWEVER, IT IS UNKNOWN WHETHER LIGHT AVOIDANCE IS ADAPTIVE OR MALADAPTIVE. LIGHT AVOIDANCE MAY REDUCE SYMPTOMS IN THE MOMENT, BUT IT IS UNCLEAR IF IT ALSO LEADS TO PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT DECREASES IN LIGHT EXPOSURE THAT NEGATIVELY IMPACT SLEEP AND WORSEN LIGHT INTOLERANCE OVER TIME. THIS IS PARTICULARLY IMPORTANT FOR YOUNGER POPULATIONS WHEN LIFELONG HABITS ARE FORMING, AND WHERE EARLY INTERVENTION MAY BE MORE BENEFICIAL. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, WE WILL CONTINUOUSLY TRACK AMBIENT LIGHT EXPOSURE AND SLEEP DURING DAILY LIFE IN ADOLESCENTS WITH AND WITHOUT MIGRAINE USING WEARABLE DIGITAL BIOSENSORS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT MIGRAINE-RELATED PHOTOPHOBIA CAUSES MALADAPTIVE LIGHT AVOIDANCE, RESULTING IN SLEEP DISRUPTION AND WORSENED LIGHT INTOLERANCE. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL CONTINUOUSLY MEASURE DAILY LIGHT EXPOSURE AND SLEEP HABITS IN 75 ADOLESCENTS (13 – 21 YEARS OLD) WITH MIGRAINE-RELATED PHOTOPHOBIA AND 75 AGE-, SEX-, AND TIME-OF-YEAR- MATCHED MIGRAINE-FREE CONTROLS. WE WILL UTILIZE TWO BIOSENSORS TO SIMULTANEOUSLY COLLECT LIGHT AND SLEEP DATA: 1) THE CHEST-WORN ACTLUMUS LIGHT DOSIMETER THAT TAKES HIGH SPECTRAL RESOLUTION MEASUREMENTS ALLOWING US TO ISOLATE “BLUE” LIGHT THAT DRIVES CIRCADIAN PHOTOENTRAINMENT, 2) GENEACTIV ACTIGRAPHY WRISTWATCH THAT PRODUCES RELIABLE MEASUREMENTS RELATED TO SLEEP TIMING AND QUANTITY. RECORDINGS WILL OCCUR FOR TWO NON-VACATION 2-WEEK PERIODS WITHIN 2 MONTHS OF THE WINTER AND SUMMER SOLSTICE. WE WILL DETERMINE IF PHOTOPHOBIA RESULTS IN REDUCED DAILY LIGHT EXPOSURE BY COMPARING ADOLESCENTS WITH MIGRAINE-RELATED PHOTOPHOBIA TO THEIR MIGRAINE-FREE PEERS. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL DETERMINE IF DAILY FLUCTUATIONS IN PHOTOPHOBIA PRECEDE REDUCTIONS IN LIGHT EXPOSURE (AIM 1). TO EVALUATE IF PHOTOPHOBIA PRODUCES SLEEP DISRUPTION BY REDUCING DAILY LIGHT EXPOSURE, WE WILL COMPARE SLEEP MIDPOINT AND TOTAL SLEEP TIME ACROSS GROUPS AND DETERMINE IF DAILY REDUCTIONS IN LIGHT EXPOSURE PREDICT DELAYED SLEEP TIME AND SHORTER SLEEP DURATIONS (AIM 2). FINALLY, WE WILL DETERMINE IF SEASONAL REDUCTIONS IN LIGHT EXPOSURE AMPLIFY THE EFFECTS OF MIGRAINE-RELATED PHOTOPHOBIA BY COMPARING PHOTOPHOBIA AND LIGHT EXPOSURE NEAR THE WINTER AND SUMMER SOLSTICE IN THOSE WITH AND WITHOUT MIGRAINE (AIM 3). OUR COMBINED EXPERTISE IN PEDIATRIC HEADACHE, VISION NEUROSCIENCE, AND SLEEP RESEARCH PLACE US IN AN IDEAL POSITION TO PURSUE THIS WORK. REGARDLESS OF THE OUTCOME, THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE FUNDAMENTAL MEASUREMENTS THAT WILL DIRECTLY INFLUENCE PATIENT GUIDANCE ON WHETHER LIGHT AVOIDANCE IS HELPFUL OR HARMFUL. IT WILL ALSO PROVIDE FOUNDATIONAL MEASUREMENTS NEEDED TO DESIGN CLINICAL TRIALS THAT EITHER PRIORITIZE GRADED LIGHT EXPOSURE (E.G. INCREASING TIME SPENT OUTDOORS) OR LIGHT AVOIDANCE (E.G. LIGHT BLOCKING LENS USE).

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SINGLE-PULSE ELECTRICAL STIMULATION TO IMPROVE SURGICAL OUTCOMES IN DRUG-RESISTANT EPILEPSY - PROJECT SUMMARY  EPILEPSY IS A NEUROLOGICAL DISORDER AFFECTING NEARLY 1% OF THE GLOBAL POPULATION, WITH A SUBSTANTIAL PORTION OF PATIENTS EXPERIENCING PERSISTENT SEIZURES DESPITE TREATMENT WITH ANTI-EPILEPTIC MEDICATIONS. FOR PATIENTS WITH FOCAL SEIZURES, SURGICAL RESECTION OF EPILEPTOGENIC REGIONS CAN BE POTENTIALLY CURATIVE, BUT SUCCESS HEAVILY DEPENDS ON ACCURATE LOCALIZATION OF THE EPILEPTOGENIC NETWORKS RESPONSIBLE FOR SEIZURE GENERATION. SINGLE-PULSE ELECTRICAL STIMULATION (SPES) HAS EMERGED AS A TOOL FOR IDENTIFYING EPILEPTOGENIC NETWORKS BY ELICITING CORTICO- CORTICAL EVOKED POTENTIALS (CCEPS), WHICH REVEAL EFFECTIVE CONNECTIVITY BETWEEN BRAIN REGIONS. HOWEVER, SPES IS NOT YET WIDELY USED IN CLINICAL SETTINGS DUE TO THREE KEY LIMITATIONS: A LACK OF STANDARDIZED STIMULATION PROTOCOLS AND COMPARISON WITH ESTABLISHED INTERICTAL BIOMARKERS OF SEIZURE-GENERATING BRAIN REGIONS, AN INCOMPLETE CLINICAL INTUITION FOR CCEPS DUE TO SPARSE SAMPLING OF INTRACRANIAL EEG, AND THERE HAS BEEN LIMITED EXPLORATION OF CCEPS TO GUIDE OTHER DIAGNOSTIC TESTS IN EPILEPSY MEDICINE, SUCH AS STIMULATION-INDUCED SEIZURES. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO TACKLE THESE LIMITATIONS USING DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS AND CONTROL THEORY TO ENHANCE THE UTILITY OF SPES IN THE EPILEPSY CLINIC, THEREBY IMPROVING LOCALIZATION OF EPILEPTOGENIC NETWORKS AND INCREASING THE CHANCES OF POST-SURGICAL SEIZURE FREEDOM. TO DO THIS, WE WILL FIRST COMPARE THE LOCALIZATION EFFICACY FOR SPES-EVOKED BIOMARKERS IN COMPARISON WITH WELL-STUDIED INTERICTAL BIOMARKERS IN A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT OF 124 PATIENTS FROM FOUR LEVEL 4 EPILEPSY CENTERS (UAB, NEW YORK UNIVERSITY, JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY, AND THE UNIVERSITY OF PENNSYLVANIA). WE WILL THEN OPTIMIZE SPES PARAMETERS, SUCH AS PULSE AMPLITUDE, PULSE WIDTH, AND POLARITY, IN A PROSPECTIVE COHORT OF 50 PATIENTS AT UAB TO IDENTIFY THE MOST ROBUST PARAMETERS FOR LOCALIZING HYPEREXCITABLE REGIONS USING BOTH THE CCEP WAVEFORM AND HYPEREXCITABILITY METRICS DERIVED FROM THE DYNAMICAL NETWORK MODELS. NEXT, WE WILL USE AN INNOVATIVE BAYESIAN NEURAL NETWORK MODEL TO PREDICT EFFECTIVE CONNECTIONS FROM A SET OF STIMULATION SITES, PIONEERING A METHOD TO IMPUTE CCEP AMPLITUDES IN REGIONS NOT DIRECTLY SAMPLED WITH IEEG ELECTRODES. LASTLY, WE WILL USE A CCEP-DERIVED DYNAMICAL NETWORK MODEL TO PREDICT STIMULATION FREQUENCIES THAT MAY BE USED TO TRIGGER SEIZURES, INCREASING THE DIAGNOSTIC YIELD FROM PATIENTS UNDERGOING INTRACRANIAL MONITORING. BY REFINING SPES PROTOCOLS AND DERIVING COMPLEMENTARY CLINICAL TESTS USING THE EVOKED RESPONSES, THIS WORK HAS THE POTENTIAL TO IMPROVE THE ACCURACY OF EPILEPTOGENIC NETWORK LOCALIZATION, DRASTICALLY REDUCE THE TIME PATIENTS SPEND IN THE HOSPITAL FOR INTRACRANIAL MONITORING, AND INCREASE THE LIKELIHOOD OF SEIZURE FREEDOM AFTER SURGICAL INTERVENTION. SUCCESSFUL OUTCOMES FROM THIS STUDY COULD BE PARADIGM-SHIFTING FOR THE DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT OF EPILEPSY, ULTIMATELY ENHANCING CLINICAL CARE FOR THIS HIGH-RISK PATIENT POPULATION.

description: MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION AND INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINE SECRETION AS MECHANISMS DRIVING CNS CONSEQUENCES OF INTERMITTENT EXPOSURE TO PATHOGENS - INCREASED APPRECIATION FOR CHRONIC MANIFESTATIONS OF INFECTION EXPOSURE, AND THE HOST INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE TO INFECTION, HAS REVEALED NOVEL FACTORS THAT COULD DRIVE NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE SUCH AS DEMENTIA AND EXCITING OPPORTUNITIES FOR PREVENTION OF THESE DEVASTATING CONDITIONS. INDEED, A ROBUST LITERATURE HAS DOCUMENTED CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) MANIFESTATIONS WITH EXPOSURE TO A PATHOGEN BOTH DURING ACUTE SICKNESS AND IN THE LONG- TERM RECOVERY PERIOD. FOR INSTANCE, WE HAVE PRELIMINARY DATA THAT INTERMITTENT VIRUS EXPOSURE IMPAIRS COGNITION, ALTERS BRAIN MICROVESSEL ENERGY METABOLISM, INDUCES NEUROINFLAMMATION, INCREASES HIPPOCAMPAL BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER PERMEABILITY, AND RESULTS IN DISTINCT TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC PROFILES RELATIVE TO AGE-MATCHED. WHILE ACCUMULATING EVIDENCE SUPPORTS CHRONIC NEUROINFLAMMATION (VIA ACTIVATED MICROGLIA AND A PROINFLAMMATORY CYTOKINE MILIEU) AS A MECHANISM BY WHICH INFECTION EXPERIENCE PERTURBS BRAIN FUNCTION, THE EXTENT TO WHICH NEUROINFLAMMATION REPRESENTS A CONVERGENCE POINT THROUGH WHICH DIVERSE PATHOGEN SUBTYPES POTENTIAL INDUCE THEIR EFFECTS REMAINS UNKNOWN. FOR THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM, IN EXPLORING THE INTERACTION BETWEEN INFECTION HISTORY, NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE VULNERABILITY, AND BOTH SYSTEMIC AND NEUROINFLAMMATION, WE WILL CONTRIBUTE FUNDAMENTAL AND CRITICALLY NEEDED KNOWLEDGE REGARDING THE CHRONIC BRAIN AND BEHAVIOR IMPACTS OF EXPOSURE TO DISTINCT PATHOGEN SUBTYPES. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE WILL 1) INVESTIGATE VIRAL INFECTION CONTRIBUTIONS TO LONG-TERM BRAIN AND BEHAVIOR FUNCTION IN NORMAL AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE MOUSE MODELS, 2) CHARACTERIZE TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC PROFILES OF DISTINCT POPULATIONS OF PATHOGEN-EXPOSED CELLS IN THE BRAIN, 3) INTERROGATE MICROGLIA AND INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES AS MECHANISMS DRIVING THESE NEUROLOGICAL CONSEQUENCES, 4) DISCERN THE EXTENT TO NEUROTROPISM AND PATHOGEN SUBTYPE IS REQUIRED FOR THESE EFFECTS. OUR APPROACH IS INNOVATIVE AS OUR RECURRENT INFECTION EXPOSURE REGIMEN REPRESENTS A DEPARTURE FROM THE SCIENTIFIC STATUS QUO AND MORE TRANSLATIONALLY MIMICS HUMAN SYSTEMIC INFECTION EXPERIENCE DURING ADULTHOOD. FURTHER, IT LEVERAGES CUTTING-EDGE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS TO COMPREHENSIVELY EXAMINE PATHOGEN-INDUCED TRANSCRIPTOMIC PROFILE SHITS AT A SUB-CELLULAR LEVEL IN BRAIN AND REVEAL NEW TARGETS. FINALLY, OUR USE OF BOTH NEUROTROPIC AND PERIPHERALLY-RESTRICTED INFECTIONS WILL ENABLE US TO DISCERN THE EXTENT TO WHICH DIFFERENT PATHOGENS CONVERGE ON SIMILAR TARGETS TO INDUCE CNS EFFECTS. OUR ACCOMPLISHED INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH TEAM OF EXPERTS IN NEUROSCIENCE, INFECTIOUS DISEASE, IMMUNOLOGY, AND NEUROLOGICAL DISEASES IS WELL-POISED TO CARRY OUT THE PROPOSED STUDIES. MORE BROADLY, A KEY COMPONENT OF THIS PROGRAM IS IN PAIRING OUR IMPACTFUL RESEARCH WITH EFFORTS TO ENGAGE KEY STAKEHOLDERS IN THE COMMUNITY THROUGH OUR ROBUST AND ESTABLISHED NEUROSCIENCE OUTREACH INITIATIVES. THESE ACTIVITIES REPRESENT A PRIORITY FOR THE NINDS AS WELL AS THE MILLIONS OF PATIENTS, CAREGIVERS, AND CLINICIANS SHOULDERING THE BURDEN OF INFECTION-INDUCED CHRONIC DISEASE.  DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AUTOMATED PROGRAMMING FOR PERSONALIZED DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION IN PARKINSONS DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SUCCESSFUL IMPLEMENTATION OF DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION (DBS) FOR TREATMENT OF PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD) HINGES ON APPROPRIATE SELECTION OF STIMULATION PARAMETERS (CONTACT CONFIGURATION, AMPLITUDE, PULSE WIDTH, FREQUENCY) TO MAXIMIZE THERAPEUTIC BENEFIT AND MINIMIZE SIDE EFFECTS. THERE IS AN URGENT NEED TO DEVELOP MORE EFFICIENT PRO- GRAMMING METHODS TO EXPAND DBS ACCESS WHILE MAINTAINING AND POTENTIALLY IMPROVING CLINICAL OUTCOMES. OB- JECTIVE AND RAPIDLY MEASURABLE ELECTROPHYSIOLOGIC BIOMARKERS NOW EXIST THAT COULD GUIDE AUTOMATED SELECTION OF STIMULATION PARAMETERS USING MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS. DBS-LOCAL EVOKED POTENTIAL (DLEP), A BRAIN SIGNAL MEASURED FROM NON-STIMULATING CONTACTS ON THE DBS ELECTRODE, HAS EMERGED AS A PROMISING MARKER OF TARGET ENGAGEMENT AND THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY IN PD. THE MOST TROUBLESOME SIDE EFFECT OF DBS ARE MUSCLE CONTRACTIONS FROM INADVERTENT SPREAD OF STIMULATION WHICH CAN BE RECORDED AS MOTOR EVOKED POTENTIALS (MEP) FROM FACE AND LIMB MUSCLES. META-ACTIVE LEARNING (META-AL) IS A NOVEL REINFORCEMENT LEARNING METHOD THAT, BY USING A DATABASE OF PRIOR PATIENTS, CAN ACTIVELY SELECT PARAMETERS IN CLOSED-LOOP TO FIND OPTIMAL PATIENT-SPECIFIC PARAMETERS IN A FEW ITERATIONS THAT MAXIMIZE DLEP AND MINIMIZE MEP. THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE AN AUTOMATED DBS PROGRAMMING PLATFORM FOR PATIENTS WITH PD. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT META-AL IS BETTER THAN ALTER- NATIVE ALGORITHMS TO EFFICIENTLY OPTIMIZE DBS PARAMETERS, AND THAT DLEP AND MEP ARE SUPERIOR BIOMARKERS TO LOCAL FIELD POTENTIAL BETA POWER FOR THIS PURPOSE. A PRACTICAL, FULLY AUTOMATED DBS PROGRAMMING SYSTEM DOES NOT EXIST – OUR MULTI-DISCIPLINARY TEAM HAS THE ENGINEERING AND CLINICAL EXPERTISE TO ACHIEVE IT. IN AIM 1, WE WILL OPTIMIZE AND VALIDATE META-AL ALGORITHM FOR AUTOMATED DBS PROGRAMMING. WE WILL BUILD A SIMULATED TRAINING ENVIRONMENT BASED ON EXPERIMENTAL DATA TO TRAIN META-AL AND TO COMPARE ITS PERFORMANCE AGAINST OTHER ALGO- RITHMS. OUR ALGORITHM WILL GENERATE VISUAL BIOMARKER RESPONSE MAPS DEPICTING THE TRADE-OFF BETWEEN THERAPEUTIC BENEFIT, SIDE-EFFECT RISK, AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DEPLOY META-AL ALGORITHM INTRAOPERATIVELY TO FIND PATIENT-SPECIFIC OPTIMAL DBS PARAMETERS. WE WILL REFINE TECHNICAL INFRASTRUCTURE TO DEPLOY META-AL IN CLOSED-LOOP DURING DBS SURGERY. WE WILL TEST THE ALGORITHM IN 40 PATIENTS WITH PD (20 SUBTHALAMIC; 20 PALLIDAL NUCLEUS TARGET). IN AIM 3, WE WILL EVALUATE THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY OF SELECTED OPTIMAL STIMULATION PARAMETERS AND COMPARE THEM TO CLINICALLY OPTIMIZED SETTINGS AND TO SETTINGS BASED ON BETA POWER. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL CONDUCT A 4-WEEK AT-HOME TESTING TO ASSESS LONG-TERM EFFICACY OF BIOMARKER-BASED STIMULATION. FINALLY, WE WILL EXPLORE HOW CLINICIANS INTER- ACT WITH AI OUTPUT TO SUPPORT AND IMPROVE CLINICIAN/MACHINE DECISION-MAKING. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PRO- JECT WILL CREATE A SET OF NOVEL ALGORITHMS AND DEFINE NECESSARY REAL-TIME RECORDING/STIMULATION PROCEDURES TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL. THE END PRODUCT WILL BE A PRACTICAL, FULLY AUTOMATED DBS PROGRAMMING SYSTEM THAT WILL BE DEPLOYABLE IN CLINICAL PRACTICE AND IN CLINICAL TRIALS COMPARING CONVENTIONAL AND AUTOMATED DBS PROGRAMMING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LRP8 AND APOLIPOPROTEIN E ALLELE-SPECIFIC MODULATION OF NEURAL REPAIR - PROJECT SUMMARY ADULT CNS TRAUMA FREQUENTLY CAUSES NEURONAL DISCONNECTION AND PERSISTENT DEFICITS DUE TO FAILED AXON REGENERATION. FOR TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY (TBI), THIS INCLUDES COGNITIVE DEFICITS AS WELL AS PROGRESSIVE DYSFUNCTION IN CHRONIC TRAUMATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY (CTE). FOR SPINAL CORD INJURY (SCI), MOTOR, SENSORY AND AUTONOMIC DEFICITS FAIL TO RESOLVE, CAUSING LIFE-LONG DISABILITY. WHILE MODEL SYSTEM SCREENING HAS IDENTIFIED MULTIPLE CANDIDATE NEURAL REPAIR PATHWAYS, APOE–LRP8 SIGNALING IS UNIQUE IN ALSO BEING IMPLICATED CLINICALLY. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT CORTICAL AXON REGENERATION REQUIRES LRP8 AND IS MODIFIED BY APOE VARIANTS. APOE2-EXPRESSING MICE SHOW REPARATIVE CORTICOSPINAL AND RAPHESPINAL AXON GROWTH WITH GREATER MOTOR FUNCTION THAN CONTROLS AFTER SCI. DISTINCT FROM APOE IN OTHER SETTINGS, THERE IS NO CHANGE IN INFLAMMATION OR SCARRING. AFTER AXOTOMY, APOE EXERTS ALLELE- SPECIFIC EFFECTS ON LRP8 LOCALIZATION AND SIGNALING IN CORTICAL NEURONS. APOE ALLELES REGULATE SYNAPTIC ORGANIZATION GENE EXPRESSION BY CORTICAL NEURONS AFTER INJURY, WITH LITTLE EFFECT ON GLIAL GENE EXPRESSION. THUS, THIS PROJECT HAS IDENTIFIED A ROLE FOR APOE–LRP8 SIGNALING IN THE SUCCESS OF AXON REGROWTH FOLLOWING CNS TRAUMA OF RELEVANCE FOR TBI AND SCI. WE AIM TO EXPLORE THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL OF TARGETING THIS PATHWAY FOR NEURAL REPAIR. IN PRELIMINARY STUDIES WITH AAV-APOE2 INJECTION AFTER TRAUMA, WE OBSERVED ROBUST INCREASES IN AXONAL GROWTH AND RECOVERY AFTER SCI. WE WILL EXTEND THESE FINDINGS BY DELAYING AAV ADMINISTRATION TO THE CHRONIC PHASE AFTER SPINAL CORD CONTUSION AND BY ASSESSING SYSTEMIC DELIVERY. WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE THE CELLULAR MECHANISM OF LRP8–APOE ACTION IN NEURAL REPAIR. WE WILL USE LRP8 NULL MICE AND STUDY GENES THAT ARE DIFFERENTIALLY EXPRESSED IN RESPONSE TO APOE2 AND SCI. ONE TARGET OF LRP8 SIGNALING IS SRC KINASE. WE WILL DETERMINE THE POTENTIAL FOR SRC KINASE INHIBITION TO ACHIEVE NEURAL REPAIR AFTER SCI. THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL UTILIZE AN ORALLY AVAILABLE BRAIN- PENETRANT KINASE INHIBITOR WITH A DIRECT PATH TO CLINICAL TRANSLATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HIGH-EFFICIENCY DEVELOPMENT OF RED GENETICALLY-ENCODED CALCIUM SENSORS USING MACHINE-LEARNING-GUIDED SCREENING AND IN VIVO VALIDATION - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT MONITORING NEURAL ACTIVITY WITH GENETICALLY ENCODED CALCIUM INDICATORS (GECIS) IS A CORNERSTONE OF MODERN NEUROSCIENCE, YET RED FLUORESCENT GECIS REMAIN SUBOPTIMAL COMPARED TO THEIR GREEN COUNTERPARTS. CURRENT RED GECIS, SUCH AS JRCAMP1 AND JRGECO1, SUFFER FROM LIMITATIONS IN BRIGHTNESS, DYNAMIC RANGE (∆F/F0), KINETICS, AND PHOTOSTABILITY, RESTRICTING THEIR USE IN DEEP-BRAIN IMAGING AND DUAL-COLOR EXPERIMENTS. ADDITIONALLY, BLUE-LIGHT PHOTOACTIVATION ARTIFACTS IN RED GECIS COMPLICATE MULTIPLEXED IMAGING WITH OPTOGENETIC ACTUATORS. A SIGNIFICANT BOTTLENECK IN IMPROVING RED GECIS IS THE SLOW, LABOR-INTENSIVE PROCESS OF ITERATIVE PROTEIN ENGINEERING. OUR CENTRAL GOAL IS TO OVERCOME THESE BARRIERS AND ENGINEER NEXT-GENERATION RED GECIS WITH ENHANCED BIOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES THAT MATCH OR EXCEED THE PERFORMANCE OF THE BEST GREEN GECIS. WE PROPOSE AN INTEGRATED, INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACH GUIDED BY THREE SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 FOCUSES ON USING MACHINE LEARNING (ML)-DRIVEN OPTIMIZATION TO PREDICT SINGLE-SITE MUTATIONS THAT IMPROVE BRIGHTNESS, CALCIUM SENSITIVITY, DECAY KINETICS, AND DYNAMIC RANGE OF RGECIS. THESE ML PREDICTIONS, TRAINED ON ~1,000 CHARACTERIZED VARIANTS DATASETS, WILL GUIDE TARGETED ENGINEERING EFFORTS, SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCING THE EXPERIMENTAL BURDEN. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ACCELERATE OPTIMIZATION BY CONSTRUCTING COMBINATORIAL MUTATIONAL LIBRARIES AT UP TO FOUR KEY SITES IDENTIFIED VIA ML AND SCREENING THESE LIBRARIES USING OUR HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING PLATFORM, CAPABLE OF FUNCTIONALLY EVALUATING THOUSANDS OF VARIANTS WITHIN HOURS. THIS AIM WILL GENERATE SYNERGISTIC MUTATION COMBINATIONS THAT PRODUCE SUPERIOR RED GECIS BEYOND WHAT SINGLE MUTATIONS CAN ACHIEVE. FINALLY, IN AIM 3, WE WILL RIGOROUSLY VALIDATE THE OPTIMIZED RED GECIS IN VIVO USING TWO-PHOTON AND THREE-PHOTON MICROSCOPY IN AWAKE AND ANESTHETIZED MICE AND RATS. THIS WILL COMPREHENSIVELY VALIDATE THEIR RESPONSE AMPLITUDES, KINETICS, AND SIGNAL-TO-NOISE RATIOS ACROSS MULTIPLE IMAGING CONDITIONS AND CORTICAL AND SUBCORTICAL BRAIN REGIONS. OUR PROJECT IS HIGHLY INNOVATIVE, AS IT UNIQUELY INTEGRATES ML-DRIVEN PREDICTIONS WITH RAPID EXPERIMENTAL VALIDATION, ACCELERATING SENSOR OPTIMIZATION WHILE MINIMIZING THE INEFFICIENCIES OF TRADITIONAL TRIAL-AND-ERROR APPROACHES. WE WILL ESTABLISH A ROBUST OPTIMIZATION PIPELINE THAT CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVES PREDICTIVE ACCURACY AND SENSOR PERFORMANCE BY ITERATIVELY REFINING OUR ML MODELS BASED ON EXPERIMENTAL FEEDBACK. THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE THE NEUROSCIENCE COMMUNITY WITH NEXT-GENERATION RED GECIS THAT MATCH OR SURPASS GREEN GECIS, ENABLING HIGH-FIDELITY DUAL-COLOR IMAGING, DEEP-BRAIN CALCIUM IMAGING, AND ADVANCED FUNCTIONAL IMAGING IN PREVIOUSLY INACCESSIBLE EXPERIMENTAL CONTEXTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INHIBITION OF ERYTHROCYTE FERROPTOSIS AS A THERAPEUTIC TARGET AFTER INTRACEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE - PROJECT SUMMARY INTRACEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE (ICH) REMAINS A DISEASE WITH HIGH MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY AND WITHOUT EFFECTIVE TREATMENT. THERE HAS BEEN IMPORTANT FOCUS ON PREVENTION OF IRON-INDUCED INJURY IN THE BRAIN AFTER ICH, BUT SURPRISINGLY LITTLE ATTENTION TO THE MECHANISMS OF ERYTHROCYTE DEATH AND HEMOLYSIS WITHIN THE HEMATOMA THAT LEADS TO THE RELEASE OF HEMOGLOBIN, HEME, AND IRON. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL EXAMINE THE IRON-INDUCED PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH (FERROPTOSIS) OF ERYTHROCYTES, A UNIQUE CELL TYPE WITHOUT NUCLEI OR MITOCHONDRIA. BASED ON PRELIMINARY DATA, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT HEME INDUCES ERYTHROCYTE FERROPTOSIS, LEADING TO CELL SWELLING AND A COORDINATED FORMATION OF CELL MEMBRANE PORES IN A HIGHLY REGULATED SERIES OF EVENTS. WE WILL TEST CANDIDATE CAUSAL PATHWAYS AND PHARMACOLOGICAL INHIBITORS TO REDUCE OR DELAY ERYTHROCYTE LYSIS AND IMPROVE OUTCOMES AFTER ICH.

description: ASSOCIATIONS OF TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY ACROSS THE LIFE COURSE WITH LATER-LIFECOGNITIVE DECLINE AND DEMENTIA RISK: A POOLED COHORT STUDY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY (TBI) IS A RECOGNIZED RISK FACTOR FOR ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (AD) AND AD RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRDS), BUT THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS AND TIME COURSE OVER WHICH TBI INCREASES THE RISK FOR AD/ADRDS ARE NOT WELL UNDERSTOOD. SUCH INFORMATION IS CRITICAL FOR DEVELOPING EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE AD/ADRD RISK AFTER TBI. NEUROTRAUMA MAY CONTRIBUTE DIRECTLY TO AD/ADRD RISK BY ACCELERATING NEURODEGENERATIVE PROCESSES ALREADY ONGOING AT THE TIME OF INJURY OR BY INITIATING DE NOVO NEURODEGENERATIVE PROCESSES. TBI MAY ALSO CONTRIBUTE INDIRECTLY IN AN ADDITIVE OR SYNERGISTIC MANNER TO AD/ADRD RISK IN COMBINATION WITH PRE-EXISTING OR POST-INJURY DEVELOPMENT OF VASCULAR-RELATED DEMENTIA RISK FACTORS (E.G., HYPERTENSION, DIABETES), WHICH MAY INFLUENCE COGNITIVE TRAJECTORIES AFTER TBI. THE OVERARCHING OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO LEVERAGE EXISTING DATA FROM 4 NIH-FUNDED ONGOING PROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDIES WITH DECADES OF FOLLOW-UP TO GAIN PREVENTATIVE AND MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO POST-TBI AD/ADRD. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT TBI IS ASSOCIATED WITH AD/ADRD RISK BY DIRECT NEURODEGENERATIVE PATHWAYS AND BY ADDITIVE OR SYNERGISTIC INDIRECT PATHWAYS (I.E., IN COMBINATION WITH OTHER DEMENTIA RISK FACTORS) THAT MAY DIFFER OVER THE LIFE COURSE. GUIDED BY ROBUST PRELIMINARY DATA, THEEXPERIENCED RESEARCH TEAM WILLTEST THIS HYPOTHESIS VIA THREE SPECIFIC AIMS.AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF CUMULATIVE TBI EXPOSURE OVER THE LIFE COURSE ON COGNITIVE TRAJECTORIES AND AD/ADRD RISK. AIM 2 WILL QUANTIFY THE INFLUENCE OF PRE- AND POST-INJURY VASCULAR RISK FACTOR COMORBIDITIES ON ASSOCIATIONS OF TBI EXPOSURE OVER THE LIFE COURSE WITH COGNITIVE TRAJECTORIES AND AD/ADRD RISK. AIM 3 WILL IDENTIFY POTENTIAL MECHANISMS FOR POST-TBIAD/ADRD BY EVALUATING ASSOCIATIONS OF TBI EXPOSURE WITH BLOOD-BASED AND BRAIN MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING BIOMARKERS OF NEURODEGENERATION AND VASCULAR DISEASE. AIMS 1 AND 2 WILL IDENTIFY HIGH-RISK POPULATION SUBGROUPS AND MODIFIABLE TARGETS FOR FUTURE POST-TBI AD/ADRD PREVENTION STRATEGIES WHILE AIM 3 WILL PROVIDE MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS. TO ADDRESS THESE SPECIFIC AIMS, WE WILL US AN ACCELERATED LONGITUDINAL (COHORT-SEQUENTIAL) DESIGN AND WILL POOL, HARMONIZE, AND ANALYZE INDIVIDUAL DATA FROM OVER 40,000 PARTICIPANTS ENROLLED IN 4 U.S. LONGITUDINAL STUDIES CHOSEN TO COVER THE LIFESPAN WITH BASELINE AGES OF 12 TO 84 YEARS AND 25 TO 40+ YEARS FOLLOW-UP: 1) THE NATIONAL LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF ADOLESCENT TO ADULT HEALTH (ADD HEALTH), 2) THE ATHEROSCLEROSIS RISK IN COMMUNITIES (ARIC) STUDY, 3) THE CORONARY ARTERY RISK DEVELOPMENT IN YOUNG ADULTS (CARDIA) STUDY, AND 4) THE MULTI-ETHNIC STUDY OF ATHEROSCLEROSIS (MESA). THE PROPOSED STUDY IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT WILL COST- EFFECTIVELY LEVERAGE EXISTING DATA TO CREATE A NEW POOLED DATASET OF UNPRECEDENTED SIZE WITH REPEATED HARMONIZED MEASURES OF TBI, VASCULAR RISK FACTORS, AND AD/ADRD-RELATED BIOMARKERS AND OUTCOMES OVER THE LIFE COURSE. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE THE KNOWLEDGE GAINED WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE STRATEGIES TO PREVENT AD/ADRDS AND PRESERVE COGNITION AMONG INDIVIDUALS WITH TBI.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NOVEL NON-VIRAL GBA1 GENE THERAPY FOR PARKINSON'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD) IS A PROGRESSIVE NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY THE LOSS OF DOPAMINERGIC (DA) NEURONS, LEADING TO SEVERE MOTOR IMPAIRMENTS AND DISABILITY. WHILE THE CURRENT STAND-OF-CARE TREATMENTS, LIKE LEVODOPA, OFFER SYMPTOMATIC RELIEF, THEY DO NOT STOP OR REVERSE NEURODEGENERATION. THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPIES TARGETING THE ROOT CAUSES OF PD. BOTH MUTATIONS IN THE GCASE-ENCODING GBA1 GENE AND MUTATION-FREE REDUCTION OF GCASE ACTIVITY INCREASE THE RISK OF PD AND DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES (DLB), AS GCASE DEFICIENCY PROMOTES TOXIC GLYCOLIPID BUILDUP AND Α-SYNUCLEIN AGGREGATION, THEREBY DISRUPTING ESSENTIAL CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ENHANCE GCASE ACTIVITY IN THE MIDBRAIN VIA SYSTEMIC GBA1 GENE THERAPY USING A COMPLEMENTARY DELIVERY STRATEGY, COMPRISING FOCUSED ULTRASOUND (FUS)-MEDIATED BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER (BBB) OPENING AND BARRIER-BREACHING BIODEGRADABLE NANOPARTICLES (NPS), AND PROMOTER OPTIMIZATION. THIS APPROACH ADDRESSES THE LIMITATIONS OF ADENO-ASSOCIATED VIRUSES, SUCH AS LIVER TOXICITY, IMMUNOGENICITY, LIMITED PACKAGING CAPACITY, AND ENORMOUS COSTS, WHILE ENABLING EFFICIENT GENE TRANSFER TO THE TARGET BRAIN AREA VIA A MINIMALLY INVASIVE ADMINISTRATION ROUTE FOR DISEASE-MODIFYING INTERVENTION. BASED ON OUR PILOT DATA SHOWING THAT INTRACRANIAL ADMINISTRATION OF OUR PATENTED NPS CARRYING GBA1 PLASMID REDUCES LB-LIKE PATHOLOGY AND MOTOR SYMPTOMS IN AN Α-SYNUCLEIN PREFORMED FIBRIL (PFF)-INDUCED MOUSE MODEL OF SPORADIC PD, IN AIM 1, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE EXPRESSION AND SAFETY OF GBA1 PLASMIDS WITH DIFFERENT PROMOTERS DELIVERED VIA OUR NPS, ADMINISTERED EITHER LOCALLY THROUGH CONVECTION-ENHANCED DELIVERY OR SYSTEMICALLY VIA TAIL VEIN INJECTION COMBINED WITH FUS-MEDIATED BBB OPENING. WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE PHYSICOCHEMICAL PROPERTIES AND PHYSIOLOGICAL STABILITY OF THESE NPS AND EVALUATE THE DOSE-DEPENDENT GBA1 TRANSGENE EXPRESSION AND LOCAL AND SYSTEMIC SAFETY PROFILES IN HEALTHY MOUSE BRAINS THROUGH IMAGING, BIOCHEMICAL, AND HISTOLOGICAL TECHNIQUES TO DETERMINE OPTIMAL DOSING. IN AIM 2, WE WILL USE GENETICALLY DEFINED AND CLINICALLY RELEVANT HUMAN CELL MODELS - INCLUDING CRISPR- EDITED SH-SY5YL444P/+ KNOCK-IN CELLS AND Α-SYNUCLEIN PFF-TREATED IPSC-DERIVED DA NEURONS FROM PD PATIENTS WITH AND WITHOUT GBA1 MUTATIONS - TO EVALUATE THE NEUROPROTECTIVE MECHANISMS OF NON-VIRAL GBA1 THERAPY. UNLIKE PRIOR STUDIES USING OVEREXPRESSION OR TOXIN-BASED MODELS, THIS AIM UTILIZES DISEASE-RELEVANT SYSTEMS AND INTEGRATES ADVANCED TRANSCRIPTOMIC AND LIPIDOMIC PROFILING TO UNCOVER DOWNSTREAM PATHWAYS AND IDENTIFY BIOMARKERS OF THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE. IN AIM 3, WE WILL EVALUATE THE THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS OF GBA1 GENE THERAPY IN THE PFF-INDUCED MOUSE MODELS OF PD WITH OR WITHOUT THE L444P GBA1 MUTATION, COMPARING INTRACRANIAL AND SYSTEMIC DELIVERY METHODS DESCRIBED ABOVE. WE WILL ASSESS MOTOR DEFICITS, DA NEURON LOSS, LEWY BODY PATHOLOGY, AND NEUROINFLAMMATION THROUGH BEHAVIORAL ASSAYS, BIOCHEMICAL ANALYSES, AND HISTOLOGICAL ANALYSES, AS WELL AS OMICS PROFILING. THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A FOUNDATION FOR THE ULTIMATE CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT OF NON-VIRAL DISEASE- MODIFYING GENE THERAPY FOR BOTH GBA1-RELATED AND IDIOPATHIC PD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EFFECT OF APOE GENOTYPE ON ENOS REGULATION AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF VCID - VASCULAR CONTRIBUTIONS TO COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA (VCID) OCCURS WHEN THE CEREBROVASCULATURE CAN NO LONGER MAINTAIN HOMEOSTASIS UNDER METABOLIC, ENVIRONMENTAL, GENETIC AND NEURODEGENERATIVE INSULTS, INCLUDING LATE-ONSET ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (LOAD). CEREBROVASCULAR FUNCTION RELIES ON ENDOTHELIAL NITRIC OXIDE SYNTHASE (ENOS) ACTIVITY, WHICH MAINTAINS ENDOTHELIAL HOMEOSTASIS, NO BIOAVAILABILITY, AND VASCULAR INTEGRITY. DYSREGULATED ENOS ACTIVITY DRIVES ENDOTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION, AND ENOS DEFICIENT MICE DEVELOP SEVERAL HALLMARKS OF VCID PATHOLOGY, INCLUDING HYPOPERFUSION, BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER (BBB) BREAKDOWN, CEREBRAL AMYLOID ANGIOPATHY, TAU PATHOLOGY, WHITE MATTER DAMAGE, AND COGNITIVE DECLINE, SUGGESTING A CENTRAL ROLE FOR ENOS IN VCID AND LOAD PROGRESSION. THE NOS3 AND APOE4 (APOLIPOPROTEIN E4) GENES ARE THE ONLY CONSISTENT GENETIC FACTOR INFLUENCING THE RISK AND PROGRESSION OF BOTH LOAD AND CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE. INTRIGUINGLY, RECENT STUDIES HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT LOAD-ASSOCIATED VASCULAR DECLINE IS MEDIATED BY ENOS DYSREGULATION IN AN APOE GENOTYPE DEPENDENT MANNER, SUGGESTING THAT APOE ISOFORMS MAY DIFFERENTIALLY INFLUENCE ENOS HOMEOSTASIS TO DRIVE VCID, THOUGH THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES SHOW THAT APOE PLAYS A CONSTITUTIVE ROLE IN MAINTAINING ENOS HOMEOSTASIS AND NO BIOAVAILABILITY IN BRAIN ENDOTHELIA. HOWEVER, APOE4 SIGNIFICANTLY IMPAIRS ENOS ACTIVITY, AND ACCELERATES MICROVASCULAR DYSFUNCTION, PARTICULARLY IN THE PRESENCE OF VCID STRESSORS, LEADING TO ENDOTHELIAL SENESCENCE, WHICH MAY DESCRIBE THE INCREASED PREVALENCE AND ACCELERATED DISEASE PROGRESSION OBSERVED IN APOE4 CARRIERS. THIS PROJECT WILL TAKE A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH IN DETERMINING THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH APOE GENOTYPE AND LOAD CONDITIONS (E.G., WESTERN DIET, PATHOGENIC AMYLOID/TAU) INFLUENCE ENOS STABILIZATION (AIM 1), AND THE RESULTING IMPACT OF ENOS DYSREGULATION ON CEREBROVASCULAR IMPAIRMENT (AIM 2) AND VCID PROGRESSION (AIM 3). TO ADDRESS THESE AIMS, THIS PROJECT WILL USE A MULTI-MODAL APPROACH IN DETERMINING THE EFFECT OF APOE GENOTYPE ON ENOS HOMEOSTASIS UNDER LOAD CONDITIONS INCLUDING: APOE EXPOSURE AND ENOS MODULATION IN BRAIN ENDOTHELIA, IN VITRO BBB INTEGRITY AND TRANSIT USING A 3D BRAIN-CHIP MODULE, IN VIVO ASSESSMENTS OF CEREBROVASCULAR ABNORMALITIES, CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW, AND BBB INTEGRITY, ALONGSIDE EVALUATIONS OF WASTE ELIMINATION AND VCID PATHOLOGY IN LOAD MICE. AT EACH OF THESE STAGES, TO STRATEGICALLY TARGET ENOS, WE WILL EMPLOY BOTH PHARMACOLOGIC AND GENETIC APPROACHES, USING A WELL CHARACTERIZED ENOS ENHANCING PEPTIDE (CAVNOXIN), ALONGSIDE ESTABLISHED ENOS MOUSE MODELS, WHICH DISPLAY CONSTITUTIVELY ENHANCED OR INHIBITED ENOS ACTIVITY. IN THE SHORT TERM, THIS PROJECT WILL NOT ONLY ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLE OF APOE GENOTYPE AND ENOS DYSREGULATION ON CEREBROVASCULAR DECLINE BUT WILL ALSO SHED LIGHT ON THE MOLECULAR UNDERPINNINGS DRIVING THE ONSET AND PROGRESSION OF VCID AND LOAD. IN THE LONG TERM, IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT THE FINDINGS FROM THIS PROJECT WILL FACILITATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS AND STRATEGIES TO TREAT NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS.

description: DETERMINING THE STOICHIOMETRY OF ENDOGENOUS VOLTAGE-GATED POTASSIUM CHANNELS IN THE BRAIN - PROJECT SUMMARY FOR NEURONS TO ACT AS THE BASIC UNIT OF INFORMATION INTEGRATION UNDERLYING ALL COGNITIVE BEHAVIORS, ION CHANNELS ARE THE ESSENTIAL MOLECULES FOR ELECTRICAL SIGNALING, INFORMATION INTEGRATION, AND CELL-CELL COMMUNICATION. TO DECODE THE BRAIN, WE MUST UNDERSTAND HOW CHANNEL PROPERTIES ARE REGULATED. BECAUSE MOST ION CHANNELS ARE FORMED AS ASSEMBLIES OF MULTIPLE PROTEINS/SUBUNITS, ACHIEVING FULL UNDERSTANDING OF NATIVE ION CHANNELS CALLS FOR A COMPREHENSIVE BLUEPRINT OF THE TYPES AND ARRANGEMENT OF EACH SUBUNIT UNDER PHYSIOLOGICAL AND PATHOLOGICAL CONDITIONS. THIS IMPORTANT KNOWLEDGE IS LACKING FOR NEARLY ALL TYPES OF NATIVE ION CHANNELS DUE TO THE LIMITATION IN TECHNOLOGY. MANY FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS CONCERNING ENDOGENOUS ION CHANNEL ASSEMBLIES REMAIN UNSOLVED. WHAT ARE THE COMPOSITIONS OF ENDOGENOUS ION CHANNELS IN NEURONS IN VIVO? HOW ARE THE COMPOSITIONS OF THE CHANNELS REGULATED BY PHYSIOLOGICAL STIMULI OR ALTERED IN PATHOLOGICAL CONDITIONS? CAN WE FIND DRUGS THAT ONLY TARGET THE MISASSEMBLED CHANNELS THAT CAUSE THE DISEASE?  IN THIS PROPOSAL, I PLAN TO ELUCIDATE THE STOICHIOMETRY OF IN VIVO ENDOGENOUS VOLTAGE-GATED POTASSIUM (KV) CHANNELS USING A NOVEL STRATEGY THAT HAS BEEN DEVELOPING IN MY LAB. THE ACTIVATION OF EACH NEURON IS UNDER STRICT TEMPORAL CONTROL, WHICH IS PRIMARILY ESTABLISHED BY ENABLING ACTION POTENTIALS TO INITIATE AT A SPECIFIC THRESHOLD AND FIRE WITH AN ADEQUATE FREQUENCY AND PATTERN. KV CHANNELS ARE HENCE A CRUCIAL GROUP OF CHANNELS TO SET AND RESET A NEURON’S ELECTRICAL STATE. TO ESTABLISH THIS PRECISE CONTROL OF ELECTRICAL STATE, KV CHANNELS FORM HETERO-TETRAMERS WITH MULTIPLE TYPES AND ARRANGEMENTS OF SUBUNITS IN A SPATIOTEMPORALLY DEPENDENT MANNER. AS A MAJOR SUBFAMILY OF KV CHANNELS, KV1 FAMILY MEMBERS CONTROLS RESTING MEMBRANE POTENTIAL AND FIRING PATTERN OF ACTION POTENTIALS. INHERITED AND DE NOVO MUTATIONS OF KV1 FAMILY MEMBERS ARE DIRECTLY LINKED TO EPILEPSY AND EPISODIC ATAXIA TYPE- 1. WHEREAS KV1 MEMBERS CAN FORM HOMO-TETRAMERS OR HETERO-TETRAMERS IN VITRO, THEY MAINLY FORM HETERO- TETRAMERS IN THE BRAIN. THE COMPOSITION AND ARRANGEMENT OF KV1 CHANNELS CONTROL THEIR VOLTAGE DEPENDENCE OF ACTIVATION AND INACTIVATION AS WELL AS THEIR LIGAND BINDING AFFINITY. DETERMINATION OF THE STOICHIOMETRY OF IN VIVO ENDOGENOUS KV1 CHANNELS WILL PROVIDE A CRUCIAL FOUNDATION TO UNDERSTAND THE INFORMATION PROCESSES AMONG NEURONAL NETWORKS IN HEALTH AND DISEASES.  TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS, WE PLAN TO INVESTIGATE THE RANGE OF STOICHIOMETRIES OF KV1 CHANNELS IN MOUSE BRAINS AND TO ELUCIDATE THE STOICHIOMETRY OF KV1 CHANNELS IN MOUSE DISEASE MODELS. WE WILL EMPLOY MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACHES THAT COMBINE SINGLE PARTICLE CRYO-EM STUDIES OF KV1 CHANNELS FROM MOUSE BRAINS WITH IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY, PATCH-CLAMP ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY AND KNOCK-IN MOUSE LINES. THESE INVESTIGATIONS WILL SHED LIGHT ON THE FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES UNDERLYING HOW ENDOGENOUS ION CHANNELS ASSEMBLE AND FUNCTION IN HEALTH AND DISEASES. THESE STUDIES MAY ALSO MAKE IT POSSIBLE TO DESIGN NOVEL DRUGS THAT TARGET DISEASE-INDUCED CHANNEL ASSEMBLIES TO TREAT PATIENTS WITH NEUROLOGICAL OR PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS WHILE LIMITING SIDE-EFFECTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PAIRED STIMULATION PLASTICITY FOR MOTOR RECOVERY - CERVICAL SPINAL CORD INJURY (SCI) OFTEN IMPAIRS THE REACH AND GRASP MOVEMENTS WHICH ARE SO IMPORTANT TO INDEPENDENT LIVING. TARGETED NEURAL STIMULATION IS A PROMISING APPROACH TO ENHANCE NEURAL CONNECTIONS AND IMPROVE FUNCTION. THIS INVOLVES ACTIVATING DIFFERENT PARTS OF A NEURAL CIRCUIT USING PAIRED STIMULI. BY CHANGING THE PRECISE TIME BETWEEN THE TWO STIMULI, IT IS POSSIBLE TO INCREASE OR DECREASE CONNECTION STRENGTH. MANY STUDIES HAVE APPLIED THIS CONCEPT TO CORTICAL CIRCUITS, BUT COMPARATIVELY LITTLE ATTENTION HAS BEEN PAID TO THE POTENTIAL FOR SUB-CORTICAL PLASTICITY TO AID RECOVERY. WE KNOW THAT REACHING AND GRASPING MOVEMENTS INVOLVE COORDINATED CONTROL BY CORTICOSPINAL AND RETICULOSPINAL DESCENDING TRACTS, ORIGINATING IN THE CORTEX AND BRAINSTEM RESPECTIVELY. THUS, EXPLOITING PLASTICITY IN SUB-CORTICAL CIRCUITS COULD ACCESS NEW AVENUES TO IMPROVE REHABILITATION. THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON TWO PROMISING METHODS FOR INDUCING PLASTIC CHANGES IN SUB-CORTICAL CIRCUITS IN MONKEYS WITH AND WITHOUT SCI. SPINAL PAIRED ASSOCIATIVE STIMULATION (SPINAL PAS) INVOLVES PAIRING TRANSCRANIAL MAGNETIC STIMULATION (TMS) OF THE MOTOR CORTEX WITH SUPRAMAXIMAL STIMULATION OF A PERIPHERAL NERVE. STARTLE INVOLVES PAIRING TMS WITH A LOUD SOUND. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SPINAL PAS AND STARTLE ACT ON CORTICOSPINAL SYNAPSES AND THE CORTICO-RETICULOSPINAL SYSTEM RESPECTIVELY. THE FIRST AIM OF THE PROJECT IS TO UNDERSTAND THE MECHANISM OF ACTION OF THESE PROTOCOLS. EXPERIMENTS IN MONKEYS WILL DETERMINE DEFINITIVELY WHICH SYNAPSES ARE MODIFIED BY THESE PROTOCOLS, AND VALIDATE COMMON METHODS USED IN HUMANS FOR ASSESSING SUB-CORTICAL CIRCUITS. THIS INFORMATION WILL PERMIT THE PRINCIPLED COMBINATION OF THE TWO PROTOCOLS, ALLOWING THEM TO ACT SYNERGISTICALLY TO INCREASE THE EXTENT OF PLASTIC CHANGE. THE SECOND AIM OF THE PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP WAYS TO ENHANCE PLASTIC CHANGES. STUDIES IN MONKEYS WILL ASSESS WHETHER COMBINING STIMULATION WITH APPROPRIATE PHARMACOLOGICAL PRETREATMENT AND SPECIFIC TASKS CAN INCREASE PLASTICITY. THE OUTPUT OF THIS RESEARCH WILL BE A HIGHLY OPTIMIZED STIMULATION PROTOCOL WITH STRONG UNDERSTANDING OF ITS UNDERLYING MECHANISMS; THIS WILL BE READY FOR TRANSLATION INTO PEOPLE WITH SCI.

description: PHENOTYPES AND CLINICAL TRAJECTORIES OF POST-STROKE DELIRIUM - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT DELIRIUM IS AN ACUTE COGNITIVE DISORDER THAT AFFECTS MORE THAN ONE-THIRD OF HOSPITALIZED ELDERLY PATIENTS AND PORTENDS HIGHER RATES OF LONG-TERM DISABILITY AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT. HOWEVER, DELIRIUM AFTER STROKE REMAINS UNDERRECOGNIZED AND POORLY UNDERSTOOD DESPITE ITS HIGH PREVALENCE AND ADVERSE IMPLICATIONS FOR POST-STROKE RECOVERY. STROKE PATIENTS ARE UNIQUELY VULNERABLE TO THE RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH DELIRIUM: THEY ARE THE ONLY POPULATION IN WHICH DELIRIUM HAS BEEN IMPLICATED IN HEALTHCARE DECISION-MAKING LEADING TO WITHDRAWAL OF LIFE- SUSTAINING TREATMENT, AND IN WHICH DELIRIUM HAS BEEN SHOWN TO DIRECTLY INTERFERE WITH POST-ACUTE REHABILITATION PLACEMENT (A CAUSAL PATHWAY THAT ACCOUNTS FOR UP TO ONE-THIRD OF THE EFFECT OF POST-STROKE DELIRIUM ON OVERALL OUTCOMES). FURTHER, STROKE PATIENTS MAY HAVE DISTINCT DELIRIUM RISK FACTORS, MECHANISMS, AND PHENOTYPES THAT FUNDAMENTALLY DIFFER FROM THOSE IN NON-NEUROLOGICAL PATIENTS WITH DELIRIUM. THERE IS A CRITICAL GAP IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLE OF DELIRIUM IN ALTERING CLINICAL TRAJECTORIES AFTER STROKE, AND AN URGENT NEED TO STRATIFY PATIENTS TO IDENTIFY THOSE WHO CAN BENEFIT FROM AGGRESSIVE CARE AND REHABILITATION DESPITE THEIR DELIRIUM. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO RIGOROUSLY CHARACTERIZE A COMPREHENSIVE SPECTRUM OF PHENOTYPES AND CLINICAL TRAJECTORIES ASSOCIATED WITH POST-STROKE DELIRIUM. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT DISTINCT TEMPORAL, MOTOR, AND CLINICAL DELIRIUM PHENOTYPES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH DIFFERING TRAJECTORIES OF POST-STROKE RECOVERY, AND THAT NOVEL, PREVIOUSLY UNRECOGNIZED DATA-DERIVED PHENOTYPES CAN BE IDENTIFIED USING ADVANCED MACHINE LEARNING METHODS. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS IN A PROSPECTIVE COHORT OF 300 HIGH-RISK STROKE PATIENTS WHO WILL UNDERGO DAILY DELIRIUM ASSESSMENTS USING THE FLUCTUATING MENTAL STATUS EVALUATION (FMSE), A NOVEL DELIRIUM ASSESSMENT TOOL DESIGNED SPECIFICALLY FOR PATIENTS WITH STROKE AND NEUROLOGICAL INJURY. AS PART OF THE STUDY’S LONGITUDINAL FOLLOW-UP ASSESSMENTS, PATIENTS WILL HAVE FUNCTIONAL, COGNITIVE, AND HEALTH-RELATED QUALITY-OF-LIFE OUTCOMES MEASURED AT 3-, 6-, AND 12-MONTHS. IN EACH AIM, WE WILL DETERMINE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN DISTINCT PHENOTYPES OF POST-STROKE DELIRIUM AND SUBSEQUENT LONG-TERM CLINICAL TRAJECTORIES. AIM 1 WILL DEFINE TEMPORAL PHENOTYPES ACCORDING TO DELIRIUM ONSET, PROGRESSION, AND RESOLUTION; AIM 2 WILL QUANTIFY HYPOACTIVE DELIRIUM PHENOTYPES AND THEIR SEVERITY VIA WRIST ACTIGRAPHY; AIM 3 WILL CLASSIFY DELIRIUM ACCORDING TO CLINICAL RISK FACTOR- DEFINED PHENOTYPES (E.G., STROKE-RELATED, INFECTIOUS, METABOLIC, MEDICATION-ASSOCIATED); AND AIM 4 WILL USE LATENT CLASS ANALYSIS TO UNCOVER NOVEL, DATA-DERIVED PHENOTYPES BASED ON AGGREGATED CLINICAL, NEUROIMAGING, ACTIGRAPHY, AND ASSESSMENT DATA. TOGETHER, THESE AIMS WILL ESTABLISH THE FIRST PHENOTYPE-BASED INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR UNDERSTANDING POST-STROKE DELIRIUM AND ITS CONSEQUENCES. RESULTS WILL ENABLE THE IDENTIFICATION OF HIGH-RISK PATIENTS AND MODIFIABLE DELIRIUM FEATURES THAT CAN BE TARGETED IN FUTURE INTERVENTION TRIALS AIMED AT REDUCING LONG-TERM DISABILITY AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AMONG STROKE SURVIVORS.

description: SCALABLE INTERFACES FOR SYNCHRONOUS PROBING OF DOPAMINE SIGNALING AND NEURONAL ACTIVITY - PROJECT SUMMARY DOPAMINE NEUROTRANSMITTERS AND NEUROMODULATORS PLAY A CENTRAL ROLE IN LEARNING AND OTHER FLEXIBLE BEHAVIORS. THESE MOLECULES ALSO CONTROL WHETHER NEURONS RESPOND (I.E., SPIKE) TO INPUT SIGNALING, AS WELL AS THE STRENGTH OF CONNECTIONS BETWEEN NEURONS. THIS TIGHT INTERACTION BETWEEN MOLECULES AND NEURONAL ACTIVITY ULTIMATELY HELPS SHAPE HOW THE BRAIN IS WIRED. HOWEVER, DOPAMINE’S FUNCTIONS HAVE LARGELY BEEN STUDIED IN ISOLATION—EITHER IN RELATION TO BEHAVIOR, IN SENTIENT ANIMALS; OR TO NEURONAL ACTIVITY, IN BRAIN TISSUE SLICES. CURRENT TECHNOLOGY DOES NOT ALLOW US TO MEASURE THESE TWO FUNCTIONS TOGETHER. HERE, WE AIM TO BRIDGE THIS GAP BY DEVELOPING AND APPLYING NEW TOOLS CAPABLE OF MEASURING THE SYNCHRONOUS INTERPLAY BETWEEN DOPAMINE AND NEURONAL ACTIVITY IN AWAKE BEHAVING ANIMALS. WE PREVIOUSLY ESTABLISHED MULTI-MODAL SYSTEMS THAT ENABLED RECORDING OF DOPAMINE AND ELECTRICAL NEURAL ACTIVITY IN NONHUMAN PRIMATES—SETTING A FOUNDATION TO BUILD THE PROPOSED TOOLS HERE. KEY UNADDRESSED NEEDS FOR MONITORING THE TARGETED CELLULAR-SCALE INTERACTIONS INCLUDE FOCAL, CELL-SPECIFIC, AND MULTI- SITE MEASUREMENTS. FOCAL SENSORS ARE REQUIRED TO PROBE THE MOLECULAR AND NEURONAL ACTIVITY WITHIN THE MICROSCALE DOMAIN IN WHICH THEY INTERACT. FURTHERMORE, THESE SENSORS SHOULD BE ABLE TO DETECT CELL-SPECIFIC NEURONAL ACTIVITY, IN THE FORM OF ACTION POTENTIALS (I.E., SPIKES). FINALLY, THESE SENSORS SHOULD BE ABLE TO RECORD FROM MULTIPLE DISTRIBUTED LOCATIONS IN THE BRAIN IN ORDER TO DELINEATE SITE-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS. THIS MULTI-CHANNEL CAPABILITY NECESSITATES SMALL SENSORS, TO REDUCE IMPLANT-INDUCED TRAUMA, WHILE ALLOWING SCALING OF CHANNEL NUMBERS. WE PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED MICRO-INVASIVE SENSORS THAT DIRECTLY ENABLE SUCH SCALABILITY WITH MINIMAL TRAUMA AND WERE SHOWN TO PROVIDE CHRONIC (> 1 YEAR) MEASUREMENTS OF DOPAMINE IN THE STRIATUM OF MONKEYS AND RODENTS. THE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE ORGANIZED AS FOLLOWS. AIM 1 IS TO DESIGN FOCAL JUXTAPOSED SENSORS CAPABLE OF MEASURING DOPAMINE AND NEURONAL ACTIVITY WITHIN MICROSCALE PROXIMITY AND TO TEST THESE SENSORS IN SIMPLE REWARD-RELATED BEHAVIORS TO VALIDATE THEIR MEASUREMENT CAPABILITIES IN MONKEYS. AIM 2 IS TO CREATE SCALABLE ARRAYS TO ENABLE MEASUREMENTS OF HOW THESE MULTI-MODAL SIGNALS ARE COORDINATED ACROSS WIDESPREAD BRAIN REGIONS (I.E., CORTEX AND STRIATUM).

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE NEURAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING TEMPORAL INTEGRATION - PROJECT SUMMARY A CENTRAL CHALLENGE IN NEUROSCIENCE IS TO UNDERSTAND HOW THE BRAIN PERFORMS FUNDAMENTAL COMPUTATIONS THAT ALLOW ANIMALS TO SENSE, INTERPRET, AND RESPOND TO THE WORLD. ONE KEY COMPUTATION IS TEMPORAL INTEGRATION, THE ABILITY TO ACCUMULATE SENSORY INFORMATION OVER TIME. THIS PROCESS IS ESSENTIAL FOR BEHAVIORS INCLUDING THE VESTIBULO-OCULAR REFLEX (VOR) IN HUMANS, WHICH STABILIZES VISION DURING HEAD MOVEMENTS, AND FOR MAINTAINING POSTURE AND COORDINATED MOVEMENT. WHEN TEMPORAL INTEGRATION IS DISRUPTED, PEOPLE CAN EXPERIENCE GAZE INSTABILITY, NYSTAGMUS, IMBALANCE, AND OTHER MOVEMENT DISORDERS. DESPITE DECADES OF RESEARCH IN VERTEBRATES, MANY OF THE CELLULAR AND NETWORK MECHANISMS UNDERLYING TEMPORAL INTEGRATION REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THIS PROPOSAL LEVERAGES THE FRUIT FLY DROSOPHILA, WHICH SENSES ANGULAR VELOCITY USING SPECIALIZED SENSORY ORGANS THAT FUNCTION LIKE GYROSCOPES, CALLED HALTERES. THE HALTERE-MOTOR SYSTEM IS ANALOGOUS TO VERTEBRATE GAZE CONTROL CIRCUITS BUT OFFERS UNIQUE EXPERIMENTAL ADVANTAGES: THE COMPLETE WIRING DIAGRAM IS KNOWN, INDIVIDUAL NEURONS CAN BE TARGETED GENETICALLY, AND NEURAL ACTIVITY CAN BE RECORDED AND MANIPULATED WITH PRECISION. WE HAVE DEVELOPED A NOVEL EXPERIMENTAL PARADIGM THAT DELIVERS CONTROLLED ROTATIONAL STIMULI WHILE ENABLING SIMULTANEOUS PHYSIOLOGICAL RECORDINGS, IMAGING, AND OPTOGENETIC MANIPULATIONS IN BEHAVING ANIMALS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL USE CONNECTOMICS TO IDENTIFY CANDIDATE NEURONS IN THE HALTERE-MOTOR PATHWAY THAT ARE LIKELY TO PERFORM TEMPORAL INTEGRATION, CONSTRUCT GENETIC DRIVER LINES FOR THEM, AND PERFORM OPTOGENETIC MANIPULATIONS TO ASSESS THEIR PUTATIVE FUNCTION. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ESTABLISH NEW PREPARATIONS FOR WHOLE-CELL RECORDINGS OF THESE NEURONS TO DETERMINE THE MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, AND NETWORK MECHANISMS THAT ALLOW THEM TO INTEGRATE SENSORY SIGNALS OVER TIME. IN AIM 3, WE WILL INTEGRATE ANATOMICAL AND PHYSIOLOGICAL DATA INTO DETAILED COMPUTATIONAL MODELS OF THE CELLS AND CIRCUITS THAT PREDICTS HOW NEURAL PROPERTIES PRODUCE TEMPORAL INTEGRATION AND GUIDE BEHAVIOR. THIS INTEGRATIVE APPROACH COMBINES GENETICS, PHYSIOLOGY, AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING TO UNCOVER THE PRINCIPLES OF TEMPORAL INTEGRATION AT MULTIPLE LEVELS, FROM SINGLE NEURONS TO CIRCUITS. BECAUSE SIMILAR MECHANISMS ARE THOUGHT TO OPERATE IN HUMAN GAZE AND POSTURE CONTROL, OUR WORK WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO DISORDERS SUCH AS GAZE- EVOKED NYSTAGMUS, BALANCE IMPAIRMENTS, AND OTHER CONDITIONS CAUSED BY NEURAL INTEGRATOR DYSFUNCTION. BEYOND HUMAN HEALTH, THESE STUDIES WILL ADVANCE FUNDAMENTAL UNDERSTANDING OF HOW NERVOUS SYSTEMS ACROSS SPECIES ACCUMULATE INFORMATION OVER TIME TO DRIVE ADAPTIVE BEHAVIOR, OFFERING A FRAMEWORK FOR FUTURE INVESTIGATIONS OF SENSORY-MOTOR COMPUTATION.

description: EXAMINING BRAIN AREAS TO IDENTIFY GENERALIZABLE NEURAL FEATURES TO IMPROVE BRAIN-COMPUTER INTERFACE PRECISION AND RELIABILITY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT: EVERYDAY LIFE REQUIRES THE ABILITY TO GRASP A WIDE VARIETY OF OBJECTS. BRAIN-COMPUTER INTERFACES (BCIS) ENABLE INDIVIDUALS WITH PARALYSIS TO REACH AND GRASP BY USING BRAIN SIGNALS TO CONTROL ROBOTIC LIMBS OR STIMULATE THEIR OWN MUSCLES. HOWEVER, USERS OFTEN STRUGGLE TO PERFORM NOVEL MOVEMENTS THAT ARE SIMILAR, BUT NOT IDENTICAL, TO PREVIOUSLY LEARNED ONES. THE PROPOSED EXPERIMENTS AIM TO IMPROVE BCI DECODERS THAT TRANSLATE NEURAL SIGNALS INTO REACHING AND GRASPING WHEN TASK CONDITIONS CHANGE. WE WILL CONDUCT THREE EXPERIMENTS TO ADDRESS THIS GOAL. AIM 1 WILL INVESTIGATE HOW COMBINATIONS OF WRIST ORIENTATION AND HAND SHAPE AFFECT GRASPING, TESTING HYPOTHESIS H1—THAT REACHING AND GRASPING ARE OBJECT-CENTRIC, WITH THE GRASP DETERMINED FIRST AND THE REACH ADJUSTED ACCORDINGLY. AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE BCI DECODERS DESIGNED TO ENHANCE MOVEMENT TIMING AND SPEED PROFILES TO RESEMBLE NATURAL MOTION, TESTING HYPOTHESIS H2—THAT CONDITION-INVARIANT NEURAL ACTIVITY IMPROVES MOVEMENT TIMING AND THAT THE PRIMARY MOTOR CORTEX BEST PROVIDES THESE SIGNALS. AIM 3 WILL EXAMINE NEURAL TUNING TO NOVEL REACH DIRECTIONS THAT ARE SIMILAR TO PREVIOUSLY LEARNED ONES, TESTING HYPOTHESIS H3—THAT INCREASING THE NUMBER OF NEURAL DIMENSIONS USED IMPROVES DECODING ACCURACY COMPARED TO TRADITIONAL LINEAR DECODERS. RECORDINGS WILL BE TAKEN FROM THE PRIMARY MOTOR CORTEX, PREMOTOR CORTEX, ANTERIOR INTRAPARIETAL AREA, AND PARIETAL REACH REGION. ANALYSES WILL RANGE FROM SINGLE-NEURON FIRING RATES TO ADVANCED NEURAL POPULATION MODELS. THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL IDENTIFY BCI-RELEVANT NEURAL FEATURES THAT ARE PRESERVED ACROSS TASKS AND CLARIFY HOW POPULATION-LEVEL ACTIVITY SUPPORTS CONSISTENT REACHING AND GRASPING UNDER VARYING CONDITIONS. IMPROVING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF NEURAL MOVEMENT ENCODING WILL LEAD TO MORE EFFECTIVE BCIS AND ROBOTIC SYSTEMS THAT BETTER REPLICATE NATURAL GRASPING, ULTIMATELY ENHANCING REHABILITATION OUTCOMES FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH MOTOR DEFICITS DUE TO BRAIN INJURY.

description: SOMATIC INSTABILITY OF GAA REPEATS IN PATHOGENESIS OF FRIEDREICH’S ATAXIA - SUMMARY FRIEDREICH’S ATAXIA (FRDA) IS A PROGRESSIVE, DEBILITATING AND LIFE SHORTENING DISEASE. IT IS ONE OF THE MOST PREVALENT INHERITED ATAXIAS THAT AFFECTS MULTIPLE ORGANS AND SYSTEMS, INCLUDING NERVOUS AND ENDOCRINE SYSTEMS, HEART, MUSCLE, HEARING AND VISION. FRDA IS AN AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE DISEASE, MOST OFTEN CAUSED BY BIALLELIC, LARGE EXPANSIONS OF GAA REPEATS IN INTRON 1 OF THE FRATAXIN (FXN) GENE. LONG GAA TRACTS LEAD TO TRANSCRIPTIONAL REPRESSION OF FXN DUE TO FORMATION OF NON-CANONICAL DNA STRUCTURES AND LOCAL CHANGES IN THE CHROMATIN ENVIRONMENT, RESULTING IN FRATAXIN DEFICIENCY. FRATAXIN IS A SMALL MITOCHONDRIAL PROTEIN ESSENTIAL FOR EFFICIENT BIOSYNTHESIS OF IRON-SULFUR (FE-S) CLUSTERS, COFACTORS OF ~200 HUMAN PROTEINS INVOLVED IN CELLULAR RESPIRATION, METABOLISM, DNA REPAIR, REPLICATION AND TRANSCRIPTION. ONSET OF FRDA VARIES FROM EARLY CHILDHOOD TO LATE ADULTHOOD AND THE DISEASE IS CHARACTERIZED BY CONSIDERABLE VARIABILITY OF PENETRANCE OF DIFFERENT SYMPTOMS. WHILE REPEAT SIZE IS THE MOST IMPORTANT KNOWN DETERMINANT OF FRDA SEVERITY, IT DOES NOT FULLY ACCOUNT FOR CLINICAL HETEROGENEITY AMONGST FRDA PATIENTS. DESPITE MANY EFFORTS, NO ADDITIONAL SIGNIFICANT FRDA MODIFIERS INFLUENCING AGE OF ONSET OR SYMPTOM VARIABILITY HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES DEMONSTRATED REMARKABLE SOMATIC INSTABILITY OF THE GAA REPEATS IN PATIENT TISSUES AS WELL AS LONGITUDINAL CHANGES IN THE NUMBER OF GAAS IN FRDA. RECENT REPORTS INDICATE THAT INTERRUPTIONS IN THE GAA TRACTS ARE COMMON AND MAY AFFECT CLINICAL PRESENTATION OF THE DISEASE. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SOMATIC GAA EXPANSION IS A CRITICAL MODIFIER OF FRDA PATHOGENESIS AND THAT THE RATE OF SOMATIC EXPANSION DEPENDS ON PRESENCE AND EXTENT OF INTERRUPTIONS IN THE GAA TRACT. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT LONGER, UNINTERRUPTED GAA TRACTS FORM STABLE NON-CANONICAL DNA STRUCTURES, ACCELERATE SOMATIC EXPANSIONS AND DECREASE FXN TRANSCRIPTION. TO MECHANISTICALLY ADDRESS THE ROLES OF SOMATIC EXPANSION AND GAA INTERRUPTIONS IN FRDA, WE WILL ANSWER THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS: HOW DO SOMATIC EXPANSIONS INFLUENCE FRDA PHENOTYPES? WHAT ARE THE MECHANISMS DRIVING SOMATIC INSTABILITY OF THE GAA REPEATS? WHAT IS THE MOLECULAR MECHANISM BEHIND INTERRUPTION-MEDIATED FRDA PHENOTYPE MODULATION? THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL UTILIZE FRDA PATIENT-DERIVED DIVIDING (IPSCS) AND NON-DIVIDING (INEURONS) CELL MODELS AND A FRDA MOUSE MODEL CARRYING AN EXPANDED GAA REPEAT TRACT IN A HUMAN FXN TRANSGENE. ISOGENIC CONTROLS GENERATED BY GENOME EDITING OF THE PATHOGENIC GAA REPEAT TRACTS IN HUMAN CELLS AND MICE WILL SERVE AS EXPERIMENTAL CONTROLS. THE EFFECT OF GAA LENGTH AND INTERRUPTION STATUS ON THE DYNAMICS OF SOMATIC EXPANSIONS WILL BE DEFINED BY LONGITUDINALLY TESTING OUR MODELS IN SOMATIC INSTABILITY ASSAYS THAT CAN BE LINKED TO FRDA PHENOTYPES. OUR GOAL IS TO DETERMINE IF GAA REPEAT INTERRUPTIONS AND THE PROPENSITY FOR SOMATIC EXPANSION CAN BE USED AS MOLECULAR FEATURES OF FRDA, AKIN TO BIOMARKERS, TO IMPROVE DISEASE TRAJECTORY PREDICTIONS, SELECTION OF PATIENTS FOR CLINICAL TRIALS, AND TO GAUGE LONG-TERM SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF REPEAT-TARGETED THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES.

description: CONTROL OF NEUROTRANSMITTER RELEASE BY MUNC13-1 - THE RELEASE OF NEUROTRANSMITTERS BY CA2+-TRIGGERED SYNAPTIC VESICLE EXOCYTOSIS MEDIATES COMMUNICATION BETWEEN NEURONS AND IS REGULATED DURING DIVERSE PRESYNAPTIC PLASTICITY PROCESSES THAT UNDERLIE MULTIPLE FORMS OF INFORMATION PROCESSING IN THE BRAIN. ELUCIDATION OF THE MECHANISMS OF NEUROTRANSMITTER RELEASE AND ITS REGULATION IS THUS CRITICAL TO UNDERSTAND BRAIN FUNCTION AND IS ALSO RELEVANT TO BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES THAT DEPEND ON SIMILAR PROTEIN MACHINERIES SUCH AS SECRETION IN NEUROENDOCRINE CELLS, Β-CELLS AND IMMUNOLOGICAL SYNAPSES. HENCE, THIS RESEARCH IS IMPORTANT NOT ONLY TO UNDERSTAND PROCESSES OF THE UTMOST BIOLOGICAL INTEREST BUT ALSO TO DEVELOP NOVEL THERAPIES FOR MANY DEVASTING DISEASES, INCLUDING NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS SUCH AS SCHIZOPHRENIA, EPILEPSY, ALZHEIMER’S AND PARKINSON’S, AS WELL AS MUSCULAR DYSTROPHIES, HYPERTENSION, DIABETES AND CANCER. EXTENSIVE RESEARCH ON THE NEUROTRANSMITTER RELEASE APPARATUS HAS YIELDED A WORKING MODEL WHEREBY THE SNARE PROTEINS SYNTAXIN-1, SNAP-25 AND SYNAPTOBREVIN PLAY A CENTRAL ROLE BY FORMING SNARE COMPLEXES THAT BRING THE VESICLE AND PLASMA MEMBRANES TOGETHER, INDUCING MEMBRANE FUSION. MUNC18-1 AND MUNC13-1 PLAY VITAL ROLES IN RELEASE BY ORCHESTRATING SNARE COMPLEX ASSEMBLY VIA A PATHWAY IN WHICH OPENING OF A SELF- INHIBITED ‘CLOSED’ CONFORMATION OF SYNTAXIN-1 BY MUNC13-1 IS A CENTRAL EVENT. IN ADDITION, THROUGH ITS MULTIDOMAIN ARCHITECTURE, MUNC13-1 CONTROLS MULTIPLE FORMS OF PRESYNAPTIC PLASTICITY THAT DEPEND ON CA2+, DIACYLGLYCEROL (DAG) AND OTHER PROTEINS SUCH AS CALMODULIN, DOC2 AND RIM, AND THAT LIKELY REGULATE THE SYNTAXIN-1 OPENING ACTIVITY OF MUNC13-1. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING SYNTAXIN-1 OPENING BY MUNC13- 1 AND PRESYNAPTIC PLASTICITY REMAIN TO BE ELUCIDATED. THE RESEARCH PROPOSED IN THIS APPLICATION IS DESIGNED TO ADDRESS THESE QUESTIONS, BUILDING ON EXCITING PRELIMINARY DATA THAT SUGGEST MULTIPLE HYPOTHESES TO BE TESTED. THREE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE PROPOSED TO WORK IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: 1. MECHANISM OF SYNTAXIN-1 OPENING BY MUN13-1; 2. CONTROL OF MUNC13-1 ACTIVITY BY CA2+, DAG, VARIOUS MUNC13-1 DOMAINS AND DOC2B; AND 3. CONTROL OF MUNC13-1 ACTIVITY BY ITS RIM-BINDING DOMAIN AND RIM. A COMBINATION OF BIOPHYSICAL TECHNIQUES, INCLUDING CRYO-ELECTRON MICROSCOPY AND TOMOGRAPHY, FLUORESCENCE SPECTROSCOPY AND NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE SPECTROSCOPY, TOGETHER WITH BIOCHEMICAL RECONSTITUTION OF MEMBRANE FUSION, WILL BE USED. ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL EXPERIMENTS PERFORMED IN A COLLABORATOR’S LAB WILL TEST THE PHYSIOLOGICAL SIGNIFICANCE OF THE IN VITRO STUDIES. THIS RESEARCH IS EXPECTED TO REVEAL THE MOLECULAR MECHANISM OF A CENTRAL STEP OF NEUROTRANSMITTER RELEASE AND TO ESTABLISH FOUNDATIONAL PRINCIPLES ON THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING KEY FORMS OF PRESYNAPTIC PLASTICITY, THUS PROVIDING CRUCIAL INSIGHTS INTO HOW PRESYNAPTIC TERMINALS FUNCTION AS MINIMAL COMPUTATIONAL UNITS IN THE BRAIN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EFFECTS OF CORTICAL IMPLANTS ON INFLAMMATORY AND CELL DEATH RESPONSES - MICROELECTRODES (ME) IMPLANTED IN THE BRAIN HAVE ENABLED THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEUROPROSTHETIC AND NEUROMODULATION TECHNOLOGIES FOR PATIENTS WITH PARALYSIS, PSYCHIATRIC, AND NEUROMOTOR DISORDERS. HOWEVER, LONG-TERM STABILITY AND FUNCTIONAL PERFORMANCE ARE CRITICAL BARRIERS FOR IMPLANTED ME AS THEY ENCOUNTER A FOREIGN BODY RESPONSE (FBR) IN THE BRAIN TISSUE, THUS LIMITING THEIR USE IN CLINICAL APPLICATIONS. THE FBR TO IMPLANTED ME IS UNIQUE AND COMPLEX DUE TO A CHRONIC, NON-RESOLVING WOUND THAT RESULTS IN CHRONIC NEUROINFLAMMATION. IN RESPONSE TO THE IMPLANT-INDUCED TRAUMA, AN ENDOGENOUS SET OF MECHANISMS, CALLED THE INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE, BECOMES ACTIVE AND IS RESPONSIBLE FOR RECOGNIZING AND TARGETING OF FOREIGN OBJECTS. LNFLAMMASOMES ARE MULTI PROTEIN STRUCTURES THAT PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN THE INITIATION OF AN INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE AND ARE CONSIDERED TO BE TRIGGERING, UPSTREAM PROTEINS SERVING AS DIRECTORS IN THE IMMUNE PATHWAY TO DRIVE PATHOGENESIS FOLLOWING TRAUMATIC INJURIES. HOWEVER, THE ACTIVATION OF INFLAMMASOMES AND THEIR EFFECT ON CHRONIC INFLAMMATION AND CELLULAR DEATH RESPONSES IN THE CONTEXT OF ME-INJURY MODEL IS NOT WELL DEFINED. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO UNDERSTAND THE CONTRIBUTION OF INFLAMMASOME ACTIVATION TO NEUROINFLAMMATION, OXIDATIVE DAMAGE AND CELL DEATH RESPONSES TO IMPROVE CHRONIC FBR AND THEREBY, ME FUNCTION. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT, AS CRITICAL INITIATORS OF THE INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE, INFLAMMASOMES ARE ACTIVATED FOLLOWING ME IMPLANTATION AND ACT AS MEDIATORS OF PYROPTOTIC CELL DEATH AT THE ELECTRODE-TISSUE INTERFACE. BASED ON OUR PRELIMINARY FINDINGS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT MODULATION OF INFLAMMASOME ACTIVATION WILL REDUCE CHRONIC INFLAMMATION WHILE PROVIDING CELLULAR PROTECTION AGAINST PYROPTOSIS. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE THE EFFECTS OF INFLAMMASOME INHIBITION ON FBR IN NEURAL IMPLANTS AND ITS IMPACT ON NEURONAL RECORDINGS. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE THE EFFECTS OF INFLAMMASOMES INHIBITION ON REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES (ROS)-MEDIATED INFLAMMASOME ACTIVATION, OXIDATIVE DAMAGE AND PYROPTOSIS AT THE ELECTRODE INTERFACE. AIM 3 WILL DEVELOP ROS-RESPONSIVE POLYMERIC COATINGS ON ME TO TRIGGER ANTIOXIDANT DELIVERY AND MINIMIZE OXIDATIVE STRESS. THE STUDY WILL USE MULTIPLE TECHNIQUES FROM LIFE SCIENCES, ENGINEERING, AND BIOCHEMISTRY TO PRODUCE A COMPREHENSIVE DATASET THAT INCLUDES: I) TRANSCRIPTOMICS OF BULK BRAIN TISSUE TO PROVIDE A MACROSCOPIC OVERVIEW OF ONGOING INFLAMMATION, II) SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS AND PROTEOMICS IN THE SAME TISSUE SLICE TO PROVIDE INFORMATION AT HIGH SPATIAL RESOLUTION AT RECORDING SITES, III) PROTEIN QUANTIFICATION METHODS SUCH AS IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY, IMMUNOBLOTS, AND MESA SCALE DISCOVERY (MSD) ENHANCED CHEMILUMINESCENT IMMUNOASSAYS (ECLIA), IV) ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, AND V) MATERIALS SCIENCE AND SURFACE CHEMISTRY TO DEVELOP ROS SCAVENGERS ON ME SURFACE. THE OUTCOMES OF THE PROJECT WILL ELUCIDATE INFLAMMASOMES SIGNALING AND ITS RELATION TO OTHER INNATE IMMUNE PATHWAYS AND ROS-MEDIATED OXIDATIVE SIGNALING. BY USING A CLINICALLY RELEVANT DRUG FOR IMMUNOMODULATION (IC100), THE ACQUIRED KNOWLEDGE WILL BE USED TO DEVELOP IMMUNOMODULATION THERAPIES TARGETING BOTH ACUTE AND CHRONIC INFLAMMATION IN NEURAL IMPLANTS TO IMPROVE THE CHRONIC FBR AND ME FUNCTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EFFECT OF FIBRIL STRUCTURE ON THE DISEASE PATHOGENESIS OF A NOVEL ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN STRAIN - PROJECT SUMMARY  CENTRAL SYNUCLEINOPATHIES HAVE HISTORICALLY BEEN CATEGORIZED BASED ON THE TYPE OF NEUROPATHOLOGICAL INCLUSIONS FOUND IN THE BRAIN AT THE TIME OF AUTOPSY, WITH GLIAL CYTOPLASMIC INCLUSIONS (GCIS) DEFINING MULTIPLE SYSTEM ATROPHY (MSA) AND LEWY BODIES (LBS) DEFINING THE LEWY BODY DISEASES – PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD), PARKINSON’S DISEASE WITH DEMENTIA (PDD) AND DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES. CRYO-ELECTRON MICROSCOPY (CRYO- EM) STUDIES DETERMINING THE HIGH-RESOLUTION STRUCTURES OF THE Α-SYNUCLEIN (Α-SYN) FIBRILS FOUND IN THESE LESIONS HAVE SHOWN THAT MISFOLDED Α-SYN ADOPTS DISTINCT STRUCTURES, OR CONFORMATIONS, IN THESE TWO GROUPS OF DISORDERS. THIS HAS BEEN CRITICAL FOR VALIDATING THE STRAIN HYPOTHESIS, OR THE IDEA THAT DIFFERENT PROTEIN STRUCTURES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH DISCRETE BIOLOGICAL CONSEQUENCES IN A PATIENT. HOWEVER, AN INCREASING NUMBER OF STUDIES INDICATE THAT MULTIPLE, AND SOMETIMES NOVEL, Α-SYN STRAINS CAN CO-EXIST IN AN INDIVIDUAL PATIENT, COMPLICATING EFFORTS TO UNDERSTAND THE MOLECULAR UNDERPINNINGS OF DISEASE. FOR EXAMPLE, CRYO-EM STUDIES ON ATYPICAL MSA PATIENTS WITH LIMBIC PREDOMINANT NEURONAL CYTOPLASMIC INCLUSIONS RESULTED IN THE DISCOVERY OF A LEWY-MSA HYBRID FOLD OF Α-SYN, SUGGESTING THAT PREVIOUSLY UNIDENTIFIED Α-SYN STRAINS CONTRIBUTE TO DISEASE HETEROGENEITY. THIS FINDING IS CONSISTENT WITH OUR RECENT ISOLATION OF AN UNDESCRIBED Α-SYN STRAIN FROM A PDD PATIENT SAMPLE EXHIBITING BIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES THAT ARE DISTINCT FROM BOTH THE MSA AND LB STRAINS. STEMMING FROM THE INCREASING IDENTIFICATION OF NEW Α-SYN STRAINS IN PATIENT SAMPLES, THERE IS A GROWING NEED TO UNDERSTAND THE SPECIFIC BIOLOGICAL CONSEQUENCES OF EACH STRAIN ON DISEASE PATHOGENESIS. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF OUR RESEARCH IS TO USE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF Α-SYN DISEASE BIOLOGY TO SUCCESSFULLY DEVELOP DIAGNOSTICS AND THERAPEUTICS FOR SYNUCLEINOPATHY PATIENTS. OUR OBJECTIVE IN THIS APPLICATION IS TO DETERMINE HOW THE MOLECULAR STRUCTURE OF A RECENTLY ISOLATED Α-SYN STRAIN IMPACTS THE ROUTE OF SPREAD TO CLINICAL TARGET AREAS IN THE BRAIN, ULTIMATELY DETERMINING THE CLINICAL PRESENTATION OF DISEASE, INCLUDING DEMENTIA. BUILDING ON THIS DISCOVERY, OUR HYPOTHESIS IS THAT STRUCTURALLY AND BIOLOGICALLY DISTINCT Α-SYN STRAINS EXHIBIT CRITICAL DIFFERENCES IN DISEASE PATHOGENESIS IN VIVO. OUR INNOVATIVE APPROACH WILL CAPITALIZE ON OUR EXPERTISE INVESTIGATING THE MSA Α-SYN STRAIN, WHICH WILL SERVE AS A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO DIRECTLY COMPARE TWO DISTINCT PATIENT-DERIVED STRAINS TO DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF FIBRIL STRUCTURE ON DISEASE BIOLOGY. IN AIM 1, WE WILL USE SERIAL PASSAGING TO FURTHER ISOLATE AND INVESTIGATE NOVEL Α-SYN SUB-STRAINS FROM PATIENT SAMPLE PDD1 AND WILL USE CRYO-EM TO RESOLVE THE NEW FIBRIL STRUCTURE(S). IN AIM 2, WE WILL ASSESS NEUROINVASION FOLLOWING PERIPHERAL INJECTIONS USING THE PDD1 AND MSA STRAINS TO DETERMINE HOW STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES IN Α-SYN FIBRIL STRUCTURE IMPACTS DISEASE PATHOGENESIS. THIS WORK IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE WE WILL GENERATE THE DEEP PHENOTYPING NEEDED TO ENABLE WIDESPREAD IDENTIFICATION OF THE NOVEL PDD SUB-STRAIN, AS WELL AS DETERMINE THE ROLE OF STRAIN DYNAMICS ON THE STRUCTURE-PHENOTYPE RELATIONSHIP IN SYNUCLEINOPATHIES.

recipient.name: CENTRE FOR INFECTIOUS DISEASE RESEARCH IN ZAMBIA

description: COMMUNITY-TASKPEN APPROACH FOR NCD MULTIMORBIDITY RESPONSE AND ENGAGEMENT OF PLHIV IN ZAMBIA" ('CAREZ') STUDY - IN THE UNITED STATES, NON-COMMUNICABLE DISEASES (NCDS) NOW ACCOUNT FOR THE MAJORITY OF DEATHS AMONG PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV (PLHIV), WITH HEART DISEASE AND CANCER BEING THE LEADING CAUSES OF DEATH AMONG AMERICAN PLHIV OVER THE AGE OF 50 YEARS. IN RESPONSE TO THE PROBLEM OF CARDIOMETABOLIC NCDS LEADING TO HEART DISEASE IN PLHIV, OUR TEAM CREATED A NOVEL EVIDENCE-BASED PACKAGE TO MANAGE HIV-NCD MULTIMORBIDITY. THIS PACKAGE, WHICH WE HAVE COINED ‘TASKPEN,’ IS BASED ON TASK-SHIFTING AN ADAPTED VERSION OF WHO’S PACKAGE OF ESSENTIAL NONCOMMUNICABLE DISEASE INTERVENTIONS (PEN) TO NON-PHYSICIAN HEALTH WORKERS. TASKPEN INCLUDES LIFESTYLE COUNSELING GUIDES, EASY-TO-FOLLOW TREATMENT ALGORITHMS, POINT-OF-CARE DIAGNOSTICS, AND PROTOCOLS FOR MULTI-MONTH DISPENSING OF NCD MEDICATIONS. DESPITE THE AVAILABILITY OF EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES LIKE TASKPEN, HOWEVER, INTEGRATED CARE REMAINS OUT OF REACH FOR MILLIONS OF PEOPLE WITH MULTIMORBIDITY FROM HIV AND CARDIOMETABOLIC NCDS IN THE US AND GLOBALLY. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, WE PROPOSE THE “COMMUNITY-TASKPEN APPROACH FOR NCD MULTIMORBIDITY RESPONSE AND ENGAGEMENT OF PLHIV IN ZAMBIA (OR ‘CAREZ’) STUDY. THE CAREZ STUDY WILL FOCUS ON INTEGRATING MOBILE CARE TEAMS, LED BY COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS, WITHIN COMMUNITY HEALTH STRUCTURES TO DELIVER SCREENING AND MANAGEMENT OF CARDIOMETABOLIC NCDS USING TASKPEN AND SUPPORTED BY MHEALTH TECHNOLOGY—A NOVEL MODEL THAT WE CALL ‘CAREZ’. TO EVALUATE THE EFFECTS OF CAREZ ON CONTROL OF BOTH HIV AND NCDS, AS WELL AS KEY IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES, WE PROPOSE TO CONDUCT A HYBRID EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION CLUSTER RANDOMIZED STEPPED-WEDGE TRIAL IN 12 URBAN COMMUNITIES OF LUSAKA, ZAMBIA. ZAMBIA IS UNIQUELY SUITED TO STUDY HIV-NCD MULTIMORBIDITY BECAUSE OF ITS ROBUST COMMUNITY HIV CARE PLATFORMS. THESE KINDS OF PLATFORMS SIMPLY DON’T EXIST IN THE US AND CAN SERVE AS AN IMPLEMENTATION LABORATORY TO DEVELOP COST-EFFECTIVE COMMUNITY-BASED APPROACHES TO PREVENT AND TREAT THE NCD RISK FACTORS LEADING TO HEART DISEASE IN PLHIV. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL GENERATE KNOWLEDGE DIRECTLY APPLICABLE TO AMERICAN HEALTH BY IDENTIFYING A REPLICABLE, SUSTAINABLE, AND SCALABLE SOLUTION TO PROMOTE IDEAL CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH FOR PLHIV IN THE US AND GLOBALLY. THIS STUDY CAN ONLY FEASIBLY BE CONDUCTED IN A SETTING WITH A HIGH PREVALENCE OF BOTH HIV AND CARDIOMETABOLIC NCDS, SUCH AS ZAMBIA, WHERE SUFFICIENT NUMBERS OF PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV AND CO-MORBID NCDS CAN BE ENROLLED INTO A TRIAL TO ENSURE ADEQUATE POWER TO GENERATE SCIENTIFICALLY ROBUST EVIDENCE. THE RIGOROUS IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE METHODS AND OUTCOME ASSESSMENT WE PROPOSE WILL ALSO ENABLE DISTILLATION OF THE CAREZ MODEL INTO ITS CORE COMPONENTS THAT CAN BE DIRECTLY ADAPTED AND APPLIED TO THE US CONTEXT. IF EFFECTIVE, CAREZ COULD REDUCE NCD MULTIMORBIDITY FOR PLHIV, AND CREATE OPPORTUNITIES FOR IMPLEMENTATION IN THE US SAFETY NET SETTINGS WHERE THE MAJORITY OF PLHIV RECEIVE THEIR HEALTHCARE, INCLUDING ENDING THE HIV EPIDEMIC (EHE) JURISDICTIONS, COMMUNITY HEALTH CENTERS, AND FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS RECEIVING RYAN WHITE HIV/AIDS FUNDING.
