description: MHEALTH AND MOBILE CLINICS FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF CARE FOR CARDIAC AND RESPIRATORY MULTIMORBIDITY (M-CARE) - HEART AND LUNG DISEASE ARE AMONG THE LEADING PREVENTABLE CAUSES OF DEATH FOR AMERICANS. THE GAP IN CARE IS WIDEST IN RURAL U.S. COMMUNITIES AND IN URBAN FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS, SOME OF WHICH SERVE THE CHIN AND BURMESE AMERICAN DIASPORA (>300,000). STAFFING SHORTAGES, LIMITED SPECIALTY ACCESS, AND COMMUNICATION BARRIERS CAN PREVENT SCREENING AND TREATMENT FOR HYPERTENSION (HTN) AND CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE (COPD). THE MHEALTH AND MOBILE CLINICS FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF CARE FOR CARDIAC AND RESPIRATORY MULTIMORBIDITY (M-CARE) PROJECT WILL DELIVER A SIMPLIFIED MOBILE CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT (CDS) TOOL AND COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER (CHW) TRAINING PACKAGE ENGINEERED FOR DIRECT TRANSFER TO AMERICAN PRIMARY CARE. INNOVATION LIES IN AN INTEGRATED MULTILINGUAL CDS THAT OPERATIONALIZES WHO PEN FOR CO-OCCURRING CARDIOPULMONARY MULTIMORBIDITY IN LOW-LITERACY SETTINGS, CO-DEVELOPED WITH A POPULATION SHARED BY THE MIZORAM STUDY SITE AND U.S., SO VALIDATED TOOLS TRANSFER WITHOUT RE-ENGINEERING. WE WORK IN INDIA BECAUSE THE DISEASE BURDEN, INFRASTRUCTURE, TRAINED CHWS, AND PARTNERSHIPS NEEDED TO VALIDATE THIS APPROACH ALREADY EXIST. IN NORTHEAST INDIA, ACTIVE TOBACCO USE REACHES 73% IN MEN AND 62% IN WOMEN, ~90% OF HTN CASES ARE UNDIAGNOSED OR UNTREATED, AND COPD PREVALENCE IS 15–25% IN ADULTS ≥40. THESE RATES PARALLEL THE HARDEST-HIT U.S. RURAL POPULATIONS WHERE THE PREVALENCE OF HTN IS ABOUT 40% AND THE PREVALENCE OF COPD IS 8%. CURRENT TOBACCO USE AMONG AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKA NATIVE ADULTS IS 34.9% — THE HIGHEST OF ANY U.S. RACIAL/ETHNIC GROUP. SINCE THE 2021 MYANMAR COUP, 50,000+ BURMESE PERSONS HAVE ENTERED MIZORAM; THE SAME POPULATIONS CONSTITUTE THE BURMESE AMERICAN DIASPORA, NOW CONCENTRATED IN U.S. CITIES—SO VALIDATED TOOLS CAN BE USABLE IN FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS SERVING THESE PATIENTS OR IN RURAL AND TRIBAL CLINICS FACING THE SAME LANGUAGE, WORKFORCE, AND ACCESS BARRIERS. USING PRISM (PRACTICAL, ROBUST IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINABILITY MODEL), WE WILL DIGITIZE WHO PEN (PACKAGE OF ESSENTIAL NONCOMMUNICABLE DISEASE INTERVENTIONS) CARDIOVASCULAR AND RESPIRATORY PROTOCOLS INTO THE CDS, TRAIN 22 CHWS, MEASURE FIDELITY, AND COMPLETE TRIAL PREPARATION. THE TRIAL EVALUATES THE CDS IN A HYBRID TYPE 2 STEPPED-WEDGE CLUSTER-RANDOMIZED TRIAL ACROSS 20 CLUSTERS (N=800) WITH A PRIMARY OUTCOME BEING CHANGE IN BLOOD PRESSURE AMONG PARTICIPANTS WITH HTN, AND SECONDARY OUTCOMES ARE CHANGE IN THE 10-YEAR WHO CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE RISK SCORE AND COPD-SPECIALIST REFERRAL COMPLETION AMONG SCREEN-POSITIVES. ADOPTION, FIDELITY, ACCEPTABILITY, FEASIBILITY, COST, AND SCALABILITY WILL BE ASSESSED THROUGH MIXED METHODS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SYSTEMS ANALYSIS AND IMPROVEMENT APPROACH TO OPTIMIZE THE CARDIOMETABOLIC CARE CASCADE (SAIA-CMD) IN CENTRAL MOZAMBIQUE - UNDIAGNOSED AND UNTREATED HYPERTENSION (HTN) AND TYPE II DIABETES (T2D) ARE THE PRINCIPAL DRIVERS OF CARDIOMETABOLIC DISEASE (CMD) GLOBALLY, DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTING HEALTH OUTCOMES IN LOW- AND MIDDLE-INCOME COUNTRIES (LMICS) SUCH AS IN MOZAMBIQUE. THIS DUAL BURDEN OF HTN AND T2D IS RAPIDLY INCREASING AS COUNTRIES UNDERGO THE EPIDEMIOLOGIC TRANSITION FROM INFECTIOUS DISEASES TO NON-COMMUNICABLE DISEASES AS PRINCIPAL CAUSES OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY. HOWEVER, DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT FOR HTN AND T2D REMAIN SUBOPTIMAL. OVER THE PAST 15 YEARS, SEVERAL IMPLEMENTATION RESEARCH STUDIES HAVE APPLIED THE SYSTEMS ANALYSIS AND IMPROVEMENT APPROACH (SAIA) TO OPTIMIZE CARE CASCADES FOR PREVENTING MOTHER-TO-CHILD HIV TRANSMISSION, ADDRESSING HTN AMONG PEOPLE WITH HIV, AND TO PILOT SAIA FOR T2D. SAIA IS HIGHLY ACCEPTABLE TO FRONTLINE CARE PROVIDERS IN HEALTH CARE SETTINGS AND HAS BEEN SHOWN TO IMPROVE SERVICE DELIVERY OF EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS AND IMPROVE CLINICAL OUTCOMES. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP A PRACTICAL AND SCALABLE MODEL FOR IMPROVING HTN AND T2D DIAGNOSIS AND MANAGEMENT SERVICES. THE STUDY BUILDS ON THE SAIA IMPLEMENTATION STUDIES BY DEVELOPING THE SAIA-CMD IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY – APPLICATION OF SAIA TO IMPROVE THE DELIVERY OF THE EVIDENCE-BASED WHO PACKAGE OF ESSENTIAL NCD INTERVENTIONS (PEN). WE WILL EVALUATE WHETHER THE SAIA-CMD STRATEGY IMPROVES HTN AND T2D AMONG COMORBID ADULTS; IDENTIFY ITS DRIVERS OF IMPLEMENTATION SUCCESS AND DESCRIBE WHETHER IMPLEMENTATION IS SUSTAINED AND ANY ADAPTATIONS MADE TO THE SAIA-CMD STRATEGY. FRAMED BY THE EXPLORATION, PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINMENT (EPIS) FRAMEWORK, WE WILL EXPLORE THE NEEDS OF PATIENTS WITH COMORBID HTN AND T2D, HEALTH SYSTEM STAKEHOLDERS, AND NATIONAL POLICIES (AIM 1A). BASED ON THIS WORK, OUR TEAM WILL REFINE SAIA-CMD FOR APPLICATION TO THE TARGETED EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTION (WHO PEN) AND WE WILL PREPARE FOR THE SAIA-CMD TRIAL BY IDENTIFYING IMPLEMENTATION DETERMINANTS, ADAPTING INTERVENTION TOOLS, AND DEVELOPING A DETAILED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (AIM 1B). THIS WILL FACILITATE OUR STUDY’S TRANSITION TO THE SAIA-CMD HYBRID TYPE III CLUSTER RANDOMIZED TRIAL IMPLEMENTATION PHASE (AIM 2) TO EVALUATE ITS EFFECTIVENESS ON INTEGRATED HTN AND T2D CASCADE OPTIMIZATION AND IDENTIFY DRIVERS OF IMPLEMENTATION SUCCESS.  FINALLY, IN THE SUSTAINMENT PHASE, WE WILL DESCRIBE SUSTAINED IMPLEMENTATION, DETERMINANTS OF SUSTAINED IMPLEMENTATION, AND STRATEGY ADAPTATIONS FOR SAIA-CMD (AIM 3). OUR RESEARCH WILL UNCOVER OPPORTUNITIES FOR HEALTH SYSTEM EFFICIENCIES THAT TAKE ADVANTAGE OF DECADES OF USG INVESTMENT IN MOZAMBIQUE, WHILE ALSO IDENTIFYING MODALITIES FOR DELIVERING CARDIOMETABOLIC CARE THAT ARE TRANSFERABLE TO THE UNITED STATES. MOREOVER, THE EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES BEING DELIVERED IN OUR STUDY, THE WHO PEN, ARE ANALOGOUS TO THE AMERICAN HEART ASSOCIATION’S RECOMMENDATIONS FOR HTN AND T2D. THUS, OUR STUDY’S IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES TO DELIVER THESE EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES WILL BE RELEVANT AND INFORMATIVE TO THE US CONTEXT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXPOSURE TO ULTRAFINE PARTICLES AND TRAFFIC-RELATED AIR POLLUTION MIXTURES AND NEUROPATHOLOGIC MARKERS OF ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS IN A COMMUNITY-BASED COHORT - PROJECT SUMMARY ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD) ARE A GROWING CONCERN IN OUR AGING POPULATION. THE IDENTIFICATION OF MODIFIABLE RISK FACTORS IS CRITICAL. GROWING EVIDENCE LINKS ADRD TO TRAFFIC-RELATED AIR POLLUTION (TRAP), A COMPLEX MIXTURE OF GASSES AND PARTICLES THAT INCLUDES ULTRAFINE PARTICLES (UFP, ≤ 100 NM DIAMETER) AND OTHER POLLUTANTS. HOWEVER, LIMITED WORK HAS EVALUATED THE EFFECTS OF TRAP MIXTURES AS A WHOLE, IDENTIFIED THE MOST RELEVANT TRAP COMPONENTS, OR ASSESSED CRITICAL EXPOSURE PERIODS RELEVANT TO NEUROPATHOLOGIC OUTCOMES. MOST EPIDEMIOLOGIC STUDIES HAVE RELIED ON CLINICAL DIAGNOSES OF COGNITIVE DECLINE, WITH RELATIVELY FEW INVESTIGATING NEUROPATHOLOGIC CHANGES THAT MAY BETTER REFLECT BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS. UFPS MAY BE PARTICULARLY NEUROTOXIC, BUT HEALTH STUDIES REMAIN LIMITED DUE TO SPARSE MONITORING DATA AND THE NEED FOR SPECIALIZED EXPOSURE ASSESSMENT. THE ADULT CHANGES IN THOUGHT (ACT) STUDY IS ONE OF THE LARGEST, MOST EXTENSIVE COMMUNITY-BASED AUTOPSY COHORTS IN THE WORLD. OUR TEAM PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED THE FIRST-OF-THEIR-KIND, UFP/TRAP EXPOSURE SURFACES USING AN INNOVATIVE MOBILE MONITORING DESIGN IN 2019 FOR THIS COHORT. THIS PROJECT WILL USE THOSE DATA AND RELATED RESOURCES TO ADDRESS KEY GAPS IN ENVIRONMENTAL EPIDEMIOLOGY AND ADRD RESEARCH. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DEVELOP AND VALIDATE THE FIRST-OF-THEIR-KIND LONG-TERM UFP EXPOSURE MODELS TO MORE ROBUSTLY SUPPORT THEIR UTILITY FOR EPIDEMIOLOGIC ADRD APPLICATIONS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ESTIMATE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN LONG-TERM EXPOSURE TO TRAP MIXTURES AND ADRD-RELATED NEUROPATHOLOGIC OUTCOMES AND IDENTIFY EXPOSURE PERIODS MOST RELEVANT TO NEUROPATHOLOGY. THIS WORK WILL GENERATE NEW EVIDENCE ON THE ROLE OF UFP/TRAP IN LATE-LIFE BRAIN HEALTH AND SUPPORT FUTURE STUDIES ON MODIFIABLE ENVIRONMENTAL RISKS FOR ADRD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MITIGATING NETWORK DYSFUNCTION UNDER AMYLOID-Β PATHOLOGY - PROJECT SUMMARY SOLUBLE AΒ OLIGOMERS CONTRIBUTE TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE BY DISRUPTING EXCITATORY AMINO ACID TRANSPORTERS (EAATS) IN ASTROCYTES AND NEURONS, ELEVATING EXTRACELLULAR GLUTAMATE. EVEN MODEST, CHRONIC GLUTAMATE ACCUMULATION PERTURBS SYNAPTIC FUNCTION, DRIVING HYPEREXCITABILITY, INTERNEURON DYSFUNCTION, AND SYNAPTIC LOSS. THIS PROJECT TESTS A MITIGATION-FIRST STRATEGY: STABILIZING NETWORK ACTIVITY DESPITE ONGOING AΒ- RELATED EAAT IMPAIRMENT. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT HIPPOCAMPAL SHARP WAVE–RIPPLES (SWRS) ARE HIGHLY SENSITIVE TO EAAT ATTENUATION AND THAT MILD HYPERPOLARIZATION RESTORES SWRS. WE THEREFORE HYPOTHESIZE THAT MILD HYPERPOLARIZATION—VIA M-CURRENT (KV7) ENHANCEMENT OR COMPLEMENTARY MECHANISMS—WILL REDUCE SWR DISRUPTIONS IN 5XFAD HIPPOCAMPAL SLICES. WE WILL QUANTIFY SWRS IN EX VIVO SLICES FROM 5XFAD MICE AND WILD-TYPE LITTERMATES ACROSS 1–9 MONTHS, SPANNING MODERATE TO ADVANCED AΒ PATHOLOGY. PHARMACOLOGY WILL PRIORITIZE KV7 CHANNEL OPENERS AND EXTEND TO ADDITIONAL CONDUCTANCES THAT BIAS MEMBRANES NEGATIVE, INCLUDING GIRK (KIR3) ACTIVATORS, BK (KCA1.1) MODULATORS, HCN (IH) MODULATORS, AND SELECTED GI/O-COUPLED RECEPTOR PATHWAYS. DOSING WILL BE GUIDED BY SWR DOSE–RESPONSE TO IDENTIFY “NEUTRAL” WINDOWS THAT PRESERVE PHYSIOLOGICAL OSCILLATIONS. IMPACT: SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION WILL ESTABLISH MILD HYPERPOLARIZATION AS A NETWORK-STABILIZING THERAPEUTIC CONCEPT FOR EARLY AD, PROVIDE A PRACTICAL SCREENING FRAMEWORK CENTERED ON SWR PRESERVATION, AND HIGHLIGHT REPURPOSABLE COMPOUNDS ALREADY INVESTIGATED FOR EPILEPSY, DEPRESSION, TBI, STROKE, AND AD SYMPTOM RELIEF. THIS MITIGATION-FOCUSED APPROACH HAS STRONG TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE AND THE POTENTIAL FOR RAPID CLINICAL IMPACT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LONGITUDINAL PATTERNS OF MULTIPLE BEHAVIORAL RISK FACTORS AND THEIR JOINT EFFECTS ON COGNITIVE AGING: EVIDENCE FROM A 24-YEAR NATIONAL COHORT - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT DEMENTIA IS A MAJOR AND GROWING PUBLIC HEALTH BURDEN, AFFECTING OVER 55 MILLION PEOPLE WORLDWIDE, WITH PROJECTIONS TO NEARLY TRIPLE BY 2050. ROUGHLY ONE-THIRD OF DEMENTIA CASES ARE ATTRIBUTABLE TO MODIFIABLE LIFESTYLE BEHAVIORS, EMPHASIZING THE NEED TO CLARIFY HOW MULTIPLE BEHAVIORS JOINTLY SHAPE RISK. PHYSICAL INACTIVITY, SMOKING, AND OBESITY ARE ESTABLISHED RISK FACTORS, YET EVIDENCE ON ALCOHOL USE AND SOCIAL ISOLATION REMAINS INCONSISTENT, OFTEN LIMITED BY SINGLE-TIMEPOINT MEASURES, INADEQUATE CONTROL FOR CONFOUNDERS, AND FAILURE TO ACCOUNT FOR LIFECOURSE DYNAMICS. HEALTH BEHAVIORS CHANGE ACROSS DECADES, INFLUENCED BY AGING, SOCIAL CONTEXT, AND COHORT EFFECTS, AND INTERACT IN COMPLEX WAYS—FOR EXAMPLE, SMOKING CESSATION MAY INCREASE BMI, WHILE SOCIAL ISOLATION REINFORCES UNHEALTHY TRAJECTORIES. THESE INTERDEPENDENCIES CREATE CUMULATIVE BEHAVIORAL PATHWAYS WITH LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCES FOR COGNITIVE RESERVE AND DEMENTIA RISK, BUT FEW STUDIES HAVE EXAMINED SUCH PATTERNS OVER EXTENDED FOLLOW-UP. THIS R03 PROJECT WILL LEVERAGE THE HEALTH AND RETIREMENT STUDY (HRS), A NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE LONGITUDINAL SURVEY OF U.S. ADULTS AGE 51+, LINKED WITH NEIGHBORHOOD CONTEXTUAL DATA, TO INVESTIGATE HOW PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, SMOKING, ALCOHOL USE, BMI, AND SOCIAL ISOLATION—COEVOLVE AND INFLUENCE COGNITIVE AGING. AIM 1 WILL MODEL LONGITUDINAL TRAJECTORIES OF INDIVIDUAL BEHAVIORS AND THEIR DEMOGRAPHIC AND NEIGHBORHOOD DETERMINANTS. AIM 2 WILL IDENTIFY JOINT MULTIBEHAVIORAL TRAJECTORIES TO CAPTURE BOTH PROTECTIVE AND HIGH-RISK CLUSTERS. AIM 3 WILL EVALUATE CUMULATIVE AND BIDIRECTIONAL ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN BEHAVIORAL TRAJECTORIES AND COGNITIVE DECLINE, MILD COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT (MCI), AND DEMENTIA INCIDENCE (1998–2022). THIS STUDY IS INNOVATIVE IN APPLYING A LIFE-COURSE PERSPECTIVE, INTEGRATING MULTIPLE BEHAVIORS SIMULTANEOUSLY, INCORPORATING HETEROGENEITY BY INDIVIDUAL AND RESIDENTIAL CHARACTERISTICS, AND EMPLOYING A SUITE OF COMPLEMENTARY LONGITUDINAL AND CAUSAL METHODS. BY ELUCIDATING HOW BEHAVIORAL PATTERNS UNFOLD AND CLUSTER OVER TWO DECADES, AND HOW THESE TRAJECTORIES DIFFERENTIALLY PREDICT COGNITIVE DECLINE AND DEMENTIA, THIS PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY PROTECTIVE BEHAVIORAL CONSTELLATIONS, HIGHLIGHT HIGH RISK SUBGROUPS, AND REVEAL CRITICAL WINDOWS FOR INTERVENTION. FINDINGS WILL DIRECTLY INFORM MULTI-DOMAIN STRATEGIES FOR DEMENTIA PREVENTION AND PUBLIC HEALTH POLICY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ELDER MISTREATMENT AND SELF-NEGLECT AMONG PEOPLE LIVING WITH DEMENTIA AND THEIR CAREGIVERS - ABSTRACT ELDER MISTREATMENT (EM) AND SELF-NEGLECT (SN) AMONG OLDER ADULTS WITH ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD) ARE URGENT BUT UNDER-ADDRESSED PUBLIC HEALTH CHALLENGES. AFFECTING AN ESTIMATED 43% AND 37% OF OLDER ADULTS WITH ADRD RESPECTIVELY, EM AND SN CONTRIBUTE TO INJURY, FUNCTIONAL DECLINE, CHRONIC ILLNESS EXACERBATION, INSTITUTIONALIZATION, AND PREMATURE DEATH. YET LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT ADRD-SPECIFIC RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS, THE IMPACT OF EM AND SN ON HEALTH OUTCOMES, OR HOW CHANGES IN DEMENTIA CARE DELIVERY INFLUENCE DETECTION AND RESPONSE. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH LEVERAGES THE UCLA ALZHEIMER’S AND DEMENTIA CARE (ADC) PROGRAM, WHICH MAINTAINS A LARGE, LONGITUDINAL DATASET THAT INCLUDES STRUCTURED DATA AND RICH, UNSTRUCTURED CLINICAL NOTES FROM DEMENTIA CARE SPECIALISTS (DCS). BUILDING ON THE PI’S PRIOR WORK DEVELOPING METHODS TO ABSTRACT EM/SN INFORMATION FROM DCS NOTES, THIS PROJECT WILL EXPAND THE EXISTING DATASET TO INCLUDE THREE COHORTS OF ADC PATIENTS (N=3,212) SPANNING PRE- AND POST-IMPLEMENTATION OF THE CENTERS FOR MEDICARE & MEDICAID SERVICES (CMS) GUIDING AN IMPROVED DEMENTIA CARE EXPERIENCE (GUIDE) MODEL — A NATIONWIDE INITIATIVE THAT ENHANCES STRUCTURED ASSESSMENT, CAREGIVER SUPPORT, AND HOME VISITS. AIM 1 WILL IDENTIFY INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH DOCUMENTATION OF EM/SN AMONG OLDER ADULTS WITH ADRD. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER DOCUMENTED EM/SN CONCERN PREDICTS SURVIVAL AND LONG-TERM CARE PLACEMENT, ADJUSTING FOR DEMENTIA SEVERITY AND COMORBIDITIES. AIM 3 WILL LEVERAGE THE GUIDE MODEL AS A NATURAL EXPERIMENT TO EXAMINE HOW CHANGES IN DEMENTIA CARE DELIVERY INFLUENCE EM/SN DETECTION AND REPORTING, AND WHETHER GUIDE PARTICIPATION MODIFIES ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL CHARACTERISTICS AND EM/SN DETECTION. THIS STUDY WILL GENERATE FOUNDATIONAL EVIDENCE ON THE MULTILEVEL DETERMINANTS OF EM AND SN IN DEMENTIA CARE, ELUCIDATE THE IMPACT OF THESE PHENOMENA ON PATIENT OUTCOMES, AND ASSESS THE ROLE NEW MODELS OF CARE CAN PLAY IN IMPROVING DETECTION AND RESPONSE. FINDINGS WILL INFORM THE DESIGN OF INTERVENTIONS THAT IMPROVE DEMENTIA CARE QUALITY, ENHANCE CAREGIVER SUPPORT, AND ADVANCE ELDER JUSTICE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AYA PATHWAYS: CHARACTERIZING COSTS OF FERTILITY PRESERVATION OPTIONS FOR ADOLESCENT AND YOUNG ADULT CANCER SURVIVORS - PROJECT SUMMARY ACROSS THE US, THERE ARE OVER 2 MILLION AYA CANCER SURVIVORS AND THAT NUMBER CONTINUES TO GROW. ABOUT 80% OF AYAS DIAGNOSED WITH CANCER BECOME LONG-TERM SURVIVORS WITH MANY LIVING WELL INTO ADULTHOOD. WITH THE GROWING NUMBER OF AYA CANCER SURVIVORS, SURVIVORSHIP PLANNING IS CRUCIAL AND INCLUDES QUALITY OF LIFE CONSIDERATIONS, LIKE FERTILITY PRESERVATION. SEVERAL CANCER TYPES AND TREATMENTS CAN CAUSE INFERTILITY, AND THE NEGATIVE EFFECTS OF INFERTILITY-RELATED DISTRESS CAN BE DEVASTATING AND LONG-LASTING—PARTICULARLY FOR AYAS. FERTILITY PRESERVATION METHODS FOR YOUNG MEN INCLUDE SPERM BANKING AND TESTICULAR TISSUE FREEZING. FOR YOUNG WOMEN, THERE ARE SEVERAL MEDICALLY-APPROPRIATE THERAPIES, INCLUDING EGG FREEZING AND OVARIAN TISSUE FREEZING. THESE THERAPIES ARE EFFECTIVE, BUT MAY ALSO BE COSTLY, AS ONLY ABOUT 20 STATES MANDATE INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR FERTILITY PRESERVATION. YET, MANY AYAS MAY STILL NOT QUALIFY FOR COVERAGE AS THEY OFTEN DO NOT MEET INFERTILITY REQUIREMENTS UNTIL THEY REACH ADULTHOOD. ADDITIONALLY, SOME PROCEDURES CAN TAKE UP TO TWO WEEKS, POTENTIALLY DELAYING THE START OF CANCER TREATMENT. THEREFORE, CHOOSING THE “RIGHT” FERTILITY PRESERVATION METHOD FOR EACH AYA AND THEIR FAMILY IS PREFERENCE-SENSITIVE. SPECIFICALLY, THIS DECISION DEPENDS ON BOTH THE MEDICAL EVIDENCE AND THE INFORMED, VALUES-CONCORDANT PREFERENCES OF THE PATIENT. WITH THE MULTITUDE OF COSTS RELATED TO AYA CANCER CARE, FINANCIAL HARDSHIPS ARE DETRIMENTAL TO THE FINANCIAL WELLBEING OF MANY AYAS AND THEIR FAMILIES. FINANCIAL HARDSHIP IS SERIOUS AND ASSOCIATED WITH DIMINISHED HEALTH-RELATED OUTCOMES AND QUALITY OF LIFE AMONG CANCER SURVIVORS. WE PROPOSE CHARACTERIZING THE COSTS OF AYA FERTILITY PRESERVATION CARE, INCLUDING THE DIRECT FINANCIAL BURDEN FROM OUT-OF-POCKET FEES AND THE UNFORESEEN INDIRECT COSTS LIKE TRANSPORTATION AND TIME OFF WORK FOR PARENTS. WE WILL INCORPORATE OUR FINDINGS INTO PATHWAYS FOR AYA TO SUPPORT AYAS AND THEIR FAMILIES AS THEY DECIDE WHETHER TO UNDERGO FERTILITY PRESERVATION AND WHICH FERTILITY PRESERVATION OPTION IS RIGHT FOR THEM. INCORPORATING FERTILITY PRESERVATION COST INFORMATION TO IMPROVE INFORMED DECISION-MAKING BY ENGAGING WITH AYAS, THEIR PARENTS, AND CLINICIANS HAS THE POTENTIAL TO PREPARE PATIENTS AND THEIR FAMILIES FOR MAKING WELL- INFORMED DECISIONS TO IMPROVE QUALITY OF LIFE INTO SURVIVORSHIP.

description: ANNOTATING THE PHENOTYPES OF VARIANTS DRIVING EMBRYONAL BRAIN TUMORS AND BIRTH DEFECTS - PROJECT SUMMARY CHILDREN WITH BIRTH DEFECTS HAVE A SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER INCIDENCE RATE OF EMBRYONAL BRAIN TUMORS. HOWEVER, THE SHARED GENETIC DEFECTS THAT DRIVE BOTH PATHOLOGIES ARE NOT FULLY UNDERSTOOD. SHARED DRIVER GENETIC VARIANTS ARE INCOMPLETELY ANNOTATED. IMPORTANTLY, THE CELLULAR PHENOTYPES INDUCED BY MANY DRIVER VARIANTS ARE UNKNOWN. THESE CRITICAL GAPS IN OUR KNOWLEDGE INHIBIT THE DEVELOPMENT OF DIAGNOSTIC GENETIC TESTS, LIMIT OUR ABILITY TO DEVELOP PRECISION THERAPIES AND CLOUD OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE ETIOLOGIES OF THESE DISEASES. THIS PROPOSAL LEVERAGES OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES OF DATA AND SAMPLES THAT ARE PART OF THE GABRIELLA MILLER KIDS FIRST DATA RESOURCE CENTER. WE PERFORMED SINGLE-NUCLEUS RNA AND EPIGENETIC ASSAYS FROM BRAIN TUMOR TISSUES THAT WERE PATIENT-MATCHED TO THOSE SEQUENCED FOR THE KIDS FIRST DATA RESOURCE CENTER VIA WHOLE-GENOME AND WHOLE- EXOME APPROACHES. THESE PATIENT-MATCHED SINGLE-CELL AND BULK-SEQUENCING DATA PROVIDE A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO IDENTIFY THE CELLULAR POPULATIONS THAT HARBOR DRIVER VARIANTS AND UNDERSTAND HOW THE PRESENCE OF THOSE VARIANTS ALTERS GENE EXPRESSION AND EPIGENETIC PHENOTYPES. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ANNOTATE KNOWN AND NOVEL DRIVER GENETIC VARIANTS THAT ARE SHARED BETWEEN EMBRYONAL BRAIN TUMORS AND CONGENITAL DISEASES WITH GENE EXPRESSION AND EPIGENETIC SIGNATURES. IN AIM 1, WE ANNOTATE EMBRYONAL BRAIN-TUMOR DRIVER VARIANTS AND THEIR PREVALENCE IN POPULATIONS WITH BIRTH DEFECTS, USING STATISTICAL METRICS OF SELECTION PRESSURE. IN AIM 2, WE IDENTIFY EXPRESSION PHENOTYPES AND EPIGENETIC SIGNATURES ASSOCIATED WITH BRAIN-TUMOR DRIVER VARIANTS AND BIRTH DEFECT-ASSOCIATED VARIANTS IN BRAIN-TUMOR AND NON-MALIGNANT CELL TYPES, USING OUR MATED SINGLE-CELL DATA AND OTHER SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA. THE RATIONALE FOR THESE STUDIES IS TWOFOLD: FIRSTLY, WE WILL IDENTIFY NOVEL VARIANTS THAT ARE DRIVERS OF BRAIN TUMOR DEVELOPMENT AND PREVALENT IN POPULATIONS WITH BIRTH DEFECTS. SECONDLY, ANNOTATING THE ABERRANT GENE EXPRESSION AND EPIGENETIC SIGNATURES INDUCED BY DRIVER VARIANTS WILL ALLOW US TO IDENTIFY THE CELL TYPES CRITICALLY AFFECTED BY THESE VARIANTS AND HYPOTHESIZE ABOUT THEIR FUNCTIONAL EFFECT. THIS PROJECT’S IMPACT COMES FROM COMBINING MULTIPLE PATIENT-MATCHED GENOMICS MODALITIES. WHILE SOME GENES ASSOCIATED WITH BOTH CANCER AND BIRTH DEFECTS ARE KNOWN, OUR PRELIMINARY DATA INDICATE THAT THIS LIST IS FAR FROM BEING COMPREHENSIVE. IDENTIFYING MUTATIONS THAT BOTH DRIVE BRAIN TUMORS AND ARE ASSOCIATED WITH BIRTH DEFECTS IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT ENHANCES OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING BOTH CONDITIONS. THIS KNOWLEDGE CAN LEAD TO IMPROVED DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS AND TARGETED THERAPIES FOR AFFECTED INDIVIDUALS. SURPRISINGLY LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW DRIVER VARIANTS ALTER CELLULAR PHENOTYPES IN CANCER AND IN DEVELOPMENT OR WHAT CELL TYPES ARE SIGNIFICANTLY ALTERED. THIS STUDY BRIDGES THAT GAP BY ASSOCIATING GENOTYPE TO PHENOTYPE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: APPLICATION OF MEDIATION MIXTURE MODELING AND MACHINE LEARNING TO UNDERSTAND HETEROGENEITY OF RISK PATHWAYS ON YOUTH'S ONSET OF SUBSTANCE USE - ABSTRACT THE LITERATURE HIGHLIGHTS THE COMPLEX INTERPLAY OF FACTORS INFLUENCING THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUBSTANCE USE. TO INCREASE THE ACCURACY OF IDENTIFYING AT-RISK GROUPS FOR SUBSTANCE USE, THIS SECONDARY DATA ANALYSIS PROJECT AIMS TO APPLY ADVANCED QUANTITATIVE METHODS IN STUDYING THE HETEROGENEITY OF RISK PATHWAYS LEADING TO YOUTH'S EARLY INITIATION OF SUBSTANCE USE, USING THE ADOLESCENT BRAIN COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT (ABCD) STUDY®, A NATIONAL LONGITUDINAL DATASET IN TRACKING YOUTHS' BEHAVIORAL HEALTH. INFORMED BY TWO MODELS IN EXPLAINING THE ETIOLOGY OF EARLY SUBSTANCE USE, THE DEVIANCE PRONENESS MODEL AND THE NEGATIVE AFFECT REGULATION MODEL, THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL EXAMINE THE FOLLOWING MEDIATION PATHWAYS: PARENT MENTAL HEALTH  YOUTH EXTERNALIZING SPECTRUM  SUBSTANCE USE; IN THE NEGATIVE AFFECT REGULATION MODEL: PARENT MENTAL HEALTH  YOUTH INTERNALIZING SPECTRUM  SUBSTANCE USE. WITH THE RECOGNITION OF THE MULTIFACETED NATURE OF THE ETIOLOGY OF SUBSTANCE USE, PRIOR STUDIES ASSUME HOMOGENEITY IN TESTING RISK MECHANISMS, REVEALING ONLY DOMINANT PATHWAYS SHARED BY MOST PARTICIPANTS, NEGLECTING SUBGROUP-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS. PRIOR STUDIES USING MACHINE LEARNING DATA-DRIVEN APPROACH PRIMARILY FOCUSED ON THE PREDICTION OF SUBSTANCE USE, WITH LESS EMPHASIS ON CONNECTING WITH THEORY- DRIVEN MEDIATION APPROACH. BUILT ON RECENT ADVANCES IN METHODOLOGY, THIS IS THE FIRST STUDY TO ENSEMBLE APPROACHES, COMBING THEORY-DRIVEN MEDIATION APPROACH AND DATA-DRIVEN MACHINE LEARNING APPROACH, TO EXPLORE THE COMPLEX INTERACTIVE FEATURES OF FACTORS IN CHARACTERIZING GROUP-SPECIFIC RISK MECHANISMS. THE STUDY AIMS TO ASSESS HETEROGENEITY IN MEDIATION PATHWAYS IN INFLUENCING EARLY SUBSTANCE USE AMONG YOUTH. SPECIFICALLY, THIS STUDY WILL EXPLORE TWO DIFFERENT APPROACHES IN ENSEMBLING MULTIPLE METHODS: DECISION TREE- STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELING (DT-SEM), AND COMBINED MEDIATION MIXTURE MODELING (MMM) AND CLASSIFICATION TREE METHOD TO ADDRESS THE MEDIATION PATHWAYS AND ASSOCIATIONS INVOLVING DISTINCT GENETIC, FAMILY AND ENVIRONMENTAL BACKGROUNDS. IN THE FORMAL APPROACH, THE MEDIATION MODEL WILL BE SPLIT INTO DIFFERENT SUBCLASSES BASED ON THE PREDICTIVE FACTORS VIA DECISION TREE MODELING. IN THE LATTER APPROACH, THE MMM COMBINES THE MIXTURE MODEL AND MEDIATION MODEL TO ESTIMATE THE HETEROGENEITY OF THEORY-DRIVEN PATHWAYS INTO SUBCLASSES, THEN, THE CLASSIFICATION TREE ESTIMATES THE PREDICTION OF THE ENUMERATED SUBCLASSES WITH A LARGE NUMBER OF OBSERVED GENETIC, FAMILY AND ENVIRONMENTAL VARIABLES TO UNDERSTAND THE FEATURES OF THE SUBCLASSES. THE EMPLOYMENT OF THESE TWO APPROACHES AIMS TO PROVIDE COMPLEMENTARY PERSPECTIVES FOR IDENTIFYING SUBGROUPS TO ENSURE A DEEPER UNDERSTANDING OF HETEROGENEITY OF MEDIATION PATHWAYS TO YOUTH SUBSTANCE USE. RESULTS WILL IDENTIFY SUBGROUPS THAT ARE VULNERABLE TO SPECIFIC RISK MECHANISMS, IN AN EFFORT TO UNRAVEL THE MULTIFACETED NATURE OF EARLY SUBSTANCE USE. ULTIMATELY, RESULTS WILL INFORM PERSONALIZED INTERVENTIONS FOR IDENTIFYING AT-RISK YOUTH WITH EARLY INITIATION OF SUBSTANCE USE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENGINEERING THE DEGRADATION OF DECELLULARIZED PLANT SCAFFOLDS FOR HARD TISSUE ENGINEERING - PROJECT SUMMARY DESPITE RECENT ADVANCES IN FABRICATION TECHNOLOGY, SYNTHETIC SCAFFOLDS DEVELOPED TO ADDRESS THE CHRONIC SHORTAGE OF DONOR TISSUES FOR CRANIOFACIAL RECONSTRUCTION ARE CONSTRAINED BY THEIR SCALABILITY, HIGH-COST IMPLICATIONS, AND INABILITY TO REPLICATE THE STRUCTURAL COMPLEXITIES OF NATURAL EXTRACELLULAR MATRICES (ECMS) THAT PROVIDE STRUCTURAL CUES FOR REGULATING CELL-MATRIX INTERACTIONS AND TISSUE FORMATION. DECELLULARIZED PLANT SCAFFOLDS, WHICH HAVE PHYSICAL AND STRUCTURAL SIMILARITIES TO NATURAL ECMS, HAVE EMERGED AS VIABLE PLATFORMS FOR CELL PROLIFERATION AND TISSUE FORMATION, HELPING TO CIRCUMVENT THE SUPPLY ISSUES, HIGH COSTS, AND LARGE-SCALE PRODUCTION CONSTRAINTS OF DECELLULARIZED TISSUE-DERIVED ECMS. ALTHOUGH ATTRACTIVE, THE PRIMARY CHALLENGE OF USING PLANT SCAFFOLDS LIES IN THEIR LIMITED DEGRADATION IN THE HUMAN TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENT DUE TO THE ABSENCE OF CELLULASES TO ATTACK THE Β(1-4) LINKAGES IN PLANT STRUCTURES. CONSEQUENTLY, DESIGNING PLANT SCAFFOLD DEGRADATION STRATEGIES HAS GARNERED INTENSE INTEREST AS AN ESSENTIAL PARADIGM TO MEDIATE TEMPORO-SPATIAL 3D TISSUE FORMATION AND REMODELING. A KEY QUESTION REMAINS WHETHER PLANT SCAFFOLD DEGRADATION CAN BE TUNED TO MATCH CELL GROWTH AND TISSUE REGENERATION TO ENHANCE THE QUALITY OF REGENERATED TISSUES. IN THIS PROJECT, WE PROPOSE TO ENGINEER THE CONTROLLED DEGRADATION OF DECELLULARIZED LUCKY BAMBOO (MODEL PLANT SCAFFOLD) AS A PLATFORM FOR BONE TISSUE ENGINEERING (MODEL TISSUE) BASED ON (I) REMOTE-CONTROLLED, ULTRASOUND-TRIGGERED CELLULASE RELEASE FROM MICROBUBBLES TO BREAK DOWN CELLULOSE IN THE PLANT STRUCTURE, AND (II) AI/MACHINE LEARNING-DRIVEN, IMAGE-GUIDED MONITORING OF DEGRADATION PROFILES. THIS WILL BE EXPLORED THROUGH THREE SPECIFIC AIMS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DEVELOP ULTRASOUND-RESPONSIVE, CELLULASE- ENCAPSULATED POLY(LACTIC-CO-GLYCOLIC ACID) (PLGA) MICROBUBBLES THAT CAN BE DIRECTLY INJECTED INTO SCAFFOLDS AND REMOTELY TRIGGERED USING ULTRASOUND TO REGULATE CELLULASE RELEASE. AIM 2 WILL CONCENTRATE ON MEASURING THE EFFECTS OF CELLULASE RELEASE ON THE DEGRADATION OF DECELLULARIZED BAMBOO SCAFFOLDS BY QUANTIFYING CHANGES IN WEIGHT, COMPRESSIVE MECHANICAL PROPERTIES, AND THE AMOUNT OF SUGAR FRAGMENTS PRODUCED FROM CELLULOSE BREAKDOWN. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL IMPLEMENT MACHINE LEARNING (ML) ALGORITHMS TO DIRECTLY PREDICT DEGRADATION LEVELS USING RAW MICRO-COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (MICRO-CT) AND ULTRASOUND IMAGES OF THE SCAFFOLDS, VALIDATED AGAINST THE PHYSICO- CHEMICAL DEGRADATION METRICS (SCAFFOLD WEIGHT LOSS, COMPRESSIVE PROPERTIES, AND SUGAR FRAGMENT DEGRADATION PRODUCTS). IN AIM 3, WE WILL QUANTIFY CELL RESPONSES TO THE CELLULASE, DECELLULARIZED SCAFFOLD, DEGRADATION PRODUCTS, AND FOCUSED ULTRASOUND WAVES. ULTIMATELY, WE ANTICIPATE THAT INSIGHTS FROM THIS PILOT STUDY WILL FACILITATE A COMPREHENSIVE FOLLOW-UP PROJECT TO DEVELOP OUR NOVEL REMOTE-CONTROLLED DEGRADATION TECHNIQUE IN VIVO, PAVING THE WAY FOR UTILIZING DECELLULARIZED PLANT SCAFFOLDS IN CRANIOFACIAL RECONSTRUCTION.

description: BRIDGING THE GAP IN PEDIATRIC TMD AND MIGRAINE THROUGH MULTIDIMENSIONAL PHENOTYPING AND PRECISION PAIN PROFILING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CHRONIC PAIN DURING ADOLESCENCE IS OFTEN UNDERRECOGNIZED AND INADEQUATELY TREATED, CONTRIBUTING TO LONG-TERM DISABILITY ACROSS THE LIFESPAN. TEMPOROMANDIBULAR DISORDERS (TMD) AND MIGRAINE ARE AMONG THE MOST DISABLING CHRONIC PAIN CONDITIONS IN ADOLESCENCE, YET THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THEIR CO-OCCURRENCE REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT NEARLY 60% OF ADOLESCENTS WITH PAINFUL TMD REPORT COMORBID HEADACHE, A SUBGROUP CHARACTERIZED BY ELEVATED PAIN INTENSITY, GREATER FUNCTIONAL IMPAIRMENT, AND INCREASED PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS. ALTHOUGH ADULT STUDIES HAVE IDENTIFIED MIGRAINE AS A SIGNIFICANT RISK FACTOR FOR THE ONSET AND PERSISTENCE OF TMD PAIN, NO PEDIATRIC STUDIES HAVE INTEGRATED MOLECULAR, SENSORY, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL DATA TO PHENOTYPE YOUTH WITH COMORBID TMD AND MIGRAINE. THIS CRITICAL GAP IMPEDES EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF HIGH-RISK SUBGROUPS AND HINDERS EFFORTS TO PERSONALIZE TREATMENT DURING A KEY DEVELOPMENTAL WINDOW, INCREASING THE RISK OF CHRONIC PAIN PERSISTENCE INTO ADULTHOOD. THE LONG-TERM OBJECTIVE OF OUR PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO ADVANCE INDIVIDUALIZED PAIN MANAGEMENT FOR YOUTH WITH COMORBID TMD AND MIGRAINE BY APPLYING MACHINE LEARNING TO STRATIFY PATIENTS BASED ON INTEGRATED BIOLOGICAL, SENSORY, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL RISK SIGNATURES. A CRITICAL FIRST STEP IS TO ESTABLISH A MULTIDIMENSIONAL DATASET ENCOMPASSING SALIVARY BIOMARKERS, QUANTITATIVE SENSORY TESTING, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL PROFILING TO CHARACTERIZE PHENOTYPIC SIGNATURES IN ADOLESCENTS WITH TMD, WITH AND WITHOUT COMORBID MIGRAINE. THIS APPLICATION WILL APPLY A NOVEL MULTIMODAL PHENOTYPING FRAMEWORK TO CHARACTERIZE NEUROIMMUNE, SENSORY, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL FACTORS CONTRIBUTING TO COMORBID TMD AND MIGRAINE IN ADOLESCENTS BY RECRUITING 140 YOUTH AGED 10 TO 17 YEARS WITH TMD MYALGIA, STRATIFIED BY THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF MIGRAINE. AIM 1 WILL QUANTIFY SALIVARY LEVELS OF PRO-INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES AND NEUROPEPTIDES, ALONGSIDE CRANIOFACIAL PRESSURE AND THERMAL PAIN THRESHOLDS, TO INVESTIGATE NEUROIMMUNE CORRELATES OF PAIN AND ALTERED NOCICEPTIVE PROCESSING. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS PAIN BURDEN, FUNCTIONAL DISABILITY, SOMATIC SYMPTOMS, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL FUNCTION USING VALIDATED, DEVELOPMENTALLY RELEVANT SELF-REPORT MEASURES, AND WILL EXAMINE THEIR CONVERGENCE WITH BIOLOGICAL AND SENSORY DATA FROM AIM 1 TO ELUCIDATE INTEGRATED BIOBEHAVIORAL MECHANISMS. COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS WILL YIELD A MULTIDIMENSIONAL DATASET THAT DIRECTLY SUPPORTS MY FUTURE R01 FOCUSED ON APPLYING MACHINE LEARNING TO PREDICT TREATMENT RESPONSE AND ADVANCE PERSONALIZED PAIN MANAGEMENT FOR YOUTH WITH COMORBID TMD AND MIGRAINE. BY INTEGRATING BIOLOGICAL, SENSORY, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL DATA, THIS STUDY WILL IDENTIFY DISTINCT CLINICAL AND MECHANISTIC PROFILES THAT DIFFERENTIATE ADOLESCENTS WITH TMD ALONE FROM THOSE WITH COMORBID MIGRAINE, LAYING THE GROUNDWORK FOR DATA-DRIVEN PHENOTYPING AND TREATMENT STRATIFICATION. THE PROPOSED WORK LEVERAGES A COLLABORATIVE, INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM OF EXPERIENCED AND EARLY-CAREER INVESTIGATORS TO ENSURE METHODOLOGICAL RIGOR AND TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEFINING MOLECULAR INTERACTIONS BETWEEN COMMENSAL RESPIRATORY VIRUSES AND THE HUMAN HOST - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT WHILE RESPIRATORY PATHOGENS HAVE RECEIVED SIGNIFICANT ATTENTION FROM THE RESEARCH COMMUNITY, WE HAVE A LIMITED UNDERSTANDING OF THE MOST ABUNDANT COMMENSAL VIRUSES IN THE HUMAN RESPIRATORY TRACT AND THEIR INTERACTION WITH THE HOST TO MAINTAIN HOMEOSTASIS IN HEALTHY INDIVIDUALS. THE PROJECT’S RESEARCH TEAM HAS SIGNIFICANTLY CONTRIBUTED TO UNDERSTANDING THE INTERACTION BETWEEN PATHOGENIC RESPIRATORY VIRUSES AND THE HUMAN HOST. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO LEVERAGE CUTTING-EDGE TECHNIQUES WE HAVE DEVELOPED IN SEQUENCING, PROTEOMICS, VIRAL GENETICS AND PRIMARY CELL MODELS TO STUDY INTERACTIONS BETWEEN COMMENSAL VIRUSES IN THE HUMAN RESPIRATORY TRACT AND THE HOST. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT COMMENSAL VIRUSES ESTABLISH UNIQUE MOLECULAR INTERACTIONS WITH THE RESPIRATORY EPITHELIUM THAT ENABLE PERSISTENCE AND MODULATE IMMUNE HOMEOSTASIS. THE RATIONALE FOR THIS PROJECT IS THAT UNDERSTANDING HOW COMMENSAL RESPIRATORY VIRUSES REPLICATE AND PERSIST IN THE HOST, WITHOUT CAUSING DISEASE, WILL OFFER INSIGHTS INTO THE FACTORS THAT INFLUENCE HOST IMMUNITY, DISEASE SUSCEPTIBILITY, AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE. THIS WILL BE TESTED VIA TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) GENERATE MOLECULAR CLONES OF THE TOP ABUNDANT COMMENSAL VIRUSES OF THE RESPIRATORY TRACT AND CHARACTERIZE VIRAL INFECTION AND HOST RESPONSES IN PRIMARY HUMAN AIRWAY ORGANOIDS (HAOS) AND 2) MAP VIRUS-HOST PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTION (PPI) NETWORKS. UNDER THE FIRST AIM, WE WILL DEVELOP MOLECULAR CLONES AND CHARACTERIZE THEIR INFECTION IN HAOS WITH SINGLE-CELL RNA-SEQUENCING. FOR THE SECOND AIM, PPI NETWORK MAPS FOR COMMENSAL RESPIRATORY VIRUSES WILL BE MAPPED WITH AFFINITY-PURIFICATION MASS SPECTROMETRY AND THE IDENTIFIED FUNCTIONAL INTERACTIONS WILL BE TESTED BY GENERATING KNOCKOUTS IN ORGANOIDS. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS INNOVATIVE AS IT GOES BEYOND THE STATUS QUO OF IDENTIFICATION OF COMMENSAL VIRUSES TO MOLECULARLY CHARACTERIZING THEIR REPLICATION AND INTERACTION WITH THE HOST. THE PROPOSED WORK IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT ADDRESSES AN IMPORTANT AND YET UNDEREXPLORED ASPECT OF RESPIRATORY HEALTH, NAMELY THE BENEFIT OF HOMEOSTATIC COLONIZATION WITH EUKARYOTIC COMMENSAL VIRUSES. ULTIMATELY, SUCH KNOWLEDGE CAN OFFER NEW INSIGHT INTO RESPIRATORY TRACT HOMEOSTASIS AND CONTRIBUTIONS OF THE COMMENSAL VIROME TO DISEASE TRAJECTORIES. TO SUPPORT THE NIH’S MISSION, THE TEAM WILL WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH ALL THE HVP CONSORTIUM INVESTIGATORS TO ENSURE THE INTEGRATION AND SHARING OF DATA, TOOLS AND RESOURCES ACROSS THE PROGRAM AND THE BROADER SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DISCOVERY OF PROKARYOTIC RNA VIRUS-HOST PAIRS THROUGH A SCALABLE REVERSE-GENETICS PLATFORM - PROJECT SUMMARY THE HUMAN VIROME IS AN EXPANSIVE AND LARGELY UNCHARTED LAYER OF THE MICROBIOME THAT CONTRIBUTES SIGNIFICANTLY TO HUMAN HEALTH AND DISEASE. RECENT METATRANSCRIPTOMIC SURVEYS HAVE UNCOVERED AN UNEXPECTED ABUNDANCE OF RNA-BASED AGENTS IN THE MICROBIOME, INCLUDING BOTH RNA VIRUSES AND CIRCULAR RNA REPLICONS THAT APPEAR TO COLONIZE BACTERIA. DESPITE THEIR PREVALENCE, THEIR BIOLOGICAL ROLES REMAIN UNDEFINED, AS THE VAST MAJORITY HAVE NEITHER BEEN ISOLATED NOR ASSIGNED DEFINITIVE BACTERIAL HOSTS. THIS LIMITS OUR ABILITY TO DETERMINE HOW THESE RNA ELEMENTS REPLICATE, HOW THEY INFLUENCE THEIR BACTERIAL HOSTS, AND THEIR OVERALL IMPACT ON HUMAN HEALTH. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ESTABLISH THE FIRST UNIFIED REVERSE-GENETICS PLATFORMS FOR RECONSTRUCTING CIRCULAR AND LINEAR RNA GENOMES DIRECTLY INSIDE BACTERIAL CELLS. FIRST, WE WILL DEVELOP RIBOZYME-DRIVEN SYSTEMS TO RECREATE CIRCULAR RNAS AND LINEAR RNA PHAGE GENOMES, ENABLING CONTROLLED RECONSTITUTION OF NEWLY DISCOVERED RNA ELEMENTS. THEN, WE WILL COMBINE THESE PLATFORMS WITH MASSIVELY PARALLEL DE NOVO GENE SYNTHESIS TO SCREEN THOUSANDS OF CANDIDATE RNA PHAGES AND CIRCRNAS FOR THEIR ABILITY TO REPLICATE IN DIVERSE HUMAN-ASSOCIATED BACTERIA. THIS WILL EXPERIMENTALLY IDENTIFY REPLICATION-COMPETENT RNA ELEMENT-HOST PAIRS. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL TRANSFORM A PORTION OF THE HUMAN RNA VIROME FROM A CATALOG OF METAGENOMIC SEQUENCES INTO TRACTABLE EXPERIMENTAL SYSTEMS. BY DEFINING GENUINE BACTERIAL HOSTS AND ESTABLISHING MODEL SYSTEMS, THIS WORK WILL UNCOVER FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES GOVERNING RNA REPLICATION IN PROKARYOTES, ILLUMINATE HOW RNA ELEMENTS CONTRIBUTE TO MICROBIOME ECOLOGY, AND PROVIDE ESSENTIAL TOOLS FOR INVESTIGATING THIS LARGELY UNEXPLORED COMPONENT OF HUMAN HEALTH.

description: SPATIAL STRUCTURE-BASED ANNOTATION OF PROTEINS FOR THE NIH HUMAN VIROME PROGRAM - PROJECT SUMMARY  STRUCTURAL ANNOTATION INFRASTRUCTURE FOR THE NIH HUMAN VIROME PROGRAM THE HUMAN VIROME PROFOUNDLY SHAPES GUT MICROBIOME COMPOSITION, HOST IMMUNITY, AND DEVELOPMENT, YET OUR FUNCTIONAL UNDERSTANDING OF ITS COMPONENTS IS LIMITED BY MASSIVE ANNOTATION GAPS. THE NIH HUMAN VIROME PROGRAM (HVP) GENERATES UNPRECEDENTED VIROME DATASETS FROM ~2,000 INDIVIDUALS, BUT 50-90% OF VIRAL SEQUENCES IN THESE DATASETS REMAIN FUNCTIONALLY UNANNOTATED  DARK MATTER . THIS ANNOTATION BOTTLENECK ARISES FROM THE FAST-EVOLVING NATURE OF VIRUSES, WHICH CAUSES PROTEIN SEQUENCES TO DIVERGE BEYOND RECOGNITION BY STANDARD HOMOLOGY SEARCH TOOLS. IN CONTRAST, PROTEIN STRUCTURES ARE SUBSTANTIALLY MORE CONSERVED THAN SEQUENCES, ENABLING FUNCTIONAL ANNOTATION EVEN ACROSS EXTREME SEQUENCE DIVERGENCE. AS DEVELOPERS OF THE EVOLUTIONARY CLASSIFICATION OF DOMAINS (ECOD) DATABASE, WE ARE UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO LEVERAGE LARGE-SCALE ALPHAFOLD-PREDICTED STRUCTURES AND STRUCTURE-GUIDED HOMOLOGY INFERENCE TO BRIDGE THIS GAP. OUR PROOF-OF-CONCEPT ANALYSIS OF 339K VIRAL PROTEINS DEMONSTRATES THAT STRUCTURE-BASED CLASSIFICATION CAN TRACE THE EVOLUTIONARY ORIGINS FOR 47-67% OF THE VIRAL PROTEOME—A 3- TO 4-FOLD IMPROVEMENT OVER SEQUENCE-BASED METHODS ALONE. WE WILL ADDRESS THE VIROME ANNOTATION CHALLENGE THROUGH TWO COMPLEMENTARY AIMS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL ESTABLISH A PRODUCTION-SCALE, AUTOMATED PIPELINE THAT PROCESSES RAW METAGENOMIC DATA THROUGH ASSEMBLY, VIRAL CONTIG IDENTIFICATION, GENE PREDICTION, 3D STRUCTURE MODELING (USING ALPHAFOLD3), AND STRUCTURAL CLASSIFICATION. KEY INNOVATIONS INCLUDE STRUCTURE-AIDED VIRAL CONTIG RESCUE AND ITERATIVE MODELING TO PROPERLY HANDLE POLYPROTEINS, OBLIGATE OLIGOMERS, AND PARTIAL PROTEINS. WE WILL APPLY THIS PIPELINE TO PROCESS HVP DATASETS, EXPECTING TO ASSIGN FOLD GROUPS (ECOD T-GROUPS) AND PREDICT GENERAL FUNCTIONS FOR 50-70% OF VIRAL DOMAINS BASED ON THE CONTEXT PROVIDED BY THE EXISTING ECOD HIERARCHY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL PARTITION 200 VIRAL-RICH STRUCTURAL FOLD GROUPS (COVERING 80% OF VIRAL DOMAINS) INTO SPECIFIC SEQUENCE FAMILIES (ECOD F-GROUPS) AND CHARACTERIZE 100 ENTIRELY NOVEL VIRAL PROTEIN FAMILIES FROM CURRENTLY UNCLASSIFIABLE DOMAINS. BY SYSTEMATICALLY INTEGRATING EXPERIMENTAL AND PREDICTIVE EVIDENCE REGARDING VIRAL PROTEIN FUNCTIONS INTO OUR CLASSIFICATION PROCESS, WE WILL PROVIDE DETAILED FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTIONS FOR EACH FAMILY. WE EXPECT TO CLASSIFY 40-60% OF VIRAL DOMAINS INTO EXISTING AND NEW FAMILIES IN ECOD (F-GROUPS). FURTHERMORE, BY GENERATING STRUCTURE-GUIDED HMM PROFILES FOR EACH FAMILY, WE WILL EMPOWER THE BROADER SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY TO PERFORM EFFICIENT SEQUENCE-BASED VIRAL PROTEIN ANNOTATION. THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A ROBUST ANNOTATION INFRASTRUCTURE INTEGRATED WITH HVP CONSORTIUM DATA SYSTEMS, TRANSFORMING VIRAL  DARK MATTER  INTO FUNCTIONALLY ANNOTATED PROTEINS. THIS RESOURCE WILL HELP THE HVP CONSORTIUM AND THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY TO DECIPHER THE EVOLUTION AND FUNCTION OF HUMAN-ASSOCIATED VIRAL PROTEINS. TESTABLE FUNCTIONAL HYPOTHESES GENERATED BY US WILL ACCELERATE THE EXPERIMENTAL CHARACTERIZATION OF CRITICAL VIRAL PROTEINS AND ULTIMATELY INFORM NOVEL STRATEGIES TO MODULATE THE VIROME FOR THERAPEUTIC BENEFIT.

description: AN INTEGRATED ANALYTICAL FRAMEWORK FOR HUMAN VIROME STUDIES: VALIDATION, STANDARDIZATION, AND STATISTICAL INNOVATION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE HUMAN VIROME PROGRAM (HVP) AIMS TO COMPREHENSIVELY CHARACTERIZE VIRAL COMMUNITIES ACROSS HUMAN BODY SITES IN HEALTH AND DISEASE. HOWEVER, VIROME RESEARCH LACKS BENCHMARKING INFRASTRUCTURE TO VALIDATE COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS, EVALUATE STATISTICAL METHODS, AND ESTABLISH QUALITY CONTROL STANDARDS. UNLIKE BACTERIAL MICROBIOME RESEARCH, WHICH BENEFITS FROM MOCK COMMUNITIES AND STANDARDIZED WORKFLOWS, VIROME RESEARCHERS CANNOT RIGOROUSLY ASSESS WHETHER TOOLS CORRECTLY IDENTIFY VIRUSES, WHETHER ABUNDANCE ESTIMATES ARE ACCURATE, OR WHETHER STATISTICAL METHODS PERFORM APPROPRIATELY ON EXTREMELY SPARSE DATA (70-95% ZEROS). THIS METHODOLOGICAL GAP THREATENS HVP SCIENTIFIC RIGOR AND REPRODUCIBILITY. THIS R03 WILL CREATE AN INTEGRATED BENCHMARKING ECOSYSTEM FOR VIROME RESEARCH COMBINING THREE ELEMENTS: (1) SYNTHETIC GROUND-TRUTH VALIDATION DATA VIA VIROFORGE, (2) VIROME-SPECIFIC DATA INFRASTRUCTURE VIA VIROMEDATA, AND (3) SYSTEMATIC STATISTICAL VALIDATION FOR SPARSE DATA. AIM 1 WILL ENHANCE VIROFORGE, A PRODUCTION-READY SYNTHETIC VIROME PLATFORM, TO GENERATE HVP-VALIDATED DATASETS COVERING DIVERSE BODY SITES, SEQUENCING PLATFORMS, AND STUDY DESIGNS INCLUDING LONGITUDINAL SAMPLING AND BATCH EFFECTS. WE WILL VALIDATE ERROR MODELS AGAINST REAL HVP CONSORTIUM DATA ENSURING SYNTHETIC DATA ACCURATELY REFLECTS ACTUAL SEQUENCING CHARACTERISTICS. AIM 2 WILL DEVELOP VIROMEDATA, A VIROME-SPECIFIC EXTENSION OF BIOCONDUCTOR’S SUMMARIZEDEXPERIMENT PROVIDING STANDARDIZED INFRASTRUCTURE AND TOOL INTEGRATION. VIROMEDATA WILL INCORPORATE BALTIMORE CLASSIFICATION, RDRP CLASSIFIER INTEGRATION, AND VIRUS-HOST ASSOCIATION TRACKING, WITH BOTH R AND PYTHON IMPLEMENTATIONS ENSURING BROAD ACCESSIBILITY. AIM 3 WILL SYSTEMATICALLY VALIDATE STATISTICAL METHODS ON SPARSE VIROME DATA, TESTING WHETHER COMPOSITIONALLY-AWARE METHODS (ANCOM-BC, ALDEX2, AITCHISON DISTANCE) OUTPERFORM BORROWED RNA-SEQ AND MICROBIOME APPROACHES (DESEQ2, BRAY-CURTIS). WE WILL EVALUATE DIFFERENTIAL ABUNDANCE METHODS, DIVERSITY METRICS, AND NORMALIZATION APPROACHES ACROSS VARYING SPARSITY LEVELS (50-95% ZEROS), GENERATING POWER CURVES AND SAMPLE SIZE RECOMMENDATIONS. THE PI SERVES AS CO-PI ON THE HVP CODCC (U24HL175772), ENSURING CONSORTIUM INTEGRATION, DATASET ACCESS, AND DISSEMINATION CHANNELS. BUILDING ON PROVEN TECHNOLOGIES (VIROFORGE V0.10.0, BIOCONDUCTOR SUMMARIZEDEXPERIMENT) MINIMIZES RISK WHILE MAXIMIZING IMPACT. DELIVERABLES INCLUDE VIROFORGE V2.0 WITH HVP-VALIDATED PARAMETERS, VIROMEDATA PACKAGES VIA BIOCONDUCTOR AND PYPI, STATISTICAL VALIDATION RESULTS WITH BEST PRACTICES GUIDELINES, AND TRAINING MATERIALS. THIS ESTABLISHES THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE BENCHMARKING PLATFORM FOR VIROME RESEARCH, PROVIDING VALIDATED TOOLS, QUALITY CONTROL STANDARDS, AND STANDARDIZED INFRASTRUCTURE ENABLING RIGOROUS, REPRODUCIBLE SCIENCE.

description: TYPE-2 CYTOKINE REGULATION OF TUFT CELL DIFFERENTIATION IN SALIVARY GLANDS - PROJECT SUMMARY TUFT CELLS ARE RARE CHEMOSENSORY EPITHELIAL CELLS THAT ACT AS SENTINELS BY SENSING ENVIRONMENTAL CUES AND RELEASING MEDIATORS SUCH AS INTERLEUKIN (IL)-25, ACETYLCHOLINE, PROSTAGLANDINS AND LEUKOTRIENES. IN INTESTINE AND AIRWAY, TYPE-2 CYTOKINES (IL-4, IL-13, IL-25) ORCHESTRATE TUFT CELL DIFFERENTIATION THROUGH A FEED-FORWARD CIRCUIT: IL- 25 FROM TUFT CELLS ACTIVATES GROUP 2 INNATE LYMPHOID CELLS, WHICH RELEASE IL-4 AND IL-13 TO DRIVE FURTHER TUFT CELL EMERGENCE FROM PROGENITORS, REMODELING EPITHELIUM AND AMPLIFYING TYPE-2 TONE. IN SALIVARY GLANDS, OUR GROUP HAS DEMONSTRATED THE PRESENCE OF TUFT CELLS IN MOUSE AND HUMAN SUBMANDIBULAR GLANDS. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES SHOW THAT MICE LACKING TUFT CELLS HAVE DISRUPTED SUBMANDIBULAR GLAND TRANSCRIPTOME, MORPHOLOGY AND SECRETION INDICATING THAT TUFT CELLS ARE REQUIRED FOR EPITHELIAL INTEGRITY IN THIS GLAND. WE ALSO OBSERVE INCREASED TUFT CELL NUMBERS IN MINOR SALIVARY GLAND BIOPSIES FROM SJÖGREN’S DISEASE PATIENTS AND IN SJÖGREN’S DISEASE -LIKE MOUSE MODEL VERSUS CONTROLS. PARTICULARLY, SJÖGREN’S DISEASE IS A SYSTEMIC AUTOIMMUNE DISORDER OF THE SALIVARY AND LACRIMAL GLANDS THAT CAUSES DRY MOUTH AND EYE AND PREDOMINANTLY AFFECTS WOMEN. IMPORTANTLY, PRIOR STUDIES REPORT THAT IL-4, IL-13, AND IL-25 ARE ELEVATED IN SJÖGREN’S DISEASE AND CONTRIBUTE TO EPITHELIAL DAMAGE, IMMUNE INFILTRATION, AND SECRETORY DYSFUNCTION, YET WHETHER THESE CYTOKINES REGULATE TUFT CELL DIFFERENTIATION IN SALIVARY GLANDS HAS NEVER BEEN TESTED. THEREFORE, THIS R03 WILL ADDRESS THIS GAP BY TESTING THE OVERALL HYPOTHESIS THAT TYPE-2 CYTOKINES ARE INVOLVED IN TUFT CELL DIFFERENTIATION IN SUBMANDIBULAR GLANDS. SPECIFICALLY, AIM 1 WILL DEFINE CYTOKINE SUFFICIENCY AND RECEPTOR REQUIREMENTS FOR TUFT CELL DIFFERENTIATION USING MOUSE AND HUMAN SALIVARY GLAND ORGANOIDS, INTEGRATING TRANSCRIPTOMIC, IMAGING AND FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS. AIM 2 WILL VALIDATE THESE PATHWAYS IN VIVO USING CYTOKINE STIMULATION, RECEPTOR-DEFICIENT STRAINS AND AUTOIMMUNE-PRONE MICE, WITH SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS AND IMMUNE PROFILING TO RESOLVE TUFT CELL-DRIVEN EPITHELIAL–IMMUNE NICHES. THIS STUDY COMPLEMENTS MY ONGOING R00, WHICH EXAMINES TUFT CELL FUNCTIONS IN SALIVARY GLAND IMMUNITY, BY FOCUSING INSTEAD ON THE UPSTREAM PATHWAYS REGULATING TUFT CELL DIFFERENTIATION WITHIN SUBMANDIBULAR GLANDS. TOGETHER, THE R00 AND R03 WILL PROVIDE A COHERENT FRAMEWORK SPANNING TUFT CELL DIFFERENTIATION, FUNCTION, AND AUTOIMMUNE DYSREGULATION, AND WILL GENERATE THE MECHANISTIC INSIGHT AND MODELS NEEDED TO LAUNCH A FUTURE R01 TARGETING TUFT CELL–CYTOKINE CIRCUITS IN SJÖGREN’S DISEASE.

description: UNVEILING THE HIDDEN HUMAN VIROME: DEFINING ANTIGENICITY AND IMMUNE RECOGNITION OF ANELLOVIRUSES - SUMMARY ANELLOVIRUSES ARE THE MOST PREVALENT PERSISTENT VIRUSES IN HUMANS, INFECTING MORE THAN 90% OF THE GLOBAL POPULATION AND REPRESENTING THE DOMINANT EUKARYOTIC COMPONENT OF THE HEALTHY HUMAN VIROME. DESPITE THEIR EXTRAORDINARY UBIQUITY, LIFELONG PERSISTENCE, AND STRONG LINKAGE TO THE IMMUNE SYSTEM, ANELLOVIRUSES REMAIN ONE OF THE LEAST UNDERSTOOD HUMAN VIRAL FAMILIES. THEIR SMALL ~3 KB GENOME ENCODES ONLY A FEW PROTEINS, MOST NOTABLY ORF1, THE PUTATIVE CAPSID AND PRIMARY IMMUNOGENIC STRUCTURAL ELEMENT. YET, NO HUMAN MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES EXIST FOR ANY ANELLOVIRUS. THIS ABSENCE OF FUNDAMENTAL MOLECULAR TOOLS HAS PREVENTED MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF VIRAL TROPISM, PERSISTENCE PATHWAYS, IMMUNE MODULATION, AND VIROME-HOST INTERACTIONS. ESTABLISHING AN ANTIGENIC AND IMMUNOLOGIC FRAMEWORK FOR ANELLOVIRUSES IS THEREFORE AN ESSENTIAL FIRST STEP TOWARD ELEVATING THEM FROM ENIGMATIC COMPONENTS OF THE VIROME TO EXPERIMENTALLY TRACTABLE VIRAL SYSTEMS. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS R03 PROPOSAL IS TO GENERATE THE FIRST HUMAN MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES AGAINST THE CONSERVED IMMUNOGENIC DOMAIN OF ANELLOVIRUS ORF1 AND TO DEFINE, FOR THE FIRST TIME, THE ANTIGENIC LANDSCAPE OF THIS HIGHLY PREVALENT VIRUS. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT DISCRETE IMMUNOGENIC EPITOPES WITHIN ORF1 CAN BE RESOLVED THROUGH HUMAN ANTIBODY RESPONSES AND STRUCTURALLY VISUALIZED BY CRYO-ELECTRON MICROSCOPY, CREATING FOUNDATIONAL RESOURCES FOR STUDYING ANELLOVIRUS BIOLOGY. THIS HYPOTHESIS IS SUPPORTED BY OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOWING ROBUST HUMAN IGG RESPONSES TO ORF1 AND BY OUR LABORATORY’S EXTENSIVE EXPERTISE IN ISOLATING RARE ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC HUMAN B CELLS AND GENERATING MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES. WE WILL PURSUE TWO COMPLEMENTARY AIMS. AIM 1 WILL GENERATE 50 FULLY HUMAN MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES BY ISOLATING ORF1-SPECIFIC MEMORY B CELLS FROM DONORS WITH DETECTABLE SEROLOGIC RESPONSES. THESE ANTIBODIES WILL BE CHARACTERIZED FOR SPECIFICITY, AFFINITY, AND CROSS-CLADE RECOGNITION, AND FIVE TO EIGHT ANTIBODY-ORF1 COMPLEXES WILL BE STRUCTURALLY DETERMINED BY CRYO-EM IN COLLABORATION WITH DR. GORAN BAJIC. AIM 2 WILL DEFINE POPULATION-LEVEL PATTERNS OF ANELLOVIRUS IMMUNITY BY PROFILING IGG, IGA, AND IGG SUBCLASS RESPONSES IN MORE THAN 3,000 SERUM SAMPLES FROM EXISTING COHORTS, INTEGRATING DEMOGRAPHIC AND EPIDEMIOLOGIC METADATA THROUGH MULTIVARIATE, SYSTEMS-LEVEL ANALYSES TO UNCOVER DETERMINANTS OF EXPOSURE, TRANSMISSION, AND IMMUNE ENGAGEMENT. THIS PROJECT WILL GENERATE THE FIRST MOLECULAR TOOLKIT FOR ANELLOVIRUS IMMUNOLOGY, INCLUDING HUMAN MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES, STRUCTURAL EPITOPE MAPS, AND DEEP SEROLOGIC DATASETS. THESE RESOURCES WILL DIRECTLY ADDRESS MAJOR KNOWLEDGE GAPS, ENABLE MECHANISTIC STUDIES OF A UBIQUITOUS YET UNDERSTUDIED VIRAL FAMILY, AND ACCELERATE BROADER EFFORTS OF THE HUMAN VIROME PROJECT. THE PROPOSED WORK WILL ESTABLISH THE FOUNDATION NECESSARY FOR FUTURE INVESTIGATIONS INTO ANELLOVIRUS PERSISTENCE, TROPISM, IMMUNE MODULATION, AND POTENTIAL UTILITY AS BIOMARKERS OR THERAPEUTIC PLATFORMS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GLUCAGON LIKE PEPTIDE-1 MEDICINE OUTCOMES IN REAL WORLD PATIENTS WITH TYPE 1 DIABETES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT GLUCAGON LIKE-PEPTIDE-1 (GLP-1) MEDICINES, INCLUDING GLP-1 AGONISTS AND GLP-1/GASTRIC INHIBITORY PEPTIDE DUAL AGONISTS, REDUCE WEIGHT, KIDNEY AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE EVENTS FOR PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES AND OVERWEIGHT/OBESITY. PEOPLE WITH TYPE 1 DIABETES (T1D) HAVE EXCESS CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE AND KIDNEY DISEASE, AND OVERWEIGHT/OBESITY PREVALENCE IS GROWING IN THIS POPULATION. THE DETRIMENTAL MILIEU OF OBESITY AND INSULIN RESISTANCE FURTHER EXAGGERATES RISK OF DIABETES-RELATED COMPLICATIONS. IN PEOPLE WITH T1D, LIMITED STUDIES HAVE EXAMINED WEIGHT RESPONSE TO GLP-1 MEDICINES AND OTHER FREQUENTLY PRESCRIBED WEIGHT LOSS MEDICINES. FURTHER, THERE IS A MAJOR KNOWLEDGE GAP ABOUT WHETHER GLP-1 MEDICINES PREVENT KIDNEY DISEASE PROGRESSION, REDUCE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, AND CAUSE RARE, SEVERE ADVERSE EVENTS IN THIS POPULATION. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS STUDY IS TO ASSESS CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT: WEIGHT LOSS, KIDNEY DISEASE, AND MAJOR ADVERSE EVENTS IN RESPONSE TO GLP-1 MEDICINES IN T1D. THIS PROJECT WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT GLP-1 MEDICINES HAVE CLINICAL BENEFITS RELEVANT TO CARDIORENAL DISEASE PROTECTION AND ARE SAFE IN A POPULATION WITH T1D. IT WILL LEVERAGE EXISTING REAL WORLD ELECTRONIC HEALTHCARE DATA FROM EPIC COSMOS, A DATABASE OF OVER 300 MILLION PEOPLE OF WHOM OVER 943,000 HAVE A T1D DIAGNOSIS. USING LONGITUDINAL, HARMONIZED DATA FROM THIS CUTTING-EDGE PLATFORM, THIS PROJECT WILL COMPARE PATIENTS WITH T1D TREATED WITH A CARDIOPROTECTIVE GLP-1 MEDICINE (LIRAGLUTIDE, SEMAGLUTIDE, DULAGLUTIDE, TIRZEPATIDE) TO ACTIVE COMPARATORS (PHENTERMINE AND METFORMIN) USING PROPENSITY SCORE-BASED METHODS TO ACCOUNT FOR BIAS DUE TO NON-RANDOM TREATMENT. THE PROJECT WILL EXAMINE THE IMPACT OF THESE DRUGS ON: CARDIOPROTECTIVE WEIGHT LOSS (≥10%) (AIM 1); COMPOSITE KIDNEY OUTCOMES INCLUDING PERSISTENT INCIDENCE: URINE ALBUMIN TO CREATINE RATIO [UACR] ≥30 MG/G OR UACR ≥300 MG/G, ≥40% EGFR DECLINE, END STAGE KIDNEY DISEASE, AND ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY (AIM 2); AND SAFETY EVENTS INCLUDING MAJOR ADVERSE CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS, ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY, AND INCIDENCE RATES OF EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT/HOSPITAL ADMISSIONS ALONG WITH ASSOCIATED DIAGNOSES (AIM 3). THIS PROJECT IS A LOGICAL EXTENSION OF THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR’S INTERVENTIONAL K23 RESEARCH PROJECT WHICH EXAMINES GLP-1 MEDICINE IMPACT ON SURROGATE CARDIOVASCULAR OUTCOME MEASURES IN ADULTS WITH T1D. THE CURRENT RESEARCH PROPOSAL FOCUSES ON IMPROVING HEALTH FOR PEOPLE WITH T1D THROUGH INNOVATIVE USE OF A CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCH PLATFORM COMBINED WITH ADVANCED CAUSAL INFERENCE METHODS. TO ACCOMPLISH THESE GOALS, THIS PROJECT ASSEMBLES A TEAM OF COMPLEMENTARY AND WELL-SUITED EXPERTS, INCLUDING AN ENDOCRINOLOGIST WITH T1D AND GLP-1 MEDICINE RESEARCH EXPERTISE, CLINICAL INFORMATICIAN, PHARMACO-EPIDEMIOLOGIST, DATA SCIENTIST, AND BIOSTATISTICIAN ALL WITH LARGE-SCALE, SECONDARY DATA ANALYTIC EXPERIENCE. THIS RESEARCH IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT ADDRESSES MAJOR KNOWLEDGE GAPS IN CLINICAL EFFICACY OF GLP- 1 MEDICINES, AND MOST FREQUENTLY PRESCRIBED COMPARATORS, IN THE T1D POPULATION, AND IT WILL INFORM EVIDENCE- BASED GUIDELINES AND FUTURE METHODOLOGY FOR INTERVENTIONAL KIDNEY AND CARDIOVASCULAR OUTCOME TRIALS IN T1D.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ANALYTIC MODELING AND TIMING CORRECTION IN DIGITAL-TO-ANALOG SIPM DETECTORS WITH CHERENKOV LUMINESCENCE FOR TOF-PET - PROJECT SUMMARY TIME-OF-FLIGHT POSITRON EMISSION TOMOGRAPHY (TOF-PET) IS A KEY IMAGING TOOL FOR DIAGNOSING AND MONITORING CAN- CER, CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, AND BRAIN DISORDERS. ITS CLINICAL UTILITY DEPENDS ON THE PRECISE TIMING OF DETECTED ANNIHILATION EVENTS, WHICH ENABLES ACCURATE LOCALIZATION OF TRACER SIGNALS. CURRENT TOF-PET SCANNERS ACHIEVE COINCIDENCE TIME RESOLUTIONS (CTR) OF 200–400 PS FULL WIDTH AT HALF MAXIMUM (FWHM) AND RELY ON SCINTILLATION PHOTONS. BECAUSE THE TIMING PERFORMANCE IS FUNDAMENTALLY LIMITED BY THE STOCHASTIC NATURE OF SCINTILLATION EMIS- SION, FURTHER SUBSTANTIAL IMPROVEMENTS TOWARD 100 PS OR BELOW ARE UNLIKELY WITH CONVENTIONAL SCINTILLATION-BASED DETECTORS, UNDERSCORING THE NEED TO EXPLORE ALTERNATIVE EMISSION PROCESSES. HYBRID CHERENKOV-SCINTILLATION DETECTORS, SUCH AS BISMUTH GERMANATE (BGO), LEVERAGE PROMPT CHERENKOV EMIS- SION FOR ULTRA-FAST TIMING, OFFERING ADDITIONAL ADVANTAGES OF LOWER COST, HIGHER DETECTION EFFICIENCY, AND NEGLIGIBLE INTRINSIC BACKGROUND. WITH CONTINUED ADVANCES IN PHOTODETECTORS, NO FUNDAMENTAL TIMING LIMITS ARE IMPOSED BY PHOTON STATISTICS. HOWEVER, ONLY A HANDFUL OF PROMPT PHOTONS ARE DETECTED PER EVENT, MAKING EVERY STAGE OF THE RADIATION DETECTOR CHAIN CRITICALLY IMPORTANT TO THE FINAL TIMING PERFORMANCE. THIS EXPLAINS WHY NO COMMERCIAL TOF-PET SCANNERS CURRENTLY EXPLOIT CHERENKOV PHOTONS. TO UNLOCK THE THEORETICAL TIMING POTENTIAL OF CHERENKOV-BASED TOF-PET, THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE, EVENT-WISE MODELING FRAMEWORK THAT TREATS THE RADIATION DETECTOR AS AN INFORMATION CHANNEL. THE FRAMEWORK WILL ESTABLISH AN ANALYTICAL MODEL THAT CAPTURES TIMING DEGRADATION FROM (1) LIGHT TRANSPORT, (2) PHOTON DETECTION, (3) CORRELATED PHOTODETECTOR NOISE, (4) READOUT ELECTRONICS, (5) DIGITIZER LIMITATIONS, AND (6) TIME PICK-OFF. EACH CONTRIBUTION CAN BE SELECTIVELY ENABLED OR DISABLED TO EVALUATE ITS IMPACT, GUIDING STRATEGIES TO PRESERVE SYSTEM- LEVEL TIMING NEAR THE THEORETICAL LIMIT. THE PROJECT WILL INTEGRATE EXPERIMENTALLY VALIDATED MODELS OF SIPM CORRELATED NOISE (AIM 1), ANALOG SIPM SIGNAL FORMATION (AIM 2), AND EVENT-WISE TIMING RECOVERY STRATEGIES (AIM 3), PROVIDING A RIGOROUS FOUNDATION TO IDENTIFY BOTTLENECKS AND OPTIMIZE TIMING EXTRACTION. BY SYSTEMATICALLY QUANTIFYING TIMING INFORMATION ON AN EVENT-BY-EVENT BASIS, THIS PROJECT WILL REVEAL WHICH DETECTOR EFFECTS LIMIT PERFORMANCE AND PROVIDE BROADLY APPLICABLE INSIGHTS FOR NEXT-GENERATION TOF-PET SYSTEMS AND LIGHT- BASED RADIATION DETECTORS, BRIDGING THE GAP BETWEEN THEORETICAL TIMING POTENTIAL AND PRACTICAL IMPLEMENTATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTRAVASCULAR ULTRASONIC TISSUE ABLATION (IVUS-TA) FOR TREATMENT OF IN-STENT RESTENOSIS - ABSTRACT IN-STENT RESTENOSIS (ISR) REMAINS A MAJOR CLINICAL CHALLENGE FOLLOWING PERCUTANEOUS CORONARY INTERVENTION (PCI), LEADING TO RECURRENT VESSEL NARROWING AND IMPAIRED BLOOD FLOW DESPITE THE WIDESPREAD USE OF DRUG-ELUTING STENTS. CURRENT TREATMENT OPTIONS—SUCH AS BALLOON ANGIOPLASTY, ATHERECTOMY, AND REPEAT STENTING—OFTEN RESULT IN LIMITED LUMINAL GAIN, VESSEL INJURY, AND HIGH RECURRENCE RATES. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP A NOVEL INTRAVASCULAR ULTRASONIC TISSUE ABLATION (IVUS-TA) TECHNIQUE CAPABLE OF PRECISELY AND SAFELY REMOVING NEOINTIMAL TISSUE AND RESIDUAL PLAQUES WITHIN STENTS THROUGH LOCALIZED HIGH-INTENSITY ULTRASOUND ENERGY DELIVERY. BY INTEGRATING A MINIATURIZED HIGH-FREQUENCY ULTRASOUND TRANSDUCER INTO A CATHETER PLATFORM, IVUS-TA ENABLES DIRECT, CATHETER- BASED ENERGY DEPOSITION THROUGH METALLIC STENT STRUTS WHILE MINIMIZING COLLATERAL DAMAGE TO SURROUNDING TISSUES. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL CHARACTERIZE THE ACOUSTIC PERFORMANCE, THERMAL EFFECTS, AND TISSUE ABLATION EFFICACY OF THE IVUS-TA SYSTEM USING EX-VIVO AND PHANTOM MODELS. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A MINIMALLY INVASIVE THERAPEUTIC MODALITY FOR ISR TREATMENT AND PROVIDE FOUNDATIONAL DATA FOR FUTURE PRE-CLINICAL TRANSLATION.

description: EXAMINING SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY RISK IN NEW JERSEY - PROJECT SUMMARY CASES OF SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY, THAT IS, UNEXPECTED AND POTENTIALLY LIFE-THREATENING EVENTS ASSOCIATED WITH LABOR AND DELIVERY, ARE LEADING CAUSES OF DEATH DURING PREGNANCY AND IN THE POSTPARTUM PERIOD IN THE UNITED STATES. MOST STUDIES ONLY ASSESS SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY DIAGNOSES MADE DURING THE DELIVERY HOSPITALIZATION OR IN THE SIX WEEKS FOLLOWING DELIVERY. YET SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY IS BELIEVED TO CONTRIBUTE TO MATERNAL DEATHS UP TO ONE YEAR POSTPARTUM. A HIGH PROPORTION OF SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY CASES ARE BELIEVED TO BE PREVENTABLE. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS TO PROVIDE CRUCIAL EVIDENCE ON SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY RISK UP TO ONE YEAR POSTPARTUM TO HELP INFORM ONGOING EFFORTS TO REDUCE MATERNAL MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY. WE WILL LEVERAGE EXISTING DATA FOR THIS STUDY, LINKING THE BIRTH RECORDS OF ALL LIVE BIRTHS IN NEW JERSEY BETWEEN 2010 AND 2022 WITH UNIFORM BILLING HOSPITAL DISCHARGE RECORDS FROM 2010 TO 2023. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL ASSESS RATES AND TRENDS IN SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY DURING THE STUDY PERIOD. THE STUDY WILL ALSO ASSESS DIFFERENCES IN THE TYPES AND TIMING OF SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY BY MATERNAL CHARACTERISTICS. THIS WILL ENABLE US TO IDENTIFY SUBGROUPS OF WOMEN WHO MAY REQUIRE ADDITIONAL PERINATAL SUPPORT AND/OR INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY RISK. THE STUDY ADDRESSES THE NICHD RESEARCH PRIORITY OF IMPROVING THE IDENTIFICATION OF WOMEN AT HIGH RISK FOR PREGNANCY-RELATED MORBIDITIES OR MORTALITY. FINDINGS FROM THE STUDY WILL PROVIDE CRUCIAL EVIDENCE TO HELP INFORM SOLUTION-ORIENTED EFFORTS TO IMPROVE MATERNAL HEALTH OUTCOMES IN NEW JERSEY AND BEYOND.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PITUITARY TRANSCRIPTIONAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE DIMINISHED LUTEINIZING HORMONE SURGE - OBESITY IS A SIGNIFICANT CAUSE OF INFERTILITY IN WOMEN, YET THE MECHANISMS LINKING EXCESS WEIGHT TO IMPAIRED REPRODUCTIVE HORMONE DYNAMICS REMAIN POORLY DEFINED. MANY WOMEN WITH OBESITY DISPLAY A “REPROMETABOLIC SYNDROME” (RMS) PHENOTYPE THAT INCLUDES LOW LUTEINIZING HORMONE (LH) AMPLITUDE, A BLUNTED OVULATORY LH SURGE AND REDUCED LUTEAL PROGESTERONE DESPITE NORMAL ESTRADIOL LEVELS. THE REDUCED LH PULSE AMPLITUDE ABSENT ANY CHANGE IN PULSE FREQUENCY IMPLICATES A DEFECT IN ESTRADIOL POSITIVE FEEDBACK AT THE PITUITARY. BECAUSE GONADOTROPES CONSTITUTE ONLY A SMALL FRACTION OF PITUITARY CELLS, THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL NETWORKS GOVERNING THEIR RESPONSE TO ESTRADIOL HAVE MAINLY REMAINED INACCESSIBLE IN VIVO. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY HOW METABOLIC DYSFUNCTION ALTERS PITUITARY RESPONSIVENESS TO ESTRADIOL AND GNRH, THEREBY REDUCING FERTILITY. USING AN OVARIECTOMIZED (OVX) EWE MODEL THAT CLOSELY RECAPITULATES THE HUMAN LH SURGE, WE HAVE SHOWN THAT OBESITY DELAYS AND BLUNTS THE ESTRADIOL-INDUCED LH SURGE, AN EFFECT REVERSED BY WEIGHT LOSS. PRELIMINARY SINGLE- NUCLEUS RNA SEQUENCING REVEALED DISTINCT ESTRADIOL-RESPONSIVE TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROGRAMS IN GONADOTROPES, INCLUDING ACTIVATION OF PGR, SMAD3, AND THE INSULIN-REGULATED TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR FOXO1. . THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS R03 IS TO DEFINE HOW OBESITY ALTERS TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND CHROMATIN ACCESSIBILITY DYNAMICS IN GONADOTROPES DURING THE PREOVULATORY PHASE. WE WILL PERFORM SINGLE-NUCLEUS MULTIOME SEQUENCING (SNRNA + SNATAC) ON PITUITARIES COLLECTED FROM NORMAL-WEIGHT AND OBESE OVX EWES 12 HOURS AFTER ESTRADIOL ADMINISTRATION. INTEGRATION OF GENE-EXPRESSION AND CHROMATIN DATA USING CREMA AND SCENIC WILL IDENTIFY OBESITY-SENSITIVE TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR REGULONS AND DEFINE THEIR EVOLUTION ACROSS THE 90-MINUTE, 6-HOUR, AND 12-HOUR STAGES OF THE ESTRADIOL-INDUCED LH SURGE. INNOVATION LIES IN APPLYING STATE-OF-THE-ART SINGLE-NUCLEUS MULTIOMICS TO THE PREOVULATORY PITUITARY, ENABLING UNPRECEDENTED RESOLUTION OF ESTROGEN-REGULATED GENE NETWORKS IN A TRANSLATIONAL LARGE-ANIMAL MODEL. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE THE IDENTIFICATION OF KEY TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS, CIS-REGULATORY CIRCUITS, AND CHROMATIN STATES OF GONADOTROPE GENE EXPRESSION DURING ESTRADIOL POSITIVE FEEDBACK. COMPARATIVE NETWORK ANALYSES WILL DELINEATE HOW OBESITY DISRUPTS REGULATORY HIERARCHIES CONTROLLING GONADOTROPE GENE EXPRESSION. THE RESULTS WILL PROVIDE A SYSTEMS-LEVEL FRAMEWORK FOR UNDERSTANDING ENDOCRINE SIGNAL INTEGRATION WITHIN THE PREOVULATORY PITUITARY AND HOW THIS FRAMEWORK MAY BE DISRUPTED UNDER CONDITIONS OF OBESITY. KEYWORDS: OBESITY, ESTRADIOL, GONADOTROPE, GNRH RECEPTOR, FOXO1, SINGLE-NUCLEUS MULTIOME, LH SURGE

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CROSS-MODAL VALIDATION OF SCALP EEG FEATURES USING CONCURRENT IEEG FOR REHABILITATIVE BCI - MILLIONS OF AMERICANS LIVE WITH MOTOR IMPAIRMENTS RESULTING FROM STROKE, SPINAL CORD INJURY, AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES. NEURO-REHABILITATIVE BRAIN-COMPUTER INTERFACE (BCI) TECHNOLOGIES OFFER A PROMISING AVENUE FOR MOTOR REHABILITATION BY TRANSLATING NEURAL SIGNALS INTO CONTROL COMMANDS FOR EXTERNAL DEVICES OR NEUROFEEDBACK. WHILE INVASIVE METHODS SUCH AS INTRACRANIAL EEG (IEEG) AND ELECTROCORTICOGRAPHY (ECOG) PROVIDE HIGH-RESOLUTION RECORDINGS AND HAVE DEMONSTRATED SUCCESS IN RESTORING MOTOR CONTROL, THEIR INVASIVENESS RESTRICTS ACCESSIBILITY AND LONG-TERM USE. IN CONTRAST, SCALP EEG IS A NON-INVASIVE METHOD WIDELY USED IN CLINICAL SETTINGS FOR ASSESSMENT AND REHABILITATION, ALLOWING STRAIGHTFORWARD MEASUREMENT OF BRAIN ACTIVITY AND EMPLOYING TECHNIQUES LIKE EEG-ELECTROMYOGRAPHY (EMG) COHERENCE TO EVALUATE MOTOR CONTROL. HOWEVER, THE SPATIAL RESOLUTION AND SIGNAL FIDELITY OF EEG ARE FUNDAMENTALLY LIMITED BY VOLUME CONDUCTION AND SKULL-INDUCED ATTENUATION, PARTICULARLY FOR HIGH-FREQUENCY ACTIVITY (E.G., >30HZ), WHICH IS BELIEVED TO ENCODE FINE-GRAINED MOTOR PLANNING AND EXECUTION. RECENT STUDIES SUGGEST THAT UNDER OPTIMAL CONDITIONS, NON-INVASIVE EEG CAN DETECT HIGH-FREQUENCY NEURAL ACTIVITY PREVIOUSLY THOUGHT TO BE INACCESSIBLE. YET THE ABSENCE OF SYSTEMATIC VALIDATION AGAINST DIRECT BRAIN RECORDINGS LEAVES A CRITICAL GAP IN UNDERSTANDING THE TRUE CORTICAL ORIGIN, RELIABILITY, AND FUNCTIONAL UTILITY OF THESE EEG FEATURES. THIS GAP IS ESPECIALLY CONSEQUENTIAL FOR APPLICATIONS REQUIRING ACCURATE SINGLE-TRIAL DECODING OF MOTOR TASKS IN REAL-TIME BCIS FOR REHABILITATION. TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP, THIS PROPOSAL LEVERAGES SIMULTANEOUS IEEG AND SCALP EEG RECORDINGS IN CLINICAL PATIENTS UNDERGOING EPILEPSY INVASIVE MONITORING. USING IEEG AS GROUND TRUTH, WE WILL ASSESS THE RELIABILITY AND FUNCTIONAL RELEVANCE OF HIGH-FREQUENCY EEG FEATURES DURING MOTOR TASKS, AND REFINE SCALP EEG-BASED NEURAL DECODING FRAMEWORKS FOR MOTOR REHABILITATION. THIS PROJECT PRESENTS A NOVEL MULTIMODAL FRAMEWORK TO UNCOVER AND VALIDATE VALUABLE YET PREVIOUSLY INACCESSIBLE SCALP EEG FEATURES USING CONCURRENT IEEG RECORDINGS. AS ONE OF THE FIRST EFFORTS TO SYSTEMATICALLY ALIGN NON- INVASIVE EEG SIGNALS WITH INTRACRANIAL GROUND TRUTH, IT AIMS TO IDENTIFY, ENRICH AND VALIDATE ROBUST, TASK-RELEVANT EEG SIGNATURES ANCHORED IN NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL DATA. BY ADDRESSING A KEY BARRIER TO THE CLINICAL TRANSLATION OF EEG-BASED BCIS, THIS WORK AIMS TO IMPROVE THEIR INTERPRETABILITY, RELIABILITY, AND THERAPEUTIC UTILITY FOR MOTOR REHABILITATION. IT DIRECTLY SUPPORTS THE BIOMEDICAL AND BEHAVIORAL MISSION OF NCMRR BY ESTABLISHING A FOUNDATION FOR DEPLOYING NON-INVASIVE BCIS IN REHABILITATION SETTINGS TO PROMOTE MOTOR RECOVERY IN INDIVIDUALS WITH CHRONIC NEUROLOGICAL IMPAIRMENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LINKING TRAINING DEFICIENCIES TO RISKY DRIVING BEHAVIORS AND ROADWAY SAFETY STRATEGIES FOR TEENAGE DRIVERS - PROJECT SUMMARY MOTOR VEHICLE CRASHES REMAIN ONE OF THE MOST SIGNIFICANT HEALTH THREATS FOR YOUNG ADULTS, WITH TEENAGE DRIVERS DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTED DUE TO THEIR LACK OF EXPERIENCE AND INADEQUATE DRIVING TRAINING. DESPITE EFFORTS BY THE DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY (DPS) AND DEPARTMENT OF MOTOR VEHICLES (DMV) TO ENHANCE DRIVER TRAINING THROUGH GRADUATED DRIVER LICENSING (GDL) PROGRAMS, THE DECLINE OF PUBLIC HIGH SCHOOL DRIVING PROGRAMS HAS LEFT MANY TEENAGERS RELIANT ON PARENT-TAUGHT INSTRUCTION, WITHOUT CONSISTENT GUIDANCE OR OVERSIGHT FROM STATE AGENCIES. THIS APPROACH INTRODUCES CRITICAL LIMITATIONS, INCLUDING VARIABILITY IN INSTRUCTIONAL QUALITY AND INSUFFICIENT EXPOSURE TO COMPLEX, REAL-WORLD DRIVING CONDITIONS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THESE TRAINING GAPS CONTRIBUTE TO BEHAVIORAL VULNERABILITIES AMONG TEENS, SUCH AS REDUCED SAFETY AWARENESS AND INCREASED RISK-TAKING, THAT ELEVATE CRASH RISK. AT THE SAME TIME, WE POSIT THAT ENHANCED ROADWAY DESIGN AND OPERATIONAL STRATEGIES CAN MITIGATE UNSAFE RESPONSES BY IMPROVING YOUNG DRIVERS’ HAZARD PERCEPTION AND DECISION-MAKING IN COMPLEX ENVIRONMENTS WITH PROPER TRAINING. FINALLY, WE RECOGNIZE THAT SOCIOECONOMIC DISPARITIES IN ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY DRIVER TRAINING AND SAFE ROADWAY INFRASTRUCTURE MAY FURTHER EXACERBATE THESE RISKS, PARTICULARLY IN LOW-INCOME COMMUNITIES.  TO ADDRESS THESE CONCERNS, WE PROPOSE A MULTI-COMPONENT MIXED-METHOD EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN COMPRISING (A) BEHAVIORAL SURVEYS, (B) INTERVIEWS, AND (C) NATURALISTIC DRIVING DATA TO ASSESS HOW VARYING LEVELS OF DRIVING TRAINING IMPACT RISK AWARENESS AND REAL-WORLD DRIVING PERFORMANCE AMONG LOW-INCOME TEEN DRIVERS. OUR INNOVATIVE DATA-DRIVEN APPROACH, LEVERAGING HISTORICAL CRASH DATA FROM THE TEXAS DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION, IDENTIFIES THE MOST CRASH-PRONE, HIGH-RISK CONDITIONS (E.G., ROUNDABOUTS, INTERSECTIONS, HIGH-SPEED ENVIRONMENTS) TO ENSURE ECOLOGICAL VALIDITY OF THIS STUDY. WE WILL EMPLOY ECONOMETRIC MODELING TO ASSESS HOW THE BREADTH AND DEPTH OF PRIOR DRIVER TRAINING THROUGH PARENTAL INSTRUCTION CORRELATE WITH RISK AWARENESS AND UNSAFE DRIVING HABITS. OUR SEMI- STRUCTURED INTERVIEW WILL SUPPLEMENT THE STATISTICAL ANALYSIS, CAPTURING IN-DEPTH, CONTEXTUALIZED INSIGHTS INTO HOW ADOLESCENTS ACQUIRE, INTERPRET, AND APPLY DRIVING KNOWLEDGE, AND HOW THESE PROCESSES INTERACT WITH HOUSEHOLD ECONOMIC CONDITIONS TO INFLUENCE PREPAREDNESS, CONFIDENCE, AND RISK PERCEPTION. WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE HOW THOSE BEHAVIORAL DEFICIENCIES TRANSLATE INTO REAL-WORLD DRIVING BEHAVIORS THROUGH NATURALISTIC DRIVING FROM GPS TRACKING DATA. WE WILL ADDITIONALLY TEST WHETHER ENHANCED ROADWAY DESIGNS AND SAFETY COUNTERMEASURES EFFECTIVELY REDUCE RISKY RESPONSES TO ROADWAY HAZARDS WHEN COMBINED WITH ADEQUATE TRAINING, USING A HIGH-FIDELITY DRIVING SIMULATION EXPERIMENT. USING VEHICLE SPEED, VEHICLE POSITION, AND HEADWAY METRICS, WE WILL CAPTURE TEEN DRIVERS’ REAL-TIME DECISION MAKING, HAZARD PERCEPTION, AND VISUOMOTOR RESPONSES WITH AND WITHOUT SAFETY FEATURES. OUR FINDINGS WILL GENERATE EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE TO INFORM POLICYMAKERS ON DESIGNING TARGETED EDUCATIONAL STRATEGIES THAT EMPHASIZE REAL-WORLD SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND RISK MANAGEMENT, AND ON IMPLEMENTING ROADWAY SAFETY COUNTERMEASURES THAT REDUCE CRASH RISKS AND FATALITIES AMONG TEEN DRIVERS.

description: EXAMINING THE IMPACT OF STATE RECESS LEGISLATION ON RECESS PROVISION IN CALIFORNIA TO INFORM IMPROVED STUDENT CARDIOMETABOLIC FITNESS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ ABSTRACT SUBSTANTIAL EVIDENCE DEMONSTRATES THAT QUALITY SCHOOL RECESS PROVIDES OPPORTUNITIES FOR PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND SOCIALIZATION, WHICH RESULTS IN INCREASED STUDENT PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, CARDIOMETABOLIC HEALTH, AND WELL-BEING. AT LEAST 30 MINUTES OF DAILY RECESS IS ASSOCIATED WITH A TWO-FOLD GREATER ODDS OF ACHIEVING RECOMMENDED PHYSICAL ACTIVITY LEVELS AND HAS BEEN DIRECTLY RELATED TO LOWER BLOOD PRESSURE, IMPROVED HIGH DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN CHOLESTEROL, AND INCREASED STUDENT CARDIORESPIRATORY FITNESS. GIVEN THAT 84% OF SCHOOL-AGE CHILDREN IN THE U.S. ATTEND PUBLIC SCHOOL, RECESS OFFERS AN UNMATCHED OPPORTUNITY TO USE EXISTING SYSTEMS TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF OUR NATION’S CHILDREN. YET NOT ALL STUDENTS HAVE ACCESS TO THIS IMPORTANT TIME IN THE SCHOOL DAY; LESS THAN 60% OF US CHILDREN HAVE AT LEAST 30 MINUTES OF RECESS A DAY. THE IMPORTANCE OF RECESS, COMBINED WITH GAPS IN PROVISION, LED CALIFORNIA (THE NATION’S LARGEST STATE) TO PASS SENATE BILL 291 (RECESS FOR ALL) MANDATING 30 MINUTES OF DAILY RECESS FOR ALL KINDERGARTEN-6TH GRADE STUDENTS IN 2024-25. HOWEVER, MY PRIOR RESEARCH ON PHYSICAL EDUCATION (PE) IN CALIFORNIA SHOWED THAT UNFUNDED LEGISLATION REQUIRING SCHOOLS DO MORE, WITHOUT PROVIDING FINANCIAL OR STRUCTURAL SUPPORTS, CAN RESULT IN LOW COMPLIANCE IN ALREADY OVERBURDENED AND UNDER- RESOURCED SCHOOLS. IT REMAINS UNKNOWN IF UNFUNDED STATEWIDE RECESS LEGISLATION CAN POSITIVELY IMPACT RECESS PROVISION, TO THE BENEFIT OF STUDENT CARDIOMETABOLIC HEALTH. THIS STUDY LEVERAGES THE NATURAL EXPERIMENT POSED BY THE PASSAGE OF RECESS FOR ALL TO 1) QUANTITATIVELY DETERMINE IF THIS LEGISLATION RESULTS IN INCREASED RECESS PROVISION BY EXAMINING CHANGES IN REPORTED RECESS MINUTES FROM BEFORE (2023-24) TO AFTER (2024-25) PASSAGE, AND 2) QUALITATIVELY DETERMINE BEST PRACTICES FOR RECESS LAW IMPLEMENTATION USING AN IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE (RE-AIM) APPROACH. AS RECESS LAWS BECOME ADOPTED NATIONWIDE, IT IS CRUCIAL TO UNDERSTAND HOW THEY IMPACT RECESS PROVISION, AS WELL AS THE POTENTIAL UNINTENDED CONSEQUENCES OF IMPOSING UNFUNDED MANDATES ON SCHOOLS, WHICH HAVE HISTORICALLY EXACERBATED EDUCATIONAL ISSUES, LEADING TO LOW COMPLIANCE AND UNIMPROVED STUDENT HEALTH OUTCOMES. FURTHER, THIS STUDY CAN INFORM THE WRITING, ADOPTION, AND ROLL-OUT OF SIMILAR LEGISLATION IN OTHER STATES, TO HAVE THE GREATEST POSITIVE IMPACT ON THE CARDIOMETABOLIC HEALTH OF ALL CHILDREN. THIS WORK BUILDS ON MY K01 MIXED-METHODS RESEARCH ON THE CARDIORESPIRATORY IMPACTS OF STATEWIDE PE LAW, WHICH HAS LED TO PURSUING RIGOROUS EVIDENCE ON OTHER SCHOOL-BASED POLICIES FOR IMPROVING YOUTH CARDIOMETABOLIC HEALTH AND FURTHERS MY IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE TRAINING AND SKILLS. THIS RESEARCH BY WILL ALSO PROVIDE THE MEANS TO HELP ME BECOME AN ACADEMIC LEADER IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING OF SCALABLE SCHOOL PHYSICAL ACTIVITY POLICY INTERVENTIONS THAT WILL REDUCE POPULATION RISK OF INACTIVITY-RELATED CHRONIC DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MINDFUL MOVEMENT: DEVELOPMENT OF A NOVEL GUIDED IMAGERY APP TO PROMOTE PHYSICAL ACTIVITY IN ADULTS WITH OVERWEIGHT OR OBESITY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT A MAJOR CHALLENGE IN THE TREATMENT OF OBESITY AND THE PREVENTION OF CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD) IS INCREASING THE PROPORTION OF ADULTS WHO CAN ADOPT AND SUSTAIN HIGH LEVELS OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY (PA). ALTHOUGH MANY FACTORS CONTRIBUTE TO POOR PA ADHERENCE AMONG ADULTS WITH OVERWEIGHT OR OBESITY, ABSENCE OF ACCESSIBLE, EFFECTIVE, THEORY-BASED PROGRAMS REMAINS A MAJOR BARRIER. THUS, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED TO DEVELOP ACCESSIBLE, EFFECTIVE, AND ECONOMICAL PROGRAMS TO PROMOTE PA ADHERENCE IN ADULTS WITH OVERWEIGHT OR OBESITY. WITHIN THE ONGOING, NIH-FUNDED K AWARD (K01 HL161417), WE HAVE DESIGNED AND ARE PILOT TESTING A PERSON-CENTERED, THEORY-BASED PA SUPPORT PROGRAM FOR ADULTS WITH OVERWEIGHT OR OBESITY, CALLED MOVE+. MOVE+ IS BASED ON THE SELF- DETERMINATION THEORY (SDT) AND TARGETS ENHANCED PA ADHERENCE IN ADULTS WITH OVERWEIGHT OR OBESITY BY ENCOURAGING THEM TO CHOOSE PA TYPES THAT ARE PERSONALLY MEANINGFUL AND INTRINSICALLY MOTIVATED. MOVE+ CONSISTS OF FOUR INTERVENTION COMPONENTS: 1) FOUR GROUP-BASED SESSIONS, 2) THREE INDIVIDUALIZED SUPPORT SESSIONS, 3) A LIVESTREAM FITNESS MEMBERSHIP AND 4) ACCESS TO ~20 GUIDED IMAGERY SESSIONS VIA AN ONLINE PLATFORM. WHILE PRELIMINARY DATA INDICATE GOOD FEASIBILITY/ACCEPTABILITY FOR COMPONENTS 1-3, THE GUIDED IMAGERY COMPONENT REQUIRES FURTHER REFINEMENT. INTERVIEW DATA FROM THE K01 AWARD INDICATE THAT WHILE MANY PARTICIPANTS SEE THE COMPONENT’S VALUE (“IT JUST CENTERS YOU”), THERE WAS A STRONG DESIRE TO RECEIVE THIS COMPONENT VIA AN APP (“…CAUSE I’M AN APP PERSON”). THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS R03 IS TO IMPROVE THE GUIDED IMAGERY COMPONENT’S ACCEPTABILITY AND FEASIBILITY PRIOR TO INCLUSION AS A MOVE+ COMPONENT IN A FUTURE R01. SPECIFICALLY, IN AIM 1, WE WILL ENGAGE CO-DESIGNERS TO DEVELOP A GUIDED IMAGERY APP, CALLED MINDFUL MOVEMENT, TO ENHANCE PA ADHERENCE AND REDUCE CVD RISK. ADULTS (N=6; AGES 18-65, BMI 25-45 KG/M2 AND INSUFFICIENTLY ACTIVE) AND CONTENT EXPERTS (N=4) WILL BE ASKED TO PROVIDE FEEDBACK ON ENHANCED AUDIO RECORDINGS, DEVELOPED USING CUTTING-EDGE GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) TECHNOLOGY, AND TO PARTICIPATE IN A SERIES OF TWO ITERATIVE FOCUS GROUPS TO CO-CREATE APP FEATURES. IN AIM 2, ADULTS (N=14) WITH BMI 25-45 KG/M2 WHO ARE INSUFFICIENTLY ACTIVE WILL EVALUATE THE APP’S DESIGN AND USABILITY OVER ITERATIVE HUMAN-CENTERED DESIGN TESTING SESSIONS. PRIMARY OUTCOMES OF ACCEPTABILITY AND FEASIBILITY WILL BE ASSESSED USING MIXED METHODS. SECONDARY OUTCOMES INCLUDE CHANGES IN SELF-REPORTED PA LEVELS, AUTOMATIC AFFECTIVE EVALUATIONS, ATTITUDES, AND MOTIVATION POST-ENGAGEMENT WITH THE APP. CONSISTENT WITH DISSEMINATION AND IMPLEMENTATION (D&I) SCIENCE, WE WILL APPLY THE MULTIPHASE OPTIMIZATION STRATEGY (MOST) AS OUR PROCESS FRAMEWORK TO HELP US SYSTEMATICALLY AND EFFICIENTLY IMPROVE THIS COMPONENT AND THE MOVE+ INTERVENTION. THIS R03 IS A CRITICAL STEP TOWARDS DEVELOPING A FUTURE NIH R01 PROPOSAL TO EVALUATE THE EFFICACY OF EACH MOVE+ COMPONENT IN A FULLY POWERED FACTORIAL TRIAL (MOST OPTIMIZATION PHASE). ESTABLISHING A SCALABLE AND EFFECTIVE THEORY-BASED PA INTERVENTION WILL IMPROVE LONG-TERM OUTCOMES FOR ADULTS WITH OVERWEIGHT OR OBESITY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXPLORING A ROLE OF MICROGLIA IN DEVELOPMENTAL EFFECTS OF EARLY LIFE ADVERSITY ON PFC GLUTAMATE RECEPTIVITY - PROJECT SUMMARY OUR PROPOSED PROJECT AIMS TO IDENTIFY A DEVELOPMENTAL ROLE FOR MICROGLIA IN THE EFFECTS OF EARLY LIFE ADVERSITY, WITH VULNERABILITY TO LATER-LIFE NEUROPSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS THAT INVOLVE PREFRONTAL CORTEX (PFC) DYSFUNCTION AS WELL AS HEIGHTENED NEUROINFLAMMATORY SIGNALING. DELETERIOUS BEHAVIORAL CONSEQUENCES OF EARLY LIFE ADVERSITY OFTEN FIRST EMERGE IN ADOLESCENCE, WHICH COINCIDES WITH A DRAMATIC PERIOD OF PFC MATURATION. WE HAVE DETERMINED THAT EARLY LIFE ADVERSITY DERAILS DEVELOPMENT OF PFC EXCITATORY SIGNALING, WITH CHANGES TO NMDA RECEPTORS (NMDAR) IN ADOLESCENCE. EARLY LIFE ADVERSITY IN THE FORM OF MATERNAL SEPARATION (MS) IN RATS CAUSES AN EARLY INCREASE IN NR2A EXPRESSION, WITH HIGHER MEMBRANE NR2A IN ADOLESCENCE AND CONSEQUENTIAL WORKING MEMORY DEFICITS. THE MECHANISMS DRIVING ALTERED NMDAR DEVELOPMENT ARE NOT KNOWN, HOWEVER WE HAVE SHOWN THAT ANTI- INFLAMMATORY TREATMENT CAN PREVENT INCREASED NR2A EXPRESSION IN MS-EXPOSED ADOLESCENTS, SUGGESTING THAT IMMUNE SIGNALING PLAYS A ROLE IN SYNAPSE REFINEMENT. MICROGLIA, THE RESIDENT IMMUNE CELLS OF THE BRAIN, DIRECTLY DRIVE BRAIN DEVELOPMENT AND RECEPTOR REGULATION VIA CYTOKINE RELEASE AND SYNAPTIC PRUNING. THE CURRENT PROPOSAL WILL TEST A DIRECT LINK BETWEEN MICROGLIAL ACTIVITY AND NR2A DEVELOPMENT IN THE CONTEXT OF EARLY LIFE ADVERSITY. NOTABLY, MICROGLIAL STATE CAN SHIFT DEPENDING ON ENVIRONMENTAL AND PHYSIOLOGICAL DEMANDS, WHICH CAN BIAS THESE CELLS TOWARDS OR AWAY DEVELOPMENTAL PROCESSES SUCH AS SYNAPTIC REFINEMENT. THESE STATE SHIFTS THEMSELVES FOLLOW A DEVELOPMENTAL TRAJECTORY WHEREBY ADVANCED OR DELAYED MICROGLIAL MATURATION CAN SUBSTANTIALLY IMPACT BRAIN DEVELOPMENT. GIVEN OUR OBSERVATION THAT NR2A INCREASES ARE ACCELERATED IN MS-EXPOSED ANIMALS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT MS YIELDS ADVANCED DEVELOPMENTAL STAGE IN ADOLESCENT MICROGLIA, AND THAT MICROGLIAL ACTIVITY DRIVES HEIGHTENED NR2A. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS IN AIM 1 USING MICROGLIAL DEPLETION IN EARLY ADOLESCENCE TO PREVENT INCREASED NR2A EXPRESSION AND WORKING MEMORY DEFICITS. WE WILL THEN TEST IN AIM 2 WHETHER MS ADVANCES THE DEVELOPMENTAL STAGE OF MICROGLIA USING RNA SEQUENCING IN ISOLATED MICROGLIA, WHICH WILL ALSO ALLOW US TO MINE TRANSCRIPTOMIC CHANGES THAT INCLUDE GENES THAT ARE INVOLVED IN SYNAPTIC REFINEMENT. TOGETHER, THIS WORK WILL SET THE STAGE FOR FUTURE PROJECTS TO TARGET MICROGLIA AND NMDA FUNCTION DURING SPECIFIC DEVELOPMENTAL WINDOWS TO PREVENT THE LONG-TERM IMPACTS OF ELA ON PFC FUNCTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DECODING THE PROTEIN BIOCHEMISTRY OF TBCK - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT GENETIC MUTATIONS IN THE GENE ENCODING FOR TBC1-DOMAIN CONTAINING KINASE (TBCK) ARE ASSOCIATED WITH TBCK ENCEPHALONEURONOPATHY (TBCKE), A RARE PEDIATRIC NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER. CHARACTERIZED BY PROFOUND INTELLECTUAL AND PHYSICAL DISABILITIES, NO TREATMENTS ARE CURRENTLY AVAILABLE FOR TBCKE. EMERGING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT TBCK PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN THE MTOR SIGNALING PATHWAY, AUTOPHAGY/LYSOSOME FUNCTION, AND MITOCHONDRIAL HOMEOSTASIS. HOWEVER, THE LACK OF DETAILED CHARACTERIZATIONS OF TBCK AT THE PROTEIN LEVEL HAS HINDERED OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE DISEASE MECHANISMS AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES. TO THIS END, WE WILL CONDUCT THE FIRST PROTEIN BIOCHEMISTRY INVESTIGATION OF HUMAN TBCK. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL USE IN VITRO ENZYME ASSAYS TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT TBCK FUNCTIONS AS A GTPASE-ACTIVATING PROTEIN BY INTERACTING WITH RAB5A. IN ADDITION, WE WILL EMPLOY FLUORESCENCE-BASED ASSAY AND HYDROGEN-DEUTERIUM EXCHANGE MASS SPECTROMETRY TO PROBE PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS OF TBCK. THE OUTCOME OF THIS PILOT PROJECT WILL CLARIFY THE CATALYTIC POTENTIAL OF THIS UNIQUE ‘DARK’ PROTEIN KINASE AND ESTABLISH THE FOUNDATION FOR UNDERSTANDING HOW TBCKE- ASSOCIATED VARIANTS ALTER THE PROTEIN STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION IN VITRO. THIS INFORMATION WILL FACILITATE UNCOVERING NOVEL DRUG TARGETS AND LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TO TREAT THIS NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER.
