description: INVESTIGATING THE STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION OF GPRC5B IN A RARE LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY - PROJECT SUMMARY G PROTEIN-COUPLED RECEPTORS (GPCRS) FOR HORMONES AND NEUROTRANSMITTERS EVOLVED TO BE ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT MEANS OF COMMUNICATION BETWEEN CELLS AND TISSUES IN HIGHER ORGANISMS. THEY ARE RESPONSIVE TO A WIDE RANGE OF STIMULI, FROM LIGHT TO SMALL MOLECULES AND PROTEINS. AS A RESULT OF THEIR EXTENSIVE INFLUENCE OVER HUMAN PHYSIOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR, MORE THAN 30% OF FDA-APPROVED DRUGS TARGET GPCRS. YET, OVER HALF OF THE NON-OLFACTORY GPCRS (AROUND 165) HAVE NOT BEEN THERAPEUTICALLY TARGETED. ONE SUCH GPCR, GPRC5B, IS A FAMILY C ORPHAN GPCR THAT HAS BEEN SHOWN TO HAVE A CRITICAL FUNCTION FOR LYMPHATIC DEVELOPMENT, REGULATION OF INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES, AND CONTROLLING VASCULAR TONE. MURINE MODELS HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT KNOCK-OUT OF GPRC5B IN SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS IS HIGHLY PROTECTIVE AGAINST THE DEVELOPMENT OF ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUES, SUGGESTING THAT GPRC5B COULD BE A NEW TARGET FOR TREATING ATHEROSCLEROSIS, WHICH AFFECTS OVER 18 MILLION AMERICANS. HOWEVER, GPRC5B’S ROLE IN THE RARE DISEASE MEGALENCEPHALIC LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY WITH SUBCORTICAL CYSTS (MLC) IS PERHAPS MOST ACUTELY STRIKING. MLC IS A DEBILITATING NEUROLOGICAL CONDITION WHERE A LACK OF VOLUME REGULATION IN ASTROCYTES RESULTS IN CHRONIC WHITE MATTER EDEMA. MOST COMMONLY, MLC IS CAUSED BY MUTATIONS IN THE MLC1 PROTEIN. HOWEVER, SOME PATIENTS WITH NO MUTATIONS IN MLC1 WERE FOUND TO HAVE HETEROZYGOUS MISSENSE MUTATIONS IN GPRC5B. THESE PATIENTS SHOWED A PARTICULARLY SEVERE MLC PHENOTYPE. PATIENTS WITH THESE GPRC5B MUTATIONS HAVE DRAMATICALLY INCREASED LEVELS OF GPRC5B PROTEIN, WHICH IN MODELS IS SUFFICIENT TO DISRUPT NORMAL VOLUME HOMEOSTASIS. HOW THESE MUTATIONS ALTER GPRC5B FUNCTION IS UNKNOWN, AND NO TREATMENT IS AVAILABLE FOR MLC. THIS WORK WILL INVESTIGATE GPRC5B TO UNDERSTAND ITS (MIS)FUNCTION IN MLC. TO ENABLE OUR STUDIES, WE WILL USE ALPACA-DERIVED ANTIBODIES, CALLED NANOBODIES (NBS), WHICH BIND ANTIGENS EXCLUSIVELY VIA THE VARIABLE DOMAIN OF THEIR HEAVY CHAIN. THESE SMALL PROTEIN TOOLS WILL FACILITATE THE DETERMINATION OF THE MOLECULAR STRUCTURE OF GPRC5B BY CRYO-EM. WE WILL ALSO USE SINGLE-MOLECULE FLUORESCENCE STRATEGIES TOGETHER WITH MOLECULAR DYNAMICS SIMULATIONS TO INVESTIGATE MOLECULAR MOVEMENTS WITHIN GPRC5B TO UNDERSTAND ITS NATIVE FUNCTIONS AS WELL AS THE EFFECT OF MLC MUTATIONS. WE BELIEVE THAT THROUGH THIS PILOT PROJECT, WE WILL GAIN VALUABLE INSIGHTS INTO THE BIOLOGY OF THIS POORLY CHARACTERIZED GPCR AND HOW MUTATIONS IN GPRC5B MAY INFLUENCE CELLULAR VOLUME CONTROL MECHANISMS, AS THOSE THAT LEAD TO MLC. LASTLY, WHILE OUR GOAL IS FOR THE TOOLS AND STRUCTURAL INSIGHTS THAT RESULT FROM THIS WORK TO ENABLE US TO TARGET GPRC5B FOR TREATING MLC, THERE IS A POTENTIAL FOR TARGETING GPRC5B IN OTHER DISEASES SUCH AS CANCER AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GENERATION AND CHARACTERIZATION OF A NOVEL CONDITIONAL SPTLC1 MOUSE MODEL TO INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF SPHINGOLIPIDS DYSREGULATION IN ALS - ABSTRACT ALTERATIONS IN SPHINGOLIPID METABOLISM ARE INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED AS CONTRIBUTORS TO NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES, INCLUDING AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (ALS). SPTLC1, ENCODING THE LONG-CHAIN BASE SUBUNIT OF SERINE PALMITOYLTRANSFERASE (SPT), CATALYZES THE FIRST AND RATE-LIMITING STEP IN SPHINGOLIPID BIOSYNTHESIS. MUTATIONS IN SPTLC1 HAVE BEEN LINKED TO HEREDITARY SENSORY AND AUTONOMIC NEUROPATHY TYPE I (HSAN1) AND JUVENILE ALS (JALS). THESE MUTATIONS DISRUPT THE BALANCE OF SPHINGOLIPIDS, IMPLICATING SPHINGOLIPID DYSREGULATION IN MOTOR NEURON VULNERABILITY. DESPITE THESE FINDINGS, THE PHYSIOLOGICAL ROLE OF SPTLC1 IN THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) REMAINS POORLY DEFINED, PRIMARILY BECAUSE GLOBAL SPTLC1 KNOCKOUT MICE ARE EMBRYONICALLY LETHAL DUE TO COMPLETE LOSS OF SPT ACTIVITY. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT HOMOZYGOUS DELETION OF SPTLC1 EXON 2 (ΔE2)—WHICH ENCODES A CRITICAL N-TERMINAL TRANSMEMBRANE DOMAIN REQUIRED FOR ER ANCHORING—CAUSES EARLY LETHALITY AND SEVERE MOTOR DYSFUNCTION, INDICATING ITS ESSENTIAL ROLE IN NEURONAL VIABILITY. INTERESTINGLY, OUR FINDINGS SUGGEST THAT TARGETED EXON 2 DELETION PRODUCES A PROTEIN THAT RETAINS PARTIAL LOCALIZATION AND RESIDUAL ENZYMATIC ACTIVITY IN VIVO, UNLIKE THE NULL PHENOTYPE OF GLOBAL SPTLC1 KNOCKOUTS. THIS PROVIDES A TRACTABLE SYSTEM TO MODEL PARTIAL SPT DYSFUNCTION, SIMILAR TO WHAT IS OBSERVED IN HUMAN ALS DISEASE. CURRENTLY, THERE ARE NO IN VIVO MODELS THAT ALLOW PRECISE DISSECTION OF SPTLC1 FUNCTION IN THE CNS. BY CREATING THE FIRST CONDITIONAL SPTLC1 ΔEXON2 MOUSE, THIS PROJECT WILL REVEAL HOW DISRUPTED SPHINGOLIPID HOMEOSTASIS DRIVES NEURODEGENERATION AND WILL ESTABLISH A FOUNDATIONAL TOOL TO STUDY METABOLIC MECHANISMS UNDERLYING ALS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MODELING ALS PATHOGENESIS USING HUMAN IPSC-DERIVED NEUROMUSCULAR ORGANOIDS - PROJECT SUMMARY TITLE: MODELING ALS PATHOGENESIS USING HUMAN IPSC-DERIVED NEUROMUSCULAR ORGANOIDS THREE-DIMENSIONAL (3D) ORGANOID MODELS DERIVED FROM HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS (IPSCS) HAVE EMERGED AS POWERFUL TOOLS FOR STUDYING HUMAN DEVELOPMENT AND DISEASE IN VITRO. NEUROMUSCULAR ORGANOIDS (NMOS), WHICH INTEGRATE SPINAL MOTOR NEURONS, SKELETAL MUSCLE FIBERS, AND GLIAL CELLS, ARE PARTICULARLY PROMISING FOR MODELING MOTOR CIRCUITRY AND NEUROMUSCULAR JUNCTIONS (NMJS), THE SYNAPSES ESSENTIAL FOR VOLUNTARY MUSCLE CONTROL. DESPITE RECENT ADVANCES, CURRENT NMO MODELS OFTEN LACK STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL MATURITY, AND THEIR ABILITY TO ACCURATELY REPLICATE HUMAN NEUROMUSCULAR CONNECTIVITY AND PHYSIOLOGY REMAINS LIMITED. FURTHERMORE, THEIR POTENTIAL AS DISEASE MODELS, ESPECIALLY FOR MOTOR NEURON DISORDERS SUCH AS AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (ALS), HAS YET TO BE FULLY REALIZED. THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS TO ESTABLISH AND VALIDATE A PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT NMO PLATFORM AND APPLY IT TO MODEL ALS PATHOLOGY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SELF-ORGANIZING NMOS DERIVED FROM HUMAN IPSCS CAN RECAPITULATE THE CELLULAR, STRUCTURAL, AND FUNCTIONAL FEATURES OF THE HUMAN NEUROMUSCULAR SYSTEM AND YIELD MECHANISTIC INSIGHT INTO ALS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL INVESTIGATE NEUROMUSCULAR DEVELOPMENTAL AND ARCHITECTURAL ALTERATIONS IN ALS NMOS COMPARED TO ISOGENIC CONTROLS. NMOS WILL BE GENERATED FROM HIPSCS DERIVED FROM JUVENILE AND EARLY-ONSET ALS SUBTYPES (ALS4 AND ALS6) AND ASSESSED FOR CELLULAR COMPOSITION, SPATIAL ORGANIZATION, AND NMJ ULTRASTRUCTURE USING IMMUNOSTAINING, CONFOCAL IMAGING, AND ELECTRON MICROSCOPY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DEFINE FUNCTIONAL DEFICITS AND SYNAPTIC CHANGES IN ALS NMOS USING MULTIELECTRODE ARRAY (MEA) RECORDINGS AND PHARMACOLOGICAL MODULATION OF SYNAPTIC ACTIVITY. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL YIELD A REPRODUCIBLE, FUNCTIONAL HUMAN NMO PLATFORM FOR STUDYING NEUROMUSCULAR DEVELOPMENT, DISEASE MECHANISMS, AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSES. THIS WORK WILL ADVANCE ORGANOID TECHNOLOGY AND ADDRESS A CRITICAL GAP IN ALS MODELING BY PROVIDING A SCALABLE, HUMAN-RELEVANT SYSTEM FOR MECHANISTIC INVESTIGATION AND FUTURE DRUG SCREENING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: VOLTAGE CLAMP FLUOROMETRY OF TMEM16A CHANNELS IN AXOLOTL OOCYTES - ABSTRACT. TMEM16A IS CALCIUM-ACTIVATED CHLORIDE CHANNEL THAT IS EXPRESSED IN SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS AND PERICYTES LINING THE BRAIN’S BLOOD VESSELS, WHERE IT CONTRIBUTES TO THE PROCESS OF VASOCONSTRICTION. HYPERTENSION UPREGULATES TMEM16A EXPRESSION, AND THEY BECOME ACTIVATED DURING ISCHEMIC STROKE, EXACERBATING THE LOSS OF BLOOD FLOW AND RESULTING TISSUE DAMAGE. AS SUCH, THEY ARE A TEMPTING AND ACCESSIBLE TARGET FOR THERAPEUTICS TO PREVENT OR MITIGATE THE EFFECTS OF A STROKE. HOWEVER, DEVELOPMENT OF DRUGS HAS BEEN HAMPERED BY THE FUNCTIONAL COMPLEXITY OF TMEM16A, WHICH HAS CAUSED DRUGS WITH PREDICTED THERAPEUTIC PROMISE TO BE CONTRAINDICATED OWING TO UNEXPECTED PHARMACOLOGY AT THE CHANNEL. IMPROVED MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF TMEM16A BIOPHYSICS AND ITS RESPONSE TO INHIBITORY COMPOUNDS, USING FUNCTIONAL APPROACHES INFORMED BY KNOWN 3D CRYO- EM STRUCTURES OF TMEM16A, WOULD BENEFIT FUTURE DRUG DESIGN AND VALIDATION OF EXISTING CANDIDATES. ONE POWERFUL SUCH APPROACH IS VOLTAGE CLAMP FLUOROMETRY, WHICH COMBINES SIMULTANEOUS FLUORESCENT TRACKING OF CONFORMATIONAL CHANGES WITHIN A PROTEIN WITH RECORDING OF RESULTING CURRENTS IN ORDER TO ASSOCIATE STRUCTURAL CHANGES WITH FUNCTIONAL OUTPUTS. HOWEVER, THIS APPROACH TYPICALLY EMPLOYS OOCYTES FROM XENOPUS LAEVIS FROGS AS AN EXPRESSION SYSTEM; THE HIGH NATIVE EXPRESSION OF TMEM16A IN THAT CELL TYPE MAKES THEIR USE FOR THIS APPROACH IMPRACTICAL. HERE, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP AND TEST A VOLTAGE CLAMP FLUOROMETRY ASSAY IN OOCYTES FROM AMBYSTOMA MEXICANUM (AXOLOTLS), AND TO USE IT TO CHARACTERIZE THE STRUCTURAL CORRELATES OF FUNCTION OF TMEM16A CHANNELS IN RESPONSE TO SALIENT STIMULI. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO HARNESS VOLTAGE CLAMP FLUOROMETRY AS BOTH A VALUABLE EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH TO BETTER UNDERSTAND STRUCTURE-FUNCTION RELATIONSHIPS OF THE TMEM16 FAMILY, AND TO DEMONSTRATE ITS VALUE AS A TOOL FOR MECHANISTIC EVALUATION OF THE PROPERTIES OF INHIBITORY DRUGS UNDER THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION FOR STROKE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING A TUMOR SUPPRESSOR ROLE FOR BAI3 IN GLIOBLASTOMA - ABSTRACT GLIOBLASTOMA MULTIFORME (GBM) IS THE MOST AGGRESSIVE PRIMARY TUMOR OF THE ADULT CNS, WITH A MEDIAN SURVIVAL OF APPROXIMATELY 15 MONTHS. WHILE GBM PROGRESSION IS DRIVEN BY EXTENSIVE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR HETEROGENEITY, THE NERVOUS SYSTEM–SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTIONAL MECHANISMS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO THIS DIVERSITY REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. ALTERNATIVE PROMOTER USAGE REPRESENTS A MAJOR SOURCE OF TRANSCRIPT AND PROTEIN ISOFORM DIVERSITY IN THE BRAIN, YET ITS FUNCTIONAL IMPACT IN MALIGNANT GLIOMA HAS NOT BEEN SYSTEMATICALLY EXPLORED. ADHESION GPCR BAI3 (ADGRB3; B3), A BRAIN-ENRICHED RECEPTOR WITH ESTABLISHED ROLES IN NEURONAL DEVELOPMENT AND SYNAPTIC ORGANIZATION, IS ABERRANTLY EXPRESSED IN HIGH-GRADE GLIOMA. HOWEVER, THE REGULATION AND FUNCTION OF B3 ISOFORMS IN THE DISEASED BRAIN ARE UNKNOWN. USING LONG-READ RNA SEQUENCING, WE IDENTIFIED TWO PREDOMINANT B3 TRANSCRIPTS GENERATED BY DISTINCT PROMOTERS: ONE ENCODING A FULL-LENGTH ISOFORM (~171.5 KDA; FL-B3) AND A SECOND ENCODING A TRUNCATED ISOFORM (~81.7 KDA; S-B3) INITIATED FROM AN ALTERNATIVE PROMOTER UPSTREAM OF EXON 18. IMMUNOBLOT ANALYSES IN GENETICALLY ENGINEERED MOUSE MODELS CONFIRM EXPRESSION OF BOTH ISOFORMS AND SUPPORT ALTERNATIVE PROMOTER–DEPENDENT GENERATION OF S-B3. BOTH ISOFORMS ARE SIGNIFICANTLY DOWNREGULATED IN GBM RELATIVE TO NORMAL BRAIN TISSUE. IMPORTANTLY, ORTHOTOPIC XENOGRAFT STUDIES DEMONSTRATE THAT RESTORATION OF S-B3, BUT NOT FL-B3, SIGNIFICANTLY PROLONGS SURVIVAL, AND PROTEOMIC PROFILING INDICATES THAT S-B3 SUPPRESSES EMT PROGRAMS AND PROMOTES A MET SHIFT. BASED ON THESE FINDINGS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT S-B3 IS A NERVOUS SYSTEM-SPECIFIC, TUMOR SUPPRESSIVE ISOFORM WHOSE EXPRESSION IS CONTROLLED BY A DISTINCT PROMOTER ACTIVE IN DEFINED NEUROANATOMICAL CONTEXTS. AIM 1 WILL IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY VALIDATE THE ALTERNATIVE PROMOTER DRIVING S-B3 EXPRESSION BY INTEGRATING CHROMATIN ACCESSIBILITY, PROMOTER-ASSOCIATED HISTONE MODIFICATIONS, TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR ANALYSES, AND REPORTER ASSAYS, AND WILL DEFINE ISOFORM-SPECIFIC EXPRESSION PATTERNS ACROSS MOUSE AND HUMAN BRAIN REGIONS. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE HOW THE S-B3 ISOFORM INFLUENCES GBM CELL BEHAVIOR WITHIN THE NEURONAL MICROENVIRONMENT USING ORTHOTOPIC XENOGRAFT TUMORIGENICITY ASSAYS, LIVE BRAIN-SLICE IMAGING, FOCUSED IN VITRO ASSAYS, AND TARGETED PROTEOMIC ANALYSES. THIS EXPLORATORY R03 WILL DEFINE A NERVOUS SYSTEM-SPECIFIC MECHANISM OF B3 ISOFORM REGULATION AND TUMOR SUPPRESSOR FUNCTION IN GBM, ESTABLISHING A FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE STUDIES ON HOW ALTERNATIVE PROMOTER USAGE SHAPES BRAIN DEVELOPMENT AND CNS DISEASE. THIS IS A NEW R03 GRANT SUBMISSION IN RESPONSE TO PA-25-122: PILOT PROJECTS INVESTIGATING UNDERSTUDIED PROTEINS ASSOCIATED WITH RARE DISEASES. GBM IS IDENTIFIED AS A RARE DISEASE BY THE NCATS GENETIC AND RARE DISEASES INFORMATION CENTER AND ADGRB3 IS ON THE LIST OF UNDERSTUDIED PROTEINS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADVANCING CAREGIVING SCIENCE: A TRANSDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH CONFERENCE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT AN ESTIMATED 63 MILLION AMERICANS PROVIDE ESSENTIAL CARE FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH CHRONIC ILLNESS OR DISABILITY. CAREGIVING SPANS THE LIFECOURSE, CROSSES HEALTH CONDITIONS, AND FORMS THE BACKBONE OF OUR LONG-TERM CARE SYSTEMS. ENSURING CAREGIVERS RECEIVE ADEQUATE EDUCATION, TRAINING, AND SUPPORT IS THEREFORE A PRESSING PUBLIC HEALTH PRIORITY. AS THE U.S. POPULATION AGES, THE DEMAND FOR CARE CONTINUES TO GROW—REACHING LEVELS MANY NOW DESCRIBE AS A PUBLIC HEALTH CRISIS—AND UNDERSCORES THE NEED FOR A WORKFORCE EQUIPPED TO GENERATE EVIDENCE-BASED SOLUTIONS. YET CAREGIVING RESEARCH REMAINS FRAGMENTED, WITH MOST CONFERENCES ORGANIZED AROUND SPECIFIC DISCIPLINES, DIAGNOSES, OR AGE GROUPS. THESE SILOS LIMIT OPPORTUNITIES TO SHARE INNOVATIONS THAT COULD ADVANCE SCIENCE ACROSS CAREGIVING POPULATIONS AND HINDER DISSEMINATION OF METHODOLOGIES APPLICABLE ACROSS AGES, DISEASES, AND DISABILITY STATUS. COORDINATED PROGRESS REQUIRES AN INTERDISCIPLINARY NETWORK OF CAREGIVING STAKEHOLDERS WORKING TOGETHER TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED APPROACHES. ADVANCING CAREGIVING SCIENCE: A TRANSDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH CONFERENCE IS A BIENNIAL CONFERENCE SERIES DESIGNED TO BRIDGE THESE SILOS BY CONVENING INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCHERS, NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS AND HEALTH CARE SYSTEM REPRESENTATIVES TO STRENGTHEN SUPPORT FOR CAREGIVERS. SPECIFIC GOALS ARE TO 1) PREPARE THE NEXT GENERATION OF CAREGIVING SCIENTISTS TO GENERATE RESEARCH THAT IS ACTIONABLE THROUGH MENTORSHIP, TRAINING, AND STRUCTURED NETWORKING ACTIVITIES, 2) FOSTER TRANSDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATIONS ACROSS THE LIFECOURSE AND DISEASES/DISABILITIES TO DRIVE INNOVATION IN CAREGIVING RESEARCH AND ITS IMPLEMENTATION, AND 3) SYNTHESIZE AND DISSEMINATE ACTIONABLE RESEARCH FINDINGS FOR STAKEHOLDERS ACROSS THE NATION INCLUDING CAREGIVERS TO MAXIMIZE IMPACT. THIS R13 PROPOSAL BUILDS ON THREE SUCCESSFUL PRIOR CONFERENCES, EACH INCREASING IN VISIBILITY AND ATTENDANCE AND SHAPED BY ATTENDEE FEEDBACK. THE CONFERENCE FORMAT INCLUDES KEYNOTE ADDRESSES FROM NATIONAL LEADERS OF CAREGIVING ORGANIZATIONS AND LEADING SCIENTISTS; PLENARY SESSIONS HIGHLIGHTING DIFFERENT RESEARCH METHODOLOGIES, AND INTERACTIVE PANEL SESSIONS WITH FUNDERS, CAREGIVERS, AND RESEARCHERS OF UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS. NETWORKING AND MENTORSHIP ARE INTEGRATED THROUGHOUT, AND EARLY-CAREER INVESTIGATORS RECEIVE TRAINING IN SECONDARY DATA ANALYSIS, TEAM-SCIENCE, MANUSCRIPT DEVELOPMENT, AND RESEARCH REPORT GENERATION. THE CONFERENCE SERIES ALIGNS WITH NIA STRATEGIC DIRECTIONS (2020–2025) BY EXPANDING THE CAREGIVING RESEARCH WORKFORCE, STRENGTHENING INTERDISCIPLINARY EXCHANGE, ADVANCING UNDERSTANDING OF INTERPERSONAL AND SOCIAL FACTORS AFFECTING CAREGIVERS AND CARE RECIPIENTS, AND DISSEMINATING EFFECTIVE SOLUTIONS ADAPTABLE ACROSS CONTEXTS AND AGE GROUPS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ALZHEIMER'S PREVENTION IN WOMEN THROUGH ANALYSIS OF KEY EXPOSOME DOMAINS (AWAKE) - PROJECT SUMMARY WOMEN REPRESENT NEARLY TWO-THIRDS OF ALL NEW ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD) CASES. MOUNTING EVIDENCE SUPPORTS SEX DIFFERENCES IN THE DETERMINANTS OF ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (AD) AND ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD) RISK, WITH VASCULAR AND HORMONAL FACTORS POTENTIALLY BEING ESPECIALLY CRITICAL FOR WOMEN. RELATIVE TO MEN, WOMEN SHOW GREATER BURDENS OF AD AND CEREBROVASCULAR PATHOLOGY, AND FASTER COGNITIVE DECLINE IN THE PRESENCE OF AD PATHOLOGY. HOWEVER, LESS ATTENTION HAS BEEN PAID TO MODIFIABLE EXPOSOME DOMAINS —THE TOTALITY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL EXPOSURES EXPERIENCED ACROSS THE LIFE-COURSE— THAT MAY DETERMINE THE DISTRIBUTION AND EFFECT OF INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL FACTORS. WOMEN ARE EXPOSED TO SOCIAL ENVIRONMENTS (E.G., FINANCIAL INSECURITY, RESIDENTIAL CONTEXT, CAREGIVING, AND WORKPLACE), PHYSICAL ENVIRONMENT (E.G., AIR POLLUTION, NOISE, GREENSPACE, NEIGHBORHOOD AMENITIES), AND POLICIES (E.G., INSURANCE COVERAGE, WORKPLACE PROTECTIONS) IN PATTERNS THAT DIFFER FROM MEN. HOWEVER, BECAUSE EACH DOMAIN DEMANDS SPECIALIZED METHODOLOGICAL EXPERTISE, THERE IS LITTLE CROSS-DISCIPLINARY INTERACTION TO DRIVE PROGRESS. TO ADDRESS THIS SIGNIFICANT GAP, WE PROPOSE THE ALZHEIMER’S PREVENTION IN WOMEN THROUGH ANALYSIS OF KEY EXPOSOME DOMAINS (AWAKE). AWAKE WILL FILL A UNIQUE NICHE BY EXAMINING HOW EXPOSOME DOMAINS —INCLUDING THE SOCIAL, PHYSICAL ENVIRONMENT, AND POLICIES— ARE ASSOCIATED WITH AD/ADRD INCIDENCE AND PROGRESSION IN WOMEN, RECOGNIZING THE COMPLEX INTERPLAY ALONG ACROSS WOMEN’S LIFE-COURSE. AWAKE WILL CONVENE AN INTERDISCIPLINARY COMMUNITY OF RESEARCHERS TO SHARE, DEBATE, RESEARCH, AND TEACH ANALYTIC METHODS BEST ALIGNED WITH THE CHALLENGES OF INCREASED ADRD RISK AMONG WOMEN. AWAKE WILL CONSIST OF TWO PHASES, STARTING WITH A SERIES OF VIRTUAL SEMINARS TO DISCUSS CONCEPTS AND STATE-OF-THE-ART METHODOLOGY, FOLLOWED BY AN IN-PERSON HANDS- ON DATA ANALYSIS WORKSHOP TWICE PER YEAR. THROUGH BI-ANNUAL IN-PERSON WORKSHOPS, AWAKE WILL (A) OFFER STRUCTURED AND IN-DEPTH ANALYTIC TRAINING FOR EACH DOMAIN, (B) FACILITATE TRAINING, GROWTH, AND PARTNERSHIPS AMONG EXPERTS IN THE FIELD, AND (C) PROVIDE A PLATFORM FOR CONSTRUCTIVE DIALOGUE ON WORKS IN PROGRESS. AFTER THE IN-PERSON WORKSHOPS, AWAKE WILL HOST BI-MONTHLY SEMINAR-STYLE WORKING GROUP MEETINGS VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE, FOLLOWING UP ON ANALYSIS, DIDACTIC SESSIONS, AND INTERPRETATION OF RESULTS. THE SESSIONS WILL BE MODERATED BY EXPERTS IN THE FIELD, WITH PARTICIPATION BY RESEARCHERS RANGING FROM DOCTORAL STUDENTS TO SENIOR SCIENTISTS. NO EXISTING VENUE BRINGS TOGETHER EXPERTS FROM MULTIPLE FIELDS TO QUANTITATIVELY ASSESS EXPOSOME DOMAINS, INCREASE AWARENESS, AND PROMOTE STRATEGIES TO MITIGATE CONTRIBUTORS TO AD/ADRD IN WOMEN. AWAKE WILL CONTRIBUTE SUBSTANTIALLY TO THE TRAINING OF A NEW GENERATION OF EXPOSOME SCIENTISTS RESEARCHING AD/ADRD IN WOMEN THROUGH CREATING A CENTRAL SOURCE OF MEASURES, GUIDANCE, AND TOOLS TO CONDUCT ADVANCED EXPOSOME DOMAIN ANALYSIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: T CELLS IN THE BRAIN (TCB2027): DECODING T CELL TARGETS IN NEURODEGENERATION - ABSTRACT T CELLS ARE KEY CONTRIBUTORS TO NEUROINFLAMMATION AND NEURODEGENERATION, YET IDENTIFYING THEIR TARGETS AND ANTIGEN SPECIFICITIES IN HUMAN NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE REMAINS A MAJOR CHALLENGE. RAPID ADVANCES IN NEUROIMMUNOLOGY, INCLUDING SINGLE-CELL MULTIOMICS, TCR REPERTOIRE SEQUENCING, AND ANTIGEN-DISCOVERY PLATFORMS, HAVE BEGUN TO RESHAPE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF T CELL BIOLOGY IN THE CNS. BUILDING ON THE SUCCESS OF TCB2024 AND TCB2025, WHICH EACH CONVENED OVER 200 NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL ATTENDEES, THE T CELLS IN THE BRAIN SERIES HAS ESTABLISHED ITSELF AS THE PREMIER FORUM FOR INTEGRATING T CELL BIOLOGY WITH HUMAN NEURODEGENERATION. THESE MEETINGS GENERATED NEW MULTI-INSTITUTIONAL COLLABORATIONS, FOSTERED TECHNOLOGY EXCHANGE AMONG IMMUNOLOGISTS, NEUROPATHOLOGISTS, T CELL ENGINEERS, AND COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGISTS, AND SUPPORTED SEVERAL EMERGING JOINT GRANT APPLICATIONS AND SHARED DATASETS. “T CELLS IN THE BRAIN (TCB2027): DECODING T CELL TARGETS IN NEURODEGENERATION” WILL ADVANCE THIS MOMENTUM BY CONSOLIDATING RECENT PROGRESS AND PROMOTING INTERDISCIPLINARY DISCUSSION TOWARD PRECISION T-CELL-BASED THERAPIES. TCB REMAINS COMMITTED TO ACTIVE EFFORTS TO ENGAGE TRAINEES, AND JUNIOR RESEARCHERS. BY UNITING INTERDISCIPLINARY EXPERTISE AND STRENGTHENING COLLABORATIVE NETWORKS, TCB2027 AIMS TO ACCELERATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE T CELL-BASED INTERVENTIONS FOR NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS.

description: TRANSCRIPTION, CHROMATIN, AND EPIGENETICS IN AGING - SUMMARY THE GOAL OF THIS FASEB MEETING “CHROMATIN AND EPIGENETICS IN AGING AND DISEASE” IS TO BRING A COMMUNITY OF RESEARCHERS TOGETHER TO ADVANCE OUR COLLECTIVE UNDERSTANDING OF EPIGENETIC MECHANISMS OF AGING AND AGE- ASSOCIATED DISEASES USING INNOVATIVE APPROACHES. EPIGENETICS AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL CHANGES ARE MAJOR HALLMARKS OF AGING AND AGE-ASSOCIATED DISEASES SUCH AS CANCER. RECENT ADVANCES IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS HAVE REVEALED STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS, REPAIR DAMAGE, AND DEVELOP THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR DISEASE. WE WILL DISCUSS FUNDAMENTAL MECHANISMS OF TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC REGULATION, NEW TECHNOLOGIES IN THIS AREA, AND NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TO TARGET AGE-RELATED DISEASES. IN THE 2026 MEETING, WE WILL INTRODUCE NEW SESSIONS ON SINGLE-CELL BIOLOGY, SEX CHROMOSOME CHANGES, AND STEM CELLS. THIS FASEB MEETING WILL BE UNIQUE IN INTEGRATING THE LATEST DISCOVERIES IN EPIGENETICS AND THEIR IMPORTANCE IN AGING AS WELL AS NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TO COMBAT AGING AND AGE-RELATED DISEASES. AS EPIGENETIC TARGETS ARE RAPIDLY BEING IDENTIFIED AGAINST AGING AND DISEASE, AND TECHNOLOGIES INCORPORATING MACHINE LEARNING ARE ACCELERATING DISCOVERIES IN EPIGENOMICS, THERE IS A CRUCIAL NEED FOR SUCH A MEETING THAT GATHERS SCIENTISTS AT THE FOREFRONT OF THESE AREAS TO DISCUSS INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACHES TO ADDRESS KEY QUESTIONS IN THE FIELD. ADDITIONALLY, TECHNOLOGICAL CHALLENGES AND QUESTIONS ABOUT THE ROLE OF EPIGENETICS IN AGING AND AGE-RELATED DISEASES REMAIN, AND IT IS ESSENTIAL THAT INVESTIGATORS IN THE CHROMATIN AND TRANSCRIPTION FIELDS GAIN A DEEPER UNDERSTANDING OF THE IMPLICATIONS OF THEIR WORK FOR HEALTH AND DISEASE. THIS CONFERENCE WILL FOSTER INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INVESTIGATORS ADDRESSING BASIC MECHANISTIC QUESTIONS, DEVELOPING NEW METHODOLOGIES, AND THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES. THE EVENT WILL PROVIDE A UNIQUELY INTERACTIVE AND INCLUSIVE ENVIRONMENT THROUGH SHORT TALKS, POSTER TEASERS, KEYNOTE TALKS, NETWORKING OPPORTUNITIES, AND MEET-THE- EXPERT EVENTS. TO SUPPORT THE GENERATION OF SCIENTISTS, THE CONFERENCE ALSO INCLUDES A FULL DAY TRAINEE PRE-MEETING KNOWN AS THE IGNITE-FORUM. THIS EVENT IS DEDICATED TO CAREER-DEVELOPMENT AND NETWORKING FOR TRAINEES AND NEW INVESTIGATORS. THIS IS AN OPPORTUNITY FOR YOUNG INVESTIGATORS TO OBTAIN FEEDBACK ON THEIR WORK, ESTABLISH A PROFESSIONAL NETWORK, AND IDENTIFY OPPORTUNITIES FOR COLLABORATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: 2026 PEDIATRIC DERMATOLOGY RESEARCH ALLIANCE (PEDRA) ANNUAL CONFERENCE - PROJECT SUMMARY PEDIATRIC SKIN DISEASES ARE HIGHLY PREVALENT AND IMPART A DEVASTATING BURDEN ON CHILDREN AND THEIR FAMILIES. YET, THE SPECIALTY OF PEDIATRIC DERMATOLOGY IS UNDERSTAFFED, THE AVAILABILITY OF FDA- APPROVED TREATMENTS IS INADEQUATE, AND THE PACE OF RESEARCH AND GUIDELINES DEVELOPMENT IN THE FIELD IS TOO SLOW. THE PEDIATRIC DERMATOLOGY RESEARCH ALLIANCE (PEDRA) WAS FOUNDED IN 2012 TO ADDRESS THESE CRUCIAL YET UNMET NEEDS. PEDRA'S PRIMARY MISSION IS TO CREATE, INSPIRE, AND SUSTAIN RESEARCH TO PREVENT, TREAT, AND CURE CHILDHOOD SKIN DISEASE. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF PEDRA IS TO LEVERAGE SUCH RESEARCH TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OUTCOMES OF CHILDREN WITH SKIN DISORDERS. ANNUAL CONFERENCES HAVE BEEN INTEGRAL TO THE SUCCESS OF PEDRA, PROVIDING A FORUM FOR EDUCATING INVESTIGATORS, IDENTIFYING AND PRIORITIZING RESEARCH NEEDS AND OPPORTUNITIES, AND DEVELOPING AND INITIATING INNOVATIVE PROJECTS. A COMBINATION OF DIDACTIC LECTURES AND PANELS, EXPERT-LED SMALL GROUP DISCUSSIONS, POSTER SESSIONS, AND UNIQUE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES ARE THE FOUNDATION OF EVERY PEDRA ANNUAL CONFERENCE. THIS PROPOSAL IS FOR THE 14TH PEDRA ANNUAL CONFERENCE, SET TO TAKE PLACE IN OCTOBER OF 2026 WITH THE FOLLOWING AIMS: 1) PROVIDE EDUCATION, PRESENTATION, AND NETWORKING OPPORTUNITIES THAT ENGAGE A BROAD AUDIENCE WHILE EQUIPPING ATTENDEES TO MAKE USE OF LIMITED TIME AND RESOURCES TO ADVANCE SCIENCE THAT IMPROVES THE LIVES OF CHILDREN WITH SKIN DISEASES AND CONDITIONS; 2) ADVANCE EXISTING RESEARCH PROJECTS AND DEVELOP NEW RESEARCH PRIORITIES AND INITIATIVES IN DISEASE AREAS AND HIGH-PRIORITY TOPICS SPANNING THE FIELD OF PEDIATRIC DERMATOLOGY; AND 3) PROVIDE A FORUM FOR THE DISSEMINATION OF FINAL AND ONGOING RESEARCH RESULTS TO A LARGE AUDIENCE THAT INCLUDES PATIENT STAKEHOLDERS, INDUSTRY REPRESENTATIVES, AND RESEARCHERS FROM MULTIPLE FIELDS INCLUDING POTENTIAL NIH COLLABORATORS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF THIS CONFERENCE ARE A MORE DEVELOPED SET OF RESEARCH SKILLS FOR CURRENT AND FUTURE PHYSICIAN-SCIENTISTS, ENHANCED PRODUCTIVITY, STRENGTHENED MULTI-STAKEHOLDER NETWORKS, AND THE CONDUCT OF HIGH-QUALITY RESEARCH. THESE ACTIVITIES WILL ACCELERATE THE PACE OF PEDIATRIC DERMATOLOGY RESEARCH, ALLOWING CLINICIANS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND, PREVENT AND TREAT SKIN DISEASE IN CHILDREN, AND GIVING PATIENTS AND FAMILIES OPTIONS TO MANAGE DISEASES AND MAKE INFORMED TREATMENT DECISIONS IN THE FUTURE.

description: 2026 ORS/PSRS 8TH SPINE RESEARCH SYMPOSIUM - SUMMARY THE PHILADELPHIA SPINE RESEARCH SOCIETY (PSRS) HAS BEEN CONDUCTING ANNUAL RESEARCH MEETINGS SINCE 2004 AND 2026 WILL BE THE 8TH BIANNUAL SPINE RESEARCH SYMPOSIUM OF THE SOCIETY IN COLLABORATION WITH THE ORTHOPAEDIC RESEARCH SOCIETY (ORS). THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS SUPPORT TO PROMOTE AND ENHANCE ATTENDANCE BY TRAINEES AND JUNIOR FACULTY AT THE 2026 ORS PSRS 8TH SPINE RESEARCH SYMPOSIUM. THE SYMPOSIUM WILL TAKE PLACE ON NOVEMBER 1-5, 2026 AT SKYTOP LODGE, PA WHICH IS A CONVENIENT LOCATION FOR BOTH THE GREATER PHILADELPHIA AND NEW YORK REGIONS. THE PRIMARY PURPOSE OF THIS CONFERENCE IS TO PROMOTE STATE-OF-THE-ART RESEARCH AND TO ENHANCE SCIENTIFIC DISCOURSE AND COLLABORATIONS IN THE BROAD FIELD OF INTERVERTEBRAL DISC BIOLOGY AND BACK PAIN RESEARCH. PREVIOUS ORS-PSRS CONFERENCES HAVE HAD AN EXCELLENT TRACK RECORD OF BRINGING TOGETHER RESEARCHERS AND CLINICIANS FROM BROAD DISCIPLINES AT VARIOUS CAREER STAGES. THE KEY FEATURES OF THE SYMPOSIUM INCLUDE, STATE-OF-THE-ART INVITED LECTURES, PEER-REVIEWED PRESENTATIONS, PANEL DISCUSSIONS, AND TRAINEE AND STUDENT PRESENTATIONS. HALLMARK FEATURES OF THIS CONFERENCE ARE ITS RELAXED AND INFORMAL ATMOSPHERE AND PURPOSEFULLY UNSCHEDULED TIME TO PERMIT INTERACTIONS AND EXCHANGE OF IDEAS AMONG PARTICIPANTS. THE MAIN THEME OF THE MEETING IS “CROSSTALK IN DISC DEGENERATION AND BACK PAIN” AND TOPICS TO BE HIGHLIGHTED INCLUDE EPIDEMIOLOGY AND CLINICAL CHALLENGES IN THE SPINE; IMAGING, BIOMECHANICS AND MECHANOBIOLOGY; MOLECULAR, CELL, AND DEVELOPMENTAL BIOLOGY OF THE DISC; CROSSTALK IN THE AGING SPINE AND PATHOMECHANISMS OF BACK PAIN; FUNCTIONAL TISSUE ENGINEERING AND BIOMATERIALS FOR SPINE REPAIR; NOVEL THERAPIES AND PRECLINICAL TRANSLATION; AND AI, VIRTUAL REALITY AND INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGIES TO REDUCE BACK PAIN AND DISABILITY. THE ORGANIZERS EXPECT PARTICIPATION FROM BASIC RESEARCHERS AS WELL AS CLINICIANS CONCERNED WITH THE DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT OF SPINAL DISORDERS INCLUDING DISC DEGENERATION AND BACK PAIN.

description: CSHL 2026 CONFERENCE ON CELL AND MEMBRANE FUSION - PROJECT SUMMARY THIS APPLICATION SEEKS PARTIAL SUPPORT FOR THE SECOND COLD SPRING HARBOR MEETING ON  CELL & MEMBRANE FUSION , TO BE HELD NOVEMBER 11-14, 2026 AT COLD SPRING HARBOR LABORATORY, NEW YORK. THIS IS THE ONLY CONFERENCE THAT BRINGS TOGETHER RESEARCHERS STUDYING CELL-CELL FUSION, VIRUS-CELL FUSION, AND INTRACELLULAR FUSION IN A SINGLE VENUE, FOSTERING CROSS-FERTILIZATION OF IDEAS ACROSS TRADITIONALLY SEPARATE FIELDS. CELL AND MEMBRANE FUSION EVENTS ARE FUNDAMENTAL TO ALL LIVING ORGANISMS AND PARTICULARLY CRITICAL FOR MUSCLE DEVELOPMENT AND REGENERATION, OSTEOCLAST FUNCTION IN BONE REMODELING, FERTILIZATION, VIRAL INFECTION, AND ORGANELLE BIOGENESIS. FAILURES IN FUSION LEAD TO CONGENITAL MYOPATHY, OSTEOPOROSIS, INFERTILITY, IMMUNE DEFICIENCY, AND SYNAPTIC TRANSMISSION DEFECTS. WE EXPECT APPROXIMATELY 150 ATTENDEES FROM AROUND THE WORLD, OF WHOM ~50% ARE EXPECTED TO BE FROM INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTIONS AND ~60% JUNIOR RESEARCHERS. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: 1) TO PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS OF RECENT DISCOVERIES IN MEMBRANE FUSION MECHANISMS; 2) TO FOSTER EXCHANGE BETWEEN BIOPHYSICISTS, STRUCTURAL BIOLOGISTS, VIROLOGISTS, AND CELL BIOLOGISTS WHO RARELY INTERACT AT DISCIPLINE-SPECIFIC MEETINGS; AND 3) TO PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR JUNIOR INVESTIGATORS TO PRESENT THEIR WORK. OUR KEYNOTE SPEAKERS ARE PROF. REINHARD JAHN (MPI GÖTTINGEN) AND PROF. GIA VOELTZ (HHMI, UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO BOULDER). SIX PLENARY SESSIONS WILL PRESENT ~50 SPEAKERS (14 CONFIRMED INVITED SPEAKERS AND ~36 SELECTED FROM ABSTRACTS). SESSION TOPICS INCLUDE MECHANISMS OF MEMBRANE FUSION, STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY OF FUSOGENS, CELL-CELL FUSION IN DEVELOPMENT AND DISEASE, MEMBRANE REMODELING, FERTILIZATION, AND EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES. THIS MEETING DIRECTLY ADDRESSES NIAMS PRIORITIES BY ACCELERATING UNDERSTANDING OF MUSCLE CELL FUSION ESSENTIAL FOR REGENERATION AND GENE DELIVERY APPROACHES FOR TREATING GENETIC MUSCLE DISORDERS AND OSTEOPOROSIS.

description: ASBMR 2026 PRE-MEETING SYMPOSIUM: BIOLOGICAL CONTROL OF BONE QUALITY: MECHANISMS AND THERAPIES - THE AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR BONE AND MINERAL RESEARCH (ASBMR) IS THE LARGEST PROFESSIONAL, SCIENTIFIC AND MEDICAL SOCIETY ESTABLISHED TO BRING TOGETHER CLINICAL AND LABORATORY-BASED INVESTIGATORS WHO ARE INVOLVED IN THE STUDY OF BONE, MINERAL AND MUSCULOSKELETAL DISORDERS. SINCE 2002, THE ASBMR HAS HELD ONE-DAY SYMPOSIA PRECEDING THE ANNUAL MEETING THAT WERE FUNDED BY AN R13 GRANT, TACKLED A SPECIFIC AND TIMELY SCIENTIFIC TOPIC, CONVENING EXPERTS AND EARLY CAREER INVESTIGATORS ALIKE. TO DATE, THESE MEETINGS HAVE BEEN VERY SUCCESSFUL WITH HIGH ATTENDANCE, ENGAGEMENT AND POSITIVE POST-MEETING REVIEWS. BASED ON THE SUCCESS OF THE PRE-MEETING PROGRAM IN CULTIVATING NEW SCIENTIFIC AND TRANSLATIONAL DIRECTIONS FOR THE MUSCULOSKELETAL FIELD, THE PRESENT APPLICATION SEEKS AN R13 GRANT TO ORGANIZE A ONE-DAY SYMPOSIUM IN AREAS WHERE DISCOVERY HAS ACCELERATED IN RECENT YEARS AND WHERE THE OPPORTUNITIES FOR TRANSLATION ARE WITHIN REACH. THE 2026 SYMPOSIUM WILL FOCUS ON “BIOLOGICAL CONTROL OF BONE QUALITY: MECHANISMS AND THERAPIES” AND ADDRESS A MOST PRESSING AND TIMELY AREA OF MUSCULOSKELETAL RESEARCH THAT IS UNDERGOING RAPID ADVANCES IN SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE THAT HAVE POTENTIAL TO IMPACT DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT OF DISORDERS WITH MAJOR CLINICAL MORBIDITY, DISABILITY AND MORTALITY. THE GOAL OF THE SYMPOSIUM IS TO FUEL AND STIMULATE PROGRESS TOWARD MORE EFFECTIVE AND NOVEL TREATMENTS FOR MUSCULOSKELETAL DISEASES, AIMING TO IMPROVE THE LIVES OF PATIENTS. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS R13 ALIGNS WITH NIH PRIORITIES BY ADDRESSING CRITICAL GAPS IN UNDERSTANDING AND TREATING CHRONIC DISEASE, INCLUDING BONE FRAGILITY. IT PROMOTES FUNDAMENTAL DISCOVERY OF THE CELLULAR, MOLECULAR, AND MATERIAL MECHANISMS CONTROLLING BONE QUALITY, ACCELERATES TRANSLATION OF THESE FINDINGS INTO DIAGNOSTICS AND THERAPIES, AND FOSTERS MULTIDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATION AMONG BASIC, TRANSLATIONAL, AND CLINICAL INVESTIGATORS. IN ADDITION, BY ENGAGING EARLY-CAREER SCIENTISTS THROUGH PRESENTATIONS AND MENTORSHIP, THE PROGRAM STRENGTHENS THE BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH WORKFORCE AND SUPPORTS THE DEVELOPMENT OF FUTURE LEADERS IN MUSCULOSKELETAL RESEARCH, CONSISTENT WITH NIH GOALS TO ADVANCE SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE AND IMPROVE PUBLIC HEALTH. THE SYMPOSIUM WILL BE HELD JUST PRIOR TO THE ASBMR 2026 ANNUAL MEETING AND THUS, ATTENDEES, INCLUDING TRAINEES, WILL BE ENCOURAGED TO JOIN THE MEETING, PROVIDING MORE OPPORTUNITIES TO ESTABLISH COLLABORATIONS, LEARN FROM OTHER MUSCULOSKELETAL RESEARCH AREAS AND IMPACT THEIR RESEARCH AND GOALS. THE PROGRAM WAS DEVELOPED BY AN ORGANIZING COMMITTEE, AND SPEAKERS HAVE CONFIRMED THEIR PARTICIPATION. THERE WILL BE POSTER SESSIONS AND PREFERENCE WILL BE GIVEN TO YOUNG INVESTIGATORS TO PRESENT THEIR ABSTRACT ORALLY TO FURTHER FACILITATE AND ENCOURAGE DIRECT INTERACTIONS BETWEEN YOUNG AND SENIOR INVESTIGATORS. THE SYMPOSIUM WILL FOCUS AND HIGHLIGHT RECENT PROGRESS ON CELLULAR, MOLECULAR AND MATERIAL MECHANISMS CONTROLLING BONE QUALITY AND HOW THEY CAN BE HARNESSED CLINICALLY.

description: SENSORY SYSTEMS: INTEROCEPTION AND EXTEROCEPTION - ABSTRACT SUPPORT IS REQUESTED FOR A KEYSTONE SYMPOSIA CONFERENCE ENTITLED SENSORY SYSTEMS: INTEROCEPTION AND EXTEROCEPTION ORGANIZED BY DRS. ALEXANDER CHESLER, STEPHEN LIBERLES AND VANESSA RUTA, WITH SCIENTIFIC PROGRAMMING INPUT FROM KEYSTONE SYMPOSIA. THE MEETING WILL TAKE PLACE JANUARY 18–21, 2027 AT KEYSTONE RESORT IN KEYSTONE, COLORADO, USA. OUR BASIC EXTERNAL SENSORY SYSTEMS—TOUCH, TASTE, VISION, HEARING, AND SMELL—ENABLE US TO PERCEIVE THE WORLD AROUND US, AND OTHER SENSORY SYSTEMS ENABLE US TO PERCEIVE AND REGULATE INTERNAL STATES. RECENT ADVANCES HAVE REVEALED THE MOLECULAR LOGIC OF HOW SOME SENSORY SYSTEMS WORK, WHILE OTHER SENSORY SYSTEMS REMAIN UNCHARTED. FIELDS OF SENSORY BIOLOGY OFTEN MAINTAIN SEPARATE CULTURES, AND ARE AT VARYING LEVELS OF MATURITY, WITH DIFFERENT FRONTIERS, UNKNOWNS, AND PERSPECTIVES. THE GOAL OF THIS KEYSTONE SYMPOSIA CONFERENCE ON SENSORY SYSTEMS: INTEROCEPTION AND EXTEROCEPTION IS TO BRING LEADING EXPERTS FROM DIFFERENT SENSORY FIELDS TOGETHER, AND TO BROADCAST CONCEPTUAL AND TECHNICAL ADVANCES ACHIEVED IN ONE SENSORY SYSTEM THAT MAY ENABLE NEW FINDINGS IN OTHERS. THE CONFERENCE PROGRAM WILL HIGHLIGHT RECENT ADVANCES IN EACH EXTERNAL SENSE: VISION, OLFACTION, TASTE, HEARING, AND TOUCH-PAIN-TEMPERATURE SENSATION, AS WELL AS NEW DEVELOPMENTS IN THE EMERGING FIELD OF INTERNAL ORGAN SENSATION. SPEAKERS WILL DISCUSS A RANGE OF TOPICS FROM (1) RECEPTORS AND SENSORY MECHANISMS, (2) NEURAL CIRCUITS, (3) BEHAVIORAL AND PHYSIOLOGICAL RESPONSES, AND (4) THE GENETIC BASIS OF SENSORY DEFICITS. FURTHER, THIS MEETING IS BEING HELD CONCURRENTLY WITH ANOTHER KEYSTONE SYMPOSIA CONFERENCE ON NEUROBIOLOGY OF APPETITE CONTROL, WHICH HAS STRONG CONNECTIONS WITH THE INTEROCEPTION PROGRAMMING IN THE SENSORY SYSTEMS CONFERENCE. THIS JOINT FORMAT ALLOWS A SHARED AND MORE IN-DEPTH FOCUS ON AN IMPORTANT AREA OF INTEROCEPTION, NOTABLY THE SENSATION AND NEUROBIOLOGY OF HUNGER AND SATIETY, PATHWAYS THAT HAVE EMERGED AS THE CENTRAL TARGETS OF SEVERAL NEW FAMILIES OF EFFECTIVE DRUGS FOR THE TREATMENT OF OBESITY, DIABETES AND MANY OTHER DISEASES. AS A RESULT, THE JOINT MEETING ALSO CREATES A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO BRIDGE BASIC RESEARCH IN SENSORY SYSTEMS WITH DIRECT INSIGHT INTO NEXT GENERATION THERAPEUTICS THAT MODULATE BRAIN-BODY COMMUNICATION.

description: PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES - ABSTRACT THIS APPLICATION REQUESTS PARTIAL FUNDING SUPPORT FOR THE 2026 FEDERATION OF AMERICAN SOCIETIES FOR EXPERIMENTAL BIOLOGY (FASEB) SCIENCE RESEARCH CONFERENCE ON PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES, ENTITLED, “SHAPING THE FUTURE OF PHOSPHATASE-TARGETED THERAPEUTICS,” TO BE HELD AT THE YOURS TRULY DC HOTEL IN WASHINGTON, DC, ON DECEMBER 14–17, 2026. PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES PLAY FUNDAMENTAL ROLES IN CELLULAR SIGNALING PATHWAYS, AND FOR MORE THAN 36 YEARS, THIS CONFERENCE HAS PROVIDED A PREMIER FORUM FOR ADVANCING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THEIR ROLES IN NORMAL PHYSIOLOGY AND HUMAN DISEASE. RECENT DISCOVERIES HAVE EXPANDED OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE FUNCTIONS AND REGULATION OF MORE THAN 1,000 PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE CATALYTIC AND REGULATORY SUBUNITS, COMPLEXES, AND ISOFORMS THAT GOVERN CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS. AS THE CAUSAL ROLES OF SPECIFIC PHOSPHATASES AND THEIR DISEASE-ASSOCIATED MUTATIONS CONTINUE TO BE ELUCIDATED, INVESTIGATORS ACROSS ACADEMIA, MEDICINE, AND INDUSTRY ARE INTEGRATING BASIC, TRANSLATIONAL, AND CLINICAL RESEARCH TO ACCELERATE THERAPEUTIC DISCOVERY. THIS CONFERENCE PROVIDES A FORUM FOR DISSEMINATING EMERGING DISCOVERIES, FOSTERING INTERDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATION, AND TRANSLATING MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES. THE 2026 MEETING REPRESENTS THE 18TH INSTALLMENT OF THIS LONG-STANDING BIENNIAL CONFERENCE, HELD CONTINUOUSLY SINCE 1990, AND REMAINS THE ONLY NORTH AMERICAN CONFERENCE DEDICATED EXCLUSIVELY TO PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES. THE MEETING WILL ALSO CONTINUE THE SUCCESSFUL PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN THE FASEB PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE CONFERENCE AND THE JAPANESE ASSOCIATION FOR PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE RESEARCH (JAPPR), STRENGTHENING INTERNATIONAL COLLABORATION AND SCIENTIFIC EXCHANGE. THE 12 SCIENTIFIC SESSIONS WILL FEATURE INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNIZED LEADERS AND EMERGING INVESTIGATORS PRESENTING ADVANCES IN STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY, SIGNALING, DISEASE MECHANISMS, DRUG DISCOVERY, AND TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE. THE 2026 KEYNOTE LECTURES WILL BE DELIVERED BY TWO INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNIZED LEADERS IN PHOSPHATASE RESEARCH: ANNE BERTOLOTTI, PHD, GROUP LEADER AT THE MRC LABORATORY OF MOLECULAR BIOLOGY (MRC-LMB), AND MICHEL TREMBLAY, PHD, DISTINGUISHED PROFESSOR AT MCGILL UNIVERSITY. THE SPECIFIC AIMS OF THE 2026 FASEB-JAPPR CONFERENCE ARE TO: (1) PRESENT AND DISCUSS THE LATEST ADVANCES IN THE STRUCTURE, REGULATION, AND FUNCTION OF PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES, WITH PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON THEIR ROLES IN CANCER AND OTHER HUMAN DISEASES AND THEIR VALIDATION AS THERAPEUTIC TARGETS; (2) HIGHLIGHT INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGIES, RIGOROUS EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES, AND EMERGING DISCOVERIES THAT INTEGRATE PHOSPHATASE BIOLOGY WITH COMPLEMENTARY SCIENTIFIC DISCIPLINES, FOSTER MULTIDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATION, AND ACCELERATE THERAPEUTIC TRANSLATION; AND (3) STRENGTHEN THE FUTURE BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH WORKFORCE BY SUPPORTING THE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF EARLY CAREER INVESTIGATORS, INCLUDING GRADUATE STUDENTS, POSTDOCTORAL FELLOWS, AND JUNIOR FACULTY, THROUGH A COLLABORATIVE AND SCIENTIFICALLY RIGOROUS ENVIRONMENT THAT PROMOTES MENTORING, NETWORKING, SCIENTIFIC EXCHANGE, AND OPPORTUNITIES TO PRESENT THEIR RESEARCH. THIS R13 PROPOSAL REQUESTS SUPPORT TO FACILITATE THE PARTICIPATION OF EARLY CAREER INVESTIGATORS AS ORAL AND POSTER PRESENTERS, ENABLING PARTICIPANTS FROM A BROAD RANGE OF INSTITUTIONS AND SCIENTIFIC DISCIPLINES TO ENGAGE WITH LEADERS IN THE FIELD, ESTABLISH COLLABORATIONS, AND ADVANCE PHOSPHATASE RESEARCH.

description: SYMPOSIUM ON REDUCING STROKE RISK AND OPTIMIZING BRAIN HEALTH IN WOMEN BY LEVERAGING PREVENTION IN MID-LIFE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT DESPITE LOWER AGE-SPECIFIC RATES OF STROKE IN WOMEN COMPARED TO MEN, STROKE HAS A DISPROPORTIONATE IMPACT ON THE LIVES OF WOMEN. IN ADDITION, MORE WOMEN THAN MEN SUFFER FROM COGNITIVE DECLINE, ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DISORDERS. THIS CONFERENCE, ENTITLED “REDUCING STROKE RISK AND OPTIMIZING BRAIN HEALTH IN WOMEN BY LEVERAGING PREVENTION IN MID-LIFE” WILL BRING TOGETHER A BROAD COALITION OF RESEARCHERS, CLINICIANS, HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, ADVOCATES, AND STROKE SURVIVORS TO DISCUSS CONTEMPORARY ISSUES RELATED TO THE PREVENTION OF STROKE AND PRESERVATION OF BRAIN HEALTH IN WOMEN, WITH A PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON THE MID-LIFE PERIOD. THE CONFERENCE WILL FOCUS ON THREE INTER-RELATED THEMES RELEVANT TO STROKE AND BRAIN HEALTH IN WOMEN: 1) PREVENTING STROKE IN WOMEN BY LEVERAGING INTERVENTIONS APPLIED IN MID-LIFE, 2) OPTIMIZING BRAIN HEALTH OF WOMEN IN LATER LIFE BY DESIGNING INTERVENTIONS IN MID-LIFE, AND 3) CLINICAL CARE TO OPTIMIZE STROKE RECOVERY AND MENTAL HEALTH OUTCOMES IN WOMEN DURING THE TRANSITIONAL CARE PERIOD. THE CONFERENCE WILL EXPAND ON PREVIOUS COLLABORATIONS AND NETWORKING INITIATED BY THE MULTIDISCIPLINARY, AD HOC WORKING GROUP ON STROKE IN WOMEN -- PREVENTION AND OUTCOMES IN WOMEN ENHANCING STROKE SUPPORT (PROWESS). THE CONFERENCE HAS BEEN DESIGNED TO SUPPORT EARLY CAREER INVESTIGATORS WORKING IN THE AREA OF STROKE, BRAIN HEALTH, SEX DIFFERENCES, AND WOMEN, WITH THE GOAL OF ASSISTING THEM TO DEVELOP FOCUSED HYPOTHESIS DRIVEN RESEARCH RELEVANT TO THE MISSION OF NINDS. THE CONFERENCE WILL RESULT IN THE DISSEMINATION OF A SUMMARY MANUSCRIPT AND DEVELOPMENT OF COLLABORATIONS TO ADVANCE FUTURE RESEARCH.

description: NEURONAL EXPERIENCE-REGULATED TRANSCRIPTION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE 2026 FEDERATION OF AMERICAN SOCIETIES OF EXPERIMENTAL BIOLOGY (FASEB) SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH CONFERENCE (SRC) ON NEURONAL EXPERIENCE-REGULATED TRANSCRIPTION WILL BE THE FIRST EVER IN-PERSON MEETING TO CONVENE RESEARCHERS SPECIFICALLY AROUND THE TOPIC OF EXPERIENCE-REGULATED TRANSCRIPTION IN THE BRAIN. OUR GOAL IS TO FACILITATE INFORMATION TRANSFER BETWEEN RESEARCHERS WITH DISTINCT APPROACHES TO EXPERIENCE-DEPENDENT TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATION AND THEREBY ACCELERATE BIOLOGICAL DISCOVERY. TOPICS OF DISCUSSION AT THE MEETING WILL INCLUDE MOLECULAR GENETICS AND GENOMICS OF ACTIVITY-REGULATED GENE TRANSCRIPTION AND TRANSLATION; THE ROLE OF TRANSCRIPTION IN LEARNING, MEMORY, AND SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY; DYSREGULATION OF TRANSCRIPTION IN DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS AND AGING; AND NEW DISCOVERIES AND TECHNOLOGIES TO STUDY EXCITATION-TRANSCRIPTION COUPLING. INVITED SPEAKERS USE A LARGE VARIETY OF CUTTING-EDGE APPROACHES INCLUDING IN VIVO MODELS, HUMAN CELLS, DYNAMIC MOLECULAR IMAGING METHODS, CRISPR-BASED EPIGENOMIC EDITING, COMPARATIVE GENOME SEQUENCE ANALYSIS, ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, AND QUANTITATIVE BIOPHYSICS.  THIS THREE-DAY MEETING WILL BE FILLED WITH RIGOROUS DISCUSSION OF RESEARCH AND WILL PROMOTE INTERACTION BETWEEN PARTICIPANTS AT ALL CAREER STAGES. OUR AGENDA FEATURES KEYNOTE PRESENTATIONS FROM TWO OF THE FOUNDERS OF THIS FIELD, WHO BRING EXCEPTIONAL EXPERIENCE AND KNOWLEDGE TO THE CONVERSATION. TALKS WILL BE SPLIT BETWEEN INVITED ESTABLISHED RESEARCHERS AND JUNIOR FACULTY, POSTDOCS, OR GRADUATE STUDENT EARLY-CAREER RESEARCHERS SELECTED FROM THE SUBMITTED ABSTRACTS. THIS WILL ENSURE A BALANCE BETWEEN DIFFERENT PERSPECTIVES AND APPROACHES TO THE FIELD AND ALLOW US TO FEATURE THE NEWEST AND MOST EXCITING SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERIES. WE WILL HAVE TWO POSTER SESSIONS TO ALLOW PRESENTATION TIME FOR ALL ATTENDEES. A COLLEGIAL ATMOSPHERE WILL BE FOSTERED THROUGH AN ARRIVAL NIGHT SOCIAL EVENT, GROUP MEALS AND COFFEE BREAKS, AND STRUCTURED AFTERNOON NETWORKING SESSIONS.

description: 12TH AQUATIC MODELS OF HUMAN DISEASES CONFERENCE - PROJECT SUMMARY: AQUATIC ANIMAL MODELS ARE ESSENTIAL PLATFORMS FOR BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH AND PROVIDE POWERFUL SYSTEMS TO STUDY HUMAN DISEASE MECHANISMS. THE AQUATIC MODELS FOR HUMAN DISEASE (AQMHD) CONFERENCE IS A ONE-OF-A-KIND MEETING THAT FEATURES A BROAD RANGE OF AQUATIC MODEL ORGANISMS, ALLOWING INVESTIGATORS TO SHOWCASE THE UNIQUE STRENGTHS OF EACH SYSTEM. AS A LONG-STANDING FORUM, AQMHD BRINGS TOGETHER RESEARCHERS ACROSS DEVELOPMENTAL, GENETIC, PHYSIOLOGICAL, AND TOXICOLOGICAL DISCIPLINES AND HAS, OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, FOSTERED COLLABORATIVE PROGRAMS, NEW SCIENTIFIC DIRECTIONS, AND SHARED COMMUNITY STANDARDS. THIS COMMUNITY-DRIVEN EFFORT CONTINUES TO REFINE RESEARCH PRIORITIES FOR BOTH ESTABLISHED AND EMERGING AQUATIC MODEL ORGANISMS. CENTERED ON THE THEME “EMERGING MODELS IN HUMAN HEALTH,” THE 2026 MEETING WILL FOCUS ON ADVANCING THE USE OF AQUATIC MODELS TO ADDRESS FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS IN HUMAN HEALTH AND DISEASE, IN ALIGNMENT WITH NIH PRIORITIES IN TRANSLATIONAL IMPACT, RIGOR, REPRODUCIBILITY, AND CROSS-DISCIPLINARY INTEGRATION. OUR SESSIONS ARE DESIGNED TO HIGHLIGHT ADVANCES IN DISEASE MODELING, HUMANIZED SYSTEMS, FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS, AND COMPARATIVE BIOLOGY, WHILE STRENGTHENING STANDARDS THAT ENHANCE THE LONG-TERM UTILITY OF AQUATIC SYSTEMS. AQMHD 2026 WILL BRING TOGETHER ESTABLISHED INVESTIGATORS, EARLY-STAGE INVESTIGATORS, POSTDOCTORAL FELLOWS, AND GRADUATE STUDENTS, WITH A PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON INCLUDING JUNIOR FACULTY SPEAKERS TO INCREASE VISIBILITY AND ACCESS TO COLLABORATIVE NETWORKS AND SHARED RESOURCES. OUR WORKSHOP LEADERS INCLUDE INDUSTRY REPRESENTATIVES WHO WILL LEAD DISCUSSIONS ON COMPUTATIONAL DRUG DISCOVERY, ADVANCED ANIMAL MODELS, AND AUTOMATED SCREENING APPROACHES, HELPING TO BRIDGE BASIC BIOLOGY DISCOVERIES WITH HUMAN HEALTH APPLICATIONS. THE MEETING WILL GENERATE SEVERAL TANGIBLE OUTCOMES, INCLUDING PUBLICATION OF A MEETING REPORT TO DISSEMINATE KEY FINDINGS AND DISCUSSIONS, A DEDICATED COLLECTION OF ARTICLES IN BIOLOGY OPEN FEATURING RESEARCH PRESENTED AT THE CONFERENCE, A BOOK ON AQUATIC MODELS TO CONSOLIDATE ADVANCES IN THE FIELD, AND A WHITE PAPER, TO BE SHARED WITH NIH PROGRAM OFFICERS, DERIVED FROM THE WORKSHOP DISCUSSIONS EMPHASIZING THE MOST URGENT PRIORITIES. NEW PROGRAMMATIC ELEMENTS WILL ENHANCE THE IMPACT OF THE MEETING, INCLUDING A COMMUNITY DISCUSSION ON INTEGRATING AQUATIC MODELS WITH HUMANIZED SYSTEMS SUCH AS ORGANOIDS AND CELL CULTURE IN ALIGNMENT WITH NIH PRIORITIES IN NEW APPROACH METHODOLOGIES, A WORKSHOP ON THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SCIENTIFIC PUBLISHING, COMMUNICATION, AND RESEARCH INTEGRITY, A FOCUSED SESSION ON NUTRITION AND CHRONIC DISEASE, AND A PROMINENT POSTER SESSION TO PROMOTE ENGAGEMENT BETWEEN TRAINEES AND INVESTIGATORS. RIGOR AND REPRODUCIBILITY WILL BE EMPHASIZED THROUGHOUT THE PROGRAM, WITH SPEAKERS EXPECTED TO ADDRESS EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN, VALIDATION, AND REPRODUCIBILITY IN BOTH PRESENTATIONS AND WRITTEN CONTRIBUTIONS. THE AQMHD 2026 WILL PROMOTE SUBSTANTIVE SCIENTIFIC EXCHANGE, UNIFY COMMUNITY STANDARDS, AND ENSURE THE CONTINUED GROWTH AND RELEVANCE OF AQUATIC MODELS IN NIH-FUNDED BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DETERMINING THE ROLE OF THE MITOCHONDRIAL PERMEABILITY TRANSITION PORE ON AGING - PROJECT SUMMARY MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION IS A HALLMARK OF AGING AND AGE-RELATED DISEASES, INCLUDING HEART ATTACK, STROKE, AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS. SEVERE MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION OFTEN RESULTS FROM THE OPENING OF THE MITOCHONDRIAL PERMEABILITY TRANSITION PORE (MPTP), A PATHOLOGICAL CHANNEL IN THE INNER MITOCHONDRIAL MEMBRANE TRIGGERED BY EXCESSIVE CYTOSOLIC CA2⁺ AND HIGH REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES (ROS) LEVELS. DURING CONDITIONS SUCH AS ISCHEMIA/REPERFUSION (I/R) INJURY, MITOCHONDRIA IMPORT CA2⁺ INTO THE MATRIX TO BUFFER CYTOSOLIC LEVELS. THIS ACCUMULATION CAN CAUSE MITOCHONDRIAL SWELLING AND MPTP OPENING, ALLOWING CA2⁺ RELEASE BACK INTO THE CYTOSOL. PROLONGED MPTP ACTIVATION LEADS TO OUTER MEMBRANE RUPTURE, FURTHER CA2⁺ RELEASE, AND ULTIMATELY, CELL DEATH. WHILE EXTENSIVELY STUDIED IN I/R-RELATED DISEASES, THE ROLE OF THE MPTP IN NORMAL AGING REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD. TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP, WE DEVELOPED A CAENORHABDITIS ELEGANS MODEL TO STUDY MPTP FUNCTION IN AGING. OUR FINDINGS REVEAL THAT MPTP ACTIVATION ACCELERATES AGING, WHILE ITS INHIBITION EXTENDS LIFESPAN, DEMONSTRATING ITS DIRECT ROLE IN LONGEVITY REGULATION (ANGELI ET AL., 2021, ELIFE). WITH ITS SHORT LIFESPAN, GENETIC TRACTABILITY, AND CONSERVED MITOCHONDRIAL PROCESSES, C. ELEGANS OFFERS A POWERFUL MODEL FOR UNCOVERING HOW THE MPTP INFLUENCES AGING. THE CELLULAR CA2⁺ SIGNALING PATHWAYS THAT REGULATE MPTP OPENING REMAIN LARGELY UNKNOWN. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGEST THAT CA2⁺ RELEASED FROM THE ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM (ER)—THE LARGEST INTRACELLULAR CA2⁺ RESERVOIR—ACTIVATES CALMODULIN, A KEY MEDIATOR OF CA2⁺-DEPENDENT SIGNALING, POSSIBLY VIA INTERACTIONS WITH KINASES, PHOSPHATASES, AND OTHER CALMODULIN-BINDING PROTEINS (CBPS). WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT AN ER-TO-CYTOPLASM CA2⁺ SIGNALING CASCADE TRIGGERS MPTP ACTIVATION, DRIVING ORGANISMAL AGING. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER ITR-1, THE ER RECEPTOR RESPONSIBLE FOR CA2⁺ RELEASE, ALONG WITH CALMODULIN (CMD-1) AND CBPS, ARE REQUIRED FOR MPTP ACTIVATION AND MPTP-DEPENDENT AGING. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL LEVERAGE THE ADVANTAGES OF C. ELEGANS TO IDENTIFY SPECIFIC TISSUES WITH A PREDOMINANT INFLUENCE ON THIS PROCESS. OUR PRELIMINARY FINDINGS INDICATE ROBUST MPTP ACTIVATION IN THE INTESTINES, WHICH SERVE MULTIPLE FUNCTIONS BEYOND DIGESTION, INCLUDING DETOXIFICATION, IMMUNITY, AND FAT METABOLISM. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS WHETHER INTESTINAL MPTP ACTIVATION IS SUFFICIENT TO DRIVE ORGANISMAL AGING. THESE STUDIES WILL PROVIDE NOVEL INSIGHTS INTO THE ROLE OF THE MPTP IN AGING, WITH BROAD IMPLICATIONS FOR HUMAN HEALTH.

description: A SYSTEMS BIOLOGY APPROACH TO UNDERSTAND THE ROLE OF KLOTHO AND ESTROGEN IN COMBATING NEURODEGENERATION - PROJECT SUMMARY TITLE: A SYSTEMS BIOLOGY APPROACH TO UNDERSTAND THE ROLE OF KLOTHO AND ESTROGEN IN COMBATING NEURODEGEN- ERATION ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS A MULTIFACTORIAL NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY IMMUNE DYSREGULATION, METABOLIC DYSFUNCTION, AND PROGRESSIVE NEURONAL LOSS. DESPITE DECADES OF RESEARCH FOCUSED ON AMYLOID-BETA PATHOLOGY, LIMITED THERAPEUTIC SUCCESS HAS PROMPTED A SHIFT TOWARD UNDERSTANDING ALTERNATIVE MECHANISMS THAT DRIVE DISEASE PROGRESSION. WOMEN ARE DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTED BY AD, PARTICULARLY IN THE PRESENCE OF THE APOE4 GENOTYPE, AND EVIDENCE INCREASINGLY IMPLICATES HORMONAL DECLINE AND IMMUNE-METABOLIC DYSFUNCTION IN THIS SEX-SPECIFIC VULNERABILITY. THIS PROPOSAL ADOPTS A SYSTEMS BIOLOGY FRAMEWORK TO INVESTIGATE THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN ESTROGEN SIGNALING, KLOTHO EXPRESSION, AND APOE GENOTYPE IN REGULATING MICROGLIAL ACTIVITY, METABOLISM, AND BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER (BBB) INTEGRITY. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT HORMONAL AND GENETIC MODULATION OF IMMUNE AND METABOLIC PATH- WAYS CREATES A WINDOW OF VULNERABILITY TO NEURODEGENERATION THAT CAN BE PREDICTED AND MODULATES. USING BOTH ORDINARY DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS (ODE) AND AGENT-BASED MODELS (ABM), THIS PROJECT WILL SIMULATE MOLECULAR SIGNALING CASCADES, CELLULAR METABOLIC REPROGRAMMING, AND SPATIAL MICROENVIRONMENT DYNAMICS IN THE HIPPOCAM- PUS. THREE SPECIFIC AIMS WILL GUIDE THIS RESEARCH: 1. EXTEND AN ODE MODEL OF NF-ΚB SIGNALING TO INCORPORATE ESTROGEN AND KLOTHO, ELUCIDATING THEIR REGULATORY  ROLES IN INFLAMMATION. 2. DEVELOP A MULTISCALE ODE MODEL TO EXPLORE HOW APOE4 AND ESTROGEN CO-REGULATE MICROGLIAL DYSFUNCTION  AND BBB BREAKDOWN. 3. INTEGRATE THESE INSIGHTS INTO A SPATIALLY EXPLICIT AGENT-BASED MODEL OF THE HIPPOCAMPUS, CAPTURING HOW  ESTROGEN AND KLOTHO MODULATE IMMUNE-CELL BEHAVIOR AND BARRIER PERMEABILITY OVER TIME. IN ADDITION TO ADVANCING UNDERSTANDING OF SEX- AND GENOTYPE-SPECIFIC AD MECHANISMS, THIS PROJECT WILL TRAIN UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN INTERDISCIPLINARY MODELING, CODING, AND BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH. STUDENTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN ALL PHASES OF THE PROJECT, INCLUDING MODEL CONSTRUCTION, DATA INTEGRATION, SIMULATION, AND DISSEMINATION OF FINDINGS AT CONFERENCES AND IN PEER-REVIEWED PUBLICATIONS. THE PROPOSED WORK HAS THE POTENTIAL TO UNCOVER NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS AND TIMING STRATEGIES, WHILE SIMULTANE- OUSLY SUPPORTING THE RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE AND EDUCATIONAL MISSION OF A PRIMARILY UNDERGRADUATE INSTITUTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ASSESSING NEEDS, CHALLENGES, HELP-SEEKING, OUTREACH, AND RESILIENCE IN MALE DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS: THE ANCHOR STUDY - PROJECT SUMMARY MEN COMPRISE OVER 30% OF THE DEMENTIA CAREGIVER POPULATION YET REMAIN OVERLOOKED IN DEMENTIA CAREGIVING INTERVENTION RESEARCH AND UNDERUTILIZE DEMENTIA CARE SERVICE. HOWEVER, AS OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES DEMONSTRATE, MALE DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS SHOW A CLEAR INTEREST IN RECEIVING SUPPORTIVE SERVICES AND INTERVENTION TAILORED TO THEIR NEEDS, SUGGESTING THAT BARRIERS RATHER THAN LACK OF INTEREST MAY EXPLAIN THEIR UNDERUTILIZATION. THERE IS A NEED FOR RESPONSIVE APPROACHES TO ENGAGE MALE DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS IN SERVICES. THUS, IT IS IMPERATIVE TO IDENTIFY STRESSORS AND RESOURCES THAT MAY IMPACT THEIR HELP-SEEKING AND SERVICE UTILIZATION, AND TO IMPLEMENT RESPONSIVE RECRUITMENT MESSAGING STRATEGIES TO INCREASE REPRESENTATION OF MALE CAREGIVERS IN BOTH DEMENTIA CAREGIVER SERVICES AND INTERVENTION STUDIES. BUILDING ON FINDINGS AND RIGOROUS METHODS FROM OUR PREVIOUS STUDIES AND LOCAL PARTNERSHIPS OVER THE PAST TEN YEARS, WE PROPOSE TO UTILIZE BOTH NATIONAL AND COMMUNITY-BASED DATA TO IDENTIFY FACTORS THAT SHAPE MALE DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS' HELP-SEEKING, SERVICE UTILIZATION, AND CAREGIVER BURDEN AS WELL AS DEVELOP, REFINE, AND DISSEMINATE EFFECTIVE MESSAGING STRATEGIES FOR ENHANCING RECRUITMENT. FIRST, GUIDED BY THE CAREGIVER STRESS PROCESS MODEL, WE WILL ANALYZE POOLED DATA ON DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS FROM THE NATIONAL SURVEY OF CAREGIVERS (NSOC, 2021, 2022, 2023) TO IDENTIFY STRESSORS AND RESOURCES ASSOCIATED WITH HELP-SEEKING, SERVICE UTILIZATION, AND CAREGIVER BURDEN COMPARING MALE AND FEMALE DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS. NEXT, USING COMMUNITY-BASED PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH (CBPR) APPROACHES, WE WILL CONDUCT FOUR FOCUS GROUPS WITH COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS (N=40) ON STRESSORS AND RESOURCES THAT IMPACT HELPSEEKING AND SERVICE UTILIZATION FOR MALE DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS. THEN, THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL WORK WITH A COMMUNITY ADVISORY BOARD TO CREATE AND REFINE EFFECTIVE MESSAGING STRATEGIES FOR ENGAGING MALE DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS. THE PROJECT'S TWO SPECIFIC AIMS ARE AS FOLLOWS: AIM 1. IDENTIFY STRESSORS AND RESOURCES ASSOCIATED WITH HELP-SEEKING, SERVICE UTILIZATION, AND CAREGIVER BURDEN FOR MALE AND FEMALE DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS. THE USE OF SECONDARY DATA WILL ALLOW FOR THE IDENTIFICATION OF PATTERNS ACROSS A LARGE, NATIONAL SAMPLE AND COMPARE SEX DIFFERENCES IN CAREGIVING EXPERIENCES. AIM 2. INVESTIGATE STAKEHOLDER PERSPECTIVES ON STRESSORS AND RESOURCES THAT INFLUENCES HELP-SEEKING AND SERVICE UTILIZATION AND REFINE MESSAGING STRATEGIES FOR RECRUITMENT OF MALE DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS INTO CAREGIVING SERVICES AND INTERVENTION STUDIES. THIS PROJECT WILL CONTRIBUTE TO SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE REGARDING EFFECTIVE RECRUITMENT TECHNIQUES AND BARRIERS TO ACCESSING CARE SERVICES FOR MALE DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS. FURTHER, THIS PROPOSAL WILL ENHANCE THE INFRASTRUCTURE AT THE KENT SCHOOL OF SOCIAL WORK AND FAMILY SCIENCE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF LOUISVILLE (UOFL) BY PROVIDING RESEARCH EXPERIENCE TO UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS WHO OTHERWISE MIGHT NOT HAVE EXPOSURE TO NIH-FUNDED RESEARCH PROJECTS. THIS R15 PROJECT WILL ALLOW UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS TO EXPERIENCE A BROAD SPECTRUM OF RESEARCH TECHNIQUES AND ACQUIRE SKILLS THAT CAN BE CARRIED OVER TO FUTURE RESEARCH CAREERS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REGULATION OF TRPM7 CHANNEL KINASE UNDER HYPO AND HYPERMAGNESEMIC CONDITIONS. - PROJECT SUMMARY T LYMPHOCYTE ACTIVATION AND PROLIFERATION IS ESSENTIAL FOR THE HUMAN ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSE. CALCIUM AND MAGNESIUM SIGNALING PATHWAYS PLAY A CRUCIAL ROLE IN THIS PROCESS, AND THEIR DEFECTS RESULT IN VARIOUS FORMS OF IMMUNODEFICIENCY AND MUSCLE DISORDERS. ~25% OF THE U.S. POPULATION IS MAGNESIUM DEFICIENT, WHICH COMPROMISES IMMUNE RESPONSE AMONG OTHER PATHWAYS. THUS, IT IS URGENT TO FULLY UNDERSTAND THESE UNDERSTUDIED PATHWAYS AND THEIR IMPACT ON IMMUNE FUNCTION. HYPERMAGNESEMIA, OFTEN ACCOMPANIES KIDNEY INJURY AND DISEASE. SEVERAL PLAYERS INVOLVED IN CALCIUM AND MAGNESIUM TRANSPORT HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED AT THE MOLECULAR LEVEL. ONE OF THEM, TRPM7, A PROTEIN WITH DUAL ION CHANNEL AND SERINE/THREONINE KINASE FUNCTION, IS PERMEABLE TO BOTH CALCIUM AND MAGNESIUM. IT IS REGULATED BY INTRACELLULAR IONIZED MAGNESIUM. TRPM7 IS HIGHLY EXPRESSED IN IMMUNE CELLS AND IS REQUIRED FOR T-CELL DEVELOPMENT AND ACTIVATION OF MACROPHAGES. BECAUSE OF THE CHANNEL- ENZYME DUALITY OF TRPM7, OVEREXPRESSION OR KNOCKDOWN OF THE FULL GENE DO NOT ADDRESS WHETHER ION FLUX OR PHOSPHOTRANSFERASE ACTIVITY UNDERLIES OBSERVED PHENOTYPES. GLOBAL KNOCKOUT OF TRPM7 GENE IN MICE RESULTS IN EMBRYONIC LETHALITY. IN ORDER TO EXAMINE TRPM7 ION TRANSPORT AND KINASE FUNCTIONS SEPARATELY, WE HAVE GENERATED A NOVEL HETEROZYGOUS MOUSE MODEL, STEMMING FROM OUR RECENT BIOPHYSICAL STUDIES OF MAGNESIUM AND PH SENSITIVITY. UNDER NORMAL OR HYPERMAGNESEMIC CONDITIONS, THE MAJORITY OF TRPM7 CHANNELS ARE INHIBITED BY CYTOPLASMIC MAGNESIUM, WHEREAS THE KINASE IS CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVE. IN THE NEW MUTANT MOUSE, A SINGLE AMINO ACID SUBSTITUTION IN TRPM7 REDUCED THE CHANNEL’S MAGNESIUM SENSITIVITY, MAKING THE CHANNELS CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVE. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE AIM TO INVESTIGATE THE CONTRIBUTION OF TRPM7 CHANNEL ACTIVITY TO T-CELL AND MACROPHAGE FUNCTION UNDER NORMAL, HYPO AND HYPERMAGNESEMIC CONDITIONS. AS EXTRACELLULAR MAGNESIUM LEVELS STRONGLY INFLUENCE IMMUNE CELLS, WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER TRPM7 CHANNEL SERVES AS THE MAIN MAGNESIUM ENTRY PATHWAY, OR THE KINASE IS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CELLULAR PHENOTYPE. WE PROPOSE THESE SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1: GENERATE AND CHARACTERIZE A TRPM7 CHANNEL MUTANT MOUSE MODEL TO ELUCIDATE TRPM7 CHANNEL/KINASE SIGNALING IN MACROPHAGES AND LYMPHOCYTES, WHICH ARE CRITICAL IMMUNE RESPONDERS. AIM 2: INVESTIGATE TRPM7 CHANNEL AND KINASE PROPERTIES IN CONDITIONS OF MG2+ DEFICIENCY AND EXCESS. AIM 3: DEFINE MG2+ AND CYTOTOXIC DIVALENT METAL CATION ENTRY, WHICH CAN IMPACT THE IMMUNE RESPONSE. COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS ARE EXPECTED TO CHARACTERIZE THE IMPORT OF MAGNESIUM BALANCE/SUFFICIENCY IN SEVERAL PATHWAYS VITAL TO HUMAN HEALTH, INCLUDING IMMUNE FUNCTION.

description: BIOMIMETIC TRIPHASIC INTERFERENCE SCREWS FOR BONE-LIGAMENT/TENDON REGENERATION: A SYNERGISTIC APPROACH COMBINING DESIGN, MANUFACTURING, AND BIOLOGICAL VALIDATION - SUMMARY STATEMENT: THIS R15 PROPOSAL AIMS TO DEVELOP NEXT-GENERATION INTERFERENCE SCREWS WITH BIOMIMETIC TISSUE-SPECIFIC ARCHITECTURES TO IMPROVE BONE-LIGAMENT/TENDON RECONSTRUCTION OUTCOMES. THE CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE STEMS FROM THE HIGH FAILURE RATES (20-25%) OF CURRENT ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT (ACL) RECONSTRUCTIONS WITHIN 7-10 YEARS, WITH NEARLY HALF REQUIRING SECOND REVISION SURGERY. THE PROJECT'S INNOVATION LIES IN CREATING THE FIRST-EVER TRIPHASIC INTERFERENCE SCREWS THAT ACTIVELY FACILITATE SIMULTANEOUS BONE AND LIGAMENT/TENDON REGENERATION THROUGH TISSUE-MIMETIC GRADIENT STRUCTURES AND ZONE-SPECIFIC BIOCHEMICAL MODIFICATIONS.   THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVES WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) DESIGN AND MANUFACTURE TRIPHASIC MATRICES WITH BONE-MIMETIC AND LIGAMENT-MIMETIC ARCHITECTURES USING ADVANCED CERAMIC/POLYMER 3D PRINTING, (2) INVESTIGATE ZONE-SPECIFIC BIMETALLIC ION MODIFICATION AND TISSUE REGENERATION CAPABILITIES THROUGH IN VITRO STUDIES, AND (3) DEVELOP AND VALIDATE OPTIMIZED INTERFERENCE SCREWS THROUGH COMPUTATIONAL MODELING AND MECHANICAL TESTING.   THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE RESEARCH TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR BIOMEDICAL AND MECHANICAL ENGINEERING UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS. AT LEAST FOUR UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS PER YEAR WILL GAIN HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE IN COMPUTER-AIDED DESIGN, ADVANCED MANUFACTURING, CELL CULTURE TECHNIQUES, AND BIOMECHANICAL TESTING. THE RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT WILL FOSTER STUDENT DEVELOPMENT THROUGH MENTORED EXPERIENCES IN 3D PRINTING, MATERIALS CHARACTERIZATION, BIO DESIGN APPARATUS SETUP AND COMPUTATIONAL ANALYSIS AND BIOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL HIGH SCHOOLS AND COMMUNITY COLLEGES TO PROVIDE SUMMER RESEARCH EXPERIENCES. ALL RESEARCH TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES SUPPORTED BY THIS AWARD WILL BE OPEN TO INTERESTED STUDENTS WITHOUT REGARD TO RACE, ETHNICITY, OR SEX, WITH PARTICIPANTS SELECTED ON THE BASIS OF DEMONSTRATED INTEREST IN ENGINEERING, ACADEMIC PREPARATION, AND READINESS TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE RESEARCH.   THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE: (1) NOVEL BIOMIMETIC INTERFERENCE SCREWS WITH VALIDATED TISSUE REGENERATION CAPABILITIES, (2) FUNDAMENTAL UNDERSTANDING OF HOW STRUCTURAL AND BIOCHEMICAL GRADIENTS INFLUENCE BONE-LIGAMENT HEALING, AND (3) DEVELOPMENT OF A SKILLED WORKFORCE IN BIOMEDICAL ENGINEERING THROUGH HANDS-ON RESEARCH TRAINING.

description: WHEN PLASTIC MEETS FLOW: MECHANOBIOLOGICAL CONSEQUENCES OF MICROPLASTIC EXPOSURE ON THE ENDOTHELIUM - PROJECT SUMMARY MICROPLASTIC CONTAMINATION REPRESENTS AN EMERGING ENVIRONMENTAL CARDIOVASCULAR RISK FACTOR, WITH PATIENTS HARBORING DETECTABLE MICROPLASTICS IN ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUES EXHIBITING AN INCREASED RISK OF CARDIOVASCULAR COMPLICATIONS SUCH AS MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION OR STROKE, YET THE MECHANISTIC PATHWAYS LINKING MICROPLASTIC EXPOSURE TO CARDIOVASCULAR PATHOPHYSIOLOGY REMAIN UNDEFINED. THE VASCULAR ENDOTHELIUM FUNCTIONS AS THE PRIMARY INTERFACE FOR MICROPLASTIC-CARDIOVASCULAR INTERACTIONS AND SERVES AS A SOPHISTICATED MECHANOSENSOR MAINTAINING VASCULAR HOMEOSTASIS THROUGH FLOW-MEDIATED RESPONSES, BUT CURRENT RESEARCH HAS FOCUSED ON BASIC CYTOTOXICITY USING STATIC CULTURE CONDITIONS THAT FAIL TO RECAPITULATE THE DYNAMIC MECHANICAL ENVIRONMENT OF THE CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM. THIS INVESTIGATION ESTABLISHES THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE CHARACTERIZATION OF MICROPLASTIC EFFECTS ON ENDOTHELIAL MECHANOBIOLOGY UNDER PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT FLOW CONDITIONS THROUGH THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1 INVESTIGATES HOW MICROPLASTIC EXPOSURE IMPAIRS ENDOTHELIAL CELL MECHANICAL INTEGRITY AND CELL-MATRIX ADHESION USING TRACTION FORCE MICROSCOPY AND CELL ADHESION ASSAYS; AIM 2 CHARACTERIZES DISRUPTION OF SHEAR STRESS-ACTIVATED MECHANOTRANSDUCTION SIGNALING PATHWAYS THROUGH IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE, WESTERN BLOT ANALYSIS, AND GENE EXPRESSION STUDIES UNDER CONTROLLED FLOW; AND AIM 3 EVALUATES ENDOTHELIAL BARRIER DYSFUNCTION AND TESTS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS USING CLINICALLY RELEVANT ANTIOXIDANTS AND ANTI-INFLAMMATORY COMPOUNDS. THE RESEARCH EMPLOYS HUMAN AORTIC AND UMBILICAL VEIN ENDOTHELIAL CELLS EXPOSED TO ENVIRONMENTALLY RELEVANT CONCENTRATIONS OF POLYSTYRENE AND POLYETHYLENE MICROPLASTICS, UTILIZING INNOVATIVE METHODOLOGY INCLUDING LAMINAR AND DISTURBED FLOW CHAMBERS, TRACTION FORCE MICROSCOPY, AND COMPREHENSIVE BARRIER FUNCTION ANALYSIS. THIS PARADIGM- SHIFTING INVESTIGATION WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION FOR MICROPLASTIC CARDIOVASCULAR RISK ASSESSMENT GUIDELINES, GENERATE PRELIMINARY DATA THAT COULD COMPLIMENT FUTURE CLINICAL STUDIES, AND TRAIN UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH TECHNIQUES COMBINING ENVIRONMENTAL TOXICOLOGY WITH CARDIOVASCULAR MECHANOBIOLOGY, PREPARING THEM TO ADDRESS COMPLEX GLOBAL HEALTH CHALLENGES WHILE DEVELOPING EXPERTISE IN CELL CULTURE, QUANTITATIVE MICROSCOPY, MOLECULAR BIOLOGY, AND DATA ANALYSIS ESSENTIAL FOR CAREERS IN BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH.
