description: CATARACT RISK AND OCCUPATIONAL EXPOSURES IN DENMARK - ABSTRACT THE AIM OF THIS PROJECT IS TO BUILD ONE OF THE FIRST LARGE-SCALE STUDIES FOCUSING ON OCCUPATIONAL CHEMICAL AND NON-CHEMICAL EXPOSURES IN RELATION TO THE RISK OF CATARACT. CATARACT WILL BE EXAMINED IN RELATION TO SPECIFIC BUT UNDERSTUDIED EXPOSURES SUGGESTED BY PREVIOUS LITERATURE. TO ADDRESS THE STUDY AIMS, THE PROJECT WILL EXTRACT DATA FROM ESTABLISHED REGISTERS IN DENMARK, WHILE USING VALIDATED JOB EXPOSURE MATRICES (JEMS) SPECIFIC TO THE DANISH WORK ENVIRONMENT TO ASSESS OCCUPATIONAL EXPOSURES. THE BURDEN OF CATARACT IS SUBSTANTIAL, YET OCCUPATIONAL-RELATED EXPOSURES ARE UNDERSTUDIED IN CATARACT OUTCOMES, MAKING THIS A NOVEL STUDY. IMPROVING UNDERSTANDING OF THESE EXPOSURES AND THEIR IMPACT ON CATARACT WILL IMPROVE PREVENTION EFFORTS, ADVANCE THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENTS, AND INFORM PUBLIC POLICY ON WORKSITE SAFETY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: FUNCTIONAL CHARACTERIZATION OF  NOVEL PHAGE SATELLITES IN MYCOBACTERIA - PROJECT SUMMARY PHAGE SATELLITES ARE MOBILE GENETIC ELEMENTS THAT DEPEND ON HELPER PHAGE FOR REPLICATION AND ASSEMBLY. THEY EXIST AS PLASMIDS, INTEGRATED CHROMOSOMAL ELEMENTS, OR INDEPENDENT INFECTIOUS PARTICLES. LACKING ESSENTIAL GENES, THEY PARASITIZE HELPER PHAGE TO COMPLETE THEIR LIFE CYCLES, CREATING DYNAMIC INTERACTIONS AMONG HOST BACTERIA, HELPER PHAGES, AND SATELLITES. PHAGE SATELLITES CAN BENEFIT THEIR BACTERIAL HOSTS BY CONFERRING IMMUNITY TO NON-HELPER PHAGES, ENHANCING VIRULENCE, AND DISRUPTING HELPER PHAGE REPRODUCTION. ONCE OVERLOOKED AS DEGRADED PHAGE, PHAGE SATELLITES ARE NOW RECOGNIZED AS MAJOR DRIVERS OF VIRUS–VIRUS INTERACTIONS, HORIZONTAL GENE TRANSFER, MICROBIAL EVOLUTION, AND BACTERIAL POPULATION DYNAMICS. THEY ALSO OFFER PROMISING APPLICATIONS IN BIOTECHNOLOGY AND PHAGE THERAPY, HOWEVER THE VAST MAJORITY OF PHAGE SATELLITES REMAIN UNEXPLORED. ONLY A SINGLE INSTANCE OF A PHAGE SATELLITE HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED IN THE ENTIRE ACTINOBACTERIA PHYLUM, AND NONE HAVE BEEN REPORTED IN MYCOBACTERIA UNTIL THE DISCOVERY OF EXTRACELLULAR PROPHAGE-INDUCING PARTICLES (EPIPS) BY OUR LABORATORY—THE FIRST PHAGE SATELLITES DISCOVERED TO INFECT THE MYCOBACTERIUM GENUS. EPIPS CONSISTENTLY TRIGGER EXCISION AND ACTIVATION OF THE HELPER PROPHAGE HERBERTWM FROM MYCOBACTERIUM AICHIENSE, ESTABLISHING A NOVEL SATELLITE–HELPER SYSTEM AND THE FIRST REPORTED IN THE MYCOBACTERIAL GENUS. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO ADVANCE FUNDAMENTAL UNDERSTANDING OF MYCOBACTERIUM PHAGE SATELLITE BIOLOGY BY DELINEATING PATTERNS OF GENE EXPRESSION DURING INFECTION, DETERMINING SATELLITE GENE FUNCTIONS THROUGH OVEREXPRESSION AND TARGETED KNOCKOUTS, AND CHARACTERIZING THEIR HOST RANGE AND PREVALENCE IN NATURAL ENVIRONMENTS THROUGH THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 WILL QUANTIFY TEMPORAL GENE EXPRESSION DYNAMICS OF THE HOST, HELPER PHAGE, AND SATELLITE DURING INFECTION BY PERFORMING RNA SEQUENCING AND MASS SPECTROMETRY-BASED PROTEOMICS AT MULTIPLE TIME POINTS FOLLOWING INFECTION WITH THE SATELLITE. AIM 2 WILL ELUCIDATE MOLECULAR FUNCTIONS OF EPIP-ENCODED GENES THROUGH INDUCIBLE OVEREXPRESSION, TARGETED GENE KNOCKOUTS, AND INTEGRATIVE STRUCTURAL BIOINFORMATICS TO PREDICT AND TEST MECHANISTIC ROLES IN REPLICATION, EXCISION, AND HELPER ACTIVATION. AIM 3 WILL DELINEATE THE HOST RANGE OF EPIPS BY TESTING HOST SPECIFICITY, CROSS-SPECIES MOBILIZATION, AND PREVALENCE ACROSS MYCOBACTERIUM AND RELATED ACTINOBACTERIA USING INFECTION ASSAYS, QPCR-BASED EXCISION TRACKING, AND COMPUTATIONAL GENOME MINING WITH SATELLITE DISCOVERY SOFTWARE DEVELOPED IN OUR LABORATORY. THIS PROJECT WILL ENHANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES GOVERNING SATELLITE–HELPER INTERACTIONS IN ACTINOBACTERIA AND MOLECULAR DETERMINANTS OF VIRAL PARASITISM. THE RESULTING INSIGHTS WILL EXPAND MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF PHAGE REGULATION, INFORM EVOLUTIONARY MODELS OF HORIZONTAL GENE TRANSFER, AND PROVIDE A FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE APPLICATIONS IN BIOTECHNOLOGY, CONTROLLING BACTERIAL INFECTIONS, AND PHAGE THERAPY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXPLORING THE IMPACT OF ENTREPRENEURSHIP ON EMOTIONAL WELL-BEING AND FINANCIAL STRESS IN INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME AND THEIR CAREGIVERS - ABSTRACT THIS PROJECT INVESTIGATES HOW INCLUSIVE FAMILY ENTREPRENEURSHIP MAY REDUCE FINANCIAL STRESS AND ENHANCE EMOTIONAL WELL-BEING IN ADULTS WITH DOWN SYNDROME (DS) AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. ADULTS WITH DS EXPERIENCE HIGH UNEMPLOYMENT AND LIMITED ACCESS TO MEANINGFUL WORK. SOME FAMILIES TURN TO ENTREPRENEURSHIP, STARTING SMALL BUSINESSES THAT INCLUDE THEIR CHILD WITH DS, AS A WAY TO CREATE CUSTOMIZED, INCLUSIVE JOBS. WHILE THIS PRACTICE IS GROWING, WE KNOW LITTLE ABOUT ITS TRUE IMPACT ON WELL-BEING AND ECONOMIC BURDEN. WE WILL RECRUIT 90 DYADS, EACH MADE UP OF AN ADULT WITH DS AND THEIR PRIMARY CAREGIVER. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE DIVIDED INTO THREE GROUPS BASED ON THE EMPLOYMENT STATUS OF THE INDIVIDUAL WITH DS: (1) UNEMPLOYED, (2) EMPLOYED IN A NON-ENTREPRENEURIAL JOB, AND (3) ENGAGED IN A BUSINESS WITH THEIR CAREGIVER. QUANTITATIVE DATA WILL MEASURE AND COMPARE EMOTIONAL WELL-BEING, FINANCIAL STRESS, AND COPING STRATEGIES ACROSS THE THREE GROUPS. WE WILL USE REGRESSION MODELS TO TEST WHETHER STRESS AND COPING PREDICT EMOTIONAL WELL-BEING AND WHETHER ENTREPRENEURSHIP MAY BUFFER STRESS ACROSS GROUPS. IN ADDITION, WE WILL CONDUCT FOCUS GROUPS WITH ENTREPRENEURIAL FAMILIES TO LEARN MORE ABOUT HOW THEY VIEW THEIR BUSINESS, WHAT CHALLENGES THEY FACE, AND WHAT BENEFITS THEY EXPERIENCE. THIS MIXED-METHOD APPROACH WILL ALLOW US TO DEVELOP A MORE COMPLETE PICTURE OF HOW ENTREPRENEURSHIP FUNCTIONS AS A FINANCIAL AND EMOTIONAL SUPPORT STRATEGY FOR FAMILIES OF INDIVIDUALS WITH DS. THIS PROJECT IS HOSTED AT AUBURN UNIVERSITY AT MONTGOMERY, A MINORITY-SERVING INSTITUTION, AND WILL DIRECTLY INVOLVE AT LEAST EIGHT PAID UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS EACH YEAR. THESE STUDENTS WILL RECEIVE HANDS-ON TRAINING IN RESEARCH DESIGN, DATA COLLECTION, ANALYSIS, AND SCIENTIFIC WRITING. THEY WILL ALSO CO-AUTHOR PAPERS AND PRESENT FINDINGS, HELPING TO BUILD THE UNIVERSITY’S RESEARCH CULTURE AND PREPARE STUDENTS FOR UNDERGRADUATE STUDY OR CAREERS IN BIOMEDICAL AND BEHAVIORAL RESEARCH. THE FINDINGS WILL INFORM INCLUSIVE EMPLOYMENT POLICIES AND HELP SHAPE FUTURE SUPPORT SYSTEMS FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH DS AND THEIR FAMILIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MOBILE MEDIA USE AND PRESCHOOLERS’ PEER INTERACTION SKILLS - PROJECT SUMMARY. SOCIAL SKILLS OF PRESCHOOL-AGED CHILDREN (3 TO 5 YEARS OLD) HAVE SHOWN A NOTABLE DECLINE OVER THE LAST DECADE, RESULTING IN INCREASED SOCIAL ANXIETY AND DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, AND WEAKER RELATIONSHIPS. LIKELY CONTRIBUTING TO THIS DECLINE IS THE INCREASE IN MOBILE MEDIA USE (I.E., TABLETS AND SMARTPHONES), WHICH HAS RISEN 180% SINCE THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. THESE RATES RAISE CONCERN, AS TIME SPENT ON MOBILE MEDIA DISPLACES CRITICAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR SOCIAL INTERACTION WITH PARENTS, CAREGIVERS, AND PEERS – ACTIVITIES KNOWN TO FOSTER SOCIAL SKILL DEVELOPMENT. THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSED STUDY IS TO EXAMINE HOW PRESCHOOLERS’ MOBILE MEDIA USE RELATES TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF PEER INTERACTION SKILLS. ADDITIONALLY, IT WILL IDENTIFY WHETHER THESE ASSOCIATIONS VARY IN RELATION TO THE TYPE OF CONTENT CHILDREN ENGAGE WITH, AND WHETHER PARENTS’ USE OF MOBILE MEDIA DURING SHARED TIME CONTRIBUTES TO THESE OUTCOMES. THE STUDY AIMS INCLUDE 1) EXAMINING HOW PRESCHOOLERS’ MOBILE MEDIA TIME PREDICTS THEIR PEER INTERACTION SKILLS; 2) IDENTIFYING PROFILES OF PRESCHOOLERS’ MOBILE MEDIA USE USING MEASURES OF TIME AND CONTENT, TO TEST IF THESE PROFILES PREDICT PEER INTERACTION SKILLS, AND TO TEST IF THE PROFILES MODERATE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CHILD MOBILE MEDIA USE AND PEER INTERACTION SKILLS; AND 3) EXAMINING HOW PARENTS’ MOBILE MEDIA USE DURING PARENT-CHILD TIME PREDICTS PRESCHOOLERS’ PEER INTERACTION SKILLS. TO ADDRESS THESE AIMS, A MULTI-INFORMANT, MULTI-ASSESSMENT, LONGITUDINAL STUDY WILL BE CONDUCTED. PARENTS OF PRESCHOOL CHILDREN (3 TO 5 YEARS OLD) WILL COMPLETE AN ONLINE BASELINE SURVEY AND PROVIDE DATA ON CHILDREN’S MOBILE MEDIA USE ACROSS 10 CONSECUTIVE DAYS, INCLUDING: 1) PASSIVE SENSING (VIA AN APP INSTALLED ON THEIR DEVICE OR DEVICES) TO CONTINUOUSLY TRACK WHO IS USING A DEVICE AND FOR HOW LONG; 2) DAILY SCREENSHOTS OF PARENTS’ AND CHILDREN’S PRIMARY DEVICE USE FOR THE PREVIOUS 24 HOURS; AND 3) PARENTS’ TIME DIARIES TO INDICATE WHEN THEY ARE AROUND THEIR CHILD. PRESCHOOLERS’ PEER INTERACTION SKILLS WILL BE CAPTURED THROUGH OBSERVATION AND TEACHER REPORTS ACROSS MULTIPLE PRESCHOOL SETTINGS IN THE CENTRAL TEXAS AREA ON FIVE DIFFERENT DAYS. FOLLOW-UP SURVEYS AND CLASSROOM OBSERVATION WILL PROCEED THREE MONTHS AFTER BASELINE. MULTILEVEL MODELS WILL EXAMINE HOW CHILDREN’S MOBILE MEDIA USE, AND PARENTS’ MOBILE MEDIA USE IN THE PRESENCE OF THEIR CHILD, PREDICTS CHILD PEER INTERACTION SKILLS. USING A WEIGHTED SYSTEM BASED ON TIME SPENT ON THE APPLICATION AND THE APPLICATION CONTENT (I.E., SOCIALLY INTERACTIVE, EDUCATIONAL, VIOLENT, AND PROSOCIAL MEASURED USING A VALIDATED CODEBOOK), DIFFERENT PROFILES OF CHILD MOBILE MEDIA USERS WILL BE DETERMINED IN A LATENT PROFILE ANALYSIS, WHICH WILL BE USED AS MODERATORS OF THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CHILDREN’S MOBILE MEDIA USE AND THEIR PEER INTERACTION SKILLS. THE RESEARCH TEAM BRINGS EXPERTISE IN CHILD DEVELOPMENT, FAMILY SCIENCE, HUMAN-COMPUTER INTERACTION, AND MEDIA MEASUREMENT, SUPPORTED BY GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS. RESULTS FROM THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE ESSENTIAL DATA TO INFORM AND ADVANCE POLICIES TO SUPPORT PRESCHOOLERS’ SHORT- AND LONG-TERM SOCIAL WELL-BEING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ORAL AND TRANSDERMAL MELATONIN TREATMENT TO IMPROVE INSUFFICIENT SLEEP IN YOUTH AT RISK FOR MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS - ABSTRACT SLEEP PROBLEMS IN CHILDHOOD AND ADOLESCENCE ARE INDEPENDENT RISK FACTORS FOR ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION.  MELATONIN MAY IMPROVE MENTAL HEALTH BY PROMOTING SLEEP OR IMPROVING AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM BALANCE.  IN ADDITION TO ORAL SUPPLEMENTS, MELATONIN CAN BE PURCHASED IN THE FORM OF LOTION WHICH MAY HAVE A MUCH LONGER HALF-LIFE IN THE BODY.  USING SALIVARY SAMPLING OVER 48 HOURS, THIS PROJECT WILL CHARACTERIZE THE TIME COURSE OF THE ABSORPTION AND METABOLISM OF LOTIONBASED MELATONIN AND WHETHER MORE SIDE EFFECTS OCCUR THAN FOUND WITH ORAL ADMINISTRATION.  IN A RANDOMIZED CROSSOVER DESIGN, 14 – 21 YEAR OLDS AT RISK FOR MENTAL HEALTH PROBLEMS WILL THEN BE ASSIGNED TO A 7-DAY TREATMENT ARM OF MELATONIN LOTION, ORAL SUPPLEMENTS, AND PLACEBO CONTROLS.  IMPACTS ON SLEEP, AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM INDICATORS, MOOD, ANXIETY SYMPTOMS, AND SIDE EFFECTS WILL BE ASSESSED.  SLEEP WILL BE MEASURED USING WRIST-WORN ACTIVITY TRACKERS AND PARTICIPANT DIARIES.  AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM BALANCE WILL BE MEASURED USING HEART RATE VARIABILITY AND SALIVARY ALPHA-AMYLASE, AND ADHERENCE TO THE PROTOCOL WILL BE CONFIRMED VIA SALIVARY MELATONIN.  ANXIETY SYMPTOMS, MOOD, AND SIDE EFFECTS WILL BE ASSESSED USING DAILY QUESTIONNAIRES.  TO PROBE POSSIBLE MECHANISMS, CHANGES IN SLEEP AND NERVOUS SYSTEM PARAMETERS WILL BE EXAMINED FOR CORRELATIONS TO ANY IMPROVEMENTS IN ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION SYMPTOMS.  OUR STUDY CAN DETERMINE WHETHER MELATONIN IS AN EFFECTIVE TREATMENT FOR ADOLESCENTS WITH INADEQUATE SLEEP, AND WHETHER SLEEP IMPROVEMENTS OR AUTONOMIC ACTIVITY ARE POTENTIAL LINKS TO IMPROVEMENTS IN DEPRESSION AND ANXIETY SYMPTOMS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ERK1/2-C-FOS/EGR1/2 PATHWAY IN GFI1- AND C/EBP -MEDIATED GRANULOPOIESIS - PROJECT SUMMARY CELL FATE CHOICE IN THE HEMATOPOIETIC SYSTEM DEPENDS ON THE EXPRESSION OF LINEAGE SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS. IN THE MYELOID LINEAGE, TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS GFI1 AND C/EBPΑ PROMOTE NEUTROPHIL DEVELOPMENT WHEREAS HIGH LEVELS OF PU.1 FAVOR MONOCYTE OVER NEUTROPHIL DEVELOPMENT. TARGETED DELETION OF GFI1 IN MICE BLOCKS NEUTROPHIL FORMATION ACCOMPANIED BY AN EXPANSION OF ATYPICAL MONOCYTES. LOSS-OF-FUNCTION MUTATIONS IN GFI1 HAVE BEEN ASSOCIATED WITH SEVERE CONGENITAL NEUTROPENIA (SCN) IN HUMANS. BONE MARROW (BM) CELLS FROM GFI1-/- MICE OR TRANSDUCED WITH THE SCN-ASSOCIATED GFI1N382S MUTANT GAVE RISE TO MONOCYTES RATHER THAN NEUTROPHILS IN RESPONSE TO G-CSF. C/EBPΑ NULL MICE LACK MATURE GRANULOCYTES WITH A SPECIFIC BLOCK IN COMMON MYELOID PROGENITOR (CMP) TO GRANULOCYTE-MONOCYTE PROGENITOR (GMP) TRANSITION. THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH GFI1 AND C/EBPΑ PROMOTE GRANULOPOIESIS ARE INCOMPLETELY UNDERSTOOD. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES SHOW THAT GFI1 INHIBITED THE ACTIVATION OF ERK1/2 AND REPRESSED THE ERK1/2 DOWNSTREAM TARGET GENES C-FOS AND EGR1. INTERESTINGLY, INHIBITION OF ERK1/2 USING THE SPECIFIC MEK1/2 INHIBITORS REDUCED THE EXPRESSION OF C-FOS AND EGR1, AND PARTIALLY RESCUED NEUTROPHIL DEVELOPMENT OF GFI1-/- BM CELLS. OUR PRELIMINARY RESULTS FURTHER INDICATE THAT C/EBPΑ DOWNREGULATED THE EXPRESSION OF C-FOS AND EGR1 BY THE 3UTRS OF THEIR MRNAS WHEREAS PU.1 UPREGULATED C-FOS AND EGR1. THUS, IT APPEARS THAT C-FOS AND EGR1 ARE THE COMMON TARGET GENES THAT ARE REGULATED BY LINEAGE SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESES THAT GFI1 AND C/EBPΑ INSTRUCT NEUTROPHIL FATE IN PART THROUGH NEGATIVELY REGULATING THE ERK1/2-C-FOS/EGR1 PATHWAY AND THAT INHIBITION OF ERK1/2 SIGNALING MAY IMPROVE GRANULOPOIESIS IN GFI1-/- MICE. THREE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE PROPOSED TO TEST THE HYPOTHESES. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER SUPPRESSION OF C-FOS AND/OR EGR1 HAS AN EFFECT ON NEUTROPHIL DEVELOPMENT OF GFI1-/- BM CELLS IN VITRO AND IN VIVO. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF MEK1/2 INHIBITION ON NEUTROPHIL DEVELOPMENT IN MOUSE GFI1-/- CMPS AND GMPS, AND IN HUMAN CD34+ BM CELLS EXPRESSING THE SCN-ASSOCIATED GFI1N382S MUTANT. WE WILL FURTHER EXAMINE WHETHER THE SPECIFIC MEK1/2 INHIBITOR TRAMETINIB ALLEVIATES NEUTROPENIA IN GFI1-/- MICE. IN AIM 3, WE WILL EVALUATE WHETHER DOWNREGULATION OF C-FOS AND EGR1 IS REQUIRED FOR C/EBPΑ-DRIVEN GRANULOPOIESIS AND WHETHER INHIBITION OF THE ERK1/2-C-FOS/EGR1/2 PATHWAY RESCUES NEUTROPHIL DEVELOPMENT OF BM CELLS FROM ENH(F/F);MX1-CRE MICE IN WHICH THE EXPRESSION OF C/EBPΑ IS MARKEDLY DECREASED. WE WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE POTENTIAL ROLES OF MICRORNAS (MIRNAS) AND RNA BINDING PROTEINS (RBPS) IN C/EBPΑ-MEDIATED DOWNREGULATION OF C-FOS AND EGR1 EXPRESSION. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH MAY REVEAL NOVEL MECHANISMS BY WHICH GFI1 AND C/EBPΑ PROMOTE GRANULOPOIESIS, AND MAY LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR THE TREATMENT OF SCN PATIENTS WITH GFI1 MUTATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING MOTOR EXIT POINT GLIA FUNCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE NERVOUS SYSTEM IS DIVIDED INTO TWO SEPARATE, YET CONNECTED, DOMAINS: THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) AND PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (PNS), IN WHICH DISTINCT CELL TYPES OFTEN CARRY OUT THE SAME BIOLOGICAL FUNCTION. FOR INSTANCE, OLIGODENDROCYTES ARE RESTRICTED TO THE CNS AND SCHWANN CELLS TO THE PNS, AND BOTH GLIAL CELL TYPES FUNCTION TO MYELINATE AXONS, FACILITATING EFFICIENT NERVE CONDUCTION. THE RATIONALE FOR THIS PROJECT IS THAT THE NERVOUS SYSTEM BOUNDARIES, CALLED TRANSITION ZONES (TZ), THAT WERE LONG THOUGHT TO BE SELECTIVELY PERMEABLE TO AXONS ONLY, ARE OCCUPIED BY DYNAMIC GLIAL CELLS AND THEIR PERMEABILITY IS PRECISELY REGULATED OVER THE COURSE OF NERVOUS SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT. WE RECENTLY CHARACTERIZED A NOVEL POPULATION OF GLIA THAT RESIDE AT THESE TZS. MOTOR EXIT POINT (MEP) GLIA ORIGINATE IN THE SPINAL CORD AND MIGRATE INTO THE PNS TO MYELINATE MOTOR AXONS. MEP GLIA ALSO REGULATE OLIGODENDROCYTE MIGRATION AT THE VENTRAL BORDER OF THE SPINAL CORD AND PREVENT OLIGODENDROCYTES TO ECTOPICALLY MIGRATE INTO THE PNS. UNLIKE TRADITIONAL MYELINATING GLIA, MEP GLIA DISPLAY CENTRAL/PERIPHERAL HYBRID CHARACTERISTICS, AND ARE CONVENIENTLY LOCATED AT THE EDGE OF THE SPINAL CORD, IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE CNS AND PNS. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS, WHICH IS FORMULATED BASED ON PRELIMINARY DATA, IS THAT THESE TWO SUBTYPES OF CNS- DERIVED GLIA CAN FUNCTION IN BOTH HALVES OF THE NERVOUS SYSTEM. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED BY THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) DEFINE MEP GLIA GENE EXPRESSION PROFILE. USING SINGLE CELL RNA-SEQUENCING ZEBRAFISH DATASETS, WE WILL USE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION TO UNCOVER ADDITIONAL MEP GLIAL MARKERS. FOR EACH VALIDATED MARKER, WE WILL CREATE REPORTER AND MUTANT LINES, AND STUDY THE FUNCTION OF GENES PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN IN THE CONTEXT OF GLIAL BIOLOGY. THIS AIM WILL GENERATE HYPOTHESIS-DRIVEN PROJECTS FOR INCOMING STUDENTS. (2) INVESTIGATE PNS MYELINATING GLIA MIGRATING INTO THE SPINAL CORD. IN A RECENT STUDY, WE GENETICALLY INDUCED THE PRESENCE OF SCHWANN CELLS AND MEP GLIA IN THE POST-EMBRYONIC SPINAL CORD. IN THIS AIM, WE WILL DETERMINE THEIR ABILITY TO PRODUCE MYELIN IN THE HEALTHY AND DEMYELINATED CNS. (3) CHARACTERIZE OLIGODENDROCYTE MYELIN IN THE PNS. THE WORKING HYPOTHESIS IS THAT AT THE CNS/PNS INTERFACE, MOTOR AXON MYELINATION INVOLVES MULTIPLE POPULATIONS OF MYELINATING GLIA, AND THIS ARCHITECTURE IS PLASTIC UPON PERTURBATIONS. WE PREVIOUSLY DEMONSTRATED THE PRESENCE OF MYELINATING OLIGODENDROCYTES ON PNS MOTOR AXONS UPON PERTURBATION, BUT THE INTEGRITY AND MAINTENANCE OF THESE ECTOPIC MYELIN SHEATHS REMAIN UNKNOWN. THIS PROJECT IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE WE PROPOSE TO INVESTIGATE A PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN SOURCE OF MYELIN-FORMING CELLS AND THEIR PLASTICITY. THE KNOWLEDGE WE WILL GAIN FROM THE PROPOSED EXPERIMENTS MAY PROVIDE AN INNOVATIVE BASIS FOR NOVEL MYELIN-REPAIR THERAPIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MULTIFUNCTIONAL INJECTABLE HYDROGEL FOR SPINAL CORD INJURY REPAIR - PROJECT SUMMARY SPINAL CORD INJURY (SCI) CREATES A COMPLEX AND INHIBITORY MICROENVIRONMENT THAT LIMITS FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY THROUGH MULTIPLE PROCESSES THAT INCLUDE INFLAMMATION AND FIBROTIC AND GLIAL SCARRING. WHILE BIOMATERIAL-BASED REGENERATIVE STRATEGIES HAVE DEMONSTRATED PROMISE, MOST APPROACHES TARGET ONLY A SINGLE ASPECT OF THE INJURY RESPONSE, FAILING TO COMPREHENSIVELY ADDRESS THE MULTIFACTORIAL BARRIERS TO REGENERATION. TO OVERCOME THIS LIMITATION, WE HAVE DEVELOPED A NOVEL PLURONIC-NORBORNENE-HYALURONAN (PLUHA) INJECTABLE HYDROGEL CAPABLE OF SIMULTANEOUSLY DELIVERING MULTIPLE BIOACTIVE CARGO, INCLUDING SMALL MOLECULE THERAPEUTICS AND PEPTIDES, IN A SINGLE PLATFORM. PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT FUNCTIONALIZATION OF PLUHA WITH BOTH A TGF-Β INHIBITOR (SB431542) AND A RESTRICTIVE GROWTH MOLECULE A (RGMA) ANTAGONIST PEPTIDE ENHANCES AXON INFILTRATION AND CONNECTIVITY IN A RAT MODEL OF SCI. HOWEVER, THE RELEASE DYNAMICS OF THESE BIOACTIVE COMPONENTS, THEIR MECHANISTIC INTERACTIONS WITH THE INJURY ENVIRONMENT, AND THEIR IMPACT ON LONG-TERM FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY REMAIN UNCLEAR. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE SIMULTANEOUS DELIVERY OF MULTIPLE THERAPEUTIC AGENTS VIA THE PLUHA PLATFORM WILL MODULATE KEY INHIBITORY PROCESSES IN THE INJURY MICROENVIRONMENT THAT LEAD TO ENHANCED AXONAL INFILTRATION, CONNECTIVITY, AND BEHAVIORAL IMPROVEMENT IN A PRECLINICAL MODEL OF CERVICAL CONTUSION INJURY. SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL INTERROGATE THE DYNAMICS OF CARGO RELEASE FROM THE PLUHA HYDROGEL AND ASSESS HOW FORMULATION PARAMETERS LIKE PLURONIC WEIGHT PERCENTAGE AND CARGO LOADING CONCENTRATION INFLUENCE RELEASE KINETICS AND DEGRADATION IN BOTH A 3D IN VITRO MODEL AND A RAT CERVICAL CONTUSION MODEL. MAGNETIC RESONANCE ELASTOGRAPHY WILL TRACK HYDROGEL DEGRADATION IN VITRO AND IN VIVO AND FLUORESCENTLY LABELING THE RGMA PEPTIDE WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO THE TIME-DEPENDENT DELIVERY OF THE CARGO TO CELL TYPES IN THE INJURY AREA OF THE CONTUSION MODEL. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE THE LONG-TERM FUNCTIONAL IMPACT OF PLUHA-MEDIATED DELIVERY OF BIOACTIVE CARGO IN THE SAME RAT CERVICAL CONTUSION MODEL USED IN AIM 1. FOUR HYDROGEL FORMULATIONS: BLANK, RGMA ANTAGONIST PEPTIDE ONLY, SB431542 ONLY, AND A COMBINATION OF BOTH WILL BE COMPARED. MOTOR AND SENSORY FUNCTION WILL BE ASSESSED OVER 12 WEEKS USING ASSAYS FOR FUNCTIONAL IMPROVEMENT, INCLUDING VON FREY FILAMENT AND CYLINDER PAW TESTING. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH THE PLUHA HYDROGEL AS A MULTIFUNCTIONAL SCAFFOLD CAPABLE OF SIMULTANEOUSLY TARGETING MULTIPLE BARRIERS TO REGENERATION IN SCI. FURTHERMORE, THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE VALUABLE RESEARCH OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERGRADUATE ENGINEERING STUDENTS AT ROWAN UNIVERSITY, FOSTERING INTERDISCIPLINARY TRAINING IN NEUROSCIENCE AND BIOMEDICAL ENGINEERING AND PROVIDING OPPORTUNITIES TO CONDUCT ANIMAL STUDIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: OVERCOMING GLUTAMATE EXCITOTOXICITY TO METABOLIC STRESS - PROJECT SUMMARY NEURAL CIRCUITS REQUIRE A LARGE AMOUNT OF ENERGY TO FUNCTION, MAKING THE BRAIN HIGHLY VULNERABLE TO METABOLIC FAILURE. WHEN ATP LEVELS ARE INSUFFICIENT, NEURONS UNDERGO A TOXIC CASCADE CHARACTERIZED BY GLUTAMATE ACCUMULATION IN THE SYNAPTIC CLEFT, OVEREXCITATION, DYSFUNCTION, AND ULTIMATELY, CELL DEATH. THESE PATHOLOGICAL EVENTS UNDERLIE SEVERAL NEUROLOGICAL CONDITIONS, FROM DIRECT METABOLIC INSULTS LIKE STROKE AND RESPIRATORY ARREST, TO NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS SUCH AS ALZHEIMER'S, PARKINSON'S, ALS, AMONG MANY OTHERS. THEREFORE, INNOVATIVE APPROACHES IDENTIFYING MECHANISMS THAT PREVENT NEURONAL DEATH AND MITIGATE DAMAGE DURING ENERGETIC STRESS ARE CRITICAL FOR INFORMING THE DEVELOPMENT OF TREATMENTS FOR MULTIPLE NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS. MY LABORATORY RECENTLY DISCOVERED THAT AVIAN NEURONS COMPLETELY AVOID THE NEUROTOXIC CASCADE TRIGGERED BY METABOLIC STRESS. THIS PROVIDES US WITH THE OPPORTUNITY TO STUDY MECHANISMS TO EVADE METABOLIC-INDUCED GLUTAMATE EXCITOTOXICITY IN A SYSTEM WITH EXCEPTIONALLY HIGH ENERGETIC DEMAND. BASED ON PRELIMINARY DATA, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THIS NEUROPROTECTION ARISES FROM SYNERGISTIC MECHANISMS MAINTAINING GLUTAMATE TRANSPORTER FUNCTION (AIM 1) AND ENHANCING GABAERGIC SIGNALING (AIM 2), WHICH PRESERVE NEURONAL FUNCTION AND VIABILITY IN VIVO (AIM 3). WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS USING AN INTEGRATIVE APPROACH THAT COMBINES PATCH-CLAMP ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, BEHAVIORAL ASSAYS, AND ADVANCED MICROSCOPY, PROVIDING HANDS-ON TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR TWO PHD STUDENTS AND EIGHT UNDERGRADUATES. THIS RESEARCH WILL ESTABLISH A FRAMEWORK FOR NEUROPROTECTION AGAINST METABOLIC GLUTAMATE EXCITOTOXICITY—CRITICAL FOR OVERCOMING NEURONAL ENERGETIC STRESS ACROSS MULTIPLE BRAIN DISORDERS—WHILE TRAINING THE NEXT GENERATION OF SCIENTISTS AND PROFESSIONALS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TSC1 REGULATION OF THE PURKINJE NEURON AXON INITIAL SEGMENT AND CEREBELLAR FUNCTION - ABSTRACT AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD) IS STRONGLY LINKED TO CEREBELLAR DYSFUNCTION. MULTIPLE LINES OF EVIDENCE INDICATE THAT IMPAIRED CEREBELLAR PURKINJE NEURON (PN) ACTIVITY CAN CONTRIBUTE DIRECTLY TO ASD-RELATED BEHAVIORS. LOSS-OF-FUNCTION MUTATIONS IN TSC1 CAUSE TUBEROUS SCLEROSIS COMPLEX (TSC), A MULTISYSTEM DISORDER FREQUENTLY ASSOCIATED WITH ASD. IN A MOUSE MODEL WITH PN-SPECIFIC TSC1 DELETION (L7/PCP2-CRE (+) ; TSC1FLOX/FLOX), PNS EXHIBIT REDUCED REPETITIVE FIRING, DECREASED AXON INITIAL SEGMENT (AIS) SODIUM CHANNEL EXPRESSION, AND A MARKED REDUCTION OF THE AIS SCAFFOLDING PROTEIN ANKYRIN-G (ANKG). THESE OBSERVATIONS SUGGEST THAT LOSS OF TSC1 RESULTS IN A DISRUPTION OF THE MOLECULAR ORGANIZATION AT THE PURKINJE NEURON AIS, AND THEREBY, IMPAIRS INTRINSIC EXCITABILITY AND CEREBELLAR FUNCTION. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO EXTEND THIS WORK AND DEFINE THE CELLULAR MECHANISMS BY WHICH TSC1 LOSS IN PNS ALTERS AIS FUNCTION, INTRINSIC FIRING, AND CEREBELLUM-DEPENDENT BEHAVIORS. AIM 1 WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT TSC1 DELETION IMPAIRS PN FIRING THROUGH AIS DYSFUNCTION, EXTENDING BEYOND THE LOSS OF AIS NAV CHANNELS, BY TESTING IF AIS POTASSIUM CHANNEL MECHANISMS THAT SHAPE REPOLARIZATION ARE ALSO DISRUPTED. AIM 1 WILL USE PATCH CLAMP ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, DYNAMIC CLAMP RESCUE STRATEGIES, AND QUANTITATIVE IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE OF AIS PROTEINS. AIM 2 WILL DIRECTLY DETERMINE WHETHER THE PN EXCITABILITY AND AIS PHENOTYPES CAUSED BY TSC1 DELETION ARE MEDIATED BY MTORC1, RATHER THAN MTORC2 SIGNALING, USING PN-TARGETED VIRAL KNOCKDOWN APPROACHES AND ASSESSING MOLECULAR, ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL, AND BEHAVIORAL OUTCOMES. AIM 3 WILL DEFINE THE MECHANISM UNDERLYING ANKG LOSS BY DISTINGUISHING AMONG REDUCED ANK3 TRANSCRIPTION, INCREASED AIS SCAFFOLD TURNOVER, OR INCREASED PROTEOLYSIS, INTEGRATING TRANSCRIPT PROFILING FROM SORTED PNS WITH PHARMACOLOGIC PERTURBATIONS AND QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF THE AIS STRUCTURE. THESE STUDIES WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW TSC1-MTOR PATHWAYS REGULATE NEURONAL EXCITABILITY AT THE AIS AND WILL PROVIDE MECHANISTIC INSIGHT INTO CEREBELLAR CONTRIBUTIONS TO ASD AND TSC. AS AN AREA PROJECT, THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE INTENSIVE TRAINING FOR SEVERAL UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENT RESEARCHERS IN ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, IMAGING, CELL-TYPE SPECIFIC MOLECULAR PROFILING, AND COMPUTATIONAL APPROACHES FOR DYNAMIC CLAMP EXPERIMENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SMARTPHONE-BASED DIGITAL COACHING FOR FALL PREVENTION AND RESEARCH TRAINING IN STROKE SURVIVORS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  FALLS ARE ONE OF THE MOST SERIOUS COMPLICATIONS FOR STROKE SURVIVORS, OFTEN LEADING TO INJURY, LOSS OF INDEPENDENCE, AND COSTLY HOSPITALIZATIONS. WHILE CURRENT ASSESSMENTS CAN IDENTIFY INDIVIDUALS AT RISK, THERE IS A CRITICAL GAP IN TRANSLATING THAT KNOWLEDGE INTO PRACTICAL, ACCESSIBLE INTERVENTIONS FOR EVERYDAY LIFE. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP AND EVALUATE A SMARTPHONE-BASED DIGITAL COACHING SYSTEM DESIGNED TO SUPPORT SAFER MOBILITY AND REDUCE FALL RISK IN STROKE SURVIVORS. OUR SPECIFIC AIMS IN THIS PROJECT ARE: 1. DEVELOP AND OPTIMIZE A SMARTPHONE-BASED COACHING PLATFORM. THE APP WILL PROVIDE PERSONALIZED REMINDERS, EXERCISE PROMPTS, AND SAFETY GUIDANCE, CO-DESIGNED WITH STROKE SURVIVORS, CAREGIVERS, AND PHYSICAL THERAPISTS TO ENSURE RELEVANCE, USABILITY, AND ACCESSIBILITY. 2. PILOT-TEST FEASIBILITY, USABILITY, AND ACCEPTABILITY IN COMMUNITY-DWELLING STROKE SURVIVORS. A SHORT-TERM PILOT STUDY (N≈40) WILL ASSESS USER ADHERENCE, SATISFACTION, AND BARRIERS TO ADOPTION, WITH EMPHASIS ON PARTICIPANTS WITH LIMITED ACCESS TO ONGOING REHABILITATION SUPPORT WHO MAY LACK CONSISTENT ACCESS TO REHABILITATION RESOURCES. IMPACT: THIS PROJECT WILL DELIVER: 1) A PROTOTYPE DIGITAL COACHING TOOL FOR FALL PREVENTION IN STROKE SURVIVORS. 2) PILOT DATA ON FEASIBILITY, USABILITY, AND IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS. 3) ENHANCED RESEARCH CAPACITY AT ROCHESTER INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY BY EMBEDDING STUDENTS IN ALL PHASES OF DESIGN, TESTING, AND ANALYSIS. STUDENT TRAINING: THE PROJECT DIRECTLY SUPPORTS THE NIH SURE MISSION BY CREATING HANDS-ON TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERGRADUATE, MASTER’S, AND PHD STUDENTS. STUDENTS WILL GAIN EXPERIENCE IN APP DEVELOPMENT, USABILITY TESTING, HUMAN-SUBJECT RESEARCH, AND DATA ANALYSIS. THIS LAYERED MENTORING MODEL WILL PROVIDE UNDERGRADUATES EARLY EXPOSURE, MASTER’S STUDENTS DEEPER TECHNICAL ROLES, AND A PHD STUDENT CONTINUITY ACROSS YEARS 2–3, BUILDING A SUSTAINABLE RESEARCH PIPELINE. RELEVANCE TO NIH AND NIGMS: THE STUDY IS INDEPENDENT OF ANY ONGOING PROJECTS AND REPRESENTS A MODEST, ACHIEVABLE STEP TOWARD SCALABLE INTERVENTIONS FOR STROKE SURVIVORS. IT ALIGNS WITH THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF GENERAL MEDICAL SCIENCES’ FOCUS ON BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH CAPACITY BUILDING, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AND HANDS-ON STUDENT RESEARCH TRAINING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MICROENVIRONMENTAL RESCUE OF AGE-RELATED CELLULAR DYSFUNCTION IN A 3D BIOPRINTED MAMMARY MODEL SYSTEM - PROJECT SUMMARY DURING THE COMPLEX PROCESS OF CELLULAR AND TISSUE DECLINE DUE TO ORGANISMAL AGING, DISEASES SUCH AS DIABETES, NEURODEGENERATION, MUSCLE ATROPHY, AND CANCER BECOME COMMONPLACE. THESE DISEASES EACH HAVE UNIQUE GENETIC FEATURES AND TARGETING THEM CAN LEAD TO THERAPIES PRESERVING TISSUE FUNCTIONS. HOWEVER, RESTORATION TO A YOUTHFUL STATE IS RARE. THUS, IT IS CRITICAL TO RESEARCH AND DESIGN METHODS OF RESTORATIVE OR PREVENTATIVE TREATMENTS TO CURE THESE DISEASES. A MAJOR CHALLENGE IN RESEARCHING AGE-RELATED TISSUE DECLINE IS ENSURING THAT THE FINDINGS RELIABLY PREDICT OUTCOMES AT THE ORGANISMAL LEVEL. TO THIS END, WE AND OTHERS HAVE DEMONSTRATED THE POWERFUL REGENERATIVE CAPABILITIES OF THE MOUSE MAMMARY GLAND DURING THE PROCESS OF MAMMARY GLAND BIOGENESIS. WHEN THE MOUSE MAMMARY GLAND IS CLEARED OF NASCENT EPITHELIAL TISSUES AND INJECTED WITH DISPERSED MOUSE MAMMARY EPITHELIAL CELLS OR TISSUE FRAGMENTS MIXED WITH CANCER CELLS, DYSFUNCTIONAL STEM CELLS, OR NORMAL NON-MAMMARY STEM CELLS, THEY ARE REDIRECTED/RESCUED WHILE FUNCTIONALLY CONTRIBUTING TO GLAND REGENERATION. OTHER DATA HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT CANCER CELLS EXPOSED TO THE REGENERATIVE EMBRYONIC ENVIRONMENT CAN ALSO BE REDIRECTED TO A NORMAL FUNCTIONAL STATE. CONSISTENT WITH THIS, OUR PRELIMINARY EVIDENCE SHOWS THAT INTERACTIONS WITH INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS CAN REDUCE TUMOR FORMATION RATES OF BREAST CANCER CELLS IN MICE. THESE DATA, COUPLED WITH THE FINDING THAT EVS ISOLATED FROM PLURIPOTENT CELLS CAN ALSO PROMOTE HEALING, BLOCK SENESCENCE, AND REDUCE MOLECULAR MARKERS OF AGING, INDICATE THAT CELLS/TISSUES CAN BE REJUVENATED VIA EXPOSURE TO A REGENERATIVE ENVIRONMENT. HOWEVER, OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS FOR WHY THIS HAPPENS IS LACKING. WHILE THE GOLD STANDARD CLEARED MAMMARY GLAND MOUSE MODEL IS AN IMPORTANT TOOL FOR STUDYING REGENERATIVE MODELS, IT IS DIFFICULT TO DETERMINE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS WHEN USED EXCLUSIVELY. TO SOLVE THIS ISSUE OUR GROUP HAS DESIGNED A LOW-COST, ADAPTABLE 3D BIOPRINTER CAPABLE OF MANUFACTURING LUMINAL CHIMERIC MAMMARY EPITHELIAL ORGANOIDS IN VITRO. THIS TOOL, IN TANDEM WITH THE MOUSE MAMMARY GLAND MODEL SYSTEM, ENABLES US TO ASK DISCREET MOLECULAR-DRIVEN QUESTIONS ABOUT HOW REGENERATIVE ENVIRONMENTS AND SIGNALING CAUSE THEIR OBSERVED EFFECTS. WE HAVE FOUND THAT AS THESE REGENERATIVE CHIMERIC ORGANOIDS FORM IN VITRO, THE EXCHANGE OF INTERCELLULAR MACHINERY, SUCH AS MITOCHONDRIA, READILY OCCURS. HERE WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THAT THE EXPOSURE OF DYSFUNCTIONAL ORGANOIDS/TISSUES TO YOUTHFUL REGENERATIVE SIGNALING REVERSES AGE-RELATED DECLINE THROUGH INTERCELLULAR TRANSFER OF MOLECULAR MACHINERY, INCLUDING MITOCHONDRIA. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE AIM TO 1: DETERMINE THE MOLECULAR EFFECT OF REGENERATIVE INTERCELLULAR TRANSFER ON AGED/SENESCENT CELLS AND 2: DETERMINE THE MOLECULAR EFFECT OF INTERCELLULAR TRANSFER ON CANCER CELLS. THESE DATA WILL ALLOW US TO UNDERSTAND A CRITICAL ASPECT OF THE REJUVENATING EFFECTS OF EXPOSURE TO REGENERATIVE ENVIRONMENTS AND, THUS, BROADEN OUR CAPABILITIES TO DEVELOP DOWNSTREAM CLINICAL TREATMENTS TO PREVENT OR CURE MANY AGE-RELATED DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GENOMIC DETERMINANTS AND ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS OF HUMAN ASSOCIATED AKKERMANSIA GROWN ON CORE HUMAN MILK OLIGOSACCHARIDES - AKKERMANSIA MUCINIPHILA IS A MUCIN-DEGRADING BACTERIUM COMMON TO THE HUMAN GUT THAT HAS BEEN SHOWN TO POSITIVELY IMPACT HUMAN HEALTH. HOWEVER, THE AKKERMANSIA GENUS IS DIVERSE, AND WE LACK A CLEAR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW THIS DIVERSITY IMPACTS THE PHYSIOLOGICAL ACTIVITY AND ECOLOGICAL DYNAMICS ACROSS THE LINEAGE. THE LONG- TERM GOAL OF OUR RESEARCH PROGRAM IS TO HELP DEVELOP TARGETED, THERAPEUTIC USES OF AKKERMANSIA, EITHER THROUGH STIMULATING ENDOGENOUS STRAINS WITH DIETARY INTERVENTIONS (~70% PREVALENCE) OR BY ADMINISTERING SPECIES AS PROBIOTICS IN A CONTEXT-DEPENDENT MANNER. BEFORE THESE THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS CAN BE REALIZED, WE NEED A DEEPER UNDERSTANDING OF THE METABOLIC STRATEGIES AND ECOLOGICAL DYNAMICS THAT ALLOW EACH AKKERMANSIA SPECIES TO COLONIZE, COMPETE, AND PERSIST IN THE GUT. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES FOR THIS APPLICATION ARE (I) TO DEFINE THE GENOMIC AND METABOLIC DETERMINANTS BY WHICH SELECT AKKERMANSIA SPECIES AND STRAINS DEGRADE NON-FUCOSYLATED, CORE HUMAN MILK OLIGOSACCHARIDES (HMOS) DURING GROWTH, AND (II) TO IDENTIFY ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS AMONG AKKERMANSIA AND OTHER HMO-DEGRADING BACTERIA OF THE INFANT GUT MICROBIOTA. THE RATIONALE FOR PRIORITIZING EXPERIMENTS USING HMOS IS THAT THEY ARE SELECTIVE, DIETARY SUBSTRATES KNOWN TO INFLUENCE THE COMPOSITION, DEVELOPMENT, AND ACTIVITY OF THE GUT MICROBIOTA EARLY IN LIFE. FURTHER, ALTHOUGH HMOS ARE TYPICALLY AVAILABLE ONLY DURING BREASTFEEDING, HMOS ARE USED IN PREBIOTIC DIETARY FORMULATIONS FOR ADULTS. THUS, THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL INFORM STRATEGIES TO STIMULATE OR ADMINISTER AKKERMANSIA THROUGHOUT HUMAN LIFE. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF THIS APPLICATION IS THAT THE INCREASED GENOMIC CAPACITY FOR SUGAR DEGRADATION OBSERVED IN SELECT AKKERMANSIA GENOMES WILL RESULT IN MORE EFFICIENT AND POTENTIALLY NOVEL MECHANISMS OF DEGRADATION OF NON-FUCOSYLATED, CORE HMOS BY THOSE SPECIES/STRAINS. FURTHER, BECAUSE OF THE MORE EFFICIENT USE OF HMOS BY THESE SPECIES, THEY WILL BE ABLE TO CO-EXIST WITH OR POTENTIALLY OUTCOMPETE OTHER HMO-DEGRADING BACTERIA. TO TEST THESE HYPOTHESES, WE WILL USE LABORATORY CULTIVATION STUDIES COUPLED WITH MULTI-OMIC (I.E., GENOMIC, TRANSCRIPTOMIC, AND METABOLOMIC) APPROACHES TO INVESTIGATE TWO INDEPENDENT, BUT COMPLIMENTARY SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) – IDENTIFY THE GENOMIC DETERMINANTS AND METABOLIC OUTPUT OF GROWTH ON THE CORE HMOS LACTO-N-TETRAOSE (LNT) AND LACTO-N-NEOTETRAOSE (LNNT) ACROSS (AIM 1A) AND WITHIN (AIM 1B) HUMAN-ASSOCIATED AKKERMANSIA SPECIES. (2) CHARACTERIZE THE ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS AMONG SELECT AKKERMANSIA AND BIFIDOBACTERIUM SPECIES WHEN CO-CULTURED ON LNT AND LNNT. THIS WORK IS EXPECTED TO HAVE A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT BECAUSE AKKERMANSIA ARE BEING PURSUED FOR VARIOUS THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS WITH AN INCOMPLETE UNDERSTANDING OF THEIR BASIC BIOLOGY. GIVEN THAT AKKERMANSIA SPECIES ARE FUNCTIONALLY DISTINCT, IDENTIFYING MECHANISMS THAT FAVOR ONE SPECIES OVER ANOTHER IN A CONTEXT-DEPENDENT MANNER MAY INFORM FUTURE THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS SPECIFIC TO A PARTICULAR DISEASE STATE OR LIFE-STAGE. STUDIES WILL BE CONDUCTED BY STUDENT SCIENTISTS AT A PRIMARILY UNDERGRADUATE INSTITUTION, SIMULTANEOUSLY FULFILLING THE RESEARCH AND TRAINING MISSIONS OF THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF GENERAL MEDICAL SCIENCES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LINK BETWEEN IMMUNOMETABOLISM AND EPIGENETICS IN MALARIA VECTOR MOSQUITO ANOPHELES STEPHENSI. - PROJECT SUMMARY MALARIA IS A DEVASTATING MOSQUITO-BORNE DISEASE, AND MOSQUITO CONTROL IS AN INDISPENSABLE STRATEGY FOR REDUCING MALARIA TRANSMISSION. EPIGENETICS RESEARCH REPRESENTS A NEW FRONTIER IN MOSQUITO BIOLOGY. IN IMMUNE CELLS, AEROBIC GLYCOLYSIS CONSTITUTES A KEY METABOLIC SHIFT CHARACTERIZED BY INCREASED LACTATE PRODUCTION. LACTATE-MEDIATED HISTONE LACTYLATION HAS EMERGED AS A CRUCIAL EPIGENETIC MECHANISM IN IMMUNE REGULATION IN VERTEBRATES. IN MOSQUITOES, INFECTION WITH MALARIA PARASITES LEADS TO ELEVATED LACTATE LEVELS, SUGGESTING THAT THIS IMMUNOMETABOLIC CHANGE MAY MODULATE THE EPIGENETIC CONTROL OF MOSQUITO IMMUNITY AGAINST THE PARASITES. IN THIS STUDY, WE WILL EMPLOY A MULTI-OMICS APPROACH TO INTEGRATE METABOLOMIC, EPIGENOMIC (VIA ATAC-SEQ AND CUT&TAG), AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC (VIA RNA-SEQ) DATA, AIMING TO ESTABLISH A MECHANISTIC LINK BETWEEN IMMUNOMETABOLISM AND EPIGENETIC REGULATION IN ANTI-PLASMODIAL IMMUNITY IN THE VECTOR MOSQUITO ANOPHELES STEPHENSI. THIS PROJECT WILL SERVE AS A ROBUST PLATFORM FOR TRAINING GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN FRONTIER RESEARCH USING CUTTING-EDGE MULTI-OMICS APPROACHES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPACT OF A VIRAL RNA SILENCING SUPPRESSOR ON SNRK1-MEDIATED AUTOPHAGY - FOOD SECURITY IS A SIGNIFICANT ISSUE WORLDWIDE, WITH HEALTH PROBLEMS RELATED TO DIET BECOMING AN INCREASED BURDEN ON SOCIETY. FOOD AVAILABILITY IS STRONGLY IMPACTED BY CROP LOSS, AND US CROPS ARE VULNERABLE TO GEMINIVIRUS DISEASES THAT ARE DIFFICULT TO CONTROL. CURRENT CONTROL MEASURES INCLUDE LIMITING GEMINIVIRUS VECTOR POPULATIONS USING PESTICIDES, WHICH ARE A SIGNIFICANT HEALTH CONCERN. PESTICIDES ARE UBIQUITOUS IN THE ENVIRONMENT AND MOST ACT BY DISRUPTING NERVOUS SYSTEM FUNCTION, AND SO RESEARCH TO DISCOVER ALTERNATIVE METHODS OF CONTROLLING GEMINIVIRUS INFECTIONS IS WARRANTED. THE ABILITY OF A HOST TO RESIST INFECTION DEPENDS ON DEFENSE-COUNTERDEFENSE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN PATHOGEN AND HOST. MANY PLANT VIRUSES, INCLUDING GEMINIVIRUSES, ENCODE RNA SILENCING SUPPRESSORS, WHICH CAN BE VIEWED AS EFFECTORS THAT SUPPRESS HOST INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSES. KEY UNANSWERED QUESTIONS IN THE GEMINIVIRUS FIELD ARE HOW RNA SILENCING AND AUTOPHAGY COORDINATE THE ANTIVIRAL RESPONSE, AND HOW VIRAL SILENCING SUPPRESSORS (VSRS) SUBVERT THAT RESPONSE. GEMINIVIRUS VSRS (AC2/C2) INACTIVATES SNRK1, AN SNF1-RELATED PROTEIN KINASE, RESULTING IN DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION OF AUTOPHAGY-RELATED GENES. IN ADDITION, GEMINIVIRUS VSRS INTERACT WITH, AND RELOCALIZE, AN ENDOGENOUS REGULATOR OF GENE SILENCING (RGSCAM). THIS SUPPORTS OUR HYPOTHESIS THAT GEMINIVIRUS VSRS SUBVERT THE SNRK1/AUTOPHAGY PATHWAY TO SUPPRESS RNA SILENCING. WE PLAN TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS WITH THREE SPECIFIC AIMS. IN AIM1, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF VSRS IN AUTOPHAGY. WE WILL DETERMINE I) THE IMPACT OF AC2 ON AUTOPHAGY, II) IMPACT OF AC2 ON SNRK1 INDUCTION OF AUTOPHAGY, AND III) IMPACT OF SNRK1 INHIBITION ON AC2 ACCUMULATION. AIM 2 WILL CHARACTERIZE THE EFFECT OF SNRK1 ON RGSCAM FUNCTION. WE WILL INVESTIGATE I) THE ROLE OF RGSCAM ON AC2 ACCUMULATION, II) ROLE OF ON AC2 AND SGS3 ACCUMULATION, AND III) ROLE OF SNRK1 ON RDR6 EXPRESSION. FOR AIM 3 WE WILL INVESTIGATE I) THE EFFECT OF AUTOPHAGY ON RNA SILENCING, AND II) THE EFFECT OF AUTOPHAGY ON HOST RECOVERY FROM INFECTION. THIS WORK WILL INCREASE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLES OF RGSCAM AND AUTOPHAGY IN REGULATION OF RNA SILENCING, PART OF THE PLANT INNATE DEFENSE RESPONSE, AND PROVIDE US WITH THE MOLECULAR BASIS OF HOW GEMINIVIRUSES TARGET AUTOPHAGY DURING INFECTION. AS PATHWAYS TARGETED BY GEMINIVIRUS VSRS ARE HIGHLY CONSERVED, LINKS BETWEEN RNA SILENCING, AUTOPHAGY AND SNRK1 REGULATION OF STRESS RESPONSES CAN HAVE IMPORTANT IMPLICATIONS FOR HOST DEFENSE AND CONTROL OF DSRNA-INDUCING PATHWAYS IN BOTH PLANTS AND MAMMALS. IT SHOULD BE NOTED THAT ABSENCE OF THE INTERFERON PATHWAY IN PLANTS, WHICH LIKE RNA SILENCING CAN BE TRIGGERED BY DSRNA, WILL SIMPLIFY DATA INTERPRETATION. MOREOVER, THIS WORK WILL PAVE THE WAY FOR DEVELOPMENT OF STRATEGIES BASED ON DISRUPTING INTERACTIONS BETWEEN VIRUS VSRS AND HOST INNATE IMMUNE PATHWAYS. THIS COULD LEAD TO BROAD- BASED RESISTANCE TO THIS RAPIDLY EXPANDING GROUP OF PLANT VIRAL PATHOGENS, INCREASING FOOD SECURITY AND IMPROVING PUBLIC HEALTH BY REDUCING HARMFUL PESTICIDE USE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A METABOLIC ENGINEERING PLATFORM FOR MACROLIDE COMBINATORIAL BIOSYNTHESIS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT A METABOLIC ENGINEERING PLATFORM FOR MACROLIDE COMBINATORIAL BIOSYNTHESIS MACROLIDES ARE NATURAL PRODUCT ANTIBIOTICS CLINICALLY USED TO TREAT BACTERIAL INFECTIONS, BUT THE EMERGENCE OF MACROLIDE RESISTANCE BLUNTS THE IMPACT OF CURRENT MEDICATIONS. MACROLIDES INHIBIT THE 50S RIBOSOMAL SUBUNIT VIA HYDROGEN BONDING TO THE 23S-RRNA CATALYTIC CENTER, RESULTING IN THE TERMINATION OF PEPTIDE TRANSLATION. THE DEOXYSUGAR MOIETIES ARE REQUIRED FOR BINDING TO THE 23S RRNA. THE PRIMARY RESISTANCE MECHANISMS FOR MACROLIDES INCLUDE POINT MUTATIONS IN 23S RRNA AND METHYLATION OF CRITICAL RESIDUES THAT INHIBIT THE INTERMOLECULAR INTERACTIONS BETWEEN THE DEOXYSUGARS AND THE 50S RIBOSOMAL SUBUNIT. THEREFORE, THERE IS A VITAL NEED TO DEVELOP NEW MACROLIDE STRUCTURAL VARIANTS TO OVERCOME DRUG RESISTANCE. STRUCTURAL MODIFICATIONS TO THE HYDROXYLATION AND GLYCOSYLATION PATTERNS ARE CHALLENGING VIA CHEMICAL SYNTHETIC AND SEMI-SYNTHETIC TECHNIQUES, SO WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A BIOSYNTHETIC SYSTEM FOR REPROGRAMMING THE PIKROMYCIN AND SPIRAMYCIN PATHWAYS. IN THIS NIH SURE R16 PROJECT, WE WILL LEVERAGE SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY TO CREATE A COMBINATORIAL BIOSYNTHESIS PLATFORM FOR DEVELOPING NEW 14-MEMBERED MACROLIDES (14-MM) AND 16-MEMBERED MACROLIDES (16-MM). TO FACILITATE THE PRODUCTION OF ANALOGS, WE WILL EXPLOIT MACROLIDE-PRODUCTION SUPERHOSTS FOR GLYCODIVERSIFICATION AND CYP450 OXYGENASE OVEREXPRESSION EXPERIMENTS. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH ARE THREE- FOLD: (1) TO DESIGN AND CONSTRUCT NOVEL BIOSYNTHETIC PATHWAYS FOR MACROLIDE PRODUCTION, (2) TO PRODUCE, ISOLATE, AND STRUCTURALLY CHARACTERIZE NEW MACROLIDE DERIVATIVES, (3) TO EVALUATE THE ANTIMICROBIAL POTENTIAL OF THESE NEW METABOLITES. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT (1) THE NATIVE GLYCOSYLTRANSFERASES WILL BE “SUBSTRATE FLEXIBLE” TO TRANSFER THE INTENDED TDP-DEOXYSUGAR DONORS TO THE MACROLIDE AGLYCONES, RESULTING IN STRUCTURAL VARIANTS WITH OPTIMIZED SACCHARIDE PATTERNS; (2) THE HETEROLOGOUSLY EXPRESSED CYP450S WILL INTRODUCE REGIOSPECIFIC HYDROXYLATIONS AND EPOXIDATIONS, GENERATING ANALOGS WITH INCREASED POTENCY. OUR SPECIFIC AIMS WILL TEST THESE HYPOTHESES: (AIM 1) WE WILL HETEROLOGOUSLY EXPRESS “SUGAR PLASMIDS” IN THE PIKROMYCIN AND SPIRAMYCIN-PRODUCING HOSTS TO PRODUCE NOVEL GLYCOSYLATED MACROLIDES, AND (AIM 2) WE WILL EXPRESS DIVERSE CYP450 ENZYMES IN THESE ORGANISMS TO INTRODUCE NEW HYDROXYL/EPOXIDE FUNCTIONALITIES INTO THE MACROLACTONE SKELETON. NEW ANALOGS WILL BE RIGOROUSLY CHARACTERIZED VIA NMR SPECTROSCOPY. THE ANTIMICROBIAL ACTIVITY WILL BE ASSESSED VIA MICROBROTH DILUTION ANTIMICROBIAL SUSCEPTIBILITY ASSAY. RIBOSOME BINDING OF THE NEW ANALOGS WILL BE TESTED IN AN E. COLI S30 LYSATE ASSAY. THIS CONTRIBUTION IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE THE EXPECTED PRODUCTION PLATFORM WILL MORE FULLY EXPLORE THE CHEMICAL SPACE OF 14-MM AND 16-MM. FURTHERMORE, THIS RESEARCH IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT IS ANTICIPATED TO RESULT IN A VALUABLE SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY PLATFORM FOR ELABORATING NEW MACROLIDE DRUG LEADS.

description: MOLECULAR MECHANISMS MEDIATING A NOVEL ESCHERICHIA COLI SIBLING INHIBITION, A SPECIFIC FORM OF INTRA-SPECIES INHIBITION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  BACTERIAL COMPETITION PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE IN REGULATING MICROBIAL POPULATIONS IN ENVIRONMENTS. SUCH INTERACTIONS HAVE HISTORICALLY YIELDED BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS OF IMMENSE MEDICAL VALUE, EXEMPLIFIED BY FLEMING’S DISCOVERY OF PENICILLIN AND THE ENSUING “GOLDEN AGE” OF ANTIBIOTIC DISCOVERY. HOWEVER, THE RISE OF MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT PATHOGENS COUPLED WITH A STAGNATION IN NEW ANTIBIOTIC DEVELOPMENT HAS CREATED AN URGENT PUBLIC HEALTH CRISIS.  WE RECENTLY DISCOVERED THAT ESCHERICHIA COLI POSSESSES A NOVEL MECHANISM OF “SIBLING INHIBITION,” WHEREBY GENETICALLY IDENTICAL E. COLI AND OTHER GRAM-POSITIVE AND GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIAL CELLS INHIBIT EACH OTHER’S GROWTH. WHEN E. COLI CELLS ARE INOCULATED IN SOFT AGAR, THEY FORM CLEAR INHIBITORY BORDERS BETWEEN EXPANDING COLONIES. SUPERNATANT COLLECTED FROM THESE BORDERS DISPLAYS BROAD-SPECTRUM ANTIBACTERIAL ACTIVITY, INCLUDING ACTIVITY AGAINST STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS, PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA, AND MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS. PRELIMINARY CHARACTERIZATION INDICATES THE ACTIVE COMPOUND, TERMED THE E. COLI SIBLING INHIBITOR, IS A HEAT- STABLE, NEGATIVELY CHARGED, HYDROPHILIC MOLECULE <500 DA, RESISTANT TO PROTEASE AND AUTOCLAVING, AND CAPABLE OF LYSING BACTERIAL CELLS INTO MEMBRANE VESICLES. THESE FINDINGS STRONGLY SUGGEST THE PRESENCE OF A PREVIOUSLY UNIDENTIFIED SMALL-MOLECULE ANTIBACTERIAL AND MAKE IT POSSIBLE TO FURTHER PURIFY AND ISOLATE THE SIBLING INHIBITOR.  WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT E. COLI SECRETES A NOVEL SIBLING INHIBITOR WITH BROAD-SPECTRUM ANTIBACTERIAL ACTIVITY THAT DISRUPTS ESSENTIAL CELLULAR PROCESSES AND CULMINATES IN CELL RUPTURE. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL: AIM 1. IDENTIFY THE CELLULAR PROCESS TARGETED BY THE SIBLING INHIBITOR USING COMPLEMENTARY APPROACHES, TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND CYTOLOGICAL PROFILING OF ANTIBIOTIC-INDUCED CHANGES. AIM 2. DETERMINE THE TEMPORAL SEQUENCE OF CELLULAR EVENTS DURING INHIBITION: CHROMOSOMAL DNA DEGRADATION, CYTOPLASMIC PROTEIN LOSS, AND MEMBRANE DISRUPTION. AIM 3. OBTAIN A PURE CHEMICAL FORM OF THE SIBLING INHIBITOR BY OPTIMIZING PRODUCTION AND ISOLATING THE ACTIVE COMPOUND(S) USING LC-MS AND HPLC-BASED PURIFICATION.  SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS WILL ESTABLISH THE CELLULAR TARGET AND MOLECULAR IDENTITY OF A NOVEL ANTIBACTERIAL COMPOUND PRODUCED BY E. COLI, ADVANCING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF BACTERIAL COMPETITION AND POTENTIALLY YIELDING A NEW CLASS OF THERAPEUTIC CANDIDATES. THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO PROVIDE RIGOROUS RESEARCH TRAINING FOR GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS AT LEHMAN COLLEGE, STRENGTHENING THE BIOMEDICAL WORKFORCE.

description: ELUCIDATING FH15-MEDIATED MODULATION OF TLR4/NF-KB IN NEUTROPHILS TO SUPPRESSINFLAMMATION IN SEPSIS AND ULCERATIVE COLITIS - THE INCREASING APPLICATION OF HELMINTH ANTIGEN-DERIVED THERAPY TO PREVENT INFLAMMATORY DISEASES REPRESENTS A PROMISING AND INNOVATIVE APPROACH. OVER THE PAST DECADE, OUR RESEARCH GROUP HAS CONCENTRATED ON FH15, A RECOMBINANT MOLECULE FROM THE FASCIOLA HEPATICA FATTY ACID BINDING PROTEIN FAMILY, WHICH EXHIBITS POTENT ANTIINFLAMMATORY EFFECTS IN ANIMAL MODELS OF SEPSIS AND ULCERATIVE COLITIS. WE HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT A SINGLE INTRAPERITONEAL (I.P.) DOSE OF FH15 ADMINISTERED TO ANIMALS ONE HOUR BEFORE OR AFTER THE ADMINISTRATION OF A LETHAL DOSE OF LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDE (LPS) OR LIVE E. COLI INFUSION SIGNIFICANTLY SUPPRESSES THE CYTOKINE STORM AND OTHER INFLAMMATORY MARKERS. ADDITIONALLY, WE FOUND THAT A SINGLE I.P. DOSE OF FH15 GIVEN THREE TIMES, TWO DAYS APART, SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVES THE DISEASE ACTIVITY INDEX (DAI) IN A DEXTRAN SULFATE SODIUM (DSS)-INDUCED ULCERATIVE COLITIS MOUSE MODEL. THESE THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS CORRELATED WITH REDUCED LEVELS OF INTESTINAL INFLAMMATORY MARKERS, DIMINISHED NEUTROPHIL INFILTRATION, AND LOWER LEVELS OF MYELOPEROXIDASE—A PROTEIN ESSENTIAL FOR NEUTROPHIL EXTRACELLULAR TRAP (NET) FORMATION. FURTHERMORE, WE DEMONSTRATED THAT FH15 CAN INHIBIT NETOSIS IN HUMAN NEUTROPHILS AND ACTS AS A TLR4 ANTAGONIST, A RECEPTOR INVOLVED IN THE IMMUNE RESPONSE AGAINST SEPSIS AND ULCERATIVE COLITIS, AS WELL AS IN NEUTROPHIL ACTIVATION AND NET RELEASE. THIS APPLICATION STEMS FROM A PREVIOUS SC1 GRANT (1SC1AI155439-01), WHICH RESULTED IN ONE PATENT, APPROXIMATELY FIVE PUBLICATIONS, AND THE GRADUATION OF THREE PHD AND ONE MS STUDENTS. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS POSITS THAT FH15 MODULATES THE TLR4/NF-ÊB SIGNALING PATHWAY TO SUPPRESS INFLAMMATION IN ANIMAL MODELS OF SEPSIS AND ULCERATIVE COLITIS, WHICH IS ASSOCIATED WITH DECREASED CONCENTRATIONS OF FREE EXTRACELLULAR DNA (EDNA) AND REDUCED NETOSIS. IN THE AIM-1 WILL DEMONSTRATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE SUPPRESSION OF INFLAMMATORY MARKERS INDUCED BY FH15 IN THE SEPSIS AND ULCERATIVE COLITIS MODELS AND THE REDUCTION OF EDNA AND NETS IN VIVO. WE WILL ISOLATE FREE EDNA FROM PLASMA IN SEPSIS AND COLITIS MICE TREATED WITH FH15 AND CHARACTERIZE THE SPECIFIC PROTEIN-DNA COMPONENTS OF THIS EDNA THROUGH IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE STAINING AND CONFOCAL MICROSCOPY. THE RESULTS WILL BE CORRELATED WITH LEVELS OF INFLAMMATORY MARKERS FOR COLITIS AND SEPSIS. IN THE AIM-2 WILL IDENTIFY THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE INHIBITORY EFFECTS OF FH15 ON NETOSIS. WE WILL ISOLATE NEUTROPHILS FROM MOUSE BONE MARROW AND ANALYZE ACTIVATION MARKERS SUCH AS CD11B, CD66B, CD62L, CD64, AND FCRI USING FLOW CYTOMETRY. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL ASSESS THE EXPRESSION OF TLR4, CD14, AND PROTEINS INVOLVED IN THE NF-ÊB PATHWAY USING QPCR AND WESTERN BLOTTING. PROXIMITY LIGATION ASSAYS WILL DETERMINE WHETHER FH15 DIRECTLY INTERACTS WITH CD14 ON THESE CELLS. WE WILL ALSO EMPLOY PROTEOMICS AND SINGLE-CELL RNA SEQUENCING TO INVESTIGATE CHANGES IN PROTEIN AND GENE EXPRESSION IN NEUTROPHILS AND IDENTIFY MOLECULES INVOLVED IN PRO-INFLAMMATORY PATHWAYS THAT MAY BE REGULATED BY FH15. THE OUTCOME OF THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE A MORE COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW F. HEPATICA MOLECULES INTERACT WITH THE IMMUNE SYSTEM AND LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A NOVEL CLASS OF ANTI-INFLAMMATORY DRUGS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TONGUE DORSUM ELEVATION AND VELOPHARYNGEAL INSUFFICIENCY - PROJECT SUMMARY  CLEFT PALATE WITH OR WITHOUT CLEFT LIP (CP+/-L) IS THE MOST COMMON CONGENITAL ANOMALY, AFFECTING 1 IN EVERY 1600 BABIES BORN IN THE UNITED STATES AND APPROXIMATELY 1 IN 700 LIVE BIRTHS GLOBALLY. VELOPHARYNGEAL INSUFFICIENCY SECONDARY TO CP+/-L, A PERSISTENT DIFFICULTY IN MANAGING THE INTERACTION OF AIRFLOW BETWEEN THE ORAL AND NASAL CAVITIES, AFFECTS SPEECH INTELLIGIBILITY AND SOCIAL ACCEPTABILITY OF SPEECH 14. OVER THE LAST 50 YEARS, CLEFT AND CRANIOFACIAL CENTERS HAVE BEEN ABLE TO ACHIEVE MORE THAN A 70% SUCCESS RATE IN THE MANAGEMENT OF VELOPHARYNGEAL INSUFFICIENCY (I.E., HYPERNASALITY, NASAL AIR EMISSION) SECONDARY TO CP+/-L 14-16. DESPITE THE TREMENDOUS ADVANCES IN SURGICAL AND PROSTHETIC MANAGEMENT OF VELOPHARYNGEAL INSUFFICIENCY, NOT ALL PATIENTS WILL IMPROVE THEIR HYPERNASAL SPEECH SUFFICIENTLY17. THEREFORE, PHYSICAL (SURGERY OR PROSTHESIS) AND FUNCTIONAL (SPEECH) TREATMENTS MAY BE NECESSARY TO ACHIEVE OPTIMUM OUTCOMES13,18,19. BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS TO ESTABLISH APPROPRIATE OROPHARYNGEAL ARTICULATION AND ORAL AIRFLOW DIRECTION HAVE SO FAR FAILED TO RESULT IN A CONSISTENT REDUCTION IN THE EFFECTS OF HYPERNASALITY.20,21 YET, SOME PATIENTS WITH HYPERNASALITY DO BENEFIT FROM BEHAVIORAL TECHNIQUES, PARTICULARLY IN CASES WHERE PALATAL SURGERY IS NOT AN OPTION, SUCH AS IN INDIVIDUALS WITH MILD HYPERNASALITY, MOTOR SPEECH DISORDERS 22, AND ANATOMICAL LIMITATIONS. GIVEN THE LINKS BETWEEN RAISED TONGUE DORSUM IN PHONETICALLY NASALIZED VOWELS IN TYPICAL SPEAKERS OF LANGUAGES SUCH AS FRENCH AND ENGLISH AND THE IMPACTS OF TONGUE DORSUM ELEVATION IN REDUCING ORAL AIRFLOW DURING THE PRODUCTION OF PRESSURE-SENSITIVE SOUNDS, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED TO DETERMINE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN TONGUE POSITIONING AND DEGREES OF VELOPHARYNGEAL INSUFFICIENCY IN INDIVIDUALS WITH VELOPHARYNGEAL DYSFUNCTION. THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN TONGUE POSITIONING AND DEGREES OF VELOPHARYNGEAL INSUFFICIENCY. THIS WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED BY USING STATE-OF-THE-ART ULTRASOUND IMAGING OF TONGUE POSITION TO OBTAIN DEGREES OF TONGUE DORSUM EXCURSION IN SPEAKERS WITH CP+/-L AND VELOPHARYNGEAL INSUFFICIENCY AND COMPARE THIS TO THOSE WITHOUT VELOPHARYNGEAL INSUFFICIENCY ACROSS CERTAIN GROUPS OF SOUNDS, CONSIDERING THE VOWEL CO-ARTICULATION EFFECTS (AIM 1). IN AIM 2, THE TONGUE DORSUM ELEVATION METRICS WILL BE OBTAINED PRE- AND POST-SECONDARY PALATAL SURGERIES TO IDENTIFY IF THE POSITIONING OF THE TONGUE DORSUM WILL CHANGE IN RESPONSE TO THE CORRECTION OF VELOPHARYNGEAL INSUFFICIENCY. THIS PROJECT IS CLOSELY ALIGNED WITH NIDCD'S STRATEGIC PLAN IN THAT IT AIMS TO HARNESS ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE THE DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT OF COMMUNICATION DISORDERS THROUGH THE TRANSLATION OF DISCOVERIES INTO CLINICAL CARE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE ROLE OF DHRS9 IN DIET-INDUCED OBESITY AND DIABETES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT: OBESITY-ASSOCIATED INSULIN RESISTANCE REMAINS INADEQUATELY STUDIED. BOTH VITAMIN DEFICIENCY AND OVERCONSUMPTION LEAD TO OBESITY AND INSULIN RESISTANCE. SPECIALIZED PRO-RESOLVING MEDIATORS (SPMS) ORIGINATE FROM OMEGA-3 FATTY ACIDS AND SERVE TO TERMINATE INFLAMMATION AND INSULIN RESISTANCE. DHRS9 PLAYS DUAL ROLE IN VITAMIN A METABOLISM AND THE INACTIVATION OF SPMS IN SKIN, LUNGS, AND TRACHEA. THE ROLE OF DHRS9 IN DIET-INDUCED OBESITY AND DIABETES IS NOT EXPLORED. THE OBJECTIVES ARE TO DEFINE HOW DHRS9 MODULATES INSULIN SENSITIVITY UNDER HIGH-FAT DIET (HFD) CONDITIONS ACROSS SEXES AND DETERMINE WHETHER RETINOID OR SPMS METABOLISM IS THE DOMINANT DHRS9-REGULATED TARGET. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT DHRS9 PROMOTES INSULIN RESISTANCE BY DISTORTING LOCAL RETINOIC ACID (RA) TONE AND/OR DAMPENING PRO-RESOLVING LIPID SIGNALS; LOSS OF DHRS9 PRESERVES INSULIN ACTION, AND METABOLITE RESCUE WILL REVEAL PATHWAY DOMINANCE. THE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE TO: 1) IDENTIFY THE ROLE OF DHRS9 IN DIET-INDUCED OBESITY AND DIABETES; AND 2) ESTABLISH WHETHER RA OR OXYLIPINS CAN RESCUE THE DIFFERENTIAL RESPONSE TO HFD SEEN IN DHRS9 KNOCKOUT MICE. THE APPROACH IS TO FEED WILD-TYPE AND DHRS9 KNOCKOUT MICE ON HFD VITAMIN-A-DEFINED AIN93 DIETS. WE WILL ALSO RESCUE THESE MICE WITH ALL-TRANS RA OR SPMS. PHENOTYPICALLY, WE WILL MONITOR THEIR PHYSIOLOGICAL PROFILES IN DIET-INDUCED OBESITY AND DIABETES. MECHANISTICALLY, WE WILL CHARACTERIZE INSULIN SIGNALING AND METABOLIC PATHWAYS, AS WELL AS VITAMIN A METABOLITES AND SPMS. ELUCIDATING THE ROLE OF DHRS9 IN DIET-INDUCED OBESITY AND DIABETES IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT WILL IDENTIFY THE ROLES OF VITAMIN A AND OMEGA-3 FATTY ACIDS IN DIET-INDUCED OBESITY AND DIABETES, ADDRESSING A FUNDAMENTAL GAP IN THE CROSSTALK BETWEEN VITAMIN A METABOLISM AND OMEGA-3 FATTY ACID DERIVED SPMS, WHILE EXPANDING RESEARCH CAPACITY AT A SURE-ELIGIBLE INSTITUTION. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT REFRAMES DHRS9 AS A BIFUNCTIONAL CONTROLLER OF RA-SPMS BIOLOGY AND DEPLOYING A MECHANISTIC METABOLITE-RESCUE STRATEGY INTEGRATED WITH TIME-RESOLVED, SEX-AWARE PHYSIOLOGY AND QUANTITATIVE MEDIATOR PROFILING. IT WILL PROVIDE REFERENCE TO EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS—DIETARY VITAMIN A MODULATION AND DHRS9-TARGETED THERAPEUTICS—TO TREAT DIET- INDUCED OBESITY AND DIABETES.

description: MACHINE LEARNING-ENHANCED MOLECULAR MODELING OF NEAR-INFRARED FLUORESCENT MATERIALS FOR BIOIMAGING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT NEAR-INFRARED (NIR) FLUORESCENCE IMAGING HAS BECOME INDISPENSABLE IN MODERN MEDICINE, ENABLING REAL-TIME VISUALIZATION FOR SURGICAL GUIDANCE AND DEEP-TISSUE DIAGNOSTICS. CURRENT FDA-APPROVED PROBES ARE LIMITED TO THE NIR-I WINDOW (650–950 NM), WHERE SCATTERING AND AUTOFLUORESCENCE COMPROMISE PERFORMANCE. THE SECOND NIR WINDOW (NIR-II, 1000–1700 NM) OFFERS DEEPER PENETRATION, REDUCED BACKGROUND, AND IMPROVED SIGNAL-TO-NOISE, YET EXISTING NIR-II PROBES, INCLUDING POLYMER DOTS (PDOTS), REMAIN CONSTRAINED BY LOW QUANTUM YIELDS DUE TO AGGREGATION-CAUSED QUENCHING (ACQ) AND NARROW ENERGY BAND GAPS. THIS GAP LIMITS CLINICAL TRANSLATION OF OTHERWISE PROMISING PDOTS, WHICH UNIQUELY COMBINE EXCEPTIONAL BRIGHTNESS, PHOTOSTABILITY, AND BIOCOMPATIBILITY. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THESE BARRIERS THROUGH MACHINE LEARNING (ML)–ENHANCED MOLECULAR MODELING INTEGRATED WITH MULTISCALE SIMULATIONS. THE OVERARCHING OBJECTIVE IS TO ESTABLISH PREDICTIVE DESIGN RULES FOR DONOR–ACCEPTOR COPOLYMERS THAT YIELD BRIGHT, STABLE, AND BIOCOMPATIBLE NIR-II PDOTS. THREE COMPLEMENTARY AIMS WILL BE PURSUED: (1) DEVELOP SUPERVISED ML MODELS TO EFFICIENTLY PREDICT ELECTRONIC COUPLING, A KEY QUANTUM DESCRIPTOR OF ACQ, ACROSS MILLIONS OF MOLECULAR DYNAMICS–SAMPLED CONFIGURATIONS; (2) APPLY UNSUPERVISED ML METHODS, INCLUDING DIMENSIONALITY REDUCTION AND FEATURE-EXTRACTION NETWORKS, TO IDENTIFY BACKBONE CONFORMATIONS THAT GOVERN BAND GAPS AND ORBITAL DISTRIBUTIONS CRITICAL FOR NIR-II EMISSION; AND (3) CURATE HIGH-LEVEL AB INITIO DATASETS OF OPTOELECTRONIC DESCRIPTORS FOR DONOR AND ACCEPTOR BUILDING BLOCKS, INTEGRATING THEM WITH EXPERIMENTAL MEASUREMENTS AND DATA-DRIVEN OPTIMIZATION TO DISCOVER PROMISING COPOLYMER FRAMEWORKS. BY UNITING ML WITH PHYSICS-BASED MODELING, THE PROJECT WILL OVERCOME COMPUTATIONAL BOTTLENECKS, REPLACE TRIAL-AND-ERROR SYNTHESIS WITH PREDICTIVE DESIGN, AND ESTABLISH TRANSFERABLE PRINCIPLES FOR NIR-II MATERIALS. OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE OPEN DATASETS, INTERPRETABLE ML MODELS, AND SYSTEMATIC GUIDELINES FOR SUPPRESSING ACQ AND ENHANCING EMISSION EFFICIENCY. THESE ADVANCES WILL ACCELERATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEXT-GENERATION FLUORESCENT PROBES FOR IMAGE- GUIDED SURGERY, ONCOLOGY, AND CARDIOVASCULAR INTERVENTIONS. BEYOND SCIENTIFIC IMPACT, THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE INTERDISCIPLINARY TRAINING AT THE INTERFACE OF CHEMISTRY, MATERIALS SCIENCE, AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, PREPARING STUDENTS FOR CAREERS IN AI-ENABLED BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ELUCIDATING THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF CANNABIDIOL (CBD) IN ALCOHOL DEPENDENCE: TARGETING NEUROADAPTATIONS IN THE BASOLATERAL AMYGDALA - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ALCOHOL DEPENDENCE AND WITHDRAWAL ARE ASSOCIATED WITH SIGNIFICANT NEUROADAPTATIONS IN THE BRAIN, PARTICULARLY WITHIN THE BASOLATERAL AMYGDALA (BLA). CANNABIDIOL (CBD) HAS SHOWN PROMISE IN MODULATING THESE NEUROADAPTATIONS, POTENTIALLY PROVIDING THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS FOR ALCOHOL USE DISORDERS. THIS PROPOSAL OUTLINES A COMPREHENSIVE INVESTIGATION INTO THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE EFFECTS OF CBD ON ALCOHOL-INDUCED NEUROADAPTATIONS IN THE BLA DURING ACUTE WITHDRAWAL AND PROTRACTED ABSTINENCE FROM ALCOHOL. SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF CHRONIC CBD TREATMENT ON GABAERGIC AND GLUTAMATERGIC TRANSMISSION IN BLA NEURONS OF NAIVE ANIMALS AND THOSE DURING ACUTE WITHDRAWAL FROM ALCOHOL. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL EXAMINE THE EFFECTS OF CBD ON WITHDRAWAL-INDUCED FOS ACTIVATION AND CANNABINOID RECEPTOR LEVELS. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL BUILD UPON THESE FINDINGS, INVESTIGATING THE LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF CBD ON THE BLA DURING PROTRACTED ABSTINENCE FROM ALCOHOL. WE WILL EXPLORE THE IMPACT OF CBD ON ALCOHOL-INDUCED NEUROADAPTATION IN THE BLA OF ANIMALS WITH A HISTORY OF ALCOHOL DEPENDENCE, NOW IN A PROLONGED ABSTINENCE PERIOD. THE PROPOSED EXPERIMENTS UTILIZE A COMBINATION OF ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL RECORDINGS, RNA SCOPE, AND IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY TECHNIQUES TO PROVIDE A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF THE EFFECTS OF CBD ON ALCOHOL- INDUCED NEUROADAPTATIONS IN THE BLA. BY ELUCIDATING THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING CBD'S INFLUENCE ON ALCOHOL-RELATED NEUROADAPTATIONS, THIS RESEARCH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR ALCOHOL USE DISORDERS AND PROMOTE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE POTENTIAL BENEFITS OF CBD IN THE TREATMENT OF ADDICTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CHAPERONE-MEDIATED AUTOPHAGY IN AGING-ASSOCIATED CARDIOVASCULAR FIBROSIS - ABSTRACT:  AGING IS ASSOCIATED WITH ACTIVATION OF PERIVASCULAR AND INTERSTITIAL CARDIAC FIBROBLASTS LEADING TO THE DEPOSITION OF LARGE AMOUNTS OF CROSS-LINKED EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX IN THE HEART AND IN THE LARGE ARTERIES. FIBROSIS IN AGING HEARTS IS ASSOCIATED WITH A UNIQUE PERTURBATION OF THE FIBROBLAST PHENOTYPE THAT REDUCES TURNOVER OF MATRIX PROTEINS, IN THE ABSENCE OF ANY CHANGES IN NEW COLLAGEN TRANSCRIPTION. CHAPERONE-MEDIATED AUTOPHAGY (CMA), THE MOST SELECTIVE FORM OF AUTOPHAGY CAN SELECTIVELY REMOVE SPECIFIC PROTEINS TO TERMINATE THEIR FUNCTION, REGULATING A RANGE OF CELLULAR PROCESSES, INCLUDING SURVIVAL, PROLIFERATION, AND DIFFERENTIATION. CMA EXHIBITS A MARKED DECLINE IN AGING TISSUES IN BOTH RODENT MODELS AND IN HUMAN CELLS THAT MAY PERTURB PROTEOME RENEWAL AND CAUSE DEFECTIVE ORGAN FUNCTION. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT DEVELOPMENT OF FIBROSIS IN AGING HEARTS IS ASSOCIATED WITH A DECLINE IN FIBROBLAST CMA ACTIVITY. ACCORDINGLY, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE AGE-RELATED CMA DECLINE IN FIBROBLASTS MEDIATES PROGRESSIVE FIBROTIC REMODELING IN AGING HEART AND VESSELS, PROMOTING DIASTOLIC DYSFUNCTION AND CONTRIBUTING TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF HEART FAILURE.  THE HYPOTHESIS WILL BE TESTED IN 3 SPECIFIC AIMS:  SPECIFIC AIM 1: TO EXAMINE THE TIME COURSE OF FIBROBLAST CMA DECLINE IN AGING HEARTS AND TO STUDY THE EFFECTS OF FIBROBLAST-SPECIFIC CMA DISRUPTION IN AGE-ASSOCIATED CARDIOVASCULAR FIBROSIS AND DYSFUNCTION. THE TIME COURSE OF FIBROBLAST CMA DECLINE IN AGING HEARTS AND VESSELS WILL BE STUDIED USING CMA REPORTER KFERQ-DENDRA MICE. MICE WITH FIBROBLAST-SPECIFIC DISRUPTION OF LAMP2A, THE CRITICAL LYSOSOMAL MEMBRANE PROTEIN INVOLVED IN BINDING AND INTERNALIZATION OF CMA SUBSTRATES, WILL BE USED TO EXAMINE THE ROLE OF FIBROBLAST CMA IN CARDIOVASCULAR AGING.  SPECIFIC AIM 2: TO EXAMINE THE EFFECTS OF FIBROBLAST-SPECIFIC CMA ACTIVATION IN DELAYING AGE-ASSOCIATED FIBROTIC CARDIAC AND VASCULAR REMODELING AND DYSFUNCTION. MICE WITH FIBROBLAST-SPECIFIC OVEREXPRESSION OF LAMP2A WILL BE USED TO STUDY THE EFFECTS OF FIBROBLAST CMA ACTIVATION ON CARDIAC AND VASCULAR AGING.  SPECIFIC AIM 3: TO DISSECT THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE EFFECTS OF CMA FAILURE ON AGING-ASSOCIATED FIBROSIS AND DYSFUNCTION AND TO IDENTIFY CMA TARGETS IN AGING MOUSE CARDIAC FIBROBLASTS. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGEST POTENTIAL EFFECTS OF CMA DISRUPTION ON THE NF-B CASCADE, MEDIATED THROUGH ACCUMULATION OF THE IB KINASE.  OUR PROPOSAL WILL TEST A NOVEL CONCEPT THAT MAY HAVE MAJOR IMPLICATIONS IN THE PATHOGENESIS OF AGING-ASSOCIATED HEART FAILURE AND MAY SUGGEST PROMISING THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BIDIRECTIONAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN PLASMA TAU PHOSPHORYLATION MARKERS AND POSTOPERATIVE DELIRIUM - PROJECT SUMMARY POST-OPERATIVE DELIRIUM (POD) AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) INCREASE THE RISK FOR ONE ANOTHER, WHICH SUGGESTS A BIDIRECTIONAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN POD AND AD. THIS RELATIONSHIP CAN BE EXPLORED USING NEW BLOOD-BASED BIOMARKERS FOR AD PATHOLOGY, SUCH AS THREONINE-217 PHOSPHORYLATED TAU (PTAU217) PROTEIN, WHICH ARE POISED TO TRANSFORM AD DETECTION, DIAGNOSIS, AND PROGNOSTICATION. A CRITICAL GAP IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN POD AND AD IS HOW AD PATHOLOGY, REFLECTED BY THESE BIOMARKERS, MAY INCREASE POD RISK AND HOW POD MAY IMPACT THE LONGITUDINAL TRAJECTORIES OF NEW AD BIOMARKERS, AND, THUS, AD PATHOLOGY. THIS APPLICATION RESPONDS SPECIFICALLY TO NOT-AG-24-030, WHICH SEEKS STUDIES THAT “ADDRESS SHORTCOMINGS OF CURRENTLY USED [AD] BIOMARKERS,…FURTHER [CHARACTERIZE AD] BIOMARKERS,…[AND/OR] IDENTIFY…A DEMENTIA/COGNITION ‘STRESS’ TEST.” WE PROPOSE THAT ELECTIVE SURGERY CAN BE VIEWED AS A “STRESS TEST” FOR THE AGING BRAIN BECAUSE SURGICAL STRESS MAY “UNMASK” NEUROCOGNITIVE VULNERABILITY, EG, DUE TO AD-SPECIFIC PATHOLOGY, RESULTING IN POD. FURTHER, WE PROPOSE THAT POD MAY ALTER THE “AD CLOCK,” A MODEL THAT PREDICTS TIME TO ONSET OF AD SYMPTOMS BASED ON LEVELS OF AD BIOMARKERS, SUCH AS PTAU217. WE POSIT THAT AFTER POD, THE AD CLOCK MAY BEGIN TO TICK—CONSISTENT WITH THE START OF ACCUMULATING AD PATHOLOGY—OR THE CLOCK MAY BEGIN TO TICK FASTER—INDICATING AN ACCELERATION IN AD PATHOLOGICAL PROGRESSION DENOTED BY A FASTER-THAN-EXPECTED RISE IN AD BIOMARKER LEVELS AFTER POD. OUR RATIONALE FOR STUDYING THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN POD AND AD-SPECIFIC PLASMA BIOMARKERS, IE PTAU217, IS TO BETTER CHARACTERIZE (A) THE EXTENT TO WHICH SURGICAL STRESS UNMASKS AD-SPECIFIC PATHOLOGY (IE, PRE-OP PTAU217) IN POD; AND (B) THE EXTENT TO WHICH POD MAY INFLUENCE AD BIOMARKER TRAJECTORIES. THESE INSIGHTS WILL ENHANCE OUR ABILITY TO PREDICT, PROGNOSTICATE, AND DEVELOP INTERVENTIONS FOR BOTH POD AND AD. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO DETERMINE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN POD AND PTAU217 LEVELS USING OUR PRE-EXISTING COHORT OF 195 SURGERY PATIENTS  65Y. IN THIS UNIQUE COHORT, 35% OF PARTICIPANTS HAD MONTREAL COGNITIVE ASSESSMENT (MOCA) SCORES CONSISTENT WITH MILD COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT (MCI), AND MORE THAN A THIRD HAD POD. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT PRE-OP PTAU217 LEVELS CORRELATE WITH POD (AIM 1) AND THAT POD IS ASSOCIATED WITH GREATER LONG-TERM INCREASE IN PTAU217, REFLECTING FASTER AD PATHOLOGY ACCUMULATION OVER MONTHS TO YEARS POSTOP. (AIM 2). SECONDARY ANALYSES WILL EVALUATE ADDITIONAL BLOOD-BASED AD BIOMARKERS. SENSITIVITY ANALYSES WILL EVALUATE MCI AND NON-MCI PATIENTS SEPARATELY. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS STUDY WILL (A) IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF THE BIDIRECTIONAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN POD AND AD; (B) ADVANCE THE CHARACTERIZATION, DIAGNOSIS, AND PREDICTION OF AD AND POD, USING NEW AD PLASMA BIOMARKERS AND ELECTIVE SURGERY AS AN AD STRESS TEST, AND (C) YIELD EVIDENCE TO GUIDE FUTURE STUDIES OF SHARED AD-POD MECHANISMS, POTENTIAL THERAPEUTICS, POD PREDICTORS (EG, PTAU217) AND AD PROGNOSTICATION (EG, VIA REFINED AD CLOCK MODELS). CLINICALLY, BETTER POD PREDICTION CAN OPTIMIZE ALLOCATION OF LIMITED RESOURCES FOR POD PREVENTION, AND IMPROVED AD PROGNOSTICATION CAN HELP PATIENTS AND THEIR FAMILIES WITH FUTURE PLANNING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REAL-LIFE DUAL-TASK TRAINING FOR OLDER ADULTS AT RISK TO FALL: A PILOT CLINICAL TRIAL - ONE IN FOUR OLDER ADULTS REPORTED A FALL IN THE LAST YEAR. THESE FALLS CAN RESULT IN NEGATIVE CONSEQUENCES ON HEALTH, QUALITY OF LIFE, AND PARTICIPATION IN MEANINGFUL ACTIVITIES. DOING TWO THINGS AT ONCE (I.E., DUAL-TASKING) INCREASES THE RISK OF FALLING FOR OLDER ADULTS. ADDITIONALLY, DUAL-TASKING BECOMES INCREASINGLY DIFFICULT FOR OLDER ADULTS AS THE COMPLEXITY OF A TASK INCREASES. DUAL-TASK TRAINING CAN IMPROVE THE ABILITY OF OLDER ADULTS TO DO TWO THINGS AT ONCE BY PROVIDING TRAINING IN ISOLATING AND SHIFTING ATTENTIONAL FOCUS BETWEEN TASKS AND THEIR COMPONENTS (E.G., COGNITIVE AND MOTOR COMPONENTS OF TASKS). WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT DUAL-TASK TRAINING EMBEDDED IN REAL-LIFE ACTIVITIES WILL RESULT IN IMPROVED DUAL-TASK PERFORMANCE, REDUCED FALL RISK, AND BETTER PARTICIPATION IN EVERYDAY ACTIVITIES (INSTRUMENTAL ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING [IADLS]) FOR OLDER ADULTS.   THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS STUDY IS TO ASSESS FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY AND SIGNAL OF EFFICACY OF A NOVEL 6-WEEK REAL- LIFE DUAL-TASK TRAINING INTERVENTION (REAL-DTT) INTERVENTION COMPARED TO A 6-WEEK EVIDENCE-BASED FALL PREVENTION INTERVENTION (FALLSTALK®). REAL-DTT WILL INCLUDE OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY WITH IADLS USING FOUR PROTOCOLIZED LEVELS (INCREASING IN TASK COMPLEXITY) OF COGNITIVE SKILLS, AND FOUR PROTOCOLIZED LEVELS OF MOTOR SKILLS FOR EACH OF THE INCLUDED IADLS (E.G., LAUNDRY, MEAL PREPARATION, CLEANING, SHOPPING, MEDICATION MANAGEMENT, PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION, DISHES/MEAL CLEAN-UP, AND MONEY MANAGEMENT). ADDITIONALLY, PARTICIPANTS WILL COMPLETE A STRUCTURED DEBRIEF ACTIVITY TO IDENTIFY HIGHER RISK FALL BEHAVIORS WITHIN IADL EXPERIENCES AND REFLECT ON WHEN THEY FOCUS ON THE MOTOR TASK VS. WHEN THEY FOCUS ON THE COGNITIVE TASK. FALLSTALK® IS AN EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIOR- CHANGE INTERVENTION THAT VARIES BASED ON THE FALL RISKS IDENTIFIED BY EACH INDIVIDUAL. IN THIS CLINICAL TRIAL, OLDER ADULTS AT RISK TO FALL (N= 66 ENROLLED, N=54 COMPLETERS) WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO REAL-DTT OR FALLSTALK®.   THE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE TO 1) ASSESS FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF THE REAL-DTT AND FALLSTALK® INTERVENTIONS AND DESCRIBE ANY DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THE INTERVENTIONS, AND 2) DETERMINE CHANGES ON DUAL-TASK PERFORMANCE (PRIMARY OUTCOME), FALL RISK, AND IADL PERFORMANCE, BETWEEN GROUPS (REAL-DTT AND FALLSTALK®) AND WITHIN GROUPS (PRE-ASSESSMENT TO POST-ASSESSMENT). OUR EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE DATA ON FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND SIGNAL OF EFFICACY OF THE NOVEL REAL-DTT INTERVENTION. THE RESULTS WILL SUPPORT APPROPRIATE MODIFICATIONS TO THE REAL-DTT INTERVENTION, DETERMINE NUMBER OF PARTICIPANTS NEEDED FOR FUTURE TRIALS, CONSIDER REFINED OUTCOME MEASURES, AND ALLOW FOR AN OPTIMIZED VERSION OF THE REAL-DTT. ULTIMATELY, IN ALIGNMENT WITH THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE ON AGING STRATEGIC PRIORITIES, THE REAL-DTT INTERVENTION WILL BE DESIGNED TO REDUCE FALL RISK AND IMPROVE PARTICIPATION IN IADLS TO PROMOTE WELL-BEING (PROMOTING EFFECTIVE/SAFE PARTICIPATION) AND INDEPENDENCE OF OLDER ADULTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ESTABLISHING INTERACTION POLYGENIC RISK SCORES FOR BLOOD OMEGA-3 FATTY ACIDS AND GENETIC VARIANTS ON INCIDENT ALL-CAUSE DEMENTIA AND ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - MODIFIED PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SECTION  THERE IS AN INCREASING INTEREST IN BEHAVIORAL APPROACHES TO SLOW AD/ADRD PROGRESSION. NOTABLY,  EVIDENCE IS EMERGING ABOUT THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DIET AT MID-LIFE AND INCIDENT AD/ADRD, WITH  PARTICULAR INTEREST IN THE ROLE OF THE OMEGA-3 FATTY ACID DOCOSAHEXAENOIC ACID (DHA). DHA IS A  PROMISING NUTRIENT DUE TO ITS ENRICHMENT IN BRAIN TISSUE BEGINNING IN UTERO, WITH RECENT  EXPERIMENTAL STUDIES REPORTING THAT DHA CAN AMELIORATE SEVERAL FEATURES ASSOCIATED WITH  AD/ADRD (I.E., AMYLOID-BETA PEPTIDE AGGREGATION, BRAIN GLUCOSE HYPOMETABOLISM,  NEUROINFLAMMATION) AND EMERGING EVIDENCE FROM SOME PROSPECTIVE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL STUDIES  SHOWING THAT HIGHER DHA INTAKES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH REDUCED RISK OF AD/ADRD. DESPITE THIS  PROMISING EVIDENCE, SOME PROSPECTIVE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL STUDIES HAVE BEEN UNABLE TO DETECT  ASSOCIATION WITH DHA LEVELS. OUR GROUP HAS BEEN AT THE FOREFRONT OF SEEKING WAYS TO EXPLAIN THESE  DIFFERENTIAL RESEARCH RESULTS. OUR PRELIMINARY RESULTS SUGGEST THAT THE USE OF BLOOD DHA LEVELS, AND  THE RECOGNITION THAT DHA MAY BE MORE IMPORTANT FOR SOME INDIVIDUALS DEPENDING ON THE GENETIC  BACKGROUND, MAY EXPLAIN THE HETEROGENEITY IN RESEARCH EVIDENCE ON THE IMPORTANCE OF DHA TO  DATE. DHA REMAINS AN IMPORTANT TARGET FOR POTENTIAL FUTURE BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTION BECAUSE LEVELS  OF DHA IN THE BRAIN ARE ALMOST EXCLUSIVELY ATTAINED FROM ITS DIETARY INTAKE. IDENTIFYING INDIVIDUALS  WHO, BASED ON THEIR GENETIC PROFILE, WILL BENEFIT THE MOST FROM INCREASING DIETARY DHA IS AN URGENT  PUBLIC HEALTH PRIORITY. HOWEVER, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT, BESIDES APOE-Ε4, THERE ARE OTHER GENETIC  VARIANTS THAT INTERACT WITH BLOOD DHA LEVELS AS PREDICTORS OF AD/ADRD. THUS, OUR INTERNATIONALLY  RECOGNIZED GROUP OF OMEGA-3 FA, GENETIC AND COGNITION EXPERTS WILL: (AIM 1) IDENTIFY GENETIC  VARIANTS THAT INTERACT WITH BLOOD DHA AS PREDICTORS OF INCIDENT ALL-CAUSE DEMENTIA (PRIMARY  ENDPOINT) AND AD (SECONDARY ENDPOINT). WE WILL BEGIN BY POOLING AVAILABLE DATA FROM 4 WELL STUDIED, HIGHLY REPUTABLE PROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDIES. DATA HARMONIZATION WILL YIELD A SAMPLE OF  OVER 515,000 PARTICIPANTS AGED 40 YEARS OR OVER AT BASELINE, N>11,000 CASES OF ALL-CAUSE  DEMENTIA, AND N>5,000 CASES OF INCIDENT PROBABLE AD, WITH AVAILABLE GENOME- WIDE GENETIC DATA.  WE WILL THEN PERFORM GENOME-WIDE INTERACTION ANALYSES IN TWO TIERS: (TIER 1) CANDIDATE SINGLE  NUCLEOTIDE POLYMORPHISMS (SNPS), I.E., THOSE ALREADY KNOWN TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH INCIDENT AD,  AD PATHWAYS OR AD BIOMARKERS, (TIER 2) DE NOVO SNPS WITH NO PRIOR EVIDENCE OF ASSOCIATION.  AIM 2. DEVELOP A PRELIMINARY INTERACTION POLYGENIC RISK SCORE (IPRS): SNPS SHOWING EVIDENCE OF  INTERACTION IN AIM 1 WILL BE COMBINED INTO A PRELIMINARY IPRS. AIM 3. QUANTIFY THE PREDICTIVE ABILITY  OF THE IPRS IN PRESPECIFIED STRATA: BY RACE, BY SEX, BY APOE-Ε4 CARRIERSHIP, AND BY DECADE OF LIFE  AT ENROLLMENT (40-49; 50-59; 60-69; 70+ YEARS). WE WILL IDENTIFY GENETIC VARIANTS THAT SHOW  PRELIMINARY EVIDENCE OF INTERACTION WITH DHA STATUS IN RISK FOR INCIDENT ALL-CAUSE DEMENTIA AND  INCIDENT PROBABLE AD AND WILL QUANTIFY THEIR CUMULATIVE IMPACT VIA IPRSS. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE  KEY EVIDENCE ABOUT THE ROLE OF PRECISION NUTRITION IN THE PREVENTION OF AD/ADRD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MACROPHAGE SPATIAL HETEROGENEITY IN REGULATING HEMATOPOIETIC AGING - ABSTRACT INFLAMMATION THAT OCCURS WITH AGE (INFLAMM-AGING) INDUCES HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELL (HSC) DIVISION WITH COMPROMISED FITNESS. HOWEVER, WE HAVE OBSERVED THAT HSCS WITHIN A SUBSET OF MARROW CAVITIES THAT LACK BONE RESORPTION ACTIVITY STAYED SOLITARY DESPITE ACTIVATION FROM INFLAMMATORY STRESS INCLUDING AGING. THESE RESULTS SUGGEST THE EXISTENCE OF A PROTECTIVE MICROENVIRONMENT IN THE NON-RESORPTIVE (NR) CAVITIES THAT SHELTERS HSCS UNDER SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION AND MAY PROTECT THEM FROM INFLAMM-AGING. LEVERAGING INTRAVITAL MICROSCOPY (IVM) AND A HSC REPORTER MOUSE (MDS1GFP;FLT3CRE, MFG), WE FOUND RESIDENT MACROPHAGES (MF) IN RESORPTIVE (RE) CAVITIES FREQUENTLY RETRIEVE CELLULAR CARGOS FROM HSCS AND RESEMBLE THE PRO-INFLAMMATORY MF PHENOTYPES IN AGED MICE. RE-RESIDENT HSCS DIVIDED INTO PAIRED DAUGHTER CELLS AFTER INTERACTING WITH MF. IN CONTRAST, NR- RESIDENT HSCS APPEAR AS NON-MOTILE SINGLETS CUDDLED BY MF BUT THIS NR-TYPE INTERACTIONS ARE DIMINISHED IN AGED MICE. ONE MECHANISM OF HSC ACCUMULATION IN AGING IS THE INCLINATION OF AGED HSCS TO DIVIDE SYMMETRICALLY- DAUGHTER CELLS CARRY THE SAME FATE BUT WITH COMPROMISED LONG-TERM REGENERATIVE POTENTIAL. INTERESTINGLY, MFG- HSCS FROM RE CAVITIES SHOWED TENDENCIES OF SYMMETRICAL DIVISION. KNOWLEDGE ON DIVISION SYMMETRY IS PRIMARILY CELL-INTRINSIC. THESE RESULTS LED TO OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT NR- AND RE-RESIDENT MF REGULATE HSC DIVISION SYMMETRY AND THE FITNESS LANDSCAPE OF AGED HSCS. WE DEVELOPED IVM-BASED METHODOLOGIES THAT CAN INTERROGATE TRANSCRIPTOMES AND FUNCTIONS OF CAVITY-RESIDENT CELLS. LEVERAGING THIS TECHNICAL INNOVATION, IN AIM1, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT MF-HSC INTERACTIONS IN RE CAVITIES PREDISPOSE HSCS TO SYMMETRIC DIVISION. WE WILL TRACK FEATURES OF DIVISION SYMMETRY DIRECITLY VIA IN VIVO IMAGING. THIS WILL BE BASED ON THE SYMMETRY OF SUBCELLULAR ALLOCATION AND MORPHOMETRY OF DAUGHTER CELLS, AS WELL AS STEMNESS AND DIFFERENTIATION MARKERS. TO LINK IMAGING OBSERVATION TO HSC PROPERTIES, CAVITY-RESIDENT HSCS WILL ALSO BE ISOLATED FOR TRANSCRIPTOMIC ASSAYS. IN AIM2, WE WILL INTERROGATE MICROENVIRONMENT MECHANISMS UNDERLYING FUNCTIONAL DIFFERENCES OF HSCS. IN AIM2A, WE WILL ISOLATE RE- VS. NR- RESIDENT MF THAT HAS TAKEN UP CELLULAR MATERIALS FROM GFP+ HSCS UNDER IVM IMAGE GUIDANCE. SINGLE-CELL RNA-SEQ WILL BE PERFORMED TO EVALUATE MF COMPOSITION AND DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION BETWEEN NR VS. RE CAVITIES AND ADULT VS. AGE GROUPS. IN AIM2B, WE WILL MODULATE THE DIFFERENTIALLY EXPRESSED PATHWAYS IDENTIFIED IN AIM2A USING SMALL MOLECULES AND MF-SPECIFIC (CSF1R-CRE) DELETION, AND TEST WHETHER IT ALTERS THE FREQUENCY OF MF-HSC INTERACTIONS, DIVISION SYMMETRY, AND REGENERATIVE POTENTIAL OF AGED HSCS. TAKEN TOGETHER, INFLAMM-AGING IS A WIDELY RECOGNIZED FACTOR THAT COMPROMISES HSC POTENCY. LEVERAGING THE TECHNICAL INNOVATIONS, WE SHOWED THAT SPATIALLY HETEROGENEOUS MF INTERACT WITH HSCS THROUGH CELLULAR CARGO TRANSFER. THIS YIELDS DISTINCT HSC FUNCTION UNDER INFLAMMATORY STRESS POTENTIALLY VIA REGULATING DIVISION SYMMETRY. ELUCIDATING THESE MECHANISMS IN SPATIAL CONTEXT WILL MARKEDLY ADVANCE THE FIELD AND PROVIDE TARGETABLE AND POTENTIALLY MORE UNIVERSAL MECHANISMS TO COUNTERACT HEMATOPOIETIC AGING. 1

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AFFECTIVE FORECASTING AND TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING ACROSS ADULTHOOD - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE TENDENCY TO DEVALUE DELAYED REWARDS IN FAVOR OF MORE IMMEDIATE REWARDS, KNOWN AS TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING, HAS SERIOUS IMPLICATIONS FOR HEALTH BEHAVIOR AND OUTCOMES. DEVELOPING STRATEGIES TO REDUCE TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING IS THEREFORE CRUCIAL. HOWEVER, EXISTING INTERVENTIONS HAVE NOT BEEN SUCCESSFUL IN EITHER HEALTHY OLDER ADULTS OR THOSE SUFFERING FROM NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS LIKE ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO ADDRESS THIS CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAP BY INVESTIGATING ANOTHER POTENTIAL STRATEGY FOR REDUCING TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING––AFFECTIVE FORECASTING. AFFECTIVE FORECASTING, OR PREDICTING ONE’S FEELINGS ABOUT RECEIVING A FUTURE OUTCOME, IS PROMISING BECAUSE IT RELIES ON PSYCHOLOGICAL AND BRAIN MECHANISMS THAT ARE PRESERVED IN OLDER AGE. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF THIS PROPOSAL IS THAT ENGAGING IN AFFECTIVE FORECASTING DURING DECISION MAKING MAY EFFECTIVELY REDUCE TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING, PARTICULARLY IN OLDER ADULTS. THIS HYPOTHESIS WILL BE TESTED BY PURSUING TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) DETERMINE THE EXTENT TO WHICH SPONTANEOUS PREDICTED FEELINGS ARE RELATED TO TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING AND IF AGE MODERATES THIS RELATIONSHIP, AND 2) DETERMINE IF ENGAGING IN DIRECTED AFFECTIVE FORECASTING CAN REDUCE TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING ACROSS ADULTHOOD. WE WILL INVESTIGATE THESE AIMS USING TWO STUDIES WITH PARTICIPANTS AGED 25-85. BOTH STUDIES WILL USE BINNED RECRUITMENT TO CREATE SAMPLES EQUALLY DISTRIBUTED ACROSS THE LIFESPAN. IN STUDY 1, PARTICIPANTS (N = 200) RECRUITED ONLINE WILL COMPLETE A WELL-ESTABLISHED INTERTEMPORAL CHOICE TASK WHERE THEY DECIDE BETWEEN SMALLER, SOONER AND LARGER, LATER MONETARY REWARDS. THEN, PARTICIPANTS WILL PREDICT HOW THEY WOULD FEEL IF THEY RECEIVED THE DELAYED REWARDS AT THE SPECIFIED TIME. THREE OF THESE REWARDS WILL BE REALIZED AFTER THE STATED TIME DELAY, AND PARTICIPANTS WILL PROVIDE IN-THE-MOMENT FEELING RATINGS UPON RECEIVING THE REWARD, USING A SMARTPHONE-BASED APP. THIS WILL ALLOW US TO INVESTIGATE THE ACCURACY OF AFFECTIVE FORECASTING FOR DELAYED MONETARY REWARDS AND ITS RELATIONSHIP WITH TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING. IN STUDY 2, PARTICIPANTS (N = 100) WILL BE RECRUITED TO AN IN-PERSON STUDY. HALF OF THE PARTICIPANTS WILL BE ASSIGNED TO COMPLETE AN INTERTEMPORAL CHOICE TASK IN WHICH THEY ENGAGE IN AFFECTIVE FORECASTING BEFORE MAKING EACH CHOICE. THIS AFFECTIVE FORECASTING CONDITION WILL ENTAIL ASKING PARTICIPANTS TO PREDICT THEIR FUTURE FEELINGS ABOUT RECEIVING A FUTURE REWARD AT THE TIME OF CHOICE. THE OTHER HALF OF THE PARTICIPANTS WILL COMPLETE A CLASSIC INTERTEMPORAL CHOICE TASK. WE WILL EXAMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THIS NEW STRATEGY AND THE ROLE OF AGE IN ITS EFFICACY. THIS RESEARCH IS EXPECTED TO YIELD CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN AFFECTIVE FORECASTING AND TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING AND HOW THESE PROCESSES ARE IMPACTED BY AGE. CONSISTENT WITH THE NIH STAGE MODEL FOR BASIC SCIENCE RESEARCH, THIS R21 PROPOSAL PROVIDES FOUNDATIONAL WORK NECESSARY FOR SUBSEQUENT R01 INVESTIGATIONS THAT WILL COMPARATIVELY EVALUATE AFFECTIVE FORECASTING AGAINST ESTABLISHED TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING INTERVENTIONS, DETERMINE THE EFFICACY FOR HEALTH-RELATED OUTCOMES, AND EXAMINE THESE MECHANISMS WITHIN CLINICAL POPULATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING INTER-ORGANELLE DYNAMICS DURING AGING - PROJECT SUMMARY WITHIN EUKARYOTIC CELLS, SPECIALIZED COMPARTMENTS KNOWN AS ORGANELLES ARE MEMBRANE BOUND UNITS THAT ALLOW FOR DISTINCT BIOCHEMICAL REACTIONS TO OCCUR. ALTHOUGH THE METABOLIC FUNCTION OF INDIVIDUAL ORGANELLES IS WELL ESTABLISHED, THE CELL MUST COORDINATE THE ACTIVITY OF THESE ORGANELLES TO MAINTAIN CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS. HOWEVER, THEIR COMPARTMENTAL NATURE PRESENTS A CHALLENGE TO THE CELL. SITES OF INTER-ORGANELLE CONTACTS ARE BECOMING INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED FOR THEIR IMPORTANCE IN MAINTAINING CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS. INDEED, ORGANELLES DO NOT ACT AS AUTONOMOUS ISOLATED UNITS BUT DYNAMICALLY INTERACT WITH ONE ANOTHER BY FORMING TRANSIENT CONTACTS. THESE CONTACT SITES FORM PLATFORMS THAT MEDIATE SIGNALING, THE TRANSFER OF MATERIALS (E.G., CA2+ AND PHOSPHOLIPIDS) AND PROMOTE ORGANELLE MORPHOLOGY CHANGES. AS ORGANELLE FITNESS IS CRITICAL FOR CELLULAR HEALTH, INTER-ORGANELLE COMMUNICATION IS VITAL FOR THE CELL TO ADAPT TO INTRA- AND EXTRACELLULAR STRESSES TO MAINTAIN CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS. WHILE ORGANELLULAR FITNESS HAS BEEN SHOWN TO DECLINE WITH AGE, THE ROLE OF INTER-ORGANELLE COMMUNICATION IN THIS DECLINE IS NOT KNOWN. MOREOVER, ORGANELLES UNDERGO MORPHOLOGICAL CHANGES DURING AGING AND IN AGE-RELATED DISEASES, YET THE REASONS HAVE REMAINED UNCLEAR. HERE, UNDER THE R21 NIH EXPLORATORY/DEVELOPMENTAL RESEARCH GRANT PROGRAM (PA-25-304), WE PROPOSE TO UTILIZE THE STRENGTHS OF C. ELEGANS, E.G., SHORT LIFESPAN, OPTICAL CLARITY AND GENETIC AMENABILITY, TO DETERMINE THE SPATIAL CONTEXT OF INTER-ORGANELLE COMMUNICATION TO IDENTIFY ORGANELLULAR SIGNATURES THAT DEVELOP DURING AGING AND PROTEOSTASIS DECLINE. THESE STUDIES WILL ESTABLISH A PLATFORM TO UNDERSTAND THE IMPACT AGING HAS ON ORGANELLE INTERACTIONS AND FUNCTION.
