description: LONG-TERM IMPACTS OF NATURAL DISASTERS ON PRIMARY CARE PROVIDER AVAILABILITY AND UTILIZATION - PROJECT ABSTRACT OVER 60 MILLION PEOPLE IN THE U.S. RESIDE IN HURRICANE-PRONE AREAS, POSING SIGNIFICANT THREATS TO HEALTHCARE INFRASTRUCTURE AND DELIVERY. DESPITE THEIR POTENTIAL FOR LONG-TERM DISRUPTION, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THEIR LASTING IMPACT ON PRIMARY CARE SERVICES AND UTILIZATION, WHICH ARE ESSENTIAL FOR PREVENTIVE SERVICES AND CHRONIC DISEASE MANAGEMENT. THESE DISRUPTIONS ARE PARTICULARLY CONCERNING FOR OLDER ADULTS, OVER 70% OF WHOM HAVE MULTIPLE CHRONIC CONDITIONS. WHILE DISASTER RESPONSE EFFORTS FOCUS ON SHORT-TERM EMERGENCY CARE, THE LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF HURRICANES ON PRIMARY CARE AND HEALTH OUTCOMES REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS EXPLORATORY PROJECT IS TO DETERMINE THE EXTENT AND DURATION OF HURRICANES’ IMPACT ON PRIMARY CARE SERVICE PROVIDERS AND UTILIZATION AMONG THE ELDERLY POPULATION. USING A RIGOROUS DIFFERENCE-IN-DIFFERENCES APPROACH AND SURVIVAL ANALYSIS, WE WILL LEVERAGE OVER A DECADE OF MEDICARE CLAIMS DATA AND HURRICANE EXPOSURE MEASURES TO ESTIMATE HOW HURRICANES DISRUPT PRIMARY CARE DELIVERY AND AFFECT HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION. THE RATIONALE FOR THIS PROJECT IS THAT UNDERSTANDING THE DURATION AND MAGNITUDE OF THESE DISRUPTIONS WILL ESTABLISH A SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE HYPOTHESIS-DRIVEN STUDIES (E.G., R01S) AND IMPROVE HOW HEALTH SYSTEMS SUSTAIN PRIMARY CARE ACCESS AFTER A DISASTER. THIS PROJECT PURSUES TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) DETERMINE THE EXTENT AND DURATION OF HURRICANES' IMPACT ON THE NUMBER OF PRIMARY CARE PHYSICIANS, NURSE PRACTITIONERS, AND FACILITY CLOSURES IN AFFECTED COMMUNITIES; AND 2) EXAMINE THE EXTENT AND DURATION OF HURRICANES’ IMPACT ON PRIMARY CARE UTILIZATION, QUALITY OF CARE, AND DIFFERENCES IN UTILIZATION AMONG THE MEDICARE POPULATION. THE RESEARCH PROPOSED IN THIS APPLICATION IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT SHIFTS THE FOCUS FROM SHORT-TERM DISASTER RESPONSE TO LONG-TERM HEALTHCARE SYSTEM RESILIENCE. BY EXAMINING PROVIDER AVAILABILITY, CARE CONTINUITY, AND UTILIZATION TRENDS BEYOND THE IMMEDIATE AFTERMATH OF HURRICANES, THIS STUDY OFFERS NOVEL INSIGHTS INTO HOW HEALTHCARE DISRUPTIONS PERSIST OVER TIME. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT FILLS A CRITICAL GAP IN UNDERSTANDING HOW HURRICANES AFFECT PRIMARY CARE SERVICES AND UTILIZATION AMONG OLDER ADULTS. DISRUPTIONS IN PRIMARY CARE CAN LEAD TO WORSENED HEALTH OUTCOMES AND INCREASED RELIANCE ON HIGH-COST EMERGENCY AND HOSPITAL SERVICES. IDENTIFYING THE EXTENT AND PERSISTENCE OF THESE EFFECTS WILL PROVIDE ESSENTIAL EVIDENCE TO IMPROVE DISASTER PREPAREDNESS EFFORTS, STRENGTHEN HEALTHCARE SYSTEM RESILIENCE, AND GUIDE RESOURCE ALLOCATION TO PROTECT VULNERABLE POPULATIONS IN HURRICANE-PRONE AREAS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISTIC EXPLORATION OF TREM2 ANTIBODIES THAT CAN SUPPRESS ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE RELATED NETWORK HYPEREXCITABILITY AND COGNITIVE DEFICITS - SUMMARY ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD), THE MOST COMMON NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER, IS ASSOCIATED WITH HYPEREXCITABILITY OF NEURAL NETWORKS AND IMMUNE CELL DYSFUNCTION. OUR PREVIOUS STUDIES SHOWED THAT AD-RELATED NETWORK AND IMMUNE DYSFUNCTIONS MAY ENGAGE IN A VICIOUS CIRCLE THAT CONTRIBUTES TO SYNAPTIC ALTERATIONS AND COGNITIVE DECLINE. OUR MOST RECENT FINDINGS SUGGEST THAT THIS CIRCLE CAN BE DISRUPTED BY TREATMENT WITH AGONIST ANTIBODIES TARGETING THE TRIGGERING RECEPTOR EXPRESSED ON MYELOID CELLS 2 (TREM2), AN INNATE IMMUNE RECEPTOR THAT, IN THE BRAIN, IS EXPRESSED PRIMARILY BY MICROGLIA. HERE WE PROPOSE TO EXPLORE THE NOVEL CONCEPT THAT AGONIST TREM2 ANTIBODIES REDUCE AD-RELATED NETWORK HYPEREXCITABILITY AND COGNITIVE DEFICITS BY INCREASING THE PRODUCTION OF A NEUROMODULATOR THAT CAN INHIBIT NEURONAL ACTIVITIES. TO OUR KNOWLEDGE, TREM2 HAS NOT YET BEEN LINKED TO THE PATHWAYS THAT REGULATE THIS NEUROMODULATOR, WHICH MAKES THIS A DARING CONCEPT TO EXPLORE. YET, THE IDENTIFICATION OF SUCH A LINK COULD SHED NEW LIGHT ON THE PATHOGENESIS OF AD, THE NEUROBIOLOGY OF TREM2, AND THE MECHANISM OF ACTION OF NOVEL THERAPEUTICS THAT ARE IN PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT OR EARLY STAGES OF CLINICAL ASSESSMENT, HIGHLIGHTING THE POTENTIAL IMPACT OF THE PROPOSED STUDY. IN AIM 1, WE WILL EXPLORE WHETHER AGONIST TREM2 ANTIBODIES INCREASE THE EXPRESSION OR ACTIVITY OF A RATE-LIMITING ENZYME INVOLVED IN THE PRODUCTION OF THE NEUROMODULATOR AND BEGIN TO DISSECT THE SIGNALING PATHWAYS INVOLVED. IN AIM 2, WE WILL EXPLORE WHETHER CONDITIONAL ABLATION OF THIS ENZYME IN MICROGLIA BLOCKS THE ABILITY OF AGONIST TREM2 ANTIBODIES TO SUPPRESS NETWORK HYPEREXCITABILITY IN MOUSE MODELS THAT DO OR DO NOT HAVE AMYLOID PLAQUES OR TREM2 HYPOFUNCTION. THESE EXPERIMENTS HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO (I) ELUCIDATE THE BIOCHEMICAL PROCESSES BY WHICH TREM2 AGONISM ALLOWS MICROGLIA TO COUNTERACT NETWORK HYPEREXCITABILITY, (II) IDENTIFY AN ENTIRELY NOVEL LINK BETWEEN TREM2 AND THE REGULATION OF AN ENZYME INVOLVED IN THE PRODUCTION OF A KEY NEUROMODULATOR, AND (III) BEGIN TO UNRAVEL THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THIS LINK, WHICH COULD IDENTIFY NOVEL ENTRY POINTS FOR THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS. AUGMENTING THE AVAILABILITY OF POTENT NEUROMODULATORS THROUGH TREATMENTS WITH AGONIST ANTIBODIES OR SMALL MOLECULES THAT ENHANCE TREM2-DEPENDENT SIGNALING PATHWAYS COULD PROVIDE AN EFFECTIVE STRATEGY TO CURTAIL NETWORK HYPEREXCITABILITY AND RELATED COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS IN AD AND OTHER CONDITIONS ASSOCIATED WITH EXCITATION/INHIBITION IMBALANCE OF NEURAL NETWORKS SUCH AS EPILEPSY AND NEUROPSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS, FURTHER BROADENING THE THERAPEUTIC IMPLICATIONS OF THIS PROJECT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXAMINING THE IMPACT OF WEATHER-RELATED BARRIERS ON PRIMARY CARE UTILIZATION IN OLDER ADULTS WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS - PROJECT ABSTRACT NATIONALLY, MISSED VISITS ARE A WIDESPREAD AND COSTLY ISSUE, WITH NO-SHOW RATES RANGING FROM 4% TO 55% AND COSTING THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM OVER $150 BILLION ANNUALLY. MISSED PRIMARY CARE VISITS ALSO POSE A SIGNIFICANT THREAT TO THE HEALTH OF ELDERLY PATIENTS AND THE EFFICIENCY OF THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM. WITH 80% OF OLDER ADULTS IN THE U.S. HAVING AT LEAST ONE CHRONIC CONDITION, CONSISTENT PRIMARY CARE IS VITAL FOR DISEASE MONITORING AND TREAT- MENT—ESPECIALLY FOR COMMON CONDITIONS SUCH AS DIABETES, HYPERTENSION, CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DIS- EASE, CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE, AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND OTHER NEUROCOGNITIVE DISORDERS. HOWEVER, MISSED VISITS DISRUPT THIS CONTINUITY OF CARE, CONTRIBUTING TO POOR HEALTH OUTCOMES, INCLUDING INCREASED MORTALITY RISK, DELAYED FOLLOW-UP, AND GREATER PATIENT ATTRITION. THESE DISRUPTIONS ARE ESPECIALLY PROBLEMATIC FOR OLDER ADULTS WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS WHO ARE MORE LIKELY TO MISS VISITS. ONE UNDERSTUDIED BARRIER TO PRIMARY CARE ACCESS IS INCLEMENT WEATHER, SUCH AS EXTREME TEMPERATURES, HIGH HEAT INDEX, AND HEAVY PRECIPITATION. WHILE SOME RE- SEARCH SHOWS A LINK BETWEEN SPECIFIC WEATHER EVENTS AND MISSED VISITS, FINDINGS VARY BY REGION, AND MOST STUD- IES HAVE NOT FOCUSED ON ELDERLY PATIENTS OR THOSE WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS. THERE REMAINS A CRITICAL GAP IN UNDER- STANDING WHO IS MOST AT RISK AND HOW MUCH PRIMARY CARE IS AFFECTED. TELEMEDICINE OFFERS A PROMISING SOLUTION, HAVING PROVEN EFFECTIVE IN REDUCING MISSED VISITS DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. BOTH PATIENTS AND CLINICIANS REPORTED SATISFACTION WITH TELEMEDICINE, PARTICULARLY WHEN IN-PERSON VISITS WERE NOT FEASIBLE DUE TO WEATHER. THIS STUDY AIMS TO QUANTIFY HOW INCLEMENT WEATHER CONTRIBUTES TO MISSED PRIMARY CARE VISITS AMONG ELDERLY ADULTS WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS AND EVALUATE WHETHER TELEMEDICINE CAN MITIGATE THESE EFFECTS BY PROVIDING AN ACCESSIBLE ALTERNATIVE DURING INCLEMENT WEATHER. USING ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD DATA FROM 2022–2025 LINKED WITH DETAILED WEATHER INFORMATION, WE WILL ASSESS THE IMPACTS OF INCLEMENT WEATHER ON PATTERNS OF MISSED VISITS, TIME INTERVALS BETWEEN APPOINTMENTS, AND SUBSEQUENT EMERGENCY OR HOSPITAL USE WITHIN A LARGE, DIVERSE POPU- LATION OF ELDERLY PATIENTS ACROSS ILLINOIS AND WISCONSIN. ULTIMATELY, THIS RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHTS TO GUIDE FUTURE INTERVENTIONS, SUCH AS PROACTIVELY SCHEDULING TELEMEDICINE VISITS AHEAD OF FORECASTED INCLEMENT WEATHER, THAT HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS CAN ADOPT TO MAINTAIN ACCESS, CONTINUITY, AND HEALTH FOR ALL PATIENTS.

description: L1 RETROTRANSPOSON CONTRIBUTION TO NORMAL BRAIN AGING AND ALZHEIMERS DISEASE IN VIVO - AMONG KEY CHARACTERISTICS OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE ARE TOXICITY FROM AMYLOID PLAQUES, NEUROFIBRILLARY TAU TANGLES, AND CHRONIC INFLAMMATION RESULTING IN THE LOSS OF COGNITIVE FUNCTION. THESE MORPHOLOGICAL CHANGES ARE PRECEDED BY ALTERED TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROFILES, INFLAMMATION, AND INCREASED DNA DAMAGE, ALL OF WHICH ARE THOUGHT TO PROMOTE NEURODEGENERATION. AMONG POTENTIAL ENDOGENOUS CONTRIBUTORS TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE IS THE LINE-1 (L1) RETROTRANSPOSON. L1 IS A REPETITIVE GENETIC ELEMENT THAT INCREASES ITS COPY NUMBER IN THE HOST GENOME THROUGH RETROTRANSPOSITION, WHICH INVOLVES BREAKING GENOMIC DNA. IN ADDITION TO RETROTRANSPOSITION, L1 EXPRESSION CAN GENERATE DNA BREAKS AND TRIGGER CGAS ACTIVATION, WHICH CAN CONTRIBUTE TO SENESCENCE, APOPTOSIS, AND INFLAMMATION OBSERVED IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE PATIENTS. L1 MRNA EXPRESSION AND RETROTRANSPOSITION HAVE BEEN DETECTED IN NORMAL HUMAN AND MOUSE BRAIN AREAS THAT ARE AFFECTED BY ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. WE HAVE REPORTED DIFFERENT PATTERNS OF ENDOGENOUS L1 EXPRESSION IN THE MALE AND FEMALE MOUSE BRAINS, WHICH MAY BE RELEVANT TO A HIGHER RISK OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE IN FEMALES. COMBINED THESE FINDINGS LEAD US TO PROPOSE THAT L1 CAN BE A PLAUSIBLE INTRINSIC GENETIC VARIABLE THAT CAN CONTRIBUTE TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE PROGRESSION IN VIVO BY TRIGGERING PERSISTENT TRANSCRIPTIONAL CHANGES CONSISTENT WITH THOSE OBSERVED IN AD PATIENTS. SEVERAL STUDIES EXPLORING TRANSPOSONS’ ROLE IN NEURODEGENERATION HAVE ESTABLISHED SOME CRITICAL CORRELATIONS AND ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN L1, AGING, AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. HOWEVER, STUDIES THAT DIRECTLY TEST L1 CONTRIBUTION TO BRAIN AGING OR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE IN VIVO CANNOT BE PERFORMED IN HUMANS. OUR AIMS ARE DESIGNED TO TEST THIS CONTRIBUTION USING MOUSE MODELS OF L1 RETROTRANSPOSITION AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. IN AIM 1, WE WILL USE AN EXISTING CUSTOM L1 TRANSGENIC MOUSE MODEL TO TEST WHETHER CHRONIC L1 TRANSGENE EXPRESSION ACCELERATES NORMAL BRAIN AGING BY TRIGGERING AGE-ASSOCIATED TRANSCRIPTIONAL CHANGES. IN AIM 2, BY USING EXISTING MOUSE MODELS OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND L1 WE WILL TEST CONTRIBUTION OF CHRONIC PHYSIOLOGICAL L1 TRANSGENE EXPRESSION TO TRANSCRIPTIONAL, HISTOLOGICAL, AND BEHAVIORAL CHANGES DURING ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE PROGRESSION. IN BOTH AIMS ENDOGENOUS L1 EXPRESSION WILL BE ASSESSED. IF SUCCESSFUL, OUR STUDIES WILL DETERMINE CLINICAL RELEVANCE OF L1 EXPRESSION TO NORMAL AGING AND/OR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE PROGRESSION, WHICH WILL HAVE IMPORTANT PRECLINICAL AND CLINICAL RAMIFICATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AGE-STRATIFIED HUMAN GUT-ON-A-CHIP MODEL TO STUDY MICROBIOME-MEDIATED EPITHELIAL AGING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT AGING OF THE HUMAN GUT IS ACCOMPANIED BY IMPAIRED BARRIER INTEGRITY, MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION, REDUCED REGENERATIVE CAPACITY, AND CHRONIC LOW-GRADE INFLAMMATION (“INFLAMMAGING”), DRIVEN BY BOTH INTRINSIC CHANGES IN EPITHELIAL CELLS AND PARALLEL SHIFTS IN THE GUT MICROBIOME. MOUNTING EVIDENCE LINKS THESE CHANGES, AND AGE- ASSOCIATED SHIFTS IN THE GUT MICROBIOME, TO HEIGHTENED INFECTION RISK, FRAILTY, COGNITIVE DECLINE, AND METABOLIC AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISORDERS. THE NEED TO UNDERSTAND THE CAUSAL MECHANISMS CONNECTING MICROBIOME AGING WITH EPITHELIAL DECLINE IS OF GREAT PUBLIC HEALTH SIGNIFICANCE. DESPITE MOUNTING CLINICAL AND EXPERIMENTAL EVIDENCE THAT AGED MICROBIOMES EXACERBATE EPITHELIAL DYSFUNCTION AND THAT YOUNG MICROBIOMES CAN RESTORE RESILIENCE, MECHANISTIC INSIGHT HAS BEEN LIMITED BY THE LACK OF HUMAN MODELS CAPABLE OF CO-CULTURING COMPLEX, STRICTLY ANAEROBIC MICROBIOMES WITH PATIENT-DERIVED EPITHELIAL TISSUES UNDER PHYSIOLOGICAL OXYGEN GRADIENTS. WE HAVE DEVELOPED A HUMAN GUT-ON-CHIP THAT SUSTAINS OBLIGATE ANAEROBES AND ORGANOID-DERIVED COLON EPITHELIUM ACROSS A CONTROLLED APICAL-BASAL OXYGEN GRADIENT. WE WILL LEVERAGE OUR GUT CHIP PLATFORM TO ESTABLISH THE FIRST AGE- STRATIFIED, HUMAN GUT-ON-CHIP PLATFORM THAT INTEGRATES ORGANOID-DERIVED YOUNG AND OLD COLON EPITHELIA AND MICROBIOMES WITHIN A DYNAMICALLY PERFUSED, OXYGEN-CONTROLLED MICROPHYSIOLOGICAL ENVIRONMENT. THE LONG-TERM OBJECTIVE IS TO ELUCIDATE HOW AGING-RELATED CHANGES IN HOST EPITHELIUM AND MICROBIOME COMPOSITION, INDIVIDUALLY AND IN CONCERT, SHAPE BARRIER FUNCTION AND INFLAMMATORY SIGNALING, DRIVING VULNERABILITY TO AGE-ASSOCIATED DISEASE. WE WILL FIRST BENCHMARK MOLECULAR AND FUNCTIONAL HALLMARKS OF COLON EPITHELIAL AGING, INCLUDING BARRIER LOSS, LINEAGE IMBALANCE, MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION, AND INCREASED SENESCENCE-ASSOCIATED SECRETORY PHENOTYPE, BY COMPARING YOUNG AND OLD ORGANOID-DERIVED EPITHELIA CULTURED UNDER PHYSIOLOGIC OXYGEN. WE WILL THEN DISSECT WHETHER AGE-ASSOCIATED MICROBIAL COMMUNITIES ACCELERATE EPITHELIAL DECLINE OR WHETHER INTRINSIC EPITHELIAL AGING PREDOMINATES, USING A CROSS-AGE EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN AND RIGOROUS MULTI-OMICS PROFILING IN THE GUT-ON-CHIP. BY RESOLVING THE DIRECTIONALITY AND MECHANISMS OF GUT MICROBIOME-EPITHELIUM CROSSTALK IN AGING, THIS WORK WILL PRODUCE THE FIRST HUMAN-RELEVANT REFERENCE STANDARDS FOR EPITHELIAL AGING PHENOTYPES, REVEAL ACTIONABLE TARGETS FOR INTERVENTION, AND LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR MICROBIOME-BASED THERAPEUTICS, PRECISION MEDICINE, AND PREVENTION STRATEGIES TO PROMOTE HEALTH SPAN IN AGING POPULATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HUMAN NEUROMUSCULAR AGING-ON-A-CHIP: MODELING MOLECULAR AND FUNCTIONAL HALLMARKS OF SKELETAL MUSCLE DECLINE - PROJECT SUMMARY SARCOPENIA, THE AGE-RELATED LOSS OF SKELETAL MUSCLE MASS, IS A LEADING CAUSE OF FRAILTY, FALLS, AND FUNCTIONAL DECLINE IN OLDER ADULTS, GENERATING OVER $20 BILLION IN ANNUAL HEALTHCARE COSTS IN THE UNITED STATES. WHILE EXERCISE, PARTICULARLY RESISTANCE AND ENDURANCE TRAINING, CAN MITIGATE SARCOPENIA, FACTORS SUCH AS COMORBIDITIES, MOTIVATIONAL BARRIERS, AND LACK OF PERSONALIZED TOOLS LIMIT ITS ACCESSIBILITY AND EFFECTIVENESS. DESPITE ITS GROWING PREVALENCE, THERE ARE NO FDA-APPROVED THERAPIES THAT DIRECTLY TARGET THE MOLECULAR UNDERPINNINGS OF SARCOPENIA. EMERGING EVIDENCE IDENTIFIES DYNAPENIA, OR LOSS OF MUSCLE STRENGTH, AS A STRONGER PREDICTOR OF AGE-RELATED MOBILITY LOSS THAN MUSCLE MASS ALONE. CENTRAL TO BOTH SARCOPENIA AND DYNAPENIA IS DETERIORATION OF THE NEUROMUSCULAR JUNCTION (NMJ) DUE TO DENERVATION AND IMPAIRED REINNERVATION DRIVEN BY MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION AND OXIDATIVE STRESS. THESE PROCESSES, ESPECIALLY IN FAST-TWITCH FIBERS, ARE POORLY CAPTURED BY RODENT MODELS, WHICH DIFFER SIGNIFICANTLY FROM HUMANS IN NMJ STRUCTURE AND REGENERATIVE CAPACITY. TO OVERCOME THESE LIMITATIONS, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A HUMAN 3D NEUROMUSCULAR MICROPHYSIOLOGICAL SYSTEM (MPS) THAT MODELS NEUROMUSCULAR AGING EX VIVO. THIS PLATFORM INTEGRATES PRIMARY HUMAN MUSCLE STEM CELLS (MUSCS) FROM YOUNG (20–30 YRS) AND AGED (60–75 YRS) DONORS, IPSC-DERIVED MOTOR NEURONS, AND FIBROGENIC PROGENITORS WITHIN A COMPARTMENTALIZED MICROFLUIDIC CHIP THAT RECAPITULATES THE HUMAN MOTOR UNIT. THE SYSTEM FEATURES OPTOGENETIC CONTROL OF MOTOR NEURON ACTIVITY VIA CHANNELRHODOPSIN-2 AND REAL-TIME CONTRACTILITY MEASUREMENTS USING EMBEDDED MAGNETIC SENSORS IN A MODULAR, SCALABLE FORMAT SUITABLE FOR HIGH-THROUGHPUT DRUG SCREENING. ENDPOINT MULTI-OMIC ANALYSES (TRANSCRIPTOMIC AND PROTEOMIC) WILL IDENTIFY MOLECULAR AGING SIGNATURES AND MECHANISTIC DRIVERS OF DECLINE. THROUGH LONGITUDINAL STUDIES OVER EIGHT WEEKS, STRATIFIED BY AGE, SEX, AND ETHNICITY, WE WILL DISSECT THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN MUSCLE STEM CELL DYSFUNCTION, NMJ DEGENERATION, AND IMPAIRED CONTRACTILE FUNCTION. THIS HUMAN-RELEVANT MODEL WILL ENABLE PERSONALIZED, HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING OF INTERVENTIONS AND PROVIDE A TRANSLATIONAL PLATFORM FOR DEVELOPING TARGETED THERAPIES AGAINST SARCOPENIA AND RELATED CONDITIONS. ULTIMATELY, THIS INNOVATIVE SYSTEM BRIDGES A CRITICAL GAP IN GEROSCIENCE BY REPLACING UNRELIABLE ANIMAL MODELS WITH A PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT TOOL TO COMBAT NEUROMUSCULAR AGING, PRESERVE MOBILITY, AND EXTEND HEALTH SPAN IN OLDER ADULTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ESTABLISHING PROCOTYLA FLUVIATILIS AS A COMPARATIVE MODEL FOR AGING RESEARCH - SUMMARY AGING REMAINS ONE OF THE MOST PRESSING BIOLOGICAL CHALLENGES, YET THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT LIMIT LIFESPAN, EVEN IN HIGHLY REGENERATIVE ANIMALS, REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. FLATWORMS ARE RENOWNED FOR THEIR STEM CELL–DRIVEN REGENERATIVE ABILITIES, BUT EVEN AMONG CLOSELY RELATED SPECIES, THEY EXHIBIT STRIKING VARIATION IN REPRODUCTIVE STRATEGIES, REGENERATIVE POTENTIAL, AND LONGEVITY. THE NORTH AMERICAN PLANARIAN PROCOTYLA FLUVIATILIS PROVIDES A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO DISSECT THESE RELATIONSHIPS: IT REPRODUCES SEASONALLY AND UNDERGOES RAPID SOMA DECLINE FOLLOWING EGG-LAYING, DESPITE MAINTAINING ABUNDANT STEM CELLS AND ROBUST REGENERATIVE ABILITIES. PRIOR STUDIES ON REGENERATION IN P. FLUVIATILIS HAVE ESTABLISHED ESSENTIAL GENOMIC RESOURCES, FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS, AND METHODS FOR MECHANISTIC STUDIES. BUILDING ON THESE TOOLS, THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH P. FLUVIATILIS AS A RIGOROUS NEW MODEL FOR AGING RESEARCH BY (1) DEFINING HOW STEM CELL FUNCTION AND TISSUE STRUCTURE CHANGE ACROSS ITS SEASONAL LIFE CYCLE, (2) MAPPING AGE-ASSOCIATED CELLULAR AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL CHANGES USING SINGLE-CELL SEQUENCING, AND (3) TESTING WHETHER CONSERVED GENETIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL REGULATORS OF LIFESPAN ALSO ACT IN THIS REGENERATIVE SPECIES. BY INTEGRATING STEM CELL BIOLOGY, MOLECULAR GENETICS, AND FUNCTIONAL PERTURBATION, THIS WORK WILL REVEAL HOW REGENERATION INTERSECTS WITH LOSS OF SOMATIC MAINTENANCE, OFFERING NEW INSIGHT INTO CONSERVED MECHANISMS THAT GOVERN TISSUE HEALTH AND LONGEVITY ACROSS SPECIES, INCLUDING HUMANS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DIGITAL FLUOROIMMUNOASSAY FOR ULTRASENSITIVE AND MULTIPLEXED DETECTION OF NEUROLOGICAL BIOMARKERS - PROJECT SUMMARY ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS A PROGRESSIVE NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER THAT BEGINS DECADES BEFORE SYMPTOMS APPEAR. EARLY PATHOLOGICAL CHANGES, INCLUDING AMYLOID-Β (AΒ) DEPOSITION AND TAU PHOSPHORYLATION, OCCUR LONG BEFORE COGNITIVE DECLINE BECOMES CLINICALLY EVIDENT. CURRENT DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS, SUCH AS CEREBROSPINAL FLUID (CSF) ASSAYS AND AMYLOID PET IMAGING, PROVIDE ACCURATE BIOMARKER READOUTS BUT ARE INVASIVE, COSTLY, AND LARGELY INACCESSIBLE, LIMITING THEIR USE FOR LARGE-SCALE SCREENING OR LONGITUDINAL MONITORING. WHILE RECENT BLOOD-BASED PLATFORMS SUCH AS LUMIPULSE G HAVE ADVANCED AD BIOMARKER DETECTION IN SYMPTOMATIC INDIVIDUALS, THEIR ANALYTICAL PERFORMANCE REMAINS INSUFFICIENT FOR ACCURATE QUANTIFICATION OF THE LOW-ABUNDANCE BIOMARKERS THAT CHARACTERIZE PRECLINICAL DISEASE. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO TRANSFORM AD SCREENING AND EARLY DETECTION BY DEVELOPING AN ULTRASENSITIVE, MULTIPLEXED, PLASMONIC-FLUOR-LINKED IMMUNOSORBENT ASSAY (P-FLISA) FOR QUANTITATIVE MEASUREMENT OF PLASMA P-TAU217, AΒ42, AND AΒ40. PLASMONIC-FLUOR NANOLABELS GENERATE FLUORESCENCE SIGNALS APPROXIMATELY 10,000-FOLD BRIGHTER THAN CONVENTIONAL FLUOROPHORES, ENABLING SINGLE-PARTICLE DETECTION WITH STANDARD FLUORESCENCE MICROSCOPY. BY CONVERTING PFLISA FROM ANALOG TO DIGITAL COUNTING MODE, THE LOWER LIMIT OF QUANTIFICATION WILL IMPROVE BY OVER 50-FOLD, ENABLING SUB-FG/ML DETECTION WITHOUT ENZYMATIC AMPLIFICATION OR SPECIALIZED INSTRUMENTS. TO ACHIEVE THE RESEARCH GOAL, TWO SPECIFIC AIMS WILL BE PURSUED. AIM 1 WILL DEVELOP AND ANALYTICALLY VALIDATE MULTIPLEXED DIGITAL P-FLISA FOR P-TAU217, AΒ42, AND AΒ40 USING WELL- CHARACTERIZED PLASMA SAMPLES BENCHMARKED AGAINST LUMIPULSE. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS CLINICAL PERFORMANCE IN 400 INDIVIDUALS WITH AMYLOID PET AND CSF DATA REPRESENTING COGNITIVELY UNIMPAIRED (AMYLOID-POSITIVE/NEGATIVE), MILD COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT, AND MILD AD DEMENTIA GROUPS. PREDICTIVE ACCURACY FOR IDENTIFYING AMYLOID-POSITIVE COGNITIVELY UNIMPAIRED INDIVIDUALS WILL BE ASSESSED USING RECEIVER OPERATING CHARACTERISTIC ANALYSES, MULTIMARKER LOGISTIC MODELS, AND REPRODUCIBILITY EVALUATIONS. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION WILL YIELD THE FIRST CLINICALLY ANCHORED, ULTRASENSITIVE, MULTIPLEXED BLOOD ASSAY THAT EXCEEDS LUMIPULSE-LEVEL ANALYTICAL PERFORMANCE AND ENABLES EARLY, ACCESSIBLE DETECTION OF AD PATHOLOGY. THIS PLATFORM WILL ESTABLISH A SCALABLE FOUNDATION FOR POPULATION SCREENING, THERAPEUTIC MONITORING, AND EXTENSION TO OTHER NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ALPHA-KETOGLUTARATE: A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY TO IMPROVE NEUROGLIOVASCULAR COUPLING AND COGNITIVE AGING IN OLDER ADULTS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  NORMAL COGNITIVE FUNCTION REQUIRES ADEQUATE BLOOD SUPPLY TO THE BRAIN TO SUPPORT NEURONAL ACTIVITY. IN THE HEALTHY YOUNG BRAIN, CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW IS RAPIDLY ADJUSTED TO MEET THE INCREASED OXYGEN AND NUTRIENT DEMANDS OF ACTIVE BRAIN REGIONS VIA A HOMEOSTATIC MECHANISM TERMED NEUROGLIOVASCULAR COUPLING (NGVC). THIS MECHANISM INVOLVES A COMPLEX INTERCELLULAR SIGNALING NETWORK BETWEEN NEURONAL, GLIAL, AND ENDOTHELIAL CELLS, WHICH COME TOGETHER TO FORM THE NEUROGLIOVASCULAR UNIT (NGVU). PRECLINICAL AND CLINICAL STUDIES DEMONSTRATE THAT EXPERIMENTALLY INDUCED NGVC DYSFUNCTION IN YOUNG ANIMALS RESULTS IN COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND THAT NGVC IS IMPAIRED IN NORMAL AGING AND IS IMPLICATED IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF AGE-RELATED COGNITIVE DECLINE. IMPORTANTLY, RESTORATION OF NGVC IN AGED ANIMALS BY TARGETED PHARMACOLOGICAL TREATMENTS IMPROVES NGVC FUNCTION AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE. HOWEVER, THERE ARE NO CLINICALLY APPROVED TREATMENTS TO REVERSE AGE-RELATED NGVC DYSFUNCTION IN HUMANS.  CELLULAR DAMAGE CAUSED BY MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION AND EXACERBATED OXIDATIVE STRESS, BOTH PROCESSES RECOGNIZED AS KEY HALLMARKS OF BRAIN AGING, HAVE BEEN LINKED TO NGVU DISRUPTION AND SUBSEQUENT NGVC DYSFUNCTION. YET, TO DATE, VERY FEW CLINICAL TRIALS HAVE TESTED ANTI-AGING INTERVENTIONS FOR THEIR ABILITY TO REDUCE OXIDATIVE STRESS SPECIFICALLY WITHIN NGVU CELLS, AND TO ASSESS THEIR EFFECTS ON NGVC RESPONSES AND COGNITION IN OLDER ADULTS. ALPHA- KETOGLUTARATE (AKG) IS AN ENDOGENOUSLY PRODUCED INTERMEDIATE OF THE TRICARBOXYLIC ACID CYCLE INVOLVED IN CRITICAL CELLULAR METABOLISM PROCESSES, BUT WHOSE LEVELS DECLINE 10-FOLD BETWEEN MIDLIFE AND OLDER AGE. THIS NATURAL DECLINE SPARKED THE INTEREST IN USING DIETARY AKG SUPPLEMENTATION AS AN ANTI-AGING INTERVENTION SUPPORTING CELLULAR ANTIOXIDANT DEFENSES AND MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION. EARLY CLINICAL TRIALS INDICATE AKG IS SAFE AND IMPROVES FRAILTY OUTCOMES IN OLDER ADULTS. HOWEVER, ITS POTENTIAL TO REDUCE OXIDATIVE STRESS WITHIN NGVU CELLS AND IMPROVE NGVC AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE IN THIS POPULATION REMAINS UNKNOWN.  CLINICALLY, MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION AND OXIDATIVE STRESS ARE ASSESSED USING CIRCULATING OR CEREBROSPINAL BIOMARKERS. HOWEVER, THESE BIOMARKERS LACK SPECIFICITY FOR THE STATUS OF INDIVIDUAL NGVU CELL TYPES. EMERGING EVIDENCE SUPPORTS THE USE OF EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES (EVS) AS POTENTIAL BIOMARKERS IN AGE-RELATED NEUROLOGICAL IMPAIRMENTS. BECAUSE EVS CARRY SURFACE MARKERS SPECIFIC TO THEIR CELL OF ORIGIN, ISOLATING AND ANALYZING EVS FROM NEURONS, ASTROCYTES, AND VASCULAR CELLS MAY PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHT INTO CELL-SPECIFIC CONTRIBUTIONS TO NGVC IMPAIRMENT AND ASSOCIATED COGNITIVE DECLINE AS WELL AS INTO CELL-SPECIFIC RESPONSES TO TARGETED INTERVENTIONS.  THIS PROPOSAL WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT AKG SUPPLEMENTATION WILL IMPROVE NGVC RESPONSES AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE IN OLDER ADULTS. WE WILL ALSO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THESE EFFECTS ARE MEDIATED BY A DECREASE IN AGE- RELATED OXIDATIVE STRESS WITHIN NGVU CELLS. THESE HYPOTHESES WILL BE TESTED IN A RANDOMIZED, DOUBLE-BLIND, PLACEBO- CONTROLLED CLINICAL TRIAL WITH 24 WEEKS OF AKG SUPPLEMENTATION IN COMMUNITY DWELLING OLDER ADULTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNRAVELING PATHWAYS TO CEREBRAL SMALL VESSEL DISEASE IN VCID AND AD WITH FERUMOXYTOL-ENHANCED MRI - ABSTRACT ANTI-AMYLOID THERAPIES HAVE ADVANCED THE TREATMENT OF ALZHEIMER’ DISEASE (AD) PROTEINOPATHY AND RELATED COGNITIVE DECLINE; HOWEVER, CLINICAL STUDIES OFTEN OVERLOOK THE CONTRIBUTION OF COMORBID CEREBRAL SMALL VESSEL DISEASE (CSVD) IN MIXED DEMENTIAS. THIS CREATES A CRITICAL GAP IN DEMENTIA RESEARCH BOTH IN UNDERSTANDING AND ADDRESSING VASCULAR CONTRIBUTIONS TO COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA (VCID) AND IN EVALUATING VASCULAR VULNERABILITIES THAT MAY INFLUENCE THE RISK OF IATROGENIC COMPLICATIONS SUCH AS AMYLOID-RELATED IMAGING ABNORMALITIES (ARIA). THE GAP LARGELY STEMS FROM THE ABSENCE OF SENSITIVE AND SPECIFIC VASCULAR BIOMARKERS CAPABLE OF DETECTING EARLY MICROVASCULAR DYSFUNCTION AND CAPTURING THE UNDERLYING PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF CSVD, THE MOST PREVALENT FORM OF VCID. MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (MRI) REMAINS THE STANDARD FOR NON-INVASIVE ASSESSMENT OF CSVD. HOWEVER, COMMONLY USED MRI MARKERS SUCH AS WHITE MATTER HYPERINTENSITIES (WMHS) ON T2-FLAIR PRIMARILY REFLECT NON- SPECIFIC DOWNSTREAM SEQUELAE OF CSVD RATHER THAN THE UNDERLYING MICROVASCULAR DYSFUNCTION. TO OVERCOME THIS LIMITATION, THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL INVESTIGATE NOVEL MICROVASCULAR MARKERS USING UNIQUE FERUMOXYTOL-ENHANCED MRI TO TEST HYPOTHESES THAT LINK SPECIFIC VASCULAR PROCESSES TO CSVD IN INDIVIDUALS WITH MIXED VCID AND AD BURDEN. IN PRELIMINARY STUDIES, WE HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT FERUMOXYTOL-ENHANCED MRI ENABLES UNIQUE AND QUANTITATIVE CHARACTERIZATION OF THE MICROVASCULATURE, INCLUDING VASCULAR DENSITY AND HEMODYNAMIC MEASURES OF MICROVASCULAR PULSATILITY. THESE TECHNIQUES HAVE NOT BEEN APPLIED TO VCID OR AD POPULATIONS. HARNESSING THE UNIQUE CHARACTERIZATION PROVIDED BY FERUMOXYTOL-ENHANCED MRI, THIS STUDY AIMS TO FURTHER OUR UNDERSTANDING OF MICROVASCULAR INVOLVEMENT IN VCID AND AD. TO ACHIEVE THIS, WE WILL CONDUCT A SINGLE-VISIT STUDY IN COGNITIVELY UNIMPAIRED INDIVIDUALS WITH BIOMARKER EVIDENCE OF BOTH VCID AND AD BURDEN (N=40; 50% AMYLOID- POSITIVE). PARTICIPANTS WILL BE RECRUITED FROM ONGOING AGING STUDIES WITH EXISTING DATA INCLUDING MEDICAL HISTORY, VASCULAR RISK FACTORS, COGNITIVE ASSESSMENTS, AND IMAGING AND BIOFLUID BIOMARKERS OF VCID AND AD. USING FERUMOXYTOL-ENHANCED MRI, WE AIM TO CHARACTERIZE THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN MICROVASCULAR PULSATILITY, VESSEL DENSITY, AND CSVD-RELATED TISSUE INJURY. OUR GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY POTENTIALLY MODIFIABLE TARGETS WITHIN CSVD PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND INVESTIGATE THE INFLUENCE OF AD ON CSVD MANIFESTATION. COMPLETION OF THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO CSVD PATHOPHYSIOLOGY IN INDIVIDUALS WITH MIXED VCID AND AD BURDEN, ESTABLISH A NOVEL IMAGING PLATFORM FOR MICROVASCULAR ASSESSMENT, AND GENERATE PRELIMINARY DATA AND RATIONALE TO SUPPORT FUTURE EXTRAMURAL FUNDING APPLICATIONS WITH BROADER SCIENTIFIC SCOPE (NIH R01). ULTIMATELY, THIS WORK WILL LAY A FOUNDATION FOR LONGITUDINAL STUDIES ON CSVD PROGRESSION THAT AIM TO IDENTIFY ITS CONTRIBUTIONS TO VCID AND GUIDE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TARGETING MODIFIABLE VASCULAR PROCESSES IN MIXED DEMENTIAS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SINGLE-MOLECULE DYNAMICS OF AMYLOID PRECURSOR PROTEIN WITH POOLED GENETIC PERTURBATIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AFFECTS OVER 6 MILLION AMERICANS, WITH AMYLOID-BETA (AΒ) PLAQUES STEMMING FROM AMYLOID PRECURSOR PROTEIN (APP) MISPROCESSING AS A CENTRAL PATHOLOGICAL DRIVER. DESPITE DECADES OF RESEARCH, THE DYNAMIC MOLECULAR MECHANISMS REGULATING APP’S ENCOUNTERS WITH Β-SECRETASE (BACE1) FOR AMYLOIDOGENIC CLEAVAGE VERSUS Α-SECRETASE (ADAM10) FOR PROTECTIVE SHEDDING REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD, HINDERED BY BULK BIOCHEMICAL ASSAYS THAT OBSCURE SINGLE-MOLECULE BEHAVIORS IN LIVE NEURONS. CURRENT ANTI-AΒ THERAPIES, SUCH AS MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES, ACHIEVE MODEST SLOWING OF EARLY COGNITIVE DECLINE BUT FAIL TO REVERSE ESTABLISHED IMPAIRMENTS, UNDERSCORING THE NEED FOR UPSTREAM INTERVENTIONS TARGETING APP PROCESSING. THIS R21 PROPOSAL DEVELOPS AN INNOVATIVE LIVE-CELL IMAGING PLATFORM THAT PERFORMS FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS SCREENS USING SINGLE- MOLECULE DYNAMIC READOUTS. WE WILL INTEGRATE SINGLE-PARTICLE TRACKING (SPT) WITH OPTICAL POOLED SCREENING (OPS) TO DEVELOP A TRANSFORMATIVE MULTIPLEXED IMAGING TECHNOLOGY CALLED SPT-OPS THAT FURTHER SHARPENS OPS SENSITIVITY AND GREATLY EXPONENTIATES SPT THROUGHPUT. WE WILL USE TWO SPT ACQUISITION MODES BALANCING BREADTH AND DEPTH: MODE 1 USES CONVENTIONAL DYES TO COLLECT SHORT MOVIES AT GENOME SCALE FOR HIT-FINDING; MODE 2 USES BRIGHT, PHOTOSTABLE, MULTICOLOR UPCONVERTING NANOPARTICLES (UCNPS) TO ENABLE LONG-DURATION, MULTIPLEXED TRACKING AT SUB-GENOME SCALE THAT CAPTURES RARE EVENTS AND PROTEIN–PROTEIN INTERACTIONS, IDEAL FOR DETAILED MECHANISTIC STUDIES. AFTER LIVE-CELL IMAGING, IN SITU SEQUENCING DECODES EACH CELL’S CRISPR PERTURBATION, AND FIXED-CELL IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE ADDS CELL-STATE CONTEXT. AIM 1 WILL DEVELOP AND VALIDATES SPT-OPS USING THE WELL-CHARACTERIZED EGFR FAMILY IN HELA CELLS, ESTABLISHING ROBUST CROSS-MICROSCOPE REGISTRATION, AUTOMATED FEATURE EXTRACTION (E.G., DIFFUSIVE STATE FRACTIONS, TRANSITION RATES, CONFINEMENT, ENDOCYTOSIS), AND THROUGHPUT BENCHMARKS. AIM 2 WILL APPLY SPT-OPS TO HUMAN IPSC-DERIVED NEURONS TO DISCOVER GENETIC MODULATORS OF APP DYNAMICS, QUANTIFYING DIFFUSION, INTERNALIZATION, AND ENCOUNTER KINETICS AMONG APP, ADAM10 (Α-SECRETASE), AND BACE1 (Β-SECRETASE) AND ALONG ENDOSOMAL PATHWAYS (RAB5/RAB7). UNSUPERVISED CLUSTERING, NETWORK ANALYSIS, AND MULTIMODAL INTEGRATION WITH AΒ READOUTS AND OTHER AD HALLMARKS WILL PRIORITIZE ACTIONABLE PATHWAY NODES. THIS PROGRAM DIRECTLY MEASURES HOW GENOTYPE RESHAPES LIVE-CELL MOLECULAR BEHAVIOR, SUPPLYING MECHANISTIC TRACTION THAT ENSEMBLE ASSAYS CANNOT PROVIDE. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE (I) A FIRST-IN-CLASS, SCALABLE PLATFORM THAT MAPS FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS THROUGH SINGLE-MOLECULE DYNAMICS, AND (II) A PRIORITIZED, MECHANISM-GROUNDED SET OF AD TARGETS THAT REDUCE APP–BACE1 ENCOUNTERS AND/OR FAVOR NON-AMYLOIDOGENIC PROCESSING, POTENTIALLY ADVANCING SAFER, MORE PRECISE THERAPEUTICS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TRANSLATOMIC CHANGES DURING CARDIAC AGING: RIBOSOMAL PROTEIN AND INITIATION FACTOR INTERACTIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY TRANSLATOMIC CHANGES DURING CARDIAC AGING: RIBOSOMAL PROTEIN AND INITIATION FACTOR INTERACTIONS MONTANA STATE UNIVERSITY  AGING PROFOUNDLY IMPACTS CARDIAC STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION, PREDISPOSING INDIVIDUALS TO CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD)—THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH IN THE U.S. AS THE POPULATION AGES, UNDERSTANDING HOW AGING REMODELS THE HEART AT THE MOLECULAR LEVEL IS CRUCIAL FOR IDENTIFYING STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE HEALTHSPAN AND REDUCE MORTALITY. CARDIAC AGING IS CHARACTERIZED BY PROTEOMIC REMODELING, FIBROSIS, LOSS OF PROTEOSTASIS, AND MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION, YET THE MECHANISMS DRIVING THESE CHANGES REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD.  EMERGING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT AGING DISRUPTS TRANSLATIONAL CONTROL, CREATING DISCORDANCE BETWEEN MRNA AND PROTEIN LEVELS. RIBOSOMES, THE CENTRAL MACHINERY FOR PROTEIN SYNTHESIS, UNDERGO COMPOSITIONAL CHANGES WITH AGE DUE TO ALTERED RIBOSOMAL PROTEIN (RP) EXPRESSION, LOSS OF STOICHIOMETRY, AND IMPAIRED ASSEMBLY. INTERESTINGLY, KNOCKDOWN OR OVEREXPRESSION OF SPECIFIC RPS CAN EXTEND LIFESPAN, SUGGESTING THAT THE RIBOSOME ACTIVELY SHAPES PROTEOMIC AND AGING OUTCOMES, POTENTIALLY THROUGH SELECTIVE MRNA TRANSLATION.  WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CHANGES IN RP SUBUNITS—USING THE LARGE SUBUNIT PROTEIN RPL13 AS A PROTOTYPE— REPROGRAM THE CARDIAC TRANSLATOME, THEREBY INFLUENCING PROTEOSTASIS AND AGING. PRELIMINARY STUDIES SHOW THAT RPL13 KNOCKDOWN (KD) IN THE DROSOPHILA HEART INDUCES TRANSCRIPTOMIC, FUNCTIONAL, AND STRUCTURAL PHENOTYPES THAT MIMIC CARDIAC AGING, INCLUDING FIBROSIS AND CONTRACTILE DECLINE. MOREOVER, RPL13 GENETICALLY INTERACTS WITH TRANSLATION INITIATION FACTORS (EIF3E, EIF3M) AND EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX GENES, SUGGESTING THAT RPL13 COORDINATES TRANSLATIONAL AND STRUCTURAL REMODELING OF THE HEART. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE HOW RPL13 KD AND OVEREXPRESSION (OE) INFLUENCE CARDIAC AGING PHENOTYPES—CONTRACTILITY, RHYTHM, FIBROSIS, AND PROTEOSTASIS—AND TEST GENETIC INTERACTIONS WITH EIF3 SUBUNITS TO IDENTIFY MODIFIERS OF AGING OUTCOMES. AIM 2 WILL COMPARE TRANSLATOMIC PROFILES OF AGED HEARTS AND RPL13-PERTURBED HEARTS USING RIBO-STAMP, AN INNOVATIVE IN VIVO METHOD THAT CAPTURES RIBOSOME-BOUND MRNAS THROUGH RNA EDITING. THESE ANALYSES WILL IDENTIFY MRNA TARGETS WHOSE TRANSLATION CHANGES WITH AGE OR RPL13/EIF3 MANIPULATION, REVEALING PATHWAYS THAT SHAPE CARDIAC AGING. USING THE GENETICALLY TRACTABLE DROSOPHILA MODEL, WHICH PERMITS PRECISE, TISSUE- AND AGE-SPECIFIC CONTROL OF GENE EXPRESSION, WE WILL DISSECT HOW RP–EIF3 INTERACTIONS REMODEL TRANSLATION DURING AGING. THIS WORK ESTABLISHES A NEW CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK WHERE SPECIFIC RIBOSOMAL SUBUNITS AND TRANSLATION FACTORS DETERMINE SELECTIVE MRNA TRANSLATION TO MODULATE CARDIAC AGING. UNDERSTANDING THESE MECHANISMS COULD UNCOVER NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS TO PRESERVE PROTEOSTASIS, MAINTAIN CARDIAC FUNCTION, AND DELAY AGE-ASSOCIATED DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: WEILL MEDICAL COLLEGE OF CORNELL UNIVERSITY

description: IMPROVING THE MENTAL HEALTH OF HOME HOSPICE CAREGIVERS THROUGH A SINGLE SESSION INTERVENTION - PROJECT SUMMARY  APPROXIMATELY 2.3 MILLION FAMILY CAREGIVERS (CGS) OF PATIENTS AT THE END OF LIFE (EOL) EXPERIENCE SIGNIFICANT MENTAL HEALTH SYMPTOMS. DESPITE SUPPORTIVE SERVICES FROM HOSPICE, 33% OF HOSPICE CGS EXPERIENCE MODERATE-TO-SEVERE ANXIETY, AND 23% OF HOSPICE CGS EXPERIENCE MODERATE-TO-SEVERE DEPRESSION. THIS CONTRASTS WITH A 6% PREVALENCE RATE NATIONALLY FOR ANXIETY OR DEPRESSION IN THE GENERAL POPULATION. FAMILY CGS OF PATIENTS RECEIVING HOME HOSPICE CARE (HOSPICE CGS) PLAY A CRUCIAL ROLE IN DAILY CAREGIVING DUTIES, PROVIDING ON AVERAGE 12.6 HOURS OF CAREGIVING PER DAY. HOWEVER, THIS RESPONSIBILITY IS ALSO ASSOCIATED WITH POORER MENTAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR THE CGS. THEREFORE, THERE IS AN URGENT NEED TO TEST FEASIBLE AND ACCEPTABLE METHODS TO PROVIDE MENTAL HEALTH CARE TO CGS OF HOME HOSPICE PATIENTS TO IMPROVE THEIR HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, WHILE ALSO ENABLING THEM TO BETTER SUPPORT THE INDIVIDUALS THEY CARE FOR.  THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO ADAPT AND TEST THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF A SINGLE SESSION INTERVENTION (SSI) AIMED AT IMPROVING THE MENTAL HEALTH OF HOME HOSPICE CGS IN A PILOT RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL (RCT) WITH A 1:1 (SSI VS. USUAL CARE) ALLOCATION. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF OUR PROPOSAL IS THAT IMPLEMENTING A SSI WILL BE FEASIBLE AND ACCEPTABLE IN HOME HOSPICE CGS AND WILL SHOW PRELIMINARY EFFICACY IN IMPROVING CG MENTAL HEALTH OUTCOMES. FOR AIM 1, WE WILL ADAPT AN SSI FOR HOSPICE CGS USING FEEDBACK FROM HOSPICE/MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS AND SSI EXPERTS. WE WILL EMPLOY A MODIFIED DELPHI APPROACH TO GATHER FEEDBACK TO REFINE OUR SSI INTERVENTION UNTIL EXPERT APPROVAL IS ACHIEVED. ADJUDICATION WILL RESULT IN AN SSI PROTOCOL AND MANUAL, WITH COMPONENTS OF MINDFULNESS AND SOLUTION-FOCUSED THERAPY, WHICH WILL BE PILOT TESTED IN AIM 2. FOR AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF IMPLEMENTING AN SSI FOR HOME HOSPICE CGS. HOME HOSPICE CGS (N = 60) WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO SSI OR USUAL CARE. FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY MEASURES WILL BE BASED ON PROCTOR'S TAXONOMY OF IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES. PRELIMINARY EFFECTS ON ANXIETY, DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, AND CG STRESS WILL BE EXPLORED.  OUR PROPOSAL IS EXPECTED TO HAVE A SIGNIFICANT AND POSITIVE IMPACT BY ESTABLISHING THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF AN SSI TO IMPROVE THE MENTAL HEALTH OF HOME HOSPICE CGS WHO ARE OFTEN OVERBURDENED AND OVERWHELMED. THE DEVELOPMENT OF CG-FOCUSED INTERVENTIONS IN HOME HOSPICE IS CRITICAL IN SUPPORTING FAMILY CGS AND IS A CENTRAL TENET OF HIGH-QUALITY PALLIATIVE AND HOSPICE CARE.

description: IN VIVO GSM MIMICRY AS A PLATFORM TO DE-RISK ALZHEIMER'S THERAPEUTICS - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT THERE IS A CRITICAL UNMET NEED FOR SAFE, ORALLY AVAILABLE, LONG-TERM THERAPIES FOR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD). G- SECRETASE MODULATORS (GSMS) REPRESENT A PROMISING THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY, BUT THEIR CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT HAS BEEN HINDERED BY THE INABILITY TO DEFINITIVELY SEPARATE THERAPEUTIC MODULATION FROM THE KNOWN TOXIC EFFECTS OF DIRECT G-SECRETASE INHIBITION IN VIVO. THIS PROJECT WILL OVERCOME THIS TRANSLATIONAL BARRIER BY DEVELOPING AN INNOVATIVE DUAL-MIMIC GENETIC PLATFORM TO DIRECTLY ADDRESS THIS CENTRAL CONTROVERSY AND DE-RISK AN ENTIRE THERAPEUTIC CLASS. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT A RATIONALLY DESIGNED GENETIC MIMIC OF GSM ACTION WILL SELECTIVELY REDUCE THE PRODUCTION OF PATHOGENIC AB42 WHILE AVOIDING THE WIDESPREAD, AB-INDEPENDENT CELLULAR PATHOLOGIES ASSOCIATED WITH ENZYMATIC INHIBITION. TO TEST THIS, WE WILL FIRST (AIM 1) USE STRUCTURE-INFORMED DESIGN AND CRISPR/CAS9 ENGINEERING TO GENERATE AND RIGOROUSLY VALIDATE A NOVEL KNOCK-IN MOUSE MODEL THAT GENETICALLY RECAPITULATES THE BIOCHEMICAL SIGNATURE OF A THERAPEUTIC GSM (NCSTN-I241D). WE WILL THEN (AIM 2) PERFORM A DIRECT, HEAD-TO- HEAD COMPARISON BETWEEN THIS NEW GSM-MIMIC AND OUR EXISTING “TOXIC” GSI-MIMIC (NCSTN-V439G) LINE USING DEEP PROTEOMIC PROFILING AND HIGH-RESOLUTION ELECTRON MICROSCOPY TO DEFINE THE MOLECULAR AND ULTRASTRUCTURAL SIGNATURES OF “SAFE” MODULATION VERSUS “TOXIC” INHIBITION, WITH EMPHASIS ON ENDOLYSOSOMAL AND TAU NETWORK INTEGRITY. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE THE FIRST DIRECT IN VIVO EVIDENCE FOR THE LONG-TERM SAFETY OF THE GSM MECHANISM, RESOLVING A KEY QUESTION THAT HAS STALLED ALZHEIMER’S DRUG DEVELOPMENT. THIS WORK WILL YIELD A PERMANENT GENETIC PLATFORM FOR SAFELY DISSECTING G-SECRETASE FUNCTION IN VIVO AND WILL ESTABLISH A MECHANISTICALLY INFORMED FOUNDATION FOR NEXT-GENERATION PHARMACOLOGICAL AND GENE-BASED THERAPIES FOR DEMENTIA.

description: HEALTH OUTCOMES FOLLOWING ENROLLMENT IN MEDICARE AMONG OLDER PEOPLE WITH HIV - EFFECTIVE ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART ) HAS TRANSFORMED HIV INTO A MANAGEABLE CHRONIC CONDITION, RESULTING IN A RAPIDLY AGING POPULATION OF PEOPLE WITH HIV (PWH). ADULTS AGED 􀀄65 ARE NOW THE FASTEST GROWING GROUP OF PWH IN THE U.S. AND FACE COMPLEX HEALTH NEEDS, INCLUDING HIGH RATES OF COMORBID CHRONIC CONDITIONS AND LIFELONG RELIANCE ON ART. AGE 65 REPRESENTS A CRITICAL TRANSITION POINT WHEN MANY PWH BECOME NEWLY ELIGIBLE FOR MEDICARE. FOR PWH, SUCCESSFUL NAVIGATION OF MEDICARE ENROLLMENT AND CONTINUITY OF COVERAGE IS ESSENTIAL TO MAINTAINING UNINTERRUPTED ACCESS TO ART AND HIV CARE. YET MEDICARE COVERAGE IS COMPLEX, OFTEN INCOMPLETE, AND HIGHLY VARIABLE ACROSS PLANS, CREATING RISK FOR COVERAGE GAPS, HIGH OUT-OF-POCKET COSTS, AND DISRUPTIONS TO HIV CARE. PWH FREQUENTLY MUST NAVIGATE MULTIPLE PAYERS AND ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS, INCLUDING MEDICARE, MEDICAID, AND RYAN WHITE-FUNDED SERVICES. GUIDANCE IS TYPICALLY PROVIDED BY ADVISORS WITH EITHER HIV-SPECIFIC EXPERTISE OR MEDICARE EXPERTISE, BUT RARELY BOTH. CHALLENGES ARE PARTICULARLY ACUTE IN THE SOUTHERN U.S., WHICH BEARS A DISPROPORTIONATE HIV BURDEN AND INCLUDES SEVERAL STATES WITH POORLY PERFORMING MEDICARE SYSTEMS. DESPITE THE SIZE AND VULNERABILITY OF THIS POPULATION, LITTLE RESEARCH HAS EXAMINED HOW PWH EXPERIENCE THE MEDICARE TRANSITION AND ONGOING COVERAGE, HOW INSURANCE-RELATED CHALLENGES AFFECT HIV CARE AND ART ADHERENCE, OR HOW ADVISORS SUPPORT PWH. TO ADDRESS THIS CRITICAL GAP, WE PROPOSE AN EXPLORATORY MIXED­METHODS STUDY ACROSS FIVE SOUTHERN STATES TO CHARACTERIZE MEDICARE NAVIGATION EXPERIENCES AMONG PWH AND THE ADVISORS WHO ASSIST THEM, AND TO EXAMINE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN INSURANCE-RELATED CHALLENGES AND HEALTH BEHAVIORS AND OUTCOMES. IN AIM 1, WE WILL CONDUCT QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS WITH PWH AGED 􀀄65 (N=35) AND WITH HEALTH BENEFIT ADVISORS, INCLUDING RYAN WHITE NON-MEDICAL CASE MANAGERS (N=15) AND STATE HEALTH INSURANCE ASSISTANCE PROGRAM ADVISORS (N=15). INTERVIEWS WILL EXAMINE BARRIERS TO ENROLLMENT OR CONTINUITY, COVERAGE STABILITY, FINANCIAL BURDEN, SOURCES OF ASSISTANCE, AND PERCEIVED EFFECTS ON HIV CARE AND ART ACCESS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ADMINISTER A SURVEY TO PWH AGED 􀀄65 (N=300) TO ASSESS PATTERNS OF INSURANCE-RELATED CHALLENGES DURING AND AFTER THE MEDICARE TRANSITION AND THEIR ASSOCIATIONS WITH ART ADHERENCE, CARE ENGAGEMENT, VIRAL SUPPRESSION, SELF-RATED HEALTH, ACUTE CARE USE, AND QUALITY OF LIFE. FINDINGS WILL INFORM IMPROVED BENEFIT NAVIGATION FOR OLDER PWH AND GUIDE DEVELOPMENT OF TARGETED INTERVENTIONS TO STRENGTHEN CONTINUITY OF HIV CARE IN AN AGING POPULATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EVALUATING HOW BIPA CONTRIBUTES TO YERSINIA PESTIS PATHOGENESIS DURING PNEUMONIC PLAGUE - PROJECT SUMMARY YERSINIA PESTIS IS ONE OF THE DEADLIEST PATHOGENS KNOWN TO MAN. DUE TO ITS SUCCESS AS A PATHOGEN, STUDY OF Y. PESTIS HAS BEEN CRITICAL TO OUR UNDERSTANDING OF BACTERIAL PATHOGENESIS AS A FIELD. THIS PROPOSAL INTRODUCES BACTERICIDAL PERMEABILITY-INCREASING PROTEIN (BPI)-INDUCED PROTEIN A (BIPA) AS AN IMPORTANT VIRULENCE FACTOR THAT REGULATES SPECIFIC PROTEINS THAT PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN THE HOST/PATHOGEN INTERACTIONS THAT DEFINE PNEUMONIC PLAGUE. BIPA REGULATES PROTEINS AT THE TRANSLATIONAL LEVEL, AND WE SHOW THAT IT CONTRIBUTES TO Y. PESTIS ADHERENCE TO MAMMALIAN CELLS AND RESISTANCE TO NEUTROPHIL-MEDIATED KILLING OF BACTERIA. THUS, BIPA AIDS Y. PESTIS IN SUBVERTING HOST DEFENSE STRATEGIES DURING PNEUMONIC PLAGUE. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS WORK IS TO DEFINE THE FUNCTION OF THE BIPA IN THE EARLY EVENTS OF PNEUMONIC PLAGUE, AND TO IDENTIFY PROTEINS REGULATED BY BIPA THAT CONTRIBUTE TO PATHOGENESIS. OUR PRELIMINARY WORK SHOWS THAT BIPA 1. MAY REGULATE PROTEINS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO BACTERIAL ADHERENCE. 2. CONTRIBUTES TO BACTERIAL RESISTANCE TO BPI AND NEUTROPHILS; AND 3. SPECIFICALLY REGULATES A NUMBER OF PROTEINS UPON ITS INDUCTION BY BPI. IN THIS PROPOSAL WE WILL USE BACTERIAL MUTANTS IN TANDEM WITH IN VITRO, EX VIVO, AND IN VIVO MURINE INFECTION TO DETERMINE IF BIPA CONTRIBUTES TO ADHERENCE, IF THE ROLE OF BIPA IN RESISTANCE TO BPI IS IMPORTANT IN VIVO, AND WE WILL IDENTIFY BIPA-REGULATED PROTEINS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO VIRULENCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DETERMINING THE ROLE FOR LNCRNAS IN TB INFECTION IN MACROPHAGES - PROJECT SUMMARY MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB) IS AN INCREDIBLY SUCCESSFUL PATHOGEN THAT SURVIVES AND REPLICATES IN INNATE IMMUNE CELLS LIKE MACROPHAGES. ALTHOUGH WE KNOW A LOT ABOUT THE CYTOKINES AND CHEMOKINES EXPRESSED BY MACROPHAGES IN RESPONSE TO MTB, THE CO- AND POST-TRANSCRIPTIONAL MECHANISMS THAT TURN THESE RESPONSES ON AND OFF REMAIN ELUSIVE. BECAUSE DISRUPTION OF THE EARLY INFLAMMATORY MILIEU PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN DETERMINING WHETHER MTB IS CONTROLLED OR GOES ON TO CAUSE ACUTE DISEASE, IT IS IMPORTANT THAT WE FULLY APPRECIATE THE COMPLEXITY OF THE INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE TO MTB. THERE IS INCREASING APPRECIATION FOR POST-TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATORY MECHANISMS IN CONTROLLING THE TIMING AND ABUNDANCE OF INNATE IMMUNE PROTEIN EXPRESSION IN MACROPHAGES. LONG NON-CODING RNAS (LNCRNAS), DEFINED AS TRANSCRIPTS GREATER THAN 500NT IN LENGTH THAT DO NOT CODE FOR PROTEIN, REPRESENT A MASSIVE FAMILY OF RNAS WITH THE POTENTIAL TO MODULATE INFLAMMATORY GENE EXPRESSION AND INFECTION OUTCOMES. ALTHOUGH THE HUMAN GENOME ENCODES OVER 20,000 LNCRNAS, WE ONLY UNDERSTAND THE FUNCTION OF A TINY FRACTION OF THESE. A MAJOR REASON OUR UNDERSTANDING OF LNCRNAS HAS LAGGED BEHIND THAT OF PROTEIN CODING GENES IS THAT TRADITIONAL CAS9-MEDIATED GENE EDITING, WHICH INDUCES DISRUPTIVE INSERTIONS OR DELETIONS WITHIN OPEN READING FRAMES (ORFS), IS INEFFECTIVE FOR LNCRNAS, AS THEY LACK ORFS. THE CARPENTER LAB HAS PIONEERED INNOVATIVE APPROACHES TO OVERCOME THIS LIMITATION; NOTABLY BY GENERATING CRISPRI LIBRARIES IN MOUSE AND HUMAN MACROPHAGES. THROUGH A PRELIMINARY SCREEN OF A LNCRNA CRISPRI LIBRARY ENGINEERED WITH A NFKB REPORTER GENE, THE CARPENTER, PATRICK, AND WATSON LABS IDENTIFIED 12 LNCRNAS REQUIRED FOR NFKB ACTIVATION WHOSE INVOLVEMENT IN MTB INFECTION WAS PREVIOUSLY UNREPORTED. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO FOLLOW UP ON THESE HITS AND EXPAND ON THIS SUCCESS. SPECIFICALLY, AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE THE ROLE OF CONSERVED CANDIDATE LNCRNAS IN REGULATING MACROPHAGE GENE EXPRESSION DURING MTB INFECTION. AIM 2 WILL IDENTIFY LNCRNAS THAT CONTROL MTB REPLICATION USING CRISPRI SCREENING OF HUMAN AND MURINE MACROPHAGES. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT MANY LNCRNAS ARE INVOLVED IN MOUNTING ANTIMYCOBACTERIAL DEFENSES, EITHER THROUGH REGULATING KNOWN INFLAMMATORY GENES/SIGNALING PATHWAYS OR BY ENCODING NOVEL SMALL ORFS. BY SCREENING ALL LNCRNAS IN HUMANS AND MICE, WE WILL OBTAIN UNPRECEDENTED INSIGHT INTO THE ROLE THESE TRANSCRIPTS PLAY IN ANTIBACTERIAL DEFENSES AND PINPOINT LNCRNAS MOST LIKELY TO PLAY A ROLE IN TUBERCULOSIS DISEASE– AS MEDIATORS OF PATHOGENESIS, PATIENT BIOMARKERS, AND POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EVOLUTIONARY PATHWAYS TO ANTIVIRAL RESISTANCE FOR INFLUENZA VIRUS - INFLUENZA VIRUS PRESENTS A RECURRING THREAT. EVOLUTION AT THE GLOBAL SCALE RESULTS IN GENETIC DRIFT AND SEASONAL EPIDEMICS, NECESSITATING ANNUAL UPDATES TO THE INFLUENZA VACCINE. NEW, EVOLUTIONARILY ADVANCED VARIANTS THAT ACQUIRE BENEFICIAL PHENOTYPES LIKE DRUG RESISTANCE OR IMMUNE ESCAPE MUST ARISE AND BE TRANSMITTED FROM INDIVIDUAL INFECTED HOSTS, AND YET, SUCH VARIANTS DETECTED ON THE GLOBAL SCALE ARE RARELY SEEN IN ACUTE INFECTIONS. INSTEAD, DIVERSITY WITHIN IN AN INDIVIDUAL IS LOW AND VARIANTS WITH A POTENTIAL FITNESS ADVANTAGE RARELY RISE TO HIGH FREQUENCY. THIS LEAVE A MAJOR KNOWLEDGE GAP – HOW DO FITTER VARIANTS ARISE WITHIN AN INDIVIDUAL TO ALLOW THEIR ULTIMATE TRANSMISSION, SELECTION AND POTENTIAL FIXATION AT THE POPULATION LEVEL? ANSWERING THIS QUESTION IS A PREREQUISITE FOR ACCURATELY PREDICTING ANTIGENIC VARIATION, THE EMERGENCE OF DRUG RESISTANCE, SEASONAL EPIDEMICS, AND OCCASIONAL GLOBAL PANDEMICS. TO BEGIN TO ADDRESS THIS, WE SEEK TO OBTAIN A CLEAR UNDERSTANDING OF THE VERY FIRST STEP IN THE PROCESS WHEN VARIANTS ARISE AND ARE THEN SELECTED. THESE TYPES OF QUESTIONS HAVE BEEN OUT OF REACH, AS THE RELATIVELY LOW LEVELS OF NATURALLY OCCURRING VARIATION WITHIN VIRAL POPULATIONS DO NOT PROVIDE SUFFICIENT INFORMATION FOR FINE-GRAINED ANALYSIS OF POPULATION DYNAMICS. WE OVERCAME THIS LIMITATION BY ENGINEERING VIRAL LIBRARIES ENCODING RANDOM NUCLEOTIDE BARCODES ON THE PA SEGMENT OF THE INFLUENZA VIRUS GENOME, CREATING RICH VIRAL POPULATIONS WITH OVER 105 UNIQUELY QUANTIFIABLE MEMBERS. THIS TECHNICAL INNOVATION HAS US POISED TO UNDERSTAND HOW ADAPTIVE VARIANTS ARISE, POTENTIALLY GET SELECTED, AND ALTER PHENOTYPES IN VIRAL POPULATIONS. IN AIM 1 WE WILL DEFINE THE PROCESSES THAT ALLOW INFLUENZA VIRUS TO REPLICATE IN THE PRESENCE OF AN EXPERIMENTAL SMALL-MOLECULE INHIBITOR. WE WILL USE OUR BARCODED VIRUSES TO IDENTIFY AND QUANTIFY VARIANT LINEAGES. EVOLUTIONARY ANALYSIS WILL ALSO REVEAL HOW THESE VARIANTS EMERGE AT THE POPULATION LEVEL, AND POSSIBLE TRADEOFFS THE VIRUSES FACES. HAVING ESTABLISHED THESE “GROUND RULES” IN AN IDEALIZED SETTING, AIM 2 WILL THEN INVESTIGATE HOW SELECTION DRIVES THE EMERGENCE OF VIRAL VARIANTS IN VIVO. THESE RESULTS WILL INFORM HOW VARIANTS ARISE IN AN INDIVIDUAL ESTABLISHING THE POTENTIAL TO BECOME THE DOMINANT LINEAGE IN THE GLOBAL POPULATION. TOGETHER, THIS WORK WILL ELUCIDATE FUNDAMENTAL PROPERTIES OF EVOLUTIONARY SELECTION DURING INFLUENZA VIRUS INFECTION, AND HOW THESE RULES ARE RESHAPED DURING REPLICATION IN VIVO.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SINGLE-CELL ANALYSIS OF ANTIBIOTIC PERSISTER SUBPOPULATIONS GENERATED BY ACINETOBACTER BAUMANNII - BACTERIAL DISEASES IN HOSPITAL SETTINGS SIGNIFICANTLY HINDER PATIENT CARE. A MAJOR CONCERN AMONG PATIENTS UNDERGOING RESPIRATORY THERAPY IS THE RISE OF MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT ORGANISMS. THESE ORGANISMS ARE EMBEDDED IN HEALTHCARE ENVIRONMENTS AND UNDERGO EVOLUTIONARY SELECTION AMONG RESIDENTS TREATED WITH MULTIPLE CLASSES OF ANTIBIOTICS. OF PARTICULAR CONCERN IS ACINETOBACTER BAUMANNII, AS THIS BACTERIUM HAS DEVELOPED RESISTANCE TO MOST COMMONLY USED ANTIBIOTICS, WITH RESISTANCE TO CARBAPENEMS BEING THE MOST ALARMING THREAT. EVIDENCE INCREASINGLY INDICATES THAT DRUG-RESISTANT ISOLATES EVOLVE FROM SENSITIVE ORGANISMS IN THESE ENVIRONMENTS, ORIGINATING FROM BACTERIAL SUBPOPULATIONS THAT SURVIVE ANTIBIOTIC EXPOSURE. THESE SUBPOPULATIONS, WHICH CANNOT GROW WHEN EXPOSED TO THE DRUG BUT CAN TOLERATE ITS PRESENCE, CAN MULTIPLY AS DRUG CONCENTRATIONS DECREASE WITHIN THE PATIENT. HIGH LEVELS OF TOLERANT SUBPOPULATIONS ARE ESPECIALLY WORRISOME BECAUSE THEY HAVE BEEN DIRECTLY LINKED TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF DRUG-RESISTANT CLINICAL ISOLATES. THEREFORE, WHEN ANTIBIOTIC LEVELS FLUCTUATE IN PATIENT TISSUES, TOLERANT SUBPOPULATIONS PROLIFERATE, GENERATING A POOL THAT ALLOWS THE SELECTION OF DRUG-RESISTANT MUTANTS. A MAJOR KNOWLEDGE GAP EXISTS REGARDING HOW DRUG RESISTANCE EVOLVES: LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THE PHYSIOLOGICAL STATES THAT LEAD TO THE FORMATION OF THESE TOLERANT SUBPOPULATIONS OR WHICH GENETIC FACTORS ARE ESSENTIAL FOR SURVIVAL AND RECOVERY FROM DRUG TREATMENT.  THIS APPLICATION AIMS TO BRIDGE THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP BY FOCUSING ON IDENTIFYING THE GENES THAT ARE CRUCIAL FOR ESTABLISHING A BACTERIAL SUBPOPULATION THAT TOLERATES THE B-LACTAM ANTIBIOTIC CARBENICILLIN. TO THIS END, IT EXPLOITS AN A. BAUMANNII MUTANT THAT DRIVES MOST CELLS INTO THIS HYPERTOLERANT STATE. TAKING ADVANTAGE OF THIS TECHNOLOGICAL BREAKTHROUGH, SUBPOPULATIONS IN AN OTHERWISE WILD-TYPE A. BAUMANNII STRAIN WILL BE IDENTIFIED THAT SHARE A GENE EXPRESSION SIGNATURE WITH THE MAJORITY POPULATION OF THE HYPERTOLERANT MUTANT. TO CHARACTERIZE THIS TOLERANCE-INDUCING PROGRAM, SINGLE-CELL RNA SEQUENCING (SCRNASEQ) TECHNOLOGY WILL BE USED, ALONG WITH FLUORESCENT REPORTERS THAT MARK THESE SUBPOPULATIONS. THESE TOOLS WILL DETERMINE WHETHER THE HYPOTHESIZED TOLERANT SUBPOPULATION OF THE WILD TYPE DEMONSTRATES HIGH VIABILITY AFTER ANTIBIOTIC CHALLENGE. ONCE THE APPROPRIATE SUBPOPULATION IS IDENTIFIED, MUTATIONS WILL BE CONSTRUCTED TO ELIMINATE THE PRODUCTION OF PROTEINS CLOSELY ASSOCIATED WITH THIS GROUP OF TOLERANT CELLS. THIS WILL HELP ASSESS WHETHER TOLERANCE TO CARBENICILLIN DECREASES AS A RESULT OF MUTATIONAL LOSS. BASED ON PRELIMINARY RESULTS AND DATA COLLECTED IN THIS PROJECT, THE GOAL IS TO DEVELOP A UNIFIED MODEL THAT CONNECTS PREVIOUS FINDINGS ON THE ROLE OF TRANSLATIONAL MISREGULATION IN PROMOTING SURVIVAL DURING ANTIBIOTIC TREATMENT WITH INSIGHTS GAINED FROM ANALYZING THE TOLERANT SUBPOPULATION.

description: IDENTIFYING PLASMODIUM LIVER-STAGE SECRETED EFFECTOR PROTEINS - PROJECT SUMMARY MALARIA, CAUSED BY PLASMODIUM, REMAINS A GLOBAL HEALTH CRISIS, WITH OVER 250 MILLION CASES AND 600,000 DEATHS ANNUALLY. THE LIVER STAGE OF INFECTION IS A CRITICAL BOTTLENECK, WHERE PLASMODIUM INVADES HEPATOCYTES, REPLICATES, AND PROGRESSES TO THE BLOOD STAGE. WHILE HEPATOCYTES MOUNT ROBUST CELL-INTRINSIC IMMUNE RE- SPONSES TO ELIMINATE THE PARASITE, SOME PLASMODIUM PARASITES EVADE THESE DEFENSES, SUGGESTING PARASITE- DERIVED MECHANISMS TO SUBVERT HOST IMMUNITY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT PLASMODIUM EXPORTS EFFECTOR PROTEINS INTO THE HEPATOCYTE CYTOPLASM, NUCLEUS, OR THE PARASITOPHOROUS VACUOLE MEMBRANE (PVM) TO NEUTRALIZE HOST IMMUNE RESPONSES, ENABLING SURVIVAL. THIS EXPLORATORY R21 PROPOSAL AIMS TO DEFINE THE SECRETOME AND IN- TERACTOME OF THE HUMAN MALARIA PARASITE PLASMODIUM FALCIPARUM (PF) AND THE MOUSE MALARIA PARASITE P. BERGHEI (PB) IN HEPATOCYTES. USING PROXIMITY-DEPENDENT BIOTINYLATION (MINITURBOID AND SPLIT-TURBOID) COUPLED WITH MICRO-PROTEOMICS AND HIGH-SENSITIVITY MASS SPECTROMETRY, WE WILL IDENTIFY PLASMODIUM PROTEINS EXPORTED TO THE HEPATOCYTE CYTOPLASM, NUCLEUS, AND PVM (SUB-AIM 1). WE WILL VALIDATE THE EXPRESSION AND LOCALIZATION OF THE CANDIDATE EFFECTORS USING CRISPR/CAS9-MEDIATED ENDOGENOUS TAGGING AND IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE MI- CROSCOPY (SUB-AIM 2). THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE MAP OF LIVER-STAGE PLASMODIUM EXPORTED PROTEINS IN HEPATOCYTES, UNCOVERING CANDIDATES THAT ARE LIKELY TO MEDIATE IMMUNE EVASION AND HOST-CELL RE- MODELING. BY IDENTIFYING CONSERVED EFFECTOR PROTEINS AND DEFINING WHEN AND WHERE THEY ACT IN THE INFECTED CELL, THIS WORK WILL LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE DISSECTION OF THEIR HOST TARGETS AND MECHANISMS OF ACTION. ULTIMATELY, THESE DISCOVERIES WILL ENABLE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL STRATEGIES TO BLOCK PARASITE SURVIVAL IN THE LIVER, POTENTIALLY LEADING TO NEW PROPHYLACTIC OR THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS. LEVERAGING CUTTING-EDGE PROTEOMIC AND MOLECULAR TOOLS, OUR PROPOSED RESEARCH ADDRESSES A CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE-GAP IN PLASMODIUM BIOLOGY AND HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM OUR UNDERSTANDING OF LIVER-STAGE MALARIA.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MULTIKINGDOM GENERATION AND TISSUE MAINTENANCE OF SPLENIC IGA PLASMA CELLS - ABSTRACT B LYMPHOCYTES THAT COME IN CONTACT WITH COMMENSAL MICROBES IN THE GUT MOUNT A SPECIFIC RESPONSE THAT LEADS TO THE GENERATION OF IMMUNOGLOBULIN A (IGA)-SECRETING PLASMA CELLS. IGA IS ESSENTIAL FOR PREVENTING COMMENSAL OUTGROWTH AND MAINTAINING INTESTINAL HOMEOSTASIS. INDEED, IGA-SECRETING PLASMA CELLS ARE ROUTINELY LOCALIZED IN THE INTESTINAL LAMINA PROPRIA, WHERE THEY CAN SECRETE ANTIBODY IN THE GUT LUMEN. HOWEVER, IGA CAN BE EASILY MEASURED IN CIRCULATION IN HUMAN AND MICE, AND IGA-SECRETING PLASMA CELLS CAN BE FOUND IN THE BONE MARROW, POINTING TO A SYSTEMIC IGA RESPONSE. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUPPORT THE EXISTENCE OF A NOVEL, COMPLEX NICHE FOR IGA-SECRETING PLASMA CELLS IN THE SPLEEN, WHICH MIGHT UNDERPIN BOTH SYSTEMIC AND LOCAL HUMORAL IMMUNITY. HOWEVER, THE REGULATION OF EXTRA-GUT IGA RESPONSE REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THEREFORE, ELUCIDATING THE FUNDAMENTAL MECHANISMS THAT REGULATE THE GENERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF IGA- SECRETING PLASMA CELLS IN THE SPLEEN REPRESENTS A CENTRAL, UNANSWERED, QUESTION IN TISSUE IMMUNOLOGY. PREVIOUS RESEARCH HAS IDENTIFIED IGA RESPONSE AGAINST DIFFERENT COMMENSAL KINGDOMS, AND SUGGESTS THAT IGA- SECRETING PLASMA CELLS MIGHT BE TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND FUNCTIONAL DIFFERENT TO IGG- AND IGM-SECRETING PLASMA CELLS. HOWEVER, THE EXTRINSIC AND INTRINSIC SIGNALS THAT CONTROL THE GENERATION AND POSITIONING OF IGA PLASMA CELLS IN THE SPLEEN REMAIN UNKNOWN. IN THIS APPLICATION WE TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT COMMENSAL BACTERIA AND COMMENSAL FUNGI GENERATE A QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT IGA RESPONSE. THIS RESPONSE ENDOWS IGA PLASMA CELLS WITH MIGRATORY RECEPTORS THAT DIRECT THEM TO DISTINCT SUB-ANATOMICAL NICHES IN THE SPLEEN. WE ALSO HYPOTHESIZE THAT INTRACELLULAR SIGNALING DIFFERS IN IGA PLASMA CELLS FOUND IN DIFFERENT AREA OF THE SPLEEN, DICTATING THEIR RESIDENCY OR EGRESS. OUR AIMS ARE: 1) TO IDENTIFY THE INTRINSIC AND EXTRINSIC CUES THAT DRIVE IGA PLASMA CELLS IN ANATOMICAL NICHES, WITH SPECIAL FOCUS ON MIGRATORY RECEPTORS THAT CONTROL IGA PC POSITION IN THE SPLEEN AND THEIR ROLE IN SUPPORTING A PROTECTIVE HUMORAL RESPONSE AGAINST PATHOGENS FROM DIFFERENT KINGDOMS; AND 2) TO DISSECT SIGNALING PATHWAYS THAT REGULATE IGA PLASMA CELLS RESIDENCY IN THE SPLEEN. THE PROPOSED STUDIES EXAMINE THE POORLY UNDERSTOOD GENERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF IGA PLASMA CELLS FOUND IN THE SPLEEN. IT IS OUR EXPECTATION THAT THESE STUDIES WILL INCREASE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW INTESTINAL COMMENSALS SHAPES B CELL RESPONSES AT DISTAL ANATOMICAL SITES FROM THE GUT. FURTHERMORE, THESE STUDIES WILL PROVIDE A FOUNDATION FOR A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DIFFERENT COMMENSAL KINGDOMS AND HUMORAL IMMUNITY IN TISSUES AND CIRCULATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CYTOSOLIC COPPER ION ACCUMULATION AND PROTEOME INTEGRITY. - PROJECT SUMMARY STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS IS A HUMAN COMMENSAL AND A LEADING CAUSE OF HOSPITAL- AND COMMUNITY-ACQUIRED INFECTIONS. ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE IN THE STAPHYLOCOCCI AND OTHER ESKAPE BACTERIAL PATHOGENS IS INCREASINGLY CONCERNING. INFECTIONS CAUSED BY ANTIBIOTIC-RESISTANT S. AUREUS RESULT IN HIGHER MORTALITY RATES, PROLONGED HOSPITAL STAYS, AND AN INCREASED FINANCIAL BURDEN. THESE FACTS UNDERSCORE THE GROWING DEMAND AND NECESSITY FOR IDENTIFYING INNOVATIVE ANTIMICROBIAL TARGETS, DISCOVERING NEW ANTIMICROBIALS, REPURPOSING EXISTING ANTIMICROBIALS, AND DEVELOPING NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES. COPPER (CU), IN BOTH IONIC AND METALLIC FORMS, HAS BEEN USED AS AN ANTIMICROBIAL FOR MILLENNIA. DUE TO THEIR EFFECTIVENESS AND THE GROWING PROBLEM OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE, THERE HAS BEEN A RENEWED INTEREST IN USING METALS TO DECREASE BACTERIAL VIABILITY IN HEALTHCARE, INDUSTRIAL, AND HOME SETTINGS. ALL S. AUREUS STRAINS EMPLOY EFFLUX PUMPS TO REMOVE CU(I) IONS AND CYTOSOLIC PROTEINS TO BUFFER AGAINST CU ION TOXICITY. THE HUMAN BODY UTILIZES CU IONS TO FACILITATE BACTERIAL CLEARANCE, AND STRAINS OF S. AUREUS THAT ARE DEFECTIVE IN REMOVING CU(I) FROM THE CYTOSOL EXHIBIT DECREASED VIRULENCE IN INFECTION MODELS. UNDERSTANDING HOW CU IONS TOXIFY S. AUREUS WILL SHED LIGHT ON MECHANISMS AND STRATEGIES THE MAMMALIAN IMMUNE SYSTEM UTILIZES TO PREVENT INFECTION. WE HAVE PROVIDED PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATING THAT CU(II) TREATMENT INCREASES PROTEIN MISFOLDING AND AGGREGATION IN S. AUREUS. WE ALSO DEMONSTRATE THAT CHEMICAL INHIBITION OF THE PROTEIN MAINTENANCE MACHINERY SYNERGIZES WITH CU(II) TO KILL BACTERIA. THIS BIOMEDICALLY RELEVANT AND INNOVATIVE PROPOSAL WILL ADDRESS THE FOLLOWING OBJECTIVES: A) CHARACTERIZE AN UNDERSTUDIED MECHANISM OF CU ION TOXICITY, B) DETERMINE THE ROLE OF THE PROTEIN HOMEOSTASIS MACHINERY IN PREVENTING CU ION TOXICITY, C) DETERMINE WHY MUTATIONS IN RPOB AND RPOC INCREASE TOLERANCE TO CU IONS, AND D) EXPLORE THE SYNERGY BETWEEN INHIBITORS OF MOLECULAR CHAPERONES AND CU IONS. COMPLETING THE HYPOTHESIS-DRIVEN WORK WILL FURTHER OUR UNDERSTANDING OF METAL ION HOMEOSTASIS AND IMBALANCE AND LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR DESIGNING AND IMPLEMENTING METAL-BASED ANTIMICROBIAL CHEMOTHERAPY. OUR FINDINGS COULD SHED LIGHT ON CONSERVED METABOLIC PARADIGMS AND DEFECTS IN CU ION HOMEOSTASIS, WHICH IS RESPONSIBLE FOR SEVERAL HUMAN DISEASES. ULTIMATELY, WE AIM TO APPLY OUR FINDINGS TO REDUCE THE BURDEN OF BACTERIAL PATHOGENS USING CU IONS, THEREBY PREVENTING OR POSITIVELY AFFECTING INFECTION OUTCOMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DECODING COCCIDIOIDES: AN LLM AI APPROACH TO GENOMIC, PHENOTYPIC, AND CLINICAL CHARACTERIZATION OF 200 CLINICAL ISOLATES - INTRODUCTION: VALLEY FEVER IS A FUNGAL DISEASE ESTIMATED TO CAUSE > 200,000 INFECTIONS YEARLY. THE IMPACT OF GENOMIC FEATURES ON CLINICAL DISEASE IS LARGELY UNEXPLORED. DURING ANTIFUNGAL THERAPY, THE DISEASE ONLY HAS ONE SPECIFIC MARKER, ANTIBODY TITERS, WHICH IS ONLY SEMI- QUANTITATIVE AND SLOWLY RESPONSIVE TO CLINICAL CHANGES. BETTER PROGNOSTIC MARKERS ARE NEEDED. LONG-TERM OBJECTIVE: THE GOAL OF THE LABORATORY IS TO DEVELOP BETTER DIAGNOSTIC AND PROGNOSTIC MARKERS OF COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS. DATA FROM THIS STUDY WILL CONTRIBUTE SIGNIFICANT INFORMATION TO THE FIELD OF VALLEY FEVER AND OPEN NEW AREAS FOR RESEARCH THAT WILL IMPROVE HUMAN HEALTH. NOT-AI-23-031 NOTICE OF SPECIAL INTEREST (NOSI): ADVANCING RESEARCH NEEDED TO DEVELOP A COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS (VALLEY FEVER) VACCINE. THIS PROJECT DIRECTLY SUPPORTS THE NIH NOSI FOR COCCIDIOIDES BY INCREASING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF CLINICAL DATA AND DEVELOP BETTER PROGNOSTIC MARKERS USING OUR COMPLEX LONGITUDINAL ABSTRACTION TOOL (CLAT) AND OUR GENOMIC DATA WILL INFORM THE POTENTIAL ROBUSTNESS OF VACCINE CANDIDATES BY PROVIDING A BROADER UNDERSTANDING OF THE COCCIDIOIDES GENOMIC SPACE. HYPOTHESES: 1 GENOMIC DIFFERENCES IN COCCIDIOIDES SPP. ARE LINKED TO CLINICAL PATHOLOGICAL CATEGORIES (E.G., PULMONARY, EXTRAPULMONARY, MENINGITIS) AND OUTCOME (RESOLUTION, SEVERE/CHRONIC DISEASE, DEATH). 2. DEEP ANNOTATION OF LONGITUDINAL PATIENT DATA (SYMPTOMS, LAB RESULTS, AND RADIOLOGY, ETC.) MAY REVEAL PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN LINKS OF CLINICAL FEATURES (E.G., ERYTHEMA NODOSUM, FATIGUE, ETC.) TO FUNGAL STRAIN. SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1: SEQUENCE THE 200 CLINICAL ISOLATES OF COCCIDIOIDES SPP. AND PERFORM GENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDIES IN CONTEXT OF CLINICAL DISEASE FEATURES. AIM 2: USING THE CLAT, ABSTRACT THE COURSE OF DISEASE FOR THE PATIENTS FROM WHICH THE 200 ISOLATES GREW. AIM 3: ANALYZE THE DATA USING A LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL (LLM) WITH A MODEL CONTEXT PROTOCOL (MCP). EXPECTED OUTCOMES AND IMPACT: WE WILL COMPLETE PRELIMINARY ANALYSES OF THE GENOMES AND ASSOCIATIONS OF CERTAIN REGIONS/FEATURES TO CLINICAL DISEASE. THE GENOMES WILL BE DEPOSITED INTO A PUBLIC DATABASE. THE ASSOCIATION OF GENOMES TO HIGHLY DETAILED PATIENT DATA MAY REVEAL HOW SOME GENOMIC REGIONS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH SPECIFIC DISEASE PRESENTATIONS. THESE ASSOCIATIONS MAY PROVIDE BOTH DIAGNOSTIC AND PROGNOSTIC INSIGHTS THAT COULD INFORM PATHOGENIC MECHANISMS AND TREATMENT APPROACHES. THE ANALYSIS USING THE LLM AND MCP MODELS WILL PROVIDE FOR DEEP AND ITERATIVE INQUIRY INTO OUR COMPLEX DATASET, MAXIMIZING THE CONCLUSIONS THAT CAN BE DRAWN FROM THE DATA.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EVOLUTION OF MULTI-DRUG RESISTANCE IN CANDIDA AURIS IN VITRO AND IN PATIENTS UNDERGOING ANTIFUNGAL TREATMENT - PROJECT SUMMARY CANDIDA AURIS IS A NEWLY EMERGED HUMAN FUNGAL PATHOGEN ASSOCIATED WITH AN EXPONENTIAL RISE IN INVASIVE CANDIDIASIS WORLDWIDE WITH MORTALITY RATES APPROACHING 68%. MOST CONCERNING IS THE UNIQUE ABILITY OF C. AURIS TO DEVELOP MULTIDRUG RESISTANCE TO ALL MAIN CLASSES OF ANTIFUNGALS. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CLINICAL ANTIFUNGAL THERAPY INDUCES DEVELOPMENT OF DRUG RESISTANCE IN C. AURIS AS WELL PHENOTYPIC AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL ALTERATIONS IMPACTING CELL FUNCTION, FITNESS AND PATHOGENIC POTENTIAL. TO THAT END, PROSPECTIVELY RECOVERED ISOLATES WHICH HAVE ACQUIRED MULTI-DRUG RESISTANCE IN PATIENTS DURING THERAPY WILL BE COMPREHENSIVELY EVALUATED FOR PHENOTYPIC, GENOMIC, AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL ALTERATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH DRUG RESISTANCE, CELL FUNCTION AND FITNESS. WHEN COMPLETED, THE PROPOSED AIMS WILL PROVIDE MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO HOW C. AURIS EVOLVES AND ADAPTS TO STRESSES TO ENSURE SURVIVAL IN THE HOST. IMPORTANTLY, THE FINDINGS GENERATED WILL AID IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF POTENTIAL ADJUNCTIVE/COMBINATORIAL THERAPIES TO OVERCOME DRUG RESISTANCE OR IDENTIFY NEW TARGETS TO ENHANCE EFFECTIVENESS OF ANTIFUNGALS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: F1FO ATP SYNTHASE INHIBITORS AS NEW DRUG LEADS FOR THE TREATMENT OF PRIMARY AMOEBIC MENINGOENCEPHALITIS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT NAEGLERIA FOWLERI IS RESPONSIBLE FOR SEVERE PRIMARY AMOEBIC MENINGOENCEPHALITIS (PAM), WHICH MOSTLY OCCURS IN HEALTHY CHILDREN AND YOUNG ADULTS WITH RECENT RECREATIONAL FRESHWATER EXPOSURE. N. FOWLERI INFECTION IS PARTICULARLY PROBLEMATIC DUE TO THE RAPID ONSET AND DESTRUCTIVE NATURE OF THE DISEASE AS WELL AS THE LACK OF EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS. ABOUT THREE-QUARTERS (71%) OF PAM PATIENTS WERE TREATED WITH AMPHOTERICIN B AND 9% OF GLOBAL CASES RECEIVED NEWLY RECOMMENDED DRUG MILTEFOSINE. DESPITE THE USE OF THESE DRUGS, THE MORTALITY RATE OF PAM IS MORE THAN 97% AND ONLY FIVE PATIENTS SURVIVED SO FAR IN THE US. THE USE OF AMPHOTERICIN B IS LIMITED BY SEVERE DOSE-LIMITING SIDE EFFECTS, THUS DEVELOPMENT OF MORE EFFECTIVE AND SAFE THERAPIES FOR PAM IS A RESEARCH PRIORITY. BECAUSE OF THE RARITY OF THE DISEASE, PHARMACEUTICAL COMPANIES DO NOT PURSUE NEW DRUG DISCOVERY FOR PAM. YET, FINDING A BETTER DRUG WOULD HAVE AN IMPACT ON PEOPLE SUFFERING FROM THIS DEADLY INFECTION ANNUALLY. DESPITE THE ROLE OF NATURAL PRODUCTS IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF DRUGS FOR OVER A CENTURY, RESEARCH ON IDENTIFYING NEW NATURAL PRODUCT-BASED ANTI-N. FOWLERI AGENTS IS LIMITED. WE TESTED THE ACTIVITY OF ABOUT 10,000 STRUCTURALLY UNIQUE MARINE MICROBIAL METABOLITE MIXTURES AGAINST N. FOWLERI AND EXAMINATION OF TOP SIX POTENT METABOLITE MIXTURES RESULTED IN THE ISOLATION OF TWO PURE COMPOUNDS. THESE TWO COMPOUNDS ARE FAST-ACTING, EXHIBITED NANOMOLAR POTENCY ON MULTIPLE STRAINS, SYNERGISTIC WITH AMPHOTERICIN B, AND ARE LESS TOXIC ON MAMMALIAN CELLS. OUR EXPERIMENTS WITH OTHER RELATED CHEMICAL INHIBITORS IDENTIFIED A POTENTIALLY NOVEL `DRUGGABLE' TARGET IN N. FOWLERI AND SINGLED OUT A NATURAL PRODUCT AS A FAST-ACTING, POTENT AMOEBICIDAL COMPOUND THAT IS SYNERGISTIC WITH AMPHOTERICIN B. THIS COMPOUND EXTENDED THE SURVIVAL OF INFECTED MICE SIGNIFICANTLY AND MORE THAN ONE-THIRD OF THE INFECTED MICE WERE CURED OF BRAIN INFECTION AFTER ONLY TWO DAYS OF TREATMENT WITH ONCE-A-DAY LOW DOSING OF THE COMPOUND. BASED ON THESE PROMISING RESULTS, WE PROPOSE TO 1) DETERMINE THE DRUG-LIKE PROPERTIES OF THESE THREE AMOEBICIDAL COMPOUNDS THROUGH IN VITRO ADME STUDIES, 2) CONDUCT TOLERABILITY AND PHARMACOKINETIC STUDIES OF THESE COMPOUNDS, BOTH MONOTHERAPY AND IN COMBINATION THERAPY WITH AMPHOTERICIN B, TO OPTIMIZE DOSING FOR EFFICACY STUDIES, AND 3) TEST IN VIVO EFFICACY OF COMPOUNDS, ALONE AND IN COMBINATION WITH THE PARTNERING DRUG AMPHOTERICIN B IN A MOUSE MODEL OF PAM CAUSED BY TWO DIFFERENT GENOTYPES. THIS STUDY IS A NECESSARY STEP TOWARD DEVELOPING THESE INHIBITORS FOR THE TREATMENT OF PAM. TO SUCCESSFULLY ACHIEVE THESE AIMS, WE RELY ON OUR EXISTING COLLABORATION THAT COMBINES THE UNIQUE EXPERTISE OF DR. DEBNATH (PI) IN NAEGLERIA PARASITE BIOLOGY AND DR. FENICAL'S EXTENSIVE BACKGROUND IN MARINE NATURAL PRODUCTS DRUG DISCOVERY (CO-INVESTIGATOR). DRS. DEBNATH AND FENICAL'S EXPERTISE AND EXPERIENCE HAS POTENTIAL TO ELEVATE OUR DRUG DISCOVERY PLATFORM TO A TRANSLATIONAL LEVEL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A HYDRO-METEOROLOGICAL MALARIA MODEL FOR ADAPTIVE AND TAILORED VECTOR CONTROL STRATEGIES IN AFRICA - PROJECT SUMMARY  A HYDRO-METEOROLOGICAL MALARIA MODEL FOR ADAPTIVE AND TAILORED VECTOR CONTROL STRATEGIES IN AFRICA SIGNIFICANT PROGRESS IN GLOBAL MALARIA CONTROL HAS BEEN ACHIEVED OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, PRIMARILY DUE TO THE WIDESPREAD SCALE-UP OF LONG-LASTING INSECTICIDE-TREATED NETS AND INDOOR RESIDUAL SPRAYING. HOWEVER, THE EMERGENCE OF INSECTICIDE RESISTANCE AND SHIFTS IN VECTOR BITING AND RESTING BEHAVIORS HAVE SUBSTANTIALLY REDUCED THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THESE CORE INTERVENTION TOOLS. ADDITIONALLY, MALARIA RISK VARIES ACROSS REGIONS DUE TO DIFFERENCES IN CLIMATE, MOSQUITO BIOLOGY, HUMAN BEHAVIOR, LAND USE, AND THE EFFECTIVENESS OF MALARIA CONTROL EFFORTS. AS MALARIA RISK FLUCTUATES DUE TO ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECOLOGICAL DYNAMICS, PREVIOUSLY EFFECTIVE CONTROL METHODS MAY BECOME LESS RELIABLE. EFFECTIVE MALARIA CONTROL REQUIRES APPROACHES THAT ADAPT TO VARIABLE ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS AND VECTOR ECOLOGY. ACCURATE MALARIA RISK PREDICTION IS CRITICAL FOR INFORMING THESE APPROACHES. HOWEVER, CURRENT METHODS FOR PREDICTING MALARIA RISK FACE SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGES. STATISTICAL MODELS THAT RELY ON CORRELATIONS BETWEEN CLIMATE VARIABLES AND MALARIA INCIDENCE OFTEN PERFORM POORLY IN ATYPICAL SCENARIOS SUCH AS DROUGHTS OR FLOODS. IN CONTRAST, MECHANISTIC MODELS TYPICALLY OPERATE AT COARSE SPATIAL SCALES AND DO NOT ADEQUATELY ACCOUNT FOR CRITICAL SURFACE HYDROLOGY PROCESSES, LIMITING THEIR ABILITY TO CAPTURE THE SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL DYNAMICS OF MALARIA RISK. THESE SHORTCOMINGS HINDER THE DEVELOPMENT OF ADAPTABLE MALARIA CONTROL SOLUTIONS. THE CENTRAL OBJECTIVE OF THIS APPLICATION IS TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A HYDRO-METEOROLOGICAL MALARIA MODEL TO IMPROVE FORECASTS OF MALARIA RISK, AND TO USE THE MODEL TO DESIGN VECTOR CONTROL STRATEGIES SUITABLE FOR VARYING ENVIRONMENTAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL CONDITIONS. TO ACHIEVE THIS OBJECTIVE, WE HAVE DESIGNED TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A HYDRO-METEOROLOGICAL MALARIA MODEL THAT INTEGRATES WEATHER FORECASTING, HYDROLOGY, VECTOR AND MALARIA EPIDEMIOLOGICAL MODEL TO ENHANCE MALARIA RISK PREDICTION, AND 2) ANALYZE SHIFTS IN MALARIA RISK RESULTING FROM ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS, WEATHER VARIABILITY, AND CHANGES IN VECTOR ECOLOGY, AND IDENTIFY ADAPTIVE VECTOR CONTROL STRATEGIES TAILORED TO LOCAL TRANSMISSION DYNAMICS. KEY OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE THE DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A NOVEL TOOL THAT USES WEATHER, HYDROLOGICAL ANALYSIS, AND DISEASE DATA TO PREDICT MALARIA RISK OVER SPACE AND TIME, AND GUIDE EFFECTIVE MOSQUITO CONTROL STRATEGIES BASED ON PREVAILING ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. ALTHOUGH THE TOOL IS VALIDATED USING ENVIRONMENTAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL DATA FROM WESTERN KENYA, THE RESULTING MODEL IS EXPECTED TO BE TRANSFERABLE ACROSS DIVERSE ECOLOGICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL SETTINGS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CONTRIBUTION OF ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM (ER) STRESS RESPONSES IN RICKETTSIA PATHOGENESIS - THE GRAM-NEGATIVE Α-PROTEOBACTERIA OF THE GENUS RICKETTSIA ARE SMALL (0.3-0.5 X 0.8-1.0 M), OBLIGATE INTRACELLULAR ORGANISMS. THEY ARE CATEGORIZED INTO FOUR (4) MAJOR GROUPS, THE SPOTTED FEVER GROUP (SFG), TYPHUS GROUP (TG), ANCESTRAL GROUP (AG) AND TRANSITIONAL GROUP (TRG), WHICH CAN BE DISTINGUISHED BY ANTIGENICITY AND INTRACELLULAR ACTIN-BASED MOTILITY. SEVERAL SFG MEMBERS OF THIS GENUS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR SEVERE HUMAN DISEASES AND INCLUDE R. CONORII, R. RICKETTSII, AND R. PARKERI.  ALTHOUGH ENDOTHELIAL CELLS ARE A PRIMARY TARGET CELL IN THE MAMMALIAN HOST, MANY NON-ENDOTHELIAL CELL TYPES INCLUDING MONOCYTES AND MACROPHAGES CAN BE READILY INFECTED. INDEED, THE ABILITY TO PROLIFERATE WITHIN PHAGOCYTIC CELLS IN VITRO HAS BEEN SUGGESTED TO BE A PHENOTYPIC CHARACTERISTIC THAT CAN DIFFERENTIATE HUMAN PATHOGENIC RICKETTSIA SPECIES FROM THOSE THAT ARE NOT ASSOCIATED WITH DISEASES IN MAMMALS. IN ADDITION, UPON ENTRY, PATHOGENIC SFG RICKETTSIA SPECIES TRIGGER GLOBAL TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND PROTEOMIC CHANGES WITHIN INFECTED TARGET CELLS THAT INCLUDE TARGETING OF PROTEOSOME FUNCTIONS AND ER STRESS RESPONSE THAT ARE PREDICTED TO FACILITATE THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN INTRACELLULAR ENVIRONMENT CONDUCIVE TO RICKETTSIAL PROLIFERATION. INFECTION OF THP-1 MACROPHAGES RESULTED IN THE UNDER-REPRESENTATION OF SUBUNITS OF THE CORE 20S PROTEOSOME AND AN INCREASE IN PROTEINS INVOLVED IN ER STRESS RESPONSES TO POSITIVELY MODULATE ER PROTEIN FOLDING AND CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS. SEVERAL BACTERIAL AND VIRAL PATHOGENS HAVE BEEN PREVIOUSLY DEMONSTRATED TO MODULATE IRE1- DEPENDENT SIGNALING EVENTS TO PROMOTE EFFICIENT REPLICATION INTRACELLULARLY. THESE RESULTS SUGGESTED THAT ACTIVATION OF A MAJOR REGULATOR OF ER STRESS RESPONSES (IRE1) AND PARTICIPTAION OF DOWNSTREAM IRE1 SIGNALING INTERMEDIATES MAY BE IMPORTANT EVENTS DURING RICKETTSIAL INFECTION. WE HAVE NOW PROVIDED COMPELLING EVIDENCE THAT PHARMACOLOGICAL INHIBTION OF IRE1 SIGNIFICANTLY DIMINISHES R. PARKERI PROLIFERATION WITHIN MAMMALIAN MACROPHAGES AND ENDOTHELIAL CELLS. THE SPECIFIC ROLE(S) OF MODULATING ER STRESS RESPONSES TO RICKETTSIA REPLICATION AND SURVIVAL IN IN VITRO AND IN IN VIVO MODELS OF DISEASE ARE NOT YET EXPLORED. VERY LITTLE IS KNOWN REGARDING THE MOLECULAR DETAILS AND MECHANISMS BY WHICH OBLIGATE INTRACELLULAR, NON-VACUOLAR BACTERIA SUCH AS RICKETTSIA SPECIES HIGHJACK ER STRESS RESPONSES FOR THEIR BENEFIT. THIS PROPOSAL WILL FOCUS ON THE FOLLOWING TWO AVENUES OF RESEARCH: A) ELUCIDATE THE ROLE OF IRE1 SIGNALING PATHWAYS AND OTHER ER STRESS RESPONSE REGULATORS TO THE  PROLIFERATION OF OBLIGATE INTRACELLULAR BACTERIA IN TARGET MAMMALIAN CELLS. B) DEFINE THE CONTRIBUTION OF MODULATING ER STRESS RESPONSES TO RICKETTSIA PROLIFERATION, INTRACELLULAR  SURVIVAL AND DISEASE PROGRESSION USING IN VIVO MURINE MODELS OF INFECTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SYNERGISTIC INHIBITION OF THE COMPLEMENT ALTERNATIVE PATHWAY BY FHR FAMILY PROTEINS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  THE COMPLEMENT SYSTEM IS A NETWORK OF CELL SURFACE-ASSOCIATED AND SOLUBLE PLASMA PROTEINS COMPRISING A PROTEOLYTIC CASCADE WITH ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS IN INNATE IMMUNE SURVEILLANCE AND INFLAMMATION. WHILE THERE ARE THREE CANONICAL COMPLEMENT PATHWAYS, THE ALTERNATIVE PATHWAY (AP) IS THE PRIMARY MEANS OF COMPLEMENT AMPLIFICATION AND INNATE IMMUNE EFFECTOR GENERATION IN VIVO. BECAUSE OF THIS, AP ACTIVITY IS TIGHTLY CONTROLLED VIA THE FUNCTIONS OF THE FACTOR H (FH) FAMILY OF REGULATORY PROTEINS, ALL OF WHOM ACT ON C3B OR ITS COMPLEXES. THE FH-RELATED PROTEINS (FHRS) SHARE MANY FEATURES WITH FH, BUT HAVE DISTINCT REGULATORY PROPERTIES THAT ARE NOT YET FULLY UNDERSTOOD. RARE GENETIC VARIANTS IN ALL FHRS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH DEVELOPING COMPLEMENT-DRIVEN PATHOLOGIES, INDICATING THAT FHRS PLAY VITAL ROLES IN CONTROLLING COMPLEMENT AP ACTIVITY IN VARIOUS CONTEXTS IN VIVO.  DESPITE THE EXISTENCE OF DEDICATED REGULATORY PROTEINS, EXCESSIVE COMPLEMENT AP ACTIVITY IS A DRIVER OF MANY AUTOIMMUNE, INFLAMMATORY AND DEGENERATIVE DISEASES. AMONG THESE ARE RARE DISEASES LIKE ATYPICAL HEMOLYTIC UREMIC SYNDROME AND PAROXYSMAL NOCTURNAL HEMOGLOBINURIA, BUT ALSO FAR MORE COMMON CONDITIONS LIKE DRY AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION – A DISEASE AFFECTING NEARLY 20 MILLION ADULTS IN THE USA. RECENT FDA APPROVALS OF SEVERAL COMPLEMENT AP INHIBITORY DRUGS HAVE DIVERSIFIED THE THERAPEUTIC LANDSCAPE, BUT THE HIGH COST OF THESE DRUGS IS A MAJOR BURDEN FOR BOTH PATIENTS AND HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS. TO DEVELOP MORE AFFORDABLE THERAPIES, THERE REMAINS A NEED TO STUDY THE BASIC MECHANISMS UNDERLYING AP INHIBITION AND REGULATION.  WE PREVIOUSLY CHARACTERIZED A POTENT AP INHIBITORY PROTEIN CALLED EFB-C. THROUGH STRUCTURE/FUNCTION STUDIES, WE FOUND THAT EFB-C INHIBITS COMPLEMENT BY STABILIZING AN OPEN CONFORMATION OF C3B THAT FORMS THE AP CONVERTASE ENZYME INEFFICIENTLY. FURTHER CONSEQUENCES OF EFB-C BINDING TO C3B HAVE NOT BEEN SYSTEMATICALLY INVESTIGATED. HOWEVER, WE RECENTLY FOUND THAT EFB-C BINDING TO C3B LEADS TO RECRUITMENT OF THE ENDOGENOUS COMPLEMENT REGULATOR, FHR2, RESULTING IN A STRONG, SYNERGISTIC INHIBITION OF THE AP. ASIDE FROM FHR2, THERE ARE FOUR ADDITIONAL FHRS (IE, FHR1, FHR3, FHR4, AND FHR5). WHEREAS FHRS 1, 2, AND 5 INHIBIT COMPLEMENT ACTIVITY, FHR4 SEEMS TO PROMOTE COMPLEMENT FUNCTION. WHETHER AND HOW EFB-C INFLUENCES THESE FHRS IS UNCLEAR.  HERE, WE WILL USE X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY TO DETERMINE HOW EFB-C BINDING TO C3B PROMOTES THE INTERACTION WITH FHR2, LEADING TO SYNERGISTIC INHIBITION OF THE AP. WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE WHETHER EFB-C BINDING TO C3B ALTERS THE FUNCTION OF THE REMAINING FHR FAMILY MEMBERS. FINALLY, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT OTHER MOLECULES WHICH SHARE THE EFB-C BINDING SITE ON C3B WILL EXERT SIMILAR EFFECTS ON FHRS AND THEREBY INHIBIT THE COMPLEMENT AP. TO DO SO, WE WILL COMPLETE A SITE-SELECTIVE PHAGE DISPLAY SCREEN TO IDENTIFY SUCH PEPTIDES AND CHARACTERIZE THEIR EFFECTS ON FHRS AND COMPLEMENT FUNCTION. COMPLETING THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE INSIGHTS INTO C3B STRUCTURE AND FHR FUNCTION, AND WILL ENABLE DEVELOPMENT OF MORE COST-EFFECTIVE THERAPIES FOR COMPLEMENT-DRIVEN DISEASES.

description: DETERMINING THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PARASITE GENETICS AND PATHOGEN BURDEN IN TRYPANOSOMA CRUZI INFECTED HOSTS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THERE ARE MANY UNANSWERED QUESTIONS CONCERNING THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN T. CRUZI AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF CLINICAL CHAGAS DISEASE. FOR EXAMPLE, IT IS OFTEN STATED THAT ~30% OF T. CRUZI INFECTED HUMANS DEVELOP CLINICAL CHAGAS DISEASE BUT THE REASONS THAT MOST DO NOT IS NOT KNOWN. ALSO, IT IS NOT CLEAR WHY T. CRUZI PERSISTS FOR THE LIFE OF MANY HOSTS, DESPITE A VIGOROUS ANTI-PARASITE IMMUNE RESPONSE, BUT IS COMPLETELY RESOLVED IN A SELECT FEW. IT IS LIKELY THAT BOTH HOST AND PARASITE FACTORS CONTRIBUTE TO THESE VARIABLE INFECTION OUTCOMES. ONE LIMITATION IN ADDRESSING THESE GAPS IN KNOWLEDGE HAS BEEN THE LACK OF METHODS TO ACCURATELY AND SENSITIVELY QUANTIFY PARASITE BURDEN OVER TIME IN HOSTS. WE HAVE RECENTLY ESTABLISHED PROTOCOLS THAT ALLOW FOR SENSITIVE AND PRECISE QUANTIFICATION OF THE RELATIVE T. CRUZI BURDEN IN ESSENTIALLY ANY INFECTED HOST AND HAVE SHOWN THAT THE STABLE PARASITE LOAD CAN VARY BETWEEN HOSTS BY OVER 1 MILLION-FOLD. ADDITIONALLY, WE HAVE ISOLATED OVER 400 PARASITE LINES FROM NON-HUMAN PRIMATES THAT EXHIBIT THESE WIDE RANGES OF PARASITE BURDEN. THE PRIMARY GOAL OF THIS STUDY WILL BE TO DETERMINE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PARASITE BURDEN IN HOSTS AND THE GENETICS OF THE T. CRUZI POPULATION IN THOSE HOSTS – IN SHORT, DOES PARASITE GENETICS LARGELY OR PARTIALLY DETERMINE THE PARASITE LOAD IN A HOST? TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL, WE WILL APPLY LOW-COVERAGE WHOLE-GENOME SEQUENCING (LCWGS) OF T. CRUZI ISOLATES FRESHLY OBTAINED FROM MULTIPLE COLONIES OF NON-HUMAN PRIMATES WHOSE PARASITE BURDEN HAS BEEN PRECISELY DETERMINED. IN ADDITION, THESE STUDIES ARE EXPECTED TO ALLOW US TO BEGIN TO ADDRESS OTHER IMPORTANT QUESTIONS ABOUT THE POPULATIONS GENOMICS OF T. CRUZI, INCLUDING: ARE DISTINCT POPULATIONS OF PARASITES CIRCULATING IN LOCATIONS SEPARATED BY 100 MILES OR MORE AND DO THE GENETICS OF THESE PARASITE POPULATION SHIFT SIGNIFICANTLY OVER TIME?; ARE DISTINCT PARASITE POPULATIONS CIRCULATING IN DIFFERENT HOST SPECIES IN THE SAME FACILITY?; HOW DIVERSE ARE THE PARASITE POPULATIONS IN AN INDIVIDUAL AND DO THESE POPULATIONS CHANGE OVER TIME AND WITH AND WITHOUT TREATMENT?. COLLECTIVELY, WE EXPECT THE COMPLETION OF THIS STUDY TO PROVIDE ANSWERS TO LONG-STANDING QUESTIONS ON ONE OF THE MAJOR AND LONG-DEBATED VARIABLES THAT IMPACT THE DEVELOPMENT OF CLINICAL DISEASE IN T. CRUZI INFECTION – THAT OF THE GENETICS OF THE INFECTING PARASITE POPULATION. THESE STUDIES ARE ALSO EXPECTED TO ESTABLISH LCWGS AS AN ESSENTIAL TOOL FOR PARASITE POPULATION GENOMICS, INCLUDING THAT OF T. CRUZI, AND TO PROVIDE THE MEANS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE DYNAMICS OF T. CRUZI TRANSMISSION IN DIFFERENT SETTINGS AND OVER TIME.
