description: A MODULAR SYNTHETIC PLATFORM FOR DESIGN OF BOTTROMYCIN ANTIBIOTICS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE EMERGENCE OF MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT (MDR) PATHOGENS SUCH AS METHICILLIN-RESISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (MRSA) AND VANCOMYCIN-RESISTANT ENTEROCOCCI (VRE) REPRESENTS AN ESCALATING GLOBAL HEALTH CRISIS. NEW ANTIBIOTICS THAT ACT BY FUNDAMENTALLY DIFFERENT MECHANISMS ARE URGENTLY NEEDED. BOTTROMYCINS ARE AN EXCEPTIONAL BUT UNDEREXPLORED CLASS OF RIBOSOMALLY DERIVED NATURAL PRODUCTS THAT INHIBIT BACTERIAL TRANSLATION THROUGH A UNIQUE EF-TU⋅TRNA–DEPENDENT MECHANISM NOT TARGETED BY ANY APPROVED DRUG. THIS DISTINCTIVE MODE OF ACTION MINIMIZES CROSS-RESISTANCE AND POSITIONS BOTTROMYCINS AS PROMISING LEADS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF FIRST-IN-CLASS ANTIBIOTICS. HOWEVER, THEIR POTENTIAL HAS REMAINED UNREALIZED BECAUSE TRADITIONAL SOLUTION-PHASE SYNTHESES ARE LENGTHY, HAZARDOUS, AND LOW-YIELDING, PREVENTING SYSTEMATIC STRUCTURE–ACTIVITY RELATIONSHIP (SAR) STUDIES. THIS PROJECT DEVELOPS A MODULAR SOLID-PHASE PEPTIDE SYNTHESIS (SPPS) PLATFORM THAT ENABLES EFFICIENT AND SCALABLE ACCESS TO AUTHENTIC BOTTROMYCIN CONGENERS AND DESIGNED ANALOGS. AIM 1 ESTABLISHES A ROBUST SPPS ROUTE TO ALL NATURAL BOTTROMYCIN DERIVATIVES, VALIDATING THE SYNTHETIC APPROACH AND PROVIDING SUFFICIENT QUANTITIES FOR REPRODUCIBLE ANTIMICROBIAL EVALUATION. THESE STUDIES WILL ESTABLISH A STANDARDIZED FOUNDATION FOR DESIGN AND SCAFFOLD SIMPLIFICATION. AIM 2 APPLIES THIS PLATFORM TO ENGINEER MECHANISM-GUIDED ANALOGS THAT PROBE AND RE- TUNE THE MOLECULAR INTERACTIONS RESPONSIBLE FOR EF-TU⋅TRNA SELECTIVITY AND TRANSLATION INHIBITION. GUIDED BY RECENT CRYO-EM STRUCTURES (REPORTED IN PREPRINT AUGUST 2025), THESE STUDIES WILL DELINEATE KEY PHARMACOPHORE ELEMENTS, IDENTIFY SITES PERMISSIVE TO MODIFICATION, AND GENERATE ANALOGS WITH EXPANDED TRNA SPECIFICITY AND IMPROVED ANTIBACTERIAL POTENCY. TOGETHER, THESE AIMS UNITE SYNTHETIC INNOVATION WITH MECHANISTIC DISCOVERY TO TRANSFORM BOTTROMYCIN FROM A SYNTHETIC CHALLENGE INTO A TRACTABLE PLATFORM FOR MECHANISM-BASED ANTIBIOTIC DESIGN. THE PROPOSED WORK DIRECTLY ALIGNS WITH NIAID’S MISSION TO COMBAT ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE BY DEVELOPING AGENTS WITH NOVEL MODES OF ACTION, WHILE SIMULTANEOUSLY PROVIDING NEW MOLECULAR TOOLS TO STUDY BACTERIAL TRANSLATION AND RESISTANCE PATHWAYS.

description: ROLE OF THE GROUP B STREPTOCOCCAL TYPE VII SECRETION SYSTEM IN THE DIABETIC WOUND - PROJECT SUMMARY DIABETES IS A COMPLEX DISEASE ASSOCIATED WITH NUMEROUS COMPLICATIONS, ONE OF THE MOST COMMON BEING WOUND INFECTIONS OF THE LOWER LIMBS. DIABETIC FOOT ULCERS (DFU) OFTEN EXHIBIT PROLONGED WOUND HEALING DUE TO THE PRESENCE OF NUMEROUS BACTERIAL PATHOGENS COUPLED WITH INFLAMMATORY BUT INEFFECTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES. STREPTOCOCCUS AGALACTIAE (OR GROUP B STREPTOCOCCUS, GBS) IS A GRAM-POSITIVE OPPORTUNISTIC PATHOGEN THAT IS COMMONLY ISOLATED FROM DIABETIC WOUNDS. WE HAVE ISOLATED BACTERIA FROM THE WOUNDS OF DIABETIC PATIENTS AND FIND A HIGH ABUNDANCE OF GBS THAT IS OFTEN CO-ISOLATED WITH OTHER BACTERIA INCLUDING STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS, ENTEROCOCCUS FAECALIS, AND MORE RARELY WITH PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH GBS PERSISTS AND INTERACTS WITH OTHER MICROBES IN THIS POLYMICROBIAL NICHE IS NOT KNOWN. TYPE VII SECRETION SYSTEMS (T7SS) ARE SPECIALIZED SYSTEMS IN ACTINOBACTERIA AND BACILLOTA BACTERIA THAT SECRETEEFFECTORS WITH MAJOR FUNCTIONSIN VIRULENCE, NUTRIENT ACQUISITION, AND INTERBACTERIAL KILLING.WE HAVE RECENTLY DESCRIBED A T7SS IN GBS THAT CONTRIBUTES TO PATHOGENESIS, BUT IT'S ROLE PROMOTING NICHE ESTABLISHMENT AND VIRULENCE IN THE DIABETIC WOUND IS UNKNOWN. WE DEVELOPED A DIABETIC MURINE MODEL OF GBS DIABETIC WOUND INFECTION AND DEMONSTRATED THAT GBS PERSISTS IN THIS ENVIRONMENT. RNA-SEQUENCING AND TN-SEQUENCING ANALYSIS HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT GBS T7SS GENES, INCLUDING THOSE ENCODING SECRETED PORE-FORMING EFFECTORS (ESXA), ARE UPREGULATED AND REQUIRED FOR FITNESS IN THE MURINE DIABETIC WOUND. FURTHER, IN OUR PREVIOUS WORK CHARACTERIZING HUMAN DIABETIC WOUND ISOLATES, ALL RECOVERED GBS STRAINS ENCODED A T7SS, SUGGESTING THE IMPORTANCE OF THIS SYSTEM. IN PUBLISHED AND PRELIMINARY IN VITRO STUDIES, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED ANOTHER T7-SECRETED TOXIN, BLTA, THAT LIMITS GROWTH OF BOTH E. FAECALIS AND P. AERUGINOSA. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT GBS T7SS CONTRIBUTES TO PERSISTENCE IN THE DIABETIC WOUND USING SECRETED EFFECTORS FOR INTERBACTERIAL COMPETITION AS WELL AS VIRULENCE TO PROMOTE SURVIVAL AND DISSEMINATION FROM THE WOUND. WE WILL ADDRESS THESE HYPOTHESES IN THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1, CHARACTERIZE THE CONTRIBUTION OF BLTA TO INTERBACTERIAL COMPETITION AND GBS NICHE ESTABLISHMENT IN THE DIABETIC WOUND; AIM 2, DETERMINE HOW PORE-FORMING ESXA EFFECTORS CONTRIBUTE TO DIABETIC WOUND INFECTION AND DISSEMINATION; AND AIM 3, EXAMINE HOW GBS AND T7SS INFLUENCES THE DIABETIC WOUND MICROBIAL COMMUNITY. THESE STUDIES WILL DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF T7SS AND SECRETED EFFECTORS TO GBS PATHOGENESIS IN THE POLYMICROBIAL ENVIRONMENT OF THE DIABETIC WOUND.

description: ROLE OF PERSISTENT SODIUM CURRENTS IN MODULATING MOSQUITO SENSORY BEHAVIOR - PYRETHROIDS, A CLASS OF INSECTICIDES TARGETING INSECT NAV CHANNELS, REMAIN A CORNERSTONE OF MOSQUITO CONTROL STRATEGIES WORLDWIDE. TRANSFLUTHRIN (TF) IS A VOLATILE PYRETHROID USED IN SPATIAL EMANATORS AS THE ACTIVE INGREDIENT. RECENTLY, THE WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION RECOMMENDED TF-BASED SPATIAL EMANATORS AS A NEW CLASS OF INTERVENTION FOR THE MALARIA CONTROL. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISM UNDERLYING TF SPATIAL REPELLENCY IS NOT UNDERSTOOD. IN PARTICULAR, SPATIAL REPELLENCY ACTS AT A DISTANCE AND DOES NOT LEAD TO INSECT PARALYSIS, WHICH IS CHARACTERISTIC OF CONTACT-BASED INSECTICIDAL ACTIVITY OF CONVENTIONAL PYRETHROIDS. MUCH RESEARCH IN SPATIAL REPELLENCY HAS HIGHLIGHTED THE IMPORTANCE OF CHEMORECEPTOR PROTEINS (E.G., ORS). HOWEVER, TF REPELLENCY IS NOT OR-DEPENDENT, BUT SOLELY MEDIATED BY ACTIVATION OF NAV CHANNELS IN AEDES AEGYPTI. WE RECENTLY DISCOVERED THAT RNA EDITING OF SODIUM CHANNEL TRANSCRIPTS FROM MOSQUITO ANTENNAE GENERATES NAV CHANNEL VARIANTS THAT CARRY A PERSISTENT CURRENT (INAP) WHEN ASSAYED IN XENOPUS OOCYTES AND THAT THESE INAP -CARRYING NAV CHANNEL VARIANTS ARE HYPERSENSITIVE TO TF COMPARED TO THOSE LACKING INAP. THESE FINDINGS PROVIDE A COMPELLING FOUNDATION FOR TESTING THE HYPOTHESIS THAT AMPLIFICATION OF INAP BY TF REPRESENTS THE ELUSIVE MOLECULAR BASIS OF TF-INDUCED SPATIAL REPELLENCY OF TF IN VIVO. AN EXTENSION OF THIS HYPOTHESIS IS THAT INAP-CARRYING ANTENNAL NAV CHANNEL VARIANTS CONTRIBUTE TO TUNING THE ANTENNAL SENSORY SYSTEM FOR DETECTING NATURAL ENVIRONMENTAL CUES ASSOCIATED WITH HOSTS, MATES, AND BREEDING SITES. IN THIS R21 APPLICATION, WE PROPOSE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. SPECIFIC AIM 1. ELIMINATION OF INAP-GENERATING RNA EDITING SITES USING CRISPR-CAS9 IN THE AE. AEGYPTI GENOME. SPECIFIC AIM 2. BEHAVIORAL ANALYSIS OF TRANSGENIC LINES MUTATED IN INAP-PRODUCING RNA EDITING SITES, WHICH WILL ENABLE US TO RIGOROUSLY CHARACTERIZE THE RNA EDITING TO ASSESS THE ROLE OF RNA EDITING OF NAV TRANSCRIPTS IN MODULATING MOSQUITO BEHAVIORS INCLUDING TF REPELLENCY IN AE. AEGYPTI. THIS RESEARCH HAS POTENTIAL TO YIELD THE FIRST EXPERIMENTAL EVIDENCE FOR THE ROLE OF RNA EDITING OF NAV TRANSCRIPTS IN SHAPING THE SENSORY PHYSIOLOGY AND ASSOCIATED BEHAVIORS IN INSECTS. RESULTS WILL PROVIDE A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR TARGETING INAP-AMPLIFICATION AS A MECHANISM OF MOSQUITO REPELLENCY, THEREBY MAKING A UNIQUE CONTRIBUTION TO ADVANCING THE INSECT SENSORY PHYSIOLOGY AND REPELLENCY FIELD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SIGNAL-INDUCED ALTERNATIVE PRE-MRNA SPLICING IN THE TLR SIGNALING PATHWAY - ABSTRACT IN THE PRESENCE OF PATHOGENS, THE TLR SIGNALING PATHWAY IS ACTIVATED AND INDUCES INFLAMMATION TO FIGHT INFECTION. HOWEVER, PERSISTENT TLR SIGNALING CAN LEAD TO CHRONIC INFLAMMATION AND RESULTING INFLAMMATORY DISEASE. ONE MECHANISM THAT LIMITS PERSISTENT TLR SIGNALING IS PRODUCTION OF ALTERNATIVE SPLICE FORMS IN THE TLR SIGNALING PATHWAY. PATHOGEN COMPONENTS SUCH AS LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDE (LPS) INDUCE THE PRODUCTION OF ALTERNATIVE SPLICE FORMS THAT ENCODE DOMINANT NEGATIVE INHIBITORS OF TLR SIGNALING. THUS, PRODUCTION OF THESE NEGATIVELY ACTING MRNA SPLICE FORMS CONSTITUTES A NEGATIVE FEEDBACK LOOP THAT PREVENTS CHRONIC INFLAMMATION. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES HAVE IDENTIFIED THE RNA BINDING PROTEINS SRSF1 AND HNRNPU AS CIS-ACTING REGULATORS OF LPS-INDUCED ALTERNATIVE SPLICING OF THE KEY TLR PATHWAY SIGNALING ADAPTOR MYD88. MOREOVER, OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES INDICATE THAT THESE SAME RNA BINDING PROTEINS LIKELY REGULATE SPLICING OF OTHER GENES IN THE TLR SIGNALING PATHWAY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SRSF1 AND HNRNPU COORDINATE LPS-INDUCED ALTERNATIVE SPLICING IN THE TLR SIGNALING PATHWAY TO ENABLE EFFICIENT TERMINATION OF INFLAMMATION. IN THE CURRENT PROPOSAL, WE WILL (1) DETERMINE HOW SRSF1 AND HNRNPU REGULATE ALTERNATIVE SPLICING IN THE TLR SIGNALING PATHWAY AND (2) DETERMINE HOW LPS REGULATES THE ACTIVITY OF SRSF1 AND HNRNPU. THESE STUDIES REPRESENT A CRITICAL STEP TOWARDS OUR GOAL OF HARNESSING THIS ALTERNATIVE SPLICING MECHANISM TO PREVENT PERSISTENT INFLAMMATION AND RESULTING INFLAMMATORY DISEASE WITHOUT ABLATING THE NECESSARY INITIAL ANTI-PATHOGEN RESPONSE.

description: EMERGENCE AND MOLECULAR EVOLUTION OF TACARIBE VIRUS AS A HUMAN PATHOGEN - ABSTRACT TACARIBE VIRUS (TCRV), A MAMMARENAVIRUS, WAS INITIALLY IDENTIFIED IN BATS IN TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO IN 1956. MORE RECENTLY, ITS PRESENCE IN THE U.S. WAS CONFIRMED IN 2012 WITH ITS ISOLATION FROM AMBLYOMMA AMERICANUM TICKS IN A FLORIDA STATE PARK. RECENT SURVEILLANCE STUDIES FOR FEBRILE ILLNESSES IN PERU LED TO A SIGNIFICANT FINDING: TCRV WAS ISOLATED FROM THE SERUM OF TWO PATIENTS EXPERIENCING ACUTE UNDIFFERENTIATED FEBRILE ILLNESS (AUFI). WHILE ONE PATIENT RECOVERED FROM THE INFECTION, THE OUTCOME FOR THE SECOND PATIENT REMAINS UNCERTAIN. COMPREHENSIVE GENOME SEQUENCING ANALYSES OF THESE PERUVIAN HUMAN TCRV ISOLATES REVEALED SEVEN AMINO ACID SUBSTITUTIONS COMPARED TO THE PROTOTYPE TCRV ISOLATE FROM TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO, WITH THREE OF THESE CRITICAL CHANGES OCCURRING IN THE GLYCOPROTEIN (GP). THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS TO EXAMINE EXPERIMENTALLY THE IN VITRO HOST RANGE OF TCRV AND ITS POTENTIALLY HIDDEN PREVALENCE IN PERU. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL DETERMINE IF THE VIRUS HAS ADAPTED TO USE THE HUMAN TRANSFERRIN RECEPTOR 1 (HTFR1) FOR CELL ENTRY, A MECHANISM IMPLICATED IN THE HUMAN DISEASE POTENTIAL OF OTHER CLADE B MAMMARENAVIRUSES. FURTHERMORE, UTILIZING OUR EXISTING COLLABORATION WITH INVESTIGATORS AT THE UNITED STATES NAVAL MEDICAL RESEARCH SOUTH (NAMRU SOUTH) LABORATORY, WE WILL ASSESS THE PREVALENCE OF TCRV IN FEBRILE PATIENTS FROM PERU. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE SPECIFIC MUTATIONS IN TCRV’S GP HAVE ENABLED THE VIRUS TO USE HTFR1 AS A RECEPTOR, THEREBY EXPANDING ITS HOST RANGE TO HUMANS, LEADING TO AN INCREASE IN AUFI CASES IN PERU OVER THE PAST YEARS. TO TEST THIS, WE WILL PURSUE TWO AIMS: 1) ESTABLISH THE PREVALENCE OF TCRV INFECTION AMONG PATIENTS DIAGNOSED WITH AUFI IN THE PERUVIAN AMAZON, BETWEEN 2020-2025, AND 2) INVESTIGATE THE VIRAL HOST RANGE, REPLICATION CHARACTERISTICS, AND HTFR1 USAGE OF HISTORICAL AND RECENT HUMAN TCRV ISOLATES. THIS PROJECT IS EXPECTED TO GENERATE CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO TCRV’S EMERGENCE. GIVEN THE PRESENCE OF TCRV IN THE U.S., UNDERSTANDING THE FACTORS DRIVING ITS EMERGENCE IS ESSENTIAL FOR DEVELOPING STRATEGIES TO PREVENT FUTURE TCRV INFECTIONS AND MITIGATE ITS PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXPLORING LGE ANTIBODIES FOR UROLOGIC CHRONIC PELVIC PAIN SYNDROME FLARE TRIGGER IDENTIFICATION AND PREVENTION - ABSTRACT INTERSTITIAL CYSTITIS/BLADDER PAIN SYNDROME AND CHRONIC PROSTATITIS/CHRONIC PELVIC PAIN SYNDROME, COLLECTIVELY REFERRED TO AS UROLOGIC CHRONIC PELVIC PAIN SYNDROME (UCPPS), ARE COMMON, COSTLY, AND DEBILITATING SYNDROMES CHARACTERIZED BY PERSISTENT BLADDER AND/OR PELVIC PAIN, AND URINARY SYMPTOMS. THE ETIOLOGY OF UCPPS IS UNKNOWN AND ITS PATHOPHYSIOLOGY IS POORLY UNDERSTOOD, MAKING TREATMENT CHALLENGING. ALTHOUGH MANY THERAPIES HAVE BEEN PROPOSED, NONE WORK CONSISTENTLY IN ALL PATIENTS, AND MOST ARE EITHER INVASIVE OR PRONE TO SIGNIFICANT SIDE EFFECTS. CLINICAL MANAGEMENT IS FURTHER CHALLENGED BY THE OCCURRENCE OF FREQUENT, PAINFUL, AND OFTEN UNPREDICTABLE SYMPTOM EXACERBATIONS OR “FLARES.” SIMILAR TO THE CONDITION AS A WHOLE, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THE CAUSES OF FLARES OR HOW TO PREVENT AND TREAT THEM. THIS QUESTION IS FURTHER COMPLICATED BY THE LARGE NUMBER OF PROPOSED FLARE TRIGGERS IN THE SCIENTIFIC AND LAY LITERATURE (>140 FOODS AND >30 ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS), AND THE SUSPECTED INDIVIDUAL NATURE OF THESE TRIGGERS (I.E. EACH PATIENT MAY HAVE A DIFFERENT SET OF TRIGGERS). THEREFORE, NEW PERSONALIZED FLARE TRIGGER IDENTIFICATION AND PREVENTION STRATEGIES ARE NEEDED—FOR EXAMPLE, STRATEGIES GUIDED BY ALLERGEN-SPECIFIC IGE (SIGE) ANTIBODY TESTING. THIS IDEA IS SUPPORTED BY SEVERAL LINES OF EVIDENCE, INCLUDING PROMISING FINDINGS FROM OBSERVATIONAL, EXPERIMENTAL, AND HISTOPATHOLOGIC STUDIES; AS WELL AS IN VITRO MECHANISTIC AND ANIMAL MODEL STUDIES. OF PARTICULAR RELEVANCE, TWO SMALL EXPERIMENTAL STUDIES OBSERVED INCREASED CONCENTRATIONS OF URINARY/BLADDER IGE ANTIBODY INDUCED-MEDIATORS AFTER ALLERGEN EXPOSURE GUIDED BY ALLERGIC SENSITIZATION TESTING IN UCPPS PATIENTS, AND THREE CASE REPORTS OBSERVED SYMPTOM IMPROVEMENT AFTER ELIMINATION OF ALLERGENS TO WHICH PATIENTS MOUNTED AN IGE ANTIBODY RESPONSE (N=10 PATIENTS COMBINED). WE ALSO RECENTLY OBSERVED A BORDERLINE STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT HIGHER PREVALENCE OF OVERALL ALLERGIC SENSITIZATION IN UCPPS CASES THAN CONTROLS (90% VS. 40%, P=0.057) IN A SMALL PILOT STUDY. HOWEVER, BEFORE WE CAN TRANSLATE THESE PROMISING FINDINGS INTO FLARE PREVENTION TRIALS, WE NEED DATA FROM AT LEAST ONE LARGE, WELL-DESIGNED STUDY TO SUPPORT A ROLE FOR SIGE ANTIBODIES IN UCPPS SYMPTOMS. WITH THE PROPOSED R21, WE PLAN TO GENERATE THESE DATA. SPECIFICALLY, WE PROPOSE TO LEVERAGE EXISTING PLASMA FROM THE NIH-SPONSORED MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH TO THE STUDY OF CHRONIC PELVIC PAIN EPIDEMIOLOGIC CASE-CONTROL STUDY (100 CASES AND 100 CONTROLS), ALONG WITH STATE-OF-THE-ART, MULTIPLEX SIGE ANTIBODY TESTING, TO INVESTIGATE WHETHER UCPPS CASES AND THOSE WITH A HIGHER FLARE BURDEN HAVE GREATER EVIDENCE OF OVERALL AND ALLERGEN-SPECIFIC SENSITIZATION THAN HEALTHY CONTROLS AND THOSE WITH A LOWER FLARE BURDEN. WE WILL ALSO EXPLORE PATIENT SUBGROUPS WITH THE STRONGEST ASSOCIATIONS. TOGETHER, THESE AIMS WILL PROVIDE MUCH-NEEDED EVIDENCE TO SUPPORT A FUTURE RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL OF FLARE PREVENTION, INFORMING NOT ONLY THE NEED FOR A TRIAL, BUT ALSO THE NATURE OF THE INTERVENTION (E.G. PERSONALIZED ALLERGEN ELIMINATION) AND THE PATIENT SUBGROUPS MOST LIKELY TO BENEFIT. THUS, THIS R21 HOLDS THE PROMISE TO INFORM NEW, SAFE, AND EFFECTIVE COMPLEMENTARY AND/OR INTEGRATIVE UCPPS MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ESTIMATING THE CAUSAL EFFECT OF EARLY PEANUT INTRODUCTION ON THE RISK OF FOOD PROTEIN ENTEROCOLITIS SYNDROME (FPIES) - PROJECT SUMMARY AND ABSTRACT BACKGROUND: FOOD PROTEIN-INDUCED ENTEROCOLITIS SYNDROME (FPIES) IS A NON-IMMUNOGLOBULIN E (IGE) MEDIATED FOOD ALLERGY WITH CLINICAL PRESENTATION OF GASTROINTESTINAL SYMPTOMS INCLUDING VOMITING AND DIARRHEA 1- 4 HOURS AFTER INGESTION OF A FOOD TRIGGER. FPIES IMPACTS 0.51% OF US CHILDREN AND MOST PRESENT WITH SYMPTOMS BEFORE AGE ONE. AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF PEANUT FPIES CASES COINCIDED WITH A MAJOR CHANGE IN CLINICAL GUIDANCE AROUND THE PREVENTION OF IGE- MEDIATED PEANUT ALLERGY. IN 2017, THE ADDENDUM GUIDELINES FOR THE PREVENTION OF PEANUT ALLERGY (PPA GUIDELINES) ENCOURAGED PEDIATRIC CLINICIANS TO RECOMMEND THE INTRODUCTION OF PEANUT CONTAINING FOODS FOR MOST CHILDREN AROUND 6 MONTHS OF AGE. WHILE THIS GUIDANCE MAY HELP PREVENT PEANUT ALLERGY, THE EARLY INTRODUCTION OF ALLERGENIC SOLIDS MAY HAVE UNINTENDED HARM FOR SOME CHILDREN. SPECIFIC AIMS AND METHODS: THIS STUDY AIMS TO ASSESS THE IMPACT OF EARLY INTRODUCTION OF PEANUT-CONTAINING FOODS ON THE RISK OF DEVELOPING PEANUT-INDUCED, FPIES. WE WILL DO THIS BY LEVERAGING DATA AND EXOGENOUS VARIATION STEMMING FROM THE INTERVENTION TO REDUCE EARLY PEANUT ALLERGY IN CHILDREN (IREACH) TRIAL. IREACH IS A PEDIATRIC PRACTICE-BASED, RANDOMIZED CONTROL TRIAL OF A CLINICIAN-FACING INTERVENTION. IN TOTAL, ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR) DATA OF 18480 INFANTS WERE COLLECTED FROM 30 PEDIATRIC PRACTICES. THIS PROJECT WILL LEVERAGE EXISTING EHR DATA AND CAREGIVER SURVEYS IN A SUBSET OF INFANTS. THE STUDY AIMS ARE AS FOLLOWS: 1) TO ESTIMATE CAUSAL MODELS OF THE INCIDENCE OF PEANUT FPIES AS A FUNCTION OF EARLY PEANUT INTRODUCTION USING EHR-VALIDATED SURVEY DATA, AND 2) TO DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF THE IREACH INTERVENTION ON CAREGIVER-REPORTED FOOD RELATED ALLERGIC REACTIONS AND FPIES INCIDENCE TO THE TOP NINE ALLERGENIC FOODS. HYPOTHESES AND EXPECTED RESULTS: OUR PRIMARY STUDY HYPOTHESES ARE BASED ON A CONCEPTUAL MODEL ASSOCIATING EARLY PEANUT INTRODUCTION EARLY WITH THE DEVELOPMENT OF PEANUT FPIES. SPECIFICALLY, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE EARLY INTRODUCTION OF PEANUT CONTAINING FOODS WILL BE ASSOCIATED WITH A HIGHER INCIDENCE OF PEANUT FPIES. SECONDARY HYPOTHESES WILL TEST SPILLOVER EFFECTS OF IREACH ON THE LIKELIHOOD OF REACTIONS TO THE OTHER TOP ALLERGENIC SOLIDS AND CORRESPONDING FPIES. SIGNIFICANCE AND EFFECTS ON OTHER RESEARCH: THE RESULTS OF THIS STUDY WILL ADDRESS A QUESTION OF GREAT PUBLIC HEALTH SIGNIFICANCE CURRENTLY BEING EXAMINED BY THE UNITED STATES PREVENTIVE SERVICES TASK FORCE. THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE THE NECESSARY EVIDENCE TO PROVIDE RATIONALE FOR A LARGE-SCALE INVESTIGATION OF THE FACTORS THAT MAKE EARLY INTRODUCTION RISKY FOR SOME CHILDREN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MYBPC1-TARGETED THERAPEUTIC DISCOVERY PLATFORM FOR TREATMENT OF DISTAL ARTHROGRYPOSIS - PROJECT SUMMARY DISTAL ARTHROGRYPOSIS (DA) IS A DISORDER THAT OCCURS IN 1 OF 3,000 LIVE BIRTHS. DA IS TYPICALLY CAUSED BY MUTATIONS IN GENES EXPRESSED IN MUSCLE, INCLUDING THE SLOW SKELETAL MYOSIN BINDING PROTEIN-C (SMYBP-C) GENE (MYBPC1). PATIENTS EXHIBIT CONGENITAL JOINT CONTRACTURES, MUSCLE WEAKNESS, REDUCED MOBILITY, AND MORBIDITY. THERE IS NO CURE FOR DA, AND THUS IT REMAINS AN UNMET MEDICAL NEED. PAINFUL JOINT CONTRACTURES IN THE HANDS AND FEET OF DA PATIENTS ARE DUE TO PERMANENT MUSCLE SHORTENING. ANY THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY THAT IMPROVES MUSCLE FUNCTION WOULD HAVE A BROAD AND MEANINGFUL IMPACT FOR PATIENTS. WE FOCUS ON SMYBP-C, WHICH HAS BEEN RECENTLY SHOWN TO REGULATE MUSCLE CONTRACTILITY AND SHORTENING AND IDENTIFIED AS A THERAPEUTIC TARGET FOR CORRECTING CONTRACTILE DYSFUNCTION IN MUSCLE DISORDERS. TARGETING SMYBP-C WITH DRUGS THAT MODULATE BINDING TO ACTIN OR MYOSIN IS A PROMISING THERAPEUTIC APPROACH. A CRITICAL BARRIER TO PROGRESS IS THAT NO SMALL-MOLECULE DRUGS ARE AVAILABLE TO SELECTIVELY TARGET SMYBP-C FOR IMPROVING MUSCLE FUNCTION AND HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING (HTS) ASSAYS BASED ON SMYBP-C HAVE NOT BEEN AVAILABLE – UNTIL NOW. THE PI, DR. COLSON, DEVELOPED NEW FLUORESCENCE LIFETIME (FLT)-BASED HTS TOOLS FOR IDENTIFYING ‘HIT’ COMPOUNDS IN CHEMICAL LIBRARIES THAT BIND TO NORMAL AND DA MUTANT SMYBP-C N- TERMINAL DOMAINS FOR STREAMLINING THOSE DRUGS AFFECTING SKELETAL MUSCLE PERFORMANCE. CO-I DR. ESPINOZA-FONSECA HAS RECENTLY DEVELOPED A MACHINE LEARNING-BASED VIRTUAL SCREENING TO IDENTIFY ADDITIONAL HITS TO ENABLE HIT-TO-LEAD OPTIMIZATION. CO-I DR. SADAYAPPAN PROVIDES TWO NEWLY CHARACTERIZED KNOCK-IN MOUSE MODELS OF HUMAN DA CARRYING MYBPC1 MUTATIONS P295L (HUMAN P319L) OR E335K (HUMAN E359K). PROMISING DRUGS PRIORITIZED BY IN VITRO BIOCHEMICAL AND BIOPHYSICAL ASSAYS AND IN SILICO AI-BASED APPROACHES AND MOLECULAR DYNAMICS SIMULATIONS WILL BE TESTED BY IN SITU AND IN VIVO CONTRACTILE PERFORMANCE IN THE DA MOUSE MODELS, SUPPORTED BY CO-I DR. GRANZIER’S MOUSE PHENOTYPING EXPERTISE. USING THESE INNOVATIVE SCREENING TOOLS AND GENETIC MODELS, IT IS NOW FEASIBLE TO IDENTIFY MODULATORS OF SMYBP-C WITH POTENTIAL TO TREAT THE UNDERLYING CONTRACTILE DYSFUNCTION IN DA. THE MAJOR GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IMPLEMENT EARLY-STAGE DRUG DISCOVERY CAMPAIGNS TARGETING THE SMYBP-C-ACTIN/MYOSIN INTERACTIONS USING BIOPHYSICAL, BIOCHEMICAL, COMPUTATIONAL, AND PHYSIOLOGICAL METHODS. WE WILL IDENTIFY SMYBP-C-TARGETING COMPOUNDS AFFECTING ACTIN OR MYOSIN INTERACTIONS AND PRIORITIZE FOR DRUG LIKENESS IN AIM 1 AND DETERMINE THE POTENCY AND SPECIFICITY OF COMPOUNDS TO AFFECT NORMAL AND DA MUSCLE FUNCTION IN AIM 2, ENABLING RIGOROUS PRE-CLINICAL VALIDATION OF THE THERAPEUTIC TARGET. WE WILL TEST THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT PHARMACOLOGIC TARGETING OF SMYBP-C CAN IMPROVE SKELETAL MUSCLE FUNCTION IN DA.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A RADIOGENOMIC APPROACH FOR VIRTUAL BIOPSY OF BONE REMODELING IN FEMOROACETABULAR IMPINGEMENT - PROJECT SUMMARY FEMOROACETABULAR IMPINGEMENT (FAI) SYNDROME IS A LEADING CAUSE OF HIP PAIN IN YOUNG ADULTS AND A STRONG MODIFIABLE RISK FACTOR FOR EARLY OSTEOARTHRITIS. MANY INDIVIDUALS WITH CAM OR PINCER MORPHOLOGIES REMAIN ASYMPTOMATIC, CREATING DIAGNOSTIC UNCERTAINTY AND LEADING TO DELAYED CARE, UNNECESSARY PROCEDURES, AND PREVENTABLE DISABILITY. MOLECULAR STUDIES SHOW THAT SUBCHONDRAL BONE, CARTILAGE, LABRUM, AND SYNOVIUM IN FAI EXPRESS INFLAMMATORY AND REMODELING GENES, IMPLICATING BONE TURNOVER AS AN UPSTREAM DRIVER OF SYMPTOMS AND DEGENERATION. AT PRESENT, NO VALIDATED NONINVASIVE BIOMARKERS EXIST TO CAPTURE THIS BIOLOGY FOR PROGNOSIS OR TREATMENT SELECTION. THIS R21 WILL TEST THE FEASIBILITY OF A RADIOGENOMIC “VIRTUAL BIOPSY” THAT LINKS ROUTINE MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (MRI) FEATURES TO BONE GENE EXPRESSION IN FAI. OUR INNOVATION IS THREEFOLD. FIRST, WE WILL ESTABLISH MOLECULAR BENCHMARKS OF BONE INFLAMMATION AND TURNOVER USING SURGICALLY DISCARDED TISSUE, CREATING THE BONE INFLAMMATION AND TURNOVER INDEX (BITI) AND A FOCUSED FIVE-GENE BITI-5 SCORE. SECOND, WE WILL DEVELOP MODELS THAT MAP MRI RADIOMICS TO THESE INDICES, ENABLING NONINVASIVE ESTIMATES OF BONE MOLECULAR ACTIVITY. THIRD, WE WILL EVALUATE WHETHER THESE VIRTUAL BIOPSY OUTPUTS IMPROVE PREDICTION OF PAIN, FUNCTION, AND CARTILAGE OUTCOMES, AND PROTOTYPE INTEGRATION INTO A CLOUD-BASED DECISION SUPPORT ENVIRONMENT. AIM 1 WILL ENROLL 40 FAI PATIENTS AND 20 CONTROLS TO DERIVE BITI AND BITI-5 FROM BULK RNA SEQUENCING. AIM 2 WILL TRAIN AND VALIDATE MRI-TO-BITI PREDICTION MODELS USING MACHINE LEARNING APPROACHES WITH SAFEGUARDS AGAINST OVERFITTING. AIM 3 WILL TEST PROGNOSTIC UTILITY IN A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT OF 200 FAI PATIENTS WITH FIVE-YEAR PATIENT- REPORTED OUTCOME MEASURES (PROMS), WHICH ARE COLLECTED YEARLY THROUGH STANDARDIZED QUESTIONNAIRES, A MINIMALLY INVASIVE METHOD OF LONGITUDINAL OUTCOME ASSESSMENT. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE VALIDATED MOLECULAR BENCHMARKS, NONINVASIVE RADIOGENOMIC MAPPINGS, AND PROOF THAT PREDICTED BITI ADDS PROGNOSTIC VALUE BEYOND CLINICAL AND IMAGING VARIABLES. THE IMPACT WILL BE A FIRST BIOLOGICALLY INFORMED IMAGING BIOMARKER FOR FAI THAT CAN IMPROVE PATIENT SELECTION FOR SURGERY, REDUCE UNNECESSARY PROCEDURES, AND ENABLE PRECISION PREVENTION OF EARLY HIP OSTEOARTHRITIS, WHILE LAYING THE GROUNDWORK FOR A MULTICENTER R01.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE ORIGIN AND FATE OF ADIPO-CAR CELLS IN PTH1R-OSXKO MICE - PROJECT SUMMARY SKELETAL FRAGILITY DUE TO LOW BONE MASS IN OSTEOPOROSIS CAUSES FRACTURES IN 50% OF WOMEN AND 25% OF MEN OVER AGE 50. REDUCED BONE MASS IS ACCOMPANIED BY INCREASED MARROW FAT. ELUCIDATING A COMMON MECHANISM FOR FAT AND BONE MASS CHANGES MAY LEAD TO CLINICALLY RELEVANT TARGETS FOR OSTEOPOROSIS TREATMENT. WITHIN THE BONE MICROENVIRONMENT BOTH BONE-FORMING OSTEOBLASTS AND FAT-LADEN ADIPOCYTES ARE DERIVED FROM MESENCHYMAL STEM CELLS (MSCS). MSC FATE RELIES IN PART ON PARATHYROID HORMONE RECEPTOR (PTH1R) SIGNALING. CONDITIONAL KNOCKOUT (CKO) OF PTH1R IN OSTERIX (OSX)-EXPRESSING OSTEOPROGENITORS IN MICE RESULTS IN SEVERE BONE LOSS WHILE CKO OF PTH1R IN PRX1-EXPRESSING MESENCHYMAL PROGENITORS LEADS TO DECREASED BONE PLUS INCREASED MARROW FAT. HOWEVER, HOW PTH1R SIGNALING INFLUENCES MESENCHYMAL LINEAGE ALLOCATION REMAINS INCOMPLETELY UNDERSTOOD. ADVANCEMENTS IN SINGLE-CELL RNA-SEQUENCING (SCRNA-SEQ) AND LINEAGE TRACING HAVE ENHANCED OUR UNDERSTANDING OF MESENCHYMAL POPULATIONS AND IDENTIFIED OSTEO- AND ADIPO- “CXCL12- ABUNDANT RETICULAR” (CAR) CELLS. WE HAVE DISCOVERED A SIGNIFICANTLY EXPANDED ADIPO-CAR POPULATION IN PTH1R- OSXKO MOUSE BONE. HOWEVER, THE ORIGIN AND FATE OF ADIPO-CAR CELLS ARE NOT CLEAR. PRELIMINARY CYTOTRACE ANALYSIS SUGGESTS THAT ADIPO-CAR CELLS ARE MORE DIFFERENTIATED THAN THEIR MESENCHYMAL PROGENITORS AND OSTEO- CAR CELLS. TO CLARIFY THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN OSX+ PROGENITORS, OSTEO-CAR, AND ADIPO-CAR POPULATIONS, WE WILL USE DNA BARCODING FOR IN VIVO LINEAGE TRACING. THIS INNOVATIVE APPROACH OVERCOMES LIMITATIONS OF CLASSICAL LINEAGE TRACING INCLUDING INABILITY TO DISTINGUISH OVERLAPPING POPULATIONS OR DETERMINE CELL ORIGIN, AND TECHNICAL DIFFICULTY WITH COMPLEX MULTI-ALLELE CROSSES. BASED ON OUR PRELIMINARY AND PUBLISHED DATA WE HYPOTHESIZE PTH1R GOVERNS THE FATE SWITCH BETWEEN OSTEO-CAR AND ADIPO-CAR POPULATIONS. IN SPECIFIC AIM 1 WE WILL OPTIMIZE DNA BARCODING-BASED LINEAGE TRACING IN THE BONE MICROENVIRONMENT. USING THE CELLTAG DNA BARCODING SYSTEM COUPLED TO SCRNA-SEQ ANALYSIS WE WILL PERFORM LINEAGE TRACING IN VITRO WITH CULTURED BONE MARROW-DERIVED MESENCHYMAL CELLS AND PILOT IN VIVO LINEAGE TRACING IN CONTROL [OSX+:GFP:CRE] AND WILDTYPE (WT) MICE. WE PREDICT THAT WE WILL SUCCESSFULLY INTEGRATE THE CELLTAG SYSTEM INTO OUR MODELS FOR LINEAGE TRACING IN THE BONE MICROENVIRONMENT. IN SPECIFIC AIM 2 WE WILL DETERMINE IF EXPANDED PTH1R-OSXKO ADIPO-CAR CELLS ARE DERIVED FROM OSX+ PROGENITORS AND GIVE RISE TO ADIPOCYTES. WE WILL IMPLEMENT OUR OPTIMIZED CELLTAG PROTOCOL TO TRANSDUCE PTH1R-OSXKO:TDTOMATO (KO) AND PTH1R-OSXWT:TDTOMATO (CONTROL) MICE VIA INTRATIBIAL INJECTION FOR SCRNA-SEQ AND LINEAGE TRACING ANALYSIS, AND IMAGE KO AND CONTROL MOUSE FEMURS TO VALIDATE ADIPO-CAR CELL ACCUMULATION AND LOCALIZATION. WE PREDICT ADIPO-CAR CELLS ARE ELEVATED DUE TO RE-ALLOCATION OF OSX+ PROGENITORS AND IN TURN GIVE RISE TO MORE ADIPOCYTES. UNDERSTANDING MSC LINEAGE HIERARCHIES IS CRUCIAL TO DEFINE THE SIGNALING PATHWAYS THAT COOPERATIVELY REGULATE MARROW FAT ACCUMULATION AND BONE LOSS.

description: IMPROVING PAIN MANAGEMENT FOR WOMEN WITH METASTATIC BREAST CANCER: DEVELOPMENT AND PROOF-OF-CONCEPT STUDY OF A VIDEOCONFERENCE HYPNOSIS INTERVENTION - SUMMARY  OVER 168,000 WOMEN ARE LIVING WITH METASTATIC BREAST CANCER (MBC) IN THE UNITED STATES. PAIN IS COMMON IN INDIVIDUALS WITH MBC, AND CAN BE ASSOCIATED WITH THE CANCER ITSELF AS WELL AS WITH CANCER TREATMENTS. NOT SURPRISINGLY, PAINMANAGEMENT IS A CRITICAL COMPONENT OF COMPREHENSIVE CANCER CARE IN THE MBC SETTING.IT IS WIDELY HELD THAT COMPREHENSIVE CANCER PAIN MANAGEMENT SHOULD INCORPORATE BOTH PHARMACOLOGIC AND NON- PHARMACOLOGIC APPROACHES. PHARMACOLOGIC APPROACHES TO MBC PAIN CAN INCLUDE OPIOIDS, ANTIDEPRESSANTS, ANTI- SEIZURE MEDICATIONS, AND CORTICOSTEROIDS. UNFORTUNATELY, SUCH TREATMENTS OFTEN HAVE SIDE EFFECTS OF THEIR OWN. FURTHERMORE, SOME PAIN MEDICATIONS MAY BE CONTRAINDICATED FOR PATIENTS WITH COMORBIDITIES, AND SOME MAY BE LESS PALATABLE TO PATIENTS FOR REASONS LIKE FEAR OF ADDICTION. FORTUNATELY, NON-PHARMACOLGIC TREATMENTS CAN HAVE MEANINGFUL BENEFITS WITH NO ADVERSE EFFECTS. HYPNOSIS IS AN EVIDENCE-BASED, MIND-BODY TECHNIQUE, WHICH HAS A LONG TRADITION IN ADJUNCTIVE CANCER SYMPTOM MANAGEMENT, ESPECIALLY FOR PAIN. HYPNOSIS HAS STRONG EFFICACY DATA FOR CONTROLLING MULTIPLE TYPES OF PAIN, HAS NO KNOWN SPECIFIC ADVERSE EFFECTS, AND SELF-HYPNOSIS CAN BE TAUGHT TO PATIENTS TO SELF-MANAGE THEIR PAIN. ADDITIONAL HYPNOSIS BENEFITS INCLUDE RAPID ONSET OF ACTION AND LOW PATIENT BURDEN. HYPNOSIS IS A PARTICULARLY APT FIT FOR THE MBC SETTING AS ONCE PATIENTS LEARN SELF-HYPNOSIS, THEY CAN USE IT TO SELF-MANAGE THE HETEROGENEOUS TYPES OF PAIN THEY EXPERIENCE.  TO OUR KNOWLEDGE, NO HYPNOSIS INTERVENTION HAS BEEN DEVELOPED OR TESTED AS A STAND-ALONE BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTION FOR THE LARGE AND GROWING NUMBER OF WOMEN LIVING WITH MBC. THOSE WITH METASTATIC CANCER OFTEN HAVE DIFFERENT NEEDS THAN THOSE WITH EARLIER-STAGE CANCERS (E.G., DIFFERING PAIN SEVERITY, CHRONICITY, HETEROGENEITY), WHICH IS WHY RESEARCH IS NEEDED FOCUSED ON THEIR EXPERIENCE. ADDITIONALLY, DESPITE PROVIDERS ROUTINELY CONDUCTING TELETHERAPY SINCE THE PANDEMIC, THERE HAVE BEEN ONLY A HANDFUL OF STUDIES TESTING VIDEOCONFERENCE HYPNOSIS (V- HYP), AND NONE IN CANCER. TELEHEALTH IS THE NEW NORM, AND IS THE LEAST BURDENSOME APPROACH FOR PATIENTS WHOSE PAIN MIGHT BE A BARRIER TO IN-PERSON ATTENDANCE. THUS, DATA IS CLEARLY NEEDED TO GUIDE TELE-HYPNOSIS INTERVENTION DESIGNS AND DELIVERY. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL BEGIN TO FILL THESE RESEARCH GAPS.  THE GOAL OF THIS STUDY, GUIDED BY THE ORBIT MODEL AND NEUROMATIX PAIN THEORY, IS TO: 1) DEVELOP, REFINE, AND TEST THE ACCEPTABILITY OF V-HYP AND VIDEOCONFERENCE ATTENTION CONTROL (V-AC) INTERVENTIONS FOR MBC PAIN (AIM 1). INTERVENTION CONTENT AND FORMAT WILL BE INFORMED BY QUALITATIVE DATA AND ACCEPTABILITY SURVEYS DURING SUCCESSIVE 5-PERSON COHORTS FOR EACH ARM [N=30 (15 V-HYP, 15 V-AC)]. WE ANTICIPATE THAT V-HYP WILL INVOLVE 3 WEEKLY SESSIONS WITH AT-HOME PRACTICE; 2) WOMEN WITH MBC (N=60) WILL BE ENROLLED IN A RANDOMIZED FEASIBILITY (AIM 2) AND PROOF-OF-CONCEPT (AIM 3) STUDY. WE WILL EXAMINE FEASIBILITY WITH REGARD TO A PRIORI BENCHMARKS, AND CHANGES IN PAIN OVER TIME (4-WEEK FOLLOW-UP). RESULTS OF THIS PROJECT WILL DIRECTLY INFORM A FUTURE RCT TO EVALUATE V-HYP EFFICACY, TO UNDERSTAND MEDIATORS AND MODERATORS OF V-HYP EFFECTS, AND TO ESTABLISH COST-EFFECTIVENESS.

description: INTERFERON-Γ IN COMBINATION WITH DONOR LEUKOCYTE INFUSION TO TREAT RELAPSED ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA AND MYELODYSPLASTIC SYNDROMES AFTER HAPLOIDENTICAL DONOR STEM CELL TRANSPLANTATION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ALLOGENEIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANTATION (ALLOSCT) OFFERS A POTENTIAL CURE FOR ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA (AML) AND MYELODYSPLASTIC SYNDROME (MDS); HOWEVER, DISEASE RELAPSE—REFLECTING FAILURE OF THE GRAFT-VERSUS-LEUKEMIA (GVL) EFFECT—REMAINS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH AFTER BOTH HLA-MATCHED AND HAPLOIDENTICAL TRANSPLANTATION (HAPLO-SCT). DONOR-DERIVED ALLOREACTIVE T CELLS MEDIATE GVL BY RECOGNIZING AND ELIMINATING RECIPIENT LEUKEMIA CELLS, YET ONLY 10–20% OF PATIENTS WHO RELAPSE AFTER ALLOSCT ACHIEVE DURABLE SURVIVAL. NEW STRATEGIES TO ENHANCE GVL WITHOUT INCREASING GRAFT-VERSUS-HOST DISEASE (GVHD) ARE URGENTLY NEEDED. PRECLINICAL STUDIES BY DR. SHLOMCHIK (CO-I) DEMONSTRATED THAT IFN-Γ RECEPTOR SIGNALING IS ESSENTIAL FOR EFFECTIVE GVL, AS LEUKEMIAS LACKING THIS PATHWAY ARE RESISTANT TO IMMUNE ELIMINATION. CONSISTENT WITH THIS, AML SAMPLES OBTAINED AT POST-TRANSPLANT RELAPSE SHOW REDUCED HLA EXPRESSION, WHICH CAN BE RESTORED BY IFN-Γ EXPOSURE. BUILDING ON THESE FINDINGS, DR. ITO (PI) CONDUCTED A PHASE I CLINICAL TRIAL COMBINING IFN-Γ WITH DONOR LYMPHOCYTE INFUSION (DLI) IN RELAPSED AML/MDS AFTER HLA-MATCHED ALLOSCT (NCT04628338; JCI INSIGHT, 2025), ACHIEVING DURABLE COMPLETE REMISSIONS (CR) IN FOUR OF SIX TREATED PATIENTS. A MULTICENTER PHASE II TRIAL IN HLA-MATCHED RECIPIENTS IS ONGOING (NCT06529731). GIVEN THE HIGHER GVHD RISK ASSOCIATED WITH HAPLOIDENTICAL DLI, THE SAFETY OF IFN-Γ IN THIS SETTING REQUIRES DEDICATED EVALUATION. MOREOVER, RELAPSE FOLLOWING HAPLO-SCT FREQUENTLY RESULTS FROM LOSS OF THE MISMATCHED HLA LOCUS THROUGH LOSS OF HETEROZYGOSITY (HLA-LOH), CONFERRING IMMUNE ESCAPE. WE THEREFORE PROPOSE A SUB- COHORT STUDY WITHIN NCT06529731 TO TEST IFN-Γ/DLI IN PATIENTS WITH RELAPSED AML/MDS AFTER HAPLO-SCT WHO HAVE MEASURABLE BONE MARROW DISEASE AND NO EVIDENCE OF HLA-LOH. PARTICIPANTS WILL RECEIVE IFN-Γ (100 ΜG SUBCUTANEOUSLY THREE TIMES WEEKLY FOR FOUR WEEKS). IF WELL TOLERATED, UP TO TWO DLIS WILL BE ADMINISTERED CONCURRENTLY WITH IFN-Γ OVER 12 WEEKS. THE PRIMARY ENDPOINT IS SAFETY, DEFINED BY THE INCIDENCE OF STEROID- AND RUXOLITINIB-REFRACTORY GVHD. SECONDARY ENDPOINTS INCLUDE PRELIMINARY EFFICACY OUTCOMES, WHILE COLLECTING SEQUENTIAL BIOSPECIMENS FOR FUTURE EXPLORATORY CORRELATIVE STUDIES CHARACTERIZING PHENOTYPIC, TRANSCRIPTIONAL, AND FUNCTIONAL CHANGES IN LEUKEMIA CELLS AND IMMUNE CELLS. USING A BAYESIAN OPTIMAL INTERVAL (BOIN) DESIGN, 6–12 PATIENTS WILL BE ENROLLED WITH PREDEFINED GVHD-BASED STOPPING RULES. IF THIS STUDY DEMONSTRATES SAFETY WITH EARLY EFFICACY SIGNALS, IT WILL PROVIDE THE FOUNDATION FOR A SUBSEQUENT PHASE II TRIAL FOCUSED ON EFFICACY, ADDRESSING A CRITICAL UNMET NEED IN POST-HAPLO-SCT RELAPSE OF AML/MDS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPROVED FIBRIN-TARGETED RADIOPHARMACEUTICAL FOR GASTRIC CANCER - GASTRIC CANCER (GC) IS ASSOCIATED WITH POOR CLINICAL OUTCOMES DUE TO A LACK OF EFFECTIVE THERAPIES. RADICAL SURGERY IS THE ONLY CURATIVE OPTION FOR LOCALIZED DISEASE. HOWEVER, MOST PATIENTS PRESENT WITH ADVANCED DISEASE AT DIAGNOSIS AND OFTEN WITH METASTASES ALREADY EVIDENT. CHEMOTHERAPY IS THE STANDARD TREATMENT FOR ADVANCED GC, BUT NEARLY ALL PATIENTS WHO INITIALLY RESPOND TO FIRST-LINE CHEMOTHERAPY EVENTUALLY RELAPSE OR EXPERIENCE DISEASE PROGRESSION. THERAPEUTIC OPTIONS BECOME INCREASINGLY LIMITED AS TREATMENT RESISTANCE DEVELOPS WITH SUBSEQUENT LINES OF THERAPY. THERE IS, THEREFORE, A CRITICAL NEED TO DEVELOP NOVEL THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES FOR PATIENTS WITH ADVANCED GC TO IMPROVE CLINICAL OUTCOMES. ONE PROMISING APPROACH FOR GC THERAPY IS RADIOLIGAND THERAPY (RLT), WHICH OFFERS ENHANCED PRECISION WHILE LIMITING HARM TO NORMAL TISSUES COMPARED TO CHEMOTHERAPY OR CONVENTIONAL RADIOTHERAPY. THE INSOLUBLE PROTEIN FIBRIN IS PRESENT IN MANY SOLID TUMORS, INCLUDING PRIMARY AND METASTATIC GC, AND ARISES FROM THE LEAK OF SOLUBLE FIBRINOGEN FROM THE BLOOD INTO THE INTERSTITIAL SPACE OF THE TUMOR, WHERE IT IS CONVERTED TO FIBRIN. FIBRIN AT MICROMOLAR CONCENTRATIONS HAS BEEN OBSERVED IN VARIOUS SOLID TUMORS, METASTASES, AND PATHOLOGICAL CONDITIONS SUCH AS THROMBOSIS BUT IS NOT PRESENT IN HEALTHY TISSUES. WE RECENTLY SHOWED THAT FIBRIN IS ABUNDANT IN TISSUE FROM PATIENT-DERIVED BIOPSIES OF PRIMARY AND METASTATIC GASTRIC ADENOCARCINOMA BUT NOT IN ADJACENT NORMAL STOMACH TISSUE. WE ALSO SHOWED THAT TUMOR FIBRIN COULD BE IMAGED IN GC PATIENTS WITH A FIBRIN-TARGETED PEPTIDE-BASED 64CU-LABELED PET PROBE DETECTING 53 PRIMARY AND METASTATIC GC LESIONS. WE THEN MODIFIED THE PET PROBE WITH THE HIGH ENERGY BETA EMITTER 90Y AS AN RLT AND USED TO EFFECTIVELY TREAT MOUSE MODELS OF GC. DESPITE THE SUCCESS OF THIS INITIAL WORK, WE NOTED TWO AREAS OF IMPROVEMENT: 1) WHOLE BODY PET SHOWED RAPID WASHOUT AND LOW UPTAKE IN OFF-TARGET ORGANS CONSISTENT WITH FIBRIN ONLY BEING PRESENT IN DISEASE OR WOUND HEALING, HOWEVER WE DID DETECT INCIDENTAL BLOOD CLOTS WITH THE PROBE IN 2/7 PATIENTS. 2) WE DEMONSTRATED THAT THE PET PROBE STAYED ON TARGET FOR AT LEAST 24 H BY IMAGING PATIENTS AGAIN A DAY AFTER DOSING, HOWEVER ABOUT 65% OF THE ACTIVITY HAD WASHED OUT CONSISTENT WITH NONCOVALENT BINDING TO AN EXTRACELLULAR TARGET. THERE IS AN OPPORTUNITY TO DEVELOP A FIBRIN-TARGETED RLT WITH PROLONGED TUMOR RETENTION AND SPECIFICITY. OUR OVERALL OBJECTIVE IN THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP A FIBRIN-TARGETED RLT THAT EXHIBITS PROLONGED RETENTION IN, AND SPECIFICITY FOR GC TUMORS COMPARED TO OUR CURRENT RLT IN ORDER TO DRAMATICALLY INCREASE THE THERAPEUTIC INDEX. WE PROPOSE TO MODIFY OUR FIBRIN-SPECIFIC PEPTIDE WITH A CHEMICAL GROUP CALLED A PRO-TAG THAT WILL COVALENTLY (IRREVERSIBLY) BIND TO FIBRIN, BUT ONLY IN THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT. WE WILL TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS IN ANIMAL MODELS OF GASTRIC CANCER. ANIMAL MODELS ARE ESSENTIAL BECAUSE THE BIODISTRIBUTION, DOSIMETRY, AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE OF RADIOPHARMACEUTICALS CANNOT BE ADEQUATELY REPLICATED IN VITRO. IF SUCCESSFUL, OUR APPROACH WILL PROVIDE A SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENT IN THE PRECISION AND EFFICACY OF RADIOLIGAND THERAPY FOR GC. MOREOVER, THIS TECHNIQUE HAS THE POTENTIAL TO BE APPLIED TO OTHER FIBRIN-RICH SOLID TUMORS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CONQUERING PAIN TOGETHER: FAMILY-BASED PAIN INTERVENTION FOR APPALACHIAN BREAST CANCER PATIENTS TAKING AETS - PROJECT SUMMARY APPALACHIA FACES A DEVASTATING CONVERGENCE OF HIGH BREAST CANCER MORTALITY AND A SEVERE PAIN EPIDEMIC. FOR BREAST CANCER PATIENTS ON LIFE-SAVING ADJUVANT ENDOCRINE THERAPY (AET), TREATMENT-RELATED PAIN IS THE PRIMARY DRIVER OF THERAPY DISCONTINUATION, DIRECTLY UNDERMINING SURVIVAL. PHARMACOLOGICAL PAIN MANAGEMENT OFFERS LIMITED BENEFIT AND CARRIES SIGNIFICANT RISK IN THIS OPIOID-AFFECTED REGION. NON-PHARMACOLOGIC INTERVENTIONS ARE IMPERATIVE, YET EXISTING PATIENT-FOCUSED MODELS SHOW LIMITED EFFECTIVENESS AND FAIL TO ADDRESS THE CULTURAL AND COMMUNITY FACTORS COMMON IN RURAL AREAS. OUR WORK HAS ESTABLISHED THAT PAIN IS NOT AN INDIVIDUAL EXPERIENCE BUT A DYADIC ONE; A CAREGIVER'S PSYCHOSOCIAL DISTRESS DIRECTLY PREDICTS WORSE PATIENT PAIN OUTCOMES. THE CONQUERING PAIN TOGETHER (CPT) INTERVENTION IS A NOVEL, DYADIC APPROACH DESIGNED TO DISRUPT THIS PATHWAY BY HARNESSING THE CORE APPALACHIAN STRENGTHS OF FAMILY AND FAITH. CPT TARGETS THE RELATIONAL MECHANISMS OF PAIN BY (1) HARNESSING RELATIONSHIP SUPPORT FOR JOINT PAIN MANAGEMENT, (2) MITIGATING DYADIC PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS, AND (3) OVERCOMING CHALLENGES THROUGH FLEXIBLE DELIVERY AND WARM HAND-OFFS TO COMMUNITY RESOURCES. THIS R21 PROPOSAL WILL DIRECTLY ADDRESS THESE GAPS THROUGH TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: 1. ADAPT THE CPT PROTOCOL VIA ITERATIVE, COMMUNITY-ENGAGED INTERVIEWS WITH APPALACHIAN BREAST CANCER DYADS (N=15) AND HEALTH PROFESSIONALS (N=5) TO ENSURE CULTURAL ALIGNMENT WITH RELIGIOUS TRADITIONS AND A FOCUS ON CANCER-SPECIFIC DISTRESS. 2. PILOT THE ADAPTED CPT IN A SINGLE-ARM FEASIBILITY TRIAL (N=30 DYADS), WITH PURPOSIVE SAMPLING TO ENSURE 50% RURAL ENROLLMENT, TO ESTABLISH BENCHMARKS FOR RECRUITMENT, ACCEPTABILITY, AND PROTOCOL ADHERENCE. BY CO-DESIGNING A CULTURALLY-GROUNDED, DYADIC INTERVENTION WITH AND FOR APPALACHIAN RURAL COMMUNITIES, THIS RESEARCH PROVIDES THE NECESSARY FOUNDATION FOR A FUTURE RCT TO TEST A SCALABLE STRATEGY TO REDUCE AET-RELATED PAIN, IMPROVE ADHERENCE, AND ULTIMATELY, ADDRESS A CRITICAL DRIVER OF CANCER MORTALITY DISPARITIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HIGH-THROUGHPUT IDENTIFICATION OF TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS THAT ENHANCE CAR T CELL EFFICACY IN SOLID TUMORS. - PROJECT SUMMARY WHILE CHIMERIC ANTIGEN RECEPTOR (CAR) T THERAPIES CAN BE HIGHLY EFFECTIVE AGAINST HEMATOLOGIC MALIGNANCIES, THEIR EFFICACY IN SOLID TUMORS IS LESS STRIKING. A MAJOR FACTOR LIMITING CAR T CELL THERAPY IN SOLID TUMORS IS THE PROGRESSIVE ACQUISITION OF A DYSFUNCTIONAL STATE TERMED “T CELL EXHAUSTION.” EXHAUSTION LIMITS T CELL PERSISTENCE AND THE ABILITY TO ELIMINATE TARGET CANCER CELLS AND ARISES IN CHRONIC VIRAL INFECTIONS AND CANCER THROUGH REPEATED ANTIGEN STIMULATION. THIS PROGRAM IS HARD-WIRED INTO ALL MATURE T CELLS TO PREVENT AUTOIMMUNE PATHOLOGY BUT INEVITABLY LEADS TO LOSS OF TUMOR CONTROL IN CANCER. GENETIC APPROACHES THAT DELETE INHIBITORY RECEPTORS OR NEGATIVE REGULATORS HAVE FAILED TO REVERSE EXHAUSTION, AND IN SOME CASES CAUSE UNANTICIPATED DEFECTS IN T CELL PERSISTENCE. BECAUSE EXHAUSTION IS A DISTINCT CELL STATE DEFINED BY MARKED TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC CHANGES, WE BELIEVE THAT OVEREXPRESSION OF TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS (TFS) COULD EXERT BROAD EFFECTS ON T CELL FUNCTION, INCLUDING EPIGENETIC REMODELING, DIFFERENTIATION, AND THE ACQUISITION OF CRITICAL FUNCTIONAL CAPACITIES. THE HUMAN GENOME ENCODES OVER 2000 TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC MODIFIERS, MAKING INDIVIDUAL ASSESSMENT OF EACH IMPRACTICAL. TO ASSESS THE IMPACT OF TF OVEREXPRESSION ON CAR T CELL FUNCTION AT SCALE, WE DEVELOPED AN IN VIVO SCREENING APPROACH THAT EVALUATES ALL HUMAN TFS IN PRIMARY HUMAN T CELLS. T CELLS ARE LENTIVIRALLY TRANSDUCED WITH A LIBRARY OF ALL HUMAN TF OPEN READING FRAMES (ORFS) AND EITHER EXPANDED IN VITRO OR TRANSFERRED INTO IMMUNODEFICIENT MICE BEARING HUMAN XENOGRAFT TUMORS THAT EXPRESS SURFACE ANTI-CD3. AFTER TWO WEEKS, T CELLS ARE ISOLATED AND SEQUENCED TO IDENTIFY TFS THAT INCREASE OR REDUCE T CELL ABUNDANCE UNDER IN VITRO AND IN VIVO CONDITIONS. USING THIS METHOD WE IDENTIFIED TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS, INCLUDING GFI1B, HOXD8, HOXC8, POU2F3, AND OTHERS, THAT INCREASE T CELL ABUNDANCE IN SOLID TUMORS. WE VALIDATED THAT EXPRESSION OF HOXD8 AND POU2F3 ENHANCES T CELL-MEDIATED TUMOR CONTROL. MANY OF THESE FACTORS HAVE NO PREVIOUSLY CHARACTERIZED ROLE IN T CELLS, AND SOME, SUCH AS THE HOX FAMILY TFS, ARE NOT EXPRESSED IN ANY ADULT LYMPHOCYTES. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THESE TFS WILL ENHANCE CAR T THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY IN PRECLINICAL MODELS AND DRIVE DISTINCT CHANGES IN THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC STATES OF T CELLS. WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER THESE TFS INCREASE EFFICACY OF CAR-T CELLS IN SOLID TUMOR XENOGRAFT MODELS AND PROFILE THE CHANGES IN TF BINDING, CHROMATIN ORGANIZATION AND GENE EXPRESSION IN THESE CAR T CELLS. ANIMALS ARE REQUIRED BECAUSE THE TRAFFICKING, INFILTRATION, AND PERSISTENCE OF HUMAN CAR T CELLS WITHIN A VASCULARIZED SOLID TUMOR CANNOT BE RECAPITULATED IN CULTURE. WE WILL THEREFORE USE IMMUNODEFICIENT NSG MICE BEARING HUMAN XENOGRAFT TUMORS, WHICH SUPPORT ENGRAFTMENT OF BOTH THE HUMAN TUMOR AND THE HUMAN CAR T CELLS, IN THE MINIMUM NUMBERS NEEDED FOR RIGOROUS STATISTICAL COMPARISON. THESE STUDIES WILL NOT ONLY ENABLE THE SELECTION OF THE MOST PROMISING CANDIDATES TO PURSUE INDIVIDUALLY OR IN COMBINATION IN CAR T CELL THERAPIES, BUT ALSO PROVIDE INSIGHTS INTO THE PLASTICITY AND REGULATION OF T CELL EXHAUSTION.

description: THE ROLE OF TERTIARY LYMPHOID STRUCTURES IN BRAIN TUMOR THERAPY WITH ONCOLYTIC ADENOVIRUSES - BRAIN TUMORS POSE FORMIDABLE CHALLENGES TO IMMUNOTHERAPY. THE UNIQUE IMMUNE ENVIRONMENT OF THE BRAIN, COMBINED WITH CLINICAL AND BIOLOGICAL BARRIERS, SEVERELY LIMITS THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY. GLIOBLASTOMA AND DIFFUSE MIDLINE GLIOMA REPRESENT THE MOST LETHAL PRIMARY BRAIN TUMORS, WITH MEDIAN OVERALL SURVIVAL OF APPROXIMATELY 12 MONTHS OR LESS. CONCURRENTLY, ADVANCES IN CANCER THERAPIES HAVE EXTENDED THE LIVES OF PATIENTS WITH EXTRACRANIAL SOLID TUMORS, LEADING TO A RISING INCIDENCE OF CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) METASTASES. METASTATIC BRAIN TUMORS AFFECT AN ESTIMATED 300,000 INDIVIDUALS ANNUALLY IN THE UNITED STATES. GIVEN THEIR PROFOUND IMPACT ON NEUROLOGICAL FUNCTION AND QUALITY OF LIFE, THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR SAFER AND MORE EFFECTIVE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES. ONCOLYTIC VIRUSES (OVS) OFFER UNIQUE ADVANTAGES IN OVERCOMING THESE CHALLENGES. BY SELECTIVELY LYSING TUMOR CELLS AND ACTIVATING BOTH INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES, OVS CAN CONVERT IMMUNOLOGICALLY “COLD” TUMORS INTO “HOT” ONES. OUR SUSTAINED HIGH-IMPACT RESEARCH ON ONCOLYTIC ADENOVIRUSES (OAS) LED TO PHASE I CLINICAL TRIALS DEMONSTRATING THAT DELTA-24-RGD IS SAFE AND CAN INDUCE DURABLE RESPONSES AND LONG-TERM SURVIVAL. BUILDING ON THIS SUCCESS, WE DEVELOPED DELTA-24-RGDOX, AN OA EXPRESSING THE IMMUNE CO-STIMULATORY MOLECULE OX40 LIGAND, WHICH ENHANCED BOTH LOCAL AND SYSTEMIC ANTITUMOR IMMUNITY IN PRECLINICAL MODELS. WHILE PRECLINICAL AND CLINICAL STUDIES SHOW THAT HOST IMMUNE RESPONSES CLEAR OVS WITHIN WEEKS, ANTITUMOR IMMUNITY OFTEN PERSISTS FOR MONTHS. THE MECHANISMS SUSTAINING THIS PROLONGED IMMUNE ACTIVITY REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. IN OUR STUDIES USING IMMUNOCOMPETENT MOUSE TUMOR MODELS AND CLINICAL SAMPLES, WE OBSERVED IMMUNE CELL AGGREGATES, SOME IDENTIFIED AS TERTIARY LYMPHOID STRUCTURES (TLS), WITHIN THE BRAINS OF OA-TREATED SUBJECTS. THE PRESENCE OF TLS CORRELATED WITH EXTENDED MEDIAN SURVIVAL. TLS HAS BEEN ASSOCIATED WITH IMPROVED RESPONSES TO IMMUNOTHERAPY ACROSS CANCER TYPES. UNLIKE SECONDARY LYMPHOID ORGANS, TLSS ARISE WITHIN THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT, MAINTAINING CONTINUOUS EXPOSURE TO TUMOR ANTIGENS AND INFLAMMATORY CUES. THIS POSITIONS THEM AS POTENT ON-SITE HUBS FOR TUMOR-SPECIFIC T CELL ACTIVATION, PARTICULARLY ADVANTAGEOUS WITHIN THE “IMMUNE-PRIVILEGED” CNS. WE ALSO OBSERVED TLSS ADJACENT TO TUMOR STROMAL CELLS EXHIBITING UPREGULATED PODOPLANIN (PDPN) EXPRESSION. WHILE PDPN+ CANCER-ASSOCIATED FIBROBLASTS REMODEL THE EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX TO PROMOTE TUMOR PROGRESSION, THEY CAN ALSO FACILITATE TLS FORMATION. BASED ON THESE FINDINGS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT OAS PROMOTE TLS FORMATION, IN PART THROUGH STROMAL REMODELING, TO SUSTAIN ANTITUMOR IMMUNITY IN BRAIN TUMORS. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE PROPOSE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1, DEFINE THE ROLE OF OA-INDUCED TLSS IN ANTITUMOR IMMUNITY IN BRAIN; AIM 2, INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF TUMOR STROMA REMODELING IN TLS FORMATION DURING OA THERAPY. THE STUDY REQUIRES IMMUNOCOMPETENT ORTHOTOPIC MOUSE MODELS BECAUSE OA-INDUCED TLS FORMATION DEPENDS ON COMPLEX INTERACTIONS BETWEEN THE TUMOR, IMMUNE SYSTEM, AND BRAIN MICROENVIRONMENT THAT CANNOT BE RECAPITULATED IN VITRO. IT WILL BE THE FIRST TO DEFINE THE ROLE OF TLSS IN OA THERAPY FOR BRAIN TUMORS. OUR FINDINGS WILL CLARIFY WHETHER TLSS ARE ESSENTIAL FOR EFFECTIVE OA THERAPY AND ESTABLISH A FOUNDATION FOR DEVELOPING NOVEL OA-BASED STRATEGIES THAT HARNESS TLS BIOLOGY TO IMPROVE THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY.

description: HARNESSING CUPROPTOSIS AGAINST CHEMORESISTANT OVARIAN CANCER - ABSTRACT HIGH-GRADE SEROUS OVARIAN CANCER (HGSOC) REMAINS THE DEADLIEST GYNECOLOGIC MALIGNANCY, WITH MOST PATIENTS RELAPSING AFTER INITIAL RESPONSE TO PLATINUM-BASED CHEMOTHERAPY. RECURRENT DISEASE IS ALMOST UNIFORMLY DRUG­RESISTANT, REFLECTING ADAPTIVE, NON-GENETIC MECHANISMS THAT ALLOW TUMOR CELLS TO SURVIVE AND REGROW FOLLOWING TREATMENT. IDENTIFYING AND TARGETING SUCH ADAPTIVE VULNERABILITIES IS A CRITICAL UNMET NEED. RECENT DISCOVERIES FROM OUR LABORATORY HAVE REVEALED A NOVEL FORM OF REGULATED CELL DEATH WE TEREMED CUPROPTOSIS, WHICH IS TRIGGERED BY COPPER OVERLOAD IN MITOCHONDRIA. CUPROPTOSIS SELECTIVELY KILLS CELLS IN A PROCESS REGUALTED BY FDX1 AND RESULTING IN COPPER TARGETING LIPOYLATED AND FE-S CLUSTER PROTEINS, LEADING TO CATASTROPHIC PROTEOTOXIC STRESS. PRELIMINARY DATA FROM OUR PATIENT-DERIVED XENOGRAFT (PDX) MODELS SHOW THAT HGSOC CELLS EXHIBIT ENHANCED SENSITIVITY TO CUPROPTOSIS, PARTICULARLY WHEN CULTURED IN ASCITES-DERIVED MEDIA THAT MIMIC THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT. NOTABLY, THE COPPER IONOPHORE ELESCLOMOL (ES), PREVIOUSLY TESTED IN CANCER CLINICAL TRIALS WITHOUT MECHANISTIC GUIDANCE, EMERGES AS A POTENT CUPROPTOSIS INDUCER IN FDX1 + HGSOC MODELS. WE HAVE FURTHER DEVELOPED A NEW ANALOG, ESCU002, WITH IMPROVED SOLUBILITY, PHARMACOKINETICS, AND IN VIVO EFFICACY. ANIMAL MODELS ARE REQUIRED BECAUSE DRUG EXPOSURE, COPPER DELIVERY, TUMOR GROWTH, ASCITES-ASSOCIATED MICROENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS, AND PLATINUM RESPONSE CANNOT BE FULLY MODELED IN VITRO. ORTHOTOPIC HGSOC PDX MODELS ALLOW US TO TEST PHARMACOKINETICS, PHARMACODYNAMIC TARGET ENGAGEMENT, AND ANTITUMOR EFFICACY IN A CLINICALLY RELEVANT AND PHYSIOLOGICAL SETTINGS.  THIS R21 PROPOSAL TESTS THE HYPOTHESIS THAT FDX1 + HGSOC CELLS ARE INTRINSICALLY SENSITIVE TO CUPROPTOSIS AND THAT INDUCING THIS PATHWAY CAN SUPPRESS TUMOR PROGRESSION AND PREVENT THE EMERGENCE OF PLATINUM RESISTANCE. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS IN THE FOLLOWING TWO AIMS:  AIM 1 WILL DEFINE THE MOLECULAR AND PHARMACODYNAMIC FEATURES OF CUPROPTOSIS IN HGSOC PDX MODELS, ESTABLISHING THE INTRACELLULAR COPPER THRESHOLD REQUIRED FOR CELL KILLING, MAPPING THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL RESPONSE, AND VALIDATING BIOMARKERS OF TARGET ENGAGEMENT IN VIVO.  AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE THE EFFICACY OF ELESCLOMOL AND ESCU002 AS SINGLE AGENTS AND IN COMBINATION WITH PLATINUM IN ORTHOTOPIC PDX MODELS, INCLUDING PHARMACOKINETIC ASSESSMENT TO CORRELATE DRUG EXPOSURE WITH ANTITUMOR EFFECTS AND BIOMARKER RESPONSES.  TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL DETERMINE WHETHER INDUCING CUPROPTOSIS IS A FEASIBLE AND EFFECTIVE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY FOR DRUG-RESISTANT OVARIAN CANCER. BY LEVERAGING IMPROVED COPPER IONOPHORES SUCH AS ESCU002, THIS WORK WILL LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR TRANSLATING COPPER-DEPENDENT CELL DEATH INTO A NOVEL TREATMENT APPROACH FOR HIGH­GRADE SEROUS OVARIAN CANCER.

description: MODELING SEPTINS' ROLES IN CANCER CELL BIOLOGY IN A SIMPLE ANIMAL - MODELING SEPTINS’ ROLES IN CANCER CELL BIOLOGY IN A SIMPLE ANIMAL ABSTRACT CANCER IS A CONSTELLATION OF PATHOLOGIES CHARACTERIZED BY RE-ACQUISITION OF CELLULAR BEHAVIORS NORMALLY ONLY EXHIBITED DURING DEVELOPMENT. IN CANCER, CELL PROLIFERATION IS MIS-REGULATED AND ERROR PRONE, AND TISSUE INTEGRITY IS COMPROMISED DUE TO DYSFUNCTIONS OF CELLULAR IDENTITY, POLARITY, ADHESION, AND MOVEMENT. THE BIOCHEMICAL IMBALANCES THAT LEAD TO THESE CANCER CELL BIOLOGY BEHAVIORS RESULT FROM CHANGES IN EXPRESSION LEVEL, AND MUTATION, OF GENES THAT ARE ESSENTIAL FOR FUNDAMENTAL DEVELOPMENTAL EVENTS. SEPTINS ARE SMALL GTP-BINDING PROTEINS THAT FORM NON-POLAR OLIGOMERIC SUBUNITS AND NON-POLAR FILAMENTS THAT, IN TURN, ASSEMBLE INTO BUNDLES AND SHEETS. SEPTINS SCAFFOLD SIGNALING PATHWAYS AND OTHER CYTOSKELETAL POLYMERS (ACTIN AND MICROTUBULES). SEPTINS’ ROLES IN CELL DIVISION, ADHESION, AND MOVEMENT, AND OTHER CANCER-RELATED CELLULAR PROCESSES IMPLICATE THEM IN CANCEROUS TRANSFORMATION AND PROGRESSION. IMPORTANTLY, SEPTIN EXPRESSION IS ABNORMAL IN, AND SERVES AS A BIOMARKER FOR, SEVERAL KINDS OF CANCER. FURTHERMORE, SEPTIN GENES HAVE HOTSPOT MUTATIONS IN A WIDE VARIETY OF CANCERS. IT IS UNKNOWN WHAT OF SEPTINS’ MANY CELLULAR FUNCTIONS ARE MOST IMPORTANT FOR PROTECTING CELLS AND TISSUES FROM CANCEROUS TRANSFORMATION. OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE CANCER CELL BIOLOGY OF SEPTINS IS ALSO CONFOUNDED BY 1) THE LARGE NUMBER OF SEPTIN GENES, EACH OF WHICH HAS MANY SPLICE FORMS, IN MAMMALIAN GENOMES, 2) THE REDUNDANCY OF DIFFERENT SEPTINS FOR EACH OTHER’S CELLULAR ROLES, AND 3) THE LOGISTICAL CHALLENGES OF IN VIVO CANCER BIOLOGY. WE WILL DEFINE THE FUNDAMENTAL CANCER CELL BIOLOGY ROLES OF SEPTINS USING A MODEL ANIMAL WITH A SIMPLIFIED SEPTIN GENE COLLECTION AND A SIMPLE BODY PLAN AND WELL CHARACTERIZED DEVELOPMENT. THE NEMATODE C. ELEGANS HAS AFFORDED MYRIAD DISCOVERIES OF ESSENTIAL, CONSERVED CANCER BIOLOGY, INCLUDING MECHANISMS OF CELL DIVISION, SIGNALING CONTROL OF CELL FATE. C. ELEGANS HAS ONLY TWO SEPTINS, WHICH ARE INTERDEPENDENT; REMOVING FUNCTION OF ONE BLOCKS THE OTHER’S STABILITY AND/OR LOCALIZATION. PRELIMINARY RESULTS THAT SET THE STAGE FOR THE PROPOSED WORK INCLUDE PROTEOMICS, HIGH-CONTENT SCREENING, AND BIOINFORMATICS, TO GENERATE A LIST OF CANDIDATE SEPTIN INTERACTORS THAT MEDIATE SEPTINS’ ROLES IN CANCER. THE EXCEPTIONALLY WELL-CHARACTERIZED DEVELOPMENT AND PHYSIOLOGY OF C. ELEGANS WILL FACILITATE SYSTEMATIC, RAPID, AND INEXPENSIVE ASSAY OF CANCER BIOLOGY: CELL FATE DETERMINATION, STEM CELL PROLIFERATION, CELL MIGRATION PATHFINDING, CELL CYCLE EXIT, DIFFERENTIATION, BASEMENT MEMBRANE INVASION. AFTER FIRST SCREENING FOR SEPTIN INTERACTORS’ ROLES IN THESE EVENTS, WE WILL TEST WHETHER THEY SUPPRESS OR ENHANCE SEPTIN PHENOTYPES, AND AFFECT SEPTIN PROTEIN STABILITY AND LOCALIZATION. IN PARALLEL WORK, WE WILL USE CRISPR/CAS9-BASED GENOME EDITING TO CREATE “AVATAR” ANIMALS THAT BEAR CANCER HOTSPOT MUTATIONS IN CONSERVED SEPTIN AMINO ACIDS THAT ARE EXPECTED TO AFFECT SEPTIN SUBUNIT ASSEMBLY. WE WILL TEST WHETHER DISEASE ALLELES AFFECT SEPTIN PROTEIN STABILITY AND POLYMERIZATION, OR ARE SUFFICIENT TO DRIVE OR ENHANCE CANCER CELL BEHAVIORS IN WELL CHARACTERIZED C. ELEGANS IN VIVO CANCER MODELS. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL UNCOVER THE CELLULAR BASES FOR SEPTINS’ INVOLVEMENT IN CANCEROUS CELLULAR BEHAVIORS AND INFORM DEVELOPMENT OF CANCER DIAGNOSTICS AND TREATMENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEFINING THE PARP14 INTERACTOME IN RIG-I ACTIVATED COLORECTAL CANCERS. - ABSTRACT OUR LAB HAS BEEN INTERESTED IN DRAWING LESSONS FROM VIRAL INFECTIONS OR AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES TO ACTIVATE THE IMMUNE SYSTEM AGAINST CANCER. TYPICALLY, CELLS RECOGNIZE VIRAL RNA OR DNA AND RAISE ALARMS THAT TRIGGER IMMUNE RESPONSES TO ELIMINATE THE INFECTED CELLS. RECENTLY, WE HAVE DISCOVERED THAT A CELLULAR RNA SENSOR IS EVEN BETTER AT ACTIVATING IMMUNE RESPONSES IN TUMORS. THIS SENSOR, CALLED RIG-I IS TRIGGERED BY VIRAL RNA MOLECULES OR SYNTHETIC NUCLEIC ACIDS DERIVED FROM VIRUSES. WE USE A SMALL PIECE OF RNA FROM THE POTENT H1N1 STRAIN OF INFLUENZA (THIS IS ~80 BASE PAIRS, CANNOT BE MADE INTO PROTEINS AND THEREFORE, SAFE) TO ACTIVATE RIG-I. WE FOUND THAT MOUSE COLORECTAL AND MAMMARY CARCINOMA CELLS SECRETE SEVERAL IMMUNE ACTIVATING PROTEINS IN RESPONSE TO RIG-I. IN PRELIMINARY EXPERIMENTS, THIS MOLECULE WAS ABLE TO SLOW DOWN THE GROWTH OF THESE CANCER CELL LINES IN MICE. SIMILARLY, WE ANALYZED PUBLIC DATASETS AND FOUND THAT MANY OF OUR GENE SIGNATURES WERE ALSO OBSERVED IN CANCER PATIENTS WITH HIGHER LEVELS OF RIG-I. AMONG OTHER GENES OF THERAPEUTIC INTEREST, WE FOUND SEVERAL PARP GENES ARE HIGHLY UPREGULATED IN PATIENTS WHO HAVE HIGHER AMOUNTS OF RIG-I. PARPS ARE IMPORTANT PROTEINS THAT FUNCTION IN DNA REPAIR BUT ALSO HAVE OTHER FUNCTIONS INCLUDING DECREASING IMMUNE RECOGNITION OF CANCERS. DRUGS THAT INHIBIT PARP1 AND 2 ARE APPROVED IN BREAST AND OVARIAN CANCER HAVE BECOME PART OF SPECIFIC TREATMENT REGIMENS. OUR RIG-I ASSOCIATED PARPS ARE RARER PARPS WHICH ARE STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION FOR THEIR ROLES IN CANCER. OUR PILOT STUDIES SHOW THAT PARP14 ACTS AS A BRAKE ON RIG-I INDUCED CELL DEATH AND DECREASES TUMOR GROWTH IN MULTIPLE MOUSE MODELS. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE HAVE PARTNERED WITH A COLLEAGUE DR. MICHAEL COHEN WHO IS A LEADING EXPERT ON PARPS. TOGETHER, WE WILL EXPLORE PARP14 FUNCTIONS IN THE CONTEXT OF RIG-I ACTIVATED COLORECTAL CANCERS USING SOPHISTICATED CHEMICAL BIOLOGY APPROACHES TO IDENTIFY THE DIRECT TARGETS OF PARP14. IF SUCCESSFUL, OUR WORK WILL CONTRIBUTE NEW UNDERSTANDING OF HOW PARP14 SIGNALING LIKELY PUMPS THE BRAKES ON RIG-I PATHWAY AND IDENTIFY POTENTIAL TARGETS FOR THERAPIES THAT CAN REMOVE THE BRAKES AND RESTORE TUMOR CELL DEATH AND ATTRACT IMMUNE ATTENTION TO CANCERS.

description: ROLE OF T-CELL-INTRINSIC NRF2 AND ITS TARGETABILITY IN MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER - SUMMARY MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER (MIBC) IS AN AGGRESSIVE SUBTYPE OF BLADDER CANCER WITH LIMITED THERAPEUTIC OPTIONS. DESPITE ADVANCES IN SURGICAL MANAGEMENT AND CHEMOTHERAPY, MIBC REMAINS ASSOCIATED WITH POOR SURVIVAL OUTCOMES. IMPORTANTLY, MIBCS ARE CHARACTERIZED BY A HIGH TUMOR MUTATIONAL BURDEN AND ROBUST T-CELL INFILTRATION INTO THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT (TME), BUT THESE T CELLS OFTEN EXHIBIT IMPAIRED CYTOTOXICITY AND PROFOUND EXHAUSTION. IMMUNE CHECKPOINT INHIBITORS, THOUGH TRANSFORMATIVE IN SOME CANCERS, PROVIDES DURABLE RESPONSES IN ONLY ~20% OF MIBC PATIENTS. THUS, THERE REMAINS A CRITICAL UNMET NEED TO UNDERSTAND THE MECHANISMS OF IMMUNE RESISTANCE WITHIN THE MIBC TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT AND TO DEVELOP THERAPIES THAT CAN RESTORE AND ENHANCE T-CELL FUNCTION TO IMPROVE PATIENT OUTCOMES. NUCLEAR FACTOR ERYTHROID 2–RELATED FACTOR 2 (NRF2) IS A TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR BEST KNOWN FOR ITS ANTIOXIDANT FUNCTIONS AND PRO-TUMORIGENIC ROLE. RECENT NEW DATA FROM OTHERS AND OUR LAB SHOW THAT, (1) NRF2 PATHWAY IS HIGHLY UPREGULATED IN TUMOR-INFILTRATING T CELLS COMPARED TO CIRCULATING T CELLS IN MIBC PATIENTS, (2) NRF2-DEPLETED CD8⁺ T CELLS DISPLAY ENHANCED CYTOTOXICITY, INCREASED IFN-G AND GRANZYME B PRODUCTION, AND GREATER INFILTRATION INTO MIBC TUMORS, (3) T CELL-SPECIFIC DELETION OF NRF2 MARKEDLY SUPPRESSES TUMOR GROWTH IN MOUSE MODELS OF MIBC, AND (4) NRF2 MODULATES T CELL METABOLISM TO ALTER EFFECTOR FUNCTIONS. TOGETHER, THESE FINDINGS IDENTIFY A PREVIOUSLY UNRECOGNIZED IMMUNESUPPRESSIVE ROLE FOR NRF2 WITHIN MIBC-INFILTRATING T CELLS AND HIGHLIGHT IT AS A TARGET TO POTENTIATE ANTITUMOR IMMUNE RESPONSES IN BLADDER CANCER. THIS R21 PROPOSAL WILL DEFINE THE IMMUNE, TRANSCRIPTIONAL, AND CLONAL CONSEQUENCES OF NRF2 INHIBITION IN T CELLS IN MOUSE MODELS OF MIBC AND ESTABLISH THE CLINICAL RELEVANCE OF T CELL–INTRINSIC NRF2 EXPRESSION IN HUMAN MIBC USING PATIENT-DERIVED TUMOR-INFILTRATING T CELLS (AIM 1). TO THERAPEUTICALLY EXPLOIT NRF2 PATHWAY IN MIBC, WE HAVE DEVELOPED AN ADVANCED AND FIRST-IN-CLASS T CELL– TARGETED NANOSPONGE PLATFORM THAT SELECTIVELY DELIVERS NRF2 INHIBITORS TO T CELLS, MINIMIZING SYSTEMIC TOXICITY AND ENABLING PRECISE IMMUNE MODULATION. THE EFFICACY OF THESE T CELL–DIRECTED NRF2-INHIBITING NANOSPONGES IN SUPPRESSING MIBC TUMOR GROWTH WILL BE EVALUATED IN PRECLINICAL MODELS (AIM 2). THESE STUDIES WILL FILL A MAJOR KNOWLEDGE GAP IN REDOX-IMMUNOMETABOLIC REGULATION OF T CELLS, UNCOVERING A KEY MECHANISM OF IMMUNE DYSFUNCTION IN BLADDER CANCER. FURTHER, IT WILL ESTABLISH T CELL–INTRINSIC NRF2 AS A TRACTABLE AND TARGETABLE IMMUNE CHECKPOINT IN BLADDER CANCER AND DELIVER A FIRST-IN-CLASS NANOTHERAPEUTIC PLATFORM FOR ITS SELECTIVE INHIBITION IN T CELLS. PARALLEL TO ANALYSES OF PATIENT-DERIVED SAMPLES, THIS PROJECT WILL EMPLOY BOTH SYNGENEIC AND CARCINOGENINDUCED MOUSE MODELS OF BLADDER CANCER TO EVALUATE THE EFFECTS OF T CELL-SPECIFIC NRF2 INHIBITION ON ANTITUMOR IMMUNITY AND THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY IN THE CONTEXT OF AN INTACT IMMUNE SYSTEM. ANIMAL MODELS ARE ESSENTIAL BECAUSE THE COMPLEX INTERACTIONS AMONG T CELLS, TUMOR CELLS, AND THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT, AS WELL AS RESPONSES TO IMMUNOTHERAPY, CANNOT BE ADEQUATELY REPLICATED USING IN VITRO SYSTEMS ALONE. THESE MODELS CLOSELY RECAPITULATE KEY IMMUNOLOGICAL AND PATHOLOGICAL FEATURES OF HUMAN MIBC AND ARE THEREFORE EXCELLENT TOOLS TO ASSESS THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL OF NRF2-TARGETED THERAPIES.

description: THC EXPOSURE AND INHIBITORY CIRCUIT PLASTICITY IN THE NEOCORTEX - ABSTRACT ___________ CANNABIS IS A WIDELY-USED DRUG THAT HAS DIVERSE COGNITIVE EFFECTS AND AT FINE SCALE CAN REGULATE PRESYNAPTIC RELEASE PROPERTIES. LONGER-LASTING EFFECTS OF PROLONGED RECEPTOR ACTIVATION, AS WOULD OCCUR IN CANNABIS USE DISORDERS, ARE NOT WELL-UNDERSTOOD. OF PARTICULAR INTEREST ARE THE EFFECTS OF ∆9-TETRAHYDROCANNABINOL (THC) – THE MAIN PSYCHOACTIVE COMPONENT OF CANNABIS – IN INFLUENCING THE ACTIVITY OF TWO MAJOR SUBTYPES OF NEOCORTICAL INTERNEURONS THAT EXPRESS THE HIGHEST LEVELS OF CANNABINOID RECEPTORS IN THE MAMMALIAN BRAIN. HERE WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THC ADMINISTRATION HAS BOTH ACUTE AND LONG-TERM EFFECTS ON THE ACTIVITY AND SYNAPTIC PROPERTIES OF THESE TWO CRITICAL POPULATIONS OF NEOCORTICAL INTERNEURONS. IN VIVO CA++ IMAGING OF VIP AND SST NEURONS FROM THC-EXPOSED ANIMALS WILL BE USED TO EVALUATE SYSTEMS-LEVEL ALTERATIONS IN INTERNEURON FUNCTION DURING SENSATION AND BEHAVIOR. IN ADDITION, HIGH-RESOLUTION FLUORESCENCE-BASED ANALYSIS OF EXCITATORY AND INHIBITORY SYNAPSES WILL BE CARRIED OUT TO QUANTITATE THC-RELATED CHANGES IN SYNAPSES ON NEOCORTICAL INTERNEURONS THAT ARE CHARACTERIZED BY VASOACTIVE INTESTINAL PEPTIDE (VIP) AND SOMATOSTATIN (SST) EXPRESSION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A MIXED METHODS EXAMINATION OF ADOLESCENT OVERDOSE AND RETURN TO HIGH-RISK DRUG USE AFTER TREATMENT - PROJECT SUMMARY-ABSTRACT THIS PROPOSAL LEVERAGES AN EXISTING ADOLESCENT DATA SET AND HIGH-RISK SAMPLE TO ANSWER A CRITICAL GAP IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF PATHWAYS TO RECOVERY AND REDUCING THE INCIDENCE OF YOUTH OVERDOSE AND DEATH. THE PERIOD FOLLOWING INPATIENT TREATMENT DISCHARGE IS A CRITICAL ONE FOR ADOLESCENTS BECAUSE A MAJORITY ARE LIKELY TO RETURN TO SUBSTANCE USE, THEY UNDERESTIMATE THEIR RISK FOR OVERDOSE, AND THEIR ACQUIRED TOLERANCE FOLLOWING TREATMENT IS MUCH LOWER THAN THEY EXPECT. ANY RETURN TO DRUG USE POSES A GRAVE DANGER, ESPECIALLY HEIGHTENED IN THE CURRENT DRUG SUPPLY CLIMATE WITH FENTANYL-LACED SUBSTANCES. ALTHOUGH THE PRECURSORS FOR A RETURN TO USING SUBSTANCES HAVE BEEN EXAMINED AMONG ALL AGES, THERE IS A CRITICAL LACK OF LONGITUDINAL INVESTIGATION OF HOW THESE FACTORS TOGETHER INFLUENCE RETURN TO DRUG USE AND INCREASE RISK FOR OVERDOSE AMONG ADOLESCENTS. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, THIS STUDY WILL CONDUCT BOTH SECONDARY DATA ANALYSIS AND NEW QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS AND FOCUS ON THE INTERSECTION OF HIGH OVERDOSE RISK AND OVERDOSE OUTCOMES BY INVESTIGATING SEVERAL KEY PREDICTORS: RECOVERY CAPITAL, SOCIAL INFLUENCE, CRIMINAL JUSTICE INVOLVEMENT, MENTAL HEALTH COMORBIDITIES, SEX, AND AGE. THE PROPOSAL CAPITALIZES ON EXISTING DATA FROM A MIXED METHOD, LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF ADOLESCENTS (AGES 12-19) WHO ENTERED INPATIENT ADDICTION TREATMENT AND ARE FOLLOWED FOR 12 MONTHS AFTER TREATMENT DISCHARGE. OF THIS SAMPLE, 52% REPORTED DIFFERENT FORMS OF HIGH-RISK DRUG USE AT BASELINE, INCLUDING A HIGH PROPORTION OF FENTANYL USE, AND THERE WAS A HIGH HISTORY OF COMORBID MENTAL HEALTH CONCERNS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL USE MULTIVARIATE LOGISTIC REGRESSION AND BAYESIAN REGRESSION TO DEVELOP PREDICTIVE MODELS OF (1) HIGH RISK FOR DRUG OVERDOSE (I.E., RETURN TO HIGH-RISK DRUG USE AND RETURN TO ANY DRUG USE) AND (2) OVERDOSE EXPERIENCE AMONG APPROXIMATELY 175 ADOLESCENTS FOR 1-YEAR FOLLOWING AN INDEX INPATIENT ADDICTION TREATMENT SESSION. IN AIM 2, WE WILL EXAMINE THE EXPERIENCES OF 30 ADOLESCENTS WHO HAVE HAD A NONFATAL OVERDOSE, AS IDENTIFIED FROM THE AIM 1 SAMPLE. WE WILL CONDUCT THIS NEW FOLLOW-UP QUALITATIVE STUDY WITH THESE ADOLESCENTS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THEIR EXPERIENCES AND HOW THIS CRITICAL PERIOD FOR OVERDOSE COULD BE BETTER ADDRESSED BY OUR CLINICAL TREATMENT AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SYSTEMS. OUR QUESTIONS WITH THESE ADOLESCENTS WHO HAVE EXPERIENCED AN OVERDOSE WILL ELICIT RESPONSES AROUND POTENTIAL PATTERNS IN RETURN TO USE AND OVERDOSE AND DRAW OUT INFORMATION ON INTENTIONAL VERSUS UNINTENTIONAL OVERDOSE EXPERIENCES AND MENTAL HEALTH COMORBIDITIES. THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS SIGNIFICANT IN THAT IT WILL FILL A CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAP IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF ADOLESCENT RELAPSE AND OVERDOSE DURING A HIGH-RISK POINT FOR FATALITY IN A SAMPLE OF INPATIENT YOUTH FOLLOWED FOR 1 YEAR AFTER TREATMENT. THE NOVEL CONCEPTS EMERGING FROM THIS APPLICATION WILL BE USED TO SUPPORT FUTURE RESEARCH IN LINE WITH NIDA’S PRIORITIES TO IDENTIFY TARGETED INTERVENTION OPPORTUNITIES FOR YOUNG PEOPLE.

description: ROLE OF IMMUNE CELL TRAFFICKING THROUGH COCHLEAR BLOOD VESSELS AND NEWLY DISCOVERED COCHLEAR LYMPHATICS IN THE FOREIGN BODY RESPONSE FOLLOWING COCHLEAR IMPLANTATION - PROJECT SUMMARY THE POST-CI INFLAMMATORY FOREIGN BODY RESPONSE (FBR) HAS BEEN LINKED WITH POORER PERFORMANCE OF CI AND LOSS OF RESIDUAL ACOUSTIC HEARING. A SIGNIFICANT BODY OF RECENT WORK HAS BEEN DEVOTED TO PROBING THE ROLE OF MACROPHAGES IN FBR POST-CI. HOWEVER, THE ROLE OF NON-MACROPHAGE IMMUNE CELLS, INCLUDING T CELLS, HAS NOT BEEN THOROUGHLY SCRUTINIZED. FURTHER, IMMUNE CELLS INFILTRATE ORGANS VIA BLOOD VESSELS AND RETURN TO THE BLOOD CIRCULATION VIA LYMPHATIC VESSELS, WHICH PLAY A CENTRAL ROLE IN INTERACTIONS AMONG MACROPHAGES AND T LYMPHOCYTES. THIS TWO-WAY TRAFFICKING OF IMMUNE CELLS HAS NOT BEEN WELL-DESCRIBED IN THE COCHLEA. MY CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT AN INTERPLAY BETWEEN IMMUNE CELL TRAFFICKING VIA THE COCHLEAR LYMPHATIC SYSTEM, IMMUNE CELL INFILTRATION FROM COCHLEAR BLOOD VESSELS, AND PATHOLOGIC T LYMPHOCYTES CONTRIBUTES TO FBR POST-CI. THIS HYPOTHESIS IS SUPPORTED BY OBSERVATION OF T LYMPHOCYTES IN IMPLANTED HUMAN COCHLEAE. IN THE MURINE MODEL OF COCHLEAR IMPLANTATION, I OBSERVED 1) T LYMPHOCYTE INFILTRATION, 2) PROLIFERATION OF LYMPHATIC VESSELS TRAFFICKING IMMUNE CELLS, 3) NEO-ANGIOGENESIS, AND 4) BLOOD-DERIVED IMMUNE CELL INFILTRATION. THE COMPOSITE OF THESE NEW DATA SUPPORTS THE NOTION THAT AN INTRICATE ‘IMMUNE SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM’ INVOLVING APCS, LYMPHATICS, T CELLS, AND BLOOD VESSELS CONTRIBUTES TO INFLAMMATORY FBR POST-CI. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO INVESTIGATE THE FUNDAMENTAL BASIS OF COCHLEAR IMMUNE RESPONSES TO DAMAGE. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS STUDY IS TO DETERMINE THE ROLE OF IMMUNE CELL TRAFFICKING VIA COCHLEAR BLOOD VESSELS AND NEWLY DISCOVERED LYMPHATIC VESSELS IN THE INFLAMMATORY FBR POST-CI. THESE PRIORITY QUESTIONS WILL BE ADDRESSED WITH THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1: TO DETERMINE THE ROLE OF IMMUNE CELL TRAFFICKING VIA COCHLEAR LYMPHATICS IN THE FBR POST-CI. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT IMMUNE CELL TRAFFICKING VIA THE COCHLEAR LYMPHATIC SYSTEM CONTRIBUTES TO FBR POST-CI. I EXPECT THAT THE FOLLOWING INTERVENTIONS WILL REDUCE FBR POST-CI: 1) INHIBITION OF POST-CI LYMPHANGIOGENESIS IN CONDITIONAL KNOCKOUT OF THE VEGFR3 GENE, A MOLECULE NECESSARY FOR LYMPHANGIOGENESIS. 2) GENETIC DISRUPTION OF IMMUNE CELL TRAFFICKING VIA LYMPHATICS IN CCR7 KNOCKOUT MICE. AIM 2: TO DETERMINE THE ROLE OF BLOOD-DERIVED IMMUNE CELLS, INCLUDING T LYMPHOCYTES, IN FBR POST-CI. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT A) BLOOD-DERIVED IMMUNE CELLS IN GENERAL, AND B) T CELLS SPECIFICALLY, CONTRIBUTE TO FBR POST-CI. I EXPECT THAT THE FOLLOWING INTERVENTIONS WILL REDUCE FBR POST-CI: 1) IMPLANTED MICE TREATED WITH A NEO- ANGIOGENESIS INHIBITOR, AN ANTI-VEGFA RECOMBINANT ANTIBODY; 2) IMPLANTATION IN CCR2 AND CX3CR1 KO MICE THAT ARE DEFICIENT IN IMMUNE CELL EXTRAVASATION FROM BLOOD VESSELS. 3) IMPLANTATION OF T CELL-DEFICIENT MICE. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE A NEW MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE IMMUNE RESPONSE FOLLOWING CI, DIRECTLY IMPACTING FUTURE CI INTERVENTIONS AND REVEALING FUNDAMENTAL MECHANISMS OF COCHLEAR INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ULTRASOUND CONTROLLED IN-SITU ANTIMICROBIAL DELIVERY SYSTEM - PROJECT SUMMARY THIS RESEARCH EXPLORES A NEW AND INNOVATIVE CLASS OF ULTRASOUND RESPONSIVE BIODEGRADABLE POLYMERS FOR DEVELOPMENT OF ON DEMAND, ULTRASOUND CONTROLLED, IN SITU ANTIBIOTIC RELEASE. DEVICE-RELATED INFECTION IS ONE OF THE MAJOR AND MOST CHALLENGING OBSTACLES IN ORTHOPEDIC AND PLASTIC SURGERY. EXISTING STRATEGIES, SUCH AS SURFACE MODIFICATIONS OR THE CONJUGATION OF ACTIVE BIOCIDES, HAVE YET TO DEMONSTRATE LONG-TERM EFFECTIVENESS FOR IMPLANTED DEVICES. ADDITIONALLY, SURGICAL COMPLICATIONS OCCUR FREQUENTLY IN INFECTED DEVICE REMOVAL, RESULTING COSTLY CARE AND POTENTIAL LONG-TERM IMPAIRMENT FOR PATIENTS. TO ADDRESS THIS CHALLENGE, WE PROPOSE AN ULTRASOUND RESPONSIVE BIOCOMPATIBLE POLYCAPROLACTONE (PCL) BASED COATING FOR INDWELLING DEVICES, WHERE IN SITU ANTIBIOTIC RELEASE IS TRIGGERED USING IMAGE GUIDED, NON-INVASIVE FOCUSED ULTRASOUND (FUS). THE KEY INNOVATION IS A LABILE POLYMER CROSSLINKING STRATEGY USING ULTRASOUND SENSITIVE DIELS-ALDER (DA) GROUPS TO REVERSIBLY LINK THE POLYMERS. THESE DA LINKERS ARE ENGINEERED TO REMAIN STABLE UNDER PHYSIOLOGICAL CONDITIONS BUT UNDERGO EFFICIENT RETRO-DA REACTIONS WHEN EXPOSED TO FOCUSED ULTRASOUND (FUS) AT SPECIFIC ENERGY LEVELS. THE RETRO REACTION OF THE DA BOND REVERTS TO THE DA STARTING MATERIALS, BREAKING THE POLYMER CROSSLINKS AND INITIATING DEPOLYMERIZATION, WHICH RESULTS IN THE RELEASE OF ENTRAPPED ANTIBIOTICS AND CAN RESTRUCTURE THE COATING SURFACE. FOCUSED ULTRASOUND STIMULATION ALLOWS FOR PRECISE SPATIOTEMPORAL CONTROL OF ACTIVATION AND REPEATED ULTRASOUND STIMULATION ALLOWS FOR SUSTAINED DELIVERY WHEN THERE IS AN IMPLANT ASSOCIATED INFECTION. THE DEFINED KINETICS OF RETRO DA CLEAVAGE REACTION IS THE KEY ENABLING FEATURE, ALLOWING THE DA-PCL COATING TO REMAIN STABLE IN PHYSIOLOGICAL CONDITIONS, BUT UNDERGO A RETRO REACTION TO RESTRUCTURE AND RELEASE DRUGS WITH THE APPLICATION OF ULTRASOUND ENERGY IN REGIMES THAT DO NOT DAMAGE TISSUE. THERE ARE THREE HYPOTHESES ADDRESSED IN THIS PROPOSAL; 1) THE RETRO DA REACTION KINETICS WILL CORRELATE WITH DEGRADATION RATES OF THE POLYMER COATING WHEN STIMULATED BY FUS BOTH IN VITRO AND IN VIVO, 2) DEGRADATION PRODUCTS WILL BE BIOCOMPATIBLE, AND 3) ANTIBIOTIC RELEASE WILL CORRELATE WITH DA REACTION BARRIERS. THE HYPOTHESES ARE TESTED IN TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1. DETERMINE THE INFLUENCE OF DA CROSS-LINK COMPOSITION ON THE FUS RESPONSE OF PCL POLYMERS, MECHANICAL PROPERTIES, CYTOTOXICITY, AND THE ASSOCIATED ANTIBIOTIC RELEASE KINETICS. AIM 2. DETERMINE THE LONG-TERM IN VIVO DEGRADATION PROFILE AND ANTIBIOTIC ACTIVITY IN AN IN VIVO BIOMATERIAL ASSOCIATED INFECTION MODEL. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO DEVELOP A NEW AND INNOVATIVE ON DEMAND DRUG ELUTING COATING SYSTEM FOR IMPLANTABLE MEDICAL DEVICES. FOCUSED ULTRASOUND OFFERS A MINIMALLY INVASIVE, IMAGE-GUIDED APPROACH TO DELIVER ANTIBIOTICS AND DEGRADE DEVICE COATINGS IN SITU WITH PRECISE SPATIOTEMPORAL CONTROL. THIS TECHNOLOGY REPRESENTS A PARADIGM SHIFT COMPARED TO CURRENT ORTHOPEDIC IMPLANTS WHICH ARE FREQUENTLY COLONIZED WITH DIFFICULT TO TREAT INFECTIONS, OFTEN REQUIRE REVISION SURGERY WITH HIGH RATES OF COMPLICATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TOWARD CNS CORRELATES OF AUTONOMIC DYSFUNCTION IN PAINFUL TMD - ABSTRACT THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DETERMINE HOW ALTERED BRAINSTEM CIRCUIT ACTIVITY AND ALTERED GLYMPHATIC FLOW RELATE TO AUTONOMIC DYSFUNCTION IN PATIENTS WITH PAINFUL TEMPOROMANDIBULAR DISORDERS (TMD), A PREVALENT FORM OF CHRONIC CRANIOFACIAL PAIN. WHILE CHRONIC TMD PAIN AFFECTS UP TO 12% OF US ADULTS, CURRENT CLINICAL TREATMENT SELECTION REMAINS TRIAL-AND-ERROR WITH MODEST EFFICACY. TREATMENT SELECTION COULD BE IMPROVED BY EVALUATION OF BOTH AUTONOMIC- AND CENTRAL- NERVOUS SYSTEMS, YET THE INTERACTIVE CONTRIBUTIONS OF AUTONOMIC/CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEMS TO TMD, AND TO CHRONIC PAIN MORE GENERALLY, ARE LARGELY UNKNOWN. TO CLARIFY AUTONOMIC/CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM CONTRIBUTIONS TO PAINFUL TMD, WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW ALTERATIONS IN BOTH BRAINSTEM CIRCUITS AND BRAIN GLYMPHATIC FLOW INTERACT WITH AUTONOMIC DYSFUNCTION AND CLINICAL SYMPTOMS. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE WILL MEASURE (1) BRAIN GLYMPHATIC FLOW, (2) BRAINSTEM CIRCUIT FMRI-INDICATED ACTIVITY, AND (3) AUTONOMIC FUNCTION, USING HEART-RATE VARIABILITY AND BARORECEPTOR SENSITIVITY METHODS, IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC PAIN (IE, TMD) VS PAIN-FREE CONTROLS. WE WILL EVALUATE BOTH AUTONOMIC AND FMRI-BASED FUNCTION TO ADVANCE TOWARD OUR LONGER-TERM GOAL OF CHARACTERIZING SENSORY-AUTONOMIC FACTORS RELATED TO TMD TREATMENT/PROGNOSIS. IN THIS PROPOSAL, OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT BRAINSTEM CIRCUIT DISRUPTION AND ALTERED GLYMPHATIC FLOW RELATE TO AUTONOMIC DYSFUNCTION, WHICH IN TURN RELATE TO SYMPTOMS OF PAIN. IN AIM 1 WE WILL CHARACTERIZE HOW ALTERED BRAINSTEM CIRCUITS RELATE TO AUTONOMIC DYSFUNCTION AND CHRONIC PAIN. AMONG NORMOTENSIVE PATIENTS WITH TMD (N=20), AND AGE- / BMI- MATCHED PAIN-FREE CONTROLS (N=20), WE WILL EVALUATE AUTONOMIC FUNCTION FROM CARDIAC AND BEAT-TO-BEAT BLOOD PRESSURE MEASUREMENTS. WE WILL COMPARE FMRI-MEASURED ACTIVITY WITHIN BRAINSTEM CIRCUITS BY MEASURING RSFC (IE, BETWEEN-REGION CORRELATED ACTIVITY). IN AIM 2 WE WILL CHARACTERIZE HOW ALTERED GLYMPHATIC FLOW RELATES TO AUTONOMIC DYSFUNCTION AND CHRONIC PAIN. AMONG THE SAME GROUPS AS IN AIM 1, WE WILL USE NOVEL FMRI SEQUENCES TO EVALUATE BRAIN GLYMPHATIC FLOW (SURROGATE MRI MARKERS). USING MULTIVARIABLE MODELS, WE WILL TEST HOW ALTERED CNS ACTIVITY RELATES TO AUTONOMIC DYSFUNCTION, AND PAIN VIA SURVEYS & QUANTITATIVE SENSORY TESTS. BY CHARACTERIZING CLINICAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN NOVEL NEUROIMAGING METRICS OF CNS FUNCTION AND AUTONOMIC DYSFUNCTION IN CHRONIC PAIN, THE PROJECT WILL LEAD TO A LONGITUDINAL INVESTIGATION TO DELINEATE HOW NEUROIMAGING/BIOBEHAVIORAL ENDPOINTS RELATE TO PATIENT PROGNOSIS. BY LINKING MECHANISTIC-CHARACTERIZATION OF SUCH ENDPOINTS ACROSS BOTH THE CENTRAL AND AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEMS IN TMD PATIENTS, WE WILL LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR INNOVATIVE FUTURE CLINICAL TRIALS INVOLVING CNS/ANS – TARGETED INTERVENTIONS FOR MODEL DEVELOPMENT TO INFORM PERSONALIZED TREATMENT SELECTION.

description: DECOY ADHESION BY VEILLONELLA ATYPICA: HAG1-MEDIATED SHIELDING OF ORAL EPITHELIUM FROM PORPHYROMONAS GINGIVALIS - MECHANISMS AND THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL - SUMMARY / ABSTRACT PERIODONTAL DISEASE IS A PREVALENT AND COSTLY CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY CONDITION THAT AFFECTS NEARLY HALF OF U.S. ADULTS AND IS DRIVEN BY COMPLEX BACTERIAL INTERACTIONS WITHIN SUBGINGIVAL BIOFILMS. AMONG THE KEY PATHOGENS, PORPHYROMONAS GINGIVALIS (PG) FUNCTIONS AS A KEYSTONE SPECIES THAT PROMOTES DYSBIOSIS AND HOST INFLAMMATION THROUGH POTENT ADHESINS, PROTEASES, AND IMMUNE MODULATION. BLOCKING PG COLONIZATION AT THE ORAL EPITHELIAL SURFACE REPRESENTS A PROMISING AND INNOVATIVE STRATEGY FOR DISEASE PREVENTION. OUR RECENT WORK IDENTIFIES VEILLONELLA ATYPICA (VA), A COMMON EARLY COLONIZER OF ORAL BIOFILMS, AS A PROTECTIVE COMMENSAL THAT MODULATES PG-INDUCED INFLAMMATION. VA ADHERES STRONGLY TO BOTH PG AND ORAL EPITHELIAL CELLS (OECS) VIA ITS GIANT YADA-LIKE SURFACE ADHESIN HAG1, A 7187-AMINO ACID AUTOTRANSPORTER. PRELIMINARY DATA REVEAL THAT WILD-TYPE VA, BUT NOT A ΔHAG1 MUTANT, MARKEDLY SUPPRESSES PG-INDUCED IL-6 AND IL-8 SECRETION IN OECS, HIGHLIGHTING A PREVIOUSLY UNRECOGNIZED “DECOY-ADHESION” MECHANISM. STRUCTURAL MODELING PREDICTS TWO FUNCTIONALLY DISTINCT HEAD DOMAINS – HAG1-HD1 MEDIATING VA-OEC ADHESION AND HAG1-HD2 MEDIATING VA-PG COAGGREGATION – SUGGESTING THAT HAG1 ACTS AS A MOLECULAR BRIDGE ANCHORING VA TO THE MUCOSA WHILE INTERCEPTING PG ACCESS TO HOST RECEPTORS. TO RIGOROUSLY DEFINE THIS MECHANISM, AIM 1 WILL DISSECT HAG1’S DOMAIN-SPECIFIC FUNCTIONS USING GENETIC DELETION MUTANTS, VA-OEC-PG CO-CULTURE ASSAYS, AND PULLDOWN-MASS SPECTROMETRY TO IDENTIFY EPITHELIAL RECEPTORS AND PG ADHESIN PARTNERS. AIM 2 WILL UNCOVER THE BROADER GENETIC REPERTOIRE REGULATING HAG1 EXPRESSION AND VA’S MODULATION OF PG- INDUCED PATHOGENESIS. A HIGH-THROUGHPUT HAG1-LUCIFERASE TRANSPOSON SCREEN, COMBINED WITH MARKERLESS MUTAGENESIS AND RNA-SEQ, WILL IDENTIFY KEY REGULATORY GENES AND SIGNALING PATHWAYS CONTROLLING HAG1 AND OTHER ADHESION-RELATED NETWORKS. IN PARALLEL, A ΔHAG1 TRANSPOSON LIBRARY WILL IDENTIFY HAG1-INDEPENDENT FACTORS AFFECTING PG VIRULENCE AND HOST INFLAMMATION, WHILE SCREENING THE VA TRANSPOSON LIBRARY FOR MUTANTS INDUCING EPITHELIAL CYTOKINES WILL REVEAL LATENT PRO-INFLAMMATORY TRAITS, CLARIFYING VEILLONELLA’S COMMENSAL VERSUS PATHOBIONT POTENTIAL. COLLECTIVELY, THIS WORK WILL ILLUMINATE A NEW PARADIGM OF COMMENSAL-DRIVEN COLONIZATION RESISTANCE, WHERE VA SHIELDS EPITHELIAL SURFACES FROM PATHOGEN-INDUCED INFLAMMATION THROUGH DOMAIN-SPECIFIC ADHESION AND GENETIC REGULATION. BY DEFINING THE MOLECULAR AND REGULATORY BASIS OF THIS NATURAL PROTECTIVE MECHANISM, THE PROPOSED STUDY LAYS THE FOUNDATION FOR NOVEL NON-ANTIBIOTIC THERAPEUTICS – SUCH AS ADHESIN-MIMETICS OR ENGINEERED PROBIOTICS – TO PREVENT PERIODONTAL AND MUCOSAL INFLAMMATORY DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMAGE-BASED DETECTION AND SPATIAL MONITORING OF SECONDARY LYMPHEDEMA IN HEAD AND NECK CANCER - SECONDARY LYMPHEDEMA (LD), A DISEASE WITH NO KNOWN CURE, IS ONE OF THE MOST SIGNIFICANT SURVIVORSHIP MORBIDITIES IN HEAD AND NECK CANCER (HNC). IF LEFT UNTREATED, CHRONIC LD CAN LEAD TO SIGNIFICANT LONG-TERM COSMETIC, FUNCTIONAL, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL CONSEQUENCES THAT ARE OFTEN IRREVERSIBLE, INCLUDING IMPAIRMENTS IN SPEECH, BREATHING, VOCALIZATION, AND SWALLOWING. MALFUNCTION OF THE LYMPHATIC SYSTEM HAS ALSO BEEN SHOWN TO PLAY A KEY ROLE IN THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF MULTIPLE DISEASE STATES, RANGING FROM CANCER GROWTH AND METASTASES TO HEART FAILURE. EARLY DETECTION, DIAGNOSIS, AND TREATMENT OF LD IS CRITICAL TO SUCCESSFUL MANAGEMENT BEFORE LD PROGRESSES TO PERMANENT FIBROSIS, AND REDUCES THE RISK OF COMPLICATIONS IN HNC. HOWEVER, THERE ARE NO RELIABLE METHODS FOR THE OBJECTIVE DETECTION AND MONITORING OF LD IN HNC. THIS PROJECT DEVELOPS A FIRST-IN-CLASS, AUTOMATED AND OBJECTIVE DETECTION AND MEASUREMENT METHODOLOGY FOR LD IN HNC. THIS METHODOLOGY IMPLEMENTS A COMBINATION OF NOVEL LEARNING-FREE COMPUTER VISION METHODOLOGIES AND SMARTPHONE INSTRUMENTATION TO SUPPORT THE GRANULAR SPATIOTEMPORAL ASSESSMENT OF LD. WE INTRODUCE A NOVEL LEARNING-FREE HEAD AND NECK DIGITIZATION ALGORITHM THAT MODELS IMPLICIT SURFACE AND 3D LANDMARKS IN A UNIFIED FRAMEWORK TO REDUCE RECONSTRUCTION UNCERTAINTIES, ADDRESS ROBUST LANDMARK REGISTRATION ACROSS MULTIPLE VIEWS, AND SUPPORT MONITORING OVER TIME. BECAUSE OUR APPROACH IS LEARNING-FREE, IT IS INHERENTLY AMENABLE TO DIFFERENT PATIENT POPULATIONS AND INDEPENDENT ON TRAINING DATA. THIS APPROACH WILL ALSO INTRODUCE A NEW, LOCALIZED IMAGE-BASED CRITERION AND OBJECTIVE SCALE FOR LD IN HNC. TOGETHER, THESE INNOVATIONS CIRCUMVENT EXISTING BARRIERS TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF IMAGE-BASED LD DETECTION AND MONITORING. FROM A CLINICAL PERSPECTIVE, THIS APPLICATION CHALLENGES THE CURRENT STANDARD OF CARE FOR HNC LD AND SEEKS TO SHIFT CURRENT RESEARCH AND CLINICAL PRACTICE PARADIGMS BY INTRODUCING A NOVEL PROTOTYPE APPROACH AND TOOL FOR HNC LD DETECTION AND MONITORING IN THE CLINIC.

description: DE NOVO DESIGN OF PRO DOMAINS FOR TGF SUPERFAMILY FOLDING, EXPRESSION, AND FUNCTION - DE NOVO DESIGN OF PRO-DOMAINS FOR TGF SUPERFAMILY FOLDING, EXPRESSION, AND FUNCTION THE TGF-Β SUPERFAMILY IS A GROUP OF CYSTEINE KNOT GROWTH FACTORS THAT PLAY ESSENTIAL ROLES IN CENTRAL DEVELOPMENTAL PROCESSES AND ARE PROMISING CANDIDATES FOR THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION. WHILE THERE ARE POTENTIAL CLINICAL USES OF THESE GROWTH FACTORS LIKE WOUND HEALING, BONE REGENERATION, AND CANCER THERAPY, UNCONTROLLED ACTIVATION OF THESE GROWTH FACTORS LIMIT BROADER APPLICATION. THESE OFF-TARGET EFFECTS INCLUDE ECTOPIC BONE FORMATION, TUMORIGENESIS, AND LIFE-THREATENING INFLAMMATION. NATURALLY PRODUCED GROWTH FACTORS ARE EXPRESSED WITH A LARGE (~300 AMINO ACID) PRO-DOMAIN. FOR MANY SUPERFAMILY MEMBERS THIS PRO-DOMAIN IS INVOLVED IN STRICT REGULATION OF GROWTH FACTOR ACTIVATION AFTER SECRETION INTO THE EXTRACELLULAR ENVIRONMENT. ACTIVATION BY CLEAVAGE OF THIS PRO DOMAIN IS NOT CONTROLLABLE FOR DESIRED THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS, WHICH FUNDAMENTALLY LIMITS BROADER DEPLOYMENT. IN THIS APPLICATION WE EXPLORE THE DESIGN OF GFS WHICH ARE INITIALLY INACTIVE, BUT CAN BE ACTIVATED BY EXTERNAL SPATIOTEMPORAL CUES. IF SUCCESSFUL, THESE DESIGNS WILL SOLVE THE OFF-TARGET CHALLENGE THAT HAS LIMITED USE OF TGF-Β SUPERFAMILY GROWTH FACTORS AS COMPONENTS OF THERAPEUTICS ACROSS BIOMEDICAL APPLICATIONS. OUR APPROACH IS BASED ON THE CREATION OF SYNTHETIC PRO-DOMAINS USING LEADING COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN TOOLS. WE WILL USE GENERATIVE AI TO DESIGN NEW PROTEINS, WHICH WILL BE EXPRESSED AS A PROTEIN FUSION WITH GROWTH FACTOR; EXPRESSION YIELD AND ACTIVITY WILL BE ASSESSED USING HIGH THROUGHPUT BIOCHEMICAL AND CELL-BASED ASSAYS. WE WILL FIRST DEMONSTRATE THIS APPROACH USING BMP-2 BECAUSE OF ITS THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL FOR BONE REGENERATION. WE WILL THEN EXTEND THIS APPROACH TO SEVEN ADDITIONAL GROWTH FACTORS, INCLUDING TGF-Β1-3 INVOLVED IN WOUND HEALING.
