description: THE EFFECT OF ELECTRONIC CIGARETTE VAPOR ON FORMATION OF INTRACELLULAR BACTERIAL COMMUNITIES AND RECURRENCE OF OTITIS MEDIA - PROJECT ABSTRACT INFECTIONS CAUSED BY NONTYPEABLE HAEMOPHILUS INFLUENZAE (NTHI) STRAINS REPRESENT A MAJOR CAUSE OF OTITIS MEDIA (OM), EXACERBATIONS OF CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE (COPD), AND BACTERIAL SINUSITIS. FURTHERMORE, NTHI CAUSES CHRONIC, TREATMENT-REFRACTORY DISEASES, IN PART BY FORMING INTRACELLULAR BACTERIAL COMMUNITIES (IBCS) WITHIN EPITHELIAL CELLS THAT PROVIDE A REFUGE FROM BOTH THE HOST IMMUNE SYSTEM, AND FROM CLINICAL INTERVENTIONS. THE BACTERIAL AND HOST ELEMENTS THAT IMPACT NTHI PERSISTENCE AND RECURRENCE OF OM ARE NOT COMPLETELY UNDERSTOOD. THEREFORE, THE DELINEATION OF HOST-PATHOGEN INTERACTIONS AND ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES THAT LEAD TO OM-DERIVED SEQUELAE WILL INFORM NOVEL THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES. CIGARETTES AND AIR POLLUTION ARE BOTH SOURCES OF TOXIC GASES AND FINE PARTICULATE MATTER THAT ARE LINKED WITH SUSCEPTIBILITY TO OM IN CHILDREN. ELECTRONIC CIGARETTE (E-CIG) UTILIZATION HAS DRAMATICALLY INCREASED IN THE PAST SEVERAL YEARS BOTH AS A TOOL FOR CESSATION OF TRADITIONAL SMOKING, BUT MOSTLY IN NEW ADOLESCENT NICOTINE USERS. THE EFFECT OF E-CIG AEROSOL AND NICOTINE ON SUSCEPTIBILITY OF CHILDREN TO OM AS WELL AS EXACERBATION AND RECURRENCE OF NTHI-MEDIATED DISEASE THUS REPRESENTS A NEW HEALTH PROBLEM THAT IS UNDERSTUDIED. FURTHER, THE CONTRIBUTION OF AEROSOL AND NICOTINE EXPOSURE WITH INCREASED INFLAMMATION, INFECTION SUSCEPTIBILITY AND FIBROSIS ASSOCIATED WITH OM ARE UNCLEAR. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT PASSIVE EXPOSURE TO E-CIG AEROSOL AND NICOTINE ENHANCES INVASION, IBC FORMATION, PERSISTENCE, AND RECURRENCE OF NTHI. EXPOSURE TO AEROSOLS IS A KNOWN RISK FACTOR FOR OM, BUT THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS INVOLVED HAVE NOT BEEN INVESTIGATED. AIM 1: DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF PRODUCTS OF E-CIG COMBUSTION AND NICOTINE ON MIDDLE EAR EPITHELIAL CELL FUNCTION AND IBC FORMATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT E-CIG AEROSOL AND NICOTINE MODULATE EPITHELIAL RESPONSES THAT PROMOTE NTHI INVASION AND IBC FORMATION IN VITRO. AIM 2: DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF THE PRODUCTS OF E-CIG COMBUSTION AND NICOTINE ON OM DISEASE SEVERITY, PERSISTENCE AND AS A STIMULUS OF RECURRENT EPISODES OF OM. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT E-CIG AEROSOL WILL PROMOTE SUPPURATIVE INFLAMMATION AND IBC FORMATION DURING EXPERIMENTAL OM, THAT WILL BE FURTHER EXACERBATED IN THE PRESENCE OF NICOTINE. FURTHERMORE, WE HAVE ESTABLISHED A PRECLINICAL MODEL WHERE IBCS REMAIN FOR WEEKS IN THE MIDDLE EAR FOLLOWING RESOLUTION OF DISEASE. WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER SUBSEQUENT EXPOSURE TO E-CIG AEROSOL WILL PROMOTE EGRESS OF NTHI FROM THESE INTRACELLULAR RESERVOIRS TO ESTABLISH A RECURRENT EPISODE OF OM. THE OUTCOMES OF OUR COMPREHENSIVE APPROACH WILL SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW ENVIRONMENTAL PARTICLES AND NICOTINE INFLUENCE NTHI PATHOGENIC LIFESTYLES THAT IMPACT PERSISTENCE AND RECURRENCE AND REVEAL NOVEL APPROACHES FOR THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS.

description: EARLY LIFE TOXICANT AND PSYCHOSOCIAL CO-EXPOSURES AND ADOLESCENT AND EMERGING ADULT HEALTH - SUMMARY MENTAL HEALTH PROBLEMS AMONG EMERGING ADULTS ARE INCREASING IN THE UNITED STATES AND WORLDWIDE. ALTHOUGH MULTIPLE EARLY LIFE RISK FACTORS FOR THESE MENTAL HEALTH PROBLEMS EXIST, THEIR INDIVIDUAL AND COMBINED IMPACTS ARE NOT YET FULLY UNDERSTOOD. FOR EXAMPLE, ADULT HEAVY METAL EXPOSURES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH MENTAL HEALTH PROBLEMS, THOUGH LIMITED RESEARCH HAS CONSIDERED EXPOSURE IN SENSITIVE EARLY LIFE PERIODS IN RELATION TO ADULT MENTAL HEALTH. IMPORTANTLY, CHILDREN EXPERIENCE OTHER EXPOSURES, SUCH AS PSYCHOSOCIAL RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS, WHICH MAY SYNERGISTICALLY INCREASE MENTAL HEALTH PROBLEMS, OR PROVIDE PROTECTION. IN ESSENCE, HEAVY METAL AND PSYCHOSOCIAL RISK EXPOSURES IN EARLY LIFE MAY INITIATE A SYNERGISTIC EFFECT, MAKING SOME INDIVIDUALS MORE SUSCEPTIBLE TO MENTAL HEALTH PROBLEMS LATER IN LIFE. CONVERSELY, POSITIVE PSYCHOSOCIAL EXPOSURES MAY BUFFER DETRIMENTAL EFFECTS OF METAL AND PSYCHOSOCIAL RISK FACTORS. CURRENTLY, ASSOCIATIONS OF METALS AND PSYCHOSOCIAL EXPOSURES WITH LATER HEALTH HAVE BEEN STUDIED IN RELATIVE ISOLATION. THESE EARLY LIFE EXPOSURES COULD INFLUENCE MENTAL HEALTH THROUGH DYSREGULATION OF PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS PATHWAYS AS CHILDREN AGE (E.G. ADOLESCENCE), THUS INCREASING RISK FOR MENTAL HEALTH PROBLEMS IN EMERGING ADULTHOOD. YET, ASSOCIATIONS OF METALS AND PSYCHOSOCIAL RISK AND PROTECTIVE EXPOSURE MIXTURES WITH PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS BIOMARKERS, SUCH AS OXIDATIVE STRESS AND ALLOSTATIC LOAD, ESPECIALLY IN SENSITIVE STRESS PHYSIOLOGY DEVELOPMENTAL PERIODS SUCH AS ADOLESCENCE, REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THE ELEMENT COHORT IS UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO ADDRESS THESE RESEARCH GAPS, SERVING AS AN INVALUABLE LONGITUDINAL SCIENTIFIC RESOURCE WITH MORE THAN 30 YEARS OF FOLLOW-UP, EXTENSIVE PRENATAL BIOSPECIMENS, AND REPEATED ASSESSMENTS WHOSE UNIQUE STUDY DESIGN SUPPORTS SCIENTIFIC INVESTIGATIONS THAT WOULD OTHERWISE BE DIFFICULT OR IMPOSSIBLE TO CONDUCT. AMONG 550 EMERGING ADULTS FOLLOWED SINCE BIRTH, WE WILL LEVERAGE ARCHIVED DATA FROM THE PRENATAL PERIOD (1997-2005), ALREADY COLLECTED BIOSPECIMENS FROM ADOLESCENCE (2013), AND DATA BEING COLLECTED IN EMERGING ADULTHOOD AS PART OF A FUNDED COHORT FOLLOW-UP STUDY (NIEHS U24ES028502). WE AIM TO 1) CHARACTERIZE EARLY LIFE PSYCHOSOCIAL FACTORS AND IDENTIFY PREDOMINANT HEAVY METALS AND PSYCHOSOCIAL PROFILES IN ELEMENT COHORT; 2) EXAMINE EARLY LIFE HEAVY METAL AND PSYCHOSOCIAL MIXTURE EFFECTS ON ADOLESCENT PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS; AND 3) EXAMINE ADOLESCENT PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS PATHWAYS BETWEEN EARLY LIFE HEAVY METAL AND PSYCHOSOCIAL MIXTURES AND EMERGING ADULT MENTAL HEALTH. NIEHS HAS CALLED FOR RESEARCH TO REDUCE INDIVIDUAL SUSCEPTIBILITY FOR LONG-TERM ADVERSE HEALTH OUTCOMES BY IDENTIFYING MIXTURE EXPOSURES AND PHYSIOLOGICAL MEDIATORS. THIS WORK WILL IDENTIFY COMBINATIONS OF METAL AND PSYCHOSOCIAL EXPOSURES THAT INCREASE RISK OR PROTECTION FOR PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS AND SUBSEQUENT MENTAL HEALTH PROBLEMS ACROSS DEVELOPMENT, PINPOINT THOSE MOST VULNERABLE, AND HIGHLIGHT OPTIMAL DEVELOPMENTAL STAGES AND MODIFIABLE TARGETS FOR INTERVENTION FOR CHILDREN ALREADY EXPOSED, WITH FINDINGS THAT WILL INFORM PREVENTION STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF AMERICANS EXPOSED TO SIMILAR ENVIRONMENTAL AND PSYCHOSOCIAL CONDITIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPACT OF METALS ON DNA AND CHROMATIN STRUCTURES AND GENE EXPRESSION - PROJECT SUMMARY  ENVIRONMENTAL METALS SUCH AS NICKEL AND CADMIUM ARE UBIQUITOUS POLLUTANTS AND CARCINOGENS THAT CAN CONTRIBUTE TO DISEASE DEVELOPMENT VIA SEVERAL MECHANISMS, INCLUDING DYSREGULATION OF GENE EXPRESSION. HOWEVER, THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS ARE NOT FULLY UNDERSTOOD. EXPOSURE TO THESE METALS CAN STIMULATE EPIGENETIC MODIFICATION (E.G. CYTOSINE METHYLATION), WHICH CAN FACILITATE THE FORMATION OF ALTERNATIVE DNA (E.G. NON-B DNA, SUCH AS Z-DNA AND H-DNA) AND CHROMATIN STRUCTURES. IN ADDITION TO CYTOSINE METHYLATION-INDUCED NON-B DNA FORMATION, EXPOSURE TO NICKEL AND CADMIUM CAN DIRECTLY STIMULATE THE FORMATION OF THESE ALTERNATIVE DNA STRUCTURES. IMPORTANTLY, NON-B DNA CAN IMPEDE TRANSCRIPTION PROGRESSION BY STALLING RNA POLYMERASES, THEREBY ALTERING GENE EXPRESSION. THUS, WE SPECULATE THAT NON-B DNA CONTRIBUTES TO METAL-INDUCED ALTERATIONS IN GENE EXPRESSION. HOWEVER, HOW EXPOSURE TO THESE UBIQUITOUS ENVIRONMENTAL METALS IMPACTS DNA STRUCTURE- RELATED ALTERATIONS IN GENE EXPRESSION IS NOT KNOWN. THUS, THE RATIONALE FOR THIS STUDY IS THAT THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED TO FILL THIS GAP IN KNOWLEDGE. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO DETERMINE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH EXPOSURE TO ENVIRONMENTAL METALS AFFECT DNA-STRUCTURE-INDUCED MODULATION OF TRANSCRIPTION, AND TO EXPLOIT THIS NEW INFORMATION TO DEVELOP NOVEL APPROACHES TO ATTENUATE DYSREGULATION OF GENE EXPRESSION. THE IMMEDIATE OBJECTIVES ARE TO DETERMINE THE EFFECTS OF METAL EXPOSURE AND CYTOSINE METHYLATION ON NON-B DNA FORMATION, CHROMATIN ASSEMBLY, AND GENE EXPRESSION IN MAMMALIAN CELLS. THE NOVEL HYPOTHESIS, THAT EXPOSURE TO ENVIRONMENTAL METALS, AND THE SUBSEQUENT EPIGENETIC MODIFICATION STIMULATES NON-B DNA-INDUCED TRANSCRIPTION MODULATION VIA ALTERATIONS IN DNA AND CHROMATIN CONFORMATIONS, WILL BE TESTED IN THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) DETERMINE THE EFFECTS OF CYTOSINE METHYLATION ON NON-B DNA STRUCTURE FORMATION, CHROMATIN CONFORMATION, AND GENE TRANSCRIPTION; AND 2) ELUCIDATE THE MECHANISMS OF NON-B DNA-INDUCED ALTERATION OF GENE EXPRESSION IN THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF ENVIRONMENTAL METALS IN MAMMALIAN CELLS. THE RESEARCH PROPOSED IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT WILL TEST A NOVEL HYPOTHESIS UTILIZING STATE-OF-THE-ART METHODOLOGIES (E.G. THE MAPIT ASSAY), CELLS FROM NOVEL TRANSGENIC MICE, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF A NEW MAMMALIAN CELL SYSTEM TO STUDY GENE EXPRESSION AT ENDOGENOUS CHROMOSOMAL LOCI. THE EXPECTED CONTRIBUTION IS THAT THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH METALS IMPACT GENE EXPRESSION AT ALTERNATIVELY STRUCTURED GENOMIC LOCI WILL BE ELUCIDATED. THIS IS EXPECTED TO HAVE A SIGNIFICANT POSITIVE IMPACT BECAUSE THE NEW INFORMATION WILL AID IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL STRATEGIES TO REDUCE DISEASE-RELATED DYSREGULATION OF GENE EXPRESSION CAUSED BY ENVIRONMENTAL CARCINOGENIC METALS AND WILL CONTRIBUTE FUNDAMENTAL NEW KNOWLEDGE IN THE AREAS OF EPIGENETIC MODIFICATION, DNA STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION, AND GENE EXPRESSION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REVEALING COMPOSITION AND STRUCTURE OF STRESS-INDUCED RNA CONDENSATION USING HIGHLY MULTIPLEXED SINGLE-MOLECULE FLUORESCENCE LABELING - PROJECT SUMMARY HOW DO CELLS SENSE AND RESPOND TO SUDDEN CHANGES IN THEIR ENVIRONMENT? AFTER DECADES OF STUDY, KEY EVOLUTIONARILY CONSERVED ASPECTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS RESPONSES REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. A CANONICAL EXAMPLE IS THE RESPONSE TO PROTEOTOXIC STRESSES: HEAT SHOCK, OXIDATIVE DAMAGE, HYPOXIA, AND SUDDEN STARVATION. IN EUKARYOTIC CELLS, THESE STRESSES CAUSE CONDENSATION OF MANY PROTEINS AND MRNAS INTO STRESS GRANULES (SGS), LARGE CLUSTERS NOW KNOWN AS BIOMOLECULAR CONDENSATES. BECAUSE NO SPECIFIC ACTIVITY IS ASSOCIATED WITH SGS, THEIR IDENTIFICATION IS BASED ON THE APPEARANCE OF MICROSCOPICALLY VISIBLE FOCI (~1 MICRON IN SIZE) CONTAINING POLY(A)+ RNA AND MARKER PROTEINS SUCH AS POLY(A)-BINDING PROTEIN. RECENT WORK FROM OUR GROUPS AND OTHERS HAVE LED TO THE KEY DISCOVERY THAT NANOSCALE CONDENSATION OF MULTIPLE COMPONENTS OF SGS, INCLUDING PROTEINS AND MRNAS, OCCURS PRIOR TO—AND EVEN IN THE ABSENCE OF—THE APPEARANCE OF SGS. IN PARTICULAR, WE HAVE DISCOVERED TRANSLATION-INITIATION-INHIBITED CONDENSATES (TIICS) OF MRNAS THAT CAN BE FOUND EVEN IN UNSTRESSED CELLS AND SERVE AS SG PRECURSORS. TIICS AND RELATED CONDENSATES SIT BELOW THE DIFFRACTION LIMIT OF FLUORESCENCE MICROSCOPY IN SIZE, SUCH THAT NO FOCI APPEAR, MAKING THESE NANOCONDENSATES ALL BUT INVISIBLE TO STANDARD METHODS. BECAUSE THE KEY ADAPTIVE STRESS RESPONSES, INCLUDING TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND TRANSLATIONAL CHANGES, OCCUR UNDER MILDER CONDITIONS WHERE SGS DO NOT FORM, NANOCONDENSATES MAY CARRY OUT MANY OR MOST OF THE ACTIVITIES CORRELATED WITH THE APPEARANCE OF SGS AND OFTEN ATTRIBUTED TO THEM. NEW CAPACITY TO CHARACTERIZE THESE NANOCONDENSATES IS THUS URGENTLY NEEDED. WHAT ARE THE COMPOSITIONS OF THESE NANOCONDENSATES? HOW MANY DIFFERENT TYPES OF NANOCONDENSATES ARE THERE, AND WHAT ARE THEIR RELATIONSHIPS TO SGS? ALL INFORMATION TO DATE WE HAVE COLLECTED USING BULK APPROACHES WHICH ARE POWERLESS TO ADDRESS THESE FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS, ALL OF WHICH UNDERPIN THE ULTIMATE QUESTION OF THE BIOLOGICAL FUNCTIONS OF NANOCONDENSATES. TO OVERCOME THESE LIMITATIONS REQUIRES SINGLE-CONDENSATE RESOLUTION, SUCH AS THE ABILITY TO TRAP NANOCONDENSATES AND QUANTIFY THEIR COMPONENTS, AND THE ABILITY TO LABEL MANY MORE MOLECULAR SPECIES THAN IN PRIOR STUDIES TO INCREASE THE RATE OF COLOCALIZATION IN NANOCONDENSATES. WE HAVE MADE METHODOLOGICAL ADVANCES THAT NOW UNLOCK BOTH OF THESE ABILITIES. FOR TRAPPING, WE HAVE ADAPTED THE ANTI-BROWNIAN ELECTROKINETIC (ABEL) TRAP FOR INTERROGATION OF BIOLOGICAL MOLECULES IN FREE SOLUTION, WHICH WE PROPOSE TO USE FOR SINGLE-CONDENSATE TRAPPING. FOR LABELING, WE HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED FRETFLUORS, A NEW FAMILY OF FLUORESCENT LABELS SPECIFICALLY ENGINEERED FOR MULTIPLEXED IMAGING OF TENS OF MOLECULAR SPECIES AT THE SINGLE-MOLECULE LEVEL, WHICH WE PROPOSE TO USE FOR TAGGING SUFFICIENT NUMBERS OF MRNAS TO ENSURE SINGLE-MOLECULE COLOCALIZATION IN TIICS. IF SUCCESSFUL, THE COMBINATION OF THESE GROUNDBREAKING METHODS WITH NEW OUR RECENT BIOLOGICAL DISCOVERIES WILL UNLOCK A WIDE RANGE OF INQUIRY, BREAKING THE LONGSTANDING DEPENDENCE ON DIFFRACTION-LIMITED IDENTIFICATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS-INDUCED CONDENSATES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TRACE METALS IN ENVIRONMENTAL MEDIA AND THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH LIVER DISEASE - PROJECT ABSTRACT CHRONIC LIVER DISEASE (CLD) IS A MASSIVE THREAT TO PUBLIC HEALTH. CLD IS A COMPLEX DISEASE SPECTRUM THAT INCLUDES HEPATIC STEATOSIS AND FIBROSIS, THE END STAGE OF WHICH IS CIRRHOSIS. PROGRESSION FROM CIRRHOSIS TO HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA (HCC) IS WELL ESTABLISHED AND HCC INCIDENCE HAS RISEN DRAMATICALLY IN THE LAST THREE DECADES. WE SEE ESPECIALLY STEEP INCREASES IN THE SOUTHEASTERN UNITED STATES. A POTENT YET UNDERSTUDIED RISK FACTOR FOR THESE CONDITIONS IS CHRONIC EXPOSURE TO ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINANTS, AS MULTIPLE CLASSES OF CHEMICALS, INCLUDING TOXIC METALS, ARE WIDESPREAD IN THE US POPULATION, WITH HIGH BURDENS IN SOUTHERN STATES AND RURAL RESIDENTS. EXPOSURE TO EVEN TRACE AMOUNTS OF TOXIC METALS, ESPECIALLY OVER LONG PERIODS OF TIME, HAS BEEN LINKED TO A WIDE RANGE OF CHRONIC DISEASES. TOXIC METALS CAN BE FOUND IN SOILS, HOUSEHOLD DUST, AND DRINKING WATER, POSING SIGNIFICANT RISKS TO THE GENERAL POPULATION. THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED TO CONNECT NON-OCCUPATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL SOURCES OF METAL EXPOSURE TO CLINICALLY ADJUDICATED LIVER DISEASE OUTCOMES. HERE, WE WILL LEVERAGE AVAILABLE BIOLOGICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SPECIMENS FROM AN ACTIVE COHORT (THE SOUTHERN LIVER HEALTH STUDY; STRIVE) FROM THE SOUTHEASTERN U.S. TO CONDUCT BOTH A CROSS-SECTIONAL (AIM 1; 800 TOTAL PARTICIPANTS) AND LONGITUDINAL (AIM 2; 300 PARTICIPANTS) STUDIES TO TEST THE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS THAT METAL CONTAMINATION INCREASES THE RISK OF CIRRHOSIS AND PROGRESSION FROM CIRRHOSIS TO HCC. SIMULTANEOUSLY, OUR WORK TESTS WHETHER MEASURING EXPOSURES DIRECTLY IN ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLES (DRINKING WATER, HOUSE DUST, AND SOIL) PREDICTS LIVER DISEASE RISK. EVEN BEYOND LIVER DISEASE, COLLECTING BIOLOGICAL SAMPLES, PARTICULARLY WHOLE BLOOD, IS CITED AS ONE OF THE MOST RATE- AND COST-LIMITING STEPS; DIRECTLY CONTRIBUTING TO SAMPLING GAPS IN LARGE COHORT STUDIES THAT MISREPRESENTS THE HETEROGENEITY OF THE GENERAL U.S. POPULATION. YET, RARELY DO STUDIES CONNECT METAL CONTAMINATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLES WITH BOTH THE BODY BURDEN AND ACTUAL DISEASE OUTCOMES. EVEN FEWER STUDIES ASSOCIATE METALS MEASURED IN ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLES WITH ADJUDICATED DISEASE PROGRESSION OVER TIME. WE WILL FIRST EXAMINE HOW METAL CONTAMINANTS MEASURED IN THE HOME ENVIRONMENT RELATE TO HOW THESE METALS ACCUMULATE IN THE BODY (I.E., THE “BODY BURDEN”) FOR 400 CIRRHOSIS PATIENTS AND 400 OTHERWISE HEALTHY INDIVIDUALS TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT EXPOSURE TO A MIXTURE OF METALS IN THE HOME ENVIRONMENT IS CROSS-SECTIONALLY ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED RISK OF LIVER FIBROSIS/CIRRHOSIS (AIM 1). NEXT, WE WILL NEST A CASE-CONTROL STUDY OF 100 PARTICIPANTS THAT HAVE PROGRESSED TO HCC AND 200 PARTICIPANTS THAT HAVE NOT PROGRESSED BEYOND CIRRHOSIS WITHIN A SIMILAR TIME FRAME TO TEST THE THAT PERSISTENT OR INCREASING CONCENTRATIONS OF METAL CONTAMINANTS IN ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLES ARE LONGITUDINALLY ASSOCIATED WITH AN INCREASED RISK OF PROGRESSION FROM CIRRHOSIS TO HCC. BY USING MULTIPLE MATRICES, OUR WORK WILL PROVIDE MUCH NEEDED INSIGHTS INTO ROUTES OF EXPOSURE TO TOXIC METAL MIXTURES EXPERIENCED BY THE GENERAL POPULATION. OUR APPROACH USING ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLING ALSO HAS IMMENSE POTENTIAL TO OFFER LESS INVASIVE, COST-EFFICIENT AND SCALABLE SAMPLING STRATEGIES, WITH THE GOAL TO HELP REDUCE THE BURDEN OF LIVER DISEASES IN THE OVERALL POPULATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TREATMENT OF CEP290-ASSOCIATED RETINAL DEGENERATION - ABSTRACT MUTATIONS IN THE CEP290 GENE ARE A LEADING CAUSE OF LEBER CONGENITAL AMAUROSIS (LCA), A HEREDITARY RETINAL DYSTROPHY THAT RESULTS IN SEVERE VISION LOSS DURING INFANCY OR EARLY CHILDHOOD. WHILE GENE AUGMENTATION THERAPY USING ADENO-ASSOCIATED VIRUS (AAV) VECTORS HAS SHOWN PROMISE IN TREATING INHERITED RETINAL DEGENERATIONS, CEP290-LCA PRESENTS SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGES DUE TO THE GENE’S LARGE SIZE AND THE DIVERSE MUTATIONS DISTRIBUTED THROUGHOUT THE GENE. EXISTING GENE THERAPY APPROACHES FOR CEP290-LCA HAVE TARGETED SPECIFIC MUTATIONS AND/OR ACHIEVED LIMITED SUCCESS IN RESTORING CEP290 GENE FUNCTION. THE PROPOSED STUDY AIMS TO OVERCOME THESE LIMITATIONS AND DEVELOP MUTATION-INDEPENDENT, GENERIC CEP290 GENE THERAPY VECTORS. WE HAVE PIONEERED AN INNOVATIVE STRATEGY THAT EMPLOYS UP TO FOUR AAV VECTORS IN CONJUNCTION WITH A UNIDIRECTIONAL DNA RECOMBINATION SYSTEM TO DELIVER AND RECONSTITUTE LARGE GENES. USING THIS APPROACH, WE HAVE SUCCESSFULLY ENGINEERED TRIPARTITE AAV-CEP290 VECTORS THAT PRODUCE FULL-LENGTH CEP290 PROTEINS EFFICIENTLY IN VITRO AND IN MOUSE RETINAS. IN THE PROPOSED STUDY, WE WILL EVALUATE AND COMPARE THE THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY OF TWO SETS OF AAV-CEP290 VECTORS IN TWO CEP290-LCA MOUSE MODELS. THE EFFICACY OF THESE GENE THERAPY VECTORS WILL ALSO BE COMPARED WITH EXISTING SPLIT-INTEIN-BASED CEP290 VECTORS. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS STUDY WILL NOT ONLY PAVE THE WAY FOR EFFECTIVE AND MUTATION-INDEPENDENT GENE THERAPIES FOR CEP290-LCA BUT ALSO PUSH THE BOUNDARIES OF WHAT IS POSSIBLE IN THE FIELD OF GENE THERAPY BY ENABLING THE DELIVERY OF LARGE GENES THAT HAVE PREVIOUSLY BEEN CHALLENGING TO TARGET.

description: UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN EXPANDING ACCESS TO DIABETIC RETINOPATHY SCREENING - 1 PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT: DIABETIC RETINOPATHY (DR) IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF BLINDNESS AMONG U.S. ADULTS.  2 ROUGHLY 20% OF PATIENTS WITH DR SUFFER FROM VISION-THREATENING COMPLICATIONS. ESTIMATES SUGGEST THAT THE VAST  3 MAJORITY OF BLINDNESS CAUSED BY DR COULD BE PREVENTED THROUGH EARLY DETECTION AND TREATMENT. TO THAT END,  4 CLINICAL GUIDELINES RECOMMEND ANNUAL DR SCREENING FOR MOST DIABETIC PATIENTS, BUT ONLY 50–70% OF PATIENTS  5 WITH DIABETES RECEIVE THIS CARE. ONE MAJOR BARRIER TO RECOMMENDED DR SCREENING IS LIMITED ACCESS TO EYE CARE 6 PROFESSIONALS.  7 RECENT INNOVATIONS IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) MAY EXPAND ACCESS TO DR SCREENING. FDA-APPROVED  8 AUTONOMOUS AI DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS DETECT DR WITHOUT REQUIRING THE INVOLVEMENT OF A PHYSICIAN. WE PROPOSE THE  9 FIRST STUDY OF HOW AI EXPANDS ACCESS TO DR SCREENING AND RECOMMENDED TREATMENT. TO DO SO, WE WILL USE 10 100% OF MEDICARE CLAIMS DATA TO IDENTIFY ADOPTION OF AUTONOMOUS AI DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS FOR DR. WE WILL ALSO 11 IMPLEMENT A QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL RESEARCH DESIGN, EXPLOITING VARIATION IN THE TIMING OF AI ADOPTION. MEDICARE 12 CLAIMS ARE AN IDEAL SETTING FOR THIS ANALYSIS, SINCE MEDICARE BEGAN REIMBURSING CLINICIANS FOR THIS CLINICAL 13 APPLICATION OF AI IN 2021. 14 AIM 1 WILL QUANTIFY THE ADOPTION OF AUTONOMOUS AI DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS FOR DR. WE WILL COMPARE THE 15 CHARACTERISTICS OF AI-ADOPTERS AND NON-ADOPTERS, TO UNDERSTAND WHETHER AI ADOPTION IS CORRELATED WITH MARKERS 16 OF CLINICAL NEED, SUCH AS EYE CARE PROFESSIONAL SHORTAGES AND LOW RATES OF DR SCREENING. 17 AIM 2 WILL TEST FOR CHANGES IN RATES OF DR SCREENING AND DIAGNOSIS, FOLLOWING AI ADOPTION. A MEDICAL 18 PRACTICE THAT ADOPTS AN AUTONOMOUS AI DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEM IS NO LONGER CONSTRAINED BY PHYSICIAN AVAILABILITY IN 19 THEIR PROVISION OF DR SCREENING SERVICES. WE THEREFORE HYPOTHESIZE AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER AND SHARE OF 20 DIABETIC PATIENTS RECEIVING ANNUAL DR SCREENING, FOLLOWING ADOPTION OF AI. WE WILL TEST FOR THIS USING A 21 DIFFERENCE-IN-DIFFERENCES RESEARCH DESIGN TO COMPARE OUTCOMES BEFORE AND AFTER ADOPTION, IN AI-ADOPTERS AND 22 NON-ADOPTERS. 23 AIM 3 WILL TEST FOR CHANGES IN RECOMMENDED TREATMENT FOR PATIENTS WITH DR, FOLLOWING AI ADOPTION. WE 24 HYPOTHESIZE THAT RATES OF RECOMMENDED TREATMENT (E.G., FOLLOW-UP VISITS TO AN EYE CARE PROFESSIONAL) FOR DR WILL 25 REMAIN THE SAME OR SLIGHTLY DECREASE FOLLOWING ADOPTION OF AUTONOMOUS AI DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS. THIS IS LARGELY 26 DUE TO THE FACT THAT PATIENTS DIAGNOSED BY AI WITH DR WILL, BY DEFINITION, NOT YET HAVE A RELATIONSHIP WITH AN EYE 27 CARE PROFESSIONAL, MAKING IT POTENTIALLY MORE DIFFICULT TO OBTAIN RECOMMENDED TREATMENT. 28 THIS STUDY RESPONDS DIRECTLY TO THE NATIONAL EYE INSTITUTE’S CALL (PAR-25-357) FOR VISION-RELATED SECONDARY 29 DATA ANALYSIS. OUR FINDINGS WILL GUIDE CLINICAL PRACTICE, MEDICARE POLICY, AND AI ADOPTION DECISIONS – WITH THE 30 ULTIMATE GOAL OF REDUCING PREVENTABLE BLINDNESS AND IMPROVING POPULATION EYE HEALTH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT OF A RAPID PROTEIN DELETION PLATFORM FOR CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM NEURONS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT DEVELOPMENT OF A RAPID PROTEIN DELETION PLATFORM FOR CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM NEURONS  THE ABILITY TO RAPIDLY DELETE PROTEINS IN NEURONS WOULD ENABLE STUDIES INTO DYNAMIC NEURAL FUNCTIONS AND PROCESSES. HOWEVER, CURRENT GENETIC APPROACHES SUCH AS KNOCKOUT OR RNA INTERFERENCE ARE SLOW, IRREVERSIBLE, OR POORLY SUITED TO POSTMITOTIC CELLS. THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP AN INNOVATIVE PLATFORM THAT WILL ENABLE SPECIFIC PROTEIN DELETION IN ADULT CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) NEURONS. THIS APPROACH WOULD HAVE A BROAD RANGE OF APPLICATIONS TO PROBE THE MOLECULAR FUNCTION OF CNS PROTEINS. FURTHER, DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE PROTEIN DELETION TECHNOLOGIES WOULD HAVE SIGNIFICANT TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL FOR TREATING ACUTE NEUROLOGICAL PERTURBATIONS, SUCH AS TRAUMATIC INJURY.  THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A NOVEL MOLECULAR GENETIC TOOL THAT ENABLES RAPID AND REVERSIBLE PROTEIN DELETION IN NEURONS THROUGH CONTROLLED PROTEASOMAL DEGRADATION. THE APPROACH EMPLOYS ANTIBODY- BASED ENGINEERED PROTEIN DEGRADERS THAT ARE DELIVERED INTRACELLULARLY USING ENDOSOMAL ESCAPE PEPTIDES OPTIMIZED FOR EFFICIENT CYTOSOLIC DELIVERY AND NEURONAL BIOCOMPATIBILITY. ONCE INSIDE NEURONS, THESE DEGRADERS BIND A DESIRED PROTEIN TARGET AND RECRUIT THE UBIQUITIN–PROTEASOME SYSTEM TO INDUCE ACUTE, TUNABLE TARGET DEGRADATION IN LESS THAN AN HOUR, PROVIDING TEMPORAL CONTROL OF PROTEOSTASIS AND PROTEIN FUNCTION. AS PROOF-OF-PRINCIPLE, THIS TECHNOLOGY WILL BE APPLIED TO DELETE KNOWN SUPPRESSORS OF AXON REGENERATION IN ADULT CNS NEURONS. THE TARGETED PROTEINS ACT ON DISTINCT PATHWAYS, HAVE DIFFERENT PROTEIN STABILITIES, AND FUNCTION IN DIFFERENT INTRACELLULAR COMPARTMENTS, TESTING THE RANGE OF THE APPROACH. AIM 1 WILL OPTIMIZE DEGRADER DESIGN AND DELIVERY PARAMETERS IN NEURONAL CULTURES. AIM 2 WILL VALIDATE THE SYSTEM’S ABILITY TO DELETE KEY INTRACELLULAR PROTEINS IN PRIMARY RETINAL GANGLION CELLS, ESTABLISHING FEASIBILITY IN A MODEL RELEVANT TO CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM INJURY.  SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION WILL YIELD A BROADLY APPLICABLE PLATFORM FOR MANIPULATING PROTEIN LEVELS IN NEURONS, PROVIDING THE NEUROSCIENCE COMMUNITY WITH A NEW CLASS OF MOLECULAR TOOLS THAT COMPLEMENT GENETIC APPROACHES TO STUDY THE CELLULAR BASIS OF NEURONAL FUNCTION, DEGENERATION, AND REPAIR.

recipient.name: THE TRUSTEES OF COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY IN THE CITY OF NEW YORK

description: METABOLIC PERTURBATIONS IN THE DEVELOPING ALBINO RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM - PROJECT SUMMARY  RETINAL GANGLION CELLS (RGCS) FROM EACH EYE EXTEND THEIR AXONS IPSI- AND CONTRALATERALLY TO THE BRAIN TO ESTABLISH THE CIRCUIT FOR BINOCULAR VISION. THE INAPPROPRIATE SIDEDNESS OF RGC PROJECTIONS IS DEBILITATING IN GENETIC DISORDERS SUCH AS ALBINISM, IN WHICH HYPOPIGMENTATION OF THE RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM (RPE) IS LINKED TO OPTIC NERVE MISROUTING AND ALTERED STEREO VISION. WE PREVIOUSLY IDENTIFIED TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATORS OF THE SPECIFICATION AND DIFFERENTIATION OF IPSI AND CONTRA RGCS, DEMONSTRATED THAT THE VENTRAL CILIARY MARGIN ZONE (CMZ) IS A SOURCE OF IPSI RGCS, AND POINTED TO THE CELL CYCLE REGULATOR CYCLIN D2 IN THE VENTRAL CMZ AS BEING CRUCIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF IPSI RGC CELL FATE. IN THE ALBINO RETINA, THESE PROCESSES AND THE CELLULAR INTEGRITY OF THE RPE IN THE ABSENCE OF MELANIN ARE DISRUPTED, MAKING THE ALBINO AN EXCELLENT COMPARATIVE MODEL FOR THE PROPOSED STUDIES: THE CMZ DISPLAYS COMPROMISED NEUROGENIC PROPERTIES INCLUDING AN EXTENDED G1 PERIOD DURING THE CELL CYCLE OF RETINAL PROGENITORS, AND DIMINISHED EXPRESSION OF CYCLIN D2, TOGETHER CAUSING REDUCED OUTPUT OF IPSI RGCS.  THE LINK BETWEEN THE PRESENCE OF MELANIN IN THE RPE IN PIGMENTED ORGANISMS AND PROPER DEVELOPMENT OF RGC PROJECTION REMAINS UNANSWERED. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT FACTORS IN THE RPE DIRECT THE CMZ AND NEURAL RETINA TOWARD THE PROPER BALANCE OF IPSI/CONTRA RGC FATES. SIGNALS FROM THE RPE THAT MAY NORMALLY REGULATE NEUROGENESIS AND THAT ARE MISSING OR DOWNREGULATED FROM THE ALBINO RPE OR ABERRANT SIGNALS THAT ARE UPREGULATED IN THE ALBINO RPE MAY CAUSE THE ALTERATIONS OF NEUROGENESIS AND, THUS, AN IMBALANCE IN THE IPSI VS CONTRA RGC POPULATIONS SEEN IN THE ALBINO. HERE WE WILL CHRONICLE THE WAYS IN WHICH THE DEVELOPING (EMBRYONIC) ALBINO RPE IS PERTURBED. WE WILL PURSUE OUR TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA INDICATING THAT MITOCHONDRIA ARE UNDER STRESS, AND CHRONICLE THESE PERTURBATIONS BY HIGH-RESOLUTION AND ELECTRON MICROSCOPY. WE WILL ALSO INTERROGATE METABOLIC AND CALCIUM DYNAMICS THAT ARE DYSREGULATED IN ALBINO V PIGMENTED RPE. THIS DISCOVERY-BASED EFFORT WILL SET THE STAGE FOR TREATING RPE WITH FACTORS THAT WILL ALLAY SUCH DYSFUNCTION IN VIVO AND IN VITRO, THAT COULD MODIFY RGC NEUROGENESIS TO ESTABLISH PROPER BINOCULAR CIRCUITRY. IMPACT: OUR STUDIES, FOR WHICH THE VISUAL SYSTEM IS SUPREMELY SUITED, WILL ILLUMINATE HOW NEURONAL DIFFERENTIATION PROGRAMS GOVERN AXON PROJECTION AND CONNECTIVITY IN THE NERVOUS SYSTEM. GENETIC DISORDERS SUCH AS ALBINISM INVOLVE INAPPROPRIATE SIDEDNESS OF RGC PROJECTIONS AND SERVE AS A MODEL FOR THESE STUDIES. AS BOTH ALBINISM AND DISORDERS IN THE MATURE EYE SUCH AS AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION (AMD) PRESENT RPE CELLULAR PATHOLOGY AND DISABLE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN RPE CELLS AND THE ADJACENT LAYER OF NEURAL RETINAL CELLS, THE PROPOSED WORK MAY SHED LIGHT ON THIS AND OTHER RETINAL DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CONTACTLESS ACTIVATION OF THE MECHANOSENSORY SYSTEM BY PHOTOACOUSTIC STIMULATION - ABSTRACT THE SOMATOSENSORY SYSTEM ENABLES PERCEPTION OF TOUCH, TEMPERATURE, PAIN, AND BODY POSITION, YET REMAINS DIFFICULT TO PROBE WITH THE SAME SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL PRECISION AVAILABLE IN RESEARCH ON THE VISUAL AND AUDITORY SYSTEMS. CURRENT METHODS FOR TACTILE STIMULATION—MECHANICAL ACTUATORS, VIBRATION MOTORS, OR ELECTRICAL STIMULATION—LACK SPATIAL RESOLUTION, REQUIRE CONTACT, OR PRODUCE DIFFUSE ACTIVATION. OPTOGENETICS OFFERS IMPROVED CONTROL BUT REQUIRES GENETIC MODIFICATION AND IS NOT BROADLY APPLICABLE. THIS PROJECT DEVELOPS A NEW METHOD BASED ON PHOTOACOUSTIC STIMULATION, IN WHICH PULSED LIGHT IS ABSORBED BY TISSUE OR DYE SENSITIZERS TO GENERATE LOCALIZED MECHANICAL FORCES THAT ACTIVATE ION CHANNELS. INITIAL STUDIES IN HUMANS DEMONSTRATE THAT SHORT PULSES OF RED OR INFRARED LIGHT CAN PRODUCE RELIABLE MECHANICAL PERCEPTS, SUGGESTING A NON-CONTACT, LABEL-FREE STRATEGY FOR SOMATOSENSORY STIMULATION. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE THIS APPROACH AS A GENERAL- PURPOSE TOOL FOR USE IN CELLS AND ANIMALS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL STIMULATE CULTURED CELLS EXPRESSING MECHANOSENSITIVE (PIEZO1/2) AND THERMOSENSITIVE (TRPV1–4) ION CHANNELS USING PULSED LIGHT, AND RECORD ACTIVATION USING CALCIUM IMAGING, FLUORESCENT ACTIVITY DYES, AND PATCH-CLAMP ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL EVALUATE BEHAVIORAL AND CORTICAL RESPONSES TO PHOTOACOUSTIC STIMULATION IN MICE, USING WIDEFIELD CALCIUM IMAGING AND VIBRATORY STIMULI AS A BENCHMARK. THE TEAM COMBINES EXPERTISE IN MATERIALS SCIENCE, ION CHANNEL BIOLOGY, AND SYSTEMS NEUROSCIENCE, AND IS CO-LOCATED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ROCHESTER. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL RESULT IN A SCALABLE, NON-INVASIVE TOOL FOR HIGH-RESOLUTION ACTIVATION OF SOMATOSENSORY STRUCTURES, ENABLING NEW STUDIES OF MECHANOTRANSDUCTION AND LAYING THE FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE APPLICATIONS IN HAPTIC PROSTHETICS AND NEUROMODULATION.

description: BIOFABRICATION OF LIVING VAGINAL GRAFTS - PROJECT SUMMARY THE VAGINA IS CENTRAL TO AN INDIVIDUAL’S SEXUALITY, SEXUAL HEALTH, BODY IMAGE, AND SENSE OF WELL-BEING. HOWEVER, BIOMATERIALS SPECIFICALLY ENGINEERED FOR RECONSTRUCTING THE VAGINA IN PROCEDURES SUCH AS VAGINOPLASTY, VAGINAL AUGMENTATION FOLLOWING CONGENITAL OR IATROGENIC SHORTENING, FISTULA REPAIR, AND UROGYNECOLOGIC PROCEDURES ARE SCARCE DUE TO A LACK OF RESEARCH. THIS IS PROBLEMATIC FOR BOTH PATIENTS AND THEIR SURGEONS. WITHIN A TISSUE, THE EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX (ECM), SPECIFIC TO EACH CELL TYPE, COMPRISES THE PRIMARY STRUCTURAL SUPPORT, REGULATES CELL GROWTH AND BEHAVIOR, AND PLAYS A KEY ROLE IN TISSUE HOMEOSTASIS. ECM COMPOSITION IS HIGHLY TISSUE-SPECIFIC— EXHIBITING DISTINCT BIOCHEMICAL, ARCHITECTURAL, AND MECHANICAL PROPERTIES TAILORED TO THE FUNCTIONAL DEMANDS OF A TISSUE. CURRENTLY, THERE ARE NO DEVICES THAT REPLICATE THE UNIQUE CELLULAR, BIOCHEMICAL AND BIOMECHANICAL CUES OF NATIVE VAGINAL ECM. TO ADDRESS THIS UNMET NEED, WE PROPOSE THAT TISSUE CONSTRUCTS FABRICATED FROM A SINGLE AUTOLOGOUS VAGINAL BIOPSY CONTAINING BOTH VAGINAL FIBROBLASTS AND SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS (SMC) ALONG WITH THEIR SPECIFIC ECM (V(FIBRO+SMC)-ECM) COULD SERVE AS A BIOMIMETIC GRAFT FOR VAGINAL RECONSTRUCTIVE APPLICATIONS THAT POSSESSES BOTH THE MECHANICAL PROPERTIES (FIBROBLASTS + ECM) AND CONTRACTILE PROPERTIES (SMC + ECM) TO FUNCTION LIKE HUMAN VAGINA. UNLIKE BIOSCAFFOLD-BASED SYSTEMS, WHICH INTRODUCE EXOGENOUS MATERIALS THAT CAN ALTER CELLULAR BEHAVIOR, WE USE A SCALABLE SCAFFOLD-FREE APPROACH THAT CREATES A MORE BIOMIMETIC MICROENVIRONMENT WHERE CELLULAR SELF-ORGANIZATION AND ECM DEPOSITION OCCUR NATURALLY, BETTER RECAPITULATING NATIVE VAGINAL TISSUE ARCHITECTURE AND FUNCTION. THE OVERALL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT AN AUTOLOGOUS LIVING GRAFT WILL BE ASSOCIATED WITH A MORE FAVORABLE OUTCOMES IN VAGINAL RECONSTRUCTIVE SURGERIES AS COMPARED TO A WIDELY USED XENOGRAFT ECM BIOSCAFFOLD. AUTOLOGOUS FIBROBLASTS AND SMCS WITHIN THEIR OWN CELL SPECIFIC ECM WILL AFFORD GRAFT STABILITY OVER TIME AS COMPARED TO THE MORE IMMUNOGENIC XENOGRAFT BIOSCAFFOLDS WHICH WILL RAPIDLY DEGRADE AND PRODUCE A CELL SPARSE PREDOMINANTLY COLLAGEN ECM. IN AIM 1 OF THE PROPOSAL, WE TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT AUTOLOGOUS V(FIBRO+SMC)-ECM GRAFTS CAN BE BIOFABRICATED FROM FIBROBLASTS AND SMCS DERIVED FROM A SINGLE FULL THICKNESS VAGINAL BIOPSY USING A SCAFFOLD FREE MICROMOLD TECHNOLOGY. OUR METRIC FOR A SUCCESSFUL OUTCOME IS THE BIOFABRICATION OF GRAFTS WITH SIMILAR COMPOSITIONAL AND FUNCTIONAL PROPERTIES TO NATIVE VAGINA. IN AIM 2, WE TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT AUTOLOGOUS V(FIBRO+SMC)-ECM GRAFTS AND GRAFTS WITH FIBROBLASTS ONLY V(FIBRO)-ECM WILL HAVE IMPROVED OUTCOMES 3 MONTHS AFTER IMPLANTATION BY VAGINOPLASTY AS COMPARED TO A CONVENTIONAL FIBROBLAST SEEDED XENOGRAFT BIOSCAFFOLD USING AN ESTABLISHED RABBIT MODEL. WE FURTHER TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT V(FIBRO+SMC)-ECM GRAFTS CONTAINING A SMOOTH MUSCLE COMPONENT WILL HAVE SUPERIOR FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES (VAGINAL CONTRACTILITY) AS COMPARED TO FIBROBLAST ONLY GRAFTS (V(FIBRO)-ECM). WE HAVE STRONG PRELIMINARY THAT SUPPORTS HIGH FEASIBILITY OF OUR PROPOSAL WHICH HAS THE POTENTIAL TO SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCE THE FIELD OF REGENERATIVE GYNECOLOGY AND IMPROVE OUTCOMES FOR THE MILLIONS OF WOMEN NEEDING RECONSTRUCTIVE VAGINAL SURGERY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: KINDERGARTEN READINESS ASSESSMENT SCORES AFTER HAVING EARLY-CHILDHOOD RESPIRATORY FAILURE (KRASHER) - UP TO 40% OF PEDIATRIC INTENSIVE CARE UNIT (PICU) PATIENTS ACQUIRE NEW MORBIDITIES DURING CRITICAL ILLNESS. RESEARCH INTO THEIR EXACT RATES, MECHANISMS AND TREATMENTS IS HAMPERED BY DIFFICULTY IN GETTING PICU SURVIVORS TO UNDERGO IN-PERSON TESTING YEARS LATER. OUR INNOVATIVE APPROACH IS TO USE THE RESULTS OF STANDARDIZED SCHOOL TESTING AS AN OBJECTIVE, PRACTICAL PICU OUTCOME MEASURE. WE ARE UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO DO THIS BECAUSE WE HAVE “KINDERGARTEN READINESS ASSESSMENT” (KRA) SCORES FROM 14 LOCAL SCHOOL DISTRICTS AVAILABLE IN OUR CHILD AND HOUSEHOLD INTEGRATED LONGITUDINAL DATA” (CHILD) SYSTEM, WHICH INTEGRATES DATA FROM ADMINISTRATIVE AGENCIES ACROSS OUR COUNTY. OUR OVERALL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT BENZODIAZEPINE SEDATIVES ARE A MODIFIABLE RISK FACTOR FOR POOR LONG-TERM PICU OUTCOMES. MOST PICU PATIENTS ON INVASIVE MECHANICAL VENTILATION (IMV) RECEIVE THESE DRUGS FOR DAYS TO WEEKS. THE IMPACT OF THESE PROLONGED EXPOSURES ON THE DEVELOPING BRAIN IS UNKNOWN, BUT EXPOSURE TO GENERAL ANESTHETICS – WHICH WORK THROUGH THE SAME RECEPTORS IN THE BRAIN – EARLY IN LIFE FOR EVEN A FEW HOURS IS ASSOCIATED WITH DECREASED SCHOOL PERFORMANCE. WE PUBLISHED A PILOT STUDY OF KRA SCORES OF CHILDREN WHO RECEIVED SEDATION WHILE ON IMV AT AGE <3YO. THESE PICU SURVIVORS (N=32) HAD LOWER RATES OF “ON-TRACK” KRA SCORES (22% VS 64%, P<0.001) AND 17-POINT LOWER TOTAL SCORES (P<0.001) VERSUS CONTROLS MATCHED ON PERTINENT SOCIO-ECONOMIC, DEMOGRAPHIC AND BIRTH DATA. NOW THAT WE HAVE ESTABLISHED PROOF-OF-CONCEPT FOR OUR APPROACH, WE WILL STUDY A LARGER COHORT IN ORDER TO ACHIEVE: AIM 1A) CONFIRM THAT PICU SURVIVORS WHO RECEIVED SEDATION DURING EARLY LIFE IMV HAVE UNFAVORABLE KRA SCORES COMPARED TO MATCHED CONTROLS. BASED ON OUR PILOT, WE ESTIMATE RETROSPECTIVELY IDENTIFYING 2000 PICU SURVIVORS WHO RECEIVED IMV WITH SEDATION AT AGE <3YO IN EITHER OF THE TWO LOCAL PICUS, OF WHOM 400 WILL HAVE KRA SCORES IN CHILD. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT PICU SURVIVORS’ KRA SCORES WILL BE LOWER THAN PROPENSITY SCORE-MATCHED CONTROLS FROM CHILD. AIM 1B) DETERMINE IF CUMULATIVE BENZODIAZEPINE EXPOSURE IS ASSOCIATED WITH UNFAVORABLE KRA SCORES. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT, AMONG PICU SURVIVORS WITH KRA DATA AVAILABLE, TOTAL BENZODIAZEPINE DOSAGE IN THE PICU WILL BE ASSOCIATED WITH WORSE KRA SCORES IN A MULTIVARIABLE MODEL INCLUDING CONFOUNDERS. AIM 2) LEVERAGE MACHINE LEARNING (ML) TO CONSTRUCT A PREDICTION MODEL THAT IDENTIFIES PICU SURVIVORS AT HIGH RISK OF HAVING KRA SCORES BELOW THE “ON TRACK” LEVEL. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT AN ML-BASED MODEL THAT INTEGRATES DATA ON SEDATION EXPOSURE AND PATIENT-SPECIFIC FACTORS WILL IDENTIFY CHILDREN AT INCREASED RISK OF UNFAVORABLE KRA SCORES. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL THUS 1) CONFIRM THAT SEDATION DURING EARLY LIFE IMV IN THE PICU IS ASSOCIATED WITH UNFAVORABLE COGNITIVE OUTCOMES AT SCHOOL ENTRY, 2) FURTHER THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTING THAT BENZODIAZEPINES ARE A MODIFIABLE RISK FACTOR FOR POOR OUTCOMES, AND 3) PROVIDE A NOVEL TOOL TO IDENTIFY PICU SURVIVORS MOST AT-RISK FOR UNFAVORABLE SCHOOL PERFORMANCE. THESE FINDINGS MAY HAVE IMMEDIATE CLINICAL IMPACT, AND ARE NEEDED TO PLAN SUBSEQUENT LARGER TRIALS DESIGNED TO IMPROVE COGNITIVE FUNCTION AT AGE 6YO.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PARENT-FACILITATED EARLY ORAL-SENSORY EXPERIENCE PROGRAM: ENHANCING NICU OUTCOMES THROUGH A FAMILY-CENTERED FEEDING APPROACH - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT PRETERM INFANTS (≤37 WEEKS GESTATIONAL AGE) ACCOUNT FOR 10% OF U.S. LIVE BIRTHS, BUT OVER 40% OF HOSPITAL-BASED INFANT CARE COSTS. A MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR TO PROLONGED HOSPITALIZATION IS DELAYED ORAL FEEDING SKILL DEVELOPMENT, WHICH INCREASES HEALTHCARE EXPENDITURES AND DELAYS FAMILY REUNIFICATION. APPROXIMATELY 42% OF PRETERM INFANTS EXPERIENCE PERSISTENT FEEDING DIFFICULTIES INTO CHILDHOOD, ADVERSELY AFFECTING GROWTH AND NEURODEVELOPMENT. EARLY INTERVENTION TO SUPPORT ORAL FEEDING IS THEREFORE CRITICAL. PARENTS OF PRETERM INFANTS ALSO EXPERIENCE HIGH LEVELS OF EMOTIONAL STRESS AND REDUCED PARENTING CONFIDENCE, WHICH CAN IMPAIR PARENT-INFANT INTERACTIONS AND CONTRIBUTE TO SUBOPTIMAL INFANT OUTCOMES. EARLY SENSORY EXPERIENCES—SUCH AS ADMINISTERING SMALL ORAL DROPLETS OF HUMAN MILK PRIOR TO GAVAGE FEEDING—HAVE DEMONSTRATED IMMUNOMODULATORY BENEFITS AND MAY PROMOTE FEEDING DEVELOPMENT. ENGAGING PARENTS IN THESE EARLY FEEDING INTERVENTIONS ADDRESSES A KEY GAP IN EARLY PARENTAL INVOLVEMENT IN NICU CARE, ENHANCES BONDING, PROMOTES RESPONSIVE CAREGIVING, AND SUPPORTS EMOTIONAL WELL- BEING. WE PROPOSE A PILOT STUDY TO ADAPT A PREVIOUSLY TESTED NURSE-DELIVERED INTERVENTION FOR PARENT DELIVERY USING A STRUCTURED COACHING MODEL GROUNDED IN GUIDED PARTICIPATION THEORY. THIS ADAPTED INTERVENTION, THE PARENT-FACILITATED EARLY ORAL-SENSORY EXPERIENCE (PEOE) PROGRAM WILL BE EVALUATED FOR FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY AND PRELIMINARY EFFECTS USING A QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL SEQUENTIAL COHORT DESIGN. SPECIFIC AIMS ARE TO: 1) EVALUATE THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF THE INTERVENTION, INCLUDING PARTICIPATION RATES, PARENT SATISFACTION, AND STUDY PROCEDURES (ELIGIBILITY SCREENING, RECRUITMENT, ENROLLMENT, AND RETENTION), AND EXPLORE INFANT AND PARENT CHARACTERISTICS THAT MAY INFLUENCE INTERVENTION DELIVERY; AND 2) CONDUCT PRELIMINARY ANALYSES TO ASSESS THE MAGNITUDE AND VARIABILITY OF INTERVENTION EFFECTS AND EVALUATE THE APPROPRIATENESS AND SENSITIVITY OF KEY OUTCOME MEASURES TO INFORM FUTURE TRIAL DESIGN. INFANT OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE WEEKLY SHORT-TERM PHYSIOLOGICAL RESPONSES DURING AND AFTER INTERVENTION SESSIONS (HEART RATE [HR], RESPIRATORY RATE [RR), OXYGEN SATURATION [SAO2], AND AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM [ANS] REGULATION), CAPTURED VIA BEDSIDE MONITORS. A SINGLE ORAL FEEDING OBSERVATION NEAR DISCHARGE WILL ASSESS INFANTS’ ABILITY TO REGULATE BOTH PHYSIOLOGIC (HR, RR, SAO2, ANS REGULATION) AND BEHAVIORAL RESPONSES (USING THE EARLY FEEDING SKILLS ASSESSMENT TOOL). ADDITIONAL DATA ON FEEDING SKILL DEVELOPMENT, GROWTH, AND HOSPITAL STAY WILL BE EXTRACTED FROM ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORDS. PARENT OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE THEIR ABILITY TO CO-REGULATE FEEDING, ASSESSED THROUGH CODED VIDEOTAPED FEEDINGS FROM A SINGLE OBSERVATION NEAR DISCHARGE. EMOTIONAL WELL-BEING AND PARENTING SELF-EFFICACY WILL BE MEASURED USING RELIABLE SELF-REPORT QUESTIONNAIRES AT ENROLLMENT, BIWEEKLY DURING THE NICU STAY, AND/OR AT DISCHARGE. DATA ANALYSIS WILL INCLUDE QUALITATIVE AND DESCRIPTIVE ANALYSES, AS WELL AS LINEAR MIXED-EFFECT MODELING. RESULTS WILL INFORM THE DESIGN OF A FUTURE MULTI-SITE CLINICAL TRIAL, SUPPORT INTERVENTION REFINEMENT, AND PROMOTE INTEGRATION OF THIS PARENT- DELIVERED INTERVENTION INTO STANDARD NICU CARE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MICRORNA MECHANISM OF ANGELMAN SYNDROME - PROJECT SUMMARY ANGELMAN SYNDROME (AS) IS A SEVERE NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY, MOTOR DYSFUNCTION, SLEEP DISTURBANCES, EEG ABNORMALITIES, AND EPILEPSY. DESPITE ITS SIGNIFICANT IMPACT, THERE IS CURRENTLY NO EFFECTIVE THERAPY FOR AS. EXISTING TREATMENTS PRIMARILY INVOLVE COMBINATIONS OF MEDICINES TO ALLEVIATE SOME OF THE MOST DEBILITATING SYMPTOMS. THERE REMAINS AN URGENT CLINICAL NEED TO IDENTIFY NOVEL MOLECULAR TARGETS THAT CAN CORRECT THE CORE PATHOLOGIES OF AS. MICRORNAS (MIRNAS) ARE ~22 NUCLEOTIDE-LONG NONCODING RNAS THAT NEGATIVELY REGULATE GENE EXPRESSION BY BINDING TO COMPLEMENTARY SITES IN THE 3’ UNTRANSLATED REGION OF TARGET MESSENGER RNAS. MIRNAS PLAY A SIGNIFICANT ROLE IN REGULATING GENE EXPRESSION AND HAVE BEEN IMPLICATED IN CONTROLLING FUNDAMENTAL NEURAL FUNCTIONS, INCLUDING NEUROGENESIS, NEURONAL MATURATION, SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY, AND EXCITATORY/INHIBITORY (E/I) BALANCE. DYSREGULATED MIRNA EXPRESSION IS INCREASINGLY IMPLICATED IN THE PATHOGENESIS OF VARIOUS NEUROLOGICAL AND NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS. WE RECENTLY CONDUCTED AN UNBIASED GENOME-WIDE MIRNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS USING HIPPOCAMPAL TISSUE COLLECTED FROM ADULT AS MODEL MICE AND THEIR WILD-TYPE (WT) LITTERMATE CONTROLS. WE IDENTIFIED A NOVEL CLUSTER OF MIRNAS, MIR-183/96/182, SIGNIFICANTLY DOWNREGULATED IN AS MICE COMPARED TO WT CONTROLS. IMPORTANTLY, TREATMENT WITH CANNABIDIOL, KNOWN TO AMELIORATE MULTIPLE PATHOLOGIES IN AS ANIMAL MODELS AND INDIVIDUALS WITH AS, REVERSED THE DOWNREGULATION OF MIR-183 AND MIR-96, AMONG OTHERS, IN AS MODEL MICE. THE PIVOTAL ROLE OF MIR- 183/96/182 IN REGULATING NEURITE OUTGROWTH, MEMORY FORMATION, AND CIRCADIAN RHYTHMS SUGGESTS ITS POTENTIAL INVOLVEMENT IN AS PATHOGENESIS. OUR STUDY AIMS TO TREAT CORE AS PATHOLOGIES BY TARGETING MIR-183/96/182. WE WILL TEST OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT MIR-183/96/182 AUGMENTATION CAN ALLEVIATE AS-ASSOCIATED PATHOLOGIES AND FUNCTIONAL ALTERATIONS IN BOTH MOUSE MODELS AND HUMAN CORTICAL ORGANOIDS (HCOS). IN AIM 1, WE WILL PROFILE THE DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION OF MIR-183/96/182 IN MOUSE BRAINS AND ASSESS THE EFFECTS OF MIR-183/96/182 AUGMENTATION ON BEHAVIORAL IMPAIRMENTS, EEG ABNORMALITIES, AND EPILEPTIC PHENOTYPES IN AS MODEL MICE. WE WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE MOLECULAR TARGETS OF MIR-183/96/182 IN REGULATING AS PHENOTYPES. WE WILL FIRST FOCUS ON CACNB4, WHICH MIRDB PREDICTS AS THE TOP BIOLOGICALLY PLAUSIBLE DIRECT TARGET WITH BINDING SITES FOR MIR- 183/96/182. TO FURTHER EVALUATE THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL OF THIS APPROACH, IN AIM 2, WE WILL VALIDATE THE DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION OF MIR-183/96/182 USING AS PATIENTS' IPSCS-DERIVED HCOS AND TEST THE EFFECTS OF MIR- 183/96/182 AUGMENTATION ON CORTICAL NEURONAL GENERATION AND ALTERED NEURAL PROPERTIES IN UBE3A-DEFICIENT ORGANOIDS. COMPLETING THIS STUDY WILL SHED LIGHT ON MIRNA MECHANISMS OF AS PATHOLOGY AND IDENTIFY MIR- 183/96/182 AUGMENTATION AS A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC APPROACH FOR AS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE VALIDITY OF THE SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY ALGORITHM. - IN MANY COUNTRIES ACROSS THE GLOBE, INCLUDING THE US, MATERNAL MORTALITY IS A LEADING HEALTH INDICATOR. AS THE RISK OF MATERNAL DEATH IS DECLINING IN MANY PARTS OF THE WORLD, IT IS ON THE RISE IN THE US, EVEN AS WE BOAST THE HIGHEST LEVEL OF HEALTH CARE EXPENDITURE AMONG WEALTHY NATIONS. THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR CLINICAL AND POLICY- LEVEL RESPONSE TARGETING FACTORS THAT PUT WOMEN AT RISK OF MATERNAL DEATH. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY STRUCTURAL CHANGE REQUIRED TO PROMOTE MATERNAL HEALTH AND MAXIMIZE THE HEALTH STATUS OF ALL REPRODUCTIVE AGE WOMEN. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS APPLICATION IS TO DETERMINE THE VALIDITY OF THE CENTERS OF DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION (CDC)-DEVELOPED SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY ALGORITHM FOR THE IDENTIFICATION OF MATERNAL NEAR- MISS CASES IN THE OBSTETRIC POPULATION OF BOSTON MEDICAL CENTER, THE LARGEST SAFETY-NET HOSPITAL IN NEW ENGLAND. THE HYPOTHESIS IS THAT THE CDC-DEVELOPED SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY ALGORITHM WILL HAVE LOW- TO MODERATE-SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY AND LOW PREDICTIVE VALUE AS IT PERTAINS TO MATERNAL NEAR-MISS. ADDITIONALLY, WE EXPECT TO IDENTIFY DIFFERENCES IN THE SUBGROUPS (DEMOGRAPHIC, SOCIOECONOMIC, HEALTH HISTORY) AT RISK FOR SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY VERSUS MATERNAL NEAR-MISS. THE RATIONALE FOR THIS PROJECT IS THAT DESPITE WIDE-SPREAD ADOPTION OF THE CDC-DEVELOPED SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY ALGORITHM IT IS UNCLEAR WHETHER SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY (PER THIS MEASURE) IS AN ADEQUATE PROXY FOR MATERNAL NEAR-MISS (NEAR DEATH MATERNAL COMPLICATIONS) SUCH THAT INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY COULD BE EXPECTED TO REDUCE THE RISK OF MATERNAL DEATH. TO DATE, WE LACK RIGOROUS VALIDATION STUDIES OF THIS TOPIC. WE PROPOSE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) EVALUATE THE VALIDITY OF SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY AS A PROXY FOR MATERNAL NEAR-MISS; AND 2) COMPARE RISK FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH MATERNAL NEAR-MISS AND SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY. THE RESEARCH PROPOSED IN THIS APPLICATION IS INNOVATIVE IN THAT IT INTERROGATES AN OTHERWISE WIDELY ACCEPTED MEASURE OF MATERNAL MORBIDITY; AND, TO OUR KNOWLEDGE, IS THE FIRST APPLICATION OF THE WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION MATERNAL NEAR-MISS APPROACH. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE WE EXPECT THAT THE FINDINGS WILL ASSESS THE VALIDITY OF THE WIDELY ADOPTED SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY ALGORITHM, THE CURRENT BENCHMARK FOR ONE OF THE DHHS HEALTHY PEOPLE 2030 GOALS (MICH-05 REDUCE SEVERE MATERNAL COMPLICATIONS IDENTIFIED DURING DELIVERY HOSPITALIZATIONS). THE PROJECT HAS HIGH POTENTIAL FOR PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT AS THE RESULTS WILL INFORM: 1) THE POLICY DECISIONS OF THE LARGEST SAFETY-NET HOSPITAL IN MASSACHUSETTS, AND 2) THE NATIONAL PREGNANCY AND CHILDBIRTH BENCHMARKS (I.E., HEALTHY PEOPLE) FOR WOMEN’S HEALTH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A UNIQUE EXPLORATION OF DEVELOPMENTAL LANGUAGE DISORDER - ABSTRACT A UNIQUE EXPLORATION OF DEVELOPMENTAL LANGUAGE DISORDER  GIVEN WIDE VARIABILITY IN THE ONSET OF LANGUAGE DEVELOPMENT, WE ASK A FUNDAMENTAL QUESTION: HOW CAN WE PREDICT WHICH CHILDREN ARE AT RISK FOR DEVELOPMENTAL LANGUAGE DELAY (DLD)? THE US PREVENTIVE SERVICES TASK FORCE (2006) STATED THAT, “SPEECH AND LANGUAGE DELAY AFFECTS 5% TO 8% OF PRESCHOOL CHILDREN, OFTEN PERSISTS INTO THE SCHOOL YEARS, AND MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH LOWERED SCHOOL PERFORMANCE AND PSYCHOSOCIAL PROBLEMS” (P. 497). HISTORICALLY DLD HAS BEEN DIAGNOSED BY NOTING THAT CHILDREN POSSESSED FEWER VOCABULARY WORDS (AND FEWER WORD COMBINATIONS) THAN THEIR PEERS. WHILE PROBLEMS IN LANGUAGE COMPREHENSION LIKELY ACCOMPANIED DLD, THERE WAS NO INSTRUMENT TO TEST OBSTREPEROUS YOUNG CHILDREN.  THIS UNIQUE PROPOSAL EXAMINES POSSIBLE RISK FOR DLD BY USING DATA FROM DELAYED LANGUAGE COMPREHENSION. THE OUTSTANDING PROJECT TEAM: 1) INVESTIGATES DELAY IN LANGUAGE COMPREHENSION, WHICH IS POTENTIALLY MORE INDICATIVE OF DEEPER LANGUAGE PROBLEMS THAN EXPRESSION; 2) MOVES BEYOND WORD COUNTS, BY EXAMINING HOW SYNTAX AND LANGUAGE LEARNING PROCESSES ARE IMPLICATED IN LANGUAGE DELAY; AND 3) EXPLORES REACTION TIME (AS WELL AS ACCURACY) TO SEARCH FOR SPECIFIC AREAS OF PROCESSING DELAY.  WE EXPLORE DATA GENERATED FROM THE NORMING OF TWO, RELATED INNOVATIVE LANGUAGE SCREENERS CREATED BY THE PI AND CONSULTANTS: THE QUICK INTERACTIVE LANGUAGE SCREENER (QUILS) FOR CHILDREN 3 TO 7 YEARS AND THE QUILS:TOD FOR CHILDREN FROM 2 TO 3 YEARS. THESE SCREENERS ARE EVIDENCE-BASED, STATE-OF THE-ART, AND AUTOMATICALLY ADMINISTERED AND SCORED. THEY ARE RELIABLE AND VALID AND CRUCIALLY, CONTAIN MORE THAN JUST VOCABULARY ITEMS: THEY TEST FOR GRAMMATICAL KNOWLEDGE AND THE ABILITY TO RAPIDLY LEARN NEW LANGUAGE ITEMS. BOTH SCREENERS COVER THE SAME THREE AREAS BUT WITH DIFFERENT ITEMS ENABLING US TO IDENTIFY WHETHER PROBLEMS DIFFER ACROSS AGES AND WHETHER DISTINCT PROFILES OF SLOW LANGUAGE LEARNERS EMERGE. HUNDREDS OF PARTICIPANTS ARE AVAILABLE FOR US TO SEARCH FOR PATTERNS THAT CHARACTERIZE CHILDREN WITH DELAYED COMPREHENSION, TO SEE WHETHER CHILDREN WHO SCORE POORLY ALSO HAVE RELATIVELY SLOWER REACTION TIMES IN SOME AREAS ON THE SCREENERS, AND TO MINE LARGE LONGITUDINAL SAMPLES (BETWEEN AGE 2 AND 3 AND BETWEEN AGE 3 AND 4) FOR WHETHER PREDICTIONS BEAR OUT ABOUT PERSISTENT DELAYS IN LANGUAGE COMPREHENSION. THE SCREENERS MAY DISTINGUISH BETWEEN CHILDREN AT RISK FOR DLD AND TYPICAL CHILDREN AFTER THE APPLICATION OF SOPHISTICATED METHODOLOGICAL ANALYSES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GUT MICROBIOME MECHANISMS OF MULTISENSORY SENSITIVITY IN PRIMARY DYSMENORRHEA - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT MENSTRUAL PAIN IS THE MOST COMMON GYNECOLOGICAL CONDITION, WITH RECENT PREVALENCE RATES ESTIMATED AT 71.1% FOR ADOLESCENT GIRLS AND YOUNG WOMEN. PRIMARY DYSMENORRHEA (PD; MENSTRUAL PAIN WITH NO IDENTIFIED PATHOLOGY) HAS A DIRECT IMPACT ON FUNCTIONING, PARTICULARLY IN ADOLESCENTS, CAUSING IMPAIRMENT IN MANY LIFE ACTIVITIES, INCLUDING SCHOOL, WORK, AND SOCIAL ACTIVITIES. MENSTRUAL PAIN IS ALSO A KNOWN RISK FACTOR FOR CHRONIC PAIN, BUT FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS TRANSITION ARE STILL POORLY UNDERSTOOD. RESEARCH HAS MOSTLY FOCUSED ON THE ROLE OF CENTRAL SENSITIZATION OF PAIN, ALTHOUGH EMERGING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS PD IS ASSOCIATED WITH SENSITIVITY TO NON-PAINFUL SENSORY MODALITIES (E.G., VISUAL, AUDITORY, TACTILE, AND VISCERAL) AS WELL, KNOWN AS MULTISENSORY SENSITIVITY (MSS), SUGGESTING SYSTEMIC ALTERATIONS IN HOW SENSORY STIMULI ARE PROCESSED. AN EXTENSIVE BODY OF RESEARCH HAS SHOWN THAT ALTERATIONS IN THE GUT MICROBIOME PLAY A KEY, CAUSAL ROLE IN VARIOUS CHRONIC PAIN SYNDROMES AS WELL AS CONTRIBUTE TO HEIGHTENED VISCERAL AND SENSORY PERCEPTION AND SENSITIVITY. THIS SUGGESTS THAT GUT MICROBIOME COMPOSITION CONTRIBUTES TO MSS AND THE EXPERIENCE OF PAIN, ALTHOUGH IT HAS NOT BEEN EXAMINED IN RELATION SPECIFICALLY IN THE CONTEXT OF PD. THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL EVALUATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN GUT MICROBIOME COMPOSITION, MSS, AND THE EXPERIENCE OF PAIN IN ADOLESCENT GIRLS, AGES 13-19, WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE PRIMARY DYSMENORRHEA. MEASURES OF PAIN (MENSTRUAL PAIN SEVERITY, MENSTRUAL PAIN INTERFERENCE, AND BODY PAIN), MSS (EVALUATED USING A COMPREHENSIVE BATTERY OF QUANTITATIVE MULTISENSORY TESTING PARADIGMS TO DETERMINE PAIN, VISUAL, AUDITORY, TACTILE, AND VISCERAL SENSITIVITIES), AND GUT MICROBIOME COMPOSITION (OBTAINED FROM A SINGLE STOOL SAMPLE) WILL BE COLLECTED. IN THIS STUDY, WE AIM TO CHARACTERIZE HOW GUT MICROBIOME COMPOSITION IS RELATED TO EACH PAIN AND MSS IN ADOLESCENTS WITH PRIMARY DYSMENORRHEA. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT GUT MICROBIOME COMPOSITION (SPECIFICALLY DIVERSITY, FUNCTIONAL PROFILE, AND LOWER ABUNDANCY OF LACTOBACILLUS) WILL BE ASSOCIATED WITH HIGHER PAIN AND HIGHER MSS. FINDINGS FROM THE STUDY HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF RISK FACTORS FOR CHRONIC PAIN, AS WELL AS SET THE STAGE FOR FUTURE RESEARCH TO EXPLORE THE TRAJECTORIES OF GUT MICROBIOME, PAIN, AND MSS OVER TIME TO ULTIMATELY DEVELOP NEW TREATMENT APPROACHES FOCUSED ON REDUCING SENSORY SENSITIVITY AND INTERVENTIONS TO ALTER GUT MICROBIOME COMPOSITION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INDUCIBLE GENE DOSAGE CORRECTION IN DOWN SYNDROME ORGANOID AND RODENT MODELS CARRYING HUMAN CHROMOSOME 21 - PROJECT SUMMARY TRISOMY (T21) OF HUMAN CHROMOSOME 21 (HSA21) IS THE MOST FREQUENT VIABLE ANEUPLOIDY IN HUMANS, WITH ANNUALLY ~6000 LIVE BIRTHS IN THE US. INCREASED HSA21 GENE DOSAGE AFFECTS DEVELOPMENT TO CAUSE DOWN SYNDROME (DS), WHICH SPANS CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE, IMMUNODEFICIENCY, AND INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY. COMPOUNDING THIS CONGENITAL BURDEN OVER THE LIFESPAN, CHILDREN WITH DS ARE PREDISPOSED TO LEUKEMIA, SHOW ELEVATED OXIDATIVE STRESS AND ACCELERATED AGING AS ADOLESCENTS, AND OFTEN DEVELOP ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) BY MIDDLE AGE. GIVEN THE LARGE NUMBER OF HSA21 GENES, IT HAS BEEN DIFFICULT TO ATTRIBUTE ANY OF THE CONGENITAL OR AGE-RELATED CONDITIONS TO INCREASED COPY-NUMBER OF SPECIFIC GENES.  BECAUSE INCREASED DOSAGE OF MULTIPLE GENES CAN SYNERGISTICALLY CONTRIBUTE TO PHENOTYPES, TRADITIONAL MOLECULAR-GENETIC APPROACHES HAVE BEEN SLOW TO ELUCIDATE HOW DS ALTERS DEVELOPMENT AND FORESHADOWS NEURODEGENERATIVE CHANGES LATER IN LIFE. IT IS UNCLEAR WHICH PHENOTYPES AT THE CELLULAR OR ORGANISMAL LEVEL MAY STILL AMENABLE TO THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION AFTER DEVELOPMENT COMPLETES, NOR WHICH TARGETS, PATHWAYS AND CELL TYPES WOULD BE MOST SUITED FOR SUCH THERAPIES.  WE RECENTLY REPORTED AN INDUCIBLE SYSTEM TO SILENCE ONE COPY OF HSA21 USING XIST, THE LONG NON-CODING RNA THAT IS ENDOGENOUSLY EXPRESSED FROM AND SILENCES THE INACTIVE X IN FEMALES. OUR XIST TRANSGENE REPRESSES GENES ACROSS HSA21, NOT ONLY IN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS (IPSCS) BUT ALSO IN IPSC-DERIVED AND POST-MITOTIC NEURONS AND ASTROCYTES, WHICH ENABLED US TO ASSESS REVERSIBLE TRANSCRIPTOMIC PHENOTYPES OF T21 IN TERMINAL CELL TYPES FOR THE VERY FIRST TIME. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE DEPLOY THIS SYSTEM AS A “DEVELOPMENTAL SCALPEL” TO: (AIM 1) USE BRAIN-REGION SPECIFIC ORGANOIDS TO DELINEATE DEVELOPMENTAL WINDOWS FOR POSSIBLE INTERVENTION AND DETERMINE ITS BENEFITS ON NEURONAL ACTIVITY, AND (AIM 2) EXPLOIT RECENT ADVANCES IN CHROMOSOME ENGINEERING TO GENERATE RAT EMBRYONIC STEM CELLS THAT CARRY THIS HSA21-XIST CHROMOSOME. OUR ULTIMATE GOAL IS TO CREATE A NEW DS RODENT MODEL THAT WOULD ALLOW SILENCING HSA21, PAVING THE WAY TO DETERMINING THE DEVELOPMENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL OUTCOMES OF PRE- AND POSTNATAL GENE DOSAGE CORRECTION. IN SUMMARY, OUR WORK AIMS TO DEFINE THE “BEST CASE” SCENARIO FOR NOVEL THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES TO DS, AND TO DETERMINE BY WHEN, DURING OR AFTER DEVELOPMENT, DELIVERABLE INTERVENTIONS NEED TO BE DEPLOYED.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PERSONALIZED PREDICTION OF HER2-INDUCED CARDIOVASCULAR ADVERSE EVENTS IN PATIENTS WITH BREAST CANCER USING ROBUST AI AND MACHINE LEARNING MODELS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT BREAST CANCER IS THE MOST COMMON CANCER AND THE SECOND LEADING CAUSE OF CANCER-RELATED DEATHS AMONG U.S. WOMEN, DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTING THOSE AGED 65 AND OLDER, WHO ACCOUNT FOR 45% OF CASES. APPROXIMATELY 25% OF BREAST CANCERS ARE HER2-POSITIVE, AN AGGRESSIVE SUBTYPE WITH A HIGHER RECURRENCE RISK. WHILE HER2-TARGETED THERAPIES (E.G., TRASTUZUMAB) HAVE SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVED SURVIVAL, THEY ALSO POSE A SUBSTANTIAL RISK OF CARDIOTOXICITY, PARTICULARLY AMONG OLDER ADULTS WITH PRE-EXISTING CARDIOVASCULAR (CV) RISK FACTORS. NOTABLY, CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD) HAS SURPASSED CANCER AS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH IN BREAST CANCER SURVIVORS AGED 65 AND OLDER. EXISTING PREDICTIVE MODELS FOR CV ADVERSE EVENTS DEMONSTRATE SUBOPTIMAL PERFORMANCE AND INCONSISTENCY ACROSS PATIENT POPULATIONS. THESE LIMITATIONS STEM FROM THE EXCLUSION OF CRITICAL CLINICAL AND DEMOGRAPHIC FACTORS, SUCH AS THE COMPLEX COMORBIDITY PROFILES OF OLDER WOMEN AND THE OMISSION OF AREA-LEVEL HEALTHCARE INFRASTRUCTURE VARIABLES THAT INFLUENCE BOTH CVD AND BREAST CANCER OUTCOMES. ACCORDINGLY, MORE ACCURATE PREDICTION MODELS ARE NEEDED THAT INTEGRATE A BROADER RANGE OF INDIVIDUAL- AND AREA-LEVEL FACTORS, ENSURING ROBUST PERFORMANCE ACROSS DIVERSE PATIENT POPULATIONS. WITHOUT SUCH MODELS, TREATMENT DECISIONS MAY REMAIN SUBOPTIMAL, LEADING TO PREVENTABLE ADVERSE OUTCOMES IN OLDER WOMEN UNDERGOING HER2-TARGETED THERAPY. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO REDUCE CV MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY AMONG OLDER WOMEN RECEIVING HER2-TARGETED THERAPY. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IMPROVE CV SAFETY BY IDENTIFYING HIGH-RISK PATIENTS AND INCORPORATING AREA-LEVEL FACTORS INTO RISK ASSESSMENT. TO ACHIEVE THIS, WE WILL CONDUCT A COHORT STUDY USING 2011-2022 SURVEILLANCE, EPIDEMIOLOGY, AND END RESULTS (SEER)-MEDICARE DATA LINKED WITH THE AMERICAN COMMUNITY SURVEY, INTEGRATING INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL CANCER DIAGNOSES, TREATMENTS, AND DEMOGRAPHICS WITH AREA-LEVEL FACTORS TO ENHANCE CV RISK ASSESSMENT. OUR FIRST SPECIFIC AIM IS TO EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF AREA-LEVEL FACTORS ON CV ADVERSE EVENTS IN OLDER WOMEN WITH HER2-POSITIVE BREAST CANCER BY APPLYING A CAUSAL INFERENCE FRAMEWORK INTEGRATED WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MACHINE LEARNING (AI/ML) METHODS. WE WILL USE PROPENSITY SCORE MATCHING AND AI/ML MODELING TO COMPARE HIGH- AND LOW-RISK AREA-LEVEL GROUPS AND IDENTIFY HIGH-RISK PATIENT SUBGROUPS THROUGH OPTIMAL CLASSIFICATION TREES. OUR SECOND SPECIFIC AIM IS TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE AN AI/ML-BASED PREDICTIVE MODEL FOR CV RISK ASSESSMENT BY CONSTRUCTING LANDMARK DATASETS THAT TRACK PATIENT DATA OVER TIME. THE MODEL WILL INCORPORATE A REWEIGHTING METHOD AND LEVERAGE THE TREE-BASED ALGORITHM TO ENHANCE ROBUSTNESS. ITS PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE AND CLINICAL UTILITY WILL BE RIGOROUSLY EVALUATED TO ENSURE ACCURATE RISK STRATIFICATION AND APPLICABILITY IN CLINICAL SETTINGS. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS STUDY WILL CLARIFY HOW INDIVIDUAL- AND AREA-LEVEL FACTORS INFLUENCE CV ADVERSE EVENTS IN OLDER WOMEN RECEIVING HER2-TARGETED THERAPY. IT WILL GENERATE A ROBUST PREDICTIVE MODEL FOR IDENTIFYING HIGH-RISK PATIENTS AND ENABLING PERSONALIZED RISK ASSESSMENT, ULTIMATELY REDUCING CV MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY WHILE IMPROVING TREATMENT DECISION-MAKING IN CARDIO-ONCOLOGY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SPARTACUS: STROKE PREVENTION WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND RISK TARGETING IN ANTICOAGULATED CARE FOR UNIQUE SOLUTIONS - SUMMARY/ABSTRACT STROKE REMAINS A DEVASTATING COMPLICATION FOR PATIENTS WITH ATRIAL FIBRILLATION (AF), EVEN WHEN THEY ARE TAKING BLOOD-THINNING MEDICATIONS. CURRENT METHODS TO PREDICT WHICH PATIENTS MIGHT STILL HAVE A STROKE WHILE ON THESE MEDICATIONS ARE LIMITED, MAKING IT DIFFICULT FOR DOCTORS TO IDENTIFY WHO NEEDS ADDITIONAL PREVENTIVE TREATMENTS. THE SPARTACUS PROJECT AIMS TO SOLVE THIS PROBLEM BY CREATING A NEW ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) TOOL THAT CAN BETTER PREDICT STROKE RISK IN AF PATIENTS ALREADY TAKING BLOOD THINNERS. OUR APPROACH WILL COMBINE DIFFERENT TYPES OF MEDICAL INFORMATION - INCLUDING HEART ULTRASOUNDS, HEART RHYTHM RECORDINGS, LABORATORY TESTS, AND PATIENT HEALTH RECORDS - TO CREATE A MORE COMPLETE PICTURE OF EACH PATIENT'S RISK. WE WILL DEVELOP AN ADVANCED AI SYSTEM CALLED MIST-MAMBA THAT CAN PROCESS ALL THIS INFORMATION TOGETHER AND IDENTIFY SUBTLE PATTERNS THAT MIGHT INDICATE HIGHER STROKE RISK. THIS SYSTEM WILL BE TESTED USING DATA FROM 2,000 PATIENTS ACROSS MULTIPLE MEDICAL CENTERS TO ENSURE IT WORKS RELIABLY. THE PROJECT HAS TWO MAIN AIMS: FIRST, TO DEVELOP THE AI SYSTEM THAT CAN HANDLE MULTIPLE TYPES OF MEDICAL DATA SIMULTANEOUSLY, AND SECOND, TO VALIDATE ITS ACCURACY IN PREDICTING STROKE RISK. WE EXPECT OUR SYSTEM TO BE AT LEAST 80% ACCURATE IN IDENTIFYING HIGH-RISK PATIENTS, WHICH WOULD BE A SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENT OVER CURRENT METHODS. IF SUCCESSFUL, SPARTACUS COULD HELP DOCTORS BETTER IDENTIFY WHICH AF PATIENTS NEED ADDITIONAL PREVENTIVE TREATMENTS BEYOND STANDARD BLOOD THINNERS, POTENTIALLY PREVENTING THOUSANDS OF STROKES AND IMPROVING PATIENT CARE. THIS WORK BRINGS TOGETHER EXPERTS IN CARDIOLOGY, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, MEDICAL IMAGING, AND STATISTICS TO TACKLE THIS IMPORTANT HEALTHCARE CHALLENGE. OUR PROJECT ALIGNS WITH NATIONAL HEALTH INITIATIVES (NHLBI'S NOT-HL-21-037) TO IMPROVE HEART DISEASE OUTCOMES THROUGH INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEEP LEARNING OF SNORING TO PREDICT COLLAPSE SITE, TREATMENT OUTCOMES, AND ITS CLINICAL TRANSLATION IN OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEA - ABSTRACT: CONTINUOUS POSITIVE AIRWAY PRESSURE (CPAP) IS AN EFFECTIVE TREATMENT FOR OSA, IN WHICH THE PATIENT MUST WEAR  AN OXYGEN MASK EVERY NIGHT. DUE TO DISCOMFORT, ONLY 30–50% OF PATIENTS CAN TOLERATE CPAP. ALTERNATIVES TO  CPAP ARE AVAILABLE, SUCH AS MANDIBULAR ADVANCEMENT DEVICES (MAD), HYPOGLOSSAL NERVE STIMULATION (HGNS),  PHARYNGEAL SURGERY, AND POSITIONAL THERAPY. THE SUCCESS OF THESE TREATMENTS OFTEN DEPENDS ON THE SITE OF UA  OBSTRUCTION. FOR EXAMPLE, HGNS THERAPY ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATES TONGUE MUSCLES. THE ELIGIBILITY TO GET HGNS  TREATMENT REQUIRES RULING OUT OF COLLAPSE OF THE SOFT PALATE, AS PATIENTS WITH THIS COLLAPSE PATTERN RESPOND POORLY  TO HGNS. THUS, IT IS CLEAR THAT TREATMENTS ARE HIGHLY SITE-OF-COLLAPSE SPECIFIC.  THE PRIMARY SITE OF COLLAPSE IS CATEGORIZED USING THE VOTE CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM, WHICH DENOTES THE VELUM (V),  LATERAL PHARYNGEAL WALLS (O), TONGUE BASE (T), AND EPIGLOTTIS (E). DRUG-INDUCED SLEEP ENDOSCOPY (DISE) IS THE  GOLD STANDARD FOR DETERMINING VOTE, WHERE AN ENDOSCOPE IS USED WHILE THE PATIENT IS UNDER SEDATION TO VISUALIZE  WHERE THE COLLAPSE OCCURS. DUE TO ITS INVASIVENESS AND HIGH COST, DISE IS UNAVAILABLE TO MOST PATIENTS.  THEREFORE, THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR A WIDELY ACCESSIBLE, NON-INVASIVE BIOMARKER THAT CAN PHENOTYPE THE AIRWAY  AND GUIDE PERSONALIZED THERAPY.  SNORING CAN SERVE AS SUCH A BIOMARKER, AS THE ACOUSTIC FEATURES OF SNORES CAN REFLECT THE STRUCTURES THAT VIBRATE  DURING UA OBSTRUCTION. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF THIS PROJECT IS THAT DEEP LEARNING MODELS CAN EXTRACT THESE  ACOUSTIC SIGNATURES FROM SNORING TO IDENTIFY THE ANATOMICAL SITE OF COLLAPSE AND PREDICT TREATMENT OUTCOMES. THIS  WORK REPRESENTS A SECONDARY ANALYSIS OF EXISTING, CLINICALLY COLLECTED DATASETS THAT INCLUDE SYNCHRONIZED SNORING,  DISE, AND SLEEP-RECORDING DATA.  WE PROPOSE A THREE-PART STRATEGY TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS. AIM 1 WILL DEVELOP DEEP LEARNING ARCHITECTURES THAT  COMBINE HANDCRAFTED ACOUSTIC FEATURES, SELF-SUPERVISED SPEECH EMBEDDINGS, AND SPECTROGRAM-BASED MODELS TO  CLASSIFY THE SITE OF COLLAPSE FROM DISE SNORING RECORDINGS. AIM 2 WILL EXTEND THE FRAMEWORK TO PREDICT HGNS  TREATMENT RESPONSE USING PRE-TREATMENT SNORE RECORDINGS. AIM 3 WILL SYSTEMATICALLY EVALUATE HOW MUCH SNORE  SAMPLING FREQUENCY IS NEEDED FOR RELIABLE CLASSIFICATION AND VALIDATE THE MODELS USING ROUTINE POLYSOMNOGRAPHY  (PSG) SNORE SENSORS.  SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A SCALABLE, NON-INVASIVE SNORE-BASED BIOMARKER FOR IDENTIFYING  UA COLLAPSE SITES AND PREDICTING TREATMENT RESPONSIVENESS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADVANCING SHARED DECISION MAKING FOR STROKE PREVENTION IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION: A META-ANALYSIS OF RANDOMIZED TRIALS OF DECISION AIDS - PROJECT ABSTRACT ATRIAL FIBRILLATION AFFECTS MORE THAN 10 MILLION AMERICANS AND IS A MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR TO STROKE, HEART FAILURE, AND PREMATURE DEATH. WHILE ORAL ANTICOAGULATION CAN REDUCE STROKE RISK BY UP TO 70%, MANY PATIENTS WITH ATRIAL FIBRILLATION ARE EITHER UNDERTREATED OR RECEIVE CARE THAT IS NOT CONCORDANT WITH THEIR VALUES AND PREFERENCES. SHARED DECISION MAKING IS A CORNERSTONE OF PATIENT-CENTERED CARE AND IS STRONGLY RECOMMENDED IN NATIONAL GUIDELINES FOR ATRIAL FIBRILLATION MANAGEMENT. DECISION AIDS—TOOLS DESIGNED TO SUPPORT SHARED DECISION MAKING BY HELPING PATIENTS UNDERSTAND THEIR OPTIONS AND PARTICIPATE IN DECISIONS—HAVE SHOWN PROMISE IN IMPROVING DECISION QUALITY AND ALIGNING TREATMENT WITH PATIENT GOALS. DESPITE THIS, CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAPS REMAIN. EXISTING STUDIES OF DECISION AIDS IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION VARY IN DESIGN, TYPE OF DECISION AIDS (CLINICIAN- VS. PATIENT-FOCUSED), POPULATIONS, AND OUTCOMES, LIMITING OUR ABILITY TO DRAW GENERALIZABLE CONCLUSIONS. THE RESEARCH PROPOSED IN THIS APPLICATION WILL ADDRESS THIS GAP THROUGH THE FIRST ANALYSIS OF COMBINED DATA FROM THREE LARGE RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS (RCTS) EVALUATING DECISION AIDS FOR STROKE PREVENTION IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION. TOGETHER, THESE TRIALS REPRESENT THE LARGEST BODY OF EVIDENCE ON SHARED DECISION MAKING INTERVENTIONS IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION AND OFFER AN UNPRECEDENTED OPPORTUNITY TO RIGOROUSLY ASSESS THEIR EFFECTIVENESS. THE WORK PROPOSED HERE WILL EVALUATE THE DECISION AIDS’ OVERALL IMPACT, IDENTIFY POPULATIONS AND CONTEXTS IN WHICH THE TOOLS ARE MORE EFFECTIVE, AND DETERMINE MECHANISMS OF ACTION. SPECIFICALLY, IN THIS RESEARCH, PATIENT-LEVEL DATA FROM THREE LARGE RCTS OF DECISION AIDS FOR STROKE PREVENTION IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION WILL BE SYNTHESIZED IN ORDER TO: (1) QUANTIFY THE OVERALL EFFECTIVENESS OF DECISION AIDS ON PATIENT- CENTERED AND CLINICAL OUTCOMES, (2) IDENTIFY THE PATIENT POPULATIONS AND SYSTEM CHARACTERISTICS IN WHICH EACH TYPE OF DECISION AID IS MORE AND LESS EFFECTIVE, AND (3) DETERMINE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH DECISION AIDS INFLUENCE TREATMENT DECISIONS AND OUTCOMES, TO INFORM IMPLEMENTATION OF PATIENT-CENTERED CARDIOVASCULAR CARE. THIS PROJECT DIRECTLY SUPPORTS NHLBI’S MISSION TO PROMOTE THE PREVENTION AND TREATMENT OF HEART, LUNG, AND BLOOD DISEASES AND ENHANCE THE HEALTH OF ALL INDIVIDUALS. BY POOLING DATA FROM THREE LARGE RCTS, THIS ANALYSIS OF INDIVIDUAL PATIENT DATA WILL PRODUCE THE MOST DEFINITIVE EVIDENCE TO DATE ON DECISION AIDS FOR STROKE PREVENTION IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION. GROUNDED IN PRINCIPLES OF DECISION SCIENCE, THE PROJECT WILL ENHANCE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW PATIENTS AND CLINICIANS MAKE COMPLEX HEALTHCARE CHOICES AND HOW THOSE CHOICES CAN BE OPTIMIZED. IT WILL INFORM FUTURE CLINICAL GUIDELINES, HEALTHCARE DELIVERY STRATEGIES, AND POLICY DECISIONS RELATED TO SHARED DECISION MAKING IN THE CONTEXT OF ATRIAL FIBRILLATION. IN ADDITION, THE STUDY WILL CONTRIBUTE ROBUST EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE TO THE FIELD OF DECISION SCIENCE, ADVANCING THEORETICAL FRAMEWORKS AND METHODOLOGICAL APPROACHES FOR EVALUATING SHARED DECISION MAKING. THE FINDINGS WILL ALSO GUIDE THE DEVELOPMENT OF SCALABLE, PATIENT-FOCUSED SHARED DECISION MAKING INTERVENTIONS ACROSS CARDIOVASCULAR CONDITIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
