description: DEEPHIV-AOU: A MULTI-MODAL DEEP LEARNING FRAMEWORK LEVERAGING THE ALL OF US RESEARCH PROGRAM FOR HIV PRECISION PREVENTION - ABSTRACT THE UNITED STATES IS CURRENTLY FALLING SHORT OF ITS  ENDING THE HIV EPIDEMIC  TARGETS, WITH HIV INCIDENCE DECLINING BY ONLY 4% ANNUALLY DESPITE A 90% REDUCTION GOAL. THIS STAGNATION IS DRIVEN BY A CRITICAL GAP IN PREEXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS (PREP) UTILIZATION AND PERSISTENCE, WHERE THE CURRENT RATIO OF PREP USERS TO NEW DIAGNOSES (15.6) REMAINS FAR BELOW THE ESTIMATED THRESHOLD (112) REQUIRED FOR POPULATION-LEVEL IMPACT. EXISTING PREVENTION EFFORTS ARE LIMITED BY TRADITIONAL PREDICTIVE MODELS THAT RELY ON UNIMODAL DATA, LACK TEMPORAL DEPTH, AND OFTEN FAIL TO GENERALIZE ACROSS DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. TO ADDRESS THESE BARRIERS, WE PROPOSE DEEPHIV-AOU, A NEXT-GENERATION MULTI-MODAL DEEP LEARNING (MDL) FRAMEWORK LEVERAGED THROUGH THE ALL OF US (AOU) RESEARCH PROGRAM. AOU PROVIDES A LARGE-SCALE, NATIONWIDE COHORT OF OVER 400,000 PARTICIPANTS WITH LINKED LONGITUDINAL ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (EHR), REFLECTING THE CHARACTERISTICS OF THE U.S. POPULATION. OUR INNOVATIVE ARCHITECTURE, USING AN INTERMEDIATE FUSION STRATEGY, INTEGRATES FOUR HETEROGENEOUS DATA STREAMS: TEMPORAL EHR SEQUENCES, GENOMICS, BEHAVIORAL SURVEYS, AND NON-MEDICAL DRIVERS OF HEALTH. AIM 1 WILL DEVELOP THE MDL FRAMEWORK TO GENERATE A DYNAMIC HIV ACQUISITION RISK SCORE AND AN INTERVENTION NON- RESPONSE LIKELIHOOD. AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE THE FRAMEWORK FOR CONSISTENCY USING ERROR PARITY METRICS AND ENSURE CLINICAL INTERPRETABILITY VIA TRANSFORMER-BASED ATTENTION MAPS. FINALLY, AIM 3 WILL ASSESS CLINICAL UTILITY AND HEALTH ECONOMIC IMPACT THROUGH MICROSIMULATION MODELING AND COST-EFFECTIVENESS ANALYSIS. BY SUCCESSFULLY BRIDGING THE GAP BETWEEN HIGH-DIMENSIONAL DATA AND CLINICAL ACTION, THIS PROJECT PROVIDES A FOUNDATION FOR PERSONALIZED HIV PREVENTION AND DIRECTLY SUPPORTS FEDERAL MANDATES TO END THE EPIDEMIC THROUGH PRECISION PUBLIC HEALTH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: FEASIBILITY, TECHNICAL PERFORMANCE, AND ACCEPTABILITY OF A WEARABLE MATERNAL STRESS TRACKER (MAST) IN MONITORING THE DAILY STRESS EXPERIENCED DURING THE POSTPARTUM PERIOD - MODIFIED PROJECT SUMMARY SECTION PROJECT SUMMARY WOMEN EXPERIENCE SIGNIFICANT POSTPARTUM STRESS DUE TO THE PHYSICAL, PSYCHOLOGICAL, AND SOCIAL ADJUSTMENTS ASSOCIATED WITH THE POSTPARTUM PERIOD. THE CURRENT POSTPARTUM FOLLOW-UP SCHEDULE DOES NOT ADEQUATELY MONITOR DAILY STRESS, AND PROLONGED UNTREATED STRESS INCREASES THE RISKS OF MATERNAL MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY. THEREFORE, THIS PILOT STUDY AIMS TO TEST THE FEASIBILITY, TECHNICAL PERFORMANCE, AND ACCEPTABILITY OF A WEARABLE MATERNAL STRESS TRACKER (MAST) IN MONITORING THE DAILY STRESS EXPERIENCED DURING THE POSTPARTUM. TO ACCOMPLISH THIS GOAL, WE PROPOSE THREE AIMS:1) INVESTIGATE THE FEASIBILITY AND TECHNICAL PERFORMANCE OF THE MAST WEARABLE DEVICE (GARMIN VIVIOSMART 4’ WRISTWATCH) TO ACCURATELY MONITOR POSTPARTUM SLEEP AND DAILY STRESS CALCULATED AS A PROPRIETARY COMPOSITE OF THE REAL-TIME MEASUREMENTS OF HEART RATE (HR), AND HEART RATE VARIABILITY (HRV). WE WILL ALSO ASSESS CONCORDANCE OF WRISTWATCH-SENSED STRESS WITH A CHRONIC STRESS BIOMARKER (HAIR CORTISOL), IN ADDITION TO BLOOD PRESSURE (BP) MONITORING AND SOCIAL NEEDS ASSESSMENTS USING THE PHENX TOOLKIT44, INCLUDING: A) HOUSING INSTABILITY B) MONEY TO PAY BILLS, C) SHUT OFF UTILITIES, D) FOOD INSECURITY, E) TRANSPORTATION, F) CHILDCARE, G) JOB INSECURITY, AND H) SAFETY. 2) EXAMINE THE ABILITY OF THE MAST WEARABLE DEVICE TO TRANSMIT THE HR AND HRV DATA USED TO DETERMINE STRESS, AND SLEEP DATA VIA BLUETOOTH TO THE MEMA APP ON THE USER'S PHONE, TRIGGER SURVEYS TO MEASURE STRESS AND DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, AND GENERATE ALERTS IN REAL-TIME BASED ON THE WOMAN’S STRESS LEVELS TO BOTH THE USER AND STUDY STAFF TO DELIVER THE IMMEDIATE PERSONALIZED INTERVENTION. 3) TO ASSESS THE USEFULNESS, ACCEPTABILITY, AND SATISFACTION WITH THE MAST WEARABLE DEVICE, THE PROCESS OF SURVEY TRIGGERS AND RESPONSES TO SURVEY QUESTIONS ABOUT THEIR STRESS AND MOOD. WE WILL RECRUIT 64 WOMEN, PROVIDE THEM WITH THE MAST IN THE POSTPARTUM PERIOD DURING THEIR BIRTH HOSPITALIZATION, AND FOLLOW THEM FOR SIX WEEKS. MAST BIOSENSOR-MEASURED OUTCOME VARIABLES ARE SLEEP QUALITY MEASURES, AND MATERNAL STRESS LEVELS CALCULATED AS A PROPRIETARY COMPOSITE OF THE HR AND HRV MEASURES. PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE PERCEIVED STRESS SCALE SCORES AND EDINBURG POSTPARTUM DEPRESSION SCALE SCORES, BP READINGS, AND PROCESS MEASURES FOR THE FREQUENCY OF TRIGGERS, ED VISITS, OR HOSPITAL ADMISSIONS IN THE FIRST SIX WEEKS AFTER BIRTH. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL OBTAIN HAIR SAMPLES AND SOCIAL NEEDS SURVEYS AT THE BEGINNING AND END OF THE INTERVENTION TO MEASURE THE CHANGE IN THE LEVEL OF CHRONIC STRESS AND SOCIAL NEEDS OVER 6-WEEKS POSTPARTUM, AND A SURVEY AND IN-DEPTH INTERVIEW TO EXPLORE THEIR EXPERIENCE OF USING THE WEARABLE DEVICE, PARTICIPANT ACCEPTABILITY, SATISFACTION, AND PERCEIVED USEFULNESS OF MAST. THIS PILOT STUDY WILL GENERATE DATA TO SUPPORT A LARGER RANDOMIZED TRIAL AND ALIGN WELL WITH THE CURRENT NIH PRIORITIES BY ADVANCING MATERNAL HEALTH, LEVERAGING DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES, AND ENABLING EARLIER IDENTIFICATION OF RISK IN POPULATIONS WITH HIGHER RATES OF ADVERSE OUTCOMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NOVEL THEORETICAL MODELS AND METHODS FOR REDUCING SOCIOECONOMIC DISPARITIES IN TOBACCO USE - ALTHOUGH TOBACCO CONTROL INTERVENTIONS HAVE REDUCED OVERALL SMOKING PREVALENCE, TOBACCO USE REMAINS A LEADING CAUSE OF PREVENTABLE DISEASE AND DEATH. THERE IS A DYNAMIC INTERPLAY OF INDIVIDUAL, SOCIAL, AND SOCIETAL FACTORS THAT UNDERLIE DIFFICULTY IN SMOKING CESSATION, PARTICULARLY FOR POPULATIONS WITH LOW INCOME OR LIMITED RESOURCES. ALTHOUGH SMOKING AND SMOKING CESSATION BEHAVIORS ARE LINKED BY COMPLEX FEEDBACK LOOPS (I.E., A SET OF BALANCING AND REINFORCING CAUSAL FEEDBACK MECHANISMS) INTERACTING AT MULTIPLE LEVELS, A MORE COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF THESE COMPLEX FEEDBACK MECHANISMS FROM A HIGHER-LEVEL SYSTEMS VIEW IS CURRENTLY LACKING. TOWARDS REDUCING THE PREVALENCE OF TOBACCO USE, A PROMISING AND INNOVATIVE APPROACH IS TO IDENTIFY STAKEHOLDER-INFORMED TARGETS OF INTERVENTIONS (OR LEVERAGE POINTS) IN MULTILEVEL FEEDBACK MECHANISMS DRIVING THE DYNAMICS OF SMOKING CESSATION. THE GOAL OF THIS R21 APPLICATION IS TO IDENTIFY AND MODEL MULTILEVEL INTERVENTION STRATEGIES THAT CAN BE PRIORITIZED FOR ADDRESSING TOBACCO USE AND TO DEVELOP A NOVEL, MULTILEVEL ADAPTIVE INTERVENTION TRIAL DESIGN THAT CAN IDENTIFY THE OPTIMAL ORDER TO TARGET MULTILEVEL LEVERAGE POINTS. AIM 1 IS TO IDENTIFY KEY LEVERAGE POINTS OF INTERVENTION FOR REDUCING SOCIOECONOMIC DISPARITIES IN SMOKING. WE WILL ACCOMPLISH THIS USING COMMUNITY-BASED SYSTEM DYNAMICS (CBSD) TO DEVELOP AN INITIAL FEEDBACK THEORY OF SMOKING AND HEALTH-RELATED SOCIAL NEEDS DYNAMICS VIA KEY INFORMANT INTERVIEWS AND GROUP MODEL BUILDING. CBSD IS AN APPROACH TO GROUP MODEL BUILDING THAT DIRECTLY INVOLVES COMMUNITIES IN THE PROCESS OF CONCEPTUALIZING, FORMULATING, AND ANALYSIS OF SYSTEM DYNAMICS SIMULATION MODELS. AIM 2 IS TO DEVELOP A NOVEL CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN TO TEST ADAPTIVE, MULTILEVEL INTERVENTIONS. BUILDING ON A FRAMEWORK FOR SEQUENTIAL, MULTIPLE ASSIGNMENT, RANDOMIZED TRIALS (SMARTS), WE WILL DESIGN AND DEVELOP THE METHODOLOGY TO ANALYZE CLINICAL TRIAL DATA THAT CAN BE USED TO IDENTIFY DYNAMIC TREATMENT REGIMENS, OR SEQUENCES OF TREATMENT THAT CHANGE ADAPTIVELY BASED ON RESPONSE, FOR MULTILEVEL INTERVENTIONS. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO CARRY OUT CONCEPTUAL WORK IN PARALLEL WITH METHODOLOGICAL WORK TO IMPROVE UPON TRIAL DESIGN AND ANALYSIS THAT CAN INFORM ADVANCEMENTS IN CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE TO REDUCE HEALTH DISPARITIES. THE NIMHD HAS CALLED FOR RESEARCH ON MULTILEVEL INTERVENTIONS TO ADDRESS HEALTH DISPARITIES, INCLUDING THROUGH STRENGTHENING THEORETICAL FRAMEWORKS THAT CAN RECOGNIZE THE COMPLEX SET OF FACTORS INVOLVED IN MULTILEVEL CHANGE. BY MODELING THE MULTILEVEL DRIVERS OF A SIGNIFICANT HEALTH DISPARITY ISSUE, IDENTIFYING LEVERAGE POINTS FOR INTERVENTION, AND ADDRESSING A GAP IN CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN, THE FINDINGS WILL COST-EFFECTIVELY INFORM THE MOST OPTIMAL SET OF MULTILEVEL INTERVENTION TARGETS THAT CAN BE FURTHER EXAMINED AND TESTED IN A FUTURE STUDY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT OF A CULTURALLY TAILORED SLEEP INTERVENTION USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR FILIPINO IMMIGRANTS - PROJECT ABSTRACT POOR SLEEP IS A PREVALENT PUBLIC HEALTH PROBLEM THAT IS ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED MORBIDITY AND HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION. EPIDEMIOLOGICAL DATA INDICATE THAT ASIAN AMERICAN ADULTS ARE AT INCREASED RISK OF EXPERIENCING SHORT SLEEP AND POOR SLEEP QUALITY. THIS RISK IS PARTICULARLY SUBSTANTIAL AMONG FILIPINO AMERICANS, ONE OF THE LARGEST SUBGROUPS OF ASIAN AMERICANS. OUR RESEARCH USING A NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE COHORT OF U.S. ADULTS FOUND THAT FILIPINO AMERICAN ADULTS HAD THE HIGHEST PREVALENCE OF SHORT SLEEP DURATION AMONG ALL POPULATION GROUPS EXAMINED. THEY ALSO REPORTED GREATER DIFFICULTY FALLING ASLEEP AND STAYING ASLEEP THAN OTHER ASIAN AMERICAN SUBGROUPS. DESPITE THE CAUSAL LINK BETWEEN POOR SLEEP AND ADVERSE PHYSICAL AND MENTAL HEALTH, NO INTERVENTION TO DATE HAS ADDRESSED SLEEP ISSUES AMONG FILIPINO AMERICANS. EXISTING NON-PHARMACOLOGICAL SLEEP INTERVENTIONS ARE EFFECTIVE IN IMPROVING SLEEP OUTCOMES, BUT THEY ARE PRIMARILY CONSTRAINED BY HIGH COSTS, LACK OF ACCESSIBILITY. EMERGING RESEARCH HAS SHOWN THAT ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)-DRIVEN LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS CAN SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE SLEEP DURATION AND QUALITY. INTEGRATING AI TECHNOLOGIES INTO SLEEP INTERVENTIONS IS HIGHLY PROMISING BECAUSE THEY ARE COST-EFFECTIVE, ENGAGING, AND OFFER AN AUTOMATED, SELF-PACED DELIVERY MODALITY. TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS, OUR TEAM DEVELOPED A GENERATIVE AI-POWERED SLEEP CHATBOT THAT DELIVERS PERSONALIZED ADVICE GROUNDED IN COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY FOR INSOMNIA (CBT-I) VIA A TEXT MESSAGING APP. IN OUR PRELIMINARY STUDY, THE CHATBOT DEMONSTRATED HIGH FEASIBILITY AND STRONG ACCEPTABILITY. PARTICIPANTS REPORTED IMPROVEMENTS IN MULTIPLE SLEEP OUTCOMES AFTER CHATBOT USE, INCLUDING LONGER SLEEP DURATION AND BETTER SLEEP QUALITY. BUILDING ON THIS WORK, WE WILL CONDUCT A SINGLE-ARM, PRE-POST STUDY TO PILOT TEST OUR GENERATIVE AI-BASED SLEEP INTERVENTION AMONG FILIPINO AMERICANS WITH POOR SLEEP. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL EXAMINE THE FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, USABILITY, AND ENGAGEMENT OF THE INTERVENTION, AS WELL AS PRE-POST CHANGES IN SLEEP OUTCOMES. USING A CONVENIENCE SAMPLING STRATEGY, WE WILL ENROLL 40 FILIPINO AMERICANS AGED 30 TO 70 YEARS WHO HAVE SHORT SLEEP DURATION AND POOR QUALITY OF SLEEP. THE STUDY WILL LAST FOR FOUR WEEKS, INCLUDING A 1-WEEK BASELINE ASSESSMENT, A 2-WEEK INTERVENTION PERIOD, AND A 1-WEEK POST-INTERVENTION ASSESSMENT. DURING THE 2-WEEK SLEEP INTERVENTION, PARTICIPANTS WILL ENGAGE WITH AN AI CHATBOT THROUGH TEXTING TO RECEIVE PERSONALIZED EDUCATION AND GUIDANCE FOR SLEEP PROMOTION. A DEBRIEFING SESSION WILL FOLLOW THE INTERVENTION TO GATHER EACH PARTICIPANT'S FEEDBACK AND IDENTIFY AREAS FOR IMPROVEMENT. THIS PROPOSED STUDY REPRESENTS A PIONEERING EFFORT TO HARNESS GENERATIVE AI TO IMPROVE SLEEP HEALTH AMONG ASIAN AMERICANS. FINDINGS FROM THIS STUDY WILL LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR FURTHER REFINEMENT AND EFFICACY TESTING OF OUR AI-BASED SLEEP INTERVENTION ON A LARGER SCALE. MORE IMPORTANTLY, THE AI-BASED SLEEP INTERVENTION HOLDS POTENTIAL FOR EXPANSION TO OTHER POPULATION GROUPS THAT EXPERIENCE POOR SLEEP.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EMPOWERING NUTRITION THROUGH GRAPHIC-STYLE STORIES: CO-DESIGNING AN ACCEPTABLE AND FEASIBLE COMMUNITY-BASED PROGRAM WITH ADULTS WITH INTELLECTUAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES AND THEIR CAREGIVERS - PROJECT SUMMARY ADULTS WITH IDD OFTEN HAVE POOR DIETARY QUALITY, CHARACTERIZED BY HIGH INTAKE OF REFINED CARBOHYDRATES, SATURATED FAT, SODIUM, AND PROCESSED FOODS, ALONG WITH INSUFFICIENT INTAKE OF FRUITS AND VEGETABLES. IN ADDITION, FOOD SELECTIVITY AND A PROPENSITY TO OVEREAT CONTRIBUTE TO POOR EATING PATTERNS. THIS, IN TURN, IS ASSOCIATED WITH A HIGHER PREVALENCE OF OVERWEIGHT AND OBESITY THAT IS APPROXIMATELY TWO TIMES HIGHER THAN WHAT IS FOUND IN THE GENERAL POPULATION. AS A RESULT, THEY ENCOUNTER INCREASED RISKS FOR CHRONIC DISEASES. WITH TOO FEW RESOURCES SPECIFICALLY TAILORED FOR THIS UNIQUELY VULNERABLE POPULATION, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED FOR AN ENGAGING AND EASY-TO- IMPLEMENT COMMUNITY-BASED NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM THAT TARGETS BOTH ADULTS WITH IDD AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. PREVIOUS STUDIES HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT NARRATIVES ARE ENGAGING, MEMORABLE, AND ACTIONABLE IN PROMOTING HEALTHY LIFESTYLES IN COMMUNITY SETTINGS, PARTICULARLY IN ADULTS WITH LOWER HEALTH LITERACY LEVELS, SUCH AS ADULTS WITH IDD. THEREFORE, WE WILL CO-DESIGN AN INNOVATIVE, THEORY-BASED NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM, EMPOWER ADULTS WITH IDD, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH ADULTS WITH IDD, THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS. THERE ARE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) TO ITERATIVELY CO-DESIGN, EMPOWER ADULTS WITH MILD IDD, AN ENGAGING AND EASY-TO- IMPLEMENT NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM WITH ADULTS WITH IDD, THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS AND TO TEST ITS ACCEPTABILITY AND FEASIBILITY AT ADSCS, AND (2) TO DETERMINE THE PRELIMINARY EFFICACY OF EMPOWER ADULTS WITH IDD ON FOOD AND BEVERAGE CONSUMPTION, AND FOOD SELECTIVITY IN ADULTS WITH IDD, AND THEIR CAREGIVERS' FOOD LITERACY TO PROMOTE HEALTHY EATING IN ADULTS WITH IDD. IN ORDER TO EXAMINE AIM 1 A DETERMINANTS ASSESSMENT WILL BE CONDUCTED WITH 45 DYADS OF ADULTS AND THEIR CAREGIVERS TO INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF GRAPHIC STYLE STORIES AND OTHER EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS. TOPICS MAY INCLUDE MYPLATE FOOD GROUPS, PORTION CONTROL, INCORPORATING FRUITS AND VEGETABLES INTO MEALS AND SNACKS, WATER CONSUMPTION, AND ALTERNATIVES TO PROCESS FOODS IN THE CONTEXT OF INTERACTION BETWEEN ADULTS WITH IDD AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. THE ITERATIVE CO-DESIGNED GRAPHIC STYLE STORIES AND OTHER EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS WILL BE TESTED FOR ACCEPTABILITY WITH 6 DYADS AND THEN 6- WEEK SHORT VERSION OF THE PROGRAM THAT INCORPORATED THOSE MATERIALS WILL BE IMPLEMENTED FOR FEASIBILITY TEST WITH 10 DYADS. AFTER THE REVISION BASED ON THE FEEDBACK THROUGH THIS PROCESS, THE PROGRAM WILL BE FINALIZED. TO EXAMINE AIM 2, THE PRELIMINARY EFFICACY OF THE FULL 6-MONTH PROGRAM WILL BE TESTED WITH 45 DYADS ON FOOD CONSUMPTION, FOOD SELECTIVITY, MOTIVATION FOR HEALTHY EATING IN ADULTS WITH IDD AND CAREGIVER'S FOOD LITERACY USING A ONE-GROUP PRE- AND POST-TEST DESIGN AT THREE ADSCS, WITH BASELINE, 3-, 6-, AND 9-MONTH ASSESSMENTS. WE EXPECT THAT THE PROGRAM ITERATIVELY CO-DESIGNED WITH ADULTS WITH IDD AND THEIR CAREGIVERS WILL BE ENGAGING AND FEASIBLE TO IMPLEMENT WITHIN COMMUNITY ADULT DAY SERVICE CENTERS AND IMPROVE FOOD CONSUMPTION OF ADULTS WITH IDD. IF SUCCESSFUL, THE PROGRAM WILL GREATLY IMPACT THE LIVES OF COUNTLESS ADULTS WITH IDD AND HELP THEM TO WARD OFF UNNECESSARY CHRONIC DISEASES CAUSED BY UNHEALTHY EATING HABITS WITH OVERALL HEALTH AND WELL-BEING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TRANSFORMING RURAL HEALTH: STRATEGIES FOR EFFECTIVE MOBILE HEALTH CLINIC DEPLOYMENT - RURAL COMMUNITIES IN SOUTHWEST OKLAHOMA FACE PERSISTENT HEALTHCARE ACCESS CHALLENGES DUE TO GEOGRAPHIC ISOLATION, PROVIDER SHORTAGES, AND LIMITED AWARENESS OF AVAILABLE SERVICES. THE PANDEMIC HIGHLIGHTED THESE CHALLENGES, LEADING THE OKLAHOMA STATE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (OSDH) TO INTRODUCE MOBILE HEALTH CLINICS (MHCS) TO EXPAND ACCESS TO ESSENTIAL TESTING AND VACCINATION SERVICES. TODAY, MHCS IN OKLAHOMA PROVIDE A RANGE OF ESSENTIAL HEALTHCARE SERVICES, INCLUDING CHRONIC DISEASE MANAGEMENT, MATERNAL HEALTH, IMMUNIZATIONS, AND PREVENTIVE SCREENINGS. HOWEVER, UTILIZATION REMAINS LOW DUE TO LIMITED PUBLIC AWARENESS, TRUST ISSUES, AND INEFFICIENT DEPLOYMENT STRATEGIES. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO OPTIMIZE MHC UTILIZATION AND RESOURCE ALLOCATION IN RURAL OKLAHOMA BY INTEGRATING COMMUNITY-DRIVEN INSIGHTS WITH GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SCIENCE (GIS)-BASED DECISION-SUPPORT TOOLS. THIS STUDY HAS TWO PRIMARY AIMS. AIM 1 SEEKS TO IDENTIFY CHALLENGES TO MHC UTILIZATION AND DEVELOP STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE COMMUNITY AWARENESS AND ENGAGEMENT. THROUGH SURVEYS AND INTERVIEWS WITH RURAL RESIDENTS, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, AND MHC STAFF, WE WILL EXAMINE CHALLENGES SUCH AS TRUST, ACCESSIBILITY CHALLENGES, AND GAPS IN SERVICE AWARENESS. FINDINGS WILL INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF TAILORED COMMUNICATION STRATEGIES AND SERVICE ENHANCEMENTS TO INCREASE MHC UPTAKE. AIM 2 FOCUSES ON DEVELOPING A DYNAMIC DECISION-SUPPORT TOOL TO OPTIMIZE MHC DEPLOYMENT. USING GIS MODELING AND REAL-TIME COMMUNITY HEALTH DATA, WE WILL CREATE AN INTERACTIVE TOOL THAT ENABLES DATA-DRIVEN DECISION-MAKING, ALLOWING HEALTH ADMINISTRATORS TO IDENTIFY HIGH-NEED AREAS AND EFFICIENTLY ALLOCATE MHC RESOURCES. THIS RESEARCH IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT COMBINES COMMUNITY-ENGAGED RESEARCH WITH ADVANCED GEOSPATIAL ANALYTICS TO ENHANCE RURAL HEALTHCARE ACCESS. UNLIKE TRADITIONAL MODELS THAT RELY ON BROAD HEALTH PROFESSIONAL SHORTAGE AREA (HPSA) DESIGNATIONS, OUR APPROACH INCORPORATES FINE-SCALE ACCESSIBILITY MEASURES, POPULATION HEALTH DATA, AND STAKEHOLDER INPUT TO ENSURE MHCS REACH THE COMMUNITIES THAT NEED THEM MOST. BY INTEGRATING MHC PATIENT RECORD DATA, SURVEY FINDINGS, AND CDC COMMUNITY-LEVEL HEALTH INDICATORS, THIS PROJECT WILL CREATE A SCALABLE FRAMEWORK FOR IMPROVING MOBILE HEALTH SERVICE DELIVERY IN RURAL AREAS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT WITH MHCS, INCREASED ACCESS TO ESSENTIAL HEALTHCARE SERVICES, AND A GIS-BASED DECISION-SUPPORT TOOL TO ENHANCE DEPLOYMENT STRATEGIES. THIS PROJECT ALIGNS WITH THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE ON MINORITY HEALTH AND HEALTH DISPARITIES (NIMHD) MISSION BY IMPROVING HEALTHCARE ACCESS IN RURAL COMMUNITIES WITH LIMITED HEALTHCARE RESOURCES. FINDINGS WILL LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR A FUTURE NIH R01 PROPOSAL, EXPANDING THE RESEARCH TO ADDITIONAL RURAL REGIONS AND REFINING MHC DEPLOYMENT STRATEGIES NATIONWIDE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A GENERALIZABLE FRAMEWORK FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A CONTINUOUS METABOLIC SYNDROME RISK SCORE IN SMALL POPULATIONS. - PROJECT SUMMARY WE AIM TO DEVELOP A CONTINUOUS METABOLIC SYNDROME (CMS) RISK SCORE BY INTEGRATING TRADITIONAL CLINICAL RISK FACTORS FOR METABOLIC SYNDROME (METS) WITH INDICATORS OF HOUSEHOLD SOCIOECONOMIC WELL-BEING (INCLUDING ANNUAL INCOME, FOOD SECURITY, AND HOUSEHOLD SIZE), BEHAVIORAL FACTORS (E.G., TOBACCO USE), STRESS LEVELS, AND CULTURAL RESILIENCE OR PROTECTIVE FACTORS. THIS EFFORT WILL UTILIZE ADVANCED STATISTICAL MODELING TECHNIQUES APPLIED TO CLINICAL RESEARCH DATA FROM A YUP’IK ALASKA NATIVE STUDY POPULATION. HEART DISEASE REMAINS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH AMONG ALASKA NATIVE MEN AND RANKS SECOND, AFTER CANCER, FOR WOMEN AND THE ALASKA NATIVE POPULATION OVERALL. AMONG YUP’IK PEOPLE, HEART DISEASE MORTALITY IS 30% HIGHER THAN THE NATIONAL AVERAGE ACROSS ALL RACIAL GROUPS. TRADITIONAL BINARY METS CRITERIA FALL SHORT IN CAPTURING GRADUAL SHIFTS IN DISEASE RISK, LIMITING OPPORTUNITIES FOR EARLY PREVENTIVE HEALTH INTERVENTIONS. IN CONTRAST, A CMS RISK SCORE PROVIDES A CLINICALLY MEANINGFUL METRIC THAT IS SENSITIVE TO SUBTLE CHANGES IN AN INDIVIDUAL’S HEALTH STATUS OVER TIME, OFFERING A MORE PRECISE ASSESSMENT OF CARDIOMETABOLIC DISEASE RISK. THE STUDY HAS TWO PRIMARY OBJECTIVES: (1) TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A SEX-SPECIFIC CMS RISK SCORE USING STANDARD METS COMPONENTS (WAIST CIRCUMFERENCE, BLOOD PRESSURE, FASTING PLASMA GLUCOSE, TRIGLYCERIDES, AND HDL-CHOLESTEROL) FOR THE YUP’IK POPULATION; AND (2) TO EVALUATE WHETHER THE PREDICTIVE POWER OF THE CMS SCORE IMPROVES WITH THE INCLUSION OF ADDITIONAL ESTABLISHED CARDIOMETABOLIC RISK FACTORS (NON-HDL-C, TC/HDL-C AND LDL-C/HDL-C RATIOS, HEMOGLOBIN A1C), SOCIOECONOMIC INDICATORS, BEHAVIORAL FACTORS, STRESS MEASURES, AND CULTURAL RESILIENCE FACTORS SUCH AS SPEAKING YUP’IK AND FOLLOWING A TRADITIONAL YUP’IK WAY OF LIFE. CARDIOMETABOLIC HEALTH DETERMINANTS IN SMALL POPULATIONS REMAIN UNDEREXPLORED, WHERE CLINICAL, SOCIAL, AND CULTURAL DIMENSIONS, INCLUDING RESILIENCE, PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE. THIS STUDY WILL BE THE FIRST TO JOINTLY MODEL BOTH RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS IN CONSTRUCTING THE CMS SCORE, PROVIDING A GENERALIZABLE FRAMEWORK FOR DEVELOPING TAILORED CMS RISK SCORES FOR OTHER POPULATIONS THAT REFLECT THEIR UNIQUE RISK AND PROTECTIVE HEALTH PROFILES.

description: IMPROVING ENGAGEMENT IN POST-INJURY MENTAL HEALTH CARE THROUGH COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER-ENHANCED TRAUMA RECOVERY SERVICES - EACH YEAR, TRAUMATIC INJURIES SUCH AS GUNSHOT WOUNDS AND MOTOR VEHICLE ACCIDENTS COST THE U.S. MORE THAN $2 TRILLION IN MEDICAL EXPENSES AND LOST PRODUCTIVITY, DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTING WORKING-AGED ADULTS (25–64). BETWEEN 20–40% OF SURVIVORS DEVELOP POSTTRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER (PTSD) OR DEPRESSION WITHIN THE FIRST YEAR, WHICH IS ASSOCIATED WITH POOR RECOVERY, IMPAIRED FUNCTIONING, AND REDUCED QUALITY OF LIFE. SURVIVORS WITH EXPOSURE TO THE FOLLOWING NEGATIVE FACTORS:  HOUSING, FOOD, AND TRANSPORTATION INSECURITY, AND FINANCIAL STRAIN, EXPERIENCE GREATER RISKS AND PERSISTENT DISPARITIES. IN OUR PRIOR WORK, NEARLY 70% OF TRAUMA SURVIVORS REPORTED AT LEAST ONE UNMET SOCIAL NEED, WHICH WAS LINKED TO ELEVATED DISTRESS AT BEDSIDE. DESPITE AMERICAN COLLEGE OF SURGEONS (ACS) BEST PRACTICE GUIDELINES REQUIRING PSYCHOSOCIAL SCREENING AND FOLLOW-UP, OVER 70% OF U.S. TRAUMA CENTERS LACK RESOURCES TO SUPPORT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ENGAGEMENT POST-DISCHARGE, AND EVEN FEWER CONDUCT SCREENING FOR THESE AFOREMENTIONED FACTORS. AS A RESULT, CRITICAL SOCIAL AND BEHAVIORAL NEEDS REMAIN UNADDRESSED, POTENTIALLY RESULTING IN POOR OUTCOMES. THE TRAUMA RESILIENCE AND RECOVERY PROGRAM (TRRP), DEVELOPED BY OUR TEAM AND ADOPTED IN 12 LEVEL I–II TRAUMA CENTERS, IS AN EVIDENCE-BASED STEPPED-CARE MODEL ALIGNED WITH ACS GUIDELINES. TRRP PROVIDES BEDSIDE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENING, PSYCHOEDUCATION, AND REFERRAL TO STEPPED MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES. WHILE FEASIBLE AND ACCEPTABLE, TRRP FOLLOW-UP ENGAGEMENT DECLINES AMONG PATIENTS WHO EXPERIENCE THESE FACTORS (30% AT 30-DAYS) COMPARED WITH THOSE WHO DO NOT (60%). TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, WE PROPOSE TRRP+, AN ENHANCED MODEL THAT INTEGRATES COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER (CHW) DELIVERED SUPPORT INTO TRRP TO PROMOTE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ENGAGEMENT AND RECOVERY. TRRP+ PRIORITIZES RESOLUTION OF BASIC SOCIAL NEEDS AS A FOUNDATION FOR HIGHER-ORDER HEALTH AND RECOVERY GOALS. THIS APPROACH ALIGNS WITH THE NIMHD RESEARCH FRAMEWORK BY ADDRESSING MULTIPLE DOMAINS (HEALTHCARE SYSTEM) AND LEVELS (INDIVIDUAL, INTERPERSONAL, COMMUNITY). AIM 1 WILL ASSESS FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF TRRP+ THROUGH AN OPEN TRIAL WITH 100 ADULT TRAUMA SURVIVORS WITH ACUTE DISTRESS AND ≥1 UNMET SOCIAL NEEDS. OUTCOMES INCLUDE RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, SERVICE ENGAGEMENT, ACCEPTABILITY, AND PRELIMINARY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES. AIM 2 WILL IDENTIFY CHALLENGES AND FACILITATORS INFLUENCING TRRP+ ADOPTIONAND SCALABILITY USING THE CONSOLIDATED FRAMEWORK FOR IMPLEMENTATION RESEARCH (CFIR) THROUGH QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS WITH PATIENTS, CHWS, AND TRAUMA STAFF. TRRP+ HAS POTENTIAL TO REDUCE DISPARITIES IN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH RECOVERY BY SIMULTANEOUSLY ADDRESSING SOCIAL AND BEHAVIORAL NEEDS. THIS R21 WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL FEASIBILITY DATA TO SUPPORT A SUBSEQUENT MULTI-SITE HYBRID EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION R01, OFFERING A SCALABLE SOLUTION FOR TRAUMA CENTERS NATIONWIDE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXPLORATORY EVALUATION OF LABOR-ASSOCIATED INFLAMMATORY PROFILES IN LOW-RISK NULLIPAROUS SUBGROUPS DURING INDUCED AND SPONTANEOUS LABOR - MATERNAL MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY REMAIN A CRITICAL PUBLIC HEALTH CHALLENGE IN THE UNITED STATES, WITH BLACK WOMEN EXPERIENCING DISPROPORTIONATELY HIGH RATES OF ADVERSE MATERNAL OUTCOMES AND CESAREAN BIRTH. RACIAL DISPARITIES IN CESAREAN BIRTH PERSIST AMONG LOW-RISK NULLIPAROUS, TERM, SINGLE, VERTEX (NTSV) BIRTHS, A STANDARDIZED POPULATION WITH SIMILAR BASELINE OBSTETRIC RISK. WITHIN THIS POPULATION, THE CESAREAN RATE IS 31.5% AMONG BLACK WOMEN COMPARED WITH 25.5% AMONG WHITE WOMEN AND 25.9% AMONG HISPANIC WOMEN. FAILED INDUCTION AND LABOR DYSTOCIA (SLOW OR ARRESTED LABOR PROGRESS) ACCOUNT FOR NEARLY HALF OF NTSV CESAREANS, AND BLACK WOMEN EXPERIENCE BOTH MORE FREQUENTLY. HOWEVER, THE PHYSIOLOGIC MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THESE CONDITIONS REMAIN UNDEFINED, AND WHETHER CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY BURDEN ALTERS PHYSIOLOGIC IMMUNE ACTIVATION DURING LABOR HAS NEVER BEEN DETERMINED. LABOR ONSET AND PROGRESSION ARE MEDIATED BY ACUTE INFLAMMATORY PROCESSES THAT AMPLIFY THROUGH COORDINATED POSITIVE FEEDBACK SIGNALING WITHIN THE CERVIX, MYOMETRIUM, FETAL MEMBRANES, AND MATERNAL CIRCULATION. WHILE PHYSIOLOGIC INFLAMMATION IS NECESSARY FOR EFFICIENT LABOR, DYSREGULATED INFLAMMATORY SIGNALING—WHETHER INADEQUATE OR EXCESSIVE—CAN IMPAIR UTERINE CONTRACTILITY AND LABOR PERFORMANCE, EVEN IN THE ABSENCE OF INFECTION. CHRONIC, LOW-GRADE INFLAMMATION, A HALLMARK OF MANY CHRONIC DISEASES, MAY ALTER RESPONSIVENESS TO LABOR-ASSOCIATED IMMUNE ACTIVATION. WE PROPOSE THAT CHRONIC INFLAMMATION DISRUPTS PHYSIOLOGIC LABOR THROUGH ONE OF TWO MALADAPTIVE PATHWAYS: (1) ATTENUATED IMMUNE RESPONSIVENESS TO ACUTE LABOR ACTIVATION OR (2) ADDITIVE INFLAMMATORY SIGNALING EXCEEDING PHYSIOLOGIC THRESHOLDS. EITHER PATHWAY MAY IMPAIR UTERINE CONTRACTILITY AND LABOR EFFICIENCY, CONTRIBUTING TO FAILED INDUCTION, LABOR DYSTOCIA, AND CESAREAN BIRTH. THESE MECHANISMS ARE BIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT TO ALL WOMEN BUT ARE HYPOTHESIZED TO BE MOST PRONOUNCED AMONG THOSE WITH ELEVATED CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY BURDEN. ACCORDINGLY, OVERSAMPLING BLACK NTSV WOMEN IS A SCIENTIFICALLY JUSTIFIED STRATEGY TO IDENTIFY INFLAMMATORY TRAJECTORIES ASSOCIATED WITH LABOR INEFFICIENCY. WE WILL ENROLL 120 LOW-RISK NTSV WOMEN (60 BLACK, NON-HISPANIC; 60 OTHER, ANY ETHNICITY) ADMITTED TO VANDERBILT UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER FOR INDUCTION OR SPONTANEOUS LABOR. GROUP-BASED TRAJECTORY MODELING WILL IDENTIFY LATENT TRAJECTORIES OF MATERNAL PLASMA INFLAMMATORY BIOMARKERS (IL-1Β, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-Α) ACROSS INDUCTION, SPONTANEOUS EARLY LABOR, AND ACTIVE LABOR, AND LINEAR MIXED-EFFECTS MODELS WILL COMPARE GROUPS TO GENERATE PRELIMINARY EFFECT SIZE AND VARIANCE ESTIMATES THAT WILL REFINE HYPOTHESES AND INFORM FUTURE ADEQUATELY POWERED STUDIES. DEFINING INFLAMMATORY TRAJECTORIES DURING LABOR WILL GENERATE FOUNDATIONAL EVIDENCE ON PHYSIOLOGIC MECHANISMS OF LABOR INEFFICIENCY. IN THE LONG TERM, THESE FINDINGS WILL INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF BIOLOGICALLY INFORMED APPROACHES FOR INDIVIDUALIZED LABOR ASSESSMENT AND CLINICAL MANAGEMENT AIMED AT REDUCING PREVENTABLE CESAREAN BIRTHS AND IMPROVING MATERNAL OUTCOMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: COVID19 AND MENTAL HEALTH WELLBEING IN TRIBAL COLLEGE & UNIVERSITY COMMUNITIES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT WHILE AMERICAN INDIAN OR ALASKA NATIVE (AIAN) COMMUNITIES EXPERIENCED DISPROPORTIONATELY HIGHER RATES OF COVID-19 INCIDENCE, HOSPITALIZATIONS, AND DEATHS, ALONG WITH RELATED MENTAL HEALTH STRESSORS COMPARED TO NON-HISPANIC WHITES, THE AIAN COMMUNITIES ALSO DEMONSTRATED UNIQUE COPING PROCESSES, INCLUDING CULTURALLY RELEVANT SOURCES OF STRENGTH, RESILIENCE, AND PROGRAMMING TO SUPPORT MENTAL, EMOTIONAL, CULTURAL, AND PHYSICAL WELLBEING. AS AIAN COMMUNITIES CONTINUE TO RECOVER FROM THE PANDEMIC AMIDST LONG COVID, IT IS IMPORTANT THAT INTERVENTIONS AND SUPPORT PROGRAMS ARE SENSITIVE TO THE UNIQUE COPING PROCESSES FOR THIS COMMUNITY TO IMPROVE THEIR PSYCHOSOCIAL HEALTH. WHILE THE LITERATURE ON COVID-19 MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE IMPACTS AMONG MAINSTREAM COLLEGE AND UNIVERSITY STUDENTS HAS EMERGED – FOR EXAMPLE, DURING COVID-19 DEPRESSION AND ANXIETY RATES WERE HIGHER AMONG YOUNG ADULTS INCLUDING COLLEGE STUDENTS THAN ANY OTHER AGE GROUP-- THERE IS A DEARTH OF RESEARCH ON THE SAME TOPIC AMONG TRIBAL COLLEGE AND UNIVERSITY (TCU) STUDENTS. THE PROPOSED R21 PROJECT, CO-DESIGNED IN RESPONSE TO PAR-23-299 BY UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) RESEARCHERS AND AMERICAN INDIAN HIGHER EDUCATION CONSORTIUM (AIHEC) PARTNERS WITH 15 YEARS OF RESEARCH COLLABORATION HISTORY EXAMINES COVID-19-ASSOCIATED MENTAL HEALTH EXPERIENCES AMONG TCU STUDENTS. THE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS OF THE RESEARCH PROJECT ARE TO (1) ASSESS THE IMPACT OF THE PANDEMIC ON TCU STUDENTS' MENTAL HEALTH (I.E., ANXIETY, DEPRESSION, SUICIDALITY) BEFORE AND DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC; AND (2) ASSESS LONGER-TERM IMPACTS OF COVID-19 ON MENTAL HEALTH AMONG TCU STUDENTS DURING THE COVID-19 RECOVERY PHASE TO EXAMINE HOW RESILIENCE FACTORS AND INSTITUTIONAL SUPPORTS MAY BUFFER NEGATIVE EFFECTS OF COVID-19 STRESSORS. DOCUMENTING RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH TCU STUDENTS’ RISK FOR INCREASED MENTAL HEALTH SYMPTOMS IN RESPONSE TO THE PANDEMIC STRESSORS WILL CLARIFY TARGETS FOR INTERVENTION DURING LARGE-SCALE CRISES.

description: STRIOSOMAL CONTROL OF DOPAMINE CIRCUIT IMPACTED BY MATERNAL IMMUNE ACTIVATION - THIS PROJECT PROPOSES TO INVESTIGATE THE INFLUENCE OF MATERNAL IMMUNE ACTIVATION (MIA) ON DOPAMINE FUNCTION WITH A LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO ELUCIDATE CIRCUIT VULNERABILITIES THAT COULD CONTRIBUTE TO SUSCEPTIBILITY NEUROPSYCHIATRIC OUTCOMES ASSOCIATED WITH DOPAMINE DYSREGULATION. THE FOCUS IS ON EVALUATING THE IMPACT OF IN UTERO IMMUNE ACTIVATION ON A STRIATAL CIRCUIT CALLED THE STRIOSOME-DENDRON BOUQUET, WHICH DIRECTLY CONTROLS DOPAMINE NEURONS IN THE SUBSTANTIA NIGRA PARS COMPACTA (SNC). AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER MIA CAUSES STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL ALTERATIONS IN THE STRIOSOME-DOPAMINE CIRCUIT. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS THE ROLE OF THE DOPAMINE-ANTAGONISTIC NOCICEPTIN SYSTEM IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTION OF THIS CIRCUIT. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT MIA DISRUPTS THE MATURATION OF STRIOSOMAL REGULATION OF DOPAMINE SIGNALING, WITH LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCES FOR BEHAVIORAL VULNERABILITY. THIS WORK WILL ELUCIDATE NOVEL DEVELOPMENTAL MECHANISMS OF DOPAMINE CIRCUIT DISRUPTION AND IDENTIFY POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTRA-INDIVIDUAL DETERMINANTS OF NEURAL OSCILLATION PHENOMENA: A STUDY OF FUNDAMENTAL SYSTEM INTERACTIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY NEURAL OSCILLATIONS PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN EFFORTS TO DERIVE OBJECTIVE MARKERS OF NEUROPSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS, TREATMENT MONITORING, AND OUTCOME. IN ADHD, FOR INSTANCE, THETA-BETA RATIO (TBR) IS USED AS AN INDEX OF HYPO- AROUSAL IN AN FDA-CLEARED DIAGNOSTIC AID, ALPHA (8-12HZ) POWER IN ASSESSMENT OF INATTENTION, AND SPECTRAL SLOPE, IN PARTICULAR FLATTENING, AS AN INDICATOR OF INTERFERENCE FROM NEURAL NOISE. YET, THE PREDICTIVE POWER OF THESE METRICS IS DEBATED, IN PART DUE TO SAMPLE HETEROGENEITY. EMERGING STUDIES POINT TO A SECOND CRITICAL BUT SPARSELY EXAMINED FACTOR, MEASUREMENT HETEROGENEITY, WITH EVIDENCE SUGGESTING CONTRIBUTIONS OF AROUSAL TO SPECTRAL SLOPE, AND MOTORIC ACTIVATION (E.G., FIDGETING) TO ALPHA POWER. THE CURRENT PROJECT TACKLES THIS PROBLEM BY (I) DEPLOYING MULTI-SENSOR MEASUREMENTS THAT CONCURRENTLY CAPTURE OBJECTIVE MEASURES OF AROUSAL (HEART RATE/VARIABILITY, GALVANIC SKIN RESPONSE, PUPIL METRICS), MOTOR ACTIVATION (BODY, LIMB, AND HEAD DISPLACEMENT & VARIABILITY) AND NEURAL OSCILLATIONS, AND (II) SAMPLING THESE MEASURES REPEATEDLY IN THE SAME INDIVIDUAL OVER A PERIOD OF 6 MONTHS TO CAPTURE WITHIN-SUBJECT VARIATION CORRESPONDING TO SYSTEM INTERACTIONS. USING THESE DATA, WE AIM TO (1) IDENTIFY THE ROLE OF MOTOR AND AROUSAL SYSTEM CONTRIBUTIONS TO VARIABILITY IN NEURAL OSCILLATIONS (TBR, ALPHA POWER, SPECTRAL SLOPE), AND (2) DETERMINE THE ROLE OF MOTOR AND AROUSAL SIGNALS IN THE PREDICTION OF BEHAVIORAL OUTCOMES FROM NEURAL OSCILLATIONS. THE OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT WILL SPEAK TO WHETHER RECONSIDERATION IS WARRANTED OF DOMINANT INTERPRETATIONS (NEURAL NOISE, HYPO-AROUSAL, VISUAL ATTENTION) OF NEURAL OSCILLATIONS, AND WILL MODEL AN APPROACH OF NESTING WITHIN-SUBJECT DESIGNS IN ADDRESSING INDIVIDUAL VARIABILITY QUESTIONS. THE PROJECT IS ALIGNED WITH A PATIENT-CENTERED, PRECISION-NEUROSCIENCE FRAMEWORK, THAT AIMS TO ENHANCE PRECISION OF BIOMARKER DISCOVERY.

description: ADVANCING YOUTH PSYCHIATRIC RESEARCH: A CO-DESIGN APPROACH TO CREATE A NEW DEVELOPMENTALLY-TAILORED AND ECOLOGICALLY-VALID ADOLESCENT EMOTIONAL FACES STIMULUS SET - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ADOLESCENCE IS A KEY PERIOD FOR THE ESCALATION OF PSYCHIATRIC CONDITIONS, INCLUDING DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, AND SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS (STBS), WHICH ARE INCREASINGLY PREVALENT AND PREDICTIVE OF CONTINUED IMPAIRMENT AND MORTALITY IN ADULTHOOD. CONCURRENTLY, ADOLESCENTS UNDERGO MAJOR NEURODEVELOPMENTAL CHANGES THAT IMPACT HOW THEY PROCESS SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL CUES AND ARE LINKED WITH PSYCHIATRIC RISK. THEREFORE, TO ADDRESS THE ADOLESCENT MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS, WE NEED TO UNDERSTAND THE NEUROBEHAVIORAL SOCIOAFFECTIVE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING PSYCHIATRIC RISK IN ADOLESCENTS. TO THIS END, RESEARCHERS LEVERAGE VALIDATED EMOTIONAL FACES STIMULI (I.E., IMAGES OF FACIAL DISPLAYS OF EMOTION); HOWEVER, MOST AVAILABLE STIMULI WERE LARGELY MADE FOR RESEARCH WITH ADULTS AND DEPICT ADULT FACES. THESE STIMULI DO NOT REFLECT OR PROVIDE ADEQUATE INSIGHT INTO ADOLESCENTS’ SOCIOAFFECTIVE PROCESSING IN THEIR SALIENT SOCIAL CONTEXT: PEERS. RESEARCHERS NEED EMOTIONAL FACE STIMULI TAILORED TO ADOLESCENTS’ DEVELOPMENTAL SOCIAL CONTEXT TO TEST ADOLESCENT-SPECIFIC SOCIOAFFECTIVE MECHANISMS OF RISK THAT CAN OPTIMIZE EARLY IDENTIFICATION AND TREATMENT OF PSYCHOPATHOLOGIES. THE GOALS OF THIS PROJECT ARE TWOFOLD. THE FIRST GOAL IS TO DEVELOP, REFINE, AND VALIDATE A NEW DEVELOPMENTALLY-TAILORED AND ECOLOGICALLY-VALID ADOLESCENT EMOTIONAL FACES STIMULUS SET, WITH INPUT FROM A YOUTH ADVISORY BOARD AND A SCIENTIST STAKEHOLDER ADVISORY BOARD. THE SECOND GOAL IS TO EXAMINE THE EXTENT TO WHICH SOCIOAFFECTIVE PROCESSING OF THESE NEW STIMULI PREDICTS UNIQUE VARIANCE IN ADOLESCENT SYMPTOMS OF ANXIETY, SYMPTOMS OF DEPRESSION, CURRENT LEVELS OF SUICIDAL IDEATION, AND LIFETIME HISTORY OF STBS. STIMULI WILL REFLECT TEENS’ SALIENT SOCIAL PARTNERS (I.E., PEERS) AND ADDRESS GAPS IDENTIFIED BY SCIENTISTS CONDUCTING DEVELOPMENTAL SOCIOAFFECTIVE PROCESSING RESEARCH ACROSS DISCIPLINES. IN PHASE 1, WE WILL SOLICIT INPUT FROM ADOLESCENT AND SCIENTIST STAKEHOLDERS IN A CO-DESIGN APPROACH TO DEVELOP A STIMULUS SET THAT BEST REFLECTS ADOLESCENTS’ REAL-WORLD PEERS. IN PHASE 2, WE WILL RECRUIT ADOLESCENTS TO MODEL FOR THE STIMULI. IMAGES WILL BE VALIDATED (E.G., EMOTION IDENTIFICATION, REPRESENTATIVENESS OF PEERS AND EMOTION) BY AGE-MATCHED YOUTH AND ADULTS. TO ENSURE EFFICIENCY AND FEASIBILITY OF STIMULUS DEVELOPMENT WITHOUT NEEDING TO RECRUIT EXCESS MODELS, STIMULI WILL BE ITERATIVELY REFINED USING IN-HOUSE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) PIPELINES. AI WILL ALSO BE USED TO ADD BACKGROUNDS TO STIMULI TO CREATE ALTERNATIVE, CONTEXTUALIZED VERSIONS (E.G., BEDROOM, PARK). IN PHASE 3, A SAMPLE OF 75 YOUTH ENRICHED FOR ANXIETY/DEPRESSION SYMPTOMS AND STBS WILL COMPLETE AN ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAM LAB VISIT. YOUTH WILL COMPLETE SYMPTOM MEASURES AND VIEW PREVIOUSLY VALIDATED ADULT FACES AS WELL AS NEW ADOLESCENT STIMULI (WITH AND WITHOUT CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUNDS). THE LATE POSITIVE POTENTIAL (LPP) WILL BE USED AS A NEURAL INDEX OF AFFECTIVE PROCESSING, GIVEN THAT THE LPP IS ASSOCIATED WITH YOUTH DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, AND STBS WHEN EXAMINED IN RESPONSE TO FACES. STIMULI WILL BE MADE FREELY AVAILABLE TO RESEARCHERS TO FACILITATE NEW DEVELOPMENTAL SOCIOAFFECTIVE PROCESSING RESEARCH EXAMINING PREVIOUSLY UNTESTABLE QUESTIONS, INCLUDING MECHANISMS OF ADOLESCENT PSYCHIATRIC RISK, DEVELOPMENTAL TRAJECTORIES, AND INDICATORS OF TREATMENT RESPONSE.

description: DEVELOPING METHODS FOR TRACKING BRAIN LIPIDS IN VIVO - PROJECT SUMMARY NEURONS AND GLIA CONTAIN THOUSANDS OF LIPIDS TO SUPPORT UNIQUE CELLULAR FUNCTIONS WITHIN SPECIFIC COMPARTMENTS. SPECIFIC LIPIDS CAN DEFINE ORGANELLE IDENTITY, INITIATE SIGNALING PATHWAYS, AND SCULPT CELL MORPHOLOGY AND FUNCTION. ALTHOUGH LIPID DYSREGULATION DRIVES NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES, THE LIPIDOME IS LESS AMENABLE TO GENETIC MANIPULATION AND VISUALIZATION THAN THE PROTEOME. WHERE DO SPECIFIC LIPIDS LIVE AND FUNCTION WITHIN BRAIN CELLS? CAN LIPIDS BE GENETICALLY TRACKED WITH A PRECISION APPROACHING THAT OF TAGGED PROTEINS? THIS PROPOSAL FOCUSES ON CREATING GENETIC TOOLS FOR TAGGING LIPID TAILS AND TRACKING LIPID HEADS IN VIVO. BY GENETIC INDUCTION AND SUBCELLULAR TARGETING OF AN ENZYME THAT MODIFIES LIPID TAILS FOLLOWED BY MASS SPECTROMETRY (“PROXIMITY LIPIDOMICS”), WE WILL DETERMINE LIPIDOMIC DIFFERENCES BETWEEN NEURONS AND GLIA. WE WILL TAG SYNAPTIC VESICLE AND ACTIVE ZONE LIPIDOMES IN NEURONS, AND ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM LIPIDOMES IN GLIA AND NEURONS. IN PARALLEL, BY USING PROTEIN DOMAINS SELECTIVE TO INDIVIDUAL LIPID HEADGROUPS, AND CONTROLS THAT LACK LIPID BINDING CAPACITY, WE WILL CREATE A GENETIC TOOLKIT FOR TRACKING THREE SPHINGOLIPIDS, TWO PHOSPHOLIPIDS, AND FREE STEROLS AT INTRACELLULAR OR EXOPLASMIC LEAFLETS. THESE STUDIES WILL MARKEDLY STRENGTHEN OUR ABILITY TO TRACK LIPIDS IN INTACT BRAINS ACROSS NEURONS AND GLIA WITH UNPRECEDENTED GENETIC CONTROL. IF SUCCESSFUL, THIS PROJECT WILL FACILITATE THE INTERPRETATION OF BULK LIPIDOMICS DATASETS BY ASSIGNING LIPIDS TO SUBCELLULAR HOMES, GENERATE HYPOTHESES FOR LIPID FUNCTION IN SPECIFIC ORGANELLES AND CELLS, AND ILLUMINATE HOW NEURONAL AND GLIAL LIPIDS FUNCTION IN THE BRAIN. THESE STUDIES WILL BROADLY INFORM OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW LIPIDS LOCALIZE TO NEURONS AND GLIA ACROSS HEALTH, AGING, AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES. AS THIS UNDERSTANDING IS FUNDAMENTAL TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF THERAPIES THAT MODULATE LIPIDS OR RELY ON LIPID QUANTITATION, THESE STUDIES WILL STRENGTHEN THE INTERPRETATION AND SELECTION OF LIPID BIOMARKERS, THEREBY SHAPING FUTURE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXPLORATION OF POTENTIAL TREATMENTS TARGETING ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN - PROJECT SUMMARY/ ABSTRACT  PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD), CHARACTERIZED BY Α-SYNUCLEIN (ΑSYN) PROTEINOPATHY AND NIGROSTRIATAL DEGENERATION, IS THE SECOND MOST COMMON NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE. NEARLY ONE MILLION PEOPLE IN THE U.S. HAVE PD, A NUMBER THAT IS EXPECTED TO RISE BY 20% BY 2030. CURRENT TREATMENTS, PRIMARILY L-DOPA AND DOPAMINE AGONISTS, PRIMARILY ADDRESS MOTOR SYMPTOMS OF PD BUT DO NOT AFFECT THE INEXORABLE PROGRESSION OF ΑSYN INCLUSION IN THE BRAIN . THUS, THERE IS A NEED TO DEVELOP NOVEL THERAPEUTICS FOR THE TREATMENT OF PD, ESPECIALLY DISEASE MODIFYING THERAPIES TARGETING PATHOLOGICAL DEPOSITS OF ΑSYN.  LEWY BODIES, A NEUROPATHOLOGICAL HALLMARK OF PD, CONTAIN AGGREGATED ΑSYN PROTEIN, 90% OF WHICH IS PHOSPHORYLATED AT SER129, COMPARED TO <4% IN NORMAL BRAINS. WHILE MULTIPLE KINASES ARE CAPABLE OF PHOSPHORYLATING ΑSYN, A SPECIFIC ISOFORM OF PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE 2A (PP2A), THE MAJOR SERINE/THREONINE PHOSPHATASE IN THE BRAIN, DEPHOSPHORYLATES THIS EPITOPE. VARIOUS PRECLINICAL FINDINGS HAVE CONFIRMED THAT REDUCING ΑSYN PHOSPHORYLATION COULD HAVE THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS. BASED ON THE EVIDENCE THAT PP2A FUNCTION IS COMPROMISED IN PD, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT PHARMACOLOGICALLY RESTORING PP2A FUNCTION WOULD HAVE DISEASE-MODIFYING EFFECTS IN PD.  WE HAVE IDENTIFIED A BRAIN-PENETRANT MACROCYCLIC TETRAPEPTIDE COMPOUND THAT REGULATES PP2A, MAKING IT A PARTICULARLY ATTRACTIVE LEAD COMPOUND TO TARGET ΑSYN DEPHOSPHORYLATION. IN PRELIMINARY STUDIES, THIS LEAD COMPOUND PARTIALLY REDUCED SER129 PHOSPHORYLATION ON ΑSYN AND SIGNIFICANTLY EXTENDED THE LIFESPAN OF MICE SEEDED WITH PREFORMED FIBRILS (PFF) OF ΑSYN IN A DOSE-DEPENDENT MANNER. FOLLOWING UP ON THIS PILOT DATA, THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL INVOLVE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 WILL ESTABLISH IF THE MECHANISM OF ACTION AND FURTHER EXTEND EFFICACY STUDIES IN A SECONDARY PFF-SEEDED MOUSE MODEL WITH NIGROSTRIATAL DEGENERATION. IN AIM 2 WE WILL SCREEN AN EXISTING LIBRARY OF RELATED COMPOUNDS IN PRIMARY NEURONS SEEDED WITH PFFS TO EXPLORE STRUCTURE-ACTIVITY RELATIONSHIPS OF THE LEAD COMPOUND FOR EFFECTS ON ΑSYN IN ORDER TO IDENTIFY COMPOUNDS WITH ENHANCED POTENCY. TOGETHER, THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO CONFIRM IF THESE MACROCYCLIC TETRAPEPTIDE FAMILY OF COMPOUNDS ATTENUATES NIGROSTRIATAL DEGENERATION AND ΑSYN PROPAGATION VIA INFLUENCING PP2A AND ITS SIGNALING PARTNERS. IF SUCCESSFUL, WE EXPECT TO DEMONSTRATE THE PROMISE OF THESE COMPOUNDS AS POTENTIAL THERAPEUTICS TO MITIGATE THE OUTCOMES OF PROGRESSIVE ΑSYN PATHOGENESIS IN THE BRAIN.

description: LATERAL HYPOTHALAMIC NEUROTENSIN NEURONS IN THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF NARCOLEPSY - PROJECT SUMMARY  UNDERSTANDING THE NEURAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING NARCOLEPSY WITH CATAPLEXY (NT1) IS CRUCIAL, CONSIDERING THE DEBILITATING AND LIFE-THREATENING NATURE OF THIS SLEEP DISORDER AND ITS HIGH PREVALENCE. PREVIOUS STUDIES HAVE ESTABLISHED THAT THE LOSS OF OREXINS (OX) IS THE FUNDAMENTAL CAUSE OF NT1 IN HUMANS AND ANIMALS. HOWEVER, THE ROLE OF NEUROTENSIN (NTS)-EXPRESSING NEURONS IN THE LATERAL HYPOTHALAMUS (LH), WHICH ARE RECIPROCALLY CONNECTED WITH OX NEURONS AND PLAY AN ANALOGOUS ROLE IN SLEEP-WAKE REGULATION, IN THE NT1 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY REMAINS UNEXPLORED. BASED ON OUR PRIOR DATA ON NTSLH NEURONS IN SLEEP-WAKE AND MUSCLE TONE CONTROL (NAGANUMA ET AL., 2019, 2025), I HYPOTHESIZED THAT ENHANCING NTSLH NEURON ACTIVITY MITIGATES SLEEPINESS AND CATAPLEXY THAT OCCURS WITH THE LOSS OF OX SIGNALING. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS IN THE PROPOSED EXPERIMENTS AND DETERMINE THE SPECIFIC CONTRIBUTION OF NTSLH SIGNALING IN NT1 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY.  TO EXAMINE IF THE ACTIVITY PATTERN OF NTSLH NEURONS IS ALTERED BY LOSS OF OX SIGNALING AND TO ASSESS ITS CAUSAL ASSOCIATION WITH NT1 SYMPTOMS, IN AIM1, WE WILL EXAMINE THE ACTIVITY DYNAMICS OF NTSLH NEURONS (BOTH AT CELLULAR RESOLUTION AND POPULATION LEVEL) ACROSS SPONTANEOUS SLEEP-WAKE CYCLES, WITH ACUTE SLEEP-DEPRIVATION (TO INDUCE SLEEPINESS), AND IN THE PRESENCE OF POSITIVE EMOTIONAL STIMULI THAT ENHANCE CATAPLEXY IN NORMAL MICE AND IN A MOUSE MODEL OF NARCOLEPSY (OXKO MICE). TO DETERMINE THE CAUSAL ROLE OF NTSLH NEURONS IN ATTENUATING CATAPLEXY AND SLEEPINESS, IN AIM 2, WE WILL SELECTIVELY ACTIVATE OR INHIBIT THE NTSLH NEURONS IN OXKO MICE USING BOTH OPTOGENETIC AND CHEMOGENETIC METHODS AND STUDY THE IMPACT ON SLEEP-WAKE BEHAVIOR AND CATAPLEXY. THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL IDENTIFY A NOVEL POPULATION OF LH NEURONS INVOLVED IN ALLEVIATING THE PRIMARY SYMPTOMS OF NT1, THEREBY, REVEALING NOVEL PHARMACOLOGICAL TARGETS FOR THE MANAGEMENT AND/OR TREATMENT OF THIS DISORDER.

description: ELUCIDATING NOVEL IMMUNOMODULATORY MECHANISMS OF NEONATAL FC RECEPTOR BLOCKADE BY EFGARTIGIMOD IN A T CELL-MEDIATED DEMYELINATING NEUROPATHY MODEL - PROJECT SUMMARY INFLAMMATORY DEMYELINATING NEUROPATHIES, SUCH AS ACUTE INFLAMMATORY DEMYELINATING POLYNEUROPATHY (AIDP), ALSO KNOWN AS THE DEMYELINATING FORM OF GUILLAIN-BARRÉ SYNDROME (GBS), AND CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY DEMYELINATING POLYNEUROPATHY (CIDP), ARE CHARACTERIZED BY IMMUNE-MEDIATED DAMAGE TO PERIPHERAL NERVES. THIS DAMAGE IS LARGELY DRIVEN BY CELLULAR IMMUNE FACTORS, INCLUDING DYSREGULATED T CELL RESPONSES AND THE PATHOLOGICAL ACTIVATION OF MACROPHAGES THAT CONTRIBUTE TO MYELIN DEGRADATION THROUGH PHAGOCYTOSIS. EFGARTIGIMOD, A RECOMBINANT HUMAN IGG1 FC FRAGMENT, ENHANCES IGG CLEARANCE BY INHIBITING THE NEONATAL FC RECEPTOR (FCRN) AND WAS RECENTLY APPROVED FOR THE TREATMENT OF CIDP IN THE USA. A CLINICAL STUDY SHOWED THAT EFGARTIGIMOD INDUCED CLINICAL IMPROVEMENT IN 67% OF CIDP PATIENTS, MOST OF THEM PREVIOUSLY WITHDRAWN FROM INTRAVENOUS IMMUNOGLOBULIN THERAPY. HOWEVER, IT IS IMPORTANT TO NOTE THAT AUTOANTIBODIES ARE DETECTED IN ONLY A SMALL SUBSET OF CIDP PATIENTS, SUGGESTING THAT EFGARTIGIMOD’S EFFECTS LIKELY EXTEND BEYOND JUST IGG AUTOANTIBODY CLEARANCE. NOTABLY, RESEARCH HAS HIGHLIGHTED THE SIGNIFICANT ROLE OF FCRN IN MODULATING CELLULAR IMMUNE RESPONSES, INCLUDING MACROPHAGE PHAGOCYTOSIS, AND ANTIGEN PRESENTATION BY CLASSICAL DENDRITIC CELLS (CDCS), WHICH ACTIVATE CD4+ AND CD8+ T CELLS. THUS, FCRN INHIBITION BY EFGARTIGIMOD MAY PROVIDE BROADER IMMUNOMODULATORY BENEFITS IN INFLAMMATORY NEUROPATHIES. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT EFGARTIGIMOD MEDIATED FCRN INHIBITION LEADS TO: 1) REDUCED MYELIN PHAGOCYTOSIS BY MACROPHAGES; 2) ALTERED ANTIGEN PRESENTATION BY CDCS, WHICH MITIGATES THE EXCESSIVE T CELL RESPONSES SEEN IN INFLAMMATORY NEUROPATHIES. TO TEST OUR HYPOTHESES, AIM 1 WILL EXAMINE THE EFFICACY OF EFGARTIGIMOD IN THE SPONTANEOUS AUTOIMMUNE PERIPHERAL POLYNEUROPATHY (SAPP) MODEL, WHICH MIMICS CIDP AND DEMYELINATING GBS; AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE WHETHER FCRN BLOCKADE WITH EFGARTIGIMOD COULD MODULATE ENDONEURIAL MACROPHAGE PHAGOCYTOSIS AND T CELL ACTIVATION IN SAPP ANIMALS. ADDITIONALLY, THE ANTIGEN PRESENTATION BY CDCS FOLLOWING EFGARTIGIMOD TREATMENT WILL BE EXAMINED BY AN IN-VITRO ASSAY. OUR APPROACHES WILL INCLUDE COMPREHENSIVE FLOW CYTOMETRY ANALYSIS OF MURINE SCIATIC NERVES AND SPLEEN, IN-VITRO ANTIGEN PRESENTATION ASSAY, ALONGSIDE BEHAVIORAL, ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL AND HISTOLOGICAL ASSESSMENTS. THIS TRANSLATIONAL STUDY AIMS TO ELUCIDATE THE IMMUNOMODULATORY MECHANISMS OF EFGARTIGIMOD-MEDIATED FCRN INHIBITION BEYOND IGG CLEARANCE, A CRITICAL STEP TOWARD DEVELOPING MORE PRECISE AND TARGETED THERAPIES FOR CIDP AND RELATED INFLAMMATORY DEMYELINATING NEUROPATHIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AAV-MEDIATED GENE SILENCING FOR THE TREATMENT OF HYPOMYELINATION WITH ATROPHY OF THE BASAL GANGLIA AND CEREBELLUM (H-ABC) - HYPOMYELINATION WITH ATROPHY OF THE BASAL GANGLIA AND CEREBELLUM (H-ABC) IS A RARE LEUKODYSTROPHY CAUSED BY SPORADIC MUTATIONS IN THE TUBB4A GENE. TUBB4A IS MAINLY EXPRESSED IN THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. THE BRAIN REGIONS WITH THE HIGHEST EXPRESSION ARE THE WHITE MATTER, CEREBELLUM, AND BASAL GANGLIA. ITS EXPRESSION IS FOUND IN NEURONS AND OLIGODENDROCYTES, AND MUTATIONS LEAD TO DEFICITS IN BOTH CELL TYPES. MUTATIONS IN TUBB4A DISRUPT THE MECHANICAL AND DYNAMIC PROPERTIES OF MICROTUBULES AND ARE LINKED TO A RANGE OF NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS. H- ABC IS A PROGRESSIVE NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE AT THE SEVERE END OF THE TUBB4A-RELATED LEUKODYSTROPHY SPECTRUM. CHILDREN WITH H-ABC GRADUALLY LOSE CONTROL OF THEIR MOTOR SKILLS, LOSING THE ABILITY TO SIT, STAND, TALK, OR WALK INDEPENDENTLY. ULTIMATELY, CHILDREN WITH H-ABC OFTEN DO NOT SURVIVE INTO ADULTHOOD. CURRENTLY, THERE ARE NO FDA- APPROVED TREATMENTS THAT CAN EFFECTIVELY MODIFY THE DISEASE’S COURSE. TO ADDRESS THIS ISSUE, WE WILL DEVELOP AN ADENO-ASSOCIATED VIRUS (AAV)-MEDIATED GENE-SILENCING APPROACH TO TREAT THIS DEVASTATING DISEASE. MUTATIONS IN TUBB4A ARE TOXIC. DOWNREGULATING TUBB4A WITH AAV-DELIVERED ARTIFICIAL MIRNAS (AMIRS) CAN EFFICIENTLY REDUCE GENE EXPRESSION ACROSS MULTIPLE CELL TYPES AND OFFER LONG-TERM THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS WITHOUT ANY KNOWN HARMFUL EFFECTS. CONSIDERING THE GENETIC CAUSE AND THE CNS FEATURES OF H-ABC, I HAVE DESIGNED AN AAV9 VECTOR TO DELIVER AMIR-TUBB4A TO SUPPRESS TUBB4A AS A TREATMENT FOR H- ABC. THE AAV9-AMIR-TUBB4A VECTOR HAS SHOWN PROMISE BY EXTENDING SURVIVAL, INCREASING BODY WEIGHT GAIN, AND DELAYING SEIZURE ONSET IN DISEASED ANIMALS THROUGH DELIVERY TO OLIGODENDROCYTES. NONETHELESS, THE THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS NEED FURTHER ENHANCEMENT BEFORE PROGRESSING TO THE NEXT STAGE. RECENTLY, AN AAV CAPSID (BI-HTFR1) WAS DEVELOPED TO BIND TO THE HUMAN TRANSFERRIN RECEPTOR (HTFR1), WHICH IS EXPRESSED ON THE BLOOD- BRAIN BARRIER. BI-HTFR1 DEMONSTRATES 40 TO 50 TIMES HIGHER REPORTER EXPRESSION THAN AAV9 IN THE CNS OF HUMAN TFRC KNOCK-IN MICE. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT SILENCING TUBB4A IN BOTH NEURONS AND OLIGODENDROCYTES USING A HIGHLY EFFECTIVE AAV CAPSID COULD SIGNIFICANTLY RESCUE THE EFFECTS OF H-ABC. THE RESEARCH AIM IS TO DEVELOP A BI-HTFR CAPSID-BASED, IV-DELIVERABLE, EFFECTIVE, AND SAFE GENE THERAPY FOR TREATING H-ABC IN A PRECLINICAL MOUSE MODEL. WE WILL CONTINUE TO IDENTIFY EFFECTIVE AMIR-TUBB4A AND GENERATE THE VECTOR GENOME EXPRESSING AMIR-TUBB4A IN BOTH NEURONS AND OLIGODENDROCYTES FOR PACKAGING INTO BI-HTFR1 CAPSID. WE WILL CROSS THE TUBB4A-D249N MICE WITH TFRC KI MICE TO GENERATE THE HABC-TFRC MICE THAT CAN BE TRANSDUCED BY BI-HTFR1 CAPSID. WE WILL EVALUATE ITS THERAPEUTIC OUTCOMES IN HABC-TFRC MICE AND THE SAFETY PROFILE IN TFRC KI MICE. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT MAY LEAD TO A CLINICAL TRIAL FOR THE TREATMENT OF HUMAN H-ABC.

description: EXTRACELLULAR VESICLE-ENHANCED MITOCHONDRIAL THERAPY FOR ALS AND NEURODEGENERATION - PROJECT SUMMARY NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES (NDS), SUCH AS AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (ALS), ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, AND PARKINSON’S DISEASE, ARE CHARACTERIZED BY PROGRESSIVE LOSS OF NERVE CELLS (NEURONS) IN THE BRAIN AND SPINAL CORD, LEADING TO SEVERE DECLINE IN MOVEMENT, MEMORY AND COGNITION. DESPITE THEIR SIGNIFICANT SOCIETAL AND PERSONAL IMPACT, EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS REMAIN ELUSIVE MAINLY DUE TO THE COMPLEXITY OF DISEASE MECHANISMS AND THE CHALLENGE OF DELIVERING THERAPEUTICS TO AFFECTED CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS). MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION IS A CENTRAL DRIVER OF NEURONAL DEGENERATION, AND MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSPLANTATION, INTRODUCING HEALTHY MITOCHONDRIA INTO DAMAGED CELLS, HAS SHOWN THERAPEUTIC PROMISE IN PRECLINICAL ND MODELS. HOWEVER, ITS TRANSLATIONAL APPLICATION IS LIMITED BY INEFFICIENT CNS DELIVERY, RESULTING FROM POOR PENETRATION OF THE BLOOD BRAIN BARRIER (BBB), MITOCHONDRIAL INSTABILITY, AND LIMITED CELLULAR UPTAKE. TO ADDRESS THESE LIMITATIONS, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A NOVEL EXTRACELLULAR VESICLE (EV)-BASED PLATFORM FOR MITOCHONDRIAL DELIVERY. EVS ARE NATURAL INTERCELLULAR COMMUNICATORS, CAPABLE OF CROSSING CELL MEMBRANES AND THE BBB TO DELIVER BIOACTIVE MOLECULES, SUCH AS NUCLEIC ACIDS, PROTEIN, AND EVEN ORGANELLES LIKE MITOCHONDRIA, BETWEEN CELLS. NOTABLY, EVS DERIVED FROM NEURAL PROGENITOR CELLS (NPC- EVS) POSSESS INTRINSIC NEUROPROTECTIVE AND REGENERATIVE PROPERTIES INHERITED FROM PARENT CELLS, MITIGATING NEURONAL DEATH AND DISEASE PROGRESSION IN PRECLINICAL MODELS OF NDS. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT CO- INCUBATION OF EVS WITH ISOLATED MITOCHONDRIA SIGNIFICANTLY ENHANCES MITOCHONDRIAL UPTAKE BY NEURAL CELLS IN VITRO AND BRAIN ACCUMULATION IN VIVO FOLLOWING NON-INVASIVE INTRANASAL ADMINISTRATION. BUILDING ON THESE FINDINGS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT NPC-EV-BASED MITOCHONDRIAL DELIVERY WILL IMPROVE CNS TARGETING AND THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY BY COMBINING THE BIOENERGETIC BENEFITS OF MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSPLANTATION WITH THE INTRINSIC DELIVERY AND THERAPEUTIC PROPERTIES OF NPC-EVS. IN THE PROPOSED STUDY, WE WILL (1) ENHANCE THE ASSOCIATION OF MITOCHONDRIA WITH NPC- EVS VIA SURFACE MODIFICATION TO IMPROVE DELIVERY TO THE CNS, AND (2) EVALUATE THE THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY OF NPC- EV-MEDIATED MITOCHONDRIAL DELIVERY IN ESTABLISHED CELLULAR AND MOUSE MODELS OF ALS. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS STUDY WILL ESTABLISH PROOF-OF-CONCEPT FOR NPC-EV-BASED MITOCHONDRIAL THERAPY AIMED AT RESTORING BIOENERGETICS IN DAMAGED NERVE CELLS AND RESCUING NEURONAL VIABILITY AND FUNCTION IN ALS AND POTENTIALLY OTHER NDS. BY OVERCOMING KEY DELIVERY CHALLENGES IN ND TREATMENT, THIS STRATEGY COMBINES THE THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS OF BOTH MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSPLANTATION AND NPC-EVS, HOLDING STRONG PROMISE TO ADVANCE THE CLINICAL TRANSLATION OF MITOCHONDRIAL THERAPIES.

description: DECODING ANTIGEN SPECIFIC CD4+ T CELLS IN TDP-43 PROTEINOPATHY - ABSTRACT AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (ALS) IS A FATAL NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER MARKED BY PROGRESSIVE MOTOR NEURON DEGENERATION AND NEAR-UNIVERSAL MISLOCALIZATION OF THE RNA-BINDING PROTEIN TDP-43. THIS PATHOLOGICAL HALLMARK DISRUPTS RNA SPLICING AND LEADS TO THE PRODUCTION OF CRYPTIC PEPTIDES. WE RECENTLY SHOWED THAT THESE CRYPTIC PEPTIDES ACT AS NEOANTIGENS, TRIGGERING ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC CD8⁺ T CELL RESPONSES AND CYTOTOXICITY TOWARD TDP-43 DEFICIENT NEURONAL CELLS. WHILE THE STIMULATION POTENTIAL OF THESE CRYPTIC PEPTIDES TO CYTOTOXIC CD8+ T CELLS IS BECOMING CLEAR, THE ANTIGENIC TARGET OF CD4⁺ T CELLS, PARTICULARLY REGULATORY T CELLS (TREGS), WHICH ARE REDUCED AND FUNCTIONALLY IMPAIRED IN ALS, REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD. IN THIS PROJECT, WE AIM TO CHART THE LANDSCAPE OF ANTIGENIC EPITOPES DERIVED FROM CRYPTIC PEPTIDES AND IDENTIFY AND VALIDATE CRYPTIC PEPTIDE SPECIFIC CD4⁺ T CELLS, INCLUDING TREGS, BY LEVERAGING OUR HIGH-THROUGHPUT AND HIGH- DIMENSIONAL PMHC CLASS II TETRAMER AND SINGLE-CELL TCR PROFILING PLATFORM (TETTCRII-SEQ-HD). WITH THE RECENT SUCCESS OF LOW-DOSE IL-2 THERAPY IN ALS THAT IS BELIEVED TO STIMULATE TREGS, THIS WORK PROVIDES AN URGENT LINK ON THE ANTIGEN TARGETS THAT TREGS IN ALS RESPOND TO. THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL PROVIDE A VALUABLE RESOURCE TO THE COMMUNITY ON CRYPTIC PEPTIDE SPECIFIC TCRS AND THEIR ANTIGENIC TARGETS THAT WILL ENABLE US TO STUDY THE CONTRIBUTION OF CD4+ T CELLS, ESPECIALLY TREG, TO THE POSSIBLE PROTECTION OF ALS. IT ALSO PROVIDES A VALUABLE SET OF THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR FUTURE IMMUNE ENGINEERING OF TREG BASED IMMUNOMODULATORY THERAPIES IN ALS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISTIC MODULATION OF HIV-ASSOCIATED PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY IN OLDER ADULTS VIA AURICULAR VAGUS NERVE STIMULATION - PROJECT SUMMARY PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY (PN) AFFECTS UP TO 60% OF PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV (PLWH), WITH AGING COMPOUNDING DECLINES IN SENSORY AND AUTONOMIC FUNCTION. HIV-ASSOCIATED PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY (HIV-PN) ARISES FROM NEUROINFLAMMATION, CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM DISINHIBITION, AND AUTONOMIC DYSREGULATION, YET MECHANISTIC BIOMARKERS AND EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS REMAIN ELUSIVE. THIS R21 PROJECT AIMS TO CHARACTERIZE THE MECHANISTIC PATHWAYS THROUGH WHICH AURICULAR VAGUS NERVE STIMULATION (AVNS), A NON-INVASIVE NEUROMODULATION TECHNIQUE, MAY MODULATE HIV-PN IN AGING PLWH. WE WILL CONDUCT A RANDOMIZED, WAITLIST-CONTROLLED MECHANISTIC TRIAL IN 70 ADULTS AGED ≥50 WITH CHRONIC HIV-PN. THE STUDY WILL ASSESS CHANGES IN HEART RATE VARIABILITY (HRV), SHORT INTERVAL INTRACORTICAL INHIBITION (SICI), WIND- UP RATIO (WUR), CONDITIONED PAIN MODULATION (CPM), AND SERUM NEUROINFLAMMATORY MARKERS (NFL, IL-1Β, TNF- Α, IL-6) FOLLOWING AVNS. MACHINE LEARNING APPROACHES WILL BE USED TO DEVELOP MULTIVARIATE BIOMARKER MODELS PREDICTIVE OF INDIVIDUAL MECHANISTIC RESPONSE. THE INNOVATION LIES IN INTEGRATING CENTRAL AND PERIPHERAL BIOMARKERS, LEVERAGING MACHINE LEARNING FOR INDIVIDUALIZED MECHANISTIC PROFILING, AND FOCUSING ON WITHIN-PERSON VARIABILITY RATHER THAN GROUP AVERAGES. THE STUDY WILL PROVIDE FOUNDATIONAL DATA FOR FUTURE MECHANISTIC TRIALS AND INFORM PRECISION NEUROMODULATORY INTERVENTIONS FOR HIV-PN, A DEBILITATING CONDITION DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTING AGING PLWH. THIS RESEARCH ALIGNS WITH NINDS AND NIH OFFICE OF AIDS RESEARCH PRIORITIES TO ELUCIDATE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS IN THE CONTEXT OF HIV AND AGING. RESULTS WILL ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF NEUROIMMUNE INTERACTIONS, INFORM PERSONALIZED INTERVENTIONS, AND ADDRESS CRITICAL GAPS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF HIV-PN IN OLDER ADULTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HEALTH CARE QUALITY AND OUTCOMES AMONG MEDICARE PATIENTS WITH GUILLAIN-BARRÉ SYNDROME - PROJECT SUMMARY GUILLAIN-BARRÉ SYNDROME (GBS) IS A RARE BUT POTENTIALLY SEVERE INFLAMMATORY NEUROPATHY (1 – 2 CASES PER 100,000 ANNUALLY) THAT CAUSES NUMBNESS, MUSCLE WEAKNESS, AND AUTONOMIC DYSFUNCTION. IN SEVERE CASES, IT CAN LEAD TO PARALYSIS, RESPIRATORY FAILURE, OR DEATH. WHILE MOST INDIVIDUALS RECOVER FOLLOWING TREATMENT WITH INTRAVENOUS IMMUNOGLOBULIN OR PLASMA EXCHANGE, OTHERS REMAIN PERMANENTLY DISABLED, AND 1-YEAR MORTALITY RANGES FROM 3 – 20%. BECAUSE GBS IS UNCOMMON, PATIENTS WITH THIS CONDITION ARE A HARD POPULATION TO STUDY. CONSEQUENTLY, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THE EXTENT TO WHICH VARIATION IN CARE DELIVERY EXISTS OR HOW IT IS ASSOCIATED WITH PATIENT OUTCOMES. CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAPS REMAIN REGARDING: 1) THE OCCURRENCE OF DIAGNOSTIC DELAYS AND THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH PATIENT OUTCOMES, 2) FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH VARIATION IN ACUTE HOSPITAL OUTCOMES, AND 3) ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY POST-ACUTE CARE AND ITS ASSOCIATION WITH RECOVERY. MOREOVER, IT IS UNKNOWN WHETHER THESE RELATIONSHIPS DIFFER BETWEEN TRADITIONAL MEDICARE AND MEDICARE ADVANTAGE PLANS, WHICH NOW ENROLL A MAJORITY OF BENEFICIARIES. TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS, WE PROPOSE A NATIONAL RETROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY OF GBS PATIENTS USING TRADITIONAL MEDICARE CLAIMS AND MEDICARE ADVANTAGE ENCOUNTER DATA FROM 2016 – 2024, LINKED WITH FACILITY-LEVEL DATA FROM CMS CARE COMPARE AND THE PROVIDER OF SERVICE FILES AS WELL AS POST-ACUTE PATIENT ASSESSMENT DATA. AIM 1 WILL QUANTIFY DIAGNOSTIC DELAYS AND DETERMINE THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH PATIENT OUTCOMES, INCLUDING MORTALITY AND TIME TO RECOVERY. AIM 2 WILL IDENTIFY PATIENT AND HOSPITAL FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH IN- HOSPITAL MORTALITY AND POTENTIALLY PREVENTABLE HEALTHCARE-ACQUIRED CONDITIONS, HIGHLIGHTING OPPORTUNITIES FOR QUALITY IMPROVEMENT IN ACUTE GBS CARE. AIM 3 WILL EVALUATE PATIENTS’ ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY POST-ACUTE CARE AND ASSESS HOW POST-ACUTE CARE FACTORS, INCLUDING QUALITY, ARE ASSOCIATED WITH RECOVERY, FUNCTIONAL IMPROVEMENT, AND MORTALITY. THE PROPOSED STUDY IS INNOVATIVE IN ITS INTEGRATION OF NATIONAL MEDICARE AND MEDICARE ADVANTAGE DATA WITH COMPREHENSIVE INFORMATION ON HOSPITAL AND POST-ACUTE CARE FACILITY CHARACTERISTICS, QUALITY MEASURES, AND PATIENT-LEVEL HEALTH ASSESSMENT DATA. TOGETHER, THESE LINKAGES WILL ENABLE US TO CONDUCT THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE EVALUATION OF CARE QUALITY AND OUTCOMES FOR GBS ACROSS THE FULL CARE CONTINUUM FROM DIAGNOSIS THROUGH RECOVERY. UNDERSTANDING WHICH GBS PATIENTS ARE AT GREATEST RISK OF EXPERIENCING DIAGNOSTIC DELAYS, ADVERSE EVENTS, AND PROLONGED RECOVERY IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT WILL IDENTIFY KEY POINTS ALONG THE CARE CONTINUUM WHERE CLINICAL AND SYSTEMS-LEVEL INTERVENTIONS, INCLUDING TARGETED QUALITY IMPROVEMENT EFFORTS, PREDICTIVE MODELING, AND DEVELOPMENT OF CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT TOOLS, ARE MOST LIKELY TO IMPROVE PATIENT OUTCOMES FOR THIS POTENTIALLY DEVASTATING CONDITION. BY ADVANCING A DATA-DRIVEN FRAMEWORK TO EVALUATE CARE DELIVERY FOR RARE NEUROLOGICAL CONDITIONS, THIS STUDY WILL ALSO ESTABLISH A GENERALIZABLE APPROACH TO IMPROVING QUALITY AND OUTCOMES FOR OTHER RARE BUT SERIOUS DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A NOVEL PIPELINE FOR ANTIGEN DISCOVERY IN GUILLAIN-BARRÉ SYNDROME USING SINGLE-CELL TCR DATA AND AI-BASED LIGAND PREDICTION - PROJECT SUMMARY GUILLAIN-BARRÉ SYNDROME (GBS) IS A POST-INFECTIOUS AUTOIMMUNE NEUROPATHY AND THE LEADING CAUSE OF ACUTE FLACCID PARALYSIS WORLDWIDE. THE DISEASE IS DRIVEN BY MOLECULAR MIMICRY: AN IMMUNE RESPONSE TO AN ANTECEDENT PATHOGEN (E.G., C. JEJUNI) GENERATES T CELLS AND ANTIBODIES THAT CROSS-REACT WITH STRUCTURALLY SIMILAR SELF-ANTIGENS ON PERIPHERAL NERVES, CAUSING DEMYELINATION AND AXONAL DAMAGE. WHILE THE DISEASE ITSELF IS HIGHLY ANTIGEN- SPECIFIC, CURRENT THERAPIES LIKE PLASMA EXCHANGE (PLEX) AND INTRAVENOUS IMMUNOGLOBULIN (IVIG) ARE ANTIGEN- INDEPENDENT. THEY ACT VIA NON-SPECIFIC REMOVAL OF PLASMA COMPONENTS OR BROAD IMMUNE MODULATION, NOT BY TARGETING THE SPECIFIC, CROSS-REACTIVE T CELLS DRIVING THE PATHOLOGY. THIS FAILURE TO TARGET THE ROOT CAUSE IS WHY UP TO ONE-THIRD OF PATIENTS SUFFER SEVERE, LONG-TERM NEUROLOGICAL DEFICITS. PRIOR RESEARCH HAS BEEN LIMITED BY A FOCUS ON PERIPHERAL BLOOD, A POOR PROXY FOR THE SITE OF PATHOLOGY. OUR PRELIMINARY SINGLE-CELL TCR-SEQ DATA ARE THE FIRST TO SYSTEMATICALLY CHARACTERIZE THE CEREBROSPINAL FLUID (CSF) AT DIAGNOSIS, THE COMPARTMENT IN DIRECT CONTACT WITH THE INFLAMED NERVE ROOTS. THESE DATA REVEAL THE CSF IS HIGHLY ENRICHED WITH CLONALLY EXPANDED, ACTIVATED EFFECTOR T CELLS, BOTH CD4+ AND CD8+, THAT ARE IMMUNOLOGICALLY DISTINCT FROM THE BLOOD. CRITICALLY, OUR IN-SILICO ANALYSIS OF A DOMINANT CD8+ CSF CLONE USING OUR PUBLISHED AI PLATFORM (TCROSS) HAS IDENTIFIED A NOVEL MOLECULAR MIMICRY AXIS: A C. JEJUNI PROTEIN AND THE HUMAN LIPID TRANSPORTER NPC1, WHICH IS ESSENTIAL FOR SCHWANN CELL MYELIN MAINTENANCE. THIS NOVEL LINK PROVIDES A DIRECT MECHANISTIC CONNECTION BETWEEN THE ANTECEDENT INFECTION AND A HIGHLY PLAUSIBLE, MYELIN-ASSOCIATED AUTOANTIGEN. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT DOMINANT, CSF-RESIDENT T CELL CLONES (BOTH CD4+ AND CD8+) RECOGNIZE A DISCRETE SET OF PATHOGENIC ANTIGENS THAT INITIATE AND SUSTAIN THE AUTOIMMUNE ATTACK. WE WILL TEST THIS BY IMPLEMENTING A NOVEL, DUAL-PIPELINE ANTIGEN DISCOVERY PLATFORM. AIM 1 WILL PERFORM A COMPREHENSIVE, LITERATURE-BASED SCREEN BY EXPRESSING DOMINANT CD4+ AND CD8+ CSF TCRS IN ROBUST, TCR-KNOCKOUT CD4+ AND CD8+ REPORTER T CELL LINES, RESPECTIVELY. WE WILL TEST THEIR REACTIVITY IN A VALIDATED APC CO-CULTURE SYSTEM AGAINST A PANEL OF KNOWN GBS-ASSOCIATED PATHOGEN- AND SELF-ANTIGENS. IN PARALLEL, AIM 2 WILL PERFORM AN AI-GUIDED DISCOVERY SCREEN FOCUSED SPECIFICALLY ON THE CD8+ T CELL COMPARTMENT. WE WILL USE THE DOMINANT CD8+ TCR SEQUENCES AS INPUTS FOR OUR PUBLISHED, FIRST-IN-CLASS AI PLATFORM (TCROSS), WHICH IS VALIDATED FOR CD8+ CDR3B SEQUENCES. THIS AIM WILL RIGOROUSLY TEST DE NOVO PREDICTIONS FROM HUMAN AND MICROBIAL PROTEOMES AND VALIDATE OUR NOVEL C. JEJUNI/NPC1 MOLECULAR MIMICRY AXIS. THIS PROJECT WILL BE THE FIRST TO SYSTEMATICALLY DECODE T CELL ANTIGEN SPECIFICITY FROM THE PRIMARY SITE OF INFLAMMATION IN GBS. BY IDENTIFYING THE DISEASE-DRIVING ANTIGENS, THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL NEW INSIGHTS INTO GBS PATHOGENESIS, DELIVER A NEW CLASS OF DIAGNOSTIC BIOMARKERS, AND ESTABLISH THE FOUNDATIONAL TARGETS FOR DEVELOPING FUTURE ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC IMMUNOTHERAPIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS SOUTHWESTERN MEDICAL CENTER

description: POST-VIRAL GUILLAIN-BARRE SYNDROME: HUMAN INBORN ERRORS OF IMMUNITY AND A NEW MODEL OF PATHOGENIC MECHANISM - PROJECT SUMMARY GUILLAIN-BARRÉ SYNDROME (GBS) WAS FIRST DEFINED AS A DISTINCT CLINICAL AND PATHOLOGICAL CONDITION BY THREE FRENCH PHYSICIANS, GUILLAIN, BARRÉ, AND STROHL IN 1916. SINCE THEN, OVER 100 YEARS OF RESEARCH HAS GREATLY IMPROVED THE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL, CLINICAL AND PATHOLOGICAL CHARACTERIZATION OF THIS DISEASE. IT IS NOW LARGELY RECOGNIZED AS AN INFECTION-TRIGGERED, IMMUNE-MEDIATED PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY. APART FROM CAMPYLOBACTER JEJUNI (C. JEJUNI), WHICH ACCOUNTS FOR ~30% OF GBS CASES, VIRAL INFECTION IS ANOTHER MAJOR TRIGGER OF GBS (~30-40%), WITH MORE THAN 10 VIRUSES INVOLVED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO SARS-COV-2 AND THE INFLUENZA, ZIKA, AND CHIKUNGUNYA VIRUSES. THE BLOOD CIRCULATING ANTI-GANGLIOSIDE ANTIBODIES, DETECTED IN ~40-50% OF THE GBS CASES, HAVE BEEN PROPOSED TO BE PATHOGENIC ESPECIALLY IN CASES PRECEDING C. JEJUNI INFECTION. YET, THE ROOT CAUSE OF DISEASE PATHOGENESIS REMAINS UNCLEAR, AS THE GANGLIOSIDE MOLECULAR MIMICRY MODEL REMAINS HYPOTHETICAL, AND THE MECHANISM FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF GBS FOLLOWING INFECTION BY THE VARIOUS VIRUSES IS EVEN MORE UNCLEAR, AS THERE NO MICROBIAL MIMICS OF GANGLIOSIDES HAVE BEEN FOUND. WE DECIDED TO DISSECT THE IMMUNOPATHOGENESIS OF POST-VIRAL GBS FOLLOWING A HUMAN MONOGENIC APPROACH. FROM WHOLE EXOME/GENOME SEQUENCING DATA OF A COHORT OF 22 PATIENTS WITH SARS- COV-2 POST-VIRAL GBS, WE DISCOVERED BI-ALLELIC DAMAGING MUTATIONS IN MAP3K6 AND OPTN, ENCODING MOLECULES CRITICAL IN THE HOST CELLULAR APOPTOSIS OR AUTOPHAGY PATHWAYS, RESPECTIVELY, IN THREE PATIENTS. WE AIM TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT 1) RECESSIVE DEFICIENCIES OF MAP3K6 AND OPTN UNDERLIE GBS PATHOGENESIS IN HUMANS, FOLLOWING INFECTION BY SARS-COV-2, AND PROBABLY OTHER VIRUSES; 2) THE UNDERLYING MECHANISM OF DISEASE MAY BE RELATED TO DEFECTIVE NEURONAL CELL SELF-REMOVAL RESULTING IN LEUKOCYTE-MEDIATED INFLAMMATION AND AUTOIMMUNITY. WE WILL CHARACTERIZE BOTH CANDIDATE GBS-CAUSING INBORN ERRORS OF IMMUNITY (IEIS) THOROUGHLY, TO DISCOVER THE MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, AND IMMUNOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF DISEASE. WE WILL ALSO SEARCH FOR NEW IEIS, RELATED TO MAP3K6 OR OPTN OR NOT, VIA WHOLE GENOME SEQUENCING OF A GROWING COHORT OF PATIENTS WITH GBS FOLLOWING INFECTION BY DIVERSE VIRUSES, AND CHARACTERIZE ALL NEW CANDIDATE IEIS IN GREAT DEPTH. THIS HIGHLY INNOVATIVE PROJECT IS SUPPORTED BY STRONG PRELIMINARY STUDIES. WE HAVE MOST OF THE REQUIRED EXPERIMENTAL TOOLS ESTABLISHED. THE CLARIFICATION OF GBS PATHOGENESIS MECHANISMS DUE TO DEFICIENCIES OF MAP3K6, OPTN AND OTHER RELATED MOLECULES WILL ENABLE US TO GAIN COMPLETELY NEW KNOWLEDGE ABOUT THE MOLECULAR AND CELLULAR BASIS OF THE IMMUNOPATHOLOGY OF POST- VIRAL GBS IN PREVIOUSLY HEALTHY PEOPLE. THE SUCCESSFUL INVESTIGATION OF A NEW MODEL OF GBS PATHOGENESIS MAY ALSO INFORM THE DESIGN OF PREVENTIVE AND THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION STRATEGIES FOR ALL THE AFFECTED INDIVIDUALS, WHILE PAVING THE WAY FOR FURTHER INVESTIGATION OF THE IMMUNOPATHOGENESIS OF GBS FOLLOWING OTHER INFECTIOUS OR NON- INFECTIOUS TRIGGERS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: TRUSTEES OF THE UNIVERSITY OF PENNSYLVANIA, THE

description: IDENTIFYING NEURODEGENERATION ALONG THE PATH OF INTRACRANIAL CST IN ALS PATIENTS USING COMBINED METABOLIC AND MICROSTRUCTURAL TRACTOMETRY - ABSTRACT: AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (ALS) IS A HETEROGENEOUS NEUROLOGICAL DISORDER WITH MANY MIMICS THAT CURRENTLY LACK RELIABLE BIOMARKERS OF UPPER MOTOR NEURON (UMN) INVOLVEMENT. A MULTI-MODAL APPROACH IS THEREFORE ESSENTIAL TO IDENTIFY ALS AND PREDICT DISEASE PROGRESSION. THIS PROJECT PROPOSES A NOVEL DATA ANALYTICAL METHOD THAT FUSES TWO CUTTING-EDGE IMAGING MODALITIES IN ORDER TO PROVIDE A MORE ACCURATE AND LOCALIZED MAPPING OF CORTICOSPINAL TRACT (CST) DAMAGE IN ALS. WE WILL ACHIEVE THIS BY CO-LOCALIZING WHOLE-BRAIN SPECTROSCOPIC IMAGING (WBSI) DATA WITH NEURITE ORIENTATION DISPERSION AND DENSITY IMAGING (NODDI)/DIFFUSION TENSOR IMAGING (DTI)- DERIVED MAPS ALONG THE PATH OF RECONSTRUCTED CST IN ALS PATIENTS. THIS WILL ALLOW FOR A SIMULTANEOUS, VOXEL-BY- VOXEL ANALYSIS OF METABOLITE ALTERATIONS AND MICROSTRUCTURAL INTEGRITY WITHIN THE INTRACRANIAL CST. A COHORT OF 40 ALS (DEFINITE OR PROBABLE) PATIENTS PRESENTING WITH MILD/MODERATE DISEASE SEVERITY AND UMN SYMPTOMS AND 20 AGE/SEX MATCHED HEALTHY INDIVIDUALS WILL UNDERGO ANATOMICAL IMAGING, WBSI AND THREE-SHELL DIFFUSION MRI ON A 3T MRI SYSTEM. FROM THIS DATA, MULTIPLE WBSI AND NODDI/DTI DERIVED PARAMETRIC MAPS WILL BE THEN GENERATED. FOR FURTHER ANALYSIS, ONLY VOXELS WITH A WHITE MATTER (WM) PROBABILITY EXCEEDING 50% WILL BE RETAINED. IN THE NEXT STEP, WHITE MATTER MAPS OF WBSI WILL BE CO-REGISTERED TO NON-DIFFUSION WEIGHTED IMAGE. SUBSEQUENTLY, A PROBABILISTIC TRACKING ALGORITHM WILL BE USED TO RECONSTRUCT BILATERAL INTRACRANIAL CSTS. EACH CST WILL THEN BE DIVIDED INTO FIVE ANATOMICAL REGIONS (SUBCORTICAL WHITE MATTER BELOW PRECENTRAL GYRUS, CENTRUM SEMIOVALE, CORONA RADIATA, POSTERIOR LIMB OF INTERNAL CAPSULE AND CEREBRAL PEDUNCLE). IN AIM 1, THE SPATIAL CONCORDANCE OF WBSI AND NODD/DTI DERIVED PARAMETRIC MAPS ALONG THE PATH OF INTRACRANIAL CST WILL BE QUANTITATIVELY ASSESSED, WITH HIGH VALUES (≥ 0.8) OF IMAGE OVERLAP INDICES INDICATING STRONG SPATIAL ALIGNMENT. IN AIM 2, A TRACTOMETRY FRAMEWORK WILL THEN BE APPLIED TO EXTRACT MULTIPLE WBSI AND NODDI/DTI DERIVED PARAMETRIC TRACT PROFILES. SUBSEQUENTLY, SEGMENT-WISE COMPARISONS WILL BE CONDUCTED ON METABOLITE AND MICROSTRUCTURAL TRACT PROFILES FROM DISTINCT CST REGIONS BETWEEN HEALTHY INDIVIDUALS AND ALS PATIENTS. ASSESSMENT OF DEGENERATION FROM DIFFERENT CST REGIONS IS VITAL FOR EVALUATING DISEASE SEVERITY, AND FOR GUIDING TREATMENT PLANNING. IN AIM 3, DATA FROM THE CST IMAGING ANALYSES ABOVE WILL BE CORRELATED TO PATIENT CLINICAL PARAMETERS INCLUDING THE REVISED ALS FUNCTIONAL RATING SCALE (ALSFRS-R) AS A MEASURE OF OVERALL DISEASE SEVERITY, THE PENN UMN SCORE AS A MEASURE OF UPPER MOTOR DYSFUNCTION, AND THE MONTREAL COGNITIVE ASSESSMENT (MOCA) AS A MEASURE OF NEUROCOGNITIVE FUNCTION. STRONG CORRELATIONS WILL ESTABLISH WBSI- AND NODDI/DTI-DERIVED PARAMETERS AS NON- INVASIVE BIOMARKERS FOR CLINICAL ASSESSMENT IN ALS. OVERALL, THIS STUDY WILL DEVELOP AN IMAGING AND ANALYTICAL PARADIGM TO IDENTIFY ALS-RELATED CHANGES FROM DISTINCT ANATOMICAL REGIONS OF INTRACRANIAL CST, THUS PROVIDING A NOVEL DIAGNOSTIC AND PROGNOSTIC CLINICAL TOOL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REGULATION OF FULL-LENGTH SPASTIN AND THE ETIOLOGY OF HEREDITARY SPASTIC PARAPLEGIA - PROJECT SUMMARY SPASTIN IS A MEMBER OF THE AAA-ATPASE FAMILY OF HEXAMERIC ENZYMES THAT USE ATP HYDROLYSIS TO SEVER MICROTUBULES. SPASTIN REMODELS THE CYTOSKELETON AND PLAYS FUNDAMENTAL ROLES IN SEVERAL CELLULAR PROCESSES, INCLUDING CELL DIVISION AND NEURONAL MORPHOGENESIS. MUTATIONS IN THE SPAST GENE, WHICH ENCODES THE SPASTIN PROTEIN, ARE THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF AUTOSOMAL-DOMINANT HEREDITARY SPASTIC PARAPLEGIA (HSP), A PROGRESSIVE NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY CORTICOSPINAL NEURONAL DEGENERATION AND LOWER LIMB SPASTICITY.  THE COMMONLY POSTULATED ETIOLOGY OF HSP IS THAT MUTATIONS REDUCE MICROTUBULE-SEVERING ACTIVITY. BECAUSE OVEREXPRESSION OF SPASTIN'S AAA-ATPASE DOMAIN FRAGMENTS MICROTUBULES AND LEADS TO THEIR DISAPPEARANCE IN CELLS, A DECREASE IN SEVERING ACTIVITY IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE MICROTUBULE MASS. PARADOXICALLY, HOWEVER, WHEN SPASTIN IS MUTATED OR KNOCKED DOWN IN MANY TISSUES, MICROTUBULE MASS DECREASES. THIS IS DUE TO A SECOND ACTIVITY OF SPASTIN, RECENTLY DISCOVERED IN OUR LAB: SPASTIN ALSO PROMOTES THE REGROWTH OF MICROTUBULE FRAGMENTS, WHICH ACT AS SEEDS, THEREBY INCREASING MICROTUBULE NUMBER AND MASS. DEPENDING ON THE BALANCE OF THE SEVERING AND REGROWTH, SPASTIN CAN EITHER DESTROY OR AMPLIFY THE MICROTUBULE CYTOSKELETON. SPASTIN IS THEREFORE A POTENTIALLY TOXIC PROTEIN WHOSE ACTIVITY MUST BE TIGHTLY CONTROLLED IN CELLS.  CURRENTLY, OUR BIOCHEMICAL AND BIOPHYSICAL UNDERSTANDING OF SPASTIN IS LIMITED BY THE INABILITY TO PURIFY THE FULL-LENGTH PROTEIN, M1. FUNCTIONAL AND STRUCTURAL STUDIES HAVE BEEN LIMITED TO TRUNCATED PROTEINS THAT LACK THE HYDROPHOBIC N-TERMINAL. IN EXCITING NEW RESULTS, WE HAVE BEEN ABLE TO EXPRESS AND PURIFY M1. SURPRISINGLY, WE FOUND THAT PURIFIED M1 HAS ROBUST MICROTUBULE-SEVERING ACTIVITY, EVEN THOUGH ITS EXPRESSION IN CELLS HAS LITTLE EFFECT ON THE MICROTUBULE CYTOSKELETON. M1 MUST BE TURNED OFF IN CELLS. THUS, OUR PRELIMINARY RESULTS SUPPORT OUR HYPOTHESIS THAT SPASTIN'S HYDROPHOBIC N-TERMINUS IS A REGULATORY DOMAIN THAT INHIBITS MICROTUBULE SEVERING AND THAT MISREGULATION MAY UNDERLIE HSP.  TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL PURSUE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: (I) CELLULAR STUDIES WILL IDENTIFY KEY RESIDUES WITHIN THE N-TERMINAL HYDROPHOBIC DOMAIN THAT ARE REQUIRED FOR MEMBRANE ASSOCIATION; AND A CHEMICALLY INDUCIBLE HETERODIMERIZATION SYSTEM WILL TEST WHETHER FORCED RECRUITMENT OF CYTOPLASMIC M87 SPASTIN TO MEMBRANES INHIBITS SEVERING. (II) WE WILL BIND PURIFIED M1 TO LIPOSOMES AND LIPID NANODISCS TO INHIBIT THE SEVERING AND RESCUE ACTIVITIES, AND TEST WHETHER THE HYDROPHOBIC DOMAIN INTERFERES WITH HEXAMERIZATION USING SINGLE-MOLECULE ASSAYS AND NEGATIVE-STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY.  SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS WILL DETERMINE WHETHER MEMBRANE RECRUITMENT IS NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT TO REGULATE SPASTIN'S MICROTUBULE SEVERING AND GROWTH ACTIVITIES. THE IN VITRO STUDIES WILL ELUCIDATE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF REGULATION AND GIVE INSIGHT INTO THE ETIOLOGY OF AXON DEGENERATION IN HSP.

description: UNCOVERING GENETIC VARIATIONS DRIVING CHANNELOPATHY IN THE NALCN COMPLEX - PROGRAM DIRECTOR/PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR (LAST, FIRST, MIDDLE): REN, DEJIAN THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVE OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO ELUCIDATE HOW GENETIC VARIATIONS/MUTATIONS IN THE NALCN CHANNEL COMPLEX CONTRIBUTE TO SEVERE DISORDERS. NALCN ENCODES A MAJOR SODIUM (NA⁺) LEAK CHANNEL THAT REMAINS ACTIVE AT THE RESTING MEMBRANE POTENTIAL (RMP) OF NEURONS. THIS CONDUCTANCE, TOGETHER WITH POTASSIUM (K⁺) CONDUCTANCE, PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN ESTABLISHING THE RMP, WHICH IN TURN REGULATES NEARLY ALL ASPECTS OF NEURONAL PHYSIOLOGY. UNLIKE THE WELL-CHARACTERIZED K⁺ CONDUCTANCES AND VOLTAGE-GATED NA⁺ CHANNELS (NAVS), THE WORKING MECHANISMS OF THE RESTING NA⁺ LEAK CONDUCTANCE HAVE REMAINED POORLY UNDERSTOOD—LIKELY DUE TO ITS RELATIVELY SMALL MAGNITUDE. OUR PREVIOUS WORK IDENTIFIED NALCN AS THE PRINCIPAL DETERMINANT OF THIS RESTING SODIUM CONDUCTANCE IN NEURONS. ALTHOUGH NALCN SHARES STRUCTURAL SIMILARITIES WITH NAVS AND VOLTAGE-GATED CALCIUM CHANNELS (CAVS), IT IS UNIQUE IN MAMMALS IN HAVING NO PARALOGS, SUGGESTING A LACK OF GENETIC REDUNDANCY AND UNDERSCORING ITS ESSENTIAL ROLE IN NEUROPHYSIOLOGY. NALCN FUNCTIONS AS PART OF A LARGER PROTEIN COMPLEX THAT INCLUDES AUXILIARY SUBUNITS UNC80 AND UNC79, WHICH WE IDENTIFIED IN MAMMALIAN BRAINS. RECENT GENETIC STUDIES HAVE LINKED MUTATIONS IN NALCN AND ITS ASSOCIATED SUBUNITS TO SEVERAL SEVERE NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS, INCLUDING IHPRF1 (INFANTILE HYPOTONIA WITH PSYCHOMOTOR RETARDATION AND CHARACTERISTIC FACIES TYPE 1), IHPRF2, AND CLIFAHDD SYNDROME (CONGENITAL CONTRACTURES OF THE LIMBS AND FACE WITH HYPOTONIA AND DEVELOPMENTAL DELAY). THESE CONDITIONS ARE CHARACTERIZED BY PROFOUND HYPOTONIA, ABSENCE OF SPEECH DEVELOPMENT, SEVERE INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY, AND PREMATURE MORTALITY. DESPITE THESE ASSOCIATIONS, THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH THESE GENETIC VARIATIONS LEAD TO DISEASE REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, WE PROPOSE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1: INVESTIGATE HOW CLIFAHDD-ASSOCIATED MUTATIONS IN THE NALCN GENE ALTER ION CHANNEL FUNCTION. AIM 2: DETERMINE HOW IHPRF2-ASSOCIATED MUTATIONS IN THE UNC80 GENE AFFECT ION CHANNEL CONDUCTANCE, SUBCELLULAR LOCALIZATION OF THE PROTEIN COMPLEX IN NEURONAL PROCESSES, AND INTER-SUBUNIT INTERACTIONS. OVERALL, WE AIM TO ESTABLISH OR REFUTE CAUSAL LINKS BETWEEN SPECIFIC GENETIC MUTATIONS AND DISEASE PHENOTYPES. OUR FINDINGS MAY LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF TARGETED THERAPIES FOR THESE DEBILITATING CONDITIONS. PAGE
