description: TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC REGULATION OF NEURAL PROGENITORFATES - IN VERTEBRATE DEVELOPMENT, THE BRAIN FORMS FROM THE ECTODERM GERM LAYER DURING GASTRULATION. WHEN THIS PROCESS GOES AWRY, STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS OCCUR. A KEY GOAL OF DEVELOPMENTAL BIOLOGY IS THEREFORE TO UNDERSTAND THE FUNDAMENTAL PROCESS WHEREBY THE BRAIN DEVELOPS FROM THE ECTODERM. THE GENERALLY ACCEPTED HYPOTHESIS FOR EARLY BRAIN DEVELOPMENT IN VERTEBRATES IS KNOWN AS THE “ACTIVATION- TRANSFORMATION MODEL” AND POSITS THAT ECTODERM IS FIRST ACTIVATED TO ANTERIOR NEURAL FATES BY MESODERM-DERIVED SIGNALS AND THEN TRANSFORMED TO POSTERIOR FATES BY GRADIENTS OF SECRETED FACTORS, BUT IT REMAINS UNCLEAR HOW THESE SIGNALS ARE ‘INTERPRETED’ BY THE ECTODERM TO PRODUCE PROGENITORS FOR DISTINCT BRAIN STRUCTURES.  A MAJOR BARRIER TO PROGRESS IN THIS AREA HAS BEEN THE LACK OF MOLECULAR DATA FOR ECTODERMAL CELLS IN THE PROCESS OF UNDERGOING ACTIVATION-TRANSFORMATION. CHALLENGES IN ASCERTAINING THE IDENTIFY OF CELLS AT EARLY STAGES (WHEN THEY DO NOT YET EXPRESS GENES INDICATIVE OF SPECIFIC FATES), HAVE LEFT US TO INFER THE DETAILS OF EARLY EVENTS BASED ON READ-OUTS LATER IN DEVELOPMENT. WE RECENTLY OVERCAME THIS BARRIER BY CARRYING OUT A SCMULTIOME TIME COURSE ANALYSIS OF ACTIVATION-TRANSFORMATION IN ZEBRAFISH, THEREBY PROVIDING COMPREHENSIVE MOLECULAR PROFILES OF CELLS DURING THIS PROCESS. WE HAVE RESOLVED NEURAL PROGENITORS FROM NEURAL CREST, PLACODAL AND EPIDERMAL PROGENITORS, AND – FOCUSING ON THE DEVELOPING HINDBRAIN – WE HAVE IDENTIFIED DISTINCT PROGENITOR POPULATIONS AT THE END OF GASTRULATION. THESE EARLY PROGENITOR POPULATIONS DO NOT YET EXPRESS HINDBRAIN-RESTRICTED GENES, YET THEY ARE TRANSCRIPTIONALLY DISTINCT FROM EACH OTHER, AND COMPUTATIONAL ANALYSES REVEAL THAT EACH PROGENITOR POPULATION IS RELATED TO DISTINCT LATER-STAGE CELL TYPES THAT FORM DIFFERENT HINDBRAIN STRUCTURES. OUR SCMULTIOME DATA REPRESENT THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE MOLECULAR ANALYSIS OF CELLS UNDERGOING ACTIVATION-TRANSFORMATION AND POSITION US TO ADDRESS KEY UNANSWERED QUESTIONS: WHAT CLASSES OF GENES CHARACTERIZE THE EARLY HINDBRAIN PROGENITOR POPULATIONS? WHAT GENES ARE ACTIVATED BY ACTIVATION-TRANSFORMATION SIGNALS AND WHAT ARE THEIR ROLES? OUR PRELIMINARY DATA ALSO REVEALED THAT THE EARLY PROGENITOR POPULATIONS ARE ONLY BEGINNING TO ESTABLISH UNIQUE PATTERNS OF CHROMATIN ACCESSIBILITY, RAISING THE QUESTIONS: WHAT DRIVES THESE CHROMATIN CHANGES? HOW DO THEY ENSURE THE FORMATION OF DISTINCT NEURAL PROGENITOR POPULATIONS? WE WILL ANSWER THESE QUESTIONS IN THE CONTEXT OF OUR HYPOTHESIS THAT ACTIVATION-TRANSFORMATION SIGNALS ALTER THE CHROMATIN STATE BY INDUCING ACCESSIBLE REGULATORY ELEMENTS THAT DRIVE DISTINCT GENE EXPRESSION PROGRAMS IN NEURAL PROGENITORS. THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF OUR PROJECT WILL ADDRESS CURRENT KNOWLEDGE GAPS AND PROVIDE VITAL INFORMATION TO BETTER UNDERSTAND, DIAGNOSE, AND – ULTIMATELY – TREAT, NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GENE-REGULATORY MECHANISMS OF STEPWISE AXON PATHFINDING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CONNECTIVITY BETWEEN NEURONS AS PART OF NEURAL NETWORKS GOVERNS INFORMATION FLOW THROUGH THE NERVOUS SYSTEM AND SHAPES BEHAVIORAL OUTPUT. GUIDANCE OF AXON TO THEIR TARGETS IS A KEY STEP IN NEURAL CIRCUIT ASSEMBLY DURING EMBRYOGENESIS, AND UNDERSTANDING THIS PROCESS IS CRITICAL, AS NEURONAL MISWIRING CAN CAUSE CIRCUIT DYSFUNCTION AND DISEASE. AXONS ARE STEERED TO THEIR TARGETS BY ATTRACTIVE AND REPULSIVE MOLECULAR CUES THAT ACTIVATE RECEPTORS ON THE AXONAL GROWTH CONE. TO REACH THEIR FINAL DESTINATIONS, NASCENT AXONS PROGRESS THROUGH SERIES OF INTERMEDIATE TARGETS, AND THEY RESPOND TO DISTINCT SETS OF GUIDANCE CUES AS THEY NAVIGATE DIFFERENT LEGS OF THEIR TRAJECTORIES. REGULATING THE AVAILABILITY OF GUIDANCE CUE RECEPTORS ON THE GROWTH CONE HAS BEEN IMPLICATED IN SHAPING DIFFERENTIAL AXON GUIDANCE RESPONSES BEFORE AND AFTER REACHING AN INTERMEDIATE TARGET, BUT IT HAS REMAINED UNCLEAR HOW EXACTLY THIS REGULATION IS ACHIEVED AND WHETHER IT OCCURS AT THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL LEVEL. USING MOUSE SPINAL COMMISSURAL NEURONS AS A MODEL SYSTEM, WE DISCOVERED THAT AXONAL CONTACT WITH THE SPINAL CORD VENTRAL MIDLINE INTERMEDIATE TARGET, THE FLOOR PLATE, CAN INDUCE CHANGES IN AXONAL PROTEIN EXPRESSION IN VITRO THAT MIMIC WHAT IS OBSERVED DURING AXON CROSSING OF THE MIDLINE IN VIVO. FURTHER, WE FOUND THAT COMMISSURAL NEURONS SEQUENTIALLY EXPRESS THE GENES ENCODING AXONAL PROTEINS THAT ARE DEPLOYED BEFORE AND AFTER AXON MIDLINE CROSSING, AND WE IDENTIFIED CANDIDATE TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS FOR REGULATION OF THESE GENES. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUPPORT A MODEL IN WHICH AXON-INTERMEDIATE TARGET CONTACT TRIGGERS CHANGES IN NEURONAL GENE EXPRESSION VIA DEDICATED TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS TO ALTER THE ABUNDANCE OF AXONAL PROTEINS AND THEREBY MODULATE GUIDANCE CUE RESPONSES. WE PROPOSE A MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH TO TEST KEY ASPECTS OF THIS MODEL. WE WILL USE GENE- REGULATORY NETWORK INFERENCE METHODS, GAIN- AND LOSS-OF-FUNCTION APPROACHES IN MOUSE EMBRYOS, AND REPORTER GENE EXPERIMENTS TO IDENTIFY TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS THAT DIRECTLY REGULATE RECEPTOR GENES CRITICAL FOR MIDLINE AXON GUIDANCE. TO PROBE THE CAUSAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN AXON-FLOOR PLATE CONTACT AND COMMISSURAL NEURON TRANSCRIPTOMIC CHANGES, WE WILL PERFORM IN VITRO EXPERIMENTS WITH CULTURED COMMISSURAL NEURONS AND FLOOR PLATE CELLS, AND WE WILL ASSESS COMMISSURAL NEURON GENE EXPRESSION IN MUTANT MICE WITH DISRUPTED AXON-FLOOR PLATE INTERACTIONS IN VIVO. GENERAL APPLICABILITY OF OUR FINDINGS TO OTHER SYSTEMS WILL BE ASSESSED IN THE FUTURE. OUR WORK WILL ELUCIDATE GENE-REGULATORY NETWORKS THAT DYNAMICALLY CONTROL GUIDANCE BEHAVIORS DURING DIFFERENT STAGES OF AXON PATHFINDING, AND IT WILL OPEN UP NEW LINES OF INVESTIGATION INTO THE MECHANISMS THAT MODULATE THE ACTIVITY OF THESE NETWORKS. DATA GENERATED UNDER THESE STUDIES WILL ALSO BE VALUABLE FOR UNDERSTANDING COMMISSURAL NEURON DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTION. BY UNRAVELING BASIC MECHANISMS OF AXON GROWTH AND GUIDANCE, OUR RESEARCH CAN PROVIDE INSIGHTS INTO NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISEASE ETIOLOGY AND INFORM THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES FOR NEURAL CIRCUIT REPAIR.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PREDICTION OF RISK OF INFANT SEIZURES USING MACHINE LEARNING (PRISM) - SEIZURES ARE COMMON NEUROLOGICAL CONCERNS IN NEWBORNS AND ARE EARLY INDICATORS OF BRAIN INJURY WITH AN INCIDENCE OF UP TO 5 INFANTS PER 1000 LIVE BIRTHS AND ARE ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED RISK OF EPILEPSY, CEREBRAL PALSY, DEVELOPMENTAL DELAYS, AND MORTALITY. THOUGH EARLY INTERVENTION CAN IMPROVE NEURODEVELOPMENTAL OUTCOMES, CONTINUOUS ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAPHY (CEEG), THE CURRENT GOLD STANDARD IN SEIZURE DETECTION, IS TIME- CONSUMING AND REQUIRES EXPERT INTERPRETATION THAT IS OFTEN UNAVAILABLE IN MANY NEONATAL INTENSIVE CARE UNITS (NICUS). EXISTING AUTOMATED SEIZURE IDENTIFICATION MODELS FOCUS ON SEIZURE IDENTIFICATION AND NOT RISK PREDICTION. THERE IS A CRITICAL GAP AND URGENT NEED FOR AUTOMATED, REAL-TIME SEIZURE RISK PREDICTION MODELS THAT ARE RELIABLE AND EFFICIENT, ENABLING EARLY RISK-INFORMED INTERVENTIONS. TO ADDRESS THIS, WE PROPOSE THE PREDICTION OF RISK OF INFANT SEIZURES USING MACHINE-LEARNING (PRISM) PROJECT, TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE RELIABLE AND CLINICALLY INTERPRETABLE SEIZURE RISK PREDICTION MODELS USING SHORT EEG (≤1 HOUR) AND MULTIMODAL DATA INTEGRATING VIDEO AND CLINICAL FEATURES WITH SHORT EEG THAT HAS NOT BEEN PREVIOUSLY TESTED. OUR HYPOTHESIS IS THAT SHORT-DURATION EEGS (≤ 60 MINUTES) CONTAIN PREDICTIVE BIOMARKERS OF SEIZURE ONSET WITHIN THE SUBSEQUENT 10 TO 23 HOURS, ACHIEVING CLINICALLY ACTIONABLE DISCRIMINATION (RECEIVER OPERATING CHARACTERISTIC AREA UNDER THE CURVE, ROCAUC ≥ 0.80). TO ENSURE FEASIBILITY, OUR TEAM CONDUCTED A STUDY ON 20 PATIENTS, INCLUDING 10 WITHOUT AND 10 WITH EEG CONFIRMED SEIZURES. FIVE DIFFERENT CLASSIFIERS WERE TRAINED AND TESTED, OUT OF WHICH DECISION TREE USING TIME AND FREQUENCY FEATURES RESULTED AS THE BEST PERFORMING MODEL, ACHIEVING AN ROCAUC 0.78 [CONFIDENCE INTERVAL, CI OF 0.44-1.00], PRECISION-RECALL (PR) AUC 0.71 [0.33-1.00], AND BRIER SCORE 0.23 [0.00-0.53], INDICATING PROMISING RESULTS WITH GOOD DISCRIMINATION AND CALIBRATION, SUGGESTING SHORT EEG CONTAINS INFORMATIVE SIGNALS NEEDED FOR SEIZURE RISK PREDICTION. IN PRISM PROJECT, WE WILL DEVELOP SEIZURE RISK PREDICTION MODEL USING EEG ONLY AND MULTIMODAL MODELS INTEGRATING VIDEO, CLINICAL, AND EEG DATA. FOR BOTH MODELS, WE WILL EXPLORE PERFORMANCE WITH 60, 45, 30, 15, 10, AND 5-MINUTE EPOCHS TO IDENTIFY THE SHORTEST DURATION OF DATA NEEDED TO RELIABLY PREDICT (ROCAUC THRESHOLD ≥ 0.70) SEIZURE RISK. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL EXPLORE MODELS WITH INDIVIDUAL DATA CATEGORIES ALONE (VIDEO ALONE AND CLINICAL VARIABLES ALONE) TO COMPLEMENT THE ANALYSIS IN EEG-ONLY MODEL. IN A SUBSEQUENT STEP, THE BEST-IDENTIFIED MODELS WILL BE DEVELOPED INTO A MODULAR SEIZURE RISK PREDICTION TOOL THAT IS RELIABLE, CLINICALLY INTERPRETABLE, AND CAN BE USED AT THE BEDSIDE. THE PRISM PROJECT WILL PROVIDE EVIDENCE FOR THE USEFULNESS AND EFFECTIVENESS OF MULTIMODAL SEIZURE PREDICTION, GUIDING FUTURE ENDEAVORS TOWARD REAL-TIME, INTEGRATED DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEMS, AND FUTURE MULTICENTER CLINICAL VALIDATION. FURTHERMORE, THIS MODEL COULD SERVE AS A FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE APPLICATIONS IN OLDER INFANTS AND PEDIATRIC POPULATIONS, BROADENING ITS CLINICAL IMPACT. THIS PROJECT ALIGNS WELL WITH NINDS PRIORITIES IN NEONATAL BRAIN INJURY, COMPUTATIONAL NEUROSCIENCE, AND TRANSLATIONAL BIOMARKER DEVELOPMENT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SPINAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING EARLY MOTOR DYSFUNCTION IN ASD - PROJECT SUMMARY (ABSTRACT) AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD) AFFECTS APPROXIMATELY ONE IN 36 CHILDREN, WITH ABOUT 80% EXHIBITING EARLY MOTOR IMPAIRMENTS THAT PRECEDE AND PREDICT LATER SOCIAL AND COMMUNICATION DEFICITS. DESPITE THEIR PREDICTIVE VALUE, THE NEURAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THESE EARLY MOTOR DYSFUNCTIONS REMAIN UNKNOWN. FOUNDATIONAL MOTOR BEHAVIORS SUCH AS MUSCULAR TONE, POSTURE, BALANCE, AND MUSCLE COORDINATION ARE GOVERNED BY SPINAL MOTONEURONS (MNS) AND THEIR DESCENDING EXCITATORY INPUTS FROM THE RETICULOSPINAL AND VESTIBULOSPINAL PATHWAYS, ALL SYSTEMS THAT MATURE EARLY IN LIFE. HOWEVER, THE STRUCTURE, CONNECTIVITY AND MOLECULAR PROFILE OF THESE SPINAL CIRCUITS HAVE NEVER BEEN EXAMINED IN ASD. THIS PROJECT WILL INVESTIGATE THE INTEGRITY AND FUNCTION OF SPINAL MNS AND THEIR DESCENDING INPUTS IN TWO COMPLEMENTARY MOUSE MODELS OF ASD: PRENATAL VALPROIC ACID (VPA) EXPOSURE, REPRESENTING ENVIRONMENTAL/EPIGENETIC RISK, AND THE 16P11.2 DELETION (DEL) MODEL, REPRESENTING A HIGH-CONFIDENCE GENETIC CAUSE. THE WORK INTEGRATES BEHAVIORAL, ANATOMICAL, MOLECULAR, AND PHYSIOLOGICAL ANALYSES TO LINK SPECIFIC CELLULAR AND CIRCUIT ALTERATIONS TO MEASURABLE EARLY MOTOR OUTCOMES. IN AIM 1, WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE DEVELOPMENT OF EARLY MOTOR DEFICITS AND ASSESS MN NUMBER, SPATIAL ORGANIZATION, AND EXPRESSION OF THREE 16P11.2 GENES—MAPK3, TAOK2, AND KCTD13—AT SINGLE-CELL RESOLUTION USING MULTIPLEX RNASCOPE AND IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE. IN AIM 2, WE WILL TEST THE RECRUITMENT AND SYNAPTIC INTEGRITY OF LUMBAR MNS BY RETICULOSPINAL AND VESTIBULOSPINAL PATHWAYS USING EX VIVO CALCIUM IMAGING AND CRE-DEPENDENT SYNAPTOPHYSIN-GFP LABELING OF DESCENDING TERMINALS. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL DEFINE HOW GENETIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL ASD ETIOLOGIES CONVERGE OR DIVERGE AT THE LEVEL OF SPINAL MOTOR CIRCUITS. BY ESTABLISHING CAUSAL LINKS BETWEEN SPECIFIC CIRCUIT DEFICITS AND EARLY MOTOR PHENOTYPES, THE PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY BIOMARKERS OF ATYPICAL MOTOR DEVELOPMENT AND PROVIDE A FOUNDATION FOR TARGETED EARLY INTERVENTIONS IN ASD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING THE ROLE OF MN1 IN CNS DEVELOPMENTAL MALFORMATIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY  MN1 C-TERMINAL TRUNCATION (MCTT) SYNDROME IS A RECENTLY DEFINED INTELLECTUAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITY (IDD) SYNDROME CHARACTERIZED BY CRANIOFACIAL DYSMORPHOLOGY, IDD, EPILEPSY, AND TWO SIGNIFICANT BRAIN MALFORMATIONS: POLYMICROGYRIA (PMG) AND RHOMBENCEPHALOSYNAPSIS (RES). THESE PHENOTYPES ARE ABSENT IN MN1 LOSS OF FUNCTION CARRIERS. MN1 ENCODES A WIDELY EXPRESSED, INTRINSICALLY DISORDERED PROTEIN THAT ACTS AS A TRANSCRIPTION COREGULATOR, WITH VARIOUS MUTATIONS AND OVEREXPRESSION LINKED TO LEUKEMIA, MENINGIOMA, AND PRIMITIVE NEURO-ECTODERMAL TUMORS. HOMOZYGOUS NULL MUTANT MICE SHOW PALATE FUSION, SKULL OSTEOBLAST DEFICITS AND HINDBRAIN SEGMENTATION DEFECTS. CEREBELLAR AND CEREBRAL CORTEX PHENOTYPES HAVE NEVER BEEN ASSESSED. SEVERAL KNOWLEDGE GAPS EXIST. HERE WE PROPOSE TO COMPARE MN1 NULL AND C-TERMINAL TRUNCATION MUTANT MICE FOR CEREBELLAR AND CEREBRAL CORTEX PHENOTYPES TO INFER ROLES FOR MN1 IN HUMAN NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS.  WE RECENTLY GENERATED THE FIRST MOUSE MODELS OF MCTT. OUR PILOT DATA SHOWS CEREBRAL CORTEX AND CEREBELLAR DEFICITS. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO ELUCIDATE THE DYSREGULATED DEVELOPMENTAL PROGRAMS LEADING TO BRAIN MALFORMATION IN THE NULL AND MCTT-ALLELES OF MN1. PMG AND RES ARE CLINICALLY IMPORTANT, YET UNDERSTUDIED BRAIN MALFORMATIONS. INDEED, THERE ARE CURRENTLY NO MOUSE MODELS OF RES AND CURRENT MOUSE-CENTRIC PARADIGMS OF CEREBELLAR DEVELOPMENT SUGGEST THAT RES SHOULD BE AN IMPOSSIBLE PHENOTYPE. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT DEFINING THE BRAIN DEVELOPMENTAL PATHOGENESIS IN MN1 MUTANT MOUSE MODELS WILL REVEAL NOVEL, YET RELATED DEVELOPMENTAL DISRUPTIONS ACROSS BRAIN REGIONS. WE PROPOSE A COMPREHENSIVE STUDY TO DEFINE POST-NATAL AND DEVELOPING CEREBRAL CORTEX AND CEREBELLAR PHENOTYPES OF NULL AND MCTT MUTANT MICE USING A RANGE OF METHODOLOGIES INCLUDING LIGHT SHEET MICROSCOPY, IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY AND IN SITU ANALYSES. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL DEFINE DISRUPTED DEVELOPMENTAL PROGRAMS UNDERLYING PMG AND RES BRAIN MALFORMATIONS, PROVIDING CRITICAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE FUNCTION OF THE MN1 GENE IN MCTT SYNDROME, WITH BROADER SIGNIFICANCE TO THE PATHOGENESIS OF BOTH PMG AND RES ACROSS MULTIPLE IDD SYNDROMES. MOREOVER, THE MCTT MUTANT MICE DEVELOPED IN THIS STUDY WILL SERVE AS IMPORTANT NEW RESOURCES FOR THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY, ADVANCING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF BRAIN DEVELOPMENT AND IDD SYNDROMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING GENES AND NEURONS ASSOCIATED WITH CIRCADIAN CHRONOTYPE ACROSS DROSOPHILA SPECIES - PROJECT SUMMARY INDIVIDUAL PEOPLE EXHIBIT VARIATION IN DAILY TIMING PREFERENCES RANGING FROM MORNING “LARKS” TO EVENING “OWLS”. THESE PREFERENCES REPRESENT STABLE CHRONOTYPES THAT INFLUENCE HEALTH RISK AND DAILY PERFORMANCE. THE FRUIT FLY DROSOPHILA MELANOGASTER IS A FOUNDATIONAL GENETIC MODEL THAT HAS YIELDED DETAILED MECHANISTIC INSIGHT INTO THE GENES AND NEURAL CIRCUITS UNDERLYING CIRCADIAN TIMEKEEPING. UNDER STANDARD LIGHT–DARK CYCLES, D. MELANOGASTER DISPLAYS TWO LOCOMOTOR ACTIVITY PEAKS—ONE NEAR DAWN AND ONE NEAR DUSK—THAT ARE TYPICALLY SIMILAR IN AMPLITUDE. BECAUSE WILD‑TYPE POPULATIONS OF D. MELANOGASTER SHOW LIMITED VARIATION IN THE RELATIVE SIZE OF THESE PEAKS, THEY OFFER FEW OPPORTUNITIES FOR IDENTIFYING GENETIC DETERMINANTS OF CHRONOTYPE. TO OVERCOME THIS CONSTRAINT, OUR PROJECT EXPANDS EXPERIMENTAL FOCUS TO INVESTIGATE CHRONOTYPE VARIABILITY ACROSS MANY SPECIES OF THE DROSOPHILIDAE FAMILY INSTEAD OF A SINGLE MODEL SPECIES. WE QUANTIFIED LOCOMOTOR ACTIVITY IN 63 RELATED DROSOPHILID SPECIES AND OBSERVED A WIDE SPECTRUM OF CHRONOTYPES, FROM STRONGLY MORNING‑BIASED TO STRONGLY EVENING‑BIASED PATTERNS. THESE RESULTS REVEAL SUBSTANTIAL PHENOTYPIC VARIATION WITHIN A SINGLE PHYLOGENETIC FAMILY, PROVIDING NEW OPPORTUNITIES TO EXAMINE GENES AND CELLS THAT INFLUENCE DAILY CHRONOTYPE PREFERENCE. HIGH‑QUALITY REFERENCE GENOME ASSEMBLIES ARE AVAILABLE FOR ALL SPECIES SURVEYED, ENABLING UNBIASED COMPARATIVE GENOMIC ANALYSES TO IDENTIFY NOVEL CHRONOTYPE‑ASSOCIATED GENES (AIM 1). BUILDING ON DECADES OF CIRCADIAN RESEARCH IN D. MELANOGASTER, WE WILL ALSO EVALUATE CHRONOTYPE-ASSOCIATED VARIATION BETWEEN SPECIES IN REGULATORY ELEMENTS AND EXPRESSION OF KNOWN CIRCADIAN GENES (AIM 2). COLLECTIVELY, THIS PROJECT AIMS TO IDENTIFY THE GENETIC AND NEURAL CORRELATES OF MORNING AND EVENING CHRONOTYPES ACROSS DROSOPHILIDAE SPECIES. WE ANTICIPATE THAT THESE FINDINGS WILL ENABLE THE DEVELOPMENT OF GENETIC MODELS TO ASSESS THE INFLUENCE OF CHRONOTYPE ON PHYSIOLOGY AND BEHAVIORAL PERFORMANCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MAPPING THE NERVE REGENERATIVE LANDSCAPE USING SUBCELLULAR SPATIAL GENOMICS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT NEURONS ARE THE FUNDAMENTAL UNITS OF THE NERVOUS SYSTEM, UNIQUELY ADAPTED TO TRANSMIT INFORMATION THROUGH THEIR POLARIZED MORPHOLOGY. THEIR LONG AXONS MAKE THEM PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TO DISTAL INJURY, WHICH REQUIRES COORDINATED REPAIR BETWEEN THE INJURY SITE AND THE SOMA TO RESTORE FUNCTION. FOLLOWING AXONAL INJURY, NEURONS ACTIVATE REGENERATION-ASSOCIATED GENE (RAG) PROGRAMS OR UNDERGO AXON SPROUTING, WHICH CAN LEAD TO BOTH FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY AND MALADAPTIVE CIRCUIT REORGANIZATION CONTRIBUTING TO NEUROPATHIC PAIN. THE ABILITY OF NEURONS TO REGENERATE IS HIGHLY VARIABLE: WHILE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) NEURONS HAVE LIMITED INTRINSIC REGENERATIVE POTENTIAL, DORSAL ROOT GANGLION (DRG) NEURONS OF THE PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (PNS) CAN REGENERATE ROBUSTLY, THOUGH FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY IN PATIENTS REMAINS INCOMPLETE. DRG NEURONS ARE A POWERFUL MODEL FOR AXONAL REGENERATION. RECENT SINGLE-CELL AND SINGLE-NUCLEUS TRANSCRIPTOMIC STUDIES (SC/SNRNA-SEQ) HAVE REVEALED OVER TEN DISTINCT DRG NEURONAL SUBTYPES WITH DIVERSE RESPONSES TO NERVE INJURY. HOWEVER, KEY CHALLENGES REMAIN: I) DIFFICULTIES IN ISOLATING LARGE DRG NEURONS WITH HIGH PURITY, LIMITING THE RESOLUTION OF SC/SNRNA-SEQ; II) INJURY-INDUCED LOSS OF SUBTYPE MARKER EXPRESSION AND ADOPTION OF EMBRYONIC-LIKE TRANSCRIPTIONAL STATES, WHICH OBSCURE CELL-TYPE-SPECIFIC RESPONSES; AND III) THE PHYSICAL DISTANCE BETWEEN INJURY SITES AND THE SOMA, COMPLICATING EFFORTS TO LINK LOCAL PHENOTYPES TO TRANSCRIPTIONAL REPROGRAMMING. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO ADDRESS THESE BARRIERS BY DEVELOPING SUBCELLULARLY RESOLVED SPATIAL GENOMICS APPROACHES TO STUDY AXON REGENERATION. FIRST, I WILL BUILD A 3D SPATIAL SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOMICS ATLAS OF NAIVE DRG IN MICE TO TRAIN A 3D MORPHOLOGY-BASED CLASSIFIER OF DRG SUBTYPES. SECOND, I WILL THEN ENGINEER A SOMA-AXON-MATCHED BARCODING SYSTEM TO DIRECTLY COUPLE SOMA TRANSCRIPTOMES WITH AXONAL REGENERATIVE PHENOTYPES. THIS INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK AIMS TO ENABLE QUANTITATIVE SINGLE-CELL ANALYSIS LINKING INTRINSIC MOLECULAR IDENTITY AND SOMA MORPHOLOGY WITH AXON REGENERATION LENGTH AND LOCAL INJURY-SITE MICROENVIRONMENT, THEREBY DISSECTING INTRINSIC AND EXTRINSIC DETERMINANTS OF REGENERATIVE HETEROGENEITY. IF SUCCESSFUL, THIS PROJECT WILL DELIVER TOOLS FOR SUBCELLULAR SPATIAL GENOMICS IN NEURAL SYSTEMS AND A HIGH-RESOLUTION ATLAS OF DRG REGENERATION. THESE INNOVATIONS WILL NOT ONLY ADVANCE FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE OF AXON BIOLOGY BUT ALSO PROVIDE INSIGHTS FOR THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR PROMOTING NERVE REPAIR.

description: CHARACTERIZATION OF ARIA BY NEUROIMAGING, PROTEOMICS, AND NEUROPATHOLOGY IN A SQUIRREL MONKEY MODEL OF SPORADIC CAA - SUMMARY CEREBRAL AMYLOID ANGIOPATHY (CAA) IS CHARACTERIZED BY THE CEREBROVASCULAR DEPOSITION OF AMYLOID-Β IN CORTICAL AND LEPTOMENINGEAL ARTERIES, ARTERIOLES, AND CAPILLARIES. CAA OFTEN OCCURS SIMULTANEOUSLY WITH ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD), CONTRIBUTING TO AD PATHOGENESIS AND MORE RAPID COGNITIVE DECLINE. THE MAJOR COMPLICATIONS IN CURRENT IMMUNOTHERAPEUTIC APPROACHES FOR AD ARE AMYLOID-RELATED IMAGING ABNORMALITIES (ARIA), WHICH ARE LINKED TO THE PRESENCE OF CAA. THE SQUIRREL MONKEY (SQM), A NEW WORLD NON-HUMAN PRIMATE SPECIES, HAS BEEN HIGHLIGHTED FOR STUDYING AD AND AD RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD) DUE TO ITS SPORADIC AMYLOID-RELATED PATHOLOGY, WITH A UNIQUE PROPENSITY FOR DEVELOPING EXTENSIVE CAA. MOREOVER, SQMS DEVELOP SPONTANEOUS ARIA, MANIFESTING AS VASOGENIC EDEMA (ARIA-E) AND CEREBRAL MICROHEMORRHAGE/SIDEROSIS (ARIA-H). OUR INITIAL PUBLISHED STUDIES SUPPORT THE USE OF SQMS FOR VALIDATING THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF OUR IMMUNOMODULATORY INTERVENTIONS PLANNED FOR HUMAN USE. IDENTIFYING DIAGNOSTIC BIOMARKERS FOR CAA AND ARIA IS ESSENTIAL TO REDUCE ARIA RISK AND IMPROVE TREATMENT STRATEGIES. THE COLLECTIVE STUDIES PROPOSED HERE ARE DESIGNED TO PROVIDE IN- DEPTH CHARACTERIZATION OF ARIA AND CAA THROUGH THE INTEGRATION OF MULTIPARAMETRIC MRI, WITH BIOFLUID BIOMARKER DATA, AND BRAIN PATHOLOGY CORRELATES. WE INTEND TO EXAMINE BRAIN MICROSTRUCTURAL INTEGRITY, ESPECIALLY WHITE MATTER (WM) MICROSTRUCTURAL CHANGES, USING DIFFUSION TENSOR AND KURTOSIS IMAGING (DTI/DKI). WE WILL UTILIZE ARCHIVED POSTMORTEM BRAINS FROM TWO COHORTS OF GERIATRIC SQMS WITH AND WITHOUT ARIA, AND YOUNG SQMS WITHOUT CAA PATHOLOGY. THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DIFFUSION IMAGING METRICS AND NEUROPATHOLOGICAL SIGNATURES WILL CLARIFY THE UTILITY OF DIFFUSION MRI IN SCREENING FOR ARIA AND CAPTURING THE OVERALL CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE BURDEN. IDENTIFYING DISTINCT LESION STATES LINKED TO SPECIFIC IMAGING AND PATHOLOGICAL SIGNATURES WILL PROVIDE A COMPREHENSIVE CHARACTERIZATION OF ARIA-ASSOCIATED FEATURES. FURTHERMORE, OUR PLASMA/CSF ASSAYS MAY HELP IDENTIFY BIOFLUID BIOMARKER SIGNATURES ASSOCIATED WITH THE ARIA MANIFESTATION CONFIRMED BY MRI AND HISTOLOGY. A STRENGTH OF THIS PROPOSAL IS THE USE OF OUR POWERFUL PROTEOMIC APPROACH THAT LEVERAGES UNBIASED MASS SPECTROMETRY COUPLED WITH LASER CAPTURE MICRODISSECTION TO PRECISELY ISOLATE AND CHARACTERIZE SPECIFIC NEUROPATHOLOGICAL LESIONS. WE PROPOSE THE FIRST COMPLETE CHARACTERIZATION OF CAA AND ARIA PROTEOMES THAT MAY FACILITATE DISCOVERIES OF VALUABLE DIAGNOSTIC MARKERS AND NOVEL DRUG TARGETS, UTILIZING OUR WELL-ESTABLISHED LOCALIZED PROTEOMIC STRATEGY. IN ADDITION, WE WILL CONDUCT COMPLEMENTARY CSF PROTEOMIC ANALYSES FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS TRANSLATIONALLY RELEVANT MODEL, OFFERING A FURTHER AVENUE FOR BIOMARKER DISCOVERY. OVERALL, THE STUDY DESCRIBED HERE WILL PROVIDE A CRITICAL FOUNDATION IN UNDERSTANDING ARIA PATHOGENESIS THAT HAS YET TO BE DISCOVERED AND DETERMINE KEY TRANSLATIONAL INSIGHT INTO THE PROCESSES DRIVING CAA.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BRAIN-SPECIFIC VULNERABILITY TO UBIQUITOUS ASPM LOSS IN MICROCEPHALY - SUMMARY/ABSTRACT PRIMARY MICROCEPHALY PRESENTS A FUNDAMENTAL QUESTION IN DEVELOPMENTAL BIOLOGY: MUTATIONS IN UBIQUITOUSLY EXPRESSED GENES CAUSE SEVERE, BRAIN-SPECIFIC GROWTH DEFICITS WHILE SPARING OTHER HIGHLY PROLIFERATIVE ORGANS. FOR EXAMPLE, ASPM (ABNORMAL SPINDLE-LIKE MICROCEPHALY-ASSOCIATED) ENCODES A CENTROSOMAL PROTEIN ESSENTIAL FOR CELL PROLIFERATION THROUGHOUT THE BODY AND IS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE MICROCEPHALY WHEN MUTATED. YET, LOSS OF ASPM RESULTS IN PROFOUND REDUCTIONS IN BRAIN SIZE AND INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY WITHOUT AFFECTING BODY STATURE OR THE STRUCTURE OF TISSUES LIKE THE KIDNEY OR INTESTINE. DESPITE ITS CLINICAL IMPORTANCE, THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS CONFERRING THIS “BRAIN-SPECIFIC VULNERABILITY” REMAIN UNKNOWN, LARGELY BECAUSE PRIOR RESEARCH HAS NOT DIRECTLY COMPARED THE MOLECULAR CONSEQUENCES OF ASPM LOSS ACROSS AFFECTED AND UNAFFECTED TISSUES. TO BRIDGE THIS GAP, WE UTILIZE A UNIQUE ASPM KNOCKOUT (KO) FERRET MODEL. WHILE ASPM KO MICE EXHIBIT MILD PHENOTYPES, OUR ASPM KO FERRETS FAITHFULLY RECAPITULATE THE SEVERE HUMAN DISEASE FEATURES—INCLUDING A 25–40% REDUCTION IN CORTICAL VOLUME, PREMATURE PROGENITOR DELAMINATION, AND ROBUST CELL DEATH—WHILE MAINTAINING NORMAL BODY SIZE. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT CORTICAL PROGENITORS POSSESS AN “INTRINSIC VULNERABILITY” DRIVEN BY CORTEX-SPECIFIC ASPM INTERACTIONS THAT ARE ABSENT IN SOMATIC TISSUES. TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS, WE PROPOSE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 WILL DEFINE THE CELLULAR AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC BASIS OF THIS VULNERABILITY: 1A) QUANTIFY PROLIFERATION AND CELL DEATH ACROSS FOUR ASPM-EXPRESSING TISSUES (CORTEX, LUNG, KIDNEY, AND INTESTINE) IN EMBRYONIC FERRETS; AND 1B) EMPLOY SEQ-SCOPE—A HIGH-RESOLUTION SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS TECHNOLOGY—TO MAP PROGENITOR-SPECIFIC STRESS RESPONSES IN SITU. AIM 2 WILL IDENTIFY THE MOLECULAR MEDIATORS OF THIS VULNERABILITY: 2A) PERFORM ANTIBODY- DIRECTED PROXIMITY LABELING TO DEFINE THE IN SITU ASPM INTERACTOME; AND 2B) PARALLEL CENTROSOME AFFINITY CAPTURE TO PROFILE CENTROSOME COMPOSITION ACROSS THE SAME FOUR TISSUES IN WT AND KO FERRETS. OUR RESEARCH WILL ELUCIDATE WHY LOSS OF THE UBIQUITOUS PROTEIN ASPM CAUSES BRAIN-SPECIFIC MICROCEPHALY, IDENTIFYING NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS OF CORTICAL PROGENITORS. MOREOVER, OUR METHODS AND CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK MAY ADVANCE THE UNDERSTANDING OF OTHER NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS WHERE THE LOSS OF UBIQUITOUSLY EXPRESSED GENES CAUSES TISSUE-RESTRICTED PATHOGENESIS.

description: UNRAVELING THE ROLE OF WATER HYACINTH IN MODULATING SCHISTOSOMIASIS TO FACILITATE SCALING A PROVEN DISEASE CONTROL INTERVENTION - SCHISTOSOMIASIS IS A DEBILITATING PARASITIC DISEASE THAT IMPOSES MAJOR HEALTH AND ECONOMIC BURDENS WORLDWIDE AND REMAINS RELEVANT TO AMERICAN HEALTH THROUGH INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL, MILITARY DEPLOYMENT, IMMIGRATION, AND GLOBAL INFECTIOUS DISEASE PREPAREDNESS. IN THE LAKE VICTORIA BASIN, MILLIONS ARE INFECTED WITH SCHISTOSOMA MANSONI, AND REINFECTION REMAINS HIGH DESPITE ANNUAL MASS DRUG ADMINISTRATION. OUR TEAM PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED AN INNOVATIVE INTERVENTION IN SENEGAL: AQUATIC VEGETATION REMOVAL (AVR) TO REDUCE SNAIL HABITAT AND INTERRUPT PARASITE TRANSMISSION. IN RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS, AVR SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCED SCHISTOSOMA INFECTIONS WHILE THE HARVESTED VEGETATION WAS CONVERTED INTO COMPOST, LIVESTOCK FEED, AND BIODIGESTER FUEL, GENERATING ECONOMIC RETURNS THAT EXCEEDED INTERVENTION COSTS. BEFORE AVR CAN BE EXPANDED TO EAST AFRICA, AN IMPORTANT SCIENTIFIC QUESTION MUST BE RESOLVED. THE DOMINANT INVASIVE AQUATIC PLANT IN LAKE VICTORIA IS WATER HYACINTH (PONTEDERIA CRASSIPES), WHICH DIFFERS ECOLOGICALLY FROM VEGETATION IN SENEGAL. PRELIMINARY ANALYSES SUGGEST A HUMP-SHAPED RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN WATER HYACINTH DENSITY AND S. MANSONI PREVALENCE. THIS PATTERN MAY RESULT FROM WATER HYACINTH SIMULTANEOUSLY INCREASING SNAIL HABITAT AND PARASITE DENSITY WHILE REDUCING HUMAN WATER CONTACT AT HIGH COVERAGE LEVELS. REMOVING HYACINTH WITHOUT UNDERSTANDING THESE MECHANISMS COULD UNINTENTIONALLY INCREASE DISEASE RISK. KENYA PROVIDES A UNIQUE NATURAL LABORATORY UNAVAILABLE IN THE UNITED STATES BECAUSE ACTIVE SCHISTOSOMIASIS TRANSMISSION OCCURS ACROSS NATURAL GRADIENTS OF WATER HYACINTH, ALLOWING ECOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL MECHANISMS TO BE STUDIED UNDER REAL-WORLD CONDITIONS. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY THE ECOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL MECHANISMS DRIVING THIS NON-LINEAR PATTERN TO ENSURE THAT AVR CAN BE SAFELY ADAPTED TO EAST AFRICA. WE WILL (1) QUANTIFY HOW WATER HYACINTH DENSITY AFFECTS SNAIL AND CERCARIAL DENSITIES USING FIELD SURVEYS, CERCARIAL SHEDDING ASSAYS, AND REMOTE SENSING, AND (2) DETERMINE HOW WATER HYACINTH INFLUENCES HUMAN WATER-CONTACT BEHAVIOR THROUGH STRUCTURED OBSERVATIONS AND HOUSEHOLD SURVEYS. BY IDENTIFYING GENERALIZABLE ECOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL MECHANISMS GOVERNING ENVIRONMENTALLY MEDIATED TRANSMISSION, THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE THE SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION FOR ADAPTING AVR TO NEW SETTINGS AND DESIGNING FUTURE INTERVENTION TRIALS. THE RESULTING KNOWLEDGE WILL BE BROADLY APPLICABLE TO ENVIRONMENTALLY MEDIATED PARASITIC DISEASES AND WILL INFORM PREVENTION STRATEGIES RELEVANT TO AMERICANS THROUGH TRAVEL MEDICINE, MILITARY DEPLOYMENT, IMMIGRATION, AND GLOBAL INFECTIOUS DISEASE PREPAREDNESS. BECAUSE THESE MECHANISMS ARE EXPECTED TO BE REPRODUCIBLE ACROSS ENDEMIC SETTINGS, THIS WORK WILL ESTABLISH PRINCIPLES THAT CAN GUIDE FUTURE IMPLEMENTATION AND EVALUATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL DISEASE-CONTROL INTERVENTIONS.

description: THE RAKAI COMMUNITY COHORT STUDY (RCCS): A RESEARCH RESOURCE - PROJECT SUMMARY THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO PRESERVE AND ENHANCE THE RAKAI COMMUNITY COHORT STUDY (RCCS), A WORLD-CLASS RESOURCE FOR INFECTIOUS DISEASE RESEARCH. CONDUCTED BY THE RAKAI HEALTH SCIENCES PROGRAM (RHSP) IN UGANDA, THE RCCS IS ONE OF THE LONGEST-RUNNING, POPULATION-BASED COHORTS FOCUSED ON INFECTIOUS DISEASES. WITH OVER 30 YEARS OF LONGITUDINAL DATA ON APPROXIMATELY 100,000 PARTICIPANTS ACROSS 34 DIVERSE COMMUNITIES, THE RCCS OFFERS A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO ADDRESS CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC QUESTIONS IN HIV AND INFECTIOUS DISEASE RESEARCH. ITS LOCATION AT AN EPICENTER OF HIV, (RE-)EMERGING INFECTIONS, TUBERCULOSIS, SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS, AND OTHER INFECTIOUS DISEASES FURTHER STRENGTHEN ITS VALUE. THE RCCS HAS PREVIOUSLY CONTRIBUTED TO MAJOR GLOBAL HEALTH DISCOVERIES WHICH HAVE IMPROVED THE LIVES OF THOSE IN THE UNITED STATES, UGANDA, AND BEYOND. WITH ITS PROVEN INFRASTRUCTURE FOR SCALABLE DATA COLLECTION, RCCS IS WELL-POSITIONED TO BECOME AN R24 RESOURCE-RELATED RESEARCH PROJECT WHICH WILL PROVIDE VITAL DATA, BIOSPECIMENS, AND RESEARCH SERVICES THAT WILL INFORM U.S. AND GLOBAL HEALTH POLICIES, PROGRAMS, AND INVESTMENTS. THE PROPOSED RCCS RESEARCH RESOURCE IS ORGANIZED AROUND FIVE CORES: ADMINISTRATIVE, FIELD/SURVEY, DATA CENTER, BIOBANK/LAB, AND COMMUNICATIONS. OVER THE NEXT FIVE YEARS (2026– 2030), AIM 1 WILL ENHANCE RCCS FOLLOW-UP BY ADDING APPROXIMATELY 100,000 PERSON-YEARS OF PARTICIPANT FOLLOW- UP DATA. ABOUT 32,000 INDIVIDUALS AGED 15 AND OLDER WILL BE SURVEYED TO ASSESS HIV INCIDENCE, VIRAL LOADS, SEXUAL NETWORKS, BEHAVIORS, NON-COMMUNICABLE DISEASES RISK FACTORS AND OUTCOMES, EMERGING INFECTIONS, AND TUBERCULOSIS WITH THE DATA COLLECTION SUPERVISED BY A FIELD/SURVEY CORE AND MANAGED THROUGH THE DATA CENTER CORE FOR POTENTIAL ADVANCED ANALYTICS AND POTENTIAL AI-DRIVEN FORECASTING. AIM 2 FOCUSES ON EXPANDING THE RCCS BIOBANK, ADDING AN ESTIMATED 55,000 NEW BIOSPECIMENS TO AN EXISTING REPOSITORY OF OVER 1 MILLION SAMPLES. THESE SPECIMENS—INCLUDING PLASMA, PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS, RESPIRATORY SPECIMENS, AND GENITAL SWABS—WILL POTENTIALLY SUPPORT NEXT-GENERATION DIAGNOSTICS, HIV CURE RESEARCH, AND BIOTECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT BENEFITING THE UNITED STATES AND GLOBAL HEALTH. AIM 3 SEEKS TO SYNERGIZE ONGOING RCCS-RELATED PROJECTS BY PROVIDING CENTRALIZED COORDINATION THROUGH THE ADMINISTRATIVE CORE, PROMOTING COLLABORATION, EFFICIENCY, AND NEW TRANSDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH. AIM 4 WILL LEVERAGE RCCS RESOURCES FOR BROADER SCIENTIFIC ACCESS, UTILIZING A COMMUNICATIONS CORE TO MANAGE PUBLIC DISSEMINATION, ONLINE DASHBOARDS, A SPECIMEN CATALOG, AND A DATA REQUEST PROCESS. OVERALL, THE RCCS RESOURCE WILL DRIVE SIGNIFICANT ADVANCES IN BASIC, TRANSLATIONAL, DIAGNOSTIC, AND APPLIED INFECTIOUS DISEASE RESEARCH, DIRECTLY SUPPORTING UNITED STATES, NIH, AND NIAID PRIORITIES. PRESERVING AND ENHANCING THIS EXCEPTIONAL RESEARCH RESOURCE WILL NOT ONLY HELP SAVE LIVES BUT ALSO GUIDE UNITED STATES HEALTH INVESTMENTS AND STRENGTHEN GLOBAL HEALTH SECURITY.

description: PRODUCTION AND DISTRIBUTION OF FILARIAL RESEARCH REAGENTS - PROJECT SUMMARY THE FILARIASIS RESEARCH REAGENT RESOURCE CENTER (FR3), A LONG-STANDING CORNERSTONE OF FILARIASIS RESEARCH, IS TRANSITIONING FROM A CONTRACT MECHANISM TO A SUSTAINABLE AND INNOVATIVE RESEARCH RESOURCE. OUR PRIMARY GOAL IS TO PROVIDE THE GLOBAL SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY WITH ESSENTIAL PARASITES AND MODELS NEEDED FOR FUNDAMENTAL AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH. WE WILL ACHIEVE THIS THROUGH THREE SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 WILL ENSURE THE CONTINUED PROVISION OF HIGH-QUALITY BRUGIA MALAYI AND B. PAHANGI RESOURCES BY INNOVATING PARASITE MAINTENANCE. WE WILL AUTOMATE INSECTARY PROCESSES AND IMPLEMENT AN ARTIFICIAL BLOOD MEAL SYSTEM TO ENHANCE EFFICIENCY, REDUCE COSTS, AND IMPROVE ANIMAL WELFARE. AIM 2 FOCUSES ON DEVELOPING SCALABLE MURINE MODELS, SUCH AS SPRAGUE- DAWLEY RATS, ATHYMIC NUDE MICE, AND CB17 SCID MICE. THESE MODELS ARE MORE TRACTABLE AND ACCESSIBLE THAN THE TRADITIONAL GERBIL, WHICH WILL ACCELERATE IN VIVO DRUG SCREENING AND LOWER ADMINISTRATIVE BARRIERS FOR RESEARCHERS. FINALLY, AIM 3 WILL DIRECTLY SUPPORT GLOBAL ELIMINATION EFFORTS FOR WUCHERERIA BANCROFTI, THE PRIMARY CAUSE OF LYMPHATIC FILARIASIS. WE WILL DEVELOP AND PROVIDE STANDARDIZED QUALITY ASSURANCE PANELS FOR MOLECULAR XENOMONITORING, A CRITICAL NEED FOR POST-ELIMINATION SURVEILLANCE. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL WORK TO DEVELOP A HUMANIZED MOUSE MODEL CAPABLE OF PROPAGATING THE COMPLETE W. BANCROFTI LIFE CYCLE, A GROUNDBREAKING ACHIEVEMENT THAT WOULD PROVIDE AN INVALUABLE PLATFORM FOR DRUG AND VACCINE DEVELOPMENT.

description: VISIONKB: A SINGLE CELL MULTI-OMICS KNOWLEDGEBASE FOR THE VISUAL SYSTEM - ABSTRACT THE DEVELOPMENT OF SINGLE-CELL OMICS TECHNOLOGIES HAS REVOLUTIONIZED OUR ABILITY TO PROFILE CELL TYPES WITH UNPRECEDENTED RESOLUTION, OFFERING TRANSFORMATIVE INSIGHTS INTO BIOLOGY. AS THESE TECHNOLOGIES BECOME WIDELY USED IN BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH, THE VOLUME AND COMPLEXITY OF THE DATA GENERATED HAVE GROWN RAPIDLY. THIS EXPLOSION OF DATA PRESENTS SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGES IN ORGANIZATION, INTEGRATION, ANALYSIS, AND ACCESSIBILITY— ESPECIALLY FOR INVESTIGATORS WITHOUT COMPUTATIONAL EXPERTISE. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ESTABLISH A COMMUNITY- ACCESSIBLE, AI-ENABLED KNOWLEDGE-BASED DATABASE FOCUSED ON THE VISUAL SYSTEM. WE WILL ORGANIZE, CURATE, AND INTEGRATE LARGE-SCALE SINGLE-CELL MULTI-OMICS DATA (E.G., SCRNA-SEQ, SNATAC-SEQ, SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS) FROM THE VISUAL SYSTEM OF HUMANS AND OTHER SPECIES. WE WILL IMPLEMENT NOVEL AI-DRIVEN TOOLS THAT ENABLE RESEARCHERS—REGARDLESS OF COMPUTATIONAL BACKGROUND—TO INTERACT WITH, EXPLORE, AND ANALYZE THE DATA THROUGH AN INTUITIVE, FLEXIBLE INTERFACE. THIS DATABASE WILL NOT ONLY ALLOW USERS TO EXPLORE PROCESSED DATA BUT ALSO SUPPORT THE INTEGRATION OF USER-GENERATED DATA AND THE CONSTRUCTION OF CUSTOM ANALYSIS, DRAMATICALLY LOWERING THE BARRIER FOR DATA REUSE AND INTERPRETATION. OUR AIMS ARE TO: SPECIFIC AIM 1: BUILD A CURATED SINGLE-CELL MULTI-OMICS REFERENCE ATLAS OF THE EYE. SPECIFIC AIM 2: DEVELOP A CODE-FREE, COLLABORATIVE DATA-ANALYSIS PLATFORM. SPECIFIC AIM 3: DELIVER AN AI-POWERED CO-PILOT FOR AUTOMATED DATA ACCESS AND INTERACTIVE ANALYSIS. DEVELOPMENT OF THE PROPOSED KNOWLEDGE-BASED DATABASE WILL SERVE THE VISION RESEARCH COMMUNITY BY ENABLING SEAMLESS INTEGRATION OF PUBLIC AND USER-GENERATED DATA, REMOVING BARRIERS TO ENTRY FOR NON-COMPUTATIONAL USERS, AND BRIDGING THE GAP BETWEEN LARGE-SCALE SINGLE-CELL OMICS DATA AND INDIVIDUAL RESEARCH APPLICATIONS. THE FRAMEWORK DEVELOPED HERE IS READILY APPLICABLE TO OTHER ORGAN SYSTEMS AND DATASETS IN GENERAL.

description: AI IN CANCER GENOMICS: EDUCATIONAL MODULES IN DC-AREA UNIVERSITIES - ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) IS TRANSFORMING CANCER RESEARCH BY ENABLING SCALABLE INTEGRATION AND INTERPRETATION OF HIGH-DIMENSIONAL GENOMIC DATA. WHEN APPLIED TO SINGLE-CELL DATASETS, AI PROVIDES DEEP INSIGHT INTO TUMOR HETEROGENEITY, CLONAL DYNAMICS, AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE - CAPABILITIES INCREASINGLY CENTRAL TO PRECISION ONCOLOGY. AI NOT ONLY ENABLES MODELING OF RESPONSE TRAJECTORIES AT THE CELLULAR LEVEL BUT ALSO ALLOWS DYNAMIC TUNING OF PREDICTIVE FRAMEWORKS FOR INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT STRATEGIES. MOREOVER, AN INCREASING NUMBER OF ANTICANCER COMPOUNDS ARE BEING IDENTIFIED AND OPTIMIZED THROUGH AI-DRIVEN DISCOVERY PIPELINES, UNDERSCORING AI’S GROWING IMPACT ON BOTH DIAGNOSTICS AND THERAPEUTICS. YET, GRADUATE- LEVEL TRAINING THAT INTEGRATES AI METHODS WITH SINGLE-CELL CANCER GENOMICS REMAINS LIMITED OR ENTIRELY ABSENT ACROSS MOST ACADEMIC INSTITUTIONS.  THIS INITIATIVE ADDRESSES A CRITICAL EDUCATIONAL GAP BY DEVELOPING, DELIVERING, AND DISSEMINATING AN INTERDISCIPLINARY GRADUATE-LEVEL COURSE TITLED AI IN CANCER GENOMICS. JOINTLY DEVELOPED BY GEORGE WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY (GWU), GEORGETOWN UNIVERSITY (GU), AND THE UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND (UMD), AND OFFERED THROUGH THE DC-REGION CROSS-REGISTRATION FRAMEWORK SUPPORTED BY PARTNER INSTITUTIONS - THE COURSE WILL EQUIP STUDENTS WITH ADVANCED COMPETENCIES IN APPLYING AI AND MACHINE LEARNING TO REAL-WORLD BULK AND SINGLE-CELL CANCER DATASETS. INSTRUCTION WILL SPAN SUPERVISED AND UNSUPERVISED LEARNING, NEURAL NETWORKS, MULTI-OMICS INTEGRATION, DIMENSIONALITY REDUCTION, AND EXPLAINABLE AI, WITH CONTENT ANCHORED IN KEY CHALLENGES IN CANCER BIOLOGY.  A MULTI-WEEK MENTORED CAPSTONE PROJECT WILL ENABLE STUDENTS TO GENERATE INTERPRETABLE, REPRODUCIBLE AI- DRIVEN ANALYSES USING PUBLISHED AND INSTITUTIONAL DATASETS, WITH STRUCTURED SUPPORT FOR PEER-REVIEWED DISSEMINATION. THE COURSE EMPHASIZES HANDS-ON, CASE-BASED LEARNING, ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS IN DATA USE, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF REPRODUCIBLE PIPELINES ALIGNED WITH CURRENT RESEARCH STANDARDS.  THE PROGRAM IS STRUCTURED AROUND THREE INTEGRATED AIMS: AIM 1: TO DESIGN AND IMPLEMENT THE MODULAR, INTERDISCIPLINARY COURSE IN COLLABORATION WITH REGIONAL ACADEMIC PARTNERS; AIM 2: TO RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE EDUCATIONAL EFFECTIVENESS THROUGH A MIXED-METHODS FRAMEWORK THAT INCLUDES PRE/POST ASSESSMENTS, PROJECT RUBRICS, REFLECTIVE FEEDBACK, AND LONGITUDINAL OUTCOME TRACKING; AND AIM 3: TO DISSEMINATE ALL INSTRUCTIONAL CONTENT, EVALUATION TOOLS, AND IMPLEMENTATION RESOURCES NATIONALLY THROUGH OPEN-ACCESS PLATFORMS, EDUCATOR WORKSHOPS, PEER-REVIEWED PUBLICATIONS, AND INDEXING IN NATIONAL TRAINING DIRECTORIES.  THIS INITIATIVE ALIGNS CROSS-INSTITUTIONAL EXPERTISE IN AI, CANCER GENOMICS, AND BIOMEDICAL EDUCATION TO DELIVER A SCALABLE AND REPLICABLE NATIONAL MODEL FOR INTERDISCIPLINARY TRAINING. IT SUPPORTS NIH PRIORITIES IN PRECISION MEDICINE, DATA SCIENCE, AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, PREPARING FUTURE SCIENTISTS TO LEAD AT THE INTERSECTION OF COMPUTATION AND CANCER BIOLOGY.

description: CREATING MODELS AND PROVIDING TRAINING IN DATA VISUALIZATION TO ENHANCE DATA REPRODUCIBILITY AND REPLICABILITY - BIOMEDICAL RESEARCHERS WHO HAVE RECEIVED TRADITIONAL DOMAIN-SPECIFIC TRAINING AS BENCH SCIENTISTS HAVE BEEN CAUGHT UNPREPARED BY THE RISE IN POPULARITY OF HIGH-THROUGHPUT DATA GENERATION APPROACHES. THESE APPROACHES ARE USED IN STUDIES WITH COMPLEX DESIGNS RESULTING IN COMPLEX MULTIVARIATE DATASETS. THIS ONLY EXACERBATES THE CHALLENGES THAT RESEARCHERS ACROSS TRAINING AND CAREER STAGES FACE. GIVEN THE GREATER ATTENTION BEING PAID TO RIGOR AND REPRODUCIBILITY THE PROBLEM IS CRITICAL. A SPECIFIC AREA WHERE CONSIDERABLE GAINS COULD MOST EASILY BE MADE IS THE GENERATION OF EFFECTIVE DATA VISUALIZATIONS. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO EMPOWER SCIENTISTS AT ANY CAREER STAGE, BUT ESPECIALLY GRADUATE STUDENTS AND POSTDOCS, TO ANALYZE THEIR DATA WITH ROBUST, RIGOROUS, AND REPRODUCIBLE APPROACHES. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS APPLICATION IS TO DEVELOP A COLLECTION OF VIRTUAL EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES THAT INDIVIDUAL OR GROUPS OF RESEARCHERS CAN USE TO STRENGTHEN THEIR DATA VISUALIZATION SKILLS. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT LEARNERS’ SKILLS WILL INCREASE WHEN POPULAR TUTORIALS AND WORKSHOPS ARE COMPLEMENTED WITH REPEATED PRACTICE USING RELEVANT DATA AND QUESTIONS WITH MODELLING BY EXPERIENCED PRACTITIONERS. THE RATIONALE FOR THIS PROJECT IS THAT IF RESEARCHERS CAN IMPROVE THEIR DATA VISUALIZATION SKILLS THEN THEY WILL HAVE TAKEN A SIGNIFICANT STEP FORWARD IN IMPROVING THE ROBUSTNESS, RIGOR, AND REPRODUCIBILITY OF THEIR RESEARCH. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH EDUCATION PROGRAM CONSISTS OF DEVELOPING AND MODELLING TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. THE FIRST WILL BE GENERATE RESOURCES THAT ENABLE RESEARCHERS TO ENGAGE IN CONSTRUCTIVE CRITIQUES OF EXISTING DATA VISUALIZATIONS AND THOSE BEING DESIGNED BY THE RESEARCHERS AND THEIR COLLEAGUES. THE SECOND AIM WILL CREATE EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS TO OVERCOME THE CHALLENGES MANY FACE IN DEVELOPING THE TECHNICAL SKILLS NEEDED TO GENERATE DATA VISUALIZATIONS. THIS GOAL WILL BE ACHIEVED BY CREATING AN IMMERSIVE TRAINING ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH PARTICIPANTS ARE ENCOURAGED TO REPRODUCE EXISTING DATA VISUALIZATIONS AND IMPLEMENTING OBSERVATIONS FROM CRITIQUES TO IMPROVE THE VISUALIZATIONS. THE RESOURCES GENERATED IN THESE AIMS WILL BE DISSEMINATED THROUGH MULTIPLE VENUES INCLUDING THE USE OF CODE CLUBS AND A UNIQUE SHIFT IN THE TYPES OF VIDEOS AVAILABLE THROUGH THE ALREADY SUCCESSFUL RIFFOMONAS YOUTUBE CHANNEL. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH EDUCATION PROGRAM IS INNOVATIVE, IN THE APPLICANT’S OPINION, BECAUSE IT REPRESENTS A SUBSTANTIVE DEPARTURE FROM THE STATUS QUO BY DRAWING FROM PRACTICES WITHIN ARTISTIC COMMUNITIES TO GENERATE A LIBRARY OF RESOURCES WHERE EXPERIENCED PRACTITIONERS WILL MODEL CRITIQUING, REPLICATING, AND CREATING NEW VISUALIZATIONS. THE PROPOSED ACTIVITIES ARE SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE THEY WILL ADDRESS THE PROBLEM OF WASTING THE SIGNIFICANT RESOURCES THAT ARE EXTENDED TO PARTICIPATE IN WORKSHOPS ONLY TO BE INEFFECTIVE BECAUSE LEARNERS DO NOT HAVE THE ADDITIONAL RESOURCES FOR DELIBERATE PRACTICE. ULTIMATELY, THE PROPOSED AIMS WILL OVERCOME THE LIMITATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH POPULAR, BUT INEFFECTIVE, METHODS OF TRAINING IN DATA VISUALIZATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BUILDING A NATIONAL BIOMEDICAL DATA SCIENCE CORPS THROUGH AI-GENE: AI-DRIVEN GENOMIC EDUCATION NETWORK - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE RAPID ASCENT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) HAS TRANSFORMED BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH AND PRACTICE. AI ALGORITHMS HAVE IMMENSE POTENTIAL TO ACCELERATE DRUG DISCOVERY, PRECISION MEDICINE, AND HUMAN HEALTH APPLICATIONS, MAKING IT ESSENTIAL THAT STUDENTS LEARN TO USE AND UNDERSTAND THESE TECHNOLOGIES. HOWEVER, THE COMPLEX AND RAPIDLY CHANGING TECHNOLOGY LANDSCAPE HAS CREATED A CRITICAL TRAINING GAP IN BIOMEDICAL EDUCATION, PARTICULARLY AT TEACHING-INTENSIVE INSTITUTIONS (TIIS). FACULTY AT THESE INSTITUTIONS ARE OFTEN ISOLATED FROM CUTTING-EDGE TOOLS AND MAY FEEL UNCOMFORTABLE TEACHING THESE NEW TOPICS, LET ALONE DEDICATING TIME AND RESOURCES TO INTEGRATE THEM INTO THEIR CURRICULA. CONSEQUENTLY, THEIR STUDENTS OFTEN LACK AWARENESS AND EXPERIENCE, CREATING A LARGE DEFICIT IN FUTURE STEM TALENT. TO MEET THIS NEED, WE PROPOSE AI-GENE, THE AI-DRIVEN GENOMIC EDUCATION NETWORK, A NATIONAL PROGRAM EMPOWERING FACULTY AT TIIS AND BEYOND TO TEACH AI AND DATA SCIENCE THROUGH AUTHENTIC, COURSE-BASED GENOMICS AND AI TECHNIQUES. OUR PROGRAM TRANSFORMS TRADITIONAL TRAINING BY ESTABLISHING AN EDUCATOR AND STUDENT COMMUNITY THROUGH THREE INITIATIVES: (1) DEVELOPING MODULAR, ADAPTABLE UNDERGRADUATE CURRICULUM MATERIALS FOR THE CLASSROOM; (2) PROVIDING COHORT-BASED TRAINING AND COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE FOR FACULTY IMPLEMENTING THIS CURRICULUM; AND (3) OFFERING SCALABLE, OPEN ACCESS ONLINE TRAINING TO FACULTY AND STUDENTS EVERYWHERE. THE CURRICULUM SPANS FUNDAMENTAL APPROACHES IN AI, SUCH AS DECISION TREES AND REGRESSION MODELS, THROUGH STATE-OF-THE-ART ARCHITECTURES (CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORKS, TRANSFORMERS) VIA THEORY-BASED DISCUSSIONS AND APPLIED LEARNING. CRUCIALLY, THESE TECHNIQUES ARE NOW CENTRAL TO NEARLY ALL ASPECTS OF GENOMICS, FROM BASECALLING SIGNAL ANALYSIS, TO DEEP LEARNING-BASED VARIANT CALLING, EXPRESSION ANALYSIS, AND SEQUENCE CLASSIFICATION, AND TO THE LATEST FOUNDATION MODELS FOR SEQUENCE-TO-FUNCTION PREDICTIONS AND CLINICAL RISK ASSESSMENT. THIS INITIATIVE WILL RESHAPE BEST PRACTICES FOR POST-SECONDARY GENOMICS AND DATA SCIENCE EDUCATION BY EQUIPPING A GENERATION OF FACULTY AND STUDENTS WITH SKILLS, CONFIDENCE, AND COMMUNITY TO EXCEL IN THE NEW DATA-INTENSIVE ERA OF BIOMEDICINE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GAMA, GATEWAY TO AMERICAN AGING DATA - SUMMARY WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP THE GATEWAY TO AMERICAN AGING DATA (GAMA), A NEW RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE THAT WILL ACCELERATE LIFE COURSE RESEARCH ON HOW MODIFIABLE EXPOSURES AMERICANS EXPERIENCE SHAPE LATER-LIFE HEALTH. HARMONIZING AND POOLING MULTIPLE LONG-RUNNING COHORTS PRESENTS AN OPPORTUNITY TO LEVERAGE EXISTING INVESTMENTS IN DATA RESOURCES TO CONDUCT NOVEL LIFE COURSE RESEARCH, WHICH IS A POWERFUL BUT UNDERSTUDIED FRAMEWORK TO UNDERSTAND THE INTRICATE DYNAMICS THAT SHAPE HOW AMERICANS DEVELOP LATER-LIFE HEALTH PROBLEMS. SPECIFICALLY, GAMA WILL HARMONIZE SURVEY DATA ACROSS FIVE NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE U.S. COHORTS: PANEL STUDY OF INCOME DYNAMICS (PSID), NATIONAL LONGITUDINAL SURVEY OF YOUTH (NLSY) 1979 COHORT, HEALTH AND RETIREMENT STUDY (HRS), NATIONAL SOCIAL LIFE, HEALTH AND AGING PROJECT (NSHAP), AND NATIONAL HEALTH AND AGING TRENDS STUDY (NHATS) AND LINK COMMON HARMONIZED ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURE DATA (E.G., PM2.5, NO2, O3, GREENSPACE) TO SURVEY PARTICIPANTS USING GEOGRAPHIC RESIDENTIAL INFORMATION. INDEPENDENTLY, EACH STUDY OFFERS OPPORTUNITIES TO STUDY THE EFFECTS OF EXPOSURES DURING CERTAIN PERIODS FOR SPECIFIC BIRTH COHORTS, BUT COMBINED, THESE STUDIES PRESENT GREATER POTENTIAL FOR SCIENTIFIC INNOVATION, SINCE THE SURVEYS COVER DIFFERENT AGE GROUPS, POPULATIONS, AND TIMES. TOGETHER WITH COMMON LINKED ENVIRONMENTAL DATA, THESE DATA CAN SPUR INNOVATIVE RESEARCH INTO HOW CERTAIN ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES DURING CHILDHOOD, MID- AND LATE-LIFE SHAPE LATER LIFE HEALTH OUTCOMES. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL DEMONSTRATE THE VALUE OF HARMONIZING AND POOLING DATA FROM MULTIPLE COHORTS IN TWO MAIN WAYS. FIRST, WE WILL POOL MIDLIFE DATA FROM THE AGE-OVERLAPPING NLSY79 AND HRS COHORTS, CREATE A LIFE COURSE SYNTHETIC COHORT, AND EXAMINE THE EFFECTS OF LOW WAGE EARNING ACROSS THE FULL LIFE COURSE ON RISK OF DISABLEMENT PROGRESSION IN LATER LIFE. SECOND, WE WILL DEMONSTRATE THE ADDED VALUE OF COMMON ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSOME DATA BY CONDUCTING A STUDY OF AIR POLLUTION AND HEALTHCARE SPENDING, REPLICATING THE FINDINGS FROM HRS USING PSID TO ESTABLISH THE RELIABILITY OF THE FINDINGS. WE WILL FURTHER EXTEND THIS WORK, ANALYZING HOW AIR POLLUTION EXPOSURE IN EARLY- AND MID-LIFE CONTRIBUTES TO HOSPITALIZATIONS IN OLDER AGE, USING BOTH HRS AND PSID, PROVIDING NEW EVIDENCE AND STRENGTHENING THE GENERALIZABILITY OF OUR EARLIER FINDINGS THAT HAVE IMPLICATIONS FOR POPULATION HEALTH AND PREVENTION. IMPORTANTLY, GAMA WILL SUPPORT ALL INTERESTED RESEARCHERS USING THE PROPOSED NEW RESOURCES FOR THEIR OWN RESEARCH THROUGH ROBUST OUTREACH ACTIVITIES. OUR EXTENSIVE DISSEMINATION EFFORTS WILL INCLUDE PROGRAMS TARGETING EARLY-CAREER INVESTIGATORS (I.E., HOSTING A HACKATHON) WITH TRAINING AND MENTORSHIP. WE WILL ALSO FOSTER INNOVATIVE RESEARCH BY ORGANIZING A PILOT PROGRAM USING HARMONIZED LIFE COURSE AND EXPOSOME DATA. IN DOING SO, IT WILL CREATE A TRANSFORMATIVE RESOURCE FOR THE RESEARCH COMMUNITY, ACCELERATING DISCOVERY ON HOW MODIFIABLE EXPOSURES DURING THE LIFE COURSE SHAPE LATER-LIFE HEALTH OUTCOMES IN THE U.S.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MULTICOMPONENT MHEALTH INTERVENTIONS FOR HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS AND THE COMMUNITY TO INCREASE CANCER SCREENING IN INDIA - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  GIVEN THAT A LARGE PROPORTION OF CANCERS ARE DETECTED AT A LATE STAGE IN INDIA, APPROACHES TO INCREASE SCREENING UPTAKE COULD HAVE A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT ON CANCER OUTCOMES. THERE IS LOW LEVEL OF AWARENESS OF CANCER RISK FACTORS, SYMPTOMS, AND IMPORTANCE OF SCREENING FOR EARLY DETECTION OF CANCERS AMONG INDIVIDUALS IN THE COMMUNITY. ADDITIONALLY, THERE IS LIMITED CANCER SCREENING KNOWLEDGE AND CAPACITY AMONG PRIMARY CARE PROVIDERS, WHO OFTEN HAVE COMPETING PRIORITIES LEAVING LIMITED TIME TO FOCUS ON CANCER SCREENING. MOBILE HEALTH (MHEALTH)-BASED EDUCATION CAN SERVE AS A POWERFUL TOOL FOR OFFERING E-LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES ON CANCER SCREENING AND CAN PROVIDE THE CONNECTIVITY REQUIRED TO LINK COMMUNITY AND HEALTH CARE SETTINGS, AS MOBILE TECHNOLOGY IS WIDELY AVAILABLE AND INEXPENSIVE. FIRST, WE WILL DEVELOP AN INNOVATIVE MHEALTH PLATFORM, THE INTEGRATED CANCER AWARENESS NETWORK (ICAN), WHICH WILL APPLY THEORY-DRIVEN CONCEPTS TO EDUCATE INDIVIDUALS ELIGIBLE FOR COLORECTAL, BREAST, OR CERVICAL CANCER SCREENING (REFERRED TO AS “PATIENTS”) AND HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS THROUGH APPS ACCESSED ON THEIR OWN MOBILE DEVICES. ICAN WILL CONNECT PATIENTS AND PROVIDERS WITH SCREENING SUPPORT STAFF AT TERTIARY MEDICAL COLLEGES WHO WILL PROVIDE COORDINATION AND NAVIGATION VIA AN INTERACTIVE DASHBOARD. SECOND, WE WILL USE IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE METHODS TO EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS, PROCESSES, AND COST-EFFECTIVENESS OF THE ICAN MHEALTH PLATFORM. WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING AIMS: R21-1. DEVELOP ICAN MHEALTH PLATFORM TO EDUCATE PRIMARY CARE PROVIDERS AND PATIENTS ON CANCER RISK FACTORS, SYMPTOMS, SCREENING TESTS, AND BENEFITS OF EARLY DETECTION VIA APPS AND CREATE DASHBOARD FOR HUBS. R21-2. PERFORM QUALITY AND USABILITY ASSESSMENT WITH KEY STAKEHOLDERS, INCLUDING PROVIDERS, PATIENTS, AND HUB STAFF TO EVALUATE THE EASE OF USE, INFORMATIONAL CONTENT, PERCEIVED USEFULNESS, AND INTERFACE AGILITY. R21-3. CONDUCT A PILOT STUDY TO EVALUATE AND FINALIZE THE ICAN MULTICOMPONENT INTERVENTION PLATFORM. R33-1. CONDUCT A CLUSTER RANDOMIZED TRIAL TO ASSESS THE IMPACT OF THE ICAN MHEALTH MULTICOMPONENT INTERVENTION PLATFORM ON CANCER SCREENING UPTAKE COMPARED TO AN EDUCATION APP OFFERED ONLY TO PROVIDERS. R33-2. USE A MIXED-METHODS APPROACH TO COMPARE IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES OF THE TWO STRATEGIES USED IN THE TRIAL, INCLUDING ACCESSIBILITY, USABILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, FEASIBILITY, AFFORDABILITY, FIDELITY, AND SUSTAINABILITY. R33-3. PERFORM ECONOMIC EVALUATIONS TO ASSESS COST-EFFECTIVENESS AND RETURN-ON-INVESTMENT SCENARIOS OF THE ICAN MHEALTH PLATFORM COMPARED TO PROVIDER EDUCATION APP ALONE.  THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE DATA-DRIVEN EVIDENCE ON THE UTILITY OF MHEALTH MULTICOMPONENT INTERVENTIONS IN CREATING AN INTERCONNECTED INFRASTRUCTURE TO OFFER ORGANIZED POPULATION-BASED SCREENING TO INCREASE UPTAKE OF CANCER SCREENING. THE STATE AND CENTRAL GOVERNMENTS IN INDIA CAN USE THE NEW EVIDENCE GENERATED TO DESIGN OPTIMAL APPROACHES TO SCALE UP THE IMPLEMENTATION OF CANCER SCREENING RECOMMENDATIONS. THE LESSON LEARNED CAN BE APPLIED TO OTHER LIMITED-RESOURCE SETTINGS.

description: COALITION FOR HEALTH, RESILIENCE AND PREVENTION (CHRP): DEVELOPING AND TESTING A NOVEL HUB AND SPOKE MODEL TO IMPLEMENT PREVENTION SERVICES IN RURAL CLINICS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT RURAL COMMUNITIES IN THE U.S. HAVE BEEN TREMENDOUSLY IMPACTED BY THE OVERDOSE AND ADDICTION CRISIS AND FACE UNIQUE RURAL-SPECIFIC FACTORS (E.G., LIMITED TREATMENT ACCESS, DISTANCE TO CARE). WE HAVE EFFECTIVE PREVENTION INTERVENTIONS THAT REDUCE RISKS OF NON-MEDICAL SUBSTANCE USE AND PREVENT CONSEQUENCES (E.G., OVERDOSE EDUCATION, NALOXONE). TO IMPLEMENT THESE STRATEGIES, IT IS ALSO CRITICAL TO ADDRESS KEY BARRIERS AND CHALLENGES IN RURAL COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING IN PEOPLE EXPERIENCING SOCIOECONOMIC HARDSHIP, VETERANS AND OTHERS, WHO HAVE SOME OF THE HIGHEST OVERDOSE RATES. THESE INTERVENTIONS IMPLEMENTED TOGETHER WITH HEALTHCARE CLINICS IN RURAL COMMUNITIES, HAVE TREMENDOUS POTENTIAL TO SAVE LIVES, BUT THE VAST MAJORITY OF RURAL AREAS CURRENTLY LACK ACCESS. WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP AND TEST A NOVEL HUB AND SPOKE MODEL/INTERVENTION CALLED COALITION FOR HEALTH, RESILIENCE AND PREVENTION (CHRP, ‘CHIRP’) TO HELP RURAL CLINICS (E.G., PRIMARY CARE AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH) ADOPT AND DELIVER EFFECTIVE PREVENTION SERVICES. HUB AND SPOKE MODELS HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED FOR OPIOID USE DISORDER (OUD) AND OTHER CONDITIONS AND ARE A COST-EFFECTIVE WAY TO SUSTAINABLY INCREASE ADOPTION AND DELIVERY OF EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS AND IMPROVE PATIENT CARE IN RURAL AREAS. MODELS VARY SUBSTANTIALLY, BUT HUB SITES CAN HELP TRAIN CLINICIANS/STAFF IN SPOKE SITES AND DELIVER CLINICAL INTERVENTIONS VIA TELEHEALTH TO PATIENTS. OTHER POTENTIAL COMPONENTS INCLUDE VIRTUAL LEARNING COLLABORATIVES AND INTERVENTIONS DIRECTLY DELIVERED FROM HUBS TO PATIENTS. HOWEVER, THIS MODEL HAS NOT BEEN ROBUSTLY LEVERAGED TO IMPLEMENT PREVENTION STRATEGIES. WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP AND TEST CHRP ACROSS RURAL COMMUNITIES IN MICHIGAN. WE ARE ADDICTION COMMUNITY AND RESEARCH LEADERS INCLUDING IN LARGE HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS CARING FOR RURAL POPULATIONS. OUR PROPOSAL BUILDS ON PRIOR WORK BUILDING/TESTING EFFECTIVE PREVENTION INTERVENTIONS AND LEADING STATE/NATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT HAVE TRAINED THOUSANDS OF HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS AND INCREASED CARE DELIVERY. DURING THE R61 DEVELOPMENTAL PHASE, WITH THE CHRP ADVISORY BOARD INCLUDING COMMUNITY PARTNERS, WE WILL HELP REFINE THE INTERVENTION, DEVELOP AN INTERVENTION TOOLKIT, AND CONDUCT FOCUSED USABILITY TESTING. IN THE R33, WE WILL CONDUCT A TYPE I HYBRID EFFECTIVENESS‐IMPLEMENTATION TRIAL WITH A STEPPED-WEDGE DESIGN, ACROSS RURAL SPOKE CLINICS. THIS PROJECT WILL HAVE HIGH PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT BY CO-DESIGNING WITH KEY COMMUNITY PARTNERS AND TESTING A HIGHLY PRAGMATIC AND SUSTAINABLE MODEL THAT CAN BE IMPLEMENTED IN RURAL HEALTHCARE CLINICS TO DELIVER EFFECTIVE PREVENTION SERVICES.

description: AN AGE-FRIENDLY LEARNING HEALTHCARE SYSTEM: A TRANSFORMATIVE DIGITAL SOLUTION FOR GERIATRICS CLINICS - PROJECT SUMMARY THE GOAL OF THE PROPOSED WORK IS TO DEVELOP AND TEST INNOVATIVE HEALTH INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) TOOLS THAT SUPPORT AN OUTPATIENT GERIATRICS CARE AGE-FRIENDLY LEARNING HEALTHCARE SYSTEM WITH A POINT OF CARE CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT (CDS) SYSTEM THAT LEVERAGES PATIENT GENERATED HEALTH DATA (PGHD) AND ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR) DATA AND POPULATION-LEVEL REPORTS THAT SUPPORT AGE-FRIENDLY HEALTH SYSTEM CARE. AGE-FRIENDLY HEALTH SYSTEM CARE IS A GENERAL APPROACH TO CARE – A TRANSFORMATIONAL MOVEMENT RATHER THAN A MODEL OF CARE – DEVELOPED AND PROMOTED BY THE INSTITUTE FOR HEALTHCARE IMPROVEMENT. AN AGE-FRIENDLY CARE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM PROVIDES CARE FOR GERIATRICS PATIENTS RELATED TO THE “4MS” – WHAT MATTERS MOST, MEDICATION, MENTATION, AND MOBILITY. AGE-FRIENDLY CARE IS TAILORED TO THE NEEDS AND VALUES OF GERIATRICS PATIENTS (E.G., WHAT MATTERS MOST TO THEM MEANING THEIR GOALS AND MOTIVATIONS) AS WELL AS ASSESSMENT AND HEALTHCARE ACTIONS RELATED TO THIS POPULATION’S SPECIFIC NEEDS SUCH AS FALLS ASSESSMENTS (MOBILITY), AVOIDANCE OF MEDICATIONS INTERFERING WITH WHAT MATTERS MOST (MEDICATIONS WITH PROBLEMATIC SIDE EFFECTS), AND ASSESSMENT AND TREATMENT FOR DEMENTIA AND DEPRESSION (MENTATION). AGE-FRIENDLY CARE IS EVIDENCE-BASED BUT WE NEED SPECIFIC AND REPEATABLE WAYS TO GATHER STRONGER EVIDENCE TO SUPPORT SPECIFIC AGE-FRIENDLY CARE ACTIONS AND TO TIE THIS CARE TO MEANINGFUL PATIENT OUTCOMES. TO FULLY REALIZE THE POTENTIAL OF AGE-FRIENDLY CARE USING THE 4MS, IT IS ESSENTIAL TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT HEALTH INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) SYSTEMS FOR EFFECTIVELY HARNESSING AND DISPLAYING DATA AT INSTITUTIONAL AND POINT OF CARE LEVELS. POINT OF CARE CDS WILL SUPPORT CLINICAL PRACTICE QUALITY OF CARE. DATA DISPLAY TOOLS FOR INSTITUTIONAL DECISION-MAKERS SUPPORT SENSE-MAKING BY DECISION-MAKER USERS BY FACILITATING THEIR ACCESS TO AND SYNTHESIS OF DATA TO DETECT PATTERNS IN SCREENING, UNDERSTAND VARIATION IN CARE PRACTICE, AND EXPLORE ASSOCIATED HEALTHCARE OUTCOMES. THROUGHOUT THE STUDY, WILL USE THE INTEROPERABLE SMART ON FHIR FRAMEWORK SUCH THAT THE TOOLS WE DEVELOP CAN BE USED ACROSS HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS. WE WILL DEVELOP PROTOTYPE AGE-FRIENDLY CARE DIGITAL TOOLS. WE WILL INCORPORATE PGHD AND EHR DATA RELEVANT TO THE 4MS IN A 4MS CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT (CDS) MODULE BUILT ON OUR EXISTING WORK IN A PROTOTYPE CLINICIAN-FACING, DYNAMIC DISPLAY. IN A PROCESS OF SUCCESSIVE ITERATION AND IMPROVEMENT WE WILL INTEGRATE PROTOTYPE AGE-FRIENDLY DIGITAL TOOLS INTO CLINICAL CARE AND OPTIMIZE WORKFLOW. WE WILL COMPLETE RIGOROUS ASSESSMENT OF INSTITUTIONAL DECISION-MAKER, CLINICIAN, AND PATIENT AND CAREGIVER USERS’ PERCEPTIONS OF USEFULNESS OF THE AGE-FRIENDLY DIGITAL TOOLS. TOOLS WILL INCLUDE A 4MS PGD COLLECTION TOOL, 4MS CDS TOOL, AND 4MS OUTPATIENT POPULATION-LEVEL REPORT. WE WILL EXAMINE THE ASSOCIATIONS OF AGE-FRIENDLY DIGITAL TOOLS AT THE POINT OF CARE WITH COMPREHENSIVENESS OF 4MS CARE AND EXPLORE ADDITIONAL HEALTH OUTCOMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
subAgency: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
description: ML-ROVER: MACHINE LEARNING TO REDUCE LABORATORY TEST OVERUTILIZATION - MORE THAN 20% OF LABORATORY TESTS IN THE INTENSIVE CARE UNIT ARE MEDICALLY UNNECESSARY. LABORATORY OVERUTILIZATION CONTRIBUTES TO REDUCED CARE QUALITY AND ADVERSE COMPLICATIONS INCLUDING IATROGENIC ANEMIA. MULTIPLE MEDICAL SOCIETIES HAVE HIGHLIGHTED THE URGENT NEED TO ADDRESS THIS PROBLEM, BUT THE VAST MAJORITY OF INTERVENTIONS IN THE LITERATURE ARE QUALITY-IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVES WITH POOR GENERALIZABILITY. THE LITERATURE IS EVEN SPARSER IN THE HIGHLY VULNERABLE PEDIATRIC POPULATION, WHO ARE MORE SUSCEPTIBLE TO IATROGENIC ANEMIA GIVEN THEIR SMALLER BLOOD VOLUMES THAN ADULT PATIENTS. WITH THE RAPID EXPANSION OF ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (EHRS) AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF MASSIVE CLINICAL DATABASES, MACHINE LEARNING (ML) HAS BECOME A PROMISING TOOL THAT CAN ADDRESS THE PROBLEM OF LABORATORY OVERUTILIZATION. WHILE FEW MODELS HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED TO PREDICT LABORATORY RESULTS IN ADULTS, AMONG PEDIATRIC PATIENTS MODEL DEVELOPMENT IS EXTREMELY LIMITED. FURTHERMORE, VERY FEW PREDICTIVE ML MODELS IN ANY CLINICAL DOMAIN ARE TRANSLATED INTO USABLE CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT (CDS). DESPITE STRONG RECOMMENDATIONS FROM NEARLY ALL BEST PRACTICE INFORMATICS RESOURCES, MOST CDS IMPLEMENTATIONS RELY ON “OUT-OF-BOX” DEPLOYMENT RATHER THAN EMPLOYING USER-CENTERED DESIGN PRINCIPLES. THIS CAN LEAVE BURDENSOME, SOMETIMES HARMFUL SYSTEMS IN PLACE WITHOUT DEMONSTRATED EFFECTIVENESS.  THIS STAGED-AWARD PROPOSAL WILL LEVERAGE THE PICU DATA COLLABORATIVE (PDC), A MULTICENTER COLLABORATION OF PEDIATRIC INTENSIVE CARE UNITS (PICUS) ACROSS THE UNITED STATES, TO DEVELOP ML-BASED CDS TO PREDICT FUTURE LABORATORY VALUES FOR THE PURPOSE OF REDUCING LABORATORY OVERUTILIZATION. IN THE R21 PHASE, ML MODELS WILL BE TRAINED ON 188,000+ UNIQUE PICU PATIENT ENCOUNTERS IN THE PDC DATABASE TO FORECAST FUTURE LABORATORY VALUES (AIM 1). CONCURRENTLY, GUIDED BY THE PRACTICAL ROBUST IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINABILITY MODEL (PRISM) FRAMEWORK, CONTEXTUAL FACTORS WILL BE IDENTIFIED TO INFORM AN ML-BASED CDS IMPLEMENTATION WITHIN THE PICU SOCIOTECHNICAL ENVIRONMENT. IN THE R33 PHASE, NEW A PRIORI IDENTIFIED FEATURES WILL BE INCORPORATED TO ENHANCE THE ML MODELS DEVELOPED IN AIM 1. THESE RETRAINED MODELS WILL BE SILENTLY EVALUATED ON PROSPECTIVE DATA FROM SELECTED PDC SITES. IN AIM 4, AN EHR-EMBEDDED CDS TOOL WILL BE DESIGNED FOR A SELECTED PDC SITE, INCORPORATING USER-CENTERED DESIGN PRINCIPLES INFORMED BY THE RESULTS OF AIM 2. THE FINAL ML MODEL FROM AIM 3 WILL THEN BE DEPLOYED IN A PILOT STUDY AT THE SINGLE SITE, WHERE WE WILL MEASURE THE IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES OF REACH AND ADOPTION.  THE RESULT OF THIS WORK WILL ESTABLISH A USEFUL, USABLE CDS TOOL TO REDUCE LABORATORY OVERUTILIZATION BASED ON MULTICENTER DATA AND FRAMED IN THE PICU CONTEXTUAL ENVIRONMENT. OUR PILOT DEPLOYMENT WILL ESTABLISH THE GROUNDWORK FOR A FUTURE EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION HYBRID MULTICENTER TRIAL. THESE PROCESSES WILL BE GENERALIZABLE AND SERVE AS A BLUEPRINT FOR DEVELOPING DATA-DRIVEN TRANSLATIONAL DECISION SUPPORT TOOLS THAT CAN BE ADAPTED TO A VARIETY OF DIVERSE HEALTHCARE SETTINGS AND SUBSEQUENTLY REDUCE DISPARITIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: USING KETAMINE TO ENHANCE MEMORY RECONSOLIDATION AND EXTINCTION OF OVERGENERALIZED FEAR IN INDIVIDUALS DIAGNOSED WITH PTSD - PROJECT SUMMARY POSTTRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER (PTSD) IS A DEBILITATING AND A CHRONIC MENTAL ILLNESS. THERE ARE CURRENTLY ONLY TWO FDA-APPROVED MEDICATIONS FOR THE TREATMENT OF PTSD, BOTH OF WHICH MAY TAKE WEEKS TO MONTHS TO REACH FULL CLINICAL EFFECTS. THE RATES OF NONRESPONSE TO THESE SELECTIVE SEROTONIN REUPTAKE INHIBITOR ANTIDEPRESSANTS ARE HIGH. THEREFORE, THERE IS A TREMENDOUS NEED TO TEST NOVEL PHARMACOLOGICAL APPROACHES TO PTSD. TRAUMA FOCUS PSYCHOTHERAPIES ON THE OTHER HAND REQUIRE A HIGH LEVEL OF COMMITMENT BY ATTENDING WEEKLY VISITS FOR A SUBSTANTIAL AMOUNT TO TIME. AN AVERAGE COURSE OF PROLONGED EXPOSURES THERAPY (PE) OR TRAUMA FOCUS CBT USUALLY LASTS ABOUT 3 MONTHS UNTIL COMPLETION WITH HIGH DROPOUT RATE AND ABOUT 50% OF COMPLETERS BEING CLASSIFIED AS NON-RESPONDERS. RECENT STUDIES DEMONSTRATED THE EFFECTIVENESS OF INTENSIVE EXPOSURE THERAPY FOR PTSD WHICH IS BEING DELIVERED WITHIN 1-2 WEEKS PERIOD THAT ARE AS AFFECTIVE AS A 3-MONTH FULL COURSE TREATMENT BUT HAVE A LOWER DROPOUT RATE.  THERE ARE EVIDENCES TO SUGGEST THAT FEAR EXTINCTION MAY BE FURTHER ENHANCED WITH THE USE OF KETAMINE, AN N-METHYL-D-ASPARTATE GLUTAMATE RECEPTOR (NMDAR) ANTAGONIST MOSTLY USED AS ANESTHETIC. INTEREST IN KETAMINE AS A POSSIBLE TREATMENT FOR PTSD BEGAN WHEN IT WAS FOUND TO ALLEVIATE DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS. TWO RECENT STUDIES HAVE REPORTED THAT KETAMINE REDUCES PTSD SYMPTOMS DURING THE COURSE OF DRUG ADMINISTRATION PERIOD AND UP TO 7-DAY POST TREATMENT, BUT ALL PARTICIPANTS CONVERT TO PTSD SOON AFTER DRUG DISCONTINUATION.  USING A BIOMARKER-INFORMED, DOUBLE BLIND PLACEBO-CONTROLLED DESIGN, THE PRESENT PROPOSAL AIMS TO EXAMINE THE EFFICACY OF KETAMINE INFUSION (0.5MG/KG VS 0.2MG/KG IN THE R61 PHASE TO ESTABLISHED DOSE; SELECTED SUPERIOR DOSE WILL ADVANCE TO THE R33), AS COMPARED TO AN ACTIVE PLACEBO (MIDAZOLAM 0.045MG/KG) IN ENHANCING POSTRETRIEVAL EXTINCTION OF CRITERION A ORIGINAL TRAUMA MEMORY. PHARMACOLOGICAL INTERVENTION WILL BE COMBINED WITH AN INTENSIVE 4-DAY EXPOSURE THERAPY, UTILIZING ELEVATED BDNF LEVELS AND INCREASED NEUROPLASTICITY, TO POTENTIALLY PRODUCE A RAPID AND SUSTAINED REDUCTION IN PTSD SYMPTOMATOLOGY. IN ADDITION, WE PROPOSE USE OF STATE-OF-THE-ART NEUROIMAGING ASSESSMENTS AT BASELINE AND AT THE END OF TREATMENT TRIAL TO GAIN INSIGHT INTO THE NEUROBIOLOGY OF PTSD AND THE NEURAL MECHANISMS DICTATING TREATMENT RESPONSE OR RESISTANCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENHANCING MALAYSIAN WORKERS' SAFETY AND HEALTH THROUGH SAFETY CULTURE AND CLIMATE MHEALTH INTERVENTIONS - THIS PROJECT DEVELOPS AND EVALUATES A LOW-RESOURCE, SCALABLE MOBILE HEALTH (MHEALTH)-BASED OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY INTERVENTION IN MALAYSIA FOR FUTURE ADAPTATION TO U.S. WORKPLACES, PARTICULARLY HIGH-RISK INDUSTRIES EMPLOYING LMIC-ORIGIN/IMMIGRANT WORKERS WHO EXPERIENCE DISPROPORTIONATELY ELEVATED INJURY RATES. OCCUPATIONAL INJURIES REMAIN A MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH CHALLENGE GLOBALLY, ESPECIALLY IN MANUFACTURING, CONSTRUCTION, AND HEALTHCARE SECTORS. ALTHOUGH SAFETY CULTURE (SC) IS AMONG THE STRONGEST PREDICTORS OF INJURY REDUCTION, MOST EVIDENCE-BASED SC INTERVENTIONS REMAIN TOO RESOURCE-INTENSIVE FOR IMPLEMENTATION AND SUSTAINABILITY IN LOW- AND MIDDLE-INCOME COUNTRY (LMIC) SETTINGS. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, WE DEVELOPED AN MHEALTH-BASED INTERVENTION REQUIRING ONLY MINIMAL TIME, INTERNET CONNECTIVITY, AND SMARTPHONE ACCESS, THEREBY MAXIMIZING SCALABILITY IN RESOURCE-CONSTRAINED ENVIRONMENTS WHILE SUPPORTING FUTURE DISSEMINATION IN VARIOUS U.S. OCCUPATIONAL SETTINGS. MALAYSIA PROVIDES A NECESSARY ENVIRONMENT FOR THIS PROJECT DUE TO ITS LARGE-SCALE HIGH-RISK INDUSTRIAL WORKFORCE, RAPIDLY INDUSTRIALIZING ECONOMY, AND ESTABLISHED RESEARCH PARTNERSHIPS CAPABLE OF SUPPORTING RIGOROUS IMPLEMENTATION AND EVALUATION. THESE CONDITIONS ARE PARTICULARLY VALUABLE AS SAFETY CULTURE INTERVENTIONS REMAIN UNDERSTUDIED IN LMICS WHERE OCCUPATIONAL RISKS AND IMPLEMENTATION BARRIERS ARE GREATER THAN THOSE TYPICALLY ENCOUNTERED IN THE UNITED STATES, CREATING A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO “STRESS-TEST” SCALABLE INTERVENTIONS PRIOR TO U.S. DISSEMINATION. MALAYSIA IS ALSO STRATEGICALLY RELEVANT TO AMERICAN ECONOMIC AND PUBLIC HEALTH INTERESTS BECAUSE ITS INDUSTRIES MANUFACTURE SEMICONDUCTORS, MEDICAL DEVICES, AND INDUSTRIAL COMPONENTS DIRECTLY INTEGRATED INTO U.S. HEALTHCARE AND CONSUMER SUPPLY CHAINS. UNSAFE WORKING CONDITIONS WITHIN THESE SECTORS MAY AFFECT SUPPLY CHAIN STABILITY, PRODUCT QUALITY, AND DOWNSTREAM U.S. PUBLIC HEALTH INTERESTS. THE PROJECT ADDITIONALLY ADDRESSES THE GROWING OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH NEEDS OF LMIC-ORIGIN/IMMIGRANT WORKERS IN THE UNITED STATES, WHO COMPRISE A DISPROPORTIONATELY INJURED SEGMENT OF THE HIGH-RISK WORKFORCE. THE VALIDATED MHEALTH ASSESSMENT TOOLS, CULTURAL ADAPTATION METHODS, AND IMPLEMENTATION FRAMEWORK DEVELOPED IN THIS PROJECT ARE SPECIFICALLY DESIGNED FOR GLOBAL-TO-LOCAL (G2L) TRANSLATION INTO U.S. WORKPLACES THAT INCLUDE VULNERABLE WORKER POPULATIONS. DURING THE COMPLETED R21 PHASE, WE:  (AIM 1) VALIDATED MALAYLANGUAGE OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY CULTURE ASSESSMENT TOOLS (CRONBACH’S Á = .89–.97); (AIM 2) DEVELOPED A MULTILEVEL MHEALTH SAFETY TRAINING INTERVENTION; AND (AIM 3) DEMONSTRATED FEASIBILITY AND IMPROVED SAFETY OUTCOMES IN A MALAYSIAN MANUFACTURING COMPANY. THE PROPOSED R33 PHASE WILL: (AIM 4) IMPLEMENT AND CROSS-VALIDATE THE INTERVENTION ACROSS MANUFACTURING, HEALTHCARE, AND CONSTRUCTION SECTORS; AND (AIM 5) ESTABLISH MALAYSIA’S FIRST NATIONAL OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY CULTURE BENCHMARK WHILE DEVELOPING A G2L ADAPTATION FRAMEWORK FOR FUTURE U.S. IMPLEMENTATION. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A SCALABLE, COST-EFFECTIVE MODEL FOR IMPROVING OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY IN LMICS WHILE INFORMING INTERVENTIONS TO PROTECT WORKERS IN THE UNITED STATES.

description: ADAPTING AND EVALUATING SMARTPHONE APP-ENHANCED HOME BLOOD PRESSURE MONITORING AMONG PREGNANT WOMEN IN GHANA - HYPERTENSIVE DISORDERS OF PREGNANCY ARE A LEADING CAUSE OF MATERNAL MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY, PARTICULARLY IN LOW-RESOURCE SETTINGS WORLDWIDE. HOME BP MONITORING IS AN EMERGING STRATEGY TO PROMOTE FREQUENT MONITORING OF BPS, HOWEVER UNIQUE CHALLENGES EXIST IN LOW-RESOURCE SETTINGS IN LMICS AND IN THE UNITED STATES. GIVEN WIDESPREAD SMARTPHONE USE IN URBAN GHANA, WE WILL LEVERAGE ACCESSIBLE TECHNOLOGY, ADAPTED TO THE GHANAIAN SETTING, TO OVERCOME BARRIERS TO HOME BP MONITORING. AIM 1 (R21) WILL ADAPT A HOME BP MONITORING SMARTPHONE APP TO THE GHANAIAN CONTEXT, USING THE ADAPT ITT FRAMEWORK. STAKEHOLDER FOCUS GROUPS AND COGNITIVE INTERVIEWS WILL BE HELD WITH GHANAIAN PREGNANT WOMEN, MIDWIVES, AND OBSTETRICIAN/GYNECOLOGISTS TO ITERATIVELY ADAPT THE SMARTPHONE APP, WITH A FOCUS ON CULTURAL RELEVANCE, LOCALLY APPROPRIATE LANGUAGE AND PHRASING, AND USEABILITY IN LOW LITERACY AND NUMERACY POPULATIONS. AIM 2 (R21) WILL ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND FIDELITY OF A SMARTPHONE APP-ENHANCED HOME BP MONITORING INTERVENTION AMONG PREGNANT PATIENTS IN GHANA. WE WILL ENGAGE 100 PREGNANT PARTICIPANTS OVER 4 WEEKS OF HOME BP MONITORING USING THE REFINED SMARTPHONE APP, AND COMPLETE PRE-AND-POST VALIDATED SCALES OF ACCEPTABILITY, APPROPRIATENESS, AND FEASIBILITY. FIDELITY WILL BE EVALUATED BY EXAMINING STORED VALUES IN THE BP MONITOR AND SMARTPHONE APP TO DETERMINE IF CONCERNING COMBINATIONS OF ELEVATED BPS AND PREECLAMPSIA SYMPTOMS CORRECTLY TRIGGER CLINICAL ALERTS. AIM 3 (R33) WILL MEASURE THE ADHERENCE TO BP MONITORING WITH A SMARTPHONE APP-ENHANCED HOME BP MONITORING INTERVENTION AMONG PREGNANT PATIENTS IN GHANA. WE WILL ENGAGE A PROSPECTIVE COHORT OF 200 PREGNANT PARTICIPANTS IN HOME BP MONITORING FROM ENROLLMENT THROUGH DELIVERY. ADHERENCE TO BP MONITORING WILL BE MEASURED BOTH AS FREQUENCY AND TIME TO DROP-OFF OF MONITORING OVER THE COURSE OF PREGNANCY. AIM 4 (R33) WILL EVALUATE THE CLINICAL RESPONSE TO ELEVATED BPS WITH A SMARTPHONE APP-ENHANCED HOME BP MONITORING INTERVENTION AMONG PREGNANT PATIENTS IN GHANA. AUTOMATIC ALERTS, TRIGGERED BY BPS AND SYMPTOMS, WILL BE SENT TO STUDY NURSES TRAINED ON CLINICAL RESPONSE PROTOCOLS. TIMELY CLINICAL RESPONSE (ROUTINE ALERT: <4 HOURS; URGENT ALERT: <1 HOUR) WILL BE EVALUATED BY COMPARING TIMES OF A RECORDED ELEVATED BP TO THE OUTGOING PHONE CALL BY THE NURSE AND SUCCESSFUL CONTACT WITH THE PARTICIPANT. APPROPRIATENESS OF CLINICAL RESPONSE WILL BE ASSESSED USING AN EXPERT CONSENSUS APPROACH. OUTCOME OF CLINICAL RESPONSE WILL BE EVALUATED BY THE PROPORTION OF PARTICIPANTS WHO ADHERE WITH CLINICAL ADVICE PROVIDED BY THE STUDY NURSE. SMARTPHONE APP-ENABLED HOME BP MONITORING IS A NOVEL STRATEGY TO ADDRESS CHALLENGES IN MANAGING HDP. IMPLEMENTING HOME BP MONITORING IN LOW-RESOURCE SETTINGS WORLDWIDE WILL PROVIDE A CRITICAL STEP TOWARD FREQUENT ASSESSMENT OF BPS, EARLIER DIAGNOSIS OF HDP, AND PREVENTION OF SERIOUS MATERNAL MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY. FINDINGS FROM THIS STUDY WILL INFORM IMPACTFUL HOME BP MONITORING INTERVENTIONS IN LOW LITERACY AND NUMERACY POPULATIONS ACROSS LMICS AND IN THE UNITED STATES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADAPTING MHEALTH TO IMPROVE HIV OUTCOMES AMONG OLDER PEOPLE WITH HIV IN UKRAINE - IN THE US, 60% OF PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV ARE OLDER ADULTS, DEFINED AS >50 YEARS, OFTEN NEGLECTED BY TREATMENT AND PREVENTION EFFORTS. CONSEQUENTLY, ONLY 63.7% OF OLDER PEOPLE WITH HIV (OPWH) IN THE US HAVE ACHIEVED VIRAL SUPPRESSION, FAR FROM THE US ENDING THE HIV EPIDEMIC GOALS. OPWH ARE VULNERABLE TO DISRUPTIONS IN HEALTH CARE SERVICES AND FREQUENTLY EXPERIENCE MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS, BOTH OF WHICH CAN LEAD TO TREATMENT INTERRUPTIONS AND INCREASED MORTALITY. KEY BARRIERS TO ART AMONG OPWH INCLUDE STIGMA, SOCIAL ISOLATION AND MULTIMORBIDITY, INCLUDING DEPRESSION. INNOVATIVE STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE ENGAGEMENT IN CARE ARE CRITICAL TO IMPROVING TREATMENT OUTCOMES AMONG OPWH. PREVIOUSLY WE DEMONSTRATED OPWH ARE INTERESTED IN PEER SUPPORT, INTERESTED IN MHEALTH TO STRENGTHEN BELONGING WITHIN A COMMUNITY, AND THAT THEY HAVE THE CAPACITY FOR SMARTPHONE USE. GLOBALLY, 80% OF OPWH LIVE IN LOW- AND MIDDLE-INCOME COUNTRIES. IN UKRAINE, OPWH ACCOUNT FOR 15% OF PEOPLE WITH NEWLY DIAGNOSED HIV ANNUALLY THOUGH OPWH ARE SIGNIFICANTLY LESS LIKELY TO INITIATE ART AND BE RETAINED IN CARE COMPARED TO YOUNGER PEOPLE WITH HIV. UKRAINE PROVIDES A HIGHLY RELEVANT SETTING IN WHICH TO ADAPT AND EVALUATE A MHEALTH INTERVENTION TAILORED FOR OPWH. POSITIVELINKS (PL) IS AN EFFECTIVE MHEALTH PLATFORM FOR IMPROVING VIROLOGIC OUTCOMES IN PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV IN THE US. PL DELIVERS APPOINTMENT REMINDERS, DAILY QUERIES (“CHECK-INS”) OF MOOD, STRESS AND MEDICATION ADHERENCE, TAILORED EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES, AND THE OPPORTUNITY TO INTERACT WITH OTHERS ON A SECURE, ANONYMOUS COMMUNITY MESSAGE BOARD (CMB). WE PROPOSE TO EXTEND THE USE OF POSITIVELINKS AMONG US OPWH, BY ADAPTING AND TESTING IT DURING HEALTH CARE SYSTEM DISRUPTIONS IN THE UKRAINIAN CONTEXT, AND TO INCORPORATE ACCEPTABLE DEPRESSION SCREENING WITH SUBSEQUENT BRIEF INTERVENTION AND REFERRAL (SBIRT) TO CLINICAL EVALUATION, WHICH CAN FACILITATE OUTCOMES FOR OPWH IN THE US.   IN THE R21 PHASE, WE PERFORMED FOCUS GROUPS DISCUSSIONS WITH OPWH AND KEY INFORMANT INTERVIEWS WITH CLINICIANS AND CLINIC ADMINISTRATORS,  IDENTIFIED ORIGINAL MHEALTH PLATFORM FEATURES TO RETAIN IN THE ADAPTED APP THAT ARE IMPORTANT FOR OPWH TO MEANINGFULLY ENGAGE IN HIV CARE. WE PERFORMED THEATER, ALPHA, AND BETA TESTING OF POSITIVELINKS UKRAINE TO EVALUATE USABILITY AND FUNCTIONALITY BY OPWH TO ENSURE THAT IT IS A TAILORED, FULLY INTERACTIVE APP SUPPORTED BY LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS. IN THE R33 PHASE, WE WILL PERFORM AN INDIVIDUALLY RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL AMONG 240 OPWH, WHO ARE NEWLY DIAGNOSED OR ON ART WITHOUT VIRAL SUPPRESSION, RANDOMIZED 1:1 TO THE PL UKRAINE INTERVENTION VERSUS TREATMENT AS USUAL, TO EVALUATE A) FEASIBILITY USING A VALIDATED FRAMEWORK, B) MULTILEVEL ACCEPTABILITY (OPWH, CLINICIANS, CLINIC ADMINISTRATORS, AND POLICY MAKERS), AND C) EFFICACY EXAMINING VIRAL LOAD SUPPRESSION AT 12 MONTHS AND SECONDARILY ART INITIATION, RETENTION AT 12 MONTHS, VL SUPPRESSION AT 6 MONTHS, AND TIME TO ART INITIATION. THESE FINDINGS WILL PROVIDE KEY DATA NECESSARY TO INFORM OPTIMIZING MHEALTH PLATFORMS FOR HIV OUTCOMES AMONG OLDER ADULTS IN THE US AND GLOBALLY.  THE MAJORITY OF INDIVIDUALS LIVING WITH HIV IN THE US ARE OLDER ADULTS, WHO ARE DIAGNOSED WITH ADVANCED HIV AND DO NOT OPTIMALLY ENGAGE IN CARE. ONLY 63.7% OF OLDER ADULTS WITH HIV IN THE US ACHIEVE VIROLOGIC SUPPRESSION, NECESSITATING INNOVATIVE STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE ENGAGEMENT IN CARE. AMONG OLDER ADULTS, BARRIERS TO ENGAGEMENT IN HIV CARE ARE SOCIAL ISOLATION, STIGMA, AND POOR MENTAL HEALTH INCLUDING DEPRESSION. FOCUSING THIS STUDY IN THE RESOURCE-LIMITED SETTING OF UKRAINE PERMITS AN EFFICIENT AND COST EFFECTIVE MEANS OF ADAPTING AN EVIDENCE-BASED MHEALTH INTERVENTION, POSITIVELINKS, TO OLDER ADULTS WITH HIV TO ENGAGE THEM IN HIV CARE, AND CONDUCTING A RCT TO ASSESS ACCEPTABILITY, FEASIBILITY, AND EFFICACY. UKRAINE HAS THE LARGEST HIV EPIDEMIC IN EUROPE WHERE ONLY 62% OF PEOPLE WITH HIV CURRENTLY ARE ON ART AND 58% HAVE ACHIEVED VIRAL LOAD SUPPRESSION. CONDUCTING THIS WORK

description: COMMUNITY–LED ADAPTATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF SBIRT FOR ALCOHOL IN TRIBAL PRIMARY CARE - PROJECT SUMMARY EXCESSIVE ALCOHOL USE CONTRIBUTES TO MORE DEATHS THAN OPIOIDS AND OTHER DRUGS COMBINED AND REMAINS A LEADING AND PREVENTABLE CAUSE OF DEATH IN THE UNITED STATES. MORTALITY FROM ALCOHOL IS HIGHEST AMONG AMERICAN INDIAN AND ALASKAN NATIVE (AI/AN) COMMUNITIES. SCREENING, BRIEF INTERVENTION, AND REFERRAL TO TREATMENT (SBIRT) IS AN EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTION FOR EARLY IDENTIFICATION AND REFERRAL TO TREATMENT OF UNHEALTHY ALCOHOL USE; HOWEVER, ITS IMPLEMENTATION IS NOT ONE SIZE FITS ALL. CULTURAL ADAPTATION IMPROVES SBIRT’S RELEVANCE AND UPTAKE, YET LIMITED WORK HAS BEEN DONE TO CULTURALLY ADAPT SBIRT IN AI/AN COMMUNITIES, WITH NONE FOCUSED IN TRIBAL PRIMARY CARE SETTINGS. IN MICHIGAN, NONE OF THE 12 TRIBAL PRIMARY CARE SETTINGS HAVE IMPLEMENTED SCREENING FOR UNHEALTHY ALCOHOL USE, BUT TRIBES HAVE IDENTIFIED THIS AS AN UNMET NEED. COMMUNITY-LED SOLUTIONS THAT ARE INTEGRATED WITHIN TRIBAL CONTINUUMS OF HEALTH SERVICES ARE NEEDED TO IMPROVE ALCOHOL-RELATED OUTCOMES. TO ADDRESS THIS CRITICAL GAP, THERE IS A COMPELLING OPPORTUNITY TO CULTURALLY ADAPT AND IMPLEMENT SBIRT FOR ALCOHOL IN TRIBAL PRIMARY CARE SETTINGS. OUR UNDERLYING HYPOTHESIS IS THAT CULTURALLY ADAPTED, EVIDENCE-BASED TOOLS WILL IMPROVE EARLY INTERVENTION AND TREATMENT FOR UNHEALTHY ALCOHOL USE IN AI/AN COMMUNITIES AND THEREBY IMPROVE DOWNSTREAM OUTCOMES. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO USE A COMMUNITY-LED APPROACH TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF AI/AN PEOPLE BY DEVELOPING, IMPLEMENTING, AND TESTING A CULTURALLY ADAPTED SBIRT FOR ALCOHOL. WE WILL USE A PARALLEL, CONVERGENT MIXED METHODS DESIGN AND A SINGLE-ARM PILOT TRIAL AT TRIBAL PRIMARY CARE SITES WITH A PARTIALLY NESTED DESIGN THAT WILL BE GROUNDED IN COMMUNITY-BASED PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH (CBPR) AND INFORMED BY THE INDIGENOUS FRAMEWORK OF ETUAPTMUMK, TWO-EYED SEEING (E/TES) THAT ENABLES INTEGRATION OF KNOWLEDGE FROM BOTH INDIGENOUS AND WESTERN PERSPECTIVES. PRINCIPLES OF CBPR AND E/TES, INCLUDING GUIDANCE FROM AN AI/AN COMMUNITY ADVISORY BOARD (CAB), WILL BE USED THROUGHOUT ALL PHASES OF THE STUDY. THEREFORE, OUR AIMS ARE TO: 1) IDENTIFY SOCIOCULTURAL AND ORGANIZATIONAL BARRIERS TO AND FACILITATING FACTORS FOR IMPLEMENTING ALCOHOL SBIRT IN TRIBAL PRIMARY CARE SETTINGS USING CONVERGENT MIXED METHODS TO IDENTIFY SBIRT IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES, 2) CULTURALLY ADAPT SBIRT FOR ALCOHOL WITH INTEGRATION OF EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS WITH TRIBAL BEST PRACTICES, AND 3) CONDUCT A PILOT CLINICAL TRIAL OF THE CULTURALLY ADAPTED SBIRT IN TRIBAL PRIMARY CARE SITES TO CHARACTERIZE CLUSTERING AND GENERATE KEY DESIGN PARAMETERS TO INFORM A POTENTIAL FUTURE INDIVIDUALLY RANDOMIZED GROUP TREATMENT (IRGT) TRIAL.. THIS APPLICATION ALIGNS WITH NATIONAL PRIORITIES TO IMPROVE EARLY INTERVENTION AND TREATMENT OF ALCOHOL. THIS INNOVATIVE APPLICATION WILL ENGAGE AI/AN COMMUNITIES TO DEVELOP AND PILOT TEST A SCALABLE PUBLIC HEALTH APPROACH TO REDUCE AUD IN TRIBAL PRIMARY CARE SETTINGS AND IMPROVE POPULATION HEALTH.
