description: GROUP SINGING OR SOLO SINGING TO IMPROVE VASCULAR HEALTH IN OLDER ADULTS WITH CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE (GOT VOICE): A FEASIBILITY STUDY - CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD) IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH IN THE COUNTRY THREATENING THE HEALTH OF THE ELDERLY. PARTICIPATION IN EXERCISE AND/OR CARDIAC REHABILITATION (CR) PROGRAMS REDUCES MORTALITY AND RISK OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT IN SECONDARY PREVENTION POPULATIONS, INCLUDING OLDER ADULTS. UNFORTUNATELY, OLDER ADULTS ARE LESS LIKELY TO PARTICIPATE IN REGULAR EXERCISE OR CR DUE TO AGE-RELATED COMPLEXITIES, INCLUDING MULTI-MORBIDITIES (ARTHRITIS, CHRONIC LUNG DISEASE, DIABETES), POLYPHARMACY, FRAILTY, DECONDITIONING, FALLS, DISABILITY, AND OTHER CHALLENGES THAT MAKE EXERCISE PARTICIPATION DIFFICULT. ALTERNATIVE REHABILITATION THERAPIES ARE NEEDED TO REDUCE CVD BURDEN AND IMPROVE HEALTH IN THE AGING POPULATION. SINGING IS A PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND THE PHYSIOLOGICAL DEMANDS OF SINGING ARE COMPARABLE WITH WALKING AT A MODERATELY BRISK PACE, SUGGESTING THAT THE HEALTH BENEFITS WITH SINGING MAY OVERLAP WITH THAT OF EXERCISE. UNLIKE TRADITIONAL PHYSICAL EXERCISE, THE IMPACT OF SINGING ON CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH, ESPECIALLY IN OLDER ADULTS, HAS NOT BEEN EXTENSIVELY STUDIED. ENDOTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION PREDICTS CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS, AND PHYSICAL EXERCISE IMPROVES VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL FUNCTION. OUR TEAM HAS BEEN THE FIRST TO DEMONSTRATE THAT SOLO SINGING IMPROVES MICROVASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL FUNCTION ACUTELY, REGARDLESS OF SINGING EXPERTISE. WE STUDIED 65 SUBJECTS (MEAN AGE 68±7, 40% WOMEN), SHOWING A SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENT IN MICROVASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL FUNCTION, AS MEASURED BY THE FRAMINGHAM REACTIVE HYPEREMIA INDEX (FRHI), AFTER 30 MINUTES OF SINGING IN THE INSTRUCTIONAL VIDEO ARM (30.9%, P=0.007) COMPARED TO THE REST CONTROL. THE OBSERVED CHANGE IN FRHI TRANSLATES INTO A ~25% REDUCTION IN CVD RISK, WHICH IS COMPARABLE TO TRADITIONAL CR PARTICIPATION. BASED ON THESE FINDINGS, THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE PLANNED FUTURE RCT IS TO TEST OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT HABITUAL SINGING OVER SEVERAL WEEKS, SIMILAR TO HABITUAL EXERCISE, WILL LEAD TO SUSTAINED AND FAVORABLE VASCULAR ADAPTATION, THEREBY LOWERING FUTURE CVD RISK. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS R34 PROPOSAL, TITLED “GROUP SINGING OR SOLO SINGING TO IMPROVE VASCULAR HEALTH IN OLDER ADULTS WITH CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE (GOT VOICE): A FEASIBILITY STUDY”, IS TO REFINE, DIVERSIFY, AND PROTOCOLIZE THE SINGING INTERVENTIONS AND TEST THE FEASIBILITY OF THE GOT VOICE PARALLEL RANDOMIZED CONTROL TRIAL DESIGN THAT WE WOULD IMPLEMENT IN THE FUTURE, LARGER CLINICAL TRIAL OF EFFICACY. FORTY-EIGHT SUBJECTS WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO EITHER (1) IN-PERSON GROUP SINGING OR (2) SOLO SINGING WITH AN INSTRUCTIONAL VIDEO SING-ALONG SERIES CREATED BY A VOICE EXPERT, OR (3) A HEALTH EDUCATION ATTENTION CONTROL ARM. ALL INTERVENTIONS ARE 12 WEEKS IN DURATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT PARTICIPATION RATES IN BOTH INTERVENTION ARMS OF GOT VOICE WILL BE SUPERIOR TO HISTORICAL TRADITIONAL CR PROGRAM PARTICIPATION RATES IN ADULTS ≥55 YEARS OLD WITH CVD. FEASIBILITY WILL BE DETERMINED BY RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, ADHERENCE, AND ACCEPTABILITY RATES. WITH A MULTI- DISCIPLINARY TEAM INCLUDING BOARD-CERTIFIED MUSIC THERAPISTS, A VOICE PROFESSOR, BIOSTATISTICIANS, A COMMUNITY MEDICINE EXPERT, AND A PREVENTIVE CARDIOLOGIST AND PHYSICIAN SCIENTIST WITH A 6+ YEAR HISTORY OF COLLABORATION, WE ARE CONFIDENT IN OUR ABILITY TO EXECUTE THE AIMS OF THIS PROPOSAL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THERABOT+: A FEASIBILITY STUDY INTEGRATING PASSIVE SENSING AND BIOFEEDBACK IN AI-DRIVEN MENTAL HEALTH SUPPORT - PROJECT SUMMARY DEPRESSION AND ANXIETY DISORDERS ARE AMONG THE MOST PREVALENT MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, AFFECTING MILLIONS OF INDIVIDUALS AND IMPOSING A SIGNIFICANT BURDEN ON INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, AND SOCIETY. DESPITE THE AVAILABILITY OF EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS, MANY PEOPLE FACE BARRIERS TO ACCESSING CARE, INCLUDING COST, STIGMA, AND LIMITED AVAILABILITY OF MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS. DIGITAL MENTAL HEALTH INTERVENTIONS, PARTICULARLY THOSE LEVERAGING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI), OFFER A PROMISING AVENUE TO INCREASE ACCESS TO PERSONALIZED, ON-DEMAND SUPPORT. HOWEVER, MOST EXISTING DIGITAL INTERVENTIONS LACK THE ABILITY TO DYNAMICALLY ADAPT TO AN INDIVIDUAL’S REAL-TIME PHYSIOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL STATE. IN RESPONSE TO THIS NEED, OUR TEAM DEVELOPED THERABOT, A GENERATIVE AI CHATBOT THAT HAS SHOWN PROMISE IN REDUCING SYMPTOMS OF DEPRESSION AND ANXIETY IN PRIOR RESEARCH. IN A RECENT RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL, THERABOT DEMONSTRATED SIGNIFICANT SYMPTOM REDUCTION COMPARED TO A WAITLIST CONTROL, HIGH USER ENGAGEMENT, AND STRONG THERAPEUTIC ALLIANCE RATINGS. TO FURTHER ENHANCE THE PERSONALIZATION AND EFFECTIVENESS OF THERABOT, THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO DEVELOP AND PILOT TEST AN ENHANCED VERSION, CALLED THERABOT+, WHICH INTEGRATES REAL-TIME BIOFEEDBACK AND PASSIVE SENSING DATA FROM SMARTPHONES. THERABOT+ WILL LEVERAGE HEART RATE VARIABILITY (HRV) BIOFEEDBACK, A MIND-BODY TECHNIQUE WITH DEMONSTRATED EFFICACY IN REDUCING STRESS AND ANXIETY. DURING PROMPTED BIOFEEDBACK SESSIONS, THERABOT+ WILL COLLECT HRV DATA THROUGH A SMARTPHONE’S CAMERA AND PROVIDE THE USER WITH PERSONALIZED FEEDBACK AND GUIDANCE ON RELAXATION TECHNIQUES, SUCH AS DEEP BREATHING AND MINDFULNESS EXERCISES. THERABOT+ WILL ALSO UTILIZE PASSIVE SENSING DATA, INCLUDING MEASURES OF SLEEP, ACTIVITY, AND SOCIAL ENGAGEMENT, TO PERSONALIZE INTERVENTIONS AND INITIATE JUST-IN-TIME ADAPTIVE INTERVENTIONS (JITAIS) WHEN POTENTIAL TRIGGERS FOR DEPRESSION OR ANXIETY ARE DETECTED. THIS R34 FEASIBILITY TRIAL WILL ENROLL 60 ADULTS DIAGNOSED WITH MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER AND/OR GENERALIZED ANXIETY DISORDER. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO RECEIVE EITHER THERABOT+ OR STANDARD THERABOT FOR EIGHT WEEKS. THE STUDY HAS THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) DETERMINE THE FEASIBILITY OF RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, AND DATA COLLECTION PROCEDURES; (2) ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF THERABOT+ COMPARED TO STANDARD THERABOT; AND (3) GATHER EXPLORATORY DATA ON THE FEASIBILITY OF COLLECTING VARIABLES (E.G., HRV, RUMINATION, PHYSIOLOGICAL FLEXIBILITY), WHICH HAVE BASIS FOR MEDIATION/MODERATION AIMS IN A SUBSEQUENT R01 APPLICATION. THIS FEASIBILITY TRIAL WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL DATA TO REFINE THERABOT+ AND INFORM THE DESIGN OF A FUTURE, FULLY POWERED RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL TO EVALUATE ITS EFFICACY IN IMPROVING MENTAL HEALTH OUTCOMES. THE LONG- TERM GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM IS TO DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE A SCALABLE, PERSONALIZED, AND ENGAGING DIGITAL THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION THAT LEVERAGES THE POWER OF AI, BIOFEEDBACK, AND PASSIVE SENSING TO INCREASE ACCESS TO CARE AND IMPROVE MENTAL HEALTH FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH DEPRESSION AND ANXIETY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPING CUSTOMIZABLE, FEASIBLE, AND EFFICIENT INFANT-TAILORED DIET ASSESSMENT METHODS - PROJECT SUMMARY CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD) IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH, AND SUBOPTIMAL CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH (CVH) IN CHILDHOOD IS ASSOCIATED WITH PREMATURE CVD IN ADULTHOOD. MOST INFANTS ARE BORN WITHOUT RISK FACTORS FOR CVD, AND THE GOAL OF PRIMORDIAL PREVENTION IS TO MAINTAIN AN IDEAL CVH. POOR DIET QUALITY IS A MAJOR, MODIFIABLE RISK FACTOR FOR CVD, YET MOST PEOPLE IN THE U.S., INCLUDING INFANTS, FAIL TO MEET NATIONAL DIETARY GUIDELINES. A MAJOR BARRIER TO DESIGNING HIGH-QUALITY CLINICAL TRIALS TO EXAMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF EARLY LIFE INTERVENTIONS ON DIET QUALITY IS THE LACK OF VALIDATED, FEASIBLE, AND COST-EFFECTIVE DIET ASSESSMENT METHODS FOR INFANTS. THIS R34 PROPOSAL WILL ADDRESS THIS GAP BY PILOTING AND VALIDATING THREE NOVEL INFANT-TAILORED DIETARY ASSESSMENT METHODS TO INFORM A FUTURE CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGNED TO IMPROVE DIET QUALITY AND OTHER COMPONENTS OF CVH DURING THE FIRST YEAR OF LIFE. THIS PILOT STUDY WILL ENROLL A TOTAL OF 120 PARENT-INFANT DYADS PARTICIPATING IN THE EARLY INTERVENTION TO PROMOTE CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH OF MOTHERS AND CHILDREN (ENRICH; NCT06272045) TRIAL TO EXAMINE THE FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, EFFICIENCY, AND ACCURACY OF THREE INFANT-TAILORED DIETARY ASSESSMENT METHODS VS. THE EXISTING GOLD STANDARD 24-HOUR DIETARY RECALL METHOD. THE AIMS ARE TO 1) ASSESS THE CRITERION VALIDITY OF THE MEDITERRANEAN EATING PATTERN FOR AMERICANS (MEPA-CHILD) SCREENER ADAPTED FOR INFANTS AT AGE 12 MONTHS; 2) ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF TWO INFANT-TAILORED ADAPTATIONS TO THE EXISTING 24-HOUR DIETARY RECALL METHOD TO CAPTURE CONTEXTUAL FACTORS AND IMPROVE EFFICIENCY AT INFANT AGES 3, 6, 9, AND 12 MONTH; AND 3) EXAMINE THE AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE EXISTING 24-HOUR RECALL METHOD AND THE TWO INFANT-TAILORED ADAPTATIONS TO THE EXISTING 24-HOUR DIETARY RECALL METHOD TO CAPTURE CONTEXTUAL FACTORS AND IMPROVED EFFICIENCY AT INFANT AGES 3, 6, 9, AND 12 MONTHS. THIS RESEARCH IS EXPECTED TO YIELD VALIDATED AND FEASIBLE INFANT-TAILORED DIET ASSESSMENT TOOLS THAT CAN BE USED IN CLINICAL TRIALS, PUBLIC HEALTH SURVEILLANCE, AND CLINICAL PRACTICE. ULTIMATELY, THIS RESEARCH WILL INFORM CLINICAL TRIALS TO EXAMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERVENTIONS TO PROMOTE OPTIMAL DIET QUALITY AND CVH IN EARLY LIFE, WHICH WILL INFORM EVIDENCE-BASED GUIDELINES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PILOT TRIAL OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY PARTNERSHIPS FOR WOMEN IN MIDLIFE WITH ELEVATED RISK FOR CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE - ABSTRACT DURING MIDLIFE (AGES 40-65), WOMEN EXPERIENCE CHANGES THAT ESCALATE THEIR RISK FOR CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD). REGULAR PHYSICAL ACTIVITY (PA) PROTECTS WOMEN AGAINST CVD RISK, PARTICULARLY AMONG THOSE WITH RISK FACTORS SUCH AS HYPERTENSION AND OBESITY. YET, DESPITE THE WIDE RANGE OF BEHAVIORAL PA PROMOTION PROGRAMS DESIGNED FOR THIS POPULATION, WOMEN SHOW INSUFFICIENT PA DURING MIDLIFE. A KEY BARRIER IS LACK OF ADEQUATE SOCIAL SUPPORT FOR PA, WHICH IS CRUCIAL TO WOMEN’S SUCCESSFUL ADOPTION AND MAINTENANCE OF PA. FORMING PA PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS (I.E., WOMEN WITH NO PRE-EXISTING RELATIONSHIP TO ONE ANOTHER) IS A PROMISING APPROACH TO MEET THIS NEED. OUR TEAM’S PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THE FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND POTENTIAL IMPACT OF A PARTNER-BASED APPROACH TO PROMOTE PA AMONG WOMEN IN MIDLIFE WITH ELEVATED CVD RISK. CRITICALLY, HOWEVER, SEVERAL KEY FEATURES OF THIS APPROACH REQUIRE ADDITIONAL TESTING: (1) EFFECTIVE PROCEDURES FOR RECRUITING, RANDOMIZING, AND RETAINING WOMEN IN A PA PROMOTION TRIAL THAT INCLUDES BOTH INDIVIDUAL PA COACHING AND PA COACHING+PARTNER ARMS, (2) EFFICIENT AND SCALABLE PROCEDURES FOR PAIRING PA PARTNERS WHO ARE MATCHED ON SPECIFIC CHARACTERISTICS, AND (3) AN ACCEPTABLE SOLUTION TO THE CHALLENGE OF WITHDRAWAL OR DISENGAGEMENT ON THE PART OF ONE PARTNER. REFINING AND FINALIZING THESE ELEMENTS ARE ESSENTIAL TO RIGOROUSLY TESTING THE EFFICACY AND MECHANISMS OF PARTNER-BASED PA INTERVENTION FOR WOMEN IN MIDLIFE WITH ELEVATED CVD RISK. TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS, WE WILL CONDUCT A PILOT TRIAL THAT USES INTENSIVE AMBULATORY ASSESSMENT THROUGHOUT A 12-WEEK PA SKILLS COACHING PROGRAM. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE N=160 INSUFFICIENTLY ACTIVE WOMEN AGES 40-65 WITH >1 CVD RISK FACTORS WHO COMPLETE BRIEF DAILY ASSESSMENTS; THIS APPROACH ALLOWS US TO TRACK PA PROGRESS, PARTNER COMMUNICATION, AND POTENTIAL MECHANISMS OF ACTION AS THEY UNFOLD IN DAILY LIFE. AT THE START OF TREATMENT, PARTICIPANTS WILL BE RANDOMIZED WITH 3:1 ALLOCATION TO RECEIVE PA COACHING+PARTNER (I.E., ANOTHER WOMAN WHO ENROLLS AT THE SAME TIME; N=120, EXPERIMENTAL) OR INDIVIDUAL PA COACHING (N=40, CONTROL) AND COMPLETE 12 WEEKS OF INTERVENTION. AT MID-TREATMENT (6 WEEKS), THOSE IN THE COACHING+PARTNER CONDITION WHOSE PARTNERS WITHDRAW OR SHOW POOR ENGAGEMENT WILL BE RE-RANDOMIZED TO (A) INDIVIDUAL COACHING, (B) COACHING+NEW PARTNER, OR (C) SELF-SELECTION FROM THESE OPTIONS, FOR THE SECOND HALF OF TREATMENT. THIS WILL ENABLE US TO EXPERIMENTALLY TEST THE BEST PATH FOR RETAINING, ENGAGING, AND PROMOTING PA WITH WOMEN WHO LOSE PARTNERS DURING THE INTERVENTION. WE WILL ACHIEVE THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: TO CONFIRM THE FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND INTEGRITY OF A RANDOMIZED TRIAL PROTOCOL INVOLVING INDIVIDUAL VERSUS PARTNER-BASED PA COACHING (AIM 1), TO DEFINE OPTIMAL PROCEDURES FOR PARTNER MATCHING AND RE-FORMATION (AIM 2), AND TO FINALIZE THE PROTOCOL FOR A FUTURE TRIAL (AIM 3). ACHIEVING THESE AIMS WILL INFORM THE FINAL PROTOCOL FOR A RIGOROUS, FULLY POWERED CLINICAL TRIAL TESTING THE EFFICACY, MECHANISMS, AND MODERATORS OF PA PARTNERSHIPS FOR WOMEN IN MIDLIFE WITH ELEVATED RISK FOR CVD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SPIRIT: A CULTURALLY GROUNDED SUPPORTIVE CARE INTERVENTION FOR CHICKASAW NATION PATIENTS WITH CANCER - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO ENHANCE CANCER CARE DELIVERY AND OUTCOMES FOR FIRST AMERICANS. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS APPLICATION IS TO DEVELOP AND PILOT A SUPPORTIVE CARE INTERVENTION CALLED SPIRIT (SUPPORTIVE PALLIATIVE INTERVENTION RESPECTING INDIGENOUS TRADITIONS) THAT ADDRESSES THE CULTURALLY INFORMED CARE NEEDS AND CONCERNS OF FIRST AMERICAN PATIENTS WITH CANCER. SPIRIT IS A COLLABORATION BETWEEN THE CHICKASAW NATION AND THE STEPHENSON CANCER CENTER (SCC), AN NCI-DESIGNATED CANCER CENTER, AT THE UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA (OU) HEALTH. OUR TEAM HAS A LONG-STANDING AND SUCCESSFUL HISTORY OF COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH TO ENHANCE CARE FOR FIRST AMERICANS WITH CANCER, INCLUDING WITH THE CHICKASAW NATION DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (CNDH), WHICH IS ONE OF THE LARGEST TRIBALLY OPERATED HEALTH SYSTEMS IN THE US. CNDH IS A PREDOMINATELY RURAL TRIBAL HEALTHCARE SYSTEM THAT, LIKE MANY TRIBAL HEALTH SYSTEMS, REFERS PATIENTS WITH CANCER TO SPECIALISTS LOCATED IN URBAN AREAS. THESE OUTSIDE SPECIALISTS MAY NOT UNDERSTAND THE NUANCES OF THE CNDH REFERRAL PROCESSES NOR THESE PATIENTS’ INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE AND VALUES. THUS, INTERVENTIONS TO STREAMLINE CANCER CARE COORDINATION ACROSS CNDH AND THE SCC ARE URGENTLY NEEDED, PARTICULARLY WITH REGARDS TO THE UNIQUE SUPPORTIVE CARE NEEDS OF FIRST AMERICANS. SPIRIT BUILDS ON A STRONG TRIBAL-ACADEMIC PARTNERSHIP, WHICH FOSTERS THE CO-DEVELOPMENT OF A CULTURALLY INFORMED SUPPORTIVE CARE INTERVENTION FOR FIRST AMERICAN PATIENTS WITH CANCER. THE INTERVENTION INTEGRATES ESTABLISHED EVIDENCE FROM THE SUPPORTIVE AND PALLIATIVE CARE LITERATURE, FACILITATED BY OUR TEAM’S EXPERTS IN PALLIATIVE CARE AND SUPPORTIVE ONCOLOGY, TO ENSURE BOTH CLINICAL RIGOR AND CULTURAL RESPONSIVENESS. IMPORTANTLY, A COMMUNITY ADVISORY BOARD OF PATIENTS WITH CANCER AND STAFF FROM CNDH AND SCC WILL GUIDE SPIRIT’S REFINEMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION IN COLLABORATION WITH THE TRIBAL HEALTH SYSTEM. WITH INPUT FROM THE COMMUNITY ADVISORY BOARD AND KEY INFORMANTS, THE INTERVENTION WILL ENTAIL PATIENT NAVIGATION, SYMPTOM MONITORING, COLLABORATIVE CARE, AND PERSONALIZED PALLIATIVE CARE. WE WILL CONDUCT AN OPEN PILOT (N=20) TO DEMONSTRATE THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF DELIVERING THE SPIRIT INTERVENTION FOR FIRST AMERICAN PATIENTS WITH CANCER. OUR HYPOTHESIS IS THAT BY DEVELOPING A CULTURALLY INFORMED SUPPORTIVE CARE INTERVENTION, WE CAN FEASIBLY DELIVER AN INTERVENTION THAT ADDRESSES THE UNIQUE NEEDS OF FIRST AMERICAN PATIENTS WITH CANCER. WE AIM TO 1) DEVELOP THE SPIRIT INTERVENTION TO PROVIDE PATIENT NAVIGATION, FOSTER PROACTIVE SYMPTOM MONITORING, ENSURE COLLABORATIVE CARE, AND PERSONALIZE PALLIATIVE CARE FOR FIRST AMERICAN PATIENTS WITH CANCER, 2) ASSESS FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF DELIVERING SPIRIT FOR FIRST AMERICAN PATIENTS WITH CANCER (N=20), AND 3) IDENTIFY FACILITATORS AND BARRIERS TO IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SPIRIT INTERVENTION.

description: FUNCTIONAL CONNECTOMICS VIA HIGH-SPEED TWO-PHOTON VOLTAGE IMAGING AND OPTOGENETICS - PROJECT SUMMARY THE GOAL OF THIS TARGETED PLANNING PROJECT IS TO ESTABLISH A NEW PARADIGM FOR “FUNCTIONAL CONNECTOMICS.” EXISTING CONNECTOMICS APPROACHES OPERATE ONLY ON POST-MORTEM TISSUE, HAVE LOW THROUGHPUT, OR SPARSELY SAMPLE A LOCAL REGION’S CONNECTOME, AND NONE CAN MEASURE THE PHYSIOLOGICAL STRENGTH OF CONNECTIONS OR TRACK HOW THEY CHANGE IN THE LIVING BRAIN. HERE WE WILL COMBINE ULTRA-FAST TWO-PHOTON VOLTAGE IMAGING (2P-FACED) WITH TWOPHOTON OPTOGENETIC STIMULATION TO ACHIEVE HIGH-THROUGHPUT MEASUREMENT AND TRACKING OF A LOCAL FUNCTIONAL CONNECTOME IN THE RODENT BRAIN. OWING TO THE HIGH SPEED AND SCALE OF 2P-FACED PAIRED WITH FAST SINGLE-CELL OPTOGENETIC STIMULATION, WE WILL BUILD A SYSTEM THAT CAN MEASURE, MONITOR, AND TRACK SYNAPTIC WEIGHTS ACROSS TENS OF THOUSANDS OF CANDIDATE SYNAPTIC CONNECTIONS IN AWAKE ANIMALS, OVER DAYS TO WEEKS TO MONTHS. UNIQUELY, THE SYSTEM WILL READ OUT BOTH SUBTHRESHOLD SYNAPTIC POTENTIALS AND SUPRATHRESHOLD SPIKES, ENABLING FOR THE FIRST TIME THE DIRECT MEASUREMENT OF BOTH MONOSYNAPTIC CONNECTIVITY AND ITS FUNCTIONAL IMPACT ON SPIKING IN THE SAME NEURONS IN VIVO. RATHER THAN TARGETING A SINGLE CIRCUIT OR BEHAVIOR, THE PLATFORM IS DESIGNED AS A GENERAL-PURPOSE SYSTEM FOR MEASURING AND DYNAMICALLY TRACKING FUNCTIONAL CONNECTOMES THROUGHOUT THE BRAIN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A MULTISCALE AND MULTISPECIES APPROACH FOR IDENTIFYING SHARED MECHANISMS OF LIMB AND FIN REGENERATION - PROJECT SUMMARY MOLECULAR AND CELLULAR PROGRAMS THAT CAN TRIGGER A SUCCESSFUL LIMB REGENERATIVE RESPONSE IN MAMMALS REMAIN ELUSIVE, NEGATIVELY IMPACTING THE LIVES OF NEARLY 2.1 MILLION PEOPLE WHO LIVE WITH LIMB LOSS IN THE UNITED STATES. TO MEET THIS CHALLENGE, MY LAB STUDIES HIGHLY REGENERATIVE SALAMANDER AND FISH SPECIES THAT CAN FULLY REGROW LIMBS AND FINS, RESPECTIVELY. IN HIGHLY REGENERATIVE SPECIES, THE PIVOTAL EVENTS GUIDING SUCCESSFUL REGENERATION INCLUDE THE RECRUITMENT OF PROGENITOR CELLS AND SCAR TISSUE RESOLUTION. FOR THE NEXT FIVE YEARS, WE AIM TO TACKLE FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS, SUCH AS: 1) WHAT ARE THE CONSERVED INSTRUCTIVE SIGNALS THAT TRIGGER REGENERATION IN HIGHLY REGENERATIVE SPECIES, 2) HOW IS SCAR-FREE TISSUE REGENERATION ACHIEVED? OUR STRATEGY LEVERAGES A MULTISCALE COMPARATIVE APPROACH TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS CANDIDATE COMPONENTS OF A CORE CELLULAR AND GENETIC TOOLKIT OF LIMB AND FIN REGENERATION. OUR APPROACH USES OUR EXISTING DATA ON LIZARD LIMB AS A NON- REGENERATIVE COMPARATIVE BENCHMARK, TOGETHER WITH THE HIGHLY REGENERATIVE MEXICAN SALAMANDER KNOWN AS AXOLOTL AND TWO FISH SPECIES: THE SENEGAL BICHIR (POLYPTERUS SENEGALUS) AND THE AFRICAN LUNGFISH (PROTOPTERUS ANNECTENS). THESE FISH SPECIES OFFER KEY ADVANTAGES RELATIVE TO TRADITIONAL TELEOST MODELS SUCH AS THE ZEBRAFISH: 1) THEY CAN READILY REGENERATE ENTIRE FINS AS ADULTS, NOT ONLY THE DERMAL FIN RAYS, AND 2) THEY SHARE 1:1 GENE ORTHOLOGY WITH LIMBED VERTEBRATES, FACILITATING COMPARATIVE STUDIES OF GENE FUNCTION. OUR PREVIOUS WORK HAS SHOWN THAT POLYPTERUS AND LUNGFISH ACTIVATE A GENETIC PROGRAM OF REGENERATION SIMILAR TO AXOLOTLS. OUR PRELIMINARY FINDINGS USING SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS REVEAL COMMON MICRO-CONSERVED DOMAINS OF GENE EXPRESSION DURING LIMB AND FIN REGENERATION. FINALLY, OUR COMPARATIVE TRANSCRIPTOMICS APPROACH IDENTIFIED THE MTOR PATHWAY AS A SHARED SIGNAL, POTENTIALLY INVOLVED IN PREVENTING SCAR-TISSUE FORMATION. HERE WE PROPOSE TO COMBINE MULTIOMICS AND COMPUTATIONAL APPROACHES TO IDENTIFY CANDIDATE GENES COMMONLY DEPLOYED DURING LIMB AND FIN REGENERATION FOR FUNCTIONAL STUDIES. AS A CASE STUDY, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH THE MTOR PATHWAY MODULATES CELLULAR EVENTS LEADING TO SCAR-FREE REGENERATION. THE SHARED MECHANISMS DEPLOYED BY THOSE HIGHLY REGENERATIVE SPECIES DURING LIMB AND FIN REGENERATION MAY UNCOVER INNOVATIVE STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE LIMB REGENERATION AND ATTENUATION OF FIBROSIS IN HUMANS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTERSECTION OF GLYCOSYLATION AND METABOLISM DURING TISSUE DEVELOPMENT - PROTEIN AND LIPID GLYCOSYLATION IS ONE OF THE MOST COMPLEX POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATIONS IN BIOLOGY, IMPACTING COUNTLESS PROCESSES ACROSS ALL KINGDOMS OF LIFE. PROTEIN-BOUND GLYCANS MEDIATE POLYPEPTIDE FOLDING, TRAFFICKING, LOCALIZATION, PROCESSING, STABILITY, ENZYMATIC ACTIVITY, AND CAN PROMOTE OR INHIBIT INTERACTIONS AMONG PROTEIN PARTNERS. GLYCOSYLATION IS A NON-TEMPLATE DRIVEN PROCESS, WHERE THE TYPE AND AMOUNT OF GLYCANS SYNTHESIZED IS DETERMINED BY AVAILABILITY OF SUGAR PRECURSORS AND EXPRESSION OF SPECIFIC BIOSYNTHETIC ENZYMES. CELLULAR GLUCOSE LEVELS AND FLUX WITHIN SUGAR PHOSPHATE METABOLIC PATHWAYS DICTATE ABUNDANCE OF THE NUCLEOTIDE-SUGAR PRECURSORS. MULTIPLE GLYCOSYLATION ENZYMES UTILIZE THE SAME METABOLIC PRECURSORS. THUS, BALANCING GLYCAN BIOSYNTHESIS AND SUGAR METABOLISM IS CRITICAL FOR NORMAL TISSUE DEVELOPMENT. THE COMPLETE REPERTOIRE OF MECHANISMS REGULATING THIS COORDINATION REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD, BUT THE NEED FOR PROPER GLYCOSYLATION IS EVIDENCED BY THE ~200 DIFFERENT INHERITED HUMAN DISORDERS CAUSED BY A PRIMARY DEFECT IN ONE OR MORE GLYCOSYLATION PATHWAYS. THESE RARE INHERITED GENETIC DISEASES, TERMED THE CONGENITAL DISORDERS OF GLYCOSYLATION (CDG), HAVE A DIVERSE BIOCHEMICAL AND GENETIC ETIOLOGY. WHILE THE NUMBER OF NEWLY IDENTIFIED CDG CONTINUES TO EXPAND, OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THEIR PATHOGENESIS AND THE AVAILABILITY OF APPROVED TREATMENTS REMAIN VERY LIMITED. THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM LEVERAGES A POWERFUL SUITE OF NOVEL TOOLS IN ZEBRAFISH TO EXPLORE HOW METABOLIC AND GLYCOSYLATION PATHWAYS CONVERGE AND COOPERATE TO CONTROL TISSUE DEVELOPMENT, AND HOW IMPAIRING THAT COORDINATION CAUSES DISEASE. USING ZEBRAFISH MODELS OF MULTIPLE CDG, INCLUDING THE MOST COMMON FORM, PMM2-CDG, OUR STUDIES COMBINE SYSTEMS-BASED ANALYSES WITH BIOCHEMICAL AND MOLECULAR APPROACHES TO UNRAVEL CDG PATHOGENESIS AT A CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR LEVEL. OUR CURRENT RESEARCH IS FOCUSED IN THREE GENERAL AREAS: 1) DEFINING HOW ALTERATIONS IN THE LEVEL OF NUCLEOTIDE SUGAR PRECURSORS BROADLY IMPACT GLYCOSYLATION – STUDIES THAT AIM TO UNDERSTAND HOW UNDERLYING DEFECTS IN PMM2 IMPACT BOTH N- AND O-LINKED GLYCANS TO DRIVE DISEASE PATHOLOGY; 2) DELINEATE HOW DEFECTS IN GLYCOSYLATION OF CADHERINS (AND THE PROTEASES THAT PROCESS THEM) IMPAIR THEIR FUNCTION TO DISRUPT TISSUE DEVELOPMENT; 3) UNCOVER HOW O-GLCNACYLATION OF KEY PROTEINS CONTRIBUTES TO DISEASE IN MULTIPLE CDG - STUDIES THAT ARE BASED ON OUR DISCOVERY THAT INCREASED O- GLCNACYLATION IN PMM2-CDG LEADS TO MODIFICATION OF KEY RATE-LIMITING ENZYMES IN THE EARLY N-GLYCOSYLATION PATHWAY. BY COMPARING MULTIPLE CDG IN A SINGLE MODEL SYSTEM, WE HOPE TO IDENTIFY THE COMMON METABOLIC- AND GLYCOSYLATION-MEDIATED MECHANISMS DRIVING DISEASE IN AFFECTED TISSUES, AND USE THIS INFORMATION TO UNCOVER AND TEST NEW THERAPIES.

description: NEXT-GENERATION SINGLE-CELL MULTIOMIC METHODS FOR QUANTIFYING CELLULAR IDENTITY - PROJECT SUMMARY IN MULTICELLULAR ORGANISMS, THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN EPIGENETIC AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC PROCESSES CREATES A COMPLEX REGULATORY NETWORK CRUCIAL FOR DETERMINING CELLULAR FATE. DISRUPTIONS TO THESE NETWORKS ARE OFTEN LINKED TO VARIOUS DISEASES, INCLUDING AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES, NEURODEGENERATIVE CONDITIONS, AND CANCERS. DESPITE ADVANCEMENTS IN UNDERSTANDING THESE INTERACTIONS, IDENTIFYING ABNORMAL INTERACTION PATTERNS SPECIFIC TO DISEASE-RELATED CELL SUBPOPULATIONS REMAINS A SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGE. THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS TO ADDRESS THIS GAP BY LEVERAGING NOVEL SINGLE-CELL BARCODING TECHNOLOGIES. THESE TECHNOLOGIES ENABLE MAPPING CELL-TYPE-SPECIFIC REGULATORY PROCESSES, INCLUDING DNA METHYLATION, HISTONE MODIFICATION, AND ALTERNATIVE RNA SPLICING. CURRENT TECHNOLOGIES HAVE LIMITATIONS, PRIMARILY IN SINGLE-OMIC MEASUREMENTS, FAILING TO ADEQUATELY CAPTURE COMPLEX INTERACTIONS WITHIN REGULATORY NETWORKS. TO OVERCOME THESE LIMITATIONS, WE PROPOSE A COMPREHENSIVE SUITE OF MULTI-OMIC SINGLE-CELL METHODS THAT CAN SIMULTANEOUSLY PROFILE DIVERSE REGULATORY PROCESSES AND INTEGRATE DATA RELATED TO CHROMATIN STATES AND TRANSCRIPT ISOFORM EXPRESSION. RECENT ADVANCEMENTS, SUCH AS PARTICLE- TEMPLATED INSTANT PARTITIONING (PIP), PROMISE TO OVERCOME TRADITIONAL BARCODING LIMITATIONS. PIP ENHANCES REPRODUCIBILITY AND EFFICIENCY IN MULTI-OMIC APPLICATIONS, LEADING US TO OUR PRELIMINARY RESULTS, WHICH INDICATE A NEW ERA IN SINGLE-CELL ANALYSIS WITH POTENTIAL REVOLUTIONARY IMPACTS ON THE STUDY OF CELLULAR BEHAVIOR AND DISEASE PROGRESSION. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO ESTABLISH ADVANCED SINGLE-CELL EPIGENETIC AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS TECHNOLOGIES THAT ENHANCE SCALABILITY, COST-EFFECTIVENESS, AND PORTABILITY. USING THE PIP BARCODING SYSTEM, WE INTEND TO IMPROVE TRANSCRIPT PROFILING AND QUANTIFICATION THROUGH SIMULTANEOUS SHORT- AND LONG-READ SEQUENCING METHODS. OUR RESEARCH WILL UTILIZE A PROBABILISTIC MODEL TO QUANTIFY TRANSCRIPTS FROM DIVERSE SEQUENCING PLATFORMS, ADDRESSING CURRENT ANALYTICAL CHALLENGES. THIS APPROACH IS DESIGNED TO YIELD DETAILED INSIGHTS INTO SPLICING EVENTS AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL DIVERSITY ACROSS VARIOUS CELL TYPES. MOREOVER, OUR INVESTIGATION AIMS TO UTILIZE PIPS FOR SINGLE-CELL MULTIOMICS TO MEASURE HISTONE MODIFICATIONS AND DNA METHYLATION. WE INCLUDE A PROOF-OF-CONCEPT STUDY THAT CAN PROFILE TRANSPOSASE-ACCESSIBLE CHROMATIN REGIONS, ENHANCING EPIGENETIC ASSAYS WITH OPTIMIZED TECHNIQUES. WE WILL TACKLE THE CHALLENGES OF QUANTIFYING MULTIOMICS DATA USING BAYESIAN METHODS, INCREASING STATISTICAL POWER AND ALLOWING US TO CAPTURE CHROMATIN STATES AT THE SINGLE-CELL LEVEL. THIS WILL PROVIDE INSIGHTS INTO EPIGENOMIC FEATURES ACROSS MILLIONS OF CELLS. THE STUDY WILL IDENTIFY REGULATORY ELEMENTS BY EXAMINING HISTONE AND DNA MODIFICATIONS ALONGSIDE RNA SPLICING. GIVEN THE BROAD IMPLICATIONS OF OUR RESEARCH, THIS WORK CAN POTENTIALLY AFFECT THE UNDERSTANDING AND TREATMENT OF AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES, NEURODEGENERATIVE CONDITIONS, AND CANCERS. THE NIH MAXIMIZING INVESTIGATORS' RESEARCH AWARD WILL SUPPORT OUR EFFORTS TO ADVANCE NOVEL MULTIOMICS TECHNIQUES RAPIDLY AND FACILITATE THE IDENTIFICATION OF NEW THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR VARIOUS DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EPITHELIAL DYNAMICS DURING DEVELOPMENTAL PROCESSES - PROJECT SUMMARY LONG TERM MAINTENANCE OF EPITHELIAL TISSUES REQUIRES CONSTANT REMODELING. AS EPITHELIA GROW THE PROCESS OF RADIAL CELL INTERCALATION CAN BE AN IMPORTANT MECHANISM FOR CELL ADDITION. HOWEVER, CONTINUED GROWTH AND CELL ADDITION (TYPICALLY VIA PROLIFERATION) CAN ALSO LEAD TO CELL CROWDING WHICH CAN DRIVE CELL EXTRUSION AS A MECHANISM TO DECREASE APICAL TISSUE AREA. IN ADDITION TO CELL EXTRUSION, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED MACROPINOCYTOSIS AS A MECHANISM FOR ALTERING APICAL SURFACE AREA IN RESPONSE TO CROWDING. MACROPINOCYTOSIS IS AN ENDOCYTIC PROCESS THAT RESULTS IN LARGE SCALE ENGULFMENT OF EXTRACELLULAR MATERIAL BUT IMPORTANTLY ALSO LEADS TO LARGE SCALE ENGULFMENT OF APICAL MEMBRANE WHICH DRAMATICALLY DECREASES APICAL SURFACE AREA. IN THIS PROPOSAL WE AIM TO UNDERSTAND THE MOLECULAR REGULATORS AND THE PHYSICAL PARAMETERS THAT MODULATE CELL INTERCALATION, CELL EXTRUSION AND MACROPINOCYTOSIS. THEME 1. PHYSICAL AND MOLECULAR REGULATION OF RADIAL INTERCALATION. MULTI-CILIATED CELL (MCC) AND IONOCYTE (IC) RADIAL INTERCALATION INTO THE SKIN OF XENOPUS EMBRYOS REPRESENTS AN EXPERIMENTALLY PLIABLE SYSTEM WHICH ALLOWS US TO ADDRESS BOTH THE PHYSICAL DEMANDS OF INTERCALATION AND THE BROADER REMODELING OF THE EPITHELIUM IN RESPONSE TO THAT INTERCALATION. WE AIM TO UNDERSTAND BOTH THE PENETRATIVE CAPACITY OF INTERCALATING CELLS AS WELL AS THE RESTRICTIVE CAPACITY OF THE EPITHELIUM AND HAVE IDENTIFIED NOVEL REGULATORS OF JUNCTIONAL INTEGRITY THAT IMPINGE ON THIS PROCESS. THEME 2. REGULATION OF BIDIRECTIONAL CELL EXTRUSION. WE HAVE RECENTLY PUBLISHED THAT ALL MCCS UNDERGO BI- DIRECTIONAL CELL EXTRUSION. THE FIRST WAVE OF BASAL CELL EXTRUSION IS REGULATED VIA NOTCH SIGNALING, AND WE WILL ADDRESS THE TEMPORAL CONTROL OF THIS REGULATION WHICH WE HYPOTHESIZE STEMS FROM A TRANSCRIPTIONAL SHIFT IN RECEPTOR SUBTYPE. ADDITIONALLY, CELLS THAT EVADE NOTCH SIGNALING ARE TARGETED FOR APICAL CELL EXTRUSION VIA A MECHANOSENSORY MECHANISM THAT WE HYPOTHESIZE IS LINKED TO CELL CROWDING AND THE NEED TO DECREASE APICAL TISSUE AREA. WE WILL ADDRESS THE CONSEQUENCE OF MODULATING CELL NUMBER / TYPE ON THE TIMING OF APICAL EXTRUSION. USING A LONG-TERM LIGHT-SHEET IMAGING PARADIGM WE HAVE IDENTIFIED NUMEROUS MACROPINOCYTOTIC EVENTS THAT INCREASE AS DEVELOPMENT PROGRESSES. IMPORTANTLY, THESE EVENTS RESULT IN A SIGNIFICANT LOSS OF APICAL SURFACE AREA AND WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SIMILAR TO APICAL CELL EXTRUSION, THESE EVENTS COUNTER CELL CROWDING BY DECREASING APICAL TISSUE AREA, BUT IN A MORE SUBTLE AND LESS PERMANENT MANNER. WE WILL ADDRESS BOTH THE REGULATION OF THESE EVENTS AND THE FUNCTIONAL CONSEQUENCE OF INHIBITING THEM, WHICH WE HYPOTHESIZE WILL ALTER CELL CROWDING THEREBY AFFECTING CELL EXTRUSION. WHILE THESE THEMES ADDRESS DISTINCT BIOLOGICAL QUESTIONS THERE IS CONSIDERABLE OVERLAP IN THE REAGENTS, EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN AND IMAGING PARADIGMS. ADDITIONALLY, IN EACH PROJECT WE WILL ADDRESS BOTH THE MOLECULAR AND PHYSICAL MECHANISM THAT REGULATE THESE PROCESSES AND WE ARE EXCITED BY HOW OUR PROJECTS SYNERGIZE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADVANCING FUNCTIONALITY AND DELIVERY OF MINIATURE CRISPR SYSTEMS THROUGH DIRECTED EVOLUTION - PROJECT SUMMARY CRISPR TECHNOLOGY HAS REVOLUTIONIZED GENOME EDITING, ENABLING PRECISE AND PROGRAMMED MODIFICATIONS PREVIOUSLY DEEMED UNATTAINABLE. HOWEVER, THE LARGE SIZE OF COMMONLY USED CRISPR NUCLEASES PRESENTS SIGNIFICANT DELIVERY CHALLENGES, PARTICULARLY FOR IN VIVO APPLICATIONS. MINIATURE CRISPR SYSTEMS, SUCH AS THE CAS9 ANCESTOR ISCB, OFFER A PROMISING ALTERNATIVE. DESPITE THEIR SIZE ADVANTAGE, MINIATURE CRISPR SYSTEMS FACE LIMITATIONS, INCLUDING REDUCED DNA BINDING AFFINITY, LOWER CATALYTIC EFFICIENCY, GREATER SEQUENCE CONSTRAINTS FOR TARGET RECOGNITION, AND, IN SOME CASES, COMPROMISED SPECIFICITY. TO FULLY UNLOCK THEIR GENOME-EDITING POTENTIAL, WE PROPOSE TO ADVANCE THE TECHNOLOGICAL CAPACITY OF MINIATURE CRISPR SYSTEMS USING DIRECTED EVOLUTION, MACHINE LEARNING-DRIVEN PROTEIN ENGINEERING, AND NOVEL DELIVERY PLATFORMS. IN PROJECT 1, WE WILL COMBINE DIRECTED EVOLUTION AND MACHINE LEARNING TO REPROGRAM THE RECOGNITION OF THE TARGET-ADJACENT MOTIF BY ISCB, AIMING TO IMPROVE ITS EFFICIENCY AND PRECISION IN TARGET SEARCH AND CLEAVAGE. IN PROJECT 2, WE WILL DEVELOP AND OPTIMIZE ISCB-DERIVED BASE AND PRIME EDITORS TO ENABLE PRECISE SEQUENCE MODIFICATIONS BEYOND STANDARD INSERTIONS AND DELETIONS. IN PROJECT 3, WE WILL ENGINEER ADENO-ASSOCIATED VIRUSES AND VIRUS-LIKE PARTICLES FOR ISCB DELIVERY, WITH A FOCUS ON NEURON, LIVER, AND IMMUNE CELLS. COLLECTIVELY, THESE EFFORTS WILL ADVANCE MINIATURE CRISPR SYSTEMS AS VERSATILE GENOME-ENGINEERING TOOLS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EVOLUTION OF STRESS RESPONSE GENE REGULATORY NETWORK IN A COMMENSAL AND OPPORTUNISTIC YEAST PATHOGEN - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT GENE REGULATORY EVOLUTION IS RAMPANT AND WIDELY RECOGNIZED AS A MAJOR DRIVER FOR PHENOTYPIC DIVERGENCE. YET OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW THE SIGNALING AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL CIRCUITS EVOLVE AT A GENETIC AND MOLECULAR LEVEL IS STILL VERY LIMITED. EXISTING KNOWLEDGE IS LARGELY DERIVED FROM STUDIES OF DEVELOPMENTAL NETWORKS AND FOCUSED ON THE CIS-REGULATORY ELEMENTS, PRECLUDING A GENERAL UNDERSTANDING. STRESS RESPONSE IS CRUCIAL FOR SURVIVAL AND NEEDS TO EVOLVE AS ORGANISMS ADAPT TO A NEW ENVIRONMENT. STUDYING THE EVOLUTION OF STRESS RESPONSES THUS SERVES AS A PROMISING MODEL TO ACHIEVE THE ABOVE GOAL. MY LAB USES A GROUP OF GENETICALLY RELATED AND YET ECOLOGICALLY DIVERSE YEASTS IN THE SACCHAROMYCOTINA SUBPHYLUM AS A MODEL CLADE, WHICH INCLUDES MULTIPLE, INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED HUMAN OPPORTUNISTIC PATHOGENS. STRESS RESPONSE EVOLUTION IS EXPECTED TO BE A KEY COMPONENT IN HOST ADAPTATION, AND THUS DISSECTING ITS EVOLUTION BETWEEN RELATED PATHOGENS AND LOW PATHOGENIC SPECIES CAN OFFER CRITICAL INSIGHT INTO HOW NOVEL PATHOGENS EVOLVED. OUR LONG TERM GOAL IS TO BROADEN AND DEEPEN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF GENE REGULATORY EVOLUTION, AND TO IDENTIFY KEY GENETIC CHANGES IN THE STRESS RESPONSE NETWORKS IN PATHOGENIC YEASTS. OUR MIRA FUNDED WORK IN THE PAST FIVE YEARS REVEALED A NOVEL MODE OF TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR (TF) EVOLUTION IN CO-TF DEPENDENCE THROUGH DIVERGENCE IN THE INTRINSICALLY DISORDERED REGIONS (IDRS). WE ALSO DISCOVERED A NOVEL ACQUIRED STRESS RESISTANCE (ASR) TRAIT IN THE PATHOGENIC YEAST C. GLABRATA BUT ABSENT IN THE RELATED S. CEREVISIAE, WHERE PHOSPHATE LIMITATION ENHANCES THE SURVIVAL BY 3-10 FOLD TO A SEVERE H2O2 CHALLENGE. WE ALSO REVEALED REPEATED EXPANSION OF AN ADHESIN FAMILY IN MULTIPLE PATHOGENIC LINEAGES AND OPTIMIZED A FLUORESCENCE DYE BASED SURVIVAL ASSAY FOR DIVERSE YEAST SPECIES THAT IS FAST AND SCALABLE. OUR SPECIFIC GOALS IN THE NEXT FIVE YEARS ARE TO 1) DETERMINE THE MECHANISM AND EVOLUTION OF IDRS AND PIONEER FACTOR ACTIVITIES IN TFS DRIVING GENE REGULATORY EVOLUTION; 2) DISSECT THE SIGNALING AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL CIRCUITS BEHIND THE DIVERGENT ASR IN C. GLABRATA AND S. CEREVISIAE; 3) DETERMINE THE EVOLUTIONARY PATTERN OF ALL ADHESIN FAMILIES (“ADHESINOME”) IN PATHOGENIC YEAST CLADES. INVESTIGATING IDR EVOLUTION AND PIONEER FACTOR ACTIVITIES IN TFS AND DISSECTING THE REWIRING OF ASR SIGNALING NETWORKS ARE CONCEPTUALLY NOVEL. THE PROPOSED WORK IS ALSO INNOVATIVE IN THE WIDE RANGE OF TECHNIQUES USED, INCLUDING SINGLE-CELL FLUORESCENCE REPORTER, IN-VITRO NUCLEOSOMAL DNA BINDING, TRANSPOSON-INSERTION SCREEN, AND CHEMICAL GENETIC PERTURBATION OF SIGNALING PATHWAYS. THIS RESEARCH IS SIGNIFICANT IN THAT IT WILL REVEAL FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES GOVERNING TF EVOLUTION AND GENE REGULATORY NETWORK WHILE PROVIDING NOVEL INSIGHT INTO THE GENETIC ADAPTATION IN PATHOGENIC YEASTS IN THEIR STRESS RESPONSE NETWORK AND ADHESIN GENE REPERTOIRE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS CONTROLLING THE DIAPAUSE-LIKE CELL STATE - PROJECT SUMMARY CELLULAR DORMANCY CAN OCCUR IN DIVERSE PHYSIOLOGICAL AND PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL CONTEXTS AS RESPONSE TO STRESS AND/OR EXTRACELLULAR SIGNALS. WE HAVE PREVIOUSLY CHARACTERIZED A DISTINCT AND REVERSIBLE QUIESCENCE STATE IN SOMATIC CELLS THAT RESEMBLES THE MOLECULAR REPROGRAMMING OF EMBRYONIC DIAPAUSE, A DORMANT STAGE OF SUSPENDED DEVELOPMENT IN SOME MAMMALIAN SPECIES, TRIGGERED BY STRESS AND ASSOCIATED WITH SUPPRESSED MYC ACTIVITY AND OVERALL BIOSYNTHESIS. WE DEMONSTRATE THAT HUMAN CELLS CAN ADOPT THIS DIAPAUSE-LIKE MOLECULAR PROGRAM IN RESPONSE TO CELLULAR DAMAGE AND/OR MICROENVIRONMENTAL CUES. WE AIM TO UNDERSTAND HOW SOMATIC CELLS CO-OPT THIS EVOLUTIONARILY CONSERVED MYC-SUPPRESSED TRANSCRIPTIONAL/METABOLIC ADAPTATION AND HOW THE DIAPAUSE-LIKE CELLS AFFECT NORMAL PHYSIOLOGY, DISEASE, AND RESPONSE TO PHARMACOLOGICAL AGENTS. WE USE OUR DIAPAUSE-LIKE CELL MODELS IN EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES THAT ADDRESS THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS: I) WHICH TRANSCRIPTIONAL MECHANISMS OVERRIDE MYC INACTIVATION AND ACTIVATE THE GENES NECESSARY FOR SURVIVAL OF DIAPAUSE- LIKE CELLS? WE HAVE NOMINATED TWO TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATORS, FOXM1 AND CDK13, AS PUTATIVE CONTROLLERS OF GENE EXPRESSION IN THIS QUIESCENT STATE AND ARE DISSECTING THEIR ROLE IN THIS CONTEXT USING CHEMICAL-GENETIC APPROACHES (E.G. DEGRON TAG GENE KNOCK-IN TECHNIQUES). II) WHAT METABOLIC CHANGES OCCUR IN DIAPAUSE-LIKE CELLS? WE HAVE OBSERVED EXTENSIVE MITOCHONDRIAL REMODELING AND INCREASED RESPIRATORY FUNCTION IN DIAPAUSE-LIKE CELLS AND WILL DISSECT THE MECHANISM/S OF THIS METABOLIC ADAPTATION AND ITS EFFECT ON THE DIAPAUSE-LIKE CELL STATE. III) HOW DIAPAUSE-LIKE CELLS EXIT QUIESCENCE AND REGAIN THEIR PROLIFERATIVE FUNCTION? WE WILL COMBINE PHARMACOLOGICAL AND GENETIC/CHEMICAL-GENETIC TOOLS (E.G. INDUCIBLE LOSS-OF-FUNCTION AND/OR GAIN-OF-FUNCTION) TO DETERMINE WHETHER REACTIVATION OF MYC AND/OR OTHER GENES IS NECESSARY OR/AND SUFFICIENT FOR DIAPAUSE-LIKE CELLS TO EXIT DORMANCY. IV) HOW DIAPAUSE-LIKE REPROGRAMMING CAN AFFECT CELLULAR PLASTICITY? BUILDING ON OUR OBSERVATIONS THAT EXIT FROM THE DIAPAUSE-LIKE STATE CAN LEAD TO SWITCH FROM LUMINAL CELL IDENTITY TOWARDS A MESENCHYMAL PHENOTYPE AND MOLECULAR PROFILE, WE WILL IDENTIFY THE MECHANISMS THAT ENABLE THIS CELLULAR PLASTICITY. COMBINED, THESE APPROACHES WILL ALLOW US TO CHARACTERIZE THE DISTINCT DIAPAUSE-LIKE QUIESCENT CELL STATE AND THE MECHANISMS THAT CONTROL THIS MOLECULAR PROGRAM IN HUMAN CELLS.

description: FUNCTION-SELECTIVE MODULATORS OF MULTIFUNCTIONAL HUB PROTEINS - FUNCTION-SELECTIVE MODULATORS OF MULTIFUNCTIONAL HUB PROTEINS PROTEIN INTERACTION NETWORKS ARE COMPLEX, YET CRITICAL TO UNDERSTAND IF WE AIM TO DISSECT BIOLOGY. FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS AND PROTEOMICS HAVE HELPED TO MAP THE PROTEINS AND INTERACTIONS IN THESE NETWORKS. TO MANIPULATE NETWORKS WITH PRECISION, HOWEVER, WE NEED SYSTEMATIC TOOLS TO SELECTIVELY INHIBIT OR STABILIZE PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS (PPI). PARTICULARLY CHALLENGING IS THE SELECTIVE MANIPULATION OF HUB PROTEINS THAT INTERACT WITH DOZENS TO THOUSANDS OF PARTNERS. OUR LAB DEVELOPS DRUG-LIKE MOLECULES AND PROTEIN ENGINEERING APPROACHES TO PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO HUB-PROTEIN FUNCTION IN HEALTH AND DISEASE. WE PROPOSE TO EXPAND TWO RESEARCH PROGRAMS TO A) DEVELOP MOLECULAR GLUES TO STABILIZE NATIVE PPIS AND B) ESTABLISH TECHNOLOGIES TO STUDY DYNAMIC PPI NETWORKS. MOLECULAR GLUE (MG) DISCOVERY IS ONE OF THE MOST IMPACTFUL NEW AREAS OF CHEMICAL BIOLOGY. MGS BIND TO A COMPOSITE SURFACE FORMED BY A PPI, INDUCING COOPERATIVITY IN THE PROCESS. MOST GLUE DISCOVERY HAS FOCUSED ON NONNATIVE COMPLEX FORMATION FOR PROTEIN DEGRADATION. BY CONTRAST, WE HAVE FOCUSED ON NATIVE INTERACTIONS, MOST NOTABLY PHOSPHOPROTEINS BOUND TO THE CHAPERONE 14-3-3. BUILDING ON THIS NIGMS-FUNDED WORK, WE NOW ASK TWO QUESTIONS: 1) CAN WE USE MGS TO RE-FORM PPI LOST TO INTERFACE MUTATIONS, USING RARE DISEASES CAUSED BY LOSS OF 14-3-3 BINDING AS RELEVANT EXAMPLES? 2) ARE OUR DISCOVERY APPROACHES AMENABLE TO NEW PPI NETWORKS, USING CHAPERONE/CLIENT COMPLEXES AS EXAMPLES? BY STABILIZING CLIENTS BOUND TO THEIR CHAPERONES, WE AIM TO FLIP THE PROTEOSTATIC SWITCH FROM PROTEIN FOLDING TO PROTEIN DEGRADATION. BY THE END OF THE GRANT TERM, WE WILL HAVE PRODUCED PROBES WITH NEW MECHANISMS OF ACTION, DEMONSTRATED A NOVEL MECHANISM FOR INDUCED PROTEIN DEGRADATION, AND GAINED INSIGHTS INTO WHAT BIOPHYSICAL FEATURES OF PPI SUPPORT MG DISCOVERY. VALOSIN CONTAINING PROTEIN (VCP/P97) IS THE CELL’S PRIMARY UNFOLDASE FOR DIFFICULT-TO-UNFOLD PROTEINS. THE VCP HOMOHEXAMER CONTAINS A DOUBLE ATPASE BARREL AND A PPI-BINDING DOMAIN THAT SITS OUTSIDE THE BARREL AND BINDS TO THREE DOZEN ‘ADAPTOR’ PROTEINS WITH VARIOUS (AND OFTEN UNKNOWN) FUNCTIONS. DURING ATP HYDROLYSIS, THE PPI DOMAIN CHANGES ORIENTATION, WHICH ALTERS THE AFFINITIES OF THESE ADAPTORS. THE IMPORTANCE OF DOMAIN ORIENTATION IS DEMONSTRATED BY GENETIC FORMS OF PROTEINOPATHY THAT ARE CAUSED BY POINT MUTATIONS IN VCP THAT ALTER N-DOMAIN DYNAMICS. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS, SUPPORTED BY DATA FUNDED BY NIGMS, IS THAT ALTERED PROTEIN DYNAMICS DISRUPT CERTAIN ADAPTOR/VCP COMPLEXES AND STABILIZE OTHERS, LEADING TO CHANGES IN SUBSETS OF VCP FUNCTION AND LONG- TERM DYSHOMEOSTASIS. TO EVALUATE OUR HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL DEVELOP TWO TECHNOLOGIES: 1) A FRET-BASED SENSOR TO MEASURE VCP CONFORMATION DIRECTLY. WE WILL MEASURE VCP CONFORMATION IN THE PRESENCE OF PPI, MUTATIONS, AND OTHER PERTURBATIONS, AND WE WILL SCREEN FOR NEW PROBE MOLECULES THAT ‘CORRECT’ CONFORMATIONAL CONTROL IN VCP. 2) PROXIMITY-BASED PROTEOMIC ASSAYS THAT WILL MAP VCP/ADAPTOR COMPLEXES TO SPECIFIC SUBSTRATES, CELLULAR NEIGHBORHOODS, AND CO-BINDING OF OTHER ADAPTORS. BY THE END OF THE GRANT TERM, WE WILL HAVE STARTED A VCP ATLAS, LINKING CONTEXT-SPECIFIC ADAPTOR BINDING (SUCH AS PROTEIN CONFORMATION) TO CELLULAR FUNCTION.

description: REGULATION OF TRANSCRIPTION INITIATION BY PROMOTER NUCLEOSOMES - THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEFINE THE MOLECULAR BASIS OF TRANSCRIPTION INITIATION AT EUKARYOTIC PROMOTERS IN CHROMATIN. THIS PROCESS REPRESENTS A CENTRAL REGULATORY POINT IN GENE EXPRESSION AT THE END OF THE SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION PATHWAY. ITS DYSREGULATION HAS BEEN IMPLICATED IN HUMAN DISEASES, INCLUDING CANCER AND NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS, AS WELL AS IN AGING-RELATED PROCESSES. THE PROTEINS RESPONSIBLE FOR TRANSCRIPTION INITIATION, A SET OF GENERAL TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS (GTFS) AND RNA POLYMERASE II (POL II), ASSOCIATE IN A SO-CALLED PRE-INITIATION COMPLEX (PIC) AT PROMOTERS, WHILE THE MEDIATOR COMPLEX, COMPOSED OF OVER 20 PROTEINS, RELAYS SIGNALS FROM GENE-SPECIFIC ACTIVATORS TO THE PIC. IN CHROMATIN, THIS INITIATION PROCESS IS TIGHTLY REGULATED BY THE PROMOTER NUCLEOSOME (THE SO- CALLED +1 NUCLEOSOME), IN COLLABORATION WITH COACTIVATOR COMPLEXES SUCH AS CHROMATIN REMODELERS, HISTONE MODIFIERS, AND HISTONE CHAPERONES, WITH ADDITIONAL LAYERS OF REGULATION BY PROMOTER-SPECIFIC HISTONE MODIFICATIONS AND VARIANTS. BUILDING ON OUR SUCCESS IN DEVELOPING A HIGHLY EFFICIENT IN VITRO TRANSCRIPTION INITIATION SYSTEM USING YEAST PIC– MEDIATOR, WE WILL ISOLATE AND DISSECT A SERIES OF PIC–MEDIATOR–COACTIVATOR COMPLEXES THAT REPRESENT STATES FROM INITIATION TO EARLY ELONGATION, AS WELL AS INTERMEDIATES FORMED PRIOR TO FULL PIC ASSEMBLY. WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING TRANSITIONS BETWEEN THESE STATES USING BIOCHEMICAL AND STRUCTURAL APPROACHES, INCLUDING CRYO-EM AND CROSS-LINKING MASS SPECTROMETRY (XL-MS), AND CRITICALLY VALIDATE THE RESULTING STRUCTURAL MODELS THROUGH FUNCTIONAL ANALYSES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: FLEXIBLE BAYESIAN METHODS FOR ZERO-INFLATED MICROBIOME DATA TO UNDERSTAND MICROBIAL COMMUNITY DYNAMICS AND FUNCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT: RECENT TECHNOLOGICAL AND COMPUTATIONAL INNOVATIONS HAVE DRAMATICALLY IMPROVED THE SCALE AND SPEED IN WHICH RESEARCHERS COLLECT AND PROCESS MICROBIOME DATA. COUPLED WITH ADVANCES IN STATISTICAL AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS FOR MICROBIOME DATA ANALYSIS, THESE DEVELOPMENTS HAVE HELPED RESEARCHERS BETTER UNDERSTAND THE VARIOUS ROLES THE MICROBIOME PLAYS IN HUMAN HEALTH AND DISEASE. THIS HAS LED RESEARCHERS TO EXPLORE THE FEASIBILITY OF MICROBIOTA-BASED DIAGNOSTICS, THERAPIES, AND PREVENTION OF DISEASE, POTENTIALLY THROUGH PERSONALIZED TREATMENT STRATEGIES. A MAJOR CHALLENGE IN DEVELOPING MICROBIOTA-BASED PERSONALIZED MEDICINE IS OUR LIMITED UNDERSTANDING OF THE MECHANISMS THAT GOVERN MICROBIAL COMMUNITY ASSEMBLY, STABILITY, AND FUNCTION. FURTHER, STATISTICAL METHODS DEVELOPED AND APPLIED TO DESCRIBE THESE MECHANISMS ARE STILL IN THEIR INFANCY, AS EVEN THE MOST BASIC INFERENTIAL TASKS ARE CHALLENGED BY THE COMPLEXITY OF MICROBIOME DATA.  THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PURSUE THE NEXT GENERATION OF STATISTICAL METHODS DESIGNED TO HELP UNLOCK THE POTENTIAL OF MICROBIOTA-BASED PERSONALIZED MEDICINE BY INTRODUCING A SUITE OF SCALABLE BAYESIAN METHODS FOR EXPLORATORY AND CONFIRMATORY MICROBIOME DATA ANALYSIS. BUILDING ON OUR UNIQUE EXPERIENCE IN MICROBIOME, MOBILE HEALTH, AND ECOLOGICAL RESEARCH, THE METHODS DEVELOPED BY MY LAB WILL BE DESIGNED TO INVESTIGATE MICROBIAL COMMUNITY ASSEMBLY, STABILITY, AND FUNCTION. EACH METHOD WILL ACCOMMODATE THE HIGH-DIMENSIONAL, OVERDISPERSED, ZERO-INFLATED, AND COMPOSITIONAL STRUCTURE CHARACTERISTIC OF MICROBIOME DATA AND WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY A USER- FRIENDLY SOFTWARE PACKAGE FOR OTHER RESEARCHERS TO APPLY AND EXTEND OUR WORK. SPECIFICALLY, THE PROPOSED METHODS WILL ALLOW RESEARCHERS TO (1) STUDY HOW MICROBES RESPOND TO, AND INFLUENCE, ABIOTIC AND BIOTIC FACTORS AND HOW THESE RELATIONS MAY DIFFER BY INTERACTIONS THEREOF; (2) INVESTIGATE HOW CLUSTERS OF MICROBIAL COMPOSITION VARY OVER TIME, SPACE, AND OTHER ENVIRONMENTAL AND HOST-ASSOCIATED FACTORS; AND (3) CHARACTERIZE STABLE STATES OF MICROBIAL COMPOSITION AND FUNCTION, IDENTIFY MOMENTS WHEN INDIVIDUALS TRANSITION THROUGH THESE STATES, AND UNDERSTAND THE MECHANISMS DRIVING THESE TRANSITIONS. ADDITIONALLY, THIS WORK WILL FACILITATE A PRODUCTIVE RESEARCH AND MEN- TORING ENVIRONMENT FOR UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS IN MY LAB THROUGH MULTIFACETED ACADEMIC, RESEARCH, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, AND COLLABORATIVE OPPORTUNITIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE DUAL IMPACT OF ACTIVE AND SILENCED TRANSPOSONS ON MEIOTIC RECOMBINATION - PROJECT SUMMARY MEIOTIC RECOMBINATION IS A FUNDAMENTAL PROCESS IN SEXUALLY REPRODUCING EUKARYOTIC ORGANISMS THAT GENERATES GENETIC DIVERSITY AND ENSURES THE ACCURATE SEGREGATION OF HOMOLOGOUS CHROMOSOMES. DISRUPTIONS IN THIS PROCESS CAN LEAD TO SEVERE CONSEQUENCES, INCLUDING INFERTILITY AND GENETIC DISORDERS. MEIOTIC RECOMBINATION IS INTRICATELY REGULATED BY BOTH GENETIC AND EPIGENETIC FACTORS. THERE IS GROWING EVIDENCE THAT TRANSPOSABLE ELEMENTS (TES), WHICH ARE PRIMARY TARGETS OF EPIGENETIC SILENCING IN BOTH PLANTS AND MAMMALS, CAN INFLUENCE RECOMBINATION BOTH GENETICALLY, THROUGH THE INDUCTION OF DOUBLE-STRAND BREAKS (DSBS), AND EPIGENETICALLY, BY INTRODUCING NEW METHYLATED AND HISTONE-MODIFIED SEQUENCES NEAR GENES. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF OUR LAB IS TO IDENTIFY AND MANIPULATE GENETIC AND EPIGENETIC FACTORS THAT INFLUENCE MEIOTIC RECOMBINATION. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO ADDRESS CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAPS IN UNDERSTANDING HOW ACTIVE AND SILENCED TES SHAPE RECOMBINATION, USING MAIZE AND RICE AS MODELS BECAUSE OF THEIR ABUNDANCE OF NATURALLY ACTIVE TES. BASED ON OUR PRELIMINARY DATA, OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT BOTH ACTIVE AND SILENCED TRANSPOSONS REMODEL RECOMBINATION LANDSCAPES BY AFFECTING CROSSOVER INTERFERENCE, THE SYNAPTONEMAL COMPLEX, DSB REPAIR, AND CHROMATIN STRUCTURE. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL FIRST INVESTIGATE HOW ACTIVE MUTATOR (MU) TRANSPOSONS IN MAIZE, WHICH INDUCE ABUNDANT DSBS DURING SPOROPHYTIC GERMLINE DEVELOPMENT AND IN GAMETOPHYTES, AFFECT RECOMBINATION. WE WILL GENERATE HIGH-RESOLUTION CROSSOVER MAPS, PERFORM A GENOME-WIDE ASSESSMENT OF RECOMBINATION FREQUENCY IN THE VICINITY OF MU INSERTIONS, AND DETERMINE WHETHER MU-DERIVED DSBS CAN INTRODUCE CROSSOVERS. WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE WHETHER MU EXCISION OR INSERTION ALTERS CHROMATIN STRUCTURE, CHROMATIN ACCESSIBILITY, AND 3D GENOME ORGANIZATION AT INSERTION SITES AND THEIR FLANKING REGIONS. SECOND, WE WILL STUDY THE IMPACT OF MINIATURE INVERTED REPEAT ELEMENTS (MITES) ON RECOMBINATION IN RICE USING RECOMBINANT INBRED LINE POPULATIONS WITH HIGH VERSUS LOW MITE COPY NUMBERS. FINALLY, WE WILL EXAMINE HOW SILENCED TES NEAR ACTIVE GENES INFLUENCE RECOMBINATION USING THE MOP1 (MEDIATOR OF PARAMUTATION 1) MUTANT, WHICH LARGELY REMOVES CHH METHYLATION NEAR GENES AND REDISTRIBUTES RECOMBINATION LANDSCAPES. WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW DNA METHYLATION AT TES AFFECTS DSB FORMATION, CROSSOVER INTERFERENCE, CHROMOSOME AXIS ORGANIZATION, SYNAPTONEMAL COMPLEX DYNAMICS, AND CHROMATIN STRUCTURE IN A SEX-SPECIFIC MANNER. THIS STUDY WILL CONTRIBUTE TO A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW TES, DNA METHYLATION, AND CHROMATIN STRUCTURE INTERACT TO SHAPE MEIOTIC RECOMBINATION LANDSCAPES IN MAIZE AND RICE, WITH BROAD IMPLICATIONS FOR OTHER EUKARYOTES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TRANSFORMING SPATIAL PROTEOMICS VIA SIMULTANEOUS MULTIPLEXED IMAGING AT SINGLE-PROTEIN RESOLUTION - PROJECT SUMMARY UNDERSTANDING BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES REQUIRES NOT ONLY MEASURING HOW MUCH OF A PROTEIN IS PRESENT, BUT ALSO KNOWING WHERE EACH PROTEIN IS LOCATED, HOW IT IS ORGANIZED, AND WITH WHOM IT INTERACTS. EXISTING MASS SPECTROMETRY–BASED PROTEOMICS METHODS PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE MOLECULAR PROFILING BUT LACK THE SPATIAL RESOLUTION NECESSARY TO RESOLVE NANOSCALE PROTEIN ORGANIZATION. IMAGING-BASED SPATIAL PROTEOMICS TECHNIQUES SUCH AS IMAGING MASS SPECTROMETRY, MULTIPLEXED ION BEAM IMAGING, AND CODEX CAN PROFILE UP TO 100 PROTEINS WITH SUBCELLULAR RESOLUTION, BUT THEY ARE LIMITED TO 200–500 NM RESOLUTION AND CANNOT VISUALIZE NANOSCALE PROTEIN ASSEMBLIES AT THE MOLECULAR SCALE. SINGLE-MOLECULE LOCALIZATION MICROSCOPY (SMLM) ACHIEVES NANOMETER PRECISION, ENABLING VISUALIZATION OF PROTEINS AT THE SCALE OF INDIVIDUAL MOLECULES. AMONG THESE METHODS, DNA-PAINT PROVIDES THEORETICALLY UNLIMITED MULTIPLEXING BUT SUFFERS FROM SLOW ACQUISITION, SEQUENTIAL IMAGING REQUIREMENTS, SAMPLE DAMAGE FROM REPEATED WASHING, SYSTEM INSTABILITY DURING MULTI-ROUND IMAGING, AND HIGH BACKGROUND IN THICK SAMPLES. THIS PROJECT INTRODUCES SIMUL-PROTEOMICS, A NEXT-GENERATION SPATIAL PROTEOMICS PLATFORM THAT ENABLES HIGH-THROUGHPUT, SIMULTANEOUS MULTIPLEXED IMAGING AT SINGLE-PROTEIN RESOLUTION. BY INTEGRATING TRANSFORMATIVE SPECTRAL PHASOR ANALYSIS, SPECTRALLY ENGINEERED PROBES SUCH AS QUANTUM DOTS, AND LIGHT SHEET ILLUMINATION, SIMUL-PROTEOMICS DIRECTLY OVERCOMES THE LIMITATIONS OF DNA-PAINT. THIS APPROACH ELIMINATES SEQUENTIAL READOUT, MINIMIZES SAMPLE PERTURBATION, AND IMPROVES SPEED BY MORE THAN 100-FOLD FOR UP TO 60-PLEXED IMAGING, ENABLING QUANTITATIVE NANOSCALE MAPPING OF PROTEIN DISTRIBUTIONS AND INTERACTIONS IN CELLS, TISSUES, AND SMALL ORGANISMS IN A SINGLE ROUND. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL DELIVER A TRANSFORMATIVE TECHNOLOGY PLATFORM CAPABLE OF RESOLVING NANOSCALE PROTEIN ORGANIZATION IN COMPLEX BIOLOGICAL SYSTEMS WITH UNPRECEDENTED THROUGHPUT. THIS WILL OPEN THE DOOR TO ANSWERING FUNDAMENTAL BIOLOGICAL QUESTIONS ABOUT PROTEIN ASSEMBLIES, SIGNALING NETWORKS, AND SPATIAL REGULATION IN HEALTH AND DISEASE. BY ACHIEVING HIGH- THROUGHPUT SINGLE-PROTEIN SPATIAL PROTEOMICS, THE PROJECT HAS THE POTENTIAL TO IMPACT DIVERSE FIELDS INCLUDING CANCER BIOLOGY, NEUROBIOLOGY, AND DEVELOPMENTAL BIOLOGY, WHILE ALSO LAYING THE GROUNDWORK FOR FUTURE TRANSLATIONAL APPLICATIONS IN DIAGNOSTICS AND THERAPEUTICS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: APPLYING NEW GENOMIC TOOLS TO STUDY CENTROMERE ORGANIZATION, REPLICATION, AND FUNCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY CENTROMERES PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN CHROMOSOME SEGREGATION DURING CELL DIVISION, YET MANY FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS ABOUT THEIR STRUCTURE, REPLICATION, AND FUNCTION REMAIN UNANSWERED DUE TO LONGSTANDING TECHNICAL CHALLENGES IN STUDYING THESE HIGHLY REPETITIVE GENOMIC REGIONS. TO OVERCOME THESE HURDLES, WE COMBINE NOVEL GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES AND MODERN GENETIC TOOLS TO INVESTIGATE BASIC CENTROMERE BIOLOGY AT UNPRECEDENTED RESOLUTION. BY BUILDING ON RECENT ADVANCES IN LONG-READ SEQUENCING AND GENOME ASSEMBLY, WE ARE GENERATING COMPLETE SATELLITE DNA ANNOTATIONS FOR A NEW GAPLESS, DIPLOID HUMAN REFERENCE ASSEMBLY. USING THIS REFERENCE ALONG WITH DIMELO-SEQ, A LONG-READ PROTEIN-DNA INTERACTION MAPPING METHOD THAT WE PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED, WE ARE MAPPING CENTROMERE-ASSOCIATED PROTEINS LIKE CENTROMERE PROTEIN A (CENP-A) ALONG LONG, SINGLE CHROMATIN FIBERS MAPPED TO THEIR EXACT LOCATIONS WITHIN EACH HUMAN CENTROMERE. THIS IS REVEALING THE FINE-SCALE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN ENDOGENOUS DNA METHYLATION, CENTROMERE PROTEIN LOCALIZATION, AND REPETITIVE DNA SEQUENCES, WHICH TEND TO BE HYPERMETHYLATED EXCEPT AT SUBREGIONS WHERE CENP-A LOCALIZES AT HIGH DENSITY. THE CAUSAL, FUNCTIONAL, AND MECHANISTIC REASONS FOR DNA HYPOMETHYLATION AT CENTROMERES REMAIN UNKNOWN AND ARE AMONG THE MOST PRESSING FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS IN CENTROMERE BIOLOGY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT LOCALIZED DNA HYPOMETHYLATION HELPS TO RESTRICT CENP-A POSITIONING AND PROMOTE THE EPIGENETIC TRANSMISSION OF CENTROMERE IDENTITY. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE ARE WORKING COLLABORATIVELY TO DISSECT THE CAUSAL AND FUNCTIONAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN DNA METHYLATION AND CENP-A POSITIONING USING DIMELO-SEQ AND CAREFULLY ENGINEERED GENETIC PERTURBATION EXPERIMENTS. MOVING FORWARD, WE ARE FURTHER REFINING DIMELO-SEQ TO QUANTITATIVELY MAP CENP-A AND OTHER PROTEINS AT SINGLE- NUCLEOSOME RESOLUTION THROUGHOUT THE CELL CYCLE TO UNDERSTAND THE STRUCTURE AND DYNAMICS OF THE INNER KINETOCHORE. WE ARE ALSO COMBINING DIMELO-SEQ WITH OTHER SINGLE-MOLECULE SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGIES TO STUDY HOW CENTROMERIC CHROMATIN IS REPLICATED AND HOW REPLICATION FORK SPEEDS VARY THROUGHOUT PERICENTROMERIC REGIONS. FINALLY, WE ARE DEVELOPING EXPERIMENTAL SYSTEMS THAT WILL ENABLE US TO UNCOVER THE SPECIFIC MECHANISMS RESPONSIBLE FOR DNA HYPOMETHYLATION AT HUMAN CENTROMERES AND FURTHER EXPLORE THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THIS HYPOMETHYLATION FOR CENTROMERE FUNCTION AND EPIGENETIC PROPAGATION. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL COMBINE CUTTING-EDGE GENOMIC APPROACHES WITH TARGETED GENETIC PERTURBATIONS TO DISSECT CAUSAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN DNA SEQUENCE, EPIGENETIC MARKS, AND CENTROMERE FUNCTION. BY OVERCOMING PREVIOUSLY INSURMOUNTABLE TECHNICAL BARRIERS, THIS RESEARCH PROMISES TO SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF CENTROMERE BIOLOGY AND CHROMOSOME SEGREGATION - PROCESSES FUNDAMENTAL TO CELL DIVISION AND GENOME STABILITY ACROSS EUKARYOTES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DAYTIME SLEEPINESS AND METHAMPHETAMINE TAKING - PROJECT SUMMARY METHAMPHETAMINE USE AND ITS ASSOCIATED HEALTH CONSEQUENCES ARE BECOMING INCREASINGLY PREVALENT BOTH IN THE UNITED STATES AND GLOBALLY. DESPITE THIS GROWING PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERN, THERE ARE CURRENTLY NO FDA-APPROVED PHARMACOTHERAPIES FOR METHAMPHETAMINE USE DISORDER. DISTURBED SLEEP-WAKE CYCLES ARE ONE OF THE MOST PROMINENT CONSEQUENCES OF METHAMPHETAMINE USE. WHILE ACTIVE METHAMPHETAMINE USE IS ASSOCIATED WITH DISRUPTED NIGHTTIME SLEEP, DISCONTINUATION OF METHAMPHETAMINE USE IS ASSOCIATED WITH EXCESSIVE DAYTIME SLEEPINESS, WHICH HAS BEEN SHOWN TO PREDICT GREATER METHAMPHETAMINE CRAVING. DESPITE THE SIGNIFICANCE OF EXCESSIVE DAYTIME SLEEPINESS ASSOCIATED WITH DISCONTINUATION OF METHAMPHETAMINE USE, THIS PHENOMENON HAS NOT BEEN STUDIED OR MODELED IN THE PRECLINICAL LITERATURE. THE PRESENT PROJECT WILL MODEL EXCESSIVE DAYTIME SLEEP FOLLOWING METHAMPHETAMINE USE IN NONHUMAN PRIMATES, STUDY ITS RELATIONSHIP TO THE MORE WELL DESCRIBED NIGHTTIME SLEEP DISTURBANCES OBSERVED WITH METHAMPHETAMINE USE, AND INVESTIGATE HOW MODAFINIL MAY MEDIATE THIS INTERACTION. OUR WORKING HYPOTHESIS IS THAT CHRONIC METHAMPHETAMINE USE CAUSES EXCESSIVE DAYTIME SLEEPINESS, AND THAT CONTINUED METHAMPHETAMINE USE IS DRIVEN, IN PART, BY ALLEVIATION OF ASSOCIATED EXCESSIVE DAYTIME SLEEPINESS. BASED ON THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE PREDICT THAT A WAKEFULNESS-PROMOTING DRUG (MODAFINIL) WILL IMPROVE SLEEP DURING ABSTINENCE AND WILL REDUCE METHAMPHETAMINE TAKING DURING ONGOING SELF-ADMINISTRATION THROUGH AMELIORATION OF EXCESSIVE DAYTIME SLEEPINESS. SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL INVESTIGATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN METHAMPHETAMINE-INDUCED DAYTIME AND NIGHTTIME SLEEP ALTERATIONS DURING DISCONTINUATION OF METHAMPHETAMINE SELF-ADMINISTRATION. RHESUS MONKEYS WILL SELF-ADMINISTER METHAMPHETAMINE INTRAVENOUSLY FOR 7 CONSECUTIVE DAYS, AND DAYTIME/NIGHTTIME SLEEP WILL BE EVALUATED FOR 2 WEEKS AFTER DISCONTINUATION OF METHAMPHETAMINE SELF-ADMINISTRATION USING ACTIGRAPHY. THESE STUDIES WILL THEN BE REPEATED WITH MODAFINIL ADMINISTRATION DURING THE FIRST 7 DAYS AFTER DISCONTINUATION OF METHAMPHETAMINE SELF- ADMINISTRATION. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN METHAMPHETAMINE-INDUCED EXCESSIVE DAYTIME SLEEPINESS AND METHAMPHETAMINE INTAKE DURING ACTIVE SELF-ADMINISTRATION. RHESUS MONKEYS WILL SELF- ADMINISTER METHAMPHETAMINE FOR 7 CONSECUTIVE DAYS, FOLLOWED BY 7 MORE DAYS OF ACTIVE SELF-ADMINISTRATION AND MORNING TREATMENT WITH VEHICLE OR MODAFINIL, AND DAYTIME/NIGHTTIME SLEEP WILL BE EVALUATED DURING ONGOING SELF- ADMINISTRATION AND AFTER A 2-WEEK DISCONTINUATION PERIOD. THE USE OF THIS NEW TRANSLATIONAL MODEL WILL ALLOW FOR DETERMINATION OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN CHRONIC METHAMPHETAMINE USE AND EXCESSIVE DAYTIME SLEEPINESS, AS WELL AS INTEGRATION WITH EVALUATIONS OF NIGHTTIME SLEEP DISRUPTIONS. MOREOVER, OUR NEW MODEL WILL ALLOW EVALUATION OF A POTENTIAL TREATMENT OF EXCESSIVE DAYTIME SLEEPINESS THAT MAY, IN TURN, REDUCE METHAMPHETAMINE SELF- ADMINISTRATION.

description: TARGETING PURINE CATABOLISM AND SIGNALING IN T CELL AUTOIMMUNITY - SUMMARY:  PROPERLY ALLOCATING METABOLIC RESOURCES IS CRUCIAL FOR SUPPORTING THE ENERGETICALLY DEMANDING PROCESSES OF T- CELL PROLIFERATION AND INFLAMMATION THAT DRIVE AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES, SUCH AS MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS AND RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS. ADDITIONALLY, METABOLITES CAN ACT AS LIGANDS THAT INTERACT WITH SPECIFIC CELL-SURFACE RECEPTORS, SHAPING THE T-CELL RESPONSE IN PHYSIOLOGICAL AND PATHOLOGICAL CONTEXTS. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO UNDERSTAND HOW PURINE NUCLE- OSIDES, SPECIFICALLY ADENOSINE AND INOSINE, REGULATE T-CELL INFLAMMATION AND EXPLORE THE POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS OF TARGETING PURINE METABOLISM AND SIGNALING IN ANIMAL MODELS OF AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES. THROUGH AN INTEGRATED ANALYSIS OF METABOLOME, STABLE ISOTOPE TRACING, TRANSCRIPTOME, AND T-CELL FUNCTION, WE HAVE REVEALED THAT EFFECTOR T CELLS CATABOLIZE (I.E., BREAK DOWN TO RELEASE ENERGY) PURINE. WE ALSO DISCOVERED THAT PURINES ENGAGE CELL SURFACE PURINE-RECEPTOR SIGNALING AND INTRACELLULAR PURINE CATABOLISM DIFFERENTLY, LEADING TO OPPOSING IMMUNE MODULATORY EFFECTS ON T CELLS. EXTRACELLULAR ADENOSINE ACTS ON THE ADENOSINE A2A RECEPTOR AND SUP- PRESSES T-CELL INFLAMMATION. ON THE OTHER HAND, EQUILIBRATIVE AND CONCENTRATIVE NUCLEOSIDE TRANSPORTERS (ENTS/CNTS), ALONG WITH ADENOSINE DEAMINASE (ADA), ALLOW T CELLS TO TAKE UP ADENOSINE AND CONVERT IT INTO ITS IMMEDIATE METABOLIC PRODUCT, INOSINE. SUBSEQUENTLY, PURINE NUCLEOSIDE PHOSPHORYLASE (PNP) BREAKS DOWN INO- SINE, PRODUCING CARBON AND ENERGY THAT SUPPORT T-CELL PROLIFERATION AND INFLAMMATION. ACCORDINGLY, GENETICALLY OR PHARMACOLOGICALLY ABLATING PURINE CATABOLIZING ENZYME PNP IN T CELLS SUPPRESSES INFLAMMATION AND AUTOIMMUN- ITY IN VIVO.  HENCE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE ADENOSINE-INOSINE AXIS ACTS AS AN IMMUNE-METABOLIC CHECKPOINT COORDINATING BIOENERGETIC AND RECEPTOR-SIGNALING RESPONSES TO REGULATE T-CELL-MEDIATED INFLAMMATION AND AUTOIMMUNITY. THE AIMS OF THIS PROPOSAL ARE TO 1) DECIPHER THE MOLECULAR AND SIGNALING MECHANISMS THAT CONTROL PURINE METABOLISM IN T CELLS; 2) DETERMINE THE OUTCOMES OF MODULATING PURINE METABOLISM AND RECEPTOR SIGNALING IN REGULATING THE EFFECTOR FUNCTION OF T CELLS; AND 3) DEVELOP AND TEST COMPLEMENTARY PHARMACOLOGICAL, GENETIC, AND METABOLIC STRATEGIES TO MODULATE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE AND AUTOIMMUNITY IN ANIMAL MODELS. THIS PROJECT’S EXPECTED OUT- COMES ARE SIGNIFICANT AS THEY WILL REVEAL THE FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES OF THE EMERGING CONNECTIONS BETWEEN CELL METABOLISM, SIGNALING, AND T-CELL AUTOIMMUNITY. NOTABLY, THE PNP INHIBITOR (FORODENSINE) AND ADA INHIBITOR (PENTOSTATIN) WERE CLINICALLY USED TO TREAT LEUKEMIA. OUR PROPOSED PRECLINICAL STUDIES ARE INNOVATIVE AS THEY WILL REPURPOSE THESE TWO DRUGS FOR TREATING AUTOIMMUNITY. THESE STUDIES ARE CRITICAL TO DEVELOPING NOVEL APPROACHES AND THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS THAT IMPROVE CLINICAL OUTCOMES OF AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES SUCH AS MULTIPLE SCLERO- SIS AND RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NK CELL TARGETING OF HIV RESERVOIR CELLS - ABSTRACT HIV-1 RESERVOIR CELLS ARE A SMALL SUBSET OF CD4 T CELLS THAT HARBOR CHROMOSOMALLY INTEGRATED HIV-1 DNA, PERSIST FOR LIFE, AND REPRESENT THE PRINCIPAL BARRIER TO CURE. HISTORICALLY, PROVIRUSES IN THESE CELLS WERE CONSIDERED LARGELY TRANSCRIPTIONALLY SILENT, ALLOWING INFECTED CELLS TO ESCAPE IMMUNE SURVEILLANCE AND RESIST HOST EFFECTOR CELLS. CHALLENGING THIS VIEW, RECENT SINGLE-CELL STUDIES DEMONSTRATE THAT RESERVOIR CELLS CAN FREQUENTLY BE TRANSCRIPTIONALLY ACTIVE AND, AS A RESULT, SUSCEPTIBLE TO HOST IMMUNE RESPONSES. IN LINE WITH THESE OBSERVATIONS, RECENT WORK SUGGESTS THAT HIV-1 RESERVOIR CELLS ARE SUBJECT TO IMMUNE-MEDIATED SELECTION PRESSURES THAT PREFERENTIALLY ELIMINATE PROVIRUSES INTEGRATED INTO PERMISSIVE CHROMATIN REGIONS THAT SUPPORT VIRAL TRANSCRIPTION, WHEREAS PROVIRUSES EMBEDDED IN REPRESSIVE HETEROCHROMATIN GAIN A RELATIVE SELECTIVE ADVANTAGE. HOWEVER, THE SPECIFIC IMMUNE MECHANISMS THAT RECOGNIZE, TARGET, AND SELECT HIV-1 RESERVOIR CELLS REMAIN POORLY DEFINED, BUT DELINEATING THESE PATHWAYS WILL BE ESSENTIAL FOR THE DESIGN OF IMMUNE-BASED STRATEGIES FOR HIV-1 CURE. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF THIS APPLICATION IS THAT HIV-1 RESERVOIR CELLS ARE VULNERABLE TO INNATE IMMUNE RECOGNITION, PARTICULARLY BY KIR2DL1-EDUCATED NK CELLS THAT ARE CO-ACTIVATED THROUGH NKG2C–HLA-E INTERACTIONS. THIS HYPOTHESIS IS SUPPORTED BY OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOWING THAT, AMONG ART-TREATED INDIVIDUALS, RESERVOIR SIZE IS SIGNIFICANTLY LOWER IN CARRIERS OF HLA-C2, AN ALLELE GROUP THAT PROMOTES NK CELL EDUCATION VIA KIR2DL1, AND IN INDIVIDUALS HARBORING PROVIRAL VPU VARIANTS THAT EFFICIENTLY DOWNREGULATE HLA-C, THEREBY TRIGGERING ACTIVATION OF KIR2DL1⁺ NK CELLS THROUGH “MISSING-SELF” RECOGNITION. FURTHERMORE, RESERVOIR SIZE WAS INVERSELY CORRELATED WITH THE FREQUENCY OF KIR2DL1⁺ NKG2C⁺ NK CELLS AND WAS STRONGLY INFLUENCED BY VIRAL PEPTIDE DIVERSITY WITHIN HLA- E–RESTRICTED EPITOPES THAT MODULATE NKG2C-DEPENDENT NK CELL ACTIVATION IN A PEPTIDE-VARIANT-SPECIFIC MANNER. TO DEFINE HOW KIR-EDUCATED NK CELLS RECOGNIZE AND TARGET HIV-1 RESERVOIR CELLS, WE PROPOSE THREE SPECIFIC AIMS. IN SPECIFIC AIM 1, WE WILL DETERMINE HOW HOST AND VIRAL GENOMIC VARIATIONS INFLUENCE THE SIZES AND CHARACTERISTICS OF THE HIV-1 RESERVOIR, WITH A PARTICULAR FOCUS ON POLYMORPHISMS WITHIN THE HLA CLASS I LOCUS AND ASSOCIATED IMMUNE GENES, THE VIRAL VPU GENE AND IN HLA-E–RESTRICTED EPITOPES. IN SPECIFIC AIM 2, WE WILL PERFORM DETAILED PHENOTYPIC AND FUNCTIONAL ANALYSES OF NK CELL SUBSETS AND OTHER IMMUNE EFFECTOR CELLS THAT ARE ASSOCIATED WITH REDUCED RESERVOIR SIZES AND DEFINE THEIR CAPACITY TO RECOGNIZE VIRALLY-ENCODED HLA-E–RESTRICTED EPITOPES IN A PEPTIDE-VARIANT-SPECIFIC MANNER. IN SPECIFIC AIM 3, WE WILL APPLY INNOVATIVE SINGLE-CELL “TRIPLE-OMICS” MICROFLUIDIC APPROACHES TO CHARACTERIZE THE PHENOTYPIC AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROFILES OF HIV-1 RESERVOIR CELLS DIRECTLY EX VIVO, ENABLING INFERENCE OF IMMUNE SELECTION MECHANISMS THROUGH TARGETED EVALUATION OF SIGNATURES ASSOCIATED WITH SUSCEPTIBILITY OR RESISTANCE TO NK CELL–MEDIATED KILLING. COLLECTIVELY, THESE STUDIES WILL SUBSTANTIALLY ADVANCE THE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW HUMAN IMMUNE RESPONSES INTERFACE WITH AND CONSTRAIN HIV-1 RESERVOIR CELLS DURING ART AND WILL CRITICALLY INFORM THE DESIGN OF IMMUNOLOGICAL STRATEGIES FOR HIV-1 CURE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PROSPECTIVE DYNAMIC BH3 PROFILING FOR CLINICAL USE IN RELAPSED OR REFRACTORY AML - PROJECT SUMMARY DISEASE RECURRENCE IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH FOR PATIENTS WITH ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA. THIS IS DRIVEN BY THE FAILURE TO ACHIEVE A SECOND REMISSION WITH AVAILABLE THERAPIES. THERE IS ALSO LIMITED GUIDANCE ON HOW TO SELECT EFFECTIVE AND AVOID INEFFECTIVE THERAPIES, WHICH ARE EQUALLY SIGNIFICANT TO PATIENT OUTCOME. TESTING FOR TARGETABLE MUTATIONS IS ONLY RELEVANT TO 50% OF PATIENTS THAT RELAPSE AND, EVEN SO, THE MAJORITY OF PATIENTS STILL DO NOT ACHIEVE A COMPLETE REMISSION WITH TARGETED SINGLE-AGENT THERAPIES. VENETOCLAX IS A BCL-2 INHIBITOR AND PRIMING AGENT THAT BOLSTERS THE EFFECTIVENESS OF DRUGS BASED ON PRECLINICAL AND CLINICAL STUDIES, BUT THERE IS LIMITED GUIDANCE ON HOW TO BEST PARTNER THERAPIES TO LEVERAGE VENETOCLAX-INDUCED APOPTOSIS. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IMPROVE THE OUTCOMES OF PATIENTS WITH RELAPSED OR REFRACTORY AML BY USING DYNAMIC BH3 PROFILING TO PROVIDE GUIDANCE ON TREATMENT SELECTION FOR INDIVIDUAL PATIENTS. THIS ASSAY MEASURES CHANGES IN APOPTOTIC PRIMING IN LEUKEMIA CELLS AFTER SHORT EX VIVO TREATMENT. THE DYNAMIC BH3 PROFILING ASSAY IS A PREDICTIVE BIOMARKER FOR IN VIVO CLINICAL RESPONSE TO VENETOCLAX, TARGETED THERAPIES AND CHEMOTHERAPY, BUT HAS NOT YET BEEN TESTED PROSPECTIVELY FOR CLINICAL USE. BASED ON THESE RECENT DATA, DYNAMIC BH3 PROFILING IS HYPOTHESIZED TO PREDICT RESPONSE AND NONRESPONSE TO THERAPIES IN PATIENTS WITH RELAPSED OR REFRACTORY AML. THE RATIONALE FOR THIS PROJECT IS THAT KNOWLEDGE OF FEASIBILITY AND BIOMARKER-GUIDED THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY, AND THE ASSOCIATED PATIENT-SPECIFIC DRUG- INDUCED MITOCHONDRIAL SENSITIVITIES WILL SET THE STAGE FOR IMPLEMENTING FUNCTIONAL BIOMARKERS INTO AML CLINICAL CARE, THEREBY PROVIDING NEW THERAPEUTIC OPPORTUNITIES. TO DEFINE THE CLINICAL ROLE AND IMPROVE THE PREDICTION POWER OF DYNAMIC BH3 PROFILING, THE FOLLOWING AIMS ARE PROPOSED: IN AIM 1, THE ROLE OF DYNAMIC BH3 PROFILING WILL BE DEFINED IN A PROSPECTIVE PHASE 2 CLINICAL TRIAL OF BIOMARKER-GUIDED THERAPY IN PATIENTS WITH RELAPSE OR REFRACTORY AML. IN THIS INVESTIGATOR-INITIATED TRIAL, PATIENTS WILL UNDERGO BIOMARKER SCREENING, WHICH WILL GUIDE THEM TOWARDS OR AWAY FROM VENETOCLAX-BASED COMBINATION THERAPIES AVAILABLE ON TRIAL. THE CO-PRIMARY OBJECTIVES ARE DETERMINING THE FEASIBILITY OF PERFORMING THE ASSAY IN REAL TIME AND PROVIDING BIOMARKER-GUIDED TREATMENT ASSIGNMENTS, AND THE EFFICACY OF BIOMARKER-GUIDED THERAPY (OVERALL RESPONSE RATE). THE SECONDARY OBJECTIVES ARE SAFETY AND LONG TERM CLINICAL OUTCOMES. CORRELATIVES TO EVALUATE FOR EVIDENCE OF CYTOTOXICITY AMONG DRUGS WITH EVIDENCE OF PRIMING WILL BE PERFORMED IN PARALLEL. IN AIM 2, THE DETECTION OF DRUG-INDUCED APOPTOTIC PRIMING BE COMPREHENSIVELY EXAMINED FOR OPPORTUNITIES TO IMPROVE RESPONSE PREDICTION BY INTRA-PATIENT ANALYSES WITH ADDITIONAL BH3 PEPTIDES AND CONSIDERATION OF AML SUBPOPULATIONS INCLUDING IMMATURE AND MATURE BLASTS. UPON SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH, THESE DATA WILL PROVIDE INITIAL PROSPECTIVE CLINICAL VALIDATION OF THE DYNAMIC BH3 PROFILING ASSAY. THESE CONTRIBUTIONS ARE EXPECTED TO PROVIDE JUSTIFICATION FOR ITS USE IN THERAPY- DECISION MAKING, WHICH WILL ADDRESS THE UNMET THERAPEUTIC NEEDS OF AML PATIENTS AND PROVIDE A STARTING POINT FOR ITS APPLICATION IN OTHER CANCERS.
