description: MOLECULAR DRIVERS OF REGIONAL AND CELLULAR VULNERABILITY TO TAU ACCUMULATION AND NEURODEGENERATION - PROJECT SUMMARY SELECTIVE REGIONAL BRAIN VULNERABILITY IS A FUNDAMENTAL FEATURE IN NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES THAT MUST BE DEEPLY UNDERSTOOD. IN TAUOPATHIES, THE BRAIN AREAS WHERE PATHOLOGICAL TAU ACCUMULATES ARE CLOSELY ASSOCIATED WITH REGIONAL ATROPHY AND BEHAVIORAL OUTCOME. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA IN POST-MORTEM HUMAN BRAIN SHOW THAT EXCITATORY NEURONS ARE MORE VULNERABLE TO TAU ACCUMULATION THAN INHIBITORY NEURONS IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE BUT ALSO OTHER TAUOPATHIES SUCH AS FTD-MAPT, PSP AND CBD. USING TRAP (TRANSLATING RIBOSOME AFFINITY PURIFICATION) AND A TAU MOUSE MODEL P301S, WE HAVE INVESTIGATED HOW SPECIFIC BRAIN REGIONS AND NEURONAL SUBTYPES ARE VULNERABLE TO TAU PATHOLOGY. WE FOCUSED ON TWO VULNERABLE BRAIN REGIONS—THE PREFRONTAL CORTEX (PFC) AND HIPPOCAMPUS—AND ONE RESISTANT REGION, THE PRIMARY VISUAL CORTEX. PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGEST THAT MEF2C, AN UPSTREAM REGULATOR, PLAYS A KEY ROLE IN MEDIATING THIS REGIONAL VULNERABILITY-RESILIENCE DICHOTOMY. IN THIS COMPETITIVE RENEWAL, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THESE MECHANISMS FURTHER, USING BOTH HUMAN POST-MORTEM BRAIN TISSUE, INNOVATIVE IN VITRO ASSAYS WITH NEURONAL IPSC MEF2C-KNOCK OUT (KO) AND A MEF2C KO MOUSE MODEL. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL INVESTIGATE MOLECULAR DIFFERENTIAL REGIONAL VULNERABILITY TO TAU PATHOLOGY USING STATE-OF THE-ART INTEGRATED SINGLE-CELL SEQUENCING AND SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS COMPARING TYPICAL ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND AN ATYPICAL FORM, POSTERIOR CORTICAL ATROPHY, WHICH STARTS TAU PATHOLOGY IN THE POSTERIOR AREAS IN THE BRAIN RATHER THAN THE MEDIAL TEMPORAL LOBE IN TYPICAL ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. IN SUMMARY, THIS PROJECT WILL VERTICALLY ADVANCE OUR KNOWLEDGE OF A FUNDAMENTAL ASPECT OF ALL NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS BY UNDERSTANDING THE MOLECULAR DRIVERS OF CELLULAR AND REGIONAL SUSCEPTIBILITY TO ACCUMULATION OF PROTEINOPATHIES SUCH AS TAUOPATHY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: STRUCTURE-BASED INVESTIGATION OF NEUROTRANSMITTERS AS MODIFIERS OF TAU AGGREGATION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT NEUROTRANSMITTERS (NTS) ARE CRUCIAL SIGNALING MOLECULES IN ANIMALS. BY ACTIVATING RECEPTORS IN NEURONAL CELL MEMBRANES, NTS PLAY WIDESPREAD ROLES IN SYNAPTIC SIGNALING. OUR PROJECT INVESTIGATES AN ADDITIONAL NOVEL ROLE FOR NTS IN MEDIATING PROTEIN AGGREGATION THROUGH DIRECT INTERACTIONS WITH CYTOSOLIC PROTEINS. THIS PROPOSAL ZEROS IN ON THE INVOLVEMENT OF MONOAMINERGIC NTS IN TAU PROTEIN AGGREGATION RELATING TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD). IN FORMER CRYOEM STUDIES, WE UNCOVERED A STRUCTURAL BASIS FOR TAU FIBRIL DISAGGREGATION BY NATURAL PRODUCT PHENOLS. BUILDING ON THAT RESEARCH, OUR STRUCTURE-ACTIVITY RELATIONSHIP STUDIES REVEALED THAT MONOAMINERGIC NTS ARE SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTORS TO TAU AGGREGATION. IN THIS REVISED R01 SUBMISSION, WE PROPOSE TO INVESTIGATE CONCENTRATION-DEPENDENT EFFECTS OF MONOAMINERGIC NTS ON TAU SEEDING—A DISEASE-RELEVANT MECHANISM BY WHICH FIBRILLAR AND OLIGOMERIC PROTEINS CATALYZE AGGREGATION. OUR AIMS TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT LEVELS OF SPECIFIC MONOAMINERGIC NTS HELP SHAPE PROTEIN AGGREGATION PROPENSITY, MAKING CERTAIN CELLS SELECTIVELY VULNERABLE. THE FOUNDATIONAL STUDIES PROPOSED HERE WILL HELP ESTABLISH A BIOPHYSICAL BASIS BY WHICH MONOAMINERGIC NTS INFLUENCE SEEDING THROUGH A FIBRIL DISAGGREGATION MECHANISM. CRUCIALLY, OUR EXPERIMENTS CONSIDER THE EFFECTS OF DISAGGREGASES ON BOTH FIBRIL AND OLIGOMER STRUCTURES, INVESTIGATING WHETHER FIBRIL DISAGGREGATION COULD LEAD TO OLIGOMER FORMATION. PRELIMINARY DATA INDICATE THAT NTS AND SYNTHETIC DISAGGREGASES ACTIVELY DISAGGREGATE OLIGOMERS AS WELL AS FIBRILS, PREVENTING THE ACCUMULATION OF EITHER MOLECULAR SPECIES. OUR EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES INTEGRATE CELL SEEDING ASSAYS, FIBRIL DISAGGREGATION MEASURES, AND ELECTRON MICROSCOPY TO DECIPHER THE MOLECULAR STRUCTURES OF FIBRIL COMPLEXES AND THE DETERMINANTS OF DISAGGREGASE POTENCY. STRUCTURAL, CELLULAR, AND BIOCHEMICAL MECHANISTIC STUDIES IN AIMS 1 AND 2 ARE COMPLEMENTED BY MEDICINAL CHEMISTRY APPROACHES IN AIM 3, WHICH FOCUS ON GENERATING SYNTHETIC DISAGGREGASES—PROVIDING AN OPPORTUNITY TO EXPAND UNDERSTANDING OF MOLECULAR DETERMINANTS THAT DEFINE DISAGGREGASE POTENCY. COLLECTIVELY, THIS WORK FILLS KEY GAPS IN KNOWLEDGE BY DEFINING WHICH NTS, PRECURSORS, AND METABOLITES FUNCTION AS TAU DISAGGREGASES, THE CONCENTRATION REGIMES IN WHICH THEY ARE EFFECTIVE, THE GOVERNING FEATURES OF THEIR POTENCY, AND THEIR BINDING SITES ON AD TAU FIBRILS. BY UNCOVERING BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS THAT REGULATE FIBRIL LOADS AND GENERATING NEW SYNTHETIC DISAGGREGASES, THIS RESEARCH LAYS THE FOUNDATION FOR MANAGING TAU AGGREGATION IN AD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: APOE AND REELIN INTERACTIONS IN ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY APOE Ε4, WHICH ENCODES APOLIPOPROTEIN E PROTEIN (APOE) Ε4, IS THE STRONGEST GENETIC RISK FACTOR FOR LATE-ONSET ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. IN THE BRAIN, APOE IS SYNTHESIZED AND LIPIDATED BY ASTROCYTES AND THEN SECRETED TO SHUTTLE CHOLESTEROL TO NEURONS. APOE BINDS TO RECEPTORS ON THE NEURON SURFACE, INCLUDING APOER2 (LRP8) AND VLDLR, AS WELL AS HEPARAN SULFATE (HS). LRP8, VLDLR, AND HS ALL BIND ANOTHER SECRETED PROTEIN, REELIN (ENCODED BY THE RELN GENE), WHICH PLAYS FUNDAMENTAL ROLES IN BRAIN DEVELOPMENT AND SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY. INTRIGUINGLY, RECENT ADVANCES INDICATE THAT REELIN SIGNALING IS A PROTECTIVE PATHWAY AGAINST NEURODEGENERATION. FOR EXAMPLE, THE RARE RELN-COLBOS VARIANT MAY PROTECT FROM THE PSEN1 E280A MUTATION. THIS CHARGE-INCREASING VARIANT H3447R HAS INCREASED AFFINITY FOR HS AND CAN INCREASE DOWNSTREAM DAB1 SIGNALING COMPARED WITH WILD-TYPE (WT) REELIN. SINGLE-NUCLEUS TRANSCRIPTOMICS HAS REVEALED THE LOSS OF RELN+ NEURONS IN THE ENTORHINAL CORTEX IN AD PATIENTS, REDUCING THIS POTENTIALLY PROTECTIVE MOLECULE. NOTABLY, REELIN-DAB1 SIGNALING MODIFIES ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE RISK IN APOE Ε44 INDIVIDUALS. REELIN PROTECTION HAS BEEN PROPOSED TO ACT THROUGH THE PATHWAY: REELIN- APOER2/VLDLR/HS-DAB1-GSK3B-PTAU, RESULTING IN REDUCED TAU PHOSPHORYLATION AND AGGREGATION. IN OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES USING A SPLIT LUCIFERASE ASSAY, WE FOUND THAT APOE Ε4 INHIBITS REELIN ACTIVATION WHILE APOE Ε3 HAS LITTLE EFFECT. FURTHERMORE, IN IPSC-DERIVED APOE Ε44 ORGANOIDS, WE FOUND THAT EXOGENOUS REELIN PROTEIN CAN REDUCE TAU PHOSPHORYLATION AND NEUROFILAMENT LIGHT CHAIN (NFL) SECRETION, A BIOMARKER OF NEURODEGENERATION. THESE EXCITING DATA, COUPLED WITH FACT THAT REELIN AND APOE BIND TO THE SAME RECEPTORS, HAVE LED US TO THE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS THAT APOE Ε4 COMPETES WITH REELIN FOR RECEPTOR AND HS BINDING, THEREBY REDUCING PROTECTIVE REELIN SIGNALING AND INCREASING ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE RISK. WE WILL TEST THIS OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS WITH A MULTI-SCALE, INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACH, WITH THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) STUDY RELN+ CELL ASSOCIATION WITH APOE Ε4 AND AD PATHOLOGY IN AD BRAINS; 2) CHARACTERIZE THE IMPACT OF REELIN ON AD MOLECULAR SIGNATURES, COMPARING APOE Ε44 VS APOE Ε33 IN 3D BRAIN ORGANOIDS WITH ISOGENIC BACKGROUND; 3) DEFINE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF HOW APOE Ε4 DIMINISHES REELIN SIGNALING. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL OFFER INSIGHTS INTO HOW APOE Ε4 INCREASES ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE RISK VIA INTERACTIONS WITH THE REELIN SIGNALING PATHWAY AND HAS THE POTENTIAL TO IDENTIFY NOVEL APPROACHES TO COUNTERACT APOE Ε4, WHICH IS PRESENT IN APPROXIMATELY HALF OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PLASTICITY RESERVE IN ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE: LONGITUDINAL INSIGHTS FROM PRECLINICAL AND PRODROMAL STAGES. - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE ATN FRAMEWORK MARKS A TURNING POINT IN ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (AD) RESEARCH, FOCUSING ON KEY BIOMARKERS LIKE AMYLOID, TAU, AND NEURODEGENERATION, WHICH ENHANCES DIAGNOSTIC METHODS AND DEEPENS OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE DISEASE. NONETHELESS, ACCURATELY IDENTIFYING THOSE ON THE CUSP OF COGNITIVE DECLINE, CRUCIAL FOR OPTIMIZING CLINICAL TRIALS, REMAINS A DIFFICULT TASK. EXISTING RESEARCH, ENCOMPASSING BOTH POSTMORTEM AND ANIMAL STUDIES, SHOWS THAT DIMINISHED NEUROPLASTICITY CAN BE DETECTED PRIOR TO THE EMERGENCE OF SYMPTOMS IN EARLY AD. WHILE THESE FINDINGS PROVIDE IMPORTANT INSIGHTS INTO NEUROPLASTICITY DEFICITS IN AD, THE LIMITATIONS OF THESE METHODOLOGIES IN LONGITUDINAL DISEASE MONITORING NECESSITATE THE EXPLORATION OF ALTERNATIVE RESEARCH APPROACHES. TRANSCRANIAL MAGNETIC STIMULATION (TMS) STEPS IN AS A VIABLE ALTERNATIVE, OFFERING NON-INVASIVE AND REPEATABLE NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL EVALUATIONS THAT CAN BE MORE ACCESSIBLE THAN TECHNIQUES LIKE PET IMAGING. OUR STUDY EMPLOYS A LONGITUDINAL, MULTI-MODAL APPROACH, INTEGRATING TMS WITH THE AIM OF TRACKING NEUROPLASTICITY CHANGES AND HOW THESE RELATE TO ATN BIOMARKERS, SUCH AS PLASMA AMYLOID BETA AND TAU, ALONGSIDE HIPPOCAMPAL NEURODEGENERATION. WE ARE POISED TO ASSESS THE EFFECTIVENESS OF A TMS-CENTRIC MODEL, COMPARE IT AGAINST A MODEL BASED ON BLOOD AND MRI BIOMARKERS, AND CONSIDER AN INTEGRATIVE MODEL THAT COMBINES BOTH. OUR GOAL IS TO ESTABLISH THE MOST RELIABLE TMS AND ATN BIOMARKERS TO PREDICT COGNITIVE DECLINE, IDENTIFYING CLEAR PREDICTOR THRESHOLDS. IN LINE WITH OPEN SCIENCE PRINCIPLES, ALL ANONYMIZED DATA FROM OUR RESEARCH WILL BE SHARED VIA OPENNEURO AND THE UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA RESEARCH DATA REPOSITORY. THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THIS STUDY STEMS FROM ITS POTENTIAL TO CONDUCT NON-INVASIVE, IN VIVO ASSESSMENTS OF AD-AFFECTED BRAIN FUNCTIONALITIES, SUBSTANTIALLY ENHANCING UNDERSTANDING OF THE DISEASE'S UNDERLYING PROCESSES AND PROGRESSION PATTERNS. THE UTILIZATION OF TMS AS A PREDICTIVE TOOL EMBODIES THE INNOVATIVE SPIRIT OF THIS RESEARCH, COMPLEMENTING AND POTENTIALLY EXPANDING THE PREDICTIVE CAPACITIES OF THE ESTABLISHED ATN FRAMEWORK. THIS STUDY IS DESIGNED TO FORTIFY LONGITUDINAL DISEASE MONITORING AND INSPIRE NEW THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES. THE COLLABORATIVE ETHOS OF THIS PROJECT, SUPPORTED BY EFFORTS TO SHARE DATA, UNDERSCORES ITS POTENTIAL TO INFLUENCE AND PROPEL THE ONGOING BATTLE AGAINST AD WITHIN THE RESEARCH COMMUNITY.

description: NEW BIOMARKERS FOR LATE DIAGNOSIS AND DIFFERENTIATION FROM AD DEMENTIA - PROJECT SUMMARY LIMBIC-PREDOMINANT AGE-RELATED TDP-43 ENCEPHALOPATHY (LATE) IS A RECENTLY CHARACTERIZED NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE DEFINED BY TDP-43 PROTEINOPATHY, PRIMARILY AFFECTING INDIVIDUALS AGED EIGHTY AND ABOVE. ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND LATE ARE BOTH COMMON BRAIN PATHOLOGIES ASSOCIATED WITH DEMENTIA AND BOTH PRESENT WITH AN AMNESTIC SYNDROME PRIMARILY AFFECTING MEMORY FUNCTION, OFTEN LEADING TO MISDIAGNOSIS. CURRENTLY, THERE ARE NO RELIABLE BIOMARKERS FOR PREMORTEM DIAGNOSIS OF LATE AND DIFFERENTIATING LATE FROM AD. ACCURATE DIAGNOSIS OF LATE, AD, AND OTHER ADRD'S IS CRITICAL FOR SELECTION OF PATIENTS FOR TARGETED THERAPIES. TO ADDRESS THIS URGENT UNMET NEED, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP FLUID BIOMARKERS FOR DIAGNOSING LATE AND DIFFERENTIATING LATE FROM AD BY DETECTING TDP-43 AND P-TAU EPITOPES IN CSF AND PLASMA; SPECIFICALLY, WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING AIMS: 1) DEVELOP TDP-43 SEED AMPLIFICATION ASSAY (SAA) AND TAU-SAA AS DIAGNOSTIC TESTS FOR LATE, 2) CHARACTERIZE THE EFFECTS OF CO-EXISTING TDP-43 PATHOLOGY ON TAU PATHOLOGY ACROSS DIFFERENT NFT BRAAK AND LATE STAGES, 3) DEVELOP NEW PHOSPHO-TAU FLUID BIOMARKERS FOR DIFFERENTIATING LATE FROM NORMAL CONTROLS AND AD DEMENTIA. WE WILL TEST OUR NEW BIOMARKERS WITH BOTH DISCOVERY AND VALIDATION COHORTS OF PREMORTEM CSF AND PLASMA SAMPLES. WE EXPECT THAT THE SUCCESSFUL IMPLEMENTATION OF THIS STUDY WILL NOT ONLY DEVELOP NOVEL DIAGNOSTIC TESTS FOR LATE, BUT ALSO FOR DIFFERENTIATION OF LATE FROM AD DEMENTIA. SUCCESSFUL TRANSLATION OF OUR FINDINGS FROM BENCH TO BEDSIDE WILL ADDRESS THESE URGENT UNMET MEDICAL NEEDS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A GLIMMER OF POSSIBILITY? GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS—INVESTIGATING THEIR INFLUENCE ON THE MIND, METABOLISM, AND EARLY RISK FOR ADRDS IN THE UNDERSTANDING AMERICA STUDY - ABSTRACT GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS AND RELATED THERAPIES (GLPS) ARE NOW USED BY MORE THAN 37 MILLION U.S. ADULTS, YET WHETHER THEY PREVENT, DELAY, OR ACCELERATE COGNITIVE DECLINE AND DEMENTIA IN REAL-WORLD POPULATIONS REMAINS UNKNOWN. TRIALS ARE SHORT-TERM AND HIGHLY SELECTED; MEDICAL RECORDS MISS THE GROWING SHARE OF USERS ACCESSING GLPS OUTSIDE TRADITIONAL CLINICAL CHANNELS; AND EXISTING SURVEYS LACK TIMELY GLP SURVEILLANCE AND OBJECTIVE PHENOTYPING. GLIMMER (GLP INFLUENCE ON METABOLISM AND MIND EXAMINED IN REAL-WORLD, REAL-TIME) IS A NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE, HIGH-FREQUENCY GLP SURVEILLANCE PLATFORM EMBEDDED IN THE UNDERSTANDING AMERICA STUDY (UAS), A PROBABILITY-BASED INTERNET PANEL OF ~14,000 U.S. ADULTS WITH 12+ YEARS OF COGNITIVE, BEHAVIORAL, AND CARDIOMETABOLIC DATA. GLIMMER ADDS THREE NEW DATA STREAMS: MONTHLY GLP SURVEILLANCE ACROSS ALL UAS PARTICIPANTS TO CAPTURE TREATMENT DYNAMICS IN NEAR REAL TIME, ANNUAL CORE SURVEYS OF IDENTIFIED USERS AND NON-USERS TO MEASURE SLOWER-CHANGING DOMAINS, AND DEEP PHENOTYPING WITH BODY COMPOSITION ASSESSMENT, CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITORING, AND DIETARY ECOLOGICAL MOMENTARY ASSESSMENT IN CONSENTING RESPONDENTS. TOGETHER, THESE CAPTURE NEW INITIATORS WITH PRE-TREATMENT BASELINES, TRACK FULL TREATMENT TRAJECTORIES, AND GENERATE THE SAMPLE SIZE, PROTOCOL EVIDENCE, AND PRELIMINARY DATA NEEDED FOR FUTURE RESEARCH. THE RESULTING PUBLICLY AVAILABLE RESOURCE WILL PROVIDE THE FIRST NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE, REAL-WORLD PLATFORM LINKING LIFECOURSE GLP USE TO COGNITIVE AGING AND ADRD RISK.

description: RURAL MICROVASCULAR CONTRIBUTIONS TO NEUROCOGNITIVE DECLINE - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT DEMENTIA RISK FACTORS, VASCULAR DISEASE BURDEN, AND PREMATURE MORTALITY ARE DISPROPORTIONATELY HIGH IN RURAL AMERICA, ESPECIALLY IN APPALACHIA AND THE MISSISSIPPI DELTA. YET, THE STRUCTURAL BRAIN CHANGES AND BIOMARKER PROFILES THAT UNDERLIE THESE DISPARITIES REMAIN ESSENTIALLY UNCHARACTERIZED BECAUSE RURAL COMMUNITIES LACK ACCESS TO ADVANCED NEURODIAGNOSTIC RESOURCES. WE ANTICIPATE THAT VASCULAR CONTRIBUTIONS TO COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA (VCID) PLAY A LARGE ROLE IN THE RISK FOR ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD) IN RURAL AREAS, WITH MIXED ALZHEIMER’S AND CEREBROVASCULAR PATHOLOGY REPRESENTING THE DOMINANT NEURODEGENERATIVE PROFILE IN OLDER ADULTS. SMALL VESSEL DISEASE (SVD), AN ACTIONABLE AND HIGHLY PREVALENT PATHOLOGY, IS TIGHTLY LINKED TO MODIFIABLE VASCULAR AND METABOLIC RISK FACTORS THAT ARE ELEVATED IN RURAL POPULATIONS. UNDERSTANDING HOW THESE RISK FACTORS SHAPE BRAIN AGING, PLASMA BIOMARKER CHANGES, AND COGNITIVE DECLINE IN RURAL AMERICA IS, THEREFORE, A CRITICAL PUBLIC HEALTH PRIORITY. OUR STUDY LEVERAGES THE UNIQUE INFRASTRUCTURE OF THE NHLBI-FUNDED RISK UNDERLYING RURAL AREAS LONGITUDINAL (RURAL) COHORT AND ITS NOVEL MOBILE EXAMINATION UNIT (MEU), WHICH HAS BROUGHT STATE-OF-THE-ART CLINICAL ASSESSMENTS AND IMAGING DIRECTLY TO REMOTE COMMUNITIES SINCE 2020. THE RURAL MICROVASCULAR CONTRIBUTIONS TO NEUROCOGNITIVE DECLINE (RURAL-MIND) STUDY WILL LEVERAGE AND EXTEND RURAL INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE ADRD SPACE BY DEPLOYING PORTABLE MRI NEUROIMAGING, ADVANCED AI-DRIVEN IMAGE ANALYTICS, REPEATED PLASMA BIOMARKER PROFILING, AND LONGITUDINAL COGNITIVE ASSESSMENTS IN 4,000 RURAL RESIDENTS ACROSS HIGH- AND LOWER-RISK COUNTIES CAREFULLY MATCHED ON POPULATION COMPOSITION AND ECONOMIC INDICATORS. THIS ECOLOGICALLY PAIRED DEPLOYMENT ENABLES REPRESENTATIVE SAMPLING OF RURAL REGIONS WITH DIFFERING CARDIOVASCULAR AND MORTALITY BURDENS, ENSURING A SCIENTIFICALLY RIGOROUS EVALUATION OF HOW ENVIRONMENTAL, COMMUNITY, AND BIOLOGICAL FACTORS INTERACT TO SHAPE DEMENTIA RISK THROUGH VCID AND ADRD. AIM 1 WILL CHARACTERIZE STRUCTURAL BRAIN CHANGES, INCLUDING ATROPHY, BRAIN AGE, AND MARKERS OF SVD, USING PORTABLE MRI, AND DETERMINE THEIR ASSOCIATIONS WITH COGNITION AND DEMENTIA. AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE HOW STRUCTURAL MRI ABNORMALITIES RELATE TO ANTECEDENT CHANGES IN PLASMA BIOMARKERS MEASURED ~5 YEARS APART (P-TAU, NFL, GFAP, INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES), REVEALING A CORRELATION BETWEEN NEURONAL INJURY, NEURODEGENERATION, AND VASCULAR BRAIN DAMAGE. AIM 3 WILL INTEGRATE VASCULAR/METABOLIC RISK FACTORS, MRI MARKERS, PLASMA BIOMARKERS, AND LONGITUDINAL COGNITION USING STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELING AND COUNTERFACTUAL MEDIATION TO IDENTIFY MECHANISTIC PATHWAYS DRIVING COGNITIVE DECLINE AND DEMENTIA. IMPACT: RURAL-MIND WILL GENERATE THE FIRST LARGE-SCALE, NEUROIMAGING-BASED DEMENTIA RISK MODEL IN RURAL AMERICA, USING METHODS SCALABLE TO ANY REMOTE OR RURAL SETTING. BY UNITING PORTABLE MRI, ADVANCED AI NEUROIMAGING, AND REPEATED BIOMARKER PROFILING WITHIN AN ECOLOGICALLY REPRESENTATIVE RURAL COHORT, RURAL-MIND WILL ILLUMINATE BIOLOGICAL PATHWAYS UNDERLYING RURAL COGNITIVE AGING AND PROVIDE ACTIONABLE TARGETS FOR EARLY DETECTION, PREVENTION, AND INTERVENTION STRATEGIES AIMED AT REDUCING ADRD DISPARITIES NATIONWIDE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT OF THERAPIES AGAINST PERTUSSIS - PROJECT SUMMARY IN THIS RENEWAL R01 PROJECT WE AIM TO ADVANCE NEW SOLUTIONS FOR PREVENTING AND TREATING PERTUSSIS (WHOOPING COUGH), A RESPIRATORY DISEASE THAT CONTINUES TO SPREAD DESPITE HIGH VACCINATION RATES. WE HAVE DEVELOPED 10 ANTIGEN MRNA VACCINES TO PROTECT AGAINST DIPHTHERIA, TETANUS AND PERTUSSIS AND EVALUATED THEM IN MODELS OF PERTUSSIS IN MICE AND RATS. BORDETELLA PERTUSSIS, THE PATHOGEN RESPONSIBLE FOR PERTUSSIS, IS ABLE TO INFECT INFANTS, CHILDREN, ADULTS, AND ELDERLY DESPITE VACCINATION. IN THIS PROJECT, WE AIM TO DEFINE VACCINE FORMULATIONS THAT BLOCK TRANSMISSION AND THEN USE THESE TARGETS TO DEVELOP ANTIBODY THERAPIES TO TREAT THE DISEASE OF PERTUSSIS IN ORDER TO DECREASE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY IN INFANTS AND DECREASE DISEASE IN OTHER POPULATIONS INCLUDING ELDERLY. A KEY FOCUS OF THE PROJECT IS TO USE THE FLEXIBILITY OF THE MRNA PLATFORM TO EVALUATE ESTABLISHED AND NOVEL ANTIGENS. TO ADDRESS THIS, WE WILL HARNESS OUR IN-HOUSE MRNA PLATFORM TO RAPIDLY PRODUCE AND TEST NOVEL ANTIGEN CANDIDATES, INCLUDING SPHB1, BRKA, VAG8, AND NOVEL ANTIGENS INCLUDING TOXIN SECRETION APPARATUS PROTEINS. THESE WILL BE DELIVERED AS MRNA VACCINES, PAIRED WITH “GENETIC ADJUVANTS” DESIGNED TO ENHANCE SPECIFIC TYPES OF IMMUNITY. WE WILL EVALUATE THESE CANDIDATES IN A NATURAL TRANSMISSION MODEL USING GREEN OLIVE BABOONS, WHICH MIMIC HUMAN PERTUSSIS TRANSMISSION MORE ACCURATELY THAN MICE OR RATS. OUR GOAL IS TO DEFINE WHICH ANTIGENS CAN GENERATE IMMUNE RESPONSES THAT BLOCK TRANSMISSION OF B. PERTUSSIS. IN PARALLEL, WE WILL DEVELOP MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES THAT CAN SERVE AS TREATMENTS FOR PERTUSSIS. WHILE SOME ANTIBODIES, SUCH AS THOSE TARGETING PERTUSSIS TOXIN, CAN REDUCE DISEASE SYMPTOMS, THEY DO NOT PREVENT TRANSMISSION. WE AIM TO DISCOVER NEW THERAPEUTIC ANTIBODIES THAT CAN BOTH TREAT ILLNESS AND HELP CLEAR THE INFECTION, REDUCING SPREAD AND IMPROVING RECOVERY IN VULNERABLE POPULATIONS, INCLUDING INFANTS, CHILDREN, AND OLDER ADULTS. THIS PROJECT WILL CREATE URGENTLY NEEDED TOOLS TO REDUCE PERTUSSIS DEATHS, IMPROVE PATIENT RECOVERY, AND LESSEN THE HEALTHCARE AND FINANCIAL BURDENS OF THE DISEASE. IN DOING SO, IT WILL ALSO ESTABLISH A NEW MODEL FOR COMBINING MRNA TECHNOLOGY AND ANTIBODY DISCOVERY TO COMBAT OTHER DISEASES SUCH AS PERTUSSIS AS WELL AS OTHER INFECTIOUS DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CHLAMYDIA ENHANCES GONOCOCCAL INFECTION THROUGH HOST INTERFERONS - PROJECT ABSTRACT CHLAMYDIA AND GONORRHEA ARE MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERNS, PARTICULARLY WITH THE EMERGENCE OF MULTIDRUG- RESISTANT NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE (NG) GLOBALLY. CHLAMYDIA-NG COINFECTIONS ARE COMMON AND OCCUR AT RATES FAR HIGHER THAN CAN BE ATTRIBUTED TO CHANCE ALONE, SUGGESTING A BIOLOGICAL INTERACTION BETWEEN THESE TWO PATHOGENS. INDEED, PEOPLE WITH CHLAMYDIA HAVE GREATER NG BURDENS THAN THOSE INFECTED WITH NG ALONE. WE RECENTLY ESTABLISHED A CRITICAL ROLE FOR TYPE I INTERFERONS (IFNS) IN PROMOTING NG SURVIVAL IN MICE. WE INITIALLY DISCOVERED THAT THE DURATION AND BURDEN OF NG VAGINAL COLONIZATION DECREASED SIGNIFICANTLY IN IFNAR-/- MICE, ANTI-IFNAR- TREATED MICE, AND IFNΕ-/- MICE. WE CHOSE TO EXAMINE IFNΕ BECAUSE IT IS HORMONALLY REGULATED AND IS ABUNDANT WITHIN THE FEMALE REPRODUCTIVE TRACK MUCOSA. INTRAVAGINAL DELIVERY OF RECOMBINANT TYPE I IFNS (IFNΒ OR IFNΕ) RESTORED NG COLONIZATION OF IFNΕ-/- MICE TO LEVELS SEEN IN WILDTYPE MICE. IT IS ESTABLISHED THAT NG SCAVENGES CMP- SIALIC ACID (CMP-SIA) FROM ITS HOST TO SIALYLATE ITS LIPOOLIGOSACCHARIDE (LOS). LOS SIALYLATION RENDERS NG RESISTANT TO KILLING BY CATHELICIDINS (LL-37 IN HUMANS AND ITS ORTHOLOG, MCRAMP, IN MICE). REMARKABLY, WE DISCOVERED THAT LOS SIALYLATION OF NG IN VIVO REQUIRES SIGNALING THROUGH IFNAR, THE TYPE I IFN RECEPTOR. LOSS OF IFNAR SIGNALING RESULTS IN NG LOS HYPO-SIALYLATION AND RAPID CLEARANCE BY MCRAMP. TYPE I IFNS ARE INDUCED WITH CHLAMYDIA INFECTION VIA THE CGAS/STING PATHWAY AND REDUCE THE CHLAMYDIAL BURDEN WITHIN THE MOUSE FEMALE GENITAL TRACT VIA IFNAR SIGNALING. TYPE II IFN (IFNΓ) IS ALSO INDUCED WITH CHLAMYDIAL INFECTION, AND CHLAMYDIA CLEARANCE REQUIRES IFNΓ-EXPRESSING CD4 CELLS. THIS PROPOSAL FOCUSES ON THE MOLECULAR PATHWAYS THAT PROMOTE NG INFECTION/DISEASE IN THE CONTEXT OF CHLAMYDIA-NG COINFECTION. WE WILL FOCUS ON SHARED IFN-STIMULATED GENE (ISG) PATHWAYS AND ENZYMES RESPONSIBLE FOR CMP-SIA BIOSYNTHESIS THAT DICTATE THE AVAILABILITY OF CMP-SIA TO NG. WE WILL ALSO STUDY COMPLEMENT RECEPTOR 3 (CR3), THE MAIN RECEPTOR MEDIATING NG INFECTION IN VIVO. PRIOR RESEARCH INDICATES A LINK BETWEEN CR3- AND IFN-MEDIATED HOST CELLULAR RESPONSES VIA TYPE I IFN-MEDIATED STING ACTIVATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CHLAMYDIA INFECTION DRIVES TYPE I AND TYPE II IFN SIGNALING AND ALTERS THE BIOLOGY OF THE GENITAL TRACT TO CREATE AN ENVIRONMENT THAT ENHANCES NG BURDEN. WE WILL USE HUMAN PRIMARY EPITHELIAL CELLS AND MICE TO MODEL NG, CHLAMYDIA, AND NG-CHLAMYDIA (CO)INFECTIONS TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS. AIM 1 WILL ASSESS THE ROLE OF IFNS IN CHLAMYDIAL ENHANCEMENT OF NG INFECTION OF THE GENITAL TRACT. THE IFN LANDSCAPE, INCLUDING IFN SIGNALING PATHWAYS AND THE CELL TYPES RESPONSIBLE FOR DRIVING AN IFN RESPONSE, WILL BE IDENTIFIED. WHETHER CR3 ENGAGEMENT BY CHLAMYDIA AND/OR NG CONTRIBUTES TO THE IFN MILIEU WILL BE DEFINED. AIM 2 WILL FOCUS ON THE EFFECT OF IFNS ON LOS SIALYLATION AND, IN TURN, NG SUSCEPTIBILITY TO KILLING BY CATHELICIDINS. WE WILL USE INNOVATIVE IN VIVO METABOLIC LABELING AND CU-FREE CLICK CHEMISTRY TO QUANTIFY THE CMP-SIA POOL AVAILABLE TO NG DURING (CO)INFECTION AND HOW THIS POOL IS REGULATED BY IFNS. THIS PROPOSAL FILLS AN IMPORTANT KNOWLEDGE GAP IN SEEKING TO ELUCIDATE THE REASON(S) FOR THE HEIGHTENED BURDEN OF NG IN THE FACE OF CHLAMYDIA COINFECTION.

description: ROLE OF HUMAN NK CELLS IN THE IMMUNE RESPONSE TO COCCIDIOIDES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  COCCIDIOIDES SPP., THE CAUSATIVE AGENT OF COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS, IS A DIMORPHIC ENVIRONMENTAL  FUNGUS FOUND IN THE SOUTHWESTERN AND WESTERN UNITED STATES AND IN CENTRAL AND SOUTH AMERICA  THAT CAN CAUSE A RANGE OF INFECTIOUS PHENOTYPES IN HUMANS, RANGING FROM ASYMPTOMATIC  PULMONARY INFECTION TO LIFE-THREATENING DISSEMINATED DISEASE. THE INCIDENCE AND RANGE OF THIS  PATHOGEN ARE EXPANDING, SO THE EARLY (INNATE) IMMUNOLOGICAL BASIS FOR DIFFERENTIAL HOST OUTCOMES  NEEDS TO BE BETTER UNDERSTOOD.  INNATE IMMUNE CELLS, INCLUDING NATURAL KILLER (NK) CELLS, EXPRESS GERMLINE-ENCODED RECEPTORS,  SOME OF WHICH SENSE FUNGAL CELL WALL CARBOHYDRATES. COCCIDIOIDES EXPRESSES CARBOHYDRATE  STRUCTURES DURING ITS COMPLEX DIMORPHIC LIFE CYCLE. IN THIS KATZ R01 PROPOSAL, I WILL MAP AT SINGLE CELL RESOLUTION THE COCCIDIOIDES LUNG GRANULOMA IN PATIENT SPECIMENS, THEN MODEL ACUTE  COCCIDIOIDES INFECTION IN HUMAN LUNG TISSUE EXPLANTS TO UNDERSTAND BOTH THE CHRONIC GRANULOMA  AND THE EARLIEST INTERACTIONS BETWEEN FUNGUS, EPITHELIAL CELLS, AND INNATE IMMUNE CELLS (AIM 1).  NK CELLS HAVE BEEN FOUND TO SENSE AND INHIBIT THE GROWTH OF SEVERAL FUNGI, INCLUDING COCCIDIOIDES,  AND THIS PROJECT PLANS TO DEFINE THE IMPLICATED COCCIDIOIDES LIGANDS AND NK CELL RECEPTORS BY  STUDYING HUMAN NK CELL ACTIVATION USING A VARIETY OF COCCIDIOIDES PREPARATIONS; BLOCKING,  OVEREXPRESSING, AND KNOCKING DOWN NK RECEPTORS; AND USING CRISPR/CAS9 TO GENERATE  COCCIDIOIDES MUTANTS DEFECTIVE IN CARBOHYDRATE PROCESSING (AIM 2).   FINALLY, THE PROPOSED WORK INVOLVES CONDUCTING AN IMMUNE PROFILING STUDY OF COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS  PATIENTS ACROSS THE SPECTRUM OF DISEASE TO IDENTIFY NK CELL PHENOTYPIC CORRELATES OF SEVERE OR  DISSEMINATED COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS (AIM 3).  IN UNDERSTANDING THE NK RESPONSE AND HOST DETERMINANTS OF PROTECTION AGAINST COCCIDIOIDES, THIS  PROJECT WILL GENERATE THE INFORMATION NECESSARY TO UNDERSTAND DIFFERENTIAL PATIENT SUSCEPTIBILITY TO  THIS FUNGUS. IT WILL REVEAL TRACTABLE TARGETS FOR AUGMENTING THE HOST RESPONSE. FOR EXAMPLE, SUGARS,  PROTEINS, GENES, OR PATHWAYS ESSENTIAL FOR NK CELL-MEDIATED INNATE IMMUNITY TO COCCIDIOIDES  COULD BE TARGETED FOR ENHANCED FUNCTION BY SMALL MOLECULES OR CELLULAR INFUSIONS IN EXPOSED,  INFECTED, AND IMMUNOCOMPROMISED PATIENTS. FINALLY, THE APPROACHES AND RESULTS FROM THIS  PROPOSAL WILL PROVIDE A ROADMAP TO SIMILAR STUDIES OF OTHER HUMAN PATHOGENIC FUNGI.

description: MECHANISM OF THE SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION ACROSS THE BACTERIAL CELL ENVELOPE - PROJECT SUMMARY ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE IS AN URGENT THREAT TO PUBLIC HEALTH, PARTICULARLY AMONG GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA, DUE TO THEIR MULTILAYERED CELL ENVELOPE STRUCTURE, WHICH INCLUDES THE OUTER MEMBRANE (OM). THE OM OUTER LEAFLET IS COMPOSED OF LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDE (LPS) MOLECULES THAT MAKE THE OM IMPERMEABLE TO VARIOUS COMPOUNDS, INCLUDING CLINICALLY USED ANTIBIOTICS. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO GAIN A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW BACTERIA BUILD AND MAINTAIN HOMEOSTASIS OF THE OM TO AID ANTIBIOTIC DISCOVERY. BACTERIAL ENVELOPE STRESS RESPONSES ARE SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION PATHWAYS THAT CONFER SIGNIFICANT INTRINSIC RESISTANCE TO ANTIBIOTICS, IMMUNE FACTORS, AND OTHER BIOLOGICAL AGENTS TARGETING THE ENVELOPE. THEY ACHIEVE THIS BY MITIGATING DAMAGE AND INHIBITING THE PENETRATION OR ACTIVITY OF THESE AGENTS. DESPITE THEIR IMPORTANCE, THE MOLECULAR SIGNALS AND ACTIVATION MECHANISMS OF STRESS RESPONSES REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD BECAUSE OF THE COMPLEXITY OF ENVELOPE BIOGENESIS. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO ELUCIDATE HOW THE REGULATOR OF CAPSULE SYNTHESIS (RCS) STRESS RESPONSE MONITORS OM INTEGRITY AND PROMOTES OM HOMEOSTASIS. RCS IS ONE OF THE MOST COMPLEX STRESS RESPONSES IN BACTERIA AND CAN TRANSDUCE THE STRESS SIGNAL FROM THE CELL SURFACE TO THE CYTOPLASM. DISRUPTIONS IN THE LPS LAYER AT THE CELL SURFACE, INCLUDING THOSE CAUSED BY CATIONIC ANTIMICROBIAL PEPTIDES (CAMPS) AND LAST-RESORT ANTIBIOTICS LIKE POLYMYXIN B, HAVE LONG BEEN KNOWN TO STRONGLY ACTIVATE RCS. THROUGH GENETIC ANALYSIS, IN VITRO AND IN VIVO BIOCHEMICAL APPROACHES, AND MOLECULAR DYNAMICS SIMULATIONS, WE AIM TO IDENTIFY THE MOLECULAR SIGNAL AND MECHANISM THAT ACTIVATES THE SENSORY PROTEIN RCSF, AND DETERMINE HOW THE STRESS SIGNAL IS TRANSDUCED ACROSS THE MULTILAYERED CELL ENVELOPE. THROUGH OUR RESEARCH, WE WILL PROVIDE A MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE WELL-ESTABLISHED ROLE OF RCS IN RESISTING CAMPS, AND FACILITATE STUDIES ON THE ROLE OF RCS IN IMMUNE EVASION, HOST SURVIVAL, AND PATHOGENESIS. MORE BROADLY, STUDIES OF RCS WILL PROVIDE A NEW MECHANISTIC PARADIGM FOR A POTENTIALLY WIDELY UTILIZED MECHANISM OF ENVELOPE STRESS RESPONSES AND HOW BACTERIA USE THEM TO PROMOTE ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE.

description: MECHANISMS OF LIPOPROTEIN SORTING AND SECRETION IN BORRELIA SPIROCHETES - ABSTRACT BACTERIAL PROTEIN SECRETION IS A FUNDAMENTAL PHYSIOLOGICAL PROCESS THAT GENERATES THE CELL ENVELOPE AND MAINTAINS ITS INTEGRITY THROUGHOUT THE BACTERIAL LIFE CYCLE. IN BACTERIAL PATHOGENS, A VARIETY OF PROTEIN SECRETION SYSTEMS HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO DEPLOY IMPORTANT VIRULENCE FACTORS TO THE BACTERIAL SURFACE, INTO THE MILIEU, OR EVEN DIRECTLY INTO EUKARYOTIC CELLS OR OTHER BACTERIA. BORRELIA SPIROCHETES, THE CAUSATIVE AGENTS OF TICK-BORNE LYME DISEASE AND RELAPSING FEVER, HAVE A UNIQUE DOUBLE-MEMBRANE ENVELOPE WITH PERIPLASMIC FLAGELLA. THE BORRELIA SURFACE LACKS LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDE AND IS INSTEAD COVERED BY ABUNDANT, IMMUNODOMINANT AND SEROTYPE-DEFINING SURFACE LIPOPROTEINS THAT SERVE AS LINCHPINS FOR TRANSMISSION AND PATHOGENESIS. A RECENT STUDY HAS SHOWN THAT TWO THIRDS OF THE ABOUT 130 LIPOPROTEINS EXPRESSED BY THE LYME DISEASE BACTERIUM BORRELIA BURGDORFERI LOCALIZE TO THE SURFACE. THEREFORE, B. BURGDORFERI IS A PERFECT MODEL ORGANISM FOR INVESTIGATIONS INTO THE SECRETION OF BACTERIAL SURFACE LIPOPROTEINS.  SEVERAL SEMINAL STUDIES HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT (I) BORRELIA SURFACE LIPOPROTEIN SECRETION DETERMINANTS COMMONLY LOCALIZE TO N-TERMINAL DISORDERED TETHER REGIONS OF THE MATURE LIPOPROTEINS, (II) TRANSLOCATION THROUGH THE OUTER MEMBRANE CAN INITIATE AT A LIPOPROTEIN'S C TERMINUS AND REQUIRES AN AT LEAST PARTIALLY UNFOLDED CONFORMATION, AND (III) BORRELIA SURFACE LIPOPROTEINS ARE ULTIMATELY ANCHORED IN THE SURFACE LEAFLET OF THE OUTER MEMBRANE BILAYER. THESE DATA SUPPORT THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THE BORRELIA SURFACE LIPOPROTEIN SECRETION PATHWAY INCLUDES A PERIPLASMIC MECHANISM THAT PREVENTS PREMATURE FOLDING OF SURFACE LIPOPROTEIN AND AN OUTER MEMBRANE TRANSLOCON COMPLEX THAT ALLOWS FOR THE FLIPPING OF LIPOPROTEINS FROM THE PERIPLASM TO THE SURFACE.  THIS PROPOSAL WILL TEST THE ABOVE HYPOTHESIS BY IDENTIFYING AND MECHANISTICALLY DEFINING THE COMPONENTS OF THE B. BURGDORFERI SURFACE LIPOPROTEIN SECRETION PATHWAY. AIM 1 WILL BUILD ON RECENT CRISPRI GENE SILENCING DATA AND EMPLOY CRYO-EM, SITE-DIRECTED MUTAGENESIS, AND QUANTITATIVE PROTEOMICS TO DETERMINE THE STRUCTURE- FUNCTION RELATIONSHIPS OF A B. BURGDORFERI OM PROTEIN SHOWN TO FACILITATE TRANSLOCATION OF LIPOPROTEINS FROM THE PERIPLASM TO THE SURFACE. AIM 2 WILL USE CRISPRI, X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY, SITE-DIRECTED MUTAGENESIS, AND QUANTITATIVE PROTEOMICS TO CHARACTERIZE THE PERIPLASMIC PROTEINS DELIVERING SURFACE LIPOPROTEINS FROM THE INNER MEMBRANE TO THE OM. AIM 3 WILL LEVERAGE TIME-LAPSE SINGLE-CELL MICROSCOPY TO TRACK LIPOPROTEIN SORTING AND SECRETION PATHWAY PROTEINS THROUGHOUT THE CELL CYCLE. THIS WILL DEFINE THE SEQUESTRATION OF THE B. BURGDORFERI LIPOPROTEOME BY BOTH PATHWAYS IN SPACE AND TIME, THEREBY ELUCIDATING THE MECHANISTIC UNDERPINNINGS OF SEQUENTIAL CHANGES IN SURFACE LIPOPROTEINS THAT ENABLES DISSEMINATED AND CHRONIC INFECTION.  TOGETHER, THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL USE NOVEL APPROACHES TO FURTHER ELUCIDATE HOW EMERGING PATHOGENS OF GLOBAL IMPORTANCE GENERATE AND MAINTAIN THEIR INTERFACE WITH THE HOST. THIS WILL ULTIMATELY YIELD BETTER TOOLS FOR DIAGNOSTICS AND IMPROVED STRATEGIES FOR PREVENTION AND TREATMENT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATION OF HUMAN IMMUNE RESPONSES IN ACUTE RICKETTSIOSES: TOWARDS DEVELOPMENT OF HOST RESPONSE-BASED DIAGNOSTICS - PROJECT SUMMARY SPOTTED FEVER GROUP RICKETTSIOSES (SFGR) ARE TICK-BORNE BACTERIAL DISEASES ENDEMIC TO ALL CONTINENTS SAVE ANTARCTICA. THEY CAN CAUSE SEVERE FEBRILE ILLNESS (SFI) THAT REQUIRES HOSPITALIZATION. IN THE US, THE HIGHEST INCIDENCE OF SFGR IS IN SOUTH-CENTRAL AND SOUTHEASTERN STATES. OUR COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH IN SRI LANKA AND IN TANZANIA HAS IDENTIFIED SFGR AS THE CAUSE OF ILLNESS IN NEARLY 10% OF PATIENTS PRESENTING TO HOSPITAL WITH SFI. THE RICKETTSIA SPP. THAT CAUSE SFGR IN SRI LANKA, TANZANIA, AND THE US—THE THREE SETTINGS CONTRIBUTING TO THIS PROJECT—ARE AT ONCE POTENTIALLY FATAL YET ALSO HIGHLY TREATABLE IF THE DISEASE IS RECOGNIZED AND TREATED WITH TETRACYCLINE ANTIBIOTICS IN THE FIRST FIVE DAYS OF ILLNESS. HOWEVER, THE CRUCIAL PROBLEM IS THAT SFGR TREATMENT DELAYS BEYOND FIVE DAYS OF ILLNESS ARE COMMON WORLDWIDE, INCLUDING IN OUR THREE SETTINGS. THIS DELAYED RECOGNITION STEMS FROM THE NON-SPECIFIC CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS OF SFGR, WHICH INCLUDE FEVER, MALAISE, HEADACHE, AND USUALLY A RASH; DELAYED RECOGNITION ALSO STEMS FROM THE LACK OF ACCURATE DIAGNOSTIC TESTS THAT CAN BE RUN ON READILY OBTAINABLE SPECIMENS (I.E., BLOOD SAMPLES AS OPPOSED TO SKIN BIOPSIES) IN THE INITIAL DAYS OF ILLNESS. THIS DIAGNOSTIC CHALLENGE LEADS TO UNDER-TREATMENT AND EXCESS PREVENTABLE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY DUE TO SFGR. THROUGH CHARACTERIZATION OF THE HUMAN HOST IMMUNE RESPONSE TO SFGR IN THESE THREE DISTINCT SETTINGS (AIM 1) AND THROUGH DEVELOPMENT OF TRANSCRIPTOMIC AND PROTEOMIC HOST RESPONSE DIAGNOSTIC CLASSIFIERS (AIMS 2 AND 3), THE PROJECT SEEKS TO ADVANCE THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF IMPROVING TIMELY RECOGNITION OF SFGR IN THE INITIAL DAYS OF ILLNESS. SFG RICKETTSIA HAVE A TROPISM FOR INFECTING VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL CELLS AND CAUSING A VASCULITIS- LIKE INFLAMMATORY PROCESS CHARACTERIZED BY ENDOTHELIAL ACTIVATION AND VASCULAR PERMEABILITY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE HOST RESPONSE TO SFGR IS SUFFICIENTLY DISTINCT FROM OTHER COMMON SFI, ALLOWING FOR DIAGNOSTIC HOST BIOMARKERS TO BE IDENTIFIED IN THE ACUTE PHASE OF ILLNESS—BIOMARKERS IDENTIFIED BY WHOLE BLOOD MRNA GENE EXPRESSION ANALYSIS (AIM 2) OR BY PLASMA AND EXTRACELLULAR VESICLE PROTEOMIC ANALYSIS (AIM 3). THE EXPERIMENTS IN AIM 1 ADDRESS A RELATED AND IMPORTANT QUESTION: WHETHER THE HUMAN IMMUNE RESPONSE TO SFGR IS CONSERVED ACROSS SPECIES AND GEOGRAPHIC LOCATIONS. ANSWERING THIS QUESTION WILL DETERMINE WHETHER HOST RESPONSE-BASED DIAGNOSTICS FOR SFGR WILL BE GLOBALLY GENERALIZABLE OR WILL REQUIRE SETTING/SPECIES-SPECIFIC OPTIMIZATION. TO ACHIEVE THESE AIMS, WE WILL USE OUR UNIQUE BIOREPOSITORY OF OVER 3,000 SFI PATIENTS, ALLOCATED BETWEEN DERIVATION AND VALIDATION SETS. THIS LARGE REPOSITORY INCLUDES APPROXIMATELY 200 SFGR CASES ENROLLED IN COHORTS FROM SRI LANKA, TANZANIA, AND THE US. THE VALIDATION SET WILL ALSO INCLUDE PROSPECTIVE SFI ENROLLMENT AND SFGR CASE ACCRUAL IN NORTH CAROLINA, A HIGHLY ENDEMIC REGION FOR SFGR IN THE US. COLLECTIVELY, THIS PROJECT IS WELL-POSITIONED TO MAKE IMPORTANT DISCOVERIES REGARDING THE HUMAN IMMUNE RESPONSE TO RICKETTSIOSES. THESE DISCOVERIES WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF HOST RESPONSE-BASED DIAGNOSTIC BIOMARKERS TO ADDRESS KEY GAPS IN THE TIMELY RECOGNITION AND MANAGEMENT OF THIS NEGLECTED SERIOUS BACTERIAL INFECTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ELUCIDATION OF MECHANISMS UNDERLYING INFLAMMATORY ARTHRITIS INDUCED BY IMMUNE CHECKPOINT INHIBITORS - PROJECT SUMMARY IMMUNE CHECKPOINT INHIBITORS (ICIS), PARTICULARLY PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH-1 INHIBITORS (PD-1I), HAVE REVOLUTIONIZED CANCER TREATMENT, AND PD-1I-BASED THERAPIES ARE WIDELY USED IN PATIENTS WITH MALIGNANCIES. HOWEVER, ICIS OFTEN CAUSE IMMUNE-RELATED ADVERSE EVENTS (IRAES), INCLUDING INFLAMMATORY ARTHRITIS (ICI-ARTHRITIS). STEROIDS, THE FIRSTLINE IRAE TREATMENT, SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCE ICI ANTITUMOR EFFICACY. THEREFORE, MECHANISM-ROOTED IMMUNOSUPPRESSION IS CRITICAL IN MANAGING ICI-ARTHRITIS; HOWEVER, ITS MECHANISM IS POORLY UNDERSTOOD. WE UNCOVERED THAT CXCR3HI CD8+ T CELLS ARE CLONALLY EXPANDED IN THE SYNOVIAL FLUID (SF) OF ICI-ARTHRITIS PATIENTS. FURTHER, THESE CELLS EXHIBIT HIGH EXPRESSION OF TISSUE-RESIDENT MEMORY (TRM) CELL-ASSOCIATED MOLECULES. IN PARALLEL, WE OBSERVED THAT TYPE II CHICKEN COLLAGEN (CII)-PRIMED MICE DEVELOP DE NOVO INFLAMMATORY ARTHRITIS UPON PD-1 INHIBITION (HEREAFTER REFERRED TO AS PD-1I ARTHRITIS). THESE MICE RECAPITULATE HUMAN PD-1I ARTHRITIS FROM CLINICAL, HISTOLOGICAL, AND IMMUNOLOGICAL PERSPECTIVES. NOTABLY, CD69HI CD103HI CD8+ T CELLS, TERMED TRM-LIKE CELLS, ARE EXPANDED IN THE JOINTS AS WELL AS CII-DRAINING LYMPH NODES IN PD-1I ARTHRITIS MICE. BASED ON OUR PRELIMINARY DATA, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT PD-1 INHIBITION BREAKS PERIPHERAL TOLERANCE OF INTRAARTICULAR TRMLIKE CELLS, INDUCING ACTIVATION AND EXPANSION OF TRM-LIKE CELLS, RESULTING IN INFLAMMATORY ARTHRITIS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL ASSESS THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH PD-1 INHIBITION PROMOTES TRM-LIKE CELL-DRIVEN ARTHRITIS USING OUR NOVEL PD-1I ARTHRITIS MODEL. FIRST, WE WILL IDENTIFY THE CELLULAR, MOLECULAR, AND EPIGENETIC CHARACTERISTICS OF TRM-LIKE CELLS IN JOINTS AND CII-DRAINING LYMPH NODES. NEXT, WE WILL DETERMINE THEIR KINETICS, DEFINE THE MECHANISM BY WHICH PD-1 INHIBITION MEDIATES THEIR ACTIVATION IN VITRO. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER TRM-LIKE CELLS ARE SUFFICIENT TO INDUCE INFLAMMATORY ARTHRITIS BY ADOPTIVE T CELL TRANSFER EXPERIMENT. THIS PROPOSAL IS IMPORTANT AS THE RESULTS WILL UNVEIL THE MECHANISMS OF PD-1I ARTHRITIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNCOVERING THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH CAMK2B LOSS PROMOTES METASTASIS AND IMMUNE SUPPRESSION IN PANCREATIC CANCER - PROJECT SUMMARY OUR PROPOSED RESEARCH EMPLOYS INNOVATIVE AND NOVEL GENETICALLY ENGINEERED MOUSE MODELS OF METASTATIC PANCREATIC CANCER TO ELUCIDATE MECHANISMS OF METASTASIS BOTH WITHIN TUMOR CELLS AND WITH THEIR INTERACTIONS WITH THE HOST. PANCREATIC CANCER PATIENTS ARE OFTEN NOT DIAGNOSED UNTIL METASTASES HAVE ALREADY FORMED, WITH THE VAST MAJORITY OF PATIENTS PRESENTING WITH OLIGOMETASTATIC DISEASE. THE STUDY OF METASTATIC DRIVERS HAS BEEN LIMITED BY CURRENT GENETICALLY ENGINEERED MOUSE MODELS, WHICH SHOW LOW METASTATIC COMPETENCY. WE HAVE IDENTIFIED CALCIUM/CALMODULIN DEPENDENT PROTEIN KINASE II BETA (CAMK2B), A CALCIUM-RESPONSIVE KINASE, AS A METASTASIS SUPPRESSING GENE WHOSE LOSS ENHANCES TUMOR METASTASIS AND CREATES A HIGHLY IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT (TME). GENETICALLY ENGINEERED MICE WITH TUMOR CELL-SPECIFIC CAMK2B KNOCKOUT FORM METASTASES IN 80% OF ANIMALS AND PRESENT WITH >25 METASTATIC LESIONS PER MOUSE, LEADING TO A DRAMATIC REDUCTION IN OVERALL SURVIVAL. ADDITIONALLY, THESE ANIMALS HAVE AN IMMUNOSUPPRESSED METASTATIC NICHE THAT IS DOMINATED BY PRO-TUMOR M2 MACROPHAGES AND LACKS CD8+ T AND NK EFFECTOR IMMUNE CELLS. UNBIASED SEQUENCING APPROACHES REVEALED THAT DELETION OF CAMK2B ENHANCES THE EXPRESSION OF LYSYL OXIDASE (LOX) FAMILY MEMBERS AND CGAS-STING SIGNALING COMPONENTS, WHICH WE PROPOSE MEDIATE THE METASTATIC AND IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE PHENOTYPES, RESPECTIVELY. AIM 1 WILL FOCUS ON EXPLORING TUMOR CELL INTRINSIC MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH CAMK2B-DELETION PROMOTES TUMOR CELL METASTASIS BY DETERMINING THE EFFECT OF THIS LOSS ON EPITHELIAL CELL IDENTITY AND PLASTICITY AND WILL ATTEMPT TO BLOCK THIS HIGHLY PLASTIC STATE THROUGH INHIBITION OF LOX SIGNALING. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE THE ROLE OF TUMOR CELL CAMK2B LOSS IN ORGANIZING A CONGENIAL METASTATIC NICHE BY FOSTERING IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE M2 MACROPHAGE CELL RECRUITMENT AND WILL SEEK TO EXPLOIT VULNERABILITIES IN CGAS-STING SIGNALING TO REVERT THIS IMMUNOSUPPRESSION. THUS, OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT TUMOR CELL CAMK2B LOSS ENHANCES PDAC METASTASIS BY ALTERING TUMOR CELL INTRINSIC MECHANISMS OF DISSEMINATION (AIM 1) AND BY CREATING A FAVORABLE METASTATIC NICHE THROUGH INTERACTIONS WITH THE HOST MICROENVIRONMENT (AIM 2). THE PROPOSED AIMS WILL DELINEATE HOW LOSS OF CAMK2B SIGNALING NETWORKS PROMOTE PANCREATIC CANCER METASTASIS AND ASSESS THE EFFICACY OF LOX-TARGETED AND STING- TARGETED THERAPIES TO BLOCK METASTASIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LEADER CELL MECHANICS AS PRIMARY REGULATORS OF COLLECTIVE TUMOR INVASION - PROJECT SUMMARY METASTASIS CONTINUES TO BE THE PRIMARY CAUSE OF MORTALITY IN BREAST CANCER PATIENTS. DESPITE NEW THERAPIES AND DIAGNOSTICS, MEDIAN OVERALL SURVIVAL HAS ONLY INCREASED BY 1.5 YEARS OVER THE PAST 3 DECADES. OVER 90% OF PATIENTS WITH METASTATIC DISEASE HAVE CIRCULATING TUMOR CELLS THAT INVADE AS CLUSTERS, YET MOST METASTATIC STUDIES FOCUS ON UNDERSTANDING HOW CIRCULATING TUMOR CELLS INVADE AS INDIVIDUAL CELLS. COLLECTIVE INVASION OR METASTASIS IS A TYPE OF CELL MIGRATION WHERE GROUPS OF TUMOR CELLS MOVE TOGETHER IN A COORDINATED FASHION. DURING COLLECTIVE INVASION, A FEW CELLS AT THE FRONT (I.E. LEADER CELLS) DEFINE THE LEADING EDGE, INTEGRATE SIGNALS FROM THE EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX (ECM) ENVIRONMENT AND SEND SIGNALS TO NEIGHBORING (FOLLOWER) CELLS. OUR WORK DEMONSTRATE LEADER CELLS MUST ARRIVE (OR POLARIZE) AT THE FRONT TO BEGIN INVASION. THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT CONTAINS MANY MECHANICAL CUES INCLUDING MATRIX ARCHITECTURE AND FLUID FLOW GRADIENTS, YET HOW THESE CUES IMPACT INVASION NOR LEADER CELL RESPONSE IS NOT FULLY UNDERSTOOD. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO EXPERIMENTALLY TEST HOW MECHANICAL ECM CUES LINK TO LEADER CELL POLARIZATION, AND ELUCIDATE THE LEADER CELL MECHANICS RESPONSIBLE FOR SENSING, INTERPRETING, AND COORDINATING COLLECTIVE INVASION. OUR HYPOTHESIS IS THAT LEADER CELL BIOPHYSICS ARE THE PRIMARY SENSORS OF MECHANICAL MATRIX CUES, MAKING LEADER CELLS THE PRIMARY DRIVERS OF COLLECTIVE INVASION. WE WILL ANSWER OUR HYPOTHESIS WITH THE FOLLOWING AIMS: (1): WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW FLUID FLOW AND MATRIX ARCHITECTURE RESULT IN DIRECTIONAL COLLECTIVE INVASION, MEDIATED BY LEADER CELL POLARIZATION (2): WE WILL INTERROGATE MECHANICAL RESPONSE OF THE COLLECTIVE CLUSTER AND THE LEADER CELLS SEPARATELY (3): WE WILL ELUCIDATE LEADER CELL MECHANOSENSORS AND ASSOCIATED PATHWAYS GOVERNING INVASION. IN OUR 3D MICROPHYSIOLOGICAL MODELS, WE WILL INCORPORATE DECELLULARIZED MATRIX (DECM) FROM PRIMARY BREAST CANCER TUMORS WHICH PROVIDES AN ACCURATE PRESENTATION OF NATIVE ECM COMPOSITION. FOR CELL SOURCE, WE WILL CULTURE PRIMARY TUMOR ORGANOID CLUSTERS. WE WILL INDUCE DYNAMIC MECHANICAL CUES FLUID FLOW AND MATRIX ARCHITECTURE, AND PERFORM LIVE-CELL IMAGING TO QUANTIFY CHANGES IN INVASION. ALSO, WE WILL QUANTIFY CHANGES IN LEADER CELL MECHANICAL RESPONSE BY MEASURING MATRIX DEFORMATION RATES AND TRACTION FORCES. WE WILL INTERROGATE VINCULIN FOCAL ADHESIONS AS A CELL-MATRIX LINKER CONNECTING LEADERS TO ECM. BASED ON OUR SINGLE CELL SEQUENCING WORK, WE WILL PROBE TOP DIFFERENTIALLY EXPRESSED MARKER, DESMOPLAKIN, AS A POTENTIAL LEADER CELL MECHANOSENSOR TO DIRECT INVASION. WE WILL PERFORM LOSS-OF-FUNCTION STUDIES WITH SYNGENEIC ORTHOTOPIC BREAST TRANSPLANT MODELS. VERTEBRATE ANIMAL MODELS ARE ESSENTIAL FOR THIS PROJECT BECAUSE THEY ENABLE IN VIVO INVESTIGATION OF COMPLEX INTERACTIONS OF TUMOR LEADER CELL MECHANICS WITH THE NATIVE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT THAT CLOSELY RECAPITULATE KEY FEATURES OF HUMAN BREAST CANCER. BY INVESTIGATING COLLECTIVE INVASION MECHANICS, WE WILL CONTRIBUTE NEW PERSPECTIVES WHICH CAN BRING NEW APPROACHES FOR THERAPY DESIGN. FURTHER, WE WILL IDENTIFY NEW MECHANICAL SIGNATURES OF COLLECTIVELY INVADING TUMOR CLUSTERS, WHICH CAN ADD TO MORE UNIVERSAL BIOMARKERS THAT CAN DIAGNOSE OR PREDICT CLUSTER-BASED METASTASIS IN PATIENTS.

description: DEVELOPMENTAL GENETICS OF TOOTH NUMBER VARIATION IN STICKLEBACKS - PROJECT SUMMARY THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY THE GENETIC CIRCUITRY REGULATING TOOTH FORMATION AND REPLACEMENT. TEETH HAVE CLASSICALLY BEEN USED AS A MODEL TO STUDY ORGANOGENESIS, AS TEETH, LIKE MOST ORGANS, DEVELOP THROUGH RECIPROCAL EPITHELIAL-MESENCHYMAL INTERACTIONS. FURTHERMORE, 30 PERCENT OF PEOPLE WORLDWIDE OVER THE AGE OF 65 HAVE NO NATURAL TEETH. THUS, KNOWLEDGE OF THE GENETIC BASIS OF TOOTH FORMATION AND REPLACEMENT HAS RELEVANCE BOTH FOR UNDERSTANDING ORGANOGENESIS, AS WELL AS FOR UNDERSTANDING HOW TEETH CAN BE REGENERATED IN VITRO AND ULTIMATELY IN VIVO. TEETH ARE DEEPLY HOMOLOGOUS TO, AND FORM SIMILARLY TO, OTHER VERTEBRATE SKIN APPENDAGES INCLUDING MAMMALIAN HAIR. ALTHOUGH GENETIC STUDIES IN MICE AND HUMANS HAVE IDENTIFIED SIGNALING PATHWAYS INVOLVED IN TOOTH FORMATION, LESS IS KNOWN ABOUT GENETIC MECHANISMS REGULATING TOOTH REPLACEMENT. IN CONTRAST, THE GENETIC BASIS OF MAMMALIAN HAIR REGENERATION HAS BEEN EXTENSIVELY STUDIED. A PARSIMONIOUS HYPOTHESIS IS THAT TEETH AND HAIR REGENERATE USING SHARED GENETIC CIRCUITRY. FISH REPLACE THEIR TEETH CONSTANTLY THROUGHOUT ADULT LIFE AND OFFER POWERFUL SYSTEMS FOR GENETIC ANALYSIS. THE SAME GENES THAT MAKE HUMAN TEETH ALSO MAKE FISH TEETH. HALF OF HUMANS MISSING TEETH HAVE MUTATIONS IN THE WNT10A GENE, AND FISH WITH WNT10A MUTATIONS ARE ALSO MISSING TEETH. WE HAVE DEVELOPED THE THREESPINE STICKLEBACK FISH (GASTEROSTEUS ACULEATUS) SYSTEM TO EXPERIMENTALLY TEST GENE AND ENHANCER FUNCTION TO LEARN THE GENETIC BASIS OF TOOTH FORMATION AND REPLACEMENT. FRESHWATER POPULATIONS HAVE EVOLVED MAJOR INCREASES IN TOOTH NUMBER COMPARED TO ANCESTRAL MARINE FISH. THE TOOTH NUMBER INCREASE ARISES LATE IN DEVELOPMENT THROUGH AN ACCELERATED TOOTH REPLACEMENT RATE. THE DIFFERENT FORMS CAN BE CROSSED IN THE LAB, ENABLING DETAILED AND UNBIASED FORWARD GENETIC ANALYSES TO MAP FACTORS CONTROLLING THE CHANGES IN TOOTH NUMBER. USING QUANTITATIVE GENETICS AND WHOLE GENOME SEQUENCING IN THIS SYSTEM, WE IDENTIFIED THE FIRST GENETIC LOCUS IN A POLYPHYODONT (A VERTEBRATE THAT HAS THE ANCESTRAL STATE OF UNDERGOING CONSTANT TOOTH REPLACEMENT THROUGHOUT ADULTHOOD) THAT REGULATES TOOTH REPLACEMENT. WE MAPPED TOOTH NUMBER TO CIS-REGULATORY VARIATION IN A TOOTH ENHANCER IN THE FOURTH INTRON OF THE BONE MORPHOGENETIC PROTEIN 6 (BMP6) GENE. IN MICE, BMP SIGNALING AND BMP6 REGULATE HAIR REGENERATION. TOGETHER THESE AND OTHER DATA SUPPORT THE HYPOTHESIS OF SHARED GENETIC CIRCUITRY REGULATING TOOTH AND HAIR REGENERATION. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, THREE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE PROPOSED. FIRST, WE WILL DETERMINE SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL INPUTS OF THIS INTRONIC BMP6 ENHANCER BY GENETIC AND GENOME EDITING EXPERIMENTS. SECOND, WE WILL TEST WHETHER TWO GENES, FOXC1B AND NFATC1A, REGULATE TOOTH REPLACEMENT AND STEM CELL QUIESCENCE SIMILAR TO HOW THEIR MAMMALIAN ORTHOLOGS REGULATE HAIR REGENERATION. THIRD, WE WILL TEST WHETHER WNT10A, ACP4, AND DRAXINA REGULATE TOOTH SPACING SIMILAR TO HOW A WNT-WNT INHIBITOR NETWORK REGULATES MAMMALIAN HAIR SPACING. TOGETHER THESE AIMS WILL REVEAL FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE OF THE GENES REGULATING TOOTH FORMATION AND REPLACEMENT, AND TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT TEETH AND HAIR REGENERATE USING SHARED GENETIC CIRCUITRY.

description: ROLE OF AUTOPHAGY IN ENAMEL DEVELOPMENT - ABSTRACT AMELOGENESIS IMPERFECTA, WHICH IS CHARACTERIZED BY CONGENITAL TOOTH ENAMEL DEFECTS, OCCURS WORLDWIDE WITH A PREVALENCE OF LESS THAN 0.5%. MAJOR CLINICAL IMPACTS INCLUDE SOCIAL EMBARRASSMENT, DENTAL PAIN, EATING DIFFICULTIES, AND EARLY TOOTH LOSS DUE TO ABNORMALLY THIN, SOFT, FRAGILE, AND DISCOLORED ENAMEL, TOGETHER WITH POOR AESTHETICS AND FUNCTIONALITY. ALTHOUGH AMELOGENESIS IMPERFECTA SIGNIFICANTLY AFFECTS QUALITY OF LIFE, ITS ETIOLOGY REMAINS LARGELY UNKNOWN OWING TO POTENTIALLY COMPLEX GENETIC AND EPIGENETIC INTERACTIONS. OUR PREVIOUS STUDIES SHOWED THAT MICRORNAS (MIRNAS)—SHORT NON-CODING RNAS THAT REGULATE EXPRESSION OF TARGET GENES AT THE POSTTRANSCRIPTIONAL LEVEL—PLAY A CRUCIAL ROLE IN THE REGULATION OF GENES ASSOCIATED WITH ENAMEL FORMATION IN HUMANS AND MICE. IN OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES, WE FOUND THAT MICE WITH AN AUTOPHAGY DEFICIENCY DISPLAYED FEATURES OF AMELOGENESIS IMPERFECTA DUE TO A FAILURE IN AMELOBLAST DIFFERENTIATION. ALTHOUGH AN INCREASING NUMBER OF STUDIES INDICATE THAT AUTOPHAGY-RELATED MOLECULES PLAY IMPORTANT ROLES IN VARIOUS CELLULAR PROCESSES, INCLUDING TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATION UNDER PHYSIOLOGICAL AND PATHOLOGICAL CONDITIONS, THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL MECHANISMS REGULATING CELL DIFFERENTIATION ARE NOT FULLY UNDERSTOOD. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT AUTOPHAGY PLAYS A CRUCIAL ROLE IN THE MAINTENANCE AND DIFFERENTIATION OF DENTAL EPITHELIAL CELLS THROUGH AUTOPHAGY-MEDIATED TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC REGULATION. WE WILL TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS IN TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. IN AIM 1 WE WILL DETERMINE HOW AUTOPHAGY DEFICIENCY ALTERS EXPRESSION OF GENES RELATED TO ENAMEL FORMATION. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL IDENTIFY THE CAUSATIVE REGULATORY NETWORKS OF GENES RELATED TO AMELOGENESIS IMPERFECTA IN AUTOPHAGY-DEFICIENT MICE. IN AIM 2 WE WILL IDENTIFY EPIGENETIC ALTERNATIONS IN AMELOBLASTS IN AUTOPHAGY-DEFICIENT MICE AND EVALUATE THE FUNCTIONAL SIGNIFICANCE OF THESE EPIGENETIC FACTORS IN CULTURED CELLS AND MOUSE MODELS. ULTIMATELY, THIS APPROACH WILL LEAD TO THE IDENTIFICATION OF NOVEL MECHANISM(S) FOR AMELOGENESIS IMPERFECTA AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS AND THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS FOR AT-RISK POPULATIONS AND FAMILIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE MICROBIOLOGY OF DENTIN INVASION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  DENTAL CARIES IS THE MOST COMMON CHRONIC DISEASE OF CHILDHOOD. SEVERE FORMS ARE COMMON, CAN CAUSE PAIN AND SERIOUS SYSTEMIC INFECTIONS, AND ARE COSTLY TO TREAT. CARIES BEGINS BY UNDERMINING THE OUTER TOOTH ENAMEL WHICH EVENTUALLY FRACTURES, CREATING A VISIBLE CAVITATION THAT EVENTUALLY REACHES THE UNDERLYING DENTIN. THE SERIOUS CONSEQUENCES OF CARIES: TOOTHACHES, PERIAPICAL INFLAMMATION AND ABSCESS, AS WELL AS FACIAL INFECTION FROM TISSUE INVASION, ALL RESULT FROM MICROBIAL ACCESS THROUGH THE DENTIN TUBULES TO THE PULP, THE LIVING CORE OF THE TOOTH. DESPITE ITS CRITICAL ROLE IN PATHOGENESIS, THE MECHANISM OF MICROBIAL INVASION OF DENTIN IS LARGELY UNSTUDIED, AND METHODS TO OVERCOME THE CHALLENGES OF STUDYING THIS HARD TISSUE ARE UNDERDEVELOPED. ONCE MICROBES DESTROY THE ENAMEL AND REACH THE DENTIN, PRELIMINARY STUDIES SUGGEST THAT THE BIOLOGY CHANGES. DENTIN, UNLIKE ENAMEL, HAS A MUCH HIGHER PROTEIN CONTENT, LOWER MINERAL CONTENT, AND IS STRUCTURED AROUND A NETWORK OF MICROCHANNELS THAT COMMUNICATE DIRECTLY WITH THE PULP. THESE CHANNELS PROVIDE A FAST-TRACK CONDUIT FOR MICROBIAL INVASION THAT IS VERY DIFFERENT FROM THE ENAMEL WITH ITS SOLID CRYSTAL STRUCTURE OVERLAID WITH A WELL- STUDIED SURFACE BIOFILM. RECENT TECHNICAL INNOVATIONS BY THIS TEAM OF INVESTIGATORS IN ADAPTING HISTOLOGIC APPROACHES HAVE PROVIDED NEW INSIGHTS. BASED ON THESE RECENT STUDIES, DENTIN CARIES APPEARS TO BE DRIVEN BY DISSOLUTION OF TOOTH STRUCTURE FROM WITHIN THE TUBULES AND EXHIBITS A UNIQUE MICROBIAL SPATIAL BIOLOGY WITHIN TUBULES THAT IS UNLIKE THAT FOUND IN SURFACE BIOFILMS. BOTH FUNGI AND BACTERIA-FILLED TUBULES ARE COMMON, BUT UNLIKE SURFACE BIOFILMS, SINGLE TUBULES PRIMARILY HARBOR EITHER FUNGI OR BACTERIA, BUT NOT BOTH. TO BETTER UNDERSTAND DENTIN CARIES, WE NEED TO FIRST SPATIALLY IDENTIFY THE SPECIES OR CONSORTIA OF SPECIES THAT ARE INVOLVED, AND THEN DETERMINE THEIR ABILITY TO INVADE TUBULES, AND THEIR ABILITY TO ADVANCE THE LESION FRONT BY DESTRUCTION OF DENTIN. AIM 1 WILL COMPREHENSIVELY DETERMINE SPECIES-LEVEL BACTERIAL AND FUNGAL MICROBIAL PROFILES IN CARIOUS DENTIN AS A FUNCTION OF DEPTH WITHIN A CARIOUS LESION USING DNA SEQUENCING OF SERIAL SECTIONS OF CARIOUS HUMAN TEETH. AIM 2 WILL CHARACTERIZE THE HIGH-RESOLUTION SPATIAL BIOLOGY OF THESE BACTERIA AND FUNGI WITHIN DENTINAL TUBULES IN HUMAN TEETH AND THEN TEST THEIR INVASIVE POTENTIAL IN AN IN VITRO DENTIN MODEL SYSTEM. AIM 3 WILL IDENTIFY THE SPECIES OR CONSORTIA OF SPECIES RESPONSIBLE FOR DEMINERALIZATION AND COLLAGEN DEGRADATION IN TUBULE INVASION, ELUCIDATING MECHANISMS OF MICROBIAL PENETRATION, DEMINERALIZATION, AND COLLAGEN DEGRADATION USING CLINICAL SAMPLES AND IN VITRO MODEL SYSTEMS THAT MIMIC THE DENTIN ENVIRONMENT. THESE AIMS ADDRESS A SIGNIFICANT AND CRITICAL STAGE OF CARIES , MICROBES INVADING THROUGH DENTIN TOWARDS THE PULP. THEY WILL IDENTIFY THE MICROBES RESPONSIBLE FOR INVASION, DEMINERALIZATION, COLLAGEN DEGRADATION AND THEY WILL BEGIN TO ELUCIDATE THE MECHANISTIC BASIS OF CRITICAL MICROBE-MICROBE INTERACTIONS. IT IS A CONCEPTUALLY INNOVATIVE NEW DIRECTION IN CARIES RESEARCH, TARGETING AN UNDERSTUDIED, AND KEY PATHOGENIC PROCESS, AND COULD LEAD TO IMPROVED PREVENTIVE AND THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR A SIGNIFICANT PUBLIC HEALTH PROBLEM.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PRECISION NANOMEDICINE TARGETING INFLAMMATORY AND OSTEOCLAST PATHWAYS IN PERIODONTAL DISEASE - TITLE PRECISION NANOMEDICINE TARGETING INFLAMMATORY AND OSTEOCLAST PATHWAYS IN PERIODONTAL DISEASE ABSTRACT PERIODONTAL DISEASE (PD), INCLUDING GINGIVITIS AND PERIODONTITIS, AFFECTS ~42% OF U.S. ADULTS AND OVER ONE BILLION PEOPLE WORLDWIDE. PROGRESSION TO CHRONIC PERIODONTITIS IS CHARACTERIZED BY UNRESOLVED INFLAMMATION, DESTRUCTION OF PERIODONTAL TISSUES, AND ALVEOLAR BONE LOSS, WHICH SIGNIFICANTLY IMPACTS ORAL AND SYSTEMIC HEALTH. DESPITE EXTENSIVE KNOWLEDGE OF MOLECULAR MEDIATORS, THERE ARE NO PRECISION THERAPEUTICS THAT DIRECTLY TARGET DISEASE-DRIVING PATHWAYS. CURRENT TREATMENTS REMAIN LARGELY PALLIATIVE, UNDERSCORING A CRITICAL UNMET NEED FOR SITE-SPECIFIC STRATEGIES THAT CAN RESTORE IMMUNE BALANCE AND PREVENT ALVEOLAR BONE RESORPTION. THIS PROPOSAL DEVELOPS AND EVALUATES INNOVATIVE NANOTHERAPEUTIC AND IMMUNOTHERAPEUTIC APPROACHES FOR PD, LEVERAGING EXPERTISE IN CELL-TYPE–SPECIFIC NANOPARTICLE DELIVERY SYSTEMS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SITE-SPECIFIC NANOPARTICLE PLATFORMS TARGETING KEY INFLAMMATORY AND OSTEOCLASTOGENIC PATHWAYS WILL ATTENUATE DISEASE PROGRESSION AND PRESERVE ALVEOLAR BONE. AIM 1 WILL EVALUATE MYELOID CELL–SPECIFIC HYALURONIC ACID–COATED NANOPARTICLES DELIVERING SIRNAS AGAINST IL-1Β AND TNF-Α TO DISRUPT PROINFLAMMATORY CYTOKINE NETWORKS AND REDUCE TISSUE INFLAMMATION. AIM 2 WILL ENGINEER OSTEOCLAST-TARGETING NANOPARTICLES FUNCTIONALIZED TO DELIVER RANK SIRNA, SUPPRESS OSTEOCLASTOGENESIS, AND PREVENT ALVEOLAR BONE RESORPTION. AIM 3 WILL ESTABLISH PROOF-OF-CONCEPT FOR NANOPARTICLE-ENABLED CAR- MACROPHAGES THAT RECOGNIZE AND ELIMINATE OSTEOCLASTS, REPROGRAM THE LOCAL MICROENVIRONMENT, AND PROVIDE SUSTAINED IMMUNOMODULATION. IMPACT. COMPLETION OF THESE STUDIES WILL ESTABLISH A SCALABLE NANOPARTICLE PLATFORM FOR PRECISION DELIVERY OF THERAPEUTICS TO INFLAMMATORY AND BONE-RESORPTIVE PATHWAYS IN PD. BY INTEGRATING IMMUNE-TARGETED AND OSTEOCLAST-TARGETED STRATEGIES, THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE INNOVATIVE APPROACHES TO PRESERVE ALVEOLAR BONE AND IMPROVE ORAL HEALTH, WHILE LAYING THE FOUNDATION FOR BROADER APPLICATIONS OF IMMUNO-NANOMEDICINE IN INFLAMMATORY BONE DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TRANSLATING RED-LIGHT THERAPY INTO RESTORATIVE DENTISTRY: CLINICAL EFFICACY AND SAFETY - ABSTRACT THE AMERICAN DENTAL ASSOCIATION (ADA) ESTIMATES THAT APPROXIMATELY 3-6 MILLION DENTAL RESTORATIONS FAIL PREMATURELY ANNUALLY IN THE U.S.1, 2 A MAJOR CONCERN IS THAT ENDODONTIC COMPLICATIONS ARE THE LEADING CAUSE OF THESE SHORT-TERM FAILURES, ACCOUNTING FOR NEARLY 80% OF THE CASES.2 THESE COMPLICATIONS ARE CLOSELY LINKED TO PERSISTENT OR EXACERBATED INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES, WHICH MAY RESULT NOT ONLY FROM THE DISEASE BUT ALSO FROM THE MECHANICAL TRAUMA OF CARIES REMOVAL, THE RESTORATIVE PROCEDURE ITSELF, AND OTHER CORRELATED BUT UNAVOIDABLE FACTORS.3-7 IN THIS CONTEXT, RED LIGHT THERAPY HAS GAINED INCREASING ATTENTION AS AN ADJUNCT APPROACH TO ENHANCE CLINICAL RECOVERY AND IMPROVE POST-OPERATIVE OUTCOMES. SYSTEMATIC REVIEWS DEMONSTRATE THAT RED LIGHT THERAPY CAN TRIPLE THE LIKELIHOOD OF SUCCESSFUL TISSUE HEALING IN ORAL PROCEDURES.8-11 THUS, EVEN IF ONLY A FRACTION OF THIS BENEFIT TRANSLATED CLINICALLY, THIS WOULD CORRESPOND TO ~300,000–1.2 MILLION FEWER FAILED RESTORATIONS ANNUALLY IN THE U.S. ON THE OTHER SIDE, A PRACTICAL CHALLENGE IN ADOPTING RED-LIGHT THERAPY IN THE DENTAL ROUTINE IS THAT THIS TREATMENT IS STILL DELIVERED AS A SEPARATE PROCEDURE, REQUIRING ADDITIONAL EQUIPMENT AND CHAIR TIME. THUS, OUR GROUP HAVE BEEN WORKING ON STRATEGIES THAT COULD INTEGRATE RED LIGHT THERAPY DIRECTLY INTO THE RESTORATIVE WORKFLOW, SO THAT THERAPEUTIC BENEFIT OCCURS AT THE EXACT MOMENT OF TISSUE STRESS. HOWEVER, THE DRAWBACK WAS THAT CURRENT RESTORATIVE MATERIALS RELIED ON CAMPHORQUINONE, A PHOTOINITIATOR THAT IS EXCLUSIVELY ACTIVATED BY THE BLUE SPECTRUM, FOR ITS HARDENING. THUS, ADDRESSING THIS CHALLENGE REQUIRED RETHINKING LIGHT ACTIVATION IN RESTORATIVE MATERIALS. TO OVERCOME THIS HURDLE, OUR GROUP SYNTHESIZED THE FIRST PHOTOINITIATOR ACTIVATED BY RED LIGHT, NOW OPENING THE DOOR TO ROUTINELY INCORPORATE RED-LIGHT THERAPY DURING CLINICAL CARE. THUS, BUILDING UPON OUR WORK, WE HAVE ASSEMBLED A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM WITH EXPERTISE IN CHEMISTRY, DENTAL BIOMATERIALS, AND TRANSLATIONAL ANIMAL MODELS FOR DENTISTRY TO BE THE FIRST TO TRANSLATE RED-LIGHT CURING FROM CONCEPT TO CLINICALLY VIABLE TECHNOLOGY, SHIFTING RED LIGHT THERAPY FROM AN ADJUNCTIVE THERAPY TO AN INTEGRATED RESTORATIVE SOLUTION. SPECIFICALLY, WE AIM TO: 1) DEFINE THE CHEMICAL, PHYSICAL, AND BIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF THE FIRST DENTAL RESTORATIVE MATERIAL FORMULATED WITH THE NOVEL RED-LIGHT-ACTIVATED PHOTOINITIATOR, AND 2) EVALUATE THE IN VIVO THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS OF RED LIGHT ON PULPAL AND GINGIVAL TISSUES USING A PORCINE MODEL. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF THIS WORK ARE TO FULLY CHARACTERIZE THE FIRST RESTORATIVE MATERIAL CURED WITH RED LIGHT AND PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE IN VIVO DATA ON THE THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS OF RED LIGHT TO PULPAL AND GINGIVAL HEALTH. THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR SUBSEQUENT CLINICAL TRIALS WITH THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF ADOPTING RED-LIGHT THERAPY IN DENTAL PRACTICE TO REDUCE TREATMENT COMPLICATIONS, MAKING A TANGIBLE IMPACT ON PATIENT OUTCOMES, AND REDUCING LONG-TERM HEALTHCARE BURDEN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF SIRNA CONJUGATES AS TOOLS FOR CNS CELL-SPECIFIC GENE MODULATION - SUMMARY THE ABILITY TO CARRY OUT EFFECTIVE GENE TARGETING IN SPECIFIC CELL TYPES IS PARAMOUNT FOR MECHANISTIC STUDIES IN THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS). CURRENT APPROACHES FOR GENE KNOCKDOWN OR KNOCKOUT HAVE BEEN USED TO ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF CNS FUNCTION IN HEALTH AND DISEASE. HOWEVER, THESE APPROACHES HAVE INHERENT LIMITATIONS. FOR EXAMPLE, CRE RECOMBINASE HAS BEEN AN INDISPENSABLE WORKHORSE TECHNOLOGY IN CNS STUDIES, BUT THE REQUIRED BREEDING AND AGING OF MULTIPLE MOUSE STRAINS IS CUMBERSOME, TIME-CONSUMING, AND EXPENSIVE, AND FACTORS SUCH AS POOR RECOMBINATION EFFICIENCY, A LACK OF CELL-SPECIFIC DRIVER STRAINS, AND UNINTENDED GERMLINE RECOMBINATION CAN REDUCE THE UTILITY OF THESE APPROACHES. ADENO-ASSOCIATED VIRUSES (AAVS) HAVE ALSO ATTRACTED ATTENTION FOR GENE MODULATION IN RECENT YEARS, BUT EVEN WHEN EVOLVED TO CROSS THE BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER AND TRANSDUCE DESIRED CELL TYPES, SUCH VIRUSES CONTINUE TO EXHIBIT SIGNIFICANT OFF-TARGET TRANSDUCTION IN THE PERIPHERY. TO OVERCOME SOME OF THESE CHALLENGES, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP AND LEVERAGE SHORT INTERFERING RNA (SIRNA) CONJUGATES, WHERE THE MOLECULAR PROPERTIES OF THE SIRNA CONJUGATE, INJECTION ROUTE, AND ADMINISTERED DOSE CAN ALL BE ADJUSTED TO DRIVE DELIVERY AND ACTIVITY IN SPECIFIC CNS CELL TYPES. IN PREVIOUSLY PUBLISHED WORK, WE DEVELOPED A LIPID-SIRNA CONJUGATE TERMED L2-SIRNA THAT EXHIBITED UNIFORM DISTRIBUTION AND ACTIVITY ACROSS THE MOUSE CNS AFTER DELIVERY VIA INTRACEREBROVENTRICULAR (ICV) INJECTION. AT THE UTILIZED DOSES, L2-SIRNA ALSO EXHIBITED TRANSIENT ACTIVITY IN THE PERIPHERY. IN UNPUBLISHED WORK, WE HAVE SHOWN THAT REDUCING THE DOSE OF L2- SIRNA AMELIORATES PERIPHERAL DRAINAGE AND SILENCING ACTIVITY, WHILE RETAINING DELIVERY TO AND KNOCKDOWN CAPABILITIES IN MANY CNS CELL TYPES INCLUDING GLIA AND MYELOID CELLS. BUILDING ON THIS EMERGING UNDERSTANDING OF SIRNA CONJUGATE STRUCTURE/FUNCTION RELATIONSHIPS, WE DESIGNED A NEW CONJUGATE WITH A TRI-MANNOSE MOIETY (“MAN3-SIRNA”) TO DIRECT UPTAKE AND ACTIVITY SPECIFICALLY IN BORDER-ASSOCIATED MACROPHAGES. FINALLY, WE SHOW THAT SIRNA “ANTIDOTES” CAN BE EFFECTIVELY DESIGNED TO INHIBIT L2-SIRNA ACTIVITY IN CELLS. IN THIS PROPOSAL, ALL OF THESE ADVANCEMENTS ARE BEING BROUGHT TOGETHER TO DEVELOP SIRNA CONJUGATES AS A PROMISING CLASS OF TECHNOLOGIES FOR CNS GENE MODULATION AND TARGETED MECHANISTIC STUDIES. IN AIM 1, WE WILL BUILD ON PRELIMINARY WORK AND RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE HOW THE ICV DOSE OF L2-SIRNA DICTATES REGIONAL AND CELL-SPECIFIC GENE SILENCING IN THE CNS VERSUS PERIPHERY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL IDENTIFY THE ICV DOSE OF MAN3-SIRNA THAT ACHIEVES SELECTIVE TARGETING OF BORDER- ASSOCIATED MACROPHAGES AND ASSESS THE LONGEVITY OF GENE SILENCING IN THESE CELLS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL DEVELOP A COMBINATION OF L2-SIRNA AND MAN3-ANTIDOTE CONJUGATES THAT ACHIEVES SILENCING OF A MYELOID CELL GENE TARGET IN MICROGLIA BUT NOT BORDER-ASSOCIATED MACROPHAGES. THESE PROOF-OF-PRINCIPLE STUDIES WILL YIELD SIRNA CONJUGATES AND EXPERIMENTAL WORKFLOWS THAT PROVIDE IMMEDIATE VALUE TO THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY, WHILE ALSO MOTIVATING THE DEVELOPMENT OF ADDITIONAL CONJUGATE DESIGNS AND DOSING SCHEMES TO FURTHER CNS CELL-SPECIFIC GENE MODULATION INITIATIVES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNDERSTANDING SMALL HEAT SHOCK PROTEIN MECHANISM - PROJECT SUMMARY THIS PROJECT CONTINUES A LONG-STANDING EFFORT TO UNDERSTAND THE MOST ENIGMATIC FAMILY OF PROTEIN CHAPERONES: THE SMALL HEAT SHOCK PROTEINS (SHSPS). THE PROTEINS THAT DEFINE THIS FAMILY WERE ORIGINALLY DISCOVERED IN EYE LENS, WHERE THEY WERE NAMED AA- AND AB-CRYSTALLIN (NOW KNOWN BY THE MORE GENERAL NAMES, HSPB4 AND HSPB5, RESPECTIVELY). IN THE LENS THEY INHIBIT THE AGGREGATION OF PROTEINS TO MAINTAIN PROTEOSTASIS IN THE ABSENCE OF EITHER PROTEIN SYNTHESIS OR DEGRADATION. MUTATIONS IN HSPB4 OR HSPB5 CAUSE CATARACTS—A DIRECT CONSEQUENCE OF THEIR CHAPERONE ACTIVITY. MUCH LESS APPRECIATED IS HSPB5’S PROTECTIVE FUNCTION TOWARDS TUBULIN/MICROTUBULES. IT IS THIS ASPECT OF SHSP BIOLOGY THAT WE WILL FOCUS ON IN THIS PROJECT. PROGRESS IN UNDERSTANDING SHSPS HAS BEEN HAMPERED BY THEIR CHALLENGING INTRINSIC PROPERTIES. IN PARTICULAR, THEY CONTAIN A HIGH CONTENT OF DISORDERED PROTEIN REGIONS AND FORM DYNAMIC, HETEROGENEOUS AND POLYDISPERSE OLIGOMERS. OVER PREVIOUS FUNDING CYCLES, WE DEVELOPED POWERFUL NEW TOOLS THAT RESOLVE RESIDUE-LEVEL FEATURES THAT HAVE LED TO A NEW CONCEPTUAL MODEL OF SHSP STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION. NEW INSIGHTS GAINED NOW PROVIDE WAYS TO INVESTIGATE AND ULTIMATELY DEFINE HOW SHSPS CARRY OUT THEIR VARIED FUNCTIONS. WE WILL BUILD ON THIS FOUNDATION TO FOCUS ON HOW HSPB5 PROVIDES CONSTANT AND CONTINUOUS PROTECTION OF THE CYTOSKELETON. THE CYTOSKELETON IS A DYNAMIC NETWORK OF PROTEIN FIBERS THAT PROVIDES STRUCTURAL SUPPORT AND SHAPE TO A CELL AND SERVES AS CONDUITS FOR THE MOVEMENT OF CRITICAL CELLULAR COMPONENTS THROUGHOUT THE CELL. WE WILL BEGIN THIS PHASE OF THE STUDY BY FOCUSING ON HSPB5’S PROTECTION OF TUBULIN/MICROTUBULES, WHICH PLAY CRITICAL ROLES IN ALL OCULAR TISSUES AND CELLS. DISRUPTION OR LOSS OF INTEGRITY OF MICROTUBULES ARE IMPLICATED IN A HOST OF CONDITIONS AND DISEASES OF THE EYE, INCLUDING CATARACT, GLAUCOMA, AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION, AND DIABETIC RETINOPATHY. UNDERSTANDING THE NATURAL WAYS THAT SHSPS PROTECT MICROTUBULES MAY PROVIDE NEW AVENUES TO TARGET OR TREAT SUCH CONDITIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LENS CONNEXINS, CELLULAR STRESS, AND CATARACTS - CATARACTS ARE THE LEADING CAUSE OF BLINDNESS WORLDWIDE. THEY ARE FREQUENTLY ASSOCIATED WITH AGING, BUT THEY CAN BE CAUSED BY CONGENITAL MUTATIONS OF LENS PROTEINS OR BY VARIOUS DISEASES INCLUDING DIABETES. THE PREVAILING DOGMA IS THAT CATARACTS ARE CAUSED BY THE ACCUMULATION OF DAMAGE TO LENS COMPONENTS (ESPECIALLY PROTEINS). WE HAVE FOUND THAT MICE CARRYING MUTATIONS OF THE LENS FIBER CELL CONNEXINS (CONNEXIN46 AND CONNEXIN50) OR ΓC-CRYSTALLIN HAVE ABNORMALITIES OF LENS IONIC HOMEOSTASIS; THESE ALTERATIONS LEAD TO THE FORMATION OF CALCIUM-CONTAINING PRECIPITATES IN THE SAME REGION AND DISTRIBUTION AS THE CATARACTS. WE HAVE ALSO FOUND THAT THE INSOLUBLE MATERIAL FROM CATARACT SURGERIES CONTAINS CALCIFIED PARTICLES. THESE FINDINGS IMPLICATE THE DISRUPTION OF IONIC HOMEOSTASIS AND FORMATION OF CALCIFIED DEPOSITS AS GENERAL PROCESSES CONTRIBUTING TO CATARACT FORMATION. IN THE PROPOSED STUDIES, WE WILL UTILIZE HUMAN LENS MATERIAL, MUTANT MICE, AND AN IN VITRO MODEL TO DEFINE ADDITIONAL FACTORS THAT CONTRIBUTE WITH IONIC IMBALANCE TO CAUSE CATARACTS. WE WILL FOCUS ON DAMAGE TO LENS PROTEINS AND CELLULAR STRESS ACTIVATION OF PROTEOLYTIC PATHWAYS AND HOW THEY RELATE TO CALCIUM DEPOSITION. THIS PROPOSAL WILL YIELD INSIGHTS INTO FUNDAMENTAL PATHOGENIC MECHANISMS OF CATARACTS AND MAY PROVIDE A NEW DIRECTION FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF PREVENTATIVE/THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE GENETIC ETIOLOGIES OF STILLBIRTH: AN EXTREME ON THE DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS CONTINUUM - ABSTRACT STILLBIRTH (SB), A DEVASTATING PREGNANCY OUTCOME IMPACTING OVER 20,000 FAMILIES ANNUALLY, REPRESENTS A PROFOUND MANIFESTATION OF DISRUPTED HUMAN DEVELOPMENT WITHIN THE BROADER SPECTRUM OF DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS (DDS). WHILE THE ETIOLOGICAL UNDERPINNINGS OF MANY SBS REMAIN ELUSIVE, GENETIC FACTORS PERTURBING FUNDAMENTAL DEVELOPMENTAL PROGRAMS ARE SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTORS. HISTORICALLY, GENETIC STUDIES OF SB HAVE BEEN CONSTRAINED BY THE CHALLENGES INHERENT IN ASSEMBLING ADEQUATELY POWERED COHORTS AND SYSTEMATIC PHENOTYPING, COUPLED WITH LIMITATIONS ON CONVENTIONAL GENOMICS TECHNOLOGIES. HOWEVER, EMERGING EVIDENCE FROM OUR GROUPS AND OTHERS INDICATES A COMPLEX GENETIC ARCHITECTURE UNDERLYING SB, ENCOMPASSING A MIXTURE OF HIGHLY DELETERIOUS VARIANTS AND A SPECTRUM OF DOMINANT AND RECESSIVE VARIANTS WITH MORE SUBTLE EFFECTS THAT ARE SHARED WITH OTHER DDS. HERE, WE ENDEAVOR TO INTERROGATE THE GENOMIC LANDSCAPE OF SB, CAPITALIZING ON FOUNDATIONAL RESOURCES CURATED BY THE FETAL GENOMICS CONSORTIUM. DURING THIS BRIDGE FUNDING PERIOD, WE WILL AGGREGATE GENOMIC AND PHENOTYPIC DATA FROM AN INITIAL SEQUENCING COHORT OF >1,000 SB CASES AND THEIR FAMILY MEMBERS. WE WILL ANALYZE SHORT-READ SEQUENCING AS A FRONT-LINE STRATEGY (AIM 1). NOVEL ASSOCIATIONS IN SB WILL BE DELINEATED THROUGH INTEGRATIVE ANALYSIS OF ALL VARIANT CLASSES AND INHERITANCE PATTERNS USING A SOPHISTICATED BAYESIAN ANALYTIC FRAMEWORK, AS WELL AS EXPLORATION OF ALL NONCODING REGULATORY ELEMENTS UTILIZING A CATEGORY-WIDE ASSOCIATION. AIM 2 WILL STRATEGICALLY LEVERAGE A MASSIVE-SCALE DATASET OF ~200,000 CASES WITH HETEROGENEOUS DDS THAT WE HAVE AGGREGATED TO COMPARE THE ARCHITECTURE OF SB AS AN EXTREME PHENOTYPE ALONG THE HUMAN DEVELOPMENTAL CONTINUUM. WE WILL ALSO COMPARE THESE DATA TO POPULATION-SCALE SEQUENCING FROM >1 MILLION INDIVIDUALS THAT WE HAVE PROCESSED IN GNOMAD, THE ALL OF US RESEARCH PROGRAM, AND OTHER RESOURCES TO IDENTIFY VARIANTS UNIQUELY ASSOCIATED WITH INVIABILITY AND NEVER SEEN IN THE GENERAL POPULATION, SOMETIMES REFERRED TO AS THE ‘INTOLEROME’. COLLECTIVELY, THIS MULTIFACETED STUDY OF SB WILL ENABLE ACCESS TO THE COMPLETE SPECTRUM OF SB-ASSOCIATED GENETIC VARIATION AT AN UNPRECEDENTED SCALE AND RESOLUTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HIV-1 TAT GENETIC VARIATION IMPACTS NEUROHIV - PROJECT ABSTRACT/SUMMARY HIV-1 VIRAL LOAD CAN BE SUPPRESSED IN PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV (PLWH) THROUGH CONSISTENT USE OF ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART). DESPITE THIS, BETWEEN 15 TO 40% OF LWH ARE PREDICTED TO SUFFER FROM HIV-ASSOCIATED NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT (NCI). ALTHOUGH THE PATHOGENESIS OF NCI IS INCOMPLETELY UNDERSTOOD, HIV-1 TRANSACTIVATOR OF TRANSCRIPTION (TAT) IS CAPABLE OF BEING SECRETED FROM INFECTED CELLS, AND ONCE EXTRACELLULAR IN THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) IT WILL INDUCE NEURONAL DYSREGULATION. EARLY IN THE INFECTION, HIV-1 ESTABLISHES A RESERVOIR IN THE BRAIN, EITHER BY ENTERING AS INFECTED PERIVASCULAR MACROPHAGES OR INFECTING RESIDENT MICROGLIA, PRIOR TO THE PATIENT RECEIVING ART. ART DOES NOT AFFECT THE PRODUCTION OF TAT, WHICH IS CONTINUALLY MADE IN THESE CELLS, LEADING TO QUANTIFIABLE LEVELS OF TAT IN THE ABSENCE OF DETECTABLE VIRAL LOAD. TAT SEQUENCE COMPOSITION VARIES WITHIN AND BETWEEN INDIVIDUALS DUE TO HIV-1’S ERROR-PRONE REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE AND HOST FACTORS SUCH AS APOBEC3G. WE HAVE SHOWN THAT THIS VARIATION IS ASSOCIATED WITH NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT (NCI), AS SHOWN BY COMPARING THE HIV-1 TAT PROTEIN SEQUENCE COMPOSITION FROM IMPAIRED AND NON-IMPAIRED PLWH WITHIN THE DREXEL MEDICINE CNS AIDS RESEARCH AND ERADICATION STUDY (CARES) COHORT. IN THE PAST 5 YEARS, WE HAVE FURTHER DEMONSTRATED THAT TAT COULD BE THE PRODUCT FROM INTACT OR DEFECTIVE VIRIONS FROM CELLULAR RESERVOIRS IN THE BRAIN NAMELY MICROGLIA AND ASTROCYTES AND OTHER PERIPHERAL TISSUES THAT CAN CAUSE BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER DISRUPTION AND NCI. RECOMBINANT TAT101 INJECTED DIRECTLY INTO THE PREFRONTAL CORTEX (PFC) OF ADULT RATS PRODUCED IMPAIRMENT IN LEARNING AND MEMORY TASKS AND EX VIVO ANALYSIS OF THE BRAIN PFC TISSUE SUGGESTED UPREGULATION OF PATHWAYS THAT INDUCE IMMUNE AND CELLULAR RESPONSE TO TOXICITY AND DOWN REGULATION OF GENES THAT ARE INVOLVED IN PROMOTING COGNITION, SYNAPTIC CONNECTIVITY AND DOPAMINE AND GLUTAMATE NEUROTRANSMISSION. THUS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT TAT PRODUCED BY MICROGLIAL AND ASTROCYTE RESERVOIRS PROMOTE NEUROTOXICITY AND NCI BY SYNERGISTIC DYSREGULATION OF DOPAMINE-GLUTAMATE HOMEOSTASIS AND HEIGHTENED IMMUNE RESPONSE PROMOTING EXCITOTOXICITY IN NEURONS. TO INVESTIGATE THIS, WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING THREE AIMS. AIM 1 WILL USE NEAR FULL-LENGTH SEQUENCING OF PROVIRAL DNA FROM CELLULAR RESERVOIRS DERIVED FROM PLWH FROM NATIONAL NEUROHIV TISSUE CONSORTIUM (NNTC) AND CARES COHORTS TO DETERMINE THE MOLECULAR ARCHITECTURE OF THE PROVIRAL RESERVOIRS AND THE TAT VARIANTS EXPRESSED. AIM 2 WILL EXPLORE THE FUNCTION OF THE DEFECTIVE RESERVOIR AND TAT VARIANTS ASSOCIATED WITH INTACT AND PARTIALLY FUNCTIONAL PROVIRUSES. AIM 3 WILL EXPLORE THE IMPACT OF TAT VARIANTS ON PROMOTING EXCITOTOXICITY IN PFC CAUSING IMPAIRED EXECUTIVE FUNCTION AND IMPULSE CONTROL DISORDERS USING AN IN VIVO MODEL OF TAT NEUROPATHOGENESIS. THESE STUDIES WILL CONTRIBUTE TO DEFINING THE DIFFERENTIAL AND SYNERGISTIC EFFECTS OF TAT IN PROMOTING NCI. OVERALL, THESE STUDIES WILL LEAD TO A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE ETIOLOGY OF HAND, POTENTIAL DEVELOPMENT OF DIAGNOSTIC ASSAY FOR HAND, AND IDENTIFICATION OF NOVEL TAT-MEDIATED TARGETS TO DEVELOP NEW THERAPEUTICS FOR TREATING NCI.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING CITRIC ACID CYCLE PERTURBATIONS IN COMPLEX I DEFICIENT MITOCHONDRIAL ENCEPHALOPATHY - ABSTRACT MITOCHONDRIAL DISEASES OCCUR IN 1 IN 4500 LIVE BIRTHS. THESE DISEASES ARE RESPIRATORY CHAIN DISORDERS IN WHICH THE MITOCHONDRIA ARE NO LONGER OPERATING EFFICIENTLY TO PRODUCE ATP, USUALLY DUE TO A PROBLEM WITH ONE OR MORE COMPONENTS OF THE OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION MACHINERY. MITOCHONDRIAL DISEASES E.G. COMPLEX I DEFICIENT LEIGH SYNDROME OFTEN MANIFEST AS ENCEPHALOPATHIES WITH FAILURE TO THRIVE AND BIOCHEMICAL DISTURBANCES INCLUDING METABOLIC ACIDOSIS. THE EFFECTIVE TREATMENT OF THESE DISEASES IS HINDERED BY OUR LACK OF UNDERSTANDING OF THE BIOCHEMICAL PATHOMECHANISMS THAT DRIVE NEURONAL DECLINE, BEYOND THE ESTABLISHED BIOENERGETIC DEFICIT IN ATP PRODUCTION. WE HAVE REPORTED CITRIC ACID CYCLE DEFICIENCIES IN THE NDUFS4 KNOCKOUT MOUSE MODEL OF MITOCHONDRIAL COMPLEX I DEFICIENCY, WITH A FOCUS ON FUMARATE. WE ESTABLISHED THE IMPACT OF FUMARATE MEDIATED MODIFICATION OF CYSTEINE RESIDUES TO MODIFY THE E2 COMPONENT OF THE Α-KETOGLUTARATE DEHYDROGENASE (Α-KGDH) COMPLEX, IMPAIRING THE ENZYMATIC ACTIVITY OF THIS COMPLEX. WE HYPOTHESIZED THAT THIS WOULD SHUNT Α-KG TOWARD 2-HYDROXYGLUTARATE (2- HG) PRODUCTION BUT INSTEAD WE FOUND A MARKED DECREASE IN 2-HG LEVELS. THIS LEADS US TO PROPOSE THAT 2-HG IS INSTEAD UTILIZED AS AN ALTERNATIVE FUEL TO GENERATE REDUCING EQUIVALENTS (FADH2) TO SUPPORT RESPIRATION, INDEPENDENT OF THE CI DEFECT. WE WILL INVESTIGATE THESE FINDINGS IN HUMAN PLASMA AND EXPLORE 2-HG AS A THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY, IN ADDITION TO CONSIDERING OTHER METABOLITES THAT MAY REGULATE ADAPTIVE METABOLIC REWIRING TO SUSTAIN NEURONAL HEALTH. WE ALSO TURN OUR ATTENTION TO AN ALTERNATIVE ROLE FOR LACTATE, ONE OF THE MOST ABUNDANT METABOLITES WHOSE ELEVATION IS A DEFINING FEATURE OF HUMAN MITOCHONDRIAL DISEASE. THERE IS SIGNIFICANT ACCUMULATION OF MICROGLIA IN THE CENTER OF THE NDUFS4 KNOCKOUT MOUSE NEUROPATHOLOGICAL LESIONS. WE PROPOSE A NOVEL RATIONALE FOR THE SUSCEPTIBILITY TO OXYGEN TOXICITY IN THIS MOUSE MODEL OF LEIGH SYNDROME. WE FURTHER THAT THIS ALSO UNDERLIES THE TRAFFICKING OF IMMUNE CELLS TO THE AFFECTED BRAIN REGIONS OF THE NDUFS4 KNOCKOUT MOUSE, THIS WILL BE TESTED USING TWO THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES. OVERALL, WE WILL BIOCHEMICALLY LINK THE CI OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION DEFICIENCY TO SELECT METABOLITE PERTURBATIONS, DEFINING BIOCHEMICAL MECHANISMS BEYOND THE UNDERLYING ATP DEFICIT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HEPARAN SULFATE-MEDIATED MECHANISMS OF ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN PATHOLOGY IN DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES (DLB) IS A PROGRESSIVE NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE CHARACTERIZED BY INTRACELLULAR INCLUSIONS OF FIBRILLAR Α-SYNUCLEIN (Α-SYN) PROTEIN. WHILE Α-SYN INCLUSIONS ARE PRIMARILY DETECTED IN SYNAPTICALLY CONNECTED NEURONS, Α-SYN IS ALSO FOUND IN THE EXTRACELLULAR FLUIDS OF DLB PATIENTS, AND IMPAIRING THE NEURONAL INTERNALIZATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS SLOWS Α-SYN PATHOLOGY IN MOUSE MODELS OF SYNUCLEINOPATHY. HEPARAN SULFATE (HS) PROTEOGLYCANS ARE GLYCOPROTEINS THAT INTERACT WITH PROTEIN FIBRILS ON THE CELL SURFACE AND IN THE SYNAPSES, PROMOTING THE CELLULAR INTERNALIZATION OF AMYLOID-Β AND PRION FIBRILS IN VITRO AND ACCELERATING THE DISEASE PROGRESSION IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND PRION-INFECTED MICE. WE AND OTHERS FOUND THAT THE CELLULAR UPTAKE OF PROTEIN FIBRILS IS PROFOUNDLY IMPACTED BY THE HS LENGTH, AND LEVEL AND PATTERN OF SULFATION, WHICH, IMPORTANTLY, VARY WITH BRAIN AGING AND NEURODEGENERATION. DATA FROM OUR LABORATORY SHOWS THAT HS IS A CRUCIAL RECEPTOR FOR THE INTERNALIZATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS IN CORTICAL NEURONS. MOREOVER, GENETICALLY DECREASING HS SULFATION PROFOUNDLY REDUCES THE FORMATION OF Α-SYN INCLUSIONS IN THE SUBSTANTIA NIGRA, HIPPOCAMPUS, AND CORTEX OF MICE INJECTED WITH RECOMBINANT Α-SYN FIBRILS AND SLOWS THE DEVELOPMENT OF BEHAVIORAL DEFICITS. OUR PILOT DRUG TESTS SUGGEST THAT DISRUPTING THE ELECTROSTATIC INTERACTIONS OF HS WITH Α-SYN FIBRILS, POTENTIALLY BY BLOCKING THE HS CELL RECEPTORS OR ALTERING THE LEVELS AND COMPOSITION OF HS, ALMOST COMPLETELY IMPAIRS THE NEURONAL INTERNALIZATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT HS CONTRIBUTES TO DLB PATHOLOGY BY PROMOTING THE NEURONAL INTERNALIZATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS. IN AIM 1, WE PROPOSE TO MEASURE HOW MANIPULATING HS CHAIN LENGTH AND SULFATION IMPACTS THE NEURONAL INTERNALIZATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS I) IN VITRO, USING CORTICAL NEURONS ISOLATED FROM MOUSE MODELS WITH SHORTER HS CHAINS OR DEFICIENT IN HS SULFATION, AND II) IN VIVO, BY MEASURING THE LEVEL AND BRAIN DISTRIBUTION OF Α-SYN INCLUSIONS, NEURONAL LOSS AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF MOTOR AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT IN MICE THAT EXPRESS SHORTER OR LESS SULFATED HS IN SELECTIVE NEURONAL POPULATIONS. WE WILL NEXT TEST THE EFFICACY OF THREE HS-TARGETED DRUGS TO MODULATE THE CHEMICAL COMPOSITION OF HS AND THE INTERNALIZATION AND AGGREGATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS IN PRIMARY CORTICAL NEURONS AND HUMAN IPSC-DERIVED NEURONS OBTAINED FROM PATIENTS WITH SYNUCLEINOPATHY (AIM 2). THROUGH THESE AIMS, WE EXPECT TO DEFINE NEURONAL HS AS A NEW, FUNDAMENTAL HOST COFACTOR CONTRIBUTING TO THE PROGRESSION OF DLB PATHOLOGY. MOREOVER, OUR STUDIES MAY UNCOVER NEW TARGETS FOR THE RATIONAL DESIGN OF NEUROPROTECTIVE THERAPIES FOR DLB PATIENTS BASED ON SELECTIVELY IMPAIRING THE INTERACTION OF HOST HS WITH Α-SYN FIBRILS.

description: SULFATED GLYCOSAMINOGLYCAN HYDROGELS FOR TREATING BRAIN VOLUME LOSS IN TBI - PROJECT SUMMARY MODERATE TO SEVERE TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURIES (MSTBIS) CAUSE SIGNIFICANT BRAIN VOLUME LOSS AND CAVITATION, WHICH CONTRIBUTES TO LIFE-LONG DISABILITIES AND POOR PROGNOSIS FOR A MAJORITY OF MSTBI PATIENTS. THE BRAIN EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX (ECM) IS A MESHWORK OF HIGHLY GLYCOSYLATED PROTEINS THAT PROVIDE STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL SUPPORT TO NEURAL CELLS IN THE BRAIN. ABERRANT HIGH MANNOSE ECM N-GLYCOSYLATION ACTIVATES THE LECTIN COMPLEMENT PATHWAY AND RECRUITMENT OF INFLAMMATORY MICROGLIA. HOWEVER, THERE ARE NO EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS AND THE ROLE OF THESE FACTORS IN PROMOTING BRAIN VOLUME LOSS IN MSTBI IS UNKNOWN. THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED TO DEVELOP RATIONALLY DESIGNED, ENGINEERED BRAIN TISSUE REPLACEMENT TECHNOLOGIES THAT CAN PREVENT BRAIN VOLUME AND FUNCTION LOSSES POST-MSTBI. WE PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED A NOVEL ENGINEERED CHONDROITIN SULFATE (ECS) GLYCOMATERIAL AND DEMONSTRATED THAT ACUTELY IMPLANTED ECS MATRICES PROMOTED SUBACUTE AND CHRONIC NEUROPROTECTION AND FUNCTIONAL VASCULAR REPAIR IN MSTBI LESIONS. OUR PRELIMINARY FINDINGS REVEAL THAT THE ABERRANT UPREGULATION OF HIGH MANNOSE N-GLYCANS IN MSTBI LESIONS CORRELATES WITH LECTIN COMPLEMENT AND MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION, AND THAT SULFATION OPTIMIZED CS OLIGOMERS CAN INHIBIT LECTIN COMPLEMENT ACTIVATION AND NEURONAL CYTOTOXITY. BASED ON THIS EVIDENCE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT INTRACAVITARY IMPLANTATION OF RATIONALLY DESIGNED ECS MATRIX CARRYING SULFATION OPTIMIZED CS OLIGOMERS WILL MITIGATE COMPLEMENT PATHWAY AND MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION INDUCED BRAIN VOLUME LOSS AFTER MSTBI. WE PROPOSE TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS IN THE FOLLOWING THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1- DETERMINE LECTIN COMPLEMENT AND MICROGLIA ACTIVATION INHIBITING EFFECTS OF SULFATION OPTIMIZED CS OLIGOMERS IN VITRO; AIM 2- ELUCIDATE MICROGLIAL REGULATION OF ABERRANT ECM REMODELING IN MSTBI; AND AIM 3 - DETERMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF SULFATION OPTIMIZED ECS MATRIX IMPLANTS IN MITIGATING CHRONIC BRAIN VOLUME AND FUNCTIONAL LOSSES AFTER MSTBI. OUR PUBLISHED AND PRELIMINARY FINDINGS PROVIDE A COMPELLING BASIS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A TARGET SPECIFIC AND DISEASE MODIFYING REGENERATIVE IMMUNOMODULATION THERAPY THAT CAN AMELIORATE ABERRANT ECM REMODELING AND BRAIN VOLUME LOSS IN MSTBI.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ROLE OF ER MEMBRANE CONTACT SITES IN SYNAPSE FORMATION AND PLASTICITY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT NEURONS ARE LARGE, POLARIZED CELLS THAT MUST COORDINATE THE FORMATION AND DYNAMIC FUNCTIONS OF SYNAPTIC CONNECTIONS. MEMBRANE CONTACT SITES (MCSS) BETWEEN CELLULAR ORGANELLES HAVE BEEN INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED AS KEY SIGNALING HUBS FOR COORDINATING A VAST ARRAY OF CELLULAR ACTIVITIES. MCS DISRUPTION UNDERLIES A NUMBER OF NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS, INCLUDING LYSOSOMAL STORAGE DISORDERS, HEREDITARY SPASTIC PARAPLEGIA, AND NEURODEGENERATION, INDICATING CRITICAL ROLES IN THE NERVOUS SYSTEM. MCSS ARE FORMED BY TETHERING PROTEINS IN ORGANELLE MEMBRANES. PDZD8, WHICH WAS RECENTLY LINKED TO INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY, IS AN ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM (ER)-RESIDENT TETHERING PROTEIN AT ER-LE/LYSOSOME AND ER-MITOCHONDRIAL MCSS, WHERE IT IS THOUGHT TO FUNCTION IN LIPID AND CA2+ EXCHANGE, RESPECTIVELY. WE IDENTIFIED PDZD8 AS A REGULATOR OF ACTIVITY-DEPENDENT SYNAPTOGENESIS THROUGH A GENETIC SCREEN IN DROSOPHILA. OUR STUDIES SUPPORT THE MODEL THAT PDZD8 PROMOTES SYNAPSE FORMATION THROUGH ITS ROLE AT ER-LE/LYSOSOME MCSS, WHERE IT PROMOTES LYSOSOME MATURATION TO ACCELERATE AUTOPHAGY DURING PERIODS OF HIGH DEMAND. WE PROPOSE A COMBINATION OF GENETIC, LIVE AND SUPERRESOLUTION IMAGING, AND PROTEOMIC STUDIES TO DEFINE PDZD8’S IN VIVO ROLE IN ACTIVITY-DEPENDENT SYNAPTOGENESIS FROM SIGNAL TO CELLULAR MECHANISM TO TARGET. MORE BROADLY, OUR STUDIES WILL ADDRESS CENTRAL OPEN QUESTIONS IN NEURONAL AUTOPHAGY AND REVEAL FUNDAMENTAL INSIGHTS INTO THE CRITICAL AND DYNAMIC ROLES OF MCSS IN THE NERVOUS SYSTEM.
