description: DEVELOPMENT OF A COMMUNITY ENGAGED TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH NETWORK TO ADVANCE SPANISH-LANGUAGE NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT IN COGNITIVE AGING RESEARCH: ECHAR-TR - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT HISPANIC OLDER ADULTS IN THE UNITED STATES EXPERIENCE A HIGHER BURDEN OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (AD/ADRD), INCLUDING EARLIER SYMPTOM ONSET AND LATER-STAGE DIAGNOSIS COMPARED TO NON-HISPANIC POPULATIONS. TIMELY DIAGNOSIS AND INTERVENTION ARE CRITICAL FOR EFFECTIVE TREATMENT AND IMPROVED OUTCOMES; HOWEVER, SIGNIFICANT GAPS REMAIN. KEY AMONG THESE IS THE LACK OF PSYCHOMETRICALLY ROBUST NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT TOOLS AVAILABLE IN SPANISH, THE PREFERRED LANGUAGE FOR NEARLY 40 MILLION HISPANIC INDIVIDUALS IN THE UNITED STATES. LIMITED AVAILABILITY OF VALIDATED TOOLS FOR DIAGNOSIS OF SPANISH-SPEAKING POPULATIONS CONTRIBUTES TO CHALLENGES IN ACCURATE CLINICAL ASSESSMENT AND EARLY DETECTION OF AD/ADRD. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO DEVELOP A NATIONWIDE INTERDISCIPLINARY TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH NETWORK DEDICATED TO RIGOROUSLY ADVANCING THE CREATION AND ROBUST VALIDATION OF SPANISH-LANGUAGE NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL TOOLS FOR AD/ADRD EVALUATIONS. THE NETWORK WILL LEVERAGE EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE FROM A COMMUNITY ENGAGED RESEARCH NETWORK – THE ECHAR NETWORK – AND WILL INVOLVE COLLABORATION AMONG NEUROPSYCHOLOGISTS, COMMUNITY PARTNERS, AND HEALTH PROVIDERS. IN PHASE I (R61), THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH THE NETWORK AND IDENTIFY COGNITIVE HEALTH NEEDS ACROSS SITES. IN PHASE II (R33), ASSESSMENT TOOLS WILL BE DEVELOPED AND PILOTED IN CLINICAL RESEARCH SETTINGS. THESE TOOLS WILL BE REFINED BASED ON PSYCHOMETRIC ANALYSES AND CROSS-SITE FEEDBACK PRIOR TO BROADER DISSEMINATION. THE PROPOSED WORK DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THE NEED FOR VALIDATED NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL TOOLS TO SUPPORT ACCURATE DIAGNOSIS AND CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING IN SPANISH-SPEAKING POPULATIONS. THIS COMMUNITY-TO-RESEARCH LAB-TOCLINIC MODEL AND MULTI-SITE TRANSLATIONAL FRAMEWORK WILL GENERATE SCALABLE TOOLS AND SHARED RESOURCES THAT ADVANCE COGNITIVE AGING RESEARCH, IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF DEMENTIA CARE FOR A RAPIDLY GROWING SEGMENT OF THE U.S. POPULATION.

description: DEVELOPMENT OF A NONHUMAN PRIMATE INFRASTRUCTURE FOR INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH ON PERIMENOPAUSE AND AGING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THIS APPLICATION RESPONDS TO PAR-25-218 TO SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE TO ADVANCE THE INTERDISCIPLINARY SCIENCE OF AGING. WE PROPOSE TO EXPAND AND FORMALIZE A UNIQUE, INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE CENTERED ON CHARACTERIZING A COLONY OF AGING FEMALE BABOONS AT THE KEELING CENTER FOR COMPARATIVE MEDICINE AND RESEARCH (KCCMR) OF THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS MD ANDERSON CANCER CENTER. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP, CHARACTERIZE, AND VALIDATE A COMPREHENSIVE NHP RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE FOR FEMALE AGING, ANCHORED TO HUMAN-DEFINED PERIMENOPAUSAL MEASURES. LEVERAGING A UNIQUE POPULATION OF AGING FEMALE BABOONS AT THE KCCRM, WE WILL INTEGRATE BEHAVIORAL, ENDOCRINE, COGNITIVE, NEUROIMAGING, BIOMARKER, AND PHYSIOLOGICAL DATA INTO THE NATIONAL BABOON RESEARCH RESOURCE (NBRR) PORTAL TO SUPPORT CROSS-DISCIPLINARY RESEARCH. IN THE R61 PHASE, WE WILL ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY AND VALIDITY OF KEY METHODS TO CHARACTERIZE PERIMENOPAUSE IN 24 BABOONS, INCLUDING 1) TRAINING FOR URINE COLLECTION TO ENABLE HORMONAL ASSAYS; 2) USING ANOGENITAL SWELLING VARIATION AS A PROXY FOR HORMONAL PROFILES; AND 3) MONITORING CARDIOVASCULAR AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY VIA MINIMALLY INVASIVE IMPLANTS. THESE EFFORTS WILL ESTABLISH FOUNDATIONAL TOOLS AND PROTOCOLS FOR SUBSEQUENT INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT. IN THE R33 PHASE, WE WILL EXPAND THE COHORT TO THE OLDEST 51 FEMALE BABOONS AND IMPLEMENT A LONGITUDINAL DESIGN TO CAPTURE MULTIMODAL DATA ACROSS NEUROLOGICAL, ENDOCRINE, PHYSIOLOGICAL, BEHAVIORAL, AND COGNITIVE DOMAINS. WE WILL HARMONIZE THESE MEASURES WITH HUMAN COHORT DATASETS (E.G., MIDUS) USING CONSTRUCT MAPPING TO ENSURE TRANSLATIONAL VALIDITY. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL DEVELOP A SCORING SYSTEM FOR EARLY LIFE STRESS (ELS) BASED ON MEDICAL AND REARING HISTORIES, PARALLELING HUMAN CUMULATIVE STRESS MODELS. BY THE CONCLUSION OF THE R33 PHASE, WE WILL HAVE CREATED A VALIDATED, SHAREABLE NHP INFRASTRUCTURE AND SUSTAINABLE PLATFORM FOR RESEARCH ON FEMALE REPRODUCTIVE AGING, ELS, NEURODEGENERATION, AND INTERVENTION STRATEGIES. THIS RESOURCE WILL SUPPORT FUTURE R01 OR U-SERIES APPLICATIONS AND ADVANCE TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH IN WOMEN’S HEALTH.

description: FROM CONCEPT TO PRACTICE: IMPLEMENTING AND SCALING AN ADVERSE EVENT REPORTING TOOLKIT FOR AGING AND SERIOUS ILLNESS RESEARCH - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CLINICAL RESEARCH IS VITAL TO IMPROVING CARE FOR OLDER ADULTS WITH SERIOUS ILLNESS (OASI), YET STANDARD SERIOUS AND NON-SERIOUS ADVERSE EVENT [(S)AE] REPORTING OFTEN FLAGS EXPECTED OUTCOMES—SUCH AS HOSPITALIZATIONS, CLINICAL DECLINE, OR DEATH—THAT ARE UNRELATED TO STUDY PROCEDURES. THIS LEADS TO EXCESSIVE EXPEDITED REPORTING, INCREASED INVESTIGATOR AND SPONSOR BURDEN, INFLATED DSMB AND IRB BURDEN, AND BARRIERS TO INCLUDING OASI IN RESEARCH. BETWEEN 2020 AND 2025, A NATIONAL MULTI-PARTNER PANEL FUNDED BY THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE ON AGING (NIA) AND COLLABORATING PEPPER CENTERS AT MOUNT SINAI AND WAKE FOREST DEVELOPED THE DECISION-MAKING FOR ADVERSE EVENT REPORTING TOOLKIT (DART)—A STAKEHOLDER-INFORMED RESOURCE COMPRISING A DECISION ALGORITHM, OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS, ANNOTATED CASE EXAMPLES, REPORTING TEMPLATES, DATA AND SAFETY MONITORING PLAN (DSMP) LANGUAGE, AND IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE TO SUPPORT CONTEXT-APPROPRIATE (S)AE CLASSIFICATION AND REPORTING IN BEHAVIORAL, HEALTH SERVICES, AND RELATED TRIALS INVOLVING OASI. THIS R61/R33 PROJECT WILL VALIDATE, REFINE, AND SCALE DART. IN THE R61 PHASE, WE WILL: (1) RETROSPECTIVELY MEASURE PATTERNS OF UNDER- AND OVER-REPORTING IN COMPLETED STUDIES TO IDENTIFY WHERE DART COULD ENHANCE THE CONSISTENCY, TRANSPARENCY, AND EFFICIENCY OF (S)AE REPORTING; (2) PROSPECTIVELY PILOT DART IN FIVE TO SIX ONGOING STUDIES TO EVALUATE FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, USABILITY, FIDELITY, AND IMPACT ON REPORTING PRACTICES; AND (3) IDENTIFY EVIDENCE-BASED IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES THROUGH QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS OF INTERVIEWS AND FOCUS GROUPS WITH PARTNERS AND USERS. TRANSITION MILESTONES INCLUDE DEMONSTRATION OF FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND FIDELITY, IMPROVED RATIONALE AND ALIGNMENT OF REPORTING PRACTICES, AND A DEFINED SET OF PRE- AND POST-ADOPTION STRATEGIES FOR SCALING. IN THE R33 PHASE, WE WILL CO-DESIGN AND DEPLOY MULTILEVEL IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES ACROSS NATIONAL AGING AND PALLIATIVE CARE RESEARCH NETWORKS TO: (4) OPERATIONALIZE NETWORK- AND STUDY-LEVEL SUPPORTS (TRAINING, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, LEARNING COLLABORATIVES, AND “SUPER-USER” MENTORING); (5) MEASURE SPREAD, KNOWLEDGE ACQUISITION, AND ORGANIZATIONAL READINESS TO ADOPT DART ACROSS NETWORKS; (6) EVALUATE STUDY-LEVEL IMPLEMENTATION EFFECTIVENESS, FIDELITY, CONFIDENCE, AND ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN ENGAGEMENT AND OUTCOMES; AND (7) DEVELOP AND PILOT A SUSTAINABILITY PLAN TO EMBED DART WITHIN PARTNER INFRASTRUCTURES AND PROFESSIONAL SOCIETIES. LEVERAGING PARTNERSHIPS WITH KEY NATIONAL RESEARCH NETWORKS, THE DART PROGRAM WILL BE SUSTAINED AS A DURABLE PLATFORM THAT PROMOTES OVERALL TRANSPARENCY, EFFICIENCY, AND CONSISTENCY IN RESEARCH ADMINISTRATION FOR RELEVANT STUDIES; ENHANCED PERSON-CENTEREDNESS IN STUDY ADMINISTRATION; AND AS A RESULT, SCIENCE THAT BENEFITS OASI.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPING MUTATION SIGNATURE EXTRACTION (MSE) FOR HUMAN TISSUES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT (PUBLIC) MUTATION SIGNATURES CHARACTERISTIC OF HUMAN CANCERS ARE A PRODUCT OF MUTAGENIC EVENTS LEADING TO CANCER- CAUSING MUTATIONS THAT INITIATE OR PROMOTE TUMORIGENESIS. THEREFORE, SCREENING FOR THESE SIGNATURES IN NORMAL TISSUES COULD AID IN CANCER EARLY DETECTION, PREVENTION, AND INTERCEPTION. THESE SIGNATURES HAVE BEEN CAPTURED BY SEQUENCING THE GENOMES OF MULTIPLE CLONES DERIVED FROM ADAPTING BRONCHIAL BRUSHINGS TO GROW IN TISSUE CULTURE, OR MORE RECENTLY, FROM SURVEYING LARGE PORTIONS OF THE GENOME FROM A VARIETY OF TISSUES BY ERROR-CORRECTED SEQUENCING. UNFORTUNATELY, THE FIRST APPROACH IS LIMITED TO THOSE VERY FEW HUMAN TISSUES THAT CAN BE CULTURED AND IS COMPLETELY IMPRACTICAL IN A CLINICAL SETTING WHILE THE SECOND APPROACH DOES NOT PROVIDE GENOME PRIVACY TO THE PATIENT AND IS LIMITED TO THE WESTERN EUROPEAN GENOME TO DIFFERENTIATE BONA FIDE MUTATIONS FROM NATURALLY OCCURRING SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE POLYMORPHISMS. THUS, A NEW METHOD IS NEEDED TO DETECT MUTATION SIGNATURES THAT NEITHER REQUIRES ESTABLISHING TISSUES TO GROW IN CULTURE NOR RELIES ON SEQUENCING LARGE PORTIONS OF THE GENOME. IN THIS REGARD, WE DEMONSTRATE THAT DEEPLY SEQUENCING A SINGLE SHORT REGION OF GENOMIC DNA BY THE NOVEL MAMMALIAN MAXIMUM DEPTH SEQUENCING (MMDS) ASSAY CAN DETECT A MUTATION SIGNATURE IN THE NORMAL TISSUES OF MICE FOLLOWING A CARCINOGEN EXPOSURE. FURTHER, BY INCREASING THE AMOUNT OF GENOMIC DNA SEQUENCED, WE PROPOSE THAT MMDS COULD ALSO IDENTIFY THE RARER MUTATION SIGNATURES IN NORMAL HUMAN TISSUES. TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP MUTATION SIGNATURE EXTRACTION (MSE) FOR NORMAL HUMAN TISSUES BASED ON MMDS IN FOUR AIMS. IN AIM 1 WE WILL DETERMINE WHICH REGION OF THE GENOME YIELDS SUFFICIENT INDEPENDENT (BARCODED) DNA FRAGMENTS FOR MSE TO CAPTURE ENOUGH MUTATIONS TO DERIVE A MUTATION SIGNATURE. IN AIM 2, WE WILL TEST AND OPTIMIZE AS NEEDED MSE TO REACH A DETECTION LIMIT REQUIRED TO DETECT THE RARE MUTATIONS OF A MUTATION SIGNATURE. IN AIM 3, WE WILL TEST AND OPTIMIZE AS NEEDED MSE TO DETECT THE MUTATIONS COMPRISING THE MUTATION SIGNATURE IN CULTURED HUMAN BRONCHIAL EPITHELIAL CELLS EXPOSED TO A TOBACCO SMOKE CARCINOGEN. FINALLY, IN AIM 4 WE WILL EVALUATE THE ABILITY OF MSE TO DETECT THE MUTATIONS OF THE SIGNATURE CHARACTERISTIC OF TOBACCO SMOKING IN ACTUAL HUMAN BRONCHIAL BRUSHINGS ISOLATED FROM PATIENTS THAT SMOKE TOBACCO. COMPLETION OF THESE FOUR AIMS WILL DEVELOP MSE TO IDENTIFY THE MUTATIONS DEFINING MUTATION SIGNATURES IN HUMAN TISSUES, ULTIMATELY FOR USE IN CANCER EARLY DETECTION, PREVENTION, AND INTERCEPTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF UTERINE PERISTALSIS IMAGING (UPI) FOR PREDICTING UTERINE RECEPTIVITY AND FROZEN EMBRYO TRANSFER OUTCOMES - SUMMARY/ABSTRACT EACH YEAR IN THE UNITED STATES, APPROXIMATELY 200,000 PATIENTS UNDERGO FROZEN EMBRYO TRANSFER (FET) IN HOPES OF ACHIEVING PREGNANCY. HOWEVER, EVEN WHEN EMBRYOS ARE OF HIGH QUALITY AND FET OCCURS DURING THE WINDOW OF IMPLANTATION, THE SUCCESS RATE REMAINS SUBOPTIMAL AT APPROXIMATELY 60%. CURRENT UTERINE RECEPTIVITY ASSESSMENT FOCUSES MAINLY ON ENDOMETRIAL PROPERTIES, NEGLECTING THE CRITICAL ROLE OF MYOMETRIAL CONTRACTILE FUNCTION, DESPITE EVIDENCE THAT EXCESSIVE UTERINE PERISTALSIS REDUCES PREGNANCY RATES BY ~50%. CLINICIANS CURRENTLY LACK TOOLS TO NONINVASIVELY AND QUANTITATIVELY ASSESS UTERINE PERISTALSIS DURING THE FET PROCEDURE. WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE UTERINE PERISTALSIS IMAGING (UPI), A NOVEL NONINVASIVE DIAGNOSTIC TECHNOLOGY THAT PROVIDES OBJECTIVE, QUANTITATIVE MEASUREMENTS OF UTERINE PERISTALSIS TO PREDICT FET OUTCOMES. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT ABERRANT, SPECIFICALLY ABNORMAL DIRECTIONAL PATTERNS OF UTERINE PERISTALSIS PREDICT PREGNANCY OUTCOMES (P<0.02), POSITIONING UPI AS A PROMISING DIAGNOSTIC PLATFORM. THE R61 PHASE (MONTHS 0–24) WILL DEVELOP A CLINICAL-GRADE UPI SYSTEM BY REPLACING STRUCTURAL MRI WITH RAPID 3D TRANSABDOMINAL ULTRASOUND AND BY CREATING AUTOMATED ALGORITHMS FOR CLASSIFYING ABERRANT PERISTALSIS. WE WILL VALIDATE THE SYSTEM IN 20 HEALTHY WOMEN AND ESTABLISH SAFETY IN 20 FET PATIENTS. QUANTITATIVE MILESTONES WITH BINARY GO/NO-GO CRITERIA WILL RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT, AUTOMATED ANALYSIS ACCURACY, PROSPECTIVE SAFETY DOCUMENTATION, AND CLINICAL WORKFLOW INTEGRATION. ALL TRANSITION CRITERIA MUST BE MET TO ADVANCE TO R33. THE R33 PHASE (MONTHS 25-60) WILL CONDUCT A PROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY ENROLLING N=100 FET PATIENTS UNDERGOING UPI ASSESSMENT AT TWO TIMEPOINTS: APPROXIMATELY 10-14 DAYS AFTER INITIATION OF ESTRADIOL PRIMING AND ON THE DAY OF FET BEFORE TRANSFER. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CERVIX- TO-FUNDUS AND FUNDUS-TO-CERVIX PERISTALSIS RATIOS, ALONG WITH PERISTALSIS FREQUENCY AND MAGNITUDE, CAN ACCURATELY PREDICT CLINICAL PREGNANCY OUTCOMES AFTER FET. WE WILL PERFORM RECEIVER OPERATING CHARACTERISTIC (ROC) ANALYSIS WITH THE PRIMARY HYPOTHESIS THAT THE CERVIX-TO-FUNDUS RATIO PREDICTS PREGNANCY WITH AN AREA UNDER THE CURVE (AUC) ≥0.70, AND DEVELOP MULTIVARIABLE PREDICTION MODELS INTEGRATING UPI METRICS WITH CLINICAL VARIABLES (AGE, BODY MASS INDEX, ENDOMETRIAL THICKNESS, EMBRYO QUALITY, FET HISTORY). WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY SCHOOL OF MEDICINE AND AFFILIATED BARNES-JEWISH HOSPITAL PROVIDE EXCEPTIONAL INSTITUTIONAL SUPPORT WITH A FERTILITY CENTER PERFORMING APPROXIMATELY 600 FET CYCLES ANNUALLY AND A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM WITH EXPERTISE IN IMAGING TECHNOLOGY, CLINICAL REPRODUCTIVE MEDICINE, BIOSTATISTICS, AND REGULATORY AFFAIRS. BY ENABLING OBJECTIVE ASSESSMENT OF UTERINE RECEPTIVITY AND MYOMETRIAL DYSFUNCTION, UPI COULD DRAMATICALLY IMPROVE PREGNANCY SUCCESS RATES FOR HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF WOMEN IN THE UNITED STATES UNDERGOING FET ANNUALLY, PARTICULARLY THOSE WITH RECURRENT IMPLANTATION FAILURE CURRENTLY ATTRIBUTED TO UNEXPLAINED CAUSES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AUTOMATED VASCULAR ACCESS DEVICE DEVELOPMENT - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CENTRAL VENOUS CATHETERIZATION AND ARTERIAL CANNULATION ARE LIFESAVING PROCEDURES PERFORMED 5-7 MILLION TIMES PER YEAR IN THE U.S., OFTEN BY LESS-EXPERIENCED PROVIDERS IN URGENT SITUATIONS. HIGH RATES OF COMPLICATION AND FAILURE (4-19%) REMAIN A PROBLEM, EVEN WITH ULTRASOUND GUIDANCE. THE ABILITY OF LESS EXPERIENCED PROVIDERS TO SAFELY AND EFFECTIVELY ACHIEVE ARTERIAL AND CENTRAL VENOUS ACCESS IS A SIGNIFICANT UNMET NEED IN EMERGENCY MEDICINE, TRAUMA AND CRITICAL CARE. VASCULAR RESCUE IS DEVELOPING A PORTABLE, SELF-CONTAINED, SELF-POWERED, SEMI- AUTOMATED VASCULAR ACCESS DEVICE (AVAD) THAT WILL ALLOW LESS-THAN-EXPERIENCED PROVIDERS TO SAFELY, QUICKLY, AND RELIABLY ACHIEVE CENTRAL VENOUS AND ARTERIAL CANNULATION. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS CATALYZE PROPOSAL IS TO MOVE THE AVAD PROTOTYPE TO SUCCESSFUL AUTOMATED CANNULATION OF THE TARGET VESSEL BY THE SHEATH, WHICH COMPETING DEVICES CANNOT DO. IN THE R61 PHASE WE WILL AUTOMATE ALL THE STEPS OF SUCCESSFUL CANNULATION. IN THE R33 PHASE WE WILL DESIGN AND BUILD THE STERILE PATIENT-SPECIFIC CASSETTE AND BEGIN THE REGULATORY PROCESS FOR FDA SUBMISSION. (R61) AIM 1: TO DESIGN, CONSTRUCT AND TEST SENSORS AND AUTOMATION TO DETECT PUNCTURE OF A BLOOD VESSEL, DISTINGUISH ARTERY VS. VEIN AND ADVANCE A GUIDEWIRE INTO THE VESSEL. R61 MILESTONE 1: SUCCESSFUL IDENTIFICATION AND CANNULATION OF A PORCINE FEMORAL ARTERY AND VEIN IN VIVO (MORE THAN 8 OUT OF 10 ATTEMPTS) WITH A GUIDEWIRE. (R61) AIM 2: TO DESIGN CONSTRUCT AND TEST A CATHETER SYSTEM TO CANNULATE THE TARGET VESSEL AUTOMATICALLY. R61 MILESTONE 2: TO DEMONSTRATE DETECTION AND SUCCESSFUL CANNULATION OF A PORCINE ARTERY AND VEIN IN VIVO (GREATER THAN 4 OUT OF 5 ATTEMPTS) WITH A CATHETER. THIS WILL BE THE PIVOTAL MILESTONE THAT WILL COMPLETE THE R61 PHASE OF THE PROJECT. (R33) AIM 3: TO DESIGN AND ENGINEER THE STERILE CASSETTE (PATIENT-SPECIFIC AND DISPOSABLE) TO INTERFACE WITH THE REUSEABLE AVAD BASE UNIT TO PUNCTURE AND CANNULATE VESSELS. R33 MILESTONE 3: DEMONSTRATE IN A PORCINE OR CADAVER MODEL (>5 CASES) A FUNCTIONAL INTERFACE FOR VASCULAR CANNULATION BETWEEN A STERILIZABLE DISPOSABLE CASSETTE AND THE AVAD BASE UNIT. (R33) AIM 4: GENERATE A REGULATORY PATH DOCUMENT TO DEFINE MILESTONES FOR FDA SUBMISSION. FUNDING OF THE CATALYZE PROPOSAL WILL ALIGN AND INTEGRATE OUR DEVICE DEVELOPMENT TEAM WITH THE EXPERTISE OF THE ACCELERATOR PARTNERS TO BRING THIS LIFE-SAVING TECHNOLOGY FORWARD TOWARDS WIDESPREAD CLINICAL USE.

description: IMPROVING SLEEP IN EARLY CHILDHOOD: A MULTILEVEL SLEEP HEALTH PROMOTION INTERVENTION FOR PRIMARY CARE - 1 PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  2 SLEEP HEALTH DISPARITIES ARE EVIDENT AS EARLY AS ONE YEAR OF AGE AND PERSIST THROUGH ADOLESCENCE. SLEEP  3 DEFICIENCY DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTS CHILDREN FROM LOW-INCOME HOUSEHOLDS AND HISTORICALLY MARGINALIZED RACIAL  4 AND ETHNIC GROUPS. EARLY CHILDHOOD SLEEP DEFICIENCY IS LINKED TO LONG-TERM HEALTH PROBLEMS, INCLUDING OBESITY,  5 METABOLIC SYNDROME, CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, AND BEHAVIORAL ISSUES. EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIORAL SLEEP  6 INTERVENTIONS ARE EFFECTIVE IN EARLY CHILDHOOD, YET FEW HAVE INCLUDED LOW-INCOME FAMILIES. PEDIATRIC PRIMARY CARE  7 OFFICES (PCOS) THAT PRIMARILY SERVE THESE FAMILIES ARE WELL POSITIONED TO ADDRESS SLEEP HEALTH DISPARITIES. WHILE  8 BOTH PARENTS AND PRIMARY CARE CLINICIANS (PCCS) IDENTIFY SLEEP AS A PRIORITY, THEY REPORT LIMITED SUPPORT,  9 RESOURCES, AND SLEEP HEALTH LITERACY AS BARRIERS TO IMPLEMENTING EVIDENCE-BASED GUIDELINES. TO ADDRESS THESE 10 GAPS, WE PROPOSE TO SYSTEMATICALLY ADAPT AND REFINE AN EVIDENCE-BASED BSI, SLEEP WELL, BEE WELL (SWBW) 11 FOR PEDIATRIC PRIMARY CARE SETTING. SWBW, GROUNDED IN SOCIAL COGNITIVE THEORY, WAS CO-DESIGNED WITH PARENTS 12 AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS FOR CONTEXTUAL AND CULTURAL RELEVANCE AND FOUND TO BE FEASIBLE AND ACCEPTABLE TO LOW- 13 INCOME FAMILIES WITH IMPROVED SLEEP HEALTH IN TODDLERS ENROLLED IN FEDERALLY FUNDED EARLY HEAD START CHILDHOOD 14 EDUCATION PROGRAMS. DURING THE R61 PHASE (YEAR 1), WE WILL USE A RAPID-CYCLE USER-CENTERED DESIGN TO ADAPT 15 SWBW FOR PCOS SERVING LOW-INCOME FAMILIES (AIM 1). ENGAGING PARENTS, PCCS, AND NATIONAL PRACTICE-BASED 16 RESEARCH NETWORK PARTNERS IN A COMMUNITY ADVISORY BOARD (CAB), WE WILL ITERATIVELY REFINE AND ADAPT SWBW 17 WHILE CONCURRENTLY FINALIZING THE STUDY PROTOCOL, MANUAL OF OPERATIONS, STUDY DOCUMENTS, AND IRB APPROVAL. IN 18 THE R33 PHASE (YEARS 2–5), WE WILL EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF SWBW IN IMPROVING CHILDREN'S SLEEP HEALTH 19 AND ASSESS THE MODIFYING EFFECTS OF SOCIAL DETERMINANTS—INCLUDING FAMILY PSYCHOSOCIAL HEALTH, HOUSEHOLD 20 CHAOS, AND NEIGHBORHOOD CONTEXT (AIM 2); DETERMINE WHETHER SWBW IMPROVES SLEEP-RELATED KNOWLEDGE, 21 ATTITUDES, BELIEFS, AND PRACTICES AMONG PARENTS AND PCCS (AIM 3); AND IDENTIFY CONTEXTUAL FACTORS INFLUENCING 22 THE REACH, ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND MAINTENANCE OF SWBW IN PEDIATRIC PRIMARY CARE (AIM 4). THE R33 23 PHASE WILL USE A 2×2 FACTORIAL QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN, ENROLLING 500 FAMILIES OVER TWO SEQUENTIAL 15-MONTH 24 RECRUITMENT WAVES AT A SINGLE PCO. IN WAVE 1, 250 FAMILIES WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO EITHER SWBW OR USUAL CARE. 25 IN WAVE 2, ALL PCCS WILL COMPLETE SIX BRIEF, WEB-BASED SLEEP HEALTH TRAINING MODULES AS PART OF ROUTINE 26 PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PRIOR TO THE RANDOMIZATION OF AN ADDITIONAL 250 FAMILIES TO SWBW OR USUAL CARE. THIS 27 DESIGN WILL GENERATE FOUR ANALYTIC ARMS, ALLOWING US TO ASSESS BOTH THE MAIN EFFECTS OF THE SWBW INTERVENTION 28 AND THE POTENTIAL ADDITIVE OR SYNERGISTIC IMPACT OF PCC SLEEP HEALTH TRAINING ON CHILD SLEEP OUTCOMES. ALIGNED 29 WITH NHLBI'S MISSION AND LIFE'S ESSENTIAL 8, OUR FINDINGS WILL INFORM FUTURE IMPLEMENTATION EFFORTS TO IMPROVE 30 SLEEP AND CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH EARLY IN LIFE AND REDUCE SLEEP HEALTH DISPARITIES IN CHILDREN.

description: DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF HUMAN NIS-LNCRNA ASO AS A NOVEL POTENTIAL DRUG TO NEUROPATHIC PAIN TREATMENT - SUMMARY CHRONIC NEUROPATHIC PAIN IS A COMPLEX AND DEBILITATING PUBLIC HEALTH PROBLEM DUE TO ITS HIGH INCIDENCE IN THE GENERAL POPULATION, ASSOCIATED SOCIAL BURDEN, AND LIMITED EFFICACY OF CURRENT TREATMENTS. OPIOIDS ARE THE LAST OPTION FOR PHARMACOLOGICAL TREATMENT OF THIS DISORDER, BUT AN OVERRELIANCE ON OPIOID PRESCRIPTION FOR PAIN MANAGEMENT CAUSES A SIGNIFICANT AND ALARMING EPIDEMIC OF OPIOID ADDICTION AND OVERDOSE DEATH. DEVELOPING SAFE, EFFECTIVE, NON-OPIOID, AND NON-ADDICTIVE APPROACHES IS THUS CRITICALLY URGENT. WE RECENTLY IDENTIFIED NERVE INJURY-SPECIFIC LONG NON-CODING RNA (NIS) AS A KEY PLAYER AND POTENTIAL TARGET IN CHRONIC NEUROPATHIC PAIN. GIVEN THAT THE HUMANIZED NIS MOUSE MODEL IS NOT FEASIBLE AND THAT NIS SEQUENCE AND ITS PROMOTER BETWEEN HUMANS AND MONKEYS ARE ALMOST IDENTICAL, THIS PROPOSAL WILL DEVELOP THE ANTISENSE OLIGONUCLEOTIDE (ASO) SPECIFICALLY TARGETING BOTH HUMAN AND MONKEY NIS AND VALIDATE IT AS A SAFE, NON-OPIOID, NON-ADDICTIVE, LONG- LASTING ANALGESICS IN THE NONHUMAN PRIMATE MODEL OF NERVE INJURY-INDUCED NEUROPATHIC PAIN. IN THE R61 PHASE, WE WILL FIRST DESIGN, SYNTHESIZE AND PURIFY TRANSLATIONALLY SUITABLE ASOS AND THEN SCREEN THESE ASO CANDIDATES BY EVALUATING THEIR INHIBITORY EFFICACIES ON HIGH GLUCOSE- OR PACLITAXEL-INDUCED INCREASES IN THE LEVELS OF NIS AND ITS DOWNSTREAM GENES, SELECTIVITY/SPECIFICITY OF THESE INHIBITORY EFFECTS, AND POTENTIAL TOXICITY IN CULTURED HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELL-DERIVED SENSORY NEURONS. INHIBITORY EFFICACY OF OPTIMAL NIS ASO (BASED ON THE CRITERIA: STRONGEST INHIBITORY EFFECT, HIGHEST SELECTIVITY/SPECIFICITY, AND LACK OF CYTOTOXICITY) WILL ALSO BE VALIDATED IN CULTURED DORSAL ROOT GANGLION (DRG) NEURONS FROM MONKEY OR HUMAN DONORS. FINALLY, SPECIFICALLY INHIBITORY EFFICACY OF INTRATHECAL OPTIMAL NIS ASO ON HUMAN NIS OVEREXPRESSION IN MOUSE MICROINJECTED DRGS WILL BE EVALUATED. THE R33 PHASE WILL FURTHER VALIDATE OPTIMAL NIS ASO IDENTIFIED ABOVE IN IN VIVO MONKEY MODEL OF NEUROPATHIC PAIN. IN SPECIFIC AIM 1, WE WILL VALIDATE DOSE-DEPENDENT AND LONG-LASTING ANTINOCICEPTION OF INTRATHECAL OPTIMAL NIS ASO AGAINST THE DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF NEUROPATHIC PAIN IN THE NONHUMAN PRIMATES WITH UNILATERAL L7 SPINAL NERVE LIGATION (SNL) USING BEHAVIORAL ASSAYS, FUNCTIONAL MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING MEASURE AND MACHINE-LEARNING DEEPLABCUT VIDEO-BASED ANALYSIS. THE EFFICACY OF INTRATHECAL OPTIMAL NIS ASO IN BLOCKING SNL-INDUCED INCREASES IN THE LEVELS OF NIS AND ITS DOWNSTREAM GENES IN INJURED DRG OF MONKEYS WILL ALSO BE EXAMINED. IN SPECIFIC AIM 2, POTENTIAL TOXICITY IN THE DRG, SPINAL CORD AND BRAIN REGIONS, CENTRAL NERVE SYSTEM-RELATED KEY DYSFUNCTIONS, AND SYSTEMIC SIDE EFFECTS FOLLOWING INTRATHECAL OPTIMAL NIS ASO WILL BE MONITORED IN THE NONHUMAN PRIMATES. COMPLETING THIS PROPOSAL WILL DEMONSTRATE NIS ASO AS A SAFE, NON- OPIOID, NON-ADDICTIVE, HIGHLY EFFICIENCY AND LONG-LASTING ANALGESICS FOR NEUROPATHIC PAIN THERAPIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DETERMINING THE POTENTIAL OF A NOVEL NON-MUSCLE MYOSIN II THERAPEUTIC IN PEDIATRIC BRAIN TUMORS - PROJECT SUMMARY DIFFUSE MIDLINE GLIOMA (DMG) IS A DEVASTATING PEDIATRIC BRAIN TUMOR WITH A MEDIAN AGE AT DIAGNOSIS OF 6-7 YEARS AND A MEDIAN SURVIVAL OF ONLY 9-12 MONTHS. THESE TUMORS ARISE IN SURGICALLY INACCESSIBLE MIDLINE STRUCTURES AND PROFOUNDLY RESIST CHEMOTHERAPY, LEAVING FOCAL RADIATION THERAPY (RT) AS THE ONLY STANDARD TREATMENT. THE DEFINING MOLECULAR HALLMARK OF DMG IS THE H3K27M HISTONE MUTATION, WHICH REPROGRAMS THE EPIGENETIC LANDSCAPE TO SUSTAIN TUMOR CELLS IN A PROLIFERATIVE, UNDIFFERENTIATED STATE AND DRIVES WIDESPREAD TRANSCRIPTIONAL DYSREGULATION. MT-125, A BRAIN PENETRANT, FIRST-IN-CLASS SMALL MOLECULE INHIBITOR TARGETING THE ACTIN-BINDING MOLECULAR MOTORS NON-MUSCLE MYOSIN IIA AND IIB (NMIIA/IIB), HAS RECENTLY ADVANCED TO PHASE 1/2 CLINICAL TESTING IN GLIOBLASTOMA (GBM), A HIGHLY AGGRESSIVE ADULT BRAIN CANCER THAT SHARES MANY FEATURES WITH DMG. DEVELOPED WITH SUPPORT FROM THE NIH BLUEPRINT NEUROTHERAPEUTICS PROGRAM (BPN), MT-125 HAS RECEIVED FDA ORPHAN DRUG (ODD) AND FAST TRACK DESIGNATIONS FOR GBM AND HAS DEMONSTRATED POTENT ANTI-TUMOR ACTIVITY IN PRECLINICAL MODELS, INDUCING GBM CELL DEATH BOTH AS A SINGLE AGENT AND IN COMBINATION WITH RT AND FDA-APPROVED KINASE INHIBITORS THROUGH A MECHANISM INVOLVING OXIDATIVE STRESS. THE RESEARCH TO ACCELERATE CURES AND EQUITY (RACE) FOR CHILDREN ACT PORTION OF THE FDA REAUTHORIZATION ACT MANDATES THAT ALL NEW ONCOLOGY DRUGS BE EVALUATED IN PEDIATRIC CANCERS WHEN THEIR MOLECULAR TARGETS ARE RELEVANT. THEREFORE, AN FDA DIRECTIVE TO EVALUATE MT-125 IN A DMG CLINICAL TRIAL IS ANTICIPATED IN THE NEAR TERM. WHILE THE FDA IS UNLIKELY TO REQUIRE ADDITIONAL NONCLINICAL TESTING TO PROCEED TO THE CLINIC FOR DMG ONCE SAFETY IS ESTABLISHED IN THE PHASE 1/2 GBM TRIAL, IT IS CRITICAL THAT DMG EFFICACY AND TOLERABILITY STUDIES BE PERFORMED TO ENSURE PHYSICIANS AND FAMILIES CAN BE FULLY INFORMED OF THE ANTICIPATED BENEFIT-RISK PROFILE. THEREFORE, THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL ESTABLISH THE PRECLINICAL EFFICACY AND DEVELOPMENTAL SAFETY PROFILE OF MT-125 IN DMG TO GUIDE CLINICAL TRIAL READINESS. DURING THE INITIAL R61 PHASE, SURVIVAL BENEFIT WILL BE EVALUATED IN A H3.3K27M DMG MODEL, COMPLEMENTED BY PHARMACOKINETIC AND TOLERABILITY ASSESSMENTS IN JUVENILE MICE. TOLERABILITY OF MT-125 IN EARLY LIFE WILL SUPPORT PROGRESSION TO THE R33 PHASE, WHERE POTENTIAL SYNERGISTIC EFFECTS BETWEEN MT-125 AND FDA-APPROVED THERAPIES, INCLUDING RT WILL BE DETERMINED IN VITRO AND IN VIVO. BECAUSE OF MYOSIN II FAMILY MEMBERS’ KNOWN PHYSIOLOGICAL ROLES, ADDITIONAL CARDIAC SAFETY AND NEURODEVELOPMENTAL INVESTIGATIONS WILL DEFINE THE COMPOUND’S EFFECTS ON THE HEART AND BRAIN MATURATION (VIA BEHAVIOR, NEUROPATHOLOGY, AND NEURONAL MORPHOLOGY ASSAYS). COLLECTIVELY, THESE STUDIES WILL DELINEATE THE THERAPEUTIC WINDOW AND INFORM THE CLINICAL DOSE RANGE TO ENSURE THE FOUNDATIONAL SAFETY AND EFFICACY DATA NECESSARY FOR INFORMED CONSENT DISCUSSIONS WITH PHYSICIANS AND FAMILIES ARE AVAILABLE WHEN CONSIDERING MT- 125 FOR CHILDREN WITH THIS UNIVERSALLY LETHAL PEDIATRIC BRAIN CANCER.

description: DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF AN ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN SEED AMPLIFICATION ASSAY USING PERIPHERAL BODILY FLUIDS OF PATIENTS AFFECTED BY PARKINSON'S DISEASE AND DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES - ABSTRACT ONE OF THE GREATEST OBSTACLES FOR DEVELOPING A DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPY FOR VARIOUS NEURODEGENERATIVE SYNUCLEINOPATHIES, INCLUDING PARKINSON'S DISEASE (PD), DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES (DLB), PD DEMENTIA (PDD) AND MULTIPLE SYSTEM ATROPHY (MSA), IS THE LACK OF EARLY AND ACCURATE DIAGNOSIS. CURRENTLY, DISEASE IS DIAGNOSED BY THE ONSET OF THE CLINICAL SYMPTOMS WITH THE HELP OF SOME NEUROIMAGING TESTS, HOWEVER AT THE TIME DIAGNOSIS IS REACHED, UP TO 70% OF DOPAMINERGIC NEURONS IN THE SUBSTANTIA NIGRA ARE ALREADY LOST. THUS, THERE IS A PRESSING UNMET NEED TO IDENTIFY BIOMARKERS THAT CAN SERVE FOR EARLY AND NON-INVASIVE BIOCHEMICAL DIAGNOSIS OF THESE DISEASES. RECENTLY, WE INVENTED AND DEVELOPED A HIGHLY SENSITIVE AND SPECIFIC ASSAY (TERMED SEED AMPLIFICATION ASSAY OR SAA) TO DETECT ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN (ΑSYN) AGGREGATES IN PATIENTS AFFECTED BY PD, DLB AND MSA, AS WELL AS PRODROMAL VERSION OF THESE DISEASES (1-5). CURRENTLY, ΑSYN-SAA IS WELL-VALIDATED TO DETECT ΑSYN PATHOLOGY IN CSF SAMPLES. HOWEVER, LUMBAR PUNCTURE IS AN INVASIVE PROCEDURE THAT PRECLUDES THE MASSIVE USE OF THE TEST, ESPECIALLY AT THE PRECLINICAL STAGE OF THE DISEASE. THE CHALLENGE TO DETECT ΑSYN AGGREGATES IN BIOLOGICAL FLUIDS OTHER THAN CSF IS THEIR LOW QUANTITY AND THE INTERFERENCE FROM OTHER COMPONENTS PRESENT IN THE FLUIDS. THE MAIN CONTEXT OF USE (COU) FOR THIS PROJECT IS THE IMPLEMENTATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF AN ASSAY TO DETECT ΑSYN PATHOLOGY IN BLOOD OR URINE SAMPLES THAT CAN BE USED TO HELP DISEASE DIAGNOSIS AS WELL AS FOR EARLY AND ROUTINE SCREENING OF INDIVIDUALS EXHIBITING SOME ABNORMALITIES THAT ARE CONSIDERED PRODROMAL VERSIONS OF SYNUCLEINOPATHIES. IN THIS PROJECT WE WILL FOLLOW UP OUR PROMISING PRELIMINARY RESULTS TO DEVELOP CONDITIONS TO ADAPT THE ΑSYN-SAA TECHNOLOGY FOR DETECTION OF ΑSYN AGGREGATES IN NON-INVASIVELY COLLECTED BIOLOGICAL FLUIDS, INCLUDING BLOOD AND URINE, VERIFY ITS ROBUSTNESS AND VALIDATE ITS SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY IN GROUPS OF PD PATIENTS AND CONTROLS, AS WELL AS INDIVIDUAL AT PRODROMAL STAGES OF THE DISEASE. DURING THE R61 PHASE, WE WILL COMPLETE ASSAY DEVELOPMENT FOR DETECTION OF ΑSYN SEEDS IN BLOOD/URINE AND PERFORM ANALYTICAL VALIDATION STUDIES OF THE BLOOD/URINE DETECTION ASSAY. IN THE R33 PHASE, WE WILL ESTIMATE CLINICAL SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY FOR THE CONTEXT OF USE AND ASSESS THE USEFULNESS OF ΑSYN-SAA FOR PRECLINICAL DETECTION OF ΑSYN PATHOLOGY IN THESE EASILY COLLECTABLE BIOLOGICAL FLUIDS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXPANDING PARTICIPATION IN RIGOR, REPRODUCIBILITY, AND TRANSPARENCY TRAINING TO CREATE SUSTAINABLE CULTURAL TRANSFORMATION - THE UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN SCHOOL OF MEDICINE AND PUBLIC HEALTH (UW SMPH) IS A PUBLIC RESEARCH UNIVERSITY AND LEADER IN TRANSLATIONAL BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH, WITH COMMITMENTS TO ADVANCING BASIC SCIENCE, IMPROVING HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR LOCAL AND GLOBAL POPULATIONS, AND TRAINING THE NEXT GENERATION OF SCHOLARS AND HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS. A LACK OF RIGOR, REPRODUCIBILITY, AND TRANSPARENCY (RRT), PARTICULARLY IN PRECLINICAL RESEARCH, IS A WELL-KNOWN BARRIER TO BIOMEDICAL PROGRESS. ALTHOUGH RRT TRAINING IS AN IDENTIFIED MECHANISM FOR SHIFTING ATTITUDES AND PRACTICES AROUND RRT, CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION OF RRT TRAINING IS OFTEN HIGHLY VARIABLE AND INSTITUTIONALLY FRAGILE. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO SHIFT THE CULTURE OF BASIC SCIENCES RESEARCH IN UW SMPH TO ONE WHERE RRT IS ROUTINELY AND UNIFORMLY TAUGHT, DISCUSSED, AND PRACTICED. OUR OVERALL OBJECTIVE IN THIS PROPOSAL IS TO: 1) LEVERAGE LOCAL EXPERTISE TO DEVELOP CONSENSUS AROUND CORE RRT COMPETENCIES RELEVANT TO DIFFERENT SUBFIELDS OF BIOMEDI-CAL RESEARCH, 2) INVENTORY EXISTING INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS AND THEIR RELEVANCE TO CORE RRT COMPETENCIES, AND 3) DEVELOP AN RRT TRAINING INTERVENTION AND INTEGRATE IT INTO THE CURRICULA OF BASIC SCIENCE PHD TRAINING PRO-GRAMS WITHIN UW SMPH. THE EARLY YEARS OF A STUDENT’S DOCTORAL EDUCATION ARE CRITICAL FOR ESTABLISHING THEIR PAT-TERNS AND HABITS OF SCIENTIFIC THOUGHT. BY INTRODUCING CORE RRT CONCEPTS TO ALL STUDENTS IN THEIR FIRST YEAR OF STUDY, WE WILL CREATE COMMON LANGUAGE AND EXPECTATIONS AROUND RRT BEFORE THEY BECOME ESTABLISHED IN INDI-VIDUAL LABS OR DISCIPLINES. FACULTY AND STAFF FROM A RANGE OF DEPARTMENTS AND DISCIPLINARY BACKGROUNDS WILL EN-GAGE IN THE DESIGN AND EXECUTION OF THIS COURSE, FURTHER AIDING THE DEVELOPMENT AND DISSEMINATION OF RRT CUL-TURE. EXPANDING THE NUMBER OF CONTENT EXPERTS INVOLVED IN TRAINING ALSO ENSURES THAT THE COURSE WILL REMAIN STA-BLE WELL BEYOND THE GRANT’S END. TO RAISE THE VISIBILITY OF RRT AND CHAMPION PARTICIPATION IN THESE INITIATIVES, WE WILL TRACK THE UPTAKE OF RRT PRACTICES ACROSS ALL FACULTY, STAFF, AND STUDENTS IN UW SMPH AND HOST THIS DATA ON A PUBLIC DASHBOARD. AT THE COMPLETION OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH, WE WILL HAVE GREATLY EXPANDED FACULTY AND STU-DENT PARTICIPATION IN RRT TRAINING AT OUR INSTITUTION, GENERATED AN INVENTORY OF RRT COMPETENCIES, MATCHED TRAINING MATERIALS TO THOSE COMPETENCIES, AND MADE TOOLKITS FOR DOING THIS WORK AVAILABLE TO OTHER INSTITUTIONS SEEKING TO COORDINATE AND ROUTINIZE RRT TRAINING FOR BIOMEDICAL SCIENCE PHD STUDENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CULTIVATING RIGOR BY ALIGNING INCENTIVES - MOVEMENT NEUROSCIENCE IS CONCERNED ABOUT SUSCEPTIBILITY TO THE REPRODUCIBILITY CRISIS AFFLICTING MANY SCIENTIFIC FIELDS, AND A RENEWED COMMITMENT TO RIGOROUS PRACTICES IS SEEN AS AN ESSENTIAL STEP TO COMBAT THIS THREAT. HOWEVER, THE INCENTIVES THAT ACADEMIC INSTITUTIONS CREATE FOR PROFESSIONAL SCIENTISTS TYPICALLY PLACE RIGOR IN STUDY DESIGN BEHIND OTHER MORE EASILY QUANTIFIABLE PRIORITIES, SUCH AS NUMBER OF PUBLICATIONS OR GRANT DOLLARS EARNED. THE NEED FOR HIGHER STANDARDS OF RIGOR TOGETHER WITH THE LACK OF INSTITUTIONAL COMMITMENT TO PROMOTING THEM MOTIVATES US TO CREATE A COMMUNITY FOCUSED ON GENERATING INCENTIVES THAT ALIGN PROFESSIONAL GOALS WITH DEVELOPING HIGHLY RIGOROUS STUDIES. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT GENERATING PERSONALLY APPEALING INCENTIVES FOR OUR COMMUNITY MEMBERS WILL CATALYZE MORE COMMITMENT TO RIGOROUS PRACTICES THAN VOLUNTARY TRAINING OR APPEALING TO A GENERAL NEED OF THE FIELD OF MOVEMENT NEUROSCIENCE. ONCE WE INCENTIVIZE MORE RIGOROUS ACTION AND ENGAGEMENT WITH OUR COMMUNITY’S PROGRAMS, WE CAN PUBLICIZE THE PRODUCTS AND BUILD GROUP BUY-IN TO CREATE A CULTURE THAT VALUES RIGOR AS A TOP PRIORITY. WE WILL CREATE INCENTIVES BY 1) OFFERING A SUPPORT MECHANISM DEDICATED TO BUILDING CREATIVE, AMBITIONS, INVESTIGATOR-INITIATED ACTIVITIES OF RIGOR. 2) OFFERING FREE CONSULTING SERVICES TO HELP LABS PLAN AND IMPLEMENT BASELINE RIGOR PRACTICES THAT THEY MAY LACK THE EXPERTISE OR TIME TO IMPLEMENT ON THEIR OWN. 3) OFFERING FREE CURRICULUM DESIGN FOR FACULTY TO CREATE RIGOR EDUCATIONAL MODULES FOR THEIR TECHNICAL SCIENCE COURSES TO REINFORCE THE IMPORTANCE OF RIGOR TO STUDENTS. 4) OFFERING A RIGOR-FOCUSED MONTHLY JOURNAL CLUB AND LARGE ANNUAL RESEARCH PRIZE FOR BEST SCHOLARSHIP THAT INCLUDES RIGOR AS A SUBSTANTIAL COMPONENT OF THE EVALUATION. WE WILL USE AN EXTERNAL EVALUATOR TO DETERMINE IF THESE INCENTIVE PROGRAMS ARE EFFECTIVE. WE WILL ACTIVELY DISSEMINATE DATA ON THE EFFICACY OF AND LESSONS LEARNED FROM THESE PROGRAMS THROUGH PAPERS, LECTURES, AND WORKSHOPS. WE WILL ALSO PROVIDE PUBLIC ACCESS TO THE MANY PRODUCTS THESE PROGRAMS WILL PRODUCE, SUCH AS THE IDEAS PROPOSED IN THE FUNDING MECHANISM, CASE STUDIES FROM OUR RIGOR CONSULTING SERVICES, AND THE EDUCATIONAL RIGOR MODULES DEVELOPED. TOGETHER, THE FUNDING, PUBLICITY, FREE-TO-USE MODEL, AND ALIGNMENT WITH INSTITUTIONAL EVALUATION METRICS OF THESE INITIATIVES WILL INCENTIVIZE FACULTY TO EXPAND THEIR ENGAGEMENT WITH PRACTICES OF RIGOR AND, IN THE LONG TERM, CREATE AN ENDURING CULTURE COMMITTED TO SCIENTIFIC RIGOR.

description: COMPARATIVE ANALYSES OF SOMATIC MUTATIONAL PROCESSES IN PRIMATES ACROSS LIFESPANS - PROJECT SUMMARY ABSTRACT THE VAST DIVERSITY IN LIFESPANS AMONG ORGANISMS PROVIDES A REMARKABLE NATURAL EXPERIMENT IN WHICH TO EXPLORE THE EVOLUTIONARY INNOVATIONS THAT HAVE SHAPED THE EXTENSIVE VARIATION OF THIS PHENOTYPE. NON-HUMAN PRIMATES REPRESENT A CRITICAL TAXON FOR UNDERSTANDING THE EVOLUTION OF HUMAN LIFESPAN DUE TO THEIR CLOSE PHYLOGENETIC PROXIMITY AND BROAD RANGE OF LIFESPANS. ONE KEY HALLMARK OF AGING IS GENOMIC INSTABILITY AND THE ACCUMULATION OF SOMATIC MUTATIONS. ONLY RECENT IMPROVEMENTS IN THE ACCURACY OF GENOME SEQUENCING HAVE ENABLED THE STUDY OF THESE MUTATIONS IN AGING TISSUES. A SUBSET OF THESE MUTATIONS CONFER GROWTH ADVANTAGES DRIVING CARCINOGENESIS, HOWEVER EMERGING EVIDENCE ALSO HIGHLIGHTS THEIR ROLE IN SEVERAL OTHER AGE-ASSOCIATED DISEASES AND POTENTIALLY AGING ITSELF. WE RECENTLY DEMONSTRATED THAT SOMATIC MUTATION RATES ARE INVERSELY CORRELATED WITH LIFESPAN IN MAMMALS, CONSISTENT WITH A POTENTIAL CAUSAL ROLE IN AGING. FURTHERMORE, COMPARATIVE GENOMICS ANALYSES WE AND OTHERS HAVE PERFORMED ACROSS SPECIES WITH DIVERSE LIFESPANS HAVE DETERMINED THAT DNA REPAIR GENES ARE KEY PLAYERS IN ADAPTATIONS TO LONG LIFE. HERE, WE PROPOSE TO CHARACTERIZE SOMATIC MUTATIONAL LANDSCAPES OF AGING IN PRIMATE SPECIES SPANNING 70 MILLION YEARS OF EVOLUTION. THESE MAPS WILL BE GENERATED ACROSS 10 TISSUE TYPES FROM A COLLECTION OF MARMOSETS, MACAQUES, BABOONS, CHIMPANZEES AND HUMANS OF DIVERSE AGES AND BOTH SEXES USING ULTRA-ACCURATE NANOSEQ MUTATION PROFILING. FOR A SUBSET OF TISSUES WE WILL ALSO PERFORM PACBIO LONG READ SEQUENCING TO ASSESS SOMATIC STRUCTURAL VARIANTS. THESE DATA WILL BE SUPPLEMENTED WITH NANOSEQ PROFILING OF SEVERAL CELL TYPES FROM 17 ADDITIONAL PRIMATE SPECIES. TOGETHER, THESE MAPS WILL ALLOW US TO ASCERTAIN HOW SOMATIC MUTATIONAL PROCESSES, INCLUDING MUTATION RATES AND SIGNATURES, VARY WITH AGE ACROSS PRIMATE SPECIES WITH DIVERSE LIFE SPANS AND LIFE HISTORIES. AS A RESULT OF THESE SOMATIC MUTATIONS AS WE AGE MANY TISSUES ALSO BECOME COLONIZED BY CLONAL EXPANSIONS OF POSITIVELY SELECTED MUTANT CELLS. TO DETERMINE HOW THESE CLONAL DYNAMICS RELATE TO SPECIES LIFESPAN WE WILL NEXT PERFORM DEEP TARGETED-NANOSEQ ON 250 GENES, KNOWN TO DRIVE CLONAL EXPANSIONS IN HUMANS, ACROSS INDIVIDUALS OF DIFFERENT AGES FROM 8 OF THE AFOREMENTIONED SPECIES. THESE ANALYSES WILL PERMIT IDENTIFICATION OF THE MUTATIONS DRIVING CLONAL EXPANSIONS, THE RATE AT WHICH THESE EXPANSIONS OCCUR DURING AGING, AND SPATIAL CLONAL DYNAMICS ACROSS THE LIFESPAN IN DIVERSE SPECIES AND TISSUES, INFORMING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW THEY CONTRIBUTE TO AGING. FINALLY, WE WILL SEEK TO IDENTIFY THE SPECIES-SPECIFIC GENETIC DETERMINANTS OF THESE SOMATIC MUTATION PHENOTYPES. WE WILL PERFORM A PHYLO-GWAS ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY THE GENES ASSOCIATED WITH DIFFERENCES IN MUTATIONAL PATTERNS AMONG SPECIES USING BOTH GENERAL PHENOTYPES (E.G. LIFESPAN, BODY SIZE) AS WELL AS THE MOLECULAR MUTATIONAL PHENOTYPES IDENTIFIED IN AIMS 1 AND 2 (E.G. MUTATION RATES, SPECTRA, AND CLONAL DYNAMICS). THESE COMPARATIVE GENOMICS APPROACHES WILL ALLOW US TO LINK BOTH BROAD PRIMATE PHENOTYPES AND QUANTIFIED MOLECULAR PHENOTYPES TO THE EVOLUTIONARY INNOVATIONS THAT HAVE IMPACTED LIFESPAN IN THE PRIMATE CLADE. TOGETHER THESE MULTI- SCALE EVOLUTIONARY COMPARISONS WILL REVEAL FACTORS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO THE DIVERSITY OF LIFE SPANS ACROSS PRIMATES AND TO ULTIMATELY IDENTIFY NOVEL TARGETS FOR INTERVENTIONS TO EXTEND HUMAN HEALTH SPAN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ACCESS TO MEDICATIONS TO TREAT OPIOID USE DISORDER IN THE MEDICARE POPULATION - ACCESS TO EFFECTIVE TREATMENT FOR OPIOID USE DISORDER (OUD) CONTINUES TO BE AN IMPORTANT PUBLIC HEALTH PROBLEM TWO DECADES AFTER THE START OF THE OPIOID CRISIS. PATIENTS DIAGNOSED WITH OUD MAY RECEIVE ONE OF THREE FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION-APPROVED MEDICATIONS TO TREAT OUD (MOUD): METHADONE, BUPRENORPHINE, AND NALTREXONE. YET, ONLY 16% OF MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES DIAGNOSED WITH OUD RECEIVED A MOUD IN 2020. IN THE ABSENCE OF MOUD, MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES WITH OUD ARE AT GREATER RISK OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY. THE LITTLE MOUD THAT IS DISPENSED TO MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES DOES NOT ACCRUE EVENLY TO DIFFERENT PATIENT GROUPS. MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES HAVE REPORTED THAT A LACK OF INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR OUD TREATMENT WAS A BARRIER TO TREATMENT. PRIOR TO 2020, MEDICARE DID NOT COVER METHADONE FOR OUD TREATMENT. EVEN IF A MEDICARE BENEFICIARY HAS COVERAGE FOR MOUD, THEY MAY NOT LIVE NEAR A PROVIDER WHO PRESCRIBES IT. FOR EXAMPLE, MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES LIVING IN RURAL AREAS HAVE LESS ACCESS TO MOUD COMPARED TO THOSE IN URBAN AREAS. SIMILARLY, NONWHITE MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES ARE LESS LIKELY TO HAVE ACCESS TO AND RECEIVE MOUD THAN WHITE BENEFICIARIES.   THE QUALITY OF INDIVIDUAL PROVIDERS AND THEIR CONTRIBUTIONS TO DIFFERENCES IN MOUD USE IS UNDERSTUDIED. DIFFERENCES IN MOUD USE CAN OCCUR DUE TO SPECIFIC PATIENTS RECEIVING CARE AT LOWER QUALITY PROVIDERS OR BECAUSE THEY RECEIVE WORSE CARE AT THE SAME PROVIDERS AS MORE ADVANTAGED PATIENTS. ACCESS TO MOUD DEPENDS ON DIFFERENT PATHWAYS. IN THIS STUDY WE WILL CONDUCT ANALYSES DESIGNED TO ASSESS BENEFICIARY ACCESS TO MOUD AND HEALTH OUTCOMES. WE WILL CALCULATE REPRODUCIBLE FACILITY-LEVEL QUALITY MEASURES OF MOUD AND HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES WITH OUD AND CONDUCT QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS WITH FACILITY STAFF ON THE QUALITY MEASURES AND TO UNDERSTAND BARRIERS TO EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT. WE PROPOSE TO STUDY THE FOLLOWING AIMS: AIM 1: QUANTIFY AND COMPARE ACCESS TO MOUD AND HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES, STRATIFYING BY BENEFICIARY (RACE/ETHNICITY, SEX, AND GEOGRAPHY), PROVIDER (SPECIALTY, GEOGRAPHY, WAIVER STATUS DURING OUR STUDY PERIOD), AND FACILITY CHARACTERISTICS (OWNERSHIP, OTP STATUS, SERVICE SETTING). AIM 1A: EVALUATE THE ROLE OF COMMUNITY CONTEXTUAL FACTORS ON ACCESS TO MOUD AND ON HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES DIAGNOSED WITH OUD. AIM 2: CONSTRUCT FACILITY-LEVEL QUALITY MEASURES REFLECTING ACCESS TO MOUD AND HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES DIAGNOSED WITH OUD AND STRATIFY FACILITIES BASED ON THEIR RELATIVE PERFORMANCE. AIM 2A: CONDUCT QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS WITH TREATMENT FACILITY CLINICIANS TO GATHER FEEDBACK ON PROPOSED MEASURES AND TO UNDERSTAND BARRIERS TO MOUD ACCESS NOT CAPTURED IN ADMINISTRATIVE DATA. MOUD IS AN EFFECTIVE FORM OF TREATMENT THAT FEW MEDICARE BENEFICIARIES DIAGNOSED WITH OUD RECEIVE. THE PROPOSED TEAM FOR THIS R01 WILL CONSTRUCT MEASURES OF USE OF MOUD TREATMENT AND HEALTH OUTCOMES OVER TIME AND USE A MIXED METHODS APPROACH TO IDENTIFY BARRIERS TO RECEIPT OF AN EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT FOR OUD.

description: MULTIDIMENSIONAL RISK PROFILES AND MECHANISMS FOR LONELINESS IN STROKE SURVIVORS: A SOCIOECOLOGICAL APPROACH - IN 2023 THE U.S. OFFICE OF THE SURGEON GENERAL DECLARED THE WIDESPREAD LONELINESS 1 AMONGST U.S. ADULTS AS A PUBLIC HEALTH CRISIS AND A PRIORITY FOR RESEARCH. THIS URGENT CALL WAS ECHOED IN THE RECENT STATEMENT FROM THE AMERICAN HEART ASSOCIATION (AHA), WHICH EMPHASIZED THE NEED FOR RESEARCH IN POPULATIONS AT RISK FOR BOTH LONELINESS AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD). STROKE AND TRANSIENT ISCHEMIC ATTACK (TIA) SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASE ONE’S LIKELIHOOD OF BECOMING LONELY. IN TURN, LONELINESS SHOWS ROBUST ASSOCIATIONS WITH FUTURE CVD EVENTS. LONELINESS IS AN EMBEDDED PHENOMENON CAUSED BY A COMPLEX SET OF INTERSECTING RISK FACTORS ACROSS INDIVIDUAL, INTERPERSONAL, AND COMMUNITY LEVELS. CRITICALLY, EXISTING RESEARCH HAS YET TO APPLY METHODS FOR EXAMINING THE WAYS IN WHICH RISK FACTORS CLUSTER TO FORM DISTINCT RISK PROFILES THAT ARE NECESSARY TO IDENTIFY BEFORE TAILORED INTERVENTIONS CAN BE DEVELOPED. RESEARCH ON LONELINESS HAS ALSO LARGELY BEEN CONDUCTED IN THE GENERAL POPULATION, WHICH NECESSARILY PRECLUDES A FOCUS ON UNIQUE RISK FACTORS FACED BY STROKE SURVIVORS (E.G., IMPAIRED COMMUNICATION DUE TO STROKE-RELATED SPEECH PRODUCTION DEFICITS). INFORMED BY THE SOCIOECOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK (SEF), THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL BE THE FIRST TO IDENTIFY DISTINCT PROFILES OF RISK FOR LONELINESS OVER THE FIRST YEAR AFTER STROKE IN THIS PRIORITY POPULATION. WE WILL LEVERAGE OUR ED-BASED RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE TO RECRUIT A REPRESENTATIVE SAMPLE OF STROKE/TIA SURVIVORS (N = 1,000) TO COLLECT DATA AT HOSPITAL DISCHARGE AND AT 1, 3, 6, AND 12 MONTHS POST-DISCHARGE. WE HYPOTHESIZE TO IDENTIFY 4-5 PROFILES OF MULTILEVEL RISK FACTORS, ASSESSED AT BASELINE (INDIVIDUAL: DIAGNOSIS [STROKE, TIA], STROKE SEVERITY, EXTENT OF PHYSICAL DISABILITY, COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT, LANGUAGE IMPAIRMENT, DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC RISK STATUS; INTERPERSONAL: PARTNER STATUS, CAREGIVER STATUS, HOUSEHOLD COMPOSITION; COMMUNITY: NEIGHBORHOOD RISK INDICES). WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THESE PROFILES WILL BE SIGNIFICANTLY ASSOCIATED WITH LONELINESS AND STROKE BURDEN OVER THE FIRST YEAR AFTER STROKE. UNDERSTANDING THE REASONS WHY CERTAIN RISK PROFILES PRECIPITATE LONELINESS INFORMS MECHANISTIC INTERVENTION TARGETS. THUS, WE WILL TEST THE PROSPECTIVE ASSOCIATION OF RISK PROFILES WITH TWO CANDIDATE MECHANISMS IDENTIFIED IN THE LITERATURE THAT MAY BE HARNESSED IN FUTURE INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE THE RISK FOR LONELINESS AND ITS ADVERSE HEALTH CONSEQUENCES: (1) SOCIAL PARTICIPATION AND (2) PURPOSE IN LIFE. WE WILL ALSO IDENTIFY DEMOGRAPHIC PREDICTORS OF RISK PROFILE MEMBERSHIP. FINDINGS FROM THIS STUDY HAVE POTENTIAL TO GUIDE THE DEVELOPMENT OF TAILORED INTERVENTIONS TO PREVENT LONELINESS AFTER STROKE AND IMPROVE RECOVERY, AS WELL AS TO INFORM THEORIES OF LONELINESS AND HEALTH ACROSS MULTIPLE LEVELS OF INFLUENCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DYNAMIC SUSTAINMENT OF EVIDENCE-BASED HEALTH PROMOTION INTERVENTIONS IN MENTAL HEALTH - PROJECT ABSTRACT ADULTS WITH SERIOUS AND DISABLING MENTAL ILLNESS (SMI) EXPERIENCE A 15-30 YEAR REDUCED LIFE EXPECTANCY PRIMARILY DUE TO MODIFIABLE CARDIOVASCULAR RISK FACTORS THAT CAN BE EFFECTIVELY ADDRESSED WITH BEHAVIORAL LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS. LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS HAVE REDUCED OBESITY-RELATED CARDIOVASCULAR RISK IN UPWARDS OF 50% OF ADULTS WITH SMI IN COMMUNITY-BASED TRIALS, EVEN AMONG THOSE TAKING ANTIPSYCHOTIC MEDICATIONS; HOWEVER, THESE INTERVENTIONS ARE RARELY SUSTAINED ONCE RESEARCH PROJECTS ARE COMPLETED. THIS LATER STAGE TRANSLATIONAL STUDY FOCUSES ON LONG-TERM SUSTAINMENT OF AN EVIDENCE-BASED LIFESTYLE INTERVENTION (INSHAPE) IMPLEMENTED IN U.S. MENTAL HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS WHERE INTEGRATED HEALTH PROMOTION IS NOT NECESSARILY PART OF THE CORE MISSION, BUT IS CRITICAL TO STEM THE TIDE OF EARLY MORTALITY IN ADULTS WITH SMI. INSHAPE IS THE ONLY LIFESTYLE INTERVENTION FOR ADULTS WITH SMI THAT HAS BEEN TESTED MULTIPLE TIMES WITH HEALTH BENEFITS REPLICATED IN TWO RCTS AND A STATEWIDE AND NATIONAL IMPLEMENTATION STUDY. THERE HAS YET TO BE AN INVESTIGATION OF LONG-TERM SUSTAINMENT OF INSHAPE OR ANY OTHER EVIDENCE-BASED HEALTH PROMOTION INTERVENTIONS FOR ADULTS WITH SMI IN MENTAL HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS. FROM 2014-2019, OUR TEAM LED AN NIMH-FUNDED TYPE 3 HYBRID EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION STUDY OF INSHAPE IN MENTAL HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS ACROSS THE U.S. IN 2023, 14 (36%) OF 39 ORGANIZATIONS THAT COMPLETED OUR PRIOR IMPLEMENTATION STUDY CONTINUED TO DELIVER INSHAPE. IN THE PROPOSED STUDY, WE WILL EVALUATE LONG-TERM SUSTAINMENT OF INSHAPE (6-8 YEARS POST-IMPLEMENTATION) ON TWO DIMENSIONS: 1) SUSTAINED DELIVERY OF THE INSHAPE PROGRAM, AND 2) SUSTAINED INSHAPE PROGRAM HEALTH BENEFITS. WE WILL LEVERAGE DATA COLLECTED IN OUR PRIOR TRIAL TO EXAMINE MULTI-LEVEL FACTORS THAT PREDICT LONG-TERM SUSTAINMENT OF INSHAPE AT 39 IMPLEMENTATION SITES; COLLECT NEW DATA ON CONTEXTUAL FACTORS, ADAPTATIONS AND FIDELITY TO INSHAPE; AND COLLABORATE WITH AN EXISTING NATIONAL NETWORK OF INSHAPE TEAMS TO DEVELOP A SUSTAINMENT PRACTICE GUIDE TAILORED FOR INSHAPE. WHILE THE PRACTICE GUIDE WILL BE BASED ON INSHAPE, IT WILL BE GUIDED BY THE PROGRAM SUSTAINABILITY FRAMEWORK AND THUS WILL INCLUDE KEY CONSIDERATIONS FOR SUSTAINING EVIDENCE-BASED HEALTH PROMOTION PROGRAMS MORE BROADLY IN MENTAL HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS. THE PROPOSED STUDY HAS HIGH PUBLIC HEALTH AND IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE IMPACT AS ONE OF THE FIRST STUDIES TO IDENTIFY ADAPTATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH SUSTAINED HEALTH PROMOTION INTERVENTIONS WHILE ALSO ADDRESSING LONGSTANDING ASSUMPTIONS ABOUT THE ‘VOLTAGE DROP’ IN INDIVIDUAL BENEFITS OF EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS AS THEY MOVE FROM IMPLEMENTATION TO SUSTAINMENT. IT IS HIGHLY INNOVATIVE AND IMPACTFUL AS ONE OF THE FIRST STUDIES TO USE PARTICIPATORY GROUP MODEL BUILDING AND TO LEVERAGE A LARGE NETWORK OF IMPLEMENTATION SITES TO IDENTIFY FACTORS, INCLUDING FIDELITY AND ADAPTATION, THAT INFLUENCE LONG-TERM SUSTAINMENT OF AN EVIDENCE-BASED HEALTH PROMOTION INTERVENTION IN MENTAL HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS AND TO BUILD ON THESE FINDINGS TO DEVELOP, EVALUATE, AND REFINE A SUSTAINMENT PRACTICE GUIDE FOR FUTURE RESEARCH AND PRACTICE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EVALUATING THE POTENTIAL OF NEURAL OSCILLATION BIOMARKERS IN A RODENT MODEL OF INTERVENTION OUTCOME VARIATION: TOWARD PERSONALIZED MENTAL HEALTH CARE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  A MAJOR CHALLENGE IN MENTAL HEALTH CARE INCLUDES INCONSISTENT OUTCOMES OF CURRENT PSYCHOTHERAPEUTIC, PHARMACOLOGIC, AND BRAIN STIMULATION INTERVENTIONS. WE THEORIZE THAT ACROSS INDIVIDUALS, HETEROGENEOUS NEURAL UNDERPINNINGS MANIFEST AT A SYSTEMS LEVEL, LEADING TO IMPAIRED DOMAINS OF FUNCTION AND SPECIFIC DIAGNOSES. THIS HETEROGENEITY CAUSES THE SAME INTERVENTION TO PRODUCE DIFFERENT OUTCOMES ACROSS INDIVIDUALS. TO OVERCOME THIS CHALLENGE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SYSTEMS-LEVEL BRAIN ACTIVITY (NEURAL OSCILLATIONS) CONTAINS THE INFORMATION NECESSARY TO PREDICT BOTH INDIVIDUAL VARIATION IN A DOMAIN OF BRAIN FUNCTION AND IDENTIFY BIOMARKERS TO GUIDE THE INDIVIDUALIZED IMPLEMENTATION OF AN INTERVENTION. TO TEST THESE HYPOTHESES, A MODEL BRAIN SYSTEM IS NEEDED WITH SUFFICIENT VARIATION AND COMPLEXITY TO PRODUCE HETEROGENEITY IN BEHAVIOR AND INTERVENTION OUTCOMES. PRIOR WORK, INCLUDING OUR OWN PRELIMINARY DATA, DEMONSTRATES SUCH BEHAVIORAL VARIATION EXISTS ACROSS INDIVIDUALS AND SEXES IN AN OUTBRED RAT STRAIN (SPRAGUE DAWLEY) PERFORMING THE DELAY DISCOUNTING TASK (DDT) AND RISK DISCOUNTING TASK (RDT). WHEN BRAIN STIMULATION (AIM 1), PHARMACOLOGIC (AIM 2) OR CHEMOGENETIC (AIM 3) INTERVENTIONS HAVE BEEN IMPLEMENTED IN THESE RATS, THEY PRODUCE HETEROGENEOUS EFFECTS ON TASK PERFORMANCE ACROSS INDIVIDUALS MAKING THIS AN EXCELLENT MODEL SYSTEM TO EVALUATE OUR HYPOTHESES. OUR PROPOSED PROOF-OF-CONCEPT STUDY WILL DETERMINE THE POTENTIAL UTILITY OF NEURAL OSCILLATIONS AS BIOMARKERS REFLECTING INDIVIDUAL VARIATION IN THE NEURAL UNDERPINNINGS OF DELAY AND RISK DISCOUNTING AND THE PREDISPOSITION OF THOSE INDIVIDUALS TO RESPOND TO INTERVENTIONS. WE WILL USE MACHINE LEARNING TO DETERMINE IF: 1) OSCILLATIONS CAN PREDICT VARIATION IN TASK PERFORMANCE ACROSS INDIVIDUALS AND TIME; 2) OSCILLATIONS CAN PREDICT INDIVIDUAL INTERVENTION OUTCOMES; AND 3) CHANGES IN OSCILLATIONS INDUCED BY INTERVENTIONS ARE PREDICTIVE OF CORRESPONDING CHANGES IN DDT OR RDT PERFORMANCE.  FURTHER ENHANCING THE TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE OF THIS PROPOSAL, THE NEURAL SYSTEMS THAT MODULATE THE VALUE OF REWARDS ASSOCIATED WITH DELAY AND RISK DISCOUNTING SHARE HOMOLOGY BETWEEN RODENTS AND HUMANS AND HAVE BEEN LINKED TO IMPORTANT CLINICAL OUTCOMES. FOR INSTANCE, THE EXCESSIVE REDUCTION OF REWARD VALUE BY DELAY RELATES TO A SIGNIFICANT RISK FOR POOR OUTCOMES IN MULTIPLE PSYCHIATRIC CONDITIONS (E.G., ADHD, SCHIZOPHRENIA AND BORDERLINE PERSONALITY DISORDER). ABNORMAL DELAY AND RISK DISCOUNTING HAVE ALSO BEEN LINKED TO SPECIFIC BEHAVIORS, INCLUDING SUICIDE, VIOLENCE AND RISKY SUBSTANCE USE, ENHANCING THE IMPACT OF THE PROPOSED STUDIES. AS AN EARLY-CAREER INVESTIGATOR, FUNDING FOR THIS PROPOSAL WOULD ALLOW ME TO LAUNCH AN INNOVATIVE TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH PROGRAM ALIGNED WITH NIMH STRATEGIC GOALS FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING SYSTEMS- LEVEL BRAIN ACTIVITY BIOMARKERS TO GUIDE THE INDIVIDUALIZED IMPLEMENTATION OF INTERVENTIONS FOR PATIENTS WITH MENTAL ILLNESS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SARS-COV-2 AND SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH IMPACT ON INFLAMMATION ASSOCIATED DEPRESSION RISK (SSIDR) - PROJECT SUMMARY RECENT FINDINGS FROM THE EMBARC STUDY HAVE SHOWN THAT SMALL LIPID MOLECULES CALLED EICOSANOIDS, WHICH ACT AS BOTH ACTIVATORS AND SUPPRESSORS OF INFLAMMATORY ACTIVITY AS WELL AS MODULATORS OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY, ARE KNOWN TO HAVE A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT ON THE SUBACUTE AND CHRONIC SEQUELAE OF SARS-COV-2, IN ADDITION TO RISK FOR UNRESOLVED IMMUNE-MEDIATED INFLAMMATORY CONDITIONS SUCH AS CVD. EICOSANOIDS HAVE ALSO BEEN FOUND TO BE A CONTRIBUTOR OF CHRONIC NEUROINFLAMMATORY CONDITIONS SUCH AS DEPRESSION IN OTHER STUDIES. ADVANCED MASS SPECTROMETRY METHODS NOW ALLOW FOR THE RAPID AND ACCURATE QUANTIFICATION OF HUNDREDS OF UPSTREAM EICOSANOID MEDIATORS REPRESENTING MULTIPLE ENZYMATIC ORIGINS. HENCE, THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO PROVIDE A MORE DETAILED UNDERSTANDING OF HOW UPSTREAM EICOSANOID PATHWAYS CAN BE VARIABLY ACTIVE, IMBALANCED, AND PERTURBED IN RELATION TO AN INDIVIDUAL’S PROPENSITY FOR DEVELOPING DEPRESSION. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE EXPERTISE OF AN INTERPROFESSIONAL TEAM, INCLUDING CURRENT MEMBERS OF THE EMBARC RESEARCH STUDY TEAM, TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT: 1) SARS-COV-2 INFECTION AND REINFECTIONS MODERATE DEVELOPMENT OF CHRONIC IMMUNE-MEDIATED NEUROINFLAMMATORY CONDITION SUCH AS DEPRESSION AS EVIDENCED BY CHANGES IN EICOSANOID PROFILES; AND 2) HEALTH IMPACTS OF SDOH COMPOUNDS DEPRESSION RISK FOLLOWING SARS-COV-2 INFECTION AND REINFECTION BY MODERATING THE NEUROIMMUNE-INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE. WE PROPOSE A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TO COMPREHENSIVELY INVESTIGATING THE COMPONENTS OF UPSTREAM INFLAMMATORY ACTIVITY IN RELATION TO OUTCOMES ACROSS THE SPECTRUM OF DEPRESSION RISK THROUGH THE COLLECTION OF LONGITUDINAL (SURVEY, CLINICAL, BIOMARKER) DATA FROM A LARGE POPULATION OF PEOPLE ALREADY ENROLLED IN THE EMBARC RESEARCH STUDY AND WILL USE A VARIETY OF METHODS (E.G., EICOSANOID PROFILING, USE OF DEMOGRAPHIC DATA SET) TO ASSESS SARS-COV-2 INFECTION AND THE SDOH IMPACT ON NEUROINFLAMMATION THAT IS ASSOCIATED WITH DEPRESSION. THIS WORK WILL PAVE THE WAY FOR FOLLOW-UP STUDIES INVESTIGATING THE EFFICACY OF ANTI-INFLAMMATORY THERAPIES, INCLUDING BOTH EXISTING AND NOVEL AGENTS, FOR MODULATING VARIATION IN DISTINCT EICOSANOIDS AND, IN TURN, MENTAL HEALTH OUTCOMES SUCH AS DEPRESSION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LONG-READ SEQUENCING TO RESOLVE THE GENOMIC ARCHITECTURE OF DEMENTIA - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT TO DATE, NO EFFECTIVE THERAPIES OR PREVENTION STRATEGIES HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED FOR TWO OF THE MAJOR FORMS OF DEMENTIA, LEWY BODY DEMENTIA (LBD) AND FRONTOTEMPORAL LOBAR DEGENERATION (FTLD). WITH NO STRATEGIES TO PREVENT OR DELAY THE ONSET OF THESE DEVASTATING DISEASES, THEIR TOLL ON THE PATIENT, FAMILY/CAREGIVER, AS WELL AS COMMUNITY AND SOCIAL HEALTHCARE WILL BE AN EVER-INCREASING BURDEN. HENCE, IT IS IMPERATIVE TO DEVELOP A THOROUGH UNDERSTANDING OF THEIR MOLECULAR PATHOGENESIS TO IDENTIFY KEY TARGETS AND PATHWAYS FOR CLINICAL INTERVENTION. AS SUCH, WE SEEK TO REVEAL THE ‘MISSING’ GENOMIC VARIATION AND DETERMINE ISOFORM-SPECIFIC, DISEASE-RELEVANT TRANSCRIPTS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO THESE PROGRESSIVE AND ULTIMATELY FATAL NEURODEGENERATIVE DEMENTIAS.  GIVEN THE FACT THAT THE VAST MAJORITY OF LBD AND FTLD PATIENTS REMAIN ETIOLOGICALLY UNEXPLAINED, DESPITE THE DISCOVERY OF MULTIPLE DISEASE-ASSOCIATED LOCI, WE WILL EMPLOY LONG-READ SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGIES, WHICH HAVE THE CAPACITY TO DETECT STRUCTURAL VARIATION (AIM 1) AND INDIVIDUAL TRANSCRIPTS (AIM 2), WHICH WOULD HAVE STAYED HIDDEN WITH STANDARD SHORT-READ SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGIES. OUR APPROACH ENABLES US TO SPAN THE ENTIRE RANGE OF GENOMIC VARIATION FROM SINGLE-NUCLEOTIDE VARIANTS AND SMALL INSERTIONS/DELETIONS, TO LARGER COPY NUMBER VARIANTS, TRANSLOCATIONS, INVERSIONS, AND REPEAT EXPANSIONS, UNCOVERING VARIANTS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE DISEASES. IN ADDITION TO THESE GENOMIC STUDIES, WE ARE PROPOSING TO OBTAIN A COMPREHENSIVE, ISOFORM- SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTOME OF POST-MORTEM BRAIN TISSUE, USING THE LATEST LONG-READ SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGY. OBTAINING THE FULL-LENGTH TRANSCRIPTOME IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT SINCE SPLICING EVENTS AND DYSREGULATED EXPRESSION HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO PLAY A CENTRAL ROLE IN BOTH NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES. FINALLY, WE PROPOSE TO USE SINGLE-NUCLEI RNA SEQUENCING, INTERROGATING THE LONG-READ TRANSCRIPTOME AT THE SINGLE-NUCLEUS LEVEL. THIS WILL NOT ONLY GIVE US AN UNPRECEDENTED OPPORTUNITY TO RELIABLY DETECT AND QUANTIFY RELEVANT INDIVIDUAL TRANSCRIPTS AND DYSREGULATED PATHWAYS/NETWORKS, BUT ALSO TO DEFINE THE CELLULAR SIGNATURES OF LBD AND FTLD IN HUMAN BRAIN TISSUE. TAKEN TOGETHER, WE ARE LEVERAGING STATE-OF-THE-ART LONG-READ SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGIES TO PERFORM DETAILED GENOMIC AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC ASSESSMENTS OF OUR UNIQUE COHORTS OF LBD AND FTLD PATIENTS, WHICH ALLOWS US TO UNRAVEL THEIR GENOMIC ARCHITECTURE, POINTING TOWARDS DISEASE DRIVERS AND MODIFIERS, AS WELL AS MUCH-NEEDED PRECLINICAL BIOMARKERS AND DRUGGABLE TARGETS.

description: DIVERSITY OF PHOSPHODIESTERASE 2A SIGNALING IN TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION IS AN EARLY FEATURE IN SUSCEPTIBLE NEURONS OF PATIENTS WITH TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY (TBI) AND ITS PROGRESSION TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND RELATED DEMENTIA (ADRD), WHILE THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS REMAIN ELUSIVE. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DETERMINE THE ROLE OF PHOSPHODIESTERASE 2A (PDE2A) IN MITOCHONDRIAL BIOENERGETIC FAILURE BY MODULATING VOLTAGE DEPENDENT ANION CHANNEL 1 (VDAC1) PHOSPHORYLATION, GATING BEHAVIOR, AND MITOCHONDRIAL DNA (MTDNA) LEAKAGE. MOREOVER, THE PROJECT AIMS TO ELUCIDATE HOW VDAC1 PHOSPHORYLATION AND OLIGOMERIZATION CONTRIBUTE TO NEUROINFLAMMATION AND NEURODEGENERATION FOLLOWING TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY (TBI) AND ITS PROGRESSION TO ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (AD). CAMP AND/OR CGMP SIGNALING PLAYS A CRUCIAL ROLE IN REGULATING THE EXPRESSION OF KEY ENZYMES IN THE ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN (ETC), THEREBY AFFECTING RESPIRATORY CHAIN FUNCTION. AS A MAJOR HYDROLASE OF CAMP AND CGMP, PDE2A EXPRESSION IS FOUND TO BE INCREASED IN THE BRAINS OF AD PATIENTS AND MICE SUBJECTED TO TBI, PRIOR TO THE ONSET OF AD-ASSOCIATED COGNITIVE DEFICITS. THIS INCREASE IN PDE2A IS CONCOMITANT WITH DECREASED CAMP AND CGMP IN BOTH THE CYTOSOL AND MITOCHONDRIA. FURTHER STUDY HAS SHOWN THAT TBI-INDUCED MITOCHONDRIAL NUCLEOID DNA (MTDNA) LEAKAGE AND RESPIRATORY DEFICITS COULD BE RESCUED BY A PDE2A INHIBITOR, SUGGESTING A NOVEL ROLE OF PDE2A IN HOMEOSTASIS IMBALANCE IN THE COGNITIVE PROCESSING. PDE2A DEFICIENCY PROMOTES PROTEIN KINASE A (PKA)-MEDIATED VDAC1 PHOSPHORYLATION, WHICH MAY REDUCE VDAC1 OLIGOMERIZATION AND IMPROVE MITOCHONDRIAL METABOLITE TRANSPORT. AMONG THE THREE PDE2A ISOFORMS, PDE2A2 CONTAINS A UNIQUE N-TERMINAL 17-AMINO-ACID SEQUENCE THAT SPECIFICALLY TARGETS IT TO MITOCHONDRIA. THIS LOCALIZATION MAKES PDE2A2 THE UNIQUE ISOFORM INVOLVED IN REGULATING LOCAL CYCLIC NUCLEOTIDE SIGNALING. BY HYDROLYZING CAMP AND/OR CGMP, PDE2A2 IMPACTS MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTIONAL INTEGRITY BY NEGATIVELY REGULATING VDAC1 PHOSPHORYLATION, MODULATING ITS GATING BEHAVIOR, AND ULTIMATELY CONTROLLING CELL FATE. THUS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT TBI-ACTIVATED PDE2A (PDE2A2)-VDAC1 AXIS CONTRIBUTES TO MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION BY ALTERING VDAC1 PHOSPHORYLATION, OLIGOMERIZATION, AND GATING BEHAVIOR, AS WELL AS INDUCING MTDNA LEAKAGE. THESE CHANGES, IN TURN, TRIGGER NEUROINFLAMMATION AND EXACERBATE PATHOLOGICAL AND COGNITIVE DEFICITS ASSOCIATED WITH AD AND DEMENTIA. OUR GROUP HAS ESTABLISHED NOVEL ANIMAL MODELS, I.E. FOREBRAIN SPECIFIC PDE2A KNOCKOUT AND FUNCTIONAL PDE2A2 KNOCKOUT MICE CROSSED TO AD MICE. USING THESE MOUSE MODELS, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE MECHANISM UNDERLYING THE EFFECTS OF ABERRANT PDE2A, PARTICULARLY PDE2A2, ON NEUROINFLAMMATION AND NEURODEGENERATION WITH A FOCUS ON VDAC1 PHOSPHORYLATION, OLIGOMERIZATION, GATING BEHAVIOR, AND MITOCHONDRIAL HOMEOSTASIS. THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO PDE2A-VDAC1 AXIS UNDERLYING MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION IN TBI ASSOCIATED WITH AD/ADRD AND ENHANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF PDE2A’S ROLE IN REGULATING COGNITION IN THE BRAIN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: COMMENSAL MICROBIOTA-MEDIATED MODULATION OF LEWY BODY DEMENTIA - PROJECT SUMMARY LEWY BODY DEMENTIA (LBD) IS THE SECOND MOST COMMON FORM OF DEMENTIA, FOR WHICH THERE ARE NO CURRENT TREATMENTS. LBD IS CHARACTERIZED BY Α-SYNUCLEIN (ΑSYN) CONTAINING LEWY BODY PATHOLOGY IN THE CORTEX AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT. LBD IS A SPORADIC DISEASE RESULTING FROM THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN GENETIC FACTORS AND ENVIRONMENTAL INFLUENCES. SNCA, THE GENE ENCODING ΑSYN, IS A MAJOR RISK GENE FOR LBD, AND GUT MICROBIOME DYSBIOSIS IS A POTENTIAL ENVIRONMENTAL DRIVER OF DISEASE. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH GUT MICROBES MAY IMPACT ΑSYN PATHOLOGY ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD. TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP, WE SCREENED GUT MICROBIOTA FROM PRODROMAL SYNUCLEINOPATHY PATIENTS AND AGE-MATCHED HEALTHY CONTROLS FOR THE ABILITY TO IMPACT SYNUCLEINOPATHY BY PERFORMING FECAL MICROBIOTA TRANSPLANTATIONS (FMTS) INTO GERM-FREE HUMAN WILDTYPE ΑSYN TRANSGENIC MICE. USING THIS IN VIVO SCREENING PROCESS, WE IDENTIFIED A MICROBIOME THAT SIGNIFICANTLY EXACERBATED CORTICAL ΑSYN PATHOLOGY AND ASSOCIATED MOTOR DEFICITS (REFERRED TO HEREAFTER AS THE ΑSYNUCLEIONOPATHY EXACERBATING COMMUNITY; AEC) AS COMPARED TO A NON-EXACERBATING CONTROL (NEC). WE ISOLATED BACTERIAL STRAINS FROM RELEVANT PATIENT STOOLS VIA ANAEROBIC CULTUROMICS AND FOUND THAT DEFINED CULTURABLE MICROBIAL CONSORTIA FROM AEC AND NEC ALSO SHOWED DIVERGENT IMPACTS ON SYNUCLEINOPATHY. IMMUNOHISTOCHEMICAL ANALYSES AND SINGLE- CELL RNA SEQUENCING OF INTESTINES AND BRAINS OF AEC-COLONIZED MICE REVEALED SIGNATURES OF NEUROINFLAMMATION, INCLUDING ALTERED GRANULOCYTE RECRUITMENT AND ACTIVATION IN THE MENINGES, AS COMPARED TO NEC-COLONIZED CONTROLS. BASED ON THESE RESULTS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SPECIFIC MICROBES AND/OR THEIR BIOACTIVE METABOLITES IN THE AEC ELICIT GUT-BRAIN IMMUNE DEVIATIONS AND ALTER SYNUCLEINOPATHY IN LBD. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DEFINE THE SPECIFIC BACTERIAL STRAINS OR MINIMAL CONSORTIA FROM THE AEC AND NEC THAT INCREASE OR DECREASE CORTICAL ΑSYN PATHOLOGY AND BEHAVIORAL DEFICITS USING TOP-DOWN AND BOTTOM-UP APPROACHES. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE THE MENINGEAL IMMUNE POPULATIONS (2.1) AND BACTERIAL METABOLITES (2.2) THAT IMPACT BRAIN PATHOLOGY. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL DEFINE POTENTIAL CAUSAL MICROBES AND METABOLITES THAT MAY CONTRIBUTE TO LBD PATHOGENESIS, REVEALING NEW BIOMARKERS FOR EARLY LBD AND LAYING THE GROUNDWORK FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW NEUROPROTECTIVE THERAPIES FOR LBD AND OTHER SYNUCLEINOPATHIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISMS OF COMPARTMENTALIZED ROS SENSING IN THE BRAIN - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT HIGH ATP PRODUCTION THROUGH OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION (OXPHOS) IN THE MITOCHONDRIA IS REQUIRED TO MEET THE ENERGY DEMANDS OF NEURONAL ACTIVITY. REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES (ROS) ARE A GROUP OF REACTIVE METABOLITES AND A BYPRODUCT OF NORMAL OXPHOS FUNCTION. AT HIGH CONCENTRATIONS, THEY CAN DESTROY NUCLEIC ACIDS AND INACTIVATE PROTEINS. THUS, NEURONS MUST BALANCE MITOCHONDRIAL ENERGY PRODUCTION WITH ROS CONTROL, BUT HOW THEY DO SO REMAINS INCOMPLETELY UNDERSTOOD. TO ANSWER THESE QUESTIONS, WE UNDERTOOK A CYSTEINE-FOCUSED BASE EDITING SCREEN TO IDENTIFY CYSTEINES THAT ARE REQUIRED FOR THE CELLULAR RESPONSE TO ROS. THIS APPROACH IDENTIFIED TWO CYSTEINES WITHIN VPS35, A COMPONENT OF THE RETROMER TRAFFICKING COMPLEX, THAT SENSE CYTOSOLIC ROS. WHEN REDUCED, VPS35 CAN SHUTTLE PLASMA MEMBRANE PROTEINS TO SUPPORT MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSLATION. OXIDATION OF THESE CYSTEINES SHUTS DOWN MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSLATION AND DECREASES ROS. THUS, MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSLATION IS A CENTRAL LEVER WITHIN THE CELL TO CONTROL ROS GENERATION. WITH THIS DISCOVERY, MANY QUESTIONS REMAIN. IT IS NOT KNOWN HOW A NEURON BALANCES ATP GENERATION WITH AN ANTI-ROS RESPONSE THAT TARGETS MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSLATION, NOR HOW THE REGULATION OF MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSLATION VARIES ACROSS DIVERSE MITOCHONDRIAL POOLS WITH DIFFERENT METABOLIC NEEDS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT INHIBITION OF MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSLATION IS A CRITICAL MECHANISM FOR REDUCING MITOCHONDRIAL ROS GENERATION IN NEURONS. WE WILL CHARACTERIZE HOW NEUROTRANSMISSION REGULATES VPS35 AND HOW MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSLATION IS CONTROLLED ACROSS THE SOMA, AXON, AND BOUTON OF HIGHLY COMPARTMENTALIZED NEURONS. THE RESEARCH PROPOSED HEREIN TAKES FULL ADVANTAGE OF A SERIES OF RECENTLY CONCEIVED METHODS: CHEMICAL PROTEOMICS, GENOME-WIDE CRISPR SCREENS AND UNTARGETED METABOLOMICS. WE WILL USE THESE IN AN INTEGRATED MANNER TO EFFECTIVELY DISSECT HOW MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSLATION UNDERLIES CELLULAR ROS IN NEURONAL BIOLOGY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTERROGATING ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN AGGREGATE-ASSOCIATED PROTEOMES TO IDENTIFY MODIFIERS OF LEWY BODY DISEASE. - 1. ABSTRACT AFTER ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, LEWY BODY DEMENTIA IS THE MOST COMMON FORM OF DEMENTIA AFFLICTING AGING INDIVIDUALS. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ADVANCE OUR MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLE THAT ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN PLAYS IN DISEASE PATHOGENESIS AND PROGRESSION OF ALZHEIMER DISEASE RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRDS) SUCH AS LEWY BODY DEMENTIA (LBD) BY DISCOVERING MOLECULAR INTERACTORS OF ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN AND DEFINING THE ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN AGGREGATE-ASSOCIATED INTERACTOME. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR ENVIRONMENT CONTRIBUTES TO ΑSYN-ASSOCIATED LEWY PATHOLOGY PROCESSES AND THAT QUANTITATIVE PROTEOMICS CAN BE APPLIED TO CAPTURE THE MOLECULAR MICROENVIRONMENT PROXIMAL TO ΑSYN AS IT FORMS OLIGOMERS, PROTOFIBRILS, AND INSOLUBLE AGGREGATES TO REVEAL KEY COFACTORS IN AGGREGATION AND NEURODEGENERATION PROCESSES. IN THIS APPLICATION WE WILL EMPLOY PROXIMITY-DEPENDENT BIOTIN IDENTIFICATION IN LIVE HUMAN NEURONS AND MOUSE BRAIN SLICES (BIOID) (AIM 1) AND IN SITU PROBE-DEPENDENT PROXIMITY PROFILING IN FIXED HUMAN PATIENT BRAIN TISSUE (PROPPR) (AIM 2) TO ENABLE BIOTINYLATION OF ΑSYN-ASSOCIATED COFACTORS UNDER PHYSIOLOGICAL AND PATHOGENIC CONDITIONS. PROXIMAL BIOTINYLATED PROTEINS WILL BE ISOLATED VIA AFFINITY PURIFICATION AND IDENTIFIED BY QUANTITATIVE MASS SPECTROMETRY. WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING COORDINATED AIMS TO ACCOMPLISH THIS GOAL: IN AIM 1 WE WILL CAPTURE, IDENTIFY, AND DIFFERENTIATE INTRACELLULAR PROTEINS IN PROXIMITY TO SOLUBLE ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN IN VITRO IN HUMAN IPSC-DERIVED NEURONS AND GLIA AND EX VIVO IN MURINE ORGANOTYPIC BRAIN SLICE CULTURES, OR IN PROXIMITY TO INSOLUBLE AGGREGATES OF ALPHA- SYNUCLEIN INDUCED BY HUMAN-DERIVED PROTEOPATHIC SEEDS. IN AIM 2 WE WILL USE IN SITU PROBE-DEPENDENT PROXIMITY PROFILING IN HUMAN POSTMORTEM BRAIN TO PROBE THE ΑSYN-ASSOCIATED PROTEOME IN DIFFERENT SYNUCLEINOPATHIES (DLB, PD, MSA), OVER TIME (COMPARING BRAIN REGIONS AFFECTED EARLY VERSUS LATE IN DISEASE COURSE), AND WITH CONSIDERATION OF COMORBID PATHOLOGIES (TAU, TDP-43, BETA-AMYLOID) TO REVEAL THE UNDERLYING GLOBAL AND LOCAL PROTEOMIC LANDSCAPE OF SYNUCLEINOPATHIES AND SHED LIGHT ON THE MOLECULAR HETEROGENEITY AND MECHANISMS UNDERLYING DISEASE. FINALLY IN AIM 3 WE WILL FUNCTIONALLY INVESTIGATE THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL ROLE OF SELECT CANDIDATE PROTEINS IN HUMAN TISSUE, CELL MODELS, EX VIVO BRAIN SLICE CULTURES OR IN VIVO IN MURINE MODELS. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS WILL SPECIFICALLY IDENTIFY MOLECULAR COFACTORS OF ΑSYN MONOMERS, OLIGOMERS, AND AGGREGATES AND DETERMINE THE PROCESSES AT PLAY DURING LEWY PATHOLOGY FORMATION, MATURATION, AND PROGRESSION.
