description: MECHANISMS OF FIBRINOGEN-MEDIATED CEREBROVASCULAR PATHOLOGY IN CEREBRAL AMYLOID ANGIOPATHY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH AIMS TO ELUCIDATE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING CEREBRAL AMYLOID ANGIOPATHY (CAA), A MAJOR CEREBROVASCULAR PATHOLOGY IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) THAT AFFECTS OVER 80% OF AD PATIENTS. CAA IS CHARACTERIZED BY THE ACCUMULATION OF AMYLOID-Β (AΒ) AROUND CEREBRAL VESSEL, PARTICULARLY WITHIN PERIVASCULAR SPACES (PVS), LEADING TO IMPAIRED CLEARANCE, VASCULAR DEGENERATION, AND CHRONIC NEUROINFLAMMATION. RECENT CLINICAL TRIALS SUGGEST A STRONG LINK BETWEEN CAA AND AMYLOID-RELATED IMAGING ABNORMALITIES (ARIA) IN PATIENTS UNDERGOING AΒ-TARGETING IMMUNOTHERAPY, UNDERSCORING THE CLINICAL RELEVANCE OF THIS PATHOLOGY. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISMS THAT DRIVE AΒ ACCUMULATION IN THE PVS AND INITIATE VASCULAR DYSFUNCTION REMAIN UNCLEAR. EMERGING EVIDENCE IMPLICATES FIBRINOGEN—A MAJOR BLOOD CLOTTING PROTEIN—IN EXACERBATING CAA PATHOLOGY THROUGH ITS INTERACTION WITH AΒ AND CO-DEPOSITION IN THE PVS. OUR RECENT STUDIES DEMONSTRATE THAT FIBRINOGEN–AΒ INTERACTION COMPLEXES DISRUPT AQUAPORIN-4 (AQP4) POLARIZATION ON ASTROCYTE ENDFEET, IMPAIRING PERIVASCULAR CLEARANCE AND PROMOTING A FEED-FORWARD CYCLE OF AΒ ACCUMULATION AND VASCULAR INJURY. NOTABLY, WE OBSERVED FIBRINOGEN EXTRAVASATION IN CAA MOUSE MODELS WITHOUT MARKED BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER (BBB) ALTERATION, SUGGESTING ALTERNATIVE MECHANISMS MAY CONTRIBUTE TO FIBRINOGEN LEAKAGE INTO THE PVS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT AGE-RELATED UPREGULATION OF CAVEOLAE-MEDIATED TRANSCYTOSIS, REGULATED BY ENDOTHELIAL CAVEOLIN-1 (CAV-1), FACILITATES FIBRINOGEN ENTRY INTO THE PVS, WHERE IT BINDS AΒ, DISRUPTS AQP4 POLARIZATION, AND PROMOTES NEUROINFLAMMATION. TO TEST THIS, WE WILL PURSUE THREE AIMS: (1) INVESTIGATE HOW FIBRINOGEN–AΒ CO- DEPOSITION IMPAIRS PERIVASCULAR CLEARANCE AND ALTERS AQP4 POLARIZATION IN CAA MOUSE MODELS AND HUMAN CAA TISSUE; (2) DEFINE THE ROLE OF CAV-1–MEDIATED TRANSCYTOSIS IN FIBRINOGEN EXTRAVASATION AND CEREBROVASCULAR PATHOLOGY; AND (3) DETERMINE THE INFLUENCE OF HUMAN APOLIPOPROTEIN E4 (APOE4) ON AΒ–FIBRINOGEN INTERACTIONS, VASCULAR DAMAGE, AND PERIVASCULAR CLEARANCE USING APOE KNOCK-IN (KI) RAT MODELS CROSSED WITH A NOVEL KNOCK-IN (KI) RAT MODEL FOR CAA. APOE4 IS THE STRONGEST GENETIC RISK FACTOR FOR LATE-ONSET AD AND IS KNOWN TO EXACERBATE CAA SEVERITY, IMPAIR AΒ CLEARANCE, AND PROMOTE VASCULAR DYSFUNCTION. INCLUDING APOE4 IN THIS STUDY ALLOWS US TO INVESTIGATE ITS SPECIFIC ROLE IN MODULATING THE FIBRINOGEN–AΒ INTERACTION, AQP4 DEPOLARIZATION, AND BBB INTEGRITY. THESE STUDIES WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHT INTO HOW APOE4 AMPLIFIES CAA PATHOLOGY AND CONTRIBUTES TO DISEASE PROGRESSION IN A GENOTYPE-DEPENDENT MANNER. THIS STUDY COMBINES NOVEL GENETIC MODELS, SPATIAL METABOLOMICS, ADVANCED IMAGING, AND HUMAN TISSUE VALIDATION TO DEFINE A PREVIOUSLY UNRECOGNIZED FIBRINOGEN–CAV-1–AQP4 AXIS IN CAA PATHOGENESIS. OUR FINDINGS WILL ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF BBB PERMEABILITY AND PERIVASCULAR CLEARANCE IN AD AND MAY IDENTIFY NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR TREATING CEREBROVASCULAR COMPLICATIONS IN CAA.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PATHOLOGICAL RELEVANCE OF TDP-43 INTERACTIONS WITH TRANSLATION MACHINERY IN NEURODEGENERATION - PROJECT SUMMARY NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES, INCLUDING AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (ALS), FRONTOTEMPORAL DEMENTIA (FTD), ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD), AND RELATED DEMENTIAS SUCH AS LIMBIC-PREDOMINANT AGE-RELATED TDP-43 ENCEPHALOPATHY (LATE) AND CEREBRAL AGE-RELATED TDP-43 WITH SCLEROSIS (CARTS), ARE CHARACTERIZED BY PROGRESSIVE NEURONAL LOSS AND THE ACCUMULATION OF PATHOLOGICAL PROTEIN AGGREGATES. AMONG THESE, TDP-43 PROTEINOPATHY HAS EMERGED AS A CENTRAL CONTRIBUTOR TO DISEASE PROGRESSION. THIS PATHOLOGICAL FEATURE INVOLVES THE MISLOCALIZATION OF TAR DNA-BINDING PROTEIN 43 (TDP-43) FROM THE NUCLEUS TO THE CYTOPLASM, WHERE IT FORMS HYPERPHOSPHORYLATED INCLUSIONS THAT DISRUPT RNA METABOLISM, MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION, AND PROTEIN HOMEOSTASIS, ULTIMATELY DRIVING NEURONAL DYSFUNCTION AND DEATH. DESPITE ITS IMPORTANCE, NO THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES SPECIFICALLY TARGETING TDP-43 TOXICITY HAVE REACHED CLINICAL APPLICATION, HIGHLIGHTING THE URGENCY OF UNDERSTANDING THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH TDP-43 AGGREGATION IS INITIATED AND SUSTAINED. WHILE DECADES OF RESEARCH HAVE CLARIFIED TDP-43’S ROLE IN RNA SPLICING AND AUTOREGULATION WITHIN THE NUCLEUS, THE PATHOLOGICAL SIGNIFICANCE OF ITS SELECTIVE CYTOPLASMIC CLUSTERING WITH TRANSLATIONAL MACHINERY REMAINS POORLY DEFINED. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES IDENTIFIED A SHORT N-TERMINAL MOTIF WITHIN TDP-43, TERMED THE TRANSLATION-RELATED PROTEIN-BINDING MOTIF (TBM), THAT MEDIATES INTERACTIONS WITH RIBOSOMAL AND TRANSLATION FACTORS. DELETION OF THIS MOTIF IN MICE (ΔTBM) INDUCES ROBUST AGE- DEPENDENT ACCUMULATION OF PHOSPHORYLATED TDP-43 INCLUSIONS, MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION, WIDESPREAD NEURONAL LOSS, AND PROGRESSIVE MOTOR AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS, CLOSELY RECAPITULATING HUMAN TDP-43 PROTEINOPATHIES. COMPLEMENTARY STUDIES IN IPSC-DERIVED HUMAN NEURONS DEMONSTRATED IMPAIRED NEURONAL ACTIVITY DESPITE PRESERVED NUCLEAR LOCALIZATION AND SPLICING FUNCTION, INDICATING THAT DISRUPTION OF TRANSLATION-RELATED INTERACTIONS, RATHER THAN NUCLEAR DYSFUNCTION, MAY BE A CRITICAL INITIATING EVENT IN DISEASE. BASED ON THESE FINDINGS, WE WILL INVESTIGATE WHETHER AND HOW LOSS OF TDP-43 INTERACTIONS WITH THE TRANSLATIONAL MACHINERY DRIVES THE INITIATION OF TDP-43 PATHOLOGY, NEUROINFLAMMATION, AND NEURODEGENERATION. THIS WORK IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT ADDRESSES A CRITICAL, UNDEREXPLORED MECHANISM OF TDP-43 PROTEINOPATHY WITH BROAD RELEVANCE TO MULTIPLE NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES. IT IS INNOVATIVE IN FOCUSING ON THE NOVEL CONCEPT THAT TDP-43 DISENGAGEMENT FROM THE TRANSLATIONAL MACHINERY MAY BE A PRIMARY DRIVER OF PATHOLOGY, IN LEVERAGING ΔTBM MICE THAT FAITHFULLY RECAPITULATE HALLMARK NEURONAL AND GLIAL TDP-43 PATHOLOGY, AND IN INTEGRATING CROSS-SPECIES APPROACHES WITH PATIENT-DERIVED TISSUES TO RIGOROUSLY ESTABLISH DISEASE RELEVANCE. BY ELUCIDATING HOW DISRUPTION OF TDP-43–TRANSLATION MACHINERY INTERACTIONS CONTRIBUTES TO DISEASE INITIATION AND PROGRESSION, THIS PROJECT MAY UNCOVER NEW MOLECULAR TARGETS FOR THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION ACROSS ALS, FTD, AD, AND RELATED DEMENTIAS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: FLUOVIEW FV4000 CONFOCAL MICROSCOPE FOR BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH IN IDAHO - THIS PROPOSAL REPRESENTS A REQUEST FROM A GROUP OF INVESTIGATORS FROM THE DEPARTMENTS OF BIOLOGICAL SCIENCES, BIOMEDICAL AND PHARMACEUTICAL SCIENCES, AND CHEMISTRY AT IDAHO STATE UNIVERSITY (ISU), AS WELL AS THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND THE UNIVERSITY OF IDAHO-ABERDEEN RESEARCH AND EXTENSION CENTER, FOR FUNDING TO ACQUIRE A SHARED-RESOURCE FV4000 CONFOCAL MICROSCOPE. THE ACQUISITION OF THE FV4000 CONFOCAL MICROSCOPE IS AN URGENT NECESSITY TO REPLACE THE EXISTING, OBSOLETE FV1000 UNIT IN OUR ADVANCED IMAGING FACILITY. THE FV4000 CONFOCAL WILL ENABLE THE ACQUISITION OF HIGH-RESOLUTION IMAGES AND THREE- DIMENSIONAL RECONSTRUCTIONS OF SPATIAL ORGANIZATION IN BOTH FIXED AND LIVE CELLS, SUPPORTING A WIDE RANGE OF RESEARCH PROJECTS FUNDED BY THE NIH AND NSF. MOREOVER, THE FV4000 CONFOCAL WILL SUPPORT EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES IN TWO VERTICAL INTEGRATED PROJECT PROGRAMS: NEUROBIOLOGY ACROSS THE LIFESPAN AND GENE REGULATORY NETWORKS, AS WELL AS THE ISU SUMMER STUDENT RESEARCH PROGRAM OF IDAHO-INBRE. THIS INITIATIVE WILL BENEFIT BOTH UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS AT ISU, AS WELL AS THOSE AT OTHER UNIVERSITIES AND RESEARCH INSTITUTES ACROSS IDAHO. RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT WILL BENEFIT FROM THE FV4000 CONFOCAL INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO 1) UNDERSTANDING HOW AGING IMPACTS REGULATORY MECHANISMS OF INSULIN SECRETION AND ITS ASSOCIATION WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES, 2) IDENTIFYING GENES ASSOCIATED WITH CRANIOFACIAL DEVELOPMENT, 3) UNDERSTANDING THE IMMUNE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING XENOBIOTIC-ASSOCIATED AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE, 4) IDENTIFYING GENE EXPRESSION PATHWAYS IN THE MITOCHONDRIA IN PLASMODIUM FALCIPARUM PARASITES THAT CAUSE MALARIA AND 4) UNDERSTANDING THE IMPACTS OF GAMMA-AMINOBUTYRIC ACID ON ASTROCYTE LIPID METABOLISM AND ITS ASSOCIATION WITH ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. THE EXPERTISE AND INSTITUTIONAL SUPPORT FOR THIS INSTRUMENT ARE EXCEPTIONAL. THE SYSTEM WILL BE HOUSED IN AND MANAGED BY THE MOLECULAR RESEARCH CORE FACILITY (MRCF) LOCATED UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF ISU OFFICE FOR RESEARCH ASSOCIATES LISA MCDOUGALL AND JASON WERTH, WHO HAVE COMBINED OVER 20 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE IN SUPERVISING THIS FACILITY AND MAINTAINING HIGH-END RESEARCH EQUIPMENT IN MICROSCOPY. ALSO, DRS. DE LA CRUZ, RAY AND SERVE (MAJOR USERS) HAVE EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN CONFOCAL MICROSCOPY. THE OFFICE FOR RESEARCH WILL BE SUPPORTING POST- AWARD EXPENSES TO ENSURE THE FV4000 CONFOCAL OPERATES OPTIMALLY THROUGHOUT ITS LIFESPAN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADVANCED RESPIROMETRY SYSTEM FOR EXPANDING RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL CAPACITY IN BIOMEDICAL SCIENCES AT UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS – FORT SMITH - THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS – FORT SMITH (UAFS) IS A PRIMARILY UNDERGRADUATE INSTITUTION SERVING ABOUT 5,500 STUDENTS FROM A DIVERSE REGIONAL POPULATION SET. MANY OF THESE STUDENTS COME FROM SMALL TO MEDIUM SIZED HIGH SCHOOLS WITH ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED BACKGROUNDS. WHEREIN MORE THAN HALF OUR STUDENTS ARE PELL GRANT ELIGIBLE AND MORE THAN 50% ARE FIRST-GENERATION COLLEGE ATTENDEES. FOLLOWING A TRANSITION TO A FOUR-YEAR UNIVERSITY IN 2002, UAFS EXPERIENCED RAPID GROWTH IN ACADEMIC PROGRAMS. HOWEVER, OUR RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE HAS NOT KEPT PACE WITH INSTITUTIONAL EVOLUTION. OUR CURRENT RESEARCH CAPACITY (EQUIPMENT AND SPACE) REFLECTS OUR COMMUNITY COLLEGE HERITAGE, HAMPERING OUR ABILITY TO PROVIDE OUR STUDENTS WITH RESEARCH EXPERIENCES. HAVING A STATE-OF THE-ART SABLE SYSTEMS RESPIROMETRY SYSTEM WILL ENABLE OUR STUDENTS, MANY OF WHOM ARE THE FIRST TO PURSUE BIOMEDICAL CAREERS, TO HAVE ACCESS TO THE SAME CALIBER OF INSTRUMENTATION AVAILABLE AT MORE-ESTABLISHED INSTITUTIONS. THE SABLE SYSTEMS RESPIROMETRY SYSTEM IS A SUITE OF EQUIPMENT THAT CAN BE USED TO MEASURE METABOLIC RATES (OXYGEN CONSUMPTION AND CARBON DIOXIDE PRODUCTION), METHANE, AND WATER FLUX. THESE METRICS CAN BE MEASURED IN ANIMALS (FROM A FRUIT FLY TO A LION), HUMANS, PLANTS, FUNGAL CULTURES, AND/OR WATER SAMPLES. THE ABILITY TO MEASURE THESE METRICS WOULD ALLOW FOR RESEARCH THAT INVESTIGATES THE IMPACTS OF STRESS, POLLUTION, AND/OR BEHAVIOR ON THE PHYSIOLOGY OF ANIMALS AND HUMANS. THIS SUITE OF EQUIPMENT WOULD ALLOW FOR A VARIETY OF PHYSIOLOGICAL RESPONSES TO BE MEASURED SUCH AS RESTING/BASAL METABOLIC RATES, EXERCISE METABOLISM, RESPIRATORY QUOTIENT, SPECIFIC DYNAMIC ACTION, GASTROINTESTINAL FERMENTATION ACTIVITY, RESPIRATORY WATER LOSS, AND WHOLE-BODY WATER LOSS. IMMEDIATE USE OF THE SYSTEM WILL ALLOW FOR INVESTIGATIONS ON THE IMPACT OF PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS ON METABOLIC RATE, EXAMINING THE POSITIVE EFFECTS OF MIND-BODY INTERVENTIONS ON METABOLIC RATE, THE IMPACTS OF MICROPLASTIC LOAD ON ANIMAL PHYSIOLOGY, DETERMINING THE IMPACTS OF AN INVASIVE PARASITE ON INTERMEDIATE HOSTS, AND MONITORING SURFACE AND GROUND WATER QUALITY. MOST BIOLOGY, PSYCHOLOGY, AND GEOCHEMISTRY MAJORS CARRY OUT UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH WHILE AT UAFS. THE UNIVERSITY SPONSORS AN ANNUAL SYMPOSIUM SHOWCASING RESEARCH ACHIEVEMENTS EACH SPRING. UAFS STUDENTS ALSO PRESENT THEIR WORK AT LOCAL AND REGIONAL VENUES. RECENT EXAMPLES INCLUDE THE ARKANSAS INBRE CONFERENCES AND THE MEETINGS OF THE ARKANSAS ACADEMY OF SCIENCE. INCORPORATION OF THIS EQUIPMENT WILL GREATLY INCREASE THE DEPTH AND BREADTH OF WORK THAT CAN BE ACCOMPLISHED AT OUR RESOURCE LIMITED INSTITUTION, ENABLING OUR STUDENTS TO PRODUCE IMPACTFUL AND PUBLISHABLE MANUSCRIPTS. THE AVAILABILITY OF THIS RESPIROMETRY SUITE WILL ALSO EXPAND THE ABILITY OF FACULTY TO SUCCESSFULLY SEEK EXTERNAL FUNDING. THE PRESENCE OF A RESEARCH- QUALITY RESPIROMETRY SYSTEM WILL OPEN NEW DOORS IN MULTIPLE COURSES IN BIOLOGY, PSYCHOLOGY, AND GEOLOGY. WHEREIN OUR STUDENTS WILL HAVE HANDS-ON, PRACTICAL EXPERIENCE WITH THESE HIGH-IMPACT RESEARCH TOOLS. WHICH WILL EXPAND THEIR SCIENTIFIC HORIZONS AND BETTER PREPARE THEM FOR FURTHER STUDY OR CAREERS IN BIOMEDICAL FIELDS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ACQUISITION OF A MATRIX-ASSISTED LASER DESORPTION/IONIZATION MASS SPECTROMETER - A TEAM OF NIH-FUNDED INVESTIGATORS REQUESTS A MATRIX-ASSISTED LASER DESORPTION/IONIZATION MASS SPECTROMETER (MALDI-MS), SPECIFICALLY AN AUTOFLEX MAX TOF/TOF MALDI-MS FROM BRUKER, A RELIABLE INSTRUMENT THAT FITS THE NEEDS OF MOST MAJOR AND MINOR USERS. THE INSTRUMENT WILL BE USED TO GAIN A DEEPER UNDERSTANDING OF A BROAD RANGE OF MOLECULES, INCLUDING PROTEINS, PEPTIDES, POLYMERS, ORGANIC SYNTHESIS PRODUCTS, AS WELL AS SETS OF MOLECULES SUCH AS PROTEOMES AND PEPTIDOMES FROM BIOLOGICAL FLUIDS. THE MALDI-MS WILL BE USED FOR FUNDED PROJECTS ON THE ANALYSIS OF PEPTIDOMES IN HUMAN SERUM AND MILK SAMPLES FROM DONORS WITH BREAST CANCER AND MATCHED CONTROLS; ANALYSIS OF SECRETOMES OF MCF7 CELLS WITH OVEREXPRESSED OR DOWNREGULATED JUMPING TRANSLOCATION PROTEIN, A CELL CYCLE REGULATOR AND PROTO-ONCOGENE; DEVELOPMENT OF NEXT-GENERATION SUBCELLULAR IMAGING REPORTERS FOR ORGANELLAR CHLORIDE USING THE “ORGANELLE CHEMOTYPE FINGERPRINTING” TECHNIQUE; DETERMINATION OF THE ROLE OF A SPECIFIC EPITHELIAL CELL TYPE RESIDING IN THE DEVELOPING INTESTINAL STEM CELL COMPARTMENT IN ZEBRAFISH; ELUCIDATION OF NEURAL PRECURSOR COMMUNICATION DURING DEVELOPMENT OF THE DROSOPHILA PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM; DEVELOPMENT OF A MOUSE MODEL OF TUBERCULOSIS THAT GENERATES HUMAN-LIKE PATHOLOGY; DETERMINATION OF THE EFFECT OF FERRITIN SUBUNIT COMPOSITION ON IRON CORE FORMATION AND THE ROLES OF PCBP1 AND NCOA4 IN THE FATE OF INTRACELLULAR FERRITIN; AND DEVELOPMENT OF RUGGED, EASY-TO-USE METHODS FOR ANALYTE DETECTION ESSENTIAL FOR ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING, FOOD SAFETY, HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING (HTS) OF DRUG CANDIDATES, AND DISEASE DIAGNOSIS. THERE IS NO MALDI-MS WITHIN A 100-MILE RADIUS FROM CLARKSON UNIVERSITY. THE NEW MALDI-MS WILL SERVE USERS FROM FOUR CLARKSON DEPARTMENTS (BIOLOGY, CHEMISTRY & BIOMOLECULAR SCIENCE/CHEMISTRY & BIOCHEMISTRY, CIVIL & ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING, AND CHEMICAL & BIOMOLECULAR ENGINEERING) AS WELL AS FROM FOUR INSTITUTIONS LOCATED IN NORTHERN NEW YORK STATE: THE STATE UNIVERSITY OF NEW YORK (SUNY) AT POTSDAM, 2) SUNY AT PLATTSBURGH, 3) ST. LAWRENCE UNIVERSITY IN CANTON, AND 4) THE TRUDEAU INSTITUTE AT SARANAC LAKE. THE MALDI-MS WILL BE LOCATED IN THE SCIENCE CENTER AND WILL BECOME PART OF THE DEPARTMENT OF CHEMISTRY & BIOMOLECULAR SCIENCE’S (CHEMISTRY & BIOCHEMISTRY) SHARED INSTRUMENT FACILITY, WHERE IT WILL BE ACCESSIBLE TO ALL CLARKSON RESEARCHERS AND FACULTY AND RESEARCHERS FROM SURROUNDING UNIVERSITIES AND INSTITUTES WITHIN A 100-MILE RADIUS. ONE HIGHLY EXPERIENCED ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR AND INSTRUMENT MANAGER WITH FULL SALARY SUPPORT FROM CBS WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DAILY OPERATION, WEEKLY MAINTENANCE, NEW USER TRAINING, AS WELL AS SCHEDULING AND CHARGING USERS FOR INSTRUMENT USAGE. THE INSTRUMENT MANAGER’S MANAGERIAL EFFORTS WILL BE COMPLEMENTED BY THE PI’S EXTENSIVE EXPERTISE USING MALDI-MS (BEGINNING WHEN HE WAS A GRADUATE STUDENT IN GERMANY IN 2000). BEYOND THE PROJECT PERIOD, CLARKSON UNIVERSITY WILL PROVIDE FUNDS FOR MALDI-MS’S SERVICE CONTRACT, TO ENSURE THAT THE INSTRUMENT IS WELL MAINTAINED AND TO ENABLE ITS USE WELL BEYOND ITS STANDARD LIFETIME.

description: PULSED ESR OXYGEN IMAGING SYSTEM (ESROI) - PROJECT SUMMARY  THE AIM OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO SUPPORT THE PURCHASE OF AN ADVANCED PULSE ELECTRON SPIN RESONANCE OXYGEN IMAGER (ESROI), ALSO KNOWN AS ELECTRON PARAMAGNETIC RESONANCE OXYGEN IMAGER (EPROI), AT CORNELL UNIVERSITY. IT WILL BE INSTALLED AT THE CORNELL MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING FACILITY (CMRIF) AND ADMINISTRATED BY THE NATIONAL RESOURCE FOR ADVANCED ELECTRON SPIN RESONANCE SPECTROSCOPY (ACERT), WHICH IS FUNDED BY THE NIGMS R24 AWARD. THE ESROI SYSTEM REQUESTED IS THE ONLY COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE ESR-BASED OXYGEN IMAGER AND WOULD BE THE FIRST ONE IN THE NORTHEAST UNITED STATES. IT ENABLES FAST, NON-INVASIVE AND ACCURATE 3D PARTIAL PRESSION OF OXYGEN (PO2) MAPPING IN HIGH SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL RESOLUTIONS ACROSS A WIDE RANGE OF SAMPLE TYPES, INCLUDING IN VITRO, IN VIVO AND EX VIVO APPLICATIONS. THERE IS A SUBSTANTIAL AND GROWING DEMAND FOR SUCH OXYGEN IMAGING CAPACITIES, AS THEY PROVIDE CRITICAL SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL INFORMATION ABOUT TISSUE OXYGENATION. THE DATA IS HIGHLY RELEVANT TO NUMEROUS BIOMEDICAL, PHYSIOLOGICAL, PATHOLOGICAL CONDITIONS, INCLUDING HYPOXIA, TUMOR, INJURY RECOVERY AND DEMENTIA. THE ESROI SYSTEM WILL BE USED BY RESEARCH GROUPS AT CORNELL, UPSTATE NEW YORK, GREATER NEW YORK CITY AND ACROSS THE NORTHEAST REGION. THE NIH-FUNDED RESEARCH PROJECTS OF THE MAJOR USERS INCLUDE: (1) MITOCHONDRIAL (DYS)FUNCTION IN ARTICULAR CARTILAGE HEALTH, DISEASE AND REGENERATION; (2) NON- INVASIVE, IN VIVO MEASUREMENT OF TISSUE OXYGEN IN ACUTE CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASES; (3) ISLET FUNCTION UPON TRANSPLANTATION; (4) IMAGE-GUIDED LIGHT DOSIMETRY IN INTERSTITIAL PHOTODYNAMIC THERAPY (I-PDT) FOR THE TREATMENT OF LOCALLY ADVANCED CANCER REFRACTORY TO CURRENT STANDARD OF CARE THERAPIES; AND (5) MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION IN OSTEOLINEAGE CELLS DURING AGING. ADDITIONAL PROJECTS FROM MINOR USERS INCLUDES: (6) SPATIALLY FRACTIONATED RADIOTHERAPY (SFRT) IN OSTEOSARCOMA; (7) ESROI IN PLANT SCIENCES: ROOT-ZONE OXYGEN DYNAMICS IN LETTUCE; (8) MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION IN THE BRAIN DURING NEURODEGENERATION OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE; (9) 3D OXYGEN IMAGING OF ENTHESIS REPAIR IN ROTATOR CUFF AND ACL INJURY MODELS; AND (10) OXYGEN DYNAMICS AND MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION DURING THE POST-CARDIAC ARREST PERIOD. ACERT IS THE ONLY NATIONAL RESOURCE IN THE UNITED STATES DEDICATED TO ESR RESEARCH AND HAS A LONG-STANDING TRADITION OF LEADERSHIP IN DEVELOPING AND PROMOTING ESR TECHNOLOGIES, INCLUDING ESR IMAGING. HOWEVER, ACERT CURRENTLY LACKS IMAGING CAPABILITIES FOR LARGE BIOLOGICAL SPECIMENS—REPRESENTING THE LAST MAJOR ESR MODALITY NOT YET AVAILABLE AT THE CENTER. ACERT’S STRATEGIC LOCATION, ROBUST INFRASTRUCTURE, PROVEN HISTORY OF TECHNOLOGICAL INNOVATION, AND WELL-ESTABLISHED SYSTEMS FOR TICKETING, RESERVATIONS, AND SERVICE TRACKING, COMBINED WITH A STRONG ADMINISTRATIVE AND OUTREACH TEAM, ENSURE EFFECTIVE OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF NEW TECHNOLOGIES. MOST IMPORTANTLY, ITS UNWAVERING COMMITMENT TO USER SUPPORT—INCLUDING A FREE-ACCESS POLICY FOR ACADEMIC USERS—POSITIONS ACERT TO SUCCESSFULLY IMPLEMENT, PROMOTE, AND EXPAND THE USE OF THE ESROI SYSTEM.

description: COMMERCIAL READINESS OF A CATHETER FOR COMPLEX PERCUTANEOUS CORONARY INTERVENTION - ABSTRACT NEARLY 1 MILLION PERCUTANEOUS CORONARY INTERVENTIONS (PCIS) ARE PERFORMED EACH YEAR IN THE US. APPROXIMATELY 70% OF THESE CASES ARE CONSIDERED COMPLEX AND REQUIRE THE TREATMENT OF CALCIFIED LESIONS, TORTUOUS VESSELS, AND MULTI-VESSEL DISEASE, OFTEN WITH TOTAL OR SUB-TOTALLY OCCLUDED LESIONS. MANY OPERATORS AVOID THESE MORE COMPLEX CASES DUE TO THE LACK OF GUIDE CATHETER SUPPORT REQUIRED TO EFFECTIVELY DELIVER CORONARY STENTS AND OTHER INTERVENTIONAL DEVICES. TO OVERCOME THIS LIMITATION, GUIDE EXTENSION CATHETERS (GEC) HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED TO HELP DELIVER STENTS IN THESE CHALLENGING ANATOMIES. HOWEVER, GECS ARE UTILIZED IN ONLY 18% OF ALL CORONARY INTERVENTIONS, MOSTLY AS A BAILOUT OPTION, BECAUSE OF THEIR INABILITY TO ACCESS MORE DISTAL TORTUOUS LESIONS IN 28% OF CASES WHICH PREVENTS STENT DELIVERY. BLUNT ENDED TUBULAR GECS ALSO HAVE SERIOUS SAFETY ISSUES WITH CORONARY ARTERY DISSECTION AND/OR PLAQUE OR THROMBUS EMBOLIZATION. SUCH LIMITED UTILIZATION DEMONSTRATES THAT A SIGNIFICANT VOLUME OF PATIENTS ARE NOT TREATED EFFECTIVELY. HENCE, CROSSLINER INC. HAS DEVELOPED A NOVEL MULTI-FUNCTIONAL GEC THAT COMBINES THE REQUIREMENT FOR DEEPER CATHETER INTUBATION WITH A MICROCATHETER LEADING TIP, AND PRE-DILATATION BALLOON ON THE LEADING ELEMENT, TO ALLOW SAFE CROSSING OF SEVERE LESIONS IN TORTUOUS CORONARY VESSELS, WITH BALLOON PRE-DILATATION, FOLLOWED BY CROSSING THE LESION WITH THE GUIDE EXTENSION AND THEN SEAMLESS STENT DELIVERY. THE COMBINATION OF A GEC WITH A SEAMLESS TRANSITION TO A MICROCATHETER-BALLOON PROVIDES THE CAPABILITY FOR EASIER AND SAFER STENT DELIVERY, WHICH CAN BE UNSHEATHED AT THE LESION AS OPPOSED TO BEING DELIVERED FROM A POORLY SUPPORTED PROXIMAL LOCATION. THIS APPROACH ENABLED BY THE CROSSLINER GEC WILL SUBSTANTIALLY IMPROVE PCI IN PATIENTS WITH COMPLEX LESIONS WHILE REDUCING RISKS, PROCEDURAL DURATION, RADIATION/CONTRAST EXPOSURE, STENT DISLODGEMENT, CORONARY DISSECTION AND PERFORATION THAT OCCUR WITH CURRENT GECS. DATA FROM PHASE II BENCH VERIFICATION STUDIES DEMONSTRATES SAFETY AND PERFORMANCE AGAINST ISO STANDARDS WHILE CONFORMING TO DESIGN SPECIFICATIONS. FORMATIVE USABILITY EVALUATION SUPPORTS THE EASE OF USE AND SAFETY, AS VALIDATED ON BENCH AND IN VIVO WHICH DEMONSTRATED A 100% TECHNICAL SUCCESS RATE, 40% REDUCTION IN TIME TO TREAT, 43% REDUCTION IN RADIATION DOSE, AND 2-3X INCREASE IN CORONARY INTUBATION DEPTH COMPARED TO CURRENT MARKET LEADING GECS. THESE RESULTS AND VALUE PROPOSITION WERE CORROBORATED BY INTERVIEWS WITH 67 INTERVENTIONAL CARDIOLOGISTS WHERE OVER 70% EXPECTED IMPROVED CLINICAL OUTCOMES AND 94% INDICATED THEY WOULD USE THE CROSSLINER GEC, RATHER THAN A CONVENTIONAL GEC. THE COMPANY IS NOW READY TO EXECUTE FINAL PRE-LAUNCH ACTIVITIES, INCLUDING SCALING OF MANUFACTURING CAPACITY AND GENERATING THE MARKETING AND TRAINING PROGRAMS NECESSARY TO ASSURE EARLY CLINICAL ADOPTION. HENCE, SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE AIMS PROPOSED IN THIS CRP APPLICATION WILL POSITION THE CROSSLINER GEC SYSTEM FOR EARLY COMMERCIAL SUCCESS AND BRING TO MARKET A HIGHLY INNOVATIVE DEVICE TO IMPROVE THE TREATMENT OF COMPLEX PCI PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: RESEARCH TRAINING IN INFECTION AND IMMUNITY - ABSTRACT THE CONTINUALLY EVOLVING RISK OF BOTH KNOWN AND EMERGING INFECTIONS CREATES CRITICAL, UNMET KNOWLEDGE GAPS THAT DEMAND WELL-TRAINED INVESTIGATORS WHO CAN ADDRESS CHALLENGES SPANNING BASIC MECHANISMS, TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH, AND CLINICAL APPLICATION. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE BAYLOR COLLEGE OF MEDICINE RESEARCH TRAINING IN INFECTION AND IMMUNITY (BCM RTII) IS TO TRAIN A NEW GENERATION OF SCIENTISTS TO SAFELY AND ETHICALLY CONDUCT MULTIDISCIPLINARY, STATE-OF-THE-ART RESEARCH IN INFECTIOUS DISEASES, WHILE EQUIPPING THEM WITH THE SKILLS TO BECOME LEADERS IN THE FIELD. THE PROGRAM WILL SUPPORT FOUR MD, MD/PHD, OR PHD POSTDOCTORAL FELLOWS EACH YEAR FOR TWO YEARS OF MENTORED TRAINING. THE TRAINING PROGRAM INCLUDES A COMPREHENSIVE CURRICULUM DESIGNED TO PREPARE FELLOWS TO THINK CRITICALLY AND INDEPENDENTLY; TO IDENTIFY IMPORTANT RESEARCH QUESTIONS; TO RIGOROUSLY AND REPRODUCIBLY GENERATE NEW KNOWLEDGE; AND TO DEVELOP AS COLLABORATIVE SCIENTISTS CAPABLE OF ADVANCING THE FIELD. THE PROGRAM FEATURES THREE TRAINING TRACKS—LABORATORY-BASED RESEARCH, PATIENT-BASED RESEARCH, AND GLOBAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH RESEARCH—LEVERAGING THE EXCEPTIONAL RESOURCES OF BCM AND THE BROADER TEXAS MEDICAL CENTER. AREAS OF RESEARCH FOCUS INCLUDE: 1) ENTERIC PATHOGENS; 2) VACCINE DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING; 3) HIV; 4) INFECTION PATHOGENESIS AND IMMUNITY; 5) TROPICAL MEDICINE AND PUBLIC HEALTH; 6) MICROBIOME AND FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS; AND 7) IMMUNOLOGY AND INFECTIONS IN IMMUNOCOMPROMISED HOSTS. TRAINEES WILL BE SUPPORTED BY A HIGHLY QUALIFIED AND WELL-FUNDED POOL OF 33 FACULTY MENTORS SPANNING ALL CAREER STAGES, WITH STRUCTURED GUIDANCE FROM BOTH MD AND PHD CO-MENTORS, INDIVIDUALIZED ADVISORY COMMITTEES, AND ROBUST RESEARCH AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES. TRAINING WILL EMPHASIZE RIGOR AND REPRODUCIBILITY, RESPONSIBLE CONDUCT OF RESEARCH, AND PROFESSIONAL SKILLS INCLUDING GRANT WRITING, LEADERSHIP, AND LABORATORY MANAGEMENT. CORE TRAINING ACTIVITIES FOR ALL MD AND PHD TRAINEES INCLUDE DEVELOPING AND MAINTAINING AN IDP, ATTENDING THE RTII CAREER TRANSITIONS SEMINARS, TAKING COURSES ON CLINICAL INVESTIGATION, GRANTS AND CONTRACTS, AND HUMAN SUBJECTS RESEARCH; PARTICIPATING IN TEAM SCIENCE AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT SEMINARS; AND ATTENDING A WEEKLY CLINICAL CASE DISCUSSION, A WEEKLY JOURNAL CLUB, AND AN ANNUAL SCIENTIFIC RETREAT. THE PROGRAM DIRECTORS ARE THOMAS GIORDANO, MD, MPH, AND INDIRA MYSOREKAR, PHD, WHO OVERSEE AND ADMINISTER THE PROGRAM GUIDED BY AN EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE, SELECTION COMMITTEE, AND INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL ADVISORY COMMITTEES. METRICS OF SUCCESS WILL INCLUDE THE PROPORTION OF FELLOWS WHO ENTER AND REMAIN IN PRIMARILY RESEARCH AND RESEARCH-RELATED FIELDS, THEIR SUBSEQUENT GRANT FUNDING, AND THEIR SCIENTIFIC CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE FIELD OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES. THE BCM RTII PROGRAM WILL BE THE ONLY T32 IN THE REGION THAT OFFERS PATIENT-BASED AND GLOBAL OR PUBLIC HEALTH CLINICAL RESEARCH TRAINING FOR POST-DOCTORAL FELLOWS ACROSS THE BREADTH OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES, COMPLEMENTING LABORATORY-BASED RESEARCH TRAINING AND FILLING A CRITICAL GAP IN NATIONAL WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT. IN DOING SO, THE BCM RTII WILL PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN SUSTAINING AND EXPANDING THE NATIONAL INFECTIOUS DISEASE RESEARCH WORKFORCE.

description: PREDOCTORAL TRAINING PROGRAM IN MOLECULAR BIOLOGY, CELL BIOLOGY, AND BIOCHEMISTRY (MCBB) - PROJECT ABSTRACT THE MOST PRESSING QUESTIONS IN BIOLOGY TODAY CAN ONLY BE ADDRESSED BY INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH EFFORTS. THE MOLECULAR BIOLOGY, CELL BIOLOGY, & BIOCHEMISTRY (MCBB) PROGRAM AT BOSTON UNIVERSITY SPANS MULTIPLE DEPARTMENTS AND DISCIPLINES, AND TRAINS STUDENTS TO USE INNOVATIVE APPROACHES TO ATTACK QUESTIONS IN MOLECULAR BIOSCIENCES. OUR GRADUATES LEAVE PREPARED FOR A BROAD RANGE OF CAREERS IN ACADEMIA, INDUSTRY, AND GOVERNMENT. THE MCBB PROGRAM IS HIGHLY COMPETITIVE, SELECTING ~6% OF APPLICANTS WITH BACKGROUNDS IN CHEMISTRY, BIOLOGY, AND ENGINEERING. INCOMING FIRST-YEAR STUDENTS CAN ROTATE IN THE LABS OF 37 AFFILIATED FACULTY MEMBERS IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF BIOLOGY, CHEMISTRY, BIOMEDICAL ENGINEERING, ELECTRICAL AND COMPUTER ENGINEERING, PHYSICS, AND COMPUTING AND DATA SCIENCES. PARTICIPATING FACULTY ARE SELECTED FOR THEIR ROBUST RESEARCH ACTIVITY AND COMMITMENT TO GRADUATE MENTORING. TO BUILD STUDENTS’ CORE ACADEMIC FOUNDATION AND COHORT RELATIONSHIPS, WE REQUIRE A SET OF TECHNICAL (MOLECULAR BIOLOGY, BIOCHEMISTRY, AND CELL BIOLOGY) AND SOFT-SKILL CLASSES (E.G. PEDAGOGY, GRANT WRITING). STUDENTS THEN TAILOR THEIR ACADEMIC CURRICULUM TO MATCH THEIR EXPERIENCE AND INTERESTS. THE PROGRAM HAS ADDED NEW FEATURES TO PROVIDE ROBUST QUANTITATIVE TRAINING: WINTER WORKSHOPS TO DEVELOP PROGRAMMING SKILLS, A NEW FALL BIOINFORMATICS COURSE, AND A SUMMER BOOTCAMP TO REINFORCE PRINCIPLES OF STATISTICS, BIOLOGICAL NUMERACY, AND REPRODUCIBLE RESEARCH. WE ALSO TRAIN STUDENTS IN EFFECTIVE ORAL COMMUNICATION THROUGH ANNUAL SEMINARS, WHICH INCORPORATE INSTRUCTION IN BEST PRACTICES AND INDIVIDUAL FEEDBACK, AND A COLLABORATION WITH BU’S COLLEGE OF COMMUNICATION. PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT INCLUDES TRAINING IN THE RESPONSIBLE CONDUCT OF RESEARCH, WORKSHOPS, A PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT CLASS, AND A COLLECTION OF >100 DIGITAL CREDENTIAL CLASSES FROM BU’S GRADUATE AND POSTDOCTORAL SUCCESS TEAM. THE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT CLASS EXPLORES VARIED CAREERS THROUGH ALUMNI CAREER PANELS AND HELPS STUDENTS DEVELOP SKILLS NEEDED TO SUCCESSFULLY COMPETE FOR JOBS. THESE SEMINARS, CLASSES, AND AN ANNUAL RETREAT ALSO HELP DEVELOP A COHESIVE COMMUNITY OF STUDENTS AS THEY PROGRESS THROUGH THEIR PHD TRAINING. THIS PROPOSAL REQUESTS FUNDING FOR STUDENTS IN YEARS 1-2 OF THEIR TRAINING, WITH TWO NEW STUDENTS ADMITTED TO THE T32 IN EACH YEAR. BU WILL FUND ONE ADDITIONAL STUDENT PER YEAR. WE WILL RIGOROUSLY ASSESS PROGRAM EFFICACY AND OUTCOMES WITH THE EXPERTISE OF BU’S OFFICE OF RESEARCH. STUDENTS IN THE PROGRAM BENEFIT FROM BU’S STRENGTHS IN SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY, BIOPHOTONICS AND IMAGING, SYSTEMS NEUROSCIENCE, MOLECULAR IMMUNOLOGY, AND BEYOND. THE PROGRAM AIMS TO CREATE A POSITIVE IMPACT BY STRENGTHENING THE NATIONAL STEM WORKFORCE WITH HIGHLY SKILLED, INTERDISCIPLINARY SCIENTISTS.

description: CAREER SUCCESS THROUGH TRANSDISCIPLINARY BIOMEDICAL SCIENCE TRAINING - PROPOSED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS AT SAN ANTONIO (UTSA), THE PURPOSE OF THE PROPOSED T32 PROGRAM, ENTITLED “CAREER SUCCESS THROUGH TRANSDISCIPLINARY BIOMEDICAL SCIENCE TRAINING”, IS TO TRAIN DOCTORAL STUDENTS IN THE BIOMEDICAL AND BEHAVIORAL (COLLECTIVELY TERMED BIOMEDICAL) SCIENCES. THE PROGRAM WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED APPROACHES TO ENHANCE OUR TRAINEES' RECRUITMENT, MENTORING AND WELLNESS, RETENTION; DEPTH OF PROFESSIONAL, OPERATIONAL, AND TECHNICAL TRAINING; AND CAREER PATH TRAJECTORY. THE PROGRAM WILL PROMOTE STUDENTS' RECRUITMENT AND ADMISSION, RETENTION, MENTORING SUPPORT, AND WELLNESS DURING THEIR STUDIES THAT GUIDE THEM TOWARDS BIOMEDICAL CAREERS. IT WILL SUPPORT TRAINEES IN BIOMEDICAL ENGINEERING, CHEMISTRY, NEUROSCIENCE, CELL, AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY, COMPUTER SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING, MECHANICAL ENGINEERING, AND PSYCHOLOGY PH.D. PROGRAMS. THREE NEW PH.D. STUDENTS WILL BE INDUCTED AND MENTORED IN THE FIRST 2 YEARS, AND FIVE NEW PH.D. STUDENTS WILL BE INDUCTED AND MENTORED IN THE LAST 3 YEARS; 21 STUDENTS ARE EXPECTED TO RECEIVE TRAINING OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROGRAM. THE GRADUATE SCHOOL WILL SUPPORT TWO ADDITIONAL SLOTS PER YEAR FOR A TOTAL OF 10 STUDENTS.  THE TOTAL NUMBER OF STUDENTS SUPPORTED FOR THIS PROGRAM WILL BE 31 STUDENTS FOR 5 YEARS OF FUNDING. THE PROPOSED INTERVENTIONS WILL PROMOTE 85% RETENTION OF ITS TRAINEES AND REDUCE TIME-TO-DEGREE FROM 4.8 TO 4.6 YEARS. TRAINING FOCUSED ON PSYCHOSOCIAL WELLNESS, MENTORING, CAREER DEVELOPMENT, AND INSTRUCTION IN METHODS FOR ENHANCING REPRODUCIBILITY ARE INTEGRATED THROUGHOUT THE TRAINING CYCLE. THE PROPOSED T32 PROGRAM HAS KEY FEATURES THAT MAKE IT INNOVATIVE AND STAGE-DEPENDENT, WITH SESSIONS EACH SUMMER DESIGNED TO FOCUS TRAINEES' ATTENTION ON CRITICAL MILESTONES OF THE FOLLOWING YEAR; SOME TRAINING WILL BE PROVIDED EARLIER TO PSYCHOLOGY STUDENTS WHO ARE IN A 3-YEAR PROGRAM. IT LEVERAGES INSTITUTIONAL RESOURCES, WITH PARTNERSHIPS IN PLACE FOR TRAINEES TO RECEIVE TRAINING FROM THE UTSA CAREER CENTER, LEADERSHIP AND VOLUNTEER SERVICES AND WELLBEING SERVICES, THE UTSA OFFICE OF RESEARCH INTEGRITY, AND GRADUATE SCHOOL. THE PROPOSED T32 TRAINING IS PROGRESSIVE, BEGINNING WITH FOUNDATIONAL TOPICS DESIGNED TO  LEVEL THE PLAYING FIELD , PROVIDING DATA SCIENCE COURSES, COMMERCIALIZATION, AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP COURSES AS FOUNDATIONS FOR ALL SUBSEQUENT TRAINING WITHIN THE PROGRAM. ALL PROPOSAL/DISSERTATION WRITING AND PRESENTATION WORKSHOPS, WELLNESS, INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY PROTECTION AND COMMERCIALIZATION/ENTREPRENEURSHIP, AS WELL AS RESUME WRITING AND MOCK CAREER INTERVIEWS WILL BE PROVIDED IN THE SUMMER, EXCEPT FIRST-SEMESTER FOUNDATIONAL TRAINING. ACADEMIC YEAR TRAINING AND PRESENTATIONS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH THE MULTI-FOCUS WEEKLY GROUP SESSIONS THAT INCORPORATE PSYCHOSOCIAL TRAINING, ALUMNI AND ROLE MODEL SCIENTIST VISITS, INTRODUCTORY TRAINING IN BUDGETING, LEADERSHIP, CLIFTON STRENGTHSFINDER, AND COLLEGE-LEVEL TEACHING. MENTORING IS A SIGNIFICANT COMPONENT OF THIS TRAINING PROGRAM, INVOLVING BEING MENTORED BY SCIENTISTS AT VARIOUS CAREER STAGES. TRAINEES WILL HAVE OPPORTUNITIES TO PRACTICE THEIR SCIENTIFIC COMMUNICATION SKILLS IN PROGRESSIVELY RIGOROUS ENVIRONMENTS FOR POSTER, ORAL, AND THREE MINUTE THESIS PRESENTATIONS.

description: STRATEGY TRIAL OF PERSONALIZED IMMUNOMODULATORY THERAPY FOR HIV-RELATED CRYPTOCOCCAL MENINGITIS - ABSTRACT  FUNGAL INFECTIONS ARE A COMMON CAUSE OF OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS (OIS) IN IMMUNOCOMPROMISED INDIVIDUALS. AMONG THE MOST SEVERE HIV-RELATED OIS IS FUNGAL MENINGITIS, WITH CRYPTOCOCCAL MENINGITIS BEING THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF ADULT MENINGITIS IN AFRICA, ACCOUNTING FOR APPROXIMATELY 19% OF HIV-RELATED DEATHS GLOBALLY. INCIDENCE IN THE UNITED STATES IS ~1.1 PER 100,000 POPULATION WITH HOSPITALIZATIONS BEING LONG AND EXPENSIVE.  CURRENT TREATMENT GUIDELINES IN BOTH THE UNITED STATES AND INTERNATIONALLY RECOMMEND INTRAVENOUS (IV) LIPOSOMAL AMPHOTERICIN B WITH ORAL FLUCYTOSINE (5FC) AND FLUCONAZOLE. HOWEVER, EVEN WITH THIS FIRST-LINE THERAPY, MORTALITY BY 10 WEEKS IS ~25% IN LOW- AND MIDDLE-INCOME SETTINGS. OUTCOMES IN HIGH-INCOME COUNTRIES ARE SIMILARLY SUBOPTIMAL, WITH ~15% EARLY MORTALITY WITHIN 90 DAYS AND ~25% MORTALITY BY 1 YEAR.  HISTORICALLY, TREATMENT HAS FOCUSED SOLELY ON ANTIFUNGAL THERAPY, LARGELY IGNORING THE HOST IMMUNE RESPONSE DUE TO ITS COMPLEXITY AND HETEROGENEITY. EMERGING HUMAN DATA SUGGEST THAT THE DAMAGE-RESPONSE IMMUNE FRAMEWORK UNDERLIES HIV-ASSOCIATED CRYPTOCOCCAL MENINGITIS. TODAY, INDIVIDUALS WITH HIV AND CRYPTOCOCCOSIS ARE MORE IMMUNOLOGICALLY COMPLEX, AS HALF PRESENT WHILE RECEIVING ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY, WHICH MAY OR MAY NOT BE EFFECTIVE FOR THAT PERSON. ADDITIONAL ANTIFUNGAL THERAPY IS UNLIKELY TO FURTHER IMPROVE OUTCOMES, AS WE HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT INDIVIDUALS WITH ENHANCED CSF EARLY FUNGICIDAL ACTIVITY (I.E., MORE RAPID FUNGAL KILLING, >0.60 LOG10CFU/ML/DAY) DO NOT HAVE BETTER SURVIVAL OUTCOMES THAN THOSE WITH MORE MODEST CSF CLEARANCE RATES (E.G. 0.20-0.30 LOG10 CFU/ML/DAY). TO FURTHER IMPROVE OUTCOMES, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT IT IS NECESSARY TO ASSESS WHERE INDIVIDUALS RESIDE ON THE DAMAGE-RESPONSE IMMUNE PARABOLA AND ADDRESS THEIR HOST IMMUNE STATUS.  WE PROPOSE A PHASE II/III PLATFORM TRIAL TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF INDIVIDUALLY CUSTOMIZED IMMUNOTHERAPY IN HIV-RELATED CRYPTOCOCCAL MENINGITIS. WE WILL CONDUCT A PHASE II TRIAL (N=40) FOLLOWED BY A PHASE III TRIAL (N=200 IN TOTAL IN THE EXPERIMENTAL ARM). TREATMENT EFFECT WILL BE COMPARED AGAINST 200 CONCURRENTLY RANDOMIZED CONTROLS RECEIVING STANDARD OF CARE ANTIFUNGAL THERAPY ALONE. ADJUNCTIVE IMMUNOTHERAPY WILL BE CUSTOMIZED BASED ON PATHOGEN BURDEN AND HOST IMMUNE STATUS, ADDRESSING TYPE 1 T HELPER CELL (TH1) DEFICITS, TH1 EXCESSIVE RESPONSES, OR INAPPROPRIATE TYPE 2 T HELPER CELL (TH2) RESPONSES. SPECIFIC AIM 1. VALIDATE THE DAMAGE-RESPONSE IMMUNE FRAMEWORK FOR HIV-ASSOCIATED CRYPTOCOCCAL  MENINGITIS TO IDENTIFY THE SUBGROUPS WITH AN IMMUNOLOGIC CONTRIBUTION TO DISEASE. SPECIFIC AIM 2. DETERMINE IF PERSONALIZED ADJUNCTIVE IMMUNOMODULATORY THERAPY IMPROVES CLINICAL  OUTCOMES IN HIV-ASSOCIATED CRYPTOCOCCAL MENINGITIS IN A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL. IMPACT: WE SEEK TO INNOVATE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINICAL MEDICINE BY TESTING PERSONALIZED IMMUNOTHERAPY TAILORED TO AN INDIVIDUAL'S IMMUNE RESPONSE AND PATHOGEN BURDEN IN CRYPTOCOCCAL MENINGITIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LEVERAGING JAK INHIBITORS TO HALT AUTOIMMUNE ATTACK INDUCED BY IMMUNE CHECKPOINT INHIBITORS - PROJECT SUMMARY IMMUNE CHECKPOINT INHIBITOR INDUCED DIABETES MELLITUS (ICI-DM) IS A RARE BUT HIGHLY MORBID, CHRONIC IMMUNE RELATED ADVERSE EVENT (IRAE) THAT OCCURS IN PATIENTS UNDERGOING CANCER IMMUNOTHERAPY. WE PROPOSE THE USE OF JANUS KINASE INHIBITORS (JAKI) TO ATTENUATE OR REVERSE THE COURSE OF ICI-DM IN PATIENTS UNDERGOING ICI THERAPY FOR TREATMENT OF SOLID MALIGNANCY. WE HAVE STRONG PRECLINICAL EVIDENCE FOR EFFICACY OF THIS AGENT USING THE NOD MOUSE MODEL, COUPLED WITH SAFETY OF USE IN PATIENTS WITH CANCER AND CLINICAL EVIDENCE FOR EFFICACY IN PATIENTS WITH EARLY ONSET, SPONTANEOUS TYPE 1 DIABETES (T1D). THIS IS A PHASE 1/2 MULTI-CENTER, OPEN-LABEL, SINGLE ARM PROSPECTIVE CLINICAL TRIAL. WE WILL USE A TWELVE WEEK COURSE OF BARICITINIB, AN ORAL JAKI, IN INDIVIDUALS WITH RECENT ONSET ICI-DM FOLLOWED BY A TWELVE WEEK OBSERVATION PERIOD. IN AIM 1, WE WILL ASSESS THE EFFICACY OF JAKI IN PRESERVING INSULIN PRODUCTION THROUGH MEASUREMENT OF C-PEPTIDE IN MIXED MEAL TOLERANCE TESTING (PRIMARY OUTCOME), ALONG WITH ADDITIONAL MEASURES OF GLYCEMIC CONTROL (SECONDARY OUTCOMES). IN AIM 2, WE WILL ASSESS THE SAFETY OF JAKI IN THIS PATIENT POPULATION, INCLUDING ONCOLOGY OUTCOMES. IN AIM 3, WE WILL ASSESS THE EFFECT OF JAKI ON THE IMMUNE ENVIRONMENT AND INVESTIGATE HETEROGENEITY IN THE ICI-DM COHORT. WE WILL ASSESS IMMUNE CELL SUBSETS USING SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING WITH ANALYSIS OF THE T AND B CELL RECEPTOR REPERTOIRES WITH CONFIRMATION OF CHANGES THROUGH FLOW CYTOMETRY AND CHANGES IN THE CYTOKINES AS PATIENTS START AND PROGRESS THROUGH JAKI EXPOSURE. WE WILL ALSO ASSESS ASSOCIATIONS OF RESPONSE TO JAKI TREATMENT WITH ISLET AUTOANTIBODIES AND T1D GENETIC RISK, WHICH ARE KNOWN HETEROGENOUS FEATURES OF ICI-DM. THESE MECHANISTIC STUDIES WILL IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW SHORT-TERM JAKI TREATMENT IMPACTS THE IMMUNE ENVIRONMENT IN INDIVIDUALS WITH AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE AND CANCER. THIS CLINICAL TRIAL WILL BE THE FIRST IN HUMANS AIMED TO PRESERVE INSULIN PRODUCTION IN PATIENTS WITH ICI-DM AND REVERSE A CHRONIC ENDOCRINE IRAE.

description: DECIPHER DOSE ACCUMULATION FOR ONLINE ADAPTIVE RADIOTHERAPY - PROJECT SUMMARY ONLINE ADAPTIVE RADIOTHERAPY (ART) ALLOWS FOR REAL-TIME ADJUSTMENTS OF RADIATION PLANS TO ACCOUNT FOR DAILY ANATOMICAL VARIATIONS BY RE-PLANNING WHILE THE PATIENT IS ON THE TREATMENT TABLE, USING NEWLY ACQUIRED IMAGES. WHILE THIS PROCESS CAN BE RESOURCE-INTENSIVE, INNOVATIONS IN WORKFLOWS BY VARIOUS TEAMS HAVE MADE ART A REALITY IN CLINICAL PRACTICE. THESE WORKFLOWS BUILD ON COMMERCIAL ONLINE ART PLATFORMS INCLUDING THE ELEKTA UNITY MR-LINAC, WHICH USES MR-GUIDED TECHNOLOGY, AND THE VARIAN ETHOS, WHICH IS A CONE BEAM CT (CBCT)-GUIDED PLATFORM. DESPITE PROGRESS IN IMPLEMENTING ONLINE ART, THERE IS UNTAPPED POTENTIAL. CURRENT SYSTEMS DO NOT ACCURATELY ESTIMATE OR DISPLAY CUMULATIVE DOSES TO DISEASE TARGETS OR SPECIFIC ORGANS AT RISK OVER THE COURSE OF TREATMENT. THE ABILITY TO ACCURATELY QUANTIFY DELIVERED DOSE IS IMPORTANT FOR CLINICIANS TO EVALUATE WHETHER DOSIMETRIC CRITERIA ARE BEING MET IN AN AGGREGATION OVER MULTIPLE FRACTIONS, AS WELL AS TO GUIDE ONLINE ART TO ACHIEVE ULTIMATE THERAPEUTIC GOALS. ACCURATE DOSE ACCUMULATION DEPENDS ON PRECISE DEFORMABLE IMAGE REGISTRATION, BUT THIS IS CHALLENGING DUE TO ANATOMICAL VARIATIONS. IN ADDITION, QUICK EVALUATION OF DEFORMATION ACCURACY FOR ONLINE ART REMAINS IMPRACTICAL, AND THE APPROPRIATE DOSE ACCUMULATION APPROACH FOR TUMOR SHRINKAGE OR DISAPPEARANCE IS UNKNOWN. DESPITE ONGOING RESEARCH ON DOSE ACCUMULATION, FEW SOLUTIONS HAVE BEEN IMPLEMENTED IN COMMERCIAL SYSTEMS, PARTICULARLY FOR MR-LINAC ONLINE ART PLATFORMS. THIS GAP REPRESENTS A SIGNIFICANT UNMET CLINICAL NEED, GIVEN THE INCREASING USE OF ONLINE ART IN CLINICS. THE PRIMARY GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)-BASED DEFORMABLE IMAGE REGISTRATION TOOLS FOR EFFECTIVE AND AUTOMATED DOSE ACCUMULATION, ADDRESSING URGENT UNMET CLINICAL NEEDS IN ONLINE ART. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT THESE AI-BASED DEFORMABLE REGISTRATION TOOLS WILL ENABLE ACCURATE AND AUTOMATED DAILY DOSE ACCUMULATION, REVEALING THE DOSIMETRIC IMPACT OF DAILY ANATOMY CHANGES. THIS INFORMATION WILL FACILITATE INFORMED ONLINE ADAPTIVE DECISION-MAKING, REDUCING NORMAL TISSUE DOSE WHILE ACHIEVING THE TARGET DOSE. WE WILL ACCOMPLISH THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL BY PURSUING THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) ALGORITHM DEVELOPMENT AND PROTOTYPING. IN THIS AIM, WE WILL DEVELOP AN AI-BASED DEFORMABLE REGISTRATION ALGORITHM SPECIFICALLY FOR DOSE ACCUMULATION, AI-BASED QUICK DEFORMATION ERROR DETECTION TOOL, AND AN AI-GUIDED INTERACTIVE DEFORMATION EDITING TOOL. 2) IMPLEMENTATION AND VALIDATION OF DOSE ACCUMULATION FOR ONLINE ART. IN THIS AIM, WE WILL IMPLEMENT AND EVALUATION DOSE ACCUMULATION TOOLS TO INFORM ONLINE ADAPTIVE PLANNING AND DECISION-MAKING FOR BOTH MR-LINAC AND ETHOS SYSTEMS. SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL RESULT IN THE FIRST INTELLIGENT, EFFICIENT, AND RELIABLE AUTOMATED DOSE ACCUMULATION SYSTEM TO FACILITATE ONLINE ART TO ADVANCE CANCER CARE. ULTIMATELY, THIS WORK WILL UNLEASH THE POWER OF ONLINE ART TO ACHIEVE BETTER PRECISION AND PERSONALIZED RADIATION ONCOLOGY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: OPTIMIZING THE DOSING OF POST-TRANSPLANTATION CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE FOR PERIPHERAL BLOOD STEM CELL TRANSPLANTATION - PROJECT SUMMARY ALLOGENEIC HEMATOPOIETIC CELL TRANSPLANTATION (HCT) IS THE ONLY POTENTIALLY CURATIVE THERAPY FOR MANY MALIGNANT AND SEVERE NONMALIGNANT HEMATOLOGIC DISEASES, BUT ITS SUCCESS HAS BEEN LIMITED BY GRAFT-VERSUS-HOST DISEASE (GVHD) AND DONOR AVAILABILITY. HIGH-DOSE (50 MG/KG/DAY) POST-TRANSPLANTATION CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE (PTCY) REDUCES THE RISKS OF SEVERE GVHD, ALLOWING DONORS THAT ARE NOT FULLY HUMAN LEUKOCYTE ANTIGEN (HLA) MATCHED (E.G., HLA-HAPLOIDENTICAL) TO BE USED NEARLY AS SAFELY AS FULLY HLA-MATCHED DONORS. THUS, HIGH-DOSE PTCY HAS GREATLY IMPROVED ACCESS TO HCT. HIGH-DOSE PTCY ALSO RECENTLY BECAME STANDARD-OF-CARE (SOC) FOR HLA- MATCHED PERIPHERAL BLOOD STEM CELL (PBSC) HCT. OUR PRECLINICAL DATA SHOWED THAT INTERMEDIATE, RATHER THAN HIGH, DOSING OF PTCY MAXIMALLY PREVENTS GVHD WHILE LEADING TO LESS TOXICITY AND BETTER IMMUNE RECOVERY. IN A PHASE I/II CLINICAL TRIAL (NCT03983850) FOR MYELOABLATIVE HLA-HAPLOIDENTICAL BONE MARROW HCT, WE FOUND THAT 25 MG/KG/DAY PTCY EFFECTIVELY PREVENTED GVHD AND ALSO HAD CLINICAL BENEFITS INCLUDING LESS TOXICITY, FASTER ENGRAFTMENT, FASTER T-CELL RECOVERY, AND LESS CYTOMEGALOVIRUS INFECTION AND BK VIRUS-ASSOCIATED CYSTITIS COMPARED WITH HIGH-DOSE PTCY. OUR ONGOING PHASE I/II TRIAL (NCT04959175) OF BONE MARROW HCT WITH REDUCED- INTENSITY CONDITIONING (RIC) AND PTCY 25 MG/KG/DAY HAS SHOWN EQUALLY PROMISING RESULTS, INCLUDING LOW RELAPSE RATES. YET, THE OPTIMAL PTCY DOSE HAS NOT BEEN DEFINED AND LIKELY WILL VARY BASED ON THE GRAFT SOURCE AND DONOR/RECIPIENT HLA DISPARITY. HERE, WE WILL OPTIMIZE PTCY DOSING FOR HCT WITH PBSC, THE GRAFT SOURCE USED FOR ~90% OF HCTS WORLDWIDE. IN AIM 1, WE WILL CONDUCT A PTCY DOSE DE-ESCALATION PHASE I/II CLINICAL HCT TRIAL WITH RIC AND PBSC GRAFTS FROM HLA-MATCHED (RELATED OR UNRELATED) OR HLA-HAPLOIDENTICAL DONORS IN SEPARATE COHORTS (NCT05436418). THIS STUDY WILL IDENTIFY THE LOWEST WEIGHT-BASED PTCY DOSE FOR EACH COHORT THAT MAINTAINS PROTECTION AGAINST SEVERE ACUTE AND CHRONIC GVHD AND GRAFT FAILURE, AND ALSO WILL ASSESS THE CLINICAL BENEFITS OF THE LOWER DOSES. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE THE PHARMACOKINETIC EXPOSURES OF PTCY AND ITS ACTIVE METABOLITES FOR EACH PATIENT AND ASSESS HOW THEY AFFECT RISK FOR GVHD AND RELAPSE, RECOVERY OF T-CELL SUBSETS CONTRIBUTING TO OR PROTECTING FROM GVHD OCCURRENCE, AND LONGITUDINAL LYMPHOCYTE SUBSET IMMUNE RECONSTITUTION. IN AIM 3, WE WILL DETERMINE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE METABOLITE EXPOSURE AND T-CELL RECEPTOR (TCR) REPERTOIRE DIVERSITY AND CLONAL DYNAMICS, ANTI-VIRAL ANTIBODY REPERTOIRES, T-CELL RESPONSES TO BK VIRUS AND HERPES VIRUSES, BK VIRAL LEVELS IN BLOOD AND URINE, AND THE SEVERITY OF BK VIRUS-ASSOCIATED CYSTITIS. FOR AIMS 2 AND 3, DIFFERENCES BETWEEN HLA-MATCHED AND HLA-HAPLOIDENTICAL HCT ALSO WILL BE ASSESSED. OUR WORK WILL LEVERAGE THE EXPERTISE OF THE THREE COLLABORATING INSTITUTIONS AND ASSOCIATED INVESTIGATORS TO OPTIMIZE THE CURRENT SOC WHILE DEEPLY PROBING THE IMPACT OF PTCY DOSING ON IMMUNE RECOVERY AND SUBSEQUENT GVHD DEVELOPMENT, RELAPSE RISK, AND INFECTIOUS COMPLICATIONS. OUR RESULTS WILL MOTIVATE AND INFORM FUTURE RANDOMIZED STUDIES TO DEFINITIVELY IDENTIFY OPTIMAL PTCY DOSING ACCORDING TO DONOR TYPE AND STEM CELL SOURCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXPLOITING LIPID METABOLISM AND DIETARY INTERVENTIONS TO SENSITIZE KRAS-DRIVEN TUMORS TO FERROPTOSIS - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT THIS PROJECT WILL DETERMINE HOW DIETARY AND THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS INFLUENCE TUMOR DEVELOPMENT, PROGRESSION, AND TREATMENT RESPONSE IN LUNG, PANCREATIC, AND COLORECTAL CANCERS. STUDIES WILL INTEGRATE HUMAN TUMOR XENOGRAFTS, IMMUNOCOMPETENT SYNGENEIC MODELS, AND GENETICALLY ENGINEERED MOUSE MODELS THAT REPRODUCE KEY ONCOGENIC ALTERATIONS AND HISTOPATHOLOGIC FEATURES OF THE CORRESPONDING HUMAN DISEASES. BOTH MALE AND FEMALE MICE WILL BE USED, WITH AGE-MATCHED CONTROLS, TO EVALUATE TUMOR GROWTH, TREATMENT RESPONSE, METABOLIC ADAPTATION, AND CONTRIBUTIONS FROM THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT. TUMOR ESTABLISHMENT AND PROGRESSION WILL BE MONITORED USING APPROPRIATE IMAGING AND ENDOSCOPIC APPROACHES, INCLUDING MICRO-COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY AND COLONOSCOPY, AND INTERVENTIONS WILL BE INITIATED ACCORDING TO PREDEFINED TUMOR-SIZE CRITERIA. EXPERIMENTAL GROUP SIZES ARE SUPPORTED BY POWER CALCULATIONS AND HAVE BEEN SELECTED TO PROVIDE ADEQUATE STATISTICAL POWER WHILE LIMITING ANIMAL USE. VERTEBRATE ANIMALS ARE REQUIRED BECAUSE TWO-DIMENSIONAL CELL-CULTURE SYSTEMS CANNOT REPRODUCE THE SYSTEMIC INTERACTIONS AMONG DIET, WHOLE-BODY METABOLISM, TUMOR GENETICS, STROMAL COMPONENTS, IMMUNE RESPONSES, AND TREATMENT EXPOSURE THAT DETERMINE TUMOR GROWTH AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE IN VIVO. THE COMPLEMENTARY USE OF XENOGRAFT, SYNGENEIC, AND GENETICALLY ENGINEERED MODELS WILL PERMIT EVALUATION OF BOTH TUMOR-CELLINTRINSIC AND HOST-DEPENDENT MECHANISMS WHILE REDUCING THE NUMBER OF GENETICALLY ENGINEERED ANIMALS REQUIRED AND MAINTAINING THE BIOLOGICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE OF THE STUDY.

description: ENVIRONMENT, GENETICS, AND EPIGENETICS OF HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA RISK IN THE US - ABSTRACT HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA (HCC) INCIDENCE IN THE US HAS TRIPLED SINCE THE EARLY 1980S. IN PARTICULAR, HCC INCIDENCE IS INCREASING FOR NON-VIRAL HCC (THOSE WITHOUT A HISTORY OF HEPATITIS B OR HEPATITIS C INFECTION). HCC IS OFTEN DIAGNOSED AT ADVANCED STAGES WHEN TREATMENTS ARE NOT EFFECTIVE, LEADING TO POOR SURVIVAL WHERE 79% OF THOSE DIAGNOSED WITH HCC DIE WITHIN FIVE YEARS. MOREOVER, RECENTLY, BOTH GLOBALLY AND IN THE US, HCC ETIOLOGY HAS SHIFTED FROM VIRAL TO NON-VIRAL-RELATED CAUSES, AND UP TO 40% OF CASES IS UNEXPLAINED BY KNOWN RISK FACTORS. THUS, IDENTIFYING NOVEL RISK FACTORS CONTRIBUTING TO THE RISING INCIDENCE AND UNDERLYING MOLECULAR MECHANISMS IS CRITICAL TO REDUCE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY, PARTICULARLY FOR NON-VIRAL HCC. EMERGING RESEARCH HAS SHOWN THAT EXPOSURES TO HARMFUL ENVIRONMENTAL TOXINS AND METALS ARE POSITIVELY ASSOCIATED WITH HCC RISK IN ASIA AND AFRICA. THESE ENVIRONMENTAL TOXINS ARE UBIQUITOUS AND INCREASINGLY PREVALENT IN THE US AND MAY PLAY AN INSTRUMENTAL ROLE IN HCC RISK. YET, AFLATOXIN AND INORGANIC ARSENIC, HUMAN CARCINOGENS, HAVE BEEN LARGELY UNEXPLORED WITH HCC RISK IN US POPULATIONS. IN ADDITION, INDIVIDUAL GENETIC PREDISPOSITION TO HCC MAY INDEPENDENTLY INFLUENCE HCC RISK AND INTERACT WITH ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES TO MODIFY RISK. EMERGING EVIDENCE SHOWS THAT THESE ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES AFFECT DNA METHYLATION PROFILES IN GENES IMPORTANT FOR HEPATOCARCINOGENESIS. THUS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT DNA METHYLATION COULD SERVE AS AN IMPORTANT SUSCEPTIBILITY MARKER OF HCC THAT COULD BE USED TO IDENTIFY AT-RISK INDIVIDUALS AND PROVIDE IMPORTANT MECHANISTIC CLUES TO DISEASE ETIOLOGY. GIVEN MOST RESEARCH HAS FOCUSED ON HIGH-INCIDENCE COUNTRIES WITH A STRONG VIRAL HCC ETIOLOGY, AND EXPOSURE TO HARMFUL ENVIRONMENTAL TOXINS AND METALS ARE UBIQUITOUS AND INCREASINGLY PREVALENT IN THE US, WE PROPOSE TO FILL THE EVIDENCE GAP ON THESE ASSOCIATIONS IN US POPULATIONS AND ASSESS RISK AMONG GROUPS DISPROPORTIONATELY EXPOSED TO HIGHER LEVELS OF EXPOSURE (E.G., LOW SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS) AND HCC RISK. WE WILL CONDUCT A COMPREHENSIVE STUDY OF THE EFFECT OF UBIQUITOUS CARCINOGENS INCLUDING AFLATOXIN, ARSENIC AND CADMIUM ON HCC RISK IN THE LARGEST POOLED, NESTED, CASE-CONTROL STUDY (N=741 INCIDENT HCC CASES AND 741 INDIVIDUALLY MATCHED CONTROLS) FROM FOUR US-BASED PROSPECTIVE COHORTS: THE MULTIETHNIC COHORT STUDY; PROSTATE, LUNG, COLORECTAL AND OVARIAN CANCER SCREENING TRIAL; SISTER STUDY; AND SOUTHERN COMMUNITY COHORT STUDY. WE WILL EVALUATE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN EXPOSURE TO ENVIRONMENTAL CARCINOGENS INCLUDING AFLATOXIN AND METAL ELEMENTS (AIM 1) WITH HCC RISK. WE AIM TO IDENTIFY GENETIC VARIANTS OF HCC IN OUR DIVERSE US POPULATIONS AND EXPLORE POTENTIAL GENE-ENVIRONMENT INTERACTION (AIM 2). IN ADDITION, WE WILL CONDUCT AN EPIGENOME-WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDY OF HCC AND EVALUATE THE INDEPENDENT AND MEDIATIONAL EFFECT OF DNA METHYLATION ON HCC RISK (AIM 3). LED BY A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM, THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE THE MOST ROBUST EVIDENCE ON THE ROLE OF CARCINOGEN EXPOSURE LEVELS ON HCC RISK AND ON RELEVANT BIOLOGICAL PATHWAYS INVOLVED IN HEPATOCARCINOGENESIS TO INFORM PREVENTION STRATEGIES FOR THIS HIGHLY FATAL DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADVANCED RETINAL IMAGING OF THE CARDIA COHORT - PROGRAM DIRECTOR/PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR (LAST, FIRST, MIDDLE): GILL, MANJOT K.; AND LLOYD-JOES, DONALD M. ABSTRACT CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES (CVD) REMAIN THE LEADING CAUSE OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY WORLDWIDE. DESPITE ADVANCES IN PREVENTION, THE BURDEN OF CVD CONTINUES TO RISE, PARTICULARLY AMONG POPULATIONS WITH HIGH EXPOSURE TO MODIFIABLE RISK FACTORS SUCH AS SMOKING, POOR DIET, AND PHYSICAL INACTIVITY. DEMENTIA IS ANOTHER LEADING CAUSE OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY THAT HAS BEEN LINKED TO CVD BY COMMON UNDERLYING RISK FACTORS AND VASCULAR PATHOLOGY. OCULOMICS IS AN EMERGING FIELD THAT INTEGRATES OCULAR IMAGING BIOMARKERS INTO THE EARLY DETECTION, RISK ASSESSMENT, AND MONITORING OF SYSTEMIC DISEASES. THE EYE IS THE ONLY ORGAN IN THE BODY THAT ALLOWS FOR DIRECT NON-INVASIVE EVALUATION OF THE MICROCIRCULATION VIA COLOR FUNDUS PHOTOGRAPHY (CFP), OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY (OCT), AND OCT ANGIOGRAPHY (OCTA). RETINAL IMAGING HAS DEMONSTRATED ITS VALUE IN DETECTING SYSTEMIC CONDITIONS SUCH AS HYPERTENSION, DIABETES, HYPERLIPIDEMIA, CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE, CVD, AND DEMENTIA, AMONG OTHERS. RETINAL CHANGES OFTEN PRECEDE CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS AND CAN THEREFORE SERVE AS BIOMARKERS FOR EARLY DETECTION AND SCREENING. ENHANCED ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)-BASED ANALYSIS OF FP AND OCTA IMAGES HAS ALSO DEMONSTRATED ASSOCIATIONS WITH PREVALENT AND INCIDENT SYSTEMIC DISEASE OUTCOMES, WITH THE OPPORTUNITY TO AUGMENT RISK ASSESSMENT FOR CVD AND CHANGE PARADIGMS IN PREVENTIVE STRATEGIES AND PERSONALIZED MEDICINE. HOWEVER, TO DATE, THE VAST MAJORITY OF OCULOMICS DATA HAVE BEEN DERIVED FROM CROSS- SECTIONAL OR SHORT-TERM PROSPECTIVE CLINICAL STUDIES OF MIDDLE-AGED AND OLDER ADULTS. THE FEW STUDIES HAVE EXAMINED THE CUMULATIVE BURDEN OF LONGITUDINAL RISK FACTORS FROM YOUNG ADULTHOOD THAT ARE ASSOCIATED WITH PRE- CLINICAL RETINAL MICROVASCULAR FINDINGS IN MIDDLE AGE. FURTHERMORE, FEW STUDIES HAVE HOLISTICALLY ASSESSED SYSTEMIC VASCULAR TARGET-ORGAN DAMAGE, AND THE CORRELATIONS BETWEEN THE AGING PATTERNS OF DISTINCT ORGANS, IN A WELL- PHENOTYPED COHORT OF INDIVIDUALS. THE CORONARY ARTERY RISK DEVELOPMENT IN YOUNG ADULTS (CARDIA) STUDY ENROLLED 5,115 BLACK AND WHITE MEN AND WOMEN PARTICIPANTS AGED 18-30 YEARS IN 1985, AND HAS PERFORMED 10 IN-PERSON EXAMINATIONS OVER THE ENSUING DECADES. CARDIA EMBODIES AN EXTRAORDINARY OPPORTUNITY TO CAPTURE PRE-CLINICAL CHANGES IN ASYMPTOMATIC INDIVIDUALS IN MID-LIFE PRIOR TO DISEASE INCEPTION, AND EXAMINE LINKS TO UPSTREAM YOUNG ADULT PRECURSORS. WE PROPOSE TO PERFORM ADVANCED, NON-MYDRIATIC CFP, OCT, AND OCTA IMAGING IN 2482 CARDIA PARTICIPANTS DURING THE YEAR 40 EXAM SCHEDULED FOR 6/2026-7/2027. WE WILL ASSESS LONG-TERM EXPOSURES TO MODIFIABLE LIFESTYLE FACTORS, AS WELL AS CUMULATIVE PHYSIOLOGIC RISK FACTOR EXPOSURES THROUGH YOUNG ADULTHOOD, AND EXAMINE ASSOCIATIONS WITH PRE-CLINICAL FEATURES OF THE RETINAL VASCULATURE IN MID- LIFE. WE WILL ASSESS THE ASSOCIATION OF RETINAL MICROVASCULATURE FINDINGS WITH CEREBRAL SMALL-VESSEL DISEASE FINDINGS ON BRAIN MRI, AND WITH COGNITIVE FUNCTION TESTS. WE WILL ALSO ASSESS CORRELATIONS OF CFP, OCTA, AND RETINAL AGE, AS CALCULATED BY AI ANALYSIS OF CFP, WITH TARGET-ORGAN VASCULAR DAMAGE IN THE HEART, BRAIN, KIDNEY, AND LUNG, AND WITH EPIGENETIC MEASURES OF ACCELERATED AGING. agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNDERSTANDING HETEROGENEITY ACROSS PTSD, MDD AND ANXIETY BY LEVERAGING LARGE-SCALE MULTIMODAL NEUROIMAGING DATASETS - PROJECT SUMMARY PSYCHIATRIC COMORBIDITIES ARE COMMON IN INDIVIDUALS WITH POSTTRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER (PTSD), MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER (MDD) AND ANXIETY DISORDERS (ANXS) SUCH AS GENERALIZED ANXIETY DISORDER (GAD), SOCIAL ANXIETY DISORDER (SAD). PATIENTS WITH MULTIPLE COMORBIDITIES OFTEN EXPERIENCE MORE SYMPTOM SEVERITY, HIGHER RISK OF SUICIDAL BEHAVIOR, GREATER IMPAIRMENTS IN NEUROCOGNITIVE FUNCTIONING, AND POORER TREATMENT OUTCOMES. DIAGNOSTIC HETEROGENEITY AND HIGH COMORBIDITY AMONG THESE MENTAL DISORDERS SIGNIFICANTLY COMPLICATING PROGRESS IN CLARIFYING UNDERLYING NEURAL MECHANISMS OF MENTAL DISORDERS, AND EFFORTS TO ADVANCE PERSONALIZED MEDICINE. TO ADDRESS THIS ISSUE AND RESPOND TO NIH’S CALL FOR PRECISION MEDICINE, OUR PROPOSAL AIMS TO UTILIZE LARGE CLINICAL AND IMAGING DATASETS, ALONG WITH EXPLAINABLE DEEP LEARNING MODELS, TO IDENTIFY NEURAL BIOMARKERS AND BIOTYPES UNDERLYING PTSD, MDD AND ANXS, AND TO ASSESS THEIR UTILITY OF CLINICAL OUTCOMES. WE WILL FIRST APPLY A TOP-DOWN RESEARCH DOMAIN CRITERIA (RDOC) APPROACH TO IDENTIFY DISTINCT BIOMARKERS. IN ADDITION, WE WILL UTILIZE A BOTTOM-UP DATA-DRIVEN COMPUTATIONAL FRAMEWORK TO IDENTIFY SHARED TRANSDIAGNOSTIC BIOTYPES TO TACKLE HETEROGENEITY ACROSS PTSD, MDD AND ANXS. WE WILL LEVERAGE MULTIMODAL NEUROIMAGING DATA INCLUDING STRUCTURAL MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (MRI) AND RESTING-STATE FUNCTIONAL MRI (RS-FMRI) FROM FOUR GLOBALLY REPRESENTATIVE LIFESPAN DATASETS: THE ENIGMA-PTSD, THE ENIGMA-MDD, THE ENIGMA-ANXIETY, AND UK BIOBANK (UKBB) DATASETS, TO TEST THE GENERALIZABILITY OF THE DEEP LEARNING MODELS, AND THE UTILITY OF THE IDENTIFIED BIOMARKERS (FROM AIM 1) AND THE DATA-DRIVEN TRANSDIAGNOSTIC BIOTYPES (FROM AIM 2) IN PREDICTING TREATMENT OUTCOMES (AIM 3). THE RESULTS OF THIS STUDY MAY ENHANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF UNIQUE AND COMMON NEURAL PROFILES ACROSS PTSD, MDD, AND ANXS, AND HELP FUTURE TREATMENT DEVELOPMENT BY PROVIDING INITIAL GUIDANCE OF SELECTING BEST TREATMENTS THAT WORKS THE BEST FOR INDIVIDUAL PATIENT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: U19: CAUSES, CONSEQUENCES, AND MODIFIERS OF HETEROGENEITY IN AGING IN A NATURALISTIC NONHUMAN PRIMATE MODEL - OVERALL ABSTRACT AGING IS A UNIVERSAL YET HETEROGENEOUS PROCESS THAT CAN VARY BOTH WITHIN AND BETWEEN INDIVIDUALS. FOR INSTANCE, WHILE SOME MAY EXHIBIT SIGNS OF CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE EARLY IN LIFE, OTHERS MAINTAIN ROBUST HEART HEALTH INTO ADVANCED AGE. DESPITE MOUNTING EVIDENCE FOR VARIATION IN HUMAN AGING, WE STILL KNOW LITTLE ABOUT ITS CROSS-SYSTEM PATTERNING, NOR ITS CAUSES OR CONSEQUENCES. THIS GAP IN UNDERSTANDING IS PARTLY DUE TO THE SCARCITY OF MULTI-TISSUE, LONGITUDINAL DATA ACROSS LIFESPANS; LIMITED EXPERIMENTAL EVIDENCE ON AGING DETERMINANTS; AND THE CHALLENGE OF CAPTURING HUMAN LIFE-COURSE EXPERIENCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL COMPLEXITIES IN LABORATORY SETTINGS. THE FREE-RANGING RHESUS MACAQUE POPULATION ON CAYO SANTIAGO ISLAND OFFERS A UNIQUE WINDOW INTO THESE COMPLEXITIES IN A NATURALISTIC SETTING. THE ISLAND HOSTS THE WORLD'S LONGEST-RUNNING PRIMATE FIELD STATION, PROVIDING RICH LONGITUDINAL DATA ON A GENETICALLY DIVERSE POPULATION THAT MIRRORS HUMAN AGING ACROSS VARIOUS DOMAINS–PHYSIOLOGICAL, COGNITIVE, SENSORY, BEHAVIORAL, AND IMMUNOLOGICAL–IN A LIFESPAN THAT IS 3-4X FASTER THAN OURS. THIS UNIQUE POPULATION FACILITATES A DETAILED EXPLORATION OF AGING IN ONE OF OUR CLOSEST RELATIVES, OFFERING INSIGHTS WITH POTENTIAL TRANSLATIONAL VALUE TO HUMAN HEALTH. THIS MULTI-DISCIPLINARY, INTEGRATIVE, U19 RESEARCH PROGRAM AIMS TO ADDRESS THE FOLLOWING THREE QUESTIONS: 1) HOW WE AGE DIFFERENTLY: HERE, WE WILL QUANTIFY AGING HETEROGENEITY WITHIN AND ACROSS INDIVIDUALS BY MAPPING INTRA- AND INTER-INDIVIDUAL VARIATION IN AGING ACROSS DIFFERENT AGING DOMAINS AND TESTING IF THIS VARIATION PREDICTS MORTALITY. 2) WHY WE AGE DIFFERENTLY: LEVERAGING THE COMPREHENSIVE PHENOTYPING FROM AIM 1, WE WILL ELUCIDATE THE MOLECULAR AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS THAT ARE CAUSES OR CONSEQUENCES OF AGING. 3) CAN WE MODIFY AGING: BUILDING ON OUR PRELIMINARY DATA AND MODIFIABLE AGING FACTORS, WE WILL TEST THE EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERVENTIONS IN MODULATING AGE-RELATED CHANGES. THROUGH BOTH IN VITRO AND IN VIVO EXPERIMENTS, INCLUDING BEHAVIORAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANIPULATIONS, WE WILL VALIDATE CAUSAL RELATIONSHIPS AFFECTING AGING AND IDENTIFY POTENTIAL STRATEGIES TO MITIGATE AGE-RELATED DECLINE. BY INTEGRATING LONGITUDINAL, MULTI-TISSUE, ANALYSES WITH MOLECULAR AND ENVIRONMENTAL INVESTIGATIONS, THIS U19 RESEARCH PROGRAM WILL DEEPEN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE COMPLEX MECHANISMS UNDERLYING AGING. THE FINDINGS FROM THIS U19 HOLD PROMISE FOR IDENTIFYING ACTIONABLE STRATEGIES TO PROMOTE HEALTHY AGING AND IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES ACROSS THE LIFESPAN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CENTER FOR RATIONAL HCV VACCINE DESIGN & EVALUATION - OVERALL PROJECT SUMMARY HEPATITIS C VIRUS (HCV) INFECTS OVER 50 MILLION PEOPLE WORLDWIDE AND REMAINS A LEADING CAUSE OF LIVER CIRRHOSIS, HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA, AND AUTOIMMUNE DISORDERS. DESPITE CURATIVE ANTIVIRALS, REINFECTION AND ONGOING TRANSMISSION UNDERSCORE THE URGENT NEED FOR A PROPHYLACTIC VACCINE. EXTREME VIRAL GENETIC DIVERSITY HAS LONG IMPEDED HCV VACCINE DEVELOPMENT, DEMANDING APPROACHES THAT FOCUS IMMUNE RESPONSES ON CONSERVED VIRAL EPITOPES RECOGNIZED BY BROADLY NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES (BNABS) AND CROSS-REACTIVE T CELLS. THE U19 COOPERATIVE CENTER FOR RATIONAL HCV VACCINE DESIGN & EVALUATION AIMS TO DEVELOP INNOVATIVE AND CLINICALLY TRANSLATABLE VACCINE CANDIDATES CAPABLE OF ELICITING POTENT BNAB AND MULTIFUNCTIONAL T CELL RESPONSES. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT UNDERSTANDING AND OPTIMIZING THE PRESENTATION OF CONSERVED EPITOPES WILL ENABLE RATIONALLY DESIGNED VACCINES TO ELICIT STRONGER AND BROADER PROTECTION THAN FIRST-GENERATION E1E2- OR T CELL-BASED CANDIDATES. PROJECT 1 WILL DEFINE THE STRUCTURAL BASIS OF CONSERVED NEUTRALIZING EPITOPES AND DETERMINE THEIR PRESENTATION ON HCV VIRIONS, VIRUS-LIKE PARTICLES, AND VACCINE IMMUNOGENS USING X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY, CRYO-EM, AND CRYO-ET. THESE STUDIES WILL REVEAL THE ORGANIZATION OF E1E2 COMPLEXES AND HOW DECOY REGIONS SUCH AS HVR1 AFFECT EPITOPE EXPOSURE. PROJECT 2 WILL DESIGN AND EVALUATE OPTIMIZED IMMUNOGENS TARGETING THE E1E2 NEUTRALIZING FACE AND BRIDGING DOMAIN USING STRUCTURE-GUIDED ENGINEERING, CONFORMATION STABILIZATION, GLYCAN MODULATION, GERMLINE TARGETING, NANOPARTICLE AND NUCLEIC ACID LIPID NANOPARTICLE PLATFORMS. CANDIDATES WILL BE BENCHMARKED AGAINST CHIRON E1E2 IN MICE AND NONHUMAN PRIMATES TO IDENTIFY TOP DESIGNS FOR GMP TRANSLATION. THE VIROLOGY IMMUNOLOGY DATA CORE WILL STANDARDIZE REAGENTS, ASSAYS, AND DATA INTEGRATION FOR AI-ASSISTED IMMUNE ANALYSIS, WHILE THE ANIMAL MODEL CORE WILL PROVIDE HUMAN IMMUNOGLOBULIN KNOCK-IN (IG-KI) MICE AND RHESUS MODELS FOR VACCINE EVALUATION. THIS HIGHLY SYNERGISTIC CENTER WILL DEFINE HCV VULNERABILITY MECHANISMS AND DELIVER OPTIMIZED VACCINE PROTOTYPES READY FOR CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AICC - AI-POWERED COORDINATING CENTER FOR THE AITC PROGRAM ON AGING AND AD/ADRD RESEARCH - PROJECT SUMMARY ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (AD/ADRD) ARE COMPLEX AND PRESSING HEALTH CHALLENGES FOR AN AGING POPULATION. ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) HAS EMERGED AS A TRANSFORMATIVE TOOL TO ACCELERATE DISCOVERY, INTEGRATION, AND TRANSLATION ACROSS AD/ADRD RESEARCH. THE NIA’S ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND TECHNOLOGY COLLABORATORY (AITC) PROGRAM WAS LAUNCHED TO UNITE REGIONAL CENTERS ADVANCING AI FOR AGING AND DEMENTIA RESEARCH. OUR PROPOSED AI-POWERED AITC COORDINATING CENTER (AITCC) WILL SERVE AS THE NATIONAL HUB FOR THIS PROGRAM, EMBEDDING AI THROUGHOUT ADMINISTRATION, RESEARCH, COMMERCIALIZATION, AND STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT TO ENHANCE EFFICIENCY, TRANSPARENCY, AND IMPACT. SPECIFICALLY, AIM 1 (ADMINISTRATION) WILL ESTABLISH AN AI-ENHANCED COORDINATION INFRASTRUCTURE TO SUPPORT PROGRAM MANAGEMENT, COMMUNICATION, EVENT ORGANIZATION, AND CROSS-CONSORTIUM INTEGRATION. BY INTEGRATING AI AGENTS AND KNOWLEDGE GRAPHS, WE WILL STREAMLINE ADMINISTRATIVE WORKFLOWS, ENABLE INTELLIGENT INFORMATION/DATA SHARING, AND ORGANIZE CONSORTIUM-WIDE DIGITAL RESOURCES FOLLOWING FAIR PRINCIPLES. AIM 2 (COMMERCIALIZATION) WILL STRENGTHEN THE TRANSLATIONAL PIPELINE BY EXPANDING BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATORY AND SBIR PATHWAYS FOR AITC INNOVATIONS, ENSURING PROMISING DISCOVERIES MOVE MORE EFFICIENTLY FROM RESEARCH TO REAL-WORLD APPLICATION. AIM 3 (RESEARCH AND CONSULTING) WILL COLLABORATE WITH AITCS ON AWARD MANAGEMENT, INCLUDING SOLICITATION, CENTRALIZED REVIEW, AND PROGRESS TRACKING, LEVERAGING BOTH ESTABLISHED PLATFORMS AND ADVANCED AI ANALYTICS TO ENHANCE FAIRNESS, EFFICIENCY, AND DATA-DRIVEN DECISION-MAKING. AIM 4 (STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT) WILL ENSURE THAT AITC TECHNOLOGIES ARE ACCESSIBLE, ADOPTABLE, AND RESPONSIVE TO THE NEEDS OF OLDER ADULTS, CAREGIVERS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS THROUGH CONTINUOUS ENGAGEMENT, BEST-PRACTICE DEVELOPMENT, AND PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH STRATEGIES. TOGETHER, THESE FOUR AIMS WILL ESTABLISH A SCALABLE, AI- POWERED, TEAM-SCIENCE FRAMEWORK THAT UNITES THE NATIONAL AITC NETWORK, ACCELERATES DISCOVERY AND TRANSLATION, AND MAXIMIZES SOCIETAL BENEFIT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: VIRAL INFECTIONS IN THE YOUNG LUNG- THE VINYL CLINICAL CONSORTIUM- DATA ANALYTICS AND COORDINATING CENTER (DACC) - PROJECT SUMMARY VIRAL LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS (VLRTIS) ARE THE LEADING CAUSE OF HOSPITALIZATION AND DEATH IN INFANTS AND YOUNG CHILDREN. MOST CHILDREN RECOVER, BUT A SUBSTANTIAL SUBSET DEVELOP SEVERE ACUTE DISEASE AND LATER SEQUE- LAE - INCLUDING RECURRENT WHEEZE, ASTHMA, IMPAIRED LUNG GROWTH, SLEEP DISRUPTION, AND NEUROCOGNITIVE EFFECTS. THE BIOLOGICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL DRIVERS THAT SEPARATE RESILIENCE FROM VULNERABILITY REMAIN POORLY DEFINED. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT EARLY-LIFE IMMUNOLOGIC, MICROBIAL, ENVIRONMENTAL, AND SOCIAL EXPOSURES INTERACT TO ESTAB- LISH MOLECULAR PHENOTYPES THAT DETERMINE BOTH ACUTE SEVERITY AND LONG TERM RISK. THE SPIN VINYL (SYSTEMATIC PHENOTYPING AND ENDOTYPING IN VIRAL INFECTIONS IN THE YOUNG LUNG) CONSORTIUM WILL UNITE COORDINATED MULTICEN- TER ENROLLMENT AND DEEPLY HARMONIZED CLINICAL, EXPOSOMIC, AND MULTI-OMIC PROFILING TO UNCOVER MECHANISMS AND ENABLE PREDICTION. WE WILL BUILD A CONSORTIUM-WIDE COHORT OF 1,500 CHILDREN AGED 0–24 MONTHS HOSPITALIZED IN THE U.S. WITH VLRTI, WITH DEEP PHENOTYPING DURING HOSPITALIZATION AND LONGITUDINAL FOLLOW-UP THROUGH AT LEAST AGE 4–5 YEARS. THIS PLATFORM WILL DEFINE CLINICAL AND MOLECULAR ENDOTYPES OF ACUTE ILLNESS; QUANTIFY HOW HOST IMMUNE PROGRAMS, MICROBIAL COMMUNITIES, THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS AND ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES SHAPE RECOVERY TRA- JECTORIES; AND IDENTIFY PREDICTORS OF LONG-TERM PULMONARY, NEUROCOGNITIVE, SLEEP, AND FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES. WE WILL LEVERAGE CONTEMPORANEOUSLY ENROLLING CONTROL POPULATIONS FOR COMPARATIVE ANALYSES TO DETERMINE THE SPECIFIC IMPACT OF VLRTI ON PRIMARY STUDY OUTCOMES. DELIVERING ON THIS VISION REQUIRES DISCIPLINED LEADERSHIP AND COOR- DINATION SO THAT EACH COMPONENT PERFORMS OPTIMALLY AND CONTRIBUTES TO A COHERENT, HIGH IMPACT PROGRAM. THIS COORDINATION WILL BE LED BY THE DATA ANALYTICS AND COORDINATING CENTER (DACC). THE DACC WILL INCORPORATE THE COMBINED EXPERTISE OF THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH DATA COORDINATING CENTER (DCC) AND THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO DEPARTMENTS OF BIOMEDICAL INFORMATICS AND BIOSTATISTICS. THE DACC WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH THE CLINICAL COORDI- NATING CENTER AND ASSOCIATED SITES TO IMPLEMENT THE SPIN-VINYL CONSORTIUM BY ESTABLISHING THE INFRASTRUCTURE TO PERFORM DEEP PHENOTYPING OF CHILDREN WITH VIRAL INFECTIONS AND FOLLOW THEM LONGITUDINALLY (AIM 1); LEAD SPIN- VINYL DATA MANAGEMENT AND ANALYSES (AIM 2); AND BUILD AND SUSTAIN THE VINYLOME: A PUBLIC-FACING DATA, BIOSPECIMEN, AND IMAGING REPOSITORY (AIM 3). WITH OVER 20 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE IN THE DESIGN, IMPLEMENTATION, AND ANALYSIS OF PEDIATRIC CLINICAL STUDIES, THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH DCC AND EXPERTS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO ARE UNIQUELY QUALIFIED TO SUPPORT THE ACCOMPA- NYING UG3/UH3 APPLICATION AND TO SUCCESSFULLY IMPLEMENT THE SPIN VINYL STUDY. COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS WILL DELIVER (1) AN INTEGRATED NATIONAL NETWORK CAPABLE OF DEEP PHENOTYP- ING ACROSS DIVERSE PEDIATRIC POPULATIONS; (2) LONGITUDINAL ANALYSES LINKING MULTI-OMIC, CLINICAL, AND ENVIRONMENTAL DATA TO OUTCOMES; AND (3) A PUBLICLY AVAILABLE DATA RESOURCE THAT TRANSFORMS UNDERSTANDING AND MANAGEMENT OF EARLY-LIFE RESPIRATORY DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE SAFETY AND CLINICAL OUTCOMES OF PSYCHEDELIC USE (SCOPE) CENTER - PROJECT SUMMARY: SCOPE CENTER OVERALL PROPOSAL THE SAFETY AND CLINICAL OUTCOMES OF PSYCHEDELIC USE (SCOPE) P50 RESEARCH CENTER BUILDS A NATIONAL RESOURCE TO ADVANCE AND SHARE RESEARCH ON PSYCHEDELIC SAFETY AND HEALTH OUTCOMES IN REAL-WORLD SETTINGS. EARLY CLINICAL TRIALS SHOWED PROMISE FOR PSYCHEDELIC MEDICATIONS TO RELIEVE DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, PTSD, AND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS. MEDIA COVERAGE HELPED DRIVE PUBLIC OPINION TO APPROVE VOTER REFERENDA IN OREGON AND COLORADO, AND LEGISLATION IN NEW MEXICO ESTABLISHING LEGAL FRAMEWORKS FOR PSYCHEDELIC SERVICES. YET THE REAL-WORLD SAFETY AND OUTCOMES OF EXPANDING PSYCHEDELIC USE REMAIN UNKNOWN. THE SCOPE CENTER PROVIDES COORDINATED, MULTIFACETED TOOLS THAT SURPASS THE REACH OF INDIVIDUAL STUDIES. THE CENTER A) CONDUCTS INTEGRATED RESEARCH ON SAFETY AND HEALTH OUTCOMES OF STATE- REGULATED AND UNREGULATED USE (E.G., TRAJECTORIES OF USE, OUTCOMES ACROSS THE LIFE COURSE, AND POLICY IMPACTS), AND B) CREATES A NATIONAL REPOSITORY OF COORDINATED DATASETS WITH HARMONIZED MEASURES AND TOOLS ACCESSIBLE TO RESEARCHERS INSIDE AND OUTSIDE THE CENTER. THE SCOPE CENTER INTEGRATES THREE CORES (ADMINISTRATIVE CORE, RESEARCH-DATA CORE, PILOT-MENTORSHIP CORE) AND TWO ADVISORY BODIES. THE ADMINISTRATIVE CORE PROVIDES ORGANIZATIONAL AND FISCAL OVERSIGHT, CONSORTIUM COORDINATION, AND DISSEMINATION. THE RESEARCH-DATA CORE OFFERS METHODOLOGICAL GUIDANCE, HARMONIZED DATA COORDINATION, STATISTICAL SUPPORT, AND PILOT DATA. THE PILOT-MENTORSHIP CORE’S PILOT AWARDS TEST INNOVATIVE HYPOTHESES USING CENTER DATA SOURCES. THE CENTER’S NATIONAL SCIENTIFIC CONSORTIUM OF PSYCHEDELIC SCIENTISTS AND THE COMMUNITY ADVISORY COUNCIL OF PRACTITIONERS, FACILITATORS, AND STAKEHOLDERS GUIDE CENTER PRIORITIES AND ENSURE RELEVANCE. THESE STRUCTURES SUPPORT THREE SYNERGISTIC RESEARCH PROJECTS. THE OPEN PSYCHEDELIC EVALUATION NETWORK (OPEN; PROJECT 1) COMPARES SAFETY AND OUTCOMES OF CLIENTS IN STATE-REGULATED SERVICES WITH PEOPLE USING PSYCHEDELICS IN UNREGULATED SETTINGS. THE PSYCHEDELIC STUDY OF AGE GROUPS EXAMINING SUBJECT OUTCOMES STUDY (PSYCHSTAGES; PROJECT 2) EXAMINES OUTCOMES OF UNREGULATED USE ACROSS ADOLESCENTS/YOUNG ADULTS (15–24), ADULTS (18–49), AND OLDER ADULTS (≥50). THE SIMULATED PSILOCYBIN MODELS AND EMULATED TRIALS FOR CONSEQUENCES AND EFFECTIVENESS STUDY (SPACE; PROJECT 3) USES EMULATED TARGET TRIALS AND SIMULATION MODELS TO PREDICT HEALTH AND POLICY OUTCOMES. TOGETHER, THE RESEARCH PROJECTS GENERATE A MOSAIC OF REAL-WORLD DATA THAT A NATIONAL PSYCHEDELIC RESEARCH COMMUNITY CAN USE TO INFORM POLICY AND THE PUBLIC. THE SCOPE CENTER TRIANGULATES RESULTS ACROSS PROJECTS, CONVENES A NATIONAL COMMUNITY OF RESEARCHERS AND STAKEHOLDERS, AND DISSEMINATES FINDINGS WIDELY TO ENSURE THAT POLICY AND CLINICAL DECISIONS ABOUT PSYCHEDELIC SERVICES REST ON RIGOROUS, TRUSTWORTHY, REAL-WORLD EVIDENCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE NON INVASIVE POST POLYPOECTOMY SURVEILLANCE STUDY (NIPPSS) - PROJECT SUMMARY AFTER REMOVAL OF COLORECTAL POLYPS (POLYPECTOMY), SURVEILLANCE COLONOSCOPY, SUCH AS A THREE-YEAR FOLLOW-UP AFTER ADVANCED POLYP REMOVAL, IS ROUTINELY RECOMMENDED. HOWEVER, SURVEILLANCE COLONOSCOPY IS ASSOCIATED WITH SEVERAL CHALLENGES. THE STRATEGY IS EXPENSIVE, INVASIVE, AND ASSOCIATED WITH RARE BUT SIGNIFICANT RISKS. COLORECTAL CANCER (CRC) MAY OCCUR EARLY IN THE SURVEILLANCE WINDOW, BEFORE COLONOSCOPY IS DUE, LEADING TO DELAYED DIAGNOSIS. PARTICIPATION IN SURVEILLANCE COLONOSCOPY IS SUBOPTIMAL, AND AS LOW AS 21% FOR THOSE WITH ADVANCED POLYPS. A COMPLEMENTARY STRATEGY THAT IS BOTH MORE FREQUENT AND MORE ACCEPTABLE--MOST FEASIBLY DONE WITH NON-INVASIVE TESTS--IS REQUIRED TO MEET THESE CHALLENGES. ONE SUCH STRATEGY IS FECAL TESTING, SUCH AS WITH THE FECAL IMMUNOCHEMICAL TEST (FIT), WHICH IS RECOMMENDED ANNUALLY FOR AVERAGE RISK SCREENING. AVAILABLE EVIDENCE SUGGESTS A STRATEGY OF SURVEILLANCE FIT IS A PROMISING NEW SURVEILLANCE PARADIGM BUT REQUIRES FORMAL INVESTIGATION VIA PROSPECTIVE TRIALS. OUR OVERARCHING GOAL IS TO DEVELOP AND EVALUATE A NON- INVASIVE, EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGY FOR POST-POLYPECTOMY SURVEILLANCE THAT MAXIMIZES PARTICIPATION AND DETECTION WHILE MINIMIZING PATIENT BURDEN AND SYSTEM STRAIN. ACCORDINGLY, WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC AIMS ACROSS TWO PROJECT PHASES (UG3 PILOT AND UH3 PRAGMATIC RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL): (1) UG3 AIM 1: PILOT AND OPTIMIZE A SURVEILLANCE FIT STRATEGY TO INFORM THE UH3 TRIAL DESIGN. FINDINGS WILL INFORM FIT THRESHOLDS, PROJECTED NUMBER OF COLONOSCOPIES, FOLLOW-UP, SAMPLE SIZE, AND OTHER STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS, FOR THE FINAL UH3 PROTOCOL; (2) UG3 AIM 2: REFINE THE SURVEILLANCE FIT PROTOCOL USING PARTICIPANT AND CLINICIAN INPUT. INPUT WILL INCLUDE BARRIERS AND FACILITATORS TO PARTICIPATION AND APPROACH TO OPTIMIZING RECRUITMENT AND ADHERENCE TO INFORM THE FINAL UH3 TRIAL PROTOCOL; (3) UH3 AIM 1: COMPARE SURVEILLANCE FIT TO USUAL-CARE COLONOSCOPY FOR ADVANCED NEOPLASIA DETECTION AMONG PATIENTS WITH PRIOR ADVANCED POLYPS. WE WILL RANDOMIZE 2,422 PATIENTS 1:1 TO THREE-YEAR COLONOSCOPY VS. ANNUAL FIT WITH IMMEDIATE COLONOSCOPY FOR ABNORMAL RESULTS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT AN ANNUAL SURVEILLANCE FIT STRATEGY IS NON-INFERIOR TO USUAL CARE COLONOSCOPY SURVEILLANCE, WITH NO MORE THAN AN ABSOLUTE 3% DIFFERENCE IN ADVANCED NEOPLASIA DETECTION AT THREE YEARS (PRIMARY OUTCOME); (4) UH3 AIM 2: ASSESS ACCEPTABILITY, BARRIERS, AND FACILITATORS FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF SURVEILLANCE FIT.. WE WILL INTERVIEW PATIENTS, PRIMARY CARE CLINICIANS, GASTROENTEROLOGY SPECIALISTS, AND GUIDELINE EXPERTS ON BARRIERS, FACILITATORS, AND IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES FOR THE NOVEL SURVEILLANCE FIT PARADIGM. THE PROPOSED STUDY IS WELL POSITIONED TO TEST WHETHER A NON-INVASIVE STRATEGY FOR POST-POLYPECTOMY SURVEILLANCE, CAN BE USED AS AN ALTERNATIVE TO THE CURRENT INVASIVE SURVEILLANCE COLONOSCOPY PARADIGM, WHICH HAS NOT CHANGED IN OVER 30 YEARS, AND THEREBY IMPACT CLINICAL PRACTICE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTRAVENOUS CALCIUM TO PREVENT SEVERE OBSTETRICAL HEMORRHAGE AT CESAREAN DELIVERY - PROJECT SUMMARY POSTPARTUM HEMORRHAGE (PPH), EXCESSIVE BLEEDING AFTER CHILDBIRTH, IS THE LEADING DRIVER OF MATERNAL DEATH AND SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY. MOST PPH IS CAUSED BY UTERINE ATONY, I.E. INEFFECTIVE UTERINE CONTRACTION AFTER DELIVERY LEADING TO UNCONTROLLED BLEEDING FROM THE PLACENTAL BED. CURRENTLY AVAILABLE UTEROTONIC TREATMENTS USED TO PREVENT AND TREAT UTERINE ATONY (OXYTOCIN, METHYLERGONOVINE, CARBOPROST, AND MISOPROSTOL) HAVE LIMITATIONS INCLUDING VARIABLE EFFICACY, ADVERSE SIDE EFFECTS, HIGH COST, AND CONTRAINDICATIONS. THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR NOVEL EFFECTIVE, INEXPENSIVE, AND WIDELY ACCESSIBLE TREATMENTS FOR UTERINE ATONY. INTRAVENOUS CALCIUM CHLORIDE IS A PROMISING CANDIDATE UTEROTONIC. CALCIUM CHLORIDE IS SHELF-STABLE, INEXPENSIVE, AND ALREADY WIDELY AVAILABLE. CALCIUM IS ESSENTIAL FOR UTERINE CONTRACTION; ITS INFLUX FROM THE EXTRACELLULAR ENVIRONMENT IS REQUIRED FOR ACTIN-MYOSIN CROSSBRIDGE FORMATION AND CONTRACTION IN THE SMOOTH MUSCLE. RETROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES IN OBSTETRIC PATIENTS HAVE SHOWN THAT LOW IONIZED CALCIUM LEVELS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH SEVERE PPH IN A DOSE-RESPONSE MANNER. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES INCLUDE TWO RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS DEMONSTRATING THAT 1000 MG INTRAVENOUS CALCIUM CHLORIDE ADMINISTERED AT CESAREAN DELIVERY IS WELL TOLERATED AND ASSOCIATED WITH REDUCED BLOOD LOSS. WE PROPOSE A MULTICENTER RANDOMIZED, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED TRIAL CONDUCTED THROUGH THE EUNICE KENNEDY SHRIVER NICHD MATERNAL FETAL MEDICINE UNITS NETWORK TO DEFINITIVELY ESTABLISH WHETHER INTRAVENOUS CALCIUM CHLORIDE REDUCES SEVERE PPH DURING INTRAPARTUM CESAREAN DELIVERY. A TOTAL OF 2900 PARTICIPANTS WILL BE RANDOMLY ASSIGNED IN 1:1 RATIO TO RECEIVE CALCIUM CHLORIDE 1000 MG OR SALINE PLACEBO VIA A 10-MINUTE INTRAVENOUS INFUSION BEGINNING AT THE TIME OF UMBILICAL CORD CLAMPING. ALL OTHER CARE INCLUDING PROPHYLAXIS AND TREATMENT WITH OXYTOCIN AND SECOND LINE UTEROTONIC MEDICATIONS WILL BE PER USUAL CLINICAL PRACTICE. AIM 1: EVALUATE WHETHER INTRAVENOUS CALCIUM CHLORIDE REDUCES THE INCIDENCE OF SEVERE PPH, DEFINED AS TRANSFUSION, SURGICAL/RADIOLOGIC HEMORRHAGE CONTROL INTERVENTION, INTENSIVE CARE UNIT ADMISSION, OR DEATH. THE TRIAL HAS 85% POWER TO DETECT A 30% RELATIVE REDUCTION IN THE PRIMARY OUTCOME AMONG CALCIUM RECIPIENTS FROM AN ANTICIPATED 11% IN PLACEBO RECIPIENTS. AIM 2: ASSESS THE SAFETY AND TOLERABILITY OF INTRAVENOUS CALCIUM CHLORIDE INFUSION, INCLUDING SEVERE ADVERSE EVENTS (SAES), ADVERSE EVENTS (AES), AND CARDIOVASCULAR EFFECTS. WE WILL MONITOR THROMBOEMBOLISM, SEIZURE, AND ANY EXTRAVASATION INJURIES AS SAES OF SPECIAL INTEREST. WE HYPOTHESIZE NO INCREASE IN SAES OR AES AMONG CALCIUM RECIPIENTS. WE ANTICIPATE THAT CALCIUM RECIPIENTS WILL EXPERIENCE LESS TACHYCARDIA AND HYPOTENSION THAN PLACEBO RECIPIENTS DUE TO BENEFICIAL OFF-TARGET EFFECTS OF CALCIUM ON THE MYOCARDIUM AND VASCULAR SMOOTH MUSCLE. IF EFFECTIVE, INTRAVENOUS CALCIUM CHLORIDE COULD BECOME A TRANSFORMATIVE INTERVENTION FOR THE PREVENTION OF PPH— IMPROVING MATERNAL OUTCOMES IN BOTH HIGH- AND LOW-RESOURCE SETTINGS.

description: SYSTEMATIC PHENOTYPING AND ENDOTYPING IN VIRAL INFECTIONS IN THE YOUNG LUNG (SPIN VINYL) - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT VIRAL LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS (VLRTIS) ARE THE LEADING CAUSE OF HOSPITALIZATION IN INFANTS AND TODDLERS, MANY OF WHOM DEVELOP SEVERE ACUTE DISEASE AND/OR LATER SEQUELAE—INCLUDING RECURRENT WHEEZE, ASTHMA, IMPAIRED LUNG GROWTH, SLEEP DISRUPTION, AND NEUROCOGNITIVE EFFECTS. BIOLOGICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL DRIVERS THAT DISTINGUISH RESILIENCE FROM VULNERABILITY REMAIN POORLY DEFINED. THE SPIN VINYL (SYSTEMATIC PHENOTYPING AND ENDOTYPING IN VIRAL INFECTIONS IN THE YOUNG LUNG) CONSORTIUM WILL ESTABLISH A HARMONIZED, MULTI-CENTER U.S. COHORT OF 1500 CHILDREN AGED 0–24 MONTHS HOSPITALIZED WITH VLRTI (BRONCHIOLITIS, PNEUMONIA, PEDIATRIC ARDS) ACROSS NINE SITES, DEEPLY PHENOTYPE PARTICIPANTS DURING ADMISSION, AND FOLLOW OUTCOMES THROUGH AT LEAST AGE 4–5 YEARS. INTEGRATED CLINICAL TRAJECTORIES, LUNG FUNCTION PHYSIOLOGY, IMAGING, EXPOSOME, OBJECTIVE ACTIVITY/SLEEP MONITORING, AND MULTI-OMICS APPROACHES WILL DEFINE SEVERITY ENDOTYPES AND PROGNOSTIC SIGNATURES THAT EXPLAIN WHO BECOMES CRITICALLY ILL AND WHO DEVELOPS LATER MORBIDITY. DURING THE UG3 PHASE, THE STEERING COMMITTEE WILL APPROVE THE COMMON PROTOCOL, STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES, TRAINING, AND CENTRALIZED BIOSPECIMEN WORKFLOWS THROUGH A DEDICATED BIOREPOSITORY. IN THE UH3 IMPLEMENTATION PHASE, FIVE CLINICAL CENTERS (UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN [CLINICAL COORDINATING CENTER], CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL OF PHILADELPHIA, ARKANSAS CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL, UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO ANSCHUTZ, AND UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA SAN FRANCISCO) AND 4 SUBSITES (NATIONWIDE CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL, CHILDREN’S NATIONAL, JOHNS HOPKINS ALL CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL, AND TEXAS CHILDREN’S) IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE DATA AND ANALYTICS COORDINATING CENTER AT THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH WILL EXECUTE AIM 1: TO ESTABLISH A MULTICENTER LONGITUDINAL COHORT AND BIOREPOSITORY PURPOSE-BUILT FOR EARLY-LIFE VLRTI, WITH STRUCTURED LONG-TERM FOLLOW-UP. AIM 2 DEFINES HOST–PATHOGEN–MICROBIOME IMMUNE PROGRAMS USING PAIRED AIRWAY AND BLOOD METAGENOMICS, BULK/SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOMICS, PROTEOMICS, PHIP-SEQ SEROLOGY/AUTOANTIBODIES, AND SCTCR/BCR WITH INCITE-SEQ; MULTI-OMIC FACTOR ANALYSIS AND LONGITUDINAL MODELING LINK CELLULAR PROGRAMS TO OUTCOMES AND NOMINATE MODIFIABLE PATHWAYS. AIM 3 WILL IDENTIFY HOST AND MICROBIAL DETERMINANTS OF SHORT- AND LONG-TERM OUTCOMES AND TRAIN VALIDATED PROGNOSTIC CLASSIFIERS. INTEGRATED SIGNATURES WILL BE DISTILLED INTO PARSIMONIOUS, CLINICALLY DEPLOYABLE PROTEIN/TRANSCRIPT PANELS TO ENABLE PRECISION RISK STRATIFICATION AND GUIDE FUTURE THERAPEUTIC AND PREVENTIVE STRATEGIES. FOUR MECHANISTIC PROJECTS WILL 1) UNCOVER BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF CORTICOSTEROID RESPONSIVENESS, 2) DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF AIR POLLUTION ON RISK AND OUTCOMES OF VLRTI, 3) IDENTIFY THE MOLECULAR SUBPHENOTYPES UNDERLYING PRETERM INFANTS’ VULNERABILITY TO VLRTI, AND 4) DEFINE LINKS BETWEEN VLRTI-INDUCED ENDOTHELIAL INJURY AND MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION AND LONG- TERM OUTCOMES. SPIN VINYL WILL DELIVER MECHANISTIC INSIGHT AND ACTIONABLE BIOMARKERS TO REDUCE THE LIFELONG BURDEN OF PEDIATRIC RESPIRATORY DISEASE. DATA, IMAGES, AND BIOSPECIMENS WILL BE BROADLY SHARED THROUGH NHLBI-DESIGNATED REPOSITORIES AND A PUBLIC “VINYLOME” PORTAL TO ACCELERATE DISCOVERY AND TRANSLATION.
