description: DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION OF THE MOTOR THALAMUS TO IMPROVE OROFACIAL MOTOR AND SPEECH PRODUCTION DEFICITS AFTER STROKE - MORE THAN 5 MILLION PEOPLE IN THE US ALONE EXPERIENCED DIFFICULTY SPEAKING (DYSARTHRIA) AS A CONSE- QUENCE OF STROKE. CURRENTLY, DYSARTHRIA IS PALLIATED WITH BEHAVIORAL SPEECH THERAPY, BUT THE EFFICACY OF THESE METHODS RELIES ON PATIENT RETENTION, LEAVING SUBJECTS WITH MODERATE AND SEVERE DEFICITS UNABLE TO EFFECTIVELY COMMUNICATE, RESULTING IN GREATER ISOLATION, DEPRESSION, AND ACCELERATED DETERIORATION OF HEALTH. PROJECT GOAL: HERE WE AIM AT TESTING THE SAFETY, FEASIBILITY AND EARLY EFFICACY OF A SYSTEM DELIVERING ELECTRICAL STIMULATION TO THE MOTOR THALAMUS TO IMPROVE SPEECH INTELLIGIBILITY IN PEOPLE WITH CHRONIC POST-STROKE DYSARTHRIA. HYPOTHESIS: IN MOST CASES, DAMAGE TO THE CORTICO-SPINAL AND CORTICO-BULBAR TRACTS CONTROLLING SPEECH MOTOR FUNCTIONS ARE INCOMPLETE, BUT THE SPARED EXCITATORY DESCENDING INPUTS ARE INSUFFICIENT TO ACTIVATE THE MOTONEURONS, LEADING TO FUNCTIONAL MOTOR PARESIS AND SPEECH PRODUCTION DEFICITS. FACILITATION OF THE ACTIVATION OF THE RESIDUAL CONNECTIONS COULD REESTABLISH THE MISSING EXCITATION RESTORING SPEECH FUNCTIONS. HERE WE HYPOTHE- SIZE THAT DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION (DBS) OF THE MOTOR THALAMUS COULD INCREASE THE EXCITABILITY OF CORTICAL MOTOR NEURONS, THUS FACILITATING THE RESIDUAL CONNECTIONS AND, AS A CONSEQUENCE, ENHANCING SPEECH PRODUCTION. THESE EFFECTS WILL BE IMMEDIATE (ASSISTIVE EFFECTS) AND WILL LEAD TO SUPERIOR LONG-TERM RECOVERY WHEN COMBINED WITH SPEECH THERAPY. ADDITIONALLY, DELIVERY OF BURSTS OF STIMULATION AT SPEECH ONSET WOULD MAXIMIZE DBS EFFICACY. PRELIMINARY DATA: WE DEMONSTRATED THESE MECHANISMS OF ACTION OF MOTOR THALAMUS DBS IN NON-HUMAN PRI- MATES. WE THEN TESTED ASSISTIVE EFFECTS OF DBS OVER OROFACIAL MUSCLES AND SPEECH PRODUCTION IN A PATIENT WITH SEVERE SPEECH DEFICITS IN CONSEQUENCE OF A TRAUMATIC INJURY IN THE CORTICAL SPINAL TRACT (SUPRA-SPINAL SEGMENT) WHO WAS IMPLANTED WITH A MOTOR THALAMUS DBS SYSTEM. WE SHOWED THAT DBS OF THE MOTOR THALAMUS SUBSTANTIALLY IMPROVED OROFACIAL MUSCLE ACTIVATION, RANGE OF MOTION DURING FACIAL EXPRESSION AND SPEECH INTELLIGIBILITY. MOREO- VER, DBS DID NOT INDUCE PAIN OR DISCOMFORT AT INTENSITIES THAT WERE NECESSARY TO OBTAIN FUNCTIONAL IMPROVEMENTS. APPROACH: IN THE UG3 PHASE OF OUR PROPOSAL (YEAR 1) WE WILL OBTAIN FDA APPROVAL FOR AN IDE STUDY EXPLORING PRELIMINARY SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF LONG-TERM DBS TO IMPROVE SPEECH INTELLIGIBILITY IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC POST- STROKE DYSARTHRIA. IN THE UH3 (YEARS 2-5) WE WILL EXECUTE AN EARLY FEASIBILITY STUDY TESTING THE EFFICACY OF MOTOR THALAMUS DBS IN COMBINATION WITH 6 WEEKS OF SPEECH THERAPY TO INCREASE OROFACIAL MUSCLE STRENGTH, AMELIORATE SPEECH PRODUCTION, AND IMPROVE SPEECH INTELLIGIBILITY IN UP TO 10 SUBJECTS WITH CHRONIC POST-STROKE DYSARTHRIA. IN THE STUDY, PATIENTS WILL BE FOLLOWED UP FOR 1-YEAR TO MONITOR LONG-TERM SAFETY AND EARLY EFFICACY AND TO COMPARE CONTINUOUS STIMULATION AND TARGETED BURSTS AT SPEECH ONSET TO INFORM THE OPTIMAL PARAMETERS FOR FOLLOW UP TRIALS. PERSPECTIVE: OUR CLINICAL TRIAL WILL BE THE FIRST TO ASSESS THE SAFETY, FEASIBILITY AND EARLY EFFICACY OF NEUROSTIMULA- TION THERAPIES TARGETING THE MOTOR THALAMUS IN PATIENTS WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE DYSARTHRIA, POTENTIALLY LEADING TO A PARADIGM-SHIFT IN SPEECH REHABILITATION. 1

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TARGETED SUSTAINED DELIVERY OF IGF-1 FOR PERIPHERAL NERVE INJURIES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT PERIPHERAL NERVE INJURIES ARE A SIGNIFICANT AND SERIOUS ISSUE CAUSING PERMANENT DISABILITY, PAIN, AND REDUCED QUALITY OF LIFE. DESPITE ADVANCEMENTS IN SURGICAL TECHNIQUES FOR NERVE REPAIR, FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES REMAIN POOR AS THE SLOW RATE OF AXON REGENERATION LEADS TO THE PROGRESSIVE, IRREVERSIBLE ATROPHY OF DENERVATED MUSCLES AND SCHWANN CELLS. THERE ARE CURRENTLY NO FDA APPROVED THERAPEUTICS TO IMPROVE PERIPHERAL NERVE REGENERATION AND FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY. INSULIN-LIKE GROWTH FACTOR 1 (IGF-1) HAS THE POTENTIAL TO IMPROVE NERVE INJURY FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES IN A MULTIMODAL FASHION BY AUGMENTING AXONAL REGENERATION WHILE ALSO MAINTAINING MUSCLE AND SCHWANN CELL VIABILITY DURING LONG REGENERATION TIMES. HOWEVER, A MAJOR CHALLENGE IN ACHIEVING THERAPEUTIC DELIVERY IS THE PROTEIN’S SHORT HALF-LIFE. THEREFORE, WE HAVE DEVELOPED A LONG-ACTING INJECTABLE (LAI) TO ENCAPSULATE IGF-1 INTO BIODEGRADABLE NANOPARTICLES THAT ARE THEN EMBEDDED WITHIN A BIOCOMPATIBLE NANOFIBER HYDROGEL COMPOSITE TO PROVIDE SUSTAINED, LOCAL RELEASE OF IGF-1. OUR IGF-1 LAI DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEM HAS DEMONSTRATED SUSTAINED RELEASE OVER SIX WEEKS AND PRODUCED A ROBUST INCREASE OF 30% IN FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY IN SMALL ANIMAL AND NON-HUMAN PRIMATE NERVE INJURY MODELS. IN THE PROPOSED STUDIES, WE WILL BUILD UPON OUR ROBUST PRECLINICAL WORK TO BRING THE FIRST TRULY EFFECTIVE THERAPY FOR PERIPHERAL NERVE INJURIES TO PATIENTS. TO DO THIS, WE WILL FIRST ESTABLISH SMALL SCALE GLP TESTING AND CLINICAL SCALE CGMP MANUFACTURING. WE WILL THEN CONFIRM THE BIOCOMPATIBILITY, SAFETY, AND RELEASE PROFILE OF THE CGMP IGF-1 LAI DELIVERY SYSTEM THROUGH PRECLINICAL STUDIES IN ANIMAL MODELS. PHARMACOKINETIC, PHARMACODYNAMIC, AND TOXICOLOGY STUDIES WILL BE CONDUCTED TO ASSESS METABOLISM, SAFETY, AND POTENTIAL ADVERSE EFFECTS TO DEFINE OPTIMAL AND MAXIMAL TOLERATED DOSES AND INFORM CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN. UPON SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF PRECLINICAL STUDIES, WE WILL PREPARE AND SUBMIT AN INVESTIGATIONAL NEW DRUG (IND) APPLICATION AND INITIATE A PHASE I CLINICAL TRIAL FOR THE IGF-1 LAI DELIVERY SYSTEM. THE PHASE I CLINICAL TRIAL WILL EVALUATE THE SAFETY, TOLERABILITY, PHARMACOKINETICS, AND PRELIMINARY EFFICACY OF THE IGF-1 LAI IN ENHANCING FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY FOLLOWING PERIPHERAL NERVE INJURIES. FOLLOWING COMPLETION OF THE CLINICAL TRIAL, WE WILL SEEK TO OBTAIN BREAKTHROUGH THERAPY DESIGNATION FROM THE FDA TO EXPEDITE FURTHER DEVELOPMENT. OUR NOVEL BIOENGINEERED DELIVERY SYSTEM FOR IGF-1 PRESENTS NOT ONLY SIGNIFICANT POTENTIAL AS THE FIRST EFFICACIOUS THERAPEUTIC FOR PERIPHERAL NERVE INJURIES, BUT ALSO AS A BREAKTHROUGH DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEM THAT ENABLES CONTINUOUS AND PRECISE ADMINISTRATION OF SMALL PROTEIN THERAPEUTICS, SUCH AS GROWTH FACTORS, IN A MANNER THAT IS CLINICALLY PRACTICAL, SAFE, AND EFFICIENT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADVANCING HD THERAPEUTICS - PROJECT SUMMARY ABSTRACT  HUNTINGTON’S DISEASE (HD) IS AN INHERITED AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE. DESPITE ITS STRAIGHTFORWARD GENETIC BASIS, HD HAS A COMPLEX PATHOGENESIS. NO FDA APPROVED TREATMENT EXISTS. IT IS NOW RECOGNIZED THAT MULTIPLE PROCESSES INTERACT TO SHORTEN NEURONAL SURVIVAL IN THE NEOSTRIATUM, AND EVENTUALLY THROUGHOUT THE BRAIN. THREE PROCESSES CONTRIBUTE TO HD: THE INHERITANCE OF MORE THAN 35 CAG TRINUCLEOTIDE CAG REPEATS IN THE HUNTINGTIN GENE, SOMATIC EXPANSION OF THESE INHERITED REPEATS OVER TIME TO YIELD OVERT 180 CAG REPEATS IN SERIES, AND ABERRANT SPLICING OF THE MUTANT HUNTINGTIN GENE TO CREATE A SHORTENED, EXON 1 GENERATED PROTEIN THAT IS THOUGHT TO HAVE HIGH PATHOGENICITY. THIS PROPOSAL WILL EMPLOY AN INNOVATIVE APPLICATION OF RNA INTERFERENCE BY USING MULTIPLE SIMULTANEOUSLY DELIVERED SIRNAS, IN A SINGLE SCAFFOLD, TO BLOCK ALL THREE PROCESSES OF HD AND DEMONSTRATE SAFETY AND EFFECTIVENESS. THE SMALL INTERFERING RNAS HAVE A NEW STRUCTURE THAT WILL BE OPTIMIZED IN THE UG3 FORMAT AND THEN ORGANIZED TO APPLY TO THE FDA FOR EVENTUAL TREATMENT OF HD PATIENTS IN THE UH3. PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE SILENCING OF FULL-LENGTH MUTANT HUNTINGTIN TO SUBSTANTIALLY REDUCE THE PROTEIN IN THE BRAIN, INCLUDING THE NEOSTRIATUM; THE MISMATCH REPAIR PROTEIN MSH3, TO STOP THE SOMATIC EXPANSION OF CAG REPEATS IN THE HUNTINGTIN PROTEIN; AND MHTT1A, THE PUTATIVE TOXIC HUNTINGTIN EXON 1 PROTEIN OF MUTANT HUNTINGTIN, UNDER THE REGULATION OF POLYA IN INTRON 1. WE SHOW THAT SILENCING THESE PROTEINS IMPROVES THE MOLECULAR SIGNATURE FOUND IN HD MODEL MICE. THE THREE SIRNAS ARE DELIVERED IN A NOVEL TRIVALENT SIRNA, WITH LONG-TERM RNAI BIOACTIVITY OVER AT LEAST THREE MONTHS AND THE POTENTIAL TO STOP THE HD PATHOGENIC PROCESS. THE TRIVALENT DISTRIBUTES THROUGHOUT THE BRAIN, INCLUDING DEEP BRAIN STRUCTURES SUCH AS THE NEOSTRIATUM (SO FAR, MICE AND SHEEP). WE SHOW CMC (CHEMISTRY, MANUFACTURING, CONTROLS) SYNTHESIS OF THE NOVEL TRIVALENT SIRNA AND PRESENT SAFETY DATA ASSURING ITS GO-NO-GO QUALITY. WE WILL TEST THE TRIVALENT SIRNA IN HD MODEL MICE AND MINIPIG IN THE UG3 (RECOMMENDED BY THE FDA), AND IN NON-HUMAN PRIMATE IN THE UH3. THE GOAL IS TO PRESENT AN IND TO THE FDA FOR THE TREATMENT OF HD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CHRONOLOGIC PALLIDAL ADAPTIVE DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION FOR THE TREATMENT OF PARKINSON'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD) IS AN INCURABLE, PROGRESSIVE, DEGENERATIVE BRAIN DISORDER THAT RESULTS IN BRADYKINESIA, RIGIDITY, TREMOR, GAIT PROBLEMS, MOTOR FLUCTUATIONS AND DYSKINESIAS, SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCING PATIENTS’ QUALITY OF LIFE. PD IS LINKED TO CONTINUING FUNCTIONAL IMPAIRMENT AND A MULTITUDE OF NON-MOTOR SYMPTOMS INCLUDING APATHY, DEPRESSION, IMPAIRED COGNITION, MEDICATION-INDUCED IMPULSIVITY AND PSYCHOSIS, AND MANY SLEEP DISTURBANCES. PD ACCOUNTS FOR OVER $26 BILLION IN DIRECT, INDIRECT, AND NON-MEDICAL COSTS ANNUALLY. DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION (DBS) OF BASAL GANGLIA IS AN FDA-APPROVED THERAPY FOR MANAGING REFRACTORY SYMPTOMS IN PD. HOWEVER, DUE TO DISEASE PROGRESSION, SYMPTOMS IN PD FLUCTUATE THROUGHOUT THE DAY WITH INCONSISTENT RESPONSE TO MEDICATIONS OVERTIME, AND THUS, A SYSTEM THAT CAN DETECT NEURAL INDICATORS OF MOTOR SYMPTOMS AND SLEEP STAGES WHILE ADAPTING THE STIMULATION AMPLITUDE CAN PERSONALIZE AND POTENTIALLY IMPROVE THERAPY. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS EARLY SAFETY AND FEASIBILITY STUDY IS TO PROVIDE PRELIMINARY DATA ON THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF ADAPTIVE DBS THERAPY [ADBS], USING A NOVEL INVESTIGATIONAL NEUROSTIMULATOR, THE NEWRONIKA ALPHADBS. IN AIM 1, THE DESIGN, VALIDATION, AND REGULATORY APPROVALS FOR THE INVESTIGATIONAL MEDICAL DEVICE WILL BE FINALIZED. IN AIM 2, WE WILL IDENTIFY PALLIDAL NEURO-INDICATORS OF PARKINSONIAN MOTOR SYMPTOMS AND SLEEP. IN AIM 3, WE WILL IMPLEMENT A SLEEP-AWARE PALLIDAL ADBS IN A SHORT DOUBLE-BLINDED CROSSOVER STUDY TO ESTABLISH THE SAFETY AND FEASIBILITY OF THE ALPHDBS. WE EXPECT THIS STUDY TO LEAD THE WAY FOR FUTURE ADBS SYSTEMS DESIGNED FOR THE MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING AND TREATMENT OF OTHER INDICATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: VALIDATION OF A LIQUID BIOPSY ASSAY FOR EARLY DETECTION OF LYMPHOMA IN PEOPLE WITH HIV - ABSTRACT THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO VALIDATE A LIQUID BIOPSY ASSAY TO ENABLE EFFECTIVE SCREENING OF NON-HODGKIN’S LYMPHOMA (NHL) IN PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV (PWH), A POPULATION THAT EXPERIENCES A SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER INCIDENCE OF NHL, ALONG WITH A NOTABLY POORER PROGNOSIS DUE TO LATE-STAGE DIAGNOSES. DESPITE IMPROVEMENTS IN THE OVERALL SURVIVAL OF PWH DUE TO COMBINATION ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY, NHL REMAINS A LEADING CAUSE OF CANCER-RELATED DEATH WITHIN THIS GROUP, AND THE MAJORITY OF CASES ARE DIAGNOSED AT ADVANCED STAGES WITH AGGRESSIVE PHENOTYPES AND EXTRA- NODAL INVOLVEMENT. EARLY DETECTION OF NHL IS CRUCIAL TO IMPROVING CLINICAL OUTCOMES IN PWH, YET THERE CURRENTLY EXISTS NO EFFECTIVE SCREENING PARADIGM IN THIS ELEVATED-RISK POPULATION. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, THE PROJECT FOCUSES ON VALIDATING A NOVEL LIQUID BIOPSY ASSAY, HIGH DENSITY METHYL-SEQ, WHICH DETECTS GLOBAL GENE SILENCING PATTERNS ASSOCIATED WITH NHL THROUGH PROMOTER METHYLATION EVENTS IN CIRCULATING CELL-FREE DNA. THIS TECHNOLOGY HAS SHOWN COMPELLING RESULTS IN PRELIMINARY STUDIES, DETECTING NHL-SPECIFIC METHYLATION SIGNALS UP TO ONE YEAR BEFORE DIAGNOSIS IN INDIVIDUALS WITH HIV. USING A UNIQUE COLLECTION OF PRE-DIAGNOSIS PLASMA SAMPLES FROM THE NIH- SPONSORED MACS/WIHS COMBINED COHORT STUDY, THIS PROJECT WILL CONDUCT BOTH ANALYTICAL AND CLINICAL VALIDATION OF THE ASSAY, ENSURING THAT IT MEETS THE RIGOROUS STANDARDS NECESSARY FOR CLINICAL ADOPTION. BY CONFIRMING THE ASSAY’S SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY FOR DETECTING NHL BEFORE SYMPTOMATIC PRESENTATION, THE PROJECT AIMS TO ESTABLISH AN EFFECTIVE SCREENING TOOL FOR NHL IN PWH, WITH THE POTENTIAL TO SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE EARLY DIAGNOSIS, TREATMENT, AND SURVIVAL OUTCOMES FOR THIS VULNERABLE POPULATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TRANSCRIPTOMIC MOLECULAR RISK CLASSIFICATION FOR CHILDREN WITH B CELL ACUTE LYMPHOBLASTIC LEUKEMIA - PROJECT SUMMARY A PRIMARY GOAL IN THE TREATMENT OF B-CELL ACUTE LYMPHOBLASTIC LEUKEMIA (B-ALL) IS PRECISE AND ACCURATE ASSESSMENT OF RELAPSE RISK TO ALLOCATE THERAPY APPROPRIATELY TO PREVENT RELAPSE IN PATIENTS AT HIGHEST RISK WHILE MINIMIZING TREATMENT-RELATED MORBIDITY IN PATIENTS AT LOWEST RISK OF RELAPSE. IN THE CHILDREN’S ONCOLOGY GROUP (COG), CURRENT RISK STRATIFICATION IDENTIFIES LIMITED PROGNOSTIC GENETIC BIOMARKERS THROUGH A MULTIMODAL TESTING STRATEGY THAT IS RESOURCE-INTENSIVE, REQUIRES MULTIPLE SAMPLES FROM EACH PATIENT, AND USES DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS THAT CANNOT DETECT MANY GENOMIC LESIONS (PAX5, IKZF1) THAT CARRY PROGNOSTIC RELEVANCE NOR PROGNOSTIC TRANSCRIPTOMIC SIGNATURES (ETV6::RUNX1-LIKE, KMT2A-LIKE, AND ZNF384-LIKE). THUS, OUR CURRENT RISK STRATIFICATION APPROACH IS INSUFFICIENT TO APPROPRIATELY ASSIGN RISK-STRATIFIED THERAPY. RECENT RETROSPECTIVE STUDIES HAVE SHOWN THAT RNA SEQUENCING (RNASEQ) AS A STAND-ALONE TEST ALLOWS DETECTION OF PROGNOSTIC MOLECULAR B-ALL SUBTYPES AND IDENTIFICATION OF ONCOGENIC DRIVERS INCLUDING GENE FUSIONS, SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE VARIANTS (SNVS), AND COPY NUMBER ABNORMALITIES (CNAS). THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IMPLEMENT EXOME CAPTURE-BASED RNASEQ FOR REAL-TIME CLINICAL USE IN RISK STRATIFICATION IN THE NEXT GENERATION OF NCTN-SUPPORTED COG CLINICAL TRIALS FOR PATIENTS WITH B-ALL. WE WILL ESTABLISH CENTRALIZED DIAGNOSTIC RNASEQ-BASED MOLECULAR CLASSIFICATION ACROSS THREE CLIA/CAP-CERTIFIED LABORATORIES WHICH WILL SERVE AS COG REFERENCE TESTING SITES. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT RNASEQ WILL ACCURATELY AND EFFICIENTLY DEFINE PROGNOSTICALLY RELEVANT MOLECULAR B-ALL SUBSETS AND, WHEN INTEGRATED WITH CURRENT CLINICAL GENOMIC TESTING, WILL ENHANCE RISK STRATIFICATION. WE WILL TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS WITH SPECIFIC AIMS FOCUSED ON DEFINING THE ANALYTICAL PERFORMANCE OF THE RNASEQ ASSAY AND HARMONIZING IT ACROSS REFERENCE LABORATORIES (AIM 1, UH2 PHASE); AND PERFORMING CLINICAL VALIDATION THROUGH CENTRALIZED MOLECULAR CLASSIFICATION FOR PATIENTS ENROLLED ON A CLINICAL TRIAL (AIM 2, UH3 PHASE). IN AIM 1, THE THREE REFERENCE LABORATORIES WILL PERFORM RNASEQ ON A PANEL OF 104 CAREFULLY SELECTED CASES WHERE EACH SAMPLE IS ALIQUOTED AND PROCESSED INDEPENDENTLY IN THE THREE LABORATORIES TO ASSESS ANALYTICAL PERFORMANCE FOR TRANSCRIPTOMIC CLASSIFICATION AND FUSION DETECTION. IN AIM 2, BANKED SPECIMENS FROM 300 PATIENTS ENROLLED AND TREATED ON THE CURRENTLY ACCRUING NCTN/COG AALL1732 TRIAL WILL BE SELECTED BASED ON DEMOGRAPHIC, CLINICAL, AND MOLECULAR FEATURES AS WELL AS RESPONSE AND OUTCOMES AND WILL BE SENT TO THE THREE REFERENCE LABORATORIES FOR END-TO-END TESTING AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC CLASSIFICATION TO VALIDATE OUR CENTRALIZED RNASEQ PLATFORM. WE WILL COMBINE THESE DATA WITH CLINICALLY AVAILABLE GENOMIC TESTING TO PROVIDE INTEGRATED RISK STRATIFICATION AS INTENDED FOR REAL-WORLD USE. THE NCTN AND COG HAVE CONSISTENTLY ESTABLISHED THE CLINICAL STANDARD FOR THE DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT OF CHILDHOOD ALL. THE RESULTS OF THIS WORK WILL NOT ONLY IMPROVE RISK STRATIFICATION FOR PATIENTS ON CLINICAL TRIALS BUT WILL ESTABLISH A NEW GOLD STANDARD FOR THE MOLECULAR CHARACTERIZATION OF ALL CHILDREN WITH B-ALL IN THE UNITED STATES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ANALYTIC AND CLINICAL VALIDATION OF A 7-PLEX MIF ASSAY FOR PREDICTIVE RESPONSE OF ADVANCED NSCLC TO ANTI-PD-1 BASED THERAPY - PROJECT SUMMARY  PD-L1 MEMBRANOUS (CELL SURFACE) EXPRESSION IN PRETREATMENT BIOPSIES IS THE MOST COMMONLY USED CORRELATE OF THE LIKELIHOOD OF RESPONSE TO ANTI-PD-1 THERAPY. THE GENERAL FINDING OF AN ASSOCIATION OF PD-L1 EXPRESSION WITH TUMOR RESPONSE TO ANTI-PD-1 THERAPY HAS BEEN SUBSTANTIATED ACROSS TENS OF THOUSANDS OF PATIENTS WITH NUMEROUS TUMOR TYPES TREATED WITH ANTI- PD-(L)1. HOWEVER, WHILE PD-L1 EXPRESSION ENRICHES FOR RESPONSE TO ANTI-PD-(L)1, IT IS NOT SUFFICIENT. ADDITIONALLY, WHILE PATHOLOGISTS DEMONSTRATE GOOD REPRODUCIBILITY FOR SCORING TUMOR CELL (TC) PD-L1 EXPRESSION BY CHROMOGENIC IHC AND LIGHT MICROSCOPY, THEY HAVE POOR REPRODUCIBILITY FOR SCORING PD-L1 EXPRESSION ON IMMUNE CELLS (IC).  OTHER RELATED FEATURES WHICH HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO IMPROVE ON THE PD-L1 BIOMARKER INCLUDE THE PROXIMITY OF PD-1 TO PD-L1, THE DENSITY OF CD8+FOXP3+ CELLS, AND CD68 AND TUMOR MARKER IMMUNOSTAINS, THE LATTER OF WHICH HELP IDENTIFY CO-EXPRESSION OF PD-L1 ON ICS AND TCS, RESPECTIVELY. A QUANTITATIVE MULTIPLEX IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE ASSAY WHICH CAPTURES ALL OF THESE FEATURES HAS BEEN DEVELOPED AND INCLUDES PD-L1, PD-1, CD8, FOXP3, CD68, A TUMOR MARKER (CYTOKERATIN AE1/3 FOR NON-SMALL CELL LUNG CARCINOMA, NSCLC), A PAN-MEMBRANE MARKER AND DAPI. THROUGH THIS ASSAY, IT IS POSSIBLE TO ENUMERATE KEY CELLULAR SUBSETS AND THEIR CO-EXPRESSION PROFILES. IT IS ALSO POSSIBLE TO INCLUDE SPATIAL PARAMETERS, INCLUDING THE DISTANCE BETWEEN PD-1 AND PD-L1, WHICH HAVE NOT PREVIOUSLY BEEN INCLUDED IN PREDICTIVE OR PROGNOSTIC SURGICAL PATHOLOGY SPECIMEN-BASED ASSAYS. THIS MIF ASSAY HAS INCREASED SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY FOR RESPONSE TO ANTI-PD1 THERAPY WHEN COMPARED TO THE ASSESSMENT OF PD-L1 EXPRESSION ALONE IN MULTIPLE TUMOR TYPES, INCLUDING MELANOMA, NSCLC, AND MERKEL CELL CARCINOMA, AMONGST OTHERS.  THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO PERFORM INTER-SITE VALIDATION OF THE MIF STAINING ASSAY AND ASSOCIATED LOCK-DOWN ALGORITHM AMONGST FOUR MAJOR ACADEMIC SITES (JOHNS HOPKINS, MD ANDERSON, YALE UNIVERSITY, AND PROVIDENCE PORTLAND MEDICAL CENTER). FOLLOWING ANALYTICAL VALIDATION, DISCOVERY AND VALIDATION COHORTS FROM 250 PATIENTS WITH ADVANCED NSCLC WILL BE USED TO ESTABLISH FINAL ASSAY PARAMETERS (INCLUDING THRESHOLDS), LINKED TO CLINICAL OUTCOMES FOLLOWING ANTI-PD-1-BASED THERAPY. THE DELIVERABLE OF THE STUDY IS A REFINED, MULTIPLEX BIOMARKER ASSAY FOR RESPONSE/RESISTANCE TO ANTI-PD-1 THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED ACROSS MULTIPLE ACADEMIC SITES. THE RESULT WILL BE A MULTIPLEX IF ASSAY THAT IS SUITABLY STAGED FOR ADVANCED DEVELOPMENT AIMED AT CLINICAL IMPLEMENTATION. WHILE NSCLC IS THE FOCUS OF THE CURRENT GRANT PROPOSAL, PRELIMINARY RESULTS SUGGEST THAT THIS ASSAY WILL ALSO HAVE GREAT VALUE IN NUMEROUS OTHER SOLID TUMOR TYPES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A NOVEL IMMUNOLOGICAL-DIRECTED PROBIOTIC FOR THE TREATMENT OF SJÖGREN’S SYNDROME - PROJECT SUMMARY OUR GOAL IS TO DEVELOP A NOVEL, IMMUNOLOGICAL-DIRECTED L. LACTIS PROBIOTIC-BASED THERAPEUTIC FOR THE TREATMENT OF SJÖGREN’S SYNDROME (SS). SS IS A PROGRESSIVE, CHRONIC AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE CHARACTERIZED BY INFLAMMATORY CELL INFILTRATION OF THE SALIVARY AND LACRIMAL GLANDS, RESULTING IN ACINAR EPITHELIAL CELL ATROPHY, CELL DEATH, AND LOSS OF EXOCRINE FUNCTION1-6. AT LEAST HALF OF SS PATIENTS DEVELOP EXTRAGLANDULAR INFLAMMATORY DISEASE AND HAVE A WIDE RANGE OF SYSTEMIC CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS THAT CAN AFFECT ANY ORGAN SYSTEM, INCLUDING CONNECTIVE TISSUE, AND 5- 10% OF PATIENTS DEVELOP LIFE-THREATENING LYMPHOMA7, 8. SS IS A DEBILITATING DISEASE AFFECTING AS MANY AS 3.1 MILLION INDIVIDUALS IN THE U.S.9, 10, WITH WOMEN BEING AT LEAST NINE TIMES MORE LIKELY TO BE AFFLICTED WITH SS THAN MEN5, 10, 11. TREATMENT OF SS REMAINS A SIGNIFICANT UNMET MEDICAL NEED. CURRENT TREATMENT RELIES ON REPLACEMENT THERAPIES SUCH AS ARTIFICIAL SALIVA AND EYE LUBRICANTS OR IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE AGENTS12, 13. WHILE WE UNDERSTAND THAT TREGS ARE IMPORTANT IN CONTROLLING SS 14-16, MULTIPLE ANTIGENS INVOLVED IN THIS DISEASE PROCESS (I.E., Α-FODRIN17-20, RIBONUCLEAR PROTEIN RO/SSA17, 21, 22, LA/SSB17, 21, 22, AND M3R22-24) MAKE ORAL TOLERANCE APPROACHES PROBLEMATIC. THUS, THE CAPACITY TO STIMULATE REGULATORY CELLS INDEPENDENT OF KNOWING THE ANTIGEN SPECIFICITY FOR THE DISEASE POSES AS AN ATTRACTIVE THERAPEUTIC APPROACH. ORIGINALLY CONCEIVED AS A HUMAN DIARRHEAL VACCINE, WE FOUND THAT COLONIZATION FACTOR ANTIGEN I (CFA/I) FROM HUMAN ENTEROTOXIGENIC E. COLI (ETEC) IS EFFECTIVE AT INDUCING AUTO-AG-SPECIFIC T REGULATORY CELLS WHEN ADMINISTERED ORALLY VIA A L. LACTIS BACTERIAL DELIVERY SYSTEM25-27, 28. TO AVOID CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH PRODUCING LARGE QUANTITIES OF CFA/I PROTEIN AND IMPROVE THE MUCOSAL PHARMACOKINETIC (PK) AND PHARMACODYNAMIC (PD) PROPERTIES OF CFA/I FOLLOWING ORAL ADMINISTRATION, WE DEVELOPED AN L. LACTIS-CFA/I EXPRESSING PRODUCT (REFERRED TO AS R-2487) AND VALIDATED ITS EFFICACY IN MULTIPLE AUTOIMMUNE MODELS. INDEED, R-2487 WAS EFFECTIVE AT REDUCING CLINICAL SYMPTOMS IN A SS ANIMAL MODEL29, 30, ALONG WITH EXPERIMENTAL MODELS OF RA, DIABETES, AND MS31-36. PRIOR SBIR AND SEED INVESTMENT FUNDING HAS ENABLED US TO EFFECTIVELY ADVANCE R-2487 TO BE POISED FOR CLINICAL TESTING. AS PART OF THESE EFFORTS, WE HELD AN FDA PRE-IND MEETING TO FINALIZE OUR IND-ENABLING PLANS AND ALIGN OUR CMC/MANUFACTURING STRATEGY WITH FDA PERSPECTIVES. THIS UG3/UH3 APPLICATION IS FOCUSED ON OBTAINING HUMAN VALIDATION FOR R-2487 BY COMPLETING A PHASE 1 SS PROOF-OF-CONCEPT CLINICAL TRIAL. THE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE: 1) ESTABLISH A SUCCESS-DRIVEN BIOMETRICS PLAN TO SUPPORT THE CLINICAL TRIAL, 2) PREPARE CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION AND FILE AN IND WITH THE FDA, 3) ESTABLISH R-2487 CLINICAL SAFETY, 4) EVALUATE R-2487 ACTIVITY AND CLINICAL BENEFIT IN SS, AND 5) CLOSE OUT THE PHASE 1 CLINICAL TRIAL TO SUPPORT FUTURE CLINICAL ENDEAVORS. SUCCESSFUL COMMERCIALIZATION OF R-2487 WILL PROVIDE A PROFOUND MEDICAL ADVANCEMENT FOR TREATING SS.

description: A TRANSFORMATIVE METHOD FOR FUNCTIONAL BRAIN IMAGING WITH SPECKLE CONTRAST OPTICAL SPECTROSCOPY - ABSTRACT ADVANCES IN NON-INVASIVE MONITORING OF HUMAN BRAIN FUNCTION UNDER NORMAL AND PATHOLOGICAL CONDITIONS WILL LEAD TO BREAKTHROUGHS IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE BRAIN IN HEALTH AND DISEASE, AND LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF DEVICES AVAILABLE FOR EVERYDAY USE, WITH APPLICATIONS SUCH AS MONITORING PATIENTS WITH BRAIN INJURIES OR NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE, STUDIES OF BRAIN FUNCTION IN NATURAL ENVIRONMENTS, AND BRAIN-COMPUTER INTERFACES. AMONG THE VARIOUS BRAIN IMAGING TECHNIQUES, FUNCTIONAL NEAR INFRARED SPECTROSCOPY (FNIRS) IS AN OPTICAL METHOD THAT IMAGES THE HEMODYNAMIC RESPONSE TO BRAIN ACTIVATION BY MEASURING THE OXY-(HBO) AND DEOXY-(HBR) HEMOGLOBIN CONCENTRATION CHANGES DUE TO BRAIN ACTIVATION. IT IS ESPECIALLY USEFUL FOR POPULATIONS AND FOR STUDIES FOR WHICH OTHER IMAGING MODALITIES ARE LIMITED, E.G. FUNCTIONAL MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (FMRI), INCLUDING FOR CHILDREN, INFANTS, AND STUDIES THAT INVOLVE MOTION AND INTERACTIONS OR REQUIRE HIGH TEMPORAL RESOLUTION. HOWEVER, FNIRS BRAIN SENSITIVITY IN ADULT HUMANS IS TYPICALLY AROUND 10%, AND FNIRS ALONE DOES NOT PROVIDE QUANTITATIVE INFORMATION ABOUT ALL THE HEMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS AS IT DOES NOT MEASURE CHANGES IN CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW (CBF). HERE, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A FIBER-BASED SPECKLE CONTRAST OPTICAL SPECTROSCOPY (SCOS) SYSTEM TO MEASURE CBF VARIATIONS DUE TO BRAIN ACTIVATION IN HUMANS. SCOS USES RELATIVELY LOW-COST COMPLEMENTARY METAL–OXIDE– SEMICONDUCTOR (CMOS) CAMERAS AS DETECTORS. THE PERFORMANCE OF SCOS CAN SURPASS THAT OF EXISTING OPTICAL SYSTEMS FOR HUMAN MEASUREMENTS OF CBF IN TERMS OF CONTRAST TO NOISE RATIO (CNR) BY AT LEAST ONE ORDER OF MAGNITUDE WITH EQUAL OR LESS COST. THE COMBINED SCOS-FNIRS SYSTEM DEVELOPED IN THE UG3 PHASE WILL PROVIDE MEASUREMENTS OF ALL THE HEMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS ASSOCIATED WITH BRAIN ACTIVATION, ACHIEVE AN UP TO 3X IMPROVEMENT IN BRAIN SENSITIVITY COMPARED WITH FNIRS ALONE, AND PERMIT ESTIMATION OF EVOKED CHANGES IN CMRO2. THE HIGH-DENSITY SCOS-FNIRS SYSTEM DEVELOPED IN THE UH3 PHASE WILL PROVIDE IMAGES OF ALL THE HEMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS WITH HIGH SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL RESOLUTION. THIS WORK WILL RESULT IN A NEW APPROACH FOR FUNCTIONAL BRAIN IMAGING AND DEMONSTRATIVE RESULTS THAT WILL MOTIVATE ADOPTION BY OTHERS AND FUTURE ADVANCEMENTS TOWARDS WEARABLE DEVICES AT A REDUCED COST.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT OF ANGIOTENSIN AT2 INHIBITORS FOR NEUROPATHIC PAIN RELIEF - PROJECT SUMMARY NEUROPATHIC CHRONIC PAIN AFFECTS ~20 MILLION AMERICANS AND BEARS MORE THAN US$500 BILLION BURDEN ON THE US ECONOMY. MOREOVER, THE WIDESPREAD USE OF ADDICTIVE OPIOID PAINKILLERS FOR CHRONIC PAIN IS THE MAJOR ROOT OF THE OPIOID ABUSE EPIDEMIC THREATENING THE WHOLE SOCIETY. AS ONLY ONE IN FOUR PATIENTS WITH NEUROPATHIC PAIN EXPERIENCES PAIN RELIEF WITH THE CURRENT TREATMENT OPTIONS, THE DISCOVERY OF NEW APPROACHES TO TREATING NEUROPATHIC PAIN IS AN UNMET MEDICAL NEED WITH A MAJOR IMPACT ON SOCIETY. TARGETING PAIN IN PERIPHERAL NERVES IS A KEY PARADIGM FOR EFFECTIVE AND SAFE ANALGESIA, WHICH CAN NATURALLY BYPASS THE CNS-MEDIATED SIDE EFFECTS AND ADDICTION. ONE OF THE MOST PROMISING AND ADVANCED PERIPHERAL TARGETS, ANGIOTENSIN AT2 RECEPTOR IS INVOLVED IN REGULATIONS OF NEURONAL MEMBRANE EXCITABILITY AND NEURITE OUTGROWTH OF PERIPHERAL SENSORY NEURONS. INHIBITION OF AT2R IN PNS HAS SHOWN EFFECT IN PRECLINICAL MODELS OF NEUROPATHIC PAIN, AS WELL AS IN PHASE II CLINICAL TRIALS, WHERE THE EMA401 DRUG CANDIDATE DEMONSTRATED ANALGESIA IN PATIENTS WITH POST-HERPETIC NEURALGIA AND DIABETIC NEUROPATHY. HOWEVER, EMA401, WHICH HAD MODEST POTENCY AND SUBOPTIMAL DRUG-LIKE PROPERTIES, WAS TERMINATED IN MAY 2019 DUE TO OFF-TARGET HEPATOTOXICITY AT HIGH THERAPEUTIC DOSES. THE LACK OF SUITABLE CANDIDATES IN THE PIPELINE STRONGLY DIFFERENTIATED FROM EMA401 CALLS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW HIGHLY POTENT AND SAFE AT2R ANTAGONISTS FOR NEUROPATHIC PAIN. WE HAVE ESTABLISHED A STRUCTURE-BASED DRUG DISCOVERY PLATFORM AND USED IT TO IDENTIFY AND OPTIMIZE A NOVEL LEAD SERIES OF AT2R ANTAGONISTS, HIGHLY EFFICIENT IN TWO MURINE MODELS ON NEUROPATHIC PAIN. OUR BEST LEAD SERIES COMPOUND SHOWED BETTER POTENCY AND IN VIVO EFFICACY THAN EMA401, AS WELL AS BETTER ADMET AND PK PROFILES, IN MOUSE, RAT AND DOG WITH MINIMAL LIVER ACCUMULATION. HERE, WE PROPOSE ADDITIONAL OPTIMIZATION OF THE LEAD ANALOGS FOCUSING ON ELIMINATING A PLATELET DEPLETION SIDE EFFECT - THE LAST REMAINING LIABILITY OF OUR CURRENT CANDIDATE. OUR PRELIMINARY RESULTS HAVE IDENTIFIED A FIRST BACKUP COMPOUND THAT MAINTAINS HIGH EFFICACY WITHOUT SIGNIFICANT PLATELET DEPLETION, SHOWING THE FEASIBILITY OF SEPARATING THE THERAPEUTIC FROM THE SIDE EFFECT. AT THE UG3 STAGE, WE WILL EMPLOY MEDICINAL CHEMISTRY OPTIMIZATION OF THE LEAD ANALOGS, COUPLED WITH THE PREVIOUSLY ESTABLISHED SCREENING FUNNEL AND VALIDATED MURINE PLATELET COUNTING ASSAYS TO IDENTIFY THE BEST NEW CANDIDATE FOR PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT. AT THE UH3 STAGE, WE WILL CONTINUE PRECLINICAL STUDIES, IND SUBMISSION, AND PHASE 1 CLINICAL STUDIES TOWARD THE CHARACTERIZATION OF THIS NOVEL SAFE AND EFFECTIVE NEUROPATHIC PAIN TREATMENT.

description: KENTUCKY CENTER FOR CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE - KENTUCKY CENTER FOR CLINICAL & TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE PROJECT SUMMARY THE KENTUCKY CENTER FOR CLINICAL & TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE (CCTS) AT THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY (UK) IS THE CTSA HUB IN THE COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY. THE CCTS IS NATIONALLY KNOWN FOR EXCELLENCE IN ITS CLINICAL RESEARCH UNIT, IN COMMUNITY-ENGAGED RESEARCH WITH SPECIAL EXPERTISE IN RURAL AREAS, IN INFORMATICS AND INTEGRATION OF DATA TO DRIVE EVIDENCE-BASED CARE AND INFORM PUBLIC HEALTH ACTION AND POLICY, AND FOR SHARING METHODS AND PARTICIPATING IN NUMEROUS CTSA CONSORTIA ACTIVITIES. OUR VISION IS TO MEASURABLY IMPROVE HEALTH BY DISCOVERING AND DISSEMINATING STRATEGIES THAT WORK WITHIN BOTH LEARNING HEALTHCARE AND LEARNING PUBLIC HEALTH SYSTEMS. THE CENTER WILL MAXIMIZE SYNERGIES REGIONALLY AND NATIONALLY FOR CONDUCTING CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH IN CARE AND IN COMMUNITIES. THIS APPLICATION DESCRIBES TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE SOLUTIONS FOR ENHANCING THE EFFICIENCY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF ALL TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH WITH EMPHASIS ON INNOVATIONS TO “TRANSFORM THE WAY THAT RESEARCH IS DONE, MAKING IT MORE RIGOROUS, MORE EFFICIENT, MORE IMPACTFUL, AND FASTER.” INTERLINKED STRATEGIC GOALS ARE 1) INNOVATING METHODS AND SHARING APPROACHES TO ACCELERATE EFFICIENT AND TRANSFORMATIVE RESEARCH, INCLUDING LEVERAGING SOPHISTICATED DATA METHODS TO IMPROVE PREVENTION AND CARE; 2) CULTIVATING REACH WITH HIGH-FUNCTIONING RESEARCH COLLABORATIONS THAT SPAN THE STATE, REGION, AND CTSA CONSORTIUM TO TACKLE HEALTH CHALLENGES IN NEW WAYS FOR HIGH IMPACT; 3) ADVANCING CAREERS AND CAPACITY OF STAFF, SCHOLARS, FACULTY, AND ORGANIZATIONS DOING TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE; AND 4) EMPOWERING INVESTIGATORS WITH AGILE RESEARCH SERVICES, HIGHEST CALIBER RESOURCES, CONSULTATIVE EXPERTISE, PILOT FUNDS, AND NEW TECHNOLOGY. FIRST FUNDED BY NIH IN 2011, THE CCTS ENGAGES A 16-COLLEGE CAMPUS, IS ENGRAFTED IN UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY HEALTHCARE, AND COLLABORATES WITH MULTIPLE NETWORKS AND ORGANIZATIONS. CCTS INFRASTRUCTURE IS ROBUST. DISTINCTIVE FEATURES INCLUDE 1) ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORD INTEGRATION VIA EPIC, SECURE NIST 800-53 COMPLIANT COMPUTING, REAL-WORLD APPLICATIONS OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS AND AI FOR ENHANCING DIAGNOSTICS, PREDICTION IN CLINICAL CARE, AND PUBLIC HEALTH DECISION MAKING; 2) FOUNDING ROLES IN TWO RURAL HEALTH RESEARCH NETWORKS, THE APPALACHIAN TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH NETWORK AND CONSORTIUM OF RURAL STATES, AND PROPOSED NEW COLLABORATIONS TO LEVERAGE THE STRENGTHS OF THE UK COOPERATIVE EXTENSION SERVICE, ENGAGE THE KENTUCKY AMBULATORY RESEARCH NETWORK, CREATE THE ENVIRONMENT AND HEALTH COALITION WITH UNIVERSITY OF LOUISVILLE, AND FORM THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY RESEARCH NETWORK ALLIANCE WITH THREE LARGE EXISTING UK NETWORKS TO ENSURE EFFICIENT STATEWIDE REACH; 3) IMPLEMENTING SHARED GOVERNANCE, MATRIX ORGANIZATION, AND DESIGN THINKING PRINCIPLES; AND 4) ESTABLISHING APPROACHES TO CONTINUOUSLY REVIEW REQUESTS FOR PILOT FUNDING, TO IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE, EVALUATE WITH REAL-TIME DASHBOARDS, AND ACCELERATE RESEARCH PROCESSES. THE CCTS IS OPTIMIZED FOR DISCOVERING, DISSEMINATING, AND DEPLOYING EVIDENCE TO ADVANCE HEALTH.
